title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purposes support to the Association of Charitable Foundations, a membership organization of over 300 grantmakers in the United Kingdom. The association offers a wide range of services and programs to support and enhance philanthropy, including conferences, publications, technical assistance and networking. Accomplishments in 2005 include representing the interests of trusts and foundations; enhancing members’ knowledge by organizing nine training events; publishing a quarterly magazine, “Trust & Foundation News”, and a monthly newsletter, “Funders News”; and encouraging the development of new grantmaking foundations in the United Kingdom.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant supports the Association of Charitable Foundations, a membership organization of over 300 grantmakers in the United Kingdom. The association will continue to offer a wide range of services and programs to support and enhance philanthropy, including conferences, publications, technical assistance, and networking. Accomplishments during 2006-2010 include increasing attendance among members at regular seminars, annual conferences, and special events; successfully representing the interests of trusts and foundations vis-à-vis key pieces of legislation; publishing a quarterly magazine, “Trust & Foundation News”, and a monthly newsletter, “Funders News”; and supporting ongoing member collaborations, such as the Woburn Place Collaborative and the Intelligent Funding Forum.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant supports the Association of Charitable Foundations, a membership organization of over 300 grantmakers in the U.K. The grantee offers a wide range of services and programs to support and enhance philanthropy, including annual conferences, publications, technical assistance, and networking. Recent accomplishments include publishing groundbreaking research on giving trends in the U.K; refreshing its Professional Development Programme to explore aspects of foundation strategy and grantmaking practice; hosting fundernetwork.org.uk, an online peer-to-peer, knowledge-sharing hub with over 500 active members; and publishing a quarterly magazine, “Trust & Foundation News”, and a monthly newsletter, “Funders’ News”. In the next grant period, the grantee will develop a series of annual publications about the role and activities of foundations, make full use of new opportunities afforded by technology and social media, and launch a new publication series aimed at promoting good practice in grantmaking.

title: International Program
description: This grant supports the Council on Foundations’ international programs, which aim to promote and facilitate responsible and effective grantmaking among its members and to support philanthropy as an essential part of strengthened civil society around the world. Accomplishments over the past three years include the publication of “The Principles of Accountability for International Philanthropy”, the launch of the Philanthropic Initiative for the Americas, the redesign and expansion of the United States International Grantmaking Web site, and work on the Centralized Repository Feasibility Project. Over the next two years, the Council will: (1) maximize opportunities for collaboration, understanding, and learning around international grantmaking; (2) promote the highest standards of accountability, diversity, and good practice for international grantmaking; and (3) advocate for an improved legal environment for international grantmaking. Founded in 1949, the Council on Foundations is a membership organization of private, community, and corporate foundations, primarily in the United States.

title: Global Philanthropy Program
description: This grant supports the Council on Foundations’ Global Philanthropy Program, which aims to promote and facilitate responsible and effective grantmaking among its members and to support philanthropy as an essential part of a strengthened civil society around the world. Accomplishments over the past two years include developing a searchable database on global giving in partnership with the Foundation Center; organizing a meeting of the Global Philanthropy Leadership Initiative in partnership with the European Foundation Centre and the Worldwide Initiatives for Grantmaker Support; and working with the Treasury Department and the Internal Revenue Service on approval of a Web-based repository for equivalency determination. Future plans include continuing support for the Global Philanthropy Leadership Initiative; continuing to work on the voluntary guidelines with the U.S. Treasury; and providing general member services to enhance international grantmaking. Founded in 1949, the Council on Foundations is a membership organization of private, community, and corporate foundations, primarily in the United States.

title: Global Philanthropy Program
description: This grant supports the Council on Foundations’ Global Philanthropy Program, which aims to promote and facilitate responsible and effective grantmaking among its members and to support philanthropy as an essential part of strengthened civil society around the world. Through this program, the grantee has developed and implemented programs and services that promote excellence in global philanthropy, advocated for regulatory reform to catalyze domestic global philanthropy, and provided leadership to the global philanthropy sector. Future plans include continuing support for the Global Grantmaking Institute, concluding the Global Philanthropy Leadership Initiative and championing its outcomes, continuing to work on achieving regulatory approval for the creation of Equivalency Determination Information Repositories, and providing general member services to enhance international grantmaking. Founded in 1949, the Council on Foundations is a membership organization of private, community, and corporate foundations, primarily in the United States.

title: Global Philanthropy Program
description: This grant supports the Council on Foundations’ Global Philanthropy Program, which helps its members undertake cross-border philanthropy and support grantees in other countries around the world. Over the past 18 months, the grantee has worked with partners on Financial Action Task Force guidelines; kept members aware of changing international regulations that impact cross-border philanthropic flows; maintained a library of resources on international grantmaking on its Website; and offered a significant amount of global programming at its conferences. Following the recent arrival of a new staff person to head the program and a subsequent stakeholder analysis, the Global Philanthropy Program will be framed around three pillars of activity: 1) effective cross-border grantmaking; 2) policy and regulation of cross-border grantmaking; and 3) global conversations and convening. Founded in 1949, the Council on Foundations is a membership organization of private, community, and corporate foundations, primarily in the United States.

title: Global Philanthropy Program
description: This grant supports the Council on Foundations’ Global Philanthropy Program, which is framed around three pillars of activity: 1) effective cross-border grantmaking; 2) policy and regulation of cross-border grantmaking; and 3) global conversations and convening. Over the past 18 months, the grantee has worked with partners on Financial Action Task Force guidelines, kept members aware of changing international regulations that impact cross-border philanthropic flows, maintained a library of resources on international grantmaking on its website, and offered a significant amount of global programming at its conferences. During this grant period, in addition to enhancing and expanding the above activities, the grantee will launch a new Global Philanthropic Strategies educational program. Founded in 1949, the Council on Foundations is a membership organization of private, community, and corporate foundations, primarily in the United States.

title: Mott Middle College Replication
description: This grant to Mott Community College will enable staff of Mott Middle College High School to provide a more in-depth response to requests to share its instructional model and innovative curriculum for high school students with school districts throughout Genesee County, the United States, and Canada. As the first multidistrict middle college high school in the country and the first to achieve North Central Association accreditation, Mott Middle College High School models “best practices” in high school reform and represents a valuable resource for other school districts struggling to address the needs of disengaged students.

title: Mott Middle/Early College Replication
description: This grant to Mott Community College will enable the staff of Mott Middle/Early College High School to continue its replication and research efforts. Through a partnership with the State of Michigan, Mott Middle/Early College High School administrative staff will direct the Center for Middle and Early College in Michigan, which provides technical assistance for the 16 nascent middle/early college high schools and operates as a hub for national dissemination of Michigan’s progress in the development of middle and early colleges. In response to requests to share its instructional model and innovative curriculum for high school students with school districts throughout Michigan, Mott Middle/Early College High School currently serves as a learning lab for “best practices” in high school reform, and represents a valuable resource for other school districts struggling to address the needs of disengaged students.

title: Mott Middle/Early College Replication
description: This grant will enable the staff of Mott Middle/Early College High School to continue its replication and research efforts. As an early adapter of the middle/early college high school model, Mott Community College is entering its 27th year of implementation and research of this blended secondary and postsecondary design. Through a partnership with the Michigan Department of Education, Mott Middle/Early College High School administrative staff will lead the Center for Middle and Early Colleges, which provides technical assistance for 45 middle/early college high schools in Michigan and operates as a hub for national dissemination of progress in the development of middle and early colleges.

title: Mott Middle/Early College Replication
description: This grant will enable the staff of Mott Middle/Early College High School to continue its replication and research efforts. As an early adapter of the middle/early college high school model, Mott Community College is entering its 27th year of implementation and research of blended secondary and post-secondary school design. Through a partnership with the Michigan Department of Education, Mott Middle/Early College High School administrative staff will lead the Center for Michigan Early and Middle College Partnerships, which provides technical assistance to 24 middle/early college high schools and 93 middle/early college programs in Michigan. In addition, the Center for Michigan Early and Middle College Partnerships will continue to serve as a hub for national dissemination of progress in the replication of the model.

Key activities include an annual conference; conferences and workshops on various community development topics and policy issues; and publications including a quarterly newsletter, research and background papers, case studies, and policy papers.

title: Career Academy Evaluation Phase II
description: This renewal grant to MDRC will partially support a continuing evaluation of career academies to determine whether these schools have an impact on postsecondary completion and degree attainment and whether the earnings impacts and employment are increasing and sustainable. The evaluation also examines a broader set of outcomes for career academy alumni including the nature of their jobs, career mobility opportunities, healthy lifestyles, civic engagement, marriage and family formation, and reductions in risk-taking behavior.

title: BRIDGE Project
grantee: National Network for Immigrant and Refugee Rights
description: The National Network for Immigrant and Refugee Rights created the project BRIDGE: Building a Race and Immigration Dialogue in the Global Era to connect immigrants, people of color and social activists.This grant will enable BRIDGE to increase immigrant community engagement; deepen the capacity of an emerging corps of immigrant and refugee community organizers through the BRIDGE Trainers Bureau; and develop new education curricula and resources to support skill-building for immigrant and refugee groups.In May 2004, the network published the BRIDGE resource manual after two years of re-testing and development with 70 community groups. In September 2005, the Second Annual Immigrant and Refugee Rights Training Institute was held. More than 100 organizers and community leaders engaged in capacity-building trainings and dialogues.

title: Nonprofit Sector Research Fund
description: This grant continues support for the scholarly work pursued by the Aspen Institute’s Nonprofit Sector Research Fund. The fund awards research grants and organizes convenings to expand knowledge of the nonprofit sector and philanthropy, improve nonprofit practices, and inform public policy related to nonprofits. In past years, Mott support was targeted at community foundation research. Most recently, research was focused on nonfinancial measures of community foundation performance. During the current grant period, Mott funds will be focused on nonprofit databases. The fund will facilitate a series of meetings, which will bring together nonprofit database organization leaders, nonprofit scholars, and key practitioners to develop and implement a work plan for strengthening nonprofit databases. These meetings will identify the highest priority challenges facing nonprofit databases, which will then be the subject of follow-up research and convening.

title: Nonprofit Public Information Project
description: This grant provides continued support for the Nonprofit Public Information Project of the Aspen Institute’s Program on Philanthropy and Social Innovation. Until recently, this project had been implemented within the institute’s Nonprofit Sector Research Fund, which Mott has supported to conduct nonprofit research since 1992. Over the past 18 months, Mott funds supported convenings of leading figures in the field of nonprofit research and data which resulted in a consensus to work with government to improve the quality, timeliness, accessibility, and efficiency of our nation’s nonprofit data collection system. During the next two years, project activities will include monitoring new policies affecting the social sector to assess impact on nonprofit data, identifying social sector data gaps and needs, conducting research on the ways in which the federal government and the social sector can work together to improve nonprofit data, and activities aimed at deepening collaboration among the data groups themselves.

title: Nonprofit Data Project
description: This grant provides continued support for the Aspen Institute’s Nonprofit Data Project. Over the past two years, Mott funds supported convenings of leading figures in the field of nonprofit research and data and work with government agencies to improve the quality, timeliness, accessibility, and efficiency of the nation’s nonprofit data collection system. The Nonprofit Data Project will include continued research and exploration on how the federal government and the social sector can work together to improve nonprofit data, as well as convenings of leading researchers and outreach and dialogue with policymakers, academics, and nonprofit and foundation leaders on developing creative and broad-based solutions to the lack of high quality, current nonprofit data. The Aspen Institute is a leading domestic think tank with an international network of partners that fosters values-based leadership and provides a neutral and balanced venue for discussing and acting on critical issues.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant continues general purposes support to the Association of Black Foundation Executives, an organization whose members are staff or board members of corporate and foundation grantmaking organizations. The association encourages increased funding of issues important to the black community and families; conducts collaborative efforts with other philanthropic membership organizations; and promotes the status, development, and number of black professionals in philanthropy. It presents educational programs, conducts and encourages research, provides technical assistance, and produces publications on philanthropy related to the African-American community.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant continues general purpose support to the Association of Black Foundation Executives, an organization whose members are staff or board members of corporate and foundation grantmaking organizations. Recent accomplishments include the promotion of fellowship program participants to leadership roles such as president and trustee; the release of two major research reports and a number of publications related to philanthropy in the black community; partnerships with other key identity-based affinity groups; and a significant increase in membership. Over the next two years, the association will continue its work to encourage increased funding of issues critical to the black community; conduct collaborative efforts with other philanthropic membership organizations; and promote the status, development, and number of black professionals in philanthropy.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant supports the Association of Black Foundation Executives, a membership organization that promotes effective and responsive philanthropy in black communities. The association is dedicated to the professional development of its members, who are staff and board members of philanthropic organizations. Recent accomplishments include: graduating the fifth class of a fellowship program for young black professionals in philanthropy, building the membership of the Black Philanthropic Network with regional associations of grantmakers, and redesigning the Race Matters Toolkit to focus specifically on the role of philanthropy in black communities. Over the next two years, the grantee’s goals are to: 1) encourage philanthropic institutions in Michigan to adopt its Framework for Responsive Philanthropy in Black Communities; 2) increase awareness within the philanthropic community on the key issues affecting black communities and possible investment strategies to address them; and 3) create greater connections among the grantee’s members through regional meetings and targeted communications.

title: General Purposes
description: The Association of Black Foundation Executives, a membership organization that promotes effective and responsive philanthropy in black communities, is dedicated to the professional development of its members who are staff and board members of philanthropic organizations. The grantee’s current goals are to: 1) encourage philanthropic institutions in Michigan to adopt its Framework for Responsive Philanthropy in Black Communities; 2) increase awareness within the philanthropic community on the key issues affecting black communities and possible investment strategies to address them; and 3) create greater connections among the grantee’s members through regional meetings and targeted communications. This grant increase will support the participation of two membership and development staff in the Council on Foundations’ fall conference for community foundations. Through its participation in the conference, the grantee will develop a more targeted strategy that considers the specific nature and opportunities of working with community foundations for impact in black communities.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant supports the Association of Black Foundation Executives, a membership organization that promotes effective and responsive philanthropy in black communities. The grantee is dedicated to the professional development of its members who are staff and board members of philanthropic organizations. Its primary areas of programming are networking and convening, professional development, training and technical assistance, and advocacy. Last year, the grantee launched its Responsive Philanthropy in Black Communities Framework and Knowledge Center. Over the next three years the grantee will focus on four primary outcomes: 1) an increased understanding within the philanthropic sector of the complex issues facing black communities; 2) effective partnerships and networks that strengthen black communities; 3) linkages within the philanthropic sector to develop coordinated strategies that leverage resources for the greatest social impact in black communities; and 4) investments of new resources targeted to priority issues and policies that impact black people and communities.

title: Land Stewardship Initiative
description: Through its Land Stewardship Initiative, the Michigan Environmental Council has worked to inform citizens, grassroots groups, and policymakers about land use issues and trends and the need for solutions that address the adverse impacts of sprawl. Although this effort has helped set a receptive climate for policy reform, only initial reforms have been enacted, and thus, the Michigan Environmental Council has been increasing its efforts to facilitate connections between land use and other related economic, social, and environmental issues and initiatives. During the next two years, the Michigan Environmental Council will build on this work to incorporate best land use practices and approaches into an array of policies and programs, particularly through its involvement with state work groups and increased outreach to promote regional collaboration, and will reinforce the link between land use policy and economic prosperity.

title: Moving Michigan Toward a World-Class Transportation System
description: Created in 1980, the Michigan Environmental Council has developed into a strong membership-based organization of more than 70 groups dedicated to informing policies and practices that help ensure protection of the environment and public health. As part of its land use and growth management work, the council has become actively engaged in transportation issues at both the state and national levels. This grant will support the council’s work to align transportation-related decisions in Michigan with emerging opportunities at the federal level; build broad support for a state transportation agenda that calls for increased investments in public transportation and nonmotorized options; and promote connections between transportation and other prominent public concerns, such as urban revitalization.

title: Moving Michigan Toward a World-Class Transportation System
description: In recent years, the Michigan Environmental Council, a statewide coalition of environmental groups, has worked to align transportation-related decisions in Michigan with emerging opportunities at the federal level; build broad support for a state transportation agenda that calls for increased investments in public transportation and nonmotorized options; and promote connections between transportation and other prominent public concerns. This renewal grant will allow the council to deepen such work through efforts to prepare the state’s metropolitan regions for world-class transit; support the implementation of existing transit system plans as models; inform decisionmaking related to transportation and state economic development investments; support effective implementation of Michigan’s Complete Streets policy; and build support for a comprehensive passenger rail system in Michigan.

title: Moving Michigan Toward a World-Class Transportation System
description: In recent years, the Michigan Environmental Council, a statewide coalition of environmental groups, has worked to align transportation-related decisions in Michigan with emerging opportunities at the federal level; build broad support for a state transportation agenda that calls for increased investments in public transportation and nonmotorized options; and promote connections between transportation and other prominent public concerns. This renewal grant will allow the grantee to continue such work with a focus on expanding state and federal resources available for transit and nonmotorized transportation options, promoting an intercity rail network in Michigan, assisting in the implementation of the new regional transit authority in southeast Michigan, and advancing other statewide transportation priorities.

The Greater Flint Arts Council will continue to serve the community with a wide variety of activities and events, including educational programs, assistance to new artists, publishing a monthly newsletter, providing exhibitions and arts brokering, operating a mini-grant program, and continuing to encourage collaborative projects between artists and agencies.

description: This grant will provide general purposes support to the Gamaliel Foundation, a network of 63 community organizations in 19 states. The Gamaliel Foundation provides local affiliates with a variety of resources including extensive leadership training programs; staff recruitment, placement, and development; opportunities for leaders and staff to meet and exchange ideas; issue research; and convening local groups to work on common issues.

title: Grantmakers East Group
geographic_focus: Bulgaria, Ukraine, Hungary, Slovenia, Czech Republic, Russia, Slovakia, Belarus, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Romania, Poland, Albania, North Macedonia, Estonia, Lithuania, Latvia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia
description: This grant supports an affinity group of the European Foundation Centre to improve the effectiveness of grantmaking in Central and Eastern Europe and the former Soviet Union and to encourage new donor activity in the region. The Grantmakers East Group was created in 1992, and its core activity is an annual meeting for grantmakers active in the region. Approximately 150 grantmakers participate in the annual meetings. The group is guided by a steering committee and administered by a secretariat housed in the European Foundation Centre. Over the years, the annual meetings have improved networking and information exchange among donors, encouraged development of new philanthropic initiatives, and promoted good grantmaking practices. In 2007-2009, the European Foundation Centre will work with the steering committee to improve the format of the annual meetings, widely disseminate meeting reports, and ensure the continuing relevance of the meetings to the changing context in the region.

title: Grantmakers East Forum
geographic_focus: Montenegro, Moldova, Romania, Belarus, Estonia, Serbia, Ukraine, North Macedonia, Albania, Hungary, Czech Republic, Poland, Lithuania, Slovenia, Latvia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Slovakia, Russia, Bulgaria, Croatia
description: This grant supports an affinity group of the European Foundation Centre to improve the effectiveness of grantmaking in Central and Eastern Europe and the former Soviet Union and to encourage new donor activity in the region. To this end, in 2010 and 2011 the center will organize the annual meeting of the group, called the Grantmakers East Forum, for interested grantmakers and donors working in this region. The center will work with the forum’s steering committee to further develop the format of the annual meetings, secure outside speakers, arrange the venue and other logistics, and disseminate the meetings reports. In 2009 the center organized the forum’s annual meeting in Berlin, Germany, to coincide with the 20th anniversary of the fall of the Berlin Wall. The annual meeting took place in Dubrovnik, Croatia, in 2008 and Tallinn, Estonia, in 2007. As in previous years, these annual meetings attracted more than 150 participants and provided opportunities for networking and information exchange, encouraged development of new philanthropic initiatives, and promoted good grantmaking practices.

To this end, in 2012 and 2013, the grantee will organize the annual meeting of the group, called the Grantmakers East Forum, for interested grantmakers and donors working in this region. In 2012, the meeting will take place in Sarajevo, Bosnia-Herzegovina. The grantee will work with the forum’s steering committee to further develop the format of the annual meetings, secure outside speakers, arrange the venue and other logistics, and disseminate the meetings’ reports. In 2010, the grantee organized the forum’s annual meeting in Tbilisi, Georgia, and in 2011, it took place in Riga, Latvia. As in previous years, these annual meetings attracted more than 150 participants and provided opportunities for networking and information exchange, encouraged development of new philanthropic initiatives, and promoted good grantmaking practices. Based in Brussels, Belgium, the European Foundation Centre is an international association of foundations and corporate funders dedicated to strengthening European philanthropy.

title: General Purposes
description: During the past 15 years, state associations of nonprofits have emerged as effective providers of services and peer-to-peer support to local nonprofit agencies. Today, the National Council of Nonprofit Associations (NCNA) serves over 22,000 members in 45 states and the District of Columbia.This grant will enable NCNA to continue to serve, strengthen and support state associations. In addition, NCNA will develop a new business model to lessen its dependence on national foundation support and serve as the lead organization for the Nonprofit Congress, an initiative to bring together the nation’s nonprofits to develop a unified vision and collective voice for the sector.In 2005, NCNA responded to more than 1,000 requests for technical assistance from members and the general public regarding all areas of nonprofit management and public policy.

title: General Purposes
description: This general purposes grant supports the National Council of Nonprofit Associations’ effort to strengthen the national network of state nonprofit associations and develop their capacity to support community-based organizations throughout the country. State associations of nonprofits have emerged as effective providers of services and peer-to-peer support to local nonprofit agencies. Recognizing the challenges facing the nonprofit sector through increased scrutiny and regulations, the council provides technical assistance, shares best practices and other relevant information, and offers networking opportunities to state and regional associations to enhance their ability to increase their members’ effectiveness and accountability and to better represent their members at the public policy level.

title: General Purposes
description: This general purpose grant supports the National Council of Nonprofit Associations’ effort to strengthen the national network of state nonprofit associations and develop their capacity to support community-based organizations throughout the country. The organization serves over 20,000 members in 41 states and the District of Columbia, linking local organizations (especially small and midsized nonprofits) to a national audience through state associations. Recognizing the challenges facing the nonprofit sector through increased scrutiny and regulations, the council continues to provide technical assistance, share best practices and other relevant information, and offer networking opportunities to state and regional associations to enhance their ability to increase their members’ effectiveness and accountability and to better represent their members at the public policy level.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant supports the National Council of Nonprofits to strengthen the national network of state nonprofit associations, and by doing so develop its capacity to support community-based organizations throughout the country. The organization serves over 20,000 members in 41 states and the District of Columbia, linking local organizations (especially small and midsized nonprofits) to a national audience through state associations. The grantee will continue to provide technical assistance, share best practices and other relevant information, and offer networking opportunities to state and regional associations. This should, in turn, increase its members’ effectiveness and accountability, as well as its capacity to represent its members at the public policy level.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant supports the National Council of Nonprofits, the nation’s largest network of nonprofits, now with more than 25,000 member organizations across the country. Its mission is to advance the vital role, capacity, and voice of charitable, nonprofit organizations. The council works through its network of state associations to amplify the collective voice of America’s charitable, nonprofit organizations (especially local, community-based, and small to mid-size). The council has helped nonprofits operate more effectively, collaborate and exchange solutions, engage in critical policy issues affecting the sector, and achieve greater impact in their communities. During the grant period, the grantee will continue to provide technical assistance to nonprofits, share best practices and other relevant information, and offer networking opportunities to state and regional associations.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant supports the National Council of Nonprofits, the nation’s largest network of nonprofits, now with more than 25,000 individual nonprofit organizational members across the country. The grantee is a trusted resource and advocate for America’s charitable nonprofits. Its mission is to advance the vital role, capacity, and voice of charitable nonprofit organizations. The grantee works through its network of state associations, individual members, and state policy allies (national organizations with policy operations in multiple states) to amplify the collective voice of America’s charitable nonprofit organizations. It has helped nonprofits operate more effectively, collaborate and exchange solutions, engage in critical policy issues affecting the sector, and achieve greater impact in their communities. A grant increase will help the council fill an unanticipated financial gap created by its engagement in international activities, primarily via its participation in CIVICUS’ Affinity Group of National Associations.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant supports the National Council of Nonprofits, the nation’s largest network of nonprofits, now with more than 25,000 member organizations across the country. Its mission is to advance the vital role, capacity, and voice of charitable, nonprofit organizations. The grantee works through its network of state associations to help nonprofits operate more effectively, engage in critical policy issues affecting the sector, and achieve greater impact in their communities. Over the past two years, the grantee expanded and strengthened as a network; advocated for policies favorable to the nonprofit sector; raised public awareness and advanced solutions regarding the government-nonprofit contracting system; and became the United States’ representative to the worldwide CIVICUS Affinity Group of National Associations. During the upcoming grant period, the grantee will strengthen the capacity of nonprofits, give voice to nonprofits through public policy advocacy, and highlight the vital roles that charitable nonprofits play in benefiting local communities.
