title: Great Lakes Aquatic Habitat Network and Fund
grantee: Tip of the Mitt Watershed Council
geographic_focus: Minnesota, Ontario, New York, Pennsylvania, Illinois, Indiana, Wisconsin, Ohio, Michigan
description: Initiated in 1996 as a project of the Tip of the Mitt Watershed Council, a well-established watershed organization in northern Michigan, the Great Lakes Aquatic Habitat Network and Fund seeks to support an effective grassroots sector working locally to protect aquatic habitats throughout the Great Lakes basin. With prior Mott support, the program has: provided small grants for aquatic habitat conservation projects, organizational development, and technical assistance; organized training and networking events; and linked local efforts to policy initiatives at the state, province, basin, and national levels. After a comprehensive review process, the council has decided to establish the program as a separate entity. Renewal support will allow the program to continue to provide services to local groups as it transitions to an independent organization in 2008.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Ontario, Ohio, Illinois, Indiana, Wisconsin, Michigan, Pennsylvania, Minnesota, New York
description: Freshwater Future has recently launched itself as a stand-alone nonprofit seeking to support community-based groups working locally to protect aquatic habitats throughout the Great Lakes basin. As a former project of Tip of the Mitt Watershed, prior Mott support provided small grants, networking opportunities, and technical assistance to such groups and will continue to do so over the next two years. The grantee will also attend to its own organizational development needs, such as revenue diversification.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Minnesota, Ontario, Ohio, Wisconsin, Michigan, Indiana, Illinois, Pennsylvania, New York
description: Freshwater Future supports community-based groups working locally to protect aquatic habitats throughout the Great Lakes Basin. With this grant increase, Freshwater Future will continue providing small grants and capacity building support to such groups. The organization will also launch a pilot program to provide technology assistance to targeted groups.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Minnesota, Wisconsin, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Illinois, Indiana, New York, Michigan, Ontario
description: Freshwater Future supports community-based groups working locally to protect aquatic habitats throughout the Great Lakes basin. With Mott support over the last 14 years, the grantee (formerly a project of Tip of the Mitt Watershed Council) has provided over $1 million to these groups in the form of small grants, technical support, and communications assistance. Additional services offered include networking opportunities, educational materials, and communications support. With this renewal, the grantee will continue to offer these programs while connecting its constituents to broader policy reform efforts. The grantee will also maintain its efforts to strengthen its own organizational capacity through board and staff development and revenue diversification.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Minnesota, Indiana, New York, Pennsylvania, Michigan, Ohio, Wisconsin, Ontario, Illinois
description: Freshwater Future supports community-based groups working locally to protect aquatic habitats throughout the Great Lakes Basin. This grant increase will support the general purposes of the organization, including a convening of Great Lakes groups to allow improved regional coordination around preventing the invasive Asian carp from gaining a foothold in the Great Lakes.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Minnesota, Pennsylvania, New York, Wisconsin, Ontario, Illinois, Michigan, Ohio, Indiana
description: Freshwater Future supports community-based groups working locally to protect aquatic habitats throughout the Great Lakes Basin. This grant increase will support the general purposes of the organization, which include providing small grants and technical assistance to local groups working to monitor and address the impacts of an oil spill in southwestern Michigan and natural gas drilling activities in northern Michigan.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Michigan, Ontario, Indiana, Wisconsin, Pennsylvania, Ohio, New York, Illinois, Minnesota
description: Freshwater Future supports community-based groups working locally to protect aquatic habitats throughout the Great Lakes basin. This grant increase will support the general purposes of the organization, which includes providing small grants and technical assistance to Michigan’s grassroots groups working to protect local water resources from the impacts of mining sulfide-based ores.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Ontario, Indiana, Wisconsin, Michigan, Pennsylvania, Ohio, New York, Illinois, Minnesota
description: Freshwater Future supports citizen groups working locally to protect and improve aquatic habitats throughout the Great Lakes Basin. With Mott support over 16 years, the grantee provided $1.5 million to these groups in the form of small grants, technical support, and capacity building assistance. A portion of this funding helped local groups address unanticipated, high priority issues, such as the 2010 oil spill in Michigan’s Kalamazoo River. With this renewal, the grantee will continue offering the full array of its technical assistance and capacity building services while connecting its constituents to key Great Lakes policy reform efforts. Freshwater Future will also strengthen its own internal capacity.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Ontario, Indiana, Michigan, New York, Pennsylvania, Ohio, Minnesota, Illinois, Wisconsin
description: Freshwater Future is a regional environmental organization that supports community-based groups working locally to protect the Great Lakes watershed. This grant increase will support the general purposes of the organization, which includes efforts to increase grassroots engagement in freshwater policy conversations in Wisconsin. The organization will also contract with regional experts to inform state-level policy reform discussions and build public support for protecting the health of Lake Superior.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Michigan, Minnesota, New York, Pennsylvania, Ontario, Ohio, Wisconsin, Illinois, Indiana
description: Freshwater Future supports citizen groups working across the Great Lakes Basin to protect and improve their communities’ rivers, lakes, and wetland ecosystems. With prior Mott support, the grantee offered an array of technical assistance and capacity-building services to grassroots groups. The organization also connected its constituents to binational and regional Great Lakes policy reform efforts to protect water quality from threats such as Asian carp and impacts from new resource extraction activities. With renewed support, the grantee will continue to strengthen the capacity of individual watershed groups while also helping amplify their collective voice on high priority regional Great Lakes issues.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Michigan, Minnesota, Wisconsin, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Illinois, Indiana, New York, Ontario
description: Freshwater Future is a regional environmental organization that supports citizen groups working across the Great Lakes Basin to protect and improve their communities’ rivers, lakes, and wetland ecosystems. With prior Mott support, the grantee offered a small grants program, capacity building services, and networking opportunities to grassroots groups. The grantee also connected its constituents to regional Great Lakes policy reform efforts to protect water quality from threats such as Asian Carp and impacts from new resource extraction activities. With renewed support, the grantee will continue to support individual groups working at the local level while also helping amplify their collective voice on high priority binational Great Lakes issues, such as reducing the occurrence of toxic algal blooms. The grantee will also take steps to strengthen its own organizational capacity.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Ohio, Minnesota, Illinois, Ontario, Indiana, Pennsylvania, New York, Wisconsin, Michigan
description: Freshwater Future, a regional environmental organization based in Michigan, supports citizens working to protect lakes, rivers, and wetlands throughout the Great Lakes Basin. Activities include supporting individuals and groups working at the local level while also helping amplify their collective voice on high priority Great Lakes policy issues. This grant increase will allow the grantee to begin addressing water infrastructure challenges and strengthen its relationships with community groups in selected Great Lakes urban areas.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Ontario, New York, Minnesota, Pennsylvania, Illinois, Indiana, Wisconsin, Ohio, Michigan
description: Freshwater Future serves a vital role as an intermediary between large organizations and smaller, grassroots groups. The grantee catalyzes action to strengthen policies to safeguard the Great Lakes by providing a small grants program, consulting services, and capacity building support. With prior support, the grantee has provided support to over 2,000 community groups, addressing local challenges and elevating voices to effect change on the state, provincial, or federal policy levels. This grant will allow the grantee to provide financial and capacity support to groups and also continue its focus on securing safe, affordable drinking water in our region’s cities as a top priority.

title: State Fiscal Analysis Initiative
description: Funding will enable the Fiscal Policy Institute to continue its analytical, educational and outreach activities in order to foster public policies that create a strong economy and broadly shared prosperity for all New Yorkers. Strengthening communications capacity will be another key priority.During the past two years, the institute played an important role in informing and framing public debates on revenue and spending issues and on new and existing policy initiatives in New York. This is one of 10 grants supporting the State Fiscal Analysis Initiative. The Fiscal Policy Institute joined this effort in 1993. Mott has also supported the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, which provides technical assistance and networking opportunities for the 35 state organizations participating in this initiative.

title: State Fiscal Analysis Initiative
description: This is one of ten grants recommended to state organizations for their participation in the State Fiscal Analysis Initiative. The Ford, Annie E. Casey, and Mott Foundations created the initiative in 1992 in order to build state capacity for timely, credible, and accessible tax and budget analysis on behalf of low- and middle-income families. The Fiscal Policy Institute joined the initiative in 1993 and is well-recognized throughout New York as an authoritative source of information on budget and tax policy issues, short- and long-term economic trends, and safety net and other low-income programs. During the renewal grant period, the grantee will prepare and disseminate analytical products across a range of issues. Other activities planned for the next two years include community outreach, public education, and strategic communications efforts. Related to this project is a grant to the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, which provides technical assistance to all 36 organizations participating in this initiative.

title: State Fiscal Analysis Initiative
description: The Ford, Casey, and Mott foundations created the State Fiscal Analysis Initiative in 1992 in order to build state capacity for timely, credible, and accessible tax and budget analysis on behalf of low- and middle-income families. As states face the challenges of devolution, issues of state fiscal policy grow even more important. This grant supports the Fiscal Policy Institute, a nonpartisan research and education organization that conducts policy research, analysis, and education to increase understanding of issues related to the fairness of New York’s tax system and the stability and adequacy of state and local public services. It is particularly concerned with safety net and poverty reduction programs, and programs that assist low- and moderate-income people in moving up the socioeconomic ladder. Related to this project is a grant to the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, which provides technical assistance to all the state organizations participating in this initiative.

title: State Fiscal Analysis Initiative
description: This is one of ten grants recommended to state organizations participating in the State Fiscal Analysis Initiative. The Ford, Casey, and Mott foundations created the initiative in 1992 in order to build state capacity for timely, credible, and accessible tax and budget analysis on behalf of low- and moderate-income families. The Fiscal Policy Institute joined the initiative in 1994 and is recognized throughout New York as an authoritative source of information and analysis. During the renewal grant period, the institute will conduct policy research, analysis, and education to increase understanding of issues related to the fairness of New York’s tax system and the stability and adequacy of public services, with a particular emphasis on programs that assist low- and moderate-income people in moving up the socioeconomic ladder. The grantee’s research will also highlight the economic challenges facing low-wage workers. Related to this project is a grant to the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, which analyzes federal budget and tax policy issues and provides technical assistance to all the state organizations participating in this initiative.

title: State Fiscal Analysis Initiative
description: This is one of ten grants recommended to state organizations as part of the State Fiscal Analysis Initiative. The Ford, Casey, and Mott foundations created the initiative in 1992 in order to build state capacity for timely, credible, and accessible tax and budget analysis on behalf of low- and middle-income families. The Fiscal Policy Institute was founded in 1991 to increase public and governmental understanding of issues related to the fairness of New York’s tax system and the stability and adequacy of state and local public services. The grantee joined the State Fiscal Analysis Initiative in 1993 and has become recognized as an authoritative source of information and analysis. During this grant period, the grantee will prepare and disseminate analyses on a range of state fiscal issues, with a particular emphasis on the state and local budget and tax policies, income, and economic security policies, and jobs, wages, and economic development policies. Related to this project is a grant to the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, which provides technical assistance to all 41state organizations participating in this initiative.

title: State Fiscal Analysis Initiative
description: This grant increase is one of ten tie-off grants to state organizations participating in the State Priorities Partnership (formerly the State Fiscal Analysis Initiative). The Ford, Annie E. Casey, and Mott foundations created the initiative in 1992 in order to build state capacity for timely, credible, and accessible tax and budget policy analyses on behalf of low- and moderate-income families. The Fiscal Policy Institute joined this effort in 1993 and has become recognized as an authoritative source of information and analysis. This grant increase will support the grantee’s ongoing analytical, communications, and coalition building efforts, with a particular emphasis on state budget and tax policy, workforce development, and economic development issues.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant increase will enable the Environmental Support Center to continue providing organizational capacity-building assistance to environmental, non-governmental organizations. During the past two years, the center has assisted more than 300 such organizations throughout the U.S.

title: General Purposes
description: The Environmental Support Center seeks to build the organizational capacity of local and state-level environmental groups through small grants, training programs, and related services. This grant increase will support the general purposes of the center, including special costs associated with successfully managing the transition to new executive leadership.

title: Living Standards of Americans
description: The goal of the project is to examine the conditions of the low-wage labor market and develop solutions that help boost earnings for low-income people. The Economic Policy Institute (EPI) was founded in 1986 to provide high-quality data-driven research and education relevant to economic and policy issues affecting working families.This grant will enable EPI to raise national awareness of the issues facing low-wage workers by conducting rigorous economic analyses on issues such as wage mobility and job retention; publishing and disseminating these analyses; enabling state and local organizations to use compiled data through the “DataZone” on the Internet; and providing technical assistance to emerging state and local organizations interested in economic analysis.Recent accomplishments included creating the “JobWatch” series, which monitors the American labor market with particular emphasis on job creation and job quality; releasing the ninth edition of the flagship publication, “The State of Working America”; and providing analyses and technical assistance on a range of issues including minimum wage, family budgets, health care insurance erosion and the benefits of full employment for low-wage workers.

title: Living Standards of Americans
description: This grant supports the work of the Economic Policy Institute that examines the conditions of the low-wage labor market and advocates solutions that help boost earnings for low-wage workers. Researchers, as well as communications and outreach staff, will work to raise national awareness of the issues facing low-wage workers by conducting rigorous economic analyses on income, wage, and employment trends; publishing and disseminating these analyses; enabling state and local organizations to use compiled data through the Internet; and providing technical assistance to emerging state and local organizations interested in economic analysis. Based in Washington, DC, the Economic Policy Institute is a nonprofit, nonpartisan think tank that seeks to broaden the public debate about strategies to achieve a prosperous and fair economy.

title: General Purposes
description: Corner House works to promote the adoption of common environmental standards for export credit agencies, in particular the World Bank, European-based export credit agencies and private banks. This grant will enable Corner House to continue research and public education work on environmental, human rights, anticorruption and development standards; monitor private-sector investment, particularly infrastructure development projects; track the impacts of specific projects and programs funded by international financial institutions, particularly in the hydropower and carbon sectors; and undertake media and educational activities on the sustainable development impacts of bilateral investment agreements, in addition to the broader issues of accountability and governance structures raised by regional and multinational trade agreements.Recently, Corner House was able to focus international attention on the counterproductive aspects of a global market in carbon, championed by the World Bank and other international financial institutions; develop new strategies for bringing concerns to the attention of private-sector investors and others in the financial community related to infrastructure development projects; and raise the awareness of international decisionmakers to the use of international investment agreements and treaties that exempt companies and investors from national environmental and social regulations.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purpose support for Corner House’s long-term goal to enhance the democratic control by communities in developed and developing countries over the decisions and investment resources that affect their lives and livelihood. To attain this goal, Corner House advocates for participatory, transparent, and accountable investment policies and practices of international financial institutions, in particular, the World Bank, European-based export credit agencies, and private banks. The focus of its work is the development of an investment framework that ensures the centrality of sustainable development objectives, as well as strengthening the safeguard policies governing the activities of international finance institutions.

title: General Purposes
description: Investment is often assumed to be an automatic route to economic growth. Corner House believes that addressing key questions about investments is essential if economic growth is to be environmentally sustainable and equitable. A central focus of the grantee’s work is to encourage public participation in decisionmaking on investments to ensure that projects that are financed promote sustainable livelihoods. Over the next two years, the grantee will continue its efforts to reform international financial institutions, in particular the World Bank; export credit agencies; and private banks. In addition, the grantee will focus on new trends emerging from the global financial crisis, including monitoring of proposed new regulations for derivatives and other complex financial vehicles and supporting efforts to construct banking and financial systems that reduce systemic risk and promote public interest goals.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purposes support for Corner House’s long-term goal to enhance the democratic control by communities in developed and developing countries over the decisions and resources that affect their lives and livelihood. To attain this goal, Corner House works to reform international finance and trade institutions, in particular the World Bank, European-based export credit agencies, and private banks. Corner House also monitors the impacts of specific projects and programs funded by other international financial institutions, particularly in the hydropower, forestry, and carbon sectors. As well, Corner House undertakes media and educational activities related to the sustainable development impacts of bilateral and international investment agreements, in addition to the broader issues of accountability and governance structures of the World Trade Organization.

title: General Purposes
description: Corner House is a research and policy organization that focuses public attention on the environmental, human rights, and social impacts of international investment flows, and advocates for policies that promote sustainable development. This grant will provide general purpose support, allowing the group to push for international investment policies and practices that are participatory, transparent, and accountable. Over the past grant period, the grantee undertook successful work, which resulted in strengthened international environmental and social guidelines for export credit agencies. With this renewal grant, the grantee will consolidate the work it has pursued over the past decade. It will also seek additional future funding sources for new initiatives focused on monitoring recent developments in private financing of energy and infrastructure projects.

title: Promoting Forest Peoples Interests in International Forest Policy Making
geographic_focus: Africa, Europe, Central America, South America, Russia
description: This grant will support the work of the Stichting Forest Peoples Programme to ensure that the rights and interests of forest peoples are given priority in the policies and programs of the World Bank Group, the Inter-American Development Bank and related private-sector activities.The project maintains a “bottom up” approach to advocacy by assisting forest peoples themselves to engage in policy debates and ensuring that the lessons learned from the program’s field projects are effectively used in the advocacy process.Recent program accomplishments included producing numerous briefings and technical reports to better inform forest-dependent communities on issues; raising awareness of the persistent gap between rhetoric and reality in World Bank policies and practices; working to promote greater accountability of the private sector and more effective regulation of investments and business ventures affecting forest-dependent communities; increasing the private sector’s awareness about the concerns of indigenous peoples with respect to extractive industries, forest law enforcement, certification programs and problems with industrial plantations; and helping develop JP Morgan-Chase Bank’s social policy, which committed the bank to respect indigenous peoples’ rights.

title: Promoting Forest Peoples Interests in International Forest Policy Making
geographic_focus: South America, Africa, Europe, Central America, Russia
description: This grant will support the work of the Stichting Forest Peoples Programme to promote sustainability in development finance. This project will ensure that the rights of forest peoples are respected by the World Bank Group, the Inter-American Development Bank, other regional development banks, and related private-sector mechanisms. This project will focus on the effective implementation of public and private international financial institutions’ environmental and social standards, as well as other relevant international standards, that aim to safeguard critical forest habitats and the rights and interests of forest peoples.

title: Promoting Forest Peoples Interests in International Forest Policy Making
geographic_focus: South America, Africa, Europe, Central America, Russia
description: The Forest Peoples Programme works to ensure that the rights and interests of forest peoples are given priority in the policies and programs of the World Bank Group and regional development banks. With prior Mott Foundation support, the program has helped to instigate one of the most important sector-wide lending reviews at the World Bank, assessing impacts of lending in the palm oil sector on the environment and livelihoods of forest-dependent communities. This project will continue its focus on assisting forest-dependent communities to engage directly in policy debates and ensure that the lessons learned from projects in the field are fed effectively into the advocacy process.

title: Promoting Forest Peoples' Interests in International Forest Policy Making
geographic_focus: Africa, South America, Europe, Russia, Central America
description: This grant will support the work of the Forest Peoples Programme to ensure that international financial institutions and other international development agencies adopt and fully comply with social and environmental policies that are in line with international standards. Over the course of this grant, the grantee has successfully ensured that indigenous peoples’ rights are protected and that effective consultation is now a key principle for multidonor funds that have been established to address forests and climate change. This project will maintain its bottom up approach by assisting forest peoples themselves to engage in policy debates and ensuring that the lessons learned are fed effectively into the advocacy process.

title: Protecting the Environment and Securing the Rights of Forest Peoples in International Development Finance
description: This grant will continue to support the work of the Forest Peoples Programme to ensure that the rights and interests of forest peoples are given priority in the policies and programs of the World Bank Group, the Inter-American Development Bank, and other international financial institutions. The Forest Peoples Programme has played a vital role in ensuring that the concerns of indigenous peoples and other forest-dependent communities are taken into consideration in the review processes of the World Bank Group’s safeguards and standards. This project will maintain their bottom up approach to advocacy by assisting forest peoples themselves to engage in policy debates and ensuring that the lessons learned from the program’s field projects are fed effectively into the advocacy process.

title: Protecting the Environment and Securing the Rights of Forest Peoples in International Development Finance
description: This grant will continue to support the work of the Forest Peoples Programme to ensure that the rights and interests of forest-dependent communities are given priority in the policies and programs of the World Bank Group, as well as the United Nations’ Green Climate Fund. The grantee is an international nonprofit that has played a vital role in ensuring that the concerns of indigenous peoples and other forest-dependent communities are taken into consideration in the review processes of the World Bank Group’s safeguards and standards. This project will continue to assist forest-dependent communities to engage in key debt finance policy debates.

title: Multilateral Financial Institutions Program
description: Both Ends Foundation has become a well-respected facilitator and convener for developing country non-governmental organizations. Both Ends Foundation’s European-based staff members provide important capacity building to non-governmental organization counterparts in developing countries. This grant increase will allow the coordinating group established to address the Regional Infrastructure Integration Initiative for Latin America to hold several meetings in Latin America and focus on developing its strategy and work plan for the next few years. The grantee will assist in coordinating this meeting as well as providing facilitation.

title: Multilateral Financial Institutions Program
description: With this renewal grant, Both Ends Foundation will continue working to improve the environmentally and socially harmful policies and practices of international financial institutions. Through this project, Both Ends Foundation provides technical and capacity building support to nongovernmental organizations in Asia, Latin America, Eastern Europe, and the former Soviet Union; works on project- and issue-specific campaigns with other nongovernmental organizations; and promotes improvements to the safeguard policies of international financial institutions, the Dutch export credit agency, and private banks. The Both Ends Foundation was established in 1990 to support the work of environmental organizations, primarily in developing and Central and Eastern European countries. The core of its activities supports connections between developed and developing countries, environment and development, and different sectors of society.

title: Multilateral Financial Institutions Program
description: With this renewal grant, Both Ends Foundation, an international organization that builds the capacity of environmental groups, will continue working to improve the environmental and social policies and practices of international finance institutions. Through this project, the grantee provides support to nongovernmental organizations in developing countries and Central and Eastern Europe, works on project and issue-specific campaigns with other nongovernmental organizations, and promotes improvements to the overall policy structure of international financial institutions and Dutch private financial institutions, including the Dutch export credit agency. With prior Mott support, Both Ends Foundation has assisted groups in the Andean region, Colombia, Bangladesh, the Mekong region, and elsewhere.

title: Multilateral Financial Institutions and Export Credit Agencies Program
description: With this renewal grant, Both Ends Foundation will continue working to improve the policies and practices of international finance institutions, so that they do not cause environmental and social harm. Over the last grant period, it played an active role in both the World Bank Environmental Policy and Energy Strategy review processes, preparing case studies that highlighted concrete issues raised by the reviews. Through this project, the grantee provides support to nongovernmental organizations in developing countries and Central and Eastern Europe, works on project and issue specific campaigns with other nongovernmental organizations, and promotes improvements to the overall policies of international finance institutions. It also works to reform the Dutch export credit agency and private banks.

title: Multilateral Financial Institutions and Export Credit Agencies Program
description: With this renewal grant, Both Ends Foundation will continue working to improve the environmental and social policies and practices of international finance institutions. Through this project, the grantee provides support to nongovernmental organizations in developing countries and Central and Eastern Europe. Over the last grant period, they provided additional assistance to nongovernmental networks in Asia and Central and Eastern Europe to share the lessons they have learned with groups in the Middle East and North Africa. During the next grant period, the grantee will take a leadership role in both coordinating Dutch and broader European civil society input into the World Bank safeguard policy review.

title: International Financial Institutions Program
description: With this renewal grant, Both Ends Foundation will continue working to improve the environmental and social policies and practices of international financial institutions. Through this project, the grantee provides support to nongovernmental organization networks in Africa, Asia, and Central and Eastern Europe. Over the last grant period, it provided additional assistance to nongovernmental networks to engage in the World Bank Group safeguard review process and the Green Climate Fund. During the next grant period, the grantee will continue its leadership role in both coordinating Dutch and broader European civil society input into the World Bank safeguard policy review, and it will help to develop new nongovernmental organization networks to address impacts of Brazilian and Chinese development finance projects.

title: International Financial Institutions Program
description: This renewal grant will allow Both Ends Foundation to continue its work to improve the environmental and social policies and practices of international financial institutions. Through this project, the grantee provides support to nongovernmental organization networks in Africa, Asia, and Central and Eastern Europe. Over the last grant period, it provided assistance to nongovernmental networks to engage in the World Bank Group safeguard review process and the Green Climate Fund. During this grant period, the grantee will continue its work to ensure that international financial institutions contribute to sustainable development in their countries of operation, with a particular focus on the World Bank Group, Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank, and Asian Development Bank.

title: International Financial Institutions Program
description: This renewal will allow Both Ends Foundation to continue its work to improve the environmental and social policies and practices of key international financial institutions. In addition, it will allow them to develop a new strategy for their work on international development finance. Planned activities include monitoring the World Bank Group’s implementation of the new environmental and social framework, the Asian Infrastructure and Investment Bank’s accountability mechanism and information disclosure policy, and the launch of the Asian Development Bank’s safeguard policy review.

title: International Financial Flows and the Environment
description: The International Financial Flows and the Environment project of the World Resources Institute provides important research and data to non-governmental organizations and key public and private institutions on international financial flows and public policy options. The overarching goal of the project is to shift patterns of development finance so that they support environmental sustainability.This grant will enable the institute to conduct research and analysis of World Bank and export credit agency policies; participate in debates and dialogues with key international financial institution officials; organize informational workshops; and provide technical expertise and guidance to private financial institutions in the development of their sustainability policies.Recent activities included analyzing the International Finance Corporation’s influence over private-sector banks in developing countries; evaluating the performance standards of the private banks that have adopted the Equator Principles; introducing specific recommendations on how export credit agencies can help developing countries transition away from fossil fuels; and creating a methodology for assessing the responsiveness of electricity sector decisionmakers to public interest concerns.

title: International Financial Flows and the Environment
description: The International Financial Flows and the Environment project of the World Resources Institute provides important research and data to nongovernmental organizations and key public and private institutions on international financial flows and public policy options. This grant increase will allow the World Resources Institute to take advantage of a unique opportunity to develop innovative financing mechanisms to compensate countries that are willing to forego exploitation of oil and gas reserves in fragile and unique ecosystems. The increase will support research, publications, technical services, and travel costs associated with a workshop that will explore potential financing options.

title: International Financial Flows and the Environment
description: The International Financial Flows and the Environment project of the World Resources Institute provides important research and data to nongovernmental organizations and key public and private institutions on international financial flows and public policy options. The overarching goal of the project is to improve the social and environmental performance of public and private international financial institutions by holding them accountable to their investors and to the communities in which they invest. With this renewal grant, the World Resources Institute will conduct research and analysis of the World Bank Group, the Inter-American Development Bank, and export credit agency policies; participate in debates and dialogues with key international financial institution officials; organize informational workshops; and provide technical expertise and guidance to private financial institutions in the development of their climate change and clean energy policies.

title: International Financial Flows and the Environment
description: The International Financial Flows and the Environment project of the World Resources Institute provides important research and data to nongovernmental organizations and key public and private institutions on international financial flows and public policy options. The overarching goal of the project is to improve the social and environmental performance of public and private international financial institutions by holding them accountable to their investors and to the communities in which they invest. During the grant period, the project will continue its research and analysis work, concentrated on decisionmakers who set the policies and design the investment portfolios that shape global markets and affect the lives of millions. The project will also sustain the programmatic focus on climate change as well as the aspirations and rights of communities affected by development projects. In addition, there will be a focus on new investments in energy infrastructure by public and private international financial institutions and policy reforms at these institutions.

title: International Financial Flows and the Environment
description: The International Financial Flows and the Environment project of the World Resources Institute works to improve the social and environmental performance of public and private international financial institutions by holding them accountable to their investors and to the communities in which they invest. Through this grant increase, the project will map the climate financing and governance proposals that have been made at the United Nations climate negotiations in order to better assess where agreements already exist or may be possible. In addition, it will convene several strategy meetings to help provide a common nongovernmental organization platform to influence the final outcomes of the climate change negotiations and develop next steps after the Copenhagen negotiating meeting.

title: International Financial Flows and the Environment
description: The International Financial Flows and the Environment project of the World Resources Institute works to improve the social and environmental performance of public and private international financial institutions by holding them accountable to their investors and to the communities in which they invest. Through this grant increase, the project will continue its work to address the financing of the response to climate change and related governance issues that have been raised by the United Nations negotiations on climate change. It will support partner organizations in developing countries to convene regional strategy meetings on climate finance leading up to the next United Nations climate meeting to be held in Mexico in late November.

title: International Financial Flows and the Environment
description: The International Financial Flows and the Environment project of the World Resources Institute provides important research and data to nongovernmental organizations and key public and private institutions on international financial flows and public policy options. The overarching goal of the project is to improve the social and environmental performance of public and private international financial institutions by holding them accountable to their investors and to the communities in which they invest. During the last grant period, the grantee took a leadership role in mainstreaming climate change into the operations of international financial institutions, improving the quality of their support for sustainable energy investments in developing countries, and ensuring that future climate finance mechanisms are strengthened by lessons from previous experience. During the current period, the project will continue its work to encourage shifts in international financial support for investments that meet high environmental and social standards and that are low-carbon and climate resilient, as well as identify and pursue opportunities to strengthen the environmental and social standards of emerging actors in development finance.

title: International Financial Flows and the Environment
description: The International Financial Flows and the Environment project of the World Resources Institute provides important research and data to nongovernmental organizations and key public and private institutions on international financial flows and public policy options. The overarching goal of the project is to improve the social and environmental performance of public and private international financial institutions by holding them accountable to their investors and to the communities in which they invest. This grant increase will support expansion of the grantee’s work related to emerging financial actors in development finance, the World Bank safeguard policy review, and new opportunities in international climate finance.

title: International Financial Flows and the Environment
description: The International Financial Flows and the Environment project of the World Resources Institute provides important research and data to nongovernmental organizations and key public and private institutions on international financial flows and public policy options. The overarching goal of the project is to improve the social and environmental performance of public and private international financial institutions by holding them accountable to their investors and to the communities in which they invest. During the last grant period, the grantee took a leadership role in the development of the Green Climate Fund and World Bank Energy Strategy Review. In addition, they began working with key Chinese institutions to address the impacts of Chinese lending to developing countries. With this grant, the project will focus on three areas: 1) impacts of outward investment by emerging economies (Brazil and China); 2) World Bank safeguard policy review; and 3) monitoring World Bank lending to meet low-carbon and climate resilient goals.

title: Sustainable Finance Center
description: The Sustainable Finance Center of the World Resources Institute provides research and data to nongovernmental organizations and key international financial institutions on the impacts of their investments and options to address these impacts. The overarching goal of the project is to improve the social and environmental performance of public international financial institutions by holding them accountable to their investors and to the communities in which they invest. This renewal grant will continue to focus on three areas — World Bank safeguard policy review; monitoring the Global Climate Fund; and the development of environmental and social standards for Brazilian and Chinese investments.

title: Sustainable Finance Center
description: The World Resources Institute is a global environmental think tank that works with governments, companies, and civil society to build solutions to urgent environmental challenges. The overarching goal of this project is to improve the social and environmental performance of public international financial institutions. This renewal grant will focus on engaging with international financial institutions to ensure that they help developing countries address climate change, monitoring of the Green Climate Fund, and developing environmental and social standards for Chinese-financed infrastructure projects.

title: Sustainable Finance Center
description: The World Resources Institute is a global environmental think tank that works with governments, the private sector, and civil society to identify solutions to urgent environmental challenges. The overarching goal of this project is to improve the social and environmental performance of public international financial institutions. This renewal grant will focus on engaging with multilateral development banks and Chinese development finance institutions to ensure that these institutions support developing countries’ transitions to a low-carbon future and align with their national climate plans.

title: Indigenous Peoples and the Environment
initiative: Reform of International Finance and Trade
description: This renewal grant will support the Indian Law Resource Center’s continuing efforts to reform World Bank and Inter-American Development Bank policies and projects that affect indigenous peoples and their environment. Most of the world’s remaining large tracts of tropical forest are inhabited by indigenous peoples who lack the legal right to manage and protect their traditional lands. These forests are increasingly threatened by unsustainable development programs supported by the multilateral development banks and other international financial institutions. Indian Law Resource Center’s program combines Washington-based policy work at the international financial institutions with capacity building for indigenous people so that they can more effectively use international rules and safeguard policies to protect their natural resources.

title: Clean Water Network
description: Since 1992, the Clean Water Network has helped local- and state-level organizations protect and restore freshwater ecosystems across the United States. By providing technical and other assistance, the network helps its members learn from one another, participate in water quality policy discussions, monitor implementation of water quality programs, and communicate more effectively with the public. Renewal support from Mott will enable the network to continue offering these services. The network is a project of the Natural Resources Defense Council, a national environmental group working on a range of issues.

title: General Purposes
description: The Clean Water Network is a network of more than 1,100 local, state, and national organizations working to protect the nation’s waterways by strengthening and implementing the Clean Water Act and related policies. By providing technical and other assistance, the network helps its members learn from one another, participate in water quality policy discussions, monitor implementation of water quality programs, and communicate more effectively with the public. Renewal support from Mott will enable the network to continue offering these services.

title: General Purposes
description: The Clean Water Network connects more than 1,200 local, state, and national organizations working to protect the nation’s waterways by strengthening and implementing the Clean Water Act and related policies. With Mott support, the network has provided technical assistance, facilitated member networking and learning opportunities, and informed water quality policy discussions. Renewal support from Mott will enable the network to continue these services while diversifying its membership base and developing strategic communications materials.

title: General Purposes
description: The Clean Water Network connects more than 1,200 local, state, and national organizations working to protect the nation’s waterways by strengthening and implementing the Clean Water Act and related policies. With prior Mott support, the network provided environmental groups with technical assistance, networking and learning opportunities, and information on water quality research and policy developments. This grant increase will support the network’s capacity building endeavors, which will include a 2011 board retreat.

title: Legal Support Services for Non-Profit Organizations
description: The Legal Resources Trust provides legal support to civil society-based organizations on issues ranging from legal education and litigation to the administration of justice. Mott’s support is specifically directed at a project that provides legal and institutional assistance on how to establish, register, and administer nonprofit organizations. Through Mott’s grant, the trust has been able to provide training in nonprofit law by producing written resource materials on nonprofit legal matters. The grant also has supported advocacy to improve the legal and fiscal environment for nonprofits. This grant will continue to provide support for this project and assist the trust to ensure that its services also reach community-based organizations involved in local development and poverty eradication in poor and marginalized areas. The grant will further support the continued provision of legal education and training in nonprofit law to civil society-based organizations.

title: Legal Support Services for Non-Profit Organizations
description: The Legal Resources Trust provides legal support to civil society organizations on issues ranging from legal education and litigation to the administration of justice. This grant supports the grantee in providing assistance on how to establish, register, and administer nonprofit organizations in South Africa. Through previous support, the grantee developed materials on nonprofit legal matters and provided training in nonprofit law to other civil society organizations and legal practitioners. It also translated some of these materials into isiXhosa, one of South Africa’s official languages, and supported the registration of nonprofits under appropriate legislation to allow them to benefit from tax laws. This grant will continue to provide support for this project. Additionally, it will assist the trust to investigate the establishment of an advice office network within the faith-based community, in particular the Methodist and Catholic churches, to respond to the growing need for legal services among poor people.

title: Legal Support Services for Non-Profit Organizations
description: The Legal Resources Trust provides legal support to civil society organizations on issues ranging from legal education and litigation to the administration of justice. This project provides support to nonprofits on how to establish, register, and administer nonprofit organizations. It also provides legal support services to community-based advice offices. Over the last two years, the grantee assisted various nonprofit organizations to register appropriately, trained paralegals in advice offices and other legal professionals on nonprofit laws, and updated materials on governance and laws that affect nonprofits. Additionally, it explored collaboration with faith-based institutions on providing services to their members on matters related to the violation of human rights. This grant will support the grantee to continue these activities, as well as update and translate some of its materials into several South African indigenous languages.

title: Legal Support Services for Non-Profit Organizations
description: The Legal Resources Trust provides legal support to nonprofit organizations on issues ranging from legal education and litigation to the administration of justice. Past support from Mott assisted the grantee to provide legal and institutional assistance on how to establish, register, and administer nonprofit organizations; train nonprofits on topics related to nonprofit law; develop a module for life orientation training in high schools on understanding local government; and to produce and disseminate resource materials on nonprofit legal matters. The grant also supported advocacy to improve the legal and fiscal environment for nonprofits in South Africa. This grant will continue to provide support for this project and further assist the grantee to explore partnerships between community advice offices and faith-based institutions. It will also enable the grantee to support legal, therapeutic, advocacy, and education interventions in communities that have experienced severe human rights violations.

title: Legal Support Services for Non-Profit Organizations
description: The Legal Resources Trust provides legal support to nonprofit organizations on issues ranging from legal education and litigation to the administration of justice. Past support from Mott assisted the grantee to provide legal and institutional assistance on how to establish, register, and administer nonprofit organizations; train nonprofits on topics related to nonprofit law; support advocacy to improve the legal and fiscal environment for nonprofits in South Africa; and to explore partnerships between community advice offices and faith-based institutions. This grant will support the grantee to continue to assist nonprofits to register as legal entities; provide legal advice and related services to nonprofits; litigate on behalf of clients when necessary; assist communities to understand their rights and proactively engage in initiatives that improve their lives; and conduct research on international best practices to regulate the work of community advice offices and paralegals.

title: Legal Support Services for Non-Profit Organizations
description: The Legal Resources Trust provides legal support to nonprofit organizations on issues ranging from legal education and litigation to the administration of justice. Past support from Mott assisted the grantee to provide legal and institutional assistance on how to establish, register, and administer nonprofit organizations; assist more than 6,000 people with legal advice and referrals; and train communities on the structures and functions of local government. This grant will support the grantee to continue to assist nonprofits to register as legal entities, provide legal advice and related services to individuals and groups, assist communities to monitor implementation of state programs and demand accountability, and strengthen governance within community advice offices.

title: General Purposes
description: Isandla Institute is a public interest think tank whose primary focus is to foster just, equitable and democratic urban settlements. It conducts research and formulates policies and strategies in the areas of local government and urban development.This grant will enable the institute to conduct research and publish articles and books on urban renewal and urban development, with a particular focus on the city of Cape Town. In addition, it will conduct nationwide research into how national policy for local government has been implemented.During the past several years, the institute worked with both national and local governments on issues including developing the regulatory framework for local economic development; integrating poverty reduction into local planning processes; and assessing municipal integrated development plans.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide continued general purpose support to the Isandla Institute, a public interest think tank with a primary focus on fostering just, equitable, and democratic urban settlements in South Africa. The institute is one of the leading research organizations in the country on issues related to local government and urban development. Utilizing innovative research and working with multiple partners, the Isandla Institute nurtures, tests, and disseminates new policy ideas intended to reduce urban inequity, poverty, racism, and social exclusion. The institute’s work will focus on building innovative partnerships, facilitate public dialogue and shared learning experiences, and information dissemination through publications and its Web site.

title: General Purposes
description: The Isandla Institute was established in 1998 as a policy research organization that focuses on the development of effective partnerships between government and the nonprofit sector on poverty alleviation and urban planning. The grantee engages in cutting edge research, knowledge sharing, development of alternative frameworks and methodologies, and consultancies to support urban development and transformation. The thematic areas it focuses on include poverty reduction, local governance, HIV in the context of human settlements planning, and urban development. Over the past two years, the grantee hosted conferences and dialogues, published papers and a book, and collaborated on research activities on governance and urban planning. This grant will support the grantee to facilitate engagement with local government and urban management using research and knowledge sharing and to develop and promote innovative models for equitable service delivery, leadership, and participatory local governance, informed by local and international experiences.

title: Great Lakes Washington Program
geographic_focus: Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, New York, Illinois, Ohio, Minneapolis, Michigan, Indiana
description: The Great Lakes Washington Program of the Northeast-Midwest Institute has long been a critical voice for the Great Lakes region in Washington, D.C. The institute provides staff to the bipartisan House and Senate Great Lakes Task Forces; promotes coalitions to sustain bipartisan efforts to protect and enhance the Great Lakes region; identifies federal policy options that can enhance ecosystem initiatives in the Great Lakes basin; and conducts briefings and issue analyses that link in-region advocates with the Washington-based policy communities. With previous support, the institute participated in the development of the Great Lakes Regional Collaborative and encouraged bipartisan support for protections against aquatic invasive species. This grant will support continued work on these and other key policy issues as they become apparent.

title: Great Lakes Washington Program
geographic_focus: New York, Ohio, Wisconsin, Michigan, Illinois, Pennsylvania, Minnesota, Indiana
description: Through its Great Lakes Washington Program, the Northeast-Midwest Institute, a nonpartisan research organization, is a key voice for the Great Lakes region in Washington, D.C. With prior Mott support, the institute has provided staff to the bipartisan House and Senate Great Lakes Task Forces, promoted coalitions to sustain bipartisan efforts to protect and enhance the Great Lakes region, identified federal policy options that can enhance ecosystem initiatives in the Great Lakes basin, and conducted briefings and issue analyses that linked in-region advocates with the Washington-based policy communities. Renewal support will allow the institute to maintain such core activities, as well as work in a focused way on the problem of aquatic invasive species.

title: Great Lakes Washington Program
geographic_focus: Ohio, Minnesota, Wisconsin, Michigan, Illinois, Pennsylvania, New York, Indiana

With prior support from Mott, the grantee has provided staff to the bipartisan House and Senate Great Lakes Task Force, promoted bipartisan coalitions to protect and enhance the Great Lakes region, provided policy analyses, and conducted briefings on issues and policies that impact the health of the Great Lakes. With this grant renewal, the grantee will continue these efforts while also providing technical research, policy analyses, and communication materials regarding the prevention of aquatic invasive species in the Great Lakes.

title: Great Lakes Washington Program

description: The Great Lakes Washington Program of the Northeast-Midwest Institute provides an important voice for the Great Lakes region in Washington, D.C. The grantee is a nonprofit think-tank dedicated to improving the economic and environmental health of states in the Northeast and Midwest regions. With prior support from Mott, the grantee facilitated diverse coalitions to protect and enhance the Great Lakes region, provided policy analyses, and conducted briefings on issues that impact the health of the Great Lakes. With this grant renewal, the grantee will continue these efforts while researching solutions to prevent the introduction of new invasive species through ships’ ballast water.

title: Great Lakes Washington Program

With prior support from Mott, the grantee facilitated coalitions to protect and enhance the Great Lakes region, provided policy analyses, and conducted briefings on issues that impact the health of the Great Lakes.
