title: Great Lakes Washington Program
geographic_focus: Minnesota, Wisconsin, Illinois, Pennsylvania, Michigan, Ohio, New York, Indiana
description: Founded in 1977, Northeast-Midwest Institute is a nonpartisan, Washington, D.C.-based nonprofit organization dedicated to promoting economic and environmental vitality for the northeastern and Midwestern regions of the United States. With prior Mott support, the grantee provided opportunities for federal decisionmakers, regional stakeholders, and other interested parties to jointly identify and promote regional Great Lakes priorities related to water quality, water conservation, habitat protection and restoration, and invasive species. With renewed support, the grantee will continue this work by undertaking research and policy analyses and translating and disseminating relevant scientific data.

title: Great Lakes Washington Program
geographic_focus: Michigan, Ohio, New York, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Illinois, Minnesota, Indiana
description: Founded in 1977, Northeast-Midwest Institute is a nonpartisan, Washington, D.C.-based nonprofit organization dedicated to promoting economic and environmental vitality for the Northeastern and Midwestern regions of the United States. With prior support from Mott, the grantee provided opportunities for federal decision makers, regional stakeholders, and other interested parties to jointly identify and promote regional Great Lakes priorities related to water quality, water conservation, habitat protection and restoration, and invasive species. With this renewal grant, the grantee will continue this work by undertaking research and policy analyses and translating and disseminating relevant scientific data. A new component will provide new members of Congress coming to Washington in 2019 with orientation, background, and support on a host of critical Great Lakes issues.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant increase to the Alabama Rivers Alliance, a statewide group, will support the organization’s general purposes, including the provision of legal and related technical assistance to advance water quality policy reforms.

title: General Purposes
description: Founded in 1997, the Alabama Rivers Alliance works to protect and restore Alabama’s waterways, among the most biologically diverse in North America. With prior Mott support, the alliance has pursued work in five core areas: engaging in public policy issues relevant to healthy rivers; supporting a network of local watershed organizations; raising public awareness about watershed values; promoting water efficiency initiatives; and building its own organizational capacity. With renewal support, the alliance will continue this and similar work, including implementation of the Alabama Water Agenda, a state-level water policy reform proposal developed by the alliance and many partner groups.

title: General Purposes
description: Founded in 1997, the Alabama Rivers Alliance works to protect and restore Alabama’s waterways which are among the most biologically diverse in North America. This grant increase will allow the grantee to continue engaging in freshwater policy issues such as the Alabama Water Agenda, which prioritizes the most important threats to the state’s water resources. The grantee will also continue to build citizen capacity to support local watersheds, monitor hydropower relicensing efforts, and build its own organizational capacity.

title: Building Citizen Capacity for Freshwater Protection
geographic_focus: Wisconsin, Mississippi, Illinois, Minnesota, Alabama, South Carolina, Michigan, Kentucky, Louisiana, Ohio, Tennessee, Indiana, Georgia
description: River Network provides organizational, technical and networking assistance to the freshwater conservation community nationwide and is very active in the Great Lakes and southeastern U.S.This grant will enable the network to deliver its core programs in the Great Lakes and Southeast and undertake other projects that benefit groups in the two regions, such as providing scholarships to attend its annual meeting. In addition, funds will be used to address internal organizational development needs.Accomplishments during the past three years included helping statewide river groups form and become more stable; training statewide groups to deliver technical services to local groups; and assisting partners in the use of the Clean Water Act.

title: Building Citizen Capacity for Freshwater Protection
geographic_focus: Wisconsin, Minnesota, Illinois, Alabama, South Carolina, Michigan, Kentucky, Louisiana, Ohio, Tennessee, Indiana, Georgia, Mississippi
description: River Network, a national organization, provides organizational, technical, and networking assistance to freshwater conservation organizations active at the state, regional, and watershed level. With prior Mott support, River Network has provided such assistance to groups in the Great Lakes and southeastern United States through a variety of programs including its publications, a well-attended annual meeting, consulting services, and a small grants program. Renewal support will allow the grantee to continue to provide such capacity-building technical assistance to freshwater conservation groups in the Great Lakes and southeastern United States.

title: Building Citizen Capacity for Freshwater Protection
geographic_focus: Mississippi, Alabama, Georgia, Michigan, Kentucky, Louisiana, Ohio, South Carolina, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Illinois, Tennessee, Indiana
description: River Network, a national organization providing capacity building services to freshwater conservation groups, works in the Great Lakes and southeastern United States with Mott support. This grant increase will help cover the expenses associated with the recruiting and hiring of a new president/CEO of the organization.

title: Building Citizen Capacity for Freshwater Protection
geographic_focus: Louisiana, South Carolina, Kentucky, Ohio, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Mississippi, Alabama, Indiana, Illinois, Tennessee, Georgia, Michigan
description: River Network has spent the last 22 years bringing together more than 5,000 freshwater organizations to enhance the protection and restoration of the nation’s rivers and waterways. With prior support, River Network has offered technical expertise, training opportunities, and small grant assistance to build the capacity of river and watershed organizations active at the state, regional, and major river basin level in the Great Lakes and southeastern United States. This grant renewal will allow River Network to continue these capacity building services in both the Great Lakes and southeastern United States.

title: Building Citizen Capacity for Freshwater Protection
geographic_focus: South Carolina, Ohio, Michigan, Wisconsin, Mississippi, Indiana, Tennessee, Georgia, Louisiana, Kentucky, Illinois, Alabama, Minnesota
description: River Network is a national environmental organization that seeks to strengthen the organizational capacity of freshwater groups in the Great Lakes and Southeast. To better connect with the other intermediary organizations working to build the institutional strength of small- and mid-sized environmental groups, the grantee helped create the Environmental Capacity Builders Network. This grant increase will help the grantee convene the group’s 2011 annual gathering to be held in Flint, Michigan. The meeting will provide opportunities for members to network, improve technical knowledge and skills, share lessons learned, and identify opportunities for collaboration.

title: Building Citizen Capacity for Freshwater Protection
geographic_focus: Illinois, Ohio, New York, Michigan, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Pennsylvania, Indiana
description: Over the past 24 years, River Network has brought together more than 5,000 freshwater organizations to collectively protect and restore the nation’s rivers and waterways. With prior Mott support, the grantee provided a variety of technical assistance services, as well as small grants to build the capacity of freshwater groups working in the Great Lakes and southeastern regions of the United States. In 2011, the grantee also helped conduct a national meeting of intermediary organizations seeking to build the capacity of environmental groups. With this two-year renewal, the grantee will provide a combination of individualized consultation, group training, regrants, and other forms of technical assistance to increase the organizational capacity and effectiveness of watershed groups in the Great Lakes Basin.

title: Building Citizen Capacity for Freshwater Protection
geographic_focus: Ohio, Michigan, New York, Illinois, Minnesota, Wisconsin, Pennsylvania, Indiana
description: River Network is a national technical assistance provider that seeks to build a strong, connected network of citizens and groups working to protect and restore waterways in the United States. With prior Mott support, the grantee delivered a variety of technical assistance services and small grants to strengthen the capacity of freshwater groups working in the Great Lakes. With this renewal, the grantee will continue to provide a combination of individualized consultation, group training, regrants, and other forms of technical assistance to support watershed groups in the Great Lakes Basin. The grantee will also conduct regional research and analyses to understand the organizational needs of its members and partners.

title: Building Citizen Capacity for Freshwater Protection
geographic_focus: New York, Ohio, Michigan, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Pennsylvania, Indiana, Illinois
description: River Network is a national environmental organization that provides technical assistance to help its 2,000 members protect freshwater resources at the regional, state, and local levels. With prior Mott support, the grantee provided a broad range of capacity building and programmatic services to freshwater groups working in the Great Lakes. With continued Mott support over the next two years, the grantee will conduct an in-depth regional research project to identify areas of the Great Lakes Basin where increased on-the-ground capacity is needed. The resulting map, and its underlying data, will help the grantee tailor its services (individualized consultations, group training, networking events, and other forms of technical assistance) to support watershed groups in the Great Lakes Basin.

title: Building Citizen Capacity for Freshwater Protection
geographic_focus: Indiana, Pennsylvania, Michigan, Illinois, Ohio, New York, Minnesota, Wisconsin
description: River Network is a national environmental organization that provides technical assistance to help its 2,000 members protect freshwater resources at the state, regional, and local levels. With prior Mott support, the grantee conducted a regional scan to identify areas of the Great Lakes Basin where increased on-the-ground capacity is needed. The results of this study helped the grantee develop new strategies to provide watershed groups with technical assistance to address drinking water safety concerns. Over the next two years, the grantee will build out its new drinking water technical support program while continuing to provide Great Lakes watershed groups with the tools, education, and access to peer networks that help them serve as effective champions for healthy rivers and sustainable communities.

title: Great Lakes Drinking Water and Healthy Rivers
geographic_focus: Indiana, Minnesota, Pennsylvania, New York, Michigan, Ohio, Illinois, Wisconsin
description: River Network is a national organization that provides training to advance organization effectiveness, and to sharpen skills and capacity to address issues like access to clean, safe, and affordable drinking water. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, River Network has developed a Drinking Water Guide, and a Water and Equity Peer Learning Cohort that provides a solid foundation to address challenges—including aging infrastructure; funding shortages; legacy pollution; and a robust regulatory framework. Renewed support will enable the grantee to build on these resources to support new organizations as they confront new challenges. They will provide training to build the capacity of Great Lakes groups around drinking water issues; provide consulting; training and mentoring around organizational effectiveness; and support robust participation at River Rally, a leading national conference.

title: Water Quality Protection
geographic_focus: Alabama, South Carolina, North Carolina, Georgia, Tennessee
description: The Southern Environmental Law Center provides regional leadership on water quality issues, as well as technical assistance to state and local groups in Alabama, Tennessee, Georgia, North Carolina and South Carolina.Funding will enable the center to work in each state to improve implementation of the Clean Water Act and related policies, with an emphasis on improving stormwater and wetland programs. During the past two years, the center and its partner groups, have strengthened stormwater standards in North Carolina; improved treatment of wetland resources in South Carolina and Georgia; and increased water quality protections for river segments that harbor threatened aquatic species in Alabama and Tennessee.

title: Water Quality Protection
geographic_focus: South Carolina, Alabama, North Carolina, Georgia, Tennessee
description: The Southern Environmental Law Center works to protect and restore water quality throughout much of the Southeast. In recent years, the center and partner organizations have had particular success improving state-level stormwater pollution controls in Georgia, Tennessee, and North Carolina. With continued Mott support, the center will work with its partners to improve implementation of the Clean Water Act and related programs, with a focus on measures that address stormwater pollution and wetlands conservation in Alabama, Georgia, Tennessee, and the Carolinas.

title: Water Quality Protection
geographic_focus: South Carolina, Tennessee, Georgia, North Carolina, Alabama
description: The southeastern United States is home to a diverse array of water resources that provide critical habitat for a wide range of aquatic life. Polluted stormwater runoff, coupled with significant wetlands loss, is threatening the region’s rivers, streams, lakes, and coasts, as well as the wildlife and people depending on them. The Southern Environmental Law Center brings extensive technical, policy, and scientific expertise to bear on critically important water quality issues. With a one-year renewal grant from Mott, the center will work to strengthen stormwater controls, enhance water quality protections, and conserve wetlands throughout the Southeast.

title: General Purposes
description: This general purposes grant provides renewal support to the International Association for Volunteer Effort. The association’s mission is to promote, support, and strengthen the development of volunteering worldwide. With more than 500 members in over 70 countries around the world, the association offers a range of services including biennial global conferences, Web-based learning and networking opportunities, and representation vis-à-vis global bodies, such as the United Nations. In 2006, in addition to its regular activities, the association organized its 19th World Volunteer Conference in New Delhi, India, that attracted 600 participants from 53 countries. In 2007-2010, the International Association for Volunteer Effort will focus on strengthening its position as a key leadership organization for volunteering worldwide, building its capacity in policy and practice development, expanding its membership and enhancing membership services, and maintaining good governance and efficient management of the organization.

title: National Network of Sector Partners
grantee: Insight Center for Community Economic Development
description: This grant renews partial support to the National Economic Development and Law Center for the National Network of Sector Partners, the national trade association for sectoral employment intermediaries and other interested parties. The National Network of Sector Partners serves as the vehicle to coordinate the national dialogue about sector initiatives, and to advance a national sector strategy that is responsive to the concerns and priorities of stakeholders. During this grant period, the trade association will undertake a strategic planning process, serve as an information clearinghouse for sector practitioners, and support a public policy agenda.

title: National Network of Sector Partners
grantee: Insight Center for Community Economic Development
description: This grant provides partial support to the Insight Center for Community Economic Development to direct the development of the National Network of Sector Partners. The network serves as the trade association for sectoral employment programs, as a vehicle to coordinate the national dialogue about sector initiatives, and to advance a national sector strategy that is responsive to the concerns and priorities of stakeholders. This year, the National Network of Sector Partners will serve as an information clearinghouse for sector practitioners, develop a marketing plan to promote increasing membership, and design and implement a public policy agenda.

title: National Network of Sector Partners
grantee: Insight Center for Community Economic Development
description: This grant provides partial support to the Insight Center for Community Economic Development to continue staffing a national trade association for sectoral employment practitioners entitled the National Network of Sector Partners. The network will continue to serve as the vehicle to coordinate the national dialogue about sector initiatives, and to advance a national sector strategy that is responsive to the concerns and priorities of its members. It will continue to develop a nonpartisan national collaborative, serve as an information clearinghouse for sector practitioners, implement a marketing plan to promote sector intervention strategies, and design and implement a sectoral employment public policy agenda.

title: National Network of Sector Partners
grantee: Insight Center for Community Economic Development
description: This grant provides support to the Insight Center for Community Economic Development for the National Network of Sector Partners, the national trade association for sector employment intermediaries and other interested parties, to continue improving employment opportunities for low-income families and communities. The Mott Foundation made the initial grant to support the conceptualization and formation of the network in 1999, and it has served as a successful model for workforce development.

title: National Network of Sector Partners
grantee: Insight Center for Community Economic Development
description: This final renewal grant to the Insight Center for Community Economic Development’s trade association will assist the grantee in continuing to improve employment opportunities for low-income families and communities. The Mott Foundation made the initial grant to support the conceptualization and formation of the National Network of Sector Partners in 1999, and it has served as a successful model for workforce development.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will enable the center to focus on increasing meaningful participation of young people in decisionmaking at the school and community levels; provide a space for young people from Bosnia’s main ethnic communities to work together on concrete initiatives to improve their society; broaden the impact of its successful programs; and cooperate with similar groups in the former Yugoslavia.The Youth Communication Center – Banja Luka, founded in 1997, promotes tolerance and understanding among youth throughout Bosnia and Herzegovina; advocates for systemic change in the country’s educational system; provides training and mentoring to youth initiatives; and participates in a wide variety of in-country and regional peace-building initiatives.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to Youth Communication Center – Banja Luka, a leading nongovernmental organization in Bosnia-Herzegovina that promotes tolerance and understanding among youth; advocates for systemic change in the country’s educational system; provides training and mentoring to youth initiatives throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina; and participates in a wide variety of in-country and regional peace-building initiatives. Continued Mott support will enable the center to strengthen its organizational capacity, diversify its funding base, and broaden the impact of its successful programs. During the past two years, the center has supported the development of 109 student councils, helped to establish voluntary services in six municipalities, and provided space and support to informal community education programs.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to a leading nongovernmental organization in Bosnia-Herzegovina that promotes tolerance and understanding among youth; advocates for greater participation of youth in decisionmaking processes in schools and communities; and develops volunteerism among youth. Continued Mott support will enable the Youth Communication Center – Banja Luka to strengthen its organizational capacities as a leader in developing volunteerism, expand its work in secondary school councils throughout the country, and diversify its funding base. During the past two years, the center strengthened a network of secondary school student councils in the Republika Srpska, one of two federal entities in the country, and supported the development of local volunteer centers in ten municipalities. The grantee is based in Banja Luka, the capital of the Republika Srpska.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to a leading nongovernmental organization in Bosnia-Herzegovina that promotes tolerance and understanding among youth, advocates for greater participation of youth in decisionmaking processes in schools and communities, and develops volunteerism among youth. Continued Mott support will enable the Youth Communication Center – Banja Luka to strengthen its organizational capacities as a leader in developing volunteerism, expanding its work in secondary school councils throughout the country, and diversifying its funding base. During the past two years, the grantee strengthened entity-level networks of secondary school student councils, which together represent nearly 400 secondary schools comprising more than 180,000 students. The grantee also conducted the first nationwide research on volunteerism and widely disseminated the results and conclusions. Other ongoing activities included operating Radio Balkan, a youth-run radio station; hosting a range of nonformal, community-based education programs; and providing psychosocial assistance to vulnerable groups through direct counseling and volunteer programs. The grantee is based in Banja Luka, the capital of the Republika Srpska.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to a leading nongovernmental organization in Bosnia-Herzegovina that promotes tolerance and understanding among youth, advocates for greater participation of youth in decisionmaking processes in schools and communities, and develops volunteerism among youth. Continued Mott support will enable the Youth Communication Center – Banja Luka to strengthen its organizational capacities as a leader in developing volunteerism, expand its work in secondary school councils throughout the country, and diversify its funding base. During the past two years, the grantee strengthened entity-level networks of secondary school student councils, which together represent 290 secondary schools — 95 percent of all secondary schools in the country — comprising more than 135,000 students. The grantee also helped national and local government agencies in Bosnia-Herzegovina develop and promote volunteerism. Other ongoing activities included operating Radio Balkan, a youth-run radio station; hosting a range of nonformal, community-based education programs; and providing psychosocial assistance to vulnerable groups through direct counseling and volunteer programs. The grantee is based in Banja Luka, the capital of the Republika Srpska.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to a leading nongovernmental organization in Bosnia-Herzegovina that promotes tolerance and understanding among youth, advocates for greater participation of youth in decisionmaking processes in schools and communities, and develops volunteerism among youth. Continued Mott support will enable the Youth Communication Center – Banja Luka to support the development and sustainability of networks of secondary school councils throughout the country; encourage youth engagement through improvements in school curricula and local governments’ youth policies; strengthen youth volunteer centers and their networks across the country; integrate career counseling and entrepreneurship training in schools; and develop regional youth-led reconciliation initiatives. Since 2014, the grantee strengthened entity-level networks of secondary school student councils and helped national and local government agencies in Bosnia-Herzegovina develop and promote volunteerism, including establishing a new network and support center for volunteerism in Republika Srpska. Other ongoing activities included operating a youth-run radio station; hosting a range of nonformal, community-based education programs; and providing psychosocial assistance to vulnerable groups through direct counseling and volunteer programs. The grantee is based in Banja Luka, Bosnia-Herzegovina.

title: General Purposes
description: Women’sNet is a women-led nonprofit that provides training, capacity building, and skills development in the information communications technology field for women in the nonprofit sector. Over the years, Mott has provided support to facilitate the promotion of gender equality through developing the capacity of women to use information communications technology for advocacy, networking, and participation in electronic policy debates. This grant will continue to provide support to Women’sNet to use information communications technology to empower women and, in particular, strengthen their leadership in the sector by ensuring that their voices are heard. Women’sNet will specifically focus on making information communications technology accessible to disadvantaged and marginalized women, providing training and support to women-led, community-based organizations to use the Internet more strategically. A strong emphasis also will be placed on linking projects, people, tools, and resources within women’s organizations through technology to enhance opportunities for collaboration and networking.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will continue to support Women’sNet, a women-led organization which provides training, capacity building, and skills development in information technology for women. Past support helped promote gender equality by developing women’s capacity to use information technology for advocacy and networking, empowering and strengthening women’s leadership at all levels, providing information technology training to girls, and also focusing on technology training for women in small businesses and community development, particularly those in poor, rural areas.

title: General Purposes
description: The Black Sash Trust is dedicated to the promotion and defense of human rights. During the past decade, the trust has provided free paralegal services to poor and marginalized communities in various provinces across South Africa.This grant will enable the trust to continue providing services to communities to ensure that they are able to access and exercise their rights. It also will continue to monitor government policies on social assistance and advocate for policy reform.During the past two years, the trust has assisted approximately 15,000 clients per year through its seven advice offices and about 5,000 through outreach work in other areas; strengthened the capacity of paralegal caseworkers through training, workshops and mentoring programs; educated the public about their rights through electronic and print media and workshops for community organizations; and participated in the activities of the Basic Income Grant coalition, an initiative aimed at promoting the development of a comprehensive social security system.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purpose support to the Black Sash Trust, a highly respected organization dedicated to the promotion and defense of human rights in South Africa. The Black Sash Trust operates a national office and seven regional offices throughout South Africa that focus on civil, political, and socioeconomic rights and provides a range of services from legal advice to consumer education and resolving labor matters. Specific activities include providing quality advice on social security and consumer protection, research and legislative monitoring, advocacy efforts aimed at improving social protections, public education workshops and information sessions, and developing rights education material for distribution and use by the print media and local radio. The trust will also continue its work in strengthening the paralegal sector to expand access to social justice by the most vulnerable South Africans.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will continue to provide support to the Black Sash Trust, a highly respected organization dedicated to the promotion and defense of human rights in South Africa. The grantee operates a national office and seven regional offices throughout South Africa that focus on civil, political, and socioeconomic rights. Previous support assisted in providing a range of services from legal advice to consumer education and labor dispute resolution. Activities in the next two years will include strengthening the paralegal sector in order to expand access to social justice for poor and vulnerable communities across South Africa.

title: General Purposes
description: The Black Sash Trust was founded in 1955 by a group of women who were fighting for the recognition of human rights for all in South Africa. It operates seven advice offices throughout South Africa that provide free legal advice and conduct rights awareness programs primarily for poor people. Previous grants supported the grantee to promote socioeconomic rights through rights education, advocacy campaigns, and monitoring government service delivery. Over the past two years, the grantee expanded its reach and offered training and support to leaders of communities on rights and how to assist their communities to access rights. Over the next two years, the grantee will continue to promote effective, comprehensive, and redistributive social protection systems in South Africa.

title: General Purposes
description: The Black Sash Trust was founded in 1955 by a group of women who were fighting for the recognition of human rights for all in South Africa. Its aim is to contribute to the creation of a society that has effective laws and comprehensive social protection for the most vulnerable. It conducts rights awareness programs for community-based organizations and poor and marginalized people. Previous grants supported the grantee to promote the realization of socioeconomic rights through rights education, advocacy campaigns, and monitoring government service delivery. Over the next two years, the grantee will train community-based organizations and members of the public about human rights and how to access them, provide the tools and information to community-based organizations on how to monitor the delivery of government services, and engage relevant government institutions on how to improve on their delivery of basic services. This grant has been made possible by a partnership with Atlantic Philanthropies in support of the community advice office sector.

title: General Purposes
description: The Black Sash Trust was founded in 1955 by a group of women who were fighting for the recognition of human rights for all in South Africa. Its aim is to contribute to the creation of a society that has effective laws and comprehensive social protection for the most vulnerable. It conducts rights awareness programs for community-based organizations and poor and marginalized people. Over the next year and a half, the grantee will train community-based organizations and members of the public about human rights and how to access them, provide the tools and information to community-based organizations on how to monitor the delivery of government services, and engage relevant government institutions on how to improve on their delivery of basic services. This grant increase will contribute to the Dullah Omar Spring School, which will offer training to an estimated 400 community-based paralegals on various subjects related to basic rights and the law. This grant increase has been made possible by a partnership with Atlantic Philanthropies in support of the community advice office sector.

title: General Purposes
description: The Black Sash Trust was founded in 1955 by a group of women who were fighting for the recognition of human rights for all in South Africa. Its aim is to contribute to the creation of a society that has effective laws and comprehensive social protection for the most vulnerable. It conducts rights awareness programs for community-based organizations and poor and marginalized people. Past support enabled the grantee to train community-based organizations and members of the public about human rights and how to access them, provide the tools and information to community-based organizations on how to monitor the delivery of government services, and launch the Dullah Omar School to train community-based paralegals. This grant will enable the grantee to continue to protect, improve, and expand social security and social protection for vulnerable people; train community-based organizations on human rights and how to access them; and work on a campaign to stop illegal deductions from the accounts of social grant beneficiaries.

title: General Purposes
description: The Black Sash Trust was founded in 1955 by a group of women who were fighting for the recognition of human rights for all in South Africa. Its aim is to contribute to the creation of a society that has effective laws and comprehensive social protection for the most vulnerable. It conducts rights awareness programs for community-based organizations and poor and marginalized people. Past support enabled the grantee to protect, improve, and expand social security and social protection for vulnerable people; train community-based organizations on human rights and how to access them; and work on a campaign to stop illegal deductions from the accounts of social grant beneficiaries. This grant will enable the grantee to monitor service delivery implementation in various government entities and give feedback for improvement, train community-based organizations on socioeconomic rights and how to demand accountability from the government, and offer support on social justice matters through a national helpline.

title: Strengthening Civil Society in Bosnia-Herzegovina and Croatia
description: The project goal is to strengthen the development of a sustainable nonprofit sector in Bosnia-Herzegovina and Croatia that is engaged in decisionmaking and policy development on behalf of its constituents and beneficiaries. To this end, CARE USA, working through CARE International, will support select grassroots, community-based civic organizations working with Roma and a national network of Roma organizations. CARE USA will provide training, technical assistance, networking opportunities, and small grants to the selected organizations and the national network. During 2005-2006, CARE USA supported four Roma organizations and three youth-led networks with grants, training, and technical assistance. CARE USA implements its programming in Bosnia-Herzegovina and Croatia through its office in Banja Luka, Bosnia-Herzegovina.

title: Strengthening Civil Society in the Western Balkans
description: The project goal is to reestablish social and community life in Bosnia-Herzegovina and to strengthen the nonprofit sector as a vehicle for public participation. To this end, CARE USA will strengthen three Roma nonprofits and increase Roma youth participation in civil society. CARE USA will conduct research on the situation of Roma youth in Bosnia-Herzegovina and use this research to plan relevant training, technical assistance, and small grants to partner organizations. During 2006-2007, the project focused on building the capacity of selected Roma nonprofit organizations and a network of over 25 other Roma organizations to participate effectively in national- and local-level policy development and advocacy on behalf of Roma communities, particularly on programs and policies aimed at poverty reduction. This project is implemented by CARE USA through the offices of CARE International in Banja Luka, Bosnia-Herzegovina.

title: Strengthening Civil Society in the Western Balkans
description: The project goal is to strengthen youth development and active participation in addressing violence and peace-building challenges in Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia, and Serbia. To this end, CARE USA will provide financial and technical assistance to eight nongovernmental organizations across the region. Selected organizations will receive support to develop and implement programs that promote peace building, address issues of masculinity and violence, and engage young people directly in community and civic initiatives. A particular focus will be given to working with community-based organizations in eastern Bosnia. During the most recent grant period, the project increased the participation of Roma youth in public life by providing financial support, training, and mentoring to three Roma-led organizations in Bosnia. This project is implemented by CARE USA through the offices of CARE International in Banja Luka, Bosnia-Herzegovina. CARE USA’s purpose is to help the developing world’s poor in their efforts to achieve social and economic well-being.

title: Strengthening Civil Society in the Western Balkans
description: The project goal is to strengthen youth development and active participation in addressing violence and peacebuilding challenges in Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia, and Serbia. To this end, CARE USA will provide financial and technical assistance to seven nongovernmental organizations across the region. Selected organizations will receive support to develop and implement programs that promote peacebuilding, address issues of masculinity and violence, and engage young people directly in community and civic initiatives. A particular focus will be given to working with community-based organizations in eastern Bosnia-Herzegovina. During the last grant period, the grantee supported three youth-led nongovernmental organizations in the Srebrenica region of eastern Bosnia-Herzegovina working to strengthen peacebuilding and eight youth nongovernmental organizations working together at the regional level to reduce violence among young men. The groups received financial support, training, and networking opportunities. This project is implemented by CARE USA through the offices of CARE International in Banja Luka, Bosnia-Herzegovina. The grantee’s purpose is to help the developing world’s poor in their efforts to achieve social and economic well-being.

title: Transatlantic Community Foundations Network
description: This renewal grant supports the Transatlantic Community Foundations Network, a learning community launched in 1999 that facilitates, nurtures, and encourages community foundation development across North America and Europe. The network brings together 54 community foundations and support organization practitioners from 14 countries for meetings that focus on shared learning, mutual skills building, and the development of information products for the network and the broader community foundation field. In its most recent three-year phase, the network has conducted 16 peer learning events and prepared the book “Local Mission-Global Vision,” which was published by the Foundation Center in the fall of 2008. For its first ten years, the network has been managed by Bertelsmann Stiftung in Germany. Community Foundations of Canada, a national membership association and participant in the network since its inception, will become the network’s new host beginning in 2009.

title: Transatlantic Community Foundations Network
description: The Transatlantic Community Foundations Network is a learning community launched in 1999 that facilitates, nurtures, and encourages community foundation development across North America and Europe. Over the past 12 years, the network has brought together more than 50 community foundation field practitioners from 14 countries for meetings focused on shared learning, mutual skills building, and information resource development. Community Foundations of Canada, a national membership association, has been the network’s host since 2009. The network will conclude its programs in 2011, although its platform, relationships, and knowledge base are expected to transfer to the Global Fund for Community Foundations. A grant increase and six-month extension are needed to support program management and transfer of the network’s resources, as well as scholarships for network members and other international field leaders to participate in the May 2011 Community Foundations of Canada biennial conference and a final, one day post-conference network learning event.

title: Transatlantic Community Foundations Network
description: The Transatlantic Community Foundation Network is a learning community launched in 1999 that facilitates, nurtures, and encourages community foundation development across North America and Europe. Community Foundations of Canada, a national membership association, has managed the network since 2009. The network will conclude its programs in 2011 while its platform, relationships, and knowledge base will be transferred to the Global Fund for Community Foundations. This grant increase will support the transfer of all information and knowledge resources that have been developed since 1999 to the Global Fund for Community Foundations’ Web site to ensure their continued availability to the community foundation field worldwide.

title: Sustainable Energy and Alternative Global Economic Policies
initiative: Reform of International Finance and Trade
description: The Institute for Policy Studies works in collaboration with non-governmental organizations, academics, parliamentarians and other stakeholders to promote financing for sustainable energy and to develop alternative proposals for the future of the global economy based on environmental sustainability, democracy and economic fairness. The development of these alternatives will provide for broad-based stakeholder input into discussions taking place at the World Bank, World Trade Organization and other trade negotiations, such as the Free Trade Area for the Americas.This grant to the institute will support ongoing research, networking, citizen education and media outreach on the environmental and community impacts of energy and extractive industry projects financed by international financial institutions and facilitated by global, regional and bilateral trade agreements.

title: Sustainable Energy and Alternative Global Economic Policies
initiative: Reform of International Finance and Trade
description: This grant to the Institute for Policy Studies will support research, networking, citizen education, and media outreach on the environmental and community impacts of energy and extractive industry projects financed by the international financial institutions and global, regional, and bilateral trade agreements. The Institute for Policy Studies works in collaboration with nongovernmental organizations, academics, parliamentarians, and other stakeholders to promote financing for sustainable energy and to develop alternative proposals for the future of the global economy based on environmental sustainability, democracy, and economic fairness.

title: Sustainable Energy and Alternative Global Economic Policies
initiative: Reform of International Finance and Trade
description: The Institute for Policy Studies works in collaboration with nongovernmental organizations, academics, parliamentarians, and other stakeholders to promote financing for sustainable energy and to develop alternative proposals for the future of the global economy based on environmental sustainability, democracy, and economic fairness. This grant increase will support publicity and outreach for a new book on alternative approaches to international development. It will also support travel and lodging costs for a strategy meeting discussing the new economic architecture that will be created as an outcome of a new United Nations climate change treaty.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to promote community organizing activities as a way of strengthening citizen participation in Slovakia. This grant will enable the Center for Community Organizing – Slovakia to strengthen its organizational capacity, expand its activities to new communities, develop new programs for densely populated urban neighborhoods and increase its work with the Roma population. In addition, the center will work to consolidate the efforts of similar nonprofit organizations; increase the effectiveness of community organizing activities in Slovakia; and share its experience with other countries in Central and Eastern Europe.Since its establishment in 1999, the center has successfully conducted campaigns around important issues facing residents in several Slovak cities; organized campaigns on the national level to promote accountability of elected representatives to citizens; and coordinated a network of similar organizations in Central and Eastern Europe.

title: Dialog Program
description: The project goal is to strengthen citizens’ participation and improve the dialogue and interaction between citizens and authorities at the community level in Romania. The Community Foundation Sibiu will strengthen and coordinate an informal network of four resource centers, which will provide information, training, and advice to community groups and individual citizens on different areas, including citizens’ rights and responsibilities, communication strategies, and coalition building. The network engages citizens in the development of their communities through a program known as “Dialog.” Since its beginning in 1993, the Dialog Program has facilitated communications and partnerships between citizens, nongovernmental organizations, local government, and businesses driven by common goals related to community development, environmental concerns, and other community problems and needs.

title: Louisiana Interfaith Together
description: Louisiana Interfaith Together is a statewide organizing project of the PICO National Networkthat consists of local organizations in the cities of New Orleans, Baton Rouge, Houma and Lafayette, as well as two parish-wide organizations in East Carroll and Pointe Coupee. This grant, coming at a time when Louisiana is still recovering from the devastating effects of hurricanes Katrina and Rita, will continue to support education activities as well as housing, jobs and environmental cleanup.

title: Louisiana Interfaith Together
description: Louisiana Interfaith Together is a statewide organizing project of PICO National Network consisting of local organizations in New Orleans, Baton Rouge, Houma-Thibodaux-Raceland, New Iberia, and Lafayette, as well as a parishwide organization in Pointe Coupee. Louisiana Interfaith Together works on a variety of issues of concern to residents with an emphasis on education and housing. Previous grants supported statewide education organizing and the response to Hurricanes Katrina and Rita. This grant will provide continued support for work to improve public education, promote affordable housing, and rebuild communities affected by the hurricanes of 2005 and additional storms since that time.

title: Louisiana Interfaith Together
description: Louisiana Interfaith Together is a statewide organizing project of PICO National Network. The project works on a variety of issues of concern to residents with an emphasis on education and housing. Previous grants supported statewide education organizing and the response to Hurricanes Katrina and Rita. This grant will provide continued support for work to improve public education and promote affordable housing.

title: Louisiana Interfaith Together
description: Louisiana Interfaith Together is a statewide organizing project of PICO National Network. The project works on a variety of issues of concern to residents with an emphasis on education and housing. Previous grants supported statewide education organizing and the response to Hurricanes Katrina and Rita. This grant will provide continued support for work to improve public education and transportation and promote affordable housing.

title: Capacity Building for the InterValley Network
geographic_focus: Vermont, Maine, New Hampshire, Connecticut, Rhode Island, Massachusetts
description: The InterValley Project is a network of related community organizations in Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Connecticut, Rhode Island, Maine and Vermont. The network’s goals are to strengthen member groups; nurture and launch new organizations; assist with coordinated actions on critical issues; and develop new strategies and models to increase the voice of communities as decisions are made affecting jobs, land and development. This grant will enable the network to increase it’s capacity for regional action; conduct at least two three-day regional leadership development institutes each year; conduct at least two regional training workshops; work with affiliates to refine and strengthen local leadership development activities; increase the regional research capacity; and develop more advanced web-based communications between member organizations.

title: Capacity Building for the InterValley Network
geographic_focus: Connecticut, Maine, New Hampshire, Rhode Island, Vermont, Massachusetts
description: InterValley Project is a network of community organizations in Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Connecticut, Rhode Island, Maine, and Vermont. This grant will support continued capacity building for the member organizations and the network itself, particularly in the areas of organizer and leader development, research, and fundraising development.

title: News and Information Programs
description: This grant provides renewal support for the news and information service of National Public Radio (NPR). For 35 years, NPR has sought to educate listeners by bringing informed discussions and insightful reporting on critical national and international issues to the air. Programs such as “Morning Edition”, “All Things Considered” and others have provided news coverage of depth and sensitivity that has become a measure of excellence, making NPR unique in American journalism. Its programming is carried by more than 800 stations in nearly every community across the United States and attracts 26 million listeners each week. The grantee’s programs are also heard around the world via satellite, cable, FM and AM radio, and are available to millions around the globe via npr.org.

title: Responsible Trade Program
initiative: Reform of International Finance and Trade
description: The Sierra Club Foundation’s mission is to explore, enjoy, and protect the wild places of the earth as well as promote the responsible use of natural ecosystems and resources. Central to the ability of communities to provide for themselves and protect their environment is creating a fair global trading system, which includes meaningful and enforceable environmental standards. This renewal grant for the Responsible Trade Program will support the continued efforts of the Sierra Club Foundation to raise awareness and engage the public, media, and policymakers on the environmental and social impacts of trade liberalization. For the next two years, the Responsible Trade Program will educate, organize, and mobilize its grassroots membership network to support environmentally responsible trade, engage the media and the public about the impact of current trade policies on the environment and about responsible policy alternatives, and build alliances with environmental and allied organizations.

title: Promoting Reforms in International Financial Institutions
description: With this grant, Environmental Defense will continue its leadership in the international effort to promote sustainable international finance and investment. Working together with civil society organizations in developed and developing countries, the grantee will focus on research, analysis, and advocacy to ensure implementation of, and compliance with, environmental and social policies in public international financial institutions and private banks. The grantee will also make small grants to provide strategic support to nongovernmental organizations in developing countries that are working to make international investments more sustainable.

title: General Purposes
description: Shelter of Flint, Inc., provides services for approximately 1,200 homeless clients per year. The vast majority of these clients are families who are homeless primarily due to economic circumstances. title: Reform of Japanese Export Credit Agencies
description: This renewal grant will allow Friends of the Earth – Japan to further its work on reform of Japanese export credit agencies and to continue its organizational capacity building work. Project activities for the next two years will include active participation in the review of the Japanese export credit agencies’ environmental guidelines; research and advocacy to add new requirements to the revised environmental and social guidelines; increased engagement with Japanese private banks that have adopted Equator Principles; continuing dialogue with the Asian Development Bank officials on strengthening the monitoring and accountability of their lending; engaging Friends of the Earth – Japan members more fully into organizational operations and activities; and enhancing collaborative activities with industry and government.

title: ECA Reform Campaign in Japan
description: This renewal grant will allow Friends of the Earth – Japan to continue its work on reform of Japanese export credit agencies and its organizational capacity building. With past Mott funding, the grantee successfully facilitated public input into the formal review and revision processes for environmental and social guidelines of key Japanese international financing agencies. Over the next two years, project objectives will include ensuring public participation and transparency in the review of the Japanese export credit agencies’ environmental and social guidelines; leading the Japanese public review of the International Finance Corporation safeguard policies; encouraging the development of strong energy investment guidelines; and strengthening the grantee’s long-term organizational sustainability and its public profile by increasing members and funding in Japan.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide partial support to Grantmakers for Children, Youth and Families. Initially established in 1985 as an affinity group of the Council on Foundations, Grantmakers for Children, Youth and Families seeks to engage member funders and grantmakers across all sectors in continually improving their grantmaking on behalf of children, youth, and families. The grantee provides a forum for grantmakers to collaborate and network as it relates to developing and refining grantmaking strategies, sharing information about effective programs, being knowledgeable of public policy developments, and dialoguing with national leaders in the field. This grant will support ongoing activities including the annual conference, networking events, and other collaborative learning opportunities.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Centre for Peace, Nonviolence and Human Rights Osijek
description: This grant supports the strengthening of a key institution in Croatia whose goals are to promote volunteerism and development of the nonprofit sector, support community-based peace building, and improve ethnic relations. During the grant period, the Centre for Peace, Nonviolence and Human Rights Osijek will focus on increasing war crimes trial monitoring in Croatia and the Balkans region; providing support services to witnesses and victims in connection with ongoing war crimes trials; and promoting mediation services as a technique for conflict resolution in schools and communities. Over the past two years, the center has coordinated regional war crimes trial monitoring activities and supported civil society development by working with other local organizations to develop a volunteer center, a regional foundation, and a regional forum of nongovernmental organizations. The center is based in Osijek, a city in eastern Croatia.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Centre for Peace, Nonviolence and Human Rights Osijek
description: This grant supports the strengthening of a key institution in Croatia whose goals are to promote volunteerism and development of the nonprofit sector, support community-based peace building, and improve ethnic relations. During the grant period, the Centre for Peace, Nonviolence and Human Rights Osijek will strengthen the quality of its core programs, including mediation, peace education, free legal aid, and war crime trial monitoring, through staff development and improved management structures. Over the past two years, the centre’s war crimes trials monitoring helped to shape the reform of the Croatian judiciary and increased national and international attention to the importance of war crimes trials in Croatia. The centre also shared its experience with school-based mediation services at regional and national levels, supported the development of volunteer centers in three cities, and purchased office space. The centre is based in Osijek, a city in eastern Croatia.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued support to Grantmakers for Education, formerly a project of the Tides Center. In 2001, Grantmakers for Education became an independent, nonprofit organization and is the largest national association that works to advance the field of education philanthropy. Its premier event continues to be an annual conference held during the fall of each year that attracts 200-300 grantmakers. The annual conference provides grantmakers with opportunities to hear from experts in the field, as well as network with peers. Grantmakers for Education provides other professional development opportunities to help funders connect with colleagues and learn from each other’s work, and disseminates information of interest to its members and the field through reports, a newsletter, and Web site. Funding will also support staffing and coordination of the Working Group on Education Organizing, a national network of more than 30 funders interested in community organizing for school improvement and reform.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued support to the Grantmakers for Education, a national association that works to advance the field of education philanthropy. Its premier event continues to be an annual conference held during the fall of each year that attracts 200-300 grantmakers. The annual conference provides grantmakers with opportunities to hear from experts in the field, as well as network with peers. The purpose of this grant increase is to provide additional support for the 2008 conference, which takes place in Baltimore, Maryland. title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued support to Grantmakers for Education, the only national association that works to advance the field of education philanthropy. With a mission to strengthen philanthropy’s capacity to improve educational outcomes and opportunities for all students, the organization helps foundation leaders and staff become more effective grantmakers by boosting their knowledge and networks. Specifically, the organization will: 1) sustain and improve overall programming and communications activities that help education grantmakers succeed in their work; and 2) provide staffing support and coordination to the Working Group on Education Organizing, a national network of more than 150 funders interested in community organizing for school improvement and reform.

title: State Fiscal and Low-Income Initiatives Project
grantee: Center on Budget and Policy Priorities
description: This grant provides ongoing support to the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities for the State Fiscal and Low-Income Initiatives Project. The overall goals of this project are to foster long-term fiscal responsibility, promote policies to reduce poverty, and ensure that the needs of less fortunate individuals are considered in policy debates. To accomplish these goals, the grantee will conduct timely research and analysis to inform policy debates and provide extensive educational and technical assistance to policymakers, nonprofit groups and the media at national and state levels. Located in Washington, D.C., the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities is one of the premiere policy research institutions in the United States.

title: State Fiscal and Low-Income Initiatives Project
grantee: Center on Budget and Policy Priorities
description: This grant will provide ongoing support to the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities for the State Fiscal and Low-Income Initiatives Project. The overall goal of this project is to conduct strategic analyses of federal and state budget priorities and fiscal policies, and programs that impact low-income populations. This grant will also support the center’s continued work to promote policy initiatives, such as the Earned Income Tax Credit, which helps low-income, working families. To accomplish these goals, the center will: monitor changes to the social safety net; prepare strategy papers and analyses of fiscal policies; facilitate networking at the state and local level for low-income advocates; and provide strategic and technical assistance to state and local policymakers, program administrators, and nonprofit organizations working on issues affecting low-income families. Located in Washington, DC, the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities is one of the premier policy research institutions in the United States.

title: State Fiscal and Low-Income Initiatives Project
grantee: Center on Budget and Policy Priorities
description: This increase will support a pilot expansion of the State Fiscal and Low-Income Initiatives Project. Additional Foundation support will enable the grantee to layer nuanced economic analysis on top of its core budget and tax policy capacity, deepening its role in the historic budget and fiscal debates that are before the nation at both the federal and state levels. Located in Washington, D.C., the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities is one of the premier policy research institutions in the United States.

grantee: Center on Budget and Policy Priorities
description: This grant provides ongoing support to the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities for the State Fiscal and Low-Income Initiatives Project. Through this project, the grantee works to expand economic opportunity and fight poverty by ensuring that federal and state governments have adequate resources to meet basic needs and invest in good schools, child care, quality health care, and other priorities. To accomplish these goals, the grantee will: 1) monitor policy and budgetary changes to the social safety net; 2) prepare strategy papers and analyses of fiscal policies; 3) facilitate networking at the state and local levels for low-income advocates; and 4) provide strategic and technical assistance to state and local policymakers, program administrators, and nonprofit organizations working on issues affecting low-income families. Located in Washington, D.C., the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities is one of the premier policy research institutions in the United States.

title: Partnership to Build Capacity in Small Nonprofits
description: The Executive Service Corps of Chicago provides in-depth technical assistance focusing on marketing, governance and leadership development. Organizations eligible for support through this project must have substantial minority leadership, meet a critical social or human service need, have an annual operating budget under $2 million, be located in a disadvantaged neighborhood in the Chicago metropolitan area, and serve a primarily low-income racial or ethnic minority population.This grant will provide continued support to the Service Corps’ Partnership to Build Capacity in Small Nonprofits program. The goal of the program is to help make the organization’s consulting services accessible and affordable to five participating nonprofits in the Chicago area that are addressing needs of the poor in disadvantaged neighborhoods.

title: Nonprofit Technology Conference
description: This grant will enable the Nonprofit Technology Enterprise Network to host the 2007 and 2008 Nonprofit Technology Conferences, designed to help nonprofits use technology more effectively. In partnership with NPower and United Way, the 2007 conference will take place in Washington, D.C., and will offer sessions on relevant topics for nonprofit technology and program staff as well as opportunities for networking and community service. Plans for the 2008 conference, which will take place in New Orleans, will be finalized after the 2007 event.In 2006, more than 800 nonprofit leaders and staff from around the world participated in the network’s three-day conference.The Nonprofit Technology Enterprise Network helps nonprofits make more effective use of technology to advance their missions.

title: International Financial Institutions Program
description: Friends of the Earth International is a worldwide federation of 71 national environmental organizations, working collectively to address global environmental issues. This grant will provide continuing support for the Friends of the Earth International’s work on international financial institutions. The focus of its work is on expanding civil society’s role in the decisionmaking processes of the international financial institutions; ensuring that there are effective safeguard policies and open, transparent decisionmaking processes at these institutions; shifting these institutions’ lending portfolios away from financing fossil fuel to renewable energy and other alternatives; and promoting alternative development approaches that contribute to sustainable development. The specific policy focus in this grant period will be on energy for sustainable societies, sustainable regional integration and infrastructure, and international coordination and communication.

title: Towards a Just Regime for Climate Change Finance
description: Friends of the Earth International is a worldwide federation of 69 national environmental organizations, working collectively to address global environmental issues. This grant will provide continuing support for the grantee’s work on international financial institutions. The focus of its work is the creation of a fair and equitable mechanism to provide financing for developing countries to address climate change — both mitigating impacts that can be avoided and adapting to impacts that cannot be avoided. Through this grant, the grantee will ensure strong developing country coordination and participation by engaging the leaders of its member organizations in the development of policy change strategies; provide useful research and data; carry out training on climate finance issues; develop a targeted media program to complement international advocacy and research work; and provide support to its national groups through small grants.

title: Supporting Climate Finance for Just and Sustainable Development
description: Friends of the Earth International is a worldwide federation of 76 environmental organizations, working collectively to address global environmental issues. Over the last grant period, the grantee was one of the key nongovernmental organizations that worked to ensure that an independent fund was established by the United Nations negotiations on climate change. In addition, in coordination with its member organization in Brazil, the grantee raised key issues related to the Inter-American Development Bank’s climate policies and the Brazilian National Development Bank’s infrastructure investments. The focus of this renewal grant will be to ensure effective finance mechanisms are developed in support of real solutions to climate change.

title: Integrating Afterschool and School-Community Partnerships
description: This grant will enable the American Youth Policy Forum (AYPF) to focus on middle and high school youth by conducting a series of learning events to inform policymakers, researchers and practitioners of the importance and role of afterschool in creating an optimal system for older youth; developing a compendium that describes effective and innovative afterschool programs for older youth who live in low-income communities or who are underserved by the education system; and continuing its dissemination of Helping Youth Succeed Through Out-of-School Time Programs, a summary of research on the impact of afterschool programs.The goal of the AYPF is to provide policymakers and their senior aides with information and experiences useful in the development of an effective youth education program and a training and transition-to-employment system for the U.S. that includes afterschool, school reform, internships, national community service and other experience-based learning methodologies.

title: Integrating Afterschool and School-Community Partnerships
description: This grant will continue to increase awareness among key stakeholders about innovative policies, practices, and programs that support high quality, expanded learning opportunities and strategies that integrate afterschool with education reform, particularly for older youth. Specifically, American Youth Policy Forum will conduct four forums and at least two webinars that will inform policymakers, researchers, and practitioners of the importance and role of expanded learning opportunities in creating an optimal education system for older youth. They will also continue dissemination of Learning Around the Clock: Benefits of Expanded Learning Opportunities for Older Youth, a research compendium of demonstrated expanded learning opportunities.

title: Integrating Afterschool and School-Community Partnerships
description: This grant increase will support the American Youth Policy Forum in organizing a timely Congressional study tour in the spring of 2011 to a unique expanded learning time pilot program in New York City. To date, Congressional staff have become most familiar with one particular expanded learning time model currently being implemented in Massachusetts which is serving as a basis to shape federal afterschool and expanded learning policy. This study tour and related project work will educate Congressional leaders and staff on a different model of expanded learning which builds upon the best practices of the 21st Century Community Learning Center program, and which emphasizes school and community partnerships.

title: Integrating Afterschool and School-Community Partnerships
description: This grant will provide support to the American Youth Policy Forum to organize a series of forums, Webinars, and discussion groups to educate key stakeholders on the important role afterschool and expanded learning opportunities play in preparing youth for college, careers, and civic engagement. The educational opportunities will inform key stakeholders on: 1) the essential characteristics and elements of successful afterschool programs, including school-community partnerships for middle and high school-aged youth; 2) the positive impact of afterschool participation on the development of youth academic and nonacademic competencies; and 3) policies that support, sustain, and expand afterschool programs.

title: Integrating Afterschool and School-Community Partnerships
description: This grant will provide support to the American Youth Policy Forum to organize a series of forums, Webinars, and discussion groups to educate key stakeholders on the important role afterschool and expanded learning opportunities play in preparing youth for college and careers. The educational opportunities will inform key stakeholders on: 1) the essential characteristics and elements of successful afterschool programs, including school-community partnerships; 2) how afterschool and expanded learning can help advance efforts to provide competency-based learning to students; and 3) how various education and youth funding streams can be leveraged to support afterschool and out-of-school time learning.

title: Promising Practices in Afterschool Programs
description: This grant will continue to support the Academy for Educational Development in its efforts to maintain the Promising Practices in Afterschool Listserv. This electronic resource is designed to provide dynamic, current, and useful information to the afterschool community in a range of content areas including: news, promising practices, funding opportunities, and professional development. In addition, the grantee will host web chats with invited experts and post the information on the www.afterschool.org Web site, which hosts the listserv and is supported by the Academy for Educational Development.

title: Promising Practices in Afterschool Programs
description: This grant will continue to support the Academy for Educational Development in its efforts to moderate and maintain the Promising Practices in Afterschool listserv. This electronic resource is designed to provide dynamic, current, and useful information to the afterschool community in a range of content areas including: news, promising practices, funding opportunities, and professional development. In addition, the grantee will use web technology to increase listserv subscribers and will use virtual learning opportunities including webinars, video clips, and live web chats conducted by content experts to share information. The grantee will also post resources on the www.afterschool.org Web site, which hosts the listserv and is supported by the Academy for Educational Development.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant supports the publication of “Alliance”, a quarterly magazine that focuses on civil society issues worldwide. Each issue includes feature articles on key topics concerning the nonprofit sector and philanthropy, interviews with sector leaders, profiles of leading civil society organizations, and regular columns such as book reviews and regional news items. Additionally, Alliance Publishing Trust produces eight issues of the “Alliance eBulletin” each year, as well as monthly articles, interviews, and reports on its Web site. Through these publishing activities, the grantee aims to facilitate the exchange of information and ideas among philanthropists, social investors, and others working for social change worldwide. Over the past nine years, 35 issues of “Alliance” magazine and 32 issues of “Alliance eBulletin” have been distributed to a readership of approximately 6,000 individuals and organizations throughout the world.

title: General Purposes
description: The Center for Community Change is a premier comprehensive technical assistance provider to grassroots community groups in low-income areas, providing hands-on technical assistance in community development, community organizing, organizational development, and public policy support to communities throughout the United States. This grant supports the center’s general operations so it can continue assisting grassroots, community-based groups in their work on pressing issues.

This general purpose grant supports the grantee so it can continue its work in assisting grassroots community-based groups.

description: The Center for Community Change is a premier comprehensive technical assistance provider to grassroots community groups in low-income areas, providing hands-on training in community development, community organizing, organizational development, and public policy support to communities throughout the United States. This general purpose grant supports the grantee’s general operations so it can continue its efforts to assist grassroots community-based groups in their work on pressing issues.

This general purpose grant supports the grantee’s general operations, so it can continue its excellent work in assisting grassroots community-based groups in their work on pressing issues.
