This general purpose grant supports the grantee’s work in assisting grassroots community-based groups in their work on advancing employment and education strategies that can positively impact the lives of individuals and families struggling to escape and avoid the challenges of poverty.

title: General Purposes
description: The Center for Community Change is a comprehensive technical assistance provider to grassroots community groups in low-income areas. The grantee provides hands-on technical assistance in community development, community organizing, organizational development, and public policy support to organizations across the United States. This general purpose grant continues support for the grantee’s efforts to build the capacity of community-based groups working to advance employment and education strategies that can positively impact the lives of low-income families and communities.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Women's Hope, Education and Training (WHEAT) Trust
description: The Women’s Hope, Education and Training Trust is a women’s development fund that supports grassroots women involved in community development and poverty alleviation. It was started by South African women educators, development professionals, academics, researchers, and activists in 1998 and serves as an intermediary grantmaking organization providing small grants, training, capacity building, leadership development, and networking opportunities. Mott has provided support to the trust to enhance its capacity as a women’s fund and to strengthen its grantmaking ability. This grant will continue to provide institutional support for the work, programs, and activities of the trust, focusing in particular on developing and strengthening its abilities to mobilize local resources for its grantmaking program and building an endowment fund.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Women's Hope, Education and Training (WHEAT) Trust
description: This grant will provide general purpose support to the Women’s Hope, Education and Training (WHEAT) Trust. The trust was established by South African women to encourage a culture of giving and support local grassroots women’s leadership development through information sharing and skills training. Past successes include providing technical support and building the capacity of grassroots women and women’s organizations. The trust’s flagship event, 1,000 Women Luncheon, is attracting a growing amount of corporate support and media attention. This and other award ceremonies have proven to be good platforms to recognize, educate, and network grantees and donors. The grantee will continue to concentrate its work in Western Cape, Eastern Cape, and Kwazulu-Natal provinces.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Women's Hope, Education and Training (WHEAT) Trust
description: This grant provides continued general purpose support to the Women’s Hope, Education and Training (WHEAT) Trust. The grantee was established to support grassroots, women-led organizations and encourages a culture of giving among individuals in South Africa. Past support enabled the grantee to improve its institutional capacity and to deliver programs that responded to the evolving realities of the women it supports. The grantee has played an important role in providing networking and leadership development opportunities for women-led community organizations throughout South Africa. Fundraising efforts attracted support from various sectors and created opportunities for sharing and promoting local philanthropy. This grant will support the continuation of these activities.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Women's Hope, Education and Training (WHEAT) Trust
description: The Women’s Hope, Education and Training Trust (WHEAT) is an intermediary grantmaker that supports community-based organizations working in poor communities throughout South Africa. Over the past two years, the grantee hosted events to bring men and women from different backgrounds together in the fight against abuse and create networking opportunities for its grantees. It held grantee convenings across the country to hear, firsthand, the challenges faced by their communities. This input has informed its future support to organizations working in these communities. The grantee also provided grantmaking services to institutions and individuals that wish to support women-led organizations. The grantee will continue to make grants to organizations that promote social justice, particularly those that focus on minority rights, economic empowerment, promoting health and wellness, and educating communities on gender equality.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Women's Hope, Education and Training (WHEAT) Trust
description: The Women’s Hope, Education and Training (WHEAT) Trust is an intermediary grantmaker that supports community-based organizations in South Africa. It provides training and makes small grants to organizations that work to empower the most marginalized groups in poor communities. Past support has enabled the grantee to provide training to community-based organizations in order to strengthen their ability to respond to the daily struggles of the communities they serve. The grantee has also produced publications that highlight the plight of women in poor communities, strengthened its partnerships with local businesses, hosted events to raise awareness on issues of inequality, and convened partners to create learning opportunities and receive feedback. This grant will support the grantee to continue making grants and implementing programs that promote gender equality, economic empowerment, health, and the protection of the environment. In addition, it will advance efforts to protect the rights of refugees and migrants.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Women's Hope, Education and Training (WHEAT) Trust
description: The Women’s Hope, Education and Training (WHEAT) Trust was established in 1998 to support women-led community-based organizations in South Africa. It makes grants and provides training to help organizations respond effectively to the needs in their communities. Previous support enabled the grantee to make grants, host fundraising events, conduct workshops for its grantees, and run awareness campaigns on pressing issues affecting the poor and marginalized in communities across South Africa. This grant will support the grantee to continue implementing similar activities.

title: Fair Share
description: Multiyear funding will support the newly established Budget Advocacy and Monitoring Resources program, a three-year intervention that builds on the results and lessons of previous programs. Fair Share will work with community organizations in the KwaZulu-Natal and Limpopo provinces, providing training and capacity building on budget advocacy and monitoring. In addition, Fair Share will conduct research and produce and disseminate publications on municipal budgeting.Among Fair Share’s recent achievements are creating awareness among community organizations of the need to actively monitor municipal expenditure as a way to influence decisionmaking at the local level; strengthening the capacity of communities, through economic literacy, to participate in municipal budgeting processes; and building partnerships with provincial departments of local government.Fair Share is a unit of the School of Government within the University of the Western Cape and was established in 1997 to promote partnerships between local government and the nonprofit sector, as well as economic literacy.

title: Fair Share
description: This grant will provide continued support to Fair Share, based at the University of the Western Cape. Fair Share’s focus is to increase the quality and extent of community participation in municipal planning and budgeting processes. Its newest initiative, the Budget Advocacy and Monitoring Resources program, will work with community organizations in Limpopo, KwaZulu-Natal, and Western Cape provinces, providing training and capacity building on budget advocacy and monitoring to both community organizations and municipal leaders. The grant will also support Fair Share to continue to conduct research, produce and disseminate publications on municipal budgeting, and share lessons learned.

title: Fair Share
description: Fair Share is a unit of the School of Government at the University of the Western Cape that focuses on building the capacity of ordinary citizens to understand and influence local budgeting processes. It also works with municipalities across South Africa sensitizing them to the needs of local communities and enhancing their ability to involve citizens in planning processes. Past support assisted Fair Share to implement three training programs that strengthened the leadership of community, service, and labor organizations. The training programs also enhanced the participation of these leaders in economic policy formulation, implementation, and evaluation. This grant will support Fair Share to continue to offer training and support to community leaders, other interested institutions, and individuals. During this period, it will focus on adapting some of the training programs and will incorporate suggestions and feedback on previous programs.

title: Women and Local Government
description: The Gender Advocacy Programme promotes a gender-just society in South Africa that helps marginalized communities, particularly women, to gain social, economic and political equality. This grant will enable the Gender Advocacy Programme to continue to build the capacity of municipal officials, politicians, civil society organizations and members of target communities to understand and prioritize issues affecting women in local planning processes.Recently, the Women and Local Government project has worked to raise the awareness of women in the Western Cape about the role and function of local government and how to hold elected representatives accountable. The programme also conducted research and policy advocacy at the national level on how to strengthen women’s participation in local government.

title: Transatlantic Community Foundation Fellowships
grantee: German Marshall Fund of the United States
description: This grant will provide continued support for a transatlantic community foundation fellowship program, a partnership between the German Marshall Fund of the United States and the King Baudouin Foundation in Belgium. The program enables participants to collaborate and exchange ideas with community foundation colleagues from across the Atlantic. In 2006, the German Marshall Fund will organize an alumni reunion conference.To date, 60 fellows have participated in the program, and more than 20 community foundations have been involved as host organizations.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant supports the Forum of Regional Associations of Grantmakers, a network of 32 city, state and multi-state grantmaker associations representing more than 4,000 grantmaking organizations and others involved in philanthropy. The forum’s mission is to strengthen regional philanthropy through its member regional associations. The forum serves its member organizations by providing resources, tools, events and partnership opportunities to build their capacity . Services include two annual conferences, monthly teleconference calls, affinity group collaborations, discounted member benefits for software products, grantmaker training curricula, annual characteristic surveys of regional associations, and knowledge management systems. The forum also has provided research and technical assistance on issues such as improving grantmaker effectiveness and accountability and state-level public policy/government relations. In the context of the forum’s New Ventures in Philanthropy initiative, the forum creates and shares knowledge to promote innovative giving in communities of color and rural communities, as well as to expand giving circles and engage professional advisors.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to the Forum of Regional Associations of Grantmakers, a network of 32 city, state, and multistate grantmaker associations representing more than 4,000 foundations, corporate giving programs, and other philanthropic organizations. The forum’s mission is to connect and support regional associations and to bring their knowledge and experience into the national conversation on philanthropy. Services to members include grantmaker education products, an annual conference, co-organization of Foundations on the Hill, conference calls and listserves, vendor discounts, annual characteristic surveys of regional associations, and a robust knowledge management system. Per its recently adopted strategic plan, the forum will establish an alliance with the Council on Foundations. In addition to its usual capacity-building services, programming will include the development of a grantmaker education initiative and the expansion of the forum’s knowledge management system.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to the Forum of Regional Associations of Grantmakers, a network of 32 city, state, and multistate grantmaker associations representing more than 4,000 foundations, corporate giving programs, and other philanthropic organizations. The grantee’s mission is to connect and support regional associations and to bring their knowledge and experience into the national conversation on philanthropy. Services to members include grantmaker education products, an annual conference, co-organization of Foundations on the Hill, conference calls and listserves, vendor discounts, annual characteristic surveys of regional associations, and a robust knowledge management system. This increase supports the grantee to engage in the LearnPhilanthropy Initiative, a collaboration of critical leaders in philanthropy aimed at developing a stronger and more effective, fieldwide system for grantmaker education.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to the Forum of Regional Associations of Grantmakers, a national network of 35 formally organized regional associations of grantmakers that collectively represent more than 4,500 foundations, corporate giving programs, and other philanthropic organizations. The forum supports philanthropy by strengthening the ability of all regional associations to fulfill their missions. It provides professional and management support services to its members and helps leverage their collective resources to support philanthropy across the country. Services to members include grantmaker education products, an annual conference, co-organization of Foundations on the Hill and District Days, conference calls and listserves, vendor discounts, annual characteristic surveys of regional associations, bi-weekly e-newsletters, a Web-based public policy platform, and a robust knowledge management system.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant supports the general purposes of the Forum of Regional Associations of Grantmakers, a national network of 34 geographically organized regional associations of grantmakers that collectively represent more than 4,300 foundations, corporate giving programs, and other philanthropic organizations. With a collective budget of $34 million and 245 staff members, the grantee is the largest organized network in American philanthropy. The grantee empowers its regional association members to be the highest quality providers of services to philanthropy in their regions and uses its collective and unique assets to inform and strengthen philanthropy throughout the country. Some of the grantee’s recent activities include co-organizing the annual Foundations on the Hill event; providing educational opportunities for members (annual conference, monthly calls, topical Webinars); hosting PolicyWorks for Philanthropy, revamping its knowledge management system; and engaging in collaborative partnerships with other infrastructure organizations. During 2013-2014, the grantee will continue to enhance these activities.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant supports the general purposes of the Forum of Regional Associations of Grantmakers, a national network of 34 geographically organized regional associations of grantmakers that collectively represent more than 5,500 participating organizations. The grantee facilitates effective philanthropy by delivering educational programming and resources, convening foundations, communicating the value of philanthropy, and sustaining and supporting regional grantmaker associations. Some of the grantee’s recent activities include co-organizing the yearly Foundations on the Hill; providing information and educational opportunities for members (annual conference, Webinars, monthly policy round-robin calls, biweekly newsletters, redesigned Web site, grantmaker education programming directory); hosting the PolicyWorks for Philanthropy project; and engaging in collaborative partnerships with other infrastructure organizations, including a data partnership with the Foundation Center. During 2015, the grantee will continue to enhance these activities.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to the Forum of Regional Associations of Grantmakers, a national network of 33 geographically organized regional associations of grantmakers that collectively represent more than 5,500 participating organizations. The grantee facilitates effective philanthropy by delivering educational programming and resources, convening foundations, communicating the value of philanthropy, and sustaining and supporting regional grantmaker associations. Some of the grantee’s recent activities include co-organizing the annual Foundations on the Hill event; providing information and educational opportunities for members (annual conference, Webinars, monthly policy round robin calls, biweekly newsletters, Website, grantmaker education programming directory); hosting the PolicyWorks for Philanthropy project; and engaging in collaborative partnerships with other infrastructure organizations. Over the next two years, the grantee will implement its New Vision of broadening its network to include national issue-based, identity-based, and practice-based funder affinity groups, thus becoming a nexus of regional and national philanthropy.

title: General Purposes
description: United Philanthropy Forum is the largest network serving philanthropy in the U.S. Membership includes 68 philanthropy-serving organizations across the U.S. that represent more than 7,000 foundations and other philanthropic organizations. During 2016–2017, the grantee developed and implemented a new vision to expand and transform their network, engaged on federal tax reform legislation and its impact on the charitable sector, strengthened partnerships and collaboration with other infrastructure organizations, and improved their financial sustainability. Continuing in 2018–2019, the grantee will continue to lead a vibrant network; maximize the individual and collective capacity and impact of their members; provide learning, knowledge, and resources to their members; and strengthen their own capacity and sustainability.

title: General Purposes
description: The European Foundation Centre is an independent membership association of foundations and corporate funders dedicated to promoting organized philanthropy in Europe and internationally.This grant will enable the center to focus on consolidating its European Union Affairs work; increasing membership; reinforcing its information and communications program; strengthening its relationship with information resource centers and national associations of donors throughout Europe; and building the capacity to serve its members more effectively.Established in 1989 by seven of Europe’s leading foundations, the center currently serves a core membership of 171 members, 350 community philanthropy initiatives, as well as an additional 50,000 organizations linked through a network of 58 information and support centers worldwide.

title: General Purposes
description: The European Foundation Centre is an independent membership association of foundations and corporate funders dedicated to promoting organized philanthropy in Europe and internationally. Established in 1989 by seven of Europe’s leading foundations, the European Foundation Centre today serves a core membership of 193 members, and 350 community philanthropy initiatives, as well as an additional 50,000 organizations linked through a network of 58 information and support centers worldwide. In 2007, the European Foundation Centre will focus on consolidating its committee structure; expanding its work related to the European Union; enhancing relationships with European foundation networks and other partners; reorganizing staff responsibilities; and improving its information, communication, and technology tools.

title: General Purposes
description: The European Foundation Centre is an independent membership association of foundations and corporate funders dedicated to promoting organized philanthropy in Europe and internationally. In 2007, the European Foundation Centre focused on the implementation of its strategic plan, which required systemic changes across its programs and organizational structure. In 2008, the European Foundation Centre will focus on: (1) implementing work plans for its four new program committees; (2) supporting the development of a European Foundation statute; (3) reviewing and strengthening relationships with key stakeholders and interest groups; (4) expanding its capacity-building activities; and (5) moving forward with a reorganized secretariat. Established in 1989 by seven of Europe’s leading foundations, the European Foundation Centre today serves over 200 core members.

title: General Purposes
description: The European Foundation Centre is an independent membership association of foundations and corporate funders dedicated to promoting organized philanthropy in Europe and internationally. In 2009, the grantee will focus on: 1) positioning public benefit foundations at the European level, with a focus on work related to the European Foundation Statute and the treatment of foundations related to value added tax; 2) developing and mainstreaming capacity-building activities for its members; and 3) redesigning the format and structure of its events, especially the annual general assembly and conference. Established in 1989 by seven of Europe’s leading foundations, the European Foundation Centre today serves a core membership of over 200 members.

title: General Purposes
description: The European Foundation Centre is an independent membership association of foundations and corporate funders dedicated to promoting organized philanthropy in Europe and internationally. In 2010, the grantee will continue to focus on: 1) positioning public benefit foundations at the European level, with a focus on work related to the European Foundation Statute and the treatment of foundations related to Value-Added Tax; 2) developing capacity-building activities for its members; 3) documenting and communicating the work of its members; and 4) connecting foundations to each other and other actors. Established in 1989 by seven of Europe’s leading foundations, the European Foundation Centre today serves over 200 core members.

title: General Purposes
description: The European Foundation Centre is an independent membership association of foundations and corporate funders dedicated to promoting organized philanthropy in Europe and internationally. In 2010, the grantee carried out a range of activities including organizing the first Foundation Week in Brussels, professionalizing the European philanthropic sector through developing new capacity building initiatives, supporting the work of several funder interest groups and networks, representing European foundations at the European Union-level, and launching a new Web site. In 2011, the grantee will introduce and implement a new strategic plan for the period 2011-2016. The new plan will focus on: 1) raising the collective voice of the European philanthropic sector; 2) creating an enabling environment for independent funders; 3) encouraging the professionalization of foundation staff and boards; and 4) increasing the visibility of European foundations. Established in 1989 by seven of Europe’s leading foundations, the European Foundation Centre currently serves over 200 core members.

title: General Purposes
description: The European Foundation Centre is an independent membership association of foundations and corporate funders dedicated to promoting organized philanthropy in Europe and internationally. In 2011, the grantee carried out a wide range of activities including organizing a successful autumn assembly with the donors and foundations networks in Europe, working with six European foundations to purchase a building in the center of Brussels that will become the focal point of European philanthropy, and assuming responsibility for GrantCraft in partnership with the Foundation Center. In 2012, the grantee will continue to focus on: 1) raising the collective voice of the European philanthropic sector; 2) creating an enabling environment for independent funders; 3) encouraging the professionalization of foundation staff and boards; and 4) increasing the visibility of European foundations. Additionally, the grantee will revise the strategy and coordination of its current interest groups and reinforce its communications and advocacy efforts around the European Foundation Statute. Established in 1989 by seven of Europe’s leading foundations, the European Foundation Centre today serves over 200 members.

title: General Purposes
description: The European Foundation Centre is an independent membership association of foundations and corporate funders dedicated to promoting organized philanthropy in Europe and internationally. title: General Purposes
description: The European Foundation Centre is an independent membership association of foundations and corporate funders dedicated to promoting organized philanthropy in Europe and internationally. title: General Purposes

Established in 1989 by seven of Europe’s leading foundations, the European Foundation Centre today serves over 200 members.

title: General Purposes
description: The European Foundation Centre is an independent membership association of foundations and corporate funders dedicated to promoting organized philanthropy in Europe and internationally. In 2014, the grantee carried out a wide range of activities, including organizing an Annual General Assembly and Conference in Sarajevo, Bosnia, and a Euro Philantopics conference in Brussels, Belgium. In 2015, the European Foundation Centre continues to focus on: 1) strengthening engagement with policies that shape and influence how foundations work in Europe; 2) advancing learning, sharing, and exploration of new ideas and opportunities for philanthropy; 3) building data and analysis on philanthropy; and 4) enhancing the visibility and understanding of philanthropy and foundations. Established in 1989 by seven of Europe’s leading foundations, the European Foundation Centre today serves over 200 members.

title: General Purposes
description: The European Foundation Centre is an independent membership association of foundations and corporate funders dedicated to promoting organized philanthropy in Europe and internationally. In 2015, the grantee carried out a wide range of activities, including organizing an annual general assembly and conference in Milan, Italy, in May and a “Euro Philantopics” conference in Brussels, Belgium, in November. In 2016, the grantee will launch a new strategic framework focusing on: 1) providing intellectual leadership on emerging policy agendas and societal trends and issues; 2) strengthening its role in promoting and supporting joint learning and cross-border collaboration on complex and urgent societal agendas; 3) deepening its work on advancing the well-being of the sector and on building data and knowledge on philanthropic practice; and 4) stepping up its role as a voice for the philanthropic sector in Europe. Established in 1989 by seven of Europe’s leading foundations, the European Foundation Centre today serves a core membership of over 200 members.

description: The European Foundation Centre is an independent membership association of foundations and corporate funders dedicated to promoting organized philanthropy in Europe and internationally. Established in 1989 by seven of Europe’s leading foundations, the European Foundation Centre serves a core membership of over 200 members.

title: General Purposes
description: Wetlands provide many benefits, yet only half of Wisconsin’s original wetlands remain, and they are threatened by a variety of unsustainable uses. Wisconsin Wetlands Association, the only statewide conservation organization solely focused on wetlands, leads diverse networks to protect and restore wetlands, while undertaking educational and training activities to engage citizens in wetlands conservation. This general purpose grant will enable the organization to maintain its leadership on wetlands issues, by providing technical assistance to a range of partners, promoting wetland protection and restoration, and expanding outreach programs. The association will also take steps to build its own internal capacity.

title: General Purposes
description: Wetlands provide a variety of benefits to freshwater ecosystems, and the Wisconsin Wetlands Association is the only statewide conservation organization solely focused on protecting and restoring these important resources in Wisconsin. With previous Mott support, the association led statewide efforts to protect and restore wetlands. This grant increase will allow the organization to continue this work by providing technical assistance to a range of partners, promoting wetland protection and restoration, and conducting education and outreach programs. The association will also take steps to build its own internal capacity.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will enable Independent Sector to pursue goals that include strengthening its capacity to provide leadership on key issues facing the nonprofit sector and building a strong membership coalition of leaders in the sector. Activities will focus on ethics and accountability, public policy and advocacy, membership sustainability, civic engagement, international issues and emerging issues. Independent Sector will continue its traditional efforts, including research, publications and the convening of an annual conference and meetings.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued general purposes support to Independent Sector, a national membership organization of more than 560 foundations, corporations, and voluntary organizations dedicated to encouraging philanthropy, volunteerism, and citizen action. Independent Sector’s work in 2007 will revolve around two main themes: (1) leading the nonprofit sector to promote vibrant communities and a healthy democracy; and (2) enhancing the effectiveness and accountability of the sector. These program themes reflect the effort to identify and refine ongoing initiatives to strengthen civic engagement and the social compact, improve grassroots advocacy capability, and bolster the nonprofit sector’s voice vis-à-vis government and the public, and continue to build upon the grantee’s work in the areas of ethics, accountability, and effectiveness.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued general purposes support to Independent Sector, a national membership organization of 600 foundations, corporations, and voluntary organizations dedicated to encouraging philanthropy, volunteerism, and citizen action. Over the past several years, Independent Sector has been playing a vigorous leadership role, building a more robust public policy and advocacy program, and a stronger membership coalition. It has provided the sector with a “national voice” before policymakers, the media, and the public-at-large at a time when challenges facing the nonprofit community are significant. Independent Sector’s work in 2008 will revolve around two main themes: enhancing the effectiveness and accountability of the nonprofit community, and leading the nonprofit community to promote vibrant communities and a healthy democracy.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued general purpose support to Independent Sector, a national membership organization of more than 600 foundations, corporations, and voluntary organizations dedicated to encouraging philanthropy, volunteering, and citizen action. For close to 30 years, the grantee has played a central role in providing the nonprofit community with a collective “national voice” to policymakers, the media, and the public-at-large. As a result of its robust record of accomplishments and strong membership, the grantee has achieved leadership standing and is instrumental in shaping an environment conducive to the missions of nonprofit organizations. During the grant period, Independent Sector’s work will revolve around three main goals: 1) strengthening the nonprofit community’s impact on public policy; 2) building a more effective, transparent, and accountable nonprofit community; and 3) promoting collaboration around overarching interests and issues.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued general purpose support to Independent Sector, a leadership forum of more than 550 charities, foundations, and corporate giving programs dedicated to advancing the common good by leading, strengthening, and mobilizing the nonprofit and philanthropic community. Major activities over the past two years include advocacy on policies affecting the nonprofit sector, efforts to promote accountability and effectiveness among charities and foundations, and programming aimed at developing next generation nonprofit leaders. The grantee’s 2011-2013 strategic plan will focus on strengthening the nonprofit and philanthropic community’s voice, leadership, and impact. Major areas of activity will include advancing public policies that support the nonprofit sector; building the advocacy capacity of nonprofits; developing a world-class talent pool of diverse nonprofit and philanthropic professionals; and helping nonprofits and foundations to increase their impact by committing to assessing effectiveness, having access to capacity building resources, and adhering to good governance and ethical practice guidelines.

title: General Purposes
description: The Independent Sector is a leadership network of more than 550 charities, foundations, and corporate giving programs dedicated to advancing the common good by leading, strengthening, and mobilizing the nonprofit and philanthropic community. This general purpose increase will be used to support the eighth annual Public Policy Action Institute, a two-day course held in conjunction with Independent Sector’s annual conference. The institute will gather approximately 150 nonprofit executives and policy advocates to gain insights on current policy issues facing the nonprofit sector and to share expertise and build strategies for effective advocacy efforts.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued general purpose support to Independent Sector, a leadership forum of more than 580 charities, foundations, and corporate giving programs dedicated to advancing the common good by leading, strengthening, and mobilizing the nonprofit and philanthropic community. Major activities over the past two years have included advocacy on policies affecting the nonprofit sector, efforts to promote accountability and effectiveness among charities and foundations, and programming aimed at developing next generation nonprofit leaders. Over the next two years, the grantee will focus on strengthening the nonprofit and philanthropic community’s voice, leadership, and impact. Major areas of activity will include advancing public policies that support the nonprofit sector, increasing nonprofit engagement in advocacy, maintaining a strong system of tax incentives for charitable giving, developing the next generation of nonprofit leaders, promoting nonprofit ethics and accountability, and expanding and deepening a diverse membership.

title: General Purposes
description: Independent Sector is a leadership forum of more than 450 charities, foundations, and corporate giving programs dedicated to advancing the common good by leading, strengthening, and mobilizing the nonprofit and philanthropic community. Currently, Independent Sector is focusing on strengthening the nonprofit and philanthropic community’s voice, leadership, and impact. Major areas of activity include advancing public policies that support the nonprofit sector, increasing nonprofit engagement in advocacy, maintaining a strong system of tax incentives for charitable giving, developing the next generation of nonprofit leaders, promoting nonprofit ethics and accountability, and expanding and deepening a diverse membership. This grant increase will enable the grantee to respond to rules governing the activities of social welfare organizations that were recently proposed by the Internal Revenue Service. The grantee plans to launch a yearlong public education campaign at the beginning of 2014.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued general purpose support to Independent Sector, a national network of more than 500 nonprofit organizations, foundations, and corporations committed to advancing the common good. The grantee offers convening opportunities, promotes sound government policies vis-à-vis nonprofits, supports strategies to foster citizen engagement, encourages high standards within the nonprofit sector, and serves as the voice of the sector. Over the next two years, the grantee will continue offering its flagship services of policy advocacy, research, publications, Webinars, and convenings. It also will conduct a series of regional field meetings around the country over the next year, which will deeply explore major trends affecting the sector and develop ideas for sector responses. One of these will be in Detroit. The grantee will also continue holding its Public Policy Action Institute, a popular learning and coalition building opportunity offered immediately prior to annual conferences.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to Independent Sector, a leadership network for nonprofits, foundations, and corporations committed to advancing the common good. Founded in 1980, the grantee fulfills its mission by: 1) convening opportunities for sector leaders to work together on key issues; 2) promoting policies that enable the nonprofit and philanthropic community to engage with public officials on a nonpartisan basis; 3) supporting the development and dissemination of strategies to strengthen volunteering, voting, giving, and other forms of citizen engagement; 4) encouraging the sector to meet the highest standards of ethical practice and effectiveness; and 5) serving as the voice of the independent sector to the media, government, business, and international voluntary communities. Over the next two years, the grantee will help the sector make its voice heard among policy makers and serve as an advocate for and disseminator of innovative solutions to ongoing and emerging needs.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to increase citizens’ involvement in resolving key environment and sustainable development issues in Romania. To this end, the Romanian Environmental Partnership Foundation will support nongovernmental organizations and community groups to effectively protect the environment, preserve and develop their natural heritage, and promote sustainable community development in Romania. In addition, the foundation will strengthen the capacity of local and national nonprofit organizations to carry out environmental advocacy and watchdog activities. Also, the foundation will focus on improving its institutional and financial sustainability. In 2006-2008, the foundation provided grants to over 150 nonprofits and diversified its funding base by raising over 25 percent of its income from local sources. The foundation was established in 1998 with the mission to strengthen the environmental movement and promote sustainable community development in Romania.

title: Impacts and Alternatives to the New Trade Regime on Environmental and Sustainability Options in Latin America
grantee: Uruguayan Study Center of Appropriate Technologies
description: This renewal grant will support continued work of the Uruguayan Study Center of Appropriate Technologies to research and analyze the impacts of trade and integration policies on the environment in South America and develop environmentally sustainable alternatives. This project will produce policy analysis from original research; disseminate research findings via a Web site, publications, and a variety of media outlets; conduct workshops with environmental organizations, citizens’ groups, academics, and local and national government officials; and develop tools for integrating environmental considerations in regional economic integration processes.

title: Impacts and Alternatives to the New Trade Regime on Environmental and Sustainability Options in Latin America
grantee: Uruguayan Study Center of Appropriate Technologies
description: This renewal grant will support continued work of the Uruguayan Study Center of Appropriate Technologies to research and analyze the impacts of trade and integration policies on the environment in South America. It will also support analysis of the impacts of the financial crisis on investments in energy and infrastructure projects in the region. This project will produce policy analyses from original research; disseminate research findings via Web sites, publications, and a variety of media outlets; conduct workshops with environmental organizations, citizens’ groups, academics, and local and national government officials; and develop tools for integrating environmental considerations in regional economic integration processes.

title: Impacts and Alternatives to the New Trade Regime on Environmental and Sustainability Options in Latin America
grantee: Uruguayan Study Center of Appropriate Technologies
description: The Uruguayan Study Center of Appropriate Technologies is a regional research organization that analyzes the impacts of trade and integration policies on the environment in South America and disseminates its findings via Web sites, publications, and a variety of media outlets. This grant increase will support an exploration of the implications of Brazil’s role in South America from a sustainable development perspective, including its investments in energy and infrastructure across the region.

This project will produce policy analyses from original research; disseminate research findings via a Website, publications, and a variety of media outlets; conduct workshops with environmental organizations, citizens’ groups, academics, and local and national government officials; and develop tools for integrating environmental considerations in the regional economic integration processes.

grantee: Uruguayan Study Center of Appropriate Technologies
description: The Uruguayan Study Center of Appropriate Technologies is a nongovernmental academic organization that carries out research and promotes sustainable development models in South America. This renewal grant will support the organization to research and analyze the social and environmental impacts of energy and infrastructure investment in South America and develop environmentally sustainable alternatives.

title: General Purposes
description: The Uthungulu Community Foundation was the first community foundation to be established in South Africa. It was officially launched in July 1999 as part of a pilot project to establish community foundations in the country funded by the Mott, Ford, and Kellogg foundations and Atlantic Philanthropies. It has grown in size and strength, winning the support of large corporations, which has contributed toward its endowment. Uthungulu’s patron is the monarch of the Zulu nation, His Majesty, King Goodwill Zwelithnini, and the foundation provides grants, support, training, services, and capacity building to community-based organizations in the uThungulu District, an impoverished area in the KwaZulu-Natal province. Mott has supported it since its inception, providing operational, administrative, technical, and infrastructure support. This grant will continue to provide support to the Uthungulu Community Foundation to ensure its growth as a strong, effective, and sustainable community foundation that is able to harness resources for the development of the communities it serves.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will continue to strengthen the Uthungulu Community Foundation, which was established in 1999 as the first community foundation in South Africa. Its mission is to harness resources to maintain a permanent endowment fund that enhances sustainable socioeconomic development of the Zululand region. Past activities include capacity-building training and technical assistance to emerging community foundations and community-based, nongovernmental organizations, collaboration with local government agencies on development issues, and grantmaking to community-based organizations to implement various community development projects. Future plans include continuation of these activities in addition to developing educational materials on organizational development issues; increasing local fund- raising activities, as well as marketing and advertising efforts; and exercising a leadership role in the South African Community Foundation Association.

title: General Purposes
description: The Uthungulu Community Foundation was established in 1999 to promote and support projects that improve the quality of life of poor people in the Zululand region of KwaZulu-Natal province. Since its inception, the grantee has focused on making grants and providing training and mentoring support to community-based organizations. It also assists organizations to access resources from other funders by brokering relations and linking donors to causes. Over the past two years, the grantee made grants to over 30 community-based organizations, participated in various national events, and supported fellow nonprofits through sharing knowledge and experiences. Over the next two years, the grantee will continue to strengthen community-based organizations through grantmaking, encouraging public participation by civil society in local governance processes, providing platforms for dialogue with youth to help young people in Zululand become entrepreneurs, and supporting projects that create jobs.

title: General Purposes
description: The Uthungulu Community Foundation promotes community development in the Uthungulu region of KwaZulu-Natal in South Africa. It makes grants to community-based organizations, implements projects that improve the quality of life of poor and marginalized people, and provides training and mentoring to organizations working in poor and under-resourced communities in the Uthungulu region. Activities over the past two years included making grants to community-based organizations, providing training on various topics related to community development, and participating in national and international learning events. This grant will support Uthungulu Community Foundation to continue making grants, providing training, and engaging with government and the nonprofit and business sectors on issues related to the community philanthropy field in South Africa.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Bulgaria, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Albania, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Serbia, Slovenia, Romania, Croatia
description: The Project on Ethnic Relations is dedicated to reducing ethnic tensions in Central and Southeast Europe and the former Soviet Union. Project staff works with political leaders to promote alternatives to conflicts, assists in the development of indigenous institutions to deal with ethnic tension, influences opinion leaders, and trains experts in this field. In 2008-2009, the grantee will pursue four major programs: (1) mediating ethnic conflicts, with a particular focus on relations between Kosovo and Serbia; (2) exploring regional issues, such as international responses to ethnic conflict in the postcommunist space; (3) building confidence between Romani communities and majority populations; and (4) training a new generation of experts.

title: MicroTest
description: Aspen Institute’s MicroTest project was created by and for practitioners interested in documenting and strengthening the level of performance in the domestic micro-enterprise field. Since its beginning in 1997, Micro Test has become a proven process through which practitioners define, debate, test and refine performance benchmarks based on actual experience serving low-income individuals.This grant will support MicroTest’s continuing efforts to expand its membership, build its sustainability, and enhance the value of the performance and outcomes data generated for its members, funders and other stakeholders.Currently, more than 70 agencies are voluntarily providing performance information to MicroTest to gain increased empirical knowledge about effective practices. MicroTest performance data also provides the basis for developing industry standards in collaboration with the Association for Enterprise Opportunity, the membership organization for micro-enterprise practitioners.

title: MicroTest
description: This grant renewal to Aspen Institute will provide continued support for MicroTest, a grassroots effort to improve the quality of antipoverty, microenterprise development programs in the United States. MicroTest was established by and for practitioners interested in documenting and strengthening the level of performance in the domestic microenterprise field. Initiated in 1997, it has become a proven process through which practitioners define, debate, test, and refine benchmarks based on actual experience serving low-income individuals. This renewal will support MicroTest’s continuing efforts to expand its membership, build its sustainability, and enhance the value of the performance and outcomes data generated for its members, funders, and other stakeholders.

title: MicroTest
description: This grant to the Aspen Institute supports the expansion of MicroTest, a grassroots effort to improve the quality of data on the performance of antipoverty, microenterprise development programs in the United States. MicroTest was established by and for practitioners interested in documenting and strengthening the level of performance in the field. Initiated in 1997, it has become a proven process through which practitioners define, debate, test, and refine benchmarks based on actual experience serving low-income individuals.

title: MicroTest
description: This grant to the Aspen Institute supports the continuation of MicroTest, a grassroots effort to improve the quality of antipoverty, microenterprise development programs in the United States, with 100 microenterprise program members. MicroTest was established by and for practitioners interested in documenting and strengthening the level of performance in the field. Initiated in 1997, it has become a proven process through which practitioners define, debate, test, and refine benchmarks based on actual experience serving low-income individuals.

title: MicroTest
description: This grant to Aspen Institute supports the creation of a data hub by MicroTest, a grassroots effort to improve the quality of antipoverty, microenterprise development programs in the United States. This hub is expected to sustain MicroTest after Mott Foundation funding has ended. MicroTest was established by and for practitioners interested in documenting and strengthening the level of performance in the field. Initiated in 1997, it has become a proven process through which practitioners define, debate, test, and refine benchmarks based on actual experience serving low-income entrepreneurs.

title: MicroTest
description: This grant supports the continuation of MicroTest, a grassroots data collection effort to improve the performance of antipoverty, microenterprise development programs in the United States. MicroTest, a program of Aspen Institute, was established by and for practitioners interested in documenting and strengthening the level of performance in the field. Initiated in 1997, it has become a proven process through which practitioners define, debate, test, and refine benchmarks based on actual experience serving low-income individuals. The Aspen Institute believes that the proposed data hub affords the greatest opportunity yet to make MicroTest sustainable as part of a larger data initiative for the entire industry.

title: MicroTest
description: This grant supports the online expansion of MicroTest, a grassroots effort conducted by the Aspen Institute, that works to improve the quality of antipoverty, microenterprise development programs in the United States. MicroTest was established by and for practitioners interested in documenting and strengthening the level of performance in the field. Initiated in 1997, it has become a proven process through which practitioners define, debate, test, and refine benchmarks based on actual experience serving low-income individuals.

title: MicroTest
description: This grant supports the expansion of MicroTest, a grassroots effort to improve the quality of antipoverty, microenterprise development programs in the United States from 13 to 64 member groups. MicroTest, a project of the Aspen Institute, was established by and for practitioners interested in documenting and strengthening the level of performance in the field. Initiated in 1997, it has become a proven process through which practitioners define, debate, test, and refine benchmarks based on actual experience serving low-income individuals.

title: MicroTest
description: This final grant for the MicroTest project will allow the Aspen Institute to successfully transition the project to an online, fee-based model. MicroTest was established by and for practitioners interested in documenting and strengthening the level of performance in the field. Initiated in 1997, it has become a proven process through which practitioners define, debate, test, and refine benchmarks based on actual experience serving low-income individuals.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will enable BoardSource to continue providing governance expertise and consulting services, research-driven and practical publications and resources, and training to thousands of nonprofit boards throughout the country. In addition, BoardSource will begin implementation of a five-year business plan centered on three strategic priorities: providing guidance to the sector on what constitutes good governance; disseminating resources that strengthen board performance; and extending the reach and impact of its work through national and regional partnerships.During 2005, BoardSource provided governance information to more than 201,000 visitors to its Web site, and regular updates on board issues through monthly e-newsletters and periodicals to more than 9,000 members.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued general purposes support to BoardSource, an organization that provides governance training, information, and leadership opportunities to increase the effectiveness of the nation’s 1.6 million nonprofit agencies. In 2007 and 2008, BoardSource will continue to provide governance expertise in the public policy and legislative arenas, consulting services, research-driven and practical publications and tools, and training to thousands of nonprofit boards throughout the country. In addition, BoardSource continues implementation of a five-year business plan which centers on three strategic priorities: providing guidance to the sector on what constitutes good governance, disseminating resources that strengthen board performance, and extending the reach and impact of its work through national and regional partnerships.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued support to BoardSource, an organization that provides governance training, information, and leadership opportunities to increase the effectiveness of the nation’s 1.6 million nonprofit agencies. In 2009 and 2010, the grantee will continue to provide governance expertise in the public policy and legislative arenas, consulting services, research-driven and practical publications and tools, and training to thousands of nonprofit boards throughout the country. In 2008, the grantee developed a new strategic plan which centers on three priorities: 1) increasing the nonprofit sector’s knowledge of good governance practices; 2) increasing the participation of targeted populations in nonprofit board service; and 3) enhancing the overall performance of nonprofit boards.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued general purpose support to BoardSource, an organization that provides governance training, information, and leadership opportunities to increase the effectiveness of the nation’s nonprofit agencies. Over the past two years, the grantee has completed several research reports including “Advancing Good Governance: How Grantmakers Invest in the Governance of Nonprofit Organizations”; “Vital Voices: Lessons Learned from Board Members of Color”; and the “Governance Index 2010”. In 2011 and 2012, the grantee will continue to provide governance expertise in the public policy and legislative arenas, consulting services, research-driven and practical publications and tools, and training to thousands of nonprofit boards throughout the country.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued general purpose support to BoardSource, an organization that provides governance training, information, and leadership opportunities to increase the effectiveness of the nation’s 2.3 million nonprofit agencies. The grantee supports, trains, and educates more than 60,000 nonprofit board leaders from across the country each year. Recent accomplishments include the publication of the “BoardSource Nonprofit Governance Index 2012”, the establishment of a learning lab of nonprofit governance, and an increase in board members trained from a few hundred in 2010 to almost 6,000 in 2012. The grantee also launched BoardSource Academy, which offers certificate programs for nonprofit leaders, board chairs, and governance trainers. Over 2013-2014, the grantee will continue to pursue the three strategic goals of its 2012-2016 plan: 1) build high impact educational and involvement programs to scale; 2) inspire and diversify a network of nonprofit leaders; and 3) expand the grantee’s reach by eliminating barriers to participation.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued general purpose support to BoardSource, an organization that provides governance training, information, and leadership opportunities to increase the effectiveness of the nation’s nonprofit agencies. Major recent accomplishments include: launching of the Stand for Your Mission Campaign; membership growth of over 220 percent in the last three years, serving over 100,000 nonprofit leaders; the rebranding and publishing of the 8th annual BoardSource Governance Index, attracting responses from over 1,000 chief executives and board chairs; hosting four cohorts of over 100 Certified Governance Trainers operating in 38 states and 5 countries; launched a new section on GuideStar called People and Governance, aimed at creating transparency; launched and expanded the Board Recruitment Center; and over 250 participants earned a Certificate of Nonprofit Board Education for nonprofit leaders, board chairs, and chief executives through the BoardSource Academy.

title: General Purposes
description: BoardSource is the leading organization in the United States that provides governance training, information, and leadership opportunities to increase the effectiveness of the nation’s nonprofit agencies. In 2015-2016, BoardSource has two main goals: 1) to serve as the national voice for board leadership, encouraging leaders to embrace advocacy as a core strategy, become transparent, and promote diversity and inclusion in the boardroom; and 2) to ensure that nonprofit organizations have access to the support they need to build a strong and effective board by expanding their board development program, providing in-depth educational and advisory services, offering support through strategic relationships, and investing in its own human and technical capacity in order to expand its reach. This grant increase will support the grantee’s efforts to challenge nonprofit organizations and their boards to consider long-term collaboration as a strategy for greater impact.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued general purpose support to BoardSource, an organization established in 1988 that provides governance training, information, and leadership development opportunities to increase the effectiveness of the nation’s nonprofit organizations. Major recent accomplishments include: launching The Power of Possibility campaign to encourage boards to consider alliances and strategic partnerships with other nonprofits; conducting the Stand For Your Mission campaign, which emphasizes a nonprofit board’s role in advocacy; developing a new Measuring Fundraising Effectiveness framework; and fieldwork for the grantee’s biennial study of nonprofit board practices. During 2017, the grantee will continue to pursue two main goals: 1) to educate leaders and support effective board service and governance; and 2) to deepen understanding and inspire action on critical sector issues.

title: Migration Rights Network
description: This grant will enable the Memorial Human Rights Center to continue assisting refugees and forced migrants, many of whom have been displaced by the war in Chechnya, through its network of 58 legal assistance centers throughout Russia. The center also will work with federal and regional government structures to address refugee and migrant issues; conduct teaching seminars on migration law; and publish seminar proceedings, manuals and reports on migration in Russia.In 1996, the center established the Migration Rights Network to address the growing human rights needs of Russia’s migrant populations. Currently, there are 58 centers in the 45 regions of Russia where 80 percent of all migrants are located. Since its inception, network staff and lawyers have given more than 100,000 consultations to migrants on asserting and protecting their rights. Also, over the past ten years, the center has organized 19 teaching seminars on migration law problems. The center was established in 1993 to protect human rights and promote civic participation in Russia.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant supports the active participation of people in the development of their communities and in the political processes shaping the future of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Centers for Civic Initiatives – Tuzla provides training, information resources, mentoring, and financial support to other nongovernmental organizations and community-based groups working to improve links between citizens and government and address key policy initiatives. Over the past two years, the grantee has monitored the work of local and district assemblies, organized get-out-the-vote campaigns, trained community groups and elected officials in participatory decisionmaking, and supported public awareness campaigns on reform issues. The grantee is based in Tuzla and works throughout Bosnia and Herzegovina.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant supports the active participation of people in the development of their communities and in the political processes shaping the future of Bosnia and Herzegovina. In 2009-2010, the Centers for Civic Initiatives – Tuzla will provide training, information resources, mentoring, and financial support to other nongovernmental organizations and community-based groups working to improve links between citizens and government and address key policy initiatives. The centers will also strengthen the accountability of decisionmakers to citizens by monitoring the work of Bosnia and Herzegovina’s state- and entity-level governments and parliaments. During the past two years, the grantee has: monitored the work of the state- and entity-level government and parliaments and 13 cantonal assemblies; provided approximately $850,000 in grants to nonprofits in Bosnia; and promoted transitional justice in Bosnia and Herzegovina by managing a local network to support witnesses.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant supports the active participation of people in the development of their communities and in the political processes shaping the future of Bosnia and Herzegovina. During 2011-2012, the Centers for Civic Initiatives – Tuzla will strengthen the accountability of decisionmakers to citizens by monitoring the work of Bosnia and Herzegovina’s state- and entity-level governments and parliaments. The grantee will also provide financial and technical support to other nonprofits to engage in advocacy and awareness-raising campaigns. Finally, the grantee will advocate for an improved legal and fiscal framework for philanthropy in the country. During the past two years, the grantee issued quarterly monitoring reports on the work of the state- and entity-level government and parliaments and 13 cantonal assemblies, carried out an assessment of the levels and quality of citizen participation in decisionmaking, and provided $2.7 million in grants to nonprofits. The grantee is based in Tuzla.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant supports the active participation of people in the development of their communities and in the political processes shaping the future of Bosnia and Herzegovina. During 2013-2014, the Centers for Civic Initiatives – Tuzla will monitor the work of the country’s state- and entity-level governments and parliaments, provide financial and technical support to other nonprofits to engage in advocacy and awareness-raising campaigns, and organize activities and tools that allow citizens to participate in decisionmaking. During the past two years, the grantee issued more than 190 monitoring reports on the work of Bosnia’s state- and entity-level governments and parliaments and cantonal assemblies, disseminated this data and analyses through a dedicated Web site, carried out annual assessments of the levels and quality of citizen participation in decisionmaking, organized national-level advocacy campaigns on key issues facing local communities in Bosnia, launched a new Internet-based television station highlighting civil society initiatives in Bosnia, and provided $2.7 million in grants to nonprofits.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant supports the active participation of people in the development of their communities and in the political processes shaping the future of Bosnia and Herzegovina. During 2015-2016, the Centers for Civic Initiatives – Tuzla will monitor the work of the country’s state- and entity-level governments and parliaments, provide financial and technical support to other nonprofits to engage in advocacy and awareness-raising campaigns, and organize activities and tools that allow citizens to participate in decisionmaking. The grantee will implement an intensive capacity building grant program targeting 12 nonprofits that are leaders in their sectors. During the past two years, the grantee issued 204 monitoring reports covering the work of 136 ministries, 220 parliamentary committees and working groups, and 760 public officials. These reports were widely disseminated and discussed with the public and key stakeholders. The grantee also carried out annual assessments of the levels and quality of citizen participation in decisionmaking, organized national-level advocacy campaigns on key issues facing local communities in Bosnia, and provided grants to other nonprofits.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant supports the active participation of people in the development of their communities and in the political processes shaping the future of Bosnia and Herzegovina. During 2017-2018, the Centers for Civic Initiatives – Tuzla will monitor the work of the country’s state- and entity-level governments and parliaments, provide financial and technical support to other nonprofits to engage in advocacy and awareness-raising campaigns, and organize activities and tools that allow citizens to participate in decisionmaking. During the past two years, the grantee issued 149 monitoring reports covering the work of federal and state ministries, parliamentary committees and working groups, and public officials. Through over 850 articles and many public events, these reports were widely disseminated and discussed with citizens and key stakeholders. The grantee also carried out annual assessments of the levels and quality of citizen participation in decisionmaking, organized national-level advocacy campaigns on key issues facing local communities in Bosnia, and provided grants for advocacy and institutional development to 19 nonprofits across 12 key sectors. The grantee is based in Tuzla, with additional offices in other major cities in Bosnia.

title: MDB and ECA Reform Campaign
description: During the past several years, Mani Tese’s Campaign for the Reform of the World Bank has significantly strengthened its capacity to address issues related to multilateral development banks, export credit agencies and foreign direct investment. The campaign has focused its work on two facets of international development – development finance and international public and private finance. This has resulted in a broader and more relevant framework for research and analysis.This grant will enable the campaign to focus on the increasing role of private sector lending in the broader context of financial liberalization and deregulation being advanced by international financial institutions and the World Trade Organization; the environmental and social implications of international financial institution support of expanded private sector lending; the potential role of new financial actors to encourage mainstream sustainable development in international financial flows; the restructuring of development finance; and the relationship between the international finance and trade policy agendas.Mani Tese, an Italian non-governmental development organization created in 1964, works at the national and international levels to further justice, solidarity and respect among peoples.

title: Mainstreaming Environmental Sustainability in Global Financial Flows North-South
description: The main goal of this project is to ensure that global financial flows contribute to internationally adopted principles that support and promote sustainable development. To achieve this goal, Mani Tese will focus on ensuring that Italian and European responsibilities in development finance continue to be an important element of Italian and European foreign policy; highlighting the connections between public-private investments, environmental sustainability, and human rights and the responsibilities of European governments; and emphasizing the need for encouraging participation, transparency, and accountability in the global investment agenda.

title: Mainstreaming Environmental Sustainability in Global Financial Flows North-South
description: The main goal of this project is to ensure that global financial flows contribute to internationally adopted principles that support and promote sustainable development. This grant increase will allow Mani Tese to play a catalytic role among Italian, European, and international nongovernmental organizations in developing alternative policy options related to the financial and economic crises. As the Group of Eight meetings will be held in Italy in 2009, Mani Tese will coordinate detailed and innovative proposals to address the financial crisis as well as climate and energy policies.

title: Mainstreaming Environmental Sustainability in Global Financial Flows North-South
description: Mani Tese is an Italian organization working on international development issues since 1964. The main goal of this project is to ensure that global financial flows contribute to internationally adopted principles that support and promote sustainable development. To achieve this goal, the main areas of focus will be to ensure that public financial institutions support sustainable development; re-regulate the financial sector; hold investors accountable for environmental and social impacts on communities in developing countries; and develop a new climate finance mechanism. Over the last grant period, the grantee created close cooperation between the project staff and the Italian banking and ethical finance sectors; and facilitated the development of new nongovernmental organization proposals to address climate finance.

title: Mainstreaming Environmental Sustainability in Global Financial Flows North-South
description: Mani Tese is an Italian organization working on international development issues since 1964. The main goal of this project is to ensure that global financial flows contribute to internationally adopted principles that support and promote sustainable development. This grant increase will support a strategic planning process to rethink nongovernmental organization strategies to address international financial institution, export credit agency, and private bank reform issues.

title: Mainstreaming Environmental Sustainability into a Changing Development Finance
description: Re:Common is an Italian organization established in 2012 that has grown out of a long established nongovernmental organization project addressing World Bank reform. The main goal of this project is to monitor the changes taking place in international development finance and ensure that this financing continues to support and promote sustainable development. This grant will support research and policy analysis, as well as public awareness and policy advocacy efforts related to a broad range of international financial institutions.

title: Mainstreaming Environmental Sustainability into a Changing Development Finance
description: Re:Common is an Italian organization established in 2012 that has grown out of a long established nongovernmental organization project addressing World Bank Group reform. The main goal of this project is to monitor the changes taking place in international development finance and ensure that this financing continues to support and promote sustainable development. Over the last grant period, the grantee worked with an international nongovernmental coalition to address fossil fuel financing by public international financial institutions. This grant will continue to support research and policy analysis as well as public awareness and policy advocacy efforts related to a broad range of international financial institutions.

title: Mainstreaming Environmental Sustainability into a Changing Development Finance
description: Re:Common is an Italian organization formed in 2012 that grew out of a long-established, nongovernmental organization project addressing World Bank Group reform. The main goal of this project is to monitor the changes taking place in international development finance and ensure that this financing continues to support and promote sustainable development. Over the last grant period, the grantee helped to coordinate and lead European nongovernmental organization efforts to influence the World Bank Group’s environmental and social safeguard policies. This grant will support research and policy analysis, as well as public awareness and policy advocacy efforts to address new development finance institutions promoting large-scale infrastructure and energy projects.

title: Centre for Development and Promotion of Voluntary Work
grantee: Association for Psychosocial Help and Development of Voluntary Work
description: Multiyear funding will enable the Association for Psychosocial Help and Development of Voluntary Work to improve its capacity to support volunteer projects; expand the program to other schools and communities in Bosnia and Herzegovina; and share its knowledge with other non-governmental organizations and schools in Southeast Europe.During the past two years, the association has successfully implemented volunteer programs in secondary and primary schools in two cantons (second-level units of local autonomy) in Bosnia and Herzegovina and the district of Brcko. In addition, it has shared its experience and expertise with organizations in Serbia and Montenegro and Kosovo.In 1996, the association was established in Bosnia to provide assistance to children, the elderly and the disabled.

title: Centre for Development and Promotion of Voluntary Work
grantee: Association for Psychosocial Help and Development of Voluntary Work
description: The project goal is to develop and promote volunteerism and public participation in community life in Bosnia-Herzegovina and Southeast Europe. Through its Centre for Development and Promotion of Voluntary Work, the Association for Psychosocial Help and Development of Voluntary Work endeavors to enable communities to address critical social needs by mobilizing human resources within the community. The association provides training to mentors who then work with volunteers in nongovernmental organizations, schools, and public institutions, and the association advocates for systemic and institutional changes and policy developments that encourage volunteerism. In 2006-2007, the association expanded the number of schools that run volunteer programs and successfully advocated for the inclusion of volunteerism in school curricula. In addition, the association increased volunteerism among elderly people and effectively introduced school-based volunteer programs that helped bridge ethnic divides. The association is based in Gracanica, Bosnia.
