title: Carnegie Moscow Center
description: This grant will enable the Carnegie Moscow Center, a Russian-based public policy institute that is part of the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, to contribute to the public debate and understanding of key domestic and foreign policy issues affecting Russia and other former Soviet Union countries by providing a neutral forum for independent scholars in both Moscow and Washington, D.C. Its programs include research and analyses; workshops, seminars and meetings; visiting lecturers; and an active outreach effort via publications, the use of Web sites and the media.Highlights of recent events include a forum on energy security in Russia and Eurasia; regional monitoring of democratic development; and conferences on Russia and the West as well as on minority rights and Islamic extremism.

title: Carnegie Moscow Center
description: The Carnegie Endowment for International Peace is a private, nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing cooperation between nations and promoting active international engagement by the United States. Through research, publishing, convening and, on occasion, creating new institutions and international networks, the grantee associates shape fresh policy approaches. In 1993, the grantee established a major public policy research center in Moscow, the Carnegie Moscow Center, devoted to analysis and understanding of the major issues facing Russia and the Commonwealth of Independent States. A grant increase will allow Carnegie Moscow Center researchers to carry out a previously unplanned examination of the context in which donor organizations operate in Russia, Ukraine, and Belarus. Dramatic political, economic, and social changes in Russia and Ukraine over the last four years and the ongoing specific challenges of Belarus make such an examination both necessary and timely. This review will help to inform future grantmaking by both the Mott Foundation and other domestic and international donors operating in these countries.

title: Carnegie Moscow Center
description: This grant supports the work of the Russian and Eurasian program of the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace, which is implemented by its Carnegie Moscow Center. The center is the leading international analytical institution for independent scholars examining contemporary Russian affairs. During the grant period, it will continue to provide a neutral venue for open discussion and debate in six key program areas including foreign and security policy, political institutions, society and the regions, religion and society, nonproliferation, and economic and energy policy. In the previous grant period, the center hosted over 200 conferences, seminars, and workshops. Its analysts produced over 250 media articles, numerous monographs and policy briefs, and contributed to the publication of seven issues of the in-house journal “Pro et Contra”. The Carnegie Moscow Center has been a key component of the grantee’s engagement in Russia since 1993.

title: Sustainable Financial Relations Project
description: Berne Declaration has been a respected voice in the international non-governmental organization community and influential in international financial institution reform efforts since 1992. The Sustainable Financial Relations Project enables Berne to work with other non-governmental organizations (NGOs) in Europe, the U.S. and developing countries on international financial institution reform.This grant will enable Berne Declaration to continue its work with partners in the U.S., Europe and developing countries on institutional reform at the World Bank, export credit agencies and private sector banks; monitor environmentally and socially harmful projects funded by these institutions; and educate officials and the public about the need to adopt more sustainable patterns of international development.Activities during the past two years included engaging in discussions with officials of the Swiss export credit agency (ECA), resulting in the strengthening of environmental and social guidelines for ECA-supported projects and the introduction of anti-corruption practices; advocating for the creation of a multi-stakeholder process that allows Swiss NGOs to participate in high-level economic ministry discussions on decisions relating to the World Bank; and participating in the international NGO network, BankTrack.

title: General Purposes
description: The Consultative Group on Biological Diversity provides a flexible, member-driven structure that promotes high quality, collaborative grantmaking in the field of biodiversity conservation. With this general purpose grant, the organization will continue to build partnerships among funders, identify funding gaps and grantmaking priorities, provide regular newsletters, organize one-on-one consultations with members, and identify and respond to emerging issues.

title: General Purposes
description: Since its founding in 1987, the Consultative Group on Biological Diversity has worked effectively to create a flexible, member-driven structure that promotes high quality, collaborative grantmaking in biodiversity. With general purpose support, the grantee will work to increase the quality and impact of private grantmaking on biodiversity conservation. Specific activities will include building partnerships among funders, identifying funding gaps and grantmaking priorities, providing regular newsletters and updates, organizing one-on-one consultations with members, and identifying and responding to emerging issues.

title: General Purposes
description: The Consultative Group on Biological Diversity helps create partnerships among environmental funders. While available for the general purposes of the organization, this grant increase is expected to be used for a consultant who will provide research, networking, and administrative support to assist a group of funders investigating the idea of a national water policy agenda.

title: General Purposes
description: The Consultative Group on Biological Diversity helps create partnerships among environmental funders across the United States. This grant increase will help the organization maintain momentum for developing a national water policy agenda. These general purpose funds will be used to hire a consultant to assist a collaboration of freshwater funders by providing research, networking, and administrative support.

title: General Purposes
description: Founded in 1987, the Consultative Group on Biological Diversity has effectively created a flexible, member-driven structure that promotes high quality, collaborative grantmaking. This general purpose grant renewal will allow the organization to continue such efforts to increase the quality and impact of private grantmaking related to biodiversity conservation.

With prior Mott support, the grantee hosted meetings of environmental grantmakers, provided regular newsletters and updates, offered individualized consultations to members, and helped foundations respond to emerging issues. With this general purpose grant renewal, the grantee will continue these activities, expand its international programs, and strengthen support for funders working to advance climate change solutions.

title: General Purposes

title: General Purposes
description: This general purpose grant supports the Biodiversity Funders Group to foster collaboration and coordination among its member foundations and to facilitate the Funders of the Amazon Basin Group, a program of the grantee. The grantee is a membership organization comprised of 78 foundations.

title: Transfrontier Cooperation Program
geographic_focus: Lithuania, Hungary, Serbia, Bulgaria, Montenegro, Russia, Slovenia, Estonia, Moldova, Belarus, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Czech Republic, Ukraine, Romania, Slovakia, North Macedonia, Poland, Latvia, Albania
description: The program goal is to promote transfrontier cooperation and development in Central/Eastern Europe and Russia. Through this program, nonprofit sector representatives, business leaders, and local and regional government officials from communities in Central/Eastern Europe and Russia border areas will meet to develop sustainable, interest-based, cross-border institutions and practices. The program supports the development of an integrated Europe and addresses the danger of new dividing lines separating the European Union accession and nonaccession countries in Central/Eastern Europe. This grant increase to EastWest Institute will support program administration costs.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant increase will enable the Bank Information Center to continue efforts to promote infrastructure development in Latin America, specifically the Regional Infrastructure Integration Initiative. In addition, funding will provide travel expenses for researchers from Latin America who are helping construct a database and Web portal that will house information on major infrastructure projects in the region.

title: General Purposes
description: Multilateral development banks play a central role in formulating development policy. They remain the largest source of development finance in the world, and the World Bank’s environmental and social policies are the single set of standards most followed by other financial institutions. The Bank Information Center supports developing country organizations in their efforts to influence the social and environmental impacts of multilateral development bank-financed projects and policies. It provides information dissemination and capacity-building activities, networking and coalition-building expertise, and advocacy support. During the next two years, activities will include providing information and technical assistance to nongovernmental organizations’ efforts to reform the World Bank and regional multilateral development banks in Africa, Asia, Central and Eastern Europe, and Latin America. This grant provides continued general purposes support to the Bank Information Center.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant increase to the Bank Information Center will support the general purposes of the center, including additional strategic planning expenses to cover a research project mapping financial flows to developing countries and analyzing the effects of these flows on international financial institutions. This request will help to enhance the Bank Information Center’s leadership and convening roles.

title: General Purposes

This grant increase will support the general purposes of the Bank Information Center, including expenses for a strategic planning conference and for planning around the 50th anniversary of the Inter-American Development Bank.

During the next two years, the grantee will provide information dissemination and capacity-building services, networking and coalition-building expertise, and advocacy support to partners around the world. This grant provides continued general purpose support to the Bank Information Center.

title: General Purposes
description: Multilateral development banks, and particularly the World Bank, have traditionally played a central role in formulating development policy and continue to be the dominant standard setters in international finance and investment. International development finance is changing, however, with the emergence of new national development banks, such as those in Brazil and China, which lag behind their international counterparts in terms of transparency, governance, and environmental and social protection policies. The Bank Information Center supports developing country organizations in their efforts to strengthen standards, particularly at the World Bank, and increasingly at national development banks. This grant increase will enable the grantee to conduct a strategic planning process to meet the new challenges in development finance, as well as to participate in technical cooperation with nongovernmental organizations in Brazil and South America.

title: General Purposes
description: The Bank Information Center has worked for 30 years on accountability and transparency at the World Bank Group, and it supports a broad network of civil society organizations in the United States, Europe, Asia, Africa, Latin America, and the Middle East in their efforts to influence and improve the social and environmental impacts of multilateral development bank-financed projects and policies. This grant will continue to provide general purposes support to the grantee to assist with its work to monitor and ensure the implementation of the new World Bank Group Environmental and Social Framework.

title: General Purposes
description: The Bank Information Center is a nongovernmental organization specialized in analyzing and strengthening social and environmental governance of international financial institutions, primarily the World Bank Group. Over the last grant period, the organization and its partners in developing countries worked on finalizing the new Environmental Social Framework of the World Bank Group. Over the next grant period, attention will be given to the implementation of the new safeguards and training partners to engage with development finance institutions.

title: General Purposes
description: Since 1994, Southwest Creations Collaborative has provided employment for very low-income Hispanic women who otherwise would be homeless. The organization’s mission is to provide low-income women in New Mexico with opportunities to increase their financial security through good jobs with consistent income, workplace flexibility to accommodate their needs, and other family supports that include onsite affordable day care, leadership development and health care.This grant will support the collaborative’s efforts to continue creating job opportunities for low-income women after Mott funding has ceased.

title: State Fiscal Analysis Initiative
description: Funding will enable the North Carolina Justice Center to inform public debates in North Carolina through effective research, analysis and outreach efforts. Other priorities include strengthening communication and outreach strategies.During the past two years, the center played an important role in informing and framing public debates on revenue and spending issues and on new and existing policy initiatives in the state.This is one of 10 grants supporting the State Fiscal Analysis Initiative. The North Carolina Justice Center joined the initiative in 1993. Mott has also supported the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, which provides technical assistance and networking opportunities for the 35 state organizations participating in this initiative.

title: State Fiscal Analysis Initiative
description: This is one of ten grants recommended to state organizations participating in the State Fiscal Analysis Initiative. The Ford, Annie E. Casey, and Mott Foundations created the initiative in 1992 in order to build state capacity for timely, credible, and accessible tax and budget analysis on behalf of low- and middle-income families. The North Carolina Justice Center joined this effort in 1994 and is recognized throughout the state as the leading nongovernmental voice on state budget and tax policy matters. During this renewal grant period, the North Carolina Justice Center will prepare and disseminate analyses on a range of state fiscal issues, with a particular emphasis on state and local tax policies and income support programs. Other activities planned for the grant period include community outreach and strategic communications. Related to this project is a grant to the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, which provides technical assistance to all 36 organizations participating in the initiative.

title: State Fiscal Analysis Initiative
description: The Ford, Casey, and Mott foundations created the State Fiscal Analysis Initiative in 1992 in order to build state capacity for timely, credible, and accessible tax and budget analysis on behalf of low- and middle-income families. The North Carolina Justice Center joined this effort in 1994 and has become recognized as an authoritative source of information and analysis in its home state. During this grant period, the grantee will prepare and disseminate analyses on a range of state fiscal issues, with a particular emphasis on the state and local tax policies affecting low-income families, education, labor market policies, and income support programs. Related to this project is a grant to the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, which provides technical assistance to all the state organizations participating in this initiative.

title: Auto Career Project
description: The Auto Career Project, sponsored by Lawrence Technological University in conjunction with the Ferndale School District, has resulted in a career academy designed to build a pathway for central city youth in Southeast Michigan into good-paying employment in the automotive industry. Over the next two years, the project will evolve into a four-year high school with an enrollment of 500. This grant increase will partially support an advertisement campaign to recruit 400 candidates for the 150 freshman slots available this year.

title: Sectoral Employment Initiative Evaluation
description: This grant will allow Public/Private Ventures to disseminate the evaluation findings of the effectiveness of sectoral strategies used by demonstration sites involved in the grantee’s Sectoral Employment Initiative. This dissemination will further enhance the view that sectoral employment initiatives are being seen as a key strategy to retain low-income people in the labor market and allow them access to decent jobs that can move them out of poverty.

title: Great Lakes Land Trust Capacity-Building Program
description: Following the launch of a national land trust accreditation program, the Land Trust Alliance is focusing on helping member land trusts prepare for the accreditation process. This grant will enable the Land Trust Alliance to provide organizational assessments, training and consultations to land trusts to enhance their organizational capacity and support land trust partnerships engaged in strategic conservation. During the past three years, the alliance built a land trust collaborative focusing on Lake Superior; assisted land trusts in Indiana, Michigan and Ohio in forming statewide networking organizations; and provided training on organizational capacity and strategic conservation issues.

title: Allowing Enterprise: Federal Microenterprise Policy Project
description: This grant will enable the Corporation for Enterprise Development to continue providing support for state microenterprise organizations with a focus on addressing industry challenges identified in the recent Aspen Institute report “Opening Opportunities, Building Ownership: Fulfilling the Promise of Microenterprise in the United States”. To accomplish this, the organization will support established and emerging state microenterprise organizations by providing technical assistance, documenting and disseminating effective practices, and administering a small grants program.During the past year, the project awarded eight grants to established state microenterprise organizations; convened, in collaboration with the Association for Enterprise Opportunity, the annual meeting for statewide microenterprise organizations; designed and completed three statewide microenterprise blueprints for growth; convened and facilitated five statewide policy academies around selected topics; and provided individualized technical assistance and topical presentations at state microenterprise organizations’ annual conferences around the country.

title: Allowing Enterprise: Federal Microenterprise Policy Project
description: This renewal grant will allow the Corporation for Enterprise Development to continue to provide capacity building support for state microenterprise organizations. Over the past 15 years, the Corporation for Enterprise Development has helped support and empower emerging and existing state microenterprise organizations and currently supports a national network of over 30 organizations through training, capacity building, and grant funding. During the grant period, the grantee will research, develop, and test effective practices and capacity building tools that will assist state microenterprise organizations in improving their performance and sustainability.

title: Allowing Enterprise: Federal Microenterprise Policy Project
description: This final grant renewal will allow the Corporation for Enterprise Development to continue to provide funding and technical assistance to six state microenterprise associations to build their capacity to network and become advocates for sustaining effective microenterprise practice, and to continue to assist in the formation of an expanded federal microenterprise policy.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will enable the Network of European Foundations for Innovative Cooperation to continue working to strengthen philanthropic cooperation among foundations and other types of organized philanthropy in Europe. The network serves as a launching pad for collaborative initiatives related to Europe and the role of Europe on the global stage. It manages donor-funded programs and initiatives related to building social capital, citizens’ rights, global governance, youth development, education and culture.In 2005, projects included the European Mercator Fund, a mechanism for supporting projects related to drug policy reform, sustainable development, immigration and health; and the Youth Empowerment Partnership Program, a collaborative initiative that addresses issues related to at-risk children and youth through community building.The network, based in Brussels, currently includes 11 foundations.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen philanthropic cooperation among foundations and other types of organized philanthropy in Europe. The Network of European Foundations for Innovative Cooperation, a nonprofit membership association for foundations, serves as a launching pad for collaborative initiatives related to Europe and the role of Europe on the global stage. The grantee manages donor-funded programs and initiatives related to promoting social capital, citizens’ rights, global governance, youth development, education, and culture. In 2006, projects included the European Mercator Fund, a mechanism for supporting projects related to drug policy reform, sustainable development, immigration, and health; and the Youth Empowerment Partnership Program, a collaborative initiative to address issues related to children and at-risk youth through community building. The network is based in Brussels, and current membership stands at 12 foundations, including the Mott Foundation.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant supports the general purposes of the Network of European Foundations for Innovative Cooperation, an international, nonprofit membership association based in Brussels. Its goal is to strengthen philanthropic cooperation among foundations, associations, voluntary organizations, and other nongovernmental organizations in Europe. The network manages several joint, donor-funded programs related to building social capital, citizens’ rights, global governance, education, and culture. During 2007, the network supported a range of initiatives in which major European foundations collaborated on issues of youth empowerment, HIV/AIDS, citizen engagement, and Europe’s role on global social issues. The network has 12 members and engages many other foundations, public donors, and other types of philanthropic organizations in its projects.

title: General Purposes
description: Metro Housing Partnership provides an array of counseling and financial assistance services to low-income homebuyers in Flint and Genesee County and serves as a link between local governments and nonprofit housing organizations.This grant will enable the organization to continue providing leadership, technical assistance and financing for housing initiatives in Flint and Genesee County. It will continue to act as a resource and technical assistance provider, at no cost, to a steadily increasing number of organizations and individuals in need of services.

title: General Purposes
description: This renewal grant will provide Metro Housing Partnership with general purposes support that will allow the organization to continue to provide leadership, technical assistance, and financing for housing initiatives in Flint and Genesee County. Metro Housing Partnership provides an array of counseling and financial assistance services to low-income homebuyers, serves as a link between local governments and nonprofit housing organizations, and has performed the critical task of facilitating the creation of a consolidated plan for housing, which is essential to acquiring state and federal grant dollars. Metro Housing Partnership will continue to act as a resource and technical assistance provider, at no cost, to a steadily increasing number of organizations and individuals.

General purpose funding will enable the grantee to continue to act as a resource and technical assistance provider, at no cost, to a steadily increasing number of organizations and individuals.

description: This grant will provide Metro Community Development, with general purpose support to carry out its mission to serve as a leader and catalyst to expand and enhance quality housing and community development initiatives in Flint and Genesee County. description: This grant will provide Metro Community Development with general purpose support to carry out its mission to serve as a leader and catalyst to expand and enhance quality community development initiatives in Flint and Genesee County. title: General Purposes
description: General purpose support to Metro Community Development will enable the grantee to continue serving as a resource and technical assistance provider, at no cost, to a steadily increasing number of partner organizations working to expand and enhance quality housing initiatives in Flint and Genesee County. Guided by a new strategic plan that focuses on housing, community development, and community and coalition building, the grantee also serves as the primary link between city and county governments and local housing organizations.

title: General Purposes
description: The mission of Metro Community Development is to serve as a leader and catalyst to expand and enhance quality housing and community development initiatives in Flint and Genesee County. The grantee serves as a key intermediary for federal and state programs designed to assist low-income people with housing and capital access needs, and implements these programs in partnership with city and county agencies and other local service providers. General purpose support to the grantee will enable the grantee to continue to serve as a no-cost resource and technical assistance provider for local partner organizations working to extend homeownership opportunities to underserved populations, and create stable and vibrant neighborhoods and communities.

title: State Fiscal Analysis Initiative
description: Funding will enable the Maine Center for Economic Policy to continue its analytical, educational, and outreach activities in order to achieve tax and budget policies and other policy changes that benefit low- and moderate-income families in the state.During the past two years, the center played an important role in informing and framing public debates on revenue and spending issues and on new and existing policy initiatives in Maine. This is one of 10 grants supporting the State Fiscal Analysis Initiative. The Maine Center for Economic Policy joined this effort in 1993. Mott has also supported the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, which provides technical assistance and networking opportunities for the 35 state organizations participating in this initiative.

title: State Fiscal Analysis Initiative
description: This is one of ten grants recommended to state organizations to participate in the State Fiscal Analysis Initiative. The Ford, Annie E. Casey, and Mott Foundations created the initiative in 1992 to build state capacity for timely, credible, and accessible tax and budget analysis on behalf of low- and moderate-income families. The Maine Center for Economic Policy joined this effort in 1994 and has grown into a leader in state fiscal policy analysis in its home state. During this grant period, the grantee will prepare and disseminate analyses on a range of state fiscal, budget, and economic issues, with a particular emphasis on policies affecting low- and moderate-income households. Additional activities planned for the grant period include coalition building and strengthening organizational capacity. Related to this project is a grant to the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities — another longstanding Mott grantee — to provide technical assistance to all 36 State Fiscal Analysis Initiative sites as part of this initiative.

title: State Fiscal Analysis Initiative
description: The Ford, Casey, and Mott foundations created the State Fiscal Analysis Initiative in 1992 in order to build state capacity for timely, credible, and accessible tax and budget analysis on behalf of low- and middle-income families. The Maine Center for Economic Policy joined this effort in 1993 and has become recognized as an authoritative source of information and analysis. During this grant period, the grantee will prepare and disseminate analyses on a range of state fiscal issues, with a particular emphasis on the state and local tax policies affecting low-income families, education, labor market policies, and income support programs. In addition, they will develop policy proposals, conduct outreach, and provide training for a wide range of agencies in their state. Related to this project is a grant to the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, which provides technical assistance to all the state organizations participating in this initiative.

title: State Fiscal Analysis Initiative
description: This is one of ten grants recommended to state organizations participating in the State Fiscal Analysis Initiative. The Ford, Casey, and Mott foundations created this initiative in 1992 in order to build state capacity for timely, credible, and accessible tax and budget analysis on behalf of low- and moderate-income families. The Maine Center for Economic Policy joined this effort in 1993 and is recognized by journalists, policymakers, and advocates as an authoritative source of information and analysis. Over the next two years, the grantee will produce and disseminate research and analyses on a range of issues, with a particular emphasis on state and local tax policies, education issues, and income support programs. Related to this project is a grant to the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, which analyzes federal budget and fiscal issues and provides technical assistance to the 41 state organizations participating in this initiative.

title: State Fiscal Analysis Initiative
description: This grant increase is one of ten tie-off grants to state organizations participating in the State Priorities Partnership (formerly the State Fiscal Analysis Initiative). The Ford, Annie E. Casey, and Mott foundations created the initiative in 1992 in order to build state capacity for timely, credible, and accessible tax and budget policy analyses on behalf of low- and moderate-income families. The Maine Center for Economic Policy joined this effort in 1994 and has become recognized as an authoritative source of information and analysis. This grant increase will support the grantee’s ongoing analytical, education, and outreach efforts externally, and organizational capacity building efforts internally.

title: Diploma Plus
description: This grant increase will enable Commonwealth Corporation to co-sponsor a conference on alternative education with the Massachusetts Department of Education. Since 1996, the Commonwealth Corporation, via its Diploma Plus project, has provided a new vision for creating pathways that help vulnerable youth finish school and prepare for college and career opportunities. This increase will provide support for the Commonwealth Corporation to co-sponsor and convene an alternative education symposium in Massachusetts with its statewide partners.

title: Diploma Plus
description: This renewal grant will enable the Commonwealth Corporation to continue to increase program quality and enhance the Diploma Plus project. Diploma Plus is a unique two-stage program that reconnects dropouts and students who have not reached their potential in traditional high schools to education and employment options. Over the next two years, the grantee will provide leadership development opportunities and technical assistance activities to schools within the Diploma Plus network. This renewal will also enable the grantee to support capacity-building aspects of the Pathways to Success by 21 initiative, a statewide effort co-convened by the Commonwealth Corporation and the Massachusetts Department of Education to encourage similar program models.

title: General Purposes
description: The Community Foundation Network, a membership organization of community foundations in the United Kingdom, supports the development and expansion of community foundations by providing technical assistance, training, data collection, research, marketing, financial assistance and advocacy.This grant will enable the network to implement national standards for community foundations and manage a $90 million, 10-year program to help community foundations work in disadvantaged communities.Currently, there are 56 network members covering 94 percent of the United Kingdom. Collectively, these community foundations provided more than $100 million in grants in 2005.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides important general purpose support to the Community Foundation Network, a membership organization of community foundations in the United Kingdom. The Community Foundation Network has supported the development and expansion of community foundations over the past 17 years by providing technical assistance, training, data collection, research, marketing, financial assistance, and advocacy. Over the next two years, the grantee will focus on increasing the profile of community foundations, managing programs that strengthen the network’s delivery capacity, improving the network’s effectiveness and efficiency, and upgrading its information technology systems. Currently, there are 56 network members covering 94 percent of the United Kingdom. Collectively, these community foundations provided over $150 million in grants in 2007, and their endowment assets now exceed $400 million.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant increase provides additional support to the Community Foundation Network, a membership organization of community foundations in the United Kingdom, to further develop a new initiative to boost sustainability of community foundations. The grantee has supported the development and expansion of community foundations over the past 17 years by providing technical assistance, training, data collection, research, marketing, financial assistance, and advocacy. In addition to its regular activities, the Community Foundation Network will sponsor an in-depth workshop on philanthropy advice and building donor relationships for community foundation practitioners from the United Kingdom, Europe, and Russia.

title: General Purposes
description: The Community Foundation Network is a membership organization of community foundations in the United Kingdom. It has supported the development and expansion of community foundations over the past 19 years by providing technical assistance, training, data collection, research, marketing, financial assistance, and advocacy. Over the next two years, the grantee will focus on providing services that will generate new funding, enable more effective work through collaboration and better use of technology, and share learning within the United Kingdom and internationally. Currently, there are 57 network members covering 98 percent of the United Kingdom. Collectively, these community foundations provided approximately $90 million in grants in 2008-2009, and their endowment assets exceed $250 million.

title: General Purposes
description: The Community Foundation Network is a membership organization of community foundations in the United Kingdom. It has supported the development and expansion of community foundations over the past 20 years by providing technical assistance, training, data collection, research, marketing, financial assistance, and advocacy. Recently, the grantee has focused its efforts on services that generate new funding, enable more effective work through collaboration and better use of technology, and share learning within the United Kingdom and internationally. Currently, there are 57 network members covering 98 percent of the United Kingdom. Collectively, these community foundations provided approximately $120 million in grants in 2009-2010, and their endowment assets exceed $400 million. With this grant increase, the grantee will organize events connected to a Worldwide Initiatives for Grantmaker Support meeting in London.

title: General Purposes
description: The Community Foundation Network is a membership organization of community foundations in the United Kingdom. Over the next two years, the grantee will focus on delivering and developing core services to its members, establishing a ventures capacity to encourage innovation among members, and developing projects that enhance the leadership of the network and its members. Currently, there are 57 network members. Collectively, these community foundations provided approximately $95 million in grants in 2010-2011, and their endowment assets exceed $430 million.

title: General Purposes
description: UK Community Foundations is a membership organization of community foundations in the United Kingdom. It has supported the development and expansion of community foundations over the past 23 years by providing technical assistance, training, data collection, research, marketing, financial assistance, and advocacy. Over the next two years, the grantee will focus on a range of activities, including uniting the community foundation movement around a shared strategy for accelerating growth; increasing the network’s efficiency, effectiveness, and accountability through member services; and building its own sustainability. Currently, there are 48 network members. Collectively, these community foundations provided approximately $255 million in grants during the past year, and their endowment assets exceeded $640 million in 2013.

description: UK Community Foundations is a membership organization of community foundations in the United Kingdom. Over the next two years, the grantee will focus on developing strategic communications and a more robust policy role, growing a stronger and more cohesive network of community foundations, and building its own sustainability. Currently, there are 48 network members. Collectively, these community foundations distributed 21,000 grants totaling over $90 million in 2015, and their endowment assets exceeded $650 million.

title: General Purposes
description: UK Community Foundations is a membership organization of 46 community foundations across the United Kingdom. It has supported the development and expansion of community foundations over the past 27 years by providing technical assistance, training, data collection, research, marketing, financial assistance, and advocacy. Over the next two years, the grantee will focus on growing a stronger and more cohesive network, reaching target audiences, and building its own sustainability. In 2017, the network members collectively distributed £77 million in grants and reached 4.7 million people across the United Kingdom.

title: General Purposes
grantee: CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation
description: CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation is an international alliance of civil society organizations committed to strengthening citizen action and civil society globally. Since its establishment more than a decade ago, it has gained respect as the leading international network promoting the development of civil society throughout the world.This grant will enable CIVICUS to build on its previous work and expand its programs and activities to achieve greater impact. In particular, CIVICUS will endeavor to consolidate and enhance its core organizational capacities and systems in order to ensure its effectiveness and sustainability.

title: General Purposes
grantee: CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation
description: CIVICUS is an international alliance dedicated to strengthening citizen action and civil society globally. This grant continues general purposes support to enable CIVICUS to enhance its core organizational systems and structures; undertake a comprehensive strategic and operational planning process for 2008-2012; and continue with the implementation of its various programs: Civil Society Index, Civil Society Watch, the CIVICUS World Assembly, Knowledge Development and Dissemination, and Participatory Governance. The grant will also assist CIVICUS with a succession planning process for a new Secretary General.

title: General Purposes
grantee: CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation
description: Established in 1993, CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation is an international alliance dedicated to strengthening citizen action and civil society globally. Recent achievements include hosting the secretariat of the Global Call to Action Against Poverty; producing regular electronic newsletters and reports on a range of issues affecting civil society; coordinating a systemic action-research program to investigate the state of civil society in more than 50 countries; facilitating research and learning of civil society governance standards and practices; and organizing an annual CIVICUS World Assembly, which brought together over 900 civil society practitioners and activists from around the globe in 2007. The grantee will continue its programs and activities in 2008, with a focus on finalizing and implementing a new Strategic Framework for 2008-2012 and ensuring a smooth transition in leadership.

title: General Purposes
grantee: CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation
description: This grant renewal provides general purpose support for CIVICUS, an international alliance established in 1993 dedicated to strengthening citizen action and civil society worldwide. Membership currently includes representatives from over 100 countries. Key partners at the global level include United Nations agencies, academic institutions, and many large international development organizations. The grantee also has consultative status with global and regional bodies such as World Bank and the Council of Europe. Key programs include: a) the Civil Society Index, a systematic action research program on the state of civil society in more than 50 countries; b) the annual World Assembly, which brought together more than 750 participants in 2008; and c) Civil Society Watch, a program that mobilizes quick, public responses to situations where the right to freedom of civic association is threatened. CIVICUS also has programs on participatory governance, development cooperation and aid effectiveness, and legitimacy, transparency, and accountability.

title: General Purposes
grantee: CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation
description: This grant renewal provides general purpose support for CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation, an international alliance established in 1993 to strengthen citizen action and civil society worldwide. Membership currently includes representatives from over 100 countries. Some of the grantee’s major programs are: 1) Civil Society Index, a research program on the state of civil society in more than 50 countries; 2) Every Human Has Rights awareness-raising and education campaign; and 3) Civil Society Watch, a program that mobilizes quick, public responses to situations where the freedom of civic association is threatened. CIVICUS also has programs on participatory governance; supporting national nonprofit associations; and legitimacy, transparency, and accountability. In 2009, it launched the Eurasia International Digital Exchange and Advocacy Network to support civil society in several former Soviet countries. Major activities in 2010 include organizing a World Assembly, releasing a new Civil Society Index report, and partnering with the United Nations Development Program.

title: General Purposes
grantee: CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation
description: Established in 1993, CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation is an international alliance dedicated to strengthening citizen action and civil society throughout the world. With members from 129 countries, the grantee’s work includes researching the state of civil society in more than 50 countries, raising awareness and education about civil society; and mobilizing quick, public responses to situations where the freedom of civic association is threatened. Of particular note in 2010 was the passage of a Special Resolution on the Freedom of Association and Assembly by the United Nations Human Rights Council, largely due to the efforts of CIVICUS; and the publication of a seminal report on global trends in civil society entitled “Civil Society: The Clampdown is Real.” In 2011, the grantee will continue to strengthen civil society by working to protect civil society rights; promoting good practices within the civil society sector; and influencing government, international institutions, and private sector policies and practices.

title: General Purposes
grantee: CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation
description: Established in 1993, CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation is an international alliance dedicated to strengthening citizen action and civil society throughout the world. With members from 129 countries, the grantee’s work includes researching the state of civil society in more than 50 countries, raising awareness and education about civil society; and mobilizing quick, public responses to situations where the freedom of civic association is threatened. In 2011, the grantee has continued to strengthen civil society by working to protect civil society rights; promoting good practices within the civil society sector; and influencing government, international institutions, and private sector policies and practices. This grant increase will provide partial support to a workshop, which will launch the South African Forum on International Solidarity. The workshop will be attended by approximately 100 delegates. The forum will subsequently give opportunities for civil society input to South Africa’s foreign policy on major global issues.

title: General Purposes
grantee: CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation
description: Established in 1993, CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation is an international alliance dedicated to strengthening citizen action and civil society throughout the world. With partners in over 100 countries, the grantee’s work includes researching the state of civil society; raising awareness and education about civil society; and mobilizing quick, public responses to situations where civil society is threatened. Major activities in 2011 included the CIVICUS World Assembly with 800 participants from 98 countries, the establishment of the Lifeline Fund to assist civic organizations under threat, the completion of the Civil Society Index in 35 countries, and the launch of the South Africa Forum for International Solidarity. In 2012, some major planned activities include the production of the 2012 Global Report on the State of Civil Society, the development and piloting of a new Civil Society Index Rapid Assessment tool, and the compilation of resources on a new generation of civil society self-regulation mechanisms.

title: General Purposes
grantee: CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation
description: This renewal grant provides general purpose support for CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation, an international alliance established in 1993 dedicated to strengthening citizen action and civil society worldwide. The grantee’s membership currently includes over 1,000 representatives from more than 100 countries. Its work includes researching the state of civil society; raising awareness and education about civil society; and mobilizing quick, public responses to situations where civil society is threatened. Major activities in 2012 included the publication of the State of Civil Society 2011 report, a World Assembly with 642 participants from 100 countries, and a participatory planning process leading to new 2013-2017 strategic directions. The grantee’s new strategic priorities for the next five years will focus on connecting different sources of citizen action, fostering the best possible enabling environment for civil society, and ensuring the maximum influence of civil society on global decisions.

title: General Purposes
grantee: CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation
description: This grant renewal provides general purpose support for CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation, an international alliance established in 1993 dedicated to strengthening citizen action and civil society worldwide. The grantee currently has 1,100 members from 121 countries. Key partners at the global level include United Nations agencies, academic institutions, and many large international development organizations. The grantee also has consultative status with global and regional bodies such as World Bank and the Council of Europe. The grantee’s programmatic work entails knowledge generation and analysis (such as the annual State of Civil Society report and the Enabling Environment Index), communications, convening, and advocacy. The grantee also has programs on participatory governance, development cooperation, and aid effectiveness, as well as legitimacy, transparency, and accountability of civil society organizations.

title: General Purposes
grantee: CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation
description: Established in 1993, CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation is an international alliance working to strengthen citizen action and civil society throughout the world, especially in areas where participatory democracy and citizens’ freedom of association are challenged. It works with members in over 145 countries to strengthen civil society. This grant renewal will continue to provide general purpose support to create opportunities for collaborative knowledge generation and collective reflection among members; build partnerships with global leaders in technology to bring the latest tools to help members connect, interact, and engage in global dialogue; and participate in notable international fora to advance the interests of civil society in global discourse and to effect change in areas of pressing global concern like climate change, financial reform, and sustainable development.

title: General Purposes
grantee: CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation
description: Established in 1993, CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation is an international alliance working to strengthen citizen action and civil society throughout the world, especially in areas where participatory democracy and citizens’ freedom of association are challenged. It works with members in over 145 countries to strengthen civil society. The grantee strives to create opportunities for collaborative knowledge generation and collective reflection among members; build partnerships with global leaders in technology to bring the latest tools to help members connect, interact, and engage in global dialogue; and participate in notable international fora to advance the interests of civil society in global discourse and to affect change in areas of pressing global concern like climate change, financial reform, and sustainable development. This grant increase will provide additional support for the 2016 International Civil Society Week and the CIVICUS World Assembly, which will be held in April 2016 in Bogota, Colombia.

title: General Purposes
grantee: CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation
description: Established in 1993, CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation is an international alliance of 3,700 members in 175 countries. Its mission is to strengthen civil society and citizen participation throughout the world, especially in areas where participatory democracy and citizens’ freedom of association are challenged. Recent accomplishments include: the hosting of a World Assembly and International Civil Society Week in Colombia in 2016; the release of annual State of Civil Society reports; and the launch of the CIVICUS Monitor, a new research tool to share reliable, timely data and analysis on civic space. This grant renewal will support CIVICUS’ development and implementation of a new 2017-2022 strategic plan, which will be finalized in July 2017. The alliance’s areas of work are likely to include strengthening of civil society by addressing capacity needs, protecting and promoting civic space through research and advocacy, and supporting citizen inclusion in global agreements.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides support to the Council on Foundations, a national membership organization of private foundations, community foundations, and corporate funders that encourage philanthropy in both the U.S. and internationally.Since its establishment in 1949, the council has served as a resource and advocate for philanthropic organizations throughout the country. The council is recognized as the organization that represents the voice of a broad spectrum of foundations.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purposes support to the Council on Foundations, a national membership organization of private foundations, community foundations, and corporate funders. The Council on Foundations is dedicated to promoting, strengthening, and enhancing services to support the field of philanthropy in both the United States and internationally. Since its establishment, the Council on Foundations has served as a resource and advocate for philanthropic organizations throughout the country. Throughout the field, the council is recognized as the organization that represents the voice of a broad spectrum of foundations.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purposes support to the Council on Foundations, a national membership organization of private foundations, community foundations, and corporate funders. The Council on Foundations is dedicated to promoting, strengthening, and enhancing services to support the field of philanthropy in both the United States and internationally. Since its establishment, the Council on Foundations has served as a resource and advocate for philanthropic organizations throughout the country. Throughout the field, the council is recognized as the organization that represents the voice of a broad spectrum of foundations. This grant increase will help support several new initiatives in communications, public policy, and research.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to the Council on Foundations, a national membership organization of private foundations, community foundations, and corporate funders. The council is dedicated to promoting, strengthening, and enhancing services to support the field of philanthropy in both the United States and internationally. Since its establishment in 1958, the council has served as a resource and advocate for philanthropic organizations. Throughout the field, the council is recognized as the main organization that represents the voice of a broad spectrum of foundations in the United States.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued general purpose support to the Council on Foundations, a national membership organization of private foundations, community foundations, and corporate funders. The grantee is dedicated to promoting, strengthening, and enhancing services to support the field of philanthropy in both the United States and internationally. Since its establishment in 1958, the council has served as a resource and advocate for philanthropic organizations throughout the country. The Council on Foundations is recognized throughout the field as the voice of a broad spectrum of foundations.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides renewal support to the Council on Foundations, a national membership organization of more than 1,800 private foundations, community foundations, and corporate funders. The council’s work on behalf of philanthropy includes government relations and advocacy, communications, standard-setting, learning opportunities, research, legal expertise, convenings, and sector leadership. In 2009, the council adopted a three-year plan that focuses on the following strategic priorities: 1) promoting philanthropy; 2) ensuring essential service delivery; 3) increasing the philanthropic infrastructure’s collective impact; 4) supporting foundation leaders; and 5) building an effective organization. Last year’s highlights included developing strong relationships with government, having more than 4,000 attendees at various educational events, and launching a strategic alliance with the Forum of Regional Associations of Grantmakers. Key activities in 2010 will include expanding the council’s Public-Private Partnership Initiative, developing an integrated knowledge management system, coordinating the Global Philanthropic Leadership Initiative, and strengthening its internal evaluation process.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides renewal support to the Council on Foundations, a national membership organization of more than 1,800 private foundations, community foundations, and corporate funders. The grantee’s work on behalf of philanthropy includes government relations and advocacy, communications, standard-setting, learning opportunities, research, legal expertise, convenings, and sector leadership. Currently, the grantee focuses on the following strategic priorities: 1) promoting philanthropy; 2) ensuring essential service delivery; 3) increasing the collective impact of the philanthropic infrastructure; 4) supporting foundation leaders; and 5) building an effective organization. Recent accomplishments include coalition-building with other philanthropic associations, the Global Philanthropy Leadership Initiative, and the Public-Philanthropic Partnership Initiative. In 2012-2013, the grantee will focus on maintaining strong government relations and legal services, improving knowledge resources, growing membership with a focus on mid-sized foundations, enhancing the ability to connect members, and developing a stable infrastructure.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides renewal support to the Council on Foundations, a national membership organization of more than 1,700 private foundations, community foundations, and corporate funders. The grantee’s work on behalf of philanthropy includes government relations and advocacy, communications, standard-setting, learning opportunities, research, legal expertise, convenings, and sector leadership. Achievements over the past couple of years include key involvement in the charitable giving coalition, graduating a cohort of prospective philanthropic leaders in its career pathways program, and developing the Global Grantmaking Institute. Over the next two years, the grantee will focus on the following four strategies: 1) delivering excellent member stewardship; 2) providing field and thought leadership that enables and promotes giving; 3) strengthening the grantee’s brand and reputation; and 4) building a resilient organization.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides renewal support to the Council on Foundations, a national membership organization of more than 700 private foundations, community foundations, and corporate funders. The grantee’s mission is to provide the opportunity, leadership, and tools needed by philanthropic organizations to expand, enhance, and sustain their ability to advance the common good. Its near-term organizational goals are to: 1) position the council as a strategic leader that advances effective and dynamic philanthropy; 2) build and cultivate a collaborative and diverse philanthropic network; 3) continue to grow an effective and nimble organizational structure, grounded in sound financial systems and processes; and 4) foster a creative, collaborative, and entrepreneurial internal culture that encourages individual investment that lends to the collective success of the grantee.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides renewal support to the Council on Foundations, a national membership organization representing over 1,000 private foundations, community foundations, and corporate funders. The grantee’s mission is to provide the opportunity, leadership, and tools needed by philanthropic organizations to expand, enhance, and sustain their ability to advance the common good. Their top-level organizational goals are to amplify the work of philanthropy, advocate for philanthropy, and strengthen the philanthropic sector. The grantee focuses its value to members within the following broad areas of work: government relations; legal affairs; member engagement; diversity, equity, and inclusion; leadership development; and research.

title: General Purposes
description: The Council of Michigan Foundations provides services for Michigan grantmakers and promotes philanthropy throughout the state. It helps grantmakers share ideas, expertise and experiences; advocates for the needs of grantmakers at the local, state and national levels; and supports the increase of philanthropic resources in the state. This grant increase will assist with staff costs and consulting costs related to strengthening membership services and collaborative work within the philanthropic sector.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant continues Mott’s membership in and general purposes support to the Council of Michigan Foundations. For its more than 400 members, the council provides educational programs, technical assistance, networking opportunities, advocacy with policymakers and regulators, and collaborative work with leading national and regional philanthropic associations across the country. Highlights of accomplishments in 2006 include launching the Essential Skills for New Grantmakers program, helping more than 35 community foundations meet national standards, initiating a corporate-community involvement teleconference series, and assisting the state of Michigan in launching the Early Childhood Investment Corporation.

title: General Purposes
description: The Council of Michigan Foundations is an organization that provides its members with educational programs, technical assistance, networking opportunities, advocacy with policymakers and regulators, and collaborative work with leading national and regional philanthropic associations. Highlights of activities in 2008 include hosting the council’s 36th annual conference, completing and disseminating research on federal excise tax to policymakers, and collaborating to design the national community foundation standards recompliance process. Over the next two years, the council’s significant activities will include working to develop strategies for grantmaking in growth management and urban revitalization, commissioning research on sustainable payout for foundations, and continuing its core operations and programs.

title: General Purposes
description: The Council of Michigan Foundations provides its members with educational programs, technical assistance, networking opportunities, advocacy with policymakers and regulators, and collaborative work with leading national and regional philanthropic associations across the country. This grant increase will support the role of the Council of Michigan Foundations in planning the 2010 convening of the Great Lakes Funders, which will meet in Traverse City, Michigan.

title: General Purposes
description: The Council of Michigan Foundations is a statewide association of grantmakers that provides its members with educational programs, technical assistance, networking opportunities, advocacy with policymakers and regulators, and collaborative work with leading national and regional philanthropic associations. Highlights in 2010 include offering 103 different educational programs for members, hosting the Michigan Land and Prosperity Summit, and organizing a strong Michigan delegation to the annual Foundations on the Hill event. Over 2011-2012, the grantee will focus on membership engagement and retention, new member recruitment, and organizational capacity through pursuing four main objectives: 1) advocacy for legislative goals; 2) operating a networked learning community; 3) supporting membership collaboration on critical issues; and 4) operating a model regional association. The grantee will also continue to host the Office of Foundation Liaison, work with Michigan’s governor to establish an Office of Urban and Metropolitan Initiatives, and support the Michigan Land Use Funders Group.

title: General Purposes
description: The Council of Michigan Foundations is a statewide association of grantmakers that provides its members with educational programs, technical assistance, networking opportunities, advocacy with policymakers and regulators, and collaborative work with leading national and regional philanthropic associations. Recently, the grantee has been focusing on membership engagement and retention, new member recruitment, and organizational capacity through pursuing four main objectives: 1) advocacy on legislative goals; 2) operating a networked learning community; 3) supporting membership collaboration on critical issues; and 4) operating a model regional association. The grantee continues to host a number of initiatives including the Office of Foundation Liaison, the Office of Urban and Metropolitan Initiatives, and the Michigan Land Use Funders Group. The grantee also organizes an annual conference. This grant increase will support a joint conference in the fall of 2012 for Michigan foundations and nonprofits, which will be co-organized by the grantee and the Michigan Nonprofit Association.

title: General Purposes
description: The Council of Michigan Foundations is a statewide association of more than 330 grantmakers that provides its members with educational programs, technical assistance, networking opportunities, advocacy with policymakers and regulators, and collaborative work with leading national and regional philanthropic associations. Highlights in 2012 include customized technical assistance for 179 members, an intergenerational toolkit for family foundations, the peer action learning network on diversity and inclusion, and a successful 40th anniversary conference held jointly with the Michigan Nonprofit Association. During 2013-2014, the grantee will focus on: 1) member services through addressing recruiting and engagement, knowledge and innovation initiatives, learning services, supporting organizations, and convening/networking services; and 2) organizational capacity by building leadership, organizational and people management effectiveness.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant increase is for the general purposes of the Council of Michigan Foundations and is expected to be used to support two special projects of interest to environmental funders interested in Great Lakes and land-use issues.

title: General Purposes
description: The Council of Michigan Foundations is a statewide association of more than 330 grantmakers that provides its members with educational programs, technical assistance, networking opportunities, advocacy with policymakers and regulators, and collaborative work with leading national and regional philanthropic associations. Highlights in 2014 include offering 92 learning programs with 2,708 program attendees, robust government relations to protect and improve the policy environment for philanthropy on both state and national levels, a 93 percent member renewal rate, and meaningful partnerships with a multitude of philanthropic and nonprofit sector infrastructure organizations. During 2015-2016, the grantee will focus on membership recruitment, retention, engagement, diversification, and perception; provision of advocacy and learning services; strategic partnerships and greater philanthropy engagement; the integration of inclusion and equity throughout the organization; updating its governance structure; and enhancing its financial sustainability. The grantee will also provide impact investing hub services.

title: General Purposes
description: The Council of Michigan Foundations is a statewide association of more than 300 grantmakers that provides its members with educational programs, technical assistance, networking opportunities, advocacy with policymakers and regulators, and collaborative work with leading national and regional philanthropic associations. During 2015-2016, the grantee has focused on membership recruitment, retention, engagement, diversification, and perception, provision of advocacy and learning services, strategic partnerships and greater philanthropy engagement, the integration of inclusion and equity throughout the organization; updating its governance structure, and enhancing its financial sustainability. This grant increase will support the research and design phase of a program to support community foundations in Michigan as they serve in a leadership role for clean energy transition in their communities. Additional funds will also support the participation of senior council staff on the board of the Worldwide Initiatives for Grantmaker Support, a global philanthropy association network.

title: General Purposes
description: The Council of Michigan Foundations is a statewide association of more than 300 grantmakers that provides its members with educational programs, technical assistance, networking opportunities, advocacy with policymakers and regulators, and collaborative work with leading national and regional philanthropic associations. With previous Mott support, the grantee focused on growing and engaging its membership, supporting statewide and regional funder collaborations; and taking steps to strengthen its organizational capacity. This grant increase will help the grantee support the Great Lakes Funder Collaboration’s annual meeting in Flint, Michigan, which will include two networking events for foundations, nonprofit representatives, and other local leaders.

title: General Purposes
description: The Council of Michigan Foundations is a statewide association of 300 grantmakers that provides its members with educational programs, technical assistance, networking opportunities, advocacy with policymakers and regulators, and collaborative work with leading national and regional philanthropic associations. Highlights from 2016-2017 include the offering of more than 100 learning programs in which 208 foundations participated, working with partners to protect and improve the policy environment for philanthropy on both state and national levels, a 94 percent membership retention rate, and meaningful partnerships with a multitude of philanthropic and nonprofit sector infrastructure organizations. During 2017-2019, the grantee will pursue eight strategies: 1) engaging members where they want to be; 2) strategically recruiting new members; 3) connecting members to the assistance they need; 4) conducting active internal evaluation and assessment; 5) growing the sector’s collective voice in public policy; 6) expanding diversity, equity, and inclusion of the sector; 7) nurturing mission-aligned social enterprise opportunities; and 8) achieving organizational effectiveness.

title: General Purposes
description: The Umtapo Centre provides training, education and capacity building in the areas of peace, human rights, race relations and reconciliation. Since its establishment, the center has worked mainly in the KwaZulu-Natal province, a region that has been wracked by interethnic and racial violence. Increasingly, it has focused on youth and young people in schools, inculcating values of tolerance, peace and respect for diversity.This grant will enable the center to continue and broaden its interventions and training programs, building on lessons learned to work with youth and communities in other parts of the country. In particular, it will focus on teachers and educators in schools and advocate for peace and antiracism education to be integrated into the school curriculum.Recent activities included establishing and providing support for youth peace centers in communities in KwaZulu-Natal; organizing an annual competition in schools to promote peace, tolerance and reconciliation; providing training and capacity building in community mobilization and advocacy to ensure that people understand and can access their rights; developing resource tools and media on peace, human rights and antiracism practice; and publishing a quarterly newsletter focusing on the challenges of building a nonracial society.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purpose support to the Umtapo Centre. The cornerstone of the centre’s work is its Peace, Human Rights, and Antiracism Education program, which engages large numbers of people, particularly youth, to create awareness and mobilize against violence and racism. Over the next year, the Umtapo Centre will consolidate its peace and antiracism resource centers into 30 schools nationally; produce three newsletters; complete two, five-day Peace, Human Rights, and Antiracism Education program training courses; conduct an impact assessment of the program; and develop an endowment fund and explore other sustainability options.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purpose support to the Umtapo Centre. The cornerstone of the centre’s work is its Peace, Human Rights, and Anti-racism Education program, which engages people throughout South Africa, particularly youth in disadvantaged schools and communities, to create awareness and mobilize against violence and racism. Over the next two years, the grantee will set up an alumni association, establish an education task force, conduct several Peace, Human Rights, and Anti-racism Education training courses, prepare various promotional materials, produce a documentary, launch additional resource centers, convene a national conference, and conduct a national evaluation workshop.

title: General Purposes
description: Umtapo Centre builds the leadership capacity of children, the youth, and community leaders to engage in critical dialogue on issues of peace, rights and responsibilities, and citizenship. Past support from Mott enabled the grantee to train youth in schools on peace and antiracism; set up peace resource centers in schools; establish an alumni association for former participants in its programs; conduct several peace, human rights, and antiracism education training courses for out-of-school youth and community leaders; prepare various promotional materials; produce a documentary on Ubuntu, an African value-based way of life; and convene a national conference on Ubuntu, antiracism, antixenophobia, and moral regeneration. This grant will continue to provide general purpose support to the grantee to implement its peace and antiracism programs.

title: General Purposes
description: Umtapo Centre implements programs that empower youth, community leaders, and women to better understand issues of peace, human rights, and antiracism in South Africa. It uses participatory popular education to create awareness and encourages communities to be involved in issues that impact their lives. Past support from Mott enabled the grantee to support the formation of peace forums for young people of different age groups, produce a quarterly newsletter which also serves as a conversation starter on various topics related to human rights, and support communities to set up self-help projects. This grant will provide general purpose support to the grantee to continue implementing programs that empower youth and communities; encourage self-reliance; and promote the principles of Ubuntu, an African philosophy that promotes humanity toward others. The grantee will also continue to build strong partnerships locally and internationally with institutions that promote the same principles.

title: General Purposes
description: Umtapo Centre provides education and training programs that promote peace, human rights, and antiracism to young people, community-based organizations, and community leaders in South Africa. It establishes peace clubs in schools and universities to build a youth leadership founded on a democratic, human rights-based culture. Past support has enabled the grantee to conduct workshops in poor communities on antiracism and peace, introduce peace clubs in schools and other areas where young people converge, and establish peace clubs at universities. This grant will allow the grantee to continue promoting peace and antiracism by providing training to youth in schools and universities, conducting awareness-raising workshops in communities, and producing educational publications. It will also introduce advice desks in all its offices to respond to human rights and anticorruption issues and strengthen partnerships with like-minded institutions locally and abroad.

title: General Purposes
description: The Umtapo Centre works to promote peace, human rights, and anti-racism education among young people and community leaders in South Africa. It provides training on topics related to peace building, hosts dialogues and campaigns to raise awareness on human rights issues, and establishes peace movements of young people in schools and universities. Past support enabled the grantee to host workshops on a variety of topics including corruption and governance, support the peace clubs and youth forums in schools on their program activities, and host dialogues on peace and anti-racism. This grant will enable the grantee to host training workshops on topics including anti-racism, anti-corruption, women and child protection, and consciousness building for self-reliance. The grantee will also partner with other institutions, including community advice offices, to increase access to information.

title: General Purposes
description: Paraprofessional Healthcare Institute (PHI) was created in 1991 as part of an initiative to replicate Cooperative Home Care Associates. PHI has been the key instrument in developing systems and training management and healthcare workers alike on how to increase worker quality and institutional productivity so that direct-care workers can advance to livable-wage employment.This grant will enable PHI to expand its healthcare worker training programs.
