In addition, this grant will strengthen worker benefit advocacy in selected states and nationally while allowing the PHI to disseminate promising practices that result in increasing workers’ productivity and benefits. Efforts are expected to impact 112,500 direct-care workers.

title: General Purposes
description: This general purposes grant will impact more than 120,000 workers through Paraprofessional Healthcare Institute’s direct practice, and many more broadly through its national policy research and advocacy efforts. The support will enable Paraprofessional Healthcare Institute to expand its network of healthcare worker training programs. In addition, this grant will strengthen healthcare worker benefit advocacy in selected states and nationally while allowing Paraprofessional Healthcare Institute to disseminate program outcomes from its Cooperative Healthcare Network and promising practices that resulted in increasing workers’ productivity and benefits.

title: General Purposes
description: This general purpose grant will impact 133,600 direct service healthcare workers through PHI’s direct practice, and many more through its national policy research and advocacy efforts. This support will enable PHI to expand its network of healthcare worker training programs. In addition, this grant will strengthen healthcare worker benefit advocacy in selected states and nationally while allowing PHI to disseminate promising practices that will result in increasing workers’ productivity and benefits.

title: General Purposes
description: This general purpose grant will impact more than 140,000 workers through PHI’s direct practice, and many more through its national policy research and advocacy efforts. The support will enable PHI to expand its network of healthcare worker training programs. In addition, this grant will strengthen healthcare worker benefit advocacy in selected states and nationally, while allowing PHI to disseminate program outcomes from its Cooperative Healthcare Network and promising practices that will result in increasing workers’ productivity and benefits.

title: General Purposes
description: This general purpose grant will impact more than 150,000 workers through PHI’s direct training practice, and many more broadly through its national policy research and advocacy efforts. The support will enable PHI to expand its network of healthcare worker training programs. In addition, this grant will strengthen healthcare worker benefit advocacy in selected states and nationally and promote promising practices that result in increasing workers’ productivity and benefits.

title: General Purposes
description: This general purpose grant will impact more than 120,000 workers through PHI’s direct practice, and many more through its national policy research and advocacy efforts. This grant will enable the grantee to expand its network of healthcare worker training programs. In addition, this grant will strengthen healthcare worker benefit advocacy in selected states and nationally, while allowing the grantee to disseminate program outcomes from its Cooperative Healthcare Network and promising practices that result in increasing workers’ productivity and benefits.

title: General Purposes
description: This general purpose grant will impact more than 267,000 workers through PHI’s direct practice, and many more through its national policy research and advocacy efforts. This support will enable the grantee to expand its network of healthcare worker training programs. In addition, this grant will strengthen healthcare worker benefit advocacy in selected states and nationally. The grantee will also disseminate program outcomes from its Cooperative Healthcare Network and the promising practices that have resulted in increasing workers’ productivity and benefits.

title: General Purposes
description: This general purpose renewal grant will provide continued funding to PHI, a 21-year-old advocacy and employment development organization targeted within the healthcare industry. During this period, the Mott Foundation has provided key support to the organization, which has become a national leader for sectoral workforce development. The current grant will enable the organization to expand its network of healthcare worker training programs and help direct-care workers to obtain sustainable employment. In addition, this grant will strengthen worker benefit advocacy in states and nationally while allowing the grantee to disseminate program outcomes.

title: General Purposes
description: This general purpose renewal grant is a part of a series of tie-off grants to ensure the successful legacy of the Paraprofessional Healthcare Institute. PHI is a 21-year-old advocacy and employment development organization that Mott has supported since it began. Impacting more than 120,000 workers through the grantee’s direct practice, many more are helped through its national policy research and advocacy efforts. This support will enable the grantee to strengthen its network of healthcare worker training programs. In addition, this grant will help test, measure, and articulate a set of strategies that focus on the employment needs of younger workers while allowing the grantee to disseminate program outcomes from its Cooperative Healthcare Network and promising practices that resulted in increasing workers’ productivity and benefits.

title: General Purposes
description: This general purpose renewal grant is part of a series of tie off and transition grants to ensure the successful legacy of PHI and also to help inform the Pathways to Opportunity program’s youth-focused employment and education exploratory efforts. PHI is a 21-year-old advocacy and employment development organization. It targets improving the lives and career advancement opportunities of more than 135,400 direct-care workers each year, including more than 31,200 young adults through its direct practice, national policy research, and advocacy efforts. This general purpose support will enable the grantee to explore the potential for its network of healthcare worker training programs to address the high youth unemployment issues utilizing the health professions as a model. In addition, this grant will help test, measure, and articulate a set of strategies that focus on the employment needs of younger workers while allowing the grantee to disseminate program outcomes from its Cooperative Healthcare Network and promising practices that resulted in increasing workers’ productivity and benefits.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will enable the Justice Alliance Education Fund to build the leadership and staffing capacity of Industrial Areas Foundation-affiliated (IAF) organizations in Oregon and Washington as well as strengthen its ability to provide leadership training and research support to the affiliates.The fund was established in 1990 to provide organizer training, research and coordination of information for organizations in Washington and Oregon that are affiliated with IAF.

title: General Purposes
description: The Justice Alliance Education Fund is a network of community organizations in Washington and Oregon affiliated with the Industrial Areas Foundation. This grant will help build the leadership and staffing capacity of the local organizations and support the continued strengthening of the Justice Alliance Education Fund as a network that provides leadership training and research support to the affiliates.

title: General Purposes
description: IAF Northwest is a network of six affiliated organizing projects in the United States, Canada, and Australia. The purpose of the network is to provide its members with training, technical assistance, research, coordination, consulting services, and to serve as a point of contact between the local affiliates and other Industrial Areas Foundation groups in the United States, Central America, Africa, and Europe. This grant will help build the leadership and staffing capacity of the local organizations and support the continued strengthening of the network to provide leadership training and research support to the affiliates.

title: General Purposes
description: IAF Northwest is a network of six affiliated organizing projects in the United States, Canada, and Australia. The purpose of the grantee is to provide training, technical assistance, research, coordination, and consulting services to each of the member groups, and serve as a point of contact between the local affiliates and other Industrial Areas Foundation groups in the United States, Central America, Africa, and Europe. This general purpose grant will help strengthen the grantee to provide leadership training and research support to the affiliates.

title: State Fiscal Analysis Initiative
description: Funding will enable the Arise Citizens’ Policy Project to focus on building support for comprehensive tax reform in Alabama. Additional priorities include exploring new communication strategies and continuing to expand its base of financial support.During the past two years, the project played an important role in informing and framing public debates on revenue and spending issues and on new and existing policy initiatives in Alabama. This is one of 10 grants supporting the State Fiscal Analysis Initiative. The Arise Citizens’ Policy Project has been involved in this effort since 1993. Mott has also supported the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, which provides technical assistance and networking opportunities for the 35 state organizations participating in this initiative.

title: State Fiscal Analysis Initiative
description: This is one of ten grants recommended to state organizations participating in the State Fiscal Analysis Initiative. The Ford, Annie E. Casey, and Mott Foundations created the initiative in 1992 in order to build state capacity for timely, credible, and accessible tax and budget analysis on behalf of low- and middle-income families. Arise Citizens’ Policy Project joined this effort in 1993 and has successfully incorporated rigorous policy analysis into its core community-organizing activities. During the renewal grant period, the grantee will prepare and disseminate analyses, with a particular emphasis on policies that benefit Alabama’s most vulnerable residents. Other activities planned for the next two years include outreach and strategic communication efforts. Related to this project is a grant to the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, which provides technical assistance to all 36 organizations participating in the initiative.

title: State Fiscal Analysis Initiative
description: The Ford, Casey, and Mott foundations created the State Fiscal Analysis Initiative in 1992 in order to build state capacity for timely, credible, and accessible tax and budget analysis on behalf of low- and middle-income families. The continued devolution of funds and decisionmaking responsibility to the states heightens the need for analyses of fiscal and budget policies at the state level. Arise Citizens’ Policy Project joined the initiative in 1993 and has grown to be a respected voice on policy issues in Alabama. Though a relatively small organization, its work has focused on establishing credibility and building grassroots support for fiscal and low-income population policy issues. Related to this project is a grant to the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, which provides technical assistance to all the state organizations participating in this initiative.

title: State Fiscal Analysis Initiative
description: This is one of ten grants recommended to state organizations participating in the State Fiscal Analysis Initiative. The Ford, Casey, and Mott foundations created the initiative in 1992 in order to build state capacity for timely, credible, and accessible tax and budget analysis on behalf of low- and moderate-income families. Arise Citizens’ Policy Project joined the initiative in 1994 and has grown to be a respected voice on budget and fiscal policy issues in Alabama. During the renewal grant period, the grantee will produce and disseminate analyses on a range of state budget, fiscal, and economic issues, with a particular emphasis on state and local policies with the potential to improve the lives of low-income people. Additional activities planned for the grant period include community outreach and strategic communications. Related to this project is a grant to the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, which analyzes federal budget and tax policy issues and provides technical assistance to the 41 state organizations participating in this initiative.

title: State Fiscal Analysis Initiative
description: This is one of ten grants recommended to state organizations participating in the State Fiscal Analysis Initiative. The Ford, Casey, and Mott foundations created the initiative in 1992 in order to build state capacity for timely, credible, and accessible tax and budget analysis on behalf of low- and moderate-income families. Arise Citizens’ Policy Project joined the initiative in 1994, and has grown to be a respected voice on budget and fiscal policy issues in Alabama. During the grant period, the grantee will produce and disseminate analyses on a range of state budget, fiscal, and economic issues, with a particular emphasis on state and local policies with the potential to improve the lives of low-income people. Additional activities planned for the grant period include community outreach and strategic communications. Related to this project is a grant to the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, which analyzes federal budget and tax policy issues and provides technical assistance to the 41state organizations participating in this initiative.

title: State Fiscal Analysis Initiative
description: This grant increase is one of ten tie-off grants to state organizations participating in the State Priorities Partnership (formerly the State Fiscal Analysis Initiative). The Ford, Annie E. Casey, and Mott foundations created the initiative in 1992 in order to build state capacity for timely, credible, and accessible tax and budget policy analyses on behalf of low- and moderate-income families. Arise Citizens’ Policy Project joined this effort in 1994 and has become recognized as an authoritative source of information and analysis on low-income issues in Alabama. This grant increase will support the grantee’s ongoing analytical and coalition-building efforts, with a particular emphasis on state budget and tax policy as well as low-income programs.

title: General Purposes
description: Funding will enable the Alliance for Nonprofit Management to co-sponsor an annual conference with the National Council of Nonprofit Associations; target its membership marketing campaign; and increase its knowledge about issues critical to the capacity-building field.During the past two years, the alliance increased its membership to 627; launched the Cultural Competency Initiative; and developed draft ethical standards on nonprofit capacity building.The mission of the alliance is to strengthen nonprofit support centers and others that deliver management and governance support services to nonprofit organizations.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued general purpose support to the Alliance for Nonprofit Management to strengthen nonprofit support centers and others that deliver management and governance support services to nonprofit organizations throughout the United States. The organization has grown its membership to over 1,100, and those members are able to reach over 250,000 nonprofits each year. Over the coming grant period, the organization will again co-sponsor an annual conference with the National Council of Nonprofit Associations, target its membership marketing campaign, expand its Cultural Competency Initiative to include diversity factors other than race, and learn extensively about issues critical to the capacity-building field.

title: General Purposes
description: The Alliance for Nonprofit Management is a multidisciplinary network of 1,300 individuals and organizations including management support, academic, professional, and philanthropic organizations dedicated to strengthening the management and performance of nonprofits. Over the years, the alliance has offered and continues to offer a variety of programs and services geared toward promoting professional development of its members, improving the quality and impact of services for nonprofits, and disseminating research on capacity building innovations to the field. In addition to supporting the continuation of programmatic activities, this grant will support the Alliance for Nonprofit Management as it undergoes major organizational transitions. Transition activities will include raising funds and searching for a new executive director; building a new governance structure; and developing a new five-year, self-sustaining business model.

title: General Purposes
description: The Alliance for Nonprofit Management is a multidisciplinary network of over 1,300 individuals and organizations including management support, academic, professional, and philanthropic organizations dedicated to strengthening the management and performance of nonprofits. Over the years, the grantee has offered a variety of programs and services geared toward promoting professional development of its members, improving the quality and impact of services for nonprofits, and disseminating research on capacity building innovations to the field. In addition to supporting the continuation of programmatic activities, this grant will support the grantee as it undergoes major organizational transitions. Transition activities will include raising funds and searching for a new executive director, adopting a new governance structure, and developing a new five-year, self-sustaining business model.

title: General Purposes
description: Kentucky Waterways Alliance is a statewide nonprofit organization working to address water quality and river protection issues. With this general purpose renewal, the alliance will continue efforts to build the capacity of local watershed groups, promote sound clean water policies, and educate the public about freshwater issues. The alliance will also take steps to build its own organizational strength, such as diversifying its revenue base.

title: General Purposes
description: Good Jobs First provides public officials, journalists and advocates with timely and accurate information on best practices in state and local economic development. Its mission is to help ensure that cities and states receive a return on their economic development investments in terms of family-wage jobs and other economically effective results that advance the alleviation of poverty.Multiyear funding will enable the organization to provide continued support to stakeholder groups, with special emphasis on deepening connections with state fiscal groups and with the smart growth/regionalism movement. The work plan also features a national conference and intensive research and publishing efforts. During the past two years, Good Jobs First provided model programs, research, technical assistance and expert testimony to help a broad spectrum of organizations become more effective at designing, implementing and monitoring economic development policies and programs.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant renewal provides partial support to the Workforce Alliance, a practitioner-focused coalition that can insert effective practice and on-the-ground experience into national policy debate about how to move low-income adults into skilled, long-term employment. The Workforce Alliance acts as a central voice for grassroots training practitioners and employers in the national debate about workforce development policy, and serves as a clearinghouse of information for practitioners, employers, and policymakers. Part of its mission is to inspire a sector approach to economic development that would grow state economies by raising local skill levels to attract new firms, build necessary infrastructure within and across industries to support their common expansion, and support workforce-oriented research and development so that local industries can re-tool and compete for new market niches.

title: General Purposes
description: This general purposes grant increase will allow the Workforce Alliance to further pursue its mission to act as a central voice for grassroots training practitioners and employers in the national debate about workforce development policy, and serve as a clearinghouse of information for practitioners, employers, and policymakers.

title: General Purposes
description: The Workforce Alliance is a practitioner-focused coalition that can insert effective practice and on-the-ground experience into national policy debates about how to move low-income adults into skilled, long-term employment. The alliance’s four-point strategy focuses on building a national, multistakeholder network; conducting or encouraging strategic research and analysis; developing communication tools for local workforce advocates; and engaging in direct and grassroots advocacy to inform public policy.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant renewal continues partial support to the National Skills Coalition, a practitioner-focused coalition that inserts effective practice and on-the-ground experience into national policy debates about how to move low-income adults into skilled, long-term employment. The coalition acts as a central voice for grassroots training practitioners and employers in the national debate about welfare-to-work and workforce development policies, and serves as a clearinghouse of information for practitioners, employers, and policymakers. The coalition’s four-point strategy focuses on: building a national, multistakeholder network; conducting or encouraging strategic research and analysis; developing communication tools for local workforce advocates; and engaging in direct and grassroots advocacy to inform public policy.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant increase will help the National Skills Coalition to reach its general purposes budget expectations and raise an additional $600,000 to expand efforts to inform public policy about the benefits of the workforce development field to local workers and employers. This effort will prevent anticipated monetary reductions in skill enhancement training and push for reforms that value job and career development training for the unemployed and underemployed.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will help the National Skills Coalition expand efforts to inform public policy about the benefits of the workforce development field to local workers and employers. This effort will help alleviate anticipated monetary reductions in skill enhancement training for the unemployed and underemployed. The grantee will push for reforms that value career development training.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purpose support to aid the National Skills Coalition, a 3,200-member, multisector coalition of skills development organizations, in its efforts to explore ways to expand its knowledge, expertise, and relationships in the adult workforce development field to inform public policy regarding the education and workforce skills needs of low-income youth. This grant will help the grantee and the adult workforce development field expand and deepen its knowledge base and advance policies that address the education (especially postsecondary) and career training needs and aspirations of low-income youth.

title: Community Involvement Program
description: The Community Involvement Program works with locally-based organizations to build capacity in community organizing so that more low-income parents are engaged in school improvement and school reform efforts. Formerly housed at New York University Institute for Education and Social Policy, the program recently has moved to Brown University’s Annenberg Institute for School Reform.This grant renewal will enable the Community Involvement Program to continue to identify, support, and assess education organizing efforts in New York City.The Annenberg Institute for School Reform works in collaboration with education reform organizations, school districts, school improvement networks and others to develop the capacity of urban communities to build and sustain programs and polices that improve teaching and learning.

title: Community Involvement Program
description: The Community Involvement Program works with community-based organizations to build capacity in community organizing so that more low-income parents are engaged in school improvement and school reform efforts. This grant renewal to Brown University will allow the Community Involvement Program to continue to identify, support, and assess education organizing efforts in New York City.

title: Citizen Engagement in the Lugansk and Donetsk Regions
description: The program goal is to help residents from economically depressed settlements revitalize their communities. During the past five years, the Regional Development Agency “Donbass” has helped engage local community residents and involve them in the renewal of 19 economically depressed settlements in four cities of eastern Ukraine.Funding over the next three years will enable the agency to introduce its community organizing and development approaches to three small towns and three rural districts with populations of up to 100,000 each. Activities will include training community leaders; convening a series of public participation workshops in each location; mapping community needs and resources; identifying key community issues; working with local leaders to design and implement development projects; and promoting citizen participation in community life through various informational channels. The agency also will share its community organizing and development approaches by providing learning opportunities to other development agencies in Ukraine and Belarus.

title: Citizen Engagement in the Lugansk and Donetsk Regions
description: The program goal is to engage residents from economically depressed settlements in eastern Ukraine in revitalizing their communities. Over the next two years, the Regional Development Agency “Donbass” will deepen its community development work in one rural and seven urban population centers in order to strengthen the capacity of leading community-based organizations to effect social change. Activities will include training community leaders, convening public participation workshops, mapping community needs and resources, advising on local development projects, and promoting citizen participation in community life. In the previous grant period, the grantee expanded its efforts to 12 new communities to engage residents in local revitalization efforts through participation in decisionmaking and in the establishment of productive social enterprises. There are now over 30 communities in which it is engaged. Initiated in 1997, the agency supports the implementation of market reforms in the economically depressed Donbass region of eastern Ukraine.

title: Citizen Engagement in the Lugansk and Donetsk Regions
description: The program goal is to engage residents from economically depressed settlements in eastern Ukraine in revitalizing their communities. Over the next two years, the Regional Development Agency “Donbass” will deepen its community development work in provincial population centers in order to strengthen the capacity of leading community-based organizations to effect social change. Activities will include training community leaders, convening public participation workshops, mapping community needs and resources, advising on local development projects, and promoting citizen participation in community life. In the previous grant period, the grantee established six community information centers to foster local civic participation. It facilitated the staging of Citizen Participation Weeks in four target communities as regular events. A new distance learning program focused on social development and participation was also instituted. Initiated in 1997, the grantee supports the implementation of market reforms to assist transformation in the Donbass region of eastern Ukraine.

title: General Purposes
description: The Northwest Federation of Community Organizations was formed in 1993 by four statewide, community-based organizations in Idaho, Washington, Oregon, and Montana to address regional, social, and economic issues impacting their low-income communities. This general purposes grant will assist the federation in building the leadership and organizing infrastructure in the Pacific and Rocky Mountain Northwest to increase economic opportunity in a coordinated manner.

title: General Purposes
description: The Northwest Federation of Community Organizations was formed in 1993 by four statewide, community-based organizations in Idaho, Washington, Oregon, and Montana to address regional social and economic issues impacting their low-income communities. This general purpose grant will assist the federation in continuing to build the leadership and organizational infrastructure to increase civic engagement and expand economic opportunity in the region.

title: General Purposes
description: The Alliance for a Just Society is a network of several statewide community organizations working to address regional social and economic issues impacting low-income communities. This general purpose grant will assist the grantee in building the leadership and organizational infrastructure needed to support organizing groups affiliated with the network.

title: General Purposes
description: The Alliance for a Just Society is a network of several statewide community organizations working to address regional, social, and economic issues impacting low-income communities. This general purpose grant will assist the grantee in building the leadership and organizational infrastructure needed to support organizing groups affiliated with the network.

title: Summer Youth Program
description: Each year, the Summer Youth Program provides funding for up to 30 agencies to operate programs focusing on improving the job skills of Flint area youth and, in selected cases, keeping younger children and youth engaged in safe activities during the summer months.This grant will enable the Genesee Chamber Foundation to continue to develop and implement summer programs that provide education and employment opportunities for approximately 400 Flint area youth ages 14-18, as well as provide productive activity for approximately 4,000 youth between the ages of 5-13 years. The 2006 program will emphasize a systemic approach to workforce development, beginning with career preparation and the creation of educational development plans for each participant; establish stronger partnerships between area employers and the Summer Youth Program; develop an understanding of and support for community service; and provide leadership training designed to connect participants with further leadership development opportunities elsewhere in the community.

title: Summer Youth Initiative and TeenQuest
description: This grant will enable the Genesee Area Focus Fund to provide education and employment opportunities in community service agencies for approximately 400 Flint area youth between the ages of 14 and 18. These teens will serve another 2,500 Flint area youth employed in summer activities. The 2007 program will continue to invest in a systemic approach to workforce development, emphasizing career preparation and promoting personal development and leadership skills for youth. In addition, the Genesee Area Focus Fund will establish a small matching fund to expand employment opportunities in the broader for-profit business community to better attract the participation of the members of the Genesee Regional Chamber of Commerce.

title: Summer Youth Initiative and TeenQuest
description: This grant will enable the Genesee Area Focus Fund to continue to implement the Summer Youth Initiative for Flint area youth. The Summer Youth Initiative provides funding for approximately 25 nonprofit agencies and businesses to employ more than 450 Flint area youth ages 14 through 18 during the summer months. In addition to providing employment, the 2008 Summer Youth Initiative will emphasize developing leadership skills, engaging in volunteerism, and exploring careers. Finally, more than 7,000 children of all ages will be served by the Summer Youth Initiative through the services provided by the agencies employing the teenagers.

title: Summer Youth Initiative and TeenQuest
description: This grant will enable the Genesee Area Focus Fund to continue to develop and implement summer and year-round programs that provide education and employment opportunities for Flint area youth. The Summer Youth Initiative provides funding to area organizations to hire Genesee County teens to work in their respective summer programs. The 2008 Summer Youth Initiative provided funding to 23 nonprofit agencies and local businesses to employ 375 teenagers. The goal for 2009 is to serve 400 teenagers in Genesee County.

title: Summer Youth Initiative and TeenQuest
description: This grant increase will enable the Genesee Area Focus Fund to augment the number of youth served by summer and year-round programs that provide education and employment opportunities for Flint area youth. The Summer Youth Initiative will provide funding to area nonprofits and for-profits to hire 586 Genesee County teens, ages 14-18 and in grades 9-12, to work in their respective summer programs.

title: Summer Youth Initiative and TeenQuest
description: This grant will enable the Genesee Area Focus Fund to continue to develop and implement summer and year-round programs that provide education and employment opportunities for Flint area youth. The Summer Youth Initiative provides funding to area nonprofits and businesses to hire Genesee County teens, ages 14-18 and in grades 9-12, to work in their respective summer programs. The 2009 Summer Youth Initiative provided funding to 22 nonprofit agencies and three local businesses to employ 473 teenagers and 28 college-aged youth as supervisors during the summer of 2009. Another 101 teenagers were employed by 12 nonprofit agencies and 2 local businesses from September through December 2009. The goal for 2010 is to serve 500 teenagers during the summer in Genesee County.

title: Summer Youth Initiative and TeenQuest
description: This grant enables the Genesee Area Focus Fund to implement job training and summer employment opportunities for Flint area youth ages 14-18 and in grades 9-12. The 2011 Summer Youth Initiative provides workforce development training to prepare Flint area teens for summer employment, funding for area nonprofits and businesses to hire teens to work in their respective summer programs, and volunteer opportunities to encourage civic engagement among Flint area youth. The 2010 Summer Youth Initiative funded 19 nonprofit agencies and seven local businesses to employ 395 teenagers and 15 youth supervisors during the summer of 2010. Another 52 teenagers were employed by seven nonprofit agencies from September through December 2010. The grantee’s goal for 2011 is to train and employ 500 teenagers through the Summer Youth Initiative.

title: Summer Youth Initiative and TeenQuest
description: This grant enables the Genesee Area Focus Fund to implement the Summer Youth Initiative, which consists of two primary components — job training and summer employment opportunities. First, eligible Flint area youth ages 14-18 and in grades 9-12 attend the TeenQuest preemployment training program for five weeks at 1 of 20 sites across the county. Upon successful completion of TeenQuest, teenagers apply for summer employment at the Summer Youth Initiative Job Fair. Summer Youth Initiative provides 100 percent of the wages for area nonprofits and 50 percent of the wages for area businesses to hire teens to work at their respective agencies during the summer months. In addition to learning valuable employment skills, the teenagers participate in volunteer opportunities to encourage civic engagement. The 2011 Summer Youth Initiative funded 17 nonprofit agencies and five local businesses to employ 392 teenagers and seven youth supervisors during the summer. The grantee’s goal for 2012 is to train and employ 500 teenagers through the Summer Youth Initiative.

title: Summer Youth Initiative and TeenQuest
description: This grant enables the Genesee Area Focus Fund to implement the Summer Youth Initiative, which consists of two primary components: job training and employment opportunities. Eligible Flint area youth, ages 14-18 and in grades 9-12, attend the TeenQuest five-week, pre-employment training program, which is offered five times throughout the school year. Upon successful completion of the TeenQuest program, area youth apply for summer employment at the Summer Youth Initiative Job Fair. The initiative provides 100 percent of the wages for area nonprofits and 50 percent of the wages for area businesses to hire youth during the summer months. In addition to learning valuable employment skills, the youth participate in volunteer opportunities to encourage civic engagement. The 2012 Summer Youth Initiative funded 19 nonprofit agencies in addition to several local businesses and governmental units to employ 495 youth. The grantee’s goal for 2013 is to train 600 and employ 500 youth through the Summer Youth Initiative.

title: Summer Youth Initiative and TeenQuest
description: This grant provides support to the Genesee Area Focus Fund to implement the Summer Youth Initiative which provides job training and employment opportunities for Genesee County teens in partnership with area nonprofit and for-profit employers. Teens first participate in the TeenQuest component, a five-week pre-employment training program, and then are eligible to apply for employment at the Summer Youth Initiative job fair. While most of the employment opportunities will still be offered in the summer, the program will transition in 2014 to being more intentional about providing year-round employment options where available.

title: Summer Youth Initiative and TeenQuest
description: This grant provides support to the Genesee Area Focus Fund to implement the Summer Youth Initiative which provides job training and employment opportunities for Genesee County teens in partnership with area nonprofit employers. Teens first participate in the TeenQuest component, a five-week pre-employment training program, and then are eligible to apply for employment at the Summer Youth Initiative job fair. While most of the employment opportunities are offered in the summer, the program also provides year-round employment options where available.

title: Summer Youth Initiative and TeenQuest
description: This grant provides support to the Genesee Area Focus Fund to implement Summer Youth Initiative and TeenQuest, which provides job training and employment opportunities for Genesee County teens in partnership with area employers. Teens first participate in the TeenQuest component, a five-week pre-employment training program, and then are eligible to apply for employment at the Summer Youth Initiative job fair. Programs such as this are particularly necessary in Flint given its current water crisis, because educational and enrichment opportunities are important interventions for teens to help mitigate the long-term impacts of such exposure.

title: Summer Youth Initiative and TeenQuest
description: This grant provides support to the Genesee Area Focus Fund to implement TeenQuest and the Summer Youth Initiative, which provide job training and employment opportunities for Genesee County teens in partnership with area employers. Teens participate in TeenQuest, a pre-employment training program, and then are eligible to apply for employment through the Summer Youth Initiative. Programs such as this are particularly necessary in Flint, given its current water crisis because educational and enrichment opportunities are important interventions for teens to help mitigate the long-term impacts of such exposure.

title: Summer Youth Initiative and TeenQuest
description: This grant provides support to the Genesee Area Focus Fund to implement TeenQuest and the Summer Youth Initiative, which provide job training and employment opportunities for Genesee County teens in partnership with area employers. Teens participate in TeenQuest, a pre-employment training program, and then are eligible to apply for employment through the Summer Youth Initiative. Programs like these are particularly important as Flint responds to the water crisis because educational and enrichment opportunities are important interventions for children and teens to help mitigate the potential long-term impacts of lead exposure.

title: Summer Youth Initiative and TeenQuest
description: This grant provides support to the Genesee Area Focus Fund to implement TeenQuest and the Summer Youth Initiative, which provide job training and employment opportunities for Genesee County teens in partnership with area employers. Teens participate in TeenQuest, a pre-employment training program, and are then eligible to apply for employment through the Summer Youth Initiative. Programs like these are particularly important as Flint continues to respond to the water crisis because educational and enrichment opportunities are crucial interventions for children and teens to help mitigate potential long-term impacts of lead exposure.

title: Community Engagement with Local Government
grantee: Trust for Community Outreach and Education
description: The Trust for Community Outreach and Education focuses on land and local governance issues mostly with remote, rural communities. It works through eight regional affiliates across the three provinces of the Western Cape, Eastern Cape and Limpopo. This grant will enable the trust to strengthen the capacity of target communities to participate in local government processes, especially in view of the upcoming local government elections; work to ensure that municipalities are responsive to the needs of communities and that they create the space for communities to participate in planning processes; build the capacity of staff, local leadership and community-based organizations to engage meaningfully and with skill in local government processes; and facilitate access to basic services like water and electricity and access to markets for farm dwellers, farmer associations and producer groups.Activities during the past three years included encouraging the establishment of community development forums to address community concerns; developing the capacity of community-based organizations to understand the different aspects, roles and responsibilities of local government; disseminating information on the role of municipalities in providing free basic services to communities; and assisting various community groups to gain access to basic services, particularly water and infrastructure.

title: Community Engagement with Local Government
grantee: Trust for Community Outreach and Education
description: The Trust for Community Outreach and Education works with mainly rural communities in the Eastern Cape, Western Cape, and Limpopo provinces assisting them in organizing into formal structures through which they are able to engage government entities that have a mandate to provide various services to them. The aim is to assist these communities to access their rights and improve their livelihoods. It works through eight regional affiliates across the three provinces. Past Mott support has strengthened the capacity of target communities to participate in local government processes and to ensured that municipalities are responsive to their needs and created the space for community participation in local planning processes. This grant will support the Trust for Community Outreach and Education to continue to work with poor communities on issues related to local government, land, and local economic development. It will continue to assist rural communities to participate in the development of municipal plans and to develop local economic development programs that will help improve their livelihoods.

title: Community Engagement with Local Government
grantee: Trust for Community Outreach and Education
description: The Trust for Community Outreach and Education is a national organization that is made up of seven regional affiliates working mainly with rural communities in Limpopo and the Eastern, Northern, and Western Cape provinces of South Africa. It has a long history of facilitating the development of local leadership and grassroots organizing, with a particular focus on livelihoods, good governance, and access to food security. Past support enabled the trust to build more effective community engagement with local government around basic service delivery, especially water, sanitation, land, and electricity. This grant will support the Trust for Community Outreach and Education to continue strengthening the voices of the rural poor to engage government and other stakeholders around their development needs and interests. Focus areas will continue to be local government, land reform and rural livelihoods, food security, water, and strengthening local organizations and leadership.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Trust for Community Outreach and Education
description: The Trust for Community Outreach and Education is a national organization that is made up of six regional affiliates that work mainly with rural communities. Its main goal is to strengthen the voice of the rural poor to engage effectively with local governments and to increase food security in these rural areas. Previous support from Mott enabled the grantee to strengthen poor people’s voices and leadership capacities in rural communities through training and mentorship support. The grantee supported the establishment of associations and assisted people to become self-employed through agricultural initiatives. Support over the next two years will enable the grantee to continue to strengthen community leadership through training, mentoring, exchange visits, and mutual learning and support. The grantee will also continue to advocate government to provide access to land for poor people and improve access to opportunities for sustainable farming.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Trust for Community Outreach and Education
description: The Trust for Community Outreach and Education is a national organization that is made up of six regional affiliates that work mainly with rural communities. Its main goal is to strengthen the voice of the rural poor, engage effectively with local governments, and increase food security in rural areas. The grantee supported the establishment of associations, assisted people to be self-employed through agricultural initiatives, and conducted policy reviews and research on agricultural issues affecting poor communities. This grant increase will support the grantee to undertake research that will analyze the role of nonprofits in supporting movement building and other forms of self-organizing. It will also reflect on the work of the six rural movements and how they have evolved over time.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Trust for Community Outreach and Education
description: The Trust for Community Outreach and Education is a national organization made up of regional affiliates that work mainly in rural communities in South Africa. Its purpose is to build strong movements of the rural poor by strengthening their leadership structures to enable them to organize and coordinate activities of rural communities. Past support has enabled the grantee to support movements of the rural poor in articulating their need for land and other resources to increase food security. It has also trained women farmers on various topics related to farming. Mott support over the next two years will assist the grantee to strengthen its affiliates and to provide funding and related resources, hands-on support, and information to assist them to give voice to the rural poor. It will also raise public awareness about the challenges faced by rural communities in securing land for agricultural use.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Trust for Community Outreach and Education
description: The Trust for Community Outreach and Education is a national organization that was established in 1983 to promote the development of poor communities in rural areas. It has regional affiliates in six provinces that represent the voice of the poor. The grantee strengthens leadership and supports affiliate members to organize and coordinate activities of rural communities. Past support has enabled the grantee to launch a national movement of rural women, support efforts to access land and marine resources, and assist farmworkers to engage effectively with government and farmowners on issues of human rights on farms. This grant will allow the grantee to extend its work to rural organizations and associations in other provinces, support the establishment of a national rural movement led by its affiliates, strengthen local leadership to lead campaigns and engage in strategic discussions with local officials in order to improve their quality of life, and promote the economic transformation of rural communities.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Trust for Community Outreach and Education
description: The Trust for Community Outreach and Education was established in 1983 to promote the development of poor communities across South Africa. It is a national organization that supports movements of farm workers, small-scale farmers, rural women, and youth. The grantee strengthens leadership and supports its affiliate members to organize themselves and respond to issues that impact their lives. Past support enabled the grantee to build a strong network of rural movements, strengthen leadership within the movements, and expand its work to other provinces. This grant will allow the grantee to continue supporting farm worker groups, small-scale farmers, fisher communities, and youth to be organized, build leadership at a local level, and improve their quality of life.

title: General Purposes
description: The Gulf Restoration Network is a diverse partnership of citizens and organizations committed to protecting and restoring the Gulf of Mexico’s coastal lands and waters, and the freshwater ecosystems linked to them. With previous support, the network has educated the public about critical gulf aquatic resources, monitored the actions of decisionmakers, and brought scientific and policy expertise to key protection efforts. With renewal support, the network will continue its efforts to restore coastal land areas, improve wetlands protection, and restore damaged water quality–all pressing needs in the aftermath of Hurricanes Rita and Katrina. The network will also work to build its own organizational capacity.

title: General Purposes
description: Headquartered in New Orleans, the Gulf Restoration Network is a diverse partnership of citizens and organizations committed to protecting and restoring the Gulf of Mexico’s coastal lands and waters and their connected freshwater ecosystems. With previous support, the network provided members, decisionmakers, and other stakeholders with region-specific information and expertise on water quality protection, wetlands rehabilitation, and coastal restoration. With renewed support, the network will continue advancing its restoration and protection goals through a multifaceted approach that includes public education, assistance to citizen groups, opportunities for broad-based collaboration, a technical review of government policies, and the monitoring of policy implementation. The network will also continue to diversify funding and strengthen overall organizational capacity.

title: General Purposes
description: A regional environmental organization, the Gulf Restoration Network is a diverse partnership of citizens and organizations committed to protecting and restoring the Gulf of Mexico’s coastal lands and waters and their connected freshwater ecosystems. With previous support, the network advanced its mission through public education, assisting citizen groups, facilitating broad-based collaborations, conducting technical reviews of government policies, and monitoring policy implementation. It is anticipated that this grant increase, will help offset costs associated with the network’s regional response to the BP oil leak in the Gulf of Mexico. These efforts will include independent monitoring of agency and corporate clean-up efforts and sharing up-to-date information across the region.

title: General Purposes
description: The Gulf Restoration Network is a regional environmental organization that represents a diverse partnership of groups working to protect and restore the Gulf of Mexico’s coastline and its connected wetlands. With previous Mott support, the grantee coordinated groups across the five Gulf Coast states, provided technical information and policy analyses, and conducted public outreach in support of increased coastal protections. Currently, the grantee is focused on helping the coastline and coastal communities recover from the oil released during the 2010 drilling disaster. This general purpose grant increase will help the grantee lead a regional collaborative to guide resources to high priority restoration projects and establish a regional citizens advisory committee to help oversee the safety of coastal and off-shore oil extraction activities.

title: Water Quality Project
description: Louisiana’s freshwater resources, while still extensive and productive, are under considerable stress. The state is one of the nation’s largest generators of toxic pollutants. This situation was made more serious by Hurricanes Rita and Katrina, which caused additional damage to environmental and public health conditions throughout southern Louisiana.This grant will support the Louisiana Environmental Action Network’s efforts to improve the state’s water quality permitting activities as well as respond to special water quality policy needs brought on by the two storms.Recent achievements include constructive reforms in Louisiana’s water permitting practices, improvements in specific water quality discharge permits and positive changes in the disposal of hurricane-related debris.

title: Water Quality Project
description: Louisiana’s freshwater resources, while extensive and productive, are under considerable stress due to a variety of pollution sources. In response, the Louisiana Environmental Action Network, a statewide membership organization, works to improve implementation of the federal Clean Water Act and related policies. Past achievements include: constructive reforms in Louisiana’s water permitting practices, improvements in specific water quality discharge permits, and positive changes in the disposal of debris left in the wake of Hurricanes Katrina and Rita. With renewed Mott support, the network will continue such efforts to fully and effectively implement existing clean water policies as well as promote incentive-based policies that would further reduce water pollution in the state.

title: Water Quality Project
description: The Louisiana Environmental Action Network, a statewide membership organization, has been working for 23 years to protect the state’s freshwater and coastal resources. Past achievements include: constructive reforms of Louisiana’s water-permitting practices, improvements in specific water quality discharge permits, and the monitoring of water quality in the lower Mississippi River. With this grant increase, the network will continue its efforts to strengthen and fully implement Louisiana’s clean water policies.

title: Water Quality Project
description: The Louisiana Environmental Action Network is a statewide membership organization that has been working for 23 years to protect the state’s most productive and important freshwater systems. With prior Mott support, the grantee helped reform Louisiana’s water permitting practices, improved specific water quality discharge permits, and responded to freshwater contamination resulting from the 2010 oil drilling disaster. This grant increase will allow the grantee to document spill-related damage to the wetlands, marshes, and estuaries along Louisiana’s coastline. The grantee will provide the collected data, and related analyses, to the partners, communities, and decisionmakers working on Louisiana’s restoration programs.

title: Protecting Freshwater Ecosystems
description: South Carolina’s exceptional freshwater ecosystems – such as its blackwater rivers, cypress/tupelo swamps, bottomland hardwood forests and the unique Carolina Bays elliptical wetlands – face threats from a number of sources. These include the loss of federal wetland protections; pollution from storm water runoff; and alteration due to the operation of hydropower dams. This grant will enable the Coastal Conservation League to continue to build support for state and local wetland and water quality protection efforts and engage in the relicensing proceedings of federally regulated hydropower facilities in the state.With previous support, the league worked to prevent the weakening of state water quality protections and helped achieve fish passage and restored flows on two rivers through the dam relicensing process.

title: Protecting Freshwater Ecosystems
description: The Coastal Conservation League is dedicated to protecting South Carolina’s natural resources, with an emphasis on the South Carolina coast. With prior Mott support, the league has achieved a number of successes, such as defending existing wetland protection policies and restoring freshwater habitats through the relicensing of hydropower dams. With continued support, the league will seek to improve implementation of the Clean Water Act through state-level policy reforms and better permitting practices; advance new state-level policies governing water withdrawals and diversions; and seek additional freshwater habitat enhancements through the completion of several hydropower relicensing projects.

title: Protecting Freshwater Ecosystems
description: The Coastal Conservation League is dedicated to protecting South Carolina’s natural resources with an emphasis on the South Carolina coast. With prior Mott support, the grantee has achieved a number of successes, such as defending existing wetland protection policies and restoring freshwater habitats through the relicensing of hydropower dams. With continued support, the grantee will seek to improve implementation of the Clean Water Act through state-level policy reforms and better permitting practices; advancement of new state-level policies governing water withdrawals and diversions; and additional freshwater habitat enhancements by the completion of several hydropower relicensing projects.

title: Protecting Freshwater Ecosystems
description: This grant increase and associated one-year grant period extension will allow the Coastal Conservation League to continue to monitor and help implement state-level policies to protect and restore natural river flows and freshwater habitat. Activities will include tracking implementation of the state’s water withdrawal policies and participating in federal dam relicensing processes.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Michigan, Minnesota, Ontario, Wisconsin, Indiana, Ohio, Illinois
description: Great Lakes United is a binational network of organizations founded in 1982 to protect and restore the Great Lakes ecosystem. With prior Mott support, the organization has worked on a range of issues such as improving regional water planning and conservation, updating deficient sewage treatment infrastructure, controlling invasive species, and building public support for new public investment in Great Lakes restoration. With renewal support, the organization will continue this and similar program work while also strengthening its own institutional capacity by broadening its membership base and diversifying its funding sources.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Minnesota, Michigan, Wisconsin, Ontario, Indiana, Ohio, Illinois
description: Great Lakes United is a binational organization promoting the protection and restoration of the Great Lakes ecosystem. This grant increase will support the general purposes of the organization, including a proposed binational workshop for environmental leaders on the future of the Great Lakes Water Quality Agreement.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Minnesota, Wisconsin, Michigan, Indiana, Ohio, Ontario, Illinois
description: Great Lakes United is a binational network of organizations founded in 1982 to protect and restore the Great Lakes ecosystem. title: General Purposes
description: Hurricane Katrina brought national attention to the need to restore Louisiana’s wetlands, natural river systems, and barrier shorelines to improve storm protection, as well as to enhance water quality and habitat. New federal and state initiatives are being proposed that could have significant beneficial impacts on coastal Louisiana. With previous support, the Coalition to Restore Coastal Louisiana, a leader in coastal restoration, has promoted policies that protect and restore the coastal environment, including programs that would restore natural river flows whenever practicable. Renewal support will enable the coalition to maximize new opportunities that have emerged post-Katrina, including promoting citizen engagement in restoration projects and supporting the development of new beneficial policies.

title: General Purposes
description: In 2005, Hurricane Katrina brought national attention to the need to restore Louisiana’s wetlands, natural river systems, and barrier shorelines as a way to improve storm protection, as well as enhance water quality and habitat. The continued public interest in protecting the region, combined with new state and federal initiatives, provides an opportunity to restore the integrity of Louisiana’s coastline and the connected freshwater ecosystems. With previous support, the Coalition to Restore Coastal Louisiana, a state leader in coastal restoration, focused on reinstating natural freshwater flows when practical. Renewed support will allow the coalition to continue to help coordinate and maximize federal, state, and local efforts to protect Louisiana’s freshwater resources.

title: General Purposes
description: The Coalition to Restore Coastal Louisiana works to protect and restore Louisiana’s coastline, which includes important wetlands and their associated freshwater sources. With past support, the coalition helped coordinate federal, state, and local efforts to protect Louisiana’s coastal areas and reinstate natural freshwater flows when practical. This grant will be available for general purposes, but it is anticipated the funds will be used to help the organization respond to the BP oil leak in the Gulf of Mexico that threatens the area’s delicate coastal wetlands. Efforts will include serving as a statewide volunteer coordinator, facilitating the national and local environmental community’s joint response, and developing a scientific recovery strategy.

title: General Purposes
description: The Coalition to Restore Coastal Louisiana seeks to protect and restore Louisiana’s coastline and the associated freshwater systems. With prior support from Mott, the grantee implemented programs to increase protections for Louisiana’s coastal wetlands, reinstate natural freshwater flows in key areas, and respond to the 2010 oil disaster in the Gulf of Mexico. This grant increase will allow the organization to help restore priority coastal wetlands from oil contamination by providing technical information and assistance to state-level decisionmakers and a variety of local, regional, and national partners.

title: Conferences on Foreign Affairs
description: This grant provides renewal support to the Southern Center for International Studies for three television conferences. Since convening the first meeting with the former U.S. secretaries of state in 1983, the grantee has produced more than 50 one-hour television programs in this series. These programs, which have been aired in 90 percent of the public broadcasting television markets across the country, provide the general public with a comprehensive annual review of the most important foreign policy and national security issues facing the United States. During the grant period, conferences are planned with former secretaries of state, defense, and possibly energy or the treasury. Video footage from the conferences is also incorporated into “The World in Transition” series, a ten-part, multimedia educational series designed to internationalize the way social studies teachers at the middle and high school levels teach world affairs. Founded more than 45 years ago, the Southern Center for International Studies is an independent center for thought and opinion on international affairs and foreign policy.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will enable the Detroit Entrepreneurship Institute to provide business development services and technical assistance to individuals receiving public assistance, dislocated workers and the working poor.The mission of the institute is to alleviate poverty through entrepreneurship and economic literacy. During the past 16 years, it has consistently carried out this mission by implementing a comprehensive “one stop” approach for providing entrepreneurial training, small business development services, technical assistance, economic literacy and access to start-up capital.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide partial support to Detroit Entrepreneurship Institute, Inc., that will enable it to continue to provide business development services and technical assistance to individuals receiving public assistance, dislocated workers, and the working poor. Over the past 17 years, the Detroit Entrepreneurship Institute has consistently carried out its mission to alleviate poverty through providing entrepreneurial training, small business development services, technical assistance, economic literacy, and access to start-up capital. Since October 1990, over 4,500 adults and youth have enrolled in business training programs, and 870 are now operating or have expanded their own small enterprises.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will enable the Committee of Voters of Ukraine to continue engaging Ukrainian citizens nationwide in the political process. The committee will mobilize volunteers to monitor elections, promote accountability of elected officials through public information activities, advise citizens on effective means of interacting with local government, educate youth on their constitutional and voting rights, and advocate for a more open, democratic process in Ukraine. In all these activities, the committee will maintain strict nonpartisanship. The committee has worked to promote open and democratic political processes in Ukraine since its inception in 1994. In that time, it has trained thousands of election observers and responded to tens of thousands of public inquiries on electoral rights. Its work directly contributed to the holding of the first fully free and fair presidential elections in Ukraine in 2004.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to foster the development of civil society in an open and democratic Ukraine. The Committee of Voters of Ukraine will mobilize volunteers to monitor elections, promote accountability of elected officials through public information activities, advise citizens on effective means of interacting with local government, educate youth on their constitutional and voting rights, and advocate for transparent and reliable election procedures in Ukraine. In 2007-2009, the grantee trained over 200,000 local election commissioners and party observers. It maintained a pool of 3,000 volunteer election monitors whose work contributed to increasingly free and fair local and national elections over this period. Its monitoring of a pilot national university entrance exam helped see new procedures established for this important anticorruption measure. Established in 1994, the Committee of Voters of Ukraine and its 148 local and regional branches work to promote open and democratic political processes in Ukraine.

title: General Purposes
description: This renewal provides general purposes support for the Harlem Children’s Zone, a comprehensive, community-building initiative designed to improve outcomes for poor children and their families in Central Harlem. Working with the entire community to address the needs of the children in the zone from birth to early adulthood, the Harlem Children’s Zone will continue to develop new programs and strengthen existing ones to provide a full spectrum of services for children and their parents. title: General Purposes
description: This grant supports the development of community education in Russia. Multiyear funding will enable the Krasnoyarsk Center for Community Partnerships to facilitate networking among regional community school development support organizations; further develop and improve existing community education programs; and publicize community schools and promote their proliferation throughout Russia. The center will work toward meeting these objectives by encouraging the networking of regional community school resource centers; conducting its own direct training and promotion activities in Russian schools and communities; and improving its institutional capacities.The center, founded in 1996, is Russia’s leading community school development support organization.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to foster civic engagement through the further development of community education in Russia. The grantee will increase the professionalism of community school educators and administrators; strengthen ties between federal and regional education authorities and the community school movement; encourage the development of school-based community initiatives; and promote more systematic information sharing across the Russian community schools network, including through the continuing development of a comprehensive community school Internet portal. The center will also focus on strengthening its own long-term sustainability as a leading community education think tank. Established in 1996, the Krasnoyarsk Center for Community Partnerships has successfully introduced and popularized the community schools model into more than 35 regions of Russia.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to foster civic engagement through the further development of community schools in Russia. The Krasnoyarsk Center for Community Partnerships will broaden the learning environment for community school practitioners, educational authorities, and other stakeholders through training, publications, and coaching. It will strengthen the network of schools and support centers through regular conferences, mentoring visits, and ongoing updating of the Web site of the community school movement. The grantee will also focus on strengthening its own institutional capacity by raising the professional qualifications of staff and through efforts to link into ongoing educational reform activities. In 2007-2009, the grantee introduced four pilot programs aimed at improving community school practice, held 15 networking events for schools and resource centers, and organized three international conferences. Established in 1996, the Krasnoyarsk Center for Community Partnerships has worked successfully to introduce and popularize the community schools model into more than 35 regions of Russia.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to foster civic engagement through the further development of community schools in Russia. The Krasnoyarsk Center for Community Partnerships will expand efforts to mainstream community schools in line with Russian educational reforms. It will strengthen the growing network of schools and support centers through regular meetings. It will foster increased knowledge sharing through Webinars, training events, and a comprehensive Internet portal. The grantee will also continue to focus on strengthening its own institutional capacity by raising the professional qualifications of staff. In 2011-2013, the grantee organized three international conferences, completely restructured and upgraded the community schools Internet portal, implemented four programs aimed at improving community school practice in areas including social tolerance and conflict resolution, and created a new center for volunteer management in Krasnoyarsk. Established in 1996, the Krasnoyarsk Center for Community Partnerships has worked successfully to introduce and popularize the community schools model into more than 35 regions of Russia.

title: Community Development Unit - Capacity Building for the Eastern Cape
description: The Community Development Unit is based at the Nelson Mandela Metropolitan University in Port Elizabeth in the Eastern Cape, a region hardest hit by the HIV/AIDS pandemic. A number of community-based organizations have been established in response to this challenge, many of them involved in running care centers for the frail, providing home-based care, and advocating on behalf of those infected and affected. Mott has been supporting the Community Development Unit to provide capacity building, institutional support, and training to many of these organizations to enhance their effectiveness and to ensure that they are able to locate funding for their vital work. This renewal grant will continue to support the work of the Community Development Unit, ensuring that it is able to extend its services to more districts in the Eastern Cape. The Community Development Unit will also provide accredited training in project management and project leadership.

title: Community Development Unit - Capacity Building for the Eastern Cape
description: This grant will continue support of the Community Development Unit based at the Nelson Mandela Metropolitan University. The university was established in 2005, as a result of a merger between the Port Elizabeth Technikon and the University of Port Elizabeth (incorporating Vista University). The unit, established 25 years ago, provides technical assistance, training and institutional support to community-based organizations that focus on health, particularly the prevention and treatment of HIV/AIDS in the Eastern Cape province. Past accomplishments of the unit include supporting, mentoring, and training community-based organizations working in the area of HIV/AIDS and developing training materials to support its interventions. Plans for the next two years include documenting, disseminating, and replicating best practices; continuing to assist community health committees; translating guides and training materials into Afrikaans; offering university students practical volunteer opportunities to learn about community development; and reviving a program of short courses with University certification.

title: General Purposes
description: The Salem Housing Community Development Corporation was created in 1984 by five Flint neighborhood organizations and a church. Its mission is to improve living conditions by providing safe, decent and affordable housing for families of limited income and to act as a catalyst to restore the neighborhoods within its service area.Funding will enable the organization, which primarily serves a 132-block area in northwest Flint, to oversee the rehabilitation of owner-occupied homes; provide home ownership programs for people preparing to buy a home; offer lease-to-purchase homes for families transitioning to self-sufficiency; support neighborhood revitalization and community building in the primary service area; and participate in civic engagement initiatives that help develop neighborhood leaders.During the past year, the organization assisted four families in purchasing homes; rehabilitated more than 25 owner-occupied houses; restored three vacant houses, which are in the process of being sold; and, with the assistance of volunteers who contributed almost 2,500 hours of work, began the restoration of five additional houses. Approximately 70 individuals graduated from Salem’s homebuyer’s class series and homeowner counseling was provided to 72 families.

title: General Purposes

In 2007, Salem Housing activities will include: sweat-equity and lease-to-purchase homeownership, owner-occupied rehabilitation, project development, property management, homeownership counseling, and community building.
