title: State Fiscal Analysis Initiative
description: Funding will enable the Massachusetts Budget and Policy Center to inform public debates through effective research, analysis and outreach efforts in Massachusetts. Other priorities include implementing new communication strategies and expanding its recently established major donor program.During the past two years, the center played an important role in informing and framing public debates on revenue and spending issues and on new and existing policy initiatives in the state.This is one of 10 grants supporting the State Fiscal Analysis Initiative. The Massachusetts Budget and Policy Center joined this effort in 1994. Mott has also supported the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, which provides technical assistance and networking opportunities for the 35 state organizations participating in this initiative.

title: State Fiscal Analysis Initiative
description: This is one of ten grants recommended to state organizations participating in the State Fiscal Analysis Initiative. The Ford, Annie E. Casey, and Mott Foundations created the initiative in 1992 in order to build state capacity for timely, credible, and accessible tax and budget analysis on behalf of low- and middle-income families. The Massachusetts Budget and Policy Center joined this effort in 1994 and is recognized throughout Massachusetts as an authoritative source of information and analysis. During this grant period, the grantee will prepare and disseminate analyses on a range of state fiscal issues, with a particular emphasis on state and local tax policies and income support programs. Other activities planned for the grant period include community outreach, strategic communications, and coalition building. Related to this project is a grant to the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, which provides technical assistance to all 36 organizations participating in this initiative.

title: State Fiscal Analysis Initiative
description: The Massachusetts Budget and Policy Center is one of ten state organizations participating in the State Fiscal Analysis Initiative. The Ford, Annie E. Casey, and Mott Foundations created the initiative in 1992 in order to build state capacity for timely, credible, and accessible tax and budget analyses on behalf of low- and middle-income families. The Massachusetts Budget and Policy Center joined this effort in 1994 and is recognized throughout Massachusetts as an authoritative source of information and analysis. This grant increase will enable the center to implement the Community Leadership Fellowship Program – a direct effort to promote a more diverse analytical staff in order to better reflect the state and communities the organization represents. The grantee will continue to prepare and disseminate analyses on a range of state fiscal issues, with a particular emphasis on state and local tax policies and income support programs. Other activities planned for the grant period include community outreach, strategic communications, and coalition building.

description: This grant increase is one of ten tie-off grants to state organizations participating in the State Priorities Partnership (formerly the State Fiscal Analysis Initiative). title: Michigan Individual Development Account Partnership
description: This grant will enable the Council of Michigan Foundations to spin off the Michigan Individual Development Account Partnership, which was established in 2000 to support the growth and development of Individual Development Account programs throughout Michigan. The initiative was the result of a public-private partnership between the Council of Michigan Foundations, the Mott Foundation, and the Michigan Department of Human Services. To facilitate this transition, the Council of Michigan Foundations will devolve its Michigan Individual Development Account Partnership roles and responsibilities to the Community Economic Development Association of Michigan, a nonprofit organization located in Lansing. The Council of Michigan Foundations is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit membership association comprised of more than 400 foundations and corporations making grants for charitable purposes.

title: General Purposes
description: The National Black United Fund promotes charitable giving and volunteerism by African Americans. It serves as a national coordinating and planning body for local affiliates that raise money primarily through employee payroll deduction and then distribute the funds to community-based nonprofits serving the African-American community.This grant will enable the fund to create communication tools that reach out to a greater number of potential community leaders; encourage greater civic engagement by citizens; and increase support for family and community development.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purposes support to the National Black United Fund, Inc., which promotes charitable giving and volunteerism by African Americans. The organization serves as a national coordinating and planning body for local affiliates that raise money primarily through employee payroll deduction and then distributes the funds to community-based nonprofits serving the African-American community. Over the next two years, the organization will focus on improving its capacity to create communication tools that reach out to a greater number of potential community leaders, encourage greater civic engagement by citizens, and emphasize greater support for family and community development.

title: Energy Futures: Reforming International Finance and Trade
initiative: Reform of International Finance and Trade
description: This grant will enable Earth Economics to improve its ability to foster collaboration between ecological economists and non-governmental organizations; educate policymakers at the local, national and international levels about the environmental costs associated with energy and infrastructure development; and ultimately, contribute to a clear vision of sustainable energy and infrastructure development.Formerly known as the Asian Pacific Environmental Exchange, a project of the Tides Center, Earth Economics is dedicated to promoting healthy ecosystems, communities and economies.

title: Environment, Development and Trade Project
initiative: Reform of International Finance and Trade
description: This grant will enable the Canadian Environmental Law Association to extend its research, outreach and advocacy work aimed at improving the environmental aspects of Canadian, North American and global trade policies. Project activities include monitoring trade negotiations and trade policies; analyzing new policy proposals; advising Canadian federal, provincial and municipal governments on issues related to trade policy and the environment; educating the public; and working with other non-governmental organizations (NGOs) to develop and promote alternative policies.During the past two years, the association responded to ongoing trade negotiations by contributing research and analysis to NGOs and government officials; published reports and presented at workshops and conferences to widely disseminate the research results, analysis and recommendations; provided legal opinions, advice and education for NGOs, government officials, international organizations and others working on trade and investment; and organized educational opportunities for youth leaders.The association, established in 1970, is a leading member of the trade and environment policy community in Canada.

title: General Purposes
description: The Funders’ Network for Smart Growth and Livable Communities is a resource and focal point for foundations, nonprofit organizations and other partners working to solve the environmental, social and economic problems created by suburban sprawl and urban disinvestment.This grant will enable the network to strengthen the abilities of funders to support organizations promoting smart growth and creating livable communities.Recent accomplishments include hosting annual conferences; coordinating meetings and projects on specific topics; developing a comprehensive Web site; and preparing issue papers and special reports.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant supports the Funders’ Network for Smart Growth and Livable Communities, a network of over 140 foundations from across the country. Its mission is to inspire, strengthen, and expand funding and philanthropic leadership that yields environmentally sustainable, socially equitable, and economically prosperous regions and communities. The grantee’s strategies are to coordinate funder education, information sharing, and relationship development; facilitate strategic initiatives and collaborations; and cultivate emerging funder interest and new opportunities for funder engagement. Services include an annual conference, publications and electronic communications, a monthly series of topical conference calls, outreach and education, and consulting services. Recent accomplishments include deepening relationships between foundations and public sector programs such as the Department of Housing and Urban Development’s Sustainable Communities Regional Planning and Strong Cities Strong Communities programs, and connecting local, regional, and national funders to each other in specific areas of interest such as older industrial cities and transportation reform.

title: Youth Transition Funders Group
description: This grant will provide partial support to the Youth Transition Funders Group (YTFG), a project of the Coalition of Community Foundations for Youth. YTFG was formed in 1997 to focus specifically on improving the transition of youth into adulthood as economically self-sufficient and productive members of society. It provides a forum for foundations to network and develop comprehensive and complementary grantmaking strategies to create opportunities for youth in transition between the ages of 16-24. Key activities in 2006 will include supporting funder collaborations, expanding the membership base, increasing field collaborations, raising awareness on cross-cutting issues and engaging youth more effectively.Since its inception, YTFG has expanded into a collaboration of 30 foundations and a national network of more than 200 local, regional and national grantmakers from across the country.

The activities supported under this increase will allow the Youth Transition Funders Group to increase outreach efforts to new funders, develop new leadership, and partner with philanthropic and other stakeholders engaged in national initiatives to improve education and employment outcomes for vulnerable youth.

title: Capacity Building Support
description: The need for additional trained and professional organizers is the most pressing need in the community organizing field today.This grant will enable the Midwest Academy to expand its efforts to identify, recruit, train and place additional professional organizers, especially Spanish-speaking organizers.Recent accomplishments included creating a new program for training senior organizers with sessions on supervision; developing a series of training sessions held in Spanish; increasing the number of participants in week-long training sessions; and placing 20 organizer interns per year.

title: Crisis Assessment Program in the Balkans
geographic_focus: North Macedonia, Montenegro, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia, Albania
description: The International Crisis Group’s (ICG) reports are geared toward policymakers, the media, and national and international organizations working in the region. Its goal is to support sustained, on-the-ground research and analysis of key issues and trends affecting the prevention and containment of violent conflict in the Western Balkans.This grant will enable ICG to focus its work in Serbia, Kosovo and Macedonia, while also monitoring developments in Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Montenegro. ICG will produce and disseminate 10 to 12 reports; publish multiple opinion pieces in major international newspapers; and initiate advocacy meetings with key decisionmakers.During the past year, ICG produced seven in-depth reports that were published in English and local languages. Although its main office is in Brussels, it has three full-time analysts based in the region.

title: Environmental Partnership for Central Europe
description: The program goal is to strengthen environmental advocacy initiatives of nonprofit organizations in Central Europe. The mission of the Environmental Partnership Foundations in the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, and Slovakia is to promote environmental protection and sustainable development. The foundations’ mission is pursued through providing small grants and technical assistance to nonprofits, as well as operating projects. During the grant period, the foundations will strengthen grassroots advocacy for sustainable development, increase their grantmaking capacity, and improve their financial sustainability. As of December 2005, the foundations have provided approximately $16 million to over 5,000 projects of citizen groups and communities in Central Europe.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purposes support to Carpathian Foundation International, a regional philanthropic and development organization. The mission of the foundation is to build the capacity of nonprofit organizations and local governments in the Carpathian Euroregion to promote economic development, cross-border cooperation, and interethnic initiatives. To this end, the foundation makes grants and provides training, technical assistance, and networking opportunities to nongovernmental organizations and local governments throughout the Carpathian Euroregion. To date, Carpathian Foundation International has awarded more than 1,300 grants totaling over $7 million to nongovernmental organizations and local governments. This grant increase will support the general purposes of the foundation, including a cross-border initiative in Hungary and Slovakia that involves citizens in decisionmaking processes regarding the future of rural areas in Europe.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purposes support to Carpathian Foundation International, a regional philanthropic and development organization. The foundation makes grants and provides training, technical assistance and networking opportunities to non-governmental organizations and local governments throughout the Carpathian Euroregion. Funding includes a grant increase to support a cross-border initiative in Hungary and Slovakia that involves citizens in decisionmaking processes regarding the future of rural areas in Europe.To date, Carpathian Foundation International has awarded more than 1,300 grants totaling more than $7 million to non-governmental organizations and local governments. The foundation has offices in Hungary, Poland, Romania, Slovakia and Ukraine.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to support the development of local communities and grassroots organizations in the Carpathian Euroregion. To this end, Carpathian Foundation International, in partnership with the network of local Carpathian foundations in Hungary, Poland, Romania, Slovakia, and Ukraine, will provide grants, technical assistance, and networking opportunities to nongovernmental organizations and local governments throughout the Carpathian Euroregion to promote economic development, cross-border cooperation, and interethnic initiatives. In addition, the foundation will strengthen its own, as well as its partners’, organizational capacities and financial sustainability. The foundation started in 1995 as a project of the EastWest Institute, and to date, it has awarded more than 1,350 grants totaling over $8 million to nongovernmental organizations and local governments. In the past two years, the foundation supported cross-border initiatives in the areas of community development, deliberative democracy, education, and cultural heritage which benefited more than 400 communities.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued general purposes support to Hispanics in Philanthropy, a grantmaker affinity group committed to increasing investments in Latino communities, expanding the participation and leadership of Latinos in the philanthropic sector, and fostering policy change to enhance equity and inclusiveness in philanthropy. The organization has built a sophisticated national infrastructure of grantmakers and community leaders and offers a wide range of services and programs to enhance and increase philanthropy for and among Latinos including: conferences and networking; research, publications, and information sharing; workshops and technical assistance; funding initiatives; and a fellowship program.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued general purpose support to Hispanics in Philanthropy, a grantmaker affinity group committed to increasing investments in Latino communities, expanding the participation and leadership of Latinos in the philanthropic sector, and fostering policy change to enhance equity and inclusiveness in philanthropy. Recent past accomplishments include providing capacity building grants to 95 Latino-serving nonprofits, training over 800 Latino leaders, and holding 26 grantee convenings across the country. During the grant period, the grantee will continue to expand and develop new models for giving to Latino communities, strengthen its infrastructure and organizational capacity, and expand its network and increase information sharing.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued general purpose support to Hispanics in Philanthropy, a grantmaker affinity group committed to increasing investments in Latino communities, expanding the participation and leadership of Latinos in the philanthropic sector, and fostering policy change to enhance equity and inclusiveness in philanthropy. Recent initiatives include HIP to College, a program to increase college attendance and retention rates for Latino students; the Latino Age Wave Initiative to meet the needs of Latino senior citizens; and the awarding of $3.2 million in capacity building grants and training to Latino community-based organizations across the country. Some of the group’s main activities over the next three years include launching an online giving platform known as HIPGive; grantmaking for several focused initiatives such as aging, education, and Latino men and boys; advocating for greater investment in local Latino nonprofits and leaders; and educating the philanthropic sector on the needs of Latinos.

title: Global Financial Correspondent
grantee: IPS/Inter Press Service - North America, Inc.
initiative: Reform of International Finance and Trade
description: The Washington D.C.-based Global Financial Correspondent of IPS/Inter Press Service-North America ensures ongoing media coverage of the roles and impacts of international financial institutions, as well as trade negotiations.This grant will enable IPS to continue to report on international financial institutions and, by supporting a correspondent in its Washington, D.C. bureau, provide systematic coverage for Inter Press Service’s newswire. In addition, IPS will work to enhance coverage of local impacts of, and alternatives to, the activities of international financial institutions; build capacity of journalists associated with IPS in developing countries to cover the institutions and issues; and ensure that its reporting receives widespread distribution to policymakers, non-governmental organizations and academics around the world.Annually, more than 100 stories are produced and distributed to newspapers and radio stations, posted on the Inter Press Service Web site, distributed through collaborating non-governmental organizations and circulated to subscribers around the world.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Association for Research on Nonprofit Organizations & Voluntary Action
description: This grant provides general purposes support to the Association for Research on Nonprofit Organizations & Voluntary Action. This membership association of more than 1,100 scholars and nonprofit practitioners promotes research on voluntary action, nonprofit organizations, philanthropy, and civil society. Over 20 percent of its members come from outside the United States. The association helps scholars gain insight into the practical concerns of nonprofit agencies, while providing nonprofit professionals with research they can use to improve the quality of life for citizens and communities. Its principal activities consist of an annual conference, publications including the Nonprofit and Voluntary Sector Quarterly, and electronic discussion groups.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Association for Research on Nonprofit Organizations & Voluntary Action
description: This grant provides renewal support to the Association for Research on Nonprofit Organizations & Voluntary Action. The association is a membership association of more than 1,300 nonprofit scholars and practitioners which provides a neutral, open forum committed to strengthening the research community in the emerging field of nonprofit and philanthropic studies. The association brings together both theoretical and applied interests, helping scholars gain insight into the day-to-day concerns of third-sector organizations, while providing nonprofit professionals with research they can use to improve the quality of life for citizens and communities. Principal activities have included an annual conference, publications including the “Nonprofit and Voluntary Sector Quarterly”, electronic discussions, and special interest groups. The association’s three main strategic goals in the near term are to: 1) diversify membership and participation in events; 2) strengthen and enrich the dialogue between researchers and practitioners; and 3) build partnerships with other nonprofit infrastructure organizations.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Association for Research on Nonprofit Organizations & Voluntary Action
description: This grant provides renewal support to the Association for Research on Nonprofit Organizations & Voluntary Action, a leading interdisciplinary community of people dedicated to fostering — through research and education — the creation, application, and dissemination of knowledge on nonprofit organizations, philanthropy, civil society, and voluntary action. Now in its 42nd year and with more than 1,100 members, the grantee brings together both theoretical and applied interests, helping scholars gain insight into the day-to-day concerns of third-sector organizations. Principal activities have included an annual conference, publications including the “Nonprofit and Voluntary Sector Quarterly”, electronic discussions, and special interest groups. The grantee’s main goals are to: 1) locate and invite new members while retaining current members; 2) build and sustain useful partnerships among academic institutions and sector infrastructure organizations; 3) further develop and enrich a continuing dialogue between university-based researchers and nonprofit practitioners; and 4) strengthen the organization.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Association for Research on Nonprofit Organizations & Voluntary Action
description: This grant provides renewal support to the Association for Research on Nonprofit Organizations & Voluntary Action, an association based in the United States that connects scholars, teachers, and practitioners interested in research on nonprofit organizations, voluntary action, philanthropy, and civil society. Founded in 1971, the grantee brings together both theoretical and applied interests, helps scholars gain insight into the daily concerns of nonprofits, and provides nonprofit professionals with connections to research they can use to improve their work. Principal activities include an annual conference, publications including the “Nonprofit and Voluntary Sector Quarterly”, electronic discussions, and special interest groups. In the past three years, the grantee’s membership has increased from 800 to 1,250 and conference attendance from less than 600 to over 850. Since 2010, the grantee has held four nonprofit public policy symposiums for university based researchers and nonprofit practitioners. The grantee will continue the above activities and strive to expand its membership and reach.

title: General Purposes
description: The Alliance for the Great Lakes, founded in 1970 as the Lake Michigan Federation, seeks to conserve and restore the Great Lakes freshwater ecosystem.This grant will enable the alliance to continue its policy, education and local conservation efforts and complete a planning process to develop a new three-year action plan.Past support helped the alliance engage in policy discussions pertaining to the Great Lakes Compact and a comprehensive Great Lakes restoration strategy; conduct organizational development activities; and deliver public education and outreach programs.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant increase will support the general purposes of the Alliance for the Great Lakes, a leading regional organization working to protect the lakes. Anticipated activities include the planning and convening of a regional meeting for environmental leaders to discuss proposals to expand oil refinery capacity in the Great Lakes basin.

title: General Purposes
description: The Alliance for the Great Lakes, founded in 1970 as the Lake Michigan Federation, seeks to conserve and restore the Great Lakes freshwater ecosystem using policy, education, and local conservation efforts. Past general support from Mott helped the alliance engage in policy discussions pertaining to the Great Lakes Compact and a comprehensive Great Lakes restoration strategy, conduct organizational development activities, and deliver public education and outreach programs. Renewal support will enable the alliance to continue these efforts as well as to work to eliminate sources of new invasive species into the Great Lakes.

title: General Purposes
description: The Alliance for the Great Lakes, founded in 1970 as the Lake Michigan Federation, seeks to conserve and restore the Great Lakes freshwater ecosystem through policy reform, public education, and local conservation projects. With previous Mott support, the alliance engaged in policy discussions regarding the Great Lakes Compact and the Great Lakes Restoration Initiative, delivered public education and outreach programs, and implemented organizational development strategies. With this renewal, the alliance will continue these efforts while strengthening programs to address water pollution and invasive species in the Great Lakes.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: New York, Michigan, Illinois, Wisconsin, Indiana
description: Founded in 1970 as the Lake Michigan Federation, the Alliance for the Great Lakes combines research and policy analyses with citizen engagement to improve the health of the Great Lakes. The organization continues to increase its presence in the region and has staff based in Illinois, Michigan, Wisconsin, New York, and Ohio. With prior support from Mott, the grantee helped implement the Great Lakes Compact, inform the Great Lakes Restoration Initiative, reduce regulated and unregulated pollutants in the Great Lakes, and advance protections against invasive species. Renewed general purpose support will allow the grantee to continue these efforts and invest in its own organizational development.

title: General Purposes
description: Founded in 1970 as the Lake Michigan Federation, the Alliance for the Great Lakes combines research and policy analyses with citizen engagement to improve the health of the Great Lakes. The grantee is based in Chicago and has staff in Michigan, New York, Ohio, and Wisconsin. With prior Mott support, the grantee helped implement the Great Lakes Compact, reduce pollution from water treatment facilities, and build public support for halting the spread of invasive species. Renewed general purpose support will allow the grantee to continue these efforts and invest in its own organizational development.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Michigan, Wisconsin, Ohio, Indiana, Illinois, Minnesota
description: The Alliance for the Great Lakes, founded in 1970, seeks to conserve and restore the Great Lakes through scientific and legal research, policy reform initiatives, and public engagement. With previous Mott support, the grantee helped develop regional strategies to address toxic algal blooms, produced a report on water quality threats from the shipping of crude oil, and engaged 15,000 volunteers to clean up coastal sites across the region. Renewed support will enable the grantee to continue improving water quality, ensuring natural water levels and flows, halting invasive species, and building stronger public support for Great Lakes protections. The grantee will also take steps to strengthen its own organizational capacity.

title: General Purposes
description: Founded in 1970 as the Lake Michigan Federation, the Alliance for the Great Lakes seeks to conserve and restore the Great Lakes freshwater ecosystem through policy reform, public education, and local conservation projects. With previous Mott support, the grantee engaged in policy discussions regarding the Great Lakes Compact and the Great Lakes Restoration Initiative, delivered public education and outreach programs, implemented organizational development strategies, and strengthened programs to address water pollution and invasive species. This renewal grant will allow the grantee to continue these efforts, while increasing efforts to address Great Lakes water issues at the local level.

title: General Purposes
description: Founded in 1970, as the Lake Michigan Federation, the Alliance for the Great Lakes seeks to conserve and restore the Great Lakes freshwater ecosystem through policy reform, public education, and local conservation projects. With previous Mott support, the grantee engaged in policy discussions around aquatic invasive species and the Great Lakes Restoration Initiative, delivered public education and outreach programs, and implemented organizational development strategies. This renewal grant will allow the grantee to continue these and similar efforts, while increasing efforts to address drinking water infrastructure issues across the basin.

title: Promoting MDB Reform From Europe
grantee: World Economy, Ecology and Development Association
initiative: Reform of International Finance and Trade
description: The World Economy, Ecology and Development Association will continue its work in Germany to promote reform of international financial institution policies and operations. To further its objectives over the next year, the project will work to strengthen environmental and social policies and practices of international financial institutions; promote increased transparency and democratic governance at the World Bank; strengthen collaborative work between non-governmental organizations; and raise public awareness of, and achieve policy reforms at export credit agencies. The project’s overall strategic focus will be on policies related to the financing of energy projects.

title: Promoting MDB Reform From Europe
grantee: World Economy, Ecology and Development Association
initiative: Reform of International Finance and Trade
description: The World Economy, Ecology and Development Association will continue its work in Germany to promote reform of international financial institution policies and operations. To further its objectives over the next year, the project will work to strengthen environmental and social policies and practices of international financial institutions; promote increased transparency and democratic governance at the World Bank; strengthen collaborative work between nongovernmental organizations; and raise public awareness of, and achieve policy reforms at, export credit agencies. The project’s overall strategic focus will be on policies related to the financing of energy projects. The project will work to increase overall awareness of the role of international financial institutions and export credit agencies in influencing energy policy worldwide and to systematically promote renewable energy.

title: Southeast Europe: Diversity and Democracy
geographic_focus: Albania, Slovenia, Bulgaria, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Serbia, Montenegro, Croatia
description: The project goal is to protect and promote minority rights by contributing to the implementation of international standards and domestic legislation in Southeast Europe, including Albania, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Greece, Kosovo, Macedonia, Montenegro, and Serbia. To this end, Minority Rights Group International will continue to work with a network of local, minority rights nongovernmental organizations on organizational capacity, research, and advocacy. Over the past three years, with the grantee’s assistance and financial support, these organizations have successfully carried out research, participated in international meetings and conferences, and monitored implementation of complex laws and treaties. With its emphasis on empowerment and capacity building for local organizations, this project is part of the grantee’s long-term exit strategy for this region. The grantee is based in London and has significant experience in research and advocacy on minority rights and participation throughout the world.

title: Leadership and Capacity Building Project
grantee: Western Organization of Resource Councils Education Project
geographic_focus: Colorado, North Dakota, South Dakota, Montana, Idaho, Wyoming, Oregon
description: The Western Organization of Resource Councils Education Project is building permanent, multi-issue, membership-based community organizations throughout the Northwest. Funding will enable the grantee to increase the capacity of grassroots leaders and professional community organizers in order to address economic issues of concern to low-income residents of the Rocky Mountain and Great Plains regions. The grantee will conduct a series of workshops, trainings, leadership schools, and exchanges, and will produce training materials. This initiative will enhance the grantee’s work on issues including natural resource policies, corporate and community relations, and agricultural reforms to benefit small- and moderate-sized family farms.

grantee: Western Organization of Resource Councils Education Project

This initiative will enhance the grantee’s work on issues including natural resources policy, corporate and community relations, and agricultural reforms to benefit small- and moderate-sized family farms. This grant provides renewal support for Western Organization of Resource Councils Education Project and its supported organization, the Western Organization of Resource Councils.

title: General Purposes
description: BankTrack focuses its efforts on building the capacity of nongovernmental organizations to monitor and influence projects supported by private international banks. This renewal grant will provide general support to BankTrack. Over the past two years, BankTrack has had an important impact on the refinement of the Equator Principles, which cover international private bank lending. Activities over the next two years will include monitoring international private bank lending policies with a particular focus on policies related to energy and climate change and human rights; tracking implementation of Equator Principles and encouraging Equator banks to address issues not currently covered by the Equator Principles; undertaking research on key emerging market banks, including Brazil, China, India, South Africa, and South Korea; and providing support to nongovernmental organizations focused on specific projects being funded by private international banks.

title: General Purposes
description: BankTrack is a network of nongovernmental organizations seeking to reform the private financial sector and steer it toward social and environmental sustainability. It focuses its efforts on building the capacity of nongovernmental organizations to monitor and influence projects supported by private international banks. This renewal grant will provide general purpose support. Activities over the next two years will include monitoring international private bank lending policies; tracking implementation of Equator Principles and encouraging Equator banks to address issues not currently covered by the principles; and providing support to nongovernmental organizations focused on specific projects being funded by private international banks.

title: General Purposes
description: BankTrack is a network of nongovernmental organizations seeking to reform the private financial sector and steer it toward social and environmental sustainability. Over the last grant period, it has strengthened its role as the key network monitoring the implementation of the Equator Principles. This renewal grant will provide general purpose support for the grantee to continue monitoring international private bank lending policies; track implementation of Equator Principles and encourage Equator banks to address issues not currently covered by the principles, including energy and climate change policies, human rights, and global banking regulation; and provide support to nongovernmental organizations focused on specific projects being funded by private international banks.

title: General Purposes
description: BankTrack is a network of nongovernmental organizations seeking to reform the private financial sector and steer it toward social and environmental sustainability. Over the last two years, the grantee mobilized civil society input into the revision of the Equator Principles, a set of social and environmental standards for private lending in developing countries, with positive results. This renewal grant will provide general purpose support for the grantee to continue monitoring international private bank lending policies; track implementation of Equator Principles, particularly related to energy and climate change policies; develop a vision of banking that supports sustainable development; and provide support and capacity building to nongovernmental organizations focused on specific projects being funded by private international banks.

title: General Purposes
description: As the number of new foundations grows, the Association of Small Foundations is playing an increasingly important role in drawing trustees of new foundations into a supportive network where they can receive high quality information on managing and administering their foundations.This grant will enable the association to continue providing technical assistance and information to its members, assisting them in becoming more effective grantmakers through conferences, seminars, mentoring programs, and production and distribution of guides, handbooks, primers and directories.The association, a national membership organization for trustee-operated foundations with few or no staff, is the largest philanthropy support organization in the country with 3,076 members and assets of $52 billion.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant continues general purpose support to the Association of Small Foundations, a national membership organization for trustee-operated foundations with few or no staff. As the number of new foundations grows, this association plays an increasingly important role in pulling trustees of new foundations into a supportive network where they can receive high quality information on managing and administering their foundations. This association is the largest philanthropy support organization in the country with 3,106 members whose assets total $67 billion. Through conferences, seminars, mentoring programs, and production and distribution of guides, handbooks, primers, and directories, the Association of Small Foundations provides technical assistance and general information to its members assisting them to become more effective grantmakers. Over the next two years, among its wide variety of offerings, the association will give particular attention to helping its members in evaluating impact, trustee leadership, understanding legislation and policy, and investment management.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant supports the Association of Small Foundations, a national membership organization for foundations with few or no staff. Established in 1995, the grantee has more than 3,000 members who donate over $3 billion per year and manage assets of approximately $60 billion. Through conferences, seminars, webinars, and production and distribution of guides, handbooks, primers, and directories, the grantee provides its members with educational programming, targeted resources, networking opportunities, and a collective voice in and beyond the philanthropic community. Over the next two years, major activities will include hosting a Katrina @ 5 conference in New Orleans and a biennial conference in Austin in 2010; frequent day-length, in-person educational events around the country as well as distance learning offerings; policy-related work on legislation affecting small foundations; and greatly enhanced evaluation activities to assess the impact of the association and its members.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant supports the Association of Small Foundations, a national membership organization for foundations with few or no staff. Established in 1995, the grantee has nearly 2,600 members located in all 50 states who donate nearly $5 billion per year and steward assets of more than $82 billion. The grantee’s mission is to enhance the power of philanthropy by providing donors, trustees, and professionals with peer learning opportunities, resources, and a collective voice in and beyond philanthropy. It is the leading source of information, tools, best practices, benchmarking, and advice for small foundations. In 2011, the grantee’s educational programs attracted 1,586 attendees. Over the next two years, major activities will include a biennial conference in 2012, greater accessibility to members via new communications technology, and in-person and distance learning events around the country. Key topics will include board self-assessment, impact, human resources, leadership, self-dealing, interpersonal effectiveness, streamlining, and technology.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant supports the Association of Small Foundations, a national membership organization for foundations with few or no staff. Established in 1995, the grantee has nearly 2,400 members who donate approximately $4 billion per year and steward assets of more than $71 billion. The grantee’s mission is to enhance the power of philanthropy by providing donors, trustees, and professionals with peer learning opportunities, resources, and a collective voice in and beyond philanthropy. It is the leading source of information, tools, best practices, benchmarking, and advice for small-staff philanthropy. In 2013, support from members covered 70 percent of its/the grantee’s operating costs. Over the next three years, the grantee will complete a strategic reframing, launch and establish a new brand, increase membership, increase support from all small-staff philanthropists, expand services, and strengthen its capacity to connect and serve its audiences through technology.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant supports Exponent Philanthropy (formerly the Association of Small Foundations), a national membership organization dedicated to serving foundations with few or no staff, philanthropic families, and individual donors. Established in 1997, the grantee has over 2,000 members who donate more than $3.5 billion per year and steward assets of more than $77 billion. The grantee’s mission is to empower philanthropists to leverage their resources to amplify their impact. It is the leading source of information, tools, best practices, benchmarking, and advice for small-staff philanthropy. Having shifted its business model over the past few years, Exponent Philanthropy has expanded support from members to cover 80 percent of its operating costs in 2016. Over the next three years, the grantee’s top priorities will be to grow its membership, increase and diversify its revenue stream, build its reputation, and strengthen and maximize its internal systems and processes to enhance stakeholder satisfaction.

title: General Purposes
description: The concept of community foundations has been germinating in South Africa since the early 1990s. From 1998 to 2002, the Southern African Grantmakers Association tested the model in over ten communities, and one of the results was the establishment of the Greater Rustenburg Community Foundation in June 2000. This foundation is one of only a few community foundations successfully developed in South Africa. Recent core activities included mobilizing and distributing resources to local nonprofits, conducting community needs assessments, providing technical assistance to 200 nonprofits through a newly established center, funding more than 50 nonprofits totaling R1.5 million, and developing a youth philanthropy program. This renewal grant will support the continuation of core activities, in addition to providing skills development and mentoring for the foundation’s managers and staff. The Greater Rustenburg Community Foundation makes grants and provides capacity-building support to community-based organizations in the Northwest province.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purposes support to Asian Americans/Pacific Islanders in Philanthropy, a grantmaker affinity group committed to expanding the participation and leadership of the diverse Asian-American community in the philanthropic sector. Founded in 1990, the organization has built a strong and growing regional infrastructure of grantmakers and community leaders. The grantee offers a wide range of services and programs to enhance and increase philanthropy by and for Asian Americans, including conference sessions, publications, technical assistance, research, networking, and information sharing. Goals for the upcoming year include membership and chapter building; leadership development opportunities at the chapter level and within the board; further development of a capacity-building initiative to support Arab, Middle Eastern, Muslim, and Southern Asian organizations through small grants and technical assistance; and organizational development goals such as adding an office and increasing staff.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to Asian Americans/Pacific Islanders in Philanthropy, a grantmaker affinity group committed to expanding the participation and leadership of the diverse Asian-American community in the philanthropic sector. The grantee’s accomplishments include growing its membership to over 600 individuals and institutions (a 10 percent increase from 2008) and awarding $550,000 in grants to over 70 community-based organizations. Goals for the upcoming year include supporting identity-based affinity groups and philanthropic initiatives through collaborative funds, community and funder briefings, and research reports; expanding its National Donor Circle; and developing a detailed communications plan and a five-year strategy.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to Asian Americans/Pacific Islanders in Philanthropy, a grantmaker affinity group whose long-term goals are to increase philanthropic resources to Asian American/Pacific Islander communities; build the infrastructure of the community by creating and testing new approaches to social justice philanthropy; promote equity, diversity, and leadership in the philanthropic sector; and strengthen the network of individuals and institutions to engage and take action to build democratic philanthropy. Some of the group’s achievements include a national gender and equity campaign to support community organizations to integrate gender analysis into their work; a civic engagement fund to support Arab, Middle Eastern, Muslim, and South Asian community-based organizations; and a public-private partnership with the White House initiative in Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders. Among the group’s efforts over the next few years will be to expand its nationwide giving circle network from 26 to 50 by the end of 2015.

title: Bretton Woods Project
description: The Bretton Woods Project of ActionAid has been a key actor on international financial institution reform issues since it was established in 1995. It works with non-governmental organizations, researchers, and officials to scrutinize and reform policies and practices of international financial institutions, particularly the World Bank. During the grant period, the Bretton Woods Project will continue in its multiple roles as a clearinghouse for information and research; an advisor to non-governmental organization networks working on reform of international financial institutions based in the United Kingdom, other European countries and developing countries; a catalyst for strategy development and policy discussions; an interlocutor between non-governmental organizations and British government officials; and a source for information on international financial institutions and their policies and practices for the media.

title: Bretton Woods Project
description: The Bretton Woods Project of ActionAid has been a key actor on international financial institution reform issues since it was established in 1995. It works with nongovernmental organizations, researchers, and officials to scrutinize and reform policies and practices of international financial institutions, particularly the World Bank. During the grant period, the Bretton Woods Project will continue in its multiple roles as a clearinghouse for information and research; an advisor to nongovernmental organization networks working on reform of international financial institutions based in the United Kingdom, other European countries, and developing countries; a catalyst for strategy development and policy discussions; an interlocutor between nongovernmental organizations and British government officials; and a source for information on international financial institutions and their policies and practices for the media.

title: Bretton Woods Project
description: The Bretton Woods Project of ActionAid has taken a leadership role in helping to develop coherent civil society positions in response to the financial crisis, ensuring that attention is paid to the role of international financial instructions and global economic governance. This grant increase will support ActionAid’s efforts to develop a concerted international strategy for addressing the re-regulation of international finance and reform of the global economic architecture.

title: Bretton Woods Project
description: The Bretton Woods Project of ActionAid has taken a leadership role in helping to develop coherent civil society positions in response to the financial crisis, ensuring attention to the role of international financial institutions and global economic governance. This grant increase will support ActionAid’s efforts to take advantage of opportunities to influence the direction of financial reform at the international level.

title: Bretton Woods Project
description: The Bretton Woods Project of ActionAid has played a key role on international financial institution reform issues since it was established in 1995. It works with nongovernmental organizations, researchers, and officials to scrutinize and reform policies and practices of international financial institutions, particularly the World Bank and International Monetary Fund. During the recent grant period, the Bretton Woods Project was successful in changing the British government’s position on requiring targets that would rapidly move the World Bank toward a low-carbon energy portfolio. The Bretton Woods Project will continue in its multiple roles as a clearinghouse for information and research; an advisor to nongovernmental organization networks working on reform of international financial institutions based in the United Kingdom, other European and developing countries; a catalyst for strategy development and policy discussions; an interlocutor between nongovernmental organizations and British government officials; and a source for information on international financial institutions and their policies and practices for the media.

title: Bretton Woods Project
description: The Bretton Woods Project of ActionAid has been a key actor on international financial institution reform issues since it was established in 1995. It works with nongovernmental organizations, researchers, and officials to scrutinize and reform policies and practices of international financial institutions, particularly the World Bank. Over the past grant period, Bretton Woods Project’s policy analysis was an important input into the design of new development objectives for World Bank lending to private banks and investment funds. The project will continue its multiple roles as a clearinghouse for information and research; advisor to nongovernmental organization networks working on reform of international financial institutions; a catalyst for strategy development and policy discussions; an intermediary between nongovernmental organizations and British government officials; and a media source for information on international financial institutions and their policies and practices.

title: Bretton Woods Project
description: The Bretton Woods Project of ActionAid has been a key actor on international financial institution reform issues since it was established in 1995. It works with nongovernmental organizations, researchers, and officials to scrutinize and reform policies and practices of international financial institutions, particularly the World Bank Group. Over the last grant period, the grantee was successful in engaging with policymakers calling for a review of private sector investment policies at the World Bank Group and other development finance institutions. With this grant, the Bretton Woods Project will continue its work to strengthen civil society networks to advocate for reform of international financial institutions; support policy reform efforts to address environmental and social impacts; and ensure that governments of developing countries have more influence at the World Bank Group and International Monetary Fund.

title: Bretton Woods Project
description: The Bretton Woods Project of ActionAid has been a key actor on international financial institution reform issues since it was established in 1995. It works with nongovernmental organizations, researchers, and officials to scrutinize and reform policies and practices of international financial institutions, particularly the World Bank Group. Over the last grant period, the project helped to ensure that key issues in the safeguard policy review remained in the forefront of policy debates, particularly via its flagship publication that reaches 13,000 policymakers. With this grant, the Bretton Woods Project will continue its work to strengthen civil society networks to advocate for reform of international financial institutions; support policy reform efforts to address environmental and social impacts; and ensure that developing country governments have more influence at the World Bank Group and International Monetary Fund.

title: Bretton Woods Project
description: ActionAid’s Bretton Woods Project has been a key actor on international financial institution reform issues since it was established in 1995. It works with nongovernmental organizations, researchers, and officials to scrutinize and reform policies and practices of international financial institutions, particularly the World Bank Group. Over the last grant period, the project helped to ensure that strong climate change commitments were made by the World Bank Group and development outcomes for bank projects were strengthened. With this grant, the Bretton Woods Project will continue its work to strengthen civil society networks to: ensure that key climate change commitments are kept and strengthened; and provide an information platform that supports civil society organizations in the United Kingdom and developing countries to support policy reform efforts.

title: Halifax Initiative
description: This grant to the Sage Centre will continue support to the Halifax Initiative. The Halifax Initiative is a coalition of Canadian nongovernmental organizations that work to promote reforms in international financial institutions. Over the next two years, the project will focus on increased parliamentary accountability over Canadian government actions at the international financial institutions; expanded Canadian public support for policies at the international financial institutions that promote environmental sustainability, equitable development, and democratic accountability; and increased public accountability of international financial institutions to international environment, labor, and human rights standards. To achieve these objectives, the Halifax Initiative will conduct research, education, and outreach to the public and policymakers; monitor international financial institutions’ projects; and advocate for policy reform and coalition building.

title: Halifax Initiative
description: This grant increase to Tides Canada Initiatives (formerly the Sage Centre) will provide continued support for its Halifax Initiative project. The Halifax Initiative project brings together a coalition of Canadian nongovernmental organizations to work to promote reforms in international financial institutions. This grant increase will allow the Halifax Initiative project to actively engage on work related to the current global financial crisis and the multilateral responses through the Group of 20 and Group of 8.

title: Halifax Initiative
description: This grant to Tides Canada Initiatives will continue to support the Halifax Initiative project. The project is a coalition of Canadian, nongovernmental organizations that works to promote reforms in international financial institutions. Over this past year, the project has facilitated nongovernmental organization responses to the global financial crisis through various fora, including the Group of Eight, Group of 20, and the United Nations. Over the next two years, the project will focus on identifying opportunities and challenges for transforming the current international financial system in the wake of the financial crisis, and continue to monitor and evaluate international financial institution policies to assess whether they protect the environment and human rights. To achieve these objectives, the Halifax Initiative project will conduct research, education, and outreach to the public and policymakers; monitor the projects of international financial institutions; and advocate for policy reform and coalition building.

title: Halifax Initiative
description: This grant to Tides Canada Initiatives will support the Halifax Initiative project, which is a coalition of Canadian nongovernmental organizations that works to promote reforms in international financial institutions. With this grant increase, the Halifax Initiative will undertake additional work related to the financial transaction tax and organize civil society activities around the leaders’ summit meetings of the Group of 20 and Group of 8, scheduled to take place in June 2010 in Canada.

title: Halifax Initiative
description: This grant to Tides Canada Initiatives will support the Halifax Initiative project. The Halifax Initiative is a coalition of Canadian nongovernmental organizations that works to promote reforms in international financial institutions. Over the next two years, the project will focus on promoting greater accountability and enhanced transparency of the World Bank’s climate finance lending through the meaningful participation of developing countries and nongovernmental organizations; adoption of energy policies at the World Bank that decrease reliance on fossil fuels and promote energy conservation and renewable energy options; and policies and programs in other areas of the World Bank’s operations that contribute to poverty reduction and environmental sustainability. To achieve these objectives, the Halifax Initiative project will conduct research, education, and outreach to the public and policymakers; monitor international financial institutions’ projects; and advocate for policy reform and coalition building.

title: Halifax Initiative
description: This grant to Tides Canada Initiatives supports the Halifax Initiative project, which focuses on promoting greater accountability and enhanced transparency of World Bank lending. The Halifax Initiative project conducts policy analysis and outreach to the public and policymakers; monitors international financial institutions’ projects; and advocates for policy reform. This grant increase will support a strategic planning review of the Halifax Initiative and assist with the development of a new funding strategy for the project.

title: Great Lakes Water Protection Program
description: The Sierra Legal Defence Fund Society, a national group in Canada with offices in Vancouver and Toronto, uses law, science and public communication to help curb water pollution impacting the Great Lakes basin. In 2004, the society produced a report that described the status of water quality policy reform in Ontario. With this grant increase, the society will update the report, using 2006 as the new baseline year.

title: Great Lakes Water Protection Program
description: Ecojustice Canada, a national organization formerly known as the Sierra Legal Defence Fund Society, provides policy and legal expertise and other technical assistance to environmental groups in Ontario working to protect the Great Lakes. This renewal grant will allow the continuation of several highly successful activities designed to reduce the impacts of pollutants on the Great Lakes. These activities include addressing toxic water pollutants, upgrading sewage infrastructure, and eliminating the introduction of aquatic invasive species.

title: Great Lakes Water Protection Program
description: Ecojustice Canada, formerly known as the Sierra Legal Defence Fund Society, provides policy and legal expertise and other technical assistance to environmental groups in Ontario working to protect the Great Lakes. With previous Mott support, the grantee worked to improve Great Lakes water quality by addressing toxic pollutants, encouraging upgrades to sewage infrastructure, and identifying ways to eliminate the introduction of aquatic invasive species. With renewed support, Ecojustice Canada will continue these initiatives while also gathering and reporting pollution data and partnering with other nongovernmental organizations around the Great Lakes Water Quality Agreement.

title: Great Lakes Water Protection Program
description: Ecojustice Canada, formerly known as the Sierra Legal Defence Fund Society, seeks to protect the Great Lakes through scientific and legal research, policy analyses, and public education. With prior Mott support, the grantee worked to improve Great Lakes water quality by addressing toxic pollutants, encouraging upgrades to sewage infrastructure, and identifying ways to eliminate the introduction of aquatic invasive species. With renewed support, the grantee will continue these initiatives while also partnering with other nongovernmental organizations around the Great Lakes Water Quality Agreement.

title: Great Lakes Water Protection Program
description: Ecojustice Canada is a national environmental organization that seeks to protect Great Lakes water quality through scientific and legal research, policy analyses, and public education. With prior Mott support, the grantee helped inform the renegotiation of the U.S.-Canada Great Lakes Water Quality Agreement, engaged in binational discussions regarding the Asian Carp threat, and sought to reduce toxic freshwater pollutants. With renewed support, the grantee will inform how the Canada-Ontario Agreement is updated to implement the new Great Lakes Water Quality Agreement. The grantee will also continue to build public support for Great Lakes water quality issues and address high priority Great Lakes threats.

title: Great Lakes Water Protection Program
description: Ecojustice Canada is a national environmental organization that seeks to protect Great Lakes water quality through scientific and legal research, policy analyses, and public education. With prior Mott support, the grantee helped inform the renegotiation of the U.S.-Canada Great Lakes Water Quality Agreement, engaged in binational discussions regarding the Asian Carp threat, and sought to reduce toxic freshwater pollutants. With renewed support, the grantee will build on this work and continue to foster public support for addressing high priority Great Lakes threats.

title: General Purposes
description: Due in part to recent changes in federal rules, operators of some hydropower dams in New York are seeking to amend licenses that were issued within the past few years. New York Rivers United, the leading group in New York working on hydropower issues, will participate in the license amendment proceedings. This grant increase, and associated grant period extension, will support the group’s general purposes, including helping to cover the expenses associated with its additional hydropower work.

title: General Purposes
grantee: National Alliance for Choice in Giving
description: The National Alliance for Choice in Giving is a membership organization of local, state and regional workplace giving funds that support various issues. Its network of 57 workplace giving federations includes more than 2,000 organizations that generate more than $100 million for the nonprofit sector annually. The alliance provides specialized training and a national forum for collaboration, information sharing and strategy development. This grant increase will enable the alliance to implement a new operational and fundraising plan, which will allow it to transition to a revenue model that will be less reliant on foundation grants.

title: Parade of Festivals
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Greater Flint Arts Council provides the leadership for a coalition of stakeholders who are helping to improve the image of Flint through increased participation in summertime festivals and events. This grant will support the council’s effort to implement a multimedia marketing and promotional campaign that seeks to maximize the impact of established events and to provide direct financial support to newer and smaller events in downtown Flint. The 2006 Parade of Festivals will include a lunchtime concert series and nine multiday events.

title: Parade of Festivals
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Greater Flint Arts Council provides the leadership for a coalition of stakeholders who are helping to improve the image of Flint through increased participation in summertime festivals and events. The Parade of Festivals is based on the premise that increasing the number and diversity of people having an enjoyable time in downtown Flint will help break down barriers to economic growth and will generate increased public interest in the redevelopment of downtown Flint. This renewal grant will allow the Greater Flint Arts Council to continue to implement a multimedia marketing and promotional campaign that seeks to maximize the impact of established events and provide direct financial support to newer and smaller events.

initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This renewal grant supports the continuation of several community festivals, which are operated by and supported through the Greater Flint Arts Council. Using a coordinated marketing strategy, the grantee leads a coalition of stakeholders that are dedicated to improving the image of Flint through increased participation in summertime festivals and events. The project seeks to break down barriers to economic growth and generate public interest in the redevelopment of downtown Flint. Since 1999, the Parade of Festivals has increased the number and diversity of people having a memorable time in downtown Flint. This year will mark the 13th year of support for the Parade of Festivals.

title: Parade of Festivals
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant supports the production and marketing coordination of a series of outdoor festivals and events that will be held in and around downtown Flint during the summer months. The Parade of Festivals was created in 1999 to enhance Flint’s image within the region and enliven the downtown area. The Greater Flint Arts Council, an organization dedicated to nurturing independent artists and arts organizations in the Flint area, manages the events. In 2013, the Parade of Festivals will include a diverse array of 21 events held between Memorial Day and mid-October.

title: Parade of Festivals
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Greater Flint Arts Council is providing the leadership for a coalition of downtown Flint stakeholders aimed at improving the image of downtown Flint through increased participation in festivals and events from June through mid-October. A marketing and promotional campaign is designed to maximize the impact of established events and cultivate newer and smaller events in downtown Flint thereby attracting new audiences each year. The 2014 Parade of Festivals will include a lunchtime concert series at the new Farmers’ Market pavilion, and a line-up of 18 festivals including nine produced by smaller arts/cultural organizations.

title: Parade of Festivals
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Greater Flint Arts Council is providing leadership for a coalition of downtown Flint stakeholders aimed at improving the image of downtown Flint through increased participation in existing summertime festivals and events. This funding supports a marketing and promotion campaign designed to maximize the impact of established events and to cultivate newer and smaller events in downtown Flint. The 2015 Parade of Festivals will include the Flint Jazz Festival, Flint Festival of Quilts, and nine independently produced festivals.

title: Parade of Festivals
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Greater Flint Arts Council continues to provide leadership for a coalition of stakeholders aimed at improving the image of downtown Flint through increased participation in existing summertime festivals and events. This funding supports a marketing and promotion campaign designed to maximize the impact of established events and to cultivate newer and smaller events in the downtown Flint area. In 2016, the Parade of Festivals will also include the first downtown restaurant week which will take place in May.

title: Parade of Festivals
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Greater Flint Arts Council continues to provide leadership for a coalition of stakeholders aimed at improving the image of downtown Flint through increased participation in summertime and early fall festivals and events. This funding supports a marketing and promotion campaign designed to maximize the impact of established events and to cultivate newer and smaller events in the downtown Flint area.

title: Parade of Festivals
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Greater Flint Arts Council continues to provide leadership for a coalition of stakeholders aimed at improving the image of the Flint area, including downtown, through increased participation in festivals and events especially during warm weather months. This funding supports a marketing and promotion campaign designed to maximize the impact of established events and to cultivate newer and smaller events in downtown Flint and neighborhoods throughout the city.
