title: Workforce Training and Technical Assistance
grantee: Insight Center for Community Economic Development
description: This grant will provide continued support to the National Economic Development and Law Center (NEDLC) for the Workforce Training and Technical Assistance project to assist in the implementation of sectoral employment initiatives in the Mississippi Delta. NEDLC will supply the sectoral employment sites with ongoing research and analysis, programmatic technical assistance, training, and resource development assistance. Through this work, NEDLC will help relocated hurricane refugees connect to livable-wage careers and assist several communities, including New Orleans, prepare residents to resume permanent employment.NEDLC is a national research and consulting organization dedicated to building economic health and opportunity in vulnerable communities. Through partnerships, it seeks to develop innovative strategies and programs that result in systemic change and help people become, and remain, economically secure.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued general purposes support to the Philanthropy Roundtable, a national association of individual donors, foundation trustees and staff, and corporate giving officers. The roundtable’s mission is to: foster excellence in philanthropy; protect philanthropic freedom; assist donors in achieving their philanthropic intent; and to help donors advance liberty, opportunity, and personal responsibility in America and abroad. Programs and services for grantmakers include: a national conference; regional meetings; publication of “Philanthropy” magazine and funder guidebooks; and “breakthrough groups” on the topics of K-12 education, conservation, higher education, and national security. Grant funds will also support the Alliance for Charitable Reform, a project of the roundtable which is dedicated to protecting the freedom and philosophical diversity of foundations.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued general purpose support to the Philanthropy Roundtable, a national association of individual donors, foundations, donor advisors, and corporate-giving programs. The roundtable works to foster excellence in philanthropy; protect philanthropic freedom; assist donors in achieving their philanthropic intent; and help donors advance liberty, opportunity, and personal responsibility in America and abroad. Significant accomplishments include convening numerous national conferences and regional meetings; publishing “Philanthropy” magazine and funder guidebooks; and creating breakthrough groups on the topics of K-12 education, conservation, and social equity. Grant funds will continue to support the aforementioned activities as well as the Alliance for Charitable Reform — a project dedicated to protect the freedom and philosophical diversity of foundations.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued general purpose support to the Philanthropy Roundtable, a national association of over 550 foundations, families, individual philanthropists, corporate giving programs, and trust and estate officers. The grantee provides a variety of programs and services for grantmakers including a national conference, regional meetings, publication of “Philanthropy” magazine, thematic publications, and public policy work. The association also offers customized services for focused affinity groups in the areas of K-12 education, conservation, national security, higher education, and economic opportunity. The grantee’s two major goals for 2011 and 2012 are to: 1) preserve the freedom and philosophical diversity of the philanthropic sector; and 2) maintain consistently high standards for participation and content in its meetings and publications with a focus on breakthrough philanthropic strategies that offer solutions for America’s greatest problems.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued general purpose support to the Philanthropy Roundtable, a national association of over 630 foundations, families, individual philanthropists, corporate giving programs, and trust and estate officers. The grantee provides a variety of programs and services for grantmakers including a national conference, regional meetings, publication of “Philanthropy” magazine, thematic publications, and public policy work. The grantee also offers customized services for focused affinity groups in the areas of K-12 education, economic opportunity, and support to veterans. The grantee’s two major goals for 2013 and 2014 are to: 1) preserve the freedom and philosophical diversity of the philanthropic sector; and 2) maintain consistently high standards for participation and content in its meetings and publications, with a focus on breakthrough philanthropic strategies that offer solutions for America’s greatest problems.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued general purpose support to the Philanthropy Roundtable, a national association of 625 foundations, families, individual philanthropists, corporate giving programs, and trust and estate officers. The grantee helps donors achieve their charitable goals and protects their freedom to give as they choose by providing a variety of programs and services for grantmakers including a national conference, regional meetings, publication of “Philanthropy” magazine, thematic publications, and public policy work. Its major topic-focused thematic areas are K-12 education reform, economic opportunity, and veterans. Beyond its routine educational programs and services, the grantee’s specific objectives for 2015 are to facilitate 10 major philanthropic breakthroughs, vigorously support public policy efforts to defend philanthropic freedom through its Alliance for Charitable Reform project, and publish an Almanac of American Philanthropy.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued general purpose support to the Philanthropy Roundtable, a national association of 650 foundations, families, individual philanthropists, corporate giving programs, trust officers, and estate officers. The grantee exists to help donors achieve their charitable goals and protect their freedom to give as they choose. It provides a variety of programs and services for grantmakers including a national conference, regional meetings, publication of “Philanthropy” magazine, thematic publications, and public policy work. Major topic-focused thematic areas include K-12 education, economic opportunity, veterans, character formation, entrepreneurship, and donor intent. Over 2017-2018, the grantee will continue its educational and convening services, particularly in the areas identified above, and vigorously support public policy efforts to defend philanthropic freedom through its Alliance for Charitable Reform project.

title: International Program
initiative: Reform of International Finance and Trade
description: Earthjustice’s International Program works to ensure that international trade institutions are more responsive to environmental concerns and more effective in promoting sustainable development. The program includes a combination of domestic and international networking and direct engagement with international trade and investment bodies. The program will focus on creating citizen access to policy and decisionmaking processes; preventing harm to humans and the environment resulting from international investment practices; creating incentives for powerful nations to advocate for stronger international safeguards; and strengthening international constituencies.

title: International Program
initiative: Reform of International Finance and Trade
description: Earthjustice’s International Program works to ensure that international trade institutions are more responsive to environmental concerns and more effective in promoting sustainable development. The program includes a combination of domestic and international networking and direct engagement with international trade and investment bodies. This grant increase and grant extension will allow Earthjustice to complete its strategic planning process.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Association for Civil Society Development - SMART
description: This grant will enable the Association for Civil Society Development – SMART to continue providing training and consultations; collecting and analyzing data on civil society development in the Rijeka region; and strengthening staff and organizational capacities.During 2005, the association provided training and direct technical assistance to more than 500 non-governmental organizations and distributed a variety of resource materials.Based in Rijeka, Croatia, the association is a professional training and resource organization for the nonprofit sector in Croatia.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Association for Civil Society Development - SMART
description: This grant provides core support to the Association for Civil Society Development – SMART, a professional training and resource organization for the nonprofit sector in Croatia. The grantee’s mission is to build the capacity of nongovernmental organizations and informal citizen groups to respond to community needs. To this end, the grantee is providing training and resources to the nonprofit sector, strengthening structured cooperation between the public and nonprofit sectors, and promoting volunteerism and philanthropy in local communities. In 2006-2008, the grantee provided training and direct technical assistance to over 550 representatives from nongovernmental organizations, informal associations, and local government and published widely distributed resource materials. Through its volunteer center, the grantee maintains a database of 26 organizations and institutions that have been trained to work with volunteers. Based in Rijeka, Croatia, the grantee is a key member of several Croatia-wide nonprofit sector networks addressing volunteerism, rural development, and professional training.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Association for Civil Society Development - SMART
description: This grant provides core support to the Association for Civil Society Development – SMART, a professional training and resource organization for the nonprofit sector in Croatia. The grantee’s mission is to build the capacity of nongovernmental organizations and informal citizen groups to respond to community needs. To this end, the grantee will provide targeted training to the nonprofit sector, strengthen structured cooperation between the public and nonprofit sectors, and promote volunteerism and philanthropy in local communities. In 2008-2010, the grantee provided training to over 950 representatives from nongovernmental organizations, informal associations, and local government and published three widely distributed resource materials. Through its volunteer center, the grantee maintains a database of 50 organizations and institutions that have been trained to work with more than 350 volunteers. Based in Rijeka, Croatia, the grantee is a member of several Croatia-wide nonprofit sector networks addressing volunteerism, rural development, and training.

title: Future Minority Teachers Initiative
description: The University of Michigan-Flint’s School of Education and Human Services is responsible for graduating the majority of new K-12 teachers employed in Flint and Genesee County. More than half of the students enrolled in the Flint schools are African American and the district is eager to recruit more teachers of color.This grant will enable the university’s Center for Service Learning and School Partnerships to continue student-centered activities at Flint Northern High School that will provide exposure to the teaching profession for students of color and increase parental involvement in each student’s college preparation. Project staff will work with Flint Northern High School graduates enrolled at the university, providing supports needed to help them graduate.

title: Community Foundation Development in Russia
description: The Charities Aid Foundation (CAF) has been providing technical assistance, support services, and more recently, challenge grants to emerging Russian community foundations. A total of 20 Russian community foundations exist throughout the country since the first one was registered in 1998. At present, Russian community foundations in aggregate award close to $1 million in grants annually.This grant will enable CAF to continue its challenge grant program to Russian community foundations. Besides matching funding for operational expenses, institutional development and endowment-building, challenge grants also will stimulate community foundations to expand their donor base, encourage giving by individuals and address social change. CAF also will continue to provide technical assistance and networking opportunities to existing and emerging community foundations.

title: Community Foundation Development in Russia
description: The program goal is to further the development of community foundations in Russia. Through this program, Charities Aid Foundation will award small grants for start-up and consolidation of new community foundations, as well as target grants to strengthen regional alliances and to identify meaningful models for effecting social change. In addition, the grantee will continue to provide ongoing technical assistance and networking opportunities to existing and emerging community foundations in Russia. This technical and financial support to the development of community foundations in Russia has seen their number grow to almost 35 with local fundraising exceeding $7 million in 2007, more than double the amount raised in 2006. Charities Aid Foundation distributes more than $500 million annually to charitable causes worldwide on behalf of individual, corporate, and trust clients. Based in the United Kingdom, it has offices in Russia, Australia, Bulgaria, India, South Africa, and the United States.

title: Community Foundation Development in Russia
description: The program goal is to further the development of community foundations in Russia. Through this program, the Charities Aid Foundation will award small grants for start-up and consolidation of new community foundations, as well as targeted grants to strengthen regional alliances and to identify meaningful models for effecting social change. In the difficult economic circumstances of 2009-2010, community foundations used challenge grants to raise four times as much from local resources. Additional technical and financial support resulted in the establishment of five regional alliances, which are well-positioned to allow members to exchange experience efficiently and to advance their collective interests more effectively. The grantee distributes more than $500 million annually to charitable causes worldwide on behalf of individual, corporate, and trust clients. Based in the United Kingdom, it has offices in Russia, Australia, Bulgaria, India, South Africa, and the United States.

title: Community Foundation Development in Russia
description: The program goal is to further the development of community foundations in Russia. Through this program, the Charities Aid Foundation will award small grants for start-up and consolidation of new community foundations, as well as targeted grants to strengthen regional alliances and to identify meaningful models for effecting social change. In 2011-2012, the program saw the establishment of six new community foundations that raised over $240,000 from local sources, or eight times the value of program-funded challenge grants. Additional technical and financial support resulted in the strengthening of five regional alliances. Two such alliances adapted influential social indicator methodologies that helped identify key social policy challenges and resource opportunities in their respective regions. The Charities Aid Foundation distributes more than $500 million annually to charitable causes worldwide on behalf of individual, corporate, and trust clients. Based in the United Kingdom, it has offices in Russia, Australia, Bulgaria, India, South Africa, and the United States.

title: Community Foundation Development in Russia
description: The program goal is to further the development of community foundations in Russia. Through this program, the Charities Aid Foundation will award small grants for start-up and consolidation of new community foundations, as well as grants to strengthen regional alliances and identify meaningful models for effecting social change. With this increase, the grantee will commission a detailed study on the state of community foundations in Russia. The study will consolidate much of the quantitative data gathered by the grantee in Russia over its many years of support to community foundations in Russia. At the same time, it will examine field-level qualitative issues related to the local, regional, and national impacts of community foundation work.

title: Community Foundation Development in Russia
description: The program goal is to further the development of community foundations in Russia. Through this program, the Charities Aid Foundation will award small grants for startup and strengthening of community foundations, as well as targeted grants to reinforce regional alliances. The grantee will also work to improve community assessment tools and to elaborate meaningful indicators of community foundation impact in Russia. In 2013-2014, the program saw the establishment of five new community foundations, bringing the total in Russia to 50. The grantee also undertook a comprehensive survey of the community foundation field in Russia and subsequently published and widely distributed its findings on the growing community leadership role played by these institutions. During the grant period, community foundations in Russia raised over $5 million from local sources. The Charities Aid Foundation distributes more than $500 million annually to charitable causes worldwide on behalf of individual, corporate, and trust clients. Based in the United Kingdom, it has offices in Russia, Australia, Bulgaria, India, South Africa, and the United States.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Princess Margarita of Romania Foundation - Romania
description: This grant will enable the Princess Margarita of Romania Foundation to support local community initiatives involving non-governmental organizations, public institutions and individual leaders in finding and implementing sustainable solutions for problems in the social services, health and education fields.Since its registration as an independent Romanian organization in 1998, the foundation has strengthened the capacity of more than 90 child protection non-governmental organizations; increased awareness of institutions and the general public about the rights of the elderly; and promoted income-generating activities in poor communities.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Princess Margarita of Romania Foundation - Romania
description: The program goal is to improve the quality of life of vulnerable people in Romanian communities. The Princess Margarita of Romania Foundation will support local initiatives involving nongovernmental organizations, public institutions, and individual leaders in finding and implementing sustainable solutions for problems in the social services, health, and education fields. In addition, the foundation will strengthen its financial stability by building an unrestricted operational reserve fund. Since its registration as an independent Romanian organization in 1998, the foundation has strengthened the capacity of over 120 child protection nongovernmental organizations, increased awareness of institutions and the general public about the rights of the elderly, and promoted income-generating activities in poor communities.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Princess Margarita of Romania Foundation - Romania
description: This grant provides core support to the Princess Margarita of Romania Foundation – Romania, which is one of the leading philanthropic organizations in the developing philanthropic sector in Romania. With oversight by members of the Romanian royal family, the grantee’s principal mission is to develop and support projects that improve health care and address special needs of children, youth, and the elderly. During the grant period, the grantee will adopt a new strategic direction for its programs and operations, develop new programs and services, and improve its cooperation with other foundations and nonprofits in Romania. In addition, the grantee will strengthen its organizational capacity and financial stability. The grantee’s key achievements to date include strengthening the capacity of over 120 child protection nongovernmental organizations, increasing awareness of institutions and the general public about the rights of the elderly, and promoting income-generating activities in poor communities.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Princess Margarita of Romania Foundation - Romania
description: This grant provides core support to the Princess Margarita of Romania Foundation – Romania, a long-time Mott grantee. Since 1990, with oversight by members of the Romanian royal family, the grantee’s principal mission has been to develop and support projects that improve health care and address special needs of children, youth, and the elderly. During the grant period, the grantee will restructure its programs and optimize the size and roles of its board and staff to reflect the changes in its operational environment and the evolving role of HRH Princess Margarita in Romanian society. The grantee’s key achievements to date include strengthening the capacity of over 120 child protection nongovernmental organizations, increasing awareness of institutions and the general public about the rights of the elderly, and promoting income-generating activities in poor communities.

title: General Purposes
description: The Pitseng Trust was established in 1998 by women in Johannesburg who were inspired by Mama Cash in the Netherlands and the Global Fund for Women. As a dedicated women’s fund, the grantee’s major goal is to support and build the capacity of local women’s organizations, especially those working on women’s economic development through grantmaking, training, and capacity building. Since its establishment, it has made a number of small grants to women-led, community-based organizations. This grant will provide support to the grantee to continue to address its many challenges and to establish itself as an effective women’s grantmaking organization.

title: General Purposes
description: The Pitseng Trust was established in 1998 by women in Johannesburg who were inspired by Mama Cash in the Netherlands and the Global Fund for Women. As a dedicated women’s fund, the grantee’s major goal is to support and build the capacity of local women’s organizations, especially those working on income generation and economic development through grantmaking, training, and capacity building. Past successes include training and mentoring a group of women’s groups through an initiative termed Nthweshe kego Rweshe Women’s Initiatives and making grants to small community-based organizations. This grant will continue support for the trust’s operations helping it become a more effective women’s grantmaking organization.

title: General Purposes
description: The Pitseng Trust was established in 1998 by women in Johannesburg who were inspired by Mama Cash in the Netherlands and the Global Fund for Women. As a dedicated women’s fund, its major goal is to support and build the capacity of local women’s organizations, especially those working on income generation and economic development through grantmaking, training, and capacity building. Past successes include training and mentoring women’s groups through an initiative termed Nthweshe kego Rweshe Women’s Initiatives and making grants to small community-based organizations. This grant increase will support the grantee in appointing a new executive director and to introduce systems that will help it become more effective.

title: General Purposes
description: The Pitseng Trust was established in 1998 by women in Johannesburg who were inspired by Mama Cash in the Netherlands and the Global Fund for Women. As a dedicated women’s fund, the organization’s major goal is to support and build the capacity of local women’s organizations, especially those working on income generation and economic development, through grantmaking, training, and capacity building. Over the past two years, the grantee supported a range of projects that grew in size and assets. As a result, three grantee-supported projects are now fully self-sufficient. The grantee also improved its organizational systems and processes, produced a newsletter on African indigenous knowledge, and introduced an electronic grantmaking system. This grant will continue support for women’s initiatives in poor communities so that they can be economically independent and able to realize their rights.

title: General Purposes
description: Pitseng Trust is a dedicated woman’s fund that supports local women’s organizations in disadvantaged communities across South Africa. It supports organizations that work on income-generation projects through grantmaking, providing training and support, and creating opportunities for the women to learn from each other. Over the past two years, the grantee supported a number of projects that are now receiving support and recognition from government and local businesses. The grantee also hosted a number of women’s dialogues in different provinces as part of its monitoring and evaluation process. This grant will support the grantee to review its role as a grantmaker and develop new approaches to its work. The grantee will continue to provide technical support to local groups for their growth and development.

title: General Purposes
description: The Eastern Cape NGO Coalition is one of the most effective networks of nongovernmental and community-based organizations in South Africa. It has developed a good working relationship with the Eastern Cape provincial government and is succeeding in organizing the nonprofit and community-based organizations in the Eastern Cape into a significant collective force. Many challenges still remain, including securing the longer-term sustainability of the coalition. This renewal grant will provide support to the coalition to continue to build and strengthen its membership, represent their interests, advocate on behalf of nongovernmental and community-based organizations in the Eastern Cape, and secure more stable sources of funding.

title: General Purposes
description: Founded in 1995, the Eastern Cape NGO Coalition is a network of more than 360 nongovernmental, community-based organizations. It has provided its members with services, technical assistance, and capacity building opportunities and helped them more effectively implement programs to meet diverse economic development, social service, and health needs of the province’s marginalized populations. The grantee is the most developed among South Africa’s nine provincial coalitions. This grant will enable the coalition to continue its research and policy work; technical assistance; capacity building; and networking and information sharing.

title: General Purposes
description: Established in 1995, the Eastern Cape NGO Coalition is an association of 140 nongovernmental, community-based, and faith-based organizations operating in the Eastern Cape province of South Africa. The members share common values based on a collective desire to combat poverty and inequality. The grantee supports advocacy, leadership development, and learning in an effort to help mobilize civil society organizations to lead socioeconomic transformation within their communities. Past support assisted the grantee to organize the nonprofit sector in the Eastern Cape province and facilitate strategic alliances between government, the nonprofit sector, and business. It also trained members on various topical subjects including understanding local governance, strategies to deal with HIV/AIDS, and land and rural development with a focus on food security. This grant will support the grantee to strengthen the networking and mutual learning among its members and to continue to train them on topics relevant to their work.

title: General Purposes
description: The Eastern Cape NGO Coalition is a provincial membership organization that works to support and promote the work of development organizations in the Eastern Cape province. It is one of the few remaining coalitions of nonprofit organizations in South Africa and has a membership of over 166 community-based, faith-based, and nongovernmental organizations. The grantee coordinates the work of its members to achieve maximum impact on social transformation and to continuously build synergies that will develop a strong sectoral or issue-based focus. Over the past two years, the grantee partnered with members working on agriculture, health, housing, human rights, and education programs to champion their causes. It also partnered with government on initiatives aimed at strengthening civil society in the province. This grant will support the grantee to promote community-led development approaches, elevate its members’ work on local philanthropy, build linkages between government and its members, and strengthen its institutional capacity.

title: General Purposes
description: The Eastern Cape NGO Coalition is a membership organization established in 1995 to support the development of nonprofits and community-based organizations in the Eastern Cape province of South Africa. The grantee has a membership of over 160 organizations and works to build relationships between government, nonprofits, and businesses that respond to poverty and inequality in the province. Previous support has enabled the grantee to partner with government and businesses on programs aimed at strengthening civil society in the province, develop a toolkit to support members build their institutional capacity, and form partnerships that advance a community-led approach to development. This grant will support the Eastern Cape NGO Coalition to continue providing a platform for government and businesses to engage with nonprofits in the province, represent its members in provincial policy dialogues, and provide training and mentoring on topics such as leadership and good governance to its members.

title: General Purposes
description: The Eastern Cape NGO Coalition is a provincial membership organization that supports and promotes the work of development organizations in the Eastern Cape province. It is one of the few remaining coalitions of nonprofit organizations in South Africa and has a membership of over 617 civil society organizations. The grantee coordinates the work of its members to achieve maximum impact on social transformation and to build synergies that will develop a strong sectoral or issue-based focus. Over the past two years, the grantee provided training to local government officials on community-led development approaches, hosted dialogues for its members to discuss topical issues, and created linkages between its members and local businesses. This grant will enable the grantee to continue promoting community-led development approaches in the Eastern Cape province; supporting the development of its members; and building partnerships between government departments, civil society organizations, and the private sector.

title: Programs to Reform Global Economic Institutions
initiative: Reform of International Finance and Trade
description: The Center for International Environmental Law was founded to strengthen international environmental law, policy, and management. This grant will support new and continuing activities in the following three areas: promoting greater accountability and stronger environmental policies in international trade law and institutions; reducing the environmental and social impacts of the World Bank and other international financial institutions’ lending programs; and promoting greater accountability, disclosure, and sensitivity to environmental concerns by private international investors in developing countries. Under this grant renewal, project activities will include researching existing policies and developing policy reform proposals, sharing information and developing joint strategies with other nongovernmental organizations, conducting outreach to government officials and managers of international financial and trade institutions, and preparing and disseminating publications on key issues.

title: General Purposes
description: The mission of the Czech Donors Forum is to support the development of civil society by promoting philanthropy and encouraging donor agencies to work together toward utilizing available resources in the most effective way.This grant will enable the forum to encourage an increase in the level of corporate and individual giving in the Czech Republic; improve the transparency and efficiency of local grantmakers; and strengthen its own organizational capacity and sustainability.Since its establishment in 1997, the forum has provided strong leadership to Czech donors as well as to the whole nonprofit sector in the Czech Republic. Currently, the forum has more than 50 regular members, which include both foundations and corporations, and is active in various regional and international initiatives.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to promote philanthropy in the Czech Republic and encourage donor agencies to work together toward utilizing available resources in the most effective way. To this end, the Czech Donors Forum will provide services to various groups of donors to increase the level of corporate and individual giving in the Czech Republic, improve the transparency and efficiency of local grantmakers, and strengthen its own organizational capacity and sustainability. In 2007-2009, the forum strengthened its services to corporations, improved tools and strategies for donations from the general public, and organized high profile conferences and award ceremonies in the field of philanthropy. Since its establishment in 1997, the forum has provided strong leadership to Czech donors as well as to the whole nonprofit sector in the Czech Republic. In addition, the forum is providing vital support to other donors’ fora in the region by coordinating Central and Eastern European Network for Responsible Giving since 2005.

title: International Community Foundation Fellows Program
grantee: City University of New York Graduate Center
description: The International Community Foundation Fellows Program of the City University of New York Graduate Center, housed within the university’s Center on Philanthropy and Civil Society, provides scholars and professionals from South Africa, Central/Eastern Europe and other world regions with opportunities to learn about community foundations through an intensive graduate program of research, seminars, conferences, mentoring and internships. Currently, City University of New York runs a three-month program for emerging leaders who are under 36 years of age and a one-month program for senior fellows over 35. This grant increase will support the participation of one Central/Eastern European in the 2006 Senior Fellows Program.

title: International Community Foundation Fellows Program
grantee: Research Foundation of the City University of New York
description: The program goal is to enhance the development of community philanthropy globally. To this end, the Research Foundation of the City University of New York, in cooperation with the City University of New York Graduate Center, runs an annual international community foundation fellowship program. Each year, the program offers emerging leaders and seasoned community foundation practitioners from foreign countries opportunities to learn about community foundations through an intensive graduate program of research, seminars, conferences, mentoring, and internships. To date, the International Community Foundation Fellows Program has provided fellowships to over 100 individuals from more than 40 countries. The program has sparked the creation of a number of new philanthropic ventures and research resources in places as diverse as Argentina, Brazil, India, Korea, the Philippines, Russia, and Ukraine.

title: International Community Foundation Fellows Program
grantee: Research Foundation of the City University of New York
description: The City University of New York Graduate Center runs an annual international community foundation fellowship program with the aim of enhancing the development of community philanthropy globally. Each year, the program offers emerging leaders and seasoned community foundation practitioners from foreign countries opportunities to learn about community foundations through an intensive graduate program of research, seminars, conferences, mentoring, and internships. To date, the International Community Foundation Fellows Program has provided fellowships to 118 individuals from more than 40 countries. This grant increase will enable the center to offer a more adequate stipend and offset rising transportation and housing costs for the five fellows expected to participate over 2008 and 2009. The Research Foundation of the City University of New York administers grants on behalf of the center.

title: International Community Foundation Fellows Program
grantee: Research Foundation of the City University of New York
description: The Center on Philanthropy and Civil Society at the City University of New York Graduate Center runs an annual international community foundation fellowship program with the aim of enhancing the development of community philanthropy globally. Each year, the program offers emerging leaders and seasoned community foundation practitioners from around the world opportunities to learn more about community foundations through an intensive graduate program of research, seminars, conferences, mentoring, and internships. Since its inception in 1989, the International Community Foundation Fellows Program has provided fellowships to 136 individuals from 50 countries. Due to the economic crisis, the center has encountered unanticipated revenue shortfalls for the second half of 2009. This grant increase will provide bridge funding so that the center can conduct its senior fellows program in the fall. The Research Foundation of the City University of New York administers grants on behalf of the center.

grantee: Research Foundation of the City University of New York
