title: General Purposes
grantee: Local Activity Support Center - CAL Association
description: The program goal is to strengthen community development in Poland. Local Activity Support Center – CAL Association will strengthen the capacity of 200 local communities to engage in effective community development, train 400 professionals in community development and “social animation,” increase its research and publication work, and strengthen cooperation with the national government in the field of community development. Since its establishment in 2000, Local Activity Support Center – CAL Association has been creating strong and integrated communities through developing local solidarity, unlocking local resources, and mobilizing local institutions to respond better to the needs of their constituencies.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued general purposes support to Community Foundations of Canada, an association of 155 community foundations which collectively hold about $2.5 billion in assets and award grants totaling more than $140 million annually. The association’s three key goals are to: (1) support established and developing community foundations in their endowment building and donor services, grantmaking, and community leadership; and as accountable stewards of community assets; (2) promote and advance philanthropy and community foundations; and (3) model philanthropic leadership in Canada and internationally. Recent programming has included the release of national marketing materials adapted from those developed by the Council on Foundations in the United States; the launch in four major Canadian cities of “Vital Signs”, a community assessment report commissioned by community foundations; and national initiatives in the areas of youth in philanthropy, environment, social justice, community leadership, and donor engagement. In the upcoming two years, Community Foundations of Canada will focus on positioning and branding community foundations as philanthropic leaders, strengthening its organizational effectiveness and excellence, and ensuring sustainability.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued general purpose support to Community Foundations of Canada, an association of 165 community foundations. The association’s three key goals are to: 1) support established and developing community foundations in their endowment building and donor services, grantmaking, and community leadership and as accountable stewards of community assets; 2) promote and advance philanthropy and community foundations; and 3) model philanthropic leadership in Canada and internationally. Recent programming has included “Vital Signs”, an annual community assessment report commissioned by community foundations and simultaneously released in 15 major Canadian cities; a highly successful biennial conference; and national initiatives in the areas of youth in philanthropy, environment, social justice, community restoration, and resources for professional advisors. In the upcoming two years, the association will focus on positioning community foundations as leaders in community philanthropy, strengthening organizational effectiveness and excellence, and ensuring sustainability of the community foundation movement and the association itself.

title: National Conference on Black Philanthropy
grantee: National Center for Black Philanthropy, Inc.
description: This grant provides partial support to the National Center for Black Philanthropy, Inc., to plan and hold the sixth National Conference on Black Philanthropy, scheduled for June 27-29, 2007, in Washington, D.C., entitled, “Philanthropy and the Covenant with Black America.” The conference theme is based on Tavis Smiley’s book, “The Covenant with Black America” and philanthropy’s response to the book and the issues it raises. The conference is expected to draw 400-500 people and will include a “Hands-on Philanthropy Day,” in which conference registrants donate time to work on a local community project. Other conference elements include pre-conference workshops, roundtables, panels, an awards dinner, and a prayer breakfast.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen civil society in Hungary through promoting and developing individual giving, corporate giving, and volunteering. Established in 1991, Eroforras Foundation (United Way Hungary) has emerged as one of the few Hungarian philanthropic funds strengthening civil society; facilitating cooperation between business and nonprofit organizations; and supporting human and healthcare services through an open, efficient, and transparent fundraising and grantmaking process. This grant supports the general purposes of the organization.

title: Building an Enabling Legal Environment for Ukraine's Nonprofit Sector
description: This grant will enable the International Center for Not-for-Profit Law to continue providing technical assistance in the drafting and implementation of legislation affecting non-governmental organizations (NGOs) and the development of philanthropy in Ukraine. The center also will undertake educational initiatives for lawyers, government officials, parliamentarians, and NGO leaders on legislation and legal issues affecting the nonprofit sector.Recent accomplishments included publishing and distributing numerous books, handbooks and manuals on NGO legislation, taxation of NGOs and public financing of NGOs; building NGO capacity in the areas of social contracting and citizen participation in decisionmaking; and providing information, consulting and training to Ukrainian NGOs, government officials, members of parliament and their staff, and representatives of international organizations.The center, established in 1993, is the only international organization providing a full range of legal services for the support and development of the legal and regulatory structure governing civil society and the nonprofit sector in emerging and developed countries around the world.

title: Building an Enabling Legal Environment for Ukraine's Nonprofit Sector
description: This program supports the development of an enabling legal and regulatory environment for Ukraine’s nonprofit sector. Grant funds will enable the International Center for Not-for-Profit Law to provide technical assistance in the drafting and implementation of legislation affecting nongovernmental organizations and the development of philanthropy. The grantee will also undertake educational initiatives for lawyers, government officials, parliamentarians, and nongovernmental organization leaders on legislation and legal issues affecting the nonprofit sector. This project builds on the grantee’s previous efforts, which have resulted in continued tax benefits for charitable organizations, reduced costs of registering legal entities, and a coherent government policy for civil society development in Ukraine. The grantee is the only international organization providing a full range of legal services for the support and development of the legal and regulatory structure governing civil society and the nonprofit sector in emerging and developed countries around the world.

title: Building an Enabling Legal Environment for Ukraine's Nonprofit Sector
description: This program supports the development of an enabling legal and regulatory environment for Ukraine’s nonprofit sector. Grant funds will enable the International Center for Not-for-Profit Law to provide technical assistance in the drafting and implementation of legislation affecting nongovernmental organizations and the development of philanthropy. The grantee will also undertake educational initiatives for lawyers, government officials, parliamentarians, and nongovernmental organization leaders on legislation and legal issues affecting the nonprofit sector. This project builds on the grantee’s previous efforts, which have resulted in improved opportunity for civic organizations to compete for government-procured goods and services, reduced costs of registering legal entities, and a coherent government policy for civil society development in Ukraine. The grantee is the only international organization providing a full range of legal services for the support and development of the legal and regulatory structure governing civil society and the nonprofit sector in emerging and developed countries around the world.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will enable the National Committee for Responsive Philanthropy to continue conducting rigorous research; producing timely and carefully prepared reports and articles; making presentations at a wide range of academic and practitioner conferences; organizing funders, policymakers and nonprofit activists for philanthropic reform; participating in advocacy coalitions; and providing technical assistance to nonprofits and foundations that support disadvantaged and disenfranchised populations. The National Committee for Responsive Philanthropy promotes greater philanthropic openness, accountability and responsiveness to politically, economically or socially disadvantaged populations and constituencies.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued general purpose support to the National Committee for Responsive Philanthropy, an organization dedicated to promoting philanthropy that serves the public good, is responsive to people and communities with the least wealth and opportunity, and is held accountable to the highest standards of integrity and openness. Besides its routine monitoring activities, over the past two years the committee has conducted research and published reports on issues in philanthropy including alternative workplace funds, strategic grantmaking in school privatization, nonprofit core operating support, and the impact of bank mergers on charitable giving. In addition to its regular watchdog activities, in the near term the committee will implement two major programs — one on grantmaking for community impact and the other on developing a set of measurable criteria for foundations to enhance the public good. The committee also will reposition its communications and increase its advocacy efforts.

title: Mobilizing Civil Society to Monitor/Reform Trade Policy in Brazil
initiative: Reform of International Finance and Trade
description: Over the past five years, ActionAid Brasil has been instrumental in strengthening the efforts of civil society actors to monitor and influence international trade policies, analyze their impacts in Brazil, and increase public awareness and press coverage of trade and investment issues. The goal of this project is to reform trade policies that negatively impact the environment and sustainable rural development in Brazil. With this renewal, ActionAid Brasil will coordinate and improve the effectiveness of nongovernmental organizations and grassroots groups to influence trade policy at the national and international level; monitor and analyze the impact of new investments aimed at regional integration; and increase nongovernmental organization capacity and policymaker involvement in reforming trade policy in favor of environmentally sustainable development.

title: Great Lakes Water Quality Project
geographic_focus: Illinois, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, New York, Indiana, Minnesota, Ohio, Michigan
description: According to a recent study, the Great Lakes ecosystem is rapidly deteriorating to the point that irreversible damage may result. Water quality stressors, such as toxins, invasive species and polluted runoff are among the chief causes.This grant will enable the National Wildlife Federation to work with partners across the Great Lakes basin to address these threats by making use of the Clean Water Act and related policies. Activities will include monitoring implementation of existing water quality standards; developing standards for uncontrolled pollutants; and reducing the impact of runoff pollution by protecting high quality wetlands.During the past two years, the federation worked to implement the Clean Water Act in the Great Lakes basin, with a particular emphasis on the control of toxic discharges from municipal wastewater treatment plants and other point sources. This work has included ensuring that states do not weaken water quality standards for mercury, a potent neurotoxin; closing loopholes in state environmental programs that otherwise would allow excessive discharges of water pollution; and improving individual discharge permits in the Lake Superior basin.

title: Great Lakes Water Quality Project
geographic_focus: Wisconsin, Indiana, Pennsylvania, Minnesota, New York, Ohio, Michigan, Illinois
description: The National Wildlife Federation, a national environmental group with a longtime presence in the Great Lakes region, will continue to work with partner organizations to help implement the Clean Water Act and related policies throughout the Great Lakes basin. In recent years, the federation has helped establish more protective standards for mercury pollution, develop new state-level policy for ballast water discharges, and establish protective rules for the mining of sulfide-based ores. With continued Mott support, the federation will maintain and expand such work. Activities will include: monitoring implementation of existing water quality standards and ballast water discharge rules; promoting improved wetland protections; and holding proposed sulfide mining activities around Lake Superior to the highest standards.

title: Great Lakes Water Quality Project
geographic_focus: New York, Minnesota, Wisconsin, Indiana, Pennsylvania, Ohio, Michigan, Illinois
description: The National Wildlife Federation, a national environmental group with a longtime presence in the Great Lakes region, works with partner organizations to help implement the Clean Water Act and related policies throughout the Great Lakes basin. In recent years, the grantee helped establish more protective standards for mercury pollution, develop new state-level policy for ballast water discharges, and establish protective rules for the mining of sulfide-based ores. This grant increase will allow the federation to respond to new opportunities to protect Michigan from the impacts of sulfide mining and to bolster a state-level wetlands policy.

title: Great Lakes Water Quality Project
geographic_focus: Wisconsin, New York, Minnesota, Illinois, Indiana, Pennsylvania, Ohio, Michigan
description: The National Wildlife Federation, a national environmental group with a longtime presence in the Great Lakes region, works with partner organizations to help implement the Clean Water Act and related policies throughout the Great Lakes Basin. With previous Mott support, the federation monitored the implementation of water quality standards, promoted wetlands protections, advanced strategies to halt invasive species, and worked to establish sound precedents for sulfide mining decisions in the Lake Superior watershed. With renewed support, the federation will continue these activities while developing strategies for emerging chemicals of concern and engaging in the renegotiation of the Great Lakes Water Quality Agreement.

title: Great Lakes Water Quality Project
geographic_focus: Illinois, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Indiana, New York, Minnesota, Michigan, Ohio
description: A national environmental group with a longtime presence in the Great Lakes region, the National Wildlife Federation works with partner organizations to help implement the Clean Water Act and related policies throughout the Great Lakes Basin. With this grant increase, the grantee will compile a report examining the laws and regulations that can protect water quality from sulfide mining impacts. This increase will also support a conference that will examine how climate adaptation measures can protect Great Lakes water quality.

title: Great Lakes Water Quality Project
geographic_focus: Illinois, Ohio, Wisconsin, Indiana, Minnesota, Pennsylvania, Michigan, New York
description: The National Wildlife Federation, an environmental group with a longtime presence in the Great Lakes region, partners with state and local organizations to help implement the Clean Water Act and related policies. With this grant increase, the federation will collaborate with partners to ensure that federally funded restoration projects are coordinated in a way that results in the greatest benefits to the health of the Great Lakes. The federation will also conduct research and engage stakeholders around protecting water quality from the impacts of hydraulic fracturing in Michigan.

title: Great Lakes Water Quality Project
geographic_focus: New York, Ohio, Wisconsin, Indiana, Illinois, Pennsylvania, Michigan, Minnesota
description: A healthy Great Lakes ecosystem is essential to supporting the 40 million people in the region who rely on the waterways for drinking water, food, jobs, and recreation. The National Wildlife Federation, a national environmental group, works with local partners to keep the Great Lakes clean by helping states improve and implement the Clean Water Act and related policies. With Mott support, the grantee’s prior efforts resulted in higher water quality standards, increased wetlands protections, greater attention to controlling invasive species, and more public engagement in Great Lakes Water Quality Agreement processes. With renewed support, the grantee will build on this work while seeking to address nonpoint source pollution, reduce environmental risks associated with the mining of sulfide-based ores, and address other priority Great Lakes issues as they emerge.

title: Sustaining the Great Lakes Project
geographic_focus: Ohio, Michigan, Indiana, Illinois, Minnesota, New York, Wisconsin, Pennsylvania
description: In December 2005, the Great Lakes governors endorsed a precedent-setting agreement that, once implemented, would provide new interstate protections against diversions outside of the Great Lakes basin and unwise water use within the basin. This grant increase will enable the National Wildlife Federation to support groups working to promote adoption of the agreement.

title: Sustaining the Great Lakes Project
geographic_focus: Ohio, New York, Michigan, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Indiana, Illinois
description: After nearly five years of negotiation, the Great Lakes governors and premiers endorsed the proposed Great Lakes-St. Lawrence River Basin Water Resources Compact and its companion binational agreement in December 2005. While this was a significant milestone, much work remains to be done as each state must ratify the compact, and Congress must provide its consent before it becomes binding. With previous support, the National Wildlife Federation, a national conservation group with a strong presence in the Great Lakes basin, has played a key leadership role by developing policy recommendations, providing scientific and legal support to decisionmakers and other nonprofit organizations, and leading public education and outreach efforts. With renewal support, the federation will continue in this role as the proposed interstate compact moves through the ratification process.

title: Sustaining the Great Lakes Project
geographic_focus: Ohio, New York, Minnesota, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Michigan, Indiana, Illinois
description: The National Wildlife Federation, a national organization with a strong presence in the Great Lakes basin, has led efforts to implement the Great Lakes Compact, and it appears that the compact may be fully operational soon. This grant increase and associated grant period extension will allow the National Wildlife Federation to plan and begin implementation of the next phase of related policy work at the state and regional levels.

title: Sustaining the Great Lakes Project
geographic_focus: Ohio, New York, Michigan, Wisconsin, Illinois, Indiana, Minnesota, Pennsylvania
description: On December 8, 2008, after an eight-year process that started with negotiations among states and provinces, and followed with ratification by the U.S. Congress, the Great Lakes-St. Lawrence River Basin Water Resources Compact became law. This accomplishment is followed by a new challenge: ensuring this compact is implemented effectively in all the Great Lakes states. Renewed support will allow the National Wildlife Federation, a national conservation group with a strong presence in the Great Lakes basin, to continue its leadership role in the region. The federation will work with regional partners and key organizations in each Great Lakes state to ensure the compact is effectively implemented at the state and regional level. The federation will advance this goal by developing policy recommendations, providing scientific and legal support to decisionmakers and other nonprofit organizations, and leading public education and outreach efforts.

title: Sustaining the Great Lakes Project
geographic_focus: Illinois, Wisconsin, Michigan, Minnesota, Indiana, New York, Pennsylvania, Ohio
description: The federal government approved the Great Lakes-St. Lawrence River Basin Water Resources Compact to protect the region’s freshwater system from projects that would divert water outside of the basin. The National Wildlife Federation, a national conservation group with a strong presence in the Great Lakes Basin, has partnered with regional and state-level organizations to ensure the compact is effectively implemented in each of the Great Lakes states. With previous support, the grantee developed relevant policy recommendations, provided scientific and legal support to its state-level partners, and led public education and outreach efforts. With this renewal, the grantee will continue these efforts with a focus on improving each state’s water management policies and strengthening the region’s ability to oversee the compact.

title: Sustaining the Great Lakes Project
geographic_focus: Michigan, Minnesota, Wisconsin, Illinois, New York, Indiana, Pennsylvania, Ohio
description: The Great Lakes-St. Lawrence River Basin Water Resources Compact was adopted to protect the region’s freshwater system from proposals to divert water outside of the basin as well as excessive in-basin use. The National Wildlife Federation, a national conservation group with a strong presence in the Great Lakes, partners with regional and state-level organizations to ensure the compact is effectively implemented in each Great Lakes state. With previous Mott support, the grantee developed policy recommendations, provided scientific and legal support to partners, and led public education initiatives. With this grant increase, the grantee will continue these efforts, paying special attention to a precedent-setting, water-withdrawal proposal in Wisconsin.

title: Sustaining the Great Lakes Project
geographic_focus: Michigan, Minnesota, Illinois, Wisconsin, Pennsylvania, Ohio, New York, Indiana
description: The Great Lakes provide habitat for fish and wildlife, serve as economic engines for various industries, and supply recreational opportunities and drinking water for more than 40 million people. One avenue for protecting this ecosystem is through the Great Lakes-St. Lawrence River Basin Water Resources Compact, which offers safeguards from water diversions outside of the Great Lakes Basin. The National Wildlife Federation, a national conservation group with a strong presence in the Great Lakes Basin, partners with regional- and state-level organizations to ensure the compact is effectively implemented. With previous Mott support, the grantee developed relevant policy recommendations, provided scientific and legal assistance to state-level partners, and lead public education efforts. This grant renewal will allow the grantee to continue this compact-related, water quantity work while also supporting the grantee’s efforts to improve water quality in the Great Lakes by addressing threats such as invasive species, toxic pollution, and harmful algal blooms.

title: Sustaining the Great Lakes Project
geographic_focus: Ohio, New York, Illinois, Minnesota, Wisconsin, Michigan, Pennsylvania, Indiana
description: The National Wildlife Federation is a nationwide conservation group with a strong presence in the Great Lakes Basin. With staff based in Ann Arbor, Michigan; Ohio; and Wisconsin, the grantee partners with state-level and local groups to protect, sustain, and restore the Great Lakes ecosystem. Previous Mott support allowed the grantee to develop freshwater policy recommendations, provide scientific and legal assistance to state-level partners, and spearhead public education efforts. Continued support will allow the grantee to protect Great Lakes water quantity and water quality, stop the spread of invasive species, improve pipeline safety, and reduce toxic algal blooms. The grantee will also take steps to develop partnerships with agribusiness and urban community groups.

title: Sustaining the Great Lakes Project
geographic_focus: Indiana, Minnesota, Illinois, Ohio, Michigan, New York, Wisconsin, Pennsylvania
description: With increased Mott support, the National Wildlife Federation, a conservation group with a strong presence in the Great Lakes, will help its Healing Our Waters coalition take steps to broaden public support for Great Lakes policies. The federation will survey coalition members; interview other rural, urban, and tribal leaders; and conduct training sessions to address leadership gaps. The grantee will also develop a five-year action plan to expand coalition membership and improve the coalition’s effectiveness on Great Lakes restoration programs. This additional capacity will also help the regional coalition take on new issues, such as protecting drinking water sources and halting the spread of invasive species.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will enable Native Americans in Philanthropy to strengthen indigenous communities by increasing philanthropic investment in Native American peoples and advancing the participation and leadership of Native Americans in the philanthropic sector. In addition to building its membership and increasing the visibility and understanding of Native American needs, it provides training and technical assistance to Native American nonprofits and leaders.The organization is a grantmaker affinity group dedicated to improving all aspects of philanthropic activity related to Native American people.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to Native Americans in Philanthropy, a grantmaker affinity group dedicated to improvement in all aspects of philanthropic activity related to Native-American people. The organization seeks to strengthen indigenous communities by increasing philanthropic investment in Native-American people and advancing the participation and leadership of Native Americans in the philanthropic sector. Recent past accomplishments include a significant increase in membership, regional gatherings on leadership and philanthropic partnerships, and demographic research on Native-American philanthropy. The current organizational focus includes leadership development, sharing lessons learned regarding investing in Native-American communities, and increased networking among Native-American communities in philanthropy.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to Native Americans in Philanthropy, a grantmaker affinity group dedicated to improvement in all aspects of philanthropic activity related to Native-American people. The organization seeks to strengthen indigenous communities by increasing philanthropic investment in Native-American communities and advancing the participation and leadership of Native Americans in the philanthropic sector. Recent past accomplishments include significant Web site enhancements, several regional convenings on leadership and philanthropic partnerships, and research on Native-American philanthropy demographics and asset mapping. The current organizational focus includes linking leadership programs nationally, increasing research and communication efforts, and increasing networking among Native-American communities in philanthropy.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to Native Americans in Philanthropy, a grantmaker affinity group dedicated to improvement of philanthropic activity related to Native-American people. The group currently has 120 individual and organizational members. Native Americans in Philanthropy seeks to increase philanthropic investment in Native-American communities and advance the participation and leadership of Native Americans in the philanthropic sector. Recent accomplishments include the delivery of training programs for grassroots Native-American organizations and grantmakers, convenings on leadership and philanthropic partnerships, research on Native-American philanthropy demographics and asset mapping, launching a regranting program to Native-American grassroots groups, and significant Web site enhancements. The current organizational focus includes linking leadership programs nationally, increasing research and communication efforts, and increasing networking among Native-American communities in philanthropy.

title: Organizational Development and Project Support
description: The Social Change Assistance Trust was established in 1984 to empower the rural poor to strengthen civil society and promote social change.This grant will enable the trust to implement programs that address community needs such as poverty, access to justice, local economic development and the development of women and youth. Recent activities included publishing a book about its role in bringing about social change in rural communities during the past two decades; participating in an event with visiting members of the Global Philanthropists Circle; strengthening staff capacity through training programs on a range of topics; providing support to 58 local economic development agencies; and launching a Web site.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Northern Cape, Province of, Western Cape, Province of the, Eastern Cape, Province of, North-West, Province of, Free State
description: The Social Change Assistance Trust works to improve the quality of life of rural people by assisting them in addressing poverty through locally developed initiatives. Mott’s support will assist community-based advice offices to implement programs that address community needs such as poverty, access to justice, and local economic development focusing, in particular, on women and youth. It will also allow the grantee to continue to provide financial resources, training, and hands-on support to between 50 and 60 advice offices in the rural areas of the Eastern, Western, and Northern Cape provinces, as well as the Northwest and Free State provinces. Its interventions will aim at addressing HIV/AIDS, local economic development, access to justice, local government service delivery, and food security.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Northern Cape, Province of, North-West, Province of, Eastern Cape, Province of, Western Cape, Province of the, Free State
description: For 25 years, the Social Change Assistance Trust has been working to improve the quality of life of rural people by addressing poverty through locally developed initiatives. Past support enabled the trust to make grants to local, community-based development agencies and provide hands-on organizational development support and mentoring to these organizations. This grant will support the grantee to continue to provide financial resources, training, and hands-on support to between 50 and 60 local, community-based development agencies in the rural areas of the Eastern, Western, and Northern Cape provinces, as well as the Northwest and Free State provinces. Its interventions will address HIV/AIDS, local economic development, access to justice, gender equity, and food security.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Northern Cape, Province of, North-West, Province of, Eastern Cape, Province of, Western Cape, Province of the, Free State
description: The Social Change Assistance Trust works to improve the quality of life of rural people in South Africa by assisting them to address poverty through locally developed initiatives. It supports rural community-based advice offices that focus on human rights, gender equity, HIV/AIDS, and local economic development. Past support assisted the grantee to fund and support community-based advice offices in the Eastern Cape, Western Cape, Northern Cape, and Northwest provinces. The grantee also piloted a peer-to-peer learning and mentoring process among its grantees and appointed established organizations to support emerging ones through horizontal learning exchanges. It also trained grantees in various areas based on need, and the topics covered included financial management, governance, fundraising, gender sensitization, and women in leadership. This grant will assist the grantee to support community-based advice offices in various provinces across South Africa through small grants and mentorship support to enable them to achieve their community development goals.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Northern Cape, Province of, Eastern Cape, Province of, North-West, Province of, Free State, Western Cape, Province of the
description: The Social Change Assistance Trust is a grantmaking organization established in 1984 that predominantly funds rural organizations in order to improve the quality of life in their communities. It supports programs that address human rights, gender equity, HIV/AIDS, and local economic development. Past support assisted the grantee to fund and support community-based advice offices in the Eastern Cape, Western Cape, Northern Cape, and Free State provinces. Over the past two years, the grantee supported community-based paralegals to access accredited training, facilitated peer-to-peer learning among advice offices, and collaborated on a program to monitor government service delivery points in mainly poor areas. This grant will support the grantee to continue to fund community-based advice offices, train and mentor paralegals and management committees in advice offices, monitor government service delivery points, and document its experiences.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Northern Cape, Province of, North-West, Province of, Western Cape, Province of the, Free State, Eastern Cape, Province of
description: The Social Change Assistance Trust is a grantmaking organization established in 1984 that predominantly funds rural organizations in order to improve the quality of life in their communities. It supports programs that address human rights, gender equity, HIV/AIDS, and local economic development. Past support assisted the grantee to support community-based advice offices in the Eastern Cape, Western Cape, Northern Cape, and Free State provinces. Over the past two years, the grantee supported community-based paralegals to access accredited training, facilitated peer-to-peer learning among advice offices, and collaborated on a program to monitor government service delivery points in mainly poor areas. This grant will support the grantee to continue to fund community-based advice offices, train and mentor paralegals and management committees in advice offices, monitor government service delivery points, and document its experiences. This grant increase has been made possible by a partnership with Atlantic Philanthropies in support of the community advice office sector.

title: General Purposes
description: Social Change Assistance Trust is a grantmaking organization established in 1984 that predominantly funds rural organizations in order to improve the quality of life in their communities. It supports programs that address human rights, gender equity, HIV/AIDS, and local economic development. Past support assisted the grantee to fund and support community advice offices in the Eastern Cape, Western Cape, Northern Cape, and Free State provinces. Over the past two years, the grantee made grants and provided training and mentoring support to community advice offices and assisted communities in the Northern Cape province to establish food gardens. This grant will support the grantee to continue to fund and provide peer learning opportunities for community advice offices. It will also train and mentor paralegals and management committees in advice offices. In addition to the four provinces already supported, the grantee will also work in the Northwest and KwaZulu-Natal provinces.

title: General Purposes
description: Social Change Assistance Trust is a grantmaking organization established in 1984 that predominantly funds rural organizations in order to improve the quality of life in their communities. It supports programs that address access to justice, gender equality, youth development, and local economic development. Past support assisted the grantee to fund and support community-based organizations in the Eastern Cape, Free State, Northern Cape, and Western Cape provinces. Over the past two years, the grantee also supported gardening projects in the Northern Cape province. This grant will support the grantee to continue to fund community-based organizations, including community advice offices; train and mentor paralegals and management committees in community advice offices; explore the establishment of a youth fund; and strengthen community-driven philanthropy by encouraging local fundraising.

title: Promoting Civil Society in the Croatian Media
description: Through reports that will be aired on Croatian national television and various independent television stations and at film festivals and other public forums, this grant will enable the Incredibly Good Institution – FADE IN to create a space in the mass media for discussion and reporting on civil society; inform individuals about issues affecting Croatia and its communities; and encourage individuals and non-governmental organizations to become active in their local communities by highlighting issues and showing success stories. The organization also will train non-governmental organizations and activists to use the media and video documentation effectively.During the past two years, the organization has been responsible for producing more than 150 short reports on a range of topics on Croatian television and conducting more than 30 media workshops.The organization is an independent, not-for-profit production company based in Zagreb, Croatia.

title: Promoting Civil Society in the Croatian Media
description: The project goal is to promote the values and accomplishments of local civic initiatives and the Croatian nonprofit sector in the media. Through production of reports that will be aired on Croatian national television and various independent television stations and at film festivals and other public forums, Incredibly Good Institution – FADE IN creates space in the mass media for discussion and reporting on civil society and encourages individuals and nongovernmental organizations to become active in their local communities by highlighting issues and success stories. In 2009-2010, the grantee will strengthen its core activities while developing sustainable, fee-generating services and products. Over the past two years, more than 250 short reports produced by the grantee on a range of topics have been aired on Croatian television. The grantee also produced public service announcements, documentary films, and a television series dealing with youth issues. The grantee is an independent, not-for-profit production company based in Zagreb.

title: General Purposes
description: The Michigan AIDS Fund was established in 1989 by the Council of Michigan Foundations. In 2005, the board of the fund approved a new strategic direction: to prevent HIV/AIDS in Michigan by increasing knowledge and awareness of the disease and its transmission. While the continuing need for efforts such as patient care and organizational capacity building are recognized, the fund’s expertise and limited resources will have the greatest impact by focusing on the prevention of HIV transmission.This grant will support core activities in line with the new mission: grantmaking and public engagement. The fund will seek out and fund innovative prevention projects. If successful, the ultimate result will be the decline in HIV infection rates in Michigan, especially in populations that have seen an alarming increase in these rates in recent years.

title: Community Foundation Leadership Team
description: This grant provides renewal support to the Council on Foundations for the work of the Community Foundation Leadership Team, whose mission is to serve as a strong voice, advocate, and resource for community foundations. Over the past seven years, the team has aided the development of the community foundation field through establishing national community foundation standards, promoting best practices, developing and disseminating marketing tools, advocating for a supportive legal and regulatory environment, and conducting research and development on technology, accountability, and organizational and professional development. Through its Plan of Action 2007-2010, the team and the council will build on past achievements and focus on creating, capturing, and sharing knowledge; enhancing the practice of community leadership; achieving operational excellence; and advancing an effective legislative agenda.

title: Community Foundation Leadership Team
description: This grant provides renewal support to the Council on Foundations for the work of the Community Foundation Leadership Team. Over the past eight years, the team has aided the development of the community foundation field through establishing national standards; promoting best practices; developing and disseminating marketing tools; advocating for a supportive legal and regulatory environment; and conducting research and development on technology, accountability, and organizational and professional development. Through its Plan of Action 2007-2010, the team has focused on being a resource and catalyst for the creation, capture, and sharing of knowledge; enhancing the practice of community leadership; strengthening organizational effectiveness; and ensuring that legislative and regulatory environments are supportive of community foundations. In 2009, main activities will include developing a knowledge system, promoting community leadership, launching the Community Foundations National Standards Board, and managing a grant program for collaborative, innovative projects.

title: Community Foundation Leadership Team
description: This grant provides support to the Council on Foundations for the work of the Community Foundation Leadership Team. Through its Plan of Action 2007-2010, the team has focused on being a resource and catalyst for the creation, capture, and sharing of knowledge; enhancing the practice of community leadership; strengthening organizational effectiveness; and ensuring that legislative and regulatory environments are supportive of community foundations. In 2009, main activities will include developing a knowledge system; promoting community leadership; launching the Community Foundations National Standards Board; and managing IdeaLab, a grant program for collaborative, innovative projects. This grant increase will support conference stipends for presenters and the videotaping of a 2009 Fall Conference session on community foundations engaging immigrant communities through transnational collaboration, based on the example of the United States and Mexico. The videotape will be placed on several Web sites and promoted through multiple communication vehicles.

title: Community Foundation Leadership Team
description: This grant provides renewal support to the Council on Foundations for the work of the Community Foundation Leadership Team. Over the past nine years, the team has aided the development of the community foundation field through establishing national standards; promoting best practices; supporting innovative collaborative projects; advocating for a supportive legal and regulatory environment; and conducting research on technology, accountability, and organizational and professional development. Through its Plan of Action 2007-2010, the team has focused on: 1) the creation, capture, and sharing of knowledge; 2) the practice of community leadership; 3) organizational effectiveness; and 4) a supportive legislative and regulatory environment. In 2010, main activities will include conducting regional learning forums and other knowledge-sharing activities, developing a strategic plan for 2011-2014, promoting community leadership, updating national marketing portfolios, and managing a grant program for collaborative, innovative projects.

title: General Purposes
description: The State Environmental Leadership Program is a national network of independent groups promoting state-level environmental policy reforms. It strengthens the organizational capacity and policy work of its member groups by hosting meetings, providing technical assistance and facilitating collaboration. This grant increase will support the general purposes of the organization.

title: General Purposes
description: Multiyear funding will enable the Center for Civil Initiatives to work with key stakeholders to build capacity to identify community needs and implement long-term and lasting solutions in seven counties in Croatia. During the past six years, the center has provided information, training and consultations to a wide range of local and international non-governmental organizations and governmental agencies on community organizing, organizational development, cross-sector cooperation, local resource development and rural economic development.The center is part of a network of community development organizations in Central and Eastern Europe, including several funded by the Mott Foundation.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to stimulate citizen activism and mobilize community resources to address critical issues facing Croatian communities. The Center for Civil Initiatives works with local community leaders and civic groups to identify community needs and implement long-term solutions. In addition, the center provides information, training, and consultations to a range of other local and international nongovernmental organizations and the Croatian government on community organizing, organizational development, local resource development, and rural economic development. In 2006-2007, the center helped to establish citizen advisory councils in 11 municipalities, assisted three local governments develop transparent grant programs for civic initiatives, trained over 50 village boards, provided technical assistance to over 60 civic groups, and worked with 11 businesses to develop corporate social responsibility programs. The center is based in Zagreb and works with other community development organizations in Croatia and in Central and Eastern Europe, including several Mott grantees.

title: General Purposes

The center is based in Zagreb and works with other community development organizations in Croatia and in Central and Eastern Europe, including several Mott grantees.

title: Running Rivers Campaign
geographic_focus: North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee, Wisconsin, Georgia, Michigan, New York, Alabama, Virginia
description: For some time, American Rivers has led efforts to improve the operation of hundreds of dams, thereby ensuring increased fish passage, adequate in-stream flows, improved water quality and other benefits to freshwater ecosystems. This grant increase will enable American Rivers to host a national conference of hydropower relicensing experts, build an education and outreach program concerning the value of water quality certification in hydropower relicensing, and update data relevant to the field.

title: Running Rivers Campaign
geographic_focus: New York, Wisconsin, Michigan, Georgia, Tennessee, Alabama, South Carolina, North Carolina
description: American Rivers, a national leader in the field of hydropower relicensing, promotes changes in the way dams are operated to ensure increased fish passage, adequate in-stream flows, improved water quality, and similar benefits for freshwater ecosystems. Renewal support will allow American Rivers to participate in key relicensing processes in the Southeast, ensure that new licenses in the Great Lakes and Southeast are implemented properly, and help local groups prepare to monitor license implementation over the long term.

title: Running Rivers Campaign
geographic_focus: Michigan, New York, Tennessee, Wisconsin, Georgia, South Carolina, Alabama, North Carolina
description: The hydropower dam relicensing process offers an opportunity to repair and circumvent some of the harm dams can cause to the health of freshwater ecosystems. American Rivers, a national voice for river conservation, provides technical assistance, policy expertise, and capacity-building assistance to conservation groups involved with hydropower project relicensing. With continued Mott support, the grantee will work to secure new licenses in the Southeast that will protect aquatic resources, ensure the proper implementation of recently granted licenses in the Great Lakes region, and promote improvements to federal policies that will make it easier to accomplish conservation objectives at the local level.

title: Coalition for Community Schools: Strategic Planning
description: The Coalition for Community Schools, a project of the Institute for Educational Leadership, began in 1998 with a series of meetings to give a united voice to organizations and institutions from different sectors that are committed to developing and maintaining community schools.This grant will enable the coalition to engage in a strategic planning process to determine how to continue to build and mobilize a strong network of partners and educate the public and policymakers about the vision of community schools.

description: This grant will continue to provide support to the Coalition for Community Schools, a project of the Institute for Educational Leadership. The coalition will continue its efforts to build and mobilize a strong network of partners and educate the public and policymakers about the vision of community schools. title: Rebirth of Volunteerism in Bulgaria
description: The program goal is to promote and develop volunteerism in Bulgaria by strengthening the capacity and outreach of a national network of volunteer centers. The National Alliance for Volunteer Action will work with its partners in the network to strengthen and coordinate training and capacity-building services, improve local and national public awareness about volunteerism, and facilitate joint initiatives of the network of local volunteer centers. In addition, the alliance will strengthen its organizational capacity and financial sustainability. Since its establishment in 2000, the alliance has established a network of eight regional volunteer centers, developed national standards for volunteer management, and raised public awareness about volunteerism in Bulgaria.

title: Rebirth of Volunteerism in Bulgaria

title: One LA Education Project
description: With nearly 9.4 million residents sprawled across the Los Angeles metropolitan area, public schools find it increasingly difficult to educate over 2.4 million school-aged children. The combination of geographic sprawl and income inequality has exacerbated racial tensions and left people in large part disconnected from one another. The Southern California Education Fund, an affiliate of the Industrial Areas Foundation, has put a priority on improving public education. The One LA Education Project is designed to nurture and facilitate a broad set of economic and social relationships within and outside of schools to build power sufficient to improve Los Angeles’ schools and communities. This grantee provides continued support to build a powerful network of relationships capable of addressing the accelerating problems of the schools in the Los Angeles metropolitan area.

title: General Purposes
description: Multiyear funding will enable the Environmental Law Service (ELS) to implement a broad range of activities to help non-governmental organizations, individuals and local municipalities make better use of the law and more effectively participate in public decisionmaking processes. The organization also will focus on enhancing its organizational capacity and strengthening its financial stability.ELS, established in 1995, provides legal counseling and training and monitors legislation compliance.

title: Grantmakers Income Security Taskforce
description: Finance Project’s Grantmakers Income Security Taskforce is an affinity group of funders who are broadly interested in the social and economic conditions that generate and perpetuate poverty. Its mission is to broaden funders’ perspectives on critical issues, deepen their understanding of issues in which they are already active, and promote strategic, collaborative grantmaking. Mott staff has been active in this affinity group since its inception. During the renewal grant period, the group will continue to provide a vehicle to assist funders in better understanding income security issues and the status and/or impact of policies and programs designed to address those issues. This work will be accomplished through working groups, quarterly meetings, special projects, and information-sharing efforts including ongoing maintenance of a funders’ listserv.

title: State Fiscal Analysis Initiative - D.C. Fiscal Policy Institute
grantee: Center on Budget and Policy Priorities
description: Funding will enable the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities to inform public debates in Washington, D.C. through effective research, analysis and outreach efforts. Other priorities include implementing new communications and outreach strategies.During the past two years, the center played an important role in informing and framing public debates on revenue and spending issues and on new and existing policy initiatives in the district.This is one of 10 grants supporting the State Fiscal Analysis Initiative. The District of Columbia Fiscal Policy Institute joined this effort in 2001. Mott-funding also enables the center to provide technical assistance and networking opportunities for the 35 state organizations participating in this initiative.

title: State Fiscal Analysis Initiative - D.C. Fiscal Policy Institute
grantee: Center on Budget and Policy Priorities
description: This is one of ten grants recommended to state organizations as part of the State Fiscal Analysis Initiative. The initiative was created by the Ford, Annie E. Casey, and Mott Foundations in 1992 in order to build state capacity for timely, credible, and accessible budget and tax analysis on behalf of low- and middle-income families. The District of Columbia’s fiscal project joined the initiative in 2000 and has become a respected source of analysis and perspective on budget and tax policy issues as well as safety net programs and broader economic trends. During the next two years, the grantee will prepare and disseminate its analytical products and strengthen its outreach to and partnerships with key audiences, including nonprofit organizations, policymakers, and the media. Related to this project is a grant to the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, which provides technical assistance to all 36 organizations participating in the initiative.

title: State Fiscal Analysis Initiative - D.C. Fiscal Policy Institute
grantee: Center on Budget and Policy Priorities
description: The Ford, Casey, and Mott foundations created the State Fiscal Analysis Initiative in 1992 in order to build state capacity for timely, credible, and accessible tax and budget analysis on behalf of low- and middle-income families. This grant will enable the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, a longtime Mott grantee and State Fiscal Analysis Initiative coordinator, to incubate a new fiscal project in the District of Columbia. The new project will be part of the broader initiative and will undertake a variety of efforts to establish its reputation as a credible research effort. Anticipated activities include: analyzing the district’s budget trends and priorities; producing reports on budget trends, revenues, and expenditures; preparing accessible education materials for other nonprofit organizations; and educating advocates, the media, and policymakers through briefings and public outreach.

title: General Purposes
description: The Association for Enterprise Opportunity (AEO) is the national trade association of organizations committed to micro-enterprise development. Founded in 1991, its mission is to increase the capacity of self-employment organizations and to serve as the forum and voice for individuals and organizations committed to expanding enterprise opportunity for people and communities with limited access to economic resources.Funding will enable AEO to foster exchange between practitioners; encourage increased investment in enterprise opportunity for low-income people by the public and private sectors; and continue to play an integral role in the development of micro-enterprise programs and policies through training and advocacy efforts.Since its inception, AEO has improved its capacity to provide valuable services to its members and has made an impact on federal micro-enterprise policy. It has provided more than 450 members with a learning forum, funding information and a policy voice.

title: General Purposes
description: Founded in 1991, the Association for Enterprise Opportunity is the national trade association of organizations committed to microenterprise development. It provides over 450 members with a forum, information, and a voice to promote enterprise opportunity for people and communities with limited access to economic resources. Since its inception, the Association for Enterprise Opportunity has made an impact on federal microenterprise policy, as well as on training the microenterprise industry. This renewal will allow the association to continue to provide critical services to develop strong and effective microenterprise programs in the United States that assist underserved entrepreneurs in starting, stabilizing, and expanding businesses.

Since its inception, this grantee has made an impact on federal microenterprise policy, as well as on training for the microenterprise industry. This renewal will allow the association to continue to provide critical services to develop strong and effective microenterprise programs in the United States that assist underserved, low-income entrepreneurs in starting, stabilizing, and expanding businesses.

title: General Purposes
description: Founded in 1991, the Association for Enterprise Opportunity is the national trade association of organizations committed to microenterprise development. It provides over 450 members with a forum, information, and a voice to promote enterprise opportunity for people and communities with limited access to economic resources. Since its inception, the grantee has made an impact on federal microenterprise policy, as well as on training the microenterprise industry. This renewal will allow the grantee to continue to provide critical services to develop strong and effective microenterprise programs in the United States that support underserved entrepreneurs in starting, stabilizing, and expanding businesses.

title: General Purposes
description: Founded in 1991, the Association for Enterprise Opportunity is a national membership organization and trade association for microfinance and microenterprise development practitioners and organizations in the United States. Renewal general purpose support will enable the grantee to continue supporting the development of strong and effective microenterprise initiatives that assist underserved entrepreneurs in starting, stabilizing, and expanding businesses.

title: General Purposes
description: The purpose of this program is to increase the level of independent funding and technical assistance available to nonprofit organizations working with children and youth in Slovakia. In 2007-2010, the Children of Slovakia Foundation, one of the leading philanthropic foundations in Central and Eastern Europe, will enhance its grantmaking programs and capacity-building services aimed at assisting the development of children and young people in Slovakia. The grantee will promote local philanthropy by implementing new fundraising methods and strengthening the professionalism of nonprofit organizations. In addition, the grantee will strengthen its organizational capacity and financial sustainability by improving operational procedures and developing more effective asset management. Since its establishment in 1996, the grantee has provided more than 1,400 grants totaling $4.5 million to nonprofit organizations working with children and youth in Slovakia. The Children of Slovakia Foundation has emerged as one of the most strategic grantmakers in Central and Eastern Europe.

title: Education Project
description: This grant will provide partial support to the Center for Community Change to continue the Education Project, an effort to assist local community-driven school reform efforts. Over the next two years, the project will focus on expanding technical assistance and outreach to organizing efforts in Ohio; providing opportunities for groups to work collaboratively across geographic and institutional lines; supporting education organizing efforts in the Gulf Coast; and publishing a regular newsletter highlighting community successes and challenges.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Center for the Development of Democracy and Human Rights
description: The Center for the Development of Democracy and Human Rights is a key Russian non-governmental organization that offers public policy expertise, runs advocacy campaigns, and offers training, consulting and information services to a broad range of civic groups on issues of democracy, civil society and human rights. The center is a leading participant in various domestic and international democracy and human rights promotion efforts. Over the next two years, the center will focus on issues such as ethnic discrimination and hate speech, military reform and alternative civil service, Russian legislation concerning human rights and civil society, legal support to the nonprofit sector in light of new legislation, and the development of a strategy for Russia’s human rights movement. The center will also initiate a training program for young people on civic participation, local community development and democratic processes in Russia.

title: General Purposes
description: The PICO National Network is a training institute for organizers and community leaders that has 48 federated projects in 16 states. The organization is comprised of 500 institutional members that consist of either congregations or community organizations, as well as 950,000 low- and moderate-income families. This general purposes grant will enable the network to expand its reach, develop grassroots leadership, recruit and train professional organizers, and increase the civic participation of low-income community residents in order to attack root causes of poverty.

title: General Purposes
description: The PICO National Network is a training institute for organizers and community leaders with 50 federated projects in 18 states. The organization is comprised of 500 institutional members that consist of either congregations or community organizations, as well as 950,000 low- and moderate-income families.This grant will enable the network to continue to expand its reach; develop grassroots leadership; recruit and train professional organizers; and increase the civic participation of low-income community residents in order to attack root causes of poverty. Funding includes an increase to support expansion efforts in response to the growing interest in developing new local organizations.

This general purpose grant will enable PICO National Network to expand its reach, develop grassroots leadership, recruit and train professional organizers, and increase the civic participation of low-income community residents in order to attack root causes of poverty.

This grant will enable the network to expand its reach, develop grassroots leaders, recruit and train organizers, and increase the civic participation of low-income community residents in order to attack root causes of poverty.

This grant increase will also help support the organization’s ongoing work to strengthen state-level organizing and clergy training.

title: General Purposes
description: PICO National Network is a network of affiliated community organizations in 18 states, including Michigan, as well as countries in Central America and East Africa. This grant will enable the network to expand its reach, develop grassroots leaders, recruit and train organizers, and increase the civic participation of low-income community residents in order to attack root causes of poverty.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Belarus, Estonia, Hungary, Ukraine, Lithuania, Poland, Slovakia, North Macedonia, Czech Republic, Georgia, Latvia
description: This grant to CEE Bankwatch Network continues support for a network of nongovernmental organizations in Central and Eastern Europe and Russia that monitors activities of international financial institutions and advocates for the adoption of environmentally sustainable development policies by these institutions. Members of the network work together to provide policy analysis, generate local participation in decisionmaking processes of these institutions, and attract international attention to key issues facing the region, Central Asia, and the Caucasus. Mott general purposes support during 2004-2006 enabled the network to expand its membership and partnerships with nongovernmental organizations across this broad region, effectively lead an international campaign focused on increasing the transparency of the European Investment Bank, and hold networking meetings and strategic planning events. The network is registered in the Czech Republic, and its executive director is based in Krakow, Poland.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Belarus, Czech Republic, Poland, Lithuania, Estonia, Hungary, Ukraine, Slovakia, Georgia, North Macedonia, Latvia
description: This grant continues support to CEE Bankwatch Network, a group of nongovernmental organizations in Central and Eastern Europe and Russia that monitors activities of international financial institutions and advocates for the adoption of environmentally sustainable development policies by these institutions. During the grant period, the network will monitor the work of the European Investment Bank, strengthen a coalition of environmental nonprofits in the Balkans to monitor development projects, and engage more deeply on climate change issues. Mott’s previous general purpose support enabled the network to expand its membership and partnerships with nongovernmental organizations across this broad region, effectively lead an international campaign focused on increasing the transparency of the European Investment Bank, and hold networking meetings and strategic planning events. The network is registered in the Czech Republic, and its executive director is based in Budapest, Hungary.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Russia, Lithuania, Poland, Georgia, North Macedonia, Bulgaria, Latvia, Ukraine, Estonia, Hungary, Slovakia, Czech Republic
description: The goal of CEE Bankwatch Network, a network of nongovernmental organizations in Central and Eastern Europe and Russia, is to monitor the activities of international financial institutions and advocate for the adoption of environmentally sustainable and climate friendly development policies by these institutions. During the grant period, the grantee will monitor the work of the European Investment Bank, increase the grantee’s outreach to the general public, and strengthen the organizational capacity and financial sustainability of the grantee and its members. The grantee’s key achievements in 2009-2010 included expanding its membership, leading a successful campaign on increasing the transparency of the European Investment Bank, and developing a new organizational structure and programmatic strategies for the grantee. The grantee is registered in the Czech Republic.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Poland, North Macedonia, Ukraine, Estonia, Slovakia, Hungary, Georgia, Czech Republic, Lithuania, Latvia, Belarus
description: The program goal is to strengthen public participation and give voice to civil society at the European Union level. To this end, the CEE Bankwatch Network, a network of nongovernmental organizations in Central and Eastern Europe and Russia, will monitor the activities of international financial institutions and advocate for the adoption of environmentally sustainable and climate-friendly development policies by these institutions. During the grant period, the grantee will monitor the effects of European Union public finance on climate change, increase its outreach to the general public, and strengthen the organizational capacity and financial sustainability of the grantee and its members. The grantee’s key achievements in 2011-2012 included leading a successful campaign on mainstreaming climate change issues in European Union policies, strengthening its collaboration with peer organizations and citizens, and developing a new organizational structure and programmatic strategies. CEE Bankwatch Network is registered in the Czech Republic, and its executive director is based in Budapest, Hungary.

title: General Purposes

title: International Society for Third-Sector Research
description: This grant increase will enable the International Society for Third Sector Research to organize a seventh international conference. The conference will bring together nonprofit scholars, researchers and practitioners to explore developments in the sector; interact with colleagues; and become informed about new ideas and debates that are going on around the world. Additional grant funds will be used to cover expenses related to planning and organizing the conference, including scholarships for participation by researchers from the developing world.

title: International Society for Third-Sector Research
description: This grant assists the International Society for Third-Sector Research, a global membership association that encourages, supports, and provides academic legitimacy to the study of the nonprofit sector around the world. Based at Johns Hopkins University, the society’s major accomplishments include convening seven biennial international research conferences; publishing special reports, conference working papers, and a scholarly journal; and convening regional meetings of research networks in Africa, Europe, Latin America and the Caribbean, and Asia and the Pacific. In 2007-2008, activities will include organizing regional network meetings in the Philippines, Brazil, and Spain; convening the directors of research centers involved in third-sector research; continuing to publish regular reports, newsletters, and a journal; and holding a biennial international conference in mid-2008 in Spain.

title: International Society for Third-Sector Research
description: This grant provides continued support to the International Society for Third-Sector Research, a global membership association with nearly 700 members from over 85 countries that encourages, supports, and provides academic legitimacy to the study of the nonprofit sector around the world. Based at Johns Hopkins University, the society’s major accomplishments include convening eight biennial international research conferences; publishing special reports, conference working papers, and a scholarly journal; and convening regional meetings of research networks in Africa, Europe, Latin America and the Caribbean, and Asia and the Pacific. In 2009-2010, activities will include organizing regional network meetings in Mexico, Taiwan, and Senegal; building research capacity in severely underserved and under-represented countries and regions; fostering an international network of directors of academic research centers focused on civil society; continuing to publish regular reports, newsletters, and a journal; and holding a biennial international conference in mid-2010 in Turkey.

title: International Society for Third-Sector Research
description: This grant provides continued support to the International Society for Third-Sector Research, a global membership association with nearly 600 members from over 85 countries that encourages, supports, and provides academic legitimacy to the study of civil society around the world. Founded in 1992 and based at Johns Hopkins University, the society’s major accomplishments include convening biennial international research conferences; publishing special reports, conference working papers, and a scholarly journal; and convening regional meetings of research networks in Africa, Europe, Latin America and the Caribbean, and Asia and the Pacific. In 2011-2012, activities will include organizing regional network meetings in Argentina, Indonesia, Japan, and South Africa; building research capacity in severely underserved and underrepresented countries and regions; fostering an international network of academic research center directors and graduate students; expanding the association’s Web site and continuing to publish a journal; and holding a biennial international conference in mid-2012 in Italy.

title: International Society for Third-Sector Research
description: This grant provides continued support to the International Society for Third-Sector Research, a global membership association with 652 members from 72 countries that encourages, supports, and provides academic legitimacy to the study of civil society around the world. Founded in 1992 and based at Johns Hopkins University, the society’s major accomplishments include convening biennial international research conferences; publishing special reports, conference working papers, and a scholarly journal; and convening regional meetings of research networks in Africa, Europe, Latin America and the Caribbean, and Asia and the Pacific. In 2013-2014, activities will include organizing regional network meetings in Chile, South Korea, and Africa; building research capacity in severely underserved and underrepresented countries and regions; fostering an international network of academic research center directors and graduate students; expanding the project’s Web site and continuing to publish a journal; and holding a biennial international conference in mid-2014 in Germany.

title: International Society for Third-Sector Research
description: This grant provides continued support to the International Society for Third-Sector Research, a global membership association with 652 members from 72 countries that encourages, supports, and provides academic legitimacy to the study of civil society around the world. Founded in 1992 and based at Johns Hopkins University, the society’s major accomplishments include convening biennial international research conferences; publishing special reports, conference working papers, and a scholarly journal; and convening regional meetings of research networks in Africa, Europe, Latin America and the Caribbean, and Asia and the Pacific. A grant increase will enable the society to support a special session on community foundations at its 11th International Conference in Muenster, Germany. The session is part of a set of projects and events marking the centennial of the community foundation field.

title: International Society for Third-Sector Research
description: This grant provides continued support to the International Society for Third-Sector Research, a global membership association with 870 members from 76 countries that encourages, supports, and provides academic legitimacy to the study of civil society. Founded in 1992 and based at Johns Hopkins University, the society’s major accomplishments include convening biennial international research conferences; publishing special reports, conference working papers, and a scholarly journal; and convening regional meetings of research networks in Africa, Europe, Latin America and the Caribbean, and Asia and the Pacific. In 2015-2016, activities will include organizing doctoral student seminars in Sweden, China, and Indonesia; hosting regional meetings in Puerto Rico, Japan, and Ghana; building research capacity in severely underserved and underrepresented countries and regions including China, the Middle East, and Russia; fostering an international network of academic research center directors; continuing to publish a journal; and holding a biennial international conference in mid-2016 in Sweden.

title: International Society for Third-Sector Research
description: This grant provides continued support to the International Society for Third-Sector Research, a global membership association with 885 members from 76 countries that encourages, supports, and provides academic legitimacy to the study of civil society. Founded in 1992 and based at Johns Hopkins University, the society’s major accomplishments include convening biennial international research conferences; publishing special reports, conference working papers, and a scholarly journal; and convening regional meetings of research networks on various continents. Over the next three years, the society’s major activities will include: 1) organizing annual PhD student seminars in several parts of the world; 2) hosting regional meetings in Africa, Asia, and Latin America; 3) expanding a network of African civil society scholars; 4) establishing an International Comparative Project on Institutional Philanthropy; 5) continuing to publish the journal “Voluntas”; and 6) holding a biennial international conference in mid-2018 in the Netherlands.

title: General Purposes
description: The Foundation Center operates five regional libraries and a network of 235 funding information centers located in professional, public-access libraries. Multiyear funding will enable the center to encourage the participation of grantseekers in the philanthropic process by making available free and fee-based training opportunities, peer sharing, research and information through a Web site, special topic e-newsletters and message boards, online and print directories, special reports, and publications. The Foundation Center, founded in 1956, will mark its 50th anniversary with a series of special events for its clients, including grantseekers, grantmakers, researchers, policymakers, the media and the general public.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides multiyear general purpose support to the Foundation Center, a national organization that collects, analyzes, and publishes information on foundations and philanthropy in its efforts to promote a fair and efficient philanthropic process. The center operates five regional libraries and a network of 348 funding information centers throughout the country. It provides training and information resources for grantseeking organizations and individuals.
