The center also produces and disseminates research on foundations and strategic communications that promote public understanding of philanthropy.

title: General Purposes
description: The Foundation Center is a national organization that collects, analyzes, and publishes information on foundations and philanthropy. The center operates five regional libraries and a network of 425 funding information centers throughout the country. It provides training and information resources for grantseeking organizations and individuals. Its databases contain profiles of approximately 100,000 grantmakers and more than 1.8 million grants around the world. The center also produces and disseminates research on foundations and strategic communications that promote public understanding of philanthropy. Over the past few years, the center has increasingly moved existing products and services online and has launched new ones using the latest communications technologies. Plans for 2010-2011 include expansion of electronic grant reporting, supporting information needs for global philanthropy development, and new research on philanthropy and critical social issues.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to the Foundation Center, a national organization that collects, analyzes, and publishes information on foundations and philanthropy. The grantee operates five regional libraries and a network of 460 funding information centers throughout the country. It provides training and information resources for grantseeking organizations and individuals. Its databases contain profiles of more than 100,000 grantmakers and more than two million grants around the world. The grantee also produces and disseminates research on foundations and strategic communications that promote public understanding of philanthropy. Its strategic priorities for 2012-2013 are to: 1) connect nonprofits to the resources they need to thrive; 2) empower donors with knowledge tools they need to be more strategic; 3) build the global data platform for philanthropy; 4) communicate philanthropy’s contribution to making a better world; 5) encourage greater transparency; and 6) ensure that technology provides a strong foundation for the grantee’s work.

title: General Purposes
description: The Foundation Center is a national organization that collects, analyzes, and publishes information on foundations and philanthropy. The grantee operates five regional libraries and a network of 460 funding information centers throughout the country. It provides training and information resources for grantseeking organizations and individuals. Its databases contain profiles of more than 100,000 grantmakers and more than two million grants around the world. The grantee also produces and disseminates research on foundations and nonprofits they support as well as strategic communications that promote public understanding of philanthropy. This grant increase will allow the grantee to merge three projects into its ongoing strategic activities. All three projects — Foundation Finances, Diversity in Philanthropy Research Metrics, and IssueLab — were supported by the Mott Foundation. As a result, tools and resources from these projects will be better positioned to reach key stakeholders, leverage impact, and ensure greater long-term value to the field.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to the Foundation Center, a national organization that collects, analyzes, and publishes information on foundations and philanthropy. The grantee operates five regional offices and a network of 483 funding information centers throughout the country. It provides training and information resources for grantseeking organizations and individuals. Its databases contain profiles of more than 100,000 grantmakers and more than three million grants around the world. The grantee also produces and disseminates research on foundations and strategic communications that promote public understanding of philanthropy. Its strategic priorities for 2014-2015 are to: 1) connect nonprofits to the resources they need to thrive; 2) empower donors with knowledge tools they need to be more strategic; 3) build the global data platform for philanthropy; 4) communicate philanthropy’s contribution to making a better world; 5) encourage greater transparency; and 6) ensure that technology provides a strong foundation for the grantee’s work.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to the Foundation Center, a national organization that collects, analyzes, and publishes information on foundations and philanthropy. The grantee operates five regional offices and a network of over 450 funding information centers throughout the country. It provides training and information resources for grantseeking organizations and individuals. Its databases contain profiles of more than 140,000 grantmakers and more than 3.8 million grants around the world. The grantee also produces and disseminates research on foundations and strategic communications that promote public understanding of philanthropy. Its strategic priorities for 2016-2017 are to: 1) connect nonprofits to the resources they need to thrive; 2) empower donors with knowledge tools they need to be more strategic; 3) build the global data platform for philanthropy; 4) communicate philanthropy’s contribution to making a better world; 5) encourage greater transparency; and 6) ensure that technology provides a strong foundation for the grantee’s work.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to the Foundation Center, an organization that collects, analyzes, and publishes information on foundations and philanthropy. The grantee serves more than six million people through its online resources, five regional offices, and a network of over 400 funding information centers throughout the United States and in nine other countries around the world. It provides training and information resources for thousands of grantseeking organizations and individuals every month by maintaining databases containing profiles of more than 140,000 grantmakers and 9.5 million grants around the world. The grantee also produces and disseminates research on foundations and strategic communications that promote public understanding of philanthropy. Their strategic priorities are to 1) connect nonprofits to the resources they need to thrive; 2) empower donors with knowledge tools to be more strategic; 3) build the global data platform for philanthropy; 4) communicate philanthropy’s contribution to making a better world; 5) encourage greater foundation transparency; and 6) ensure that technology provides a strong foundation for the center’s work.

title: Capacity Building in the South on Globalization and Sustainable Development
initiative: Reform of International Finance and Trade
description: The Third World Network Berhad is an international network of organizations and individuals involved in research and policy analysis of global issues and their impact on developing countries.This grant will enable the network to continue participating in the ongoing trade discussions taking place at the World Trade Organization. A continued presence in Geneva will enable the network to build on the progress made over the past five years by increasing the awareness of the impacts of international finance and trade on sustainable development, and strengthening the capacity of non-governmental organizations and decisionmakers in developing countries to effectively participate in international discussions on these issues.During the past grant period, the network’s work was critical in assisting developing country negotiators prepare for the World Trade Organization ministerial meeting in Hong Kong. In particular, it played a critical role in the negotiations and discussions on industrial tariffs and services.

title: Capacity Building in the South on Globalization and Sustainable Development
initiative: Reform of International Finance and Trade
description: Third World Network Berhad is an international network of organizations and individuals involved in research and policy analysis of global issues and their impact on developing countries. Through this grant, Third World Network Berhad will continue its presence in Geneva to actively participate in the ongoing trade discussions taking place at the World Trade Organization. This continued presence in Geneva will allow Third World Network Berhad to build on progress made over the last seven years by increasing the awareness of the impacts of international finance and trade on sustainable development and strengthening the capacity of nongovernmental organizations and decisionmakers in developing countries to effectively participate in international discussions on these issues.

title: Strengthen Philanthropy in South Africa
description: This grant will enable the Synergos Institute’s southern African regional office to foster a culture of giving and strengthen indigenous philanthropy in South Africa and the broader region. Activities will include institutional development of the philanthropic sector, training, capacity building, research, conferences, seminars and workshops, and networking.Achievements during the past three years included providing advisory support to partners and other stakeholders in the philanthropy and civil society sectors, both in the southern Africa region and more globally; connecting partners in South Africa and the region to international philanthropy conversations and networks; supporting research and case studies on key challenges in philanthropy and social justice; disseminating tools and resources for grantmakers and philanthropists; providing technical assistance to partners and other stakeholders; convening learning forums and dialogue and capacity-building events; facilitating staff and board development for indigenous grantmaking organizations; and promoting wider regional grantmaker networks and affinity groups.The institute, founded in 1986, promotes collaborative approaches to overcoming poverty and fostering sustainable development in developing countries.

title: General Purposes
description: The Synergos Institute was established to coordinate and strengthen philanthropy globally. Mott provided previous support to strengthen philanthropy in the southern Africa region through a regional office in South Africa. The regional office has since established itself as a South African nonprofit with its own staff and local board. This grant will provide support to the local Synergos nonprofit to strengthen philanthropic and nonprofit organizations in South Africa and the broader southern Africa region. Particular emphasis will be given to building philanthropy for social justice. Synergos will provide training, support, and technical assistance to independent foundations, grantmakers, community foundations, and other bridging organizations. The grantee will also provide networking opportunities, facilitate debates and discussions, and support advocacy to strengthen indigenous philanthropy in South Africa and the broader southern Africa region.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide continued general purpose support to Synergos Institute (Southern Africa) in their efforts to strengthen grantmaking organizations and the philanthropic sector in Southern Africa. In collaboration with partners, the grantee works to mobilize resources and bridge socioeconomic divides to reduce poverty, increase equity, and advance social justice in Southern Africa. Building on its strength as a convener, connector, advisor, knowledge broker, partnership builder, and deep understanding of the development challenges of the region and social justice philanthropy, Synergos will focus on inclusive partnerships to address systemic challenges, leadership development, and knowledge generation and dissemination.

title: General Purposes
description: Synergos Institute (Southern Africa) promotes systemic change in Africa by strengthening collaborative leadership and supporting partnerships that promote equitable access to basic human rights and services among governments, civil society institutions, and the private sector. Mott has provided general purpose support to the grantee to implement its various programs, including convening leaders of philanthropic organizations from southern Africa for mutual learning and sharing experiences. The grantee also supported the African Senior Fellows network, a network of experienced civil society leaders committed to collaborative efforts that address the underlying causes of poverty and inequality. This grant will continue to provide general purpose support to the grantee. One of the key activities over the next two years will be promoting the growth of philanthropy in Africa through building the leadership capacity of key grantmaking institutions.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to build social development capacity in Central/Eastern Europe and Russia. To this end, the Development School, a registered charity in the United Kingdom, offers two validated postgraduate learning programs: one for social development practitioners and the other for leaders of grantmaking foundations in the region. A total of 32 people are participating in residential learning sessions, one-on-one work with tutors, and independent research and writing assignments. By the end of the grant, students will be required to attend additional residential sessions and complete dissertations, which will be reviewed and confirmed by university examination boards. During the grant period, the Development School will focus entirely on completing both postgraduate programs. The Development School is managed from London, and most residential sessions are held in Hungary.

title: General Purposes
description: The Altamaha River and its major tributaries drain more than 14,000 square miles, making it the largest watershed in Georgia and the fourth largest on the East Coast. The river is one of the most biodiverse in North America. The Altamaha Riverkeeper was founded in 1999 to protect and restore the habitat, water quality and flow of the mighty river from its headwaters in north Georgia to its terminus at the Atlantic Ocean. This grant increase will support the organization’s continued work to reduce water pollution, protect forested wetlands, promote sound water management policy and build organizational capacity.

title: Study on Education Organizing and Academic Improvement
grantee: Northwest Bronx Community and Clergy Coalition
description: This grant will provide partial support to the Northwest Bronx Community and Clergy Coalition for the group’s education organizing work. The education work will focus primarily on: 1) deepening the leadership skills of parents and youth engaged in the organizing work; 2) more closely uniting and coordinating the youth and parent organizing efforts; and 3) winning local campaigns for school improvements especially in the area of additional facilities, small schools, school safety, school funding, and teacher quality. In addition, this grant will enable the organization to participate in the Foundation’s eight-site study exploring the contribution of education organizing to education reform efforts.

title: Study on Education Organizing and Academic Improvement
grantee: Northwest Bronx Community and Clergy Coalition
description: The Northwest Bronx Community and Clergy Coalition conducts education organizing work and participates in the Foundation’s eight-site study exploring the contribution of education organizing to education reform efforts. This grant increase will support a professional development program for the two education organizers.

title: Study on Education Organizing and Academic Improvement
grantee: Northwest Bronx Community and Clergy Coalition
description: The Northwest Bronx Community and Clergy Coalition is a multi-issue, multiconstituency organizing group. The organization participated in the Foundation’s eight-site study exploring the contribution of education organizing to education reform efforts. This grant represents a final tie-off grant to the organization for this work.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to increase the effectiveness of grantmaking and improve the conditions for philanthropy in Slovakia. To this end, the Slovak Donors Forum will improve the quality, efficiency, and variety of member services; strengthen individual and corporate philanthropy in Slovakia; enhance transparency and accountability of nonprofit organizations; and improve communication and interaction within the nonprofit sector. In addition, the forum will strengthen its institutional capacity by broadening its membership base, strengthening collaboration among members, and improving the professional skills of its staff. The Slovak Donors Forum was initiated in 1996 as an informal body and was registered in 2000 as an association of grantmakers. Currently, the forum has 22 regular members and 4 observers. The forum’s key achievements include providing effective support to the Slovak grantmaking community, promoting philanthropic activities in Slovakia, and establishing partnerships with international donor networks.

title: Southeast Land Trust Capacity-Building Program
geographic_focus: South Carolina, Virginia, Alabama, Louisiana, North Carolina, Tennessee, Mississippi, Georgia
description: Just over 90 local land trusts are active in the four southeastern ecoregions of interest to Mott’s freshwater ecosystems grantmaking. With previous support, the Land Trust Alliance, a national provider of technical assistance to land trusts, has worked in the region to build land trust effectiveness, encourage strategic planning and partnerships, accelerate the pace of private land conservation, and help ensure the permanence of land conservation achievements. Renewal support will enable the alliance to continue this work with an emphasis on helping land trusts prepare for a new voluntary land trust accreditation process.

title: Southeast and Great Lakes Land Trust Capacity-Building Program
geographic_focus: Alabama, Georgia, Mississippi, Tennessee, Louisiana, North Carolina, Virginia, South Carolina
description: The Land Trust Alliance builds the capacity of local and regional land trusts to partner with private landowners, local governments, and federal agencies to protect natural ecosystems. With prior Mott support, the alliance has provided guidance, mentoring, and targeted grant awards and technical assistance to land trusts in support of their freshwater conservation work. With continued Mott support, the alliance will increase the pace and quality of land conservation activities in priority freshwater ecosystems, while advancing strategic conservation planning for land trusts working to protect and restore rivers, lakes, and wetlands in the Great Lakes basin and southeastern United States.

title: Southeast and Great Lakes Land Trust Capacity-Building Program
geographic_focus: Mississippi, Virginia, South Carolina, Alabama, Georgia, Tennessee, Louisiana, North Carolina
description: The Land Trust Alliance, a national organization serving land trusts in the United States, builds the capacities of land trusts to protect freshwater ecosystems and water quality in regions of interest to the Mott Foundation. With prior Mott support, the grantee has provided numerous land trusts in the Great Lakes and southeastern United States with training, guided organizational assessments, mentoring, and financial assistance. With continued Mott support, the grantee will continue to increase the pace and quality of land conservation activities in the Great Lakes Basin and southeastern United States, while advancing the strategic conservation of priority freshwater ecosystems in both regions. Funds in the first year of the grant will also be used to launch a network of Gulf Coast land trusts working together in response to the BP oil spill.

title: Strengthening Land Trusts and Promoting Collaboration to Conserve Freshwater Ecosystems in the Great Lakes Basin
geographic_focus: Michigan, Pennsylvania, New York, Wisconsin, Indiana, Minnesota, Illinois, Ohio
description: The Land Trust Alliance is the national organization that helps build the capacity of individual land trusts while also representing land trust interests at the federal level. With prior Mott support, the grantee has helped many land trusts in the Great Lakes Basin and southeastern United States better protect land and freshwater resources. Over the next two years, the grantee will focus its Mott-supported efforts in the Great Lakes. Activities will include facilitating land trust collaborations, promoting strategic freshwater conservation, increasing public engagement, and providing capacity-building services to a range of land trusts.

title: Strengthening Land Trusts and Promoting Collaboration to Conserve Freshwater Ecosystems in the Great Lakes Basin
geographic_focus: Michigan, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, New York, Indiana, Minnesota, Illinois, Ohio
description: The Land Trust Alliance is a national organization that helps build the capacity of individual land trusts while also representing land trust interests at the federal level. With prior Mott support, the grantee’s Midwest office helped Great Lakes land trusts improve their abilities to protect land and freshwater resources. With continued Mott support over the next two years, the grantee will provide Great Lakes land trusts with technical assistance and regrants aimed at building organizational capacity, promoting freshwater conservation, and supporting local conservation projects in collaboration with watershed groups and community-based organizations.

title: Strengthening Land Trusts and Promoting Collaboration to Conserve Freshwater Ecosystems in the Great Lakes Basin
geographic_focus: Pennsylvania, New York, Indiana, Illinois, Ohio, Wisconsin, Michigan, Minnesota
description: Formed in 1982, the Land Trust Alliance is a national conservation organization that helps build the capacity of individual land trusts while also representing land trust interests at the federal level. With prior Mott support, the grantee has helped many land trusts in the Great Lakes Basin better protect land that is connected to freshwater resources. With prior Mott support, the grantee provided technical assistance and regrants aimed at building the organizational capacity of its members in the Great Lakes region. With renewed support, the grantee will continue to look for opportunities to promote land conservation strategies that provide significant freshwater benefits. The grantee will also work with local organizations to support specific conservation projects and help members develop land stewardship strategies to build resiliency for a changing climate.

title: Strengthening Land Trusts and Promoting Collaboration to Conserve Freshwater Systems in the Great Lakes Basin
geographic_focus: Wisconsin, Michigan, Illinois, Pennsylvania, Indiana, New York, Minnesota, Ohio
description: The Land Trust Alliance is a national organization that provides technical support, training, and assistance to support land conservation, acquisition, and protection. With this renewal grant from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has lifted land trusts in the Great Lakes region to the point where they are performing better than land trusts across the nation. With renewed support, and following a model developed in the Chesapeake Bay, the grantee will investigate the viability of using land trust-related strategies to reduce polluted runoff in distressed Great Lakes watersheds. The grantee will continue to develop excellence among land trusts in the region, and will provide capacity support for enhanced communications and education.

title: Florida Statewide Education Reform Project
description: This grant will enable People Acting for Community Together (PACT) to continue the Florida Statewide Education Reform Project, a grassroots community organizing effort. A coalition of nine congregation-based community organizations will work together on a statewide effort to establish high quality standards for Florida’s Voluntary Universal Pre-Kindergarten program. In addition, each organization will work on local education-related issues. Participating organizations will receive assistance with capacity building, leadership development and training, and opportunities to share challenges, successes and strategies from their local campaign work.PACT was founded in 1988 by a group of interfaith religious leaders who were concerned about the growing powerlessness and alienation confronting low- and moderate-income people in Dade County, Florida. Since then, PACT has expanded to 28 institutional members including churches, synagogues and schools, representing more than 400,000 people from Anglo, Hispanic and Haitian/West Indian and English-speaking Caribbean communities.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to support people’s engagement in and awareness of local and national decisionmaking processes and to encourage transparency and accountability of national and local government in Croatia. Building on its success in mobilizing volunteer election monitors, GONG’s work has expanded to three key program areas: monitoring local and national elections and raising public awareness of election processes; increasing public confidence and participation in local and national assemblies; and networking with similar organizations in Central and Eastern Europe and relevant international organizations. Over the past two years, GONG has monitored local elections, provided educational activities for first-time voters in high schools across Croatia, and published a guide and online resource related to public administration. GONG has an office in Zagreb and four regional offices.

title: General Purposes
description: The negotiation process for relicensing 13 large hydroelectric dams on the Catawba-Wateree river system in North and South Carolina is nearing completion. This grant will enable the coalition to participate in the final stages of the relicensing process and potentially support monitoring of the initial implementation of a newly granted license.Prior funding to the Catawba-Wateree Relicensing Coalition supported efforts to promote the adoption of a collaborative approach to the relicensing process, conduct public education and outreach efforts, and directly participate in the relicensing process.

title: General Purposes
description: The relicensing of 13 large hydroelectric dams on the Catawba-Wateree River system in North and South Carolina is nearing completion. Prior funding to the Catawba-Wateree Relicensing Coalition, an organization representing diverse stakeholders, supported public education and outreach efforts and enabled the coalition to directly participate in the relicensing process. This renewal grant will support the coalition’s continued engagement in the final stages of the relicensing process and the early stages of license implementation.

title: Identifying Promising Practices
description: This grant will continue to support the efforts of Learning Point Associates of collecting and disseminating promising practices for afterschool practitioners. This will include examples of high quality afterschool activities that are rich with educational content and support opportunities for success in academics, career opportunities, or job training. Learning Point Associates also will document cases in which comprehensive school reform incorporates afterschool activities. In addition, Learning Point Associates will work with the Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative, a consortium of national organizations working to further statewide afterschool networks and provide expertise on quality programming.

title: Identifying Promising Practices
description: This grant will continue to support the efforts of Learning Point Associates to collect and disseminate promising practices for school day and afterschool educators. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) produce an expanded learning opportunities research brief focused on promising practices and lessons learned from school reform models; 2) track American Recovery Reinvestment Act stimulus funding used for afterschool programs; and 3) continue to work with the Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative, a consortium of national organizations providing technical assistance to statewide afterschool networks in their efforts to further afterschool policies and practices.

title: Identifying Promising Practices
description: This grant to American Institutes for Research will support their efforts to collect and disseminate promising practices for school day and afterschool educators. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) produce a research brief focused on cost-effective afterschool and expanded learning strategies; 2) provide technical assistance and resources on expanded learning to states and districts; and 3) continue to work with the Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative, a consortium of national organizations providing technical assistance to the statewide afterschool networks in their efforts to further afterschool policies and practices.

title: Identifying Promising Practices
description: This grant to American Institutes for Research will continue to support their efforts to collect and disseminate promising practices for school day and afterschool educators. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) develop tools and resources to assist afterschool educators in cultivating noncognitive skills or personal learning competencies for youth; 2) provide technical assistance and resources on expanded learning programs to states and districts; and 3) continue to work with the Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative, a consortium of national organizations providing technical assistance to the statewide afterschool networks, in their efforts to further afterschool policies and practices.

title: Identifying Promising Practices
description: This grant to American Institutes for Research will continue to support their efforts to collect and disseminate promising practices for school day and afterschool educators. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) develop tools and resources to assist afterschool educators in cultivating social and emotional learning and workforce development; 2) provide technical assistance and resources on afterschool and summer learning programs to states and districts; and 3) continue to work with the Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative, a consortium of national organizations providing technical assistance to the statewide afterschool networks in their efforts to further afterschool policies and practices.

title: Identifying Promising Practices
description: This grant to American Institutes for Research will continue to support their efforts to collect and disseminate promising practices for school day and afterschool educators. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) develop tools and resources to assist afterschool educators in cultivating social and emotional learning, college and career readiness, and workforce development; 2) provide technical assistance and resources on afterschool and summer learning programs to states and districts; and 3) continue to work with the Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative, a consortium of national organizations providing technical assistance to the statewide afterschool networks in their efforts to further afterschool policies and practices.

title: Freshwater Leadership Initiative
geographic_focus: Alabama, Mississippi, Tennessee, Indiana, Wisconsin, New York, Georgia, Minnesota, Ontario, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Michigan, Illinois, North Carolina, South Carolina
description: Through the Freshwater Leadership Initiative, the Institute for Conservation Leadership aims to improve the organizational capacity of freshwater conservation groups in the Great Lakes and Southeast, as well as strengthen collaborative efforts among such organizations.This grant will enable the institute to continue helping freshwater conservation groups use a blended approach of workshops, intensive training, consulting, facilitation and coaching to meet the developmental needs of the groups.Accomplishments during the past two years included providing one-day workshops to more than 170 groups; consulting more intensely with 16 groups; and producing an organizational assessment workbook for all-volunteer groups.

title: Freshwater Leadership Initiative
geographic_focus: Alabama, Indiana, Mississippi, Michigan, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Illinois, New York, Wisconsin, North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia, Tennessee, Ontario, Minnesota
description: Strong leadership, organizational capacity, and networking skills are needed for organizations to successfully conserve and protect aquatic resources in the Great Lakes and southeastern United States. The Institute for Conservation Leadership strengthens the effectiveness and long-term capacity of organizations through consulting, training, coaching, and meeting facilitation. With previous support, the institute has aided groups with strategic planning, fundraising, leadership development, and board engagement. Renewal support will enable the institute to help organizations in the Great Lakes and southeastern United States focus on capacity building and enhanced leadership skills, while allowing the institute to further develop its own internal capacity and program development.

title: Freshwater Leadership Initiative
geographic_focus: New York, South Carolina, Illinois, Wisconsin, Georgia, North Carolina, Tennessee, Pennsylvania, Ontario, Ohio, Michigan, Alabama, Indiana, Mississippi, Minnesota
description: The Institute for Conservation Leadership builds the capacity of environmental organizations through consulting, training, coaching, meeting facilitation, and research to help groups more effectively accomplish their missions. With previous support, the institute has helped strengthen organizations in the Great Lakes and Southeast that are focused on freshwater issues through help with strategic planning, fundraising, leadership development, and board engagement. With renewed support, the institute will use these capacity-building tools to help organizations adapt to the changing economic environment with a focus on strengthening leadership teams, fundraising capabilities, and the strategic use of volunteers.

title: Freshwater Leadership Initiative
geographic_focus: Ontario, Pennsylvania, North Carolina, Georgia, Mississippi, Michigan, Ohio, Tennessee, New York, Wisconsin, South Carolina, Illinois, Minnesota, Alabama, Indiana
description: The Institute for Conservation Leadership is a national technical assistance provider that builds the capacity of environmental organizations through a blended approach of training, consulting, facilitating, and coaching. With previous Mott support, the grantee helped strengthen freshwater groups in the Great Lakes and Southeast by assisting with strategic planning, fundraising, leadership development, board engagement, and other organizational development needs. With this renewal, the institute will focus its services on more intensive support to organizations and coalitions addressing high priority freshwater restoration and protection issues in the Great Lakes and southeastern regions of the United States.

title: Freshwater Leadership Initiative
geographic_focus: Ohio, Georgia, South Carolina, Tennessee, Ontario, Pennsylvania, North Carolina, New York, Michigan, Wisconsin, Illinois, Minnesota, Alabama, Indiana, Mississippi
description: The Institute for Conservation Leadership is a national technical assistance provider that builds the capacity of environmental organizations through training, consulting, facilitating, and coaching. With previous Mott support, the grantee helped strengthen freshwater groups in the Great Lakes and Southeast by assisting with strategic planning, fundraising, leadership development, board engagement, and other organizational development needs. With this renewal, the grantee will offer a range of intensive capacity building support services to organizations and coalitions addressing high priority freshwater restoration and protection issues in the Great Lakes region.

title: Freshwater Leadership Initiative
geographic_focus: Ohio, Ontario, New York, Illinois, Indiana, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Pennsylvania, Michigan
description: The Institute for Conservation Leadership is a national technical assistance provider that builds the capacity of environmental organizations through training, consulting, facilitating, and coaching. With previous Mott support, the grantee helped strengthen freshwater groups in the Great Lakes region by assisting with strategic planning, fundraising, leadership development, board engagement, and other organizational development needs. With this renewal, the grantee will provide in-depth, capacity building support services to selected organizations and coalitions addressing high priority freshwater restoration and protection issues in the Great Lakes region. The grantee will also undertake a regional assessment of the capacity needs of freshwater groups.

title: Freshwater Leadership Initiative
description: The Institute for Conservation Leadership is a national technical assistance provider that builds the capacity of environmental organizations through training, consulting, facilitating, and coaching. With previous Mott support, the grantee initiated an in-depth regional assessment of the capacity needs of freshwater groups focusing on leadership development. This grant increase will allow the grantee to complete this research and develop services that meet the needs of Great Lakes freshwater organizations.

title: Freshwater Leadership Initiative
description: The Institute for Conservation Leadership is a national technical assistance provider that builds the capacity of environmental organizations through training, consulting, facilitating, and coaching. With previous Mott support, the grantee facilitated a regional assessment of the capacity needs of Great Lakes groups and their leaders. With renewed support, the grantee will develop and provide strategic capacity building and professional development services for freshwater nonprofits in the Great Lakes region.

title: Environmental Grantmakers Association and Funders Network on Trade and Globalization
description: This grant will support several efforts of the Rockefeller Family Fund’s Environmental Grantmakers Association, including the annual fall retreat and the Funders Network on Trade and Globalization, a working group of the Environmental Grantmakers Association. The association’s activities provide venues for environmental grantmakers to gain a stronger awareness and understanding of the challenges confronting the environmental community, as well as to discuss grantmaking strategies and explore areas for collaboration.

title: Environmental Grantmakers Association and Funders Network on Trade and Globalization
description: This renewal grant will support several efforts of the Rockefeller Family Fund’s Environmental Grantmakers Association, including the activities covered by Mott’s annual membership dues, the association’s biennial Federal Policy Briefing, and the association’s Funders’ Network on Trade and Globalization. The association helps environmental grantmakers gain a stronger awareness and understanding of the challenges confronting the environmental community, as well as discuss grantmaking strategies and explore areas for collaboration. Past accomplishments include the hosting of an annual fall retreat for all association members and the organizing of funder delegations that attend international trade meetings.

title: General Purposes
description: This renewal grant will provide general purposes support to the Environmental Grantmakers Association. Additional funding will provide support for the 2008 State of the States meeting and the 2009 Federal Policy Briefing. Activities of the grantee provide venues for environmental grantmakers to gain a stronger awareness and understanding of the challenges confronting the environmental community, as well as to discuss grantmaking strategies and explore areas for collaboration.

title: General Purposes
description: This renewal grant will provide general purpose support to the Environmental Grantmakers Association. The association provides venues for environmental grantmakers to gain a stronger awareness and understanding of the challenges confronting the environmental community, as well as to discuss grantmaking strategies and explore areas for collaboration.

title: General Purposes
description: Environmental grantmakers with shared interests are using a range of Web-based and other tools to map the collective impact of their grantmaking. This grant increase will support the general purposes of the Environmental Grantmakers Association, which includes convening a one-day workshop for teams involved in such mapping activities in order to network and identify best practices.

title: General Purposes
description: This renewal grant will provide general purpose support to the Environmental Grantmakers Association. Activities of the grantee provide venues for environmental grantmakers to gain a stronger awareness and understanding of the challenges confronting the environmental community, as well as to discuss grantmaking strategies and explore areas for collaboration. Over the next grant period, the grantee will also work to expand its coverage of global environmental issues.

title: General Purposes
description: This renewal grant will provide general purpose support to the Environmental Grantmakers Association. Activities of the grantee provide venues for environmental grantmakers to gain a stronger awareness and understanding of the challenges confronting the environmental community, as well as to discuss grantmaking strategies and explore areas for collaboration. Over the next grant period, the grantee will also expand its work, connecting global and domestic environmental issues.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to the Environmental Grantmakers Association for its activities to support environmental grantmakers. The grantee expects to use this grant increase to support additional costs related to facilitating increased funder collaboration on water issues.

title: General Purposes
description: This renewal grant will provide general purpose support to the Environmental Grantmakers Association, which offers venues for environmental grantmakers to share knowledge and foster debate on critical environmental issues. In particular, the grantee’s annual retreat is an important forum that allows grantmakers to network and discuss common goals.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purpose support to the Environmental Grantmakers Association, which offers venues for environmental grantmakers to share knowledge and foster debate on critical environmental issues. In particular, the grantee’s annual retreat is an important forum that allows grantmakers to network and discuss common goals.

title: New Models for Global Economic Governance
initiative: Reform of International Finance and Trade
description: This grant renewal will support continued research to examine the social and environmental impacts of trade agreements and economic integration in the Western Hemisphere. The Global Development and Economic Institute of Tufts University will contribute to the trade policy negotiation process through empirical research, continued collaboration with Mexican economists and academics, and expanded research collaborations with global experts and specialists in Latin America. Research findings will be disseminated in peer-reviewed research publications and to popular audiences and policymakers.

title: Study on Education Organizing and Academic Improvement
description: This grant will provide partial support to Oakland Community Organizations for the Small Schools Campaign. Oakland Community Organizations recently won a commitment from the school district to establish new, small autonomous schools designed to raise academic standards, especially in lower-income neighborhoods. This grant is for the follow-up project, the Small Schools Campaign, which will organize parents and teachers citywide to act as educational reform leaders and ensure effective implementation of the new schools. In addition, this grant will enable the organization to participate in the Foundation’s eight-site study to explore the contribution of education organizing to education reform efforts in low-performing districts and schools.

title: General Purposes
description: The International Center for Transitional Justice was established in 2001 to provide assistance to countries grappling with past human rights abuses. Based in New York City, the center operates in more than 30 countries, including the Balkans and South Africa, and provides research, technical assistance, legal counsel and policy recommendations to governments and nonprofit organizations.This grant will enable the center to expand its programs in the Middle East, North Africa and French-speaking Africa; establish field offices in Europe and Africa; focus on strengthening its civil society partnerships; build a strategic rapid response program; and improve its evaluation efforts.The center has undertaken more than 250 missions to more than 30 countries during the past five years.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to support the continued organizational and programmatic development of the International Center for Transitional Justice, which was established in 2001 to provide assistance to countries grappling with past human rights abuses. The center operates in more than 30 countries, including the Balkans and South Africa, providing research, technical assistance, and policy recommendations to governments and civil society organizations. During the grant period, the center will respond to urgent requests for assistance around the world; develop new programs that will keep it on the cutting edge of transitional justice work; and strengthen its institutional capacity by improving knowledge management, monitoring and evaluation, and communications. During the previous grant period, the center provided policy advice in Uganda and Kenya, built and strengthened institutions in Liberia and Columbia, empowered leaders and practitioners in the field through training and fellowship programs, and conducted research that led to new policy options. The center is based in New York City.

title: Senior Fellows Program
description: The Senior Fellows Program, created by the Synergos Institute in 1999, identifies talented foundation leaders from key philanthropic institutions worldwide and links them to a global learning and service network. Senior fellows serve as peer consultants to developing foundations and associations of grantmakers around the world, and their work produces knowledge on trends and innovative models.This grant will enable the institute foster a greater sense of ownership of the network by the senior fellows; increase the global impact of the network; provide more opportunities for all fellows to be engaged in the program; and capture and disseminate the knowledge generated by the network more effectively.During the past year, activities included diversifying the geographical composition of senior fellows from 25 countries to 28; providing senior fellows with varied learning opportunities; enabling senior fellows to provide technical assistance and capacity-building to emerging community foundations and grantmakers throughout the world; and establishing an advisory committee of five current senior fellows to select the next class of senior fellows, review program achievements and shortcomings, and plan for the future.

title: Senior Fellows Program
description: The Senior Fellows Program identifies talented leaders from key philanthropic and civil society institutions worldwide and links them to a global learning and service network. Senior fellows serve as peer consultants to developing foundations and associations of grantmakers around the world, and their work produces knowledge on trends and innovative models, which the Synergos Institute distributes to a wide audience. The current senior fellows’ network is comprised of 82 fellows from 28 countries. Since the program began in 2000, the fellows have conducted more than 200 workshops, seminars, and consultancies. Founded in 1986, the Synergos Institute promotes collaborative approaches that bring rich and poor together, along with other relevant groups and institutions, to overcome poverty and foster sustainable development in developing countries.

title: Senior Fellows Program
description: The Synergos Institute’s Senior Fellows Program links civil society leaders in a worldwide learning, service, and action network. The network strengthens the capacities of these leaders and provides them with opportunities to be catalysts in partnerships that address the systemic causes of poverty and promote sustainable social change. Senior fellows serve as peer consultants to developing community foundations and other civil society organizations around the world, and their work produces knowledge on trends and innovative models which the Synergos Institute distributes to a wide audience. The current senior fellows network is comprised of 100 fellows from 30 countries. In 2010-2011, the program will add up to 30 new fellows and provide networking, convening, peer learning, collaboration, and service opportunities. Founded in 1986, the Synergos Institute promotes collaborative approaches that bring rich and poor together, along with other relevant groups and institutions, to overcome poverty and foster sustainable development in developing countries.

title: General Purposes
description: Georgia contains some of the most biologically rich waters in the continental United States, providing immeasurable economic, community, and aesthetic benefits. With previous support, the Georgia River Network, a state leader in river conservation and restoration efforts, has promoted new beneficial river policies, assisted citizens with organizing watershed groups and helped to build those groups’ capacity to protect and restore rivers, and strengthened its own institutional capabilities. Renewal support will enable the network to continue to coordinate statewide partnerships and promote sound policies, increase its outreach to new watershed groups, and work to build the organization’s financial and operational strength.

title: General Purposes
description: Georgia River Network engages citizens to protect and restore the state’s rivers by supporting watershed groups and informing policy. Georgia contains some of the most biologically rich rivers in the continental United States, and many of its waters are considered globally outstanding for their diverse aquatic life. With prior Mott support, the grantee promoted beneficial river policies, helped citizens organize watershed groups, enhanced these groups’ capacities to protect and restore rivers, and strengthened its own institutional capabilities. This grant renewal will allow the network to continue providing capacity building and other technical services to Georgia’s river and watershed groups.

title: General Purposes
description: The Vital Voices Global Leadership Network continues to grow and currently includes 5,000 women in 85 countries. It has successfully engaged leading experts and connected them with emerging leaders and social entrepreneurs working to bring about change in their home countries.This grant will enable the network to focus on developing a truly interactive, global Web site to foster knowledge-sharing among network members; creating and distributing a series of publications to promote the sharing of “lessons without borders” within the network; and producing a series of educational films that will connect trainees and network members with world-class experts and inspirational leaders.

title: Program to Establish and Enforce Performance Standards for Hydropower Dams to Restore Aquatic Diversity
geographic_focus: Alabama, New York, North Carolina, South Carolina
description: Hydropower dams provide many benefits, such as electrical power and flood control, but they also impact freshwater biodiversity by changing river flows and restricting fish passage. The Natural Heritage Institute, one of the nation’s leading experts on the licensing of hydropower facilities, provides strategic advice, scientific expertise, and other technical help to national- and state-level organizations active in such proceedings. Prior support has allowed the institute to provide free or low-cost assistance to organizations involved in relicensing processes in the Great Lakes and Southeast, and renewal support will help the institute continue to play this important technical assistance role.

title: Program to Establish and Enforce Performance Standards for Hydropower Dams to Restore Aquatic Diversity
geographic_focus: South Carolina, North Carolina, Alabama, New York
description: The operating licenses for hydropower facilities extend for 30-50 years, so the process of renewing licenses presents unique opportunities to include new provisions geared toward ecosystem restoration. The Natural Heritage Institute, a national organization using interdisciplinary research and legal skills to solve environmental problems, provides its expertise to conservation and community groups engaged in relicensings. With Mott support since 2001, the institute has assisted such groups in the Great Lakes and southeastern United States, helping to achieve many improvements in the operation of hydropower dams in both regions. Continued support from Mott will enable the institute to sustain its work, primarily in the Southeast where several major relicensings are moving toward completion.

title: Program to Establish and Enforce Performance Standards for Hydropower Dams to Restore Aquatic Diversity
description: With this grant increase, the Natural Heritage Institute will continue to provide legal, scientific, and technical assistance to partner groups engaged in hydropower relicensing processes in South Carolina and Alabama.

title: Bridges to the Future Before and Afterschool Program
description: Since 1998, United Way of Genesee County has been operating Bridges to the Future, an afterschool program for elementary to high school students that encourages positive youth development through safe, accessible, and challenging activities that appeal to students’ diverse interests. The United Way of Genesee County Bridges to the Future program is now being implemented in more than 100 schools in all 21 local school districts. This grant will provide funds to supplement more than $800,000 in state funding for Bridges to the Future and enable United Way of Genesee County to sustain a full range of activities at each site.

title: Bridges to the Future Before and Afterschool Program
description: Since 1998, United Way of Genesee County has been operating Bridges to the Future, an afterschool program for elementary to high school students that encourages positive youth development through safe, accessible and challenging activities that appeal to students’ diverse interests. The United Way of Genesee County Bridges to the Future program now is being implemented in more than 100 schools in all 21 county school districts.This grant will provide funds to supplement more than $800,000 in state funding for Bridges to the Future and enable United Way of Genesee County to sustain a full range of activities at each site. Funding includes a grant increase to support the exploration and implementation of additional programmatic services for middle school and high school youth in the Westwood Heights School District.

title: Bridges to the Future Before and Afterschool Program
description: United Way of Genesee County works in partnership with the Flint Community Schools and the Genesee Intermediate School District to operate Bridges to the Future, an afterschool program for students in kindergarten through ninth grade. The program encourages positive youth development through safe, accessible, and challenging activities that appeal to students’ diverse interests. Bridges to the Future is offered in more than 100 schools in all 21 Genesee County school districts. According to a recent third-party evaluation, more than 90 percent of parents whose children attend Bridges to the Future report that their children do better in school and learn new things as a result of the program. Mott funding will provide partial support for the program’s operations during the 2007-2008 year, enabling United Way of Genesee County to continue refining the Bridges to the Future model while seeking a sustainable long-term funding stream.

title: Bridges to the Future Before and Afterschool Program
description: This grant will provide support to the United Way of Genesee County for the Bridges to the Future Before and Afterschool Program. The program is designed to improve the cognitive, socio-emotional, and physical outcomes for children in kindergarten through ninth grade by providing academic, cultural, and recreational enrichment in safe, school-based programs. In partnership with the Genesee Intermediate School District and the Flint Community Schools, the program operates in more than 100 sites in 21 school districts. During this grant period, the initiative will focus on refining its program model and providing professional development to the providers in its network. Established in 1922, the United Way of Genesee County supports local nonprofits in the areas of basic needs, child/youth development, older adults, and strengthening families.

title: Bridges to the Future Afterschool Program
description: This grant will provide support to the United Way of Genesee County for the Bridges to the Future Afterschool Program. For the 2009-10 program year, Bridges will begin to implement a new strategic plan that provides a research-based, high quality afterschool program model to students with the greatest needs. To develop this plan, the United Way of Genesee County, Genesee Intermediate School District, and Flint Community Schools considered questions of governance, management structure, program structure, criteria for selecting schools and sites, quality development, and staffing. The program will place renewed emphasis on positive student outcomes for learning and youth development. A system of shared support for professional development and curriculum will be put into place for 44 sites with funding from the 21st Century Community Learning Centers and the Foundation. Established in 1922, the United Way of Genesee County supports local nonprofits in the areas of basic needs, child/youth development, older adults, and strengthening families.

title: Engaging Black Donors in Philanthropy
description: This grant provides partial support to the Twenty-First Century Foundation for its Engaging Black Donors in Philanthropy initiative, a program that connects African-American assets with black-led charities. The initiative will continue to promote strategic giving in the African-American community with a new focus on targeted messages and an enhanced level of individual cultivation. During this grant period, the Twenty-First Century Foundation will focus its efforts on a targeted donor education and marketing campaign to include a quarterly e-newsletter and the launch of a Black Philanthropy Index surveying priorities for giving and action for its donor constituency.

title: Alliance for Quality Education: Statewide Education Financing Reform Project
grantee: Public Policy and Education Fund of New York
description: The Alliance for Quality Education: Statewide Education Financing Reform Project was organized in late 1999 to build a coalition of community organizations and other education stakeholders who were interested in working on school finance reform and education improvements in New York State, especially for children from economically disadvantaged communities. This grant to the Public Policy and Education Fund of New York supports continued organizing work to empower local residents to help shape the future of education financing throughout the state through coalition building, a media strategy, training of local leaders, and organizing public forums to educate the public. This grant increase and extension will also provide partial support for an intensive public education campaign taking place between April and June 2007.

title: Alliance for Quality Education: Statewide Education Financing Reform Project
grantee: Public Policy and Education Fund of New York
description: The Alliance for Quality Education: Statewide Education Financing Reform Project was organized in late 1999 to build a coalition of community organizations and other education stakeholders who were interested in working on school finance reform and education improvements in the state of New York, especially for children from economically disadvantaged communities. This renewal grant to the Public Policy and Education Fund of New York supports continued organizing work to empower local residents to help shape the future of education financing throughout the state. In addition to community organizing, the work will include coalition building, a media strategy, training of local leaders, and organizing public forums to educate the public.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will enable Grantmakers for Effective Organizations (GEO) to continue working to build stronger, more effective nonprofits. Activities include providing a forum for foundation professionals to share research and best practices; offering access to tools and other information to improve nonprofit effectiveness; encouraging organizational effectiveness and its value in strengthening nonprofits; and identifying and filling the leadership development needs of the nonprofit community.GEO, established in 1997, is a coalition of grantmakers committed to building strong and effective nonprofit organizations.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to Grantmakers for Effective Organizations, an organization focused on improving nonprofit results by supporting changes in grantmaker practice. Grantmakers for Effective Organizations has increased the understanding of organizational effectiveness and its value in strengthening nonprofits, and has used its Change Agent Project to identify changes that substantially improve nonprofits’ ability to succeed. The grantee will continue to provide a forum for foundation professionals to share research and best practices, offer tools and other information to improve nonprofit effectiveness, and work to identify and address leadership development needs in the nonprofit community.

title: General Purposes
description: Grantmakers for Effective Organizations focuses on improving nonprofit results by creating tools aimed at advancing grantmaker practices. The grantee has improved its membership programs and increased member engagement, created a content-extensive Web site database, and used its due diligence tool to identify due diligence practices that also serve to strengthen the grantmaker-grantee relationship. During the grant period, the grantee will continue to provide a forum for foundation professionals to share research and best practices, offer tools and other information to improve nonprofit effectiveness, and work to identify and address leadership development needs in the nonprofit community.

title: General Purposes
description: Grantmakers for Effective Organizations is an association of more than 380 grantmaking organizations committed to building strong and effective nonprofit organizations. The grantee helps grantmakers improve practices in areas which have been identified by innovators in the field as critical to nonprofit success. It carries out this work through a variety of products and services, including conferences, peer learning opportunities, publications, action learning, an online resource library, newsletters, and networking opportunities. Its objectives are to promote innovation, raise awareness, build knowledge, and support change leading to improved grantmaker effectiveness. Last year, the grantee continued to support grantmakers with multiple peer-to-peer learning opportunities, including two topical conferences, more than a dozen skill-building workshops, and two new publications on the emerging topics of empathy and networks. It will explore the following content areas in 2012 and beyond: capacity building, cofunding, learning for improvement, working with intermediaries, and stakeholder engagement.

title: General Purposes
description: Grantmakers for Effective Organizations is an association of more than 500 grantmaking organizations committed to building strong and effective nonprofit organizations. The grantee helps grantmakers improve practices in areas which have been identified by innovators in the field as critical to nonprofit success. It carries out this work through a variety of products and services, including conferences, peer learning opportunities, publications, an online resource library, newsletters, and networking opportunities. Its objectives are to promote innovation, raise awareness, build knowledge, and support behavior change leading to improved grantmaker effectiveness. Last year, the grantee continued to support grantmakers with multiple peer-to-peer learning opportunities including three conferences, two community-of-practice programs, and five new publications on topics such as networks, nonprofit collaborative capacity, and funding movements. In 2014, it will launch a Change in Philanthropy initiative, a set of approaches aimed at supporting foundation leaders’ efforts to spark fundamental change within their institutions.

title: General Purposes
description: Grantmakers for Effective Organizations is a diverse community of 546 grantmakers representing more than 5,000 individuals that provides grantmakers with resources and connections to build knowledge and improve practice in areas that are most critical to nonprofit success. It does this by organizing conferences and peer-learning programs, producing original publications, and providing networking tools to connect members. Last year, the grantee continued to support grantmakers with multiple peer-to-peer learning activities including two conferences, three senior leader convenings, four member conference calls, four Webinars, and five new publications on topics such as foundation culture, collaboration, and strengthening nonprofit capacity. It also launched its Change Incubator, an 18-month intensive program for a small set of foundation staff. In addition to continuing this work in 2016-2017, the grantee will conduct human-centered design workshops and form an Equity and Effectiveness Advisory Group to develop programming on diversity, equity, and inclusion.

title: 21st Century Community Learning Centers Summer Institute
description: This grant will enable Synergy Enterprises to provide logistical and conference support to the 2006 21st Century Community Learning Centers Summer Institute in San Diego, California.The purpose of the summer institute is to provide workshops to familiarize approximately 2,000 grant recipients with grant administration assistance and successful strategies in improving the content, management and quality of afterschool programs. The annual Summer Institute is one of the training and technical assistance activities that Mott sponsors as part of its partnership with the U.S. Department of Education.

title: 21st Century Community Learning Centers Summer Institute
description: This grant to Synergy Enterprises, Inc., will provide funding for the 2007 Summer Institute that supports the 21st Century Community Learning Centers initiative. The 21st Century Community Learning Centers initiative provides grants to inner-city and rural schools working in close cooperation with community organizations and other education and youth development agencies to provide expanded learning opportunities outside of regular school hours for children in a safe and smart environment. The purpose of this three-day conference is to provide workshops to familiarize grant recipients with grants administration assistance and with successful strategies in implementing reading, mathematics, science, and arts into afterschool programs. The annual conference is one of the training and technical assistance activities the Mott Foundation sponsors as part of its partnership with the U.S. Department of Education.

title: 21st Century Community Learning Centers Summer Institute
description: This grant will provide funding for the 21st Century Community Learning Centers Summer Institute in 2008, a project of Synergy Enterprises, Inc. The 21st Century Community Learning Centers initiative provides grants to inner-city and rural schools working in close cooperation with community organizations and other education and youth development agencies to provide expanded learning opportunities outside of regular school hours for children in a safe and smart environment. The purpose of this conference is to provide workshops to familiarize grant recipients with grants administration assistance and with successful strategies in supporting academic content, using innovative content, using data effectively, and building the capacity of staff. The annual summer institute is one of the training and technical assistance activities the Mott Foundation has agreed to sponsor as part of our partnership with the U.S. Department of Education. This year’s event will commemorate the 10th Anniversary of the Summer Institute.

title: 21st Century Community Learning Centers Summer Institute
description: This grant to Synergy Enterprises, Inc., will provide funding for the 2009 21st Century Community Learning Centers Summer Institute. The 21st Century Community Learning Centers initiative provides grants to innercity and rural schools working in close cooperation with community organizations and other education and youth development agencies to provide afterschool programs outside of regular school hours for children in a safe and smart environment. The purpose of this three-day conference is to provide workshops to familiarize grant recipients with grant administration assistance and successful strategies in implementing high quality afterschool programs. The annual summer institute is held in partnership with the U.S. Department of Education.

title: 21st Century Community Learning Centers Summer Institute
description: This grant to Synergy Enterprises, Inc., will provide funding for the 21st Century Community Learning Centers Summer Institute. The 21st Century Community Learning Centers initiative provides grants to innercity and rural schools working in close cooperation with community organizations and other education and youth development agencies to provide afterschool programs outside regular school hours for children in a safe and smart environment. The purpose of this three-day conference is to provide workshops to familiarize grant recipients with grants administration assistance and with successful strategies in implementing high quality afterschool programs. The annual summer institute is held in partnership with the U.S. Department of Education.

title: 21st Century Community Learning Centers Summer Institute
description: This grant to Synergy Enterprises, Inc., will provide funding for the 21st Century Community Learning Centers 2011 Summer Institute, held in partnership with the U.S. Department of Education. The 21st Century Community Learning Centers initiative supports nearly 2 million children and youth in over 10,000 school-community afterschool programs across the country. The purpose of the annual summer institute is to provide state 21st Century Community Learning Centers administrators with technical assistance and strategies to improve the quality of school-community afterschool programs.

title: 21st Century Community Learning Centers Summer Institute
description: This grant will provide funding for the 21st Century Community Learning Centers 2012 Summer Institute, held in partnership with the U.S. Department of Education. The 21st Century Community Learning Centers initiative supports nearly 2 million children and youth in over 10,000 school-community afterschool programs across the country. The purpose of the annual summer institute is to provide 21st Century Community Learning Centers state administrators with technical assistance and strategies to improve the quality of school-community afterschool programs.

title: 21st Century Community Learning Centers Institute
description: This grant will provide funding to support the convening of the 21st Century Community Learning Centers Institute, held in partnership with Foundations, Inc., and the U.S. Department of Education. The 21st Century Community Learning Centers initiative supports nearly 2 million children and youth in over 10,000 school-community afterschool programs across the country. The purpose of the convening is to provide afterschool and expanded learning programs, specifically 21st Century Community Learning Centers administrators, with technical assistance and strategies to improve the quality of school-community afterschool programs.

title: 21st Century Community Learning Centers Institute
description: This grant will provide funding to support a convening of the 21st Century Community Learning Centers, held in partnership with Foundations, Inc., and the U.S. Department of Education. The 21st Century Community Learning Centers initiative supports nearly 2 million children and youth in nearly 11,000 school-community afterschool programs across the country. The purpose of the convening is to provide afterschool, specifically 21st Century Community Learning Centers administrators, with technical assistance and strategies to continue to enhance the quality of school-community afterschool programs.

title: 21st Century Community Learning Centers Summer Institute
description: This grant will provide funding to support a convening of the 21st Century Community Learning Centers, held in partnership with Synergy Enterprises, Inc., and the U.S. Department of Education. The 21st Century Community Learning Centers initiative supports nearly 2 million children and youth in over 11,000 school-community afterschool programs across the country. The purpose of the annual summer institute is to provide afterschool administrators, specifically the 21st Century Community Learning Centers administrators, with technical assistance and strategies to continue to enhance the quality of school-community afterschool programs.
