description: This grant will provide funding to support a convening of the 21st Century Community Learning Centers, held in partnership with Synergy Enterprises, Inc., and the U.S. Department of Education. The 21st Century Community Learning Centers initiative supports nearly 2 million children and youth in over 11,000 school-community afterschool programs across the country. The purpose of the annual summer institute is to provide afterschool administrators and staff with technical assistance and strategies to continue to enhance the quality of school-community afterschool programs.

title: 21st Century Community Learning Centers Summer Institute
description: This grant will provide funding to support a convening of the 21st Century Community Learning Centers, held in partnership with Synergy Enterprises, Inc., and the U.S. Department of Education. The 21st Century Community Learning Centers initiative supports nearly 2 million children and youth in over 11,000 school-community afterschool programs across the country. The purpose of the annual summer institute is to provide afterschool administrators and staff with technical assistance and strategies to continue to enhance the quality of school-community afterschool programs.

title: Educational Equity Network
description: The Educational Equity Network is a project of Claremont Graduate University that addresses racial disparities in education outcomes. The project is implemented through several sites that have developed an approach to educational disparities by combining antiracism training with work within school systems and communities.Funding will support specialized training for teachers, counselors and administrators; meetings of the equity network for information sharing; adult leadership participation in an educational equity institute; and the preparation and publication of lessons learned from the project.During 2005, accomplishments included meetings of site leaders from the national network of antiracism community building sites; increased support for and communication through a Web site as a means of collecting and disseminating information relevant to the field; and the development of national strategies to address areas of disparity.

title: Roundtable on Comprehensive Community Initiatives: Project on Race and Community Revitalization
description: This grant will provide partial support for the Project on Race and Community Revitalization of the Aspen Institute’s Roundtable on Comprehensive Community Initiatives. This project aims to focus greater attention on racial equity in community building and democratic decisionmaking. It also focuses on developing a critical mass of leaders who are more attuned to race as a structural problem and who will be better able to identify or develop strategies for recognizing and dealing with race issues. Recent work has included further refinement of the curriculum and tools for a Racial Equity and Society Seminar and training of community foundations and other leaders from seven locations around the country. Future support will capitalize on the work with community foundations through peer learning among participants and distillation and dissemination of case studies from key locations.

title: Roundtable on Comprehensive Community Initiatives: Project on Race and Community Revitalization
description: The Aspen Institute works to develop practical leadership through nonpartisan seminars and policy programs designed for leaders in business, government, the media, education, the arts, and the independent sector. This grant will provide partial support for the Project on Race and Community Revitalization of the Roundtable on Comprehensive Community Initiatives, which focuses greater attention on racial equity in community building and democratic decisionmaking. It also focuses on developing leaders who are more attuned to race as a societal issue and will be able to identify or develop strategies for recognizing and dealing with race issues. Recent work has included further refinement of the curriculum and tools for the Seminar on Racial Equity and Society and training of community foundation and other leaders from seven locations around the country. Future support will capitalize on the work with community foundations through peer learning among participants and developing and disseminating case studies.

title: Supporting Emerging Education Organizing
description: This grant will enable the National Training and Information Center (NTIC) to continue working to strengthen grassroots community organizations involved in education reform initiatives. Specific objectives include providing technical assistance to community organizations to create local school funding campaigns that engage corporate, government and community stakeholders; developing local and national leadership teams equipped to win education reform on the issue of school finance; increasing collaboration for education reform among parents, students, schools, churches and advocacy organizations; and building community-corporate partnerships at the local and national levels to work toward solutions to budget shortfalls and develop plans for the future of education funding.Since the mid-1990s, NTIC has been working to train staff and leaders from many community organizations seeking to strengthen community-driven school reform initiatives. Beginning in 2001, the organization added a regranting component to support education organizing initiatives.

title: International Financial Institution Reform and Capacity Building
description: Les Amis de la Terre has been working to promote international financial institution reform since 1995. This grant will enable the organization to focus reform efforts on strengthening the environmental and social safeguard policies of European financial institutions, the French export credit agency (ECA), French private banks and the World Bank. In addition, Les Amis de la Terre will ensure that monitoring and compliance mechanisms are developed for these higher standards; support organizational capacity-building projects; and strengthen the international export credit reform network.Recent efforts have focused on reforming the French ECA and the World Bank; managing the International ECA Reform Network; producing a toolkit for the creation of new local groups in France; and conducting training sessions for volunteers in media relations.

title: International Financial Institution Reform and Capacity Building
description: Les Amis de la Terre has been actively engaged in encouraging the French government to support international financial institution reform since 1995. With this grant, it will focus reform efforts on strengthening the environmental and social safeguard policies of European financial institutions, the French export credit agency, French private banks and insurance companies, and the World Bank. The grantee will ensure monitoring and compliance mechanisms are developed for these higher standards. This grant will also support organizational capacity-building projects.

title: International Financial Institution Reform and Capacity Building
description: Les Amis de la Terre was founded in 1970 and has been actively engaged in encouraging the French government to support international financial institution reform since 1995. Over the last grant period, it was successful in getting changes at French private banks, particularly related to the development of climate policies. With this grant, it will continue to focus on strengthening environmental and social safeguard policies and ensuring that climate policies are in place at European financial institutions, the French export credit agency, French private banks, and the World Bank. This grant will also support organizational capacity building activities.

title: International Financial Institution Reform and Capacity Building
description: Les Amis de la Terre has been actively engaged in encouraging the French government to support international financial institution reform since 1995. As a result of its work, the French government has a stronger stance on the World Bank’s climate and energy policies. As well, French private bank and insurance companies have developed sectoral lending policies related to energy. With this grant, Les Amis de la Terre will focus on World Bank and French private banks’ environmental and social safeguard policies, as well as shifting the lending of these institutions to more renewable and energy efficient projects. This grant will also support organizational capacity building projects.

title: Centre for Civil Society
description: The Centre for Civil Society, based at the University of KwaZulu-Natal, was established to promote the study and analysis of the nonprofit sector in South Africa and the wider African continent. It produces research; offers scholarships to those who want to study civil society; runs workshops and seminars; convenes conferences; and disseminates knowledge and publications on the pressing issues facing the civil society sector. This grant will continue to support the work and programs of the center, particularly as related to understanding the challenges that the sector is presently facing and what needs to be done to build a strong and accountable nonprofit sector that is adequately resourced through private and public funding.

title: Centre for Civil Society
description: The Centre for Civil Society, based at the University of KwaZulu-Natal’s School of Development Studies, was established to promote the study and analysis of the nonprofit sector in South Africa and the wider African continent. Previous funding from the Mott Foundation supported the center to produce research, offer scholarships to those who want to study civil society, run workshops and seminars, convene conferences, and disseminate knowledge and publications on the pressing issues facing the civil society sector. This grant will support the Centre for Civil Society to continue conducting innovative research and to critically engage with civil society. It will build on its experiences in academic teaching, hosting seminars, and publishing and conducting research, and it will maintain community outreach efforts that include providing opportunities for civil society scholarships and access to information, networking, and advocacy.

title: Centre for Civil Society
description: The Centre for Civil Society, based at the University of KwaZulu-Natal, was established to promote the study and analysis of the nonprofit sector in South Africa and the wider African continent. It produces research, offers scholarships to those who want to study civil society, runs workshops and seminars, convenes conferences, and disseminates knowledge and publications on the pressing issues facing the civil society sector. Past support enabled the program to continue to conduct research on topical issues facing civil society in South Africa and on the African continent; support and mentor community activists to improve the living conditions within their communities; collaborate with civil society organizations to seek solutions for various social challenges; and publish books and papers on topics related to political economy, civil society, culture and social movements, among others. This grant will continue to support the grantee to undertake these activities.

title: Centre for Civil Society
description: The University of KwaZulu-Natal is one of the largest universities in South Africa. It was formally established in January 2004, after the merger of the Universities of Natal and Durban-Westville. The Centre for Civil Society, based at the University of KwaZulu-Natal, was established to promote the study and analysis of the nonprofit sector in South Africa and the wider African continent. Past support assisted the grantee to teach subjects related to civil society and social justice philanthropy, support community scholars and social movements on matters related to provision of basic services to poor people, and to conduct research and publish on various topics related to civil society, political economy, and environmental justice. This grant will support the Centre for Civil Society to continue with these activities.

title: Centre for Civil Society
description: The University of KwaZulu-Natal was formally established in January 2004 as a result of a merger of the Universities of Natal and Durban-Westville. The Centre for Civil Society, established at the University of KwaZulu-Natal, promotes the study of civil society in South Africa, generates and shares knowledge, and creates debate and reflection on the nature of civil society in South Africa and the African continent. Past support enabled the centre to support community scholars to solve problems faced by their communities, teach subjects related to civil society on the development studies Masters program, conduct studies on social movements and protests relating to the delivery of basic services, and conduct research on various topics related to political economy; climate and environmental justice; and civil society. This grant will support the Centre for Civil Society to continue these activities.

title: Centre for Civil Society
description: The University of KwaZulu-Natal was formally established in 2004 as a result of a merger between the Universities of Durban Westville and Natal in South Africa. The Centre for Civil Society was established at the University of KwaZulu-Natal and promotes the study of South African civil society as a legitimate area of scholarly activity. It generates and shares knowledge on topical issues, builds partnerships with civil society, and facilitates debate and reflection on the nature of civil society. Past support enabled the grantee to host events to discuss civil society challenges in the KwaZulu-Natal province. Additionally, the grantee supported community scholars to address challenges in their communities; generate academic knowledge; conduct research on social, environmental, and economic justice; and teach courses in the development studies Master’s program. This grant will provide continued support to facilitate the community scholars program, conduct research on the various forms of participation at the local level, and partner with other civil society organizations in the KwaZulu-Natal province to promote social cohesion.

title: Centre for Civil Society
description: The University of KwaZulu-Natal was formally established in 2004, as a result of a merger between the Universities of Durban Westville and Natal in South Africa. The Centre for Civil Society, established at the University of KwaZulu-Natal, promotes the study of South African civil society as a legitimate area of scholarly activity. It generates and shares knowledge on topical issues related to civil society, builds partnerships between academia and civil society, and facilitates debate and reflection on the nature of civil society. Past support enabled the grantee to host events to discuss civil society challenges in the KwaZulu-Natal province. Additionally, the grantee supported community scholars to encourage interaction between academia and practice; generated academic knowledge on civil society; conducted research on social, environmental, and economic justice; and taught courses in the development studies Master’s program. This grant will enable the grantee to continue implementing these activities.

title: Federal and State Asset Policy Project
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This renewal grant enables the Corporation for Enterprise Development to continue developing and promoting state and federal asset-building policies for lower-income Americans. To realize this goal, the corporation will conduct policy research, educate policymakers, and engage a broad constituency of practitioners and other allies in asset-building advocacy. The corporation has played a key role in advancing asset-building strategies, first by promoting Individual Development Accounts and, more recently, Children’s Savings Accounts and other policies to encourage and induce savings in low- and moderate-income households. The Corporation for Enterprise Development, an economic development intermediary, is headquartered in Washington, D.C., and is a long-time grantee of the Mott Foundation.

title: Federal and State Asset Policy Project
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant enables the Corporation for Enterprise Development to develop and promote state and federal asset-building policies for low-income Americans. Given bipartisan interest in savings strategies, a key objective of this project is to translate legislative interest and support into federal and state policies that create savings incentives and opportunities at scale over the long term. To realize this goal, the grantee will engage in policy development, policymaker education, coalition building, strategic communications, research, and technical assistance and training efforts. The Corporation for Enterprise Development, an economic development intermediary, is a key national leader in the asset-building movement and a longtime grantee of the Mott Foundation on asset building and microenterprise issues.

title: Federal and State Asset Policy Project
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant enables the Corporation for Enterprise Development to develop and promote state and federal asset building policies for lower-income Americans. Given the tremendous bipartisan support for Individual Development Accounts, primary importance will be placed on translating that support into a federal policy capable of financing and delivering these accounts at scale over the long term. To realize this goal, the grantee will engage in a series of complementary activities, including policy development, policymaker education, coalition building, strategic communications, research, and technical assistance and training. An Individual Development Account is a matched savings account for lower-income Americans that can be used for high return investments such as buying a first home, attending college, or starting a small business. Located in Washington, DC, the Corporation for Enterprise Development, an economic development intermediary, is a key national leader in the asset building movement.

title: Federal and State Asset Policy Project
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant enables the Corporation for Enterprise Development to develop and advance policy and programmatic solutions that are grounded in the ideas, research, and practices of the asset-building field. To realize this goal, the grantee will engage in a series of complementary activities, including policy development and policymaker education, coalition building, and strategic communications. The Corporation for Enterprise Development, an economic development think tank, is a key intermediary in the asset-building field and a longtime grantee of the Mott Foundation on both microenterprise and asset-building issues.

title: Federal and State Asset Policy Project
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This renewal grant will enable the Corporation for Enterprise Development to continue its efforts to ensure that by 2025 every child in the United States has a children’s savings account. To achieve its vision, the grantee organizes its efforts into four main categories: community practice, applied research, public policy, and stakeholder engagement. Mott funding will support the grantee’s work at the state and regional levels. Located in Washington, D.C., the grantee is a national research, practice, and policy intermediary that works to create economic opportunities that alleviate poverty.

title: Advancing the Children's Savings Account Field
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant will support the Corporation for Enterprise Development’s efforts to ensure that by 2025 every child in the United States has a children’s savings account. To achieve its vision, the grantee organizes its efforts into four main categories: community practices, applied research, public policy, and stakeholder engagement. Mott funding will support the grantee’s community practice and stakeholder engagement efforts at the national, state, and local levels. Located in Washington, D.C., the Corporation for Enterprise Development is a national research, practice, and policy intermediary whose mission is to create economic opportunities that alleviate poverty.

title: Advancing the Children's Savings Account Field
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant will continue support for Prosperity Now’s efforts to ensure that every child in America has a children’s savings account by 2025. To achieve this mission, Prosperity Now will: 1) continue to build the capacity of individual organizations delivering children’s savings accounts; 2) expand on the larger movement of knowledge sharing and innovation strategy in the children’s savings account field; and 3) leverage public policy to increase the scale of children’s savings accounts. Mott funding will support Prosperity Now’s technical assistance, research, networking, and stakeholder engagement efforts at the national, state, and local levels. Prosperity Now is a national research, practice, and policy intermediary whose mission is to ensure everyone in our country has a clear path to financial stability, wealth, and prosperity.

title: Increasing Citizen Participation in Community Life Through Media
description: The project goal is to increase citizen participation in community life by strengthening local town councils and fostering positive communication between the public and local authorities on issues of community concern.This grant will enable the Center for Civic Cooperation to educate community residents and authorities through public meetings and debates, direct contact, and the production of a series of call-in programs on local radio stations. The project will target local communities in 10 municipalities in western Bosnia and Herzegovina.Since 2002, there have been more than 1,000 participants in the center’s activities. Topics for discussion on the radio programs were selected in consultation with local journalists, local residents, local representatives and other non-governmental organizations.

title: Increasing Citizen Participation in Community Life Through Media
description: The overall project goal of the Center for Civic Cooperation is to promote vibrant local democracy by increasing people’s participation in local decisionmaking in two districts of western Bosnia-Herzegovina. Activities during the next two years will foster communication between citizens and local officials, raise awareness about issues of local concern, and strengthen local town councils as mechanisms for active public participation in decisionmaking processes. During the past two years, the grantee has produced radio programs where local representatives are on hand to discuss issues with journalists and answer questions from people who call the program, organized public debates on topics raised on the radio programs, and strengthened 20 local town councils in ten municipalities. The grantee is based in Livno, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and has been working on local democracy development since 1996.

title: Increasing Citizen Participation in Community Life Through Media
description: The overall project goal is to promote vibrant local democracy by increasing people’s participation in local decisionmaking in two districts of western Bosnia-Herzegovina. During the next two years, the Center for Civic Cooperation will foster communication between citizens and local officials, raise awareness about issues of local concern, and strengthen local town councils as mechanisms for active public participation in decisionmaking processes. As a result of project activities during the past two years, the number of active town councils increased significantly. The center provided financial and technical support to 18 town councils and trained more than 120 council members. The grantee is based in Livno, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and has been working on local democracy development since 1996.

title: Increasing Citizen Participation in Community Life Through Media
description: The overall project goal is to promote vibrant local democracy by increasing people’s participation in local decisionmaking in two districts of western Bosnia-Herzegovina. During the next two years, the Center for Civic Cooperation will foster communication between citizens and local officials, raise awareness about issues of local concern, and strengthen local town councils as mechanisms for active public participation in decisionmaking processes. A key component of the project will be to strengthen the existing 141 town councils and help establish 11 additional councils. As a result of project activities, during the past two years, the number of active town councils increased significantly as well as the role of these councils in promoting local-level civic engagement in decisionmaking. The grantee provided financial and technical support to town councils and raised public awareness about the town councils through radio call-in programs and printed materials. The grantee is based in Livno, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and has been working on local democracy development since 1996.

title: Increasing Citizen Participation in Community Life Through Media
description: The overall project goal is to promote vibrant local democracy by increasing people’s participation in local decisionmaking in Bosnia-Herzegovina. During the next two years, the Center for Civic Cooperation will strengthen local town councils as mechanisms for active public participation in decisionmaking processes in 19 municipalities, including nine in which the grantee has not yet worked, in southwestern Bosnia-Herzegovina. Through training, networking, documentation and sharing of best practices, outreach through radio and other media, publishing, and active monitoring, the targeted local town councils will foster communication between citizens and local officials and directly impact issues of local concern. A key component of the project will be to strengthen the existing 157 town councils and help to establish and strengthen 154 additional councils. During the past two years, the number of active town councils increased significantly as has the role of these councils in promoting local-level civic engagement in decisionmaking. The grantee provided financial and technical support to town councils and raised public awareness about the town councils through radio call-in programs and printed materials. The grantee is based in Livno, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and has been working on local democracy development since 1996.

title: Civil Society Resource Centre Program
description: This grant will support the development of the nonprofit sector in southern Croatia by developing the human and organizational capacities of volunteer-based nonprofit organizations. During the next two years, the association will work to increase the professionalism of leaders of non-governmental organizations, encourage cross-sector partnerships, and promote volunteerism and greater citizen participation in the sector and community life. Over the past two years, the association has increased outreach to organizations and communities in the counties surrounding the city of Split, where the association is based, and has worked with the local governments in three cities to establish cross-sector cooperation. The Association “Mi” has encouraged volunteerism and supported the nonprofit sector locally and nationally through various activities since its founding in 1996.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to support the development of civil society and the nonprofit sector in southern Croatia by developing the human and organizational capacities of volunteer-based nonprofit organizations. Building on this experience, the association will offer a range of services to the nonprofit sector in four counties, promote volunteerism, strengthen cross-sector cooperation at community levels, and encourage civic engagement and local resource mobilization to meet community needs. During the last two years, Association “Mi” provided basic training and technical assistance to hundreds of nonprofits on organizational development, project implementation, volunteerism, and quality assurance monitoring; assisted nonprofits and local governments to develop cross-sector charters of cooperation; and supported the establishment of municipal-level civil society forums. Based in Split, the Association “Mi” has supported the nonprofit sector through various activities since its founding in 1996.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to support the development of civil society and the nonprofit sector in southern Croatia by developing the human and organizational capacities of nonprofit organizations and promoting volunteerism. Building on this experience, the Association “Mi” will offer a range of services to the nonprofit sector in four counties, promote volunteerism, strengthen cross-sector cooperation at community levels, and encourage civic engagement and local resource mobilization to meet community needs. During the last two years, the grantee provided basic training and technical assistance to hundreds of nonprofits on organizational development, project implementation, volunteerism, and quality assurance monitoring; managed a regional forum for nonprofits; and helped establish an elderly care center and a local foundation. Based in Split, the Association “Mi” has supported the nonprofit sector through various activities since its founding in 1996.

title: General Purposes
description: The Workshop for Civic Initiatives Foundation assists civic leaders, citizen groups and non-governmental organizations to effectively address the needs of their communities and constituencies. This grant increase will enable the foundation to provide training and small grant support to various local stakeholders for grassroots activities; build the capacity of grassroots organizations to raise local resources; and develop the professional skills of trainers. In addition, the foundation will promote local philanthropy and corporate social responsibility.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to support the development of local communities and grassroots organizations in Bulgaria. Workshop for Civic Initiatives Foundation is assisting civic leaders, citizen groups, and nongovernmental organizations to effectively address the needs of their communities and constituencies. The foundation also is working actively with the business community and public authorities on the local level to stimulate partnerships and the sharing of resources. During the grant period, the foundation will provide tailored training and small-grant support to various local stakeholders for grassroots activities, build the capacity of grassroots organizations to raise local resources, and promote local philanthropy and corporate social responsibility. Since its establishment in 2001, the foundation has raised and distributed more than $1 million in grants; provided training to 250 grassroots nonprofit organizations; and experimented successfully with innovative resource mobilization strategies and tools, including Web-based giving and corporate volunteering.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to support the development of local communities and grassroots organizations in Bulgaria. The Workshop for Civic Initiatives Foundation is assisting civic leaders, citizen groups, and nongovernmental organizations to effectively address the needs of their communities and constituencies. The grantee is also working actively with the business community and public authorities on the local level to stimulate partnerships and the sharing of resources. During the grant period, the grantee will provide tailored training and small-grant support to various local stakeholders for grassroots activities, build the capacity of grassroots organizations to raise local resources, and promote local philanthropy and corporate social responsibility. In addition, the grantee will support the development of community foundations in Bulgaria. In the past three years, the grantee provided more than $700,000 in small grants to over 300 grassroots organizations, distributed software donations of $300,000 in market value to 70 large nonprofits, and facilitated the establishment of three new community foundations.

title: General Purposes
description: The mission of the Workshop for Civic Initiatives Foundation is to support the development of local communities and grassroots organizations in Bulgaria. During the grand period, the grantee will provide tailored training and small grant support to various local stakeholders for grassroots activities, build the capacity of grassroots organizations to raise local resources, and promote local philanthropy and corporate social responsibility. In addition, the grantee will provide software products and expert advice in new technologies to local and national nonprofits. The grantee will also strengthen its own organizational capacity and increase its permanent assets. During the past grant period, the grantee provided $1.1 million in grants to 246 projects in 198 different locations in Bulgaria; provided training to 569 organizations; donated software products with a market value of over $300,000 to 218 nonprofit organizations; and raised $208,000 for its endowment, which was matched by the Mott Foundation. The grantee is based in Sofia, Bulgaria.

title: General Purposes
description: The mission of the Workshop for Civic Initiatives Foundation is to support the development of local communities and grassroots organizations in Bulgaria. During the grand period, the grantee will provide tailored training and small grant support to various local stakeholders for grassroots activities; build the capacity of grassroots organizations to raise local resources; and promote local philanthropy and corporate social responsibility. In addition, the grantee will provide software products and expert advice in new technologies to local and national nonprofits. The grantee will also strengthen its own organizational capacity and increase its permanent assets. During the past grant period, the grantee provided $1.3 million in grants to 435 projects in over 50 different locations in Bulgaria, developed individual and corporate philanthropy, and strengthened its organizational capacity and financial sustainability. The grantee is based in Sofia, Bulgaria.

title: General Purposes
description: Environment-People-Law (EPL) is a leading Western Ukrainian non-governmental organization promoting the environmental rights of citizens through advocacy, education, information and legal assistance.Multiyear funding will enable EPL to organize its work according to four major program areas: advocacy, legal clinic, European integration, and outreach. In addition, EPL will further develop staff capacity and expand its local base of support.Significant accomplishments over the past five years include operating a highly successful environmental law clinic program through which more than 70 law students received training in public interest law and worked on more than 200 environmental cases; working to protect the Danube Delta, for which the organization’s senior lawyer won the prestigious Goldman Prize in 2006; and actively participating in the Environmental Law Alliance Worldwide network, including hosting its 2004 annual meeting.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to protect and promote the environmental rights of citizens in Ukraine. Over the next two years, the grantee will work to expand access to environmental information, increase participation in environmental decisionmaking, and promote environmental justice. It will organize its work across five major program areas: advocacy, legal education, research and preventive monitoring, outreach, and international cooperation. During 2006-2009, the grantee successfully challenged the Ukrainian government for failing to undertake necessary impact assessments in the proposed development of the Danube-Black Sea canal. It also successfully advocated for the exclusion of impact assessment reports from the register of confidential state documents. Over 1,000 consultations on environmental rights were provided, and over 30 students participated in the environmental law clinic. Founded in 1994, Environment-People-Law is a leading, western Ukrainian, nongovernmental organization whose mission is to promote the environmental rights of citizens through advocacy, education, information, and legal assistance.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to ensure public participation and engagement in decisions and processes affecting the environmental rights of citizens in Ukraine. Over the next two years, the grantee will work to expand access to environmental information, increase participation in environmental decisionmaking, and promote environmental justice. It will organize its work across three major program areas: advocacy, information and analysis, and international cooperation. In the period 2009-2011, the grantee successfully pushed for greater information transparency within the Ukrainian Ministry of Environment and Natural Resources. Its analyses also contributed to the Ukrainian government issuing a plan for meeting its obligations under the Aarhus Convention. A co-founder of the Danube Civil Society Forum, it was the only Ukrainian entity to comment on the European Union Draft Strategy for the Danube Region. Founded in 1994, Environment-People-Law is a leading Ukrainian nongovernmental organization whose mission is to promote the environmental rights of citizens through advocacy, education, information, and legal assistance.

title: General Purposes
description: Focus: HOPE has served thousands of low-income Detroiters since the civil rights organization was founded in 1968. More than 9,000 people, mostly young African- Americans, have graduated from Focus: HOPE’s manufacturing and technology training programs, giving them an opportunity to climb the ladder of economic success. In addition, Focus: HOPE also feeds approximately 43,000 families every month as it pursues the dual mission of alleviating poverty and advancing civil rights.Funding will support the organization’s efforts to maintain retention levels so that more students complete the Machinist Training Institute program and receive a bachelor’s or associate’s degree from the Center for Advanced Technologies; continue to deliver the food distribution program for those in need; complete strategic reviews and plans for future sustainability of programs; and improve marketing efforts.

title: General Purposes
description: Focus: HOPE’s manufacturing and information technology training programs have enabled over 9,200 graduates to climb the ladder of economic success. These individuals represent a vast, untapped labor pool, especially those who have been historically denied access to training opportunities. Focus: HOPE breaks down barriers to success for these individuals with tools of empowerment including education, training, and supportive services. Focus: HOPE has recently faced the challenge of a declining manufacturing economy in southeast Michigan, as well as continuing declines in enrollment partially caused by reductions in government tuition assistance. This renewal grant will help leverage the investments by other foundations, businesses, and public-sector supporters to sustain the organization.

title: General Purposes
description: Focus: HOPE, celebrating its 40th anniversary in 2009, continues to provide a comprehensive array of workforce training, education, social supports, childcare, and food distribution services in Detroit. As with most organizations in Michigan, the grantee is facing the challenges of a declining manufacturing economy in southeast Michigan. This renewal grant will help to leverage the investments by other foundations, businesses, and public-sector supporters to sustain the organization.

title: General Purposes
description: Focus: HOPE continues to provide a comprehensive array of workforce training, education, social supports, childcare, and food distribution services in Detroit. As with most organizations in Michigan, Focus: HOPE is facing the challenges of a declining manufacturing economy in southeast Michigan. This renewal grant will help to leverage the investments by other foundations, businesses, and public-sector supporters to sustain the organization.

title: General Purposes
description: The Foundation has been a longtime and consistent supporter of Focus: HOPE since making an initial grant in 1981. The grantee’s manufacturing and information technology training programs have enabled over 9,200 graduates to climb the ladder of economic success. Continued general purpose support is critical to help the organization create training that proactively addresses the changing workforce needs of employers as Detroit begins to show signs of recovery. This grant will also help the grantee implement a compressive plan to tackle the toughest problems confronting the communities in the immediate area surrounding its Detroit campus.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purpose support to Focus: HOPE to continue to deliver an array of comprehensive workforce training, education, social supports, childcare, and food distribution services to low-income residents in Detroit. For over four decades, the grantee has set out to impact the lives of hundreds of thousands of individuals across southeast Michigan through education and training, meeting basic needs, neighborhood development, and other efforts. Continued general purpose support is critical to help the organization sustain its programming in both a challenging fiscal climate and shifting labor market. This renewal grant will help the grantee implement a comprehensive plan to address the issues confronting the neighborhoods in the immediate area surrounding its campus, as well as leverage investments by other foundations, businesses, and public-sector supporters to sustain the organization.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purpose support to Focus: HOPE to deliver an array of comprehensive workforce training, adult education, social supports, childcare, and food distribution services to low-income residents in Detroit. Since 1981, Focus: HOPE has been one of the country’s most effective antipoverty and civil rights organizations whose sole mission has been to help individuals acquire the skills necessary to gain and maintain successful employment, career advancement, and access to the economic mainstream. This renewal grant will help the grantee implement a comprehensive plan to address the issues confronting the neighborhoods in the immediate area surrounding its campus, as well as leverage investments by other foundations, businesses, and public sector supporters to sustain its overall core activities.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purpose funding to Focus: HOPE to deliver an array of comprehensive workforce training, adult education, social supports, childcare, and food distribution services to low-income residents in Detroit. For 45 years, Focus: HOPE has been one of the country’s most effective antipoverty and civil rights organizations. Its unique mission is to help individuals acquire the skills necessary to gain and maintain successful employment, career advancement, and access to the economic mainstream. This renewal grant will help the grantee implement a comprehensive plan to address the issues confronting the neighborhoods in the immediate area surrounding its campus, as well as leverage support from other foundations, businesses, and public-sector supporters to sustain its core activities.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purpose support to Focus: HOPE to continue to deliver its comprehensive workforce training, education, social supports, childcare, and food distribution services to low-income residents in Detroit. For nearly five decades, Focus: HOPE has been a national leader in innovative and sustaining solutions to positively impact the lives of hundreds of thousands of individuals across southeast Michigan through its unique blend of education and training, basic needs, neighborhood development, and local economic development efforts. Continued general purpose support is critical to help the grantee sustain its programming during Detroit’s socioeconomic rebirth and the dynamic shifts in the regional labor market, especially for low-income youth. This renewal grant continues support for Focus: HOPE’s plan to address the issues confronting the neighborhoods in the immediate area surrounding its campus, while leveraging support from other sources including foundations, businesses, and public-sector partners to sustain the grantee’s efforts to serve the community.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide renewal general purpose support to Focus: HOPE, an antipoverty and civil rights organization serving low-income residents of Detroit’s Oakman Boulevard neighborhood. Co-founded in 1968 by Father William Cunningham and Eleanor Josaitis, Focus: HOPE’s mission is to provide intelligent and practical solutions to overcome racism, poverty, and injustice. Mott funding will help support the grantee’s three core lines of work: the supplemental food program, workforce development training, and comprehensive neighborhood and educational revitalization.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will renew general purpose support to Focus: HOPE, an antipoverty and civil rights organization serving low-income residents of Detroit’s Oakman Boulevard neighborhood. Co-founded in 1968 by Father William Cunningham and Eleanor Josaitis, Focus: HOPE’s mission is to provide intelligent and practical solutions to overcome racism, poverty, and injustice. Mott funding will help support the grantee’s three core lines of work: the supplemental food program, workforce development training, and comprehensive neighborhood and educational revitalization.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will renew general purpose support to Focus: HOPE, an antipoverty and civil rights organization serving low-income residents of Detroit’s Oakman Boulevard neighborhood. Mott funding will help support the grantee’s continued effort to transition its three main lines of work—supplemental food, workforce development training, and comprehensive neighborhood and educational revitalization—into a relevant and sustainable business model.

title: Study on Education Organizing and Academic Improvement
description: The American Institute for Social Justice is working with the Association of Community Organizations for Reform Now, commonly known by the acronym ACORN, in Chicago to organize parents, students, and community members to improve the failing schools by focusing on two goals: improving teacher quality and retention and creating small schools. This Chicago-based project is one of eight sites in the Foundation’s study to explore the contribution of community organizing to improving student achievement.

title: Afterschool and Community Learning Network
description: This grant will support the College of Charleston Foundation in continued development of the Afterschool and Community Learning Network. The Afterschool and Community Learning Network will continue to serve and complement existing groups working in support of afterschool programs by raising and exploring emerging policy issues and future opportunities for afterschool, such as increasing family connections to student learning and introducing afterschool into discussions regarding adequate and equitable education. Activities include providing technical assistance and advice to statewide afterschool networks, education groups, and youth development-based organizations.

title: Afterschool and Community Learning Network
description: This grant increase will support the College of Charleston Foundation in developing a comprehensive publication detailing the services, impact, and successes of the 21st Century Community Learning Centers initiative. Building upon the initiative’s growth over the past ten years, this publication will synthesize research, student data, case studies, and interviews about the 21st Century Community Learning Centers initiative in order to educate stakeholders and inform future education and afterschool initiatives.

title: Afterschool and Community Learning Network
description: This grant will support the College of Charleston Foundation in continued development of the Afterschool and Community Learning Network. The network serves and complements existing groups working in support of afterschool programs by raising and exploring emerging policy issues and future opportunities for afterschool, such as increasing family connections to student learning and introducing afterschool into discussions regarding adequate and equitable education. The grantee will provide technical assistance and advice to statewide afterschool networks, education groups, and youth development-based organizations.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued support to a community philanthropy and rights defense organization in southern Ukraine. The Kherson Regional Charity and Health Foundation helps the poor and socially excluded through direct material aid and legal assistance on the protection of their rights. Charitable programs include providing surgical equipment and training for a local tuberculosis hospital and supporting talented children from low-income families. Through its network of public consulting centers, the grantee provides informational, social and legal assistance to approximately 5,000 individuals annually; trains civic activists in advocacy skills; and conducts advocacy campaigns on pressing social issues. Besides working locally, the grantee has established and will continue to develop a nationwide network of 77 advocacy organizations in 26 Ukrainian regions. The Kherson Regional Charity and Health Foundation also will continue to develop its philanthropic programs within the Kherson region; provide information, training, and methodological support to lawyers and consultants on human rights in eight eastern and southern Ukrainian regions; and invest in the professional development of its staff.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to promote both citizen access to information and participation in democratic processes in Ukraine. Over the next three years, the grantee will conduct a series of polls and media roundtables, publish analytical reports, participate in voter education and issue-awareness campaigns and coalitions, conduct exit polls for national elections, support a network of Ukrainian think tanks, and promote Ukraine’s Euro-Atlantic integration. The grantee’s exit polls during the Orange Revolution in 2004 were critical to pushing for free and fair elections, and the grantee continues to shape debate on Ukraine’s European orientation. Established in 1992, Democratic Initiatives Charitable Foundation is a leading public policy institution in Ukraine specializing in gathering and analyzing independent sociological data and ensuring that it reaches policymakers, the media, and the wider public.

title: Global Philanthropy Forum: Annual Conference
grantee: World Affairs Council of Northern California
description: The annual conference of the Global Philanthropy Forum is designed to build a learning community of donors committed to international causes. Since the inaugural conference in 2002, more than 380 people annually have participated in the event. This grant will enable the World Affairs Council of Northern California to explore the role of aid, trade, debt relief and private-sector enterprise in international development using a case-study approach. The conference, which is usually held on the Stanford University campus, will be held in Washington, D.C. in 2006 to expose new philanthropists to social entrepreneurs, nonprofit leaders and think tank scholars who are advancing policy goals through research, direct action and public engagement.The council is a nonprofit, nonpartisan educational organization devoted to engaging the public in a discussion of the transnational issues of tomorrow.

title: Global Philanthropy Forum
grantee: World Affairs Council of Northern California
description: The Global Philanthropy Forum is a project of the World Affairs Council of Northern California. The forum’s mission is to build a learning community of donors and social investors committed to international causes and to inform, enable, and enhance the strategic nature of their giving. At present, the forum is comprised of a network of over 600 donors. Its feature activity is an annual conference, which attracts more than 400 participants. In a recent survey, more than one-third of conference attendees reported increasing international giving as a direct result of their participation. Other forum services include on-site and conference call programs, a summer seminar, online and written resources, and an ongoing service of donor-recipient matchmaking and strategic advice. In 2007-08, the forum intends to develop and begin implementing a strategic plan which will allow it to devise and move to a sustainable financial model.

title: Global Philanthropy Forum
grantee: World Affairs Council of Northern California
description: The Global Philanthropy Forum is a project of the World Affairs Council of Northern California. The forum’s mission is to build a learning community of donors and social investors committed to international causes and to inform, enable, and enhance the strategic nature of their giving. At present, the forum is comprised of a network of over 750 donors and 60 members. Its feature activity is an annual conference, which last year attracted more than 500 participants and featured high profile speakers such as Desmond Tutu, Mary Robinson, and Richard Branson. Other forum services include on-site and conference call programs, a summer seminar, online resources, and an ongoing service of donor-recipient matchmaking and strategic advice. In 2009, the forum will continue its services, seek to build and refresh a lasting learning community, and offer its members entry into a wide variety of opportunities provided by partners such as the Aspen Institute.

title: Global Philanthropy Forum
grantee: World Affairs Council of Northern California
description: The Global Philanthropy Forum is a project of the World Affairs Council of Northern California. The forum’s mission is to provide best-in-class learning opportunities to donors and foundations committed to making a demonstrable difference on global issues. At present, the forum is comprised of a network of over 750 donors and 43 members. Its feature activity is an annual conference, which last year attracted 434 participants and featured high profile speakers. Other forum services include on-site and conference call programs, a summer seminar, online resources, and an ongoing service of donor-recipient matchmaking and strategic advice. In 2010, the forum will continue its services, seek to build and refresh a lasting learning community, and offer its members entry into a wide variety of opportunities provided by partners such as the Aspen Institute. The World Affairs Council of Northern California is a nonprofit, nonpartisan educational organization devoted to engaging the public in a discussion of the transnational issues of tomorrow.

At present, the forum is comprised of a network of over 750 donors. Its main activity is an annual conference, which last year attracted 473 participants. Other services in 2010 included learning events in the San Francisco Bay Area, a donor trip to Liberia, online resources, and donor-recipient matchmaking. In 2011, the forum will host an annual conference and provide other learning and partnering opportunities to its constituency. The World Affairs Council of Northern California is a nonprofit, nonpartisan educational organization devoted to engaging the public in a discussion of the transnational issues of tomorrow.
