grantee: World Affairs Council of Northern California
description: The Global Philanthropy Forum is a project of the World Affairs Council of Northern California. The forum’s mission is to build a community of donors and social investors committed to international causes and to inform, enable, and enhance the strategic nature of their work. At present, the forum consists of a network of over 750 donors of which 61 are members. Its main activity is an annual conference which attracted 472 participants last year. Other forum services in 2011 included learning events in the San Francisco Bay Area, online resources, and donor-recipient matching. In 2012 and 2013, the forum will host annual conferences in Washington, D.C., and the Bay Area, provide other learning and partnering opportunities to donors, and expand its constituency. The World Affairs Council of Northern California is a nonprofit, nonpartisan educational organization devoted to engaging the public in a discussion of the transnational issues of tomorrow.

title: Global Philanthropy Forum
grantee: World Affairs Council of Northern California
description: The Global Philanthropy Forum is a project of the World Affairs Council of Northern California. The project’s mission is to build a community of donors and social investors committed to international causes and to inform, enable, and enhance the strategic nature of their work. Forum services include an annual conference, learning events in the San Francisco Bay Area, online resources, and donor-recipient matchmaking. Over the past several years, the grantee has established partnerships and helped organize gatherings of philanthropists in Brazil, Columbia, and Singapore. In 2014-2015, the grantee will host annual conferences in the Bay Area and in Washington, D.C., and provide other learning and partnering opportunities. It will launch the first conference of the Africa Philanthropy Forum in 2014 in Addis Ababa. The World Affairs Council of Northern California is a nonprofit, nonpartisan educational organization devoted to engaging the public in a discussion of the transnational issues of tomorrow.

title: Global Philanthropy Forum
grantee: World Affairs Council of Northern California
description: The Global Philanthropy Forum is a project of the World Affairs Council of Northern California. The forum’s mission is to build a community of donors and social investors committed to international causes and to inform, enable, and enhance the strategic nature of their work. Forum services include an annual conference, learning events in the San Francisco Bay Area, online resources, and connecting donors with recipients. Over the past several years, the forum has established partnerships and helped organize gatherings of philanthropists in Brazil and Africa. In 2016-2017, the forum will host annual conferences in the Bay Area and provide other learning and partnering opportunities. It will co-organize annual conferences of the Africa and Brazil Philanthropy Fora. The World Affairs Council of Northern California is a nonprofit, nonpartisan educational organization devoted to engaging the public in a discussion of the transnational issues of tomorrow.

title: Global Philanthropy Forum
grantee: World Affairs Council of Northern California
description: Founded in 2001, the Global Philanthropy Forum is a project of the World Affairs Council of Northern California. The project aims to build, sustain, and continuously revitalize a learning community of private donors and social investors committed to international causes. Through conferences, tailored programs, and individual contacts, the project connects donors to one another and to foundation executives, policymakers, issue experts, leaders of civil society organizations, and social entrepreneurs. Over the past several years, the project has established partnerships and helped organize gatherings of philanthropists in Brazil and Africa. In 2018, the grantee will host annual conferences in the Bay Area and in London. The project will continue to provide other learning and partnering opportunities, including its affiliate relationships with the Brazilian and African Philanthropy Forums. The World Affairs Council of Northern California is a nonprofit, nonpartisan educational organization devoted to engaging the public in a discussion of the transnational issues of tomorrow.

title: General Purposes
description: Creating Effective Grassroots Alternatives provides capacity-building support to local initiatives working for community change in Bulgaria. It focuses on marginalized and ethnically diverse communities, particularly the Roma, and the capacity and ability of these communities to access local, national and European development resources.This grant will support efforts to build the capacity of community groups to mobilize local resources, promote community leadership and engage in income-generation projects; encourage networking among Roma and non-Roma groups working to access development resources and promote youth leadership; and raise awareness about the importance of inclusive public participation in decisionmaking at the community level. Recent accomplishments included building the capacity of more than 90 Roma groups involved in local and national activities; launching access-to-education programs in four localities in Bulgaria that benefited more than 46,000 Roma children; piloting income-generating programs for six Roma communities in rural areas; publishing case studies, documentaries and research papers to increase public awareness about Roma issues; and sharing experiences as a member of both the Central and Eastern European (CEE) Citizens Network and the Community Development in CEE Network.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to increase public participation in local decisionmaking and community development in Bulgaria. Creating Effective Grassroots Alternatives, a Bulgarian, nongovernmental organization, will provide capacity building support to local community initiatives working for community change through self-organization and dialogue with local government. In addition, the grantee will strengthen its organizational capacity and financial sustainability. Established in 1995, the grantee has been focusing on marginalized and ethnically diverse communities, particularly the Roma, and the capacity and ability of these communities to access local, national, and European development resources. The grantee’s past achievements include supporting the development of over 50 community, nonprofit organizations in ethnically mixed communities in Bulgaria, facilitating networking and coalition building among organizations working with Roma, and providing input in policy development processes concerning Roma.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to increase public participation and inclusion of minorities in community development in Bulgaria. To this end, Creating Effective Grassroots Alternatives, a Bulgarian nongovernmental organization, will provide capacity building support to local community initiatives working for community change through self-organization and dialogue with local government. More specifically, the grantee will focus on improving public attitudes toward the Roma and strengthening educational achievements of Roma children. Established in 1995, the grantee has been focusing on marginalized and ethnically diverse communities, particularly the Roma, and the capacity and ability of these communities to access local, national, and European development resources. The grantee’s past achievements include supporting the development of over 50 community nonprofit organizations in ethnically mixed communities in Bulgaria, facilitating networking and coalition building among organizations working with Roma, and providing input on policy development processes concerning Roma.

title: Acquisition of Lake Michigan Coastal Preserve
description: The Grand Traverse Regional Land Conservancy (GTRLC), with support from Mott and other public and private sources, has purchased approximately 6,000 acres, including two miles of shoreline on Lake Michigan in Michigan’s Benzie and Manistee counties.This property, which includes sand dunes up to 330 feet in height, provides important habitat for rare and threatened plant species, migratory birds and butterflies, bald eagles, and a variety of mammal species. It is adjacent to several other protected shoreline parcels. Approximately 1,650 acres of the protected property will be managed as a nature preserve, with public access allowed.GTRLC, established in 1991, serves a five-county region in northwestern, lower Michigan. It mission is to protect significant natural, scenic and farm lands.

title: Acquisition of Lake Michigan Coastal Preserve
description: With Mott and other private and public support, the Grand Traverse Regional Land Conservancy purchased approximately 6,000 acres, including two miles of Lake Michigan shoreline, in Michigan’s Benzie and Manistee counties. This ecologically outstanding property, which includes sand dunes up to 330 feet in height, provides important habitat for rare and threatened plant species, migratory birds and butterflies, bald eagles, and a variety of mammal species. Importantly, it is adjacent to several other protected shoreline parcels. Approximately 1,650 acres of the property will be managed as a nature preserve, with public access allowed. The Foundation provided support to the grantee in the form of a zero-interest land contract and bargain sale on the nature preserve portion of the property. This grant increase represents the final deed transfer.

title: Coordination of Mexico's Community Foundations Group
grantee: Centro Mexicano para la Filantropia, A.C.
description: The Centro Mexicano para la Filantropia, A.C. (Mexican Center for Philanthropy) is Mexico’s leading philanthropic support organization. It provides a range of services to established and newly emerging community foundations in Mexico, including training and technical assistance in strategic planning, endowment management, assessing community needs, and governance. It also promotes the community foundation field in Mexico and provides community foundations with networking opportunities regionally and internationally through conferences, workshops, mentoring and peer exchanges. This grant increase will support the continuation of the program through the end of 2006.

title: Coordination of Mexico's Community Foundations Group
grantee: Centro Mexicano para la Filantropia, A.C.
description: This grant supports the efforts of Centro Mexicano para la Filantropia, A.C. (Mexican Center for Philanthropy) to develop community foundations in Mexico. The center is Mexico’s leading philanthropic support organization. It provides a range of services to established and newly emerging community foundations in Mexico, including training and technical assistance in strategic planning, endowment management, assessing community needs, and governance. It also promotes the community foundation field in Mexico and provides community foundations with networking regionally and internationally through conferences, workshops, mentoring, and peer exchanges.

title: General Purposes
description: Tennessee’s rivers and streams support a rich diversity of plant and animal life, yet the state’s waters face a variety of threats, including pollution from sewage plants and stormwater runoff, creating a pressing need for more effective protections. With previous Mott support, the Tennessee Clean Water Network, a state leader in promoting water quality improvements, has worked to enhance and protect water quality and increase citizen involvement in water policy decisions. Renewal support will enable the network to build the capacity of local groups, promote policies to improve the health of waters statewide, and strengthen the organization’s own capacity to grow its board, membership, and funding base.

title: General Purposes
description: The Tennessee Clean Water Network is a statewide organization that works at the local and state levels to promote the adoption and implementation of clean water policies. With prior Mott support, the network has worked to put in place programs that protect relatively pristine waterways and clean up polluted ones; monitor state agency implementation of such water quality policies; and provide training and technical assistance to local watershed groups. With this grant, the network will continue such program efforts while also working to build its own organizational capacity by diversifying its funding sources, improving its external communications, and other means.

title: Africa Grantmakers Affinity Group
description: The Africa Grantmakers Affinity Group, a project of the Tides Center, is a membership-based organization of U.S.private foundations that fund in Africa. It provides a unique opportunity for foundations to learn and share with each other their grantmaking in Africa, especially as many of these foundations do not have offices in Africa. It also provides opportunities for networking, peer learning and exchanges, sharing of best practices, and collaborative funding.This grant will provide support for various programs and activities, particularly those related to knowledge building and knowledge sharing about grantmaking in Africa. This includes hosting an annual retreat where representatives from the foundations come together to talk about their work and to look at the many challenges they face.

title: Africa Grantmakers Affinity Group
description: The Africa Grantmakers Affinity Group, a program of the Tides Center, is a membership-based organization that funds in Africa. Since 2000, the grantee has organized member retreats in the United States that provide a platform for members and other funders to come together to share and learn from each other on issues of common interest and to improve the effectiveness of their grantmaking strategies for Africa. In February 2008, the Africa Grantmakers Affinity Group will hold its annual retreat in Johannesburg and will combine the event with a conference on resource mobilization, to which a range of stakeholders working in the African continent will be invited. This grant increase will support the Africa Grantmakers Affinity Group to organize this event.

title: Africa Grantmakers' Affinity Group
description: The program goal is to improve the field of grantmaking in Africa. Since 2001, the Africa Grantmakers’ Affinity Group, a project of the Tides Center, has served as a resource for funders supporting development efforts in Africa. Its activities include organizing an annual retreat to provide space for funders to network and address practical issues of common concern. It also conducts special research projects to track funding trends and provide information regarding where funders are active. Past support contributed to its various programs and activities, in particular, knowledge building and knowledge sharing about grantmaking in Africa. In 2008, the group hosted its first annual retreat on the African continent followed by a conference in Johannesburg. This grant will support the grantee to continue serving grantmakers working in Africa and strengthening collaboration among them.

title: Africa Grantmakers' Affinity Group
description: The Africa Grantmakers’ Affinity Group, a project of the Tides Center, works to improve the field of grantmaking in Africa. Since 2001, it has served as a resource for grantmakers’ funding development efforts in Africa. Its activities include hosting annual retreats that bring members together in a peer learning environment to share information on issues of common interest. It also produces research on various topics related to funding in Africa. Over the next two years, the Africa Grantmakers’ Affinity Group will continue to focus on building, sharing, leveraging, and brokering knowledge about funding support for development efforts in Africa. It will also initiate a strategic process that will explore changes in the development landscape and philanthropy in Africa and how these changes impact its operations.

title: Africa Grantmakers' Affinity Group
description: The Africa Grantmakers’ Affinity Group, a project of the Tides Center, is a network of organizations and individuals funding development work in Africa. Since 2000, it has served as a resource for grantmakers funding in Africa and works to deepen their understanding of development trends in countries they work in. Past support enabled the Africa Grantmakers’ Affinity Group to develop a new strategic plan that will guide the work of the group for the next three years, convene annual conferences that bring together grantmakers working across Africa to learn from one another, and host Webinars on topical issues affecting its members. This grant will support the group to grow and strengthen the pool of philanthropic resources to Africa by working with members to identify key points of leverage and new opportunities. It will also promote strategic partnerships and collaboration between current members and private philanthropists in Africa and convene grantmakers and experts to discuss issues related to their work in Africa to build a strong, connected, and informed network of grantmakers.

title: Africa Grantmakers' Affinity Group
description: The Africa Grantmakers’ Affinity Group, a project of the Tides Center, is a network of diverse groups and individuals funding efforts that benefit communities in Africa. Its activities help new and experienced funders build strong professional relationships and deepen their knowledge of current developments in Africa to leverage philanthropy to Africa. Past support enabled the Africa Grantmakers’ Affinity Group to continue bringing together funders working in Africa to learn about developments in Africa, share information on their work, and inform their grantmaking practices and produce a report in collaboration with the Foundation Center on philanthropic giving to Africa from foundations based in the United States. This grant will support the Africa Grantmakers’ Affinity Group to continue convening funders interested in Africa, providing information to members on funding to Africa, and connecting philanthropy support organizations whose work benefits African communities.

title: Africa Grantmakers' Affinity Group
description: The Africa Grantmakers’ Affinity Group, a project of the Tides Center, is a network of organizations and individuals that fund efforts which benefit communities in Africa. Its main objective is to build a strong network of funders that are informed and connected in order to have robust, effective, and responsive philanthropy that benefits African communities. Past support has enabled the project to convene funders working in Africa, establish a network of support organizations working in Africa, and share knowledge on developments and trends in Africa through various communication mediums. This grant will enable the grantee to continue hosting the annual conference, including hosting the 2020 conference in Johannesburg. In addition, the Africa Grantmakers’ Affinity Group will host webinars and specific regional meetings and generate knowledge on trends and funding that is targeting Africa.

title: Great Lakes Revolving Loan Fund
geographic_focus: Ohio, New York, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Illinois, Michigan, Minnesota, Indiana
description: The Great Lakes Revolving Loan Fund provides short-term financing for the protection of ecologically significant freshwater sites in the U.S. portion of the Great Lakes basin. Since its inception in 2001, and with Mott support, the fund has helped protect 13,839 acres valued at $49.8 million. This grant increase will build the fund’s corpus. The Conservation Fund is an organization that uses revolving loan funds as a primary strategy to conserve land and water resources nationwide.

title: Great Lakes Revolving Loan Fund
geographic_focus: Minnesota, Michigan, New York, Wisconsin, Indiana, Pennsylvania, Illinois, Ohio
description: The Great Lakes Revolving Loan Fund provides short-term financing for the protection of ecologically significant freshwater sites in the portion of the Great Lakes basin located in the United States. Since its inception in 2001, the fund has helped protect about 20,000 acres valued at nearly $56 million. This grant increase will build the fund’s corpus, allowing it to meet a growing demand for conservation project financing. The fund is a project of the Conservation Fund, a national organization which uses revolving loan funds as a means to conserve land and water.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen local-level democracy and civil society in Serbia and Montenegro by supporting the development of an indigenous grantmaking organization that provides small grants to local nongovernmental organizations and civic groups. Over the next two years, the Balkan Community Initiatives Fund will distribute $500,000 annually in grants to community-based organizations in Serbia and Montenegro, provide training and information resources to these organizations, and promote corporate and individual philanthropy at local and national levels. In 2005-2006, the fund made over 100 grants totaling approximately $410,000. The Balkan Community Initiatives Fund is a registered grantmaking organization in Serbia and works through a core staff based in Belgrade and a field office in Podgorica, Montenegro.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen local-level democracy and civil society in Serbia by supporting the development of the Balkan Community Initiatives Fund – Serbia, an indigenous grantmaking organization that provides small grants to local nongovernmental organizations. Over the next two years, the fund will distribute $850,000 annually in grants to community-based nonprofits in Serbia, provide networking and training opportunities to these organizations, and promote philanthropy at local and national levels. In addition, the fund will build its organizational capacities and sustainability through improved monitoring and evaluation mechanisms and long-term financial planning. In 2007-2008, the fund made over 170 grants totaling approximately $1,350,000. The fund is a registered grantmaking organization in Serbia and works through a core staff based in Belgrade. In 2008, its field office in Montenegro became an independent foundation.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen local level democracy and civil society in Serbia by supporting the development of the Balkan Community Initiatives Fund – Serbia, an indigenous grantmaking organization that provides small grants to local nongovernmental organizations. Over the next two years, the fund will distribute grants to community-based nonprofits in Serbia, provide networking and training opportunities to these organizations, and promote philanthropy at local and national levels. In addition, the fund will build its organizational capacities and sustainability through long-term financial planning and diversification of its funding base. In 2009-2010, the fund made over 150 grants totaling approximately $1,800,000. The fund is a registered grantmaking organization in Serbia and works through a core staff based in Belgrade.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen local-level democracy and civil society in Serbia by supporting the development of the Balkan Community Initiatives Fund – Serbia, an indigenous grantmaking organization that provides small grants to local nongovernmental organizations. Over the next two years, the grantee will distribute $520,000 annually in grants to community-based nonprofits in Serbia, provide networking and training opportunities to these organizations, and promote philanthropy at local and national levels. In addition, the grantee will build its organizational capacities and sustainability through long-term financial planning and diversification of its funding base. In 2012, the grantee will launch an endowment-building program designed to raise over $750,000 over the next five years. In connection with this program, the grantee will invest additional funds into building staff capacities, organizing events, bringing on additional staff, and engaging consultants as needed. In 2009-2010, the grantee made over 150 grants totaling approximately $1,800,000. The grantee is a registered grantmaking organization in Serbia and works through a core staff based in Belgrade.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen local-level democracy and civil society in Serbia by supporting the development of the Balkan Community Initiatives Fund – Serbia, an indigenous grantmaking organization that provides small grants to local nongovernmental organizations. Over the next two years, the grantee will distribute more than $600,000 annually in grants to community-based nonprofits in Serbia, provide networking and training opportunities to these organizations, and promote philanthropy at local and national levels. In addition, the grantee will build its organizational capacity and sustainability through long-term financial planning, diversification of its funding base, and the development of an endowment. During 2011-2013, the grantee continued to be the leading grantmaker for community-based nonprofits. In 2012, the grantee made over 120 grants totaling approximately $793,000. The grantee also strengthened the philanthropic field by playing a leadership role in the newly established Serbian Philanthropic Forum. The fund is a registered grantmaking organization in Serbia and works through a core staff based in Belgrade.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen philanthropy and encourage civic participation in Serbia by supporting the development of the Trag Foundation (formerly, the Balkan Community Initiatives Fund – Serbia), an indigenous grantmaking organization based in Belgrade. During the next two years, the grantee will aim to distribute more than $1.4 million annually in grants to community-based nonprofits in Serbia, provide networking and training opportunities to these organizations, and promote philanthropy at local and national levels. In addition, the grantee will build its organizational capacities and sustainability through long-term financial planning, diversification of its funding base, and the development of an endowment. During 2013-2015, the grantee continued to be the leading grantmaker for community-based nonprofits, providing 231 grants totaling $1,877,572 in 137 communities in Serbia. Additionally, with partners in the Western Balkans, the grantee designed and began implementation of a multiyear, European Commission-funded regional program to promote and develop philanthropy in the region. The Trag Foundation is registered in Serbia and works through a core staff based in Belgrade.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen philanthropy and encourage civic participation in Serbia by supporting the development of the Trag Foundation, an indigenous grantmaking organization based in Belgrade. During the next two years, the grantee will aim to distribute more than $2.5 million annually in grants to community-based nonprofits in Serbia; provide networking and training opportunities to these organizations; and promote philanthropy at local, national, and regional levels. In addition, the grantee will build its organizational capacities and sustainability through diversification of its funding base and the development of its endowment. During 2015-2017, the grantee awarded 188 grants totaling more than $3.8 million and coordinated a regional network of grantmakers in the Balkans.

title: School Board Leadership to Promote High Quality Extended-Day Learning for All Students
description: This grant will continue to support the efforts of the National School Boards Association to advance school leadership and policy development with respect to the creation of afterschool opportunities for all students. This work will support the grantee’s efforts to develop and disseminate resources that will enable and encourage local school boards to provide policy leadership for building and sustaining effective community-school partnerships to implement programs that expand the school day beyond traditional hours. The grantee will also focus on the need to develop resources and craft communication strategies for school boards associations who recognize the value of afterschool, while raising awareness among school board members who may not fully understand the benefits of quality afterschool activities. In addition, technical assistance will be provided to support state associations.

title: School Board Leadership to Promote High Quality Extended-Day Learning for All Students
description: This grant will continue to support the efforts of the National School Boards Association to advance school leadership and policy development in support of afterschool opportunities for all students. Specifically, this project will continue building the capacity of school board leaders in playing a critical role in examining how students are educated and developing strategic plans with various stakeholders at the local, state, and national levels to create seamless learning opportunities for all students based on the needs of their respective districts and communities. To accomplish this, the National School Boards Association will raise awareness among school board members regarding how quality afterschool programs can help improve education, and build the capacity of state school board associations to better support and promote extended learning opportunities.

title: School Board Leadership to Promote High Quality Extended-Day Learning for All Students
description: This grant increase will enable the National School Boards Association to further build the capacity of school board leaders to advance high quality afterschool programs by building awareness through meetings and informational documents. The grantee is working to advance school leadership and policy development in support of afterschool opportunities for all students by examining how students are educated and developing strategic plans with various stakeholders at the local, state, and national levels to create seamless learning opportunities based on the needs of their respective districts and communities.

title: EU Campaign to Reform Export Credit Agencies
description: FERN’s work aims to integrate environmental and social considerations into the decisionmaking and operations of European export credit agencies. During the grant period, FERN will focus its work on the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development’s review of its guidelines addressing export credit agencies’ environmental impacts. In addition, FERN will monitor and keep European Union officials informed of key projects funded or being considered by European export credit agencies that are not coherent with European Union environmental, social and human rights policies. FERN also will begin discussions among European organizations working on export credit agency reform to consider recent macroeconomic changes that impact international investment flows and the policies regulating those investments.

title: EU Campaign to Reform Export Credit Agencies
description: FERN’s work aims to integrate environmental and social considerations into the decisionmaking and operations of European export credit agencies. During the grant period, the grantee will focus its work on the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development’s review of its guidelines addressing export credit agencies’ environmental impacts. In addition, the grantee will monitor and keep European Union officials informed of key projects funded or being considered by European export credit agencies that are not consistent with European Union environmental, social, and human rights policies. As well, FERN will begin discussions amongst European organizations working on export credit agency reform to consider recent macroeconomic changes that impact international investment flows and the policies regulating those investments.

title: EU Campaign to Reform Export Credit Agencies and International Financial Flows
description: FERN works to ensure that international capital flows contribute to environmental protection and sustainable development in developing and transitional countries. Through FERN’s efforts, environmental guidelines for export credit agencies were adopted by the Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development and financing for a number of destructive projects have been cancelled. During the grant period, the grantee will continue its work coordinating European, nongovernmental efforts to reform export credit agencies and expand its work on European carbon emissions trading.

title: EU Campaign to Reform Export Credit Agencies and International Financial Flows
description: FERN works to ensure that international capital flows contribute to environmental protection and sustainable development in developing and transitional countries. This grant increase will allow the grantee to provide analysis for the European Union public review of financial market regulations, with a particular focus on regulation of carbon markets as they expand to include forests.

title: EU Campaign to Reform Export Credit Agencies and International Financial Flows
description: FERN’s work on global economic policy aims to ensure that international capital flows driven by policies and programs of the European Union contribute to environmental protection and sustainable development. During the last grant period, the grantee’s work led to the creation of new European Union requirements that European export credit agencies more fully report on the projects they guarantee. In addition, the grantee has raised attention to the problems of financial regulation of the European emissions trading system, ensuring that it is part of the discussions on revised European financial regulations. Over the next grant period, the grantee will monitor the implementation of the new export credit regulation and assess new areas of work related to the international financial flows that should be addressed.

title: General Purposes
description: The Steve Biko Foundation was established in 1998 in support of the leadership and vision of the late Stephen Bantu Biko, one of the founding figures of the black consciousness movement in South Africa, who was brutally murdered by the South African security forces in September 1977. It works mainly with young people, youth organizations and schools to bridge the racial, ethnic and social divides that decades of institutionalized racial division and segregation have left behind.This grant will enable the Steve Biko Foundation to continue its various programs and activities, particularly those that focus on identity, leadership and development.During the past two years, the organization has encouraged national dialogue through lectures and seminars, including the annual Steve Biko Memorial Lecture; hosted the Matthew Goniwe Youth Leadership Conference, which provides a space for learning, exchange of experience and sharing among youth drawn from diverse constituencies; and organized seminars and workshops on topics ranging from globalization, to women and development, to culture and history.

title: General Purposes
description: Founded in September 1998, the Steve Biko Foundation is a nonprofit trust that gives contemporary meaning and expression to the leadership legacy of the late Bantu Stephen Biko. Biko was one of the founding figures of the black consciousness movement in South Africa and was murdered by the South African security police in September 1977. The foundation’s main objective is to promote, nurture, and develop community-based leadership across the race, color, and ethnic divide. During the past grant period, the foundation met this objective by promoting national dialogue through lectures, seminars, publications, as well as implementing programs focusing on arts, culture, and identity; economic justice; and social development. Future plans include the continuation and expansion of programs, substantially increasing the foundation’s staff; greater focus on policy development, research, and publications; and fundraising for an endowment.

title: General Purposes
description: Established in 1998, the Steve Biko Foundation seeks to nurture and develop community leadership, especially among the youth, as a means to promote civic participation in politics, the economy, and culture. It also promotes public dialogue on government policy, popular culture, and race relations through a series of lectures and seminars. The Steve Biko Foundation is inspired by the leadership legacy of Steven Bantu Biko, one of the founding figures of the black consciousness movement in South Africa who was murdered by the security police in September 1977. In the past two years, the grantee supported youth and entrepreneurship programs in the Eastern Cape province, most notably the Expressions of Identity program for youth, which uses art to address social challenges. The program has attracted a lot of interest and the grantee has requests for assistance to implement similar programs in various communities. This grant will continue to support the Steve Biko Foundation’s efforts to nurture and affirm fundamental human values.

title: General Purposes
description: Established in 1998, the Steve Biko Foundation seeks to nurture and develop community leadership — especially among the youth — to promote civic participation in politics, the economy, and culture. The grantee is inspired by the leadership legacy of Steven Bantu Biko, one of the founding figures of the black consciousness movement in South Africa who was murdered by the security police in September 1977. In the past two years, the grantee conducted public lectures, seminars, and dialogues on topical issues and supported various projects in arts and culture, economic justice, and social development. It also piloted “FrankTalk”, a program for young people committed to utilizing their skills and experience for the advancement of South African society. This grant will continue to support the grantee’s efforts to nurture and affirm fundamental human values. The primary focus over the next two years will be launching and running the Steve Biko Centre, a legacy project that will house the majority of its programs and will allow for the expansion of its work.

title: General Purposes
description: Established in 1998, the Steve Biko Foundation is a community development organization inspired by the legacy of Bantu Stephen Biko, one of the founders of the black consciousness movement in South Africa. Its main objective is to encourage active citizenship and social action among the youth in politics, culture, and the economy. In the past two years, the grantee hosted public lectures and seminars on various topical issues including xenophobia, launched the Steve Biko Centre — a community center erected in Biko’s hometown of Ginsberg in the Eastern Cape Province — and piloted the Frank Talk program to promote public education and discourse between young professionals. This grant will support the Steve Biko Foundation to continue to host public lectures, seminars, and dialogues that educate young people about the history of the country and the Bill of Rights. The grantee will also continue to support programs that promote arts and culture, economic justice, and social development.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Russia, Czech Republic, Bulgaria, Slovakia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Poland, Romania
description: The program goal is to encourage grassroots, civic participation in decisionmaking processes throughout Central and Eastern Europe and the Newly Independent States. To this end, this grant supports a vibrant network of nongovernmental organizations working in the field of community organizing. During the next two years, the network will undertake a strategic planning exercise in order to address key challenges associated with its growth and new issues facing the region; organize annual Citizen Participation Week events in 17 countries; and offer training and information services to its members. In 2006-2007, the CEE Citizens Network increased the skills and capacities of community leaders, facilitated joint initiatives among network members, and raised awareness about civic participation throughout the region. Initiated in 2001 as a project of the Center for Community Organizing – Slovakia, the network registered as an independent organization in 2005. The network has 31 members representing 17 countries. Many of the network’s members are Mott Foundation grantees.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Bulgaria, Slovakia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Poland, Russia, Romania, Czech Republic
description: The program goal is to encourage grassroots, civic participation in decisionmaking processes throughout Central and Eastern Europe and the former Soviet Union. To this end, this grant supports a vibrant network of nongovernmental organizations working with citizens and local communities. During the next two years, the network will organize its annual Citizen Participation Week simultaneously in 17 countries, conduct a study to benchmark levels of citizen participation across the region, promote participation through innovative uses of technology, and strengthen cooperation with other networks. In 2008-2009, the CEE Citizens Network developed partnerships with several important European networks and held two annual training events. The network also organized events in countries represented by the network as part of its annual Citizen Participation Week. Initiated in 2001 as a project of the Center for Community Organizing – Slovakia, the network registered as an independent organization in 2005. The network has 31 members representing 17 countries. Many of the network’s members are Mott Foundation grantees.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Slovakia, Bulgaria, Czech Republic, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Russia, Poland, Romania
description: The program goal is to encourage grassroots, civic participation in decisionmaking processes throughout Central and Eastern Europe and the former Soviet Union. To this end, this grant increase responds to unanticipated opportunities to strengthen the capacity of network members to work with citizens and local communities. In addition to its other planned activities, CEE Citizens Network will organize one or more study visits for members and build mentoring relationships for members with experienced community organizers. In 2008-2009, the grantee developed partnerships with several important European networks and held two annual training events. The grantee also organized events as part of its annual Citizen Participation Week. Initiated in 2001 as a project of the Center for Community Organizing-Slovakia, the grantee registered as an independent organization in 2005. The grantee has 31 members representing 17 countries. Many of the grantee’s members are Mott Foundation grantees.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Slovakia, Bulgaria, Czech Republic, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Russia, Poland, Romania
description: The goal of the organization is to encourage grassroots, civic participation in decisionmaking processes throughout Central and Eastern Europe and the former Soviet Union. To this end, the CEE Citizens Network is seeking increased funding to organize additional consulting visits to local community organizing projects, convene coordination meetings of a growing informal network of European experts and practitioners, and organize partnership building and fundraising visits of this network’s leaders to the United States. In 2008-2010, the grantee developed partnerships with several important European networks and held three annual training events. The grantee also organized events in countries represented by the grantee as part of its annual Citizen Participation Week. Initiated in 2001 as a project of the Center for Community Organizing-Slovakia, the grantee registered as an independent organization in 2005. The grantee has 31 members representing 17 countries. Many of the grantee’s members are Mott Foundation grantees.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Slovakia, Czech Republic, Bulgaria, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Russia, Poland, Romania
description: The program goal is to encourage grassroots, civic participation in decision making processes throughout Central and Eastern Europe and the former Soviet Union. To this end, CEE Citizens Network will organize its annual Citizen Participation Week and Citizen University involving partner organizations from more than 20 countries in the region, conduct a study to benchmark levels of citizen participation across the region, promote participation through innovative uses of technology, and strengthen cooperation with other networks. In 2010-2011, the grantee developed partnerships with several important European networks and held two annual training events. The grantee also organized events in countries represented by the grantee as part of its annual Citizen Participation Week and Citizen University. Initiated in 2001 as a project of the Center for Community Organizing – Slovakia, the grantee registered as an independent organization in 2005. The grantee has 35 members representing 18 countries. Many of the grantee’s members are Mott Foundation grantees.

title: California Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant to the University of California – Davis will continue to support California’s need to build a statewide, inclusive network of afterschool stakeholders. This grantee is part of the first cohort of Mott-funded statewide afterschool networks. This renewal is an achievement grant, which continues to provide core support to the network, while also encouraging new ideas designed to align and integrate afterschool and education systems. Each network receiving an achievement grant is expected to share lessons learned and products with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: California Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the University of California – Davis to coordinate the California Statewide Afterschool Network. In addition to continuing the network’s core work to advance afterschool programs in California, it will complete a multiyear project to develop and implement a statewide delivery system of high quality science, technology, engineering, and math experiences during out-of-school time, including the establishment of innovation centers. Through this project, the network seeks to significantly raise the science and math test scores of California students. The network will also share lessons learned and products with other statewide afterschool networks to ensure that new models and best practices are incorporated nationally.

title: California Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the University of California – Davis which coordinates the California Statewide Afterschool Network. The California Statewide Afterschool Network will focus on building capacity for long-term success and advancing systems change for afterschool and expanded learning in California. Over the next three years, the network will support the development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool and expanded learning programs. The specific initiatives will include: 1) advancing the professional learning systems across the expanded learning and school day; and 2) refining, disseminating, and promoting the California quality standards for afterschool.

title: California Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant to the Foundation for California Community Colleges will support the development of the California Statewide Afterschool Network to continue to build an afterschool and summer learning system that improves outcomes for children and youth through school-based or school-linked afterschool programs. Over the next three years, the network will support the development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) establishing a work group on K-12 partnerships connected to the California Department of Education-After School Division; 2) connecting the afterschool field to funding opportunities to sustain and expand programs; and 3) engaging the Regional Technical Assistance Providers to implement a process of continuous quality improvement for afterschool programs.

title: California Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Foundation for California Community Colleges, which coordinates the California Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) expanding social-emotional learning training strategies to build the capacity of the afterschool field; 2) educating the field, partners, and stakeholders on local and state afterschool funding initiatives to increase support for workforce development; 3) developing a plan to strengthen the California Statewide Afterschool Network’s governance and sustainability; and 4) participating in the development and distribution of new afterschool program content in collaboration with the Foundation’s thematic partners.

title: General Purposes
description: The Afterschool Alliance supports the vision that all children and youth — particularly those in underserved populations — will have access to quality, affordable afterschool programs. The specific goals of the alliance are to serve as a national information source on afterschool programs and resources; be an effective voice for expanding the quality of afterschool programs; encourage the development of local, state and national afterschool constituencies and systems; and communicate the impact of afterschool programs on children, families and communities.This grant will enable the alliance to raise public awareness of afterschool programs and resources and continue developing its organizational infrastructure.In 2005, Lights on Afterschool – a nationwide celebration of local events designed to call attention to the importance of afterschool programs – had more than 8,000 rallies involving approximately 1 million Americans.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant to the Afterschool Alliance will provide general purposes support to fulfill its vision that all children and youth — particularly those in underserved populations — will have access to quality, affordable afterschool programs. The specific goals are: to serve as a national information source on afterschool programs and resources; to be an effective voice for expanding the quality of afterschool; to encourage the development of local, state, and national afterschool constituencies and systems; and to communicate the impact of afterschool programs on children, families, and communities.

title: General Purposes
description: This renewal grant to the Afterschool Alliance will continue to support its efforts to be the national voice for the afterschool field, and the main organizing body for the afterschool movement. Its vision is that all children and youth — particularly those in underserved populations — will have access to quality, affordable afterschool programs. The Afterschool Alliance is working to effect policy change to make afterschool a national priority, and plans to accomplish that through the following goals: 1) serving as an information source on afterschool programs and resources; 2) being an effective voice for afterschool in efforts to expand quality afterschool programs; 3) encouraging the development of local, state, and national afterschool constituencies and systems; and 4) communicating the impact of afterschool programs on children, families, and communities.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant increase supports the general purposes of the Afterschool Alliance in its efforts to be the national voice for the afterschool field, and the main organizing body for the afterschool movement. This grant increase to the Afterschool Alliance will support a partnership with Fight Crime: Invest in Kids to educate federal policymakers and the public about the benefits and importance of increasing investments in high quality afterschool programs, especially for low-income, disadvantaged youth.

title: General Purposes
description: This renewal grant will allow the Afterschool Alliance to continue to support the vision that all children and youth — particularly those in underserved populations — will have access to quality, affordable afterschool programs. In 2009, the Afterschool Alliance will renew its position as the national voice of afterschool as the nation considers education reform, families struggle with economic challenges, the public embraces a renewed sense that government plays a vital role in shaping success, and a new administration takes office. Specifically, the Afterschool Alliance will continue to focus on the following as ongoing priorities concerning the afterschool field: 1) serving as an information source on afterschool programs and resources; 2) being an effective voice for afterschool in efforts to expand quality afterschool programs; 3) encouraging the development of local, state, and national afterschool constituencies and systems; and 4) communicating the impact of afterschool programs on children, families, and communities.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will allow the Afterschool Alliance to continue its efforts to ensure that all children and youth — particularly those in underserved populations — will have access to quality, affordable afterschool programs. The grantee serves as the lead voice and organizer of the field; works with policymakers to advance opportunities for afterschool; and ensures that the field’s lessons inform various policy fronts and other education reform initiatives. Specifically, the grantee will continue its work on the following priorities: 1) serving as an information source on afterschool programs and resources; 2) being an effective voice for afterschool in efforts to expand quality afterschool programs; 3) encouraging the development of local, state, and national afterschool constituencies and systems; and 4) communicating the impact of afterschool programs on children, families, and communities. In addition, the grantee will work with the Mott-funded, statewide afterschool networks and the afterschool field to help afterschool programs access federal stimulus dollars.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will allow the Afterschool Alliance to continue its efforts to ensure that children and youth, particularly those in underserved populations, will have access to engaging afterschool opportunities that inspire learning and achievement in school and in life. The grantee serves as a critical voice and organizer of the field, works with federal policymakers to advance opportunities for afterschool, and ensures that the field’s lessons inform national education and youth policy initiatives. Specifically, the grantee will continue to: 1) serve as an information source on afterschool programs and resources; 2) be an effective voice for afterschool in its efforts to expand quality afterschool programs; 3) encourage the development of local, state, and national afterschool constituencies and systems; and 4) communicate the positive impact of afterschool programs on children, families, and communities. In addition, the grantee will work with the 39 Mott-funded statewide afterschool networks as a member of the national Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative.

title: General Purposes
