title: General Purposes
description: The Bulgarian Charities Aid Foundation (BCAF) promotes workplace and payroll giving plans; administers corporate giving programs; trains non-governmental organizations (NGOs) on local resource mobilization and financial management; and advocates for a legal and fiscal environment that encourages philanthropy.This grant will enable the organization to provide information and analysis on a wide range of philanthropic development issues; encourage businesses to increase the level and effectiveness of corporate giving; introduce new methods and technologies, such as online and text messaging, to increase the level and effectiveness of individual giving; offer technical assistance to NGOs to improve their access to resources; and advocate for improving the legal and fiscal environment for philanthropy in Bulgaria.BCAF was established in 1995 as a result of extensive consultation between Charities Aid Foundation in the U.K. and leading Bulgarian foundations.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to mobilize financial resources and promote philanthropy in Bulgaria. During the grant period, the Bulgarian Charities Aid Foundation will promote workplace and payroll giving schemes, administer corporate giving programs, train nongovernmental organizations on local resource mobilization and financial management, and advocate for a legal and fiscal environment that encourages philanthropy. The foundation was established in 1995 with the mission to develop philanthropy in Bulgaria and increase resources available for charitable purposes. The foundation is on the forefront of developing innovative approaches to unlocking financial resources through individual and corporate giving in Bulgaria. The foundation’s key achievements in 2006-2007 included raising over $470,000 from individuals and companies in Bulgaria for regranting, providing training in local resource mobilization to 40 nonprofits; and consulting over 50 companies on their philanthropic programs.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to mobilize financial resources and promote philanthropy in Bulgaria. To this end, the Bulgarian Charities Aid Foundation will promote workplace and payroll giving schemes, administer corporate giving programs, and train nongovernmental organizations on local resource mobilization and financial management. The foundation was established in 1995 with the mission to develop philanthropy in Bulgaria and increase resources available for charitable purposes. The foundation is on the forefront of developing innovative approaches to unlocking financial resources through individual and corporate giving in Bulgaria. The foundation’s key achievements in 2008-2009 include raising over $850,000 from individuals and companies in Bulgaria for regranting, developing philanthropic programs for seven new companies, and organizing 6,000 hours of corporate volunteering.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to mobilize financial resources and promote philanthropy in Bulgaria. To this end, the Bulgarian Charities Aid Foundation will promote workplace and payroll giving schemes, administer corporate giving programs, and train nongovernmental organizations on local resource mobilization and financial management. In addition, the grantee will develop and adopt a new business model for its operation to secure its long-term financial sustainability. The grantee’s key achievements in 2010-2011 included raising over $500,000 from individuals and companies in Bulgaria to support individual beneficiaries and nonprofits, developing philanthropic programs for companies, and organizing corporate volunteering. Based in Sofia, the grantee was established in 1995 with the mission to develop philanthropy in Bulgaria and increase resources available for charitable purposes.

title: Municipal Leadership for Disconnected Youth
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
geographic_focus: Baltimore Independent City, Philadelphia, San Diego, San Francisco, Boston, Corpus Christi
description: This grant will enable the National League of Cities Institute – a research, education and training affiliate of the National League of Cities – to increase the capacity of mayors and other municipal leaders to launch cross-system efforts that expand education options for disconnected youth. During the most recent phase of this initiative, the institute focused on documenting effective practices of cross-system work in order to build a knowledge base to ground and support future outreach and technical assistance efforts. During the second phase of this initiative, emphasis will shift from documenting effective practices to providing more direct assistance to cities by working with municipal leaders to expand best practices and models that result in improved cross-system efforts for youth.

title: Municipal Leadership for Disconnected Youth
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
geographic_focus: Boston, Baltimore Independent City, San Francisco, Philadelphia, San Diego, Corpus Christi
description: This grant will enable the National League of Cities Institute, a research, education, and training affiliate of the National League of Cities, to continue to increase the capacity of municipal leaders in launching cross-system efforts that expand education options for disconnected youth. In the most recent phase of this initiative, the National League of Cities Institute provided direct technical assistance to cities by working with municipal leaders to expand best practices and models that result in improved cross-system efforts for disconnected youth. During the final phase of this initiative, the grantee will provide another round of direct technical assistance to a new cohort of cities, develop a resource guide to help cities assess strategies/investments for disconnected youth, and expand outreach efforts to municipal leaders and national organizations to advocate for increased capacity and resources to reengage youth.

title: Municipal Leadership for Disconnected Youth
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
geographic_focus: Boston, Philadelphia, San Diego, San Francisco, Baltimore Independent City, Corpus Christi
description: This grant will enable the National League of Cities Institute, a research, education, and training affiliate of the National League of Cities, to continue to increase the capacity of municipal leaders in forging cross-system collaborations that address the needs of disconnected youth. During the most recent phase of this effort, the grantee assisted a select group of cities in developing employment strategies for disconnected youth as a result of new opportunities via the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act. In the next phase of this initiative, the grantee will launch a new technical assistance effort to assist a more experienced cohort of cities in an effort to develop promising practices for a larger network of cities and municipal leaders across the country interested in improving outcomes for disconnected youth.

title: Municipal Leadership for Disconnected Youth
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant will enable the National League of Cities Institute, a research, education, and training affiliate of the National League of Cities, to continue to increase the capacity of municipal leaders to lead cross-system efforts that expand education options for disconnected youth. In the most recent phase of this initiative, the grantee assisted 20 cities in developing strategies for improving outcomes for disconnected youth. The grantee also developed an online database of 53 promising city initiatives focused on re-engaging disconnected youth. During the final phase of this initiative, the grantee will identify opportunities to build the capacity of additional cities and municipal leaders to advance local disconnected youth initiatives, continue to document disconnected youth strategies in cities around the country via its online database, and form/support a cohort of learning communities from cities within its network to discuss disconnected youth issues.

title: Municipal Leadership for Disconnected Youth
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant will enable the National League of Cities Institute, a research, education, and training affiliate of the National League of Cities, to continue to increase the capacity of municipal leaders to form cross-system efforts that expand education options for disconnected youth. In the most recent phase of this initiative, the National League of Cities Institute engaged nearly 40 cities across two overlapping peer learning networks focused on the expansion of dropout reengagement centers and the achievement of young men of color. These networks have provided the grantee strategic insight on the ways in which cities are seeking to reengage disconnected youth, address the specific needs of young men of color, and advance promising policies/strategies. Recommended support will enable the grantee to sustain and strengthen these networks and explore ways to deepen the focus of each network on postsecondary access and success strategies, from preparation to affordability and savings, given the surge in city leaders’ interest in and commitment to issues of college access and completion.

title: Cities Building Bridges to Postsecondary Success
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: Cities can play an important role in helping families prepare financially for their children’s college education. Engaging more municipal leaders on these issues offers important opportunities to advance children’s savings accounts. This renewal grant will enable the National League of Cities Institute to work with a select group of municipal leaders to explore options for integrating financial strategies, including savings accounts, into broader efforts to promote college access and success. The overall goal of this project is to develop a strong new set of city-level examples that illustrate the potential of children’s savings accounts as a promising strategy to increase families’ financial preparedness for college. Located in Washington, D.C., the grantee is a research, education, and training affiliate of the National League of Cities.

title: Cities Building Bridges to Postsecondary Success
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This renewal grant will enable the National League of Cities Institute to help municipal leaders integrate citywide and regional children’s savings account initiatives into their college readiness, access, and success programming. The grantee will continue to create educational materials, broker technical assistance, and provide opportunities for peer learning among municipal leaders. The overall goal of this project is to establish a strong set of city-level examples that illustrate the potential of children’s savings accounts as a promising component of comprehensive efforts to increase postsecondary success. Established in 1958 and located in Washington, D.C., the grantee is a research, education, and training affiliate of the National League of Cities.

title: Justice and Reconciliation in the Balkans
geographic_focus: Serbia, Montenegro, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia
description: Multiyear funding will enable the International Center for Transitional Justice to assist the governments and non-governmental organizations (NGOs) in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, and Serbia and Montenegro to respond to a legacy of human rights abuses in order to prevent the repetition of such violations in the future. The organization also works to advance accountability, promote institutional reform and respond to the needs of victims.During the past two years, the center has provided direct assistance to key NGOs in the region working on transitional justice issues; conducted workshops and seminars for students and practitioners of transitional justice; and monitored and published reports on war crimes documentation, war crimes trials and vetting processes. In order to support its work in the Western Balkans and elsewhere, the center opened an office in Brussels in August 2005.The center was established in 2001 to promote accountability by helping countries develop effective responses to human rights abuse.

title: Justice and Reconciliation in the Balkans
geographic_focus: Serbia, Croatia, Montenegro, Bosnia and Herzegovina
description: The project goal is to support a range of governmental and nongovernmental initiatives in Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia, Kosovo, and Serbia to address issues of truth, reconciliation, and justice in response to wars and human rights abuses during the 1990s. The International Center for Transitional Justice will assist the governments and nongovernmental organizations in these countries to respond to a legacy of human rights abuses in order to prevent future violations, advance accountability, promote institutional reform, and respond to the needs of victims. In 2006-2007, the center provided technical assistance to a coalition of research and documentation centers; built the capacity of civic leaders and practitioners on transitional justice issues through retreats, fellowships, and seminars; and published analytical reports on various aspects of transitional justice initiatives in the Western Balkans. The center’s program in the former Yugoslavia is coordinated jointly from its headquarters in New York and its Brussels office.

title: General Purposes
description: The Centre for Anti-Racism and Anti-Sexism Trust focuses on transforming attitudes and practices through training and facilitation, research, and initiatives to develop and implement action plans to combat racism and sexism. The organization recently changed its operating name to Caring About Rights and Responsibilities Across Societies, to reflect a new direction and orientation in its approach, which will examine how issues of poverty and socioeconomic inequalities contribute to the perpetuation of racism and racial discrimination. This grant will provide support to the organization for this process of reorientation, particularly as this relates to integrating questions of economic justice into its training programs and enhancing the capacity of its staff and associates to deal with the socioeconomic challenges of building a nonracial democracy in South Africa.

title: General Purposes
description: Ditshwanelo CAR²AS assists people and communities in South Africa to better understand and deal with the impact of racism and sexism at both the individual and institutional level. Past efforts focused on transforming attitudes and practices through training and facilitation, research, and programs that combat racism and sexism. This grant will support the continuation of these activities for the next two years, when the major focus will be on establishing a learning and advocacy development center for rights-based learning; expanding a dialogue program; training facilitators; and using these facilitators to transform organizations and government agencies by addressing issues of racism, sexism, and economic justice.

title: General Purposes
description: Ditshwanelo CAR²AS assists people and communities in South Africa to better understand and deal with the impact of racism and sexism at both the individual and institutional level. Over the past few years, it provided services to a range of institutions including government, business, and the nonprofit sector to promote healing and reconciliation and combat racism. Ongoing work includes an intervention with the Golden Lions Rugby Union to tackle racism in sport. The grantee will also provide support to the South African Human Rights Commission to address racism and promote reconciliation and community healing in the small town of Skierlik in the Northwest province. Support will also be provided to organizations in Kenya to deal with ethnic conflicts and to promote peace to prevent a repeat of the post-election violence of 2007.

title: Expansion of Training and Technical Assistance to ACORN Organizations
description: The American Institute for Social Justice provides leadership and staff training, technical assistance, research, and project support to community organizing groups, including the Association of Community Organizations for Reform Now, commonly known by the acronym ACORN, one of the largest community organizing networks. This grant will support the American Institute for Social Justice’s efforts to expand the training and technical assistance provided to local ACORN groups to help them identify, recruit, and train additional organizers; provide ongoing professional and personal development opportunities for organizers; hold local and regional training events for leaders; develop new chapters; form partnerships with other organizing networks; and develop long-range, self-sufficiency plans for financial support.

title: Expansion of Training and Technical Assistance to ACORN Organizations
description: The American Institute for Social Justice provides leadership and staff training, technical assistance, research, and campaign support to community organizing groups, including the Association of Community Organizations for Reform Now, commonly known by the acronym ACORN, one of the largest community organizing networks. This grant supports the organization’s efforts to expand the training and technical assistance provided to local ACORN groups. This grant increase supports a new opportunity to provide training in San Juan, Puerto Rico.

title: General Purposes
description: Multiyear funding will enable the Association for Community Relations to carry out research to establish the current state of, and opportunities for, philanthropy in Romania; build the capacity of nonprofit organizations to raise local resources through the provision of training and technical assistance; disseminate information about fundraising mechanisms and successful practices; and develop innovative fundraising programs. Activities also will build on existing efforts to develop philanthropy throughout the region.Recent accomplishments included publishing two studies on the state of philanthropy in Romania; developing and maintaining a Web site to serve as a resource for fundraising practitioners; disseminating a monthly newsletter; launching a payroll-giving program; and creating a comprehensive training and consultancy program for non-governmental organizations.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to promote and develop philanthropy in Romania. During the grant period, the Association for Community Relations will carry out research to establish the current state of and opportunities for philanthropy; build the capacity of nonprofit organizations to raise local resources by providing training and technical assistance; disseminate information about fundraising mechanisms and successful practices; and develop innovative fundraising programs. Activities will also build on existing efforts to develop philanthropy throughout Central and Eastern Europe. The association’s past achievements include publishing two comprehensive studies on funding for nonprofit organizations in Romania, organizing annual conferences on corporate philanthropy, raising awareness about existing incentives for philanthropy for businesses and individuals, and supporting fundraising efforts of nonprofit organizations on the local and national levels.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to develop philanthropy in Romania. During the grant period, the Association for Community Relations will carry out research on the current state of philanthropy; build the capacity of nonprofit organizations to raise local resources by providing training and technical assistance; disseminating information about fundraising mechanisms and successful practices; and developing innovative fundraising programs. The grantee’s past achievements include publishing studies on funding for nonprofit organizations in Romania, organizing annual conferences on corporate philanthropy, raising awareness about existing incentives for philanthropy for businesses and individuals, and supporting fundraising efforts of nonprofits on the local and national levels. This grant increase will enable the grantee to provide additional services to two recently established community foundations and develop a long-term national strategy for community foundation development in Romania.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to promote and develop philanthropy in Romania. During the grant period, the Association for Community Relations will build the capacity of nonprofit organizations in Romania to raise local resources by providing training and technical assistance; improve the level and quality of corporate giving by providing consultancy to national and multinational businesses; strengthen philanthropy on the community level by supporting the initiation and development of community foundations; and improve the visibility of the philanthropic sector by carrying out research and disseminating information about successful practices. Activities will also build on existing efforts to develop philanthropy throughout Central and Eastern Europe. In 2008-2009, the grantee organized two conferences on corporate philanthropy, raised awareness about existing incentives for philanthropy for businesses and individuals, and supported fundraising efforts of nonprofits. Based in Cluj-Napoca, Romania, the Association for Community Relations was established in 2001 with the mission to promote and develop philanthropy in Romania.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to promote and develop philanthropy in Romania. During the grant period, the Association for Community Relations will build the capacity of nonprofit organizations in Romania to raise local resources by providing training and technical assistance, improve the level and quality of corporate giving by providing consultancy to national and multinational businesses, strengthen philanthropy on the community level by supporting the initiation and development of community foundations, and improve the visibility of the philanthropic sector by carrying out research and disseminating information about successful practices. Activities will also build on existing efforts to develop philanthropy throughout Central and Eastern Europe. In 2010-2011, the grantee organized two conferences on corporate philanthropy, raised awareness about existing incentives for philanthropy for businesses and individuals, and facilitated the establishment of three new community foundations. Based in Cluj-Napoca, Romania, the Association for Community Relations was established in 2001 with the mission to promote and develop philanthropy in Romania.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to promote and develop philanthropy in Romania. During the grant period, the Association for Community Relations will build the capacity of nonprofit organizations in Romania to raise local resources, introduce new giving mechanisms and programs, improve the level and quality of corporate giving, strengthen community philanthropy and community foundations, and improve the visibility of the philanthropic sector in Romania. In addition, the grantee will strengthen its financial sustainability by building its long-term assets and an endowment. Also, the grantee will strengthen its regional cooperation with peer organizations and individual professionals in the field of philanthropy development. In 2012-2013, the grantee helped more than ten advocacy organizations to start fundraising from local sources, facilitated the establishment of six new community foundations, and introduced donations through direct debit in partnership with six major Romanian banks. Based in Cluj-Napoca, Romania, the Association for Community Relations was established in 2001 with the mission to promote and develop philanthropy in Romania.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to promote and develop philanthropy in Romania. During the grant period, the Association for Community Relations will build the capacity of nonprofit organizations in Romania to raise local resources, strengthen the infrastructure for philanthropy, strengthen community philanthropy and community foundations, and improve the visibility of the philanthropic sector in Romania. The grantee will also work to strengthen its regional cooperation with peer organizations and individual professionals in the field of philanthropy development, and its financial sustainability by building its long-term assets and an endowment. In 2014-2015, the grantee raised over $3.5 million through innovative giving mechanisms, including giving circles and short text messages; helped more than 60 nonprofit organizations to start fundraising from local sources; and facilitated the establishment of three new community foundations. Based in Cluj-Napoca, Romania, the Association for Community Relations was established in 2001 with the mission to promote and develop philanthropy in Romania.

title: Community Foundation Initiative in Germany
description: This grant continues partial funding for the Community Foundation Initiative in Germany, a project originally started by the Bertelsmann Stiftung and now managed by the Bundesverband Deutscher Stiftungen (the Association of German Foundations). Currently, there are 150 community foundations in Germany with a combined capital of more than 53 million Euro. This program provides these new and emerging German community foundations with a range of support services, including technical assistance, peer learning workshops, information sharing opportunities, legal advice, and an accreditation process. In addition to these ongoing activities, in 2008-2010, the Community Foundation Initiative in Germany plans to deepen its connections with community foundations in neighboring Eastern European countries through workshops and site visits. Bundesverband Deutscher Stiftungen represents the foundation community in Germany.

title: IFI Small Grants Fund
description: This grant increase will assist with travel costs for a Global Greengrants Fund representative to participate in a panel discussion at the Environmental Grantmakers Association annual retreat. The panel will highlight the outcomes of the Global Greengrants Fund’s regranting program that the Foundation supports.

title: Sectoral Employment Impact Study: Random Assignment Evaluation
description: The purpose of this grant renewal to Public/Private Ventures is to continue a random assignment evaluation and provide technical assistance to three sectoral training initiatives: the Wisconsin Regional Training Partnership in Milwaukee, Per Scholas in the Bronx, and Jewish Vocational Services of Boston. Past studies of sectoral employment programs funded by the Foundation have illustrated employment success, job retention, and increased earnings. The primary purpose of this study, if successful, is to influence public policy by specifically proving the effectiveness of sectoral training on increased earnings and job retention.

title: Sectoral Employment Impact Study: Random Assignment Evaluation
description: This renewal grant to Public/Private Ventures continues support for an impact study of three sectoral employment programs: the Wisconsin Regional Training Partnership in Milwaukee, Jewish Vocational Services in Boston, and Per Scholas in the Bronx. The purpose of the study is to provide highly credible evidence to policymakers and practitioners about the ability of well-designed and well-implemented sectoral employment programs to produce significant increases in the employment and earnings of low-income workers.

title: Sectoral Employment Impact Study: Random Assignment Evaluation
description: This renewal grant to Public/Private Ventures will support an impact study of three sectoral employment programs — the Wisconsin Regional Training Partnership in Milwaukee, Jewish Vocational Services in Boston, and Per Scholas in the Bronx. The goal is to provide highly credible evidence to practitioners and policymakers that well-implemented sectoral employment training programs produce significant increases in employment and earnings for low-skilled, unemployed, or underemployed populations.

title: Sectoral Employment Impact Study: Random Assignment Evaluation
description: Given the significant findings of the Sectoral Employment Impact Study and the goal of influencing public policy, Public/Private Ventures proposes an enhanced communications strategy to make the results of both the initial and final analyses of the data more widely available. This grant increase will cover the cost of additional dissemination activities, a one-day conference for academics with an interest in workforce development and poverty issues, and enhanced outreach to national and local media.

title: Microenterprise and Disability: Building the Momentum
description: Micro-enterprise programs are assisting the most disadvantaged entrepreneurs in the U.S. with intensive, cost-effective services that help individuals start and sustain viable businesses. However, out of approximately 600 micro-enterprise programs nationwide, only a small percentage target their products and services to people with disabilities and the agencies that serve them.This grant will enable the Abilities Fund to refine its referral process; continue to build the technical capacity and accessibility of micro-enterprise programs; and connect micro-enterprise and rehabilitation professionals to enable individuals with disabilities to realize full inclusion and access to mainstream micro-enterprise development services.The Abilities Fund is the first and only nationwide community developer and financial institution targeted exclusively to advancing entrepreneurial opportunities for individuals with disabilities.

title: African American Philanthropy Initiative (AAPI)
description: This grant will provide renewal support to Associated Black Charities for its African American Philanthropy Initiative, a project designed to build the capacity of the organization, develop and deliver educational and outreach materials, and create opportunities to promote institutional philanthropy within the African-American community. The initiative provides charitable giving information to different segments of Maryland’s black community including wealthy African Americans, high-tech and small business entrepreneurs, and their financial advisors. It also offers charitable vehicle options that help donors in their giving, such as donor-advised funds.

title: Southeastern Rivers and Streams Support Fund
description: The rivers and streams of the Southeast are considered globally significant due to the aquatic biodiversity they support. Since 1998, World Wildlife Fund has dedicated staff to coordinate and strengthen freshwater conservation efforts in the region. This grant increase will enable World Wildlife Fund to expand its existing small grant program to support the efforts of environmental organizations working collaboratively to address state-level water quality policy issues in Tennessee.

title: Southeastern Rivers and Streams Support Fund
description: Through its Southeastern Rivers and Streams Support Fund, the World Wildlife Fund, an international conservation organization, provides small grants and networking opportunities to organizations committed to protecting and restoring aquatic resources in the Cumberland, Mobile, and Tennessee river basins. With prior Mott funding, the support fund has been used to build the capacity of local, state, and regional organizations, fostering a stronger collective voice for regionwide conservation. With continued Mott support, the support fund will be used to promote the implementation of the Clean Water Act and related programs, and support policies and practices that address stormwater and water conservation concerns in Alabama, Tennessee, and portions of other states in the previously mentioned river basins.

title: Southeastern Rivers and Streams Support Fund
description: The Southeastern Rivers and Streams Support Fund of the World Wildlife Fund, a global conservation organization, builds the capacity of freshwater conservation organizations in the southeastern United States by providing small grants and related technical assistance. This grant increase, and associated grant period extension, will enable the World Wildlife Fund to continue to provide such small grants while also working to recruit new donors to underwrite the small grants program.

title: Community-Based Organizations, Gender and Water Provision
description: The Mvula Trust partners with government to ensure access to safe and sustainable water services for mainly poor, rural communities. Recently, the trust launched a project between local governments and communities wherein community-based organizations are contracted by the municipalities as water service providers, with a strong emphasis on ensuring that women participate in the process. This grant will enable the trust to continue implementing the project and support replication of the project in other localities.The Mvula Trust, founded in 1993, is a non-governmental organization committed to improving the health and welfare of poor and disadvantaged communities in South Africa’s rural and peri-urban areas.

title: Pre-accession Partnerships for Rural Europe
grantee: Swedish Federation of Rural Economy and Agricultural Societies
geographic_focus: Slovenia, Poland, Lithuania, Hungary, Romania, Slovakia, Bulgaria, Latvia, Estonia, Czech Republic
description: The goal of the Pre-accession Partnerships for Rural Europe (PREPARE) program is to help European Union new member states and candidate countries create strong partnerships in order to effectively access and utilize EU funding.This grant will enable the Swedish Federation of Rural Economy and Agricultural Societies to continue working with a network of non-governmental organizations in Western and Eastern Europe to promote multinational exchange focused on rural development. Activities will include in-country training to promote dialogue and cooperation between different actors in rural development; multinational exchanges; and international networking to support rural development efforts.To date, program activities included developing and strengthening national networks in Latvia, the Czech Republic and Lithuania; laying the groundwork for networks in Bulgaria, Romania and Croatia; maintaining a Web site; organizing international gatherings of the PREPARE network in Bulgaria (2004) and in Lithuania (2005); and conducting traveling workshops in Romania, Bulgaria, Latvia and Lithuania directly preceding the network meetings.

title: Pre-accession Partnerships for Rural Europe
geographic_focus: Poland, Turkey, Slovenia, Lithuania, Hungary, Bulgaria, Latvia, Romania, Croatia, Slovakia, Estonia, Czech Republic
description: The program goal is to strengthen civil society in European Union new member states and accession countries. To this end, the Latvian Rural Forum will continue to work with a network of nongovernmental organizations in Western and Eastern Europe to promote multinational exchange focused on rural development. This program will help the European Union new member states and candidate countries create strong partnerships in order to access and utilize European Union funding effectively. During the grant period, the grantee will promote dialogue and cooperation between different actors in rural development, facilitate multinational exchanges, and support international networking for rural development. Past project results include developing strong national rural development networks in Eastern Europe, strengthening international cooperation, and strengthening national networks’ input into European-level rural policy development. Since its establishment in 2005, the grantee has been promoting sustainable rural development policies and providing services to over 80 member organizations in Latvia.

title: Pre-accession Partnerships for Rural Europe
geographic_focus: Hungary, Turkey, Slovenia, Romania, Belarus, Serbia, Slovakia, Czech Republic, North Macedonia, Latvia, Estonia, Lithuania, Croatia, Kosovo, Poland, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, Albania, Bulgaria

Past project results include developing strong national rural development networks in Eastern Europe, strengthening international cooperation, and strengthening national networks’ input into European-level rural policy development. title: DART Organizers Institute
grantee: Direct Action and Research Training Center (DART)
description: The greatest need identified in the field of community organizing is for additional trained organizers, a professional role that demands a sophisticated and disciplined skill set, including the ability to develop and challenge leaders, identify and facilitate training needs, analyze social and economic conditions, learn about a community’s local history, develop hundreds of relationships across all sectors of a community, and lead critical evaluation and reflection sessions on the organization’s development and work. This grant will support a response to this need by funding the Organizers Institute of the Direct Action and Research Training Center.

title: DART Organizers Institute
grantee: Direct Action and Research Training Center (DART)
description: The greatest need identified in the field of community organizing is for additional trained organizers, a professional role that demands a sophisticated and disciplined skill set including the ability to: develop and challenge leaders; identify and facilitate training needs; analyze social and economic conditions; learn a community’s local history; develop hundreds of relationships across all sectors of a community; and lead critical evaluation and reflection sessions on the organization’s development and work. This grant will support a response to this need by funding an organizers institute founded by the Direct Action and Research Training Center.

title: DART Organizers Institute
grantee: Direct Action and Research Training Center (DART)
description: The greatest need identified in the field of community organizing is for additional trained organizers, a professional role that demands a sophisticated and disciplined skill set, including the ability to develop and challenge community leaders, identify and facilitate training needs, analyze social and economic conditions, develop hundreds of relationships across all sectors of a community, and lead critical evaluation and reflection sessions on the organization’s development and work. This grant will support a response to this need by funding the Organizers Institute sponsored by the Direct Action and Research Training Center.

title: DART Organizers Institute
grantee: Direct Action and Research Training Center (DART)
geographic_focus: South Carolina, Ohio, Michigan, Florida, Kentucky
description: The greatest need identified in the field of community organizing is for additional trained organizers, a professional role that demands a sophisticated and disciplined skill set, including the ability to develop and challenge community leaders, identify and facilitate training needs, analyze social and economic conditions, develop hundreds of relationships across all sectors of a community, and lead critical evaluation and reflection sessions on the grantee’s development and work. The DART Organizers Institute, sponsored by the Direct Action and Research Training Center (DART), has an excellent record in responding to this need. This grant increase will support the expansion of the institute to include two full training cycles in 2012.

title: DART Organizers Institute
grantee: Direct Action and Research Training Center (DART)
description: The greatest need identified in the field of community organizing is for additional trained organizers, a professional role that demands a sophisticated and disciplined skill set, including the ability to develop and challenge leaders, identify and facilitate training needs, analyze social and economic conditions, learn a community’s local history, develop hundreds of relationships across all sectors of a community, and lead critical evaluation and reflection sessions on the grantee’s development and work. This grant will provide continued support to the DART Organizers Institute conducted by Direct Action and Research Training Center (DART).

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide two years of general purposes support to the American Arab Heritage Council, legally recognized as the American International Forum. In recent years, this organization has developed from a network of volunteers into a nonprofit with permanent staff and has expanded its educational outreach and cultural programs. Activities of the organization include a variety of seminars, educational outreach activities, and services intended for Arab Americans. These programs aim to promote better understanding and tolerance and prevent backlash toward Arab Americans and Muslims in the Flint area.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will enable NPower Michigan to expand and improve services by leveraging partnerships with other organizations. In 2006, NPower Michigan and the Michigan Nonprofit Association will begin sharing office space in Detroit, merge together a membership base of 850 nonprofits and jointly distribute a monthly newsletter. In addition, promising collaborative ventures have been established with New Horizons (basic computer training), Microsoft, PMV Tech, Accenture and NuSoft Solutions. Nonprofits in Michigan will benefit by receiving private sector technology expertise guided by NPower consultants familiar with the mission-driven focus and context of the nonprofit sector.

title: ECA-Iberia Campaign
description: EURONATURA has taken the lead in assisting Spanish and Portuguese environment and development non-governmental organizations in their work on reform of each country’s export credit agencies. Since 2001, the work of Iberian organizations to address export credit agency reform has grown. The main goal of this project is to encourage the Portuguese and Spanish export credit agencies to require environmental impact assessments of all proposed projects; disclose relevant information; and adopt environmental and social criteria for their project financing. To achieve these goals, during the grant period, EURONATURA will undertake research on Iberian export credit agency investments; enhance knowledge and understanding of Iberian public investment in Latin America and Africa; and encourage Portuguese and Spanish government officials to promote reform of Iberian export credit agencies.

title: ECA-Iberia Campaign
description: EURONATURA has taken the lead in assisting Spanish and Portuguese environment and development nongovernmental organizations in their work on reform of each country’s export credit agencies. The main goal of this project is to encourage the Portuguese and Spanish export credit agencies to require environmental impact assessments of all proposed projects, disclose relevant information, and adopt environmental and social criteria for their project financing. This grant increase will cover additional costs associated with the production of a report on Portuguese and Spanish export credit agencies and increased personnel costs during the grant period extension.

title: General Purposes
description: The mission of the Information Centre is to support the development of southern Slovakia by providing a wide range of services to non-governmental organizations (NGOs), local municipalities and small entrepreneurs.This grant will enable the center to improve the quality of its services; strengthen its role in local policy development; and increase the effectiveness of a network of similar information centers in southern Slovakia.During the past two years, the center provided information, training and consultancy services, as well as regular meeting and networking opportunities, to more than 270 NGOs; established the Southern Slovak Civic Information Network; and worked to combat the isolation of southern Slovakia by participating in various international programs.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant increase is for the general purposes of Environmental Law Alliance Worldwide including costs of its annual international meeting. This meeting will bring together approximately 60 grassroots environmental professionals from around the world working to reform international financial institutions and strengthen policies to protect public health and the environment. Environmental Law Alliance Worldwide is a network of over 300 local environmental leaders in 60 countries working to protect the environment through the development and enforcement of standards, policy, and law.

title: General Purposes
description: International financial institutions, both public and private, play a key role in financing energy and infrastructure projects around the world that will have important impacts on the environment. With this grant, Environmental Law Alliance Worldwide will continue to provide legal, scientific, technical, and organizational support to its network of local leaders, who are monitoring and analyzing energy and infrastructure investments. Support will also enable the grantee to convene environmental leaders from around the world for the 2009 Environmental Law Alliance Worldwide Annual Meeting, where the grantee’s partners will share lessons on working with international financial institutions and gain skills that help them protect critical ecosystems and the communities that depend on those ecosystems.

title: General Purposes
description: International financial institutions, both public and private, play a key role in financing energy and infrastructure projects around the world that will have important impacts on the environment. With this grant, Environmental Law Alliance Worldwide will continue to provide legal, scientific, technical, and organizational support to its network of local leaders, who are monitoring and analyzing energy and infrastructure investments and working to ensure that impacts to communities and the environment are considered in adopting and reforming the policies that regulate international carbon finance. Support will also enable the grantee to convene environmental leaders from around the world for the 2010 and 2011 Environmental Law Alliance Worldwide annual meetings.

title: General Purposes
description: International financial institutions, both public and private, play a key role in financing energy and infrastructure projects around the world that will have important impacts on the environment. With this grant, Environmental Law Alliance Worldwide will continue to provide legal, scientific, technical, and organizational support to its network of local leaders, who are monitoring and analyzing energy and infrastructure investments. Support will target leaders in emerging economies such as Brazil, China, India, and South Africa and will provide them with the tools they need to address the priorities and impacts of new dynamics in global finance. This grant will also enable the grantee to convene environmental leaders from around the world for the 2012 Environmental Law Alliance Worldwide annual meetings.

title: General Purposes
description: International financial institutions, both public and private, play a key role in financing energy and infrastructure projects around the world that will have important impacts on the environment. With this grant increase, Environmental Law Alliance Worldwide will continue to provide legal, scientific, technical, and organizational support to its network of local leaders, who are monitoring and analyzing energy and infrastructure investments. Support will target leaders in emerging economies such as Brazil, China, India, and South Africa and will provide them with the tools they need to address the priorities and impacts of new dynamics in global finance. This grant increase will enable the grantee to provide a training internship for a young advocate working on international environmental advocacy in Colombia.

title: General Purposes
description: As the world population and middle class expand, so does public investment in energy and infrastructure. Investment by national development banks, particularly in Brazil and China, have surpassed World Bank lending and are driving energy and infrastructure development in Latin America, Asia, and Africa often without the application of strong social and environmental safeguards. With this grant, Environmental Law Alliance Worldwide will strengthen its network of experts to provide legal, scientific, technical, and organizational support to local leaders, who are monitoring and analyzing energy and infrastructure investments. This grant will also enable the grantee to convene environmental leaders from around the world for the 2014 Environmental Law Alliance Worldwide annual meeting.

title: General Purposes
description: International financial institutions, and increasingly national development banks, play a key role in financing energy and infrastructure projects around the world, which have both social and environmental impacts. This general purpose grant increase to Environmental Law Alliance Worldwide will help support the 2014 annual meeting, which brings together scientific and environmental leaders to share experiences, discuss the state-of-the-art in legal and scientific standards worldwide, and collaborate on new strategies to address energy resource extraction and its finance. This increase will enable the grantee to co-host the annual meeting in Germany.

title: General Purposes
description: The Environmental Law Alliance Worldwide works with public interest attorneys around the world to strengthen environmental and social standards for development finance of large-scale energy and infrastructure projects. Investments by national development banks, particularly in Brazil and China, have surpassed World Bank lending and are driving energy and infrastructure investment in developing countries, often without the application of strong social and environmental safeguards. With this grant, the grantee will provide legal, scientific, and organizational support to environmental leaders to ensure that development finance respects the highest environmental and social standards.

title: General Purposes
description: The Environmental Law Alliance Worldwide is a nongovernmental global alliance of attorneys and scientists who collaborate to protect the environment and communities. This general purpose grant will support the grantee to provide networking, legal, and scientific services to its members in 80 countries.

title: Development of Products and Services
description: After several years of preparatory work, 3iG International Interfaith Investment Group (3iG) was established as an independent, multi-faith nonprofit organization in 2005. Its mission is to carry out activities that promote and facilitate faith investments in sustainable development. This grant will enable 3iG to develop education and outreach services, organize conferences, create an Internet portal and initiate a proactive brokerage for sustainable investments.

title: Development of Products and Services
description: This renewal grant will provide partial support for the development of products and services by 3iG International Interfaith Investment Group. Created to promote the ethical and moral transformation of the asset management practices and investment activities of the world’s faith communities, the organization has the potential to influence the reallocation of hundreds of billions, possibly trillions, of dollars over the next several decades. Major activities during the grant period include enhancing the organization’s Web site as a clearinghouse of best practices and data on investing responsibly; expanding a help desk to advise on proactive investment policies; organizing workshops and meetings; and increasing the number and diversity of faith group members. After four years of incubation by the Alliance of Religions and Conservation, the grantee became an independent organization based in the Netherlands in 2005.

title: General Purposes
description: Satyagraha produces a monthly newspaper published in KwaZulu-Natal that aims to help communities in the region move away from the racial and ethnic divisions of the past. Based on the values of Mahatma Gandhi, the newspaper advocates peace, tolerance and nonviolence. One of its main areas of focus is Indo-African relations in a part of South Africa that continues to experience tensions and conflict between the Indian and African communities. This grant will enable the organization to continue publishing the monthly newspaper; improving its Web site to make it more reader-friendly and increase distribution; introducing a Zulu section of the newspaper, which is the main African language in the region; electronically documenting interviews and material; and developing teaching and other resources for distribution and wider dissemination. In addition, the organization will use the centenary of the birth of Satyagraha – the form of passive resistance and nonviolent struggle pioneered by Mahatma Gandhi in 1906 in South Africa – to highlight its work and organize a number of workshops, seminars and lectures.

title: General Purposes
description: Satyagraha – In Pursuit of Truth is a nonprofit organization that works through the media to transform society to move away from the racial and ethnic divisions of the past. It publishes a monthly newspaper that promotes a culture of nonviolence, peace, national and religious reconciliation, and tolerance. This grant will continue to support the monthly publication of the newsletter to promote reconciliation and nation building. Other activities will include outreach programs to schools, human rights awareness-raising campaigns, facilitating the online availability of the newspaper, and developing a curriculum on peace and nonviolence for high school and tertiary learners.

title: General Purposes
description: Satyagraha – In Pursuit of Truth is a nonprofit organization that works to transform society and promotes racial reconciliation and ethnic tolerance through the media. For the last six years, Satyagraha has published a monthly newspaper in Durban, KwaZulu-Natal, that promotes a culture of nonviolence, historic knowledge, civic and community awareness, and diversity. This grant will continue to support the monthly publication of the newspaper as well as Satyagraha’s other activities including a high school outreach and youth program, human rights awareness campaigns, and the development of a student research library.

title: General Purposes
description: The Cahaba River is the longest remaining free-flowing river in the Mobile River basin and is one of the most biologically diverse rivers in North America. Founded in 1988, the Cahaba River Society works to restore and protect the Cahaba River watershed and its rich diversity of life. This grant will enable the society to continue efforts to improve land-use planning in the watershed; implement environmental education programs; provide technical assistance to local planning boards; reduce various forms of pollution to the river; and build its own organizational capacity.With previous support, the society began implementing recommendations made within the Upper Cahaba Watershed Study and provided education and outreach programs.

title: Civil Rights Project: Education Initiative
description: This grant will provide partial support to Harvard University for the Harvard Civil Rights Project: Education Initiative. Through the initiative, the Harvard Civil Rights Project provides research and analysis on the civil rights dimension of two major interrelated education policy challenges — the impact of No Child Left Behind and the dropout/graduation crisis. In the most recent phase of this initiative, the Harvard Civil Rights Project has geared its analysis toward helping state- and community-level advocates and legislators promote research-based policy recommendations that result in more equitable outcomes and greater opportunities for poor and minority youth. During the next phase of the initiative, the Harvard Civil Rights Project will develop a model dropout accountability statute for states; extend its work into the southwest (particularly in the state of Texas); monitor the reauthorization of No Child Left Behind; and collaborate with other leading education and policy groups in building supports for greater educational opportunities for poor and minority youth.

title: Civil Rights Project: Education Initiative
description: This grant will provide support to the University of California – Los Angeles for the Civil Rights Project: Education Initiative. Through the initiative, the Civil Rights Project provides research and analysis on the civil rights dimension of two major, interrelated education policy challenges – – the impact of No Child Left Behind and the dropout crisis. During the next phase of this initiative, the Civil Rights Project will continue to develop a model dropout accountability statute for states, extend its research and analysis, monitor the reauthorization of No Child Left Behind, and collaborate with other leading education and policy groups in building supports for greater educational opportunities for poor and minority youth.

title: Information and Training Programme
geographic_focus: Hungary, Bulgaria, Slovakia, Lithuania, Poland, Czech Republic, Estonia, Slovenia, Romania, Latvia
description: The program goal is to raise awareness among nongovernmental organizations in Central/Eastern Europe and the former Soviet Union about the implications and opportunities of European Union accession. Building upon its extensive experience in Brussels and throughout the European Union, the European Citizen Action Service will continue to provide organizations in Central/Eastern Europe and the former Soviet Union with relevant information, training opportunities, and study visits regarding European Union policies, legislation, and funding procedures. The European Citizen Action Service launched this program in 2002, and to date, more than 480 individuals from 220 organizations in 16 countries have benefited from this program. Since its establishment in 1990, the grantee has been strengthening the participation of nongovernmental organizations on European Union policy development, promoting citizens’ free movement rights, and campaigning for transparency in the European Union institutions.

title: Afterschool Mentoring Resources
description: This grant will enable the MENTOR/National Mentoring Partnership to provide national mentoring guidelines for programs, including afterschool programs across the country. Through MentorPRO – a computer-based system used to track, collect and analyze information – MENTOR/National Mentoring Partnership will emphasize accountability and empower mentor programs to track their adherence to promising practices. This work will build on the Elements of Effective Practices toolkit, which provides specific guidelines to programs. Emphasis will be placed on addressing the needs of immigrant youth, reaching hard-to-reach youth, and ensuring that programs address multicultural differences between youth and adults.

title: Afterschool Mentoring Resources
description: This grant will continue to support MENTOR/National Mentoring Partnership in providing national mentoring guidelines to programs, including afterschool programs across the country. Specific emphasis will be placed on addressing the needs of immigrant and refugee youth, and older adults who are important resources for helping to close the mentoring gap.

title: General Purposes
grantee: National Center for Black Philanthropy, Inc.
description: The National Center for Black Philanthropy encourages giving and volunteerism among African Americans, and educates the public on African American philanthropy.This grant will enable the center to convene three regional meetings in 2006 and plan its Sixth National Conference on Black Philanthropy, to be held in Washington, D.C. in 2007. The center will also continue its endowment training workshop for African-American organizations in conjunction with its conferences; expand its Black Business and Philanthropy Initiative; develop partnerships to expand and market philanthropic giving in the black community; and work on efforts to expand membership and self-generated income.During the past two years, the center convened five regional meetings as well as its Fifth National Conference on Black Philanthropy; promoted increased participation through its Black Business and Philanthropy Initiative; and continued its various endowment training and public education programs.

title: General Purposes
grantee: National Center for Black Philanthropy, Inc.
description: This general purpose grant renewal will help the National Center for Black Philanthropy, Inc., an organization that has encouraged giving and volunteerism among African Americans and educated the public on African-American philanthropy since 1997. During the previous grant period, the organization was able to hold three regional conferences and one national conference, continue its research on black business owners’ giving habits, and provide philanthropy workshops and endowment training. With continued support, the National Center for Black Philanthropy will convene its 14th regional meeting in 2008, and hold its seventh National Conference on Black Philanthropy in 2009. In addition to continuing its endowment and fundraising training workshops for African-American organizations, running its Black Business and Philanthropy program, and publishing a book titled “A Philanthropic Covenant with Black America”, the National Center for Black Philanthropy will focus on building its funding, management, and programmatic capabilities to ensure its long-term survival.

title: Training of Local Government Councillors and Communities in KwaZulu-Natal
description: The Democracy Development Program supports democracy at the local level in KwaZulu-Natal through capacity building of local government and civil society institutions to ensure that both are prepared for meaningful participation in local decisionmaking processes. This grant will enable the program to continue promoting community participation and establish a culture of democracy and cooperation at the local level through training and capacity building for ward committee members and municipal officials.Since 2002, the program has conducted training for ward committees — the formal structures through which communities participate in local government — for three district municipalities in the KwaZulu-Natal province, assisting them in dealing effectively with their challenges.

title: Training of Local Government Councillors and Communities in KwaZulu-Natal
description: The Democracy Development Program works with civil society and government institutions in the KwaZulu-Natal province to promote citizen participation, a human rights culture, and good governance. Mott’s support will promote community participation and entrench a culture of democracy and cooperation at the local level through the training of ward committee members (the elected structures that represent community interest at local government level), traditional structures, municipal councilors, and officials. This grant will support the Democracy Development Program to continue to promote community participation and to work with the same community and local government structures. It will use the lessons from the first phase of the program to inform its interventions with the various stakeholders.

title: Training of Local Government Councillors and Communities in KwaZulu-Natal
description: The Democracy Development Programme works with civil society and government institutions in KwaZulu-Natal province in South Africa to promote citizen participation in local governance processes, a human rights culture, and good governance. This grant supports community participation and a culture of democracy and cooperation at the local level through the training of ward committee members, the elected structures that represent community interest at local government level, and municipal councilors and officials. The grantee initiated this project in 2004, and to date, 56 training workshops have been held with various municipal and civil society structures. Over the next two years, major activities will include revising the book “Partners in Transformation”, conducting and evaluating training workshops for municipal and community representatives, and facilitating multistakeholder community forums.

title: Training of Local Government Councillors and Communities in KwaZulu-Natal
description: The Democracy Development Programme works to promote democracy in the KwaZulu-Natal province of South Africa by encouraging community participation in local decisionmaking processes and good governance by local authorities. The Training of Local Government Councillors and Communities in KwaZulu-Natal project supports community participation processes and builds a culture of democracy and cooperation at the local level through training local government officials, traditional leaders, and ward committee members elected to represent the interests of communities at the local level. The project also creates spaces for dialogue between communities and their local municipal representatives. Mott support over the past two years assisted the grantee to set up engagement forums to improve communication between communities and municipalities in the province. Over the next two years, the grantee will continue to promote community participation in local governance processes, strengthen governance among partner municipalities, and expand its work to the Western Cape province.

title: Training of Local Government Councillors and Communities in KwaZulu-Natal
description: The Democracy Development Programme was established in 1993 to promote citizen participation, human rights, and good governance in the KwaZulu-Natal province in South Africa. It works with local government institutions, civil society organizations, and communities to encourage accountability and civic engagement. Past support has enabled the grantee to train ward committee members (elected officials representing community interests at local government), traditional leaders, civil society leaders, and communities in order to promote social cohesion, cooperation, and a culture of democracy and inclusiveness. This grant will allow the grantee to continue providing training that encourages mutual accountability and dialogue between the local governance structures and other sectors of society. It will also raise public awareness of citizens’ rights and responsibilities through media and other platforms.

title: Training of Local Government Councillors and Communities in KwaZulu-Natal
description: The Democracy Development Programme was established in 1993 to promote democracy, good governance, and citizen participation in the democratic process in South Africa. It works in the KwaZulu-Natal Province and provides training to municipal officials and communities to improve their understanding of their rights and responsibilities. Past support has enabled the grantee to implement training programs, enhance their training material, and facilitate dialogue between political and traditional leadership in communities to build cohesion. This grant will enable the grantee to continue providing training to communities and officials to deepen their understanding of the role of local government and facilitate dialogue between various community structures. In addition, the grantee will partner with local community radio stations to increase its footprint and educate communities about the role of local government within communities.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will enable the Spirals Trust to continue to work with communities, groups and individuals on issues of identity and values to encourage transformation, healing and social justice. Emphasis will be on restoring identities that were violated by the injustices of the past and promoting human rights, dignity and equality. Key areas of work over the next two years will include a youth empowerment program, community-based organizations working on issues of HIV/AIDS and training educators in the Eastern Cape.Specific activities during the past two years included running an internship program to train staff from other nonprofits in the region in the methods of conflict mediation, facilitation and healing; designing and facilitating a curriculum in education and life skills for youth, in partnership with the University of Rhodes in Grahamstown in the Eastern Cape; conducting workshops on youth empowerment in many of the rural areas in the Eastern Cape; and organizing training programs for resident leaders at Rhodes University. In 2005, Spirals Trust also conducted a comprehensive external evaluation of its work and developed a plan for its future activities. The Spirals Trust works with communities in the Eastern Cape that were affected by violence and conflict during the years of struggle against apartheid.

title: Joint Tax Policy Center
description: The Urban Institute-Brookings Institution’s Joint Tax Policy Center produces objective, timely and accessible information to help policymakers and other stakeholders identify and evaluate current and emerging tax policy options. The center’s long-term goal is to help inform and shape the terms of debates where tax policy is considered.This grant will enable the center to study the migration of federal income security and other social policy from spending programs to the tax code and the implications of such shifts for low-income families.In the four years since its creation, the center has developed into a primary information source on tax policy for journalists. In 2005, the center was cited in more than 350 major media articles including 69 citations in the New York Times, the Wall Street Journal and the Washington Post.

title: Joint Tax Policy Center
description: Tax policy continues to have a central place on the national agenda and, given long-term deficit projections, is likely to stay there for the foreseeable future. Moreover, the nation’s social safety net is provided increasingly in the form of tax subsidies, such as the earned income tax credit, rather than traditional public assistance programs. This grant will provide ongoing support to the Urban Institute’s and its partner, the Brookings Institution’s Joint Tax Policy Center. Using its own tax model and other resources, the center produces timely analyses of current tax proposals and long-term analyses of systemic tax and related spending issues and communicates these results to the public and policymakers in a timely and innovative manner. In the long run, the center’s goal is to help shape the terms of the debate in which tax policy is considered. Mott Foundation funds will be directed toward studying the migration of federal income security and other social policy from spending programs to the tax code and the implications of such shifts for low-income families.

title: Joint Tax Policy Center
description: Tax policy continues to command attention on national and state policy agendas, and given long-term deficit projections, it is likely to stay there for the foreseeable future. Moreover, a growing segment of the nation’s social safety net is provided in the form of tax subsidies — notably the earned income and child tax credits. This grant will provide ongoing support to the Urban Institute and the Brookings Institution’s Joint Tax Policy Center. Using its own tax model and other data sources, the center produces timely analyses of tax and related spending issues, and communicates these results to the public and policymakers in a timely and innovative manner. In the long run, the center’s goal is to help shape the terms of debates in which tax policy is considered. Among other areas of focus, Mott funds will be directed toward studying the migration of federal income security and other social policy, from spending programs to the tax code, and the implications of such shifts for low-income families.

title: Joint Tax Policy Center
description: Tax policy continues to figure centrally in the nation’s key economic decisions. Although recent spending reductions and revenue increases have reduced near-term deficits, long-term imbalances remain a central concern. Renewal grant support will enable the Urban Institute’s Joint Tax Policy Center to continue providing policymakers, tax analysts, the media, and the public with accurate, unbiased, timely, and understandable information about the tax policy choices facing our nation. Using its own tax model and other resources, the center produces timely analyses of current tax proposals and long-term analyses of systemic tax and related spending issues and communicates these results to the public and policymakers in a timely and innovative manner. In the long run, the center’s goal is to help shape the terms of the debate in which tax policy is considered. The Urban Institute — a Washington, DC-based think tank — gathers data, conducts research, evaluates programs, offers technical assistance overseas, and educates Americans on social and economic issues to foster sound public policy and effective government.

title: Joint Tax Policy Center
description: Tax policy continues to have a central place on the national agenda and, given long-term deficit projections, is likely to stay there for the foreseeable future. Moreover, the nation’s social safety net increasingly is provided in the form of tax subsidies, such as the earned income tax credit, rather than traditional public assistance programs. This grant will provide ongoing support to the Urban Institute and the Brookings Institution’s Joint Tax Policy Center. Using its own tax model and other resources, the center produces timely analyses of current tax proposals and longer-term analyses of systemic tax and related spending issues and communicates these results to the public and policymakers in a timely and innovative manner. In the long run, the center’s goal is to help shape the terms of the debate in which tax policy is considered. Mott funds will be directed toward studying the migration of federal income security and other social policy from spending programs to the tax code and the implications of such shifts for low-income families.

title: Managing Water Resources for Today and Tomorrow
description: In December 2005, the Great Lakes governors issued the proposed Great Lakes Compact, a new, ecologically based approach to managing water withdrawals and diversions throughout the portion of the Great Lakes basin in the United States. Clean Wisconsin, a statewide environmental group with a long-standing interest in Great Lakes issues, was engaged in the policy discussions leading up to the release of the draft interstate compact and has been involved in subsequent work to implement the compact. With renewed support from Mott, Clean Wisconsin will continue efforts to promote broad engagement in adoption of the compact, as well as help create and implement related state-level water conservation policies.

title: Managing Water Resources for Today and Tomorrow
description: For nearly 40 years, Clean Wisconsin has played a leadership role on statewide environmental issues, with a sustained interest in maintaining the health of the Great Lakes. With previous Mott support, the grantee worked to support a comprehensive regional policy for managing Great Lakes water withdrawals and diversions that resulted in the passage of the Great Lakes Compact. Clean Wisconsin is now turning its attention to ensuring full implementation of the compact at the state level. This grant increase, and associated grant period extension, will allow the grantee to help develop a solid foundation for compact implementation in the state and inform policies that will reduce future demand for Great Lakes water.

title: Managing Water Resources for Today and Tomorrow
description: Clean Wisconsin is a leader on statewide environmental issues in Wisconsin and has had a sustained interest in maintaining the health of the Great Lakes for many years. With previous Mott support, the grantee worked to support a comprehensive regional policy for managing Great Lakes water withdrawals and diversions that resulted in the passage of the Great Lakes Compact. Clean Wisconsin is now turning its attention to ensuring full implementation of the compact as well as the development and implementation of related state-level policies to protect groundwater resources and promote water conservation at the municipal level.

title: Center to Serve Historically Black Colleges and Universities
initiative: Historically and Predominantly Black Colleges and Universities
geographic_focus: Louisiana, Kentucky, Virginia, Florida, South Carolina, Mississippi, Alabama, Texas, Tennessee, Georgia, North Carolina
description: This grant renewal will provide partial support to the Southern Education Foundation for its Center to Serve Historically Black Colleges and Universities. As in the first years of the project, accreditation will continue to provide the framework for research, technical assistance, and training for leaders of black colleges. From 2003 to 2007, the grantee convened expert advisory committees, organized informational workshops and meetings, commissioned research, provided technical assistance, and awarded minigrants to schools approaching accreditation review. Over the next three years, the grantee will continue this work with a particular focus on measuring student learning outcomes, governance, and technology policy and practice. In 2007, the Southern Education Foundation celebrates the 140th year of its founding. It is the South’s only regional nonprofit focused exclusively on improving education for low-income students and communities from pre-school through higher education.

title: Center to Serve Historically Black Colleges and Universities
initiative: Historically and Predominantly Black Colleges and Universities
geographic_focus: Alabama, South Carolina, Florida, Texas, Mississippi, Georgia, Louisiana, Kentucky, Tennessee, Virginia, North Carolina
description: This grant renewal will provide partial support to the Southern Education Foundation for its Center to Serve Historically Black Colleges and Universities. From 2003 to 2007, the grantee convened expert advisory committees, organized informational workshops and meetings, commissioned research, provided technical assistance, and awarded minigrants to schools approaching accreditation review. From 2007 to 2010, the grantee continued this work with a particular focus on measuring student learning outcomes, governance, and technology policy and practice. With this renewal, these activities will continue, along with an initiative to reach out to Hispanic serving institutions to help them with accreditation.
