title: Organizers' Forum
description: The Organizers’ Forum, a project of the Tides Center, was conceived by a group of highly experienced community organizers from several networks across the United States as a means for creating opportunities for experienced organizers to continue their professional development. The Organizers’ Forum offers a setting in which experienced organizers can reflect on their work, develop a set of high standards and expectations for the profession, and develop new skills and mentoring relationships.

title: Education Organizing Study
geographic_focus: Philadelphia, New York, Los Angeles, Chicago, Oakland, Milwaukee, Miami, Austin
description: This grant will support the completion of a six-year study designed to provide a longitudinal exploration of the contribution of community organizing to school improvement and increased student achievement.The study focuses on the work of eight sites that have demonstrated the ability to produce school improvement over the past decade and will document a range of ways in which community organizing strategies produce concrete educational improvements for low-income children. Findings from this study will be invaluable for promoting effective partnerships between parents, community organizations and schools in low-income communities.The original grantee for this study was New York University’s Institute for Education and Social Policy. The principal investigator has moved to Brown University’s Annenberg Institute for School Reform.

title: Education Organizing Study
geographic_focus: Philadelphia, Chicago, Milwaukee, Miami, Austin, Oakland, New York, Los Angeles
description: This grant to Brown University supports the completion of a six-year study designed to provide a longitudinal exploration of the contribution of community organizing to school improvement and increased student achievement. The study focuses on the work of eight sites that have demonstrated the ability to produce school improvement over the past decade and will document a range of ways in which community organizing strategies produce concrete educational improvements for low-income children. The findings from this study will be invaluable for promoting effective partnerships between parents, community organizations, and schools in low-income communities. This grant increase will support the expenses associated with a convening of representatives from the eight sites, along with the research team and advisory committee.

title: Education Organizing Study
geographic_focus: Los Angeles, Austin, New York, Philadelphia, Chicago, Miami, Milwaukee, Oakland
description: The purpose of this grant increase to Brown University is to support a six-year study designed to provide a longitudinal exploration of the contribution of community organizing to school improvement and increased student achievement. This grant increase, and associated one-year extension, provides funding for a dissemination and communications strategy, message development, conferences and convenings, media promotion, and staff support.

title: Study on Education Organizing and Academic Improvement
description: This grant will support the Eastern Pennsylvania Organizing Project’s education work focused on school safety, reading, small schools, professional development and teacher distribution. In addition, funding will enable the project to participate in a Mott-funded study to examine the contribution of education organizing to reform efforts in low-performing districts and schools.During the past two years, the project continued to negotiate with the school district over a small schools policy; successfully advocated for the replacement of one of the oldest school facilities in the city; hosted a three-day training event that is now required for principal candidates to prepare them for understanding and working with the community; and participated in a coalition working for distribution of more qualified teachers in distressed schools.

title: Study on Education Organizing and Academic Improvement
description: People Acting for Community Together (PACT) – a congregation-based community organizing group in Miami, Florida – is one of eight sites participating in Mott’s study to explore the contribution of community organizing in education reform of low-performing districts and schools.In addition to supporting PACT’s participation in the study, this grant will support its overall education organizing activities, which is now focused on reading improvement, preschool access and quality, and teacher quality.

title: Study on Education Organizing and Academic Improvement
description: This grant will support the Austin Interfaith Sponsoring Committee’s study on education organizing work which will focus on developing leaders, including parents, teachers and principals; continuing to work with national experts on the provision of Learning Academies for pastors, parents, teachers and community leaders; and developing the “teacher pipeline” project to help long-term school employees become certified teachers. In addition to supporting the group’s community-driven education reform efforts, this grant will enable the organization to participate in the Foundation’s study to explore the role of education organizing in education reform efforts in low-performing districts and schools.Austin Interfaith, founded in 1985 and affiliated with the Industrial Areas Foundation, works to develop leaders and build power to address issues identified by the community.

title: Study on Education Organizing and Academic Improvement
description: This grant will provide tie-off support to Austin Interfaith Sponsoring Committee for the organization’s education organizing work. For the past several years, Austin Interfaith Sponsoring Committee has focused on developing leaders, including parents, teachers, and principals; working with national experts to develop and sponsor Learning Academies for pastors, parents, teachers, and community leaders; and developing a “teacher pipeline” project to help long-term school employees become certified teachers. In addition, the organization also participated in the Foundation’s study to explore the role of education organizing in education reform efforts in low-performing districts and schools.

title: Strengthening the Voice of Civil Society in the Global Arena
grantee: Institute for Agriculture and Trade Policy
initiative: Reform of International Finance and Trade
description: Due to the complexities of trade in the context of globalization, there is a growing sense that the reliance on tariff reduction as the main path to opening markets is a strategy that is no longer viable. The Institute for Agriculture and Trade Policy works to address these concerns and ensure that multilateral institutions contribute to sustainable development.This grant will enable the institute to continue monitoring global trade discussions; promote approaches to fair trade; work to ensure that new biofuel strategies contribute to sustainable development; support efforts to ensure that water sector investments promote equitable and sustainable water use; and encourage the democratization of global governance.During the past two years, the institute has been engaged in key global trade discussions and the processes leading up to them, including disseminating information, writing and publishing papers, planning joint strategy meetings with non-governmental organization networks, and hosting events and public debates. In each of these areas, it worked together with local, national and international coalitions.

title: Strengthening the Voice of Civil Society in the Global Arena
grantee: Institute for Agriculture and Trade Policy
initiative: Reform of International Finance and Trade
description: The need for a multilateral trading system that is democratic, accountable, and participatory, as well as one that respects and promotes fundamental human rights, the environment, and sustainable development, has never been more apparent. The dismal state of the Doha Round of trade negotiations at the World Trade Organization is a clear signal that the intended benefits from international trade and investment rules have not been achieved. The Institute for Agriculture and Trade Policy has worked to address these concerns and ensure that multilateral institutions contribute to sustainable development. During the grant period, the grantee will continue to monitor global trade discussions, promote approaches to fair trade, work to ensure that new biofuel strategies contribute to sustainable development, and work to democratize global governance.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen the nonprofit sector in Northwest Russia. The Saint-Petersburg NGO Development Centre will focus on two key areas of activity. First, a resource center function will provide ongoing consulting, training, and other support services to the sector while also promoting partnership activities among nonprofits and between this sector and local or regional governments. The second area of focus will be a philanthropy development program aimed at developing individual giving and corporate social responsibility in this region. The center has been instrumental in increasing the professionalism of community-based organizations and, through its “Kind Peter” charitable giving campaign, has introduced new approaches to individual giving to Saint-Petersburg. Established in 1994, the Saint-Petersburg NGO Development Centre is one of the leading support organizations contributing to the growth of the nonprofit sector and philanthropy in Russia.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen the nonprofit sector in Northwest Russia. The Saint-Petersburg NGO Development Centre will focus on two key areas of activity. First, a resource center function will provide ongoing consulting, training, and other support services to the sector while also promoting partnership activities among nonprofits and between the sector and local or regional governments. The second area of focus will be a philanthropy development program aimed at developing individual giving and corporate social responsibility in this region. In 2008, through its “Kind Peter” charitable giving campaign, the grantee was able to encourage over 1,200 residents of Saint Petersburg to contribute over $500,000 in cash and in-kind contributions to support community, charitable initiatives. Established in 1994, the Saint-Petersburg NGO Development Centre is one of the leading support organizations contributing to the growth of the nonprofit sector and philanthropy in Russia.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen the nonprofit sector in Northwest Russia. The Saint-Petersburg NGO Development Centre will focus on three key areas of activity. First, it will provide ongoing consulting, training, and other support services for both registered organizations and unregistered initiative groups. Second, it will continue work on developing philanthropy and corporate social responsibility in St. Petersburg and beyond. Finally, it will work to promote partnership activities among nonprofits and between the sector and local or regional governments. In 2009-2011, the Kind Peter charitable giving campaign raised over $600,000 in cash and in-kind contributions to support community charitable initiatives. This model was subsequently adopted in four other Russian cities and led to the creation of a community foundation in St. Petersburg. Established in 1994, the Saint-Petersburg NGO Development Centre is one of the leading support organizations contributing to the growth of the nonprofit sector and philanthropy in Russia.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen the nonprofit sector in Northwest Russia. The Saint-Petersburg NGO Development Centre will focus on three key areas of activity. First, it will provide ongoing consulting and training as well as partnership development support for registered organizations and unregistered initiative groups. Second, it will continue to promote philanthropy and corporate social responsibility through its Kind Peter community foundation and festival. Finally, it will work to strengthen its own internal management and governance. In 2011-2013, the Kind Peter charitable giving campaign more than tripled the value of funds raised to over $700,000 in cash and in-kind contributions for community charitable initiatives. In the same period, the grantee led over 100 capacity building events, involving more than 4,000 participants. Established in 1994, the Saint-Petersburg NGO Development Centre is one of the leading support organizations contributing to the growth of the nonprofit sector and philanthropy in Russia.

title: NGO Capacity Building and Networking in Montenegro
description: This grant will enable the United Nations Development Programme in Montenegro to focus on increasing public participation through nonprofit sector involvement in policy development and advocacy on issues of anticorruption. The program will provide small grants and organize training, technical assistance and networking opportunities for community-based citizen groups and national-level advocacy organizations.In 2004-2005, the program successfully mobilized public participation through the nonprofit sector in the formulation of important national policy and strategy documents, including the Development and Poverty Reduction Strategy paper.

title: Securing New York's Water Future
description: In December 2005, the Great Lakes governors released the proposed Great Lakes Compact, which would address all new water withdrawals and diversions within the portion of the basin located in the United States. Going forward, each of the eight Great Lakes states must ratify the compact and establish administrative programs to enact its provisions. Over the past several years, Environmental Advocates of New York, a leading statewide environmental group, has educated the public and decisionmakers in New York about the compact and related issues. With renewal support, the organization will continue its efforts to educate a wide range of constituencies about the compact and related issues through direct public outreach, media work, and opinion leader education.

title: Securing New York's Water Future
description: Since adoption of the Great Lakes Compact in late 2008, Environmental Advocates of New York has been working to help implement the interstate agreement in New York state. With this grant increase and associated grant period extension, the advocates will continue to participate in the development of state rules pertaining to the compact. The organization also will engage in public communication activities aimed at educating policymakers about Great Lakes issues and securing new public funding for Great Lakes restoration.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to promote and develop volunteerism in Hungary. To this end, the Volunteer Center Foundation will strengthen the capacity and outreach of a national network of volunteer centers, improve its training and capacity-building services, increase local and national public awareness about volunteerism, and facilitate joint initiatives of the network of local volunteer centers. In addition, the foundation will strengthen its organizational capacity and financial sustainability. Since its establishment in 2002, the foundation has established a network of local volunteer centers, developed national standards for volunteer management, published studies, and raised public awareness about volunteerism in Hungary.

title: State EITC Initiative
description: According to the U.S. Census Bureau, the federal Earned Income Tax Credit helped 4.8 million people, including 2.6 million children, out of poverty in 2001 – more than any other government program. The success of the plan has led a number of states to enact state Earned Income Tax Credits that supplement the federal credit; in total, 19 states now offer credits that piggyback on the federal credit.This grant will enable the Hatcher Group to provide strategic communications, technical assistance and networking opportunities to nonprofit organizations working in coalitions to establish or expand Earned Income Tax Credit policies at the state level. Specifically, Mott funds will be used to help advocates raise awareness among policymakers, journalists and other stakeholders about Earned Income Tax Credits and their role in alleviating poverty, and to provide easy access to information and materials about effective advocacy through an online information resource center.Since 2002, when this project began, the Hatcher Group has helped organizations in more than 20 states strengthen their strategic communications capacity. The Hatcher Group is a Bethesda, Maryland-based, public affairs firm that works exclusively for foundations and nonprofit organizations on workforce development, welfare and urban social policy issues.

title: State EITC Initiative
description: This grant will enable the Hatcher Group to provide strategic communications technical assistance to nonprofit organizations working in coalitions to establish or expand Earned Income Tax Credit policies at the state level. Specifically, Mott’s funds will be used to help advocates raise awareness among policymakers, journalists, and other key stakeholders about the credit and its role in alleviating poverty. The grantee will also provide advocates with easy access to information and materials about effective advocacy through an online information resource center. Since 2002, when this project began, the grantee has helped groups in over 20 states strengthen their strategic communications capacity. The Hatcher Group is a Bethesda, Maryland-based, for-profit, public affairs firm that works exclusively for foundations and nonprofit organizations on workforce development, welfare, and urban social policy issues.

title: State EITC Initiative
description: This grant will enable the Hatcher Group to provide strategic communications technical assistance to nonprofit organizations working in coalitions to establish or expand the Earned Income Tax Credit, Child Tax Credit, and other tax policies that aid working families. Mott funds will be used to help advocates raise awareness among policymakers, journalists, and other key stakeholders about the credits and their role in alleviating poverty. The grantee will also provide advocates with easy access to information and materials about effective advocacy through an online information resource center. Since 2002, when this project began, the grantee has helped groups in over 20 states strengthen their strategic communications capacity. The Hatcher Group is a Bethesda, Maryland-based, for-profit, public affairs firm that works exclusively for foundations and nonprofit organizations on workforce development, welfare, and urban social policy issues.

title: Women and Local Government Project
geographic_focus: Angola, Botswana, Seychelles, Lesotho, Malawi, Zimbabwe, South Africa, Namibia, Mozambique, Mauritius, Tanzania, Swaziland, Zambia
description: Gender Links conducts research, training, and advocacy to encourage the promotion and attainment of gender equality in South Africa.Funding will enable Gender Links to conduct research on the experiences of women in local government and train municipal councilors on how to integrate gender issues into local municipal programs.During the past several years, Mott supported a pilot project aimed at promoting the role of women in politics, particularly at the local level. The project trained municipal councilors on gender, communications and local government.

title: Women and Local Government Project
geographic_focus: Zimbabwe, South Africa, Angola, Botswana, Swaziland, Lesotho, Seychelles, Malawi, Namibia, Mozambique, Mauritius, Tanzania, Zambia
description: This grant will provide partial support to Gender Links to continue its effort to encourage and promote gender equity in South Africa. The grantee provides training, conducts research, and supports advocacy to ensure the attainment of gender equality in South Africa and the broader Southern African region. While prior work has concentrated on researching the role of women in politics in South Africa, developing strategies for mainstreaming gender in local government, and disseminating these findings, this grant will focus on supporting the implementation of action plans. Gender Links will provide ongoing support for the roll out of gender action plans in all nine South African provinces, provide training to councilors in two additional major municipalities, and develop a flagship project around the 2010 Soccer World Cup.

title: Women and Local Government Project
geographic_focus: Malawi, South Africa, Lesotho, Zimbabwe, Tanzania, Swaziland, Zambia, Namibia, Seychelles, Mozambique, Mauritius, Botswana, Angola
description: Gender Links is a research, training, and advocacy nonprofit organization established in 2001 to encourage the promotion and attainment of gender equality, particularly in and through the media. Past support enabled it to research the role of women in politics in South Africa and the southern Africa region. The grantee disseminated the findings and used them in advocacy campaigns to promote the increased representation of women in politics. Through this grant, the grantee will support the implementation of action plans for addressing gender-based violence by South African municipalities. It will also convene the first Gender Justice and Local Government Summit, showcasing good practices by local governments in addressing gender-based violence. The summit will bring together local government stakeholders from at least eight countries in southern Africa and will convene parallel seminars on promoting women’s representation and effective participation in local government structures.

title: Reforming the Global Economy for a Sustainable Future
description: Friends of the Earth (FoE) is the U.S. affiliate of an international network of environmental organizations in 70 countries. Through this project, Friends of the Earth works to strengthen environmental policies in the institutions and negotiations that govern international finance and trade.This grant will enable FoE to address the environmental and social impacts of key development financiers and new global financial actors; advocate for a shift of global investment from conventional energy to sustainable and renewable energy; promote the financing of sustainable infrastructure; advocate for sustainable and socially equitable development in conflict areas; and advocate for sustainable international trade and investment policies.During the past two years, FoE led intensive efforts to ensure that the World Bank implemented the recommendations of the Extractive Industries Review; advocated for the development of a new environmental policy at the Inter-American Development Bank; and continued to lead NGOs in encouraging private banks to improve their social and environmental lending standards.

title: Advancing Sustainability in Development Finance
description: Friends of the Earth is the United States affiliate of an international network of environmental organizations in 70 countries. Through this project, Friends of the Earth works to strengthen environmental policies in the institutions that invest capital for projects in developing countries. During this grant period, the objectives of the project will be to continue to hold international financial institutions and other financiers accountable by advocating for sustainable development of the extractive industry sector; effectively address new financing institutions, particularly those new institutions in developing countries; and ensure that development resources are deployed in ways that benefit the poor, particularly given the new climate-related financing.

title: Advancing Sustainability in Development Finance
description: Friends of the Earth is the United States affiliate of an international network of environmental organizations in 70 countries. Friends of the Earth works to strengthen environmental policies in the institutions that invest capital for projects in developing countries. This grant increase will allow Friends of the Earth to conduct a carbon finance research project that will provide background on the array of investments that make up carbon finance; analyze the governance, equity, and environmental effectiveness of these investments; and provide strategic analysis of policy options being considered in climate change discussions.

title: Advancing Sustainability in Development Finance
description: Friends of the Earth is the United States affiliate of an international network of environmental organizations in 70 countries. Through this project, the grantee works to effectively respond to the environmental and social impacts of international development finance and monitor climate change and energy-related financing to ensure that they safeguard the environment and benefit the poor. During this grant period, Friends of the Earth will monitor the policies and activities of key players in development finance, especially with respect to resource extraction projects around the world; advocate for responsible international climate-related financing and technology; and monitor the World Bank’s climate change initiatives.

title: Advancing Sustainability in Development Finance
description: The international program of Friends of the Earth works to effectively respond to the environmental and social impacts of international development finance as well as monitor climate change and energy-related financing to ensure that they safeguard the environment and benefit the poor. With this grant increase, the grantee will provide more extensive information on the role, effectiveness, and regulation of a carbon trading scheme as a key component of climate change policy in the United States.

title: Advancing Sustainability in Development Finance
description: The international program of Friends of the Earth works to effectively respond to the environmental and social impacts of international development finance as well as monitor climate change and energy-related financing to ensure that they safeguard the environment and benefit the poor. With this grant increase, the grantee will provide more extensive information on the role, effectiveness, and regulation of a carbon trading scheme as a key component of United States and global climate change policy.

title: Advancing and Protecting Sustainability Standards in Development Finance
description: Friends of the Earth is the United States affiliate of an international network of environmental organizations in 76 countries. Through this project, the grantee works to strengthen environmental policies in public and private international finance institutions. Over the last grant, it was successful in ensuring that domestic regulations on carbon trading and export credit agencies were strengthened. As well, the grantee provided training for Chinese organizations to address their public and private bank policies. With this grant, the project objectives are to ensure that international development finance is governed by robust environmental and social standards and the level of climate finance is adequate and deployed in ways that safeguard the environment, benefit the poor, and promote social justice.

title: Advancing and Protecting Sustainability Standards in Development Finance
description: Friends of the Earth is the United States affiliate of an international network of environmental organizations in 76 countries. Through this project, the grantee works to strengthen environmental policies in public and private international finance institutions. This grant increase will provide support for an organizational planning process.

title: Advancing and Protecting Sustainability Standards in Development Finance
description: Friends of the Earth is the United States affiliate of an international network of environmental organizations based in 70 countries. Through this project, the grantee works to advance environmental and social safeguards of key international development finance institutions; and ensure that financing for low-carbon development in developing countries (known as climate finance) is adequate, democratically governed, and adheres to high environmental and social standards. The grantee’s policy work over the last grant period contributed to significant increases in domestic export credit agencies lending for renewable energy and to the Chinese adoption of new guidelines for their lending to developing countries. Over the next grant period, the grantee will undertake research, monitoring, and advocacy on World Bank safeguards; provide advocacy assistance to Chinese organizations to test the new Chinese lending guidelines; and monitor the design of the international climate finance mechanism, as well as develop policy proposals for its environmental and social standards.

title: Advancing and Protecting Sustainability Standards in Development Finance
description: Friends of the Earth is the United States affiliate of an international network of environmental organizations based in 70 countries. Through this project, the grantee will work to advance environmental and social safeguards of key international development finance institutions; and ensure that financing for low-carbon development in developing countries (known as climate finance) is adequate, democratically governed, and adheres to high environmental and social standards. This increase will provide additional staff capacity to address the World Bank safeguard review and United Nations climate finance discussions.

title: Advancing and Protecting Sustainability Standards in Development Finance
description: Friends of the Earth is the United States affiliate of an international network of environmental organizations based in 70 countries. Through this project, it works to advance environmental and social safeguards of key international development finance institutions and ensure that financing for low-carbon development in emerging countries (known as climate finance) is democratically governed and adheres to high environmental and social standards. The grantee’s policy work over the last grant period contributed to significant improvement of Chinese lending policies to developing countries. Over this next grant period, the grantee will provide assistance to Chinese organizations to improve their lending guidelines, and monitor the first year of operation of the international climate finance mechanism, Green Climate Fund.

title: Advancing and Protecting Sustainability Standards in Development Finance
description: Friends of the Earth is the U.S. affiliate of an international network of environmental organizations based in 70 countries. Through this project, it works to advance environmental and social standards of key international development finance institutions and ensure that financing for renewable energy is democratically governed and adheres to globally recognized environmental and social standards. The grantee’s work over the last grant period contributed to improvements of Chinese policies governing their lending to developing countries. In addition, it played an important role in the development of the United Nations’ Green Climate Fund’s first year of projects addressing greenhouse gas mitigation. During this grant period, the grantee will continue its work addressing Chinese-led development finance institutions, such as the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank and the New Development Bank. It will also work to advance transparency and accountability as well as address environmental, social, and developmental impacts of other public development finance institutions, including the United States’ Overseas Private Investment Corporation, the African Development Bank, and the Green Climate Fund.

title: Advancing and Protecting Sustainability Standards in Development Finance
description: Friends of the Earth is the U.S. affiliate of an international network of environmental organizations based in 70 countries. Through this project, it works to advance environmental and social standards of key international development finance institutions and ensure that financing for renewable energy is democratically governed and adheres to globally recognized environmental and social standards. The grantee’s work over the last grant period contributed to improvements in Chinese development finance policies and extension of environmental and climate safeguards to the new U.S. development finance institution. During this grant period, the grantee will continue its work addressing Chinese-led development finance, including the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank. It will also work for increased investment in renewable energy in Africa with a particular focus on providing energy access to rural, off-grid communities in the region.

title: Developing Community-Based Organizations in Romania
grantee: PACT - Partnership for Community Action and Transformation Foundation
description: The project goal is to build the capacity of informal groups and grassroots non-governmental organizations in southern Romania to engage in the development of their communities.This grant will enable PACT – Partnership for Community Action and Transformation Foundation to provide training, field consultancy, small grants and networking opportunities to 15 grassroots organizations whose activities address the local needs of marginalized groups. Continued funding builds on previous support to the Romanian Association for Community Development for this program.Past achievements included strengthening the capacity of 36 community groups and organizations to develop and implement successful community projects; building coalitions; and mobilizing local resources.

title: Grassroots Coordination
description: Working closely with leaders in more than a dozen states, the Leadership Conference Education Fund has built a state coalition infrastructure providing grassroots organizations with the opportunity to convene and work together to educate and mobilize the public around important civil rights issues such as judicial independence, immigration and other concerns. This grant will enable the fund to provide continued technical assistance to these state-based coalitions, including programmatic and legal training for community leaders; media and message development training for community leaders; maintaining and updating tools and resources available to grassroots and state-level organizations and coalitions, including a Web site; and convening coalition leaders from more than a dozen states to share ideas and best practices.

title: General Purposes
description: GuideStar is the largest and best-known provider of information about nonprofit organizations in the United States, with data on over 1.5 million charitable institutions in its database, millions of users of its free public services, and thousands of customers for its paid services. GuideStar’s data services provide greater transparency for the nonprofit sector, encourage charitable giving by building public interest and trust, and enable individuals and institutions involved with charitable activities and organizations to make better decisions. Renewed general purposes support will help GuideStar continue developing and marketing paid services, provide new services to individual donors, and invest in technology in order to complete its transition to a sustainable business model in which earned income represents the organization’s largest source of revenue.

title: General Purposes
description: GuideStar is the largest and best-known provider of information about nonprofit organizations in the United States, with data on over 1.7 million nonprofit organizations in its database. Millions use its free public services, and thousands use its paid services. Its database also includes 3.3 million nonprofit tax return forms. GuideStar’s data services provide greater transparency for the nonprofit sector, encourage charitable giving by building public interest and trust, and enable individuals and institutions involved with charitable activities and organizations to make better decisions. This grant increase will support a major project to update the GuideStar Web site and database to accommodate the recently revamped nonprofit tax return form, the IRS Form 990.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued general purpose support to GuideStar, the premier source of information about nonprofit organizations in the United States. With data on over 1.7 million nonprofit organizations in its database, millions of users of its free public services, and thousands of customers for its paid services, GuideStar has become an invaluable source of information to nonprofits and grantmakers. The grantee’s data services provide greater transparency for the nonprofit sector, encourage charitable giving by building public interest and trust, and enable individuals and institutions involved with charitable activities and organizations to make better decisions. Over the next two years, the grantee plans to expand and improve its free public services; launch new customized data service packages; implement more advanced search capabilities; connect to other Web sites through strategic partnerships; develop additional value-added benchmarking and analytic tools; and explore the provision of fee-based research, consulting, and due diligence services for specific clients.

title: General Purposes
description: GuideStar is the premier source of information about nonprofit organizations in the United States, with data on over 1.7 million nonprofits in its database, millions of users of its free public services, and thousands of customers for its paid services. The grantee’s data services provide greater transparency for the nonprofit sector, encourage charitable giving by building public interest and trust, and enable individuals and institutions involved with charitable activities and organizations to make better decisions. The grantee has recently launched a strategic planning process in order to meet the increasing demand for high-quality and actionable data on nonprofits. In particular, the grantee expects that the planning process will help identify how it can: 1) help donors and nonprofits identify high performing organizations; 2) bundle data and tools into a variety of packages for various kinds of users; and 3) step up the pace of innovation. This grant increase will provide partial support for the planning process.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued general purpose support to GuideStar, the premier source of information about nonprofit organizations in the United States. With data on over 1.8 million nonprofits in its database, millions of users of its free public services, and thousands of customers for its paid services, GuideStar has become an invaluable source of information to nonprofits and grantmakers. The grantee’s data services provide greater transparency for the nonprofit sector, encourage charitable giving by building public interest and trust, and enable individuals and institutions involved with charitable activities and organizations to make better decisions. Plans over the next two years include creating and marketing universally accepted nonprofit data standards, optimizing data collection and management techniques and processes, maximizing data sharing with nonprofits, enabling simplified data provision by nonprofits through enhanced delivery tools, distributing nonprofit data and tool packages to partner sites, and creating a flexible development resource for rapid technological innovation.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued general purpose support to GuideStar, the premier source of information about nonprofit organizations in the United States. With data on over 1.8 million nonprofits in its database, millions of users of its free public services and thousands of customers for its paid services, GuideStar has become an invaluable source of information to nonprofits and grantmakers. Plans over the next two years include creating and marketing universally accepted nonprofit data standards, optimizing data collection and management techniques and processes, maximizing data sharing with nonprofits, enabling simplified data provision by nonprofits through enhanced delivery tools, distributing nonprofit data and tool packages to partner sites, and creating an agile development resource for rapid technological innovation. A grant increase will allow the grantee to work with the Technology Affinity Group to develop a common database of standard grant information.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued general purpose support to GuideStar, the premier source of information about nonprofit organizations in the United States. With data on over two million nonprofits in its database, millions of users of its free public services, and thousands of customers for its paid services, GuideStar has become an invaluable source of information to nonprofits and grantmakers. The grantee’s data services provide greater transparency for the nonprofit sector, encourage charitable giving by building public interest and trust, and enable individuals and institutions involved with charitable activities and organizations to make better decisions. Over the next two years, the grantee plans to shift from being only a Web site with financial data about nonprofits to a platform offering multidimensional data about social change. This will involve developing new online products and tools such as a common profile, issue pages, nonprofit sector indices, open data partnerships, and mobile device delivery.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued general purpose support to GuideStar, a leading source of information about nonprofit organizations in the United States. GuideStar has 2.8 billion pieces of data on 2.5 million individual organizations, and 7.1 million individual users of its Web site. Another 185 Web sites and applications are powered by GuideStar data. The grantee’s data services provide greater transparency for the nonprofit sector, encourage charitable giving by building public interest and trust, and enable individuals and institutions involved with charitable activities and organizations to make better decisions. Most recently, the grantee has launched a fieldwide collection mechanism for quantitative programmatic data through its Platinum Nonprofit Profile level. Over the next two years, the grantee will continue to implement its GuideStar 2020 strategic plan, calling for better and broader data collection, data distribution, and data innovation.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued general purpose support to GuideStar, a leading source of information about nonprofit organizations in the United States. The grantee maintains 3.5 billion pieces of data on 2.6 million organizations and has 9 million individual users of its website per year. Their data services provide greater transparency for the nonprofit sector, encourage charitable giving by building public interest and trust, and enable individuals and institutions involved with charitable activities and organizations to make better decisions. Currently, 153,000 nonprofits share data directly to the grantee’s database, and it has 232 data distribution partners. During the current grant period, the grantee will continue to implement its GuideStar 2020 strategic plan, calling for better and broader data collection, data distribution, and data innovation.

title: War Crimes Trials Coverage Project
geographic_focus: Serbia, Montenegro, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina
description: This grant will enable the International Research & Exchanges Board to provide training for journalists covering domestic war crimes trials across the Western Balkans region. Expanded coverage by local journalists of proceedings in The Hague and in domestic courts will deepen people’s understanding of the wars and conflicts in the region during the 1990s.During 2005-2006, the board supported nine journalists reporting from The Hague. These journalists provided approximately 200 articles and reports on the court proceedings.The board, based in Washington, D.C., has extensive experience supporting free and independent media around the world.

title: War Crimes Trials Coverage Project
geographic_focus: Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, Croatia
description: The project goal of the International Research & Exchanges Board is to expand coverage by journalists from Bosnia, Croatia, Kosovo, Macedonia, Montenegro, and Serbia of the proceedings of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia in The Hague. Through this project, more than 25 journalists from over 15 television, radio, and print media in the Western Balkans have traveled to The Hague to provide first-hand coverage of the historic proceedings of the tribunal. Coverage by these local journalists has deepened people’s understanding of the events in the region during the 1990s. In the final phase of the project, the grantee will support approximately 30 journalists from more than ten local media outlets in the Western Balkans to report from the tribunal until it closes down in 2008. The grantee is based in Washington, D.C., and has worked extensively in the Balkans to support the development of independent journalism and media.

title: General Purposes
description: The Karoo Centre for Human Rights promotes democracy and assists rural communities understand and access their rights.This grant renewal will enable the center to offer a two-year training program for paralegals in collaboration with the Walter Sisulu University; provide organizational development support in areas such as financial management, governance and general management to staff and advice committees in 45 advice offices in the Western, Eastern and Northern cape provinces; and explore options for the provision of legal advice to people living with HIV/AIDS.Recent accomplishments included training 30 paralegals on various modules relating to law and human rights; providing mentoring and support to community-based advice offices; developing a strong network of paralegals and advice offices within the three provinces; educating communities about their rights and how to access them; and conducting research to establish the extent to which the rights of people living with HIV/AIDS are protected with a view to developing programs that address the needs of this target group.

title: General Purposes
description: The Karoo Centre for Human Rights works to promote access to justice by poor and marginalized communities in the Eastern, Western, and Northern Cape provinces. This grant will support the centre to continue providing training and mentoring support to community-based advice offices in these provinces to enable them to educate communities about their rights and how to access them. The centre works in mostly rural areas and small towns, which are characterized by high levels of illiteracy, poverty, and unemployment. The advice offices are often the only places that community members can go to for legal advice and for gaining access to social grants and related government services, which makes their continued existence critical for these communities.

title: General Purposes
description: The Karoo Centre for Human Rights works to promote access to justice by poor and marginalized communities in the Eastern, Western, and Northern Cape provinces. The centre supports advice offices in mostly rural areas and small towns, providing them with hands-on support in areas including the development of appropriate organizational systems and structures, dealing with case work, and governance. It also facilitates training of paralegals in collaboration with the Walter Sisulu University in the Eastern Cape province. This grant increase will support the centre to strengthen its internal systems and structure.

title: General Purposes
description: The Karoo Centre for Human Rights was established in 1998 to promote the advancement of human rights through training of paralegals and communities on the access and understanding of basic human rights. The grantee works with poor and marginalized communities in the Eastern, Western, and Northern Cape provinces of South Africa, in areas characterized by high levels of illiteracy, poverty, and unemployment. Previous support enabled the grantee to provide training and mentoring support to community-based advice offices in these provinces to enable them to educate communities about their rights and how to access them. This renewal grant will support the grantee to participate in networks and collaborations aimed at improving access to justice and human rights for poor people.

title: Responsibility for the Future - The Way Forward
description: This grant will enable Freedom House to focus on broadening public support at the community level for dealing with the past in Serbia and Montenegro as a means of building a positive future in the region. To this end, Freedom House will help grassroots civic organizations connect with and participate in national and regional initiatives related to dealing with the past and carry out community-level, awareness-raising projects.During the past year and a half, Freedom House awarded $115,000 in small grants to nine organizations. Examples of projects that were supported include the production of a series of four half-hour episodes for television on specific human rights atrocities during the past 10 years; a series of six roundtables bringing together a cross-section of actors to discuss transitional justice in Serbia and Montenegro; and a regional film festival focused on the recent past.

title: Philanthropic Consulting Initiative
description: The Leadership Conference Education Fund works to help bridge the gap between antiracist organizations and potential funders. This grant will enable the fund to focus on assisting race-focused nonprofits in developing and maintaining healthy relationships with funding organizations; increasing funders’ understanding of antiracist work and assisting them in assessing their institutional needs around race and diversity as it relates to grantmaking practices; and helping community leaders and local funders design and implement effective programs to document and advance the skills of both grantseekers and grantmakers.Since its inception in 2003, the project has directly engaged more than 250 representatives of foundations in discussions related to racial equity and maintained contacts with philanthropic organizations, community-based practitioners, researchers and advocates through a dedicated Web site and publications.

title: Philanthropic Initiative for Racial Equity
description: This grant continues support for the Philanthropic Initiative for Racial Equity, a program of the Tides Center. Begun in 2003, the program’s goal is to build the amount and effectiveness of resources aimed at combating institutional and structural racism through capacity building, education, and convening grantmakers and grantseekers. A key goal for the next two years is to solidify a movement within philanthropy making racial equity a fundamental, ongoing part of this sector. Major activities include conducting workshops with regional associations of grantmakers, other funding networks, and issue-based and identity-based affinity funders; testing and assessing tools to measure impact of racial equity grantmaking; collaborating with partners to vet tools and resources to assist grantmakers; and producing papers and reports related to grantmaking issues in the field of racial equity.

title: Philanthropic Initiative for Racial Equity
description: The Tides Center sponsors and provides financial and human services and administrative oversight to nearly 200 projects nationwide that fit in three program areas: 1) community development and services; 2) environment and health; and 3) policy, strategy, and global initiatives. This grant continues support for the Philanthropic Initiative for Racial Equity, a program of the Tides Center. Begun in 2003, the program’s goal is to build the amount and effectiveness of resources aimed at combating institutional and structural racism through capacity building, education, and convening grantmakers and grantseekers. Major activities include conducting workshops with regional associations of grantmakers and other funders, testing and assessing tools to measure the impact of racial equity grantmaking, and producing papers and reports related to grantmaking issues in the field of racial equity.

title: Philanthropic Initiative for Racial Equity
description: The Tides Center sponsors and provides financial and human services and administrative oversight to nearly 200 projects nationwide that fit in three program areas: 1) community development and services; 2) environment and health; and 3) policy, strategy, and global initiatives. This grant continues support for the Philanthropic Initiative for Racial Equity, a program of the Tides Center. The program’s goal is to build the amount and effectiveness of resources aimed at combating institutional and structural racism through capacity building, education, and convening grantmakers and grantseekers. Since it began in 2003, the program has engaged hundreds of foundation representatives in discussions of racial equity focusing specifically on how they can advance the mission of achieving racial equity through their philanthropic organizations. In 2010-11, the program will continue to conduct workshops with regional associations of grantmakers and other funders, test and assess tools to measure the impact of racial equity grantmaking, and produce papers and reports related to grantmaking issues in the field of racial equity.

title: Philanthropic Initiative for Racial Equity
description: The Tides Center sponsors and provides financial and human services and administrative oversight to nearly 200 projects nationwide that fit in three program areas: 1) community development and services; 2) environment and health; and 3) policy, strategy, and global initiatives. This grant continues support for the Philanthropic Initiative for Racial Equity, a program of the Tides Center. Since it began in 2003, the program has engaged hundreds of foundation representatives in discussions of racial equity focusing specifically on how they can advance the mission of achieving racial equity through their philanthropic organizations. In 2011-12, the program will continue to conduct workshops with regional, issue-based, and identity-based funder networks; provide assistance to the Racial Justice Funders Roundtable; and develop new projects that place a greater emphasis on increasing the effectiveness of resources aimed at eradicating institutional and structural racism.

title: Philanthropic Initiative for Racial Equity
