Begun in 2003, the program’s goal is to build the amount and effectiveness of resources aimed at combating institutional and structural racism through capacity building, education, and convening grantmakers and grantseekers. Major activities include conducting workshops with regional associations of grantmakers and other funders, testing and assessing tools to measure the impact of racial equity grantmaking, and producing papers and reports related to grantmaking issues in the field of racial equity.

title: Informing State Legislatures: Statewide Afterschool Policy
description: This grant will enable the National Conference of State Legislatures to continue its work of educating state legislators about the value of afterschool and its contributions to current education policy. Objectives will include compiling and disseminating data from all 50 states on the status of afterschool funding; continuing to provide technical assistance to emerging and current statewide afterschool networks as a part of the Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative, a group of national organizations working to support the development of statewide networks through technical assistance; and overseeing collaborative efforts with the National Governors Association and the Council of Chief State School Officers to provide intensive technical assistance on furthering afterschool policies with state leadership teams. Specifically, this collaborative effort will provide teams of state legislators, education chiefs and governor’s policy advisors with technical assistance opportunities to advance deeper connections between afterschool and improving public education.

title: Informing State Legislatures: Statewide Afterschool Policy
description: This grant increase will allow the National Conference of State Legislatures to fund additional states in its collaborative work with the National Governors Association and the Council of Chief State School Officers to provide technical assistance on furthering afterschool policies with state leadership teams. This collaborative effort is designed to provide teams of state legislators, education chiefs, and governor’s policy advisors with opportunities to advance deeper connections between afterschool and improving public education.

title: Informing State Legislatures: Statewide Afterschool Policy
description: This grant will continue to support the National Conference of State Legislatures in its work to educate state legislators about the value of afterschool and its contributions to education policy. Specifically, the National Conference of State Legislatures will: 1) publish a summary and guide on the state role in afterschool initiatives; 2) collect data and publish a legislative brief on how states fund afterschool through the school finance formula; 3) publish a retrospective report on state activities resulting from the first round of Supporting Student Success grants; 4) convene an advisory committee of state legislators to advise staff of ongoing activities; 5) support legislators who are planning deeper links between afterschool and state education systems through oversight and co-implementation of the next round of Supporting Student Success grants; 6) continue support of the statewide afterschool networks through participation in the Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative; and 7) provide legislative technical assistance in the form of testimony, legislative language consultation, and other speaking and meeting opportunities. The Supporting Student Success project will be done in partnership with the Council of Chief State School Officers and the National Governors Association Center for Best Practices.

title: Informing State Legislatures: Statewide Afterschool Policy
description: This grant increase will allow the National Conference of State Legislatures to fund additional states in its collaborative work with the National Governors Association and the Council of Chief State School Officers to provide technical assistance on furthering afterschool policies with state leadership teams. This collaborative effort is designed to provide teams of state legislators, education chiefs, and governors’ policy advisors with opportunities to advance deeper connections between afterschool and improving public education.

title: Informing State Legislatures: Statewide Afterschool Policy
description: This grant will continue to support the National Conference of State Legislatures in its work to educate state legislators about the value of afterschool and its contributions to the expanded learning opportunities conversation and other education policy discussions. Specifically, the National Conference of State Legislatures will: 1) produce a series of co-published materials, in partnership with the Harvard Family Research Project, that provide a neutral, nonpartisan summary of expanded learning opportunities research and policy implications; 2) establish an expanded learning opportunities listserv to increase electronic communications and share information with legislators; 3) provide technical assistance opportunities to legislators to promote deeper understanding of the significance of afterschool and its promises as a tool to meet state education goals; 4) co-implement and oversee the next round of Supporting Student Success grants; 5) continue support of the statewide afterschool networks through participation in the Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative; and 6) partner with the Council of Chief State School Officers and the National Governors’ Association on the Supporting Student Success project.

title: Informing State Legislatures: Statewide Afterschool Policy
description: This grant will continue to support the National Conference of State Legislatures in its work to educate state legislators about the value of afterschool and to build state capacity to implement high quality afterschool and expanded learning opportunities. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) produce and disseminate briefs for legislators on the connections between afterschool research, policy, and practice; 2) expand communication efforts with legislators, legislative staff, and the statewide afterschool networks through written, electronic, and video mediums; 3) continue to support the networks as part of the Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative with an increased focus on effective data-sharing practices; and 4) support states to host convenings on afterschool issues.

title: Informing State Legislatures: Statewide Afterschool Policy
description: This grant increase will support the National Conference of State Legislatures in its work to educate state legislators about the value of high quality afterschool and expanded learning opportunities. Specifically, the grantee will help statewide afterschool networks develop and share data on afterschool and expanded learning opportunities with stakeholders.

title: Informing State Legislatures: Statewide Afterschool Policy
description: This grant will continue support to the National Conference of State Legislatures in its work to educate state legislators about the value of afterschool and to build state capacity to implement high quality afterschool and summer learning opportunities. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) lift up afterschool and summer learning as a mechanism to close the achievement and opportunity gaps; 2) connect afterschool and summer learning to college and career readiness and dropout prevention; 3) engage legislators on the topic of afterschool and summer learning; 4) expand communication efforts with legislators, legislative staff, and the statewide afterschool networks; and 5) continue to support the statewide afterschool networks as part of the Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative with an increased focus on effective data sharing practices.

title: Informing State Legislatures: Statewide Afterschool Policy
description: This grant increase will support the National Conference of State Legislatures in its work to educate state legislators about the value of high quality afterschool and summer learning opportunities. Specifically, the grantee will help statewide afterschool networks develop and share data on afterschool and summer learning opportunities with stakeholders.

title: Informing State Legislatures: Statewide Afterschool Policy
description: This grant will continue to support the National Conference of State Legislatures in its work to educate state legislators about the value of afterschool and to build state capacity to implement high quality afterschool and summer learning opportunities. Specifically, the National Conference of State Legislatures will: 1) develop resources on the role afterschool and summer learning can play in state education; 2) connect afterschool and summer learning to social and emotional learning and workforce development; 3) engage legislators on the topic of afterschool and summer learning; and 4) continue to support the statewide afterschool networks as part of the Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative, with an increased focus on effective data sharing practices.

title: Informing State Legislatures: Statewide Afterschool Policy
description: This grant will continue to support the National Conference of State Legislatures in its work to educate state legislators about the positive impact of afterschool and to build state capacity to implement high-quality afterschool and summer learning opportunities. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) develop resources on the role afterschool and summer learning can play in state education, including to advance social and emotional learning and workforce development; 2) engage legislators on the topic of afterschool and summer learning; 3) implement the Supporting Student Success project to raise visibility of afterschool and summer learning on pressing education issues; and 4) continue to support the statewide afterschool networks as part of the Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative, with an increased focus on effective data sharing practices.

title: General Purposes
description: Ikhala Trust, established in 2000, is an indigenous grantmaker that provides small grants to community-based organizations in the Eastern Cape, one of the poorest provinces in South Africa. In addition to small grants, mostly in the areas of HIV/AIDS and local economic development, the trust provides training, capacity building and institutional support to these organizations.This grant will enable Ikhala Trust to continue activities that include implementing effective evaluation, capacity building and organizational development strategies to support and monitor the recipients of its grants; organizing project management workshops, field visits and learning events; hosting an annual learning conference where it will bring its grantees together to network; and documenting success stories to mobilize additional resources for community-based development

title: General Purposes
description: This grant continues support for the Ikhala Trust, an indigenous funder that provides small grants to community organizations primarily for HIV/AIDS prevention and economic development in South Africa’s Eastern Cape region. The trust also provides technical assistance and training on organizational and resource development issues through workshops, seminars, and conferences. Future activities include continuing its core programs while also increasing efforts to support grantees, providing advocacy training, helping to increase funding to grantees from individual donors, and improving governance and management of the trust through board development and staff assessment. Since its inception in 2002, the trust has assisted more than 140 grassroots organizations.

title: General Purposes
description: The Eastern Cape is one of the poorest provinces in South Africa. It is largely rural, with high levels of unemployment resulting in migration to bigger cities for employment opportunities. Ikhala Trust works in poor communities of the Eastern Cape province to support small community-based initiatives through small grants and relevant training support. Over the last two years, the small grants program provided support to these communities for various issues including health promotion, home-based care support, and the promotion of entrepreneurial activities. This grant will continue to support poor communities in the Eastern Cape province to implement community development programs. The grantee will make an average of 25 grants per year to deserving organizations. The grantee will also train community-based organizations in the province and educate community members about their rights and how to access services from government departments.

title: General Purposes
description: Ikhala Trust works in poor communities of the Eastern Cape Province of South Africa to support small community-based initiatives through small grants and relevant training opportunities. Over the last two years, the grantee’s grantmaking assisted these communities on various issues including health promotion, home-based care support, and the promotion of entrepreneurial activities. This general purpose grant increase will support the grantee to conduct action research on the different ways in which asset-based and citizen-led community development approaches have been used by community foundations and other indigenous grantmakers in South Africa.

title: General Purposes
description: Ikhala Trust is a community grantmaker working in one of the poorest provinces in South Africa, the Eastern Cape. It makes small grants and provides training to community-based organizations in poor and rural communities. Over the past two years, the grantee made small grants to community-based organizations working with HIV/AIDS patients, orphans and vulnerable children, nutritional health, and entrepreneurial projects. It also led the establishment of a network of organizations that promote the use of the asset-based community development approach in transforming communities. This approach encourages the use of local assets as a basis for community development. Over the next two years, the grantee will continue to make small grants, provide training to community-based organizations on the asset-based community development approach, host learning events for grantmakers and other development organizations to exchange lessons and experiences, and develop practical tools that will support its grantees when applying the principles of the asset-based community development approach.

title: General Purposes
description: Ikhala Trust is a grantmaker that supports community-based organizations in poor communities across the Eastern Cape Province in South Africa. It makes small grants and provides training on various topics related to community development. Over the past two years, the grantee supported the growth of the asset-based community development approach in the province and nationally. This approach encourages the use of local assets as a basis for community development. It also continued to make small grants to support community-based organizations that respond to various challenges in their communities. Over the next two years, the grantee will finalize a practical toolkit on how to implement the asset-based community development approach, continue to make small grants, and provide training on the asset-based community development approach and other organizational development techniques to community-based organizations.

title: General Purposes
description: The Ikhala Trust makes small grants to community-based organizations in the Eastern Cape province in South Africa. It also supports organizations that respond to the daily struggles of poor communities by providing training on relevant topics. Over the past two years, the grantee made small grants and promoted the asset-based community development approach to development. It also provided capacity building training to new community-based organizations and those that needed certain skills to become functional and accountable. This grant will assist the grantee to continue supporting community development by making small grants, conducting action research to assess the impact of its work, and providing training on the asset-based community development approach. It will also pilot a monitoring and evaluation process with its grantees and produce case studies and visual material that can be used to make the case for support from local businesses.

title: General Purposes
description: The Ikhala Trust is a community grantmaker that makes small grants to community-based organizations in the Eastern Cape province in South Africa. It also provides training to organizations working in poor communities to encourage an asset-based approach to community development. In addition, the grantee also piloted a monitoring and evaluation process with its grantees to collate more accurate qualitative and quantitative data on the impact of their support. This grant will enable the grantee to continue its work with community-based organizations, provide training to organizations to improve their skills, and introduce the asset-based community development approach to new grantees. Additionally, the grantee will consolidate the monitoring and evaluation process and introduce it to all its grantees.

title: General Purposes
description: The Charities Aid Foundation-Southern Africa promotes corporate and individual philanthropy and giving in South Africa and the broader southern African region. Mott has provided support to encourage the growth of corporate philanthropy and develop workplace giving in South Africa. This renewal grant will continue to provide institutional support to the organization to implement its various programs and projects in South Africa, which mainly involve mobilizing resources for the benefit of the nonprofit sector in the country. During the grant period, the grantee will also look at establishing an endowment fund to ensure its longer-term sustainability. Charities Aid Foundation-Southern Africa is part of Charities Aid Foundation-United Kingdom, which has provided an endowment challenge grant that Charities Aid Foundation-Southern Africa needs to match from local funders in South Africa and the region.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purpose support to the Charities Aid Foundation-Southern Africa. The foundation promotes corporate and individual giving in South Africa and southern Africa with an emphasis on workplace giving and corporate matching gifts. In 2007-2008, the foundation ran volunteer programs for employees and over 12,862 hours were donated through its matching gifts programs. The foundation also distributed R5.63 million to nonprofit organizations, and advised on R12.5 million of corporate social investment funds. Over 350 nonprofits benefited from its work. During the next two years, the foundation will continue to promote giving and provide support services to business, government, and civil society to improve their planning and management of social development programs. It will also undertake research on relevant topics for the field and raise funds for grants to other nonprofits.

title: General Purposes
description: The Charities Aid Foundation-Southern Africa promotes corporate and individual giving in South Africa and southern Africa with an emphasis on workplace giving and corporate matching gifts. In 2009-2010, the grantee ran volunteer programs for employees who donated over 14,000 hours through its matching gifts programs. The grantee also facilitated the distribution of R9.6 million to nonprofit organizations and advised on millions of rands worth of corporate social investment funds. Four hundred forty-two nonprofits benefited from its work. This general purpose grant increase will assist the foundation in its efforts to conduct research on the state of local giving in South Africa.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purpose support to the Charities Aid Foundation-Southern Africa, which promotes corporate and individual giving in South Africa with an emphasis on workplace giving and corporate matching gifts. In 2009-2010, the foundation distributed around R14 million to nonprofit organizations, assisted over 500 nonprofits either through financial support or in-kind contributions, and facilitated the donation of tens of thousands of volunteer hours from various South Africans to nonprofit organizations. It also assisted companies to develop corporate social investment policies and strategies to improve developmental impact and corporate citizenship and assisted the banking sector to develop a volunteering policy and framework. Over the next two years, the foundation will continue to promote giving and provide support services to businesses, government, and the nonprofit sector to improve their planning and management of social development programs. It will also conduct a national survey on individual giving and promote best practices on giving.

title: General Purposes
description: Charities Aid Foundation Southern Africa works to increase the amount and impact of investment in the nonprofit sector by promoting corporate and individual giving and volunteering in South Africa. In 2011-2012, the grantee distributed almost R4 million and other donations to over 400 nonprofit organizations; increased the number of volunteer hours donated to nonprofit organizations from that of previous years; refined volunteering policies and procedures for its corporate clients; designed and implemented training on organizational development to its client nonprofits; and participated in the development of an Independent Code of Governance for nonprofits in South Africa. Over the next two years, the grantee will continue to provide advisory services on corporate social investment strategies and promote employee volunteering in community development initiatives. It will also continue to manage various employee giving programs on behalf of clients.

title: General Purposes
description: Charities Aid Foundation Southern Africa works to increase the amount and impact of investment in the nonprofit sector by promoting corporate and individual giving and volunteering in South Africa. In 2013-2014, the grantee mobilized over 700 volunteers to work on various projects benefitting over 3,500 people; raised over R4.6 million through ten employee-giving programs that benefitted 284 nonprofits; unlocked R1.9 million for three nonprofits from corporates and individuals; and conducted research on individual giving in the Gauteng province, South Africa. Over the next two years, the grantee will continue to unlock resources for nonprofits from the corporate sector, grow its corporate client base, and provide strategic advice to corporations on appropriate policies and strategies for volunteering, payroll giving, and grantmaking. They will also provide training and related support to nonprofits and campaign for increased giving by individuals.

title: General Purposes
description: Charities Aid Foundation Southern Africa works to promote corporate and individual giving and volunteering in South Africa in order to strengthen the effectiveness of the nonprofit sector. It supports companies to develop strategies that respond appropriately to community needs, allows employees to be actively involved in community development initiatives, and strengthens the nonprofit sector to work more effectively. Past support enabled the grantee to mobilize volunteers in support of civil society initiatives, disburse funds to worthy causes, link businesses to vetted nonprofit organizations, and provide strategic guidance to companies setting up corporate social investment initiatives. Over the next two years, the grantee will continue to manage employee involvement programs for companies, unlock resources from the corporate sector in support of nonprofits, provide advice to corporates on their strategies and policies, advance thought leadership on topics related to civil society, and provide related support to nonprofits.

title: Building Capacity Through Diversity
grantee: Arab Community Center for Economic and Social Services (ACCESS)
description: The Arab Community Center for Economic and Social Services’ (ACCESS) Building Capacity Through Diversity project is a cultural diversity training project developed for members of Michigan’s environmental and land-use community. It grew out of the need within the state’s environmental community to build the capacity of its groups, both individually and collectively, to better address the concerns of diverse constituencies in their environmental growth management and land-use work.This grant will enable the project to focus on developing ongoing networking and support for past training participants; working with three to five environmental and land-use organizations to conduct projects involving internal organizational work exploring race and diversity within their own organization or public events exploring race, ethnicity and culture in environmental and land use issues; offering an antiracism/cultural diversity training retreat in western Michigan; and presenting two public forums addressing race and diversity issues as they relate to environmental and land use issues in Michigan.During the first two years of the project, ACCESS assembled an advisory committee of individuals with expertise in environmental and race relations issues to provide guidance and support in developing the project. Following the development of an appropriate training curriculum, 56 participants – representing a diversity of race, gender, and age – were involved in two years of training sessions.

title: Balkan Trust for Democracy
grantee: German Marshall Fund of the United States
geographic_focus: Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Albania, Croatia, Serbia, Romania, Montenegro, Bulgaria
description: The goal of the Balkan Trust for Democracy is to support democratic governance and strengthen democratic political institutions in Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Serbia and Montenegro, Macedonia, Romania, and Bulgaria and to advance cross-border cooperation in this region to promote the political, social and economic development necessary to ensure long-term stability. The German Marshall Fund of the United States set up the trust, a grantmaking fund that operates through an office in Belgrade, in August 2003. Since that time, the trust has made more than 200 grants totaling $4,420,000.This grant increase provides continued support to the trust.

title: Balkan Trust for Democracy
grantee: German Marshall Fund of the United States
geographic_focus: Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Albania, Croatia, Serbia, Bulgaria, Romania, Montenegro
description: The project goal is to: (1) support democratic governance and strengthen democratic political institutions in Albania, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia, Serbia, Montenegro, Macedonia, Romania, and Bulgaria; and (2) advance cross-border cooperation in this region with the aim of promoting the political, social, and economic development necessary to ensure long-term stability. To achieve these goals, the German Marshall Fund of the United States set up a grantmaking fund, called the Balkan Trust for Democracy, which operates as a project of the grantee through an office in Belgrade. The trust is supported by the grantee, the United States Agency for International Development, the Mott Foundation, various European governments, and other European and American private foundations, with the goal of attracting other donors to the trust over time. Since its establishment in August 2003, the trust has made more than 300 grants totaling over $8 million.

title: General Purposes
description: The mission of the Michigan Suburbs Alliance is to unite and strengthen Michigan’s core urban and suburban communities through research, regional cooperation, public education, and public policy development. The alliance has developed as an important voice on issues affecting the fiscal, economic, and environmental health of communities and metropolitan areas in Michigan. This grant renewal will enable the alliance to build on the groundwork established and implement its strategic plan focused on strengthening the capacity of core communities to attract redevelopment investment, encouraging enhanced regional cooperation and resource sharing among communities, and establishing a shared urban policy agenda.

title: General Purposes
description: The mission of the Michigan Suburbs Alliance is to unite and strengthen Michigan’s core urban and suburban communities through research, regional cooperation, public education, and public policy development. The alliance has developed as an important voice on issues affecting the fiscal, economic, and environmental health of communities and metropolitan areas in Michigan. This grant increase will support the organization’s effort to invest in board and staff training and development in order to strengthen organizational capacity.

title: General Purposes
description: The Michigan Suburbs Alliance is dedicated to advancing redevelopment, regional cooperation, and public policy reform throughout southeast Michigan. Formed by representatives from 14 metro Detroit suburbs in 2002, the alliance harnesses the power of southeast Michigan’s 1.9 million inhabitants to address disinvestment in older cities. The alliance has grown to include the mayors and city managers of 31 mature, inner-ring suburbs, representing more than 1 million residents. This grant increase and grant period extension will provide general purpose support to the alliance, which will allow it to continue its support of these communities, including helping them understand and access appropriate opportunities that arise from the federal stimulus package.

title: LDIR Flint Replication
description: Developed by the Asian Pacific American Legal Center of Southern California with support from the Mott Foundation’s Civil Society program, Leadership Development in Interethnic Relations is a community-based leadership training initiative that has proven to be an important element of Flint and Genesee County’s ongoing efforts to address issues of racial and interethnic relations. Continued support to the YWCA of Greater Flint will enable staff to assess the replication, continue to gather feedback on the community’s response to the program, develop programs and curriculum, as well as market and recruit for a third cycle. This grant increase will provide bridge funding to cover programmatic and administrative expenditures in response to a funding shortfall.

title: LDIR Flint Replication
description: Developed by the Asian Pacific American Legal Center of Southern California, with support from the Mott Foundation’s Civil Society program, Leadership Development in Interethnic Relations (LDIR) is a community-based leadership training initiative that has proven to be an important element of Flint and Genesee County’s ongoing efforts to address issues of racial and interethnic relations.This renewal grant to the YWCA of Greater Flint will provide continuing support for programmatic and administrative expenditures of this program. During the grant period, LDIR will assess the replication; continue to gather feedback on the community’s response to the program; develop programs and curriculum; as well as market and recruit for a third cycle of leadership training. Funding includes a grant increase to provide bridge funding to cover programmatic and administrative expenditures.

title: Northern Great Lakes Forest Project
description: The Nature Conservancy established the Great Lakes Forest Project to protect, through fee acquisition and conservation easements, more than 270,000 acres of forested land in Michigan’s Upper Peninsula. The project is a model conservation solution that supports the local timber economy, sustains the local tax base and maintains public access for outdoor recreation. This grant increase will support acquisition and stewardship costs.

title: Northern Great Lakes Forest Project
description: Through its Northern Great Lakes Forest Project, the Nature Conservancy, an international conservation organization, will protect more than 270,000 acres of forested land in Michigan’s Upper Peninsula. To date, about 23,000 acres have been protected through fee acquisition, and 150,000 acres have been protected through a working forest conservation easement. This grant increase will be used for additional acquisition and stewardship costs.

title: Northern Great Lakes Forest Project
description: Through its Northern Great Lakes Forest Project, the Nature Conservancy, an international conservation organization, will protect more than 270,000 acres of forested land in Michigan’s Upper Peninsula. This grant increase will be used for additional acquisition and stewardship costs, bringing Mott’s total commitment to the project to $10 million.

title: Northern Great Lakes Forest Project
description: The Michigan chapter of the Nature Conservancy, an international conservation organization, recently completed a multiyear project that protected more than 270,000 acres of forest land in Michigan’s Upper Peninsula. This grant increase supports the conservancy’s efforts to document and celebrate the completion of the project — the largest single such endeavor in the state’s history — through a variety of means including a major event for project stakeholders and an educational video.

title: Missouri Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the University of Missouri – Columbia in continuing the development of the Missouri Statewide Afterschool Network. This grantee is part of the first cohort of Mott-funded statewide afterschool networks. This renewal is an achievement grant, which continues to provide core support to the network, while also encouraging new ideas designed to align and integrate afterschool and education systems. Each network receiving an achievement grant is expected to share lessons learned and products with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: Missouri Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the University of Missouri-Columbia 4-H Center for Youth Development to coordinate the Missouri Statewide Afterschool Network. In addition to continuing the network’s core work to advance afterschool programs in Missouri, it will complete a multiyear project to create an integrated professional development system for youth professionals. The network seeks to improve the overall quality of afterschool programs through increasing the knowledge and skills of afterschool program staff and administrators. To ensure that new models and best practices are incorporated nationally, the grantee will share lessons learned and products with the other statewide afterschool networks.

title: Missouri Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the University of Missouri – Columbia which coordinates the Missouri Statewide Afterschool Network. The Missouri Statewide Afterschool Network will focus on building capacity for long-term success and advancing systems change for afterschool and expanded learning in Missouri. Over the next three years, the network will support the development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool and expanded learning programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) developing a comprehensive state campaign to increase the number of quality afterschool programs for Missouri youth; 2) increasing the number of quality professional development and college-level classes available for afterschool professionals; and 3) expanding the availability of science, technology, engineering, and math in afterschool programs.

title: Missouri Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the University of Missouri – Columbia which coordinates the Missouri Statewide Afterschool Network to continue development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) increasing communications activities to build public awareness about the importance of afterschool and the network; 2) providing microgrants to local programs to start or enhance STEM partnerships in their communities; and 3) developing resources and hosting trainings to support the afterschool field in serving children with special needs.

title: Illinois Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will continue to support the Illinois Center for Violence Prevention in its coordination of the Illinois Statewide Afterschool Network, which has been developing a public/private network of stakeholders to build a statewide afterschool system. This renewal is an achievement grant, which continues to provide core support to the network, while also encouraging new ideas designed to align and integrate afterschool and education systems. Each network receiving an achievement grant is expected to share lessons learned and products with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: Illinois Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Voices for Illinois Children to coordinate the Illinois Statewide Afterschool Network. In addition to continuing the network’s core work to advance afterschool programs in Illinois, it will complete a multiyear project to support and coordinate a new statewide youth development council. The statewide council is mandated by new legislation in Illinois, the Afterschool Youth Development Act, focused on coordinating and strengthening the state’s afterschool and youth development services. Through serving as the key facilitator of the council, the network seeks to expand youth development systems in Illinois. To ensure that new models and best practices are incorporated nationally, the network will share lessons learned and products with the other statewide afterschool networks.

title: Illinois Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Voices for Illinois Children which coordinates the Illinois Statewide Afterschool Network. The Illinois Statewide Afterschool Network will focus on building capacity for long-term success and advancing systems change for afterschool and expanded learning in Illinois. Over the course of this project, the network will create new policy initiatives, continue to build and nurture strong education partnerships, and develop messaging around state-specific data. The network’s initiatives will include: 1) expanding an afterschool champions program for educators in the state; 2) creating statewide quality standards on afterschool; and 3) activating a college and career readiness committee to link afterschool and academic success.

title: Illinois Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant to Voices for Illinois Children will support the development of the Illinois Statewide Afterschool Network to continue to build an afterschool and summer learning system that improves outcomes for children and youth through school-based or school-linked afterschool programs. Over the course of this grant, the network will support the development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) hosting six regional meetings to expand statewide afterschool champions; 2) creating a map and directory of afterschool programs in Illinois; and 3) developing statewide quality standards on afterschool.

title: Illinois Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Metropolitan Family Services which coordinates the Illinois Statewide Afterschool Network to continue development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. title: New Hampshire Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will continue to support PlusTime NH in developing New Hampshire’s statewide afterschool network. title: New Hampshire Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: Southeastern Regional Education Service Center, Inc.

In addition, the network will complete a comprehensive evaluation of the 21st Century Community Learning Centers program. To ensure that new models and best practices are incorporated nationally, the network will share lessons learned and products with the other statewide afterschool networks.

title: South Carolina Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will continue to support the South Carolina Afterschool Alliance Statewide Afterschool Network to strengthen and guide high quality, afterschool programming and policies for South Carolina’s children and youth, particularly low-income and hard-to-reach populations. description: This grant increase will provide emergency support to the South Carolina Statewide Afterschool Network. Ultimately, this support will assist the South Carolina Statewide Afterschool Network to regain its position as a robust network with a durable financial and organizational structure.

title: South Carolina Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the South Carolina Afterschool Alliance to coordinate the South Carolina Statewide Afterschool Network. Over the next three years, the network will continue to advance its core work while further strengthening its sustainability in light of state fiscal challenges. title: Rhode Island Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will continue to support the United Way of Rhode Island to further the Rhode Island Statewide Afterschool Network, a statewide afterschool network expanding and supporting high quality afterschool programs so that Rhode Island’s children are safe, supervised, and prepared to lead productive lives. This renewal is an achievement grant, which continues to provide core support to the network, while also encouraging new ideas designed to align and integrate afterschool and education systems. Each network receiving an achievement grant is expected to share lessons learned and products with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: Rhode Island Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the United Way of Rhode Island to coordinate the Rhode Island Statewide Afterschool Network. The network seeks to help communities in Rhode Island rethink their approach to summer school, promote greater collaboration among teachers and community partners, and begin the conversation about shared accountability for academic outcomes between school districts and community-based organizations. To ensure that new models and best practices are incorporated nationally, the network will share lessons learned and products with the other statewide afterschool networks.

title: Rhode Island Statewide Afterschool Network

Over the next three years, the network will seek to further institutionalize afterschool and expanded learning into the fabric of the education system in Rhode Island. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) developing a local ambassador program for afterschool and expanded learning to assist in raising awareness of the importance of expanded learning; 2) creating professional development opportunities that help afterschool and expanded learning programs further develop essential skills in the youth they serve; and 3) developing a statewide data system and measurement tools for the expanded learning field, including the 21st Century Community Learning Centers grantees.

title: Rhode Island Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the United Way of Rhode Island which coordinates the Rhode Island Statewide Afterschool Network to continue development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) increasing communications activities to build public awareness about the importance of out-of-school time; 2) working with the Grantmakers Council of Rhode Island to increase partnerships with local funders in support of out-of-school time; and 3) providing professional development for out-of-school time practitioners focused on increasing literacy skills for young people in Rhode Island.

title: North Carolina Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: Public School Forum of North Carolina

title: Vermont Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Champlain Valley Educator Development Center in continuing the development of the Vermont Statewide Afterschool Network. This grantee is part of the first cohort of Mott-funded, statewide afterschool networks. This renewal grant will continue to provide core support to the network, while also encouraging new ideas designed to align and integrate afterschool and education systems. In addition to continuing its work in building the field of afterschool in Vermont, the network will strengthen school/afterschool linkages to improve student outcomes and increase educational gains by requesting that programs from across the state create and submit video vignettes that highlight innovative learning opportunities used in their programs. The network will share lessons learned and products with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: Vermont Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Champlain Valley Educator Development Center, which coordinates the Vermont Statewide Afterschool Network. The network seeks to strengthen afterschool and expanded learning programs by developing a new partnerships for expanded learning model, which will exemplify strong partnerships between schools, communities, and afterschool programs to support student success. In addition to continuing the network’s core work to advance afterschool in Vermont, it will complete a multiyear project to: 1) develop and promote a new partnerships for expanded learning model; 2) increase the number of strong school-community partnerships throughout the state; and 3) research, document, and track examples of credit-bearing expanded learning and afterschool opportunities.

title: Vermont Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant to Vermont Afterschool will support the development of the Vermont Statewide Afterschool Network to continue to build an afterschool and summer learning system that improves outcomes for children and youth through school-based or school-linked afterschool programs. Over the next three years, the network will support the development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) engaging with program providers and other partners to promote lifelong health and child wellness through afterschool programs; 2) collecting statewide data on program availability, distribution, structure, and funding; and 3) supporting the adoption and statewide implementation of the Youth Program Quality Intervention assessment in afterschool and summer learning programs.

title: Vermont Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Vermont Afterschool, which coordinates the Vermont Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) working with the state Expanded Learning Opportunities Committee to explore educational equity in afterschool and summer programs; 2) increasing professional development opportunities focused on work-based learning and college/career pathways for young people; 3) expanding new partnerships and funding avenues to support the afterschool field in addressing adverse childhood experiences; and 4) participating in the development and distribution of new afterschool program content in collaboration with the Foundation’s thematic partners.

title: Kansas Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: University of Kansas Center for Research, Inc.

In addition to continuing the network’s core work to advance afterschool programs in Kansas, it will complete a multiyear project to build a statewide system for afterschool focused on science, technology, engineering, and math through policy, sustainability, and quality efforts. The network seeks to support a growing statewide economy focused on science, technology, engineering, and math by using afterschool to develop students’ skills to meet future workforce demands. title: Supporting the National Network of Statewide Afterschool Networks
description: This grant will continue to support the Collaborative Communications Group in its efforts to develop and grow the National Network of Statewide Afterschool Networks. Currently, the Foundation is providing partial support to 32 statewide networks, with an additional eight expected to join in the future. This project will foster cooperation and collaboration in states across the country and create opportunities for sharing strategies and challenges for furthering statewide policies that support the quality and sustainability of afterschool programs. Specifically, this grant will convene meetings and audio-conference calls, maintain a Web site and listserv, develop resources and tools, and document learnings. The Collaborative Communications Group will also assist the Mott-funded Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative in its efforts to provide technical assistance to the statewide afterschool networks. Additionally, in an effort to address the professional development needs of these networks, a leadership institute will be developed for individuals managing their statewide efforts.

title: Supporting the National Network of Statewide Afterschool Networks

title: Supporting the National Network of Statewide Afterschool Networks

title: Supporting the National Network of Statewide Afterschool Networks

The grantee will also coordinate the Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative, which now includes eight national organizations. This project will include new strategies to increase efficiency and effectiveness, such as incorporating new technology and the distribution of new afterschool publications to inform national and state afterschool policy.

title: Supporting the National Network of Statewide Afterschool Networks
description: This grant increase will support the Collaborative Communications Group in creating a more coordinated and comprehensive approach to the Learning Beyond the Classroom portfolio convenings and to enhance support to the Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative. The grantee will: 1) provide conference and logistical support for a meeting that will bring together all of the Mott grantees in the Learning Beyond the Classroom portfolio and several grantees in the Vulnerable Youth portfolio; and 2) contract to provide strategic and technical support to the Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative.

title: Supporting the National Network of Statewide Afterschool Networks
description: This grant increase will allow the Collaborative Communications Group to ramp up their work with the statewide afterschool networks and additional partners in support of the 21st Century Community Learning Centers program. The grantee will: 1) develop a Web site that will include resources for the afterschool and education field to promote school and afterschool models; 2) work with other key partners to develop a strategic communications plan targeted at school leaders; and 3) engage key partners, including the statewide afterschool networks, state education agencies, and 21st Century Community Learning Center representatives, in discussions and strategic meetings.

title: Supporting the National Network of Statewide Afterschool Networks
description: This grant increase will enable the Collaborative Communications Group to continue to expand their work with the statewide afterschool networks and additional partners in support of the 21st Century Community Learning Centers program. Collaborative Communications Group will support the networks to disseminate new research and engage additional educators; hold statewide summits; support briefings on new afterschool research; and highlight the promising practices demonstrating that afterschool and summer learning programs are essential for children and youth.

title: Supporting the National Network of Statewide Afterschool Networks
description: This grant increase will support Collaborative Communications Group to continue to grow their work with the Expanded Learning and Afterschool Project and reach out to the remaining nine non-network states to foster additional statewide afterschool networks. The grantee will work with organizations in these nine states to bring representatives to the 2013 Statewide Afterschool National Network annual meeting. Organization representatives will participate in discussions and work sessions on issues most critical to building an afterschool network, focusing on partnerships, sustainability, and quality. The inclusion of all 50 states will strengthen the Statewide Afterschool Network and the Expanded Learning and Afterschool Project.

title: Supporting the National Network of Statewide Afterschool Networks
description: This grant will enable the Collaborative Communications Group to support the Statewide Afterschool Networks and the Expanded Learning and Afterschool Project. title: Supporting the National Network of Statewide Afterschool Networks

title: Study on Education Organizing and Academic Improvement

description: This grant will provide partial support to the Community Coalition for Substance Abuse Prevention and Treatment to continue to implement an initiative to provide universal access to college preparatory courses for south Los Angeles high schools. This project is intended to reduce dropout rates, improve college preparedness, and boost college attendance. In addition, this grant will enable the organization to participate in the Foundation’s eight-site study to explore the contribution of education organizing to education reform efforts in low-performing districts and schools.

title: Central Eurasia Leadership Academy
geographic_focus: Azerbaijan, Uzbekistan, Afghanistan, Kazakhstan, Armenia, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan
description: This grant supports an innovative, transformational leadership program targeting two former Soviet regions — Central Asia and the Caucasus — in need of international attention and assistance. The goal of the program is to promote regional cooperation, international integration, and peace and security in Central Eurasia. Through training workshops, policy seminars and other capacity-building opportunities, the Global Network Foundation (GNF) will build the skills of promising leaders from Central Eurasia and raise awareness about these regions among Western leaders.GNF was established in 2002 by the Society of International Business Fellows (SIBF). Its mission is to facilitate global philanthropy in partnership with foundations, corporations and individuals by leveraging the expertise, relationships and resources of SIBF members toward further global understanding.

title: Community Development in Ukraine Through Community School Programs
description: The program goal is to expand and improve the community school model in Ukraine. To this end, Ukrainian Step by Step Foundation will establish regional training centers, train trainers, and introduce courses on community schools into teacher training institutes. The grantee will also promote social entrepreneurship among students, fostering innovative business education programs linked to community development goals; promote quality standards in the implementation of community school programs; support the development and growth of student councils within schools; and facilitate the development of an informal network of community schools at the regional, national, and international levels. By the end of the grant period, the number of community schools across all regions of Ukraine is forecast to reach almost 200. This project builds on successful efforts to introduce the community school model to over 100 schools in the past three years. The Ukrainian Step by Step Foundation was created as an independent foundation in 1999 with the aim of facilitating educational development and innovative educational initiatives in Ukraine.

title: Community Development in Ukraine Through Community School Programs
description: Beginning with seven schools in 2003, the Ukrainian Step by Step Foundation has expanded the number of community schools to 447 in 25 of Ukraine’s 27 regions by mid-2010. Hundreds of school teachers and administrators have received training on community schools through regional teacher training institutes using curricula that were developed by the grantee. Over the next three years, the grantee will expand the program to another 360 schools; promote the adoption of international quality standards; work with education officials and regional teacher training institutes to improve and expand the community school curriculum; advocate for policy changes that will institutionalize the best practices of community schools; and assemble, develop, and maintain an online database of resources on community school development. The Ukrainian Step by Step Foundation was created as an independent foundation in 1999 with the aim of facilitating educational development and innovative educational initiatives in Ukraine.

title: Community Development in Ukraine Through Community School Programs
description: The Ukrainian Step by Step Foundation was created as an independent foundation in 1999 with the aim of supporting educational development, facilitating the implementation and dissemination of innovative educational initiatives, and encouraging the development of nonprofit and charitable organizations working in the area of education in Ukraine. Since 2003, it has worked successfully to introduce and develop community schools in Ukraine as a model for democratic education and community engagement. A grant increase will allow the grantee to produce a training video intended to promote the understanding and practice of community schools in Ukraine and beyond.

title: Community Development in Ukraine Through Community School Programs
description: The program goal is to further extend and embed the model of community schools in Ukraine. To date, the Ukrainian Step by Step Foundation has increased to over 800 the number of schools that are using or operating under community school principles. In-service teacher training institutes in all 27 of Ukraine’s regions provide systematic support for this expansion through training curricula developed by the grantee. In Lviv, the grantee’s efforts resulted in inclusion of community schools as a priority program area in the regional educational development strategy. In 2014-2016, the grantee will shift focus from expansion to consolidation and sustainability of community schools. It will advocate for adoption of international quality standards as a participatory monitoring tool for community school development. It will also seek adoption of further state-funded regional educational programs which include community schools at their core. The Ukrainian Step by Step Foundation was created as an independent foundation in 1999 with the aim of facilitating educational development and innovative educational initiatives in Ukraine.

title: Community Development in Ukraine Through Community School Programs
description: The program goal is to further extend and embed the model of community schools in Ukraine. The Ukrainian Step by Step Foundation has increased the number of schools that are operating under community school principles to over 800. In-service teacher training institutes in all 27 of Ukraine’s regions provide systematic support for this expansion through training curricula developed by the grantee. In 2014-2016, the grantee will shift focus from expansion to issues of sustainability and adoption of international quality standards and implementation of state-funded regional educational programs, which include community schools at their core. A grant increase will support training and assistance to community schools that are struggling to integrate children and their families that have been displaced due to the fighting in eastern Ukraine. The Ukrainian Step by Step Foundation was established in 1999 with the aim of facilitating educational development and innovative educational initiatives in Ukraine.

title: Community Development in Ukraine Through Community School Programs
description: The program goal is to further extend and embed the model of community schools in Ukraine. To date, the Ukrainian Step by Step Foundation has increased to over 800 schools that are using or operating under community school principles. The grantee continued to provide and refine curricula for all 22 in-service teacher training institutes controlled by Ukrainian authorities. The Ministry of Education has adopted the International Quality Standards for Community Schools that the grantee helped develop as a monitoring tool for school development. In addition, the grantee piloted specialized programs for internally displaced persons in four regions. In 2017-2019, the grantee will shift focus from expansion to consolidation and sustainability of community schools in the context of progressive education reforms in Ukraine. It will work to enhance and disseminate an improved model of participatory quality assessment for Ukrainian schools while strengthening key areas of teaching and learning around entrepreneurship. The Ukrainian Step by Step Foundation was created in 1999 with the aim of facilitating educational development and innovative educational initiatives in Ukraine.

title: Asset Building Program
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: Established in 2002, New America Foundation’s Asset-Building Program seeks to significantly broaden the ownership of assets in America, especially among low- and moderate-income households, thereby providing all Americans with both the means to get ahead and a direct stake in the overall success of the U.S. economy. To achieve this goal, the program works in three areas: policy research and development, communications and information dissemination, and policymaker education.This grant will enable New America Foundation to continue generating new knowledge about the benefits of broadly shared wealth; attracting new audiences to asset building concepts through media and communications efforts; creating new constituents for asset building among policymakers and other high-profile public figures and opinion makers; and developing and advancing new policies to help low-income Americans build assets.

title: Asset Building Program
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: The New America Foundation’s Asset Building Program seeks to broaden the ownership of assets in America, especially among low- and moderate-income households, thereby providing all Americans with increased financial security as well as a direct stake in the success of our economy. title: Asset Building Program
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: The New America Foundation’s Asset Building Program seeks to broaden the ownership of assets in America, especially among low- and moderate-income households, thereby providing all Americans with increased financial security, as well as a direct stake in the success of our economy. To achieve this goal, the program conducts policy research, develops asset policy ideas, educates policymakers, and communicates the benefits of asset building to journalists and the general public. The New America Foundation is a public policy institute whose purpose is to bring new voices and ideas to the fore of America’s public discourse by investing in outstanding individuals and ideas that transcend the conventional political spectrum.

title: Asset Building Program
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: The New America Foundation’s Asset Building Program seeks to broaden access to economic resources through increased savings and asset ownership, thereby providing families with enhanced economic security, a potential pathway out of poverty, and the means to pursue their aspirations. To advance this vision, the program conducts policy research, develops policy ideas, educates policymakers, and communicates the benefits of asset building to diverse audiences including journalists, program administrators, and the general public. This renewal grant will support the grantee’s efforts to promote children’s savings account programs and policies primarily across states. The specific activities proposed for the grant period include: 1) working with state and local stakeholders to develop and promote children’s savings account policy ideas; 2) highlighting children’s savings account program design and implementation best practices; and 3) advancing policymakers’ understanding and leadership of children’s savings account strategies. The New America Foundation is a public policy institute whose purpose is to bring new voices and ideas to the fore of America’s public discourse by investing in outstanding individuals and ideas that transcend the conventional political spectrum.

title: Flint Healthcare Employment Opportunities Project
description: The Greater Flint Health Coalition was established in 1992 to improve the health status of Genesee County residents and to improve the quality and cost-effectiveness of the healthcare delivery system.This grant will enable the coalition’s Flint Healthcare Employment Opportunities Project to work with health industry employers to restructure their hiring, retention and promotional practices for healthcare employees. In addition, the project will continue to enroll new clients, provide career paths for existing clients and participate in regional economic development initiatives.The project recently was selected by the U.S. Department of Labor to participate in a 13-county initiative designed to help diversify the regional economy.

title: Building Excellence, Sustainability and Trust (BEST) Nonprofit Capacity Building
description: This grant will provide continued support to the United Way of Genesee County for the Building Excellence, Sustainability and Trust project, which is an initiative designed to build the capacity of Genesee County nonprofit organizations to meet the ever increasing needs of their clients and the community. A second cohort of nine Genesee County nonprofit agencies has completed an organizational assessment and with this funding will receive capacity building and technical assistance by a vetted pool of experienced consultants. Evaluations to assess the internal and external effectiveness of participating agencies as well as the program’s impact on the community will continue. The other funders of this local collaboration include the Community Foundation of Greater Flint and the Ruth Mott Foundation.

description: This grant increase will enable the Community Foundation Network to provide key staff to direct the Worldwide Initiative for Grantmakers Support network. Currently, there are more than 100 grantmaker associations across some 40 countries participating in the network. The staff and board members of these organizations benefit significantly from international exchange, information services, networking and peer-to-peer learning opportunities.

title: Worldwide Initiatives for Grantmaker Support
description: The project goal is to promote and develop philanthropy globally. Worldwide Initiatives for Grantmaker Support is a global network linking grantmaker associations and support organizations through international exchange, information services, networking, and peer-to-peer learning opportunities. During 2003-2006, the network was hosted by the European Foundation Centre in Brussels. Accomplishments during this period included increasing the membership from 85 to 140; organizing eight peer learning events and exchange visits; producing several publications on relevant topics; and convening important meetings and events, such as the Community Foundation Global Symposium in Berlin in 2004 and the Worldwide Initiatives for Grantmaker Support Forum in Bangkok in 2006. From January 2007 through 2010, the network will be hosted by the Asia Pacific Philanthropy Consortium in Manila.

title: Worldwide Initiatives for Grantmaker Support
description: The project goal is to promote and develop philanthropy globally. Worldwide Initiatives for Grantmaker Support is a global network linking grantmaker associations and support organizations through international exchange, information services, networking, and peer-to-peer learning opportunities. During 2007-2008, the network was managed by the Asia Pacific Philanthropy Consortium in Manila. Accomplishments during this period include adding thirteen new members, organizing seven peer learning events and exchange visits, and producing several publications on relevant topics. During 2009-2010, in addition to continuing its capacity-building activities for grantmaker associations and support organizations, the network will focus on ensuring its own institutional sustainability. The Asia Pacific Philanthropy Consortium is an independent association of grantmaking institutions and organizations that support the growth and development of philanthropy in the Asia Pacific region.

title: General Purposes
description: The goal of Worldwide Initiatives for Grantmaker Support is to strengthen the global infrastructure for philanthropy. The grantee is a global network linking grantmaker associations and support organizations through international exchange, information services, networking, and peer-to-peer learning opportunities. During 2007-2010, the network was hosted by the Asia Pacific Philanthropy Consortium in the Philippines. Recent accomplishments include the organization of peer learning events and exchange visits, the hosting of a global forum, and the publication of two global philanthropy status reports. As of the beginning of 2011, the grantee has incorporated as a nonprofit organization in the United States and established an office in Brazil. During this grant period, the grantee will pursue three main objectives: 1) strengthen its institutional capacity; 2) secure its financial sustainability; and 3) strengthen its role as a global leader advocating for an enabling environment for philanthropy.

Recent accomplishments include the hosting of a global forum, organization of Webinars and peer learning events, the development of several useful knowledge products, the creation of a Global Philanthropy Data Charter and associated web site, and the expansion of paid membership. During the grant period, the grantee will pursue the following strategic areas: 1) thought leadership; 2) network building and engagement; 3) knowledge and capacity building; and 4) governance and sustainability. This will include the preparation of a global forum in 2017, 16 Webinars, four face-to-face regional learning and sharing meetings, a toolkit on transparency and accountability, case studies on local cultures of giving, two new reports for the Infrastructure in Focus Series, and other activities.

title: General Purposes
description: Worldwide Initiatives for Grantmaker Support is a global network linking 86 philanthropic associations and support organizations from 35 countries through international exchange, information services, networking, and peer-to-peer learning opportunities. While working in different contexts, the grantee’s members share a common vision of a strong, global philanthropic community that strives to build more equitable and just societies around the world. The grantee works in the following strategic areas: 1) thought leadership; 2) network building and engagement; 3) knowledge and capacity building; and 4) governance and sustainability. Over the next two years, this will include the preparation of a global forum in 2017, 16 Webinars, four face-to-face regional learning and sharing meetings, a toolkit on transparency and accountability, case studies on local cultures of giving, two new reports for an Infrastructure in Focus Series, and other activities. This grant increase will support a recruitment process for a new executive director.

title: General Purposes
description: Worldwide Initiatives for Grantmaker Support is a global network linking 140 philanthropic associations and support organizations from 39 countries through international exchange, information services, networking, and peer-to-peer learning opportunities. The network has been pursuing the following strategic areas: 1) leadership and advocacy; 2) network building and engagement; 3) knowledge and capacity development; and 4) governance and sustainability. During 2017-2018, the grantee will hold a global forum, continue working on enabling the environment for philanthropy, establish 2-3 affinity groups, conduct 15 webinars, develop four case studies for the Global Philanthropy Data Charter program, and draft a Global Landscape of Philanthropy report, among other activities. Established in 2000, Worldwide Initiatives for Grantmaker Support has operated as a project of the Council on Foundations, European Foundation Center, and the Asia Pacific Philanthropy Consortium. It was incorporated in the United States in 2010 and established an office in Sao Paulo, Brazil, in 2011.

title: Environmental Partnership for Central Europe - Endowment Building
description: The Ekopolis Foundation’s project goal is to strengthen the financial stability of the Environmental Partnership for Sustainable Development member organizations. To this end, the partnership members from the Czech Republic, Hungary, Romania, and Slovakia will conduct fundraising campaigns in their respective countries as well as a joint international campaign with the goal of raising over $1.6 million for their endowments and reserve funds during 2007-2010. Members of the Environmental Partnership for Sustainable Development provide grants and capacity-building services to nonprofits in their respective countries. At the beginning of 2007, their collective endowment had reached $7 million.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to promote citizen participation in decisionmaking processes through supporting a leading Russian public policy center and its efforts to strengthen other regional public policy centers in Russia. During 2008-2010, Strategy Center will continue its programs in the areas of budget transparency, corruption prevention, and public monitoring of government bodies. It will add a new advisory function to assist informal citizen participation in social and economic rights protection activities. In addition, Strategy Center will provide information services, networking opportunities, and technical assistance to other Russian regional public policy centers. Established in 1993, Strategy Center is a prominent, independent, analytical institution which links community initiatives and nongovernmental organization advocacy efforts with public policy development. It has recently helped establish six new public policy centers in Russia and regularly supports the work of over 70 other such institutions.

title: Replicate Sectoral Initiatives
description: This grant will continue support to the Interfaith Education Fund to replicate and expand the scale of its sectoral employment initiatives throughout the Southwest. The grantee’s sectoral employment initiatives define the skills required to succeed in targeted, hard-to-fill occupations with viable career ladders, and then recruit, train, and develop low-income adults so that they are qualified and ready to fill employers’ needs for skilled workers. Multiyear funding will enable the Interfaith Education Fund to replicate its work in Phoenix; Houston; Monroe, Louisiana; and Los Angeles, and increase the number being served by initiatives in San Antonio, El Paso, Austin, the Lower Rio Grand Valley, and Tucson.

title: Replicate Sectoral Initiatives
description: This grant will continue to support the Interfaith Education Fund’s efforts to replicate and expand sectoral employment initiatives. These initiatives have demonstrated how social and economic benefits can be achieved through investments in long-term training for those who otherwise would not have the opportunity. The grantee’s work with sectoral employment initiatives defines the skills required to succeed in targeted, hard-to-fill occupations with viable career ladders, and then recruits, trains, and develops low-income adults so that they are qualified and ready to fill employers’ needs for skilled workers. Funding will enable the grantee to increase the number being served by existing initiatives in Texas, Arizona, Iowa, and Louisiana and to work with leaders in several California cities, as well as Albuquerque, New Mexico, to launch similar strategies in their communities.

title: Building a Statewide Coalition for Education Improvement in Wisconsin
grantee: Citizen Action of Wisconsin Education Fund
description: This grant will provide partial support to the Citizen Action of Wisconsin Education Fund for organizing efforts to increase the power of low-income residents to become effective education advocates in their communities. Most of the community organizing efforts are centered in Milwaukee, the largest school system in the state that also serves the majority of low-income students and students of color; however, the organization also works at the state level to secure education funding. The project goals include working to improve educational opportunities for students in low-income neighborhoods by focusing on sustaining and expanding funding for afterschool programs, recruiting and training new community leaders, and increasing the participation of low-income residents in grassroots organizing activities.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Arizona, Iowa, New Mexico, Louisiana, California, Texas, Nebraska
description: The Interfaith Education Fund (IEF) was created in 1989 to assist organizations affiliated with the Industrial Areas Foundation in addressing conditions affecting their communities. IEF provides professional organizing, research and technical support for the local organizations and has a record of success in the areas of economic development and education reform.This grant will enable IEF to build the capacity of its 27 member organizations in seven states in the areas of leadership training, staff supervision, professional organizer development, program evaluation and issue research in response to needs expressed locally.During the past two years, IEF has focused much of its attention on renewing a vigorous public debate on the role and value of public education. Four large regional workshops were held that focused on the struggle to balance the necessity for accountability with the needs of students and teachers to have the opportunity for creative and genuine learning. Also, IEF leaders have worked to develop the new “Civic Academy,” a six-session training institute designed to teach the history, role and value of the public sector in the U.S. IEF’s most demanding work during the past two years was the organizing of evacuees from communities affected by hurricanes Katrina and Rita.
