title: Southern Water Management Project
geographic_focus: Georgia, Alabama, North Carolina, Tennessee, South Carolina
description: The rivers and streams of the southeastern United States support plant and animal communities with globally significant biological diversity. Challenges to these habitats are mounting as the South’s population grows, creating a need for long-term water management that will conserve natural resources while meeting human demand. With previous support, the Southern Environmental Law Center, a leader in protecting water resources in the Southeast, has led efforts to develop state and regional water management plans that will sustain aquatic habitat locally and regionally. Renewal support will enable the center to maximize opportunities to promote water resource planning on a watershed basis; support the development of new, sustainable policies; and monitor progress by states in meeting protection goals.

title: Southern Water Management Project
geographic_focus: Georgia, Alabama, North Carolina, Tennessee, South Carolina
description: The recent cycle of droughts in the Southeast has led states to acknowledge the need for better water management. The significant population growth predicted for the region also increases the need to create and implement sustainable water management plans. The Southern Environmental Law Center, a well-respected regional group, works to protect the biodiversity of the Southeast’s freshwater resources as states and localities make water management decisions. In recent years, the center has worked with partner organizations to improve water management policies in Georgia, North Carolina, and neighboring states. With continued support from Mott, the center will help implement policies recently adopted in Georgia, while seeking new policy reforms in North Carolina, South Carolina, and other states.

title: Southern Water Management Project
geographic_focus: Georgia, Alabama, Tennessee, North Carolina, South Carolina
description: The Southern Environmental Law Center, a leading regional environmental group, works to protect the biodiversity of the Southeast’s freshwater resources as states and localities make water management decisions. In recent years, the grantee has worked with partner organizations to improve water management policies in five southeastern states: North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia, Alabama, and Tennessee. With continued support from Mott, the grantee will help implement policies recently adopted in many of these states and push for additional policy improvements in all of them.

title: Southern Water Management Project
geographic_focus: Georgia, Alabama, Tennessee, North Carolina, South Carolina
description: The Southern Environmental Law Center, a leading regional environmental group, works to protect the biodiversity of the Southeast’s freshwater resources at the federal, state, and local levels. With continued support from Mott, the grantee will help design and implement water management policies in five states with an emphasis on promoting water conservation and efficiency measures. The project will also include efforts to slow the push for new reservoirs when they are unnecessary and improve the operation of existing hydropower dams in order to enhance freshwater habitat.

title: Southern Water Management Project
geographic_focus: North Carolina, Tennessee, Alabama, Georgia, South Carolina
description: The Southern Environmental Law Center, a leading regional environmental group, works to protect the biodiversity of the Southeast’s freshwater resources. The grantee will continue to help design and implement water management policies in five states with an emphasis on promoting water use efficiency. The project will also include efforts to slow the push for new reservoirs when they are unnecessary and improve the operation of existing hydropower dams in order to enhance freshwater habitat. Special attention will be given to ongoing efforts by the state of Alabama to develop a comprehensive water management policy.

title: Southern Water Management Project
geographic_focus: Tennessee, Alabama, North Carolina, Georgia, South Carolina
description: With this grant increase, the Southern Environmental Law Center, a leading regional environmental organization, will research new approaches to water management from across the United States to inform related policy reform efforts in Georgia.

title: Southern Water Management Project
geographic_focus: North Carolina, Tennessee, Alabama, Georgia, South Carolina
description: The Southern Environmental Law Center, a regional public-interest law group, uses a blend of legal and policy strategies to address water management challenges facing five southeastern states of interest to Mott: North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia, Alabama, and Tennessee. The grantee will continue its regionwide efforts to promote comprehensive, science-based water planning; make water conservation and efficiency the cornerstone of state and local water policies; recover and maintain healthy flows in the Southeast’s waterways; and ensure that new water infrastructure proposals are necessary and cost-effective.

title: U.S./Mexico Border Philanthropy Partnership
geographic_focus: Arizona, Texas, Mexico, California, New Mexico
description: This grant continues support to the U.S.-Mexico Border Philanthropy Partnership, formed in 2002, in order to expand philanthropy and improve the quality of life in the U.S.-Mexico border region. Currently, 19 community foundations are members of the partnership. Over the past five years, members have shared best practices, learned together about important border issues, leveraged almost $20 million to strengthen their institutional capacities and support programs in their border communities, and developed cross-border ties. In its next phase, the partnership plans to become an independent nonprofit organization. Its membership base will expand to include not only community foundations but also other types of border philanthropic institutions, programs, and individuals. The International Community Foundation will take a leadership role in transitioning the partnership from a Synergos Institute-managed project to a new entity and also act as the partnership’s fiscal sponsor until the new entity becomes fully incorporated.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: California, Arizona, Texas, Mexico, New Mexico
description: The U.S.-Mexico Border Philanthropy Partnership was launched in 2002 with a vision toward improving the quality of life in the U.S.-Mexico border region. For its first six years, the partnership was run as a project of the Synergos Institute and mainly focused on building community philanthropy institutions. In 2008, the partnership became an independent, locally driven, binational entity. Its membership expanded to involve other types of foundations, corporate giving programs, philanthropic individuals, academics, and nonprofit organizations in the border region. Goals for the next two years are to: 1) catalyze new and more effective leadership in the border region; 2) offer a robust member services program; 3) create a diversified and socially responsible membership base; 4) expand and strengthen relationships and organizations collaborating across the border; 5) enhance communication to become the voice for philanthropy in the border region; and 6) establish a sustainable organization with diverse revenue streams.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Mexico, New Mexico, Texas, Arizona, California
description: The U.S.-Mexico Border Philanthropy Partnership was launched in 2002 with a vision toward improving the quality of life in the U.S.-Mexico border region. Initially, the partnership was run as a project of the Synergos Institute and focused mainly on community foundations. In 2008, the partnership became an independent, locally driven, binational entity involving all types of foundations, corporate giving programs, philanthropic individuals, academics, and nonprofit organizations in the border region. Over the past two years, the partnership grew from 45 to 90 members, provided capacity building technical assistance to members, facilitated connections between organizations from various sectors, and significantly raised awareness of cross-border issues. Goals for the next two years include continuing to grow the partnership, offering a robust member services program; increasing the effectiveness of border-serving organizations; strengthening family asset-building programming in a binational context; and implementing the U.S.-Mexico Data Collaborative Project.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: New Mexico, Mexico, Texas, Arizona, California
description: The U.S.-Mexico Border Philanthropy Partnership was launched in 2002 as a project of the Synergos Institute, mainly focused on community foundation development. In 2008, the partnership became an independent binational entity involving all types of foundations, corporate giving programs, philanthropic individuals, academics, and nonprofit organizations. Its mission is to support a network of organizations that build prosperity through leadership, collaboration, and philanthropy in the U.S.-Mexico border region. Over the past four years, the partnership has grown from 45 to 218 members, provided capacity-building technical assistance to members, facilitated connections between organizations from various sectors, and significantly raised awareness of cross-border issues. Goals for the next two years include expanding membership and offering a robust member services program, leading and advocating on transborder issues of interest to members, strengthening the philanthropic capacity of transborder communities, strengthening the partnership’s own internal capacity and infrastructure, and implementing the U.S.-Mexico Data Collaborative Project.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: New Mexico, Texas, Mexico, California, Arizona
description: The U.S.-Mexico Border Philanthropy Partnership was launched in 2002 as a project of the Synergos Institute, mainly focused on community foundation development. In 2008, the grantee became an independent binational entity involving all types of foundations, corporate giving programs, philanthropic individuals, academics, and nonprofit organizations. Its mission is to support a network of organizations that build prosperity through leadership, collaboration, and philanthropy in the U.S.-Mexico border region. Over the past six years, the grantee has grown from 45 to 275 members, provided capacity building technical assistance to members, facilitated connections between organizations from various sectors, and significantly raised awareness of cross border issues. Goals for the next two years include expanding membership and offering a robust member services program, leading and advocating on transborder issues of interest to members, strengthening the philanthropic capacity of transborder communities, strengthening the grantee’s own internal capacity and infrastructure, and implementing the U.S.-Mexico Borderlands Mapping Project.

title: General Purposes
description: The BBB Wise Giving Alliance produces in-depth evaluative reports on national charities based on comprehensive standards for charity accountability and publishes a quarterly magazine, the “Better Business Bureau Wise Giving Guide”. National charities meeting the standards can apply to participate in the alliance’s National Charity Seal program. This grant will enable the alliance to expand its coverage of national charities; improve and integrate local Better Business Bureau charity review programs; and extend the use and recognition of the National Charity Seal. With the recent launch of an online charity reporting and evaluation system, the alliance has dramatically increased the number of reports on national charities (approximately 800 annually), as well as the number of National Charity Seal holders (122).

title: Strengthening Nonprofit Fiscal Sustainability, Accountability, and Civic Participation
description: The Strengthening Nonprofit Fiscal Sustainability, Accountability and Civic Participation project is focused on defending and expanding nonprofit policy advocacy by making sure federal grantees understand the rules covering advocacy-related activities.This grant will provide support to the final year of the project. Activities will include completing the three-volume guide, “Nonprofit Advocacy and Living with Federal Funds”; continuing to monitor and report on changes to federal grant rules; and providing technical assistance and training on those rules to nonprofit organizations.During the past year and a half the project developed basic, up-to-date research on federal grant rules regarding advocacy; created a detailed outline for a three-part, user-friendly primer on the federal grant rules governing advocacy; posted basic materials on-line; delivered presentations regarding grant rules at numerous conferences and meetings around the country; and provided technical assistance to numerous additional organizations via e-mail and telephone.

title: General Purposes
description: The Center for Effective Philanthropy provides management and governance tools to help foundations define, assess and improve overall performance. In the spring of 2003, the center began the first phase of the Foundation Governance Project in order to help community foundation leaders better understand the performance of their foundations.This grant will provide general support to the center as it launches Phase III of the Foundation Governance Project; pilots a new initiative that studies foundation strategy development; continues to mine grantee perception data and publish a second report; expands the use of various assessment tools; continues to promote publications, research and assessment tools through its newsletter and presentations at national and regional conferences; and hosts a conference that will explore the challenges of improving foundation performance.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purposes support to the Center for Effective Philanthropy. The center provides management and governance tools to define, assess, and improve overall foundation performance. Since launching its first assessment tool in 2003, more than 120 foundations have commissioned the center’s Grantee Perception Report and have made significant improvements as a result. The center has developed four other assessment tools. Its research reports on topics such as effectiveness indicators, governance, strategy, and grantee-grantor relationships have influenced practice at many of the country’s largest foundations. Over the next two years, the center will broaden its research agenda, expand its assessment tool offerings, undertake important programming, and develop a stronger infrastructure through new hiring, investments in technology, and the establishment of a West Coast office.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purpose support to the Center for Effective Philanthropy, which provides management and governance tools to define, assess, and improve the overall performance of foundations. Since launching its first assessment tool in 2003, the center has developed another six, and about 170 foundations have used these tools to make significant improvements to their organizations. The center’s research on topics such as effectiveness indicators, governance, strategy, and grantee-grantor relationships has influenced the practices of many of the country’s largest foundations. Over the next two years, the center will broaden its research agenda, expand its assessment tool offerings, and publish and disseminate several case studies, research reports, and newsletters.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purpose support to the Center for Effective Philanthropy. Established in 2000, the grantee is a nonprofit organization focused on helping philanthropic funders better define, assess, and improve their effectiveness and intended impact. The grantee’s research, assessment tools, programming, and communications provide data and insight that encourage improvement. Upcoming initiatives over the next two years include: several new research publications on foundation topics such as operational benchmarking, understanding of their ultimate beneficiaries, and further analysis of transparency; improving the grantee’s core assessment tools as well as the development of new advisory service offerings; greater visibility through a redesigned Web site and blog, op-eds, and increased focus on programming and Webinars; and executing beneficiary surveys via the center’s YouthTruth Project to provide the perspective of students to their schools, districts/networks, and funders.

title: Training Ethnic Communities to Protect Their Rights
description: The program goal is to build the capacity of ethnic minority organizations in Russia to protect their rights through effective interaction with local government authorities and law enforcement agencies. Through the Center for Interethnic Cooperation’s training programs, participants in no fewer than 15 regions of Russia will establish joint outreach projects in each location and will subsequently monitor the implementation of these projects aimed at fostering tolerance for ethnic minorities. The program will also strengthen links between ethnic minority associations across Russia and build their capacity for collective action. To date, the center’s efforts have resulted in six regional governments in Russia providing substantial financial support to programs promoting ethnic tolerance in local communities. Since 1997, the center has worked to combat ethnic discrimination through a combination of research, training of minority organizations, and promotion of social dialogue with government agencies.

title: Export Credit Agency/International Finance Institution Reform Program
description: Pacific Environment has done critical work to catalyze international work to reform the policies of export credit agencies and undertake broad public and media outreach on high profile projects funded by export credit agencies. This grant increase will support Pacific Environment’s efforts to expand its work in Japan to reform Asian export credit agency policies and bolster its work on the environmental impacts of the Sakhalin-II oil and gas pipeline in the Russian Far East.

title: Responsible Finance Campaign
description: Pacific Environment’s Responsible Finance Campaign promotes environmental and social policies among public and private international finance institutions. The principal focus of its work is on the oil, gas, mining, and forestry investments made in the Pacific Rim region. Pacific Environment has successfully persuaded international lending institutions to be more open, accountable, and responsive to community concerns. Over the grant period, it will emphasize project-specific monitoring, particularly of the Sakhalin II oil and gas project in the Russian Far East. In addition, this renewal grant will support Pacific Environment’s increased efforts to reform Japanese financing agencies, continued leadership role in international export credit reform efforts, and expanded focus on international private bank reform.

title: Responsible Finance Campaign
description: Pacific Environment’s Responsible Finance Campaign promotes environmental and social policies among public and private international finance institutions. The principal focus of its work is on the oil, gas, mining, and forestry investments made in the Pacific Rim region. Building on the grantee’s past successes in reforming international finance institutions, it will expand efforts to reform the policies and practices of key public and private international finance institutions over the next two years. Pacific Environment’s work will have a global impact on social and environmental standards for large-scale extractive and energy projects while also creating precedent-setting policies to ensure that international financial institutions apply improved standards around the world.

title: Responsible Finance Campaign
description: With Mott support, Pacific Environment promotes environmental and social policies among public and private international finance institutions. The principal focus of its work is on resource extraction and fossil fuel sectors addressing environmental, social, developmental, corruption, and general accountability concerns. Over the past grant, the grantee’s work helped to shape new policies at domestic export credit agencies that surpass all other international financial institutions on greenhouse gas emission reductions. Building on the grantee’s past successes in reforming international finance institutions, it will expand efforts to address greenhouse gas emissions and limit financing of fossil fuel projects by domestic export credit agencies over the next two years.

title: Responsible Finance Campaign
description: With Mott support, Pacific Environment promotes environmental and social policies among international finance institutions. The principal focus of its work will be on fossil fuel lending and climate change. Over the past two years, the grantee’s work helped to ensure that lending for renewable energy projects by domestic export credit agencies increased substantially. With this renewal grant, the grantee will build on its success in expanding renewable energy lending by domestic export credit agencies and the World Bank Group, as well as monitoring similar lending for infrastructure projects.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant promotes democratization, decentralization, and cooperation among states and ethnic groups in the Western Balkans. The Center for Regionalism works with other nongovernmental organizations, political and civic leaders, and government officials to develop and implement initiatives addressing specific cross-border issues and facilitating dialogue among ethnic, religious, and national groups. In 2005-2006 the grantee organized five regional meetings of government officials and nongovernmental organizations to promote the normalization of political, economic, and cultural relations among Croatia, Bosnia, and Serbia; helped to reestablish links between nongovernmental organizations in Serbia proper and Kosovo through exchanges and study visits; and organized community-based, roundtable discussions on issues of responsibility, truth, justice, and reconciliation relating to the wars of the last decade. The center is based in Novi Sad, Serbia, and works closely with organizations in Bosnia, Croatia, and Kosovo on a range of activities.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant promotes democratization, decentralization, and cooperation among states and ethnic groups in the Western Balkans. During 2009-2010, the Center for Regionalism will support regional cooperation and reconciliation through a range of mutually reinforcing initiatives, including organizing meetings and working groups to address specific issues of common concern among Croatia, Bosnia, Kosovo, Montenegro, and Serbia; strengthening a regional association of multiethnic towns and cities; and initiating and participating in activities to enable people in Serbia and the region to deal with the past. In 2007-2008, the grantee organized regional meetings of government officials and nongovernmental organizations to promote the normalization of political, economic, and cultural relations among Croatia, Bosnia, and Serbia and helped to reestablish links between nongovernmental organizations in Serbia and Kosovo through exchanges and study visits. The center is based in Novi Sad, Serbia.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant promotes democratization, decentralization, and cooperation among states and ethnic groups in the Western Balkans. During 2011, the Center for Regionalism will support regional cooperation and reconciliation through a range of mutually reinforcing initiatives, including organizing meetings and working groups to address specific issues of common concern among Croatia, Bosnia, Kosovo, Montenegro, and Serbia; strengthening a regional association of multiethnic towns and cities; and initiating and participating in activities to enable people in Serbia and the region to deal with the past. In 2009-2010, the grantee organized regional meetings of government officials and nongovernmental organizations to promote the normalization of political, economic, and cultural relations among Croatia, Bosnia, and Serbia and helped to reestablish links between nongovernmental organizations in Serbia proper and Kosovo through exchanges and study visits. The center is based in Novi Sad, Serbia.

title: Community Transformation and Capacity Building Programme
grantee: Project for Conflict Resolution and Development
description: The Project for Conflict Resolution and Development works primarily in the Eastern Cape province of South Africa to conduct research, as well as design and facilitate processes that enable disadvantaged and/or at-risk communities and organizations to deal with conflict and transformation. Previous Mott support enabled the organization to provide training and support to ward committees, the formal structures through which communities participate in local government, in the Cacadu district municipality in the Eastern Cape province. This also involved conducting good governance surveys of the local municipalities within the district and training and mentoring mediators on conflict resolution. This grant will support the grantee to train ward committees and community development workers in the Eastern Cape province and to provide training and support for the successful resolution of conflicts in the implementation of development projects.

title: Community Transformation and Capacity Building Programme
grantee: Project for Conflict Resolution and Development
description: The Project for Conflict Resolution and Development works in the Eastern Cape province conducting research and designing and facilitating processes that enable disadvantaged and at-risk communities and community-based organizations to better deal with conflict and transformation. With prior Mott funding, the project provided training and support to ward committees, the formal structures through which communities participate in local government in various municipalities and districts of the Eastern Cape. Past activities also included conducting good governance surveys in local municipalities and training and mentoring mediators on conflict resolution. This renewal grant will support continuation of capacity- building activities for ward committees, community development workers, and community-based organizations for several municipalities in the Eastern Cape. It will also provide training and support for the resolution of conflicts within communities.

title: Building the Field of Community Organizing
description: This grant will enable the Center for Community Change to continue working to build the field of community organizing. Activities will focus on three major areas: strengthening low-income, grassroots organizations in selected regions of the country; building community organizing infrastructure in specific states; and establishing a community organizing “pool of talent” for the field. The goal of this work is to increase the resources and build permanent capacity in targeted regions of the U.S. to increase the ability of low-income residents to shape the programs that affect their lives.During the past two years, the center identified five geographic regions of the country; inventoried organizing activities in each region and created a national map of community organizations; developed a plan to build relationships with key organizing groups and allies in each region, with the goal of bringing organizations together to work on state issues; completed a demographic and infrastructure power analysis of each region and an issue opportunity analysis for each state and/or region; determined which target geographic areas and constituencies needed focused technical assistance to become more effective; and delivered national expertise on subjects such as taxes, fiscal policy, education, job creation and health care.

title: Building the Field of Community Organizing
description: This grant will assist the Center for Community Change in its efforts to build the field of community organizing. While the field of community organizing has been growing, significant gaps in reach and effectiveness currently prevent it from becoming a more powerful catalyst for fighting poverty. With this grant, the grantee’s work will focus on three major areas: 1) strengthening low-income, grassroots organizations in selected regions of the country; 2) building community organizing infrastructure in specific states; and 3) establishing a community organizing “pool of talent” for the field. The ultimate goal of this work is to increase resources and build permanent capacity to increase the ability of low-income residents to shape the programs and policies that affect their lives.

title: Building the Field of Community Organizing
description: The Center for Community Change is working to build the field of community organizing by: 1) strengthening low-income, grassroots organizations in selected regions of the country; 2) building community organizing infrastructure in specific states; and 3) establishing a training institute for new organizers. The goal of this work is to increase resources and build permanent capacity to increase the ability of low-income residents to shape the programs and policies that affect their lives. This grant increase will support additional technical assistance and training provision to local community organizing groups.

title: Building the Field of Community Organizing
description: This grant will assist the Center for Community Change in its efforts to build the field of community organizing. While the field of community organizing has been growing, significant gaps in reach and effectiveness currently prevent it from becoming a more powerful catalyst for fighting poverty. With this grant, the grantee’s work will focus on three major areas: 1) strengthening low-income, grassroots organizations in selected regions of the country; 2) building community organizing infrastructure in specific states; and 3) establishing a community organizing pool of talent for the field. The ultimate goal of this organizing work is to increase resources and build permanent capacity in the targeted regions to increase the ability of low-income residents to shape the programs and policies that affect their lives.

title: Building the Field of Community Organizing
description: While community organizing has been expanding, significant gaps in reach and effectiveness currently prevent it from becoming a more powerful catalyst for fighting poverty. This grant increase will assist the Center for Community Change in its efforts to build the field of community organizing by contracting with training and technical assistance professionals to respond to an increased demand from the field. The ultimate goal of this organizing work is to increase resources and build permanent capacity to increase the ability of low-income residents to shape the programs and policies that affect their lives.

title: Building the Field of Community Organizing
description: This grant will assist the Center for Community Change in its efforts to build the field of community organizing. While the field of community organizing has been growing, significant gaps in reach and effectiveness currently prevent it from becoming a more powerful catalyst for fighting poverty. With this grant, the grantee’s work will focus on three major areas: 1) strengthening low-income, grassroots organizations in selected regions of the country; 2) building community organizing infrastructure in specific states; and 3) establishing a community organizing pool of talent for the field. The ultimate goal of this organizing work is to increase resources and build permanent capacity in the targeted regions to increase the ability of low-income residents to shape the programs and policies that affect their lives.

title: Promoting Policies for Disconnected Youth: Building Systems to Reconnect Youth to Education and Jobs
grantee: Center for Law and Social Policy
description: This renewal grant will enable the Center for Law and Social Policy to continue to promote federal and state policies that increase the proportion of young people who, at the age of 25, have a high school diploma, a post-secondary degree, and are employed in jobs with career advancement possibilities. In the most recent phase of this project, the Center for Law and Social Policy worked to help states and local communities build infrastructure, connect systems, and blend resources toward a systems-based effort that focuses on reconnecting disconnected youth. During the next phase of this initiative, the Center for Law and Social Policy will continue to raise awareness on disconnected youth issues, advance policy efforts related to the building of alternative education pathways, monitor the reauthorization of youth-serving federal programs, and facilitate the networking of communities that are engaged in cross-system efforts to bring attention to the needs of disconnected youth.

title: Promoting Policies for Disconnected Youth: Building Systems to Reconnect Youth to Education and Jobs
grantee: Center for Law and Social Policy
description: This grant increase will enable the Center for Law and Social Policy to extend its work on promoting federal and state policies that increase the proportion of young people who have a high school diploma at the age of 25 and can access post-secondary education and career options. Through this project, the grantee has developed a youth policy agenda toward raising awareness of the dimensions of the disconnected youth problem and advancing policy and practice focused on comprehensive solutions. With this grant increase, the grantee will build on its current efforts to assure that the issues of disconnected youth are prominent in ongoing national and federal policy deliberations.

title: Reconnecting the Disconnected: Building Systems to Reconnect Youth to Education and Jobs
grantee: Center for Law and Social Policy
description: This grant will enable the Center for Law and Social Policy to promote federal and state policies that will, over time, increase the proportion of young people who at age 25 have a high school diploma, a post-secondary credential, and are employed in jobs with career advancement opportunities. In the next phase of this effort, the grantee will continue its work to improve the education and labor market outcomes for disconnected youth, especially youth of color and those residing in communities of social/economic distress.

title: Reconnecting the Disconnected: Building Systems to Reconnect Youth to Education and Jobs
grantee: Center for Law and Social Policy
description: This grant will enable the Center for Law and Social Policy to continue to promote federal and state policies that will increase the proportion of young people who at age 25 have a high school diploma, a postsecondary credential, and are employed in jobs with career advancement opportunities. In the most recent phase of this initiative, the grantee pursued an agenda related to raising the visibility of the disconnected youth challenge and comprehensive approaches to solutions. Recommended support will allow the grantee to continue its work to improve the education and labor market outcomes for disconnected youth and those residing in communities where the need is the greatest.

title: Stimulating Civil Society to Protect the Environment in the Russian Far East and Siberia
description: This grant will continue support to Pacific Environment, a U.S.-based nonprofit organization that provides long-term technical assistance and training to environmental organizations in the Russian Far East and Siberia. Pacific Environment will work with its Russian partners in their efforts to engage communities in monitoring and decisionmaking regarding major natural resource exploitation projects. As these projects take on an increasingly international character, Russian environmental organizations will develop growing links with counterparts in countries such as China and Japan in order to find ways of broadening civic engagement in advocacy activities. Pacific Environment has over ten years’ experience working with partners in the Russian Far East and Siberia who have become increasingly capable in documenting environmental abuses, and in advocating in favor of improved practice.

title: Stimulating Civil Society to Protect the Environment in the Russian Far East and Siberia
description: The program goal is to strengthen grassroots advocacy organizations in the Russian Far East and Siberia. This grant will continue support to Pacific Environment, a nonprofit organization based in the United States that provides long-term technical assistance and training to a coalition of environmental organizations in this vast region. The grantee will assist its Russian partners in their efforts to engage communities in monitoring and campaigning regarding major natural resource exploitation projects. It will facilitate joint advocacy campaigns, engaging international partners where appropriate. It will undertake intensive organizational development work with key partners, supporting these efforts through a grantmaking program. During the previous grant period, coalition partners successfully campaigned for closure of the single biggest source of pollution affecting Lake Baikal and also worked closely with Chinese counterparts to limit impacts of a new gas pipeline. Founded in 1987, Pacific Environment has over ten years’ experience working with advocacy organizations in the Russian Far East and Siberia.

title: Mott Foundation Leadership Academy
description: The Mott Foundation Leadership Academy was created in 2001 to develop teamwork and leadership skills for youth that will help them succeed in school, in the workplace and in personal relationships. Operated in tandem with the Summer Youth Program, which provides workforce preparation training and employment for youth ages 14-18 in Flint and Genesee County, the leadership academy serves approximately 300 young people, most of whom live in the city of Flint and come from economically disadvantaged households.This grant will enable the Genesee Chamber Foundation to provide ongoing support for this youth development activity and better understand workforce preparation issues confronting schools and young people.

title: Retention and Wage Progression Strategies
description: This grant will enable the Wisconsin Regional Training Partnership to continue to strengthen and improve its retention and wage progression activities on behalf of those participants selected and still active in the Mott-funded random assignment sectoral employment impact study. The majority of the funds will support a placement/retention specialist who will provide an extra dimension to client placement and post-placement services.

title: Retention and Wage Progression Strategies
description: This grant will enable Per Scholas to support job retention, wage progression, and other work support activities for participants in the Mott-funded random assignment sectoral employment impact study. Per Scholas will provide job retention and wage advancement services to those already employed, job placement services to those seeking employment, and reenrollment in training for those who dropped out or never attended training. The benefit of these services should be more participants employed at higher wages.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Coalition for Promotion and Protection of Human Rights
description: This grant supports a vibrant and important network of nine human rights organizations in Croatia, called the Coalition for Promotion and Protection of Human Rights. Coalition members share a common mission to monitor and promote the implementation of rights and protections guaranteed by the constitution and laws of Croatia as well as international treaties and standards. The coalition facilitates cooperation among members with the goals of developing their skills and building their capacities; addressing public policy issues affecting their beneficiaries; exchanging information; accessing new financial resources; and collaborating with other nongovernmental organizations, government bodies, and international organizations. In 2005-2006, the coalition continued advocacy initiatives aimed at improving the availability of free legal services for indigent people in Croatia, monitoring minority rights protection, and improving decisionmaking processes within the coalition. The coalition is separately registered and has a small staff based in Osijek.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Coalition for Promotion and Protection of Human Rights
description: This grant supports the development of a vibrant and important network of nine human rights organizations in Croatia, called the Coalition for Promotion and Protection of Human Rights. During the grant period, the coalition will monitor and report on the implementation of rights protection mechanisms; educate and raise awareness of the public on the importance of respecting human rights; and build the capacity of coalition members and other nonprofits involved in the protection of human rights in Croatia. In 2007-2008, the coalition continued advocacy initiatives aimed at improving the availability of free legal services for indigent people in Croatia, monitored and issued reports on minority rights protection, strengthened cooperation with relevant Croatian government bodies, and launched its Web site. The coalition has a small staff based in Osijek, Croatia, and is well networked with other nonprofits nationally and internationally.

title: Volunteerism Development in the Privolzhsky Federal District
grantee: Center for the Support of Democratic Youth Initiatives
description: The program goal is to engage youth in civic life through volunteer activities that raise awareness about people’s rights and responsibilities in an important region of central Russia–the Privolzhsky Federal District. The grantee will engage high school and university students in helping elderly victims of Soviet political repression; conduct training seminars, meetings, and distance learning courses to promote volunteering and to foster good volunteer management practices among regional civic organizations; and establish a center to coordinate international volunteer activities. The grantee will also conduct summer expeditions to document former Soviet prison camps and will organize volunteer work camps at the Perm-36 Memorial Center of the History of Political Repression, another important Mott grantee in the region. These efforts to preserve the past and to promote understanding of this history have involved well over 500 youth volunteers. Established in 1998, the Center for Support of Democratic Youth Initiatives works to promote ideals of community service and human rights awareness in young people by confronting the tragic history of political repression.

title: Volunteerism Development in the Privolzhsky Federal District
grantee: Center for the Support of Democratic Youth Initiatives
description: The program goal is to foster civic engagement through promotion of volunteer activities that raise awareness about people’s rights and responsibilities. The Center for the Support of Democratic Youth Initiatives will engage students in helping elderly victims of Soviet political repression; conduct learning and outreach activities to promote volunteerism and foster good volunteer management practices among regional civic organizations; and initiate efforts to establish corporate volunteer programs in the Privolzhsky federal region. The grantee will also conduct expeditions to document former Soviet prison camps and will organize volunteer work camps at the Perm-36 Memorial Center of the History of Political Repression. In the previous grant period, the grantee engaged over 1,000 people in its volunteer development activities and organized over 4,300 visits to victims of repression. Established in 1998, the grantee promotes ideals of community service and human rights awareness in young people by confronting the tragic history of political repression.

title: Retention and Wage Progression Strategies
description: This grant will enable Jewish Vocational Services to retain employment and secure higher wages for participants in the Mott-funded random assignment sectoral employment impact study. Funding will be used to support the hiring of a case manager/employment specialist who will provide intensive case management services, retention counseling, and “next step” planning; serve as an intermediary between employee and supervisor; and provide reemployment services for those participants who lose their jobs.

title: Complete Landscaping at University Park
description: This grant will provide funding to the City of Flint to complete infrastructure improvements and landscaping for the second phase of University Park Estates, a subdivision of newly constructed, single-family houses located just north of River Village in the city. This upscale subdivision constitutes the first new, market-rate housing built in the city in over 30 years. Staff is recommending this grant to provide funds to complete infrastructure improvements for this new subdivision totaling 109 housing units.

title: Leading Edge States Project
grantee: Center for Law and Social Policy
description: The recent reauthorization of the 1996 federal welfare reform law imposes rigid and restrictive work requirements that will require most states to make dramatic changes to their Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) programs between now and the end of September. This grant increase will enable the Center for Law and Social Policy to provide technical assistance to help state policymakers, administrators and program providers interpret and implement the new law. The center will also generate a set of policy briefs to help states understand the choices before them and identify promising programs and practices that emerge under the new regulations.

title: Leading Edge States Project
grantee: Center for Law and Social Policy
description: This grant will provide renewal support to the Center for Law and Social Policy for its Leading Edge States Project. Within the context of state workforce development and welfare programs, a key objective of this project is to promote the most promising strategies for improving the economic well-being of low-income families and their children. The grantee will help states and other governments adopt these approaches through technical assistance, convening, research, and policy analysis activities. The Center for Law and Social Policy is a 30-year-old national research and public policy organization which produces policy analysis and offers technical assistance on a range of issues, including welfare reform and workforce development.

title: Community School Development
description: Nova Skola was established in 1996 to advocate for reforms in the Czech educational system that address the needs of marginalized children and communities. This grant will enable Nova Skola to provide technical assistance to existing community schools; introduce the community education concept in at least 40 new schools and community centers; exchange experience and best practice with community education movements in Eastern Europe and the former Soviet Union; and strengthen its own organizational capacity.Since 2000, Nova Skola has promoted the community education concept as an effective approach to improving the quality of education provided in poor neighborhoods, especially in areas with a significant Roma population.

title: Support Center Development
description: The program goal is to promote and develop networking and collaboration among nonprofit support centers in Hungary. To this end, the Eastern-Hungarian Community Service Foundation will facilitate an informal network of 14 nonprofit support centers throughout Hungary to introduce national quality standards for nonprofit services, support joint marketing of nonprofit services, strengthen communication and interaction among nonprofit support centers in Hungary, and develop international cooperation with similar organizations in Europe. The network was established in 2000 to assist nonprofit support centers in fulfilling their mission, ensure cooperation among support centers, and represent their interests at the national level. The network’s past achievements include developing the capacity of network members, strengthening the network governance and operational procedures, and implementing joint publicity and advocacy initiatives on behalf of the network.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will enable the Slovak Rural Parliament to create and promote sustainable rural development policies; increase the capacity of individuals, community groups and local institutions to participate in rural development programs; increase the level of resources available for rural development; and strengthen its organizational capacity and financial sustainability.Slovak Rural Parliament was established in 2000 as a membership organization of individuals and organizations with the mission of improving the life of people living in rural Slovakia. Recent accomplishments included facilitating local access to resources for rural development; training experts in rural development and European Union funding mechanisms; and establishing a network of 30 local communication centers for improving the flow of information to and from rural areas.

title: Institutional Development Program
description: The program goal is to ensure independent funding for nonprofit organizations in Slovakia. Since its establishment in 1992, the Open Society Foundation has played an important role in supporting civil society development as well as political, economic, and social reforms in Slovakia. During the grant period, the grantee will strengthen its financial stability by diversifying its income base; increasing the relevance and impact of its grantmaking programs by thoroughly assessing local needs; and increasing its organizational capacity by providing training for its core staff.

title: General Purposes
description: Socia – Social Reform Foundation was established in 2002 to support systemic reforms of social service provision, increase the quality of life of socially disadvantaged groups and strengthen social cohesion in Slovak society.Multiyear funding will enable the foundation to provide financial and technical support to social service non-governmental organizations (NGOs); contribute to the development of policies relating to social services; and increase its organizational sustainability.Key achievements in 2004-2005 included awarding $535,000 to more than 40 NGOs; providing training and technical assistance to more than 120 social service NGOs; and improving networking and cooperation among social service NGOs.

title: Local Government Transformation Project
description: Afesis-corplan works to ensure that civil society participates in local government processes and holds local government accountable for service delivery and decisionmaking. Mott supported Afesis-corplan to implement a good governance survey instrument to provide feedback to municipalities on how communities rate their performance, particularly in relation to meeting development targets and facilitating community participation in decisionmaking. The grant also assisted it to implement a key performance indicator model for ward committees, the formal structures through which communities participate in local government to assess and monitor the performance of municipalities. This grant will assist Afesis-corplan to further implement these models and to initiate interventions for communities to assess and monitor municipal financial accountability in the Eastern Cape, Western Cape, and Mpumalanga provinces.

title: Local Government Transformation Project
description: Afesis-corplan works to ensure that civil society participates in local government processes and holds local government accountable for service delivery and decision making. With previous support, the grantee implemented a good governance survey instrument to provide feedback to municipalities on how communities rate their performance, particularly in relation to meeting development targets and facilitating community participation in decision making. It also implemented a key performance indicator model for ward committees, the formal structures through which communities participate in local governance, to assess and monitor the performance of municipalities. This grant will assist the grantee to further implement these models and to initiate interventions for communities to assess and monitor municipal financial accountability.

title: Strengthening Democracy at the Local Level
description: The Electoral Institute of South Africa works with civil society organizations, government officials, and politicians to strengthen their capacity to engage effectively in democratic governance and sustainable service delivery at the local level. During the grant period, Mott supported a pilot project in the Eastern Cape province aimed at strengthening the capacity and effectiveness of ward committees, the formal structures through which communities participate in local government. This grant will support the Electoral Institute of South Africa to train and support civil society organizations in the Eastern Cape and Mpumalanga provinces to engage constructively with local government focusing on decisionmaking processes around service delivery at the local level.

title: Strengthening Democracy at the Local Level
description: The Electoral Institute of South Africa works across the African continent to promote democratic governance, human rights, and citizen participation in a peaceful environment. This grant will provide continued support to the institute to work with civil society organizations, government officials, and politicians in Mpumalanga province, South Africa, to strengthen their capacity to engage effectively in democratic governance and sustainable service delivery at the local level. Past achievements include developing a scorecard and advocacy toolkit that allow civil society organizations to rank the current state of affairs in various municipalities regarding the delivery of basic services like water, electricity, and sanitation. Specifically, the grant renewal will support the institute’s work in the Gert Sibande District Municipality, Mpumalanga province, to train and support civil society organizations to enhance their capacity to engage constructively with local government and provide input to decisions that affect delivery and services at the local level.

title: Practical Legal Skills Training and Support for Paralegals
geographic_focus: Eastern Cape, Province of, Northern Cape, Province of, Western Cape, Province of the
description: The Centre for Rural Legal Studies focuses on protecting and promoting the rights of farmworkers and their families in the Eastern, Western, and Northern Cape provinces. This grant will continue to support the Centre for Rural Legal Studies to train and mentor paralegals in these community-based organizations to provide services to farmworkers and marginalized communities. It also will support the Centre for Rural Legal Studies to conduct research to establish the nature and causes of labor disputes and look at ways to proactively address these problems through educating both farmworkers and farmowners.

title: Practical Legal Skills Training and Support for Paralegals
description: This grant will provide continued support to the Centre for Rural Legal Studies, an organization that focuses on protecting and promoting the rights of farmworkers and their families in the Eastern, Western, and Northern Cape provinces of South Africa. Past achievements include assisting paralegals working in community-based advice offices to effectively represent clients on labor-related matters, the majority of whom do not have access to basic labor rights and due process. In the next two years, the grantee will train paralegals in Alternative Dispute Resolution and labor law legislation to enable them to develop the skills and knowledge to assist farm and rural workers in labor disputes. Paralegals will also learn how to campaign for effective enforcement of labor legislation and highlight working conditions of marginalized rural workers. The centre will also evaluate the use and impact of Alternative Dispute Resolution over the past four years.

title: Practical Legal Skills Training and Support for Paralegals
description: This grant will provide continued support to the Centre for Rural Legal Studies, an organization that focuses on protecting and promoting the rights of farmworkers and their families in the Eastern, Western, and Northern Cape provinces of South Africa. Past achievements include assisting paralegals working in community-based advice offices to effectively represent clients on labor-related matters, the majority of whom do not have access to basic labor rights and due process. This was achieved through training paralegals and providing hands-on support. In the next two years, the grantee will train paralegals on various areas including Alternative Dispute Resolution, labor law legislation, action research methodologies, and basic office administration. It will also offer hands-on support and mentoring to paralegals to ensure that the training is implemented properly.

title: General Purposes
description: The Centre for Rural Legal Studies works to protect and promote the rights of farmworkers and their families in the Western Cape province of South Africa. Past achievements include assisting paralegals working in community-based advice offices to effectively represent clients on labor-related matters, the majority of whom do not have access to basic labor rights and due process. The grantee trained paralegals on various areas including Alternative Dispute Resolution, labor legislation, action research methodologies, and basic office administration. It also offered hands-on support and mentoring to paralegals to ensure that the training was implemented properly. Over the next two years, the grantee will assist with the establishment and strengthening of farm and rural community-based organizations in the central Karoo region of the Western Cape province to enable them to assist poor people to realize their rights. It will also continue to support community advice offices, conduct research and advocacy, and provide backup legal services to people on farms.

title: General Purposes
description: The Centre for Rural Legal Studies works to protect and promote the rights of farmworkers and their families in the Western Cape province of South Africa. Past achievements include assisting with the establishment and strengthening of farm and rural community-based organizations in the central Karoo region of the Western Cape province to enable people who live and work on farms to realize their rights. It also conducted research and advocacy and provided backup legal services to people on farms. This grant will support the grantee to continue to assist farmworkers from rural areas of the central Karoo region of the Western Cape province to establish organizations that will help them access and realize their rights. The grantee will also develop the leadership capacity of these organizations to enable them to organize farmworkers to take collective action on issues that affect their lives. This grant has been made possible by a partnership with The Atlantic Philanthropies in support of the community advice office sector.

title: General Purposes
description: The Centre for Rural Legal Studies works to protect and promote the rights of farmworkers and their families in the Western Cape Province of South Africa. Past achievements include leading a campaign for clean water and decent sanitation for farmworker communities, and strengthening the institutional capacity of farmworker organizations. This grant will enable the grantee to train paralegals and boards of community advice offices in the Western Cape Province on a range of topics that ensure their survival and enable them to respond adequately to key issues that affect the lives of farm dwellers and the rural poor. The grantee will also strengthen the organizing skills of farmworker organizations, and assist them to monitor the enforcement of rights and policies on issues that affect farmworkers and farm dwellers.

title: UNESCO Oliver Tambo Chair of Human Rights: Democratic Governance and Participatory Development at the Local Level
description: The UNESCO Oliver Tambo Chair of Human Rights, based at the University of Fort Hare, was established through funding by UNESCO to advance human rights, respect for democratic values, peace, and social justice. Mott provided support to implement a project to train and build the capacity of local government officials, traditional leaders, and community representatives to understand their respective roles, responsibilities, and duties at the local level of government. This renewal grant will support the continuation and further development of this project through ongoing dialogues, trainings, capacity building, and research. The University of Fort Hare is based in Alice in the Eastern Cape, and is one of the oldest and most respected of the historically black universities in the country.

title: Americas Program
description: The Center for International Policy’s Americas Program explores policy options for development and integration in the Americas that are both workable and grounded in the principles of environmental protection, sustainable and equitable economic development, multilateralism, and respect for human rights. By producing policy reports, issue briefs, commentary, and educational materials, the Americas Program offers credible and timely analysis to influence policymakers, contribute to public debates, and strengthen nongovernmental organizations’ analyses of trade and environment in the Latin America region. This proposed renewal grant will support continued research, analysis, translation, and distribution of publications to bring critical perspectives about social and environmental issues into ongoing negotiations on regional trade agreements and to regional policy debates about investments in energy and infrastructure in Latin America.

title: Americas Program
description: The Americas Program, a project of the Center for International Policy, explores policy options for development and integration in the Americas that are grounded in the principles of environmental protection, sustainable and equitable economic development, multilateralism, and respect for human rights. By producing policy reports, issue briefs, commentary, and educational materials, the Americas Program offers credible and timely analyses to influence policymakers, contribute to public debates, and strengthen nongovernmental organizations’ analyses in the Latin America region. This renewal grant will support continued research, analysis, translation, and distribution of publications to bring critical perspectives about social and environmental issues into ongoing negotiations on regional integration discussions and policy debates about investments in energy and infrastructure in Latin America.

title: General Purposes
initiative: Reform of International Finance and Trade
description: The Forum on Democracy and Trade was established in 2002 to enhance the national dialogue on trade by reinforcing the importance of state and local government involvement in the negotiating processes as well as connecting trade and globalization to state and local concerns about sustainable economic development. This general purposes grant will support the Forum on Democracy and Trade’s continued work with state and local governments in the United States on international trade and investment policy and will allow for further development of its work in Latin America. Past support has helped to develop a strong network of state-level trade oversight committees and multistate working groups on key sectors.

title: Western Balkans Cohesion Initiative
geographic_focus: Serbia, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina
description: The overall project goal is to promote a more informed debate on social, economic, and political developments in the Western Balkans in order to secure stability and prosperity in this region. To this end, the European Stability Initiative, a European think tank, will build local capacities for policy-relevant research and analysis; carry out field-based studies and assessments; and stimulate discussions on policy issues through seminars, public presentations, and bilateral meetings. The grantee will link practitioners and policymakers at local and national levels by helping translate on-the-ground realities into concrete policy recommendations. Particular emphasis will be given to the current debate about further European Union enlargement in the Western Balkans. During 2005-2007, the grantee worked with three new think tanks in the region; published six major reports; and participated in numerous conferences, debates, and bilateral meetings related to regional developments. The grantee’s main office is in Berlin. It has a field office in Istanbul and analysts located in Belgrade and Pristina.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will enable the Forum of Tuzla Citizens to foster local democractic development in the community of Tuzla in central Bosnia and Herzegovina through the promotion of the rights and responsibilities of citizens and local government. The forum also will work to strengthen Bosnia and Herzegovina’s development as a stable, multiethnic and democratic state and work with other key non-governmental organizations in the region to improve relations between Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Serbia, and Montenegro.Recent activities included organizing a series of workshops and seminars in local communities for representatives of the local authorities, citizens, nonprofit representatives and the media on practical aspects of local governance.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to increase public participation in decisionmaking and strengthen democratic practices at local and national levels in Bosnia-Herzegovina. The Forum of Tuzla Citizens works to foster local democracy development in the community of Tuzla in central Bosnia through the promotion of the rights and responsibilities of citizens and local government. The grantee is also prominent on the national level, working to strengthen Bosnia-Herzegovina’s development as a stable, multiethnic, and democratic state. Finally, the grantee works with other key nongovernmental organizations in the region to improve relations between Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia, Montenegro, and Serbia. Recent activities include organizing a series of workshops and seminars in local communities for representatives of the local authorities, citizens, nonprofit representatives, and the media on European standards of local self-governance; monitoring sessions of local municipal councils and informing citizens about these sessions; and increasing awareness of the past through public debates and other events.

title: Capacity Building for Associations of Families of Missing Persons
geographic_focus: Montenegro, Serbia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina
description: The overall project goal is to assist associations of families of missing persons from Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia, Kosovo, Montenegro, and Serbia to become more effective organizations and positive forces for change, particularly with respect to issues of dealing with the past in the Western Balkans. To this end, the International Commission on Missing Persons supports the work and organizational development of associations of families of missing persons through workshops and regional conferences, tailored expert consultancy, policy development and advocacy, and small grants. In 2005-2006, the commission organized four regional workshops for associations from different ethnic/religious communities and two regional conferences, convened stakeholders and experts on a range of transitional justice issues, and provided small grants to associations to carry out concrete projects. The commission is a joint initiative of various governments, led by the United States, to identify persons missing as a result of armed conflicts in the former Yugoslavia.

title: Capacity Building for Associations of Families of Missing Persons
geographic_focus: Croatia, Kosovo, Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina
description: The overall project goal is to assist associations of families of missing persons from Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia, Kosovo, Montenegro, and Serbia to become more effective organizations and positive forces for change, particularly with respect to issues dealing with the past in the Western Balkans. To this end, the International Commission on Missing Persons supports the work and development of associations of families of missing persons through workshops and regional conferences, tailored consultancy, and financial support for projects. During the previous grant period and with Mott support, the grantee organized regional intergroup workshops for associations from different ethnic/national groups, financially supported specific projects related to dealing with the past, and strengthened national and regional coordination structures among associations. The commission is a joint initiative of various governments, led by the United States, to identify persons missing as a result of armed conflicts in the former Yugoslavia. It is based in Sarajevo, Bosnia-Herzegovina.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen the environmental movement in Bulgaria. During the grant period, the Bulgarian Environmental Partnership Foundation will provide small grants and technical assistance to non-governmental organizations and community groups in the fields of environment and community development; raise awareness of the general public about key environmental issues in Bulgaria; and increase its organizational sustainability. Since its establishment in 2003, the foundation has provided grants and technical assistance to more than 135 environmental initiatives in Bulgaria.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen citizen participation at the grassroots level in Bulgaria. During the grant period, the Bulgarian Environmental Partnership Foundation will provide small grants and technical assistance to nongovernmental organizations and community groups in the fields of environment and community development, raise awareness of the general public about key environmental issues in Bulgaria, and increase its organizational capacity and financial sustainability. Since its establishment in 2003, the grantee has established itself as a key indigenous grantmaker in Bulgaria. In 2008-2009, the grantee provided grants to over 60 grassroots environment and community development initiatives and ran awareness raising campaigns in the areas of nature conservation, biodiversity, sustainable tourism, renewable energy, and climate change.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen the capacity of a key grantmaker to support citizen participation at the grassroots level in Bulgaria. During the grant period, the Bulgarian Environmental Partnership Foundation will provide small grants and technical assistance to nongovernmental organizations and community groups in the fields of environment and community development, raise awareness of the general public about key environmental issues in Bulgaria, and increase its organizational capacity and financial sustainability. Since its establishment in 2003, the grantee has developed into a key indigenous grantmaker in Bulgaria. In 2010-2011, the grantee provided grants to over 80 grassroots environment and community development initiatives and ran awareness-raising campaigns in the areas of nature conservation, biodiversity, sustainable tourism, renewable energy, and climate change.

title: General Purposes
description: The Romanian Donors’ Forum is an association of eight local and international donors active in Romania. It was formally registered in December 2004. Prior to this, the forum functioned for five years as an informal network, hosted by the Princess Margarita of Romania Foundation.This grant will enable the forum to strengthen its organizational capacity, increase its membership and develop services for members. The forum will also promote philanthropy by providing information and analysis to the nonprofit, business and government sectors and by working to improve the image of the nonprofit sector in Romania.The forum’s main achievements include increasing the level of cooperation among donors and pioneering initiatives for increasing the accountability and transparency of the Romanian nonprofit sector.

title: Promoting Popular Understanding of the Equality Act Project
description: The Promotion of Equality and Prevention of Unfair Discrimination Act, passed by the South African Parliament in 2000, specifically indicates that legislation promoting equality and preventing unfair discrimination must be promulgated by the country’s first democratically elected parliament.This grant increase will assist the South African Human Rights Commission in co-hosting a colloquium on education and diversity to review the progress made in reversing the legacy of racially unequal education inherited from apartheid.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to promote youth volunteerism and community service in Russia. The Constructive Approach Foundation develops, implements, and supports programs that increase the involvement of youth in civic activity to address social issues in their communities. Over the next two years, the grantee will promote the integration of youth community service in education, the expansion of regional youth volunteer centers, and the development of social partnerships to provide greater opportunities for youth service learning. This service learning model of youth engagement has been adopted by 24 educational institutions, while educational authorities in six Russian regions have committed to supporting further implementation of this approach. Established in 2000, the Constructive Approach Foundation provides technical, methodological, informational, and financial support to develop and implement innovative approaches to promoting youth community engagement at both the practical and policy levels.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen institutions and mechanisms in Russia that ensure people’s rights are respected and that laws and policies to protect these rights are promulgated and implemented. Citizens’ Watch, a leading watchdog and advocacy organization located in Saint Petersburg, will strive to: promote citizens’ access to justice; reform the police service and the police education system; protect crime victims’ rights; and combat racism and ethnic intolerance. To date, Citizens’ Watch has had success in piloting juvenile probation services, in fostering independence of magistrates’ courts, and in promoting tolerance education both in ordinary schools and in police training programs. While its programs focus on Northwest Russia, they also serve to create models that can be replicated throughout the country.

title: General Purposes
description: The Environmental Rights Center “Bellona” is a unique Russian organization that links the environment with human rights, nationally and internationally. It provides technical assistance, scientific and legal expertise, and information to citizens and Russian and international institutions on nuclear safety issues and the oil and gas industry.This grant will enable the center to promote human rights in a safe and favorable environment; monitor environmental and human rights abuses; and help citizens engage in environmental decisionmaking. In addition, the center will monitor Russian environmental legislation and provide legal counsel in cases of environmental violations.During the past two years, accomplishments included the production and international dissemination of a report on the need to reform the Russian nuclear industry. The center also published 10 editions each year of the Environment & Rights journal in printed editions and also electronically; trained 17 university students from St. Petersburg in professional environmental reporting skills; trained 26 law students in human rights advocacy who, in turn, provide technical assistance and legal counsel to a number of local non-governmental organizations; and provided legal counsel by staff lawyers to citizens on a wide range of environmental and human rights cases.

title: Integrated Education for a New Learning Day: Professional Development Across Sectors
description: This grant will continue to support Foundations, Inc., and its partners in disseminating the Afterschool Academies to afterschool and education stakeholders. This initiative forged a model of professional development that integrated informal, experiential, and youth development approaches of afterschool with school-based content and skills. The project will specifically promote and support systems that lead to sustainable professional development of staff and leaders across diverse programs and extend core knowledge of effective afterschool education to diverse stakeholders in education and youth development. For hosting and outreach, Foundations, Inc., and their partners — Education Development Center and Community Network for Youth Development — will work with afterschool and school leaders to present at national conferences and meetings.

title: Building State Capacity and Supporting Statewide Afterschool Networks
grantee: Council of Chief State School Officers
description: This grant will enable the Council of Chief State School Officers to continue to provide technical assistance to the statewide afterschool networks as a partner of the Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative (a group of national organizations working to support the development of statewide networks through technical assistance); provide collaborative opportunities for the existing network of state agency staff that implement the 21st Century Community Learning Centers and Supplemental Educational Services programs; support the development of its Extended Learning Opportunities task force; and develop a tool kit to provide additional guidance to states focused on state-level policy development.
