The council will also co-implement a project with the National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and the National Conference of State Legislatures to provide intensive technical assistance to further afterschool policies with state leadership teams comprised of state legislators, education chiefs, governors’ policy advisors and statewide afterschool network leaders.During the past eight years, the council has worked with its membership, the chief state school officers and the state education agencies to increase their understanding of the critical role that their agencies can play in expanding and sustaining high-quality afterschool opportunities that are widely available to those that need them.

title: Building State Capacity and Supporting Statewide Afterschool Networks
grantee: Council of Chief State School Officers
description: This grant will continue to support the Council of Chief State School Officers to help build state capacity among its members to implement federal legislation and support policies that expand the availability of high quality, afterschool programs. The council will: 1) provide technical assistance to the statewide afterschool networks as a partner of the Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative, a group of national organizations working together to support the statewide networks; 2) provide collaboration opportunities for state agency staff that implements the 21st Century Community Learning Centers and Supplemental Educational Services programs; and 3) manage and expand an online toolkit to support state-level implementation efforts. The council will also continue to partner with the National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and the National Conference of State Legislatures to engage leadership teams of state legislators, education chiefs, governors’ policy advisors, and statewide afterschool network leaders to further statewide afterschool policies.

title: Building State Capacity and Supporting Statewide Afterschool Networks
grantee: Council of Chief State School Officers
description: This grant will continue to support the Council of Chief State School Officers to build state capacity to implement high quality afterschool and expanded learning opportunities. The grantee will work with seven states to focus on eliminating barriers to student participation in expanded learning opportunities that award credit, and provide more seamless partnership and integration between traditional education and the afterschool community. In addition, the grantee will continue to: 1) provide technical assistance to the statewide afterschool networks as part of the Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative; 2) partner with the National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and the National Conference of State Legislatures to engage teams of state legislators, education chiefs, governors’ policy advisors, and statewide afterschool network leaders to further statewide afterschool policies; and 3) share resources to support states in their implementation efforts.

title: Building State Capacity and Supporting Statewide Afterschool Networks
grantee: Council of Chief State School Officers
description: This grant increase will continue to support the Council of Chief State School Officers to build state capacity to implement high quality afterschool and expanded learning opportunities. The grantee will expand work with seven states to focus on eliminating barriers to student participation in expanded learning opportunities that award credit, and provide more seamless partnership and integration between traditional education and the afterschool community. In addition, the grantee will continue to: 1) provide technical assistance to the statewide afterschool networks as part of the Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative; 2) partner with the National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and the National Conference of State Legislatures to engage teams of state legislators, education chiefs, governors’ policy advisors, and statewide afterschool network leaders to further statewide afterschool policies; and 3) share resources to support states in their implementation efforts.

title: Partnership for Sustainable Development in Central Europe
geographic_focus: Czech Republic, Latvia, Poland, Romania, Slovakia, Hungary
description: The program goal is to increase citizens’ understanding of and influence over the decisions about European Union funding for regional development in Central and Eastern Europe. The National Society of Conservationists will promote the effective use of structural funds in regional development by supporting local action plans, strengthening national networking among nonprofits involved in regional development, and advocating for improvements in current practices at the European Union level. The grantee will implement this program with partners in six new member states. In addition, the program partners will extend their work to Bulgaria. The National Society of Conservationists has been implementing this program since 2003. Past achievements include disseminating information on good practice in sustainable regional development, supporting national watchdog networks monitoring European Union funds, and advocating for effective and sustainable use of European Union funding.

title: Partnership for Sustainable Development in Central Europe
geographic_focus: Hungary, Latvia, Poland, Czech Republic, Romania, Bulgaria, Netherlands, Slovakia
description: The program goal is to increase citizens’ understanding of and influence over the decisions about European Union funding for regional development in Central and Eastern Europe. The National Society of Conservationists will promote the effective use of European Union Structural Funds in regional development by supporting local action plans, strengthening national networking among nonprofits involved in regional development, and advocating for improvements in current practices at the European Union level. The grantee will implement this program with partners in seven new member states. Based in Budapest, Hungary, the National Society of Conservationists has been implementing this program since 2003. Past achievements include disseminating information on good practice in sustainable regional development, supporting national watchdog networks monitoring European Union funds, and advocating for the effective and sustainable use of European Union funding.

title: Partnership for Sustainable Development in Central Europe
geographic_focus: Hungary, Czech Republic, Romania, Poland, Bulgaria, Netherlands, Latvia, Slovakia
description: The program goal is to increase citizens’ understanding of and influence over the decisions about European Union funding for regional development in Central and Eastern Europe. During the grant period, the National Society of Conservationists will promote the effective use of European Union Structural Funds in regional development and thorough application of the partnership principle between governments and civil society in decisionmaking related to the future allocation of funds. Also, the grantee will document and share its experiences in monitoring the European Union funding practices with a wide range of interested stakeholders, including nonprofit organizations and local authorities. In addition, the grantee will explore new funding opportunities for supporting this project in the future. The grantee will implement this program with partners in seven new member states. Past project achievements include disseminating information on good practice in sustainable regional development, supporting national watchdog networks monitoring European Union funds, and advocating for the effective and sustainable use of European Union funding.

title: act4europe Campaign - EU Accession Countries
geographic_focus: Czech Republic, Romania, Bulgaria, Lithuania, Hungary, Estonia, Slovenia, Latvia, Poland, Slovakia
description: The project goal is to involve nongovernmental organizations from the European Union new member states and accession countries in the debate regarding the future of the European Union. In order to coordinate and encourage nonprofit sector input into this debate, a coalition of European nongovernmental organization networks created a campaign called act4europe. The Social Platform network coordinates the campaign. During the grant period, the campaign will address issues related to the ratification of the European Constitution and accessibility of European Union structural funds. This grant increase will enable the Social Platform to widely disseminate the project results, conduct an evaluation of the act4europe Campaign, and prepare a new strategy for its future.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen public monitoring and oversight of government bodies in Ukraine at the national, regional, and local levels. This grant continues support to the Civil Society Institute, which works to increase the public’s knowledge of their rights and of mechanisms to protect these rights. The grantee will conduct detailed monitoring of current and proposed legislation impacting nonprofit organizations and people’s rights and freedoms, while also educating legislative officials about effective law-making procedures. It will also monitor information transparency and accessibility of local and regional councils and administrations as a means of promoting informed public participation in local decisionmaking. The institute has made significant contributions to the ongoing process of local administration reform in Ukraine, while also publishing numerous accessible handbooks on citizens’ rights. These have been key components of the Civil Society Institute’s work since its inception in 1997.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to increase the responsiveness of government bodies in Ukraine at the national, regional, and local levels. The Civil Society Institute will conduct detailed monitoring of legislation impacting nonprofit organizations and people’s rights and freedoms while also educating legislative officials about effective lawmaking procedures. It will work with local and regional partners to promote informed public participation in decisionmaking aimed at improving community development outcomes. It will also seek to train a new generation of independent policy professionals capable of carrying on and expanding this work. In the period 2008-2010, the grantee analyzed over 150 pieces of legislation and prepared over 50 detailed analytical briefs on issues related to local territorial development, while participating in a similar number of public policy discussions. Founded in 1997, the Civil Society Institute supports the development of civil society in Ukraine through public legal education, policy analysis, and promotion of participatory local development.

title: GAPS: Success Connections
description: In the 2003-2004 academic year, approximately 36 percent of the students who enrolled in the Flint Community Schools in the previous four years graduated from high school. More than half of the students that drop out do so in the ninth grade. The GAPS: Success Connections program is a “transition intervention” strategy developed by Mott Middle College High School faculty to help prevent school dropout by focusing on the transition from middle school to high school. This renewal grant to Mott Community College will provide three additional years of support for this program.

title: GAPS: Transition Program
description: This renewal grant to Mott Community College provides three additional years of support for the GAPS: Transition Program, which is a transition intervention strategy developed by Mott Middle Early College High School faculty. The program, previously known as GAPS: Success Connection, helps to increase the number of early college graduates by offering students college readiness skills, coaching, and early college preparation. Approximately 400 students will transition from middle school to high school at Mott Middle Early College High School during the grant period.

title: GAPS: Transition Program
description: This grant will enable Mott Community College to continue the GAPS: Transition Program. The program, which is an intervention strategy developed by Mott Middle Early College High School staff, assists students in making the transition from middle school to the more rigorous middle/early college high school setting. Recommended support will allow Mott Community College to provide high school and college readiness services in the summer and academic year for students entering Mott Middle Early College High School. Approximately 400 students will benefit from services via the GAPS: Transition Program.

title: GAPS: Transition Program
description: This grant will enable Mott Community College to continue the GAPS: Transition Program. The program, which is a dropout intervention strategy developed by Mott Middle Early College High School staff, assists students in making the transition from middle school to the more rigorous middle/early college high school setting. Funding will allow the grantee to provide high school and college readiness services in the summer and throughout the school year for students entering Mott Middle Early College High School.

title: Advancing Freshwater Conservation in the Great Lakes Region
description: This grant increase will enable the Great Lakes program of the Nature Conservancy to continue efforts to support conservation work at selected sites, while also developing a strategic plan that will orient the conservancy’s future engagement on freshwater conservation issues in the Great Lakes basin. Recently, the program disseminated information on freshwater sites that are priorities for conservation.

title: Center for Nonprofit Sector Research
grantee: Society for the Study of the Nonprofit Sector
description: The program goal is to improve information, research, and policy development on the nonprofit sector in the Czech Republic and in Central and Eastern Europe. To this end, the Society for the Study of the Nonprofit Sector will develop the Center for Nonprofit Sector Research in cooperation with the Masaryk University in Brno, Czech Republic. The center will carry out systematic research on the Czech nonprofit sector, generate analytical materials, and make its findings widely available. Based on the data and reports produced, the center will enhance dialogue about the Czech nonprofit sector. In addition, the center will establish regular contacts with nonprofit sector researchers in other Central and Eastern European countries and will initiate joint projects. Since its establishment in 2003, the center has produced a number of reports and other publications with reliable, objective, and systematic information about various aspects of nonprofit sector development in the Czech Republic.

title: General Purposes
description: Community Connections provides organizational development and capacity building training as well as other supports for community-based organizations, mainly in the Western Cape. It also advocates on behalf of these organizations and encourages them to network more effectively and look at collective ways in which they can try to mobilize resources for activities and programs.This grant will enable Community Connections to continue its organizational development training, capacity building, and advocacy work on behalf of grassroots, community-based organizations.Recent accomplishments included contact with more than 70 community-based organizations and more than 300 community workers through its community capacity-building program; promoting the interests of community-based organizations through networking, showcase events, international partnerships and advocacy work; and producing publications, toolkits and training material for the community-based organization sector.

title: General Purposes
description: Community Connections provides organizational development training and technical assistance to build institutional capacity of community-based organizations in the Western Cape province. It primarily supports nonprofits focused on local economic and community development, HIV/AIDS, early childhood development, women empowerment, arts and culture, the environment, and poverty eradication. Past core activities included providing organizational development trainings and workshops, developing a computer resource center, partnering with several organizations for consultancies, promoting networking between community organizations and local government, and publishing training materials. This renewal grant will support the continuation of core activities through trainings, workshops, consultancies, publications, expanding the resource center’s activities, and providing opportunities for peer learning and networking. Community Connections is a membership-based nonprofit that was founded in 2000 to address issues of poverty.

title: General Purposes
description: Community Connections was initiated in 2000 by a group of volunteer community workers to support community-led development through strengthening the capacity of community-based organizations to transform society. It provides organizational development training and technical assistance to build the institutional capacity of community-based organizations in the Western Cape province in South Africa. It primarily supports nonprofits focused on local economic and community development, HIV/AIDS, early childhood development, women empowerment, arts and culture, the environment, youth, and poverty eradication. Previous support from the Mott Foundation assisted the grantee to train, mentor, and support community organizations and to promote networking between community organizations and local government. This renewal grant will support the grantee to continue providing organizational development support and training to community-based organizations in the Western Cape province. It will also provide materials and information through its resource center, which it makes available to community workers and community-based organizations.

title: General Purposes
description: Community Connections was established in 2000 by a group of community workers to promote community-led development in the Western Cape province in South Africa. It supports community-based organizations so that they are able to drive development within their communities. The grantee has achieved this by implementing various initiatives that promote active civic participation and amplifying the voice of ordinary citizens. Over the past two years, the grantee piloted the Integrated Community Development Program, which fosters and grows community activism and translates it to tangible improvements in the daily lives of poor people. It also provided organizational development support to community-based organizations with a strong emphasis on their connectedness to the communities they serve. This grant will support the grantee to expand its work to other communities, conduct learning events for community-based organizations, train community workers as community development facilitators, and strengthen its new organizational structure.

title: Smart Growth Policy Reform in Michigan
description: The Michigan Land Use Institute has been working since the mid-1990s to promote land-use policy reform through its research, communications and coalition-building efforts. The institute’s work has helped to foster implementation of some measures recommended by the bipartisan Michigan Land Use Leadership Council. However, only initial reforms have been enacted and much work remains to be done to achieve substantive change. During the next 18 months, Michigan Land Use Institute will continue to inform growth management policy discussions through high quality research, communications and coalition-building efforts with key stakeholders across the state.

title: Rios Vivos Coalition IFI Program
description: Ecoa – Ecology and Action works to protect the Pantanal and the Cerrado regions in the upper Paraná River basin, as well as the Amazon region in Brazil, and carries out projects that promote sustainable development. This grant increase and project extension will allow Ecoa – Ecology and Action and its partners to undertake additional research on large dams and biofuels. This grant increase will ensure that Latin American groups and their research and analysis will be part of global discussions on standards and safeguards for biofuel development, as well as major waterway development in key areas of South America.

title: Monitoring Environmental Impacts of Financial Flows for Infrastructure and Energy in South America
description: Ecoa – Ecology and Action has worked for nearly 20 years to protect and promote sustainable development in the Pantanal and Cerrado regions of the upper Paraná River basin, as well as the Amazon region in Brazil. Through this renewal grant, Ecoa – Ecology and Action will continue to lead a coalition of organizations monitoring the environmental impacts of new and proposed investments in energy and infrastructure in this region. This coalition will work with communities to identify local concerns and bring those concerns to the international public and private investors in order to change projects with serious environmental and social impacts. The grant will also support additional research on the expansion of biofuels production in the region, which will ensure that Latin American organizations will be an integral part of global discussions on standards and safeguards for biofuel development.

title: Monitoring Environmental Impacts of Financial Flows for Infrastructure and Energy in South America
description: Ecoa – Ecology and Action works to protect the Pantanal and the Cerrado regions in the upper Paraná River basin, as well as the Amazon region in Brazil, and carries out projects that promote sustainable development. This grant renewal will allow the grantee and its partners to continue to collaborate on research, advocacy, and information dissemination related to the environmental and social impacts of large-scale infrastructure projects (highways, dams, and waterways) in Brazil and Argentina and to participate in national and regional networks aimed at holding international financial institutions and private sector investors accountable to environmental norms. This grant renewal will also support continued research and analysis on standards and safeguards for biofuel development in Brazil, with a focus on protecting vulnerable wetlands in the Pantanal.

title: Monitoring Environmental Impacts of Financial Flows for Infrastructure and Energy in South America
description: Ecoa – Ecology and Action works to protect the Pantanal region, as well as promote sustainable development in the broader Plate River system in Brazil, Argentina, Paraguay, and Bolivia. This grant renewal will allow the grantee to continue its work monitoring investments in energy and infrastructure by the Inter-American Development Bank and to expand its focus on the investment policies and practices of the Brazilian National Development Bank in this important freshwater ecosystem.

title: Monitoring Environmental Impacts of Financial Flows for Infrastructure and Energy in South America
description: Ecoa – Ecology and Action works to protect the Pantanal region, as well as promoting sustainable development in the broader Plate River system, in Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, and Paraguay. The overall goal of the project is to raise standards and improve environmental and social policies at public-sector financial institutions in South America. This grant renewal will allow Ecoa – Ecology and Action to continue its work monitoring investments in energy and infrastructure by public-sector financial institutions, including the Inter-American Development Bank, and the Brazilian Development Bank in this important freshwater ecosystem.

title: Monitoring Environmental Impacts of Financial Flows for Infrastructure and Energy in South America
description: Ecoa – Ecology and Action works to protect the Pantanal region and to promote sustainable development in the broader Plate River system, which spans Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay. The overall goal of the project is to raise standards and improve environmental and social policies at public sector financial institutions in South America. This grant renewal will allow the grantee to continue its work monitoring investments in energy and infrastructure by public sector financial institutions, including the Inter-American Development Bank and the Brazilian Development Bank in this important freshwater ecosystem.

title: Monitoring Environmental Impacts of Financial Flows for Infrastructure and Energy in South America
description: Ecoa – Ecology and Action is a respected nongovernmental organization working to strengthen social and environmental standards of public investment in energy and infrastructure in South America. This grant renewal will enable the grantee to continue its work monitoring investments in energy and infrastructure by the Inter-American Development Bank and the Brazilian Development Bank in Brazil and within the broader Plate River system, which spans Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Paraguay, and Uruguay.

title: Monitoring Environmental Impacts of Financial Flows for Infrastructure and Energy in South America
description: Ecoa-Ecology and Action is a respected nongovernmental organization working to strengthen social and environmental standards of public investment in energy and infrastructure in South America. Over the previous project period, the grantee was instrumental in strengthening social and environmental safeguards at key development finance organizations and achieved a suspension of 144 hydroelectric projects slated for the world’s largest wetlands, the Pantanal, until a strategic environmental assessment of impacts is completed in 2020. This grant renewal will enable the grantee to continue its work monitoring investments in energy and infrastructure, and compliance with environmental and social standards by key development financiers in South America.

title: Reform of Multilateral Development Banks and Japanese ECA/Overseas Development Assistance
grantee: Japan Center for a Sustainable Environment and Society (JACSES)
description: The Japan Center for a Sustainable Environment and Society works to promote an environmentally sustainable and socially equitable society in Japan and throughout the world. Its multilateral development bank and development finance reform program works to eliminate environmentally destructive projects and to promote sustainable development in developing countries. For this project, the organization will continue to encourage greater integration of environmental and social considerations into the policies and practices of Japan’s development finance institutions, as well as encourage the Japanese government to support reform of multilateral development banks. To further the objectives of this project, the grantee will continue its efforts to engage in policy dialogue with key decisionmakers, undertake policy research, coordinate and disseminate information, and strengthen cooperative ties with international nongovernmental organizations and local groups.

title: Reform of Multilateral Development Banks and Japanese ECA/Overseas Development Assistance
grantee: Japan Center for a Sustainable Environment and Society (JACSES)
description: The Japan Center for a Sustainable Environment and Society works to promote an environmentally sustainable and socially equitable society in Japan and throughout the world. Its international financial institutions and development finance reform program works to eliminate environmentally destructive projects and promote sustainable development in developing countries. For this project, the organization will encourage greater integration of environmental and social considerations into the policies and practices of Japan’s development finance institutions as well as convince the Japanese government to support reform of international financial institutions’ policies. To further the objectives of this project, the grantee will engage in policy dialogue with key decisionmakers, undertake policy research, coordinate and disseminate information, and strengthen cooperative ties with international, nongovernmental organizations and local groups.

title: Accountability and Transparency of the Japan Bank for International Cooperation
description: Mekong Watch was established to address and prevent the negative impacts of development projects funded particularly by official Japanese development assistance in the Mekong Region. To achieve this goal, Mekong Watch will continue monitoring controversial projects and researching the relevant policies and practices of international financial institutions; developing resources for the public by compiling the information gathered through monitoring and research activities; and advocating for improving the policies and performance of international financial institutions, in order to resolve or prevent negative environmental and social impacts from their projects.

title: Advocacy for Accountability and Transparency of the International Financial Institutions in Asia
description: Mekong Watch was established to address and prevent the negative impacts of development projects funded particularly by official Japanese development assistance. To achieve this goal, the grantee undertakes research, policy dialogues, and other education and information activities. During the grant period, Mekong Watch will: 1) continue its work to raise awareness about the new environmental and social guidelines of the official Japanese development assistance agencies, including the Japanese export credit agency; 2) begin the dialogue to establish safeguard policies at the Japan External Trade Organization similar to environmental and social guidelines of the Japanese international financial institutions; 3) support initiatives by affected communities in the Mekong region to use the newly established compliance mechanisms of Japanese international financial institutions and the Asian Development Bank; 4) undertake research and analysis of emerging public financial institutions in China and Thailand in order to establish a foundation for future Mekong Watch activities related to these institutions; and 5) commission an independent assessment of its work in these areas.

title: Capacity Building
grantee: Community Chest of the Western Cape
description: The Community Chest of the Western Cape is one of the oldest grantmaking organizations in the region involved with very poor and vulnerable groups. It makes small grants to community-based organizations working in the areas of community development and poverty alleviation. Mott provided support for its capacity-building and training program to ensure that community organizations have the necessary structures and systems in place to access funding from the grantee and other local, intermediary grantmaking bodies. This renewal grant will support the grantee to continue with its community-based capacity development and training, focusing in particular on rural and urban grassroots organizations that are engaged in critical development work, but are unable to access funding because they do not have the necessary management and organizational systems in place.

title: Capacity Building
grantee: Community Chest of the Western Cape
description: Established in 1928, the Community Chest of the Western Cape is affiliated with United Way International. It makes grants and provides training to community-based organizations in the Western Cape province. The training enables organizations to build appropriate systems and structures to operate as professional institutions and to meet the application criteria of funders. Through previous support from Mott, the organization held training courses for organizations in Cape Town and rural areas in the Western Cape province, including special training for youth leaders. This grant continues support to the grantee to train community-based organizations working on development and poverty alleviation. Future plans include the continuation and expansion of the courses to more rural areas, using in-house and external training facilitators; developing a customized database to better monitor the impact of the training; upgrading educational materials; and broadly disseminating the training model in South Africa.

title: Capacity Building
grantee: Community Chest of the Western Cape
description: The Community Chest of the Western Cape provides support to community-based organizations in the Western Cape Province of South Africa. It makes grants and provides organizational development and governance training to community-based organizations. The training program enables newly established organizations to set up structures and systems required to function as professional institutions and meet the application requirements from funders. Past support enabled the organization to expand the training program to more rural areas using in-house and external facilitators, develop a customized database to manage information on the training program, and focus more resources on entry-level courses. This grant will support the grantee to continue to train community-based organizations in urban and rural areas, and develop additional courses that focus on youth development. Future plans include revamping training material, offering elective workshops to develop specific skills such as financial and volunteer management, and collaborating with similar institutions to deliver widespread training.

title: Capacity Building
grantee: Community Chest of the Western Cape
description: The Community Chest of the Western Cape provides support to community-based organizations in the Western Cape Province of South Africa. It does this through making grants, providing training, conducting community conversations, and making in-kind donations to organizations working in the province. The capacity building program provides skills training to leaders of community-based organizations and other community development practitioners. Over the last two years, the grantee provided training to organizations on various themes including governance, organizational development, project management, volunteer management, and youth financial literacy. This grant will support the grantee to continue to train community-based organizations and build their ability to respond effectively to the needs of the communities they serve. It will also strengthen its community engagement efforts and incorporate inputs from local communities into its programs where appropriate and relevant.

title: Capacity Building
grantee: Community Chest of the Western Cape
description: The Community Chest of the Western Cape was established in 1928 to support community-based organizations in Cape Town in the Western Cape Province. It provides training, conducts community conversations, and makes grants and in-kind donations to organizations working in the province. The capacity building program provides skills training to leaders of community-based organizations and other community development practitioners. Over the last two years, the training program has built leadership and management capacity within community-based organizations, enabling the organizations to access funding and other resources in the province. It has also partnered with universities and state-owned entities to deliver training on subjects such as organizational development and financial management to its students and constituencies. This grant will support the Community Chest of the Western Cape to continue providing training to community-based organizations on topics related to building leadership and organizational capacity, facilitate regular talks on philanthropy to encourage effective local giving, and host community conversations on topical issues affecting communities to build social cohesion.

title: Capacity Building
grantee: Community Chest of the Western Cape
description: The Community Chest of the Western Cape was established in 1928 to support community-based organizations working in the Western Cape province. It makes grants, provides training, and encourages dialogue on issues affecting civil society in South Africa. The Capacity Building Program provides training on a variety of topics including financial management, governance, and fundraising. Past support enabled the grantee to train leaders of nonprofits, host dialogues to encourage cross learning among nonprofits, and establish partnerships with other institutions to extend the reach of the training. This grant will enable the grantee to continue to provide training to improve the capacity of community-based organizations, deepen partnerships with local government, ensure that more organizations can access the training, and host conversations that keep nonprofits knowledgeable about the latest developments in the country.

title: General Purposes
description: The Foundation for Human Rights was established with support from the European Union to implement a human rights funding program in South Africa. It has since evolved into one of the most significant indigenous grantmakers in the country supporting the development and strengthening of a culture of human rights in South Africa. It still receives the bulk of its funding from the European Union, but is looking increasingly to local funders to secure its long-term sustainability. Mott has provided institutional support to the grantee, as well as funding for its programmatic work in areas related to Mott’s own grantmaking interests in the paralegal and advice office sector, race and ethnic relations, and reconciliation. This grant will continue to provide general purposes support to the Foundation for Human Rights, specifically focused on strengthening its role as an indigenous grantmaker and expanding and growing its local sources of funding.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purpose support to the Foundation for Human Rights, established with support from the European Union to implement a human rights funding program in South Africa. The organization has evolved into one of the most significant indigenous grantmakers in the country supporting the development and strengthening of a culture of human rights in South Africa. The grantee supports civil society-based organizations and public institutions to promote, protect, and advance human rights, especially grassroots and community organizations involved in addressing poverty and inequality. Prior support allowed it to enhance and strengthen its role as an indigenous grantmaker, especially as this relates to its internal systems of governance, finance and administration, legal capacity, grants administration, and project management. This grant will continue support to the organization to provide better access to marginalized communities to strengthen their ability to access their rights, raise the awareness of constitutional rights, and increase participation in the democratic process.

title: General Purposes
description: The Foundation for Human Rights was established with support from the European Union to implement a human rights funding program in South Africa. It is now one of the most significant indigenous grantmakers in the country supporting the development and strengthening of a culture of human rights in South Africa. It still receives the bulk of its funding from the European Union, but is increasingly looking to local funders to secure its long-term sustainability. Mott has supported the grantee to strengthen its internal capacity, refine its plans, and establish a civil society resource center with the materials it has gathered over the years. This grant will continue to provide general purpose support to the grantee to strengthen its internal systems and promote the work of the human rights sector. Additionally, the grantee will support community advice offices by promoting networking and collaboration among key stakeholders.

title: General Purposes
description: The Foundation for Human Rights was established with support from the European Union to implement a human rights funding program in South Africa. It still receives the bulk of its funding from the European Union and is one of the most significant grantmakers in the country supporting the development and strengthening of a culture of human rights in South Africa. Mott has supported the grantee to strengthen its internal capacity, refine its plans, and establish a civil society resource center with materials it has gathered over the years. This grant will continue to provide general purpose support to the grantee to promote the realization of human rights in South Africa. Additionally, the grantee will continue to support community-based advice offices, programs to raise awareness and knowledge of the Constitution, and research programs on socioeconomic rights.

title: General Purposes
description: The Foundation for Human Rights was established with support from the European Union to implement a human rights funding program in South Africa. It still receives the bulk of its funding from the European Union and is one of the most significant grantmakers in the country supporting the development and strengthening of a culture of human rights. Mott has supported the Foundation for Human Rights to strengthen its internal capacity and has contributed to its research programs. This grant will provide general purpose support to the grantee to improve awareness of constitutional rights with an emphasis on socioeconomic rights and on vulnerable groups; enhance participatory democracy through public policy dialogues on constitutional rights; increase research on socioeconomic rights; and strengthen the capacity, engagement, and participation of civil society organizations in the realization of constitutional rights. The grantee will also make grants to community advice offices and design and implement programs that promote their sustainability.

title: General Purposes
description: The Non Profit Consortium specializes in the enabling of legal and fiscal environments for nonprofits in South Africa. It is one of the few organizations in the country that has a dedicated focus on nonprofit law, providing advocacy, training, capacity building and research. It was actively involved in shaping the nonprofit act and tax-exemption provisions that the new, nonracial democratic government introduced after 1994.This grant will enable the organization to continue providing training and capacity building to nonprofits, particularly community-based organizations, that will help them understand and benefit from the legal and fiscal provisions available to them. The grant also will support research, dissemination of information and advocacy on behalf of the nonprofit sector to improve the enabling environment.

title: Capacity Building for Development
description: The Sustainability Institute is a training and learning center, focusing on facilitating the sustainability of community development projects. Mott provided support to design and pilot a training program targeting staff and leaders of community-based organizations. The program uses a combination of face-to-face, distance learning, and online methods and is aimed at building the knowledge and skills of community-based development workers involved in local development and poverty eradication. This grant will continue to provide support to the Sustainability Institute to work with a number of partners in the country to offer this training program on a national scale. It will also support the grantee’s efforts to ensure that this program is accredited by the relevant authorities, which will assist in securing funding from the appropriate state structures.

title: Capacity Building for Development
description: The Sustainability Institute is a training and learning center that works to facilitate and enhance the sustainability of community development projects. Past support enabled it to design and pilot a training program on principles of community development practice for leaders of community-based organizations. The program uses a combination of face-to-face, distance learning, and online methods and is aimed at building the knowledge and skills of community-based workers who are involved in local development and poverty eradication. An online learning community was established to encourage inputs into the development of learning materials for the program and to create a platform for sharing experiences. This grant will continue to provide support to the grantee to work with a number of partners in South Africa to offer this training program on a national scale. The institute will also expand the curriculum to include basic themes on sustainability.

title: PRODDER and Thusanang
description: The Southern African NGO Network is a civil society-based organization that provides information technology services to the nonprofit sector in South Africa. Prior Mott support provided for the development of a grantmaker database and a Web site with an online directory of South African nonprofits and funding information for the development sector. This renewal grant will assist the Southern African NGO Network to expand the database, improve its functioning, and provide even more detailed information about the nonprofit sector in the country such as financial statements, annual reports, and significant accomplishments. The aim is to enhance the accountability of the nonprofit sector, promote transparency, and use technology to strengthen the sector as a whole.

title: PRODDER and Thusanang
description: The Southern African NGO Network is a one-stop Internet information resource for nonprofits in South Africa. Through its services, programs, and products, it supports the effective use of information technology within the country’s civil society sector. During the previous grant period, the network developed and upgraded an information portal; expanded PRODDER, an online directory of nonprofits; and helped build nonprofit institutional capacity through research, conferences, workshops, e-news, and technical publications. This grant will support the ongoing improvement of the portal, expand its outreach to new nonprofits, and monitor and evaluate the use and effectiveness of the portal. Also, the network will shift the focus of the portal so it becomes more of a platform for the nonprofit sector.

title: NGO Pulse and PRODDER
description: The South African NGO Network supports the use of information communication technologies by civil society for social change. It provides the nonprofit sector with a platform to access, communicate, and disseminate information that is relevant to the sector. Past support enabled the grantee to train nonprofit organizations on social media tools, participate in focus group discussions, and upgrade its portal to a platform that allows nonprofits to upload information. This grant will support the grantee to continue providing information communication technology products and services to the nonprofit sector. Additionally, the grantee will grow the number of nonprofit organizations with access to information communication technologies, generate more content for the portal and other communication tools, and strengthen its income-generating efforts.

title: NGO Pulse and Prodder
description: The Southern African NGO Network provides information and communication technology products and services to civil society organizations in South Africa. It supports the effective use of information communication technologies for social change. The portal is a platform used by civil society organizations to access information, share knowledge, and network with other like-minded organizations. Past support enabled the grantee to provide a platform for debate, commentary, and analysis of topical issues in South Africa; and to produce a development directory known as Prodder. This grant will support the grantee to create online support for nonprofits, produce a print version of Prodder, and continue to explore various opportunities and interventions to enhance the information communication technology capabilities of nonprofits in the country. It will continue to evaluate the portal to ensure that the services provided respond to the needs of nonprofits in the country.

title: NGO Pulse and Prodder
description: The Southern African NGO Network was founded in 1987 to provide information communication technologies products and services to civil society organizations in South Africa. It strengthens the civil society sector by making information communication technologies accessible and affordable for nonprofit organizations working to effect social change. The NGO Pulse is a platform used by nonprofits to share knowledge, make information accessible, and connect with other organizations on issues of common interest to strengthen the role of civil society organizations. Past support enabled the network to expand and diversify its services to nonprofits, create an online support facility accessible to all nonprofit organizations, and partner with other organizations on various projects to improve access to information on civil society organizations. This grant will allow the grantee to continue to connect civil society organizations, provide information communication technology solutions for nonprofits, make information available on development issues, and provide an online platform for dialogue on topical issues affecting civil society in the country.

title: NGO Pulse and Prodder
description: The Southern African NGO Network was founded in 1987 to provide information communications technologies products and services to civil society organizations in South Africa. It makes information communications technologies accessible and affordable for nonprofits and community-based organizations. The NGO Pulse and Prodder is a platform used by nonprofits to share information about developments in the sector and connect with other organizations on issues of common interest. Past support enabled the grantee to provide a comprehensive directory of nonprofits in the country, enhance the Website to make it more accessible, and provide updated information on issues related to civil society. This grant will support the grantee to continue to make information technology available to nonprofits and encourage dialogue on topical issues affecting civil society.

title: NGO Pulse and Prodder
description: The Southern African NGO Network was established in 1987 to provide information communication technology services to civil society organizations in South Africa. Past support enabled the grantee to provide training on the use of communication technologies to community-based organizations in marginalized communities, maintain a platform for dialogue and knowledge sharing for civil society organizations, and create a link between civil society organizations and potential funders. This grant will support the grantee to partner with similar organizations in the southern African region to increase its reach and impact. It will also continue to implement programs that make information communication technologies accessible to civil society organizations.

title: General Purposes
description: The District Six Museum Foundation was established to mark the forced removal of people of color from District Six by the apartheid state during the 1960s. It has since developed into an important national memorial site involved in programs and activities that promote healing and reconciliation. Mott has provided general institutional and operational support to the museum for its work, including oral history projects, educational outreach, and assisting people who had their land returned, to come back to the area. This grant will continue to provide general purposes support, focusing on strengthening the capacity of the museum, particularly as this relates to developing the Sack Futeran Complex–a building that has been purchased adjacent to the museum–to expand the museum, establish a theatre, arts and crafts market, and conference facility, all of which will assist in ensuring its long-term sustainability.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide continued general support to the District Six Museum Foundation. Following the end of apartheid, the museum was created to commemorate this tragic human event and has become one of the country’s leading memorial sites and a beacon of healing and reconciliation. The museum serves as a place of reflection and contemplation and community interaction; an institution for challenge and advocacy; and a memorial to courage and dignity for all of South Africa. Through its collections, exhibitions, educational programs, and community gatherings, the museum tells the stories of forced removals and assists in the reconstitution of the community of District Six and Cape Town.

title: Participatory Local Governance Program
description: Planact supports community processes that enhance good governance at the local level and facilitates engagement between communities and their local governments for improved service delivery. Mott supported Planact to train and support civil society organizations and ward committees in poor and marginalized communities in the Gauteng province to enable them to participate in municipal planning processes. Planact also supported municipalities to effectively engage communities in decisionmaking processes that affect their lives and conducted research aimed at enhancing its work. This grant will support Planact to continue to train and support ward committees, municipal councilors, government officials, and community members on community participation and other topics related to good governance. Research and advocacy will also be undertaken to draw lessons from its work in order to improve on its intervention strategies and to share these lessons with relevant policymakers.

title: Participatory Local Governance Program
description: This program supports community processes that enhance good governance at the local level and facilitates engagement between communities and their local governments for improved service delivery. Past achievements include training ward committees and civil society organizations in poor, marginalized communities so they can fully participate in municipal planning processes. Municipalities were supported to effectively engage communities in decisionmaking processes through workshops. Research and evaluation, public policy analysis, and advocacy also formed part of the program. This grant will support continuation of workshops and training on community engagement and other topics related to democracy and good governance for ward committees, councilors, government officials, and community members. Research and evaluation will also be undertaken to determine lessons learned in order to improve intervention strategies. Established in 1985, Planact works mainly in the urban areas of the Gauteng province, helping to build the capacity of community-based organizations to participate in local governance.

title: Repayable Loan for Facilities Maintenance
description: During the course of the repayable grant, it has become clear that the International Institute of Flint can no longer afford to own and operate its building. These additional funds will allow the organization to explore options and initiate a strategy to divest itself of their building and property.

title: Repayable Loan for Facilities Maintenance
description: In 2003, the International Institute of Flint was awarded a repayable grant to help rebuild its financial and programmatic capacity. Grant increases will support the operation and maintenance of the International Institute of Flint. The institute serves approximately 3,200 immigrants annually by providing legal counseling, language and citizenship classes, and translation and interpretation services.

title: International Finance and the Amazon Program
description: International Finance and the Amazon Program, a project of Amazon Watch, Inc., monitors and works to influence extractive industry and infrastructure projects financed by international financial institutions and private banks. This grant increase will allow Amazon Watch to meet time-sensitive and urgent programmatic needs for the coming year. The grantee will hire independent consultants to provide engineering and other technical analyses for key energy and infrastructure projects planned for the Andean Amazon region. As well, more in-depth analyses and background studies on large-scale infrastructure development in the Andean Amazon region will also be undertaken.

title: International Finance and the Amazon Program
description: The International Finance and the Amazon Program of Amazon Watch monitors and works to influence extractive industry and infrastructure projects financed by international financial institutions and private banks. This renewal grant will support Amazon Watch to strengthen the capacity of constituencies in Amazon countries, particularly environmental and indigenous organizations, to influence and hold accountable international financial decisionmakers for the environmental and social impacts of new and proposed energy and infrastructure projects. The grant will also support community monitoring of planned and existing international financial institution investments in energy and infrastructure in the Amazon region.

title: International Finance and the Amazon Program
description: International Finance and the Amazon Program, a project of Amazon Watch, monitors and works to influence extractive industry and infrastructure projects financed by international financial institutions and other public and private banks. This renewal grant will support Amazon Watch to strengthen the capacity of constituencies in Amazon countries, particularly environmental and indigenous organizations, to influence and hold accountable international financial decisionmakers for the environmental and social impacts of energy and infrastructure projects. The grant will also support monitoring of emblematic highway, waterway, and hydroelectric dam projects in the Amazon region.

title: International Finance and the Amazon Program
description: International Finance and the Amazon Program, a project of Amazon Watch, monitors and works to influence extractive industry and infrastructure projects financed by international financial institutions and other public and private banks. This renewal grant will support the grantee to strengthen the capacity of constituencies in Brazil, Peru, and Ecuador, particularly local and indigenous organizations, to influence and hold accountable international financial decisionmakers for the environmental and social impacts of energy and infrastructure projects. Work will focus on the proposed Belo Monte hydroelectric dam, as well as energy investments in Peru and Ecuador.

title: Strengthening Native American Philanthropy
description: The Strengthening Native American Philanthropy program aims to increase the number of Native American philanthropic institutions and programs that actively support the Native American nonprofit sector and Native American communities, and to facilitate opportunities for collaboration among these institutions and their non-Native American counterparts. In designing the program, First Nations Development Institute consulted with tribes, Native American associations, and peer organizations–all of which expressed an interest in initiating their own philanthropic programs. The initiative includes efforts in the areas of research, documentation, information services, regional conferences, and advocacy for a sound legal environment for tribal foundations.

title: Rede Brasil: Brazilian Network on Multilateral Financial Institutions
description: INESC is a Brazilian research and education organization that promotes citizen empowerment and participation in public policy, human rights protection, and sustainability discussions related to economic and social policy. With this grant increase, INESC will work with the Brazilian network on international financial institutions to broaden discussions on regional integration issues in Latin America. INESC will expand the opportunities for dialogue between non-governmental organizations and parliamentarians; conduct a pilot study among parliamentarians from South America to assess the current status of the debate about regional integration; and organize a workshop during the upcoming South American Summit to be held in Bolivia in November 2006.

title: Finance for Sustainable Development in South America
description: INESC is a Brazilian research and education organization that promotes sustainability in economic and social policy. This grant will provide continued support for the project Rede Brasil: Brazilian Network on Multilateral Financial Institutions. Rede Brasil is a network of over 80 nongovernmental organizations that has been instrumental in increasing public participation in decisionmaking about Brazilian economic policy and related infrastructure and energy investments. Rede Brasil monitors investments from public and private international financial institutions, as well as regional finance mechanisms such as the Brazilian Bank for Economic and Social Development and the newly created Bank of the South. Over the next two years, Rede Brazil members will focus on educating and informing parliamentarians, as well as strengthening the network’s linkages with Latin American and international nongovernmental organizations working to make regional integration investments more sustainable.

title: Finance for Sustainable Development in South America
description: This grant increase to INESC will support a coordinated effort to increase accountability and sustainability of public sector and international investments in energy and infrastructure in South America. It will also provide ongoing support for coordination of the Brazil Network on multilateral banks, as well as efforts to engage parliamentarians and other elected officials in promoting increased transparency and accountability for investments related to regional integration. INESC is a nongovernmental organization established in 1979 for the promotion and strengthening of representative and participative democracy in Brazil.

title: Finance for Sustainable Development in South America
description: This renewal grant to INESC will support a coordinated effort to increase accountability and sustainability of Brazilian public sector and international investments in energy and infrastructure in South America. It will also provide ongoing support for coordination of the Brazil network on multilateral financial institutions, as well as efforts to engage parliamentarians and other elected officials in promoting increased transparency and accountability for investments in the Amazon region. INESC is a nongovernmental organization established in 1979 for the promotion and strengthening of representative and participative democracy in Brazil.

title: Finance for Sustainable Development in South America
description: This grant renewal to INESC will support a coordinated effort to increase accountability and sustainability of public sector and international investments in energy and infrastructure in South America. It will also provide support for ongoing monitoring of national and international public finance of large energy and infrastructure development in Brazil and abroad, particularly in the Amazon rainforest. INESC is a nongovernmental organization established in 1979 for the promotion and strengthening of representative and participative democracy in Brazil.

title: Finance for Sustainable Development in South America
description: This grant renewal to INESC will support a coordinated effort to increase accountability and sustainability of public sector and international investments in energy and infrastructure in South America. It will also provide support for coordination of efforts to educate public officials in promoting increased transparency and accountability for investments related to regional integration. INESC is a nongovernmental organization established in 1979 for the promotion and strengthening of representative and participative democracy in Brazil.

title: Finance for Sustainable Development in South America
description: INESC is a nongovernmental organization established in 1979 for the promotion and strengthening of representative and participative democracy in Brazil. This grant will support a coordinated effort to increase accountability and sustainability of public sector and international investments in energy and infrastructure in South America. It will also provide support for coordination of efforts to educate decisionmakers in promoting increased transparency and accountability for investments related to regional integration.

title: Finance for Sustainable Development in South America
description: INESC is a nongovernmental organization established for the promotion and strengthening of representative and participative democracy in Brazil. It will celebrate its 40-year anniversary in 2019. Over the former grant period, the organization made important contributions to the transparency of public finance in Brazil and internationally at the New Development Bank. Over this grant period, the institute will focus on defending social and environmental standards for development in the Brazilian Amazon and promote strong international standards at national and international financial institutions.

title: State of the Nation Project
description: The “State of the Nation” is a publication produced by the Human Sciences Research Council, which annually reviews the political, social and economic situation in South Africa, particularly from the civil society point of view. The publication looks specifically at government policies over the preceding year and analyzes the impact that these policies have had on the different sectors of society. There is always a special feature article on the annual State of the Nation address that the president delivers to parliament and the implications this could have for the country in the year ahead. Mott has supported the first three publications of the “State of the Nation”. This grant will support the annual production of the “State of the Nation” for the next two years.

title: Enlaces America: Building Constituencies for a Sustainable Future
grantee: Heartland Alliance for Human Needs & Human Rights
initiative: Reform of International Finance and Trade
description: The Heartland Alliance’s project, Enlaces America, works to ensure that leadership capacity is developed within the Latin American immigrant community in the U.S. to create an active constituency working for reform of policies and practices of international finance and trade institutions. This grant increase will support travel stipends for Latin American community leaders in the U.S. to participate in a major policy conference in Los Angeles.

title: Enlaces America: Building Constituencies for a Sustainable Future
grantee: Heartland Alliance for Human Needs & Human Rights
initiative: Reform of International Finance and Trade
description: The Heartland Alliance’s project, Enlaces América: Building Constituencies for a Sustainable Future, aims to ensure that leadership capacity is developed amongst the Latin American immigrant community in the United States to create an active constituency working for reform of policies and practices of international finance and trade institutions. This grant increase will support travel and related expenses for the United States and Latin American leaders to participate in the Migrant Summit of the Americas. These leaders and speakers would provide expert input on energy and infrastructure investments in Latin America.

title: CEE/NIS Public Interest Law Networks: Peer to Peer Information and Training Exchanges
grantee: Columbia University in the City of New York
geographic_focus: Czech Republic, Russia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Latvia, Montenegro, Ukraine, Slovenia, Estonia, Poland, Moldova, Romania, Serbia, North Macedonia, Lithuania, Slovakia, Croatia, Albania, Hungary, Bulgaria, Belarus
description: This grant provides continued support for Columbia University’s Public Interest Law initiative, which promotes the development of a public interest law infrastructure in Central/Eastern Europe and the Newly Independent States (the countries that until 1991 were constituent republics of the former USSR). The project provides technical assistance for strategic litigation on freedom of information and association issues; expands clinical legal education programs on women’s and children’s rights and environmental law; and publishes technical handbooks and papers. Regional legal experts provide training and other assistance; encourage networking; and share lessons learned through workshops, seminars, publications and the project’s Web site.

title: General Purposes
grantee: PILnet: The Global Network for Public Interest Law
geographic_focus: Montenegro, Serbia, Belarus, North Macedonia, Croatia, Romania, Hungary, Poland, Estonia, Slovenia, Moldova, Ukraine, Czech Republic, Albania, Slovakia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Lithuania, Latvia, Bulgaria, Russia
description: The program goal is to promote active civic engagement through public interest law programs as well as advocacy initiatives by nongovernmental organizations in Central and Eastern Europe, Russia, and selected other countries. The Public Interest Law Institute’s program areas include promoting access to justice for socially vulnerable, poor, and disadvantaged people; fostering new generations of public interest lawyers by making legal education more practice oriented; leveraging private sector legal resources for the public good through institutionalized pro bono programs; and building the advocacy skills of nonprofits working on freedom of expression, access to information, antidiscrimination, and other relevant issues. With staff in New York, Budapest, and Moscow, the institute provides expert advice and technical assistance and facilitates peer-to-peer learning and information exchange among a wide range of experts, nonprofits, and public sector actors.

title: New Mexico Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the New Mexico Community Foundation in continuing to further the New Mexico Out-of-School Time Network, the statewide afterschool network composed of state agencies, state and local policymakers, community-based organizations, and other key decisionmakers. This renewal is an innovation grant, which continues to provide core support to the network, while also encouraging new ideas designed to build or enhance positive systemic changes that further policies and practices for school-based/school-linked afterschool programs. In addition to continuing its work in building the field of afterschool in New Mexico, the network will use its ten Regional Point Organizations to expand the scope and breadth of statewide afterschool efforts. Each network receiving an innovation grant is expected to share lessons learned and products with the national network of statewide afterschool networks. This grantee is part of the second cohort of Mott-funded statewide afterschool networks.

title: New Mexico Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will continue to support the New Mexico Public Education Department in the advancement of the New Mexico Statewide Afterschool Network. This grantee is part of the third cohort of Mott-funded, statewide afterschool networks. In addition to continuing its core work building the field of afterschool, the New Mexico Statewide Afterschool Network will increase awareness of and advocacy for afterschool programs by: 1) developing and implementing a marketing and communication plan, and 2) developing a strong, statewide coalition. Lessons learned and products will be shared with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: New Mexico Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will continue to support the New Mexico Public Education Department in the advancement of the New Mexico Statewide Afterschool Network, known formally as the New Mexico Afterschool Alliance. In addition to continuing its core work of building the field of afterschool, the network also continues to develop and strengthen partnerships and engage education and social service organizations in aligning and implementing quality afterschool standards; promoting the adoption of the standards by regulatory agencies; and developing a statewide quality system for afterschool programs. Lessons learned and products developed will be shared with the National Network of Statewide Afterschool Networks.

title: New Mexico Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant to Explora will support the development of the New Mexico Statewide Afterschool Network to continue to build an afterschool and summer learning system that improves outcomes for children and youth through school-based or school-linked afterschool programs. Over the next three years, the network will support the development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) creating a communications plan to raise awareness of the importance of out-of-school time programs; 2) increasing the sustainability of the network; and 3) creating regional workshops and webinars to better serve rural and tribal out-of-school time providers.

title: New Mexico Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Explora, which coordinates the New Mexico Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships, and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) develop and implement an annual Partner Forum on key issues for the afterschool field; 2) develop a statewide system of evaluation that includes a self-assessment, continuous improvement strategies, and rigorous impact evaluation; 3) conduct high-quality professional development and leadership training; and 4) support the development and distribution of the new afterschool program content in collaboration with the Foundation’s thematic partners.

title: Arizona Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will continue to support the Arizona School-Age Coalition in furthering the Arizona Out-of-School Time Network, a statewide afterschool network composed of state agencies, state and local policymakers, community-based organizations, and other key decisionmakers. This innovation grant will continue to provide core support to the network, while also encouraging new ideas designed to build or enhance positive systemic changes that further policies and practices for school-based/school-linked afterschool programs. In addition to continuing its work in building the field of afterschool in Arizona, the network will create a policy strategy focused on safety and crime reduction. Each network receiving an innovation grant is expected to share lessons learned and products with the national network of statewide afterschool networks. This grantee is part of the second cohort of Mott-funded statewide afterschool networks.

title: Arizona Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will continue to support the Arizona Center for Afterschool Excellence to further the Arizona Statewide Afterschool Network, a statewide afterschool network designed to raise awareness, build capacity and sustainability, and promote the importance of safe, high quality, affordable afterschool programs. This grantee is part of the second cohort of Mott-funded, statewide afterschool networks. This project will continue to provide core support to the network, while also encouraging new ideas designed to align and integrate afterschool and education systems. In addition to continuing its work in building the field of afterschool in Arizona, the grantee will design and conduct a multipronged education and awareness campaign targeting key stakeholders. The network will share lessons learned and products with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: Arizona Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Arizona Center for Afterschool Excellence which coordinates the Arizona Statewide Afterschool Network. The network seeks to improve afterschool program quality across the state by developing and promoting a comprehensive quality improvement system. In addition to continuing its core work to advance afterschool in Arizona, the network will complete a multiyear project to: 1) work with education and afterschool stakeholders to develop and promote the adoption of afterschool standards that support formal education; 2) endorse program assessment tools that align with the standards; and 3) design a multitiered professional development system.

title: Arizona Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant to the Arizona Center for Afterschool Excellence will support the development of the Arizona Statewide Afterschool Network to continue to build an afterschool and summer learning system that improves outcomes for children and youth through school-based or school-linked afterschool programs. Over the next three years, the network will support the development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) sponsoring a statewide mayoral summit; 2) cultivating new relationships with potential philanthropic partners to support the afterschool field; and 3) creating new training materials on the Arizona quality standards and the self-assessment tool.

title: Arizona Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Arizona Center for Afterschool Excellence, which coordinates the Arizona Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) creating an outreach and partnership plan for tribal and rural communities; 2) developing a comprehensive plan to increase resources for afterschool programs; 3) developing a quality seal program to support quality work and help promote program effectiveness; and 4) participating in the development and distribution of new afterschool program content in collaboration with the Foundation’s thematic partners.

title: Washington Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will continue to support the YWCA of Seattle-King County-Snohomish County in furthering the Washington Statewide Afterschool Network, a network composed of state agencies, state and local policymakers, community-based organizations, and other key decisionmakers. This renewal is an innovation grant, which continues to provide core support to the network, while also encouraging new ideas designed to build or enhance positive systemic changes that further policies and practices for school-based/school-linked afterschool programs.
