In addition to continuing its work in building the field of afterschool in Washington, the network will develop and implement a model that will assist other states in convening stakeholders to further investments in afterschool. Each network receiving an innovation grant is expected to share lessons learned and products with the national network of statewide afterschool networks. This grantee is part of the second cohort of Mott-funded statewide afterschool networks.

title: Washington Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will continue to support the YWCA of Seattle-King County-Snohomish County in developing the Washington Statewide Afterschool Network. The network is working to provide direct support, training, information, and funding assistance to enable communities to provide positive afterschool activities for youth. This grantee is part of the second cohort of Mott-funded, statewide afterschool networks. This renewal grant continues to provide core support to the network, while also encouraging new ideas designed to align and integrate afterschool and education systems. In addition to continuing its work in building the field of afterschool in Washington, the network will engage a diverse set of community stakeholders to strengthen the role of afterschool programs in the health of young people. The network will share lessons learned and products with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: Washington Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the YWCA of Seattle-King County-Snohomish County, which coordinates the Washington Statewide Afterschool Network. The grantee seeks to advance high quality, expanded learning and afterschool programs as a key strategy to closing the achievement gap in Washington state. In addition to continuing the Washington Statewide Afterschool Network’s core work to advance afterschool in Washington, the grantee will complete a multiyear project to: 1) develop and implement a state plan to better integrate afterschool programs with the state education system; and 2) design a comprehensive communications campaign to build public awareness around the needs and benefits of quality and diverse afterschool opportunities.

title: Washington Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support School’s Out Washington, which coordinates the Washington Statewide Afterschool Network. The grantee seeks to advance high quality, expanded learning and afterschool programs as a key strategy to closing the achievement gap in Washington state. In addition to continuing the network’s core work to advance afterschool in Washington, the grantee will complete a multiyear project to: 1) develop and implement a state plan to better integrate afterschool programs with the state education system; and 2) design a comprehensive communications campaign to build public awareness of the needs and benefits of quality and diverse afterschool opportunities.

title: Washington Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant to School’s Out Washington will support the development of the Washington Statewide Afterschool Network to continue to build an afterschool and summer learning system that improves outcomes for children and youth through school-based or school-linked afterschool programs. Over the next three years, the network will support the development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) creating a campaign to increase state investment in afterschool and summer learning; 2) implementing an outreach plan to engage providers, parents, youth, and other stakeholders from across the state; and 3) extending the state’s afterschool STEM (science, technology, engineering, and math) pilot program to add an additional cohort each year.

title: Washington Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support School’s Out Washington, which coordinates the Washington Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) designing a toolkit to educate key stakeholders on the importance of afterschool; 2) developing a comprehensive plan to increase resources for afterschool programs, quality initiatives and the afterschool network; 3) designing a quality seal program to support quality work and help promote program effectiveness for districts and parents; and 4) participating in the development and distribution of new afterschool program content in collaboration with the Foundation’s thematic partners.

title: Connecticut Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will continue to support the Connecticut State Department of Education in furthering the Connecticut Statewide Afterschool Network, a statewide afterschool network composed of state agencies, state and local policymakers, and other key decisionmakers. This renewal is an innovation grant, which continues to provide core support to the network, while also encouraging new ideas designed to build or enhance positive systemic changes that further policies and practices for school-based/school-linked afterschool programs. In addition to continuing its work in building the field of afterschool in Connecticut, the network will use technology-based tools to improve effectiveness and efficiency, and increase communication between stakeholders. Each network receiving an innovation grant is expected to share lessons learned and products with the national network of statewide afterschool networks. This grantee is part of the second cohort of Mott-funded statewide afterschool networks.

title: Connecticut Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: Connecticut Network for Children and Youth, Inc.
description: This grant will continue to support the Connecticut After School Network in systematically building a statewide afterschool network composed of state agencies, state and local policymakers, afterschool providers, and the private sector. This grantee is part of the second cohort of Mott-funded statewide afterschool networks. This renewal grant continues to provide core support to the network, while also encouraging new ideas designed to align and integrate afterschool and education systems. In addition to continuing its work in building the field of afterschool in Connecticut, the Connecticut After School Network will focus on raising the quality of afterschool programs by improving linkages between afterschool and school day learning and facilitating informal support networks of program managers and site coordinators. The network will share lessons learned and products with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: Connecticut Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: Connecticut Network for Children and Youth, Inc.
description: This grant will provide continued support to the Connecticut After School Network to advance afterschool in Connecticut. In addition to supporting the core work of the network, this grant will include the design and implementation of a public awareness campaign to advance afterschool and expanded learning opportunities across the state. Specifically, the network will complete a multiyear project to: 1) develop new communications tools including a series of policy briefs; and 2) increase the level of stakeholder engagement among parents, educators, business leaders, funders, and policymakers.

title: Connecticut Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: Connecticut Network for Children and Youth, Inc.
description: This grant to the Connecticut After School Network will support the development of the Connecticut Statewide Afterschool Network to continue to build an afterschool and summer learning system that improves outcomes for children and youth through school-based or school-linked afterschool programs. Over the next three years, the grantee will support the development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) creating a new afterschool data initiative to document the current status of afterschool programs in Connecticut; 2) coordinating a strategy to increase state funding for afterschool programs; and 3) expanding and improving training and professional development supports that will promote a continuous quality improvement for afterschool and summer learning programs.

title: Connecticut Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: Connecticut Network for Children and Youth, Inc.
description: This grant will support the Connecticut After School Network to continue development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) increasing communications activities to build public awareness about the importance of afterschool; 2) developing a comprehensive plan to increase resources for afterschool programs; 3) expanding training content and resource materials on social-emotional learning, mental health, and parent engagement; and 4) participating in the development and distribution of new afterschool program content in collaboration with the Foundation’s thematic partners.

title: New York Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will enable the After-School Corporation to continue the New York Statewide Afterschool Network, a statewide afterschool network composed of state agencies, state and local policymakers, community-based organizations, and other key decisionmakers. This innovation grant will continue to provide core support to the network, while also encouraging new ideas designed to build or enhance positive systemic changes that further policies and practices for school-based/school-linked afterschool programs. In addition to continuing its work in building the field of afterschool in New York, the network will: develop a user guide to its program quality tool that will allow program staff and site directors to access information easily; and create a professional development institute for afterschool program managers. Each network receiving an innovation grant is expected to share lessons learned and products with the national network of statewide afterschool networks. This grantee is part of the second cohort of Mott-funded statewide afterschool networks.

title: New York Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will continue to support the New York Statewide Afterschool Network, a project of the After-School Corporation. It will strengthen and guide high quality afterschool programming and policies for New York’s children and youth, particularly low-income and hard-to-reach populations. This grantee is part of the second cohort of Mott-funded, statewide afterschool networks. This renewal grant will continue to provide core support to the network, while also encouraging new ideas designed to align and integrate afterschool and education systems. In addition to continuing its work in building the field of afterschool in New York, the network specifically will strengthen the links between afterschool, summer learning, and expanded learning opportunities with the state public education system. The network will share lessons learned and products with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: New York Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the After-School Corporation, which coordinates the New York Statewide Afterschool Network. In addition to continuing the network’s core work to advance afterschool in New York, it will complete a multiyear project to better connect the afterschool learning system with the wide range of public agencies that serve youth and families including public health, safety, and workforce development. The network seeks to align the overall youth-serving system in New York to: 1) develop more high quality afterschool opportunities; 2) improve service coordination; 3) bring together disparate funding streams; and 4) leverage best practices to better serve young people as they prepare for success in college, careers, and life.

title: New York Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: New York State Network for Youth Success, Inc.
description: This grant to AfterSchool Works! New York will support the development of the New York Statewide Afterschool Network to continue to build an afterschool and summer learning system that improves outcomes for children and youth through school-based or school-linked afterschool programs. Over the next three years, the network will support the development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) developing regional afterschool science, technology, engineering, and math (STEM) networks; 2) increasing high quality, fee-for-service professional development activities that strengthen the field; and 3) assessing the current professional development landscape and developing a plan to address educators’ needs.

title: New York Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: New York State Network for Youth Success, Inc.
description: This grant will support the New York State Network for Youth Success, which coordinates the New York Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) educating key stakeholders on the need for a statewide data system for afterschool and summer learning programs; 2) developing a comprehensive plan to increase resources for afterschool and summer learning programs and the Network for Youth Success; 3) expanding the number of accredited afterschool programs in New York to increase quality programs across the state; and 4) participating in the development and distribution of new afterschool program content in collaboration with the Foundation’s thematic partners.

title: Ohio Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: Ohio Child Care Resource & Referral Association
description: This grant will support the Ohio Child Care Resource & Referral Association in furthering the Ohio Statewide Afterschool Network, a network composed of state agencies, state and local policymakers, community-based organizations, and other key decisionmakers. This renewal is an innovation grant, which continues to provide core support to the network, while also encouraging new ideas designed to build or enhance positive systemic changes that further policies and practices for school-based/school-linked afterschool programs. In addition to continuing its work in building the field of afterschool in Ohio, the network will focus on the opportunity to use Temporary Assistance for Needy Families funding to support afterschool programs. Each network receiving an innovation grant is expected to share lessons learned and products with the national network of statewide afterschool networks. This grantee is part of the second cohort of Mott-funded statewide afterschool networks.

title: Ohio Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: Ohio Child Care Resource & Referral Association
description: This grant to the Ohio Child Care Resource & Referral Association will continue to support Ohio’s need to build a statewide, inclusive network of afterschool stakeholders. This grantee is part of the second cohort of Mott-funded statewide afterschool networks. This project will continue to provide core support to the network, while also encouraging new ideas designed to align and integrate afterschool and education systems. In addition to continuing its work in building the field of afterschool in Ohio, the network will work with existing and new partners from organizations supporting learning and education initiatives to embed high quality afterschool and extended learning opportunities to support student success. The network will share lessons learned and products with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: Ohio Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: Ohio Child Care Resource & Referral Association
description: This grant will support the Ohio Child Care Resource and Referral Association which coordinates the Ohio Statewide Afterschool Network. The network seeks to increase the capacity of afterschool programs to document their positive impacts on children, youth, and families. In addition to continuing the network’s core work to advance afterschool in Ohio, it will complete a multiyear project to: 1) develop a toolkit and a community of practice to help afterschool programs collect and use data to document and share their positive results to schools, funders, and stakeholders; 2) publish a series of white papers that highlight areas in which afterschool and expanded learning programs support student achievement; and 3) establish a new statewide initiative on data and accountability.

title: Ohio Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant to Voices for Ohio’s Children will support the development of the Ohio Statewide Afterschool Network to continue to build an afterschool and summer learning system that improves outcomes for children and youth through school-based or school-linked afterschool programs. Over the next three years, the network will support the development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) developing a new afterschool data initiative on the availability and locations of afterschool programs; 2) coordinating a strategy to increase state funding in support of afterschool programs; and 3) creating nutrition guidelines for afterschool programs.

title: Ohio Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Healthcare Collaborative of Greater Columbus, which coordinates the Ohio Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) developing a comprehensive communications and outreach plan about the importance of afterschool; 2) developing a comprehensive plan to increase resources for afterschool programs and the Ohio Statewide Afterschool Network; 3) enhancing the mapping and data collection of afterschool programs across the state; and 4) participating in the development and distribution of new afterschool program content in collaboration with the Foundation’s thematic partners.

title: Nebraska Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will continue to support the expansion of the Nebraska Statewide Afterschool Network in its efforts to build sustainable afterschool programs in Nebraska. This project will allow the network to focus on creating statewide afterschool funding and supporting sustainability of local programs. Nebraska Children and Families Foundation is part of the second cohort of Mott-funded statewide afterschool networks. This renewal is an innovation grant, which continues to provide core support to the network while also encouraging new ideas designed to build or enhance positive systemic changes that further policies and practices for school-based/school-linked afterschool programs. Each network receiving an innovation grant is expected to share lessons learned and products with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: Nebraska Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will continue to support the Nebraska Children and Families Foundation in the advancement of the Nebraska Statewide Afterschool Network. This grantee is part of the third cohort of Mott-funded, statewide afterschool networks. In addition to continuing its core work building the field of afterschool, the Nebraska Statewide Afterschool Network will work with state- and community-level policymakers to develop partnerships, policies, and practices necessary to grow and sustain more community learning centers featuring high quality afterschool programs in Nebraska. Lessons learned and products will be shared with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: Nebraska Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Nebraska Children and Families Foundation which coordinates the Nebraska Statewide Afterschool Network. In addition to continuing the network’s core work to advance afterschool in Nebraska, it will complete a multiyear project to develop and launch a statewide coalition of city-wide, out-of-school time systems. The network seeks to cultivate strong rural and urban partnerships to effectively promote state-level policy change in support of additional high quality expanded learning opportunities in Nebraska’s highest need communities. To ensure that new models and best practices are incorporated nationally, the network will share lessons learned and products with the other state networks.

title: Nebraska Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase to Nebraska Children and Families Foundation will support the Nebraska Statewide Afterschool Network in hosting an afterschool and summer science, technology, engineering and math systems building institute for statewide afterschool networks and partners. The institute will provide participants an opportunity to share best practices and emerging models, while working with national experts at the forefront of afterschool and summer science, technology, engineering and math.

title: Nebraska Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant to Nebraska Children and Families Foundation will support the Nebraska Statewide Afterschool Network to continue to build an afterschool and summer learning system that improves outcomes for children and youth through school-based or school-linked afterschool programs. Over the next three years, the network will support the development of policy, partnerships, and quality initiatives to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific projects will: 1) expand and enhance Nebraska’s statewide coalition of citywide expanded learning opportunity systems; 2) develop new career and technical education afterschool programming; and 3) coordinate and support the expansion of a statewide professional development system and coaching opportunities across Nebraska.

title: Nebraska Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Nebraska Children and Families Foundation, which coordinates the Nebraska Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships, and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) create a high-level advisory group of young business leaders to increase supportive partnerships; 2) develop, adopt, and promote voluntary expanded learning quality standards; 3) launch the Expanded Learning Opportunities Design Center to serve as a hub for strategic partnerships and projects to support rural programs; and 4) support the development and distribution of the new afterschool program content in collaboration with the Foundation’s thematic partners.

title: Iowa Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Chrysalis Foundation in furthering the Iowa Afterschool Alliance, a statewide afterschool network composed of state agencies, state and local policymakers, community-based organizations, and other key decisionmakers. This renewal is an innovation grant, which continues to provide core support to the network, while also encouraging new ideas designed to build or enhance positive systemic changes that further policies and practices for school-based/school-linked afterschool programs. In addition to continuing its work in building the field of afterschool in Iowa, the network will create “Iowa’s Blueprint for Afterschool.” This document will catalogue issues affecting afterschool in the state, while putting forth a comprehensive policy and funding plan for afterschool in Iowa. Each network receiving an innovations grant is expected to share lessons learned and products with the national network of statewide afterschool networks. This grantee is part of the second cohort of Mott-funded statewide afterschool networks.

title: Iowa Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will continue to support the Chrysalis Foundation in its coordination of the Iowa Statewide Afterschool Network, which has been developing a public/private network of stakeholders to build a statewide afterschool system. This grantee is part of the second cohort of Mott-funded, statewide afterschool networks. This renewal grant will continue to provide core support to the network, while also encouraging new ideas designed to align and integrate afterschool and education systems. In addition to continuing its work in building the field of afterschool in Iowa, the network will identify two regions in the state to develop and implement a model for an expanded learning day for youth in middle and high school. The network will share lessons learned and products with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: Iowa Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Chrysalis Foundation, which coordinates the Iowa Statewide Afterschool Network. In addition to continuing the network’s core work to advance afterschool in Iowa, it will complete a multiyear project to implement an extensive outreach project to expand the network’s relationships, gather data, and increase knowledge of high quality afterschool programs across the state. Specifically, the network will: 1) align outreach activities with other key policy initiatives, including the Governor’s STEM Initiative, expanded learning initiatives, the third-grade reading campaign, and summer learning; 2) develop a data collection and dissemination strategy; and 3) develop and promote a comprehensive understanding of afterschool in Iowa.

title: Iowa Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant to the Chrysalis Foundation will support the development of the Iowa Statewide Afterschool Network to continue to build an afterschool and summer learning system that improves outcomes for children and youth through school-based or school-linked afterschool programs. Over the next three years, the network will support the development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) engaging new policymaker champions in support of afterschool and summer learning; 2) creating a new database initiative to document the current state of afterschool in Iowa; and 3) expanding and improving the training and professional development opportunities to improve the reach and quality of afterschool programming.

title: Iowa Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Iowa Children’s Museum, which coordinates the Iowa Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) creating a sustainable infrastructure for Out of School Time programs through partnerships; 2) supporting education policies to strengthen support for Out of School Time initiatives through statewide efforts; 3) expanding continuous improvement systems to promote high quality programs; and 4) participating in the development and distribution of new afterschool program content in collaboration with the Foundation’s thematic partners.

title: Massachusetts Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will enable Child Development for Kids to coordinate the Massachusetts Afterschool Partnership, a statewide afterschool network promoting quality afterschool opportunities for all children and youth in Massachusetts. This grantee is part of the second cohort of Mott-funded statewide afterschool networks. This renewal is an innovation grant, which continues to provide core support to the network, while also encouraging new ideas designed to build or enhance positive systemic changes that further policies and practices for school-based/school-linked afterschool programs. In addition to continuing its work in building the field of afterschool in Massachusetts, the network will: establish the summer learning initiative; create the Massachussetts Afterschool Funders Alliance; continue to support the development of statewide afterschool policies; and develop an online community for the afterschool field. Each network receiving an innovation grant is expected to share lessons learned and products with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: Massachusetts Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Child Development for Kids, Inc., in continuing to manage the Massachusetts statewide afterschool network which expands and supports high quality afterschool programs so that Massachusetts’ children are safe, supervised, and prepared to lead productive lives. This grantee is part of the second cohort of Mott-funded, statewide afterschool networks. This renewal continues to provide core support to the network, while also encouraging new ideas designed to align and integrate afterschool and education systems. In addition to continuing its work in building the field of afterschool in Massachusetts, the network will develop an initiative to build positive, systemic change that furthers cooperative school-linked, afterschool programs. The network will share lessons learned and products with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: Massachusetts Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Massachusetts Afterschool Partnership which coordinates the Massachusetts Statewide Afterschool Network. In addition to continuing the network’s core work to advance afterschool in Massachusetts, it will complete a multiyear project to establish a coordinated, statewide vision for afterschool and expanded learning. Specifically, the network will: 1) design and implement a policy campaign to support the development of afterschool and expanded learning policies that are linked with education reform efforts; 2) develop and implement a public awareness campaign to increase knowledge of the impact of quality afterschool programming on student outcomes; and 3) create a toolkit to support educators, policymakers, and afterschool and expanded learning stakeholders in assessing state and federal education policy.

title: Massachusetts Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant to the Massachusetts Afterschool Partnership will support the development of the Massachusetts Statewide Afterschool Network to continue to build an afterschool and summer learning system that improves outcomes for children and youth through school-based or school-linked afterschool programs. Over the next three years, the grantee will support the development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) launching an Afterschool Matters communications and marketing campaign to increase media presence in print, electronically, and on social media; 2) increasing investments to support quality afterschool programs; and 3) developing afterschool standards to be used in the state’s quality rating and improvement system.

title: Massachusetts Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Massachusetts Afterschool Partnership, which coordinates the Massachusetts Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) designing a new afterschool data sharing model for districts and afterschool programs; 2) establishing a business advisory team to support afterschool programs and the network; 3) cultivating a community of practice for afterschool educators at local, state, and national levels to share promising practices, data, new resources and educational strategies; and 4) participating in the development and distribution of new afterschool program content in collaboration with the Foundation’s thematic partners.

title: Downtown Property Purchase
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will allow the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation to purchase the former Mega Coney Island property located on Martin Luther King Boulevard in downtown Flint. The Uptown Reinvestment Corporation’s supporting organization, the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, works to improve the quality of life for Flint’s residents through investment in projects that revitalize the downtown district. The purchase and subsequent redevelopment of the Mega Coney Island site will serve this charitable purpose by reducing blight, providing an opportunity for job creation, and adding to the economic vitality of downtown.

title: Flint Youth Theatre Operating Support
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: Since being established in 1957, the Flint Youth Theatre (FYT) has grown into a resident theater company that provides Flint area audiences with unique intergenerational programming and is nationally recognized as a model youth theater. Each year thousands of students are exposed to the theater and have the opportunity to pursue and develop their creative potential through its drama school and outreach efforts in area schools. FYT attracts multi-aged audiences to its theater productions, many of which are locally developed and intended to engage the community and stimulate thoughtful discussion on critical issues and historical topics.This grant will enable FYT to continue to provide quality programs and services that educate, inspire, entertain, and involve Flint students and the community in meaningful ways.

title: Operating Support
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant increase to the Flint Cultural Center Corporation will provide additional operating support to cover the revenue shortfall for the 2005-06 fiscal year. The additional support will allow the corporation to end the year with a balanced budget and not require the use of unrestricted assets.

title: Operating Support
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Flint Cultural Center Corporation operates The Whiting, Sloan Museum, Longway Planetarium, and Flint Youth Theatre/Bower Theater on the 30-acre Flint Cultural Center campus. Last year, nearly 300,000 students and adults attended or participated in a variety of cultural, educational, and instructional programs and activities at the Flint Cultural Center. In addition to offering national touring artists and live theater, the corporation also focuses on providing educational programming, both on site and in the schools. This grant will support operating costs for the Flint Cultural Center Corporation.

title: Operating Support
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Flint Cultural Center Corporation operates Whiting Auditorium, Sloan Museum, Longway Planetarium, and Flint Youth Theatre/Bower Theater on the 30-acre Flint Cultural Center campus. Approximately 250,000 students and adults will attend or participate in a variety of cultural, educational, and instructional programs and activities at these cultural center organizations this year. In addition to offering national touring artists and live theater, the corporation also focuses on providing educational programming, both on-site and in the schools. Like other cultural organizations around the country, earned income from admissions and fees, combined with endowment income, does not provide sufficient revenue to maintain facilities and operate programs. This grant will provide operating support to the Flint Cultural Center Corporation for the benefit of its facilities, member organizations, and programs.

title: Operating Support
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Flint Cultural Center Corporation operates Whiting Auditorium, Sloan Museum, Longway Planetarium, and Flint Youth Theatre/Bower Theater on the 30-acre Flint Cultural Center campus. Approximately 250,000 students and adults attended or participated in a variety of cultural, educational, entertainment, and instructional programs and activities at these cultural center organizations last year. In addition to offering national touring artists and live theater, the corporation also focuses on providing educational programming, both on-site and in local schools. Like other cultural organizations around the country, earned income from admissions and fees, combined with endowment income, does not provide sufficient revenue to maintain facilities and operate programs. This grant will provide support to the Flint Cultural Center Corporation for general operations, campus facilities, and programs.

title: Operating Support
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture

initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide operating support to the Flint Cultural Center Corporation. description: This grant to the Flint Cultural Center Foundation will support several capital improvements to the buildings on the Flint Cultural Center campus — Whiting Auditorium, Sloan Museum, Buick Gallery, Longway Planetarium, and Bower/Flint Youth Theatre. title: General Purposes
grantee: Community Law and Rural Development Centre
description: The Community Law and Rural Development Centre promotes an environment for equitable access to justice for rural and marginalized communities in the KwaZulu-Natal and Eastern Cape provinces.Multiyear funding will enable the center to provide support to paralegals and advice centers across the two provinces, enabling them to educate communities about their rights and how to access them. Recent activities included assisting thousands of poor people to access legal services and recover monies owed to them; resolving community conflicts through alternative dispute resolution methods; encouraging communities to participate in local government planning processes; raising the awareness of communities about their legal and human rights; and providing training and support to paralegals and paralegal management committees to ensure that they are able to effectively discharge their duties.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Community Law and Rural Development Centre

description: The Community Law and Rural Development Centre promotes equitable access to justice for rural and marginalized communities in the KwaZulu-Natal and Eastern Cape provinces through providing support, training, and funds for advice offices and paralegals. This grant increase will support the organization in meeting a budget shortfall and support advice offices that are part of the organization, through which it provides legal advice to poor and marginalized communities on their rights and how to access these rights.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Community Law and Rural Development Centre
geographic_focus: Eastern Cape, Province of, KwaZulu-Natal, Province of
description: The Community Law and Rural Development Centre supports communities in rural and marginalized areas of the KwaZulu-Natal and Eastern Cape provinces to access their rights by supporting 35 advice offices based within these communities. Paralegals within these advice offices handle various matters on behalf of community members, including access to social security information, unemployment insurance claims, unfair dismissals in the workplace and other labor matters, and compensation for road accidents. This grant will help to strengthen advice offices through training of paralegals and providing hands-on support to ensure that they provide relevant and effective services to communities. It will also introduce new programs that build on its experiences to ensure that community members are able to access basic services from their local governments and resources for community development and poverty eradication projects. This will be accomplished in partnership with local actors including chiefs and community-based organizations.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Community Law and Rural Development Centre
geographic_focus: Eastern Cape, Province of, KwaZulu-Natal, Province of
description: The Community Law and Rural Development Centre, established in 1989, provides access to justice services to poor communities in rural areas of KwaZulu-Natal and Eastern Cape provinces of South Africa. It has a network of 30 advice offices that provide free legal advice and other services to thousands of poor people, including access to social security, claiming unemployment insurance benefits, unfair dismissals in the workplace, and other labor matters. Past support assisted the centre to train and mentor paralegals within advice offices, who in turn assisted community members to access services from government and challenge decisions and institutions that violated their rights. title: Study to Increase Success for Low-Income Adults in Community College
description: Breaking Through: Helping Low-Skilled Adults Enter and Succeed in College and Careers is a three-year national initiative conducted by Jobs for the Future. Its goal is to expand effective strategies for helping low-skilled, low-income adults enter and succeed in community college occupational degree and credential programs and consequently succeed in the labor market. This grant will support continued testing and evaluation of selected strategies being implemented by 16 community colleges in communities and states across the nation. Activities include strengthening and expanding “best practices” at participating institutions; increasing attention to the needs of low-skilled adults within the community college field; and promoting policies at state and federal levels that serve to deepen and accelerate the adoption of strategies that improve outcomes for low-skilled adults in community college degree programs.

title: Study to Increase Success for Low-Income Adults in Community College
description: The purpose of this renewal grant to Jobs for the Future is to support the final year of “Breaking Through”, an initiative aimed at expanding the capacity of community colleges to help adults with low literacy and mathematic skills advance into and succeed in college-level professional and technical programs that prepare them for family-supporting jobs. Funds will support continued testing and evaluation of program strategies being implemented in 26 community colleges across the United States. Key activities include focused grant management of funded colleges to ensure delivery of promised outcomes, technical assistance, peer learning, leadership development among community college presidents, tool development, publications, and completion of a third-party evaluation.

title: FERC Relicensing Engagement in the Mobile Bay Basin
description: The Mobile Bay Basin is host to one of the greatest arrays of aquatic freshwater species in the continental U.S. Yet the region has experienced a staggering loss of biodiversity that can primarily be attributed to the habitat loss and fragmentation caused by dams and other modifications to rivers and streams. The relicensing of several hydropower facilities in the basin provides a valuable opportunity to improve conditions for the wealth of remaining freshwater species.This grant will enable the World Wildlife Fund’s Southeastern Rivers and Streams Program to promote the protection and enhancement of aquatic ecosystems during the relicensing processes under way in the Mobile Bay Basin.

title: General Purposes

description: The Southern Education Foundation’s Education Summers Youth Leadership Initiative provides a multiracial, multiethnic group of 15 talented students enrolled in southern colleges and universities with valuable experiences in the fields of education, workforce preparedness and economic growth. title: Transitional Justice Program
description: The goal of this grant increase is to support ongoing cooperation among the Humanitarian Law Center and its regional partners, the Research and Documentation Center Sarajevo in Bosnia and Herzegovina and Documenta in Croatia, both of which are Mott grantees. Additional grant funds will be used to pay the partial salary of one staff member at the Humanitarian Law Center to facilitate ongoing communication, coordination, and joint project development and implementation. The overall project goal is to support the successful transition of the Humanitarian Law Center, one of the most prominent human rights organizations in the Western Balkans, to an institution for documentation and research of humanitarian law and human rights abuses stemming from the violent conflicts in the region since 1991.

title: Transitional Justice Program
description: This grant increase will support ongoing cooperation among the Humanitarian Law Center in Serbia and its regional partners, the Research and Documentation Center Sarajevo in Bosnia and Herzegovina and Documenta in Croatia, both of which are Mott grantees. Additional grant funds will be used to pay the partial salary of one staff member at the Humanitarian Law Center to facilitate ongoing communication, coordination and joint project development and implementation; and to pay the partial costs of an external consultant to facilitate the organizational and programmatic development of the center. The overall project goal is to support the successful transition of the Humanitarian Law Center, one of the most prominent human rights organizations in the Western Balkans, to an institution for documentation and research of humanitarian law and human rights abuses stemming from the violent conflicts in the region since 1991.

title: General Purposes
description: The overall program goal is to establish the conditions for dealing with the past in Serbia and the broader region. To this end, the Humanitarian Law Center researches and documents war crimes and other human rights abuses stemming from the regime of Slobodan Milosevic in Serbia and the violent conflicts in the former Yugoslavia during the 1990s. Over the past two years, the center built an extensive archive of documentation; increased the archive’s accessibility to researchers, prosecutors, and decisionmakers; and supported efforts to raise public awareness about issues of truth, justice, and reconciliation. During the grant period, the center will focus on continuing to build its archive and improve accessibility, establishing a regional coalition of organizations addressing dealing with the past issues, and building the center’s organizational and programmatic capacities. The center is based in Belgrade, Serbia, and has a field office in Pristina, Kosovo.

title: General Purposes
description: The overall program goal is to establish the conditions for dealing with the past in Serbia and the broader region. To this end, the Humanitarian Law Center researches and documents war crimes and other human rights abuses stemming from the regime of Slobodan Milosevic in Serbia and the violent conflicts in the former Yugoslavia during the 1990s. Over the past two years, the center built an extensive archive of documentation; increased the archive’s accessibility to researchers, prosecutors, and decisionmakers; and helped to build a coalition of key stakeholders supporting a regional victims’ commission. The center also strengthened its governance by establishing a new board of directors. During the grant period, the center will support the coalition for a regional victims’ commission, research killed and missing persons in Kosovo, promote public awareness of war crimes through documentation and educational activities, and build the center’s organizational and programmatic capacities. The center is based in Belgrade, Serbia.

title: General Purposes
description: The overall program goal is to establish the conditions for dealing with the past in Serbia and the broader region. To this end, the Humanitarian Law Center researches and documents war crimes and other human rights abuses stemming from the regime of Slobodan Milosevic in Serbia and the violent conflicts in the former Yugoslavia during the 1990s. During the past two years, the center has built up its war crimes database and archive, represented victims in compensation lawsuits, published information about war crimes, and provided secretariat support and leadership to a growing coalition calling for a Balkan-wide victims’ commission. During the grant period, the grantee will support the coalition for a regional victims’ commission, research killed and missing persons in Kosovo, promote public awareness of war crimes through documentation and educational activities, and build the center’s organizational and programmatic capacities. The center is based in Belgrade, Serbia.

title: General Purposes
description: The overall program goal is to establish the conditions for dealing with the past in Serbia and the broader region in order to restore the rule of law and prevent future conflict. To this end, the Humanitarian Law Center researches and documents war crimes and other human rights abuses stemming from the regime of Slobodan Milosevic in Serbia and the violent conflicts in the former Yugoslavia during the 1990s. During the grant period, the grantee will continue to focus on truth-telling and truth-seeking activities, with a focus on victims and their rights and including calling for the establishment of a regional victims’ commission. The grantee will also increase its formal and informal educational activities, drawing on the extensive archive and documentation it has collected during the past 20 years. During the past two years, the grantee completed the process of documenting the names of more than 13,000 killed and missing persons in Kosovo and published and promoted a book containing data on human losses in Kosovo in 1998. The grantee also led an initiative that gathered more than 500,000 signatures throughout the former Yugoslavia in support of a regional victims’ commission. The grantee is based in Belgrade, Serbia.

title: General Purposes
description: The overall program goal is to establish the conditions for dealing with the past in Serbia and the broader region in order to restore the rule of law and prevent future conflict. To this end, the Belgrade-based Humanitarian Law Center researches and documents war crimes and other human rights abuses stemming from the regime of Slobodan Milosevic in Serbia and the conflicts in the former Yugoslavia during the 1990s. During the grant period, the grantee will finalize its work on creating a comprehensive register of human losses in the former Yugoslavia and strengthen its advocacy and educational programming. The grantee will use its extensive archive and documentation to develop advocacy and educational programming that will help to create a culture of democratic values and inclusion in Serbia and other countries of the Balkan region. During the past two years, the grantee continued its research on persons killed or missing in Kosovo, advocated for the establishment of a regional victims commission, assisted more than 200 victims to pursue reparations cases in Serbia, and organized three summer schools on transitional justice for more than 75 young people from across the Balkans.

title: General Purposes
description: The overall program goal is to establish the conditions for dealing with the past in Serbia and the broader region in order to restore the rule of law and prevent future conflict. The Belgrade-based Humanitarian Law Center researches and documents war crimes and other human rights abuses stemming from the regime of Slobodan Milosevic in Serbia and the conflicts in the former Yugoslavia during the 1990s. Using its research and documentation, the grantee informs the public about war crimes and the role of perpetrators; supports institutional reform; encourages community- and societal-level efforts of victims to tell their stories; and educates young people about the importance of truth, justice, and accountability. During 2017–2019, the grantee will also launch a campaign to establish a public documentation center in Belgrade that allows greater public access to its archive and database. During the past two years, the grantee significantly increased the number of documents in its archive, completed documentation of 13,568 victims of the war in Kosovo, supported efforts to establish a regional victims’ commission, and organized summer schools on transitional justice.

title: General Purposes
description: The United Way of Genesee County, celebrating its 90-year anniversary, supports a network of local nonprofit human service and health organizations. This general purpose renewal grant will enable it to continue funding community programs that serve the needs of over 35,000 area residents. The grantee focuses its funding priorities on basic needs/strengthening families, child/youth development, and older adults. It also administers several projects including the BEST capacity building project, participates in numerous collaboratives, and serves as fiscal sponsor for several area programs.

title: General Purposes
description: United Way of Genesee County supports a network of local nonprofit human service organizations. This general purpose renewal grant will enable it to continue funding community programs that serve the needs of over 35,000 area residents. The United Way of Genesee County is transitioning to align with the national funding priority areas which include education, health, and income stability. Additionally, it will fund programs in the area of basic needs. The grantee also administers several projects (including the BEST capacity building project), participates in numerous collaboratives, and serves as fiscal sponsor for several area programs.

title: General Purposes
description: The United Way of Genesee County is a health and human services organization providing critical funding to various organizations in four core support areas: education, health, financial stability, and basic needs. This general purpose renewal grant will enable the grantee to continue funding community programs that serve the needs of over 40,000 area residents. The United Way of Genesee County provides nonprofit sector capacity support through fiduciary services, grants that support human services sector systems, and the BEST Project.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support and capacity building to the United Way of Genesee County, a health and human services organization serving the residents of Genesee County through four community impact focus areas: education, health, financial stability, and basic needs. In 2014, the board of directors adopted a three-year strategic plan focused on addressing governance, community impact, fund development, and internal capacity. Over the next year, the grantee will continue working on implementation of the strategic plan while serving the local nonprofit sector with a focus on community impact.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant increase will provide the United Way of Genesee County with enhanced capacity to address the needs of citizens in the city of Flint experiencing high levels of lead in the city’s drinking water supply. The United Way of Genesee County will work with community partners to provide lead-eliminating water filters to city of Flint residents receiving water from the Flint River, with priority given to the most at-risk populations.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to the United Way of Genesee County, a health and human services organization serving the residents of Genesee County through four community impact focus areas: education, health, financial stability, and basic needs. In addition to the core support areas, the United Way of Genesee County provides nonprofit sector capacity support through aligned fiduciary services and the Building Excellence, Sustainability, and Trust Project. Since October 2015, the grantee has raised more than $3 million in funds for the Flint water crisis.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to the United Way of Genesee County, a health and human services organization serving the residents of Genesee County through four community impact focus areas: education, health, financial stability, and basic needs. In addition to the core support areas, the grantee provides nonprofit sector capacity support through aligned fiduciary services and the Building Excellence, Sustainability and Trust Project. Since September 2015, the grantee has raised more than $3.7 million in funds for the Flint water crisis and continues to be a key partner agency working toward recovery.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to the United Way of Genesee County, a health and human services organization serving the residents of Genesee County through four community impact focus areas: education, health, financial stability, and basic needs. In addition to the core support areas, the grantee provides nonprofit sector capacity support through aligned fiduciary services and specific capacity building activities. Since September 2015 the grantee has raised more than $4.6 million in funds for the Flint water crisis and continues to be a key partner agency working toward recovery.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to the United Way of Genesee County, a health and human services organization serving the residents of Genesee County through four community impact focus areas: education, health, financial stability, and basic needs. In addition to the core support areas, the grantee provides nonprofit sector capacity support through aligned fiduciary services and specific capacity building activities. Since September 2015, the grantee has raised more than $4.6 million in funds for the Flint water crisis and continues to be a key partner agency working toward recovery.

title: RuralNet Development
description: This grant will support the efforts of the Center for Rural Assistance to strengthen a network of Romanian community development organizations; publish a white paper on the status of rural development in Romania; participate in rural policy development; and monitor the implementation of government rural development programs. In addition, the center will develop and promote professional standards for community development workers.Recent accomplishments include strengthening Romanian community development organizations; promoting community development vis-à-vis donors and decisionmakers; and cooperating with other relevant networks active at the national and international levels.The center was established in 2000 to support the development of rural communities in Romania by increasing their capacity to manage resources to address local needs. In 2002, the center initiated RuralNet – an informal network of non-governmental organizations (NGOs) active in the field of rural and community development – to strengthen learning and exchange of best practices among these NGOs and to influence development policies and practices in Romania. Currently, there are 24 NGOs participating in the network.

title: General Purposes
grantee: National Association of Regional Development Agencies
description: This grant will enable the National Association of Regional Development Agencies to promote modern, sustainable community and regional development policies by building the capacities of its member organizations; strengthening the network of regional and local development agencies in the Ukraine; and advocating for policy improvements at the national, regional and local levels. Planned activities over the next three years include organizing training workshops and policy feedback meetings, commissioning and publishing research papers, conducting annual forums for members, maintaining an Internet portal, and arranging study tours for members both within Ukraine and abroad.The mission of the association is to contribute to the development of civil society in Ukraine by establishing long-lasting institutional mechanisms aimed at further advancement of key European principles such as partnership and decentralization.

title: Addressing the Dropout Crisis in Our Cities
geographic_focus: Portland, New York, Boston, San Jose, Philadelphia
description: This grant will enable five cities – Boston, New York, Philadelphia, Portland, Oregon, and San Jose, California – to implement strategies and action plans to improve the educational options and outcomes of out-of-school and underserved youth. The strategies and action plans will draw on activities completed during the initial 18 months of the multi-phase initiative. In addition, this grant also will provide support for two additional sites – Las Vegas and Washington, D.C. – that have shadowed the work of the original five sites and assist them in developing a strategic plan and timeline to improve supports and options for out-of-school youth in their communities.In late 2004, in partnership with the Youth Transition Funders Group, the Coalition of Community Foundations for Youth funded efforts in the five cities to develop strategies to reconnect dropouts and near dropouts with quality learning opportunities, develop data systems to guide and assess such strategies, and raise the visibility of the dropout crisis and its impact on out-of-school youth.

title: Race, Violence and Citizenship
grantee: Centre for the Study of Violence and Reconciliation
description: The Center for the Study of Violence and Reconciliation works in the areas of transitional justice, criminal reform, victim empowerment, and reconciliation. Mott provided support to examine whether there was a relationship between the violence plaguing South Africa and the legacy of hatred, prejudice, and exclusion left behind by the country’s violent racial past. The project further looked at the initiatives to address racial violence, the impact that these initiatives were having, and ways of preventing racially motivated conflict. Through detailed action research, it was able to gain deeper insights into these issues. It also looked at its own challenges and developed equity principles, which has seen more people of color in senior management positions. This renewal grant will provide support to build on the lessons learned, including sharing these lessons more widely and integrating them into the functioning of the organization.

title: Race, Violence and Citizenship
grantee: Centre for the Study of Violence and Reconciliation
description: The Center for the Study of Violence and Reconciliation works in the areas of transitional justice, criminal reform, victim empowerment, and reconciliation. Past efforts examined whether there is a relationship between the violence plaguing South Africa and the legacy of hatred, prejudice, and exclusion left behind by the country’s violent racial past. The center looked further at the initiatives addressing racial violence, the impact that these initiatives were having, and ways of preventing racially motivated conflict. It also developed its own equity principles, which has resulted in more people of color in senior management positions. This grant increase will provide support to expand the center’s work on issues of xenophobia and related intolerances. In response to the recent xenophobic attacks in South Africa, the center has resolved to expand its work in this area and address potential underlying causes of the violence such as social and political marginalization and issues of identity, discrimination, and exclusion.

title: Race, Violence and Citizenship
grantee: Centre for the Study of Violence and Reconciliation
description: This grant continues support to the Centre for the Study of Violence and Reconciliation to conduct action research, advocacy, and public policy programs for the prevention of community-based collective violence. Recent activities focused on investigating judgments of equity courts, analyzing racial intolerance and xenophobia in selected communities, facilitating community dialogues to ease tensions with migrant and refugee populations, and finding nonviolent ways to resolve conflicts. Future plans include analyzing collective violence due to xenophobia and service delivery protests in the Gauteng province, developing community-based pilot intervention strategies promoting nonviolent resolutions to conflict; assisting the government in developing appropriate policies to deter violent attacks; and disseminating research analyses and case studies. The Centre for the Study of Violence and Reconciliation is a South African policy and research center working on various aspects of violence and reconciliation.

title: Learning Through Practice: Building Partnerships Between Organizations of the Urban Poor and Local Authorities
description: The Community Organisation Urban Resource Centre conducts and disseminates research on the challenges faced by local government, particularly as it relates to areas of poverty in cities and informal urban settlements.This grant will enable the center to help communities living in informal settlements gain access to land and basic services; and conduct research and disseminate findings on the plight of the homeless in South African towns and cities.Notable achievements have included creating opportunities through networking for poor people to unite, organize and communicate at the local and global levels; establishing a partnership to secure and redistribute church-owned land to poor communities; strengthening a coalition of grassroots organizations that seeks partnership-based solutions to urban poverty; working with the city of Durban to enhance service delivery to informal settlements within the city; and partnering with the cities of Johannesburg and Cape Town to improve housing delivery to informal settlements.

title: Learning Through Practice: Building Partnerships Between Organizations of the Urban Poor and Local Authorities
description: The Community Organisation Urban Resource Centre provides support to networks of urban and rural poor communities to enable them to learn from one another and to use their collective power to advocate for support for community-initiated development projects, particularly housing projects, from government and other stakeholders. Previous Mott support has assisted communities living in informal settlements to access land and basic services for housing and to conduct research and disseminate findings on the plight of the homeless in South African towns and cities. This grant will enable the Community Organisation Urban Resource Centre to continue providing support to poor communities to access formal housing and basic services through engagement with government, particularly at the local level.

title: Learning Through Practice: Building Partnerships Between Organizations of the Urban Poor and Local Authorities
description: The Community Organisation Urban Resource Centre provides support to networks of urban and rural poor communities across South Africa. The centre encourages these networks to learn from one another and to use their collective power to advocate for support for community-initiated development projects, particularly housing projects, from government and other stakeholders. Past support enabled the centre to assist communities living in informal settlements to access land and basic services for housing. The centre also conducted research and disseminated findings on the plight of the homeless in South African towns and cities. This grant will support the centre to continue its work to improve the living conditions of people in informal settlements by facilitating various community-driven processes and the establishment of a network of community-based organizations that represent the needs of poor people.

title: General Purposes
description: The Community Organisation Resource Centre provides support to networks of urban and rural poor communities across South Africa. The grantee encourages these networks to learn from one another and use their collective power to advocate for support for community-initiated development projects, particularly housing projects, from government and other stakeholders. Past support enabled the grantee to improve the living conditions of people in informal settlements by facilitating various community-driven processes and to establish a network of community-based organizations that represent the needs of poor people. This grant will enable the Community Organisation Resource Centre to continue to support people-driven processes that empower community-based organizations and their leaders and encourage partnerships with local authorities. The grantee will support efforts aimed at improving living conditions in informal settlements and strengthening partnerships with relevant government entities and other civil society institutions.

title: General Purposes
description: The Community Organisation Resource Centre works to improve the quality of life for poor people living in slums across South Africa. The grantee assists communities to develop tools, knowledge, and resources that can be used to engage government on issues related to housing and settlement upgrading. As part of the South African Alliance of Shack Dwellers International, the grantee provides technical support to the alliance and facilitates access to local government structures. Past support has enabled the grantee to support networks of informal settlements to set up a finance facility to fund informal settlement upgrading projects, partner with local municipalities on informal settlement upgrading and housing projects, and develop the leadership within the network and communities to engage with local authorities. This grant will support the grantee to continue to develop the capabilities of community-based organizations and community networks, and support pro-poor and people-centered development projects that respond to the need for decent living areas.

title: General Purposes
description: The Community Organisation Resource Centre works to improve the quality of life for people living in slums across South Africa. It supports movements and networks of slum dwellers to enable them to engage government on the improvement of their living areas. The grantee provides technical support to the South African Alliance of Shack Dwellers International. Previous support has enabled the grantee to assist communities to partner with local municipalities in upgrading informal settlements, support women’s groups to build their income-generating initiatives and contribute to a savings fund, and support the grantee to engage in policy dialogues on informal settlement upgrades. This grant will enable the grantee to continue supporting networks of slum dwellers and building linkages between government and communities. The grantee will also assist communities to develop the tools, knowledge, and resources necessary to engage with government on issues related to informal settlement upgrading.

title: General Purposes
description: The Community Organisation Resource Centre works to improve the quality of life for people living in slums across South Africa. It supports movements and networks of slum dwellers to enable them to engage government on the improvement of their living areas. The grantee supports the Federation of the Urban Poor and the Informal Settlement Network. It is part of Shack Dwellers International—a network of community-based organizations of the urban poor in 32 countries and hundreds of cities and towns across Africa, Asia, and Latin America. Previous support has enabled the grantee to build strong social movements of slum dwellers, promote co-productive partnerships between the movements and municipalities, and support women’s groups to build their income-generating initiatives and contribute to a savings fund. This grant will enable the grantee to continue supporting networks of slum dwellers and building linkages between government and communities. In addition, the grantee will build knowledge and refine tools that are used by networks to engage with government on their informal settlement improvement work.

title: Training for Leaders of Nonprofit Organizations
description: Common Purpose South Africa brings leaders and opinionmakers together from the private, public and nonprofit sectors to network, exchange experiences and deliberate on the major challenges facing South Africa in its transition to a nonracial democracy. This provides leaders from the public and private sectors with an opportunity to gain a better appreciation of the role that the nonprofit sector plays and the valuable contribution that it makes to the development of the country.This grant will enable nonprofit leaders to participate in various Common Purpose South Africa programs and activities and provide funding for Common Purpose South Africa to look at expanding the program.Accomplishments during the past two years included building bridges across racial, ethnic and other divides; enhancing the ability of leaders to tackle the challenges facing them in their own field and the wider community; maximizing the use of resources through partnerships and by identifying common problems where resources can be shared; and engaging the next generation of leaders.

title: Training for Leaders of Nonprofit Organizations
description: Common Purpose South Africa operates educational programs to equip leaders and decisionmakers with the information and understanding they need to more effectively shape the future of their city or region. The grantee offers programs in Johannesburg and Cape Town designed for emerging as well as established leaders of all ages, backgrounds, and from all sectors — public, private, and nonprofit. All programs and activities share the same long-term goals: better decisionmaking in all sectors, more effective solutions to common problems, more engaged and active citizens, and ultimately, stronger communities. This grant will provide continued support to ensure the participation of leaders from the nonprofit sector in the grantee’s various programs and activities. During 2008, the grantee will explore extending programs into the Eastern Cape or KwaZulu-Natal provinces.

title: Training for Leaders of Nonprofit Organizations
description: Common Purpose South Africa promotes effective leadership in complex and multicultural situations through leadership development programs. Its programs, offered in Johannesburg and Cape Town, include the Meridian, Matrix, Navigator, and International Navigator, and offer leadership development to established and emerging leaders. These programs aim to improve decisionmaking resulting in more effective solutions to common problems and more engaged and active citizens, as well as to develop a new generation of leaders who lead beyond their authority. All the programs include participants from the public, private, and nonprofit sectors. Past support enabled the grantee to subsidize the participation of nonprofit sector leaders in its programs, who would otherwise not have been able to afford the cost of the programs. This grant renewal will support the continued participation of nonprofit sector leaders in the leadership development programs offered by the grantee.

title: Partnership in Philanthropy and Social Entrepreneurship
description: This grant will support a partnership in philanthropy and social entrepreneurship between the University of KwaZulu-Natal and the University of Bologna’s Masters in International Studies in Philanthropy program in Italy. This is a multidisciplinary master’s program, which provides post-graduate training in all aspects of philanthropy through an accredited and recognized master’s degree. A previous Mott grant to the University of Bologna to develop the partnership with the University of KwaZulu-Natal supported a fellowship for an African student to enroll in the course and a faculty member to be a guest lecturer at Bologna. Current funding will enable two students from the University of KwaZulu-Natal to enroll in the master’s program in Italy, as well as two interns from the University of Bologna to visit the University of KwaZulu-Natal. It will support tuition, travel, staff exchanges, accommodations and administration costs.

title: Partnership in Philanthropy and Social Entrepreneurship
description: This grant will provide continued support to the University of KwaZulu-Natal for a partnership in philanthropy and social entrepreneurship with the Masters in International Studies in Philanthropy program based at the University of Bologna in Italy. This is a multidisciplinary program, which provides postgraduate training in all aspects of philanthropy through an accredited and recognized master’s degree. In addition to an exchange in students between the University of KwaZulu-Natal and the University of Bologna, the institutions will expand and enhance the academic offerings to students, and joint research activities will provide additional philanthropy resources to the sector.

title: International Commission on the Balkans
grantee: German Marshall Fund of the United States
description: The goal of the International Commission on the Balkans is to develop a coherent vision for the political and economic reforms that are necessary for the Western Balkans to be peaceful, stable and prosperous, and to integrate fully with Europe and the West. This grant increase will enable the German Marshall Fund of the United States to conclude its work with three follow-up study visits to the Balkan region, a brief assessment report and a working conference in Rome with key actors from the region.

title: Coalition for New Philanthropy
description: The Coalition for New Philanthropy is a collaborative project that provides African-American, Latino and Asian-American donors with tools and information to increase the impact of their individual and collective philanthropy. In addition to the Support Center for Nonprofit Management, five organizations are partnering in this effort.This grant will enable the coalition to conduct a variety of outreach activities and educational programs, including trainings and technical assistance, launching new donor circles and fields of interest funds, completing research on employee networks, and sharing best practices and lessons learned. Training sessions and workshops will be expanded to include ethnic funds and other donor vehicles in San Francisco, Oakland and Chicago.During the past year, the coalition convened 15 events for donors and potential donors in which the needs of various ethnic communities were discussed; held two meetings for professional advisors to the donor community; provided educational outreach and technical assistance to donor circles and funds; and developed and disseminated information and reports through regional and national conferences. Through these activities, the coalition reached nearly 2,000 donors and 11 professional advisors in 2005.

title: Coalition for New Philanthropy
description: This grant provides partial support to a collaborative project that provides African-American, Latino, and Asian-American donors with new tools and information to increase the impact of their individual and collective philanthropy.
