In addition to the Support Center for Nonprofit Management, five organizations are partnering in this effort and include Asian American Federation of New York, the Center for Philanthropy and Civil Society at the Graduate Center of the City University of New York, the Hispanic Federation, the New York Regional Association of Grantmakers, and the Twenty-First Century Foundation. A variety of outreach, educational, and support activities are planned in 2007, including educating new donors; convening meetings and trainings; underwriting the creation of communications, marketing, and training tools; disseminating curriculum guides and information on lessons learned; and providing technical assistance support.

title: Community Foundation Futures
description: This grant provides continued support to research that explores emerging issues, as well as promising innovations in the community philanthropy field. The centerpiece of the project was the 2005 release of “On the Brink of New Promise: The Future of U.S. Community Foundations” report, produced by Blueprint Research & Design, Inc. Over the past two years, the report and ideas expressed in it have saturated the community foundation field through widespread distribution, public presentations, consulting engagements, an online application toolkit, and four follow-up “Future Matters” reports. This has had a profound impact on individual community foundations, as well as broad field strengthening initiatives. Over the upcoming 15-month grant period, the grantee will produce and promote four additional “Future Matters” reports and coordinate with and advise two other major community foundation development support initiatives.

title: Center for Service Learning and School Partnerships
description: The University of Michigan-Flint’s Center for Service Learning and School Partnerships works to connect faculty, staff and students with community-based projects that have a significant impact on the development of campus and community leadership, civic engagement, teacher professional development and community collaborations.This grant will enable the center to continue building a stronger relationship between the university and the Greater Flint community in which it operates.To date, the center has initiated more than 25 service-learning courses; a yearly community orientation for new faculty; and a competitive scholar program that awards honorary cords to graduating students who have volunteered more than 300 hours of community service and stipends to those who have given more than 140 hours of their time during a single semester.

title: Effective Messages for Fiscal and Tax Policy
description: This grant will enable the Communications Consortium Media Center to continue helping Mott’s State Fiscal Analysis Initiative grantees assess their communications needs, expand media contacts and explore new communications technologies, such as Web conferencing. The anticipated outcome of this project is more sophisticated and strategic communications activities among the state fiscal groups. During the pilot grant, the center helped several grantees design and begin implementing strategic communications plans that supported their policy objectives on tax and budget issues.The center, established in 1988, is dedicated to helping nonprofit organizations use media and new telecommunications technologies for public education and policy change.

title: SEED Universal Policy Initiative
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This renewal grant will provide partial support for Washington University’s research and program management activities within the Savings for Education, Entrepreneurship, and Downpayment Initiative. The initiative is a multifaceted demonstration of children’s savings accounts as a tool to increase savings and promote financial security, especially among low-income families. The initiative began in 2003 and will continue through 2008. The grantee is a key leader in the asset-building field, and is widely recognized as launching the movement with the release of the seminal book, “Assets and the Poor”.

title: SEED Universal Policy Initiative
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This renewal grant provides ongoing support to Washington University for a statewide demonstration of children’s savings accounts. Because the demonstration is being conducted within the state of Oklahoma’s existing college savings plan system, it could serve as a prototype policy for scaling up asset-building opportunities for an infinite number of families. Key goals during this grant period are to: 1) select participating families at random from state birth records and assign them to treatment and control groups; 2) coordinate and manage first-year implementation and problem-solving efforts; 3) undertake account monitoring research and reporting; and 4) develop and implement a communications plan. The grantee is a key leader in the asset-building field and is widely recognized for launching the movement with release of the seminal book, “Assets and the Poor”.

title: SEED Universal Policy Initiative
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant provides continuing support to Washington University for a statewide demonstration of children’s savings accounts. Because the demonstration is being conducted within the state of Oklahoma’s existing college savings plan system, it could serve as a prototype policy for scaling up asset-building opportunities from thousands to millions of families. Key goals for the grant period are to: 1) coordinate and manage third-year implementation efforts; 2) undertake account monitoring research and reporting activities; and 3) communicate research findings and other learnings to a broad group of stakeholders, including policymakers and the media.

title: SEED Universal Policy Initiative
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant provides continuing support to Washington University for a statewide demonstration of children’s savings accounts. Because the demonstration is being conducted within the state of Missouri’s existing college savings plan system, it could serve as a prototype policy for expanding asset-building opportunities from thousands to millions of families. Key goals for the grant period are to: 1) manage the fourth year of implementation activities; 2) undertake account monitoring research and reporting efforts; and 3) communicate research findings and other lessons to a broad group of stakeholders, including policymakers and the media.

title: SEED Universal Policy Initiative
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant provides continuing support to Washington University for a statewide demonstration of children’s savings accounts. Because the demonstration is being conducted within the state of Oklahoma’s existing college savings plan system, it could serve as a prototype policy for expanding asset-building opportunities from thousands to millions of families. Key goals for the grant period are: 1) manage year four implementation activities; 2) undertake account monitoring research and reporting efforts; and 3) communicate research findings and other lessons to a broad group of stakeholders, including policymakers and the media.

title: Expanding Child Development Accounts for Educational Success and Lifelong Asset Building
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant provides support for Washington University’s research, communications and policy development work on children’s savings account strategies at the state and national levels. In the short-term, the grantee’s goal is to increase the amounts families save for their children’s education and, in doing so, increase postsecondary education access and completion rates, particularly among low- to moderate-income students. Long-term, the grantee views children’s savings accounts as the first phase of a save and invest society, where domestic social policy includes lifelong saving opportunities and other asset-based policies that drive social protection (especially education), economic development, and financial security goals.

title: Expanding CSAs for Educational Success and Lifelong Asset Building
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant provides support for Washington University’s research, communications, and policy development work on children’s savings account strategies at the state and national levels. In the short-term, the grantee’s goal is to increase the amounts families save for their children’s education and, in doing so, increase postsecondary education access and completion rates, particularly among low- and moderate-income students. In the long term, the grantee views children’s savings accounts as the initial phase of a broader effort to embed inclusive and lifelong asset-building opportunities into the fabric of domestic social policy in ways that support educational, economic development, and financial security goals.

title: Expanding CSAs for Educational Success and Lifelong Asset Building
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant provides continuing support for Washington University’s research, communications, and policy development efforts to advance children’s savings account strategies at the state and national levels. In the short term, the grantee’s goal is to expand opportunities for all families to save for their children’s education, and in doing so, increase postsecondary education aspirations, access, and completion rates, particularly among low- to moderate-income students. Long term, the grantee views children’s savings accounts as the initial phase of a broader effort to embed inclusive and lifelong asset-building opportunities into the fabric of domestic social policy in ways that support educational, economic development, and financial security goals.

title: Asset Policy Initiative of California
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: The Asset Policy Initiative of California was established in 2003 to create lifelong asset-building opportunities for every Californian. During the previous grant period, the grantee helped enact California’s split tax refund legislation, which will enable taxpayers to direct their refunds into multiple accounts — an important step in helping families begin the asset-building process. During the next two years, Mott funds will support the initiative’s three core goals: elevating asset building to an actionable priority among public, private and nonprofit leaders; implementing a statewide asset-building agenda for California; and developing, testing and promoting products and services that provide California’s working families with opportunities to build assets. The Earned Assets Resource Network was founded in 2001 to provide working families with the tools — financial education, access to mainstream financial services, and matched savings opportunities — to build assets and create financial stability.

title: Asset Policy Initiative of California
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant will support the Earned Assets Resource Network’s efforts to promote the development and sustainability of state and federal programs and policies that expand asset-building incentives and opportunities for low- and moderate-income families. Objectives of the project include: 1) engaging new constituencies to leverage sustained support for asset-development strategies; 2) informing the public and policymakers about how assets contribute to individual, family, and community economic well-being; and 3) testing innovative policies that bring asset-building opportunities to broad segments of the public. The grantee is a San Francisco-based nonprofit dedicated to helping low-wage workers break the cycle of poverty and create new cycles of prosperity. This is one of eight grants aimed at building the capacity of state asset-building coalitions to effectively promote the development of state asset policies.

title: General Purposes
description: Multiyear funding will enable the Organization for Civil Initiatives (OCI) to work with local community leaders and grassroots citizen groups in Croatia to build capacity for identifying community needs and implementing long-term and lasting solutions. In addition, the center provides information, training and consultations to local government authorities and a wide range of non-governmental organizations on community organizing, cross-sector cooperation, local resource development and rural economic development.During the past two years, OCI worked directly with local NGOs and community leaders in seven counties in eastern and southern Croatia. OCI provided training for community organizers in 26 local communities and provided direct, follow-up assistance to many of these communities; participated in the distribution of approximately $300,000 to 42 community projects and provided technical assistance to 150 NGOs in association with the Academy of Educational Development; and worked with local governments to strengthen town councils and village boards.OCI, created in 1992, is part of a network of community development organizations in Croatia and Central and Eastern Europe.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant supports activities to promote greater public participation in decisionmaking and to mobilize community resources to address critical issues facing local communities in Croatia. The Organization for Civil Initiatives works with local community leaders and grassroots citizen groups to build capacity to identify community needs and implement long-term solutions. In addition, the grantee provides information, training, and consultations to local government authorities and nongovernmental organizations on community organizing, cross-sector cooperation, local resource development, and rural economic development. Over the last two years, the grantee worked directly with local governments, nongovernmental organizations, and community leaders in seven counties in eastern and southern Croatia on a wide range of activities, including establishing forums of civic initiatives, strengthening a new community foundation, building the capacity of village boards, and providing training on community organizing. The grantee is based in Osijek, Croatia, and works primarily in eastern and southern Croatia.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant supports activities to promote greater public participation in decisionmaking and to mobilize community resources to address critical issues facing local communities in Croatia. The Organization for Civil Initiatives will work with local community leaders and grassroots citizen groups to build capacity to identify community needs and implement long-term and lasting solutions. Working primarily in rural communities, the grantee will provide information, training, and consultations to local government authorities and nongovernmental organizations on community organizing, cross-sector cooperation, local resource development, and rural economic development. During 2008-2009, the grantee expanded its involvement in cross-sector partnerships designed to improve the implementation of its objectives and activities. The grantee diversified its funding base, including establishing an accounting service for other nonprofits and local businesses. The grantee was an active participant in various nonprofit forums and supported the development of a new community foundation in Osijek. The grantee is based in Osijek, Croatia, and works primarily in eastern and southern Croatia.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant supports activities to promote greater public participation in decisionmaking and to mobilize community resources to address critical issues facing local communities in Croatia. The Organization for Civil Initiatives will work with local community leaders and grassroots citizen groups to build capacity to identify community needs and implement long-term and lasting solutions. Working primarily in rural communities, the grantee will provide information, training, and consultations to local government authorities and nongovernmental organizations on community organizing, cross-sector cooperation, local resource development, and rural economic development. During 2010-2011, the grantee implemented three European Union-funded projects related to rural economic development, organized a wide range of programs designed to increase civic participation in communities, and supported the development of social entrepreneurship among local nonprofits. The grantee also focused on increasing staff capacity to design and implement European Union-funded projects. The grantee was an active participant in various nonprofit forums and supported the development of a new community foundation in Osijek. The grantee is based in Osijek, Croatia, and works primarily in eastern and southern Croatia.

title: Strengthening Capacities for Regional Civil Society Development in Croatia
grantee: National Foundation for Civil Society Development
description: This grant will enable the National Foundation for Civil Society Development to devise appropriate strategies and strengthen its capacity for working at local and regional levels in Croatia. During the grant period, the organization will strengthen its partnerships with regional nonprofit sector infrastructure organizations, including local grantmaking organizations, through targeted grant support, coordination of related activities and initiatives, networking opportunities, and training and information programs.During the past year and a half, the organization maintained regional coordinators in four offices across Croatia. These coordinators organized strategic planning meetings and focus groups in each region for the purpose of developing the foundation’s approaches to building nonprofit sector infrastructure and resourcing local civic initiatives through its grantmaking. Based in Zagreb, the organization is an independent grantmaking foundation supported with state lottery funds.

title: Timok Regional Development Center
description: The Timok region is located in the eastern part of Serbia.Through the Timok Regional Development Center, the Timok Club promotes sustainable social and economic development and improves the lives of people living in the region. This grant will enable the center to encourage community decisionmaking and strengthen cooperation among local government, businesses, non-governmental organizations and the media. In addition, the organization will work to link the eastern part of Serbia with national-level development initiatives, as well as regional Western Balkan networks and programs.

title: Quaker Peace and Social Witness: Dealing with the Past in Bosnia, Croatia, and Serbia and Montenegro
grantee: Religious Society of Friends in Britain (Quakers)
geographic_focus: Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, Croatia
description: The goal of the project is to support efforts in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, and Serbia and Montenegro to deal with issues of truth, responsibility and accountability with respect to the wars and violent conflicts in the region during the 1990s. Multiyear funding will enable the Religious Society of Friends in Britain (Quakers) to identify and support unofficial truth and reconciliation processes where they are happening; develop them where they are not; and provide links between people and organizations engaged in these processes for their mutual sustainability.Recent accomplishments included helping grassroots groups in rural Bosnia and Herzegovina to address past issues in their communities; providing training to Croatian war veterans; and organizing retreats and seminars for youth in Serbia and Montenegro.

title: Crafting Michigan's Water Management Program
grantee: Tip of the Mitt Watershed Council
description: Tip of the Mitt Watershed Council works with partner groups to promote comprehensive water management policy reform in Michigan. Recently, the council participated in educational efforts that helped lay the groundwork for a new state law addressing many key water policy issues. This grant increase, and associated grant period extension, will enable the council to complete policy analysis and public communication materials on a range of water management topics still facing the state, including ratification of the Great Lakes Compact.

title: Supporting Afterschool Evaluation and Research
description: This grant will enable the Harvard Family Research Project at Harvard University to continue to compile, disseminate and generate high quality online research and evaluation resources; create and disseminate research-based publications for researchers, practitioners and policymakers; and provide evaluation-related technical assistance to national, state and local afterschool stakeholders. Through these efforts, the project will contribute to the afterschool research community and support the translation of this knowledge into practice and policy.During the past two years, the project developed a national database of evaluations of afterschool programs, with 162 profiles posted; published four issues of the Evaluation Exchange periodical on afterschool programs; created two sets of publications targeted to both researchers/evaluators and practitioners, offering theoretical substance and practical advice on how to improve evaluation practice and program quality; organized two symposia on critical afterschool issues; participated on national advisory boards; and provided technical assistance to support members of the National Network of Statewide Afterschool Networks.

title: Supporting New Day for Learning Evaluation and Research
description: This grant will provide continued support to the Harvard Family Research Project at Harvard University in its efforts to build and support connections in afterschool research, practices, and policies. The Harvard Family Research Project will: 1) continue to maintain the only national database of afterschool research studies and evaluations and expand it to include efforts to promote “A New Day for Learning”; 2) use publications and research briefs to inform afterschool stakeholders of the latest research and evaluation information; 3) explore new ways to engage policymakers and practitioners using social media platforms; 4) expand technical assistance through the use of Web-based tutorials aimed at improving professional development; 5) continue participation in the ongoing national dialogue about afterschool in order to identify key issues and strengthen the conversation between researchers, policymakers, and practitioners; and 6) convene a virtual community of evaluators to discuss how to evaluate the complex efforts to integrate school, afterschool, summer, and community services and share lessons learned.

title: Supporting New Day for Learning Evaluation and Research
description: This grant will provide continued support to the Harvard Family Research Project at Harvard University in its efforts to build and support afterschool research, practices, and policies. Specifically, the Supporting New Day for Learning Evaluation and Research will: 1) continue to maintain the only national database of afterschool research studies and evaluations; 2) continue to develop research briefs and synthesize others with the purpose of getting and using information for program, systems, and policy improvements; and 3) identify more effective ways of disseminating research to an audience that includes policymakers and practitioners. Harvard Family Research Project’s intent is to ensure that all children and youth have equal access to a set of integrated school, afterschool, summer learning, and other supports to create the new and diverse learning opportunities that youth need to graduate from high school with the broad knowledge and skills necessary for success in the 21st century’s global economy and community.

title: Supporting Expanded Learning and Afterschool Research
description: This grant will provide continued support to the Harvard Family Research Project at Harvard University in its efforts to build and support afterschool and expanded learning research, practices, and policies. Specifically, this project will: 1) continue to develop research briefs for program, systems, and policy improvements; 2) document and share new and effective approaches by schools and afterschool programs to expand learning opportunities; and 3) provide technical assistance as part of the Supporting Expanded Learning and Afterschool Research Project. Through this initiative, the grantee will continue to provide the field with credible and current information through effective communication strategies such as video, podcasts, and Webinars; and support the development of effective afterschool and expanded learning approaches.

title: Building a Comprehensive National After-School Initiative
description: This grant will enable the After-School All-Stars to continue efforts to implement comprehensive afterschool programming for its 15 city affiliates. Program components, projects, activities, and processes to engage children and produce learning will be examined and shared across sites. By developing and refining these program components, the After-School All-Stars will be better positioned to establish quality in its network of sites and share projects, practices and activities.The After-School All-Stars is committed to strategic planning, and will focus on building quality and sustainability across its affiliate sites and strengthening the core organization.

title: Funding Strategies for Statewide Afterschool Networks
description: This grant will enable the Finance Project to continue its efforts to expand the capacity of the afterschool field in developing and sustaining quality programs. This will primarily be done by developing tools and technical assistance resources to facilitate improved sustainability and financing at the state and local levels. Specifically, the project will provide technical assistance to the statewide afterschool networks around finance, sustainability, governance, strategy development and implementation; offer targeted technical assistance to individual state networks focused on their unique sustainability efforts; and support the development of the afterschool field by convening stakeholders and disseminating best practices.The Finance Project is a part of the Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative, a consortium of national organizations working to support the statewide afterschool networks.

title: Funding Strategies for Statewide Afterschool Networks
description: The Finance Project will continue to expand the capacity of the afterschool field to develop and sustain quality programs by: 1) providing technical assistance to individual, statewide afterschool networks on issues related to finance, sustainability, and the implementation of network strategies; 2) delivering targeted technical assistance to the collective group of statewide afterschool networks through meetings and teleconferences as a part of the Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative; and 3) developing tools and technical assistance resources to support local- and state-level initiatives, facilitate improved sustainability, and increase understanding of strategies for financing professional development for the afterschool workforce.

title: Funding Strategies for Statewide Afterschool Networks
description: The Finance Project will continue to expand the capability of the afterschool field to develop and sustain quality programs by: 1) providing targeted technical assistance to individual statewide afterschool networks on issues related to finance, sustainability, and the implementation of network strategies; 2) delivering technical assistance to the collective group of statewide afterschool networks through meetings and teleconferences as part of the Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative; and 3) building the afterschool field by utilizing Web-based capacity to share knowledge and technical assistance resources broadly.

title: Funding Strategies for Statewide Afterschool Networks
description: This grant increase will support the Finance Project to expand their technical assistance work with the statewide afterschool networks. Specifically, the Finance Project will: 1) conduct a scan and analysis of the financial health of the networks; 2) provide rapid response and increased technical assistance to designated networks; and 3) deliver customized and intensive support to certain statewide afterschool networks. The overall goal of this technical assistance is to ensure that the statewide afterschool networks continue to operate as highly effective and efficient collaborative initiatives during difficult fiscal times.

title: Funding Strategies for Statewide Afterschool Networks
description: The Finance Project will continue to support state efforts to expand and strengthen afterschool programs by: 1) building the capacity of the statewide afterschool networks on issues related to finance and sustainability; 2) providing coaching and consultation to the networks to explore improved models of operation; 3) researching and developing materials, tools, and resources to support the networks; and 4) continuing to serve as part of the Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative.

title: Maximizing Gubernatorial Support for Extra Learning Opportunities
grantee: National Governors Association Center for Best Practices
description: This grant will enable the National Governors Association Center for Best Practices to continue assisting governors and their policy advisors to address education and other policy challenges through afterschool activities. Project goals include providing assistance and grants to states to hold governors’ summits to advance state afterschool policies; supplying targeted technical assistance to governors’ offices; publishing two issue briefs on how afterschool programs can support state initiatives; supporting redevelopment of a Web site to provide information on afterschool policy solutions and research; and continuing to provide support to the statewide afterschool networks through the Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative, a group of national organizations working to support the development of statewide networks through technical assistance. The center will also co-implement a project with the Council of Chief State School Officers and the National Conference of State Legislatures to provide intensive technical assistance on furthering afterschool policies with state leadership teams comprised of state legislators, education chiefs, governors’ policy advisors and statewide afterschool network leaders.

title: Gubernatorial Leadership to Transform the Learning Day and Year
grantee: National Governors Association Center for Best Practices
description: This grant will continue support to the National Governors Association Center for Best Practices in its efforts to help governors and their key education advisors support student success by transforming the learning day and year. The grantee will: 1) continue the Supporting Student Success initiative; 2) convene two expert roundtables on time and learning; 3) publish two issue briefs based on information and ideas from the roundtables; 4) sponsor two knowledge-building opportunities for governors’ offices; 5) provide targeted technical assistance to governors’ offices; 6) establish a time and learning Web site; and 7) continue as an Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative for the statewide afterschool networks. The center will also work with the Council of Chief State School Officers and the National Conference of State Legislatures to commission a report detailing policy changes and lessons learned from the first round of Supporting Student Success initiative states.

title: Gubernatorial Leadership to Transform the Learning Day and Year
grantee: National Governors Association Center for Best Practices
description: This grant will continue to support the National Governors Association Center for Best Practices in its efforts to help governors and their key education advisors advance student success by supporting afterschool and expanded learning opportunities. Specifically, this grant will enable the grantee to: 1) further develop competency-based education systems that benefit students in afterschool and expanded learning programs; and 2) continue to support the statewide afterschool networks as a member of the Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative.

title: Making Afterschool a City Priority
description: This grant will enable the Institute for Youth, Education, and Families of the National League of Cities to engage more mayors, council members and other municipal officials in building citywide afterschool systems by taking advantage of promising practices and lessons learned. Specific project goals include providing intensive technical assistance to the existing and new cities; enhancing, strengthening and expanding the Afterschool Policy Advisors Network of municipal leaders; and convening a second National City Afterschool Summit to bring together municipal leaders across the nation. The institute also will provide support to the Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative by connecting municipal leaders to the statewide afterschool networks.Founded in 1924, the National League of Cities is the membership organization of municipal governments and state municipal leagues in the U.S. Members include more than 17,000 municipalities, which constitute 88 percent of all municipalities in the U.S.

title: City Leaders Engaged in Afterschool Reform and a New Day for Learning
description: This grant will provide continued support to the National League of Cities Institute to engage city leaders in afterschool initiatives. The City Leaders Engaged in Afterschool Reform and A New Day for Learning initiative will: 1) provide technical assistance to cities with the development of citywide afterschool systems; 2) host state or regional summits to expand and deepen partnerships between municipal leaders and statewide afterschool networks; 3) convene a third National City Afterschool Summit with a possible focus on how city/business partnerships are critical for addressing afterschool needs; 4) collect and disseminate promising practices that raise the visibility of older youth’s afterschool needs and programs; 5) document municipal afterschool investment in selected cities; and 6) continue to raise awareness about city roles in expanding afterschool opportunities.

title: City Leaders Engaged in Afterschool Reform and a New Day for Learning
description: This grant will provide continued support to the National League of Cities Institute to engage city leaders in afterschool initiatives. Specifically, this project will: 1) support the statewide afterschool networks and their efforts to engage municipal leaders; 2) provide ongoing technical assistance to selected cities seeking to strengthen key elements of their citywide afterschool systems; and 3) raise awareness among municipal leaders of promising practices and city roles in building high quality expanded learning systems.

title: City Leaders Engaged in Afterschool Reform and a New Day for Learning
description: This grant will support the National League of Cities Institute to engage city officials in afterschool initiatives and highlight the importance of continuing investments in afterschool at the federal, state, and local levels. Specifically, this project will: 1) support statewide afterschool networks in their efforts to engage municipal leaders; 2) develop a research and communications initiative highlighting mayoral voices to feature the importance of afterschool programs at the local level and 21st Century Community Learning Centers funding at the federal level; and 3) continue to raise awareness among municipal leaders of promising practices and city roles in building high quality afterschool and expanded learning systems.

title: City Leaders Engaged in Afterschool Reform and a New Day for Learning
description: This grant will support the National League of Cities Institute to engage city officials in afterschool and summer learning initiatives and highlight the importance of continuing support for afterschool programs at the federal, state, and local levels. Specifically, this project will: 1) support statewide afterschool networks in their efforts to engage municipal leaders; 2) expand its research and communications initiatives highlighting mayoral voices that bring attention to the importance of afterschool programs; and 3) continue to raise awareness among municipal leaders of promising practices and city roles in building high quality afterschool and summer learning systems.

title: City Leaders Engaged in Afterschool Reform and a New Day for Learning
description: This grant increase will support the National League of Cities Institute in its work to expand the involvement of municipal leaders in statewide afterschool networks and local afterschool and summer learning efforts. Specifically, the grantee will help statewide afterschool networks host statewide mayoral summits on afterschool and summer learning.

title: City Leaders Engaged in Afterschool Reform and a New Day for Learning
description: This grant will support the National League of Cities Institute to engage city officials in afterschool and summer learning initiatives and highlight the importance of continuing support for afterschool programs at the federal, state, and local levels. Specifically, this project will: 1) support statewide afterschool networks in their efforts to engage municipal leaders; 2) expand the National League of Cities Institute’s communications initiatives to connect afterschool programs with the top priorities in cities; 3) continue to raise awareness among municipal leaders of promising practices and city roles in building high quality afterschool and summer learning systems; and 4) elevate and support municipal leaders for city-led community schools’ initiatives as a strategy to increase access to and investments in afterschool.

title: City Leaders Engaged in Afterschool Reform
description: This grant will support the National League of Cities Institute to engage city officials in developing high-quality afterschool and summer learning initiatives at the federal, state, and local levels. Specifically, this project will: 1) support statewide afterschool networks in their efforts to engage municipal leaders; 2) expand the grantee’s communications initiatives to connect afterschool programs with the top priorities in cities; and 3) continue to raise awareness among municipal leaders in building high-quality afterschool and summer learning systems.

title: Expand Business Sector Support for Afterschool
description: This grant will continue to support Corporate Voices for Working Families in its efforts to expand the support of the business sector for afterschool programs and policies. Specifically, the project will: 1) continue to educate the business community about the importance of afterschool; 2) convene a business summit for corporate executive officers and key afterschool stakeholders; 3) communicate values embedded in the Mott-funded report, “A New Day for Learning” and the link to workforce development; 4) produce a series of communication materials; and 5) conduct a communication outreach campaign.

title: Increase Awareness Among State Legislatures, Law Enforcement, and Business
description: Fight Crime: Invest in Kids is a national, bipartisan child advocacy organization made up of more than 1,500 police chiefs, sheriffs, district attorneys and victims of violence.This grant will enable the organization to continue educating the public and policymakers about the importance of increasing investments in high quality afterschool programs, especially for low-income, disadvantaged youth. Activities will include producing and disseminating reports for policymakers, the media and other interested parties; expanding membership and strengthening capacity by recruiting new law enforcement leaders and crime survivors; generating media coverage and increasing public awareness of research findings; educating federal and state policymakers and opinion leaders about the benefits of afterschool investments; and collaborating with national, state and local advocacy organizations on behalf of afterschool. In addition, the organization will pay particular attention to educating California policymakers on the implementation of Proposition 49, which has generated $430 million in new state afterschool funding.

title: Just Consulting Initiative
description: The Movement Strategy Center’s Just Consulting Initiative is a network of consultants who share a commitment to create organizational development practices, frameworks and tools to support social justice organizations and who have created a training curriculum around these principles. These tools have the potential to broadly impact the organizational development field and bridge organizational development and racial justice work in a new way.This grant will enable the center to test and refine the curriculum; disseminate the principles and the curriculum broadly and through popular venues; and present the work at various trainings and conferences.The center, founded in 2001, is a national intermediary that engages youth and adults across issues and regions. It encourages collaboration and joint strategizing to develop more effective movements for democracy, equity and social change.

title: Capacity Building: Building the Donor Base
description: The Asian American Justice Center has emerged as a key leader, not only within the Asian Pacific American community, but also in the broader civil rights and social justice community. To become truly self-sustaining, however, it is imperative that the center strengthen its efforts to develop donors.This grant will enable the center to further develop a major donor initiative and a direct mail campaign in order to increase support for its work. Specific activities will include developing a comprehensive fundraising strategy; formally engaging the members of its National Advisory Council (NAC) to lend expertise and assistance to fundraising activities and campaigns and to use fundraising experience as an additional filter in the selection of new NAC members; marketing and promoting the major donor program, the President’s Circle, whose members have given a minimum of $1,000; launching a challenge grant program as a tool for encouraging individual contributions; and creating a Law Partners Advisory Council to increase both in-kind and cash contributions from attorneys and law firms.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to consolidate and strengthen the philanthropic community in Bulgaria. During the grant period, the Bulgarian Donors’ Forum will increase its membership, develop its services for member and nonmember organizations, cooperate with similar organizations in Central and Eastern Europe on efforts to develop philanthropy, and strengthen its organizational capacity and financial sustainability. The forum was established in 2004 with the mission to promote the development of civil society and philanthropy in Bulgaria. The forum’s past achievements include increasing its membership substantially in a short period of time, providing high quality services to its members and other clients, pioneering new giving mechanisms, and actively participating in international initiatives of donor associations in Europe and globally.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to consolidate and strengthen the philanthropic community in Bulgaria. During the grant period, the Bulgarian Donors’ Forum will increase its membership, develop its services for member and nonmember organizations, cooperate with similar organizations in Central and Eastern Europe on efforts to develop philanthropy, and strengthen its organizational capacity and financial sustainability. The forum was established in 2004 with the mission to promote the development of civil society and philanthropy in Bulgaria. During 2007-2010, the forum’s achievements included increasing its membership, providing high quality services to its members and other clients, pioneering new giving mechanisms, and participating actively in international initiatives of donor associations in Europe and globally.

title: General Purposes
description: The purpose of this grant increase is to enable a key philanthropy support organization in Bulgaria, the Bulgarian Donors’ Forum, to take advantage of new opportunities to strengthen its organizational capacity. More specifically, the grantee will strengthen its senior staff skills for creative strategic planning, develop second-tier leadership within its program staff, and document and analyze its experience in philanthropy development in Bulgaria and Eastern Europe. The grantee was established in 2004 with the mission to promote and develop civil society and philanthropy in Bulgaria. Over the years, the grantee increased its membership substantially, provided high quality services to its members and other clients, pioneered new giving mechanisms, and participated actively in international initiatives of donor associations in Europe and globally.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to consolidate and strengthen the philanthropic community in Bulgaria. During the grant period, the Bulgarian Donors’ Forum will increase its membership, develop its services for member and nonmember organizations, advocate for improvements in the environment for philanthropy in Bulgaria, cooperate with similar organizations in Europe and globally on efforts to develop philanthropy, and strengthen its organizational capacity and financial sustainability. The grantee was established in 2004 with the mission to promote the development of civil society and philanthropy in Bulgaria. During 2010-2013, the grantee’s achievements included attracting new members, providing high quality services to its members and other clients, pioneering new giving mechanisms, and publishing influential research and analyses on a wide range of philanthropy-related subjects.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to consolidate and strengthen the philanthropic community in Bulgaria. During the grant period, the Bulgarian Donors’ Forum will advocate for improvements in the operating environment for philanthropy in Bulgaria, increase the level and quality of philanthropic giving, cooperate with similar organizations in Europe and globally on efforts to develop philanthropy, develop its services for member and nonmember organizations, and strengthen its organizational capacity and financial sustainability. The grantee was established in 2004 with the mission to promote the development of civil society and philanthropy in Bulgaria. During the past grant period, the grantee advocated for a more enabling environment for philanthropy and civil society development on the national and European Union levels, promoted ethical standards and good practice in philanthropy, increased the level of individual and corporate donations to charitable causes, and facilitated the establishment of two private foundations by wealthy individuals. The grantee is based in Sofia, Bulgaria.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen civil society participation in environmental decisionmaking in the Czech Republic. During the grant period, Green Circle will improve the communication and interaction among environmental nongovernmental organizations, strengthen the cooperation between the environmental movement and other civil society subsectors, raise public awareness on sustainable development issues, and strengthen public participation in environmental decisionmaking. Green Circle is a membership organization with 27 formal and 70 informal members, including many of the most important environmental nongovernmental organizations in the Czech Republic. The grantee provides a wide variety of services to its members, including information, technical assistance, legal advice, networking opportunities, discussion platforms, and administrative services.

title: General Purposes
grantee: GURT Resource Center for NGO Development
description: Established in 1995, the GURT Resource Center for NGO Development is a leading information and support center for Ukrainian non-governmental organizations. It provides technical assistance, training, consultation, publications and a range of information services to help strengthen the Ukrainian nonprofit sector. The center also encourages nonprofit partnerships among local government and business and focuses on introducing young Ukrainians to the philanthropic field and the important role citizens and civil society play in the development of their country. This grant increase will enable the center to update and market its Web portal and undertake a thorough strategic planning process which will lead to improved governance and management.

title: General Purposes
grantee: GURT Resource Center for NGO Development
description: The program goal is to support social transformation in Ukraine through development of a strong, diverse, and vibrant civil society. The GURT Resource Center for NGO Development will provide technical assistance, training, consultation, publications, and a range of information services to help strengthen nongovernmental organizations throughout Ukraine. It will work to foster effective partnerships between civil society organizations and local governments. It will promote a number of innovative practices in the mapping of social services and in the establishment and organization of self-help groups. The grant will build on the center’s successful efforts of promoting its information and knowledge resources which have seen readership of its core news bulletin increase by over 30 percent. In the previous grant period the center conducted organizational development activities for over 5,000 participants. Established in 1995, the center is one of the leading sources for social information and expertise in Ukraine.

title: General Purposes
grantee: GURT Resource Center for NGO Development
description: The program goal is to support social transformation in Ukraine through development of a strong and vibrant civil society. The GURT Resource Center for NGO Development will provide a range of technical assistance, training, and information services to help strengthen nongovernmental organizations throughout Ukraine. Work will focus on enhancing the interactivity and learning functions of its Internet portal. The grantee will also work to foster increasingly productive partnerships between civil society organizations and local governments, while continuing efforts to introduce standards and measures of organizational effectiveness. The grant builds on the grantee’s successful efforts at promoting its information resources, which have seen use of its increasingly sophisticated Internet portal triple in three years. In 2008-2010, the grantee conducted over 200 organizational development, training, and networking activities for beneficiaries throughout Ukraine. Established in 1995, the GURT Resource Center for NGO Development is one of the leading sources of social information and expertise in Ukraine.

title: General Purposes
grantee: GURT Resource Center for NGO Development
description: The program goal is to support social change in Ukraine through the development of a strong and vibrant civil society. Through training and direct project implementation, the GURT Resource Center for NGO Development will aim to further disseminate participatory approaches to community development and decisionmaking across Ukraine. Additionally, the grantee will continue to strengthen its information provision by enhancing the interactivity and learning functions of its Internet portal. The grant builds on the grantee’s successful efforts at strengthening its role as a key provider of information on social development, which have seen the use of its increasingly sophisticated Internet portal more than double in the period 2011-2013. The grantee also successfully introduced participatory planning approaches to ten communities, resulting in the establishment of community development plans with broad-based support. Established in 1995, the GURT Resource Center for NGO Development is one of the leading sources of information and expertise for civil society in Ukraine.

title: Analysis of Expenses and Compensation in Large and Mid-Size Foundations
description: Building upon prior research that examined administrative expenses and compensation practices of the 10,000 largest U.S. foundations, this grant will enable the Foundation Center to more fully analyze spending patterns during the years 2001-2003. Staff will analyze how operating characteristics influence the expenses of independent, corporate and community foundations. The research effort will tap data and expertise of the Foundation Center, Urban Institute’s Center on Nonprofits and Philanthropy, and GuideStar. Research findings will be published and broadly disseminated to those with interest in the foundation field.The Foundation Center, established in 1956, is dedicated to fostering public understanding of the foundation field by collecting, organizing, analyzing and disseminating information on foundations, corporate giving and related subjects. Its audiences include grantseekers, grantmakers, researchers, policymakers, the media and the general public.

title: Building Support for the Georgia Water Plan
description: This grant will enable the Georgia Wildlife Federation to continue coordinating a network of groups involved in the development of a statewide water management plan. In addition, the federation will directly participate in the water plan development process in several ways, such as serving on advisory committees.During the past two years, the federation hosted and facilitated membership meetings, recruited new members, enhanced internal and external communication practices, and regranted funds to member groups. The federation is the oldest and largest member-supported conservation organization in Georgia.

title: Georgia Comprehensive Statewide Water Management
description: The Georgia Wildlife Federation, the oldest and largest member-supported conservation organization in Georgia, helps coordinate a network of groups involved in the development and implementation of a statewide water management plan. Past accomplishments include: hosting and facilitating membership meetings, recruiting new members, enhancing internal and external communication practices, and regranting funds to member groups. With renewed Mott support, the federation will continue to play this important coordination role, as well as participate directly in the implementation of the statewide water management plan at the state, watershed, and local levels.

title: Georgia Comprehensive Statewide Water Management
description: The Georgia Wildlife Federation, the oldest member-supported conservation organization in Georgia, helps coordinate a network of groups seeking to influence the implementation of Georgia’s recently adopted statewide water management plan. The federation provides technical assistance to partner groups, convenes and facilitates network meetings, and engages directly on water management policy issues. With this grant increase and associated grant period extension, the grantee will continue to play this important coordination role.

title: Georgia Comprehensive Statewide Water Management
description: Georgia’s waters support myriad aquatic ecosystems and play a key role in the state’s economy. However, poor management, record droughts, and recent legal rulings have created an urgent need for the state to develop sustainable water use policies. The Georgia Wildlife Federation, the state’s oldest and largest member-supported conservation organization, promotes water conservation, efficiency, and sound water management through its members and as a leader of the Georgia Water Coalition. With a two-year renewal from Mott, the federation will continue to promote and implement conservation-based approaches to water management.

title: Georgia Comprehensive Statewide Water Management
description: The Georgia Wildlife Federation, the oldest member-supported conservation organization in Georgia, helps coordinate a network of groups seeking to influence the implementation of Georgia’s statewide water management plan. The grantee provides technical assistance to partner groups, convenes and facilitates network meetings, and engages directly on water management policy issues. With a two-year grant renewal, the grantee will continue to promote and implement conservation-based approaches to water management.

title: Georgia Comprehensive Statewide Water Management
description: The Georgia Wildlife Federation, the oldest member-supported conservation organization in Georgia, helps coordinate a network of groups seeking to improve the state’s management of its water resources. The grantee provides technical assistance to partner groups, convenes and facilitates network meetings, and engages directly on water management policy issues. With a two-year grant renewal, the grantee will continue to promote and implement conservation-based approaches to water management.

title: Institutional Development
description: The program goal is to support the strengthening and expansion of community foundations as a means of mobilizing local resources across Russia. The Community Foundation Partnership will work toward this goal by focusing on three main objectives: 1) creating a common identity and purpose and shared base values among its members; 2) supporting learning and professional development opportunities within the membership; and 3) creating a nationally favorable environment supportive of community foundation development in Russia. During the previous grant period, the grantee established a virtual library of information resources for existing and potential members; developed a selection of training materials for both developing and established foundations; and offered regular training and networking events for members, such as the annual conference of Russian community foundations. The Community Foundation Partnership has been an informal voluntary collaboration since 2003, registering as an independent organization in November 2006. It currently consists of 26 community foundation members.

title: Institutional Development
description: The program goal is to support the development of community foundations across Russia. The Community Foundation Partnership will work toward this goal by focusing on three main objectives: 1) creating a common identity and purpose among its members; 2) promoting professional development of members’ staff through an annual community foundation school; and 3) ensuring greater coherence and cohesiveness within the partnership and among regional alliances through joint programs and standards. In 2011-2012, the grantee continued to develop its virtual library of information resources while delivering a range of training and networking opportunities for members. The grantee also successfully advocated for inclusion of community foundations within the designation of socially oriented organizations, qualifying them for access to a range of government funding mechanisms. Subsequently, the grantee, regional alliances, and a number of individual foundations won competitive federal grants established for such groups. The Community Foundation Partnership has been an informal, voluntary collaboration since 2003, registering as an independent organization in November 2006. It currently consists of 26 community foundation members.

title: Institutional Development
description: The program goal is to support the strengthening and expansion of community foundations as a means of mobilizing local resources across Russia. The Community Foundation Partnership will work toward this goal by creating a range of products and services for both its existing and prospective membership. It will become a “virtual” library of information resources for members, through which it will systematically collate and disseminate best practices in foundation operations. The partnership will develop a selection of training materials for both developing and experienced foundations and will stage regular training and networking events for members, including the annual conference of Russian community foundations. Internships and mentoring relationships will be fostered in order to strengthen links across the membership. The Community Foundation Partnership has been an informal, voluntary collaboration since 2003, registering as an independent organization in November 2006. It currently consists of 16 community foundation members.

title: Next Generation Human Rights Activists and Social Marketing in Russia
description: The Center for Strategic & International Studies collaborates with the Russian human rights organization, Memorial, to select and train young leaders and managers of regional human rights groups in strategic planning, social marketing and advocacy. The goal is for these leaders, in turn, to focus on raising awareness among youth. This grant increase will enable the center to conduct focus groups, public opinion surveys, training and public awareness campaigns.

title: New Day for Learning: Support for the Time, Learning, and Afterschool Task Force
description: This grant will support Collaborative Communications Group in its continued efforts to support the Time, Learning, and Afterschool Task Force composed of policymakers, practitioners, researchers, and educators. In “A New Day for Learning”, the task force set forth a vision to create a seamless learning system with enriching learning opportunities throughout the traditional school day, afterschool, and year round. To stimulate the conversations among key stakeholders needed to implement this vision, Collaborative Communications Group will: 1) develop and disseminate materials that further the vision and implementation of “A New Day for Learning”; 2) support a speaker’s bureau; 3) develop policy recommendations; 4) share public opinion research that examines attitudes of parents, educators, policymakers, and community leaders regarding the ideas in the report; and 5) support meetings and conference calls for the task force.

title: A New Day for Learning: Support for the Time, Learning, and Afterschool Task Force
description: This grant will support Collaborative Communications Group in its continued efforts to support the Mott-funded “A New Day for Learning” Task Force composed of policymakers, practitioners, researchers, and educators. In the “A New Day for Learning” report, the task force sets forth a vision to create a seamless learning system with enriching learning opportunities throughout the traditional school day, afterschool, and year-round. To stimulate the conversations among key stakeholders needed to implement this vision, Collaborative Communications Group will: 1) update and disseminate the “A New Day for Learning” report and executive summary; 2) convene potential “A New Day for Learning” demonstration sites; 3) create a Web site, including a report fulfillment center; 4) share public opinion research that examines attitudes of parents, educators, and policymakers; and 5) support the “A New Day for Learning” Task Force with materials and convenings.

title: Support for the New Day for Learning Community
description: This grant will support Collaborative Communications Group in its continued efforts to support the Mott-funded New Day for Learning demonstration sites developing seamless learning systems that improve student success and include afterschool and summer learning opportunities throughout the day, year-round, and offered in multiple places throughout a community. This project will allow ten district-community partnerships (San Francisco; Providence, Rhode Island; Atlanta; Chicago; Charleston, South Carolina; Denver; Flint; Omaha; Peekskill, New York; and St. Paul) to participate in a learning community that includes opportunities for exchanging ideas and lessons learned, examining new initiatives, and receiving technical assistance from a cadre of Mott grantees. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) convene meetings and site visits for the demonstration sites and New Day for Learning Advisory Board; 2) manage an interactive Web site; 3) organize audio conferences for the demonstration sites; and 4) provide support to the advisory board, Mott-funded technical assistance resource experts, and the statewide afterschool networks in connecting and sharing information and resources with the sites.

title: Support for the New Day for Learning Community
description: This grant will support Collaborative Communications Group in its continued efforts to support the two, Mott-funded New Day for Learning sites in San Francisco and Providence and other participating communities. The sites are working to develop seamless learning systems to ensure that young people have the academic knowledge and skills they need to be successful in school, work, and life. This project will allow ten district-community partnerships (San Francisco, CA; Providence, RI; Atlanta, GA; Chicago, IL; Charleston, SC; Denver, CO; Flint, MI; Omaha, NE; Peekskill, NY; and St. Paul, MN) to participate in a learning community that includes opportunities for exchanging ideas and lessons learned, examining new initiatives, and receiving technical assistance. Specifically, Collaborative Communications Group will: 1) manage an interactive online workspace; 2) organize monthly audio conferences for the New Day for Learning sites; and 3) provide guidance on policy news and changes.

title: Convening Meetings of Afterschool Grantees
description: This grant will support Collaborative Communications Group by providing conference and logistical support for a meeting that will bring together Mott afterschool grantees to encourage sharing, collaboration, and networking opportunities. This meeting will help to further the quality and sustainability of afterschool programs, support school/community partnerships, and develop quality afterschool systems while also emphasizing the concepts in the Mott-funded report “A New Day for Learning”. This meeting will be held in conjunction with the 2008 National Network of Statewide Afterschool Networks meeting in Clearwater, Florida.

title: Convening Meetings of Afterschool Grantees and State Education Agencies
description: This grant will enable the Collaborative Communications Group (CCG) to provide conference and logistical support for two 2006 convenings that will build connections among practitioners, advocates, researchers, policymakers and state education agency representatives to further the quality and sustainability of afterschool programs and school/community partnerships. The first meeting will bring together Mott afterschool grantees to encourage sharing, collaboration and networking opportunities. The second meeting will convene state education agency representatives administering the 21st Century Community Learning Centers and Supplemental Educational Services programs to further strategies for implementing effective afterschool programs. The latter meeting will be held in partnership with the U.S. Department of Education and the Council of Chief State School Officers.CCG is a team of professionals who use innovative communications strategies, products and technologies to bring people together for the improvement of organizations, schools and communities.

title: Development of Belarusian NGO Capacity in the Field of Environmental Protection
description: This grant will enable ISAR to support public participation in environmental decisionmaking processes at the community level in Belarus. Through its representative office in Minsk, ISAR provides small grants and information resources to local grassroots groups that address environmental issues.During the past five years, ISAR distributed 116 grants totaling $208,000 to environmental groups in more than 40 Belarusian cities and towns. The grants supported projects ranging from environmental education and ecotourism to habitat protection and environmental advocacy initiatives.ISAR was founded in 1983 as the Institute for Soviet and American Relations to encourage citizen diplomacy and facilitate exchange between the U.S. and the Soviet Union. Its current mission is to support citizen activists and grassroots non-governmental organizations in their efforts to create just and sustainable societies by building advocacy skills, supporting community environmental problem-solving initiatives, galvanizing international environmental campaigns and increasing public participation in environmental decisionmaking.

title: Development of Belarusian NGO Capacity in the Field of Environmental Protection
description: The program goal is to strengthen citizen engagement in local decisionmaking through the establishment and support of environmental advocacy centers in Belarus. ISAR will provide grants and technical support to equip these centers to carry out advocacy efforts in support of Local Agenda 21, environmental justice, and public environmental monitoring. A small grants program for organizations working on these and related public participation issues will also be implemented. This project builds on previous efforts aimed at strengthening the capacity of grassroots environmental groups. Over the last seven years, ISAR has distributed grants to 139 recipients totaling $317,000 in over 40 Belarusian cities and towns. Grants have supported projects ranging from environmental education and ecotourism to habitat protection and environmental advocacy. Established in 1983, ISAR’s mission is to support citizen activists and grassroots organizations in their efforts to create just and sustainable societies.

title: Development of Belarusian NGO Capacity in the Field of Environmental Protection
description: The program goal is to strengthen citizen engagement in local decisionmaking through the establishment and support of environmental advocacy centers in Belarus. ISAR will provide grants and technical support to equip these centers to carry out advocacy efforts in support of the United Nations’ Local Agenda 21, environmental justice, and monitoring of environmental issues by civic groups. A small grants program for organizations working on these and related public participation issues will also be implemented. ISAR made initial grants to three advocacy centers in 2008 and additionally provided ten small grants to local organizations supporting projects ranging from environmental education and ecotourism to habitat protection and environmental advocacy. In the last nine years, ISAR awarded over 150 grants totaling more than $400,000. Established in 1983, ISAR’s mission is to support citizen activists and grassroots organizations in their efforts to create just and sustainable societies.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will enable Interfaith Funders to continue commissioning and disseminating research on faith-based community organizing; sponsoring workshops, funder briefings and other learning sessions; and organizing meetings for practitioners to consider issues that challenge the field.During the past year, the organization worked to increase philanthropic support for congregation-based organizing; assisted practitioners in the field by sponsoring a study tour/site visit to faith-based community organizing groups in Los Angeles; and encouraged faith leaders, especially in the Jewish community, to include studies of community organizing in seminary preparation. Interfaith Funders is an affinity group of grantmakers working to expand sources of support for faith-based community organizing.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purposes support to Interfaith Funders, a learning community and informal affinity group of grantmakers working to expand sources of support for faith-based community organizing. Interfaith Funders commissions and disseminates research on faith-based community organizing; sponsors workshops, funder briefings, and other learning sessions; and convenes practitioners to consider issues that challenge the field.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purpose support to Interfaith Funders, a learning community and informal affinity group of grantmakers working to expand sources of support for faith-based community organizing. Interfaith Funders commissions and disseminates research on faith-based community organizing; sponsors workshops, funder briefings, and other learning sessions; and convenes practitioners to consider issues that challenge the field.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purpose support to Interfaith Funders, a learning community and informal affinity group of grantmakers working to expand sources of support for faith-based community organizing. Interfaith Funders commissions and disseminates research on faith-based community organizing; sponsors workshops, funder briefings, and other learning sessions; and convenes practitioners to consider issues that challenge the field.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant increase will provide additional general purpose support to Interfaith Funders, a learning community and informal affinity group of grantmakers working to expand sources of support for faith-based community organizing. The grantee commissions and disseminates research on faith-based community organizing; sponsors workshops, funder briefings, and other learning sessions; and convenes practitioners to consider issues that challenge the field.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purpose support to Interfaith Funders, a learning community and informal affinity group of grantmakers working to expand sources of support for institution-based community organizing. Interfaith Funders commissions and disseminates research on institution-based community organizing; sponsors workshops, funder briefings, and other learning sessions; and convenes practitioners to consider issues that challenge the field.

title: Building the Capacity of Michigan's Workforce System
description: The program goal is to build Michigan’s workforce development capacity at the state and regional level through a series of initiatives including development of regional skills alliances, creation of regional workforce plans, and evaluation of alternative staffing pilots as part of reshaping the Work First policy in Michigan. This grant increase will support the Corporation for a Skilled Workforce in assisting with the launch of the Mid-Michigan Workforce Innovation in Regional Economic Development initiative.

title: Building the Capacity of Michigan's Workforce System
description: This grant will enable the Corporation for a Skilled Workforce to continue building mid-Michigan’s regional workforce development capacity through a series of initiatives that include creating a small business development infrastructure; reflecting on lessons learned in reshaping the state’s workforce policy; implementing the federally funded Workforce Innovation in Regional Economic Development initiative; and evaluating an alternative staffing pilot in Flint designed to facilitate jobs for the hard-to-employ. Funding includes a grant increase to assist with the launch of the workforce development initiative.Corporation for a Skilled Workforce, established in 1991, works to help communities thrive in a knowledge and skill-driven economy.

title: Building the Capacity of Michigan's Workforce System
description: The purpose of this renewal grant to the Corporation for a Skilled Workforce is to continue support for the mid-Michigan Workforce Innovation in Regional Economic Development initiative, known as WIRED, through activities that will improve services for entrepreneurs and small businesses, and assist in understanding and changing public opinion about economic opportunity within the region. A second purpose is to create a next-generation, adult education system that supports and advances the state of Michigan’s No Worker Left Behind initiative and other workforce transformation efforts.

title: Building the Capacity of Michigan's Workforce System
description: The program goal of this renewal grant to the Corporation for a Skilled Workforce is to build mid-Michigan’s regional workforce development capacity through a series of initiatives that support enhancing sector and employer strategies across the state, growing entrepreneurship and building communities of engaged entrepreneurs and resources, and reinventing adult learning and basic skills delivery throughout the state.

title: Building the Capacity of Michigan's Workforce System
description: The program goals of this grant to the Corporation for a Skilled Workforce are to enhance sectoral employment policy and improve relations with small business employers in Michigan, create a program that will improve the entrepreneurial culture in the state’s low-income communities, increase the availability and effectiveness of adult basic education in Michigan, and assist in developing a sustainability plan for the Mid-Michigan Innovation Team, the regional economic development initiative operated by Prima Civitas.

title: Building the Capacity of Michigan's Workforce System
description: This renewal grant will support the ongoing work of the Corporation for a Skilled Workforce, together with Prima Civitas, to build the Mid-Michigan regional development coalition and initiatives, and provide increased strategic support and technical assistance to the Michigan Department of Energy, Labor and Economic Growth during leadership transitions. In addition, this renewal grant will enable the grantee to carry forward crucial state policy agendas begun during its work with the Michigan Department of Energy, Labor and Economic Growth, including providing strategic support for Earn and Learn, a planned sectoral career training program for the jobless in Michigan. The grantee will also continue to enhance the state’s policy commitment and financial investment in adult learning, and advocate for training and education as a key lever for job creation and economic recovery in Michigan.

title: Building the Capacity of Michigan's Workforce System
description: The program goal of the Corporation for a Skilled Workforce is to build mid-Michigan’s regional workforce development capacity through a series of initiatives including, creation of a small business development infrastructure, reflections on lessons learned in reshaping the state’s workforce policy, implementation of the federally funded Workforce Innovation in Regional Economic Development initiative and evaluation of an alternative staffing pilot at Flint STRIVE designed to facilitate employment for the hard-to-employ.

title: Building the Capacity of Michigan's Workforce System
