description: The program goal of the Corporation for a Skilled Workforce is to build mid-Michigan’s regional workforce development capacity through a series of initiatives including creation of a small business development infrastructure, reflections on lessons learned in reshaping the state’s workforce policy, implementation of the federally funded Workforce Innovation in Regional Economic Development initiative, and evaluation of an alternative staffing pilot in Flint designed to facilitate employment for the hard-to-employ.

title: Building the Capacity of Michigan's Workforce System
description: The goal of the program is to expand the economic opportunity for youth who face challenges in completing high school, along with entering and staying engaged in the workforce. Through the support of this grant, Corporation for a Skilled Workforce will identify and expand strategies for helping disconnected youth in Michigan along with using data to assess the strategy outcomes.

title: Building the Capacity of Michigan's Workforce System
description: The goal for this project of the Corporation for a Skilled Workforce is to build mid-Michigan’s regional workforce development capacity through a series of initiatives including creation of a small business development infrastructure, reflections on lessons learned in reshaping the state’s workforce policy, implementation of the federally funded Workforce Innovation in Regional Economic Development initiative, and evaluation of an alternative staffing pilot in Flint designed to facilitate employment for the hard-to-employ.

title: Patriot Act Compliance Project: Technical Assistance for Mott Grantees
description: This grant will enable CompuMentor to provide technical assistance to Mott’s regranting grantees. In 2004, the Foundation began requiring regranting grantees to check the names of sub-grantees against terrorist watch lists. In 2004 and 2005, CompuMentor provided technical assistance to 83 grantees in 18 different countries through a support network offering training, document sharing and hands-on coaching. Building on the developed capacity and lessons learned thus far, CompuMentor will continue this assistance to approximately 15 international and 30 domestic grantees.CompuMentor is one of the oldest and most comprehensive technology assistance organizations serving the nonprofit sector. Its mission is to help nonprofit organizations achieve their goals through the effective use of technology.

title: Patriot Act Compliance Project: Technical Assistance for Mott Grantees
description: This grant renewal will provide support to CompuMentor to deliver technical assistance to Mott’s regranting grantees. In 2004, the Foundation began requiring regranting grantees to check the names of sub-grantees against terrorist watch lists. Since 2004, CompuMentor has provided technical assistance to over 100 Mott grantees in 20 countries through a support network comprised of training, document sharing, and hands-on coaching. Building on the developed capacity and lessons learned thus far, CompuMentor will continue this assistance in 2007 to approximately 12 international and 24 domestic grantees. Founded in 1987, CompuMentor is one of the oldest and most comprehensive technology assistance organizations serving the nonprofit sector. Its mission is to help nonprofit organizations achieve their goals through the effective use of technology.

title: Building Stronger Standards for Global Finance
geographic_focus: United States, Japan, Canada, Germany, Netherlands, Switzerland
description: The next year is a critical period in the ongoing development of environmental and social policies at international financial institutions. The approval of the International Finance Corporation’s (the private sector lending arm of the World Bank) performance standards will launch a number of other review processes for export credit agencies as well as private banks that have adopted the Equator Principles. In addition, non-governmental organizations (NGOs) will continue to work to improve the International Finance Corporation’s standards as they are adopted and monitor implementation of these new standards.This grant will enable Peregrine Environmental Consulting (PEC) to take advantage of this opportunity by providing research, policy analysis and coordination for NGOs working to strengthen global environmental standards for public and private lending institutions.During the past year, PEC worked to improve the International Finance Corporation’s Performance Standard Review consultation process by ensuring that the review period was extended, securing the release of critical documents and expanding the number of NGO consultations. PEC also worked to expand the type and number of organizations involved in international financial institution reform, including groups concerned with biodiversity conservation and toxics.

title: IFI Monitor
initiative: Reform of International Finance and Trade
description: The International Financial Institutions Monitor works to improve the ability of non-governmental organizations in the region of Latin America to develop viable solutions to the problems caused by policies and practices of international financial institutions. By providing communications tools, and information and analysis in both English and Spanish, to non-governmental organizations, the project will greatly reduce the information gap that has hampered the effectiveness of international financial institution policy reform efforts jointly undertaken by grassroots, regional and international organizations. The project will also strengthen the ability of non-governmental organizations to deal effectively with their own governments.

title: Latin American IFIs Monitor
initiative: Reform of International Finance and Trade
description: The Instituto del Tercer Mundo’s project, Latin American IFIs Monitor, provides a centralized source of information and analysis for networks of environmental, nongovernmental organizations and opinion leaders in the Latin American region on the policies and practices of international financial institutions. This project addresses the information gap that has hampered the effectiveness of international financial institution policy reform efforts. The project will improve the ability of nongovernmental organizations to coordinate, within the region and internationally, and to promote more sustainable investments in regional infrastructure and energy.

title: Fulfilling the Dream Fund
description: The goal of the Fulfilling the Dream Fund is to help redefine how the United States thinks about, talks about, and achieves racial and gender inclusion and how to realign these aspirations with the country’s core democratic values. The Fulfilling the Dream Fund aims to raise and disburse $20 million to support expanded access to opportunity for racial and ethnic minorities and women, renewing and strengthening the American dream. This grant to Public Interest Projects will provide funds toward regranting to support projects and research.

title: Fulfilling the Dream Fund
description: The goal of the Fulfilling the Dream Fund is to help redefine how the United States thinks about, talks about, and achieves racial and gender inclusion and how to realign these aspirations with the country’s core democratic values. The Fulfilling the Dream Fund aims to raise and disburse $20 million to support expanded access to opportunity for racial and ethnic minorities and women, thus renewing and strengthening the American dream. This grant to Public Interest Projects will provide funds toward regranting to support affirmative action projects and research.

title: Think Tank on Philanthropy
grantee: City University of New York Graduate Center
description: The Center on Philanthropy and Civil Society at the City University of New York Graduate Center is testing the value of establishing a policy think tank on foundations and philanthropy. The proposed think tank would be a collaborative model serving the dual purpose of producing policy-relevant research and also becoming a reservoir and “go-to place” for both new and existing research on foundations.This grant supports stage one in which a collaborative model will be tested. Activities will include commissioning papers by scholars on foundation impact; conducting literature reviews on evaluation and foundation impact; developing an advisory committee to guide the project; conducting a sample study; convening a conference bringing together information gathered from the research and sample study; publishing and disseminating the conference proceedings; and raising funds for next stages of the project.

title: Enriching Afterschool Programs Through Community Education
description: This grant will continue to support the National Community Education Association in its efforts to develop opportunities for educators and community members to work together for mutual benefit. The organization will also rededicate itself to the mission of supporting the needs of community educators at the national level by tying together leadership training, networking, representation, and advocacy. The grantee will also implement a communications campaign to target public education professionals and convey the benefits of incorporating best practices from community education into their daily work.

title: Connect US Fund
description: This grant will provide renewal support to the Connect US Fund, a funding collaborative of the Tides Foundation. Other contributors to the fund are the Ford and Hewlett Foundations, Open Society Institute, and the Rockefeller Brothers Fund. The goal of Connect US is to promote a vision of responsible global engagement in which United States’ power and influence are employed in a manner perceived worldwide as legitimate and responsive to the interests of major stakeholders in the international community. In 2004 and 2005, Connect US awarded 72 grants to support the advocacy efforts of 56 organizations and helped build approximately nine new partnerships, particularly among organizations based in Washington, D.C., and grassroots groups working in other parts of the country. In 2007 and 2008, Connect US will undertake a $7 million program of grantmaking and operational activities to help inform the public debate leading to the change in administration in 2009. Since 1976, the Tides Foundation has worked with donors to strengthen community-based organizations and the progressive movement through innovative grantmaking and philanthropic services.

title: General Purposes
description: The overall goal of the Foundation’s support to the Belgrade Fund for Political Excellence is to consolidate Serbia’s democratic transformation and to facilitate accession to the European Union and integration into Euro-Atlantic structures. Established in November 2003, the fund provides training and networking opportunities to existing and emerging political and civic leadership in Serbia through a variety of educational seminars, lectures, and other events. In 2005-2006, approximately 70 representatives from government, political parties, and civil society participated in the fund’s yearlong seminar series. The fund is based in Belgrade and is networked with other similar institutions in Eastern Europe.

title: General Purposes
description: The overall goal of Mott’s support to the Belgrade Fund for Political Excellence is to consolidate Serbia’s democratic transformation and to facilitate accession into the European Union and integration into Euro-Atlantic structures. The fund will provide training and networking opportunities to existing and emerging political and civic leadership in Serbia through a variety of educational seminars, lectures, and other events. In 2007-2008, the fund organized over 75 events, including several one-day seminars and conferences and shorter public debates, meetings, lectures, and roundtable discussions. A total of approximately 70 representatives from government, political parties, and civil society participated in the fund’s yearlong seminar series. Established in November 2003, the fund is based in Belgrade and is networked with other similar institutions in Eastern Europe.

title: General Purposes
description: The overall goal of the Foundation’s support to the Belgrade Fund for Political Excellence is to consolidate Serbia’s democratic transformation and to facilitate accession to the European Union and integration into Euro-Atlantic structures. The grantee will provide training and networking opportunities to existing and emerging political and civic leadership in Serbia through a variety of educational seminars, lectures, and other events. In 2009-2010, the grantee organized its core program of annual seminars for political party members and civic leaders as well as its special program for young political leaders. The grantee further developed and expanded programs that serve local political and civic leaders from key regions of Serbia, including south Serbia and Sandzak. The grantee also organized a variety of high-level conferences and events designed to promote dialogue on and awareness of Serbia’s European integration process. Established in November 2003, the grantee is based in Belgrade and is networked with other similar institutions in Eastern Europe.

title: General Purposes
description: The Mpilo Ministries Trust was established to provide administrative, office and logistical support to enable Archbishop Desmond Tutu to respond to the many requests for his counsel, leadership and moral guidance on issues ranging from racism to peace building to reconciliation. The Archbishop himself receives no payments from the trust, which is run by an administrative assistant and other support staff. This grant will provide support for office expenses, staff salaries and other related costs to ensure that the trust is able to handle the numerous demands placed upon the Archbishop to visit conflict-ridden parts of the world, deliver keynote speeches, promote healing and reconciliation, and work toward peace and racial tolerance.

title: Emerging Practitioners in Philanthropy Project
description: The Emerging Practitioners in Philanthropy Project addresses the professional needs of emerging young grantmakers, particularly individuals of color. It also helps meet the corresponding need for the foundation field to train and retain well-prepared and diverse new talent. The program provides scholarships for young grantmakers to access training, education and networking opportunities. This grant will enable the New World Foundation to provide funding and technical assistance, as well as resources, to develop a network of local affiliates that will build leadership skills, provide access to resources and create networking opportunities for the next generation of grantmakers.The New World Foundation has supported organizations working to strengthen and expand the active participation of all citizens in American democracy since 1954.

title: Emerging Practitioners in Philanthropy Project
description: This grant will provide continued support to the New World Foundation’s efforts to strengthen the next generation of grantmakers and other philanthropic leaders. The Emerging Practitioners in Philanthropy Project addresses the important, previously unmet, professional needs of emerging young grantmakers, particularly those of color. It also helps meet the corresponding need for the foundation field to train and retain well-prepared and diverse new talent. The project’s professional development fund provides scholarships for up to ten emerging grantmakers to attend the same training, education, and networking opportunities often afforded only to more senior staff. A convening of scholarship recipients will allow additional networking opportunities and a forum to share experiences.

title: Emerging Practitioners in Philanthropy Project
description: This grant will provide continued support to the New World Foundation’s efforts to strengthen the next generation of grantmakers and other philanthropic leaders. The New World Foundation has supported organizations working to strengthen and expand civil rights and the active participation of citizens in American democracy since 1954. With a particular focus on grantmakers of color, the Emerging Practitioners in Philanthropy Project addresses the professional needs of emerging young professionals in philanthropy, while also assisting the foundation field in the training and retention of well-prepared and diverse new talent. The project’s Professional Development Fund provides scholarships for up to ten emerging grantmakers each year to attend training, education, and networking opportunities often afforded only to more senior staff. To date, 29 emerging grantmakers have received scholarships through this program. In addition, the newly created Next Generation Scholarship Fund enabled 34 diverse emerging leaders to attend the annual Council on Foundation’s Leadership Summit. A convening of scholarship recipients will allow additional networking opportunities and a forum to share experiences.

title: Emerging Practitioners in Philanthropy Project
description: The Tides Center provides fiscal sponsorship and essential organizational, financial, and personnel services to over 200 projects working to advance progressive and social change nationwide. This grant will provide support to the Emerging Practitioners in Philanthropy Project. With a particular focus on grantmakers of color, the project addresses the professional needs of emerging young professionals in philanthropy. To date, the project’s Professional Development Fund has provided scholarships to 57 emerging grantmakers for training, education, and networking opportunities and its Next Generation Scholarship Fund has enabled 77 diverse emerging leaders to attend the annual Council of Foundations Leadership Summit. During the grant period, the project will award scholarships to emerging professionals, increase the amount of alumni-specific content at convenings, expand awareness of its programs, and increase collaboration with identity-based affinity groups.

title: Emerging Practitioners in Philanthropy Project
description: The Tides Center provides fiscal sponsorship and essential organizational, financial, and personnel services to over 200 projects working to advance progressive and social change nationwide. This grant will provide support to Emerging Practitioners in Philanthropy, a project of the Tides Center. With a particular focus on people of color, the project addresses the professional needs of emerging young professionals in philanthropy. To date, the project has provided scholarships to nearly 100 emerging grantmakers for training, education, and networking opportunities. Grant support will allow the project to execute its newly adopted strategic plan, with a focus on building extraordinary leaders for foundations and the communities they impact, and increasing generational collaborations within philanthropy to build better foundations for a better world.

title: Flint IDA Collaborative
description: This grant increase will enable the local Individual Development Account (IDA) program, known as the Genesee Area Investment Network$, to more than double the number of savings accounts available to low-income households in Flint and Genesee County, from 88 to 206. In the third year of a three-year Mott Foundation grant to Legal Services of Eastern Michigan, this savings program, with a waiting list of over 100 individuals, has successfully provided matched savings accounts for individuals to save for microenterprise, education and job training, homeownership, transportation, and foreclosure prevention.

title: Flint IDA Collaborative
description: This grant renewal to Legal Services of Eastern Michigan will allow the local Individual Development Accounts program, known as the Genesee Area Investment Network$, to allocate 90 additional Individual Development Accounts to low-income individuals in Genesee County. In its fourth year, this savings program has successfully provided matched savings accounts for individuals for microenterprise, education and job training, homeownership, transportation, and foreclosure prevention, with 36 individuals graduating and reaching their specific savings goal. In 2006, the Foundation provided a grant increase to more than double the number of savings accounts available to low-income households in Flint and Genesee County from 89 to 206. With these 90 proposed new accounts and Mott’s past investments in the program, the Genesee Area Investment Network$ will provide nearly 300 accounts to local residents by 2010.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Slovenia, Latvia, Serbia, Romania, Lithuania, Montenegro, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Hungary, Czech Republic, Slovakia, Croatia
description: The program goal is to support the development of an enabling legal environment for civil society in Central and Eastern Europe and Russia and the European Union neighborhood. The European Center for Not-for-Profit Law carries out this goal by promoting an effective legal and fiscal framework for nonprofits; improving the legal framework for volunteerism and other forms of public participation; strengthening governance and accountability in the nonprofit sector; and assisting nonprofit organizations to participate in the European Union accession process. Major accomplishments during 2005-2007 included assisting in the development of improved laws on nongovernmental organizations in Croatia, Serbia, Macedonia, Romania, and Moldova; developing laws on volunteerism in Bosnia, Croatia, Hungary, Macedonia, and Serbia; and assisting in the development of a government-civil society cooperation agreement in Bosnia. Established in 2003, the center is based in Budapest, Hungary.

title: Building the Capacity of Southern Environmental Nonprofits through Technology Planning and Assistance
geographic_focus: Alabama, North Carolina, Tennessee, Georgia, Mississippi, South Carolina, Louisiana
description: Advances in communication and information technology over the past several years have dramatically transformed the way organizations do business. Due to a lack of knowledge concerning acquisition and management of appropriate technology, much of the nonprofit sector has failed to take advantage of opportunities for increased efficiency and organizational effectiveness.With this grant, NetCorps will provide technology assessment, planning and implementation services to 20 southeastern environmental groups focused on freshwater ecosystem conservation and provide ongoing support to groups that have already worked through the technology assessment process.During the past two years, NetCorps worked with 10 southeastern organizations focused on freshwater conservation to develop comprehensive technology plans that reflect and support organizational missions, goals and objectives. Efforts included the installation of new computer systems and a server upgrade for the Western North Carolina Alliance; a server upgrade and reconfiguration and a new Web site for the Catawba River Foundation; and an upgrade of all computer systems and the launch of a new Web site for the Coosa River Basin Initiative.

title: Building the Capacity of Freshwater Ecosystem Organizations through Technology Planning and Assistance
geographic_focus: Indiana, New York, Ohio, Georgia, Pennsylvania, Michigan, Minnesota, Wisconsin, Alabama, North Carolina, South Carolina, Mississippi, Tennessee, Illinois, Louisiana
description: Information and communication technologies can help nonprofit organizations strengthen their capacity and improve program effectiveness. NetCorps, a national nonprofit technology assistance organization, will use this grant to help 30 organizations that are focused on freshwater ecosystem conservation in the Great Lakes and Southeast assess their technology needs and develop and implement strategic technology plans to fill those needs. NetCorps will also provide ongoing support to similar groups that have already undergone technology assessments and are well along in the implementation phase.

title: Community Challenge
description: This grant will provide partial funding for Phase III of the Community Challenge, coordinated by the Community Foundation of Greater Flint in conjunction with the Flint Club. The purpose of the Community Challenge is to transform the way public decisionmaking is conducted in Genesee County by demonstrating the power of citizen involvement and developing new patterns of collaborative leadership.Phase I of the Community Challenge was launched in June 2003. Six community-wide meetings were held over the course of nine months involving several hundred participants to identify the issues the community felt were most important to its future. In June 2004, Phase II began with the formation of work groups around four priorities: Downtown Flint, Visual Change, Economic Development and Education. Formal leaders identified with each of these issues were recruited to serve as conveners of the groups. Hundreds of area residents worked with these groups to bring about some of the desired changes identified during Phase I.

title: Resident Research Fellow
description: The Genesee Institute, an affiliate of the Genesee County Land Bank, provides technical assistance, planning and research for urban revitalization and sustainable neighborhoods. A major initiative of the Genesee Institute is the Resident Research Fellow program, which brings graduate students and recent graduates to live and work in downtown Flint. This grant increase will provide funding for an additional resident research fellow for the summer of 2006.

title: Michigan Alternative Staffing Partnership
description: In the decade since the welfare reform legislation known as the Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunities Reconciliation Act, the nation’s welfare rolls have significantly declined. While many people have successfully transitioned to employment and self-sufficiency, there remain a significant number of persistent welfare cases. This renewal grant to Flint Area Specialized Employment Services, Inc., will continue funding for the development of a program that uses temporary employment and supportive services to transition persistent welfare clients to sustainable employment.

title: Achieve Temporary Employment Services
description: This renewal grant will provide funding for Flint Area Specialized Employment Services, Inc., to continue to provide alternative staffing services to Genesee County Department of Human Services clients. In the decade since welfare reform, the nation’s welfare rolls have significantly declined. While many people have successfully transitioned to employment and self-sufficiency, there remains a significant number of persistent welfare cases. Alternative staffing can be an effective mechanism for helping to transition these clients from welfare to employment.

title: General Purposes
description: Ednannia is a key indigenous grantmaker in Ukraine, having distributed more than 1,000 grants totaling close to $1.7 million for projects initiated by local grassroots groups throughout Ukraine. It also provides valuable consulting, training, information resources and networking opportunities to grassroots Ukrainian civic organizations. Initially focused on the environment, Ednannia currently supports local community initiatives addressing a wide range of issues, including health, social care, youth, education, agriculture, economic opportunity and others.This grant will enable Ednannia to continue providing small grants and capacity-building training and assistance to grassroots groups. It also will help build its own capacity to raise funds from domestic sources, as well as to stimulate local philanthropy by requiring local match funding by its grantees.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to provide small grants and technical assistance to grassroots groups in Ukraine aimed at strengthening civil society and improving the quality of life in Ukrainian communities. Having expanded from an initial focus on the environment, Ednannia supports local community initiatives addressing a wide range of issues, including health, social care, youth, education, agriculture, economic opportunity, and others. In 2009-2011, Ednannia will continue providing small grants and capacity-building training and assistance to grassroots groups. It will also build its own capacity to raise funds from domestic sources, as well as to stimulate local philanthropy through local funding matching requirements of its grantees. In the most recent grant period, Ednannia awarded almost $400,000 to a wide range of grassroots initiatives in the areas of human rights promotion and protection. Established as an indigenous grantmaker in 1999, Ednannia is known for its rigorous, transparent, responsive, and effective grantmaking.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen community-based organizations and local philanthropy throughout Ukraine. Having expanded from an initial focus on the environment, Ednannia has increasingly positioned itself as a supporter of a wide range of community-based initiatives. It will continue this work in 2012-2014 through ongoing support for the development of community foundations in Ukraine. In addition, it will operate a voucher-based training market where it will seek to match training providers with organizations seeking capacity building support. In addition, the grantee will undertake a substantial internal organizational review as it positions itself for further development. Most recently, the grantee has helped foster the emergence of 13 prospective community foundations. Having recently won a tender to manage the voucher-financed training system, it has facilitated 44 targeted capacity building initiatives for Ukrainian organizations. Established as an indigenous grantmaker in 1999, Ednannia is known for its rigorous, transparent, responsive, and effective grantmaking.

title: Colorado Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will continue to support the Colorado Foundation for Families and Children to further the Colorado Statewide Afterschool Network, a statewide afterschool network connecting providers, policymakers, and others throughout Colorado to demonstrate that afterschool programs work and are a vital part of community life. This grantee is part of the third cohort of Mott-funded statewide afterschool networks. This renewal is an innovation grant, which continues to provide core support to the network, while also encouraging new ideas designed to build or enhance positive systemic changes that further policies and practices for school-based/school-linked afterschool programs. Each network receiving an innovation grant is expected to share lessons learned and products with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: Georgia Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will continue to support the United Way of Metropolitan Atlanta in developing the Georgia Statewide Afterschool Network. Participants in the Georgia Statewide Afterschool Network represent government agencies, nonprofit organizations, foundations, and other key afterschool stakeholders. This grantee is part of the third cohort of Mott-funded statewide afterschool networks. This renewal is an innovation grant, which continues to provide core support to the network, while also encouraging new ideas designed to build or enhance positive systemic changes that further policies and practices for school-based/school-linked afterschool programs. Each network receiving an innovation grant is expected to share lessons learned and products with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: Georgia Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will continue to support the United Way of Metropolitan Atlanta in the advancement of the Georgia Statewide Afterschool Network. This grantee is part of the third cohort of Mott-funded, statewide afterschool networks. In addition to continuing its core work building the field of afterschool, the Georgia Statewide Afterschool Network will continue efforts toward acquiring state-level support for policy and system changes while implementing a new strategy that focuses on best practices and the passage of afterschool policies at the local level. The network will position itself as a provider of high quality professional development and a broker of high quality technical assistance to contribute to the development of strong standards associated with afterschool programming including professional development standards. The local policy support strategy is designed to gain the support of policymakers who will become advocates for afterschool programming. Lessons learned and products will be shared with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: Georgia Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will continue to support the United Way of Greater Atlanta which coordinates the Georgia Statewide Afterschool Network. Participants in the network represent government agencies, nonprofit organizations, foundations, and other key afterschool stakeholders. This renewal is an achievement grant, which continues to provide core support to the network, while also encouraging new ideas designed to build or enhance positive systemic changes that further policies and practices for school-based/school-linked afterschool programs. Each network receiving an achievement grant is expected to share lessons learned and products with the National Network of Statewide Afterschool Networks.

title: Georgia Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant to Voices for Georgia’s Children will support the development of the Georgia Statewide Afterschool Network to continue to build an afterschool and summer learning system that improves outcomes for children and youth through school-based or school-linked afterschool programs. Over the next three years, the network will support the development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) creating a map and database to assist families in accessing afterschool and summer learning programs; 2) increasing the sustainability of the network; and 3) building systems of continuous improvement for afterschool programs.

title: Georgia Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Voices for Georgia’s Children, which coordinates the Georgia Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships, and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) develop research briefs connecting afterschool to key topics including substance abuse and juvenile justice; 2) launch a new online learning system for afterschool professionals; 3) create new programming focused on supporting children’s behavioral health in afterschool; and 4) support the development and distribution of the new afterschool program content in collaboration with the Foundation’s thematic partners.

title: Michigan Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Michigan Association of United Ways in the continued development of the Michigan Statewide Afterschool Network to improve quality and access to afterschool programs for Michigan youth. This grantee is part of the third cohort of Mott-funded statewide afterschool networks. The Michigan Statewide Afterschool Network is committed to providing statewide leadership to build and sustain high quality afterschool programs. This renewal is an innovation grant, which continues to provide core support to the network, while also encouraging new ideas designed to build or enhance positive systemic changes that further policies and practices for school-based/school-linked afterschool programs. Each network receiving an innovation grant is expected to share lessons learned and products with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: Michigan Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will continue to support the Michigan Association of United Ways in the advancement of the Michigan Statewide Afterschool Network. This grantee is part of the third cohort of Mott-funded, statewide afterschool networks. In addition to continuing its core work building the field of afterschool, the Michigan Statewide Afterschool Network will create a statewide afterschool professional development system aligned with national and state education initiatives that support student success. The network envisions that all students will have access to high quality, innovative science, technology, engineering, and mathematics activities and programs linked to school standards that develop inquiry and discovery to prepare them for college, work, and life. Lessons learned and products will be shared with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: Michigan Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Michigan Association of United Ways which coordinates the Michigan Statewide Afterschool Network. In addition to continuing the network’s core work to advance afterschool in Michigan, it will complete a multiyear project connecting afterschool and the broader education movement and increasing science, technology, engineering, and math awareness. The network seeks to deepen the connection between afterschool and the broader education movement by linking afterschool and summer learning opportunities to education policy. To ensure that new models and best practices are incorporated nationally, the network will share lessons learned and products with other state networks.

title: Michigan Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant to the Michigan Association of United Ways will support the Michigan Statewide Afterschool Network to continue to build an afterschool and summer learning system that improves outcomes for children and youth through school-based or school-linked afterschool programs. Over the next three years, the network will support the development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will: 1) develop strategic communications to build public awareness about the importance of expanded learning and summer learning programs; 2) implement a development plan to increase sustainability for the network; and 3) increase knowledge and capacity of expanded learning professionals to support college and career readiness in afterschool programs.

title: Michigan Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase to the Michigan Association of United Ways will support building the capacity of the Michigan Statewide Afterschool Network. Specifically, this project will support: 1) a data collection project to better identify the availability of afterschool programs for children and families in Michigan; 2) the development and implementation of a communications plan to build awareness of the importance of afterschool programs; and 3) a funder advisory committee to assist in supporting afterschool programs in Michigan.

title: Michigan Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Michigan Association of United Ways, which coordinates the Michigan Statewide Afterschool Network. The network will focus on building capacity for long-term success to advance afterschool and summer learning in Michigan. During the course of the grant, the network will support the development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool and summer learning programs. The specific initiatives will include: 1) finalizing and advancing a policy action agenda with strategic partners and afterschool stakeholders; 2) advocating for dedicated afterschool state funding through strategic partnerships; and 3) expanding statewide accessibility and utilization of program quality resources and tools to the afterschool field.

title: Minnesota Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will continue to support the Minnesota Department of Education in the development of the Minnesota Statewide Afterschool Network, a coalition of public and private organizations dedicated to ensuring beneficial options for youth to learn, develop, and contribute during nonschool hours. This grantee is part of the third cohort of Mott-funded statewide afterschool networks. This renewal is an innovation grant, which continues to provide core support to the network, while also encouraging new ideas designed to build or enhance positive, systemic changes that further policies and practices for school-based/school-linked afterschool programs. Each network receiving an innovation grant is expected to share lessons learned and products with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: Minnesota Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will continue to support the Minnesota Department of Education in the advancement of the Minnesota Statewide Afterschool Network. This grantee is part of the third cohort of Mott-funded, statewide afterschool networks. In addition to continuing its core work building the field of afterschool, the Minnesota Statewide Afterschool Network will coordinate and support policy and systems building efforts at the local level across the state by concentrating its policy efforts on strengthening the capacity of local partners — cities, schools, tribal nations, and regional collaborations — to ensure that children and youth have access to high quality afterschool learning opportunities. This will be accomplished through the following strategies: increasing recognition of high quality afterschool through publicized awards and recognition events highlighting innovation and best practices; instituting learning academies to bring together partners and champions; and creating and implementing a social media campaign to build statewide support for afterschool. Lessons learned and products will be shared with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: Minnesota Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will continue to support the Minnesota Department of Education in the coordination of the Minnesota Statewide Afterschool Network, a coalition of public and private organizations dedicated to ensuring beneficial options for youth to learn, develop, and contribute during nonschool hours. In addition to continuing the network’s core work to advance afterschool in Minnesota, it will design and implement a comprehensive strategy intended to secure additional resources for afterschool programs. The network will also implement a statewide community learning initiative to increase the collaboration between schools and afterschool programs, and to provide new learning opportunities for native youth in Minnesota. To ensure that new models and best practices are incorporated nationally, the network will share lessons learned and products with other state networks.

title: Minnesota Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant to the Minnesota Department of Education will support the Minnesota Statewide Afterschool Network to continue to build an afterschool and summer learning system that improves outcomes for children and youth through school-based or school-linked afterschool programs. Over the next three years, the network will support the development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will: 1) increase communications activities to build public awareness about the importance of afterschool; 2) develop a fundraising strategy to diversify funding sources for the network; and 3) create a framework to coordinate, align, and better leverage existing expertise and resources for professional development.

title: Minnesota Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Ignite Afterschool, which coordinates the Minnesota Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships, and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include:1) conduct a scan of college and career pathway initiatives in Minnesota; 2) create new technical assistance and training resources for Ignite Afterschool’s continuous quality program improvement initiative; 3) increase access to high-quality afterschool programs in partnership with community schools; and 4) support the development and distribution of the new afterschool program content in collaboration with the Foundation’s thematic partners.

title: Pennsylvania Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will continue to support the Center for Schools and Communities of the Central Susquehanna Intermediate Unit in the development of the Pennsylvania Statewide Afterschool Network. This grantee is part of the third cohort of Mott-funded statewide afterschool networks. This renewal is an innovation grant, which continues to provide core support to the network, while also encouraging new ideas designed to build or enhance positive systemic changes that further policies and practices for school-based/school-linked afterschool programs. Each network receiving an innovation grant is expected to share lessons learned and products with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: Pennsylvania Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will continue to support the Center for Schools and Communities of the Central Susquehanna Intermediate Unit in the advancement of the Pennsylvania Statewide Afterschool Network. This grantee is part of the third cohort of Mott-funded, statewide afterschool networks. In addition to continuing its core work building the field of afterschool, the Pennsylvania Statewide Afterschool Network will focus on creating a seamless system for lifelong education and employment success. The long-term outcome for this grant focuses on building a comprehensive professional development system that links afterschool, early childhood, K-16 education, and workforce development systems to assure an effective cradle-to-career life skills system. Lessons learned and products will be shared with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: Pennsylvania Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Center for Schools and Communities of the Central Susquehanna Intermediate Unit which coordinates the Pennsylvania Statewide Afterschool Network. Part of the third cohort of Mott-funded statewide afterschool networks, this network will continue its statewide partnership efforts to promote access to and the growth of sustainable, high quality out-of-school-time programs that promote positive youth development. The network will also partner with the Pennsylvania Department of Education to align out-of-school-time programs with school reform initiatives designed to boost student achievement, increase attendance, decrease dropout rates, and increase the number of students who graduate from college or are career-ready.

title: Pennsylvania Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant to the Central Susquehanna Intermediate Unit will support the development of the Pennsylvania Statewide Afterschool Network to continue to build an afterschool and summer learning system that improves outcomes for children and youth through school-based or school-linked afterschool programs. Over the next three years, the network will support the development of policy, partnerships, and quality initiatives to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) producing two data reports on the impact of out-of-school time programming in Pennsylvania; 2) developing strategies to increase the sustainability of the network; and 3) developing quality standards for afterschool programs.

title: Pennsylvania Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Central Susquehanna Intermediate Unit, which coordinates the Pennsylvania Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships, and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) recruit and develop a diverse group of key champions across the state; 2) conduct a statewide survey with career and technical education centers and workforce development boards to increase partnerships with afterschool and summer learning programs; 3) foster a coordinated approach to college and career ready opportunities for afterschool students; and 4) support the development and distribution of the new afterschool program content in collaboration with the Foundation’s thematic partners.

title: Michigan Sulfide Ore Mining Project
description: Proposals to mine metals locked up in sulfide-based ores pose a serious risk to the freshwater resources of Michigan’s Upper Peninsula. In recent years, the state adopted a new set of protective standards governing such mining activities. With this grant, the Sierra Club Foundation, a foundation established to support the work of the Sierra Club and its affiliates, will support the work of the Michigan Chapter of the Sierra Club to monitor and participate in the implementation of Michigan’s new mining rules and related state and federal policies so that Michigan’s freshwater resources are protected adequately.

title: Examining the Drivers of Sprawl in Michigan
description: While Michigan is one of the most aggressive states in the use of economic development incentives to attract and retain jobs, the state has simultaneously suffered from many economic development challenges. These include very high infrastructure costs due in part to sprawl and inefficient land use. Good Jobs First has undertaken this study to examine the outcomes of Michigan’s economic development incentive programs and determine if modifications in their use could lead to better land use as well as improved results for employers, workers and communities. This grant increase will support a more extensive and wider dissemination of the research products.

title: Increasing Media Capacity of Community Organizing Groups
description: Communications Leadership Institute’s SPIN Project provides accessible and affordable communications consulting, training, coaching, networking opportunities and tools in response to the needs of community organizing groups. Funding will provide partial support for the SPIN Project’s primary training forum, the SPIN Academy, which will place an increased emphasis on helping groups understand the frames within which messages are heard and understood by the American public. The SPIN Academy will also work with participants to develop messages to more effectively communicate goals.

title: Increasing Media Capacity of Community Organizing Groups
description: Communications Leadership Institute provides accessible and affordable communications consulting, training, coaching, networking opportunities, and tools in response to the needs of community organizing groups. This grant increase will support a special training opportunity, the Executive Training Program, which helps community organizing staff build a communications culture within their organizations.

title: Partnerships for Change
description: Through the Partnerships for Change project, the Land Information Access Association has demonstrated successful approaches for designing and enacting effective intergovernmental land-use planning and management policies and programs. This collaborative project, which includes the Michigan Municipal League, Michigan Townships Association, Michigan Association of Planning, and Michigan State University Extension, has provided in-depth technical assistance to local governments to foster new intergovernmental policy and program improvements. During the next three years, the grantee will build on this success in generating replicable and well-documented models of interjurisdictional land-use planning and management. By utilizing the project infrastructure already established, it is expected that this project will expand support among local officials, foster the adoption of additional cooperative approaches, and build momentum for statewide improvements in land-use planning.

title: Partnerships for Change
description: Through the Partnerships for Change project, the Land Information Access Association helps local governments in Michigan design and enact effective, intergovernmental land-use planning and management policies and programs. This grant increase will allow the association to assist the citizens of the city of Ecorse, located in southeast Michigan, to envision a better future and become more actively involved in local decision making processes.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Pro Vobis National Resource Center for Volunteering
description: In 2007-2008, Pro Vobis Volunteer Center will work with governmental agencies and the media to increase the visibility of volunteerism; support public institutions to involve volunteers effectively; strengthen the network of volunteer centers in Romania; and increase its own institutional capacity and sustainability. The center has been promoting and developing volunteerism as a viable resource for solving community problems in Romania since 1992. The center’s past achievements include promoting volunteerism at the national level; organizing conferences and meetings to discuss the development of volunteerism in Romania; and providing training to people and institutions interested in volunteerism. In addition, the center has developed a network of local volunteer centers throughout Romania.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Pro Vobis National Resource Center for Volunteering
description: The program goal is to strengthen volunteerism in Romania. During the grant period, Pro Vobis Volunteer Center will work with governmental agencies and the media to increase the visibility of volunteerism, support public institutions to involve volunteers effectively, strengthen the network of volunteer centers in Romania, and increase its own institutional capacity and sustainability. In the past two years, the center coordinated an annual national volunteer week attracting over 6,000 participants each year; organized conferences and meetings to discuss the development of volunteerism in Romania; provided training to people and institutions interested in volunteerism; and established a representative office in the capital of Bucharest to strengthen its advocacy work. Based in Cluj-Napoca, the center has been promoting and developing volunteerism as a viable resource for solving community problems in Romania since 1992.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Pro Vobis National Resource Center for Volunteering
description: The goal of Pro Vobis National Resource Center for Volunteering is to work with nongovernmental organizations, governmental agencies, and the media to increase the visibility of volunteerism, strengthen the network of volunteer centers in Romania, support public institutions to involve volunteers effectively, and increase its own institutional capacity and sustainability. In the past two years, the grantee coordinated an annual national volunteer week attracting over 5,000 participants, organized conferences and meetings to discuss the development of volunteerism in Romania, and provided training to people and institutions interested in volunteerism. Based in Cluj-Napoca, the grantee has been promoting and developing volunteerism as a viable resource for solving community problems in Romania since 1992.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Pro Vobis National Resource Center for Volunteering
description: The program goal is to strengthen volunteerism in Romania. To this end, Pro Vobis National Resource Center for Volunteering will work with nongovernmental organizations, governmental agencies, companies, and the media to increase understanding and appreciation of the role and contribution of volunteers in Romania. In addition, the grantee will support various government, nongovernment, and business organizations to involve volunteers effectively. Also, the grantee will increase its own institutional capacity and sustainability. In the past two years, the grantee coordinated an annual national volunteer week attracting over 4,000 participants, organized conferences and meetings to discuss the development of volunteerism in Romania, and provided training to government and nongovernment institutions interested in volunteerism. Based in Cluj-Napoca, the grantee has been promoting and developing volunteerism as a viable resource for solving community problems in Romania since 1992.

title: National Panel to Strengthen the Nonprofit Sector
description: This grant provides continued partial support to Independent Sector for a national panel to study ways of strengthening the nonprofit sector including philanthropic institutions. The panel was convened in 2004 and issued recommendations aimed at improving the oversight and governance of charitable organizations in two reports in 2005 and 2006. Many of these recommendations became law in charitable reform provisions of the Pension Protection Act of 2006. Subsequently, the panel appointed an advisory committee which developed a set of 33 Principles for Good Governance and Ethical Practice. These principles will be released at Independent Sector’s fall 2007 conference. Grant funds will support the preparation, printing, and initial dissemination of two separate reports: (1) a brief practitioner guide for nonprofit staff and board members; and (2) a detailed reference guide of both the principles and the panel’s work for self-regulation system administrators and scholars.

title: Advancing Good Governance and Ethical Practice Initiative
description: This grant provides partial support to Independent Sector for a program to advance nonprofit governance, transparency, and ethical conduct. The Advancing Good Governance and Ethical Practice Initiative is a continuation of the work begun by the Panel on the Nonprofit Sector. The panel was convened in 2004 and issued recommendations aimed at improving the oversight and governance of nonprofit organizations in two reports in 2005 and 2006. Many of these recommendations became law in charitable reform provisions of the Pension Protection Act of 2006. Subsequently, the panel appointed an advisory committee that developed the Principles of Good Governance and Ethical Practice Initiative, which was released at Independent Sector’s Fall 2007 conference. Through this initiative, Independent Sector will raise awareness of the principles among nonprofit organizations, federal and state public officials, and key members of the media. The initiative will also assist nonprofits in using the principles to evaluate and improve their own governance and management practices.

title: Brooklyn Expansion
description: Independence Care System (ICS) operates a Medicaid-managed, long-term care plan that provides and coordinates a comprehensive range of health and social services for individuals with severe disabilities.This grant will enable Independence Care System to expand into Brooklyn, add approximately 1,000 members, employ 1,500 healthcare aides by the end of 2006 and sustain career opportunities for a large number of home healthcare workers.ICS is a nonprofit organization committed to assisting people with disabilities to live independently. During the past year, ICS increased its membership from 600 to 735.

title: Update of "Jobs and the Urban Poor"
description: This grant will enable the Aspen Institute to update and disseminate its seminal publication, “Jobs for the Urban Poor,” that defined sectoral employment development. Sectoral workforce development has been the vanguard among workforce development programs in terms of developing positive working relationships with employers and using those relationships for the benefit of low-income workers. The purpose of updating the publication is to raise the profile of the sectoral workforce development field with public and private sector funding audiences. Two new flagship publications will describe the scope of the field, the range of strategies and practice, key highlights of accomplishments, targeted examples illustrating the range of current practice, and important challenges to the strategy.

title: CEE NGO Fellowship Program
grantee: Trust for Civil Society in Central and Eastern Europe
geographic_focus: Slovenia, Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, Bulgaria, Ukraine, Romania, Slovakia
description: The program goal is to strengthen leadership in the nonprofit sector in Central and Eastern Europe. To this end, the Trust for Civil Society in Central and Eastern Europe will partner with several European foundations to support fellowships for Central and Eastern European nonprofit leaders with their counterparts in Western Europe. The fellowships aim to build the capacity of participating organizations through developing the professional skills of key staff members. At the same time, the fellowships will initiate and deepen cooperation between Western and Eastern European organizations. In 2005-2007, 36 fellows from Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, Romania, Slovakia, Slovenia, and Ukraine have benefited from the program by improving their professional skills, developing important contacts with peers in Western and Eastern Europe, and sharing these new skills and contacts with their own organizations.

title: CEE NGO Fellowship Program
grantee: Trust for Civil Society in Central and Eastern Europe
description: The program goal is to strengthen leadership in the nonprofit sector in Central and Eastern Europe. To this end, the Trust for Civil Society in Central and Eastern Europe will partner with several European foundations to support fellowships for Central and Eastern European nonprofit leaders with their counterparts in Western Europe. The fellowships aim to build the capacity of participating organizations through developing the professional skills of key staff members. At the same time, the fellowships will initiate and deepen cooperation between Western and Eastern European organizations. In 2008-2010, 24 fellows from 13 Eastern European countries have benefited from the program by improving their professional skills, developing important contacts with peers in Western and Eastern Europe, and sharing these new skills and contacts with their own organizations.

title: Legislative and Regulatory Congressional Outreach
description: Through its Legislative and Regulatory Congressional Outreach project, the Council on Foundations is able to retain strategic assistance on public policy issues related to private foundations. This grant increase will enable the council to maintain presence and vigilance related to policy issues during the upcoming months.

title: Building the Capacity of Philanthropy in Alaska
description: This grant will continue to help the Alaska Community Foundation build its organizational capacity to grow philanthropy throughout the state of Alaska. Since becoming a statewide community foundation in 1998, the Alaska Community Foundation has grown its assets from under $500,000 to approximately $30,000,000, developed its staff and operational capacity, and diversified its board. It is currently in the middle of a five-year, capacity-building program supported by the Ford, Kellogg, Mott, Murdock, and Rasmuson foundations. The Alaska Community Foundation hopes to reach its goal of $50,000,000 in endowment funds by the end of the program in 2009. During 2008, the foundation will focus its efforts on increasing outreach to professional financial advisors; enhancing communications to the general public; and developing geographic, community-based, affiliate funds. Mott funds will be used primarily for public relations and marketing.

title: Evaluation of Neighborhood Small Grants Program
description: This grant will enable the Neighborhood Small Grants Network, which is a project of the Cleveland Foundation, to conduct a retrospective evaluation of the Mott Foundation’s Community Foundation and Neighborhood Small Grants Program and similar programs undertaken by funders in recent years. The evaluation will help the network build a substantial base of information about effective funding approaches that support capacity building of grassroots community organizations.The Cleveland Foundation was the first community foundation in the nation and provides leadership for the community foundation field in the critical areas of grantmaking, asset development and community leadership.

title: Evaluation of Neighborhood Small Grants Program
description: This grant supports a retrospective evaluation of Mott’s early community foundation and neighborhood small grants program and similar programs by recent funders. An evaluation was conducted by Grassroots Grantmakers, a network of funders investing in resident-driven programs through small grants, under the supervision of the Cleveland Foundation. The evaluation will help the network and other foundations and donors build a substantial base of information about effective funding approaches that support capacity building of grassroots community organizations. A grant increase will allow for broader dissemination of an executive summary of the evaluation report.

title: WINGS Forum 2006
description: The Worldwide Initiatives for Grantmaker Support, a project of the European Foundation Centre, is organizing a global conference in November 2006 for associations of grantmakers and other grantmaker support organizations. Two hundred participants from all over the world will come together in Bangkok, Thailand, to measure growth of the sector, showcase learning and accomplishments, demonstrate and inspire collaborative work, and explore specific interest areas in the field of philanthropy. This grant increase will support the costs of organizing the event.

title: Project QUEST Evaluation
description: This grant renewal allows Public/Private Ventures to continue the random assignment evaluation started in 2006 so that the city of San Antonio can discern the impact that Project QUEST is having on the earnings and employment of its citizens. Project QUEST’s mission is to identify the skills required to succeed in targeted, hard-to-fill occupations and then recruit, train, and develop skills so that the workers are qualified and ready to meet employers’ needs. Project QUEST is a sectoral employment program that develops a plan to allow participants to support themselves financially while attending long-term training, and offers support services and comprehensive counseling while they are in training and conducting their job search.

title: Project QUEST Evaluation
description: The purpose of this grant is to provide support that will allow Public/Private Ventures to complete a random assignment evaluation of Project QUEST. The grantee expects to publish the final report on this project in late 2013. The report will examine whether participating in Project QUEST improved participants’ employment and earnings over control group members at two and four years after random assignment, and will concentrate on the implications for sector-focused training in partnership with community colleges.

title: Project QUEST Evaluation
description: The purpose of this grant is to allow Public/Private Ventures to continue a random assignment evaluation of Project QUEST. The grantee expects to publish the final report on this project in late 2013. The report will examine whether participating in Project QUEST improved participants’ employment and earnings over control group members at two and four years after random assignment, and will concentrate on the implications for sector-focused training in partnership with community colleges.

title: Project QUEST Evaluation
description: The purpose of this grant is to provide support that will allow Public/Private Ventures to complete a random assignment evaluation of Project QUEST. The grantee expects to publish the final report on this project in early 2014. The report will examine whether participating in Project QUEST improved participants’ employment and earnings over control group members at two and four years after random assignment, and will concentrate on the implications for sector-focused training in partnership with community colleges.

title: Project QUEST Evaluation
description: The purpose of this final grant is to provide support that will allow the Economic Mobility Corporation to complete a random assignment evaluation of Project QUEST. The report will examine whether participating in Project QUEST improved participants’ employment and earnings over control group members at two and four years after random assignment, and will concentrate on the implications for sector-focused training in partnership with community colleges.

title: Project QUEST Evaluation
description: Since 1993, Project QUEST has helped San Antonio residents access skills training to achieve its goals of promoting long-term employment and higher incomes among residents while meeting local businesses’ needs for skilled workers and enhancing the area’s economic vitality.This grant will enable Public/Private Ventures (P/PV) to conduct a longitudinal study using a random assignment design to determine Project QUEST’s impact on helping unemployed and underemployed San Antonio residents stay in the labor market and increase their wages over time. The study will allow city leaders to determine the impact the program is having on local residents to justify their present general fund investment in this sectoral employment initiative and safeguard the promise of future investment.P/PV, established in 1977, is experienced in analyzing public policy, conducting research, providing technical assistance, and designing and evaluating demonstrations, with a particular focus on youth and employment issues.

title: Benton Harbor Replication
description: In the wake of civil disturbances in Benton Harbor, Michigan in the summer of 2003, Governor Jennifer Granholm appointed a task force to develop strategies that address the underlying problems of poverty and joblessness in this high-unemployment community. Following a year of discussion and analysis, the Benton Harbor Task Force identified job training programs for young men as the highest priority in the community. As a result, East Harlem Employment Service, Inc., has been asked by the Benton Harbor Task Force to plan, develop, and implement a STRIVE program in Benton Harbor. This renewal grant will support the continued development and implementation of the STRIVE program.

title: Benton Harbor Replication
description: In the summer of 2003 and in the wake of civil disturbances in Benton Harbor, Michigan, Governor Jennifer Granholm appointed a task force to develop strategies that address the underlying problems of poverty and joblessness in this high unemployment community. Following a year of discussion and analysis, the Benton Harbor Task Force identified job-training programs for young men as the highest priority in the community. As a result, a STRIVE program was designed and implemented in Benton Harbor. This final renewal grant to Flint Area Specialized Employment Services, Inc., will leverage state support for this STRIVE effort in West Michigan.

title: General Purposes
description: The Mozaik Community Development Foundation uses grantmaking, research, capacity building and advocacy to create conditions for social cohesion across Bosnia and Herzegovina. Particular emphasis is given to mobilizing local human and financial resources to meet needs prioritized by local communities. This grant increase will support efforts to foster local resource mobilization, one of the key program objectives. Additional activities include organization of a 2006 regional conference in Sarajevo.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal of the Mozaik Community Development Foundation is to promote public participation in decisionmaking and community development through targeted grantmaking and support to community-based action. The grantee is a national-level, Bosnian foundation established in 2000. The foundation uses grantmaking, research, capacity building, and advocacy to create the conditions for social cohesion across Bosnia-Herzegovina. Particular emphasis is given to needs assessment and prioritization by local communities and mobilizing local human and financial resources to meet these needs. In 2006, the foundation awarded over 80 small grants totaling approximately $110,000. The foundation also supported community facilitation activities and technical assistance in connection with its grantmaking and organized the first regional conference on resource mobilization. The foundation is based in Sarajevo and works throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina and is networked with other grantmaking institutions in the Balkans and Eastern Europe.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to promote public participation in decisionmaking and community development through targeted grantmaking and support to community-based action. Mozaik Community Development Foundation is a national-level, Bosnian foundation established in 2000. Particular emphasis will be given to stimulating philanthropy at local and national levels to meet community needs.
