The foundation also launched two social enterprises that employ women in rural communities and scaled up the successful YouthBank model to more than 15 municipalities. The foundation is based in Sarajevo, works throughout Bosnia-Herzegovina, and is networked with other grantmaking institutions in Europe.

title: General Purposes
description: The Mozaik Community Development Foundation is a national-level, Bosnian foundation established in 2000. The grantee’s goal is to promote public participation in decisionmaking and community development through targeted grantmaking and support to community-based action. This grant increase will help launch an endowment building program designed to raise more than $750,000 over the next five years.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to promote public participation in decisionmaking and community development through targeted grantmaking and support for community-based action. The grantee is a national-level, Bosnian foundation established in 2000 and based in Sarajevo. In 2013-2014, the Mozaik Community Development Foundation will use grantmaking, research, capacity building, social enterprise development, and advocacy to improve the conditions for local-level development across Bosnia-Herzegovina. Particular emphasis will be given to youth social entrepreneurism. The grantee will also build its endowment through local and international fundraising initiatives. In 2011-2012, the grantee supported 550 community initiatives with small grants totaling over $1 million, and these initiatives leveraged significant financial and in-kind contributions locally. The grantee also strengthened its wholly owned social enterprise, which employs 20 full-time and over 120 seasonal workers, many of whom were previously unemployed women living in rural communities. Additionally, the grantee scaled up the successful YouthBank model to more than 30 municipalities.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to promote public participation in decisionmaking and community development through targeted grantmaking and support to community-based action. The Mozaik Foundation is a national-level, Bosnian foundation established in 2000 and based in Sarajevo. In 2015-2016, the grantee will implement a revised, far-reaching strategy focused on enabling young, innovative social entrepreneurs to play a bigger role in Bosnia’s social and economic transformation. Building on its successful implementation of the YouthBank model — an approach to engaging young people in grantmaking and community action — over the next two years, the grantee will use grantmaking, technical assistance, research, and advocacy to identify young community leaders and develop their potential. Additionally, the grantee will build its endowment through local and international fundraising initiatives. In 2013-2014, the grantee supported 760 community initiatives with small grants totaling approximately $1 million, and these initiatives leveraged significant financial and in-kind contributions locally.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to promote public participation in decisionmaking and community development, particularly for young people, through technical assistance, capacity building, and grantmaking. The Mozaik Foundation is a national-level foundation established in 2000 and based in Sarajevo. In 2017–2018, the grantee will implement a revised, far-reaching strategy focused on enabling young, innovative social entrepreneurs to play a bigger role in Bosnia-Herzegovina’s social and economic transformation. Building on its successful implementation of the YouthBank model, an approach to engaging young people in grantmaking and community action, the grantee will use grantmaking, technical assistance, research, and advocacy to identify young community leaders and develop their potential. Additionally, the grantee will build its endowment through local and international fundraising initiatives. During 2015–2016, the grantee piloted and refined its new strategy, supporting 285 community initiatives with small grants, which leveraged additional financial and in-kind contributions locally. In addition, 18 ideas for social enterprises received initial support and three received start-up seed funding.

title: CEO Council
description: The CEO Council is a corporate outreach and advocacy program of the National Organization on Disability. In 2004 and 2005, Booz Allen and Hamilton undertook a pro bono analysis of the CEO Council, including both its fundraising and programmatic potential. The review helped shape the current program of the council, which now provides needed information and materials to corporate leaders who actually make the decisions about the hiring of people with disabilities.This grant will enable the organization to hire a program director and deputy director for the council; enhance Web site offerings and other communications products; and increase public exposure through briefings on Capitol Hill and outreach to the media.The National Organization on Disability, founded in 1982, works to promote the acceptance and full participation of men, women and children with physical and mental disabilities in all aspects of life.

title: General Purposes
description: Project QUEST is a nationally recognized sectoral employment program that defines the skills required to succeed in targeted, hard-to-fill occupations and recruits, trains and develops adult workers so that they are qualified and ready for employment.This grant will provide continued support to Project QUEST, demonstrating the social and economic benefits achieved through investments in comprehensive skills training. The support will also build the capacity of the agency to participate in a random assignment evaluation verifying the social and economic benefits it delivers to its graduates. Project QUEST has placed more than 2,100 participants in jobs providing family-sustaining wage levels. Alumni graduating in 2005 had a pre-training income of $8,457 and a $32,000 average income one year after graduation.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purposes support to Project QUEST, Inc. As a nationally recognized sectoral employment program, Project QUEST, Inc., defines the skills required to succeed in targeted, hard-to-fill occupations, then recruits, trains, and develops adults so that they are qualified and ready for employment. Project QUEST, Inc., has placed over 2,500 participants in jobs paying family-sustaining wage levels. A Texas Workforce Commission study indicates that approximately 95 percent of those participants remain employed a year later. The average annual family income for Project QUEST, Inc.’s 2006 graduates is over $34,000 at placement, a significant increase over the pre-training average annual family income of only $8,900.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purpose support to Project QUEST, Inc. As a nationally recognized sectoral employment program, Project QUEST defines the skills required to succeed in targeted, hard-to-fill occupations, then recruits, trains, and develops adults so that they are qualified and ready for employment. Project QUEST has placed over 2,100 participants in jobs paying family-sustaining wage levels. A 2006 Texas Workforce Commission study indicates that approximately 95 percent of those participants remain employed a year later. Verifications of pay show that alumni who graduated in 2004 are currently earning an average wage that is more than 200 percent higher than incomes before training.

title: Community-Based Civil Society Support Project
description: This grant increase will provide additional funds to support the organizational and programmatic development of the Foundation for Democratic Initiatives, an emerging, indigenous grantmaking organization in Kosovo. The foundation’s mission is to increase public participation in decisionmaking; stimulate cross-sector cooperation; and improve the effectiveness, transparency and accountability of Kosovo’s public institutions by providing grants to local non-governmental organizations and community-based civic groups. The foundation works throughout Kosovo and is based in the town of Gjakova.

title: General Purposes
description: The project goal is to strengthen local level democracy and civil society in Kosovo. To this end, this grant supports the organizational and programmatic development of the Foundation for Democratic Initiatives, an emerging, indigenous grantmaking organization in Kosovo. Over the next two years, the grantee will focus on consolidating its grantmaking programs around its core mission; diversifying its funding base; and strengthening staff, board, and management capacities. In 2005-2007, the grantee awarded over 80 grants, totaling more than $700,000. The foundation also engaged expert consultants to conduct an extensive strategic review and planning process. The foundation is based in Gjakova, Kosovo, and works throughout Kosovo.

title: Administrative Support
description: The project goal is to strengthen local-level democracy and civil society in Kosovo. To this end, this grant supports the organizational and programmatic development of the Foundation for Democratic Initiatives, an indigenous grantmaking organization in Kosovo focused on community-led development initiatives. Over the next two years, the grantee will focus on consolidating its grantmaking programs around its core mission; diversifying its funding base; and strengthening staff, board, and management capacities. During the last two years, the grantee awarded more than 30 grants supporting a range of community initiatives and provided networking and training opportunities to its grantees. The foundation also engaged expert consultants to conduct an extensive strategic review and planning process. The foundation works throughout Kosovo and recently relocated its offices to Pristina, the capital of Kosovo.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to stimulate community-based civic engagement and resource mobilization in Bosnia-Herzegovina. To this end, the Community Foundation Tuzla will work with community leaders, civic associations, youth groups, local district officials, school officials, and local businesses to stimulate community involvement and resource development in the municipality of Tuzla. The foundation will share its experiences with other communities and community-based organizations in Bosnia-Herzegovina. During the past two years, the foundation operated a community center and granted approximately $36,000 in support of local community development projects, including to Tuzla-area community schools. The foundation also actively engaged young people in its governance and grantmaking. Based in Tuzla, the foundation is networked with other community foundations and community-based organizations working with youth in Europe.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to stimulate community-based civic engagement and resource mobilization in Bosnia-Herzegovina. During 2010-2011, the Tuzla Community Foundation will focus on grantmaking programs that empower young people, stimulate public participation in community development initiatives, and promote community school development. The foundation will also share its experiences with other communities and community-based organizations in Bosnia-Herzegovina. During the past two years, the foundation consolidated its grantmaking programs and helped several of its operational projects become independent initiatives. In the same period, the foundation improved the administration of its community small grants program and increased giving through its Youth Bank program. With the goal of building a local base of financial support, the foundation launched programs to recognize and support individual donors to the foundation. Based in Tuzla, the foundation is networked with other community foundations and community-based organizations working with youth in Europe.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to stimulate community-based civic engagement and resource mobilization in Bosnia-Herzegovina. During 2012-2013, the Tuzla Community Foundation will play a convening and capacity building role in the community, support community initiatives and projects through grants, strengthen philanthropy locally through fund development and outreach to the community, and develop its board and staff capacities for leadership and management. During the past two years, the grantee supported and trained community organizers and community councils in marginalized neighborhoods, engaged more than 60 young people in decisionmaking on grant programs through its YouthBank project, supported community projects for community school and community center development. Based in Tuzla, the grantee is networked with other community foundations and community-based organizations working with youth in Europe.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to stimulate community-based civic engagement and resource mobilization in Bosnia-Herzegovina. During 2014-2015, the Tuzla Community Foundation will play a convening and capacity building role in the community, support community initiatives and projects through grants, strengthen philanthropy locally through fund development and outreach to the community, and develop its board and staff capacities for leadership and management. During the previous grant period, the grantee increased the number of direct beneficiaries from 3,000 in 2011 to more than 6,500 in 2012, supported more than 220 community groups with small grants and 65 families in need through is solidarity fund, implemented community research using the Vital Signs methodology, engaged more than 60 young people in decisionmaking on grant programs through its YouthBank project, and managed over $65,000 in targeted support for community school and community center development. Based in Tuzla, the grantee is networked with other community foundations and community-based organizations working with youth in Europe.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to stimulate community-based civic engagement and resource mobilization in Bosnia-Herzegovina. During 2016-2017, the Tuzla Community Foundation will play a convening and capacity building role in the community, support community initiatives and projects through grants, strengthen philanthropy locally through fund development and outreach to the community, and develop its board and staff capacities for leadership and management. During the previous grant period, the grantee expanded the number of local communities in which it is active from 10 to 22 in Tuzla and surrounding towns. Through a variety of programs, the grantee awarded 417 grants totaling approximately $788,000. In addition, the grantee directly engaged 160 community members, including many young people, in the work of the community foundation through its board, grantmaking committees, expert advisory bodies, and working groups. Established in 2005 in Tuzla, the grantee is networked with other community foundations and community-based organizations working with youth in Europe.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to stimulate community-based civic engagement and resource mobilization in Bosnia and Herzegovina. During 2018–2020, the Tuzla Community Foundation will play a convening and capacity building role in the community; support community initiatives and projects through grants; strengthen philanthropy locally through fund development and outreach to the community; and develop its board and staff capacities for sustainability, leadership, and management. During the previous grant period, the grantee awarded 199 grants totaling approximately $240,000 through programs targeting community-based citizen engagement, community school development, environmental issues, and youth poverty. The projects directly benefited 5,633 Tuzla residents. Established in 2005 in Tuzla, the grantee collaborates with other community foundations and community-based organizations working with youth in Europe.

title: Institutional and Programmatic Development Support
description: The project goal is to stimulate local philanthropy and improve the capacity for strategic grantmaking that supports the participation of women in decisionmaking processes at local and national levels. To this end, this grant supports the institutional and programmatic development of the Reconstruction Women’s Fund, an emerging indigenous grantmaking organization in Serbia. During the grant period, the grantee will provide grants to local women’s organizations and civic initiatives in Serbia. Mott support during this period will allow the grantee to develop new programs that complement the fund’s grantmaking, provide training and networking opportunities for the fund’s grantees, build the fund’s capacity through evaluation and networking, promote the fund’s activities to a wider audience, and broaden fundraising efforts. Over the past two years, the fund conducted research on Diaspora giving, provided professional development opportunities for key staff, and networked with similar funders in Europe and the United States.

title: Institutional and Programmatic Development Support
description: The project goal is to stimulate local philanthropy and improve the capacity for strategic grantmaking that supports the participation of women in decisionmaking processes at local and national levels in Serbia. To this end, the grant supports the institutional and programmatic development of the Reconstruction Women’s Fund, a Serbian grantmaking organization. During the grant period, Mott support will allow the grantee to increase networking with other women’s initiatives in Serbia and internationally, broaden fundraising efforts, promote the fund’s activities to a wider audience, and provide training to the fund’s grantees. During the past two years, the fund developed its nongrantmaking activities including publishing and direct training and technical assistance to vulnerable groups, raised awareness of the fund by increasing collaboration with women’s initiatives in Serbia and regional networks, and provided professional development opportunities for key staff. The fund is based in Belgrade, Serbia, and works throughout Serbia.

title: Institutional and Programmatic Development Support
description: The program goal is to improve the capacity for strategic grantmaking that supports the participation of women in decisionmaking processes at local and national levels in Serbia. To this end, the grant supports the institutional and programmatic development of the Reconstruction Women’s Fund, a Serbian grantmaking organization. During the grant period, Mott support will allow the grantee to increase networking with other women’s initiatives in Serbia and internationally, engage in participatory strategy development, and broaden local fundraising efforts. During the past two years, the fund increased financial and in-kind donations from local sources, raised awareness of the fund by increasing collaboration with women’s initiatives in Serbia and regional networks, and strengthened links with Roma women activists and other women’s groups in Serbia. The fund is based in Belgrade, Serbia, and works throughout Serbia.

title: Institutional and Programmatic Development Support
description: The project goal is to improve the capacity for strategic grantmaking that supports the participation of women in decisionmaking processes at local and national levels in Serbia. During the past two years, the grantee strengthened its networking and convening activities, bringing together diverse activists around common issues. The grantee also leveraged financial and in-kind donations from local sources. The grantee is based in Belgrade, Serbia, and works throughout Serbia.

title: Institutional and Programmatic Development Support
description: The project goal is to improve the capacity for strategic grantmaking that supports the participation of women in decisionmaking processes at local and national levels in Serbia. To this end, this grant supports the institutional and programmatic development of the Reconstruction Women’s Fund, a Serbian grantmaking organization. Specifically, during the grant period, the grantee will engage individual donors and other local sources of support in its work, strengthen outreach to young women by including them in programs and as volunteers in the organization, improve monitoring and evaluation systems across all program areas, expand and deepen partnerships with other civil society organizations, and develop long-term sustainability strategies. During the past two years, the grantee piloted new approaches to local fundraising, diversified its funding base, developed a multiyear strategic plan, engaged new volunteers, and expanded and scaled up new programming. The grantee is based in Belgrade, Serbia, and works throughout Serbia.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant increase will provide partial support for a regional conference on transitional justice to be organized by the Research and Documentation Center Sarajevo in cooperation with its partners, the Humanitarian Law Center in Serbia and Montenegro and Documenta in Croatia, both of which are Mott grantees. The increase also will support ongoing cooperation among these three organizations by partially covering the salary of one staff member to facilitate regional communication and joint project implementation.

title: General Purposes
description: The project goal is to support the organizational and programmatic development of a permanent institute for documentation and research of war crimes and human rights abuses in Bosnia-Herzegovina. The mission of the Research and Documentation Center Sarajevo is to investigate and gather facts, documentation, and data about war crimes and human rights abuses during the war in Bosnia. Over the past two years, the grantee has made substantial progress in building up its extensive archive of documentation; organizing, preserving, and making accessible this documentation for researchers, prosecutors, other nongovernmental organizations, victims and their families, and decisionmakers; and supporting efforts to raise public awareness about the past. The grantee is based in Sarajevo and has field offices in Gorazde and Brcko.

title: General Purposes
description: The project goal is to support the organizational and programmatic development of a permanent institute for documentation and research of war crimes and human rights abuses in Bosnia-Herzegovina. The mission of the Research and Documentation Center Sarajevo is to investigate and gather facts, documentation, and data about war crimes and human rights abuses during the war in Bosnia. Over the past two years, the grantee has made substantial progress in building up its extensive archive of documentation; organizing, preserving, and making accessible this documentation for researchers, prosecutors, other nongovernmental organizations, victims and their families, and decisionmakers; and supporting efforts to raise public awareness about the past. The grantee is based in Sarajevo and has field offices in Brcko, Gorazde, and Srebrenica.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant increase will support the ongoing work of Documenta, specifically in developing regional cooperation with the Humanitarian Law Center in Belgrade and the Research and Documentation Center Sarajevo. The overall program goal is to build a democratic culture based on human rights and the rule of law in Croatia and the Western Balkans region by encouraging Croatian society to deal with the legacy of war crimes and human rights abuses committed during the 1990s in Croatia and by Croatian forces in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to build a democratic culture based on human rights and the rule of law in Croatia and the Western Balkans region by stimulating Croatian society to deal with the legacy of war crimes and human rights abuses in the region. To this end, Documenta will research and gather documentation about the wars and conflicts during the 1990s; facilitate public discussion and debate on the issue of dealing with the past; monitor war crimes trials in Croatia and the region; and provide support to victims and witnesses participating in war crimes trials. Over the past two years, Documenta increased its technical capacity for maintaining data and documentation; gathered oral histories about events in specific regions of Croatia; organized debates and conferences on dealing with the past; commissioned a public opinion survey on dealing with the past; and monitored war crimes trials in Croatia. Documenta works closely with leading similar organizations in Serbia and Bosnia-Herzegovina. Documenta is based in Zagreb.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to build a democratic culture based on human rights and the rule of law in Croatia by stimulating Croatian society to deal with the legacy of war crimes and human rights abuses in the region. To this end, Documenta will research and gather documentation about the conflicts during the 1990s, facilitate public discussion and debate, monitor war crimes trials in Croatia and the region, and work with other groups across the region to establish a regional victims’ commission. During the past two years, Documenta increased its technical capacity for maintaining data and documentation, gathered oral histories about events in specific regions of Croatia, organized debates and conferences throughout Croatia on dealing with the past, issued reports on war crimes trials, and played a leadership role in establishing a Balkan-wide coalition to support a regional victims’ commission. Based in Zagreb, Documenta works with similar organizations in Serbia and Bosnia-Herzegovina.

title: General Purposes
description: The grantee’s mission is to build a democratic culture based on human rights and the rule of law in Croatia by stimulating Croatian society to deal with the legacy of war crimes and human rights abuses in Croatia and the region. To this end, Documenta will: 1) research and document human loss and collect oral histories; 2) facilitate public discussion and debate on issues of dealing with the past; and 3) monitor war crimes trials in Croatia and the region. The grantee is also working with other groups across the region to establish a regional victims’ commission. During the past two years, the grantee conducted extensive interviews and analyzed documentation in order to identify more than 2,200 victims from one war-torn county in Croatia; increased its library of recorded oral histories to 125 videos; participated in a regional coalition to establish a regional victims’ commission including organizing local and national consultation events; and helped to establish the human rights house in Zagreb. Based in Zagreb, Documenta actively works with similar organizations in the Western Balkans.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to build a democratic culture based on human rights and the rule of law in Croatia by stimulating Croatian society to deal with the legacy of war crimes and human rights abuses in Croatia and the region. To this end, Documenta will: 1) research and document human losses and collect oral histories; 2) facilitate public discussion and awareness of issues of dealing with the past; and 3) monitor war crimes trials in Croatia and the region. Documenta also will work with other groups across the region to continue developing a regional victims’ commission. During the past two years, the grantee conducted extensive interviews and analyzed documentation in order to identify more than 3,900 additional victims’ names, bringing the total documented victims to over 9,300; increased its library of recorded oral histories to 370 videos; participated in a regional coalition to establish a regional victims’ commission, including organizing local and national advocacy and awareness raising events; and organized nine study visits to sites of war crimes in the region for more than 400 participants. Based in Zagreb, Documenta actively works with similar organizations in the Western Balkans.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to build a democratic culture based on human rights and the rule of law in Croatia by stimulating Croatian society to deal with the legacy of war crimes and human rights abuses in Croatia and the region. To this end, Documenta will: 1) research and document human losses and collect oral histories; 2) facilitate public discussion and awareness of issues of dealing with the past; and 3) monitor war crimes trials in Croatia and the region. The grantee is also working with other groups across the region to establish a regional victims’ commission. During the past two years, the grantee conducted extensive interviews and analyzed documentation in order to identify 5,307 additional victims’ names, bringing the total documented victims in its database to 14,569; increased its library of recorded oral histories to 446 videos, with 211 available on its Web site; participated in a regional coalition to establish a regional victims’ commission, including organizing local and national advocacy and awareness-raising events; and upgraded its Web site and information systems. Based in Zagreb, Documenta actively works with similar organizations in the Western Balkans.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to build a democratic culture based on human rights and the rule of law in Croatia by stimulating Croatian society to deal with the legacy of war crimes and human rights abuses in Croatia and the region. To this end, Documenta will: 1) research and document human losses and collect oral histories; 2) facilitate public discussion and awareness of issues of dealing with the past; and 3) monitor war crimes trials in Croatia and the region. The grantee is also working with other groups across the region to establish a regional victims’ commission. During the past two years, the grantee conducted extensive interviews and analyzed documentation in order to identify 1,658 additional victims’ names, bringing the total documented victims in its database to 16,227; increased its library of recorded oral histories to 455 videos; organized local and national educational events related to the fate of missing persons and dealing with the past; participated in a regional coalition to establish a regional victims’ commission, including organizing local and national advocacy and awareness-raising events; and upgraded its website and information systems. Based in Zagreb, Documenta actively works with similar organizations in the Western Balkans.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant increase supports the overall programmatic and organizational development of the Youth Initiative for Human Rights following a period of rapid growth in the number of staff and range of activities. Additional funds will be used to cover costs associated with organizing staff retreats and planning sessions during the summer and fall of 2006, conducting training for staff, and upgrading financial management systems. The overall program goal is to engage the public, and young people in particular, in constructive dialogue and action with respect to dealing with the past in order to strengthen accountability and the rule of law. To this end, the Youth Initiative for Human Rights raises public awareness about the facts and circumstances surrounding the conflicts during the 1990s in the Western Balkans; advocates for justice for the victims of war crimes and human rights abuses; and promotes accountability on the part of government and governmental agencies.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to engage the public and young people, in particular, in constructive dialogue and action that promote and strengthen rule of law, accountability, and reconciliation in Serbia and the Western Balkan region. Through a variety of activities, Youth Initiative for Human Rights focuses on building the capacity of young people to address these issues and on increasing dialogue among young people from all sides of the conflicts in the former Yugoslavia. Over the past two years, the grantee has educated young people about the importance of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia, advocated for greater transparency in domestic war crimes trials, and established a foundation to support youth activism. The grantee is based in Serbia and has a field office in Pristina, Kosovo, as well as partner organizations in Bosnia-Herzegovina and Montenegro.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to engage young people in political processes and civic activism in order to promote and strengthen the rule of law, accountability, and transitional justice in Serbia and the Western Balkan region. Through a variety of activities, Youth Initiative for Human Rights focuses on building the capacity of young people to address these issues and on increasing dialogue among young people from all sides of the conflicts in the former Yugoslavia. Over the past two years, the grantee has strengthened its network of national offices in the former Yugoslavia, operated a grantmaking foundation that supports local youth-led projects, established a policy school for young people, and built a platform for broad-based youth activism called “My Initiative”. The grantee is based in Serbia and has a field office in Pristina, Kosovo, as well as partner organizations in Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia, and Montenegro.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to engage young people in political processes and civic activism in order to promote and strengthen the rule of law, accountability, and transitional justice in Serbia and the Western Balkan region. Through a variety of activities, Youth Initiative for Human Rights will focus on building the capacity of young people to address these issues and on increasing dialogue among young people from all sides of the conflicts in the former Yugoslavia. Over the past two years, the grantee operated training programs on human rights and democratic values for young people, published an annual report on the implementation of key laws, launched a human rights Web portal, and organized youth exchanges for Albanians and Serbs. On the regional level, the grantee organized its annual Days of Sarajevo event in Belgrade, which increases connections between young people in these two cities, and participated in the regional coalition to establish a victims’ commission for the former Yugoslavia. The grantee is based in Serbia and has partner organizations in Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia, Kosovo, and Montenegro.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to engage young people in political processes and civic activism in order to promote and strengthen the rule of law, accountability, and transitional justice in Serbia and the Western Balkan region. Through a variety of activities, Youth Initiative for Human Rights will focus on building the capacity of young people to address these issues and on increasing dialogue among young people from all sides of the conflicts in the former Yugoslavia. Over the past two years, the grantee played a leadership role in the regional coalition to establish a victims’ commission for the former Yugoslavia by coordinating a successful regional campaign to collect over 500,000 signatures in support of the commission. The grantee also organized the annual Days of Sarajevo event in Belgrade, which increases connections between young people in these two cities, exchanges between youth in Kosovo and Serbia, training programs on human rights and democratic values for young people, and a young leaders and activists forum. The grantee is based in Belgrade and works throughout the country.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to engage young people in decisionmaking processes and civic initiatives in order to promote and strengthen the rule of law, accountability, and transitional justice in Serbia and the Western Balkan region. Through a variety activities, Youth Initiative for Human Rights will build the capacity of young people to address these issues. The grantee will also create opportunities for cooperation and dialogue among young people from across the former Yugoslavia. Over the past two years, the grantee worked with partners in the region to design and implement youth exchanges and to advocate for the establishment of a government-funded, large-scale, long-term youth exchange program modeled on the Franco-German Youth Office. The grantee also organized training programs on human rights and democratic values for young people and a young leaders and activists’ forum. At the community level in Serbia, the grantee supports the participation and leadership of young people in awareness-raising and problem-solving initiatives. The grantee is based in Belgrade and works throughout the country.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to engage young people in decisionmaking processes and civic initiatives in order to promote and strengthen the rule of law, accountability, and transitional justice in Serbia and the Western Balkan region. Through a variety activities, Youth Initiative for Human Rights will build the capacity of young people to address these issues. The grantee will also create opportunities for cooperation and dialogue among young people from across the former Yugoslavia. Over the past two years, the grantee worked with partners in the region to design and implement exchanges and study visits for more than 600 young people and to advocate for the establishment of a government-funded, large-scale, long-term youth exchange program modeled on the Franco-German Youth Office. The grantee also organized training programs on human rights and democratic values for young people and convened a summit for more than 150 young leaders from the Western Balkans, Europe, and conflict and post-conflict societies around the world, as well as governmental officials from the European Union, member states, and the United States, to discuss youth participation. At the community level in Serbia, the grantee supports the participation and leadership of young people in awareness-raising and problem-solving initiatives and provided formal and nonformal educational opportunities for more than 1,000 young people. The grantee is based in Belgrade.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Albania, Montenegro, Croatia, Kosovo, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia
description: The project goal is to strengthen the leadership capacities of young people from Southeast Europe by supporting an emerging, action-oriented network of young professionals. The Transfuse Association supports cooperation and dialogue among its members through an annual conference and general assembly, a Web site and online members’ directory, a leadership development program, and ad hoc activities facilitated by a small program staff based in Berlin, Germany. In 2005, the association organized its annual conference in Ohrid, Macedonia, and brought high level speakers in to discuss European integration policies toward the Balkans. In 2006, the association organized its annual conference in Sarajevo, Bosnia, and focused on religion and politics. Also in 2006, the association launched a new leadership development program for members and other young leaders from Southeast Europe. The Transfuse Association currently has 75 members that are primarily from the Western Balkans, Bulgaria, Greece, Moldova, Romania, and Turkey.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Bulgaria, Moldova, Romania, Montenegro, Greece, Turkey, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Serbia, Albania
description: The project goal is to strengthen the leadership capacities of young people from Southeast Europe by supporting an action-oriented network of young professionals. In 2009, the association will hold the tenth annual conference of the network entitled “Europe and the World in 2020,” in Istanbul, Turkey. In 2007, the association organized its annual conference in Berlin, focusing on issues of state building in the Western Balkans. By the end of 2008, the association completed two of its yearlong leadership development programs and launched the third for 29 young people from ten Southeast European countries as well as Austria, Germany, Ireland, Italy, and the United States. The Transfuse Association currently has 86 members that are primarily from the Western Balkans, Bulgaria, Greece, Moldova, Romania, and Turkey.

title: Community School Development in Moldova
description: The program goal is to extend the model of community schools in Moldova. Project activities will focus on: democratizing both classroom practice and school governance; building school-community partnerships for sustainable local development; and developing the nationwide community school network. Step by Step Moldova has successfully introduced the model into 22 schools, training over 400 teachers in principles of cooperative learning underpinning community education. As a result, a range of social and vocational services have been developed in participating communities through active community involvement. Step by Step Moldova has promoted democratic change in Moldova’s education system since 1994.

title: Community School Development in Moldova
description: The program goal is to extend the model of community schools in Moldova. Project activities will focus on further developing the nationwide community school network by developing the capacity of schools to improve community-based learning and catalyze local development initiatives. Step by Step Moldova will seek to expand the network by linking with national education reforms aimed at decentralizing decisionmaking. It will widely advocate for greater recognition of community schools as valuable community institutions, using case studies of effective community partnerships which have addressed both learning and development needs. In 2007-2010, the grantee increased the number of community schools from 22 to 49, trained over 1,500 school stakeholders in relevant practice, and developed a team of nearly 40 mentors and trainers to work with schools and communities on their partnership activities. Step by Step Moldova has promoted democratic change in Moldova’s education system since 1994.

title: Community School Development in Moldova
description: The program goal is to further extend the model of community schools in Moldova. Project activities will focus on developing the nationwide community school network by developing the capacity of schools to improve community-based learning and catalyze local development initiatives. Step by Step Moldova will focus on strengthening eight regional clusters in order to better target training needs and facilitate peer learning and exchange. It will conduct a detailed mapping of community school needs and capacities in order to apply resources most effectively. In 2010-2012, the grantee increased the number of community schools from 60 to almost 150, developed a team of nearly 50 mentors and trainers to work with schools and communities on their partnership activities, and successfully moved to have key elements of community school practice incorporated into teacher training curricula. Step by Step Moldova has promoted democratic change in Moldova’s education system since 1994.

title: Community School Development in Moldova
description: The program goal is to further extend the model of community schools in Moldova. Project activities will focus on continuing to bring community school practice into the mainstream of Moldovan educational policy. Step by Step Moldova will give particular attention to developing capacity around social inclusion for schools as a critical part of the latter’s educational and community outreach functions. In addition, it will further strengthen regional hubs for peer learning, self-assessment, and school improvement across its network. In 2012-2014, the grantee increased the number of community schools to 171; improved the skills of 50 trainer-facilitators working across eight regional hubs; and successfully attracted international resources to support capacity building related to social inclusion, in response to needs identified through school self-assessments. Step by Step Moldova has promoted democratic change in Moldova’s education system since 1994.

title: Community School Development in Moldova
description: The program goal is to further strengthen the model of community schools in Moldova. Project activities will focus on continuing to bring community school practice into the mainstream of Moldovan educational policy. Step by Step Moldova will focus efforts on improving the quality and democratic character of learning in schools, engaging communities in ensuring successful inclusion practices in community schools, and strengthening approaches for schools to promote lifelong learning. In 2014-2016, the grantee trained over 500 teachers and other school stakeholders in critical aspects of community school practice. It introduced new training modules around financial knowledge and management as schools take on greater responsibility for raising financial resources. The grantee also successfully managed regional hubs as centers for exchanging knowledge and practice related to community engagement activities for schools. Step by Step Moldova has promoted democratic change in Moldova’s education system since 1994.

title: General Purposes
description: The Moscow School of Political Studies is the leading educational institution promoting democracy and civil society in Russia today. To date, more than 6,000 people have participated in the school’s seminars on a wide array of topics in the areas of political science, economics, government, law, media and civil society. The school’s mission is to contribute to the building of an open democratic society in Russia based on respect for the rule of law, observance of human rights and the encouragement of civic initiative.This grant will enable the organization to focus on a new generation of leaders who are on average 35 years old and who play important and increasingly influential roles in Russia’s social and political life. Through its four program areas — seminars, publications, a Web site and an alumni association — the school provides a unique forum for dialogue and enlightenment among young Russian leaders.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen the leadership skills of Russia’s emerging political, civic, and business elites. Through its four program areas — seminars, publications, a Web site, and an alumni association — the Moscow School of Political Studies will provide a unique forum for dialogue and learning for young Russian leaders. Particular attention will be given to working with leaders at the local and regional levels, with over 175 regional workshops and seminars planned. Regional leaders will also participate in a program of national-level workshops, as well as in seminars abroad. Over 30 regional and federal seminars have been conducted in the most recent grant period, involving nearly 1,000 participants. Established in 1992 and based in Moscow, the school seeks to contribute to the building of an open democratic society in Russia based on respect of the rule of law, strict observance of human rights, and the encouragement of civic initiative.

title: General Purposes

Through its four program areas — seminars, publications, a Web site, and an alumni association — the grantee will provide a unique forum for dialogue for young Russian leaders. Attention will increasingly focus on leaders at the local and regional levels, with over 20 regional workshops and seminars planned. The program of national-level and international workshops will also continue. Over 30 regional and federal seminars have been conducted in the most recent grant period, involving over 3,000 participants. In addition, alumni developed over 50 local and regional initiatives aimed at furthering the school’s democratic ethos. Established in 1992 and based in Moscow, the grantee works toward building an open, democratic society in Russia based on the rule of law, strict observance of human rights, and the encouragement of civic initiative.

title: New York Statewide Organizing
description: Community Voices Heard is a community organization in New York City with a broad base of low-income leaders working to improve economic opportunity by impacting the shape of public policies and the administration of programs affecting poor people. The organization has trained more than 15,000 people and has 3,750 dues-paying members. The purpose of this project is to support the continued expansion of the organizing model in other cities in New York and to help increase the capacity of the organization to support a wider range of work while continuing to be successful in New York City.

title: North End Soup Kitchen
grantee: Catholic Charities of Shiawassee and Genesee Counties
description: For 63 years, Catholic Charities of Shiawassee and Genesee Counties has provided intervention services for individuals and families in crisis. More than 80 percent of those served are nonCatholic, and last year the organization served over 165,000 meals and provided over 102,000 items to families with low or no income. Funding will support meals and other activities at the North End Soup Kitchen and its extension sites, which are all located in the city of Flint. Services at the North End Soup Kitchen include providing a hot meal every day, sack lunches, hygiene and basic needs items, and summer youth camps. Demand for these services is expected to be very high, as families and individuals are forced to make painful choices in this difficult economy.

description: Catholic Charities of Shiawassee and Genesee Counties provides intervention services for individuals and families in crisis including daily hot meals, sack lunches, hygiene and basic needs items, and summer youth camps through services at the North End Soup Kitchen and its extension sites. title: General Purposes
description: The National Employment Law Project has 35 years of experience working on employment issues for low-wage workers. This grant will provide general purposes support to continue its work in research, analysis, publications, and technical assistance on issues related to low-wage workers, the poor, and the unemployed. This grant will also support the organization’s efforts to continue and expand its outreach and service to community organizations throughout the country.

title: Investment Treaty News
initiative: Reform of International Finance and Trade
description: This grant will provide continued funding for the International Institute for Sustainable Development’s electronic news service, “Investment Treaty News”. Formerly INVEST-SD, “Investment Treaty News” covers the piecemeal regime of international rules governing foreign investment flows and the emerging policy implications of these rules, particularly their sustainable development impacts. The “Investment Treaty News” monitors new treaty negotiations, summarizes legal disputes between foreign investors and host governments, and publicizes events and resources related to this expanding field.The institute was founded in 1990 to promote sustainable development in public and private sector decisionmaking internationally and within Canada.

title: Investment Treaty News
initiative: Reform of International Finance and Trade
description: This grant will provide continued funding for the International Institute for Sustainable Development’s well-regarded electronic news service, “Investment Treaty News”. “Investment Treaty News” covers the piecemeal regime of international rules governing foreign investment flows and the emerging policy implications of these rules, particularly its sustainable development impacts. The “Investment Treaty News” monitors new treaty negotiations, summarizes legal disputes between foreign investors and host governments, and publicizes events and resources related to this field. In the next grant period, there will be detailed coverage of such high profile arbitrations as disputes over international affirmative action policies (primarily the Black Economic Empowerment policies in South Africa) and the land-use planning and permitting for gold mining in the United States.

title: Wisconsin Alliance for Excellent Schools
description: The Institute for Wisconsin’s Future is the sponsor of the Wisconsin Alliance for Excellent Schools, a coalition of organizations working to expand education funding and opportunities for children in Wisconsin, especially in low-income communities. The activities of the coalition include organizing parent, student, educator, and citizen groups to work together for increased school funding; conducting research on funding adequacy; and developing community outreach materials.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant increase will enable Parents for Public Schools to expand its capacity to provide more direct assistance and leadership training to its 25 community-based chapters located in 14 states. Parents for Public Schools is working with its local chapters to help them become more stable and develop a more focused school reform agenda.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide partial support to Parents for Public Schools as the organization continues to expand and strengthen its network of parent-based chapters. The Parents for Public Schools model works to overcome barriers such as race, ethnicity, and income in order to build a broad-based organization of parents working together to improve their schools. The national office of Parents for Public Schools provides training and technical assistance to local chapters, especially those reaching out to underrepresented families.

title: General Purposes
description: Parents for Public Schools works to overcome barriers such as race, ethnicity, and income in order to build a broad-based organization of parents working together to improve their schools. The national office of Parents for Public Schools provides training and technical assistance to local chapters, especially those reaching out to underrepresented families. The general purpose grant has provided partial support to Parents for Public Schools as the organization continued to expand and strengthen its network of parent-based chapters. This grant increase will support the organization’s increased focus on communications and evaluation as part of the work in Mississippi, as well as an expanded partnership with the Institute for Parent Leadership to provide additional training to members.

title: Reconnecting Dropouts to Mainstream Activities
description: This grant increase will enable the American Youth Policy Forum to document and profile the options and efforts available to reconnect out-of-school youth in Flint and Genesee County with educational and employment opportunities. Using a similar case study approach that was used for the initial 12 communities profiled in the Reconnecting Dropouts to Mainstream Activities project, the American Youth Policy Forum will study and document the programs and policies in the Flint and Genesee County area to gain a greater understanding of the education and employment opportunities available to assist young people who have dropped out of school.

title: Reconnecting Dropouts to Mainstream Activities: Highlighting Effective Policies and Practices to Expand Opportunities for High School
description: This grant will enable the American Youth Policy Forum to educate policymakers and community stakeholders about effective policies and practices that reconnect disconnected youth to education and employment opportunities. In the most recent phase of this project, the American Youth Policy Forum focused on documenting dropout recovery efforts in 12 communities that have developed innovative models to reconnect out-of-school youth to education and employment training options. Building on the work completed in the most recent phase of the project, the American Youth Policy Forum will facilitate a series of field trips for local and state leaders to communities implementing systems serving out-of-school youth, provide technical assistance to state and local leaders on expanding options for such youth, and work with a broad range of groups in developing policy priorities and field-building activities to bring more attention to the needs of out-of-school youth.

title: Educating Policymakers on Effective Strategies for Dropouts and Disconnected Youth
description: This grant will enable the American Youth Policy Forum to continue to bring more attention to the issues and challenges of dropouts and disconnected youth. During the most recent phase of this project, the grantee facilitated a series of field trips for local and state leaders to communities implementing efforts to serve dropouts and disconnected youth; provided technical assistance to state and local leaders on expanding educational options for such youth; and worked with a broad range of groups in developing policy priorities and field-building activities that bring more attention to the needs of the target population. In the next phase of this effort, the American Youth Policy Forum will refocus its efforts and place particular emphasis on informing federal stakeholders of specific strategies that result in policy advances and improved opportunities for dropouts and disconnected youth.

title: Strengthening the Education Pipeline: Areas for Impact Related to Disconnected Youth
description: This grant will enable the American Youth Policy Forum to continue to provide timely and relevant information on the importance of serving the disconnected youth population. The grantee recently held a series of forums on Capital Hill to inform federal stakeholders on the disconnected youth and dropout challenge; researched critical policy issues and areas that remain a challenge for practitioners/policymakers to implement efforts on behalf of the target population; and convened a workgroup of experts, key leaders, researchers, and practitioners to identify research-supported best practices that increase support for disconnected youth. In the next phase of this effort, the grantee will undertake a set of capacity-building activities to increase capacity at the federal and state levels to support a disconnected youth agenda and leverage resources to ensure that all students succeed.

title: Connecting and Collaborating with Key Stakeholders to Build Pathways to Education and the Workforce for Disconnected Youth
description: This grant will enable the American Youth Policy Forum to continue to inform and educate policymakers, practitioners, and other stakeholders on critical issues relevant to the disconnected youth population. During the most recent phase of this project, the grantee published a number of policy issue briefs and held a series of Capitol Hill forums and webinars focused on addressing the needs of disconnected youth within the current education reform framework. In the final phase of this project, the grantee will focus on strategically building capacity across a diverse set of stakeholders, primarily at the state and local level, to ensure that a coordinated system of education and workforce pathways are available to disconnected youth.

title: National Guard ChalleNGe Program Evaluation
description: This grant will provide support to MDRC to continue the National Guard ChalleNGe Program Evaluation project. During the first phase of the project, MDRC developed a random assignment design for 3,000 students, selected 10 state ChalleNGe programs to participate in the study, and fielded a post-random assignment survey on earnings, education, and program experiences. Continued support will enable MDRC to complete the final phase of the project and examine the long-term effects of promising youth-serving programs.

title: Rowe Mixed-Use Center in Downtown Flint
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This repayable grant to the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation will provide additional funds to complete the redevelopment of the Rowe Mixed-Use Center in Downtown Flint. The Rowe Mixed-Use project will include 75,000 square feet of office, restaurant, and residential space and bring an additional 200 jobs to downtown Flint. The Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation will partner with Uptown Reinvestment Corporation to provide a short-term construction loan to the project which will be repaid with proceeds from the insurance settlement, bank financing, and the sale of additional tax credits.

title: Bridges Technical Assistance
description: Bridges to the Future, a countywide afterschool program administered by the United Way of Genesee County, in partnership with the Genesee Intermediate School District and the Flint Community Schools, serves approximately 13,000 students at more than 100 sites. Since 2005, the University of Michigan has worked with local program partners to understand and overcome institutional and organizational barriers to the development of sustainable funding strategies. It also has worked to understand the evolution, operations, activities, and performance of the current program.This grant will enable the University of Michigan to develop a sustainability plan for the program in addition to continuing information gathering and analysis for the purpose of recommending strategies and activities that will assure the successful management of Bridges to the Future and its long-term existence.

title: General Purposes
description: The Virginia Organizing Project is a statewide grassroots community organization that is multicultural and multi-issue, addressing the concerns of poor people and distressed communities. Member organizations of the Virginia Organizing Project have a track record of success at the local and regional levels, and they have seen several significant accomplishments as a statewide organization. This grant increase will support the general purposes of the organization, including the creation and dissemination of a training video on community organizing and community organizers.

title: General Purposes
description: The Virginia Organizing Project is a statewide grassroots community organization that is multicultural and multi-issue, addressing the concerns of poor people and distressed communities. Member organizations of the Virginia Organizing Project have a track record of success at the local and regional levels, and they have seen several significant accomplishments as a statewide organization. This grant increase will support the general purposes of the organization, including the involvement of a Michigan-based community organizer in the documentary and training video on community organizing and community organizers.

title: General Purposes
description: Virginia Organizing Project is a statewide grassroots community organization that is multicultural and multi-issue, addressing the concerns of poor people and distressed communities. This grant will provide general purpose support to the grantee by providing coordination, training, research, and technical assistance to organizations across the state.

title: General Purposes
description: The Virginia Organizing Project is a statewide multi-issue, multiconstituency community organizing network focusing on the concerns of poor and working-class communities. This grant will provide general purpose support to the grantee, which provides coordination, training, research, and technical assistance to affiliated organizations across the state.

title: General Purposes
description: Virginia Organizing, Inc., is a statewide multi-issue, multiconstituency community organizing network focusing on the concerns of poor and working class communities. The organization has a robust organizing internship program, and there is an opportunity to expand this program during the summer of 2011. This grant increase will support the organization’s temporary expansion of the internship program.

title: Community Schools in Russia: Uniting Efforts
description: The program goal is to promote the development of community schools in Russia as one of the most effective institutional forms for public participation in community life. The New Eurasia Foundation will build on a successful program of grants and training support for a growing network of community school development support centers in 18 regions of Russia, with at least three new centers to be added in Northwest Russia. The program will also make networking and information exchange among leading Russian community school experts and practitioners more systematic through an expanding Internet portal, a rigorous shared training methodology, and regular meetings of community educators. Founded in 2004 by the Eurasia Foundation, the Madariaga European Foundation, and Russia’s Dynasty Foundation, the New Eurasia Foundation seeks to preserve and strengthen civil society in Russia and to promote the country’s integration into the world community.

title: Civic Expeditions - Civil Influence
description: The program goal is to promote civic awareness and activism in Russia’s smaller urban centers as well as to transfer to those communities the knowledge and skills related to defending public interests and people’s rights. The Perm Civic Chamber will conduct “civic expeditions” to seven small cities and towns in four regions of Russia. Visiting participants will conduct training seminars, exhibitions, public discussions, lectures, press conferences, and meetings with a broad variety of local people, organizations, and institutions to heighten local inhabitants’ abilities to address civic issues. The main focus will be on communities where civic activism is muted, but where demonstrated potential exists, in order to demonstrate possible approaches to fostering participation in difficult contexts. In recent years, the grantee and its partners have undertaken over 60 expeditions throughout Perm and neighboring regions. Founded in 1996, the Perm Civic Chamber’s mission is to provide informational, organizational, legal, and technical support to civil initiatives in the Perm region and other regions of Russia.

title: Civic Expeditions - Civil Influence
description: The program goal is to promote civic awareness and activism in Russia’s smaller urban centers. The Perm Civic Chamber will gather information on successful civil control activities from across Russia. The grantee will conduct civic expeditions to two small cities within the Perm region, conducting workshops on how to adopt these successful strategies. These will be supplemented by further seminars in the city of Perm, which will also target government officials, including the regional human rights ombudsman, in order to generate a greater understanding of civil control methods. In 2008-2009 the grantee and its partners conducted civic expeditions in four communities in Perm and neighboring regions. The grantee also began to document and disseminate examples of effective civic activism in order to support the ongoing growth of independent civic activity. Founded in 1996, the Perm Civic Chamber’s mission is to provide informational, organizational, legal, and technical support to civil initiatives in the Perm region and throughout Russia.

title: Perm United Support Service for Noncommercial Groups and Organizations
description: The program goal is to strengthen the capacity of local civic groups to promote positive change in their communities. The Perm Civic Chamber will establish a united support service for regional civic organizations that will focus on capturing and sharing innovative civic activism strategies while also promoting essential organizational management practices within client organizations. Drawing on a coalition of groups with diverse expertise in these areas, the united support service will also engage with experts in previously underexplored fields like event management and new media. In 2010-2011, the grantee and its partners conducted four civic expeditions in the Perm region and additional educational workshops for the regional rights ombudsmen. They continued to document and disseminate examples of effective civic activism in print and online in order to support the ongoing growth of independent civic activity. Founded in 1996, the Perm Civic Chamber’s mission is to provide informational, organizational, legal, and technical support to civic initiatives in the Perm region and throughout Russia.

title: Perm United Support Service for Noncommercial Groups and Organizations
description: The program goal is to strengthen the capacity of local civic groups to promote positive change in their communities. The Civil Action Foundation will provide support services for regional civic organizations. Services will focus on promoting innovative citizen activism strategies across a range of civic issues with growing public resonance. These services will also seek to promote essential organizational management practices within client organizations. In 2011-2013, the grantee and its partners provided consulting support to groups working on issues as diverse as effective condominium management to medical provision for diabetes sufferers to public oversight of government agencies. They also gathered and actively disseminated information on over 120 successful cases of citizen activism from across Russia. Founded in 2005, the Civil Action Foundation’s mission is to provide informational, organizational, legal, and technical support to civil initiatives in the Perm region and throughout Russia.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to improve the effectiveness of independent rights organizations located in Russia’s regions. The Fulcrum Foundation will use a two-pronged approach to support the development and strengthening of human rights promotion and protection activities. First, it will provide targeted grants and technical assistance to key regional organizations working on classic civil and political rights issues and seeking to heighten the acceptance of these concepts in regional public life. At the same time, it will support grassroots groups engaged in a broader agenda of citizen self-organizing through regular grant competitions. In the most recent grant period, the grantee made over 60 grants to regional rights organizations across Russia. Registered in 1999, the Fulcrum Foundation supports civic initiatives aimed at encouraging the establishment of a rule-of-law state, protection of constitutional rights and freedoms, and legal education of the general public.

title: Institute for Innovation in Workforce Policy and Practice
description: Passed by Congress in 1998, the federal Workforce Investment Act requires the establishment of business-led Workforce Investment Boards in local communities across the country. The purpose of the Workforce Investment Boards, of which there are approximately 600 nationally, is to oversee the expenditure of Workforce Investment Act funds and to design and implement local workforce development systems.This grant will enable the National Association of Workforce Boards (NAWB) to finalize the design and begin the implementation of the first comprehensive technical assistance and capacity improvement program for Workforce Investment Boards across the country.NAWB supports and promotes the work of its members through a comprehensive program of advocacy, technical assistance and communications activities.

title: Institute for Innovation in Workforce Policy and Practice
description: The federal Workforce Investment Act, passed by Congress in 1998, requires the establishment of business-led workforce investment boards in local communities across the country. The purpose of the workforce investment boards, of which there are approximately 600 nationally, is to oversee the expenditure of Workforce Investment Act funds and to design and implement local workforce development systems. This renewal grant will provide partial support to the National Association of Workforce Boards to implement the first comprehensive technical assistance and capacity improvement program for workforce investment boards across the country.

title: Institute for Innovation in Workforce Policy and Practice
grantee: National Center on Education and the Economy
description: The federal Workforce Investment Act, passed by Congress in 1998, requires the establishment of business-led Workforce Investment Boards in local communities across the country.
