title: Federal Budget Advocacy
grantee: Center on Budget and Policy Priorities
description: This grant will support the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities’ efforts to inform policymakers and the public about federal budget proposals under consideration in Congress. In order to reduce the deficit, the federal government is seriously considering significant cuts in a range of spending programs, many of which help working families.Funding will enable the center to work with national, state and local organizations to raise awareness about the implications of federal budget proposals. The center is a nonpartisan, nonprofit research organization and policy institute that analyzes government policies and programs, particularly those affecting low- and moderate-income people

title: Federal Budget Advocacy
grantee: Center on Budget and Policy Priorities
description: This grant provides support to the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities to assist in a broad-based effort to inform policymakers and the public about the implications of federal proposals to cut funding for key domestic programs and to change budget rules and program structures in a way that leads to even deeper cuts down the road. Mott funds will support two primary components of this effort: grants to state organizations to allow them to build effective coalitions, and a national coordinator at the center who will function as a bridge between national policy debates and state efforts. The Center on Budget and Policy Priorities is a Washington, D.C.-based think tank widely respected for its timely and credible analyses of federal budget and tax policies. The center also coordinates the State Fiscal Analysis Initiative.

title: Federal Budget Initiative
description: Faced with an ongoing deficit environment, federal policymakers will continue to consider deep cuts in domestic discretionary and entitlement spending programs that could potentially have severe ramifications for the nation’s social and economic priorities. This grant will enable the Hatcher Group to continue providing strategic communications assistance to state groups working to educate policymakers, the media, and the public about the federal deficit and various deficit reduction proposals under consideration. The Hatcher Group is a Washington, D.C.-based public affairs firm that helps improve the advocacy efforts of nonprofit organizations by connecting its research and knowledge to key audiences who shape public policy.

title: Federal Budget Advocacy
description: This grant will enable the Workforce Alliance to assist in broad-based efforts to inform policymakers, the media and the public about the implications of federal proposals to cut funding for key domestic programs and to change budget rules and program structures in a way that leads to even deeper cuts in the future. Mott funds will support communications strategies and a national coordinator at the alliance who will serve as a liaison, connecting workforce development organizations to state and national budget advocacy coalitions.The Workforce Alliance is a diverse coalition of experienced leaders from the field of workforce development who advocate for more effective federal policies to help more workers obtain the skills they need and to help more businesses hire the skilled workers they need to compete in today’s economy.

title: Federal Budget Initiative
description: This grant provides support to the Workforce Alliance to assist in broad-based efforts to inform policymakers, the media, and the public about the implications of federal proposals to cut funding for key domestic programs and to change budget rules and program structures in a way that leads to even deeper cuts in the future. Mott funds will support communication strategies and, among other staff, the national coordinator who serves as a liaison who connects workforce development organizations to state and national budget advocacy coalitions. The Workforce Alliance is a diverse coalition of experienced leaders from the field of workforce development who advocate for more effective federal polices that help: 1) workers obtain the skills they need to advance; and 2) businesses get the skilled workers they need to compete in today’s economy.

title: Building Effective Local Government and Community Interface
description: The Education and Training Unit works with community-based organizations to deepen democracy and community involvement in development. Mott supported it to provide training, develop resource materials, and enhance the capacity of local government, community development workers, and community-based organizations to improve service delivery to poor communities. This grant will assist the Education and Training Unit to provide support for building an effective interface between communities and local government around the key areas of local governance, democracy, and HIV/AIDS and to make available information and training materials on areas including access to basic human rights, local government, and HIV/AIDS.

title: Building Effective Local Government and Community Interface
description: The Education and Training Unit provides training and capacity building to civil society organizations and local government entities around issues of HIV/AIDS prevention and treatment. This program focuses on improving the interface and coordination of services to HIV/AIDS victims at the grassroots level among local government, business, and civil society through development of resource materials, information sharing, training, and building the capacity of those providing services to AIDS victims. Past activities included convening two national training workshops and many community workshops; updating and distributing pertinent manuals; and using a Web site to inform policymakers and service providers. Future plans include continuation of training and capacity-building efforts in 100 municipalities and emphasizing greater involvement of HIV/AIDS clients in the development of strategies and activities.

title: Red Ink Studios - Flint
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: Red Ink Studios is an underground artist movement that transforms underutilized buildings into free studio space for artists. Red Ink Studios – Flint, a project of the Genesee Area Focus Council, is the local replication of this national arts and economic revitalization approach. Since its establishment in 2005, Red Ink Studios – Flint has hosted more than 2,000 visitors to the studios and sold more than $15,000 of art by more than 20 local artists. This grant increase will enable Red Ink Studios – Flint to continue serving as an instrument of economic and community revitalization in Flint.

title: Red Ink Studios - Flint
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: Red Ink Studios is an artist movement that transforms underutilized buildings into free studio space for artists. Located in the Royalite Building next to the Flint Farmers Market, Red Ink Studios – Flint is a replication of this arts and economic revitalization approach. Red Ink Studios – Flint is providing working studio space to approximately 30 artists and hosts frequent exhibitions and shows. This renewal grant to the Genesee Chamber Foundation will support the continued development of Red Ink Studios – Flint as an instrument of economic and community revitalization.

title: Red Ink Studios - Flint
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: Red Ink Studios – Flint, a project of the Genesee Area Focus Fund, is an artist movement that transforms underutilized buildings into free studio space for artists. Located in the Royalite building next to the Flint Farmers Market, Red Ink Studios – Flint has developed into an important contributor to Flint’s art community by providing working studio space to artists and hosting frequent exhibitions and shows. This renewal grant will support the continued development of Red Ink Studios – Flint as an instrument of community revitalization.

title: Red Ink Studios - Flint
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: Red Ink Studios, a project coordinated by the Genesee Area Focus Fund, is an artist movement that transforms underutilized buildings into free studio space for artists. Located in the Royalite building next to the Flint Farmers Market, Red Ink Studios – Flint has developed into an important contributor to Flint’s arts community. For three years, Red Ink Studios – Flint has provided rent-free studio space and showcase exhibitions for up-and-coming artists. Red Ink Studios – Flint recently hired a new director and is poised to continue developing as an important contributor to the arts and community revitalization in Flint.

title: Budgeting for National Priorities
description: This grant provides ongoing support for the Budgeting for National Priorities project. The project seeks to convince political leaders in Washington and the general public of the need to restore fiscal discipline in ways that result in: a) an efficient and effective government whose benefits and costs are fairly shared; and b) a strong economy whose growth potential is enhanced by public and private investments. To accomplish these goals, the Brookings Institution conducts research, policy analyses, and outreach activities, all aimed at defining the magnitude of the federal deficit problem and producing policy solutions that will command the attention of federal policymakers. During the past four years, the project published a range of educational and policy products, which received extensive attention by the media, policymakers, and other influential stakeholders. Located in Washington, D.C., the Brookings Institution is widely recognized and valued as a nonpartisan, balanced source of policy research and analysis.

title: Budgeting for National Priorities
description: This grant will provide continuing support to the Brookings Institution for its Budgeting for National Priorities project. The project seeks to promote greater fiscal responsibility by developing new ideas, educating the public, and finding common ground among federal fiscal experts and policymakers. To accomplish these goals, the grantee conducts research, policy analyses, and outreach activities, all aimed at defining the magnitude of the federal deficit problem and producing policy solutions that will attract the attention and support of federal policymakers. During the past several years, the project has produced a range of educational and policy materials that received extensive attention by the media, policymakers, and other influential stakeholders. Located in Washington, DC, the Brookings Institution is widely recognized and valued as a nonpartisan, balanced source of policy research and analysis.

title: Center on Children and Families
description: This grant will enable the Brookings Institution’s Center on Children and Families to identify and promote policies of state governments and higher education institutions that have the most promise for helping low- and moderate-income students afford and attain a college credential. To accomplish this goal, the Center on Children and Families will produce and disseminate research and policy analyses that bring attention to critical issues and identify policy solutions that increase the effectiveness of financial aid as a tool to drive college access and completion. During the past several years, the project has produced a range of educational and policy materials that received extensive attention by the media, policymakers, and other influential stakeholders. Located in Washington, D.C., the Brookings Institution is widely recognized and valued as a nonpartisan, balanced source of policy research and analysis.

title: Asset-Building Capacity-Building Meetings
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant will support networking meetings and other learning opportunities for the Foundation’s grantees and other organizations working in the asset-building field. These meetings provide grantees and other asset-building stakeholders a unique space for the exchange of ideas and strategies, problem-solving, and for the development of potential collaborations. Washington University will develop content for meetings, Webinars, and conference calls with the Foundation’s grantees and other organizations. In addition to convener, the grantee will function as a documentation partner, mining each meeting for important insights and lessons learned and broadly disseminating that information in order to continue expanding knowledge in the asset-building field. Washington University is a private research university founded in 1853 and located in suburban St. Louis, Missouri. The University’s Center for Social Development was created in 1994 to create and study innovations in public policy that enable individuals, families, and communities to formulate and achieve life goals, and contribute to the economy and society.

title: Alternative Staffing Demonstration
description: As the temporary employment services sector increasingly serves as a point of entry to employment for disadvantaged jobseekers, several nonprofit workforce development organizations have developed alternative staffing programs. These nonprofit services provide temporary employment opportunities while simultaneously addressing the clients’ barriers to employment. This renewal grant will provide Goodwill Temporary Services in Austin, Texas with funds to participate in a four-site demonstration project investigating the labor market outcomes for disadvantaged jobseekers participating in an alternative staffing program.

title: Alternative Staffing Technical Assistance and Evaluation
description: This renewal grant will provide funds for Public/Private Ventures to conduct the second year of the Alternative Staffing Demonstration. description: This renewal grant will provide funds for Public/Private Ventures to conduct the third and final year of the Alternative Staffing Demonstration. description: This grant will support the launch of the Alternative Staffing Association, which will directly benefit existing and aspiring alternative staffing practitioners by providing services designed to help them expand their markets, operate more effectively and develop new funding sources. By strengthening and expanding the sector, greater numbers of people with barriers to employment will be able to enter and advance in the workplace.Since 1978, the ICA Group has promoted human and economic development through the creation of model employee-owned businesses and community-based projects that save and create jobs for low-income people.

title: Understanding Race and Skin Color
description: The Africa Genome Education Institute was started by some of South Africa’s leading social scientists, geneticists, and ethicists to conduct research on issues of race, ethnicity, and genetics to challenge the notions of racial superiority and inferiority, which characterized the country during the apartheid period. Mott provided support to it for research, publication, public education, and dissemination. Through promoting a more scientific understanding of the question of race, the Africa Genome Education Institute is making a significant contribution toward debunking many of the myths and stereotypes about race and ethnicity that still exist within public opinion. Its work with schools, educators, and learners is particularly important in promoting tolerance and respect for diversity. This grant will continue to support the work of the Africa Genome Education Institute, especially as this relates to using objective scientific research to educate people and communities about racial prejudice, discrimination, and stereotyping.

title: Understanding Race and Skin Color
description: The Africa Genome Education Institute conducts research on issues of race, ethnicity, and genetics to challenge the notions of racial superiority and inferiority, which characterized the country during the apartheid period. Mott provided support for the institute’s research, publishing, public education, and dissemination of materials. Through promoting a more scientific understanding of race, the grantee is making a significant contribution toward debunking many of the myths and stereotypes about race and ethnicity that still exist within public opinion. Its work with schools, educators, and students is particularly important in promoting tolerance and respect for diversity. This grant increase will support the Institute to distribute the findings of its research and to use the findings to create curriculum support materials, including the production of short books, newspaper supplements, CD-ROMs, DVDs, and a Web site for teachers to use in teaching evolutionary biology.

title: General Purposes
description: The Apartheid Museum is widely acknowledged as the preeminent institution dealing with South Africa’s apartheid history. It was specifically established to tell the story of the rise and fall of apartheid, the atrocities and human rights violations committed, the resistance mounted, and the eventual triumph of democracy. The museum continues to play a vital part in the country’s efforts to transcend the divisions of the past, serving as a stark reminder of the disastrous consequences of racism and discrimination, and as a salutary lesson never to repeat the past again. Mott’s support is for the operation of the museum, particularly as this relates to education, community outreach, and public awareness. This renewal grant will continue to support the work of the museum aimed at promoting understanding, tolerance, respect for diversity, and reconciliation.

title: General Purposes
description: The Apartheid Museum is widely acknowledged as the preeminent institution dealing with South Africa’s apartheid history. It was specifically established to tell the story of the rise and fall of apartheid, the atrocities and human rights violations committed, the resistance mounted, and the eventual triumph of democracy. In the past two years, the museum held various exhibitions on the lives of antiapartheid activists, including Nelson Mandela. It also continued to attract students and visitors from all over the world to the museum and to train history teachers in Gauteng province on how to teach about apartheid. This grant will continue to support the work of the museum and assist it to introduce new programs. It will also design an interactive exhibition on South Africa’s Truth and Reconciliation Commission and encourage visitors to add personal stories of human rights violations under apartheid.

title: General Purposes
description: South African History Online is a live Web site committed to promoting and popularizing the study of South African history and culture that challenges and corrects the distortions and biases of the country’s colonial and apartheid past. It is specifically, although not exclusively, aimed at students and provides research and other support material for teachers, academics, and educators. The site is widely accessed and has been adopted in some schools as part of the history curriculum. Mott’s support will enhance the capacity of the staff, strengthen the research, expand the Web site, and widen its reach. This grant will continue to provide general support to South African History Online for its work directed at producing an objective and inclusive account of South Africa’s past, which can contribute to the building of a just and nonracial society.

title: General Purposes
description: South African History Online is a live Web site committed to promoting and popularizing the study of South African history and culture that challenges and corrects the distortions and biases of the country’s colonial and apartheid past. It is specifically, although not exclusively, aimed at students and provides research and other support material for teachers, academics, and educators. The site is widely accessed and has been adopted in some schools as part of the history curriculum. Mott provided support to enhance the capacity of the staff, strengthen the research, expand the Web site, and widen its reach. This grant increase will support the grantee to update its online materials to comply with the new schools’ curriculum introduced in 2008. In light of the recent xenophobic attacks and school violence, it will also produce educational materials that advance social cohesion and the values of the Constitution, particularly tolerance, gender equality, democracy, and adopting nonviolent means to resolve conflicts.

title: General Purposes
description: South African History Online is a live Web site committed to promoting and popularizing the study of South African history and culture that challenges and corrects the distortions and biases of the country’s colonial and apartheid past. Its main activities include developing history curricula for high school students, and conducting research and making available online the history of the country, particularly the history of the struggle for liberation. The site is widely accessed, and the curriculum developed has been adopted in some schools as part of the history curriculum. Mott provided support to enhance the capacity of the staff, strengthen the research capacity, develop and update the schools’ curriculum, and expand the Web site and widen its reach. This grant will continue to support South African History Online for its work directed at producing an objective and inclusive account of South Africa’s past, which contributes to building a just and nonracial society.

title: General Purposes
description: South African History Online was established in 2000 to address the biased way in which the history and cultural heritage of South Africans was represented in educational and cultural institutions. Its mission is to break the silence of the country’s past and to create the most comprehensive online encyclopedia of South African history and culture. Past support enabled the grantee to change its Web site format to enable visitors to navigate it better; expand the liberation struggle history archives in time to mark the 100-year celebrations of the African National Congress in January 2012; produce an online arts and culture classroom; and develop online heritage tours for the cities that hosted the 2010 Soccer World Cup matches. Activities over the next two years will include the development of an online encyclopedia; expansion of the education, outreach, and internship programs; and building a history portal that will promote the writing, studying, and teaching of history.

title: General Purposes
description: The South African History Online was established in 2000 to promote South African history and to address the biased way in which history was represented. It provides a Web site dedicated to promoting the study and teaching of history and creating a comprehensive online encyclopedia of South African cultural heritage. Past support enabled the grantee to enhance the Web site format and make information more easily accessible, launch an internship program providing experiential learning opportunities for history students, and initiating and establishing a public history program in Namibia in partnership with local organizations. Activities over the next two years will include improving the capacity of staff to respond to the growing demand for information and knowledge from the Web site, providing support to other southern African countries to develop similar public history Web sites, and updating the online history material that is used by schools and universities.

title: General Purposes
description: South African History Online was founded in 2000 to provide a nonpartisan, unbiased, online account of South Africa’s history. It provides a comprehensive online encyclopedia and popular history programs on South Africa and African history and cultural heritage. Past support has enabled the grantee to maintain a comprehensive database with relevant content, improve the quality of its website, and build partnerships with academic institutions and government departments to continually improve the content on the website. This grant will support the grantee to generate new content, develop history classroom resources for teachers and learners, host events to create awareness of the importance of history, strengthen partnerships with universities, and continue to support other African countries to build similar online history platforms.

title: Local Government and Institution Building
grantee: Trust for Community Outreach and Education
description: The Trust for Community Outreach and Education is an affiliate organization that works with mainly rural communities in various provinces throughout South Africa in the areas of local governance and land acquisition. Mott supported it to work with its affiliate in the Eastern Cape, the Cala University Students Association, to ensure that communities understand their rights and participate in local government decisionmaking processes that affect their lives. This grant will continue to support this work to assist, in particular, on mobilizing and organizing rural communities in the Sakhisizwe municipality in the Eastern Cape province to demand better service delivery from the municipality, especially in the provision of basic services like water, sanitation, and electricity. The grant will also support efforts to ensure that the municipality engages communities when developing municipal plans and budgets in order to facilitate the improved provision of basic services by the local municipality.

title: General Purposes
description: Ithembalabantu Community Resource Centres is a membership-based organization that provides a platform for networking and mutual support for paralegals in seven community resource centres in and around eThekwini in the KwaZulu-Natal province. With Mott support, the grantee provided capacity building to its members through training interventions and mentoring to ensure that the communities they serve know and understand their rights and are able to access these rights. This grant will strengthen the organizational structure, systems, and procedures, and will enable the grantee to facilitate training interventions and networking opportunities for its members. The grantee will also assist its members in developing fundraising and sustainability strategies.

title: Research, Training and Case Studies Programme
description: The Impumelelo Innovations Award Trust rewards innovative projects and best practices in the public sector and public-private partnerships that reduce poverty and improve the quality of life of the poor. Mott supported it to promote the replication of innovative public sector projects through training and engaging local government officials who have the responsibility to deliver services to the poor. This grant will continue to support Impumelelo Innovations Award Trust to conduct research and publish materials on various areas of service delivery including housing, water, and sanitation. It will also conduct sector training workshops for government officials, particularly those working at the local government level.

title: Research, Training and Case Studies Programme
description: The Impumelelo Innovations Award Trust contributes to efficient service delivery at the local level by rewarding innovation and best practice in the public sector and in partnerships involving the public, private, and civil society sectors. Approximately R1 million is distributed annually to the most exceptional poverty reduction projects. The aim of this program is to encourage the replication of innovative good governance projects identified through the awards program. Over the past two years, the trust conducted capacity-building and skills training workshops for government and civil society leaders and published case studies based on award winning projects. This grant will provide continued support to the trust for its skills training workshops targeting civil society and public sector officials, using previous award winners as trainers. The trust will also undertake research that links policy and practice in the areas of criminal justice, education and training, health care, service delivery, and welfare and publish four case studies of best practice in these sectors.

title: Community Law Centre - Local Government Project
description: The Community Law Centre at the University of the Western Cape works in the areas of decentralization and democratic governance, specifically focusing on provincial constitutions, intergovernmental relations, and local government. The grantee works to strengthen the local sphere of government to be more efficient in the delivery of services by enhancing its understanding of its mandate and the legal framework of local governance. The Community Law Centre also supported the production and publication of the Local Government Bulletin, which is used to disseminate good practices on cooperative governance between the national, provincial, and local spheres of government and to keep local councilors and officials informed about legal and policy developments in topical and relevant areas. This grant will support the Community Law Centre to strengthen cooperative government between local government and other spheres of government and to provide hands-on support to local governments to understand and meet the demands of cooperative government.

title: Community Law Centre - Local Government Project
description: The local government project of the Community Law Centre, located at the University of the Western Cape, focuses on providing research, advice, education and training around issues of government decentralization, governance practices at the local municipal and provincial levels, and intergovernmental relations. The goal is to promote and strengthen local government for democracy and development. Past activities include conducting research on issues relevant to local governments and disseminating the results through publications. The centre has also hosted training workshops, seminars, conferences, and undertaken consultancies for various local governments and the national department responsible for coordinating local governments and intergovernmental relations. This grant will support the continuation of these research activities and the provision of technical assistance to local and provincial governmental entities and civil society organizations interacting with local municipalities.

title: Community Law Centre - Local Democracy, Peace, and Human Security Project
description: The local government project of the Community Law Centre, located at the University of the Western Cape, focuses on providing research, advice, education, and training around issues of government decentralization, governance practices at the local municipal and provincial levels, and intergovernmental relations. The goal is to promote and strengthen local government for democracy and development. Past activities include conducting research on issues relevant to decentralization and local governance and disseminating the results through publications. The center has also hosted training workshops, seminars, and conferences, and has undertaken consultancies for various local governments and the national department responsible for coordinating local governments and intergovernmental relations. Over the last few years, the project has expanded to work in various countries across the African continent on issues of decentralization, peace, and security. This grant will support the continuation of these research activities and the provision of technical assistance to local and provincial governmental entities and civil society organizations interacting with local municipalities.

title: Community Law Centre - Multi-Level Government Initiative
description: The University of the Western Cape was established in 1960 by the apartheid government to serve the colored population in the Western Cape province of South Africa. The Multi-Level Government Initiative is a project of the Community Law Centre, located within the University of the Western Cape. The project supports governments, donors, scholars, and civil society organizations to establish local governments and other state institutions that promote peace, development, and the rule of law in Africa. Past activities included providing policy and technical advice and assistance on a range of issues related to local governance and decentralization to national, provincial, and local government structures. The center has also conducted research on the socioeconomic and service delivery obligations of local government in South Africa and published the results widely in national and international publications. This grant will support the continuation of research and the development of tools that will be used to gather data on various topics related to decentralization.

title: Community Law Centre - Multi-Level Government Initiative
description: The University of the Western Cape was established in 1960 to serve the colored population of the Western Cape Province in South Africa. The multilevel government initiative is a project of the Community Law Centre at the university to support governments, scholars, and civil society to research, design, and implement systems of multilevel government and the rule of law in South Africa. It strengthens national, provincial, and local government through targeted and evidence-based interventions. Past support has enabled the center to provide policy and technical advice to the government on issues related to governance. This grant will enable the center to continue to provide support to government and to conduct studies to measure the frequency of service delivery protests and the levels of compliance with legislative norms by provincial and local governments. The center will also improve available tools for gathering data on multilevel government and make information available through public lectures, seminars, and workshops.

title: Community Law Centre - Multi-Level Government Initiative
description: The University of the Western Cape was established in 1960 to provide tertiary education to the colored population of the Western Cape Province in South Africa. The multilevel government initiative is a project of the Dullar Omar Institute based at the law faculty of the university. It is a multidisciplinary research initiative that focuses on governance challenges within the state, and develops tools to measure government’s performance at local, provincial, and national levels. Past support has enabled the Dullar Omar Institute to develop several barometers that measure government performance and delivery. This grant will enable the institute to consolidate the barometers into one comprehensive instrument that will be used to produce data on an array of issues.

title: Building Accountability Capacity in the Not-for-Profit Sector to Enhance Corporate Governance
description: The Accountability Institute South Africa provides training, capacity building, and organizational support to nonprofits in South Africa, focusing on issues of accountability, reporting, and governance. The institute has worked closely with selected nonprofits to put in place proper financial and accountability systems to improve their governance and reporting. This renewal grant will enable the grantee to build on the lessons learned and experiences gained, and to continue to implement its accountability model with civil society organizations in South Africa, including Mott grantees. The Accountability Institute South Africa will focus on issues of strategy, structure, systems, staffing, and skills, in addition to questions of accountability, reporting, and governance.

title: General Purposes
description: Drawing inspiration from City Year USA, City Year South Africa was established to mobilize the youth of South Africa to contribute to the upliftment of poor and marginalized communities and promote development. Recruited from a cross-section of youth representing all the racial, ethnic, and religious groups in the country, City Year South Africa service leaders participate in an intensive, yearlong volunteering program, aimed at addressing South Africa’s main needs and challenges. Mostly, the youth leaders have worked in schools in poor, black townships in Johannesburg and Soweto, providing instruction, after-school programs, and support to school children from historically disadvantaged backgrounds. This grant will continue to support the general purposes of the organization, including support for City Year South Africa’s youth service program, as well as the expansion of this program to other poor communities in the Gauteng province.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant continues support to City Year South Africa, an organization that focuses on encouraging the national youth service movement by training young adults, ages 18-25, and providing them with service opportunities at schools and in their local communities. Upon completion of their 10-month program, participants are assisted with job placement, additional vocational training, and other educational opportunities. Achievements over the past year include graduating 356 participants, providing service to 4,400 children in afterschool programs, engaging more than 9,600 children in other programs and activities, and completing 11 special service days in which community work projects were implemented. Future plans include diversifying the pool of applicants, increasing focus on literacy and personal development, improving service activities that concentrate on education and the environment, and developing a similar training and service program for younger, high school-age students.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Northern Cape, Province of, Western Cape, Province of the
description: The Dioceses of Oudtshorn, Cape Town, Keimos, Upington, and De Aar, mainly rural towns in the Western and Northern Cape, came together to establish a rural development agency — DOCKDA Rural Development Agency — to serve as a conduit for funding small projects in these rural areas. Mott provided support to develop and strengthen it as an indigenous, intermediary grantmaker to fund rural development organizations in these poor and marginalized communities. With Mott’s support, DOCKDA Rural Development Agency has been able to enhance its development role, providing funding, capacity building, monitoring, and support to community-based organizations in many of the poorest rural areas in the country. Mott’s renewal grant will continue to support the general operational, institutional, and staff costs of the organization, as it works to find ways to assist rural communities to become more empowered and self-reliant.

title: General Purposes
description: DOCKDA Rural Development Agency is an intermediary grantmaker that supports the work of rural development organizations in poor, marginalized communities. Over the last two years, it worked with home-based care organizations in the Northern Cape Province, strengthening organizational capacity, mentoring the leaders of these organizations, and assisting with fundraising. It trained 135 adults in various areas including basic administration, tourism, and computers to improve their chances of finding employment. The grantee will continue to work with rural communities in the Northern Cape Province to build civil society and citizen capacity to achieve gender equality, enhance strategies to prevent gender-based violence, and reduce the spread and impact of HIV/AIDS. The agency will make grants to community-based organizations and empower unemployed adults in rural areas through education and skills development.

title: General Purposes
description: DOCKDA Rural Development Agency is an intermediary grantmaker that supports rural development organizations in poor, marginalized communities in the Northern Cape province of South Africa. Over the past two years, the grantee developed a program to strengthen community responses to various development challenges, in particular, the AIDS epidemic, in the rural areas of the Northern Cape province. It strengthened leadership and worked in collaboration with leaders from community-based organizations to ensure that the interventions were relevant for the needs of the communities served. This grant will continue to provide general purpose support to the grantee. The main activities over the next two years will include grantmaking to organizations that facilitate programs on gender equality; promoting health and wellness within target communities; and mentoring small community-based organizations that provide home-based care to terminally ill patients, particularly those with AIDS.

title: General Purposes
description: DOCKDA Rural Development Agency is an intermediary grantmaker that supports community-based organizations in poor communities in the Northern Cape province of South Africa. Over the past two years, the grantee trained community-based organizations to respond to challenges such as the high prevalence of HIV, food security, and gender-based violence. It also provided mentorship support to leaders of these organizations and created opportunities for mutual learning among them. The grantee will continue to develop its knowledge of the social issues it tries to address through staff training; making grants to community-based organizations in the Northern Cape province and supporting their efforts to secure funds from the government and the private sector; and training and mentoring organizations that deliver programs on health and wellness, and gender equality.

title: General Purposes
description: DOCKDA Rural Development Agency is a community grantmaker that supports community-based organizations working in the Northern Cape Province in South Africa. It provides capacity development training and makes grants to women-led organizations that respond to various social issues in their communities. Previous support has enabled the grantee to make grants, train and mentor leaders of community-based organizations, and conduct workshops on matters affecting the communities. In addition, the grantee partnered with the government to create employment opportunities for women living in rural areas. This grant will support the grantee to continue to make grants and provide training to community-based organizations on various topics including life skills and health. It will also bring together community-based organizations to discuss issues that are most prevalent in their communities such as substance abuse and gender-based violence to find a common solution.

title: General Purposes
description: DOCKDA Rural Development Agency is a community grantmaker that supports community-based organizations working in the Northern Cape Province in South Africa. It makes small grants and provides capacity development training to organizations working in the John Taolo Gaetsewe district in Kuruman, Northern Cape. Previous support enabled the grantee to provide training to community-based organizations in the district, conduct research on topical issues affecting the communities it serves, and set up a field office in the village of Batlharos to improve access. This grant will support the grantee to continue providing training to leaders of community-based organizations, making grants in response to various needs in the communities it serves, and implementing programs that promote gender equity. The grantee will also work with schools to provide training on topics related to the personal and social well being of students.

title: General Purposes
description: The Harold Wolpe Memorial Trust focuses on fostering debate and discussion, especially as this relates to the strengthening of civil society as a critical and independent voice in promoting democracy in South Africa. The sector’s preoccupation with leadership and succession issues, in addition to facing funding shortfalls, has unfortunately meant that not much debate or discussion is taking place on the challenges that it needs to confront as the country enters the second decade of its nonracial democracy. Mott’s prior grant to the Harold Wolpe Memorial Trust provided support for it to host talks on these critical issues, creating a space for policymakers, academics, civil society activists, and government officials to discuss and exchange ideas on the key questions relating to the building of democracy in South Africa and the role of civil society. The grant further supported the dissemination and publication of these talks and debates to ensure the involvement and participation of a wider and more diverse audience. This grant will continue to support the work, activities, and programs of the grantee, including an evaluation which will look at how effective it has been and the impact it is having.

title: General Purposes
description: The Harold Wolpe Memorial Trust focuses on fostering debate and discussion, especially as this relates to the strengthening of civil society as a critical and independent voice in promoting democracy in South Africa. This grant increase will enable the trust to hold an open dialogue series in Cape Town, focusing on topics related to the political climate in South Africa and the need to strengthen democracy at this time in the country’s history.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support the work, activities, and programs of the Harold Wolpe Memorial Trust. The trust focuses on fostering critical and intellectual thinking, debate, and discussion, especially as this relates to the strengthening of civil society as a critical and independent voice in promoting democracy in South Africa. Through its open dialogues, lectures, and seminars held throughout the country, policymakers, academics, civil society activists, and government officials have the intellectual space to conduct critical dialogue, exchange ideas, and inform public debate around social, political, economic, and cultural issues facing South Africa. In addition, the trust uses its Web site and publications to disseminate the ideas and outcomes of these talks and debates to ensure the involvement and participation of a wide and diverse audience.

title: General Purposes
description: The West Coast Community Foundation makes grants and provides support and training to community organizations in the West Coast region of the Western Cape, one of the poorest and most under-resourced parts of the province. Mott provided funding for institutional, operational, and staff support to help develop the West Coast Community Foundation as a viable community foundation in the West Coast region. This grant will continue to provide such support with an emphasis on governance, resource mobilization, infrastructure development, and asset building. The grant will also assist the West Coast Community Foundation with marketing and promotion, as it seeks to build an endowment fund for its long-term sustainability.

title: General Purposes
description: The West Coast Community Foundation supports community development in the West Coast region of the Western Cape province through grants and by providing training and capacity building for community-based organizations. It serves one of the poorest and most under-resourced areas in the country. Recent efforts focused on strengthening staff, developing operational policies and procedures, conducting training workshops for local nonprofit service providers, grantmaking, and asset development planning. Future plans include partnering with local municipal governments to fund basic services, undertaking an evaluation, and asset development emphasizing increased outreach to the white Afrikaners in the area to build trust and support.

title: General Purposes
description: The West Coast Community Foundation was founded in 2001 to support community development in the West Coast district of the Western Cape Province of South Africa. It provides grants, conducts training on various topics related to community development, and facilitates networking opportunities for community-based organizations in this area. With previous Mott support, the grantee introduced an asset-based approach to encourage communities to use available resources to drive their own development and be able to hold government accountable. This renewal grant will support the foundation to continue providing training and making grants to community-based organizations in the West Coast. The foundation will also continue building networks and strengthening relations with wealthier communities to access local resources and further strengthen local communities through the asset-based, community-driven approach.

title: General Purposes
description: The West Coast Community Foundation was established in 2001 to support community development in the West Coast district of the Western Cape Province of South Africa. The grantee makes grants, conducts training on various topics related to community development, and facilitates networking opportunities for community-based organizations in this area. Previous support from the Mott Foundation assisted the grantee to promote an asset-based approach and encourage communities to use available resources to drive their own development and be able to hold government accountable. This grant increase will enable the grantee’s staff to attend a training-of-trainers program on the asset-based community development approach to strengthen its training capacity.

title: General Purposes
description: The West Coast Community Foundation promotes community-led development in poor and marginalized communities in the West Coast district of the Western Cape Province in South Africa. It makes grants to community-based organizations and provides training on various topics related to community development. Previous support from the Mott Foundation assisted the grantee to facilitate networking and fundraising opportunities for community-based organizations in this area, promote staff development through various training programs, strengthen its partnerships with other nonprofits, government, and business, and promote youth involvement in philanthropy. This grant will support the grantee to continue supporting community-based organizations and promote an asset-based approach to community development.

title: General Purposes
description: The West Coast Community Foundation was established in 1998 to support community-led development in the West Coast region of the Western Cape Province in South Africa. It makes grants and trains community-based organizations on various topics to assist them to effectively respond to development needs in their communities. Previous support enabled the grantee to make small grants, support efforts to advance community foundations in South Africa, participate in several youth philanthropy events locally and abroad, and establish an endowment fund as part of its sustainability plan. This grant will support the grantee to continue training community-based organizations, refine its grantmaking approach to ensure that it is responsive to local needs, improve communication tools to strengthen its profile and visibility, and strengthen partnerships with communities and other sectors that impact its work.

title: General Purposes
description: The West Coast Community Foundation was established in 1998 to support community-led development in the West Coast region of the Western Cape Province in South Africa. It makes grants and trains community-based organizations to respond effectively to development needs in their communities. Previous support enabled the grantee to train community-based organizations, refine its grantmaking approach to ensure that it is responsive to local needs, improve communication tools to strengthen the grantee’s profile and visibility, and strengthen partnerships with communities and other sectors that impact its work. This grant will support the continuation of these activities.

title: Local Philanthropy Social Franchise
description: This grant will support efforts of the Local Philanthropy Social Franchise program, a project of the Dobrota Foundation, to thoroughly study various community philanthropy models and approaches in Central/Eastern Europe and Russia and make internal improvements based on this learning. Activties include documenting its structure, policies, processes and procedures, obtaining International Standards Organization quality certification and replicating this model to at least two post-Soviet communities with accompanying training, mentoring and adaptation.The mission of the Dobrota Foundation is to fight poverty through the revival of public charity and the development of social partnerships in the Eastern Ukrainian city of Donetsk.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to build the capacity of Ukraine to integrate more closely with European and Euro-Atlantic structures through the application of Polish and European experience. In order to fulfill its mission, the Polish Ukrainian Cooperation Foundation “PAUCI” has identified five primary focus areas: (1) advocacy for closer integration with European and Euro-Atlantic structures; (2) implementation of administrative and local government reform processes; (3) adoption of international and European Union business standards; (4) application of internationally recognized ethical standards in public life; and (5) youth empowerment. The grantee will build on its successful operating and grantmaking programs, which included distribution of over $430,000 in grants for cross-border initiatives. Created in 2005, the foundation is the successor to the Polish-America-Ukraine Cooperation Initiative which sought to share Polish experience in market and democratic transition.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to build the capacity of Ukraine to integrate more closely with European and Euro-Atlantic structures through the application of Polish and European experience. To this end, the Polish Ukrainian Cooperation Foundation “PAUCI” has identified five primary focus areas: (1) advocacy for closer integration with European and Euro-Atlantic structures; (2) promotion of local government reform; (3) adoption of international and European Union business standards; (4) application of internationally recognized ethical standards in public life; and (5) youth empowerment. In 2008-2009, the grantee regularly convened a broad cross section of Ukrainian policymakers and civic activists in a range of training events, major international conferences, and policy-oriented workshops aimed at understanding and influencing European Union policy toward Ukraine. Created in 2005, the foundation is the successor to the Polish-America-Ukraine Cooperation Initiative, which sought to share Polish experience in market and democratic transition.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to promote public participation in government decisionmaking in Ukraine. The grantee will monitor and raise public awareness about the performance of Ukrainian parliamentarians and local governments. It will work to strengthen the capacity of local analytical centers to evaluate government performance. Results of this oversight will be widely and regularly distributed, and a specialized information service will be developed to circulate additional information of broader social interest. The grantee has successfully carried out comprehensive accountability monitoring of Ukrainian political parties and representatives, produced thousands of publicly accessible evaluation reports, and contributed to greater public understanding of the operations of the country’s democratic institutions. Since 2001, the Open Society Foundation – Ukraine has promoted participatory democracy and open society in Ukraine by actively engaging voters and civic organizations at all stages of the political process.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to promote effective public oversight and participation in government decisionmaking in Ukraine. The Open Society Foundation – Ukraine will regularly monitor and distribute findings about the performance of Ukrainian national legislative and executive authorities and political parties. The grantee will provide expertise and consulting support to regional partners focusing on local administrative and governance reform. It will also develop its own training capacity to educate local governments and nongovernmental organizations to introduce effective public participation mechanisms. During 2007-2008, the grantee refined a comprehensive methodology for monitoring Ukrainian political institutions. In addition, through a new Web site, a variety of regularly issued publications, and over 100 print and broadcast media stories, the grantee’s monitoring reports contributed to greater public awareness of the operations of the country’s democratic institutions. Since 2001, the Open Society Foundation – Ukraine has promoted participatory democracy and an open society in Ukraine.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to promote effective public oversight and participation in decisionmaking in Ukraine. The Open Society Foundation – Ukraine will regularly monitor and distribute findings about the performance of Ukrainian national legislative and executive authorities and political parties. It will support regional partners focusing on local government, with particular emphasis on mechanisms for enhancing local development strategies. The grantee will further develop its own training capacity to educate local governments and nongovernmental organizations on effective use of public participation mechanisms. During 2009-2010, the grantee successfully expanded its watchdog functions to encompass national-level executive and legislative bodies. Through a new Web site, a variety of publications, and over 100 print and broadcast media stories, the grantee’s monitoring reports contributed to greater public awareness of the operations of the country’s democratic institutions. Since 2001, the grantee has promoted participatory democracy and an open society in Ukraine.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to promote public participation in policymaking in Ukraine. The Europe XXI Foundation is a leading Ukrainian think tank whose mission is to contribute to Ukraine’s European and Euro-Atlantic integration through democratization of governance and strengthening public participation in policy development. The grantee works to strengthen the capacity, impact, and credibility of civil society organizations as contributors to the public policy process. Over the next three years, the grantee will examine and apply the lessons from the democratic transitions in its East European neighbors and the impact these transitions have had on engaging civil society in public policy dialogue. In the previous grant period, the grantee successfully concluded its first “Advocacy School” for civil society organizations, and it cohosted the fifth World Movement for Democracy conference in Kyiv. Founded in 1998, the Europe XXI Foundation facilitates public participation in the policy process as a means of securing Ukraine’s development as a European democracy.

title: General Purposes
description: The Community Development Resource Association is an organizational development nonprofit that supports other nonprofits in South Africa and internationally. Mott has supported it to share its resources, experiences, and insights of the past 17 years with the wider civil society community in South Africa. The focus is on facilitating practices and interventions that benefit poor and marginalized community-based organizations that struggle with capacity building and accessing resources. This renewal grant will continue to support the grantee to provide services to civil society organizations to help them realize their goals. The focus will remain on facilitating practices and interventions that benefit poor and marginalized communities, particularly in the areas of capacity development and accessing resources.

title: General Purposes
description: The Community Development Resource Association is one of the oldest organizations in South Africa working on strengthening nonprofit organizations. It works with development practitioners, organizations, and movements that are engaged in social transformation with poor and marginalized communities. It has provided technical assistance in organizational development to nonprofits and development agencies by conducting action research; promoting improved policies and practices; sponsoring training courses, workshops, seminars, and dialogues; and through consultancies. This grant will support the continuation of these efforts to strengthen primarily South African nonprofits at the local community, regional, and national level, as well as governmental agencies and university departments. The association will also continue to work worldwide by networking, undertaking consultancies, and sponsoring and facilitating conferences related to organizational development practices and the promotion of social change.

title: General Purposes
description: The Community Development Resource Association is a South African organization that provides organizational development support to nonprofits and development agencies throughout the world. It facilitates training courses, seminars, and dialogues for development practitioners, organizations, and movements that are engaged in social change with poor and marginalized communities. Previous Mott support assisted the grantee in launching an annual digest, documenting the experiences of development practitioners and challenges facing the sector. This grant renewal will continue to support efforts to strengthen primarily South African nonprofits at local, regional, and national levels, as well as governmental agencies and university departments and to promote a people-centered approach to development. The grantee will also continue to work worldwide by networking, undertaking consultancies and sponsoring and facilitating conferences related to organizational development practices and the promotion of social change.

title: General Purposes
description: The Community Development Resource Association provides training on organizational strengthening to nonprofits in South Africa; the southern Africa region; and on a limited basis, internationally. It works with organizations, development practitioners, and other partners to support the development of poor and marginalized communities. Past support from Mott assisted with activities including conducting workshops to support organizations going through change, leading peer learning processes and exchanges, and training development practitioners. This grant will support the grantee to continue to provide institutional training for nonprofits at a community, regional and national level; strengthen its international networks; and provide consultancy services with the support of its associates.

title: Diversity Advancement Project
description: This grant will provide continued support to the Tides Center for the Diversity Advancement Project. The goals of the project are to develop tools and resources that advocates and grassroots groups can use to generate public support for prodiversity policies and engage others to promote a more productive public discussion about the value of diversity among target constituencies. Specific work includes conducting research on contextual and environmental opportunities that create openness to discourse; developing model communication frames including messages, metaphors and symbols for use with target constituencies; creating an advisory board to guide the work; and developing a set of tools that advocates can use to improve their public education efforts to expand the base of support for race-conscious policies and programs.During the past year, specific accomplishments included meeting with advocates and community leaders from Michigan, North Carolina, California and Mississippi; convening a multi-disciplinary advisory board for the project; identifying researchers and possible organizational partners; developing criteria for site selection; identifying four possible sites for testing (Grand Rapids and Oakland County, Michigan; Denver, Colorado; California; and North Carolina); and developing a work plan that focuses on the two Michigan sites for initial testing.

title: New Philanthropists: Development of Giving
description: The program goal is to promote international private and family philanthropy. To this end, Charities Aid Foundation initiated a program to encourage high net-worth individuals from middle-income countries to become effective philanthropists. Activities include researching private and family giving among high net-worth individuals; working with relevant networks of wealth managers and financial advisors; developing donor-advised funds and support services; and providing technical assistance and advice to donors. In 2006, Charities Aid Foundation concentrated these activities in Russia, Ukraine, Brazil and Mexico, and leveraged over $20 million in new philanthropic assets. Expansion is planned for South Africa, India and China. Mott funds will continue to support the costs of one staff person and travel-related expenses.

title: New Philanthropists: Development of Giving
description: The program goal is to promote international private and family philanthropy. To this end, Charities Aid Foundation initiated a program to encourage high-net-worth individuals from middle-income countries to become effective philanthropists. Activities include researching private and family giving among high-net-worth individuals, working with relevant networks of wealth managers and financial advisors, developing donor-advised funds and support services, and providing technical assistance and advice to donors. During the first two years of the program, Charities Aid Foundation concentrated these activities in Russia, Ukraine, Brazil, and Mexico. As a result, Charities Aid Foundation has increased its client base in these countries from three to ten clients with proposed assets of $700 million and facilitated the creation of at least six new private foundations. Mott funds will continue to support the costs of one staff person and travel-related expenses.

title: New Philanthropists: Development of Giving
description: The program goal is to promote international private and family philanthropy. To this end, Charities Aid Foundation initiated a program to encourage high-net-worth individuals from middle-income countries to become effective philanthropists. Activities have included researching private and family giving among high-net-worth individuals, working with relevant networks of wealth managers and financial advisors, developing donor-advised funds and support services, and providing technical assistance and advice to donors. This grant increase will support evaluation and dissemination of project results and travel costs for international speakers at donor education courses in Russia and Brazil. Registered in 1974 as a charity in the United Kingdom, Charities Aid Foundation possesses a unique combination of charitable status and the ability to provide banking services that enables it to help donors and charities both in the United Kingdom and abroad.

title: Georgia Water Policy Project
description: Both foundations and grantee organizations need to periodically evaluate past and current work so that future efforts will be as effective as possible. In 2003, selected Mott grantees undertook such an evaluation project, producing a report that described the status of water policy reform in the Great Lakes and southeastern U.S. This grant increase will enable the Upper Chattahoochee Riverkeeper Fund, one of the original report’s authors, to update information on water management policy reform efforts in the southeastern U.S.

title: Georgia Water Policy Project
description: Georgia’s rapid population growth, combined with periods of severe drought, has put a strain on Georgia’s water resources. In response, the state recently embarked on a process that will produce Georgia’s first comprehensive, statewide water management plan. Over the past several years, the Upper Chattahoochee Riverkeeper Fund, one of the state’s largest and most effective major watershed groups, has pushed for improved water management policies at the state level. With renewal support, the riverkeeper will engage in the statewide process on a number of levels as well as assist other citizen groups that wish to participate. The riverkeeper will also seek to influence water management policies within the Atlanta metropolitan region and between Georgia and neighboring states.

title: Georgia Water Policy Project
description: Based in Atlanta, the Upper Chattahoochee Riverkeeper Fund is a leader at the local, state, and regional levels on water management policy reform efforts. With this grant increase and associated grant period extension, the riverkeeper will continue its work to help implement water-use plans for the Atlanta region, put into practice the recently adopted statewide water management plan, monitor proposals for new reservoirs, and network with partner organizations that share an interest in the Apalachicola-Chattahoochee-Flint rivers basin.

title: Georgia Water Policy Project
description: The Chattahoochee River watershed supports diverse aquatic life, but it has been stressed by multiple water demands, including from the explosive growth of metropolitan Atlanta. Record-setting droughts, coupled with conflicts over access to water from the Chattahoochee, have highlighted the need for more sustainable water management. The Upper Chattahoochee Riverkeeper works to protect and conserve the watershed by securing strong water policies at the local, state, regional, and federal levels. Over the next two years, the riverkeeper will promote sustainable water policies and programs that will ensure adequate supplies of clean water for both human and aquatic communities.

title: Georgia Water Policy Project
description: Based in Atlanta, the Upper Chattahoochee Riverkeeper is a leader at the local, state, and regional levels on water management policy reform efforts. With prior Mott support, the grantee has promoted sustainable water policies and programs that ensure adequate supplies of clean water for both human and aquatic communities. Over the next two years, the grantee will continue to engage in such work with a focus on advancing water conservation and efficiency, defining metro Atlanta’s future water needs, monitoring proposed water supply projects, and promoting healthy ecological river flows.

title: Georgia Water Policy Project
description: Based in Atlanta, the Chattahoochee Riverkeeper is a leader at the local, state, and regional levels on water management policy reform efforts. With prior Mott support, the grantee has promoted sustainable water policies and programs that ensure adequate supplies of clean water for people and nature. Over the next two years, the grantee will continue to engage in such work with a focus on advancing water conservation and efficiency, monitoring proposed water supply projects, and promoting healthy ecological river flows.

title: Beautification of City Entrances
description: This grant increase will enable the city of Flint to purchase additional mowing equipment to continue beautification and ongoing maintenance efforts around the freeway entrances and exits and along the freeway service drives that lead into the city. This cleanup and beautification work is being done to improve the appearance and public perceptions about the city, as well as contribute to the revitalization efforts under way downtown.

title: Afterschool Professional Development National Clearinghouse
description: This grant increase continues to support the Collaborative Communications Group in creating Web-based professional development resources for afterschool staff by also designing a complementary printed publication. The development of these resources is being guided by a national advisory group and via a research process that includes focus groups, peer reviews, and a survey of the afterschool field. The online resource and publication will include recommended core competencies for the afterschool profession, as well as staff supports and guidelines for identifying and accessing appropriate staff development. These tools will better help afterschool staff and directors understand and access appropriate professional development that will lead to higher quality afterschool experiences for program participants, and move toward a comprehensive professional development system for afterschool staff and directors.

title: Improving Nutrition in Afterschool Programs
description: This grant will continue to support the Food Research and Action Center to improve and expand nutrition supports in afterschool programs for school-age children. This work will help improve children’s nutrition, health, learning ability, and general well-being, while simultaneously strengthening afterschool programs. This initiative focuses on six key areas: 1) increasing access to the afterschool and summer nutrition programs; 2) developing a guide for connecting school-day and afterschool nutrition programs; 3) explaining the effects of food insecurity, poor nutrition, and obesity on mental health; 4) examining the impact of special dietary needs on food policy; 5) honoring high quality afterschool programs, which have effectively implemented strong nutrition efforts; and 6) developing a media toolkit focused on obesity and hunger and its impact on low-income children and families.

title: Principals: Leading After-School Learning Communities
grantee: National Association of Elementary School Principals Foundation
description: This grant provides continued support to the National Association of Elementary School Principals Foundation in its efforts to increase principals’ awareness of how afterschool complements school-day learning. Funding will also support the engagement of elementary school principals in ongoing conversations about their potential role in implementing concepts in “A New Day for Learning”, a Mott-funded report dedicated to helping individuals responsible for the well-being of children and youth, rethink methods of learning using afterschool as a resource. This grant will also enable the grantee to provide symposiums, workshops, and tools principals can use in working with their schools and communities.

title: Rethinking Time and Learning: Dissemination of "A New Day for Learning"
description: This grant provides continued support to the George Lucas Educational Foundation to create practical tools for enabling action related to the Mott-funded Time, Learning, and Afterschool Task Force report, “A New Day for Learning”. Specifically, video vignettes and accompanying materials will be developed and available online to facilitate dissemination and local adaptation of exemplary afterschool/extended-learning programs. In addition, new web tools will be designed to increase the accessibility and usability of products as well as using multiple web-based media platforms to further disseminate resources. This will allow teachers, administrators, afterschool stakeholders, and other interested parties to gain a firm understanding of the necessary steps to realize the vision described in “A New Day for Learning”.

title: Rethinking Time and Learning: Dissemination of "A New Day for Learning"
description: This grant provides continued support to the George Lucas Educational Foundation to create practical tools for implementing the five elements outlined in the Mott-funded Time, Learning, and Afterschool Task Force report, “A New Day for Learning”. These elements include expanding the definition of student success, using research-based knowledge about how students learn best, fostering collaboration, integrating various learning approaches and places, and providing new opportunities for leadership and professional development. Using a multimedia approach, this project will capture promising practices inside innovative schools and learning environments around the country, and develop practice tools that will allow teachers, administrators, afterschool stakeholders, and other interested parties to gain a better understanding of the steps needed to make the most use of school and community resources. This project will also add knowledge to the field by providing detailed information and tips on improving schools and will continue the development of Web-based materials that share tools for change.

title: Rethinking Time and Learning: Dissemination of "A New Day for Learning"
description: This grant will support the George Lucas Educational Foundation in its efforts to develop communications to launch the rollout of recommendations from the Task Force on Time, Learning, and Afterschool report funded by the Mott Foundation. The report, tentatively titled “A New Day for Learning,” will present the case for redefining methods of learning, using alternate conceptions of time, and supporting partnerships between schools and afterschool educators. The George Lucas Educational Foundation will produce multimedia editorial content related to the themes of the report in its magazine “Edutopia”, e-newsletters, its Web site and short documentary films. Through these channels, the coverage is expected to reach at least 250,000 education professionals.

title: A New Day for Learning Social Marketing Campaign
description: This grant will continue to support GMMB, Inc., in the implementation of a social marketing plan that will build broad-based support for the vision outlined in the 2007 Mott-funded report, “A New Day for Learning”. This grant will allow the grantee to carry out public awareness and communication activities as part of a multiyear effort to create a culture of communitywide responsibility for providing students with meaningful ways to become successful learners and citizens. Specifically, this project will build on the lessons learned from afterschool to engage policymakers, educators, and community organizations in developing a comprehensive learning system that provides students with multiple ways of learning throughout the day and year-round, anchored to high standards and aligned to educational resources. GMMB will accomplish this through customized traditional and digital media, leveraging partnerships, and using various forms of advertising to target a wide-ranging audience.

title: A New Day for Learning Social Marketing Campaign
description: This grant will continue to support GMMB, Inc., in the implementation of a social marketing plan to build broad-based support for the vision outlined in the 2007 Mott-funded report, “A New Day for Learning”. This grant will allow the grantee to carry out public awareness and communication activities as part of a multiyear effort to create a culture of communitywide responsibility for providing students with meaningful ways to become successful learners and citizens.
