Specifically, this project will build on the lessons learned from afterschool to engage policymakers, educators, and community organizations in: 1) developing comprehensive learning systems that provide students with multiple ways of learning throughout the day and year-round that are anchored to high standards; and 2) ensuring that existing and new resources are available. The grantee will accomplish this with Websites, testimonial videos, and toolkit materials to help key stakeholders educate policymakers.

title: A New Day for Learning Social Marketing Campaign
description: This grant will continue to support GMMB, Inc., to develop and implement a communications strategy aimed at educating policymakers on the 21st Century Community Learning Centers program and afterschool programs. This project will: 1) strengthen the narrative that afterschool programs provide valuable enrichment opportunities that increase academic achievement; 2) highlight the unique role of the 21st Century Community Learning Centers’ funding stream in providing innovative enrichment and academic opportunities for young people; and 3) provide strategic communications counsel and support for the Foundation’s initiative to promote best practices for afterschool and expanded learning opportunities.

title: A New Day for Learning Social Marketing Campaign
description: In January 2007, the Mott-funded Time, Learning, and Afterschool Task Force released “A New Day for Learning” report, which calls for the alignment of school-day and afterschool resources as an opportunity to develop a comprehensive learning system that provides students with multiple ways of learning throughout the day and year-round, anchored to high standards and aligned to educational resources throughout the community. This grant to GMMB will support the development of a multiyear social marketing plan, implementation of first-year activities, and the launch of an advertising campaign to build broad-based support for action on achieving “A New Day for Learning” in America. The advertising campaign will engage a number of strategies to increase public support and action for the concepts embodied in “A New Day for Learning”.

title: Detroit Area Study on Financial Services
description: This grant increase will provide additional support to the University of Michigan Law School for a study examining financial services usage patterns in Detroit. Specifically, the Detroit Area Study will survey and analyze: how and why low- and moderate-income people in the Detroit metropolitan area use certain types of financial services; the costs and benefits of such services; and how such persons might respond to new types of cost-effective financial products tailored to their needs and that experience suggests might plausibly be offered by banks, credit unions and/or thrifts. To carry out this research agenda, the law school is contracting with the university’s Survey Research Center, which is nationally renowned for its methodological and technical expertise. The resulting research will contribute to the academic literature, inform asset-building programs operating around the country, and provide guidance to federal and state policymakers about the financial services needs of low- and moderate-income households.

title: New Agenda for a New Michigan
description: This grant will enable Michigan Future, Inc., to lead a multiyear project designed to provide Michigan leaders with new ideas on how to better position Michigan for success in an increasingly knowledge-driven and entrepreneurial economy. To develop and communicate this agenda, Michigan Future, Inc., will examine characteristics of successful regions around the country and engage the state’s key thought leaders in debating which of those ideas would best help move Michigan forward. The final recommendations resulting from the series of caucuses would be synthesized and disseminated through a strategic communications plan designed to build a new, nonpartisan constituency for the proposed new agenda. Michigan Future, Inc., has assembled a diverse team of experts to implement the research agenda, and a geographically diverse leadership council to provide overall project direction.

title: New Agenda for a New Michigan
description: This grant will enable Michigan Future to continue a multiyear project designed to provide Michigan leaders with ideas on how to better position Michigan for success in an increasingly knowledge-driven and entrepreneurial economy. To develop and communicate this agenda, Michigan Future will examine characteristics of successful regions around the country and engage the state’s key thought leaders in debating which of those ideas would best help move Michigan forward. Michigan Future has assembled a diverse team of experts to implement the research agenda, and a geographically diverse leadership council to provide overall project direction.

title: New Agenda for a New Michigan
description: This grant increase will enable Michigan Future, Inc., to continue a multiyear project designed to provide Michigan leaders with ideas on how to better position Michigan for success in an increasingly knowledge-driven and entrepreneurial economy. To develop and communicate this agenda, the grantee will examine characteristics of successful regions around the country and engage the state’s key thought leaders in debating which of those ideas would best help move Michigan forward. The grantee has assembled a diverse team of experts to implement the research agenda, and a geographically diverse leadership council to provide overall project direction.

title: Smart Teachers As Role Models (STAR) Initiative
description: This renewal grant will provide support to the Phelps-Stokes Fund for the second year of development of a national clearinghouse to assist programs designed to increase the number of African-American men teaching in public elementary schools, such as the Call Me MISTER program in South Carolina. Activities in the second year of the project include convening practitioners and experts; commissioning research papers and program development materials; launching a Web-enhanced communications platform; and providing technical assistance to the program planning process in Flint, Michigan. Since its founding in 1911, the Phelps-Stokes Fund has facilitated the growth of human development by serving as an incubator to many nationally and internationally known programs and institutions, including the United Negro College Fund.

title: Smart Teachers As Role Models (STAR) National Initiative
description: This grant will provide partial support to the Phelps-Stokes Fund for the Smart Teachers As Role Models National Initiative. In recent years, a number of programs have emerged at institutions of higher education seeking to increase the number of minority men teaching in K-8 public schools. This initiative seeks to bolster these programs and promote new efforts at other institutions. Through this project, practitioners can share information, establish networks of support that will strengthen their individual programs and institutions, and have a body of research to draw upon as they, too, seek support for their programs. During the grant period, activities include further developing a Web communications platform; commissioning a series of papers; organizing a conference and series of meetings for scholars and practitioners; further developing the empowerment co-curricula; and establishing partnerships with black colleges to use the resources of the program. The Phelps-Stokes Fund, established in 1911, conducts research on human development and manages educational and international exchange programs in the United States and Liberia.

title: Research and Technical Assistance to Community Organizing Groups
description: This grant will provide partial support to the National Employment Law Project to provide research and technical assistance to community organizations working on issues related to jobs, wages, and economic development. This work, formerly housed at the Brennan Center for Justice, is responsive to requests for training and technical assistance from organizations across the United States, including many current and former Mott grantees. The focus of this project is to provide assistance to organizations working on issues of jobs, wages, and regional economic development.

title: Research and Technical Assistance to Community Organizing Groups
description: This grant will provide partial support to the National Employment Law Project to provide research and technical assistance to community organizations working on issues related to jobs, wages, and economic development. This work is responsive to requests for training and technical assistance from organizations across the United States, including many current and former Mott grantees.

title: Research and Technical Assistance to Community Organizing Groups
description: This grant will provide partial support to the National Employment Law Project to provide research and technical assistance to community organizations working on issues related to jobs, wages, and economic development. This work is responsive to requests for training and technical assistance from organizations across the United States, including many current and former Mott grantees. The focus of this project is to provide assistance to organizations working on issues of jobs and regional economic development.

title: Alternative Staffing Field Documentation Study
description: As the temporary employment services sector increasingly serves as a point of entry to employment for disadvantaged job seekers, several nonprofit workforce development organizations have developed alternative staffing organizations. These nonprofit services provide temporary employment opportunities while simultaneously addressing the clients’ barriers to employment.This grant will enable the University of Massachusetts-Boston, in partnership with Public/Private Ventures, to conduct the second year of a documentation study of four Mott-funded alternative staffing organizations. The study will provide data and information necessary to advance workforce development policy and practice related to alternative staffing programs.Activities during the first year of the study included conducting pre-demonstration site-visits;planning and coordinating the first all-site meeting; developing data collection plans; designing data collection instruments and procedures; conducting baseline site visits; providing contextual research; and initiating reporting procedures.

title: Alternative Staffing Field Documentation Study
description: This renewal grant will provide funds for the University of Massachusetts-Boston to conduct the third and final year of the Alternative Staffing Field Documentation Study. As the temporary employment services sector increasingly serves as a point of entry to employment for disadvantaged jobseekers, several nonprofit workforce development organizations have developed alternative staffing organizations. These nonprofit services provide temporary employment opportunities while simultaneously addressing the clients’ barriers to employment. The University of Massachusetts-Boston is partnering with Public/Private Ventures to conduct a documentation study of four Foundation-funded alternative staffing organizations. The study will provide data and information necessary to advance workforce development policy and practice around alternative staffing programs.

title: Caring to Change
description: The aim of Caring to Change, a project of the Aspen Institute, is to promote fresh thinking about how foundations can achieve social change by drawing on the wisdom and experience of nonprofit and foundation staff not usually involved in strategy development. Project activities and outputs will include: interviews and small group discussions with about 200 nonprofit leaders and foundation staff (with a positive overrepresentation of younger people and people of color); publications and presentations based on developing ideas regarding changes in philanthropic strategies; a retreat of about 25 senior philanthropic leaders to deliberate new foundation strategies to promote social change; a peer support group of funders applying the new strategies; status reports on resultant new foundation initiatives; a final report and comprehensive presentation package that recapitulates project ideas; and web-based and other mechanisms for broader continuing discussion.

title: Caring to Change
description: The aim of Aspen Institute’s Caring to Change project is to promote fresh thinking about how foundations can achieve social change by drawing on the wisdom and experience of nonprofit and foundation staff not usually involved in strategy development. Over the past 18 months, over 100 interviews with nonprofit leaders and foundation staff have been conducted, with a special emphasis on reaching out to younger leaders and people of color. A Web site for presenting and exchanging emerging themes and ideas has been launched, and a working paper is being drafted in advance of a February 2009 retreat of 25 senior philanthropic leaders to deliberate new foundation strategies to promote social change. A grant extension and increase will provide the time and funds necessary to promote strategies emerging from the retreat and to support an informal affinity group of funders applying the new strategies.

title: Building Capacity and Alliances for International Financial Institutions Monitoring
description: This renewal grant to Sobrevivencia, a Paraguayan nongovernmental organization, will support its continued efforts to research the potential impacts of large-scale infrastructure development in the region. Sobrevivencia will focus its work on the proposed infrastructure projects being funded through the Initiative for Regional Infrastructure Integration of South America in critical ecosystems in Paraguay and adjacent countries of Bolivia, Brazil, and Argentina. It will provide technical assistance to communities and grassroots organizations working to address the impacts of such large infrastructure projects; conduct creative community and public education activities; develop capacity in organizations working for natural resource conservation and indigenous rights throughout the Southern Cone; and participate in, and provide leadership for, international nongovernmental organization networks to reform international financial institutions. Sobrevivencia was founded in 1986 to conduct research and public education on conservation and environmental issues in Paraguay and the Southern Cone region of South America.

title: Building Capacity and Alliances for International Financial Institutions Monitoring
description: This renewal grant to Sobrevivencia, a Paraguayan nongovernmental organization, will support its efforts to increase the capacity of communities and government agencies to participate effectively in decisionmaking related to large-scale investments in infrastructure and energy in Paraguay, as well as the neighboring countries of the Paraná-Paraguay River Basin. Sobrevivencia will continue its program of technical assistance, training, and capacity building aimed at improving the design and implementation of local, national, and regional development plans, and at minimizing the negative environmental impacts of large infrastructure projects such as dams and waterways.

title: Building Capacity and Alliances for International Financial Institutions Monitoring
description: This renewal grant to Sobrevivencia, a Paraguayan nongovernmental organization, will support its efforts to increase the capacity of communities and government agencies to participate effectively in decisionmaking related to investments in infrastructure and energy in Paraguay, as well as the neighboring countries of the Plate River Basin. The grantee will continue its program of technical assistance, training, and capacity building aimed at improving the design and implementation of local, national, and regional development plans and at minimizing the negative environmental impacts of large infrastructure projects such as dams and waterways.

title: Building Capacity and Alliances for International Financial Institutions Monitoring
description: This renewal grant to the nongovernmental organization, Sobrevivencia, will support its efforts to increase the capacity of communities and government agencies to effectively engage in decisions about infrastructure and energy investments in Paraguay. Many such projects address climate change issues as well. Sobrevivencia will continue its program of technical assistance, training, monitoring, and capacity building aimed at improving development plans and at minimizing negative social and environmental impacts of large infrastructure projects, such as dams and waterways.

title: Building Capacity and Alliances for International Financial Institutions Monitoring
description: This renewal grant to Sobrevivencia, a nongovernmental organization in Paraguay, will support their work on large-scale energy and infrastructure finance in the country. The grantee helps build the capacity of impacted communities and governmental agencies to influence the flow of international finance for large hydroelectric projects and address climate change.

title: Human Rights, Environment and Accountability at International Financial Institutions
grantee: Center for Human Rights and Environment
initiative: Reform of International Finance and Trade
description: This renewal grant to the Center for Human Rights and Environment in Argentina will support its initiative to bring public and private investments into compliance with international environmental and human rights law and globally accepted environmental standards. It will focus specifically on influencing the investments made as part of the Initiative for Integration of Regional Infrastructure in South America due to the extensive environmental and social implications of these large financial flows into the region. Activities will focus on the environmental and social impacts of a major regional natural gas pipeline, as well as on assessment of existing mechanisms for public oversight of such projects and identification of new opportunities to ensure access to justice for affected communities.

title: Florida Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant to the Children’s Services Council of Florida will support the development of the Florida Statewide Afterschool Network to provide leadership to advocate for the development, enhancement, and sustainability of innovative, high quality afterschool programs and policies. This grantee is part of the fourth cohort of Mott-funded statewide afterschool networks. This renewal is an innovation grant, which continues to provide core support to the network, while also encouraging new ideas designed to build or enhance positive systemic changes that further policies and practices for school-based/school-linked afterschool programs. Each network receiving an innovation grant is expected to share lessons learned and products with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: Florida Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Children’s Services Council of Florida to coordinate the Florida Statewide Afterschool Network. In addition to continuing the network’s core work to advance afterschool programs in Florida, the network will complete a multiyear project to: 1) implement a statewide Let’s Get to Work campaign focused on increasing funding for afterschool programs; and 2) conclude the development of a Florida afterschool professional development system. To ensure that new models and best practices are incorporated nationally, the network will share lessons learned and products with the other statewide afterschool networks.

title: Florida Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Children’s Services Council of Florida which coordinates the Florida Statewide Afterschool Network. The Florida Statewide Afterschool Network will focus on building capacity for long-term success and advancing systems change for afterschool and expanded learning in Florida. Over the next three years, the network will support the development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool and expanded learning programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) developing a campaign to support increased state funding for afterschool programs; 2) creating new professional development opportunities for afterschool providers and administrators; and 3) implementing a communication and outreach strategy to raise the visibility of the network and the afterschool field.

title: Florida Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Children’s Services Council of Florida which coordinates the Florida Statewide Afterschool Network to continue development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) increasing communications activities to build public awareness about the importance of out-of-school time; 2) developing a comprehensive plan to increase resources for afterschool programs and the network; and 3) creating a Pathway to Quality workgroup to increase professional development on Florida’s quality standards for afterschool programs.

title: Oregon Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant to the Willamette Education Service District will support the development of the Oregon Statewide Afterschool Network to expand quality afterschool services for children, youth, and families throughout Oregon. This grantee is part of the fourth cohort of Mott-funded, statewide afterschool networks. This renewal is an innovation grant, which continues to provide core support to the network, while also encouraging new ideas designed to build or enhance positive, systemic changes that further policies and practices for school-based/school-linked afterschool programs. Each network receiving an innovation grant is expected to share lessons learned and products with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: Oregon Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: Oregon Association for the Education of Young Children
description: This grant will support the Oregon Association for the Education of Young Children to coordinate the Oregon Statewide Afterschool Network. In addition to continuing the network’s core work to advance afterschool programs in Oregon, it will develop and implement a comprehensive strategy to better incorporate the needs of parents into afterschool policy and programming. In addition, the network will conduct a needs assessment of the afterschool workforce. This work will also inform a new state expanded learning opportunities task force expected to be established in 2012. The network seeks to help afterschool providers and policymakers better utilize data to drive decisionmaking and to build the case for afterschool. To ensure that new models and best practices are incorporated nationally, the network will share lessons learned and products with the other statewide afterschool networks.

title: Oregon Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: Oregon Association for the Education of Young Children
description: This grant will support the Oregon Association for the Education of Young Children which coordinates the Oregon Statewide Afterschool Network. The Oregon Statewide Afterschool Network will focus on building capacity for long-term success and advancing systemic change for afterschool and expanded learning in Oregon. Over the next three years, the network will support the development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will seek to increase the quality and sustainability of expanded learning opportunities throughout the state by working to create: 1) a new statewide evaluation system for afterschool and summer programs; 2) state policies to support summer learning opportunities; and 3) partnerships with schools and colleges to accelerate dual credits in science, technology, engineering, and math for students.

title: Oregon Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: Oregon Association for the Education of Young Children
description: This grant increase to the Oregon Association for the Education of Young Children will support the Oregon Statewide Afterschool Network in hosting an institute focused on afterschool science, technology, engineering, and math for statewide afterschool networks and partners. The institute will provide participants an opportunity to share best practices and emerging models, while working with national experts at the forefront of afterschool and summer science, technology, engineering, and math programming.

title: Oregon Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: Oregon Association for the Education of Young Children
description: This grant will support the Oregon Association for the Education of Young Children which coordinates the Oregon Statewide Afterschool Network to continue development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) increasing communications activities to build public awareness about the importance of afterschool; 2) developing a comprehensive plan to engage new stakeholders and increase resources for afterschool programs; and 3) creating a digital badging system for professional development in the afterschool field.

title: Oklahoma Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant to the Oklahoma Institute for Child Advocacy supports the development of the Oklahoma Statewide Afterschool Network to ensure that quality afterschool programs are a state priority by engaging public- and private-sector support and resources. This grantee is part of the fourth cohort of Mott-funded statewide afterschool networks. This renewal is an innovation grant, which continues to provide core support to the network, while also encouraging new ideas designed to build or enhance positive systemic changes that further policies and practices for school-based/school-linked afterschool programs. Each network receiving an innovation grant is expected to share lessons learned and products with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: Oklahoma Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Oklahoma Institute for Child Advocacy to coordinate the Oklahoma Statewide Afterschool Network. In addition to continuing the network’s core work to advance afterschool in Oklahoma, it will complete a multiyear project to build an afterschool system of career and college readiness programs to develop students’ workforce skills and expose them to emerging career opportunities, particularly in science, technology, engineering, and math fields. The network seeks to leverage the resources of public and private partners to increase the potential of career success of Oklahoma’s children and strengthen the state’s economic competitiveness. To ensure that new models and best practices are incorporated nationally, the network will share lessons learned and products with the other statewide afterschool networks.

title: Oklahoma Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Communities Foundation of Oklahoma, which coordinates the Oklahoma Statewide Afterschool Network. In addition to continuing the network’s core work to advance afterschool in Oklahoma, it will complete a multiyear project to build an afterschool system of career and college readiness to develop students’ workforce skills and expose them to emerging career opportunities, particularly in the fields of science, technology, engineering, and math. The network seeks to leverage the resources of public and private partners to increase the potential of career success of Oklahoma’s children and strengthen the state’s economic competitiveness.

title: Oklahoma Statewide Afterschool Partnership
description: This grant will support partnership development among afterschool stakeholders in Oklahoma and enable the establishment of a cohesive statewide afterschool network. The Oklahoma Public School Resource Center will bring together a diverse group of key decisionmakers and supporters around issues impacting afterschool and summer learning programs. With this Oklahoma Statewide Afterschool Partnership grant, the grantee will hold a leadership convening on afterschool and organize a steering committee to develop a plan to expand afterschool opportunities in the state.

title: Oklahoma Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Oklahoma Public School Resource Center to continue a statewide afterschool network in Oklahoma. Over the next three years, the Oklahoma Statewide Afterschool Network will build a statewide coalition in support of afterschool programs and coordinate a unified vision to inform policy and quality afterschool initiatives. During this grant, the network’s initiatives and priorities will include: 1) informing and engaging key stakeholders in the network; 2) assessing afterschool programs throughout Oklahoma; and 3) creating a communications plan to raise awareness of the afterschool field and the network.

title: Oklahoma Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Oklahoma Public School Resource Center, which coordinates the Oklahoma Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) developing a comprehensive communications and outreach plan about the importance of afterschool; 2) convening an afterschool and business consortium to support work experience for youth; 3) creating a coordinated data management and sharing system for the afterschool field; and 4) participating in the development and distribution of new afterschool program content in collaboration with the Foundation’s thematic partners.

title: Maine Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will continue to support the University of Maine at Farmington to develop the Maine Statewide Afterschool Network to facilitate the creation of quality, affordable afterschool programming that meets the needs of families. This grantee is part of the fourth cohort of Mott-funded, statewide afterschool networks. This renewal is an innovation grant, which continues to provide core support to the network, while also encouraging new ideas designed to build or enhance positive, systemic changes that further policies and practices for school-based/school-linked afterschool programs. Each network receiving an innovation grant is expected to share lessons learned and products with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: Maine Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the University of Maine at Farmington to coordinate the Maine Statewide Afterschool Network. In addition to continuing the network’s core work to advance afterschool programs in Maine, it will complete a multiyear project to establish a system of credit attainment for school-linked, afterschool opportunities. The network seeks to create a model for standards-based, school-linked, afterschool programs that provide youth with personalized learning opportunities and credit toward graduation in afterschool settings. To ensure that new models and best practices are incorporated nationally, the network will share lessons learned and products with the other statewide afterschool networks.

title: Maine Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the University of Southern Maine which coordinates the Maine Statewide Afterschool Network. The Maine Statewide Afterschool Network will focus on building capacity for long-term success and advancing systems change for afterschool and expanded learning in Maine. Over the next three years, the network will support the development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool and expanded learning programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) developing afterschool policy connecting to the school day; 2) developing a financing plan for school-based and school-linked afterschool programs; and 3) creating a statewide system of evaluation.

title: Maine Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the University of Southern Maine which coordinates the Maine Statewide Afterschool Network to continue development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) increasing communications activities to build public awareness about the importance of afterschool; 2) increasing dedicated afterschool resources through new partnerships with businesses, philanthropy, schools, and communities; and 3) further developing afterschool quality systems, including the Quality Rating and Improvement System in Maine.

title: Smart Teachers As Role Models (STAR) Initiative
description: This grant will provide support for the Flint Smart Teachers as Role Models Initiative, which focuses on providing a leadership development curriculum for students in a teacher education program at Mott Community College, Baker College, and University of Michigan-Flint, in order to address the scarcity of African-American male teachers in the elementary and secondary schools of Flint and Genesee County. This funding will support the implementation of the initiative in each of the local colleges with educational degree programs. The program is part of a larger national replication effort, based on the Call Me MISTER program, also funded by the Foundation, to provide educational support and assistance to male students of color pursuing a career in K-12 education.

title: Smart Teachers As Role Models (STAR) Initiative
description: This grant to Mott Community College will provide support for the second cohort of students participating in the Smart Teachers as Role Models Initiative. The program provides leadership development curriculum for students in the teacher education programs at Mott Community College, Baker College, and University of Michigan-Flint to address the scarcity of African-American male teachers in the elementary and secondary schools of Flint and Genesee County. The program is part of a larger national replication effort, based on the Call Me MISTER program, also funded by the Foundation, to provide educational support and assistance to male students of color pursuing a career in K-12 education.

title: Smart Teachers As Role Models (STAR) Initiative
description: This renewal grant will provide support for the third cohort of students participating in the Smart Teachers as Role Models (STAR) Initiative. The program provides leadership development curriculum for students in the teacher education programs at Mott Community College, Baker College, and University of Michigan-Flint to address the scarcity of African-American male teachers in the elementary and secondary schools of Flint and Genesee County. The program evolved as part of a larger national replication effort, based on the Call Me MISTER program that was funded by the Foundation, to provide educational support and assistance to African-American male students pursuing a career in K-12 education at Clemson University in Clemson, South Carolina.

title: Smart Teachers As Role Models (STAR) Initiative
description: This renewal grant will provide support for the fourth cohort of students participating in the Smart Teachers As Role Models (STAR) Initiative. The program provides leadership development curriculum for students in the teacher education programs at Mott Community College, Baker College, and the University of Michigan-Flint to address the scarcity of African-American male teachers in the elementary and secondary schools of Flint and Genesee County.

title: Smart Teachers As Role Models (STAR) Initiative
description: This renewal grant will provide support for the fifth cohort of students participating in the Smart Teachers As Role Models (STAR) Initiative. The program provides leadership development curriculum for students in the teacher education programs at Mott Community College, Baker College, and the University of Michigan-Flint to address the scarcity of African-American male teachers in the elementary and secondary schools of Flint and Genesee County.

title: Smart Teachers as Role Models (STAR) Initiative
description: Based on the Call Me Mister program at Clemson University, Smart Teachers as Role Models (STAR) Initiative is a Flint replication of the Clemson model, which was designed to increase the number of African-American and Latino male teachers in urban districts. In its seventh year, the program is a collaboration between Baker College, Mott Community College, and University of Michigan-Flint. Using a cohort model, it is designed to teach specific educational strategies, career planning, and classroom management which will enable the participants to become model teachers and administrators in Flint area elementary and secondary schools.

title: Smart Teachers as Role Models (STAR) Initiative
description: This grant will enable Mott Community College to continue to administer the Smart Teachers as Role Models (STAR) Initiative. Modeled after the Call Me Mister program at Clemson University, the initiative is aimed at increasing the number of African-American and Latino male teachers in Flint area elementary and secondary schools. The initiative is a collaboration between Baker College, Mott Community College, and the University of Michigan-Flint and is designed to provide participants in formal teaching education and certification programs at partnering institutions with added supports to ensure that they are prepared to teach in local area K-12 classrooms. Recommended support will enable Mott Community College to continue the replication and implementation of the program design.

title: Smart Teachers as Role Models (STAR) Initiative
description: This grant will enable Mott Community College to continue to administer the Smart Teachers as Role Models (STAR) Initiative. Modeled after the Call Me Mister program at Clemson University, the initiative is aimed at increasing the number of African-American and Latino male teachers in Flint area elementary and secondary schools. The initiative is a collaboration between Baker College, Mott Community College, and the University of Michigan-Flint and is designed to provide participants in teaching education programs with professional development supports to ensure that they are prepared to teach in K-12 classrooms. Recommended support will allow the grantee to continue the replication and implementation of the Smart Teachers as Role Models Initiative.

title: Smart Teachers as Role Models (STAR) Initiative
description: This grant will enable Mott Community College to continue to administer the Smart Teachers as Role Models Initiative. Modeled after the Call Me Mister program at Clemson University, the Smart Teachers as Role Models Initiative is aimed at increasing the number of African-American and Latino male teachers in Flint area elementary and secondary schools. The initiative is a collaboration between Baker College, Mott Community College, and the University of Michigan-Flint and is designed to provide participants in teacher education programs with professional development supports to ensure that they are prepared to teach in K-12 classrooms.

title: Smart Teachers As Role Models (STAR) Planning Initiative
description: The Smart Teachers As Role Models (STAR) program, administered by the Phelps-Stokes Fund of Washington, D.C., was developed to recruit, train, certify and secure teaching positions for African-American men. The program, which began as a local initiative at Clemson University in South Carolina, seeks to build upon its experiences and develop a national network. Representatives of Mott Community College (MCC), Baker College and the University of Michigan-Flint began discussions about developing a local replication of the Smart Teachers As Role Models program in order to address the shortage of male, African-American, K-8 teachers in Genesee County. This grant will support the initial planning of a local replication of the STAR program.MCC – opened in 1923 as Flint Junior College – currently serves more than 16,000 students at its various campuses and extension centers in Genesee, Lapeer, Shiawassee and Tuscola counties. It will serve as the host agency for this initiative and provide office space, project supervision and grant development resources.

title: Home Program for Vulnerable Populations
description: Many owner-occupied homes that provide stability for neighborhoods are owned by senior citizens with fixed incomes. To ensure that they retain home ownership and unlock the value of their asset, the Federal Housing Administration and Fannie Mae have created the Reverse Mortgage Program. This program enables senior citizens to borrow against the equity of their homes and remain in them for the rest of their lives. Lenders recover their principal, plus interest, when the home is sold.Since many fixed-income senior citizens in the City of Flint fall short of the federal eligibility requirements, this grant will enable Metro Housing Partnership to help them gain eligibility for the Reverse Mortgage Program through a short-term loan fund. In turn, this fund will allow more senior citizens to access the benefits of the Reverse Mortgage program. The repayment of the short-term loan will be a fraction of the payment that would be owed on a conventional second mortgage.The mission of Metro Housing Partnership, founded in 1992, is “to serve as a leader and catalyst to expand and enhance quality housing initiatives in Flint and Genesee County.”

title: Family Child Care Provider Network
description: This renewal grant to 4C Child Care Unlimited will provide funds for the implementation of home-based childcare businesses for women transitioning from welfare to self-sufficiency in Genesee County. The goal of the project is to help welfare recipients become financially self-sufficient by offering early childhood professional development and business opportunities. Additionally, the project will provide other welfare-to-work participants with safe and affordable childcare options. This project is being developed in partnership with the Michigan Department of Human Services.

title: Family Child Care Provider Network
description: This grant to 4C Child Care Unlimited will provide funds for the continuation of the Family Child Care Provider Network in Genesee County. This program helps welfare recipients become financially self-sufficient by providing training and supportive services as they develop and implement licensed childcare businesses in their own homes. To date, the program has trained 11 participants — four are licensed and open for business, another four are licensed and looking for appropriate housing, and the other three are working toward licensing. During this grant period, Family Child Care Provider Network plans to provide training to eight additional individuals and increase the number of quality childcare placements in the community by 48 children.

title: Family Child Care Provider Network
description: The goal of the Family Child Care Provider Network is to help welfare recipients become financially self-sufficient by offering early childhood professional development and business opportunities. This grant will enable 4C Child Care Unlimited to provide funds for the planning and development of home-based, child-care businesses for women transitioning from welfare to self-sufficiency in Genesee County. Additionally, the project will provide other welfare-to-work participants with safe and affordable child-care options. This project is being developed in partnership with the Michigan Department of Human Services and the Michigan Department of Labor and Economic Growth.4C Child Care Unlimited is a resource, referral, training and advocacy agency established in 1970 in response to community concerns about child care.

title: Evaluation of the Genesee Health Plan
description: This grant increase will allow Health Management Associates to complete a more thorough impact analysis that will assess the effects of expanded health coverage for Genesee County residents through the Genesee Health Plan, using a variety of quantitative and qualitative indicators. Healthcare coverage for the uninsured will be measured in terms of its impact on community economics and stability.

title: CEENERGI - Central and Eastern European Network for Responsible Giving
geographic_focus: Hungary, Poland, Russia, Romania, Ukraine, Slovakia, Czech Republic, Bulgaria
description: The project goal is to increase the level and effectiveness of corporate giving in Central and Eastern Europe. To this end, donors’ fora in Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, Romania, and Slovakia will establish and further develop the Central and Eastern European Network for Responsible Giving. The network addresses a number of critical issues associated with corporate giving both at national and regional levels, including current low levels of corporate contributions to the nonprofit sector, ineffective grantmaking practices, and a lack of collaboration between corporate donors and the rest of the philanthropic community. This grant increase provides additional funds to expand the network and carry out activities in Ukraine.

title: CEENERGI - Central and Eastern European Network for Responsible Giving
geographic_focus: Ukraine, Romania, Slovakia, Russia, Poland, Czech Republic, Hungary, Bulgaria
description: The project goal is to increase the level and effectiveness of corporate giving in Central/Eastern Europe. To this end, donors forums in Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, Romania and Slovakia will establish and further develop the Central and Eastern European Network for Responsible Giving. The network addresses a number of critical issues associated with corporate giving both at national and regional levels. Additional funding will support efforts to expand the network and carry out activities in Ukraine, Hungary and Poland.

title: CEENERGI - Central and Eastern European Network for Responsible Giving
geographic_focus: Russia, Czech Republic, Poland, Hungary, Bulgaria, Ukraine, Slovakia
description: The project goal is to increase the level and effectiveness of corporate giving in Central and Eastern Europe. To this end, donors’ fora in Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, and Slovakia will continue cooperating within CEENERGI – Central and Eastern European Network for Responsible Giving, which is an informal network of donor associations in the region. During the grant period, Czech Donors Forum will address a number of critical issues associated with corporate giving, both at national and regional levels, including current low levels of corporate contributions to the nonprofit sector, ineffective grantmaking practices, and a lack of collaboration between corporate donors and the rest of the philanthropic community. Since its establishment in 2005, the network has carried out a series of activities, both at national and regional levels, including researching corporate philanthropy, promoting good practice in corporate giving, and providing technical assistance to corporations on their philanthropic programs.

title: CEENERGI - Central and Eastern European Network for Responsible Giving
geographic_focus: Russia, Bulgaria, Poland, Ukraine, Czech Republic, Slovenia, Hungary
description: The project goal is to increase the level and effectiveness of corporate and individual giving in Central and Eastern Europe. To this end, donors’ fora in Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, Russia, Slovakia, and Ukraine will continue cooperating within CEENERGI – Central and Eastern European Network for Responsible Giving, which is an informal network of donor associations in the region. Czech Donors Forum will address a number of critical issues associated with corporate giving both at the national and regional levels, including current low levels of corporate contributions to the nonprofit sector and a lack of collaboration between corporate donors and the rest of the philanthropic community. In addition, the grantee will explore ways of encouraging systematic and effective individual giving in the region. In 2008-2009, the grantee produced research on corporate philanthropy, promoted good practice in corporate giving, and provided technical assistance to corporations on their philanthropic programs.

title: Ontario Freshwater Learning Network
description: Most freshwater conservation nonprofits in Ontario are all-volunteer or lightly staffed. For the conservation community to be effective, such organizations must become strong and stable. This grant will enable the Sustainability Network to help build the capacity of such conservation groups through a series of three leadership development retreats to be held during the next two years. Approximately 15 leaders will participate, drawn primarily from organizations engaged in implementing new source water protection rules. The network also will offer three shorter management workshops for larger audiences of freshwater conservation leaders.The Sustainability Network, established in 2003, provides management assistance and training to the nonprofit environmental community in Canada.

title: Global Freshwater Team
geographic_focus: Michigan, Pennsylvania, Indiana, Georgia, New York, Tennessee, Minnesota, Illinois, Ohio, Wisconsin
description: The Nature Conservancy’s Global Freshwater Team, formerly called the Sustainable Waters Program, provides technical assistance on protecting natural river flows. With this grant increase, and associated one-year extension, the team will develop technical tools and provide assistance to partners in the Great Lakes and southeastern United States.

title: Global Freshwater Team
geographic_focus: Michigan, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Illinois, Minnesota, Ohio, Indiana, Georgia, New York, Tennessee
description: Hydrologic alteration, the byproduct of many human activities that modify natural hydrological systems, is considered to be one of the greatest and fastest-growing threats to river ecosystems. At the same time, there are important opportunities in both the Great Lakes and southeastern states to make lasting improvements to programs that protect environmentally beneficial river flows.This grant will enable the Sustainable Waters Program of The Nature Conservancy (TNC) to work with TNC state chapters and other non-governmental organizations to develop model water management approaches and apply them in specific Great Lakes and southeastern states.Founded in 1951, TNC is a private, international conservation group. Its mission is to preserve plants, animals and natural communities that represent the diversity of life by protecting the lands and water they need to survive.

title: Arkansas Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant to Arkansas State University will support the development of the Arkansas Statewide Afterschool Network to establish a structure that improves outcomes for children and youth through school-based/school-linked afterschool programs. This grantee is part of the fourth cohort of Mott-funded statewide afterschool networks. This renewal is an innovation grant, which continues to provide core support to the network, while also encouraging new ideas designed to build or enhance positive, systemic changes that further policies and practices for school-based/school-linked afterschool programs. Each network receiving an innovation grant is expected to share lessons learned and products with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: Arkansas Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Arkansas State University to coordinate the Arkansas Statewide Afterschool Network. In addition to continuing the network’s core work to advance afterschool in Arkansas, the network will complete a multiyear project that will implement key recommendations of the Governor’s Task Force on Afterschool and Summer Programs. This will include: 1) establishing out-of-school time leadership academies in five regions of the state to expand afterschool opportunities; and 2) conducting a fiscal mapping project to identify state and local resources that can be used to fund quality afterschool and summer programs. To ensure that new models and best practices are incorporated nationally, the network will share lessons learned and products with the other statewide afterschool networks.

title: Arkansas Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Arkansas State University which coordinates the Arkansas Statewide Afterschool Network. The Arkansas Statewide Afterschool Network will focus on building capacity for long-term success and advancing systems change for afterschool and expanded learning in Arkansas. Over the next three years, the network will support the development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool and expanded learning programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) implementing a communications strategy to promote afterschool in Arkansas; 2) providing standardized professional development opportunities for afterschool practitioners; and 3) expanding the quality improvement models for afterschool programs.

title: Arkansas Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Arkansas State University which coordinates the Arkansas Statewide Afterschool Network to continue development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) increasing communications activities to build public awareness about the importance of out-of-school time; 2) increasing dedicated out-of-school time funding through new partnerships with business and philanthropy; and 3) expanding and activating local and regional out-of-school time coalitions to serve as hubs for professional development and partnerships.

title: Wisconsin Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: Marshfield Clinic Research Institute, a Division of Marshfield Clinic, Inc.
description: This grant to the Marshfield Clinic Research Foundation will support the development of the Wisconsin Statewide Afterschool Network to connect key decisionmakers and resources to establish a statewide structure that fosters policies supporting high quality afterschool programs. This grantee is part of the fourth cohort of Mott-funded statewide afterschool networks. This renewal is an innovation grant, which continues to provide core support to the network, while also encouraging new ideas designed to build or enhance positive systemic changes that further policies and practices for school-based/school-linked afterschool programs. Each network receiving an innovation grant is expected to share lessons learned and products with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: Wisconsin Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: Marshfield Clinic Research Institute, a Division of Marshfield Clinic, Inc.
description: This grant will support the Marshfield Clinic Research Foundation to coordinate the Wisconsin Statewide Afterschool Network. In addition to continuing the network’s core work to advance afterschool programs in Wisconsin, it will: 1) complete a multiyear project to create a comprehensive statewide system of professional development for school-age afterschool programs; and 2) pilot a comprehensive afterschool model with the Green Bay Area School District. The network seeks to ensure that afterschool programs across the state are of high quality and meet the needs of diverse populations. The network will share best practices, new models, and lessons learned with the other statewide afterschool networks.

title: Wisconsin Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: Marshfield Clinic Research Institute, a Division of Marshfield Clinic, Inc.
description: This grant will support Marshfield Clinic Research Foundation which coordinates the Wisconsin Statewide Afterschool Network. The Wisconsin Statewide Afterschool Network will focus on building capacity for long-term success and advancing systems change for afterschool and expanded learning in Wisconsin. Over the next three years, the network will support the development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool and expanded learning programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) expanding relationships with school-based and school-affiliated afterschool programs; 2) placing AmeriCorps members in programs to implement the afterschool case management system; and 3) developing new training and technical assistance opportunities for afterschool professionals.

title: Wisconsin Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: Marshfield Clinic Research Institute, a Division of Marshfield Clinic, Inc.
description: This grant will support the Marshfield Clinic Research Institute which coordinates the Wisconsin Statewide Afterschool Network to continue development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) increasing communications activities to build public awareness about the importance of afterschool; 2) developing a comprehensive plan to increase resources for afterschool programs and the network; and 3) developing tools and resources for afterschool programs on trauma-informed care, adverse childhood experience, and behavioral guidance.

title: Working Poor Families Project
description: The Working Poor Families Project (WPFP) was designed to educate the broad public, as well as key stakeholders, about how state workforce development policies and practices can benefit working poor adults.This grant will enable WPFP to extend their work to five new states. These states will use the framework of indicators to enhance their capacity to educate state policymakers and to identify specific conditions and areas for improvement. Each new state will produce a final State Policy Assessment Report that presents data and analyses on key conditions and policies as well as offers recommendations and an overall agenda for strengthening state policies. In addition, the project will continue to partner with 20 state organizations that have completed their first year in WPFP and produced a State Policy Assessment Report.During the past year, WPFP engaged nonprofit organizations in four new states and continued working with the original 16 states; generated national and state data; convened two cross-state meetings and one policy academy; produced a policy brief; and developed working relationships with important national state policy initiatives such as the National Governor’s Association Sector Academy.

title: Working Poor Families Project
description: The purpose of this grant renewal for the Working Poor Families Project is to strengthen state policies that support and facilitate the economic advancement of low-income working families. During the course of the grant period, Brandon Roberts + Associates will work with 24 states, conduct a learning academy on state economic development policy, and produce a national report highlighting the extent and conditions of low-income working families in the United States and recent changes to their conditions.

title: Working Poor Families Project
description: Brandon Roberts + Associates’ Working Poor Families Project is designed to educate the broad public, as well as key stakeholders, on how state workforce development policies and practices can benefit working poor adults. Its purpose is to strengthen state policies that support and facilitate the economic advancement of low-income working families.

title: Working Poor Families Project
description: This grant renewal to Brandon Roberts + Associates for the Working Poor Families Project will continue the work of 25 state-level organizations to assess the conditions of working poor families to advance toward economic self-reliance, support a national meeting of state poverty organizations, conduct a policy academy, and produce a set of state policy briefs, all of which will be aimed at improving the economic self-sufficiency of low-income working families.

title: Working Poor Families Project
description: The Working Poor Families Project of Brandon Roberts + Associates is designed to educate the public, as well as key stakeholders, on how state workforce development policies and practices can benefit working poor adults. This information provides a foundation for strengthening resources and services available to working poor adults, thus leading to improvements in their ability to succeed in the labor market. The primary goal of the project is to strengthen state policies that support and facilitate the economic advancement of low-income working families.

title: Workforce Development Opportunities for Vulnerable Youth
description: This grant increase will enable ROCA, a community-based organization in Chelsea, Massachusetts, to extend its workforce development project on vulnerable youth. ROCA’s newly piloted workforce development effort is aimed at providing training and transitional employment in the hospitality industry to high risk youth. Through the project, ROCA has assisted more than 40 high risk youth — surpassing the initial target of 20-30 young people — in acquiring the needed skills for entry and/or career advancement in the hospitality industry. Due to its success in providing these quality training and employment experiences, ROCA seeks to extend the project. With this grant increase, ROCA will strengthen its workforce and transitional employment model and provide additional opportunities to more youth in its targeted communities. Additional grant funds will also be used to increase ROCA’s capacity in integrating and implementing high quality workforce development services for vulnerable youth.

title: Community Organizing - Education Documentary
description: Women Make Movies is currently producing a documentary on community-driven school reform. The documentary was originally focused on the Oakland Community Organization in Oakland, California and the Northwest Bronx Community and Clergy Coalition in the Bronx, New York. This grant increase will support the inclusion of the Boston Parent Organizing Project. The documentary is intended for broadcast on public television and will be constructed so that shorter segments can be used for targeted audiences.

title: Community Learning Project
description: The Community Learning Project is an initiative of Community Catalyst, a Boston-based technical assistance and advocacy organization. The purpose of the Community Learning Project is to engage people with extensive experience in community organizing and community development to explore ways to build a stronger infrastructure for learning in the field of community and social change. The project has three goals: 1) training a new generation of organizational development specialists and equipping them with the knowledge and capacity to work with grassroots groups; 2) expanding university-based education on community change and organizing; and 3) developing models for reconnecting veterans of community organizing with their successors to provide mentoring, training, and support.

The purpose of this grant increase is to take advantage of new opportunities to expand the original scope of work to additional sites.

title: Westwood Heights Housing Initiative
description: This grant will enable Genesee County Habitat for Humanity to participate in the Westwood Heights Housing Initiative, a collaborative effort among several local units of government and several nonprofit organizations to provide housing and community development resources for a mixed-income neighborhood in Mt. Morris Township. Genesee County Habitat for Humanity will construct five homes to the total collaborative goal of 31 new or rehabilitated homes in Westwood Heights. The collaborative may serve as a model for delivering concentrated housing and neighborhood development resources in Flint and Genesee County.Genesee County Habitat for Humanity is one of more than 1,900 affiliates of Habitat for Humanity International.

title: General Purposes
description: GreaterGood South Africa created an interactive Web site and portal dedicated to promoting a culture of philanthropy and giving in South Africa. The site serves as a conduit to unlock and channel resources for development. Through it, individuals and businesses can contribute funds, resources, time, or expertise to a diverse range of civil society organizations involved in tackling the many challenges that South Africa faces. The site also provides for nonprofit and community-based organizations to profile themselves and to make requests for resources for their various activities, projects, and programs. In its relatively short period of existence, it has already made a significant contribution to strengthening local philanthropy, winning many prizes for its innovative approach to resource mobilization. This grant will continue to provide institutional and administrative support to GreaterGood South Africa to develop, extend, and promote the Web site and portal, as well as enhance its local philanthropy work.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide continued general purpose support to GreaterGood South Africa, a Web-based, interactive portal site committed to promoting a culture of philanthropy and giving in South Africa. The grantee connects social investors with the development world in meaningful and innovative ways to strengthen civil society, eradicate poverty, promote social justice and equality, and create positive change in communities. Activities over the next two years will include: expanding giving channels to facilitate greater resources flowing to the development sector; reaching out to new groups of social investors; promoting socially responsible investment opportunities as alternative funding mechanisms for nonprofits and other investors; assessing the organization’s impact on giving and the social development sector; and expanding services to the corporate sector.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide continued general purpose support for GreaterGood South Africa, an organization that connects givers with good causes and promotes responsible giving by the public and the private sector. It uses a Web-based interactive portal site to promote a culture of philanthropy and giving in South Africa. The grantee has successfully connected social investors with the development world in meaningful and innovative ways that strengthen civil society, reduce poverty, promote social justice and equality, and create positive change in communities. Activities over the next two years will include transforming existing platforms into engaging tools and information hubs that South Africans and those wishing to invest in South Africa will find valuable, expanding existing leadership forums to increase knowledge sharing between civil society and corporate South Africa, and continuing to advocate and build the knowledge and practice of social impact investing by strengthening the South African Network for Impact Investing.

title: General Purposes
description: GreaterGood South Africa promotes a culture of giving in South Africa by connecting givers with good causes. It provides online giving facilities to the public and connects social investors to the development sector to strengthen civil society and promote social change. Over the last two years, the grantee continued to develop innovative ways to encourage responsible giving by the public and private sector and to build knowledge sharing between the private sector and nonprofit organizations. Activities over the next year will include refocusing and simplifying the online giving facility by partnering with organizations that specialize in online giving, consolidating all online activities to provide comprehensive information that is meaningful to those interested in the development sector, and providing support to nonprofits to enhance their ability to attract financial support and other resources.

title: Federal Budget Advocacy Project
description: This grant provides support to the State Environmental Leadership Program to assist in broad-based efforts to inform policymakers, the media, and the public about the federal deficit and implications of various proposals designed to reduce the budget deficit and/or reform the budget process. Ultimately, the goal of these efforts is to ensure that sufficient federal resources will be available in the short and long term, to address key social priorities in our country. The grantee will use Mott funds to support communication activities, technical assistance, and provide small grants to a select number of its member organizations. The State Environmental Leadership Program is a nationwide network of over 50 independent, nonprofit, public interest, multi-issue environmental advocacy organizations that work to effect strong state environmental protection policies.

title: Federal Budget Advocacy Project
description: This grant provides support to the State Environmental Leadership Program to engage state and local environmental groups in broad-based efforts to inform policymakers, the media, and the public about the federal deficit and implications of various proposals designed to reduce the budget deficit and/or reform budget processes. Ultimately, the goal of these efforts is to ensure that sufficient federal resources will be available in the short and long term to address key social priorities in our country. The grantee will use Mott funds to support communications activities and technical assistance, and to provide small grants to a select number of its member organizations. The State Environmental Leadership Program is a nationwide network of over 50 independent, nonprofit, public interest, multi-issue, environmental advocacy organizations that work to effect strong state environmental protection policies.

title: Citizens' Europe Programme
description: The program goal is to engage citizens and international partners in a constructive dialogue on the issues that shape Europe’s global future. Through this program, the Madariaga College of Europe Foundation has successfully contributed to bridging the gap between European civil society actors and European Union decisionmakers. This has been achieved through convening regular workshops and roundtables and publishing numerous books, reports, and articles on issues facing Europe. In 2008-2009, the grantee will focus on three main issue areas — engaging citizens, empowering Europe, and preventing conflicts. Established in 1998, the Madariaga College of Europe Foundation is an independent operating foundation dedicated to promoting original thinking on the role of the European Union in an era of global change.
