title: Wireless Genesee
description: Wireless and broadband technology is becoming a part of the required infrastructure for communities. Much like road, sewer and water improvements, future development will rely heavily on systems that provide more effective Internet access and other technology supports.This grant will support the research and design of Wireless Genesee, a project to create a countywide wireless system.The Genesee Chamber Foundation was created to promote the public welfare of Genesee County, including support for the Genesee Regional Chamber of Commerce.

title: NPO Institution Building Project
description: The Tiyakene Development Fund works with nonprofits in South Africa to improve their operating and management capacity. It also works on issues of strategic planning, financial management and good governance. This grant will enable the fund to continue working with nonprofits, particularly Mott grantees, on issues of financial sustainability, good governance, accountability, strategic planning, administrative systems and proper financial management.

title: NPO Institution Building Project
description: This grant will provide continued support to the Tiyakene Development Fund’s NPO Institution Building Project. Tiyakene Development Fund is an organizational development group that works with nonprofits on improving their organizational systems, financial health, and management capacity. This project was started in 2005 because of the growing number of nonprofits in South Africa that were facing organizational difficulties ranging from financial mismanagement, to poor governance, and lack of strategic focus. The program has expanded from training offered to selected nonprofits, to also include institutional supports to help nonprofits transfer the skills learned into their organizational systems and processes. Capacity-building support now consists of four components: (1) training; (2) systems development; (3) in-house support and mentoring; and (4) peer support groups.

title: Collaborative for Arab-American Philanthropy: Supporting Arab-American Empowerment through Strategic Philanthropy
grantee: Arab Community Center for Economic and Social Services (ACCESS)
description: This grant continues support to the National Network for Arab-American Communities, a national program of the Arab Community Center for Economic and Social Services. The goal is to encourage strategic philanthropy in the Arab-American community through research, training, and technical assistance; outreach activities; provision of donor services; and development of informational materials. For the next two years, focus will be on expanding outreach activities, developing toolkits for donors and professional advisors, increasing donor services, developing an online resource center, creating youth philanthropy programs, initiating giving circles, and implementing a public awareness campaign. A leadership circle of Arab-American philanthropists will continue to provide overall guidance and develop a plan to institutionalize and sustain the program.

title: Collaborative for Arab-American Philanthropy
grantee: Arab Community Center for Economic and Social Services (ACCESS)
description: This grant continues to support the Collaborative for Arab-American Philanthropy, a national program of the Arab Community Center for Economic and Social Services, a human services organization committed to the development of the Arab-American community in all aspects of its economic and cultural life. The program encourages strategic philanthropy in the Arab-American community through research, training, and technical assistance; outreach activities; provision of donor services; and development of informational materials. During this grant period, the program will focus on strengthening strategic communications through print and e-communications, developing the Leadership Circle members as philanthropic leaders by utilizing expert training, and educating and cultivating new donors through donor outreach events.

title: Center for Arab American Philanthropy
grantee: Arab Community Center for Economic and Social Services (ACCESS)
description: This grant continues support to the Center for Arab American Philanthropy, which is a national program of the Arab Community Center for Economic and Social Services. The goal is to encourage strategic philanthropy in the Arab-American community through research, training, technical assistance and development of informational materials; conduct donor outreach activities; and provide donor services such as donor-advised funds. This program is evolving into a national ethnic community foundation. Activities during the next year will include developing a communications and marketing plan; providing professional development for the center’s advisory board; expanding donor services and donor-advised funds; creating a plan to build a permanent endowment; and conducting research on faith-based grantmaking. An advisory board of Arab-American philanthropists will continue to provide overall guidance for programs and services to help institutionalize and sustain the program.

title: Collaborative for Arab-American Philanthropy: Supporting Arab-American Empowerment through Strategic Philanthropy
grantee: Arab Community Center for Economic and Social Services (ACCESS)
description: The National Network for Arab-American Communities is a national program of the Arab Community Center for Economic and Social Services (ACCESS). Its goal is to promote strategic philanthropy in the Arab-American community.This grant will support efforts to develop Arab-American philanthropy through research, creation of informational materials and effective methods for reaching donors, and an outreach program to cultivate a core group of Arab-American philanthropists to work with the network.ACCESS is a human services organization committed to the development of the Arab-American community in all aspects of its economic and cultural life.

title: Addressing Race and Race Relations in a New Century
description: The Study Circle Resource Center, a program of the Paul J. Aicher Foundation, created a guide to help communities involve large numbers of people, from all racial and ethnic backgrounds, in conversations aimed at community change. Recent revisions focus a greater level of awareness on the need for dialogue to be accompanied by corresponding opportunities to link that dialogue to strategies for collective action and sustained change.This grant will enable the center to disseminate the “Facing Racism in a Diverse Society” study guide. A marketing brochure and Web-based seminars will be used to explain the guide, which will be available in print and on the center’s Web site. In addition, a small group of communities will be selected to receive more in-depth technical assistance, participate in learning exchanges and share lessons learned with the field.Since its founding in 1982, the Paul J. Aicher Foundation has worked to bring the wisdom of everyday people to bear on the critical social and political issues of our time. Working at the grassroots level, it creates ways to link democratic theory and democratic practices.

title: Great Lakes Program
description: With this grant increase, River Alliance of Wisconsin, an organization dedicated to the protection and restoration of the state’s rivers, will prepare a retrospective document on the organization’s 15-year effort to promote the removal of small, obsolete dams as a river restoration tool.

title: Great Lakes Program
description: The River Alliance of Wisconsin, a statewide river protection group, has an active program in the Great Lakes basin, where more than half of the state’s population resides. Program activities are organized under three categories of work: river revitalization, water policy reform, and local group support. Over the last two years, the alliance has had a number of achievements, such as developing a river revitalization program for the Root River, contributing to the state’s implementation of the Great Lakes Compact, and piloting a citizen’s water quality monitoring program. Over the next two years, the alliance will continue and expand upon such program work, as well as build its own organizational strength through a variety of means.

title: Great Lakes Program
description: A statewide environmental organization, the River Alliance of Wisconsin has a strong presence in the Great Lakes Basin, which covers more than one-third of Wisconsin’s land area and is home to more than half of the state’s population. With prior funding, the alliance worked to strengthen implementation of the Clean Water Act and related policies, developed a revitalization program for the Root River, contributed to the state’s implementation of the Great Lakes Compact, and piloted a citizen’s water quality monitoring program. Renewed support will allow the alliance to build on these efforts and also broaden the scope of its urban rivers efforts, continue major fish passage projects, expand invasive species programs, support watershed groups, and invest in its own organizational development.

title: Great Lakes Program
description: The River Alliance of Wisconsin, a statewide environmental organization, has a strong commitment to improving the health of Great Lakes’ waterways. With prior Mott funding, the grantee helped maintain public support for water quality protections, engaged in state processes for implementing the Great Lakes Compact, helped finalize a revitalization plan for the Root River, and participated in regional freshwater policy discussions. With this grant, the grantee will build on these efforts and also work to revitalize the Manitowoc River, provide capacity building assistance to watershed groups, monitor the implementation of hydropower relicenses, advance priority fish passage projects, and invest in its own organizational development.

title: Great Lakes Program
description: The River Alliance of Wisconsin, a statewide environmental organization, has a strong commitment to improving the health of the Great Lakes ecosystem. With prior Mott funding, the grantee helped increase public support for water quality protections, engaged in state processes for implementing the Great Lakes Compact, helped address aquatic invasive species issues, and participated in regional freshwater policy discussions. With this grant, the grantee will build on these efforts and also provide capacity building assistance to watershed groups, monitor the implementation of hydropower relicenses, partner with business leaders and faith-based groups to demonstrate support for Great Lakes issues, and invest in its own organizational development.

title: Great Lakes Program
description: The River Alliance of Wisconsin is a statewide environmental organization that works to improve the health of the Great Lakes ecosystem. Prior support has enabled the grantee to help address aquatic invasive species issues, inform state-level implementation of the Great Lakes Compact, engage the public on water quality protections, provide capacity-building assistance to watershed groups, and monitor hydropower licenses. With renewed support, the grantee will continue these activities and develop a new focus on helping urban communities address municipal water infrastructure challenges. The grantee will also build its own internal capacity by updating its data management systems.

title: Great Lakes Program
description: River Alliance of Wisconsin is celebrating 25 years of empowering citizens to protect water resources in Wisconsin – including Lakes Michigan and Superior – for the benefit of people and the environment. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the organization has sought to protect Wisconsin waters from mining and farm pollution and has formed a Clear Water Business consortium to support its efforts and campaign. The organization has protected and restored waters including advocating for strong decisions under the Great Lakes Water Resources Compact. With renewed support, the organization will continue its efforts in the Great Lakes basin to reform policy and safeguard Wisconsin water resources; build deeper ties through its Clear Water Business network and its Clear Water Farm program and raise awareness and support to prevent the introduction and spread of invasive species.

title: Great Lakes Program
description: The River Alliance of Wisconsin was established in 1993 to protect and restore Wisconsin’s rivers. With a membership of river and watershed groups, as well as individual citizens, the River Alliance seeks to educate the state’s residents about the importance of healthy rivers and streams; develop and promote public policies to protect and restore those waterways; and help build the capacity of local river protection groups around the state. This grant will help the alliance implement its policy, capacity building, and river restoration programs in the Great Lakes portion of the state, as well as help build its own capacity.

title: Tulane Environmental Law Clinic Water Quality and Wetlands Project
description: Louisiana’s extraordinary freshwater resources support important fisheries and wildlife, and its marshes act as storm buffers and help improve water quality. These vital resources are at risk from pollution, development, and poorly planned post-hurricane construction. With prior Mott support, the Tulane Environmental Law Clinic, a program of Tulane University, has worked with community and environmental groups to help better implement the Clean Water Act in order to protect and restore Louisiana’s critical aquatic resources. The clinic will continue to provide policy, legal, and outreach assistance to abate pollution discharges, protect wetlands, encourage stronger government leadership, and increase public involvement in freshwater conservation.

title: Tulane Environmental Law Clinic Water Quality and Wetlands Project
description: Louisiana’s freshwater systems foster abundant and diverse wildlife, while also serving as important economic and social assets for human communities. The Tulane Environmental Law Clinic, a program of Tulane University, works to protect and restore these critical freshwater resources. With prior Mott support, the clinic partnered with community and environmental groups to clean up mercury contamination, reduce sewage pollution, and protect wetlands. With this grant increase, the clinic will continue its water quality and wetlands protection efforts by providing policy, legal, and technical assistance to partners; encouraging public engagement; and responding to community needs related to the Gulf of Mexico oil spill.

title: Tulane Environmental Law Clinic Water Quality and Wetlands Project
description: The Tulane Environmental Law Clinic, a program of Tulane University, works to protect and restore Louisiana’s important freshwater systems, including its coastal wetlands. With prior Mott support, the grantee partnered with community and environmental groups to clean up mercury contamination, reduce sewage pollution, and assist in responding to the 2010 oil drilling disaster in the Gulf of Mexico. With this grant increase, the grantee will provide legal and technical assistance to partners and citizens working to maximize freshwater protections through the ongoing remediation and protection efforts related to the oil spill.

title: Tulane Environmental Law Clinic Water Quality and Wetlands Project
description: Louisiana’s extraordinary freshwater resources are undergoing stress due to coastal wetland loss, surface water pollution and related threats.This grant will enable the Tulane Environmental Law Clinic (TELC) to provide legal and other assistance to community and environmental organizations engaged in implementing the Clean Water Act to protect and restore the state’s freshwater resources. The clinic will focus on reducing water pollution discharges and protecting wetlands through community outreach, policy reform, and the provision of legal and other technical assistance.TELC, a program of the Tulane University Law School, uses a combination of students and professional staff to help community and environmental groups implement the Clean Water Act and related policies. Tulane University was founded in 1834 and has 11 schools and colleges offering undergraduate, graduate and professional degrees.

title: Rhodes University Legal Aid Clinic: Advice Office Project
description: The Rhodes University Legal Aid Clinic provides free, legal advice and related services to poor people in the Eastern Cape province. It handles criminal and civil cases, drafting of contracts and wills, labor disputes, housing and land cases, family law, and consumer rights cases. Mott’s support will provide training and mentoring to paralegals and advice offices that provide paralegal advice to poor communities and assist these communities to access their rights. It will also provide institutional support to advice offices to enable them to do their work in a more effective manner.

title: Rhodes University Legal Aid Clinic: Advice Office Project
description: Rhodes University was founded in 1904 and is one of the oldest universities in South Africa with a reputation as a centre of excellence. The Rhodes University Legal Aid Clinic: Advice Office Project is part of the law faculty at Rhodes University, and its main aim is to improve access to justice in poor areas. Its activities include assisting poor people with legal advice and related services and supporting paralegal advice offices in the Eastern Cape provinces. Past support enabled the clinic to provide training and mentoring support to advice office paralegals; provide financial support to select advice offices; and assist clients requiring legal support and representation. This grant will support the Rhodes University Legal Aid Clinic to continue to train and mentor advice office workers, and to provide financial support to advice offices. The clinic will also offer an off-site service to advice offices to allow them to access professional advice from attorneys when dealing with complicated legal matters.

title: Rhodes University Legal Aid Clinic: Advice Office Project
description: Rhodes University was founded in 1904 and is one of the oldest universities in South Africa with a reputation as a center of excellence. The Rhodes University Legal Aid Clinic: Advice Office Project is part of the law faculty at Rhodes University, and its main aim is to improve access to legal services in poor areas. Its activities include assisting poor people with legal advice, running human rights awareness campaigns, and supporting paralegal advice offices in the Eastern Cape province. Past support enabled the clinic to provide training and mentoring support to advice office paralegals, provide financial support to select advice offices, and assist clients requiring legal support and representation. This grant will support the grantee to continue to train and mentor advice office workers, provide financial support to advice offices, and offer on- and off-site services to advice offices to allow them to access professional advice from attorneys when dealing with complicated legal matters.

title: Rhodes University Legal Aid Clinic: Advice Office Project
description: Rhodes University was founded in 1904 and is one of the oldest universities in South Africa with a reputation as a center of excellence. The Rhodes University Legal Aid Clinic: Advice Office Project activities include assisting poor people with legal advice, running human rights awareness campaigns, and supporting paralegal advice offices in the Eastern and Western Cape provinces. Past support enabled the clinic to provide training and mentoring support to advice office paralegals, provide financial support to select advice offices, and assist clients requiring legal support and representation. This grant will support the Rhodes University Legal Aid Clinic to continue to train advice office paralegals on subjects including various aspects of the law, organizational management, and fundraising. The clinic will also continue to provide backup legal services to advice offices in the Eastern and Western Cape provinces, and will make grants to at least 13 advice offices. This grant has been made possible by a partnership with Atlantic Philanthropies in support of the community advice office sector.

title: Rhodes University Legal Aid Clinic: Advice Office Project
description: Rhodes University was founded in 1904 and is one of the oldest universities in South Africa with a reputation as a center of excellence. The Rhodes University Law Clinic: Advice Office Project is part of the law faculty at Rhodes University, and its activities include assisting poor people with legal advice, running human rights awareness campaigns, and supporting paralegal advice offices in the Eastern and Western Cape provinces. Past support allowed the clinic to provide training and mentoring support to advice office paralegals, provide financial support to select advice offices, and assist clients requiring legal support and representation. This grant increase will support the Rhodes University Legal Aid Clinic to enhance backup legal services to community advice offices and to make additional grants to community advice offices. This grant increase has been made possible by a partnership with Atlantic Philanthropies in support of the community advice office sector.

title: Rhodes University Law Clinic: Advice Office Project
description: Rhodes University was founded in 1904 and is one of the oldest universities in South Africa with a reputation as a center of excellence. The Rhodes University Law Clinic: Advice Office Project is part of the law faculty at Rhodes University, and its activities include assisting poor people with legal advice, running human rights awareness campaigns, and supporting paralegal advice offices in the Eastern and Western Cape provinces. Past support enabled the clinic to provide training and mentoring support to advice office paralegals, provide financial support to select advice offices, and assist clients requiring legal support and representation. This grant will support the grantee training of over 100 advice office paralegals on subjects including management, organization development, fundraising, and various aspects of the law. The grantee will also continue to fund and provide backup legal services and administrative support to advice offices in the Eastern and Western Cape provinces.

title: Rhodes University Legal Aid Clinic: Advice Office Project
description: The Rhodes University Legal Aid Clinic: Advice Office Project was established in the 1970s to provide free, legal services to poor communities in the Eastern Cape province. The clinic, which is based in Grahamstown with a branch in Queenstown, handles cases on various matters including family law, housing and land disputes, and consumer law. It also provides hands-on support to paralegals and advice offices throughout the province, which in turn provide paralegal advice to poor communities and assist these communities in accessing their rights.This grant will help build the capacity of and provide support for the community-based advice offices and paralegals. It also will facilitate accredited training of paralegals and provide grants to advice offices.

title: Institutional Development
grantee: Inter Ethnic Initiative for Human Rights Foundation
description: This grant will enable the Inter Ethnic Initiative for Human Rights Foundation to increase its capacity to influence national and international policies regarding human and minority rights. Main project activities will include increasing board and staff capacities; developing new research, training and consultancy services and marketing these services to relevant public institutions, international organizations and nonprofit organizations; and establishing a reserve fund to leverage European Union funding.The foundation, established in 1996, is a leading Bulgarian non-governmental organization that works to improve ethnic relations at the grassroots and national levels.

title: Using LEHD Data to Evaluate WIA
description: Multiyear funding will enable the Urban Institute to conduct an outcomes evaluation of the impacts of the Workforce Investment Act by using data from the Longitudinal Employer Household Dynamics Program at the Census Bureau. Results from the evaluation could affect future reauthorization of the Workforce Investment Act and show how one-stop offices across the country use their allocated funds. In addition, the project could impact both research and practice in the area of econometric program evaluation, and provide plausible alternatives to costly and time-consuming random assignment evaluations.The Urban Institute, founded in 1968, is a nonpartisan, economic and social policy research organization.

title: Student Housing Operating Costs
description: This grant will support the development and operations of student housing on the University of Michigan-Flint campus. The University of Michigan will develop, finance and construct the 309-bed, $21 million facitity — which will be the first student housing development for the University of Michigan-Flint.Currently, 6,400 students are enrolled in the university, with 99 percent of the students traveling to campus by car each day. The university intends to continue its tradition of service to commuter and nontraditional students while simultaneously increasing the student body through the introduction of the new residential component. The on-campus student housing will be open for the fall 2008 semester.

title: Program for Automotive Renaissance in Michigan
description: This grant increase will allow the Center for Automotive Research to continue the Global Automotive Marketing Alliance, an initiative that introduces automotive suppliers to world markets through trips to international trade shows. The increase will also partially subsidize the cost of such trips for small, Flint area suppliers, and support the preparation of a marketing exhibit on behalf of participating suppliers at the Society of Automotive Engineers World Congress to be held in Detroit in April 2008.

title: Program for Automotive Renaissance in Michigan
description: With 17 automotive plants slated to be closed during the next two years, the Michigan automobile industry is at immediate risk of losing thousands of jobs. The impact on the entire Michigan economy, including supplier job losses, could result in the loss of at least 250,000 jobs.Multiyear funding will enable the Center for Automotive Research (CAR) to establish a program for forming industry collaborations; help the industry compete in global markets; and form a public/private job training consortium to develop a training curriculum that will help produce the internationally competitive autoworker of the future.CAR conducts a wide variety of research related to the automobile industry. It maintains strong relationships with industry, government agencies, universities, research institutes, labor organizations and other stakeholders in the international automotive community.

title: Global Fund for Community Foundations
description: The program goal is to strengthen community foundations globally. To this end, the Worldwide Initiatives for Grantmaker Support and the European Foundation Centre created a grantmaking fund focusing on community foundations and their support organizations in developing and transitioning countries around the world. The fund’s objectives include demonstrating the potential of community foundations as instruments for achieving community empowerment; building long-term local resources through the promotion and development of local philanthropy; and promoting peer-to-peer learning among community foundation initiatives throughout the world. Additional grant funds will support an in-depth consultation process on the future of the fund as an independent entity. The European Foundation Centre is an independent membership association of foundations and corporate funders dedicated to promoting organized philanthropy in Europe and internationally.

title: Global Fund for Community Foundations
description: The program goal is to strengthen community foundations globally. To this end, the Worldwide Initiatives for Grantmaker Support and the European Foundation Centre created a grantmaking fund focusing on community foundations and their support organizations in developing and transitioning countries around the world. The fund’s objectives include demonstrating the potential of community foundations as instruments for achieving community empowerment; building long-term local resources through the promotion and development of local philanthropy; and promoting peer-to-peer learning among community foundation initiatives throughout the world. Additional grant funds will support targeted technical assistance to emerging community foundations in Tanzania and Moldova. The European Foundation Centre is an independent membership association of foundations and corporate funders dedicated to promoting organized philanthropy in Europe and internationally.

title: Global Fund for Community Foundations
description: The program goal is to strengthen community foundations globally. To this end, the Worldwide Initiatives for Grantmaker Support and the European Foundation Centre created a grantmaking fund focusing on community foundations and their support organizations in developing and transitioning countries around the world. The fund’s objectives include demonstrating the potential of community foundations as instruments for achieving community empowerment; building long-term local resources through the promotion and development of local philanthropy; and promoting peer-to-peer learning among community foundation initiatives throughout the world. Additional grant funds will support the operations of the fund during the first half of 2009 as it transitions from a project of the European Foundation Centre to an independent entity. The European Foundation Centre is an independent membership association of foundations and corporate funders dedicated to promoting organized philanthropy in Europe and internationally.

title: Global Fund for Community Foundations
description: The program goal is to strengthen community foundations globally. To this end, the Worldwide Initiatives for Grantmaker Support and the European Foundation Centre created a grantmaking fund focusing on community foundations and their support organizations in developing and transitioning countries around the world. The fund’s objectives include building institutional capacity among community foundations and similar philanthropic organizations; promoting collaboration and networks which advance the field of community foundations; and building connections between the community foundation field and policymakers, governments, and international development agencies. To date, the fund has awarded $1.8 million in grants to 100 community foundations and philanthropy support organizations in 40 countries. The European Foundation Centre is an independent membership association of foundations and corporate funders dedicated to promoting organized philanthropy in Europe and internationally.

title: Small Grants and Capacity Building Program
description: The program goal is to strengthen community foundations globally. To this end, the Global Fund for Community Foundations will manage a Small Grants and Capacity Building Program focusing on community foundations and their support organizations in developing and transitioning countries around the world. Program activities in 2010 include making 10 to 15 grants to individual community foundations, providing direct technical assistance support to grantees, and documenting grantees’ activities and learning. The grantee is a global, grassroots grantmaker seeking to promote community foundations and other local philanthropic institutions in the global south and in the emerging economies of Central and Eastern Europe. Prior to its registration as an independent organization in late 2009, the Global Fund for Community Foundations project awarded $2.2 million in grants to 120 community foundations and philanthropy support organizations in 40 countries.

title: Small Grants and Capacity Building Program
description: The program goal is to strengthen community foundations globally. To this end, the Global Fund for Community Foundations will manage a small grants and capacity building program focusing on community foundations and their support organizations in developing and transitioning countries around the world. Through this program, the grantee has provided grants to ten community foundations, launched a new Web site, and developed a database and evaluation methodology. In 2011, the grantee will focus this program on youth civic engagement and constituency building work in Asia. Program activities will include providing small grants to individual community foundations, organizing peer learning events, creating learning groups of grantees, and documenting grantees’ activities and learning. Registered as an independent organization in late 2009, the grantee is a global, grassroots grantmaker seeking to promote community foundations and other local philanthropic institutions in the global south and in the emerging economies of Central and Eastern Europe.

title: Small Grants and Capacity Building Program
description: The program goal is to strengthen community foundations globally. To this end, the Global Fund for Community Foundations will manage a small grants and capacity building program focusing on community foundations and their support organizations in developing and transitioning countries around the world. Through this program, the grantee has provided grants to 27 community foundations from 20 countries and organized two international meetings involving these grantees. In 2012, the grantee will continue to focus on community foundations involved in youth civic engagement. Additionally, the grantee will pilot a peer learning and grantmaking project focused on community foundations and the environment. Program activities will include providing small grants to individual community foundations, organizing peer learning events, creating grantee learning groups, and documenting grantees’ activities and learning. Registered as an independent organization in late 2009, the Global Fund for Community Foundations is a global, grassroots grantmaker seeking to promote community foundations and other local philanthropic institutions in the global south and in the emerging economies of Central and Eastern Europe.

To this end, the Global Fund for Community Foundations will manage the small grants and capacity building program focusing on community foundations and their support organizations in developing and transitioning countries around the world. title: Small Grants and Capacity Building Program
description: The program goal is to strengthen community foundations globally. The Global Fund for Community Foundations manages a small grants and capacity building program focusing on community foundations and their support organizations in low- and middle-income countries. Through this program, the grantee has provided grants to 35 community foundations from 24 countries for youth-focused projects and to 13 organizations from 10 countries for environment-focused projects. In 2016, the grantee will launch an open call for proposals to explore a wider set of critical issues identified by community foundations. The grantee will provide small grants to community foundations for a range of activities, including data collection, research, and local convening. The Global Fund for Community Foundations is a grassroots grantmaker working to promote and support institutions of community philanthropy around the world.

title: Small Grants and Capacity Building Program
description: The program goal is to strengthen community foundations globally. The Global Fund for Community Foundations manages a small grants and capacity building program focusing on community foundations and their support organizations in low- and middle-income countries. Through this program, the grantee has provided grants to 35 community foundations from 24 countries for youth-focused projects, to 13 community foundations from 10 countries for environment-focused projects, and to 12 community foundations from 11 countries for projects addressing critical issues identified by the community foundations themselves. In 2017, the grantee will continue to provide small grants to community foundations for a range of activities, including data collection, research, and local convening. The Global Fund for Community Foundations is a grassroots grantmaker working to promote and support institutions of community philanthropy around the world.

title: Global Fund for Community Foundations
description: This grant will enable the Worldwide Initiatives for Grantmaker Support and the European Foundation Centre (EFC) to develop and manage a grantmaking fund focusing on community foundations and their support organizations in developing and transitioning countries around the world. The fund’s objectives include demonstrating the potential of community foundations as instruments for achieving community empowerment; building long-term local resources through the promotion and development of local philanthropy; strengthening national-level networks of and support organizations for community foundations; and promoting peer-to-peer learning among community foundation initiatives throughout the world.EFC was founded in 1989 by seven of Europe’s leading foundations. Its mission is to promote philanthropy in Europe.

title: Making Washington Work
description: This grant will provide partial support to the Committee for Economic Development (CED) for the first year of “Making Washington Work,” an effort to help promote integrity, accountability and transparency in government.Funding will support research on various dimensions of the current political environment to help inform CED subcommittee discussions. During the first year of the project, CED will begin two papers covering issues such as lobbying abuses, ethical standards, redistricting and citizen apathy. In future years, additional papers may be commissioned to cover further aspects of the Washington political environment. CED also will engage in complementary outreach efforts, including forums, media outreach and polling.The Committee for Economic Development is an independent, nonpartisan organization of business and education leaders dedicated to policy research on major economic and social issues.

title: Mid-Michigan United Way Collaborative
description: Across the U.S., United Way organizations are facing significant challenges as they strive to adapt to changing demographics, increased financial pressures and fundraising competition. United Way organizations in economies like Michigan’s face particular challenges. A continued decline in manufacturing jobs, greater demands on services and the need to downsize the nonprofit sector even while service needs increase have put stresses and pressure on United Way organizations.This grant will support a planning process that will enable eight United Ways in lower Michigan, including the United Way of Genesee County, to explore new and collaborative ways of working together and consolidating their marketing and services. The first year of the project will focus on a strategic planning effort to determine the most beneficial types of joint resources, the openness of each individual entity to participating in regional work, and the financial commitments and savings that are likely to result from this effort.

title: Accelerating State Adoption of Sectoral Strategies
grantee: National Governors Association Center for Best Practices
geographic_focus: Michigan, Illinois, New Mexico, Ohio, Massachusetts, Louisiana, Maryland, Pennsylvania, Washington, North Carolina
description: The National Governors Association Center for Best Practices, the National Network of Sector Partners, and the Corporation for a Skilled Workforce have come together to coordinate an initiative that in the past two years has significantly expanded the environment for states to adopt sectoral strategies and state workforce development policies that support sectoral employment. Sectoral strategies attempt to prepare workers by developing a deep understanding of important industries in their region, and partnering with area employers to create training and other services that both support the industries’ competitiveness and connect workers to good-paying jobs. Sector projects focus on jobs in industries including healthcare, information technology, construction, and manufacturing. This renewal grant will continue to expand and institutionalize sectoral strategies in states where they have been established, increase the number of states that establish sectoral strategies, and expand knowledge of sectoral strategies in states that have limited knowledge of them in order to increase the number of states where policy formation is under way.

title: Accelerating State Adoption of Sectoral Strategies
grantee: National Governors Association Center for Best Practices
geographic_focus: Illinois, Michigan, New Mexico, Ohio, Louisiana, Maryland, Pennsylvania, Massachusetts, Washington, North Carolina
description: Multiyear funding will support a collaboration of the National Governors Association, the National Network of Sector Partners and the Corporation for a Skilled Workforce, created to increase opportunities for states to promote specific industry sector initiatives. Activities will include expanding and institutionalizing sectoral strategies in states where they have been established; increasing the number of states that establish sectoral strategies; and building knowledge of sectoral strategies in states that have limited knowledge of them in order to increase the number of states where policy formation is underway.The National Governors Association Center for Best Practices was established to help governors and their staff develop and implement innovative solutions to the governance and policy challenges facing them in their states.

title: Downtown Development Authority Security Program
description: This grant will allow the Flint Downtown Development Authority to continue to expand the security program in the central business district. The security program will include increasing off-duty police patrol hours from 50 hours a week to around-the-clock coverage of nearly 100 hours a week. Another feature of the program will be to continue operating a security camera monitoring program and expand camera installation in the downtown area.

title: Downtown Development Authority Security Program
description: This grant will allow the Flint Downtown Development Authority to implement an expanded security program in the central business district. The security program will include increasing off-duty police patrol hours from 30 hours a week to more than 100 hours a week. Another feature of the program has been installing and operating a security camera system for the downtown area that businesses and other properties could link into with compatible equipment.

title: Downtown Security Program
description: This renewal grant will allow the City of Flint to replace the Flint Downtown Development Authority as manager of the security program in the central business district. The security program will include two dedicated police officers serving from 7:00 p.m. until 3:00 a.m. Monday through Saturday. There is currently one assigned officer serving the downtown during the day shift.

title: Downtown Development Authority Security Program
description: This grant will enable the Flint Downtown Development Authority (DDA) to implement a security program that will include increasing off-duty police patrol hours from 30 hours a week to more than 50 hours a week; installing and operating a security camera system for the downtown area that businesses and other properties can link into with compatible equipment; and establishing a downtown Parking Violations Bureau to sustain the program.The DDA, established in 1977, encourages collaboration among businesses and community organizations in efforts to revitalize downtown Flint.

title: General Purposes
description: “Nonprofit Quarterly” was launched as a national journal in late 1999 as a publication of Third Sector New England. In 2006, “Nonprofit Quarterly” spun off into an independent publication. Since that time, the periodical has grown its print journal and online subscriber base by over one-third and increased its share of earned revenue from 41 percent to over 70 percent. It enjoys widespread credibility and a well-respected brand identity among its readers, which include small storefront nonprofits to large nonprofit institutions. In addition, policymakers and academics find the journal to be a useful blend of critical analysis, research, and practitioner wisdom. Funding will allow the Nonprofit Quarterly to enhance its sustainability by building the number of paid print journal subscribers, increasing Web site traffic, systematizing special coverage as a business line, and planning and testing two additional business lines.

title: General Purposes
description: The “Nonprofit Quarterly” was launched as a national journal in late 1999 as a publication of Third Sector New England and, in 2006, spun off into an independent publication. The periodical has developed widespread credibility and a well-respected brand identity among its readers — small- to mid-sized nonprofits, policymakers, and academics — by offering a blend of critical analysis, research, and practitioner wisdom. Since 2008, the “Nonprofit Quarterly” has transitioned from a quarterly print journal with a fairly static Web site to a journal available in print and online flash format with an interactive Web site offering free daily annotated newswires, weekly newsletters and advice columns, and periodic trend alerts. The “Nonprofit Quarterly” has also increased its subscriber base by 32 percent. This grant will enable the “Nonprofit Quarterly” to enhance its sustainability by implementing a new business model, optimizing its use of technology, and expanding collaborative journalism opportunities.

title: General Purposes
description: Nonprofit Quarterly is a premier source of information, research, and critical analysis on the nonprofit sector. In 2008, “Nonprofit Quarterly” transitioned from being solely a quarterly print journal with a fairly static Web site to a journal available both in print and in an online flash format with an interactive Web site offering free daily annotated newswires, weekly newsletters and advice columns, and periodic trend alerts. At present, “Nonprofit Quarterly” has an online audience of almost 30,000 readers, and its print journal is sent to another 5,500 subscribers. A grant increase will contribute to the grantee’s capital campaign to support its new business plan. The plan will move the organization to a new publishing model that will greatly increase the number of readers, convert them into donors and sponsors, and more fully engage them through a collaborative journalism approach.

title: General Purposes
description: “Nonprofit Quarterly” was launched as a national journal in late 1999 as a publication of Third Sector New England and, in 2006, spun off into an independent publication. Since 2008, “Nonprofit Quarterly” has transitioned from being solely a quarterly print journal to include an online presence with an interactive Web site offering free daily annotated newswires, weekly newsletters and advice columns, and periodic trend alerts. The mission of “Nonprofit Quarterly” is to promote an active and engaged democracy. Online, it is a source for information and dialogue about democratic activism. In print, it is a serious management journal, which is research-based but geared to practitioner use. General purpose support will be used to maintain and further build “Nonprofit Quarterly” as a critical resource for nonprofits, philanthropy, and the social sector.

title: General Purposes
description: The “Nonprofit Quarterly” was launched as a national journal in late 1999 as a publication of Third Sector New England and, in 2006, spun off into an independent publication. Since 2008, it has transitioned from being solely a quarterly print journal to include an online presence with an interactive Web site offering free daily annotated newswires, weekly newsletters and advice columns, and periodic trend alerts. Nonprofit Quarterly’s mission is to promote an active and engaged democracy. In 2011, it adopted a collaborative journalism model. Online, “Nonprofit Quarterly” has become a source for critical reporting on trends, organizational operations, and dialogue regarding practice for civil society in the 21st century. In print, it is a serious management journal which is research based, but geared to practitioner use. General purpose support will be used to further build Nonprofit Quarterly as a critical resource for nonprofits, philanthropy, and the social sector.

title: General Purposes
description: The “Nonprofit Quarterly” was launched as a national journal in late 1999 as a publication of Third Sector New England and, in 2006, spun off into an independent publication. Since 2008, it has transitioned from being solely a quarterly print journal to including an online presence with an interactive Web site offering free daily annotated newswires, weekly newsletters and advice columns, and periodic trend alerts. The grantee’s mission is to promote an active and engaged democracy. In 2011, it adopted a collaborative journalism model. Online, the Nonprofit Quarterly has become a source for critical reporting on trends, organizational operations, and dialogue regarding practice for civil society in the 21st Century. In print, it is a serious management journal which is research based, but geared to practitioner use. General purpose support will be used to further build the grantee as a critical resource for nonprofits, philanthropy, and the civil sector.

title: Nonprofit Quarterly
description: The Nonprofit Quarterly was launched as a national journal in late 1999 as a publication of Third Sector New England. It enjoys widespread credibility and a well-respected brand identity among its readers, ranging from small storefront nonprofits to large nonprofit institutions. In addition, policymakers and academics find the magazine to be a useful blend of critical analysis, research and practitioner wisdom.This grant will support the transition of the Nonprofit Quarterly to a project of the newly formed Nonprofit Information Networking Association. This transition will enable the Nonprofit Quarterly to capitalize on its national identity, expand its readership and maintain its editorial focus.The Nonprofit Information Networking Association sponsors activities that strengthen the work of individual nonprofit organizations as well as the nonprofit sector as a whole.

title: Genesee County Prosperity Campaign
description: This grant to the American Institute for Social Justice will provide funds for Flint ACORN to continue the Genesee County Prosperity Campaign. Flint ACORN will work with low-income families throughout Genesee County, but with an emphasis on the areas in the city of Flint with the highest concentration of families living below the poverty level. This campaign will build the membership of Flint ACORN, seek to identify and train local leaders, and help low-income citizens maximize the benefits for which they are eligible.

title: Genesee County Prosperity Campaign
description: This grant will enable the American Institute for Social Justice to support efforts to launch the Genesee County Prosperity Campaign. The Flint branch of the Association of Community Organizations for Reform Now (ACORN) will work with low-income families throughout Genesee County, with an emphasis on the areas in the city of Flint with the highest concentration of families living below the poverty level. The campaign will seek to bring millions of federal dollars to the community by helping low-income citizens maximize the benefits for which they are eligible. Through door-to-door organizing and technical assistance, low-income residents will receive help in securing Earned Income Tax Credits, food assistance and other benefits for which they qualify.The American Institute for Social Justice provides leadership and staff training, technical assistance, research and campaign support to community organizing groups with an emphasis on groups affiliated with ACORN, one of the nation’s largest community organizing networks.

title: Technical Assistance to the Gulf Coast
description: The American Institute for Social Justice is the training, research, and technical assistance provider to community organizations affiliated with the Association of Community Organizations for Reform Now, commonly known as ACORN. The Technical Assistance to the Gulf Coast project has provided increased and intense technical assistance to community organizations devastated by Hurricane Katrina. This extension and grant increase will provide partial support for additional activities related to this work.

title: Center for Workforce and Economic Development
description: This project will enable the American Association of Community Colleges to create and pilot the Center for Workforce and Economic Development. The goal of the center is to improve the economic prosperity of businesses, workers and communities by making best practices common practice throughout the community college network in Ohio, Michigan, Illinois and Indiana. To this end, the center will bring together community colleges with workforce boards, economic development entities, labor-market intermediaries and other community organizations.The association, founded in 1920, speaks for and represents the interests of the nation’s accredited two-year colleges and their 11.6 million students. Its mission is to “build a nation of learners by advancing America’s community colleges.”

title: Georgia Clean Water Project
description: The majority of Georgia’s waterways are considered too polluted for fishing or swimming, and two pollution sources account for much of this pollution: direct discharges from wastewater treatment plants and polluted runoff from the state’s many construction sites. The Clean Water Act includes provisions that address such pollution sources, and GreenLaw, a statewide group formerly known as the Georgia Center for Law in the Public Interest, will continue to work with citizen groups across the state to help implement these water quality programs. Activities will include promoting protective clean-up standards, monitoring water quality permits, and improving stormwater management practices.

title: Georgia Clean Water Project
description: GreenLaw works statewide in Georgia to promote the development and implementation of sound environmental policies. With prior Mott support, the organization has provided legal and other technical assistance to watershed groups monitoring the implementation of the Clean Water Act. This grant increase and associated grant period extension will allow GreenLaw to continue to provide such support through 2010, including a series of workshops on Clean Water Act issues for local groups and individuals.

title: Georgia Clean Water Project
description: About 60 percent of Georgia’s waterways are currently too polluted for fishing or swimming. The two major sources of this pollution are direct discharges from wastewater treatment plants and polluted runoff from construction sites. The Clean Water Act includes provisions that address such pollution sources.Multiyear funding will enable the Georgia Center for Law in the Public Interest to work with citizen groups to help implement water quality programs across the state. Activities will include promoting protective clean-up standards, monitoring water quality permits and improving stormwater management practices.The center is a nonprofit public interest law agency dedicated to helping Georgia citizens participate in the development and effective implementation of public policy and laws to protect the state’s natural resources.

title: Advancing Sustainability in Microenterprise
description: This grant renewal will provide project funding for the Aspen Institute’s Economic Opportunity Program to continue to advance the domestic microenterprise field toward greater sustainability. During the first year, the Aspen Institute researched and documented a set of key findings with respect to nonprofit sustainability, which are relevant to microenterprise development. Based on this research, the proposed work is designed to provide critical tools and knowledge to both practitioners and engaged funders. In addition, the grantee will provide ongoing staff support to a group of funders interested in supporting the domestic microenterprise field.

title: Advancing Sustainability in Microenterprise
description: For the last two years, grants to the Aspen Institute from the Mott Foundation have focused on the issue of sustainability for the microenterprise development field in the United States. This grant represents the final installment for this three-year program to help advance the sustainability of the microenterprise field through work focused on both advancing practice and increasing funder support.

title: Tracking Trends for the Microenterprise Field
description: For the last three years, Mott Foundation grants to the Aspen Institute have focused on the issue of sustainability for the microenterprise development field in the United States. The grantee hopes to build on this work by further developing the Funders Group, addressing key concerns expressed by members, and expanding dissemination through greater use of Web and video technologies.

title: Tracking Trends for the Microenterprise Field
description: For the last four years, this project of the Aspen Institute has focused on the issue of sustainability for the microenterprise development field in the United States. The grantee hopes to build on this work by further developing the Microenterprise Funders Group, addressing key concerns expressed by members, and expanding dissemination of promising practice through greater use of Web and video technologies.

title: Advancing Sustainability in Microenterprise
description: The work of the Aspen Institute’s Economic Opportunity Program has been crucial in determining the attributes of promising practices in the micro-enterprise industry.This grant will enable the program’s Advancing Sustainability in Microenterprise project to continue disseminating the publication, “Opening Opportunities, Building Ownership: Fulfilling the Promise of Microenterprise in the United States,” and provide ongoing staff support to an emerging group of funders interested in supporting the domestic micro-enterprise field. The goal of the project is to build the sustainability of the micro-enterprise field by providing critical tools and knowledge to both practitioners and engaged funders.

title: Policy, Leadership & Gender Studies "Dialogue Circles"
description: This grant will provide continued support to the Policy, Leadership & Gender Studies “Dialogue Circles” program at the Gordon Institute of Business Science based at the University of Pretoria. The Centre for Policy, Leadership & Gender Studies was launched to assist in finding solutions to the many challenges that South Africa still faces in overcoming its apartheid past. The “Dialogue Circles” program creates opportunities for interaction and exchange across the different sectors of South African society to explore common solutions to the divides of race, poverty, and gender. Specifically, the program targets current and emerging leaders in business, government, and civil society, providing learning opportunities and the space for them to share perspectives, engage in critical thinking, and explore their roles in improving the current socioeconomic situation in the country.

title: Policy, Leadership & Gender Studies "Dialogue Circles"
description: Based at the University of Pretoria, the Gordon Institute of Business Science was established in 2000 and is one of the leading business schools in South Africa. The Dialogue Circles program creates opportunities for interaction and exchange across the different sectors of South African society to explore common solutions to the divides of race, poverty, and gender. The program provides current and emerging leaders in business, government, and civil society with learning opportunities and the space to share perspectives, engage in critical thinking, and explore their roles in improving the socioeconomic situation in South Africa. Past support contributed to programs that facilitate dialogue and strengthen leadership capacity among the youth, middle managers and top executives from business, government, and the nonprofit sector. This grant supports the grantee to implement these core programs and to create spaces for dialogue and exchange on topical issues.

title: Policy, Leadership & Gender Studies "Dialogue Circles"
description: The Gordon Institute of Business Science, based at the University of Pretoria, was established in 1999 with funding from a South African entrepreneur and has grown into a leading business school. It recently launched the Centre for Policy, Leadership and Gender Studies to address the many challenges still facing South Africa in overcoming its apartheid past.This grant will provide support for the center’s “Dialogue Circles” program, which aim to create opportunities for interaction and exchange across the different sectors of South African society to explore common solutions to the divides of race, poverty and gender. The programs will target current and emerging leadership in business, government and civil society, and provide the space for them to share perspectives and explore the roles they can play in improving the current socioeconomic situation in the country.

title: Increasing Self-Sufficiency in U.S. Microenterprise Programs
description: In the second year of a three-year national effort, this grant will allow ACCIÓN USA to continue to achieve greater scale and efficiency in lending to microentrepreneurs and disseminate the lessons learned to the microenterprise field in the United States. ACCIÓN USA is a private, nonprofit organization that provides credit and business training to low- and moderate-income microentrepreneurs. During the first year of the project, ACCIÓN USA piloted Internet lending nationwide, created a new credit scoring model, and pursued strategic national and regional partnerships. It will further develop these innovations in 2007, allowing it to reach more entrepreneurs than any domestic microenterprise program.

title: Increasing Self-Sufficiency in U.S. Microenterprise Programs
description: This renewal grant will allow ACCION USA to complete work on innovations launched to increase the scale and efficiency of its microlending. In the coming year, ACCION USA will work to develop its Internet lending platform, microcredit scoring system, and strategic partnerships initiative. In coordination with the Aspen Institute’s Economic Opportunity Program, ACCION USA’s experiences will be documented and disseminated to a broad audience of microenterprise practitioners and stakeholders.

title: Increasing Self-Sufficiency in U.S. Microenterprise Programs
geographic_focus: Miami, Atlanta, Boston, Detroit, Tucson, Puerto Rico, Phoenix, Los Angeles
description: Although the domestic micro-enterprise industry has demonstrated considerable accomplishments, one of its greatest challenges is to serve even more aspiring micro-entrepreneurs.This grant will enable ACCION USA to expand its lending services to more micro-entrepreneurs. Activities will include introducing and testing new financial products that are identified through additional market research as meeting the needs of low-income entrepreneurs; utilizing technology to reach greater numbers of micro-entrepreneurs more efficiently; innovating and streamlining loan underwriting and servicing; developing regional and national strategic partnerships with other lenders and entities to leverage resources; and exploring opportunities for consolidation in the field. In addition, ACCIÓN will disseminate best practices and lessons learned through on site training sessions, publications and workshops. ACCIÓN USA is a private, nonprofit organization that provides credit and business training to low- and moderate-income micro-entrepreneurs.

title: Developing a State Micro-Enterprise Delivery System
description: This grant will allow Corporation for a Skilled Workforce, in collaboration with the Aspen Institute, to launch a capacity-building and policy initiative to support Michigan organizations serving microentrepreneurs. With a declining manufacturing base, loss of population, and limited government resources, microenterprise development can provide employment for citizens and opportunities to increase their incomes. However, there is a clear need for capacity building among Michigan’s microenterprise programs as well as policy efforts aimed at connecting microenterprise development to the state of Michigan’s entrepreneurship agenda.

title: Developing a State Micro-Enterprise Delivery System
description: Micro-enterprise development can provide employment for citizens and opportunities to increase their incomes.In order to effectively integrate micro-enterprise development into the state of Michigan’s economic development strategy, this grant will enable the Corporation for a Skilled Workforce (CSW) – in collaboration with the Aspen Institute – to conduct an environmental assessment of micro-enterprise development services currently available in Michigan; assess demand and/or market for business development and financing services to serve emerging and existing small business entrepreneurs; analyze how Michigan’s micro-enterprise development field can strengthen its role in supporting the goals of the state of Michigan’s broader economic development and entrepreneurship strategies; and create a report outlining the gaps and barriers that need to be addressed to create a more conducive environment for micro-enterprise development in Michigan. CSW – based in Ann Arbor, Michigan – was established in 1991 as a workforce development policy and change management organization. Its mission is to help communities thrive in a knowledge and skill-driven economy.

title: National Land Trust Training and Accreditation Program
description: Recent public scrutiny has highlighted the need for a uniform level of competency throughout the land trust sector. The Land Trust Alliance has responded in many ways, including the launch of a national land trust accreditation program.This grant will enable the alliance to assist land trusts across the country prepare for accreditation through trainings and other means, as well as establish an independent commission that will oversee the accreditation review process itself. As the umbrella organization representing more than 1,500 land trusts across the nation, the alliance is well-positioned to undertake such an important task.

title: Building Career Ladders for Low-Income People
description: The community college system has the potential to help low-income working adults with skill deficits, but the system has historically been inaccessible to them and/or poorly equipped to meet their needs. The purpose of this renewal grant to Aspen Institute is to design and implement a demonstration to test strategies and explore opportunities and barriers related to collaboration between community colleges and community-based organizations in helping low-income workers make substantial improvements in their skills and earning capacity. The findings from the demonstration will be synthesized in a publication that will lay out the key elements of how these partnerships promote career advancement among low-income populations.

title: Building Career Ladders for Low-Income People
description: This renewal grant to the Aspen Institute will support a three-year demonstration to evaluate the most promising workforce training partnerships between community-based organizations and community colleges in a range of settings. The final research results will be synthesized in a publication that will lay out the key elements that are discovered about how such partnerships promote career advancement among low-income populations.

title: Building Career Ladders for Low-Income People
description: This grant to the Aspen Institute will continue to support a demonstration that will provide in-depth experience with the most promising workforce training partnerships between community-based organizations and community colleges. The target of this pilot will be disadvantaged adults and the barriers they face in obtaining credit-based, postsecondary education that leads to career and economic advancement.

title: Building Career Ladders for Low-Income People
description: This grant to the Aspen Institute will continue to support a national demonstration. This project will document the activities and outcomes of six community college, nonprofit collaborations, including Mott Community College and Flint Strive, that employ sectoral approaches to employment development. The selected initiatives will provide a mix of academic and nonacademic services to low-income adult students in order to help them enter employment and/or advance within a specified industry sector. The project will provide a learning forum for these selected initiatives that will allow for the exploration of key aspects to forming, expanding, and sustaining this type of industry-focused collaborative effort. The key lessons that emerge from this learning, and the outcomes the projects achieve, will be broadly communicated to program leaders in the community college and nonprofit worlds, as well as to policymakers and program investors.

title: Building Career Ladders for Low-Income People
description: This renewal grant will allow Aspen Institute to mine the data collected at six demonstration sites in order to learn more about community college/nonprofit sector partnerships. These types of partnerships have great potential to combine industry-recognized training and credentials with a range of supportive services to address the wide range of barriers to skills attainment and career advancement that many low-income adults struggle to overcome. In a growing number of locations, such partnerships have proven successful and offer instructive models. The work of building and growing such partnerships at the scale that is needed is complicated by many factors such as bureaucratic and structural challenges, inflexibility or incompatibility of funding structures and performance indicators, and historical and personal dynamics among institutions. This project will develop a set of tools and products that will support local leaders’ efforts to adopt the community college/nonprofit partnership approach and will encourage investors and policymakers to support these collaborative efforts.

title: Building Career Ladders for Low-Income People
description: This grant will enable the Aspen Institute to undertake a planning initiative that will examine promising workforce training partnerships between community-based organizations and community colleges and consider how they might be adapted to a range of settings. The institute also will summarize existing information about the needs of disadvantaged adults and the barriers to their success in obtaining credit-based, postsecondary education that leads to career and economic advancement. Research emphasis will be placed on ways in which community-based organization/community college partnerships have reduced barriers to success for low-income individuals. Elements of the research will be synthesized in a publication that will lay out some of the key elements that are known about how these partnerships promote career advancement among low-income populations.The institute works to develop practical leadership in today’s world through nonpartisan seminars and policy programs designed for leaders in business, government, the media, education, the arts and the independent sector from democratic societies worldwide.

title: Latino Pathways Initiative
description: The Latino population faces a unique set of challenges in the area of employment. The Latino Pathways Initiative, a project of MDC, was developed to create partnerships of employers, community colleges, grassroots Latino organizations and workforce agencies to improve employment opportunities for workers in Latino communities.This grant will enable MDC to provide planning assistance, technical support and a learning process for the partnerships as they develop; and implement sectoral employment programs. The initiative will be piloted in Greensboro and Charlotte, North Carolina. Career employment sectors to be pursued in Charlotte include healthcare and public service; sectors to be pursued in Greensboro include healthcare and retail.MDC is a community economic development intermediary specializing in planning, technical assistance and policy development services.

title: Expansion of Transitional Jobs Program
description: Chrysalis has provided transitional and temporary employment opportunities to the chronic homeless population of Los Angeles’ skid row since 1986. With a reputation as an exemplary program serving one of the hardest-to-serve populations, Chrysalis is a national model of market-based, workforce development. Despite its successes, Chrysalis is struggling to keep up with the demand created by approximately 91,000 homeless people per day in Los Angeles County. This grant increase will provide support for documentation of Chrysalis’ efforts to develop new market-based transitional employment strategies for the hard-to-employ.

title: Expansion of Transitional Jobs Program
description: Since 1986, Chrysalis has provided transitional and temporary employment opportunities for the chronic homeless population of Los Angeles’ skid row district. With a reputation as an exemplary program serving one of the hardest-to-serve populations, Chrysalis is a national model of market-based workforce development. Despite their successes, Chrysalis is struggling to keep up with the demand created by approximately 91,000 homeless people in Los Angeles County.Multiyear funding will enable Chrysalis to conduct research, planning and development of new market-based transitional employment strategies. In addition, the University of California-Los Angeles will document and evaluate the process to glean information about establishing market-based programs for the hard-to-employ.

title: Area 13 Sponsor-A-Champ Program
description: The mission of Special Olympics is to provide year-round sports training and competition in a variety of Olympic-type sports for children and adults with intellectual disabilities. Special Olympics Michigan is one of the largest chapters in the world with more than 12,400 participants and 39 area programs including Area 13, which serves Genesee and Lapeer counties. Area 13 Special Olympics currently serves 1,158 athletes, aged 8 and older, in 18 sports throughout the year.This grant is will provide matching funds to the Area 13 Sponsor-A-Champ program to ensure that Special Olympics programming is available to local, Flint-area athletes. In 2006, Area 13 activities will provide training and competition programming for athletes of all ages and abilities.

title: Technical Assistance for Trade Adjustment Assistance
description: The Trade Adjustment Assistance (TAA) program, established under the Trade Act of 1974, provides aid to workers who lose their jobs or whose hours of work and wages are reduced as a result of increased imports. TAA offers a variety of benefits and re-employment services to assist unemployed workers in preparing for and obtaining suitable employment.This grant will enable the National Employment Law Project (NELP) to increase participation in the federally mandated Trade Adjustment Assistance program by making Michigan – especially community groups, local governments and workforce agencies in the Greater Flint-Saginaw region – more knowledgeable about program rules, more informed about the program’s shortcomings, and more prepared to work together to improve its administration and address its deficiencies. In addition, NELP has enlisted assistance from its national partner, The Workforce Alliance, to assist with outreach to Michigan’s workforce development leaders to improve access to training under the state’s workforce development, vocational education and regional economic development programs.For more than 25 years, NELP has focused on improving the lives of the working poor and the unemployed by expanding their employment rights and their access to support systems such as unemployment compensation and job training programs.

title: Technical Assistance for Trade Adjustment Assistance
description: A number of Michigan workers are still losing jobs because of the decline in the domestic automobile industry, and many must face the reality of finding a new career. With this grant renewal, the National Employment Law Project will continue to bolster Michigan’s knowledge of how to piece together a rapid and effective response to severe job loss and economic dislocation. This renewal includes piloting a career center in Flint, increasing utilization of retraining programs like the state’s No Worker Left Behind program, and establishing a rapid response system in state government for plant closings.

title: Technical Assistance for Trade Adjustment Assistance
description: Mott provides partial support to the National Employment Law Project to bolster Michigan’s knowledge of how to piece together a rapid and effective response to severe job loss and economic dislocation. The purpose of this grant increase is to provide additional funding for a one-day training session for leaders of community groups and other nonprofit organizations in Michigan in order to provide an overview of dislocated worker programs and other types of assistance available to help jobless workers. The training is focused on community-based organizations because these groups often come in contact with such workers.

title: Technical Assistance for Trade Adjustment Assistance
description: This grant will continue support to the National Employment Law Project to bolster Michigan’s and Flint’s knowledge of how to piece together a rapid and effective response to severe job loss and economic dislocation. The grantee’s technical assistance initiative promotes a battery of better practices that have proven more effective in getting workers to participate in retraining and take fuller advantage of a range of dislocated worker programs. In Flint, the grantee will continue to deploy a dislocated worker facilitator. The grantee has assisted with a number of rapid response/dislocation events; worked with local community, religious, and nonprofit agencies; and promoted a worker retraining agenda with Genesee County stakeholders.
