title: Technical Assistance for Trade Adjustment Assistance
description: The National Employment Law Project’s technical assistance initiative continues to provide support to Michigan and Flint to piece together a rapid and effective response to severe job loss and economic dislocation. The initiative promotes a battery of better practices that have proven to be effective in getting workers to participate in retraining and take full advantage of a range of dislocated worker programs. The dislocated worker facilitator office has assisted with a number of rapid response/dislocation events; worked with local community, religious, and nonprofit agencies; and promoted a worker retraining agenda for Genesee County’s dislocated automobile workers. This grant increase will support a statewide conference for community groups, state and local officials, workforce agency leaders, and dislocated workers program operators to review effective state and local policies.

title: Technical Assistance for Trade Adjustment Assistance
description: Mott provides partial support to the National Employment Law Project to bolster Flint’s knowledge of how to piece together a rapid and effective response to severe job loss and economic dislocation. The purpose of this grant is to provide a dislocated worker program and other types of assistance available to help jobless workers. The program is very visible to dislocated workers in Flint because it is housed at Career Alliance.

title: Technical Assistance for Trade Adjustment Assistance
description: The overall goal of this grant is to increase participation in the federally mandated Trade Adjustment Assistance program by making Michigan, and especially the Greater Flint-Saginaw region’s community groups, local governments, and workforce agencies, more knowledgeable about program rules, more informed about the program’s shortcomings, and more prepared to work together to improve its administration and address its deficiencies. In addition, the National Employment Law Project has enlisted assistance from its national partner, The Workforce Alliance, to assist with outreach to Michigan’s workforce development leaders to improve access to workforce training under the state’s workforce development, vocational education, and regional economic development programs.

title: Incentive Scholarship Program for Hurricane Katrina Recovery
initiative: Historically and Predominantly Black Colleges and Universities
description: In the aftermath of Hurricane Katrina, financial difficulties threaten the educational future of Dillard students, many of whom come from Louisiana communities affected by the storm. In response, Dillard has launched a campaign seeking $4.9 million to provide up to 1,600 students with incentive scholarships.This grant will provide 200 students with scholarships for the fall 2006 and spring 2007 semesters. To be eligible for these Mott scholarships, students must demonstrate financial need, maintain a minimum 2.5 cumulative grade point average, maintain full-time enrollment status and perform community service related to post-Katrina community rebuilding efforts.Dillard University, established in 1930 from the merger of Straight College and New Orleans University, was named in honor of James Hardy Dillard, whose distinguished service in the education of African Americans in the South forms an important chapter in the history of American education.

title: Campus Reconstruction and Student Assistance for Hurricane Katrina Recovery
initiative: Historically and Predominantly Black Colleges and Universities
description: Hurricane Katrina severely damaged Xavier University’s campus and forced the cancellation of the fall 2005 semester. Although much of the restoration work will continue for months, the initial cleanup and reconstruction effort progressed well and allowed the university to reopen for classes on campus in January 2006.This grant will provide assistance for the reconstruction of laboratories, classrooms and offices, as well as the replacement of essential instrumentation and core facilities. Further, it will provide scholarship and financial aid support to approximately 10 students with documented financial need.Xavier University was established in 1915 in New Orleans as a liberal arts college.

title: Pappas Scholarship and Endowment Growth Initiative
description: The Foundation for Mott Community College was created in 1986 to attract private contributions for Mott Community College and to raise the college’s profile as a countywide community asset. This grant will contribute to the Foundation for Mott Community College’s current Endowment Growth Initiative. Half of the interest drawn from this contribution will support the college’s general endowment. The other half will support the Dr. Charles N. Pappas Scholarship Endowment Fund, which will award $500 annually to four eligible students. The college intends to rename its Presidential Conference Center after Dr. Pappas, a former president of the institution who established its national reputation of innovation, growth and access.

title: Congressional Program
description: The Congressional Program, developed by Aspen Institute, helps members of Congress better understand critical public policy issues. Established in 1983, the program convenes conferences that bring together members of Congress with top academics, experts and leaders to discuss ideas and analyze various policy alternatives. Support comes only from U.S. philanthropic foundations; no government, corporate or special interest funding of any kind is accepted. Honoraria are not paid to members of Congress, scholars, or speakers. No lobbyists are permitted to attend the meetings and press coverage is not allowed.Funding will support the 2006 Congressional Program, which will conduct four-day conferences on U.S. policy in Latin America; high school reform; U.S.-China relations; challenges for U.S. policy with political Islam; and cooperative efforts of the U.S., Russia and Europe. In addition, the program will host 25 to 30 informational breakfast meetings in the U.S. Capitol.

title: Pakistan Earthquake Reconstruction Operation
description: The earthquake in northern Pakistan in October 2005 was devastating, with an estimated 80,000 fatalities.This grant will provide support to the Aga Khan Foundation U.S.A. (AFK USA) for the Pakistan Earthquake Reconstruction Operation. The focus of the project will be to rebuild people’s lives after the emergency relief phase has ended. Emphasis will be on restoring livelihoods and basic social service infrastructure, as well as community-based activities that will enhance disaster preparedness and mitigation in the future. AKF USA, established in 1981 and based in Washington, D.C., is a nonprofit, non-denominational development agency dedicated to improving the quality of life in some of the poorest regions of Asia and Africa.

title: Operating Support
description: The Louisiana Disaster Recovery Foundation was established immediately after Hurricane Katrina to provide assistance to Louisiana citizens through a network of Louisiana nonprofit organizations. The foundation received nearly $13 million in private donations and is expected to receive a larger amount from the Bush-Clinton Katrina Fund. Every dollar received for the benefit of the people of Louisiana will go directly to the relief and recovery efforts under way. This grant will provide support for operating costs of the foundation, enabling it to strengthen grassroots, faith-based and other nonprofit organizations engaged in immediate and long-term relief and recovery efforts in the areas of education, housing, healthcare, legal assistance and jobs; develop a new infrastructure for education, housing, healthcare, job creation and legal assistance; provide affected populations access to immediate relief resources and to poverty and equity advocacy organizations; and encourage citizens to participate in rebuilding their community.

title: General Purposes
description: This general purpose grant to International Rivers will support its efforts to protect rivers, assist communities impacted by large dam projects, and encourage the development of alternative technologies for meeting community water and energy needs. To achieve these goals, the grantee will undertake research, education, and advocacy with a global network of local communities, nongovernmental organizations, and other partners. The objectives for the grant period will be to raise awareness of the need to shift investments from large-scale river infrastructure projects to small-scale, sustainable, community-based solutions; strengthen the capacity of local organizations to defend their rivers and participate in discussions on water and energy infrastructure; and encourage sustainable solutions for meeting water, energy, and flood management needs. The grantee will also continue to work to persuade Chinese banks to adopt international, social, and environmental standards and to improve the environmental sustainability policies of other institutions financing large-scale dam projects.

title: General Purposes
description: This general purpose renewal grant to International Rivers will support its continued efforts to protect rivers, assist communities impacted by large dam projects, and encourage the development of alternative technologies for meeting community water and energy needs. To achieve these goals, the grantee will undertake research, education, and advocacy efforts in collaboration with its global network of local communities, nongovernmental organizations, and other partners. The objectives for the grant period will be to uphold strong international social and environmental standards at international financial institutions; protect critical river systems that are being targeted for large-scale river infrastructure development; and strengthen the capacity of local organizations to defend their rivers and participate in discussions on climate change and water and energy infrastructure.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant to International Rivers provides support for its ongoing efforts to protect rivers, assist communities impacted by large dam projects, and encourage the development of alternative technologies for meeting community water and energy needs. The organization plans to use this grant increase to partially fund a strategic planning process aimed at strengthening organizational capacity to confront new challenges around climate change and water and energy infrastructure.

title: General Purposes
description: This general purpose grant provides support for the ongoing efforts of International Rivers to protect rivers, assist communities impacted by large dam projects, and encourage the development of alternative technologies for meeting community water and energy needs. The grantee plans to use this grant increase to provide seed funding to expand its Brazilian regional office, so it can work more effectively on Brazilian investments in hydroelectric dams across the Amazon region.

title: General Purposes
description: This general purpose renewal grant to International Rivers will support its continued efforts to protect rivers, assist communities impacted by large dam projects, and encourage the development of alternative technologies for meeting community water and energy needs. To achieve these goals, the grantee will undertake research, education, and advocacy efforts in collaboration with its global network of local communities, nongovernmental organizations, and other partners. Over the next two years, International Rivers will focus on the following three objectives: 1) improve the environmental and social policies of institutions involved in building dams, with a particular focus on emerging actors in Brazil and China, and re-emerging dam financiers such as the World Bank; 2) support a selected number of efforts to stop a few highly destructive dam projects that pose particularly grave threats to ecosystems and communities and where there is a significant opportunity to link project campaigns to policy changes; and 3) promote sustainable and economically sound energy solutions and improved river basin planning and management.

title: General Purposes
description: This general purpose renewal grant to International Rivers will support its continued efforts to protect rivers, assist communities impacted by large hydroelectric dam projects, and encourage development of alternative technologies for meeting community water and energy needs. To achieve these goals, the grantee will conduct research, education, and advocacy efforts in collaboration with its global network of local communities, nongovernmental organizations, and other partners. International Rivers is one of the most effective international organizations working to protect rivers.

title: General Purposes
description: The goals of the International Rivers Network are to protect rivers, assist communities impacted by large dam projects, and encourage the development of alternative technologies for meeting community water and energy needs. To achieve these goals, the network undertakes research, education and advocacy efforts with a global network of local communities, non-governmental organizations and other partners.This grant will support efforts to promote energy and water solutions for sustainable development; prevent destructive infrastructure projects, and where such projects have been undertaken, promote reparations for affected communities and restoration of ecosystems; support networks in Latin America, Asia and Africa to highlight sustainable water and energy alternatives; and increase the network’s visibility by improving public education and outreach efforts.

title: Communities Of, By and For the People
description: The program goal is to improve the quality of life in Russian communities by strengthening partnerships between government and citizens, improving public involvement in community development strategies and targets, and increasing local- and regional-level expertise in evaluation. To achieve these goals, the grantee will move to broaden the dissemination of an Effective Community Governance model throughout three regions in Siberia, while also introducing it in new pilot communities outside those regions. The project will consist of workshops, semiannual networking meetings, on-site and distance consulting, and a summary forum for interested parties beyond program participants. Among other results during the first phase of the project, one pilot city was established with a special office dedicated to engaging citizen groups in local governance. A range of local authorities and public policy centers around Russia have shown active interest in incorporating the governance model. The Siberian Civic Initiatives Support Center was founded in 1995 to support democratic reform in Siberia and to promote opportunities for people to engage in civic life.

title: Communities Of, By and For the People
description: The program goal is to improve the quality of life in Russian communities by strengthening partnerships between government and citizens through effective public participation in community development strategies. The Siberian Civic Initiatives Support Center will refine application of the Effective Community Governance model to include greater emphasis on economic development strategies, while also working to improve citizen input on local budgeting. Work will focus on the Irkutsk, Altai, and Tyumen regions, with additional efforts made to develop a core of civic advocacy specialists in smaller communities throughout the area. Under the previous grant, a distance learning course for government officials and civic activists was introduced. Citizens’ Councils emerged in Angarsk as vehicles for organized civic activism, while use of the model in struggling one-company towns identified viable alternative development opportunities. Founded in 1995, the grantee fosters citizen participation and promotes a political, social, and economic environment recognizing the value of civic initiatives.

title: Communities Of, By and For the People
description: The program goal is to improve the quality of life in Russian communities by strengthening partnerships between government and citizens through effective public participation in community development. The Siberian Civic Initiatives Support Center will refine its approach to improving community-level governance to include greater emphasis on economic development, while also building the community’s capacity to assess the outcomes of participatory development strategies on improved quality of life. Work will focus on the Irkutsk, Krasnoyarsk, and Tyumen regions and will include heightened efforts to target youth in these regions. With the previous grant, over 70 local government officials and civic activists undertook a tailored distance learning course. The regional government of Irkutsk oblast established a business development fund responding in part to local efforts to diversify the economy from reliance on a single employer. Founded in 1995 and based in the Siberian city of Novosibirsk, the grantee fosters citizen participation and promotes a political, social, and economic environment recognizing the value of civic initiatives.

title: Communities Of, By and For the People
description: The program goal is to improve the quality of life in Russian communities by strengthening community development partnerships between government and citizens. The Siberian Civic Initiatives Support Center will work to see citizens play a central role in the elaboration of community strategic development plans in participating municipalities in the Irkutsk, Krasnoyarsk, and Tyumen regions. It will also seek to further improve the independent evaluation capacity among citizens’ groups to assess progress in achieving development goals. Additionally, it will seek to capture successful cases of effective community governance for replication and scaling. During 2012-2014, groups supported by the grantee participated in planning and evaluation across a range of local issues, including education reform, development of eco-business, and health care delivery, resulting in greater government accountability and improved services. Founded in 1995 and based in the Siberian city of Novosibirsk, the grantee fosters citizen participation and promotes a political, social, and economic environment recognizing the value of civic initiatives.

title: Communities Of, By and For the People
description: The Siberian Civic Initiatives Support Center works in Siberia to strengthen partnerships between government and citizens; increase public involvement in community development efforts; and expand local- and regional-level expertise in evaluation.This grant will enable the center to introduce an innovative Community Governance Model and Community Indicators System to five pilot communities in Siberia. It will provide a series of five training seminars, support to local work groups, on-site and distance consulting, a Russian-language publication, and a summary forum for interested parties beyond program participants. The program includes assistance with drafting and reviewing assessments, strategies, indicator systems, action plans and public awareness programs for participating communities.The center was founded in 1995 to support democratic reform in Siberia. Its mission is to foster citizen participation and a political, social and economic environment that recognizes the value of civic initiatives and promotes opportunities for people to become active.

title: Community Indicators and Governance Improvement
description: This grant will support a continued partnership between Epstein & Fass Associates and the Siberian Civic Initiatives Support Center in the dissemination and implementation of Effective Community Governance approaches in Russia. In this second phase, the grantee will focus support on building capacity for community strategic planning and on developing, understanding, and applying community quality of life indicators. The grantee will provide tailored training and individualized consulting support to both its implementing partner and to the target communities. This work builds on the successful introduction of the Effective Community Governance model in six pilot communities in Siberia, which have generated a variety of innovative, community-based, decisionmaking initiatives. Established in 1985, Epstein & Fass Associates helps clients design performance management strategies that fit their vision, goals, and community context.

title: Community Indicators and Governance Improvement
description: This grant will enable Epstein & Fass Associates to provide training, consulting and technical assistance to the Siberian Civic Initiatives Support Center, another Mott grantee.The center will introduce Epstein & Fass’ Effective Community Governance Model and Community Indicators System to pilot communities in Siberia and train Russian regional experts. Epstein & Fass also will conduct field research and introduce its community governance approaches in Ukraine, facilitated by the National Association of Regional Development Agencies and the Regional Development Agency “Donbass,” both key Mott grantees in Ukraine.Epstein & Fass Associates is a New York-based, nonprofit consulting firm with expertise in community indicators and governance.

title: Community Foundations Standards Project
description: In response to the strong desire by U.S. community foundations to forge a consensus on national standards, the Council on Foundations launched a field-wide consultation and debate five years ago. Community foundations believed that national standards would distinguish community foundations from other charitable options, guide sound policies and accountable practices, and build the capacity of community foundations to carry out their missions.As a result, the National Standards for U.S. Community Foundations’ project is well under way, with more than 500 community foundations declaring their intent to comply with standards. This grant will enable the council to support the review process; provide technical assistance to community foundations that are attempting compliance; craft policy recommendations that are emerging as a result of the standards work; and foster awareness of the value of the standards process among community foundations and others.The council, founded in 1949, is a membership organization of private, community and corporate foundations, primarily in the U.S. Its mission is to promote responsible and effective philanthropy.

title: Building Acquisition
description: While known primarily for the Crim Festival of Races held in August of each year, the Crim Fitness Foundation has developed into an organization promoting year-round health and physical fitness. The organization seeks to expand the reach of its programs for youth and adults, and to increase its visibility for sponsors, volunteers and participants.This grant will enable the Crim Fitness Foundation to purchase a portion of the Genesee County Land Bank building to serve as its headquarters. The space will also serve as a meeting place for training program participants, for a new retail operation selling running and fitness-related products, and for a Crim Hall of Fame and Museum.The Crim Fitness Foundation was established in 2005 to support programs and activities that foster healthy lifestyle choices and to encourage community participation. The annual event draws more than 14,000 participants to downtown Flint on race day.

title: Durant Hotel Project
description: To further its mission of community revitalization and the rehabilitation of vacant structures, the Genesee County Land Bank Authority recently purchased the Durant Hotel. Built in 1919, the hotel was named for William C. Durant, founder of General Motors. It served for decades as the central city’s major hotel and meeting place.This grant will enable the Land Bank to develop a plan for the re-use of the Durant Hotel.The Land Bank works in collaboration with the Genesee County Treasurer’s Office to prevent tax foreclosure on area homes and bring tax-reverted properties back into productive use. Through partnerships with public, private, and nonprofit stakeholder groups, it encourages reinvestment in the more than 4,000 residential, commercial and industrial properties it has acquired through the tax foreclosure process since its inception in 2002.

title: Water Quantity Protection and Conservation Project
description: Wisconsin plays a pivotal role in Great Lakes water policy, as demonstrated recently by the state’s consideration of the Great Lakes Compact. Over the past two years with partial Mott support, Midwest Environmental Advocates, a statewide environmental law and policy group, has worked with partners and other stakeholders to implement the compact, improve the state’s groundwater withdrawal policies, and promote water conservation measures. With renewal support, the organization will continue its efforts in these areas of water management policy reform by participating in key stakeholder committees, educating decisionmakers and the public, and helping coordinate the efforts of the environmental community as a whole.

title: Water Quantity Protection and Conservation Project
description: Midwest Environmental Advocates, a statewide environmental law group in Wisconsin, has been involved in implementing the Great Lakes Compact since its adoption in late 2008. With this grant increase and associated grant period extension, the organization will continue to monitor applications for water withdrawals and diversion, promote water conservation measures required by the compact, and participate in efforts to reform the state’s groundwater policies.

title: Water Quantity Protection and Conservation Project
description: The passage of the Great Lakes Compact in 2008 created historic opportunities for Great Lakes states to enact sustainable water conservation and management programs. Wisconsin is in an important position to significantly influence Great Lakes water policy as it develops standards for the withdrawal, use, and protection of its surface waters and groundwater. Midwest Environmental Advocates promotes sound management practices that will ensure lasting protections of the region’s waters. With a two-year renewal from Mott, the organization will work with state and regional leaders to establish state-level programs that implement the compact, protect groundwater resources, and promote water conservation.

title: Water Quantity Protection and Conservation Project
description: The passage of the Great Lakes Compact in 2008 created historic opportunities for Great Lakes states to enact sustainable water conservation and management programs. Wisconsin is in an important position to significantly influence Great Lakes water policy as it develops standards for the withdrawal, use, and protection of its surface waters and groundwater. Midwest Environmental Advocates, a statewide environmental law group in Wisconsin, promotes sound management practices that will ensure lasting protections of the region’s waters. With a two-year renewal from Mott, the organization will work with state and regional leaders to establish state-level programs that implement the compact, protect groundwater resources, and promote water conservation.

title: Water Quantity Protection and Conservation Project
description: Wisconsin has 1,000 miles of shoreline on Lake Michigan and Lake Superior. Midwest Environmental Advocates, a statewide environmental law group in Wisconsin, promotes sound management practices to ensure lasting protections for both of these Great Lakes. With prior Mott support, the grantee worked in Wisconsin to implement the Great Lakes-St. Lawrence River Basin Water Resources Compact, protect groundwater resources, and promote water conservation measures. This renewal will allow the grantee to continue these efforts to protect water quantity while also seeking to ensure Wisconsin upholds strong water quality protections.

title: Water Quantity Protection and Conservation Project
description: Midwest Environmental Advocates, a statewide nonprofit organization working in Wisconsin, partners with communities to ensure long-term protections are in place for the rivers, lakes, and aquifers within the Lake Michigan and Lake Superior watersheds. With prior support, the grantee helped implement the Great Lakes-St. Lawrence River Basin Water Resources Compact, protected ground water resources, and took steps to decrease freshwater contaminants. This renewal will allow the grantee to continue those efforts, while also developing a volunteer network of retired agency experts to assist communities in improving the health of their local rivers, lakes, and aquifers.

title: Clean and Abundant Great Lakes Water Project
description: Midwest Environmental Advocates is a Wisconsin-based nonprofit that provides technical assistance to communities to sustain clean and abundant fresh water. Prior Mott support has helped the grantee raise awareness, forge new caucuses of leaders on clean water issues and protect against harmful diversions of Great Lakes water. This grant will allow the grantee to protect groundwater that feeds Lake Michigan from dairy pollution, ensure water withdrawal proposals for new industries comply with strict requirements, and deepen the engagement of new groups it has formed beyond awareness to action.

title: Water Quantity Protection and Conservation Project
description: The state of Wisconsin will be instrumental in the implementation of the Great Lakes Compact, a proposed interstate agreement governing water withdrawals and diversions in the U.S. portion of the Great Lakes basin. Wisconsin officials also are discussing ways to improve other water conservation and groundwater protection policies.This grant will enable the Midwest Environmental Advocates (MEA) to engage in these three interrelated policy processes by participating in key stakeholder committees; educating decisionmakers and the public; and helping coordinate the efforts of the environmental community as a whole.MEA, a statewide environmental organization, provides legal and technical assistance to community groups and other environmental interests working for clean water and clean air in Wisconsin.

title: General Purposes
description: Flint Club began in 2001 as an organization representing people who have left the city of Flint to pursue education or careers, but to whom the city remains a source of pride and interest. In 2006, Flint Club expanded beyond its virtual community model to include local programming and an office in Flint. The organization remains focused on connecting local activities to national perspectives and resources, and on empowering people to enrich the sense of pride and quality of life in Flint regardless of where they live.

title: General Purposes
description: Flint Club began in 2001 as an organization representing people who have left the city of Flint to pursue education or careers, but to whom the city remains a source of pride and interest. In 2006, Flint Club expanded beyond its virtual community model to include local programming and an office in Flint. The organization remains focused on connecting local activities to national perspectives and resources, and on empowering people to enrich the sense of pride and quality of life in Flint regardless of where they live.

title: General Purposes
description: The Flint Club began in 2001 as an organization representing people who have left the city of Flint to pursue education or careers, but to whom the city remains a source of pride and interest. In 2006, the Flint Club expanded beyond its virtual community model to include local programming and an office in Flint. In 2008, over 1,100 people participated in a variety of activities of the Riverbank Park Festival Series held in Downtown Flint. The Flint Club remains focused on connecting local activities to national perspectives and resources, and on empowering people to enrich the sense of pride and quality of life in Flint, regardless of where they live.

title: General Purposes
description: The Flint Club began in 2001 as an organization representing people who have left the city of Flint to pursue education or careers, but to whom the city remains a source of pride and interest. In 2006, Flint Club expanded beyond its virtual community model to include local programming and an office in Flint. The grantee is focused on connecting local activities to national perspectives and resources, and on empowering people to enrich the sense of pride and quality of life in Flint, regardless of where they live. Working to attract and retain talent, promote positive images of the city, and engage the community, the grantee will continue to use local impact initiatives designed to create safe, entertaining, and positive activities in Flint.

title: General Purposes
description: Flint Club is an organization representing people who have left the city of Flint to pursue education or careers, but to whom the city remains a source of pride and interest. Since its establishment in 2001, Flint Club has created a virtual community-based network of more than 500 members.This grant will enable the organization to concentrate on community development by empowering people in the network to enrich the sense of pride and quality of life in Flint regardless of where they live.

title: Protecting the Great Lakes
description: Despite progress over the past few decades, the Great Lakes continue to face significant threats that imperil their ecological vitality and affect human uses. With renewed Mott support, Environmental Defence, a national environmental group based in Toronto, will continue to help lead the environmental community’s efforts to address these threats by working to implement the Ontario Clean Water Act, foster policy reforms through the review of the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, and take a series of steps to implement the Great Lakes Blueprint, an action plan developed by the environmental community. Grant funds in the first year will also be used to assess how climate change may impact the region’s freshwater resources and actions that could be taken to adapt to such impacts.

title: Protecting the Great Lakes
description: Environmental Defence, which works across Canada to protect environmental and human health, has led efforts to position Great Lakes water quality issues at the top of the provincial and Canadian national agendas. With Mott support, the organization has worked to increase Great Lakes protections through the Ontario Clean Water Act, the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, and the Great Lakes Blueprint, an action plan developed by the environmental nonprofit community. This grant increase will further these efforts through a public awareness campaign linked to the newly published book, “Slow Death by Rubber Duck,” which illustrates how toxic chemicals impact human health.

title: Protecting the Great Lakes
description: Based in Toronto, Environmental Defence is a national environmental organization with a demonstrated commitment to improving water quality in the Great Lakes basin. With previous Mott support, Environmental Defence helped implement the Ontario Clean Water Act, foster policy reforms through the review of the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, and advance the Great Lakes Blueprint, an action plan developed by the environmental community. Renewed support will allow the organization to continue to seek innovative, equitable, and cost-effective solutions to Great Lakes water quality problems. Efforts will include engaging in the U.S.-Canada Great Lakes water quality renegotiations, strengthening Ontario’s water policies, and increasing public understanding of Great Lakes issues.

title: Protecting the Great Lakes
description: Despite progress over the past 30 years, water pollution continues to threaten environmental and human health in the Canadian portion of the Great Lakes basin. Recently, several water quality policy reform opportunities have come together that could improve Great Lakes protections.This grant will enable Environmental Defence to engage the environmental community in the adoption and implementation of the Ontario Clean Water Act and the review of the Canadian Environmental Protection Act. It also will lead an effort to develop a comprehensive plan for Canadian action aimed at protecting and restoring the Great Lakes.Environmental Defence, a national environmental group based in Toronto, works across Canada to protect the environment and human health.

title: General Purposes
description: The Chitalishte Development Foundation supports a network of Bulgarian chitalishte – community centers with a long history of supporting literacy, education and community development. This grant will enable the foundation to build chitalishte capacity by providing information, training and technical assistance; increase the support for chitalishte by establishing effective partnerships with relevant government and non-governmental organizations; and develop its own organizational capacity by strengthening human resources, diversifying the funding base and developing new services.Since its creation in 2004, the foundation has worked to build the capacity of chitalishta to bring positive changes and development in local communities.

title: Flint and Genesee County Community Development Project
description: This renewal grant will provide the Flint office of the Local Initiatives Support Corporation with funds to continue providing technical assistance to local housing efforts. title: Flint and Genesee County Community Development Project
description: In 2002, the Michigan office of the Local Initiatives Support Corporation (LISC) began working closely with the Genesee County Treasurer to conduct an assessment of the potential for housing development in Genesee County. This partnership has resulted in the creation of a satellite LISC office serving Flint and Genesee County. Known as Flint LISC, this office brings resources and expertise to the community to expand housing programs and assist local nonprofit organizations and community development corporations.With a focus on affordable housing and urban redevelopment, this grant will enable Flint LISC to provide local organizations with technical assistance as well as access to loans and grants. During the next year, the organization will continue to focus its efforts on assisting the Genesee County Land Bank Authority, implementing the Sasaki River District redevelopment strategy, and assisting neighborhood and community groups in Flint.

title: General Purposes
description: This general purpose support grant to the Michigan Nonprofit Association will allow it to continue and expand its work to strengthen the nonprofit sector in Michigan in the areas of accountability, governance, and transparency. During the grant period, the association will place special emphasis on public policy and advocacy work, including educating policymakers on critical issues impacting Michigan nonprofits, keeping the state’s nonprofits informed of the issues that impact the sector, and providing tools to help nonprofits become more effective advocates.

title: General Purposes
description: The Michigan Nonprofit Association works to strengthen the nonprofit sector in Michigan in the areas of accountability, governance, and transparency. This general purpose grant increase will enable the Michigan Nonprofit Association to expand its training services in order to meet the increased volume of demand.

title: General Purposes
description: This general purpose grant to the Michigan Nonprofit Association will allow it to continue its mission to strengthen the nonprofit sector in Michigan and expand its work in the areas of accountability, governance, and transparency. In the past year, the association has offered events and trainings attended by thousands of individuals, increased capacity building support to Michigan nonprofits, and compiled research and information on the status and needs of the nonprofit sector in the state. During the grant period, the association will place special emphasis on public policy and advocacy work, including educating policymakers on critical issues impacting Michigan nonprofits, keeping the state’s nonprofits informed of the issues that impact the sector, and providing tools to help nonprofits become more effective advocates.

title: General Purposes
description: This general purpose grant to the Michigan Nonprofit Association will allow it to continue its mission to strengthen the nonprofit sector in Michigan and its work in the areas of public policy, civic engagement and education, and capacity building. In the past year, the grantee has offered events and trainings attended by thousands of individuals, increased capacity building support to Michigan nonprofits, and compiled research and information on the status and needs of the nonprofit sector in the state. During the grant period, the grantee will continue research, advocacy, and education on public policy issues; work with its partners to promote local- and state-level civic engagement strategies for volunteer centers, nonprofits, and K-12 and higher education institutions; and deliver statewide capacity building programs, as well as work with identified organizations on strategic local and regional capacity building.

title: General Purposes
description: This general purpose grant to the Michigan Nonprofit Association will allow it to continue its mission to strengthen the nonprofit sector in Michigan and its work in the areas of public policy, civic engagement and education, and capacity building. During the grant period, the grantee will continue research, advocacy, and education on public policy issues; build lasting connections between nonprofit organizations and other community stakeholders; build and support civic engagement in communities; and build nonprofit capacity through diversity and inclusion.

description: This grant will enable the Michigan Nonprofit Association (MNA) to strengthen the nonprofit sector in Michigan. MNA will focus on educating policymakers on critical issues impacting Michigan nonprofits, keeping the state’s nonprofits informed of the issues that impact the sector and providing tools to help nonprofits become more effective advocates. MNA also will distribute and promote various tools developed to assist Michigan nonprofits in self-assessment and best practices and develop a new legal compliance initiative to build familiarity and awareness of Michigan statutory requirements that apply to nonprofit organizations.MNA, established in 1992 as the Michigan Nonprofit Forum, works to promote the awareness and effectiveness of Michigan’s nonprofit sector, and advance the cause of volunteerism and philanthropy in the state of Michigan.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, Bulgaria, Romania
description: The program goal is to promote regional cooperation among journalists that results in more accurate and objective analyses of political, social, and economic developments in the Balkan region. The Balkan Investigative Reporting Network is the regional coordination center for a network that includes six other media organizations across the Balkans. The grantee and other network members work together to regularly analyze key transition issues for the public and policymakers, publish weekly reports, and organize training events and public debates. During the past two years, the grantee has published over 110 issues of “Balkan Insight” with more than 600 analytical reports, in-depth analyses, and investigations, and it has improved its Web site, which is part of a longer-term plan to offer income-generating publishing, training, and research services. The grantee is based in Sarajevo, and the network includes member organizations in Bosnia-Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Kosovo, Macedonia, Montenegro, Romania, and Serbia.

title: General Purposes

The grantee is based in Sarajevo, and the network includes member organizations in Bosnia-Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Kosovo, Macedonia, Romania, and Serbia.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Montenegro, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Serbia, Kosovo
description: The program goal is to promote regional cooperation among journalists that results in more accurate and objective analyses of political, social, and economic developments in the Balkan region. The grantee, the Balkan Investigative Reporting Network, is the regional coordination center for a network of four independent media organizations and various editors, journalists, and trainers across the Balkans. The network is dedicated to creating professional, independent media in Southeast Europe as an essential component of developing democracy and a market economy in the region. The grantee is based in Sarajevo, and the network includes member organizations in Bosnia-Herzegovina, Kosovo, Macedonia, and Serbia.

geographic_focus: Bulgaria, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Romania, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia
description: The Balkan Investigative Reporting Network supports the operation and joint activities of a network of seven independent, non-governmental organizations in Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Kosovo, Macedonia, Romania, and Serbia and Montenegro. This grant will support the network’s mission to build and strengthen an interconnected cadre of investigative journalists across the Balkans that regularly analyzes key transition issues for the public and policymakers. The thematic focus of the network includes European integration, dealing with the past, war crimes, minority rights, corruption, good governance and economic development.

title: Capacity Building and Expansion
description: Iowa Citizens for Community Improvement is a community organizing group with a 30-year history and a mission to work with Iowans of all ethnic backgrounds, particularly low- and moderate-income families, to provide people with the training and skills to be effective spokespersons for their own issues and concerns. Iowa Citizens for Community Improvement is successfully building an inter-racial, inter-ethnic, urban-rural organization and sharing the experience in training sessions with other community organizing groups around the country. This project will support the organization’s training efforts as well as its work to develop new chapters in selected regions of the state, continue building the relationships between members from urban and rural communities, and build relationships with community organizing groups in neighboring Kansas.

title: Michigan Communications Project
description: Through its Michigan Communications Project, Community Media Workshop has helped to improve the communications capacity of Mott grantees and other nonprofits across Michigan, including through specific outreach to grantees in the Building Organized Communities and Growth Management and Urban Revitalization portfolios. During the next 12 months, Community Media Workshop will provide technical assistance to additional nonprofit groups, deepen the relationships that have already been fostered, and utilize new and cutting-edge electronic channels to expand its reach and impact.

title: Michigan Communications Project
description: This grant will enable the Community Media Workshop (CMW) to provide communications capacity-building support to Mott grantees and other nonprofits across the state of Michigan, including specific outreach to grantees in the Building Organized Communities and Growth Management and Urban Revitalization portfolios. The project will have three phases that will take place over a period of nine months and will include a series of workshops, a conference, and one-on-one follow-up consulting.CMW was established in 1989 to encourage and foster a closer understanding of how to use mass communication to the benefit of charitable and communication organizations. Its staff includes journalists and media-relations experts that provide trainings and other tools to community-based groups to connect with the media to promote news and important stories to the public.

title: Research on Immigration Issues
description: The Four Freedoms Fund was created to help the philanthropic sector build and strengthen organizations working with immigrants and refugees.This grant will enable Public Interests Projects (PIP) to support the fund by providing research, analysis and consultation to the staff of various foundations who are seeking to understand more about national trends, federal and state legislative changes, and key organizations related to immigration issues.PIP was formed in 1984 to advocate for issues of timely interest to consumers and the general public. Currently, PIP operates grantmaking, technical assistance and strategic planning programs for institutional and individual donors interested in social justice and human rights issues

title: General Purposes
description: The National Housing Institute serves the field of community and economic development by disseminating information on theory and best practices. Its major venue for dissemination is “Shelterforce”, a publication widely read by students and practitioners in the field of community development.This grant will provide partial support for “Shelterforce” articles on community organizing theory and practice.The National Housing Institute, founded in 1975, is an independent nonprofit organization that examines the issues causing the crisis in housing and community in America.

title: Community Organizing Book
description: For many decades, low- and moderate-income communities and people of color have worked to improve their neighborhoods and their lives through community organizing. This grant will enable the National Housing Institute to document the history, successes, failures and challenges of the Association of Community Organizations for Reform Now (ACORN) and how it has responded to the economic and social shifts over the past 30 years.The book is part of a larger project at the National Housing Institute, an organization founded in 1975 to research the key issues affecting affordable housing and community development.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to nurture and strengthen democratization and good governance in Serbia by increasing public — and especially youth — participation in decisionmaking processes at all levels. To this end, Civic Initiatives will work to strengthen the nonprofit sector, improve interethnic relations, provide civic education, promote educational reform, and increase the capacity of young people and youth organizations. In 2006-2007, the grantee assisted over 25,000 representatives from more than 2,000 nongovernmental organizations through its training and consultation programs and distributed a monthly newsletter to 2,000 subscribers. The grantee is a leader in a national federation of nonprofits, which works to improve the relationship with the government and create a favorable legal and fiscal environment. In 2006, the grantee involved more than 5,000 young people in activities that reached over 500,000 people in 52 communities. Established in 1996, Civic Initiatives is one of the largest and most successful nongovernmental organizations in the Western Balkans region.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to nurture and strengthen democratization and good governance in Serbia by increasing public participation in decisionmaking processes at all levels. To this end, Civic Initiatives will work to strengthen the nonprofit sector, improve interethnic relations, provide civic education, promote educational reform, and increase the capacity of young people and youth organizations. In 2008-2009, the grantee assisted over 150,000 representatives from more than 2,000 nonprofits through training, technical assistance, and information resources. The grantee is a leader in a national federation of nonprofits that works to improve the relationship with government and create a favorable legal and fiscal environment. Through its youth programming, the grantee worked with the Ministry of Youth and Sport and a network of nonprofits to lead a consultative process to develop a comprehensive youth policy and youth action plan in Serbia. Established in 1996, Civic Initiatives is one of the largest and most successful nongovernmental organizations in the Western Balkans region.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to increase public participation in decisionmaking processes at all levels, particularly among young people. During the grant period, Civic Initiatives will work to strengthen the nonprofit sector, provide citizens with tools and opportunities for meaningful engagement in community- and national-level decisionmaking, advocate for improvements in the Serbian educational system, and promote human rights. During the next two years, the grantee will strengthen its board, promote new leadership within the organization, and consolidate programming. In 2010-2011, the grantee helped to improve cooperation and communication between the government and nonprofits, conducted research on the nonprofit sector, strengthened youth engagement in municipalities across Serbia through work with local government youth offices and newly established youth councils, launched YouthBuild in southern Serbia, and supported more than 15 schools to introduce democratic governance. The grantee is a leader in a national federation of nonprofits that works to improve the relationship with government and create a favorable legal and fiscal environment. Established in 1996, Civic Initiatives is one of the largest and most experienced nongovernmental organizations in the Western Balkans region.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to support and strengthen democratic values and good governance in Serbia. During the grant period, Civic Initiatives will build the capacity of the nonprofit sector; provide citizens with tools and opportunities for meaningful engagement in community- and national-level decisionmaking; and advocate for improvements in key policy areas, such as education, human rights, youth, and the nonprofit sector. During the next two years, the grantee will complete a leadership transition, strengthen its board, and consolidate programming around strategic objectives identified in a recent review process. In 2012-2013, the grantee improved cross-sector cooperation in four towns, engaged a wide range of nonprofits in consultations on key policy issues, ran a competition recognizing good practice in youth participation by local communities, provided training and technical assistance to nonprofits, expanded the YouthBuild model in two regions of Serbia, and conducted research on the nonprofit sector. The grantee is a leader in a national federation of nonprofits that works to improve the relationship with government and create a favorable legal and fiscal environment. Established in 1996, Civic Initiatives is one of the largest and most experienced nongovernmental organizations in the Western Balkan region.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to support and strengthen democratic values and good governance in Serbia. During the grant period, Civic Initiatives will build the capacity of the nonprofit sector; provide citizens with tools and opportunities for meaningful engagement in community- and national-level decisionmaking; and advocate for improved policy development and implementation in areas related to education, human rights, youth, and the nonprofit sector. Over the next two years, the grantee will complete a leadership transition, strengthen its board, and consolidate programming around strategic objectives identified in a recent review process. In 2014-2015, the grantee enhanced its role as a resource center for civil society development in Serbia, providing targeted technical assistance to 400 nonprofits, 40 networks, and over 1,000 individual practitioners. The grantee was a leader and active participant in national and regional networks and provided input to policy development through extensive monitoring and reporting activities. Established in 1996, Civic Initiatives is based in Belgrade.

title: General Purposes
description: Since the advent of democracy in Serbia and Montenegro in October 2000, the nonprofit sector has played an important role in helping to consolidate democratic changes and facilitate public participation in decisionmaking processes at local and national levels. The nonprofit sector must continue to help create local ownership of the country’s new democracy, especially by engaging those segments of the population — such as young people and minorities — at risk of being left out of the transition process.This grant will support Civic Initiatives’ efforts to strengthen the nonprofit sector, provide civic education, improve interethnic relations, promote educational reform, and increase the capacity of young people and youth organizations in Serbia and Montenegro.Civic Initiatives, which was established in 1996, is one of the largest and most successful non-governmental organizations in the Western Balkans region.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Center for Development of Non-Governmental Organizations
description: The program goal is to promote greater public participation in decisionmaking processes in Montenegro. To strengthen the role and capacities of the domestic nonprofit sector, the Center for Development of Non-Governmental Organizations will work through a series of mutually reinforcing program areas, including increasing citizen engagement in public policy development; providing training and consultations to nonprofit organizations and government representatives; promoting philanthropy; and publishing a monthly magazine and other resource materials. During the grant period, particular emphasis will be given to increasing the organization’s ability to provide services on a fee basis, training staff and increasing financial transparency of the organization. The grantee is a leading nonprofit organization in Montenegro, based in the capital, Podgorica.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goals are to involve more people in Bosnia and Herzegovina in decisionmaking processes and to support the development of the nonprofit sector as an effective vehicle for civic participation. The Centre for Promotion of Civil Society will work toward these goals by playing an active leadership role in the nonprofit sector and carrying out a range of activities in its two main program areas: public policy and civil society. These activities will include training and consultations for local government and civic groups; publishing a monthly journal with information on European policies, standards, and practices relevant to local government officials; and compiling a range of practical resource materials for local government officials in the local language. Finally, the grantee will serve as a resource center for the nonprofit sector, providing resources and information, training, and networking opportunities for the sector on key issues. During the past two years, the center built a database of nonprofit organizations in Bosnia and Herzegovina and strengthened cross-sector cooperation in 50 municipalities. The center is based in Sarajevo and has two field offices in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goals are to involve more people in Bosnia and Herzegovina in decisionmaking processes and to support the development of the nonprofit sector as an effective vehicle for civic participation. The Civil Society Promotion Center will work toward these goals by playing an active leadership role in the nonprofit sector and carrying out a range of activities in its two main program areas: public policy and civil society. Key activities will include training and consultations for local government and civic groups; publishing a monthly journal with information on European policies, standards, and practices relevant to local government officials; and compiling a range of practical resource materials for local government officials in the local language. Finally, the grantee will serve as a resource center for the nonprofit sector, providing resources and information, training, and networking opportunities for the sector on key issues. During the past two years, the center strengthened nonprofit sector and local government cooperation in 30 municipalities by helping to establish and implement cooperation agreements between these two sectors.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goals are to involve more people in Bosnia and Herzegovina in decisionmaking processes and to support the development of the nonprofit sector as an effective vehicle for civic participation. The Civil Society Promotion Center will work toward these goals by playing an active leadership role in the nonprofit sector and carrying out a range of activities at the national and local levels. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) facilitate nonprofit sector networking aimed at strengthening the role of nonprofits in civil society development; 2) support informal civic activism taking place outside traditional nonprofit structures; 3) advocate for an improved legal and fiscal environment for nonprofits and increased cross-sector cooperation; 4) improve the accountability and transparency of the nonprofit sector; 5) provide capacity building tools and resources to nonprofits and civic groups; and 6) build the grantee’s capacity as a resource center for nonprofits. During the past two years, the grantee has strengthened local- and national-level networks among nonprofits and organized essential capacity building training to hundreds of nonprofits throughout the country.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goals are to involve more people in Bosnia and Herzegovina in decisionmaking processes and to support the development of the nonprofit sector as an effective vehicle for civic participation. The Civil Society Promotion Center will work toward these goals by playing an active leadership role in the nonprofit sector and carrying out a range of activities at the national and local levels. These activities include: 1) facilitating nonprofit sector networking; 2) supporting civic engagement taking place outside traditional nonprofit structures; 3) advocating for an improved legal and fiscal environment for nonprofits and increased cross-sector cooperation; 4) improving the accountability and transparency of the nonprofit sector; and 5) providing capacity-building tools and resources to nonprofits and civic groups. During the past two years, the grantee has provided small grants for community-level civic initiatives, introduced a system of quality assessment for nonprofits, strengthened cross-sector partnerships, provided information and technical assistance via its Website, and promoted corporate social responsibility. The grantee is based in Sarajevo.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will enable the Centre for Promotion of Civil Society to play an active leadership role in the nonprofit sector and carry out a range of activities in its two main program areas: public policy and civil society. These activities will include training and consultations for local government and civic groups; publishing a monthly journal with information on European policies, standards and practices relevant to local government officials; and compiling a range of practical resource materials for local government officials in the local language. In addition, the organization will serve as a resource center for the nonprofit sector, providing information, training, and networking opportunities for the sector on key issues.Based in Sarajevo, the center has three field offices in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

title: Institutional and Programmatic Development Support
description: The project goal is to increase the participation of young refugees and displaced people in all aspects of decisionmaking and social life in Serbia. To this end, Group 484 will promote the rights of forced migrants and engage young people in communities to work actively with young forced migrants. Specifically, the grantee will enhance the protection of the right to cultural identity in multiethnic local communities, improve capacities for minority rights protection, promote European standards in the field of migration, and support the creation and implementation of a national youth strategy. In 2006-2007, Group 484 engaged youth volunteers to support the return of young refugees from Western Europe and advocated for the improvement of the status of forced migrants in the labor market. In addition, the grantee built staff capacities through annual performance monitoring and educational/training opportunities for staff. Group 484 is based in Belgrade and cooperates with various European networks of refugee-assisting organizations.

title: Institutional and Programmatic Development Support
description: The project goal is to increase the participation of young refugees and displaced people in all aspects of decisionmaking and social life in Serbia. To this end, Group 484 will promote the rights of forced migrants and engage young people in communities to work actively with young forced migrants. During 2010-2011, the grantee will develop systematic volunteer opportunities for young people to work directly with vulnerable, minority communities and refugees and engage young people in advocacy for minority rights. In 2008-2009, the grantee worked with universities in the cities of Belgrade, Nis, and Kragujevac to organize practical field-based work experience for students. Through various other projects, more than 500 trained volunteers provided direct assistance to vulnerable groups throughout Serbia. The grantee also supported the development and implementation of the government’s National Youth Strategy by monitoring and providing technical assistance to 11 resource centers across Serbia. Group 484 is based in Belgrade and cooperates with various European networks of organizations assisting refugees.

title: Institutional and Programmatic Development Support
description: The project goals are to increase the participation of young refugees and displaced people in all aspects of decisionmaking and social life in Serbia and to strengthen the grantee’s capacity for effective research, analysis, and advocacy. To this end, the grantee will promote the rights of forced migrants and engage young people in communities to work actively with young forced migrants. During 2012-2014, the grantee will focus on contributing to creating an open, tolerant, and diverse society by increasing participation and activism among young people in 10 to 13 towns across Serbia. During the previous grant period, the grantee carried out a range of direct project activities in local communities and conducted national-level advocacy. Specifically, the grantee trained more than 300 teachers and youth workers to use literature and culture to promote cultural awareness and tolerance. More than 500 young people were directly involved in project activities across 17 communities. Group 484 is based in Belgrade and cooperates with various European networks of organizations assisting refugees.

title: Institutional and Programmatic Development Support
description: The project goals are to increase the participation of young refugees and displaced people in all aspects of decisionmaking and social life in Serbia and to strengthen the grantee’s capacity for effective research, analysis, and advocacy. To this end, Group 484 will promote the rights of forced migrants and engage young people in communities to work actively with young forced migrants. During 2014-2016, the grantee will strengthen local-level programming that empowers and engages young people in building an open and inclusive society, provide training and practical experience in intercultural dialogue to students in university education and social work and policy programs, and engage with peer organizations at the national level to promote better policies and practices in the field. Group 484 is based in Belgrade.

title: Institutional and Programmatic Development Support
description: Currently, there is a large population of refugees and displaced people, known as forced migrants, throughout Serbia and Montenegro.This grant will support a series of activities designed to promote the rights of forced migrants and actively engage young people in working with forced migrants at the community level. Group 484 was established in 1996 in response to the influx of a large number of refugees from Croatia to Serbia and Montenegro. The name is derived from the founders’ first organized assistance to 484 families from Croatia. Its mission is to promote solidarity, cooperation and tolerance in Serbia and Montenegro and the region as a basis for building civil society.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Network for the Affirmation of NGO Sector - MANS
description: The program goal is to combat corruption, reduce poverty levels, and promote sustainable development in Montenegro by supporting good governance and public participation in decisionmaking processes. To this end, the Network for the Affirmation of NGO Sector – MANS will raise awareness about mechanisms for public participation in decisionmaking processes, build the capacity of the nonprofit sector to facilitate public participation, and monitor implementation and enforcement of anticorruption regulations. During 2006-2008, the grantee successfully challenged the ability of government officials to simultaneously hold other public offices, and through public awareness-raising and joint advocacy campaigns with international organizations, the grantee helped to force the government to develop and adopt an action plan for the implementation of the National Program for Combating Corruption and Organized Crime. The network is a leading organization in the fields of advocacy, monitoring, and capacity building in Montenegro and is based in Podgorica.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Network for the Affirmation of NGO Sector - MANS
description: The program goal is to combat corruption, reduce poverty levels, and promote sustainable development in Montenegro by supporting good governance and public participation in decisionmaking processes. To this end, the Network for the Affirmation of NGO Sector – MANS will raise awareness about mechanisms for public participation in decisionmaking processes, build the capacity of the nonprofit sector to facilitate public participation, and monitor implementation and enforcement of anticorruption regulations. During 2008-2010, the grantee helped to bring about important changes in policies and practices of key institutions and in public awareness of governance issues through activities to: 1) mobilize and engage young people and other community groups to fight corruption: 2) provide free legal services to over 700 citizens; 3) direct monitoring and advocacy campaigns; 4) conduct joint projects with investigative journalists; and 5) engage in strategic litigation. The network is a leading organization in the fields of advocacy, monitoring, and capacity building in Montenegro and is based in Podgorica.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Network for the Affirmation of NGO Sector - MANS
description: The program goal is to combat corruption, reduce poverty levels, and promote sustainable development in Montenegro by supporting good governance and public participation in decisionmaking processes. To this end, the Network for the Affirmation of NGO Sector – MANS will raise awareness about mechanisms for public participation in decisionmaking processes, build the capacity of the nonprofit sector to facilitate public participation, and monitor implementation and enforcement of anticorruption regulations. During the grant period, the grantee will promote accountability and transparency in governmental decisionmaking with the goal of reducing corruption and fighting organized crime. During 2010-2012, the grantee helped to improve the implementation of Montenegro’s freedom of information law, worked with parliament to institutionalize citizen-based monitoring of sessions and increase information about parliamentarians and decisionmaking processes, and increased citizen engagement and governmental transparency on planning and development decisions. The grantee also engaged in regular strategic planning and staff development activities. Based in Podgorica, the grantee is a leading organization in the fields of advocacy, monitoring, and capacity building in Montenegro.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Network for the Affirmation of NGO Sector - MANS
description: The program goal is to combat corruption, reduce poverty levels, and promote sustainable development in Montenegro by supporting good governance and public participation in decisionmaking processes. To this end, the Network for the Affirmation of NGO Sector – MANS will strengthen and raise awareness of mechanisms for public participation in decisionmaking processes, build the capacity of the nonprofit sector to facilitate public participation, and monitor implementation and enforcement of anticorruption regulations. Specific focus will be given to increasing the number of community volunteers involved in its program activities, strengthening local nonprofits’ capacities to fight corruption, and expanding cooperation with investigative journalists across the Balkan region. The grantee is based in Podgorica.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Network for the Affirmation of NGO Sector - MANS
description: The program goal is to combat corruption and organized crime and to promote public participation in decisionmaking processes. To this end, the Network for the Affirmation of NGO Sector – MANS will carry out investigations into cases of corruption and organized crime, provide free legal assistance to citizens reporting corruption, increase citizens’ use of Montenegro’s freedom of information procedures, and monitor legal frameworks designed to combat corruption and organized crime. The grantee will also strengthen its program management capacities, increase cooperation with investigative journalists’ associations in Montenegro and the wider region, and improve its data and communications security systems. During 2014-2016, the grantee provided legal aid to more than 1,000 citizens who were reporting corruption, built the capacity of five local nonprofits to effectively monitor corruption in their communities, received international recognition for investigative reports on organized crime in Montenegro, and improved access to information by supporting citizens to submit more than 22,000 requests and following up on denials in 9,000 instances. The grantee is based in Podgorica.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Network for the Affirmation of NGO Sector - MANS
description: The goal of the Network for the Affirmation of NGO Sector – MANS is to combat corruption, reduce poverty levels and promote sustainable development in Montenegro by encouraging good governance and public participation in decisionmaking processes.This grant will enable the network to carry out a range of activities to raise awareness about mechanisms for public participation in decisionmaking processes; build the capacity of the nonprofit sector to be a vehicle for greater public participation; and monitor implementation and enforcement of specific anticorruption regulations.The network – based in Podgorica, the capital of Montenegro – is a leading organization in the fields of advocacy, monitoring and capacity building in Montenegro. Recently, it became the Montenegrin partner for Transparency International.

title: Engaging Young People in Facing the Past
grantee: Helsinki Committee for Human Rights in Serbia
description: As Serbia and Montenegro begin the process of European Union (EU) accession, it is critical that issues of truth telling and justice for victims of the recent wars in the region do not slip from the EU’s agenda or the concern of the society at large.This grant will enable the Helsinki Committee for Human Rights in Serbia to conduct a range of educational and outreach activities targeting young people across the country. Activities will include seminars, field visits to Srebrenica (the site of the worst atrocities during the Bosnian War), panel discussions and youth leadership development.The committee was established in 1994 to monitor and analyze social and political trends that affect human and minority rights as well as the process of democratic transition in Serbia and Montenegro.

title: Court Support Network
grantee: Helsinki Committee for Human Rights in Republika Srpska
description: The project goal is to build a constituency for justice in Bosnia-Herzegovina and the work of the War Crimes Chamber of the Bosnian State Court, in particular. To this end, the Helsinki Committee for Human Rights in Republika Srpska works with local organizations and other stakeholders to raise public awareness about the work of the War Crimes Chamber of the Bosnian State Court and provide assistance to victims and potential witnesses. During 2008-2009, the grantee will continue to work toward this goal by producing television programs, publishing printed material, and providing direct technical assistance and support in the city of Bijeljina in the northeast of Bosnia. During 2006-2007, the grantee established a telephone hotline for citizens to obtain and provide information about war crimes trials, organized public debates, produced several television programs about war crimes trials before the War Crimes Chamber of the Bosnian State Court, and organized visits to the chamber for young people and other citizens from the Bijeljina region. The grantee is located in the city of Bijeljina and has been active since 1996.

title: Court Support Network
grantee: Helsinki Committee for Human Rights in Republika Srpska
description: The project goal is to build a constituency for justice in Bosnia-Herzegovina and the work of the War Crimes Chamber of the Bosnian State Court in particular. To this end, the Helsinki Committee for Human Rights in Republika Srpska works with local organizations and other stakeholders to raise public awareness about the work of the War Crimes Chamber of the Bosnian State Court and provide assistance to victims and potential witnesses. During 2010-2011, the grantee will continue to work toward this goal by producing television programs, publishing printed material, and providing direct technical assistance and support in the city of Bijeljina and the northeast region of Bosnia. During 2008-2009, the grantee organized public debates, produced several television programs about war crimes trials before the War Crimes Chamber of the Bosnian State Court, and organized visits to the chamber for young people and other citizens from the Bijeljina region. The Helsinki Committee for Human Rights in Republika Srpska is located in the city of Bijeljina and has been active since 1996.

title: Court Support Network
grantee: Helsinki Committee for Human Rights in Republika Srpska
