description: This grant will enable the Helsinki Committee for Human Rights in Republika Srpska to establish a local network of organizations and institutions in the western region of Bosnia and Herzegovina. By providing information and other assistance at the community level, the organizations and institutions within this network will promote the legitimacy of the State War Crimes Chamber and create a social climate that is supportive to victims and witnesses. This work will be part of a nationwide court support network that, when fully realized, will consist of up to eight non-governmental organizations throughout the country.The Helsinki Committee for Human Rights in Republika Srpska is located in the city of Bijelina and has been active since 1996.

title: Interreligious Dialogue and Cooperation in Bosnia
grantee: Interreligious Council in Bosnia and Herzegovina
description: The project goal is to promote dialogue and cooperation between Bosnia-Herzegovina’s religious communities in order to build a multiethnic, democratic society. To this end, the Interreligious Council in Bosnia and Herzegovina, a Bosnia-Herzegovinan, nongovernmental organization, will work with local leaders of Bosnia-Herzegovina’s four major religions and members of these religious communities to build awareness of each other’s beliefs, customs, and practices and to foster joint activities at the local level. The council will work directly with theology students, women, and young people to raise awareness and promote constructive interreligious dialogue. During the past two years, the council organized eight meetings for theological students from all faiths, brought together experts to discuss ways to promote interreligious dialogue in the country, and organized a weeklong summer camp for young people to learn about different religious customs and traditions. The council was established in 1997 through the joint commitments of the leaders of Bosnia-Herzegovina’s Islamic, Orthodox, Catholic, and Jewish religious communities.

title: Interreligious Dialogue and Cooperation in Bosnia
grantee: Interreligious Council in Bosnia and Herzegovina
description: The project goal is to promote dialogue and cooperation between Bosnia-Herzegovina’s religious communities in order to build a multiethnic, democratic society. To this end, the Interreligious Council in Bosnia and Herzegovina, a nonprofit, nongovernmental organization, will work with local leaders of Bosnia-Herzegovina’s four major religions and members of these religious communities to build awareness of each other’s beliefs, customs, and practices and to foster joint activities at the local level. The council will work directly with local community leaders, theology students, women, and young people to raise awareness and promote constructive interreligious dialogue. During the past two years, the council organized four meetings for theological students from all faiths, assisted women believers to organize community activities, and organized activities for young people to learn about different religious customs and traditions. In 2009, the council opened local chapters in four small towns around the country. The council was established in 1997 through the joint commitments of the leaders of Bosnia-Herzegovina’s Islamic, Orthodox, Catholic, and Jewish religious communities.

title: Interreligious Dialogue and Cooperation in Bosnia
grantee: Interreligious Council in Bosnia and Herzegovina
description: This grant will enable the Interreligious Council, a Bosnian non-governmental organization, to work with local leaders of Bosnia’s four major religions and members of these religious communities to build awareness of each other’s beliefs, customs and practices and to foster joint activities at the local level.The council was established in 1997 through the joint commitments of leaders of the Islamic, Orthodox, Catholic and Jewish communities in Bosnia.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to raise awareness about the past and develop the values of human rights and rule of law in Serbia and other countries in the Western Balkans. To this end, Vojvodanka — Regional Women’s Initiative, a nongovernmental organization in Serbia, will organize annual human rights festivals in 2008 and 2009 that will include documentary films, photography, poster art, creative workshops, and public discussions. With a particular focus on young people, the festivals provide an interactive space for individuals to learn about and engage in a range of issues linked to the region’s past and other key issues. In 2006 and 2007, the annual festivals traveled to over 11 cities and towns and attracted more than 20,000 people. The grantee is based in Novi Sad, Serbia, and works with other local organizations across the region to produce each annual festival.

title: General Purposes
description: The goal of the organization is to raise awareness about the past and develop the values of human rights and rule of law in Serbia and Montenegro. This grant will enable Vojvodanka – Regional Women’s Initiative to organize annual human rights festivals in 2006 and 2007 that will include documentary films, photography and poster exhibits, creative workshops and public discussions. The festivals will travel to more than 20 towns and villages in Serbia and Montenegro and the Western Balkans region and provide an interactive space for individuals to learn about and engage with a range of issues linked to the region’s past.Vojvodanka was established in Serbia in 2000 as a regional center for the collection and dissemination of information on the protection and promotion of human rights and freedoms, with a special emphasis on women’s rights.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Direct Action and Research Training Center (DART)
description: This grant increase will provide general purposes support to Direct Action and Research Training Center, a training, consulting, and development center that supports a network of faith-based community organizations. The primary activities of the network include: 1) enhancing and expanding leadership training; 2) enhancing and expanding the supervision of local organizers; 3) augmenting the organizer internship program to train the next generation of community organizers; 4) creating new organizing opportunities; and 5) intervening in troubled organizations and consulting with newer organizations.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Direct Action and Research Training Center (DART)
description: This grant will provide general purpose support to Direct Action and Research Training Center, which is a training, consulting, and development center that supports a network of congregation-based community organizations in 22 cities across six states. The primary activities of the network include: 1) providing leadership training and development; 2) supervising and mentoring local organizers; 3) training and developing new professional community organizers; 4) creating new organizing opportunities; 5) consulting with newer organizations; and 6) providing guidance to troubled organizations.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Direct Action and Research Training Center (DART)
description: Direct Action and Research Training Center (DART) was founded in 1982 to develop congregation-based community organizations. There are now 22 metropolitan organizations affiliated with DART in Indiana, Michigan, Ohio, Florida, Virginia, and Kentucky. Each local organization has its own leaders, staff, and funding base and develops campaigns to win tangible improvements on issues such as education reform, affordable housing investments, and job training programs. Senior staff work with local organizations to provide technical assistance and consultation on membership development, leadership recruitment and training, organizational development, financial stability, and campaign design and implementation.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Direct Action and Research Training Center (DART)
description: Direct Action and Research Training Center (DART) was founded in 1982 to develop congregation-based community organizations in Indiana, Ohio, Florida, Virginia, and Kentucky. Each local organization has its own leaders, staff, and funding base. The organizations develop campaigns to win tangible improvements on issues such as education reform, affordable housing investments, and job training programs. This grant allows senior staff to work with local organizations to provide technical assistance and consultation on membership development, leadership recruitment and training, organizational development, financial stability, and campaign design and implementation.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Direct Action and Research Training Center (DART)
description: This grant will enable the Direct Action and Research Training Center (DART) to enhance and expand leadership training for community organizers; build the supervision skills of local organizers; strengthen the organizer internship program to train the next generation of community organizers; create new organizing opportunities; and provide assistance and consultation to newer organizations.DART was founded in 1982 to develop congregation-based community organizations. Currently, there are 21 metropolitan organizations affiliated with DART in the states of Indiana, Michigan, Ohio, Florida, Virginia and Kentucky. Each local organization has its own leaders, staff, and funding base and develops campaigns on issues such as education reform, affordable housing investments, fair immigration policies and job training programs.

title: General Purposes
description: The Seventh Generation Fund is a national organization providing technical assistance, training, convening, and consultation to Native American people in six issue areas: arts and cultural expression; environmental health and justice; building alliances between the Native American people of North America and South America; youth leadership development; protecting sacred places; and economic self-reliance and sustainability. Seventh Generation Fund, which began participating in Mott’s Intermediary Support for Organizing Communities program in 1990, received its final grant for that purpose in 2005. This general purposes grant is intended to enable the organization to phase out of its role in the Mott-funded program without disrupting its work on behalf of the Native American communities it serves.

title: General Purposes
description: The Seventh Generation Fund is an indigenous, nonprofit organization dedicated to promoting and maintaining the uniqueness of native peoples throughout the Americas by offering programs that integrate advocacy, small grants, training and technical assistance, media experience and fiscal management, and lending its support and extensive expertise to indigenous grassroots communities.

title: General Purposes
description: The Seventh Generation Fund is an indigenous nonprofit organization dedicated to promoting and maintaining the uniqueness of Native peoples throughout the Americas by offering programs that integrate advocacy, small grants, training and technical assistance, media experience and fiscal management, and lending its support and extensive expertise to indigenous grassroots communities.

title: General Purposes
description: The Seventh Generation Fund addresses six issue areas: arts and cultural expression; environmental health and justice; alliance-building between the Native American people of North America and South America; youth leadership development; protection of sacred places; and economic self-reliance and sustainability. The fund, which had participated in Mott’s Intermediary Support for Organizing Communities program since 1990, received its final grant for that purpose in 2005. Since its establishment in 1977, the fund’s primary goal has been to rebuild indigenous communities and renew Native America through community healing, appropriate technologies, traditional living and small-scale development.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Association of Community Foundations in Bulgaria
description: The program goal is to support community philanthropy and community foundation development in Bulgaria. During the grant period, the Association of Community Foundations in Bulgaria will improve the quality of its services to members and nonmembers, raise awareness of the general public and relevant institutions about the community foundation concept, and increase the level of resources available to community foundations by building partnerships with key donors. The association was established in 2005 to facilitate exchange of information and experience among its members, strengthen members’ organizational capacity, and represent Bulgarian community foundations at national and international levels. The association currently includes ten existing community foundations, and it is open to emerging community foundations in Bulgaria. The association’s past achievements include strengthening its members’ organizational capacity, developing national standards for community foundations, and increasing the visibility of Bulgarian community foundations.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Association of Community Foundations in Bulgaria
description: The program goal is to support community philanthropy and community foundation development in Bulgaria. During the grant period, the Association of Community Foundations in Bulgaria will improve the quality of its services to members and nonmembers, raise awareness of the general public and relevant institutions about the community foundation concept, and increase the level of resources available to community foundations by building partnerships with key donors. The association was established in 2005 to facilitate exchange of information and experience among its members, strengthen members’ organizational capacity, and represent Bulgarian community foundations at national and international levels. The association currently includes ten existing community foundations, and it is open to emerging community foundations in Bulgaria. The association’s past achievements include strengthening its members’ organizational capacity, assisting initiative groups interested in developing new community foundations, and increasing the visibility of Bulgarian community foundations.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Association of Community Foundations in Bulgaria
description: This grant will enable the Association of Community Foundations in Bulgaria to increase the effectiveness of information and experience exchange among its members; improve the quality of its services to members and nonmembers; raise awareness of the general public and relevant institutions about the community foundation concept; and increase its organizational capacity by strengthening its human resources, diversifying its funding base and developing new services.The association, established in 2005, works to facilitate the exchange of information and experience among its members, strengthen members’ organizational capacity, and represent Bulgarian community foundations at national and international levels. It currently includes 10 existing community foundations and is open to emerging community foundations in Bulgaria.

title: Foreign Trade Zone Operations
description: The Foreign Trade Zone program was created by the U.S. government in the 1930s to facilitate international trade and increase the global competitiveness of companies based in the U.S. Several industrial areas in Flint and the area around Bishop International Airport are designated as Foreign Trade Zones but have never been activated and used as local economic development tools.This grant will enable the Genesee Chamber Foundation to activate Flint’s Foreign Trade Zones and provide training and outreach to help generate economic and job creation activities. The trade zone program promotes economic growth by creating and retaining jobs in the community. In addition, it will be a valuable asset for attracting new businesses and new investment in the community.The Genesee Chamber Foundation was created to receive and administer funds for educational, scientific and charitable purposes and for the public welfare of Genesee County, Michigan, including support for the Genesee Regional Chamber of Commerce.

title: Fair Housing Center
description: The Fair Housing Center was established in 1997 by Legal Services of Eastern Michigan (LSEM) in response to persistent housing discrimination in Genesee County. The center conducts testing and enforcement of housing discrimination and seeks to eliminate discrimination through outreach and education in Flint and Genesee County. A contractual error caused by the regional office of the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development has resulted in a one-year loss of funding for this program. This grant will provide one year of interim funding for the Fair Housing Center.LSEM is a nonprofit law firm that has offered free civil legal assistance to the poor since 1951. It currently serves both urban and rural areas in 10 mid-Michigan counties from three offices, and is organized into legal specialties so that clients have the greatest focus of legal expertise available to them.

title: Internships for Eastern European Community Foundation Managers
description: This grant will provide internships for managers of Eastern European community foundations to help them become familiar with relevant practices of community foundations in the United Kingdom. The Capital Community Foundation (CCF) will select up to 20 Russian and Ukrainian community foundation managers, with little or no international experience, for internships. The nine-day internship program will include visits to several British community foundations in and around London, as well as in-depth presentations and discussion sessions on community foundation management, governance, fund development, grantmaking processes and other relevant topics. After 2006, CCF will extend the program to community foundation managers in other Eastern European countries.

title: Redevelopment of the Mott Block
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant increase will provide support to the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation to complete the redevelopment of several buildings in a critical block on the east side of South Saginaw Street in downtown Flint. The vacant and unused buildings between the Mott Foundation building and Second Street are being redeveloped through a public-private partnership for office, retail, and residential loft uses. The grantee will provide the grant funds to its supported organization, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, which intends to utilize the funds to invest in the project.

title: Redevelopment of the Mott Block
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will provide partial support to the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation to participate in the redevelopment of several buildings in a critical block on the east side of South Saginaw Street in downtown Flint. The vacant and unused buildings will be redeveloped through a public-private partnership for office, retail, and residential loft purposes. The Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation will provide the grant funds to its supported organization, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, which intends to utilize the funds to invest in the project.

title: Endowment Fund
description: This grant will provide support to an endowment fund for the Stefan Batory Foundation. The goal of the endowment-building program is to raise $14.1 million and increase the foundation’s total endowment to $35 million by the end of 2009. At the same time, the foundation is committed to continuing its grantmaking programs and maintaining an annual budget of at least $4 million.The Stefan Batory Foundation is the largest local grantmaker supporting civil society development in Poland. It also supports programs in other countries in the region, including Belarus, Moldova and Ukraine.

title: Creating Career Development Through Temporary Employment
description: This grant increase will provide funds for Springboard Forward to complete the three-year implementation and measurement of its career mobility and job retention services for low-wage and entry-level employees in the retail industry. Springboard Forward has designed programs and services that increase retention for low-skilled employees, while simultaneously demonstrating the business benefits of employee retention services to employers.

title: Creating Career Development Through Temporary Employment
description: This grant will enable Springboard Forward to implement and measure the results of its career mobility and job retention services for low-wage and entry-level employees in the retail industry. To measure the effectiveness of its services, and to create change in the entry-level labor market, the grantee will partner with a major retail firm providing business solutions that increase employee productivity and retention, decrease costs, and improve management decisionmaking based on data associated with employee performance. The results of this project will be widely disseminated within the workforce development, social policy and business communities.The mission of Springboard Forward, founded in 2002, is to transform the landscape for the working poor by partnering with businesses and community organizations to promote a new model of career advancement for low-wage workers.

title: Capacity Building
description: This grant will provide funding to Whaley Children’s Center for building the capacity of its staff in crisis prevention and intervention. The mission of Whaley Children’s Center is to serve troubled youth and teach them how to succeed as individuals by providing a continuum of services to meet the social, emotional, and academic needs of the children and their families. These children are considered to be at the highest risk for behavioral and psychological problems resulting from severely abusive and neglectful family environments. In order to ensure the safety of the children and workers during traumatic incidents, this project will allow staff members to participate in professional development, training, and skill-building activities related to conflict resolution, crisis prevention, de-escalation techniques, and relationship building.

title: Developing Private Giving in Ukraine
description: The program goal is to increase the number of Ukrainian citizens supporting nonprofit organizations. The Center for Philanthropy will launch a program to expand individual giving in Ukraine by: (1) encouraging individuals to give through a public awareness campaign targeted at changing peoples’ attitudes toward philanthropy; (2) improving the capacity of Ukrainian nonprofit organizations to solicit donations from individuals through an education program on appropriate fundraising techniques; and (3) conducting a research and publication program focused on financial sustainability for civil society organizations. In the previous grant period, promotional and advisory efforts by the center, in cooperation with a range of civil society partners, contributed both to the President of Ukraine declaring a national Day of Charitable Activities, as well as to the government adopting a formal concept for cooperation with civil society. It also succeeded in securing European accreditation for its professional fundraising course. The Center for Philanthropy was founded in 1997 with the mission of developing the culture of philanthropy in Ukraine by encouraging citizen participation and independent social action.

title: Developing Private Giving in Ukraine
description: The program goal is to strengthen philanthropy in Ukraine. The Center for Philanthropy will work to expand individual giving in Ukraine by: 1) encouraging individuals to give through a public awareness campaign targeted at changing people’s attitudes toward philanthropy; 2) researching giving habits and publishing key findings to support financial sustainability of civil society organizations; and 3) improving the capacity of Ukrainian civil society organizations, especially in rural areas, to solicit donations from individuals through an education and capacity-building program on appropriate fundraising techniques. In 2008-2009, the center co-organized the annual Philanthropist of the Year award, raising the profile of philanthropy across Ukraine. It also conducted important surveys on trends of individual giving and detailing the financial position of civil society organizations in Ukraine. The Center for Philanthropy was founded in 1997 with the mission of developing the culture of philanthropy in Ukraine by encouraging citizen participation and independent social action.

title: Developing Private Giving in Ukraine
description: This grant will enable the Center for Philanthropy to expand individual giving in Ukraine by launching a public awareness campaign targeted at changing people’s attitudes toward philanthropy; improving the capacity of Ukrainian nonprofit organizations to solicit donations from individuals through an education program on appropriate fundraising techniques; and informing Ukrainian nonprofits, the government and the public about the percentage philanthropy concept – whereby taxpayers can designate a certain percentage of their annual income tax to be paid to a charitable organization.The center was founded in 1997 to provide informational and analytical resources to the nonprofit sector. Its mission is to develop a culture of philanthropy in Ukraine by encouraging citizen participation and independent social action.

title: International Conference: The Challenge of the New Populism
description: This grant will enable the Centre for Liberal Strategies Foundation to organize a three-day international conference entitled “The Challenge of the New Populism” on May 10-11, 2006. The purpose of the conference is to bring together leading academics, politicians and civic activists to discuss the various issues and challenges arising from the new populism and to formulate a range of responses. More than 120 participants are expected, including more than 30 specially invited guests and speakers from Europe, Central/Eastern Europe, the U.S. and Chile. The center, established in 1994 in Bulgaria, is an independent think tank whose mission is to carry out activities that promote public debate.

title: Downtown Detroit Strategic Planning Project
description: The University of Michigan Graduate Real Estate Development Program is a unique academic program focused on “progressive development.” Its goal is to promote alternatives to conventional sprawl-oriented development, including downtown revitalization, New Urbanism, suburban town center development, affordable housing, conservation development, green building, smart growth and regionalism. Through an interdisciplinary approach, the program brings together UM’s graduate schools of business, natural resources and environment, and architecture and urban planning.This grant will support revitalization efforts in downtown Detroit and contribute to efforts to influence policy and practice around urban revitalization in Michigan.

title: Policy Evaluation Project
description: Currently, many low- and moderate-income households are saving little for retirement. To encourage increased savings among these households, the Brookings Institution’s Policy Evaluation Project is conducting an experiment to test the effects of matching rates and other savings incentives on savings behavior.This grant will enable the project to analyze, report on and communicate results from the experiment to policymakers, journalists and savings advocates. Among other impacts, these results will help inform current and future debates about new directions for a U.S. savings policy.The Policy Evaluation Project is known for producing high quality research findings in a timely manner, providing a strong base of evidence to assess new policy ideas, and incorporating successful ideas into the policy formulation process.

title: Public Works Program
grantee: Demos: A Network for Ideas and Action
description: Demos believes that current public views and discourse about government not only present a real danger for our democracy but also undermine society’s ability to address current and future challenges and pursue emerging opportunities. To address this dynamic, Demos established the Public Works Program to foster a general recognition of the essential role of government in achieving the common good. The organization conducted extensive communications research in order to identify ways to communicate more effectively about the public sector and its purpose. This grant will enable Demos to complete its research and, more importantly, support extensive public education, training, and outreach efforts using the research findings. Founded in 2000, Demos is a nonprofit, nonpartisan organization committed to building a society where America can achieve its highest democratic ideals.

title: Public Works Program
grantee: Demos: A Network for Ideas and Action
description: Demos: A Network for Ideas and Action believes that current public views and discourse about government not only present a real danger for our democracy but also undermine government’s ability to address current and future social and economic challenges. The Public Works Program is confronting this dynamic directly by engaging nonprofits, elected officials, and the media in reclaiming public debate about government and its critical role in promoting the common good. Mott funds will support the grantee’s ongoing research, public education, training and outreach efforts, which provide these target audiences with effective strategies and tools for shifting public opinion about government and creating a sound base for debating the important issues facing the nation today and into the future. Founded in 2000, Demos is a nonprofit, nonpartisan organization committed to building a society where America can achieve its highest democratic ideals.

title: Public Works Program
grantee: Demos: A Network for Ideas and Action
description: Demo: A Network for Ideas and Action believes that current public views and discourse about government not only present a real danger for our democracy but also undermine government’s ability to address current and future social and economic priorities. The Public Works Program is confronting this challenge directly by engaging nonprofits, elected officials, and the media in reclaiming public debate about government and its critical role in promoting the common good. Mott funds will support the grantee’s ongoing research, public education, training, and outreach efforts, which provide these target audiences with effective strategies and tools for informing public opinion about government and creating a sound base for debating the important issues facing the nation today and into the future. Founded in 2000, Demos is a nonprofit, nonpartisan organization committed to building a society where America can achieve its highest democratic ideals.

title: Public Works Program
grantee: Demos: A Network for Ideas and Action
description: Demos: A Network for Ideas and Action created the Public Works Program to foster a general recognition of the essential role of government in achieving the common good. This grant will enable the network to complete research and support extensive public education, training and outreach efforts to communicate information about the public sector and its purpose.Founded in 2000, Demos is a nonprofit, nonpartisan organization committed to building a society where America can achieve its highest democratic ideals.

title: Production of "Faustus"
geographic_focus: Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Montenegro
description: This grant will enable the East West Centre Sarajevo to adapt and produce a theatrical piece based on Christopher Marlowe’s “Dr. Faustus” to be performed throughout the Balkans from June 2006 through March 2008. The underlying values of tolerance, diversity, multiculturalism, and meaningful collaboration among different ethnic societies will be featured in this production. Haris Pasovic, a successful and well-respected Bosnian playwright, will produce the play. He recently directed and produced Hamlet, placing it in a Muslim-Turkish setting, and also Romeo and Juliet, which focused on religious diversity, tolerance and understanding.The organization’s mission is to create artwork in the domain of theater, film, television, literature and other media as a means to understanding and promoting democratic principles and values and advocating for dialogue, exchanges and the increase of understanding between Eastern and Western cultures.

title: Building the Capacity of Belarus' Analytical Community
description: The program goal is to strengthen an independent public policy community in Belarus. The Pontis Foundation will work with the Belarusian Institute of Strategic Studies to foster a network of policy fellows who will examine specific policy issues and present proposals and analyses accessible to both the public and government. Drawing on Slovak experience, the partners will publish the Belarus Yearbook, an annual digest of data and analysis incorporating the work of policy fellows. An international conference examining policy options for Belarus will be held in Ukraine. Finally, the Pontis Foundation will work to cement its ties to the independent analytical community in Belarus by strengthening the organizational capacity of its Belarusian partner, the emergence of which, in 2007, is the key result of the first phase of this project. Established in 1997, the grantee supports the development of the nonprofit sector in Slovakia as well as democratization programs in Cuba, Serbia, Iraq, and Belarus.

title: Building the Capacity of Belarus' Analytical Community
description: The program goal is to strengthen an independent public policy community in Belarus. The Pontis Foundation will work with the Belarusian Institute of Strategic Studies to develop the latter’s institutional capacity through a program of training and mentoring. Together they will foster a network of policy fellows and aspiring analysts who will examine specific policy issues and present analyses accessible to the public and government through annual policy conferences and in publications like the Belarus Yearbook. In 2008-2010, the partners held two international policy conferences, including an unprecedented event in Minsk held under the patronage of the European Union delegation, which included a large number of government attendees. They also published and distributed two editions of the Belarus Yearbook, an authoritative analysis of key policy issues facing Belarus. Established in 1997, the Pontis Foundation supports the development of the nonprofit sector in Slovakia as well as democratization programs in Cuba, Serbia, Iraq, and Belarus.

title: Building the Capacity of Belarus' Analytical Community
description: The program goal is to strengthen an independent public policy community in Belarus. The Pontis Foundation will work with the Belarusian Institute of Strategic Studies to develop its institutional capacity through a program of fellowships and mentoring. This will include the newly established Vitaliy Silitski Fellowship in memory of the institute’s founding director. The partners will foster a network of policy fellows and aspiring analysts who will examine key issues and present analyses accessible to the public and government through publications like the Belarus Yearbook and through regular public presentations. In 2010-2012, the partners supported eight fellows who contributed to the publication of two editions of the Belarus Yearbook. The grantee was also asked to serve on an advisory committee for the Slovak Ministry of Foreign Affairs dealing with Belarus. Established in 1997, the Pontis Foundation supports the development of the nonprofit sector in Slovakia as well as democratization programs in Cuba, Serbia, Iraq, and Belarus.

title: Building the Capacity of Belarus' Analytical Community
description: The program goal is to improve the policymaking capacity of Belarus’ independent think tanks and analytical centers, with a focus on enhancing the public policy debate on the future of Belarus and securing a communication platform both among and between these institutions and internationally.This grant will enable the Pontis Foundation to establish a Belarus Standing Conference for Transformation — an independent, civil body enhancing public discussion in the country and increasing attention to Belarus abroad; create a common virtual communication platform, including a quarterly newsletter, a monthly expert panel and a quarterly analytical publication; organize meetings of Belarusian academics, policymakers, journalists and non-governmental organization (NGO) representatives; and provide research and travel grants to Belarusian analysts.The Pontis Foundation works to strengthen the development and long-term financial sustainability of Slovak NGOs; support the development of corporate philanthropy and corporate social responsibility; and promote civil society development in Belarus and other post-communist countries.

title: Arrábida Meetings
description: This grant will enable the Fundação Oriente to organize the 2006 meeting series convened at the Convento da Arrábida located just outside Lisbon, Portugal. The meetings are attended by academics, students and professionals in various fields, as well as the general public. In 2006, the major areas of discussion will center on transatlantic relations, the rising global roles of China and India, changes in the European welfare state, immigration, and other topics.The Fundação Oriente was established in 1988 with the goal of supporting cultural, educational, artistic and philanthropic activities, particularly in Portugal and Macao.

title: Masters in Education for Afterschool Leaders
description: This grant will enable Citizen Schools, in partnership with Lesley University School of Education, to develop an online format to enhance national participation in a Master’s Degree in Out-of-School-Time Education and Leadership. The graduate program is designed to create new leadership for the growing afterschool sector by specifically preparing talented and motivated individuals to develop and direct high quality afterschool programs. The broadest impact will be made by modifying the current course to include an online content component. This project will strengthen the overall afterschool field.Citizens Schools, founded in 1995, is a middle school afterschool program based in Boston that blends real-world learning projects with rigorous academic and leadership development activities to prepare students for success in high school, college, the workforce and civic life.

title: Learning Beyond the Classroom Evaluation
description: Harvard University’s Harvard Family Research Project is submitting this grant increase request to support the evaluation of Mott’s Learning Beyond the Classroom grantmaking strategy. The Learning Beyond the Classroom evaluation will be used in combination with other portfolio evaluations to provide an analysis of the effectiveness of Pathways Out of Poverty grantmaking.

title: Evaluation of Statewide Afterschool Networks
description: This grant to Harvard University will support the Harvard Family Research Project in its efforts to evaluate the Mott-funded statewide afterschool networks, a multistate effort to further the policies and practices necessary to develop and sustain quality afterschool programs. Mott has supported the statewide afterschool networks since 2002. Deliverables for the project include: 1) self-assessment tools for the statewide afterschool networks; 2) technical assistance to the networks to support this effort; and 3) an evaluation on the effectiveness of the overall statewide afterschool initiative.

title: Follow-up Study of Former TASC Participants
description: This grant will enable Policy Studies Associates to analyze the high school performance of former New York City middle-school students who participated in afterschool programs sponsored by The After-School Corporation. The project will address whether high school students who participated in the middle school afterschool program show higher attendance, steadier academic progress, lower dropout rates and lower levels of delinquent behavior. This follow-up evaluation will contribute to the growing body of afterschool research necessary to support both the quality and sustainability of programs.Policy Studies Associates, founded in 1982, focuses on research and evaluation in education, especially K-12 initiatives designed to improve the academic learning and personal development of disadvantaged children and youth.

title: Afterschool Trainer Approval Project
description: This grant will enable the National Afterschool Association to improve the quality of afterschool programs, specifically the quality of professional development provided to afterschool staff working directly with children and youth. In developing this system, the association will work in collaboration with a committee of national experts in staff development, training and afterschool programming. The project aims to: develop better quality assurance for training in the afterschool field; set a standard for the type of facilitator/trainer that is most effective for developing quality afterschool practitioners; and offer a seal of approval for trainers/facilitators of afterschool frontline staff. The National AfterSchool Association is well positioned to be the conferring entity for the approval system, as it is a membership group of afterschool staff and not a training entity.

title: Tiger Woods Learning Center Evaluation
description: The Tiger Woods Learning Center is a state-of-the-art, technology-enhanced facility that seeks to combine positive youth development and high quality education in a variety of career-oriented, out-of-school programs targeting low-income 4th to 12th grade minority students in southern California. This study will help the Tiger Woods Foundation, its partners, and other community development and educational institutions better understand the value of a unique out-of-school curriculum rooted in science, math and language arts. Information from this study will be used to improve and expand programs, and aid in disseminating lessons learned and resources for the broader afterschool field.

title: Impact of Program and Practice Characteristics on Participant Outcomes
description: This grant increase will enable the University of California – Irvine to carry out further research based on the Mott-funded Study of Promising After-School Programs to include the collection of data from an estimated 1,000 student participants in the Study of Early Child Care and Youth Development. Longitudinal data from kindergarten through high school will be collected to examine the long-term impact of afterschool on cognitive, psychosocial, and behavioral outcomes on participants. This unprecedented study will complement the grant’s original projects that consist of a series of studies focused on understanding the specific features and practices of the programs that facilitate positive participant outcomes.

title: Impact of Program and Practice Characteristics on Participant Outcomes
description: This grant increase will enable the University of California – Irvine to prepare a series of three reports based on longitudinal studies of the short-term and long-term effects of out-of-school time activities on children and youth. The reports will draw on two large research projects previously funded by the Mott Foundation: the “Study of Promising After-School Programs” and the “Study of Early Child Care and Youth Development.” These reports will be used to help inform decisionmaking and to educate policymakers, educators, and the public.

title: Impact of Program and Practice Characteristics on Participant Outcomes
description: This grant increase will enable the University of California – Irvine to update, finalize, and release study findings on the impact of afterschool and expanded learning opportunities on academic and social outcomes. Specifically, this will include the implementation of a dissemination strategy to: 1) produce and release research briefs; 2) present at scholarly meetings including the annual meeting of the American Educational Research Association; 3) present to afterschool and expanded learning stakeholders; and 4) publish the findings in scholarly journals. The dissemination of these results will help to inform decisionmaking and to educate policymakers, educators, and the public.

title: Impact of Program and Practice Characteristics on Participant Outcomes
description: This grant will enable the University of California – Irvine to carry out further research based on the Mott-funded Study of Promising After-school Programs. The project will consist of a series of studies focused on understanding the specific features and practices of the programs that facilitate positive participant outcomes. Findings from these follow-up studies will provide the field with detailed information aimed at improving the effectiveness of programs, particularly for a growing Latino youth population. Specifically, the projects will identify the impact of structural, organizational, content and process features on participants’ academic, social, psychological and behavioral development and the structural and cultural features of afterschool programs that enhance Latino participants’ academic and social development as well as their emotional and physical well-being.

title: Aligning High School Afterschool with School Reform
description: This grant will support After School Matters and its partners in convening local jurisdictions to develop actionable citywide strategies leading to improved outcomes for high school youth. Specifically, select cities will partner with experts from across the country to increase the availability of high quality afterschool programs that are aligned with high school improvement strategies by creating action plans. The proposed efforts are a continuation of the work begun by After School Matters, The Trust Corporation, Boston After-School and Beyond, and their intermediary partners in the Collaborative for Building After-School Systems in which two national conferences were held to improve the alignment of high school afterschool with school reform.

title: Aligning High School Afterschool with School Reform
description: This grant increase will allow After School Matters and its partners to continue their work in improving the design of high school afterschool programs in order to help increase the graduation rates of urban youth. This project strives to advance the work begun by After School Matters, The DC Children and Youth Investment Trust Corporation, Boston After-School and Beyond and other partners to build awareness and support the alignment of afterschool with high school reform strategies. Specifically, this grant increase will support the development of a national policy and advocacy strategy that supports coordinated resources and quality programming for older youth.

title: City Intermediaries: A Systems Theory of Change
grantee: DC Children and Youth Investment Trust Corporation
description: This grant will enable the DC Children and Youth Investment Trust Corporation, in partnership with Boston After School & Beyond and Chicago’s After School Matters, to host two national conferences on how high school afterschool programs can keep youth in school and help them succeed academically. This work seeks to further integrate the practices of afterschool into the broader education field’s strategies to meet the needs of young people, particularly low-income students of color. This project also will examine how high quality afterschool program models can be aligned with high quality high school reform efforts to improve graduation rates.The organization was formed in 1999 to link public and private resources, creativity and commitment to strategically address the long-term needs of children, youth and families in e Washington, D.C. Its goal is to create a sustainable network of effective programs that encourages the healthy development of children and young people through support for quality out-of-school time programs and opportunities.

title: Report Card on San Diego Children
description: This grant will support the Report Card on San Diego Children, a project of the Children’s Initiative. The project will enable the citizens of San Diego to identify the most pressing issues facing children and families; analyze trends and their impact on families and communities; prioritize public and private efforts on behalf of children and families; and make recommendations for policy and program development that lead to systematic change.The Children’s Initiative is dedicated to assisting children, youth and families reach their full potential by working for integrated service delivery systems that promote the values of collaboration and prevention, and for measurable outcomes in the fields of health, education, safety and economic security.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will enable the Rural Workshop Foundation to provide a range of technical assistance and information services and programs to promote sustainable rural development in Hungary and Central/Eastern Europe. Assistance will include training and capacity building; mediation, facilitation and convening activities; a microgrant program for rural areas; and partnering with European and North American agencies to link local Hungarian efforts to regional and international programs on rural development.The organization was created in 1996 by a group of Hungarian experts, academics and practitioners involved in rural and regional development. Its mission is to stimulate horizontal multistakeholder cooperation at national and international levels between local and rural development initiatives, international networks, think tanks, businesses, and foundations interested in rural development.

title: Enhancing Fund Development for London Communities
description: The program goal is to build the capacity of an important, London-wide community foundation to raise funds from wealthy individuals and the business community in the United Kingdom. Program accomplishments to date include securing almost 500,000 Great Britain Pounds in seven new private funds; making significant inroads into the professional advisor field in London; and developing a district fund model. Additionally, Capital Community Foundation was successful in its bid to receive a 2.1 million GBP challenge grant from the government. In 2009-2011, the grantee will hire an assistant director for development to enhance its ongoing fund development activities and ensure that it meets the government’s challenge grant. The grantee’s mission is to improve the communities of London by supporting peoples’ ideas and initiatives. The foundation was created in 1995 as the South East London Community Foundation. In 2005, the foundation changed its name and its area of benefit to the whole of London.

title: Enhancing Fund Development for London Communities
description: This grant will enable the Capital Community Foundation to assemble an advisory group comprised of 15 influential and wealthy individuals; engage 20 financial advisors in recommending the foundation to their clients; develop links with companies by managing their funds and programs; learn from best practices in the United Kingdom and the U.S. in the area of fund development; and increase the foundation’s assets over the next two years.The foundation’s mission is to improve the communities of London by supporting people’s ideas and initiatives. Created in 1995 as the South East London Community Foundation, the foundation changed its name and its area of benefit to the whole of London in 2004.

title: Increasing Private Donations to the Russian Nonprofit Sector
description: The program goal is to involve more Russian citizens in supporting nonprofit organizations by improving their capacity to collect private donations and develop supportive constituencies. Building on its successful staging of a certified professional fundraising course, as well as over 30 training workshops involving 600 participants, the NGO School will work to improve organizations’ abilities to utilize the Internet and the growing social networking phenomenon to promote genuine grassroots fundraising. A dedicated fundraising Web site will be established to support this initiative. Additional activities will include a series of fundraising and resource mobilization workshops; ongoing experience sharing through meetings of a Fundraiser’s Club; and further enhancement of the grantee’s own fundraising capacity, based on its success in raising over 100,000 rubles for its course scholarships. Having evolved out of Charities Aid Foundation Russia, the NGO School provides a range of services supporting the professional growth of the nonprofit sector in Russia.

title: Increasing Private Donations to the Russian Nonprofit Sector
description: The program goal is to involve more Russian citizens in supporting nonprofit organizations by improving their capacity to collect private donations and develop supportive constituencies. The NGO School will work to strengthen the professional skills of the fundraising community through a series of fundraising and resource mobilization workshops and through ongoing experience sharing within a fundraisers’ club. It will also seek to use and catalogue successful fundraising strategies employed by a pilot project called the Live! Foundation, aimed at demonstrating the potential impact of innovative fundraising strategies in Russia. In 2008-2009, the grantee involved over 200 fundraisers in its training activities and saw the Live! Foundation raise over $40,000 from individuals at its inaugural fundraising event in Moscow. The NGO School was registered in 2002 and provides a range of services supporting the professional growth of the nonprofit sector in Russia.

title: Increasing Private Donations to the Russian Nonprofit Sector
description: The program goal is to promote individual giving in Russia. The Moscow office of the Charities Aid Foundation will promote growth in online giving through its blago.ru giving platform. It will also provide formal training courses and consultations to help Russian charities improve their fundraising skills and build greater financial resilience. The grantee will also widely disseminate best practices related to individual giving and targeted fundraising. In 2010-2012, in cooperation with the NGO School, the grantee staged two fundraising schools for professionals from across Russia. The blago.ru Web site saw individual donations increase in number by over 60 percent in 2011 and in value by almost 50 percent, to nearly $250,000. Based in the United Kingdom, the Charities Aid Foundation has offices in Russia, Australia, Bulgaria, India, South Africa, and the United States. It distributes more than $500 million annually to charitable causes worldwide on behalf of individual, corporate, and trust clients.

title: Increasing Private Donations to the Russian Nonprofit Sector
description: The program goal is to promote private giving in Russia. The Moscow office of the Charities Aid Foundation will promote growth in online giving through improvements to its www.blago.ru online giving platform. It will simultaneously launch a media and advertising campaign to foster awareness of, and inclination toward, opportunities for individual giving. The grantee will also widely disseminate best practices related to individual giving and targeted fundraising. In 2012-2014, the grantee staged two fundraising schools for professionals from across Russia. The www.blago.ru site saw the number of individual donations more than double, with their value increasing over this period by 90 percent to nearly $450,000. The site was also able to raise over $13,000 for its own operations. Based in the United Kingdom, the Charities Aid Foundation has offices in Russia, Australia, Bulgaria, India, South Africa, and the United States. It distributes more than $500 million annually to charitable causes worldwide on behalf of individual, corporate, and trust clients.

title: Increasing Private Donations to the Russian Nonprofit Sector
description: This grant will enable the NGO School to improve the capacity of Russian nonprofits to attract supporters and collect private donations. The NGO School will focus on three pilot regions – Moscow, Krasnodar and Nizhni Novgorod – and partner with leading non-governmental organizations (NGOs) in the latter two regions to implement the program. Activities will include researching existing techniques of soliciting donations from individuals and developing and testing new methods and approaches; clarifying and classifying all relevant legal aspects and issues; developing and implementing demonstration projects; providing training and coaching opportunities to project participants; and creating opportunities for information and experience exchange among a wide array of Russian nonprofit organizations through meetings of a Fundraisers’ Club and Web-based resources.The NGO School grew out of the work of the Charities Aid Foundation representative office in Russia, which was established in 1993 with the goal of supporting the development of civil society, philanthropy and the nonprofit sector in Russia. Today, its main goals are to provide information and legal support for NGOs, support the professional growth of the nonprofit sector, and develop relationships between NGOs and the commercial, governmental and nonprofit sectors in Russia.

title: Polish-Russian Cooperation Bridge for Active Communities Development
grantee: BORIS Association - Support Office for the Movement of Social Initiatives
description: This grant will enable the BORIS Association – Support Office for the Movement of Social Initiatives to assist in the transfer of knowledge between Polish and Russian non-governmental organizations (NGOs) in the areas of activating local communities, developing social marketing, and increasing philanthropy and social investment. The project will focus on the regions of Mazowsze in Poland and Nizhni Novgorod in Russia.Activities will include training seminars, study visits, internships, implementation of local community projects, technical assistance, publications on best practices, a project evaluation and a final conference. Results of the project will be broadly disseminated in both countries and are expected to lead to other partnership projects between Russia and Poland.Established in 1999, the organization’s mission is to encourage NGOs and public institutions to better respond to the needs of their communities in Warsaw and surrounding areas.

title: Institutional Development
description: The program goal is to strengthen organized philanthropy in Ukraine. This grant will assist the Ukrainian Philanthropists Forum to improve services for members, provide professional support to the wider philanthropic community, and raise the profile of philanthropy in Ukraine. The grantee will stage a variety of topical conferences and workshops for both members and a wider audience. An information and consulting center will be established to address professional development needs of philanthropic institutions. A new Web portal and a variety of publications will be used to communicate to the public about philanthropic trends. In 2007-2008, the grantee organized conferences on corporate social responsibility, community foundations, and standards in philanthropy. It co-organized the “Philanthropist of the Year” competition and published exclusive reports on charitable institutions and corporate philanthropy. Formally registered in 2005, the Ukrainian Philanthropists Forum is an association of local and international donors which promotes responsible and effective philanthropy for the development of Ukrainian society.

title: Institutional Development
description: The program goal is to strengthen organized philanthropy in Ukraine. To this end, this grant will assist the Ukrainian Philanthropists Forum to improve services for members, provide professional support to the philanthropic community, and raise the profile of philanthropy in Ukraine. The grantee will provide conferences and workshops for members and a wider audience. It will build its capacity for research and analysis through regular surveys of philanthropic trends in Ukraine. An improved Web portal and social media presence will help raise public understanding of philanthropy. In 2009-2010, the grantee organized a major research project, conference, and follow-up discussions focusing on philanthropy in times of crisis. In addition to 40 thematic events, the grantee also initiated publication of the “Philanthropic ABCs” series of practical guides for philanthropists. Formally registered in 2005, the Ukrainian Philanthropists Forum is an association of local and international donors promoting responsible and effective philanthropy in Ukraine.

title: Institutional Development
description: The program goal is to strengthen organized philanthropy in Ukraine. To this end, the Ukrainian Philanthropists Forum will strengthen its role as a platform for discussion and interaction among philanthropic organizations in Ukraine, develop its capacity for advocacy and policy development work, and increase professionalism in the philanthropic field. In addition, the grantee will participate actively in relevant international philanthropy development initiatives, including the Worldwide Initiatives for Grantmaker Support network. In 2011-2012, the grantee increased its membership, organized two international conferences on philanthropy, coordinated civil society efforts to improve the legal environment for philanthropy in Ukraine, and carried out a series of events to promote individual and corporate volunteering. Formally registered in 2005, the Ukrainian Philanthropists Forum is an association of 26 local and international donors promoting responsible and effective philanthropy in Ukraine.

title: Institutional Development
description: The program goal is to strengthen organized philanthropy in Ukraine. This grant will assist the Ukrainian Grantmakers Forum in its efforts to broaden its membership base and improve the quality of services provided to members. Key services will include information and publications, training workshops for staff of member organizations, advisory services to newly established foundations, and research on the state of philanthropy. Outreach activities, including an annual conference, a “Top-Philanthropist” competition, and active engagement with existing and potential corporate donors, will increase membership by over 50 percent during the grant period. Formally registered in 2005, the Ukrainian Grantmakers Forum is an association of local and international donors whose mission is to promote responsible and effective philanthropy for the development of Ukrainian society.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to increase civic activism and community engagement in Ukraine. Civic Network OPORA will work to strengthen regional networks of citizen activists throughout the country who can engage effectively in both regional and national advocacy campaigns and public monitoring activities. Key advocacy topics will include provision of housing and communal services, improved local government transparency, and an antitobacco campaign. The grantee will continue its monitoring of recently introduced independent university entrance tests and subsequent enrollment procedures. It will conduct nonpartisan long- and short-term public monitoring of upcoming presidential and parliamentary elections. In 2008, it initiated a coalition of 50 nongovernmental organizations to advocate for housing reform and oversaw a national effort to monitor standardized university entrance exams. Established in 2006, Civic Network OPORA has conducted a number of successful local, regional, and national public-interest campaigns on issues ranging from local historic preservation to national health promotion policy.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to increase civic activism and community engagement in Ukraine. Civic Network OPORA will work to strengthen regional networks of citizen activists throughout the country who can engage effectively in both regional and national advocacy campaigns and watchdog activities. The grantee will continue its monitoring of independent university entrance tests and subsequent enrollment procedures. It will conduct nonpartisan, long- and short-term public monitoring of upcoming parliamentary elections. In 2009-2011, it expanded the number of housing reform resource centers from four to ten. Its efforts to monitor standardized university entrance exams and subsequent admissions processes have contributed to the maintenance of these exams in the face of political and other pressure. Established in 2006, the grantee has conducted a number of successful local, regional, and national public interest campaigns on issues ranging from local historic preservation to a national health promotion policy.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to increase civic activism and community engagement in Ukraine. Civic Network OPORA will work to strengthen regional networks of citizen activist groups working on issues including local government transparency and communal services provisions. The grantee will continue its monitoring of independent university entrance tests and subsequent enrollment procedures to combat corruption in this realm. It will also conduct nonpartisan, long- and short-term public monitoring of the 2015 presidential elections. In 2011-2013, its expanded network of housing reform resource centers moved toward greater sustainability through membership fee support. Its monitoring of standardized university entrance exams and subsequent admissions processes has contributed to the maintenance of these exams in the face of political and other pressure. Established in 2006, Civic Network OPORA has conducted a number of successful local, regional, and national public interest campaigns on issues ranging from local historic preservation to a national health promotion policy.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to increase civic activism and community engagement in Ukraine. To this end, this grant supports the organizational and programmatic development of the Civic Network OPORA, a Ukrainian nongovernmental organization with offices throughout the country. During the grant period, the grantee will engage citizens to address issues, such as education and housing, through monitoring, participation in decisionmaking, and advocacy. The grantee will also involve citizens in parliamentary oversight activities and conduct nonpartisan public monitoring of the 2015 local elections. In 2013-2015, Civic Network OPORA organized domestic, citizen-led election monitoring of presidential, parliamentarian, and local elections. The grantee also supported housing associations in seven communities, raising residents’ awareness of energy efficiency and housing rights and responsibilities. In the field of higher education reform, the grantee promoted transparency in admissions processes by increasing citizen-monitoring and collaborating effectively with the Ministry of Education and Science.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to increase civic activism and community engagement in Ukraine. During the grant period, the Civic Network “OPORA” will engage citizens to address issues around housing, communal services, and energy efficiency. The grantee will also conduct parliamentary oversight activities and nonpartisan public monitoring of the 2019 presidential and parliamentary elections. In 2015-2017, Civic Network “OPORA” organized domestic, citizen-led election monitoring of local elections using innovative mobile monitoring teams. Its observation work received over 1,400 mentions in varied media outlets. The network also participated in over 300 events to support greater effectiveness of housing associations, raising residents’ awareness of energy efficiency and housing rights and responsibilities. In the field of higher education reform, Civic Network “OPORA” completed its efforts on monitoring entrance exams, with 90 percent of respondents confirming trust in the testing process. Established in 2006, Civic Network “OPORA” is an independent, national network of civic activists whose mission is to develop Ukrainian society on the principles of transparent policymaking.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to increase civic activism and community engagement in Ukraine. The grantee will work to strengthen regional networks of citizen activists throughout the country through regular residential workshops and distance learning courses. The regional networks will apply this knowledge in implementing both regional and joint national advocacy and public awareness campaigns. Key topics of the proposed campaigning may include provision of housing and communal services and local government transparency. These activities will help strengthen ties and improve coordination among regional advocacy partners. Civic Network OPORA has conducted a number of successful, local, public interest campaigns since its establishment in 2006.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to improve the observance of fundamental rights and freedoms in Ukraine. Drawing on its network of 23 member organizations throughout the country, the Ukrainian Helsinki Human Rights Union will work to protect victims of rights abuse through a network of legal advice centers and a program of strategic litigation. It will regularly monitor and report on the state of rights protection in Ukraine. The grantee will work to raise public awareness of human rights through a range of educational activities targeting young people and grassroots activists and will continue hosting an annual human rights documentary film festival. In 2008-2010, the grantee provided over 13,000 consultations through its legal advice centers and provided training to 350 educators and activists on key rights issues in Ukraine. Established in 2004, the union works to promote practical observance of the range of international human rights instruments to which Ukraine is a party.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to engage with active citizens and nonprofit groups to strengthen the protection of fundamental rights and freedoms in Ukraine. Through its network of 23 member organizations, the Ukrainian Helsinki Human Rights Union will work to raise public awareness of human rights through a range of informational and educational activities, including an annual human rights documentary film festival. It will continue a program of strategic litigation highlighting critical instances of rights abuse. The grantee will also monitor and report on the state of rights protection in Ukraine and will help establish a Human Rights House as a focal point for rights promotion. In 2011, the grantee provided over 11,000 consultations through its legal advice centers and saw traffic to its Web site almost triple to 424,000 unique visitors. Established in 2004, the Ukrainian Helsinki Human Rights Union works to promote practical observance of the range of international human rights instruments to which Ukraine is a party.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to engage with active citizens and nonprofit groups to strengthen the protection of fundamental rights and freedoms in Ukraine. To this end, the Ukrainian Helsinki Human Rights Union will strengthen its network and the capacities of its more than 20 members to: 1) promote and protect human rights through a range of information and educational activities; 2) increase strategic litigation and direct representation of victims through regional legal advice centers; and 3) monitor, research, and analyze the state of human rights in Ukraine. During 2012-2014, the grantee provided human rights training and educational opportunities for lawyers and community activists throughout Ukraine and published a range of books, leaflets, and online resource materials related to international human rights law. The grantee helped establish a Human Rights House as a focal point for rights promotion. The grantee supported and strengthened a network of 13 legal advice centers that provided 9,144 consultations. During the grant period, the grantee also co-organized three annual human rights documentary film festivals, the most recent of which attracted more than 40,000 people. Established in 2004, the Ukrainian Helsinki Human Rights Union works to promote practical observance of the range of international human rights instruments to which Ukraine is a party.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to engage with active citizens and nonprofit groups to strengthen the protection of fundamental rights and freedoms in Ukraine. Established in 2004, the grantee works to promote practical observance of the range of international human rights’ instruments to which Ukraine is a party. The grantee supports a network of more than 30 members around the country to: 1) promote and protect human rights through a range of information and educational activities; 2) increase strategic litigation and direct representation of victims through regional legal advice centers; and 3) monitor, research, and analyze the state of human rights in Ukraine. The grantee also supports a Human Rights House training and information center. A grant increase will allow the grantee to respond to the emerging and urgent need to increase training in local government/civic group interactions with a rights perspective and upgrade the Human Rights House facilities to accommodate an overall increased training demand.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen the protection of fundamental rights and freedoms in Ukraine. Through its network of 29 member organizations, the Ukrainian Helsinki Human Rights Union will work to raise public awareness of human rights through a range of monitoring, information, advocacy, and educational activities, including an annual human rights documentary film festival. It will continue a program of strategic litigation highlighting critical instances of rights abuse and oversee the work of a growing network of local public reception offices offering primary legal assistance to the community. In 2014-2016, the grantee provided over 37,000 consultations through its legal advice centers, which grew from 17 to 29. Through its analytical work, it contributed to the development of a National Strategy for Human Rights in Ukraine and subsequent National Action Plan for its implementation. Established in 2004, the Ukrainian Helsinki Human Rights Union works to promote practical observance of the range of international human rights instruments to which Ukraine is a party.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to improve the observance of fundamental rights and freedoms in Ukraine. Drawing on its network of 25 member organizations throughout the country, the Ukrainian Helsinki Human Rights Union will work to protect victims of rights abuse through a network of legal advice centers. It will regularly monitor and report on the state of rights protection in Ukraine. Through strategic litigation, it will take on key legal cases focusing on precedent-setting rights issues. The grantee will work to raise public awareness of human rights through a range of educational activities, including an annual documentary film festival. At the same time, efforts will be made to strengthen the capacity of the membership, with particular attention given to streamlining information exchange across the network. Established in 2004, the union works to promote practical implementation of the range of international human rights instruments to which Ukraine is a party.

title: Belarusian Social Information Bureaus
grantee: Working Community of Associations of Social Organizations
description: The program goal is to help Belarusian citizens understand and realize their rights related to social benefits and services. The grantee will work with the Belarusian Association of Social Workers to strengthen a national network of 12 social information bureaus in Belarus. Bureau staff will be trained in such practices as volunteer development and community activism. The bureaus will manage an informational database aimed at local residents seeking advice or redress on social, economic, and consumer issues. In the most recent grant period, this comprehensive database was thoroughly overhauled and updated, and project staff received training in new methods aimed at improving information and service provision for local citizens. Created in 2000 and based in Poland, the Working Community of Associations of Social Organizations is a federation of regional social work associations, which represents the interests of socially marginalized individuals and groups.

title: Belarusian Social Information Bureaus
grantee: Working Community of Associations of Social Organizations
description: The program goal is to help Belarusian citizens protect their rights and receive social services. The grantee will work in close partnership with the Belarusian Association of Social Workers to promote the sustainable development of a national network of 12 social information bureaus in Belarus. Staff of these bureaus will receive training and consulting assistance on such issues as volunteer development, cooperation with local government, and community activism. In addition, these bureaus will manage a unified database of social and legal assistance information accessible to local residents seeking assistance or redress on social, economic, and consumer issues. The grantee and its Belarusian partner will also conduct public information campaigns to familiarize more Belarusians with the bureaus and the services they offer. Created in 2000 and based in Poland, the Working Community of Associations of Social Organizations is a federation of regional social work associations, which seeks to represent the interests of socially marginalized individuals and groups.

title: Strategic Planning
description: Midwest Community Foundations’ Ventures (MCFV) is a supporting organization of the Council of Michigan Foundations (CMF). In October 2005, CMF’s board approved a recommendation to add representatives to the board of MCFV from the states of Ohio, Illinois and Indiana.This grant will provide facilitation assistance for strategic planning and program implementation. Anticipated outcomes from the six-month planning process include a three-year business plan, agreement on project priorities and an implementation plan, a plan for the delivery of technical assistance for compliance with community foundation standards, and a communications plan.

title: General Purposes
