description: This grant renewal will provide general purposes support to the Resource Center, a local agency that provides volunteer and information services in Flint and Genesee County. The agency was formed in 1997 through the merger of several long-standing local entities: Leadership Flint, the Flint Executive Service Corps, and the United Way’s Voluntary Action Center and First Call for Help Service. The Resource Center’s mission is to “mobilize people and resources to creatively solve community problems.” Continued general purposes support will help the Resource Center address the community’s volunteer and information services needs.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant renewal will provide general purpose support to the Resource Center, a local agency that provides volunteer and information services in Flint and Genesee County. The agency was formed in 1997 through the merger of several long-standing local entities: Leadership Flint, the Flint Executive Service Corps, and the United Way’s Voluntary Action Center and First Call for Help services. The Resource Center’s mission is to “mobilize people and resources to creatively solve community problems.” Continued general purposes support will help the Resource Center address the community’s volunteer and information services needs.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant renewal will provide general purpose support to Resource Genesee, a local agency that provides volunteer and information services in Flint and Genesee County. Formed in 1997 through the merger of several long-standing local entities (Leadership Flint, the Flint Executive Service Corps, and the United Way’s Volunteer Center and First Call for Help programs), the grantee’s mission is to mobilize people and resources to creatively solve community problems. Continued general purpose support will help the grantee address the county’s volunteer and information services needs.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant renewal will provide general purpose support to Resource Genesee, a local agency that provides volunteer and information services in Flint and Genesee County. The agency was formed in 1997 through the merger of several long-standing local entities: Leadership Flint, the Flint Executive Service Corps, and the United Way’s Voluntary Action Center and First Call for Help services. Resource Genesee’s mission is to mobilize people and resources to creatively solve community problems. Continued general purpose support will help the grantee address the community’s volunteer and information services needs.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will enable the Resource Center to continue providing volunteer and information services in Flint and Genesee County. The center was formed in 1997 through the merger of several long-standing local entities: Leadership Flint, Flint Executive Service Corps, and the United Way’s Voluntary Action Center and First Call for Help Service.

title: Social Justice Programme
description: The Diakonia Council of Churches is an ecumenical organization consisting of member churches and church agencies in KwaZulu-Natal. It works through the churches promoting effective engagement in social justice issues. By convening workshops, seminars, and briefings at the community level and disseminating educational materials, the council has fostered peace, healing, and reconciliation; increased participation in democratic governance; advocated for socioeconomic rights of the poor; promoted gender awareness and equity; and enabled effective responses to the HIV/AIDS pandemic. This grant will support continuation of these social justice programs for the next two years.

title: Social Justice Programme
description: The Diakonia Council of Churches is an interchurch agency working with churches and church organizations to promote justice, development, and peace in the KwaZulu-Natal province of South Africa. It works through member churches to promote effective engagement in social justice issues, as well as issues related to economic and environmental justice. The Social Justice Programme fosters peace, healing, and reconciliation within various communities. It also works to increase people’s participation in democratic governance, particularly at the local level, in order to give them a voice in government planning processes. Past support assisted the grantee to convene workshops, seminars, and briefings at the community level on topics including stress and trauma, conflict and mediation, and democracy and governance. The grantee also supports groups to implement income-generating projects to improve their livelihoods.

title: Social Justice Programme
description: Diakonia Council of Churches created the Social Justice Programme to foster peace, promote healing and reconciliation, address the marginalization and discrimination of social groups, and develop effective responses to the HIV/AIDS pandemic.This grant will enable the council to implement the program through residential workshops; trauma healing and counseling sessions; and advocacy on behalf of the poor, vulnerable and marginalized.Diakonia Council of Churches is an interfaith agency with a long history of opposing apartheid and working with communities to promote justice, development and peace.

title: Community Healing and Development Program
description: The Cradock Masizame Community Development Centre was established to serve as a vehicle for development in the area of Cradock and surrounding towns in the Eastern Cape. Cradock is a small, rural town in the Eastern Cape that was in the forefront of the struggle against apartheid. Its fierce resistance led to it being targeted by the apartheid regime, with many atrocities committed against the black community. Through previous support, the centre implemented a community healing and development process that sought to assist the community to overcome its violent past, facilitate intracommunity dialogue, and promote reconciliation. The programs involved a wide range of people within the community including youth, teachers, women’s groups, and church ministers. This grant will assist the Cradock Masizame Community Development Centre to continue with this work.

title: Community Healing and Development Program
description: Cradock is a small, rural town in the Eastern Cape that was in the forefront of the struggle against apartheid. Its fierce resistance made it a target of the apartheid regime, with many atrocities committed against the black community. The most brutal was the 1985 assassination – by mostly white, state security forces – of four of the community’s most prominent black leaders, a case infamously referred to as the “Cradock Four.” Today, many are still devastated and traumatized by these events of the past, and the old divisions between whites and blacks persist.This grant will enable the Cradock Masizame Community Development Centre to support a community healing and development process to assist the community in overcoming its violent past, facilitate intracommunity dialogue and promote reconciliation. The program will be based on the lessons and recommendations of South Africa’s Truth and Reconciliation Commission, and are designed to deal with both the individual and the collective. It will use a combination of oral interviews, meetings, workshops and seminars.The center was established in 1989 to serve as a vehicle for development in the area of Cradock and surrounding towns in the Eastern Cape.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide continued general purpose support to the Institute for Healing of Memories, an organization created to contribute to the healing of individuals and communities affected by the political conflict and violence during apartheid, and to share South Africa’s experience of dealing with its past with the broader international community. The institute’s core program is its Healing of Memories workshops, which provide a safe space for dialogue and openness to deal with issues such as reconciliation, forgiveness, dealing with the past, restorative justice, peace-building, and conflict resolution. In addition to workshops for individuals coping with the aftermath of apartheid, it has applied the same methodology to three new challenges facing South Africa: criminal violence in prisons, refugees, and HIV/AIDS.

title: General Purposes
description: The Institute for Healing of Memories was created to contribute to the healing of individuals and communities affected by the political conflict and violence during apartheid and to share South Africa’s experience of dealing with its past with the broader international community. The institute’s core program is its Healing of Memories workshops, which provide a safe space for dialogue and openness to deal with issues such as reconciliation, forgiveness, dealing with the past, restorative justice, peace building, and conflict resolution. Past achievements include working with youth to teach them about the past and reconciliation and conducting healing workshops for refugees, prisoners, and people infected by HIV/AIDS. This grant will assist the institute to continue with these activities and strengthen its partnership and collaboration with various institutions that implement programs related to healing and reconciliation.

title: General Purposes
description: The Institute for Healing of Memories was created to contribute to the healing of individuals and communities affected by the political conflict and violence during apartheid and to share South Africa’s experience of dealing with its past with the broader international community. The grantee’s core program is its Healing of Memories workshops, which provide a safe space for dialogue and openness to deal with issues such as reconciliation, forgiveness, dealing with the past, restorative justice, peace building, and conflict resolution. In addition to workshops for individuals coping with the aftermath of apartheid, it has applied the same methodology to three new challenges facing South Africa: criminal violence in prisons, refugees, and HIV/AIDS. This grant increase will provide continued general purpose support to the grantee.

title: General Purposes
description: The Institute for Healing of Memories was created to contribute to the healing of individuals and communities affected by the political conflict and violence during apartheid and to share South Africa’s experience of dealing with its past with the broader international community. The core program is its Healing of Memories workshops, which provide a safe space for dialogue and openness to deal with issues such as reconciliation, forgiveness, dealing with the past, restorative justice, peace building, and conflict resolution. It has applied the same methodology to other challenges facing South Africa including criminal violence in prisons, refugees, and HIV/AIDS. Past achievements include working with youth to teach them about the past and reconciliation; conducting healing workshops for interfaith communities, refugees, prisoners, and people infected by HIV/AIDS; and getting accreditation from a South African university for its training programs.

title: General Purposes
description: The Institute for Healing of Memories was created to contribute to the healing of individuals and communities affected by the political conflict and violence during apartheid and to share South Africa’s experience of dealing with its past with the broader international community. The core program is its Healing of Memories workshops, which provide a safe space for dialogue and openness to deal with issues such as reconciliation, forgiveness, dealing with the past, restorative justice, peace building, and conflict resolution. Past achievements include creating a knowledge hub on healing, trauma, reconciliation, and transformative justice; facilitating community conversations to improve tolerance among diverse groups; and conducting healing workshops for various groups including interfaith communities, refugees, prisoners, and people infected by HIV/AIDS. This grant renewal will support the Institute for Healing of Memories to continue supporting various individuals and communities in their healing journeys.

title: General Purposes
description: The Institute for Healing of Memories was created to contribute to the healing of individuals and communities affected by the political conflict and violence during apartheid and to share South Africa’s experience of dealing with its past with the broader international community. It works in five provinces across South Africa, and the core program is its Healing of Memories workshops, which provide a safe space for dialogue and openness to deal with issues such as reconciliation, forgiveness, dealing with the past, restorative justice, peace building, and conflict resolution. Past achievements include hosting dialogues in response to xenophobic attacks in South Africa to promote tolerance and understanding; documenting stories of healing through print and digital media; and hosting an international conference called Culture Genocide: Journey of Indigenous Healing. This grant renewal will support the grantee to continue supporting various individuals and communities in their healing journeys.

title: General Purposes
description: The Institute for Healing of Memories was established in 1998 to contribute to the healing of individuals and communities affected by political conflict and violence during apartheid and to share South Africa’s experience of dealing with its past with the broader international community. The institute offers healing workshops, counseling sessions, seminars, and discussions on such issues as reconciliation, forgiveness, dealing with the past, restorative justice, peacebuilding and conflict resolution. By providing a safe space for dialogue and openness, it has developed a unique model for dealing with emotions such as anger, hatred and guilt, which includes an experiential way of learning about and from the past.This grant will support the various activities and work of the institute, in particular its Healing of Memories workshops, which are at the core of its programs.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide continued general purpose support to the Institute for Justice and Reconciliation, one of the leading organizations dealing with issues of transitional justice, truth and reconciliation commissions, and peace building in Africa. The institute focuses on the challenges of reconciliation and nation building in South Africa, following the many years of racial conflict as a result of the system of apartheid. The institute works with communities affected by conflict, conducts research on issues of transitional justice and reconciliation, supports efforts aimed at peace building, and uses the experience of South Africa’s peaceful transition to democracy to assist and advise other countries, particularly in Africa, to find nonviolent solutions to their own conflicts.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will continue general purpose support to the Institute for Justice and Reconciliation, one of Africa’s leading organizations dealing with peace building and transitional justice issues. It focuses on the challenges of reconciliation and nation building in South Africa stemming from apartheid. The institute has worked with communities affected by conflict, conducted research on transitional justice issues and reconciliation, supported peace building efforts, and used the experience of South Africa’s peaceful transition to democracy to assist and advise other African countries in finding nonviolent solutions to their own conflicts. Major activities in the next period include tracking and analyzing reconciliation trends in post-conflict societies in South Africa and the region; providing policy advice and facilitating dialogues; implementing community engagement activities to advance post-conflict reconstruction and development; and developing educational resources.

title: General Purposes
description: The Institute for Justice and Reconciliation was formed by leading members of South Africa’s Truth and Reconciliation Commission. It focuses on the challenges of reconciliation and nation building in South Africa, following the many years of racial conflict as a result of the system of apartheid. The Institute works with communities affected by conflict; conducts research on issues of transitional justice and reconciliation; supports efforts aimed at peace building; and uses the experience of South Africa’s peaceful transition to democracy to assist and advise societies in other parts of the world.This grant will enable the institute to implement its work and various programs on reconciliation and transitional justice in South Africa and the broader African continent over the next two years.

title: Capacity Building Assistance
description: South End in Port Elizabeth in the Eastern Cape was a victim of apartheid’s notorious Group Areas Act, which prohibited people of color from living in areas declared white. The occupants of South End, mainly colored people of mixed descent, were forcibly removed in the 1960s and 1970s and relocated to far, outlying areas. Many of the former residents believe that the memory of what happened should be preserved for future generations and have come together to establish a museum documenting the forced removal and the impact that this had on the lives of all those who were affected. This planning grant will provide support to the South End Museum Trust to use the services of a consultant to assess its strengths and weaknesses; develop a workplan on the museum’s capacity needs; and make recommendations on how to secure its long-term sustainability.

title: Truth in Translation Project
description: The Truth in Translation Project was created to tell the story of South Africa’s Truth and Reconciliation Commission from the perspective of the interpreters who translated the testimony into the many languages spoken in South Africa. Presented in the form of a play accompanied by music, the project aims to highlight the trauma, anger, sadness and healing that accompanied South Africa’s attempt to deal with the political violence and human rights abuses of the apartheid past.This grant will enable Colonnades Theatre Lab to take the play to all the areas in South Africa that still struggle to come to terms with the conflicts of the past , as well as to international audiences in conflict-ridden places like Palestine, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Northern Ireland.The Colonnades Theatre Lab was established in 2005 to promote the arts and culture in South Africa, specifically performance drama.

title: Citizen Base Initiative
description: The Citizen Base Initiative program aims to identify and reward innovative strategies that enhance the sustainability of civil society-based organizations in Southern Africa. Through this program, Ashoka Innovators for the Public will continue to identify and recognize civil society organizations that have been effective in building their sustainability. Learning circles and publications will be used to share information and best practices with social entrepreneurs and the sector. The organization will also continue to build and strengthen its partnerships with academic institutions to develop the skill base of individuals within social organizations and build the capacity of those organizations. To date, a total of 83 organizations and 111 individuals have participated in the learning circles and benefited from the exchanges. Ashoka was established in 1990 to promote social entrepreneurship, community development, and the sustainability of the civil society sector in South Africa and the southern Africa region.

title: Citizen Base Initiative
description: Ashoka Innovators for the Public was established in 1990 to promote social entrepreneurship, community development and the sustainability of the civil society sector in South Africa and the southern Africa region. This grant will enable Ashoka Innovators for the Public to host an annual competition to recognize civil society organizations that have been effective in building their sustainability. Strategies that will be considered include social enterprises, community wealth, investment opportunities, and innovative ways of recovering and reducing costs. The grant also will support training and development, dissemination of knowledge and best practices, and capacity building for organizations.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide continued general purpose support to the Community Based Development Programme. The grantee works mainly with community-based organizations in some of the poorest and most marginalized regions of South Africa, providing capacity building, leadership training, and organizational development skills to empower their members to develop sustainable livelihoods and participate more effectively in local economic development. Its two primary initiatives are the Community Empowerment for Development program that provides organizational capacity building to enhance their effectiveness and the Development Management course that offers specific training to middle- and senior-level leaders of nonprofit organizations.

title: General Purposes
description: The Community Based Development Programme provides leadership and organizational development training to empower community-based organizations in poor communities to participate more effectively in local economic development initiatives that improve the quality of people’s lives. Previous support enabled it to implement the Community Empowerment for Development program, which provided organizational capacity building to enhance the effectiveness of community-based organizations in Gauteng and Mpumalanga provinces. This grant will provide continued support to the grantee to train, mentor, and support community-based organizations in some of the poorest and most marginalized regions of South Africa. It will also run the Development Management Certificate course in collaboration with the University of the Witwatersrand in Johannesburg, which offers specific training to middle- and senior-level leaders of nonprofit organizations.

title: General Purposes
description: The Community Based Development Programme provides leadership and organizational development training to community-based organizations working in poor communities in South Africa. The training courses empower community-based organizations to participate meaningfully in local economic development initiatives designed to improve the lives of marginalized communities. Previous support enabled the grantee to provide organizational strengthening training to enhance the effectiveness of community-based organizations through its Community Empowerment for Development program. This grant will provide continued funding to train and support community-based organizations in existing communities and to identify community-based organizations that need similar training in other communities. It will also help build the Women in Social Empowerment program, which offers specific training to women working in small scale farming.

title: General Purposes
description: The Community Based Development Programme (CBDP) provides training and capacity building for grassroots and community-based organizations to enable them to be more effective in achieving their goals and objectives. It provides training and support in administrative and financial skills, project management, procedures of meetings, record keeping, marketing, fundraising, and report writing.This grant will enable CBDP to work with poor and vulnerable communities in the Greater Johannesburg Metropolitan Municipality, providing capacity building, leadership training and organizational development skills.The CBDP was established in 1989 by the Kagiso Trust and University of the Witwatersrand to transfer development and management skills to nonprofit leaders. It focuses on community development and community leadership.

title: Umzimkulu Professionals Initiative
description: The Umzimkulu Professionals Initiative project was started by local black professionals from Umzimkulu, a very poor and rural area in the Eastern Cape. These professionals, who have been fortunate enough to do well, believe that they have a responsibility to contribute to the development of their community by giving something back in the form of funds, skills, expertise and time.This grant will support the growth, development and strengthening of the Umzimkulu Professionals Initiative as a viable, indigenous and community-based philanthropic initiative. The initiative will identify challenges and projects with the community and then seek the necessary resources to respond to these challenges and implement various projects. The emphasis in selecting projects is focused on poverty eradication, local economic development and long-term sustainability. The Kromhoek Development Trust was established in late 2005 to raise and manage funding for development on behalf of the Kromhoek Community in the Eastern Cape.

title: Research and Capacity Building
grantee: Volunteer and Service Enquiry Southern Africa
geographic_focus: Zambia, Botswana, Malawi, South Africa, Zimbabwe
description: Volunteer and Service Enquiry Southern Africa focuses on developing knowledge and profiling and linking community service and volunteering programs through research, capacity building and the support of an information network throughout South Africa and the southern African region. Presently, it is engaged in a five-country study that focuses on civic service and volunteering in Botswana, South Africa, Malawi, Zambia and Zimbabwe. Part of the study involves building the capacity of local researchers to be able to document the size, nature and scope of volunteering programs and policies in their respective countries. This grant will enable all local researchers to attend a two-day training and capacity-building workshop in South Africa.

title: Afterschool Pilot Project
description: The Nelson Mandela Children’s Fund was established by former South African President Nelson Mandela to address the plight of children in South Africa. The Nelson Mandela Children’s Fund seeks to change the way in which society treats children and youth in order to improve their lives. This grant will enable the fund to pilot an afterschool supplementary education program in partnership with Mindset Network, a multimedia, interactive, educational project aimed at improving teaching and learning in South African schools, particularly among disadvantaged groups and communities. The program will provide afterschool instruction, especially in mathematics and the sciences; training in the use of information and communication technology; and teaching of life skills to enable young people to make informed choices around issues of sexuality, HIV/AIDS, career planning and civic responsibility.

title: Microenterprise Finance in Areas Affected by Hurricanes Katrina and Rita
description: This grant will enable Enterprise Corporation of the Delta (ECD) to provide more than $2 million in microenterprise loans to nearly 100 low-income and minority small business owners whose assets were destroyed by hurricanes Katrina and Rita. ECD will partner with Hope Community Credit Union, which has opened no-fee checking and savings accounts for individuals and businesses affected by the storms. The project builds on strong networks with faith- and community-based organizations that work closely with low-income residents, and on the credit union’s ability to leverage grant funds with insured deposits.ECD is a nonprofit organization dedicated to strengthening communities, building assets and improving lives in economically distressed areas in the Mid South.

title: Neighborhood Redevelopment and Greenbelt Project
description: Located a few blocks north of downtown Flint, the Hurley Medical Center provides clinical excellence through regional services that offer the highest level of care available in mid-Michigan. As a major institutional presence, the center has the potential to be a catalyst for the development of a vibrant, mixed-use, urban area in central Flint.This grant will provide partial support to the Hurley Foundation to create and implement the Neighborhood Redevelopment and Greenbelt Project. The project is a component of the center’s Master Facility and Land Use Development Plan for the hospital’s main campus and surrounding properties.The Hurley Foundation was created in 1993 to facilitate charitable fundraising for the medical center. Its goal is to foster Hurley’s leadership role in addressing issues that affect the well-being of mid-Michigan residents.

title: Repairs to Durant-Dort Carriage Company Office Building
description: This grant will enable the Genesee County Historical Society to repair the first floor of the Durant-Dort Carriage Company office building, which has been dropping because of a rotting floor support frame and joists. Constructed in 1896 at 315 West Water Street in Flint, the building was the original headquarters of the Durant-Dort Carriage Company and eventually the birthplace of General Motors. Designated a National Historic Landmark in 1975, the building currently houses the Genesee County Historical Society and the Flint Area Convention and Visitors Bureau. The building’s public meeting spaces also are used by various community groups including Carriage Town Historic Neighborhood Association, Genesee Freenet, Buick Club of America, Downtown Challenge groups, Sister Cities and Wireless Genesee.The Historical Society was established in 1863 to encourage the collection and preservation of historic materials and encourage greater public interest in the historical activities of Genesee County.

title: Downtown Relocation and Expansion
description: The Community Foundation of Greater Flint (CFGF) serves a vital role in the charitable and nonprofit community in the Flint area. Recently, it completed a strategic plan that will continue to build upon strengths, as well as focus on new and critical issues in the community. As a result of the strategic plan, the organization will need to relocate to a larger office.This grant will provide funds to offset the increased occupancy costs that will result from CFGF’s office relocation. To combine the need for more office space with the goal of supporting the redevelopment of downtown Flint, CFGF is moving into a renovated building on South Saginaw Street.CFGF, founded in 1988 through the merger of the Flint Public Trust and the Flint Area Health Foundation, works to improve the quality of life for people in the Greater Flint area.

title: Developing a New Generation of Nonprofit Leaders
description: This grant will support the planning stage of the Center for Community Change’s program to identify and train a new generation of leaders capable of building and managing nonprofit organizations. With an emphasis on recruiting people from low-income communities and communities of color, the project will develop new and creative methods for staff recruitment, promote existing training efforts, and utilize best practices to create new training programs to increase the scale of nonprofit leadership development in the U.S.The Center for Community Change provides technical assistance in community development, community organizing, organizational development and public policy support to grassroots community groups in low-income areas throughout the U.S.

geographic_focus: Illinois, New Mexico, Georgia, California, Texas, Connecticut
description: The Appleseed Foundation is a network of nonprofit organizations with expertise in public interest law. This grant will provide partial support for research, technical assistance, and training on the No Child Left Behind law for local community organizations.

title: Research and Technical Assistance on No Child Left Behind Law
geographic_focus: Connecticut, Washington, Illinois, Texas, North Carolina, Georgia, New Mexico
description: No Child Left Behind (NCLB) is designed as a market accountability system for public schools that identifies parents and communities as keys for change and improvement. The question remains, however, whether this market accountability system is functioning effectively; that is, whether parents and other community members receive, understand and can act on the information gathered under NCLB. This grant will provide partial support for research, technical assistance and training on NCLB for local community organizations. The project will include a series of interviews and surveys in 20 school districts to find out what principals, teachers, parents and community groups know about NCLB and the parent engagement provisions. Based on the findings, training and assistance will be provided to parents and community groups in the same 20 school districts on what NCLB means for them and how they can use the provisions of the law to improve their schools. In addition, the project will include canvassing school districts throughout the country to identify model parent information and involvement programs. The Appleseed Foundation is a network of nonprofit organizations with expertise in public interest law. Working at the local level to identify and address community issues, Appleseed Centers form partnerships to develop practical solutions to issues in public education, health care, child welfare and immigration.

title: Bulgarian Community Foundations Development Fund
grantee: Trust for Civil Society in Central and Eastern Europe
description: The program goal is to support the development of local philanthropy and community foundations in Bulgaria. During the grant period, the Trust for Civil Society in Central and Eastern Europe will provide funding to the existing community foundations in Bulgaria to match their locally raised grantmaking funds and strengthen their fundraising capacities. The trust was established in 2000 by a consortium of private grantmaking foundations, including the Mott Foundation. The trust supports the development and long-term stabilization of civil society in Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, Romania, Slovakia, and Slovenia. During 2001-2007, the trust disbursed over $35.7 million in grants. This grant increase will enable the Bulgarian community foundations to increase the level of locally raised regranting funds and explore new funding sources and strategies.

title: Bulgarian Community Foundations Development Fund
description: The program goal is to support the development of local philanthropy and community foundations in Bulgaria. During the grant period, the Workshop for Civic Initiatives Foundation will provide funding to community foundations in Bulgaria to match their locally raised grantmaking funds and strengthen their institutional capacities. In addition, the foundation will support initiative groups with strong potential to develop community foundations in at least three new localities. Also, the foundation will cooperate with the Association of Community Foundations in Bulgaria to promote the concept of community foundations and to increase the level of resources available to them from private and public sources. Since its establishment in 2001, the foundation has distributed more than $1 million in grants and provided training to over 250 grassroots, nonprofit organizations. This project was previously supported with grants to the Trust for Civil Society in Central and Eastern Europe.

title: Bulgarian Community Foundations Development Fund
description: The program goal is to support the development of local philanthropy and community foundations in Bulgaria. During the grant period, the Workshop for Civic Initiatives Foundation will provide institutional development grants to ten existing community foundations in Bulgaria to strengthen their institutional capacities and improve their fundraising and fund development strategies. In addition, the grantee will support initiative groups with a strong potential to develop community foundations in at least three new localities. Also, the grantee will cooperate with the Association of Community Foundations in Bulgaria to promote the concept of community foundations and to increase the level of resources available to them from private and public sources. Key project results to date include strengthening the role of community foundations as key supporters for local grassroots organizations; raising twice the amount of the project grant funding from local resources; and establishing new community foundations in three of the largest cities in Bulgaria, including the capital Sofia.

title: Bulgarian Community Foundations Development Fund
description: The program goal is to support the development of local philanthropy and community foundations in Bulgaria. Also, the grantee will strengthen youth involvement in philanthropy and community development by developing a network of at least 15 YouthBanks in Bulgaria. Key project results in the past two years include strengthening the leadership role of community foundations in local development, establishing two new community foundations, and promoting new philanthropic initiatives on the local level, including collaborative giving circles and YouthBanks. The grantee is based in Sofia, Bulgaria.

title: Widening "Youth Today" Web Presence
description: This grant will enable the American Youth Work Center to upgrade and overhaul its Web site in order to create greater synergy between its “Youth Today” print publication and online equivalent. Since 1992, the American Youth Work Center has published “Youth Today”, a nationally distributed newspaper aimed at practitioners in the youth-service field. “Youth Today” provides independent coverage of promising practices, issues, trends, research and policies that shape the provision of services to youth, with special emphasis on disadvantaged youth. This grant also will enable the American Youth Work Center to improve the design and layout of “Youth Today”.

title: Strengthening Policies and Practices for Out-of-School Youth
description: This grant increase will enable the National Youth Employment Coalition to extend its work on identifying and developing policies and practices that support education options for students who have dropped out or are at risk of dropping out of school. Through this project, the National Youth Employment Coalition has worked with states and local communities to link their education reform efforts with strategies that integrate the needs of out-of-school youth. With this grant increase, the National Youth Employment Coalition will build on its state-level work by adding the state of Michigan as one of its profiled sites in the project. This increase will also provide an opportunity for select staff at the National Youth Employment Coalition to participate in a series of trainings to enhance their communications capacity in supporting the expansion of alternative education pathways for dropouts and near dropouts.

title: Expanding Education Options for Struggling Students and Disconnected Youth: Building Capacity and Informing Policy
description: This grant will enable the National Youth Employment Coalition to continue to work with states, local communities, and other leading groups in expanding education options for disconnected youth. Over the past two years, the grantee has engaged a subset of states and local communities in identifying and developing policies and practices that support educational pathways for students who are at risk or have already dropped out of school. During the next phase of this effort, the National Youth Employment Coalition will help build capacity at the local and state levels by serving as a technical resource provider to interested and targeted communities, developing a set of core policy principles on expanded options for disconnected youth, and informing the national policy discussion on the issues and needs of such youth.

title: Building Capacity and Informing Policy to Better Serve Disconnected Youth
description: This grant will enable the National Youth Employment Coalition to continue to work with states, communities, and other stakeholders to expand education options for disconnected youth. Over the past two years, the grantee has engaged in a multifaceted effort to help build the capacity of systems and organizations that serve struggling students and disconnected youth. During the next phase of this effort, the grantee will convene a series of peer-to-peer learning exchanges to encourage local and state leaders to develop better strategies for serving disconnected youth and intensify efforts to inform national policy discussions to place the needs of such youth more firmly on the nation’s agenda.

title: Building Capacity and Informing Policy to Better Serve Disconnected Youth
description: This grant will enable the National Youth Employment Coalition to continue to help build the capacity of youth-serving systems and organizations to serve disconnected youth. During the most recent phase of this project, the grantee served as a resource to those working to expand education options for disconnected youth by facilitating peer-to-peer learning exchanges through publications, convenings, and providing technical assistance to policymakers, member organizations, and other stakeholders. Recommended support will enable the grantee to build the evidence base for expanding quality practice to serve disconnected youth and inform national policy discussions at the state and federal levels.

title: Building Capacity and Informing Policy to Better Serve Disconnected Youth
description: This grant will enable the National Youth Employment Coalition to continue to help build the capacity of systems and organizations to serve disconnected youth. In 2014, the grantee will celebrate its 35th anniversary. The grantee has been one of the few youth-centered organizations working in the intersection of policy and practice to expand education options for disconnected youth. Through peer-to-peer learning exchanges, convenings, policy forums, and technical assistance, the grantee has worked to improve the coordination of activities among national stakeholders in the areas of education, employment, and training on behalf of disconnected youth. Recommended support will enable the grantee to build the evidence base for expanding quality practice to serve disconnected youth and inform national policy discussions at the state and federal levels.

title: Strengthening Policies and Practices for Out-of-School Youth
description: This grant will enable the National Youth Employment Coalition to work with states, local communities, education systems and leading policy groups to develop viable options and alternative pathways to a diploma for dropouts and potential dropouts. Through this project, the coalition will help strengthen the linkages between local and state reform efforts that integrate strategies for out-of-school youth and support the expansion of alternative education pathways.The coalition is a broad-based membership organization dedicated to promoting employment, education and training opportunities for traditionally underserved youth. During the past few years, it has worked to expand its education efforts by linking them to broader reform measures that focus on raising standards, increasing graduation rates and integrating strategies for out-of-school youth within current reform efforts.

title: Policy Strategies and Actions Addressing the Needs of High School Dropouts in the South
description: This grant will enable the Southern Education Foundation to continue to monitor dropout rates in Alabama, Louisiana, and Mississippi in an effort to focus more attention on the consequences of students in the South not completing school. In the most recent phase of the project, the grantee developed a strategically placed network of advocates in the targeted states to push for more effective programs and policies that reduced dropout rates and refocused attention on the thousands of students who dropped out of school in the aftermath of Hurricane Katrina. During the next phase, the grantee will encourage the development of dropout recovery programs, monitor the implementation of new and innovative policies that reduce dropout rates, convene stakeholders on addressing graduation/dropout issues, and disseminate key reports and findings on short- and long-term strategies that address the needs of dropouts in the South.

title: Policy Strategies and Actions Addressing the Needs of High School Dropouts in the South
description: This grant will enable the Southern Education Foundation to continue to promote and build policy strategies and actions that address the needs of high school dropouts in the South. In the most recent phase of this project, the grantee monitored the implementation of new and innovative dropout policies in Alabama and Louisiana, encouraged education officials in Mississippi to create an office of dropout prevention, and convened regional stakeholders to discuss additional efforts that address the needs of dropouts. During the next phase, the grantee will continue to make the dropout issue a top policymaking priority in the South, as funding opportunities surface via new federal mandates/efforts to improve schools and graduation rates.

title: Policy Strategies and Actions Addressing the Needs of High School Dropouts in the South
description: This grant will enable the Southern Education Foundation to continue to promote and build policy strategies and actions that address the needs of high school dropouts in the South. In the most recent phase of this project, the grantee assisted stakeholders in Alabama, Louisiana, and Mississippi in utilizing federal funds to address the issue of dropouts and identifying discrepancies under new mandates to calculate/report high school graduation rates. During the next phase, the grantee will continue to make the dropout issue a top policymaking priority in the South by examining the correlation between high rates of school suspensions and low rates of high school graduation, particularly for minority males, across the broader region.

title: Policy Strategies and Actions Addressing the Needs of High School Dropouts in the South
description: Following Hurricane Katrina, many young people in the South had their educations temporarily interrupted or postponed indefinitely. Graduation rates in many southern states are some of the lowest nationwide, and the storm’s impact is putting more students at risk of not graduating.This grant will enable the Southern Education Foundation to monitor dropout rates in Alabama, Louisiana and Mississippi in an effort to begin laying the groundwork for efforts that advance policies and practices to address the needs of dropouts in the South. The Southern Education Foundation is a Georgia-based regional public charity that works to improve education policy and practice in the South.

title: Improving Outcomes for Out-of-School Youth in Michigan
description: This grant will enable Michigan’s Children to continue its intermediary efforts in the Improving Outcomes for Out-of-School Youth in Michigan project. As the statewide intermediary for this project, Michigan’s Children has been central in launching and spearheading this initiative from identifying the four communities participating in this project — Detroit, Flint, Grand Rapids, and Kalamazoo — to raising awareness on the need to ensure that out of-school youth have a chance to earn a diploma. Recommended support will allow the grantee to assist participating sites in the project to develop strategies and plans to move policy and practice in a direction to improve outcomes for out-of-school youth in their communities.

title: Improving Outcomes for Out-of-School Youth in Michigan
description: This grant will enable Michigan’s Children to continue its intermediary efforts via the Improving Outcomes for Out-of-School Youth in Michigan project. As the statewide intermediary for this initiative, Michigan’s Children has brought unprecedented attention to the issue of students failing to graduate from high school by working with key state departments, interagency task forces, and communities to assess the current investments and public policies that create barriers or opportunities for young people to complete school. Recommended support will allow the grantee to continue to provide advocacy support and targeted technical assistance to local partnerships across the state interested in advancing strategies to reconnect dropouts to education and/or career training opportunities.

title: Improving Outcomes for Out-of-School Youth in Michigan
description: This grant will enable Michigan’s Children to continue to bring attention to the issue of students failing to graduate from high school in Michigan. Over the course of this initiative, the grantee has contributed greatly to expanding the dialogue on high school graduation by working with key state departments, interagency taskforces, and communities to assess the current investments and public policies that create barriers or opportunities for young people to complete school. Recommended support will allow the grantee to sustain its presence in advancing strategies to reconnect dropouts to education and assist the grantee in restructuring and refocusing its core organizational capacity during this period.

title: Improving Outcomes for Out-of-School Youth in Michigan
description: This grant will enable Michigan’s Children to continue to bring attention to the issue of students failing to graduate from high school in Michigan. Throughout this initiative, the grantee has served as a leading voice on ensuring that the needs of dropouts and other underserved students are included in the state’s ongoing efforts to improve student achievement. Recommended support will allow the grantee to sustain its presence in advancing strategies that move students through high school and onto college and career opportunities.

title: Improving Outcomes for Out-of-School Youth in Michigan
description: In mid-2006, the state of Michigan approved measures to increase the graduation requirements for students to support workforce needs. Under these requirements, the challenge for the state is to create a balanced approach for making high school more demanding, while at the same time promoting efforts and specialized opportunities for out-of-school youth and students at the margins to earn a diploma.This grant will enable Voices for Michigan’s Children (VMC) to promote the development of local and state systems to track and serve out of-school and underserved youth. Specifically, VMC will analyze policy and resource barriers; mobilize key state-level stakeholders; build public will for policies and investments; and provide policy and advocacy support to a limited number of sites interested in improving supports and outcomes for out-of-school youth in their communities.VMC works with policymakers, communities and the public to improve the quality of life for children and their families and to ensure that every child in Michigan has an opportunity to become a healthy, productive and responsible adult.

title: Summer Fun Program
grantee: Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint
description: This renewal provides support to the Summer Fun Program operated by the Boys & Girls Club of Greater Flint. Mott funds support the required, part-time adult personnel and other direct expenses for the Early Bird Pilot program. The Summer Fun Program has become the largest single-site summer program in Genesee County. As in the past, the program will offer an Early Bird Pilot program for children of working parents and a daily program that will serve 240 youth a day between the ages of 7 and 17.

title: Summer Fun Program
grantee: Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint
description: This renewal grant provides support to the Summer Fun Program operated by the Boys & Girls Club of Greater Flint. Mott funds support the part-time adult personnel required and other direct expenses for the Early Bird program, which is a daily program for children of working parents that will serve up to 250 youth a day between the ages of 7 and 17. The Summer Fun Program has become the largest, single-site summer program in Genesee County.

title: Summer Fun Program
grantee: Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint
description: As part of the national network, the Boys & Girls Club of Greater Flint opened in 1998 in the Sylvester Broome Center and relocated in 2004 to the site of the former Sobey Elementary School. The grantee’s purpose is to provide a safe space to learn and grow for young people of all backgrounds, with special concern for those from disadvantaged circumstances. Another goal is to help these youth develop the qualities needed to become responsible citizens and community leaders. The aim of this grant is to support the growth of the club’s Summer Fun Program through the provision of extra staffing in order to pilot morning programs and to increase the number of youth who can be served on a daily basis.

title: Summer Fun Program
grantee: Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint
description: For the past two summers, the Boys & Girls Club of Greater Flint (BGC) has provided a 10-week Summer Fun Program involving hundreds of area youth. The program has experienced rapid growth, expanding from an average of 70 youth served per day in 2004 to an average of 140 in 2005, with attendance spikes sometimes resulting in service to 200 students per day. This grant will support the growth of the Summer Fun Program by providing extra staffing in order to pilot morning programs and increase the number of youth who can be served on a daily basis.The mission of BGC, established in 1998, is to provide a safe space to learn and grow for young people of all backgrounds, with special concern for those from disadvantaged circumstances. It also helps youth develop the qualities needed to become responsible citizens and community leaders.

title: Communities for Public Education Reform
description: This grant will provide support to Public Interest Projects for the Communities for Public Education Reform, a project designed to attract additional funding to the field of education organizing as well as to help strengthen the effectiveness and visibility of education organizing strategies. The project is currently partnering with four local sites to regrant matching dollars for city, county, regional, or statewide community-driven reform projects.

title: Fund for Education Organizing
description: Community organizing for school reform has dramatically changed during the past 20 years. Currently, there are more than 100 community organizations working to address education issues. Recently, education organizing intermediary organizations have been created to help improve the capacity of groups to access data, researchers, training and resources. As the field of education organizing continues to expand, it will need additional supports, including philanthropic dollars.This grant will support the Public Interest Projects’ Fund for Education Organizing, created to attract additional funding to the field of education organizing and strengthen its efforts. The fund will partner with up to six sites to regrant matching dollars for city, county, regional or statewide community-driven reform projects.Public Interest Projects was formed in 1984 to advocate for issues of timely interest to consumers and the general public. It operates grantmaking, technical assistance and strategic planning programs for institutional and individual donors interested in social justice and human rights issues.

title: Strategic Planning
description: The Applied Research Center is an independent public policy research institute focusing on issues of race and equity. The center’s director of 15 years will be retiring this year and passing leadership of the organization on to an internal candidate who will assume the position of president and executive director.This grant will enable the center to undertake a strategic planning process aimed at reassessing and refining its strategic direction through board retreats, conducting an environmental scan, assessing organizational strengths and weaknesses and increasing staff and board investment in the goals of the organization.

title: Flint STRIVE Academy Summer Youth Project
description: This grant to Flint Area Specialized Employment Services, Inc., will support the Flint STRIVE Academy Summer Youth Project, a ten-week summer youth employment project for 25 at-risk youth ages 14 through 19. Youth will be employed by Flint STRIVE’s Achieve Employment Services. In addition, during the ten-week period, youth will participate in Freedom School Concepts, a cultural program designed to build intergenerational respect, self-esteem, anger management, and other character-building activities. This initiative advances the Mott Foundation’s interest in increasing summer activity options for disadvantaged youth during these trying times of job loss and unemployment.

title: Flint STRIVE Academy Youth Empowerment Program
description: This renewal grant to Flint Area Specialized Employment Services, Inc., will support the Flint STRIVE Academy Youth Empowerment Program, a youth employment and academic achievement project for youth ages 14 through 19. Forty youth will be employed by Flint STRIVE’s ACHIEVE Employment Services during the summer, and 25 youth will receive followup services throughout the academic year. This initiative increases summer activity options for disadvantaged youth and encourages academic achievement.

title: Flint STRIVE Academy Youth Empowerment Program
description: This renewal grant supports the Flint STRIVE Academy Youth Empowerment Program, an employment and academic achievement project for youth ages 14 through 18, a program of Flint Area Specialized Employment Services, Inc. Approximately 40 area youth will be employed by Flint STRIVE’s ACHIEVE Employment Services during the summer, and many will receive case management services throughout the academic year. Supporting the Flint STRIVE Academy Youth Empowerment Program increases summer activity options for disadvantaged youth and encourages academic achievement.

title: Flint STRIVE Academy Youth Empowerment Program
description: This grant to Flint Area Specialized Employment Services, Inc., will support the Flint STRIVE Academy Youth Empowerment Program, an employment and academic achievement program for at-risk youth ages 14-18. The program provides employment training and placement during the summer months and follow-up support services during the school year. Through attitudinal training, exposure to positive role models, and tutoring, the program aims at encouraging youth to finish high school and empowering them to make rewarding occupational and career choices.
