title: Flint STRIVE Academy Summer Youth Project
description: This grant will support the Flint STRIVE Academy Summer Youth Project, a 10-week summer youth employment project for 40 low-income youth ages 14 through 19. Twenty youth will be employed in beautification and gardening projects at public housing sites and another 20 by Flint STRIVE’s ACHIEVE Employment Services. In addition, during the 10-week period youth will participate in Freedom School Concepts, a cultural program designed to address issues of intergenerational respect, self-esteem, anger management and other character-building activities.Flint Area Specialized Employment Service (FASES) was established in 2001 to provide workforce training and job placement assistance to low-skilled workers in Genesee County. FASES operates Flint STRIVE, a replication of the national soft-skills training program developed by East Harlem Employment Services.

title: Organizers Renewal Fund
description: The role of community organizing has taken on increased importance in promoting strategies that will result in equitable rebuilding plans in areas affected by Hurricane Katrina. Even as they are being called on to do more work, the staff of community-based organizations in Louisiana and other states affected by the storm also are coping with the loss of their own homes and communities.This grant will enable the Louisiana Disaster Recovery Foundation to provide resources so that local community organizers can apply for short-term sabbaticals. The Organizers Renewal Fund will award grants of up to $3,000 for organizers to take a short leave of absence from work to rest.The foundation was established in the aftermath of hurricanes Katrina and Rita to provide resources for the relief, recovery and betterment of Louisiana’s people and communities. It works with private, nonprofit organizations.

title: Support to the Paralegal Consultative Process
description: The Black Sash Trust is dedicated to the promotion and defense of human rights. Through its network of advice offices, it provides hands-on legal advice and related services to rural and poor communities. This grant increase will provide additional support to the Black Sash Trust to enhance capacity-building support for the members of the National Alliance for the Development of Community Advice Offices (formerly known as the steering committee for advice offices and paralegals), an initiative aimed at strengthening the community-based paralegal and advice office sector and advocating for increased government support to ensure its long-term sustainability.

title: National Alliance for the Development of Community Advice Offices
description: The National Alliance for the Development of Community Advice Offices, hosted by the Black Sash Trust, is a network of organizations providing hands-on legal advice and other social services to poor and marginalized communities. Mott supported the alliance to conduct research on the size and scope of the community-based paralegal sector, the results of which are being used to advocate government for resources to fund advice offices, and in turn, help poor communities to gain access to justice. Mott support also enabled the alliance to develop an information technology system for advice offices, which will present a more accurate picture of the work done by these offices to government and other stakeholders. This grant renewal will support the alliance’s continued advocacy efforts aimed at improving access to justice for poor communities. The Black Sash Trust was established in 1955 as a voluntary white women’s organization working against the injustices of apartheid and became a trust in 1995.

title: National Alliance for the Development of Community Advice Offices
description: The National Alliance for the Development of Community Advice Offices, a project of Black Sash Trust, is a network of organizations that provide hands-on legal advice and other social services to poor and marginalized communities. Mott supported the alliance to conduct research on the size and scope of the community-based paralegal sector, the results of which are being used to advocate government for resources to fund advice offices and, in turn, help poor communities gain access to justice. Mott support also enabled the alliance to develop an information technology system for advice offices, which will present a more accurate picture of the work done by these offices to government and other stakeholders. This grant increase will enable the alliance to employ a coordinator in KwaZulu-Natal province to implement tasks identified by stakeholders in that province. The Black Sash Trust was established in 1955 as a voluntary, white women’s organization working against the injustices of apartheid and became a trust in 1995.

title: Support to the Paralegal Consultative Process
description: The Black Sash Trust is dedicated to the promotion and defense of human rights. Through its network of offices, it provides hands-on paralegal services to rural and poor communities. This grant is aimed at addressing major challenges facing the community-based paralegal sector by supporting a process directed at finding solutions for the sustainability of the sector and strengthening its role of assisting poor and marginalized communities in accessing their rights.

title: Operations Endowment Fund
description: This grant will provide support to the Community Foundation of Greater Flint to increase the organization’s Operations Endowment Fund. The Community Foundation of Greater Flint continues to serve a vital role in the charitable and nonprofit community in the Flint area. The organization is guided by a strategic plan that will continue to build upon strengths, as well as focus on new and critical issues in the community.

title: Operations Endowment Fund
description: The Community Foundation of Greater Flint (CFGF) serves a vital role in the Flint area’s charitable and nonprofit community. It recently completed a strategic plan that will continue to build upon strengths, as well as focus on new and critical issues in the community.This grant will provide support to CFGF’s Operations Endowment Fund. CFGF, founded in 1988 through the merger of the Flint Public Trust and the Flint Area Health Foundation, works to improve the quality of life for people in the Greater Flint area.

title: Forum on National Security and Civil Liberties in Russia
grantee: Woodrow Wilson International Center for Scholars
description: This grant will enable the Woodrow Wilson International Center for Scholars to hold a constructive policy forum of international experts on national security and civil liberties. As many countries grapple with terrorism, there is a great need to analyze the trade-off between defense of national security and protection of civil liberties and human rights. The forum will be held as one of the events of the Civil G8-2006 project, a Russian government-sanctioned initiative to facilitate discussion of issues on the Group of Eight summit agenda by non-governmental representatives from various countries. The forum will be held in Moscow two weeks prior to the Group of Eight summit meeting in Saint Petersburg.The Woodrow Wilson International Center for Scholars is an interdisciplinary institute that provides scholarships in the humanities and social sciences and encourages dialogue between the worlds of academia and public affairs. It was established in 1968 within the Smithsonian Institution.

title: Tapology Dance Festival for Youth
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will support the Tapology Dance Festival for Youth to be held in October 2007. The Flint Institute of Music, in collaboration with Creative Expressions Dance Studio, will host the festival on the campus of the Flint Cultural Center. Tapology provides a unique opportunity to expose and train local youth in the art of tap dance while filling an important role within the institute’s ongoing efforts to diversify its programming. The festival draws students from throughout mid-Michigan to receive instruction from visiting artists and seasoned performers to perform in tap competitions. Several hundred students from Flint schools attend dance classes and learn about the history of tap. The weekend event will feature two public performances by the visiting artists at the University of Michigan-Flint theater.

title: Tapology Dance Festival for Youth
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to the Flint Institute of Music will provide continued support for the annual Tapology Dance Festival for Youth held on the Flint Cultural Center campus. The festival is a collaborative effort with Tapology, Inc., to introduce children, ages 8 to 18, to the art of tap dance and offer instruction by professional artists to aspiring young dancers. An educational component to the festival offers 1,000 Flint public school students an opportunity to learn about the history of tap, receive instruction from performing artists, and gain an appreciation for the music and culture it represents. Dance studio students from throughout Michigan and other states attend workshops and receive mentoring from professional dancers from around the country. The festival culminates in a student dance competition and public performance by the professional dancers.

title: Tapology Tap Dance Festival for Youth
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to the Flint Institute of Music will provide continued support for the annual Tapology Tap Dance Festival for Youth held on the Flint Cultural Center campus. The festival is a collaborative effort with Tapology, Inc., to introduce children, ages 8 to 18, to the art of tap dance and offer instruction by professional artists to aspiring young dancers. Other partners include the Flint Public Library, local media, and other cultural center organizations. Students from dance studios throughout Michigan and other states attend workshops and receive mentoring from professional dancers from around the country. Several hundred Flint public school students are brought to the campus to learn about the history of tap, receive tap instruction, and gain an appreciation for the music and culture it represents. The festival also includes a student dance competition and public performance by the professional dancers.

title: Tapology Tap Dance Festival for Youth
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to the Flint Institute of Music will provide continued support for the annual Tapology Tap Dance Festival for Youth held on the Flint Cultural Center campus. The festival is a collaborative effort with Tapology, Inc., to introduce children, ages 8 to 18, to the art of tap dance and to offer instruction by professional artists to aspiring young dancers. Other partners include the Flint Community Schools, the Flint Public Library, local media, and other cultural center organizations. Students from dance studios throughout Michigan and other states attend workshops and receive mentoring from professional dancers from around the country. In addition, several hundred Flint public school students are brought to the campus to learn about the history of tap, receive tap instruction, and gain an appreciation for the music and culture it represents. The festival also includes a student dance competition and public performance by the professional dancers.

title: Tapology Tap Dance Festival for Youth
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The annual Tapology Dance Festival for Youth is a collaborative effort between the Flint Institute of Music and Tapology, Inc., to preserve the heritage of tap dance as an American art form. The festival brings local school children to the cultural center campus to expose them to the art of tap dance, provides workshops for dance students of all skill levels, and brings in professional artists to work with students and perform a public concert. The purpose of this grant is to support the guest artist fees and travel, and the purchase of a new dance floor. The festival and activities leading up to the weekend event are expected to serve nearly 2,000 students and concert attendees.

title: Tapology Tap Dance Festival for Youth
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The annual Tapology Dance Festival for Youth is a collaborative effort between the Flint Institute of Music and Tapology, Inc., to preserve the heritage of tap dance as an American art form. The festival brings local school children to the cultural center campus to expose them to the art of tap dance, provides workshops for dance students of all skill levels, and brings in professional artists to work with students and perform a public concert. While Tapology undertakes activities throughout the year, this grant specifically supports the four-day festival, which is expected to serve nearly 2,500 students and concert attendees.

title: Tapology Tap Dance Festival for Youth
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The annual Tapology Tap Dance Festival for Youth is a collaborative effort between the Flint Institute of Music and Tapology, Inc., to preserve the heritage of tap dance as an American art form. The festival brings local school children to the cultural center campus to expose them to the art of tap dance, provides workshops for dance students of all skill levels, and brings in professional artists to work with students and perform at local extended care facilities. A tap competition is also held, and competition winners perform on stage along with professional dancers for a public concert at The Whiting. While Tapology undertakes activities throughout the year, this grant supports the four-day festival, which is expected to serve 2,100 students, seniors, and concert attendees.

title: Tapology Tap Dance Festival for Youth
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide partial support to the annual Tapology Tap Dance Festival for Youth, a collaborative effort between the Flint Institute of Music and Tapology, Inc., to preserve the heritage of tap dance as an American art form. The four-day festival on the Flint Cultural Center campus introduces local students to the art and history of tap. It also brings in professional artists to provide instruction for beginners as well as more advanced workshops for experienced young dancers. The festival culminates with a tap competition and a public concert where competition winners perform along with professional dancers on stage at The Whiting.

title: Tapology Tap Dance Festival for Youth
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide partial support to the annual Tapology Tap Dance Festival for Youth, a collaborative effort between the Flint Institute of Music and Tapology, Inc., to preserve the heritage of tap dance as an American art form. The four-day festival, in partnership with the Flint Community Schools and Flint Cultural Center institutions, introduces local students to the art and history of tap. It also brings in professional artists to provide instruction for beginners, as well as more advanced workshops for experienced young dancers. The festival culminates with a tap competition followed by a public concert where the competition winners perform along with professional dancers on stage at The Whiting.

title: Tapology Tap Dance Festival for Youth
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide partial support to the annual Tapology Tap Dance Festival for Youth, a collaborative effort between the Flint Institute of Music and Tapology, Inc., to preserve the heritage of tap dance as an American art form. The four-day festival, in partnership with the Flint Community Schools, YouthQuest, and the Flint Cultural Center institutions, provides exposure for local students to the art and history of tap. Professional artists provide instruction for beginners, as well as more advanced workshops for experienced young dancers. The festival culminates in a tap competition and public concert where competition winners perform along with professional dancers on stage at The Whiting. Tap dance increases physical activity and enhances cognitive development for participants.

title: Tapology Tap Dance Festival for Youth
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide partial support to the annual Tapology Tap Dance Festival for Youth, a collaborative effort between the Flint Institute of Music and Tapology, Inc., to preserve the heritage of tap dance as an American art form. In partnership with the Flint Community Schools, YouthQuest, and the Flint Cultural Center institutions, the four-day festival provides exposure for local students to the art and history of tap. Professional artists provide instruction for beginners, as well as more advanced workshops for experienced young dancers. The festival culminates in a tap competition and public concert where winners perform along with professional dancers on stage at The Whiting. Tap dance increases physical activity and enhances cognitive development for participants.

title: Tapology Youth Outreach
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide partial support for Tapology outreach programs. Tap dance is an enduring American art form that increases physical activity and enhances cognitive development for participants. In partnership with local schools, community centers, YouthQuest, and the Flint Institute of Music, Tapology provides area youth with an introduction to tap dance through Visiting School Days and offers regular classes for beginners to advanced students. Each year the Tapology, Inc., programming culminates into a four-day festival that provides exposure for local students to the art and history of tap. Professional artists provide instruction for beginners, as well as more advanced workshops for experienced young dancers. Students compete for an opportunity to perform at the public concert alongside professional dancers on stage at The Whiting.

title: Tapology Youth Outreach
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide partial support for Tapology outreach programs. Tap dance is an enduring American art form that increases physical activity and enhances cognitive development for participants. In partnership with local schools, community centers, and the Flint Institute of Music, the grantee provides area youth with an introduction to tap dance through Visiting School Days and offers regular classes for beginners to advanced students. Each year Tapology outreach programming culminates into a four-day festival that provides exposure for local students to the art and history of tap. Professional artists provide instruction for beginners, as well as more advanced workshops for experienced young dancers. Students compete for an opportunity to perform at the public concert alongside professional dancers on stage at The Whiting.

title: Tapology Dance Festival for Youth
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Flint Institute of Music (FIM) has worked collaboratively with Flint’s Creative Expressions Dance Studio and the Flint Public Library to introduce children, ages 8 to 18, to the art of tap dance during its annual Tapology Dance Festival for Youth.This grant will support the development of the festival. Funds will be used for production-related costs, including guest artist fees and rentals.FIM, which began with the founding of the Flint Community Music Association in 1917, annually provides instruction to nearly 3,000 students, along with music and dance performances to approximately 225,000 Flint area residents.

title: Intermodal Center
description: This grant increase to Bishop International Airport Authority will provide partial support for the continued development of an intermodal hub at Bishop International Airport. The intermodal hub will allow cargo and goods to move from one form of transportation to another, and will increase the region’s capacity to recruit and retain employers that utilize a cargo infrastructure. In partnership with the Genesee Regional Chamber of Commerce, the intermodal hub is being designed to help diversify the regional economy, support and expand existing industries, and create and retain good jobs.

title: Intermodal Center
description: This grant increase to Bishop International Airport Authority will provide partial support for the continued development of an intermodal hub at Bishop International Airport. The intermodal hub will allow cargo and goods to move from one form of transportation to another, and will increase the region’s capacity to recruit and retain employers that utilize a cargo infrastructure. In partnership with the Genesee Regional Chamber of Commerce, the intermodal hub is being designed to help diversify the regional economy, support and expand existing industries, and create and retain good jobs.

title: Intermodal Center
description: This grant increase will provide partial support to complete the intermodal hub at Bishop International Airport. The intermodal hub will allow cargo and goods to move from one form of transportation to another, and will increase the region’s capacity to recruit and retain employers that utilize a cargo infrastructure. In partnership with the Genesee Regional Chamber of Commerce, the intermodal hub is being designed to help diversify the regional economy, support and expand existing industries, and create and retain good jobs.

title: Intermodal Center
description: This grant to the Bishop International Airport Authority will provide partial support for the development of an intermodal hub at Bishop International Airport. The intermodal hub will allow cargo and goods to move from one form of transportation to another, and will increase the region’s capacity to recruit and retain employers that utilize a cargo infrastructure. In partnership with the Genesee Regional Chamber of Commerce, the intermodal hub will be used to help diversify the regional economy, support and expand existing industries, and create and retain good jobs.

title: Capacity Building
description: In 2004, the Genesee Area Focus Council, the Flint-Genesee Economic Growth Alliance, the Flint Area Chamber of Commerce and the Metropolitan Chamber of Commerce began a planning process to consolidate into one entity. As a result, the newly formed Genesee Regional Chamber of Commerce will provide an array of economic development, education and business development services in the Foundation’s home community of Flint and Genesee County, Michigan.This grant to the Genesee Chamber Foundation, the fundraising arm of the Genesee Regional Chamber of Commerce, will provide funds to build the capacity of the new organization during the transition and start-up period.

title: Graffiti Chronicles
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will support the expansion of one of the theatre’s recent plays, “Graffiti Chronicles,” for traveling performances to 18 sites in Flint and Genesee County. This grant will support the production costs of these performances, including stipends for artists and technical support, as well as the cost of set design and transportation. The Floyd McCree Theatre is a Flint-based performing arts organization. Its mission is to provide a vehicle for local African-American young adults to explore and refine their talents in the areas of acting, dance, music, and creative writing through the creation of stage productions that reflect their cultural and historical experiences. The theatre currently presents four plays each season and has forged collaborative relationships with a number of local nonprofits with the objective of developing the theatre’s audience.

title: Graffiti Chronicles
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Floyd McCree Theatre is a Flint-based performing arts organization whose mission is to provide a vehicle for inner city youth to explore and refine their talents in the areas of acting, dance, music and creative writing through the creation of stage productions that reflect their cultural and historical experiences. The theatre currently presents four plays per season and has forged collaborative relationships with a number of local nonprofits with the objective of developing the theatre’s audience. This grant will support the development of a revised version of one of the theatre’s recent plays, “Graffiti Chronicles”, for traveling performances to up to 20 sites in Flint and Genesee County. This grant will support the production costs of these performances, including stipends for artists and technical support, as well as the cost of set design and transportation.

title: H.I.R.E. Network Study
description: More than 650,000 people are released from state and federal prisons every year and hundreds of thousands more are released from local jails. Approximately two million people with criminal records are added to the labor market every year. With more than 71 million criminal records on file in the United States, there are a significant number of ex-offenders seeking to enter or re-enter the labor market.This grant will enable the Legal Action Center’s National Helping Individuals Re-enter Through Employment Network (H.I.R.E.) to conduct a study that will highlight effective practices and strategies for assisting job seekers with criminal records, and to disseminate the findings and recommendations to leaders of local and state workforce development systems.For more than 25 years, the center has worked to combat the prejudice that keeps individuals and their treatment providers out of the mainstream of society. It is the only nonprofit law firm and policy organization in the U.S. that fights to protect the legal rights of and improve public policies and services for people with histories of alcoholism or addiction, people with HIV and AIDS, and people with arrest or conviction records.

title: Haskell Community Center
description: This grant will assist the city of Flint in offering a summer enrichment program to disadvantaged youth ages 5-14. The nine-week summer program entitled Renaissance Project Day Camp will be housed at Haskell Community Center and serve more than 120 youth. Eight youth between the ages of 14-17 will be employed as supervisors and mentors. Academic services will include art and reading, math, writing tutorials. Participants also will enjoy travel experiences, cultural visits, and daily breakfast and lunch.The city of Flint, founded in 1855, has been a grantee of the Foundation since 1937.

title: Economic Development Project for Low-Income Men
grantee: Center for Family Policy and Practice
description: The Center for Family Policy and Practice will continue to implement a project that addresses the specific needs and concerns of low-income, noncustodial parents in the provision of workforce development and other social services. To further the reach of the Mott-funded Fathers At Work Initiative and to ensure that recent fatherhood and marriage promotion legislation achieve their objectives from a policy and service-provision perspective, the grantee will publish and disseminate a series of white papers. The analysis and dissemination of the white papers will help to promote the delivery of effective services to low-income, noncustodial parents.

title: Economic Development Project for Low-Income Men
grantee: Center for Family Policy and Practice
description: This grant will support the implementation of a project to promote an understanding of the specific needs and concerns of low-income noncustodial parents for workforce development programs and other social services. To further the reach of the Fathers At Work Initiative, and to ensure that recent fatherhood and marriage promotion legislation achieve their objectives from a policy and service-provision perspective, the Center for Family Policy and Practice will publish and disseminate a series of white papers. The analysis and dissemination of the white papers will help to promote the delivery of effective services to low-income noncustodial parents.The center, founded in 1995, is a national policy agency dedicated to enhancing the situations of low-income families and families of color in the U.S.

title: Environmental Capacity Builders Network
description: Intermediary organizations, typically called “capacity-building groups,” exist to help local, state and regional environmental organizations address the many institutional pressures they face. In order to maximize their impact, nearly 30 capacity-building groups in the U.S. and Canada are forming an Environmental Capacity Builders Network.This grant will enable the Institute for Conservation Leadership (ICL), one of the network’s founding member groups, to facilitate the organization of three annual meetings of the network and support related projects between the annual events.Established in 1988 with support from the National Wildlife Federation and the Pew Charitable Trusts, ICL’s mission is “to train and empower volunteer leaders and to build volunteer institutions that protect and conserve the environment.”

title: New Safety Net Directions
description: This grant will provide funding to the Urban Institute to develop a framework and policy agenda to strengthen the nation’s safety net. The drawn-out reauthorization debate and repeated short-term extensions of the 1996 federal welfare reform law stalled the progress of research and innovation in the field. There is a need for better information about promising approaches to address the needs of the hardest-to-serve and new directions for supporting working families both on and outside welfare. Building on various ongoing projects and Mott-funded research completed in 2006, the Urban Institute will produce in-depth papers on specific program options, inform national discussion, and develop a policy agenda for policymakers and advocates that will help increase the success of the work, economic security, and child well-being of low-income working families.

title: New Safety Net Directions
description: This grant will enable the Urban Institute to conduct research that will help frame policy discussions regarding a new social safety net. There is a need for better information about promising approaches to address the needs of the hardest to serve and new directions for supporting working families both on and outside welfare. Building on recent and ongoing research projects, the institute proposes to assess and identify potential strategies for helping families struggling with major problems that sharply constrain work, and for low-wage workers.The Urban Institute was founded in 1968 to provide objective, nonpartisan research. Its objectives are to sharpen thinking about society’s problems and efforts to solve them, improve government decisions and their implementation, and increase citizen awareness about important public choices.

title: Strengthening the Capacity of Freshwater Groups in the Southeast and Great Lakes
geographic_focus: Tennessee, Indiana, New York, Wisconsin, Illinois, Michigan, Mississippi, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Minnesota, Alabama, Georgia, North Carolina, South Carolina
description: The Environmental Support Center, a national organization, provides organizational capacity-building assistance to regional, state, and local organizations working on environmental protection issues. With Mott support over the last two years, the center has provided small grants and other technical assistance to more than 25 freshwater conservation organizations in the Great Lakes and southeastern United States. The center will continue to provide similar support to the freshwater conservation community in both regions for an additional year.

title: Strengthening the Capacity of Freshwater Groups in the Southeast and Great Lakes
geographic_focus: Mississippi, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Alabama, Michigan, Wisconsin, Georgia, New York, Minnesota, North Carolina, Illinois, South Carolina, Indiana, Tennessee
description: The Environmental Support Center builds the institutional capacity of environmental groups working at the local, state, and regional levels. With this grant increase and associated grant period extension, the center will continue to provide such services to groups engaged in freshwater conservation activities in the Great Lakes and southeastern United States.

title: Strengthening the Capacity of Freshwater Groups in the Southeast and Great Lakes
geographic_focus: South Carolina, North Carolina, Indiana, Tennessee, Minnesota, New York, Alabama, Wisconsin, Georgia, Pennsylvania, Michigan, Illinois, Ohio, Mississippi
description: The Environmental Support Center was created in 1990 by state and national leaders from the environmental and funding communities out of concern about the ability of community-based groups to sustain their effectiveness over time. Over the next two years with Mott support, the center proposes to regrant funds and offer related organizational capacity-building assistance to approximately 20-30 groups in the Southeast and Great Lakes region engaged in the conservation of freshwater resources. In addition to matching organizations with consultants and training opportunities in the areas of communications, fundraising, strategic planning, and community outreach, the center will provide numerous opportunities for peer exchange and support.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Heart of the Lakes Center for Land Conservation Policy
description: This grant increase is for the general purposes of the Heart of the Lakes Center for Land Conservation Policy, a land trust service center in Michigan. The grantee anticipates using the additional funds to support its Advancing Conservancy Excellence program, which helps land trusts prepare for a voluntary accreditation process.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Heart of the Lakes Center for Land Conservation Policy
description: The Heart of the Lakes Center for Land Conservation Policy was founded in 2004 to support the efforts of land conservation organizations across the state. With prior Mott support, the center has promoted tax incentives and other policies that reward private land conservation, educated decisionmakers and the public about the benefits of public lands, and helped land trusts across the state become more effective and sustainable organizations. With renewed support, the center will undertake similar efforts while also tending to its own internal organizational needs, such as revenue diversification.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Heart of the Lakes Center for Land Conservation Policy
description: The Heart of the Lakes Center for Land Conservation Policy was founded in 2004 to support the efforts of land conservation organizations across the state. With prior Mott support, the center has promoted tax incentives and other policies that reward private land conservation, educated decisionmakers and the public about the benefits of public lands, and helped land trusts across the state become more effective and sustainable organizations. With renewed support, the grantee will undertake similar efforts while also tending to its own internal organizational needs, such as revenue diversification.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Heart of the Lakes Center for Land Conservation Policy
description: This grant increase provides general purpose support to the Heart of the Lakes Center for Land Conservation Policy, a statewide group representing the interests of local land trusts. The grantee plans to use the additional funds to promote public understanding of how the current state policy framework helps land trusts do their work effectively.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Heart of the Lakes Center for Land Conservation Policy
description: The Heart of the Lakes Center for Land Conservation Policy was founded in 2004 to support the efforts of land conservation organizations across the state. With prior Mott support, the grantee has promoted tax incentives and other policies that reward private land conservation, educated decisionmakers and the public about the benefits of public lands, and helped land trusts across the state become more effective and sustainable organizations. With renewed support, the grantee will undertake similar efforts while also tending to its own internal organizational needs, such as revenue diversification.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Heart of the Lakes Center for Land Conservation Policy
description: The Heart of the Lakes Center for Land Conservation Policy was founded in 2004 to support the efforts of land trust organizations in Michigan. Since 2006, the grantee’s 30 members permanently protected 186,000 acres of open space, farmland, and forests. With prior Mott support, the grantee successfully concluded its Advancing Conservancy Excellence Program which helped 12 Michigan land trusts gain national accreditation. The grantee also provided member services, reviewed and informed conservation policies, and began to help members explore community engagement opportunities. With renewed support, the grantee will continue these activities and take steps to strengthen its internal operations.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Heart of the Lakes Center for Land Conservation Policy
description: The Heart of the Lakes Center for Land Conservation Policy was founded in 2004 to support the efforts of land conservation organizations across Michigan. With prior Mott support, the grantee has promoted tax policies that reward private land conservation, educated decisionmakers and the public about the benefits of public lands, helped land trusts across the state become more effective and sustainable organizations, and improved its own organizational capacity. With renewed support, the grantee will continue to undertake similar efforts while working to strengthen relationships among disparate groups, engage new constituencies, and make a stronger economic case for conservation.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Heart of the Lakes Center for Land Conservation Policy
description: Heart of the Lakes Center for Land Conservation Policy is Michigan’s only institution whose mission is to serve and support land conservancies in the Great Lakes state. With previous support, the grantee helped its members—34 land conservancies—preserve hundreds of thousands of acres of forests, coastlines, and farmlands. As of December 2017, 648,456 acres have been protected. With renewed support for its general operations, the grantee will continue and expand efforts to advance conservation priorities in Michigan, including identifying additional sources of funding for protection of land and water resources.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Heart of the Lakes Center for Land Conservation Policy
description: Land conservation in Michigan – the only state entirely within the Great Lakes basin – directly contributes to the protection of the rivers, streams and wetland areas associated with the basin and ultimately, the Great Lakes themselves. In recent years, the capacity of state agencies to maintain the lands they currently hold, much less protect new land, has declined due to budget cuts. Recognizing the impact this has on their work, private land conservancies formed the Heart of the Lakes Center for Land Conservation Policy to bolster the work of the public sector.This grant will enable the center to promote the value of land conservation, assist local and regional land conservancies across Michigan, and build its internal capacity.

title: Northeast Minnesota Program
description: The Minnesota Environmental Partnership, an independent statewide network of more than 80 groups, has a long-term commitment to Lake Superior through its Northeast Minnesota Program. With prior Mott support, the partnership has built the capacity of local community groups, addressed Great Lakes’ interests through state-level public policy initiatives, and represented Minnesota in many regional policy discussions. With continuing support, the partnership will maintain these programs with a particular focus on addressing pressing issues, such as the spread of aquatic invasive species and water pollution from new proposed mining activities. The partnership will also seek to build its own institutional strength by diversifying its revenue base and other means.

title: Northeast Minnesota Program
description: The Minnesota Environmental Partnership, an independent statewide network of more than 80 groups, has a long-term commitment to Lake Superior through its Northeast Minnesota Program. With prior Mott support, the partnership strengthened the capacity of freshwater groups, addressed Great Lakes’ interests through state-level public policy initiatives, and represented Minnesota in regional policy discussions. With continued support, the grantee will maintain these programs with a focus on addressing issues such as the spread of aquatic invasive species and water pollution from proposed mining of sulfide-based ores. The grantee will also build organizational capacity through a variety of means.

title: Northeast Minnesota Program
description: The Minnesota Environmental Partnership, an independent statewide network of more than 80 groups, has a long-term commitment to Lake Superior through its Northeast Minnesota Program. With prior Mott support, the grantee advanced Great Lakes protections by informing state-level and regional policy discussions. This grant increase will allow the partnership to address the emerging threat from the mining of sulfide-based ores in the Lake Superior watershed. To ensure the greatest water quality protections, the partnership will coordinate statewide efforts, provide information and outreach to stakeholders, conduct legal and technical reviews of mining proposals, and employ applicable Clean Water Act tools.

title: Northeast Minnesota Program
description: The Minnesota Environmental Partnership, an independent statewide network of more than 80 groups, has had a long-term commitment to Lake Superior through its Northeast Minnesota Program. With prior Mott support, the partnership raised the profile of Lake Superior as a statewide concern, helped secure funds for Great Lakes’ protection and restoration, improved citizen capacity to protect Great Lakes’ tributaries, worked to maintain policies key to Lake Superior’s long-term health, and sought to increase citizen engagement in the permitting process for Minnesota’s first copper/nickel mine. With renewed support, the grantee will continue these efforts while also building its own organizational capacity as well as strengthening the capacity of partner organizations.

title: Northeast Minnesota Program
description: The Minnesota Environmental Partnership, an independent statewide network of more than 80 groups, has had a long-term commitment to Lake Superior through its Northeast Minnesota Program. With prior Mott support, the grantee raised the profile of Lake Superior as a statewide priority, worked to improve freshwater protections from invasive species, and increased citizen engagement in the environmental review of Minnesota’s first copper/nickel mining proposal. With renewed support, the grantee will continue these efforts while also engaging in the review of new proposals that address potential risks to the health of Lake Superior. The grantee will also build its own organizational capacity and help strengthen the capacity of partner organizations.

title: Northeast Minnesota Program
description: The Minnesota Environmental Partnership, an independent statewide network of more than 80 groups, has had a long-term commitment to Lake Superior through its Northeast Minnesota Program. The grantee leads its members in setting annual priorities related to freshwater, energy, and other environmental and conservation issues in Minnesota. With prior Mott support, the grantee helped protect Lake Superior by monitoring Clean Water Act implementation and taking steps to address invasive species. The grantee also focused on increasing citizen engagement and strengthening its own internal capacity as well as that of partner organizations. With renewed support, the grantee will continue those efforts while also taking steps to address mercury pollution in the Lake Superior basin.

title: Great Lakes Program
description: The Minnesota Environmental Partnership has been the state’s leading coalition of over 70 conservation and environmental groups since 1998. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has helped protect Lake Superior from water quality, invasive species, and other threats and has represented Minnesota groups at the Healing Our Waters Coalition, a region-wide organization of Mott grantees and partners. The grantee has taken important steps to strengthen its engagement with tribal organizations. With renewed support, the grantee will continue important work on invasive species, clean water, resource extraction and leading Minnesota groups to engage with the broader coalition of Great Lakes leaders. This grant includes a one-time increase to enable the group to complete strategic planning, including an emphasis on broadening engagement with tribes and expanding its communication expertise with state-wide polling on key issues.

title: Northeast Minnesota Program
description: Water pollution and other factors threaten the health of Lake Superior in Minnesota, while at the same time, a number of important regional policy discussions about the Great Lakes are under way that require Minnesota’s participation and leadership.This grant will enable the Minnesota Environmental Partnership to address environmental threats and policy reform opportunities. Funding will support the partnership’s Duluth-based Northeast Minnesota Program, as well as coordinate the collaborative development of a Great Lakes action agenda for its member groups.The partnership, a statewide network of environmental groups incorporated in 1998, works to strengthen the effectiveness of the Minnesota environmental community in protecting and enhancing the state’s natural resources.

title: Water Quality Project
geographic_focus: South Carolina, New York, Pennsylvania, Georgia, Michigan, Louisiana, Wisconsin, North Carolina, Minnesota, Mississippi, Tennessee, Kentucky, Alabama, Ohio, Illinois
description: Stormwater runoff is one of the most serious problems confronting freshwater ecosystems across the United States, as contaminants washed from roads, rooftops, construction sites, and residential and commercial properties degrade the quality of our freshwater resources. River Network is a national leader in efforts to address this pollution by educating freshwater groups about the Clean Water Act and its water quality protection programs. With previous support, the network assisted local partners in tackling stormwater issues and associated wetlands protection challenges, while increasing the groups’ collective expertise of the Clean Water Act. With renewed funding, the network will continue its work in the Great Lakes and Southeast to strengthen stormwater policies and permits, maximize the use of stimulus funding for water infrastructure, and increase the watershed community’s understanding of the Clean Water Act.

title: Water Quality Project
geographic_focus: Michigan, Wisconsin, Pennsylvania, Ohio, New York, Minnesota, Illinois
description: River Network is a national organization that provides technical assistance to environmental nonprofits working to improve water quality in their states’ lakes and rivers. With previous support, the grantee helped groups in the Great Lakes and Southeast increase their expertise on the Clean Water Act, work with state and municipal partners to better manage stormwater pollution, and improve selected ecosystems’ abilities to absorb and filter rainwater. With renewed funding, the grantee will help state-level environmental organizations, watershed groups, and other diverse stakeholders in the Great Lakes understand how Clean Water Act tools can improve water quality. River Network will provide groups with Clean Water Act research and information, trainings, and consulting services and will also facilitate collaborative efforts.

title: Water Quality Project
geographic_focus: Michigan, Pennsylvania, New York, Minnesota, Ohio, Wisconsin, Illinois
description: River Network is a national organization that provides technical assistance to environmental nonprofits working to improve water quality in river and lake systems. With previous support, the grantee helped state-level environmental organizations, watershed groups, and other stakeholders engage in Clean Water Act processes to improve Great Lakes water quality. The grantee provided individuals and groups with Clean Water Act research and information, trainings, and consulting services. With renewed support, the grantee will continue offering such services while facilitating collaborations to ensure adequate Clean Water Act implementation in every Great Lakes state.

title: Water Quality Project
geographic_focus: South Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, New York, Alabama, Illinois, Mississippi, Georgia, Kentucky, Tennessee, Minnesota, Michigan, Wisconsin, Louisiana, North Carolina
description: The river systems of the Great Lakes and southeastern United States support diverse ecosystems, as well as myriad human uses. However, many streams, lakes, and wetlands have been seriously degraded by stormwater and the pollution it carries, making stormwater runoff perhaps the single most serious problem confronting freshwater ecosystems. River Network is a national leader in efforts to address stormwater pollution by educating freshwater groups about the Clean Water Act and its water quality protection programs. Support for the network will enable it to assist local partners in tackling stormwater issues and associated wetlands protection challenges, while increasing expertise with the Clean Water Act in general.

title: From Unemployment to Work Project
grantee: Insight Center for Community Economic Development
description: According to the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, temporary employment ranks among the fastest growing industries and is expected to be among those that provide the most new jobs in the years ahead. During the past 15 years, the temporary employment industry has become a leading method of labor market entry for welfare recipients and other low-skilled, low-income and disadvantaged job seekers. As the temporary staffing industry becomes more rooted in the country’s economy, it is unclear what policies and regulations have been or could be put in place to support alternative staffing organizations that offer higher wages, fringe benefits and job training.This grant will enable the National Economic Development and Law Center to conduct an analysis and make recommendations on national and state policies that affect temporary employment and alternative staffing strategies.NEDLC is a national research and consulting organization dedicated to building economic health and opportunity in vulnerable communities. Through partnerships with a diverse range of organizations, it works to develop innovative strategies and programs that result in systemic change and help people become, and remain, economically secure.

title: Completion of Atwood Stadium Renovation
description: This grant to the Community Foundation of Greater Flint is for the completion of the historic renovation of Atwood Stadium. The grant will enable the Atwood Stadium Authority to continue the renovation of the interior of the stadium and thereby complete its historic preservation initiative. Project activities include repairing walls around the playing field, replacement of missing brick and limestone and damaged concrete slabs, and renovation of the ticket booth at the west entrance.

title: Atwood Stadium Seating
description: Atwood Stadium has been a hub of community life in Flint since 1929. This grant to the Community Foundation of Greater Flint will partially support the refurbishment of the west-end seating and the deteriorated concrete sections in the former box seating areas at Atwood Stadium. This grant is intended to build upon the grassroots fundraising efforts of the Atwood Stadium Authority. Approximately $300,000 in additional funding is needed to complete the renovation.

title: Building Support for Summer Learning
description: This grant will continue to support the National Center for Summer Learning at Johns Hopkins University to develop summer learning opportunities for young people by ensuring that summer learning is integrated into efforts to redesign systems of teaching and learning. This grant will allow the center to provide technical assistance to communities with an interest and capacity for including summer as a stronger part of a comprehensive, 12-month vision for expanding learning opportunities for young people. To accomplish these objectives, the center will engage school systems, the afterschool community, and municipal leadership in reinventing summer school, and will support the New Day for Learning demonstration sites and public awareness campaign.

title: Building Support for Summer Learning
description: This grant will support the National Summer Learning Association to develop summer learning opportunities for young people by ensuring that summer learning is integrated into efforts to redesign systems of teaching and learning. Specifically, this grant will provide technical assistance to communities with an interest and capacity for including summer as a stronger part of a comprehensive, 12-month vision for expanding learning opportunities for young people. To accomplish these objectives, the National Summer Learning Association will engage school systems, the afterschool community, and municipal leadership in reinventing summer school and will support the New Day for Learning demonstration sites and public awareness campaign.

title: Building Support for Summer Learning
description: This grant will support the National Summer Learning Association in its efforts to improve the quality, expand the access, and increase the demand for summer learning programs across the country. The grantee will: 1) capture, analyze, and disseminate data, best practices, and outcomes from recent investments in summer learning programs, particularly 21st Century Community Learning Centers; and 2) provide technical assistance to help state and district leaders, statewide afterschool networks, and other stakeholders use summer learning opportunities to support more students in being career ready from high school and graduating from college.

title: Building Support for Summer Learning
description: This grant will support the National Summer Learning Association in its efforts to explore how afterschool and summer learning programs can create seamless results-based systems of learning for children and youth through common goals around data, quality, and access. The grantee will: 1) develop and promote a research agenda to demonstrate the role that connected afterschool and summer learning programs play in accelerating education priorities; 2) identify and translate research and best practices on afterschool and summer learning into actionable tools for policymakers, educators, and statewide afterschool networks; and 3) build awareness and capacity of key stakeholders to expand access to high quality afterschool and summer learning programs through publications and trainings.

title: Building Support for Summer Learning
description: This grant will support the National Summer Learning Association in its efforts to increase access to high quality summer learning programs across the country. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) support the statewide afterschool networks in developing summer learning opportunities for children and youth; 2) raise public awareness about the importance of summer learning; and 3) educate and inform the field on best practices for summer learning.

title: Building Support for Summer Learning
description: This grant will support the National Summer Learning Association in its efforts to increase access to high-quality summer learning programs across the country. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) support the statewide afterschool networks in developing summer learning opportunities for children and youth; 2) raise public awareness about the importance of summer learning; and 3) educate and inform the field on best practices for summer learning.

title: Building Support for Summer Learning
description: This grant will enable the Center for Summer Learning to develop high-quality summer learning opportunities for young people. The goal of the project is to encourage a broad coalition of stakeholders to increase public support for investments in summer programs. The center will develop targeted messages; engage in public opinion research; convene public forums; and work to raise public awareness about the valuable role that summer learning programs can play in achieving student success. Specifically, the project will address the benefit that summer learning programs can have on young people in low-income communities.The center, based at Johns Hopkins University, seeks to make summer learning a priority across the country.

title: Education and Economic Development Initiatives
description: This renewal grant provides funds for the Genesee Area Focus Fund and its supported organization, the Genesee Regional Chamber of Commerce, to conduct economic development and education initiatives. The economic development goals for the chamber are to attract new jobs and investment, retain existing firms, introduce and improve products and services, and strengthen partnerships. The goal of the education program is to serve as the voice of business for workforce, training, and education initiatives that result in a trained and educated workforce. Additionally, the grantee will serve business needs by linking education programs with the business community.

title: Education and Economic Development Initiatives
description: This grant increase will provide additional funds for the Genesee Area Focus Fund and its supported organization, the Genesee Regional Chamber of Commerce, to conduct economic development and education initiatives. The economic development goals for the chamber are to attract new jobs and investments, retain existing firms, introduce and improve products and services, and strengthen partnerships. The goal of the education program is to serve as the voice of business for workforce, training, and education initiatives that result in a trained and educated workforce. Additionally, the organization will serve business needs by linking education programs with the business community.

title: Education and Economic Development Initiatives
description: This grant increase will provide additional funds for the Genesee Area Focus Fund and its supported organization, the Genesee Regional Chamber of Commerce, for a new senior leadership staff position for the education and economic development initiatives.

title: Education and Economic Development Initiatives
description: This renewal grant provides partial support for the Genesee Area Focus Fund and its supported organization, the Genesee Regional Chamber of Commerce, to increase their capacity to conduct economic development and education initiatives. Unlike most traditional chamber of commerce organizations, the Genesee Regional Chamber of Commerce serves as the area’s economic development agency and as a direct provider of educational programming. As the regional economy continues to transition, there is a need for increased capacity for business and government leaders to work together to retain and create jobs and investment.

title: Education and Economic Development Initiatives
description: This renewal grant provides partial support for the Genesee Area Focus Fund and its supported organization, the Genesee Regional Chamber of Commerce, to continue providing local economic development and education initiatives. Unlike most traditional chamber of commerce organizations, the Genesee Regional Chamber of Commerce serves as the area’s economic development agency and as a direct provider of educational programming.

title: Education and Economic Development Initiatives
description: This renewal grant provides partial support for the Genesee Area Focus Fund and its supported organization, the Flint and Genesee Chamber of Commerce, to continue to deliver economic development and education and training services to the Flint area. The chamber focuses on increasing business investment, job creation, and industry diversification through business retention, expansion, and attraction activities as well as entrepreneurial support services. The grantee enhances the area’s economic competitiveness and quality of life by providing workforce education and training programming across all age levels, and by engaging in special initiative projects.

title: Education and Economic Development Initiatives
description: This renewal grant provides partial support for the Genesee Area Focus Fund and its supported organization, the Flint and Genesee Chamber of Commerce, to continue to deliver economic development and education and training services to the Greater Flint area. The Flint and Genesee Chamber of Commerce aims to increase business investment, industry diversification, and job creation through its business attraction, retention and expansion services, and entrepreneurial assistance activities. In addition, the grantee helps to enhance the area’s economic competitiveness and quality of life by providing the community with workforce education, training programs, and special initiative projects.

title: Education and Economic Development Initiatives
description: This renewal grant provides partial support for the Genesee Area Focus Fund and its supported organization, the Flint & Genesee Chamber of Commerce, to continue to deliver economic development and education and training services to the Flint area, and to build Flint’s economic resilience to recover from the local water crisis. The chamber focuses on increasing business investment, job creation, and industry diversification through business retention, expansion, and attraction activities, as well as entrepreneurial support services. The chamber also enhances the region’s economic competitiveness and quality of life by providing workforce education and training programming across all age levels, and by engaging in special initiative projects with strategic partners.

title: Education and Economic Development Initiatives
description: This grant provides increased support for the Genesee Area Focus Fund and its support organization, the Flint & Genesee Chamber of Commerce. The chamber focuses on increasing business investment, job creation, and industry diversification through business retention, expansion, and attraction activities as well as entrepreneurial support services. The chamber also enhances the region’s economic competitiveness through workforce education and training across all age levels. In response to the water crisis, the chamber will promote economic resilience in Flint through partnerships that provide grants and low-interest loans for small businesses struggling to recover from the lead water emergency.
