The chamber focuses on increasing business investment, job creation, and industry diversification through business retention, expansion, and attraction activities, as well as entrepreneurial support services. The grantee enhances the region’s economic competitiveness and quality of life by providing workforce education and training programming across all age levels, and by engaging in special initiative projects with strategic partners.

title: Education and Economic Development Initiatives
description: As the Genesee County economy and community continues to change, community leadership organizations are forging new paths of cooperation and collaboration. These new efforts to collaborate have fueled the recent integration of the Flint Area Chamber of Commerce, Genesee Area Focus Council, Metropolitan Chamber of Commerce and the Flint-Genesee Economic Growth Alliance into one entity: the Genesee Regional Chamber of Commerce. This grant to the Genesee Chamber Foundation will support the Genesee Regional Chamber of Commerce’s economic development and education programs.

title: International Program
description: This grant will support the launch of a formal program by the Independent Sector (IS) to strengthen, expand and increase the effectiveness of the international grantmaking and charitable activity of Independent Sector members and to strengthen international civil society by working with global and national civil society infrastructure organizations. Activities will include developing a compendium on U.S. laws and regulations affecting international grantmaking and charitable activity; conducting peer learning events with global civil society infrastructure organizations; hosting international interns; and inviting speakers from other countries to participate in IS’s annual conferences.IS is the leading U.S. nonpartisan leadership forum for charities, foundations and corporate giving programs.

title: General Purposes
description: The National Center for Family Philanthropy promotes philanthropic values, vision, and excellence across generations of donors and donor families. The center ensures that family donors and their advisors have access to the highest quality information and the encouragement needed to articulate, pursue, and achieve their charitable missions; understand and meet their governance and management needs; and have a significant, positive impact on the lives and work of those they support. Since 1997, the grantee has done this through conducting research, developing and providing knowledge resources, training, and consulting on issues concerning family philanthropy. During 2010-2011, the grantee will encourage and help family foundations conduct self-assessments on their grantmaking effectiveness; publish a book entitled “The Power to Produce Wonders: The Value of Family Philanthropy”; conduct research and develop an assessment tool on the role of family foundation chief executives; and facilitate new collaborations with other philanthropic infrastructure organizations.

title: General Purposes
description: The National Center for Family Philanthropy promotes philanthropic values, vision, and excellence across generations of donors and donor families. The grantee ensures that family donors and their advisors have access to the highest quality information and the encouragement needed to articulate, pursue, and achieve their charitable missions; understand and meet their governance and management needs; and have a significant, positive impact on the lives and work of those they support. Since 1997, the grantee has done this through conducting research, developing and providing knowledge resources, training, and consulting on family philanthropy issues. During 2012-2013, the grantee will increase its outreach to community foundations and other donor-advised fund managers; offer a trustee education program; establish relationships with financial institutions; assist non-United States donor support organizations; expand partnerships with other philanthropic infrastructure organizations; and complete work on the revision of “Splendid Legacy,” a seminal 10-year old guide to creating a family foundation.

title: General Purposes
description: The National Center for Family Philanthropy promotes philanthropic values, vision, and excellence across generations of donors and donor families. The grantee ensures that family donors and their advisors have access to the highest quality information and the encouragement needed to articulate, pursue, and achieve their charitable missions; understand and meet their governance and management needs; and have a significant, positive impact on the lives and work of those they support. Since 1997, the grantee has done this through conducting research, developing and providing knowledge resources, training, and consulting on family philanthropy issues. During 2014-15, the grantee will expand the public’s understanding of and appreciation for family philanthropy by launching a research initiative in partnership with the Urban Institute investigating five key research topics; host a biannual convening for up to 250 family philanthropists; enhance the practice of family philanthropy, helping families to be more effective and achieve greater impact; and understand and meet the needs of giving families.

title: General Purposes
description: Founded in 1997, the National Center for Family Philanthropy is the only national nonprofit organization dedicated exclusively to families who give and those that work with them. The grantee provides research, expertise, and networking opportunities to philanthropic families. Its organizational objectives are to: 1) cultivate leadership and good governance; 2) support and inspire effective practice; and 3) ensure the availability of critical information resources. The grantee’s network extends to more than 12,000 family philanthropists. One recent achievement was the release of a first-ever nationally representative benchmark study, the “Trends in Family Philanthropy Report”. The resultant data elevated seven key findings that will be integrated into the grantee’s programmatic offerings over the next two years. These include annual chief executive officer retreats, trustee education events, monthly Webinars, issue briefs, online courses, monthly newsletters, a biannual forum, peer networks, a community foundation initiative, and an online knowledge center.

title: General Purposes
description: Founded in 1997, the National Center for Family Philanthropy is the only national nonprofit dedicated exclusively to families who give and those who work with them. The center provides resources, expertise, and support to families in order to transform their values into effective giving that makes a lasting impact on the communities they serve. In its 20-year history, the grantee has presented more than 750 workshops, has published more than 50 books and issue briefs, has collected more than 3,000 information resources in its online Knowledge Center, and has more than 14,000 followers and subscribers to its newsletters. The grantee’s five-year goal is to provide resources, expertise, and direct support and guidance to more than 5,000 families engaged in philanthropy and indirect support to an additional 10,000 families.

title: General Purposes
description: The National Center for Family Philanthropy is the only resource center that focuses solely on effective family giving. It offers its expertise, information, knowledge and services to strengthen philanthropic families and related philanthropic organizations in the U.S. and around the world. In addition to the broader needs of philanthropic families, the center tailors its programming to support the following constituent groups: family foundations, community foundations, communities of color and professional advisors.Multiyear funding will enable the center to improve and expand its online educational resources; create a new format for delivery of its online monthly teleconference series; attract new community foundations as subscribers and content partners for its online service; gather survey data on the challenges and practices of family foundations; and provide support to emerging donors and philanthropic leaders in communities of color.

title: Broadcasting Operation Project
description: Michigan Television, WFUM-TV, is a nonprofit public television station based at the University of Michigan-Flint. Despite its digital broadcasting capacity, Michigan Television is hampered by its operation from two separate locations. Since 2002, the studios, administrative offices and most of the staff have been located in the William S. White Building on the Flint campus of the University of Michigan. However, master control operations are still located in the station’s former facilities on the Mott Community College campus. The purpose of this grant is to facilitate the reunion of Michigan Television’s broadcast operations center with the rest of the station and to support the replacement of the station’s remote master control equipment with state-of-the-art digital equipment that will enable Michigan Television to fulfill federally mandated regulations and realize greater operating efficiency.

title: Fellowship Program
geographic_focus: Georgia, Ohio, Louisiana, Minnesota, Indiana, United States, Alabama, New York, Illinois, North Carolina, Tennessee, Mississippi, South Carolina, Wisconsin
description: This grant will enable the Environmental Leadership Program (ELP) to build a stronger, more collaborative, and more inclusive environmental movement through its national fellowship program. Semi-annual retreats are the cornerstone of the fellowship program, including a spring retreat for each new fellowship class and a joint summer retreat for all active fellows each year. Following the first retreat, each fellow develops a personal leadership plan that includes specific goals and activities for the remainder of his or her two-year fellowship. ELP provides a small grant of up to $5,000 that serves as seed money to implement projects the fellows otherwise might not have the opportunity to complete.The Environmental Leadership Program began its National Fellows program seven years ago.

title: Frank Manley Endowment Fund/Flint Olympian/CANUSA Games
description: Conceived as a capstone to summer athletic activities for youth, the annual Flint Olympian Games began in 1957, while the CANUSA Games, an international competition with the city of Hamilton, Ontario, began one year later. In honor of the event’s founder, Frank J. Manley, the executive committee of the Flint Olympian and CANUSA games established a fund, the purpose of which is to support community education and youth activities in Flint and Genesee County. The fund has been used for many years to support the Olympian and CANUSA games.The Flint Olympian and CANUSA games are celebrating their 50th anniversaries during 2006 and 2007. This grant will support a permanent endowment created to honor the 50th anniversaries of both events.The Community Foundation of Greater Flint was created in 1988 with the merger of the Flint Public Trust and Flint Area Health Foundation. It works to support capacity building, improve nonprofit effectiveness, advance philanthropy and encourage innovation in the Greater Flint area.

title: Social Justice Infrastructure Funders
description: This grant will provide support to the New World Foundation’s Social Justice Infrastructure Funders program, a learning community of program officers from various foundations who are working together to learn about successful and innovative philanthropic approaches to investing in the field of community organizing. A goal of the program is to help build a more robust public sector capable of creating widespread social and economic opportunity in the U.S.Since 1954, the New World Foundation has supported organizations working to strengthen and expand civil rights and encouraged active participation of citizens in American democracy.

title: Ecological Design Principles
description: In its four years of existence, the Genesee County Land Bank has acquired more than 4,000 properties. To address the need for maintenance of these properties and continue steps to implement elements of the Sasaki Flint River District plan, this grant will enable the Genesee Institute – in partnership with the University of Michigan School of Natural Resources and Environment – to conduct a one-year ecological design initiative. The project goal is to incorporate ecological design principles for vacant lands and brownfield sites in the city of Flint.The Genesee Institute, an affiliate of the Land Bank, was created in 2005 to provide technical assistance to jurisdictions interested in establishing their own land banks and opportunities for planning and research on issues related to vacant properties, sustainable neighborhoods and urban sprawl.

title: Sloan Facility Assessment and Planning
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to the Flint Cultural Center Corporation will support a planning process and facility assessment for the Sloan Museum. Sloan has not had any major renovations since its construction in 1966. In addition, the operations of Sloan are spread among multiple buildings. A committee has been formed with representatives from the cultural center, the education community, and other key stakeholders to develop a vision for the future direction of Sloan and work with museum and exhibition consultants to determine the facility needs of Sloan to best serve the community. The consultants will help define the spatial needs of Sloan and develop multiple design alternatives, including how changes could be incorporated into the existing facilities, as well as how it might look in a new facility. Cost estimates will be developed for the most promising alternative designs.

title: Pablo Eisenberg Public Interest Fellowship
description: This grant provides support to create an endowment fund for the Pablo Eisenberg Public Interest Fellowship at Georgetown University’s Public Policy Institute. This fellowship will be the first of five endowed awards at the institute aimed at preparing exemplary students, especially people of color, for public interest leadership. Selected first-year students at the institute will receive a tuition scholarship and a stipend accompanying a placement in a public interest organization for one academic year. The fellows will be mentored by a current public interest leader and be exposed to numerous valuable training, networking, and leadership development opportunities. The fellowship honors Pablo Eisenberg, one of the most influential voices in philanthropy and the nonprofit sector for over three decades and a strong advocate of social and economic justice for the poor and disenfranchised. Mr. Eisenberg recently retired after eight years of a senior fellowship at the Georgetown University’s Public Policy Institute.

title: Advanced Technology and Renewable Energy Research Building
description: Kettering University’s Center for Fuel Cell Systems and Powertrain Integration recently launched the Fuel Cells and Advanced Technologies Commercialization Incubator to help emerging businesses seeking to commercialize high-tech products and services.This grant will match funds from the U.S. Department of Commerce and the Michigan Economic Development Corporation to construct a new 21,000 square-foot building providing research and manufacturing space for new and emerging alternative energy and advanced technology business start-ups. The new building will provide high-end laboratory, business incubation, and business commercialization space required to support the expanding needs of the center.

title: International Program
description: Oil Change International is a research and advocacy organization that works to encourage progress in the energy industry toward an environmentally and socially sustainable energy future. The grantee’s International Program focuses on reforming the energy-related lending of public multilateral financial institutions, export credit agencies, and key private financial institutions. Over this grant period, it will undertake the following activities: participate in international discussions, including Group of Eight leaders’ fora on climate and the United Nations’ negotiations on climate change; continue to develop the international and U.S. nongovernmental organization coalitions to end public financing of international oil and gas projects; and address the investment distorting incentives that are imbedded in the valuation of oil and gas companies in order to encourage investors to shift to sustainable energy investments.

title: International Program
description: Oil Change International is a research and policy reform organization that works to encourage progress in the energy industry toward an environmentally and socially sustainable energy future. The grantee’s International Program focuses on reforming the energy-related lending of public, multilateral financial institutions, export credit agencies, and key private financial institutions. Over the next grant period, it will build upon its successes from the last grant period at shifting of fossil fuel subsidies toward clean energy access for the poor. To accomplish this goal, the grantee will analyze and present research papers highlighting the scope, as well as the environmental and social implications, of current global fossil fuel subsidies and organize a global nongovernmental organization coalition to build awareness among developed country decisionmakers.

title: International Program
description: Oil Change International is a research and policy reform organization working to encourage progress in the energy industry toward a sustainable energy future. The grantee’s international program focuses on reforming the energy-related lending of public multilateral financial institutions, export credit agencies, and key private financial institutions. Over the grant period, it will build upon its successes from the last grant period in shifting fossil fuel subsidies toward clean energy access for the poor. To accomplish this goal, the grantee will analyze and present research papers highlighting the scope, as well as the environmental and social implications, of current global fossil fuel subsidies and organize a global nongovernmental organization coalition to build awareness among emerging market countries’ decisionmakers.

title: International Program
description: Oil Change International is a research and policy reform organization working to encourage progress in reducing emissions from greenhouse gases and address energy access for the poor in developing countries. The grantee’s international program focuses on reforming the energy-related lending of public multilateral financial institutions, export credit agencies, key private financial institutions, and government subsidies for fossil fuels. Over the last grant period, the grantee helped to secure positive policy shifts in World Bank lending on energy and provided key policy research on fossil fuel subsidies. For the next grant period, it will continue its work analyzing and researching the scope, as well as the environmental and social implications, of current global fossil fuel subsidies. In addition, the grantee will continue its leadership in an international nongovernmental organization coalition to build awareness among emerging market countries’ decisionmakers.

title: International Program
description: Oil Change International is a research and policy reform organization working to encourage progress in reducing emissions from greenhouse gases and address energy access for the poor in developing countries. Its International Program focuses on reforming the energy-related lending of public multilateral financial institutions, export credit agencies, key private financial institutions, and reducing government subsidies for fossil fuels. Over the last grant period, the grantee helped increase transparency of financial flows to the energy sector and monitor commitments by international financial institutions and governments to shift their energy financing practices. With this renewal, it will continue its work analyzing and researching the scope, as well as the environmental and social implications, of current global fossil fuel subsidies. In addition, the grantee will refine and improve its database that tracks international financial institution financing of fossil fuels and work with Brazilian organizations to include Brazilian government financing of fossil fuel projects.

title: International Program
description: Oil Change International has worked over the last decade to increase the transparency of international financial institution lending in the energy sector, ensuring that there is clearer data to inform policymakers in their discussions with these institutions as well as in international climate negotiations. Over the last grant period, the grantee has significantly expanded its tracking of public finance for fossil fuels, expanding the data to include all of the major multilateral development banks. With this renewal grant, the grantee will continue its research and media outreach work to shift multilateral and bilateral financing away from fossil fuel projects and toward support for renewable energy.

title: International Program
description: Oil Change International has worked over the last decade to increase the transparency of international financial institution lending in the energy sector, ensuring that there is clearer data to inform policymakers. The overarching goal of this project is to shift international development finance away from fossil fuels to support for clean energy and energy access for the poor in rural areas. Over the last grant period, the grantee has significantly expanded its tracking of public finance for fossil fuels, expanding the data to include all of the major multilateral development banks. With this renewal grant, the grantee will continue its work in support of renewable energy and energy access. The grantee will increase its monitoring of international public financing for energy projects to African countries, with a particular focus on the financing for energy access projects and off-grid renewable projects.

title: International Program
description: Oil Change International is a research and advocacy organization founded in 2005 that works to encourage progress in the energy industry toward an environmentally and socially sustainable energy future. Oil Change International focuses on reforming the energy-related lending of public multilateral financial institutions, export credit agencies and key private financial institutions. It will pursue these objectives by bringing together a diverse range of groups working on international environment, debt and development policy issues to share experiences and better coordinate their activities; building awareness among the public and policymakers of the need for environmental and social reforms; conducting and disseminating research; engaging directly with decisionmakers at key institutions; and developing better tools to enable both the institutions that finance oil and gas extraction as well as the oil and gas industry itself to incorporate environmental costs and benefits into their decisionmaking.

title: State Fiscal Analysis Initiative
description: This is one of ten grants recommended to state organizations to participate in the State Fiscal Analysis Initiative. The Ford, Annie E. Casey, and Mott Foundations created the initiative in 1992 in order to build capacity for timely, credible, and accessible tax and budget analysis on behalf of low- and middle-income families. The Enterprise Corporation of the Delta joined the initiative in 2007 and has established itself as a source of credible information on budget and tax policy as well as broader economic issues in the state of Mississippi. Activities planned for the renewal grant period include research, community outreach, and strategic communications efforts. Related to this project is a grant to the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, which provides technical assistance to all 36 organizations participating in this initiative.

title: State Fiscal Analysis Initiative
description: The Ford, Casey, and Mott foundations created the State Fiscal Analysis Initiative in 1992 in order to build state capacity for timely, credible, and accessible tax and budget analysis on behalf of low- and middle-income families. The Enterprise Corporation of the Delta joined the initiative in 2007 and has established itself as a source of credible information on budget and tax policy as well as broader economic issues in the state of Mississippi. Activities planned for the renewal grant period include research, community outreach, and strategic communications efforts. Related to this project is a grant to the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, which provides technical assistance to all the state organizations participating in this initiative.

title: State Fiscal Analysis Initiative
description: This is one of ten grants recommended to state organizations participating in the State Fiscal Analysis Initiative. The Ford, Casey, and Mott foundations created the initiative in 1992 in order to build state capacity for timely, credible, and accessible tax and budget analyses on behalf of low- and moderate-income families. Hope Enterprise Corporation joined the initiative in 1994 and is recognized throughout Mississippi as an authoritative source of information and analysis. Activities planned for the grant period include research, strategic communications, and coalition building efforts. Related to this project is a grant to the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, which analyzes federal budget and tax policy issues and provides technical assistance to all the state organizations participating in this initiative.

title: State Fiscal Analysis Initiative
description: This is one of ten grants recommended to state organizations as part of the State Fiscal Analysis Initiative. The Ford, Casey, and Mott foundations created the initiative in 1992 in order to build state capacity for timely, credible, and accessible tax and budget analysis on behalf of low- and middle-income families. Hope Enterprise Corporation joined this effort in 2007 and has become recognized as an authoritative source of information and analysis. During this grant period, the grantee will prepare and disseminate analyses on a range of state fiscal issues, with a particular emphasis on the state and local tax policies affecting low-income families, labor-market policies, and income-support programs. Related to this project is a grant to the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, which provides technical assistance to all 41 state organizations participating in this initiative.

title: State Fiscal Analysis Initiative
description: This grant increase is one of ten tie-off grants to state organizations participating in the State Priorities Partnership (formerly the State Fiscal Analysis Initiative). The Ford, Annie E. Casey, and Mott foundations created the initiative in 1992 in order to build state capacity for timely, credible, and accessible tax and budget policy analyses on behalf of low- and moderate-income families. Hope Enterprise Corporation joined this effort in 2007 and is becoming recognized as an authoritative source of information and analysis. This grant increase will support the grantee’s ongoing analytical, communications, and coalition building efforts, with a particular emphasis on state budget and tax policy, education, healthcare, and poverty issues.

title: State Fiscal Analysis Initiative
description: Funding will enable the Enterprise Corporation of the Delta to launch a state fiscal project for Mississippi, including fiscal and economic analyses. In addition, funding will help support communication and outreach activities designed to raise awareness among local media, community-based organizations and policymakers about policies that assist low- and moderate-income Mississippians.The Enterprise Corporation of the Delta is a nonprofit intermediary organization whose mission is to spur economic development in the Delta regions of Arkansas, Mississippi and Louisiana.This is one of 10 grants supporting the State Fiscal Analysis Initiative. Mott has also supported the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities, which provides technical assistance and networking opportunities for the 35 state organizations participating in this initiative.

title: Reforming Energy Investment
description: PLATFORM has been active with the international network of nongovernmental organizations working to reform international financial institutions and private banks. The grantee has become recognized as a center of expertise on the impacts of oil and gas exploration globally. Through this project, PLATFORM will bring its expertise to assist international nongovernmental organizations’ efforts to reform global investment in oil and gas development. The grantee will undertake activities pertaining to reforming lending policies of private financial institutions and increasing capacity of civil society.

title: Reforming Energy Investment
description: PLATFORM has been active with the international network of nongovernmental organizations working to reform international financial institutions and private banks. The grantee has become recognized as a center of expertise on the impacts of oil and gas exploration globally. During the previous grant period, the grantee assisted communities in Africa, Asia, Central Asia, and the Middle East address the financing of energy projects that would have adverse environmental, health, and economic impacts. Through this project, the grantee will bring its expertise to assist international nongovernmental organizations’ efforts to reform global investment in oil and gas development.

title: Reforming Energy Investment
description: PLATFORM has been active with the international network of nongovernmental organizations working to reform international financial institutions and private banks’ lending in the energy sector. During the past grant, the grantee assisted communities in Africa and Central Asia to address the impacts of energy projects in their countries, which led to changes in national policies on oil and gas contracts as well as greater transparency. Through this project, the grantee will bring its expertise to assist international nongovernmental organizations’ efforts to reform global investment in oil and gas development.

title: Reforming Energy Investment
description: PLATFORM has been active with the international network of nongovernmental organizations working to reform international financial institutions and private banks’ lending in the energy sector. Over the past grant period, the grantee assisted communities in Africa and Central Asia to address the impacts of energy projects in their countries, which led to changes in national policies on oil and gas contracts as well as greater transparency. Through this grant, the grantee will continue to bring its expertise to address public and private investment in oil and gas development. The grantee will also use this grant to explore fossil fuel investments of emerging economies, focusing on assisting organizations in Brazil and China to address their countries’ fossil fuel investment.

title: Reforming Energy Investment
description: PLATFORM is active with the international network of nongovernmental organizations working to reform international financial institutions and private banks’ lending in the energy sector. In recent years, it has assisted communities in Africa and Central Asia to address the impacts of energy projects in their countries, which has led to changes in oil and gas contracts as well as greater transparency. This grant increase will allow the grantee to continue its work to reduce the negative impacts of new energy infrastructure projects on the environment. In addition, it will expand the audience for their research to reach a wider range of civil society organizations in Africa.

title: Reforming Energy Investment
description: PLATFORM has been active with the international network of non-governmental organizations working to reform international financial institutions and private banks. PLATFORM has become recognized as a center of expertise on the impacts of oil and gas exploration globally. Through this project, PLATFORM will undertake activities in the following areas: reforming lending policies of private financial institutions; increasing capacity of civil society; and ensuring that lessons are learned from the Baku-Tbilisi-Ceyhan pipeline.

title: General Purposes
description: This general purpose grant to Urgewald will support its efforts to establish strong, binding environmental and social standards for international financial institutions and to garner ongoing public support for responsible and accountable financial institutions. To achieve these goals, Urgewald undertakes research, education, and advocacy efforts with a global network of local communities, nongovernmental organizations, and other partners. This grant will support Urgewald’s continued services to nongovernmental organizations from developing and transition countries where German companies and banks are involved; policy advocacy efforts to ensure progressive German policies and decisions within the multilateral development banks; oversight of Germany’s export credit agency and other similar government-backed financial instruments; dialogues with private banks on developing progressive policies and practices; and consumer and general public education on the impact of German investments on people and the environment in developing countries.

title: General Purposes
description: This general purpose grant to Urgewald supports its efforts to establish strong, binding environmental and social standards for international financial institutions and to garner ongoing public support for responsible and accountable financial institutions. This grant increase will allow the grantee to hire a senior staff person to more actively monitor World Bank accountability mechanisms, new climate finance funds, and the International Finance Corporation’s performance standard review process.

title: General Purposes
description: This general purposes grant to Urgewald will support its efforts to establish strong, binding environmental and social standards for international financial institutions and to garner ongoing public support for responsible and accountable financial institutions. To achieve these goals, Urgewald undertakes research, education and advocacy efforts with a global network of local communities, non-governmental organizations and other partners. The objectives for the grant period will be to provide support to non-governmental organizations from developing and transition countries where German financial institutions are involved; to work toward German policies and decisions with regard to multilateral development banks that ensure stronger environmental and social safeguards; to act as a watchdog of Germany’s export credit agency and other government financial instruments, such as financial guarantees; to further develop Urgewald’s dialogue with private banks on innovative and timely reforms intended to protect the environment and promote sustainable development; and to further educate the general public regarding the environmental impacts of German bank lending and the application of Germany’s policies in international public and private banking.

title: Truth in Translation Project - Balkans Tour
geographic_focus: North Macedonia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia
description: The project goal is to share experiences from South Africa’s process of truth, justice, and reconciliation with people from the Western Balkans. The grantee, the Colonnades Theatre Lab, Inc., has developed a stage production with music-called “Truth in Translation” that tells the story of the South African Truth and Reconciliation Commission through the eyes of the interpreters who translated the testimony of all those who appeared before the commission into the many languages spoken in the country. This grant will support staging of the play and related events in the Western Balkans over a five-week period in 2008. The play’s Western Balkans tour will be carried out in cooperation with nongovernmental organizations in the region working on issues of dealing with the past and transitional justice. The Colonnades Theatre Lab, Inc. was established in 1973 to promote independent theater.

title: Truth in Translation Project - Balkans Tour
geographic_focus: North Macedonia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia
description: The project goal is to share experiences from South Africa’s process of truth, justice, and reconciliation with people from the Western Balkans. The grantee, the Colonnades Theatre Lab, Inc., has developed a stage production with music — “Truth in Translation” — that tells the story of the South African Truth and Reconciliation Commission through the eyes of the interpreters who translated the testimony of all those who appeared before the commission into the many languages spoken in the country. This grant increase will partially cover additional costs associated with a longer tour in the Balkans that includes more performances and workshops than originally planned. The play’s Western Balkans tour will be carried out in cooperation with nongovernmental organizations in this region working on issues of dealing with the past and transitional justice. The Colonnades Theatre Lab, Inc., was established in 1973 to promote independent theater.

title: Truth in Translation Project - Balkans Tour
geographic_focus: North Macedonia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia
description: The Colonnades Theatre Lab in South Africa developed Truth in Translation – a stage production with music – to tell the story of South Africa’s Truth and Reconciliation Commission through the eyes of interpreters who translated the testimony of all those who appeared before the commission.This grant will support production of the play and related events in Serbia, Macedonia, and Bosnia and Herzegovina over a four-week period in early 2007. The Western Balkans tour will be carried out in cooperation with non-governmental organizations in the region working on issues dealing with the past and transitional justice.The Colonnades Theatre Lab was established in 2005 to promote arts and culture, with an emphasis on performance drama .

title: Future of Community Education
description: This grant will support the National Community Education Association in its efforts to reenergize the community education field by undergoing a comprehensive organizational strategic planning process. This will enable the association to rebuild itself as a strong, flexible organization committed to embedding the historical values of the community education field into a 21st Century society, while addressing the needs of a changing economic and social environment. This effort will require a reexamination of the mission, vision and goals of the organization, as well as a concrete exploration of how new efforts will result in the vibrancy and growth of the community education field. During the strategic planning process, a new executive director, interim manager, and training director also will be hired.

title: Latino Family Engagement and Best Practices in Afterschool
description: This grant will support the National Council of La Raza in integrating their affiliate afterschool practitioners into a network that will address the needs and challenges of Latino children in afterschool programs. The network will be composed of current affiliates that offer afterschool programs and will: a) be an important medium of communication among Latino-serving afterschool affiliates; b) build a strong bloc of advocates for Latino needs at the local and national level in afterschool settings; and c) provide members constant access to information on best practices and changing needs in the afterschool field.

title: Latino Family Engagement and Best Practices in Afterschool
description: This grant will continue to support the National Council of La Raza in advancing their Network of Affiliate Afterschool Providers to address the needs and challenges of Latino children in afterschool programs. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) develop core qualities for successful expanded learning opportunities and a database to collect program data; and 2) support capacity building for affiliates around program development and advocacy. The core qualities for successful expanded learning opportunities, and the use of the database system will strengthen the grantee’s professional development, technical assistance, and other support services. It will also make available concrete data to promote the importance of expanded learning opportunities programs that can in turn support the advancement of public policies benefitting programs serving Latino and English language students.

title: Latino Family Engagement and Best Practices in Afterschool
description: This grant will continue to support the National Council of La Raza in advancing their Network of Affiliate Afterschool Providers to address the needs and challenges of Latino children in afterschool programs. The grantee will: 1) disseminate best practices and resources that focus on high quality expanded learning for Latino students and their families; 2) engage a variety of stakeholders to build support for initiatives addressing the needs of Latino students, including teachers, policymakers, and families; and 3) continue to build the capacity of the grantee’s expanded learning network to promote awareness of the need for quality afterschool learning programs for Latino youth.

title: Latino Family Engagement and Best Practices in Afterschool
description: This grant will enable the National Council of La Raza to examine the access issues of Latino families as they relate to afterschool. This will help the afterschool field respond appropriately to the needs of this population. Project goals include gaining a greater understanding of the afterschool work being conducted by Latino-serving community organizations; developing recommendations for effective afterschool programs; and documenting successful methods of increasing afterschool participation for Latino families.The council works to advance the economic, social and political participation of Latinos in the U.S. through training, organizing and service.

title: Roadmap to Afterschool for All
description: This grant will support the Afterschool Alliance in developing a financial roadmap for afterschool that will provide more accurate information on how much funding is needed to reach the goal of high quality afterschool programs for all. The roadmap will: assess current investments in afterschool programs from the public sector, parents, foundations, and businesses; and estimate the added investment necessary at each level to provide quality afterschool for all those who desire it. The report will also create benchmarks for measuring progress and help elucidate the roles of private organizations and public agencies in providing quality afterschool systems. The Afterschool Alliance plans to strategically survey eight to 10 states about their afterschool program funding and produce a companion report, which will analyze federal, state and local funding streams.

title: West Virginia Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant to the West Virginia University Research Corporation will support the development of the West Virginia Statewide Afterschool Network to expand quality afterschool services for children, youth, and families throughout West Virginia. This grantee is part of the fifth cohort of Mott-funded, statewide afterschool networks. This renewal grant will continue to provide core support to the network, while also encouraging new ideas designed to build or enhance positive systemic changes that further policies and practices for school-based/school-linked afterschool programs. In addition to continuing its work in building the field of afterschool in West Virginia, the grantee will improve the academic enrichment and reinforcement capabilities of program staff to build high quality skills during afterschool hours that will help students learn and achieve. The network will share lessons learned and products with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: West Virginia Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the West Virginia University Research Corporation which coordinates the West Virginia Statewide Afterschool Network. In addition to continuing the network’s core work to advance afterschool in West Virginia, it will complete a multiyear project to elevate the contribution and leadership of afterschool programs in a statewide effort to promote healthy lifestyles for children and families. The network will: 1) coordinate with the West Virginia Department of Health and Human Resources and Department of Education to promote healthy lifestyles to improve student outcomes; 2) develop policy briefs on health and wellness best practices; 3) develop state regulations for physical activity in afterschool programs; and 4) provide families access to nutrition information and healthy foods through afterschool programs.

title: West Virginia Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant to the West Virginia University Research Corporation will support the development of the West Virginia Statewide Afterschool Network to continue to build an afterschool and summer learning system that improves outcomes for children and youth through school-based or school-linked afterschool programs. Over the next three years, the network will support the development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) conducting an expanded environmental scan to document the current status of afterschool programs in West Virginia; 2) developing a comprehensive communications and outreach plan on afterschool to educate policymakers; and 3) developing a self-assessment tool to evaluate progress toward achieving the West Virginia afterschool quality program standards.

title: West Virginia Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the West Virginia University Research Corporation, which coordinates the West Virginia Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) expanding the West Virginia Afterschool Ambassador program to recruit new champions for afterschool; 2) developing a comprehensive plan to increase resources for afterschool programs; 3) developing training to support the afterschool field on opioid prevention and childhood trauma; and 4) participating in the development and distribution of new afterschool program content in collaboration with the Foundation’s thematic partners.

title: West Virginia Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the West Virginia University Research Corporation in its efforts to develop the West Virginia statewide afterschool network. The network will support and sustain a statewide partnership to raise awareness of the importance and accessibility of afterschool programs, share criteria related to best practices, and promote sustainability of afterschool programs. The West Virginia network plans to address public policy and infrastructure development while working to broaden the definition of learning. Because of the network’s activities, stakeholders will be better able to articulate the role that afterschool programs can play in meeting the developmental needs of young people. This grantee is part of the fifth cohort of Mott-funded statewide afterschool networks.

title: Utah Statewide Afterschool Network
location: Salt Lake City, UT, United States
description: This grant to Voices for Utah Children will continue to support the development of the Utah Statewide Afterschool Network in its efforts to develop, enhance, and sustain innovative, high quality afterschool programs and policies. This grantee is part of the fifth cohort of Mott-funded, statewide afterschool networks. This project will continue to provide core support to the network, while also encouraging new ideas designed to build or enhance positive systemic changes that further policies and practices for school-based/school-linked afterschool programs. In addition to continuing its work in building the field of afterschool in Utah, the network will create a comprehensive afterschool and community school professional development system to ensure high quality programs that meet the needs of a diverse population. The network will share lessons learned and products with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: Utah Statewide Afterschool Network
location: Salt Lake City, UT, United States
description: This grant will provide continued support to Utah Afterschool Network. The network seeks to advance student achievement by establishing common indicators of student success, and establishing new policies and procedures for sharing student data among schools and afterschool programs. In addition to continuing the network’s core work to advance afterschool in Utah, it will complete a multiyear project to: 1) establish a policy agenda focused on increasing student data sharing between schools and afterschool programs; 2) select pilot sites to test a data sharing model that focuses on common indicators of student achievement and program quality, and provides actionable data; 3) administer a statewide survey to afterschool programs to gather information on methods of data collection, sharing, and usage; and 4) develop a strategic communications strategy to promote the connection between data sharing, program quality, and improved student outcomes.

title: Utah Statewide Afterschool Network
location: Salt Lake City, UT, United States
description: This grant to the Utah Afterschool Network will support the development of the Utah Statewide Afterschool Network to continue to build an afterschool and summer learning system that improves outcomes for children and youth through school-based or school-linked afterschool programs. Over the next three years, the network will support the development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) developing a communication strategy to support sustainable school-based/school linked afterschool programs; 2) creating a funding map to identify federal, state, and local funds being used for afterschool throughout Utah; and 3) supporting a statewide system of evaluation that includes self-assessment and continuous improvement strategies and rigorous impact evaluation.

title: Utah Statewide Afterschool Network
location: Salt Lake City, UT, United States
description: This grant will support the Utah Afterschool Network, which coordinates the Utah Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) expanding the continuous improvement model for Out of School Time programs to promote measurable program quality; 2) supporting state, local, and education policies to strengthen support for Out of School Time initiatives through statewide efforts; 3) creating a sustainable infrastructure for Out of School Time programs; and 4) participating in the development and distribution of new afterschool program content in collaboration with the Foundation’s thematic partners.

title: Utah Statewide Afterschool Network
location: Salt Lake City, UT, United States
description: This grant will support Voices for Utah Children in its efforts to expand and mobilize the Utah Statewide Afterschool Network. The purpose of the network is to expand and mobilize community collaborations and public/private partnerships that result in quality, sustainable afterschool programming throughout Utah, especially for low-income children and hard-to-reach populations. Goals of the network include: creating a sustainable structure of statewide, regional, and local partnerships focused on supporting statewide policy development; supporting the development of statewide policies that will secure the resources to sustain afterschool programs; and supporting statewide systems to ensure afterschool programs are of high quality. This grantee is part of the fifth cohort of Mott-funded statewide afterschool networks.

title: Delaware Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Family & Workplace Connection in its efforts to develop the Delaware Statewide Afterschool Network, a network formally created in 2005 that endorses the goal of all school-age children to be academically, socially, culturally and physically healthy. The network, along with its partners, will work to: create a long-term policy voice for afterschool programs; advocate for policies that support high quality programs; support the afterschool workforce; increase public awareness regarding afterschool programs; build bridges between public schools and community-based organizations; and support family-centered practices. This grantee is part of the fifth cohort of Mott-funded statewide afterschool networks.

title: Proposition 49 Regional Orientations
description: This grant will support the University of California – Davis, in partnership with the California Department of Education, in an effort to provide information and technical assistance to new afterschool grantees in the state of California. This work is based on the projected dramatic increase in the number of publicly funded afterschool programs as a result of Proposition 49. Proposition 49, along with other state and federal funding sources, will raise the level of support for afterschool programs in the state to approximately $700 million. This grant will support 11 regional orientation conferences that will provide state grantees with information regarding program quality, evaluation and fiscal requirements. Regional orientations will be a coordinated effort by the California Department of Education, the California Afterschool Network, and the state-legislated California Advisory Committee on Before and Afterschool Programs.

title: General Purposes
description: This general purpose renewal grant will focus on strengthening the Center for Socio-Environmental Support’s administrative, operational, and resource mobilization capacity. The grantee is a Brazilian grantmaking and capacity-building organization founded by a group of Brazilian nongovernmental organizations. Its mission is to provide both technical and financial support for the work of community organizations and nongovernmental organizations throughout Brazil and neighboring countries. It supports organizations that monitor environmentally damaging projects; develops coordinated strategies to expand sustainable development options for local communities, and works to make large-scale energy and infrastructure investments more environmentally and socially sustainable.

title: General Purposes
description: This general purpose renewal grant will focus on strengthening the administrative, operational, and resource mobilization capacity at the Center for Socio-Environmental Support. The grantee is a Brazilian grantmaking and capacity building organization founded by a group of Brazilian nongovernmental organizations. Its mission is to provide both technical and financial support for the work of community organizations and nongovernmental organizations throughout Brazil and neighboring countries. It supports organizations that monitor environmentally damaging projects; develop coordinated strategies to expand sustainable development options for local communities; and work to make large-scale energy and infrastructure investments more environmentally and socially sustainable.

title: General Purposes
description: This general purpose renewal grant will focus on strengthening the Center for Socio-Environmental Support’s administrative, operational, and resource mobilization capacity, as well as providing funds for regranting related to environmental impacts of large-scale hydrological dams and other infrastructure investments. The grantee is a Brazilian grantmaking and capacity building organization founded by a group of Brazilian nongovernmental organizations. Its mission is to provide both technical and financial support for the work of community organizations and nongovernmental organizations throughout Brazil and neighboring countries. It supports organizations that monitor environmentally damaging projects; develop coordinated strategies to expand sustainable development options for local communities; and work to make large-scale energy and infrastructure investments more environmentally and socially sustainable.

title: General Purposes
description: This general purpose renewal grant will focus on strengthening the Socioenvironmental Fund – CASA’s administrative, operational, and resource mobilization capacity, as well as providing funds for regranting related to environmental and social impacts of large-scale energy and infrastructure development in South America. The grantee is a Brazilian-based grantmaking and capacity building organization founded by a group of South American nongovernmental organizations. Its mission is to promote environmental conservation, sustainability, and democracy by supporting and strengthening the capacities and initiatives of civil society in South America.

title: General Purposes
description: Socioenvironmental Fund CASA is a Brazilian-based organization focused on making small grants and building capacity in communities impacted by large-scale development. The grantee was founded by a group of South American nongovernmental organizations ten years ago. Its mission is to promote environmental conservation and sustainability by supporting and strengthening the capacities and initiatives of civil society in South America. This grant will allow the grantee to strengthen its administrative, operational, and resource mobilization capacity.

title: General Purposes
description: This general purposes grant will focus on strengthening the Center for Socio-Environmental Support’s administrative, operational, and resource mobilization capacity over the next two years. The Center for Socio-Environmental Support is a Brazilian grantmaking and capacity building organization founded by a group of non-governmental organizations. Its mission is to provide both technical and financial support for the work of community organizations and non-governmental organizations throughout Brazil and neighboring countries. It supports organizations that monitor environmentally damaging projects in their communities; develop strategies to expand sustainable development options for local communities, particularly new energy alternatives; and work to reform policies and practices of international financial institutions. Over the next two years, the grantee will solidify its grantmaking, advisory, and operational structures; establish proper administrative and accountability mechanisms; and mobilize local financial and technical resources from Brazil and other neighboring countries for regranting and capacity building.

title: Towards a Shared NGO Vision and Strategy on the Role of Agrofuels in Addressing Climate Change
description: FERN works to create changes at the European Union level to achieve the conservation and sustainable management of all forests, respect for rights of forest peoples, and greater transparency of international financial institutions. Through this renewal grant, FERN will continue to develop a nongovernmental organization strategy and coordinate an emerging coalition working to ensure that biofuel policies and investments will contribute rather than undermine efforts to tackle global warming, biodiversity conservation, and sustainable development.

title: Developing a Common NGO Vision on Bio-Energy
description: While biofuels can hold great promise, there are concerns that massive global production could lead to tropical rainforests being converted to palm oil plantations and grasslands being converted to sugar cane plantations.This short-term grant to FERN will provide resources to develop a longer-term bioenergy project that engages European, U.S.and developing country non-governmental organizations in a discussion on the types of safeguards and policies that need to be in place as bioenergy development continues. Activities to be undertaken with this grant include identifying a group of non-governmental organizations involved in bioenergy that represent a good regional mix as well as a wide range of expertise and understanding of the multiple aspects of the bioenergy debate; organizing a two-day meeting of this group; identifying gaps in research and analysis; and developing a follow-up project plan.

title: General Purposes
description: This general purpose grant to the NGO Forum on ADB will support its efforts to support and build the capacity of nongovernmental and community organizations in Asia to influence the policies and practices of the Asian Development Bank. The focus will be on reducing negative environmental and social impacts of projects funded by the Asian Development Bank. To achieve this goal, the grantee will undertake research, education, and advocacy efforts with a regional network of local community and nongovernmental organizations and other partners. Through this grant, the NGO Forum on ADB will provide high quality and timely information to its network, initiate and disseminate research and analysis of existing projects and policies, develop recommendations for reform of Asian Development Bank policies and practices, build capacity of network members, and act as a convener of network-wide strategic and tactical planning.

title: General Purposes
description: The NGO Forum on ADB has advocated for sustainable development and policies that are fair and beneficial to local communities and the environment in the Asian region for nearly two decades. It works to improve public participation, access to information, and good governance in the Asian Development Bank. Its capacity building activities have helped to infuse diverse expertise in its member organizations in order to change various Asian Development Bank policies, including the promotion and improvement of the accountability mechanism. This renewal grant will support the organization’s overall goal of strengthening the capacity of civil society organizations and affected communities in the Asia-Pacific region. These groups will address the Asian Development Bank policies, projects, and programs that negatively impact the environment and their communities. To achieve this goal, the organization will carry out research, advocacy, and capacity building programs.

title: General Purposes
description: For nearly two decades, the NGO Forum on the Asian Development Bank has advocated for sustainable development and policies that are fair and beneficial to local communities and the environment in the Asian region. It works to improve public participation, access to information, and good governance in the Asian Development Bank. This grant increase will support the general purposes of the organization, including the participation of civil society organizations in the Asia-Pacific region to attend a global meeting on climate finance.

To achieve this goal, the organization will carry out research, advocacy, and capacity building programs.

It works to improve public participation, access to information, and good governance in the Asian Development Bank. Over the next two years, the grantee will focus its policy advocacy work on the Asian Development Bank’s safeguard and energy policy reviews. In addition, they will expand their capacity building efforts for their member groups to assist them in being better able to effectively use these accountability mechanisms as well as creating a project-monitoring database.

title: General Purposes
description: The NGO Forum on ADB has promoted sustainable development and advocated for policies that are fair and beneficial to local communities and the environment in the Asian region for nearly two decades. This grant increase will be available for the general purposes of the grantee, including assistance with research and convenings to assess how the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank policies will compare to the existing Asian Development Bank polices and lending modalities.

title: General Purposes
description: The NGO Forum on ADB has advocated for sustainable development policies that are beneficial to local communities and the environment in the Asian region for two decades. It works to improve public participation, access to information, and good governance in the Asian Development Bank and the new Chinese development finance institutions. Over the next two years, the grantee will focus its policy work on the review of the Asian Development Bank’s safeguard policy as well as monitoring the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank’s initial project lending.

title: General Purposes
description: This general purposes grant to the NGO Forum on ADB will support its efforts to build the capacity of non-governmental and community organizations in Asia to address the policies and practices of the Asian Development Bank. The focus will be on decreasing negative environmental and social impacts as well as increasing sustainable development. To achieve this goal, the NGO Forum on ADB will undertake research, education and advocacy efforts with a regional network of local community and non-governmental organizations and other partners. Through this grant, the NGO Forum on ADB will provide high quality and timely information to its network; initiate and disseminate research and analysis of existing projects and policies; develop recommendations for reform of Asian Development Bank policies and practices; build capacity of network members; and act as a convener of networkwide strategic and tactical planning.

title: Laura Bush Foundation's Gulf Coast School Library Recovery Initiative
grantee: Community Foundation for the National Capital Region
description: This grant will provide support for the Laura Bush Foundation’s Gulf Coast School Library Recovery Initiative, whose goal is to re-establish book collections in the libraries of the schools devastated or severely damaged by the 2005 hurricanes. Approximately 100 school libraries were completely destroyed, and an additional 100 school libraries received extensive damage. A minimum of $50,000 is required to provide a very basic elementary school print library; the cost for a basic secondary school library is a minimum of $100,000. As part of a competitive grant process, schools must provide information on the school’s pre-hurricane and post-hurricane student population, faculty, facilities, school services, management, and library, with particular emphasis on plans and progress for rebuilding of the school and the library. Three rounds of grants benefiting 40 schools took place in 2006, and additional rounds over the next two to three years are planned depending on contributions received. The Laura Bush Foundation is a fund of the Community Foundation for the National Capital Region established in 1973 to primarily serve residents of the Greater Washington region, including Montgomery County, Prince George’s County and Northern Virginia.

title: Constituency Building and Outreach on Land Use and Equitable Development
description: The purpose of this project is to help build an informed constituency of Michigan residents who will advocate for improved policies related to land use and urban reinvestment. MI*Voice is a coalition of county-based community organizations affiliated with the Gamaliel Foundation. Together, these organizations represent more than 120 congregations in five counties working together to address issues of common concern, especially those impacting state land-use policy. This grant increase will support an increased training agenda that will include representatives from other nonprofits in Michigan.

title: Constituency Building and Outreach on Land Use and Equitable Development
description: MI*Voice, based in Detroit, Michigan, is a coalition of faith-based community organization. Together, these organizations represent more than 120 congregations in five counties working together to address issues of common concern, especially those impacting state land-use policy. With prior Mott support, the grantee helped build an informed constituency of Michigan residents supporting improved policies related to land use and public transportation. With this grant renewal, the grantee will continue working to increase public engagement in transportation reform decisions, in part by providing technical assistance to groups and citizens and by participating in statewide coalitions.

title: Constituency Building and Outreach on Land Use and Equitable Development
description: MI*Voice is a coalition of county-based community organizations affiliated with the Gamaliel Foundation. Together, these organizations represent more than 120 congregations in five Michigan counties working collaboratively to address issues of common concern, especially those impacting state land-use policy. This grant will enable MI*Voice to provide leadership training to 150 new leaders; offer advanced leadership training to 60 leaders; host 125 issue education workshops attracting at least 2,000 residents; increase the membership base in each of the five county-based organizations; help each organization develop an action plan; host five countywide summits on land use and growth management; and work with each local organization to identify and implement next steps for their work.

title: New York Thruway Alliance
description: This grant will enable Interfaith Action to house the New York Thruway Alliance, a coalition of PICO and Gamaliel-affiliated organizations in Buffalo, Syracuse, Albany and Rochester. The goal of the alliance is to build a leadership and constituency base to address issues of economic development and urban reinvestment in the upstate region of New York.Interfaith Action is the Rochester, New York-affiliate of the PICO National Network. Started in 1994 as a result of a community meeting called to examine the challenges confronting Rochester-area families, Interfaith Action now includes 16 member congregations working together to improve the city and the Upstate New York region.

title: YouthBuild Flint/Genesee
description: As a national network of more than 225 local programs, YouthBuild creates opportunities for low-income youth to rebuild their lives and communities through a commitment to work, education and responsibility. A new collaborative effort between Career Alliance and Metro Housing Partnership has secured federal funding for a YouthBuild site in Flint, Michigan. This grant will provide support for YouthBuild Flint/Genesee as it launches its first year of operations.

title: General Purposes
description: The purpose of this grant is to continue to incubate a new workforce intermediary aimed at job retention and wage advancement for the disadvantaged and working poor. The mission of the Economic Mobility Corporation is designing, developing, and evaluating promising upward mobility strategies for low-income Americans.

title: General Purposes
description: The purpose of this grant is to continue to incubate a new workforce intermediary aimed at job retention and wage advancement for the disadvantaged and working poor. The mission of the Economic Mobility Corporation is designing, developing, and evaluating promising upward mobility strategies for low-income Americans.

description: The purpose of this grant is to support a workforce intermediary aimed at job retention and wage advancement for the disadvantaged and working poor. The mission of the Economic Mobility Corporation is to design, develop, and evaluate promising upward mobility strategies for low-income Americans.

title: General Purposes
description: This general purpose grant will support a workforce intermediary aimed at job retention and wage advancement for the disadvantaged and working poor. The mission of the Economic Mobility Corporation is to design, develop, and evaluate promising upward mobility strategies for low-income Americans. In addition, the grantee serves an important role in studying programs and projects vital to the workforce development sector.

title: Center for Economic Mobility
description: This grant will partially support a new national workforce program devoted to low-income worker wage advancement and job retention. The Center for Economic Mobility will identify and support programs and policies that enable low-income people to acquire the education, skills and relationships needed to secure employment opportunities that enable them to support themselves and their families.The Vera Institute of Justice conducts research and evaluation on important justice issues and provides public officials and civic leaders with expert assistance to advance safety, well-being and justice.

title: Capacity Building
description: The Visually Impaired Center has been providing vision rehabilitation services to the blind and visually impaired population in Michigan’s Genesee, Lapeer and Shiawassee counties since 1970. It serves approximately 200 blind and visually impaired persons per year by providing both home- and center-based instruction in vision rehabilitation including independent living skills, computer classes, Braille instruction and use of low vision aids.This grant will provide capacity building support to help the Visually Impaired Center explore options to become sustainable in the future.

title: Merger Technical Assistance
grantee: National Council on Alcoholism and Addictions, Greater Flint Area, Inc.
description: This grant increase will allow the National Council on Alcoholism and Addictions, Greater Flint Area, Inc., to finalize a programmatic merger with Catholic Charities of Shiawassee and Genesee Counties. Late last year, the National Council on Alcoholism and Addictions, Greater Flint Area, Inc., transferred its outpatient substance abuse prevention and treatment services to Catholic Charities of Shiawassee and Genesee Counties. While the Mott Foundation’s original grant helped to offset transition and relocation expenses of the merger, this increase will cover the costs associated with dissolving the National Council on Alcoholism and Addictions, Greater Flint Area, Inc., including accounting fees, legal services, and other outstanding obligations.

title: Merger Technical Assistance
grantee: National Council on Alcoholism and Addictions, Greater Flint Area, Inc.
description: This grant will provide the National Council on Alcoholism and Addictions, Greater Flint Area, Inc. with technical support to merge with the Catholic Charities of Shiawassee and Genesee Counties. Mott funding will offset the transition and relocation costs related to the merger and ensure that the community will have access to quality mental health and substance abuse services in the future.Established in 1952 as a general information center on alcohol abuse, the council provides outpatient substance abuse prevention and treatment services to economically underprivileged children, individuals and families.

title: General Purposes
description: Few regions in the United States have experienced the sustained economic trauma that Flint has while simultaneously demonstrating a remarkable community resilience. One expression of this resilience is the commitment that faith institutions have made in responding to the multiple challenges facing families and neighborhoods. In 2006, clergy and lay leaders from seven different denominations founded and incorporated Flint Area Congregations Together as a vehicle to address issues of poverty, violence, inadequate education, blight, and other concerns facing Flint and the region. Flint Area Congregations Together is an affiliate of the PICO National Network. This general purpose grant will provide partial support as the organization pursues its goals and objectives.
