This general purpose grant will provide partial support as the organization pursues its goals and objectives.

title: General Purposes
description: Few regions in the U.S. have experienced the sustained economic trauma of Flint, which has lost three-quarters of its manufacturing jobs in the past two decades. At the same time, the community has demonstrated remarkable resilience and is in the process of becoming a regional medical, educational and cultural center in mid-Michigan. One expression of this resilience has been the commitment that faith institutions have made to remaining in the city and responding to the multiple challenges facing families and neighborhoods. Several of these churches have joined together to begin a congregation-based community organizing project called Flint Area Congregations Together, an affiliate of the PICO National Network. Funding will provide partial support to the organization during the start-up phase.

title: South America Small Grants Program
description: Global Greengrants Fund is an international collaborative of environmental donors established in 1993 to strengthen grassroots environmental NGOs by providing small grants to groups in developing countries. This grant increase will expand the capacity of Global Greengrants Fund’s South America Small Grants Program by supporting local communities’ efforts to actively participate in public discussions on regional infrastructure. In addition, the small grants fund will address emerging issues related to energy production, including biofuel production in South America; large dam expansion; and other resource extraction activities that will have major impacts on ecosystems, the natural resource base, and community livelihoods. Activities to be supported through the small grants will be educational meetings as well as strategy and training sessions.

title: South America Small Grants Program
description: Global Greengrants Fund is an international collaborative of environmental donors established in 1993 to strengthen grassroots, environmental, nongovernmental organizations by providing small grants to groups in developing countries. This grant increase will cover the travel and lodging costs for the grantee’s staff to make a presentation at a training workshop on private philanthropy for high-net-worth individuals and their advisors in Brazil.

title: South America Small Grants Program
description: Global Greengrants Fund is an international collaborative of environmental donors established in 1993 to strengthen grassroots, environmental, nongovernmental organizations by providing small grants to groups in developing countries. This renewal grant will continue support for a small grants fund for South American community organizations. These small grants support local communities’ efforts to actively participate in public discussions on regional integration infrastructure projects (highways, waterways) in South America, that are being funded by multilateral and regional financial institutions. In addition, the small grants fund will address issues related to energy production, including biofuel production in South America; large dam expansion; and other resource extraction activities. Grants will support meetings, applied research, educational campaigns, and capacity building.

title: South America Small Grants Program
description: Global Greengrants Fund is an international collaborative of environmental donors established in 1993 to strengthen grassroots, environmental, nongovernmental organizations by providing small grants to groups in developing countries. This renewal grant will expand and continue support for a small grants fund for South American community organizations. These small grants support local communities’ efforts to actively participate in public discussions on regional infrastructure projects (highways, waterways) and energy production in South America, that are being funded by multilateral and regional financial institutions, including the Brazilian National Development Bank. Grants will support meetings, applied research, educational initiatives, and capacity building.

title: South America Small Grants Program
description: The Center for Socio-Environmental Support is a grantmaking and capacity building organization focused on providing small grants and trainings to strengthen grassroots, environmental, nongovernmental, and civil society organizations. This grant renewal will support the small grants program in South America to build capacity in local communities impacted by large-scale energy and infrastructure projects, which are funded by international and national financial institutions, including the Brazilian Development Bank.

title: South America Small Grants Program
description: The Center for Socio-Environmental Support is a grantmaking and capacity building organization focused on strengthening grassroots environmental and civil society organizations. This grant increase will support a study to identify the challenges of providing access to clean, renewable energy to underserved communities in South America and provide recommendations on how to establish and improve programs for expanding access to energy.

title: South America Small Grants Program
description: The Socio-Environmental Fund CASA is a grantmaking and capacity building organization focused on providing small grants to strengthen community, environmental, and civil society organizations. This grant will renew support for the South American Regional Fund to support local communities impacted by large-scale energy and infrastructure projects, which are financed by international and national financial institutions, including the Brazilian Development Bank.

title: South America Small Grants Program
description: Socio-Environmental Fund CASA is a small grantmaking and capacity building organization focused on strengthening grassroots environmental and civil society organizations. This grant increase will enable the organization to coordinate and fund indigenous and civil society leaders to attend the International Funders of Indigenous Peoples Conference and two coordination meetings in Lima, Peru in 2016.

title: South America Small Grants Program
description: The Socioenvironmental Fund CASA is a grantmaking and capacity building organization focused on providing small grants to strengthen community, environmental, and civil society organizations. This grant will renew support for the South America Small Grants Program, which supports local communities and groups working on issues of energy infrastructure and sustainable finance throughout South America.

title: South America Small Grants Program
description: The Socio-Environmental Fund CASA is a grantmaking and capacity building organization focused on providing small grants to strengthen community, environmental, and civil society organizations. Over the past grant period, the grantee made 150 small grants in seven South American countries. This grant will renew support for the South America Small Grants Program to support local communities and groups working on issues of energy infrastructure and sustainable finance throughout South America.

title: South America Small Grants Program
description: This grant will enable the Global Greengrants Fund to establish a small grants fund for South American community organizations. These small grants will support local communities’ efforts to participate in public discussions on a regional infrastructure initiative for South America, which will be funded by the World Bank, the Inter-American Development Bank and other regional financial institutions. In addition, the small grants fund will address emerging issues related to energy production, including biofuel production in South America; large dam expansion; and other resource extraction activities that will have major impacts on ecosystems, the natural resource base and community livelihoods. Activities to be supported through the small grants will be educational meetings as well as strategy and training sessions.Global Greengrants Fund is an international collaborative of environmental donors established in 1993 to strengthen environmental non-governmental organizations by providing small grants to groups in developing countries.

title: Flint Graduation and Dropout Research Project
description: This grant will enable Editorial Projects in Education, through its research center, to assist the Flint Community Schools in evaluating its graduation and dropout rate data. Editorial Projects in Education will provide the district with an informed view of the number of students who are completing school and an in-depth understanding of the scope and nature of the causes and consequences of the graduation crisis in Flint and Genesee County. Activities for the project include: developing a statistical graduation profile; examining the social and economic consequences of students failing to complete school; and developing an early warning/predictor system that identifies students at greater risk of dropping out of school.

title: Field-Level Evaluation of Technology Services
description: This grant will provide partial support for the second and third years of a three-year evaluation of the nonprofit technology service field. The goals of the evaluation are to: assess the impact of technology on nonprofit organizational efficiency and mission achievement; understand the impact and effectiveness of services provided by technology service providers; and build evaluation capacity of technology service providers and establish systems to support ongoing, collaborative evaluation efforts among them. The evaluation is being conducted by NPower, a national network of nonprofit technology assistance providers, in partnership with the Nonprofit Technology Enterprise Network, a membership organization of people and organizations who help nonprofits understand and employ technology. The evaluation will include technology assistance benchmark analyses and case study development at the organizational level, as well as research at the sector level to develop a set of evaluation resources for technology service providers, nonprofit organizations and funders.

title: General Purposes
description: The Midwest Community Foundations’ Ventures is a supporting organization of the Council of Michigan Foundations. Having renamed itself from the Michigan Community Foundations’ Ventures and expanded its geographical scope to include Illinois, Ohio, and potentially Indiana, the grantee develops and manages collaborative initiatives that deliver continued innovation in the community foundation field. These include: (1) community-building initiatives (retaining local and regional wealth for philanthropy, strengthening the community foundation role of civic engagement, and promoting sustainable development through better land use); (2) resource-building programs (sharing best practices for marketing and development, facilitating regional marketing, and supporting and leveraging national standards); and (3) capacity-building tactics (advancing board development, expanding technical assistance, and building sustainable infrastructure for regional associations).

title: General Purposes
description: Midwest Community Foundations’ Ventures exists to build stronger communities through collaborative activities by community foundations, primarily in Michigan, Ohio, Indiana, and Illinois. Initiatives focus on advancing innovation and growth through researching opportunities, facilitating networking and mutual learning, providing technical assistance, promoting National Standards for U.S. Community Foundations, capturing efficiencies, and serving as a pilot region for efforts with potential broader application. Recent achievements include increasing the number and quality of submissions for national standards compliance and launching IRA charitable rollover and Roth IRA conversion marketing portfolios. In 2010-2012, work will include the provision of training on financial administration, sustainability, and succession planning; the preparation of toolkits on business model innovation and match-day events; and a retreat for chief executives. The organization will also conduct preliminary research on a potential multiyear initiative to build community foundation capacity to lead economic revitalization in eight small- and medium-sized automotive communities.

title: General Purposes
description: The Midwest Community Foundations’ Ventures – formerly the Michigan Community Foundations’ Ventures – is a supporting organization of the Council of Michigan Foundations. Since changing its name, it has expanded its geographical scope to include Illinois, Ohio and potentially, Indiana.This grant will enable the organization to continue to develop and manage community-building initiatives, resource-building programs and capacity-building tactics for the community foundation field. In addition, funding will build on past grants to support a community foundation research and development incubator and a regional marketing initiative.

title: Strini Moodley Leadership Fund
description: Strini Moodley was one of the founders of South Africa’s black consciousness movement. A contemporary comrade and colleague of the late Steve Bantu Biko, father of the black consciousness movement in South Africa, Strini was incarcerated on Robben Island for five years for his beliefs in a free, democratic, just, and nonracial South Africa. During his life, he was also jailed on numerous other occasions, regularly tortured by the South African security police, and constantly placed under banning orders and house arrests, which limited his access to people and prevented him from pursuing his professional career as a journalist. This grant will provide support to the Umtapo Centre, the organization he founded, to establish the Strini Moodley Leadership Fund to honor his contribution to the struggle for freedom in South Africa. The fund will be dedicated to supporting critical dialogue and leadership development in South Africa and on the African continent. It also will be a forum for debate and discussion on all the challenges that face South Africa as it struggles to build a nonracial democracy which respects equality, diversity, and tolerance.

title: PICO-ACORN Communications Capacity Building
description: For several years, local community organizations affiliated with the Association of Community Organizations for Reform Now (ACORN) and PICO National Network have had increasingly good relationships. Although the networks have different histories and organizing approaches, local groups have worked in the same cities and regions on similar issues that are critical to working families.This grant will enable ACORN Institute to strengthen the capacity of these two community organizing networks through joint planning and training in the field of communications, and building the communications infrastructure within each of the networks.The mission of the ACORN Institute, founded in 2001, is to provide leadership development and training to help low- and moderate-income people improve their communities.

title: Diversity in Philanthropy Project
description: This grant supports the Diversity in Philanthropy Project, an initiative designed to advance strategic interventions for equity, diversity, and inclusion in philanthropy. The previous grant enabled the project to coordinate with leading research and professional organizations to develop new data-gathering approaches, engage approximately 1,000 field leaders and executives in high level conversations on diversity issues, and develop a national advisory group of leading CEOs, trustees, and network executives to guide the project. The next phase of the project will focus on four activities: promoting regionally based pilot efforts to improve field data and reporting; producing and disseminating diversity best practice case studies; piloting the first regional voluntary initiatives among committed foundations; and promoting further field-building and collaboration in support of diversity-focused funds. The New York Regional Association of Grantmakers is a membership organization of foundations, corporate-giving programs, and other philanthropies in the metropolitan New York region and beyond.

title: Diversity in Philanthropy Project
description: The New York Regional Association of Grantmakers is a membership organization of foundations, corporate-giving programs, and other philanthropies in the metropolitan New York region and beyond. This grant increase supports the Diversity in Philanthropy Project, an initiative designed to advance strategic interventions for equity, diversity, and inclusion in philanthropy. While the project is designed to be time limited, the promotion of diversity and inclusive practices must be carried forward by leading philanthropic sector infrastructure groups and networks. The grantee has therefore expanded the project’s scope to include a fieldwide, multiyear, strategic planning process. The initiative will help strengthen the diversity work and leadership of five anchor organizations on this issue in order to support them in carrying this work forward over time.

title: Diversity in Philanthropy Project
description: This grant will provide partial support to CIF of The San Francisco Foundation for the Diversity in Philanthropy Project, an initiative designed to advance strategic interventions for equity, diversity, and inclusion in philanthropy. This phase of the project will build on recommendations made by an advisory committee and will focus around five activities: executive consultations and consensus building to set an industry-wide agenda; creation of key elements of a voluntary compact among leading private foundations to address diversity within their own institutions; improvements in data and applied research to produce more informative and useful field diversity data; initiating new leadership recognition; and promoting a series of high level executive conversations to identify promising practices and ideas to expand foundation inclusiveness and effectiveness.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued general purpose support to CFLeads, an organization which aims to build the leadership capacity of community foundations. In 2007, the grantee was chosen as the main implementation partner to foster community leadership by the Council on Foundations’ Community Foundations Leadership Team. During the past year, the grantee created and managed the work of a high-profile National Task Force on Community Leadership, which developed two frameworks on community leadership — one for individual community foundations and one for the field. The grantee also launched two community leadership networks which in total include representatives from 17 community foundations. In 2009, CFLeads will complete the work of the two existing community leadership networks and launch two new ones. It will also publish and promote the use of the National Task Force on Community Leadership’s frameworks throughout the community foundation field and prepare a two-day curriculum on public policy for community foundations.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued general purpose support to CFLeads, an organization which aims to build the leadership capacity of community foundations in the United States. Since 2007, CFLeads has been the Council on Foundations Community Foundations Leadership Team’s main implementation partner to foster community leadership. The grantee has developed frameworks and tools on community leadership for both individual community foundations and the community foundation field. The grantee has also conducted intensive workshops for networks of community foundations, hosted Webinars for hundreds of participants, designed sessions and/or presented at several philanthropic conferences, and developed coursework on public policy. The grantee is currently developing educational programming and training tools that can be more broadly disseminated and easily adapted. Over the next year, it will continue to act as the leading developmental, educational, and consulting organization on community leadership for community foundations.

title: General Purposes
description: CFLeads helps community foundations advance the practice of community leadership to build thriving communities. The grantee has developed frameworks, training programs, and other resources for both individual community foundations and the community foundation field. In 2010, the grantee developed the following products for community foundations: a public policy curriculum and faculty guide; a community leadership discussion guide; online tools; a summary of model donor engagement activities; and a self-evaluation instrument for measuring community leadership capacity. Educational offerings also included a regional learning forum, a community leadership cluster seminar series, two field-wide webinars, and two sessions at the Council on Foundations’ fall conference. In 2011, the grantee will continue to act as the leading developmental, educational, and consulting organization on community leadership for community foundations. Planned offerings include an executive leadership network, issue networks, community leadership assessments, and information resources. CFLeads is currently a supporting organization to the Greater Kansas City Community Foundation.

title: General Purposes
description: CFLeads (formerly the Coalition of Community Foundations for Youth) aims to build the leadership capacity of community foundations grounded in values of equity and inclusion, with particular emphasis on racial and ethnic diversity. CFLeads’ main programmatic activity during the grant period will be to work with and through the Council on Foundations’ Community Foundation Leadership Team to foster community leadership among community foundations. This work will involve the creation and management of a National Task Force on Community Leadership, as well as the launching of two regional leadership networks composed of 10-15 community foundations each. CFLeads is in the process of creating an alliance with Stanford University’s John W. Gardner Center for Youth and Their Communities. General purposes funding will help CFLeads to implement this alliance and to build institutional capacity for a more robust focus on community leadership.

title: Diversity in Philanthropy Field Scan
description: Based on a variety of conversations and initiatives currently under way, the field of philanthropy appears to have renewed interest in tackling the question of how to increase diversity and inclusion within philanthropy. This project has undertaken a field scan in order to identify, describe, and assess existing resources for supporting and training diverse staff in philanthropy, as well as to seek resources that help organizations more effectively understand and utilize diverse perspectives. Renewal support will allow Rockefeller Philanthropy Advisors to finalize and test the report with the field, disseminate to key audiences, and undertake additional communications work, including possible op-ed type essays and two monographs that address important issues related to diversity in philanthropy.

title: Diversity in Philanthropy Field Scan
description: Rockefeller Philanthropy Advisors provides research and counsel on charitable giving; develops philanthropy programs; and offers complete program, administrative, and management services for foundations and trusts. Over the past decade, Rockefeller Philanthropy Advisors served more than 100 clients and facilitated over $850 million in gifts/grants to more than 40 countries. The field of philanthropy has a renewed interest in increasing diversity and inclusion, and a variety of conversations and initiatives are under way. This project has disseminated a field scan identifying resources for supporting and training diverse staff in philanthropy, as well as resources that help organizations more effectively understand and utilize diverse perspectives. This grant increase allows the grantee to increase dissemination of the original report, and to produce and disseminate two additional monographs that address important issues related to diversity in philanthropy.

title: Diversity in Philanthropy Field Scan
description: Based on a variety of conversations and initiatives currently under way, the field of philanthropy appears to have renewed interest in tackling the question of how to increase diversity and inclusion within philanthropy. The diversity “challenge” for foundations includes both attracting a diverse talent pool to consider a career in philanthropy rather than the private sector, and fully including the voices and perspectives of that diverse talent pool in the decisionmaking of philanthropy. The proposed program, a project of Rockefeller Philanthropy Advisors, will scan the field in order to identify, describe, and assess existing resources for supporting and training diverse staff in philanthropy, as well as seek resources that help organizations more effectively understand and utilize diverse perspectives.

title: Construction Trades Employment Project
grantee: Faith Access to Community Economic Development
description: As the labor market in the Flint area has changed over time, youth who are not college bound face increased difficulty in finding livable wage employment. While high school graduates were once able to find employment in manufacturing plants, they are now faced with few options for entry-level employment that lead to self-sufficiency. This grant to Faith Access to Community Economic Development will provide funds for a planning process that will develop a construction trades training program for youth in the city of Flint. The planning process will engage schools, employers, housing agencies, workforce development organizations and community residents in the planning of enhanced services for youth interested in housing and construction trades.

title: HELP Team Mobile Classrooms
geographic_focus: New Orleans, Biloxi, Bay Saint Louis, Mobile
description: This grant will support the State Educational Technology Directors Association in its efforts to develop mobile classrooms for schools in areas affected by Hurricanes Katrina and Rita. The effort will be coordinated by the Hurricane Education Leadership Team, a collaboration of information technology companies, government agencies and foundations that are focused on recovery efforts in five Gulf Region states. It will outfit five schools with mobile classrooms consisting of 25-30 wireless laptops, a wireless access point, other technological assets, and provide professional development. The five schools will also create a learning community to collaborate, share and develop leadership. The mobile classrooms will be used after school, as well as during the regular school day, and will facilitate the creation of a 21st Century learning environment for young people.

title: Asset Funders Network
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant provides partial support to the New York Regional Association of Grantmakers to manage the Asset Funders Network. The network was created in 2005 to build a community of grantmakers committed to asset-building issues. Its ultimate goal is to increase both the amount and the impact of philanthropic funding on asset-building activities. Activities planned for the two-year grant period include hosting in-person meetings and conferences, organizing a conference call series, and developing an information clearinghouse. Since its inception in 2005, the network has established a stable advisory structure and grown a base of 20 active members.

title: Asset Funders Network
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant provides partial support to Philanthropy New York to manage the Asset Funders Network. The network was created in 2005 to build a community of grantmakers committed to asset building issues. Its ultimate goal is to increase both the amount and the impact of philanthropic funding on asset building activities. Activities planned for the two-year renewal grant period include organizing in-person meetings and conferences, hosting a monthly webinar series, and supporting the development of regional networks. Since its inception in 2005, the network has established a stable steering committee structure and grown a base of eight contributing members and nearly 100 active participants.

title: Asset Funders Network
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant provides partial support to Philanthropy New York for the ongoing activities of the Asset Funders Network. The network was created in 2005 to build a community of grantmakers committed to asset-building issues. Its ultimate goal is to increase both the amount and the impact of philanthropic funding on asset-building issues. Activities planned for the two-year grant period include hosting in-person meetings and conferences, and webinars. Since its inception in 2005, the network has established a stable advisory committee, implemented a membership structure, and grown its base of active members.

title: Asset Funders Network
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant provides partial support to Philanthropy New York to manage the Asset Funders Network. The Mott Foundation helped create the network in 2005 in order to build a community of grantmakers committed to asset building issues. The grantee’s ultimate goal is to increase both the amount and impact of philanthropic funding on asset building issues. Activities planned for the two-year grant period include hosting in-person meetings and conferences, organizing a conference call series, and developing a working group focused on children’s savings accounts. Since its inception in 2005, the network has established a stable advisory structure and grown a base of 100 active members.

title: Asset Funders Network
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant provides partial support to Philanthropy New York to manage the Asset Funders Network. The Mott Foundation helped create the network in 2005 in order to build a community of grantmakers committed to asset building issues. The grantee’s ultimate goal is to increase both the amount and impact of philanthropic funding on asset building issues. Since its inception, the network has established a stable advisory structure and grown a solid base of members. Activities planned for 2017-2018 include in-person meetings and conferences, a webinar series, and a working group focused on children’s savings accounts. Philanthropy New York enhances and increases the ability of organizational and individual philanthropists located in the New York region.

title: Asset Funders Network
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant provides partial support to the New York Regional Association of Grantmakers to manage the Asset Funders Network. The network was created to increase both the amount and the impact of philanthropic funding on asset-building activities. Activities planned for the two-year grant period include hosting in-person meetings and conferences, organizing a conference call series, and developing an information clearinghouse. Since its inception in 2005, the network has established a stable advisory structure and grown a base of 20 active members.

title: Community Data and Benchmarking Project
description: The Genesee Chamber Foundation is a supporting organization of the Genesee Regional Chamber of Commerce organized to receive and administer funds for educational and charitable purposes and the public welfare of Genesee County, Michigan. This grant to the Genesee Chamber Foundation will provide funds to establish an “economic dashboard.” The Genesee Chamber Foundation will contract with the Upjohn Institute to develop a process that provides data, establishes community benchmarks, identifies needs, and prioritizes new initiatives. The Community Data and Benchmarking Project will allow the Genesee Regional Chamber of Commerce and Genesee Chamber Foundation to continue to play a leadership role in enhancing economic vitality, community development, and quality of life throughout Genesee County.

title: Organizing After Natural Disasters
geographic_focus: Asia, Central America, Haiti, United States
description: This grant supports a project of ActionAid International USA to organize an exchange among community organizers and leaders from disaster-affected communities in Asia and the Americas. The purpose of this exchange is to share experiences about ways that poor and vulnerable people have been engaged in a reconstruction process, strengthen the capacity of grassroots organizations to influence rebuilding policies in post-disaster situations, and document and disseminate best practices. Participants for this project will be selected on the basis of their role and experience in organizing in a post-disaster situation as well as on their connections to networks of organizations that will serve to disseminate the lessons learned. This grant increase will support the organization in covering additional costs incurred in organizing the exchange.

title: Organizing After Natural Disasters
geographic_focus: Asia, Haiti, Central America, United States
description: This grant will support a project that will enable community organizers and leaders from disaster-affected communities in Asia and the Americas to share experiences about ways that poor and vulnerable people have been engaged in a reconstruction process; strengthen the capacity of grassroots organizations to influence rebuilding policies in post-disaster situations; and document and disseminate best practices. Participants will be selected on the basis of their role and experience in organizing in a post-disaster situation as well as their connections to networks of organizations that will serve to disseminate the lessons learned.ActionAid works in more than 40 countries to fight poverty and highlight crucial issues related to basic human rights including food, shelter, work, education and healthcare. ActionAid International USA encourages practical collaboration and mutual learning between grassroots groups in the U.S. and their counterparts in other ActionAid countries.

title: Communicating the Costs of Sprawl
description: Numerous studies have documented the negative social, fiscal and environmental impacts of sprawl on urban, suburban and rural communities. These findings were underscored by the recommendations of the bipartisan Michigan Land Use Leadership Council, particularly those calling for solutions to uncoordinated land-use planning among Michigan’s local units of government. At the same time, there has been a tremendous change over the past several years in the way people communicate, gather information and participate in community decisionmaking. With this grant, the Land Information Access Association will initiate a regional communications demonstration project that explores innovative communications methods for stimulating a regionwide discussion on land use. The project will focus on the greater Traverse City region.

title: Barry Gaberman Lecture Fund
description: The King Baudouin Foundation United States, in cooperation with the Worldwide Initiatives for Grantmaker Support, has launched the Barry Gaberman Lecture Fund. This fund will support the Barry Gaberman Lecture on Global Philanthropy, which will take place every four years at the Worldwide Initiatives for Grantmaker Support Forum. The first lecture will be given by Barry Gaberman at the closing plenary of the 2006 forum in Bangkok, Thailand. Subsequent lectures will be given by leaders in the field of philanthropy.

title: Building Expansion
description: The Food Bank of Eastern Michigan distributes surplus food to the hungry in 22 counties in eastern Michigan. Through a network of 380 partner agencies, the food bank distributed 15 million pounds of food in 2005; however, this represents only a fraction of the needs of low-income families, children and the elderly in its service area. The food bank is at its capacity in the amount of food it can store and process in its current 42,000 square foot facility. This grant will provide partial support to the food bank in adding 7,000 square feet of refrigerated and freezer space to its current facility. This additional temperature-controlled space will allow the food bank to take advantage of the increasing availability of nutritious, fresh produce and frozen products. Following the expansion, food distribution will increase 10 percent and the Food Bank of Eastern Michigan will have the capacity to meet area needs for the next 15 years.

title: Institutional Development
description: The program goal is to strengthen civil society influence on national policies and practices regarding local development in Bulgaria. Established in 1995, the Foundation for Local Government Reform is a leading Bulgarian nongovernmental organization working effectively on improving the performance of local governments and broadening public understanding of the problems and importance of local development in Bulgaria. During the grant period, the foundation will focus on increasing its organizational capacity and diversifying its funding base. Project activities include organizing staff training and professional development in the areas of local development, strategic planning, and European Union policies and funding mechanisms. Also, the foundation will develop new research, training, and consultancy services and will market these services to relevant public institutions, international organizations, and nongovernmental organizations.

title: Financial Analysis
description: This grant increase will allow the YWCA of Greater Flint to improve the organization’s accounting and financial reporting systems. The YWCA of Greater Flint is a nonprofit organization located in downtown Flint that has provided the community with critical, mission-driven programming and services for almost 100 years. With the original grant, the organization hired expert financial services to complete a financial analysis and make recommendations for developing new accounting procedures and systems. However, additional funds are needed to implement the recommended changes.

title: Financial Analysis
description: The YWCA of Greater Flint is a nonprofit organization located in downtown Flint, Michigan that has provided the community with critical, mission-driven programming and services for almost 100 years. The organization has begun a comprehensive analysis and evaluation of its facilities, programming, and board and staff development.This grant will enable the YWCA of Greater Flint to hire expert financial services to assist them in analyzing and improving the organization’s accounting and financial reporting systems.

title: Local Government Support Programme
description: This grant will assist the Centre for Public Participation in its efforts to advocate for and facilitate public participation in governance processes, particularly at the local level. The centre works to strengthen public participation in governance, advance the achievement of civil, political, and socioeconomic rights and improve people’s quality of life. The Local Government Support Programme will utilize capacity-building training workshops, foster relationships between civil society and their elected local leaders, and promote social accountability in government processes to advance effective engagement between communities, civil society organizations, and municipalities in the KwaZulu-Natal province.

title: Local Government Support Programme
description: The Centre for Public Participation works in KwaZulu-Natal province of South Africa to strengthen public participation in governance and advance the achievement of civil, political, and socioeconomic rights and poverty alleviation. The Local Government Support Programme helps to build bridges between communities and elected leaders at the local government level in order for people to realize their rights and access basic services such as water, electricity, and housing. Past support enabled the grantee to facilitate workshops and conduct training for nonprofit organizations to understand and engage with public participation policies, mechanisms, and processes. It also provided platforms for engagement between nonprofit organizations and government; trained government officials on appropriate ways to engage communities meaningfully around the development of local plans; and exposed nonprofit representatives to government budgeting processes. This grant will support the grantee to continue with these activities.

title: Local Government Support Programme
description: The Centre for Public Participation advocates for and facilitates the participation of communities in governance, particularly at the local level. It works to make an impact on policy, knowledge and practice in relation to community participation in local government. This grant will enable the center to train civil society organizations in KwaZulu-Natal to understand municipal processes and mobilize their communities to participate in local decisionmaking, especially related to their own development.

title: Prima Civitas
description: Michigan State University established the Prima Civitas program to aid regional economic development in mid-Michigan. This grant to the university will enable Prima Civitas to manage the three-year, $15 million Workforce Innovation in Regional Economic Development grant program. Prima Civitas will work to attract additional resources to grow the economic development infrastructure in ways that benefit the many diverse communities of mid-Michigan. This economic development infrastructure will play a pivotal role in the region’s ability to attract companies in the emerging business sectors that ultimately will be the job providers of the future global economy.

title: National Transitional Jobs Network
grantee: Heartland Alliance for Human Needs & Human Rights
description: The National Transitional Jobs Network, a program of the Heartland Alliance for Human Needs & Human Rights, is a national coalition of organizations supporting the field of transitional employment. Over the past several years, the grantee has become a key leadership organization in the workforce development field with more than 120 dues-paying members representing government officials, policy advocates, workforce practitioners, funders, and community organizations. This renewal grant will support the program’s services to the transitional employment field.

grantee: Heartland Alliance for Human Needs & Human Rights

title: National Transitional Jobs Network
grantee: Heartland Alliance for Human Needs & Human Rights
description: The National Transitional Jobs Network, a program of the Heartland Alliance for Human Needs & Human Rights, is a national coalition of organizations dedicated to helping chronically unemployed Americans back to work. Since its founding, the network has become a key leader in the workforce development field, with more than 120 dues-paying members representing government officials, policy advocates, workforce practitioners, funders, and community organizations. This renewal grant will support the organization’s ongoing efforts to advance effective employment solutions that combine wage-paid work, jobs skills training, and supportive services to help individuals facing barriers to employment succeed in the workforce.

title: National Transitional Jobs Network
grantee: Heartland Alliance for Human Needs & Human Rights
description: The National Transitional Jobs Network, a program of the Heartland Alliance for Human Needs & Human Rights, is a national coalition of organizations dedicated to helping chronically unemployed Americans find work. Since its founding, the network has become a key leader in the workforce development field, with more than 120 dues-paying members representing government officials, policy advocates, workforce practitioners, funders, and community organizations. This grant will support the grantee’s ongoing efforts to advance effective employment solutions that combine wage-paid work, jobs skills training, and supportive services to help disconnected youth facing barriers to employment succeed in the workforce.

title: National Transitional Jobs Network
grantee: Heartland Alliance for Human Needs & Human Rights
description: The National Transitional Jobs Network, a program of the Heartland Alliance, is a national coalition of organizations supporting the field of transitional employment. Over the past several years, the National Transitional Jobs Network has become a key leadership organization in the workforce development field with more than 120 dues-paying members representing government officials, policy advocates, workforce practitioners, funders, and community organizations. This grant will support the program’s services to the transitional employment field.

title: Film Documentary "Life in Grade 12"
description: This grant will support the organization, Women Make Movies, to produce a documentary about education in South Africa since the democratic changes in 1994. Titled, “Life in Grade 12”, the documentary chronicles the lives of four black students as they focus on getting through the final year of their formal high school education. Passing the final school examination is extremely important for black South Africans as this very often determines not only whether or not they will gain access to a university, but also what kind of employment opportunities they can aspire toward. The documentary, therefore, not only examines issues related to education, but also looks at the connections between school, community, and family, and the role that education plays in the transition from apartheid to democracy.

title: Structural Phase of the Children's Hospital
description: This grant will provide support to the Nelson Mandela Children’s Fund to undertake the final steps in the establishment of a dedicated children’s hospital in Gauteng, South Africa. Based on the overwhelming need for improved health-care services for children in South Africa, a feasibility study has been conducted to determine the size and specialties of a new children’s hospital, and potential sites have been identified. The next phase in the development of the hospital is to produce a detailed business plan and secure the licensing necessary to open a children’s hospital. Work will include establishing the governance and management structure, designing the hospital, developing fundraising plans and marketing strategies, and selecting the appropriate location. If built, the hospital will bear the name of Nelson Mandela. The Nelson Mandela Children’s Fund is a grantmaking and development organization focused on children and youth in South Africa.

title: Feasibility Study for the Proposed Children's Hospital in Gauteng, South Africa
description: This grant will provide support to the Nelson Mandela Children’s Fund to undertake a feasibility study on the establishment of a dedicated children’s hospital in Gauteng, which will, if built, bear the name of Nelson Mandela. The feasibility study will be carried out by a professional consulting organization over a six-month period and will test the viability and examine all aspects of creating such a hospital in the country. Mott’s grant will partially support the consultant’s fees, local travel and administrative costs.

title: Community Schools Quality Partnership
description: The project goal is to strengthen the development of community schools in Central/Eastern Europe and Russia. The Ukrainian Step by Step Foundation will lead a multinational team to refine and disseminate community schools’ self-assessment standards. Local partners will be trained in the application of assessment measures and will assist no fewer than 80 schools in devising and implementing resultant improvement plans. Outcomes will be presented at an international conference and posted on the project Web site. In the earlier phase of the project, the partners produced detailed standards for community schools, which were drawn from the varied experience of Ukraine, Russia, Moldova, and the Czech Republic, as well as the United Kingdom. They also produced and piloted a self-assessment guide for schools and related training manual and a Web site. Established in 1999, the Ukrainian Step by Step Foundation is an independent foundation which seeks to facilitate educational development and innovative educational initiatives in Ukraine.

title: Community Schools Quality Partnership
description: The project goal is to strengthen the development of community schools in Central/Eastern Europe and Russia. The Ukrainian Step by Step Foundation will lead a multinational team to further refine and disseminate community schools’ self-assessment standards and practices aimed at improving school performance. Partners in ten countries will be trained in the application of assessment measures and will assist no fewer than 50 additional schools in devising and implementing school improvement plans. Case studies of assessment practice and resulting improvement plans will be developed and presented at an international conference and posted on the project Web site. In 2009-2010, the standards and accompanying self-assessment guide for schools were translated into eight languages and were used by over 80 schools to develop improvement plans. Established in 1999, the Ukrainian Step by Step Foundation is an independent foundation which seeks to facilitate educational development and innovative educational initiatives in Ukraine.

title: Community Schools Quality Partnership
description: The project goal is to strengthen the development of community schools in Central/Eastern Europe and Russia and beyond. The International Association “Interactive Open Schools” will lead a multinational team to further disseminate self-assessment standards and practices of community schools aimed at improving school performance and student attainment. Partners in ten countries will share best practices in community school development with a growing range of stakeholders. They will conduct research into the educational attainment levels within community schools to demonstrate the effectiveness of the model. They will also provide new assessment materials for use nationally and internationally. In 2011-2013, the partners created a Russian and English language compendium of case studies detailing successful use of the self-assessment tool in changing school management and practice. The program was also expanded to formally include Poland and Mongolia. Established in Bosnia-Herzegovina in 2004, the grantee works to promote school development, democratization of school administration, and cooperation between schools and their local communities.

title: Community Schools Quality Partnership
description: The project goal is to strengthen the development of community schools in Central/Eastern Europe and Russia and beyond. The International Association “Interactive Open Schools” will lead a multinational team to further disseminate community schools’ self-assessment standards and practices aimed at improving school performance and student achievement. Partners in 11 countries will share best practices in community school development with a growing range of stakeholders. They will conduct research into the educational achievement levels within community schools to demonstrate the effectiveness of the model. They will also provide new assessment materials for use nationally and internationally. In 2013-2015, the partners developed additional resources to strengthen and promote community schools, including a manual on parental engagement in community schools. To promote the core principles of a community school, the partners created a promotional video, leaflet, and poster in Russian and English. The partners conducted a series of international- and national-level Webinars and redesigned and updated the project’s Website. Established in Bosnia-Herzegovina in 2004, the grantee works to promote school development, democratization of school administration, and cooperation between schools and their local communities.

title: Community Schools Quality Partnership
description: The project goal is to strengthen the development of community schools in Central/Eastern Europe and Russia. To this end, the Ukrainian Step by Step Foundation will lead a project to define and apply quality standards in teaching, participation, and outreach with a group of regional partners. Standards will draw on the differing experiences and approaches of community education practice in Ukraine, Russia, Moldova, and the Czech Republic, as well as the United Kingdom. This variety will encourage the creation of robust, yet flexible, standards responsive to the evolving priorities of participating schools as community education expands in the project countries. Project outcomes will be valuable both for those schools wishing to adopt the community school model and for those already experienced and wishing to improve their capacities in key areas. The Ukrainian Step by Step Foundation was created as an independent foundation in 1999 with the aim of facilitating educational development and innovative educational initiatives in Ukraine.

title: MegaCity Project
description: The Human Rights Media Trust produces films and documentaries that educate people about human rights. This grant will support the trust to develop a six-part documentary drama series designed to de-mystify the workings of local government and to make it more accountable and effective. The series was conceived by a writer and academic who has extensive experience in local government and popular culture and will raise awareness on current challenges facing local government. It will cover a range of topical issues like the nature of service delivery and the challenges thereof, and the mechanisms used by local governments to enhance community participation in municipal decisionmaking. It will also explore how the media can enhance municipal accountability.

title: Advice Office Support Project
grantee: Association of University Legal Aid Institutions Trust
description: This grant will provide continued support to the Association of University Legal Aid Institutions Trust for its advice office support project. The trust promotes access to justice for poor and marginalized communities through fostering partnerships between legal aid institutions attached to universities in South Africa and community-based advice offices. Through this project, the trust has provided funding and other forms of support to community-based advice offices to ensure that they effectively provide legal and related services to the country’s poor. Working through established access to justice clusters, specific activities included training and mentorship to paralegals working in community-based advice offices; capacity-building assistance to advice offices; back-up legal services to paralegals and direct legal assistance to indigent communities; and educational materials and information sessions to inform people as to their rights and where to get assistance.

title: Advice Office Support Project
grantee: Association of University Legal Aid Institutions Trust
description: The Association of University Legal Aid Institutions Trust promotes access to justice for poor and marginalized communities through fostering partnerships between legal aid institutions attached to universities in South Africa and community-based advice offices. The Association of University Legal Aid Institutions Trust has provided support to community-based advice offices to ensure that they effectively provide legal and related services to the country’s poor. Project activities have included training and mentorship to paralegals working in community-based advice offices, capacity building assistance to advice offices, backup legal services to paralegals, direct legal assistance to indigent communities, and workshops to inform people about their rights and how to access them. The grantee will continue with these activities, and strengthen networks and collaboration among institutions working in the community-based advice office sector.

title: Advice Office Support Project
grantee: Association of University Legal Aid Institutions Trust
description: The Association of University Legal Aid Institutions Trust promotes access to justice for poor and marginalized communities through fostering partnerships between legal aid institutions attached to universities in South Africa and community-based advice offices. The grantee has provided support to community-based advice offices to ensure that they effectively provide legal and related services to the country’s poor. Past support has enabled the grantee to conduct workshops to inform people about their rights and how to access them; train and mentor paralegals working in community-based advice offices on various aspects of the law; provide backup legal services to paralegals; and assist poor people with free legal advice and related services. This grant will support the grantee to continue supporting paralegals to provide legal services to poor people and to strengthen networks and collaboration among institutions working in the community-based advice office sector.

title: Advice Office Support Project
grantee: Association of University Legal Aid Institutions Trust
description: The Association of University Legal Aid Institutions Trust promotes access to justice for poor and marginalized communities through fostering partnerships between legal aid institutions attached to universities in South Africa and community-based advice offices. Past support has enabled the grantee to make small grants to advice offices; conduct workshops, including tailor-made sessions for school children and to inform people about their rights and how to access them; train and mentor paralegals working in community-based advice offices on various aspects of the law and office administration; provide backup legal services to paralegals in advice offices; and assist poor people with free legal advice and related services. This grant will support the Association of University Legal Aid Institutions Trust to continue training and supporting paralegals to provide legal services to poor people, make small grants to advice offices, and host workshops for community members on human rights and how to access them.

title: Advice Office Support Project
grantee: Association of University Legal Aid Institutions Trust
description: The Association of University Legal Aid Institutions Trust promotes access to justice for poor and marginalized communities through fostering partnerships between legal aid institutions attached to universities in South Africa and community-based advice offices. Past support has enabled the grantee to make small grants to advice offices, conduct workshops to inform people about their rights and how to access them, train and mentor paralegals working in community-based advice offices on various aspects of the law and office administration, provide backup legal services to paralegals in advice offices, and assist poor people with free legal advice and related services. This grant will provide support to train paralegals on various aspects of the law, train management committees on governance, make small grants to advice offices and university law clinics, provide legal assistance to poor people, and host workshops for community members and school children on human rights and how to access them.

title: Advice Office Support Project
grantee: Association of University Legal Aid Institutions Trust
description: The Association of University Legal Aid Institutions Trust promotes access to justice for poor and marginalized communities through fostering partnerships between legal aid institutions attached to universities in South Africa and community-based advice offices. This grant will provide funding and other forms of support to community-based advice offices to ensure that they effectively provide legal and related services to their respective communities. This will be achieved through regranting to an average of ten advice offices, training and mentoring of paralegals working in advice offices, and providing assistance for the efficient administration of these offices. Attorneys also will provide hands-on support to disadvantaged communities on legal cases, which the paralegals are unable to handle or resolve.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to Participative Development Initiative, an organization that assists communities in implementing sustainable programs through training and mobilization of resources from their local governments for development initiatives. It advocates for the sustainable use of natural and human resources for economic and social development in South Africa. Established in 1998, the Participative Development Initiative has successfully provided training and mentoring support to hundreds of community-based initiatives in several provinces across South Africa. Working with civil society organizations and Ward Committees in targeted communities, the grantee will provide education and training for community members to develop a culture of self-reliance, help identify sustainable projects based on available human and natural resources, teach communities how to engage in local government planning and resource allocation processes, and advocate for community-initiated sustainable development projects.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to Participative Development Initiative, an organization that assists communities with implementing sustainable programs through education and mobilization of resources from their local governments for development initiatives. Past achievements include working in targeted communities in the KwaZulu-Natal province to: provide education and training for community members to expand their understanding of sustainable development and develop a culture of self-reliance; help communities identify and prioritize sustainable projects in the areas of education, natural resource management, sustainable economic development, and basic needs; teach communities how to engage in local government planning and resource allocation processes; and advocate for community-initiated sustainable development projects.

title: General Purposes
description: The Participative Development Initiative assists communities in implementing sustainable programs through training and mobilization of resources from their local governments for development initiatives. It advocates for the sustainable use of natural and human resources for economic and social development. Mott’s previous support helped build the institutional capacity of community-based structures to enable them to implement sustainable development programs. The grantee will train members of ward committees, the structures through which communities participate in local government, and community-based organizations to develop and implement sustainable economic development programs at the local level. The grantee will further assist community members to engage and negotiate with local governments to ensure that community-initiated programs are included in local government planning processes and will provide hands-on assistance and guidance in the implementation of the development projects identified by the target communities.

title: Good Governance Learning Network
description: Isandla Institute is a policy research organization that focuses on the development of effective partnerships between government and the nonprofit sector, especially in terms of poverty alleviation. It coordinates the Good Governance Learning Network, an alliance of 16 South African nonprofit organizations that promotes good local governance. Network members have undertaken joint research and advocacy activities on issues including public participation, access to municipal information, municipal performance management and budgeting, and corruption. A report was produced and published in 2008, providing a civil society commentary on the state of governance in South Africa. Isandla Institute took over the coordination of the network from the Foundation for Contemporary Research in 2008, and this grant will support Isandla Institute to continue implementing activities that promote advocacy, networking, and sharing of experiences among civil society organizations working in the area of governance.

title: Good Governance Learning Network
description: Isandla Institute is a policy research organization that focuses on the development of effective partnerships between government and the nonprofit sector, especially in terms of poverty alleviation. It coordinates the Good Governance Learning Network, a network of South African nongovernmental organizations that promotes participatory, effective, accountable, and pro-poor local governance. Through previous support, members of the Good Governance Learning Network undertook research that explored partnerships between government and communities in the delivery of basic services like water, electricity, and housing. The network also published the annual State of Local Governance Reports. The 2011 report was titled “Recognising Community Voice and Dissatisfaction” and paved the way for fruitful engagement between members of the network and government in exploring ways to improve participatory local governance. This grant will support Isandla Institute to continue implementing activities of the Good Governance Learning Network.

title: Good Governance Learning Network
description: The Isandla Institute works to promote poverty alleviation and human rights by fostering effective partnerships between government and the nonprofit sector. It promotes dialogue and exchange, policy research, networking, and information dissemination on issues related to local governance and democracy. The grantee coordinates the Good Governance Learning Network, a network of South African nonprofits that promote participatory, effective, accountable and pro-poor local governance. Previous support enabled the grantee to publish two state of local governance reports titled “Active Citizenship Matters” in 2013 and “Community Resilience and Vulnerability in South Africa” in 2014. This grant will support the Isandla Institute to continue implementing activities of the Good Governance Learning Network such as producing knowledge through research, promoting learning among members, building strong partnership with local government, and producing annual state of local governance reports.

title: Good Governance Learning Network
description: Isandla Institute works to generate knowledge and build partnerships that promote poverty alleviation and human rights in South Africa. It conducts research, facilitates dialogues, disseminates information, and encourages networking on issues related to local governance and democratic and sustainable urban habitats. The grantee coordinates the Good Governance Learning Network, a national network of nonprofits that promotes participatory democracy, people-centered development, and effective local governance. Past support enabled the grantee to host learning seminars for members of the network and publish two “The State of Local Governance” annual reports in 2015 and 2016. This grant will enable the grantee to continue supporting the activities of the Good Governance Learning Network, including coordinating learning events for members, generating knowledge through research, growing membership, and nurturing partnerships with local government.

title: Good Governance Learning Network
description: The Foundation for Contemporary Research contributes to sustainable poverty alleviation interventions at the local level by facilitating municipal-community partnerships. It coordinates the Good Governance Learning Network, a loose alliance of 13 South African nonprofit organizations that work to promote good local governance. This grant will assist the Foundation for Contemporary Research to provide a platform for networking, learning, and sharing of experiences for members of the Good Governance Learning Network. Members will also undertake joint research and advocacy activities on issues, including public participation, access to municipal information, municipal performance management and budgeting, political systems and processes, corruption and poor administration. A “State of Local Government” report will be published annually and will provide a civil society commentary on the state of local government and governance in South Africa.

title: Diversity Training
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide continued funding to the Flint Institute of Music to implement Phase 3 of its diversity plan. Like similar organizations throughout the country, the Flint Institute of Music faces major challenges in increasing the number of minority participants, audiences, and staff that are reflective of the community it serves. Phases 1 and 2 identified cultural, racial, and economic barriers that prevent individuals from accessing the institute’s programs and provided diversity training to staff, faculty, and board members to improve cultural awareness, sensitivity, and competence through all aspects of the organization. Phase 3 will focus on further training and the transfer of training skills to staff, defining measurements of success, and the development of sustainability strategies to embed diversity practices throughout the organization.

title: Diversity Training
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide funding to the Flint Institute of Music to implement a key component of its diversity plan. The Flint Institute of Music, like similar organizations throughout the country, faces major challenges in increasing the number of minority participants, audiences, and staff that are reflective of the community it serves. Based on interviews with staff and other key stakeholders and data collected from patrons and the community from surveys and focus groups, barriers that prevent minorities from accessing the institute’s programs were identified. Using the information learned, diversity and inclusion training will be developed and implemented for staff, facility, and board members to improve cultural awareness, sensitivity, and competence through all aspects of the organization.

title: Making Michigan the Great Lakes Compact Leader
description: The Michigan Environmental Council, a leading statewide environmental organization, has helped coordinate the work of the environmental community on the Great Lakes Compact and related water management policy reforms. With this grant increase and associated grant period extension, the council will continue to work with partner groups to promote the compact and help implement new water-use policies recently adopted by the state.

title: Making Michigan the Great Lakes Compact Leader
description: Michigan has much to gain from conserving and wisely managing its water resources, which help define the state and support its economy. The Great Lakes Compact and the new Michigan-specific programs implementing it are precedent-setting tools for better water management. The Michigan Environmental Council, which works to protect vital water resources around the state, provided strong leadership in the development phase of the compact and new state programs. With continued support from the Mott Foundation, the council will work to ensure that the state’s new water programs are effectively implemented and that communities are fully engaged in the process of water management.

title: Making Michigan the Great Lakes Compact Leader
description: In December 2005, the Great Lakes’ governors released a proposed interstate compact that, once ratified, will establish a new, ecologically based program to manage water withdrawals and diversions throughout the United States portion of the basin. The Michigan Environmental Council, a statewide organization with more than 70 member groups, will help lead the efforts of the Michigan environmental community to educate citizens, state officials, and other opinion leaders about the compact and related water management policy reform issues.

title: Operating Support
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: Downtown Flint is currently in the midst of several redevelopment efforts that seek to reintroduce market-rate housing, restaurants, and commercial vitality to the city center. The Uptown Reinvestment Corporation has been a leader in the efforts to revitalize downtown Flint and has set up a supporting organization, Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, to raise funds for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation. This grant will support the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation’s continued downtown redevelopment efforts and other charitable purposes.

title: Virtual Call Center
description: More than four million Americans work in call centers answering the phones for companies that pay them to take reservations, resolve billing issues, provide product information, take orders, and provide technical support. It is estimated that 112,000 of these agents work from home-based workstations. This renewal grant will provide partial support to the National Telecommuting Institute, Inc., as it continues to develop strategies to create call center jobs for homebound individuals with disabilities.
