title: Virtual Call Center
description: Over four million Americans work in call centers answering telephones for companies that pay them to take reservations, resolve billing issues, provide product information, take orders, and provide technical support. As of January 2006, an estimated 112,000 of these agents worked from home-based workstations. This grant will provide partial support to the National Telecommuting Institute, Inc., as it continues to develop strategies to create call-center jobs for homebound individuals with disabilities.

title: Older Adult Services
description: This grant will provide gap funding for Jewish Community Services to continue to provide senior nutrition and transportation services until the Senior Services millage passed in Genesee County is implemented. As the community’s population ages, requests for nutrition and transportation assistance continue to increase. At the same time, federal, state and local funding for senior programs has decreased steadily over the past few years. Foundation support will partially cover the costs of Jewish Community Services’ senior nutrition and local transportation programs. Funding through the Senior Services millage will likely become available in 2007.

title: Stone Street/Manhattan Place Project
description: This grant will provide partial funding for the development of 14 homeownership opportunities in the Flint Carriage Town Neighborhood. The project will include nine units of new construction and five rehabilitated structures. Development activities will take place on 20 contiguous parcels of property that were assembled by the Genesee County Land Bank Authority’s foreclosure process and others that were donated by the Carriage Town Historic Neighborhood Association.

title: Workforce Project for Young Veterans
description: AMVETS National Service Foundation has served the needs of American veterans as a volunteer-led, nonpartisan organization since 1947. A 2006 symposium on the needs of young veterans highlighted a series of critical issues facing approximately six million young veterans, including the needs of the veterans returning from operations in Iraq and Afghanistan. This renewal grant will provide partial support for the grantee to continue to implement an action plan to address the employment and workforce development needs of young veterans.

title: Workforce Project for Young Veterans
description: AMVETS National Service Foundation has served the needs of American veterans as a volunteer-led, nonpartisan organization since 1947. A recent symposium on the needs of young veterans highlighted a series of critical issues facing approximately six million young veterans, including the needs of the veterans returning from operations in Iraq and Afghanistan. This grant will provide partial support for AMVETS National Service Foundation to implement an action plan to address the employment and workforce development needs of young veterans.

title: State Healthcare Workforce Initiative
description: This grant renewal will enable the New Hampshire Community Loan Fund to continue to provide improved in-home care for New Hampshire’s growing elderly population by improving the wages and benefits of direct care workers. The grant should result in new programs and practices being embedded in the state that improve care for the homebound elderly and the jobs of the direct care providers.

title: State Healthcare Workforce Initiative
description: This grant will enable the New Hampshire Community Loan Fund and Quality Care Partners to engage state policy in providing improved in-home care for New Hampshire’s growing elderly population by improving the wages and benefits accruing to direct-care workers. Subsequently, more women will enter and remain on this career path, thus improving the quality of care for the state’s elderly, home-bound residents.

title: Job Creation Loan Fund
description: The Genesee Chamber Foundation is a supporting organization of the Genesee Regional Chamber of Commerce organized to receive and administer funds for educational and charitable purposes and the public welfare of Genesee County, Michigan. This grant to the Genesee Chamber Foundation will support the launch of a Job Creation Loan Fund, which will help generate employment opportunities for displaced workers in the greater Flint community. Initially, and with certain conditions, the grantee will provide a forgivable, ten-year loan to an organization to be formed for the development of a national customer service center in Flint. The center will provide support to customers of ParkingCarma, a computerized parking guidance service. It is anticipated the center could produce about 150 jobs and enhance the county’s image in economic development circles.

title: Capital Improvements
grantee: American Red Cross — East Central Bay-Michigan Chapter
description: This grant will provide support for capital improvements to the American Red Cross – Genesee-Lapeer Chapter. Created in 1917, the American Red Cross – Genesee-Lapeer Chapter is a humanitarian organization that provides relief to victims of disasters and helps people prevent, prepare for, and respond to emergencies 24 hours a day, 365 days a year. For 90 years, people in the greater Flint community have counted on the local chapter for the lifesaving skills, emergency assistance, and information they need to be safe at home, in school, and in the workplace. Mott Foundation funding will be used for much-needed improvements to the agency’s computer systems and building.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to improve the quality of life in Romanian communities through promoting and developing individual giving, corporate giving, and volunteering. To this end, United Way Romania will improve its organizational policies and procedures, enlarge its pool of long-term volunteers, increase the effectiveness of its fundraising, and improve the quality and impact of the projects it supports. In addition, the grantee will explore the possibility of managing giving campaigns and supporting nonprofit organizations outside Bucharest. United Way Romania was established in 2004. It manages workplace giving campaigns where funds raised from individual workers are matched by their companies. These funds are distributed to nonprofit organizations providing social services in the area of greater Bucharest. In 2007-2008, the grantee raised over $1.9 million and supported 45 projects.

title: General Purposes
description: The goal of United Way Romania is to improve the quality of life in Romanian communities through promoting and developing individual giving, corporate giving, and volunteering. To this end, the grantee will expand its corporate donor support base, increase the effectiveness of its fundraising, enlarge its pool of long-term volunteers, and improve the quality and impact of the projects it supports. In addition, the grantee will use highly skilled volunteers to increase the capacity of its staff in Bucharest, Timisoara, and Cluj. United Way Romania was established in 2004. It runs workplace giving campaigns where funds raised from individual workers are matched by their companies. These funds are distributed to nonprofit organizations providing social services in the area of greater Bucharest. In 2009-2010, despite the economic crisis, the grantee raised over $1.2 million through payroll giving and supported 67 projects.

title: Planning a Southern Sector Initiative
grantee: Insight Center for Community Economic Development
description: This grant will support technical assistance from the Insight Center for Community Economic Development through its project, the National Network of Sector Partners. This national trade association for sectoral employment practitioners will develop and implement a southern sectoral employment initiative. Sectoral employment development aims to help low-income workers find, keep, and advance in good-paying jobs, while also improving the regional economy by addressing labor-market needs in targeted industry sectors. This initiative will be geared toward expanding support for sector initiatives in the South and creating upward mobility for low-wage, low-skilled workers.

title: Gulf Coast Alternative Staffing Project
description: Nearly three years after Hurricanes Katrina and Rita devastated Louisiana’s Gulf Coast, the region is still trying to recover from the disaster. Despite a low unemployment rate, there are approximately 750,000 people who are employable, but are unable to find work. Alternative staffing organizations, which are temporary staffing firms owned and operated by community-based agencies, have the potential to bridge the gap between the needs of employers and employees. This renewal grant to Public/Private Ventures will support the continued development of two or three alternative staffing organizations serving the New Orleans area.

title: Gulf Coast Alternative Staffing Project
description: Over the past two years, Public/Private Ventures has managed an effort to launch three alternative staffing organizations in Louisiana’s Gulf Coast region, an area that is still recovering from the aftereffects of Hurricanes Katrina and Rita. Alternative staffing organizations, which are temporary staffing firms owned and operated by community-based agencies, have the potential to bridge the gap between the needs of employers and employees. With this grant increase, Public/Private Ventures will continue to support, manage, and evaluate the implementation of the three alternative staffing projects.

title: Gulf Coast Alternative Staffing Project
description: Over the past three years, Public/Private Ventures has managed an effort to launch three alternative staffing organizations in Louisiana’s Gulf Coast region, an area that is still recovering from the aftereffects of hurricanes Katrina and Rita. Alternative staffing organizations, which are temporary staffing firms owned and operated by community-based agencies, have the potential to bridge the gap between the needs of employers and employees. With this renewal grant, the grantee will continue to support, manage, and evaluate the implementation of the three alternative staffing projects.

title: Gulf Coast Alternative Staffing Project
description: Over the past three years, Public/Private Ventures has managed an effort to launch three alternative staffing organizations in Louisiana’s Gulf Coast region. Alternative staffing organizations are temporary staffing firms owned and operated by community-based agencies that bridge the gap between the needs of hard-to-employ individuals and employers. With this renewal grant, the grantee will continue to support and evaluate the implementation of three alternative staffing projects while developing and publishing two reports that outline the scope of the work done by alternative staffing organizations, the services they provide, and how they can complement other workforce development services in the communities they serve to help advance the field. The grantee will also provide pre-launch support for a potential alternative staffing organization in Flint, Michigan being developed by Goodwill Industries of Mid-Michigan.

title: Gulf Coast Alternative Staffing Project
description: The Southwest Center for Economic Integrity will continue to manage an effort to launch and sustain three alternative staffing organizations in Louisiana’s Gulf Coast region. Alternative staffing organizations are temporary staffing firms owned and operated by community-based agencies that bridge the gap between the needs of hard-to-employ individuals and employers. With this final renewal grant, the grantee will support and evaluate the implementation of three alternative staffing projects while developing and publishing two reports that outline the scope of the work done by alternative staffing organizations, the services they provide, and how they can complement other workforce development services in the communities they serve to help advance the field.

title: Gulf Coast Alternative Staffing Project
description: This grant to Public/Private Ventures will support the research, planning, and implementation of alternative staffing programs in New Orleans, Louisiana and in Gulfport, Mississippi. The Congressional Budget Office estimates that Hurricane Katrina has resulted in the loss of more than 400,000 jobs across the Gulf Coast region. Additionally, many of the new reconstruction jobs are being staffed by day-labor brokers. Alternative staffing programs, which are temporary staffing companies owned and operated by community-based agencies, will connect residents to employment and help ensure that workers receive the compensation and protections they are entitled to under the law.

title: First Jobs Program
description: This grant will provide partial support to develop an alternative staffing strategy for the working poor and ex-offenders in the Bronx. Through a workforce development approach called Managed Work Services, VIP Community Services uses a temporary-to-permanent approach for hard-to-place jobseekers. The model embodies best practices in engaging unemployed or underemployed individuals, while also providing a solid business solution for employers.

title: First Jobs Program
description: This grant will provide funds for a pilot project that will provide employment and promote career development for youth aging out of the foster care system. VIP Community Services is implementing a summer pilot of the First Jobs Program, developed by Managed Work Services of Portland, Maine. The program utilizes an alternative staffing employment model coupled with counseling and case management to help youth transition from the foster care system to independence.

title: Great Lakes Ecosystem Project
description: The Ohio Environmental Council, a leading statewide organization, works to protect and restore Lake Erie and its tributaries by engaging the public and policymakers in freshwater ecosystem conservation. The council provides scientific and technical expertise on the Clean Water Act and related water policies, mentoring and leadership to local and regional organizations, and policy expertise on Lake Erie pollution and restoration issues. With continued Mott support, the council will promote new funding for Lake Erie restoration, seek strong implementation of the Great Lakes Compact, expand its partnerships, and build its organizational capacity.

title: Great Lakes Ecosystem Project
description: The Ohio Environmental Council leads statewide efforts to protect and restore Lake Erie and its tributaries by providing information and technical assistance to citizens, nonprofits, and decisionmakers. With prior Mott support, the council provided members, partners, and policymakers with expertise on implementing the Clean Water Act and related policies; capacity building assistance for nonprofits; and policy, legal, and scientific information on issues related to Lake Erie pollution and water withdrawals. With this renewal, the council will continue these efforts while also seeking strong implementation of the Great Lakes Compact, informing stormwater management policies and regulations, engaging in statewide and regional efforts to prevent invasive species, and investing in its own organizational capacity.

title: Great Lakes Ecosystem Project
description: The Ohio Environmental Council, a statewide environmental organization, leads efforts to protect and restore Lake Erie waterways. The grantee provides information and technical assistance to citizens, nonprofits, and decisionmakers. With prior Mott support, the grantee sought to implement the Great Lakes Compact, helped improve stormwater management policies, engaged in statewide and regional efforts to prevent invasive species, and invested in its own organizational capacity. With this renewal, the grantee will continue these efforts and explore new ways to build the capacity of watershed groups working in the Lake Erie ecosystem.

title: Great Lakes Ecosystem Project
description: The Ohio Environmental Council, a statewide environmental organization, leads efforts to protect and restore the Lake Erie ecosystem. The grantee provides scientific, legal, and policy analyses and technical assistance to citizens, nonprofits, and decisionmakers. With prior Mott support, the grantee helped Ohio implement the Great Lakes Compact, engaged in statewide and regional efforts to prevent invasive species, and invested in its own organizational capacity. With this renewal, the grantee will continue these efforts while also focusing on reducing pollutants into Lake Erie waterways.

title: Great Lakes Ecosystem Project
description: The Ohio Environmental Council, a statewide environmental organization, leads efforts to protect and restore Lake Erie. With prior Mott support, the grantee informed freshwater policy reforms in Ohio and took steps to build its own organizational capacity. This grant increase will help the grantee through a leadership transition and will offset costs for a conference that will build the skills of senior staff of Great Lakes environmental groups.

title: Great Lakes Ecosystem Project
description: The Ohio Environmental Council is a statewide environmental organization that leads efforts to protect and restore Lake Erie and its tributaries. The grantee provides scientific, legal, and policy analyses and technical assistance to citizens, nonprofits, and decisionmakers. With prior Mott support, the grantee helped implement the Great Lakes Compact, prevent invasive species, and address toxic algal blooms in Lake Erie. With renewed support, the grantee will continue these programmatic efforts, launch a new five-year strategic plan, and invest in staff trainings and leadership development opportunities.

title: Great Lakes Ecosystem Project
description: The Ohio Environmental Council is a statewide environmental organization that leads efforts to protect and restore Lake Erie and its tributaries. The grantee provides scientific, legal, and policy analyses and technical assistance to citizens, nonprofits, and decision makers. With prior Mott support, the grantee has helped implement the Great Lakes Compact, prevent invasive species, and address toxic algal blooms in Lake Erie while also addressing its own organizational development needs. With renewed Mott support, the grantee will continue these efforts, with an increased focus on integrated water management and development of local leadership capacity.

title: Great Lakes Ecosystem Project
description: Several policy reform opportunities, including the possible adoption of the Great Lakes Compact and the push for new ecosystem restoration funding, have converged to address many of the threats faced by Lake Erie and its tributaries. The Ohio Environmental Council, a premier statewide organization with a long history of work in the Lake Erie basin, will help lead the environmental community’s response to such reform opportunities. The council will also build its own organizational capacity so that it can sustain its long-term commitment to environmental protection in the Lake Erie basin and statewide.

title: Institutional Development
description: The project goal is to enlarge and strengthen the membership base of the Russia Donors Forum in order to establish long-term sustainability of the organization. This grant will support its efforts to make membership development more strategic and systematic. At the same time, by providing more targeted services and engaging members more actively in the forum’s work, the project will seek to strengthen professional capacity within Russia’s philanthropic community. The Russia Donors Forum has successfully increased its membership and represented member interests since it was officially established in 2002, reflecting the growing importance of indigenous philanthropy in Russia. The grantee promotes the development of democratic civil society in Russia by enhancing the effectiveness of organized grantmaking through networking, information sharing, and collaborative initiatives among active grantmakers.

title: Land Lease of the Mott Block
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will provide a 50-year land lease to the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation to facilitate the redevelopment of several buildings in a critical block on the east side of South Saginaw Street in downtown Flint. The vacant and unused buildings between the Mott Foundation Building and Second Street will be redeveloped through a public-private partnership for office, retail, and residential loft purposes. The Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation will make the land available to its supported organization, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, which intends to redevelop the leased parcels.

title: Great Lakes Compact Strategic Communications
geographic_focus: Minnesota, Illinois, Ohio, Wisconsin, Michigan, Pennsylvania, Indiana, New York
description: The Great Lakes Compact, a proposed interstate compact that would govern water withdrawals and diversions throughout the portion of the basin in the United States, is now under serious consideration in most of the Great Lakes states. State-level and local conservation organizations will be engaged in the associated policy discussions. With this grant, the State Environmental Leadership Program, a national organization that supports groups working at the state level, will provide technical assistance to the environmental community in the Great Lakes states on how to effectively communicate with the public about the compact. Project activities will include message development, a regional meeting of communication professionals, training workshops in selected states, and individualized consulting. On-line resources will also be made available.

title: Black Sea Trust for Regional Cooperation
grantee: German Marshall Fund of the United States
geographic_focus: Georgia, Russia, Azerbaijan, Russia, Armenia, Moldova, Ukraine, Bulgaria, Turkey, Romania
description: The project goal is to: (1) support democratic governance and strengthen democratic political institutions in Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bulgaria, Georgia, Moldova, Romania, Turkey, Ukraine, and parts of Russia; and (2) advance cross-border cooperation in this region with the aim of promoting political, social, and economic development necessary to ensure long-term stability. To achieve these goals, the German Marshall Fund of the United States created a grantmaking fund called the Black Sea Trust for Regional Cooperation, which operates as a project of the grantee through an office and small staff in Bucharest, Romania. Launched officially in the fall of 2007, the trust hired an executive director, established its office in Bucharest, and identified and convened an international advisory board. The trust made its first grant in December. Beginning with 2008, the trust anticipates an average grantmaking budget of $2 million per year. The trust is supported by the grantee, the United States Agency for International Development, the Latvian and Romanian governments, and the Mott Foundation, with the goal of attracting other donors to the trust over time.

title: Ambassador City Summit
description: This grant will provide partial support for Metro Housing Partnership to join with the Flint Area Association of Realtors to host the Ambassador City Summit. The summit will address critical issues affecting the real estate market and homeownership in Flint and Genesee County, and includes the participation of the real estate community, banks, nonprofit housing and neighborhood agencies, and local units of government. Further, this grant will support Metro Housing Partnership’s efforts to develop a comprehensive housing plan for Flint and Genesee County.

title: Technical Assistance for Downtown Flint Revitalization
description: New efforts for cooperation and collaboration have fueled the recent integration of the Flint Area Chamber of Commerce, Genesee Area Focus Council, Metropolitan Chamber of Commerce, and the Flint-Genesee Economic Growth Alliance into one entity, the Genesee Regional Chamber of Commerce. Through its support organization, the Genesee Area Focus Fund, efforts to revitalize the community and its economy are continuing. This grant will allow the Genesee Area Focus Fund to provide a loaned staff member to the nonprofit Uptown Reinvestment Corporation for work on its charitable efforts to revitalize downtown Flint.

title: Technical Assistance for Downtown Flint Revitalization
description: New efforts for cooperation and collaboration have fueled the recent integration of the Flint Area Chamber of Commerce, Genesee Area Focus Council, Metropolitan Chamber of Commerce and the Flint-Genesee Economic Growth Alliance into one entity, the Genesee Regional Chamber of Commerce. Through its support organization, the Genesee Chamber Foundation, efforts to revitalize the community and its economy are continuing. This grant will enable the Genesee Chamber Foundation to provide a loaned executive to the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation to work on its charitable efforts to revitalize downtown Flint.

title: Mid-Michigan Innovation Team Learning Communities Initiative
description: The purpose of this grant is to ensure the continuation of the work done by the Mid-Michigan Innovation Team Learning Communities Initiative after federal funding through the Mid-Michigan Workforce Innovation in Regional Economic Development initiative ends. During the grant period, the Prima Civitas Foundation will continue to manage the Mid-Michigan Innovation Team, which will continue its work of regional collaboration and development by creating the final Mid-Michigan Workforce Innovation in Regional Economic Development activity reports; establish four focuses aimed at regional development and sustainability, leadership and strategy, research and technology, and communication and engagement; and begin work on two statewide initiatives focused on talent and innovation.

title: Mid-Michigan Innovation Team Learning Communities Initiative
description: The purpose of this grant to Prima Civitas Foundation is to build learning communities throughout the mid-Michigan region in advanced manufacturing, alternative energy, entrepreneurship, healthcare, and construction. The establishment of coherent learning communities for these sectors will strengthen connections among stakeholders from across the region, enhance information sharing, and spark strategic discussion on industry challenges and opportunities. The result should be integrated strategies in the economic sectors that accelerate change and innovation.

title: Demonstrating Scale in Domestic Microenterprise
description: The Scale Academy, a project of the Aspen Institute, provides technical assistance and peer-learning activities to eight microenterprise organizations with potential to achieve greater scale in service delivery. By the end of this grant, these eight organizations will realize a marked increase in the number of clients served and/or loans made. Up to 30 additional organizations will have increased their capacity to achieve scale through participating in short-term programs of training and technical assistance directed at critical skills. Finally, another 100 to 150 organizations will be assisted through in-person and online training at training institutes, conferences, and through MicroPro, the Association for Enterprise Opportunity’s new web resource.

title: Demonstrating Scale in Domestic Microenterprise
description: This grant to the Aspen Institute will provide partial funding for third-year activities designed to both provide continuing grants to the grantees, and increase peer learning and technical assistance opportunities. In addition, the grantee will collect MicroTest data recording the performance of the grantees with respect to scale, efficiency, targeting, and costs, and will continue to document this demonstration’s accomplishments. The grantee will also organize dissemination activities in conjunction with the Association for Enterprise Opportunity’s annual conference, and potentially other venues as well.

title: Demonstrating Scale in Domestic Microenterprise
description: This renewal grant to Aspen Institute provides partial funding for fourth-year activities designed to provide final tie-off grants to the subgrantees, offer more peer-learning and technical assistance opportunities for all Scale Academy members, and complete the documentation of learning from this first round of the Scale Academy. The Association for Enterprise Opportunity will organize dissemination activities in association with its annual conference and potentially other venues as well.

title: Demonstrating Scale in Domestic Microenterprise
description: This renewal grant to the Aspen Institute provides partial funding for the Scale Academy for Microenterprise Development. The academy is an initiative designed to provide funding, peer learning, and technical assistance to high performing microenterprise development organizations committed to scaling up their operations to serve more aspiring entrepreneurs. Through participation in the academy, member organizations are expected to strengthen their capacities, achieve a marked increase in the number of clients served and/or loans made, and work together to advance each other’s progress.

title: Demonstrating Scale in Domestic Microenterprise
description: This renewal grant to the Aspen Institute provides partial funding for the Scale Academy for Microenterprise Development. The academy is an initiative designed to provide funding, peer learning, and technical assistance to high performing microenterprise development organizations committed to scaling up their operations to serve more aspiring entrepreneurs. Through participation in the academy, member organizations are expected to strengthen their capacities, achieve a marked increase in the number of clients served and/or loans made, and work together to advance each other’s progress.

Through participation in the academy, member organizations are expected to strengthen their capacities, achieve a marked increase in the number of clients served and/or loans made, and work together to advance each other’s progress.

title: Demonstrating Scale in Domestic Microenterprise
description: This renewal grant to the Aspen Institute provides partial funding for the Scale Academy for Microenterprise Development. The academy is an initiative designed to provide funding, peer learning, and technical assistance to high performing microenterprise development organizations committed to scaling up their operations to serve more aspiring entrepreneurs. Through participation in the academy, member organizations are expected to strengthen their capacities, achieve a marked increase in the number of clients served and/or loans made, and work together to advance each other’s progress.

title: Demonstrating Scale in Domestic Microenterprise
description: This grant will provide funding for the Aspen Institute to launch a four year demonstration project aimed at increasing the number of low-income entrepreneurs served by the U.S. microenterprise industry. The challenge of reaching larger numbers of microentrepreneurs is a long-standing issue in the U.S. microenterprise field, with its 500 programs currently serving less than a million individuals annually. During the start-up year of the demonstration, eight participants with potential to achieve greater scale in service delivery will be selected to receive financial support, technical assistance, and peer learning opportunities. The participants will explore promising scale-up strategies and help to develop the technical assistance and training services needed to assist additional microenterprise programs.

title: Public Awareness Campaign Planning
description: This grant will allow the Association for Enterprise Opportunity to develop a multimedia campaign that will raise awareness about the impact of microenterprise development in the United States. Although it is regaining momentum, the domestic microenterprise industry must create language and messages that better convey the field’s economic development purposes, target markets and outcomes to practitioners, funders, and policymakers. Funding will allow the Association for Enterprise Opportunity, the national trade association for microenterprise practitioners, to outline the parameters of this work, which will include: conducting market research, creating a brand, developing an internal and external communications strategy, and monitoring and evaluating the implementation of these activities.

title: Kearsley Street Connection Study
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: In its redevelopment strategy for downtown Flint, Sasaki Associates, Inc., recommended the reopening of Kearsley Street through the University of Michigan-Flint campus. The closed street is currently a complicating factor in transit between the Flint Cultural Center campus and downtown Flint. This grant will allow the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation to work collaboratively with the University of Michigan-Flint to study the feasibility of reopening Kearsley Street to reconnect downtown Flint and the Cultural Center.

title: Tällberg Online
description: This grant will provide partial support for the development and deployment of an online community by the Tällberg Foundation. The purpose of Tällberg Online is to provide the existing worldwide Tällberg network with the opportunity to continue to extend conversations begun at the annual forum, facilitate ongoing contact with the various projects under way throughout the network, as well as foster and track new ideas and efforts through online discussions and virtual forums. The Web site was launched prior to the Tällberg Forum in late June 2007 and will be enhanced over the next two years. The Tällberg Foundation, established in 1981, aims to help leaders grow as human beings and act with purpose when managing the challenges of global interdependence.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Federation of Congregations United to Serve
description: Federation of Congregations United to Serve operates as both a local community organization in Orlando, Florida and as a network for other community organizations in Florida and Alabama affiliated with PICO National Network. These organizations are working effectively to build positive relationships between individuals and institutions to help solve problems associated with poverty and social isolation. General purpose funding will support the growth and development of this statewide network.

title: General Purposes
description: The South African Institute for Advancement, also known as Inyathelo, was established in 2002 to promote philanthropy, leadership development, and resource development for the nonprofit sector in South Africa. Recent activities include facilitating workshops and training programs on fundraising for nonprofits, convening and mentoring donors, developing and distributing informational materials for donors and nonprofits, and introducing youth philanthropy activities. Future activities will focus on the philanthropic sector and nonprofit sustainability. Inyathelo will continue to expand its training programs to Gauteng and KwaZulu-Natal provinces and will conduct 54 workshops, symposia, retreats, and other events in 2009 for the donor community and the nonprofit sector.

title: General Purposes
description: The South African Institute for Advancement, also known as Inyathelo, was established in 2002 to promote philanthropy, leadership development, and resource development for the nonprofit sector in South Africa. Recent activities include facilitating workshops and training programs on fundraising for nonprofits, convening and mentoring donors, developing and distributing materials for donors and nonprofits, and introducing youth philanthropy activities. Inyathelo will host a donor conference to promote discussions between grantmakers operating in South Africa on challenges and experiences with grantmaking. The conference is aimed at building effective and impactful philanthropy.

title: General Purposes
description: The South African Institute for Advancement, also known as Inyathelo, was established to promote philanthropy and to develop leadership capacity in the South African nonprofit sector. Mott has provided general purpose support to the grantee to implement various programs including training on fundraising for nonprofits; convening and mentoring donors on appropriate ways of giving; developing and distributing information for donors and nonprofits; and hosting the philanthropy awards, which have become a major event in the philanthropy circles in South Africa. The grantee also hosted a donors’ conference in 2010 that brought together South African and international donors for the first time to share experiences and seek ways to collaborate in supporting social development initiatives. This grant will support the grantee to deepen its training for nonprofits; expand its resource centre; and offer an advisory service to support nonprofit leaders to develop viable sustainability strategies for their organizations.

title: General Purposes
description: The South African Institute for Advancement, also known as Inyathelo, was established to promote a culture of philanthropy and develop a strong and stable civil society sector in South Africa. While working with organizations to develop their ability and attract support, the grantee promotes social responsibility, personal philanthropy, volunteerism, and self-reliance. Mott has provided general purpose support to the grantee to implement various activities including training on fundraising and capacity development, providing resources and information for nonprofits, promoting corporate and individual social giving through dialogues, hosting the philanthropy awards, and convening the Private Philanthropy Circle, a network of local foundations and trusts aimed at sharing grantmaking experiences. This general purpose grant increase will support costs associated with the Private Philanthropy Circle.

title: General Purposes
description: The South African Institute for Advancement, also known as Inyathelo, was founded to promote philanthropy, leadership development, and fundraising for the nonprofit sector in South Africa. Mott previously made grants to it to provide leadership training and mentoring for women leaders in the nonprofit sector and to establish a peer learning cooperative for leaders of community foundations and small to intermediate local grantmakers. This grant will provide institutional support to Inyathelo for its own programs and activities. Particular emphasis will be placed on developing an endowment for the organization to ensure its long-term sustainability and supporting its work aimed at unlocking local resources for development and poverty eradication and assisting nonprofits to develop a more professional approach to fundraising.

title: Researching the History of Community Organizing
description: The purpose of this project is to create a historical record and a system for documenting the history of community organizing in the United States. Through research and interviews, the Center for Community Change will collect and organize data and stories, publish the results, and also post the results on the Internet for use by other researchers and writers.

title: Fourth of July Riverbank Park Concert
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant increase will cover the additional costs associated with the Fourth of July weekend concert at Riverbank Park in downtown Flint. Additional transportation and other logistical costs were incurred when the Flint Institute of Music was required to find a substitute nationally recognized group, the Fifth Dimension, to headline the concert following the withdrawal of the previously booked act.

title: Music in the Parks
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide partial support to the Flint Institute of Music for its Music in the Parks concert series. The 2008 free summer concert series will include seven performances at various parks and other locations throughout Genesee County. This year, the series will include two major concerts that will include nationally recognized artists along with the Flint Symphony Orchestra — the annual Riverbank Park concert in downtown Flint as part of the Fourth of July activities and a concert at the Flint Cultural Center during the Buick Club of America’s national meet and General Motors’ 100th Anniversary Celebration in mid-July. The other five concerts will feature local jazz, gospel, and folk groups. Music in the Parks is geared to attract diverse audiences by performing in different locations and offering a variety of music styles.

title: Music in the Parks
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide partial support to the Flint Institute of Music for its Music in the Parks concert series. The 2009 free summer concert series will include four performances at various parks in Flint and Genesee County. This year, the Flint Symphony Orchestra will perform at two concerts, including a downtown concert with the Motown group, The Contours. Concerts featuring gospel music and other local groups will also be held. Music in the Parks attracts a diverse audience by offering residents an opportunity to enjoy a wide variety of live musical performances in different locations throughout the community.

title: Music in the Parks
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant increase will provide partial support to the Flint Institute of Music for its 2010 Music in the Parks summer concert series. The 2010 free summer concert series included four performances at various parks in Flint and Genesee County. The Flint Symphony Orchestra performed at two concerts, including a downtown concert during the Back to the Bricks car cruise that featured the rock ‘n’ roll band, “Flash Cadillac”. The other concerts featured gospel music and an ensemble of female vocalists. Music in the Parks attracts a diverse audience by offering residents an opportunity to enjoy a wide variety of live musical performances in different locations throughout the community.

title: Music in the Parks
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide partial support to the Flint Institute of Music for its 2011 Music in the Parks concert series. The free summer concerts will include four performances at various parks in Flint and Genesee County. The Flint Symphony Orchestra will perform at two concerts, including a downtown concert with Motown artist, Sonny Turner, formerly of the Platters. Other concerts will feature local gospel music groups and a jazz ensemble from Detroit. The overall goal of Music in the Parks is to enrich the lives of people in Flint and Genesee County by offering residents an opportunity to enjoy a wide variety of live musical performances in different locations throughout the community.

The Flint Symphony Orchestra will perform at two concerts, including the downtown Flint concert, which will be held in conjunction with the annual Back to the Bricks car event. The overall goal of Music in the Parks is to enrich the lives of people in Flint and Genesee County by offering residents an opportunity to enjoy a wide variety of live musical performances in different locations throughout the community.

description: This grant will provide partial support to Flint Institute of Music’s 2013 Music in the Parks concert series. This summer’s series will expand to five concerts held at sites throughout Genesee County between July and September of 2013. The Flint Symphony Orchestra will perform at two concerts, including the downtown Flint concert, which will be held in conjunction with the annual Back to the Bricks car event. The overall goal of Music in the Parks is to enrich the lives of people in Flint and Genesee County by offering all residents an opportunity to enjoy a wide variety of live musical performances at these free summer concerts held throughout the community.
