title: Music in the Parks
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide partial support to the Flint Institute of Music’s 2015 Music in the Parks concert series. This summer’s series will include six concerts held at sites throughout Genesee County between June and September 2015. The Flint Symphony Orchestra will perform at two concerts, including the downtown Flint concert, which will be held in June with a Flag Day theme. The overall goal of Music in the Parks is to enrich the lives of people in Flint and Genesee County by offering all residents an opportunity to enjoy a wide variety of live musical performances at free summer concerts held throughout the community.

title: Music in the Parks
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant provides partial support to the Flint Institute of Music’s 2016 Music in the Parks concert series. This summer’s series will include four concerts held at sites throughout Genesee County between June and August 2016. The Flint Symphony Orchestra will perform two concerts, including a downtown Flint concert, which will be held following the Crim Festival of Races’ Michigan Mile. Additional Music in the Parks concerts will take place at Crossroads Village, Mott Park, and Max Brandon Park. The overall goal of Music in the Parks is to enrich the lives of people in Flint and Genesee County by offering all residents an opportunity to enjoy a wide variety of live musical performances at these free summer concerts held throughout the community.

title: Music Around Town
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Music Around Town series is the next chapter in the broad community partnership formerly known as Music in the Parks. Since 1991, the Flint Institute of Music has worked to provide a variety of musical offerings in the community to better meet the needs of residents. This year’s Music Around Town program will offer seven concerts in collaboration with Flint area institutions in various high profile locations including Applewood Estate, Max Brandon Park, and downtown Flint. In addition to the traditional series, this year will kick off the May the Fourth Be With You 4th of July celebration which will feature the Flint Symphony Orchestra performing movie scores in coordination with the fireworks display.

title: Music Around Town
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Music Around Town series, formerly known as Music in the Parks, is the next chapter in the broad community partnership led by the Flint Institute of Music. Since 1991 the Flint Institute of Music has worked to provide a variety of musical offerings in the community to better meet the needs of residents. This year’s Music Around Town program will expand beyond six summer concerts to include eleven concerts throughout the year. The program is offered in collaboration with Flint area institutions in various high-profile locations including the Crim Festival of Races starting line in downtown Flint, Max Brandon Park, and Longway Planetarium.

title: Music Around Town
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Music Around Town series, formerly known as Music in the Parks, is the next chapter in the broad community partnership led by the Flint Institute of Music. Since 1991 the grantee has worked to provide a variety of musical offerings in the community to better meet the needs of residents. This year’s Music Around Town program will include eight concerts throughout the year. The program is offered in collaboration with Flint area institutions in various high-profile locations including the Crim Festival of Races starting line in downtown Flint, Atwood Stadium, and Longway Planetarium.

title: Fourth of July Riverbank Park Concert
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide funding for the Flint Institute of Music’s Fourth of July Riverbank Park concert. As part of the institute’s Music in the Parks series, the concert will be part of the July 4th festival that will take place in downtown Flint. The event attracts thousands to downtown Flint, which helps showcase revitalization efforts under way downtown. Building on the institute’s focus to diversify its programming, this year’s concert will feature a nationally known minority artist in addition to the Flint Symphony Orchestra, which should help attract an even larger, more diverse audience to downtown.

title: Action Research Project: Sustainable Public Space Management in Croatia
description: The project goal is to encourage constructive public participation in policy development and community decisionmaking in Croatia. To this end, the project will focus on the timely and critical issue of public space management at local levels in Croatia. The Multimedia Institute will work closely with other leading Croatian nongovernmental organizations and experts to assess current participatory planning practices in Croatia; link local government officials, civic leaders, and experts with an interest in this field; highlight the importance of participatory approaches to better outcomes; and promote best practices in public space management through a demonstration project in Zagreb. Through these activities, the project will generate user friendly, Web-based resources and initiate an informal network of experts and practitioners. Based in Zagreb, the Multimedia Institute’s programming combines the use of cutting edge information and communication technology with social activism, particularly among young people.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen women’s participation in community development initiatives and in local- and national-level decisionmaking. To this end, this grant supports the organizational and programmatic development of the Kosova Women’s Network, a network of Kosovar women’s nongovernmental organizations. The network supports its members through advocacy, networking activities, capacity-building opportunities, and joint campaigns. With 88 member organizations from all of Kosovo’s ethnic communities, in 2008-2009, the network raised public awareness about the need for public financing of women’s shelters and women’s participation in political life, conducted research to inform relevant public policy debates, and provided development and technical assistance to network members. During the grant period, the network will focus on empowering women to participate in politics and decisionmaking processes, promoting compliance with a code of conduct for members, and increasing cooperation between Albanian and Serb women’s organizations.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen women’s participation in community development initiatives and in local- and national-level decisionmaking. To this end, this grant supports the organizational and programmatic development of the Kosova Women’s Network, a network of women’s nongovernmental organizations. The grantee supports its members through opportunities for exchange, capacity building, and joint campaigns. With more than 80 members from all of Kosovo’s ethnic communities, the grantee is instrumental in promoting and protecting the rights of women and girls in Kosovo. In 2010-2011, the grantee raised public awareness about gender equality mechanisms in Kosovo, undertook two citizen-led advocacy campaigns, and provided development and technical assistance to network members. During the grant period, the grantee will focus on empowering women to participate in politics and decisionmaking processes at municipal and national levels, engaging in advocacy and awareness-raising campaigns on key issues facing women, and building the capacity of the network and its members to work effectively at local levels and engage in joint projects nationally. Kosova Women’s Network was established in 2000 and is based in Pristina.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen women’s participation in community development initiatives and in local- and national-level decisionmaking. To this end, this grant supports the organizational and programmatic development of the Kosova Women’s Network, a network of more than 70 women’s nongovernmental organizations. The grantee supports its members through opportunities for exchange, capacity building, and joint campaigns. In 2012-2013, the grantee raised public awareness about gender equality mechanisms in Kosovo, provided development and technical assistance to network members, increased its staff, and diversified its funding base. The grantee also established a separate Kosovo Women’s Fund that provides small grants to community-based initiatives. During the grant period, the grantee will continue its core work on empowering women to participate in politics and decisionmaking processes at municipal and national levels and building the capacity of the grantee and its members to work effectively at local levels and engage in joint projects nationally. The grantee was established in 2000 and is based in Pristina.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen women’s participation in community development initiatives and in local- and national-level decisionmaking. To this end, this grant supports the organizational and programmatic development of the Kosova Women’s Network, a network of Kosovar women’s nongovernmental organizations. The network supports its members through advocacy, networking activities, capacity-building opportunities, and joint campaigns. In 2008-2009, the network will focus on empowering women to participate in politics and decisionmaking processes, preventing trafficking of women and girls and assisting victims of trafficking, improving access to and the quality of women’s healthcare, and strengthening member organizations’ capacities. Based in Pristina, the network has 81 members located throughout Kosovo and representing all ethnic groups.

title: Confronting the Past in Serbia
description: The project goal is to build support within Serbian society for constructive efforts to deal with the legacies of Serbia’s involvement in the wars of the 1990s in the former Yugoslavia. With a focus on women activists and local women’s groups as catalysts of change in this process, during 2007-2009, Women in Black carried out a number of interrelated activities designed to engage women in transitional justice, including organizing visits to memorials and commemorations of war crimes and providing transitional justice training to more than 300 women in its network. In 2009-2011, the grantee will continue these activities and monitor war crimes trials and increase the use of theater, art, and film to raise public awareness of gender perspectives in transitional justice issues. Based in Belgrade, Serbia, Women in Black was established in 1991 as a network of women activists who opposed the wars in the former Yugoslavia.

title: Confronting the Past in Serbia
description: The project goal is to build support in Serbia and the Balkan region for constructive efforts to deal with the legacies of the wars of the 1990s in the former Yugoslavia. With a focus on women activists and local women’s groups as catalysts of change in this process, during 2009-2011, Women in Black carried out a number of interrelated activities designed to engage women in transitional justice, including organizing visits to memorials and commemorations of war crimes sites, monitoring and raising public awareness of war crimes trials, and providing training and support to women activists across Serbia. In 2011-2013, the grantee will continue these activities and focus on providing a diverse range of educational and awareness-raising activities in order to reach a broader audience. The grantee will also expand its cooperation with women activists in Bosnia, Croatia, Montenegro, and Kosovo. Based in Belgrade, Serbia, Women in Black was established in 1991 as a network of women activists who opposed the wars in the former Yugoslavia.

title: Confronting the Past in Serbia
description: The project goal is to deepen democratic values in Serbia and the Balkan region by strengthening the rule of law, respect for human rights, and civic participation. To this end, Women in Black increases the active role of women in constructive efforts to deal with the legacies of the wars of the 1990s in the former Yugoslavia, bolsters women’s participation in social and political decisionmaking processes, and expands women’s impact on shaping post-conflict society and civil society in Serbia and the wider region. During 2011-2013, the grantee carried out a number of interrelated activities designed to engage women in transitional justice, including organizing visits to memorials and commemorations of war crimes sites, monitoring and raising public awareness of war crimes trials, and providing training and support to women activists across Serbia. In 2013-2015, the grantee will continue these types of activities and focus on providing a diverse range of educational and awareness-raising activities in order to reach a broader audience. The grantee will also expand its cooperation with women activists in Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia, Montenegro, and Kosovo. Based in Belgrade, Serbia, Women in Black was established in 1991 as a network of women activists who opposed the wars in the former Yugoslavia.

title: Confronting the Past in Serbia
description: The project goal is to deepen democratic values in Serbia and the Balkan region by strengthening the rule of law, respect for human rights, and civic participation. To this end, Women in Black increases the active role of women in constructive efforts to deal with the legacies of the wars of the 1990s in the former Yugoslavia, bolsters women’s participation in social and political decisionmaking processes, and expands women’s impact on shaping postconflict society and civil society in Serbia and the wider region. During 2013-2015, activities included organizing visits to memorials and commemorations of war crimes sites; organizing regular educational discussion groups; supporting new community-based women’s groups; using exhibitions, street theater, and public actions to raise awareness; launching a new regional initiative to provide women a platform for publicly stating facts about the crimes committed against them and their consequences; and providing training and support to women activists across Serbia. In 2015-2017, the grantee will continue these types of activities and focus on providing a diverse range of educational and awareness-raising activities in order to reach a broader audience. The grantee will also expand its cooperation with women activists in Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia, Montenegro, and Kosovo. Based in Belgrade, Serbia, Women in Black was established in 1991 as a network of women activists who opposed the wars in the former Yugoslavia.

title: Confronting the Past in Serbia
description: The project goal is to build support within Serbian society for constructive efforts to deal with the legacies of Serbia’s involvement in the wars of the 1990s in the former Yugoslavia. With a focus on women activists and local women’s groups as catalysts of change in this process, Women in Black will conduct trainings, publish reference materials, facilitate trial monitoring, and organize visits to memorials and commemorations in order to engage women in transitional justice initiatives. Based in Belgrade, Serbia, Women in Black was established in 1991 as a network of women activists who opposed the wars in the former Yugoslavia.

title: Global Civil Society and Transitional Justice: Western Balkans Case Study
grantee: London School of Economics and Political Science
description: The project goal is to analyze the role of civil society in advancing both justice and the broader process of democratic transition in countries experiencing transition from war to peace and/or repression to democracy. Researchers at London School of Economics and Political Science will study the scope and characteristics of civil society engagement in transitional justice at local, national, regional, and global levels. The Western Balkans will be used as a case study because civil society there is engaged in transitional justice at multiple levels. This grant supports research in the Western Balkans and a two-day meeting with local and international experts in Belgrade, Serbia. In 2008, the results of this analysis will be published in the flagship annual publication of the school’s Global Civil Society Programme, the Global Civil Society Yearbook.

title: Ralph Bunche Societies National Initiative for Minority Leadership Development
initiative: Historically and Predominantly Black Colleges and Universities
description: This grant will provide renewal support to the Phelps Stokes Fund for the Ralph Bunche Societies. Open to all, but with an emphasis on minority students, the Ralph Bunche Societies are extracurricular undergraduate student associations dedicated to providing exposure, access, and opportunity through a global focus across the curriculum and in career development. Students will increase their global and cultural awareness, develop foreign language skills, and hone their leadership skills. Students will also gain knowledge and insight into the life and legacy of Dr. Ralph Johnson Bunche. Over the next two years, planned activities include organizing leadership conferences, conducting outreach to future host institutions, providing internships and mentoring for students, and awarding fellowships to student leaders. Since its founding in 1911, the Phelps Stokes Fund has facilitated the growth of human development by serving as an incubator to many nationally and internationally known programs, including the Archbishop Tutu Southern African Scholarship Fund and the United Negro College Fund.

title: Ralph Bunche Societies
description: This grant will provide renewal funds to the Phelps Stokes Fund for the Ralph Bunche Societies. Funds will be used to develop and/or strengthen the will and capacity of historically black colleges and universities to globalize the education they provide by offering events and opportunities in international settings. The geographic focus will be in the South, in general, and in North Carolina, in particular. This work will build upon the expanded notion of global leadership via Ralph Bunche and the Ralph Bunche Societies frameworks already in place at other institutions.

title: Ralph Bunche Societies National Initiative for Minority Leadership Development
initiative: Historically and Predominantly Black Colleges and Universities
description: This grant will provide support to the Phelps-Stokes Fund for the establishment of Ralph Bunche Societies at colleges and universities, particularly historically black colleges and universities and other minority-serving institutions. As a trustee at the grantee organization for over 20 years, Dr. Ralph Bunche deeply influenced its goals of human dignity, education, racial harmony, democracy, and peace. The goals of this project include addressing the need for greater minority involvement in the international arena, better preparing minority students to become active participants in the global community, and expanding the academic and career opportunities for students, particularly minorities. The first year of the grant period will focus on establishing the tools and partnerships necessary to launch a pilot Ralph Bunche Society at Winston-Salem State University in North Carolina. In year two and beyond, the grantee will expand the number of societies and host expansion and leadership conferences. Established in 1911 by the will of Caroline Phelps-Stokes, the Phelps-Stokes Fund has facilitated the growth of human development by serving as an incubator to many nationally and internationally known programs and institutions.

title: 50th Anniversary Capital Campaign
description: This grant represents a contribution to the Foundation Center’s 50th Anniversary Capital Campaign. For the past 50 years, the Foundation Center has been the leading organization serving grantseekers, grantmakers, researchers, media, and the public through a broad array of information and education products and services. In 2006, recognizing significant changes in the philanthropic landscape and the need to improve its capacity to take on 21st century challenges, the center launched a four-year, $15 million campaign to build its information, research, nonprofit capacity building, and public outreach services. Campaign funds will also be used to increase the center’s long-term reserves and to create a venture fund that will enable it to respond quickly to unexpected developments.

title: Community Foundation Insights
description: This grant provides startup support to Community Foundation Insights, a project of FSG Social Impact Advisors. The aim of the project is to strengthen the sustainability and leadership of community foundations by collecting, analyzing, benchmarking, and providing online access to financial and operational data from community foundations across the country; identifying and providing “how-to” manuals on best practices; conducting fieldwide research; and providing technical assistance to smaller community foundations. Community Foundation Insights has the full support of the Community Foundation Leadership Team of the Council on Foundations and a total of 22 community foundations of all sizes have committed funds for startup costs. The project subsequently is expected to become financially self-sustaining through modest annual subscription fees.

title: Capacity Building
grantee: Center for Law and Social Policy
description: This grant will provide support to the Center for Law and Social Policy for the external assessment phase of its organizational capacity-building initiative. The Center for Law and Social Policy is a national public policy organization which, for over 30 years, has been consistently among the most effective and highly regarded advocacy organizations in the country through its work on welfare reform, childcare, child support enforcement, and workforce development at both the state and federal levels. An external review will provide the grantee with a better understanding of how the organization is perceived by external stakeholders, including policymakers, funders, and partner organizations, and guide its comprehensive capacity-building process.

title: Capacity Building
grantee: Center for Law and Social Policy
description: This grant will provide support to the Center for Law and Social Policy for the external assessment phase of its organizational capacity building initiative. The Center for Law and Social Policy is a national public policy organization which, for over 30 years, has consistently been among the most effective and highly regarded advocacy organizations in the country, working on welfare reform, childcare, child support enforcement, and workforce development at both the state and federal levels. An external review will provide the Center for Law and Social Policy with a better understanding of how the organization is perceived by external stakeholders, including policymakers, funders, and partner organizations, and guide its comprehensive capacity-building process.

title: Michigan TANF Learning Convening
description: The Corporation for a Skilled Workforce seeks to develop a network for states interested in learning about best practices and evidence-based approaches to successfully move families into employment and out of poverty. The network of officials from six to eight states–including Michigan–will provide an ongoing vehicle for joint problem solving, sharing of innovative ideas, and development of best practices. The grantee will convene the participating officials two to three times annually, while facilitating ongoing communications between in-person meetings through conference calls and electronic means. Corporation for a Skilled Workforce is a national, nonprofit policy and research organization based in Ann Arbor, Michigan.

title: Study of Education Organizing
description: Community organizing has emerged as a powerful force for the reform of public education in low-income communities. Over the past two decades, hundreds of organizing groups have worked to address the improvement of local schools, making significant impacts on improving policy and practice at the school, district, and state levels. While these accomplishments show the potential of the field, only recently are researchers developing a detailed understanding of the mechanisms through which education organizing accomplishes its goals. This research, a project of Harvard University, will build on earlier research, including the Mott-funded eight-site study of community-driven reform, with a focus on examining the processes critical to success or failure in education organizing.

title: Study of Education Organizing
description: Community organizing has emerged as a powerful force for the reform of public education in low-income communities. Over the past two decades, hundreds of organizing groups have worked to address the improvement of local schools, making significant impacts on improving policy and practice at the school, district, and state levels. While these accomplishments show the potential of the field, only recently are researchers developing a detailed understanding of the mechanisms through which education organizing accomplishes its goals. This research project conducted by Harvard University will build on earlier research, including the Mott-funded, eight-site study of community-driven reform, with a focus on examining the processes critical to success or failure in education organizing.

title: Study of Education Organizing
description: Community organizing has emerged as a powerful force for the reform of public education in low-income communities. Over the past 15 years, hundreds of organizing groups have worked to address the improvement of local schools, making significant impacts on improving policy and practice at the school, district, and state levels. While these accomplishments show the potential of the field, there is not yet a detailed understanding of the mechanisms through which education organizing accomplishes its goals. This research, a project of Harvard University will build on earlier research including the Mott-funded eight-site study of community-driven reform with a focus on examining the processes critical to success or failure in education organizing.

title: Expansion of Home Visit Model
grantee: Parent Teacher Home Visit Project Inc.
description: The Parent-Teacher Home Visit Project began as a project of Sacramento Area Congregations Together, an affiliate of PICO National Network. The project proved to be successful, and in 2002, the Parent-Teacher Home Visit Project was separately incorporated in order to facilitate the expansion of the project. Working with local community groups, project staff provided training to parents and teachers for effective home visits. The success led the California State Legislature to appropriate funds for teacher pay and training. Mott funding will support the training of teachers and an expansion of the program to other states.

title: Michigan Breaking Through
description: This grant aims to expand the capacity of Mott Community College to help adults with low literacy and mathematic skills advance into and succeed in college-level professional and technical programs that prepare them for family-supporting jobs. The college will pilot a more efficient pathway from remedial classes to certificate or degree completion in four career areas offered at the school: 1) business management; 2) healthcare; 3) manufacturing; and 4) human services. If the pilot phase proves successful, then Mott Community College will implement these efficiencies in all of their certificate and degree programs.

title: Boston Youth Transitions Taskforce: Supporting City Partnerships to Address the Dropout Crisis
description: This grant will enable the Boston Private Industry Council to continue to convene and support a citywide partnership aimed at addressing and raising the visibility of the dropout crisis. Through this project, the grantee has successfully led and convened the Boston Youth Transitions Taskforce in piloting specific programmatic interventions and advancing a policy agenda that strengthens districtwide efforts and increases resources and supports to improve outcomes for dropouts. During the next stage of this project, the Boston Private Industry Council will deepen its work and begin to identify ways to design, fund, build, and sustain a portfolio of new educational pathways and options that meet the demands and needs of dropouts.

title: Boston Youth Transitions Taskforce: Supporting City Partnerships to Address the Dropout Crisis
description: This grant will enable the Boston Private Industry Council to continue to convene and support a citywide partnership aimed at addressing and raising the visibility of the dropout crisis. Through this project, the grantee has successfully led and convened the Boston Youth Transitions Taskforce in developing programmatic interventions and advancing a policy agenda that strengthens districtwide efforts to improve outcomes for youth dropping out of school. During the next stage of this project, the grantee, in its role as convener of the Boston Youth Transitions Taskforce, will identify ways to design, support, build, and sustain a portfolio of educational pathways and options that meet the demands and needs of dropouts.

title: Boston Youth Transitions Taskforce: Supporting City Partnerships to Address the Dropout Crisis
description: This grant will enable the Boston Private Industry Council to continue to convene and support a citywide partnership aimed at addressing and raising the visibility of the dropout crisis. Through this project, the grantee has been instrumental in advancing a graduation and dropout agenda by convening the Boston Public Schools and 30 youth-serving agencies to develop programmatic interventions and districtwide efforts that improve outcomes for dropouts. Since embarking on this effort, the four-year graduation rate has increased 5.5 percentage points, and the dropout count has decreased by 40 percent. During the final phase of this effort, the grantee will inform local and state policy discussions and support new pilot practices in the area of dropout prevention/recovery.

title: Boston Youth Transitions Taskforce: Supporting City Partnerships to Address the Dropout Crisis
description: This grant will enable the Boston Private Industry Council to continue to convene and support a citywide partnership aimed at addressing and raising the visibility of the dropout crisis. Over the past few years, the grantee has worked to improve the educational options and outcomes for out-of-school and underserved youth through Boston’s participation in the Coalition of Community Foundations for Youth’s Addressing the Dropout Crisis in Our Cities project. Building on the work completed in this earlier project, the grantee will lead and convene the Boston Youth Transitions Taskforce in its implementation of strategies and action plans to strengthen districtwide efforts that improve outcomes for dropouts.

title: Brown and Mendez Dialogues on Multiple Pathways to Graduation
description: This grant will enable the Intercultural Development Research Association to continue its work in building the capacity of African-American and Latino communities in the South and Southwest on key education issues. During the most recent phase of this project, the grantee facilitated a series of cross-race dialogues in Alabama, Louisiana, and Mississippi to create a common discourse between black and Latino stakeholders on increasing access and opportunities to graduation pathways for minority students. In the next phase of this effort, the grantee will leverage and scale up its work nationally via hosting regional convenings and developing Web-based resources that provide a model for cross-race dialogue and action on improving the educational achievement of minority and low-income students.

title: Brown and Mendez Dialogues on Multiple Pathways to Graduation
description: This grant increase will enable the Intercultural Development Research Association to extend its work in building the capacity of African-American and Latino communities in the South on key education issues. Through this project, the Intercultural Development Research Association is assisting black and Latino stakeholders in building a new community context that centers on examining education issues across racial boundaries. With this grant increase, the Intercultural Development Research Association will build on its current efforts to assist partners in the targeted states/communities to connect regionally to discuss strategies and plans for improving the achievement of minority and low-income students.

title: Pathways to Graduation: The Mendez and Brown Project to Expand Pathways to Graduation for African American and Latino Students
description: This grant will enable the Intercultural Development Research Association to continue its work in building the capacity of African-American and Latino communities in the South and Southwest on key education issues. Through this project, the grantee has facilitated a series of cross-race dialogues to help create a common discourse between black and Latino stakeholders on increasing access and opportunities to graduation pathways for minority students. During the final phase of this initiative, the grantee will leverage and expand its work to new states and communities in the targeted regions, as well as nationally to continue to provide a model for cross-race dialogue and action on improving the achievement of minority students.

title: Brown and Mendez Project to Expand Pathways to Graduation for African American and Latino Students
description: This grant will enable the Intercultural Development Research Association to facilitate a series of cross-race dialogues between African-American and Latino communities in the South and Southwest on education issues. The Intercultural Development Research Association is a Texas-based organization committed to strengthening schools that work for all children. Using the school segregation court cases of Brown vs. the Board of Education and Mendez vs. Westminster as the backdrop, the Intercultural Development Research Association will work to create a common discourse on expanding pathways to graduation for minority children. Through this project, the Intercultural Development Research Association will provide a model for cross-race dialogue and action, build a policy agenda and action blueprint on dropout prevention and recovery and improved graduation rates, and cultivate a legacy of shared leadership and accountability for African-American and Latino stakeholders on education issues.

title: General Purposes
description: The Community Training and Assistance Center provides consulting and technical assistance to community-based organizations and institutions throughout the United States. This general purpose grant will support the organization’s ongoing work with communities to provide high quality training, research, evaluation, and policy support services.

title: High School Diploma Completion Initiative
description: This grant will provide continued support to Lansing Community College for its High School Diploma Completion Initiative. Under this initiative, high school dropouts from three area intermediate school districts are provided an opportunity to complete their graduation requirements while simultaneously earning credits toward an associate’s degree and/or various occupational certificate programs. Continued support will allow the grantee to strengthen and expand the model for the purpose of potential replication at other community colleges within Michigan and nationally.

title: High School Diploma Completion Initiative
description: This grant will provide continued support to Lansing Community College for the further development of its High School Diploma Completion Initiative. The initiative offers students who have dropped out of high school a second chance to earn a diploma. Participating students also simultaneously earn credits toward an associate’s degree and/or other occupational certificate programs while completing their high school graduation requirements. A third phase of support will enable Lansing Community College to strengthen and expand this high school-to-college model for potential replication at other community colleges and educational settings within Michigan and nationally.

title: High School Diploma Completion Initiative
description: This grant will provide continued support to Lansing Community College for its High School Diploma Completion Initiative. The initiative provides students who have dropped out of high school between the ages of 16 and 19 with a chance to earn a diploma and credits toward an associate’s degree and/or occupational certificate. Recommended support will enable the grantee to strengthen and enhance this blended high school-to-college model that comprehensively integrates education, career, and employment opportunities for dropouts and students who are at risk of dropping out of high school and need a different educational experience.

title: High School Diploma Completion Initiative
description: This grant will provide continued support to Lansing Community College for its High School Diploma Completion Initiative. The initiative provides students who have dropped out of high school between the ages of 16 and 19 with a chance to simultaneously earn a diploma and credits toward an associate’s degree and/or occupational certificate. Recommended support will enable the grantee to integrate a work-based learning component within this blended high school-to-college model.

title: High School Diploma Completion Initiative
description: This grant will provide tie-off support to Lansing Community College for the High School Diploma Completion Initiative. The initiative provides students who have dropped out of high school with an opportunity to concurrently earn their high school diploma and credits toward an associate’s degree or an occupational certificate. This support will enable the grantee to continue implementing the High School Diploma Completion Initiative and identify additional revenue sources for this work.

title: High School Diploma Completion Initiative
description: This grant will provide partial support to Lansing Community College for the High School Diploma Completion Initiative. The High School Diploma Completion Initiative is an effort between Lansing Community College and three area intermediate school districts to provide students who have dropped out of school with an opportunity to earn a diploma and receive career and technical education training. Under the High School Diploma Completion Initiative, high school dropouts from partnering intermediate districts will complete their graduation requirements while simultaneously earning credits toward an associate’s degree and/or various occupational certificate programs.

title: Opening Career Pathways
description: This grant will provide support to YouthBuild USA for the second year of the Opening Career Pathways project. Through the project, the grantee is aligning education strategies with sectoral workforce preparation strategies to provide students in its network with opportunities to transition into post-secondary education and training opportunities in high-growth and high-demand industries. During the first year of the project, the grantee selected 14 sites serving nearly 800 students across its network to participate in the initiative and to begin testing and developing comprehensive career development strategies. Support in year two of the project will allow the grantee to outline program curriculum needs to properly prepare youth for career ladders in the most promising sectors and coordinate a wide range of supports from within and outside of the network to assist students in connecting to community colleges, training programs, employment associations, and workforce-led efforts.

title: Opening Career Pathways
description: This grant will provide support to YouthBuild USA for the Opening Career Pathways project. Through this project, the grantee is aligning education and sectoral workforce preparation strategies to provide students in its network with opportunities to transition into post-secondary education and training opportunities in high growth, high demand industries. This grant will enable YouthBuild to expand the initiative to more sites/programs; provide technical assistance to participating sites to ensure continued progress in implementing career development strategies; build the capacity and knowledge of participating programs to provide long-term support for graduates; and form partnerships with employers in high demand industry sectors and community colleges.

title: Opening Career Pathways: Developing Sector Strategies to Position Low-Income Youth for Careers in High-Demand Sectors
description: This grant will provide support to YouthBuild USA for the Opening Career Pathways project. In an effort to align education and sectoral workforce preparation strategies, YouthBuild has identified, strengthened, and disseminated effective career development strategies that provide students in its network with access to postsecondary education and economically viable career opportunities. Support will enable the grantee to advance its education and sectoral workforce efforts by working with and deepening partnerships in the construction and healthcare industry sectors, mapping opportunities and potential career ladders in two additional industry sectors, and developing a cadre of sector leaders within the network.

title: Opening Career Pathways: Developing Sector Strategies to Position Low-Income Youth for Careers in High-Demand Sectors
description: This grant will provide support to YouthBuild USA for the Opening Career Pathways project. Through this project, the grantee is aligning education and sectoral workforce strategies to provide students in its network access to advanced opportunities in the construction and healthcare industry. This focused career development effort has allowed the grantee to create articulation agreements with postsecondary institutions, develop certification training pathways, and identify placement and apprenticeship opportunities in the above industries. Recommended support will enable the grantee to deepen and expand its education and sector-based activities in key metropolitan areas and develop a statewide sector strategy, in one to three states, where there is a large presence of YouthBuild programs and/or affiliates.

title: Opening Career Pathways: Developing Sector Strategies to Position Low-Income Youth for Careers in High-Demand Sectors
description: This grant will provide support to YouthBuild USA to continue to align education and sector-based strategies to provide students in its network access to advanced opportunities in high-demand occupations. Through this project, the grantee has worked with 11 affiliate programs in Los Angeles and New York in developing: focused articulation agreements with six community colleges, certification training pathways, and placement and apprenticeship opportunities for students in the construction and healthcare industries. Over the past year, 781 students enrolled in this focused career development effort with 584 completing, 385 earning industry certifications, and 468 moving into entry-level employment and/or further postsecondary opportunities. Recommended support will enable the grantee to deepen and expand its education and sector-based activities to 25 affiliate programs across five regions.

title: Opening Career Pathways: Developing Sector Strategies to Position Low-Income Youth for Careers in High-Demand Sectors
description: This grant will provide support to YouthBuild USA to continue to align education and sector-based strategies to provide students in its network access to advanced opportunities in high demand occupations. Through this project, the grantee has worked with affiliate programs in developing focused articulation agreements with community colleges, certification training pathways, and placement and apprenticeship opportunities for students in the construction and healthcare industries. Over the past year, students enrolled in this focused career development effort have successfully moved into entry-level employment and/or further postsecondary opportunities. Recommended support will enable the grantee to deepen and expand its education and sector-based activities to additional affiliate programs across the United States.

title: Opening Career Pathways
description: Through its Opening Career Pathways project, this grant will enable YouthBuild USA to align education strategies with sectoral workforce preparation strategies. YouthBuild USA provides low-income youth between the ages of 16-24 with opportunities to work toward a GED or a high school diploma, learn job skills to serve their communities by building affordable housing, and transform their lives and roles in society. Through the Opening Career Pathways project, YouthBuild will work with ten sites in its network to strengthen, document, and replicate effective career development strategies where vulnerable youth can gain access to education and career opportunities that lead to economic self-sufficiency. Recommended support will provide 975 students across the YouthBuild USA network with opportunities to transition into post-secondary education and training opportunities and career pathways in high growth and high demand industries. This grant will support the planning and initial implementation phase.

title: Great Lakes Economic Initiative
geographic_focus: Wisconsin, Iowa, Michigan, Illinois, Ohio, Minnesota, Pennsylvania, West Virginia, New York, Indiana, Missouri
description: In partnership with a network of academic, public policy, business, and civic organizations, the Brookings Institution’s Metropolitan Policy Program launched a multiyear research and policy development initiative in 2005 to improve the economic vitality of the Great Lakes region. A framing report, “The Vital Center: A Federal-State Compact to Renew the Great Lakes Region”, was shared through a series of well-attended briefings of civic, business, political, labor, and media leaders at nearly a dozen major cities throughout the region. This renewal grant will provide funds for the grantee to continue to translate the report’s recommendations into actions that can be taken by the region’s government, education, and business communities to advance a winning economic vision for the Great Lakes region.

title: Philadelphia Youth Transitions Collaborative: Supporting City Partnerships to Address the Dropout Crisis
description: This grant will enable the Philadelphia Youth Network to continue to convene and support a citywide partnership aimed at addressing and raising the visibility of the dropout crisis. Through this project, the grantee has successfully led and convened the Philadelphia Youth Transitions Collaborative in piloting specific programmatic interventions and advancing a policy agenda that strengthens districtwide efforts and increases resources and supports to improve outcomes for dropouts. During the next stage of this project, the Philadelphia Youth Network will deepen its work and begin to identify ways to design, fund, build, and sustain a portfolio of educational pathways and options that meet the demands and needs of dropouts.

title: Philadelphia Youth Transitions Collaborative: Supporting City Partnerships to Address the Dropout Crisis
description: This grant will enable the Philadelphia Youth Network to continue to convene and support a citywide partnership aimed at addressing and raising the visibility of the dropout crisis. Through this project, the grantee has successfully led and convened the Philadelphia Youth Transitions Collaborative in developing programmatic interventions and advancing a policy agenda that strengthens districtwide efforts to improve outcomes for dropouts. During the next stage of this project, the grantee, via its role as convener of the Philadelphia Youth Transitions Collaborative, will deepen its work and identify ways to design, support, build, and sustain a portfolio of educational pathways and options that meet the demands and needs of dropouts.

title: Philadelphia Youth Transitions Collaborative: Supporting City Partnerships to Address the Dropout Crisis
description: This grant will enable the Philadelphia Youth Network to continue to convene and support a citywide partnership aimed at addressing and raising the visibility of the dropout crisis. Through this project, the grantee has been instrumental in advancing a graduation and dropout agenda by convening the school district of Philadelphia and key education, government, nonprofit, and service providers in developing programmatic interventions and districtwide efforts that improve outcomes for dropouts. Since embarking on this initiative, the on-time graduation rate has increased nine percentage points, and more than 2,000 new educational seats have been created for off-track students in Philadelphia. Recommended support will enable the grantee to undertake a new research agenda on graduation challenges and opportunities, identify new high school models for high risk populations, and inform local and state policy discussions on dropout prevention/recovery.

title: Philadelphia Youth Transitions Collaborative: Supporting City Partnerships to Address the Dropout Crisis
description: This grant will enable the Philadelphia Youth Network to continue to convene and support a citywide partnership aimed at addressing and raising the visibility of the dropout crisis. Over the past few years, the Philadelphia Youth Network has worked to improve the educational options and outcomes for out-of-school and underserved youth through Philadelphia’s participation in the Coalition of Community Foundations for Youth’s Addressing the Dropout Crisis in Our Cities project. Building on the work completed in this earlier project, the Philadelphia Youth Network will lead and convene the Philadelphia Youth Transitions Collaborative in its implementation of strategies and action plans to strengthen districtwide efforts that improve outcomes for dropouts.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purposes support to Priority Children. The organization was created in 1989, under the leadership of Mott Children’s Health Center, to mobilize a community-wide effort aimed at improving the quality of life for children in Genesee County. Today, Priority Children is recognized as an effective community resource, one that brings people and organizations together to advocate on behalf of the county’s children and families. General purposes support will allow the organization to continue to provide leadership on children- and family-related issues and help the community to solve problems by sponsoring community forums, workshops, task forces, and other events.

title: Endowment for the Center to Serve Historically Black Colleges and Universities
initiative: Historically and Predominantly Black Colleges and Universities
geographic_focus: Texas, Louisiana, Kentucky, Alabama, North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia, Mississippi, Florida, Tennessee, Virginia
description: This grant will provide support to partially endow the Center to Serve Historically Black Colleges and Universities at the Southern Education Foundation. Black colleges have been a focus of the grantee’s work for many years. Most recently, programs have addressed issues such as accreditation, alumni development, graduation rates in the sciences, teacher training, technology planning, and Hurricane Katrina recovery. This grant will leverage endowment matching funds from the Mellon Foundation and allow the grantee to achieve its program endowment goal of $6 million. In 2007, the Southern Education Foundation celebrates the 140th year of its founding. It is the South’s only regional nonprofit focused exclusively on improving education for low-income students and communities from preschool through post-secondary education.

title: Renovation and Endowment for the Ruth Rawlings Mott Auditorium
description: This grant will provide support to Olivet College for the renovation of and endowment for the Ruth Rawlings Mott Auditorium, which is located adjacent to the Charles Stewart Mott Academic Center. With seating for 400, the 8,316 square foot auditorium is the only indoor lecture hall facility of its type on campus. In recent years, the college has managed with the auditorium’s limited amenities, but the condition of the facility is deteriorating. The seats, lighting, heating and cooling system, sound system, carpet, and roof are in need of replacement. Renovations to the auditorium will provide state-of-the-art upgrades to be used for some of the college’s most prominent events, such as the President’s Opening Convocation, Honor’s Convocation, the Lecture and Symposium Series, new student orientation, as well as speakers brought in by various academic departments. Founded in 1844, Olivet College is a private, four-year liberal arts institution located in south central Michigan.

title: Revitalizing America's Older Industrial Cities
description: The Brookings Institution Metropolitan Policy Program is beginning a multiyear effort to help revitalize America’s older industrial cities. The project builds from work begun in 2005 to provide an empirically grounded definition of a weak market city, identify those cities that fit the definition, and produce a framing report that provides leaders with a clearer understanding of the major demographic and market forces affecting older industrial cities. The primary goal of the project is to provide guidance and recommendations on the policy reforms necessary to improve the economic competitiveness of these cities.

title: Institutional Development
description: The program goal is to facilitate efficient information exchange between civic organizations, funders, state authorities, media, and the public in Ukraine. This grant provides institutional development support to strengthen the professional and technological capacity of Ukraine’s most prominent Internet portal for civic initiatives and nonprofit organizations. The portal is an Internet resource that provides a broad spectrum of interactive services designed to raise the effectiveness of Ukrainian nonprofits. These include searchable databases, Web page hosting services, discussion forums, analytical and research materials, nonprofit sector news, and other features. In 2007-2010, the Civic Space portal saw average monthly visitor numbers increase to over 15,000. Web hosting, consulting, and communication services were systematically provided to over 200 organizations. Civic Space was initiated in 2002 as a project of the International Renaissance Foundation. Having registered as an independent organization in 2005, it continues to develop and provide a range of Internet-focused support services to the Ukrainian nonprofit sector.

title: Institutional Development
description: The program goal is to facilitate efficient information exchange between civic organizations, funders, state authorities, media, and society in Ukraine. This grant provides institutional development support to Ukraine’s most prominent Internet portal for civic initiatives and nonprofit organizations. The portal is an Internet resource that provides a broad spectrum of interactive services, which can raise the effectiveness of Ukrainian nonprofits. These include searchable databases, Web page hosting services, discussion forums, analytical and research materials, nonprofit sector news, and other features. Additionally, the portal will provide information and resources related to corporate social responsibility and philanthropy in Ukraine. Civic Space was initiated in 2002 as a project of the International Renaissance Foundation. Having registered as an independent organization in 2005, it continues to develop and provide a range of Internet-focused support services to the Ukrainian nonprofit sector.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: New York, West Virginia, Michigan, Ohio, Pennsylvania
description: The Harriet Tubman Center for Recruitment and Development of Organizers was founded in 2006 as a project of several affiliates of the Gamaliel Foundation in order to fill a void in the recruitment and development of professional and competent community organizers. In 2008, the center separated from MI*Voice and formed a separate nonprofit corporation. This grant will provide partial general purpose support.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Michigan, New York, Ohio, Pennsylvania, West Virginia
description: The Harriet Tubman Center for Recruitment and Development of Organizers was founded in 2006 as a project of several affiliates of the Gamaliel Foundation in order to fill a void in the recruitment and development of professional and competent community organizers. In 2008, the center separated from the Gamaliel Foundation of Michigan and formed a separate nonprofit corporation. This grant will provide partial general purpose support.

geographic_focus: Michigan, New York, Ohio, West Virginia, Pennsylvania
description: The Harriet Tubman Center for Recruitment and Development of Organizers was founded in 2006 as a project of several affiliates of the Gamaliel Foundation in order to fill a void in the recruitment and development of professional and competent community organizers. In 2008, the center separated from the Gamaliel Foundation of Michigan and formed a separate nonprofit corporation. This grant increase will provide partial general purpose support.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: West Virginia, Ohio, Michigan, Pennsylvania, New York
description: The Harriet Tubman Center for Recruitment and Development of Organizers was founded in 2008 to train community organizers with an emphasis on working in Michigan and the Midwest. The organization also incubates new community organizing initiatives. This grant will provide partial general purpose support.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: West Virginia, New York, Michigan, Pennsylvania, Ohio
description: The Harriet Tubman Center for Recruitment and Development of Organizers was founded in 2008 to train community organizers with an emphasis on working in Michigan and the Midwest. The grantee also incubates new community organizing initiatives. This grant will provide partial general purpose support.

title: Organizer Training Program
geographic_focus: Michigan, Ohio, West Virginia, Pennsylvania, New York
description: The lack of trained organizers is the single greatest unmet need identified in the field of organizing. MI*Voice, a coalition of Michigan-based community organizations affiliated with the Gamaliel Foundation, is working in cooperation with Gamaliel organizations in five states to establish an organizer training program to recruit, train, place, and mentor community organizers to staff organizations in Michigan, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Upstate New York, and West Virginia. This grant will provide partial support for the new Institute for Organizer Recruitment and Development.

title: Clean and Green
description: Through property tax foreclosure, the Genesee County Land Bank Authority owns more than 2,100 vacant residential lots throughout Genesee County, with the majority of the lots located in the city of Flint. Through its Clean and Green program, the authority partners with community-based organizations to maintain these vacant lots and design various neighborhood greening projects. Participants in the program gain both leadership and job skills. This grant provides partial support to the program, which aims to encourage community residents’ long-term ownership in the maintenance and beautification of lots within their neighborhoods.

title: Third Avenue Enhancement Program
description: In their 2004 report, Sasaki Associates, Inc., recommended transforming Third Avenue into a signature street to provide an improved connection between Kettering University and the University of Michigan-Flint, as well as to support ongoing revitalization efforts in central Flint. This grant to the City of Flint will provide partial support for a $5.2 million reconstruction of Third Avenue and reconfiguration from four lanes to two lanes with a new center turn lane. Additionally, the project will include a streetscape enhancement designed to create an attractive thoroughfare, new lighting for pedestrians and vehicle traffic, a bicycle lane, sidewalk benches, enhanced crosswalks, and plantings. The project will be environmentally friendly by creating rain gardens for water runoff.

title: Genesee Business Center
description: This grant will provide continued support to the Genesee County Land Bank Authority for the Genesee Business Center. The Genesee Business Center provides prime office, commercial, research, and light manufacturing space with convenient access to major highways and Bishop International Airport. The Genesee Regional Chamber of Commerce has partnered with the Land Bank to market the facility and recruit tenants that contribute to Genesee County’s economic growth. The chamber, in collaboration with other area and state economic development organizations, provides business entrepreneurial and economic development services at the center.

title: Genesee Business Center
description: This grant will provide continued support to the Genesee County Land Bank Authority for the Genesee Business Center. The center provides prime office, commercial, research, and light manufacturing space with convenient access to major highways and Bishop International Airport. While the center is more than two-thirds occupied, rental revenue is still not sufficient to cover the costs to operate and maintain this large facility.

title: Genesee Business Center
description: The Genesee County Land Bank Authority acquired the Great Lakes Technology Center in 2005 as part of a partnership with the Genesee Regional Chamber of Commerce. The plan for the facility is to create a business incubator and entrepreneurial center, and to recruit tenants that contribute to Genesee County’s economic growth. This grant will allow Genesee County Land Bank Authority to continue to implement the economic development strategy until the facility generates sufficient rental income for sustainability.

title: Building Nonprofit Leadership Initiative
description: BoardSource is a national organization that seeks to increase the effectiveness of nonprofit organizations by strengthening their boards of directors. Through the Building Nonprofit Leadership Initiative, BoardSource, in partnership with the United Way of Genesee County, brings national experience, as well as promising practices and emerging trends in nonprofit governance, to Flint and Genesee County. Goals for the initiative include leveraging community networks to inspire potential board leaders; preparing candidates for and connecting them to board service opportunities; educating boards in recruitment best practices; providing individualized support and technical assistance to nonprofit organizations; and providing ongoing educational resources and training for nonprofit leaders.

title: Building Nonprofit Leadership Initiative
description: This renewal grant for the Building Nonprofit Leadership Initiative supports a partnership between BoardSource and the United Way of Genesee County. BoardSource is a national organization that seeks to increase the effectiveness of nonprofit organizations by strengthening their boards of directors. Goals for the initiative include training boards in fund development, educating boards in recruitment best practices, and providing individualized support and technical assistance to nonprofit organizations.

title: Building Nonprofit Leadership Initiative
description: BoardSource seeks to increase the effectiveness of nonprofit organizations by strengthening their boards of directors, but the organization rarely has the opportunity to work in any one community in a sustained and in-depth manner. The Building Nonprofit Leadership Initiative in Flint and Genesee County is a partnership between BoardSource and the United Way of Genesee County to provide training, consulting, tools, and resources to enhance the governance capacity of local leaders and their service on the boards of many nonprofit organizations. Goals for this project include redefining the community’s understanding of what board service means, shifting the culture of board service in Genesee County, increasing the effectiveness of nonprofit boards of directors, and improving board governance practices.

title: 40th Anniversary Challenge Campaign
description: The Center for Community Change was founded in 1968 and has been a Mott Foundation grantee since 1976. The grantee provides consultation, training, research, and technical assistance to help local residents develop the capacity to participate effectively in shaping the policy decisions that affect their families and communities. The organization’s 40th Anniversary Challenge Campaign is designed to raise $15 million to support a venture fund for new opportunities, leadership development, and institutional support.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purpose support to the William J. Clinton Foundation, a public charity established in 1997 by the 42nd president of the United States. The mission of the organization is to strengthen the capacity of people throughout the world to meet the challenges of global interdependence. To advance this mission, the foundation operates a number of domestic and international programs, including the Alliance for a Healthier Generation, the Clinton Foundation HIV/AIDS Initiative, the Clinton Climate Initiative, the Clinton Global Initiative, and the Economic Opportunity Initiative. The foundation works principally through partnerships with like-minded individuals, organizations, corporations, and governments, often serving as an incubator for new policies and programs.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purposes support to the William J. Clinton Foundation, a public charity established in 1997 by the 42nd President of the United States. The mission of the organization is to strengthen the capacity of people throughout the world to meet the challenges of global interdependence. To advance this mission, the foundation operates a number of domestic and international programs, including the Alliance for a Healthier Generation, the Clinton Foundation HIV/AIDS Initiative, the Clinton Climate Initiative, the Clinton Global Initiative, and the Urban Enterprise Initiative. The foundation works principally through partnerships with like-minded individuals, organizations, corporations, and governments, often serving as an incubator for new policies and programs.

title: AW2 Careers Project
description: This grant increase will provide funds to the National Organization on Disability to help the U.S. Army expand the AW2 (America’s Wounded Warriors) Careers Project from three to twelve sites. The AW2 Careers Project is an employment and life skills strategy for the 5,700 severely injured and wounded soldiers and veterans of the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan.

title: AW2 Careers Project
description: This grant will provide funds to the National Organization on Disability to help the United States Army design, test, and implement an employment strategy for the Wounded Warrior program for severely wounded veterans. Since the launch of the global war on terrorism, more than 30,000 service men and women, mostly soldiers in the United States Army, have been injured. Among the injured, more than 1,500 have suffered trauma so severe that they qualify for the Wounded Warrior program. Typically, soldiers endure months of rehabilitation before they retire from the military and return to civilian life. The Wounded Warrior program seeks to ensure that this transition is as constructive as possible.

title: Electronic Filing of Forms 990
description: This grant supports the Urban Institute’s National Center for Charitable Statistics to continue providing electronic filing of federal and state Forms 990 for nonprofits through its 990 online system. Since its launch in 2004, nearly 17,000 nonprofit returns and extensions have been created using the system, which thus far has been offered at no charge. Electronic filing systems for six states also have been created. Over the next three years, the Urban Institute expects to make the system largely self-supporting through user fees. Grant funds will support maintaining the 990 online Web site, facilitating policy analysis and development, integrating federal and state electronic filing systems, and assisting the Internal Revenue Service with the development of systems required to provide electronic filing data to the public.

title: Oversight and Regulation of Charitable Organizations
grantee: Columbia University in the City of New York
description: This grant to Columbia University in the City of New York provides continued support to the Attorneys General Oversight and Regulation of Charitable Organizations project of the National State Attorneys General Program at Columbia Law School. The goal of the project is to foster a comprehensive approach by state attorneys general to protect charitable assets and ensure their lawful, highest, and best use in the public interest. Over the past two years, through two national conferences, consultations and visits to state attorney general offices, trainings, and a Web site, the project served as: 1) a catalyst for issues development and information exchange among attorneys general, other stakeholders, and scholars; and 2) a resource for attorneys general seeking information and assistance on law enforcement or negotiation efforts. Over the next two years, the project will continue its educational activities and conduct annual conferences on topics such as fraud prevention and the relationship between state regulators and the federal government.

title: Oversight and Regulation of Charitable Organizations
grantee: Columbia University in the City of New York
description: This grant provides continued support to the Attorneys General Oversight and Regulation of Charitable Organizations project of the National State Attorneys General Program at Columbia Law School, Columbia University in the City of New York. The goal of the project is to foster a comprehensive approach by state attorneys general to protecting charitable assets and ensuring their lawful, highest, and best use in the public interest and in the manner their donors intended. Through national conferences, trainings, online materials, and consultations to state attorneys general offices, the project has been an educational resource for attorneys general and their staff and has facilitated dialogue with nonprofit practitioners and scholars. Over the next two years, the project will continue to enhance and broaden these activities. Columbia University is one of the top academic and research institutions in the world. One of the university’s 13 graduate and professional schools, Columbia Law School is a leading center of legal scholarship.

title: Oversight and Regulation of Charitable Organizations
grantee: Columbia University in the City of New York
description: This grant provides continued support to the attorneys general Oversight and Regulation of Charitable Organizations project of the National State Attorneys General Program at Columbia Law School. The goal of the project is to foster a comprehensive approach by state attorneys general to protecting charitable assets and ensuring their lawful, highest, and best use in the public interest and in the manner their donors intended. Through national conferences, trainings, online materials, and one-on-one consultations, the project has been an educational resource for attorneys general and their staff and has facilitated dialogue with nonprofit practitioners and scholars. Besides a continuation of the above, project activities over the next two years will include research to codify state charities regulation enforcement resources, practices, and outcomes. Columbia Law School is a leading center of legal scholarship at Columbia University, one of the world’s top academic and research institutions.

title: Regulation of Nonprofits and Philanthropy
description: The Regulation of Nonprofits and Philanthropy project is a continuation of the Oversight and Regulation of Charitable Organizations project which had been part of the Columbia Law School’s National State Attorneys General Program. The project provided an important educational resource for attorneys general and their staff on protecting charitable assets and ensuring their best use in the public interest and facilitated dialogue between state-level charities, regulators, and nonprofit practitioners and scholars. Over the past two years, it also did a mapping of state charities regulation enforcement resources, practices, and outcomes. The project is now transitioning to a new host, the Urban Institute’s Center on Nonprofits and Philanthropy. At its new venue, the Regulation of Nonprofits and Philanthropy project will expand its mission to become a platform for the study of the entire regulatory framework of the United States’ charitable sector, both at the state and federal levels.

title: Regulation of Nonprofits and Philanthropy
description: The program goal is to support a healthy policy environment for the nonprofit sector and philanthropy. The Regulation of Nonprofits and Philanthropy project provides a platform for ongoing dialogue, investigation, and interaction about the federal and state regulatory framework for the sector among state charities officials, federal regulators, researchers, and practitioners. Most recently, the project has produced a research report on state charities regulation and enforcement. Findings were presented at various relevant conferences, and a roundtable will be held in late September 2016 to identify research gaps and needs that will become a research agenda for future work. Issues to be addressed are: obtaining financial data for charities offices; federal and state oversight of nonprofit governance; and revisions to Forms 990 and 990PF. The project is implemented by the Center on Nonprofits and Philanthropy at the Urban Institute, a think tank that builds knowledge about the nation’s social and fiscal challenges.

title: Regulation of Nonprofits and Philanthropy
description: The program goal is to support a healthy policy environment for the nonprofit sector and philanthropy. The Regulation of Nonprofits and Philanthropy project aims to document, enhance understanding, and promote dialogue related to the state and federal regulatory framework and its impact on charities, philanthropy, and the nonprofit sector. The project engages attorneys general and other state officials, federal regulators, academics, researchers, and nonprofit practitioners. In the past two years, the project has produced several research products on state and federal charities regulation and enforcement which have been presented at several relevant stakeholder gatherings and have spawned additional research and dialogue. Over the next two years, the project will continue producing further research and analysis on state and federal regulatory issues affecting the charitable sector; conduct two discussion forums; and disseminate research papers, briefs, and a compendium of papers. The project is implemented by the Center on Nonprofits and Philanthropy at the Urban Institute—a think tank that builds knowledge about the nation’s social and fiscal challenges.

title: Oversight and Regulation of Charitable Organizations
grantee: Columbia University in the City of New York
description: This grant will provide support to the Attorneys General Oversight and Regulation of Charitable Organizations project of the National State Attorneys General Program at Columbia Law School at Columbia University in the City of New York. The goal of the project is to foster a comprehensive approach by state attorneys general to protecting charitable assets and ensuring their lawful, highest, and best use in the public interest. It will foster the development of best practices around guidelines and regulatory tools for attorneys general, educate them and other stakeholders about these best practices, facilitate communication between attorneys general and the regulated communities, and promote the presence of attorneys general in the national discourse about these issues. The project also will be poised to recommend and assist the implementation of joint strategies, such as coordinated responses to national legislation, regulations, and government agencies.

title: New Economy Initiative for Southeast Michigan
description: The Community Foundation for Southeast Michigan launched the New Economy Initiative to speed the transition of Southeast Michigan to the new knowledge-based economy. Since its inception in 2007, this philanthropic collaborative has made grants and investments to support economic development infrastructure, innovative enterprises, and educational programs that prepare adults for the new economy. Renewal grant funds will support the initiative’s second phase, which will focus more tightly on creating new enterprises, attracting capital, and generating jobs through innovation and entrepreneurship.

title: New Economy Initiative for Southeast Michigan
description: The Community Foundation for Southeastern Michigan launched the New Economy Initiative to speed the transition of southeast Michigan to the new knowledge-based economy. Since its inception in 2007, this philanthropic collaborative has made grants and investments to support economic development infrastructure, innovative enterprises, and educational programs that prepare adults for the new economy. This grant increase will support the initiative’s second phase, which focuses on three key activities: continuing to develop the innovation network; expanding the entrepreneurial culture in the city of Detroit; and developing new ideas and programs to strengthen the innovation ecosystem.

title: New Economy Initiative for Southeast Michigan
description: The Community Foundation for Southeast Michigan launched the New Economy Initiative to speed the transition of southeast Michigan to the new knowledge-based economy. Since its inception in 2007, this philanthropic collaborative has provided grants and developed partnerships to support economic development infrastructure, innovative enterprises, and educational programs that prepare adults for the new economy. This grant increase will support staff and operations, and related consulting services for the initiative.
