description: The Community Foundation for Southeast Michigan launched the New Economy Initiative for Southeast Michigan to speed the transition of southeast Michigan to the new, knowledge-based economy. title: New Economy Initiative for Southeast Michigan
description: The Community Foundation for Southeast Michigan is leading the New Economy Initiative, an effort to raise and distribute $100 million to foster economic growth and to speed the transition of Southeast Michigan to the new knowledge-based economy. This philanthropic collaborative will make grants and investments to support economic development infrastructure, innovative enterprises, and educational programs that prepare adults for the new economy.

title: Symphony History Book and "Peter and the Wolf" Performance
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide support for two projects to be undertaken by the Flint Institute of Music. To commemorate the 90th anniversary of the Flint Symphony Orchestra, the Flint Institute of Music will write and publish a book to document the achievements and history of this outstanding musical institution. A scheduled 2008-2009 performance of “Peter and the Wolf” will feature dancers from the Flint Youth Ballet and musicians with the Flint Youth Symphony Orchestra. There will be one public presentation, as well as two performances for area school children, at The Whiting. Priority will be given to Flint schools and other local school districts without music programs. Schools will receive a voucher to assist with transportation costs, as well as a study guide and a CD of the music to help teachers prepare students for the performance.

title: Seven-Year Plans for Generational Change: An Environmental Partnership Between the United Nations and Faith Organizations
description: This grant provides support for a collaborative effort between the Alliance of Religions and Conservation and the United Nations. Under the leadership of the Secretary-General, the United Nations has established a formal partnership with world faith groups to address issues of the environment and climate change. In November 2009 in Windsor, England, 31 faith groups and 18 secular organizations made long-term commitments to the living planet. Bahai, Buddhist, Christian, Daoist, Muslim, Jewish, and Shinto faiths are engaged in creating and implementing long-term plans, offering practical models of constructive civil society engagement on the subjects of assets, education, pastoral care, lifestyles, media and advocacy, partnerships, and eco-twinning. During the grant period, these faith groups will receive assistance on implementing their plans. New initiatives and partnerships among religious and secular organizations will also be facilitated.

title: Seven-Year Plans for Generational Change: An Environmental Partnership Between the United Nations and Faith Organizations
description: This grant will provide support for a partnership between the Alliance of Religions and Conservation and the United Nations. Under the leadership of the Secretary-General, the United Nations has established a formal partnership with world faith groups to address issues of the environment and climate change. Bahai, Buddhist, Christian, Daoist, Muslim, Jewish, and Shinto faiths are engaged and creating long-term action plans, offering practical models of constructive engagement on the subjects of assets, education, pastoral care, lifestyles, media and advocacy, partnerships and eco-twinning, and celebration. On November 4, 2009, in association with both the BBC World Service and Google, faith communities around the world will announce their seven-year plans. A series of films highlighting aspects of the seven key areas will be shown during the 24-hour launch event. A major conference will also take place at Windsor Castle or St. Paul’s Cathedral in London.

title: Ready to Govern: Developing a Strategy for Kosovo's First 120 Days
description: The project goal is to help the Kosovar leadership to develop a sound strategy for governance during the first 120 days following the United Nations’ decision on Kosovo’s independence. To this end, the East-West Management Institute, in cooperation with the Project on Justice in Times of Transition and with the support of the Rockefeller Brothers Fund, brought together a small group of significant international and American experts with relevant experience and key senior members of the Kosovar administration for an intensive, two-day meeting at the Rockefeller Pocantico Conference Center outside of New York City in April 2007. The meeting produced a concrete strategic plan for the first 120 days of independence and a broadened network of advisors and experts for the Kosovar leadership to draw on during this period. The East-West Management Institute is based in New York and has implemented several projects in Kosovo since 1999.

title: Minnesota Great Lakes Agenda
description: Historically, Lake Superior has been the most pristine of the Great Lakes, but development and industrial pollution are threatening its water quality and aquatic habitat. In 2006, the Minnesota Environmental Partnership, a statewide network of groups, led the development of the Minnesota Great Lakes Agenda that calls for actions to protect the lakes. Since that time, the partnership and other stakeholders have worked to implement key aspects of the agenda, such as controls on mercury pollution and implementation of the Great Lakes Compact. With renewal support from Mott, the work to implement other aspects of the agenda, such as addressing the water quality impacts from mining activities, will continue.

title: Minnesota Great Lakes Agenda
description: Pressures on Lake Superior, and the Great Lakes generally, are on the rise, but new opportunities to positively influence Great Lakes policy in Minnesota and regionally are also presenting themselves. To capitalize on such opportunities, the Minnesota Environmental Partnership, a statewide network of groups engaged in environmental protection, helped develop the Minnesota Great Lakes Agenda in early 2007. This grant will provide partial support for the implementation of the agenda by the partnership and other stakeholders. Water quality issues and related concerns will be addressed through a variety of means such as policy work, media communications, and public outreach.

title: Truth and Reconciliation Commission (TRC) Project
description: This grant will provide support to South African History Archive Trust in its efforts to make the work of South Africa’s Truth and Reconciliation Commission more accessible to a wider audience. Despite a rich body of material generated by the truth and reconciliation process, there is a concern that most South Africans have not had access to this information. Specifically, this grant will fund a component aimed at tertiary education students that includes compiling a CD ROM set of all 78 Truth and Reconciliation Commission Special Report television programs; and producing an accompanying booklet containing detailed findings, commentary, and relevant research links. This resource will be disseminated, free of charge, to tertiary institutions and organizations that work in the field of transitional justice and reconciliation, particularly those that work with apartheid victim/survivor groups.

title: Ray Murphy Memorial Lecture Series
description: Following Ray Murphy’s untimely death in March 2007, Philanthropy Ireland created the Ray Murphy Memorial Lecture Series. Commencing in early 2008, the lecture series has consisted of an annual lecture delivered by an international leader in philanthropy. To date, the grantee has organized five Ray Murphy lectures, and this increase will extend the series through 2018. The lecture series targets key figures in the international and Irish philanthropic communities. In addition to recognizing Murphy’s role as a pioneer in the philanthropy field, the lecture series encourages the further development of philanthropy in Ireland through exposure to current trends in international philanthropy. Created in 2003, Philanthropy Ireland is an association of charitable trusts, foundations, and corporations in Ireland.

title: Ray Murphy Memorial Lecture Series
description: Following Ray Murphy’s untimely death in March 2007, Philanthropy Ireland created the Ray Murphy Memorial Lecture Series. Commencing in early 2008, the lecture series will consist of an annual lecture delivered by an international leader in philanthropy. The target audience for the lectures will be key figures in the international and Irish philanthropic communities. Each lecture will be recorded and published on the grantee’s Web site, and at the end of the ten-year lecture series, all lectures will be published as a stand-alone publication. In addition to recognizing Murphy’s role as a pioneer in the philanthropy field, the lecture series is expected to encourage the further development of philanthropy in Ireland through exposure to current trends in international philanthropy. Created in 2003, Philanthropy Ireland is the association of charitable trusts, foundations, and corporations in Ireland.

title: Teen CEO Initiative
description: This grant to Mott Community College will fund a six-week learning experience for 30 economically disadvantaged youth who are interested in entrepreneurship. The goal of the summer camp is to demonstrate the feasibility of operating an entrepreneurial education program for economically disadvantaged youth that provides them with a learning and leadership experience that will influence their future and identify their early potential to be entrepreneurs. Program participants will develop business plans and stage a showcase of business plans at the Flint Farmers’ Market. The program will award entrepreneur certificates, $300 stipends, and provide access to seed capital to implement the best business concepts.

title: Teen CEO Initiative
description: This renewal grant to Mott Community College will fund a six-week experiential learning initiative for 30 economically disadvantaged youth who are interested in entrepreneurship. The goal of the summer camp is to demonstrate the feasibility of operating an entrepreneurial education program for economically disadvantaged youth that provides them with a learning and leadership experience that will influence their future and identify their early potential to be entrepreneurs. Program participants will develop and stage a showcase of business plans. The program will award entrepreneur certificates and $300 stipends, and will provide access to seed capital to implement the best business concepts.

title: Teen CEO Initiative
description: This renewal grant to Mott Community College will fund a six-week learning experience for 30 economically disadvantaged youth who are interested in entrepreneurship. The goal of the Teen CEO Initiative is to demonstrate the feasibility of operating an entrepreneurial education program for economically disadvantaged youth that provides them with a learning and leadership experience that will influence their future and identify their early potential to be entrepreneurs. During this summer camp, program participants will develop business plans and stage a showcase of their plans. The program will award entrepreneur certificates and stipends, and will provide access to seed capital to implement the best business concepts.

title: Teen CEO Initiative
description: Mott Community College provides a six-week entrepreneurial experience for 30 economically disadvantaged teenagers, aged 14-18. This renewal grant supports the Teen CEO Summer Camp program, which teaches students the basic skills required to launch a successful new business venture. Using tested business curriculum and experiential learning opportunities, the participants work together, competing against other teams to develop the strongest business plan. to win all (or a portion) of the $10,000 of start-up capital to fund the new businesses. The program will award entrepreneur certificates and stipends, and will provide access to seed capital to implement the best business concepts.

title: Teen CEO Initiative
description: This renewal grant provides support to Mott Community College for the Teen CEO Initiative, which offers a six-week summer camp entrepreneurial experience for 30 economically disadvantaged teenagers aged 14-18. Using tested business curriculum and experiential learning opportunities, the initiative teaches students about the basic skills required to launch a successful new business venture. Participants compete against each other to develop the strongest business plan to win all or a portion of an award of $10,000 startup capital to fund the new business.

title: Teen CEO Initiative
description: This renewal grant provides support to Mott Community College for the Teen CEO Initiative, which offers a six-week summer camp entrepreneurial experience for 25 economically disadvantaged teenagers ages 14-18. Using tested business curricula and experiential learning opportunities, the Teen CEO Initiative teaches students the basic skills required to launch a successful new business venture. Participants are eligible to receive an award of $1,000 to fund their new business based on the strength of their business plan.

title: Teen CEO Initiative
description: This renewal grant provides support to Mott Community College for the Teen Creating Economic Opportunity Initiative, which offers a seven-week entrepreneurial learning and leadership experience for 45 disadvantaged youth between the ages of 14-18. The objectives of the program are to: 1) provide participants with the competencies needed to operate a business, including business plan development; 2) offer youth additional skill building opportunities through mentorships and job shadowing; 3) help students develop a higher education career pathway plan; and 4) pilot a special program track dedicated to encouraging entrepreneurship around applied technology and manufacturing. Upon completion, 15 participants will be eligible to receive $1,000 of venture capital seed money to launch their enterprise.

title: Teen CEO Initiative
description: This renewal grant will provide support to Mott Community College for the Teen CEO Initiative, which offers a seven-week entrepreneurial learning and leadership experience for 45 disadvantaged youth between the ages of 14-18. The objectives of the program are to: 1) provide participants with the competencies needed to operate a business, including business plan development; 2) offer additional skill-building opportunities through mentorships and job shadowing; 3) help students develop a higher education career pathway plan; and 4) offer a program track dedicated to encouraging entrepreneurship around applied technology and manufacturing. Upon completion, 15 participants will be eligible to receive $1,000 in seed money to launch their venture.

title: Teen CEO Initiative
description: This renewal grant will provide support to Mott Community College for the Teen CEO Initiative. The goal of the initiative is to provide disadvantaged youth with a summertime opportunity to build their entrepreneurial business skills, explore higher education, and investigate career pathways after high school.

title: Teen CEO Initiative
description: This renewal grant will provide support to Mott Community College for the Teen CEO Initiative. The goal of the project is to provide disadvantaged youth with a summertime opportunity to build their entrepreneurial business skills, explore higher education, and investigate career pathways.

title: Teen CEO Initiative
description: This grant will support the newly expanded Teen CEO Initiative at Mott Community College. The goal is to provide youth ages 14-18 with a year-round entrepreneurship experience. In addition to a summertime component, the expansion includes a 34-week after school program that will assist young people in acquiring the skills needed to launch a business and/or prepare them with the skills needed to enter into higher education or the workforce.

title: Teen C.E.O. Initiative
description: This renewal grant will provide support to Mott Community College for the Teen Creating Economic Opportunity Initiative. The goal of the project is to provide disadvantaged youth with a summertime opportunity to build their entrepreneurial business skills, explore higher education, and investigate career pathways.

Program participants will develop business plans, and stage a showcase of business plans at the Flint Farmers’ Market. The program will award entrepreneur certificates and stipends, and provide access to seed capital to implement the best business concepts.

title: Democracy, Organizing and Islam
description: Metro Industrial Areas Foundation, Inc., is leading and supervising a project in Chicago and other cities where Muslim leadership in community organizing is being developed. This effort has contributed to the development of the Industrial Areas Foundation affiliates, as well as to the growth and development of the participating Islamic institutions. This grant renewal will support expansion of this effort, as well as a parallel effort to recruit Jewish institutions to participate in institution-based community organizing.

title: Democracy, Organizing and Islam
description: This grant will provide support to Metro Industrial Areas Foundation to lead and supervise a project in Chicago and other cities where Muslim leadership in community organizing is being developed. This effort is expected to contribute to the development of the Industrial Areas Foundation affiliates, as well as to the growth and development of the participating Islamic institutions. The grantee will continue to implement a curriculum of training, expanding the recruitment of a new generation of Muslim and other organizers committed to working in an interfaith environment.

title: Democracy, Organizing and Islam
description: Metro Industrial Areas Foundation, Inc., is leading and supervising a project in Chicago and other cities where Muslim leadership in community organizing is being developed. This effort has contributed to the development of the Industrial Areas Foundation affiliates, as well as to the growth and development of the participating Islamic institutions. This grant increase will support expansion of this effort, as well as a parallel effort to recruit Jewish institutions to participate in institution-based community organizing.

title: Democracy, Organizing and Islam
description: This grant will provide support to Metro Industrial Areas Foundation, Inc., to lead and supervise a project in Chicago and other cities where Muslim leadership in community organizing is being developed. This effort is expected to contribute to the development of the Industrial Areas Foundation affiliates as well as to the growth and development of the participating Islamic institutions. Metro Industrial Areas Foundation will organize a conference during 2008 to gather the leaders and organizers working with the participating Islamic institutions for the purposes of refining and testing a curriculum of training, expanding the recruitment of a new generation of Muslim and other organizers committed to working in a multifaith environment, and disseminating the lessons learned from this organizing experience.

title: NPower Michigan
description: This grant provides operating support to the Michigan Nonprofit Association for NPower Michigan, now a program of the association as the result of a recent merger. NPower Michigan is a member of a national network of providers of high quality, unbiased, affordable, and appropriate technology assistance to nonprofit organizations. NPower Michigan has assisted more than 400 Michigan nonprofits since starting operations in 2002 through consulting, training, and publications. Mott funding will enable NPower Michigan to complete the transition from an independent entity to a program of the Michigan Nonprofit Association, as well as to make a transition to a new business model. NPower Michigan projects that it will be able to generate all its income from fees for services by 2009 through offerings which will include technology assessments, project implementation consulting, help desk and remote assistance, and annual technology budgeting advice.

title: Community Foundation Development Fund
grantee: Academy for the Development of Philanthropy in Poland
description: The program goal is to strengthen the community foundation field in the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, and Slovakia — commonly referred to as the Visegrad countries. To this end, the Academy for the Development of Philanthropy in Poland will provide tailor-made grantmaking and technical assistance programs, facilitate networking, and provide learning opportunities to community foundations in the Visegrad countries. In addition, the grantee will strengthen the Visegrad networks and associations of community foundations. Since its establishment in 1998, the grantee has supported the development of over 20 community foundations in Poland and gained a reputation as one of the leading philanthropy development organizations in Central and Eastern Europe. During the past grant period, the grantee carried out a thorough needs assessment of 44 community foundations, provided grants and technical assistance to 37 of them, organized the first community foundation conference in the Visegrad countries, and developed a wide variety of Web-based learning resources for community foundations.

title: Community Foundation Development Fund
grantee: Academy for the Development of Philanthropy in Poland
description: The program goal is to strengthen the community foundation field in the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, and Slovakia — commonly referred to as the Visegrad countries. To this end, the Academy for the Development of Philanthropy in Poland will provide tailor-made grantmaking and technical assistance programs, facilitate networking, and provide learning opportunities to community foundations in the Visegrad countries. In addition, the grantee will strengthen the Visegrad networks and associations of community foundations. Since its establishment in 1998, the grantee has supported the development of over 20 community foundations in Poland and gained a reputation as one of the leading philanthropy development organizations in Central and Eastern Europe. During the past grant period, the grantee provided grants and technical assistance to more than 40 community foundations, organized exchange visits and group meetings, and developed a wide variety of web-based learning resources for community foundations. The grantee is based in Warsaw, Poland.

title: Community Foundation Development Fund
grantee: Academy for the Development of Philanthropy in Poland
description: The primary program goal is to strengthen the community foundation field in the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, and Slovakia — commonly referred to as the Visegrad countries. The Academy for the Development of Philanthropy in Poland will provide tailor-made grantmaking and technical assistance programs, facilitate networking, and provide learning opportunities to community foundations in the Visegrad countries. In addition, the grantee will strengthen the Visegrad networks and associations of community foundations. Building on the success of program activities over the past eight years, with this grant increase, the grantee will explore opportunities for raising additional resources to expand the geographical scope of the program beyond the Visegrad countries and provide grant support to the community foundation field in the wider Central and Eastern Europe and Russia regions. During the past grant period, the grantee provided grants and technical assistance to more than 40 community foundations, organized exchange visits and group meetings, and developed a wide variety of Web-based learning resources for community foundations. The grantee is based in Warsaw, Poland.

title: Community Foundation Development Fund
grantee: Academy for the Development of Philanthropy in Poland
description: The program goal is to strengthen the community foundation field in Central and Eastern Europe. To this end, the Academy for the Development of Philanthropy in Poland will provide tailor-made grantmaking and technical assistance programs to community foundations in the region to stimulate innovation in identifying local responses to global challenges, including population movement, education for all, and sustainable cities. In addition, the grantee will explore opportunities to increase its grantmaking fund and open it up to community foundations throughout Europe. Since its establishment in 1998, the grantee has supported the development of over 20 community foundations in Poland and gained a reputation as one of the leading philanthropy development organizations in Central and Eastern Europe. During the past grant period, the grantee provided grants and technical assistance to 38 community foundations, organized exchange visits and group meetings, and developed a wide variety of web-based learning resources for community foundations. The grantee is based in Warsaw, Poland.

title: Community Foundation Development Fund
grantee: Academy for the Development of Philanthropy in Poland
description: The program goal is to strengthen the capacity of community foundations in Europe to contribute to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. To this end, the Academy for the Development of Philanthropy in Poland will provide tailor-made grantmaking and technical assistance programs to community foundations in Europe to stimulate innovation in identifying and implementing local responses to global challenges. The grantee will develop a series of learning materials to support community foundations in their work on the global goals. In addition, the grantee will work on leveraging funds from other sources for this program. During the past grant period, the grantee provided 29 grants totaling $500,000 to community foundations in 13 countries and published 11 case studies of community foundations successfully developing local solutions to global challenges. The grantee is based in Warsaw, Poland.

title: Community Foundation Development Fund
grantee: Academy for the Development of Philanthropy in Poland
description: The program goal is to ensure independent funding for community foundation development in the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, and Slovakia (the Visegrad countries). To this end, the Academy for the Development of Philanthropy in Poland will survey community foundation needs and capacities, provide tailor-made grantmaking and technical assistance programs, and facilitate networking among community foundations in the Visegrad countries. Since its establishment in 1998, the grantee has supported the development of over 20 community foundations in Poland and gained a reputation as one of the leading philanthropy development organizations in Central and Eastern Europe.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to consolidate and strengthen the philanthropic community in Hungary. During the grant period, the Hungarian Donors Forum will increase its membership, develop its member services, increase its organizational capacity and financial sustainability, and cooperate with similar organizations in Central and Eastern Europe on efforts to develop philanthropy. The forum was formally registered in 2005, and its mission is to promote philanthropy, support the development of civil society, and improve the effectiveness and impact of indigenous grantmakers in Hungary. The grantee’s main achievements to date include organizing the annual Top Philanthropist award for corporate donors, delivering capacity building workshops to its members, and promoting good grantmaking practice.

title: General Purposes
description: The project goal is to establish the Hungarian Donors Forum as a full-fledged association of indigenous grantmakers. The mission of the forum is to promote philanthropy, support civil society, and improve the effectiveness and impact of indigenous grantmakers. During the grant period, the forum will expand its membership, strengthen its organizational capacity, improve its services, and increase its international activity. The forum was officially registered in December 2005 and currently has ten members. The forum’s past achievements include providing information and analysis on a wide variety of issues related to philanthropy and grantmaking to its members, relevant government and academic institutions, and the media.

title: General Purposes
grantee: National Association of Citizens Advice Bureaux
description: The program goal is to empower Romanian citizens and communities to exercise their rights and responsibilities. The mission of the National Association of Citizens Advice Bureaux in Romania is to support the development of civil society through informing and engaging citizens. During the grant period, the association will improve its services, strengthen its sustainability, raise the profile of citizen counseling, and advocate for improvements in government policies regarding access to information on citizens’ rights and responsibilities in Romania. The association was established in 2002 and currently has 49 members. In the past two years, the association provided capacity-building programs to its members; strengthened its communication and fundraising strategies; and published a series of studies, including research on labor rights of Romanian migrant workers within the European Union after Romania joined it in 2007.

title: General Purposes
grantee: National Association of Citizens Advice Bureaux
description: The goal of National Association of Citizens Advice Bureaux is to empower Romanian citizens and communities to exercise their rights and responsibilities. To this end, the grantee will improve its services to members and nonmenbers, strengthen its sustainability, raise the profile of citizen counseling, and advocate for improvements in government policies regarding access to information on citizens’ rights in Romania. The association was established in 2002 and currently has 37 members. In the past two years, the association provided capacity building programs to its members; strengthened its communication and fundraising strategies; and published a series of studies, including research on the transparency of decisionmaking in local public administration.

title: General Purposes
grantee: National Association of Citizens Advice Bureaux
description: The program goal is to empower Romanian citizens and communities to exercise their rights and responsibilities. To this end, the National Association of Citizens Advice Bureaux in Romania will improve its information and advice services to members and nonmembers, develop new services related to community development, raise the profile of citizen counseling, and advocate for improvements in government policies regarding access to information on citizens’ rights in Romania. In addition, the grantee will increase its organizational capacity, strengthen its financial sustainability, and improve its visibility vis-à-vis public institutions and the general public. Based in Bucharest, Romania, the grantee was established in 2002 and currently has 37 members. In the past two years the grantee provided capacity building programs to its members, strengthened its communication and fundraising strategies, and explored possibilities to establish citizen advice bureaux in the Western Balkans.

title: General Purposes
grantee: National Association of Citizens Advice Bureaux
description: The program goal is to empower Romanian citizens and communities to exercise their rights and responsibilities. The mission of the National Association of Citizens Advice Bureaux in Romania is to support the development of civil society through informing and engaging citizens. To this end, the association provides capacity-building services to citizens’ advice bureaus in Romania and represents their interests at national and international levels. In addition, the association conducts research on citizens’ needs for information and advice and advocates for changes in government policies regarding access to information on citizens’ rights and responsibilities. The association was established in 2002 and currently has 50 members. During the grant period, the association will expand its membership, improve its services, strengthen its sustainability, and raise the profile of citizen counseling in Romania.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to consolidate and strengthen the philanthropic community in Poland. During the grant period, the Polish Donors Forum will increase its membership, develop its member services, advocate for an enabling environment for civic participation and philanthropic activity, and cooperate with similar organizations in Central and Eastern Europe on efforts to develop philanthropy. The forum was set up in 2002 and formally registered in September 2004. The forum’s mission is to support the development of civil society and organized philanthropy in Poland and promote best practices in grantmaking. Currently, the forum has 12 members and 7 observers, the majority of which are indigenous grantmakers. The forum’s main achievements to date include organizing high profile events to promote philanthropy, delivering workshops on effective grantmaking, and representing the donor community vis-à-vis the government, the business sector, and civil society in Poland.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to consolidate and strengthen the philanthropic community in Poland. During the grant period, the Polish Donors Forum will increase its membership, develop its services for member and nonmember organizations, and cooperate with similar organizations in Central and Eastern Europe on efforts to develop philanthropy. The forum was set up in 2002 and formally registered in September 2004. The forum’s mission is to support the development of civil society and organized philanthropy in Poland and promote best practices in grantmaking. Currently, the forum has eight members and four observers, the majority of which are indigenous grantmakers. The forum’s main achievements to date include organizing high profile events to promote philanthropy, delivering workshops on effective grantmaking, and advocating for an enabling legal and fiscal environment for civil society and philanthropy development in Poland.

title: General Purposes
grantee: PACT - Partnership for Community Action and Transformation Foundation
description: The program goal is to build the capacity of informal groups, grassroots nonprofit organizations, and community enterprises in southern Romania to engage in the development of their communities. To this end, PACT – Partnership for Community Action and Transformation Foundation will provide training, field consultancy, small grants, and networking opportunities to grassroots organizations whose activities address the local needs of marginalized groups. In addition, the foundation will provide training and facilitation services to initiative groups in southern Romania interested in developing community foundations. The foundation will document and share its experience in community and social economy development nationally and internationally. In 2007-2009, the foundation strengthened the capacity of 32 community groups to develop and implement successful community projects, build coalitions, and mobilize local resources. Established in 2006, the foundation is based in Bucharest, Romania.

title: General Purposes
grantee: PACT - Partnership for Community Action and Transformation Foundation
description: The program goal is to build the capacity of grassroots nonprofit organizations, community foundations, and community enterprises in southern Romania to engage in the development of their communities. To this end, PACT – Partnership for Community Action and Transformation Foundation will provide training, field consultancy, small matching grants, and networking opportunities to grassroots organizations whose activities address the local needs of marginalized groups. In addition, the grantee will provide training and facilitation services to initiative groups in southern Romania interested in developing community foundations. Also, the grantee will strengthen its fundraising strategies and capacities and will start building its endowment. During the past two years, the grantee strengthened the capacity of over 20 grassroots organizations to develop and implement successful community projects and facilitated the establishment of two community foundations. Established in 2006, the grantee is based in Bucharest, Romania.

grantee: PACT - Partnership for Community Action and Transformation Foundation
description: The program goal is to build the capacity of grassroots nonprofit organizations and community enterprises in southern Romania to engage in the development of their communities. To this end, PACT – Partnership for Community Action and Transformation Foundation will provide training, field consultancy, small matching grants, and networking opportunities to grassroots organizations whose activities address the local needs of marginalized groups. During the past two years, the grantee trained more than a 100 community leaders in participatory project planning and management and strengthened the capacity of 23 grassroots organizations to develop and implement successful community projects. Established in 2006, the foundation is based in Bucharest, Romania.

title: General Purposes
grantee: PACT - Partnership for Community Action and Transformation Foundation
description: PACT – Partnership for Community Action and Transformation Foundation provides training, field consultancy, small matching grants, and networking opportunities to grassroots organizations whose activities address the needs of marginalized groups in the local communities in southern Romania. In addition, the grantee supports the development of community leadership and social entrepreneurship. An important focus for the grantee during the current grant period is strengthening its long-term organizational sustainability and developing permanent regranting funds. This grant increase will enable the grantee to engage in a structured strategic planning and organizational capacity building process that will result in improving its fundraising strategies and capacities, expanding its donor and supporter base, and preparing a detailed plan for a future endowment building campaign.

title: General Purposes
grantee: PACT - Partnership for Community Action and Transformation Foundation
description: The program goal is to build the capacity of grassroots nonprofit organizations and community enterprises in southern Romania to engage in the development of their communities. To this end, PACT – Partnership for Community Action and Transformation Foundation will provide training, field consultancy, small matching grants, and networking opportunities to grassroots organizations whose activities address the local needs of marginalized groups. In addition, the grantee will strengthen its fundraising strategies and capacities and will start building its permanent assets. During the past two years, the grantee trained community groups and local authorities in 49 communities, raised funds for regranting from sources in Romania to support 54 community projects, and strengthened its leadership position in the field of community development and social economy. Established in 2006, the grantee is based in Bucharest, Romania.

title: General Purposes
grantee: PACT - Partnership for Community Action and Transformation Foundation
description: The program goal is to build the capacity of informal groups, grassroots nonprofit organizations, and community enterprises in southern Romania to engage in the development of their communities. To this end, PACT – Partnership for Community Action and Transformation Foundation will provide training, field consultancy, small grants, and networking opportunities to grassroots organizations whose activities address the local needs of marginalized groups. In addition, the foundation will document and share its experience in community and socio-economic development and strengthen its fundraising strategies. Past achievements include building the capacity of 54 community groups to develop and implement successful community projects, build coalitions, and mobilize local resources. As a result, participating organizations gained broader community support and improved the lives of their target groups.

title: Future Bound: Preparing the Next Generation for a World of Change
description: This grant will provide partial support for Future Bound: Preparing the Next Generation for a World of Change. The Center for Strategic and International Studies, together with the American Association of State Colleges and Universities and the New York Times, has launched a major effort to educate students in colleges and universities in the United States to be globally competent and engaged citizens. This unique partnership presents a remarkable opportunity to contribute to the thinking of a vital cross-section of 3.7 million students at 430 public colleges and universities. The project’s structure is based on the “Seven Revolutions” research–the internationally recognized program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies that assesses seven “revolutionary” drivers of change out to the year 2025 and beyond. Grant funds will support faculty development workshops, publication of edited monographs based on the “Seven Revolutions” framework, stipends for intern-scholars, and additional research and project support. Founded in 1962, the Center for Strategic and International Studies is the only institution of its kind that maintains resident experts on all the world’s major geographical regions, in addition to key functional areas such as international finance, the emerging markets, United States foreign policy, and national security issues.

title: International Journal of Transitional Justice
grantee: Centre for the Study of Violence and Reconciliation
description: The Centre for the Study of Violence and Reconciliation is a policy and research center working on various aspects of violence and reconciliation. This grant will provide support to the Centre to produce the International Journal of Transitional Justice in partnership with the Human Rights Centre at the University of California, Berkley. Published three times a year by Oxford University Press, the journal carries refereed articles in the field of transitional justice to share information and knowledge to deepen understanding, build on the lessons learned, record best practices, and develop universally accepted standards in the field. The journal strives to encourage debate and discussion across disciplines and geographic areas in the field of transitional justice and serves as a reference source for academics, researchers, and practitioners. To encourage submissions by global south-based writers, a Fellows Programme will help participants develop their writing and technical skills during a six-week residency in South Africa.

title: International Journal of Transitional Justice
grantee: Centre for the Study of Violence and Reconciliation
description: This grant will support the Centre for the Study of Violence and Reconciliation to produce the International Journal of Transitional Justice in partnership with the Human Rights Centre at the University of California, Berkley. The journal will be published by Oxford University Press and will carry refereed articles in the field of transitional justice, a rapidly evolving area of study focusing on the strategies, policies, and legislative frameworks employed by international institutions, states, and civil society bodies to deal with the legacy of human rights abuses and to effect political and social reconstruction in the aftermath of endemic civil conflicts. It will bring researchers and practitioners together from a wide range of disciplines and from various parts of the world to share information and knowledge to deepen the understanding of the issues related to transitional justice and to record best practices. The journal will publish scholarly articles, promote research, carry book reviews, encourage debate and discussion, and organize seminars on all the issues relevant to the field of transitional justice.

title: Participatory Radio as a Means for Community Development in Russia
description: The program goal is to promote processes that strengthen public participation in the development of communities. The Foundation for Independent Radio Broadcasting will continue to strengthen a growing network of participatory community radio stations based in universities across Russia. Specifically, the grantee will provide training and technical support to forge links between university students, faculty, community groups, and local listeners in order to establish independent and progressive information sources in participating communities. New Internet-based technologies will be used to create and share programming among all participating stations. In 2007-2010, the grantee helped develop the technical and editorial capacity of ten university radio stations, involving over 600 student journalists and community representatives. Over 330 podcasts on current and community affairs were created and are accessible to a national audience. The Foundation for Independent Radio Broadcasting has worked in Russia since 1999 to provide training for radio journalists and promote educational programming for Russian audiences.

title: Participatory Radio as a Means for Community Development in Russia
description: The program goal is to promote processes that strengthen public participation in the development of communities. The Foundation for Independent Radio Broadcasting will continue to develop the concept of participatory community radio stations based in universities across Russia. Focusing on a core group of five universities, and engaging less intensively with 12, the grantee will undertake a range of training activities aimed at ensuring a self-sustaining model of local radio stations based within universities but reporting on community realities. Initial efforts will also be made to formalize a network of university-based community radio stations. In 2010-2012, the participating stations produced over 400 podcasts from across the country. The grantee held five intensive training workshops and two national competitions to identify the best stories of the year. The Foundation for Independent Radio Broadcasting has worked in Russia since 1999 to provide training for radio journalists and promote educational programming for Russian audiences.

title: Participatory Radio as a Means for Community Development in Russia
description: The program goal is to promote processes that strengthen public participation in the development of communities. To this end, the Foundation for Independent Radio Broadcasting will continue to develop a network of student community radio stations across Russia. Special attention will be given to fostering the increasingly local character of stations through editorial content and training for community-based curators. In addition, the grantee will work with existing university partners to secure growing institutional support to ensure the future sustainability of the network of stations. In 2012-2014, participating editorial teams submitted almost 140 stories on notable issues and people in their local communities. The reorganization of the project Web site into distinct sections for each local team helped foster both greater identity for each team and increased cross-fertilization of story ideas. The Foundation for Independent Radio Broadcasting has worked in Russia since 1999 to provide training for radio journalists and promote educational programming for Russian audiences.

title: Participatory Radio as a Means for Community Development in Russia
description: The program goal is to promote processes that strengthen public participation in the development of communities. The Foundation for Independent Radio Broadcasting will create a replicable model of participatory community radio stations based in universities across Russia. Specifically, the foundation will provide training and technical support to forge links between Russian university students, faculty, community stakeholders, and local listeners, with the goal of establishing stations that can serve as influential and progressive voices in their communities. New Internet-based technologies will be used to create and share programming among all participating stations. This community radio network will be initiated in nine communities across Russia during the grant period. The grantee has worked in Russia since 1999 to provide training for radio journalists and technicians and to promote educational programming for Russian radio audiences.

title: Assessing the State of Play on Climate Change and Forests
description: Forests have suddenly reappeared in public discourse as one of the critical factors in how humans will mitigate and global ecosystems will adapt to climate change. Recent climate change data has noted that current levels of deforestation are producing levels of greenhouse gas emissions equal to or surpassing those coming from the global transport sector. The current expansion in biofuels could either help solve the global climate change problem or exacerbate it. There is no research and analysis currently available to understand fully whether biofuels will be a blessing or a curse. This grant will provide funding to the Center for International Forestry Research, the preeminent international research center on forest management, to undertake research and analysis on the prospects for reducing greenhouse gas emissions by avoiding deforestation and degradation of forested areas, as well research and analysis on the impacts of biofuel development on forested areas.

title: Property Acquisition/Demolition
description: This grant increase will provide additional funds to support Kettering University’s efforts to remove blighted structures near its campus. Kettering University is participating in a variety of neighborhood redevelopment efforts, including the Hurley Medical Center redevelopment project, the redesign of Third Avenue into University Boulevard, and the development of the outdoor learning space at the Flint Children’s Museum. Removing severely blighted structures adjacent to the campus will contribute to the neighborhood’s redevelopment efforts.

title: Property Acquisition/Demolition
description: This grant increase will provide additional support for Kettering University’s efforts to remove blighted structures near its campus. Kettering University is participating in a variety of neighborhood redevelopment efforts, including the Hurley Medical Center redevelopment project, the redesign of Third Avenue into University Boulevard, and the development of the outdoor learning space at the Flint Children’s Museum. Removing severely blighted structures adjacent to the campus will contribute to the neighborhood’s redevelopment efforts.

title: Property Acquisition/Demolition
description: This grant will provide support for Kettering University’s efforts to remove blighted structures near its campus. Kettering University is participating in a variety of neighborhood redevelopment efforts, including the Hurley Medical Center redevelopment project, the redesign of Third Avenue into University Boulevard, and the development of the Flint Children’s Museum’s outdoor learning space. Removing severely blighted structures adjacent to the campus will contribute to the neighborhood’s redevelopment efforts.

title: Journalism That Matters
description: This grant increase will provide additional support for “Journalism That Matters”, an initiative of the Journalism/Communications department at the University of Massachusetts-Amherst. The overall goal of the initiative is to facilitate critical discussion on the future and sustainability of journalism. Its unique approach is to assemble editors, publishers, academics, entrepreneurs, and independent journalists who focus on defining the ownership, management, location, and sustainability of “next newsroom” prototypes. Additional funds will be used to support a conference on June 4-5, 2008, at the University of Minnesota. The University of Massachusetts-Amherst, the flagship campus of the University of Massachusetts system, was established in 1867 as a land-grant agricultural college.

title: Journalism That Matters
description: This grant will provide partial support for the Journalism That Matters conference which will take place in Washington, D.C., on August 7-8, 2007. The goal of the conference is to facilitate critical discussion on the future and sustainability of journalism. The unique approach of this effort is to assemble editors, publishers, writers, researchers, academics, entrepreneurs, public advocates, independent and “citizen” journalists who will focus on defining the ownership, management, location and sustainability of a “next newsroom” prototype in at least one community in the United States, to launch in early- to mid-2008. The conference is intended to be the start of a long-term effort to nurture the “next newsroom” prototype. As a result, this grant will also support post-conference follow-up efforts, including assisting in developing the support base in the host community, advising on selection of technical and marketing tools and resources, establishing of the desired ownership structure, documenting of start-up efforts (for replication), engaging investors or funders (depending on the ownership format), and assisting in defining staff requirements and recruiting efforts. The University of Massachusetts – Amherst, the flagship campus of the University of Massachusetts system, was established in 1867 as a land-grant agricultural college.

title: Regional Leadership Council
description: The Genesee Area Focus Fund has partnered with a group of community leaders to form the Regional Leadership Council to create a proactive community-building project. The Regional Leadership Council recently completed Phase I, in which it identified key community issues to serve as an action agenda to help improve the social and economic environment of the greater Flint region and recreate the sense of entrepreneurialism which has been central to the history of this region. This grant increase will support Phase II of the Regional Leadership Council.

title: Regional Leadership Council
description: The Genesee Area Focus Fund has partnered with a group of community leaders to form the Regional Leadership Council to create a proactive community-building project. The purpose of the Regional Leadership Council is to identify three or four key community issues that will serve as an action agenda to help improve the quality of life, the social and economic environment of the greater Flint region, and recreate the sense of entrepreneurialism which has been central to the history of this region.

title: Automotive Strategies for Genesee County
description: The Center for Automotive Research will use Mott grant funds to develop a strategy for investing in Genesee County’s automotive assets to render maximum returns to the community in terms of increasing business for its firms and employment for its residents. This research initiative will detail Genesee County’s current automotive assets (companies, products, education, and labor), forecast future automotive trends in markets and technologies over the next ten years, estimate the impact of these trends on Genesee County’s automotive industry, and articulate a strategy for the county to pursue.

title: Global Leadership Consortium
description: The program goal is to galvanize emerging leaders to solve critical global challenges. In 2008, the EastWest Institute created the Global Leadership Consortium, a network of independent policy institutions from around the world. The institute recruited internationally renowned players to participate in the network; convened consortium members to plan their mission, agenda, and action items; and initiated “Global Lens”, an online publication to present an international exchange of views on critical global security events and issues. In the upcoming grant period, the consortium will address human sustainability and security, preventive diplomacy, and global governance through: a monthly online publication, “Global Lens”; researching and developing breakthrough solutions on security issues through the collaborative work of international task forces and working groups; and convening consortium members and other thought leaders. Founded in 1980, EastWest Institute is an international, nonpartisan organization with centers in Brussels, New York, and Moscow.

title: Global Leadership Consortium
description: The program goal is to galvanize emerging leaders and practitioners to solve critical global challenges. To this end, EastWest Institute will create a global network of 24 solutions-oriented leaders who share a vision of working together to create effective approaches to critical global security issues. Through a careful selection process, EastWest Institute will ensure that the Global Leadership Consortium is a genuine partnership of world leaders from across sectors, regions, and institutions. Network members will meet twice a year as a group and will form subnetworks, focused on specific security issue areas. The Global Leadership Consortium’s initial geographic focus will be on Russia, Ukraine, the Balkans, Turkey, and South Africa. Founded in 1980, EastWest Institute is an international, nonpartisan organization with centers in Brussels, New York, and Moscow.

title: Michigan Defining Moment Campaign
description: The Center for Michigan was recently established to create a statewide citizen movement to help improve our economy, fix our dysfunctional politics, and provide reasoned hope for the future. The organization’s first major initiative is the Michigan Defining Moment Campaign. This grant will provide partial funding for the first phase of this civic engagement campaign that will engage 10,000 Michigan residents in creating a new vision for the state.

title: Afterschool Training Toolkit
description: This grant will support the Southwest Educational Development Laboratory in its efforts to ensure broad access among afterschool providers to resources and training that foster the implementation of effective academic enrichment practices. This project will support:1) the development and dissemination of print-based professional development resources that will help afterschool staff integrate academic learning opportunities into their programs; and 2) a series of training events for members of the Mott-funded statewide afterschool networks and others who provide guidance and assistance to afterschool programs. These activities will ensure broad awareness and utilization of research-based practices that can positively impact the academic engagement and performance of afterschool participants.

title: A Meeting of the State Education Agencies
grantee: Council of Chief State School Officers
description: This grant will support the Council of Chief State School Officers in planning and convening the next meeting of the state education agencies that administer the 21st Century Community Learning Centers and the Supplemental Education Services programs. The purpose of this meeting is to give state education agency staff an opportunity to share challenges and effective implementation strategies related to administering afterschool-related programs; to consider potential strategies focused on aligning and coordinating these and other funding streams at the state and local levels; and to network with their peers across states and programs. This meeting will be held in partnership with the United States Department of Education.

title: Improved Financing to Support A New Day for Learning
description: This renewal grant will continue support to Cross & Joftus, LLC in its efforts to inform policymakers, education reform advocates, and program leaders seeking to implement reforms that focus on restructuring time and learning. The work is connected to the Mott-funded report, “A New Day for Learning” and will provide written resources and technical assistance to support the financing of these efforts. Deliverables will include: 1) providing technical assistance to the New Day for Learning sites on financing issues that include providing support on budgeting and reforms to school finance formulas; and 2) exploring ways to reform federal education spending that allow for better coordinating of resources across programs and agencies. Written products and other learning from this work will be shared broadly with the field through electronic media and strategic partnerships with national organizations working to support similar efforts.

title: Improved Financing to Support a New Day for Learning
description: This grant will support Cross & Joftus, LLC in its efforts to provide financial options to policymakers, education reform advocates, and program leaders seeking to implement reforms that focus on restructuring time and learning. This work is connected to the Mott-funded report, “A New Day for Learning”. Deliverables will include: 1) a document on financing approaches and case studies for restructuring time and learning that will support communities to make better use of existing resources; and 2) technical assistance to statewide afterschool networks and others in utilizing these financial approaches. Written products will be shared broadly through electronic media and partnerships with organizations working to support similar efforts.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Upper Karoo Advice and Development Agency
description: The Upper Karoo Advice and Development Agency was established in 2003 to facilitate access to justice for poor and marginalized communities in the Northern Cape province through providing institutional support to community-based advice offices that work in these communities. This grant will assist the Upper Karoo Advice and Development Agency to train and mentor community-based advice offices and paralegals throughout the province to enable them to assist poor and marginalized communities on legal and related social matters. The agency will also advocate for the improvement in the delivery of basic services to poor people and will assist advice offices to initiate sustainable development interventions, particularly economic development projects that advance the interests of poor and marginalized communities.

title: Michigan Fund for Innovation and Entrepreneurship
description: The Michigan Fund for Innovation and Entrepreneurship will be launched by the University of Michigan, in partnership with other state-supported colleges and universities, to help the state of Michigan transition from a manufacturing-based economy to a knowledge-based economy. This renewable fund will have three components that will redefine Michigan’s approach to launching new businesses and industries. The three components are a Gap Fund, a Talent Retention Fund, and an Entrepreneurial Education Fund. Taken together, these funds will launch a new era for concentrated business development and entrepreneurship across the state.

title: Flint River Corridor Alliance Administrative Management
description: With this grant increase and associated grant period extension, the Center for Applied Environmental Research at the University of Michigan-Flint will continue to provide administrative support and organizational capacity building assistance to the Flint River Corridor Alliance.

title: Flint River Corridor Alliance Administrative Management
description: The Center for Applied Environmental Research at the University of Michigan-Flint provides administrative support and capacity-building services to the Flint River Corridor Alliance. The alliance engages partners from government, the private sector, the local community, and nonprofit groups in efforts to revitalize the Flint River and its neighboring communities. With Mott support, the center will provide data management, board development, fundraising and membership assistance, coordination activities, and community outreach services to the alliance to help it meet its goal of reinvigorating the natural and man-made environments along the Flint River.

title: Flint River Corridor Alliance Administrative Management
description: The Center for Applied Environmental Research at the University of Michigan-Flint provides administrative support and capacity building services to the Flint River Corridor Alliance. The alliance engages partners from government, private sector, local community, and nonprofit groups in efforts to revitalize the Flint River and its neighboring communities. With Mott support, the center will provide a range of technical assistance to help the alliance meet its goal of reinvigorating the natural and man-made environments along the Flint River. The center will also continue to assist the alliance with its strategic planning.

title: Flint River Corridor Alliance Administrative Management
description: The Flint River Corridor Alliance is composed of public, private, and nonprofit sector stakeholders interested in the restoration and redevelopment of the area around the Flint River. With support from this grant, the University of Michigan-Flint’s Center for Applied Environmental Research will provide the alliance with organizational development technical assistance and administrative support for one year. The center will provide assistance on issues of board development and governance, database and information management, marketing and communications, membership development, meeting management, fundraising, media relations, and workplan development. The Flint campus of the University of Michigan serves more than 6,500 full- and part-time students seeking undergraduate and graduate degrees. It places a priority on outreach and service to the community.

title: Debt Reduction
grantee: Boy Scouts of America - Port Huron
description: The Boy Scouts of America – Tall Pine Council is one of the largest youth organizations serving Genesee, Lapeer, and Shiawassee counties, and focuses on character development, leadership, physical fitness, and citizenship. In 1999, the council purchased the Camp Sherwood property, which was adjacent to Camp Holaka, from the Detroit Area Girl Scout Council. Although the Boy Scouts of America – Tall Pine Council has sold off adjacent property and paid toward the debt annually, a significant balance remains. Retiring this debt will allow the organization to move forward with significant programmatic increases as a result of no longer needing to divert general operating money to debt service. Of particular interest to the council is increasing its urban scouting and urban classroom programs.

title: Afterschool in California: Fostering Learning Communities
description: This grant will support the California Statewide Afterschool Network in partnership with the Center for Community School Partnerships at the University of California – Davis and the California Department of Education to establish professional learning communities among new and current afterschool programs across the state. Learning communities will engage in a series of facilitated conversations around member-identified issues, as well as issues common to all communities such as collaboration and alignment with the regular day program or implementation of defined programmatic elements. This work is relevant because of the significant increase in afterschool funding available in the state due to the implementation of Proposition 49. It is expected that the professional learning community conversations will give rise to substantial knowledge and subsequent action that will be of statewide and national significance for influencing policy, informing practice, and improving professional development.

title: A Model Development Impact Study
description: Established in 1945, the Michigan Association of Planning is dedicated to promoting comprehensive community planning that includes opportunities for a variety of housing, employment, commercial, cultural, and recreational amenities. This project seeks to bridge the disconnect between land use and transportation planning decisions and provide a new framework for development decisions in Michigan. Support will enable the development, dissemination, and adoption of A Model Development Impact Study ordinance along with a model planning process that integrates land use and transportation planning for meaningful regional cooperation.

title: "Truth in Translation" Flint Residency
description: In 2006, the Mott Foundation made a grant to Colonnades Theatre Lab of South Africa for development of a play about the interpreters who staffed the post-apartheid Truth and Reconciliation Commission. The play, “Truth in Translation”, views South Africa’s past and present through the eyes of these interpreters, who translated testimony before the commission into the nation’s 11 official languages. As part of the production’s United States tour in the summer of 2007, the Flint Cultural Center Corporation will host the theater company for a one-week Flint residency, including free public performances, interactive workshops with community members, South African films screened at the Flint Institute of Arts, and a variety of other activities related to the Midwest premier of “Truth in Translation”.

title: Labor Day Weekend Celebration
description: This grant to Mott Community College will provide partial support for a Labor Day celebration to be held on the Flint Cultural Center campus. The United Auto Workers will host the weekend event titled, “Ordinary People Changing the World”, that will center around the unveiling of a new permanent exhibit honoring the 1936-37 Sit-down Strike in Flint, Michigan. The 44-day strike was the most significant labor event in United States history and the birth of organized labor. Sloan Museum, located on the cultural center campus, will house this exhibit that will capture the story of the 44-day labor strike. In addition to the ribbon-cutting ceremony, a variety of activities are planned to attract area residents of all ages and interests, including a youth basketball tournament, classic car show, lectures, and musical concerts.

title: Genesee Early College
description: This grant will provide partial support for Genesee Early College, a middle early college sponsored by the Genesee Intermediate School District, in partnership with University of Michigan-Flint. The purpose of Genesee Early College is to provide local students from disadvantaged and underrepresented communities the opportunity to complete high school while simultaneously earning up to 60 college credits. Genesee Early College instruction focuses on preparing students for careers in healthcare. It is one of six such programs established in Michigan as a result of planning grants from the Michigan Department of Education.

title: Genesee Early College
description: This renewal grant will provide partial support for Genesee Early College, a middle early college sponsored by the Genesee Intermediate School District, in partnership with the University of Michigan-Flint. The purpose of Genesee Early College is to provide local students from disadvantaged and underrepresented communities the opportunity to complete high school while simultaneously earning up to 60 college credits. Genesee Early College instruction focuses on preparing students for careers in healthcare. It is one of 12 early college programs established in Michigan and one of six Michigan early colleges focused on healthcare as a result of planning grants from the Michigan Department of Education.

title: Genesee Early College
description: This renewal grant will provide partial support for Genesee Early College, an early college sponsored by the Genesee Intermediate School District, in partnership with the University of Michigan-Flint. The purpose of Genesee Early College is to provide local students, with an interest in healthcare-related fields, the opportunity to complete high school while simultaneously earning up to 60 college credits. Genesee Early College is one of 12 early college programs established in Michigan as a result of planning grants from the Michigan Department of Education. With an overall graduation rate of 98.5 percent, Genesee Early College is notable because it is the only early college in Michigan located on the campus of a four-year university.

title: Genesee Early College
description: Genesee Early College is a five-year early college located on the campus of the University of Michigan-Flint and is the only early college in Michigan housed at a four-year institution. The purpose of the early college model is to expose students to college education with the opportunity to earn up to 60 credits at the host college. After four years of operation, Genesee Early College, administered by the Genesee Intermediate School District, has graduated three classes with an average graduation rate of 99 percent. This renewal grant will help fund the operating costs of the early college.

title: Genesee Early College
description: This grant will enable the Genesee Intermediate School District to support key programmatic activities of the Genesee Early College. Currently in its sixth year of implementation, the Genesee Early College is a cutting-edge educational program administered by the grantee in collaboration with the University of Michigan-Flint. The Genesee Early College is an early college high school focused on preparing interested students from Genesee County area high schools for academic and professional careers in health-related fields. After five years of operation, Genesee Early College has graduated four cohorts with an average graduation rate of 99 percent. Recommended support will help fund the operating costs of the Genesee Early College during the 2013-14 school year.

title: Genesee Early College
description: This grant will enable the Genesee Intermediate School District to support the Genesee Early College. Genesee Early College is an Early College High School that operates in collaboration with the University of Michigan-Flint and six major healthcare facilities. The early college recruits students from anywhere in Genesee and Lapeer counties who are capable of succeeding at the university level and have a genuine interest in health- or STEM-related careers. Genesee Early College gives students the opportunity to earn up to 60 transferable college credits and a high school diploma upon completion of high school. This school has graduated five cohorts with more than 95 percent of these students enrolling in a post-secondary institution.

title: Genesee Early College
description: This grant will enable the Genesee Intermediate School District to support the Genesee Early College. Genesee Early College is an innovative educational program administered by the grantee in collaboration with the University of Michigan-Flint and six healthcare partners in the region. The focus of the project is to prepare high school students for academic and professional careers in health-related fields. Genesee Early College students can earn up to 60 transferable college credits, as well as a high school diploma, upon graduation. Foundation support will help fund the operating costs of Genesee Early College during the 2015-2016 school year.

title: Genesee Early College
description: This grant will support the Genesee Early College. Genesee Early College program, an innovative, educational program administered by the Genesee Intermediate School District in collaboration with the University of Michigan-Flint and six healthcare partners in the region. The focus of the project is to prepare high school students for academic and professional careers in health and the science, technology, engineering, and math fields. Students can earn up to 60 transferrable college credits as well as a high school diploma. Faculty will encourage students to enroll in Environmental Justice, a course that focuses on the Flint water crisis and provides youth with a platform to share their thoughts about the crisis on campus and in the community.

title: Genesee Early College
description: Genesee Early College is an innovative, educational program administered by the Genesee Intermediate School District in collaboration with the University of Michigan-Flint and six healthcare partners in the region. The focus of the project is to prepare high school students for academic and professional careers in health and science, technology, engineering, and math fields. Students can earn up to 60 transferable college credits as well as a high school diploma. Faculty will encourage students to enroll in Environmental Justice, a course that focuses on the Flint water crisis from a youth’s perspective.

title: Genesee Early College
description: Genesee Early College is an innovative, educational program administered by the Genesee Intermediate School District in collaboration with the University of Michigan-Flint and six healthcare partners in the region. The focus of the project is to prepare high school students for academic and professional careers in health and science, technology, engineering, and math fields. Students can earn up to 60 transferable college credits as well as a high school diploma and scholarship money for higher education.

title: Genesee Early College
description: Genesee Early College is an innovative, educational program administered by the Genesee Intermediate School District in collaboration with the University of Michigan-Flint and six healthcare partners in the region. The focus of the project is to prepare high school students for academic and professional careers in health and sciences, technology, engineering, and math fields. Students can earn up to 60 transferable college credits, as well as a high school diploma and scholarship money for higher education.

title: Genesee Early College
description: This grant will provide partial support for Genesee Early College, a new middle early college sponsored by the Genesee Intermediate School District, in partnership with the University of Michigan-Flint. The purpose of the Genesee Early College is to provide local students from disadvantaged and underrepresented communities the opportunity to complete high school while simultaneously earning up to 60 college credits. Genesee Early College instruction focuses on preparing students for careers in healthcare. It is one of six such programs being established in Michigan as a result of planning grants from the Michigan Department of Education. The school’s college partner is the University of Michigan-Flint, a four-year degree-granting institution.

title: Institutional Development
description: The project goal is to strengthen the community foundation field in Slovakia.
