During the grant period, the Association of Slovak Community Foundations will strengthen its advocacy and representative role, improve its current services for members, promote community foundations as vehicles for community development in Slovakia, and increase its organizational capacity and financial sustainability. The association was established in 2003 with the mission to develop the community foundation field in Slovakia, strengthen the capacity of its members, and represent Slovak community foundations at national and international levels. Currently, the association has nine members that serve about 35 percent of the territory of Slovakia. In the past two years, the association developed a long-term organizational development strategy, provided learning and networking opportunities to its members, and increased the visibility of the Slovak community foundation field nationally and internationally.

title: Institutional Development
description: The project goal is to strengthen the community foundation field in Slovakia. During the grant period, the Association of Slovak Community Foundations will improve its current services for members, develop new services, promote community foundations as vehicles for community development in Slovakia, and carry out a thorough strategic planning process for the future financial sustainability of the association and its members. The association was established in 2003 with the mission to develop the community foundation field in Slovakia, strengthen the capacity of its members, and represent Slovak community foundations at national and international levels. Currently, the association has 12 members that serve about 40 percent of the territory of Slovakia. Since 1994, when the first Slovak community foundations were established, the association’s members have awarded more than 3,500 grants totaling $1.5 million.

title: Wyoming Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will continue to support the Wyoming Community Foundation in the advancement of the Wyoming Statewide Afterschool Network. This grantee is part of the sixth cohort of Mott-funded, statewide afterschool networks. In addition to continuing its core work building the field of afterschool, the Wyoming Statewide Afterschool Network will: focus on designing a statewide longitudinal research and needs assessment to determine the effectiveness of afterschool programs in the state; continue to ensure that policies related to afterschool are utilized more strategically; and ultimately create a comprehensive policy recommendation for a high quality professional development system of standards and curriculum for the afterschool workforce focused on student outcomes through more efficient use of state and federal funding. Lessons learned and products will be shared with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: Wyoming Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Wyoming Community Foundation which coordinates the Wyoming Statewide Afterschool Network. Its mission is to develop and promote quality school-based, school-linked afterschool environments and programs focused on improving positive outcomes for youth and families. The network is developing a continuum of services and will have the capacity to: 1) compile critical data; 2) raise public awareness; 3) develop key systems around professional development; and 4) provide the state with information on issues relating to the needs of afterschool programs and their providers.

title: Wyoming Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant to the Wyoming Community Foundation will support the Wyoming Statewide Afterschool Network to continue to build an afterschool and summer learning system that improves outcomes for children and youth through school-based or school-linked afterschool programs. Over the next three years, the network will support the development of policy, partnerships, and quality initiatives to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will: 1) develop a communications plan to raise awareness of the network and afterschool and summer learning in Wyoming; 2) create a development plan for the network that increases sustainability; and 3) provide trainings around the state on quality, STEM, and social and emotional learning.

title: Wyoming Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Wyoming Community Foundation, which coordinates the Wyoming Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships, and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) expand pilot projects in areas throughout the state focusing on STEM and career development; 2) develop future leaders and afterschool professionals that are prepared to create and thrive in a new economy through entrepreneurship, careers and leadership; and 3) support the development and distribution of the new afterschool program content in collaboration with the Foundation’s thematic partners.

title: Wyoming Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Wyoming Community Foundation in its efforts to develop the Wyoming Statewide Afterschool Network. Its mission is to support and promote quality school-based and school-linked afterschool environments and programs focused on improving positive outcomes for youth and families. The Wyoming Statewide Afterschool Network is developing a continuum of services and will have the capacity to: 1) compile critical data; 2) raise public awareness; 3) develop key systems around professional development; and 4) provide the state with information on issues relating to the needs of afterschool programs and their providers. This grantee is part of the sixth cohort of Mott-funded statewide afterschool networks.

title: Indiana Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will continue to support the Indiana Association of United Ways in the advancement of the Indiana Statewide Afterschool Network. This grantee is part of the sixth cohort of Mott-funded, statewide afterschool networks. In addition to continuing its core work building the field of afterschool, the Indiana Statewide Afterschool Network will create a sustainable structure of statewide, regional, and local partnerships focused on expanding college/career readiness experiences for K-12 children and youth in afterschool programs. Lessons learned and products will be shared with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: Indiana Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Indiana Association of United Ways, which coordinates the Indiana Statewide Afterschool Network in its efforts to build sustainable afterschool systems that align with and link to education and workforce development. The vision of the network is to establish an infrastructure of support to mobilize community resources on behalf of children, youth, and families. The purpose of the network is to provide both the structure and mechanisms for bringing together a range of stakeholders with a common vision of improving the lives of youth through school- and community-based afterschool programs.

title: Indiana Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant to the Indiana Afterschool Network, Inc., will support the Indiana Statewide Afterschool Network to continue to build an afterschool and summer learning system that improves outcomes for children and youth through school-based or school-linked afterschool programs. Over the next three years, the network will support the development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will: 1) create a communications plan to increase awareness of the need for afterschool programs in Indiana; 2) develop a comprehensive fundraising plan to diversify funding sources for the network; and 3) expand training and resources to support implementation of the Indiana Afterschool Standards.

title: Indiana Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Indiana Afterschool Network, which coordinates the Indiana Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships, and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) increase the connection between afterschool programs and school personnel and practices; 2) formulate and launch a badging system for the afterschool programs; 3) develop new practices to support recruitment and development of afterschool staff; and 4) support the development and distribution of the new afterschool program content in collaboration with the Foundation’s thematic partners.

title: Indiana Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Indiana Association of United Ways in its efforts to develop the Indiana Statewide Afterschool Network. The vision of the Indiana Statewide Afterschool Network is to establish an infrastructure of support to mobilize community resources on behalf of children, youth, and families. The purpose of the network is to provide both the structure and mechanisms for bringing together a range of stakeholders with a common vision of improving the lives of youth through school- and community-based afterschool programs. This grantee is part of the sixth cohort of Mott-funded statewide afterschool networks.

title: Maryland Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will continue to support Baltimore’s Safe & Sound Campaign in the advancement of the Maryland Statewide Afterschool Network. This grantee is part of the sixth cohort of Mott-funded, statewide afterschool networks. In addition to continuing its core work building the field of afterschool, the Maryland Statewide Afterschool Network will: increase participation in the federal at-risk supper and summer meals programs; leverage out-of-school time programs as a portal to identifying and enrolling eligible young people and their families in federal and state benefit programs; and identify, share, and replicate best practices in recruiting and integrating young people with disabilities in afterschool programs. Lessons learned and products will be shared with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: Maryland Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Baltimore’s Safe & Sound Campaign which coordinates the Maryland Statewide Afterschool Network. In addition to continuing the network’s core work to advance afterschool in Maryland, it will complete a multiyear project addressing science, technology, engineering, and math and healthy behaviors. The network seeks to explore and build the intersections of their science, technology, engineering, and math learning focus and healthy behaviors work through innovative and engaging activities in the out-of-school time space. To ensure that new models and best practices are incorporated nationally, the network will share lessons learned and products with the other state networks.

title: Maryland Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant to the Fund for Educational Excellence will support the Maryland Statewide Afterschool Network to continue to build an afterschool and summer learning system that improves outcomes for children and youth through school-based or school-linked afterschool programs. Over the next three years, the network will support the development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will: 1) develop a communications plan to help build on the success of Maryland Youth at 3PM and increase awareness of the need for afterschool programs in Maryland; 2) develop a plan to diversify funding sources for the network; and 3) provide training, resources, and mentoring to afterschool programs.

title: Maryland Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase to the Fund for Educational Excellence will support the Maryland Statewide Afterschool Network in hosting an institute focused on afterschool STEM for statewide afterschool networks and partners. The institute will provide participants an opportunity to share best practices and emerging models, while working with national experts at the forefront of afterschool and summer STEM programming.

title: Maryland Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Fund for Educational Excellence, which coordinates the Maryland Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships, and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) partner with the Governor’s Office on Service & Volunteerism to pilot a new afterschool volunteer recruitment strategy; 2) facilitate a learning community focused on equity and inclusion for afterschool professionals; 3) refine and enhance communications strategies for the network; and 4) support the development and distribution of the new afterschool program content in collaboration with the Foundation’s thematic partners.

title: Maryland Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Baltimore’s Safe & Sound Campaign in its efforts to develop the Maryland Statewide Afterschool Network. The purpose of the network is to maximize statewide efficiency by increasing the number of afterschool opportunities for children and improving the quality of these programs. The network will seek to collaborate with local and regional initiatives currently under way, with the goal of unifying these efforts and avoiding any duplication.

title: Kentucky Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Ohio Valley Educational Cooperative in its efforts to continue to develop the Kentucky Statewide Afterschool Network. Through the statewide afterschool network, afterschool programs in Kentucky will have access to research-based, best practices and will help ensure that children will have access to the supports they need to succeed. The Kentucky Statewide Afterschool Network will systematically organize, mobilize, and communicate with afterschool stakeholders to advocate for increased funding and support for afterschool programs at the local, state, and national levels. This grantee is part of the sixth cohort of Mott-funded, statewide afterschool networks.

title: Kentucky Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will continue to support the Ohio Valley Educational Cooperative in the advancement of the Kentucky Statewide Afterschool Network. This grantee is part of the sixth cohort of Mott-funded, statewide afterschool networks. In addition to continuing its core work building the field of afterschool, the Kentucky Statewide Afterschool Network will increase the quality of afterschool services for children and youth through the development and implementation of a Kentucky School-Age Quality Framework. The Kentucky School-Age Quality Framework will include the following components: program standards, core competencies, a school-age credential, trainer/training information resources, school-age regulation modifications, and accreditation and quality rating systems. Lessons learned and products will be shared with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: Kentucky Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Ohio Valley Educational Cooperative which coordinates the Kentucky Statewide Afterschool Network. Through the statewide afterschool network, afterschool programs in Kentucky will have access to research-based best practices and will help ensure that children will receive the supports they need to succeed academically and socially. Statewide afterschool network partners are committed to the goals of providing safe and interesting learning environments, addressing achievement gaps, raising academic performance, and enhancing the development of youth to enable the success of Kentucky’s children and to prepare them to graduate from college and be career-ready.

title: Kentucky Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant to Save the Children will support the development of the Kentucky Statewide Afterschool Network to continue to build an afterschool and summer learning system that improves outcomes for children and youth through school-based or school-linked afterschool programs. Over the next three years, the network will support the development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) develop a communications plan to raise awareness of the network and out-of-school time programs in Kentucky; 2) develop a new financing plan to increase support for the network; and 3) host regional Afterschool Super-Summits to provide training for out-of-school time professionals.

title: Kentucky Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Save the Children Federation, which coordinates the Kentucky Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships, and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) develop a comprehensive communications plan about the importance of afterschool; 2) provide support to community coalitions aimed at boosting education priorities through afterschool programs; 3) develop a community of practice for afterschool programs from various organizations; and 4) support the development and distribution of the new afterschool program content in collaboration with the Foundation’s thematic partners.

title: Kentucky Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Kentucky Child Now! in its efforts to develop the Kentucky Statewide Afterschool Network. Through the statewide afterschool network, afterschool programs in Kentucky will have access to research-based best practices and will help ensure that children will have access to the supports they need to succeed. Statewide afterschool network partners are committed to the goals of providing safe and interesting learning environments, addressing achievement gaps, raising academic performance, and enhancing the development of youth to enable the success of Kentucky’s children. This grantee is part of the sixth cohort of Mott-funded statewide afterschool networks.

title: New Jersey Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will continue to support the New Jersey School-Age Care Coalition in the advancement of the New Jersey Statewide Afterschool Network. This grantee is part of the sixth cohort of Mott-funded, statewide afterschool networks. In addition to continuing its core work building the field of afterschool, the New Jersey Statewide Afterschool Network will continue to build effective partnerships and develop policy support for afterschool by redefining their afterschool programming to reflect Expanded Learning Opportunity principles and developing a set of standards (the Program Quality Standards). Lessons learned and products will be shared with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: New Jersey Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the New Jersey School-Age Care Coalition which coordinates the New Jersey Statewide Afterschool Network. Through the network, the grantee intends to strengthen links among policymakers, funders, practitioners, and consumers to facilitate effective planning and efficient implementation of a coordinated system of high quality afterschool programs for children throughout New Jersey. Over the next three years, the network will continue to increase support for and awareness of afterschool programs and provide leadership and professional development activities, including training in the area of common core standards. This grantee is part of the sixth cohort of Mott-funded, statewide afterschool networks.

title: New Jersey Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant to the New Jersey School-Age Care Coalition will support the New Jersey Statewide Afterschool Network to continue to build an afterschool and summer learning system that improves outcomes for children and youth through school-based or school-linked afterschool programs. Over the next three years, the network will support the development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) conducting a thorough communications assessment and developing improved communications assets about the network and afterschool in New Jersey; 2) supporting afterschool system-building work in Newark, Trenton, and Bridgeton to expand access to programs; and 3) developing and implementing new training on social emotional learning for afterschool providers.

title: New Jersey Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the New Jersey School-Age Care Coalition, which coordinates the New Jersey Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships, and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) engage New Jersey’s Afterschool Ambassadors Alumni to foster champions; 2) survey the afterschool field on the New Jersey Quality Standards for Afterschool to inform new quality and policy initiatives; 3) build the capacity, leadership and quality across New Jersey’s afterschool sector; and 4) support the development and distribution of the new afterschool program content in collaboration with the Foundation’s thematic partners.

title: New Jersey Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the New Jersey School-Age Care Coalition in its efforts to develop the New Jersey Statewide Afterschool Network. Through the network, the grantee intends to strengthen the existing linkages among policymakers, funders, practitioners, and consumers to facilitate effective planning and efficient implementation of a highly coordinated system of services for all children in afterschool programs throughout New Jersey. Over the next three years, the grantee will commit various resources to advance the afterschool needs of youth through a public awareness campaign that will provide opportunities for policymakers to invest additional resources into quality afterschool programs. This grantee is part of the sixth cohort of Mott-funded statewide afterschool networks.

title: Kosovo Task Force
description: The project goal is to support Kosovar government and civil society institutions to address challenges associated with the resolution of Kosovo’s political status. In the period leading up to and immediately following determination of Kosovo’s status, Kosovar leaders will need to draw on internal and external resources and experience to meet pressing needs requiring urgent and sophisticated responses. The Kosovo Task Force will include civil society leaders and government representatives and will work with the government to access relevant international expertise, develop an effective communications and public outreach strategy, and organize an international donors’ conference. The task force will liaise with international experts, maintain contact with local community leaders, and support specific projects that engage the public in decisionmaking on issues facing Kosovo. Based in New York but with extensive experience in Kosovo, the East-West Management Institute will manage and coordinate the task force, including securing funding for the task force’s work.

title: Promising Practices in Afterschool: Global Literacy
description: This renewal grant will continue to support Asia Society in its efforts to raise awareness, build capacity, and stimulate new opportunities to integrate global literacy into afterschool initiatives. The grantee will work closely with leading states and consultants to develop tools, materials, and training opportunities to add to the afterschool field. Specifically, this project will foster working partnerships among states with strong afterschool networks and professional development models, and strengthen school and afterschool connections by bringing state afterschool teams together with state education policymakers and school practitioners for the Partnership for Global Learning conference.

title: Promising Practices in Afterschool: Global Literacy
description: This renewal grant will continue to support Asia Society in its efforts to raise awareness, build capacity, and stimulate new opportunities to integrate global literacy into afterschool initiatives. The overall goals of the project are to increase the quality and quantity of global learning in afterschool programs and enable collaboration between schools, afterschool programs, and community organizations to realize a new definition of student success in the 21st century. Specifically, the grantee will work closely with leading statewide afterschool networks and experts to further develop tools, materials and training opportunities to add to the afterschool field. In addition, Asia Society’s International Studies Schools Network of secondary schools, afterschool experts, and national advisors will develop a planning process to align school-day curriculum and afterschool experiential learning to help youth achieve global competence.

title: Promising Practices in Afterschool: Global Literacy
description: This renewal grant will continue to support Asia Society in its efforts to raise awareness, build capacity, and stimulate new opportunities to integrate global learning into afterschool initiatives. This project will enable collaboration between schools, afterschool programs, and community organizations to advance global learning in various education settings as a way to produce globally competent and college-ready graduates. Specifically, the grantee will work closely with leading statewide afterschool networks to: 1) increase the quality and quantity of global learning in afterschool programs; and 2) increase systemic supports for global learning in afterschool through the development of supportive policies at the local, state, and federal levels, and increase public awareness.

title: International Approaches and 21st Century Competencies
description: This renewal grant will continue to support Asia Society in its efforts to raise awareness, build capacity, and stimulate new opportunities to integrate global literacy into afterschool initiatives. The overall goals of the project are to inform afterschool and expanded learning policy and practice with lessons learned from high performing education systems in other countries, and as a result, to realize a new definition of student success in the 21st century. This project will include international research, work with the statewide afterschool networks and the grantee’s Global Cities Education Network, and the development of recommendations of international best practices to align school-day curriculum and afterschool experiential learning to help youth achieve global competence.

title: International Approaches and 21st Century Competencies
description: This renewal grant will continue to support Asia Society in its efforts to raise awareness, build capacity, and stimulate new opportunities to integrate global learning into afterschool and summer learning programs. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) share national and international best practices in education with the afterschool field with a focus on social and emotional learning and workforce readiness; and 2) provide technical assistance to the statewide afterschool networks to support program outcomes related to 21st century competencies, workforce development, and civic engagement.

title: Promising Practices in Afterschool: Global Literacy
description: This grant will support the Asia Society in its efforts to raise awareness, build capacity, and stimulate new initiatives in integrating global literacy into afterschool programs. The Asia Society will identify an advisory group to help collect, promote, and disseminate promising practices for the afterschool field. To ensure that afterschool stakeholders have access to this information, a print guide, video, and companion Web site will provide concrete examples and steps on how to successfully plan and integrate global literacy in both existing and newly established afterschool and summer programs.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant continues support to the After-School All-Stars to strengthen its organization and expand its programs into a greater number of communities. The mission of the After-School All-Stars is to provide comprehensive afterschool programs for at-risk, middle school students to keep them safe and help them achieve in school and in life. This grant will help the After-School All-Stars support its affiliated chapters with programs, products, and services, increasing the quality and sustainability of their programs.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant continues support to the After-School All-Stars to strengthen the organization and build capacity to better serve the entire afterschool field. The mission of the After-School All-Stars is to provide comprehensive afterschool programs for at-risk, middle school students to keep them safe and help them achieve in school and in life. This grant will help the After-School All-Stars enhance program quality and staff training, best practice sharing, program evaluation, and national office capacity.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant continues support to the After-School All-Stars to strengthen its organization and expand its programs into a greater number of communities. The mission of the After-School All-Stars is to provide comprehensive afterschool programs for at-risk, middle school students to keep them safe and help them achieve in school and in life. This grant will help the grantee support its affiliated chapters with program evaluation, staff training, professional development, chapter technical assistance, advocacy, and knowledge-sharing with peer and partner organizations to increase the quality and sustainability of their programs.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant increase will enable representatives from the After-School All-Stars and statewide afterschool networks to participate in a summit on afterschool convened by the University of Southern California’s Schwarzenegger Institute to raise awareness of the importance of afterschool programs. The summit will include leaders from education, afterschool, government, business, and nonprofit sectors from throughout the United States.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant continues support to the After-School All-Stars to strengthen their chapters and continue to drive quality afterschool programming across the country. The grantee’s mission is to provide comprehensive afterschool programs for at-risk, middle school students to keep them safe and help them achieve in school and in life. This grant will help the grantee to support its affiliated chapters with staff training, professional development, chapter technical assistance, and knowledge-sharing with peer and partner organizations to increase the quality and sustainability of their programs.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support the After-School All-Stars to continue to drive quality afterschool programming across the country. The mission of the grantee is to provide comprehensive afterschool programs for at-risk middle school students to keep them safe and help them achieve in school and in life. This grant will help the grantee to: 1) support its affiliated chapters with staff training, professional development, and quality improvement; and 2) engage leaders in the afterschool field to assist in developing new program curricula, resources and innovative projects to increase the quality and sustainability of afterschool programs.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides support to the After-School All-Stars to strengthen its organization and expand its programs into a greater number of communities. The mission of the After-School All-Stars is to provide comprehensive afterschool programs for at-risk middle school students that keep children safe and help them achieve in school and in life. This grant will help the After-School All-Stars support its affiliated chapters with programs, products, and services, increasing the quality and sustainability of their programs.

title: Effective School-Community Partnerships
description: This grant increase supports New Visions for Public Schools in its efforts to better study and document extended learning opportunities and develop multischool, multipartner strategies to enable an entire community to align existing and new resources around graduating more students prepared to succeed in careers or college. This grant increase will allow the grantee to support a third implementation site in the “A New Day for College and Career Readiness Campaign.” Adding an additional site will enhance study efforts focused on increasing student achievement through strong community partnerships and extended learning opportunities and create tools that will help advance local efforts to increase student achievement. This work will help to advance the Mott-funded report, “A New Day for Learning”, which examines the opportunity that afterschool provides to make the case for increased collaboration between sectors to support children and youth.

title: Effective School-Community Partnerships
description: This grant will allow New Visions for Public Schools to better study and document extended learning opportunities and develop multischool, multipartner strategies to enable an entire community to align existing and new resources around graduating more students prepared to succeed in careers or college. Through a partnership with Policy Studies Associates, New Visions for Public Schools will: 1) research and develop case studies that examine current efforts focused on increasing student achievement through strong community partnerships and extended learning opportunities; and 2) create tools that will help advance local efforts to increase student achievement. This work will help to advance the Mott-funded report, “A New Day for Learning”, which examines the opportunity that afterschool provides to make the case for increased collaboration between sectors to support children and youth.

title: Next Generation of Accountability for Out-of-School Education
description: This grant will provide continued support to Education Sector in its efforts to identify and analyze accountability-related innovations currently being used in afterschool and nontraditional educational settings. This phase of the work will break down many of the barriers to an integrated accountability system, help establish a common language among stakeholders on opposing sides of the debate, explore the use of technology to enable a more seamless integration of learning opportunities, and engage opposing sides to determine shared goals and identify specific accountability strategies that will lead to the best student outcomes. The goal of this effort is to overcome the conceptual and political obstacles to make progress toward a broader accountability system that accounts for and creates greater integration among schools, youth development programs, and other social service providers.

title: Next Generation of Accountability for Out-of-School Education
description: This grant will provide continued support to Education Sector in its efforts to examine a variety of approaches to integrating school-based learning with out-of-school time resources and supports, and analyze the governance, finance, and staffing challenges inherent in connecting schools with community partners. Specifically, this project will: 1) produce a policy research report on staffing for in-and out-of-school learning; 2) conduct an exploratory project to understand the role of community support/resistance in district turnaround decisions; and 3) engage in a targeted effort to share current policy recommendations on shared accountability, assessment, data integration, and expanded learning opportunities. This work will result in lessons and recommendations for states, cities, and communities around the country that are working to strengthen their capacity to improve outcomes for their neediest children.

title: Next Generation of Accountability for Out-of-School Education
description: This grant will support Education Sector in its efforts to identify and analyze accountability-related innovations currently being used in afterschool and nontraditional educational settings. The report produced from this research will: 1) examine how these strategies work in practice, the tools’ benefits and drawbacks, and the feasibility of bringing such innovations to a broader scale in traditional public school systems; and 2) propose a series of questions for educators and policymakers to consider as they try to develop an accountability system that will offer a more complete picture of how our students are gaining the competence they need to succeed in life. Additionally, through three events, Education Sector will start cross-sector dialogues that will enable growth in a broader definition and assessment of student learning and develop actionable next steps in creating a more comprehensive accountability system.

title: Technical Assistance on Land Use and Growth Management
description: Throughout the United States, and especially here in Michigan, there is an intensifying pattern of unequal economic competition among local jurisdictions accompanied by inefficient, environmentally damaging land use and development practices that threaten every community. The increasing geographic income stratification, which has already had devastating consequences for poor and minority communities, has begun to curtail educational and job opportunities and the quality of life for working and middle class families, especially those in first-ring suburbs. Ameregis has documented these trends, and will provide technical assistance to Michigan-based grantees working on growth management and urban revitalization.

title: Creating Lasting Change for Children in New Orleans
description: This grant will support Save the Children in continuing to provide mental health programs to Hurricane Katrina-affected children in New Orleans. The grant will also extend psychosocial services to additional children as they return to the city and struggle to adjust to the post-Katrina environment. In addition, the grantee will pilot a new afterschool program, primarily designed to improve resilience in young people. To improve program sustainability, Save the Children partners with local communities and school districts to implement its programs during the school day and after school hours.

title: Summer Programs in New Orleans
description: This grant will support Save the Children’s summer programs in New Orleans and community development work in transitional housing sites. Transitional housing sites are temporary trailer park homes for families who lost their homes during Hurricane Katrina. By supporting 11 summer programs for children in southeast Louisiana, Save the Children is helping community-based organizations provide safe, enriching environments for over 8,000 children and helping working parents ensure their children are cared for during the day when school is not available. Save the Children will also bring their Safe and Protective Communities Project to Louisiana, which helps residents build a sense of community and empowers them to increase safety for children, raise community awareness, and identify solutions to community problems.

title: Improving Outcomes for Out-of-School Youth in Michigan
description: Through this grant, the Grand Rapids Community Foundation will work to improve policy and practice to prevent young people from dropping out of school, provide multiple pathways for graduation, re-engage those who have already left school, and encourage support for such youth toward a post-secondary experience and/or entry into the labor market. Grand Rapids is one of three citywide partnership sites participating in the Improving Outcomes for Out-of-School Youth in Michigan project.

title: Improving Outcomes for Out-of-School Youth in Michigan
description: This grant will enable the Kalamazoo Community Foundation to continue to support a countywide partnership aimed at improving the educational supports and opportunities for out-of-school youth. Through this project, the grantee has led and convened a partnership of stakeholders in building a framework that addresses the issue of dropouts and disconnected youth in Kalamazoo. During the next stage of this project, the grantee will deepen its work and continue to develop partnerships with key stakeholders to reconnect dropouts to education and/or career training opportunities.

title: Improving Outcomes for Out-of-School Youth in Michigan
description: This grant will enable the Kalamazoo Community Foundation to continue to support a countywide partnership aimed at improving the educational supports and opportunities for out-of-school youth. Through this project, the grantee has led and convened a partnership of stakeholders in developing an infrastructure that identifies dropouts and assists them in connecting to existing education and/or career training opportunities. During the next stage of this project, the grantee will deepen its work by exploring new alternative education pathways and designs and engaging new stakeholders in building public support to improve educational opportunities for students.

title: Improving Outcomes for Out-of-School Youth in Michigan
description: Through this grant, the Kalamazoo Community Foundation will work to improve policy and practice to prevent young people from dropping out of school, re-engage those who have already left school, and encourage support for such youth toward a successful, post-secondary experience and/or entry into the labor market. Kalamazoo is one of three citywide partnership sites participating in the Improving Outcomes for Out-of-School Youth in Michigan project.

title: Improving Outcomes for Out-of-School Youth in Michigan
description: This increase will enable City Connect Detroit to participate in a national learning network on expanding education options for out-of-school youth. Detroit is one of three citywide partnership sites participating in the Improving Outcomes for Out-of-School Youth in Michigan project. This increase will help cover travel costs to attend national learning network meetings. The increase will also allow the grantee to include youth in planning activities for the project.

title: Improving Outcomes for Out-of-School Youth in Michigan
description: This grant will enable City Connect Detroit to continue to support a citywide partnership aimed at improving the educational supports and opportunities for out-of-school youth. Through this project, the grantee has led and convened a partnership of stakeholders in building a framework that addresses the issue of dropouts and disconnected youth in Detroit. During the next stage of this project, the grantee will deepen its work and continue to develop partnerships with key stakeholders in building local capacity to develop and implement strategies that ensure out-of-school youth have a chance to earn a diploma.

title: Improving Outcomes for Out-of-School Youth in Michigan
description: Through this grant, City Connect Detroit will work to improve policy and practice to prevent young people from dropping out of school, re-engage out-of-school youth, and encourage support for such youth toward a successful, post-secondary experience and/or entry into the labor market. Detroit is one of three citywide partnership sites participating in the Improving Outcomes for Out-of-School Youth in Michigan project.

title: Labor Market, Economic, Social, Civic, and Fiscal Consequences of Dropping Out of High School in Michigan
description: This grant will enable the Center for Labor Market Studies at Northeastern University to further analyze the social and economic consequences of students failing to complete school in Michigan. During the most recent phase of this project, the center analyzed the links between the educational attainment of adults in Michigan and an array of labor market indicators. In addition to deepening the analysis on the fiscal and economic costs that Michigan incurs due to completion and graduation issues, the center will also examine state and local efforts that address the labor market difficulties of youth between the ages of 16-24 in the United States.

title: Labor Market, Economic, Social, Civic, and Fiscal Consequences of Dropping Out of High School in Michigan
description: This grant will enable the Center for Labor Market Studies at Northeastern University to assess and study the fiscal and economic costs of students failing to complete school in Michigan. Through this project, the center will analyze the links between the educational attainment of adults in Michigan and an array of labor market indicators and focus on the federal, state, and local fiscal consequences of high school dropouts in Michigan with comparisons for the nation. The center will also place special research emphasis on the cities of Flint, Detroit, Grand Rapids, and Kalamazoo.

title: Moving Ideas to Market Initiative
description: This renewal grant will support the beginning stages of the implementation process resulting from the last grant period’s planning activities. Prima Civitas Foundation began the Moving Ideas to Market Initiative to create incentives, visions, and an action plan for mid-Michigan’s higher education institutions to collaborate around commercialization and entrepreneurship. To further this initiative, the grantee has created five action teams that will focus on: 1) K-12 entrepreneurship education; 2) post-secondary entrepreneurship education; 3) growth of early-stage ideas and businesses; 4) university-industry partnerships; and 5) Web-based social networking and resources. The end goal is integrated strategies that will accelerate change and innovation.

title: Moving Ideas to Market Initiative
description: This grant will enable the Mid-Michigan Innovation Team, a project of the Prima Civitas Foundation, and its partners to take the lead in coordinating a series of regional activities that could serve as statewide pilots, to facilitate broad-based understanding and dialogue around academia’s role as a commercialization engine for an economically distressed region. In addition, this initiative will identify exemplary practices that will help a broader base of students, entrepreneurs, and potential investors to share in the largess that academic systems can offer business innovators.

title: Moving Ideas to Market Initiative
description: This grant increase will allow the Prima Civitas Foundation to engage CBS Radio via WWJ Newsradio 950 to implement, in several significant ways, the Igniting Innovation in Michigan project featuring the Moving Ideas to Market Initiative. WWJ Newsradio 950 will work with the grantee to create a series of Moving Ideas to Market vignettes beginning in June that would air on several Detroit area and other statewide stations. In addition, Moving Ideas to Market will be a key component in a one-day expo this fall that will feature breakout sessions, networking, entrepreneurial key speakers, and entrepreneurial support organization presentations.

title: Moving Ideas to Market Initiative
description: This grant will enable the Prima Civitas Foundation, and its partners, to take the lead in coordinating a series of regional activities that will facilitate a broad-based understanding and dialogue around academia’s role as a commercialization engine for an economically distressed region. This initiative has identified exemplary practices that have helped a broader base of students, entrepreneurs, and potential investors to share in the largess that academic systems can offer business innovators.

title: Moving Ideas to Market Initiative
description: This grant will enable the Mid-Michigan Innovation Team, a project of the Prima Civitas Foundation and its partners, to take the lead in coordinating a series of regional activities that could serve as a statewide pilot to energize entrepreneurial talent in mid-Michigan and across the state at the K-12 and post-secondary levels. In addition, this initiative will identify exemplary practices that will help a broader base of students, entrepreneurs, and potential investors to share in the returns that academic systems can offer business innovators.

title: Moving Ideas to Market Initiative
description: This grant will enable the Innovation and Entrepreneurship team of the Prima Civitas Foundation to design and pilot a series of programs to advance and showcase entrepreneurial culture and best practices within four sectors of the entrepreneurship ecosystem: K-12 school systems, community colleges, international and immigrant entrepreneurs, and new and emerging industries. This project represents a new phase in the work of the Moving Ideas to Market initiative, which has spent the past six years building the capacity of economic and workforce development service providers to support entrepreneurial activity. The next phase will emphasize identifying, demonstrating, and disseminating best practices in entrepreneurship education and supportive services, with the intention of spurring replication projects across the state.

title: Higher Education and Commercialization Opportunities
description: This grant will enable the Mid-Michigan Innovation Team, a project of the Prima Civitas Foundation, and its partners to take the lead in coordinating a series of regional activities that could serve as statewide pilots, to facilitate broad-based understanding and dialogue around academia’s role as a commercialization engine. In addition, this initiative will identify exemplary practices that will help a broader base of students, entrepreneurs, and potential investors to share in the largess that academic systems can offer business innovators.

title: Hydrocarbons Program
description: This grant increase will provide support to consolidate Oxfam America’s work on oil and gas extraction in Peru, with a particular focus on policy change within international financial institutions, corporations, and governments. The grantee will work to ensure that communities affected by projects, such as the Camisea gas project in Peru, will have the capacity and support to ensure that such projects contribute to their sustainable development. Oxfam America was founded in 1970 to work to end global poverty through saving lives, strengthening communities, and campaigning for policy change. The organization works at the global level to address social injustice through its policy advocacy, public education and research, and emergency assistance programs.

title: Hydrocarbons Program
description: This grant will provide support to consolidate and expand Oxfam America’s work on oil and gas extraction, with a particular focus on policy change within international financial institutions, corporations, and governments. Oxfam America will work to ensure that communities affected by projects, such as the Camisea oil and gas project in Peru, will have the capacity and support to ensure that such projects contribute to their sustainable development. Oxfam America was founded in 1970 to work to end global poverty through saving lives, strengthening communities, and campaigning for policy change. Oxfam America helps people gain the skills to change their future. It also works at the global level to address social injustice through its policy advocacy, public education and research, and emergency assistance programs.

title: National Commission on Adult Literacy
grantee: Council for Advancement of Adult Literacy
description: This grant will provide renewal support to the Council for Advancement of Adult Literacy for the second phase of the National Commission on Adult Literacy. Over the course of two years, this prestigious group of business, political, philanthropic, and education leaders studied the challenges of adult education and workforce development facing the nation. On June 26, 2008, the commission released a final report with recommendations to achieve the goal of serving 20 million adults annually by the year 2020. Phase two of the project will begin implementation of the commission’s recommendations by convening workshops, undertaking research and analysis, and pursuing a communications strategy. Established in 2001, the grantee organization is an independent, national public charity dedicated to transforming the nation’s adult education enterprise into an adult education and workforce skills system that meets the needs of the 21st century.

title: National Commission on Adult Literacy
grantee: Council for Advancement of Adult Literacy
description: This grant will provide partial support for the National Commission on Adult Literacy administered by the Council for Advancement of Adult Literacy. Demographic evidence and workforce trends indicate that the adult education and literacy system needs fundamental reforming and redirection so that, on a scale unprecedented in history, adults aged 16 to 64 can obtain high quality service needed for jobs and life in 21st century America. Launched in July 2006, the commission is the most important, influential assemblage of national leaders ever to convene for an extended period of time to plan for the future of adult education and literacy in this country. The commission is expected to recommend dramatic changes in the purposes and structure of adult education and literacy as a core part of the solution to America’s highest priority problems. An extensive messaging and dissemination campaign will promote a final report to be issued in mid-2008. The Council for Advancement of Adult Literacy is an independent public charity formed in 2001 to help move the adult education and literacy system from the margins to the mainstream of American education.

title: Encouraging Development of Non-Governmental Organizations in Belarus
grantee: Association for International Education and Exchange
description: The program goal is to support civil society development in Belarus by strengthening Belarusian nongovernmental organizations. The grantee, a German nonprofit organization with extensive experience in Belarus, will work with United Way Belarus, the country’s leading support center for nonprofit organizations, to provide a range of Internet-based information and capacity-building resources. They will also provide an array of training and consulting services to Belarusian civil society groups. Registered in 1990, the Association for International Education and Exchange jointly owns, with the Minsk city administration, a facility in Minsk that is used for meetings bringing together civil society organizations, business people, and government officials. Since 2001, it has managed the German government-financed Belarus Support Program, a small grants program fostering civil society partnerships between Germany and Belarus.

title: Encouraging Development of Non-Governmental Organizations in Belarus
grantee: Association for International Education and Exchange
description: The program goal is to support civil society development in Belarus by strengthening Belarusian nongovernmental organizations. The Association for International Education and Exchange, a German nonprofit organization with experience in Belarus, will work with United Way Belarus, the country’s leading support center for nonprofit organizations, to provide a range of Internet-based information and capacity building resources. The grantee and its partner will also provide an array of training and consulting services to Belarusian civil society groups. In 2010-2012, the grantee supported United Way Belarus in its efforts to continue development and operation of its Internet portal for Belarusian civil society (www.ngo.by). Overall usage increased fourfold, and usage from outside Minsk — where there has always been a lack of relevant legal, financial, and programmatic information for nongovernmental organizations — increased by over 50 percent. Registered in 1990, the grantee, together with the Minsk city administration, own a facility in Minsk that is used for meetings that bring together civil society organizations, business people, and government officials. Since 2001, it has managed the German government-financed Belarus Support Program, a small-grants program fostering civil society partnerships between Germany and Belarus.

title: Encouraging Development of Non-Governmental Organizations in Belarus
grantee: Association for International Education and Exchange
description: The program goal is to support civil society development in Belarus. The Association for International Education and Exchange, a German nonprofit organization with extensive experience in Belarus, will work with United Way Belarus, the country’s leading support center for nonprofit organizations, to provide a range of online and offline information and capacity building resources to civil society groups. In 2012-2014, the grantee supported United Way Belarus in its efforts to continue improvement of its Internet portal for Belarusian civil society. The portal saw an increase in monthly users of 25 percent throughout 2013 to over 35,000 monthly users. The online/offline legal training program produced a cohort of alumni who have gone on to provide further pro bono consulting for Belarusian nonprofits. The grantee, registered in 1990, owns jointly with the Minsk city administration a facility there that is used for meetings bringing together civil society, business, and government representatives. Since 2001, it has managed the German government-financed Belarus Support Program, a small-grants program fostering civil society partnerships between Germany and Belarus.

title: Encouraging Development of Non-Governmental Organizations in Belarus
grantee: Association for International Education and Exchange
description: The program goal is to support civil society development in Belarus. The Association for International Education and Exchange, a German nonprofit organization with lengthy experience in Belarus, will work with United Way Belarus, the country’s leading support center for nonprofit organizations, to provide a range of online and offline information and capacity-building resources to civil society groups. In 2014-2016, the grantee supported United Way Belarus in its efforts to continue improvement of its Internet portal for Belarusian civil society. The portal consolidated its level of regular usage to over 35,000 monthly users. United Way Belarus increased its own international profile, which in turn provided new funding and partnership opportunities for its client organizations. Registered in 1990, the grantee owns jointly with the Minsk city administration a facility there that is used for meetings bringing together civil society, business, and government representatives. Since 2001, the grantee has managed the German government-financed Belarus Support Program, a small-grants program fostering civil society partnerships between Germany and Belarus.

title: Encouraging Development of Non-Governmental Organizations in Belarus
grantee: Association for International Education and Exchange
description: The program goal is to support civil society development in Belarus by building the capacity of Belarusian nongovernmental organizations. The grantee, a German nonprofit organization with more than ten years’ experience supporting civil society in Belarus, will work in partnership with United Way Belarus, the country’s leading support center for nonprofit organizations. The program will include the provision of a wide array of informational, training, and consulting services to Belarusian civil society groups. The Association for International Education and Exchange, registered in 1990, and the Minsk city administration own the IBB-Minsk Center, a social and conference facility in Minsk. Since 2001, it has managed the German government-financed Support Program for Belarus, a small grants program fostering civil society partnerships between Germany and Belarus.

title: Developing Corporate Social Responsibility in Ukraine
description: The program goal is to promote corporate philanthropy at the local level in Ukraine. The Princes-Benefactors Ostrozkiy Foundation will work in no fewer than five regions to link local charitable organizations with local business and media partners to increase philanthropic activity in these regions. Regular media events, roundtable discussions, and philanthropy forums will be held in each participating region. In addition, the grantee will provide training support to local organizations to build their marketing and fundraising capacities. A regular series of publications and promotional materials will also be developed in support of local initiatives. Local competitions for most effective media coverage of philanthropic activities will be staged, as will a “Top Philanthropist” contest for local donors from participating regions. Founded in 1995, the mission of the Princes-Benefactors Ostrozkiy Foundation is to support regional charitable organizations and socially disadvantaged people by providing information, consultations, and technical and financial assistance.

title: Case Studies on Youth Organizing for Education Reform
description: Research for Action is a nonprofit organization founded in 1992 to conduct education research and evaluation with an emphasis on civic engagement and community outreach. Research for Action works with school districts, educational institutions, and community organizations to improve the educational opportunities for poor and disabled students. The grantee has studied the ways in which youth-led organizations have engaged in education reform, built leadership and power, and collaborated with other organizations and allies. The primary purpose of this project is to document that learning by publishing an academic case study on youth-led education organizing in Philadelphia.

title: General Purposes
description: The South End Museum Trust was established to commemorate the forced removal of people of color from the South End in Port Elizabeth in the Eastern Cape during the apartheid period. The museum was started by volunteers and community members, many of them former residents with very little expertise in museums, especially museums of conscience. Mott provided a planning grant to the trust to bring a consultant on board to assess its strengths and weaknesses, develop a work plan on its capacity needs, make recommendations on how to secure its long-term sustainability, and refine a vision and mission for the museum. Through additional support from Mott, the museum is currently implementing the outcomes of this strategic planning process, focusing specifically on developing the museum as a community resource that can contribute to promoting healing and reconciliation not only in the Eastern Cape, but also nationally. The grant increase will enable the museum to engage fundraising and marketing experts to assist with efforts to ensure its financial sustainability.

title: General Purposes
description: South End Museum Trust was established to commemorate the forced removal of people of color from the South End in Port Elizabeth in the Eastern Cape province during the apartheid period. The museum not only documents this shameful episode in South Africa’s history, but also serves as a testament to the resilience and courage of the communities that were relocated to far, outlying areas while their homes, businesses, and places of worship were destroyed. Previous support from the Foundation enabled the development of the museum as a community resource that can contribute to promoting healing and reconciliation not only in the Eastern Cape, but also nationally. This grant will provide general purpose support to the grantee to continue to upgrade its facilities and enhance its programs to provide an inspiring, dynamic, and meaningful visitor experience. Activities over the next two years will include conducting exhibitions focusing on the history of the area; holding regular lessons for school learners; and documenting the history of forced removals countrywide.

title: General Purposes
description: South End Museum Trust was established to commemorate the forced removal of people of color from the South End in Port Elizabeth in the Eastern Cape during the apartheid period. The museum not only documents this shameful episode in South Africa’s history, but also serves as a testament to the resilience and courage of the communities that were relocated to far, outlying areas while their homes, businesses, and places of worship were destroyed. The museum was started by volunteers and community members, many of them former residents with very little expertise in museums, especially museums of conscience. Mott provided a planning grant to South End Museum Trust to hire a consultant to assess its strengths and weaknesses, develop a workplan for its capacity needs, make recommendations on how to secure its long-term sustainability, and refine a vision and mission for the museum. This general purposes grant will provide support to the museum to implement the outcomes of this strategic planning process, focusing specifically on developing the museum as a community resource that can contribute to promoting healing and reconciliation not only in the Eastern Cape, but also nationally.

title: Support for Short-Term Domestic Monitoring of Parliamentary Elections in Ukraine - 2007
description: The program goal is to ensure free, fair, and open parliamentary elections in Ukraine through support to public monitoring and observer efforts. The Eurasia Foundation will provide financial and training support to local partner organizations in four central regions of Ukraine with documented histories of problematic elections. The partner organizations will conduct short-term monitoring of election campaigns and procedures; train and oversee election-day observers; hold regular press conferences to publicize monitoring and observation results; and build their own internal capacities to continue with monitoring of elections and related processes. Established in 1993, the Eurasia Foundation has extensive experience in grantmaking and technical support to indigenous organizations throughout the former Soviet Union, promoting democratic development and economic transformation.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Milwaukee Innercity Congregations Allied for Hope
description: This grant will provide general purposes support to Milwaukee Innercity Congregations Allied for Hope, a multi-issue, multiconstituency, congregation-based community organizing group in greater Milwaukee, Wisconsin. The organization focuses on leadership development and training in order to build a powerful organization that can act effectively on behalf of the interests of its members.

title: Redevelopment of the Durant Hotel
description: This grant will provide partial support for the redevelopment of the historic Durant Hotel in downtown Flint. The Durant Hotel and two contiguous parcels of property were acquired by the Genesee County Land Bank Authority for the purpose of a redevelopment project that will contribute to Flint’s downtown revitalization. The building will be renovated into 118 market-rate apartments oriented toward students and faculty of the local colleges and universities. The project will be a federally certified historic rehabilitation with one- and two-bedroom apartments ranging from 650 to 950 square feet.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to Ireland’s association of grantmakers. Initiated in 1998 as an informal network and then formally registered in 2003, Philanthropy Ireland’s mission is to represent, develop, and inspire an effective and robust philanthropic sector in Ireland. Over the grant period, Philanthropy Ireland will focus its efforts on connecting directly with existing and potential philanthropists and wealth advisors; promoting an enabling environment for philanthropy; and providing relevant services to private philanthropic organizations and other stakeholders in Ireland.

title: Youth Empowerment Partnership Programme in Ireland
description: The project goal is to promote innovation and collaboration in the field of youth and community empowerment. To this end, the Irish Youth Foundation will support multistakeholder approaches to work with young people at risk in Dublin’s North-East Inner City. Young people and various public and private stakeholders in the neighborhood will also be supported to participate in the Youth Empowerment Partnership Programme, a transnational network of foundations and local community stakeholders working on youth and community empowerment. The Irish Youth Foundation is based in Dublin and was founded in 1985 with the mission to support projects and programs that make a positive difference in the lives of young Irish people in need.

title: Strengthening the Roles of National Parliaments and the Mercosur Parliament on South American Integration Processes
description: This grant will support INESC’s initiative to engage parliamentarians in debate about regional integration issues in South America. The project will expand the discussion among organized civil society groups and elected parliamentarians in the South American Common Market countries, as well as the newly inaugurated South American Common Market parliament. Through this project, INESC will inform and educate parliamentarians to actively engage in decisionmaking on the different integration projects by their national governments, international financial institutions, and regional governance mechanisms. The issues to be addressed include transborder water and electricity generation, as well as the encroachment of agriculture and livestock farming on primary forest areas and other bioregions to meet increased agricultural and biofuel demands.

title: General Purposes
description: Faith Action for Community Equity is an institution-based, community organization in Hawaii. Now affiliated with the Gamaliel Foundation, the grantee was established with the assistance of the Center for Community Change through Mott’s Intermediary Support for Organizing Communities program. The organization has grown steadily and now has a membership base of 53 institutions representing people from a wide variety of ethnic backgrounds on the islands of Oahu and Maui. This grant will provide general purpose support to the organization.

title: General Purposes
description: Faith Action for Community Equity is a multi-issue community organization in Hawaii affiliated with the Gamaliel Foundation. The organization has 52 institutional members representing people from a wide variety of ethnic backgrounds on the islands of Oahu and Maui. This grant will provide general purpose support to the organization.

title: General Purposes
description: Faith Action for Community Equity is a multi-issue community organization in Hawaii. The organization has 52 institutional members representing people from a wide variety of economic and ethnic backgrounds on the islands of Oahu, Maui, and Hawaii. This grant will provide general purpose support to the organization.

title: General Purposes
description: Faith Action for Community Equity is an institution-based community organization on the Hawaiian island of Oahu. The organization was established with the assistance of the Center for Community Change through Mott’s Intermediary Support for Organizing program. The organization has grown steadily and now has a membership base of 25 institutions representing people from a wide variety of ethnic backgrounds. In 2007, after nearly ten years as an unaffiliated community organization, Faith Action for Community Equity joined the Gamaliel Foundation network. The grantee formerly received Mott support for a project on education improvement. This grant will provide general purposes support as work begins to establish sister organizations on other islands.

title: Training Organizers for the Immigrant Community
description: Interfaith Worker Justice was founded in 1996 to help religious communities engage in issues facing low-wage and immigrant workers by developing relationships with local worker centers or by helping to begin such centers. By 1998, the grantee had 29 affiliates and by 2007, that number had grown to 60. The purpose of this project is to: a) support a new staff member who will coordinate the training and technical assistance to the local volunteers; and b) explore opportunities to provide additional training to local volunteers and seek funding to support paid positions as professional organizers.

title: Training Organizers for the Immigrant Community
description: Interfaith Worker Justice was founded in 1996 to help religious communities engage in issues facing low-wage and immigrant workers by developing relationships with local worker centers or by helping to begin such centers. By 1998, the grantee had 29 affiliates, and by 2007, that number had grown to 60. The purpose of this project is to coordinate the training and technical assistance to local volunteers and explore opportunities to provide additional training, as well as seek funding to support paid positions as professional organizers.

title: Training Organizers for the Immigrant Community
description: Interfaith Worker Justice was founded in 1996 to help congregations engage in issues facing low-wage and immigrant workers by developing relationships with local worker centers or by helping to begin such centers. The purpose of this project is to coordinate the training and technical assistance to local volunteers and to provide additional training for professional organizers to work with immigrant communities.

title: Training Organizers for the Immigrant Community
description: Interfaith Worker Justice was formed in 1996 to help religious communities engage in issues facing low-wage and immigrant workers by developing relationships with local worker centers or by helping to begin such centers. By 1998, the grantee had 29 affiliates, and by 2007, that number had grown to 60. The purpose of organizing at worker centers is to invite these workers into the larger community so that they can participate in civic deliberation and decisionmaking and build networks of relationships across race, class, income, and ethnicity. This project will support a new staff member who will coordinate the training and technical assistance for local volunteers. It will also enable the grantee to explore opportunities to provide additional training to local volunteer organizers and seek funding to hire professional organizers.

title: Publication of "America's Nonprofit Sector: A Primer"
description: This grant to the Foundation Center provides support to publish a third edition of “America’s Nonprofit Sector: A Primer” by Dr. Lester Salamon. The book provides a concise overview of the structure and operation of the nonprofit sector in the United States presented in a straightforward and coherent fashion. Originally published in 1992 and updated in 1999, “America’s Nonprofit Sector: A Primer” is now the standard introductory text in courses on the nonprofit sector in colleges and universities around the country. Over 30 colleges and universities have adopted the book for this purpose, and many more have placed orders. Altogether, sales of the second edition have reached close to 10,000 copies; however, this edition was based on data that in many cases was current only through the mid-1990s. Many important developments have occurred over the past eight years that would be useful to capture in a revised edition.

title: Develop a Food Stamps Employment Program for Michigan
description: This grant will enable the Corporation for a Skilled Workforce, in partnership with Social Venture Solutions, Inc., to work with the Michigan Department of Human Services and the Department of Labor and Economic Growth to create a pilot project in Michigan to test the viability of a full-scale Food Stamps Employment and Training Program across the state. This effort seeks to: increase the number of food stamp recipients who have access to Food Stamps Employment and Training Program services, including education, training, and employment assistance; leverage the current investment of public and private nonfederal funds in the workforce development system to improve and broaden services; and increase the enrollment rate among eligible food stamp recipients who are not currently enrolled in the food stamp program.

title: Holding Amazon Megaprojects to Account
grantee: Friends of the Earth - Brazilian Amazonia
description: For the past decade, South America has experienced a massive development wave, accompanied by considerable investments in regional transport and energy infrastructure that has begun to traverse sensitive Amazonian ecosystems. Friends of the Earth-Amazon Program is working to ensure there is improvement in the public review and project finance requirements for these projects, as well as requiring a more robust environmental and social impact assessment. One focus of this work will be a large waterway and hydropower project along the Madeira River, which impacts an estimated 220 million acres in the Amazon region. Through this grant, Friends of the Earth-Amazon Program will strengthen its consultative processes with leading international financial institutions to reduce the social and environmental impacts of this project on both the ecosystem and communities of the Amazon.

title: Holding Amazon Megaprojects to Account
grantee: Friends of the Earth - Brazilian Amazonia
description: For the past decade, South America has experienced a massive development wave, accompanied by considerable investments in regional transport and energy infrastructure that traverses sensitive Amazonian ecosystems. Friends of the Earth – Amazon Program is working to ensure there is improvement in the public review and finance requirements for these projects, as well as requiring a more robust environmental and social impact assessment. Through this grant increase, the grantee will strengthen its regional coordination efforts to promote more sustainable investment policies for public financial institutions in Brazil, as they take an increasingly important role as a regional financier for infrastructure and energy, both domestically and in neighboring countries.

title: Holding Amazon Megaprojects to Account
grantee: Friends of the Earth - Brazilian Amazonia
description: For the past decade, South America has experienced a massive development wave, accompanied by considerable investments in regional transport and energy infrastructure that has begun to traverse sensitive Amazonian ecosystems. Friends of the Earth – Brazilian Amazonia is working to ensure there is improvement in the public review and project finance requirements for these projects, as well as requiring a more robust environmental and social impact assessment and the application of environmental and social safeguards policies.
