The principle focus of this work will be increasing sustainability criteria for the investments of the Brazilian National Development Bank, which is currently the largest public funder of energy and infrastructure projects in South America.

title: Holding Amazon Megaprojects to Account
grantee: Friends of the Earth - Brazilian Amazonia
description: For the past decade, South America has experienced a massive development wave, accompanied by considerable investments in regional transport and energy infrastructure that has begun to traverse sensitive Amazonian ecosystems. Friends of the Earth – Brazilian Amazonia is working to ensure there is improvement in the public review and project finance requirements for these projects, as well as requiring a more robust environmental and social impact assessment and the application of environmental and social safeguard policies. This grant increase will support additional research and outreach on transparency standards and information policies at the Brazilian Development Bank, which is currently the largest public funder of energy and infrastructure projects in South America.

title: Improving the Sustainable Performance of Financial Institutions in Brazil
grantee: Friends of the Earth - Brazilian Amazonia
description: Over the past decade, Brazilian development finance in South America has been fueling a wave of investments in regional energy and infrastructure that is pressuring sensitive ecosystems, including the greater Amazon rainforest. Friends of the Earth – Brazilian Amazonia, a nonprofit environmental organization dedicated to promoting sustainable and transparent development policies and practices, is working to ensure that these public and private investments are subject to the highest standards of transparency and accountability, as well as environmental and social safeguards. The principle focus of this work is to increase the sustainability criteria used by the Brazilian Development Bank, which is currently the largest public funder of energy and infrastructure projects in South America.

title: Improving the Sustainable Performance of Financial Institutions in Brazil
grantee: Friends of the Earth - Brazilian Amazonia
description: Brazilian development finance has fueled a wave of investment in energy and infrastructure in South America that is pressuring sensitive ecoregions, such as the Amazon rainforest. Friends of the Earth – Brazilian Amazonia is a nonprofit environmental organization that was a pioneer in efforts to improve transparency, accountability, and strong environmental and social standards for public investments specifically in energy and infrastructure. The principle focus of this project has been on standards used by the Brazilian Development Bank, currently one of the largest funders of development and regional integration in South America.

title: Holding Amazon Megaprojects to Account
grantee: Friends of the Earth - Brazilian Amazonia
description: South America is being swept by a massive development wave, fueled by the economic expansion due to natural resource commodity production. This development is being accompanied by considerable investments in regional transport and energy infrastructure that will traverse the sensitive Amazonian ecosystem. Friends of the Earth – Amazon is working to ensure there is improvement in the public review and project finance requirements for these projects, as well as requiring a more robust environmental and social impact assessment. The focus of the work will be on a large waterway and hydropower project with impacts over an estimated 220 million acres in the Amazon region. Through this grant, the grantee will strengthen its consultative processes with leading international financial institutions to reduce the social and environmental impacts of this project on both the ecosystem and communities of the Amazon.

title: Research and Education on Equal Opportunity in Michigan
grantee: Michigan Roundtable for Diversity and Inclusion
description: Last November, Michigan voters overwhelmingly supported a ballot initiative designed to eliminate affirmative action in public employment and education in the state. Although the outcome of the ballot initiative was disappointing for advocates of affirmative action, important opportunities remain for continuing and reshaping conversations around race, equity, and diversity in Michigan. This grant to Michigan Roundtable for Diversity and Inclusion will support a conference in late 2007 to review the current legal and social framework for diversity programs in the wake of Proposal 2, create avenues to provide members with best practices around equity issues in a post-affirmative action environment, and work toward beginning to create a framework to facilitate ongoing research and information dissemination regarding the impact of Proposal 2.

title: Public Monitoring of the Oil and Gas Projects on Sakhalin
description: Just offshore of the small island of Sakhalin in the Russian Far East lay massive oil and gas reserves. Due to the unique ecosystem and economically important fish stocks that rely on the pristine area, the Sakhalin Island oil and gas projects require public monitoring and oversight, as they could impact local environment and community livelihoods as well as have global ocean and fishery implications. Through the grantee’s vigilance over the past few years, the project design for the island’s oil and gas pipelines has been modified, and stronger international standards are being developed, which will be crucial as Arctic oil and gas exploration expands. Through this grant, Sakhalin Environment Watch will continue to provide public environmental and social monitoring of these energy projects. In addition, this grant will allow the organization to be part of a broad assessment of environmental threats in the Russian Far East.

title: Public Monitoring of the Oil and Gas Projects on Sakhalin
description: Just offshore of the small island of Sakhalin in the Russian Far East lay massive oil and gas reserves. It is estimated that the exploitable reserves are 45 billion barrels of oil equivalent (combined oil and gas reserve estimates). Due to the unique ecosystem and economically important fish stocks that rely on these ecosystems, all of the Sakhalin Island oil and gas projects require public monitoring and oversight as they have had — and will have — a sizable impact on the local environment and community livelihoods. Through the Sakhalin Environment Watch’s vigilance over the past few years, the project design for the island’s oil and gas pipelines has been modified, and stronger international standards are being developed, which will have broad implications for oil and gas exploration elsewhere. Through this grant, Sakhalin Environment Watch will provide public environmental monitoring of these energy projects. This project will ensure that the global spotlight will not fade once the oil and gas pipelines are complete.

title: Economic Development Marketing Program
description: Flint’s economy was dominated by a manufacturing and automotive industry that brought wealth, jobs, and infrastructure to the community. As the global economy shifted, however, the Flint area has experienced a sharp decline in manufacturing and automotive employment. The Genesee Area Focus Fund is helping to create a new model for local economic development. This grant will provide data and analysis that will guide the creation of a new strategy for creating jobs and growing the local economy.

title: Evaluation of the Workforce Development Grants Portfolio
description: This grant will provide support to the Vera Institute of Justice for its independent evaluation of the Mott Foundation’s workforce development objectives in the Pathways Out of Poverty program. The results of the evaluation will contribute to the development of a new or revised Pathways Out of Poverty plan in 2009.

title: Community Outreach on Housing Foreclosure and Predatory Lending
description: PICO National Network represents the voices of families and communities hardest hit by housing foreclosures in the United States, voices that have been largely excluded from the policy debate. As an organization comprised of more than 1,000 religious congregations, the grantee serves as a vehicle for people affected by the foreclosure crisis to come together, educate themselves, conduct research, and promote credible solutions. Working closely with other community organizations, research organizations, advocates, and allies, the grantee will work on several goals aimed at remediating loans, stopping foreclosures, and changing regulations and policies in order to better protect working families.

title: Community Outreach on Housing Foreclosure and Predatory Lending
description: PICO National Network represents the voices of families and communities hardest hit by housing foreclosures in the United States, voices that have been largely excluded from the policy debate. As an organization comprised of more than 1,000 religious congregations. The grantee serves as a vehicle for people affected by the foreclosure crisis to come together, educate themselves, conduct research, and promote credible solutions. Working closely with other community organizations, research organizations, advocates, and allies, the grantee will work on several goals aimed at remediating loans, stopping foreclosures, and changing regulations and policies in order to better protect working families.

title: Community Outreach on Housing Foreclosure and Predatory Lending
description: The Center for Responsible Lending is a nonprofit, nonpartisan research and policy organization dedicated to protecting homeownership and family wealth by working to eliminate abusive financial practices. The grantee has worked with industry participants including Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac to reform practices; the U.S. Department of Defense to ban payday lending to military personnel; community-based organizations to assist families facing foreclosure; and advocacy groups to modify state policies and regulations. The grant will provide partial support to an initiative to reach out to community leaders in selected states to provide research and training for community leaders and policymakers in order to assist existing borrowers and implement lending standards.

title: Endowment Building
description: The project goal is to strengthen the financial stability of the Bulgarian Environmental Partnership Foundation. To this end, the foundation will conduct a fundraising campaign in Bulgaria with the goal of raising over $50,000 for its endowment fund from local sources during 2011-2012. The foundation’s mission is to strengthen civil society and the environment movement in Bulgaria by providing funding and technical assistance to nongovernmental organizations in the fields of environment and community development. In addition, the foundation runs operational programs to promote concepts and practices of sustainable development in local communities. The foundation is a member of the Environmental Partnership for Sustainable Development Association together with its sister foundations from the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, Romania, and Slovakia. Since its establishment in 2003, the foundation has provided grants and technical assistance to over 280 environmental initiatives in Bulgaria.

title: Endowment Building
description: The project goal is to strengthen the financial stability of the Bulgarian Environmental Partnership Foundation. The grantee will conduct a fundraising campaign in Bulgaria with the goal of raising over $40,000 for its endowment fund during 2007-2009. The grantee’s mission is to strengthen civil society and the environment movement in Bulgaria by providing funding and technical assistance to nongovernmental organizations in the fields of environment and community development. In addition, the grantee runs operational programs to promote concepts and practices of sustainable development in local communities. The grantee is a member of the Environmental Partnership for Sustainable Development Association together with its sister foundations from the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, Romania, and Slovakia. Since its establishment in 2003, the grantee has provided grants and technical assistance to over 135 environmental initiatives in Bulgaria.

title: Young Male Initiative
description: This grant will enable the Harlem Children’s Zone to continue to develop a program exclusively for black and Latino males. The Harlem Children’s Zone is a comprehensive community-building initiative focused on improving outcomes for poor children and their families in Harlem. Through the Young Male Initiative, the grantee is providing nearly 300 fifth- through eighth-grade boys with intensive academic, mentoring, social development, and recreational activities. Renewal support will allow the grantee to further develop the Young Male Initiative as an intervention that addresses the life, education, and employment needs of males of color.

title: Young Male Initiative
description: This grant will enable the Harlem Children’s Zone to pilot and develop a program exclusively for black and Latino males. The Harlem Children’s Zone is a comprehensive, community-building initiative focused on improving outcomes for poor children and their families in Harlem. This initiative will provide 200 fifth- and sixth-grade minority males with intensive academic, mentoring, social development, and recreational activities to help channel them toward more positive pursuits. Through this initiative, the Harlem Children’s Zone will also track and follow the participants in this pilot throughout high school and college. This initiative will also supplement existing Harlem Children’s Zone afterschool programs.

title: Leadership Change: National Superintendent of the Year Forum
description: This grant will support the American Association of School Administrators in its efforts to introduce 50 of the top superintendents in the country to the ideas contained in the Mott-funded report, “A New Day for Learning”. Funding will support a portion of the Leadership for Change: National Superintendent of the Year Forum panel presentation and small group discussions on A New Day for Learning, and the development of a white paper. The National Superintendent of the Year has honored outstanding school system leaders from across the country for the past 20 years.

title: Evaluation of Vulnerable Youth Strategies
description: This grant increase will enable MDRC to conduct a series of in-person interviews with grantees participating in the evaluation of the Vulnerable Youth portfolio. This increase will help cover the costs associated with MDRC conducting these in-person meetings and convening two grantee group meetings in Washington, D.C., and Boston, Massachusetts.

title: Evaluation of Vulnerable Youth Strategies
description: This grant will enable MDRC to conduct an external evaluation of the funding and programmatic activities of the Mott Foundation’s Vulnerable Youth grantmaking portfolio. This review and assessment will focus on whether the strategies under the Vulnerable Youth portfolio are making progress toward improving the education and employment opportunities for dropouts and other underserved students. In addition to assessing progress, this review will document how strategies have been expanded in the field and how the Foundation’s work to inform policy, improve practice, and assess promising strategies influenced these efforts.

title: Evaluation of Community Organizing Strategies
description: As part of an internal program planning effort, Community Catalyst will provide an assessment of the Mott Foundation’s Building Organized Communities and Community-Driven Reform portfolios of the Pathways Out of Poverty program. This assessment is aimed at determining the extent to which the grantmaking has met the goal of identifying, testing, and expanding efforts to create pathways out of poverty for low-income families and communities.

title: Evaluation of Income Security Strategies
description: This grant will enable the Center for American Progress to conduct an external evaluation of grantmaking activities under the Mott Foundation’s income security portfolio between 2000 and 2007. This review will assess progress, relative to baseline, on the outcomes sought for the grantmaking portfolio. In addition to progress, the final evaluation report will show examples of how the income security grantmaking strategies have been expanded in the field, how the Foundation’s work to inform policy, improve practice, and evaluate promising strategies influenced these efforts, and what impact the Foundation’s investment in these strategies had on poverty alleviation. The Center for American Progress is a national think tank dedicated to improving the lives of Americans through ideas and action.

title: Government Performance Improvement Initiative
description: The purpose of the Government Performance Improvement Initiative, a project of the Council of Michigan Foundations, is for the state of Michigan to utilize private consulting companies to achieve at least $30 million in cost savings and revenue enhancement by January 31, 2008. The priority areas to achieve these savings have been identified and include shared financial services and process improvement, pension transformation, and revenue enhancement.

title: Green Corps Urban Youth Program
description: Cleveland Botanical Garden’s Green Corps Urban Youth Program provides disadvantaged students with work-study experiences that add relevance to their high school education, encourages them to consider college education or vocational training, and prepares them to become responsible employees. During the initial grant period, funding supported an independent evaluation of the program, which found significant positive impacts on students’ leadership skills, social networks, and overall workforce readiness. This grant will enable the grantee to disseminate the evaluation findings to relevant audiences, with a particular emphasis on youth-serving organizations. Founded in 1930, Cleveland Botanical Garden engages people of all ages, backgrounds, and abilities in experiencing the jobs of gardening and understanding the interdependence of plants, animals, people, and the environment.

title: Green Corps Urban Youth Program
description: This grant will enable the Cleveland Botanical Garden to conduct a five-year longitudinal evaluation of its Green Corps Urban Youth Program. The program is an urban, horticulture-based, work-study program for at-risk high school students that promotes academic success, workforce readiness, and valuable life skills. Mott support will allow the Cleveland Botanical Garden to hire an outside evaluator to assess the impact of its program on students’ academic performance in school, enrollment in post-secondary education, and/or workforce placement.

title: Code Enforcement Project
description: This grant will allow the city of Flint to contract with part-time legal professionals to process a significant backlog in default judgments for municipal civil infractions. Activities will include processing and collecting fines for code infractions that adversely affect the health, safety, and welfare of the public.

title: Getting Ahead of Sprawl
description: The Michigan Land Use Institute works to strengthen Michigan’s urban and rural communities by engaging the public and informing decisionmakers through a combination of research and public engagement. With prior Mott support, the institute has provided education, strategic communications, and technical support to encourage broad-based citizen input into development of the Grand Vision, a regional land-use and transportation framework to guide future growth in the six-county area surrounding Traverse City. With renewed support, the institute will continue its efforts to coordinate public participation in the implementation of this groundbreaking regional development plan.

title: Initiative to Promote Transportation Choices in the Grand Traverse Region
description: The Michigan Land Use Institute works to strengthen Michigan’s urban and rural communities by engaging the public and informing decisionmakers through a combination of research and public outreach. With prior Mott support, the grantee has provided education, strategic communications, and technical support to encourage broad-based citizen input into development of the Grand Vision, a regional land-use and transportation framework to guide future growth in the six-county area surrounding Traverse City. With renewed support, the grantee will focus its efforts on implementing the transportation elements of the Grand Vision and participate in related state-level policy reform efforts.

title: Initiative to Promote Transportation Choices in the Grand Traverse Region
description: The Michigan Land Use Institute works to strengthen Michigan’s urban and rural communities by engaging the public and informing decisionmakers through a combination of research and public outreach. With prior Mott support, the grantee has focused on implementing the transportation elements of the Grand Vision, a regional land-use and transportation framework to guide future growth in the six-county area surrounding Traverse City. With renewed support, the grantee will continue its transportation work, building public appreciation for, and promoting utilization of, transit, walking, and other transportation options. The grantee will also participate in related state-level policy reform efforts.

title: Getting Ahead of Sprawl
description: After more than two years of collaboration among a diverse group of stakeholders, the Grand Traverse region of Michigan has launched a historic land use and transportation planning process that will set a vision for the region’s growth for the next 50 years. A world-class team of consultants has been hired to lead the project, which will involve conducting a series of public visioning sessions, generating models of various growth scenarios, and selecting a preferred scenario to guide land use and transportation development in the region. The Michigan Land Use Institute will work with local officials and citizens throughout the region to provide input into the planning effort and generate broad public support for implementation of the vision which results from the process.

title: Evaluation of World Bank Small Grants Program
description: The World Bank’s Small Grants Program aims to promote civic engagement for the empowerment of marginalized and vulnerable people. Funded by the World Bank’s Development Grant Facility, the program is one of only a few grant mechanisms through which the World Bank directly supports civil society organizations. This grant will provide funding for an independent evaluation of the small grants program. The evaluation will be conducted by Pact Institute, with guidance from a multidisciplinary advisory team, which will include representatives from the World Bank, beneficiary organizations, private foundations, and other nonprofit organizations. Evaluation findings will be available to the public.

title: Summit on Microfinance
description: This grant will partially support the first Summit on Microfinance in the United States to be held in San Antonio, Texas. The summit will be hosted by ACCION Texas, probably the largest-scale microenterprise lender in the United States with more than 500 borrowers annually. Its purpose is to shed light on the many accomplishments of the domestic microenterprise movement.

title: Promoting Equity and Racial Justice Fund
description: The city of Flint and Genesee County continue to struggle with issues of social equity and racial justice. Building on the community’s renewed energy and focus as a result of the recent residency of the Truth in Translation theater group, the Community Foundation of Greater Flint is taking a long-term approach to developing systemic solutions to issues of equity and racial justice by increasing its ability to build local capacity to address these issues. The fund will be used to support small- to medium-sized projects that promote equity and racial justice, educate the community, encourage dialogue, promote understanding of one another, and support research that strengthens local grantmaking and other projects addressing these issues.

title: Microenterprise Evaluation
description: This grant to the Nebraska Community Foundation will allow the Center for Rural Entrepreneurship to assess grants made by the Mott Foundation in the microenterprise portfolio within its Pathways Out of Poverty program. The purpose of the assessment is to determine to what extent they have met the program’s mission of identifying, testing, and expanding efforts that create pathways out of poverty for low-income people and communities.

title: Management Technical Assistance
description: This grant will provide technical assistance to develop sound financial systems as well as professional recruiting to help select a highly skilled chief executive officer for Career Alliance. Career Alliance is the local Michigan Works! agency and home of Genesee and Shiawassee counties’ Workforce Investment Board, which administers more than $21 million in adult and at-risk youth training funds.

title: Planning a Fund Raising Strategy
description: This grant will enable East Harlem Employment Service, Inc., to add job skill training to its nationally renowned attitudinal or soft-skill training program throughout its national program network. Mott funds will be used to assemble a group of national advisors to plan the development of a new fundraising arm to undertake paying for the significant cost of a skill building strategy. Mott funding will also support the preliminary research required to understand what form this fundraising arm should take.

title: Core Operational Support
description: MaAfrika Tikkun is an indigenous grantmaker that was started in 1995 by a prominent South African business family to provide support to disadvantaged black communities. It funds community upliftment projects focusing on education and health, especially HIV/AIDS, targeting children, youth, and the aged. It works with community-based organizations that have a history of involvement in their communities, providing training, mentoring, and leadership development. Past support contributed to institutional development and strengthening the grantee as an indigenous grantmaking organization. This grant will continue to support MaAfrika Tikkun to strengthen its institutional capacity and to partner with community groups, other organizations, and government to empower disadvantaged communities.

title: Core Operational Support
description: Afrika Tikkun was established in 1995 by a prominent South African business family to provide education, health, and social services to children, youth, and families by building and managing centers of excellence in South African townships. Its goal is to empower communities to develop a new generation of productive citizens. The grantee has built strong relationships with the business sector and government and has received considerable support from its networks, making it possible to provide world class facilities to marginalized communities. To provide relief and development support, the grantee partners with community-based organizations to ensure ownership and continuity of programs. Past support contributed to the grantee’s community centers of excellence, its efforts to build stronger linkages with government departments and businesses, and the development of a new institutional identity. This grant will support the grantee to strengthen current institutional systems, develop a comprehensive monitoring and evaluation system, and improve the quality of care at the community centers.

title: Core Operational Support
description: Afrika Tikkun was established in 1995 by the Lubner family to provide education, health and social services to children and their families in poor communities. The grantee builds and runs community development centers in townships in Gauteng and the Western Cape provinces of South Africa and implements programs designed to respond to the development needs of a child at all stages of their lives. The grantee works with community-based organizations and leaders in communities to ensure that programs are informed by the communities. Past support enabled the grantee to evaluate its current programs and introduce a monitoring and evaluation system for ongoing assessment of its programs. This grant will support the grantee to finalize the implementation of the monitoring and evaluation system, implement programs in line with the needs of the communities it supports, and introduce additional management systems to ensure optimal delivery of programs and good governance.

title: Core Operational Support
description: MaAfrika Tikkun is an indigenous grantmaker that was started in 1995 by a prominent South African business family to provide support to disadvantaged black communities. It funds community upliftment projects, focusing on education and health, especially HIV/AIDS, targeting children, youth, and the aged. The grantee works with community-based organizations that have a history of involvement in their communities, providing training, mentoring, capacity building, and leadership development. It strives to build the leadership, capacity, and sustainability of the community-based organizations enabling them to manage the projects. This grant is aimed at strengthening MaAfrika Tikkun as an indigenous grantmaker enabling it to continue empowering disadvantaged communities with the necessary structures and skills to increasingly look after their own requirements.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support LA’s BEST in securing high quality afterschool education, enrichment, and recreation programming for 28,000 elementary students in 180 school sites. Specifically, grant funding will support the continued and sustained delivery of the LA’s BEST program over one year including day-to-day operations, program implementation, and training activities that effectively remove the barriers to children’s academic and social development and make them available to learn. The grantee’s mission is to provide a safe and supervised afterschool education, enrichment, and recreation program for elementary school children ages 5 to 12 in the city of Los Angeles.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support LA’s BEST in securing high quality afterschool education, enrichment, and recreation programming for 28,000 elementary students in 180 school sites. The grant will also help with the development and implementation of a strategic communications campaign aimed at promoting the value of community-led afterschool and expanded learning programs that support a balance of social, emotional, physical, and academic development for youth across the nation.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant increase continues support to LA’s BEST in securing high quality afterschool education, enrichment, and recreation programming for 28,000 elementary students in 180 school sites. This increase also provides partial support for the 25th anniversary afterschool program gala.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant increase will support LA’s BEST in securing high quality afterschool education, enrichment, and recreation programming for 28,000 elementary students in 195 school sites. This increase also provides support for the annual family dinner event honoring retiring President and CEO Carla Sanger.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support LA’s BEST in securing high quality afterschool education, enrichment, and recreation programming for 28,000 elementary students in 195 school sites. The grant will support the continued and sustained delivery of the LA’s BEST program over two years including day-to-day operations, program implementation, and training activities that effectively remove the barriers to children’s academic and social development and make them available to learn.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant increase will support LA’s BEST in securing high quality afterschool education, enrichment, and recreation programming for 29,000 elementary school students in 195 school sites. Specifically, this grant provides support for the annual family dinner event which will highlight partners of LA’s BEST and the children and families served through the program.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support LA’s BEST in securing high quality afterschool education, enrichment, and recreation programming for 25,000 elementary students in 193 school sites and 6,500 students in summer programming. The grant will support the continued and sustained delivery of the LA’s BEST program over two years including day-to-day operations, program implementation, and training activities that effectively remove the barriers to children’s academic and social development.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support LA’s BEST in securing high-quality afterschool education, enrichment, and recreation programming for 25,000 elementary students in 200 school sites and up to 8,000 students in summer programming. The grant will support the continued and sustained delivery of LA’s BEST program over two years including day-to-day operations, program implementation, and training activities that effectively remove the barriers to children’s academic and social development.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support LA’s BEST in serving more than 26,000 children in 180 afterschool programs throughout the City of Los Angeles. LA’s BEST is a unique partnership, which includes the City of Los Angeles, the Los Angeles Unified School District, community-based organizations, and the private sector. LA’s BEST aims to offer high quality, afterschool education, enrichment, and recreation programs for children between the ages of 5 and 12. Each LA’s BEST site creates a safe haven for economically disadvantaged children by providing homework assistance, supporting core academic skills, and offering enriching activities at no cost to parents.

title: Speak Truth to Power
description: “Speak Truth to Power” is a multifaceted education initiative that brings much-needed attention to courageous human rights activists around the world and the continuing human rights problems that they and their countries face. What began as a book of interviews of more than 50 human rights defenders on four continents grew into an ongoing project that includes a play based upon the defenders’ words, traveling photographic exhibitions, educational curricula, a documentary film, and public service announcements. This grant to Robert F. Kennedy Memorial will provide partial support for bringing the play, photographic exhibitions, curricula, and public discussion forums to Johannesburg and Cape Town. Hosted by prominent South African institutions and individuals, the South Africa production of “Speak Truth to Power” will feature human rights heroes from the African continent and will highlight the relevance of human rights issues to South Africa’s history and its future.

title: Site-based Freshwater Conservation in the Great Lakes Basin
geographic_focus: Ohio, New York, Wisconsin, Indiana, Michigan, Illinois, Pennsylvania, Minnesota
description: Climate change is beginning to impact the Great Lakes ecosystem, yet it is a challenge to develop conservation strategies that address climate change because of the uncertainty surrounding site-specific impacts and the lack of detailed information on species and systems that are most vulnerable to harm. The Nature Conservancy, an international conservation organization, works in the Great Lakes states and in Ontario to develop and implement sound conservation strategies to protect and restore the Great Lakes. With support from Mott, the conservancy will produce climate action plans for three key Great Lakes aquatic systems that will serve as models for “climate-ready” conservation action plans throughout the Great Lakes Basin.

title: Site-based Freshwater Conservation in the Great Lakes Basin
geographic_focus: Wisconsin, New York, Pennsylvania, Ohio, Indiana, Illinois, Minnesota, Michigan
description: Conservation of the Great Lakes region is a global priority for The Nature Conservancy, a leading international conservation organization. The conservancy’s Great Lakes program works to abate threats to freshwater biodiversity across the Great Lakes basin by working with diverse partners. With partial support from Mott, the Great Lakes program will develop conservation action plans for key freshwater sites and assist its partners in taking conservation action at high priority areas throughout the Great Lakes basin.

title: General Purposes
description: The project goal is to strengthen the community foundation field in the Czech Republic. During the grant period, the Czech Association of Community Foundations will improve its services for members, promote community foundations as vehicles for community development in the Czech Republic, support the development of new community foundations, and identify new sources of revenue for the association and its members. The association was established in 2006 with the mission to develop the community foundation field in the Czech Republic, strengthen the capacity of its members, and represent Czech community foundations at the national and international levels. Currently, the association has eight members including five community foundations and three support organizations involved in providing services to community foundations and other grantmakers at the local level. In 2008-2009, the association provided information, consultations, and networking opportunities to its members.

title: General Purposes
description: The project goal is to strengthen the community foundation field in the Czech Republic. During the grant period, the Czech Association of Community Foundations will improve its current services for members and develop new services, promote community foundations as vehicles for community development in the Czech Republic, support the development of new community foundations, and identify new sources of revenue for the association and its members. The association was established in September 2006 with the mission to develop the community foundation field in the Czech Republic, strengthen the capacity of its members, and represent Czech community foundations at the national and international levels. Currently, members include four community foundations and three support organizations involved in providing services to community foundations and other grantmakers at the local level. Since its establishment, the association has been providing information, consultations, and networking opportunities to its members.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purpose support to the Committee for Economic Development. The organization’s policy programs focus on four vital areas of our economy and society: education, from pre-kindergarten, primary, and secondary education, to college and continuous learning; workforce development; international trade and financial stability; and long-term economic growth, including the federal budget, productivity, and technology. The organization engages a national constituency of business and academic leaders, public officials, policymakers, community groups, and other concerned citizens in this work and broadly disseminates recommendations and publications to them, while conducting business forums and town meetings across the country. In 2008, major programs are planned on healthcare, human resources in education, and early childhood care and development. Since its founding in 1942, the Committee for Economic Development has been bringing business innovation and thinking to bear on public policy development.

title: Workforce Services Model Expansion
description: Rubicon Programs Incorporated is a high performing, multiprogram workforce development organization serving the high needs areas of the San Francisco Bay region. With the guidance and direction of a strategic plan that was conducted in 2006, the organization is undertaking a strategic expansion of its workforce services model that helps people to overcome the barriers of homelessness, poverty, and disabilities. The grantee’s experience will provide a model for additional regional approaches to workforce development.

title: Workforce Services Model Expansion
description: Rubicon Programs Incorporated is a high performing, multiprogram workforce development organization serving the high needs areas of the San Francisco Bay region. With the guidance and direction of a strategic plan that was introduced in 2006, the organization is undertaking a strategic expansion of its workforce services model that helps people to overcome the barriers of homelessness, poverty, and disabilities. The grantee’s experience will provide a model for additional regional approaches to workforce development.

title: Federal Policy Initiative
description: This grant will support the work of the National Employment Law Project on the Trade Adjustment Assistance program while promoting other key safety net and worker training policies. This Federal Policy Initiative is especially focused on bringing the voices of state and local need to national policy discussions. The grantee is committed to accomplishing this by forging alliances that work from the community level to the federal level.

title: Federal Policy Initiative
description: The purpose of the Federal Policy Initiative is to provide extensive technical assistance to stakeholders and policymakers working on workforce issues, focusing most particularly on fixing the administrative and programmatic barriers that the National Employment Law Project has experienced with the Trade Adjustment Assistance program while working with local communities.

title: Michigan Sectoral Skills Academy
description: This grant will enable the Michigan Works! Association to initiate a staff training program patterned after the Aspen Institute’s nationwide sectoral employment training program. The Michigan Sectoral Skills Academy will offer two different training opportunities. One three-day training session will serve as a primer and be open to all Michigan Works! agency staff from a senior executive to an entry-level worker. The second two day training will be open to different Michigan Works! teams who are implementing or have implemented a sectoral strategy and would like to expand upon that project.

title: Community Universities
description: The project goal is to strengthen the capacity of selected regional universities to contribute to locally defined community development priorities in Russia. The project will consist of three key elements: capacity building of universities with respect to community outreach and development of responsive community services; participatory community needs assessments focused on identifying priority projects and the resources available and necessary to implement them; and grant-funded community development projects aimed at enhancing availability and relevance of university resources to local communities. Established in 2003, the New Eurasia Foundation, has extensive experience in working to modernize Russian universities, as well as in expanding the community schools model in Russia. Its work is aimed at fostering a broad range of cross-sectoral partnerships to assist in Russia’s social and economic development.

title: General Purposes
description: This renewal grant will support the work of the Flint Jewish Federation, Flint’s largest Jewish-serving organization, and in particular, its signature fundraiser, the Donald Riegle Community Service Award event. Additionally, this grant will support other fundraising efforts sponsored by the Flint Jewish Federation, which aids Russian-Jewish refugees who have relocated to Genesee County.

title: General Purposes
description: This renewal grant will support the work of the Flint Jewish Federation, Flint’s largest Jewish-serving organization, and in particular, its signature fundraiser, the Donald Riegle Community Service Award event. Additionally, this grant will support other fundraising efforts sponsored by the Flint Jewish Federation, which aids Russian-Jewish refugees who have relocated to Genesee County.

title: General Purposes
description: This renewal grant will support the work of the Flint Jewish Federation, Flint’s largest Jewish-serving organization, including its signature fundraiser, the Donald Riegle Community Service Award event and the Daniel Pearl Memorial Humanity in Harmony Program. This grant will also support programs, social services, and activities that benefit the entire Flint Community, including immigration services, transportation services, and nutrition programs for seniors.

title: General Purposes
description: This general purposes grant will support the work of the Flint Jewish Federation, including its annual fundraiser, the Donald Riegle Community Service Award event. This grant will also support the Flint Jewish Federation’s fundraising efforts and the work of aiding Russian Jewish refugees in relocating to Genesee County.

title: Bill Maynes Fund for Future Leaders of Eurasia
geographic_focus: Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Russia, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Armenia, Georgia, Moldova, Uzbekistan, Belarus, Ukraine
description: The goal of the Bill Maynes Fund for Future Leaders of Eurasia is to honor the work of Bill Maynes in promoting stable and prosperous societies in the former Soviet Union. It will recognize outstanding individuals who have made significant contributions to efforts in their respective countries to build a middle class, strengthen independent media, promote open and responsive governance, and empower local communities. Individual fellowships will consist of tailor-made programs of meetings and related events designed to give fellows a platform for articulating their vision of the future of their societies, as well as to learn best practices in their given field of interest. Established in 1993, the Eurasia Foundation is a privately managed grantmaking and operating foundation focused on civil society, public administration and policy, and private enterprise development throughout the former Soviet Union.

title: Transforming Philanthropy Through Diversity and Inclusion
description: The Council of Michigan Foundations is a membership association comprised of more than 350 foundations and grantmaking corporations. Since 2001, and as a strategy to help fulfill its mission of enhancing, improving, and increasing philanthropy, the council has worked to advance diversity and inclusion throughout the philanthropic sector. This renewal grant will support the second year of the council’s five-year Transforming Philanthropy Through Diversity and Inclusion project. Building on the research, planning, and development accomplished during the previous grant period, the council will increase diversity and inclusion within its own organization, disseminate diversity-related research findings, launch a networking/social learning Web site, hold a symposium on social equity and philanthropy, and implement a youth internship and executive fellowship program.

title: Transforming Michigan Philanthropy Through Diversity and Inclusion
description: The Council of Michigan Foundations is a membership association comprised of more than 350 foundations and grantmaking corporations. Since 2001, the council has used the strategy of advancing diversity and inclusion throughout the philanthropic sector to help fulfill its mission of enhancing, improving, and increasing philanthropy. This renewal grant will support the third year of the council’s Transforming Michigan Philanthropy Through Diversity and Inclusion project. Building on the research, planning, and program development and implementation accomplished during the previous grant period, the council will increase diversity and inclusion within its own organization, disseminate results of the first Peer Action Learning Network cohort, recruit six new member foundations to participate in the 2011 cohort, hold a symposium on closing opportunity gaps in Michigan, provide training workshops and post-training assistance to Youth Advisory Council members, and implement a mentorship program for individuals who hold mid-level professional positions in philanthropy.

title: Transforming Michigan Philanthropy Through Diversity and Inclusion
description: The Council of Michigan Foundations is a membership association comprised of more than 350 foundations and grantmaking corporations. Since 2001, the council has used the strategy of advancing diversity and inclusion throughout the philanthropic sector to help fulfill its mission of enhancing, improving, and increasing philanthropy. This renewal grant will support the fourth year of the council’s Transforming Michigan Philanthropy Through Diversity and Inclusion project. Building on the research, planning, and program development and implementation accomplished during the previous grant period, the council will increase diversity and inclusion within its own organization, disseminate results of the first Peer Action Learning Network cohort, recruit six new member foundations to participate in the 2012 cohort, hold a symposium on closing opportunity gaps in Michigan, provide training workshops and post-training assistance to Youth Advisory Council members, and implement a mentorship program for individuals who hold mid-level professional positions in philanthropy.

title: Transforming Michigan Philanthropy Through Diversity and Inclusion
description: This renewal grant will support the fifth year of the Council of Michigan Foundations’ Transforming Michigan Philanthropy Through Diversity and Inclusion project. The grantee is a membership association comprised of more than 350 foundations and grantmaking corporations. Since 2001, the grantee has used the strategy of advancing diversity and inclusion throughout the philanthropic sector to help fulfill its mission of enhancing, improving, and increasing philanthropy. Building on the research, planning, and program development and implementation accomplished during the previous grant period, the grantee will continue to increase diversity and inclusion within its own organization, offer a third cohort for the Peer Action Learning Network program and a second year of the mentoring initiative for the Forum for African-Americans in Philanthropy, and provide training workshops and post-training assistance to Youth Advisory Council members, including a job shadowing program.

title: Transforming Michigan Philanthropy Through Diversity and Inclusion
description: This one-year renewal grant will help support the Phase II efforts of the Council of Michigan Foundations and the Transforming Michigan Philanthropy Through Diversity and Inclusion initiative. The grantee is a membership association comprised of more than 350 foundations and grantmaking corporations. Since 2001, the grantee has used the strategy of advancing diversity and inclusion throughout the philanthropic sector to help fulfill its mission of enhancing, improving, and increasing philanthropy. Building on the research, planning, program development, and implementation accomplished during Phase I of the Transforming Michigan Philanthropy Through Diversity and Inclusion initiative work, Phase II will offer more mentor and mentee opportunities for African-American, Arab-American, and Hispanic-American demographics; produce a fourth Passing the Leadership Baton event in Southeast Michigan; continue to offer joint programming for Emerging Practitioners in Philanthropy and Young Nonprofit Professionals Network; and pilot the first multigenerational Family Retreat for Arab Americans.

title: Transforming Philanthropy Through Diversity and Inclusion
description: As a result of a growing awareness of the need for greater diversity and inclusion within philanthropy, the Council of Michigan Foundations included in its 2001 strategic planning process an emphasis on diversity and inclusion, and encouraged its members to take similar steps. This focus is reflected in a variety of training programs, exploratory task forces, and partnerships that the council has participated in since 2001, as it works toward actualizing its commitment to diversity. The grantee formalized this commitment with a board resolution approved in 2006. This grant will support the council’s current Transforming Philanthropy Through Diversity and Inclusion project, which represents the second five-year phase of its efforts to advance diversity and inclusion with Michigan’s philanthropic sector.

title: Diversity in Philanthropy Research Metrics
description: Established in 1956, the Foundation Center’s mission is to connect domestic nonprofits and grantmakers to each other and provide helpful tools and information in order to strengthen the nonprofit sector. The grantee maintains a comprehensive database on grantmakers and operates research, education, and training programs designed to advance philanthropy at every level. This renewal grant will provide support to the grantee for its Diversity in Philanthropy Research Metrics project. The Foundation Center will build upon its extensive base of research conducted over the last grant period to develop a national system of collecting, analyzing, and disseminating data on diversity in philanthropy as well as propose a plan for implementation. The institutionalization of such a system will ensure that foundations are able to collect and have access to high quality data on diversity in the years ahead.

title: Diversity in Philanthropy Research Metrics
description: Established in 1956, the Foundation Center’s mission is to connect nonprofits and grantmakers in the United States to each other and to provide helpful tools and information in order to strengthen the domestic nonprofit sector. The grantee maintains a comprehensive database on domestic grantmakers and operates research, education, and training programs designed to advance philanthropy at every level. This renewal grant will provide support to the grantee for its Diversity in Philanthropy Research Metrics project. The grantee will build upon its extensive base of research conducted over the last grant period to continue developing a national system of collecting, analyzing, and disseminating data on diversity in philanthropy. The institutionalization of such a system will ensure that foundations are able to collect and have access to high quality data on diversity in the years ahead.

title: Diversity in Philanthropy Research Metrics
description: Established in 1956, the Foundation Center’s mission is to connect domestic nonprofits and grantmakers to each other and provide helpful tools and information in order to strengthen the nonprofit sector. The grantee maintains a comprehensive database on grantmakers and operates research, education, and training programs designed to advance philanthropy at every level. This renewal grant will provide support to the grantee for its Diversity in Philanthropy Research Metrics project. The grantee will build upon its extensive base of research conducted over the last grant period to develop a national system of collecting, analyzing, and disseminating data on diversity in philanthropy, as well as propose a plan for implementation. Work for the upcoming grant period will focus on collecting comprehensive data on foundation staff and boards in order to better understand the demographics of those working in and governing philanthropic institutions.

title: Diversity in Philanthropy Research Metrics
description: Established in 1956, the Foundation Center’s mission is to connect nonprofits and grantmakers in the United States to each other and to helpful tools and information in order to strengthen the nonprofit sector. The Foundation Center maintains a comprehensive database on grantmakers in the United States and operates research, education, and training programs designed to advance philanthropy at every level. This grant will provide support to the Foundation Center for its Diversity in Philanthropy Research Metrics project. The project will develop a plan for a national system of collecting, analyzing, and disseminating data on diversity in philanthropy. The development of such a system will ensure that foundations are able to collect and have access to high quality data on diversity in the years ahead.

title: Civil Society Contact Group
description: The program goal is to strengthen the dialogue between nongovernmental organizations and European Union institutions. To this end, Social Platform will coordinate an informal working group of large nongovernmental organizations’ groupings or “platforms” working on the European Union level in eight sectors: social, environment, development, education, human rights, public health, women, and culture. The working group was created in 2002 to promote a transparent and structured dialogue between civil society and European Union institutions. During the grant period, the working group will raise awareness of the importance of European Parliament elections in 2009 among nongovernmental organizations, build cross-sector civil society alliances, and produce tools and resources for engaging nongovernmental organizations in debates related to the European Parliament elections. The working group will focus specifically on engaging nongovernmental organizations from the European Union new member states. Social Platform is based in Brussels and represents over 1,700 European social nonprofit organizations.

title: Strategic Initiatives
description: Kettering University, the only fully cooperative engineering and management university in the United States, has been an integral component of Flint’s higher education system since 1919. The university has 2,134 full-time undergraduate and 466 graduate students for the 2008-2009 academic year. This renewal grant will provide partial funding for components of a multiyear series of initiatives aimed at increasing enrollment, providing merit-based scholarships for incoming students, and raising $125 million to support campus growth and the endowment.

title: Strategic Initiatives
description: This grant provides renewal support for key initiatives at Kettering University, an anchor institution of higher education in the Flint community. In 2010, the university will focus its strategic attention on need-based scholarships; pre-college programs; marketing and fundraising efforts; laboratory equipment and upgrades; and collaboration with the Flint Cultural Center institutions on arts education programs for Kettering students. As a private university, Kettering has positioned itself to compete with lower cost public institutions by launching degree programs in high demand fields, building state-of-the-art laboratories, and establishing partnerships with institutions of higher education overseas and in the United States. The co-op experience continues to attract students, and applications in 2009 were at an all time high. According to the “U.S. News and World Report”, Kettering ranks second nationally for mechanical engineering programs. The value of its endowment in 2009 was $48 million.

title: Strategic Initiatives
description: This grant provides renewal support for key initiatives at Kettering University, an anchor institution of higher education in the Flint community. In 2011, the university will focus its strategic attention on need-based scholarships, a new marketing and branding campaign, Web site redesign, pre-college programs, and fundraising efforts, all with an emphasis on enrollment recovery.

title: Transformational Initiatives
description: This grant provides renewal support for key initiatives at Kettering University, an anchor institution of higher education in the Flint community. In 2012, under the leadership of a new president, the university will focus its strategic attention on increasing enrollment through targeted recruitment, program development, need-based scholarships, and pre-college programs; a branding and marketing campaign; transformation of the convenience store at Chevrolet and University avenues into a police mini-station and eatery; and increasing alumni engagement.

title: Transformational Initiatives
description: This grant increase provides support for key initiatives at Kettering University, an anchor institution of higher education in the Flint community. In 2012, under the leadership of a new president, the university will focus its strategic attention on increasing enrollment, launching a branding and marketing campaign, contributing to the economic revitalization of Flint and the region, and increasing alumni support and participation.

title: Transformational Initiatives
description: This grant increase provides support for key initiatives at Kettering University, an anchor institution of higher education in the Flint community. In the coming year, the grantee will continue its strategic attention on increasing enrollment, launching a branding and marketing campaign, contributing to the economic revitalization of Flint and the region, and increasing alumni support and participation.

title: Transformational Initiatives
description: This grant increase provides support for key initiatives at Kettering University, an anchor institution of higher education in the Flint community. In the coming year, the grantee will continue its strategic attention on increasing enrollment, launching a branding and marketing campaign, contributing to the economic revitalization of Flint and the region, and increasing alumni support and participation.

title: Strategic Initiatives
description: Kettering University, the only fully cooperative engineering and management university in the United States, has been an integral component of Flint’s higher education system since 1919. The university has 2,070 full-time, undergraduate students and 519 graduate students for the 2007-2008 academic year. This grant will provide initial funding for components of a multiyear series of initiatives aimed at increasing enrollment, providing merit-based scholarships for incoming students, and raising $125 million to support campus growth and the endowment.

title: Founder's Conference Room of the New Headquarters Building
description: This grant will provide partial support for the Founder’s Conference Room of the New Headquarters Building of the United States Institute of Peace. Construction of this 154,000 square foot building will begin in early 2008 and be completed in 2010. Located on Washington’s National Mall, the new headquarters will help the institute meet a growing demand for its services and outreach in conflict resolution, applied conflict management, and peacemaking activities worldwide. A Public Education Center, with exhibit space for displays and interactive programs appealing to students and the general public, will also be located in the building in addition to conference rooms for training professionals in conflict resolution.

title: Good Business Initiative: A Microenterprise Development Program
description: This grant to Goodwill Industries International, Inc., will continue to support the development of a microenterprise model that can be replicated among Goodwill organizations nationwide. The grantee will model its replication after the Atlanta Goodwill program entitled “BusinessNOW”. This demonstration will pilot microenterprise within a financial strengthening continuum in two Goodwill affiliates and share lessons learned with the entire Goodwill network. Tools and concepts developed will be shared with the 168 North American Goodwill organizations via learning events, webinars, and an extranet knowledge management system entitled “MyGoodwill”.

title: Good Business Initiative: A Microenterprise Development Program
description: This planning grant to Goodwill Industries International, Inc., will support the development of a microenterprise model that can be replicated at the local level among Goodwills nationwide. Goodwill affiliates, who currently operate microenterprise ventures, are observing individuals from disadvantaged communities achieve the goal of long-term financial stability. The grantee will be able to collect information from the Atlanta Goodwill program, BusinessNOW, and other Goodwill microenterprise programs to determine what lessons can be learned and replicated in other affiliate locations.

title: General Purposes
description: The Flint River Watershed stretches across several counties and includes dozens of cities and towns. More than a half-million people drink groundwater affected by the Flint River or use it as a backup water supply, while fish and wildlife depend on the river and its tributaries. Yet, stormwater runoff, habitat loss, and other pollution sources are degrading the watershed, threatening the human and wildlife communities that depend on it. The Flint River Watershed Coalition works to improve the watershed through sound science, public education, and policy development. Past efforts have included river cleanup events and water quality monitoring activities. With a renewal grant from Mott, the coalition will build its organizational capacity, increase its educational outreach, and promote strong watershed stewardship.

title: General Purposes
description: The Flint River and its tributaries are an important recreational resource for the region’s residents while also providing important habitat for a variety of freshwater species and other wildlife. The Flint River Watershed Coalition works to protect the Flint River and its tributaries through a variety of means, including public education, policy reform, and hands-on monitoring and restoration activities. With renewal support, the grantee will remain focused on the work it currently has under way: building the organization’s advocacy efforts as the voice of the Flint River; maintaining its signature education programs; sustaining the grantee’s outdoor programs; and attending to the group’s own organizational development needs.

title: General Purposes
description: The Flint River and its tributaries are an important recreational resource for the region’s residents while also providing important habitat for a variety of freshwater species and other wildlife. The Flint River Watershed Coalition works to protect the Flint River and its tributaries through a variety of means. With renewal support, the grantee will maintain all of its education and outreach efforts and place a strong emphasis on efforts to encourage restoration activities and engage decisionmakers. In addition, the grantee will focus considerable attention on the revitalization of the waterfront areas in the city of Flint and attend to its own organizational development needs.

title: General Purposes
description: The Flint River, which runs through the heart of the city of Flint, is an underutilized asset for both community residents and local businesses. With previous Mott support, the Flint River Watershed Coalition conducted a variety of programs to protect the Flint River and its tributaries and build public awareness about this valuable freshwater resource. With this grant increase, the grantee will continue education and outreach efforts with an emphasis on building public support for restoring the downtown section of the Flint River.

title: General Purposes
description: The Flint River Watershed Coalition was incorporated in 1998 and works to protect the Flint River, its shoreline, and connected tributaries. The Flint River is an important resource for the region’s residents, freshwater species, and other wildlife. With prior Mott support, the grantee conducted education and outreach efforts with an emphasis on building public support for restoring the downtown section of the Flint River. With renewed general purpose support, the grantee will continue to engage in riverfront development planning and implementation, operate youth and adult environmental education programs, and conduct its own organizational assessment to improve its capacity to protect the Flint River watershed.

title: General Purposes
description: The Flint River and its tributaries are an important recreational resource for the region’s residents while also providing important habitat for a variety of freshwater species and other wildlife. The Flint River Watershed Coalition works to protect the Flint River and its tributaries, which includes efforts to correct misconceptions about the river’s generally good and improving health. With renewal support, the grantee will maintain all of its education and outreach efforts as well as attend to its own organizational development needs. This will include efforts to enhance the urban sections of the river in Flint and designate the entire 142-mile stretch of the river as a National Water Trail.

title: General Purposes
description: Incorporated in 1998, the Flint River Watershed Coalition represents concerned citizens, local government, business interests, educational institutions, and others who feel strongly that the Flint River and its tributaries are vital resources that need to be protected, preserved, and improved. With offices located in Flint, Michigan, the coalition works within seven counties throughout the nearly 1,400 square mile watershed. This general purpose grant will support the coalition’s efforts to improve public understanding of the values of the Flint River, engage citizens in active watershed stewardship, restore the health of the Flint River ecosystem, and strengthen its organizational capacity.

title: Alabama Urban Stormwater Project
description: The Mobile Baykeeper works to protect and restore water quality in the Mobile Bay drainage basin, which covers two-thirds of Alabama and is the fourth largest watershed in North America. With past Mott support, the grantee helped strengthen Alabama’s stormwater policies by coordinating citizen participation in policy review processes, educating local officials and private-sector partners, and training citizens to monitor stormwater programs. With this grant renewal, the organization will continue these efforts while reinforcing local implementation of the full range of stormwater protections. A portion of the grant will also be used to help coordinate the Alabama nonprofit community’s response to the Gulf of Mexico oil spill.

title: Alabama Urban Stormwater Project
description: With more than 3,500 members across the state, Mobile Baykeeper seeks to protect and restore Alabama’s largest freshwater system — the Mobile Bay watershed. With prior Mott support, the grantee worked to reduce stormwater pollution, one of the most significant threats to the rivers draining into Mobile Bay. Specifically, the grantee helped strengthen Alabama’s stormwater policies by engaging in policy review processes, educating local officials and private sector partners, and training citizens to monitor stormwater programs. The grantee also helped advance the restoration of Alabama’s coastal wetlands after the 2010 oil drilling disaster in the Gulf of Mexico. This grant increase will allow the grantee to continue protecting water quality in Alabama by informing state-level stormwater policy reform processes and engaging in state and regional efforts to address ongoing oil spill impacts.

title: Alabama Urban Stormwater Project
description: Stormwater runoff in urban areas is one of the top water quality threats across Alabama. Fortunately, many of the state’s stormwater pollution control programs are up for review. The Mobile Baykeeper, a well-established group with statewide reach, will lead a collaborative effort to influence the outcome of these policy review processes as well as the implementation of the rules that result. Specific activities will include coordinating the participation of citizens in the administrative rulemaking processes, educating local officials and private-sector partners on the benefits of environmentally friendly development practices, and training citizens to monitor implementation of the stormwater programs.

title: Flow 2008 Project
description: The Instream Flow Council, a nongovernmental organization formed by state and provincial agency personnel in the United States and Canada, works to improve the effectiveness of instream flow policies through a variety of programs, including an annual meeting. For the first time, the council is opening its annual conference to a wider audience, including freshwater conservation organizations from the Great Lakes basin and southeastern United States. The conference will provide scientific, policy, and networking assistance to attendees, with a goal of improving the ability of diverse stakeholders to cooperatively solve instream flow problems in the United States and Canada. Mott funds will be used to subsidize the participation of smaller nonprofit organizations as well cover other conference expenses.

title: General Purposes
description: The Grand Traverse Regional Land Conservancy, a land trust serving a five-county region in northwest lower Michigan, has protected over 33,000 acres and manages 33 nature preserves. In 2009, the conservancy made substantial progress in a number of areas, including: protecting more than 900 additional acres, maintaining over 30 miles of trails and building new trails, becoming a nationally accredited land trust, and operating a very successful volunteer program. With continued general purpose support, the conservancy will maintain its multipronged approach to protecting the land and water resources of its region, which will include an emphasis on preserving lands in key river corridors. The conservancy will also build its own organizational capacity through a variety of means during the grant period.

title: General Purposes
description: The Grand Traverse Regional Land Conservancy, a land trust serving a five-county region in northwest lower Michigan, has protected over 36,500 acres and manages 33 nature preserves. In 2011 alone, the grantee made substantial progress in a number of areas, including: protecting more than 1,300 additional acres; building or improving hiking trails on three properties; hosting 110 events, such as public hikes and volunteer workdays; and monitoring the more than 200 conservation easements it holds. With continued general purpose support, the grantee will maintain its multipronged approach to protecting the land and water resources of its region, while also building its own organizational capacity through a variety of means.

title: General Purposes
description: The Grand Traverse Regional Land Conservancy, a land trust serving a five-county region in northern Michigan, has conserved over 34,000 acres, protected more than 100 miles of shoreline, and manages 34 nature preserves. Over the last two years, the grantee made substantial progress in a number of areas, including: protecting more than 1,000 additional acres; building 10 miles of additional hiking trails; engaging in policy discussions that impact land conservation in Michigan; and updating their strategic plan. With continued general purpose support, the grantee will maintain its multipronged approach to protecting the land and water resources of its region, while also building its own organizational capacity through a variety of means.

title: General Purposes
description: The Grand Traverse Regional Land Conservancy serves a five-county region in northwest lower Michigan. The grantee has protected over 39,000 acres and 121 miles of shoreline, and manages 34 nature preserves. Over the last two years, the grantee hosted 38 events, hikes, bike rides, and demonstrations that drew more than 500 participants from within the region. With continued general purpose support, the grantee will maintain the full suite of its programs and launch a new capital campaign.

title: General Purposes
description: The Grand Traverse Regional Land Conservancy, founded in 1991, is a land trust serving a five-county region in northwest lower Michigan. During the last grant period, the grantee launched a multiyear capital campaign to accelerate its work to protect and maintain important natural areas, scenic views, and farmland in its service area. Thus far, the campaign has been quite successful, and this grant renewal will help the grantee maintain the campaign’s momentum. The grantee will also continue to build its organizational capacity so that it remains a high-performing land trust.

title: General Purposes
description: The Grand Traverse Regional Land Conservancy, a land trust serving a five-county region in northwest lower Michigan, has developed a comprehensive land and water conservation vision which identifies about 60,000 acres of priority working lands and 60,000 acres of natural lands that warrant some form of protection. General purpose support from the Mott Foundation will help the conservancy build the organizational capacity it needs to take on this ambitious agenda. Specific activities over the next two years will include developing and implementing the use of innovative conservation finance tools; refining the organization’s volunteer, annual giving, and communications programs; exploring new ways to collaborate with nontraditional partners; and developing a planned giving program.

title: Goodwill Staffing Services
description: Through its local and regional chapters, Goodwill Industries International, Inc., provides temporary staffing services to 14,600 people annually. The temporary staffing program is an integral component of the grantee’s mission of providing services to persons with disabilities or other disadvantageous conditions. This renewal grant will provide partial support to create a national network to strengthen staffing services for individuals with barriers to employment.

title: Goodwill Staffing Services
description: Through its local and regional chapters, Goodwill Industries International, Inc., provides temporary staffing services to 14,600 people annually. The temporary staffing program is an integral component of the grantee’s mission of providing services to persons with disabilities or other disadvantageous conditions. This grant increase will provide support to the grantee to serve its national network of alternative staffing.

title: Goodwill Staffing Services
description: Through its local and regional chapters, Goodwill Industries International, Inc., provides temporary staffing services to 14,600 people annually. The temporary staffing program is an integral component of the grantee’s mission of providing services to persons with disabilities or other disadvantageous conditions. This grant will provide partial support for Goodwill Industries International, Inc., to create a national network to strengthen its staffing services for individuals with barriers to employment.

title: Regional Advocacy Fund
description: The program goal is to strengthen the capacity of nongovernmental organizations in the Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, and Slovakia to influence public policy at the regional, national, and European Union levels.
