To this end, the Stefan Batory Foundation will survey the needs and capacities of national-level networks, coalitions, and umbrella organizations of nonprofits involved in advocacy work; provide tailor-made grantmaking and technical assistance programs; and facilitate networking among its grantees. In addition, the foundation will strengthen its capacity to design and manage international grantmaking programs. The foundation was established in 1988 by the American philanthropist George Soros and a group of Polish democratic leaders. For over 18 years, the foundation has been the primary nongovernmental source of funding for hundreds of Polish nonprofit organizations. The foundation has expanded its programs to other countries in the region, including Belarus, Moldova, and Ukraine.

title: Philanthropication thru Privatization Initiative
description: In 2008, together with the Johns Hopkins University Center for Civil Society Studies, the East-West Management Institute launched a Philanthropication thru Privatization project to explore and promote capturing a portion of the proceeds of privatization sales as a means for building community-based philanthropic endowments. The Mott Foundation provided early support to the project’s case-building phase during which the project’s implementers clarified the concept, conducted research to identify 539 cases of this phenomenon around the world, and generated a detailed analysis report. The next dissemination and implementation phase will involve the development of best-practice materials and guidance manuals, dissemination of project results, and assistance for the implementation of philanthropication thru privatization processes in four to six target countries. Founded in 1988, the East-West Management Institute works to strengthen democratic societies by bringing together government, civil society, and the private sector to build accountable, capable, and transparent institutions.

title: Philanthropication thru Privatization Initiative
description: In 2008, together with the Johns Hopkins University Center for Civil Society Studies, the East-West Management Institute launched a Philanthropication thru Privatization initiative to explore and promote capturing a portion of the proceeds of privatization sales as a means for building community-based philanthropic endowments. Crown achievements of the project thus far have been the publication of an in-depth report on the 540 instances of foundations created through such privatization transactions, a major international conference on the subject, the launch of a Web site, and the preparation of case studies and guidance materials. The next phase will involve further preparation and dissemination of best-practice materials and guidance manuals and assistance for the implementation of pilot projects in four to six target countries. Founded in 1988, the East-West Management Institute works to strengthen democratic societies by bringing together government, civil society, and the private sector to build accountable, capable, and transparent institutions.

title: Philanthropication thru Privatization Initiative
description: In 2008, together with the Johns Hopkins University Center for Civil Society Studies, the East-West Management Institute launched a Philanthropication thru Privatization Initiative to explore and promote capturing a portion of the proceeds of privatization sales or other forms of government transfer of assets as a means for building community-based philanthropic endowments. Project achievements thus far have been the identification of over 550 instances of foundations created through such transactions, two major international conferences on the subject, the launch of a website, the publication of a book called “Philanthropication Thru Privatization: Building Permanent Endowments for the Public Good,” launching several pilot efforts in widely disparate regions of the world, and the preparation of case studies and guidance materials on implementation. The next phase will involve the further development of case studies, the completion and dissemination of implementation guidance manuals, the preparation of a revised edition of the book, and assistance for the implementation of pilot projects in Uzbekistan, China, Brazil, and Africa. Founded in 1988, the East-West Management Institute works to strengthen democratic societies by bringing together government, civil society, and the private sector to build accountable, capable, and transparent institutions.

title: Philanthropication thru Privatization Initiative
description: In many less-developed regions of the world, privatization sales are a huge potential source of funds for community-focused philanthropic endowments. A number of examples exist around the world, such as healthcare conversion foundations in the United States and bank foundations in Italy. The East-West Management Institute, together with the Johns Hopkins University Center for Civil Society Studies, is launching a “Philanthropication thru Privatization” project to explore and promote capturing a portion of the proceeds of privatization sales as a means for building community-based philanthropic endowments. This grant will provide support for a planning and discovery phase during which a small core team will organize the initiative, investigate, and develop a list of examples from around the world of the creation of charitable endowments out of the privatization of formerly public or nonprofit assets, and determine promising pilot test areas for future “philanthropication thru privatization” campaigns and projects. Founded in 1988, the East-West Management Institute promotes the rule of law, civil society, and free market systems globally.

title: U.S. Nonprofit Infrastructure Study
description: The “Nonprofit Quarterly”, the nation’s premier journal on nonprofit practice and policy, recently completed a study on the current state of the support system for nonprofit organizations in the United States, with special attention paid to philanthropy and research. The study included mapping and analysis of nonprofit and philanthropic infrastructure, as well as interviews and articles by nonprofit experts. These were published in the Winter 2008 issue of “Nonprofit Quarterly”, which is being broadly distributed through national nonprofit and philanthropic networks. The grantee also provided the study’s funders with a report that included a trends analysis and recommendations, as well as additional studies on various aspects of nonprofit and philanthropic infrastructure. Additional funding will allow the grantee to study and write an article for its Summer 2009 issue on successful collaborations and partnerships among national infrastructure groups.

title: U.S. Nonprofit Infrastructure Study
description: Through its publishing arm, the “Nonprofit Quarterly”, the Nonprofit Information Networking Association will conduct a study examining the support infrastructure for the nonprofit sector and philanthropy. The research will result in a special “Nonprofit Quarterly” edition with 40,000 copies to be broadly distributed through national nonprofit and philanthropic networks. This edition will be an update and expansion of the last “Nonprofit Quarterly” special issue on the nonprofit sector infrastructure, which was published in 2004.

title: Sustaining Michigan Regional Skills Alliances
description: This grant to Public Policy Associates, Inc., will develop a base of knowledge about Regional Skills Alliances that does not currently exist. This work will allow the Mott Foundation to continue its catalytic role on sectoral workforce development in Michigan. Sectoral employment components such as Regional Skills Alliances can help companies increase their competitiveness and contribute to their regional economies. Regional Skill Alliances can also help attract more firms to an area once the area begins to be perceived as a hub for a particular industry. As these results become more widespread, Michigan’s economy should benefit.

title: Three Year Plan for Growth and Renewal in the City of Flint
description: This renewal grant to Genesee County Habitat for Humanity is for the second phase of a housing development plan. The organization is collaborating with neighborhood-based organizations, nonprofit housing organizations, and local units of government to construct 15 new homes in the Grand Traverse neighborhood over a three-year period from 2008-2010. This concentrated development, in a central Flint neighborhood, will include 250 hours of volunteer labor by each partner family, and each home will be ENERGY STAR Certified.

title: Three Year Plan for Growth and Renewal in the City of Flint
description: This renewal grant will allow Genesee County Habitat for Humanity to complete the third phase of a housing development project. Over the past two years, the organization collaborated with neighborhood-based groups, nonprofit housing agencies, and local units of government to construct 15 new and rehabilitated homes in the Grand Traverse neighborhood. Each partner family selected for a home is required to provide 250 hours of sweat equity, and every home will be Energy Star certified. Since 1990, Genesee County Habitat for Humanity has built 60 homes in Genesee County.

title: Three Year Plan for Growth and Renewal in the City of Flint
description: Genesee County Habitat for Humanity works to eliminate poverty and homelessness by partnering with low- and moderate-income families to construct new homes. The organization is partnering with neighborhood-based organizations, nonprofit housing organizations, and local units of government to construct 15 new homes in the Grand Traverse neighborhood over the next three years. This concentrated development in a central Flint neighborhood will include 250 hours of volunteer labor by each partner family, and each home will be Energy Star certified.

title: Civil Initiatives for Public Benefit Support Service
grantee: Civic Analysis and Independent Research Center
description: The program goal is to promote effective civic activism among informal citizen groups in Russia. The grantee will strengthen its public consultation and mentoring services for such groups. It will further develop its online database of learning resources and successful case studies and will work to foster peer learning among initiative groups. Regular public events and dialogue will focus on equipping both civic organizations and local authorities with the understanding necessary to promote more effective and responsive government services. In 2008-2009, the grantee staged over 80 such events. Through its interregional Civil Policy School, it brought together organizations from across Russia to contribute recommendations on government reforms of the interior ministry and police. The Civic Analysis and Independent Research Center was established in 2007 by a group of Perm-based human rights groups seeking to support the development of a new generation of rights activists in Russia.

title: Civil Initiatives for Public Benefit Support Service
grantee: Civic Analysis and Independent Research Center
description: The program goal is to promote effective civic activism among informal citizen groups in Russia. The grantee will facilitate a series of capacity building workshops and related events for civic groups. They will also work to develop popular public spaces to foster and promote active citizenship. In addition, regular public events and dialogue will focus on equipping both civic groups and local authorities with the understanding necessary to promote more effective and responsive government service. Working with a variety of local groups in 2010-2011, the grantee succeeded in limiting a reduction of obstetric services in local hospitals, reducing administrative burdens on small businesses, and securing public oversight of planning and development in Perm. The Civic Analysis and Independent Research Center was established in 2007 by a group of Perm-based human rights groups seeking to support the development of a new generation of rights activists in Russia.

title: Civil Initiatives for Public Benefit Support Service
grantee: Civic Analysis and Independent Research Center
description: The Civic Analysis and Independent Research Center was established in 2007 at the recommendation of an informal group of Perm-based human rights and advocacy organizations. The grantee focuses on providing apolitical support to citizens and civic groups seeking information and assistance across a range of social, economic, environmental, and cultural rights issues. With this increase, the grantee will conduct additional research into the communications tools and strategies available to civic activists in Russia. The results of this research will help the grantee provide more focused assistance to organizations and initiative groups using the public benefit support service.

title: Civil Initiatives for Public Benefit Support Service
description: The program goal is to promote effective civic activism among both organized and informal citizen groups in Russia. The Productive Initiatives Development Society will take over responsibility for delivery of support services for regional civic organizations from its partner, the Civic Analysis and Independent Research Center. The grantee will provide training and consulting support to local civic groups seeking to solve practical public interest issues. They will also strengthen peer-to-peer networks of citizens and nonprofits to improve skill sharing among local actors committed to improving local quality of life. In 2014, the grantee carried out a range of targeted trainings, consultations, and public workshops reaching over 6,000 engaged citizens. Through the Understandable City and Understandable Healthcare projects, the grantee and local partners produced information about local city services and healthcare to help make these more accessible to local inhabitants. The Productive Initiatives Development Society was established in 1998 by a group of Perm-based civic activists seeking to support the development of a new generation of rights activists and active citizens in Russia.

title: Civil Initiatives for Public Benefit Support Service
grantee: Civic Analysis and Independent Research Center
description: The program goal is to promote capacities for civic awareness and effective civic activism among informal citizen groups in Russia. The grantee will establish a public reception and consultation center for such groups seeking assistance in asserting or defending social, economic, and civil rights in the face of administrative or other violations. It will also create and maintain a “virtual”, Internet-based consulting service and discussion forum, with an associated library of information resources. A civil policy school will be held in the second year of the project, bringing together representatives of groups from other parts of Russia who previously benefited from virtual consultations and subsequently executed effective projects. The Civic Analysis and Independent Research Center was established in 2007 by a group of Perm-based human rights groups seeking to support the development of a new generation of rights activists in Russia.

title: General Purposes
description: The project goal is to strengthen the capacity of nongovernmental organizations in Bulgaria to use Internet communication technology to engage effectively in public policy development and advocacy. To this end, the BlueLink Foundation will maintain an Internet portal through which Bulgarian nongovernmental organizations communicate, network, share, and engage in joint activities; provide training and technical assistance to nongovernmental organizations in networking, advocacy, and effective use of electronic communication tools; and develop specific tools for online communication, campaigning, and advocacy. In 2008-2009, the grantee provided cutting-edge, practical, and effective information and communication services to its clients; developed its independent media products; and participated in national and international partnerships and joint projects. The BlueLink Foundation was established in 1999 and supports Bulgarian nonprofit organizations to use the Internet and electronic communication as strategic tools for achieving their missions.

title: General Purposes
description: The project goal is to strengthen the capacity of nongovernmental organizations in Bulgaria to use Internet communication technology to engage effectively in public policy development and advocacy. To this end, the BlueLink Foundation will maintain an Internet portal through which Bulgarian nongovernmental organizations may communicate, network, share, and engage in joint activities; provide training and technical assistance to nongovernmental organizations in networking, advocacy, and effective use of electronic communication tools; develop specific tools for online communication, campaigning, and advocacy; and strengthen its organizational capacity and financial sustainability. The BlueLink Foundation was established in 1999 and supports Bulgarian nonprofit organizations to use the Internet and electronic communication as strategic tools for achieving their missions.

title: Flint GM 100th Celebration
description: The Genesee County Historical Society will produce a series of community celebration events to celebrate the 100-year anniversary of General Motors during the week of July 13-20, 2008. Events will be organized around the Buick Club of America’s National Meet that will be held on the grounds of the Flint Cultural Center from July 16-19, 2008.

title: Scaling Up Career Paths for the Low-Skilled at Community Colleges
description: This renewal grant to Jobs for the Future, in partnership with the National Council for Workforce Education, will support a new generation of college innovation, building from Breaking Through, a national initiative aimed at expanding effective strategies for helping low-skilled, low-income adults enter and succeed in community college occupational degree and credential programs, and succeed in the labor market.

title: Scaling Up Career Paths for the Low-Skilled at Community Colleges
description: This renewal grant to Jobs for the Future, in partnership with the National Council on Workforce Education, will support a new generation of college innovation building off of Breaking Through. Breaking Through is a national initiative aimed at expanding effective strategies for helping low-skilled, low-income adults enter and succeed in community college occupational degree and credential programs and succeed in the labor market. Portland Community College and the Community College of Denver will implement the final steps in their plans to scale up their successful Breaking Through demonstration projects. Their work will continue to be tracked closely by robust data collection and a rigorous evaluation.

title: Scaling Up Career Paths for the Low-Skilled at Community Colleges
description: This renewal grant to Jobs for the Future, in partnership with the National Council on Workforce Education, will support a national meeting of community college learning networks and associated capacity building and leadership development activities associated with Breaking Through, an initiative aimed at expanding effective strategies for helping low-skilled, low-income adults enter and succeed in community college occupational degree and credential programs and then succeed in the labor market.

title: Scaling Up Career Paths for the Low-Skilled at Community Colleges
description: Jobs for the Future, in partnership with the National Council for Workforce Education, will support a new generation of college innovation building upon “Breaking Through”, an earlier Mott Foundation-supported national initiative. This initiative is aimed at expanding effective strategies for helping low-skilled, low-income adults enter and succeed in community college occupational degree/credential programs and subsequently succeed in the labor market.

title: Creating Career Paths for the Low-Skilled in Michigan Colleges
description: This renewal grant will continue the highly productive state community college network activities begun in 2008, add development education as a policy and program priority for the state, and continue to build the network’s capacity and influence to prepare low-skilled adults for post-secondary pathways to occupational credentials.

title: Creating Career Paths for the Low-Skilled in Michigan Colleges
description: Jobs for the Future, in partnership with the National Council for Workforce Education, seeks renewal funding to support a state-level, community college initiative in Michigan, including Mott Community College, that will create and expand pathways designed to move low-skilled adults to college-level certificates and degrees.

title: Creating Career Paths for the Low-Skilled in Michigan Colleges
description: This grant to Jobs for the Future, in partnership with the National Council for Workforce Education, will support a state-level community college initiative in Michigan that will create and expand pathways designed to move low-skilled adults to college-level certificates and degrees.

title: Creating Career Paths for the Low-Skilled in High Poverty Areas
description: Jobs for the Future, in partnership with the National Council for Workforce Education, will implement a High Poverty Area Initiative to build and strengthen post-secondary pathways for low-skilled adults in the Lower Rio Grande Valley. The High Poverty Area Initiative is building upon the implementation design and strategies used previously in Breaking Through, including a funded demonstration site and local/national peer learning opportunities, as well as adapting the Breaking Through structure to a multisector, regional partnership with closely aligned postsecondary and workforce development agendas.

title: Creating Career Paths for the Low-Skilled in High Poverty Areas
description: This renewal grant will enable Jobs for the Future, in partnership with the National Council on Workforce Education, to implement a high poverty area initiative to build and strengthen postsecondary pathways for low-skilled adults in the Lower Rio Grande Valley in Texas. Both a healthcare and green construction sectoral initiative will be developed at South Texas College for low-skilled adults, including adults in the region with low literacy skills in Spanish.

title: Creating Career Paths for the Low-Skilled in High Poverty Areas
description: This renewal grant will enable Jobs for the Future, in partnership with the National Council on Workforce Education, to continue a high poverty area initiative to build and strengthen postsecondary pathways for low-skilled adults in the Lower Rio Grande Valley in Texas. Both a healthcare and green construction sectoral workforce training initiative have been developed at South Texas College for low-skilled adults, including adults in the region with low literacy skills in Spanish.

title: Creating Career Paths for the Low-Skilled in High Poverty Areas
description: This grant will allow Jobs for the Future and its partner, the National Council for Workforce Education, to identify, support, and convene a network of community colleges located in the Lower Rio Grande Valley that have an institutional commitment and capacity to move adults with low skills to college-level certificates and degrees. This initiative would build upon and connect to current networking practices and implementation strategies pioneered by Jobs for the Future in a previous Mott Foundation-funded program that enabled adult students to enter and succeed in community college occupational degree and credential programs. Over three years, the scope of work will include a funded demonstration project at one college in the Lower Rio Grande Valley; a robust peer learning network among a set of interested colleges located there; connection to the national community college learning network; and technical assistance, knowledge development, and network facilitation. This first-year grant is envisioned as a period to lay the groundwork for a full-scale launch of the high poverty area initiative beginning in the second year.

title: Capturing Synergy of IDB Meetings to Build Latino Immigrant Capacity
geographic_focus: Caribbean, Central America, Mexico, South America, United States
description: The National Alliance of Latin American and Caribbean Communities is a network of community-based organizations led by immigrants from Latin America and the Caribbean, which seeks to build transnational leadership capacity in order to advocate effectively for public policies that address the root causes of migration. This grant will support a capacity-building program for Latin American and Caribbean immigrants, focused on international financial flows and regional integration. This capacity building will include coordinated advocacy, media and communication, and overall public education work around the 50th anniversary of the Inter-American Development Bank, which will be marked in 2009.

title: Building Latino Immigrant Capacity on Regional Integration
description: The National Alliance of Latin American & Caribbean Communities is a network of community-based organizations led by immigrants from Latin America and the Caribbean. Over the past grant period, the grantee worked to ensure that there is improved evaluation of the impacts of the Inter-American Development Bank’s lending and that measures are in place to ensure that this bank’s investments are climate-friendly. This renewal grant will continue to support a capacity building program for Latin American and Caribbean immigrants focused on international financial flows and regional integration.

title: Building Latino Immigrant Capacity on Regional Integration
description: The National Alliance of Latin American & Caribbean Communities is a network of community-based organizations led by immigrants from Latin America and the Caribbean. Over the past grant period, the grantee worked to ensure that a better understanding of the relationship between migration and development, as well as the role that international financial institution lending plays in this nexus. This grant will continue to support capacity building for Latin American and Caribbean immigrant leaders to understand and articulate alternative and sustainable visions for development, as well as strategies for associated regional integration and investment.

title: Capturing Synergy of IDB Meetings to Build Latino Immigrant Capacity
description: The National Alliance of Latin American and Caribbean Communities will use the opportunity of the 2008 annual meeting of the Inter-American Development Bank, to be held in Miami, to bring together nongovernmental organizations in the United States, working on international environment and development issues, and Latin American immigrant leaders to address the environmental and social impacts of investments in Latin America. In coordination with other Mott grantees, the grantee will organize a series of workshops leading up to the annual meeting, as well as a public forum during the meeting. In addition, they will work with other nongovernmental organizations to organize seminars and workshop events to be held parallel to the official meeting.

title: Endowment for Sustainable Future
description: The program goal is to strengthen the financial sustainability of a leading Czech foundation whose mission is to promote and strengthen civil society in the Czech Republic. To this end, VIA Foundation will run an endowment-building program to raise at least $1 million and increase its total endowment to $3.3 million by the end of 2012. In addition, the foundation will strengthen its overall fundraising strategies and capacities. The foundation was established in 1997 as the successor organization of the American Foundation for a Civil Society. Since its establishment, the foundation has provided grants to more than 2,000 projects of nonprofit organizations in the Czech Republic, Slovakia, and Ukraine. In addition to grant support, the foundation provides capacity-building and networking opportunities to its grantees and actively participates in policy development relating to civil society and philanthropy.

title: Endowment for Sustainable Future
description: The program goal is to strengthen the financial sustainability of a leading Slovak foundation whose mission is to support systemic reforms of social service provision, increase the quality of life of socially disadvantaged groups, and strengthen social cohesion of Slovak society. To this end, Socia – Social Reform Foundation will run an endowment-building program to raise $600,000 and increase its total endowment to at least $1 million by the end of 2012. In addition, the foundation will strengthen its overall fundraising strategies and capacities and replace its foreign funding sources with local sources. The foundation is the successor organization of the work of the Cooperating Netherlands Foundations and was registered in May 2002. During 2002-2006, the foundation has distributed over $3.4 million in grants. In addition to grant support, the foundation provides capacity-building and networking opportunities to its grantees and actively participates in policy development relating to social services.

title: PHI - Michigan
description: This grant renewal will allow PHI to continue to deepen its presence in Michigan by improving career advancement opportunities and the training infrastructure for direct-care healthcare workers in the state. PHI will help secure expanded healthcare coverage for thousands of direct-care healthcare workers in Michigan who do not have healthcare coverage, and assisting Michigan direct-service healthcare workers to attain measurable progress toward economic self reliance. Finally, through this grant, PHI will continue building a Michigan-based PHI Midwest Regional Center to expand the impact of its efforts to other states in the region.

title: PHI - Michigan
description: This grant renewal will allow PHI to continue to deepen its presence in Michigan by improving career advancement opportunities and the training infrastructure for direct-care healthcare workers in the state, and assist Michigan direct-care workers to attain measurable progress toward economic self-reliance. Finally, through this grant, the grantee will continue building a Michigan-based PHI Midwest Regional Center to expand the impact of its efforts to other states in the region.

title: PHI - Michigan
description: This renewal grant will focus on improving the jobs of the direct-care workforce in Michigan. The grantee will inform public policymakers in Michigan of direct-care workforce issues through distribution of its revised Michigan Direct-Care Workforce Fact Sheet and other state and national research and data. PHI will also expand its work to help direct-care workers achieve economic self-sufficiency through a targeted income enhancement initiative, will work as part of a consumer coalition to assist state policymakers with implementation of the Affordable Care Act helping to ensure that it provides the best possible benefits for this workforce, and will pursue long-term care training initiatives in Michigan with a particular focus on playing a strong role in the state’s Personal and Home Care Aide State Training Program.

title: PHI - Michigan
description: This renewal grant will focus on improving the jobs of the direct-care workforce in Michigan. The grantee will inform public policymakers in Michigan about direct-care workforce issues through distribution of its revised Michigan Direct-Care Workforce Fact Sheet and other state and national research and data. PHI will also expand its work to help direct-care workers achieve economic self-sufficiency through a consumer coalition to assist state policymakers with the implementation of the Affordable Care Act. The effort will help ensure the best possible benefits for this workforce, and pursue long-term care training initiatives in Michigan with a particular focus on playing a strong role in the state’s personal and home care aide state training program.

title: PHI - Michigan
description: This renewal grant will focus on improving the jobs of the direct-care workforce in Michigan. PHI will inform public policymakers in Michigan about direct-care workforce issues through distribution of its revised Michigan Direct-Care Workforce Fact Sheet and other state and national research and data. The grantee will also expand its work to help direct-care workers achieve economic self-sufficiency through consumer coalitions to assist state policymakers with the implementation of the Affordable Care Act. The effort will help ensure the best possible benefits for this workforce, and pursue long-term care training initiatives in Michigan with a particular focus on playing a strong role in the state’s personal and Home Care Aid State Training Program.

title: PHI - Michigan
description: This grant will allow PHI to deepen its presence in Michigan by: improving career advancement opportunities and the training infrastructure for direct service healthcare workers in the state; securing expanded healthcare coverage for thousands of direct service healthcare workers in Michigan who do not have healthcare coverage; and helping Michigan direct service healthcare workers to attain measurable progress toward economic self-reliance. Finally, through this grant, PHI will begin to establish a Michigan-based PHI Midwest Regional Center to expand the impact of its efforts to other states in the region.

title: Building Communication Capacity
description: This renewal grant to PHI will enable the organization to continue to enhance its communications capabilities. Specifically, it will allow PHI to hire consultants to develop media plans; produce professional, learner-centered curricula that allows for the dissemination of PHI’s unique training programs; improve its national clearinghouse on direct service healthcare workforce employment; and increase its usage of new Internet tools.

title: Building Communication Capacity
description: This renewal grant to PHI will enable the organization to continue to enhance its communications capabilities. Specifically, the grantee will strengthen federal and state policy communications, enhance their online presence, strengthen how they market their training services, develop new curricula and other publications, and expand their media presence.

title: Building Communication Capacity
description: This grant to PHI will enable the organization to enhance its communications capabilities. Specifically, it will allow PHI to increase its number of staff professionals; consolidate and upgrade its Website; hire consultants to develop media plans; produce professional, learner-centered curricula that allow for the dissemination of PHI’s unique training programs; improve its national clearinghouse on direct service healthcare workforce employment; and increase its usage of new Internet tools.

title: Community Foundation History Project
description: This grant provides support for the research and writing of a book on the history of community foundations in the United States on the occasion of the 100th anniversary in 2014 of the establishment of the first community foundation. The author of the book is Eleanor Sacks, a historian who also has extensive practitioner and consulting experience in the community foundation field. The Lilly Family School of Philanthropy at Indiana University is overseeing the project. Although the manuscript is not expected to be published until 2015, a preview booklet of the content, which will set the history of United States community foundations in a global context, will be available in 2014. The booklet will be shared at venues such as the biennial conference of the International Society for Third Sector Research in Muenster, Germany, and at the Council on Foundations’ fall conference for community foundations in Cleveland, Ohio.

title: Community Foundation History Project
description: This grant to Indiana University-Purdue University Indianapolis provides support for the research and writing of a book on the history of community foundations in the United States. The manuscript will be finished in 2013 and published in 2014 to coincide with the 100th anniversary of the establishment of the first community foundation. The book will be scholarly, but also accessible to a more general audience, which will include academic researchers, as well as community foundation practitioners, public policymakers, and donors, both nationally and internationally. The Center on Philanthropy at Indiana University will oversee the project. The author will be Eleanor Sacks, a historian who also has extensive practitioner and consulting experience in the community foundation field.

title: Facility Renovation and Capacity Building
grantee: Family Service Agency of Mid Michigan
description: The Family Service Agency of Mid Michigan was founded in 1945 with a grant from the Junior League of Flint and the Council of Social Agencies. In 2007, the agency merged with the Visually Impaired Center to better serve low-income families in Genesee County. The Family Service Agency of Mid Michigan offers children and family services, in-home eldercare, legal guardianship, Social Security representative payee services, and services for the visually impaired. These populations, which are among the community’s most vulnerable, are growing in size, and services for them are desperately needed. As a result of the recent merger with the Visually Impaired Center, the agency now owns a building which is in an ideal location, but needs considerable renovation in order to be suitable for its needs. This grant will assist with renovations and associated building costs in order for the Family Service Agency of Mid Michigan to better serve its clients.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant continues general purpose support to the Direct Care Alliance. The organization is a nationwide and state-based alliance of direct-care workers, employers, and people of all ages and disabilities who use long-term services, care, and supports. First initiated as a project of the Paraprofessional Healthcare Institute, the alliance works at the intersection of three key policy issues: 1) quality long-term care for consumers; 2) workforce development for low-income workers; and 3) economic and social justice for women. The alliance addresses these issues by directly engaging key stakeholders — workers, consumers, and employers — in grassroots advocacy initiatives.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant constitutes the third and final renewal of general purpose support to Direct Care Alliance, Inc. The goal of Direct Care Alliance is to build an empowered and valued professional, direct-service healthcare workforce, which is essential to ensuring high quality services, a life of dignity and respect, autonomy, and opportunity for all to participate in community life.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant to the Direct Care Alliance, Inc., will launch a comprehensive, multiyear, multipronged strategy to improve working conditions for direct-care workers and address the policy and social barriers that ignore and undervalue the essential direct-care workforce sector. The goal is to improve the long-term care workforce with appropriate training, pay, benefits, and other supports, thereby stabilizing the fastest growing sector in healthcare, improving the lives of hundreds of thousands of working women and their families, and enabling our nation’s elders to enjoy independent living with quality of care, services, and supports.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Parent Teacher Home Visit Project Inc.
description: The Parent/Teacher Home Visit Project began as a project of Sacramento Area Congregations Together, an affiliate of PICO National Network. The project proved to be successful, and in 2002, the grantee was separately incorporated in order to facilitate the expansion of the project. Working with local community groups, project staff provides training to parents and teachers for effective home visits which have improved student outcomes. The success led the California State legislature to appropriate funds for teacher pay and training to districts throughout California, and the project is being replicated in other localities across the country.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Parent Teacher Home Visit Project Inc.
description: The Parent/Teacher Home Visit Project works with local community groups to provide training to parents and teachers on effective home visits, which have been shown to improve student outcomes. This success led the California State Legislature to appropriate funds for teacher pay and training to districts throughout California, and the project is also being replicated in other localities across the country. This grant increase will provide partial support for the launch of a new national data collection and analysis plan and the formation of a national advisory committee to guide future expansion.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Parent Teacher Home Visit Project Inc.
description: The Parent/Teacher Home Visit Project began as a project of Sacramento Area Congregations Together, an affiliate of PICO National Network. The project proved to be successful, and in 2002, the Parent/Teacher Home Visit Project was separately incorporated in order to facilitate the expansion. The model is now being replicated across the country. Working with local community groups, the staff provides training to parents and teachers for effective home visits which have improved student outcomes.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Parent Teacher Home Visit Project Inc.
description: The Parent/Teacher Home Visit Project began as a project of Sacramento Area Congregations Together, an affiliate of PICO National Network. The project proved to be successful, and in 2002, the Parent/Teacher Home Visit Project was separately incorporated in order to facilitate the expansion of the project. Working with local community groups, project staff provides training to parents and teachers for effective home visits. The success led the California state legislature to appropriate funds for teacher pay and training to districts throughout California, and the project is being replicated in other locales across the country.

title: Evaluation of Income Security Strategies
description: This grant will enable Brandeis University’s Institute on Assets and Social Policy to conduct an external evaluation of asset-building grantmaking activities under the Mott Foundation’s Income Security portfolio between 2000 and 2007. This review will assess progress, relative to baseline, on the outcomes sought for the grantmaking portfolio. In addition to progress, the final evaluation report will show examples of how the asset-building grantmaking strategies have been expanded in the field; how the Mott Foundation’s work to inform policy, improve practice, and evaluate promising strategies influenced these efforts; and what impact the Foundation’s investment in these strategies had on poverty alleviation. The institute is dedicated to the social mobility of individuals and families, particularly those traditionally left out of the economic mainstream, and to the expansion of the middle class.

title: General Purposes
description: The Communications Network is an affinity group of foundation communications professionals whose mission is to improve the effectiveness and accountability of foundations by promoting and strengthening the strategic practice of communications in philanthropy. In 2008-2009, the grantee increased its membership from 200 to 350; offered online professional development programs; conducted research on emerging forms of digital communications technologies; and produced publications on topics designed to inform and advance communications practices. During 2010-2012, the grantee intends to: 1) increase membership to 500; 2) conduct research on topics related to social media and the role of communications professionals in advocacy efforts; 3) collect new demographic data and compare the findings to a previous study of foundations with communications-focused positions; and 4) offer high quality learning opportunities through annual conferences, a webinar series, an interactive Web site, and other social media tools.

title: General Purposes
description: The Communications Network is a membership organization that promotes the use of consistent, strategic communications as an integral part of effective philanthropy. The grantee connects communications professionals working in philanthropy and the nonprofit sector to each other for guidance and mentoring and regularly sponsors learning and networking opportunities through webinars and an annual conference. Over the past two years, the grantee’s membership has grown from 350 to 480 members; its annual conferences have drawn over 300 participants each time; and it has offered four webinars per year. Last year, the grantee revised its mission and scope to include communications professionals from nonprofit organizations, as well as foundations. During 2013-2015, the grantee will expand its membership to include nonprofit communications professionals and noncommunications staff at foundations. It will continue to offer online resources and programming, as well as its annual conferences.

title: General Purposes
description: The Communications Network is a membership organization that promotes the use of consistent, strategic communications as an integral part of effective social sector work. The network connects communications professionals working in foundations and nonprofit organizations to each other for guidance and mentoring, and regularly sponsors learning and networking opportunities. Over the past two years, the grantee’s membership has grown from 500 to 800 members. In 2015, its annual conference had a record 526 attendees. Other offerings during the past two years include a research study on social sector communicators, publication of a bi-annual print journal, a monthly e-newsletter, and 19 Webinars. The grantee recently adopted a new strategic plan with three main objectives: to provide thought leadership on strategic social sector communications, increase member and influencer engagement, and increase and diversify revenue.

title: General Purposes
description: The Communications Network is an affinity group of foundation communications professionals whose mission is to improve the effectiveness and accountability of foundations by promoting and strengthening the strategic practice of communications in philanthropy. Through regular programs, annual conferences, publications, and a Web site, the network offers members and other philanthropic stakeholders the opportunity to learn about effective practice as well as emerging trends. In 2008-2009, the Communications Network intends to: (1) increase membership from 200 to 300; (2) develop and promote a series of standards in foundation communications; (3) conduct an initial benchmarking survey to determine the current state of communications practice in foundations; (4) offer high quality learning opportunities through annual conferences, webinar series, and a revamped Web site; (5) develop an evaluation toolkit; and (6) conduct a study on improving foundation communications through new digital technologies.

title: Program Related Investment
description: ShoreBank Corporation is launching a $51,750,000 common equity fundraising effort to dramatically increase the scale and impact of its work that benefits low-income and other underserved communities by stimulating economic opportunity. This program-related investment will allow the Mott Foundation to purchase 133 shares of common stock, (2.66 Investment Units), 67 of which will have voting rights, at a cost of $997,500. This investment is being made because of ShoreBank Corporation’s enviable track record of stimulating economic opportunity for low-income people.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Regional Foundation for Local Development Zamah
description: The program goal is to encourage civic initiatives in rural communities in three counties in central Croatia. During the grant period, the Regional Foundation for Local Development Zamah will provide grants, organize training, raise public awareness about civic responsibility, and promote philanthropy. In 2008-2009, the foundation supported more than 80 projects totaling over $220,000. Direct grantmaking was complemented by training and roundtable discussions and work with local businesses and local government officials to encourage transparent and effective funding mechanisms for civic initiatives. In 2010-2011, the grantee will continue to support participatory community development initiatives with grants, capacity building, and technical assistance. The grantee will strengthen its organizational capacities by increasing the number of full-time staff to three and developing a volunteer and membership base. The grantee was established in 2006 and is based in Zagreb.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Regional Foundation for Local Development Zamah
description: The program goal is to encourage the economic and social development of rural communities in central Croatia. To this end, during the grant period the Regional Foundation for Local Development Zamah will provide grants, organize training, raise public awareness about civic responsibility, facilitate cross-sectoral cooperation, and promote philanthropy. In 2010-2011, the grantee supported more than 80 projects totaling approximately $200,000. The grantee also organized events to stimulate local philanthropy, including organizing the first Women’s Philanthropy Award. Direct grantmaking was also complemented by training and roundtable discussions and work with local businesses and local government officials to encourage transparent and effective funding mechanisms for civic initiatives. In 2012-2013, the grantee will continue to support participatory community development initiatives with grants and will diversify funding for this work by raising funds from local communities, businesses, and local governments for targeted grantmaking programs. The grantee will strengthen its organizational capacities by increasing the number of active volunteers. The grantee was established in 2006 and is based in Zagreb.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Regional Foundation for Local Development Zamah
description: The program goal is to encourage the economic and social development of rural communities in central Croatia. During the grant period, the Regional Foundation for Local Development Zamah will provide grants, organize training, raise public awareness about civic responsibility, facilitate cross-sectoral cooperation, encourage social entrepreneurship, and promote philanthropy. In 2012-2013, the grantee supported a wide range of community projects with direct grant support totaling more than $260,000 and by helping to secure local financial and in-kind donations. Direct grantmaking was complemented by trainings and technical assistance to recipients. The grantee also worked with local businesses and government officials to encourage transparent and effective funding mechanisms for civic initiatives. Through various events and activities, including an annual Women’s Philanthropy Award and workshops in primary schools, the grantee stimulated and promoted philanthropy. In 2014-2015, the grantee will continue to support participatory community development initiatives with grants and will diversify funding for this work by raising funds from individuals, businesses, and local governments. The grantee will strengthen its organizational capacities by increasing the number of staff. The grantee was established in 2006 and is based in Zagreb.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Regional Foundation for Local Development Zamah
description: The program goal is to encourage the economic and social development of rural and urban communities in central Croatia. During the grant period, the Regional Foundation for Local Development Zamah will provide grants, organize training, raise public awareness about civic responsibility, facilitate cross-sectoral cooperation, encourage social entrepreneurship, and promote philanthropy. In 2014-2015, the grantee supported 65 community projects with direct grant support totaling more than $160,000 and by helping to secure local financial and in-kind donations. Direct grantmaking was complemented by trainings and technical assistance to recipients. The grantee also worked with local businesses and government officials to encourage transparent and effective funding mechanisms for civic initiatives. In 2016-2017, the grantee will continue to support participatory community development initiatives with grants and will diversify funding for this work by raising funds from individuals, businesses, and local governments. Through various events and activities, including an annual Women’s Philanthropy Award and workshops in schools, the grantee will stimulate and promote philanthropy. The grantee was established in 2006 and is based in Zagreb.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Regional Foundation for Local Development Zamah
description: The program goal is to encourage civic initiatives in rural communities in four counties in central Croatia. To this end, the Regional Foundation for Local Development Zamah will provide grants, organize training, raise public awareness about civic responsibility, and carry out advocacy initiatives. In 2008, the grantee will make up to 50 grants totaling $136,500 to mobilize community-based resources to address local issues and concerns. Direct grantmaking will be complemented by work with local businesses and local government officials to encourage transparent and effective funding mechanisms for civic initiatives. As a new organization, the grantee will strengthen its organizational capacities by increasing the number of full-time staff to two, retaining reliable financial and accounting services, securing and outfitting adequate office space in Zagreb, and building contacts with key business leaders. The organization was established in 2006 by a group of community development experts working with the Center for Civil Initiatives, a long-time Mott grantee.

title: 2008 Assets Learning Conference
description: This grant will enable the Corporation for Enterprise Development to host the 2008 Assets Learning Conference, the premiere networking and learning event in the asset-building field. This year’s event will take place September 11-13, 2008, and provide an opportunity for leaders from all sectors to discuss the best ways to improve financial security for all Americans, but especially those from low- and moderate-income households. Headquartered in Washington, D.C., the Corporation for Enterprise Development is a longtime grantee of the Mott Foundation.

title: McCree-Ative Performing Arts Academy
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will support a year-round fine arts program for Flint’s innercity youth. One of the goals of the Floyd McCree Theatre is to instruct African-American youth in the fine arts and provide a venue to display their talent. Despite bold efforts made by several community organizations, including the Flint Youth Theatre, there is still a need for more youth-centered urban arts. To address the lack of accessible fine arts education, the Floyd McCree Theatre will offer fine arts programming that will train students in drama, music, and dance.

title: McCree-Ative Performing Arts Academy
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This renewal grant will support a yearlong fine arts program for Flint’s innercity youth. One of the goals of the Floyd McCree Theatre is to instruct African-American youth in the fine arts and provide a venue to display their talent. To address the lack of accessible fine arts education, the grantee will offer a program that will train students in drama, music, and dance.

title: McCree-Ative Summer Stock Academy
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will support a summer fine arts program for Flint’s inner-city youth. One of the goals of the Floyd McCree Theatre is to instruct African-American youth in the fine arts and provide a venue to display their talent. Despite bold efforts made by several community organizations, including the Flint Youth Theatre, there is still a void in the area of youth-centered urban arts. To address the lack of accessible fine arts education, the Floyd McCree Theatre will offer a pilot summer stock program that will train students in drama, music, and dance for ten weeks this summer. In the fall, the students will perform a classic African-American musical that will showcase their talents for the community.

title: Gear Up Michigan Project
description: This renewal grant to EduGuide will support a Web-based college readiness program. The program will provide assessments, personalized education roadmaps, and financial aid assistance for 1,000 families with high school students in the Flint area. EduGuide is a nongovernmental, educational support firm that works with universities, teachers, and families to increase student achievement, especially for first-generation college students.

title: Gear Up Michigan Project
description: This renewal grant to EduGuide will support a Web-based college readiness program. The program will provide online mentoring, academic assessments, personalized education roadmaps, and financial aid assistance for 1,500 families with high school students in the Flint area. EduGuide is a nongovernmental educational support firm that works with universities, teachers, and families to increase student achievement, especially for first-generation college students.

title: Gear Up Michigan Project
description: EduGuide is a nongovernmental educational support firm that works with universities, teachers, and families to increase student achievement, especially for first-generation college students. This renewal grant will provide college readiness information to economically disadvantaged high school students. The program will provide financial aid assistance, online mentoring, academic assessments, and personalized education roadmaps for high school students, primarily those enrolled at Flint Northern and Flint Northwestern.

title: GEAR UP Michigan Project
description: EduGuide, an educational nonprofit agency, has established a Web-based platform that provides online mentoring to students. From that platform, the grantee offers a host of online resources for children, parents, and professionals to establish developmental goals, recognize academic and social hurdles, and strategies to assist a child to reach and complete post-secondary education. This grant supports the grantee’s work in Flint to reach low-income and first-generation college students with e-mentoring and other online tools to help navigate the secondary and post-secondary educational systems.

title: Gear Up Michigan Project
description: This grant to Partnership for Learning will support a pilot, Web-based college readiness program. The program will provide assessments, personalized education roadmaps, and financial aid assistance for 400 families of ninth-graders in the Flint area. Partnership for Learning is a nongovernmental educational support firm that works with universities, teachers, and families to increase student achievement, especially for first-generation college students.

title: Nonprofit Listening Post Project
description: The Nonprofit Listening Post Project monitors in a systematic and timely way what is happening to nonprofit organizations in the United States. Key features include: a network of over 1,000 grassroots nonprofits that serve as the project’s listening posts on the major fieldwide developments; regular surveying of these organizations using a rapid turnaround, web-based technology; roundtable discussions among the innovative executives identified through these surveys; case studies examining particularly interesting innovations in more depth; and regular, broadly distributed communiqués on survey and roundtable results. A grant extension and increase will align the grant period with the project’s other funders and render more efficient planning and reporting. During this period, the project will examine local taxation of nonprofits, government contracting with nonprofits, and nonprofit charitable status. The project is conducted by the Center for Civil Society Studies at the Johns Hopkins University, one of America’s premier research universities.

title: Nonprofit Listening Post Project
description: The Nonprofit Listening Post Project monitors in a systematic and timely way what is happening to nonprofit organizations in the United States. Key features include a network of over 1,150 grassroots nonprofits that serve as the project’s listening posts on the major fieldwide developments; regular surveying of these organizations using a rapid turnaround, web-based technology; roundtable discussions among the innovative executives identified through these surveys; case studies examining particularly interesting innovations in more depth; and regular, broadly distributed communiqués on survey and roundtable results. Launched eight years ago, the project has had visible impact on policymakers, nonprofit practitioners, and foundations. During the upcoming grant period, likely topics to be examined include the nonprofit sector’s value proposition, nonprofit fee income, and government relations with nonprofits. The project is conducted by the Center for Civil Society Studies at Johns Hopkins University, one of America’s premier research universities.

title: Nonprofit Listening Post Project
description: The Nonprofit Listening Post Project monitors in a systematic and timely way what is happening to nonprofit organizations in the United States. Key features include a network of over 1,150 grassroots nonprofits that serve as the project’s listening posts on the major fieldwide developments; regular surveying of these organizations using a rapid turnaround, Web-based technology; roundtable discussions among the innovative executives identified through these surveys; case studies examining particularly interesting innovations in more depth; and regular, broadly distributed communiqués on survey and roundtable results. This grant increase will support the engagement of an outside consultant to help answer several important questions about the need for up-to-date data on key nonprofit trends and challenges and the value and effectiveness of the project in meeting this need. The project is conducted by the Center for Civil Society Studies at Johns Hopkins University, one of America’s premier research universities.

title: Nonprofit Listening Post Project
description: The Nonprofit Listening Post Project monitors in a systematic and timely way what is happening to nonprofit organizations in the United States. Key features include a network of over 1,150 grassroots nonprofits that serve as the project’s listening posts on the major fieldwide developments; regular surveying of these organizations using a rapid turnaround, Web-based technology; roundtable discussions among the innovative executives identified through these surveys; case studies examining particularly interesting innovations in more depth; and regular, broadly distributed communiqués on survey and roundtable results. This grant increase will support the completion of survey work and widespread dissemination of findings about the value proposition of the nonprofit sector, elevating the issue and stimulating a broader conversation on the topic at a time of great challenge to nonprofits. The project is conducted by the Center for Civil Society Studies at Johns Hopkins University, one of America’s premier research universities.

title: Nonprofit Listening Post Project
description: This grant supports the Nonprofit Listening Post Project of the Center for Civil Society Studies at Johns Hopkins University. The project is designed to improve the management and operation of nonprofit organizations and the policy environment within which they operate by equipping managers and board members, public policymakers, assistance providers, and other stakeholders with more timely information about the significant challenges facing American nonprofits and about the coping strategies that innovative nonprofit managers are applying in response to them. Launched five years ago, the project has had visible impact on policymakers, nonprofit practitioners, and foundations. In its next phase, the project will broaden its coverage both substantively and geographically. This will include the addition of a component by which an initial set of six states, including Michigan, will participate in national-level surveys, produce state-level reports, and organize activities. The Michigan Nonprofit Association will be an implementing partner.

title: Kearsley Street Connector
description: This grant will provide the University of Michigan-Flint with funds to reopen Kearsley Street through the campus. Kearsley Street, a cross street through central Flint, is currently closed to vehicular traffic through the university campus, which results in a perceived and real disconnect between key institutions and neighborhoods in central Flint. The reopened Kearsley Street will incorporate traffic-calming techniques that promote vehicular and pedestrian safety, noise and vibration-dampening methods for nearby classroom buildings, and attractive landscaping.

title: Building Capacity in Micro-Enterprise in Michigan
description: Local Initiatives Support Corporation is dedicated to helping nonprofit community development organizations transform distressed neighborhoods into healthy and sustainable communities of choice and opportunity — good places to work, do business, and raise children. This three-year grant will enable the grantee to provide technical assistance and capacity building support to Michigan’s micro-enterprise practitioners; coordinate a state micro-enterprise association; promote state policy that supports micro-enterprise development; and invest in local, regional or state micro-enterprise loan funds to increase access to capital for emerging entrepreneurs.

title: Back to the Bricks/Bikes on the Bricks
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Flint Area Convention & Visitors Bureau has worked in partnership with area car and motorcycle enthusiasts to develop two summertime events in downtown Flint: Back to the Bricks and Bikes on the Bricks. In four years, Back to the Bricks has grown from a small, one-day car show to a five-day event, while Bikes on the Bricks is developing into a major motorcycle show. This renewal grant will provide funds to expand on the success of both events.

title: Back to the Bricks/Bikes on the Bricks
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Flint Area Convention & Visitors Bureau has worked in partnership with area car and motorcycle enthusiasts to develop three summertime events in downtown Flint: Le Champion Pave, Back to the Bricks, and Bikes on the Bricks. Back to the Bricks has grown from a small, one-day car show in 2005, to a five-day event, while Bikes on the Bricks is developing into a major motorcycle show. This renewal grant will provide funds to expand on the success of both events by increasing advertising avenues. This is the inaugural year for the cycling race, Le Champion Pave. In 2009, the events attracted over 256,000 visitors and had approximately 28,000 cars and 3,000 motorcycles on display.

title: Back to the Bricks/Bikes on the Bricks
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Flint Area Convention & Visitors Bureau has worked in partnership with area car, motorcycle, and cycling enthusiasts to develop three summertime events in downtown Flint: Back to the Bricks, Bikes on the Bricks, and Le Champion Pave. Back to the Bricks has expanded from a small, one-day car show in 2005 to a five-day event, while Bikes on the Bricks is developing into a three-day show. In its inaugural year, 185 cyclists competed in Le Champion Pave. In 2010, the events attracted over 308,000 visitors to downtown Flint. This renewal grant will provide funds to expand on the success of each event.

title: Back to the Bricks/Bikes on the Bricks
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This renewal grant will assist the Genesee Area Focus Fund to publicize and promote two signature summer events in downtown Flint, the Back to the Bricks auto festival, and the Le Champion Pave bicycle race. Since it began in 2005, Back to the Bricks has grown from a one-day to a five-day event, which now attracts 35,000 participants and 450,000 spectators. Le Champion Pave, a professional cycling event launched last year, is expected to attract 350 racers, and 3,000-4,000 spectators. Together, these events help to improve the public perception of Flint as a destination for recreation and leisure.

title: Back to the Bricks Marketing
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: Back to the Bricks has grown from a small, one-day car show developed by the Flint Area Convention & Visitors Bureau in 2005, to a five-day event run by an independent nonprofit organization. In 2012, the events attracted over 500,000 visitors and had approximately 40,000 cars on display in downtown Flint. This grant will provide funds to help promote the event.

title: Back to the Bricks/Bikes on the Bricks
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Flint Area Convention & Visitors Bureau has worked in partnership with area car and motorcycle enthusiasts to develop two summertime events in downtown Flint: Back to the Bricks and Bikes on the Bricks. Back to the Bricks has grown from a small, one-day car show in 2005, to a four-day event, while Bikes on the Bricks is still in the beginning stages. In 2007, the events attracted over 50,000 visitors and had approximately 9,000 cars and 50 motorcycles on display. This grant will provide funds to expand on the success of both events by increasing advertising avenues.

title: Strategic Plan for Financial Stability and Realignment of Academic and Administrative Services
initiative: Historically and Predominantly Black Colleges and Universities
description: This grant will provide support to Fisk University for its financial stability and realignment of academic and administrative services. Among Historically Black Colleges and Universities, Fisk University consistently ranks among the top academically. Its 63 percent graduation rate is exemplary given its high number of low-income, first-generation college students. More Fisk alumni earn doctorate degrees in the natural sciences than African-American graduates from any other college or university in America. In order to maintain its tradition of excellence, the university is currently realigning its academic and administrative programs to address financial difficulties. Initial cost-saving measures include reducing administrator salaries, removing deferred maintenance from the budget, and discontinuing certain sports programs. At the same time, officials have begun implementing plans to increase revenue through enrollment management and fundraising.

title: Rethink Federal Aid to Elementary and Secondary Education
description: This grant will support the Center on Education Policy in adopting a research-based, factual approach to determine whether the right national policies for education are in place and what future national policies should look like. This project will include: 1) understanding effective approaches for increasing student learning; 2) assessing the respective roles in education of the federal, state, and local governments; 3) recognizing differences among the states; 4) balancing accountability with assistance, and 5) acknowledging factors outside the schools that have powerful effects on what happens within schools. The Center on Education Policy will assemble an advisory panel of respected education experts to determine specific details and commission 10-15 papers from nationally known experts for dissemination.

title: Comparative Rural Economy Survey
description: This grant will enable the Carsey Institute at the University of New Hampshire to conduct a comparative rural economy survey of Michigan’s Upper Peninsula. This survey will be used by Northern Initiatives, a nonprofit affiliate of ShoreBank Corporation, to aid local communities and small businesses in developing a regional strategy of marketing nature tourism opportunities. Finally, this comparative survey will allow the economy of the Upper Peninsula to be compared with other rural regions such as the Mississippi Delta and Appalachia.

title: GEAR UP College Day Program
description: This grant will support the GEAR UP College Day Program, a partnership between Central Michigan University and Flint Community Schools. GEAR UP is a national college readiness initiative that targets students in grades 7-12 to increase the number of students who successfully complete a post-secondary degree. By receiving mentoring, tutoring, parent education, and attending campus visits through participation in the GEAR UP program, students are better prepared to enter and complete a college degree program. This grant will also support an evaluation of the GEAR UP College Day Program.

title: GEAR UP College Day Program
description: This renewal grant will support the GEAR UP College Day Program, a partnership between Central Michigan University, Kettering University, and Flint Community Schools. GEAR UP is a national college readiness initiative that reaches students in grades 7-12, the purpose of which is to increase the number of students who successfully complete a post-secondary degree. By receiving mentoring, tutoring, and parent education, and attending campus visits through participation in the GEAR UP program, students are better prepared to enter and complete a college degree program.

title: GEAR UP College Day Program
description: Gaining Early Awareness and Readiness for Undergraduate Programs is a federally funded program designed to increase the number of low-income and disadvantaged students attending college. The state of Michigan receives and redistributes federal funds to various educational providers in the state. Central Michigan University received funding from the state of Michigan to work with Flint Community School and charter school enrollees living in the Flint area. This grant will support the work of Central Michigan University with a cohort of 100 students in grades 7-12 who are eligible for assistance through this program. By receiving mentoring, tutoring, parent education, and attending campus visits through participation, students are better prepared to enter and complete a college degree program.

title: GEAR UP College Day Program
description: This grant will provide partial support to the GEAR UP College Day program, a partnership between Central Michigan University and Flint Community Schools. GEAR UP is a national college readiness initiative that targets students in grades 7-12 and whose purpose is to increase the number of students who successfully complete a post-secondary degree. By receiving mentoring, tutoring, parent education, and attending campus visits through participation in the GEAR UP program, students are better prepared to enter and complete a college degree program. This grant will also support an evaluation of the GEAR UP College Day program.

title: Development of Human Capital Through Social Marketing
description: The program goal is to increase public understanding of and support for principles of human rights in Russia. Information Agency MEMO.RU will further develop and share its capacity to use social marketing techniques in targeted campaigns to foster active engagement of Russian citizens and to promote human rights. In 2009-2011, the grantee collaborated with the Andrei Sakharov Foundation to launch a fundraising campaign to support the creation of an apartment-museum, reaching over half the campaign goal in three months, and spawning a new youth movement promoting Sakharov’s democratic values. In 2012-2013, the grantee will expand its existing campaign promoting the values of Andrei Sakharov beyond Moscow. Additionally, it will use its experience in the Kirov region as a basis upon which to franchise the social marketing approach to local organizations. Information Agency MEMO.RU was established in 2002 as an information agency offshoot of the leading human rights organization Memorial with the aim of presenting information about human rights issues in a professional and widely accessible manner.

title: Development of Human Capital Through Social Marketing
description: The program goal is to increase public understanding of and support for principles of human rights and civic engagement in Russia. LLC MEMO will use social marketing techniques to foster active engagement of Russian citizens around rights-related issues. It will conduct sociological surveys to identify key issues around which people can organize and will conduct resulting online and offline marketing and advertising campaigns to foster engagement. In 2011-2013, the grantee’s nonprofit partner, Information Agency MEMO.RU, concluded its work in the Kirov region, having facilitated the development of a self-sustaining initiative group focused on local environmental issues. In the Vologda region, it initiated a campaign of historical preservation aimed at securing the region’s unique but threatened heritage of wooden architecture. LLC MEMO was established in 1997 as a commercial partner of Information Agency MEMO.RU. It provides a range of services aimed at promoting its partner’s public information and social marketing efforts. Profits generated by LLC MEMO are used to further support its nonprofit partner’s mission.

title: Development of Human Capital Through Social Marketing
description: The program goal is to increase public understanding of and support for principles of human rights and civic activism in Russia. To this end, Information Agency MEMO.RU will develop its capacity to use social marketing techniques including opinion surveys, focus groups, and resulting campaigns to foster active engagement of Russian citizens in civic life and in defense of human rights. Work will include a program aimed at promoting the democratic values of Andrei Sakharov. A series of campaigns will aim to increase civic activism of young people in the Kirov region. A “social franchising” component will focus on building capacity of regional partners to conduct effective social marketing campaigns on similar issues. Information Agency MEMO.RU was established in 2002 as an information agency offshoot of the leading human rights organization “Memorial” with the aim of presenting information about human rights issues in a professional and widely accessible manner.

title: Informing Public Policy
