description: The purpose of this grant to Opportunity Finance Network is to ensure broad awareness and understanding of the potential of Community Development Financial Institutions to contribute to sound, sustainable future policy solutions to the existing credit crisis. This funding will enable the grantee to produce and distribute informational and educational materials chronicling the solid track record community development credit unions, community development banks, and community development loan funds have achieved in lending to low-income borrowers. This educational campaign will be aimed at policy organizations, the media, and other financial interests.

title: Training for HUD Tenants
description: The Boston Affordable Housing Coalition was founded in 1983 to preserve and improve affordable housing, protect tenants’ rights, promote resident control and ownership, and improve the quality of life in U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development-assisted housing in Massachusetts. The organization has achieved a national reputation for its training programs. The purpose of this grant is to support a training program for board members and staff organizers from across the United States in order to provide updates on changes in federal and state regulations.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Martin Luther King, Jr. National Memorial Project Foundation, Inc.
description: This grant will provide support for the construction of the Martin Luther King, Jr. National Memorial in Washington, DC. The memorial will be situated on a four-acre site along the Tidal Basin, adjacent to the FDR Memorial and on a diagonal line between the Jefferson and Lincoln Memorials. It will be the first memorial on the National Mall honoring an average citizen — not a president or war veteran — and the first on the mall dedicated to a person of color. The design will highlight poignant excerpts of King’s writings and speeches on a 500-foot, crescent-shaped wall that will frame the memorial space. The National Park Service estimates that the memorial and its nearby visitors’ center will receive many of the 22 million people who visit the mall each year. Core construction is scheduled to begin in November 2008 with a plan to dedicate the memorial in 2010.

title: SFAI Succession Planning Technical Assistance
description: Succession planning is a sound risk management practice — it is critical to ensuring the continued effectiveness of an organization before and after a leadership transition. Since 1997, through its Executive Transitions program, CompassPoint Nonprofit Services has provided succession planning/leadership transition technical assistance to over 400 nonprofit organizations. This grant will enable the grantee to deliver such services to five of the Mott Foundation’s State Fiscal Analysis Initiative grantees, each of whom will undergo an executive and/or founder transition within the next three to four years. CompassPoint Nonprofit Services is a nonprofit organization whose mission is to increase the impact of Bay Area nonprofit, community-based organizations and the people who work and volunteer in them.

title: Great Lakes Urban Exchange
description: The Brookings Institution’s Metropolitan Policy Program provides decisionmakers with cutting-edge research and policy assessments for improving the health and prosperity of cities and metropolitan areas. Previous support for the institution’s Great Lakes Urban Exchange initiative created a network of young adults in metropolitan areas across Michigan and the other Great Lakes states to help increase the region’s pool of talented young people. With a grant renewal, this project will further develop its network and will help young leaders effectively engage in urban revitalization efforts in Michigan and the entire Great Lakes region.

title: Great Lakes Urban Exchange
description: The Metropolitan Policy Program of the Brookings Institution has established itself as a leading center that examines the role of public policy, private sector initiatives, and market forces and demographic changes in shaping metropolitan growth patterns. Recently, this has included identifying ways that communities can attract and retain talented young people. This grant will support the engagement of young adults in Michigan through the Great Lakes Urban Exchange, a project designed to build a network of young leaders in cities across the Great Lakes who will engage and link other young professionals in promoting the attributes of these urban communities.

title: Institutional Development Project
description: The project goal is to strengthen the community foundation field in Poland. During the grant period, the Federation of Polish Community Foundations will develop high quality services for members, attract new members, promote community foundations as vehicles for community development in Poland, and promote and develop local philanthropy. The grantee was registered in 2008 with the mission to strengthen the community foundation movement in Poland and promote local giving. Currently, the grantee has eight founding members and is working to expand its membership. There are 21 community foundations in Poland that serve about 3.5 million people on 10 percent of the territory of Poland. Since 1998, when the first Polish community foundations were established, the community foundations have accumulated over $2 million in endowment funds and awarded $4.2 million in small grants.

title: Institutional Development Project
description: The project goal is to strengthen the community foundation field in Poland. During the grant period, the Federation of Polish Community Foundations will develop high quality services for members, attract new members, promote community foundations as vehicles for community development in Poland, and promote and develop local philanthropy. The federation was registered in 2008 with the mission to strengthen the community foundation movement in Poland and promote local giving. Currently, the federation has eight founding members and is working to expand its membership. There are 21 community foundations in Poland that serve about 3.5 million people on 10 percent of the territory of Poland. Since 1998, when the first Polish community foundations were established, the community foundations have accumulated over $2 million in endowment funds and awarded $3.2 million in small grants.

title: Great Lakes Climate Change Adaptation Workshop
geographic_focus: Illinois, Indiana, Wisconsin, New York, Michigan, Pennsylvania, Ohio, Minnesota
description: The effects of climate change in the Great Lakes region are expected to be quite serious, impacting shipping channels, commercial fisheries, natural habitats, and more. To protect the region’s long-term economic, social, and environmental health, it will be necessary to integrate climate change information into the resource management decisions made by public and private organizations and make appropriate public policy adjustments. To assist in addressing this climate information gap, Michigan Sea Grant, part of the University of Michigan’s School of Natural Resources and Environment, will hold a workshop for selected members of the Great Lakes funding and policy community. Mott funds will provide partial support for the meeting activities, including the preparation of briefing materials in advance of the meeting and distribution of a final report with recommended action steps.

title: State Fiscal Policy Conference
grantee: Center on Budget and Policy Priorities
description: First held in 1994, the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities’ annual State Fiscal Policy conference is now the largest gathering of national- and state-level nonprofits that are concerned with the effect of budgets and tax policies on the public programs that aid low- and moderate-income families. At the event, attendees strengthen their analytical skills, develop relationships with peers in other states, and identify valuable resources to support their efforts. Mott support will enable the grantee to plan and host the 2008 conference, which will be held in Washington, D.C. in November. The Center on Budget and Policy Priorities was founded in 1981 to analyze federal budget priorities, with particular emphasis on the impact of various budget choices on low-income Americans.

title: Monitoring Kosovo Public Services
description: The project goal is to enhance public participation in decisionmaking processes by improving accountability and transparency of public service administration at local levels in Kosovo. The Balkan Investigative Reporting Network Kosovo will create a network of reporters who will monitor and report on activities in the judicial, health, and education services across Kosovo. Project activities will include recruiting and training reporters in Kosovo’s seven main regions; establishing relationships with local authorities to allow access to courts, healthcare facilities, and schools; and preparing in-depth investigative reporting pieces to be part of the grantee’s popular television talk program called “Life in Kosovo”. The grantee is a registered, nongovernmental organization in Kosovo and part of a Balkan network of similar organizations in six countries (each with the same name).

title: Strengthening Peruvian Civil Society for Social and Environmental Monitoring of IIRSA and Camisea
description: This grant will provide coordination support for national-level civil society coalitions in Peru working to improve the environmental and social sustainability of large-scale infrastructure and energy projects in Peru. Asociación Civil Labor will carry out strategic analyses, conduct workshops, and provide logistical support to inform national dialogues on energy policy. It will provide similar support to a coalition of Peruvian organizations that are concerned about the social and environmental impacts of major highway, hydroelectric dams, and other infrastructure being financed as part of the Initiative for Integration of Regional Infrastructure for South America.

title: Strengthening Peruvian Civil Society for Social and Environmental Monitoring of IIRSA and Camisea
description: This grant will provide coordination support for two important, national-level civil society coalitions in Peru working to improve the environmental and social sustainability of large-scale infrastructure and energy projects in Peru. Asociación Civil Labor will carry out strategic analysis, conduct workshops, and provide logistical support to a network working on the Camisea gas pipeline. It will provide similar support to an emerging coalition of Peruvian organizations that are concerned about the social and environmental impacts of major highway, hydroelectric dams, and other infrastructure being financed as part of the Initiative for Integration of Regional Infrastructure for South America.

title: College Entrepreneurship Program
description: This renewal grant will support the College Entrepreneurship Program operated by LAUNCH, a program within the Outreach Department at the University of Michigan-Flint. Through this program, local college students receive targeted education about starting small businesses and participate in various activities to develop their business ideas. LAUNCH, formerly known as the Center for Entrepreneurship, provides entrepreneurial assistance to high school and college students as well as traditional business owners within Genesee County.

title: College Entrepreneurship Program
description: This renewal grant will support the College Entrepreneurship Program operated by University Outreach, a department within University of Michigan-Flint. Through this program, local college students receive targeted education about starting small businesses and participate in various activities to develop their business ideas. University Outreach provides entrepreneurial assistance to college students as well as traditional business owners within Genesee County.

title: Innovation Incubator
description: This renewal grant will support the Innovation Incubator, formerly known as the College Entrepreneurship Program, operated by University Outreach, a department within the University of Michigan-Flint. Through this program, local college students receive comprehensive education about starting small businesses or social entrepreneurship ventures and participate in various activities to develop their business ideas. University Outreach provides entrepreneurial assistance to college students as well as traditional business owners within Genesee County.

title: Innovation Incubator
description: The purpose of this grant is to support the Innovation Incubator at the University of Michigan-Flint. The incubator houses various for-profit and nonprofit student business ventures, provides training for potential and existing entrepreneurs, and helps to connect the university to the community in a tangible manner. The mission of the incubator is to create real-world learning experiences for students that support the economic revitalization in Flint and create a social good.

title: Innovation Incubator
description: This renewal grant supports the Innovation Incubator at the University of Michigan-Flint’s Office of University Outreach. The incubator promotes entrepreneurship and creativity by assisting students and community members in creating sustainable for-profit businesses and nonprofit organizations. Through this program, local college students and community members receive extensive training and education on how to start small businesses or social entrepreneurship ventures in various activities to help develop their business ideas.

title: Innovation Incubator
description: This renewal grant supports the Innovation Incubator at the University of Michigan-Flint’s Office of University Outreach. The incubator helps to promote entrepreneurship among students and community members in the Greater Flint area. Through this program, the University of Michigan-Flint’s students and community members are coached on developing their business ideas and receive training and education on how to start small businesses or social entrepreneurship ventures. Selected student businesses are eligible to receive business incubation space within the Innovation Incubator’s office complex.

title: Innovation Incubator
description: This renewal grant supports the Innovation Incubator at the University of Michigan-Flint’s Office of University Outreach. The Innovation Incubator helps to promote entrepreneurship among students and community members in the Greater Flint area. Through this program, participants are coached on developing their business ideas and receive training and education on how to start small businesses or social entrepreneurship ventures. Selected student businesses are offered business incubation space within the Innovation Incubator’s office complex, while others receive virtual office space that includes a business mailing address and coaching.

title: College Entrepreneurship Program
description: This grant will support the College Entrepreneurship Program operated by LAUNCH, a department within University of Michigan-Flint’s University Outreach. Through this program, local college students will receive targeted education about starting a small business and participate in various activities to develop their business ideas. LAUNCH was known previously as the Center for Entrepreneurship.

title: Genesee County Out-of-School Youth Initiative
description: This grant will enable the Community Foundation of Greater Flint to continue to support a countywide partnership aimed at improving the educational supports and opportunities for out-of-school youth. Through this project, the grantee has led and convened a partnership of stakeholders in building a framework that addresses the issue of dropouts and disconnected youth in Flint/Genesee County. During the next stage of this project, the grantee will deepen its work and continue to develop partnerships with key stakeholders in building local capacity to develop strategies and efforts that ensure out-of-school youth have a chance to earn a diploma.

title: Genesee County Out-of-School Youth Initiative
description: This grant will enable the Community Foundation of Greater Flint to continue to support a countywide partnership aimed at improving the educational supports and opportunities for out-of-school youth. Through this project, the grantee has led and convened a partnership of stakeholders in building a framework that addresses the issue of dropouts in Flint/Genesee County. During the next stage of this project, the grantee will focus on raising awareness on the plight of out of-school youth and building stronger connections to local and statewide stakeholders that can help develop strategies and efforts to ensure out-of-school youth have a chance to earn a diploma.

title: Genesee County Out-of-School Youth Initiative
description: This grant will enable Resource Genesee to continue to support a countywide partnership aimed at improving the educational supports for out-of-school and disconnected youth. In the most recent phase of this initiative, the coalition authored a report and launched a companion Website that profiles the challenges of disconnected youth in Genesee County and provides a set of action steps, strategies, and resources to reconnect this population to the mainstream economy. This grant will allow the grantee to support and convene the countywide coalition of youth-serving agencies and programs to develop strategies and action steps to ensure out-of-school youth have a chance to earn a diploma.

title: Genesee County Out-of-School Youth Initiative
description: This grant will enable Resource Genesee to continue to support a countywide coalition aimed at improving the educational supports for out-of-school and disconnected youth. In the most recent phase of this initiative, the grantee convened a summit on disconnected youth, launched an online resource guide to link disconnected youth to community resources, and partnered with Career Alliance on the design of an onsite reengagement center where disconnected youth can receive services. This grant will allow the grantee to convene this coalition of 36 youth-serving agencies/programs to develop strategies to ensure out-of-school and disconnected youth can earn a high school credential.

title: Genesee County Out-of-School Youth Initiative
description: This grant will enable Resource Genesee to continue to support a countywide coalition aimed at improving the educational supports for out-of-school and disconnected youth. As a growing partnership of committed nonprofit, public, education, and human service agencies in Genesee County, the coalition has accelerated a community discussion on the issues faced by disconnected youth and how best to engage youth, parents, caregivers, and governmental leaders to produce better practices and outcomes for this population. This grant will allow the grantee to convene this coalition of 36 youth-serving agencies to develop strategies to ensure disconnected youth acquire education/work experiences.

title: Genesee County Out-of-School Youth Initiative
description: This grant will enable Resource Genesee to continue to support a countywide coalition aimed at improving the educational supports for out-of-school and disconnected youth. As a growing partnership of nonprofit, public, education, and human services agencies in Genesee County, the grantee has accelerated a community discussion on the issues faced by disconnected youth and how best to engage youth, parents, caregivers, and governmental leaders to produce better practices and outcomes for this population. This grant will allow the grantee to convene this coalition of more than 20 youth-serving agencies and provide services to youth though ReMix, a virtual case management resource center/system.

title: Genesee County Out-of-School Youth Initiative
description: Through this grant, the Community Foundation of Greater Flint will work to improve policy and practice to prevent young people from dropping out of school, re-engage those who have already left school, and encourage support for such youth toward a successful post-secondary experience and/or entry into the labor market. Flint/Genesee County is one of four sites participating in the Improving Outcomes for Out-of-School Youth in Michigan project.

title: Indust-REAL Project: Providing Career and Technical Education Opportunities for Vulnerable Youth
description: This grant will enable the Indianapolis Private Industry Council to pilot a comprehensive career and technical education effort for vulnerable youth. Through the Indust-REAL project, the grantee will partner with Ivy Tech Community College, employers, and other workforce community partners in designing an effort by which students who have dropped out of high school can work toward a diploma or GED and earn industry-recognized occupational certificates and college credits. The Indust-REAL project will provide students with the opportunity to complete an accelerated, industry-based, post-secondary training program; develop job-readiness/retention skills; participate in job-shadowing activities; and secure employment in a series of in-demand and regionally based occupational tracks.

title: Improving Life Outcomes for Young Black Males
description: This grant will enable the Charles Hamilton Houston Institute at Harvard University to identify and document targeted strategies and promising interventions that improve opportunities and life chances for black males in education, employment, and healthcare access and treatment. The findings of this project will be synthesized in a series of reports and issue briefs and disseminated to key stakeholders including policymakers, educators, and advocates as a guide for practical and policy approaches that improve outcomes for black males.

title: Schools for the Future: Integrating Career and Technical Education into New Alternative Education Models
description: This grant will enable School & Main Institute to continue to develop and model a new high school design entitled Schools for the Future. Schools for the Future is an alternative education model designed especially for students who are far behind academically, including those who have dropped out and are now interested in earning a diploma and preparing for postsecondary education and career training. Recommended support will allow the grantee to fully develop the tools, curriculum, and training modules necessary to implement and pilot the Schools for the Future model in one to three interested school districts in 2011-2012.

title: Schools for the Future: Developing New High School Pathways and Innovations for At-Risk and Struggling Students
description: This grant will enable School & Main Institute to continue to develop and model a new small high school design entitled Schools for the Future. Schools for the Future is an alternative education model designed especially for students significantly behind academically, including those who have dropped out and are now interested in earning a diploma and preparing for postsecondary education and career training. Recommended support will allow the grantee to finalize the tools, curriculum, assessment products, and professional development and training modules needed to launch the first Schools for the Future site in 2011 and explore additional opportunities for replication in one or two other sites in 2012.

title: Schools for the Future: Developing New High School Pathways and Innovations for At-Risk and Struggling Students
description: This grant will enable School & Main Institute to continue to develop and model a new small high school design entitled Schools for the Future. Schools for the Future is an alternative and competency-based model designed especially for students two grade levels behind, including those who have dropped out and are now interested in earning a diploma and preparing for post-secondary education and career training. The grantee successfully launched the first Schools for the Future site in Jacksonville, Florida for 100 students in 2011 in partnership with Duval County Public Schools. Recommended support will allow the grantee to continue to develop the model, curriculum, and tools needed to support the ongoing implementation of the initial pilot site in Jacksonville, Florida, as well as support the start-up of the second pilot site in Detroit, Michigan in 2012.

title: Schools for the Future: Developing New High School Pathways and Innovations for At-Risk and Struggling Students
description: This grant will enable School & Main Institute to continue to develop and model a new small high school design entitled Schools for the Future. Schools for the Future is a competency-based model designed for students who are multiple grade levels behind, including dropouts who are now interested in earning a diploma and going on to post-secondary study. In 2012, the grantee successfully opened the second Schools for the Future site in Detroit, Michigan for 104 students to complement the pilot site that was launched in 2011 in Jacksonville, Florida. Recommended support will allow the grantee to continue to develop the model, provide ongoing implementation support to sites in Detroit and Jacksonville, and move forward to open two to four new sites in Michigan and/or other states in 2014.

title: Schools for the Future: Developing New High School Pathways and Innovations for At-Risk and Struggling Students
description: This grant will provide continued support to School & Main Institute for its Schools for the Future model. Schools for the Future is a competency-based model designed for students who are behind by multiple grade levels, including dropouts who are now interested in earning a diploma and going on to postsecondary study. In 2013, the grantee provided program support to sites in Detroit and Jacksonville, Florida, to implement the Schools for the Future design. Recommended support will enable the grantee to continue to develop the model, provide ongoing implementation support to existing sites, and launch a new site in Hartford, Connecticut in partnership with Our Piece of the Pie, a youth and education nonprofit.

title: Schools for the Future: Integrating Career and Technical Education into New Alternative Education Models
description: This grant will enable the School & Main Institute to research and develop a new alternative education model and prototype for vulnerable youth. The Schools for the Future project is an effort to blend career and technical education research and practice into an alternative education model where students can meet academic requirements and standards and participate in a sequence of courses focused on career development/preparedness and post-secondary education pursuits. Recommended support will enable the grantee to complete a research brief on exploring innovations and strategies that take a more targeted and integrated approach toward building career and employment options for students who are significantly behind in course credits, have dropped out of school, have academic skills as low as the fourth grade, and might benefit from a model that emphasizes career and technical education.

title: Impact of the New York State Non-Custodial Parent Earned Income Tax Credit
grantee: Columbia University in the City of New York
description: Research shows that the characteristics of many low-income, noncustodial fathers matched those of long-term welfare recipients whose employment rates were increased by the Federal Earned Income Tax Credit. These conclusions supported the New York state proposal for a Non-Custodial Parent Earned Income Tax Credit, which was passed in 2006. This grant to Columbia University in the City of New York will support a study designed to document and disseminate the employment benefits of this expanded Earned Income Tax Credit.

title: Workforce Development Study of Immigrant Workers
description: This grant to the Economic Mobility Corporation, a project of the Vera Institute of Justice, will fund a workforce development study to learn about the current state of the field, including efforts to increase the skills and earnings of immigrant workers. The project will investigate efforts led by nonprofit organizations, community colleges, unions, and employer associations that seek to help immigrant workers to advance in the labor market. This includes sectoral employment strategies; efforts to support entrepreneurship; bridge programs to connect workers in English as a Second Language classes to community colleges and other skills training; organizing efforts; and other innovative strategies tailored to the needs and experiences of immigrants living in the United States.

title: Flint Farmers Market Improvements
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will provide support for the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation’s efforts to improve the Flint Farmers Market. The Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation will help repair the existing parking lot, create a community meeting room, and obtain a master renovation plan for the Flint Farmers Market.

title: Center for the Nonprofit Community
description: This grant provides support for Independent Sector’s newly purchased building in Washington, D.C. The grantee aims to establish a nucleus in the nation’s capital around which to gather, nurture, and expand ongoing public policy collaboration for the entire nonprofit sector. The grantee plans to cover the $33.5 million acquisition and improvement costs through bond and traditional commercial financing and fundraising efforts, as well as its own reserves. Besides additional office space to support a more robust public policy, advocacy, and leadership agenda, the Center for the Nonprofit Community will include a conference facility, a reference library, guest office spaces, and technology for virtual meetings. Independent Sector is a coalition of leading nonprofits, foundations, and corporations that aims to strengthen nonprofit initiative, philanthropy, and citizen action in the United States.

title: Defining Poverty Reduction Strategies
description: Development of a new Pathways Out of Poverty plan is under way, including evaluation of progress since 2000; reconsideration of the program’s goals, objectives, and strategies; and development of new outcomes sought and baseline data. The primary purpose of this project is to solicit and disseminate the opinions of top scholars regarding key policy initiatives that will most help reduce poverty over the next decade. This grant to Brookings Institution will enable the team to incorporate external, expert perspectives into the strategic planning process. Founded in 1927, Brookings Institution is an independent, nonpartisan organization devoted to research, analysis, education, and publications focused on policy issues.

title: Amachi Collaborative
grantee: Big Brothers Big Sisters of Flint and Genesee County
description: This renewal grant will support the Amachi Collaborative, a partnership between Big Brothers Big Sisters of Greater Flint and Motherly Intercession to provide support services for children of incarcerated parents. The goal of this partnership is to provide these children with mentoring, academic support, and visitations with their incarcerated parent. Big Brothers Big Sisters of Greater Flint was a participant in the BEST project.

title: Amachi Collaborative
grantee: Big Brothers Big Sisters of Flint and Genesee County
description: This renewal grant will support the Amachi Collaborative, a partnership between Big Brothers Big Sisters of Greater Flint and Motherly Intercession, to provide support services for children of incarcerated parents. The goal of this partnership is to provide these children with mentoring, academic support, and visitations with their incarcerated parent.

title: Amachi Collaborative
grantee: Big Brothers Big Sisters of Flint and Genesee County
description: This grant will support collaboration between Big Brothers Big Sisters of Greater Flint and Motherly Intercession to provide support services for children of incarcerated parents. The goal of this partnership is to provide these children with mentoring, academic support, and visitations with their incarcerated parent. The grantee was a participant in the BEST project.

title: Summer Tot Lot Program
description: This grant will support the Summer Tot Lot Program, which is a preschool program for children aged 4-6 that provides at-risk youth with the academic and social skills necessary for future educational success. The program, created in 1941 as a component of the Flint Community Schools Community Education initiatives, will expand to address the academic, social, and nutrition/fitness development of children, as well as provide parenting support for their caregivers.

title: Summer Tot Lot Program
description: This renewal grant will support the Flint Community Schools’ Summer Tot Lot Program, which is a preschool program for children aged 4-5 that provides at-risk youth with the academic and social skills necessary for future educational success. The program, created in 1955 as a component of the Flint Community Schools Community Education initiatives, will expand to address the academic, social, and nutrition/fitness development of children, as well as provide parenting support for their caregivers.

title: Summer Tot Lot Program
description: This renewal grant supports the Flint Community Schools’ Summer Tot Lot Program, which is a preschool program for children aged 4-5, that provides at-risk youth with the academic and social skills necessary for future educational success. The program, created in 1955 as a component of the Flint Community Schools Community Education initiatives, addresses the academic, social, and nutrition/fitness development of children and equips parents and caregivers with the necessary skills to support their children.

title: Summer Tot Lot Program
description: This renewal grant supports the Summer Tot Lot Program, a project of the Flint Community Schools, which is a preschool program for children aged four to five years old that provides at-risk youth with the academic and social skills necessary for future educational success. The program, created in 1955 as a component of the Flint Community Schools community education initiatives, addresses the academic, social, and nutrition/fitness development of children and equips parents and caregivers with the necessary skills to support their children.

title: Summer Tot Lot Program
description: This renewal grant supports the Flint Community Schools’ Summer Tot Lot Program, which is a preschool program for children aged four to five years, that develops school readiness skills in its participants and teaches parenting skills to the participating caregivers. Created in 1955 as a component of the Flint Community Schools Community Education initiatives, the Summer Tot Lot Program addresses literacy, social skills, and health in preschool children.

title: Summer Tot Lot Program
description: This renewal grant will support the Flint Community Schools’ Summer Tot Lot Program, a preschool program for children ages four and five that provides at-risk children with the academic and social skills necessary for future educational success. The Summer Tot Lot Program has been a part of the Flint Community Schools’ summer education programming since 1955 and addresses the academic, social, and nutrition/fitness development of children, while providing their caregivers with parenting support.

title: Summer Tot Lot Program
description: This renewal grant will support the Flint Community Schools’ Summer Tot Lot Program, an early education program for at-risk children ages four and five that provides them with the academic and social skills necessary for future educational success. The program has been a part of the Flint Community Schools’ summer education programming since the late 1930s and addresses the academic, social, and nutrition/fitness development of children, while providing their caregivers with parenting support.

title: Summer Tot Lot Program
description: This renewal grant will support the Flint Community Schools’ Summer Tot Lot Program, an early education program for at-risk children ages four and five that provides them with the academic and social skills necessary for future educational success. The Summer Tot Lot Program has been a part of the Flint Community Schools’ summer education programming since the late 1930s and addresses the academic, social, and nutrition/fitness development of children, while providing their caregivers with parenting support, which has become even more important with the issues surrounding the city’s water system.

title: Summer Tot Lot Program
description: This renewal grant will support the Flint Community Schools’ Summer Tot Lot Program, an early education program for at-risk children ages four and five that provides them with the academic and social skills necessary for future educational success. The Summer Tot Lot Program has been a part of the Flint Community Schools’ summer education programming since the late 1930s and addresses the academic, social, and nutrition/fitness development of children, while providing their caregivers with parenting support. These types of support are especially important for children who may have been exposed to lead during the Flint water crisis.

title: Summer Tot Lot Program
description: This grant will support the Flint Community Schools’ Summer Tot Lot Program, which is a preschool program for children aged 4-6 that provides at-risk youth with the academic and social skills necessary for future educational success. Created in 1955 as a component of the Flint Community Schools Community Education initiatives, the program will be expanded to address the academic, social, and nutrition/fitness development of children, as well as provide parenting support for their caregivers.

title: Diversity Fellowship Program
description: Proteus Fund is a national organization that works with individual donors and foundations to advance social equity goals through strategy development, research, and fund management. Since 1997, the grantee has awarded nearly $50 million to organizations across the country that work to promote democracy, human rights, and peace. This grant will provide partial support to the grantee for its Diversity Fellowship Program, which focuses on expanding ethnic minority leadership in the philanthropy profession. The program was developed in 2006 by Associated Grant Makers, which successfully managed three cohorts of program fellows. In 2010, Proteus Fund became the new home for the program and, during the grant period, will place a minimum of four fellows in various philanthropic organizations in the region.

title: Diversity Fellowship Program
description: Associated Grant Makers is a regional association of grantmakers whose mission is to support the practice and expansion of effective philanthropic giving. Associated Grant Makers’ membership consists of 125 grantmaking foundations, corporations, and philanthropic advisory services in Massachusetts and New Hampshire. This grant will provide partial support to Associated Grant Makers for its Diversity Fellowship Program, which focuses on expanding ethnic minority leadership in the philanthropy profession. Since it began in fall 2006, the Diversity Fellowship Program has completed two years placing ten fellows at various philanthropic organizations in the region.

title: Flint Institute of Arts Endowment Fund
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to the Community Foundation of Greater Flint will create an endowment fund for the benefit of the Flint Institute of Arts. The Flint Institute of Arts is an important asset to the community and provides a variety of cultural opportunities for area residents, including displays of its permanent collection and special exhibitions, an art school that offers studio classes for all skill levels, and educational programs for children and adults. The institute recently completed a major renovation and expansion of its building, adding new galleries and expanding the art school, and last year’s attendance exceeded 100,000 for the first time. Annual operating costs have increased, and this endowment will help support building and programming expenses.

title: Conference on Progressive Consumption Taxation
grantee: American Enterprise Institute for Public Policy Research
description: In spite of widespread criticism of the current tax system, there have been few comprehensive efforts to make the tax code simpler, fairer, and more conducive to economic growth. However, practical concerns, including the expanding reach of the Alternative Minimum Tax and shortfalls in several important entitlement programs, provide a strong impetus for considering reform efforts in the near-term. This grant will enable the American Enterprise Institute for Public Policy Research to host a conference on progressive consumption taxation. The event will engage a bipartisan group of noted scholars and experts in a discussion of the merits and shortcomings of consumption taxation strategies, separately and in comparison to other recommended alternatives. Located in Washington, D.C., the grantee is a nonprofit think tank dedicated to research and education on issues of government, politics, economics, and social welfare.

title: American Dream Demonstration Evaluation
grantee: University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill
description: The American Dream Demonstration, which ran from 1998 to 2002, was a large-scale, experimental study assessing the efficacy of Individual Development Accounts. Results from the demonstration helped propel bipartisan interest in increasing the savings and wealth of low-income households as a strategy to complement traditional, income-based poverty alleviation programs. This grant will enable researchers at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill to collect a fourth wave of survey data in order to assess the long-term impacts from the demonstration. The study will provide policymakers, practitioners, and researchers with the first evidence on the long-term impacts and cost effectiveness of Individual Development Account programs.

title: Just for the Kids
description: This grant will provide partial support to the Michigan Chamber Foundation for the Just for the Kids Best Practices Institute for High Priority Schools for 2008. The institute was designed to build relationships between school leaders from both high performing and high priority schools to share successful processes and practices and to create coaching or mentoring partnerships that can assist the high priority schools. Through this process, the Just for the Kids Best Practices Institute for High Priority Schools has been able to facilitate the transformation of 15 schools and will now attempt to do the same with six more high priority schools from across the state of Michigan.

title: ICTY Legacy Website Development
description: The project goal is to support the process of dealing with the past in the former Yugoslavia by raising public awareness in this region about the work of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia. To this end, the tribunal is implementing an ambitious communication and legacy program that will provide information and resources to the public in the Bosnian, Serbian, and Croatian languages long after the tribunal has completed its work in 2010. Central to this program is a dedicated Web site that enables global audiences, and especially those in the former Yugoslavia, to have easy access to its legal findings and an extensive range of specially designed new materials and content. Mott support will be used during the 18-month grant period to pay the expenses of a full-time translator. The tribunal was established by the United Nations in 1993 and is based in The Hague, Netherlands.

title: National School Curriculum Support
description: The South African Holocaust Foundation is dedicated to the creation of a just and caring society in which human rights and diversity are respected and valued. The grantee uses the lessons from the Holocaust to highlight issues related to human behavior, fragility of freedom, and the need for vigilance in preserving democratic values. Past support enabled the grantee to train teachers throughout the country on how to teach about the Holocaust and its universal lessons for human rights. Its belief is that Holocaust history helps students to develop an understanding of the consequences of prejudice, racism, and stereotyping. The grantee will continue to train senior teachers throughout the country as trainers on Nazi Germany, the Holocaust, and its universal lessons on humanity. These teachers will in turn provide ongoing training to grades nine and eleven teachers in their respective provinces.

title: National School Curriculum Support
description: The South African Holocaust Foundation is a human rights education organization dedicated to creating a more just and caring society based on a culture of respect for diversity and a commitment to democracy. Using the history of Nazi Germany and the Holocaust as a framework and case study, the foundation developed educational materials for South African high school learners. Its belief is that Holocaust history helps students develop an understanding of the consequences of prejudice, racism, and stereotyping. This grant supports training of senior teachers and curriculum advisors to have the capacity and tools to facilitate ongoing, regionally based training programs for high school teachers, enabling them to better deliver high quality lessons on Nazi Germany and the Holocaust as recently mandated by the South African Education Department.

title: Mobilizing Citizens and Coalitions for Managed Growth Across Southeast Michigan
description: Since its inception in 1970, the Ecology Center has worked for a safe and healthy environment where people live, work, and play. Based in Ann Arbor, Michigan, the center has developed a reputation across the state and the Midwest as a leader in developing innovative programs; and over the past decade, the organization has become increasingly engaged in issues related to growth management in southeast Michigan. Support will help the center deepen its work and relationships in the southeast metropolitan region and strengthen the link between growth management and urban revitalization.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen local-level democracy and civil society in Montenegro by supporting the development of an indigenous grantmaking organization. To this end, the Fund for Active Citizenship will increase its grantmaking aimed at encouraging civic activism and addressing the needs of vulnerable people. In addition, the fund will provide technical assistance and capacity development opportunities to its grantees and the nonprofit sector through workshops, documenting case studies and good practice in the field, and networking key actors. The fund will also raise awareness and promote cross-sector collaboration on issues of public participation in decisionmaking and philanthropy development. During 2008-2010, the fund awarded 49 grants totaling $550,000, organized forums and training programs for its grantees, published the first-ever study on philanthropy in Montenegro, and launched the annual excellence in philanthropy prize. Prior to its registration in January 2008, the fund had been the local branch of the Belgrade-based Balkan Community Initiatives Fund, a long-time Mott grantee.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen local-level democracy and civil society in Montenegro by supporting the development of an indigenous grantmaking organization. To this end, the Fund for Active Citizenship will increase its grantmaking aimed at encouraging civic activism and addressing the needs of vulnerable people. In addition, the grantee will provide technical assistance and capacity development opportunities to its grantees and the nonprofit sector through workshops, documenting case studies and good practice in the field, and networking key actors. The grantee will also raise awareness and promote cross-sector collaboration on issues of public participation in decisionmaking and philanthropy development. During 2010-2011, the fund awarded more than 60 grants totaling in excess of €400,000, organized forums and training programs for its grantees, cooperated with national and local governments to improve distribution of public funds to nonprofits, and organized annual excellence in philanthropy prizes. The fund is based in Podgorica and works throughout Montenegro.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen local-level democracy and civil society in Montenegro by supporting the development of an indigenous grantmaking organization. To this end, the Fund for Active Citizenship will increase its grantmaking aimed at encouraging civic activism and addressing the needs of vulnerable people. In addition, the grantee will provide technical assistance and capacity development opportunities to its grantees and the nonprofit sector through workshops, documenting case studies and good practice in the field, and networking key actors. The grantee will also raise awareness and promote cross-sector collaboration on issues of public participation in decisionmaking and philanthropy development. During 2012-2013, the grantee awarded approximately 100 grants totaling in excess of $520,000, organized forums and training programs for its grantees, worked with Montenegrin diaspora to increase giving to civic initiatives, researched public opinions about local philanthropy, and organized annual excellence in philanthropy prizes. The grantee is based in Podgorica.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen local-level democracy and civil society in Montenegro by supporting the development of an indigenous grantmaking organization. The Fund for Active Citizenship will increase its grantmaking aimed at encouraging civic activism and addressing the needs of vulnerable people. In addition, the grantee will provide technical assistance and capacity development opportunities to its grantees and the nonprofit sector through workshops, documenting case studies and good practice in the field, and networking key actors. The grantee will also raise awareness and promote cross-sector collaboration on issues of public participation in decision making and philanthropy development. During 2014-2015, the grantee awarded 81 grants totaling approximately $400,000, provided direct consultancy and organized networking and training programs for its grantees, worked with Montenegrin diaspora to increase giving to civic initiatives, researched public opinions about local philanthropy, and organized annual excellence-in-philanthropy prizes. The Fund for Active Citizenship is based in Podgorica, Montenegro.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen local level democracy and civil society in Montenegro by supporting the development of an indigenous grantmaking organization. During the next two years, the Fund for Active Citizenship will distribute approximately $250,000 to $350,000 annually in grants to community-based organizations in Montenegro, provide training and information resources to these organizations, and promote corporate and individual philanthropy at local and national levels. In addition, the fund will convene grassroots organizations and activists and local and national government officials in order to strengthen dialogue on overcoming structural and systematic obstacles to public participation in decisionmaking. Prior to its formal registration as a Montenegrin nongovernmental organization in January 2008, the fund had been the local branch of the Belgrade-based Balkan Community Initiatives Fund, a longtime Mott grantee. The fund is based in Podgorica, Montenegro.

title: Option on Character Inn
description: This grant will provide the Crim Fitness Foundation with funds to extend their nonbinding purchase option on the Character Inn in downtown Flint. The Crim Fitness Foundation is looking at developing the former hotel into a center to provide education and training that promotes healthy lifestyles and addresses the problem of childhood obesity. It is likely that the building will be redeveloped as a mixed-use facility.

title: Sustainable Finance Project
description: After many years of working to ensure a robust and accountable environmental and social safeguard system for international financial institutions, many stakeholders now feel that new and different ways of improving these policies and accountability systems must be considered. Through this grant increase, the Program on International and Comparative Environmental Law at the American University’s Washington College of Law will continue its efforts to evaluate current sustainable finance standards, monitor the climate change-related policies of financial institutions, strengthen and use existing accountability systems to support affected communities in specific cases, and seek new approaches to increasing accountability of public and private financial institutions.

title: Sustainable Finance Project
description: Over the past two decades, nongovernmental organizations have successfully advocated for international financial institutions to develop environmental and social policies as well as internal accountability systems, which are designed to allow affected communities a means to ensure that environmental and social policies are actually implemented. Many stakeholders now feel that new and different ways of improving these policies and accountability systems must be considered as well as consideration of the need for developing external accountability systems. Through this grant, the Program on International and Comparative Environmental Law at the American University’s Washington College of Law will evaluate current sustainable finance standards, monitor the climate change-related policies of financial institutions, strengthen and use existing accountability systems to support affected communities in specific cases, and seek new approaches to increasing accountability of public and private financial institutions.

title: Athletics Programs Study
description: This grant will support an exploratory study of varsity athletics at the University of Michigan-Flint. A 35-member Blue Ribbon Commission on Athletics Programs, in conjunction with a college athletic consulting firm, will examine the potential contribution that an athletic program would have on the University of Michigan-Flint.

title: Turnaround Consultant
description: The YWCA of Greater Flint has worked toward eliminating racism and empowering women in the greater Flint community for over 40 years. Today, however, the organization finds itself at an important crossroads, and to ensure continued success, it will need to develop a comprehensive plan focusing on its operation, financial stability, programming, staffing, and building requirements. This grant will enable the grantee to retain the strategic planning assistance of the management consulting firm that conducted its financial and operational viability assessment during the previous grant period.

title: Turnaround Consultant
description: This grant will enable the YWCA of Greater Flint to hire a management consulting firm to help plan its future course. The organization has worked toward eliminating racism and empowering women in the greater Flint community for over 40 years. Today, however, the YWCA of Greater Flint finds itself at an important crossroads, and to ensure continued success, it will develop a comprehensive plan focusing on its operation, financial, programming, staffing, and building requirements. The management consulting firm will guide the YWCA of Greater Flint through this in-depth and arduous process.

title: Supporting Local Knowledge: Small Grants for Energy and Infrastructure
description: Many communities around the world are being impacted by investments in large-scale energy and infrastructure projects. Global Greengrants Fund has developed an efficient and effective mechanism for delivering small grants to local nongovernmental organizations at an appropriate scale. This grant will support the expansion of its small grants programs for community-based efforts to protect the environment and increase public input into decisionmaking about energy and infrastructure projects in Russia, Eastern Europe, and the Central Asian Republics.

title: Supporting Local Knowledge: Small Grants for Energy and Infrastructure
description: Many communities around the world are being impacted by investments in large-scale energy and infrastructure projects. Global Greengrants Fund has developed an efficient and effective mechanism for delivering small grants to local nongovernmental organizations at an appropriate scale. This grant will support Global Greengrants Fund to expand its small grants programs for community-based efforts to protect the environment and increase public input into decisionmaking about energy and infrastructure projects in Russia, Eastern Europe, and the Central Asian Republics.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Center for Health, Environment and Justice
description: Communities dealing with chemical pollution problems face technical issues that can be extremely complex. The Center for Health, Environment and Justice, a national organization now in its 30th year, plays a critical role by providing technical assistance to local groups addressing such toxic waste issues and by networking local groups so that they can learn from one another, connect with nontraditional partners, and speak with a collective voice. Mott’s general purpose support will help the center maintain and expand its technical assistance programs and support state-specific efforts to promote children’s health and more protective chemical use policies.

title: Temporary Staffing Firms and the Hard-to-Employ
grantee: Insight Center for Community Economic Development
description: Despite the challenging national economy over the past year, the growth in the temporary employment sector has been strong, and industry payroll since 1990 has expanded by an average of 14 percent annually. As the overall temporary industry has grown, so too has temporary employment for low-skilled, low-income, and disadvantaged jobseekers. This grant will support the Insight Center for Community Economic Development’s efforts to create standards for staffing agencies that receive certain types of public funds that would offer greater protection to hard-to-employ people.

title: Alternative Staffing Outcomes for Job Candidates and Employers
description: Alternative staffing organizations put the staffing services model to work for job candidates who face labor market barriers. They have a dual goal of providing job brokering for workers who face barriers to employment as well as delivering staffing services for customers who need workers. This renewal grant will provide funds for the University of Massachusetts – Boston to continue to analyze and document the job placement outcomes for clients of four alternative staffing organizations, including a comparison with hard-to-employ clients of conventional staffing firms.

title: Alternative Staffing Outcomes for Job Candidates and Employers
description: Alternative staffing organizations put the staffing services model to work for job candidates who face labor market barriers. They have a dual goal of providing job brokering for workers who face barriers to employment, as well as delivering staffing services for customers who need workers. This renewal grant will provide funds for the University of Massachusetts – Boston to continue to analyze and document the job placement outcomes for clients of four alternative staffing organizations, including a comparison with hard-to-employ clients of conventional staffing firms.

title: Alternative Staffing Outcomes for Job Candidates and Employers
description: Alternative staffing organizations put the staffing services model to work for job candidates who face labor market barriers. They have a dual goal of providing job brokering for workers who face barriers to employment, as well as delivering staffing services for customers who need workers. This renewal grant will provide funds for the University of Massachusetts – Boston to broadly disseminate the wealth of data collected during the Alternative Demonstration II project, which studied four alternative staffing organizations in great detail over a three-year period. The grant will also support production of three brief reports focused on the experience of employers using alternative staffing organizations, the role of alternative staffing organizations in job brokering, and participant outcomes and work trajectories.
