They have a dual goal of providing job brokering for workers who face barriers to employment as well as delivering staffing services for customers who need workers. This grant will provide funds for the University of Massachusetts-Boston to continue to analyze and document the job placement outcomes for clients of four alternative staffing organizations, including a comparison with hard-to-employ clients of conventional staffing firms.

title: Exhibitions-Comic Book Art
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to the Flint Institute of Arts will sponsor two exhibitions of comic book art. Comics, Heroes, and American Visual Culture will feature more than 80 original drawings and paintings by some of the most well-known contributors to the comic book and comic strip genres. “Beyond the Frame: African-American Comic Book Artists” will present the work of several well-established, as well as emerging, African-American artists working in commercial, self-published, and Web-based comic book and graphic novel art. These two unique exhibitions of comic book, comic strip, and graphic novel art will be presented in the Hodge Gallery from January 24 through April 26, 2009.

title: General Purposes
grantee: AGORA Platform: Active Communities for Development Alternatives
description: The program goal is to support the development of local communities and grassroots organizations in Bulgaria. The AGORA Platform: Active Communities for Development Alternatives supports the network of Bulgarian chitalishte and increases chitalishte capacity to bring positive changes and development in local communities. A chitalishte is a specific, Bulgarian, community-based, nongovernmental institution with a 200-year history of supporting literacy, education, and community development. During the grant period, the grantee will build chitalishte capacity by providing information, training, and technical assistance; increase the support for chitalishte by establishing effective partnerships with relevant governmental and nongovernmental institutions; and develop its own organizational capacity by strengthening its human resources, diversifying its funding base, and developing new services. The grantee’s achievements in 2008-2010 included experimenting successfully with innovative community development approaches, expanding and strengthening its membership, and establishing strong partnerships with relevant governmental and nongovernmental organizations.

title: General Purposes
grantee: AGORA Platform: Active Communities for Development Alternatives
description: The program goal is to support the development of local communities and grassroots organizations in Bulgaria. To this end, the AGORA Platform: Active Communities for Development Alternatives will support a network of Bulgarian chitalishte and increase chitalishte capacity to bring positive changes and development in local communities. A chitalishte is a specific, Bulgarian, community-based, nongovernmental institution with a 200-year history of supporting literacy, education, and community development. During the grant period, the grantee will build chitalishte capacity by providing information, training, technical assistance, and seed funding; increase the support for chitalishte by establishing effective partnerships with relevant governmental and nongovernmental institutions; and develop its own organizational capacity by strengthening its human resources, diversifying its funding base, and developing new services. The grantee’s achievements in 2011-2013 included increasing the level of civic participation, volunteering, and giving in 37 localities; expanding and strengthening its membership; and establishing strong partnerships with relevant governmental and nongovernmental organizations.

title: General Purposes
grantee: AGORA Platform: Active Communities for Development Alternatives
description: The program goal is to support the development of local communities and grassroots organizations in Bulgaria. To this end, AGORA Platform: Active Communities for Development Alternatives will support a network of Bulgarian chitalishte and increase chitalishte capacity to bring positive changes and development in local communities. A chitalishte is a specific, Bulgarian, community-based, nongovernmental institution with a200-year history of supporting literacy, education, and community development. During the grant period, the grantee will build chitalishte capacity by providing information, training, technical assistance, and seed funding; increase the support for chitalishte by establishing effective partnerships with relevant governmental and nongovernmental institutions; and develop its own organizational capacity by strengthening its human resources, diversifying its funding base, and developing new services. The grantee’s achievements in 2014-2016 included increasing the level of civic participation, volunteering, and giving in 24 localities; establishing strong partnerships with relevant governmental and nongovernmental organizations; and developing partnerships with peer organizations from Turkey. The grantee is based in Sofia, Bulgaria.

title: General Purposes
grantee: AGORA Platform: Active Communities for Development Alternatives
description: The program goal is to support the development of local communities and grassroots organizations in Bulgaria. The AGORA Platform – Active Communities for Development Alternatives supports the network of Bulgarian chitalishte and increases chitalishte capacity to bring positive changes and development in local communities. A chitalishte is a specific, Bulgarian, community-based, nongovernmental institution with a 200-year history of supporting literacy, education, and community development. During the grant period, the grantee will build chitalishte capacity by providing information, training, and technical assistance; increase the support for chitalishte by establishing effective partnerships with relevant government and nongovernmental institutions; and develop its own organizational capacity by strengthening its human resources, diversifying its funding base, and developing new services.

title: GrantsFire
description: GrantsFire is a system which captures and publishes grant information using Web 2.0 tools and technology, including the machine-readable “hGrants” format. Incorporating GrantsFire into the Foundation Center’s own electronic reporting program, currently used by 450 foundations worldwide, will improve the timeliness and accuracy of foundation grant data. The Mott Foundation previously supported the development of GrantsFire through a grant to Solpath, a nonprofit technology consulting firm. Solpath launched the GrantsFire Web site, created “hGrants” specifications, and developed a grants aggregator, a feed validator, and a MicroEdge GIFTS plug-in. Solpath has agreed to transfer the system to Foundation Center, which is expected to expand the use of GrantsFire. The Foundation Center is a national nonprofit service organization dedicated to fostering public understanding of the foundation field by collecting, organizing, analyzing, and disseminating information on foundations, corporate giving, and related subjects.

title: GrantsFire
description: This grant provides support for the further development and promotion of GrantsFire, a system which aggregates and publishes grants information using Web 2.0 tools and technology. Currently in an initial pilot phase, GrantsFire makes up-to-date information on philanthropic grants widely and easily accessible through a network-centric strategy. GrantsFire will pull recently published grants information from known foundation Web site feeds according to a simple unified standard. Grants data will be pooled, and the collective data will be made searchable and publishable by key words and other sort criteria. Ultimately, GrantsFire will bring down the cost and raise the timeliness and accessibility of grants data collection. The GrantsFire initiative is being led by Solpath, a nonprofit organization created specifically to develop solutions that improve foundation grants management processes and software systems.

title: Joint Venture Development
description: Washington Interfaith Network, an affiliate of the Industrial Areas Foundation, is a multiracial, multiconstituency community organization in the District of Columbia. In the last three years, it has worked to secure public financing to help rebuild some of the city’s long-neglected neighborhoods. To fulfill its ongoing neighborhood development goals, Washington Interfaith Network is creating a joint venture real estate development company that will provide for community input in development decisions, as well as a small source of funding to the central organizing work. This grant will provide support for the start-up and planning phase.

title: Community Development in Volga Region
description: The program goal is to introduce new methods of activating communities, increasing local resource mobilization, and promoting social investment in Russia. The Sluzhenye Association will expand its training program for social animators who will help mobilize and advise civic groups. It will increase the capacity of local activity centers to act as focal points for community planning and resource mobilization, with a particular focus on developing individual giving. The grantee will support the further development of the Dobriy Nizhny charity festival organized collectively by the centers. During 2008-2009, the grantee trained 22 social animators and helped establish 10 local activity centers. The first annual Dobriy Nizhny festival of giving raised over $10,000 in cash and a greater amount of in-kind contributions, primarily from individuals. Established in 1994, the Sluzhenye Association is a leading provider of support and services for nongovernmental organizations and community leaders in the Nizhny Novgorod region.

title: Community Development in Volga Region
description: The program goal is to institutionalize effective methods of activating communities, increasing local resource mobilization, and promoting social investment in Russia. The Sluzhenye Association, located in Nizhny Novgorod, will expand its training program for social animators who will help mobilize and advise civic groups. It will increase the capacity of community-based, independent local activity centers to act as focal points for community planning and resource mobilization, while promoting efforts to link such local centers into a national network. The grantee will support the further development and geographic expansion of the Dobriy Nizhny (Kind Nizhny) charity festival organized collectively by the centers. In 2010-2011, the grantee expanded the network of local activity centers and social animators in the Volga region and was one of the first organizations to win a federal grant for socially oriented organizations. Established in 1994, the Sluzhenye Association is a leading provider of support and services for nongovernmental organizations and community leaders in the Nizhny Novgorod region.

title: Community Development in Volga Region
description: The program goal is to institutionalize effective methods of activating communities, increasing local resource mobilization, and promoting social investment in Russia. The Sluzhenye Association, located in Nizhny Novgorod, will continue to expand the community of social animators and local activity centers through a series of annual training workshops and Webinars. It will also strengthen ties and cross-learning with other community-based civic initiatives across Russia through regular skill-sharing events. During 2012-2014, the grantee expanded the network of centers and animators in the Volga region. It supported over 30 microprojects ranging from establishing a sports club for at-risk youth to providing volunteer renovation services and supplies for low-income families to protect against winter cold. As part of the Dobriy Nizhny festival, the grantee also established an informal coalition of charities seeking to promote public trust in charitable activity. Established in 1994, the Sluzhenye Association is a leading provider of support and services for nongovernmental organizations and community leaders in the Nizhny Novgorod region.

title: Community Development in Volga Region
description: The program goal is to introduce new methods of activating communities, increasing local resource mobilization, and promoting social investment in Russia. Building on its two-year partnership project with the BORIS Association – Support Office for the Movement of Social Initiatives (of Poland), the Sluzhenye Association will introduce “social animators” as an innovative approach to engaging with active citizens at the community level in Nizhny Novgorod and three neighboring regions. Activities will include training workshops equipping participants to harness local citizen initiatives. Local activity centers will provide a focal point for citizens to develop plans for community action and improvement. Social animators will additionally be trained in local resource mobilization techniques to help finance community projects. A final workshop will be held to compare and learn from different experiences and methodologies in advancing citizen engagement in Russia. Established in 1994, the Sluzhenye Association is a leading provider of support and services for nongovernmental organizations and community leaders in the Nizhny Novgorod region.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to Derecho Ambiente y Recursos Naturales which works to monitor energy and infrastructure policies and projects and their impacts on the environment in Peru. The grantee also provides legal and technical assistance to indigenous communities and nongovernmental organizations and networks, so they can promote more environmentally and socially sustainable practices for energy development in Peru.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant increase provides general purpose support for the organization Derecho Ambiente y Recursos Naturales, which works to monitor energy and infrastructure policies and projects and their impacts on the environment in Peru. This grant increase will enable the organization to carry out a strategic planning process and expand legal and technical assistance to indigenous communities working on climate finance in Peru.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support for the organization Derecho Ambiente y Recursos Naturales, which works to monitor energy and infrastructure policies and projects and their impacts on the environment in Peru. The grantee also provides legal and technical assistance to indigenous communities and nongovernmental organizations and networks, so they can promote more environmentally and socially sustainable practices for energy development in Peru and across the Amazon basin.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant renewal provides general purpose support to Derecho Ambiente y Recursos Naturales, which works to monitor energy and infrastructure policies and projects and their impacts in Peru and the Peruvian Amazon. Derecho Ambiente y Recursos Naturales also provides legal and technical assistance to indigenous communities and nongovernmental organizations and networks to enable them to promote more environmentally and socially sustainable practices for energy development in Peru and across the Amazon Basin.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant increase provides support to Derecho Ambiente y Recursos Naturales to host and organize events with national, regional, and international civil society during the World Bank Annual Meeting in Lima, Peru, in October 2015.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant renewal provides general purpose support to Derecho Ambiente y Recursos Naturales, which works to monitor energy and infrastructure policies and projects and their impacts in Peru and the Peruvian Amazon. The grantee also provides legal and technical assistance to indigenous communities and nongovernmental organizations and networks to enable them to promote more environmentally and socially sustainable practices for energy development in Peru and across the Amazon Basin.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to the organization Derecho Ambiente y Recursos Naturales which works to monitor energy policies and projects and their impacts on the environment in Peru. Derecho Ambiente y Recursos Naturales also provides legal and technical assistance to indigenous communities and nongovernmental organizations and networks, so they can promote more environmentally and socially sustainable practices for energy development in Peru.

title: Center on Philanthropy Panel Study
description: This grant provides partial support for the Center on Philanthropy Panel Study, an ongoing research study that collects detailed data on the giving and volunteering habits of several thousand American households over time and over generations. It is conducted in conjunction with the Institute for Social Research’s Panel Study of Income Dynamics at the University of Michigan, which has surveyed families since 1968 and to which a philanthropy component was added in 2001. The dataset produced by the study is the best, most accurate resource for measuring giving and volunteering in the United States and is used extensively by researchers. Founded in 1987, the Center on Philanthropy at Indiana University is a leading academic center dedicated to increasing the understanding of philanthropy and improving its practice through research, teaching, public service, and public affairs.

title: Philanthropy Panel Study
description: This grant provides partial support for the Philanthropy Panel Study, an ongoing research study that collects detailed data on the giving and volunteering habits of several thousand American households over time and over generations. It is conducted in conjunction with the University of Michigan Institute for Social Research’s Panel Study of Income Dynamics, which has surveyed families since 1968 and to which a philanthropy component was added in 2001. The dataset produced by the study is the best, most accurate resource for measuring giving and volunteering in the United States and is used extensively by researchers. The Lilly Family School of Philanthropy at Indiana University was founded in 2012. The school is dedicated to improving philanthropy by training and empowering students and practitioners to be innovators and leaders who create positive and lasting change in the world. The school’s predecessor, the Center on Philanthropy, was founded in 1987.

title: Philanthropy Panel Study
description: This grant provides partial support for the Philanthropy Panel Study, an ongoing research study that collects detailed data on the giving and volunteering habits of several thousand American households over time and over generations. It is conducted in conjunction with the University of Michigan Institute for Social Research’s Panel Study of Income Dynamics, which has surveyed families since 1968 and to which a philanthropy component was added in 2001. The dataset produced by the study is the best, most accurate resource for measuring giving and volunteering in the United States and is used extensively by researchers. The Lilly Family School of Philanthropy at Indiana University was founded in 2012. The school is dedicated to improving philanthropy by training and empowering students and practitioners to be innovators and leaders who create positive and lasting change in the world. The school’s predecessor, the Center on Philanthropy, was founded in 1987.

title: Center on Philanthropy Panel Study
description: This grant provides partial support for the Center on Philanthropy Panel Study, an ongoing research study to collect detailed data describing defining characteristics and the philanthropic behavior of American families. The study follows giving and volunteering habits of 8,000 households over time and over generations as families mature, face differing economic circumstances, and encounter changes in their family size, health, and other factors. It is conducted in conjunction with the Institute for Social Research Panel Study of Income Dynamics at the University of Michigan, which has surveyed families since 1968 and to which a philanthropy component was added in 2001. The data set produced by the study is the best, most accurate resource for measuring giving and volunteering in the United States and is used extensively by researchers. Founded in 1987, the Center on Philanthropy at Indiana University-Purdue University Indianapolis conducts research, offers academic programs, and provides philanthropic services.

title: Study of Race Relations in Genesee County
grantee: City of Flint Human Relations Commission
description: This grant will provide support to the City of Flint Human Relations Commission for a race relations study. The purpose of this study is to understand the relationships between local ethnic and racial groups and determine how race relations affect Genesee County. The study is based in part on the 2007 Pew Research Center study and the 1995 Genesee County race relations study.

title: Dissemination of Public Participation Procedures by Involvement of Youth in Community Life
description: The project goal is to increase the capacity and motivation of young people to promote the accountability of local government in Russia. InEcA-consulting will work in two communities in Western Siberia to strengthen the understanding and use of effective techniques to engage citizens in local government decisionmaking. The grantee will also work with the Novokuznetsk branch of Kemerovo State University to develop an accredited course on public participation for students and local officials. In 2009-2010, InEcA-consulting fostered the development of youth networks in three regions which, in turn, worked closely with local authorities to develop strategies to address environmental and social issues within their communities. Established in 1995 in the industrial and mining region of Kemerovo in Western Siberia, the grantee promotes efficient environmental management practices and effective public participation procedures. It operates in conjunction with Information Ecological Agency, which implements civic engagement and environmental information projects on a not-for-profit basis.

title: Dissemination of Public Participation Procedures by Involvement of Youth in Community Life
description: The project goal is to increase the capacity and motivation of young people to promote the accountability of local government in Russia. InEcA-consulting will work in two communities in Western Siberia to strengthen the understanding and use of effective techniques to engage citizens in local government decisionmaking. The grantee will also work with the Novokuznetsk branch of Kemerovo State University to refine an accredited course on public participation for students and local officials. In 2011-2012, InEcA-consulting fostered the development of youth networks in three regions which, in turn, worked closely with local authorities to develop strategies to address environmental and social issues within their communities. Established in 1995 in the industrial and mining region of Kemerovo in Western Siberia, the grantee promotes efficient environmental management practices and effective public participation procedures.

title: Dissemination of Public Participation Procedures by Involvement of Youth in Community Life
description: The project goal is to increase capacity and motivation of young people to promote accountability of local government in Russia. InEca-consulting will work in three communities in Western Siberia to introduce effective techniques for using public hearings and other mechanisms to engage citizens in local government decisionmaking. At the same time, it will work closely with local authorities to demonstrate the positive benefits of civic engagement. Together, youth organizations, citizens groups, and local officials will identify priority issues and will implement pilot projects aimed at their resolution. Established in 1995 and located in the industrial and mining region of Kemerovo in Western Siberia, the grantee works to promote efficient environmental management practices and effective public participation procedures. It operates in conjunction with Information Ecological Agency, which implements civic engagement and environmental information projects on a not-for-profit basis.

title: Sakhalin Watershed Council Network Initiative
description: The project goal is to promote public participation in decisionmaking in order to maximize local benefits from resource exploitation. The Sakhalin Salmon Initiative Center will do this through strengthening the capacity of a network of watershed councils on Sakhalin Island off Russia’s Pacific Coast. These community-based councils will represent the varied interests of a watershed’s resident population, users, and visitors. They will provide input on policy, economic, and restoration activities, encouraging civil society to channel community knowledge to government decisionmakers. In 2009-2010, a total of five such councils were created, and the network established formal agreements with regional and federal agencies to assist in developing antipoaching and other protection policies. The Sakhalin Salmon Initiative Center was established in 2007 following a three-year consultation process among government, scientists, business, and civic organizations and aims to promote sustainable, community-based development in a context of large-scale natural resource exploitation.

title: Russian Far East Public Watershed Council Network Initiative
description: The project goal is to promote public participation in decisionmaking in order to maximize local benefits from resource exploitation. To this end, the Wild Salmon Center will continue to strengthen the capacity of a network of watershed councils in the Russian Far East. In 2011-2012, these community-based councils successfully represented the varied interests of the watersheds’ resident populations, users, and visitors. They provided input on policy, economic, and restoration activities, encouraging civil society to channel community knowledge to government decisionmakers. In 2013-2014, project activities include supporting council strategy implementation, conducting outreach and recruiting new leadership, facilitating learning between the councils, providing expert training, and supporting the development of policy recommendations. Established in 1992, the Wild Salmon Center promotes the conservation and sustainable use of wild salmon ecosystems across the Pacific Rim.

title: Russian Far East Public Watershed Council Network
description: The project goal is to promote public participation in decision making related to local resource use and conservation. The Wild Salmon Center will continue to strengthen the capacity of a network of watershed councils in the Russian Far East. Project activities will include supporting council strategy implementation, conducting outreach and recruiting new leadership, facilitating learning among the councils, providing expert training, and supporting the development of policy recommendations. In 2013-2014, these community-based councils successfully represented the varied interests of the watersheds’ resident populations, users, and visitors. In addition to conducting over 700 antipoaching raids, the councils successfully advocated to reintroduce controlled sportfishing on some territories. The Bolshaya River conservation plan in Kamchatka won international recognition as a model of integrated community management. Established in 1992, the Wild Salmon Center promotes the conservation and sustainable use of wild salmon ecosystems across the Pacific Rim.

title: Russian Far East Public Watershed Council Network
description: The project goal is to promote public participation in decisionmaking related to local resource use and conservation. Wild Salmon Center will continue to strengthen the capacity of a network of watershed councils in the Russian Far East. Project activities will include supporting council strategy implementation, identifying opportunities for sustainable financing, facilitating learning between the councils, providing expert training, and continuing engagement with local communities in habitat preservation. In 2015-16, these community-based councils successfully represented the varied interests of the watersheds’ diverse stakeholders, achieving a benchmark of 50 percent membership of civil society representatives. In addition to conducting over 500 antipoaching raids annually, the councils engaged more than 5,000 residents in a variety of conservation and education activities. One council successfully challenged operations of a gold mining concern which threatened viability of a whole salmon habitat. Established in 1992, Wild Salmon Center promotes the conservation and sustainable use of wild salmon ecosystems across the Pacific Rim.

title: Sakhalin Watershed Council Network Initiative
description: The project goal is to promote public participation in decisionmaking in order to maximize local benefits from resource exploitation. This will be done through the creation of a network of watershed councils on Sakhalin Island off Russia’s Pacific Coast. These community-based organizations will serve to address the varied interests of a watershed’s resident population, users, and visitors. They will develop and strategically distribute input on policy, economic, and restoration activities, allowing civil society to provide community knowledge to government decisionmakers. The councils will receive small annual grants to implement local projects identified as essential in addressing local economic or environmental priorities. The Sakhalin Salmon Initiative Center was established in 2007 following a three-year consultation process. The initiative involves a wide range of local, national, and international stakeholders from government, business, and civil society and aims to promote sustainable, community-based development in a context of large-scale natural resource exploitation.

title: Leadership Through Philanthropy
grantee: Leadership Education for Asian Pacifics, Inc.
description: Leadership Education for Asian Pacifics is a national, nonprofit organization dedicated to developing full participation for Asian and Pacific Islanders in work and community opportunities through leadership, empowerment, and policy. It has a very successful leadership curriculum which includes a focus on philanthropic leadership. For this Leadership Through Philanthropy project, the grantee has partnered with the National Black MBA Association, National Black United Fund, National Society of Hispanic MBAs, and Volunteer Consulting Group to redesign and modify the curriculum to fit the needs of the Latino and African-American communities. The end goal is to foster and train leaders and, in the process, teach their members and constituents about the critical role that philanthropy plays in their larger leadership responsibilities.

title: Assets Learning Project
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: Important practice and policy achievements have been made in the asset building field over the past decade, yet several challenges remain. Most notably, scale — defined as expanding successes from thousands to millions of families in a cost-efficient manner — remains elusive. This renewal grant will enable Brandeis University to support the development of policy initiatives that address the issue of scale and other asset building challenges by continuing to document and disseminate information about promising strategies. Brandeis University’s Institute on Assets and Social Policy is a public policy institute whose mission is to conduct research that informs policies and practices that broaden wealth, and improve the social and economic well-being of American households.

title: Assets Learning Project
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant will support ongoing management of learning communities for the Foundation’s asset-building grantees. These communities provide grantees and other asset-building stakeholders a unique space for the exchange of ideas and strategies, problem-solving, and for the development of potential collaborations. As the facilitator of these communities, Brandeis University’s Institute on Assets and Social Policy will develop content for meetings, Webinars, and conference calls with the Foundation’s grantees. Project staff will also serve as an evaluation partner, monitoring meetings and other activities for important insights and lessons and sharing that information with the asset-building field. Brandeis University’s Institute on Assets and Social Policy is a public policy institute whose mission is to conduct research that informs policies and practices that broaden wealth and improves the social and economic well-being of American households.

title: Assets Learning Project
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: Important policy and practice achievements have been made in the asset-building field over the past decade, yet major challenges remain. Most notably, scale — defined as expanding successes from thousands to millions of families in a cost efficient manner — remains elusive. This grant will enable Brandeis University to make a significant strategic contribution to the development of asset-building policy initiatives that address such challenges by implementing a four-year project of evaluation, documentation, and networking. The Assets Learning Project will collect, analyze, and disseminate information about promising asset initiatives and leverage that information to advance policy, practice, and funding for asset building. Brandeis University’s Institute on Assets and Social Policy is a public policy institute whose mission is to conduct research to inform policies and practices that broaden wealth and improve the social and economic well-being of American households.

title: Diversity and Inclusiveness Program
description: The Council on Foundations, a membership association of 2,100 grantmaking organizations worldwide, focuses on government relations and advocacy, communications, standard-setting, learning opportunities, research, legal expertise, and convenings to assist the philanthropic sector in advancing the common good. Through the Diversity and Inclusiveness Program, the council has completed a five-year study and report on chief executive officer demographics; convened grantmaking organizations to develop a strategy focused on promoting diversity and inclusiveness in hiring practices; and developed a grantee demographic data collection tool and template. This grant will continue to provide partial support to the Council on Foundations to launch a project designed to promote inclusive practices in the search, identification, hiring, and retention processes throughout the philanthropic field; develop diversity and inclusiveness-focused educational programming and tools; conduct debriefings for policymakers as well as monitor state and federal advocacy efforts on diversity, inclusiveness, and equity; and pilot the grantee demographic data collection and analysis project.

title: Diversity and Inclusiveness Program
description: The Council on Foundations, a membership association of 2,100 grantmaking organizations worldwide, focuses on government relations and advocacy, communications, standard-setting, learning opportunities, research, legal expertise, and convenings to assist the philanthropic sector in advancing the common good. Through the Diversity and Inclusiveness Program, the grantee has begun to develop a diverse pipeline of trustee and executive-level talent coming into the sector; provided outreach and communications about the importance of diversity; created educational tools that promote diversity and inclusion as part of effectiveness; and supported a fieldwide collaboration designed to increase diversity across the field. This grant will provide partial support to the grantee to continue the important work of promoting diversity and inclusion in the field of philanthropy.

title: Diversity and Inclusiveness Program
description: The Council on Foundations was formed to promote responsible and effective philanthropy and has a membership of 2,100 grantmaking foundations and giving programs worldwide. The council provides the opportunities, leadership, and tools that philanthropic organizations need to expand, enhance, and sustain their ability to advance the common good. This grant will provide partial support to the council for its Diversity and Inclusiveness Program, which has three main goals: 1) increase the diversity of trustee and executive-level talent in philanthropy; 2) create educational programming on the value and definition of diversity and inclusiveness as a tool of effectiveness; and 3) increase awareness of the importance of diversity and inclusiveness within the philanthropic sector.

title: Mobilizing Local Communities to Prevent Domestic Violence
grantee: National Center for Prevention of Violence "ANNA"
description: The program goal is to engage citizens and civil society organizations in grassroots responses to violence against women and girls in the Southern Federal District of Russia. To this end, the National Center for Prevention of Violence “ANNA” and its local partners will work to increase public awareness about gender-based violence and to create an atmosphere of intolerance toward such violence within local communities. Community mobilization teams will be trained in outreach skills, cross-cultural awareness, and social marketing techniques aimed at engaging a broad cross-section of their communities in activities to prevent rights abuses. In 2008-2010, the grantee undertook detailed research into public awareness of gender-based rights abuse, strengthened capacity of three local partner organizations to address these issues, and secured cooperation and engagement of a range of government officials and community leaders to support efforts to prevent gender-based violence. Established in 1995, the National Center for Prevention of Violence “ANNA” provides social, economic, and legal assistance to women and children in crisis.

title: Mobilizing Local Communities to Prevent Domestic Violence
grantee: National Center for Prevention of Violence "ANNA"
description: The program goal is to achieve sustainable grassroots citizen engagement by building the capacity of civil society organizations to respond to a key issue facing communities in the Northern Caucus region of Russia. To this end, the National Center for Prevention of Violence “ANNA” and its local partners will build upon their successful efforts to address gender-based violence through raising public awareness of the issue and partnering with law enforcement agencies. Specifically, they will aim to generate community accountability — where communities themselves intervene to prevent such violence in peaceful ways. In 2010-2012, the grantee and its partners established a critical collaboration with local law enforcement bodies, religious councils, and educational institutions, all of which helped break down taboos related to gender-based violence. Over 100 workshops, educational activities, and community discussions were staged throughout the region. Established in 1995, the National Center for Prevention of Violence “ANNA” provides social, economic, and legal assistance to women and children in crisis.

title: Mobilizing Local Communities to Prevent Domestic Violence
grantee: National Center for Prevention of Violence "ANNA"
description: The program goal is to achieve sustainable grassroots citizen engagement by building the capacity of civil society organizations and local communities to respond to gender-based violence, a key issue facing communities in the Northern Caucasus region of Russia. To this end, the National Center for Prevention of Violence “ANNA” and its local partners will foster community accountability — where communities themselves intervene to peacefully prevent such violence. Specifically, the grantee will raise public awareness and understanding of the issues and strengthen the capacities of nonprofits and local communities in the targeted regions actively to condemn, prevent, and combat violence against women. In 2012-2014, the grantee and its partners established community mobilization teams that work directly in local communities in the region by organizing workshops, educational activities, and community discussions. Significant progress was also made in improving networking and collaboration among local nonprofits in different parts of the Northern Caucasus engaged in the field of violence against women. Established in 1995, the National Center for Prevention of Violence “ANNA” provides social, economic, and legal assistance to women and children in crisis.

title: Mobilizing Local Communities to Prevent Domestic Violence
grantee: National Center for Prevention of Violence "ANNA"
description: The program goal is to increase involvement of local communities in the prevention of violence against women and girls in the Southern Federal District of Russia. The grantee and its local partners will work to increase public awareness about gender-based violence and to generate an atmosphere of intolerance toward such violence within local communities. Community mobilization teams will be trained in outreach techniques, cross-cultural awareness, and appropriate counseling skills in order to coordinate project activities in their respective regions. In addition, partners will work together to build collaboration among governmental agencies, including health care providers, law enforcement bodies, and schools, to provide appropriate services and support for women and girls who are victims of violence. Established in 1995, the National Center for Prevention of Violence “ANNA” provides social, economic, and legal assistance to women and children in crisis. It coordinates the National Network Against Violence, which today unites over 160 organizations across Russia.

title: TimeBank
description: The program goal is to promote civic engagement and the mobilization of community resources through volunteerism. During the previous grant period, the grantee was able to adapt the British TimeBank model, a volunteer brokering system, and successfully establish a TimeBank in Nizhni Novgorod involving over 500 registered volunteer users. In 2011-2013, Nizhni Novgorod Voluntary Service staff will conduct study visits to other countries with successful experience with TimeBank implementation in order to learn and further adapt different approaches to the TimeBank model, expand the TimeBank model to two new Russian regions, create a strong regional and interregional network, increase the number of participants, and establish the sustainability and independence of the Nizhni Novgorod TimeBank. Established in 1997, Nizhni Novgorod Voluntary Service works with local businesses and charities to promote civic and community activism among young people.

title: TimeBank
description: The program goal is to promote civic engagement and the mobilization of community resources through volunteerism. During the previous grant period, the grantee was able to refine the British TimeBank model, a volunteer brokering system, and quadruple the number of registered users to over 3,000. Self-financing TimeBanks have successfully been established in two additional regions. The grantee is also initiating a network of TimeBanks in six countries. In 2014-2015, Nizhni Novgorod Voluntary Service staff will work to further increase awareness of, and participation in, TimeBank activities both in established regions and in as many as ten new territories. It will also work to link Russian efforts to develop this model of volunteering more closely with partners in countries within the European Union and the former Soviet space. Established in 1997, Nizhni Novgorod Voluntary Service works with local businesses and charities to promote civic and community activism among young people.

title: TimeBank
description: The program goal is to promote civic engagement and the mobilization of community resources through volunteerism. The Nizhni Novgorod Voluntary Service will develop the “TimeBank” volunteer brokering system in Nizhni Novgorod and, ultimately, the surrounding regions of Russia. The grantee will conduct an intensive public awareness campaign focused on volunteerism. Its staff will undergo training in the use of time-matching software and volunteer management and motivation. Staff members will undertake study visits to Britain to see established TimeBanks in operation. Nizhni Novgorod Voluntary Service will contract with and train six local partner organizations who will oversee the development of the model in their towns. At the end of this initial two-year period, Nizhni Novgorod Voluntary Service expects to have no fewer than 1,000 people regularly contributing time and services to the TimeBank. Established in 1997, Nizhni Novgorod Voluntary Service works with local businesses and charities to promote civic and community activism among young people.

title: Technical Assistance on Land Bank Implementation
description: In developing the Genesee County Land Bank, Genesee County initiated a program for urban land reform that has become a national model. As a result, Genesee County has seen the rehabilitation of formerly abandoned houses, conveyance of hundreds of side lots to next-door neighbors, demolition of hundreds of abandoned structures, maintenance of thousands of empty lots, development of neighborhood greening and gardening projects, and other development projects. This model has spread to at least ten communities in Michigan. The purpose of this grant to Genesee Institute is to provide partial funding for the provision of technical assistance to up to ten additional communities to help them create or sustain a land bank authority.

title: General Purposes
description: The project goal is to improve the quality and effectiveness of policy development and implementation in Bosnia-Herzegovina. To this end, the Centre for Socio-Economic Studies “Populari,” a think tank established in late 2007, promotes informed debate on social, economic, and political developments through a variety of activities and analytical reports. During the grant period, the center will carry out field-based studies and assessments and stimulate discussion of policy issues through seminars, public presentations, and bilateral meetings. The center will focus on monitoring and promoting European Union integration and accession; the ownership and management of state property and how this complicates Bosnia-Herzegovina’s state-building efforts; and working with young people in high schools and colleges to stimulate critical thinking about the country’s future. In 2008-2010, the center produced important reports as well as a documentary film based on solid, field-based research and covering such timely issues as the country’s progress toward European Union accession and its inclusion in the European Union’s visa-free regime.

title: General Purposes
description: The project goal is to improve the quality and effectiveness of policy development and implementation in Bosnia-Herzegovina. To this end, the Centre for Socio-Economic Studies “Populari,” a think tank established in late 2007, promotes informed debate on social, economic, and political developments through a variety of activities, research, and analytical reports. During the grant period, the grantee will carry out field-based studies and assessments and stimulate discussion of policy issues through seminars, public presentations, and bilateral meetings. The grantee will focus on: monitoring and promoting European Union integration and accession; the effectiveness of state and local governance; and innovative, local-level social enterprise initiatives. In 2010-2012, the grantee conducted field-based research on the challenges Bosnia will face as it progresses in the European Union accession process, governmental transparency and efficiency in delivering essential public services, and the status of state-owned property. The grantee is based in Sarajevo, Bosnia.

title: General Purposes
description: The project goal is to improve the quality and effectiveness of policy development and implementation in Bosnia-Herzegovina. To this end, the Centre for Socio-Economic Studies “Populari,” a think tank established in late 2007, promotes informed debate on social, economic, and political developments through a variety of activities, research, and analytical reports. The grantee will focus on monitoring and promoting European Union integration and accession; the effectiveness of state and local governance; and innovative, local-level social enterprise initiatives. In 2012-2014, the grantee conducted field-based research on how to meet the conditions for the country’s successful accession to the European Union, governance challenges that impact the delivery of essential public services, relatively minor reforms that could yield significant economic benefit, and the status of philanthropy in Bosnia. The grantee is based in Sarajevo, Bosnia.

title: General Purposes
description: The project goal is to improve the quality and effectiveness of policy development and implementation in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Populari, a Bosnian think tank established in 2007, promotes informed debate on social, economic, and political developments through a variety of activities, research, and analytical reports. During the grant period, the grantee will work at national and European Union levels and with a range of partners to carry out field-based studies and assessments and stimulate discussion of policy issues through seminars, public presentations, and bilateral meetings. The grantee will focus on the region’s European Union integration and accession process and countering the rise of illiberalism and populism in Bosnia-Herzegovina and the wider Balkan region. In 2014-2016, the grantee conducted extensive field research and produced six in-depth reports on topics including security challenges in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Balkan region’s common foreign policy objectives, and relations between Bosnia-Herzegovina and Turkey. Populari is registered in Bosnia-Herzegovina and has staff and associated researchers based in Sarajevo, Berlin, Brussels, Pristina, and Belgrade.

title: General Purposes
description: The project goal is to improve the quality and effectiveness of policy development and implementation in Bosnia-Herzegovina. To this end, the Centre for Socio-Economic Studies “Populari,” a newly established think tank, will promote more informed debate on social, economic, and political developments through a variety of activities and analytical reports. During the grant period, the Populari will develop its capacity for policy-relevant research and analysis; carry out field-based studies and assessments; design and implement pilot development projects using evidence-based research techniques; and stimulate discussion of policy issues through seminars, public presentations, and bilateral meetings. Established in late 2007, over the last six months the grantee has produced two high-profile reports, coproduced a documentary film, and participated in several international conferences on Balkans policy.

title: General Purposes
grantee: National Center on Philanthropy and the Law
description: The National Center on Philanthropy and the Law, an academic center located at New York University School of Law, is the only institution of its kind focused on the single discipline of law and philanthropy. The center’s goals of increasing the knowledge of students, faculty, practitioners, nonprofit managers, and policymakers in the area of law and philanthropy; improving the practice of law in this field; and increasing the efficacy of the nonprofit sector are realized through eight core activities: curriculum development, scholarly research, conferences, library collection, bibliography, fellowships, placement and career counseling, and faculty development. Activities over the grant period will include hosting conferences, scholarly research and publications on nonprofit legal issues, providing job placement and career counseling for law students and lawyers interested in the nonprofit sector, maintaining and updating a nonprofit legal library and bibliography, and providing fellowships in nonprofit law for up to four law school graduates.

title: Dissemination of Tools and Resources
description: This grant will provide support to the Tiger Woods Foundation to expand its technical assistance efforts through the Tiger Woods Learning Center. The Tiger Woods Learning Center provides afterschool and summer programs focused on engaging and interactive learning opportunities related to career fields for middle and high school students. This grant will support the planning and implementation of a series of Career Conferences that incorporate hands-on activities and professionals from the field into sessions for students with a parallel set of workshops for parents and educators on career and college awareness. The Career Conference program will be piloted at the Tiger Woods Learning Center and include other Mott grantees as participants.

title: Impacts of Large-scale Infrastructure Projects and Development in the Peruvian Amazon
description: This grant will support the Instituto del Bien Común, a nonprofit technical assistance organization, to develop and promote environmental and social standards for oil and gas and infrastructure investments in the Peruvian Amazon and to minimize the negative impacts of large-scale energy and infrastructure projects on the environment and local communities. The grantee will provide local communities in the Andean Amazon with maps, policy analyses, and strategic advice on infrastructure and oil and gas investments, so they can have a more informed voice in shaping these investments to be more sustainable.

title: Impacts of Large-scale Infrastructure Projects and Development in the Peruvian Amazon
description: This grant will support the Instituto del Bien Común, a nonprofit, technical assistance organization, to develop and promote environmental and social standards for oil and gas and infrastructure investments in the Peruvian Amazon and to minimize the negative impacts of large-scale energy and infrastructure projects on the environment and local communities. The Instituto del Bien Común will provide local communities in the Andean Amazon with maps, policy analysis, and strategic advice on infrastructure and oil and gas investments so they can have a more informed voice in shaping these investments to be more sustainable.

title: Accountability for Integration and Infrastructure Investments in Peru
description: This grant will provide continued support to the Centro Peruano de Estudios Sociales, a Peruvian public policy research center for sustainable regional planning processes in southern Peru. This grant will also support consolidation of a new regional network on extractive industries in Latin America. This project provides training and information to local authorities and key opinion leaders and creates spaces for public debate on strategies for shaping infrastructure and energy investments to make them less environmentally damaging and more supportive of local sustainable development.

title: Accountability for Integration and Infrastructure Investments in Peru
description: This grant increase will support the Centro Peruano de Estudios Sociales, a Peruvian public policy research center, for its efforts to strengthen sustainable regional planning processes in southern Peru and bring increased accountability and transparency to extractive industries in Latin America. This project provides training and information to local authorities and key opinion leaders and creates spaces for public debate on strategies for shaping infrastructure and energy investments to make them less environmentally damaging and more supportive of local sustainable development.

title: Accountability for Integration and Infrastructure Investments in Peru
description: This grant will support the Centro Peruano de Estudios Sociales to provide training and analysis to regional planning processes in southern Peru, including strategies for shaping infrastructure investments in that region. This project will provide training and information to local authorities and key opinion leaders and will convene different sectors of civil society, including business leaders, environmental organizations, farmers groups, and other community organizations in facilitated dialogues that will focus on how to make infrastructure investments less environmentally damaging and more supportive of local sustainable development.

title: Strengthening Civil Society Engagement in Regional Integration and Infrastructure Investments in Colombia
grantee: Instituto Latinoamericano para una Sociedad y un Derecho Alternativos
description: This grant will support the Instituto Latinoamericano de Servicios Legales Alternativos, a Colombian, nonprofit organization that works on civic engagement across a variety of issues, to provide analysis and information on energy and infrastructure investments in the Amazon region to local communities and local and regional authorities. The grant will also support efforts to strengthen nongovernmental organization and community participation in decisionmaking about investments by the international and regional financial institutions, with a particular focus on the environmental and social effects of infrastructure and energy projects.

title: Strengthening Civil Society Engagement in Regional Integration and Infrastructure Investments in Colombia
grantee: Instituto Latinoamericano para una Sociedad y un Derecho Alternativos
description: This grant will support the Instituto Latinoamericano para una Sociedad y un Derecho Alternativos, a Colombian, nonprofit organization that works on civic engagement across a variety of issues, to promote informed public participation in the development, design, and implementation of energy and infrastructure projects, as well as investments aimed at addressing climate change through training and information sharing. The grant will also support efforts to ensure that social and environmental safeguard policies for these kinds of projects are applied by both international and regional financiers in South America.

title: Strengthening Civil Society Engagement in Regional Integration and Infrastructure Investments in Colombia
grantee: Instituto Latinoamericano para una Sociedad y un Derecho Alternativos
description: This grant will support the Instituto Latinoamericano de Servicios Legales Alternativos, a Colombian, nonprofit organization that works on civic engagement across a variety of issues, to provide analysis and information on energy and infrastructure investments in Colombia to local communities and local and regional authorities. The analysis will include information about the scope and potential environmental and social impacts of these projects, and strategies for pressing international financial institutions to live up to their environmental and social commitments. The grant will also support coordination of a civil society gathering in parallel to the 2009 annual governors meeting of the Inter-American Development Bank in Medellín, Colombia, where organizations will reflect on lessons learned from five decades of development investments in the region.

title: Increasing Civil Society Access to Emerging Technology
description: This grant will provide CompuMentor with support to: (1) establish an office in Warsaw to better serve countries in Central/Eastern Europe and Russia with its TechSoup social venture, a program through which major technology providers donate information technology to nonprofits and libraries; (2) provide technology guidance and training to help Mott Foundation grantees meet the requirements associated with USA Patriot Act compliance; and (3) extend NetSquared, a program which helps nonprofits use social media effectively for mission advancement globally. CompuMentor is a leading nonprofit technology assistance organization, which aims to increase the ability of civil society organizations globally to access and harness emerging technology tools and resources.

title: Las Artes de Mexico
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will support the efforts of the Flint Institute of Arts to promote the Las Artes de Mexico, an exhibition celebrating the rich and diverse artistic traditions of Mexico. A gala event will open the exhibition at the art institute and will be part of a series of activities being coordinated citywide during Hispanic Heritage Month. As part of the gala, local Hispanic/Latino restaurateurs will prepare authentic cuisine, and the Ballet Folklorico from Veracruz, Mexico will provide live entertainment. Ballet Folklorico is a dance group of high school and college students that perform traditional dances representing the various states of Mexico and the indigenous dances of Veracruz.

title: Out-of-School-Time eLearning Platform
description: This grant will support the BELL Foundation in its efforts to provide its training modules for afterschool and summer program practitioners in the use of high quality educational programming. This initiative includes the design, development, and implementation of an eLearning system for delivering training to program staff in an efficient, cost-effective, and scalable manner. With this project, the BELL Foundation hopes to: 1) improve outcomes for children by delivering effective, standardized training to program staff; 2) provide content that deepens and expands the skill sets of a diverse group of educators; and 3) deliver training activities that are efficient and scalable to reach as many children as possible.

title: Strengthening Forest Governance Through REDD
description: The world is losing over 18 million acres of forest per year, primarily in the tropical areas of Africa, Asia, and Latin America, which has serious implications for the world’s poor, its biodiversity, and climate change. The 2007 meeting of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change agreed to incorporate the first serious consideration of forest protection as a key element of reducing greenhouse gas emissions. With this grant, the World Resources Institute will use its expertise in environmental governance and forestry to develop clear criteria for assessing and improving forestry governance as a prerequisite to any discussion on whether and how market forces should be used as incentives for tropical forest conservation.

title: Campaign for Youth: Elevating Disconnected Youth as a Priority and Policy Agenda Item for a New Administration and Congress
grantee: Center for Law and Social Policy
description: This grant will provide support to the Campaign for Youth, a project of the Center for Law and Social Policy, to increase the visibility of disconnected youth issues as a national priority and policy agenda item. The Campaign for Youth is a coalition of national youth policy and direct service organizations committed to bringing attention to the needs of young people who are out of work, out of school, and out of the mainstream. Support will enable the Campaign for Youth to hire a senior-level staff person to coordinate the coalition’s efforts and engage a communications firm to assist in message development and other communication/media strategies to elevate the challenges and solutions for disconnected youth.

title: The Vanishing Middle Class Documentary
description: This grant will help WBUR, the National Public Radio affiliate located at Boston University, underwrite a radio documentary project entitled “The Vanishing Middle Class”. Specifically, the project will consist of an hour-long documentary examining what it means to be middle class today, and a follow-up series comparing the growing middle-class struggle in two states — Massachusetts and Michigan. “Inside Out” documentary is a production of WBUR and is a major player in the public radio system. The station produces several nationally distributed and award-winning programs, including “Car Talk”, “On Point”, and “Here and Now” for Public Radio International.

title: Integration Investments and Indigenous Peoples in South America
description: The Indian Law Resource Center is one of the preeminent nongovernmental organizations in the United States working to promote indigenous peoples from around the world since 1978. This renewal grant will support the grantee’s work to increase the capacity of indigenous organizations and communities to protect their environment. The project will combine Washington-based policy work at the international financial institutions with capacity building for indigenous people so that they can more effectively use international rules and safeguard policies to protect their natural resources. In particular, the project will help communities reduce the impact of infrastructure and energy projects in South America where such projects are threatening the environment and local livelihoods.

title: Integration Investments and Indigenous Peoples in South America
description: The Indian Law Resource Center a nongovernmental organization working to promote the interests of indigenous peoples from around the world since 1978. This renewal grant will support the grantee’s efforts to promote strengthened safeguard policies at multilateral development banks that are consistent with international legal standards and increased transparency and accountability to ensure that environmental and social protections are upheld and respected. A key goal of this project is to shift financing away from unsustainable infrastructure and energy projects that are likely to cause irreversible and irreparable harm to the environment, by promoting the participation and interests of indigenous and other local communities whose lives and livelihoods depend on the health of these ecosystems.

title: Integration Investments and Indigenous Peoples in South America
description: The Indian Law Resource Center is a preeminent nongovernmental organizations based in the United States and working since 1978 to promote the interests of indigenous peoples from around the world. This renewal grant will support the grantee’s efforts to promote strengthened safeguards at international financial institutions and increased transparency and accountability to ensure social and environmental protections are respected. A key goal of this project is to shift development finance away from unsustainable energy and infrastructure projects that are likely to cause irreversible harm to the environment by promoting the participation of indigenous and local communities in decisionmaking about development in sensitive ecosystems on which they depend.

title: Integration Investments and Indigenous Peoples in South America
description: The Indian Law Resource Center is a preeminent U.S.-based nongovernmental organization working since 1978 to promote the interests of indigenous people from around the world. This grant increase will support the grantee’s efforts to build capacity and transfer technical assistance related to public participation and strengthening adherence to social and environmental standards by the Brazilian Development Bank.

title: Integration Investments and Indigenous Peoples in South America
description: Founded in 1978, the Indian Law Resource Center is a nonprofit organization dedicated to protecting and promoting the rights of indigenous peoples in North, Central, and South America. The grantee intends to build on its 15 years of work addressing public sector financial institutions that fund energy and infrastructure projects in South America. By incorporating the Brazilian Development Bank and the Inter-American Development Bank into their scope of work, the grantee will expand promoting stronger safeguards and increased accountability by these financial institutions to help ensure social and environmental protections are respected.

title: Integration Investments and Indigenous Peoples in South America
description: Founded in 1978, the Indian Law Resource Center is a nonprofit organization dedicated to protecting and promoting the rights of indigenous peoples in North, Central, and South America. During the last grant period, the grantee made important progress on indigenous peoples safeguard policy at international financial institutions and on building dialogue between Amazon indigenous networks and public financial institutions. During the next grant period, the grantee will focus on strengthening the indigenous peoples safeguard at international financial institutions, and advancing a stand-alone indigenous safeguard at the Brazilian Development Bank.

title: Integration Investments and Indigenous Peoples in South America
description: The Indian Law Resource Center is one of the preeminent nongovernmental organizations in the United States working to promote indigenous peoples from around the world since 1978. This grant will support the grantee’s work to increase the capacity of indigenous organizations and communities to protect their environment. The project will combine Washington-based policy work at the international financial institutions with capacity building for indigenous people, so that they can more effectively use international rules and safeguard policies to protect their natural resources. In particular, the project will help communities reduce the impact of destructive infrastructure and energy projects in selected areas of Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru where such projects are threatening the environment and local livelihoods.

title: Consolidating Membership
description: Established in 1989, the European Foundation Centre is an international association of foundations and corporate funders dedicated to strengthening European philanthropy. Through this program, the centre will undertake a number of activities to consolidate its membership and improve its services to members. Program activities include: (1) implementing a new fee structure; (2) enhancing Internet communications; (3) creating a strategic communications plan; (4) reviewing capacity-building programs with the aim of creating a member-oriented capacity-building strategy; (5) implementing new guidelines for its interest groups; (6) improving information and communication technology, including launching a new Web site and implementing new software packages to manage internal and external information more effectively; and (7) enhancing representation of Central and Eastern European and community philanthropy organizations in all its networks and committees.

title: Governance Programme
description: The South African Institute for Advancement, also known as Inyathelo, promotes philanthropy in South Africa and helps develop the capacity of philanthropic institutions and nonprofit organizations to achieve their objectives in a sustainable manner. This grant will support Inyathelo’s effort to contribute to the development of a stronger, well-informed nonprofit and philanthropy sector, as well as build its capacity to assist the sector with issues such as legal compliance, governance, accountability, and taxation. Specific activities will include focused research pertaining to both the nonprofit and philanthropy sectors, the development of accessible knowledge resources, the development of partnerships with relevant organizations, and capacity-development workshops. Inyathelo was established in 2002 to offer services to nonprofits including organizational capacity building, information resources, practical training, and other support services that ensure a professional and sustainable approach for acquiring resources that advance the goals of institutions.

title: Investigating the Redefined Role of Civil Society in a Maturing Democracy
description: This grant supports the Centre for Policy Studies to explore how South African civil society will adjust and position itself in relation to new leadership in the African National Congress, the dominant political party in South Africa, and a new government administration after the 2009 national elections. Research will include interviews with key government and civil society leaders. Several reports on research findings will be produced and widely disseminated. Additionally, a conference will be convened for civil society leaders and others to discuss the research findings. Established in the late 1980s, the Centre for Policy Studies is an independent research organization that focuses on economic and social policy, governance, human rights, and civil society.

title: Overture Program and Partnership with Flint Institute of Music
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide continued support to the Sphinx Organization to offer a continuum of music instruction to underserved students in Flint, Michigan. The overture program, which introduces students to classical music and the violin, will expand to five Flint elementary schools. It will provide up to 75 students with free group violin lessons after school. Students from the program will be eligible for additional private lessons at the school and for scholarships to take more advanced violin lessons and classes at the Flint Institute of Music at no cost. In addition, the Harlem Quartet, a premier ensemble comprised of Sphinx national competition winners, will come to Flint for a one-week residency. These experienced artists will provide master classes, lessons, and chamber music coaching to students and hold free public performances for the community.

title: Overture Program and Partnership with Flint Institute of Music
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This renewal grant will provide continued support to the Sphinx Organization to offer a continuum of music instruction to underserved students in Flint, Michigan. The Sphinx Overture program, which introduces students to classical music and the violin, will expand to six Flint elementary schools. The program will provide students with free group violin lessons after school. Students from the program will be eligible for additional private lessons at the school from program instructors and for scholarships to take more advanced violin lessons and classes at the Flint Institute of Music at no cost. In addition, the Catalyst Quartet, a premier ensemble comprised of Sphinx competition alumni, will come to Flint for a residency. These experienced artists will provide master classes, lessons, and chamber music coaching to students and hold free public performances for the community.

title: Overture Program and Partnership with Flint Institute of Music
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This renewal grant will provide continued support to the Sphinx Organization to offer a continuum of music instruction to underserved students in Flint, Michigan. The Sphinx Overture program, which introduces students to classical music and the violin, will operate in all 12 of the elementary schools in the Flint Community Schools system. The program provides students with instruments and free group violin lessons after school. Students in the program are eligible for additional private lessons with program instructors at the school, as well as scholarships to take more advanced violin lessons and classes at the Flint Institute of Music at no cost. In addition, the Sphinx Catalyst Quartet will come to Flint for a performance and residency. These experienced artists will provide master classes, lessons, and chamber music coaching to students and hold free public performances for the community.

title: Overture Program and Partnership with Flint Institute of Music
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This renewal grant will provide continued support to the Sphinx Organization to offer a continuum of music instruction to underserved students in Flint. The Sphinx Overture program introduces students to classical music and basic violin instruction. The afterschool program will operate in all 12 Flint elementary schools during the 2013-14 school year. In addition, students from the program are eligible for group and private lessons at the Flint Institute of Music at no cost. An artist residency will bring accomplished Sphinx musicians to Flint for two different weeks that will include performances to introduce classical music and instruments to school groups, visits to Overture sessions, workshops, and a free concert held as part of the final Overture student recital.

The Sphinx Overture Program, which introduces students to classical music and the violin, is offered in all elementary Flint Community Schools. The program will provide students with free group violin lessons after school. Students in the program will be eligible for additional private lessons at the school from program instructors and for scholarships to take more advanced violin lessons and classes at the Flint Institute of Music.

The Sphinx Overture Program, which introduces students to classical music and the violin, will serve all Flint public elementary schools. The program will provide students with free group violin lessons after school. Through a partnership with the Flint Institute of Music, students from the program will be eligible for additional private lessons and more advanced violin lessons and classes at no cost. In addition, Overture students and their families have access to a range of other cultural experiences and enrichment activities including artist-in-residence workshops and performances as well as tickets for the Flint Symphony Orchestra, Flint Youth Symphony, and select shows at The Whiting.

The Sphinx Overture Program, which introduces students to classical music and violin, will serve all Flint public elementary schools. The program will provide students with free, afterschool group violin lessons. Music education supports cognitive stimulation and learning, and literacy skill development which are important for children exposed to lead. In addition, Sphinx Overture students and their families have access to a range of other cultural experiences and enrichment activities including artist in residence workshops and performances.
