The Sphinx Overture program, which introduces students to classical music and violin, serves all Flint public elementary schools. In partnership with YouthQuest and the Crim Fitness Foundation, the program will provide students with free, afterschool group violin lessons. Music education supports cognitive stimulation and learning, and literacy skill development. Through a partnership with the Flint Institute of Music, students from the program will be eligible for more advanced violin lessons and classes at no cost. In addition, Sphinx Overture students and their families have access to a range of other cultural experiences and enrichment activities including artist-in-residence workshops and performances.

title: Partnership with Flint Institute of Music
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will allow the Sphinx Organization to offer a continuum of instruction to low-income students in Flint, Michigan. The grantee has gained national attention making classical music accessible and more relevant to young people of color. This project will build on Sphinx programming already in Flint, by offering elementary students the opportunity to continue their music study in partnership with the Flint Institute of Music. Sphinx overture program graduates will be able to take violin lessons and classes at the music institute at little or no cost to students. In addition, the Harlem Quartet, a premier ensemble comprised of Sphinx national competition winners, will come to Flint for a one-week residency. These experienced artists will provide master classes, lessons, and chamber music coaching to students and hold a free public performance for the community.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to improve people’s lives in the area of Cluj, Romania, by developing local philanthropy and fostering civic activism. To this end, the Cluj Community Foundation will engage local stakeholders in identifying solutions to priority community needs, develop new fundraising strategies and sources of funding, improve its grantmaking systems and processes, and strengthen its organizational capacity and financial sustainability. The foundation was registered in January 2008 with the mission to improve the quality of life of people in the Cluj area through mobilizing and distributing local resources in support of local development initiatives. Over the past year, the foundation raised over $45,000 from local companies, individuals, and public sources and distributed small grants to 42 local projects related to children and youth.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to improve people’s lives in the Odorheiu Secuiesc region in Romania by developing local philanthropy and fostering civic activism. To this end, the Odorheiu Secuiesc Community Foundation will engage local stakeholders in identifying solutions to priority community needs, mobilizing local resources to address these needs, and making decisions about the allocation of the funds raised. In addition, the foundation will improve its grantmaking systems and processes and strengthen its organizational capacity and financial sustainability. The foundation was registered in January 2008 with the mission to encourage philanthropic behavior and local initiatives which improve the quality of life of people from the Odorheiu Secuiesc region. During the past six months, the grantee has raised over $40,000 from local businesses for its grants programs and operating costs.

title: Nevada Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Community Chest, Inc., to coordinate the Nevada Statewide Afterschool Network. In addition to continuing the network’s core work to advance afterschool programs in Nevada, it will complete a multiyear project to develop and implement school-age afterschool standards in Nevada. The network will also support policy change that will promote the development of high quality afterschool programs. To ensure that new models and best practices are incorporated nationally, the network will share lessons learned and products with the other statewide afterschool networks.

title: Nevada Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support After-School All-Stars which coordinates the Nevada Statewide Afterschool Network. The Nevada Statewide Afterschool Network will focus on building capacity for long-term success and advancing systems change for afterschool and expanded learning in Nevada. Over the next three years, the network will support the development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will seek to increase the quality and sustainability of expanded learning opportunities throughout the state by working to: 1) support programs throughout the state to adopt the Nevada Quality Standards for out-of-school time programs; 2) establish new statewide professional development opportunities; and 3) expand the network to support the growth of afterschool programs.

title: Nevada Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the After-School All-Stars to implement a partnership initiative focused on developing policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The grant will support the grantee to: 1) develop partners among afterschool stakeholders in Nevada; 2) establish a cohesive statewide afterschool network; 3) host a partner convening on afterschool; and 4) establish a steering committee for the partnership.

title: Nevada Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Community Chest, Inc., in its efforts to develop the Nevada Statewide Afterschool Network. The grantee and the Nevada Statewide Afterschool Network seek to create a sustainable structure that is focused on advocacy and policies that ensure out-of-school-time opportunities for all of Nevada’s school-aged youth, support the development and growth of the structure through networking, and support statewide systems to ensure that programs are of high quality. The Nevada Statewide Afterschool Network will systematically organize, mobilize, and communicate with out-of-school-time stakeholders to advocate for increased funding and support for afterschool programs at the local, state, and national levels. This grantee is the seventh cohort of Mott-funded statewide afterschool networks.

title: Strengthening America's Future Initiative
grantee: Center for the Study of the Presidency and Congress
description: This grant will provide support for the Strengthening America’s Future Initiative at the Center for the Study of the Presidency and Congress. In order to assist the presidential transition and new administration, the grantee will conduct a comprehensive net assessment to identify the critical challenges, the crosswalks between them, and the cost of inaction. With the assistance of a prominent steering committee, an innovations and synergies team, and specific issue teams, the grantee will develop a conceptual framework that will recommend prioritized, synergetic solutions to address the nation’s most pressing issues. The White House, congressional leaders, and the general public will be engaged through a series of briefings and an interactive Web site.

title: Innovations for the Microenterprise Field
description: This grant will allow the Aspen Institute to continue to conduct research on innovation that represents a potential solution to the challenge of sustainability for domestic microenterprise programs — a new business model in which microenterprise programming is embedded within a university setting and uses volunteer student resources that significantly lower the cost of service delivery.

title: Innovations for the Microenterprise Field
description: The Aspen Institute’s Innovations for the Microenterprise Field project provides funding for developing college student leaders in university-based microenterprise programs. Mott support has helped the project assist with the development of a campus microfinance alliance to help volunteer students start and strengthen services for microentrepreneurs. This grant will allow the grantee to support the institutionalization of the campus microfinance alliance to offer internship programs for student leaders, and to conduct research on student-based programs.

title: Innovations for the Microenterprise Field
description: This grant will allow the Aspen Institute to research an innovation that represents a potential solution to the challenge of sustainability for domestic microenterprise programs — a new business model in which microenterprise programming is embedded within a university setting and uses volunteer student resources that significantly lower the cost of service delivery.

title: Norman C. Francis Endowed Scholarship Fund
initiative: Historically and Predominantly Black Colleges and Universities
description: This grant will provide support for an endowed scholarship fund named in honor of Dr. Norman C. Francis. America’s longest serving college president, Francis celebrates his 40th anniversary as the leader of Xavier University of Louisiana in 2008. Under his visionary leadership, Xavier has become an internationally recognized institution of higher learning. Forty years ago, the university budget was under $20 million, and enrollment was fewer than 800 students. Today, Xavier’s student enrollment is approaching 4,000, and the budget exceeds $80 million. The New Orleans skyline has been transformed thanks to the new buildings constructed during his tenure. The university’s recovery from the devastation of Hurricanes Katrina and Rita demonstrates the resilience of the institution Francis has built over the years. In recognition of Francis’s commitment to excellence and service in higher education, the university will establish an endowed scholarship fund in his name. Scholarship recipients will exemplify his character by displaying perseverance toward academic success, as well as strong ethical behavior and a commitment to community service.

title: Resources for Evaluating Community Organizing
description: The Alliance for Justice works to strengthen the voice of the nonprofit and philanthropic sectors in important public policy debates by giving tax-exempt organizations a better understanding of the laws that govern their participation in the policy process. The purpose of this grant is to provide partial support to the organization’s new guide on how to assess and evaluate community organizing.

title: Resources for Evaluating Community Organizing
description: The Alliance for Justice works to strengthen the voice of the nonprofit and philanthropic sectors in important public policy debates by giving tax-exempt organizations a better understanding of the laws that govern their participation in the policy process. The purpose of this project is to develop a guide on assessing and evaluating community organizing. This grant increase will support that project and the organization’s effort to promote the guide’s usage.

description: The Alliance for Justice works to strengthen the voice of the nonprofit and philanthropic sectors in important public policy debates by giving tax-exempt organizations a better understanding of the laws that govern their participation in the policy process. title: Organizing for Education Improvement
description: Flint Area Congregations Together is a community organization affiliated with PICO National Network. The members of have identified public education in Flint as an important issue and are proposing a two-year project to investigate and conduct research and possible interventions to improve the schools.

title: Making Good on a Promise: Creating New Designs for Graduation and Postsecondary Success for Off-Track Youth
description: This grant will enable Jobs for the Future to partner with cities and districts in developing new back-on-track school designs that graduate and create post-secondary pathways for out-of-school youth. In the most recent phase of this initiative, the grantee assisted a cohort of cities, namely, Jacksonville, Las Vegas, Philadelphia, Portland, and New York, in identifying strategies that create education pathways for students who are not on track for graduation. Continued support will allow the grantee to implement and test college-connected school designs that build a bridge to post-secondary access and success and meet the needs of students who are at different points on the graduation continuum.

title: Making Good on a Promise: Creating New Designs for Graduation and Postsecondary Success for Off-Track Youth
description: This grant will enable Jobs for the Future to continue to partner with a peer network of six cities in developing a new Back-on-Track school design that provides a pathway to graduation and postsecondary education and credentials for off-track students. In the most recent phase of this initiative, Jobs for the Future worked with stakeholders in Boston, Chicago, Mobile, New York City, Portland, and Philadelphia to accelerate the development and testing of a college-connected school design that builds a bridge to postsecondary access and success and meets the needs of students who are at different points on the graduation continuum. Recommended support will allow the grantee to move to a fully operational Back-on-Track design ready for on-the-ground implementation in cities and states across the country.

title: Making Good on a Promise: Expanding Community Efforts to Raise Graduation Rates for Disconnected Youth
description: This grant will enable Jobs for the Future to assist local intermediaries in Philadelphia, Portland, and Las Vegas in disseminating their best practices and lessons learned in implementing reforms to address the issue of dropouts. Through this project, the grantee will use the documented successes and experiences of intermediaries in the targeted cities to expand the number of communities undertaking efforts to improve the educational outcomes for students off-track for graduation. In addition to developing the capacity of emerging communities in regions where the dropout problem is acute, the grantee will also assist in developing statewide policy strategies in addressing the dropout crisis.

title: REDD, Trading, and Governance
description: The outcome of the 2007 meeting of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change is to incorporate the first serious consideration of forest protection as a key element of reducing greenhouse gas emissions. Those discussions could offer the prospect of reducing greenhouse gas emissions that come about from deforestation as well as protecting biodiversity of forests and the livelihoods of forest-dependent communities. Current proposals, however, could give rise to perverse outcomes in which forest-dependent communities’ tenure rights are taken away and biodiversity is reduced. To assist in developing a stronger agreement, FERN will organize an invitation-only, strategy meeting of international climate negotiation, forest governance, property rights, and carbon trading experts.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to develop the potential of primary and secondary schools to be catalysts for increased openness, tolerance, inclusiveness, and participatory decisionmaking in local communities in Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia, and Serbia. To this end, the International Association “Interactive Open Schools” based in Tuzla, Bosnia-Herzegovina, will work with more than 25 schools in Tuzla, Osijek (Croatia), and Novi Sad (Serbia) to conduct training, create networking opportunities, and provide informational resources to teachers and school administrators as well as parents and students. The association is part of the broader community school movement in Central and Eastern Europe and Russia that during the past two years has developed comprehensive quality standards for open, community-based schools.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to develop the potential of primary and secondary schools to be catalysts for increased openness, tolerance, inclusiveness, and participatory decisionmaking in local communities in Bosnia-Herzegovina. To this end, the International Association “Interactive Open Schools”, based in Tuzla, Bosnia-Herzegovina, will work with more than 30 schools in Tuzla to conduct training, create networking opportunities, and provide informational resources to teachers and school administrators as well as parents and students. The grantee will also be a resource for schools and other nonprofits working in the field of education in Croatia, Serbia, and the wider Balkan region. In 2011-2012, the grantee provided educational and support services to school administrators, teachers, and school clubs and associations and disseminated information and resources regionally. The grantee is part of the broader community school movement in Central and Eastern Europe and Russia that, during the past two years, has developed comprehensive quality standards for open, community-based schools.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to develop the potential of primary and secondary schools to be catalysts for increased openness, tolerance, inclusiveness, and participatory decisionmaking in local communities in Bosnia-Herzegovina. To this end, the International Association “Interactive Open Schools” based in Tuzla, Bosnia-Herzegovina, will work intensively with more than 40 schools annually in Tuzla to conduct training, create networking opportunities, and provide informational resources to teachers and school administrators as well as parents and students. The grantee will also be a resource for schools and other nonprofits in Croatia, Serbia, and the wider Balkan region that are promoting community education and community school principles and practices. In 2013-2014, the grantee provided training and other support services to school administrators, teachers, and school clubs and associations and disseminated information and resources regionally. By the end of 2014, approximately 70 schools in the Tuzla region had participated in one or more of the grantee’s activities.

title: SafeHouse Shelter
description: The YWCA of Greater Flint has been serving the Flint and Genesee County community for 100 years with a mission of empowering women and eliminating racism. This grant will provide partial support for the grantee’s SafeHouse, the emergency shelter component of the Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault Services, which is the only resource program of its kind in Genesee County. SafeHouse offers 24-hour access to a secure shelter facility with security and trained staff on site at all times as well as access to all Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault Services. During the previous grant period, more than 500 individuals were sheltered and provided with services at SafeHouse.

title: SafeHouse Shelter
description: The YWCA of Greater Flint has been serving the Flint and Genesee County community for 100 years with a mission of empowering women and eliminating racism. The organization currently has one primary program area — Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault Services. This grant will provide partial support for the grantee’s SafeHouse, the emergency shelter component of the Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault Services, which is the only resource program of its kind in Genesee County. SafeHouse offers 24-hour access to a secure shelter facility with security and trained staff on site at all times as well as access to all Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault Services.

title: Funders Network on Trade and Globalization-Mapping of Global Financial Institutions
description: Community Partners was established in 1992 to meet a growing need for management and capacity-building services by civic and social entrepreneurs to strengthen their work. During this grant period, the Funders Network on Trade and Globalization project will assist funders to develop a shared strategic understanding of funding challenges and opportunities in critical areas, and promote strategic and collaborative grantmaking around a specific issue or initiative. The project will focus on developing tools and gathering data to assist funders in understanding key global economic institutions and the possible leverage points for influencing these institutions to make their functions more transparent, democratic, and accountable.

title: Belgrade NGO Partnership Capacity Building
grantee: Helsinki Committee for Human Rights in Serbia
description: The project goal is to strengthen the capacities of three leading nongovernmental organizations in Serbia whose work is fundamental to the country’s process of dealing with the recent past and ongoing European integration. The three organizations — the Helsinki Committee for Human Rights in Serbia, the Lawyers Committee for Human Rights, and Pescanik — are established human rights organizations that have track records of accomplishments achieved under very difficult external circumstances over the past decade in Serbia. With the grantee taking the lead, these groups will work with a nonprofit management consulting firm to design and implement a set of organizational and programmatic capacity-building activities. Additionally, the grantee and its partners will develop concrete, joint initiatives that draw on each other’s expertise and advance each organization’s mission. The grantee is based in Belgrade, Serbia.

title: Feasibility Study for the Adaptive Re-Use of Capitol Theatre
description: This grant will support a feasibility study for the adaptive re-use of the Capitol Theatre for the University of Michigan-Flint’s Music Department. The university’s music department does not have adequate rehearsal or dedicated performance space in the academic classroom building where they are located. The university’s music department, one of only a few programs in the area accredited by the National Association of Schools of Music, risks losing their accreditation if these facility issues are not addressed. This study will identify the rehearsal, performance, and department space needs of the university, estimate rehabilitation costs, evaluate the acoustics of the renovated theatre, and project operating expenses.

title: Police Segways
description: This grant will provide funds to the city of Flint to support a new policing program in downtown Flint. The Flint Police Department is utilizing Segway vehicles to increase and improve their response time and visibility on the streets of downtown Flint.

title: General Purposes
description: The Jeremiah Group is a multiracial, multi-issue organization in metropolitan New Orleans. The organization is affiliated with the Industrial Areas Foundation. The membership is comprised of faith-based and secular institutions in Orleans and Jefferson Parishes. The grantee’s goal is to develop a base of grassroots leaders who have the capacity to act in the interest of families and communities during neighborhood discussions and public deliberations.

description: The Institute for Wisconsin’ s Future is a research and action center established in 1994 to provide information on state issues and disseminate that information through community organizing and other community-based groups throughout Wisconsin. title: General Purposes
description: The Eastern Pennsylvania Organizing Project was founded in 1993 as an affiliate of PICO National Network. The organization works on issues related to public safety, housing and economic development, job creation and training, and improving public education. The grantee has participated in the Foundation’s six-year study of community-driven reform. This is a one-time, tie-off, general purpose grant.

title: Documentation of IAF Community Organizing in Wisconsin
description: A new institution-based community organizing initiative in Wisconsin presents itself as an excellent opportunity to document in “real time” a unique organizing initiative from its inception. The Center for Community Change will contract with a researcher/writer to document the experience of the leaders and organizers as this project develops. This documentation will be used to inform the field of community organizing, researchers on community organizing, and funders.

title: Washington Asset Building Coalition
description: This grant will support the efforts of Solid Ground Washington in promoting the development and sustainability of state and federal programs and policies that expand asset-building incentives and opportunities for low- and moderate-income families. Objectives of the project include: 1) engaging new constituencies to leverage sustained support for asset-development strategies; 2) informing the public and policymakers about how assets contribute to individual, family, and community economic well-being; and 3) strengthening the capacity of the asset coalition. The grantee is a Washington-based nonprofit dedicated to achieving a just and caring community, free from poverty, injustice, and neglect. This is one of eight grants aimed at building the capacity of state asset-building coalitions to effectively promote the development of state asset policies.

title: Arkansas Assets Coalition
description: This grant will enable the Southern Good Faith Fund to promote asset building among low- and moderate-income people in Arkansas and Mississippi by organizing a permanent, broad-based, asset-building coalition and by developing and advancing a comprehensive assets policy agenda. To accomplish these objectives, Mott funds will be used to engage new constituencies in state asset-building activities and advocate for policies that expand savings opportunities and incentives. The Southern Good Faith Fund is a nonprofit affiliate of Southern Bancorp, a $575 million Community Development Financial Institute and one of the nation’s largest rural development banks. This is one of eight grants aimed at building the capacity of state asset-building coalitions to effectively promote the development of state asset policies.

title: State Asset Coalition Learning Project
description: This grant provides support to the Center for Public Policy Priorities to enhance the reach and effectiveness of “RAISE Texas,” a statewide coalition formed in 2005 to expand access to asset-building products and financial education for low- and moderate-income Texans. Objectives for the three-year grant period are to: 1) expand the coalition’s influence by increasing and diversifying the membership; 2) advance statewide, asset-building policies, products, and programs; and 3) measure the impact and effectiveness of specific asset-building activities. This is one of eight grants aimed at building the capacity of state asset-building coalitions to effectively promote the development of state asset policies.

title: State Asset Coalition Learning Project
description: This grant will enable Community Action New Mexico to further its efforts to create a statewide asset-building coalition, thereby establishing a diverse and sustainable structure of partnerships focused on informing and advancing the state asset policies for low- and moderate-income households in New Mexico. Mott funding primarily will support the addition of a staff person to organize nonprofit organizations and other targeted stakeholders around a comprehensive asset-building framework. Located in Albuquerque, New Mexico, Community Action New Mexico is a statewide, nonprofit organization dedicated to strengthening the network of community action agencies working to end poverty in New Mexico. This is one of eight grants aimed at building the capacity of state asset-building coalitions to effectively promote the development of state asset policies.

title: Illinois Asset Building Group
grantee: Heartland Alliance for Human Needs & Human Rights
description: This grant to the Heartland Alliance for Human Needs & Human Rights will support the Illinois Asset Building Group to promote the development and sustainability of state and federal programs and policies that expand asset-building incentives and opportunities for low- and moderate-income families. Objectives of the project include: 1) engaging new constituencies to leverage sustained support for asset-development strategies; 2) informing the public and policymakers about how assets contribute to individual, family, and community economic well-being; and 3) testing innovative policies that bring asset-building opportunities to broad segments of the public. This is one of eight grants aimed at building the capacity of state asset-building coalitions to effectively promote the development of state asset policies.

description: The Isaiah Institute is a community organizing and community capacity building organization working in Louisiana and Mississippi. The grantee works primarily with small, unaffiliated black churches to teach the arts and disciplines of community organizing to pastors so that they can become more effective leaders and advocates for their communities.

title: Alternative Staffing Employment and Enterprise Outcomes
description: Alternative staffing organizations put the staffing services model to work for job candidates who face labor market barriers. They have a dual goal of providing job brokering for workers who face barriers to employment as well as delivering staffing services for customers who need workers. This renewal grant will provide funds for Goodwill Staffing Services to continue to participate in an evaluation of job placement outcomes for clients of four alternative staffing organizations, including a comparison with hard-to-employ clients of conventional staffing firms.

description: Alternative staffing organizations put the staffing services model to work for job candidates who face labor market barriers. This third and final renewal grant will provide funds for Goodwill Staffing Services to continue to participate in an evaluation of job placement outcomes for their clients. The grant will also be used to disseminate the results of the evaluation and pursue additional marketing activities to grow the organization’s customer base as it moves to being self-sufficient.

This renewal grant will provide funds for Emerge Community Development to continue to participate in an evaluation of job placement outcomes for clients of four alternative staffing organizations, including a comparison with hard-to-employ clients of conventional staffing firms.

title: New Day for Learning: Connecting and Supporting Business Partnerships
description: This grant will support the Institute for a Competitive Workforce in its efforts to connect “A New Day for Learning” demonstration sites and statewide afterschool networks to the business community. Through technical assistance, informational materials, conference calls, webinars, national conferences, and introductions to U.S. Chamber of Commerce members who are potential partners, the grantee seeks to engage corporate members in providing more students with a successful pathway between educational attainment and a prepared workforce. The Institute for a Competitive Workforce, an affiliate of the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, promotes high educational standards and effective workforce training systems so that they are aligned with each other and with today’s rigorous business demands.

title: Expanded Learning Time
description: This grant increase supports Citizen Schools in its efforts to educate stakeholders about the benefits and challenges of integrating afterschool education with the school day and how expanded learning time can inform educational restructuring. This grant increase will allow the grantee to produce a toolkit to be used as another resource that will help school-based and out-of-school time practitioners take full advantage of expanded learning time initiatives. The toolkit will supplement two reports that discuss issues accompanying expanded learning time and the research impact that expanded learning time has had in pilot schools.

title: Expanded Learning Time
description: This grant will support Citizen Schools in producing two reports that discuss issues accompanying expanded learning time and the research impact that expanded learning time has in their piloted schools. Citizen Schools is a national network of afterschool education programs for middle school students that complement classroom learning by engaging students in hands-on learning projects, and that works with schools to integrate afterschool education into a longer school day and year for all students. Specifically, this project will provide a research-based issue brief on the benefits and challenges of integrating afterschool education with the school day, and a policy paper targeted at district, state, and federal policymakers, other philanthropic organizations, and educational evaluators about the benefits of expanded learning time and how expanded learning time can inform educational restructuring.

title: Expanded Learning Time/New York City
description: This grant renewal will continue support to the After-School Corporation in evaluating the impact and implementation of its Expanded Learning Time/New York City initiative. This evaluation will assess the impact of the program in which students spend at least 30 percent more time on learning. The evaluation will assess four main areas: 1) actions of participating schools and community-based organization partners in increasing and enriching student learning time; 2) experiences of participating students; 3) effect on student performance; and 4) patterns of growth in educational performance due to expanded learning time. The After-School Corporation is a not-for-profit organization that has been helping school leaders and community organizations create high quality, school-based afterschool programs.

title: Expanded Learning Time/New York City
description: This grant will support the After-School Corporation in its Expanded Learning Time/New York City initiative. This project builds upon the accomplishments of community-based organizations and local education leaders by expanding student learning opportunities in a structured, systematic, and sustainable manner and will use a broad range of metrics to determine the benefits of providing children with the rich and varied expanded learning experiences they need to succeed in the 21st century. By demonstrating the feasibility as well as the benefits of this paradigm shift, the demonstration also seeks to influence the structure and content of state and national school reform efforts that seek to close the achievement gap through a longer school day and year. Specifically, this project will increase student learning time by at least 30 percent for at least half of the students at 11 New York City public schools. The After-School Corporation is a not-for-profit organization that has been helping school leaders and community organizations create high quality, school-based afterschool programs.

title: Incubator Without Walls/Microlending Program
description: This grant will capitalize a microlending program at Metro Community Development. Through a newly created community development financial institution, the grantee will implement a microlending program that provides microenterprise support to local businesses, with a special emphasis on downtown entities. Local entrepreneurs will receive technical assistance and microloans to assist new and existing businesses.

title: Incubator Without Walls/Microlending Program
description: This grant will provide microenterprise support to local downtown businesses through the development of a small business incubator and microlending program for downtown Flint. Local entrepreneurs will receive technical assistance and microloans to develop new and existing businesses. The program is one of several entrepreneurship programs administered by LAUNCH, formerly known as the Center for Entrepreneurship, a component of the University Outreach department at the University of Michigan-Flint.

title: Immigration Services
description: This renewal grant will provide support for the Immigration Services project operated by the American Arab Heritage Council. The goal of the grantee is to preserve Arabic heritage and support for Arab Americans in Genesee County. Over time, the programming has expanded to include diversity education, interfaith dialogues, and immigration services. With this support, the grantee will help immigrants navigate the American legal system and become acclimated to life in Genesee County by providing immigration forums, training volunteers to assist with immigration casework, and offering citizenship classes.

title: Immigration Services
description: Established in 1988, the American Arab Heritage Council serves the needs of Arab-Americans and other recent immigrants in Genesee County through programming such as diversity education, interfaith dialogues, and immigration services. This renewal grant will provide support to the grantee for the Immigration Services project. During the grant period, the project will continue to help immigrants navigate the American legal system and become acclimated to life in Genesee County by providing immigration forums, training volunteers to assist with immigration casework, and offering citizenship classes.

title: Immigration Services
description: Established in 1988, the American Arab Heritage Council serves the needs of Arab-Americans and other recent immigrants in Genesee County through programming such as diversity education, cultural programming, and immigration services. This renewal grant will provide support to the grantee for immigration and translation services. During the grant period, the project will continue to help immigrants from all backgrounds navigate the American legal system and become acclimated to life in Genesee County by providing immigration forums, training volunteers to assist with immigration casework, and offering citizenship classes.

title: Immigration Services
description: Established in 1988, the American Arab Heritage Council serves the needs of Arab-Americans and other recent immigrants in the Genesee County area through programming such as immigration services, diversity education, and cultural programming. During the grant period, the project will continue to help immigrants from all backgrounds navigate the American legal system and become acclimated to life in the United States by providing immigration forums and educational workshops, assisting with immigration casework, offering translation services, and leading citizenship classes.

description: Established in 1988, the Arab American Heritage Council serves the needs of Arab-Americans and other recent immigrants in the Genesee County area through programming such as immigration services, diversity education, and cultural events. Over time, programming has expanded to include diversity education, interfaith dialogues, and immigration services. With this support, the grantee will help immigrants navigate the American legal system and become acclimated to life in Genesee County by providing immigration forums, training volunteers to assist with immigration casework, and offering citizenship classes.

title: San Francisco New Day for Learning
description: This grant will support the San Francisco School Alliance to work in conjunction with the San Francisco Unified School District in implementing a citywide community school expansion effort. This project seeks to build upon the New Day for Learning Initiative to create a citywide model which aligns afterschool, student support services, and community schools through the development of: 1) a full service community school division within the district; and 2) a comprehensive approach to afterschool and expanded learning services that are available for students as part of a community school model. This project will provide policymakers and practitioners with tangible, visible examples of the value of strengthening the linkages between community schools, afterschool programs, and education.

title: San Francisco New Day for Learning
description: This grant will support the San Francisco School Alliance in implementing the San Francisco New Day for Learning initiative. This initiative seeks to create cohesive, protected pathways for students to learn morning through night, year-round, in settings throughout the city of San Francisco. The grantee will develop, pilot, communicate, and disseminate a concrete, leading-edge, out-of-the-box educational model for a New Day for Learning in San Francisco, and also realign policy, program, and funding levers necessary to institutionalize out-of-school time initiatives and replicate its New Day for Learning educational model. Collaborative partners include the San Francisco Unified School District; the San Francisco Department of Children, Youth and Their Families; San Francisco Communities of Opportunity; and the Office of the Mayor of San Francisco. As part of this initiative, San Francisco will be in a learning community of eight other district-community partnerships that includes Flint, Michigan. The project will provide policymakers and practitioners with tangible, visible examples of the value of strengthening the linkages between afterschool and education.

title: North Carolina Asset Building Policy Task Force
description: This grant will enable MDC to promote the development and sustainability of state and federal programs and policies that expand asset-building incentives and opportunities for low- and moderate-income families. Activities planned for the three-year grant period include: raising awareness of asset-building through effective messaging to the media, public, and policymakers; and engaging practitioners, parents, and youth to inform policy design and establish a wider advocacy network. MDC is a regional nonprofit organization based in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, whose mission is to help organizations and communities close the gaps that separate people from opportunity. This is one of eight grants aimed at building the capacity of state asset-building coalitions to effectively promote the development of state asset policies.

title: Maryland CASH Campaign
description: This grant provides support to the Job Opportunities Task Force for its Maryland CASH Campaign — a network of asset-building programs that promote economic security for Maryland workers. Objectives of the grant include: 1) engaging new constituencies in state asset-building activities; 2) advocating for policies that expand savings opportunities and incentives; and 3) expanding the availability of financial education and counseling. The Maryland CASH Campaign is the only program focused solely on providing asset building and other financial security opportunities to low-income Marylanders. This is one of eight grants aimed at building the capacity of state asset-building coalitions to effectively promote the development of state asset policies.

title: Medical School Feasibility Study
description: This grant will provide support to the Hurley Foundation, and its supported organization the Hurley Medical Center, for a feasibility study for developing a medical school in Flint, Michigan. Founded in 1908, Hurley Medical Center is a 443-bed, public, nonprofit, teaching medical center affiliated with academic institutions such as Michigan State University, the University of Michigan, Mott Community College, and Henry Ford Health System. With more than 35,000 healthcare sector jobs in Genesee County, the sector is poised to be an economic driver for the region. This planning grant will help support a potential source for jobs and economic growth in Flint.

title: International Centre of Excellence for Community Schools
description: The program goal is to develop the International Centre of Excellence for Community Schools as a focal point for knowledge exchange among practitioners from around the world. Based in the United Kingdom and with broad experience in promoting the community school agenda, ContinYou will oversee the ongoing development and formal registration of the centre. It will work to raise the profile of community schools among educational authorities, peer organizations and networks, and funders around the world. It will also continue to develop and deliver a range of training and consulting services to help build the capacity of community school support organizations. During 2009-2011, the grantee mapped the presence of community schools in over 65 countries and identified an informal taxonomy of community schools to assist in better targeting support. Established in 2003, ContinYou offers supplementary learning opportunities in the United Kingdom to people who have gained the least from formal education and training.

title: General Purposes
grantee: International Centre of Excellence for Community Schools
description: The program goal is to promote the development of community schools around the world. The International Centre of Excellence for Community Schools will work to raise the profile of community schools among educational authorities, peer organizations and networks, and funders internationally. It will also continue to develop and deliver a range of training and consulting services to help build the capacity of community school support organizations. From inception until 2012, the grantee provided a cycle of Webinars on topical issues in community education. It also led a series of training workshops for international partners on issues including social inclusion and quality standards. It mapped community schools in over 65 countries and identified an informal taxonomy of these schools to assist in better targeting support. Formally registered in 2013, the International Centre of Excellence for Community Schools began as a project of the former British educational charity ContinYou. It seeks to draw on and disseminate the growing and diverse experiences of community schools practice internationally.

title: General Purposes
grantee: International Centre of Excellence for Community Schools
description: The program goal is to promote the development of community schools around the world. The International Centre of Excellence for Community Schools will raise the profile of community schools among educational authorities, peer organizations and networks, and funders internationally. The grantee will continue to develop and deliver a range of capacity building services to community school support organizations, with a growing focus on partners in Africa. In 2013, the grantee grew its list of regular contacts to over 4,000 schools, agencies, and support organizations worldwide, and completed a detailed survey on community school needs and opportunities in Africa. The grantee organized four Webinars on issues including partnership, leadership, and social inclusion, drawing heavily on the experience of partners in Central and Eastern Europe. Formally registered in 2013, the grantee began as a project of the British educational charity ContinYou, and seeks to draw on and disseminate the growing experiences of community schools practice internationally.

title: General Purposes
grantee: International Centre of Excellence for Community Schools
description: The program goal is to promote the development of community schools around the world. The International Centre of Excellence for Community Schools will raise the profile of community schools among educational authorities, peer organizations and networks, and funders internationally. It will continue to develop and deliver a range of capacity building services and resources to community school support organizations, with a growing focus on partners in Africa. In 2014-2015, the grantee helped introduce quality standards to a network of over 500 community schools in Southern Africa while also helping launch a community schools development program in Bulgaria. It also created a specialized training program on entrepreneurship for community schools. Formally registered in 2013, the International Centre of Excellence for Community Schools began as a project of the British educational charity ContinYou.

title: General Purposes
grantee: International Centre of Excellence for Community Schools
description: The program goal is to promote the development of community schools around the world. The International Centre of Excellence for Community Schools will raise the profile of community schools among educational authorities, peer organizations and networks, and funders internationally. It will continue to develop and deliver a range of capacity-building services and resources to community school support organizations, with a growing focus on partners in Africa. In 2016-2017, the grantee helped introduce quality standards to a network of schools in seven countries of Southern Africa while also initiating partnerships in a further eight countries on the continent. The grantee also created a specialized training program on entrepreneurship for community schools and delivered over 30 training events around the world. Formally registered in 2013, the grantee began as a project of the British educational charity “ContinYou.” It seeks to draw on and disseminate the growing experiences of community schools practice internationally.

title: International Centre of Excellence for Community Schools
description: The program goal is to establish the International Centre of Excellence for Community Schools in Europe as a focal point for knowledge exchange among practitioners from around the world. Based in the United Kingdom and with broad experience in promoting the community schools agenda, ContinYou will support the establishment of the centre during the grant period. Program activities will include establishing governance structures and procedures, hiring key staff, and elaborating an initial development strategy. The aim of the centre will be to provide a range of consulting and other support services to its anticipated membership and more broadly to community educators. It will also provide a forum for exchange of experience and methodological materials through planned publications, conferences, and specialized workshops. Established in 2003, ContinYou offers learning opportunities in the United Kingdom to people who have gained the least from formal education and training.

title: Presidential Transition Project of the National State Attorneys General Program
grantee: Columbia University in the City of New York
description: This grant provides partial support to Columbia University in the City of New York for the law school’s Presidential Transition Project of the National State Attorneys General Program. The Mott Foundation has supported the Charities Law Project of this program since 2006. This summer, the president of the National Association of Attorneys General requested that the program design and implement a presidential transition project through which the next presidential administration can work effectively with state attorneys general. Program consultants include several former state attorneys general and key staff of state attorneys general offices. Using their credibility and expertise, the program consultants will facilitate dialogues between state attorneys general and both candidates’ transition teams. After the election, program consultants will continue to assist attorneys general, as well as the Office of Presidential Transition, various departments and federal agencies, and issue advocates, in understanding each others’ priorities and concerns, including issues pertaining to nonprofit regulation and oversight.

title: Providence New Day for Learning
description: This grant will support the Providence After School Alliance to work in conjunction with the Providence Public School District to support and evaluate a citywide afterschool and expanded learning initiative. This project seeks to build upon the New Day for Learning initiative which was focused on a citywide model integrating afterschool, student support services, and community schools. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) implement a joint assessment and evaluation plan to document best practices and policies on an integrated citywide model; and 2) disseminate best practices to afterschool and expanded learning stakeholders. This project will provide policymakers and practitioners with tangible, visible examples of the value of strengthening the linkages between community schools, afterschool programs, and education.

title: Providence New Day for Learning
description: This grant will support the Providence After School Alliance in implementing the Providence New Day for Learning initiative. This initiative seeks to launch a New Day for Learning that spans grades 6-12 and closely links the school day with the vast network of afterschool supports available in the community to create a seamless day for students that redefines how, where, and when students learn. A diverse array of partners will initiate cultural and institutional change that creates a more interlinked system to support Providence, Rhode Island’s youth and to change the current culture of independent entities operating in fragmented ways. As part of this initiative, Providence will be in a learning community of eight other district-community partnerships that includes Flint, Michigan. The project will provide policymakers and practitioners with tangible, visible examples of the value of strengthening the linkages between afterschool and education.

title: Rural Microenterprise Development
description: This grant will provide partial support to the Center for Rural Affairs for its Rural Microenterprise Development project, which will work to ensure the long-term existence, expansion, proper execution, and awareness of the United States Department of Agriculture’s Rural Microentrepreneur Assistance Program, which was established by the 2008 Farm Bill. The grantee will provide training, technical assistance, and small loans to rural small business owners. During the course of the grant period, the grantee will conduct outreach work, engage grassroots leaders as to the potential of microenterprise, submit formal comments on how to improve proposed regulations, and assist rural small businesses to develop strong proposals for funding.

title: Rural Microenterprise Development
description: The Center for Rural Affairs was established in 1973 by rural Nebraskans concerned about the loss of economic opportunities in their communities and has since grown to be a nationally recognized policy analysis, advocacy, and grassroots outreach organization. This grant will provide partial support to the grantee for its Rural Microenterprise Development project, which will work to ensure the long-term existence and expansion of the United States Department of Agriculture’s Rural Microentrepreneur Assistance Program, established by the 2008 Farm Bill to provide training, technical assistance, and small loans to rural small business owners. During the grant period, the grantee will conduct advocacy and outreach work, engage grassroots leaders as to the potential of microenterprise, submit formal comments on how to improve proposed regulations, and assist rural small businesses to develop strong proposals for funding.

During the grant period, the grantee will conduct advocacy and outreach work, engage grassroots leaders as to the potential of microenterprise, and assist rural small businesses to develop strong proposals for funding.

title: Freight and Connectivity Study for Genesee County
description: This grant to the Genesee County Metropolitan Planning Commission will provide a portion of the required local matching funds to conduct a study of the major transportation corridors in Flint and Genesee County. These highways are major shipping routes between the United States and Canada, as well as the transportation backbone that connects Flint to other Michigan cities and states. For years, the I-75/US-23 interchange has been identified as a transportation “choke point,” hindering the movement of freight in, out, and through Genesee County. The study will identify the best solutions for improving connectivity between these major north/south and east/west corridors, which will aid local traffic movement and foster economic development efforts.

title: Program for Automotive Labor and Education
description: Now that the automotive market has stabilized, automakers and suppliers have regained their focus on future human resource needs. The products themselves and the processes used to make them are changing at a rapid pace, which means it is difficult for educators and workforce development professionals to stay abreast of the technological changes and to understand and incorporate the impact of those changes on skill needs, both for new graduates and incumbent workers alike. The grant renewal of the Program for Automotive Labor and Education uniquely positions the Center for Automotive Research to bridge this gap through its industry-driven, research-based approach to supporting a network of corporate, labor, education, training, workforce development, and government leaders.

title: Program for Automotive Labor and Education
description: This grant will provide support to the Center for Automotive Research for the development of the Program for Automotive Labor and Education. The grantee has served the automotive industry and the communities it operates in for more than 25 years with unbiased research and multidisciplined expertise. The Program for Automotive Labor and Education is an industry-driven, research-based initiative that will conduct research on the size of the automotive workforce and timing of any potential new hiring, as well as provide a forecast of skill needs and a review of best practice programs and curricula. The program will also provide research assistance to the National Employment Law Project to help it certify automaker and supplier locations for Trade Adjustment Assistance.

title: Community Jam Against Violence
description: This grant will support the production costs for LA’s BEST 16th Annual Community Jam Against Violence. This event brings children, families, and community together to share students’ thoughts and feelings on decrying the violence in their lives using different artistic mediums. The event will feature celebrities and is supported by various major companies. All proceeds from the event will support the work of the grantee.

title: Federal Microenterprise Policy Expansion Project
description: This grant to the Corporation for Enterprise Development will allow it to endorse federal policies that increase low-income people’s access to credit and technical assistance to start and operate small businesses. Some of the activities to be pursued during the grant period include convening the Microenterprise Anti-Poverty Policy Consortium, a multiagency effort to advance policy initiatives in support of microenterprise; promoting microenterprise as an eligible economic activity under the Temporary Assistance for Needy Families program; including small business development as an eligible use for retirement savings accounts; expanding the existing infrastructure of community-based nonprofits that support entrepreneurs; and advocating for increased federal investment in microenterprise.

title: Federal Microenterprise Policy Expansion Project
description: This grant will allow the Corporation for Enterprise Development to advocate for federal policies that increase low-income people’s access to credit and technical assistance to start and operate small businesses. Some of the activities to be pursued during the grant period include convening the Microenterprise Anti-Poverty Policy Consortium, a multiagency effort to inform public policy of the poverty reducing impacts of microenterprise; promoting microenterprise as an eligible economic activity under the Temporary Assistance for Needy Families program; and expanding federal investment in microenterprise programs through the Small Business Administration’s business assistance and lending program.

title: Federal Microenterprise Policy Expansion Project
description: The Corporation for Enterprise Development will provide technical assistance and work in partnership with Small Business Administration officials and program officers to ensure that low-income business owners, including new entrepreneurs, have access to training and financing. It will work with the Small Business Administration to enhance various programs’ capacity to reach low-income business owners and new entrepreneurs in meaningful ways. It will educate legislators on microenterprise development services and the value of investing federal funding to support microentrepreneurs.

title: Federal Microenterprise Policy Expansion Project
description: The goal of the Corporation for Enterprise Development’s Federal Microenterprise Policy Expansion Project is to advocate for federal policies that increase low-income people’s access to credit and technical assistance to start and operate small businesses. Some of the activities to be pursued during the grant period include convening the Microenterprise Anti-Poverty Policy Consortium, a multiagency effort to advance policy initiatives in support of microenterprise; promoting microenterprise as an eligible economic activity under the Temporary Assistance for Needy Families program; promoting small business development as an eligible use for retirement savings accounts; expanding the existing infrastructure of community-based nonprofits that support entrepreneurs; and preserving and expanding federal investment in microenterprise through the Small Business Administration’s Business Assistance and Lending program.

title: General Purposes
description: The goal of Community Foundation Slagalica is to stimulate greater public participation in decisionmaking and community building in five counties in eastern Croatia. During the grant period, the grantee will provide grants, organize training, raise public awareness about civic responsibility, and promote local philanthropy. The foundation will attract individual and corporate donors and design grantmaking programs that target youth and marginalized groups in local communities. During 2009-2010, the foundation worked with the National Foundation for Civil Society Development to design and implement grantmaking programs for local civic initiatives in Eastern Slavonia, managed two donor-advised funds, and launched a successful fundraising campaign that attracted individual donations in support of community projects. The foundation is based in Osijek and works in five counties in eastern Croatia.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to stimulate greater public participation in decisionmaking and community building in five counties in eastern Croatia. During the grant period, the Community Foundation Slagalica will provide grants, organize training, raise public awareness about civic responsibility, and promote local philanthropy. The grantee will attract individual and corporate donors and design grantmaking programs that target youth and marginalized groups in local communities. Since its establishment in 2008, the grantee has awarded more than 140 grants totaling approximately $240,000 across 90 local communities in eastern Croatia. During 2011-2012, the first entirely locally funded grant program was established in Osijek and made 16 grants totaling approximately $22,000. The grantee also managed two donor-advised funds and launched an Osijek-based “philanthropists club.” The foundation is based in Osijek and works in five counties in eastern Croatia.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to stimulate greater public participation in decisionmaking and community building in five counties in eastern Croatia. During the grant period, the Community Foundation Slagalica will provide grants, organize training, raise public awareness about civic responsibility, and promote local philanthropy. The grantee will attract individual and corporate donors and design grantmaking programs that target youth and marginalized groups in local communities. Since its establishment in 2008, the grantee has awarded more than 200 grants totaling approximately $535,000 across 90 local communities in eastern Croatia. During 2013-2014, the grantee developed and expanded approaches to strengthening local philanthropy, including managing donor-advised funds, increasing membership in its Philanthropists’ Club, educating students about philanthropy and promoting philanthropy in schools, and soliciting donations from the public. The grantee is based in Osijek and works in five counties in eastern Croatia.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to stimulate greater public participation in decisionmaking and community building in five counties in eastern Croatia. During the grant period, the Community Foundation Slagalica will provide grants, organize training, raise public awareness about civic responsibility, and promote local philanthropy. The grantee will attract individual and corporate donors and design grantmaking programs that target youth and marginalized groups in local communities. During 2015–2016, the grantee awarded over 60 grants in local communities in eastern Croatia. The grantee also assisted various government ministries to administer and monitor more than 50 grants; promoted philanthropy by working in 13 schools through lectures, exhibitions, and mentoring; organized an annual award ceremony recognizing local, outstanding philanthropic activities; and organized local events as part of the national Philanthropy Week campaign. The grantee is based in Osijek and works in five counties in eastern Croatia.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to stimulate greater public participation in decision making and community building in five counties in eastern Croatia. During the grant period, the Community Foundation Slagalica will provide grants, organize training, raise public awareness about civic responsibility, and carry out advocacy initiatives. The foundation was established in 2007 by two nongovernmental organizations in eastern Croatia, both of which are long-term Mott grantees. Building on the extensive experience of these two organizations, the foundation will help local communities implement more participatory decision-making processes, stimulate civic involvement in improving community life, and mobilize local resources for local projects and activities. The foundation is based in Osijek and works in five counties in eastern Croatia.

title: Transportation for America: Making the Michigan Connection
description: Smart Growth America is a national organization promoting smart growth policies and practices, including walkable neighborhoods and high quality transit services. With prior Mott support, the grantee has helped partner organizations in Michigan engage in related transportation policy discussions at the federal level and implement such policies and programs at the state and local levels. This grant increase, and associated grant period extension, will allow the grantee to develop a strategic plan for its future activities in Michigan, while continuing its outreach and technical assistance.

title: Transportation for America: Making the Michigan Connection
description: Established in 2000, Smart Growth America is a nationwide network of organizations working to protect natural areas and environmental health, revitalize communities, and increase transportation and housing choices. Its recent work includes initiation of Transportation for America, an effort that seeks to inform federal transportation policy discussions through engaging state and local organizations. With this grant, Smart Growth America will connect Michigan organizations to the federal transportation discussions as part of the Transportation for America activity. This work will help ensure that the state’s interests and needs are addressed at the federal level and that state groups are adequately prepared for effective implementation of the emerging transportation policies.

title: Collaborative for Educational Change
description: Boston organizing groups have joined with funders to create the Collaborative for Educational Change. Led by Hyde Square Task Force, the purpose of the project is to unite the forces and interests of all the members to work on education reform. A previous grant supported the planning process and initial work of the collaborative. The purpose of this grant is to support the efforts of the next phase, including the development of a shared work plan, shared decisionmaking system, and communications framework.

title: Collaborative for Educational Change
description: Boston organizing groups have joined with funders to create the Collaborative for Educational Change. Led by Hyde Square Task Force, the purpose of the program is to unite the forces and interests of all the collaborative’s members to work on education reform. Even as the collaborative has worked to develop a shared work plan and decisionmaking system, training in education organizing has continued to be an important aspect of the group’s work. This grant increase supports training and technical assistance to several youth organizing groups in Michigan, including Neutral Zone, Generation of Promise, ACCESS Youth Team, Youthville, Affirmations, Youth Voice, Seaholm High School Leadership and Service, and Michigan Roundtable for Diversity and Inclusion-Youth Leadership Team.

title: Collaborative for Educational Change
description: Boston organizing groups have joined with funders to create the Collaborative for Educational Change. Led by Hyde Square Task Force, the purpose of the program is to unite the forces and interests of all the members to work effectively on education reform. The purpose of this grant is to support the planning process and initial work of the collaborative as the members craft agreements to establish the structure (including leadership, decisionmaking, and funding); identify issues; develop working groups to conduct research; identify action strategies; provide joint training for local youth, parents, and organizers; and connect with an emerging national network of organizing groups, and particularly youth organizing groups focused on education improvement.

title: Collaborative for Education Organizing
grantee: Community Foundation for the National Capital Region
description: The Community Foundation for the National Capital Region led an effort to form the Collaborative for Education Organizing, a partnership of funders and community-based organizations working together to improve public education in Washington, D.C. The program is focused on increasing the college-ready graduation rate in Washington, D.C.’s public schools. This grant will provide partial support to the work of the collaborative.

title: Collaborative for Education Organizing
grantee: Community Foundation for the National Capital Region
description: The Community Foundation for the National Capital Region led an effort to form the Collaborative for Education Organizing, a partnership of funders and community-based organizations working together to improve public education in Washington, D.C. The program is focused on increasing the college-ready graduation rate in Washington, D.C.’s public schools. This grant will provide partial support for the work of the program.

This collaborative is focused on increasing the college-ready graduation rate in Washington, D.C.’s public schools. This grant increase will provide partial funding for a series of convenings aimed at bringing regional leaders together to support community engagement strategies.

grantee: Community Foundation for the National Capital Region
description: The Community Foundation for the National Capital Region led an effort to form the Collaborative for Education Organizing, a partnership of funders and community-based organizations working together to improve public education in Washington, D.C. The Collaborative for Education Organizing is focused on increasing the college-ready graduation rate in Washington, D.C.’s public schools. This grant will provide partial support for the work of the collaborative.
