grantee: Community Foundation for the National Capital Region
description: The Community Foundation for the National Capital Region led an effort to form the Collaborative for Education Organizing, a partnership of funders and community-based organizations working together to improve public education in Washington, D.C. The program is focused on increasing the college-ready graduation rate. This grant will provide partial support for the work of the collaborative.

title: Youth Development Institute: Developing Community-Based Career and Technical Education Strategies for Youth Who Have Dropped out of School
description: This grant will enable the Youth Development Institute, a program of the Tides Center, to continue to develop and model a vocational pathway into work and further education for students who have dropped out of school with low academic levels. The institute is New York-based and partners with community-based organizations, schools, and colleges to create programs that help young people transition into adulthood. Continued support will enable the institute to further identify and assess promising academic and career approaches for strengthening the education and career pathways for youth who have dropped out of school and/or are at risk of doing so.

title: Youth Development Institute: Developing Community-Based Career and Technical Education Strategies for Youth Who Have Dropped out of School
description: This grant will enable the Youth Development Institute, a program of the Tides Center, to continue to develop a community-based career and technical education pathway into work and further education for students who have dropped out of school with low academic skill levels. The Youth Development Institute is a New York-based program that partners with community-based organizations, schools, and colleges to create programs that help young people transition into adulthood. The grantee will create more efficient technical assistance strategies that are responsive to partnering program sites’ needs, refine the educational curricula, and further develop the work-related components of the community-based career and technical education pathway model.

title: Youth Development Institute: Developing Community-Based Career and Technical Education Strategies for Youth Who Have Dropped out of School
description: This grant will enable the Youth Development Institute, a program of the Tides Center, to develop and pilot a vocational pathway into work and further education for students who have dropped out of school with low academic levels. The Youth Development Institute is a New York-based entity that partners with community-based organizations, schools, colleges, and others to create programs that help young people transition into adulthood. Recommended support will enable the institute to undertake a research-focused effort that begins to lay the groundwork for the expansion of education and employment pathways where low-skilled youth can meet specific academic and credential requirements via participation in courses focused on workforce preparedness and post-secondary access.

title: Building Capacity for New Day for Learning Communities
description: This grant will support the Annenberg Institute for School Reform at Brown University to continue to provide technical assistance through the final phase of the New Day for Learning initiative in Providence, Rhode Island. This project will ensure that the last phase of the New Day for Learning initiative is successful by: 1) providing technical assistance to the Mayor’s Children and Youth Cabinet to sustain the New Day for Learning work beyond the grant period; 2) working with the New Day for Learning evaluator to summarize best practices; and 3) developing recommendations to inform national and state afterschool models.

title: Building Capacity for New Day for Learning Communities
description: This grant will support the Annenberg Institute for School Reform at Brown University to assist communities in the implementation of the recommendations from the 2007 “A New Day for Learning” report. This grant will provide technical assistance in selected communities to advance school and community redesign efforts that embody “A New Day for Learning” elements, which include expanding the definition of student success, using research-based knowledge about how students learn best, fostering collaboration across all sectors, integrating various learning approaches and places, and providing new opportunities for leadership and professional development. To accomplish these objectives, the project will support site-based efforts by helping teams set priorities, identify learning and developmental needs, and design common or site-tailored products to address those learning needs.

title: Capacity-Building Technical Assistance
description: Since 2003, the National Conference of State Legislatures has been building an infrastructure to work with state lawmakers and their staff on developing comprehensive policy approaches to help families achieve economic success. A principal part of this work has been familiarizing policymakers with asset-building concepts. This grant will enable the conference to help inform state lawmakers about asset-building policy frameworks and strategies, and help our state asset coalition grantees increase their understanding of how to effectively work with state legislatures. To this end, the grantee will produce a series of informational materials for its members, including legislative briefs, Webinars, and podcasts, and provide technical assistance to Mott’s asset-building grantees. The National Conference of State Legislatures is the constituent body of legislators from all 50 states. The organization has a staff of approximately 175 in two locations — Denver and Washington, DC.

title: Financial Services Industry Survey
description: This recommendation will enable the Center for Financial Services Innovations to organize a research effort that identifies the key trends facing the financial services industry over the next seven to ten years, and interprets those trends for stakeholders in the asset-building field. The proposed study will provide the asset-building field the context it needs to be proactive in developing future directions that pave the way for saving, asset building, and financial prosperity for low- and moderate-income families. The grantee was founded in 2004 as a nonprofit affiliate of Chicago-based ShoreBank Corporation.

title: AutoSave Demonstration
description: Federal and state governments currently support a variety of programs and policies to encourage saving. However, most of these programs are focused on long-term goals, with consequent restrictions on use and penalties for withdrawals other than those tied to a specific goal. Currently, no systematic savings program exists to intentionally encourage savings that are unrestricted and not oriented toward specific long-term goals, such as emergency or contingency savings. MDRC is requesting support to test the AutoSave concept, a savings strategy that uses the workplace as the portal to initiate and sustain the accumulation of unrestricted savings for emergencies and/or short-term uses. Mott funds will enable the grantee to continue field testing this new savings intervention in at least five diverse workplace settings. The primary deliverable from this pilot phase will be a memorandum summarizing the early operational lessons, including employer and employee take-up and attitudes toward savings and the AutoSave concept. Established in 1974, MDRC is a nonprofit research institute headquartered in New York City.

The primary deliverable from this pilot phase will be a memorandum summarizing the early operational lessons, including employer and employee participation and attitudes toward savings and the AutoSave concept. Established in 1974, MDRC is a nonprofit research institute headquartered in New York City.

title: Alternative Staffing Project
grantee: Catholic Charities Archdiocese of New Orleans
description: Catholic Charities Archdiocese of New Orleans is one of three organizations in Louisiana’s Gulf Coast region that has worked over the past three years to launch an alternative staffing program. Alternative staffing organizations, which are temporary staffing firms owned and operated by community-based agencies, have the potential to bridge the gap between the needs of employers and employees. This type of employment effort will help an area that is still recovering from the aftereffects of Hurricanes Katrina and Rita. With this renewal grant, the grantee will continue to implement and operate an alternative staffing project.

title: Alternative Staffing Project
grantee: Catholic Charities Archdiocese of New Orleans
description: This grant provides support for a nonprofit staffing agency operated by the Catholic Charities Archdiocese of New Orleans. The agency, which was developed as part of Mott’s Alternative Staffing Demonstration project, helps individuals with multiple barriers to employment gain employment and valuable work experience. This program will help a region that is still rebuilding its workforce as a result of Hurricanes Katrina and Rita. This renewal grant will support the operations of the program as it moves toward self-sufficiency.

title: Alternative Staffing Project
grantee: Catholic Charities Archdiocese of New Orleans
description: Years after hurricanes Katrina and Rita devastated Louisiana’s Gulf Coast, the region is still trying to recover from the disaster. Despite a low unemployment rate, there are approximately 750,000 people who are employable but unable to find work. Alternative staffing organizations, which are temporary staffing firms owned and operated by community-based agencies, have the potential to bridge the gap between the needs of employers and employees. This grant will support the continued development of Catholic Charities Archdiocese of New Orleans, one of three alternative staffing organizations created to serve people with barriers to employment in the south Louisiana area.

title: Alternative Staffing Project
description: UpLIFTD is one of three organizations in Louisiana’s Gulf Coast region that has worked over the past three years to launch an alternative staffing program. Alternative staffing organizations, which are temporary staffing firms owned and operated by community-based agencies, have the potential to bridge the gap between the needs of employers and employees. This type of employment effort will help an area that is still recovering from the aftereffects of Hurricanes Katrina and Rita. With this renewal grant, the grantee will continue to implement and operate an alternative staffing project.

title: Alternative Staffing Project
description: Alternative staffing organizations put the staffing services model to work for job candidates who face labor market barriers. They have a dual goal of providing job brokering for workers who face barriers to employment, as well as delivering staffing services for customers who need workers. This renewal grant will provide funds for Options for Independence to continue to participate in an evaluation of job placement outcomes for clients of four alternative staffing organizations, including a comparison with hard-to-employ clients of conventional staffing firms.

title: Alternative Staffing Project
description: Alternative staffing organizations put the staffing services model to work for job candidates who face labor market barriers. This renewal grant will provide funds for Options for Independence to complete participation in a three-year evaluation of job placement outcomes for the clients of four alternative staffing organizations, including a comparison with hard-to-employ clients of conventional staffing firms.

title: Alternative Staffing Project
description: Years after hurricanes Katrina and Rita devastated Louisiana’s Gulf Coast, the region is still trying to recover from the disaster. Despite a low unemployment rate, there are approximately 750,000 people who are employable but unable to find work. Alternative staffing organizations, which are temporary staffing firms owned and operated by community-based agencies, have the potential to bridge the gap between the needs of employers and employees. This grant will support the continued development of Options for Independence, one of three alternative staffing organizations created to serve people with barriers to employment in the south Louisiana area.

title: Cross-Network Professional Development
grantee: Northwest Bronx Community and Clergy Coalition
description: Northwest Bronx Community and Clergy Coalition is a 30-year-old, broad-based community organization. The organization builds power through relational organizing and issue campaigns that recruit and train individuals, as well as institutional members, to win concrete victories that improve the lives of the residents of the Northwest Bronx. Elsewhere in New York, other community organizations are also building influence to achieve the aspirations of local residents. The purpose of this grant is to provide support for a one-year planning effort to bring together staff and key leaders from more than a dozen organizations for shared training, professional development, and research in order to explore the possibility of developing a network of community organizations that can work in a coordinated fashion.

title: Capacity Building
description: For the past 32 years, the Crim Fitness Foundation has contributed to the physical and economic health of the community. With a signature 10-mile road race, an array of health and physical fitness programs in local schools, and the largest adult training program in the country, the Crim Fitness Foundation is an important contributor to efforts to improve the quality of life in Genesee County. With this grant, the organization will improve and strengthen local efforts and expand services to other Michigan communities.

title: Capacity Building
description: For the past 32 years, the Crim Fitness Foundation has contributed to the physical and economic health of the community. With a signature 10-mile road race, an array of health and physical fitness programs in local schools, and the largest adult training program in the country, the grantee is an important contributor to efforts to improve the quality of life in Genesee County. With this grant, the grantee will improve and strengthen local efforts, and will expand services to other Michigan communities.
