description: For the past 37 years, the Crim Fitness Foundation has contributed to the physical and economic health of the community. With a signature 10-mile road race, an array of health and physical fitness programs in local schools, and the largest adult training program in the country, the grantee is an important contributor to efforts to improve the quality of life in Genesee County. With this grant, the grantee will improve and strengthen local efforts and expand services to other Michigan communities.

title: Capacity Building
description: For the past 37 years, the Crim Fitness Foundation has contributed to the physical and economic health of the community. With a signature 10-mile road race, an array of health and physical fitness programs in local schools, and the largest adult training program in the country, the Crim Fitness Foundation is an important contributor to efforts to improve the quality of health and wellness in Genesee County. With this grant, the grantee will continue to improve and strengthen local efforts, and will expand services to other Michigan communities.

title: Capacity Building
description: The Crim Festival of Races is one of the country’s premier road running events. As the flagship event, the 10-mile race attracts top American and international distance runners. Additionally, the Crim Fitness Foundation provides race sponsorship for a half-marathon, and the organization provides annual health and fitness services to approximately 10,000 elementary school students in Genesee County. This grant will support enhancements to both the elite athlete program as well as the CrimFit Youth Program.

title: Community Foundation Development Program
description: The program goal is to support the community foundation movement in Romania. To this end, the Association for Community Relations, in partnership with the Romanian Environmental Partnership Foundation and PACT – Partnership for Community Action and Transformation, both Mott grantees, will provide funding and technical assistance to strengthen the two newly established community foundations in Cluj-Napoca and Odorheiu Secuiesc. In addition, the grantee will initiate and support the development of new community foundations in at least four locations in the next two years. The grantee’s activities will include promoting the community foundation concept, assisting local groups during the registration process, and providing funding and technical assistance to the newly established community foundations. During the previous two years, the grantee helped to establish two new community foundations and supported five initiative groups to explore community foundation development. Also, the grantee supported the development of local philanthropy and resource mobilization and provided support to two existing Romanian community foundations. The grantee is based in Cluj-Napoca.

title: Community Foundation Development Program
description: The program goal is to support the community foundation movement in Romania. To this end, the Association for Community Relations, in partnership with the Romanian Environmental Partnership Foundation and the Romanian Federation of Community Foundations, will provide funding and technical assistance to strengthen the 11 existing community foundations in Romania. In addition, the grantee will initiate and support the development of new community foundations in at least three locations in the next two years. The grantee’s activities will include promoting the community foundation concept, assisting local groups during the registration process, and providing funding and technical assistance to the newly established community foundations. During the previous two years, the grantee helped to establish four new community foundations and supported five initiative groups to explore community foundation development. Also, the grantee supported the development of local philanthropy and resource mobilization. The grantee is based in Cluj-Napoca.

title: Community Foundation Development Program
description: The program goal is to support the community foundation movement in Romania. To this end, the Association for Community Relations, in partnership with the Romanian Federation of Community Foundations, will provide funding and technical assistance to strengthen the 12 existing community foundations in Romania. In addition, the grantee will initiate and support the development of new community foundations in at least four locations over the next two years. The grantee’s activities will include promoting the community foundation concept, assisting local groups during the registration process, and providing funding and technical assistance to the newly established community foundations. During the previous two years, the grantee helped to establish one new community foundation and supported eight initiative groups to explore community foundation development. Also, the grantee supported the development of local philanthropy and individual giving. The grantee is based in Cluj-Napoca.

title: Community Foundation Development Program
description: The program goal is to support the community foundation movement in Romania. To this end, Association for Community Relations, in partnership with the Romanian Federation of Community Foundations, will provide funding and technical assistance to strengthen the 16 existing community foundations in Romania. In addition, the grantee will initiate and support the development of new community foundations in at least four locations over the next three years by promoting the community foundation concept, assisting local groups during the registration process, and providing funding and technical assistance to the newly established community foundations. The grantee will also create a pool of local and international experts and practitioners to work with Romanian community foundations on issues of effectiveness and sustainability and will strengthen the links between the Romanian and European community foundations movements. During the previous two years, the grantee helped to establish three new community foundations and supported six initiative groups to explore community foundation development. The grantee also supported the development of local philanthropy and individual giving. The grantee is based in Cluj-Napoca.

title: Community Foundation Development Program
description: The program goal is to support the community foundation movement in Romania. To this end, the Association for Community Relations, in partnership with the Romanian Environmental Partnership Foundation and PACT – Partnership for Community Action and Transformation (both Mott grantees), will provide funding and technical assistance to strengthen the two newly established community foundations in Cluj-Napoca and Odorheiu Secuiesc. In addition, the grantee will initiate and support the development of new community foundations in at least four locations in the next two years. The grantee’s activities will include promoting the community foundation concept, assisting local groups during the registration process, and providing funding and technical assistance to the newly established community foundations. Since its establishment in 2001, the grantee has been working in the field of local philanthropy and resource mobilization and has been instrumental in the establishment of the two existing Romanian community foundations.

title: Endowment for Sustainable Future
grantee: Academy for the Development of Philanthropy in Poland
description: The program goal is to strengthen the financial sustainability of a leading Polish foundation whose mission is to strengthen philanthropy and civil society in Poland. To this end, the Academy for the Development of Philanthropy in Poland will run an endowment-building program to raise at least $1 million and increase its total endowment to $1.8 million by the end of 2013. In addition, the grantee will strengthen its overall fundraising strategies and capacities. The grantee was established in 1998 as the successor organization of the Academy for Educational Development in Poland. The grantee provides grants, capacity-building programs, and networking opportunities to local nonprofit organizations and community foundations. Currently, the grantee is supporting a network of 42 local, philanthropic, grantmaking organizations in Poland, 20 of which are community foundations. Since 2008, the grantee has been running a regional capacity-building program for community foundations in the Visegrad countries with support from the Mott Foundation.

title: 25th Anniversary Capacity Building Campaign
description: Hispanics in Philanthropy works to diversify the field of philanthropy, improve Latino communities, and engage institutional funders and individual donors in strategic philanthropy. In honor of its 25th anniversary, the grantee has launched an initiative focused on its own institutional capacity and sustainability. This grant will enable the grantee to hire a consultant to conduct an organizational assessment as well as an in-depth analysis of its main grantmaking model — the Funders’ Collaborative for Strong Latino Communities.

title: Riverfront Residence Hall Expansion
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This repayable grant increase will provide support to the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation to expand the Riverfront Residence Hall project, increasing the number of available beds from 243 to 541 for the 2010 academic year. The 16-story building, originally constructed as the Hyatt Regency Hotel, has been converted into a state-of-the-art residence hall for local universities. The grantee will provide the grant funds to its supported organization, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, which intends to utilize the funds to invest in the project.

title: Purchase and Renovation of the Character Inn for Student Housing
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This repayable grant will provide support to the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation for the acquisition and redevelopment of the former Character Inn in downtown Flint. The 16-story building, originally constructed as a Hyatt Regency hotel, will be converted into a state-of-the-art student residence hall. The Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation will provide grant funds to its supported organization, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, which intends to utilize the funds to invest in the project.

title: Growth Plan
description: This grant will provide partial support to YouthBuild USA to undertake a series of programmatic activities outlined in its growth plan strategy. Over the next few years, YouthBuild USA aims to take the YouthBuild program model to full scale in the United States, as well as expand internationally. This grant will enable the grantee to enhance core activities in its international efforts, conduct a random assignment impact study, continue Hurricane Katrina-related activities in the Gulf Coast, launch a training fellowship program for local program directors, and augment general operating procedures related to the growth plan.

title: Flint Youth Theater Transition
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will support the transition of the Flint Youth Theater to the governance of the Flint Institute of Music. The Flint Youth Theater has been operated by the Flint Cultural Center Corporation since its move from the Flint Community Schools in 2003. Having the youth theater and drama school become part of the Flint Institute of Music (which includes the Flint Symphony Orchestra and the Flint School of Performing Arts) will consolidate all of the cultural center’s performing arts operations in one organization. Both organizations focus primarily on performing arts education and the production of artistic presentations. Even though the entities already partner and collaborate in several activities, this restructuring will create even greater programmatic opportunities.

title: Capacity Building
description: The grant provides support for capacity building to the National Organization on Disability. A recently approved strategic plan identifies three organizational priorities for capacity building: board development, fundraising, and communications. Over the next three years, the board will be expanded with new members from diverse skill sets and backgrounds. Further, senior executives will be hired to manage budgets and diversify sources of funding. Finally, a director of communications will be hired to develop a communications strategy, redesign the organization’s Web site, and produce newsletters and other materials for policymakers in government, foundation, and business sectors. Founded in 1982, the organization’s mission is to expand the participation and contribution of America’s 54 million men, women, and children with disabilities in all aspects of life.

title: ViabilityNet - Regional NGO Capacity Building Program
geographic_focus: Bulgaria, Slovakia, Ukraine, Montenegro, Czech Republic, Romania, Albania, North Macedonia, Hungary, Lithuania, Moldova, Serbia, Poland, Latvia, Austria, Belarus, Germany, Estonia, Slovenia
description: The program goal is to promote and develop independent civic action in Central and Eastern Europe. To this end, the VIA Foundation will increase the capacity of leading nongovernmental organizations in the region to provide effective capacity building programs and development assistance to nonprofits in their respective countries. Also, the grantee will expand the geographic scope of the program to include participants from 19 countries from both Western and Eastern Europe, including Belarus, Bulgaria, the Czech Republic, Hungary, Moldova, Poland, Romania, Serbia, Slovakia, and Ukraine. During the previous grant period, the grantee created successful partnerships with nonprofit capacity building providers in Bulgaria, Hungary, Romania, and Slovakia and helped them develop more effective programs and services for their beneficiaries. Since its establishment in 1997, the grantee supported more than 2,100 projects of nonprofit organizations in the Czech Republic, Slovakia, and Ukraine with grants and technical assistance. The VIA Foundation is based in Prague, Czech Republic.

title: ViabilityNet - Regional NGO Capacity Building Program
description: The program goal is to promote and develop independent civic action in communities in Central and Eastern Europe. To this end, the VIA Foundation will strengthen the leadership skills and capacities of 60 individual civic leaders and their nongovernmental organizations, provide grants to the participating organizations to implement social change projects in their communities, and facilitate exchange and joint action among the participating organizations. During the past grant period, the grantee improved the ViabilityNet – Regional NGO Capacity Building Program content and assistance methodology, provided training and technical assistance to 31 civic leaders from Central and Eastern Europe, funded 31 social change projects in these leaders’ communities, and supported networking and peer learning among program participants. The VIA Foundation is based in Prague, Czech Republic.

title: ViabilityNet - Regional NGO Capacity Building Program
geographic_focus: Hungary, Poland, Serbia, Romania, Slovakia, Czech Republic
description: The program goal is to promote and develop independent civic action in Central and Eastern Europe. To this end, the VIA Foundation will strengthen the capacity of leading nongovernmental organizations in the region to provide effective capacity building programs and development assistance to nonprofits in their respective countries. Initially, the program will include participants from the Czech Republic, Hungary, Romania, Serbia, and Slovakia, where the grantee has already established good working relationships with local partners. In the next phase, the program will be opened to other countries in the region as well. Since its establishment in 1997, the grantee has provided grants to more than 2,000 projects of nonprofit organizations in the Czech Republic, Slovakia, and Ukraine. In addition to grant support, the grantee provides capacity building and networking opportunities to its grantees and actively participates in policy development relating to civil society and philanthropy. The VIA Foundation is based in Prague, Czech Republic.

title: NGO-BG: Legitimacy Through Visibility, Knowledge and Shared Resources
description: The project goal is to strengthen the nonprofit sector in Bulgaria by increasing its transparency, visibility, legitimacy, and internal cooperation. To this end, the Bulgarian Center for Nonprofit Law will upgrade and expand the national Web portal for nonprofit organizations, which is the only database and media tool that collects and disseminates timely and accurate information about all aspects of the activities of nonprofit organizations in Bulgaria. In addition, the grantee will facilitate the development of networks and campaigns of nonprofit organizations aiming at improving the policy environment for their work, increasing their effectiveness, and improving the visibility of their achievements. Also, the grantee will strengthen its relationships with the media and the donor community to increase their engagement with the nonprofit sector. During the past grant period, the grantee increased the technical capabilities of the Web portal, improved the visibility and transparency of active nonprofit organizations, and improved communication between donors and nonprofits in Bulgaria. Established in 2001 and based in Sofia, Bulgaria, the grantee’s mission is to promote and develop civil society in Bulgaria.

title: NGO-BG: Legitimacy Through Visibility, Knowledge and Shared Resources
description: The program goal is to strengthen the nonprofit sector in Bulgaria by increasing its transparency, visibility, legitimacy, and internal cooperation. To this end, the Bulgarian Center for Nonprofit Law will upgrade and expand the national Web portal for nonprofit organizations, which is the only database and media tool that collects and disseminates timely and accurate information about all aspects of the activities of nonprofit organizations in Bulgaria. In addition, the grantee will facilitate the development of networks and campaigns of nonprofit organizations aiming at improving the policy environment for their work, increasing their effectiveness, and improving the visibility of their achievements. Also, the grantee will strengthen its relationships with the media and the donor community to increase their engagement with the nonprofit sector. Since its establishment in 2001, the grantee has become the leading source of information, advice, and technical assistance on a wide range of legal and institutional issues related to the Bulgarian nonprofit sector.

title: Pan Hellenic Council Mentorship Project
grantee: Big Brothers Big Sisters of Flint and Genesee County
description: Big Brothers Big Sisters of Greater Flint provides one-on-one mentoring to disadvantaged children in Genesee County through a variety of targeted programs. This grant will support an initiative to develop mentorships in the African-American community through African-American fraternities and sororities (commonly referred to as Black Greek Letter Organizations). The grantee will coordinate efforts for the Big Brothers Big Sisters agencies and the local affiliates of the National Pan Hellenic Council, which oversees the Black Greek Letter Organizations in Genesee, Saginaw, and Ingham counties, to increase their involvement in formal mentorship activities.

title: Pan Hellenic Council Mentorship Project
grantee: Big Brothers Big Sisters of Flint and Genesee County
description: Big Brothers Big Sisters of Greater Flint provides one-on-one mentoring to disadvantaged children in Genesee County through a variety of targeted programs. This grant will support the Flint replication of a national initiative of Big Brothers Big Sisters of America, which develops mentorship in the African-American community through African-American fraternities and sororities (more commonly referred to as Black Greek Letter Organizations). In 1991, the grantee and Alpha Phi Alpha partnered to establish the first Black Greek Letter Organization mentorship program in conjunction with a national mentorship organization. As the lead agency, Big Brothers Big Sisters of Greater Flint will coordinate efforts for the Big Brothers Big Sisters agencies and the local affiliates of the National Pan Hellenic Council, which oversees the Black Greek Letter Organizations in Genesee, Saginaw, and Ingham counties, to increase their involvement in formal mentorship activities.

title: Witherbee's Market
grantee: Flint Neighborhood Improvement and Preservation Project, Inc.
description: This grant will support the Flint Neighborhood Improvement and Preservation Project’s efforts to open a full-service grocery store in downtown Flint. With the addition of new apartments and student dormitories, many more residents are living downtown, and the need for typical support services, such as a grocery store, are increasing. Witherbee’s Market will be a 10,000 square foot, neighborhood grocery store that will carry green produce, dry goods, dairy, meat, fish, bakery goods, and a deli, offering downtown residents convenient access to nutritious, affordable foods. The site has 27 off-street parking spaces and the business is expected to hire 15 employees.

title: Annual Conference
description: This grant provides partial support to Independent Sector for its 2009 Annual Conference. Independent Sector is a coalition of leading nonprofits, foundations, and corporations that aims to strengthen nonprofit initiative, philanthropy, and citizen action in the United States. In an effort to increase efficiency, Independent Sector will collaborate with the Council of Michigan Foundations — an association that serves grantmakers and advances giving in Michigan — to combine their 2009 annual conferences into one. The conference will bring together chief executive officers, trustees, senior-level professionals, and emerging leaders from approximately 500 local and national organizations to share their experiences, innovative approaches, and practical solutions to address the challenges of today.

title: Community Education Training
description: This grant provides support to St. Louis Public Schools for the implementation of full-service schools where community-based organizations and public and/or private entities collaborate with the school to provide students, families, and the community access to comprehensive services. Specifically, this grant will support professional development and self-assessment activities for district and community stakeholders designed to fully prepare them for complete, full-service school implementation. Professional development sessions will be facilitated by nationally recognized consultants with expertise in the design and implementation of full-service schools.

title: Metal Muscle Mentoring Program
description: This grant will provide scholarships for 19 students, 15 of whom are attending either Beecher High School or Hamady High School in Flint, both Title I schools with a free/reduced lunch rate of over 90 percent and mostly minority student populations. The scholarships will allow students to participate in Metal Muscle, Kettering University’s robotics team for the 2010 season.

title: FIRST Robotics Team
description: This grant will provide support to Kettering University for the Flint FIRST Robotics team. Student participants and their adult mentors work together to build a robot that will be used in regional and national competitions to challenge other teams’ robots in performing specific tasks. FIRST Robotics provides students critical exposure to hands-on science, technology, engineering, and mathematics learning experiences in a fun and positive team environment.

title: Metal Muscle FIRST Robotic Team
description: This grant will provide scholarships for eight students of Beecher High School, a Title I school with a free/reduced lunch rate of over 90 percent and a mostly minority (African-American) student population. The scholarships will allow students to participate in Metal Muscle, Kettering University’s FIRST Robotics team for the 2009 season.

title: Community Development Financial Institution (CDFI) Program
description: This grant increase will enable Metro Housing Partnership to develop additional loan products for suppliers and small businesses related to the automotive industry. A previous Mott grant supported the organization’s efforts to become Genesee County’s only community development financial institution. These institutions provide loans and mortgages for businesses and residents in underserved and distressed urban communities.

title: Community Development Financial Institution (CDFI) Program
description: This renewal grant will enable Metro Community Development to acquire funding from the Small Business Administration to capitalize its Community Development Financial Institution. As the county’s only Community Development Financial Institution, the grantee will fill the void created by the dissolution of the Community Capital Development Corporation and leverage federal dollars available for distressed and underserved urban communities.

title: Community Development Financial Institution (CDFI) Program
description: This capacity building grant will provide Metro Community Development with the requisite technical assistance necessary to acquire funding from the Small Business Administration to capitalize its Community Development Financial Institution Program. As one of two such institutions in the county, the grantee is working to leverage federal dollars available for distressed and underserved urban communities.

title: Community Development Financial Institution (CDFI) Program
description: This grant will enable Metro Housing Partnership to acquire the necessary certification to become a Community Development Financial Institution by supplementing the funds provided by a technical assistance grant from the U.S. Department of Treasury. By obtaining certification, the grantee will fill the void created by the dissolution of the Community Capital Development Corporation and leverage significant federal dollars available for distressed and underserved urban communities.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint
description: This renewal grant will provide general purpose support for the Boys & Girls Club of Greater Flint. The organization, revived in 2004, now offers year-round afterschool activities for children aged 7-17 in two locations: the recently reopened Haskell Community Center and the former Sobey Elementary School. The Boys & Girls Club of Greater Flint focuses on six areas of programming: family and community support services, educational support services, health services, creative/arts services, summer program support, and transportation services.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint
description: This renewal grant will provide general purpose support for the Boys & Girls Club of Greater Flint. The organization, revived in 2004, now offers year-round afterschool activities for children aged 7-17 in two locations: the recently reopened Haskell Community Center and the former Sobey Elementary School. The grantee focuses on six areas of programming: family and community support services, educational support services, health services, creative/arts services, summer program support, and transportation services. This year, the grantee’s programming will include the coordination of national service volunteers at various nonprofits across Genesee County through the launch of its National Service Accelerator Initiative.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint
description: This renewal grant provides general purpose support to the Boys & Girls Club of Greater Flint. Focusing on five areas of youth development: leadership, arts, fitness, life skills, and education, the grantee offers year-round programming to children, ages 7-17, at two facilities in the city of Flint: the Averill Avenue site and the Haskell Community Center. Additionally, the grantee houses the staff director for the National Service Accelerator Initiative, which provides matching funds for Flint area nonprofit agencies utilizing volunteers through any of the Corporation for National and Community Service programs.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint
description: This renewal grant provides general purpose support to the Boys & Girls Club of Greater Flint. Focusing on five areas of youth development (leadership, arts, fitness, life skills, and education), the grantee offers year-round programming to children ages 7-17 at two facilities in the city of Flint: the Averill Avenue site and the Haskell Community Center. Additionally, the grantee houses the staff director for the National Service Accelerator Initiative, which provides matching funds for Flint area nonprofit agencies utilizing volunteers through any of the Corporation for National and Community Service programs.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint
description: This renewal grant provides general purpose support to the Boys & Girls Club of Greater Flint. Focusing on education, creativity, physical activity and health, and family support services, the grantee offers year-round programming to over 3,500 children, ages 7-17, at two locations in the city of Flint: the Averill Avenue site and the Haskell Community Center. Additionally, the grantee houses the staff director for the National Service Accelerator Initiative, which provides matching funds for Flint area nonprofit agencies utilizing volunteers through any of the Corporation for National and Community Service programs.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint
description: This renewal grant provides general purpose support to the Boys & Girls Club of Greater Flint. Focusing on education, creativity, physical activity and health, and family support services, the grantee offers year-round programming to all young people in the Flint area between the ages of 7 and 17 at two locations in the city of Flint (Averill Avenue and Haskell Community Center).

title: General Purposes
grantee: Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint
description: This renewal grant provides general purpose support to the Boys & Girls Club of Greater Flint Focusing on education, creativity, physical activity and health, and family support services, the Boys & Girls Club of Flint offers year-round programming to all young people in the Flint area between the ages of 7 and 17 at the Averill Avenue location. Programs such as this are particularly necessary in Flint given its current water crisis because educational and enrichment opportunities are important interventions for individuals from birth to young adulthood to help mitigate the long-term impacts of exposure to lead.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint
description: This renewal grant provides general purpose support to the Boys & Girls Club of Greater Flint. Focusing on education, creativity, physical activity and health, and family support services, the grantee offers year-round programming to young people between the ages of 7 and 17 in the Flint area at the Averill Avenue location. Programs such as this have been particularly necessary in Flint during the water crisis knowing that educational and enrichment opportunities are important interventions to help mitigate the long-term impacts of exposure to lead.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint
description: This renewal grant provides general purpose support to the Boys & Girls Club of Greater Flint. Focusing on education, creativity, physical activity and health, and family support services, the grantee offers year-round programming to young people between the ages of 7 and 17 in the Flint area. Programs such as this have been particularly necessary in Flint during the water crisis given that educational and enrichment opportunities are important interventions to help mitigate the long-term impacts of exposure to lead.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint
description: This renewal grant provides general purpose support to the Boys & Girls Club of Greater Flint. Focusing on education, creativity, physical activity and health, and family support services, the grantee offers year-round programming to young people between the ages of 7 and 17 in the Flint area. The grantee operates two sites, one located on the east side of the city and the other on the south side of the city. Programs such as this have been particularly necessary in Flint during the water crisis given that educational and enrichment opportunities are important interventions to help mitigate the long-term impacts of exposure to lead.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint
description: This grant will provide general purpose support for the Boys & Girls Club of Greater Flint. The organization offers year-round, afterschool programming for children aged 7-17 in a youth-exclusive facility. Located at the remodeled Sobey community school, the Boys & Girls Club of Greater Flint focuses on six areas of programming services: family and community support, educational support, health, creative/arts, summer program support, and transportation.

title: 2-1-1 Call Center Start-Up
description: Resource Genesee offers a range of much-needed services to the greater Flint community including leadership and civic engagement training for up-and-coming community leaders, volunteer recruitment and placement, and information and referral services. Resource Genesee will expand its services by contracting with an existing 2-1-1 call center to respond to all callers seeking human services and/or volunteer information. This grant will provide the grantee with the start-up costs to establish a 2-1-1 human services information hotline for Genesee County residents.

title: General Purposes
description: The Southern California Education Fund provides the technical assistance and capacity building training necessary to support organizations affiliated with the Industrial Areas Foundation in Los Angeles County, the greater San Diego and San Francisco regions, and elsewhere in southern California. This general purpose grant will support the overall needs and work of the organization.

title: General Purposes
description: The Southern California Education Fund provides the technical assistance and capacity building training necessary to support organizations affiliated with the Industrial Areas Foundation in Los Angeles County, the Greater San Diego and San Francisco regions, and elsewhere in southern California. This general purpose grant will support the overall needs and work of the organization.

title: General Purposes
description: The Southern California Education Fund provides the technical assistance and capacity-building training necessary to support a countywide community organization in Los Angeles called One LA. Affiliated with the Industrial Areas Foundation, One LA is a nonpartisan, multiethnic organization comprised of dues-paying congregations, schools, unions, and nonprofit organizations. In the last two years, the grantee has launched additional organizations in San Diego and the Bay Area. This general purpose grant will support the overall needs and work of the organization.

title: BeHeard!
description: This grant will help continue the BeHeard! communications initiative. BeHeard! was launched in 2006 by the Woodcock Foundation in collaboration with several other foundations and individuals in response to overwhelming evidence that the nonprofit community was not keeping pace with the major technological and messaging changes happening in the communications universe. BeHeard! has helped a broad sample of nonprofit, community-based organizations realize their potential to expand and engage their constituencies — particularly through the use of aspirational messaging and online communications.

title: City of Flint Government Analysis
description: This grant increase will provide additional support to Prima Civitas Foundation to assist the city of Flint with improving the performance and management of municipal operations. Prima Civitas Foundation, a regional economic development nonprofit agency, will use its expertise in governmental operations to help reorganize city departments and help them operate more effectively.

title: City of Flint Government Analysis
description: This grant increase will provide additional support to the Prima Civitas Foundation to continue to assist the city of Flint with improving the performance and management of municipal operations. Prima Civitas Foundation, a regional economic development nonprofit agency, uses its expertise in governmental operations to help reorganize city departments and help them operate more effectively.

title: City of Flint Government Analysis
description: Because of a change in the administration of the city of Flint, coupled with uncertain budget deficits and a new budget required in a short timeframe by the state of Michigan, there is a need to engage in a performance and management review of city functions. Prima Civitas Foundation, a regional economic development nonprofit agency, will assist the city with improvements to the performance and management of the city budget and municipal operations.

title: Mainstreaming Civic and Community Engagement into Social Development
description: The program goal is to strengthen the institutional capacity of the New Eurasia Foundation in the fields of civic engagement and community development and to encourage the central role of citizen participation in such development efforts in Russia. To that end, the grantee will seek to integrate its work with community schools and universities into a more comprehensive vision of cross-sectoral partnerships for community development. Its Innovation Fund for Community Development will continue to shape and respond to community development priorities and opportunities through leveraged financial support. In 2009-2011, the grantee introduced and embedded community schools training methodologies into 13 teacher training institutes across Russia, and engaged 10 pilot universities in concrete efforts to support local community development. Established in 2003, the New Eurasia Foundation works to foster a broad range of cross-sectoral partnerships to assist in Russia’s social and economic development.

title: Mainstreaming Civic and Community Engagement into Social Development
description: The program goal is to promote greater civic engagement and participatory community development practices in Russia. To these ends, this grant will strengthen the institutional capacity of the New Eurasia Foundation to be a leader in these fields. During the grant period, the grantee will seek to combine its work with community schools and universities into a more integrated vision of cross-sectoral partnerships for community development. Its Innovation Fund for Community Development will seek to leverage additional support in responding to emerging opportunities for mainstreaming civic engagement. In 2011-13, the grantee fostered three robust sustainable clusters of community education support institutions in Central Russia, Eastern Siberia, and the North Caucasus. Participating universities systematically analyzed and catalogued community engagement models and prepared these for dissemination to peers. Established in 2003, the New Eurasia Foundation works to foster a broad range of cross-sectoral partnerships to assist in Russia’s social and economic development.

title: Mainstreaming Civic and Community Engagement into Social Development
description: The program goal is to strengthen the institutional capacity of the New Eurasia Foundation in the fields of civic engagement and community development. The project aims to encourage the central role of public participation and citizen engagement in community development efforts in Russia. To that end, the grantee will seek to integrate its work with community schools and universities into a more comprehensive vision of cross-sectoral partnerships for community development. It will establish a flexible “innovation fund for community development” that can both shape and respond to community development priorities and opportunities through leveraged financial support. Finally, the project will result in the expansion of the grantee’s capacity to effectively identify, raise funds for, and learn from community development initiatives from across and outside Russia. Established in 2003, the New Eurasia Foundation works to foster a broad range of cross-sectoral partnerships to assist in Russia’s social and economic development.

title: Area XIII Program Support
description: Special Olympics Michigan provides year-round sports training and athletic competition in a variety of Olympic-type sports for children and adults with intellectual disabilities, giving them the opportunity to develop physical fitness, various motor and cognitive skills, self-confidence, and friendships. The grantee offers its services free of charge and accepts all participants regardless of ability level. Special Olympics Michigan-Area XIII serves Genesee and Lapeer counties, and currently serves approximately 1,152 “special” athletes with opportunities to train and compete in 20 sporting events throughout the year.

title: Merger Assistance
description: The Child Advocacy Center of Genesee County is a community-based organization designed to meet the unique needs of the Genesee County community by providing a safe, child-friendly setting for the forensic interviews of children who have allegedly been sexually or severely physically abused. This grant will enable the center to merge with the Consortium on Child Abuse and Neglect – an organization dedicated to educating and advocating against child abuse and neglect in Genesee County. The merged organization will provide comprehensive and coordinated advocacy, education, prevention, and investigative services for children in Genesee County.

title: N.E.W. Life Center
description: Established in 1941, St. John Vianney Parish, a Catholic church located in Flint, Michigan, serves 700 local families through various forms of community outreach and ministry. St. John Vianney Parish extends its services to low-income women and their families in Flint and Genesee County through the North End Women’s Life Center. The center offers literacy and adult education, emergency assistance, computer skills, and afterschool and summer youth programs. The center also offers women with low to no income an intense, three-year program that encourages life change through personal growth, basic skill development, and self-esteem building as well as employment. During the grant period, the center will implement a self-contained work environment by launching two small-scale enterprises — a catering and sewing business.

title: SMART Program
description: Established in 2004 within the Center for Advancing Research and Solutions for Society at the University of Michigan, the SMART Program has worked in city regions around the world on a new mobility approach, which supports connected, multimodal, sustainable, and accessible transportation. Building on this successful model, this grant will support efforts that link transportation, business, economic, and community leaders from across southeast Michigan.

title: SMART Program
description: Established in 2004 within the Center for Advancing Research and Solutions for Society at the University of Michigan, the SMART Program has worked in city regions around the world on a new mobility approach, which supports connected, multimodal, sustainable, and accessible transportation. Building on this successful model, this grant will support a forum or “link tank” that brings together transportation, business, economic, and community leaders from across the southeast Michigan region. This will include hosting major gatherings and developing supporting materials and Web-based tools and maps.

title: Masterpieces of European Painting
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will support the Masterpieces of European Painting exhibit at the Flint Institute of Arts. A part of the permanent collection of the Museo de Arte de Ponce in Puerto Rico, the masterpieces are an extraordinary collection of European paintings spanning six centuries and nine nationalities. The exhibit of 56 large-scale paintings opened on November 28, 2008, and ran through March 8, 2009, and is one of the most prestigious exhibitions in Flint Institute of Art’s history. These European masterpieces are being shown for the first time in North America and as the only Midwest venue, Flint Institute of Arts’ visitors had a unique opportunity to view this rare collection.

title: Urban Alternatives House
description: This grant supports the Urban Alternatives House, a green renovation project operated by the University of Michigan-Flint. Originating in 2009 with funding from the Kresge Foundation’s Green Building Initiative, University of Michigan-Flint began the process of renovating a formerly abandoned property (519 Garland Street) in the historic Carriage Town district. Unfortunately, that property was destroyed by arson and the collaborative team began looking for a new location. Currently on 924 Eddy Street in the Central Park neighborhood, a new property has been identified that, once renovated, will house the new Urban Alternatives House project. The mission of the project is to teach sustainable living to Flint area secondary and post-secondary students and support green building practices for renovations and demolitions of Genesee County Land Bank-owned properties.

title: Urban Alternatives House
description: This grant is for the development of a green building renovation through the University of Michigan-Flint’s University Outreach, entitled the “Urban Alternatives House”. Leveraging a grant from the Kresge Green Building Initiative, this grant will enable the grantee to complete the planning phase of the project. Located at 519 Garland Street, in the historic Carriage Town district, the Urban Alternatives House will serve to teach sustainable living, support green building on Genesee County Land Bank-owned properties, and combat climate change. This project is a collaboration between the University of Michigan-Flint, the Genesee County Land Bank, and THA Architects.

title: General Purposes
description: Founded in 1996, the Keweenaw Land Trust has protected over 3,000 acres in Michigan’s Keweenaw Peninsula, which extends into Lake Superior — the largest freshwater lake in the world. With previous Mott support, the trust worked to build its own organizational capacity while implementing conservation, stewardship, and educational programs to protect and restore the Keweenaw Peninsula’s important natural areas and watersheds. With renewed Mott support, the trust will continue these efforts and will also invest in board and staff development.

title: General Purposes
description: Founded in 1996, the Keweenaw Land Trust has protected over 3,000 acres in the Keweenaw Peninsula, which extends into Lake Superior — the largest freshwater lake in the world. The trust works to protect and restore the peninsula’s natural areas, watersheds, and distinctive landscapes by holding conservation easements, establishing public nature preserves, and educating and engaging the public. With Mott support, the trust will continue these conservation efforts while also focusing on capacity-building activities such as developing a strategic plan, refining a communications plan, and moving toward national accreditation.

title: Michigan's Advanced Energy Economy Initiative
description: The federal economic stimulus package offers Michigan a unique, short-term opportunity to advance the state’s economic development initiatives focused on alternative energy and job creation. Due to a variety of factors, however, the state government lacks the capacity to take full advantage of this opportunity. With support from Mott and other Michigan foundations, the Council of Michigan Foundations, a nonprofit membership association, will assist the state of Michigan by providing the short-term assistance of a consulting firm. The firm will help position the state to secure, and spend wisely, federal stimulus funds in two priority areas: energy efficiency and renewable energy generation.

title: American Federation of Teachers Innovation Fund
grantee: American Federation of Teachers Educational Foundation
description: This grant will support the American Federation of Teachers Educational Foundation in its efforts to encourage the involvement of teachers in education reform processes. Specifically, this grant will provide support to the grantee to launch an innovation fund that will provide financial and organizational resources for educator- and union-generated ideas that seek to both raise student achievement and build partnerships with administrators, parents, and community and business leaders. This project also directly supports Building Community Schools and Partnerships, one of three strategies the American Federation of Teachers is pursuing to improve public education.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen organized philanthropy in Russia. Officially registered in 2002, the Russia Donors Forum promotes effective and organized grantmaking supporting the development of a democratic civil society in Russia. Currently, the grantee has 33 members and over 100 companies participating in its events and projects. It has published popular books and reports on the development of philanthropy in contemporary Russia and has become an expert on corporate philanthropy and endowments. Continued Mott support will assist the grantee to improve member services, provide professional support to the philanthropic community, and raise the profile of philanthropy. The grantee will focus on growing its membership, increasing professional consultations and training opportunities, providing reliable information on the current and future role of philanthropy in Russia, enhancing its position as one of the key players in formulating and articulating donors’ interests in Russia, and increasing international cooperation.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen organized philanthropy in Russia. Existing general purpose support allows the Russia Donors Forum to focus on growing its membership, increasing professional consultations and training opportunities, and providing reliable information on the current and future role of philanthropy in Russia. An increase in this support will allow the grantee to commission a detailed survey on the state of institutional philanthropy in Russia’s regions. This detailed examination of regional philanthropy will form the centerpiece for discussion at the 2013 annual conference of the Russia Donors Forum.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen organized philanthropy in Russia. The grant will assist the Russia Donors Forum to improve member services, provide professional support to the philanthropic community, and raise the profile of philanthropy. The grantee will enhance its online services and information while continuing to expand its growing publishing and conference program. It will work closely with relevant partners to advocate for improvements in the environment for philanthropy. It will also work to strengthen standards and codes of conduct for members, aiming ultimately to become a formal, self-regulating association for Russian donors. Since 2007, the grantee has increased its membership to 50 organizations. It has published popular books on the development of philanthropy in contemporary Russia and has successfully promoted donor transparency through its annual report contests. Officially registered in 2002, the Russia Donors Forum promotes effective and organized grantmaking supporting the development of a democratic civil society in Russia.

title: Michigan Participation Project - 2010 Census
description: The Michigan Nonprofit Association serves as a statewide network for the nonprofit sector, a resource center on effective management practices, and an advocate for the nonprofit community. As a program of the Michigan Nonprofit Association, the Michigan Participation Project will work to coordinate and strengthen the nonprofit community’s efforts to achieve a complete count in the 2010 census. The Michigan Participation Project will mobilize Michigan nonprofits to educate and engage communities around the 2010 census to ensure that everyone is counted. Major activities will include convening a statewide Nonprofit Complete Count Committee, mapping and targeting hard-to-count communities, coordinating with government officials, implementing a communications strategy, developing a train-the-trainer network, offering briefings/trainings for organizations, and providing minigrants to nonprofits.

title: Grand Vision Collaborative Efforts
description: The Grand Vision is a blueprint for Traverse City and six adjacent counties in northwest Michigan that seeks to maintain the traditional character of the region’s small towns and natural landscapes, while working to bring new prosperity to the region. The product of more than three years of work by thousands of citizens, business leaders, and elected officials, the Grand Vision integrates environmental, transportation, and development interests. The Rotary Charities of Traverse City, a public organization focused on the welfare of the Traverse City region, has been crucial to the development of the Grand Vision. With support from Mott, the grantee will help lead coordination and communication efforts to implement the Grand Vision and sustain broad community support for it.

title: Community Foundation School
description: The program goal is to foster the development of community foundations in Ukraine. Through this program, Ednannia will seek to strengthen the capacity and practice of local philanthropic organizations. It will provide technical assistance and networking opportunities to existing and emerging community philanthropy organizations in Ukraine and will also facilitate peer exchanges and mentoring opportunities with partners in neighboring countries. The grantee will also launch a matching grants program to stimulate local giving for the institutional development and operating expenses of Ukrainian community foundations. In 2010-2011, the grantee successfully developed a range of capacity building materials and initiatives for potential community foundations in Ukraine, resulting in the emergence of four strong pilot foundations. Established as an indigenous grantmaker in 1999, Ednannia is well regarded for its rigorous, transparent, responsive, and effective grantmaking in support of community-level, grassroots organizations throughout Ukraine.

title: Community Foundation School
description: The program goal is to foster the development of community foundations in Ukraine. Ednannia will seek to strengthen the capacity and practice of local philanthropic organizations. It will provide technical assistance and networking opportunities to existing and emerging community philanthropy organizations in Ukraine and will facilitate peer exchanges and mentoring opportunities with partners in neighboring countries. The grantee will also make grants to community foundations for a variety of purposes including matching local giving and capacity development. In 2011-2013, the grantee increased its support from 4 to 21 emerging and developing community foundations. Collectively, these organizations raised over $750,000 in cash and in-kind donations, and in addition to operational programs, they distributed over $75,000 in grants. Established as an indigenous grantmaker in 1999, Ednannia is well regarded for its rigorous, transparent, responsive, and effective grantmaking in support of community-level, grassroots organizations throughout Ukraine.

title: Community Foundation School
description: The program goal is to foster the development of community foundations in Ukraine. To this end, Ednannia, a national support organization for community foundations in Ukraine, will strengthen the capacity and practice of existing community foundations and facilitate the development of at least three new community foundations by providing training, advice, and small grants. In addition, the grantee will support the exchange and joint action among community foundations by organizing various learning events and strengthening their newly established network, the Alliance for Community Foundations. The grantee will also increase the information and knowledge about the Ukrainian community foundation field by conducting and disseminating research and analyses. In 2014-2015, the grantee established three new community foundations, strengthened the capacity of community foundations to respond to the emergency situation related to the armed conflict in Ukraine, and increased its own organizational capacity and expertise. Established as an indigenous grantmaker in 1999, Ednannia is well regarded for its rigorous, transparent, responsive, and effective grantmaking in support of community-level, grassroots organizations throughout Ukraine.

title: Community Foundation School
description: The program goal is to foster the development of community foundations in Ukraine. To this end, Ednannia, a national support organization for community foundations in Ukraine, will strengthen the capacity and practice of existing community foundations and, where appropriate, facilitate the development of new community foundations by providing training, advice, and small grants. In addition, the grantee will support the exchange and joint action among community foundations by organizing various learning events across the network and with European counterparts. Also, the grantee will increase the information and knowledge about the Ukrainian community foundation field by conducting and disseminating research and analyses. In 2016–2017, the grantee conducted 35 capacity-building events for community foundations. These organizations distributed over $1 million dollars for more than 150 projects in their communities. The grantee and its local partners also developed a community needs assessment tool to help better allocate grant resources. Established as an indigenous grantmaker in 1999, Ednannia is well regarded for its rigorous, transparent, responsive, and effective grantmaking in support of community-level, grassroots organizations throughout Ukraine.

title: Community Foundation School
description: The program goal is to foster the development of community foundations in Ukraine. Through this program, Ednannia will seek to strengthen the capacity and practice of local philanthropic organizations. It will provide technical assistance and networking opportunities to existing and emerging community philanthropy organizations in Ukraine and will also facilitate peer exchanges and mentoring opportunities with partners in neighboring countries. The grantee will also launch a matching grants program to stimulate local giving for Ukrainian community foundations’ institutional development and operating expenses. Established as an indigenous grantmaker in 1999, Ednannia is well-regarded for its rigorous, transparent, responsive, and effective grantmaking in support of community-level, grassroots organizations throughout Ukraine.

title: Asset Building Policy Project
grantee: Community Economic Development Association of Michigan
description: This grant increase supports the Community Economic Development Association of Michigan’s ongoing efforts to promote the development and sustainability of state and federal programs and policies that expand asset building incentives and opportunities for low- and moderate-income families in Michigan. Objectives for the next year include: 1) engaging new stakeholders to further a statewide asset building agenda; 2) educating state policymakers about asset building strategies and goals; and 3) working with state government and each department as it considers the programming implications that asset building policy has for its investments and outcomes. The grantee is a Lansing-based, nonprofit member organization dedicated to rebuilding neighborhoods and revitalizing communities throughout Michigan. This is one of nine grants aimed at building the capacity of state asset building coalitions to effectively promote the development of state asset policies.

title: Asset Building Policy Project
grantee: Community Economic Development Association of Michigan
description: This grant will support the efforts of the Community Economic Development Association of Michigan to promote the development and sustainability of state and federal programs and policies that expand asset-building incentives and opportunities for low- and moderate-income families. Objectives for the two-year grant period include: 1) engaging new stakeholders to further asset-building goals; 2) educating policymakers about asset-building strategies and goals; and 3) working in each department within state government as it considers the programming implications that asset-building policy has for its investments and outcomes. The grantee is a Lansing-based nonprofit member organization dedicated to rebuilding neighborhoods and revitalizing communities throughout Michigan. This is one of nine grants aimed at building the capacity of state asset-building coalitions to effectively promote the development of state asset policies.

title: Capacity Building in the South on Climate Change and Sustainable Development
description: The Third World Network Berhad was established in 1987 as an international network of organizations and individuals involved in research and policy analysis of global issues and their impact on developing countries. With this grant increase, the grantee will inform developing country negotiators about the implications of climate finance proposals being put forth for consideration at the United Nations climate change negotiations to be held in Mexico in December 2010. A series of briefing documents and workshops will be prepared for the developing country negotiators, with a particular focus on carbon trading as a mechanism for addressing global mitigation and adaptation costs related to climate change.

title: Capacity Building in the South on Climate Change and Sustainable Development
description: The Third World Network Berhad was established in 1987 as an international network of organizations and individuals involved in research and policy analysis of global issues and their impact on developing countries. Over the last grant period, they were able to provide key policy analyses that assisted developing country negotiators and civil society. Through this grant, the grantee will contribute to the development of policies that assist poor developing countries address climate change, in particular the development of national climate action plans. The grantee will also provide important capacity-building activities for developing country nongovernmental organizations as well as country negotiators working on the international climate agreement.

title: Capacity Building in the South on Climate Change and Sustainable Development
description: Third World Network Berhad was established in 1987 as an international network of organizations and individuals involved in research and policy analysis of global issues and their impact on developing countries. Over the last two years, the grantee was able to provide key policy analyses related to the United Nations’ climate negotiations that assisted developing country negotiators and civil society. With this grant renewal, the grantee will contribute to the development of policies that assist poor developing countries address climate change, in particular the development of the Green Climate Fund, a new international funding mechanism. The grantee will also provide important capacity building activities for developing country nongovernmental organizations, as well as country negotiators working on the international climate agreement.

title: Capacity Building in the South on Climate Change and Sustainable Development
description: The Third World Network Berhad was established in 1987 as an international network of organizations and individuals involved in research and policy analysis of global issues and their impact on developing countries. Through this grant, the grantee will contribute to the development of a financing mechanism as part of the final outcome of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change, which will ensure the full implementation of such an agreement. Third World Network Berhad will also provide important capacity-building activities for developing country nongovernmental organizations as well as country negotiators working on the international climate agreement.

title: Ensuring Development and Climate Finance Support Sustainable Development
description: The Center for International Environmental Law was founded in 1989 to strengthen international environmental law, policy, and management. This grant will support activities that promote and seek stronger implementation of sound environmental and social policies and practices at international financial institutions. Grant funds will also be used to ensure there are strong environmental and social standards for climate finance and that communities benefit from and meaningfully participate in decisionmaking on climate finance. During the last grant, the grantee led efforts to enhance World Bank environmental and social standards, as well as strengthen the World Bank’s energy strategy. Activities supported by this grant include research and analysis of existing policies, development of policy reform proposals, and coordination of nongovernmental organizations’ coalitions addressing climate finance and safeguard policies.

title: Ensuring Development and Climate Finance Support Sustainable Development
description: The Center for International Environmental Law was founded in 1989 to strengthen international environmental law, policy, and management. This grant will support activities that promote and seek stronger implementation of sound environmental and social policies and practices at international financial institutions. Mott support will be used to advocate for continued robust, mandatory standards at the World Bank in light of its safeguard policy review, and ensure that the United Nation’s Green Climate Fund incorporates strong environmental and social standards for climate finance. During the last two years, the grantee led efforts to ensure that World Bank environmental and social safeguards covered new World Bank Group lending, as well as strengthened monitoring of its private-sector lending via the financial markets.

title: Ensuring Development and Climate Finance Support Sustainable Development
description: The Center for International Environmental Law was founded in 1989 to strengthen international environmental law, policy, and management. This grant will support activities that promote and seek stronger implementation of sound environmental and social policies and practices at international financial institutions. Over the next grant period, the grantee will continue its work to ensure strong environmental and social standards at the World Bank Group as well as the United Nation’s Green Climate Fund. Over the last two years, the grantee has been a strong voice calling for clear and consistent standards that reflect international best practice. They have built support for maintaining and strengthening World Bank Group safeguards among key policymakers.

title: Ensuring Development and Climate Finance Support Sustainable Development
description: The Center for International Environmental Law was founded in 1989 to strengthen international environmental law, policy, and management. This grant will support activities that promote and seek stronger implementation of sound environmental and social policies and practices at international financial institutions. Over the next grant period, the grantee will continue its work to ensure strong environmental and social standards at the World Bank Group, as well as the United Nation’s Green Climate Fund. Over the last two years, the grantee has been a strong voice calling for clear and consistent standards that reflect international best practice and has built support for maintaining and strengthening World Bank Group safeguards among key policymakers.

title: Ensuring International Financial Flows Support Sustainable Development
description: The Center for International Environmental Law was founded in 1989 to strengthen international environmental law, policy, and management. It is one of the leading nongovernmental organizations active at the intersection of economic integration and the protection of environment and human health nationally, regionally, and internationally. This grant will support activities in the following areas: promote and seek stronger implementation of sound environmental and social policies and practices at international financial institutions and other financial entities; and help to use new climate initiatives undertaken by the international financial institutions to leverage changes in existing energy lending portfolios. For this grant, project activities will include researching existing policies and developing policy reform proposals, sharing information and developing joint strategies with other nongovernmental organizations, conducting outreach to government officials and managers of international financial institutions, and preparing and disseminating publications on key issues.

title: Building a New Economy that Addresses Climate and Global Finance
description: The Institute for Policy Studies works in collaboration with nongovernmental organizations, academics, parliamentarians, and other stakeholders to develop alternative proposals for the future of the global economy based on environmental sustainability, democracy, and economic fairness. This grant increase will support policy research on national and global responses to the economic crisis, with a particular focus on the role of financial transaction taxes, excess concentration of the financial industry, and derivatives reform.

title: Global Finance for Climate Sustainability
description: The Institute for Policy Studies works in collaboration with nongovernmental organizations, academics, and other stakeholders to promote financing for sustainable energy and to develop alternative proposals for the future of the global economy based on environmental sustainability, democracy, and economic fairness. This grant will support policy research on the linkages between financial sector reform and innovations in funding for addressing climate change. This grant will also support coordination with other organizations in the United States, Europe, and the developing world aimed at identifying policy alternatives and financing mechanisms that would reduce greenhouse gas emissions and promote low-carbon, sustainable development.

title: Global Finance for Climate Sustainability
description: The Institute for Policy Studies works in collaboration with nongovernmental organizations, academics, and other stakeholders to promote financing for sustainable energy and to develop alternative proposals for the future of the global economy based on environmental sustainability, democracy, and economic fairness. This grant increase will support training materials and workshops for policy advocates on public and private finance mechanisms for climate mitigation and energy. Support will enable the grantee to consolidate the curriculum from an initial pilot course and develop new materials tailored to the issues that will be debated at the Rio+20 meetings that will be held in Brazil in June 2012.

title: Global Finance for Climate Sustainability
description: The Institute for Policy Studies works in collaboration with nongovernmental organizations, academics, and other stakeholders to promote financing for sustainable energy and to address climate change. Over the last grant period, it helped to build important new alliances with the financial sector and other private-sector groups to address the challenge of financing low-carbon development for developing countries, also known as climate finance. This renewal grant will support policy research and civil society coordination on climate finance, the World Bank’s energy lending portfolio, and international energy and infrastructure finance.

title: Global Finance for Climate Sustainability
description: The Institute for Policy Studies works in collaboration with nongovernmental organizations, academics, and the financial sector to promote financing for sustainable energy and to address climate change. Over the last grant period, it worked to ensure that the United Nations’ Green Climate Fund lives up to its mandate of helping developing countries transition to clean energy development. The grantee also continued its efforts to build alliances with the financial sector and other private-sector groups to address the challenge of financing low-carbon development for developing countries, also known as climate finance. This renewal grant will support policy research and civil society coordination on the early implementation of the Green Climate Fund, innovative financing for the fund, and use of the fund to promote developing country micro-, small-, and medium-sized enterprises working to provide renewable energy options.

title: Building a New Economy that Addresses Climate and Global Finance
description: The Institute for Policy Studies works in collaboration with nongovernmental organizations, academics, parliamentarians, and other stakeholders to promote financing for sustainable energy and to develop alternative proposals for the future of the global economy based on environmental sustainability, democracy, and economic fairness. This grant will support policy research on global responses to the economic crisis and global climate change. This grant will also support coordination with other organizations in the United States, Europe, and the developing world aimed at identifying policy alternatives and financing mechanisms that would reduce greenhouse gas emissions and promote low-carbon, sustainable development.

title: General Purposes
description: The Genesee County Parks & Recreation Commission has been dedicated to providing all the residents of Genesee County with affordable, quality recreational and educational facilities. The parks are widely utilized as accessible and inexpensive recreational and nature opportunities for local residents, and attendance in most facilities has either held constant or increased despite the recent critical economic conditions. This grant will enable Genesee County to continue regular operation and maintenance of its parks’ facilities, conduct much-needed maintenance and improvement projects, and strategically reduce its budget for continued quality community service.

title: General Purposes
description: The Genesee County Parks & Recreation Commission is dedicated to providing all the residents of Genesee County with affordable, quality, recreational and educational facilities. The Genesee County Parks are widely utilized as accessible and inexpensive recreational and nature opportunities for local residents, and attendance in most facilities has either held constant or increased despite the recent critical economic conditions. This renewal grant will enable the grantee to continue regular operation and maintenance of its facilities, conduct much-needed maintenance and improvement projects, and strategically reduce its budget for continued quality community service.
