The Genesee County Parks are widely utilized as accessible and inexpensive recreational and nature opportunities for local residents, and attendance in most facilities has either held constant or increased despite the recent critical economic conditions. This grant will enable the grantee to continue regular operation and maintenance of county park facilities, conduct much-needed maintenance and improvement projects, and strategically reduce its budget while maintaining quality community service.

title: General Purposes
description: Genesee County Parks & Recreation Commission has been dedicated to providing the residents of Genesee County with affordable, quality recreational and educational facilities. The Genesee County parks are widely utilized as accessible and inexpensive recreational and outdoor opportunities for local residents, and attendance in most facilities has either held constant or increased despite the recent critical economic conditions. This grant will enable the grantee to continue regular operation and maintenance of county park facilities, maintain current levels of programming, and support outreach and community engagement efforts.

title: General Purposes
description: Genesee County Parks & Recreation Commission has been dedicated to providing all the residents of Genesee County with affordable, quality recreational and educational facilities. The Genesee County parks are widely utilized as accessible and inexpensive recreational and outdoor opportunities for local residents, and attendance in most facilities has either held constant or increased despite the recent critical economic conditions. This grant will enable the grantee to continue regular operation and maintenance of county park facilities, current levels of programming, and outreach and community engagement efforts.

title: General Purposes
description: The Genesee County Parks & Recreation Commission is dedicated to providing all residents of Genesee County with affordable, quality recreational and educational facilities. The Genesee County parks are widely utilized as accessible and inexpensive recreational and outdoor opportunities for residents, and attendance in most facilities has either held constant or increased despite the recent critical economic conditions. This grant increase will support continued operation and maintenance of county park facilities, including designated City of Flint parks; ongoing community engagement; and extension and expansion of the cooperative work between the City of Flint and Genesee County Parks & Recreation Commission. The educational activities and opportunities to increase physical activity provided through parks programs and facilities in Flint are important strategies to mitigate the potential effects of lead exposure.

title: General Purposes
description: Genesee County Parks & Recreation Commission has been dedicated to providing all the residents of Genesee County with affordable, quality recreational and educational facilities. The Genesee County parks are widely utilized as accessible and inexpensive recreational and nature opportunities for local residents, and attendance in most facilities has either held constant or increased despite the recent critical economic conditions. This grant will enable Genesee County to continue regular operation and maintenance of county park facilities, conduct much-needed maintenance and improvement projects, and strategically reduce its budget for continued quality community service.

title: Civil Society Summit
description: The program goal is to support new areas of cooperation between civil society organizations in the United States and Russia. The grant will support the participation of American and Russian rights activists in a civil society summit to run in parallel with the official meeting of Presidents Obama and Medvedev in July 2009. In addition to a human rights and rule of law component, the summit will involve specialists in press and new media, community development, youth empowerment and education, public health, and environment. Conference participants will identify issues and areas of common interest in which they can share experiences in order to engage cooperatively over the coming years. Established in 1962, the Center for Strategic & International Studies is a nonprofit, public policy research organization with expertise on a wide range of defense and security, regional stability, and transnational issues and challenges.

title: Truth in Translation Project - Documentary Film
description: The project goals are to support the development and distribution of a film about the play “Truth in Translation” and to produce an educational archive that will accompany the final version of the film. During the next 12 months, Michael Lessac, the play’s creator and a filmmaker, will work with film editors to create a feature-length film that weaves together the play’s narrative and the impact of the play on audiences and communities where it was performed. With this film, the “Truth in Translation” project will become not only a theater piece about South Africa’s struggle to come to grips with its past, but a broader narrative about similar struggles around the world in very different contexts and how people can learn from and be inspired by situations that are very different from their own. Colonnades Theatre Lab, Inc., will work with a commercial distributor to release the film. The grantee was founded by Michael Lessac in 1973 in New York City as a developmental center for theater and film.

title: Summer Youth Program
description: The purpose of the grant is to provide a nutrition, fitness, and wellness summer camp for elementary school students in the Flint community. The camp was designed to complement the academic day camp program offered by the Flint Community Schools and provide students with a holistic, healthy living program. This three-week program administered by the City of Flint is a collaboration of several youth-serving entities, including the Crim Fitness Foundation and the CANUSA Association.

title: Technology Upgrade
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Flint District Library serves as a resource for research, education, enrichment, and entertainment to residents of the city of Flint and Genesee County. The library has been an asset to the Flint area community for over 50 years and currently has over 62,000 cardholders. The library provides free access to a collection of 432,000 books, audio, video, and subscriptions as well as high-speed wired and wireless Internet access, expert assistance, and computer literacy training. During the grant period, the Flint District Library will enhance and expand its services to both adults and children by replacing some technological systems including the automated catalog and check-out, telephone and voicemail, and pay-for-print and library card systems. In addition, the library will create a children’s computer-assisted literacy station in each of its four locations.

title: Flint Farmers Market Parking Lot
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: Seven years ago, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation took over the management of the Flint Farmers Market. During that time, the corporation and its supported organization, the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, have upgraded the facilities, added vendor variety, increased advertising, and expanded programs for low-income customers. The market is a countywide destination, and during the summer, it is not uncommon for 5,000 customers to visit on any given Saturday. During the grant period, the grantee will continue making improvements to the Flint Farmers Market by repairing the parking lot, which has deteriorated from consistent usage over time.

title: General Purposes
description: GreatNonprofits is a new nonprofit organization whose mission is to promote greater nonprofit excellence through feedback and transparency, to help inspire and inform prospective donors and volunteers, and to enable nonprofit organizations in the United States, regardless of their marketing ability or budget, to get their message out to the public. The grantee has recently launched a Web site and syndicated database that enables people who have had direct experience with a nonprofit to share their opinions about nonprofits. It is the first and largest source of stakeholder reviews about nonprofits which is freely available online. Reviews are posted by nonprofits’ clients, volunteers, donors, partners, professionals in the field, or members of the general public. After a pilot testing phase in Pittsburg and San Francisco, GreatNonprofits is expanding the service to a national level by providing their nonprofit reviews functionality to the Web sites of GuideStar, Network for Good, Hands On Network, and others.

title: Organizing Apprenticeship Program
grantee: Bend the Arc: A Jewish Partnership for Justice
description: The recruitment and training of professional organizers is among the most commonly identified barriers to the growth of community organizing. In particular, organizing groups articulate a strong interest in identifying and hiring organizers who reflect and are knowledgeable about the diverse communities in which they work, including diverse faith communities. In response to this need, Jewish Funds for Justice has launched an interfaith organizing apprenticeship program. This grant will provide partial support for this initiative.

In particular, organizing groups articulate a strong interest in identifying and hiring organizers who reflect on and are knowledgeable about the diverse communities in which they work, including diverse faith communities. In response to this need, Bend the Arc: A Jewish Partnership for Justice has launched an interfaith organizing apprenticeship program. This grant will provide partial support for this initiative.

grantee: Bend the Arc: A Jewish Partnership for Justice

In response to this need, Jewish Funds for Justice proposes to launch an interfaith organizing apprenticeship program. This grant will provide partial support for the first year of this initiative.

title: Common Core Standards: Implications for Education Reform and Expanded Learning Opportunities
grantee: National Governors Association Center for Best Practices
description: This grant will support the National Governors Association Center for Best Practices in bringing together key stakeholders to consider ways that states can expand access to effective afterschool programs to better ensure students have access to opportunities needed to meet the academic expectations being defined in the Common Core Standards Initiative. Led by the National Governors Association Center for Best Practices and the Council of Chief State School Officers, 48 states and territories have agreed to join the Common Core Standards, an initiative to develop common college- and career-ready standards that states can voluntarily adopt. This grant will support: 1) four policy forums on the implications of common core standards for education reform and afterschool; 2) three policy papers based on information from these forums; 3) conference calls and conferences to build knowledge in governors’ offices; and 4) technical assistance to state leaders implementing the common core standards that will help them utilize afterschool to achieve educational outcomes.

title: South Dakota Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support South Dakota Voices for Children which coordinates the South Dakota Statewide Afterschool Network. The network seeks to further improve the sustainability and quality of afterschool programs by securing state-dedicated funding for afterschool programs. In addition to continuing the network’s core work to advance afterschool in South Dakota, it will complete a multiyear project to support the advancement of learning for students beyond the school day by: 1) developing a policy proposal for a dedicated state afterschool funding stream; 2) promoting public awareness about the gaps in afterschool programming due to lack of funding and the benefits of greater access for children and families; and 3) increasing geographical access to quality afterschool programs in underserved areas.

title: South Dakota Statewide Afterschool Partnership
description: This grant to the Young Men’s Christian Association of Rapid City, Inc., will support partnership development among afterschool stakeholders in South Dakota and will enable the establishment of a cohesive statewide afterschool network. The grantee will bring together a diverse group of key decisionmakers and supports around issues impacting afterschool and summer learning programs. Through this South Dakota Statewide Afterschool Partnership grant, the grantee will hold a partner convening on afterschool and develop a comprehensive framework to expand afterschool opportunities in South Dakota.

title: South Dakota Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant to the YMCA of Rapid City will support the development of the South Dakota Statewide Afterschool Network to continue to build an afterschool and summer learning system that improves outcomes for children and youth through school-based or school-linked afterschool programs. Over the next three years, the network will build a statewide coalition in support of afterschool programs and coordinate a unified vision to inform policy and quality afterschool initiatives. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) hosting an annual summit for the afterschool field and partners in South Dakota; 2) increasing partnerships and quality initiatives in support of afterschool programs; and 3) developing a toolkit and self-assessment on best practices.

title: South Dakota Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support EmBe, which coordinates the South Dakota Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships, and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) create a State of Afterschool in South Dakota’s report; 2) develop an afterschool Quality Rating Improvement System and self-assessment tool; 3) support hands-on STEM activities and programs throughout the state; and 4) support the development and distribution of the new afterschool program content in collaboration with the Foundation’s thematic partners.

title: South Dakota Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support South Dakota Voices for Children in its efforts to develop the South Dakota Statewide Afterschool Network. The grantee seeks to create a sustainable structure that is focused on advocacy and policies that ensure afterschool opportunities for all of South Dakota’s school-aged youth, support the development and growth of the structure through networking, and support statewide systems to ensure that programs are of high quality. The grantee will systematically organize, mobilize, and communicate with afterschool stakeholders to advocate for increased funding and support for afterschool programs at the local, state, and national levels. This grantee is the eighth cohort of Mott-funded, statewide afterschool networks.

title: Foundations for Education Excellence
description: This grant increase will support the Foundation Center in its efforts to provide education funders the most up-to-date and relevant information about funding within the federal American Recovery and Reinvestment Act. Specifically, this increase will allow the Foundation Center to: 1) manage project administration and coordination; 2) perform maintenance, updates, and create new features for the Web portal; 3) collect, analyze, and summarize key research and recommendations around the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act; 4) host an average of two webinars or teleconferences per month through June 2010; 5) inform education funders through the ongoing delivery and expansion of its weekly newsletter; 6) hold a national conference for key stakeholders; and 7) develop and license access to a customized education edition of “Philanthropy In/Sight.”

title: Foundations for Education Excellence
description: This grant will continue to support the Foundation Center in its efforts to provide education funders with the most up-to-date, relevant, and in-depth information about education reform to help drive strategy development. Specifically, the Foundation Center will: 1) reorganize the content of the Web-based portal and add other relevant features to the site; 2) launch Philanthropy In/Sight – Education Edition, a custom-designed data visualization tool to help education grantmakers assess areas where their funding investments might have the greatest impact; 3) issue research briefs, shifting the focus of the e-newsletter to include more state information and update the research area of the Web-based portal; 4) support the Moving Forward conference by providing statistical information on education-related funding; and 5) hold a monthly series of teleconferences and webinars during the coming year that will focus on issues of most concern to education grantmakers working on long-term reform efforts.

title: Foundations for Education Excellence
description: This grant will support the Foundation Center in its efforts to help education grantmakers and other stakeholders make informed decisions about how to maximize and leverage public and private dollars to support education. This grant will support maintenance of a Web-based portal that serves as a knowledge hub. It will also support creation of an E-newsletter, two to three Webinars and teleconferences, and development of two reports on education reform topics of interest to grantmakers. This project will foster more funding and interest in education reform and facilitate greater collaboration between public, private, and nonprofit entities working toward shared education reform policies.

title: Foundations for Education Excellence
description: This grant will support the Foundation Center in its efforts to provide education funders the most up-to-date and relevant information about funding within the federal American Recovery and Reinvestment Act. Specifically, this grant will provide support to the grantee to develop and maintain a Web-based platform that would serve as a central hub of valuable information and knowledge for education funders seeking information, news, and knowledge focusing on education reform, with special emphasis on the four priority areas outlined in the education portion of the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act. This project will promote shared understanding among stakeholders focused on education reform and help maximize the use of public and private dollars.

title: Addressing Achievement Gaps Symposium "After the Bell Rings: Learning Outside of the Classroom and Its Relationship to Student Academic Achievement"
description: This grant will support the Educational Testing Service in its effort to educate scholars, policymakers, and practitioners on leading research, practice, assessment, and ideas for public policy related to supplementary education, including afterschool. Funding will support the grantee’s 12th annual Addressing Achievement Gaps Symposium titled, “After the Bell Rings: Learning Outside of the Classroom and Its Relationship to Student Academic Achievement”. The symposiums identify and address important complex education issues that are most challenging to educators, researchers, and policymakers and provide information and ideas for improvement to attendees from around the United States and the world.

title: Lessons for Tomorrow Workshops and Conference
description: This grant provides partial support to Partners for Democratic Change for a conference and workshops examining model programs and best practices in the fields of international development, democracy building, conflict resolution, and change management. The goal is to encourage governments, policymakers, donors, and practitioners to utilize lessons learned in developing improved, more effective international development policies and strategies for the 21st Century. These activities will celebrate and mark the 20th anniversary of Partners for Democratic Change, an international nongovernmental organization committed to building sustainable local capacity to advance civil society and a culture of change and conflict management worldwide.

title: Regulating Speculation
grantee: Institute for Agriculture and Trade Policy
description: The United States is considering the development of a carbon trading market as a mechanism to address climate change. Given the fact that the carbon emissions permits for such a trading system are considered a commodity like corn or wheat, the ability of the United States commodity futures system to monitor a carbon trading market in the United States has been called into question. In the United States and Europe, there are now efforts to strengthen the regulation of commodity futures markets to address both the problems of speculation in this market as well as the implications of the United States developing a carbon market. Over the last grant period, the Institute for Agriculture and Trade Policy has provided information and analysis that has allowed for a more informed discussion of the commodity markets. In this next grant period, it will work with national and international nongovernmental organizations as well as researchers and regulators to develop proposals to regulate commodity markets, with particular focus on impacts of a potential global carbon market.

title: Regulating Speculation
grantee: Institute for Agriculture and Trade Policy
description: Carbon trading has continued to be the focus for providing financing to address climate change. Given the fact that the carbon emissions permits for such a trading system are considered a commodity like corn or wheat, the ability of the United States and European commodity futures system to monitor a carbon trading market has been called into question. In the United States and Europe, there are now efforts to strengthen the regulation of commodity futures markets to address the problems of speculation in this market. Over the last grant period, the Institute for Agriculture and Trade Policy provided information and analysis that allowed for a more informed discussion of the commodity markets and the nexus with carbon markets. In this next grant period, it will work with national and international nongovernmental organizations, as well as researchers and regulators to develop public comments on the rulemaking for commodity markets, with particular focus on impacts of a national carbon market.

title: Regulating Carbon Markets
grantee: Institute for Agriculture and Trade Policy
description: One of the key mechanisms that the United States is considering to address climate change is the development of a carbon trading system. Given the fact that the carbon emissions permits for such a trading system are considered a commodity like corn or wheat, the ability of the regulatory system to monitor a carbon trading system in the United States should be assessed. The global financial crisis and the commodity price spikes of 2008 highlighted the inadequacies of the financial regulatory system in the United States. To contribute to the policy discussions, the Institute for Agriculture and Trade Policy will document the risks of a deregulated carbon market; work with a nongovernmental organization coalition in the United States to ensure there is meaningful regulation of carbon trading markets; work with European organizations to advance a coordinated transatlantic response to commodity market speculation; and work with international nongovernmental organizations to ensure that the international climate change negotiations call for a well-regulated carbon trading market.

title: 30th Anniversary Benefit Gala
description: This grant will provide partial support to the Corporation for Enterprise Development’s 30th Anniversary Benefit Gala focused on “Creating the Future of Economic Opportunity”, as well as its inaugural national innovation summit. The anniversary benefit gala will recognize “champions” of the asset-building and enterprise development sectors, while the innovation summit will spotlight opportunities for innovation and investment in economic development, financial restructuring, healthcare, community and workforce development, education, and youth. The events will take place on October 29, 2009, and will provide an opportunity for leaders from all sectors to discuss the best ways to improve financial security for all Americans, especially those from low- and moderate-income households. Headquartered in Washington, DC, the Corporation for Enterprise Development is a longtime grantee of the Mott Foundation.

title: Creating Commercialization Opportunity at Community Colleges
description: The American Association of Community Colleges will use grant funds to implement a two-year demonstration that will help community colleges understand their potential to function as virtual business incubators, to spawn and foster new small business development opportunities in direct response to market needs and niche. In doing so, participating colleges will demonstrate ways for established business leaders and emerging small business entrepreneurs to forge productive, symbiotic relationships that stimulate the growth of new local businesses.

title: Creating Commercialization Opportunity at Community Colleges
description: The program goal of this grant to the American Association of Community Colleges is to execute a small demonstration that will help community colleges understand their potential to function as virtual incubators to spawn and foster new small business development opportunities in direct response to market need and niche. In doing so, participating colleges will demonstrate ways for mature business leaders and emerging small business entrepreneurs to forge productive, symbiotic relationships that stimulate the growth of new local businesses.

title: Creating Commercialization Opportunity at Community Colleges
description: During this time of economic stress, the purpose of this planning grant to the American Association of Community Colleges is to design a small demonstration that will help community colleges understand their potential to function as “virtual incubators,” to spawn and foster new small business development opportunities in direct response to market need and niche. In doing so, participating colleges will demonstrate ways for mature business leaders and emerging small business entrepreneurs to forge productive, symbiotic relationships that stimulate the growth of new local businesses.

title: Poverty Special Report
description: Over the last dozen years, a number of new ideas and strategies have emerged to fight poverty, evolving well beyond the cash support of the welfare era. Extending support to the working poor through refundable tax credits and other work supports, building programs to enhance the mobility of individuals to more supportive labor markets, helping families build a base of assets, and other initiatives are intended not only to lift households temporarily above the poverty line, but also to break the multigenerational cycle of poverty and build a platform for economic success. For its September 2009 issue, The “American Prospect” is preparing a special report highlighting many of these new approaches to poverty. This grant will support production of the special report, as well as its dissemination within the low-income advocacy community, among policymakers, and among relevant media outlets.

title: Public Attitudes on Financial Reforms
description: The mismanagement of risk by major financial firms and the ensuing financial crisis of 2008-2009 contributed to the loss of millions of jobs and homes and erased trillions of dollars in retirement savings. A coalition of more than 200 organizations was formed to support financial reform. The purpose of this grant to Public Interest Projects is to support public interest research to explore Americans’ understanding of the issues involved in the reform of financial regulations and then to disseminate that research to community organizations and advocates seeking a voice in the development of new policies.

title: Public Attitudes on Financial Reforms
description: The mismanagement of risk by major financial firms and the ensuing financial crisis of 2008-2009 contributed to the loss of millions of jobs and homes and erased trillions of dollars in retirement savings. A coalition of more than 200 organizations has formed seeking to support financial reform and understand public attitudes regarding such reform. The purpose of this grant to Public Interest Projects is to support research to explore Americans’ understanding of the issues involved in the reform of financial regulations.

title: Relocation Support
description: The European Foundation Centre is an independent membership association of foundations and corporate funders dedicated to promoting organized philanthropy in Europe and internationally. Since its founding in 1989, the European Foundation Centre has operated out of an office in Brussels, Belgium. As the organization grew, office space was also rented in the connecting building, and by the end of 2008, the grantee employed approximately 30 staff and interns who were spread evenly across the two buildings. In January 2009, a gas leak in the main building rendered it uninhabitable, and the entire staff had to move to the adjacent building. The grantee has identified new offices that better suit its needs; however, there are considerable unanticipated expenses associated with the move. This grant will assist the European Foundation Centre with its substantial relocation expenses.

title: Health Care Impact Study
description: In an effort to improve the health status of Genesee County residents and to improve the quality and cost-effectiveness of the healthcare delivery system, the Greater Flint Health Coalition will lead the Health Care Impact Subcommittee of the mayor’s local auto task force in a study to evaluate and address the impact of the automotive crisis on the community’s healthcare system. The study will establish and compare a pre-economic crisis baseline and the current picture of the healthcare system in Genesee County, as well as project future impacts, and develop a process to monitor and intervene.

title: Development of Multifunctional Social Center
description: The program goal is to increase public support for principles of human rights and civic activism in Russia. To this end, the Andrei Sakharov Foundation will continue efforts to create a public space for broad-based discussion and promotion of human rights and democratic thought. These will include both online and offline discussions, debates, and cultural events, with a growing focus on engaging young people on relevant issues. In 2010-2011, the grantee expanded its online presence, resulting in almost 10,000 viewers of its discussions posted online. Its campaign for a museum in Andrei Sakharov’s Moscow apartment spawned the youth Sakharov Movement which also campaigns to raise the profile of Andrei Sakharov as a uniquely Russian exponent of human rights and liberal values. Founded in 1993, the Andrei Sakharov Foundation works to promote the democratic ideals of Soviet dissident Andrei Sakharov and honor victims of totalitarian oppression.

title: Development of Multifunctional Social Center
description: The program goal is to increase public support for principles of human rights and civic engagement in Russia. To this end, the Andrei Sakharov Foundation will continue to create a public space for broad-based discussion and promotion of human rights and democratic thought. In addition to expert discussions, it will host theater productions, documentary photography exhibits, and other events. While a comprehensive fundraising strategy to engage individual donors will be developed, increased efforts will be made to disseminate discussions and events through a variety of online channels. In the period 2011-2013, the grantee expanded its network of online partners, resulting in over 10,000 people viewing its discussions online. Its human rights debate program “gogol.tv” was seen by over 90,000 viewers. Founded in 1993, the Andrei Sakharov Foundation works to promote the democratic ideals of Soviet dissident Andrei Sakharov and to honor victims of totalitarian oppression.

title: Development of Multifunctional Social Center
description: The program goal is to increase public understanding of and support for principles of human rights and civic activism in Russia. To this end, the Andrei Sakharov Foundation will undertake a series of complementary activities aimed at creating an independent public space for discussion and promotion of human rights, history, and democratic thought. These will include public discussions and debates focusing on key issues of rights protection and civic consciousness in contemporary Russia. A cinema club targeted at students will screen a variety of films on pertinent themes and provide an opportunity to promote further discussion with filmmakers and other experts. The foundation will use its exhibition space to curate public exhibits and events on issues of historical memory and contemporary human rights concerns. Founded in 1993, the Andrei Sakharov Foundation works to promote the democratic ideals of Soviet dissident, Andrei Sakharov, and honor victims of totalitarian oppression.

title: State Asset Coalitions Succession Planning Technical Assistance
description: Succession planning is a sound risk management practice, critical to ensuring the continued effectiveness of organizations, including coalitions, before and after leadership transitions. Since 1997, through its Executive Transitions program, the grantee has provided succession planning/leadership transition technical assistance to over 400 nonprofit organizations. This grant will enable the organization to deliver such services to the nine state asset policy coalitions the Mott Foundation currently supports. CompassPoint Nonprofit Services is a nonprofit organization whose mission is to increase the impact of Bay Area nonprofit, community-based organizations and the people who work and volunteer for them.

title: UNESCO Oliver Tambo Chair of Human Rights: Enhancing Participatory Development and Social Awareness Among Women and Youth at the Local Level
description: The UNESCO Oliver Tambo Chair of Human Rights, based at the University of Fort Hare in South Africa, was established through funding by UNESCO to advance human rights, respect for democratic values, peace, and social justice. Past support enabled the chair to train and support women and youth in the Nkonkobe region of the Eastern Cape province to meaningfully participate in local governance and decisionmaking processes that affect their lives. The training enabled these groups to explore emerging economic opportunities, especially through the municipal and other government processes and increased their chances to become employed. This grant will assist the UNESCO Oliver Tambo Chair of Human Rights to continue to empower women and young people to enhance their skills so that they can become self-reliant and self-sufficient. It will also expand the project to other areas within the Nkonkobe region and will raise awareness on human rights and how people can engage as active citizens for their basic needs to be realized.

title: UNESCO Oliver Tambo Chair of Human Rights: Enhancing Participatory Development and Social Awareness Among Women and Youth at the Local Level
description: The UNESCO Oliver Tambo Chair of Human Rights, based at the University of Fort Hare in South Africa, was established through funding by UNESCO to advance human rights, respect for democratic values, peace, and social justice. Past support enabled the chair to train and support women and youth in the Nkonkobe region of the Eastern Cape province to meaningfully participate in local governance and decisionmaking processes that affect their lives. The training enabled these groups to explore emerging economic opportunities, especially through municipal and other government processes and increased their chances of employment. This grant will assist the UNESCO Oliver Tambo Chair of Human Rights to continue to empower women and young people to enhance their skills so that they can become self-reliant and self-sufficient. The grantee will use lessons from prior years to strengthen the program and will conduct research and document the work to contribute to the knowledge on models of community engagement.

title: UNESCO Oliver Tambo Chair of Human Rights: Enhancing Participatory Development and Social Awareness Among Women and Youth at the Local Level
description: The UNESCO Oliver Tambo Chair of Human Rights, based at the University of Fort Hare in South Africa, was established through funding by UNESCO to advance human rights, respect for democratic values, peace, and social justice. This project builds on another Mott-funded project implemented by the chair entitled “Democratic Governance and Participatory Development at the Local Level”, which successfully brought together municipal and traditional leaders to work harmoniously within the Nkonkobe municipality. The project trained traditional and community leaders, municipal councilors, and community-based groups on various aspects of governance. This grant will help the chair to build the capacity of women and youth to meaningfully participate in local governance and decisionmaking processes that affect their lives. Through training, it will also enable them to take advantage of emerging economic opportunities and to access employment, in order to improve the quality of their lives.

title: Central European Forum
geographic_focus: Czech Republic, Hungary, Poland, Bulgaria, Romania, Slovakia
description: The project goal is to contribute to the debate about the results of the transformational processes that have been taking place in Central and Eastern Europe in the 20 years after the fall of the Berlin Wall and the future development prospects of the region and Europe as a whole. To this end, Project Forum will organize a series of online debates and educational public events, which will culminate in a two-day, international conference, entitled “The Central European Forum,” on November 17-18, 2009, in Bratislava, Slovakia. The grantee will follow up on the conference with a series of online publications and debates on issues raised during the conference. Established in 2006, the grantee promotes dialogue among civic activists, journalists, and academics on the issues of democracy and development in Central and Eastern Europe via a multilingual Internet portal and a number of social networking media tools.

title: Organizing Training in CEE
description: The project goal is to strengthen the capacity of nonprofits and communities in Central and Eastern Europe to use community organizing principles and techniques to engage community residents in addressing issues of common concern. To this end, the Center for Community Change in Washington, D.C., will support United States-based community organizers to provide training and advice to community leaders and nonprofits in Central and Eastern European countries and to consult on the development of a European network for community organizing. During the previous grant period, the center supported three training visits to the region by experienced community organizers. More than 150 people in six countries were trained in community organizing, and several important local initiatives were strengthened. The Center for Community Change is a long-established technical assistance provider with expertise in community organizing.

title: Organizing Training in CEE
description: The Center for Community Change is a technical assistance and training intermediary located in the United States. The organization has a long and successful history of providing training in the skills and disciplines of community organizing. The goal of this project is to strengthen the capacity of nonprofits and communities in Central and Eastern Europe to use community organizing principles and techniques to engage community residents in addressing issues of common concern.

title: Organizing Training in CEE
description: The Center for Community Change is a technical assistance and training intermediary located in the United States. The organization has a long and successful history of providing training in the skills and disciplines of community organizing. The goal of this project is to strengthen the capacity of nonprofits and communities in Central and Eastern Europe to use community organizing principles and techniques to engage community residents in addressing issues of common concern.

title: Organizing Training in CEE
description: The Center for Community Change is a long-established technical assistance provider with expertise in community organizing. This grant will provide support to an initiative seeking to train staff and leaders in Central and Eastern Europe in the arts and disciplines of community organizing. During the grant period, the grantee will organize three conferences to provide training in community organizing.

title: Partnership to Address Funding/Grantmaking Practices in South Africa
description: The South African Institute for Advancement promotes philanthropy in South Africa and assists civil society organizations to raise funds. This grant will support the grantee to conduct research on the funding practices of two state agencies, the National Development Agency and the National Lotteries Distribution Trust Fund. The project will explore ways in which civil society can collaborate with these institutions and inform their funding practices based on the development needs of the country. Research on the past practices of these institutions will be undertaken using evidence from organizations that have received funding from them. Examples of lotteries in other countries and what informs their practices will also be investigated and compared with the practices of the National Lotteries Distribution Trust Fund. The findings will be disseminated and used to advocate for improved funding practices by the state agencies.

title: Coverage of the Education Economic Stimulus Package
description: This grant will support Editorial Projects in Education, through “Education Week” and www.edweek.org, to provide in-depth coverage of the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act and offer analysis of the stimulus program’s implications on education for policymakers at every level of public education, from the federal government to local districts. Specifically, this grant will provide support to present: 1) breaking news of federal and state policy; 2) analysis guiding readers through the stimulus program’s rules and regulations; 3) articles on how the stimulus program is reshaping the education debate and setting the national education policy agenda; 4) coverage of specific initiatives as they develop at the state, district, and school levels; and 5) journalism tracking the expenditure of $100 billion in education aid. “Education Week” is the premier education publication and read by audiences such as policymakers, practitioners, advocates, and government officials.

title: Evaluation of New Day for Learning Sites
description: This grant will support WestEd in developing and conducting an evaluation of the New Day for Learning district-community partnerships that are implementing the elements outlined in the New Day for Learning report. The New Day for Learning framework builds on Mott’s afterschool work and focuses on providing a seamless learning system to improve student success that includes afterschool learning opportunities throughout the day, year-round and offered in multiple places throughout a community. These elements include expanding the definition of student success, using research-based knowledge about how students learn best, fostering collaboration, integrating various learning approaches and places, and providing new opportunities for leadership and professional development. The district-community partnerships include San Francisco; Providence, Rhode Island; Atlanta; Chicago; Charleston, South Carolina; Denver; Flint; Omaha; Peekskill, New York; and St. Paul. This project will provide the demonstration sites with immediate feedback and provide lessons learned to the field.

title: Black Male Donor Collaborative: Expanding Opportunity and Increasing Achievement Among Marginalized Males
grantee: Youth Sports of Northern New Jersey
description: This grant will enable Youth Sports of Northern New Jersey to identify proven practices that expand education and life opportunities for marginalized males. The grantee is a for-profit consulting firm that specializes in assisting nonprofit organizations to develop initiatives explicitly aimed at engaging males of color. Recommended support will enable the grantee to develop a series of strategy papers and link related efforts by funders, researchers, and practitioners, to help inform a potential investment strategy on supporting marginalized males.

title: Massachusetts Asset Building Coalition
grantee: United Way of Massachusetts Bay and Merrimack Valley
description: This grant provides support to the United Way of Massachusetts Bay and Merrimack Valley to advance support for programs, policies, and practices that help low- and moderate-income families build assets. Among other strategic objectives, support from the Mott Foundation will help enable the grantee to strengthen the Massachusetts Asset Building Coalition by increasing and diversifying its membership, developing and implementing a media and messaging strategy, and developing a public policy campaign. This is one of ten grants aimed at building the capacity of asset-building coalitions to effectively create an enduring infrastructure for asset-policy development across states.

title: General Purposes
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Buckham Fine Arts Project was incorporated in 1984 by a group of area artists who saw the need for an exhibition/performance venue in downtown Flint that would direct its creative attention to presenting unique and contemporary arts in all forms for the benefit of Flint and mid-Michigan. Over the past 26 years, more than 300 exhibitions of visual art; poetry readings; performance art events; and dance, music, and film presentations have taken place. Over 5,000 artists from all over Michigan have presented their work in the grantee’s gallery space. This grant will assist the grantee in continuing its monthly exhibitions, adding three more events per month, increasing fundraising efforts, continuing its quarterly newsletter, and building organizational capacity.

title: General Purposes
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Buckham Fine Arts Project was incorporated in 1984 by a group of area artists who saw the need for an exhibition/performance venue in downtown Flint that would direct its creative attention to presenting unique and contemporary art in all forms for the benefit of Flint and mid-Michigan. Over the past 27 years, more than 300 exhibitions of visual art; poetry readings; performance art events; and dance, music, and film presentations have taken place. Over 5,000 artists from all over Michigan have presented their work in the grantee’s gallery space. This grant will assist the grantee in continuing its monthly exhibitions, adding three more events per month, increasing fundraising efforts, continuing its quarterly newsletter, and building organizational capacity.

title: General Purposes
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant provides general purpose support for the Buckham Fine Arts Project, also known as Buckham Gallery. The grantee was incorporated in 1984 by a group of artists who saw the need for a contemporary gallery in downtown Flint. Over the past 30 years, the grantee has held more than 300 exhibitions of visual art, poetry readings, performance art events, dance, music, and film presentations. Buckham Gallery showcases local, regional, and international artists.

title: General Purposes
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant provides general purpose support for Buckham Fine Arts Project, also known as Buckham Gallery. The grantee was incorporated in 1984 by a group of artists who saw the need for a contemporary gallery in downtown Flint. Over the past 30 years, the grantee has held more than 300 exhibitions of visual art, poetry readings, performance art events, dance, music, and film presentations. Buckham Gallery showcases local, regional and international artists.
