initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant provides general purpose support for the Buckham Fine Arts Project, also known as Buckham Gallery. The grantee was incorporated in 1984 by a group of artists who saw the need for a contemporary gallery in downtown Flint. Over the past 30 years, the grantee has held more than 300 exhibitions of visual art; poetry readings; performance art events; and dance, music, and film presentations. Buckham Gallery showcases local, regional, and international artists.

title: General Purposes
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Buckham Fine Arts Project was incorporated in 1984 by a group of area artists who saw the need for an exhibition/performance venue in downtown Flint that would direct its creative attention to presenting contemporary art in all forms for the benefit of Flint and mid-Michigan, focusing on works and concepts that are not being provided by other area organizations. Over the past 25 years, more than 275 exhibitions of visual art; poetry readings; performance art events; and dance, music, and film presentations have taken place. Over 5,000 artists from all over Michigan have presented their work in the grantee’s gallery space. The state of Michigan, which historically has provided about one-third of the project’s operating support, eliminated its funding for 2010 due to state budget cuts. This grant will assist the grantee in continuing its regular schedule of events and provide funds to support efforts to broaden its base of donors, increase fundraising efforts, and stabilize its long-term financial situation.

title: Foundation Finances Project
description: This grant provides support to the Foundation Center for the purpose of expanding its database on the finances of almost 2,000 of the nation’s largest foundations and for building a foundation benchmarking tool. This work builds on the Foundation Expenses Project, a Mott-supported, multiyear collaboration between the Foundation Center, the Urban Institute, and GuideStar. Through the Foundation Finances Project, the grantee will build upon that data and analysis to issue and disseminate a variety of informative, updated reports; create a flexible tool to enable grantmakers to benchmark themselves against their peers; and provide custom searches and database sets for associations of grantmakers. The Foundation Center is a national nonprofit service organization dedicated to fostering public understanding of the foundation field by collecting, organizing, analyzing, and disseminating information on foundations, corporate giving, and related subjects.

title: Flint 21st Century Community Policing
description: The City of Flint is facing a significant public safety challenge. Crime and violence are increasing across the city, while the city’s budget crisis has caused a simultaneous reduction in the police force and public safety resources. The mayor of Flint is addressing the issue by reviving community policing strategies in collaboration with the Michigan State University School of Criminal Justice. This renewal grant will support the second year of the Flint 21st Century Community Policing project.

title: Flint 21st Century Community Policing
description: The City of Flint continues to face a significant public safety challenge. Crime and violence across the city remain high, while the city’s ongoing budget crisis has caused a simultaneous reduction in the police force and public safety resources. The City of Flint’s emergency manager has outlined a public safety plan that aims to address public safety issues in Flint. Grant funding will support the implementation of that plan.

title: Flint 21st Century Community Policing
description: The City of Flint continues to face a significant public safety challenge. Crime and violence across the city remain high, while the city’s ongoing budget crisis has caused a simultaneous reduction in the police force and public safety resources. The City of Flint’s emergency manager has outlined a public safety plan that aims to address public safety issues in Flint. Grant funding will support the continued implementation of that plan.

title: Flint 21st Century Community Policing
description: The City of Flint continues to face major public safety challenges as it seeks to implement the public safety plan adopted in 2012. This grant increase advances implementation of the plan through support for continuation of community policing initiatives and development of best practices to assist the department in maximizing its limited resources.

title: Flint 21st Century Community Policing
description: The city of Flint is facing a significant public safety challenge. Crime and violence are increasing across the city, while the city’s budget crisis has caused a simultaneous reduction in the police force and public safety resources. Newly elected Mayor Dayne Walling is addressing the issue by reviving community policing and neighborhood foot patrols. The Flint 21st Century Community Policing effort will work in collaboration with the Michigan State University School of Criminal Justice to operate in all nine wards of the city to reduce all categories of crime through community policing efforts.

title: Repayable Grant to Promote Health and Fitness in Elementary Schools
description: The Crim Fitness Foundation has entered into a partnership with the Michigan Governor’s Council on Fitness and the Flint Community Schools to implement a fitness and nutrition program for elementary school children in the Flint Community Schools. The Physical Education and Nutrition Education Working Together program provides curricula, activities, supplies, nutrition education, and teacher professional development and training. This grant increase will allow the grantee to run this program and access state and federal funds.

title: Repayable Grant to Promote Health and Fitness in Elementary Schools
description: The Crim Fitness Foundation has entered into a partnership with the Michigan Governor’s Council on Fitness and the Flint Community Schools to implement a fitness and nutrition program for elementary school children in the Flint Community Schools. The Physical Education and Nutrition Education Working Together program provides curricula, activities, supplies, nutrition education, and teacher professional development and training. This renewal grant will allow the grantee to administer this program and access state and federal funds.

title: Repayable Grant to Promote Health and Fitness in Elementary Schools
description: The Crim Fitness Foundation has entered into a partnership with the Michigan Governor’s Council on Fitness and the Flint Community Schools to implement a new fitness and nutrition program for elementary school children in the Flint Community Schools. The Physical Education and Nutrition Education Working Together program will provide curricula, activities, supplies, nutrition education, and teacher professional development and training. This partially repayable grant will allow the program to leverage state and federal funds.

title: Race to the Top-Michigan - Michigan Department of Education
description: This grant will support the Council of Michigan Foundations in its effort to partner with Learning Point Associates to assist the Michigan Department of Education and the Governor’s Office in the development of applications and related work for the Race to the Top federal grant competition for states. Specifically, the grant funding will support the development and/or implementation of four initiatives including: the Michigan Integrated Education Reform Plan; applying for Race to the Top funding; state and local Race to the Top policy evaluation; and support to districts applying for competitive funds. If federal funding is awarded, it is predicted that this plan will jump-start Michigan’s economy with a cadre of college- and career-ready graduates as well as position the state as an education reform leader in a new age.

title: Clean and Green Partnership
description: This grant will support the Clean and Green Partnership at the Genesee County Land Bank Authority. With about 18,000 abandoned properties in the city of Flint, many owned by the land bank, the city of Flint and the land bank are working cooperatively to more efficiently clean and maintain these properties. In addition to mowing weeds and removing trash from vacant lots, the grantee is boarding and securing abandoned buildings, completing minor renovations to houses, and preparing lots for urban gardening. While federal funds have been secured to allow the land bank to hire workers to clean up and maintain these properties, additional equipment is needed to allow them to double their workforce and the number of properties they can maintain. The grantee will hire over 100 displaced and unemployed workers for this project.

title: Intermodal Project
description: Economic development efforts in Genesee County have recently focused on the potential of intermodal projects to create jobs and stimulate economic growth. An intermodal project seeks to create efficiencies by combining the transportation infrastructure with the trade and logistics industry. With an intermodal facility at Bishop International Airport recently completed, the next effort led by the Genesee Regional Chamber of Commerce and its supporting organization, the Genesee Area Focus Fund, is to create a truck-to-rail intermodal project at a brownfield site in the city of Flint.

title: Growing Role of Brazil in Latin America
description: This project supports IPS-Inter Press Service in Montevideo, Uruguay to increase the quality and quantity of journalistic coverage of infrastructure and energy issues in South America and globally. This project will pay particular attention to exploring the role that Brazil is playing in large-scale investments in transport and power generation infrastructure across the region. The grantee is a global news agency operating in over 100 countries, working in Latin America for four decades, and has a network of journalists reporting from every country in the region.

title: Growing Role of Brazil in Latin America
description: This project supports the IPS-Inter Press Service in Montevideo, Uruguay to increase the quality and quantity of journalistic coverage of Brazilian development finance of energy and infrastructure in South America and globally. This project will focus on exploring the role that Brazil is playing in large-scale investments in energy through its national development bank and in the emerging development bank of Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa. IPS-Inter Press Service is a global news agency operating in more than 100 countries that has been working in Latin America for four decades and has a network of journalists reporting from every country in the region.

title: Growing Role of Brazil in Latin America
description: This project supports the Inter-Press Service in Montevideo, Uruguay to increase the quality and quantity of journalistic coverage of Brazilian, and increasingly Chinese, financing of energy and infrastructure in South America and globally. This project will continue to pay particular attention to exploring the role that Brazil plays in large-scale energy investments through its national bank and the New Development Bank founded by Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa. IPS-Inter Press Service is a global news agency operating in more than 100 countries that has been working in Latin America for four decades and has a network of journalists reporting from every country in the region.

title: Growing Role of Brazil in Latin America
description: This project supports the IPS-Inter Press Service in Montevideo, Uruguay to increase the quality and quantity of journalistic coverage of energy and infrastructure development finance in Brazil and South America. This project will focus on raising public awareness of the social and environmental impacts of large-scale energy finance versus the opportunities and benefits of financing renewable energy for sustainable development. IPS-Inter Press Service is a global news agency operating in more than 100 countries and has been working in Latin America for more than 50 years with a network of journalists reporting from many countries in the region.

title: Growing Role of Brazil in Latin America
description: This project supports IPS-Inter Press Service in Montevideo, Uruguay to increase the quality and quantity of journalistic coverage of infrastructure and energy issues in South America. This project will pay particular attention to exploring the role that Brazil is playing in large-scale investments in transport and power generation infrastructure across the region. IPS-Inter Press Service, a global news agency operating in over 100 countries, has been working in Latin America for four decades and has a network of journalists reporting from every country in the region.

title: Monitoring Infrastructure Investments in Argentina
location: Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires, Argentina
description: This grant will support Fundación Ambiente y Recursos Naturales to monitor the effective implementation of environmental sustainability, transparency, and public participation rules and policies in energy projects supported by international financial institutions, the Brazilian Development Bank, and other sources of public finance in Argentina. Information generated will be disseminated to policymakers, media, and the public with the goals of shaping policies for future sustainable energy investments and building networks with organizations across South America that are monitoring energy investments. The grantee is a nongovernmental, environmental organization based in Buenos Aires that has worked for the past 25 years to promote sustainable development through policy, law, and civic engagement.

title: Monitoring Infrastructure Investments in Argentina
location: Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires, Argentina
description: This grant will support Fundacion Ambiente Y Recursos Naturales to monitor the effective implementation of environmental sustainability, transparency, and public participation policies and regulations in energy projects supported by international financial institutions, and Brazilian and Chinese development institutions, in Argentina. Information generated will be disseminated to policymakers, media, and the public with the goals of shaping policies for sustainable energy investments and building networks with organizations across South America that are monitoring energy investments in the region. The grantee is a nongovernmental environmental organization based in Buenos Aires that has worked for the past 25 years to promote sustainable development through policy, law, and civic engagement.

title: Monitoring Infrastructure Investments in Argentina
location: Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires, Argentina
description: This grant will support Fundacion Ambiente y Recursos Naturales to monitor the effective implementation of environmental sustainability, transparency, and public participation policies and regulations in energy projects supported by international financial institutions, and Brazilian and Chinese development institutions, in Argentina. Information generated will be disseminated to policymakers, media, and the public with the goals of shaping policies for sustainable energy investments and building networks with organizations across South America. The grantee is a nongovernmental environmental organization based in Buenos Aires that has worked for the past 27 years to promote sustainable development through policy, law, and civic engagement.

title: Monitoring Infrastructure Investments in Argentina
location: Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires, Argentina
description: This grant will support Fundación Ambiente y Recursos Naturales to analyze current and proposed energy investments by international financial institutions in Argentina as well as national energy strategies. The project will monitor a set of high profile projects including hydroelectric energy, natural gas, biofuels, and renewable energy. Information generated on these projects will be disseminated to policymakers, media, and the public, with the goal of both improving existing projects and shaping policies for future sustainable energy investments. Fundación Ambiente y Recursos Naturales is a nongovernmental environmental organization based in Buenos Aires that has worked for the past 25 years to promote sustainable development through policy, law, and civic engagement.

title: Impacts of Investments of the Brazilian National Development Bank on Regional Sustainability
description: This renewal will support the second phase of a case study being conducted in an important watershed in South America, where the Brazilian Development Bank has significant investments in large energy and infrastructure projects. Specifically, the information generated from this study of the Belo Monte Hydroelectric Power Plant on the Xingu River, a main tributary to the Amazon River in the Amazon rainforest, will be used to engage the Brazilian Development Bank to improve compliance and safeguards of financing large energy and infrastructure projects. Instituto Socioambiental is a Brazilian public interest nonprofit organization focused on integrated solutions to environmental and social problems in the region. This case study will build on decades of fieldwork and relationships with communities and key organizations in the region.

title: Impacts of Investments of the Brazilian National Development Bank on Regional Sustainability
description: This renewal grant will support public oversight and scientific monitoring of environmental and social impacts of energy and infrastructure investment by the Brazilian National Development Bank in the Amazon rainforest. Specifically, the project will build upon knowledge and relationships created previously from case studies and monitoring of the Belo Monte hydroelectric power plant in the Xingu basin of the Brazilian Amazon. The Instituto Socioambiental is a Brazilian public interest nonprofit organization focused on integrated solutions to environmental and social challenges in the region. This project renewal will support consolidation of fieldwork to build a scientific baseline of information regarding the impacts of the Belo Monte project on biodiversity, aquatic species, and local forest-dependent communities.

title: Impacts of Investments of the Brazilian National Development Bank on Regional Sustainability
description: The Brazilian National Development Bank is the main public financier of one of Brazil’s largest hydroelectric projects, located in the Xingu Basin of the Brazilian Amazon. The project, Belo Monte, is emblematic of large-scale energy development in the region and the focus for monitoring environmental and social impacts of energy and infrastructure investment. This grant increase to Instituto Socioambiental will support the systemization and publication of geo-referenced mapping and population data on aquatic species in an Atlas of the project’s impacts.

title: Impacts of Investments of the Brazilian National Development Bank on Regional Sustainability
description: This renewal will support ongoing scientific monitoring of environmental and social impacts of energy and infrastructure investment by the Brazilian Development Bank in the Amazon rainforest, with a specific focus on compliance with social and environmental standards for the Belo Monte hydropower project. The Instituto Socioambiental is a Brazilian public interest nonprofit organization focused on integrated solutions to environmental and social challenges in the region. This project renewal supports the continuation of a monitoring program that is innovating policies and measures to mitigate the impacts of large-scale energy development projects.

title: Impacts of Investments of the Brazilian National Development Bank on Regional Sustainability
description: The Instituto Socioambiental is a Brazilian nonprofit organization focused on integrated solutions to environmental and social challenges in the Amazon region. This grant will support ongoing scientific monitoring of environmental and social impacts of energy and infrastructure investment by the Brazilian Development Bank in the Amazon rainforest, with a specific focus on compliance with social and environmental standards for the Belo Monte hydroelectric project on the Xingu River. Results of the independent monitoring will contribute to the development of a water management system to mitigate the social and environmental impacts derived from the deviation of up to 80 percent of the Xingu River flows; development of reparation plans for impacted river-dwelling communities forcibly evicted from their lands; and accounting of the social and environmental liabilities in the event of a sale of the project.

title: Impacts of Investments of the Brazilian National Development Bank on Regional Sustainability
description: This project will produce case studies on two important watersheds in South America, where the Brazilian National Development Bank has significant existing and planned investments in infrastructure and energy projects. The information generated by the case studies will inform a strategy for engaging the Brazilian National Development Bank in developing policies for sustainable investments and increasing transparency and accountability in its lending practices. The Instituto Socioambiental is a Brazilian public interest nonprofit organization formed to develop integrated solutions to social and environmental problems. This project will build on more than a decade of field work and relationships with other key environmental organizations and networks in the region.

title: General Purposes
description: The Community Development Foundation Western Cape was founded in 2007 to strengthen local giving and support the development of poor communities in the Western Cape province of South Africa. It improves the quality of life of poor people in various communities in the province by supporting initiatives aimed at recognizing the communities’ potential and assets and using them to meet their own social needs. The grantee enhances leadership capacity in targeted communities to create a force that is able to address community challenges and engage effectively with government and businesses. Support over the past two years assisted the grantee to make grants, provide training and mentorship support, host a multicountry peer learning initiative, foster emerging community foundations, strengthen its organizational structure and management systems, and document its work. This grant will support ongoing efforts to encourage local giving through various local initiatives, improve the grantee’s profile, and support a network that advances community philanthropy in Southern Africa.

title: General Purposes
description: The Community Development Foundation Western Cape was founded in 2007 to support community-based initiatives in the Western Cape Province of South Africa. It promotes local giving as a tool to respond to local needs and improve the quality of life in poor communities. The grantee strengthens local leadership, develops young people, and builds relationships with communities and businesses to build a culture of philanthropy in target communities. Support over the past two years enabled the grantee to build partnerships with local businesses, access resources to expand current initiatives, and create job opportunities for young people from poor communities. This grant will support the grantee to extend current initiatives to other communities, deepen efforts to promote local giving, strengthen its organizational structure and management systems, provide training and mentorship support to community-based organizations, and make small grants for community initiatives.

title: General Purposes
description: The Community Development Foundation Western Cape was established in 2007 to support communities in the Western Cape province in South Africa. It makes small grants to community-based organizations and implements programs that support marginalized people. The grantee supports women’s income-generating initiatives, builds local leadership, promotes a healthy environment, and develops young people. Past support has enabled the grantee to strengthen partnerships with local government in promoting food gardens, support initiatives that create employment for youth from poor communities, and support community-based environmental initiatives. This grant will allow the grantee to continue supporting community-based organizations, extend its work to other communities, and promote local giving. It will also support youth initiatives and women’s projects that create work opportunities and break the cycle of poverty in poor communities.

title: General Purposes
description: The Community Development Foundation of the Western Cape works to support the development of communities in the Western Cape province in South Africa. It was established in 2007 and builds the capacity of small community-based structures, promotes the development of young people, establishes women’s self-help initiatives, and makes small grants to community-based organizations. Past support enabled the grantee to establish community funds in several communities. Additionally, the grantee has supported initiatives that promote the development of youth, participated in learning events in the region, and supported other emerging community foundations. This grant will enable the Community Development Foundation of the Western Cape to continue implementing projects that encourage communities to improve their quality of life.

title: General Purposes
description: The Community Development Foundation Western Cape is a community grantmaker that was established in 2007. It was incubated by the Foundation for Community Work, a community development organization based in Cape Town, South Africa. The grantee supports community initiatives in the Western Cape province through making small grants, partnering with communities in implementing their programs, and building local philanthropy by encouraging giving circles and asset-building initiatives within communities. It also facilitates dialogue platforms for community members to share experiences and learn from each other in order to address various challenges affecting their communities. This grant will support the grantee to implement programs that encourage and enhance local giving within communities and to strengthen community efforts aimed at improving the quality of their lives.

title: Support to the Social Entrepreneurship Program
description: The Gordon Institute of Business Science, based at the University of Pretoria, was established in 1999 and has since grown into one of South Africa’s leading business schools. The Centre for Leadership and Dialogue at the Gordon Institute of Business Science works with leaders interested in social change. The centre hosts dialogues on complex issues facing South Africa and the world through the Network for Social Entrepreneurs. The network implements the Social Entrepreneurship Program and other programs that inspire leaders to think creatively about solutions to social problems. Past support from Mott assisted with training and facilitation of a series of dialogues on various topics related to social change and the creation of platforms for engagement and partnerships between nonprofits and businesses. This grant will support the grantee to continue hosting dialogues and seminars on topics related to building local philanthropy, raising the voice of South African civil society, and promoting an asset-based approach to community development.

title: Support to the Social Entrepreneurship Program
description: The Gordon Institute of Business Science was established in 1999 to provide high quality business and management education. Based at the University of Pretoria, the business school runs the Centre for Leadership and Dialogue and provides training to leaders interested in social change. The Network for Social Entrepreneurs, a division of the center, provides training on social entrepreneurship and related programs and offers dialogue platforms on a range of social issues. The programs examine complex issues of social and economic development and attract leaders of nonprofits, business, and government. Past support has enabled the network to host dialogue platforms that bring together all sectors of society to discuss topics related to social change. The network also deepened training on citizen-led development, hosted an online platform to make information accessible, and created spaces for sharing knowledge and resources. This grant will support the Centre for Leadership and Dialogue to continue to strengthen civil society through dialogues and seminars, promote local economies and citizen-led development, and provide spaces for civil society to explore philanthropic solutions to societal challenges.

title: Support to the Social Entrepreneurship Program
description: The Centre for Leadership and Dialogue at the Gordon Institute of Business Science develops leaders and hosts strategic dialogues to discuss the most urgent and complex challenges facing South Africa and the world. Over the last few years, the grantee has developed a reputation for excellence as one of South Africa’s leading centers for learning and debate in social entrepreneurship and nongovernmental organization leadership. This grant will support the centre’s Social Entrepreneurship Program to strengthen the leaders of South African nonprofits and enable them to lead vibrant and relevant institutions. The grantee will host dialogues and seminars on themes related to strengthening the voice of civil society; asset based, community-driven development; and building local philanthropy. It will also provide an online platform for networking among nonprofits, and for accessing materials and resources from around the world on nonprofit development.

title: Support to Provincial Advice Office Forums
grantee: National Alliance for the Development of Community Advice Offices
description: The National Alliance for the Development of Community Advice Offices was initiated in 2005 to strengthen and sustain the community advice office sector in South Africa. Advice offices provide free legal advice and related services to poor people to enable them to realize their socioeconomic and human rights. The aim of this project is to strengthen the voice of advice offices through collaboration and joint campaigns. Past support enabled the grantee to assist with the establishment of nine provincial forums, seven of which received technical and financial support to build cohesion among advice offices. This grant renewal will support the grantee to continue to provide technical and financial support to ensure that provincial forums assist advice offices to advance their causes. It will also assist the Mpumalanga and Northern Cape provincial forums to consolidate their leadership structures.

title: Support to Provincial Advice Office Forums
description: The Black Sash Trust is a human rights organization that promotes justice and equality in South Africa. The National Alliance for the Development of Community Advice Offices, a project of Black Sash, is an alliance of organizations committed to providing access to justice for poor and marginalized people. It works to ensure the sustainability of the community-based advice office sector. The grantee believes that advice offices play a crucial role in assisting poor people to access legal advice and related services to ensure that their human rights and dignity are upheld. This grant will build the leadership and management capacity of newly established provincial advice office forums, whose role is to coordinate advice offices at a provincial level. The forums will help mobilize support to build the capacity of advice offices in an effort to make them sustainable and accountable and will create relevant platforms for engagement between advice offices and other stakeholders.

title: Materials Development and Website Management for Paralegal Training
description: The Education and Training Unit focuses on democracy, development, and human rights education in South Africa. It specializes in training, facilitation, and materials development for community-based organizations, public servants, and public representatives. Past support assisted the Education and Training Unit to develop and disseminate a Paralegal Training Manual to community-based paralegals, advice workers, and community activists who provide legal advice and related services to poor people. The manual covers a range of subjects that concern poor people including consumer protection, housing, protection of children, labor law, sexual offenses, refugees, and asylum seekers. Over the next two years, the grantee will disseminate a revised paralegal training manual; train users of the manual; update materials online to cover new laws and other relevant topical information; and conduct research for the next edition of the manual, scheduled for release in 2015.

title: Materials Development and Website Management for Paralegal Training
description: The Education and Training Unit focuses on democracy, development, and human rights education in South Africa. It specializes in training, facilitation, and materials development for community-based organizations, public servants, and public representatives. Past support assisted the grantee to develop and disseminate a Paralegal Training Manual to community-based paralegals, advice workers, and community activists who provide legal advice and related services to poor people. The manual was made available both online and in hard copy, and covered subjects including consumer protection, land, housing, and family law. Over the next two years, the grantee will provide community advice offices and other community-based organizations with simple, accurate, and up-to-date information on all aspects of the law that affect poor people. It will update and disseminate a revised Paralegal Training Manual, train users of the manual as requested, and continuously update materials online to cover new laws and other relevant topical information.

title: Materials Development and Website Management for Paralegal Training
description: Education and Training Unit focuses on democracy, development, and human rights education in South Africa. It specializes in training, facilitation, and materials development for community-based organizations, public servants, and public representatives. Past support allowed the grantee to update and disseminate a Paralegal Training Manual to community-based paralegals, advice workers, and community activists who provide legal advice and related services to poor people. The grantee also trained paralegals and youth activists on how to use the manual. The manual was made available both online and in hard copy, and covered subjects including environmental law, democracy and public participation, land, housing, and small business law. With this grant, the grantee will continue printing and disseminating the paralegal manual, keeping the website up to date, training paralegals and other civil society groups on how to use the manual, and doing research for the next edition of the manual.

title: Materials Development and Website Management for Paralegal Training
description: The Education and Training Unit focuses on democracy and development in South Africa. It specializes in training, facilitation, and materials development for community-based organizations, public servants, and public representatives. This grant will assist the grantee to develop and disseminate training and resource materials for community-based paralegals, advice workers, and community activists who provide legal advice and related services to poor people. The materials will cover a range of subjects that concern poor people including consumer protection, housing, protection of children, labor law, sexual offenses, refugees, and asylum seekers. The grantee will distribute printed manuals to deserving organizations that do not have access to the Internet and will make the materials available online free of charge through its Web site. Over the next two years, the grantee will continue to update the materials to cover new laws and other relevant topical information.

title: Technical Support and Dialogue Platform
description: SGS Consulting is based in Johannesburg, South Africa, and has been in operation for over 10 years. It has provided consultation services to a wide range of organizations, including various United Nations agencies, regional economic commissions across Africa, civil society organizations, and bilateral and multilateral agencies. The grantee’s assignments have focused on HIV/AIDS, as well as planning, strategy, and capacity development. With Mott support, the grantee will provide organizational development and other technical assistance to civil society organizations that work within the themes of building philanthropy and providing access to justice for poor people.

title: Technical Support and Dialogue Platform
description: SGS Consulting is a for-profit consultancy firm based in Johannesburg, South Africa, and has been in operation for over 15 years. It has provided consultancy services to organizations including United Nations agencies, regional economic commissions across Africa, civil society organizations, and bilateral and multilateral agencies. The Technical Support and Dialogue Platform project was initiated in 2010 to provide technical support to Mott Foundation grantees in South Africa and offer them opportunities to convene around issues of common interest. Past support enabled the grantee to provide organizational development and other institution building support to civil society organizations that work within the themes of building philanthropy and providing access to social justice for poor people. Over the next year, the grantee will continue to support organizations that work in these sectors to network, dialogue on topical and relevant issues, and improve their delivery of programs. It will also engage government, the private sector and academic institutions to explore linkages with nonprofit organizations in the delivery of development programs.

title: Technical Support and Dialogue Platform
description: SGS Consulting is a consultancy firm based in Johannesburg, South Africa, and has been in operation for over 15 years. The grantee has provided consultancy services to organizations including United Nations agencies, regional economic commissions across Africa, civil society organizations, and bilateral and multilateral agencies. The Technical Support and Dialogue Platform project began in 2010 to provide technical support to civil society organizations in South Africa and offer them opportunities to convene around issues of common interest. Past support enabled the grantee to provide organizational development and other institution building support to civil society organizations including providing opportunities for them to network, hosting dialogues on topical and relevant issues, and assisting organizations to improve on their delivery of programs. The grantee also engaged government, the private sector, and academic institutions to explore linkages and collaborations with nonprofit organizations in the implementation of development programs. This grant will continue support to SGS Consulting to provide technical assistance to civil society organizations to deal with various institutional capacity challenges.

title: Technical Support and Dialogue Platform
description: SGS Consulting is based in Johannesburg, South Africa. It has provided consultancy services to organizations including various United Nations agencies, other multilateral agencies, civil society organizations, and private foundations. The Technical Support and Dialogue Platform project began in 2010 to provide technical support to civil society organizations in South Africa and offer them opportunities to convene around issues of common interest. Past support enabled the grantee to provide organizational development and other institution building assistance to civil society organizations working in the community advice office and philanthropy development sectors. Activities included providing opportunities for organizations to network, hosting dialogues on topical and relevant issues, commissioning research on areas of interest, and assisting organizations to improve on their delivery of programs. This grant will support the grantee to work with organizations active in the community advice office and philanthropy development fields to help them deal with various institutional capacity challenges and to facilitate growth in these fields.

title: Technical Support and Dialogue Platform
description: SGS Consulting is a consultancy firm based in Johannesburg, South Africa. It has provided consultancy services to organizations including various United Nations’ agencies, other multilateral agencies, civil society organizations, and private foundations. The Technical Support and Dialogue Platform project began in 2010 to provide technical support to civil society organizations in South Africa and offer them opportunities to convene around issues of common interest. Past support enabled the grantee to provide organizational development and other institution-building assistance to civil society organizations working in the community advice office and philanthropy development sectors. This grant increase will enable the grantee to support civil society organizations to strengthen their communications capacity.

title: Technical Support and Dialogue Platform
description: SGS Consulting provides consulting services to civil society organizations, private foundations, and multilateral agencies. The Technical Support and Dialogue Platform, a project of SGS Consulting, provides technical support and assistance to organizations working in the community advice office and philanthropy development sectors in South Africa. Past support enabled the grantee to support the growth of these sectors and provide opportunities for organizations to convene on topics of common interest. Activities included building cooperation between organizations working in the same areas, assisting organizations to improve on the delivery of their programs, and commissioning research on areas of interest. This grant will enable the grantee to work with organizations in the community advice office and philanthropy development sectors to help them build knowledge of their respective fields, deal with capacity challenges, and increase the flow of resources to enable growth and strengthening of organizations.

title: PolicyWorks for Philanthropy
description: PolicyWorks for Philanthropy is an initiative led by a consortium of six regional associations of grantmakers and managed by the Council of Michigan Foundations. The program’s goal is to build the capacity of regional associations’ staff and boards to engage policymakers in support of a vibrant and effective philanthropic sector. Since its launch in 2009, the initiative has raised awareness about the importance of engaging policymakers and begun to build the capacity of 20 regional associations of grantmakers to do so effectively. In 2011, grant funds will support the implementation of activities that will strengthen the capacity and catalyze increased action by at least 22 regional associations nationwide on public policies of interest to their members. The Council of Michigan Foundations is a membership association of grantmakers with the mission to enhance, improve, and increase philanthropy in Michigan.

title: PolicyWorks for Philanthropy
description: PolicyWorks for Philanthropy is a multiyear initiative of the Forum of Regional Associations of Grantmakers that seeks to build the capacity of its members’ staff, board, and volunteer leaders to engage policymakers in support of a vibrant and effective philanthropic sector. Since its launch in 2009, the initiative has strengthened the capacity of 20 regional associations to engage policymakers on public policies of interest to their members. Over the next two years, the initiative will continue to raise awareness, build capacity, and catalyze action of regional associations of grantmakers and their members to engage with policymakers. The Forum of Regional Associations of Grantmakers is a national network of 35 members that collectively represent more than 4,300 foundations, corporate giving programs, and other philanthropic organizations. PolicyWorks is a key part of the grantee’s long-term strategy to ensure that philanthropy is understood and appreciated by officials at all levels of government.

title: PolicyWorks for Philanthropy
description: PolicyWorks for Philanthropy is an initiative led by a consortium of six regional associations of grantmakers and managed by the Council of Michigan Foundations. The project’s goal is to build the capacity of regional associations’ staff and boards to engage policymakers in support of a vibrant and effective philanthropic sector. Since its launch in 2009, PolicyWorks has collected baseline data to confirm sufficient demand for the project; conducted an outreach campaign to recruit regional associations; and organized an awareness campaign targeting regional associations’ trustees and members promoting the value and benefits of proactively engaging policymakers. Grant funds will support the development and implementation of activities that will strengthen the capacity and catalyze increased action by 21 regional associations nationwide on public policies of interest to their members. The Council of Michigan Foundations is a membership association of grantmakers with the mission to enhance, improve, and increase philanthropy in Michigan.

title: Issue Lab
description: This grant will support the continued collaboration of the Foundation Center, a key nonprofit sector institution providing knowledge resources to both grantseekers and grantmakers, and IssueLab, a small nonprofit which electronically archives, distributes, and promotes research produced by the nonprofit sector. Since May 2010, the two organizations have collaborated on a number of projects of mutual interest. Over the next two years, the two organizations will produce collaborative tools that will enhance the ability to manage, provide free access to, and preserve the nonprofit sector’s knowledge assets. This, in turn, will determine the future relationship between the two organizations. Joint activities will include content integration and resource development for two main Foundation Center information resources, the consolidation of research collections, and the development of a vision and plan for next generation knowledge services for the nonprofit sector.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant supports the work of IssueLab, an organization which archives, shares, and advocates for broader mobilization of nonprofit knowledge. The grantee archives nonprofit research in a way that is optimized for search engine indexing across all listings; locates and archives hard-to-find research from smaller organizations; provides free and open online access to all research in its collection; archives work in 34 different issue areas enabling users to relate work across traditional issue silos; provides search tools that allow users to filter the collection on multiple dimensions; offers editorial and curatorial services that help users to summarize findings and understand specific fields of practice; makes extensive cross referencing available, enabling users to more easily find similar and related research; and advocates for the broad use of open licenses by nonprofits and foundations and the overall adoption of open access standards. In 2010, IssueLab will continue, expand, and improve this work.

title: Technical Assistance for Mexican Community Foundations
description: This grant will support an organizational, capacity building, technical assistance funding facility for members of the Alliance of Mexican Community Foundations. The U.S.-Mexico Border Philanthropy Partnership will competitively award small, technical assistance grants of between $1,000 and $5,000 for projects that advance the community foundations’ fundraising and resource development capacity, develop their boards, and improve their administrative and financial operations. The grantee will compile project results and report these back to the community foundations for their collective learning. This initiative is one of three programming components (the other two are leadership development and challenge grants for grantmaking and endowment building) being supported by a funder collaborative of the Inter-American, Kellogg, and Mott foundations created to support the development of Mexican community foundations. Established in 2002, the U.S.-Mexico Border Philanthropy Partnership is a bi-national membership organization whose goal is to strengthen and grow community philanthropy in the U.S.-Mexico border region.

title: General Purposes
description: The Michigan Unemployment Insurance Project recruits and trains law students to provide free assistance to unemployed workers who are filing unemployment claims and to those whose claims for unemployment benefits have been denied. The area of service is focused on Southeastern Michigan (including Genesee County), where a majority of Michigan’s jobless workers live. By assisting these individuals in obtaining unemployment insurance benefits, the organization helps struggling families, stressed communities, and Michigan’s economy.

title: General Purposes
description: The Michigan Unemployment Insurance Project recruits and trains law students to provide free assistance to unemployed workers who are filing unemployment claims and to those whose claims for unemployment benefits have been denied. By assisting these individuals in obtaining unemployment insurance benefits, the grantee helps struggling families, stressed communities, and Michigan’s economy. This grant increase will support the grantee’s expansion into Genesee and Ingham counties.

title: General Purposes
description: The Michigan Unemployment Insurance Project recruits and trains law students to provide free assistance to unemployed workers who are filing unemployment claims and to those whose claims for unemployment benefits have been denied. By assisting these individuals in obtaining unemployment insurance benefits, the grantee helps struggling families, stressed communities, and Michigan’s economy.

title: Michigan Unemployment Insurance Initiative
description: The Michigan Unemployment Insurance Initiative, a project of the Michigan League for Human Services, will provide advice and assistance on unemployment insurance to Michigan’s jobless workers in order to mitigate poverty among the unemployed, slow down mortgage foreclosures, reduce the number of jobless leaving our communities to find work elsewhere, and bring additional dollars into local economies.

title: Ensuring Healthy River Flows
description: American Rivers, an organization working throughout the United States, will assist conservation leaders in the Southeast to attend a national conference on how to protect and restore natural river flows. Such flows are necessary to support aquatic life, floodplains, wetlands, water supply, and recreational uses.

title: Ensuring Healthy River Flows
geographic_focus: South Carolina, Georgia, North Carolina, Alabama
description: Communities in the southeastern United States need reliable, cost-effective water supplies, while also maintaining healthy river flows, so that the region’s rich aquatic biodiversity is not put at risk. American Rivers, a national freshwater conservation organization with a strong presence in the region, will promote the adoption and implementation of policies that sustain river flows for human and ecological needs, advocate for water efficiency solutions, and encourage wise water use planning at the regional, state, and local levels. Working closely with regional, state, and local partner groups, the grantee will concentrate its efforts in four states — Alabama, Georgia, North Carolina, and South Carolina.

The grantee will concentrate its efforts in four states — Alabama, Georgia, North Carolina, and South Carolina — working closely with regional, state, and local partner groups.

title: Ensuring Healthy River Flows
geographic_focus: Alabama, South Carolina, Georgia, North Carolina
description: American Rivers, a national organization dedicated to protecting and restoring river ecosystems, has an active program in the southeastern United States. With these additional funds, the grantee will provide support to partner organizations that are working to promote healthy river flows and integrated water management practices.

title: Ensuring Healthy River Flows
geographic_focus: Alabama, South Carolina, Georgia, North Carolina
description: In the southeastern United States, it is necessary to secure sustainable water supplies for healthy aquatic ecosystems and adequate sources of fresh water for society. American Rivers, a national conservation organization with a strong presence in the region, will promote the adoption and implementation of policies that sustain river flows for human and ecological needs, advocate for water efficiency solutions, and encourage water conservation planning at the regional, state, and local levels. American Rivers works with partner organizations in Alabama, Georgia, North Carolina, and South Carolina.

title: Ensuring Healthy River Flows
geographic_focus: Alabama, South Carolina, Georgia, North Carolina
description: Even though the southeastern United States is often thought of as water-rich, it can be a challenge in the region to secure sustainable water supplies for healthy aquatic ecosystems and adequate sources of freshwater for society. American Rivers, a national conservation organization with a strong presence in the region, promotes the adoption and implementation of policies that sustain river flows for human and ecological needs, advocates for water efficiency solutions, and encourages water conservation planning at the regional, state, and local levels. The grantee works with partner organizations in Alabama, Georgia, North Carolina, and South Carolina. This renewal grant will allow American Rivers to continue this important work as the region faces ongoing and emerging water issues and challenges.

title: Ensuring Healthy River Flows
description: Communities in the southeastern United States need reliable, cost-effective water supplies while also maintaining healthy river flows so that the region’s rich aquatic biodiversity is not put at risk. American Rivers, a national freshwater conservation organization with a strong presence in the region, will promote the adoption and implementation of policies that sustain river flows for human and ecological needs, advocate for water efficiency solutions, and encourage wise water use planning at the regional, state, and local levels. The grantee will concentrate its efforts in three states — Georgia, North Carolina, and South Carolina — working closely with regional, state, and local partner groups.

title: Alabama Water Management Project
description: With this grant increase, the Alabama Rivers Alliance will enhance its outreach and education efforts in support of statewide water management policy reform. Special efforts will be made to build collaborative working relationships with nontraditional partners, such as agricultural and business groups.

title: Alabama Water Management Project
description: With more than 77,000 miles of rivers and streams, Alabama ranks sixth in the nation for the most continually flowing waterways and is a global hot spot of freshwater biodiversity. Despite the importance of the state’s water resources, Alabama lacks statewide water management policies that adequately address water withdrawals, diversions, and similar concerns. The Alabama Rivers Alliance, a statewide network of river groups and enthusiasts, will continue to lead a collaborative effort to build support for comprehensive water management policy reform. The grantee will also participate in related activities, such as the relicensing of hydropower dams and efforts to resolve interstate water use conflicts.

title: Alabama Water Management Project
description: With more than 77,000 miles of rivers and streams, Alabama ranks sixth in the nation for the most continually flowing waterways and is a global hot spot of freshwater biodiversity. Despite the importance of the state’s water resources, Alabama lacks statewide water management policies that adequately address water withdrawals, diversions, and similar concerns. The Alabama Rivers Alliance, a statewide network of river groups, will continue to lead an effort to build support for comprehensive water management policy reform. The grantee will also participate in related activities, such as the relicensing of hydropower dams and efforts to resolve interstate water use conflicts.

title: Alabama Water Management Project
description: Over the past two years, the Alabama Rivers Alliance, a statewide environmental organization, has made progress toward achieving a statewide water management policy, reforming hydropower operating licenses, and advancing other water management work in Alabama. With additional support from Mott, the grantee will continue to advocate for a statewide water management plan, collaborate with conservation partners to address interstate water conflicts, and monitor the development and implementation of major hydropower licenses.

title: Alabama Water Management Project
description: With more than 77,000 miles of rivers and streams, Alabama ranks sixth in the nation for the most continually flowing waterways and is a global hot spot of freshwater biodiversity. Despite the importance of the state’s water resources, Alabama lacks statewide water management policies that adequately address water withdrawals, diversions, and similar concerns. The Alabama Rivers Alliance, a statewide network of river groups and enthusiasts, will lead a collaborative effort to build support for comprehensive water management policy reform. The alliance will also participate in related activities, such as the relicensing of hydropower dams, efforts to resolve interstate water use conflicts, and discussions to promote voluntary water conservation measures at the local level.

title: General Purposes
description: National People’s Action is a network of grassroots organizations in low-income communities across the United States. The grantee provides training, technical assistance, and consultation to member organizations and participates on the national level in partnerships and coalitions working on issues related to economic opportunity. This general purpose grant will provide partial support for the organization’s core mission.

title: General Purposes
description: National People’s Action (formerly National Training and Information Center) is a network of grassroots organizations in low-income communities across the United States. The grantee provides training, technical assistance, and consultation to member organizations and participates on the national level in partnerships and coalitions working on issues related to economic opportunity. This general purpose grant will provide partial support for the organization’s core mission.

title: Federal Policy for Distressed Urban Cities
grantee: Initiative for a Competitive Inner City
description: This grant will enable the Initiative for a Competitive Inner City to construct a framework for developing a regional policy approach that addresses social and spatial equity in terms of economic development, opportunity, and well-being in the economically distressed urban areas within regions.

title: Replicating Successful Sector Employment Program
description: The purpose of this grant is to identify the components needed to successfully replicate sector employment initiatives. Specifically, CSR, Incorporated intends to examine how variations among successful programs relate to the programs’ effectiveness in achieving their outcomes. The goal is to identify the essential features of sector programs and under what circumstances they are most likely to succeed. The major product will be an implementation and replication guide that can be used by practitioners, policymakers, and funders to help inform new sector initiatives and strengthen existing efforts.

title: General Purposes
description: The Goodwill Association of Michigan was formed by the ten independent Goodwill organizations in the state in the early 1990s. The goal of the organization is to help each of the state’s Goodwill organizations increase collaboration and provide better services to people with disabilities and barriers to employment. This grant will allow the grantee to continue to serve the state’s Goodwill organizations and will allow it to develop a framework to provide greater workforce development services throughout the state.

title: General Purposes
description: Goodwill Association of Michigan was formed by the ten independent Goodwill organizations in the state in the early 1990s. The goal of the organization is to help each of the state’s Goodwill organizations to increase collaboration and to provide better services to people with disabilities and barriers to employment. This grant will allow the grantee to continue to serve the state’s Goodwill organizations and will allow it to develop a framework to provide better, more effective workforce development services throughout the state.

title: General Purposes
description: The Goodwill Association of Michigan was formed by the ten independent Goodwill organizations in the state in the early 1990s. The goal of the organization is to help each of the state’s Goodwill organizations to increase collaboration and to provide better services to people with disabilities and barriers to employment. This grant will allow the grantee to continue to serve the state’s Goodwill organizations and develop a framework to provide greater workforce development services throughout the state.

title: Building Green Energy and Technology Pathways
description: This grant will enable San Francisco State University to continue to develop an integrated high school and postsecondary career academy model on green energy and technology pathways. During the most recent phase of this effort, the grantee engaged regional stakeholders to develop the curriculum and tools necessary to implement a career and technical education-focused framework in nine schools in the Bay area where students are provided contextualized instruction, training, and credentialing in green technologies such as biofuels, solar, transportation, and green building. Mott funding will allow San Francisco State University to further develop this model by adding an online platform to assist students in linking classroom instruction with technical knowledge and field experience in the green sector.

title: Building Green Energy and Technology Pathways
description: This grant will enable San Francisco State University to develop an integrated high school and postsecondary career academy model focused on green energy and technology pathways. The goal of this effort is to create new green career pathways that offer a challenging, comprehensive program of study leading to postsecondary options, green apprenticeships, green jobs, and/or other careers in science and technology disciplines. Recommended support will allow the grantee to research and engage regional stakeholders to develop the tools and curriculum necessary to implement a green energy/technology and career and technical education school model.

title: Career Pathways Program
description: This grant will enable the Youth Connection Charter School to continue to develop and model a blended high school, postsecondary, and career training initiative entitled the Career Pathways Program. The program accelerates the progress of off-track students toward graduation, postsecondary matriculation, professional credentialing, and career track training over a three-year course of study. Currently, there are eight schools, serving nearly 900 students, piloting the Career Pathways Program. Recommended support will enable the grantee to further develop this model, which provides students with an opportunity to earn a high school credential and college credit focused on a career area.

title: Career Pathways Program
description: This grant will enable the Youth Connection Charter School to continue to develop and model a blended secondary, postsecondary, and career training initiative entitled the Career Pathways Program. The program provides dropouts and off-track students access to an accelerated and structured system of career-track opportunities as the context for high school learning and postsecondary education. Currently, there are eight schools serving 900 students piloting the program. Recommended support will enable the grantee to broaden its programmatic efforts to facilitate activities that enhance the model’s ability to better prepare students for postsecondary success.

title: Career Pathways Program
description: This grant will enable the Youth Connection Charter School to continue to develop and model a blended secondary, postsecondary, and career training initiative titled the Career Pathways Program. The program provides dropouts and off-track students access to an accelerated and structured system of career-track opportunities as the context for high school learning and postsecondary education. Currently, there are eight schools piloting the Career Pathways Program. Over the last year, 429 students earned their high school diploma, 110 students earned college credit via dual enrollment opportunities, and 46 earned industry/occupational certifications as a result of this effort. Recommended support will enable the Youth Connection Charter School to broaden its programmatic efforts to facilitate activities that enhance the model’s ability to better prepare students for postsecondary options and success.

title: Career Pathways Program
description: This grant will enable the Youth Connection Charter School to continue to develop and model a blended secondary, postsecondary, and career training initiative titled the Career Pathways Program. This program provides dropouts and off-track students access to an accelerated and structured system of career-track opportunities as the context for high school learning and postsecondary education. Currently, there are 14 schools, an increase from the initial five pilot sites in 2010, implementing the program. Recommended support will enable the grantee to broaden its efforts to embed the program across its 20-school network and facilitate activities to enhance the model’s ability to prepare students for postsecondary programs and success. Nearly 4,000 students will have access to the program.

title: Career Pathways Program
description: This grant will enable the Youth Connection Charter School to develop the Career Pathways Program. Founded in 1997, the grantee is a multisite alternative high school network that provides students a second chance to earn a high school diploma and prepare for higher education and the world of work. The Career Pathways Program is an effort to accelerate the progress of off-track students toward graduation, postsecondary matriculation, professional credentialing, and career track training. Recommended support will enable the grantee to pilot a model that provides students an opportunity to earn a high school diploma and college credit focused in a career area.

title: Technology and Afterschool
description: This grant will support Wireless Generation to develop ThirdSpace 2.0, the next edition of ThirdSpace, which was created to connect in-school and out-of-school educators. Building on the evaluation of the original ThirdSpace pilot, the grantee will develop ThirdSpace 2.0 to: 1) ensure the system is more user friendly for a wider audience; 2) increase the security and student privacy of the technology; 3) enhance the student assessment component; and 4) support new training options for educators. This project will result in a technology tool that is easier to use, adaptable to a variety of schools and programs, and scalable to support student learning and collaborative instruction to help students achieve success in school and in life.

title: ThirdSpace: Data-Driven Accountability in Afterschool
description: This grant will support Wireless Generation in conducting necessary research and design work to develop a system to measure student performance in afterschool programs that will complement the national Common Core Standards Initiative. Building upon the latest technology and the idea that afterschool programs often bridge the public space of school and the private space of home, the overall goal of the assessment tool is to advance a student assessment system that measures 21st century skills, such as the ability to work on a team, along with core academic skills. In so doing, the tool will help incentivize greater accountability in afterschool programs and in schools for raising student performance in both academic and nonacademic areas. This grant supports the discovery phase of the project and will: 1) identify a set of afterschool partners to pilot a test version of the tool called ThirdSpace; 2) select the most appropriate metrics of 21st Century skills to include in ThirdSpace; 3) address the challenges that in-school and afterschool educators will face in implementing an afterschool assessment system; 4) develop a plan for how to build ThirdSpace, including the duration and resources necessary after the discovery phase, and how the grantee will apply its existing Honeycomb data-display technology; and 5) engage funders, states, and districts to support and invest in the development of the ThirdSpace system.

title: Education Funders Strategy Group
description: This grant will support the National Public Education Support Fund in its efforts to help maximize philanthropy’s effectiveness in improving public education systems in the United States, from birth to career, through public policy reform. Specifically, this grant will allow the National Public Education Support Fund to: 1) provide a forum for leading education foundations to communicate and collaborate in leveraging systemic policy reforms; 2) facilitate communication between key federal policymakers and funders; 3) promote the development of a world-class education system in the United States by providing philanthropists and policymakers with an international perspective of policies and practices in top-performing countries; and 4) maximize the members’ philanthropic impact by facilitating joint action to achieve greater effectiveness at a lower cost to individual foundations.

title: Landscapes from the Age of Impressionism
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will support the Flint Institute of Arts’ Landscapes from the Age of Impressionism exhibit. The 38 Impressionism paintings from the Brooklyn Museum of Art’s permanent collection include many of the finest examples of mid-19th through early 20th-century French and American landscapes. Also on display were Impressionist and Post-Impressionist paintings from the institute’s permanent collection and other loaned artwork, which allowed the Flint Institute of Arts to fully illustrate this important period in the history of art, in both Europe and the United States. The exhibit opened on February 5, 2010, and ran through May 2, 2010.

title: Endowment Funds
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to the Community Foundation of Greater Flint will add to endowment funds established for the benefit of the community foundation, the Flint Cultural Center Corporation, the Flint Institute of Arts, and the Flint Institute of Music. These endowments will provide general operating support to these important community institutions. The grantee continues to serve a vital role in the charitable and nonprofit community in the Flint area by encouraging giving, as well as by providing grants and programs that improve the quality of life for all Genesee County residents and focus on critical issues in the community. The Flint Cultural Center offers a variety of programs; live performances; hands-on learning experiences; music, dance, drama, and art instruction; and hosts community events for area residents of all ages and backgrounds.

title: Membership and Administrative Support
description: This grant supports the membership and administrative costs of the Network of European Foundations for Innovative Cooperation, a nonprofit membership association based in Brussels. Its goal is to strengthen philanthropic cooperation among foundations, associations, and other nongovernmental organizations in Europe. The grantee manages a range of initiatives in which major European foundations collaborate on issues of youth empowerment, HIV/AIDS, citizen engagement, cultural policy development, integration and migration, religion and democracy, Roma education, and Europe’s role on global social issues. During 2011, a staff of two will manage and organize regular meetings of the board and the general assembly. The grantee currently has 13 members and engages many other foundations, public donors, and other types of philanthropic organizations in its projects.

title: Membership and Administrative Support
description: This grant supports the membership and administrative costs of the Network of European Foundations for Innovative Cooperation, a nonprofit membership association based in Brussels. Its goal is to strengthen philanthropic cooperation among foundations, associations, and other nongovernmental organizations in Europe. title: Youth Empowerment Partnership Programme
description: The project goal is to improve the lives of young people at risk through coordinated efforts and strategic alliances of actors from the public, private, and independent sectors. To this end, the Network of European Foundations for Innovative Cooperation will support the implementation of the Youth Empowerment Partnership Programme in 18 local communities in eight European countries by convening participating foundations, managing grant support from foundations and other donors, and building new partnerships to support the project’s activities. The project will also include creating a new management structure for the program to be in place by 2012. In 2010, a project team based in Berlin assisted local sites with intensive monitoring, evaluation, and documentation of outcomes; provided specific capacity building and technical support to local practitioners; organized transnational networking and exchanges for young people from the local sites and other stakeholders; and developed and disseminated information resources throughout the network. Based in Brussels, the grantee is a network of foundations that acts as a launching pad for new initiatives emphasizing innovative approaches to addressing social and political challenges facing Europe.

title: Youth Empowerment Partnership Programme
grantee: International Academy Berlin for Innovative Pedagogy, Psychology and Economy gGmbH
description: The project goal of the International Academy for Innovative Pedagogy, Psychology and Economy gGmbH is to bring about sustainable change in local communities across Europe through innovative approaches to youth empowerment and community development. To this end, the grantee will develop a resource center that will support local communities to implement youth empowerment approaches; facilitate networking and learning opportunities for young people, practitioners, and policymakers; document and assess good practices in the field; and disseminate data and analysis related to youth empowerment. Building on ten years of implementing the Youth Empowerment Partnership Programme — a collaborative initiative of several European and domestic foundations, the grantee and the Network of European Foundations — the grantee will continue to work with the existing 15 local sites involved in the project and seek to expand this number. The resource center will be a project of the grantee, which will be based in Berlin, Germany. A staff of three to four people will run the resource center, and strategic guidance will be provided by a steering committee made up of stakeholders in the project, including young people.

title: Youth Empowerment Partnership Programme
grantee: International Academy Berlin for Innovative Pedagogy, Psychology and Economy gGmbH
description: The project goal of International Academy for Innovative Pedagogy, Psychology and Economy gGmbH is to bring about sustainable change in local communities across Europe through innovative approaches to youth empowerment and community development. To this end, the grantee operates a resource center that supports local communities to implement youth empowerment approaches; facilitates networking and learning opportunities for young people, practitioners, and policymakers; documents and assesses good practices in the field; and disseminates data and analysis related to youth empowerment. The Youth Empowerment Partnership Programme was a collaborative initiative of several European and domestic foundations, the grantee, and the Network of European Foundations from 2001 to 2011. In 2012, a new phase, designed to deepen and expand the work, was launched by the grantee. Building on the program’s successes to date, the grantee will work with the existing 15 local sites involved in the project and develop innovative approaches to working in a wider range of communities. A particular focus in 2013 will be given to entrepreneurship training for youth in communities with fewer opportunities. The resource center has a staff of three people, and strategic guidance is provided by a steering committee made up of stakeholders in the project, including young people. The grantee is based in Berlin, Germany.

The program was established in 2001 through the collaboration of several European and domestic foundations, the grantee, and the Network of European Foundations. Since 2012, the grantee has acted as the secretariat and resource center for the program. More than 250 young people were directly involved in activities in the program’s local sites. Funding for the grantee’s work and for the local program sites was diversified, including securing multiple project grants from the European Commission. The grantee is based in Berlin, Germany.
