description: This grant will support the Genesee County Land Bank Authority’s Clean and Green initiative for the summer of 2011 through the summer of 2012. The grantee is nationally acclaimed as a leader in acquiring and managing vacant properties and restoring them to productive use. Since its inception in 2002, it has acquired more than 13,500 properties, and has a current inventory of 9,600 properties. The grantee’s initiative simultaneously enhances the quality of neighborhoods in Flint and promotes citizen stewardship by engaging neighborhood groups in mowing and maintaining vacant lots and planting gardens.

description: This grant will provide funds for the Genesee County Land Bank Authority to continue to employ a professional planning and development team to coordinate and implement interventions to stabilize neighborhoods and reuse vacant properties. The grantee developed and operates one of the most successful programs to reclaim vacant and abandoned property in the nation. Since its inception, it has acquired more than 13,500 properties through the tax foreclosure process and currently manages an inventory of 8,100 properties.

title: Capital Improvements
description: The Genesee County Parks & Recreation Commission is dedicated to providing all residents of Genesee County with affordable, quality recreational and educational facilities. The Genesee County Parks are widely utilized as accessible and inexpensive opportunities for local residents to experience recreation and nature. Attendance at most facilities has either held constant or increased despite the recent critical economic conditions. This grant will enable the grantee to continue its critical maintenance and restoration projects by replacing Bridge #4 of the Huckleberry Railroad.

title: Capital Improvements
description: The Genesee County Parks & Recreation Commission is dedicated to providing all residents of Genesee County with high quality recreational and educational facilities and programs. Genesee County parks are widely utilized as accessible and affordable opportunities for local residents to experience recreation and nature. Attendance at most facilities has either held constant or increased even during difficult economic times. This grant will enable the grantee to perform critical maintenance for Engine 152 of the Huckleberry Railroad at Crossroads Village.

title: Capital Improvements
description: The Genesee County Parks & Recreation Commission is dedicated to providing all the residents of Genesee County with affordable, quality recreational and educational facilities. The Genesee County parks are widely utilized as accessible and inexpensive recreational and nature opportunities for local residents, and attendance in most facilities has either held constant or increased despite the recent critical economic conditions. This grant will enable the commission to replace approximately four and a half miles of railroad track used solely by the Huckleberry Railroad and restore the pedestrian bridge that links the trails through For-Mar Nature Preserve and Arboretum.

title: Repayable Grant to the Ex-Offender Community Service Employment Initiative
description: Flint Downtown District Weed and Seed, a project of the United Way of Genesee County, has been awarded a federal grant to operate an Ex-Offender Community Service Employment Initiative. In partnership with New Paths, Inc., and the Genesee County Land Bank Authority, the program will provide supportive services and transitional employment for 75 to 125 ex-offenders in Genesee County. New Paths will offer various counseling services and career planning assistance to participants, while the Land Bank will provide on-the-job training and work experience to help ex-offenders assimilate back into society. The goals of the program are to reduce recidivism, create jobs for ex-offenders, increase public safety, and improve the physical appearance of Flint neighborhoods. Because the federal funding is delivered through a quarterly reimbursement process, this repayable grant will provide the United Way with sufficient funds to operate the program.

title: GoodTemps
description: Through its GoodTemps staffing service, Goodwill Industries of West Michigan is providing jobs for people with barriers to employment. As one of the only alternative staffing services in Michigan, GoodTemps is the base for expanding this effective workforce development technique to other Goodwill organizations across the state. This grant will provide support for the client services offered through GoodTemps and allow the organization to continue to support development of other alternative staffing programs throughout Michigan.

description: In response to the vacant property crisis in communities across America, the Genesee Institute and the National Vacant Properties Campaign combined to form the Center for Community Progress. This national center promotes policy, research, and technical assistance intended to help communities reduce the effects of blight associated with vacant, abandoned, and underutilized properties. This grant increase will provide partial support for training, technical assistance, a Flint-specific initiative relating to vacant property issues, and work refining the application of the concept of shrinking cities.

description: This renewal grant provides partial support to the Center for Community Progress to further its mission of combating the negative effects of property vacancy and abandonment in post-industrial urban areas. Headquartered in Flint and with offices in Washington, D.C., the grantee addresses these issues at the federal, state and local levels through a combination of research, policy reform and advocacy, technical assistance and capacity building, and communications programs.

title: Church-School Partnership
description: This grant will support the Church-School Partnership, a project of Flint Community Schools. The program seeks to increase the number of African-American male volunteers in the schools by partnering with places of worship that are in close proximity to a community school and recruiting volunteers from those congregations. The school administrators believe that the additional presence of positive male role models will help to reduce student violence, increase civility, and assist with behavior management through informal mentoring relationships.

title: Michigan Community College Green Jobs Training Network
description: This grant will promote continuous learning and collective work regarding green workforce development through a Michigan community college Learning and Action Network using virtual and other means. This will include on-call project coaching by Jobs for the Future, on-site support from National Wildlife Federation field coordinators, a best-practices and educational product Web site with interactive features, an employment “pipeline” approach to build strong partnerships between community colleges and regional green sector employers, and an innovation fund to provide minigrants for a number of capacity or technical needs.

title: Michigan Cultural Data Project
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant provides partial support for a statewide, online database for Michigan arts organizations. The database is part of the Michigan Cultural Data Project, a partnership between ArtServe Michigan and the Pew Charitable Trusts. The project will provide Michigan arts organizations and funders with comprehensive data regarding the financial support and economic impact of arts regionally and statewide. As the Michigan nonprofit voice of arts and culture, ArtServe Michigan enhances the state’s arts and culture sector through advocacy, capacity building, and strategic communications.

title: Michigan Cultural Data Project
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant provides partial support for the creation of a statewide, online database for Michigan arts organizations. The database is part of the Michigan Cultural Data Project, an initiative of ArtServe Michigan and the Pew Charitable Trusts. The project will provide Michigan arts organizations and funders with comprehensive data regarding the financial support and economic impact of arts regionally and statewide. As the Michigan nonprofit voice of arts and culture, ArtServe Michigan enhances the state’s arts and culture sector through advocacy, capacity building, and strategic communications.

title: Flint/Genesee Earn & Learn Initiative
description: This grant will enable Career Alliance, Inc., to continue the Earn & Learn Initiative in Flint and Genesee County targeting disconnected youth ages 18-24, unemployed adults (particularly minority males), and ex-offenders re-entering the workforce. In the first year of this initiative, Career Alliance, Inc., provided 278 individuals with training, subsidized employment and credentialing opportunities in career pathways such as construction and healthcare. The initiative is designed to spark immediate entry-level work opportunities while simultaneously increasing participants’ skills and helping them manage barriers to success. This grant will enable the grantee to assist current and an additional 150 participants in maintaining and/or enhancing their work skills to make the transition from subsidized employment to more permanent job placements. The Foundation’s investment in this initiative will be matched 1:1 by both the Open Society Foundations and the state of Michigan.

title: Flint/Genesee Earn & Learn Initiative
description: This grant will enable Career Alliance, Inc., to implement the Earn & Learn Initiative in Flint and Genesee County, targeting 264 disconnected youth (18-24), young minority males (including former prisoners reentering the workforce), and chronically unemployed adults. The initiative is designed to spark immediate entry-level work opportunities, while simultaneously increasing workers’ skills and helping them manage barriers to success. The Mott Foundation’s investment in the Earn & Learn Initiative will be matched one-to-one by both the Open Society Institute and the state of Michigan.

title: Rent and Utility Assistance Program
description: Since 1893, the Salvation Army of Genesee County has been working to alleviate hardship by assisting Genesee County residents with basic-level needs such as rent and utility payments, emergency shelter, food and personal needs items, and transportation. This grant will support the Salvation Army of Genesee County in expanding its rent and utility assistance program to meet the growing needs of families in the community.

title: Increasing Food Distribution and Access
description: The Food Bank of Eastern Michigan started in 1981 as a small grassroots community organization to distribute surplus food to those in need throughout Genesee County, as well as 21 other counties in eastern Michigan. The food bank solicits, stores, and distributes approximately 18 million pounds of food annually, either directly or through a network of more than 400 partner agencies which include soup kitchens, church pantries, homeless shelters, and other charities. This grant will enable the grantee to upgrade its inventory control system with a bar scanning module and provide additional high protein food items for Genesee County food pantries.

title: Increasing Food Distribution and Access
description: The Food Bank of Eastern Michigan started in 1981 as a small grassroots community organization to distribute surplus food to those in need throughout Genesee County, as well as 21 other counties in eastern Michigan. The food bank solicits, stores, and distributes over 21 million pounds of food annually, either directly or through a network of more than 400 partner agencies which include soup kitchens, church pantries, homeless shelters, and other charities. This grant will enable the grantee to purchase additional high protein food items for distribution to Genesee County residents and buy another fork lift to assist with the growing amounts of food being handled in the warehouse.

title: Increasing Food Distribution and Access
description: This grant will provide funds to the Food Bank of Eastern Michigan to purchase high protein food items such as meat, eggs, peanut butter, and beans. For those who experience a shortage of food, high protein items are a necessary source of good nutrition. While the Food Bank of Eastern Michigan has proven to be a model in addressing the acquisition, storage, and distribution of food items, purchasing high protein foods decreases the possibility of running out of these highly nutritious items even when donations are inconsistent.

title: Increasing Food Distribution and Access
description: This grant will provide funds to the Food Bank of Eastern Michigan for the benefit of the Eastside Nazarene Compassionate Mission and Carriage Town Ministries to procure highly nutritious food, personal care items, and program services like mobile pantry items. The Food Bank of Eastern Michigan provides healthy, nutritious food to the most vulnerable community members through its partnerships with more than 200 agencies in the city of Flint.

title: Increasing Food Distribution and Access
description: The Food Bank of Eastern Michigan started in 1981 as a small, grassroots community organization distributing surplus food to those in need throughout Genesee County, as well as 21 other counties in eastern Michigan. The food bank solicits, stores, and distributes approximately 18 million pounds of food annually, either directly or through a network of more than 400 partner agencies which include soup kitchens, church pantries, homeless shelters, and other charities. This grant will enable the Food Bank of Eastern Michigan to implement technology and facility upgrades that will help increase food distribution by an estimated 10 percent.

title: Program Expansion
description: Since its inception in 1983, the Shelter of Flint, Inc., has provided a critical safety net for homeless single women, women with children, and men with children. The shelter offers a comprehensive set of support programs and transition services that fulfill its mission of helping homeless individuals and families work toward permanent stability. Assistance includes: emergency shelter, transitional housing, support services, and outreach. This grant will increase the Shelter of Flint’s capacity to serve more clients by improving the literacy/GED program, implementing a new intake procedure, and providing improved access to existing community services.

title: Flint 21st Century Community Policing Technical Assistance
description: The City of Flint is facing a significant public safety challenge. Crime and violence are increasing across the city, while the city’s budget crisis has caused a simultaneous reduction in the police force and public safety resources. The mayor of Flint is addressing the issue by reviving community policing strategies in collaboration with the Michigan State University School of Criminal Justice. This renewal grant will support the second year of training, technical assistance, and evaluation of the Flint 21st Century Community Policing Technical Assistance project.

title: Flint 21st Century Community Policing Technical Assistance
description: The city of Flint continues to face a significant public safety challenge. Crime and violence across the city remain high, while the city’s ongoing budget crisis has caused a simultaneous reduction in the police force and public safety resources. With technical assistance from Michigan State University’s Department of Criminology, the city of Flint’s emergency manager has outlined a public safety plan that aims to address public safety issues in Flint. This renewal grant will support the third year of training, technical assistance, and evaluation to assist the city of Flint in implementing important changes in its police department and other public safety functions.

title: Flint 21st Century Community Policing Technical Assistance
description: The city of Flint continues to face a significant public safety challenge. Crime and violence across the city remain high, while the city’s ongoing budget crisis has caused a simultaneous reduction in the police force and public safety resources. With technical assistance from Michigan State University’s Department of Criminology, the city of Flint’s emergency manager has outlined a public safety plan that aims to address public safety issues in Flint. This renewal grant will support the fourth year of training, technical assistance, and evaluation to assist the city of Flint in implementing important changes in its police department and other public safety functions.

title: Flint 21st Century Community Policing Technical Assistance
description: The city of Flint continues to face a significant public safety challenge. Crime and violence across the city remains high, while the city’s ongoing budget crisis has caused a simultaneous reduction in the police force and public safety resources. With technical assistance from Michigan State University’s Department of Criminology, the city of Flint’s emergency manager and a new police chief have outlined a public safety plan that aims to address public safety issues in Flint. This grant increase will support the fourth year of training, technology enhancements, technical assistance, and evaluation to assist the city of Flint in implementing important changes in its police department and other public safety functions.

title: Flint Police Department Technical Assistance
description: The city of Flint continues to face a significant public safety challenge. Crime and violence across the city remains disproportionately high, while the city’s ongoing budget crisis has caused a severely limited police force. With technical assistance from Michigan State University’s Department of Criminology, the city of Flint’s emergency manager and a new police chief continue to view public safety as a high priority for the city. This renewal grant will support a sixth year of training, technology system upgrades, technical assistance, and evaluation to assist the city of Flint in implementing important changes in its police department and other public safety functions.

title: Flint 21st Century Community Policing Technical Assistance
description: The city of Flint is facing a significant public safety challenge. Crime and violence are increasing across the city, while the city’s budget crisis has caused a simultaneous reduction in the police force and public safety resources. Mayor Dayne Walling is addressing the issue by reviving community policing and neighborhood foot patrols. The Michigan State University School of Criminal Justice will provide training, technical assistance, and evaluation of the Flint 21st Century Community Policing effort.

title: Transportation Reform
description: A group of mayors and city managers helped establish the Michigan Suburbs Alliance in 2002 to unite communities in southeast Michigan through innovative, regional strategies and public policy reforms. As part of its mission to strengthen older communities, the grantee has sought to ensure that Michigan’s transportation policies and initiatives maximize environmental, social, and economic benefits. With previous Mott support, the grantee provided technical assistance and training to municipal staff and community groups engaging in transportation decisions. With renewed support, the grantee will continue this work with a particular focus on improving and implementing transportation plans in southeast Michigan.

title: Transportation Reform
description: A group of mayors and city managers helped establish the Michigan Suburbs Alliance in 2002 to unite and strengthen urban and surrounding older communities of southeast Michigan through innovative regional strategies and public policy reforms. The grantee has emerged as an important voice on issues affecting the fiscal, economic, and environmental health of metropolitan areas in Michigan. This grant will support the grantee’s efforts to reform transportation policies in southeast Michigan in a way that promotes equitable and ecologically sustainable outcomes. The grantee will accomplish this by providing technical assistance and training to municipal representatives and community groups, growing the network of engaged civic leaders, and researching sustainable transit-funding options.

title: NCCS Community Platform
description: The NCCS Community Platform is a project of the National Center for Charitable Statistics, which is housed within the Urban Institute’s Center on Nonprofits and Philanthropy. The platform is an online database and comprehensive, interactive resource for community engagement and problem solving. Besides data on nonprofit organizations, the platform includes demographic and economic data, knowledge resources, and interactive tools that facilitate collaborative planning and action. The platform is now live in 13 sites across the United States. Over the next two years, the center forecasts launching the platform in another 20 communities while it continues its outreach and improvements to the platform’s technology, content, and training offerings. The Urban Institute is an independent think tank that gathers data, conducts research, evaluates programs, offers technical assistance overseas, and educates Americans on social and economic issues to foster sound public policy and effective government.

title: NCCS Community Platform
description: The NCCS Community Platform is a project of the National Center for Charitable Statistics, which is housed within the Urban Institute’s Center on Nonprofits and Philanthropy. The platform is an online database, toolkit, and resource hub that allows communities and their nonprofits to work together in new and more effective ways. The platform describes, classifies, and maps community programs, resources, and nonprofits; incorporates census and other demographic and economic neighborhood-based data; and provides tools for authorized users and nonprofit organizations to update and enrich information in the database, share resources, and organize and manage community projects. Over the next two years, the platform will be launched in 30 to 40 communities across the United States. The Urban Institute is an independent think tank that gathers data, conducts research, evaluates programs, offers technical assistance overseas, and educates Americans on social and economic issues to foster sound public policy and effective government.

title: Catalyzing Governance Reforms of International Financial Institutions
description: This grant will support research and monitoring of reforms at the International Monetary Fund and other global financial institutions with the goal of making these institutions more accountable and effective at promoting sustainable, equitable growth. Support will enable New Rules for Global Finance to monitor Group of 20 commitments related to global crisis prevention and financial regulation. The grantee convenes nongovernmental organizations and researchers from developed and developing countries to identify and promote politically feasible and technically sound solutions to issues of economic governance and international finance.

title: Engaging Stories that Build Communities: The New Journalism Illumination Project
description: This grant will provide funding to Journalism That Matters to support conferences and activities that work to develop and advance the field of journalism. Efforts will focus on finding, nurturing, and incubating promising innovations for a news ecosystem — the information exchange among public, government, and institutions that can inform, inspire, engage, and activate a full range of public voices.

title: Engaging Stories that Build Communities: The New Journalism Illumination Project
description: This grant increase will provide funding to Journalism That Matters to support conferences and activities that work to develop and advance the field of journalism. Efforts will focus on finding, nurturing, and incubating promising innovations for a news ecosystem, the information exchange among public, government, and institutions that can inform, inspire, engage, and activate a full range of public voices.

title: Journalism That Matters
description: This grant will support a collaboration between “Journalism That Matters” and the Donald W. Reynolds Journalism Institute at the University of Missouri – Columbia to hold two conferences on the future of journalism. A 2010 conference in Detroit will focus on how the voices of people of color can be more present in the news. In 2011, another conference will convene in the Piedmont/Triad area of North Carolina, which is reinventing itself after an economic crash following the downfall of the textile industry. Approximately 100 media innovators will come together for each three-day conference to share innovations and ideas already in process in the new media landscape. The University of Missouri, founded in 1839, has a diverse enrollment with 30,200 students from every county in Missouri, every state in the nation, and 100 countries.

title: Emergency Relief for Earthquake in Haiti
description: This grant provides support to Dartmouth College for emergency relief in Haiti. On January 12, 2010, a massive earthquake struck the Caribbean country of Haiti, causing catastrophic damage in the capital city of Port-au-Prince and the surrounding areas. Immediately after the earthquake, Dartmouth College began deploying medical teams to Haiti to assist the relief group, Partners in Health, an organization co-founded in 1987 by Dr. Jim Yong Kim, the president of Dartmouth, and Dr. Paul Farmer. Dartmouth plans to send at least six teams of doctors and nurses, together with the necessary medical supplies. The Dartmouth teams are assigned as needed by Partners in Health and work in its clinics and affiliated hospitals throughout Haiti.

title: Rede Brasil: Civil Society Eye on the G-20
description: This grant to INESC aims to strengthen citizen oversight of the role of the Brazilian government in financial sector reform and provide input into international debates concerning financial regulation regimes that reduce risk and increase opportunity for sustainable development. The project will strengthen the capacity of nongovernmental organizations in Brazil, particularly the members of the Brazil Network on multilateral financial institutions, to monitor and analyze the participation of the Brazilian government in the financial reform efforts of the Group of 20 nations. It will build on a decade of experience with international financial institutions to generate informational materials in Portuguese for organizations in Brazil and complement this information with capacity building workshops and coordination with national and international networks promoting meaningful international financial sector reform.

title: Capacity Building in Developing Countries on Global Economic Architecture
description: The 2008 financial crisis and the ensuing economic crisis are the most severe crises to face the global economy since the Great Depression. To address these crises, it is important to address both developed and developing country issues. Established in 1994 by agreement with the United Nations Secretary General, the South Centre is an intergovernmental think tank for developing countries. It provides analyses of development problems and experience as well as intellectual and policy support required by developing countries for collective and individual action, particularly in the international arena. This project will provide research into key issues of the financial and economic crises in order to increase the capacity of developing countries to better participate in the governance of the global financial and economic systems.

title: Life Science Cluster Economic Impact Analysis
description: The Genesys Health Foundation oversees charitable gifts and grants for the Genesys Health System and Genesys Regional Medical Center in order to address community healthcare needs and improve access to healthcare services for those who are underserved. This grant will enable the grantee to complete an economic feasibility study that will supply data to support economic revitalization and job creation in Genesee County and the surrounding area. Specifically, the feasibility study will help identify potential competencies and collaborative business opportunities for life science education, medical and technology development, and advanced biomedical and simulation modeling within the healthcare, education, research, and commerce sectors in Genesee County.

title: Nonprofit Employment Data Project
description: The Center for Civil Society Studies at Johns Hopkins University created a method to disclose federal data on nonprofit employment collected through the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics’ Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages. The center subsequently assembled a decade (1999-2009) of quarterly data on nonprofit employment and volunteering for 45 states and Washington, D.C., and published a comprehensive report, “Holding the Fort: Nonprofit Employment During a Decade of Turmoil”. In the upcoming grant period, the center will make a nonprofit employment dataset available to the public through a new, web-based, interactive database so that nonprofit practitioners, public officials, academics, and the general public can have accessible and timely information on nonprofit employment and wages in user-friendly, graphic formats. Johns Hopkins University is one of America’s premier research universities. The Center for Civil Society Studies seeks to improve understanding and the effective functioning of nonprofit, philanthropic, and civil society organizations.

title: Nonprofit Employment Data Project
description: The Nonprofit Employment Data Project charts nonprofit employment, wages, and finances over time and in relation to other industries. A collaboration between the Johns Hopkins University’s Center for Civil Society Studies, state employment security agencies, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, and state nonprofit associations, the project offers the most up-to-date, in-depth analyses now available on economic aspects of the nonprofit sector. Past results include the publication of a comprehensive national report based on nonprofit employment data over 1999-2009 and several state-level reports. Having configured and integrated Bureau of Labor Statistics and other data into a single database, the center is testing a public access Web site which it plans to launch and market over the next 18 months. Johns Hopkins University is one of America’s premier research universities. The Center for Civil Society Studies seeks to improve understanding and the effective functioning of not-for-profit, philanthropic, and civil society organizations.

title: Nonprofit Employment Data Project
description: The Nonprofit Employment Data Project charts nonprofit employment, wages, and finances over time and in relation to other industries. A collaboration between the Johns Hopkins University’s Center for Civil Society Studies, state employment security agencies, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, and state nonprofit associations, the project offers the most up-to-date, in-depth analyses now available on economic aspects of the nonprofit sector. Having configured and integrated U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics and other data into a single database, the center is developing a public access Web site. This grant increase will allow for the full development, testing, marketing, and initial operating costs for the site.

title: Nonprofit Employment Data Project
description: The Nonprofit Employment Data Project is a collaboration between the Johns Hopkins University’s Center for Civil Society Studies and the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics that charts nonprofit employment, wages, and finances over time and in relation to other industries. Past results include the publication of a comprehensive national report based on nonprofit employment data over 1999-2009 and several state-level reports. Last year the grantee launched a user-friendly, interactive database called Nonprofit Works —which provides nonprofit employment data through 2012. During the upcoming 18 months, the center and bureau will work to develop and input 2015 data into Nonprofit Works. The center will also market the database and take steps to enhance its long-term sustainability. Johns Hopkins University is one of America’s premier research universities. The Center for Civil Society Studies seeks to improve the understanding and effective functioning of not-for-profit, philanthropic, or civil society organizations.

title: Nonprofit Employment Data Project
description: The Center for Civil Society Studies at Johns Hopkins University has created a method to disclose federal data on nonprofit employment collected through the Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages, a data source operated by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics. In cooperation with the bureau, the center will develop a robust database on nonprofit employment by state and county going back 20 years, analyze this data, and create a public use access point for it. The center plans to produce a series of reports and a major book presenting this data and analyzing the dynamics it reveals, as well as establish an on-line database that researchers, state nonprofit associations, funders, and other stakeholders can use. Johns Hopkins University is one of America’s premier research universities. The Center for Civil Society Studies seeks to improve understanding and the effective functioning of not-for-profit, philanthropic, or civil society organizations.

title: Middle School Family Resource Centers
grantee: Genesee County Department of Human Services
description: Piloted in 2003, the Genesee County Department of Human Services family resource centers are housed in an elementary or middle school and staffed by experienced social workers who provide case management services for students receiving food, cash, and medical assistance. Currently, there are six family resource centers in Flint, which are located at three elementary schools, two middle schools, and one charter K-12 school. This grant will support the first phase of parent empowerment programming at the family resource centers. The program will be available to all family resource center participants but will focus on families being served at Durant Tuuri Mott Elementary School and Holmes Middle School.

title: Middle School Family Resource Centers
grantee: Genesee County Department of Human Services
description: Piloted in 2003, the Genesee County Department of Human Services Family Resource Centers were housed in an elementary or middle school and staffed by experienced social workers who provided case management services for students receiving food, cash, and medical assistance. Governor Snyder has redesigned the Family Resource Center model into the Pathways to Potential program, where social workers will be placed at each of the Flint elementary schools by 2013. In addition to providing cash and food benefits, social workers will assist parents with wraparound and support services, especially helping to increase the bond between educators and parents. Currently, the Pathway to Potential pilot sites in Flint are Washington, Bryant, and Durant Tuuri Mott elementary schools. One of the methods used to provide wraparound services is parent empowerment programming, which increases parental involvement. This grant will support parent empowerment programming at the three Pathways to Potential pilot sites.

title: Middle School Family Resource Centers
grantee: Genesee County Department of Human Services
description: This grant will support the expansion of two Genesee County Department of Human Services family resource centers. By creating a resource center in McKinley Middle School and expanding services in Holmes Middle School, the organization will provide caseworker services to the 80 percent of middle school children attending Flint Community Schools. The State of Michigan Department of Human Services has developed 69 family resource centers across the state. Piloted in 2003, each family resource center is housed in an elementary or middle school and staffed by experienced social workers who provide the case management services for students receiving food, cash, and medical assistance.

title: Planning and Administrative Support
grantee: Youth Initiative for Human Rights - Bosnia
description: The project goal is to strengthen youth engagement and activism on issues of transitional justice and human rights promotion. Through this project, the Youth Initiative for Human Rights – Bosnia, a nongovernmental organization in Bosnia and Herzegovina, is developing its organizational and programmatic capacities to empower and train young people to be more involved in shaping how Bosnian society deals with the legacy of war, addresses ongoing human rights issues, and integrates into the wider Europe. This grant increase will assist the grantee with a funding shortfall for this project. Registered in Bosnia in late 2009, the grantee was formerly the branch office of the Serbian Youth Initiative for Human Rights, a long-time Mott grantee.

title: Planning and Administrative Support
grantee: Youth Initiative for Human Rights - Bosnia
description: The project goal is to strengthen youth engagement and activism on issues of transitional justice and human rights promotion. To this end, grant funds will be used to help the Youth Initiative for Human Rights – Bosnia, a newly registered nongovernmental organization in Bosnia and Herzegovina, develop its organizational and programmatic capacities to empower and train young people to be more involved in shaping how Bosnian society deals with the legacy of war, addresses ongoing human rights issues, and integrates into the wider Europe. Specific activities will include training and mentoring for key staff on financial management and administration, establishing an office in Banja Luka, and strengthening the role of the organization’s governing board. Registered in Bosnia in late 2009, the grantee was formerly the branch office of the Serbian Youth Initiative for Human Rights, a long-time Mott grantee.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant supports New Visions for Public Schools in its effort to fundamentally re-envision secondary education in New York City. The grantee’s New Century High Schools Initiative seeks to improve student achievement in 76 New York City public schools and demonstrate that students in urban schools can graduate in large numbers ready for college and careers by creating schools that combine rigorous academic programs with innovative teaching, personalized learning environments, and deep ties to local communities. Specifically, this grant will allow the grantee to: 1) develop schools’ human capacity; 2) build instructional supports in the ninth grade; 3) engage parents and families; and 4) create a college and career roadmap. This work aligns with the Mott-funded report, “A New Day for Learning,” which examines the importance of integrating school and community resources in improving student success.

title: Three-Year Evaluation of YouthQuest Afterschool Initiative
description: This grant will provide support for a Three-Year Evaluation of the YouthQuest Afterschool Initiative. In 2009-10, the program began implementation of a new strategic plan focused on positive outcomes in learning and development for high need students. This evaluation will allow for continuous program improvement by providing timely feedback on program implementation, quality, and effectiveness. School principals, site coordinators, and students will complete annual surveys, and annual observations will take place at ten sites. Annual reports will compare implementation results with findings from evaluations of similar afterschool initiatives in other communities. Policy Studies Associates, Inc., located in Washington, D.C., has conducted major evaluations of afterschool programs in Boston, New Jersey, New York City, and other locations across the country.

title: Accelerating Automotive Innovation
description: This grant will provide renewal support for an initiative to unleash intellectual property from the automotive sector to aid other sectors of the economy through job creation and economic development. Ultimately, the AutoHarvest Foundation seeks to connect the vast universe of ideas and talent in the automotive supply chain with national labs, universities, and independent investors. In this phase, focus will be placed on connecting Flint and Genesee County universities and organizations to the AutoHarvest Foundation network.

title: Accelerating Automotive Innovation
description: This grant will provide support for a new initiative to unleash intellectual property from the automotive sector to aid other sectors of the economy through job creation and economic development. The Accelerating Automotive Innovation project will develop a comprehensive tool to link the automotive industry and accelerate collaboration. Ultimately, the AutoHarvest Foundation seeks to connect the vast universe of ideas and talent in the automotive supply chain with national labs, universities, and independent investors.

title: Scaling What Works
description: This grant will provide partial support to Grantmakers for Effective Organizations, an organization focused on increasing the effectiveness of nonprofits and grantmakers by promoting and advocating for the use of philanthropic resources to advance nonprofit organizational effectiveness. Through the Scaling What Works project, the grantee will serve as convener, liaison, and information broker between the White House Office of Social Innovation and Civic Participation, the Corporation for National and Community Service, and the field of philanthropy. The grantee will work to build partnerships between philanthropy and government to support the successful implementation and strategic direction of the $50 million federally funded Social Innovation Fund — a new public-private investment vehicle designed to reduce poverty and inequities by increasing economic opportunity; preparing America’s youth for success in school, work, and citizenship; and promoting healthy lifestyles and reducing the risk factors that can lead to illness.

title: General Purposes
description: Through bipartisan and interfaith dialogues, the Faith & Politics Institute works to bridge racial, religious, and political divisions among elected officials, while promoting reflective and ethical leadership. Since 1991, the grantee has engaged hundreds of members of Congress, Congressional staff, and their constituents in dialogues that encourage collaborative and visionary leadership practices and foster healing, civility, and respect. During 2012-2013, the grantee will offer several programs including weekly reflection groups for members of Congress and Congressional staff, educational public forums, experiential pilgrimages to national and international sites of historical significance, and skill-building workshops and retreats.

title: Achieving the Dream
description: This renewal grant will continue to support Mott Community College’s enrollment in Achieving the Dream. Achieving the Dream, started by the Lumina Foundation, is a process dedicated to making the student success agenda a priority at community colleges and with state and national policymakers and stakeholders. To create and implement student success strategies, Achieving the Dream provides on-campus coaching with faculty, staff, and leadership; assistance with data collection and analysis; access to information on innovative and successful practices; networking opportunities and resources to address barriers; and guidance on engaging the college and community in supporting student success.

title: Achieving the Dream
description: This grant will support enrollment in Achieving the Dream at Mott Community College. title: Clinton Global Initiative
description: This grant will provide support for the Clinton Global Initiative, a project of the William J. Clinton Foundation. The grantee is a public charity established in 1997 by the 42nd president of the United States. The mission of the organization is to strengthen the capacity of people throughout the world to meet the challenges of global interdependence. In 2005, President Clinton established the Clinton Global Initiative to turn ideas into action and to help the world move beyond the current state of globalization to a more integrated global community of shared benefits, responsibilities, and values. By gathering world leaders from a variety of backgrounds, the initiative creates a unique opportunity to channel the capacities of individuals and organizations to realize change. The 2011 annual meeting will take place September 19-22 in New York City.

title: Energy Council for the City of Flint
description: This grant will provide support to the Genesee Area Focus Fund for the creation of an Energy Council for the City of Flint. A diverse group of community stakeholders (universities, schools, government, and business) will convene regularly in 2010 to develop ideas, identify projects, and seek funding to further the sustainability agenda of the Flint area. In June 2010, a delegation will travel to Leksand, Sweden to participate in a global conference on the green economy. Representatives will also visit the city of Linköping for discussions with government and business officials about economic development and sustainability strategies.

title: YouthQuest After School Initiative
description: This renewal grant will provide continued support to the Genesee Area Focus Fund for the YouthQuest After School Initiative. The mission of YouthQuest is to provide children with opportunities to grow through a safe, engaging, and exciting afterschool learning experience, surrounded with caring, responsible adults and sustained by an involved, contributing community. In its first year, YouthQuest provided more than 1,500 children at 15 area schools with afterschool programs four days per week, three hours per day, 36 weeks per school year, and six weeks during the summer.

title: YouthQuest After School Initiative
description: This renewal grant will provide continued support to the Genesee Area Focus Fund for the YouthQuest After School Initiative. The purpose of YouthQuest is to provide children and youth with opportunities to grow and learn through a safe, engaging, and exciting afterschool learning experience, surrounded with caring, responsible adults and sustained by an involved, contributing community. YouthQuest fulfills this purpose through six core program elements: academic support, enrichment activities, physical fitness/healthy behaviors, nutrition/nutrition education, youth development/leadership skill building, and family and community engagement.

title: YouthQuest After School Initiative
description: This grant will provide support to the Genesee Area Focus Fund for the YouthQuest After School Initiative, formerly known as the Bridges to the Future Afterschool Program. The mission of YouthQuest is to provide children with opportunities to grow through a safe, engaging, and exciting afterschool learning experience, surrounded with caring, responsible adults and sustained by an involved, contributing community. YouthQuest’s program is designed to fulfill this mission through the following objectives: academics, technology, visual/performing arts, career preparation, life skills, recreation fitness/sport, family involvement, community involvement, and youth advisory councils. The afterschool program will operate on the school year calendar beginning approximately the third week of school. YouthQuest will also provide a six-week summer program in 2011. The Genesee Area Focus Fund, a supporting organization of the Genesee Area Focus Council and Genesee Regional Chamber of Commerce, is a consortium of nonprofit, educational, and business leaders with a focus on economic development issues that affect the competitive economy and quality of life in Genesee County.

title: Moving Forward Conference
grantee: Council of Chief State School Officers
description: This grant will support the Council of Chief State School Officers in convening a Moving Forward meeting to help teams of key leaders from states, school districts, and the philanthropic community to: 1) practically address the funding cliff that most communities and states across the nation are facing; and 2) determine how best to leverage resources, including financial and intellectual capital, to increase the chances of true transformational education change. The focus will be on key leverage points in the existing system — including human capital, student supports, assessment and accountability, and information systems, among others — that must shift for innovation to occur. State teams will share strategies and articulate needs, and national experts in education finance and system transformation will be available to provide information and tools for further work.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Montenegro, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Serbia, Kosovo
description: The program goal is to encourage, support, and facilitate active civic participation that strengthens Serbia’s democratic development and European integration processes. To this end, the Heartefact Fund makes small grants to local nonprofits; organizes exchanges and study visits; and supports, develops, and produces film and theater projects. All of the grantee’s activities are designed to promote creative approaches to confront the nationalism and ethnic mistrust that characterizes the region and raise awareness of the importance of human rights’ protection. During 2010-2011, the grantee developed its grantmaking programs and supported more than 15 local projects; produced and toured a play that examines attitudes toward dealing with the conflicts of the 1990s; and organized regional festivals using art, theater, and film to raise awareness of social and political issues. With Mott support during the past two years, the fund strengthened staff and board capacities and built its national and regional network of partners and beneficiaries. Established in 2009, the grantee is based in Belgrade, Serbia, and works in Serbia and the Western Balkan region.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Montenegro, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Serbia, Kosovo
description: The Heartefact Fund makes small grants to local nonprofits; organizes exchanges and study visits; and supports, develops, and produces film and theater projects that encourage, support, and facilitate active civic participation that strengthens Serbia’s and the region’s democratic development and European integration processes. All of the grantee’s activities are designed to promote creative approaches to confronting the nationalism and ethnic mistrust that characterizes the region and raising awareness of the importance of human rights protection. This grant increase will allow the grantee to expand its regional programming and deepen its cooperation with other nonprofits working with film and theater as a tool for dealing with the past and promoting reconciliation. Activities will include organizing a screening and workshop at a documentary film festival in Przren, Kosovo, featuring a new film about the play “Truth in Translation”.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Croatia, Serbia, Kosovo, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro
description: The program goal is to encourage, support, and facilitate active civic participation that strengthens Serbia’s democratic development and European integration processes. To this end, the Heartefact Fund makes small grants to local nonprofits; organizes exchanges and study visits; and supports, develops, and produces film and theater projects. All of the grantee’s activities are designed to promote creative approaches to confronting the nationalism and ethnic mistrust that characterizes the region and raise awareness about the importance of human rights protection. During 2012-2013, the grantee developed its grantmaking programs and supported more than 15 local projects annually with grants totaling over 100,000 Euros; produced and toured two new plays; organized regional festivals using art, theater, and film to raise awareness of social and political issues; and facilitated exchanges and discussions between experts and practitioners in key fields in Kosovo and Serbia. Additionally, during the past two years, the grantee engaged in strategic planning and strengthened staff and board capacities and built its national and regional network of partners and beneficiaries. Established in 2009, the grantee is based in Belgrade, Serbia, and works in Serbia and the Western Balkan region.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant supports the organizational and programmatic development of the Heartefact Fund, an operational and grantmaking foundation with a particular expertise and focus on using theater and the creative arts to address nationalism, ethnic mistrust, and other important social issues in Serbia and the wider region. The grantee makes small grants to local nonprofits; organizes exchanges and study visits; and supports, develops, and produces film and theater projects. All of the grantee’s activities are designed to promote and build sustainable regional cooperation. During 2014-2015, the grantee developed five new theater productions and organized regional tours of previously produced plays. The grantee also provided 25 small grants to community-based nonprofits that work on the normalization of regional relations, the promotion of rights and freedoms, and the empowerment of marginalized groups. It also launched an initiative called Art Friendly to encourage corporate and individual giving in support of socially engaged cultural projects. Additionally, during the past two years, the grantee engaged in strategic planning, strengthened staff and board capacities, and built its national and regional network of partners and beneficiaries. Established in 2009, Heartefact Fund is based in Belgrade, Serbia, and works in Serbia and the Western Balkan region.

title: Planning and Administrative Support
geographic_focus: Montenegro, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Serbia, Kosovo
description: The project goal is to build the organizational and programmatic capacities of the Heartefact Fund during its first years of operation. Established in July 2009, the fund will make grants; provide technical assistance; convene artists, filmmakers, theater directors, and others; and directly engage in the development and production of film and theater projects. All of the grantee’s activities will be designed to promote creative approaches to confronting the nationalism and ethnic mistrust that characterizes the region and raise awareness of the importance of human rights protection. In this way, the grantee will be linked to existing transitional justice initiatives in the region, working on these issues in new ways. Grant funds will be used to cover core operating expenses; provide training to staff, board, and other stakeholders; and network with beneficiaries and partners.

title: Planning and Administrative Support
grantee: Centre for Research, Documentation and Publication
description: The project goal is to support the Centre for Research, Documentation and Publication to develop its organizational and programmatic capacities for work on justice and reconciliation in Kosovo and the wider region over the long term. Formally registered as a nonprofit organization in Kosovo in February 2010, the grantee’s mission is to gather documentation, conduct research, disseminate information and analysis, and raise public awareness about the legacies of conflict and human rights abuses in Kosovo. During 2010-2011, the grantee provided leadership in Kosovo in a campaign to launch a regional victims’ commission; consulted widely with civil society, victims’ associations, and government on strategies for transitional justice in Kosovo; and planned longer-term programmatic strategies for the grantee. During the grant period, the grantee will carry out a series of workshops with civil society actors and government agencies and officials to build consensus about transitional justice strategies in Kosovo. Mott funds will also be used during the grant period to support the grantee’s organizational development and administrative costs, allowing it to continue to fundraise, build partnerships, and disseminate information about transitional justice. The grantee is based in Pristina.

title: Planning and Administrative Support
grantee: Centre for Research, Documentation and Publication
description: The project goal is to support the Centre for Research, Documentation and Publication to develop its organizational and programmatic capacities for work on justice and reconciliation in Kosovo and the wider region over the long term. The grantee’s mission is to gather documentation, conduct research, disseminate information and analysis, and raise public awareness about the legacies of conflict and human rights abuses in Kosovo. During 2012-2013, the grantee improved the capacity of civil society organizations and government institutions to implement transitional justice approaches and promote reconciliation in Kosovo. Through research and consultations with stakeholders, the grantee planned its longer-term, programmatic operational strategies. During the grant period, the grantee will carry out in-depth research on key issues impacting transitional justice in Kosovo, including the fate of missing persons, preserving state archives, public apologies and commemorations, and lustration and vetting mechanisms. The grantee will also address its organizational and programmatic development needs, including diversifying funding, building new partnerships, and training staff. The grantee is based in Pristina.

title: Planning and Administrative Support
grantee: Centre for Research, Documentation and Publication
description: The project goal is to help the newly established Centre for Research, Documentation and Publication develop its organizational and programmatic capacities to work on justice and reconciliation in Kosovo and the wider region over the long term. Formally registered as a nonprofit organization in Kosovo in February 2010, the grantee’s mission is to gather documentation, conduct research, disseminate information and analysis, and raise public awareness about the legacies of conflict and human rights abuses in Kosovo. Through a wide range of project activities, the grantee will contribute to improving interethnic relations and strengthening respect for human rights and multiculturalism in Kosovo. A particular focus of the grantee’s work over the next two years will be to advocate for the establishment of a regional victims’ commission in the former Yugoslavia. Mott funds will be used during the grant period to support the grantee’s organizational development and administrative costs.

title: Institutional and Programmatic Development Support
description: The project goal is to strengthen the capacity of Community Building Mitrovica — a nongovernmental organizational in Mitrovica, Kosovo — to lead and support economic, social, and civic redevelopment in the deeply divided city of Mitrovica. With a strong emphasis on the participation of people from all of the city’s ethnic groups, the grantee works to bridge divisions by building economic, cultural, social, and political links across the community. In order to continue playing this important role, the organization will strengthen its capacities for civic leadership by improving management within the organization, developing the financial management and planning skills of core staff, establishing a governing board, and upgrading information technology systems. Based in downtown Mitrovica, Community Building Mitrovica has been active since 2001 and is well recognized as a community leader.

title: General Purposes
description: This renewal grant provides support to the Prima Civitas Foundation as it embarks on an expanded mission to assist the entire state of Michigan. Founded in 2006, the Prima Civitas Foundation’s first five years were focused on economic development and provision of technical assistance to local units of government throughout mid-Michigan. The strategic plan for the next five years includes an expansion of services statewide and enhanced services in mid-Michigan.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant renews support to the Prima Civitas Foundation to pursue a broad range of initiatives and strategies designed to make Michigan globally competitive in the new economy. Begun in 2005 with the mission of transforming mid-Michigan’s economy, the grantee now works statewide to build networks that connect Michigan’s knowledge assets with catalytic opportunities for economic growth. During the grant period, the grantee will continue to implement a strategic plan focused on promoting international trade; attracting international businesses; and recruiting, retaining, and developing a 21st century workforce. Through the Flint Area Reinvestment Office, a program of Prima Civitas, the grantee will also continue to maintain a strong focus on the Greater Flint region.
