title: General Purposes
description: The purpose of this grant is to ensure the continuation of the work done by the Mid-Michigan Innovation Team Learning Communities Initiative after federal funding through the Mid-Michigan Workforce Innovation in Regional Economic Development initiative ended. During the grant period, the Prima Civitas Foundation will continue to manage the Mid-Michigan Innovation Team, which will continue its work of regional collaboration and development; establish focuses aimed at regional development and sustainability, leadership and strategy, research and technology, and communication and engagement; and begin work on two initiatives working with mid-Michigan colleges and universities focusing on small business development and innovation.

title: Informing the Public about Issues in International Finance and Sustainability: Carbon Market
description: Since 1977, the Center for Investigative Reporting has independently produced hundreds of investigations for television, print media, radio, and the Web. Its reports have appeared in numerous news outlets and national news programs, and it has had a strong track record of investigating environmental issues, policies, and protections. Over the next year, the grantee will focus on the development of a global carbon market. One of the key elements of an international climate mitigation and finance strategy has been the development of a global carbon market that would allow for the buying and selling of greenhouse gas emission permits known as carbon trading. Outside of individuals in the financial sector, very little is known about the ways that the growing carbon markets actually work. Through this project, the grantee will undertake a yearlong investigative reporting effort to address the dearth of accessible information on the workings of the carbon markets.

title: Endowment for the Chair for Leadership and Ethics
grantee: School for Ethics and Global Leadership
description: In 2009, the Center for the Study of the Presidency and Congress initiated an effort to endow a Chair for Leadership and Ethics. The purpose of the endowment is to develop and implement a portfolio of programs to enhance leadership, ethics, and integrity in government, education, business, and other professions. Programs will be developed for high school students as well as government, bar associations, and business groups in order to promote a better understanding and application of the principles of leadership and integrity.

title: Capital Improvements
description: The YWCA of Greater Flint has worked toward eliminating racism and empowering women in the greater Flint community for over 40 years. In 2009, the organization provided emergency shelter and temporary housing to 302 women and 236 children escaping abuse; provided 635 individuals with counseling, legal advocacy, and supportive services; and offered prevention education to 2,165 students and community members. The grantee also offers 24-hour emergency response support to sexual assault survivors and, in fall 2010, will begin to provide transitional housing for young women (ages 18-20) who have aged out of the foster care system. To help ensure long-term sustainability and uninterrupted emergency shelter and transitional housing services, this grant will enable the YWCA of Greater Flint to make much-needed repairs and improvements to the facility’s boiler and chiller systems.

title: Pre-College Summer Residential and Academic Year Bridge Program
description: This grant will enable the University of Michigan-Flint, via the Office of Educational Opportunity Initiatives, to expand its pre-college summer residential and academic year bridge program for students from the Flint, Beecher, and Westwood Heights school districts. In 2010, 50 rising ninth-grade students participated in a linked comprehensive summer and yearlong academic pilot that enabled students to experience college, learn about the college processes, and most importantly, take academic courses for skill-building purposes. During the next phase, recommended support will enable the grantee to continue the overall program by bringing back the initial cohort of 50 students as rising tenth-graders and adding a new cohort of 50 rising ninth-graders to participate in the program during the summer of 2011 and through the subsequent 2012 academic year.

title: Pre-College Summer Residential and Academic Year Bridge Program
description: This grant will enable the University of Michigan-Flint, via the Office of Educational Opportunity Initiatives, to continue its Pre-College Summer Residential and Academic Year Bridge Program for students from the Flint, Beecher, and Westwood Heights school districts. As a result of this effort, participating students have raised grade point averages and benefited from numerous tutoring and mentoring activities that have aided in their academic and personal development. In 2011, the program was expanded by adding a second cohort of students to participate in this linked and comprehensive summer and yearlong academic program. Recommended support will enable the Office of Educational Opportunity Initiatives to continue the overall program by bringing back the initial two cohorts of 100 students as rising tenth- and eleventh-graders and adding a new cohort of 50 rising ninth-graders to participate in the program in the summer of 2012 and through the subsequent 2013 academic year.

title: Pre-College Summer Residential and Academic Year Bridge Program
description: This grant will enable the University of Michigan-Flint, via the Office of Educational Opportunity Initiatives, to continue its Pre-college Summer Residential and Academic Year Bridge Program for students from the Flint, Beecher, and Westwood Heights school districts. As a result of this effort, participating students have increased grade-point averages and benefited from numerous tutoring and mentoring activities that have aided in their academic and personal development and kept them on track for graduation. In 2012, the program expanded by adding a third cohort of students to participate in this comprehensive summer and yearlong academic program. Recommended support will enable the Office of Educational Opportunity Initiatives to continue the overall program by bringing back the initial three cohorts of 125 students as rising 10th-, 11th-, and 12th-graders and adding a new cohort of 45 rising 9th-graders to participate in the program in the summer of 2013 and through the 2014 academic year. The year 2013 will mark the first time that a full cohort of students from the 9th through 12th grades will participate in this effort on the University of Michigan-Flint campus.

title: Committed to Excellence and Opportunity Program
description: This grant will enable the University of Michigan-Flint, via the Office of Educational Opportunity Initiatives, to continue the Committed to Excellence and Opportunity Program for pre-college students from the Flint, Beecher, and Westwood Heights school districts. Participating students have increased their grade-point averages and benefited from numerous tutoring and mentoring activities that have aided in their academic development. Seventy-two percent of the students from the pilot cohort in 2010 are still enrolled and are set to graduate and enter college in 2014. Recommended support will allow the program to expand from 170 to 520 students. This expansion is made possible through the Office of Educational Opportunity Initiatives’ restructuring that brought all of its pre-college programs under the Committed to Excellence and Opportunity program. This year will mark the first time the program will be at full scale for grades 6-12.

title: Committed to Excellence and Opportunity Program
description: This grant will enable the University of Michigan-Flint, through its Office of Educational Opportunity Initiatives, to continue the Committed to Excellence and Opportunity Program for students from the Flint, Beecher, and Westwood Heights school districts. The goal is to create and maintain a pipeline-to-college preparatory program that will equip young people from low-income families and minority students with the knowledge and skills necessary to enter into and succeed in college.

title: Committed to Excellence and Opportunity Program
description: This grant will enable the University of Michigan-Flint’s, Office of Educational Opportunity Initiatives, to continue the pre-college Committed to Excellence and Opportunity Program for students from the Flint, Beecher, and Westwood Heights school districts. The goal is to create and maintain a pipeline-to-college preparatory program that will equip young people from low-income families and minorities with the knowledge and skills necessary to enter and succeed in college. In response to the water crisis and children exposed to lead, program participants will complete a civic engagement activity designed to help Flint elementary students increase their literacy and other academic skills.

title: Committed to Excellence and Opportunity Program
description: This grant will enable the University of Michigan-Flint, via the Office of Educational Opportunity Initiatives, to continue the Committed to Excellence and Opportunity Program for students from the Flint, Beecher, and Westwood Heights school districts. The goal is to refine and maintain a pipeline-to-college preparatory program that will equip disadvantaged young people from low-income families and minorities with the knowledge and skills necessary to enter and succeed in college and career. In response to the water crisis and children exposed to lead, program participants will complete a civic engagement activity designed to help Flint elementary students increase their literacy and other academic skills.

title: Committed to Excellence and Opportunity Program
description: This grant will enable the University of Michigan-Flint, via the Office of Educational Opportunity Initiatives, to continue the Committed to Excellence and Opportunity Program for students from the Flint, Beecher, and Westwood Heights school districts. The goal is to maintain a pipeline-to-college preparatory program that equips disadvantaged youth from low-income families and minorities with the knowledge and skills necessary to enter and succeed in college and career. The program offers academic enrichment courses, leadership development workshops, project-based learning, and college visits and cultural excursions that help students and caretakers make informed decisions about post-secondary education and youth’s long-term goals.

title: Committed to Excellence and Opportunity Program
description: This grant will enable the University of Michigan-Flint, via the Office of Educational Opportunity Initiatives, to continue the Committed to Excellence and Opportunity Program for students from the Flint Community, Beecher Community, and Westwood Heights school districts. The goal is to maintain a pipeline-to-college preparatory program that equips disadvantaged youth from low-income families and minorities with the knowledge and skills necessary to enter and succeed in college and career. The program offers academic enrichment courses, leadership development workshops, project-based learning, and college visits and cultural excursions that help students and caretakers make informed decisions about post-secondary education and youth’s long-term goals.

title: Pre-College Summer Residential and Academic Year Bridge Program
description: This grant will enable the University of Michigan-Flint, via the Office of Educational Opportunity Initiatives, to pilot and expand a precollege summer residential and academic year bridge program for rising ninth-grade students. The goal of this initiative is to provide 50 students from the Flint, Beecher, and Westwood Heights school districts with a linked comprehensive summer and yearlong academic experience that will allow participating students to experience college, explore potential areas of study, learn about the college-going process, and most importantly take academic courses for skill-building purposes.

title: Flint Farmers Market Roof Repair
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: In 2002, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation began operating and maintaining the Flint Farmers Market. Since then, the corporation and its supporting organization, the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, have installed a new electrical system, repaved the parking lot, added vendor variety, increased advertising, and expanded programs for low-income customers. The market is a centrally located, countywide destination for fresh produce and locally grown food. During the grant period, the grantee will repair and replace portions of the roof and ceiling beams.

title: General Purposes
description: The Philanthropic Collaborative is a nonpartisan organization that brings together foundations, nonprofits, and elected officials to provide information to policymakers and the general public about the positive impact of philanthropy. Its mission is to promote understanding about the important role foundations play in improving America’s communities and how foundation giving generates substantial and widespread economic and social benefits for all Americans. Over the past two years the grantee has commissioned and disseminated studies on measuring the benefits foundation giving has on the American economy, on the economic benefits of grantmaking in the health field, and on foundations’ response to the recent economic crisis. Upcoming studies will include, among other topics, the impact of foundation giving on jobs in America. Over the remainder of 2010 and 2011, the grantee plans to produce and disseminate economic analyses of philanthropy, conduct education and communication work — especially among policymakers — and expand its membership.

title: Downtown Festivals
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will support the development and production of festivals in the Flint business district by the Flint Downtown Development Authority. The mission of the organization is to foster economic development in the city center through partnerships and collaborations. To ensure the economic vitality of the burgeoning downtown merchants, the city must increase and maintain a significant level of patronage, both from local consumers and out-county visitors. The grantee plans to provide high quality entertainment that will encourage more foot traffic and draw additional clientele downtown.

title: Downtown Festivals
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: To ensure the economic health of the downtown business district, the Flint Downtown Development Authority must increase and maintain a significant level of patronage, both from local residents and out-county visitors. The grantee plans to provide high quality entertainment that will encourage more foot traffic and draw new visitors downtown. This renewal grant will help achieve this goal by funding the creation of eight new festivals, as well as supporting key annual festivals, such as Bikes on the Bricks and monthly festivals like Art Walk.

title: Downtown Festivals
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant supports the production of a series of outdoor events aimed at bringing visitors to downtown Flint in every month of the year. Downtown events help to increase foot traffic, boost sales at local businesses, and elevate downtown Flint as a regional destination for arts, culture, and entertainment. This grant increase will support the Bikes on the Bricks festival, a popular motorcycle event that attracts tourists from across the Midwest.

title: Downtown Festivals
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will support the Fourth of July Festival in downtown Flint. In cooperation with a local nonprofit formed by Flint Northwestern High School alums, a family-friendly carnival will take place as part of the holiday weekend. The mission of the Flint Downtown Development Authority is to foster economic development in the city center through partnerships with organizations and businesses working to revitalize the city.

title: Downtown Festivals
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant supports Fourth of July fireworks for Flint. In cooperation with a local nonprofit formed by Flint Northwestern High School alums, a family friendly carnival took place as part of the holiday weekend and was a prime spot for families to view fireworks from downtown. The mission of the Flint Downtown Development Authority is to foster economic development in the city center through partnerships with organizations and businesses working to revitalize the city.

title: Downtown Festivals
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant supports Fourth of July fireworks for Flint. The downtown Independence Day celebration includes a fireworks viewing party at the Flint Farmers’ Market and Rutherford Ramp, and a symphony concert at Atwood Stadium. The mission of the Flint Downtown Development Authority is to foster economic development in the city center through partnerships with organizations and businesses working to revitalize the city.

title: Flint Fireworks
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: Since 2010 the Flint Downtown Development Authority has presented the official Flint Independence Day fireworks display. In 2017 Flint area residents gathered in multiple locations throughout the city including parks, neighborhoods, and community venues such as the Flint Farmers’ Market and Atwood Stadium to watch the fireworks and celebrate the holiday. The fireworks are visible from throughout the city and the grantee estimates 10,000 or more individuals watch the show in various locations each year. This grant will support the 2018 fireworks display.

title: Flint Fireworks
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: Since 2010, the Flint Downtown Development Authority has presented the official Flint Independence Day fireworks display. In 2018, Flint area residents gathered in multiple locations throughout the city including parks, neighborhoods, and community venues to watch the fireworks and celebrate the holiday. Beginning in 2017, the fireworks became a part of the Flint Symphony Orchestra community concert at Atwood Stadium, a partnership with the Flint Institute of Music. The fireworks are visible throughout the city and the grantee estimates 10,000 or more individuals watch the show in various locations each year. This grant will support the 2019 fireworks display.

title: Fourth of July Festival
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will support the Fourth of July Festival in downtown Flint. In cooperation with various local businesses and community nonprofits, the Flint Downtown Development Authority will offer a three-on-three basketball tournament, free carnival, and a fireworks display for area residents. The grantee’s mission is to foster economic development in the city center through partnerships and collaborations.

title: Louisiana Effective Leadership Program
description: This grant will provide support to the United States-Southern Africa Center for Leadership and Public Values at Duke University for the Louisiana Effective Leadership Program. The program was created as a training vehicle to address glaring, longstanding leadership deficits in Louisiana laid bare by Hurricanes Katrina and Rita. In particular, those disasters revealed the lack of a sustained commitment to developing and advancing effective leaders, those who consistently base their decisions on universally valid moral values. From 2008 to 2010, 44 fellows completed the program. Members of each class participate in retreats; work with personal executive coaches throughout the year; complete required readings and online leadership self-assessments; define and advance planning for three (small group) public policy advocacy projects (each focused on social equity for low-income people and their children); complete their fellowship year at a closing retreat in Cape Town, South Africa; and assess their fellowship experience. During the grant period, the third and fourth classes of fellows will go through the program.

title: Property Acquisition
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will provide funds to the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation to acquire several parcels across from the Great Lakes Technology Centre. The acquisition is part of the city of Flint’s overall strategy to improve the South Saginaw Street corridor between Atherton and Hemphill roads. The two structures on the property will be removed, and the site will be converted to green space, providing Saginaw Street access to the city-owned Windiate Park. The grantee will provide the grant funds to its supported organization, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, which intends to utilize the funds to purchase the property.

title: Promoting Environmental and Social Standards in the Financial Sector
description: This grant will support Urgewald’s efforts to establish strong, binding environmental and social standards for international financial institutions and to garner ongoing public support for responsible and accountable financial institutions. To achieve these goals, the grantee undertakes research, education, and advocacy efforts with a global network of local communities, nongovernmental organizations, and other partners. During the previous grant, the grantee helped shape the human rights policy of the German ministry of development to ensure that vulnerable groups and the environment are not negatively impacted by large-scale infrastructure and energy investments. During this grant period, the grantee will undertake policy advocacy efforts to ensure progressive German policies and decisions at international financial institutions, particularly related to the World Bank safeguard and extractive industry reviews; monitor Germany’s export credit agency; and organize dialogues with private banks on developing policies and practices that support sustainable development.

title: Promoting Environmental and Social Standards in the Financial Sector
description: This grant will support Urgewald’s efforts to establish strong, binding environmental and social standards for international financial institutions and to garner ongoing public support for responsible and accountable public international financial institutions. To achieve these goals, the grantee undertakes research, education, and advocacy efforts with a global network of local communities, nongovernmental organizations, and other partners. Over the past grant period, the grantee has highlighted key issues related to the scope of the World Bank Group safeguard policies and the inclusion of global norms related to indigenous communities. During this grant period, the grantee will continue its advocacy efforts to ensure strong German policies and decisions at international financial institutions, particularly related to the World Bank and other European international financial institution safeguard policy reviews.

title: Promoting Environmental and Social Standards in the Financial Sector
description: Urgewald works to establish strong, binding environmental and social standards for international financial institutions and to garner ongoing public support for responsible and accountable public international financial institutions. To achieve these goals, the grantee undertakes research, education, and advocacy efforts with a global network of local communities, nongovernmental organizations, and other partners. This grant increase will expand the scope of their efforts to include the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank and the 2016 Asian Development Bank annual meeting to be held in Germany.

title: Promoting Environmental and Social Standards in the Financial Sector
description: Urgewald works to establish strong, binding environmental and social standards for international development finance institutions and to garner ongoing public support for responsible and accountable public international financial institutions. To achieve these goals, the grantee undertakes research, education, and advocacy efforts with a global network of local communities, nongovernmental organizations, and other partners. Urgewald has played a key role in ensuring that the World Bank Group’s environmental and social safeguards continue to maintain the highest standards for development finance lending. Over the next grant period, the grantee will provide an analysis of the impacts of international development finance and the environmental and social standards needed to protect communities.

title: Promoting Environmental and Social Standards in the Financial Sector
description: Urgewald works to establish strong, binding environmental and social standards for international development finance institutions and to gain ongoing public support for responsible and accountable public international financial institutions. To achieve these goals, the grantee undertakes research, education, and advocacy efforts with a global network of local communities, nongovernmental organizations, and other partners. Urgewald has played a key role in ensuring that the World Bank Group and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank’s environmental and social framework continue to maintain the highest standards for development finance lending. Over the next grant period, the grantee will monitor implementation of these banks’ environmental and social policies and ensure that their lending is in support of global goals on energy access.

title: Promoting Environmental and Social Standards in the Financial Sector
description: This grant will support Urgewald’s efforts to establish strong, binding environmental and social standards for international financial institutions and to garner ongoing public support for responsible and accountable financial institutions. To achieve these goals, the grantee undertakes research, education, and advocacy efforts with a global network of local communities, nongovernmental organizations, and other partners. This grant will support the grantee’s assistance to nongovernmental organizations from developing and transition countries where German companies and banks are involved; policy advocacy efforts to ensure progressive German policies and decisions within the multilateral development banks; oversight of Germany’s export credit agency and other similar government-backed financial instruments; and dialogues with private banks on developing progressive policies and practices.

title: Eco-Separation of the Chicago Area Waterway System to Prevent Invasion of Asian Carp
geographic_focus: Pennsylvania, New York, Ohio, Ontario, Indiana, Michigan, Wisconsin, Minnesota
description: The Chicago area waterway system offers the most direct highway for Asian Carp and other aquatic invasive species to swim into the Great Lakes from the Mississippi River system. Severing this connection remains one of the highest priorities for protecting the Great Lakes’ ecosystem. With previous Mott support, the Great Lakes Commission worked with regional decisionmakers and stakeholders on a report that analyzed the best options for constructing a barrier between the two watersheds. Governed by delegations from each of the Great Lakes states and provinces, the grantee was established in 1955 to protect and conserve the water resources of the Great Lakes Basin. With this grant, the grantee will disseminate, and build upon, the findings of its report and work with a range of partners to inform and expedite a permanent Asian Carp solution for the Chicago area waterway system.

title: Eco-Separation of the Chicago Area Waterway System to Prevent Invasion of Asian Carp
geographic_focus: Minnesota, Wisconsin, Indiana, Michigan, Ontario, Ohio, Pennsylvania, New York
description: Governed by delegations from each of the Great Lakes states and provinces, the Great Lakes Commission was established in 1955 to protect and conserve the water resources of the Great Lakes Basin. An urgent threat is that of Asian Carp, an invasive species that is poised to enter and disrupt the Great Lakes ecosystem. Electric barriers have not stopped the invasive fish from arriving at the doorstep of Lake Michigan via its connections to the Mississippi River. With partial Mott support, the commission will bring together decisionmakers and stakeholders from across the Great Lakes to identify how to restore the natural division between the two water bodies as a way to halt Asian Carp movement while also providing economic, social, and environmental benefits to the region.

title: Program Support
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Flint Institute of Music is the home of the Flint Symphony Orchestra, the Flint School of Performing Arts, and the Flint Youth Theatre. The Flint Institute of Music is focused on providing a variety of music, dance, and theatre opportunities for residents of all ages. Annually, about 300,000 children and adults take lessons, receive educational programming, and attend concerts and performances offered by the grantee. This grant will provide support for: 1) a community-wide band and orchestra festival for area high school musicians; 2) phase 1 of the development of Flint Youth Theatre’s original production of “The Nourish Project”; 3) a world class violinist to perform with the Flint Symphony Orchestra; and 4) development of a new strategic plan for the music institute.

title: Program Support
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Flint Institute of Music is the home of the Flint Symphony Orchestra, the Flint School of Performing Arts, and the Flint Youth Theatre. The Flint Institute of Music is focused on providing a variety of music, dance, and theatre opportunities for residents of all ages. Annually, nearly 300,000 children and adults take lessons, receive educational programming, and attend concerts and performances offered by the institute. This grant will provide support: 1) to the Black Classical Music Family Festival; 2) to extend the ABC12 television broadcast of the symphony’s Holiday Pops concert and the Music in the Parks Back to the Bricks performance; 3) to assist with the hosting of the Limonest (France) Youth Symphony Orchestra in Flint; and 4) for strategic planning and professional development costs of the Flint Youth Theatre.

title: Kearsley Streetscape
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to the Flint Cultural Center Corporation will provide the local match requirement for the Kearsley Streetscape project. Kearsley Street runs through the middle of the Flint Cultural Center campus and connects the campus to the downtown. A transportation enhancement grant from the Michigan Department of Transportation will fund nearly half of the project’s cost. The Kearsley Streetscape project is intended to slow the flow of traffic through the campus, improve the appearance of the street, and make it more pedestrian friendly, for both walking and bicycling. The project will add crosswalks; create bicycle lanes; install new ornamental, energy-efficient streetlights; repair sidewalks; and add trees and other landscaping.

title: Kearsley Streetscape
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to the Flint Cultural Center Corporation will allow engineering work to be completed on the proposed Kearsley Streetscape enhancements. Kearsley Street runs through the middle of the Flint Cultural Center campus and connects the campus to the downtown. A conditional commitment by the Michigan Department of Transportation will fund about one half of the project’s construction cost. The Kearsley Streetscape project is intended to slow the flow of traffic through the campus, improve the appearance of the street, and make it more pedestrian friendly, for both walking and bicycling. The project will add crosswalks; create bicycle lanes; install new ornamental, energy-efficient lighting; repair sidewalks; and add trees and other landscaping.

title: Diaspora Philanthropy Conference and Toolkit
description: The program goal is to encourage the growth and effectiveness of diaspora philanthropy globally. Based on a long and successful track record in this field, the American Ireland Fund will produce a Global Diaspora Strategies Toolkit with practical examples on how to develop diaspora philanthropy programs. The toolkit will be a guide for governments, corporations, foundations, and individuals interested in developing programs in this area. Following the production of the toolkit, the grantee will work together with the U.S. State Department to organize a conference. The conference will focus on best practices in diaspora philanthropy and will highlight the work being done in this field throughout the world. The grantee is part of a global group of organizations called the Ireland Funds. Its mission is to be the largest worldwide network of people of Irish ancestry and friends of Ireland dedicated to raising funds to support programs of peace and reconciliation, arts and culture, education, and community development throughout Ireland.

title: Affinity Group for National Associations
grantee: CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation
description: The program goal is to strengthen the capacity of national associations of civil society organizations globally. The Affinity Group for National Associations, an initiative of CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation, accomplishes this through convening, coordinating, information-sharing, skills building, and networking activities. Over the next two years, the grantee will convene annual and regional meetings of the national associations; develop a resource guide for national associations and their members to be used for workshops and trainings; organize peer learning exchange visits; provide back-office support to regional networks of national associations; help national associations with developing membership strategies; provide advice on working with governments; and create communities of practice on issues of legitimacy, transparency, and accountability. The affinity group currently has 60 members from around the world. CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation is an international alliance established in 1993 to strengthen citizen action and civil society worldwide.

title: Affinity Group of National Associations
grantee: CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation
description: The program goal is to strengthen the capacity of national associations of civil society organizations globally. The Affinity Group of National Associations, a network which currently has 64 members from around the world, is managed by CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation. Over the past several years, member convenings, working groups, and peer learning exchanges have focused on issues such as relations between civil society and government, transparency and accountability, an enabling environment for civil society, and the development of advocacy tools. Over the next two years, the project goals are to develop four strong regional subgroups, foster international solidarity against national civil society restrictions, extend the membership base, facilitate knowledge-sharing opportunities, realign working groups with thematic and network priorities, and enhance capacity development opportunities. CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation is an international alliance established in 1993 to strengthen citizen action and civil society worldwide.

title: Affinity Group of National Associations
grantee: CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation
description: The program goal is to strengthen the capacity of national associations of civil society organizations globally. The Affinity Group of National Associations, a network which currently has 87 members from around the world, is managed by CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation. Over the past two years the network convened and nurtured regional subgroups, fostered solidarity within the network, maximized the exchange of opportunities and resources, better aligned the network with CIVICUS initiatives, and developed capacities and shared knowledge. Over the next two years, the network’s goals are to strengthen the role and services of the network as an effective global hub for national associations, to facilitate exchanges for better solidarity and interconnectivity between national and regional associations, and to strengthen the legitimacy and accountability of the network. CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation is an international alliance established in 1993 to strengthen citizen action and civil society worldwide.

title: Affinity Group for National Associations
grantee: CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation
description: The program goal is to strengthen the capacity of national associations of civil society organizations globally. The Affinity Group for National Associations, an initiative of CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation, accomplishes this through convening, coordinating, information sharing, skills building, and networking activities. Over the next two years, the association will convene annual and regional meetings of the national associations; develop a resource guide for national associations and their members to be used for workshops and trainings; organize peer learning exchange visits; provide back-office support to regional networks of national associations; help national associations with developing membership strategies; provide advice on working with governments; and create communities of practice on issues of legitimacy, transparency, and accountability. The association currently has 58 members from around the world. CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation is an international alliance established in 1993 to strengthen citizen action and civil society worldwide.

title: Michigan Latino Nonprofit Leadership Academy
description: This grant will support the participation of five Latino nonprofits from Flint in the Michigan Latino Nonprofit Leadership Academy. Organized by the Center for Leadership Innovation, the academy will offer a year-long transformative experience focusing on the self-development of emerging Latino nonprofit leaders, organizational capacity building, and peer-to-peer networking.

title: Virginia Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Virginia Child Care Resource and Referral Network which coordinates the Virginia Statewide Afterschool Network. In addition to continuing the network’s core work to advance afterschool in Virginia, the network will work to increase the availability of high quality afterschool programs through developing and implementing new afterschool program standards and an afterschool quality model. The grantee will also pilot new afterschool programs to increase youth access to learning opportunities in science, technology, engineering, and math. To ensure that new models and best practices are incorporated nationally, the network will share lessons learned and products with other state networks.

title: Virginia Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant to Alternatives, Inc., will support the Virginia Statewide Afterschool Network to continue to build an afterschool and summer learning system that improves outcomes for children and youth through school-based or school-linked afterschool programs. Over the next three years, the network will support the development of policy, partnerships, and quality initiatives to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific projects will: 1) create a sustainable structure of statewide, regional, and local partnerships, particularly school-community partnerships, to increase coordination and support for out-of-school time programs; 2) create a database of funders focused on out-of-school time, STEM, and resource data; and 3) create a professional development endorsement procedure for out-of-school time programs to adopt recommended quality models.

title: Virginia Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support James Madison University, which coordinates the Virginia Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships, and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) build key champions focused on STEM and afterschool to help address the growing workforce needs in Virginia; 2) develop an afterschool map by region to showcase current investments in afterschool throughout Virginia; 3) deepen the focus on college and career readiness within afterschool programs; and 4) support the development and distribution of the new afterschool program content in collaboration with the Foundation’s thematic partners.

title: Virginia Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Virginia Child Care Resource and Referral Network in its efforts to develop the Virginia Statewide Afterschool Network. The Virginia Statewide Afterschool Network seeks to sustain, nurture, and grow the network comprised of key agencies, organizations, and stakeholders from across Virginia. The network will be committed to increasing capacity and support to coordinate a system of high quality afterschool that supports the academic, social, emotional, and physical development of children and youth. Lessons learned and products will be shared with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: Building Acquisition
description: The Robert E. Weiss Advocacy Center for Children and Youth was created from a merger of the Child Advocacy Center of Genesee County and the Consortium on Child Abuse and Neglect. The grantee focuses on two aspects of child abuse and neglect: protection for children who need immediate help and prevention services that will break the cycle of abuse. The grantee is a community-based organization that is uniquely designed to provide comprehensive and coordinated advocacy, education, prevention, and investigative services for children in Genesee County. This grant will enable the grantee to acquire the property that currently serves as one of its two locations and fits the unique functional needs of the agency and the very vulnerable children it serves.

title: Employment Training for the Staff
description: The Disability Network was founded in 1993 to provide services and supports to people with any type of disability in Flint and Genesee County. The grantee connects people and organizations with services and programs that provide advocacy, technology, financial, educational, employment, accessibility, housing, healthcare, and basic living assistance to people with disabilities. The purpose of this grant is to enable 20 members of the grantee’s staff and employment counselors to participate in interview training in order to increase the effectiveness and efficiency of the network’s employment services.

title: Great Lakes Program
description: The Michigan Environmental Council, a leading statewide environmental policy group based in Lansing, works on a range of water policy activities facing the state, including effective implementation of the Great Lakes Compact, the Clean Water Act, and related matters. With renewal support, the grantee will continue to play this important state-level policy role while also building its own organizational capacity through a variety of means, such as expanding outreach to individual donors.

title: Great Lakes Program
description: The Michigan Environmental Council, a leading statewide environmental policy group based in Lansing, works on a range of water policy activities facing the state, including effective implementation of the Great Lakes Compact, the Clean Water Act, and related matters. With renewal support, the grantee will continue to play this important state-level policy role while also building its own organizational capacity through a variety of means.

title: Great Lakes Program
description: The Michigan Environmental Council is a leading statewide organization committed to protecting freshwater ecosystems. Previous support allowed the grantee to address a range of water policy issues, including implementation of the Great Lakes Compact and Clean Water Act and preventing the spread of aquatic invasive species. With this grant increase, the grantee will examine ways to broaden its freshwater protection programs to address the drinking water management challenges facing communities in Michigan.

title: Great Lakes Program
description: Founded in 1980, Michigan Environmental Council is a statewide environmental nonprofit organization based in Lansing. With prior Mott support, the grantee helped implement the Great Lakes Compact, the Clean Water Act, and other freshwater policies that protect and restore the Great Lakes ecosystem. In light of Flint’s drinking water crisis, the grantee also examined ways to update its freshwater protection programs to address the types of water infrastructure challenges facing Michigan’s older industrialized cities. With renewed support, the grantee will continue its focus on reforming and implementing freshwater policies while also developing new, integrated approaches to addressing the safety, efficiency, and affordability of drinking water, stormwater, and wastewater systems at the municipal level.

title: Creating a 21st Century Water Management System in Michigan
description: Founded in 1980, the Michigan Environmental Council is one of Michigan’s premier voices in Lansing for protection of the Great Lakes and Michigan’s environment. With prior support, the grantee focused on drinking water in the wake of Flint’s water crisis, interviewed local and national experts, performed background research, created a drinking water tool kit, and a new drinking water framework. They remain active on critical state policy discussions including a new lead and copper rule and funding for water infrastructure. With this renewal grant, the grantee will organize its work to make water governance transparent and accountable, compile maps and data to raise awareness of drinking water problems and solutions, seek policy and funding improvements to protect the Great Lakes, and seek to elevate water as a high-priority topic for Michigan residents.

title: Great Lakes Program
description: While the economic and environmental importance of Michigan’s water resources is widely recognized, the state’s lakes, rivers, and wetlands are under significant stress due to a combination of factors. The Michigan Environmental Council, a leading statewide environmental policy group based in Lansing, proposes a full range of activities to address the water quality and water quantity challenges facing the state, including effective implementation of the Great Lakes Compact, Clean Water Act, and related state policies. The grantee will also build its own organizational capacity through a variety of means, such as launching new fundraising initiatives for individual donors.

title: Great Lakes Water Program
description: The Great Lakes provide social, recreational, and economic benefits to the state of Wisconsin. Clean Wisconsin is a statewide environmental organization committed to protecting and restoring its state’s portion of the Great Lakes ecosystem. With this grant, the grantee will seek to improve implementation of the Great Lakes Compact, strengthen high priority water management and water quality policies, and protect the Great Lakes from mining-related threats. Clean Wisconsin will also build its own organizational capacity.

title: Great Lakes Water Program
description: Clean Wisconsin is a statewide environmental organization committed to protecting and restoring the portion of the Great Lakes ecosystem that falls within Wisconsin’s boundaries. With prior Mott support, the grantee helped reform and implement water management and water quality policies while also strengthening its own organizational capacity. This grant increase will allow the grantee to conduct technical analyses related to a major Great Lakes water diversion request and also enhance public communications efforts.

title: Great Lakes Water Program
description: More than half of Wisconsin’s population lives within the Great Lakes watershed. This freshwater ecosystem provides residents with an array of important social, recreational, and economic benefits. Clean Wisconsin is a statewide environmental organization that seeks to protect and restore Great Lakes waterways. With previous Mott support, the grantee helped implement the Great Lakes Compact, reduce pollution into Great Lakes waterways, and protect groundwater resources. With renewed support, the grantee will continue these efforts while developing staff leadership skills and improving public outreach strategies.

title: Great Lakes Water Program
description: More than half of Wisconsin’s population lives within the Great Lakes watershed, and Clean Wisconsin is a statewide environmental organization that seeks to protect and restore Great Lakes waters. With prior Mott support, the grantee helped implement the Great Lakes Compact, reduce pollution into Great Lakes waterways, and protect groundwater resources. With renewed support, the grantee will continue such efforts by promoting measures that protect surface water, groundwater, and drinking water; building partnerships with a wide variety of stakeholders and partners; and strengthening its own organization with a focus on board development.

title: Great Lakes Water Program
description: The Great Lakes ecosystem provides economic, cultural, and social benefits to all Wisconsin residents. Clean Wisconsin is a statewide environmental organization committed to keeping the Great Lakes healthy. With this grant, the grantee will seek to improve implementation of the Great Lakes Compact, strengthen high priority water management and water quality policies, and protect the Great Lakes from mining-related threats. The grantee will also build its own organizational capacity through efforts such as diversifying revenue streams.

title: Great Lakes Water Program
description: Ontario has nearly 3,000 miles of Great Lakes shoreline — more than any single state in the United States. Based in Toronto, Environmental Defence is a national environmental organization with a demonstrated commitment to protecting the Great Lakes. With previous Mott support, the grantee informed the development and implementation of the U.S.-Canada Great Lakes Water Quality Agreement, conducted research and analyses to strengthen Ontario’s water policies, built public support for Great Lakes issues, and took measures to strengthen its internal operations. With renewed Mott support, the grantee will continue these efforts in partnership with nonprofit, private, and public partners in Ontario.

title: Great Lakes Water Program
description: Ontario has nearly 3,000 miles of Great Lakes shoreline — more than any single state in the United States. Based in Toronto, Environmental Defence is a national environmental organization with a demonstrated commitment to protecting the Great Lakes. With previous Mott support, the grantee assisted with implementation of the U.S.-Canada Great Lakes Water Quality Agreement, conducted research and analyses to strengthen Ontario’s water policies, and took measures to build its organizational capacity. With renewed Mott support, the grantee will continue these efforts, with a specific focus on reducing harmful algal blooms, decreasing toxic pollution, and building public support for protecting the Great Lakes.

title: Great Lakes Water Program
description: Ontario has nearly 3,000 miles of Great Lakes shoreline—more than any single state in the United States. Based in Toronto, Environmental Defence is a national environmental organization with a demonstrated commitment to protecting the Great Lakes. With previous Mott support, the grantee undertook a range of activities including assisting with implementation of the U.S.-Canada Great Lakes Water Quality Agreement, conducting research and analyses to strengthen Ontario’s water policies, and building its own organizational capacity. With renewed support, the grantee will build on these past efforts, with a focus on further implementation of meaningful policy commitments, through activities in five core areas.

title: Safeguarding the Great Lakes
description: The Great Lakes are facing threats that include toxic algae blooms, excess nutrients, and other pollution. Lake Erie is plagued by increasingly frequent algae blooms, which threaten drinking water and fish, clog intake pipes, and deter visitors. To help address these issues, and secure long-lasting protection for the Great Lakes and Ontario’s source water, Environmental Defence Canada has used previous support from the Mott Foundation to work with community and government leaders, to advance Ontario and Canadian water protection policies and programs. With renewed support, the grantee will engage and educate stakeholders, and participate in opportunities to help ensure the health and restoration of the Great Lakes.

title: Great Lakes Water Program
description: Based in Toronto, Environmental Defence is a national environmental organization with a demonstrated commitment to protecting the Great Lakes. With previous Mott support, the grantee worked in Ontario to improve Great Lakes water quality by increasing public engagement and influencing relevant policies. With this grant, Mott will support the full breadth of the organization’s Great Lakes efforts, including both water quality and water management initiatives. Specifically, the grantee will work with regional partners to inform the development and implementation of the U.S.-Canada Great Lakes Water Quality Agreement; strengthen Ontario’s water policies, in part through research and analyses; and build public support for Great Lakes issues. The organization will also take measures to strengthen its internal operations.

title: Lake Superior Water Quality Project
description: Minnesota has almost 200 miles of shoreline along Lake Superior, with many more miles of waterfront along rivers that drain into the lake. These waterfront properties provide important ecological habitats and also attract vacationers, retirees, families, recreational users, and industries. The Minnesota Center for Environmental Advocacy, a statewide nonprofit environmental organization, seeks to balance these uses with the help of legal and scientific information. With previous Mott support, the grantee conducted technical reviews of proposals to mine sulfide-based ores, provided data and analyses to the agencies responsible for managing environmental risks, and helped build citizen awareness. With renewed support, the grantee will continue to protect the Lake Superior basin by ensuring the Clean Water Act requirements are upheld and by helping improve wetland policies, assisting municipalities in updating water protection practices, and helping stop the spread of aquatic invasive species.

title: Lake Superior Water Quality Project
description: Lake Superior holds ten percent of the world’s available fresh surface water and is the most pristine of all the Great Lakes. The Minnesota Center for Environmental Advocacy, founded in 1974, is a nonprofit organization that uses law, science, and research to protect Minnesota’s portion of the Lake Superior watershed. With prior support, the grantee partnered with government agencies and other nonprofits to address threats posed by mining projects, wetlands destruction, aquatic invasive species, and polluted sediment runoff. This renewal will allow the grantee to continue helping the state of Minnesota comply with the Clean Water Act, improve wetlands policies, update shoreline protections, and stop the spread of invasive species in Lake Superior.

title: Lake Superior Water Resources Project
description: The Minnesota Center for Environmental Advocacy has been a leading legal and scientific voice for Minnesota’s environment since 1974. With previous Mott support, the grantee has advocated for the protection of Minnesota wetlands; worked to restore Lake Superior watersheds; sought to protect Lake Superior from invasive species; worked to improve access and affordability to clean, safe water in Minnesota; and sought to protect the Lake Superior watershed from threats from mining activities. With continued support, the grantee will advance efforts to protect Lake Superior from invasive species coming from ballast water discharges, ensure that solutions to drinking and wastewater infrastructure address affordability and protect against nitrate pollution, and protect against mining threats and reform mining laws to protect Lake Superior. Funding will also help to secure a consultant to guide an effort to improve their outreach and engagement with diverse constituencies.

title: Minnesota Sulfide Ore Mining Project
description: The Minnesota Center for Environmental Advocacy is a statewide nonprofit environmental organization with a commitment to using law, science, and research to preserve and protect Lake Superior and its connected waterways. With Mott support, the grantee will conduct technical reviews of proposals to mine sulfide-based ores and will provide feedback to the agencies responsible for managing environmental risks. The grantee will also work with partners to improve public awareness of water quality threats and increase citizen participation in public engagement processes.

title: General Purposes
description: Partners for Democratic Change is an international organization committed to building sustainable capacity to advance civil society and a culture of change and conflict management worldwide. The grantee works with practitioners at 20 independent networked centers providing leadership development, training, technical assistance, and knowledge advancement. In the coming year, the grantee will develop new centers; promote change management processes around key issues such as anticorruption, youth violence prevention, democratic governance in Muslim societies, and climate change; and ensure ongoing quality services by improving core skills, developing an evaluation plan, increasing academic alliances, and improving knowledge management systems within the centers’ network.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Boy Scouts of America - Port Huron
description: This grant provides general purpose funds to support the array of outdoor, educational, and leadership programming offered through the Boy Scouts of America – Tall Pine Council to children, youth, and their families in Genesee, Lapeer, and Shiawassee counties. The grantee operates two camp sites within the tricounty area. In addition to serving youth who participate in the area’s various boy scout and cub scout troops, Tall Pine Council operates an urban scouting program that serves urban youth who are economically and educationally at risk.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Boy Scouts of America - Port Huron
description: The Boy Scouts of America – Tall Pine Council is one of the largest youth organizations serving Genesee, Lapeer, and Shiawassee counties with over 14,000 youth (ages 5 to 20) participating annually. The grantee focuses on character development, leadership, physical fitness, and citizenship to fulfill its mission of preparing young people to make ethical choices throughout their lifetime. Services are delivered through a variety of programs, including Cub Scouts, Boy Scouts, Varsity Scouting, Venturing, and Exploring. In addition, the Learning for Life program provides a school-based program for special-needs students, and the Urban Scouting initiative brings scouting to young people, mostly in inner cities, for whom scouts is not always easily accessible.

title: Louisiana Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Education’s Next Horizon which coordinates the Louisiana Statewide Afterschool Network. Building on successful efforts to convene policymakers, afterschool providers, youth and families, businesses, school districts, regional funders, state agencies, and youth advocates to formalize a governance structure and decisionmaking process for the network, the grantee’s efforts will focus on building a sustainable state afterschool infrastructure and the capacity to respond to demands for high quality afterschool programs across the state. Lessons learned and products created will be shared with the National Network of Statewide Afterschool Networks.

title: Louisiana Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant to Louisiana Tech University will support the Louisiana Statewide Afterschool Network to continue to build an afterschool and summer learning system that improves outcomes for children and youth through school-based or school-linked afterschool programs. Over the next three years, the network will support the development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will: 1) leverage partnerships with key stakeholders and state agencies to increase coordination and support for afterschool programs; 2) increase the capacity of the network to provide quality training for afterschool programs in the state; and 3) host regional summits on quality afterschool practices and provide professional development for afterschool staff.

title: Louisiana Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Louisiana Tech University, which coordinates the Louisiana Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships, and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) collect and analyze data to create a statewide report on afterschool in Louisiana; 2) coordinate a quality-based evaluation process for Louisiana’s STEM-based afterschool programs; 3) foster sustainability for afterschool programs; and 4) support the development and distribution of the new afterschool program content in collaboration with the Foundation’s thematic partners.

title: Louisiana Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Education’s Next Horizon in its efforts to develop the Louisiana Statewide Afterschool Network. The network seeks to develop a strategy for the long-term sustainability of afterschool programs and the network. First steps include convening policymakers, afterschool providers, youth and families, businesses, school districts, regional funders, state agencies, and youth advocates to formalize a structure and decisionmaking process for the network. The network will also map the landscape of afterschool programs in Louisiana and conduct a statewide needs assessment for training and professional development. Lessons learned and products will be shared with the national network of statewide afterschool networks.

title: Developing Central Office for ACCION USA
description: ACCION USA seeks to expand its services to meet the growing needs of small businesses. This network heads into its 20th year in the United States. It has established a goal to serve one million entrepreneurs by 2020. In order to meet this goal efficiently and effectively, a centralized approach for building the program to scale will be developed. This grant will help finance a central office dedicated to developing, nurturing, and advancing a network of world class microfinance organizations in order to create lasting economic vibrancy for low-income, small business owners and their communities across the United States.

title: Downtown Security
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will provide support to the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation to promote safety and security in downtown Flint. The grantee will provide the grant funds to its supported organization, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, to provide for a uniformed security presence to patrol, both on foot and in car, the area around the 400 and 500 blocks of South Saginaw Street in downtown Flint.

title: Downtown Security
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant provides support to the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation to promote safety and security in downtown Flint. The grantee will provide grant funds to its supported organization, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, for a uniformed security presence to patrol — on foot and in car — the area around the 400 and 500 blocks of South Saginaw Street in downtown Flint. This grant increase will provide for a second uniformed security guard to patrol this area.

title: Downtown Security
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will provide support to the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation to promote safety and security in downtown Flint. The grantee will provide the grant funds to its supported organization, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, for a uniformed security presence to patrol, both on foot and in car, the area around the 400 and 500 blocks of South Saginaw Street in downtown Flint.

title: Downtown Security
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will provide support to the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation to promote safety and security in downtown Flint. The grantee will provide funds to its supported organization, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, to contract the services of uniformed security guards to patrol the area around the 400 and 500 blocks of South Saginaw Street in downtown Flint and the emerging Health and Wellness District.

title: Downtown Security
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This renewal grant will continue support to the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation to promote public safety and security in downtown Flint. The grantee will provide grant funds to its supported organization, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, to contract services of uniformed security guards to patrol redevelopment areas in downtown Flint.

title: Downtown Security
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will provide renewal funds to the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation to promote safety and security in downtown Flint. The grantee is dedicated to supporting revitalization projects in downtown Flint that enhance quality of life and provide local and regional access to jobs, food, healthcare, and other essential services. The Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, a supported organization of the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, will contract services of uniformed security guards to patrol the areas around the 400 and 500 blocks of South Saginaw Street in downtown Flint and the adjacent Health and Wellness District to the east of Saginaw Street.

title: Downtown Security
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will provide renewal funds to the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation to promote safety and security in downtown Flint. The grantee is dedicated to supporting revitalization projects in downtown Flint that enhance quality of life and provide local and regional access to jobs, food, healthcare, and other essential services. The Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, a supported organization of the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, will contract services of uniformed security guards to patrol the areas around the 400 and 500 blocks of South Saginaw Street in downtown Flint and the adjacent Health and Wellness District to the east of Saginaw Street for regular security rotation and special events.

title: Downtown Security
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will support the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation’s efforts to promote safety and security in downtown Flint. The grantee is dedicated to supporting revitalization projects in downtown Flint that enhance quality of life and provide local and regional access to jobs, food, healthcare, and other essential services. The Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, a supported organization of the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, will contract services of uniformed security guards to patrol the areas around the 400 and 500 blocks of South Saginaw Street in downtown Flint and the adjacent Health and Wellness District to the east of Saginaw Street for regular security rotation and special events.

grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will support the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation’s efforts to promote safety and security in downtown Flint. The grantee is dedicated to supporting revitalization projects that enhance quality of life and provide local and regional access to jobs, food, healthcare, and other essential services. The Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, a supported organization of the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, will contract services of uniformed security guards to patrol the areas around the 400 and 500 blocks of South Saginaw Street and the adjacent Health and Wellness District.

title: Downtown Security
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will support the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation’s efforts to promote safety and security in downtown Flint. The Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, a supported organization of the grantee, will contract services of uniformed security guards to patrol the areas around the 400 and 500 blocks of South Saginaw Street and adjacent alleys and districts.

title: Downtown Security
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will support the expansion of a pilot project by the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation and its supporting organization, the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, to promote safety and security in downtown Flint. A uniformed security presence will patrol on foot and in car the area around the 400 and 500 blocks of South Saginaw Street in downtown Flint.

title: Michigan Transportation Reform Partnership
description: The Michigan Environmental Council, a statewide environmental organization representing more than 70 partner groups, has continued to deepen and expand its role as a leader in transportation policy issues in recent years. This includes serving as lead coordinator and convener in developing a transportation reform partnership in Michigan that includes a diverse network of key organizations from across the state. This renewal grant will allow the grantee to continue developing and strengthening the partnership to move Michigan toward a seamless, multimodal transportation system; increase investment in underfunded modes that expand transportation access; foster citizen engagement in transportation policy decisions; and improve the connection between transportation planning and community economic development.

title: Michigan Transportation Reform Partnership
description: The Michigan Environmental Council, a statewide environmental organization representing more than 70 partner groups, has continued its role as a leader in transportation policy issues in recent years. This includes serving as coordinator and convener of a transportation reform partnership in Michigan that includes a diverse network of key organizations from across the state. This renewal grant will allow the grantee to continue developing and strengthening the partnership to move Michigan toward a seamless, multimodal transportation system; increase investment in all transportation modes; foster citizen engagement in transportation policy decisions; and improve the connection between transportation planning and community economic development.

title: Michigan Transportation Reform Partnership
description: This grant increase will support the Michigan Environmental Council’s efforts to coordinate a network of groups across the state that seeks to move Michigan toward a seamless, multimodal transportation system and increase investment in all transportation modes. The grantee is a statewide environmental organization representing more than 70 partner groups.

title: Michigan Transportation Reform Partnership
description: The Michigan Environmental Council, a statewide environmental organization representing more than 70 partner groups, has become deeply engaged in transportation policy issues in recent years. With the council as lead coordinator and convener, this grant will build a transportation reform partnership in Michigan that includes a diverse network of key organizations from across the state. The grant will support work to move Michigan toward a seamless, multimodal transportation system; increase investment in underfunded modes that expand transportation access; foster citizen engagement in transportation policy decisions; and improve the connection between transportation planning and community economic development.

title: Flint Wayfinding Project
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: As investments in downtown Flint progress, it has become apparent that newcomers and longtime residents alike are finding it difficult to find the way to their desired destinations. This is true whether they are travelling by car, bus, bicycle, or on foot. Flint needs a comprehensive and easy-to-use system to address the mobility needs of visitors and residents. The Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation will provide the grant funds to its supported organization, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, to develop such a long-term and comprehensive wayfinding plan for Flint’s central business district and surrounding institutional destinations. In addition to developing such a plan, the grant will also cover early implementation costs.

title: Great Lakes Sulfide Ore Mining Project
grantee: Great Lakes Indian Fish and Wildlife Commission
description: Representing the interests of 11 Ojibwe tribes, the Great Lakes Indian Fish and Wildlife Commission is a nonprofit organization that helps its members manage natural resources on tribal lands and in areas where members have treaty-guaranteed rights to hunt, fish, and gather. The mining of sulfide-based ores (sulfide mining) poses significant water quality threats to tribally important areas around Lake Superior. With prior Mott support, the commission prepared a report examining how tribes can engage in permitting and monitoring sulfide mining operations. This grant renewal will allow the grantee to implement report recommendations, which include conducting research, engaging with technical experts, and developing water quality data across the region to inform policy discussions, permitting processes, and environmental reviews.

title: Great Lakes Sulfide Ore Mining Project
grantee: Great Lakes Indian Fish and Wildlife Commission
description: Representing the interests of 11 Ojibwa tribes, the Great Lakes Indian Fish and Wildlife Commission is a nonprofit organization that helps its members manage natural resources on tribal lands and in areas where members have treaty-guaranteed rights to hunt, fish, and gather. The mining of sulfide-based ores (sulfide mining) poses significant water quality threats to tribally important areas around Lake Superior. With prior Mott support, the grantee conducted research, engaged technical experts to analyze specific water quality threats, and gathered water quality data across the region to inform policy discussions, permitting processes, and environmental reviews. This grant renewal will allow the commission to continue these efforts that improve the ability of the tribes to inform and participate in decisionmaking processes related to protecting the health of the Great Lakes.

title: Great Lakes Sulfide Ore Mining Project
grantee: Great Lakes Indian Fish and Wildlife Commission
description: Representing the interests of 11 Ojibwa tribes, the Great Lakes Indian Fish and Wildlife Commission is a nonprofit organization that helps its members to manage natural resources on tribal lands and in areas where members have treaty-guaranteed rights to hunt, fish, and gather. The mining of sulfide-based ores (sulfide mining) poses significant water quality threats to tribally important areas around Lake Superior. With prior Mott support, the grantee conducted research, engaged technical experts, and developed the expertise of tribal staff to inform policy discussions, permitting processes, and environmental reviews. The grantee will continue these efforts, along with a new water internship, to improve tribes’ ability to participate in decisionmaking related to protecting the health of the Great Lakes.

title: Tribal Science, Training and Communications Project
grantee: Great Lakes Indian Fish and Wildlife Commission
description: The Great Lakes Indian Fish and Wildlife Commission works with tribal governments in Michigan, Wisconsin, and Minnesota to protect tribal interests in the ecology of ceded territories in the northern portions of those states. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has identified and implemented steps to participate effectively in the permitting and environmental review of mining operations. With renewed support, the grantee will develop and use a model to better understand groundwater movement near mining operations, work to restore an important whitefish and lake trout spawning reef in Michigan’s Upper Peninsula, and expose students to careers in natural resource management and tribal self-governance.

title: Great Lakes Sulfide Ore Mining Project
grantee: Great Lakes Indian Fish and Wildlife Commission
description: Representing the interests of 11 Ojibwe tribes, the Great Lakes Indian Fish and Wildlife Commission is a nonprofit organization that helps its members manage natural resources on their land across the Great Lakes. The commission also assists members in protecting and enhancing their treaty-guaranteed rights to hunt, fish, and gather on tribal land transferred to U.S. federal control. Interest in the mining of sulfide-based ores has increased in the last few years, raising concerns about possible water quality impacts on the associated ecosystems and natural resources. With Mott support, the commission will prepare a report examining how tribes can fully participate in the processes for permitting and monitoring sulfide mining operations on land where tribes have hunting and fishing rights.

title: Territory of Development: Community Mobilization in Ukraine
description: The project goals are to strengthen local-level civic participation in decisionmaking and to build social capital and cohesion in Ukraine. To these ends, the Municipal Center for Humanistic Technologies “AHALAR” will mobilize local communities in Ukraine to effectively address and resolve issues of common concern.
