Through its training school, the grantee will train over 70 local activists to become social animators — promoters in their communities of effective community organizing and communications techniques. Online and social media resources will supplement offline training activities and will provide further communication channels with local communities. In 2010-2012, the grantee successfully trained 80 social animators from communities throughout Ukraine. This resulted in the implementation of over 20 sustained community projects. The project will emphasize dissemination of results and learning through two national-level conferences and publication of a handbook for practitioners. Established in 1994, the grantee is based in Chernihiv, Ukraine, and works with community leaders and activists throughout Ukraine.

title: Territory of Development: Community Mobilization in Ukraine
description: The project goals are to strengthen community-based citizen self-organization and to build social capital and cohesion in Ukraine. To these ends, the Municipal Center for Humanistic Technologies “AHALAR” will build the capacity of community leaders to be agents of participatory local development. Through its training workshops, technical assistance, and study tours, the grantee will facilitate more widespread civic engagement within participants’ respective communities. The grantee’s online platform will be expanded to include crowdfunding capability for community projects. A systematic communications campaign will link online and offline activities to build public awareness of citizen self-organization. During 2012-2014, over 100 community activists participated directly in the grantee’s cycle of training workshops and study tours and helped implement over 45 community-based projects. These included a local battery recycling program and an online resource of local social, cultural and economic resources. Established in 1994, the grantee is based in Chernihiv, Ukraine, and works with community leaders and activists throughout Ukraine.

title: Territory of Development: Community Mobilization in Ukraine
description: The project goal is to strengthen community-based citizen self-organization and to build social capital and cohesion in Ukraine. To achieve this, the Municipal Center for Humanistic Technologies “AHALAR” will build the capacity of community leaders to be agents of participatory local development. Through its training workshops, technical assistance, and study tours, the grantee will facilitate more widespread civic engagement within participants’ respective communities. It will also seek to develop at least two urban engagement hubs drawing on the growing alumni of its training and development programs. In the period 2014-2016, over 120 community activists participated directly in the grantee’s cycle of training workshops and study tours and helped implement over 40 community-based projects. Its community action-focused website now features over 650 examples of small-scale projects and regularly attracts more than 4,000 monthly visitors. Established in 1994, the grantee is based in Chernihiv, Ukraine, and works with community leaders and activists throughout Ukraine.

title: Territory of Development: Community Mobilization in Ukraine
description: The project goals are to strengthen local-level civic participation in decisionmaking and build social capital and cohesion in Ukraine. To this end, the Municipal Center for Humanistic Technologies “AHALAR” will mobilize local communities in Ukraine to effectively address and resolve issues of common concern. Specific activities will include organizing a series of trainings, study visits, and small pilot projects for community animators, other nonprofits, and the media from across Ukraine. Through these activities, more than 80 people will be trained and supported to carry out concrete projects. The project will emphasize dissemination of results and learning through two national-level conferences and publication of a handbook for practitioners. The center is based in Chernihiv, Ukraine, and works with community leaders and activists throughout Ukraine.

title: Drug Awareness Educational Campaign
description: This grant will provide funds to the Drug Free America Foundation, Inc., to wage an informational campaign to refute the legalization propaganda that seeks to normalize and legalize marijuana both for medical and nonmedical purposes. Grant funds will be used to focus on informing and training advocates to better disseminate the message against marijuana use.

title: Drug Awareness Educational Campaign
description: This grant will provide funds to the Drug Free America Foundation, Inc., to wage an informational campaign to refute the legalization propaganda that seeks to normalize and legalize marijuana both for medical and nonmedical purposes. Grant funds will be used to focus on informing and training advocates to better disseminate the message against marijuana use.

title: European Network of National Associations
geographic_focus: Malta, Estonia, Bulgaria, Portugal, Norway, Lithuania, Croatia, Austria, Romania, Slovenia, Ireland, Spain, Montenegro, Poland, United Kingdom, Turkey, Hungary, Latvia, Germany
description: The program goal is to strengthen citizen participation and give voice to civil society at the European Union level. To this end, the National Council for Voluntary Organisations will facilitate the development of the European Network of National Associations. The network was established in 2009 as an informal network of national-level, multisector associations of nonprofit organizations from 17 European countries, including seven countries from Central and Eastern Europe. The network’s mission is to enable national associations to work together and represent effectively civil society in high-level dialogue and interaction with the European Union institutions. Since its establishment, the network has organized three general meetings of its members to discuss programmatic and organizational issues, attracted new members, and successfully raised funds for its activities. The grantee was established in 1919 in England to support the development of a dynamic voluntary and community sector and represent civil society vis-à-vis the government. The grantee has over 8,000 members and is very successful in civil society capacity building and policy development on the national and European levels.

title: Kindergarten to College Evaluation
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: In August 2010, the city of San Francisco launched the Kindergarten to College Evaluation program, a children’s savings account initiative that automatically opens college savings accounts for families when they enroll their children in a kindergarten class. By September 2012, 100 percent of the city’s kindergarten population will have such accounts. With implementation well under way, the Earned Asset Resource Network’s goal for the renewal grant period is to expand its ongoing study of the evaluation to other initiatives and leverage this information to promote children’s savings accounts across the country. The grantee will identify best practices for replication and disseminate those findings in ways that encourage other communities to implement children’s savings account initiatives in cities or at the state level. Based in San Francisco, Earned Asset Resource Network, Inc., is dedicated to helping low-income families and individuals break the cycle of poverty and create new cycles of prosperity.

title: Kindergarten to College Evaluation
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: In 2011, the City and County of San Francisco launched the Kindergarten to College Program, the first universal and automatic children’s college savings program in the country. Since then, the program has opened 18,000 accounts and encouraged participating families to save over $1 million of their own funds. As the lead nonprofit partner in the Kindergarten to College Program, the Earned Asset Resource Network, Inc., helped design the program and works with the City and County of San Francisco to strengthen and improve program implementation. Renewal support will enable the grantee to design and pilot a new technology platform to simplify program administration and encourage greater participation. Based in San Francisco, the grantee is dedicated to helping low-income families and individuals break the cycle of poverty and create new cycles of prosperity.

title: Kindergarten to College Evaluation
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: In August 2010, the city of San Francisco launched the Kindergarten to College program, a children’s savings account initiative that automatically opens college savings accounts for families when they enroll their children in a kindergarten class. Because the program provides an important opportunity to expand stakeholder understanding of good policy design for such initiatives, it is critical to evaluate, from the very early stages of implementation, the program’s impact on savings, children’s college aspirations, and parent and children’s financial capabilities. Through this grant, the Earned Assets Resource Network will employ multiple Kindergarten to College evaluation strategies to assess how effective the marketing has been in promoting the program; how effective the program design has been in encouraging follow-on contributions by participating parents from a wide range of socioeconomic and ethnic backgrounds; and what impact participation in the program has had on the financial capabilities of parents and on children’s college aspirations. Based in San Francisco, the grantee is dedicated to helping low-income families and individuals break the cycle of poverty and create new cycles of prosperity.

title: Medical Transportation Program
description: Since 1977, Catholic Outreach has been serving the homeless and low- to no-income population of Genesee County. The grantee offers several services at no charge to its clients, including: eviction and utility payment assistance; food and personal items pantry, which distributes nonperishable grocery and hygiene items; and the St. Christopher Children’s Medical Transportation Program, which transports seriously ill children for specialized medical treatment in Detroit, Ann Arbor, and Lansing. The economic downturn has resulted in a decrease in donations and, inversely, an increase in demand for services. This grant will enable the continued operation of the medical transportation program, which transports over 120 children on approximately 400 runs annually.

title: Medical Transportation Program
description: Since 1977, Catholic Outreach has been serving the homeless and low- to no-income population of Genesee County. The grantee offers several services at no charge to its clients, including: eviction and utility payment assistance; food and personal items pantry, which distributes nonperishable grocery and hygiene items; and the St. Christopher Children’s Transportation Program. The Medical Transportation Program, which started in 1992, transports seriously ill children for specialized medical treatment in Detroit, Ann Arbor, and Lansing. The economic downturn has resulted in a decrease in donations and, inversely, an increase in demand for this service. This grant will enable the continued operation of the Medical Transportation Program, which transports over 150 children (and some adults) to 400 medical appointments annually.

title: Medical Transportation Program
description: Since 1977, Catholic Outreach has been serving the homeless and low- to no-income population of Genesee County. The grantee offers several services at no charge to its clients, including: eviction and utility payment assistance; food and personal items pantry, which distributes nonperishable grocery and hygiene items; and St. Christopher’s Children’s Transportation Program, which transports seriously ill children for specialized medical treatment in Detroit, Ann Arbor, and Lansing. The recent economic downturn has resulted in a decrease in donations and, inversely, an increase in demand for services. This grant will enable the continued operation of St. Christopher’s Transportation Program, which transports over 120 children on approximately 400 runs annually, while new forms of funding are explored.

title: Double Up Food Bucks Project
description: This grant will provide ongoing support to the Fair Food Network’s Double Up Food Bucks Project at the Flint Farmers’ Market. The project provides food stamp recipients with incentives to purchase fresh fruits and vegetables at farmers’ markets and vegetable stands in Michigan. In addition to increasing access to healthy foods, the project aids local farmers in reaching more diverse markets. The Flint site is part of a statewide replication initiative, as well as larger efforts to embed fresh food incentives into federal food assistance policy. The Mott Foundation’s investment in this project will be matched by the Open Society Foundations as part of the Special Fund for Poverty Alleviation’s grantmaking initiatives in Michigan.

title: Double Up Food Bucks Project
description: This grant will provide ongoing support to the Fair Food Network’s Double Up Food Bucks Project at the Flint Farmers’ Market. The project provides supplemental nutrition assistance program recipients with incentives to purchase fresh fruits and vegetables at farmers’ markets and vegetable stands in Michigan. In addition to increasing access to healthy foods, the project aids local farmers in reaching more diverse markets. The Flint site is part of a statewide replication initiative, as well as a larger effort to embed fresh food incentives into federal food assistance policy.

title: Double Up Food Bucks Project
description: This grant will provide additional support to the Fair Food Network’s Double Up Food Bucks Project in Flint. The project provides incentives to supplemental nutrition assistance program recipients to purchase fresh fruits and vegetables and dairy products at the Flint Farmers’ Market and grocery stores in Flint. Good nutrition, especially foods high in iron, calcium, and vitamin C, can help mitigate the impact of lead exposure to Flint children and adults. The project will engage in a strategic marketing campaign to encourage all eligible families to enroll in the program, increase usage of incentives, and provide reliable nutrition information to Flint area families.

title: Double Up Food Bucks Project
description: This grant will provide additional support to the Fair Food Network’s Double Up Food Bucks program in Flint. The program provides incentives for supplemental nutrition assistance program recipients to purchase fresh fruits and vegetables and dairy products at the Flint Farmers’ Market and participating grocery stores in Flint. Good nutrition, especially foods high in iron, calcium, and Vitamin C, can help mitigate the impact of lead exposure for Flint children and adults. The program engages in extensive marketing activities to encourage all eligible families to enroll in the program, increase usage of incentives, and provide reliable nutrition information to Flint area families.

title: Double Up Food Bucks Project
description: The purpose of this grant is to increase the affordability of fresh produce to Genesee County families receiving food assistance from the state of Michigan. Fair Food Network, in partnership with the Flint Farmers Market, will replicate the Double Up Food Bucks project launched last year at Detroit’s Eastern Market. Local families receiving supplemental nutrition assistance program funds will receive a dollar-for-dollar match when purchasing food with their cash assistance card at the Flint Farmers Market. This project is part of a larger initiative supported by Open Society Institute to alleviate poverty in Michigan.

title: 2010 Legislative Leadership Program
description: Over the past three decades, the Institute for Public Policy and Social Research at Michigan State University has built a reputation for applying cutting-edge research to pressing public policy issues and building problem-solving relationships between the academic and policymaker communities. One of its premier programs is the Legislative Leadership Program, an educational program for newly elected state policymakers that provides information and dialogue about critical issues. This grant will enable the institute to include the topic of Michigan’s transportation system and related policy considerations as an area of focus within the 2010 Legislative Leadership Program.

title: Downtown Redevelopment Project
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will provide funds for the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation to redevelop the property at 124 W. First Street in downtown Flint. The renovated building will provide a permanent location for Flint Local 432, a nonalcoholic, live music club and performance space founded in 1985, which serves persons aged 14 to 25.

title: Diplomas Count: The Graduation Project
description: This grant will provide partial support to Editorial Projects in Education to provide an ongoing and independent resource to the field on issues of high school graduation and reform via its “Diplomas Count” publication. In 2011, the grantee published the sixth edition of “Diplomas Count” and a series of complementary issue briefs that address and explore the college readiness, access, and completion landscape as it relates to preparing students for post-secondary education and the 21st Century workforce. Recommended support will enable the grantee to publish the seventh edition of its “Diplomas Count” report and focus new research on the linked issues of high school graduation and college readiness.

title: Diplomas Count: The Graduation Project
description: This grant will provide partial support to Editorial Projects in Education to provide an ongoing and independent resource to the field on issues of high school graduation through its “Diplomas Count” publication. In 2012, the grantee published the seventh edition of “Diplomas Count” that provided an in-depth exploration of high school graduation and the larger reform landscape encompassing high school improvement efforts, as well as the movement to a college readiness, access, and completion mandate. Recommended support will enable the grantee to publish the eighth edition of its “Diplomas Count” report and focus new research on the linked issues of high school graduation and college readiness.

title: Diplomas Count: The Graduation Project
description: This grant will provide lead and partial support to Editorial Projects in Education to provide an independent resource to the field on issues of high school graduation through its “Diplomas Count” publication. In 2013, the grantee published the eighth edition of “Diplomas Count”. The publication provided an in-depth exploration of high school graduation and the larger education reform landscape. Recommended support will enable the grantee to publish the next two editions of Diplomas Count and focus new research and coverage on emerging issues in high school reform and college readiness.

title: Diplomas Count: The Graduation Project
description: This grant will provide partial support to Editorial Projects in Education to provide an ongoing and independent resource to the field on issues of high school graduation and reform. Over the past five years, the grantee has engaged in a body of work devoted to raising public awareness on the challenges the nation faces in ensuring that all students earn a diploma. Recommended support will enable the grantee to publish its Diplomas Count report, convene key stakeholders, develop strategic partnerships with other leading organizations, and spotlight promising strategies for reducing dropout rates to better prepare students for postsecondary education and the 21st century workforce.

title: Debt Reduction
description: Since 1986, Wellness AIDS Services, Inc., has been providing Genesee County with two main types of services: 1) HIV/AIDS prevention information and skill-building activities; and 2) resource coordination and counseling services for those who are infected and affected by HIV/AIDS. The grantee provides resource coordination and counseling services to more than 250 clients each year and is the only organization in Genesee County that provides this particular service. Over the years, the grantee has helped thousands of individuals by tailoring its outreach, testing, education, and training programs for the most at-risk populations. This grant will enable the grantee to pay off the debt owed on its facility and ensure that the organization is able to continue providing high level services to the Flint community.

title: Global Philanthropy Leadership Initiative
description: The Global Philanthropy Leadership Initiative is a joint project of the Council on Foundations, the European Foundation Centre, and the Worldwide Initiatives for Grantmaker Support. The aim of the initiative is to facilitate and enhance the impact of cross-border philanthropy. A task force comprising of foundation leaders from around the world will guide work in three areas: 1) improving the legal environment for global philanthropy; 2) developing models/vehicles for pooling resources together and increasing collaboration; and 3) identifying key political moments and levers to engage with policymakers/multilateral organizations. The task force will assess and inform the current thinking in the three areas and design a process through which a diverse group of people can explore and jointly shape the agenda and eventual product of the initiative. The process is expected to result in concrete and actionable recommendations that will advance the growth, effectiveness, and influence of global philanthropy.

title: YouthBuild in the Western Balkans
description: The project goal is to increase levels of youth civic participation and initiative for positive social action in the Western Balkans. To this end, YouthBuild USA will strengthen and expand its programs in at least three communities with the goal of demonstrating the program’s effectiveness and scaling it up to other parts of the region. Building on its successes during the previous two years, the grantee will engage up to 400 young people in community improvement projects, build the capacity of local professionals and nonprofits to implement its programs in the region, and establish a multistakeholder consortium willing and able to carry the YouthBuild program forward in the Western Balkans. During 2011-2012, programs were piloted in five communities in Bosnia-Herzegovina and Serbia, involving a total of 580 young people. The grantee will implement this project through its YouthBuild International division and a network of local nonprofit partners.

title: YouthBuild in the Western Balkans
description: The primary project goal is to increase levels of youth civic participation and initiative for positive social action in the Western Balkans. To this end, YouthBuild USA will strengthen and expand YouthBuild programs in at least three communities with the goal of demonstrating the program’s effectiveness and scaling it up to other parts of the region. Building on the success of the programming in the Western Balkans, with this grant increase the grantee will carry out exploratory work in Bulgaria and Romania in preparation for possible introduction of its programs to these two countries in 2015. The grantee will implement this project through its YouthBuild International division and a network of local nonprofit partners.

title: YouthBuild in Southeast Europe
description: The project goal is to increase levels of youth civic participation and initiative for positive social action in Southeast Europe. To this end, YouthBuild USA will strengthen existing YouthBuild programs in Bosnia-Herzegovina and Serbia and establish new programs in Bulgaria and Romania. YouthBuild is a model for helping young people learn life and job skills, serve their communities, and gain practical work experience. The grantee will also build support for the program from diverse stakeholders with the goal of sustaining established program sites and scaling up the program to other parts of the region. Working closely with local partner organizations during the previous two years, the grantee engaged more than 400 young people in programs in seven locations in Bosnia-Herzegovina and Serbia. These participants made a significant impact on their communities through peacebuilding campaigns, upgraded schools and rural homes, new playgrounds, and mentoring of children. The grantee will implement this project through its YouthBuild International division and a network of local nonprofit partners.

title: YouthBuild in Southeast Europe
description: The project goal is to increase levels of youth civic participation and initiative for positive social action in Southeast Europe. YouthBuild USA will support YouthBuild programs in Bulgaria, Romania, and Serbia. YouthBuild is a model for helping young people learn life and job skills, serve their communities, and gain practical work experience. During the grant period, more than 250 young people annually will engage in an intensive, full-time educational program addressing a range of practical and life skills and will participate in community service projects. The grantee will also build support for the program from diverse stakeholders in order to sustain established program sites and expand the program to other parts of the region. During 2015–2016, more than 500 young people participated in YouthBuild programs. These participants made a significant impact on their communities through housing construction for Roma families, repairs to parks and playgrounds, and organizing events for children and elderly people. The grantee will implement this project through its YouthBuild International division and a network of local nonprofit partners.

title: YouthBuild in the Western Balkans
description: The project goal is to increase levels of youth civic participation and initiative for positive social action in the Western Balkans. To this end, YouthBuild USA will pilot programs in at least two communities with the goal of demonstrating the program’s effectiveness and scaling it up to other parts of the region. In each pilot community, young people will receive training, counseling, and mentoring and will directly engage in planning and implementing community improvements, such as building or improving playgrounds and other public spaces and upgrading and weatherizing houses. Young people involved in the project will develop leadership and practical skills by analyzing community development processes, facilitating planning meetings, and interacting with community members. During the grant period, the grantee will develop a network of nonprofits and experts that will provide technical assistance to the program over the long term. YouthBuild USA, will implement this project through its YouthBuild International division and a newly established, affiliated nonprofit in Belgrade, Serbia, called YouthBuild Fond Za Balkan.

title: Breaking the Rules-Film Project
description: Promises Films was established in 1996 and produces educational media with regard to public issues, particularly in the areas of conflict, human rights, social justice, and history. “Breaking the Rules” is a 48-minute documentary film that tells the little-known story of white South Africans who joined the struggle against apartheid. It explores why white South Africans, who were otherwise living a comfortable and privileged life, risked their lives to fight for a free and just society. The story is told through the voices and memories of five individuals from diverse political and cultural backgrounds who expressed their opposition to apartheid in different ways. Through the eyes of its characters, the film also tells the contemporary story of South Africa today where fissures are emerging along racial lines. Prior funding from Mott supported the filming of some of the footage and editing for “Breaking the Rules”. This grant will assist Promises Films to complete the film and will contribute to conducting final interviews, editing, and other post production activities.

title: Breaking the Rules-Film Project
description: Five Star Films is a film and video production company specializing in creative and compelling social issue documentary and educational programming for international audiences. Breaking the Rules is a 90-minute feature documentary film that tells the story of the whites who fought against apartheid as allies in the struggle for justice in South Africa. The story is told through the voices and memories of five individuals from diverse political and cultural backgrounds who expressed their opposition to apartheid in different ways. All five were born into the lives of white privilege, yet each made the choice to dedicate their lives to fight racial oppression. The film journeys through five decades of life under apartheid, starting in the 1950s until changes happened in the 1990s. This grant will support the grantee to film more footage for Breaking the Rules and to edit it.

title: Coats for Kids
description: The Old Newsboys of Flint began in 1924 as a replication of a similar program in the Detroit area. The organization receives much of its revenue from a one-day paper sale, and in 1924, that paper sale allowed it to put warm clothing and a toy under the tree for 201 children. Since then, the grantee has touched the lives of 760,000 children. Today, one of three crucial programs offered by this organization is a coat and boot program. Of the 103 elementary schools in Genesee County, 100 participate in the program by providing between 10 and 20 coat and boot referrals each. Many households are forced to choose between heat, food, and healthcare — new coats and boots may not even be considered. Funding will provide 1,333 additional coat and boot referrals to the Genesee County elementary schools in the highest need areas, particularly Flint, Beecher, and Westwood Heights.

title: Flint Public Health and Medical Campus
description: Founded in 1855, Michigan State University is one of the top research universities in the world. During the grant period, the grantee will begin the planning and implementation process of a Flint Public Health and Medical Campus, one of two flagship campuses for Michigan State University’s College of Human Medicine. In addition to Flint, the other flagship campus is the Secchia Center in Grand Rapids which opened in 2010. The Flint Campus will be designed to model a new way to think about doctors and their relationships to patients, their professions, and the communities where they live. This integration of medical training for family- and community-based doctors and public health could be a national model that will create healthier communities and a more cost-effective health system.

title: Circle of Blue Great Lakes Project
geographic_focus: Ohio, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Michigan, New York, Illinois, Pennsylvania, Indiana
description: The push for new sources of oil and gas has the potential to impact water quality and water availability in the Great Lakes region. Additionally, the effects of climate change are already being seen in the Great Lakes. The Pacific Institute, through its Circle of Blue Great Lakes Project, will help broaden and deepen public knowledge and discussion about the impact of new energy exploration and climate change on the freshwater resources of the Great Lakes. Working with journalism students from Ball State University, the grantee will develop and distribute five original reports. The Pacific Institute is a leading international think tank, based in Oakland, California, working on freshwater issues and related matters.

title: General Purposes
description: Created in 1988, the Community Foundation of Greater Flint has established itself as a major local philanthropic entity that helps individuals, families, businesses, and nonprofit organizations achieve their charitable goals by providing tools and resources that make giving easy, flexible, and effective. Over the years, the organization’s assets have grown from $10 million to more than $125 million with over 10,000 contributors, and has awarded more than $64 million in grants to the greater Flint area from over 380 charitable funds. This grant will provide the grantee with general purpose support.

title: Transformative Organizing Initiative
grantee: Bend the Arc: A Jewish Partnership for Justice
description: Since the 1980s, Jewish Funds for Justice has supported work to strengthen low-income communities by funding community development and community organizing activities. The Transformative Organizing Initiative is a program designed to strengthen community organizing by focusing on both the organization and the personal development of professional organizers and grassroots leaders. This grant will provide partial support for the initiative.

title: Promoting Philanthropic Culture in Bulgaria
description: The program goal is to strengthen the culture of philanthropy in Bulgaria. To this end, the Bulgarian School of Politics will promote strategic philanthropy among various actors in the field of philanthropy, strengthen the philanthropic practice of its alumni, and develop a resource center on philanthropy at the school. This project’s past achievements include organizing high profile public events on the role of philanthropy, publishing two books and a series of research papers on philanthropy, and increasing the level of giving among its trainees and alumni. The school was established in 2001 with the mission to build a community of civic and political leaders who share democratic values and participate actively in national and international political and public life. Since 2001, more than 500 Bulgarian and 180 Central and Eastern European leaders, including members of parliament, party leaders, and civic activists, have graduated from the school. The school is engaging its trainees in philanthropic initiatives as part of the trainees’ public policy development work.

title: Promoting Philanthropic Culture in Bulgaria
description: The program goal is to strengthen the culture of philanthropy in Bulgaria. To this end, the Bulgarian School of Politics will strengthen the philanthropic practice of its trainees and alumni, promote strategic philanthropy among various actors in the field of philanthropy, and develop a resource center on philanthropy at the school. Past achievements include providing technical assistance to over 110 young leaders from political parties, state administration, and civil society to engage in philanthropic work; promoting new forms of philanthropic giving; and publishing research on the media coverage of philanthropy in Bulgaria. Based in Sofia, the school was established in 2001 with the mission to build a community of civic and political leaders who share democratic values and participate actively in national and international political and public life. Since 2001, more than 650 Bulgarian and 260 Central and Eastern European leaders, including members of parliament, party leaders, and civic activists, have graduated from the school. The school is engaging its trainees in philanthropic initiatives as part of the trainees’ public policy development work.

title: Promoting Philanthropic Culture in Bulgaria
description: The program goal is to strengthen the culture of philanthropy in Bulgaria. To this end, the Bulgarian School of Politics will carry out systematic research on various issues related to philanthropy, including trends in philanthropic giving, the effectiveness of current philanthropic practices, and the impact of philanthropy in Bulgaria. In addition, the school will facilitate public debates on philanthropy through social and mainstream media. Also, the school will introduce a specific module on philanthropic giving coupled with a practical philanthropic project in its training program for young civic and political leaders. The school was established in 2001 with the mission to build a community of civic and political leaders who share democratic values and participate actively in national and international political and public life. Since 2001, more than 400 Bulgarian and 150 Central and Eastern European leaders, including members of parliament, party leaders, and civic activists have graduated from the school. The school is engaging its trainees in philanthropic initiatives as part of the trainees’ public policy development work.

title: General Purposes
description: The Village Information Center was established in 1976 and has published hundreds of issues of the “East Village Magazine”. “East Village Magazine” is a monthly nonprofit magazine written by and for Flint residents and nonprofit groups that focuses on issues directly affecting the quality of life in Flint neighborhoods. The magazine is distributed by volunteers throughout the city of Flint, reaching a reader base of about 12,000 people. In addition to publishing the magazine, the grantee trains its volunteers in professional writing and journalism and provides a literary outlet for city residents. This grant will provide the grantee with capacity building and some technological support.

title: General Purposes
description: The Village Information Center was established in 1976 and has published 580 issues of “East Village Magazine”. “East Village Magazine” is a monthly nonprofit magazine written by and for Flint residents and nonprofit groups that focuses on issues directly affecting the quality of life in Flint neighborhoods. The magazine is distributed entirely by volunteers throughout the city of Flint, reaching a reader base of about 14,000. In addition to publishing the magazine, the grantee trains its volunteers in professional writing and journalism and provides a literary outlet for city residents. This grant will enable the grantee to restructure its operations and redesign its Website.

title: International Student Recruitment
description: This grant will provide continuing support to the University of Michigan-Flint International Center for recruitment of international students. Funds will be used for international travel for recruiters, financial scholarships, and housing incentives to attract prospective students. The project also supports student leadership and intercultural development activities to bolster student retention.

title: International Student Recruitment
description: This grant will provide funds to the University of Michigan-Flint International Center to provide support for recruitment of international students through increased funding of international travel for recruiters and scholarship incentives to attract prospective students. The project also builds in support after student recruits arrive on campus, through leadership development and student life programming.

title: South Saginaw Street Redevelopment Plan
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will provide funds to the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation to acquire several parcels across from the Great Lakes Technology Center. The acquisition is part of the city of Flint’s overall strategy to improve the South Saginaw Street corridor between Atherton and Hemphill roads. The grantee will provide the grant funds to its supported organization, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, to purchase and clean up seven properties in the South Saginaw Street corridor.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to a nationwide network of foundation grant managers. The Grants Managers Network improves grantmaking by advancing the knowledge, skills, and abilities of grants management professionals and by leading grantmakers to adopt and incorporate effective practices that benefit the philanthropic community. Currently, the grantee has over 2,400 members from more than 1,200 grantmaking organizations who represent the breadth of the philanthropic community including small family foundations, prominent national foundations, grantmaking public charities, and socially responsible corporations. Besides serving the needs of grants managers through online resources, publications, research, regional meetings, and an annual conference, the grantee will partner with the Technology Affinity Group of the Council on Foundations to update a much-needed field survey of grants management software.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to a nationwide network of foundation grant managers. The Grants Managers Network improves grantmaking by advancing the knowledge, skills, and abilities of grants management professionals and by leading grantmakers to adopt and incorporate effective practices that benefit the philanthropic community. Currently, the network has over 3,000 individual members from more than 1,500 grantmaking organizations that represent the breadth of the philanthropic community including small family foundations, prominent national foundations, grantmaking public charities, and socially responsible corporations. Besides serving the needs of grants managers through online resources, publications, research, regional meetings, and an annual conference, the grantee has launched a three-year, $1.8 million core support campaign to expand its capacity to better serve more grantmakers. The grantee will use a portion of Mott funding to support this campaign.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to a national network of foundation grants managers. The Grants Managers Network improves grantmaking by advancing the knowledge, skills, and abilities of grants management professionals and by leading grantmakers to adopt and incorporate effective practices that benefit the philanthropic community. Currently, the network has 1,700 members from more than 1,000 grantmaking organizations who represent the breadth of the philanthropic community including small family foundations, prominent national foundations, grantmaking public charities, and socially responsible corporations. The network is supported by more than 200 grantmaking organizations that recognize its contribution to the field of philanthropy. Besides serving the needs of grants managers through online resources, publications, research, regional meetings, and an annual conference, in 2011, the grantee will, in partnership with the Technology Affinity Group of the Council on Foundations, update a much-needed field survey of grants management software.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: South Africa, Brazil, India, Russia, China
description: The Philanthropy Bridge Foundation’s mission is to bridge class, cultural, and institutional divides between people in emerging market countries through engaging individuals and companies in proactive and responsible philanthropy. The grantee aims to engage new wealth in the East and South in strategic and transparent philanthropy to ensure that the incredible wealth, which is now becoming available in countries previously seen as beneficiaries of aid, is put to good use. The grantee also aims to build a bridge between new wealth and the nonprofit sector in emerging market countries to make nonprofits more sustainable and to increase their legitimacy in their countries. Planned activities include tailored initiatives to engage specific individuals in strategic philanthropy; meetings and conferences for wealthy individuals in Russia, China, Brazil, South Africa, and the Middle East; and workshops for public charities to improve their understanding of donors in emerging markets.

title: Monica Patten Endowment Fund
description: This grant contributes to the Monica Patten Endowment Fund, a component fund of the Community Foundations of Canada’s All for Community Endowment Fund, which is a permanent endowment established in 2008 to provide income to help offset the organization’s operational costs. The grantee: 1) supports established and developing community foundations in their endowment building and donor services, grantmaking, and community leadership; 2) promotes and advances philanthropy and community foundations; and 3) models philanthropic leadership in Canada and internationally. Retiring Chief Executive Monica Patten has led Community Foundations of Canada since 1993, during which time she built the organization from a group of 28 community foundations to a strong and vibrant national network of more than 170 community foundations across Canada. The Monica Patten Endowment Fund has been established by Community Foundations of Canada’s board of directors in tribute to Ms. Patten’s 17 years of extraordinary service and leadership.

title: Towards a Better Understanding of Civil Society in Africa
description: Social Surveys contributes to social transformation through specialist social research. For the past two decades, the grantee has conducted many studies for clients working in different sectors throughout Africa. In 2011, the grantee initiated a research study entitled “Towards a Better Understanding of Civil Society in Africa – a Multi-country Perspective.” This study will offer new thinking on how civil society in Africa can be better understood and defined. This grant will support the second phase of the study, which will include presenting the findings of phase one, collecting new empirical data on civil society in South Africa, conducting interviews with civil society leaders in Southern Africa to capture their perspectives, and finding existing data to test definitions of civil society and their inclusiveness.

title: Towards a Better Understanding of Civil Society in Africa
description: Social Surveys contributes to social development and transformation through expert social research. For the past two decades, the grantee has conducted many large-scale surveys in South Africa and other African countries for an array of clients. In 2011, it initiated a research study entitled “Towards a Better Understanding of Civil Society in Africa — a Multi-country Perspective,” to better understand how civil society in Africa is conceived. Mott support for the study assisted the grantee to consult experts in various sectors, gather domestic, unpublished literature to better understand how civil society is defined on the continent, and conduct community-based research to examine civil society formations more closely. This grant will support the third phase of the study, which will gather further data on the size and nature of civil society in South Africa. The research will include interviews with a representative sample of civil society organizations in South Africa.

title: Towards a Better Understanding of Civil Society in Africa
description: Based in South Africa, Social Surveys contributes to African social transformation through conducting specialist research that improves development policies and strategies. Since its establishment in 1987, it has conducted many studies for a wide range of clients in the public, private, and nonprofit sectors. This grant will support the first phase of a research study on “Towards a Better Understanding of Civil Society in Africa — a Multi-country Perspective.” The major activities will include consultations with various stakeholders in South Africa, a literature review, development of an African conceptual framework for civil society in consultation with civil society institutions and other stakeholders from across the continent, and the design of the formative research to be conducted in South Africa. While this research is multicountry, the initial focus will be southern Africa, with the inception study undertaken in South Africa.

title: Conflict Resolution Training for Advice Offices
grantee: Project for Conflict Resolution and Development
description: The Project for Conflict Resolution and Development works primarily in the Eastern Cape Province of South Africa and focuses on training community-based organizations to deal effectively with conflict within their communities. It works mainly with poor communities that receive little or no support from other sources, including the state. Past support enabled the grantee to train and mentor community-based paralegals in advice offices on mediation and dispute resolution. It also fostered good working relationships and cooperation among participating advice offices to enable them to share knowledge and experiences. This grant will assist the grantee to continue to train and mentor community-based paralegals on topics related to conflict resolution. It will also develop and refine training materials on conflict resolution and approach university law clinics to consider using them for the training of paralegals.

title: Conflict Resolution Training for Advice Offices
grantee: Project for Conflict Resolution and Development
description: The Project for Conflict Resolution and Development works primarily in the Eastern Cape Province of South Africa and focuses on training community-based organizations to deal effectively with conflict within their communities. It works mainly with poor communities that receive little or no support from other sources, including the state. Past support enabled the grantee to train and mentor community-based paralegals in advice offices on mediation and dispute resolution. It also fostered good working relationships and cooperation among participating advice offices to enable them to share knowledge and experiences. This grant will assist the grantee to train and mentor a new group of community-based paralegals on topics related to conflict resolution. It will also collaborate with experienced paralegals in training and in supporting the new participants, refine training materials on conflict resolution, and pilot a program on peace building with two advice offices. This grant has been made possible by a partnership with Atlantic Philanthropies in support of the community advice office sector.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Project for Conflict Resolution and Development
description: The Project for Conflict Resolution and Development works primarily in the Eastern Cape province of South Africa and focuses on training community-based organizations to deal effectively with conflict within their communities. It works mainly with poor communities that receive little or no support from other sources. Past support enabled the grantee to train and mentor community-based paralegals in advice offices on mediation and dispute resolution and to pilot a program on peace building with two advice offices. Activities over the next two years will include conducting a survey of the types of conflicts community advice offices in all nine provinces deal with and methods they use, designing relevant programs to address gaps, training and mentoring community-based paralegals on topics related to conflict resolution, and working with schools to develop programs for safer schools.

title: Conflict Resolution Training for Advice Offices
grantee: Project for Conflict Resolution and Development
description: The Project for Conflict Resolution and Development works primarily in the Eastern Cape province of South Africa and focuses on training community-based organizations to deal effectively with conflict at the community level. It works mainly with poor communities that receive little or no support from other sources, including the state. The objective of this project is to assist community-based advice offices to effectively manage and resolve conflicts both within their institutions and on behalf of the communities they serve. The grantee will develop training materials and train and mentor community-based paralegals on mediation and dispute resolution. It will also offer hands-on support to paralegals on mediating community disputes when conflicts arise.

title: General Purposes
description: The project goal is to enhance public participation in decisionmaking processes by improving accountability and transparency of public institutions in Kosovo. The Balkan Investigative Reporting Network Kosovo will combine hard-hitting journalism and civic activism to encourage people to be informed and engaged in this critical period in Kosovo’s history. Specific activities will include training investigative journalists and field researchers; systematic monitoring of public institutions with a focus on courts, health services, and education; and producing high quality print and broadcast media designed to inform the public and policymakers. During 2010-2011, the grantee produced a weekly current affairs television program, which was one of the most popular news programs in Kosovo; contributed to regional and national news publications; monitored the performance of courts, hospitals, and schools in 26 municipalities; and prepared detailed reports and analyses based on the information collected. The grantee is a registered nongovernmental organization in Kosovo based in Pristina and part of a Balkan network of similar organizations in six countries.

title: General Purposes
description: The project goal is to enhance public participation in decisionmaking processes by improving accountability and transparency of public institutions in Kosovo. The Balkan Investigative Reporting Network Kosovo will combine hard-hitting journalism and civic activism to encourage people to be informed and engaged in this critical period in Kosovo’s history. Specific activities will include training investigative journalists and field researchers; systematic monitoring of public institutions with a focus on courts, health services, education, and public procurement; and producing high quality print and broadcast media designed to inform the public. Over the past year, the grantee produced a weekly current affairs television program, which with over 350,000 viewers per week was one of the most popular news programs in Kosovo; contributed to regional and national news publications; monitored the performance of courts, hospitals, and schools in 26 municipalities; and prepared detailed reports and analyses based on the information collected. The grantee is a registered nongovernmental organization in Kosovo based in Pristina and part of a Balkan network of similar organizations (each with the same name) in six countries.

title: General Purposes
description: The project goal is to enhance public participation in decisionmaking processes by improving accountability and transparency of public institutions in Kosovo. The Balkan Investigative Reporting Network Kosovo will combine hard-hitting journalism and civic activism to encourage people to be informed and engaged in this critical period in Kosovo’s history. Specific activities will include training investigative journalists and field researchers; systematic monitoring of public institutions with a focus on courts, health services, education, and public procurement; and producing high quality print and broadcast media designed to inform the public and policymakers. During 2015-2016, the grantee produced two weekly television programs that include in-depth reporting and debates; published two online, weekly magazines; contributed to regional and national news publications; monitored the performance of courts, hospitals, and schools in 26 municipalities as well as the implementation of bilateral agreements with Serbia on the normalization of relations; and prepared detailed reports and analyses based on the information collected. The grantee is a registered nongovernmental organization in Kosovo based in Pristina and part of a Balkan network of similar organizations (each with the same name) in six countries.

title: General Purposes
description: The goal of Balkan Investigative Reporting Network Kosovo is to enhance public participation in decisionmaking processes by improving accountability and transparency of public service administration at local levels in Kosovo. The grantee will combine hard-hitting journalism and civic activism to encourage people to be informed and engaged in this critical period in Kosovo’s history. Specific activities will include training investigative journalists and field researchers, producing four television programs per month focused on justice in Kosovo, publishing annual monitoring reports on key issues, and producing 100 episodes of its flagship “Life in Kosovo” current affairs television program. The grantee is a registered nongovernmental organization in Kosovo based in Pristina and part of a Balkan network of similar organizations in six countries (each with the same name).

title: Saginaw Bay Initiative
description: With this grant increase, the Nature Conservancy will continue to work with the agricultural community in the Saginaw Bay Watershed to implement best management practices that will improve water quality and restore freshwater habitat.

title: Saginaw Bay Initiative
description: With this grant increase, the Nature Conservancy will continue to work with the agricultural community in the Saginaw Bay Watershed to implement best management practices that will improve water quality and restore freshwater habitat.

title: Saginaw Bay Initiative
description: With this grant increase, the Nature Conservancy will continue to work with the agricultural community in the Saginaw Bay Watershed to implement best management practices that will improve water quality and restore freshwater habitat.

title: Saginaw Bay Initiative
description: Polluted runoff from land-use practices is a major threat to the health of the Saginaw Bay in Lake Huron, an estuary that the Nature Conservancy, a global conservation group, has identified as a high priority for protection and restoration. To address this problem, the grantee has developed science-based tools that will allow resource managers to determine where to implement agricultural best management practices in the watershed and how much of a given practice to apply to achieve optimal conservation results. With this renewal, the grantee will continue to work with the agricultural community in the Saginaw Bay Watershed to implement such best management practices, which will be aided by major federal support under the Resource Conservation Partnership Program.

title: Saginaw Bay Initiative
description: With this grant increase, The Nature Conservancy will work with partner organizations to restore urban segments of the Flint River, a major river within the Saginaw Bay Watershed. This work will focus on providing advice on the Flint River Restoration Project, an effort to improve the health and flows of the Flint River and provide safe recreation opportunities for Flint’s residents and visitors.

title: Saginaw Bay Initiative
description: Spanning 5.5 million acres and 22 counties, the Saginaw Bay Watershed is the largest in Michigan. The Nature Conservancy is striving to improve water quality and quantity in this system to ensure a healthy and resilient future for Saginaw Bay and all the life it supports. The grantee has developed ecologically based conservation goals, created computer models to target those goals, and forged critical partnerships to implement the goals. During the last two years, the grantee has helped secure millions of dollars in funding directed toward on-the-ground conservation in the highest priority places in the watershed. With continued Mott support, the grantee will enhance implementation of its program in the watershed and share lessons learned with colleagues across the Great Lakes and globally.

title: Saginaw Bay Initiative
description: The Nature Conservancy, a global conservation organization with a deep presence in Michigan, is striving to balance agricultural and environmental needs and improve water quality and quantity in the Saginaw Bay watershed. With prior Mott support, the grantee undertook a number of activities to promote the adoption of agricultural conservation practices, leading to quantifiable reductions in phosphorous and sediment pollution. With continued funding, the grantee will maintain and expand such programs.

title: Saginaw Bay Initiative
description: Polluted runoff from land-use practices is a major threat to the health of the Saginaw Bay in Lake Huron, an estuary that the Nature Conservancy, a global conservation group, has identified as a high priority for protection and restoration. To address this problem, the conservancy proposes to develop science-based tools that will allow resource managers to determine where in the watershed to implement agricultural best management practices and how much of a given practice to apply to achieve optimal conservation results. The conservancy will work with key partners, such as Michigan State University, and share the lessons learned in the Saginaw Bay watershed with practitioners in similar basins around the Great Lakes and nationally.

title: Healing Our Waters - Great Lakes Coalition
geographic_focus: Illinois, Pennsylvania, New York, Michigan, Wisconsin, Ohio, Minnesota
description: The Great Lakes are facing compounding threats from a variety of sources, including polluted runoff, invasive species, and severe rain events. These challenges are too great for any single organization to take on alone. The National Wildlife Federation, a national environmental group with a commitment to the Great Lakes, seeks to strengthen the network of Great Lakes’ organizations working to improve water quality, halt invasive species, and increase funding for habitat restoration projects. With this grant, the grantee will provide small grants, communications assistance, and networking opportunities through the Healing Our Waters – Great Lakes Coalition.

title: Developing Additional Reports for the Sectoral Employment Impact Study
description: Public/Private Ventures recently published “Tuning In to Local Labor Markets: Findings From the Sectoral Employment Impact Study.” Based on the study, as well as feedback from leading academics, policymakers, and practitioners, the grantee will explore this data in more depth and produce a series of short reports to inform those interested in sectoral employment strategies.

title: One Stop Housing Resource Center
description: This grant will provide funds to Resource Genesee to supply emergency services through its One Stop Housing Resource Center. The center provides emergency services to the homeless and near homeless in Flint and Genesee County. Emergency services that will be provided with the grant funds include emergency motel stays, emergency travel, MTA bus passes, gas cards, and critical document assistance.

title: One Stop Housing Resource Center
description: This grant will provide funds to Resource Genesee to supply emergency services through its One Stop Housing Resource Center. The center provides emergency services to the homeless and near homeless in Flint and Genesee County. Emergency services that will be provided with these grant funds include emergency motel stays, emergency travel, MTA bus passes, gas cards, and critical document assistance.

title: One Stop Genesee
description: This grant will help Resource Genesee provide direct client assistance and basic need services to struggling area residents through its One Stop Genesee program. Funding will allow Resource Genesee to assist citizens who are in need of emergency hotel stays, gas cards, food cards, emergency travel support, bus passes, gas cards, and critical document assistance. The grantee also helps struggling residents work through the immediate and long-term needs of the homeless or near-homeless.

title: One Stop Housing Resource Center
description: This grant will provide funds to Resource Genesee to supply emergency services through its program, One Stop Housing Resource Center. The center provides emergency services to the homeless and near-homeless in Flint and Genesee County. Emergency services that will be provided with the grant funds include emergency motel stays, emergency travel, MTA bus passes, gas cards, and critical document assistance.

title: Glass Exhibitions
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will support the glass exhibits at the Flint Institute of Arts. The LINO TAGLIAPIETRA IN RETROSPECT: A Modern Renaissance in Italian Glass exhibit featured 169 objects ranging from large works and major installations to small goblets and vessels. Lino Tagliapietra is widely revered as the maestro of glassblowing, an inspiring teacher, and the elder statesman linking the glass centers of Venice and the Pacific Northwest. The TIFFANY LAMPS: Articles of Utility, Objects of Art exhibit included over 40 lamps in an array of colors, sizes, and decorative styles. This display presented the first in-depth look at the Tiffany Studios’ deliberate effort to produce lamps that balance artistry with utility and profitability. The exhibition opened on May 23, 2010, and ran through August 15, 2010.

title: Dr. M. Richard Shaink Presidential Fund for Student Success
description: This grant will provide funds to the Foundation for Mott Community College for the Presidential Fund for Student Success, which was established to honor Dr. M. Richard Shaink. Funds will be used to support the Achieving the Dream Initiative, which aims to help student groups who have traditionally faced significant barriers to success.

title: Deepwater Horizon Spill Response
description: The legal, policy, and public education dimensions of the Deepwater Horizon spill are more prominent now than they were in the weeks following the disaster. Participating in such policy debates requires a high level of technical expertise and policy acumen, but many of the engaged nongovernmental organizations lack such capacity. With this grant, the Institute on Water Resources Law and Policy, a unit of Tulane University, will provide technical assistance of this type to the environmental community, other stakeholders, and the relevant government agencies themselves.

title: Evaluation of YearUp - A Sectoral Youth Initiative
geographic_focus: Boston, New York, District of Columbia
description: YearUp is a sectoral initiative that helps young adults from low-income, urban communities focus on acquiring the skills needed to succeed in two industries, information technology and investment operations. The results from an analysis of participants’ outcomes two years after they were randomly assigned to take part in an evaluation were very positive — program participants accessed jobs with higher hourly wages and earned greater annual earnings than did people in the control group. This grant will allow the Economic Mobility Corporation to continue the evaluation by conducting an additional wave of follow-up interviews in order to learn about study participants’ employment and educational outcomes three and one-half years after first being assigned to the study.

title: Working Past Disasters: Mapping Post-Disaster Economies & Linking Two-Year Schools with Industry
description: This grant will enable the Greater New Orleans Development Foundation to research and map emerging post-disaster economies related to disaster mitigation and response and environmental cleanup in Louisiana. The project will foster public/private partnerships between industry and area community colleges that will result in curriculum and program changes designed to provide appropriate training and certifications so that a local workforce is available to meet the demands of emerging economies in a particular region.

title: Repurposing Closed Automotive Facilities in the Mid-Michigan Region
description: There is a long history of automotive manufacturing facility closings in mid-Michigan, because the auto industry has been operating in the region for over a century. Many communities in the region are struggling with the monumental task of formulating a strategic plan for repurposing these facilities and the properties they occupy. The goal is to replace a significant portion of lost labor income and tax base once generated by these facilities. Assisting communities in repurposing former auto facilities is the next logical step for the Automotive Communities Partnership program. This grant to the Center for Automotive Research, its strong ties to the automotive industry, and a federal grant to study auto facility repurposing will make this research effort very successful.

title: Mid Michigan Good Temp Alternative Staffing Organization
description: This grant will support the first full year operation of a nonprofit staffing organization in Flint, Michigan managed by Goodwill Industries of Mid-Michigan, Inc. Nonprofit staffing organizations have a dual goal of providing job brokering and support services for workers who face barriers to employment, as well as delivering dependable workers to organizations that have growing labor demands. As the Michigan and Genesee County economies continue to improve, this project will allow individuals who might not otherwise be able to enter the labor market gain valuable work experience and skills.

title: Mid Michigan Good Temp Alternative Staffing Organization
description: This grant to Goodwill Industries of Mid-Michigan, Inc., will support the expansion of the alternative staffing organization in Genesee County, Michigan. Alternative staffing organizations provide job brokering for workers who face significant barriers to employment and deliver commercial staffing services for customers who need workers. The program places individuals in temporary jobs as a way of building skills, creating work histories, and eventually attaining permanent jobs.

title: Mid Michigan Good Temp Alternative Staffing Organization
description: This grant to Goodwill Industries of Mid-Michigan, Inc., will support the expansion of the alternative staffing organization in Genesee County, Michigan. Alternative staffing organizations provide job brokering for workers who face significant barriers to employment and deliver commercial staffing services for customers who need workers. The program places individuals in temporary jobs as a way of building skills, creating work histories, and eventually attaining permanent jobs.

title: Mid Michigan Good Temp Alternative Staffing Organization
description: This planning grant to Goodwill Industries of Mid-Michigan, Inc., will support the creation of an alternative staffing organization in Genesee County, Michigan. Alternative staffing organizations provide job brokering for workers who face significant barriers to employment and deliver commercial staffing services for customers who need workers. Once under way, the program will place individuals in temporary jobs as a way of building skills, creating work histories, and eventually, attaining permanent jobs.

title: Modernizing "Youth Today" to Reach a Larger Audience
description: This grant will support the American Youth Work Center to move its “Youth Today” print publication toward a modern, online digital media product that will expand readership and increase subscriptions. Since 1992, the grantee has published “Youth Today”, a nationally distributed newspaper aimed at practitioners in the youth service field. “Youth Today” provides independent coverage of promising practices, issues, trends, research, and policies that shapes the services to youth, with special emphasis on disadvantaged youth. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) enhance the “Youth Today” Web site design and functionality to help subscribers better navigate the expanding archive of information; and 2) launch a marketing campaign to promote “Youth Today” more broadly and increase paid subscriptions in the next two years.

title: International Financial Institution (IFI) Reform Project
description: Energy is vital to improving the quality of life for the poor, providing income-generating opportunities, and increasing productivity in all sectors, yet nearly 1.5 billion people still lack access to electricity in developing countries. The World Bank and other international financial institutions have not adequately addressed this energy-poverty challenge. Through this project, the Sierra Club Foundation will seek to strengthen the World Bank’s environmental and social standards, as well as encourage investment in projects that reduce energy poverty while also reducing greenhouse gas emissions and minimizing environmental harm. Over the last grant period, its policy work contributed to significant increases in domestic export credit agencies lending for renewable energy and the creation of the Green Climate Fund.

title: International Financial Institution (IFI) Reform Project
description: Through this project, the Sierra Club Foundation will seek to strengthen the World Bank’s environmental and social standards, as well as encourage investment in projects that provide modern energy services to poor, rural communities in developing countries, commonly referred to as energy access. Such projects can also reduce greenhouse gas emissions and minimize environmental harm. This grant increase will cover costs associated with the planning and facilitation of a meeting to address innovative financing mechanisms to address energy access in developing countries.

title: International Financial Institution (IFI) Reform Project
description: The World Bank and other international financial institution lending have had negative social and environmental impacts on communities in developing countries. To address these challenges, the Sierra Club Foundation’s International Financial Institution Reform Project works to ensure that the World Bank safeguard policies remain strong and are seen as the global standard for development finance. In addition, this project works to ensure that the United Nations’ Green Climate Fund adopts and implements robust standards for all of its projects. Over the last two years, there has been positive progress at the World Bank and the Green Climate Fund in developing and revising environmental and social safeguard policies and ensuring that fewer fossil fuel projects are funded.

title: International Financial Institution (IFI) Reform Project
description: The mounting evidence is that developing countries will be most impacted by climate change and will have an urgent need to make use of efficient, renewable energy. However, World Bank lending to developing countries does not address the energy needs of poor people and constrains long-term efforts to alleviate poverty in these countries. To address these challenges, the Sierra Club Foundation’s International Financial Institution Reform Project will seek to ensure that the World Bank energy policy limits lending for fossil fuel projects; strengthens and fully implements export credit agency reforms in the United States; increases lending awareness among decisionmakers on the environmental and social impacts of World Bank and other international financial institutions; and builds alliances with environmental and other nongovernmental organizations, especially local groups impacted by international financial institution-funded projects.

title: Collaborative Master Plan and Implementation Strategy
description: With prior Mott support, the Alliance for Economic Success conducted the Understanding Wind Initiative, a community education and engagement process in Manistee and Benzie Counties (Michigan), designed to inform the debate around a proposed wind energy farm. The community dialogue, engendered by the initiative, led to the widespread conclusion that the townships in the region need a shared land development vision and master plan. With continuing support, the grantee will coordinate the development of such a master plan, as well as a collaborative implementation strategy.

title: Understanding Wind Initiative
description: A major wind energy farm has been proposed for townships straddling the border of Manistee and Benzie counties in the northwestern portion of Michigan’s Lower Peninsula. Such an energy project offers many potential benefits but has also raised concerns about impacts to the region’s natural values and community character. The Alliance for Economic Success, a regional, economic development, nonprofit organization based in Manistee, will coordinate a community education project on wind energy so that citizens and local leaders have the information they need to independently evaluate wind energy proposals and decide, as a community, how to proceed.

title: CEELI Institute Sustainability and Program Development Support
description: The project goal is to strengthen the rule of law in Central and Eastern Europe and Russia by supporting the sustainability of a permanent institute for postgraduate education and research in Prague, Czech Republic. Since 1999, the Central and East European Law Initiative Institute has hosted more than 1,200 students from 35 countries for a variety of training courses, conferences, and seminars. Housed in a completely refurbished 19th century villa in Prague, the institute has state-of-the-art lecture halls, conference rooms, computer centers, offices, and a library, as well as nearly 40 residential rooms. During the grant period, Friends of the CEELI Institute will contribute to the sustainability of the institute by seeding the development of new courses and servicing and reducing the institute’s debt connected to its renovation over the last several years. Friends of the CEELI Institute is a nonprofit based in Washington, D.C., that was set up to support the institute.

title: National Service Fund
description: A project of the Community Foundation of Greater Flint, the National Service Fund will help the Greater Flint area take better advantage of federal funds provided by the Corporation for National and Community Service by providing matching grants to eligible public charities and governmental units for the recruitment, selection, training, and ongoing support of national service participants working in the Flint area. The matching funds will provide a much-needed boost of human capital to tackle significant challenges in the areas of education, public safety, health, and the environment. The fund will be supported by the Flint National Service Accelerator, a project of the Boys & Girls Club of Greater Flint, which includes a full-time coordinator working to integrate AmeriCorps members into organizations throughout the Flint area.

title: Flint National Service Accelerator Fund
description: The Community Foundation of Greater Flint, created in 1988 with the merger of the Flint Public Trust and the Flint Area Health Foundation, has emerged as a major local philanthropic entity. Its funding focus is around systems-building, capacity-building, improving nonprofit effectiveness, advancing philanthropy, and supporting innovation. The Flint National Service Accelerator Fund, administered by the Community Foundation of Greater Flint in partnership with the Boys and Girls Club of Greater Flint, helps the Greater Flint area take better advantage of national service volunteers through federal funds provided by the Corporation for National and Community Service.
