The Flint National Service Accelerator Fund provides matching grants to eligible public charities and governmental units for the recruitment, selection, training, and ongoing support of national service participants working in the Flint area. The matching funds provide a much-needed boost of human capital to tackle significant challenges in the areas of education, public safety, health, and the environment.

title: Flint National Service Accelerator Fund
description: The Community Foundation of Greater Flint was created in 1988 with the merger of the Flint Public Trust and the Flint Area Health Foundation. Its funding is focused on increasing literacy rates in Genesee County, improving Flint neighborhoods, increasing access to healthy food, and advancing philanthropy. The Flint National Service Accelerator Fund, administered by the grantee in partnership with the Boys & Girls Club of Greater Flint, helps the Flint area take advantage of state and national service volunteers through state and federal funds provided by the Corporation for National and Community Service. The fund provides matching grants to eligible public charities and governmental units for the recruitment, selection, training, and ongoing support of national service participants working in the Flint area. The matching funds provide a much-needed boost of human capital to tackle significant challenges in the areas of education, public safety, health, and the environment.

title: Flint National Service Accelerator Fund
description: This grant increase will enable the Community Foundation of Greater Flint to provide financial resources for Flint area nonprofits and initiatives to recruit, train, and retain national service members for programs like Operation AmeriCorps.

title: Flint National Service Accelerator Fund
description: The Community Foundation of Greater Flint was created in 1988 with the merger of the Flint Public Trust and the Flint Area Health Foundation. Through discretionary grantmaking, the grantee focuses on the areas of literacy, neighborhoods, healthy food, and advancing philanthropy. Additionally, donor-advised funds, scholarships, special initiatives, and other donor vehicles contribute to local nonprofits each year. The Flint National Service Accelerator Fund, administered by the Community Foundation of Greater Flint in partnership with the United Way of Genesee County, helps Flint area agencies leverage state and national service members through the Corporation for National and Community Service and its affiliates. Matching grants provide resources to local nonprofit agencies for the required member cost share, training, and travel reimbursement.

title: Flint National Service Accelerator Fund
description: The Community Foundation of Greater Flint was created in 1988 with the merger of the Flint Public Trust and the Flint Area Health Foundation. Through discretionary grantmaking, the grantee focuses on the areas of literacy, neighborhoods, healthy food, and advancing philanthropy. The Flint National Service Accelerator Fund, administered by the grantee, in partnership with the United Way of Genesee County, helps Flint area agencies leverage state and national service members through the Corporation for National and Community Service and its affiliates. Flint area service members support projects aligned with the Corporation for National and Community Service priorities including education, public safety, health, and the environment. Activities also include assisting Flint residents and nonprofits during the Flint water crisis. Matching grants provide resources to local nonprofit agencies for the required member cost share, training, and travel reimbursement.

title: Flint National Service Accelerator Fund
description: The Flint National Service Accelerator Fund helps Flint area agencies leverage state and national service members through the Corporation for National and Community Service and its affiliates. Flint area service members support projects aligned with the City of Flint’s master plan and the Corporation for National and Community Service priorities including education, public safety, health, and the environment. Focus areas in Flint include community education, literacy, urban safety, nutrition, and assisting Flint residents and nonprofits to recover from the Flint water crisis. Matching grants provide resources to local nonprofit agencies for the required member cost share, training, and travel reimbursement. The fund is held at the Community Foundation of Greater Flint and is administered in partnership with the United Way of Genesee County.

title: National Service Fund
description: With this grant, the Community Foundation of Greater Flint will establish a National Service Fund to help the Greater Flint area take better advantage of federal funds provided through the Corporation for National and Community Service by providing matching grants to eligible public charities and governmental units to fund the recruitment, selection, training, and ongoing support of national service participants working in the Greater Flint area. The matching funds will result in a much-needed boost of human capital to tackle significant challenges in the areas of education, public safety, health, and the environment. The fund will be supported by the National Service Accelerator Initiative, a project of the Boys & Girls Club of Greater Flint, and includes a full-time coordinator who will help local groups identify and successfully integrate AmeriCorps members, VISTA volunteers, and other national service participants into their programming efforts.

title: Strengthening Institutional Capacity to Provide ICT Support to NGOs in CEE/Russia
geographic_focus: Russia, Bulgaria, Ukraine, Belarus, Romania, Montenegro, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Poland, Croatia, Kosovo, Serbia
description: The project goal is to strengthen the capacity of nongovernmental organizations in Central and Eastern Europe and Russia to access modern information and communication technologies and use them effectively to increase the impact of their work. To this end, Fundacja TechSoup will build a strong infrastructure for distributing technology products to nongovernmental organizations in the region in partnership with leading, local nonprofits and provide technical assistance to communities of practitioners utilizing technology for civic activism. Fundacja TechSoup was established in 2009 in Warsaw, Poland. Together with its sister organization, TechSoup Global, the grantee facilitates the donation and distribution of technology products from over 40 leading companies, including Microsoft, Adobe, and Cisco. The two organizations have brokered over seven million donations in 35 countries with a value of more than $2.1 billion. In the past two years, the grantee organized a series of online and offline events for technology-oriented nongovernmental organizations, including a two-day learning event in Bosnia and Herzegovina with more than 140 participants.

title: Strengthening Institutional Capacity to Provide ICT Support to NGOs in CEE/Russia
description: The project goal is to strengthen the capacity of nongovernmental organizations in the Central and Eastern Europe and Russia region to access modern information and communication technologies and use them effectively to increase the impact of their work. To this end, Fundacja TechSoup, in partnership with leading local nonprofits, will build a strong infrastructure for distributing technology products to nongovernmental organizations in the region and provide technical assistance to communities of practitioners utilizing technology for civic activism. A specific goal over the next two years will be to create new working relationships and initiate programs with partners in Ukraine and Moldova. Fundacja TechSoup was established in 2009 in Warsaw, Poland. Together with its sister organization, TechSoup Global, the grantee facilitates the donation and distribution of technology products from over 40 leading companies, including Microsoft, Adobe, and Cisco. Over the past two years, the grantee expanded its network of technology-oriented nongovernmental organizations in the region and organized a series of online and offline events, including a two-day learning event in Bosnia and Herzegovina with more than 150 participants and a competition for technology-related, social change projects in Turkey.

title: Strengthening Institutional Capacity to Provide ICT Support to NGOs in CEE
description: The project goal is to strengthen the capacity of nongovernmental organizations in Central and Eastern Europe to access modern information and communication technologies and use them effectively to increase the impact of their work. Fundacja TechSoup, in partnership with leading local nonprofits, will deliver comprehensive training programs in the effective use of information and communication technologies, build a strong infrastructure for distributing technology products to nongovernmental organizations in the region, and provide technical assistance to communities of practitioners utilizing technology for civic activism. Over the past two years, the grantee expanded its network of technology-oriented nongovernmental organizations in the region and organized a series of online and offline events, including workshops on the effective use of information and communication technologies for over 1,400 participants. The grantee also organized software donations with an estimated value of $12 million to over 2,000 nonprofit organizations in the region. The grantee is based in Warsaw, Poland.

title: Strengthening Institutional Capacity to Provide ICT Support to NGOs in CEE/Russia
geographic_focus: Serbia, Poland, Croatia, Montenegro, Ukraine, Romania, Russia, Bulgaria, Belarus, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo
description: The project goal is to strengthen the capacity of nongovernmental organizations in the Central and Eastern Europe and Russia region to access modern information and communication technologies and use them effectively to increase the impact of their work. To this end, Fundacja TechSoup will build a strong infrastructure for distributing technology products to nongovernmental organizations in the region in partnership with leading local nonprofits; launch GuideStar-type data collection systems in several countries; and support communities of practitioners utilizing technology for civic activism. In support of these objectives, the grantee will employ two new senior staff members to manage the above activities. Fundacja TechSoup was established in 2009 in Warsaw, Poland. Together with its sister organization, TechSoup Global, the grantee facilitates the donation and distribution of technology products from over 40 leading companies, including Microsoft, Adobe, and Cisco. As of September 2010, the two organizations have brokered over 6.6 million donations in 35 countries with a value of more than $2 billion.

title: Football Stories: Bosnian Tour
description: The project goal is to promote tolerance, understanding, and diversity as key democratic values in Bosnia-Herzegovina. To this end, the East West Centre Sarajevo will develop a theater performance called Football Stories and tour Bosnia-Herzegovina, visiting ten towns. Football Stories will be an original production that focuses on rising xenophobia, nationalism, and violence in society, which often become most visible during football matches. Each performance will be accompanied by workshops and discussions that address issues raised by the play. The grantee is an independent, nonprofit organization that creates and produces theater and other cultural events. Established in 2005, the grantee is based in Sarajevo and works nationally and internationally.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide funds to the Center for Michigan as it works to bolster Michigan’s statewide civic engagement. Operating in a nonpartisan fashion, the grantee has established itself as an independent source of information and education for the public on important policy issues, providing a link between citizens and the political system, engaging citizens in conversation, and ultimately having an impact on public policy. With this grant, the grantee will focus its work on three main areas: intensifying Michigan’s focus on early childhood education, expanding the “Bridge” magazine’s public issues journalism, and launching the next phase of public engagement campaigns.

title: Capacity Building
description: This grant will provide funds to the Center for Michigan as it works to bolster Michigan’s statewide civic engagement. Operating in a nonpartisan fashion, the Center for Michigan has established itself as an independent source of information and education for the public on important policy issues, providing a link between citizens and the political system, engaging citizens in conversation, and ultimately having an impact on public policy. With this grant, the Center for Michigan will continue its work with a focus on engaging and informing.

title: Hub for Agents of Social Change
description: The project goal is to strengthen young people’s capacities for and commitment to active participation in civic life on the local and national levels in Bulgaria. To this end, the Ideas Factory Association will provide training and capacity building to young activists, provide funding for small campaign and advocacy projects of individual activists and informal youth groups, and document and publicize creative activist practices from Bulgaria and around the world. In addition, the grantee will provide physical space and administrative support to youth activists and groups for projects and activities that are in line with the grantee’s mission. Ideas Factory Association was established in 2006 with the mission to strengthen civil society and youth participation in civic life in Bulgaria. The grantee’s key achievements to date include establishing a team of trainers and consultants experienced in creative activist approaches and techniques, providing training to young activists, organizing successful campaigns to stop illegal construction in protected natural reserves in Bulgaria, and initiating a youth festival of creative social and environmental initiatives. The grantee is based in Sofia, Bulgaria.

title: Hub for Agents of Social Change
description: The project goal is to strengthen young people’s capacities for and commitment to active participation in civic life on the local and national levels in Bulgaria. To this end, the Ideas Factory Association will provide training and capacity building to young activists and social entrepreneurs, provide funding for small projects of individuals and informal youth groups, and document and publicize creative activist practices from Bulgaria and around the world. In addition, the grantee will increase its collaboration with like-minded organizations in Central and Eastern Europe in order to strengthen youth movements in the region. Also, the grantee will improve its communications, operational capacity, and financial sustainability. Based in Sofia, Bulgaria, Ideas Factory Association was established in 2006 with the mission to strengthen civil society and youth participation in civic life. The grantee’s key achievements in the past two years include creating and piloting new methodologies for organizational capacity building, providing training and technical assistance to 34 young leaders and supporting their projects, organizing the sixth edition of a youth festival of creative social and environmental initiatives, and establishing working partnerships with local governments and public institutions. The grantee is based in Sofia, Bulgaria.

title: Gulf Coast Mapping & Outreach Project
description: Oxfam America is a nonprofit organization that seeks to elevate citizen voices in the decisionmaking processes that impact social, economic, and environmental systems. In the aftermath of the oil drilling disaster, the grantee helped its Gulf of Mexico partners respond to the ongoing impacts of crude oil contamination along the coast. With this grant, the grantee will continue connecting local groups to state, regional, and national efforts aimed at restoring and protecting the Gulf of Mexico’s coastal wetlands and related ecosystems. Specifically, the grantee will collaboratively develop and disseminate maps and data to prioritize the restoration of areas that have both high ecological value and economic importance for vulnerable coastal communities in Louisiana and Mississippi.

title: Flint and Genesee YES Network
description: This grant will provide funds to Kettering University to support the Flint and Genesee YES Network. The project is a collaborative among the city’s colleges and universities, business and economic leaders, and youth working to promote a youth entrepreneur culture within the region. By coordinating community initiatives to educate and support youth-led social and commercial ventures, the network aims to foster youth entrepreneurship as a path to formal employment and a sustainable regional economy.

title: National Expansion Initiative
description: This grant will enable Per Scholas to develop a sustainability plan for a new program site in Columbus, Ohio, and to conduct feasibility studies on two additional sites in Cincinnati, Ohio and St. Louis, Missouri. The plan development and studies will be followed by an implementation phase.

title: Strategic Expansion Planning
description: This grant will enable Per Scholas, a highly effective sectoral workforce development program in the information technology industry, to develop a program expansion plan to add three additional communities as program sites. The plan development will be followed by an implementation phase that will end December 2012.

title: Global Leadership Awards
description: This grant provided funds to Vital Voices Global Partnership for sponsorship of the Global Leadership Awards benefit held in Washington, DC on June 6, 2012. The benefit honored women leaders advancing economic, political, and social progress in their communities and beyond. Funds raised by the event are used to invest in emerging women leaders around the world — pioneers of economic development, political participation, and human rights.

title: Global Leadership Awards
description: This grant provides support to Vital Voices Global Partnership for sponsorship of the Global Leadership Awards benefit held in Washington, D.C., on April 2, 2013. The benefit honors women leaders advancing economic, political, and social progress in their communities and beyond. Funds raised by the event are used to invest in emerging women leaders around the world representing pioneers of economic development, political participation, and human rights.

title: Global Leadership Awards Benefit
description: This grant will provide funds to Vital Voices Global Partnership for sponsorship of the 10th Annual Global Leadership Awards Benefit to be held in Washington, D.C., on April 12, 2011. The benefit will honor women leaders advancing economic, political, and social progress in their communities and beyond. Funds raised by the event are used to invest in emerging women leaders around the world — pioneers of economic development, political participation, and human rights.

title: After School Program Emergency Support
grantee: New Hampshire Coalition Against Domestic and Sexual Violence
description: This grant will allow the New Hampshire Coalition Against Domestic Violence to provide supervision and administrative support for 25 AmeriCorps members working in afterschool programs throughout New Hampshire. The AmeriCorps members were formally associated with the now defunct PlusTime New Hampshire, which was the fiduciary for the state’s afterschool network. When PlusTime abruptly closed in December 2010, it left the AmeriCorps members with no way to complete their terms of service or continue their work with thousands of children in New Hampshire. The grant will leverage approximately $250,000 in federal funds to support high quality afterschool programs in New Hampshire.

title: Climate Adaptation Survey
geographic_focus: Alabama, South Carolina, Georgia, Tennessee, North Carolina
description: Climate change is affecting water resources across the country, including the southeastern United States, making it necessary for resource managers to integrate this emerging reality into their plans and projects. EcoAdapt, a national organization dedicated to building the field of climate change adaptation, will address this need by surveying natural resource managers in the southeastern United States. The goal of the survey will be to identify and document model approaches to site-based freshwater conservation activities in the face of climate change. The results of the survey will be documented and disseminated through a variety of means, most notably by using the Climate Adaptation Knowledge Exchange, a Website maintained by the grantee for the purpose of sharing climate adaptation knowledge.

title: Climate Adaptation Survey
geographic_focus: South Carolina, Georgia, Tennessee, North Carolina, Alabama
description: EcoAdapt is a national organization dedicated to building the field of climate change adaptation. With this grant increase, the grantee will complete a survey of natural resources managers in the southeastern United States to identify and document model approaches to site-based, freshwater conservation activities in the face of climate change. The results of the survey are scheduled to be released on the occasion of the Second National Adaptation Forum in May 2015.

title: Great Lakes Climate Adaptation Survey
geographic_focus: Michigan, Pennsylvania, Indiana, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Ontario, Illinois, Ohio, New York
description: Climate change is affecting the Great Lakes region making it necessary for regional resource managers to integrate this new reality into their plans and projects. There is a consequential need for consolidated information and case studies about how this can be done most effectively. EcoAdapt, a national organization dedicated to building the field of climate change adaptation, will address this need by surveying natural resource managers in the Great Lakes Basin. The goal of the survey will be to identify and document model approaches to site-based freshwater conservation activities in the face of climate change. The results of the survey will be documented and disseminated through a variety of means, most notably by using the Climate Adaptation Knowledge Exchange, a Web site developed by the grantee for the purpose of sharing climate adaptation knowledge.

title: MyAccountCard Evaluation
description: Over 50 million adults in the United States are unbanked or underbanked. These disproportionately low-income and minority Americans lack access to safe financial accounts, which are an important vehicle for savings and a precursor to lifelong asset building. Through this grant, the Mott Foundation will partner with the U.S. Department of Treasury and the Urban Institute to evaluate outcomes from the MyAccountCard pilot program that will offer one million low- and moderate-income tax filers a fully reloadable, low-cost, prepaid account card that can be used for point-of-sale purchases, bill payment, or automated teller machine withdrawals. The card also features a linked savings account. Using 2011 tax season data, Urban Institute will examine use of the prepaid card product to determine whether it is an effective strategy to help people move into the financial mainstream, avoid costly alternative financial services, and accumulate savings.

title: America's Shrinking Cities
description: This grant supports the American Assembly’s April 2011 forum on America’s Shrinking Cities. Founded in 1950 by Dwight Eisenhower and affiliated with Columbia University, the grantee commissions research and produces a series of public affairs forums that convene leading authorities representing a broad spectrum of perspectives and interests. Through facilitated conversation and reflection on background papers, participants at America’s Shrinking Cities conference will jointly develop recommendations that will guide policymakers, practitioners, and others in helping post-industrial cities to reposition themselves as economically viable and livable places. Recommendations will be published and disseminated through the American Assembly’s extensive mailing list.

title: Kathy A. Agard Endowed Fellowship in Community Philanthropy
description: This grant contributes to the Kathy A. Agard Endowed Fellowship in Community Philanthropy at Grand Valley State University. The aim of the fellowship is to assist students interested in studying community philanthropy, including individual giving, community foundations, giving circles, and public foundations. Two Agard fellows per year will engage in independent research or work on advanced projects aimed at expanding the understanding of individual or organized philanthropy. The fellowship honors Dr. Kathy Agard, recently retired executive director of the Dorothy A. Johnson Center for Philanthropy, an academic center at Grand Valley State University which focuses on increasing the efficiency and effectiveness of the charitable sector by conducting research, teaching effective practices, and providing pathways to service. The grantee is located in Michigan’s second largest metropolitan region of Grand Rapids. Its mission is to educate students to shape their lives, their professions, and their societies.

title: Connecting Leaders Fellowship Program
description: This renewal grant will support the Connecting Leaders Fellowship Program of the Association of Black Foundation Executives that provides outstanding professional development opportunities to African-American philanthropic staff. Since 2005, 50 men and women have participated in the program, with several participants advancing to executive-level positions within the field. The core components of the fellowship program are the week-long leadership summit, the executive coaching, and the monthly distance learning calls. In 2010, the fellowship program was redesigned to offer fellows greater opportunity to understand the connection between philanthropy and black communities in midsized cities. As a result of the Foundation’s support and the new emphasis on smaller communities, the grantee has decided to host the leadership summit in Flint for a second year, where the participants will gain an increased understanding of how institutional and grassroots philanthropy can impact midsized communities.

title: Connecting Leaders Fellowship Program
description: This grant will support the Connecting Leaders Fellowship Program of the Association of Black Foundation Executives that provides outstanding professional development opportunities to African-American philanthropic staff. Since 2005, 50 men and women have participated in the program, with several participants advancing to executive-level positions within the field. The core components of the fellowship are the week-long leadership summit, the executive coaching, and the monthly distance learning calls. In 2010, the fellowship was redesigned to offer fellows greater opportunity to understand the connection between philanthropy and black communities in midsized cities. With continued support from Mott and a new emphasis on smaller communities, the grantee has decided to host the leadership summit in Flint, where the participants will gain an increased understanding of how institutional and grassroots philanthropy can impact midsized communities.

title: Louisiana Water Institute
description: For the past several years, stakeholders in Louisiana have discussed the need for an independent, science-based institute that could effectively address the state’s coastal restoration challenges. The sense of urgency for such an institute grew in 2010, when the oil spill in the Gulf of Mexico showed the world the importance of Louisiana’s coastland and offshore waters. The Baton Rouge Area Foundation, a highly respected community foundation, is working with public officials and private stakeholders to turn this institute idea into a reality. With partial funding from Mott, the grantee will complete early stage planning for the institute, with the goal of launching the new organization in early 2012.

title: Establishment of Education Policy Institute
description: This grant will provide funds for Furman University to operate the White-Riley-Peterson Policy Institute in its second year, bringing together a diverse group of 15 emerging leaders from the afterschool and education fields to serve as fellows. Over the course of a year, fellows will be exposed to policy experts, an intensive policy curriculum, and national networking opportunities. Fellows will complete the program able to positively contribute to the development of policies that support afterschool and expanded learning opportunities for children across the country.

title: Establishment of Education Policy Institute

Over the course of a year, fellows will be exposed to policy experts, an intensive policy curriculum, and national networking opportunities. Fellows will complete the program able to positively contribute to the development of policies that support afterschool and summer learning opportunities for children across the country.

Fellows will complete the program being able to positively contribute to the development of policies that support afterschool and summer learning opportunities for children across the country.

title: Education Policy Institute
description: This grant will provide funds for Furman University to operate the White-Riley-Peterson Policy Institute which brings together a diverse group of 15 emerging leaders from the afterschool and education fields to serve as fellows. Fellows will complete the program being able to positively contribute to the development of policies that support afterschool and summer learning opportunities for children across the country.

title: Establishment of Education Policy Institute
description: This grant will allow Furman University to create and pilot the White-Riley-Peterson Policy Institute that will bring together a diverse group of 15 emerging leaders from the afterschool and education fields to serve as fellows. Furman University faculty and staff will work with national partners to design the institute and develop a competitive applicant pool. Over the course of a year, the fellows will be exposed to policy experts, an intensive policy curriculum, and national networking opportunities. Emerging policy leaders will complete the program with the ability to positively contribute to the development of policies that support afterschool and expanded learning opportunities for children across the country.

title: Climate Resilient Communities
geographic_focus: Wayne, Washtenaw, Monroe, Livingston, Ingham, Oakland, Jackson
description: The Huron River Watershed Council, one of the most respected organizations of its type in the Great Lakes Basin, has launched a model process to address climate change impacts, the Climate Resilient Communities project. Early results include new information on cultivating and sustaining tree species and a more coordinated approach to managing river flows. With additional support, the grantee will help implement the climate change adaptation strategies already identified, continue to distribute reliable climate information to interested parties, and work with stakeholders to integrate climate change considerations into local hazard mitigation planning.

title: Adapting to Climate Change at the Watershed Scale
geographic_focus: Wayne, Ingham, Washtenaw, Jackson, Oakland, Monroe, Livingston
description: Local communities in the Great Lakes basin already are beginning to notice impacts from climate change, and many of the most serious consequences will impact the hydrologic cycle. The Huron River Watershed Council, one of the most well-respected organizations of its type in the Great Lakes basin, proposes to develop a climate adaptation plan for its home watershed through a series of workshops and work groups over the course of 12 months. The process and action plan will be captured in a summary document that will be shared with regional, national, and binational entities working on climate change, so that the experience in the Huron River watershed can serve as a model for other local efforts and inform the policy development process.

title: Transition Support
description: Since 1922, the United Way of Genesee County has raised funds to support local agencies that provide a variety of human services to area residents. In recent years, fundraising has been difficult because of changing community demographics and the increased quantity and sophistication level of direct fundraising by nonprofit agencies. This increase will provide support for the grantee to search for a permanent executive director to continue to strengthen the organization to serve Genesee County nonprofits and residents.

title: Transition Support
description: Since 1922, the United Way of Genesee County has raised funds to support local agencies that provide a variety of human services to area residents. In recent years, fundraising has been a challenge due to changing community demographics and the increased level of direct fundraising by nonprofit agencies. This grant will provide support for the grantee to search for an interim executive director to help restructure the organization to better serve the community and incorporate more modern fundraising practices.

title: Flint/Genesee Earn & Learn Initiative - Regranting Partnership with Open Society Foundations
description: This grant will enable Career Alliance, Inc., to continue the Earn & Learn Initiative in Flint and Genesee County targeting disconnected youth ages 18 to 24, unemployed adults (particularly minority males), and exoffenders reentering the workforce. In the first phase of this initiative, the grantee provided 278 individuals with training, subsidized employment, and credentialing opportunities in career pathways such as construction and healthcare. The initiative is designed to spark immediate entry-level work opportunities while simultaneously increasing participants’ skills and helping them manage barriers to success. Recommended support will enable the grantee to assist current and an additional 150 participants in maintaining and/or enhancing their work skills to make the transition from subsidized employment to more permanent job placements. The Open Society Foundations’ (formerly Open Society Institute) investment in the Earn & Learn Initiative will be matched 1:1 by both the Mott Foundation and the state of Michigan.

title: Flint/Genesee Earn & Learn Initiative - Regranting Partnership with Open Society Foundations
description: This grant increase will enable Genesee/Shiawassee Michigan Works! to complete the final phase of the Flint/Genesee Earn & Learn Initiative. Launched in 2011, this initiative was designed to help disconnected youth (ages 18-24), unemployed adults (particularly minority males), and ex-offenders reentering the workforce enhance their work skills and ultimately secure unsubsidized employment opportunities. Genesee/Shiawassee Michigan Works! is one of three sites participating in the initiative — additional sites are located in Detroit and Saginaw. All three sites were supported by a public-private partnership between the State of Michigan, Michigan grantmakers, and the Open Society Foundations. This grant increase will support three primary program activities: education/training, subsidized employment, and supportive services.

title: Flint/Genesee Earn & Learn Initiative - Regranting Partnership with Open Society Foundations
description: This grant will enable Career Alliance, Inc., to implement the Earn & Learn Initiative in Flint and Genesee County, targeting 264 disconnected youth (18-24), young minority males (including former prisoners reentering the workforce), and chronically unemployed adults that want to re-enter the workforce. The initiative is designed to spark immediate, entry-level work opportunities while simultaneously increasing workers’ skills and helping them manage barriers to success. The grantee will partner with its higher education partners — Mott Community College, Baker College, and University of Michigan-Flint — to provide career pathways to help individuals advance through training and acquire postsecondary credentials and a living-wage job. The Open Society Foundations’ (formerly Open Society Institute) investment in the Earn & Learn Initiative will be matched 1:1 by both the Mott Foundation and the state of Michigan.

title: General Purposes
description: The Desmond Tutu Peace Centre was founded by Archbishop Emeritus Desmond Tutu and his wife, Leah, in 1998 to encourage and inspire future generations to commit themselves to work for world peace, facilitate dialogue and debate on topical issues in South Africa, create platforms for the voices of the marginalized to be heard, find peaceful ways of resolving conflict, and inspire leaders to choose peace over confrontation. This grant will support the grantee to implement its programs that include hosting an annual peace summit for youth, training teachers and high school students from violent neighborhoods around Cape Town on how to resolve conflict peacefully, hosting annual lectures celebrating the life of Archbishop Tutu, and holding public dialogues that address topical issues that broadly affect society.

title: Strengthening Capacity and Outreach
description: The project goal is to increase civic engagement in holding local government institutions accountable in Kosovo. To this end, FOL Movement will strengthen its capacity to organize and mobilize participation in decisionmaking processes, particularly at the municipal level. During the grant period, the grantee will establish and maintain its presence in four key municipalities, expand and broaden its membership and volunteer base, and launch an anticorruption resource center. During 2011-2013, the grantee focused on programming in Gjakova and Podujeva, expanded its general assembly membership, and gathered volunteers from across Kosovo. Established as an independent, nonprofit organization in 2009, FOL Movement has successfully engaged citizens in direct actions to hold government officials accountable for their decisions, highlight corruption, and promote transparency. The organization is based in Prishtina.

title: Strengthening Capacity and Outreach
description: The project goal is to increase civic engagement in holding local government institutions accountable in Kosovo. To this end, FOL Movement will strengthen its capacity to organize and mobilize participation in decisionmaking processes, particularly at the municipal level. During the grant period, the grantee will further develop and expand specific mechanisms for monitoring local government and stimulating public participation in decisionmaking. The grantee will also conduct an independent evaluation of its work and launch a new strategic planning process. During 2013-2015, the grantee monitored and reported on public procurement practices in three municipalities and shared the results widely in Kosovo. The grantee also researched the lack of government investment in certain key sectors in five municipalities. The results were shared with citizens during a campaign in these municipalities called FOL’s Week, designed to inform citizens and engage them in dialogue with local government about priorities in their municipalities. Established as an independent, nonprofit organization in 2009, FOL Movement has successfully engaged citizens in direct actions to hold government officials accountable for their decisions, highlight corruption, and promote transparency. The organization is based in Prishtina.

title: Strengthening Capacity and Outreach
description: The project goal is to increase civic engagement in holding local governmental institutions accountable in Kosovo. To this end, FOL Movement will strengthen its capacity to organize and mobilize participation in decisionmaking processes, particularly at the municipal level. During the grant period, the grantee will establish its presence in three key municipalities, expand and broaden its membership, and create a pool of up to 1,000 active volunteers from across the country. Established as an independent, nonprofit organization in 2009, the grantee has successfully engaged citizens in direct actions to hold government officials accountable for their decisions, highlight corruption, and promote transparency. The organization is based in Prishtina.

title: YouthBank Development in Turkey
description: The project goals are to encourage youth engagement in community development and stimulate local philanthropy in Turkey. To these ends, the Community Volunteers Foundation will support the development of the YouthBank model in Turkey. During the grant period, the grantee will support and develop five existing YouthBanks and establish five more. During the two years, these YouthBanks will support more than 180 community initiatives. In finding locations for the new YouthBanks, emphasis will be given to smaller cities and towns across Turkey where young people have fewer opportunities. Specific activities will include training, mentoring, study visits, and technical assistance to YouthBanks, as well as financial support for local projects identified by YouthBanks in their communities. During 2011-2012, the grantee supported the development of six YouthBanks in five different locations in Turkey and organized extensive network and training opportunities for participants, including exchange visits with YouthBanks in Armenia. The Community Volunteers Foundation was established in 2002 and is a national-level nonprofit working to increase youth activism through volunteerism. The foundation is based in Istanbul.

title: YouthBank Development in Turkey
description: The project goals are to encourage youth engagement in community development and stimulate local philanthropy in Turkey. To these ends, the Community Volunteers Foundation will support the development of YouthBank, a model for youth-led, community-based grantmaking, in Turkey. During the grant period, the grantee will support and develop existing YouthBanks and establish three more. The grantee will provide financial support for local projects identified by YouthBanks in their communities and support the capacity of young people and other stakeholders in YouthBank through training, mentoring, networking, and study visits. Additionally, the grantee will experiment with the adaptation of YouthBank to other contexts, including school dormitories, culture houses, and youth centers, with the goal of scaling up the number of YouthBanks in operation in Turkey. During 2013-2015, the grantee increased the number of YouthBanks that it runs from 5 to 11, organized extensive network and training opportunities for participants, and commissioned an in-depth, independent impact analysis of YouthBank in one community. Based in Istanbul, the Community Volunteers Foundation was established in 2002 and is a national-level nonprofit working to increase youth activism through volunteerism.

title: YouthBank Development in Turkey
description: The project goals are to encourage youth engagement in community development and stimulate local philanthropy in Turkey. The Community Volunteers Foundation supports the further development of YouthBank—a model for youth-led, community-based grantmaking—in Turkey. During the grant period, the grantee will focus on creating a model for the sustainability of YouthBanks in Turkey. Local YouthBank participants will be trained in identifying and working with local funders, and the grantee will create a special YouthBank fund that will manage locally raised funds and report to donors. At the same time, the grantee will continue to provide training and support to the local YouthBank practitioners and their local government and nonprofit sector partners in order to build their capacity for self-management. Based in Istanbul, the Community Volunteers Foundation was established in 2002 and is a national-level nonprofit working to increase youth activism through volunteerism.

title: YouthBank Development in Turkey
description: The project goals are to encourage youth engagement in community development and stimulate local philanthropy in Turkey. The Community Volunteers Foundation will support the development of the YouthBank model in Turkey. Building on the success of a pilot project in which the grantee launched three YouthBanks — two in Istanbul and one in the city of Samsun on the Black Sea coast — the grantee will continue to support and develop these three YouthBanks and expand the project to include three additional sites during the grant period. Specific activities will include training, mentoring, study visits, and technical assistance to YouthBanks as well as financial support for local projects identified by YouthBanks in their communities. The Community Volunteers Foundation was established in 2002 and is a national-level nonprofit working to increase youth activism through volunteerism. The foundation is based in Istanbul.

title: School of Activism
description: The project goals are to promote constructive youth activism, provide civic education, and engage young people in the work of civil society organizations in Kosovo. Through this project, the Initiative for Progress will further develop its School of Activism, which is designed to provide young people across Kosovo with the skills and confidence needed to become active citizens in their communities. During the grant period, approximately 560 young people will participate in the school. Following each session of the school, participants will engage in community activities that address a pressing need or issue. The grantee will assist participants to organize these activities. During the summer of 2011, the school gathered approximately 150 young people for a series of theoretical courses and practical, hands-on trainings and workshops designed to give them the motivation, knowledge, and skills needed to be active in their communities. A second such summer school was implemented in 2012. Follow up activities organized by the grantee with participants included creating opportunities for high school students to voice their concerns and dialogue with school officials and an awareness campaign about the hazards of smoking. The grantee is based in Ferizaj and has a project office in Pristina.

title: School of Activism
description: The project goals are to promote constructive youth activism, provide civic education, and engage young people in the work of civil society organizations in Kosovo. Through this project, the Initiative for Progress will further develop its School of Activism, which is designed to provide young people with the skills and confidence needed to become active citizens in their communities. During the grant period, approximately 400 young people will participate in the school. Following each session of school, participants will engage in community activities that address a pressing need or issue. The grantee will assist participants to organize these activities. During 2013-2014, more than 400 young people of diverse backgrounds and ethnicities, including young people from Kosovo’s Serbian community, participated in the school. Sessions of the school were organized in 14 municipalities, including many small, rural communities, where young people do not have many opportunities to be active. In addition to theoretical courses, trainings, and workshops, participants engaged in follow-up activities organized by the grantee. The grantee is based in the city of Ferizaj.

title: School of Activism
description: The project goals are to promote constructive youth activism, provide civic education, and engage young people in the work of civil society organizations in Kosovo. During the grant period, the Initiative for Progress will provide young people with the skills and confidence needed to become active citizens in their communities. Approximately 280 young people will participate in training programs and workshops designed to prepare young people to be leaders in their communities and to advance their learning and employment prospects. The grantee will also engage past participants in its training programs to become mentors for young people. Mentors will be supported to develop programs in their communities. Finally, the grantee will work with the Ministry of Education to introduce a curriculum on active civic participation in high schools in Kosovo. During 2015–2016, 174 young people of diverse backgrounds and ethnicity participated in the program. The grantee is based in the city of Ferizaj.

title: School of Activism
description: The project goals are to promote constructive youth activism, provide civic education, and engage young people in the work of civil society organizations in Kosovo. With one of the youngest populations in Europe, Kosovo faces tremendous challenges related to high youth unemployment, a failing education system, rising violence in schools, and low levels of youth participation in decisionmaking processes. Through this project, the Initiative for Progress will share its experience and approaches in Ferizaj with young people in other towns and cities by establishing a Kosovo-wide School of Activism. In each of the two summers over the next 18 months, 330 high school and university students from across Kosovo will participate in two-week courses with a curriculum designed and taught by experts, academics, and experienced activists. The grantee is based in Ferizaj and has a project office in Prishtina.

title: Promoting Sustainability in Energy and Infrastructure Investments in Latin America
description: This project would support the Interamerican Association for Environmental Defense, a nonprofit environmental law and policy organization that brings together a skilled team of experts in Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Mexico, Peru, and the United States to participate in the review processes and international negotiations that guide energy and infrastructure investments in Latin America. The grantee will focus on promoting compliance with international norms and standards on environmental sustainability, particularly in the areas of energy investments and climate-related investments. Support will also be provided to strengthen and expand the coalition of nongovernmental organizations working toward sustainable energy and investment policies in South America.

title: Promoting Sustainability in Energy and Infrastructure Investments in Latin America
description: The Interamerican Association for Environmental Defense is a nonprofit environmental law and policy organization that brings together a skilled team of experts in Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Mexico, Peru, and the United States to participate in the regional processes and international negotiations that guide energy and infrastructure investments in Latin America. With Mott support, the grantee will focus on promoting compliance with international norms and standards on environmental sustainability, particularly in the areas of energy investments and climate-related investments. Support will also be provided to strengthen and expand coalitions of nongovernmental organizations working toward sustainable energy and investment policies in South America.

title: Promoting Sustainability in Energy and Infrastructure Investments in Latin America
description: The Interamerican Association for Environmental Defense is a nonprofit environmental law and policy organization that brings together a skilled team of experts in Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Mexico, Peru, and the United States to participate in the regional processes and international negotiations that guide energy and infrastructure investments in Latin America. With this grant increase, the grantee will focus on contributing to initiatives that provide clean energy access to South American rural communities, and strengthen engagement surrounding energy investments and climate-related investments of the Green Climate Fund.

title: Promoting Sustainability in Energy and Infrastructure Investments in Latin America
description: The Interamerican Association for Environmental Defense is a nonprofit environmental law and policy organization of skilled experts in Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Mexico, Peru, and the United States that participates in the regional processes and international negotiations that guide energy and infrastructure investments in Latin America. Over the course of this grant, the grantee will work to ensure that infrastructure and energy investments in Latin America support environmental sustainability, national priorities, and local sustainable development.

title: Promoting Sustainability in Energy and Infrastructure Investments in Latin America
description: The Interamerican Association for Environmental Defense is a nonprofit environmental law and policy organization in Latin America and the United States that participates in the regional processes and international negotiations to guide sustainable energy and infrastructure investments in Latin America. Over the previous grant period, the grantee worked to ensure that national and international financial institutions applied strong social and environmental standards to energy infrastructure development finance in Latin America. Over the next grant period, the grantee will engage in a review of the social and environmental framework of a major regional development bank in Latin America and disseminate information and analysis of international best practice for environmental impact review processes.

title: Promoting Sustainability in Energy and Infrastructure Investments in Latin America
description: This grant will provide support for the Interamerican Association for Environmental Defense, a nonprofit environmental law and policy organization that brings together a skilled team of experts in Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Mexico, Peru, and the United States to work on promoting compliance with international norms and standards on environmental sustainability, particularly in the areas of energy investments and climate-related investments. This project will also provide support for tracking implementation of energy and climate policies at the World Bank and Inter-American Development Bank.

title: Detroit/Wayne Earn & Learn Initiative - Regranting Partnership with Open Society Foundations
description: This grant will enable Southwest Housing Solutions to continue implementing the Earn & Learn Initiative in Southeast Michigan, targeting disconnected youth ages 18 to 24, formerly incarcerated prisoners, and chronically unemployed individuals who want to reenter the workforce. The initiative is designed to spark immediate entry-level work opportunities while simultaneously increasing workers’ skills and helping them manage barriers to success. The grantee will work with a variety of local service providers, training and education partners, and employers to implement this initiative. The Open Society Foundations’ (formerly Open Society Institute) investment in the Earn & Learn Initiative will be matched 2:1 by the Kellogg and Skillman foundations, the New Economy Initiative, and the state of Michigan.

title: Detroit/Wayne Earn & Learn Initiative - Regranting Partnership with Open Society Foundations
description: This grant will enable Southwest Housing Solutions to implement the Earn & Learn Initiative in Southeast Michigan, targeting 850 disconnected youth (18-24) and 260 formerly incarcerated prisoners and chronically unemployed individuals residing that want to re-enter the workforce. The initiative is designed to spark immediate, entry-level work opportunities while simultaneously increasing workers’ skills and helping them manage barriers to success. The grantee will work with a variety of local service providers, training and education partners, and employers to implement this initiative. The Open Society Foundations’ (formerly Open Society Institute) investment in the Earn & Learn Initiative will be matched 2:1 by Kellogg and Skillman Foundations, the New Economy Initiative, and the state of Michigan.

title: Office of Urban and Metropolitan Initiatives
description: This grant will provide funds to the Council of Michigan Foundations for support of the Office of Urban and Metropolitan Initiatives. This office will provide Michigan’s governor with the staffing resources needed to help with the development of policies related to the economic development of core cities and urban regions in Michigan. Specifically, the office aims to focus on economic impact and job growth initiatives including transportation and infrastructure, public services, land use and sustainability, housing, and workforce and economic development.

title: Office of Urban and Regional Initiatives
description: This grant will provide funds to the Council of Michigan Foundations for the establishment of the Office of Urban and Regional Initiatives. This office will provide Michigan’s governor with the staffing resources needed to help with the development of policies related to the economic development of core cities and urban regions in Michigan. The director will work closely with the governor’s economic development team, the Office of Urban and Regional Initiatives, and Michigan’s Departments of Transportation and Treasury.

title: General Purposes
description: After a concerted effort over the last year to restructure and downsize operations, Public/Private Ventures has decided, given current trends in program evaluation and resource constraints among both public and private funders, that it will be necessary to cease operations on or around July 31, 2012. This grant will help this longtime Foundation partner close responsibly by supporting the transfer of all intellectual property to third parties, wrapping-up or transferring existing projects, and retaining needed legal and accounting support to dissolve the organization.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will help Public/Private Ventures stabilize its current fiscal situation and implement a new business model focused on helping practitioners better develop and use performance and evaluation data within their programs. The organization experienced significant financial pressure as a result of the downturn in the economy and was forced to begin making significant structural reforms including reductions in its workforce, renegotiating its office space lease, and outsourcing. Despite its significant efforts, the grantee is still projecting a shortfall in 2011 and 2012. Following Mott’s lead pledge, several other foundations have pledged nearly $1.1 million to help this key partner in program evaluation to implement its reform strategy. This new core support will allow the organization to focus on executing research and demonstration projects in the areas of youth development, criminal justice, and workforce development.

title: Connecting Global Philanthropy to Community Philanthropy
description: The project goal is to raise awareness among individual philanthropists around the world about the value of community foundations. To this end, the Synergos Institute is working to connect global philanthropists with existing community foundations in the countries where they reside and the regions of their philanthropy in the developing world. In the project’s first phase, the grantee identified and surveyed over 70 persons involved in either global or community philanthropy, drawing mainly from its Global Philanthropists Circle and Senior Fellows Program. Many were brought together in focus groups at events in Mexico, Brazil, India, and the United States. In the next phase, the grantee will conduct at least four more regional convenings, survey participants, and broadly disseminate findings and recommendations. Founded in 1986, the Synergos Institute promotes collaborative approaches that bring rich and poor together, along with other relevant groups and institutions, to overcome poverty and foster sustainable development in developing countries.

title: Connecting Next Generation Philanthropists to Community Philanthropy
description: The program goal is to educate young philanthropists on the potential of community philanthropy. Over the next two years, using Mexico as a laboratory, Synergos Institute will bring together next-generation philanthropists and community foundation leaders to promote the concepts of strategic philanthropy and bridging leadership, thus creating cross-understanding between the two groups as a basis for future collaboration. The process will involve an initial assembly in a retreat-like setting, two workshops, a final commencement session, and an optional personal reflection retreat. This will be followed by publication and dissemination of the learnings from the process, which will inform further efforts both in Mexico and other places. Founded in 1986, the Synergos Institute promotes collaborative approaches that bring rich and poor together, along with other relevant groups and institutions, to overcome poverty and foster sustainable development in developing countries.

title: Connecting Global Philanthropy to Community Philanthropy
description: The project goal is to raise awareness among individual philanthropists around the world about the value of community foundations. To this end, Synergos Institute will connect philanthropists with existing community foundations in their communities of residence and the regions of their philanthropy. Through research, surveying, mapping, site visits, convenings, and structured meetings, the project will strengthen the capacity and confidence of community foundations from developing countries in interacting with individual philanthropists. The project will mainly focus on, but not be limited to, members of Synergos’ Global Philanthropists Circle, approximately half of whom are from the Global South. The grantee will also make use of the expertise and relationships of its senior fellows who have strong connections to community foundations. Founded in 1986, the Synergos Institute promotes collaborative approaches that bring rich and poor together, along with other relevant groups and institutions, to overcome poverty and foster sustainable development in developing countries.

title: Savings and the Recession
description: This grant will enable Pew Charitable Trusts to commission original research that explores the impact of the nation’s economic recession and budding recovery on Americans’ personal savings rates. The project will be a collaboration between Pew and the Mott Foundation, with the two institutions working together on the selection of research projects, collaborating on and co-branding three unique reports or publications, and co-hosting a series of events to promote dissemination of the findings and policy implications. The partnership will leverage the financial investment of both institutions to raise public, media, and policymaker awareness of the importance of personal savings for supporting American families and promoting their upward mobility.

title: Constituent Voice in Philanthropy
description: This project supports the planning phase of a multiyear partnership between Keystone Accountability and the Worldwide Initiatives for Grantmaker Support, a network of philanthropic membership associations and support organizations. The aim is to provide grantee and beneficiary feedback services to local grantmakers through the network. Keystone Accountability, a United States charitable organization with offices in the United Kingdom and South Africa, has developed the constituent voice method, which draws from tested customer satisfaction techniques and adapts them to philanthropy in order to increase social impact. Through an iterative consultation process, the grantee will test the market and agree on designs for tools and support services that would allow network members to offer constituent voice services. Project activities will include: 1) an initial survey and request for expressions of interest; 2) workshops and other engagements at network events; 3) business plan development; and 4) the development of a registry of support.

title: Lenore Croudy Student Success Fund
description: This grant will provide funds to the Foundation for Mott Community College for the Lenore Croudy Student Success Fund, which was established to honor Lenore Croudy and her dedication to the success of students.

title: East West Performing Arts Centre
description: The project goal is to support the establishment of a new performing arts center in Sarajevo, Bosnia-Herzegovina. The center will be designed to embody the multiethnic promise of Sarajevo and the country and help restore dignity to a society that once prided itself on being a meeting point of East and West. During the grant period, East West Centre Sarajevo, an independent, nonprofit theater company in Sarajevo, will complete all legal procedures connected with obtaining the building site and ownership and operation of the future performing arts center, contract to undertake preparation of the site for construction, and create and implement a fundraising strategy for the construction of the center. An international, high-level advisory committee will also be established to guide the development of the project. East West Centre Sarajevo was established in November 2005 and has produced many widely acclaimed theater pieces that have toured Bosnia-Herzegovina and internationally.

title: National Center for Education Organizing
description: The National Center for Education Organizing at the Annenberg Institute for School Reform at Brown University will support the field of education organizing by providing training, technical assistance, research, and policy analysis to community organizations working on education improvement at the local, state, and national levels. This grant will support the infrastructure of the program, including the establishment of an advisory board which will include prominent leaders from the fields of research, policy, and practice; the identification of staff; and the identification of a team of consultants and field associates to work with organizations across the United States.

title: Policy and Messaging Strategies for Afterschool Networks
description: This grant will continue to support FowlerHoffman in identifying current opportunities for the statewide afterschool networks, assisting in the development of the Expanded Learning and Afterschool Project, and making recommendations for how to advance afterschool programs and the networks in the future. This project will include ongoing technical assistance to the networks on messaging and policy development, and a review of policy trends to help develop a long-term vision for the afterschool field. In addition, the grantee will work with the Foundation to immediately apply insights and strategies as they are learned to best position afterschool programs and the statewide afterschool networks moving forward.

title: Policy and Messaging Strategies for Afterschool Networks
description: This grant will continue to support FowlerHoffman in identifying current opportunities for the statewide afterschool networks, assisting in the development of the expanded learning and afterschool project, and making recommendations for how to advance afterschool programs and the networks in the future. In addition, this project will include the development of an assessment protocol for the statewide afterschool networks, and support for potential new statewide afterschool networks.

title: Policy and Messaging Strategies for Afterschool Networks
description: This grant will continue support to FowlerHoffman to identify current opportunities for the statewide afterschool networks and make recommendations for how to advance afterschool programs and the networks for the future. In addition, this project will include the integration and oversight of a network assessment protocol for the statewide afterschool networks, and finally, the grant will provide support for the establishment of a network or partnership entity to serve the eight states currently without statewide afterschool networks.

title: Supporting Statewide Afterschool Networks
description: This grant will continue support for FowlerHoffman to provide comprehensive technical assistance to the statewide afterschool networks. Over the next two years, the grantee will focus on: 1) advising and supporting the 50 statewide networks and partnerships to increase network sustainability and effectiveness; and 2) assisting in the implementation of the assessment protocol for the statewide afterschool networks. In addition, FowlerHoffman will continue to identify current opportunities for the statewide afterschool networks and make recommendations for how to advance afterschool programs and the networks for the future.

title: Supporting Statewide Afterschool Networks
description: This grant will continue support for FowlerHoffman to provide comprehensive technical assistance to the statewide afterschool networks. Over the next two years, the grantee will focus on: 1) advising and supporting the 50 statewide afterschool networks to increase network sustainability and effectiveness; and 2) assisting in the implementation of the assessment protocol for the statewide afterschool networks. In addition, the grantee will continue to identify current opportunities for the statewide afterschool networks and make recommendations for how to advance afterschool programs and the networks for the future.

title: Supporting Statewide Afterschool Networks
description: This grant will continue support for FowlerHoffman to provide comprehensive technical assistance to the statewide afterschool networks. Over the next year, the grantee will focus on: 1) advising and supporting the 50 statewide afterschool networks to increase network sustainability and effectiveness; 2) assisting in the implementation of the assessment protocol for the statewide afterschool networks; and 3) supporting the implementation of the thematic partnerships and the Mott Afterschool App. In addition, the grantee will continue to identify current opportunities for the statewide afterschool networks and make recommendations for how to advance afterschool programs and the networks for the future.

title: Policy and Messaging Strategies for Afterschool Networks
description: FowlerHoffman will survey existing messaging strategies for afterschool programming, identify current opportunities for the statewide networks, and make recommendations for how to advance afterschool programs and the networks in the future. This project will include a review of policy trends, new research and polling data in order to help develop a long-term vision for the afterschool field, and the statewide networks. In addition, the grantee will work with the Foundation to immediately apply insights and strategies as they are learned to best position afterschool programs and keep the statewide afterschool networks moving forward.

title: RoadMAP Project
description: The Common Counsel Foundation was founded in 1988 to provide support to community-based organizations. This grant will provide support to the grantee’s RoadMAP project, a capacity building program specifically designed for grassroots organizations.

title: Programmatic and Operational Development Support
description: The project goal is to build the capacity of the Ana and Vlade Divac Foundation to stimulate increased corporate and individual philanthropy in Serbia and to be a leading foundation in the country’s emerging philanthropic sector. During the next two years, the grantee will participate in a newly emerging Serbian donors forum, promote the role of philanthropy among individuals and corporations, build its capacity as a grantmaker, and strengthen board and staff capacities. During 2011-2012, the grantee added key staff positions, strengthened management and governance capacities, developed its first strategic plan, and expanded its individual and corporate donor base. The grantee was established in 2007 and carries out a range of development programs targeting youth, refugees, and internally displaced people and is based in Belgrade, Serbia.

title: Programmatic and Operational Development Support
description: The project goal is to build the capacity of the Ana and Vlade Divac Foundation to stimulate increased corporate and individual philanthropy in Serbia and to be a leading foundation in the country’s emerging philanthropic sector. Specifically, during the next two years, the grantee will strengthen leadership and management capacities within the foundation; further engage the board in strategic planning; and develop a long-term sustainability strategy, including the possibility of establishing an endowment. During 2013-2014, the grantee expanded its individual and corporate donor base, developed its grantmaking capacities, worked with an organizational development expert, increased its involvement in the Serbian Philanthropic Forum and other philanthropic networks nationally and regionally, and strengthened its youth empowerment programming. The grantee was established in 2007 and carries out a range of development programs targeting youth, refugees, and internally displaced people. The fund is based in Belgrade, Serbia.

title: Programmatic and Operational Development Support
description: The project goal is to support the Ana and Vlade Divac Fund to build its capacity to stimulate increased corporate and individual philanthropy in Serbia and to be a leading foundation in the country’s emerging philanthropic sector. With Mott support, the grantee will add key staff positions and strengthen management and governance capacities. The grantee was established in 2007 by Vlade Divac, a successful professional basketball player, and his wife, Ana, with their own funds and proceeds from fundraising events connected with Mr. Divac’s retirement from professional basketball in the United States. The grantee has successfully implemented a range of humanitarian programs and raised substantial funding from the corporate sector, private donations, and through innovative fundraising campaigns and techniques. The grantee is based in Belgrade, Serbia.

title: Creating an Audible Legacy
description: The Constitutional Court Trust was established in 1995, and its objective is to promote the rule of law, constitutionalism, and judicial independence in the African region. This grant increase will support the completion of the Audible Legacy project, whose aim is to capture the memories and experiences of the judges of South Africa’ s first Constitutional Court, their successors, and others who were active during the formative years of the court. These records will be collated into an oral history of the court, covering the period from inception to the end of the first period of the court’s existence. The collection will be housed in the Constitutional Court Library and at the University of the Witwatersrand for access via digital catalogue and possible remote access. The materials will be made available to scholars and the general public at no cost.

title: Creating an Audible Legacy
description: The Constitutional Court Trust was established in 1995, and its objective is to promote the rule of law, constitutionalism, and judicial independence in the African region. This grant will support the Audible Legacy project, whose aim is to capture the memories and experiences of the judges of South Africa’s first Constitutional Court. It will also capture the memories of their successors and others who were active during the formative years of the Court while these memories are still relatively fresh. These records will be supplemented with materials from television and radio broadcasting archives, and collated into an oral history of the Court, covering the period from inception to the end of the first period of the Court’s existence. The collection will be housed in the Constitutional Court Library for immediate access via its digital catalogue and possible remote access once available. The materials will be made available to scholars and the general public at no cost.

title: Green and Healthy Homes Initiative
description: This grant supports coordination and administrative oversight of the Flint Green and Healthy Homes Initiative. A collaboration of more than 40 local agencies, this initiative seeks to improve the health, safety, and well-being of low-income children and their families through assessment and remediation of sub-standard housing conditions. The Green and Healthy Homes Initiative is coordinated nationally through the National Coalition to End Childhood Lead Poisoning. The local host for the initiative is Priority Children, a Flint-based child advocacy organization with the mission of improving the quality of life for children and families in Genesee County.

title: Youth Organizing for Education Reform
description: The Institute for Democracy, Education, and Access at the University of California – Los Angeles was launched in 2000 with the goal of using the university’s research capacity and commitment to support community-based organizations working to address critical problems in public education. The purpose of this project is to examine the educational, labor market, and civic trajectories of young adults, ages 18-26, who participated in youth organizing campaigns in California during the last decade. It will compare the survey and interview responses of these young people to the responses of a random sample of more than 2,000 Californians in the same age group.

title: Saginaw Earn & Learn Initiative
description: This grant will enable the county of Saginaw to continue implementing the Earn & Learn Initiative in Saginaw County, targeting disconnected youth (18-24), formerly incarcerated prisoners, and chronically unemployed individuals that want to reenter the workforce. The initiative is designed to spark immediate entry-level work opportunities while simultaneously increasing workers’ skills and helping them manage barriers to success. The grantee will work with local service providers, training and education partners, and employers to implement this initiative. The Mott Foundation’s support for the Earn & Learn Initiative will be matched 1:1 by the Open Society Foundations and the state of Michigan.

title: Saginaw Earn & Learn Initiative
description: This grant will enable the County of Saginaw to implement the Earn & Learn Initiative, targeting up to 90 disconnected youth (18-24), young minority males (including former prisoners reentering the workforce), and chronically unemployed adults in the Saginaw area. The initiative is designed to spark immediate, entry-level work opportunities, while simultaneously increasing workers’ skills and helping them manage barriers to success. The Mott Foundation’s investment in the Earn & Learn Initiative will be matched 1:1 by both the Open Society Institute and the state of Michigan.

title: Philanthropy, Policy and Technology Project
