description: This grant provides partial support for the Philanthropy, Policy and Technology Project, which recognizes that new forces, such as global connectivity, new enterprise forms, new advocacy rules, and market mechanisms as sources for social good, will ultimately require a new policy framework. Three scholarly workshops will be convened that result in the publication of an edited volume of philanthropy and public policy. A series of 10 monthly public symposia will bring together leaders in various relevant fields to inform the scholarly work with practical insights. A visual mapping project will identify the key policy issues and major regulatory and legislative agencies within the main policy domains that affect the social sector. The project will be implemented by Stanford University’s Center on Philanthropy and Civil Society, a research center at a leading university that develops and shares knowledge to improve philanthropy, strengthen civil society, and effect social change.

title: Mexican Community Foundation Development
description: The Inter-American Foundation is managing a development program that focuses on the 17 members of Comunalia, a network of Mexican community foundations. During the past two years, the program has supported the training of a cadre of 40 emerging community foundation leaders, the launch of a challenge grant program requiring local matching, technical assistance for Comunalia members, and a strategic planning process for Comunalia. This grant increase will allow for the further development of the leadership training program, a current assessment of the Mexican community foundation field, and exchanges between Comunalia members and with community foundation practitioners in other countries of the hemisphere. The Inter-American Foundation is an independent United States government agency created by Congress in 1969 to channel development assistance directly to the organized poor in Latin America and the Caribbean.

title: Mexican Community Foundation Development
description: This grant will support the second phase of a seven-year program to develop Mexican community foundations. The Inter-American Foundation manages a program that focuses on the 17 members of Comunalia, a network of Mexican community foundations. During the past four years, the program has supported the training of 40 emerging community foundation leaders, a challenge grant program that leveraged Mexican support for grassroots initiatives at a 3:1 ratio, and institutional strengthening of Comunalia and its members. Over the next three years, the grantee will continue to support the institutional strengthening of Comunalia and its members, a sub-grant challenge mechanism for community projects, and grants for applied research, donor engagement and education, and evaluation. The Inter-American Foundation is an independent United States government agency created by Congress in 1969 to channel development assistance directly to the organized poor in Latin America and the Caribbean.

title: Mexican Community Foundation Development
description: This grant will support the first phase of a six-year program to develop Mexican community foundations. The Inter-American Foundation will manage a program that will focus on members of Comunalia, a recently created network of Mexican community foundations. Over the next three years, the program will develop a trained cadre of 40 emerging community foundation leaders, enhance Comunalia members’ grantmaking capacity for grassroots initiatives through a challenge grant program requiring local matching, strengthen the institutional capacity of Comunalia members through technical assistance, and help consolidate Comunalia as a viable member support organization. The contributions of the Mott and Inter-American foundations, totaling approximately $800,000, are expected to leverage an additional estimated $1.6 million mainly from Mexican national and local sources. The Inter-American Foundation is an independent United States government agency created by Congress in 1969 to provide development assistance directly to the organized poor in Latin America and the Caribbean.

title: Developing the London Community Foundation
description: The program goal is to build the capacity of an important, London-wide community foundation to raise funds from wealthy individuals and the business community. To this end, the Mott Foundation supports salary costs related to the London Community Foundation’s development activities. Due to increased development efforts initiated in 2011, the grantee attracted seven new individual and four new corporate fundholders at a higher level than in the past, increased the amounts of existing individual and corporate fundholders, and attracted 51 new individual donors to its 500 for London initiative. Additionally, the grantee raised its profile during the past year through renaming, rebranding, and launching the foundation in high profile events. In 2012-2013, the grantee will continue to attract new fundholders and donors; improve donor care systems; and build the profile of the organization through events, marketing, and social media.

title: Developing the London Community Foundation
description: The program goal is to build the capacity of a London-wide community foundation to raise funds from wealthy individuals and the business community. To this end, the Mott Foundation supports salary costs related to the London Community Foundation’s development activities. Due to increased development efforts initiated in 2011, the grantee has attracted eight new individual and six new corporate fundholders at a higher level than in the past, increased the amounts of existing individual and corporate fundholders, and attracted 52 new individual donors to its 500 for London initiative. Additionally, the grantee raised its profile during the past year through events, marketing, and social media. In 2013-2014, the grantee will continue to attract new fundholders and donors, improve donor care systems, and build the profile of the organization.

title: Developing the London Community Foundation
description: The program goal is to build the capacity of a Londonwide community foundation to raise funds from wealthy individuals and the business community. To this end, the Mott Foundation supports salary costs related to the London Community Foundation’s development activities. Due to increased development efforts initiated in 2011, the grantee grew its endowment significantly and increased its grantmaking capacity and ability to respond to community needs. Additionally, the grantee raised its profile through events, marketing, and social media. During 2015-2017, the grantee will continue to attract new fundholders and donors, grow its endowment, and build the profile of the organization. The London Community Foundation was created in 1995 as the South East London Community Foundation. In 2005, the grantee changed its name and its area of benefit to the whole of London.

title: Developing the London Community Foundation
description: The program goal is to build the capacity of an important, London-wide community foundation to raise funds from wealthy individuals and the business community. To this end, the Mott Foundation will provide partial support for a development manager position at the Capital Community Foundation. This staff member will play an important role in attracting new fundholders and donors; launching the London Community Foundation; improving donor care systems; and building the profile of the organization through events, marketing, and social media. The grantee’s mission is to improve the communities of London by supporting people’s ideas and initiatives. The grantee was established in 1995 as the South East London Community Foundation. In 2005, the grantee changed its name and its area of benefit to the whole of London.

title: Metropolitan Policy Program
description: Many business leaders and economists are calling for a retooling of the American economy, especially in older, industrial states such as Michigan. The Metropolitan Policy Program at the Brookings Institution, an internationally known think tank, is well-positioned to assist in the development and deployment of such a strategy for economic renewal. With prior support, the grantee helped prepare a metropolitan growth plan for Michigan that was quite well received. With continuing support, the grantee will help implement aspects of the growth strategy in Michigan while undertaking a full range of other work to promote the economic competitiveness of metropolitan areas domestically and globally. This will include original research, policy, tool development, and networking activities.

title: Metropolitan Policy Program
description: Many business leaders and economists are calling for a retooling of the American economy, especially in older, industrial states such as Michigan. The Metropolitan Policy Program at the Brookings Institution, an internationally known think tank, is well-positioned to assist in the development and deployment of such a strategy for economic renewal. With continuing support, the grantee will undertake a range of work to promote the economic competitiveness of metropolitan areas domestically and globally, including older industrial cities such as Flint. Activities will include original research, policy advocacy, analytical tool development, and network building.

title: Michigan's Next Economy
description: The recent recession has led many business leaders and economists to call for a retooling of the American economy, especially in places particularly hard hit like Michigan. The next economy, according to this view, should be driven by the growth of exports, the use of low-carbon energy sources, a reliance on innovation, and the expansion of opportunity for all citizens. The Metropolitan Policy Program of the Brookings Institution, an internationally known think tank, is well-positioned to assist in the development and deployment of such a strategy for economic renewal. Over the next year, the grantee will conduct research, engage in policy work, and develop best practices designed to advance the next economy in Michigan and the Great Lakes region.

title: Institutional Development
description: The program goal is to strengthen private, individual philanthropy in Bulgaria by providing institutional support to one of the first private foundations in Bulgaria, the Dimitar Berbatov Foundation. During the grant period, the grantee will increase its organizational capacity and improve its financial sustainability. Also, the grantee will advocate for a better environment for the development of philanthropy in Bulgaria. In addition, the grantee will develop partnerships with other Bulgarian individual philanthropists to promote philanthropy as a tool for social development. The grantee’s key project achievements in the area of institutional development in the past two years include strengthening the grantee’s human resources, developing working partnerships with public institutions, and diversifying its funding base. The grantee is based in Sofia, Bulgaria.

title: Institutional Development
description: The program goal is to strengthen private, individual philanthropy in Bulgaria by providing institutional support to one of the first private foundations in Bulgaria, the Dimitar Berbatov Foundation. During the grant period, the grantee will recruit and train professional staff, strengthen its board, develop a new strategic program plan, and improve its communication and fundraising strategies. In addition, the grantee will develop partnerships with other Bulgarian individual philanthropists to promote philanthropy as a tool for social development. Also, the grantee will refurbish its offices and provide meeting space and administrative support to individual philanthropists that are considering initiating philanthropic activities or improving their philanthropic practice. The grantee’s key achievements to date include creating funding partnerships with a number of corporate donors in Bulgaria and running successful media campaigns targeting children’s health issues, as well as grantmaking programs focusing on sports and education for children and young people.

title: School of Civic Participation
description: The project goal is to foster citizen participation in local communities in Ukraine. To this end, the Institute of Socio-Cultural Management will train a new cohort of up to 60 community activists as part of its School of Civic Participation, while further enhancing skills of graduates of the first session of the school. Participants will receive ongoing support in pursuing community projects through the grantee’s local activity centers, which will be based within existing community institutions and will serve as focal points for facilitating community-based initiatives. Successful examples of community mobilization in Ukraine will be regularly disseminated through publications, a regional television program, and a dedicated Web site. In 2012-2013, local activity centers were established in 20 communities throughout Ukraine, and a regional television channel dedicated a new program to the work of community activists. Registered in 2001 and based in Kirovohrad, the Institute of Socio-Cultural Management promotes social action, accountability, and citizen participation in public life in Ukraine, with a particular focus on community-level initiatives.

title: School of Civic Participation
description: The project goal is to foster citizen participation in local communities in Ukraine. To this end, the Institute of Socio-Cultural Management will train a new cohort of 40 community activists, or social animators, as part of its School of Civic Participation. In addition, it will conduct a training-of-trainers workshop for 20 graduates of the first two sessions of the school. Participants will receive ongoing technical assistance in pursuing their community development projects. Successful examples of community mobilization in Ukraine will be regularly disseminated through publications and a dedicated Web site. Since 2012, the grantee has trained a total of 102 social animators from 70 local communities, mostly small towns and villages in eastern and southern Ukraine. Registered in 2001 and based in Kirovograd, the Institute of Socio-Cultural Management promotes social action, accountability, and citizen participation in public life in Ukraine, with a particular focus on community-level initiatives.

title: School of Civic Participation
description: The project goal is to foster citizen participation in local communities in Ukraine. The Institute of Socio-Cultural Management will train a new cohort of 40 community leaders, or “social animators,” as part of the School of Civic Participation. In addition, the grantee will conduct a training-of-trainers workshop for 40 graduates of the previous sessions of the school. Participants will receive ongoing technical assistance in pursuing their projects, with newly included material on utilizing social media for community initiatives. Successful examples of community mobilization in Ukraine will be regularly disseminated through publications and a dedicated website. Since 2015, the grantee’s training manual of community development success stories has been downloaded almost 7,000 times. Participants have implemented 251 local initiatives in 45 communities throughout Ukraine. Registered in 2001 and based in Kirovohrad, the grantee promotes social action, accountability, and citizen participation in public life in Ukraine, with a particular focus on community-level initiatives.

title: School of Civic Participation
description: The project goal is to foster citizen participation in local communities in Ukraine aimed at resolving issues of common concern. To this end, the Institute of Socio-Cultural Management will initially train and mentor up to 60 community activists. These activists will constitute the heart of local activity centers, which will be based within existing community institutions and will serve as focal points for facilitating community-based initiatives. Examples of best practices on community mobilization in Ukraine will subsequently be disseminated through the publication of relevant handbooks and through a dedicated Web site. The experience of community animators and highlights of projects conducted within the program will form the centerpiece of a final conference. Registered in 2001 and based in Kirovohrad, the Institute of Socio-Cultural Management promotes social action, accountability, and citizen participation in public life in Ukraine, with a particular focus on community-level initiatives.

title: Texas Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the United Ways of Texas which coordinates the Texas Statewide Afterschool Network. The Texas Statewide Afterschool Network will focus on building capacity for long-term success and advancing systemic change for afterschool and expanded learning in Texas. Over the next three years, the network will support the development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool and expanded learning programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) developing a Quality Improvement System for out-of-school time programs; 2) working to secure a state-level funding stream for afterschool programs; and 3) building the capacity of programs through partnerships with funders, regional networks, and education policy leaders.

title: Texas Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: Texas Partnership for Out of School Time
description: This grant will support the Texas Partnership for Out of School Time which coordinates the Texas Statewide Afterschool Network to continue development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) increasing communications activities to build public awareness about the importance of afterschool; 2) developing a comprehensive plan to increase resources for afterschool programs; and 3) provide support necessary for out-of-school time programs to assist in the adoption of quality standards.

title: Texas Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the United Ways of Texas to coordinate the new Texas Statewide Afterschool Network in Texas. The network will work to create an afterschool system, and as a new network, will work to increase high quality afterschool opportunities in the state. The network will bring together youth-serving organizations, state agencies, and other key stakeholders, and will complete a statewide mapping study of afterschool services and needs. To ensure that new models and best practices are incorporated nationally, the network will share lessons learned and products with the other statewide afterschool networks.

title: State Children's Savings Account Assessment
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: Engage Strategies prepared 15 high quality, comprehensive state assessment reports that provided the Foundation and its grantees with strategic information about the opportunity and challenges for promoting children’s savings accounts across the country. The reports answer questions such as: How can this strategy best be framed to garner support? Who are the most effective spokespersons? and, most importantly, How might Mott Foundation support leverage change? This grant increase and extension will enable the grantee to expand their analysis to include up to 15 additional states. This additional information will help the Foundation identify high impact grantmaking opportunities and help our grantees and other stakeholders shape their advocacy strategies and identify critical partners necessary to achieve results. Based in South Carolina, Engage Strategies is a for-profit consulting firm that provides strategic guidance and analytical services to foundations, businesses, and nonprofit organizations.

title: State Children's Savings Account Assessment
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant will enable Engage Strategies to prepare comprehensive state reports that provide strategic information about the opportunities and challenges for promoting children’s savings accounts in various states. The reports will answer questions such as: How can this strategy best be framed to garner support? Who are the most effective spokespersons? and, most importantly, Would a Mott investment leverage change? These assessments will not only help the Foundation target high impact investments but will also help grantees shape their advocacy strategies and identify critical partners necessary to achieve results. Based in South Carolina, Engage Strategies is a for-profit consulting firm that provides strategic guidance and analysis services to foundations, businesses, and nonprofit organizations.

title: BASIC South Initiative
description: Given the growing importance of emerging market countries, such as Brazil and China, in the global financial system, there is a need for civil society in these countries to play a greater role in shaping international development policies. This project is an effort to develop a network of nongovernmental organizations from emerging market countries. This new network will address financing for renewable and low-carbon energy for the poor in developing countries as well as undertaking related actions to address climate change. This grant increase will support a meeting with NGO representatives from the key emerging market economies to finalize a long-term vision and five to ten-year work plan for the network.

title: BASIC South Initiative
description: The BASIC South Initiative project is an effort to develop a network of nongovernmental organizations from emerging economies, like Brazil and China. This new network will address financing for renewable and low-carbon energy in developing countries, as well as broad sustainable development goals that emerging economies might promote. This grant increase to South Africa Development Fund will support civil society organization meetings parallel to the BRICS Summit to be held in Durban, South Africa.

title: BASIC South Initiative
description: Emerging market countries have become a strong political block in international political and economic discussions, particularly on climate and energy policies. While the United States and Europe continue to have a strong and powerful voice within international finance institutions and the United Nations, an era has begun in which the interests of emerging market economies are clearly playing a critical role. With this changing global power dynamic, there is a need for civil society in these countries also to play a greater role in shaping international policies. This project of the South Africa Development Fund is an exploratory effort to bring together the environment and development nongovernmental organizations in emerging market countries to capitalize on their strength and diversity. This new network will address financing for renewable and low-carbon energy for the poor in developing countries, as well as undertaking related actions to address climate change. During its first year, the project will focus on establishment of the network, strategic engagement on the international financial institution’s energy strategies and lending policies, and participation in key United Nations’ meetings.

title: Philanthropy Infrastructure Development in Turkey
description: The project goal is to strengthen the infrastructure for philanthropy in Turkey. To this end, the Third Sector Foundation of Turkey will provide training, technical assistance, networking opportunities, and knowledge resources to individuals, foundations, and corporations in Turkey who are interested in improving their philanthropic practices. The grantee will also further develop community philanthropy in Turkey by continuing to champion the community foundation model and introducing new mechanisms for local giving. During the grant period, the grantee will increase its organizational and programmatic capacities to provide philanthropy and community foundation support services to the broader field in Turkey. Over the last two years, the grantee published guides to giving for individuals, foundations, and corporations; raised awareness about community foundations; prepared a case study on Turkey’s only community foundation; and conducted a feasibility study on community foundation development in Turkey. Based in Istanbul, the Third Sector Foundation of Turkey was established in 1993 by Turkey’s leading associations and foundations and is a vital support network and resource center for its more than 100-member associations and foundations, as well as the sector in general.

title: Philanthropy Infrastructure Development in Turkey
description: The project goal is to strengthen the infrastructure for philanthropy in Turkey. This grant increase will allow the grantee to respond to a new opportunity to assist in the development of a local grantmaking organization. This work will complement the project’s core objectives by strengthening international and local philanthropy directed to rights-based nonprofits. Also, through this additional work, the grantee will increase its organizational and programmatic capacities to provide support services to Turkey’s growing philanthropic sector. Based in Istanbul, the grantee was established in 1993 by Turkey’s leading associations and foundations and today is a vital support network and resource center for its more than 100-member associations and foundations as well as the sector in general.

title: Philanthropy Infrastructure Development in Turkey
description: The project goal is to strengthen the culture of giving and the infrastructure for philanthropy in Turkey. To this end, the Third Sector Foundation of Turkey will provide training, technical assistance, networking opportunities, and knowledge resources to individuals, foundations, and corporations in Turkey who are interested in improving their philanthropic practices. The grantee will also further develop community philanthropy in Turkey by continuing to champion the community foundation model and introducing new mechanisms for local giving. During 2013-2015, the grantee organized peer-learning and skill-building events for individuals and families, foundations, companies, and local civic initiatives to build the capacity for more strategic philanthropy. The grantee also collected and published inspiring stories of individual philanthropy, piloted two giving circle events, and explored opportunities for community philanthropy in Turkey. Established in 1993, the grantee is a resource center for its more than 100 member associations and foundations, as well as the sector in general.

title: Philanthropy Infrastructure Development in Turkey
description: The project goal is to strengthen the culture of giving and the infrastructure for philanthropy in Turkey. To this end, the Third Sector Foundation of Turkey will provide training, technical assistance, networking opportunities, and knowledge resources to individuals, foundations, and corporations in Turkey who are interested in improving their philanthropic practices. The grantee will also organize a national-level conference on philanthropy. During 2015–2017, the grantee organized peer-learning and skill-building events for individuals and families, foundations, companies, and local civic initiatives to build the capacity for more strategic philanthropy; raised awareness of the importance of philanthropy and trends in strategic giving; and collected and published inspiring stories of individual philanthropy. Established in 1993, the grantee is a resource center for its more than 100 member associations and foundations, as well as the sector in general.

title: Philanthropy Infrastructure Development in Turkey
description: The project goal is to strengthen the infrastructure for philanthropy in Turkey. To this end, the Third Sector Foundation of Turkey will: 1) develop a long-term strategy for strengthening philanthropy in Turkey; 2) update its research and resources on philanthropy in Turkey and raise awareness of the importance of philanthropy; and 3) promote and adapt the community foundation model in Turkey. During the grant period, the grantee will also increase its organizational and programmatic capacities to provide philanthropy and community foundation support services to the broader field in Turkey. Based in Istanbul, the Third Sector Foundation of Turkey was established in 1993 by Turkey’s leading associations and foundations and today is a vital support network and resource center for its more than 100 member associations and foundations, as well as the sector in general.

title: TechWorks
description: This grant will provide funds to Kettering University for the TechWorks program, Kettering’s technology business accelerator. TechWorks contributes to the economic development of Flint and the surrounding region by providing services and facilities dedicated to helping technology entrepreneurs grow their companies while they perfect the application of the underlying technology.

title: Saginaw Earn & Learn Initiative - Regranting Partnership with Open Society Foundations
description: This grant will enable the County of Saginaw to continue implementing the Saginaw Earn & Learn Initiative, targeting disconnected youth (18-24), formerly incarcerated prisoners, and chronically unemployed individuals who want to reenter the workforce. The initiative is designed to spark immediate entry-level work opportunities while simultaneously increasing workers’ skills and helping them manage barriers to success. The county will work with local service providers, training and education partners, and employers to implement this initiative. The Open Society Foundations’ (formerly Open Society Institute) support for the Saginaw Earn & Learn Initiative will be matched by the Mott Foundation and the state of Michigan.

title: Saginaw Earn & Learn Initiative - Regranting Partnership with Open Society Foundations
description: This grant will enable the County of Saginaw to implement the Earn & Learn Initiative in Saginaw County, targeting 80 disconnected youth (18-24), young minority males (including former prisoners re-entering the workforce), and chronically unemployed adults that want to re-enter the workforce. The initiative is designed to spark immediate, entry-level work opportunities while simultaneously increasing workers’ skills and helping them manage barriers to success. The grantee will collaborate with its higher education partner — Delta College — to provide customized education and training activities that meet the needs of local employers. The Open Society Foundations’ (formerly Open Society Institute) investment in the Earn & Learn Initiative will be matched 1:1 by both the Mott Foundation and the state of Michigan.

title: Nonprofits Integrating Community Engagement (NICE)
description: The Nonprofits Integrating Community Engagement project will help nonprofits learn to build civic capacity by partnering with the communities they serve and where they work. To this end, the Alliance for Nonprofit Management will partner with the Building Movement Project to develop state-of-the-art materials, tools, case examples, and training modules. The grantee will also create venues to distribute the resultant resources to support organizations and communities that embrace this approach. The Building Movement Project is an initiative that encourages nonprofit service providers to enhance civic engagement and social change, promote the common good, and address generational shifts in leadership. The Alliance for Nonprofit Management, a membership association that delivers management and governance support services to nonprofit organizations, will manage the Nonprofits Integrating Community Engagement project. This project builds on past Mott support to the Building Movement Project, which developed a methodology for how service providers can support resident engagement.

title: Nonprofits Integrating Community Engagement (NICE)
description: The program goal is to help nonprofits learn to build civic capacity by partnering with the communities they serve and where they work. In 2014, the Alliance for Nonprofit Management and the Building Movement Project launched the Nonprofits Integrating Community Engagement project to increase constituent voice as a core practice of nonprofit service delivery. The partners introduced the project to their constituencies, created an advisory committee, and created a training curriculum. Over the next year, they will implement this curriculum, establish a nonprofit consultant affinity group, and broadly disseminate what the project has to offer. The Building Movement Project is an initiative that encourages nonprofit service providers to enhance civic engagement and social change, promote the common good, and address generational shifts in leadership. The Alliance for Nonprofit Management, a membership association that delivers management and governance support services to nonprofit organizations, will manage the Nonprofits Integrating Community Engagement project.

title: Nonprofits Integrating Community Engagement (NICE)
description: In 2012, the Building Movement Project began developing resource materials to help nonprofits in the United States build civic capacity by partnering with the communities they serve and where they work. In 2014, along with the Alliance for Nonprofit Management, the grantee launched the Nonprofits Integrating Community Engagement project. As a result, a full training curriculum guide was developed, a nonprofit consultant affinity group was established, and the nonprofit consultant field was informed of the project’s offerings. Over the next two years, the project’s implementers will conduct outreach, disseminate the guide, advise practitioners on its use, and evaluate the project. The Nonprofits Integrating Community Engagement project is an initiative that encourages nonprofit service providers to enhance civic engagement and social change, promote the common good, and address generational shifts in leadership. Third Sector New England, a provider of nonprofit capacity building, leadership, and management service to nonprofit organizations, will manage the Nonprofits Integrating Community Engagement project.

title: Building Civic Capacity by Nonprofit Service Organizations
grantee: Demos: A Network for Ideas and Action
description: The Building Civic Capacity by Nonprofit Service Organizations project will teach domestic nonprofits how to build civic capacity by partnering with the communities in which they serve and work. To this end, the grantee will document current methods and develop state-of-the-art materials, tools, case examples, and training modules. The grantee will also create viable venues to distribute the information and tools to support organizations and communities that are embracing this approach. The project will be implemented by the building movement project, an initiative that encourages nonprofit service providers to enhance civic engagement and social change, promote the common good, and address generational shifts in leadership. The building movement project is managed by Demos: A Network for Ideas and Action, a national, nonpartisan, multi-issue think tank that combines research, policy development, and advocacy to influence public debate and catalyze change.

title: Communicating About Expanded Learning Time
description: This grant will support FrameWorks Institute, a nonprofit think tank that creates communications strategies to impact social problems, conduct research, and develop a communications strategy aimed at impacting the public’s perception of education and expanded learning time. The project is also being supported by a funding collaborative that includes the Nellie Mae Education Foundation, the Ford Foundation, the William and Flora Hewlett Foundation, and the NoVo Foundation. In addition to conducting communications research that will support afterschool programs, this project will support the Foundation in building relationships with other funders who are making significant investments in education, expanded learning time, and school reform.

title: Opportunity to Learn - Midwest
description: The national Opportunity to Learn Campaign is an effort to build public will for education reforms that support opportunities for all children to learn and succeed, especially children in low-income communities. Opportunity to Learn integrates grassroots organizing, policy advocacy, and research to promote support for the resources needed to provide a fair and substantive opportunity to learn. This grant will provide partial support to the Institute for Wisconsin’s Future to lead the effort to establish an Opportunity to Learn campaign in the Midwest.

title: Opportunity to Learn - Midwest
description: The national Opportunity to Learn Campaign is an effort to build public will for education reforms that support opportunities for all children to learn and succeed, especially children in low-income communities. Opportunity to Learn integrates grassroots organizing, policy advocacy, and research to promote support for the resources needed to provide a fair and substantive opportunity to learn. This grant will provide partial support to the Institute for Wisconsin’s Future to lead the effort to establish an Opportunity to Learn campaign in the Midwest.

title: Building Organizing Capacity in Louisiana
description: One Voice is a policy research and training organization. Its mission is to provide training and technical assistance to community-based organizations on issues such as access to and use of data, social and political network mapping, issue research, data and issue analysis, and understanding the public sector. This grant will provide partial support for a project to build the capacity of nonprofit organizations in Louisiana with a focus on community organizing groups.

title: Poverty Initiative
grantee: Union Theological Seminary in the City of New York
description: Union Theological Seminary in the City of New York founded the Poverty Initiative in 2004 as an effort to bridge gaps between community organizations, religious communities, and the academy with the goal of better understanding and addressing the causes of poverty in the United States by developing leaders to work on issues in low-income communities. This grant provides partial support for the year-long training program.

title: Civic Engagement Academy
grantee: MOSES Metropolitan Organizing Strategy Enabling Strength
description: MOSES Metropolitan Organizing Strategy Enabling Strength is a Gamaliel-affiliated community organizing group working in metropolitan Detroit. The current membership consists of 38 congregations and 15 other member institutions (including schools, service providers, and civic organizations). This grant provides partial support for a civic leadership training program being offered to the community.

title: Building Capacity in Southwestern Michigan
description: The Michigan Organizing Project was founded in Muskegon in 1991 as an institution-based community organizing group. The organization later expanded to Grand Rapids and Kalamazoo and subsequently developed chapters in small- and medium-sized cities in west and southwest Michigan. This grant will provide partial support for the capacity building and leadership transition activities as the organization prepares for staff transition.

title: General Purposes
description: PICO United Florida is part of the PICO National Network. The mission of the grantee is to build a network of congregation-based community organizations that train local leaders to analyze and address issues of concern to local communities. More than 200 congregations representing ten different religious denominations and faith traditions are part of the grantee’s network. This grant will support the general purposes of the organization, including leadership training, research, and consultation with local PICO affiliates.

title: PICO - Florida
description: PICO National Network is a community organizing network with local affiliates in 17 states and in Central America and East Africa. This grant will provide partial support to the organization’s effort to provide training, consulting, technical assistance, and research to build a statewide community organizing initiative in Florida.

title: Protecting Healthy River Flows for Georgia
description: A number of factors has put the health of Georgia’s rivers at risk, including growing water demands throughout the state and the Atlanta metro area in particular. The Georgia River Network, a statewide organization serving the needs of Georgia’s river groups, will participate in, and lead efforts to, positively influence the outcome of water management policy discussions at the metro, state, and interstate levels. This will include leadership roles in two coalitions working on such issues, one at the state level and the other at the interstate level. The grantee will promote water conservation and water use efficiency as a fiscally prudent and environmentally sustainable way to address the state’s water supply needs.

title: Protecting Healthy River Flows for Georgia
description: Georgia ranks third in the nation for aquatic biodiversity, and the state’s waterways provide a range of other social benefits from recreation to drinking water. At the same time, a number of factors threaten the health of Georgia’s rivers, including the growing water demands throughout the state, and particularly Atlanta, the region’s largest metro area. The Georgia River Network, a statewide organization serving the needs of Georgia’s river groups, will participate in and lead efforts to positively influence the outcome of water management policy discussions at the metro, state, and interstate levels. This will include leadership roles in two coalitions working on such issues, one at the state level and the other at the interstate level.

title: Enhancing Transportation Equity in Michigan
description: The Governor’s Council on Physical Fitness, Health and Sports seeks to improve the health of Michigan residents. A nonprofit organization, the Michigan Fitness Foundation, was created to implement the council’s mission. The foundation seeks to inform policies and programs that promote healthy livable communities, schools, and neighborhoods throughout Michigan, with an emphasis in low-income, urban communities. In accordance with its mission, the grantee helped lead initiatives to modernize Michigan’s transportation systems. With prior Mott support, the grantee provided technical assistance to a statewide collaborative seeking to address the transportation needs of all Michigan residents, including the full spectrum of ages, physical abilities, socioeconomic levels, and racial/ethnic backgrounds. With renewed support, the grantee will continue assisting its partners by providing trainings, convenings, and small grants to build the capacity of the statewide collaborative and its members, broaden pubic engagement, and support important, community-level transportation projects.

title: Enhancing Transportation Equity in Michigan
description: The Governor’s Council on Physical Fitness, Health, and Sports seeks to improve the health of Michigan residents. A nonprofit organization, the Michigan Fitness Foundation was created to implement the council’s mission. The grantee works to inform policies and programs that promote healthy and livable communities, schools, and neighborhoods throughout Michigan, with an emphasis on low-income, urban communities. In accordance with its mission, the grantee has helped lead initiatives to modernize Michigan’s transportation systems. This grant will allow the grantee to help a statewide transportation collaborative understand and address the transportation needs of all Michigan residents, including the full spectrum of ages, physical abilities, socioeconomic levels, and racial/ethnic backgrounds. As part of this effort, the grantee will provide minigrants to encourage the engagement of leaders from diverse communities and support important, community-level transportation projects.

title: Integrating Transportation, Health, and Community Placemaking
description: Established in 1945, the Michigan Association of Planning is dedicated to promoting sound comprehensive community planning that benefits the residents of Michigan and includes opportunities for a variety of housing, employment, and commercial activities, as well as cultural and recreational amenities. This renewal grant will allow the organization to continue developing and strengthening its efforts to promote model programs and approaches that intentionally integrate innovative transportation applications with the practices of healthy urban design and placemaking, with a particular interest in promoting social equity and related messaging and communications. This renewal project will include: 1) developing and sharing a common language for discussing health and equity within communities, particularly when working within transportation; 2) enhancing the use of new and different techniques for inclusive outreach and engagement during planning processes; and 3) elevating the understanding and value of incorporating health, inclusion, and fairness into planning and transportation processes among planners.

title: Integrating Transportation, Health, and Community Placemaking
description: Established in 1945, the Michigan Association of Planning is dedicated to promoting sound comprehensive community planning that benefits the residents of Michigan and includes opportunities for a variety of lifestyles and housing, employment, commercial activities, and cultural and recreational amenities. This grant will support the organization’s work to develop and disseminate a comprehensive model program that intentionally integrates innovative transportation applications, including complete streets, with the practices of healthy urban design and placemaking. This will include: 1) selecting a community, or a cluster of adjacent communities, to serve as a project pilot site; 2) conducting site analysis and asset mapping; 3) hosting workshops and clinics to develop a set of recommendations for changes to plans and ordinances; 4) applying the model process in up to two additional communities; and 5) producing a handbook to encourage replication in other communities.

title: Water Quality Project
geographic_focus: Indiana, Minnesota, Michigan, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Ontario, Illinois, New York, Wisconsin
description: The Great Lakes Environmental Law Center is a not-for-profit, public interest, environmental organization established in 2008 to protect the Great Lakes and the communities that depend on them. With prior Mott support, the grantee partnered with freshwater groups and citizens to maintain and improve Great Lakes water quality protections related to toxins, nonpoint source pollution, invasive species, and other sources of contamination. The grantee also engaged in regional collaborations to ensure that each Great Lakes state meets the requirements set by the Great Lakes-St. Lawrence River Basin Water Resources Compact. With renewed support, the grantee will continue this work, paying particular attention to opportunities to collaborate with local groups in southeastern Michigan to increase local engagement in high priority Great Lakes efforts.

title: Water Quality Project
geographic_focus: Indiana, Minnesota, New York, Illinois, Wisconsin, Pennsylvania, Michigan, Ontario, Ohio
description: The Great Lakes Environmental Law Center was established in 2008 as a not-for-profit environmental organization with a mission to protect the Great Lakes ecosystem. With prior support, the grantee helped prevent pollution and maintain water levels in Great Lakes waterways by evaluating permit applications; analyzing water quality policies; and working with state agencies to ensure proper implementation of freshwater programs. With renewed support, the grantee will continue this work and also partner with citizens groups in southeastern Michigan to increase local engagement on high priority Great Lakes’ efforts.

title: Water Quality Project
geographic_focus: Indiana, Minnesota, Michigan, Ohio, Illinois, Pennsylvania, Ontario, Wisconsin, New York
description: The Great Lakes Environmental Law Center is a not-for-profit, public interest, environmental organization established in 2008 to protect the Great Lakes and the communities that depend upon them. With this grant, the grantee will work with freshwater groups and citizens to maintain and improve Great Lakes water quality protections related to toxics, nonpoint source pollution, invasive species, and other sources of contamination. The grantee will also help ensure that each Great Lakes state meets the requirements set by the Great Lakes-St. Lawrence River Basin Water Resources Compact.

title: Greenovation Hub
description: This project has helped to foster civil society discussions with Chinese national development banks and other financial institutions to address its investments in developing countries outside China. This project also will help to foster dialogue and collaboration among nongovernmental organizations in developing countries, especially with South American organizations, to address energy and infrastructure investments in the region. Forward Works is a Chinese nonprofit organization formed in 2011 to assist in the development of Chinese environmental, nongovernmental organizations and enhance their capacity by providing training and strategic planning.

title: Monitoring Chinese Development Finance and Global Climate Policy
grantee: Beijing Greenovation Forwards Culture Communication Co. Ltd.
description: The newly established Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank and the New Development Bank could provide important financing for the vast infrastructure needs of developing countries. However, this financing will only be beneficial if those investments benefit local communities and do not negatively impact the environment. As a new actor in development finance, China can learn from the decades of experience of the existing international financial institutions, as well as establish new international standards for development finance lending and build environmental and social safeguards. This grant to Greenovation Hub will provide continued support for Chinese nongovernmental organizations to engage with the Chinese government on the need to shift Chinese investments to low-carbon green infrastructure and to account for environmental and social impacts.

title: Greenovation Hub
description: Forward Works is a Chinese nonprofit organization formed in 2011 to assist in the development of Chinese environmental nongovernmental organizations and enhance their capacity by providing training and strategic planning. Through this project, innovative initiatives will be developed to help foster civil society discussions in China to address its investments to developing countries, funded and guaranteed by Chinese national development banks, particularly related to energy and infrastructure projects. This project will also help to foster dialogue and collaboration among nongovernmental organizations in developing countries, especially with Brazil, India, and South Africa, on issues related to sustainable energy access for the poor.

title: Saginaw Bay Watershed Initiative Network
description: The Saginaw Bay drainage basin is home to more than 1.4 million residents in 22 Michigan counties. This freshwater system is compromised by pollution and habitat degradation. The Saginaw Bay Watershed Initiative Network was launched in 1996 to improve waterway health while strengthening surrounding communities. The project is operated by the Conservation Fund, a national organization that seeks to jointly promote conservation and economic development. The grantee’s Michigan office, located in Bay City, oversees the network to help promote economic, environmental, and social sustainability in the Saginaw Bay area. With prior Mott support, the grantee increased the number of regrants made for local projects and also provided technical assistance and opportunities for public engagement. With renewed support, the grantee will continue this work and will also undertake strategic planning and evaluation activities.

title: Saginaw Bay Watershed Initiative Network
description: Founded in 1985, the Conservation Fund is a national organization that promotes conservation and sustainable economic development. The grantee’s Michigan office oversees the Saginaw Bay Watershed Initiative Network, which seeks to advance economic, environmental, and social sustainability in the Saginaw Bay area. With prior Mott support, the network maintained its regrants program, provided technical assistance and opportunities for public engagement, and completed strategic planning and evaluation activities. With renewed support, the grantee will continue this work, analyze septic waste policies in the Saginaw Bay region, and host community meetings to help its programs address the needs of all residents in the watershed.

title: Saginaw Bay Watershed Initiative Network
description: Founded in 1985, The Conservation Fund is a national organization that promotes conservation and sustainable economic development. The grantee’s Michigan office oversees the Saginaw Bay Watershed Initiative Network, which seeks to advance economic, environmental, and social sustainability in the Saginaw Bay area. With this grant, the grantee will continue leveraging funds to develop conservation and recreation projects, complete an analysis of septic pollution, and address access to communities of diverse populations in the Saginaw Bay basin.

title: Saginaw Bay Watershed Initiative Network
description: Saginaw Bay’s network of rivers, lakes, and streams form Michigan’s largest drainage system. These waterways collect water runoff from about 15 percent of the state’s total land area and channel it into Lake Huron. The ecosystem filters many sediments and toxins from water, but it cannot keep up with the heavy pollution load coming from such a large surface area. Habitat destruction and other threats also reduce the system’s ability to control floods, support wildlife, and provide additional economic and recreational resources. The Saginaw Bay Watershed Initiative Network was launched in 1996 to improve waterway health while strengthening surrounding communities. The initiative is run by the Bay Area Community Foundation which seeks to encourage philanthropy in the Saginaw Bay area. Over the next two years, Mott support will allow the grantee to increase regranting for local projects that benefit the Saginaw Bay ecosystem and achieve social and economic goals.

title: Center on Nonprofits and Philanthropy
description: This grant provides operating support to the Urban Institute’s Center on Nonprofits and Philanthropy. The center seeks to improve understanding of civil society and nonprofit sector performance by conducting rigorous research and analysis, developing data, and promoting dialogue on policy issues affecting nonprofits and philanthropy. Core activities of the center include: updating, expanding, and providing access to the center’s National Nonprofit Data System; supporting efforts to improve government data on nonprofits; and conducting research, convenings, and publishing to inform public policy and practice on nonprofits and philanthropy. Research areas over the past grant period included nonprofit-government contracts and grants, donor-advised funds, and nonprofit data and transparency. The Urban Institute is an independent think tank that gathers data, conducts research, evaluates programs, offers technical assistance overseas, and educates Americans on social and economic issues to foster sound public policy and effective government.

title: Center on Nonprofits and Philanthropy
description: This grant will provide support to the Urban Institute’s Center on Nonprofits and Philanthropy. The center seeks to improve understanding of civil society and nonprofit sector performance by conducting rigorous research and analysis, developing data, and promoting dialogue on policy issues affecting nonprofits and philanthropy. This grant will support core activities of the center such as: updating, expanding, and providing access to the center’s National Nonprofit Data System; developing additional sites for the center’s community database platforms; supporting efforts to improve government data on nonprofits; developing trend data on the nonprofit sector; improving nonprofit data standards and methods; and enhancing the center’s communications via social media and Webinars. The Urban Institute is an independent think tank that gathers data, conducts research, evaluates programs, offers technical assistance overseas, and educates Americans on social and economic issues to foster sound public policy and effective government.

title: Jobs for America's Graduates
description: This grant will enable Career Alliance, Inc., to continue the Jobs for America’s Graduates program at two Flint-area high schools. In 2011, the grantee piloted this national school-to-work program model at Flint Northern and Northwestern high schools as a targeted dropout prevention program for students who are most at-risk of dropping out of school. In the pilot year, more than 80 students were provided a series of year-round classroom and work-based learning experiences from academic and counseling supports to skills training and summer employment. Recommended support will allow Career Alliance, Inc., to strengthen and expand the Jobs for America’s Graduates program at these two high schools.

title: Jobs for America's Graduates
description: This grant will enable Career Alliance, Inc., to continue the Jobs for America’s Graduates program at two Flint area high schools. The program is the nation’s largest school-to-work model aimed at preventing dropouts among young people who are most at risk. In 2012, the grantee provided 130 students from Flint Northern and Northwestern high schools with a series of year-round classroom and work-based learning experiences such as academic and counseling supports, skills training, and summer employment. Recommended support will allow Career Alliance, Inc., to strengthen and expand the Jobs for America’s Graduates program at Flint Southwestern and Northwestern high schools.

title: Jobs for America's Graduates
description: This grant will enable Genesee/Shiawassee Michigan Works! to pilot the Jobs for America’s Graduates program model at Flint Southwestern and Northwestern high schools. The program is a national school-to-work initiative aimed at assisting students who are most at-risk of dropping out of school. Recommended support will allow the grantee to provide students at these schools with classroom and work-based learning experiences that result in a high school credential, postsecondary study, and further training that leads to a career.

title: Jobs for America's Graduates
description: This grant will enable Career Alliance, Inc., to pilot the Jobs for America’s Graduates program model at Flint Northern and Northwestern high schools. The program is a national school-to-work initiative aimed at assisting students who are most at-risk of dropping out of school. Recommended support will allow the grantee to provide students at these schools with classroom and work-based learning experiences that result in a high school credential, postsecondary study, and further training that leads to a career.

title: Building New Workforce and Community College Pathways in the Dental Industry
description: This grant will continue to support Pew Charitable Trusts to assist community college administrators and state workforce development officials in developing a roadmap for training new and emerging types of dental providers at community colleges and/or other nontraditional settings. In the most recent phase of this project, the grantee formed an advisory group of community college and workforce development stakeholders and produced a report on the need for new dental providers and the role community colleges can play in developing and training them. Recommended support will enable the grantee to develop and advance a communications plan/strategy and provide technical assistance to states that are uniquely positioned to establish new dental provider models.

title: Building New Workforce and Community College Pathways in the Dental Industry
description: This grant will enable the Pew Charitable Trusts to inform and work with community college administrators and state workforce development officials to develop a roadmap for training new and emerging types of primary care dental providers at the nation’s community colleges or other nontraditional settings. The United States is experiencing a perfect storm in the dental health industry due to an aging workforce and projections of limited growth in the future supply of dental providers. The goal of this project is to generate a high level of interest in developing partnerships with community colleges and workforce development leaders to develop new middle-skill employment pathways for high school graduates and others in the dental health industry that pay family sustaining wages and do not require a four-year degree.

title: General Purposes
description: The Genesee Health Plan provides basic health services to about 26,000 uninsured adults in Genesee County who do not have health insurance and do not qualify for Medicare and Medicaid. The grantee is the only local health plan in Michigan funded directly by the community through a special millage. With general purpose support, the grantee will continue to help many local residents receive healthcare services.

title: Eleanor M. Josaitis Fund for Focus: HOPE
description: The Eleanor M. Josaitis Fund for Focus: HOPE recognizes the extraordinary commitment that Eleanor Josaitis made to the Detroit community. The fund will make a lasting contribution to the work of Focus: HOPE. The fund will support donor-designated Focus: HOPE programs and can be either expendable or endowed. The goal of the fund is to raise $10 million.

title: Master Plan for a Sustainable Flint
description: This renewal grant supports the creation of a master plan and its early implementation stages for the city of Flint. A master plan will advance a new vision for a sustainable future for the city and will serve to coordinate investments in the city’s redevelopment. The planning process is led by the city’s planning department in conjunction with a professional consulting team and involves extensive public input. The grant will cover expenses for finishing the master planning document, as well as the creation of a revised zoning code and a municipal capital improvement plan.

title: Master Plan for a Sustainable Flint
description: This grant will leverage funding from the Department of Housing and Urban Development to support the creation of a master plan for the City of Flint. The master planning process offers the city and its people an opportunity to collectively chart a future direction for Flint and, through the resulting plan, coordinate communication and decisionmaking around land use, economic development, and private and public investments. The process will also help the city assess and align its organizational and other resources in order to promote the efficiency and effectiveness of public and private development. The grant will build the capacity of the city’s planning function by supporting planning staff, and will help the city engage outside planning expertise.

title: SeeYourImpact Pilot
description: The SeeYourImpact.org model for charitable giving educates the general public using social media tools about major areas of need and enables individual donors to give small gifts ($25-$200) to people through trusted organizations. This grant will allow SeeYourImpact.org to evaluate their model for domestic charities by running and evaluating fundraising campaigns for five to six foundation grantees or their related, locally based affiliates. The grantee will test the effectiveness and efficiency of its technology platform for acquiring, managing, and maintaining small donors. This bottom of the pyramid funding strategy could add significant revenue streams for local, community-oriented nonprofits delivering critical social services at a time when traditional funding sources are stretched thin. A portion of the funds will be used to test the efficacy of a challenge grant competition for leveraging individual small donors.

title: Michigan State Parks and Outdoor Recreation Panel
description: Michigan’s parks system preserves, protects, and showcases the state’s vast and outstanding natural resources and promotes related outdoor recreation opportunities. Michigan United Conservation Clubs, a statewide conservation group, seeks to maintain and improve these resources as a part of Michigan’s outdoor heritage. With previous Mott support, the grantee facilitated the work of Michigan’s Blue Ribbon Panel on State Parks and Outdoor Recreation. The panel’s report outlined a forward-thinking vision for Michigan parks and provided recommendations for state and county parks’ long-term success and sustainability. With renewed support, the Michigan United Conservation Clubs will help implement key recommendations by: 1) conducting program planning for a statewide initiative to engage citizens and organizations interested in natural resource protections; and 2) facilitating public participation in Michigan’s Public Land Management Plan.

title: Michigan State Parks and Outdoor Recreation Panel
description: Michigan United Conservation Clubs, a statewide conservation group, seeks to protect and restore Michigan’s vast array of natural resources. With previous Mott support, the grantee facilitated the work for Michigan’s Blue Ribbon Panel on State Parks and Outdoor Recreation and the state’s public land management plan. This grant increase will enable the grantee to build on this work by obtaining regional citizen input into development of Michigan’s new water strategy plan.

title: Michigan Land and Water Policy Project
description: Michigan United Conservation Clubs, a statewide conservation group, seeks to protect and restore Michigan’s vast array of natural resources. The grantee has developed expertise in helping facilitate public engagement in state planning processes, such as the development of Michigan’s Blue Ribbon Panel on State Parks and Outdoor Recreation and the state’s public land management plan. With previous Mott support, the grantee helped coordinate citizen input into the development of Michigan’s new water strategy plan and also began a project to assess opportunities for improving statewide collaboration and public engagement on high priority water and land conservation issues. With this renewal, the grantee will focus on improving the health of rivers in Michigan. The grantee will also facilitate coalition efforts to help improve how hydroelectric facilities impact river flows.

title: Michigan Land and Water Policy Project
description: Michigan United Conservation Clubs is the largest statewide conservation organization in the nation. Its membership includes over 40,000 hunters, anglers, trappers, and conservationists. With previous support, the grantee facilitated coalition efforts to reduce hydroelectric facilities’ impacts on downstream water quality and water flows. With renewed support, the grantee will continue monitoring hydroelectric operations and engage in other freshwater policy reform opportunities in Michigan, such as those related to open-net aquaculture. The grantee will also develop a report showing the economic benefits of hunting, fishing, and trapping in Michigan.

title: Michigan State Parks and Outdoor Recreation Panel
description: The parks system in Michigan preserves, protects, and showcases the vast and outstanding natural resources and outdoor recreation opportunities the state has to offer. Because of their importance, it is critical that the state carefully and strategically plan for the parks’ long-term success and sustainability. A blue-ribbon panel will be created by the state to develop a vision for the future of the state parks and recommend steps the state should take to achieve such a vision. The panel’s scope of work will include consideration of local and county park systems as well. The Michigan United Conservation Clubs, a well-established and respected statewide conservation group, will provide information and technical support to the volunteer panel, enabling it to complete its work within 14 months.

title: An Illustrated Guide to Poverty in 21st Century America
description: Grove Consultants International will design a series of communication tools to illuminate the vexing issues and innovative solutions associated with the changing nature of poverty in the United States. This project will use animated video and social media tools to describe both the complexity of problems and short fallings of the systems designed to address those problems. The grantee’s work will allow the Foundation and its grantees to contribute to the public discourse on poverty and help shape the agendas and actions of practitioners, policymakers, and philanthropic partners in supporting effective solutions for addressing poverty.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purpose support to Project QUEST, Inc., a community-based workforce development program in San Antonio that provides low-earning adults the education and work experiences they need to get good paying jobs. This grant will help Project QUEST, Inc., implement important organizational reforms and train 416 individuals in the coming year with an average starting wage of $19.40 per hour. The program targets low-income, minority, first-generation college students who lack the necessary education and credentials to obtain quality employment.

title: Cultivating Community Engagement
description: This grant provides partial support for the second phase of the Cultivating Community Engagement project. The project has the following objectives: 1) uncover and document practices among community foundations that promote and support stronger citizen engagement in shaping the community’s future; 2) test the identified practices through a peer learning network in which network participants adopt and adapt the new practices; and 3) refine and disseminate recommendations on best practices and examples of effective community engagement to community foundation professionals. In its first phase, a 34-person panel was recruited and convened. The panel oversaw and contributed to the development of a case statement and key practices for community engagement by community foundations. In the second phase, the panel’s findings will be finalized, tested through a peer learning network, refined, and disseminated. CFLeads is a national learning cooperative that advocates for and advances the practice of community leadership among community foundations.

title: Cultivating Community Engagement
description: CFLeads is a national learning cooperative that advocates for and advances the practice of community leadership among community foundations. The Cultivating Community Engagement project has the following objectives: 1) uncover and document practices among community foundations that promote and support stronger citizen engagement in shaping the community’s future; 2) test the identified practices through a peer learning network in which network participants adopt and adapt the new practices; and 3) refine and disseminate recommendations on best practices and examples of effective community engagement to community foundation professionals. In its first phase, a 34-person panel oversaw and contributed to the development of a case statement and key practices for resident engagement by community foundations. In the second phase, the panel has been testing the findings through a peer learning network. A grant increase will allow the grantee to synthesize, publish, and broadly disseminate the results throughout the community foundation field.

title: Cultivating Community Engagement
description: This grant provides partial support for the third phase of the Cultivating Community Engagement project. In the first phase, CFLeads convened a national panel that oversaw and contributed to the development of a case statement and key practices for resident engagement by community foundations. In the second phase, eight community foundation teams participated in a learning network to advance their own resident engagement practices. This led to case studies and a guidebook that were broadly disseminated throughout the United States community foundation field. The third phase will consist of a peer learning program for eight to ten Michigan community foundations to help them advance their community leadership and resident engagement practices. Afterwards, the grantee will produce a summary report and a video highlighting a story of impact from one of the participating foundations. CFLeads is a national learning cooperative that advocates for and advances the practice of community leadership among community foundations.

title: Cultivating Community Engagement
description: This grant to CFLeads provides partial support for the first phase of the Cultivating Community Engagement project. The project has the following objectives: 1) locate and document practices among community foundations that promote and support stronger citizen engagement in shaping the community’s future; 2) test the identified practices through a peer learning network in which network participants adopt and adapt the new practices; and 3) refine and disseminate recommendations on best practices and examples of effective community engagement to community foundation professionals. The project’s first phase will consist of: 1) two, in-person and one virtual meeting of a panel of approximately 30 experts; and 2) production and dissemination of a roadmap for community foundations that want to strengthen their community engagement capacity to engage a broad citizenry to solve local problems. CFLeads is a national learning cooperative that advocates for and advances the practice of community leadership among community foundations.

title: Flint US Ignite Expansion
description: This grant will provide support to US Ignite to develop and expand ultrafast broadband network applications in Flint, Michigan. The grantee was established by the Office of Science and Technology Policy, Executive Office of the President of the United States, and the National Science Foundation. The grantee’s goal is to bring together government entities, academic institutions, nonprofit organizations, and technology companies for the development of applications and services to operate over ultrafast broadband networks in six priority areas, including healthcare, energy, education, transportation, public safety, and advanced manufacturing.

title: Flint Ignite Expansion
description: This grant will provide support to US Ignite to develop and expand ultrafast broadband network applications in Flint, Michigan. The grantee was established by the Office of Science and Technology Policy, Executive Office of the President of the United States, and the National Science Foundation. The grantee’s goal is to bring together government entities, academic institutions, nonprofit organizations, and technology companies for the development of applications and services to operate over ultrafast broadband networks in six priority areas, including healthcare, energy, education, transportation, public safety, and advanced manufacturing.

title: U.S. Ignite Phase I
description: One Economy Corporation seeks support for the planning phase of the U.S. Ignite project. U.S. Ignite is a public/private partnership initiated by the Office of Science and Technology Policy, Executive Office of the President of the United States, and the National Science Foundation. The goal of the partnership is to bring together government entities, academic institutions, not-for-profit organizations, and technology companies for the development of applications and services to operate over ultra-fast broadband networks in such areas as commerce, healthcare, energy, and education.

title: University Square Project
description: This grant will provide funds to Carriage Town Ministries to create a park and garden space at the corner of University Avenue and Grand Traverse Street. Transitioning from a parking lot to a park, the new space will help beautify this important intersection within the historic Carriage Town neighborhood, create a venue for community use and programming, and provide meaningful work for residents of Carriage Town Ministries as they perform upkeep on the property.

title: S. Jean Simi Fund for the Arts
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide funds to the Community Foundation of Greater Flint for the S. Jean Simi Fund for the Arts. The fund provides support for the arts to include music, theater, and the performing and visual arts, with a focus on the youth of Flint and Genesee County.
