title: City of Flint Fiscal Technical Assistance
description: The city of Flint is currently under the authority of an emergency manager and is seeking all possible avenues for cost savings and efficiencies. It is undertaking an external review of its financial functions in order to examine whether there are additional efficiencies that could be realized. In addition, the review will include the analysis of possible economies of scale with other units of government within the area.

title: Michigan Communities for Financial Empowerment Network
grantee: Community Economic Development Association of Michigan
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: The Michigan Communities for Financial Empowerment Network is a network of cities, including San Francisco, Newark, and San Antonio, committed to advancing effective and large-scale financial empowerment initiatives locally and nationally. Since 2008, the network’s member cities have developed and implemented basic banking and savings programs; developed citywide infrastructure for free financial education and counseling; launched public education campaigns; and used the member cities’ voices to advance policies and practices that create a safe financial services marketplace for their residents. This grant will enable the Community Economic Development Association of Michigan to bring the network’s best practices to the state of Michigan. Mott funds will support outreach, technical assistance, and networking activities. The overall goal of this project is to develop a robust network of local, municipal leaders who are actively engaged in driving financial empowerment strategies for low- and moderate-income families throughout the state. The grantee is a nonprofit membership organization dedicated to rebuilding neighborhoods and revitalizing communities throughout Michigan.

title: Michigan Communities for Financial Empowerment Network
grantee: Community Economic Development Association of Michigan
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: The Cities for Financial Empowerment Coalition is a network of cities, including San Francisco, Newark, and San Antonio, committed to advancing effective and large-scale financial empowerment initiatives locally and nationally. Since 2008, the coalition’s member cities have developed and implemented basic banking and savings programs; developed citywide infrastructure for free financial education and counseling; launched public education campaigns; and used the member cities’ voices to advance policies and practices that create a safe financial services marketplace for their residents. This grant will enable the Community Economic Development Association of Michigan to bring the coalition’s best practices to the state of Michigan. Mott funds will support outreach, regranting, technical assistance, and networking activities. The overall goal of this project is to develop a robust network of local municipal leaders who are actively engaged in driving financial empowerment strategies for low- and moderate-income families throughout the state. The grantee is a nonprofit membership organization dedicated to rebuilding neighborhoods and revitalizing communities throughout Michigan.

title: Michigan Communities for Financial Empowerment Network
grantee: Community Economic Development Association of Michigan
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: The Cities for Financial Empowerment Coalition is a network of cities committed to advancing effective financial empowerment strategies locally and nationally. These strategies include: research on consumer banking and the use of financial services by low- and moderate-income populations; access to high quality financial information, education, and counseling; and access to savings and asset-building opportunities. This grant will enable the Community Economic Development Association of Michigan to continue promoting financial empowerment practices in Michigan and share Michigan’s lessons nationally. Mott funds will support outreach, technical assistance, and networking activities, specifically focused on children’s savings account programs. The overall goal of this project is to develop a network of local municipal leaders who are actively engaged in driving financial empowerment strategies for low- and moderate-income families throughout the state. The grantee is a nonprofit membership organization dedicated to rebuilding neighborhoods and revitalizing communities throughout Michigan.

title: Earn & Learn Initiative Cross-Site Documentation and Networking
description: The Earn & Learn Initiative is an education, training, and subsidized employment program that will help low-income youth — particularly young minority males and former prisoners re-entering the workforce — solidify basic skills while attaining credentials with labor market value. This grant will enable the Corporation for a Skilled Workforce to support implementation of the initiative by helping to identify, synthesize, and disseminate information that enhances program impact through accelerated adoption of effective practices. To accomplish this goal, the grantee will provide technical assistance to and coordinate learning across the Detroit, Flint, and Saginaw program sites. The Earn & Learn Initiative is being implemented in partnership with the state of Michigan, local workforce development agencies, and regional and national grantmaking organizations, including the Open Society Foundations.

title: Victoria S. Levin Endowment Fund
grantee: Society for Research in Child Development
description: This grant will provide funds to the Society for Research in Child Development for the Victoria S. Levin Award for Research on Children’s Mental Health by Early Career Scientists. The endowment fund recognizes the dedication of Victoria S. Levin in fostering children’s healthy development through encouraging the best science by the brightest new investigators to address the best ways to foster children’s mental health in the first five years of life. The endowment fund will provide an annual award for an early career investigator.

title: Multi-Agency Grants Initiative: Advice Office Regranting Project
description: The Humanist Institute for Cooperation with Developing Countries (commonly referred to as HIVOS – South Africa) is part of the Dutch-based nongovernmental organization, HIVOS – Netherlands, which was established in the 1950s and works in many countries around the world to alleviate poverty and build stronger civil societies. The Multi-Agency Grants Initiative, managed by the grantee, is a collaborative venture between various donors funding in South Africa. Its purpose is to provide a responsive mechanism for making small grants to community-based organizations, including community-based advice offices. In the past year, Mott support allowed the grantee to regrant to community advice offices in the Free State province to provide free legal advice and related support to poor people. Mott funds also supported training and mentoring activities to strengthen the advice offices. This grant will support HIVOS – South Africa to continue working with advice offices in the Free State province.

title: Multi-Agency Grants Initiative: Advice Office Regranting Project
description: The Humanist Institute for Cooperation with Developing Countries (commonly referred to as HIVOS – South Africa) is part of the Dutch-based nongovernmental organization, HIVOS – Netherlands, which was established in the 1950s and works in many countries around the world to alleviate poverty and build stronger civil societies. The Multi-Agency Grants Initiative, managed by HIVOS – South Africa, is a collaborative venture among various donors in South Africa. Its purpose is to provide a responsive mechanism for making small grants to community-based organizations, including community-based advice offices. Past support enabled the grantee to regrant to community advice offices in the Free State province that provide free legal advice and related support to poor people and to support training and mentoring activities to strengthen the advice offices. This grant will allow the grantee to continue to provide financial and institutional strengthening support to six advice offices in the Free State province.

title: Multi-Agency Grants Initiative: Advice Office Regranting Project
description: Hlanganisa Institute of Development Southern Africa NPC, previously known as Hivos – South Africa, was established in 2006 to seek new and innovative solutions to persistent social challenges. The Multi-Agency Grants Initiative, managed by the grantee, is a collaborative venture between various funders in South Africa. Its purpose is to provide a responsive mechanism for making small grants to community-based organizations, including community advice offices. Past support enabled the grantee to re-grant to community advice offices in the Free State province and support training and mentoring activities to strengthen the advice offices. This grant will enable the grantee to support six community advice offices in the Free State province that provide legal advice and related services to poor and marginalized people, particularly people living and working on farms.

title: Multi-Agency Grants Initiative: Advice Office Regranting Project
description: The Humanist Institute for Cooperation with Developing Countries (commonly referred to as Hivos – South Africa) is part of the Dutch-based nongovernmental organization, Hivos – Netherlands, which was established in the 1950s and works in many countries around the world to alleviate poverty and build stronger civil societies. The Multi-Agency Grants Initiative, managed by the grantee, is a collaborative venture between various donors. Its purpose is to provide a responsive mechanism for the provision of small grants to community-based organizations, including community-based advice offices. This grant will provide financial support to community-based advice offices in the Free State province. Also, the advice offices will receive training and mentoring to help them improve their own operations, governance, and sustainability. The aim is to enhance the performance of these advice offices so that they are able to offer poor people a better and improved service based on local requirements.

title: Endowment for Sustainable Future
description: The program goal is to strengthen the financial sustainability of a leading Bulgarian foundation that supports the development of local communities and grassroots, nonprofit organizations in Bulgaria through tailored capacity-building and funding programs. To this end, the Workshop for Civic Initiatives Foundation will run an endowment building program to raise at least $250,000 to match the $500,000 provided by the Mott Foundation and increase its total endowment to at least $1 million by the end of 2015. Through this process, the grantee will strengthen its overall fundraising strategies and capacities and access new sources of funding. The grantee has a long-term commitment to strengthening its role as a grantmaker in the field of civil society development and maintaining its annual grantmaking budget at the level of at least $400,000. Established in 2001, the grantee is working to support community development, active civic participation, integration of marginalized groups, and mobilization of local resources for social development through providing training, consultancy, and small grants to grassroots organizations and community leaders. In addition, the grantee is managing a national program that is supporting existing and new community foundations in Bulgaria.

title: Champions Suspension Program
description: This grant will provide support to PW Empowerment Group, Inc., for the Champions Suspension Program. The program is a supplemental education program for students who have been suspended/expelled from the Flint Community Schools or other local school districts. Recommended support will enable the grantee to enhance the academic and wraparound supports provided to students in the program.

title: Developing Philanthropy in Emerging Markets
description: The program goal is to enhance the development of philanthropy in emerging market countries. To this end, Alliance Publishing Trust will support the finalists of the Olga Alexeeva Memorial Prize to travel to the Emerging Societies – Emerging Philanthropies International Forum in Peterhoff, Russia in 2013, and to the WINGS Forum in Istanbul, Turkey, in 2014. The prize was envisioned during a 2012 seminar organized to honor the late Olga Alexeeva’s significant contributions to the field of philanthropy globally. Besides commemorating Olga’s memory, the prize is envisioned to be a field-building exercise that acknowledges individuals who have demonstrated remarkable leadership, creativity, and results in developing philanthropy for progressive social change in an emerging market country or countries. Alliance Publishing Trust is a registered United Kingdom charity that aims to facilitate the exchange of information and ideas among philanthropists, social investors, and others working for social change worldwide.

title: Developing Philanthropy in Emerging Markets
description: The program goal is to enhance the development of philanthropy in emerging market countries. To this end, Alliance Publishing Trust will organize a two-day seminar in London in early 2012 to honor Olga Alexeeva’s significant contributions to the field of philanthropy globally. The seminar will capture Olga Alexeeva’s experience and ideas and ensure that her important work to develop philanthropy in emerging market countries is continued. The grantee will broadly disseminate the findings from the seminar through the publication of a toolkit. Seminar participants will include people who worked closely with Olga Alexeeva over the years as well as others working in this field. Alliance Publishing Trust is a registered U.K. charity that aims to facilitate the exchange of information and ideas among philanthropists, social investors, and others working for social change worldwide.

title: The Other America and Anti-Poverty Policies 50 Years Later
description: The National Poverty Center at the Gerald R. Ford School of Public Policy at the University of Michigan was established in 2002 as a university-based, nonpartisan research center with a mission to conduct and promote multidisciplinary, policy-relevant research, mentor and train emerging scholars, and inform public discourse on the causes and consequences of poverty. This grant will provide support for a project to analyze the current realities of poverty, explore possible philanthropic investments to alleviate the causes and/or effects of poverty, and inform the public discourse about opportunities to expand more effective economic participation to low- and moderate-income families.

title: International Cartoon Art Exhibit
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will support the Creating a Common Language: International Cartoon Art Exhibit at the Flint Institute of Arts. This exhibit is from the collection of international cartoons depicting political and social issues belonging to the Aydin Dogan Foundation of Istanbul, Turkey. The exhibit will include artwork from the 300 finalists of the annual international cartoon competition held by the Dogan Foundation for nearly 30 years. The competition provides artists from diverse ethnic and cultural backgrounds to use cartoons as a common language to promote tolerance and understanding of others. The exhibition will run from September 2012 through December 2012.

title: Expanded Learning and Afterschool Initiative
description: This grant will continue to support the After-School Corporation and the collaborative for building after-school systems in developing expanded learning and afterschool models that engage community partners. In particular, the grantee will provide technical assistance and resources to build awareness and knowledge of the value and assets that community organizations bring to the delivery of afterschool and expanded learning programs. This project will enable the grantee to continue to: 1) support school leaders in harnessing the value and resources that community organizations bring to the delivery of educational opportunities to low-income students; and 2) work to strengthen partnerships that help students stay on track to graduate from high school and be college- and career-ready.

title: Expanded Learning and Afterschool Initiative
description: This grant will allow the After-School Corporation to contribute to the development of school models that engage community partners based on the principles of high quality afterschool programs. The grantee will participate in the development of the initiative by: 1) creating technical assistance tools and materials for school and district leaders; 2) providing technical assistance to school districts; and 3) developing a long-term technical assistance plan for implementing new afterschool programs in schools. Ultimately, this project will help communities and schools use their resources to make better use of student learning time that prepares youth for college, careers, and life.

title: Endowment for Sustainable Future
description: The program goal is to strengthen the financial sustainability of the Balkan Community Initiatives Fund – Serbia, a private, independent, Serbian grantmaking foundation based in Belgrade. Through its grantmaking, training, networking assistance, and leadership, the grantee promotes active civic participation in decisionmaking and community development throughout Serbia, particularly in the country’s smaller towns and isolated regions. As part of its long-term financial sustainability strategy, the grantee will launch an endowment-building program designed to raise $750,000 over the next five years. To match the contribution from the Mott Foundation, the grantee will solicit support from individuals, corporate donors, and other donor agencies operating in Serbia. Additionally, during the grant period, the grantee will contribute a portion of the income it earns from services and rental of office space it owns. Established in 1999 as a charity registered in the United Kingdom and then subsequently registered in Serbia in 2004, the grantee has developed into one of the leading grantmakers in Serbia and the region.

title: Endowment for a Sustainable Future
description: The program goal is to strengthen the financial sustainability of the Mozaik Community Development Foundation, a private, independent, Bosnian grantmaking foundation based in Sarajevo. Through its grantmaking, training and networking assistance, social enterprise development, and leadership, the grantee promotes active civic participation in decisionmaking and community development throughout Bosnia. As part of its long-term financial sustainability strategy, the grantee will launch an endowment-building program designed to raise $750,000 over the next five years. To match the contribution from the Mott Foundation, the grantee will target support from individuals, corporate donors, and other donor agencies operating in Bosnia. Additionally, during the grant period the grantee will contribute to the endowment a portion of the revenue from two social enterprises it owns in Bosnia. Established in 2000, the grantee has developed into one of the strongest and most dynamic and innovative nonprofits in Bosnia and the wider region.

title: LearnPhilanthropy
description: LearnPhilanthropy is a collaborative program to build an online, fieldwide hub for grantmaker learning. The project is being developed by a network of grantmakers and philanthropy support professionals so that the philanthropic infrastructure can more efficiently and effectively serve the field. Incubated by the Council on Foundations and the Forum of Regional Associations of Grantmakers, LearnPhilanthropy currently has 30 content partners consisting of a wide variety of philanthropic support organizations. This grant will enable LearnPhilanthropy to transition to being hosted at the Johnson Center for Philanthropy, a unit of the College of Community and Public Service at Grand Valley State University in Grand Rapids, Michigan. The grant will also support completing a Web redesign process; expanding the number of new content sources; developing new partnerships with philanthropic journals, infrastructure organizations, and other content providers; and defining and implementing a business model that will lead to sustainable funding.

title: LearnPhilanthropy
description: LearnPhilanthropy is a collaborative initiative to build an online, fieldwide hub for grantmaker learning. The project was developed by a network of grantmakers and philanthropy support professionals so that the philanthropic infrastructure can more efficiently and effectively serve the field. Incubated by the Council on Foundations and the Forum of Regional Associations of Grantmakers, LearnPhilanthropy is now hosted by the Johnson Center for Philanthropy, a unit of the College of Community and Public Service at Grand Valley State University in Grand Rapids, Michigan. It currently has 59 content partners consisting of a wide variety of philanthropic support organizations. This grant will support establishing online training opportunities for new grantmakers, the continued development of content partner relationships, improving site design, increasing user traffic, maintaining and developing relationships with other philanthropy infrastructure organizations, developing a sustainable revenue model, and aligning resources within the Johnson Center’s Institute for Foundation and Donor Learning.

title: LearnPhilanthropy
description: LearnPhilanthropy is a collaborative initiative to build an online, fieldwide hub for grantmaker learning. The project was developed by a network of grantmakers and philanthropy support professionals so the philanthropic infrastructure can more efficiently and effectively serve the field. Incubated by the Council on Foundations and the United Philanthropy Forum, LearnPhilanthropy is now hosted by the Dorothy A. Johnson Center for Philanthropy, a unit of the College of Community and Public Service at Grand Valley State University in Grand Rapids, Michigan. It currently has 67 content partners consisting of a wide variety of philanthropic support organizations. This grant will support recruiting more content providers, increasing traffic to the site, adding new content, and developing online courses for new foundation staff and trustees.

title: LearnPhilanthropy
description: LearnPhilanthropy is a collaborative initiative to build an online, fieldwide hub for grantmaker learning. The project is being developed by a network of grantmakers and philanthropy support professionals so that the philanthropic infrastructure can more efficiently and effectively serve the field. Incubated by the Council on Foundations and the Forum of Regional Associations of Grantmakers, LearnPhilanthropy has 28 content partners consisting of a wide variety of philanthropic support organizations. This grant will enable LearnPhilanthropy to continue to develop and refine its content, community, web portal, and business model throughout a critical year in which this collaborative and fieldwide initiative is first transitioning to a more permanent structure and governance, and then scaling up to meet field demand. The Council on Foundations is a membership association of more than 1,700 independent, operating, community, public, and company-sponsored foundations, and corporate giving programs in the United States and abroad.

title: Tax Policy and Charities Project
description: The Tax Policy and Charities Project aims to provide research and analysis to inform policymakers as they consider changes to the tax code that may affect nonprofit organizations. Project products include a Web site, conferences, and roundtable discussions on specific tax policy issues; broader use of existing data and improved data modeling and simulation capabilities for better analyses; and a series of research papers, policy briefs, articles, congressional testimony, and other material on major tax and charity issues. The project is implemented by two reputable policy centers that are part of the Urban Institute, the Urban-Brookings Tax Policy Center and the Center on Nonprofits and Philanthropy. The Urban Institute is a national think tank that gathers data, conducts research, evaluates programs, offers technical assistance overseas, and educates Americans on social and economic issues in order to foster sound public policy and effective government.

title: Tax Policy and Charities Project
description: The Tax Policy and Charities Project aims to: 1) make available the latest information on changes to the nonprofit sector because of tax policy modifications; 2) finance research to improve tax policy; and 3) involve scholars and policy officials in both analysis and discussion of new tax proposals. Activities will include conferences and roundtable discussions on specific tax policy issues and a series of research papers, policy briefs, articles, congressional testimony, and other materials regarding major tax and charity issues. Recent outputs include estimates of the impact of presidential candidates’ tax proposals on charitable giving and a brief on the universal charitable tax deduction. The project is implemented by the Urban-Brookings Tax Policy Center of the Urban Institute. The Urban Institute is a national think tank that gathers data, conducts research, evaluates programs, offers technical assistance overseas, and educates Americans on social and economic issues to foster sound public policy and effective government.

title: Tax Policy and Charities Project
description: The Tax Policy and Charities Project aims to provide research and analysis to inform policymakers as they consider changes to the tax code that may affect nonprofit organizations. Project products include a Web site, two major and two minor conferences per year on specific tax policy issues; broader use of existing data and improved data modeling and simulation capabilities for better analyses; and a series of research papers, policy briefs, fact sheets, and other material on major tax and charity issues. The project will be implemented by two reputable policy centers that are part of the Urban Institute, the Urban-Brookings Tax Policy Center and the Center on Nonprofits and Philanthropy. The Urban Institute is a national think tank that gathers data, conducts research, evaluates programs, offers technical assistance overseas, and educates Americans on social and economic issues to foster sound public policy and effective government.

title: Expanding Access and Success for Low-Skilled Adults
description: This grant will enable Jobs for the Future to continue to support two critical activities of its Foundation-supported Breaking Through Initiative. Breaking Through is a community college initiative aimed at expanding effective strategies to assist low-skilled adults to prepare for and succeed in occupational and technical degree programs. Currently, there are more than 41 community colleges in 22 states implementing various strands of Breaking Through. Recommended support will allow the grantee to host a national convening of Breaking Through sites and provide continued support for Breaking Through activities in Michigan via the Center for Student Success at the Michigan Community College Association.

title: Africa Grantmakers Network
description: The Southern Africa Trust supports civil society organizations in southern Africa to participate effectively and with credibility in policy dialogues so that the voices of the poor can have better impact in the development of public policies. The African Grantmakers Network is a continentwide network of African grantmaking organizations established to facilitate networking and learning among these institutions. Past Mott support contributed to the establishment of the network’s secretariat, grantmaker convenings, research, and membership development. This grant will support the African Grantmakers Network to enhance thought leadership on African philanthropy, contribute to building resilient African philanthropic institutions by setting standards for good governance and accountability, convene country- and regional-level peer learning events, and build a repository of knowledge on African philanthropy.

title: Africa Grantmakers Network
description: Southern Africa Trust supports civil society organizations in southern Africa to participate effectively and with credibility in policy dialogues so that the voices of the poor can have better impact in the development of public policies. The African Grantmakers Network is a continent wide network of African grantmaking organizations established to facilitate networking and learning among these institutions. Past Mott support for the network contributed to enhancing thought leadership on African philanthropy, participation in continental and international events to advance African philanthropy, convening peer learning events on subjects like good governance and accountability, and building a repository of knowledge on African philanthropy. This grant will assist the African Grantmakers Network to: host the 2014 biennial assembly, convene peer learning events for sharing of experiences among African grantmakers, strengthen the secretariat, conduct research that will result in the establishment of a philanthropy barometer for Africa, and participate in international events to advance African philanthropy.

title: Africa Philanthropy Network
description: The Southern Africa Trust supports civil society organizations in southern Africa to participate effectively and with credibility in policy dialogues so that the voices of the poor can have better impact in the development of public policies. The Africa Philanthropy Network, previously known as the African Grantmakers Network, is a continent wide network of African grantmaking organizations established to facilitate networking and learning. Past support for the network contributed to the hosting of the 2015 biennial assembly, convening peer learning events for sharing of experiences among African grantmakers, strengthening the network secretariat, conducting research, and participating in international events to advance African philanthropy. This grant will assist the Africa Philanthropy Network to lead conversations to define African philanthropy and its role in the global philanthropy discourse, restructure and rebrand the network, convene leaders and wealthy Africans to discuss their role in Africa’s development, and host learning events for members.

title: Africa Philanthropy Network
description: The Southern Africa Trust supports civil society organizations in southern Africa to participate effectively and with credibility in policy dialogues so that the voices of the poor can have a better impact in the development of public policies. The Africa Philanthropy Network is a continent-wide network of grantmakers and other philanthropic institutions, set up to promote learning and networking. Past support enabled the network to participate in international events to advance African Philanthropy, strengthen its membership, and set up internal systems. This grant will enable the grantee to host its biennial conference that brings together all members across the continent. It will also strengthen connections with similar organizations in the continent, host learning events for members, and build the brand of the network.

title: Africa Grantmakers Network
description: The Kenya Community Development Foundation was founded in 1997 to support Kenyan communities to drive their own development priorities by linking them to resources and information. It promotes sustainable development approaches, including local resource mobilization and helping communities to utilize resources they have rather than depend on external resources. The Africa Grantmakers Network, a project of the Kenya Community Development Foundation, is a continentwide network of African grantmakers launched in 2009 to facilitate networking and mutual learning among established and emerging African philanthropic institutions. It focuses on elevating the role of wealthy Africans as key to realizing greater governance, development, and general welfare of Africa. This grant will support research activities on various forms of giving in Africa, mobilizing rich Africans to give to deserving causes, and holding a conference for African grantmakers in South Africa to share knowledge and experiences.

title: Generation Celebration
description: The program goal is to foster a widespread culture of giving in Ukraine. Using its Web platform, the Garage Gang Kollektiv will stimulate creative methods of online crowdfunding while building diverse sources of support for initiatives in the areas of sustainable development, social integration, participation in cultural life, and civic engagement. The grantee will link its online efforts with offline activities to engage socially responsible businesses in philanthropic projects promoted through the site. It will also develop a mentoring and skill-sharing exchange for activists. In the period 2012-2014, 23 projects were successfully financed, raising almost $250,000. Among these was a brand new online news broadcast which provided crucial independent coverage of the winter protests in Ukraine. Garage Gang Kollektiv was established in 2009 in order to support organizations and individuals which could collaborate creatively in addressing the challenges of community and social development.

title: Culture of Giving: Powering Strategic Philanthropy
description: The program goal is to foster a widespread and sophisticated culture of giving in Ukraine. Using its web platform, the Garage Gang Kollektiv will stimulate creative methods of online crowdfunding, drawing on both individual and institutional donors. It will seek to develop a more sustained process of social investment through its crowdfunding platform, supplemented with targeted mentoring, impact assessment and feedback, and sharing knowledge of successful projects. The grantee will link its online efforts with offline activities to engage socially responsible businesses in philanthropic projects promoted through the site. In the period 2014-2016, 99 projects were successfully financed, raising almost $240,000. The platform also saw increased regularity of giving and actively mentored project developers in 13 new regions. Garage Gang Kollektiv was established in 2009 in order to support organizations and individuals who could collaborate creatively in addressing the challenges of community and social development.

title: Generation Celebration
description: The program goal is to foster a widespread culture of giving in Ukraine. Through the Generation Celebration project, the Garage Gang Kollektiv will stimulate creative methods of domestic fundraising while building diverse sources of support for initiatives in the areas of sustainable development, social integration, participation in cultural life, and civic engagement. Using its Web platform www.biggggidea.com, the grantee will link its online efforts with offline activities to encourage, identify, and channel support to creative community projects and social innovations. Garage Gang Kollektiv was established in 2009 in order to build a nationwide network of forward-thinking individuals, businesses, and nongovernmental organizations that could collaborate creatively in addressing the challenges of community and social development. Though based in Kyiv, its active promotion of Web-based initiatives combined with offline travelling road shows give it a national profile.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to mobilize local communities in western Ukraine to effectively address and resolve issues of common concern. General purpose support will assist the West-Ukrainian Resource Center in the fulfillment of its mission to promote the development of civil society through the support of community social and economic initiatives. It will do this through a mix of grants and capacity building in the fields of rural community development, adult education, and social integration of returning labor migrants. In 2012-2014, the grantee worked with 23 communities in five regions of Ukraine, introducing models of community self-management in the absence of local councils, as well as small-scale community economic development bodies to foster local business growth. The West-Ukrainian Resource Center was founded in 1994 as a support organization for regional nongovernmental organizations and has since become a leading resource for community development practice in Ukraine.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to mobilize local communities in Ukraine to effectively address and resolve issues of common concern. General purpose support will assist the West-Ukrainian Resource Center to promote the development of civil society through the support of community, social, and economic initiatives. It will do this through a mix of grants and capacity building in the fields of rural community development, adult education, and social integration of migrants and internally displaced persons. In 2014-2016, the grantee worked with 41 communities in seven regions of Ukraine introducing models of community self-management to address challenges of local administrative reform. It also helped incubate community economic development bodies to foster local business growth as a means to assist with the integration of new categories of migrants. The West-Ukrainian Resource Center was founded in 1994 as a support organization for regional nongovernmental organizations and has since become a leading resource for community development practice in Ukraine.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to mobilize local communities in western Ukraine to effectively address and resolve issues of common concern. General purpose support will assist the West-Ukrainian Resource Center in the fulfillment of its mission to promote the development of civil society through the support of community initiatives. Its goals are threefold — to strengthen local communities by supporting local, results-oriented community development initiatives; increase productive cooperation between the state, businesses, and civil society organizations at the community level; and develop the capacities of local and regional civic groups through the delivery of quality educational, consulting, and informational services to these groups. The West-Ukrainian Resource Center was founded in 1994 as a support organization for regional, nongovernmental organizations. Since then, it has become a leader in the provision of consulting and training services on issues of organizational administration, territorial management, and community development.

title: Act Now
description: The program goal is to strengthen active citizen engagement in local community development in Ukraine. Under the Act Now project, the East Europe Foundation will promote the use of information and communication technologies as tools for citizen mobilization and responsive local government. The grantee will expand the Open City Web platform from six to ten cities while also advocating for its inclusion in national Open Government initiatives. The grantee will also work to identify crowdfunding and other resource mobilization strategies to support civic initiatives arising under the project. In 2012-2013, the grantee successfully developed the platform and linked it to the information systems of six local authorities. As a result, over 260 local issues ranging from garbage collection to utilities maintenance were successfully resolved. The East Europe Foundation was registered in 2007 as an indigenous Ukrainian foundation and supports initiatives in such areas as corporate social responsibility, citizen engagement, and public-private partnerships.

title: Act Now
description: The program goal is to strengthen active citizen engagement in local community development in Ukraine. Under the Act Now project, the East Europe Foundation will promote the use of information and communication technologies as tools for citizen mobilization and responsive local government. In 2014-2015, the grantee successfully expanded the number of participating municipalities from 5 to 18. Effective use of the Open City Internet platform resulted in the resolution of almost 4,000 local issues. In Phase 3, the grantee will seek to expand the platform from 18 to more than 40 municipalities. It will enhance its functionality to encourage greater citizen engagement initiatives and will seek to ensure sustainability of the project through establishment of a social enterprise in partnership with the Ukrainian Association of Open Cities. The East Europe Foundation was registered in 2007 as an indigenous Ukrainian foundation and supports initiatives in such areas as corporate social responsibility, citizen engagement, and public-private partnerships.

title: Act Now
description: The program goal is to strengthen active citizen engagement in local community development in Ukraine. Under the Act Now project, the East Europe Foundation will promote the development and use of information and communication technology as a tool for citizen mobilization. The grantee will help develop and test a map-based Internet portal to enable citizens in six pilot communities to inform government departments about local community issues and to monitor any steps taken by responsible government departments in response to identified problems. In addition, the portal will provide an online forum that can assist offline community groups to self-organize and take responsibility for addressing these issues collectively, if the government cannot or does not address them on its own. The East Europe Foundation was registered in 2007 as the localized descendant of the Eurasia Foundation office in Ukraine and supports initiatives in such areas as corporate social responsibility, citizen engagement, and public-private partnerships.

title: Low Wage Work: What Can We Do to Improve Job Quality
description: This grant to Aspen Institute will provide partial support for a series of roundtable discussions that will examine low-wage work in several different industry sectors including food service, retail trade, and construction. The forums will provide the opportunity for in-depth discussions on improving job quality, compensation, benefits, and advancement opportunities for low-wage workers and their families. The goal of the project is to increase awareness and illuminate strategies for improving opportunities and conditions in traditionally low-wage industries among policymakers, the business community, and workforce practitioners.

title: Low Wage Work: What Can We Do to Improve Job Quality
description: This grant to Aspen Institute will provide partial support for a series of roundtable discussions that will examine low-wage work in several different industry sectors, including food service, retail trade, and construction. The forums will provide the opportunity for in-depth discussions on improving job quality, compensation, benefits, and advancement opportunities for low-wage workers and their families. The goal of the project is to increase awareness and illuminate strategies for improving opportunities and conditions in traditionally low-wage industries among policymakers, the business community, and workforce practitioners.

The goal of the project is to increase awareness and illuminate strategies for improving opportunities and conditions in traditionally low-wage industries among policy makers, the business community, and workforce practitioners.

title: Jobs and Microenterprise
description: The goal of the project is to show how the microenterprise sector contributes to job creation and economic opportunity. The grant to Aspen Institute will support both quantitative and qualitative analyses of the impact microenterprise development has on job creation. The results of the study will provide detailed information for practitioners, funders, and policymakers on the role microenterprise plays in job creation and community economic recovery.

title: Dealing with the Past - Transitional Justice in Kosovo
description: The project goals are to support greater active civic participation on issues of dealing with the past and to strengthen democratic values in Kosovo. Through activities under this project, Integra will complement other national and regional initiatives aimed at increasing public engagement on dealing with Kosovo’s recent past. Specifically, the grantee will produce up to 100 documentary films about the personal stories of victims from all sides of the conflict in Kosovo and the broader region. The grantee will organize screenings and educational events in Kosovo and the region using these films and expand its capacity to disseminate films and related information online. During 2012-2013, the grantee produced more than 50 documentary films with victims from Kosovo with various ethnic, religious, and national backgrounds and organized screenings, including on television, to raise awareness of issues of accountability and justice in Kosovo. Established in 2003, Integra is a nonprofit nongovernmental organization registered in Kosovo by a group of young people.

title: Dealing with the Past - Transitional Justice in Kosovo
description: The project goals are to support greater active civic participation on issues of dealing with the past and to strengthen democratic values in Kosovo. Through activities under this project, Integra will complement other national and regional initiatives aimed at increasing public engagement on dealing with Kosovo’s recent past. Specifically, the grantee will produce up to 30 documentary films about the personal stories of victims from all sides of the conflict in Kosovo and the broader region. The grantee will organize screenings and educational events in Kosovo and the region using these films and expand its capacity to disseminate films and related information online. Additional activities will explore the role of arts and culture in raising awareness and engaging people constructively on the sensitive issues of the region’s recent past. During 2014-2015, the grantee produced 30 documentary films with victims from the region and organized screenings to raise awareness of issues of accountability and justice in Kosovo. Established in 2003, Integra is a nonprofit nongovernmental organization registered in Kosovo by a group of young people whose mission is to promote good governance and the protection of human rights for all people of Kosovo.

title: Dealing with the Past - Transitional Justice in Kosovo
description: The project goals are to support greater active civic participation on issues dealing with the past and to strengthen democratic values in Kosovo. Through activities under this project, Integra will complement other national and regional initiatives aimed at increasing public engagement on dealing with Kosovo’s recent past. Specifically, the grantee will produce a series of documentary films about the personal stories of victims from all sides of the conflict in Kosovo, organize educational events throughout the country using these films and other original theater pieces, and produce radio talk show programs to raise awareness about dealing with the past. Established in 2003, Integra is a nonprofit, nongovernmental organization registered in Kosovo by a group of young people. The mission of the organization is to promote good governance and the protection of human rights for all people of Kosovo.

title: Art for Social Change
description: The project goal is to encourage, empower, and enable young people in Turkey to be actively engaged in strengthening democratic values and bridging the country’s cultural, ethnic, and social divides. To this end, Anadolu Kultur will link young people in cities in the eastern, predominately Kurdish part of Turkey with young people in cities in the western part of Turkey. Building on the grantee’s previous work in these regions, the project will provide training and support to groups of young people between the ages of 20 and 28 from each region to engage in collaborative photography and film projects aimed at sharing stories about their lives, regions, and communities. The resulting 10 to 12 projects will be widely exhibited in Turkey and used to stimulate discussion and awareness among a broader group of young people. During the previous grant period, the grantee worked with 24 young people from Batman, Canakkale, Diyarbakir, and Izmir to create eight projects addressing a range of topics. Based in Istanbul but working extensively in eastern Turkey, Anadolu Kultur was established in 2002 with the mission of contributing to the development of a pluralist, open-minded society through improved cultural exchange and dialogue across Turkey’s diverse regions and communities.

title: Art for Social Change
description: The project goal is to encourage, empower, and enable young people in Turkey to be actively engaged in strengthening democratic values and bridging the country’s cultural, ethnic, and social divides. To this end, Anadolu Kultur will link young people in cities in the eastern, predominately Kurdish part of Turkey with young people in cities in the western part of Turkey. The resulting projects will be exhibited in Istanbul and made available through an online platform and used to stimulate discussion and awareness among a wider group of young people. Based in Istanbul but working extensively in eastern Turkey, Anadolu Kultur was established in 2002 with the mission of contributing to the development of a pluralist, open-minded society through improved cultural exchange and dialogue across Turkey’s diverse regions and communities.

To this end, Anadolu Kultur will link young people in two cities (Diyarbakir and Batman) in the eastern, predominately Kurdish part of Turkey with young people in two cities (Canakkale and Izmir) in the western part of Turkey. title: General Purposes
grantee: Truth, Justice and Memory Studies Association
description: The program goal is to strengthen the role of nonprofits in Turkey in promoting civic engagement on issues of justice and accountability. The Truth, Justice and Memory Studies Association will focus on empowering local human rights and other nonprofits working on documenting and raising awareness of Turkey’s history of human rights abuses, particularly the 30-year, ongoing Kurdish conflict. Specifically, the grantee will work collaboratively with other nonprofits in Turkey to establish common standards and approaches for recording and retrieving data on human rights violations; facilitate the sharing and exchange of data among nonprofits in the field; promote cooperation on advocacy, monitoring, and dissemination; and raise awareness of international experiences and practices. During 2012-2013, the grantee conducted field research on human rights abuses, published two reports based on its research, supported four local human rights nonprofits, and strengthened its staff and organizational capacities. Based in Istanbul, the grantee works throughout Turkey.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Truth, Justice and Memory Studies Association
description: The program goal is to strengthen the role of nonprofits in Turkey in promoting civic engagement on issues of justice and accountability. The newly established Truth, Justice and Memory Studies Association will focus on empowering local human rights groups and other nonprofits working on documenting and raising awareness of Turkey’s history of human rights abuses, particularly the 30-year, ongoing Kurdish conflict. Specifically, the grantee will work collaboratively with other nonprofits in Turkey to establish common standards and approaches for recording and retrieving data on human rights violations; facilitate the sharing and exchange of data among nonprofits in the field; promote cooperation on advocacy, monitoring, and dissemination; and raise awareness of international experiences and practices. Based in Istanbul, the grantee works throughout Turkey.

title: Towards Enhanced Civic Activism and Sustainable Civic Participation in Montenegro
description: The project goal is to increase and enhance active civic participation in the development of local communities in Montenegro. To this end, Civic Alliance, a national-level, nonprofit based in the capital, Podgorica, will carry out research and analysis of levels and effectiveness of civic participation in Montenegro, with the goal of identifying needs and opportunities to enhance engagement. Based on this understanding, the grantee will organize training and capacity building support for local nonprofits and provide support to projects with a number of selected community-based nonprofits. The grantee will assist community-based groups and initiatives to use the media effectively, establish and run nonprofit organizations, and organize and mobilize community members around priority issues. During 2012-2014, the grantee worked intensively with seven nonprofits across Montenegro to build their capacity to work with citizen groups, engage in strategic planning, manage communications, and carry out joint initiatives. Based in Podgorica, Civic Alliance was established in 2011 by two prominent nonprofits in Montenegro in order to take advantage of programmatic synergies and to share resources.

title: Towards Enhanced Civic Activism and Sustainable Civic Participation in Montenegro
description: The project goal is to increase and enhance active civic participation in the development of local communities in Montenegro. To this end, Civic Alliance, a national-level nonprofit based in the capital, Podgorica, will train community-based nonprofits, develop and pilot innovative tools for increasing civic participation, and carry out research and analysis of levels and effectiveness of civic participation in Montenegro. During 2014-2016, the grantee worked intensively with nine nonprofits across Montenegro to build their capacity to work with citizen groups, carried out and published a comprehensive analysis of civic participation in Montenegro, and partnered with local nonprofits to carry out community initiatives. Civic Alliance was established in 2011 by two prominent nonprofits in Montenegro in order to take advantage of programmatic synergies and to share resources.

title: Towards Enhanced Civic Activism and Sustainable Civic Participation in Montenegro
description: The project goal is to increase and enhance active civic participation in the development of local communities in Montenegro. To this end, Civic Alliance, a national-level nonprofit based in the capital, Podgorica, will work with three local nonprofits to deliver a set of services and information resources to citizens and civic initiatives in three communities — Bijelo Polje, Ulcinj, and Niksic. Based on the specific needs and issues in each community, the grantee and its partners will assist community-based groups and initiatives to use the media effectively, establish and run nonprofit organizations, and organize and mobilize community members around priority issues. The grantee and its partners will also assist the targeted communities by raising awareness of key local issues to the national level, particularly through national print and television media. Based in Podgorica, Civic Alliance was established in 2011 by two prominent nonprofits in Montenegro in order to take advantage of programmatic synergies and to share resources.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Southern African Community Grantmakers Leadership Forum
description: The Southern African Community Grantmakers Leadership Forum is a membership organization of community grantmakers. It promotes social justice grantmaking as a vehicle for social change and brings together members in a knowledge-sharing partnership to enhance their growth and strengthen their ability to provide maximum benefit to the communities they serve. Previously, the grantee hosted learning events for its members, built strong partnerships with structures that have similar values, and increased its membership to include other experienced community grantmakers in the southern African region. Activities for the next two years will include continuing to convene face-to-face learning events and Webinars for members to deepen their knowledge, building cohesion among members in the southern African region, developing links with community grantmakers in other countries, and documenting its history and contribution to the community grantmaking field.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Southern African Community Grantmakers Leadership Forum
description: The Southern African Community Grantmakers Leadership Forum is a membership organization established in 2010 to support the development of community grantmakers in the southern Africa region. It brings together leaders of community grantmaking organizations in a knowledge-sharing partnership to strengthen their ability to provide maximum benefit to the communities they serve. Previously, the grantee hosted peer learning events for members, participated in regional learning events, and reorganized its institutional structure to improve effectiveness. This grant support will allow the grantee to continue bringing together leaders of community grantmaking organizations to learn from each other, support the development of young people working in the field of philanthropy, build stronger linkages with continental and other regional networks, and provide information and material that is useful to building the community grantmaking field in southern Africa.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Southern African Community Grantmakers Leadership Forum
description: The Southern African Community Grantmakers Leadership Forum is a network of community grantmakers that was founded in 2010. It brings members together in a learning and knowledge-sharing environment to strengthen their ability to effectively support the communities they serve. Leaders of community grantmaking organizations share experiences, resources, and skills to improve their practice and strengthen the community philanthropy field in southern Africa. Previous support enabled the grantee to host learning events for members, support collaboration efforts among members, and participate in regional and global learning events on community philanthropy. This grant will support the grantee’s efforts to host learning events for its members, increase its membership and reach in southern Africa, develop communications platforms that encourage knowledge sharing among members, and become more active in regional and global networks of grantmakers.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Southern African Community Grantmakers Leadership Forum
description: The Southern African Community Grantmakers Leadership Forum was established in 2010 to connect leaders of community grantmaking organizations in the southern Africa region. It brings together established and emerging leaders to develop their knowledge and expertise and strengthen their institutions and the field. Past grants enabled the grantee to nurture emerging leaders and provide them with the necessary support to take up new roles and responsibilities as leaders in their organizations. This grant will support the network in continuing to bring together members in a learning and sharing platform, conduct research on community philanthropy in the region, produce learning material and other publications to build a knowledge repository for the network and the field, and participate in regional and international events to profile the network and learn from the field globally.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Southern African Community Grantmakers Leadership Forum
description: The Southern African Community Grantmakers Leadership Forum is a membership organization of community grantmakers that promotes leadership development and peer learning among its members. It evolved from a project initiated by Synergos in 2005, the Southern African Community Grantmakers Leadership Cooperative. The grantee brings its members together in a knowledge-sharing partnership to strengthen social justice philanthropy in southern Africa. Its main objective is to enhance the growth, professionalism, and sustainability of community grantmakers in the region in order to maximize their social impact and benefit to the communities they serve. This grant will support the grantee to build stronger linkages between community grantmakers in the southern African region; maintain relations with governments and the private sector; provide a platform for reflection, dialogue, and leadership development; and partner with structures that have similar values to set the African agenda for community philanthropy.

title: Examining the Role of Emergency Savings for Family Financial Security
description: This project, conducted by the University of Wisconsin-Madison, will support staff’s exploration and framing of emergency savings strategies as part of the Pathways Out of Poverty program’s strategic planning process. The first project deliverable will be a framing paper that will articulate the rationale for emergency savings and describe the opportunities and challenges associated with emergency savings initiatives. Second, the grantee will commission up to 12 white papers, each exploring an approach (or model) that could potentially facilitate emergency savings among low- and moderate-income households. The resulting set of papers will be presented for critical assessment by asset-building leaders at a symposium planned for November/December 2012. Finally, the grantee will publish the framing paper, white papers, and symposium report/conclusions in an edited volume that will be disseminated to policymakers, researchers, and other asset-building stakeholders. The volume will also be made available online.

title: Implementation of the Great Lakes Compact
geographic_focus: Minnesota, Ohio, Wisconsin, Indiana, New York, Illinois, Pennsylvania, Michigan
description: The Great Lakes Compact, an interstate agreement, is intended to sharply limit the diversion of waters outside the Great Lakes Basin and improve the management of water resources within the basin. The Natural Resources Defense Council, a national environmental organization with a strong regional presence in the Midwest, will provide tools and expertise at the regional and state levels to help implement the compact’s water conservation and efficiency elements.

title: Implementation of the Great Lakes Compact
geographic_focus: Minnesota, Indiana, Ohio, Wisconsin, Illinois, Pennsylvania, New York, Michigan
description: The Natural Resources Defense Council is an international environmental organization with a strong presence in the Great Lakes region. With prior Mott support, the grantee worked closely with state and local partners to improve how water quality policies are implemented in the Great Lakes states. The grantee focused its efforts on the Great Lakes Compact, an interstate agreement that limits the diversion of waters outside the Great Lakes basin and improves the management of water resources within the basin. In particular, the grantee helped analyze the region’s first out-of-basin water withdrawal request from the City of Waukesha, Wisconsin. With renewed Mott support, the grantee will continue helping states fulfill the compact’s water conservation requirements and implement other programs and policies to encourage the efficient use of water from the Great Lakes watershed.

title: Implementation of the Great Lakes Compact
geographic_focus: Pennsylvania, Indiana, Ohio, Minnesota, Wisconsin, Michigan, Illinois, New York
description: The Great Lakes Compact, an interstate agreement, is intended to prevent the diversion of waters outside the basin and to effectively manage the use of water within the basin. Despite some recent positive signs, the Great Lakes states have been slow to implement the compact, including its water conservation and efficiency provisions. The Natural Resources Defense Council, a national organization with a strong regional presence, will provide tools and expertise at the regional and state levels to help implement the compact’s water conservation and efficiency elements.

title: Second Century Project
description: This grant provides support to the Second Century Project, a seminar series for leaders of community foundations to: 1) examine and reflect deeply on the challenges facing the field; 2) document current responses to those challenges; 3) formulate recommendations for securing the health of community philanthropy for a new generation; and 4) contribute to a body of research relevant to community foundations, anchor institutions, and urbanization. It will result in the publication of a book and multimedia content timed for the 100th anniversary of the community foundation field in 2014. The Chicago Community Trust is one of the nation’s largest and oldest community foundations. Founded in 1915, the grantee’s mission is to lead and inspire philanthropic efforts that measurably improve the quality of life and the prosperity of the Chicago region.

title: African American History Calendar
description: This grant will provide funds to the Mount Hermon Missionary Baptist Church to produce 2014 and 2015 African American History Calendars for distribution by the African American Inspiration radio program.

title: African American History Calendar
description: This grant will provide funds to the Mount Hermon Missionary Baptist Church to produce 2013 African American History calendars for distribution by the African American Inspiration radio program.

title: Program Support
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to the Flint Cultural Center Corporation will provide support for two major projects — Discover Dinosaurs and Other Prehistoric Creatures and Mamma Mia! The 14-week dinosaur exhibit at Sloan Museum and Longway Planetarium will feature large, robotic dinosaurs. In addition, there will be a variety of hands-on activities and interactive displays, including a virtual dinosaur simulator, as well as family activities, science workshops, and educational programming. The Whiting will host two performances of Mamma Mia!, the world’s number one show, with more productions playing internationally than any other musical. The show is based on the songs of ABBA, a Swedish musical group from the 1970s and 1980s.

title: Workforce Intermediaries
description: Community colleges have captured the attention of a variety of leaders trying to develop solutions to the nation’s workforce challenges. Many note the importance of community colleges in training a highly skilled workforce that can contribute to a growing and globally competitive economy. However, the community college’s core competency of providing education, while necessary, is insufficient to the task of guiding workers in developing needed skills and translating those skills to meeting current demand in their local labor markets. This grant to Aspen Institute will provide research and analysis into the growing trend of community college and nonprofit partnerships that are addressing many of the challenges faced by low-income adults who need access to education with clear links to employment opportunities.

title: General Purposes
description: Community Building Mitrovica leads and supports a wide range of projects with a strong emphasis on the participation of people from all of the city’s ethnic groups into concrete activities and community development initiatives. The grantee’s activities during the grant period will include strengthening accountability and transparency of governmental decision-making through citizen-led monitoring activities, empowering young people and women to be active in the community and across ethnic divisions, implementing a large community infrastructure investment program, and strengthening communication across borders through media and cultural events. During 2012-2013, the grantee supported the further development of three independent organizations that grew out of its projects, conducted a range of educational programming in peacebuilding and human rights, organized the International Youth Conference of the Forum for Cities in Transition, and increased its leadership and management capacities.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to bridge divisions in the city of Mitrovica, Kosovo, by building economic, cultural, social, and political links across this divided community. Community Building Mitrovica, a nonprofit registered in 2003 and based in Mitrovica, leads and supports a wide range of projects with a strong emphasis on the participation of people from all of the city’s ethnic groups into concrete activities and community development initiatives. The grantee’s activities during the grant period will include promoting entrepreneurship and a supportive business environment for young people and women, engaging in conflict mediation and transitional justice initiatives, strengthening accountability and transparency of governmental decisionmaking through citizen-led monitoring activities, and building the capacity of civil society in the community. Additionally, the grantee will update its strategic plan and provide training opportunities for staff. During 2014-2015, the grantee developed a toolkit for citizen-led monitoring of local government based on its experience and strengthened the business skills of 106 women through targeted training.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to bridge divisions in the city of Mitrovica, Kosovo, by building economic, cultural, social, and political links across this divided community. Community Building Mitrovica, a nonprofit based in Mitrovica, leads and supports a wide range of projects with a strong emphasis on the participation of people from all of the city’s ethnic groups into concrete activities and community development initiatives. The grantee’s activities during the grant period will include strengthening accountability and transparency of governmental decisionmaking through citizen-led monitoring activities, empowering young people and women to be active in the community and across ethnic divisions, implementing a large community infrastructure investment program, and strengthening communication across borders through media and cultural events. The grantee will also strengthen the role of its board, ensure staff capacities through training and networking opportunities, and seek to diversify its funding base.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Youth Initiative for Human Rights - Bosnia
description: The program goal is to strengthen youth engagement and activism on issues of transitional justice and human rights promotion in Bosnia and Herzegovina. To this end, the Youth Initiative for Human Rights – Bosnia, a nongovernmental organization in Bosnia and Herzegovina, will organize networking, training, and educational activities designed to empower young people to be more involved in shaping how Bosnian society deals with the legacy of war, addresses ongoing human rights issues, and integrates into the wider Europe. During 2012-2013, the grantee organized trainings, summer camps, study trips, and events to mark important dates, such as the Srebrenica genocide and international human rights day, and supported youth groups to carry out projects in their communities. Registered in Bosnia in late 2009 and based in Sarajevo, the grantee was formerly the branch office of the Serbian Youth Initiative for Human Rights, a long-time Mott grantee.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Youth Initiative for Human Rights - Bosnia
description: The program goal is to strengthen youth engagement and activism on issues of transitional justice and human rights promotion in Bosnia and Herzegovina. The Youth Initiative for Human Rights – Bosnia, a nongovernmental organization in Bosnia and Herzegovina, will organize networking, training, and informal educational activities designed to empower young people to be more involved in shaping how Bosnian society deals with the legacy of war, addresses ongoing human rights issues, and integrates into the wider Europe. During 2014-2015, the grantee continued to develop interactive, innovative approaches to raising awareness among the general public and young people, in particular, about key human rights issues facing their society and communities. Using social media and face-to-face activities, the grantee supported young people to lead and carry out projects in their communities. The grantee also organized trainings, summer camps, study trips, and events to mark important dates, such as the Srebrenica genocide and international human rights day. Registered in Bosnia in late 2009 and based in Sarajevo, the grantee was formerly the branch office of the Serbian Youth Initiative for Human Rights, a long-time Mott grantee.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Youth Initiative for Human Rights - Bosnia
description: The program goal is to strengthen youth engagement and activism on issues of transitional justice and human rights promotion in Bosnia and Herzegovina. To this end, the Youth Initiative for Human Rights – Bosnia, a nongovernmental organization in Bosnia and Herzegovina, will organize networking, training, and educational activities designed to empower young people to be more involved in shaping how Bosnian society deals with the legacy of war, addresses ongoing human rights issues, and integrates into the wider Europe. During 2010-2011, the grantee implemented a wide range of new programming and strengthened management and staff capacities. The grantee continued to develop interactive, innovative, and dynamic approaches to raising awareness among the general public and young people, in particular, about key human rights issues facing their society and communities. Particular emphasis will be given to including young people from isolated communities in the grantee’s activities and networks. Registered in Bosnia in late 2009, the grantee was formerly the branch office of the Serbian Youth Initiative for Human Rights, a long-time Mott grantee.

title: Afterschool Communications Project
description: This grant will continue to support the Collaborative Communications Group to provide targeted communications, policy, and research support to the statewide afterschool networks and the afterschool field as part of the Expanded Learning and Afterschool Project. The Expanded Learning and Afterschool Project is a 50-state initiative to help schools and communities leverage the time beyond school to accelerate student achievement by sharing research on high quality afterschool and expanded learning; identifying best practices on afterschool programs; and sharing affordable, sustainable, and effective expanded learning approaches. As part of the Expanded Learning and Afterschool Project, this grant will continue to support the development of new communications strategies and policy approaches to advance the afterschool field.

title: Afterschool Communications Project
description: This grant will continue to support the Collaborative Communications Group to provide targeted communications, policy, and research support to the statewide afterschool networks and the afterschool field as part of the Expanded Learning and Afterschool Project. The Expanded Learning and Afterschool Project is a 50-state initiative to help schools and communities leverage the time beyond the school day to accelerate student achievement by sharing research on high quality afterschool and expanded learning; identifying best practices on afterschool programs; and sharing affordable, sustainable, and effective expanded learning approaches. As part of the expanded learning and afterschool project, this grant will continue to support the development of new communications strategies and policy approaches to advance the afterschool field.

title: Afterschool Education and Outreach Project
description: This grant will continue to support the Collaborative Communications Group’s Afterschool Education and Outreach Project to sustain the statewide afterschool networks and the afterschool field through education and outreach in policy development, communications, and research. To advance afterschool programs, this project will build bridges between federal, state, and local government and the afterschool field and will assist the networks as they navigate changes underway with federal education policy, state and federal budget challenges, and the longer school-day debate.
