title: Flint Journal Property Acquisition
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: The Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation was created in 2004 and is a supporting organization to the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, a public charity dedicated to urban revitalization, economic development, and job creation in downtown Flint, and a critical partner in a number of important downtown revitalization projects which have received Foundation support and are intended to combat urban decay. The grantee will use the grant to support the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation’s downtown revitalization efforts. Grant funds will be used to purchase the Flint Journal properties, encompassing approximately 5.5 acres and including a 125,000 square foot office building constructed in the 1920s; a 76,000 square foot processing plant constructed in 2003; and approximately 250 parking spaces. The acquisition of the Flint Journal property is strategic to the further revitalization of the downtown area. Approximately 25,000 square feet of the original building will be renovated to house the Michigan State University medical education and Masters of Public Health program. The remaining property will be used for other charitable purposes.

title: Organizational Review
description: During the course of several decades of declining enrollment in the Flint Community Schools, budget adjustments have been made, but there has been no formal evaluation of the personnel, support services, administration, and noninstructional service needs of the school district. The grantee will contract with Plante & Moran, which specializes in working with school districts on issues such as this, to evaluate the organizational structure and operations of the school district and identify cost reduction or containment opportunities, including staffing levels at its central office and schools; building utilization; utility costs; transportation, custodial, and food service operations; compensation, including salary and benefits; and outsourcing. Recommendations from the study will be shared with the Flint Board of Education, the community, and the Foundation.

title: Public Safety for Back to the Bricks
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to the Genesee Area Focus Fund will provide funds to support public safety enforcement and traffic patrolling at the Back to the Bricks festival in downtown Flint this August. Public safety policing is an essential component of the success of the festival, which is anticipated to attract 500,000 exhibitors and festival goers, and contributes to the local economy. In previous years, the city of Flint has traditionally absorbed the cost of police and traffic control services for the event; however, in its present financial circumstance, the city is unable to provide these services free of charge in 2012.

title: NEF Anniversary Project
description: The project aims to assist European decisionmakers to change gears and transform their policy thinking from crisis thinking to future thinking. To this end, the Network of European Foundations for Innovative Cooperation will initiate back-channel talks on the future of European integration. These talks will involve a group of 25 decisionmakers as well as 25 innovators from science, banking, economics, civil society, and the arts. The talks will explore how the European Union should differentiate itself in the future and will develop a priority list for European Union policymakers. Registered in 2002, the Network of European Foundations for Innovative Cooperation is an international organization that aims to strengthen the potential for cooperation between foundations at the European level. This project celebrates the network’s tenth anniversary.

title: Digital Learning in Afterschool
description: The Alliance for Excellent Education increases educational opportunities for young people through digital learning in afterschool programs. At the forefront of educational approaches, digital learning will play an increasingly important role in how students learn, and will enable afterschool programs to deliver new learning opportunities in the future. The grantee seeks to ensure that digital learning is effective, particularly for struggling secondary school students, and to support afterschool programs, school districts, and communities to provide their students with these beneficial experiences that help accelerate their academic achievement. Specifically, this project will include: 1) development of a research and policy brief that examines the role of digital learning in supporting disadvantaged students; and 2) dissemination of policy recommendations and best practices to the education and afterschool fields.

title: Digital Learning in Afterschool
description: This proposal will support the Alliance for Excellent Education to increase educational opportunities for young people through digital learning in afterschool programs. At the forefront of educational approaches, digital learning will play an increasingly important role in how students learn, and will enable afterschool programs to deliver new learning opportunities in the future. Through working with the statewide afterschool networks, the grantee seeks to increase the number of afterschool programs which utilize digital learning. Specifically, this project will include: 1) research to identify successful examples of digital learning and collaboration between in-school and afterschool programs; 2) development and dissemination of digital learning resources for the afterschool field; and 3) work with the statewide afterschool networks to develop policy and practice for digital learning in the afterschool setting.

title: Exploring Statewide Data Systems for 21st Century Community Learning Centers
description: This grant will continue to support the American Institutes for Research to conduct a review of statewide data and data systems, including the 21st Century Community Learning Centers programs. Specifically, the grantee will continue to: 1) identify successful state and local data systems; 2) conduct a meta-analysis of evaluation findings; and 3) identify best practices and promising data systems and procedures to share data. The overall goal of this project is to improve the availability and quality of afterschool data by promoting a better understanding of statewide afterschool data systems.

title: Exploring Statewide Data Systems for 21st Century Community Learning Centers
description: This grant will support the American Institutes for Research to conduct a review of statewide data and data systems for 21st Century Community Learning Centers programs. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) convene an advisory group; 2) conduct a review of the published literature on data use and collection in afterschool; 3) identify successful state and local data systems; and 4) identify best practices for policy development and procedures to share data. The overall goal of this project is to improve the availability and quality of afterschool data by promoting a better understanding of statewide afterschool data systems.

title: VISTA Project
description: This grant will allow the Afterschool Alliance to increase the quality and visibility of afterschool programs through building a network of AmeriCorps VISTAs skilled in afterschool issues. The VISTAs will work to enhance the capacity of the statewide afterschool networks and increase implementation of afterschool meals programs. Additionally, the grantee will expand the scope of the AmeriCorps VISTA program by hosting several additional VISTAs focused on STEM (science, technology, engineering, and math) learning opportunities within the afterschool field.

title: VISTA Project
description: This grant will allow the Afterschool Alliance to increase the quality and visibility of afterschool programs through the network-building efforts of AmeriCorps VISTA members skilled in afterschool issues. The VISTA members will work to enhance the capacity and effectiveness of statewide afterschool networks, increase implementation of the afterschool meals programs, and support STEM (science, technology, engineering, and math) learning opportunities within the afterschool field.

title: VISTA Project
description: This grant will allow the Afterschool Alliance to increase the quality and visibility of afterschool programs through the network building efforts of AmeriCorps VISTA members skilled in afterschool issues. The VISTA members will work to: 1) enhance the capacity of statewide afterschool networks; 2) increase implementation of the afterschool meals programs; 3) support STEM (science, technology, engineering, and math) learning opportunities within the afterschool field; and 4) establish strong links between community partners and afterschool or summer learning programs to increase access to high quality education, enrichment, and mentoring opportunities for young men of color as part of President Obama’s My Brother’s Keeper initiative.

title: VISTA Project
description: This grant will allow the Afterschool Alliance to increase the quality of afterschool programs through the network-building efforts of AmeriCorps VISTA members skilled in the issues relevant for children and families attending afterschool programs. The VISTA members will work to: 1) enhance the capacity of statewide afterschool networks; 2) increase implementation of the afterschool meals programs; 3) support STEM learning opportunities within the afterschool field; and 4) increase access to high quality education, enrichment, and mentoring opportunities for young men of color as part of the My Brother’s Keeper initiative.

title: VISTA Project
description: This grant will allow the Afterschool Alliance to partner with AmeriCorps VISTA to: 1) enhance the capacity of statewide afterschool networks; 2) increase utilization of the afterschool meals program; 3) support STEM learning opportunities within the afterschool field; and 4) increase access to high quality education, enrichment, and mentoring opportunities for young men of color.

title: VISTA Project
description: This grant will allow the Afterschool Alliance to partner with AmeriCorps VISTA to: 1) enhance the capacity of statewide afterschool networks; 2) increase utilization of the afterschool meals program; 3) support STEM learning opportunities within the afterschool field; and 4) increase access to high-quality education, enrichment, and mentoring opportunities for young people of color.

title: VISTA Project
description: This grant will allow the Afterschool Alliance to continue to build on two complementary initiatives that will generate additional support for afterschool programs at the federal, state, and local levels. The initiatives are: 1) coordinating an AmeriCorps VISTA effort to continue to build the capacity of the statewide afterschool networks; and 2) conducting election eve polling to learn about voters’ perceptions of and concerns regarding afterschool and expanded learning time.

title: Increasing Science, Technology, Engineering and Math in Afterschool
description: This grant will allow McLean Hospital to support the program in education, afterschool and resiliency to continue to serve as the lead technical assistance and assessment advisor for the statewide afterschool networks on science, technology, engineering, and math opportunities in afterschool programs. As part of a comprehensive partnership initiative with the Noyce Foundation, the program in education, afterschool and resiliency will: 1) provide technical assistance and training, along with the Afterschool Alliance; 2) coordinate the development of program and student assessment tools; and 3) conduct a multistate study to better assess program quality and the impact on students who participate in informal science programs. The overall goal of this partnership project is to increase the availability of high quality informal science education for students attending afterschool programs, and to increase the number of students who are interested in pursuing careers in the science, technology, engineering, and math fields.

title: Increasing Science, Technology, Engineering and Math in Afterschool
description: This grant will enable McLean Hospital to support the Program in Education, Afterschool and Resiliency to continue to serve as the lead assessment advisor for the statewide afterschool networks on STEM opportunities in afterschool programs. As part of a comprehensive partnership initiative with the Noyce Foundation, the Program in Education, Afterschool and Resiliency will: 1) conduct a qualitative and quantitative outcome assessment of 150 programs in ten states; 2) create a data system that can be accessed annually to provide information on STEM learning in afterschool programs; and 3) develop a summative report that can be distributed to policymakers, funders, and key stakeholders. The overall goal of this program is to increase the availability of high quality informal science education for students attending afterschool programs and to increase the number of students who are interested in pursuing careers in STEM fields.

title: Increasing Science, Technology, Engineering and Math in Afterschool
description: This grant will allow McLean Hospital to support the Program in Education, Afterschool and Resiliency to continue to serve as the lead assessment advisor for the statewide afterschool networks on STEM opportunities in afterschool programs. As part of a comprehensive partnership initiative with the Noyce Foundation, the Program in Education, Afterschool and Resiliency will: 1) continue the study of afterschool STEM programs in at least 11 states; 2) provide technical assistance to participating networks and programs in the areas of data collection and quality assessments; 3) incorporate student outcome measures that are performance-based into the study; and 4) continue to build the capacity of the statewide networks to collect afterschool and youth data.

title: Increasing Science, Technology, Engineering and Math in Afterschool
description: This grant will allow McLean Hospital to support the program in education, afterschool & resiliency to serve as a lead technical assistance advisor for the statewide afterschool networks on science, technology, engineering, and math opportunities in afterschool programs. The program in education, afterschool & resiliency will provide technical assistance, along with the Afterschool Alliance, as part of a comprehensive partnership initiative with the Noyce Foundation. The overall goal of this partnership project is to increase the availability of high quality, informal science education for students attending afterschool programs, and to increase the number of students who are interested in pursuing careers in the science, technology, engineering, and math fields.

title: Increasing Literacy Proficiency for the Hispanic Dual Language Learner
description: This grant will support the Massachusetts Afterschool Partnership to create a program that will become a national model to increase literacy proficiency for Latino English language learner students. Specifically, the Massachusetts Afterschool Partnership will: 1) create a literacy curriculum for use in afterschool and summer; 2) develop national policy recommendations for English language learner students; 3) conduct a data-driven analysis of the program model; and 4) design and promote a national best practices model. The overall goal of this project is to help close the educational achievement gap between lower income English language learner students and higher income English speaking peers.

title: Increasing Literacy Proficiency for the Hispanic Dual Language Learner
description: This grant will support the Massachusetts Afterschool Partnership to continue programs that will become a national model to increase literacy proficiency for Latino English Language Learner students. Specifically, the Massachusetts Afterschool Partnership will: 1) provide an afterschool and summer learning enrichment program for English Language Learner students; 2) conduct a data-driven analysis of the program model; 3) refine and promote a national “best practices” model; and 4) develop national policy recommendations to support English Language Learner students in afterschool programs. The overall goal of this project is to help close the educational achievement gap between lower income English Language Learner students and higher income English speaking peers.

title: Increasing Literacy Proficiency for the Hispanic Dual Language Learner
description: This grant will support Child Development for Kids, Inc., to develop a demonstration project to design and implement an afterschool literacy proficiency program for Dual Language Learner Hispanic students. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) develop a national demonstration project; 2) design a literacy curriculum for afterschool and summer; 3) promote common goals for increasing student proficiency in English Language Arts; and 4) collect and analyze program data to inform policy development. The overall goal of this project is to improve educational success for Hispanic children by reaching them during the critical hours after school.

title: Transition Support
description: This grant will provide funds to the Institute for Global Ethics for transition support following the sudden passing of the grantee’s founder. The grant increase will provide for an interim director to be hired and immediately evaluate and establish plans for the grantee’s sustainability.

title: Transition Support
description: This grant will provide funds to the Institute for Global Ethics for transition support following the sudden passing of the grantee’s founder and the subsequent time spent evaluating and establishing plans for the organization’s sustainability under an interim executive director. The grant will support the new president and CEO as he begins to lead the organization forward with a new strategic plan in place.

title: Transition Support
description: This grant will provide funds to the Institute for Global Ethics for transition support following the sudden passing of the organization’s founder. A temporary director or manager has been identified, will be hired, and will immediately evaluate and establish plans for the organization’s sustainability.

title: Real Estate Development Support Services
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will serve to increase the level of community and economic development capital available to Flint and Genesee County. Through its supporting organization, the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation will contract with the National Development Council to provide consulting services that assist local developers in accessing federal and state financing resources for community and economic development projects.

title: Real Estate Development Support Services
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This renewal grant will serve to increase the level of community and economic development capital available to Flint and Genesee County. With its supporting organization, the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation will contract with the National Development Council to provide consulting services that assist local developers in accessing federal and state financing resources for community and economic development projects. In partnership with its support organization, the grantee has played a critical role in leading and managing real estate and economic development revitalization projects in downtown Flint.

grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation

Through its supporting organization, the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation will contract with the National Development Council to provide consulting services that assist local developers in accessing financing resources for community and economic development projects through federal programs.

title: Special Edition on Poverty
grantee: Demos: A Network for Ideas and Action
description: Marking the 50th anniversary of the publication of “The Other America”, Michael Harrington’s influential book on poverty, Demos: A Network for Ideas and Action will publish a special issue of “The American Prospect” magazine that explores poverty in America with a view to stimulating discussion from diverse perspectives about the causes and conditions of poverty and putting forward new ideas and solutions.

title: National Workforce Commission Creation and Feasibility Study
description: This grant will provide partial support to the Bipartisan Policy Center to investigate through interviews, roundtable discussions, and policy research if conditions are favorable for launching a larger initiative to reformulate workforce development policy in the United States. Despite persistent high unemployment, the country continues to lack a coordinated workforce development system or even a consensus of who is responsible for training the nation’s workforce. The results from this effort will inform practitioners, policymakers, and funders on the potential ways for reforming and reformulating the myriad of programs that currently constitute our country’s investments in developing a skilled workforce.

title: Research and Writing on Organizing and Housing
description: The National Housing Institute is dedicated to fostering decent, affordable housing and a vibrant community for everyone. Through its magazine, “Shelterforce”, its Website www.nhi.org, and its blog, Rooflines, the grantee helps focus on high-impact housing and community development policies and practices. This grant will support in-depth reporting and publication of the community engagement and community development process at Harmony Oaks, a former public housing site in New Orleans, Louisiana.

title: EPA in the European System
description: The program goal is to strengthen the voice of civil society from Central and Eastern Europe on the European Union level. To this end, the Environmental Partnership Association, a network of the Environmental Partnership Foundations in six Central and Eastern European countries, will strengthen the collaboration among its members, develop working relationships with peer organizations on the regional and global levels, and strengthen its advocacy work on the European Union level in the areas of environment and civil society. The grantee’s mission is to organize and support the international cooperation of member organizations with the aim to strengthen the contributions of environmental organizations for the sustainable development of Europe. During the past three years, the grantee established its representative office in Brussels to enhance its communications and advocacy work on the European Union level and carried out a number of successful regional initiatives, including the Europe-wide Tree of the Year Award.

title: EPA in the European System
description: The program goal is to strengthen the voice of civil society in Central and Eastern Europe on the European Union level. To this end, the Environmental Partnership Association — a network of environmental foundations in five Central and Eastern European countries — will increase its capacity to interact with the European Union institutions, develop new partnerships with peer organizations on the European Union level, and explore various possibilities for developing a stronger future role for itself and its members on the European Union level. In addition, the grantee will promote and expand beyond its current member countries one of its environmental protection initiatives, the European Tree of the Year contest, to engage with like-minded organizations throughout Europe and strengthen its international outreach. Members of the network worked together informally from the early 1990s until 2004, when they officially established the grantee as an independent organization. The grantee’s mission is to organize and support the international cooperation of member organizations with the aim to strengthen the contributions of environmental organizations for the sustainable development of Europe. Over the years, the grantee has implemented various programs, including developing greenways and sustainable tourism and promoting alternative energy sources.

title: South-South Investment: Environmental Impacts in South America
description: Chinese investments in the economies of South America are much larger and more influential than most had previously acknowledged. The realization of their importance was highlighted by research that Tufts University published through this project. The project’s research also presented a compelling case for Chinese authorities to pay more attention to environmental standards in their investments outside China. This renewal grant will continue research on the impact of Chinese investments in the economies of South America, while also beginning research to address Brazilian investment impacts in neighboring countries.

title: China in Latin America: Environmental and Developmental Dimensions
description: In just over a decade, China has emerged as one of the most important trade and investment partners for Latin American nations. While there has been research on the economic impacts for developing countries from Chinese overseas investment, there has been relatively little attention to how this investment contributes to or impedes sustainable development in developing countries. Through this project, Tufts University researchers will track and analyze China’s investment activities in Latin America and its impact on sustainable development. In addition, the project will help to establish a working group to ensure that the research reaches local communities and policymakers.

title: Strengthening the Bread Houses Network in Bulgaria
description: The program goal is to strengthen the participation of marginalized groups and individuals in the lives of their communities throughout Bulgaria. To this end, the International Council for Cultural Centers, a Bulgaria-registered nonprofit, will expand and strengthen its network of bread houses in Bulgaria, increase the capacity of the local bread house coordinators to implement projects and engage marginalized groups, and explore the possibilities of turning bread houses into successful social enterprises. Bread houses are community centers that host bread baking and various other activities for groups of people of very diverse backgrounds, thus encouraging relationships across ethnic and religious origins and social status. The model has been successful in increasing the social capital in communities and strengthening civic spirit as well as increasing the skills, self-esteem, and employability of the participating individuals. Since its establishment in 2008, the grantee has been developing bread houses around the world, and now they exist in 12 countries.

title: Strengthening the Bread Houses Network in Bulgaria
description: The program goal is to strengthen the participation of marginalized groups and individuals in the lives of their communities throughout Bulgaria. To this end, the International Council for Cultural Centers will expand and strengthen its network of bread houses in Bulgaria, support the transformation of two bread houses into successful social enterprises, and develop a Web-based, practice-oriented training program for social entrepreneurs. Bread houses are community centers that host bread baking and various other activities for groups of people of very diverse backgrounds, thus encouraging relationships across ethnic and religious origins and social status. The model has been successful in increasing the social capital in communities and strengthening civic spirit as well as increasing the skills, self-esteem, and employability of the participating individuals. During the past grant period, the grantee improved the physical space, strengthened the team capacities, and expanded the programs and services in nine bread houses in eight of the largest cities in Bulgaria; successfully transformed two of the bread houses into self-sustainable social enterprises; and promoted the bread house model in nine new cities and towns. Since its establishment in 2008 in Sofia, Bulgaria, the grantee has been developing bread houses around the world, and now they exist in 18 countries.

title: Strengthening the Bread Houses Network in Bulgaria
description: Since its establishment in 2008 in Sofia, Bulgaria, the International Council for Cultural Centers has been developing bread houses around the world, and now they exist in 18 countries. Bread houses are community centers that host bread baking and various other activities for groups of people of very diverse backgrounds, thus encouraging relationships across ethnic and religious origins and social status. The grantee will expand and strengthen its network of bread houses in Bulgaria, expand its programs for refugee community inclusion through bread-making activities, support the transformation of five bread houses into successful social enterprises, and promote the bread houses model nationally and internationally. The program goal is to strengthen the participation of marginalized groups and individuals in the lives of their communities throughout Bulgaria. The model has been successful in increasing the social capital in communities; strengthening civic spirit; and increasing the skills, self-esteem, and employability of the participating individuals. During the past grant period, the grantee established two new bread houses, organized over 400 bread-making events with more than 4,500 participants, introduced a special program for refugee inclusion and involved 110 refugees, and increased its income from paid services threefold.

title: Strengthening the Bread Houses Network in Bulgaria
description: The program goal is to strengthen the participation of marginalized groups and individuals in their communities throughout Bulgaria. To this end, the International Council for Cultural Centers, a Bulgaria-registered nonprofit, will expand and strengthen its network of bread houses in Bulgaria, increase the capacity of the local bread house coordinators to implement projects and engage marginalized groups, and explore the possibilities of turning bread houses into successful social enterprises. Bread houses are community centers that host bread baking and various other activities for groups of people of very diverse backgrounds, thus encouraging relationships across ethnic and religious origins and social status. The model has been successful in increasing the social capital in communities and strengthening civic spirit as well as increasing the skills, self-esteem, and employability of the participating individuals. Since its establishment in 2008, the grantee has developed into a global network of active and committed volunteers who share the same vision of empowering people at the grassroots level using a combination of traditional and modern community development approaches. The grantee has been developing bread houses around the world since 2009, and now they exist in 12 countries.

title: International YouthBank Support Model
geographic_focus: Italy, Bulgaria, Montenegro, Ireland, Russia, Croatia, Romania, Georgia, Kosovo, Czech Republic, Moldova, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Turkey, Serbia, Belgium
description: The program goal is to increase youth involvement in local philanthropy development and civic action by strengthening the YouthBank movement in the Central and Eastern Europe and Russia region. YouthBank is a successful model for youth-led grantmaking and philanthropy. The Community Foundation for Northern Ireland will provide capacity-building services to national YouthBank movements in the region, facilitate dialogue and interaction among these movements, and support the institutionalization of YouthBank International as a support organization. Based in Belfast, the grantee has facilitated the growth and development of young people as fundraisers and grantmakers using the YouthBank model since 1999. In the past grant period, the grantee supported the development of YouthBanks in six new countries, developed Web-based learning resources, and organized a series of networking events for the national movements. Now, YouthBanks exist in 28 countries.

title: International YouthBank Support Model
description: The program goal is to increase youth involvement in local philanthropy development and civic action by strengthening the YouthBank movement in the Central and Eastern Europe region. YouthBank is a successful model for youth-led grantmaking and philanthropy. The Community Foundation for Northern Ireland will provide capacity building services to national YouthBank movements in the region, facilitate dialogue and interaction among these movements, and support the institutionalization of YouthBank International as a support organization. Based in Belfast, the grantee has facilitated the growth and development of young people as fundraisers and grantmakers using the YouthBank model since 1999 which now exist in 28 countries. During the past grant period, the grantee expanded the YouthBanks in four countries in the region, developed web-based learning resources, and organized a series of networking events for the national movements.

title: International YouthBank Support Model
geographic_focus: Italy, Serbia, Turkey, Ireland, Germany, Bulgaria, Moldova, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Russia, Belgium, Croatia, Romania, Georgia, Kosovo, Poland, Czech Republic, Montenegro
description: The program goal is to increase youth involvement in local philanthropy development and civic action by strengthening the YouthBank movement in the Central and Eastern Europe and Russia region. To this end, the Community Foundation for Northern Ireland will develop resource materials and advisory services for newly established YouthBank movements, facilitate dialogue and interaction among national YouthBank movements in the region, and explore various opportunities to develop a permanent support infrastructure for the YouthBank movement in the region and globally. The foundation has facilitated the growth and development of young people as fundraisers and grantmakers using the YouthBank model since 1999. Now YouthBanks exist in more than 25 countries.

title: Community Foundation Centennial
description: The 100th anniversary of the founding of the first community foundation in the United States in 1914 provides a unique opportunity for philanthropy to demonstrate critical leadership in recognition of this milestone. The Council on Foundations has been organizing and coordinating efforts to commemorate the community foundation field’s centennial. These include partnerships with colleague organizations and networks on projects such as What’s Next for Community Philanthropy and the book, “Here for Good, a Centennial Communications Toolkit”, the gathering and dissemination of a regular series of exemplary stories and case studies, a video contest, and other activities. This grant increase will allow the grantee to host 20 presenters and participants from around the globe at its upcoming fall conference for community foundations which will be the capstone event of the field’s centennial. The Council on Foundations is a national membership organization of close to 1,700 private foundations, community foundations, and corporate funders.

title: Community Foundation Centennial
description: The 100th anniversary of the founding of the first domestic community foundation in 1914 provides a unique opportunity for the field of philanthropy to demonstrate critical leadership in recognition of this milestone. The Council on Foundations will establish a special project office, which will be responsible for designing, implementing, coordinating, and supporting centennial activities to provide maximum benefit to the communities and to philanthropy. While planning is still in its early stages, anticipated centennial activities may include general promotion of community philanthropy, a global symposium of community foundations, an enhanced fall conference in 2014, the publication of a history of community foundations, and development of tools and resources that will guide community foundations into their second century. The Council on Foundations is a national membership organization of more than 1,700 private foundations, community foundations, and corporate funders.

title: Strengthening the Capacity of Youth to Protect and Restore Their Rights
grantee: Association of Ukrainian Human Rights Monitors on Law Enforcement
description: The program goal is to increase youth awareness of and engagement with the promotion and protection of human rights in Ukraine. To achieve this, the Association of Ukrainian Human Rights Monitors on Law Enforcement will educate young people about their rights with respect to treatment by state officials, including law enforcement, and engage young people in systematic efforts to assert civil control over the work of law enforcement agencies in Ukraine. In addition, the grantee will strengthen the capacity of nonprofits working with youth to promote and protect human rights. During 2012-2014, the grantee conducted in-depth workshops on key issues related to human rights abuses by law enforcement, provided a range of learning opportunities for young people, engaged young people in campaigns to monitor and document law enforcement performance and activities, and established a coalition of nonprofits working on civic oversight of police and other law enforcement agencies. Established in 2010 by former staff of the Human Rights Monitoring Department of the Ukrainian Ministry of Internal Affairs, the grantee’s mission is to develop effective means of civil control over Ukraine’s law enforcement agencies. Through its 16 offices nationwide, it works also to broker constructive relationships between these agencies and civil society organizations.

title: Strengthening the Capacity of Youth to Protect and Restore Their Rights
grantee: Association of Ukrainian Human Rights Monitors on Law Enforcement
description: The program goal is to increase youth awareness of and engagement with the promotion and protection of human rights in Ukraine. To achieve this, the Association of Ukrainian Human Rights Monitors on Law Enforcement will educate young people about their rights with respect to treatment by state law enforcement agencies and engage them in systematic efforts to assert civil control over these agencies’ work. In addition, the grantee will strengthen the capacity of nonprofits working with youth to promote and protect human rights. During 2014-2016, the grantee’s systematic monitoring of police performance was used to refine practice within the reformed police service. It also produced an array of online, offline, and mobile resources providing advice to citizens on how to interact with law enforcement agencies. Established in 2010 by former staff of the Human Rights Monitoring Department of the Ukrainian Ministry of Internal Affairs, the grantee’s mission is to develop effective means of civil control over and cooperation with Ukraine’s law enforcement agencies.

title: Strengthening the Capacity of Youth to Protect and Restore Their Rights
grantee: Association of Ukrainian Human Rights Monitors on Law Enforcement
description: The program goal is to build the capacity of youth-oriented, nongovernmental organizations to participate in broad-based efforts to promote respect for rights and elimination of abuses. To achieve this, the Association of Ukrainian Human Rights Monitors on Law Enforcement will engage young people in a systematic effort to assert civil control over the work of law enforcement agencies in Ukraine. In addition, through public campaigns and further training of local youth monitors, the grantee will develop networks of existing regional and national youth organizations to further advance the cause of preventing abuse of rights. Established in 2010 by former staff of the Human Rights Monitoring Department of the Ukrainian Ministry of Internal Affairs, the grantee’s mission is to develop effective means of civil control over Ukraine’s law enforcement agencies. Through its 16 offices nationwide, it also works to broker constructive relationships between these agencies and civil society organizations.

title: Security Assessment
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to the Flint Cultural Center Corporation will support a campus-wide security assessment. Utilizing the experience and expertise of an outside consultant, individual assessments will be done for each building on the cultural center campus, including Flint Institute of Arts, Flint Institute of Music, Flint Youth Theatre, Longway Planetarium, Sloan Museum, Buick Automotive Gallery, Whiting Auditorium, and Flint Public Library. The results of this study will be used by each individual organization to update and improve their security strategies and will also identify ways that the organizations can work together to improve the overall security on the campus.

title: Property Management Software for Land Banks
description: This grant will enable the Genesee County Land Bank Authority to improve its property management function through the purchase and installation of customized property management software. Utilization of the software will enable the grantee to increase the efficiency and effectiveness of its property management decisionmaking. The grantee developed and operates one of the most successful programs to reclaim vacant and abandoned property in the nation. Since its inception, it has acquired more than 13,500 properties through the tax foreclosure process and currently manages an inventory of 8,100 properties.

title: C. S. Mott Foundation Community Philanthropy Chair
description: This is the second in a series of grants that will support the establishment of an endowed faculty chair at the Indiana University School of Philanthropy. A C. S. Mott Foundation Community Philanthropy Chair will be one of 20 planned endowed chairs at this school. Such a faculty position will enable Indiana University to improve community philanthropy by deepening the knowledge base needed to develop more informed decisionmaking toward the aggregation of resources, capacities, and connections to produce better outcomes in local communities. The university will match the earnings from the endowment to fund the chair. This is one of several projects linked with the 2014 centennial of community foundations highlighting the Mott Foundation’s legacy in this area. Indiana University is a major multicampus public research institution, grounded in the liberal arts and sciences, and a world leader in professional, medical, and technological education.

title: C. S. Mott Foundation Chair on Community Foundations
description: This is the third in a series of grants that will support the establishment of an endowed faculty chair at Indiana University. A C. S. Mott Foundation Chair on Community Foundations will be one of 20 planned endowed chairs at this school. Such a faculty position will enable Indiana University to improve community philanthropy by deepening the knowledge base needed to develop more informed decisionmaking toward the aggregation of resources, capacities, and connections to produce better outcomes in local communities. The university will match the earnings from the endowment to fund the chair. This is one of several projects linked with the 2014 centennial of community foundations highlighting the Mott Foundation’s legacy in this area. Indiana University is a major multicampus public research institution, grounded in the liberal arts and sciences, and a world leader in professional, medical, and technological education.

title: C.S. Mott Foundation Chair on Community Foundations
description: This is the fourth and final in a series of grants that supports the establishment of an endowed faculty chair at Indiana University’s Lilly Family School of Philanthropy. With this grant increase, the C. S. Mott Foundation Chair on Community Foundations endowment will be fully funded, with the Foundation’s total contribution of $1.5 million unlocking an equivalent match from Indiana University to bring the endowment to its minimum initial $3 million level as stipulated by the university. This will be one of 20 planned endowed chairs at this school. This faculty position will enable Indiana University to deepen the knowledge base about community foundations that will in turn serve to produce better outcomes in local communities. Indiana University is a major multicampus public research institution, grounded in the liberal arts and sciences, and a world leader in professional, medical, and technological education.

title: C. S. Mott Foundation Community Philanthropy Chair
description: This grant will support the establishment of an endowed faculty chair at the Indiana University School of Philanthropy. A C. S. Mott Foundation Community Philanthropy Chair will be one of 20 planned endowed chairs at this school. Such a faculty position will enable Indiana University to improve community philanthropy by deepening the knowledge base needed to develop more informed decisionmaking toward the aggregation of resources, capacities, and connections to produce better outcomes in local communities. The university will match the earnings from the endowment to fund the chair. This is one of several projects linked with the 2014 centennial of community foundations highlighting the Mott Foundation’s legacy in this area. Indiana University is a major multicampus public research institution, grounded in the liberal arts and sciences, and a world leader in professional, medical, and technological education.

title: BRICS Action Project
description: ActionAid USA addresses key policies related to poverty reduction and sustainable development globally. It is a member of ActionAid International, which has member organizations that are working in more than 40 countries to fight poverty. Through this project, the grantee will continue to press for increased civil society engagement at meetings of the BRICS grouping (Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa), as well as advocate for transparency, environmental, and social standards for BRICS institutions. Over the last grant period, the grantee launched a civil society network to build awareness in BRICS countries and provide an analysis of these countries’ investments in other developing countries. This work led to an important conference that created a rare opportunity for the civil society network and key BRICS governments to discuss environmental and social impacts of their investments.

title: BRICS Action Project
description: ActionAid USA addresses key policies related to poverty reduction and sustainable development globally. It is part of ActionAid International, which has member organizations that are working in more than 40 countries to fight poverty. Through this project, ActionAid USA will work to increase civil society presence and leadership at leaders’ meetings and parallel events of BRICS grouping (Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa); ensure that nongovernmental organizations from BRICS countries play a greater role in advocacy at the Group of 20 and United Nations climate negotiations; and increase advocacy in BRICS countries on their governments’ policies related to sustainable development, international economic governance, and development finance. This grant will focus on undertaking research, developing a policy agenda, creating education and communication tools, and developing an international nongovernmental organization network.

title: Monitoring BNDES Investments in Energy and Infrastructure
description: National development banks, such as those in Brazil and China, are increasingly dominating development finance in energy and infrastructure in South America. To carry forward lessons learned from work on international financial institutions and build capacity, deeper understanding of standards, as well as cooperation between civil society in South America and China, are important. This grant increase will support iBase to produce and disseminate two reports on Chinese and Brazilian development finance standards, as well as participate in convenings with global and Chinese civil society.

title: Monitoring BNDES Investments in Energy and Infrastructure
description: This grant will support iBase, the Brazilian Institute of Social and Economic Analysis, to work with other nongovernmental groups and communities in South America affected by the operations of the Brazilian Development Bank. Work will focus on capacity building and joint strategy development to improve transparency and strengthen social and environmental safeguards, particularly as they apply to energy and infrastructure development in Brazil and the region.

title: Monitoring BNDES Investments in Energy and Infrastructure
description: iBase works with nongovernmental groups and communities in South America to identify and monitor the impacts of Brazilian Development Bank energy and infrastructure finance. This grant renewal will enable the grantee to continue to monitor and analyze the Brazilian Development Bank, as well as increasing investments from Chinese and new international financial institutions.

title: Monitoring BNDES Investments in Energy and Infrastructure
description: This grant will support a leading civil society organization, iBase (Brazilian Institute of Social and Economic Analysis) to work with other nongovernmental groups and communities in South America affected by the operations of the Brazilian Development Bank. Work will focus on capacity building and joint strategy development to improve transparency and strengthen social and environmental safeguards at the bank. Special attention will be given to energy and infrastructure investments in the greater Amazon rainforest and other ecologically sensitive regions.

title: Heroes Gala Honoring Lloyd Reuss
description: This grant will provide funds to the Detroit Symphony Orchestra for its second annual Heroes Gala. This year, Lloyd Reuss will be honored for his exemplary leadership and support of the Detroit Symphony Orchestra and for his philanthropic activities in Detroit.

title: Wildlife Trade Programme
description: The Alliance of Religions and Conservation and its partners will work to address and positively impact biodiversity conservation. Key to this will be engaging the world’s faith leaders to promote the conservation of biodiversity, climate change resilience, and sustainable and spiritually principled living. These partnerships will work to raise awareness and create messaging and activities to help refute the practices of illegal killing, trade, and use of endangered wildlife in China, India, Indonesia, and Africa.

title: Wildlife Trade Programme
description: The Alliance of Religions and Conservation and the World Wildlife Fund – United States will partner to address and positively impact biodiversity conservation. Key to this will be engaging the world’s faith leaders to promote the conservation of biodiversity, climate change resilience, and sustainable and spiritually principled living. These partnerships will work to raise awareness and create messaging and activities to help refute the practices of illegal killing, trade, and use of endangered wildlife in China, India, Indonesia, and Africa.

title: Model Transit Project
description: Founded in 1970, the Ecology Center is a national environmental organization that is based in Michigan. The grantee seeks to encourage energy efficiencies as a way to address urban environmental impacts while improving the quality of life for families. With prior Mott support, the grantee sought to reduce energy use by improving public transportation options in Washtenaw County. With this grant increase, the grantee will research how state and municipal energy policies could help reduce carbon pollution and lower heating expenses for low-income households.

title: Model Transit Project
description: Founded in 1970, the Ecology Center is a national environmental organization that is based in Michigan. With prior Mott support, the grantee sought to improve public transportation options in southeast Michigan and explore related opportunities to reduce energy costs for low-income families across the state. With this grant, the grantee will engage its partners to inform how Washtenaw County implements its new transit plan aimed at improving residents’ low-cost, environmentally friendly options for accessing jobs, education, healthcare services, and recreational opportunities.

title: Model Transit Project
description: Founded in 1970, the Ecology Center is a national environmental organization that has maintained a special focus on its home region in southeast Michigan. With this grant, the grantee will contribute to the refinement and implementation of a countywide public transportation system in Washtenaw County. Building on significant public input to date, the grantee will help ensure the transit plan moves forward in a way that serves the needs of all residents. The grantee will also leverage lessons learned from this process to advance a comprehensive regional transportation solution in southeast Michigan, as well as informing transportation policies at the state level.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen active civic participation in public policy development and implementation in Bulgaria. To this end, the Institute for Public Environment Development will monitor government policies and practices and advocate for greater transparency and accountability, produce credible data and analyses on the implementation of key government policies and programs, and promote transparency and ethical standards during elections. In addition, the grantee will strengthen its own institutional capacity and financial sustainability. The grantee was established in 2003 with the mission to promote civic participation and democratic accountability in public institutions in Bulgaria. The grantee is based in Sofia, Bulgaria.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen active civic participation in public policy development and implementation in Bulgaria. To this end, the Institute for Public Environment Development will monitor government policies and practices and advocate for greater transparency and accountability, produce credible data and analyses on the implementation of key government policies and programs, promote effective public policies, and advocate for greater access for citizens to public information. In addition, the grantee will strengthen its own institutional capacity and financial sustainability. The grantee was established in 2003 with the mission to promote civic participation and democratic accountability in public institutions in Bulgaria. During the past grant period, the grantee provided technical assistance to a number of public institutions to open large data sets to the public; trained nonprofits and journalists to process, analyze, and visualize open data; and monitored the implementation of various public policies and published its analyses in various media. The grantee is based in Sofia, Bulgaria.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen active civic participation in public policy development and implementation in Bulgaria. To this end, the Institute for Public Environment Development will build new tools for public participation based on modern information and communication technologies, increase the knowledge and capacity of nonprofits to use these tools, and strengthen the interaction between the nonprofit and technology communities. In addition, the grantee will monitor government policies and practices and advocate for greater transparency and accountability. Also, the grantee will educate young voters and promote transparency and ethical standards during elections. Established in 2003 with the mission to promote civic participation and democratic accountability in public institutions in Bulgaria, the grantee has worked successfully on developing digital tools for e-government in Bulgaria, increasing public access to key government data, monitoring the implementation of various public policies, monitoring elections, and participating in various nonprofit coalitions tackling corruption and abuse of power by public institutions and corporations.

title: INSPIRE - Initiative for Strategic Philanthropy and Intelligent Resources
geographic_focus: Romania, Slovakia, Ukraine, Czech Republic, Bulgaria, Turkey
description: The program goal is to strengthen individual and institutional philanthropy in the Central and Eastern Europe and Russia region. To this end, the Association for Community Relations will continue to develop and manage INSPIRE – Initiative for Strategic Philanthropy and Intelligent Resources. More specifically, the grantee, in cooperation with other capacity building providers from Western Europe, will recruit and train philanthropy development practitioners to become philanthropy advisors working directly with individual philanthropists and foundations to improve their giving practices. In addition, the grantee will facilitate networking and exchange among the program participants. The grantee will also pilot workshops for groups of young philanthropists in Bulgaria and Romania who want to develop their practice in strategic philanthropy. Over the past two years, the grantee developed a comprehensive set of training materials and tools, trained 28 philanthropy advisors from ten countries, and supported exchange and networking among the trainees. Established in 2001, the Association for Community Relations primarily promotes and develops philanthropy in Romania. Over the past several years, it expanded its international activities and partnerships in the Central and Eastern Europe and Russia region.

title: INSPIRE - Initiative for Strategic Philanthropy and Intelligent Resources
description: The program goal is to strengthen individual and institutional philanthropy in the Central and Eastern Europe region. To this end, the Association for Community Relations will continue to develop and manage INSPIRE – Initiative for Strategic Philanthropy and Intelligent Resources. More specifically, the grantee, in cooperation with other capacity building providers from Western Europe, will recruit and train 30 philanthropy development practitioners to become philanthropy advisors working directly with individual philanthropists and foundations to improve their giving practices. In addition, the grantee will facilitate networking and exchange among the program participants, explore opportunities for institutionalizing this network as an independent organization, and develop and publicize a series of learning resources on strategic philanthropy and social entrepreneurship. In the past two years, the grantee developed a comprehensive set of training materials and tools, trained 18 philanthropy advisors from eight countries, supported exchange and networking among the trainees, and trained 20 community foundations from Poland and Ukraine in providing advice on strategic philanthropy to their donors. The grantee is based in Cluj-Napoca, Romania.

title: INSPIRE - Initiative for Strategic Philanthropy and Intelligent Resources
grantee: Association for the Practice of Transformation
geographic_focus: Czech Republic, Bulgaria, Romania, Turkey, Slovakia, Ukraine
description: The program goal is to strengthen individual and institutional philanthropy in the Central and Eastern Europe region. To this end, the Association for the Practice of Transformation will continue to develop and manage INSPIRE – Initiative for Strategic Philanthropy and Intelligent Resources. More specifically, the grantee will develop and deliver a philanthropy leadership program to 10 to 14 philanthropy development practitioners. In addition, the grantee will facilitate networking and exchange among the program participants, develop and publicize a series of resources on innovative practices in strategic philanthropy, and strengthen the contribution of philanthropy development organizations in the region to global conversations and initiatives. In the past two years, the grantee trained 30 philanthropy advisers from six countries, strengthened and enlarged the INSPIRE – Initiative for Strategic Philanthropy and Intelligent Resources network, and supported exchange and learning among network members. The grantee is based in Brasov, Romania.

title: INSPIRE - Initiative for Strategic Philanthropy and Intelligent Resources
geographic_focus: Romania, Czech Republic, Ukraine, Bulgaria, Slovakia, Turkey
description: The program goal is to strengthen individual and institutional philanthropy in the Central and Eastern Europe and Russia region. To this end, the Association for Community Relations will establish INSPIRE – Initiative for Strategic Philanthropy and Intelligent Resources. More specifically, the grantee, in cooperation with other capacity building providers from Western Europe, will recruit and train philanthropy development practitioners to become philanthropy advisors — the first in the region — working directly with individual philanthropists and foundations to improve their giving practices. In the first phase, the initiative will include participants from Bulgaria, Romania, Turkey, and Ukraine and later will expand in Central and Southeast Europe. The initiative is building on a past training program for strengthening the skills of community foundation practitioners to work with individual donors supported by Mott through a grant to the Community Foundation Network (United Kingdom) in 2009-2011.

title: Flint Health and Wellness District
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will provide partial support for the redevelopment of the Flint Journal properties and surrounding area, a $31.8 million project that will create a health, education, and wellness district in downtown Flint. The project includes three major components: 1) renovation of the former Flint Journal headquarters building into office space for the new Michigan State University Flint Public Health and Medical Campus; 2) reuse of the Flint Journal printing press building as the new home of the Flint Farmer’s Market; and 3) demolition of the Genesee Towers building and creation of an urban park space. The project will support the revitalization of downtown Flint and elimination of blight, and will directly benefit city residents, especially low-income residents, by making fresh food and healthcare options more accessible. The Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation receives and administers funds for charitable purposes and for the public welfare of Genesee County, Michigan, including support for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation.

title: Flint Health and Wellness District
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will fund predevelopment expenses related to the redevelopment of the Flint Journal properties and surrounding area, a $32 million project that will create a health, education, and wellness district in downtown Flint. The project includes three major components: 1) renovation of the former Flint Journal headquarters building into office space for the new Michigan State University Flint Public Health and Medical Campus; 2) reuse of the Flint Journal printing press building as the new home of the Flint Farmer’s Market; and 3) demolition of the Genesee Towers building and creation of an urban park space. The project is in keeping with recommendations laid out in Sasaki and Associate’s master plan for downtown Flint, and its subsequent site plan for the project area. The Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation receives and administers funds for charitable purposes and for the public welfare of Genesee County, Michigan, including support for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation.

title: Flint Public Health and Medical Campus Endowment
description: Founded in 1855, Michigan State University is one of the top research universities in the world. During the grant period, the grantee will realize its goal of moving its public health program to Flint, which will become one of two flagship campuses for Michigan State University’s College of Human Medicine. The Program in Public Health is primarily online, but will support up to 500 students working on their masters of public health degree, seven research-intensive faculty who will deliver significant National Institute of Health funding, and several core medical education faculty. Research topics for the public health program have been determined based on community need and involvement, and the program is designed to be deeply embedded in the local community with positive community outcomes as a stated goal. Endowment funding will support the college’s establishment of public health research programs in Flint and support core research faculty involved in the public health program.

title: Flint Public Health and Medical Campus Endowment
description: Founded in 1855, Michigan State University is one of the top research universities in the world today. During the grant period, Michigan State University will realize its goal of moving its public health program to the Flint campus, which is one of two flagship campuses for Michigan State University’s College of Human Medicine. The Program in Public Health is primarily online, but will support up to 500 students working on their Masters of Public Health degree, seven research-intensive faculty who will deliver significant National Institute of Health funding, and several core medical education faculty. Research topics for the public health program have been determined based on community need and involvement, and the program is designed to be deeply embedded in the local community with positive community outcomes as a stated goal. Endowment funding will support the core research faculty involved in the public health program.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen active civic participation on the local and national levels in Romania. To this end, the Resource Center for Public Participation will build the capacity of nongovernmental organizations and civic groups to participate effectively in decisionmaking, monitor key public institutions and advocate for greater transparency and responsiveness to citizens’ voices, and promote civic participation as a key element of a functioning democracy. The grantee’s mission is to support public participation in policymaking and decision making and to promote greater transparency and accountability of public institutions. During the previous grant period, the grantee built the capacity of over 30 nonprofit organizations, civic groups, and individual leaders to advocate on a wide variety of issues of public interest; facilitated nonprofit coalitions to engage in policy discussions with the government on the local and national levels; and advocated for transparency of the decisionmaking processes in the public sector. The center is based in Bucharest, Romania.
