title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen active civic participation on the local and national levels in Romania. To this end, the Resource Center for Public Participation will build the capacity of nongovernmental organizations and civic groups to participate effectively in decisionmaking, monitor key public institutions and advocate for greater transparency and responsiveness to citizens’ voices, and promote civic participation as a key element of a functioning democracy. The grantee was established in 2006 as a successor to the civil society program of the National Democratic Institute. The grantee’s mission is to support public participation in policymaking and decisionmaking and to promote greater transparency and accountability of the public institutions. In the past six years, the grantee pioneered and developed community organizing in Romania. In addition, the grantee has a strong track record in developing and implementing programs that address issues of corruption and inefficiency in the public sector. The grantee is based in Bucharest, Romania.

title: Alabama Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant to Auburn University will support the development of the Alabama Statewide Afterschool Network to continue to build an afterschool and summer learning system that improves outcomes for children and youth through school-based or school-linked afterschool programs. Over the next three years, the network will support the development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) developing both a marketing and public awareness strategy for the Alabama Afterschool Community Network and afterschool programs; 2) mapping the existing landscape of afterschool/summer programs and STEM (science, technology, engineering, and math) efforts in Alabama; and 3) hosting regional forums focused on quality standards, professional development, and STEM implementation in support of career and workforce development.

title: Alabama Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Auburn University, which coordinates the Alabama Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) creating research-based reports to educate key stakeholders on the importance of afterschool programs; 2) developing a comprehensive plan to increase resources for afterschool programs and the Alabama Statewide Afterschool Network; 3) enhancing the mapping of afterschool and child care centers programs across the state; and 4) participating in the development and distribution of new afterschool program content in collaboration with the Foundation’s thematic partners.

title: Alabama Statewide Afterschool Network
description: Auburn University seeks to develop a statewide afterschool network to better address the needs of children, youth, and families during afterschool hours in Alabama. To improve the quality and availability of afterschool programs in Alabama, Auburn University’s Truman Pierce Institute at the College of Education will create a network of youth-serving organizations, state agencies, and other key stakeholders, including the Alabama Community Education Association.

title: Community Foundation Global Online Atlas
description: This grant supports the creation of the first comprehensive atlas of the international community foundation movement. As part of its contribution to the 100th anniversary of the community foundation field in 2014, the Cleveland Foundation is partnering with the Foundation Center, the Global Fund for Community Foundations, the Worldwide Initiatives for Grantmaker Support, and several data and communications specialists to develop a freely accessible, international online platform of information about community foundations worldwide. Through extensive surveying and research, data is being collected, interpreted, and field-tested. Besides data, the atlas will tell the stories of community foundations around the world through rich and compelling narratives and photos. This grant increase will support activities related to boosting the survey response rate from underrepresented regions around the world and subsequent additional analysis and writing. Founded in 1914, the Cleveland Foundation is the nation’s oldest community foundation.

title: Online Global Community Philanthropy Information Resources
description: The project goal is to create an online, global platform for the community philanthropy field to be able to network and share tools, resources, and knowledge. In 2014, the Cleveland Foundation launched the Community Foundation Atlas, which has provided directory information for over 1,800 community foundations worldwide as well as impact stories and research on community foundation characteristics. The Foundation Center will upgrade the atlas through an iterative process, engaging the field in a series of meetings and workshops held around the world. The information gathered will be used to draft a research paper that will result in the creation of necessary tools and resources for the online platform. As the project progresses, the Foundation Center will continue to engage the field and update and maintain a worldwide community foundation directory. Established in 1956, the Foundation Center is dedicated to fostering public understanding of the foundation field by collecting, organizing, analyzing and disseminating information on foundations, corporate giving, and related subjects.

title: Community Foundation Global Online Atlas
description: This grant will support the creation of the first comprehensive atlas of the international community foundation movement. As part of its contribution to the 100th anniversary of the community foundation field in 2014, the Cleveland Foundation will partner with the Foundation Center, the Global Fund for Community Foundations, the Worldwide Initiatives for Grantmaker Support, and several data and communications specialists to develop a freely accessible, international online platform of information about community foundations worldwide. The atlas will build a sense of community among community philanthropists around the globe through storytelling, data sharing, and dialogue. Through extensive surveying and research, data will be collected, interpreted, and field-tested. Besides data, the atlas will tell the stories of community foundations around the world through rich and compelling narratives and photos. An interactive wiki will also be created. Founded in 1914, the Cleveland Foundation is the nation’s oldest community foundation.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to support community- and national-level civic engagement in the promotion and protection of human and minority rights in Turkey. Established in 2007, the Hrant Dink Foundation has become an important proponent of civil society. The grantee focuses on strengthening the culture of dialogue, empathy, and peace in Turkey through a range of activities, including conducting and commissioning research; publishing books and reports; gathering and sharing documentation of the past; organizing summer schools and other educational activities; organizing film, music, literature, and other festivals; and providing grants and fellowships. During 2013-2014, the grantee launched a series of new projects to support dialogue and normalization of relations between Turkey and Armenia, including a small-grants program and travel stipends and fellowships for journalists and other professionals. In addition, the grantee successfully raised funds for the renovation costs of a new office building that provides it with greater capacity to organize public events and educational activities. Through fundraising campaigns, the grantee attracted donations from individuals and businesses in Turkey and abroad. The grantee also made progress in consolidating its work around core program areas and strengthening its management and operational capacities for larger-scale programming. The grantee is based in Istanbul.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to support community- and national-level civic engagement in the promotion and protection of human and minority rights in Turkey. Established in 2007, the Hrant Dink Foundation has become an important proponent of civil society. During the grant period, the grantee will focus on strengthening the culture of dialogue, empathy, and peace in Turkey through a range of activities, including conducting and commissioning research; publishing books and reports; gathering and sharing documentation of the past; organizing summer schools and other educational activities; organizing film, music, literature, and other festivals; and providing grants and fellowships. During 2015-2017, the grantee moved into a new building, which allowed it to expand its programming and engage wider and more diverse audiences. The grantee also significantly expanded and made more accessible its library and archive and published 12 books and a variety of reports. The grantee also made progress in consolidating its work around core program areas and strengthening its management and operational capacities for larger-scale programming. The grantee is based in Istanbul.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to support community- and national-level civic engagement in the promotion and protection of human and minority rights in Turkey. Established in 2007 following the assassination of Hrant Dink, a leading Armenian journalist and human rights activist, the Hrant Dink Foundation has become an important proponent of civil society. The grantee focuses on strengthening the culture of dialogue, empathy, and peace in Turkey through a range of activities, including conducting and commissioning research; publishing books and reports; gathering and sharing documentation of the past; organizing summer schools and other educational activities; organizing film, music, literature, and other festivals; and giving awards that recognize the grantee’s core values. Building on five years of successful but rapid growth, the grantee will consolidate its work around core program areas and strengthen management and operational capacities for more efficient and effective programming that strengthens democratic values in Turkey. A key strategic goal for the grantee over the next two years is to further expand both the number and diversity of people it reaches. The grantee is based in Istanbul.

title: Michigan Benefits Access Initiative
description: The Michigan Benefits Access Initiative, a project of the Michigan Association of United Ways, was created to connect a greater number of families in Michigan to a range of public benefits that help promote household economic stability. Led by a partnership between the state of Michigan, foundations, and local nonprofit organizations, the initiative couples extensive outreach efforts with technology in order to help more families who may be eligible for benefits access them. This one-time grant will support the initiative’s technology component. When completed, the technology will fully bundle all key benefits and allow applicant/client documentation upload capability so that applications for benefits will not only be provided at human services agencies, but also at community action agencies, homeless shelters, health clinics, learning centers, and other neighborhood locations.

title: Advice Office Programme
description: The Rural Legal Trust was established in 2000 to provide legal services to farmworkers, farm dwellers, and the rural poor in South Africa whose rights were being violated. It works in the Free State, Mpumalanga, North West, and Northern Cape provinces. Past support assisted the grantee to train and mentor community-based paralegals and farmworker representatives on various aspects of the law and on topics related to the provision of basic services to poor people. The topics covered included mediation, opening files for clients, and procedures to follow when dealing with the eviction of people from farms. This grant will assist the Rural Legal Trust to continue to train, mentor, and support paralegals in community advice offices and farmworker representatives that assist farming communities when their rights are violated. It will also establish a Web-based case management system to log cases from farmworkers and other clients that will enable a more effective resolution of cases.

title: Advice Office Programme
description: The Rural Legal Trust was established in 2000 to provide legal services to farmworkers, farmdwellers, and the rural poor in South Africa whose rights were being violated. It works in the Free State, Mpumalanga, North West, and Northern Cape provinces. Past support assisted the grantee to train and mentor community-based paralegals and farmworker representatives on various aspects of the law and on topics related to the provision of basic services to poor people. The topics covered included mediation, opening files for clients, and procedures to follow when dealing with the eviction of people from farms. This grant increase will assist the grantee to continue to train, mentor, and support paralegals in community advice offices and farmworker representatives that assist farming communities when their rights are violated. It will also enhance a Web-based case management system to log cases from farmworkers and other clients that will allow for a more effective resolution of cases. This grant increase has been made possible by a partnership with Atlantic Philanthropies in support of the community advice office sector.

title: Advice Office Programme
description: Rural Legal Trust was established in 2000 to provide legal services to farmworkers, farm dwellers, and the rural poor in South Africa whose rights were being violated. It works in the Free State, Gauteng, Mpumalanga, North West, and Northern Cape provinces. Past support assisted the grantee with efforts to train and mentor community-based paralegals and farmworker representatives on various aspects of the law and on topics related to the provision of basic services to poor people. The topics covered include mediation, opening files for clients, fundraising, and procedures to follow when dealing with the eviction of people from farms. The grantee also developed a case management system to be used by community advice offices to capture cases they deal with and to develop a database. This grant will continue to support the grantee to assist community advice offices and farmworker representatives in their efforts to improve the living and working conditions of people on farms.

title: Advice Office Programme
description: The Rural Legal Trust provides legal services to farmworkers, farm dwellers, and poor people in rural communities. Established in 2000 to work with rural farm communities in the Eastern Cape, Northern Cape, North West, Mpumalanga, and Gauteng provinces in South Africa. Past support enabled the grantee to work with community advice offices and farmworker representatives on issues related to farmworker rights. This included providing training on topics such as mediation, fundraising, and case management. The grantee produced informational materials that can be used by farmworkers to defend themselves against unfair labor practices and other human rights violations. This grant will allow continuing support and training of paralegals and farmworker representatives. It will also support efforts to bring together networks of farm committees to share experiences, connect with other structures that support farmworker communities, and uphold their basic human rights.

title: Advice Office Programme
description: The Rural Legal Trust was established in 2000 to provide legal services to farm dwellers and the rural poor in South Africa whose rights were being violated. It seeks to foster collaboration between communities and the government through dialogue and improved engagements. It works with other nonprofits in rendering its services, including advice offices that serve farming communities. This grant will support the grantee to train and mentor community-based paralegals that work in advice offices on various aspects of the law and on topics related to the provision of basic services to poor people. The topics that will be covered include fundraising, mediation, opening files for clients, and procedures to follow when dealing with the eviction of people from farms. Other activities will include establishing a research unit and publishing regularly on issues that affect the communities served, and conducting awareness-raising workshops in rural areas related to the provision of basic services and people’s rights and responsibilities.

title: Change4ever Campaign
description: The Southern Africa Trust was established in 2005 to support civil society organizations in southern Africa to participate effectively and with credibility in policy dialogues. The Change4ever Campaign was launched in 2007 to raise awareness about levels of poverty and create platforms for the public to participate in finding solutions. Past support enabled the grantee to host a fundraising dinner to raise funds for poverty alleviation initiatives and create awareness about poverty. The grantee also facilitated learning exchanges among youth from southern Africa on poverty alleviation initiatives. This grant will support the grantee to create platforms for local giving to local causes, continue raising awareness about poverty, and raise the profile of philanthropy.

title: Change4ever Campaign
description: The Southern Africa Trust was established in 2005 to support civil society organizations in southern Africa to participate effectively and with credibility in policy dialogues. The grantee supports efforts to reduce poverty in the region by generating knowledge on poverty issues, making grants to organizations that work to reduce poverty, and creating space for dialogue. The Change4ever Campaign, a project of the Southern Africa Trust, was established to promote local giving for lasting solutions to overcoming poverty and inequality. The campaign makes giving for social change desirable and accessible. Previous support has enabled the grantee to host giving circle events to raise funds for identified causes, profile local philanthropists to raise awareness about local giving, work with public figures and use mainstream media to create awareness about poverty, and support regional networks of indigenous grantmakers to build local philanthropy. This grant will allow the grantee to deepen the work of the Change4ever Campaign by generating knowledge about local giving and raising local resources to alleviate poverty.

title: Change4ever Campaign
description: Southern Africa Trust was established in 2005 to support lasting solutions to poverty across the southern African region. It produces knowledge on poverty issues, makes grants to organizations that work to reduce poverty, and promotes dialogue on poverty-related matters. The Change4ever Campaign, a project of Southern Africa Trust, is a public fundraising campaign that aims to make giving for lasting social change desirable. The campaign highlights social issues and raises funds to respond to them. Previous support enabled the Southern Africa Trust to promote giving by profiling ordinary citizens and hosting giving circle events to raise funds for good causes. This grant will support the grantee to build on the success of the Change4ever Campaign by continuing to profile individuals that give back to their communities and host giving circle events to raise funds for more organizations. The grantee will also partner with other organizations to host giving events targeted at high-net-worth individuals.

title: Change4ever Campaign
description: The Southern Africa Trust was founded in 2005 to support civil society organizations in southern Africa to participate effectively and with credibility in policy dialogue. Based in South Africa, the grantee supports civil society organizations that promote public policy dialogue on poverty issues. The Change4ever Campaign, a project of the Southern Africa Trust, was launched in 2007 to raise awareness about the levels of poverty in the region. It does this by exposing the public to the daily challenges faced by communities living in poverty. The campaign makes collective giving for lasting change interesting to a new generation of givers. This grant will support the Southern Africa Trust to build public awareness and appreciation of the role that civil society can play in the fight against poverty through the Change4ever Campaign. It will also provide platforms for ordinary people to give to causes that promote poverty alleviation. The campaign will be piloted in South Africa, and if successful, it will be expanded throughout southern Africa.

title: Model Transportation Project
description: Established in 1981, Disability Advocates of Kent County provides a full array of services throughout Kent County, which has a population of 600,000. As its mission, the grantee advocates and facilitates action by persons with disabilities and the community to achieve equal access for all, including transportation options and services. This grant increase will support the grantee’s work to deepen and expand civic engagement in the community related to transportation decisions, as well as to help link learning and sharing of best practices among other transportation corridor planning efforts in the state. This will include: 1) undertaking a range of activities, from listening sessions to social media, which engage a diverse constituency; 2) coordinating in-person gatherings, electronic sharing, and other efforts that support networking and peer-to-peer learning; and 3) disseminating information and tools statewide to elevate best practices.

title: Merit Bank
description: The program goal is to develop and expand a platform for supporting local community projects with in-kind donations, money, or volunteer time in Russia. Cloudwatcher will coordinate this Merit Bank, which operates on the basis of assigning tradable exchange units in return for contributions of time, goods, or money. These tradable units in turn can be used as donations for other projects, creating a growing circle of participation and contribution. Staff will help local citizens identify key local challenges, refine social projects for possible support, and identify additional resource contributors from within and outside the community. They will also manage the technical issues associated with tracking participants’ accounts. A gallery of potential projects proposed by local residents will be publicized through a Web site operated by Cloudwatcher — butovo.bankzaslug.ru — and also through public events. Established in 2005, Cloudwatcher works throughout Russia to promote innovative developments in philanthropy, volunteerism, and social entrepreneurship.

title: Outreach to New Freshwater Constituencies Project
description: The University of Michigan’s School of Natural Resources and Environment seeks to protect the Earth’s resources and promote a sustainable society through research, education, and public outreach. With prior Mott support, the grantee released a report assessing staff and board diversity within Great Lakes freshwater organizations. While progress has been made, more remains to be done for environmental groups to reflect the communities they serve. The grantee will develop an online platform to connect environmental groups with multicultural candidates of all levels of experience. The grantee will also launch a graduate fellowship program with a focus on the Great Lakes region.

title: Outreach to New Freshwater Constituencies Project
description: The University of Michigan’s School of Natural Resources and Environment seeks to protect the earth’s resources and promote a sustainable society through research, education, and public outreach. With prior Mott support, the grantee developed two leadership programs aimed at preparing undergraduate and graduate students to engage in environmental efforts. In its first two years of operation, the grantee’s graduate program served 39 participants. Students were placed in summer fellowships with philanthropic and nonprofit partners in the Great Lakes region as well as other parts of the country. With renewed Mott support, the grantee will enhance connections between its graduate and undergraduate programs and research the status of internal staffing and external partnerships in environmental organizations. The grantee will also convene Great Lakes organizations to help them develop and implement plans to engage a broader constituency.

title: Broadening Cross-Cultural Participation and Diversity in Great Lakes Advocacy
description: Now in its seventh year, this project of the University of Michigan is nationally recognized for outstanding results: it provides intensive training to cohorts of 30 graduate student fellows per summer and helps nonprofit environmental organizations in the Great Lakes and nationally to reach their goals and commitments to enhancing diversity. The grantee operates a similar program for undergraduate students. Nonprofit environmental groups recognize the need to increase diversity in their organizations and broaden participation in environmental programming. With renewed support, the grantee will enhance pathways for workers to participate in the environmental labor force, build a pipeline of diverse environmental workers, build a network that will foster mutual aid and support, and continue to monitor and report on advances in diversity in environmental organizations.

title: Outreach to New Freshwater Constituencies Project
geographic_focus: Minnesota, Pennsylvania, New York, Indiana, Illinois, Wisconsin, Ontario, Ohio, Michigan
description: The University of Michigan’s School of Natural Resources and Environment seeks to protect the Earth’s resources and promote a sustainable society through research, teaching, and public outreach. Based in Ann Arbor, the university takes a special interest in Great Lakes issues and provides a valuable contribution to the region’s scientific knowledge and skill base. The university also leads nationally recognized programs that promote multicultural engagement in environmental policies and programs. The grantee seeks to leverage this expertise to increase citizen participation in crafting sustainable, innovative solutions to the region’s freshwater problems. With Mott support, the grantee will assist Great Lakes environmental nonprofits in refining face-to-face and online networking and outreach mechanisms, as a way to expand constituencies and strengthen partnerships that advance sustainable, effective Great Lakes policies.

title: Promoting Integrated Water Management in the Great Lakes
description: American Rivers, a national organization based in Washington, D.C., with offices in the Great Lakes region, is dedicated to protecting and restoring freshwater resources. With prior Mott support, the grantee worked at the municipal and state levels in the Great Lakes region to promote water conservation, support the use of green stormwater infrastructure, and identify best practices for coordinating urban water management decisions. With renewed support, the grantee will continue these activities with a specific focus on urban areas and will develop a Great Lakes-focused strategic plan to guide efforts over the next five years.

title: Promoting Integrated Water Management in the Great Lakes
description: American Rivers is a national water conservation organization that protects and restores the nation’s waterways, with a special focus on the Great Lakes. The grantee’s main office is in Washington, D.C., but it also has staff based in the Great Lakes region. With past Mott support, the grantee provided technical assistance to municipal staff and freshwater groups to promote sustainable stormwater infrastructure by using Clean Water Act tools. The grantee also completed a five-year strategic plan for its Great Lakes regional programs. With renewed support, the grantee will continue to provide technical assistance to Great Lakes cities seeking to improve water quality by applying the principles of integrated water management and will publish a report assessing how Great Lakes states oversee drinking water policies.

title: Promoting Integrated Water Management in the Great Lakes
geographic_focus: Ohio, Indiana, New York, Minnesota, Illinois, Wisconsin, Illinois, Pennsylvania, Michigan, Wisconsin
description: American Rivers is a leading national voice on healthy rivers and plays a key role in helping cities and communities, both within the Great Lakes basin and nationally, address clean water challenges. With prior Mott support, the grantee’s Great Lakes program has pivoted from focusing on water resource protection and restoration to advancing solutions to protect drinking water and a more holistic approach to using, treating, delivering, cleaning and managing water resources. (This approach is referred to as Integrated Water Management.) This renewal grant will complete a citizens guide to drinking water in the Great Lakes, connect professional nongovernmental organization leaders with community leaders to address drinking water challenges, and connect regional leaders (bigger nongovernmental organizations and smaller community groups) with national policy discussions around protecting water for people.

title: Promoting Integrated Water Management in the Great Lakes
description: American Rivers, a national organization based in Washington, D.C., and with offices in the Great Lakes region, is dedicated to protecting and restoring freshwater resources. With this grant, the grantee will work at the municipal and state levels in the Great Lakes region to promote policies and practices that improve water efficiency, support the use of green stormwater infrastructure, demonstrate effective water conservation and restoration activities, and reduce flooding. A portion of the grant will also be used to support an organization-wide, strategic planning process.

title: Community Advice Office Sustainability Project
grantee: National Alliance for the Development of Community Advice Offices
description: The National Alliance for the Development of Community Advice Offices seeks to strengthen and sustain the community advice office sector in South Africa. Community advice offices provide free basic legal advice and other social services to the poor. Mott supported the grantee to reorganize the sector through facilitating national sector dialogues to agree on key priorities, galvanizing support for the regulation and development of minimum standards for the sector, and establishing the Association of Community Advice Offices of South Africa, a national membership-based initiative. This grant will support the grantee to build the capacity of community advice offices through accessing and linking them with relevant training opportunities and conduct research to help articulate the value of community advice offices and, in turn, unlock funding for advice offices from various stakeholders, particularly government . This grant has been made possible by a partnership with Atlantic Philanthropies in support of the community advice office sector.

title: Community Advice Office Sustainability Project
grantee: National Alliance for the Development of Community Advice Offices
description: The National Alliance for the Development of Community Advice Offices was initiated in 2005 as an alliance of seven civil society organizations aimed at strengthening and sustaining the community advice office sector in South Africa. It is committed to the long-term development of community advice offices as a way of ensuring access to justice within poor communities. Community advice offices provide free, basic legal advice and other social services to poor people. Past support assisted the grantee to link advice offices with relevant training opportunities and to conduct research to help articulate the value of community advice offices. This support will enable the grantee to conduct research and publish on matters related to the community advice office sector, advocate for state support of community advice offices, improve opportunities for community advice offices to access financial support from a variety of sources, and support the Association of Community Advice Offices of South Africa to strengthen its institutional capacity.

title: Community Advice Office Sustainability Project
grantee: National Alliance for the Development of Community Advice Offices
description: The National Alliance for the Development of Community Advice Offices was initiated in 2005 as an alliance of seven civil society organizations aimed at strengthening and sustaining the community advice office sector in South Africa. Past support assisted the grantee to link advice offices with relevant training opportunities and conduct research to help articulate the value of community advice offices. This grant will enable the grantee to conduct research on matters related to the community advice office sector, advocate for state support of community advice offices, improve opportunities for community advice offices to access financial support from a variety of sources, and strengthen its own institutional capacity.

title: Community Advice Office Sustainability Project
grantee: National Alliance for the Development of Community Advice Offices
description: The National Alliance for the Development of Community Advice Offices was initiated in 2005 to strengthen and sustain the community advice office sector in South Africa. Community advice offices provide free basic legal advice and other social services to poor people. Initially, the alliance was hosted by the Black Sash Trust before becoming an independent institution in March 2012. Mott-supported activities have included conducting research on the size and scope of the community advice office sector, developing an information technology system to present an accurate picture of the work of advice offices, and establishing provincial forums to help coordinate and build a cohesive voice for the sector. This grant will support the National Alliance for the Development of Community Advice Offices with efforts to unlock funding for community advice offices from various stakeholders, encourage community advice offices to use a case management system that shows the impact of interventions, and explore the establishment of a sustainability fund for community advice offices.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant supports Philanthropy for Active Civic Engagement, a learning community of funders established in 2006 doing work in the fields of civic engagement, service, and democratic renewal. Currently, the community includes 30 funders. Recent efforts have focused on: 1) service as a civic pathway out of poverty; 2) the relationship between new forms of information delivery and civic engagement; 3) strategies for civic engagement in Detroit; and 4) accountability and transparency in philanthropy. The community does its work through in-person gatherings, webinars, commissioning research papers, publications in philanthropic media, and sessions on topics important to the community at various philanthropic events. The community will continue its work in the above four areas over the next two years and is also exploring the area of transpartisan political reform.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant supports Philanthropy for Active Civic Engagement, a learning community of funders established in 2006 doing work in the fields of civic engagement, service, and democratic renewal. Currently the grantee includes 23 funders. Past efforts have focused on issues including the civic engagement of noncollege-bound youth, efforts by local governments to reinvent the way they interact with citizens and promoting service as a civic pathway out of poverty. The grantee is currently working on five different projects: 1) exploring the linkage between information and engagement; 2) promoting better understanding between those involved in civic engagement and diversity/inclusion work; 3) examining the impact of the transparency and accountability movements in the field of philanthropy; 4) helping Detroit funders deal more effectively with the civic engagement aspect of their local work; and 5) promoting the concept of service as a civic pathway out of poverty and into opportunity.

title: Conference Sponsorship
description: The program goal is to support learning among foundation professionals so that they can improve their performance. This grant will provide partial funding to the Center for Effective Philanthropy to conduct their 2013 biennial national conference, Pursuing Results: Effective Foundation Practice, in Detroit, Michigan. Approximately 300 foundation chief executive officers, trustees, and senior executives are expected to attend. Established in 2000, the grantee aims to advance the practice of philanthropy by providing the management and governance tools needed to define, assess, and improve overall foundation performance. Its mission is to provide data and create insight so philanthropic funders can better define, assess, and improve their effectiveness and, as a result, their intended impact. Besides its conferences, the grantee provides foundations with performance assessment tools, conducts research, and provides other educational programs.

title: Flint Community Schools Young Scientists
description: Through a partnership between the Cranbrook Educational Community’s Institute of Science and the Flint Community Schools, Flint students in grades seven and eight will receive supplemental educational opportunities in science that correspond with grade-level content. Programming offered by the grantee will include access to the institute’s staff, collections, and resources; an opportunity for Flint families to spend a day at the institute, including transportation; annual membership passes to the institute and affiliated museums that families can check out for unlimited use; rich, in-depth professional development for faculty; and a summer program for a smaller group of Flint students.

title: Flint Community Schools Young Scientists
description: Through a partnership between the Cranbrook Educational Community’s Institute of Science and the Flint Community Schools, Flint students in grades K-12 will receive supplemental educational opportunities in science that correspond with grade-level content. Programming offered by the grantee will include access to the institute’s staff, collections, and resources; an opportunity for Flint families to spend time at the institute, including transportation; unlimited use annual membership passes to the institute and affiliated museums; rich, in-depth professional development for faculty; and paid internship opportunities for 11th- and 12th-grade students.

title: Flint Community Schools Young Scientists
description: Cranbrook Educational Community will partner with Flint Community Schools to provide students in grades K-12 with supplemental educational opportunities in science and the arts that correspond to grade-level content. Programming will include access to the Cranbrook Educational Community’s staff, collections, and resources; family visitation days; museum membership passes; professional development for teachers; and paid student internships.

title: Flint Community Schools Young Scientists
description: The Cranbrook Educational Community will partner with Flint Community Schools to provide students in grades K-12 with supplemental educational opportunities in STEM that correspond to grade-level content, which has become even more important with the issues surrounding the city’s water system. Programming will include access to the grantee’s staff, collections, and resources; a family visitation day; family science festivals at each of the Flint Community Schools; professional development for teachers; and paid student internships.

title: Flint Community Schools Young Scientists
description: The Cranbrook Educational Community will partner with Flint Community Schools to provide students in grades K-12 with supplemental educational opportunities in STEM that correspond to grade-level content, which has become even more important with the issues surrounding the city’s water system. Programming will include access to the grantee’s staff, collections, and resources; a family visitation day; family science festivals at each of the Flint Community Schools; professional development for teachers; and paid student internships.

title: Flint Community Schools Young Scientists
description: The Cranbrook Educational Community will partner with Flint Community Schools to provide students with supplemental educational opportunities in STEM that correspond to grade-level content. The focus this year will be to provide intensive STEM curriculum and experiences for fourth grade students at Holmes STEM Academy, along with summer internships for the district’s high school students.

title: Flint Community Schools Young Scientists
description: The Cranbrook Educational Community will partner with Flint Community Schools to provide students with supplemental educational opportunities in STEM that correspond to grade-level content. Programming will include classroom outreach, intercession support, and internship experiences for high school students.

title: Flint Community Schools Young Scientists
description: Through a partnership between the Cranbrook Educational Community’s Institute of Science and the Flint Community Schools, Flint students in grades seven and eight will receive supplemental educational opportunities in science that correspond with grade-level content. Programming offered by the grantee will include access to the institute’s staff, collections, and resources; an opportunity for Flint families to spend a day at the institute, including transportation; annual membership passes to the institute and affiliated museums that families can check out for unlimited use; rich, in-depth professional development for faculty; and a summer program for a smaller group of Flint students.

title: Developing and Sustaining College Access Programming
description: This grant will enable Rutgers University Foundation to develop a college access and success toolkit for stakeholders in K-12 and beyond who are interested in developing pre-college bridge programming for underserved students. Using the Rutgers Future Scholars program as the backdrop, Rutgers University hosted a national convening in 2013 for more than 220 attendees across 20 states working in the pre-college and college access field. This convening spotlighted the most creative and effective approaches for preparing low-income and minority students for college. In building off the 2013 convening, recommended support will allow the grantee to provide a free, open source guide and compendium on best practices in pre-college programming and support the ongoing evaluation activities of its Rutgers Future Scholars model.

title: Developing and Sustaining College Access Programming
description: This grant increase will allow the Rutgers University Foundation to continue the development of a college access and success toolkit for stakeholders interested in developing pre-college programs for underserved students. In 2013, Rutgers University hosted a national convening spotlighting the most effective approaches for preparing low-income and minority students for college. With this grant increase, the grantee will build on the 2013 convening and produce an open source guide on best practices in pre-college programming and assist five higher education institutions in adapting the Rutgers Future Scholars model.

title: Developing and Sustaining Pre-College Bridge Programs
description: This grant will enable Rutgers University Foundation to convene a national forum where practitioners, supporters, and policymakers in the college access arena can discuss the current context, practice, accomplishments, and challenges for developing and sustaining precollege bridge programming in the United States. Using the Rutgers Future Scholars program as a backdrop, this grant will allow the grantee to profile its experience in implementing a precollege bridge program to a national audience for the purpose of promoting the most creative and effective programs for ensuring college access and success. This program is one of the more promising precollege efforts focused on preparing low-income students for college. Recommended support will also allow the grantee to enhance its 12th grade curriculum and support its ongoing evaluation efforts of the model.

title: International Conference on Education
description: This grant will support The After-School Corporation to host an international convening of senior education officials and policymakers to exchange information and ideas to improve education policy and practice in the United States, specifically related to how time and learning should be best used to prepare young people for college and career success. This convening will include education leaders from Finland, China (Shanghai), South Korea, Singapore, Germany, Brazil, and Canada.

title: Assets & Education Initiative
grantee: University of Kansas Center for Research, Inc.
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: Early evidence on the relationship between college savings accounts and college enrollment played a prominent role in motivating policymakers in San Francisco to establish the Kindergarten-to-College initiative, which provides every child in the city a matched, college savings account at kindergarten enrollment. This grant will enable the University of Kansas Center for Research, Inc., to further examine the relationship between children’s savings and the educational outcomes of children in order to strengthen the policy case for, maintain momentum behind, and spur broader adoption of children’s savings accounts. Mott funds will support the grantee’s independent research activities and projects in collaboration with other institutions, including the Department of Education. Grant funds will also support dissemination efforts aimed at making assets and education research more accessible to practitioners, policymakers, the media, and the general public. The grantee has provided professional social work education for over 60 years.

title: Assets & Education Initiative
grantee: University of Kansas Center for Research, Inc.
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: The University of Kansas Center for Research, Inc., is the leading research organization examining the relationship between educational savings and education outcomes for children, particularly low- and moderate-income children. This grant increase will enable the grantee to expand its current research activities and begin collecting program data on select children’s savings account initiatives in the United States. This information, including total number of accounts as well as participation and savings levels, will provide practitioners and policymakers with important information about how these models are performing.

title: Education and Youth Organizing Project
description: Flint Area Congregations Together is a multi-issue, multiconstituency, community organizing group in Genesee County, Michigan. Leaders from the organization have researched approaches that the community can use to help improve school performance and authentically engage youth in analyzing and helping to solve problems in the community. This grant will help support the costs associated with these priority issues.

title: John W. Porter Distinguished Chair in Urban Education Endowment
description: This grant will provide funds to the Eastern Michigan University Foundation for the John W. Porter Distinguished Chair in Urban Education Endowment. The grant provides for an annual appointment of renowned scholars and is designed to provide opportunities for learning and leadership in the fields of urban and community education and actively expand Eastern Michigan University’s role in urban school districts in Michigan with an emphasis on school-community partnerships.

title: Global Civil Society Information System
description: This grant will support the continued development of a system to provide global data on philanthropy, civil society organizations, and volunteering. The Global Civil Society Information System will help integrate data on civil society organizations, philanthropy, and volunteerism into countries’ economic statistics; provide vastly improved access to information on civil society organizations worldwide to both donors and beneficiaries; and increase the transparency of civil society organizations. The Johns Hopkins Center for Civil Society Studies will work with the United Nations Statistics Division to improve their guidance to countries on gathering statistics about nonprofit institutions. It will also test the feasibility of a partnership with TechSoup Global in an initial set of pilot countries to secure information on individual civil society organizations for which data is being assembled as part of national economic statistics. The Center for Civil Society Studies is part of Johns Hopkins University, one of America’s premier research universities.

title: Global Civil Society Information System
description: This grant will support the continued development of the Global Civil Society Information System. This system will help countries integrate data on civil society organizations, philanthropy, and volunteerism into their economic statistics; provide vastly improved access to information on civil society organizations worldwide to both donors and beneficiaries; and increase the transparency of civil society organizations. The Center for Civil Society Studies will work with the United Nations Statistics Division to complete revisions to its guidance to countries on gathering statistics about nonprofit institutions. In partnership with TechSoup Global, it will also pilot the use of data coming out of this effort for at least six European countries. The grantee will then encourage implementation of the resulting procedures into the statistical systems of select non-European countries. The Center for Civil Society Studies is part of Johns Hopkins University, one of America’s premier research universities.

title: Global Civil Society Information System
description: The project goal is to enhance the quality, reliability, and accessibility of national level data on nonprofit organizations and volunteering around the world. Over the past several years, the Center for Civil Society Studies at Johns Hopkins University has been working with the United Nations Statistics Division on revisions and expansions to the United Nations Handbook on Nonprofit Institutions in the System of National Accounts — its guidance to countries on gathering statistics about nonprofit institutions. The grantee will complete the process of securing official approval for the handbook, disseminate the revised and updated version, and encourage implementation of the resulting broadened civil society sector statistical procedures into the statistical systems of countries around the world. This will lay the groundwork for a proposed global online, accessible civil society information system.

title: Global Civil Society Information System
description: This grant will support the development of a system to provide global data on philanthropy, civil society organizations, and volunteering. The Global Civil Society Information System will help integrate data on civil society organizations, philanthropy, and volunteerism into countries’ economic statistics; provide vastly improved access to information on civil society organizations worldwide to both donors and beneficiaries; and increase the transparency of civil society organizations. The Johns Hopkins Center for Civil Society Studies will work with the United Nations Statistics Division to improve their guidance to countries on gathering statistics about nonprofit institutions. It will also test the feasibility of a partnership with TechSoup Global in an initial set of pilot countries to secure information on individual civil society organizations. The center is part of Johns Hopkins University, one of America’s premier research universities.

title: Education Trust - Midwest
description: Education Trust, Inc., provides research; training for educators, parents, business organizations, and others; and wide dissemination of data and analysis with the goal of helping raise student achievement, especially among minority and poor students. This grant will support the grantee’s work in Michigan and other Midwestern states.

title: Flint Diaper Bank
description: This grant will provide funds to the Food Bank of Eastern Michigan to support the Flint Diaper Bank program in providing diapers to low-income Genesee County residents. By utilizing the food bank’s sophisticated distribution system, the Flint Diaper Bank can ensure that these diapers will reach the community’s neediest families. In its first year of operation, the Flint Diaper Bank served over 3,600 children under the age of three with diapers.

title: Flint Diaper Bank
description: This grant will provide funds to the Food Bank of Eastern Michigan to support the Flint Diaper Bank program in providing diapers to low-income Genesee County residents. By utilizing the Food Bank of Eastern Michigan’s sophisticated distribution system, the Flint Diaper Bank can ensure that diapers will reach the community’s most needy families and help relieve the stress of families and caretakers who often must choose between supplying diapers for their babies or purchasing other basic necessities.

By utilizing the grantee’s sophisticated distribution system, the Flint Diaper Bank can ensure that diapers will reach the community’s most needy families and help relieve the stress of families and caretakers who often must choose between supplying diapers for their babies or purchasing other basic necessities.

title: Flint Diaper Bank
description: The program goal is to obtain approximately 90,000 diapers for low-income families in the Flint area. The Food Bank of Eastern Michigan is serving as the fiscal sponsor for the Flint Diaper Bank. The Food Bank of Eastern Michigan started in 1981 as a small, grassroots community organization to distribute surplus food to those in need throughout Genesee County, as well as 21 other counties in eastern Michigan. The grantee solicits, stores, and distributes over 21 million pounds of food annually, either directly or through a network of more than 400 partner agencies, which include soup kitchens, church pantries, homeless shelters, and other charities. By utilizing the grantee’s sophisticated distribution system, the Flint Diaper Bank can ensure that these diapers will reach the community’s neediest families.

title: TFN Global - Developing TFN in CEE/Russia
description: The primary program goal is to increase the level and impact of individual philanthropy in the Central and Eastern Europe and Russia region. The Funding Network, a giving circle based in the United Kingdom, will expand its work across the region and support local nonprofits and initiative groups interested in starting similar giving circles in their countries. More specifically, the grantee will provide information, technical assistance, and mentoring and will facilitate regional and international contacts and exchanges among its partners. Building on the success of its activities in the past two years, with this grant increase and funds from other donors, the grantee will organize a two-day international conference in London to strengthen the network of its partner organizations from different parts of the world, facilitate skill building and sharing of best practices, and introduce new tools for monitoring and evaluating the impact of partners’ work in their countries. There will be significant participation in the event from Central and Eastern Europe and Russia.

title: TFN Global - Developing TFN in CEE/Russia
description: The program goal is to increase the level and impact of individual philanthropy in the Central and Eastern European region. To this end, The Funding Network, a giving circle based in the U. K., will strengthen the capacity of its current partner organizations in the region and establish partnerships with new organizations interested in starting similar giving circles in their countries. More specifically, the grantee will provide information, technical assistance, and mentoring and facilitate regional and international contacts and exchanges among its partners. The grantee will also document, publish, and disseminate success stories and lessons learned from the development of these giving circles in the Central and Eastern European region. Established in London in 2002 by a group of private philanthropists with the mission to increase the level, scope, and impact of charitable giving, the grantee now works in 15 countries around the world. In the past grant period, the grantee supported its 23 partner organizations in six Central and Eastern European countries to stage 55 events with more than 1,800 donors and raise close to $1 million for 150 projects. In addition, the grantee organized the first conference of its international network with 45 delegates representing 32 partner organizations.

title: TFN Global - Developing TFN in CEE/Russia
geographic_focus: Eastern Europe, Australia and New Zealand, Southern Europe, Western Europe, South America, South Africa
description: The program goal is to increase the level and impact of individual philanthropy in the Central and Eastern European region and globally. To this end, The Funding Network, a giving circle based in the U. K., will strengthen the capacity of its current partner organizations in the region and establish partnerships with new organizations interested in starting similar giving circles in their countries. More specifically, the grantee will provide information, technical assistance, and mentoring and facilitate regional and international contacts and exchanges among its partners. Established in London in 2002 by a group of private philanthropists with the mission to increase the level, scope, and impact of charitable giving, the grantee now works in 20 countries around the world. In the past grant period, the grantee supported eight partner organizations in five Central and Eastern European countries to stage events in 30 cities, expanded its programs with new partners in five countries, and published an impact report about its work in the Central and Eastern European region.

title: TFN Global - Developing TFN in CEE/Russia
geographic_focus: Bosnia and Herzegovina, Turkey, Russia, Bulgaria, Ukraine, Germany, Serbia, Croatia, United Kingdom, Romania
description: The program goal is to increase the level and impact of individual philanthropy in the Central/Eastern Europe and Russia region. To this end, Funding Network, a giving circle based in the United Kingdom, will expand its work across the region and support local nonprofits and initiative groups interested in starting similar giving circles in their countries. More specifically, the grantee will provide information, technical assistance, and mentoring and facilitate regional and international contacts and exchanges among its partners. Also, the grantee will document, publish, and disseminate success stories and lessons learned from the development of these giving circles in the Central/Eastern Europe and Russia region. Established in London in 2002 by a group of private philanthropists with the mission to increase the level, scope, and impact of charitable giving, the grantee has staged over 120 events in the United Kingdom, Canada, and South Africa. Through these activities, the grantee has raised over 4.2 million pounds from more than 4,000 philanthropists in support of 600 small and medium nonprofit organizations.

title: Promoting Philanthropy in CEE/Russia
description: The project goal is to increase the level and effectiveness of private philanthropy in Southeast Europe. To this end, the Zing Foundation, also known as Bolder Giving, will provide support to key Mott grantees in Bulgaria, Romania, Serbia, and Turkey and will strengthen their capacity to use donor storytelling as an effective strategy for increasing local giving. In addition, the grantee will identify and profile diaspora donors from these four countries to inspire them to give back to causes in their countries of origin. Also, the grantee will prepare a toolkit on storytelling strategies and techniques for its partners and other interested nonprofits. The grantee will also experiment with donor education Webinars for donors and foundation leaders interested in strategic philanthropy in these four countries. Since its launch in 2007, the grantee has been inspiring and supporting people to engage in philanthropic work at their full lifetime potential. During the past grant period, the grantee provided training and consultancy to key Mott grantees in Bulgaria, Romania, Serbia, and Turkey and supported them to develop and publicize 35 inspirational donor stories from the four countries.

title: Promoting Philanthropy in CEE/Russia
description: The project goal is to increase the level and effectiveness of private philanthropy in Southeast Europe. To this end, the Zing Foundation, also known as Bolder Giving, will establish working partnerships with key Mott grantees in Bulgaria, Romania, Serbia, and Turkey and will strengthen their capacity to use donor storytelling as an effective strategy for increasing local giving. In addition, the grantee will support project participants to establish relationships with major donors in their countries and encourage these donors to work together both in country and across borders to inspire others to give more. Since its launch in 2007, the grantee has been inspiring and supporting people to engage in philanthropic work at their full lifetime potential. The grantee’s key achievements in the past include collaborating with Bill and Melinda Gates on their Giving Pledge, developing a library of over 100 stories of people who give significant portions of their income or wealth and using these stories to inspire others to give, and providing training and technical assistance to community foundations in the United States on donor storytelling methods.

title: Backup Legal Services for Advice Offices
description: ProBono.Org is a public interest legal clearinghouse that was established in 2006 to encourage legal professionals to provide free legal services to poor and vulnerable people in South Africa. This project was initiated in 2010 to facilitate relationships between community advice offices and attorneys in small towns and rural areas so that poor people can access free legal services close to where they live. The project is currently implemented in the Limpopo, Northwest, and Gauteng provinces. Past support enabled the grantee to recruit attorneys in small and rural towns to participate in this project, offer training and support to paralegals in community advice offices, and conduct human rights awareness campaigns in collaboration with community advice offices. This grant will support the grantee to continue to recruit attorneys in small towns and pair them with advice offices to enable them to help paralegals in advice offices solve difficult cases.

title: Backup Legal Services for Advice Offices
description: ProBono.Org is a public interest legal clearinghouse established in 2006 to encourage legal professionals to provide free legal services to poor and vulnerable people in South Africa. This project facilitates relationships between community advice offices and attorneys in small towns and rural areas so that poor people can access free legal services close to where they live. The project is currently implemented in the Limpopo and Gauteng provinces. Past support enabled the grantee to work with experienced paralegals in community advice offices to recruit attorneys in small and rural towns to participate in this project, offer training and support to paralegals, and conduct human rights awareness campaigns in collaboration with community advice offices. This grant will provide support to build a case management system to better understand cases affecting communities and to continue to link attorneys in small towns with advice offices to enable them to help paralegals in advice offices solve difficult cases and assist advice office clients.

title: Backup Legal Services for Advice Offices
description: ProBono.Org is a public interest legal services clearinghouse that was established in 2006 with the aim of encouraging legal professionals to provide free legal services to poor and vulnerable people in South Africa. Established in 2010, the community advice office support project facilitates relationships between community advice offices and attorneys in small towns and rural areas so that poor people can access free legal services close to where they live. The project is currently implemented in the Limpopo, Northwest, and Gauteng provinces. To date, 33 law firms have been successfully recruited to participate in this project. This grant will support the grantee to recruit more lawyers in small and rural towns to offer free legal services to poor people, offer training and support to paralegals in community advice offices, and conduct human rights awareness campaigns in collaboration with community advice offices.

title: Advice Office Training and Support
grantee: Community Law and Rural Development Centre
geographic_focus: KwaZulu-Natal, Province of, Eastern Cape, Province of
description: The Community Law and Rural Development Centre was established in 1989 to empower rural communities in the Eastern Cape and KwaZulu-Natal provinces of South Africa to actively participate in their social and economic development. Mott has supported the grantee for many years to provide legal advice and human rights education through a network of advice offices located throughout the two provinces. This grant will support the Community Law and Rural Development Centre to assist advice offices in KwaZulu-Natal and Eastern Cape provinces to register as independent entities and develop the skills of staff and management committees on topics including financial management, fundraising, report writing, and computer skills. The aim is to lessen the dependence of the advice offices on external support by providing the tools and confidence necessary to enable them to operate smoothly. Paralegals from the advice offices will also receive ongoing training on relevant aspects of the law.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Court Street Village Non-Profit Housing Corporation
description: This grant will provide general purpose support to the Court Street Village Non-Profit Housing Corporation to carry out its mission to improve central city neighborhoods adjacent to downtown Flint. Founded in 1986, the grantee engages with stakeholders to enact comprehensive strategies for neighborhood stabilization and revitalization. The grantee will continue to pilot its Neighborhood Investment for Community Enhancement Initiative launched in 2013 in the Central Park neighborhood. If the concept proves successful, the grantee plans to replicate the model in other central city locations.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Court Street Village Non-Profit Housing Corporation
description: This grant provides general purpose support to Court Street Village Non-Profit Housing Corporation to improve central city neighborhoods adjacent to downtown Flint. The destabilizing effects of the water crisis on Flint’s housing markets requires that neighborhoods enact comprehensive strategies for neighborhood stabilization and revitalization. Court Street Village Non-Profit Housing Corporation will fulfill this role through pursuit of its Neighborhood Investment for Community Enhancement initiative, which engages neighborhood residents and outside agencies in blight elimination, financial investment, crime prevention, and landlord/tenant support.
