description: This grant will provide general purpose support to Court Street Village Non-Profit Housing Corporation to carry out its mission to improve central city neighborhoods in Flint. Founded in 1986, the grantee engages stakeholders in the areas surrounding downtown Flint in developing and enacting comprehensive strategies for neighborhood stabilization and renewal. Support will enable the grantee to maintain a full-time staff person to oversee neighborhood improvement efforts, and will assist the grantee in piloting the Neighborhood Investment for Community Enhancement initiative in Central Park. If successful, the grantee plans to replicate the program in other neighborhoods.

title: Capital Improvements
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant provides support for capital improvements to the roof and exterior walls of the Greater Flint Arts Council building in order to restore its structural integrity. The Greater Flint Arts Council is an independent agency providing support to local artists and arts organizations throughout Greater Flint. The grantee strives to be a catalyst for increased artistic and cultural programming for Flint’s ethnically diverse community, and to enrich the community with an array of culturally diverse services, educational programs, publications, and events.

title: Learning in Afterschool & Summer Project
description: This grant will provide support to the Partnership for Children and Youth to contribute to the Expanded Learning and Afterschool Project, as well as the Learning in Afterschool & Summer Project. Blogs, videos, and articles by national afterschool and educational leaders developed for this program will focus on engaged learning and learning time after school and in the summer. The grant will also support hosting a conference entitled How Kids Learn. Ultimately, the aim of the program is to improve access and the quality of out-of-school time learning to help expand learning opportunities for disadvantaged youth.

title: Holy Angels Warming Center
grantee: Catholic Charities of Shiawassee and Genesee Counties
description: Catholic Charities of Shiawassee and Genesee Counties provides intervention services for individuals and families in crisis. More than 80 percent of those served are nonCatholic, and the organization serves over 150,000 meals, provides over 100,000 items to families with low or no annual income, and provides temporary shelter to homeless individuals and families in Genesee County. This grant will allow the grantee to operate a warming center near downtown Flint to protect homeless residents from the winter elements, both day and night.

title: Nina's Place
description: The YWCA of Greater Flint has been serving the Flint and Genesee County communities for 100 years with a mission of empowering women and eliminating racism. This grant will provide partial support for the Nina’s Place program, which provides safe, long-term shelter to young women who were formerly in foster care and are homeless and without family support. Nina’s Place offers 24-hour access to a secure shelter facility with trained staff on site at all times, as well as access to educational and employment resources, and structure and support to begin to achieve goals, complete daily activities, and cope with the emotional repercussions of past traumas.

title: Center for Arab American Philanthropy Endowment Fund
grantee: Arab Community Center for Economic and Social Services (ACCESS)
description: This grant enables the Center for Arab American Philanthropy, which is a national program of the Arab Community Center for Economic and Social Services (ACCESS), to sponsor a year-long challenge to grow endowed assets. Gifts from donors establishing endowed funds will receive a fifty-cent match for every dollar donated. The grantee works to encourage strategic philanthropy in the Arab-American community through research, training, technical assistance, and development of informational materials; conducts donor-outreach activities; and provides donor services such as donor-advised funds. This is a national ethnic community foundation which needs support to continue to cultivate its donor base.

title: Center for Arab American Philanthropy Endowment Fund
grantee: Arab Community Center for Economic and Social Services (ACCESS)
description: This grant enables the Center for Arab American Philanthropy, which is a national program of the Arab Community Center for Economic and Social Services (ACCESS), to sponsor a yearlong challenge to grow endowed assets. Gifts from donors establishing endowed funds will receive a 50-cent match for every dollar donated. The program works to encourage strategic philanthropy in the Arab American community through research, training, technical assistance, and development of informational materials; conducts donor outreach activities; and provides donor services such as donor-advised funds.

title: Global Alliance for Community Philanthropy Secretariat
description: The Global Alliance for Community Philanthropy is a multidonor collaborative aimed at expanding and deepening the role of community philanthropy in strengthening local development efforts. Activities within the framework of the alliance include: 1) piloting community philanthropy projects; 2) learning, research, and evaluation; and 3) communication and representation to global stakeholders. In its role as the Global Alliance for Community Philanthropy Secretariat, the Global Fund for Community Foundations will track, compile, and analyze members’ programming; coordinate and conduct mutual learning efforts; disseminate knowledge both internally and externally; and promote community philanthropy as a valuable development practice. During the first year of this project, the grantee focused on organizing meetings, recruiting staff, and developing a database. Registered as an independent organization in late 2009, the Global Fund for Community Foundations is a global, grassroots grantmaker seeking to promote community foundations and other local philanthropic institutions in the Global South and in the emerging economies of Central and Eastern Europe.

title: Global Alliance for Community Philanthropy Secretariat
description: The Global Alliance for Community Philanthropy Secretariat is a multidonor collaborative aimed at expanding and deepening the role of community philanthropy in strengthening local development efforts. Activities within the framework of the alliance include: 1) piloting community philanthropy projects; 2) learning, research, and evaluation; and 3) communication and representation to global stakeholders. In its role as the Global Alliance for Community Philanthropy Secretariat, the Global Fund for Community Foundations will continue to track, compile, and analyze members’ programming; coordinate and conduct mutual learning efforts; disseminate knowledge both internally and externally; and promote community philanthropy as a valuable development practice. During 2015-2016, the grantee convened four partner meetings, published six research papers, organized the Global Summit for Community Philanthropy in Johannesburg, and contributed substantively to numerous conferences and publications. Registered as an independent organization in 2009, the Global Fund for Community Foundations is a global, grassroots grantmaker seeking to promote community foundations and other local philanthropic institutions in the Global South and in the emerging economies of Central and Eastern Europe.

title: Global Alliance for Community Philanthropy Secretariat
description: The Global Alliance for Community Philanthropy is a multidonor collaborative aimed at expanding and deepening the role of community philanthropy in strengthening local development efforts. Planned activities within the framework of the alliance include: 1) piloting community philanthropy projects; 2) learning, research, and evaluation; and 3) communication and representation to global stakeholders. The Global Fund for Community Foundations is the secretariat for the initiative. In this capacity, the grantee will track, compile, and analyze members’ programming; coordinate and conduct mutual learning efforts; disseminate knowledge both internally and externally; and promote community philanthropy as a valuable development practice. Registered as an independent organization in late 2009, the Global Fund for Community Foundations is a global, grassroots grantmaker seeking to promote community foundations and other local philanthropic institutions in the Global South and in the emerging economies of Central and Eastern Europe.

title: What's Next for Community Philanthropy
description: The goal of the What’s Next for Community Philanthropy project is to engage the community foundation field in exploring new and existing models and approaches for serving their communities through an innovation and design process. The project will involve three workstreams: 1) discovery and framing; 2) interactive design sessions; and 3) synthesis, documentation, testing, and sharing. Final outputs will include a short report, a series of speeches and Webcasts, a Web site, creative tools such as infographics and consultations to help community foundations to prototype, and pilot new approaches. This grant increase will support development of additional accessible, user-friendly products, and their broad dissemination. The What’s Next for Community Philanthropy project will be led by the Monitor Institute, which has recently become part of the global strategy firm Deloitte Consulting LLP and is a separate sub-brand underneath Monitor Deloitte.

title: What's Next for Community Philanthropy
description: The goal of the What’s Next for Community Philanthropy project is to engage the community foundation field in exploring new and existing models and approaches for serving their communities through an innovation and design process. The project will use a conceptual framework called Ten Types of Innovation which was developed by Doblin, Monitor Deloitte’s innovation strategy firm. The process will involve three workstreams: 1) discovery and framing; 2) interactive design sessions; and 3) synthesis, documentation, testing, and sharing. Final outputs will include a short report, a series of speeches and Webcasts, a Web site, creative tools such as infographics and consultations to help community foundations to prototype and pilot new approaches. The What’s Next for Community Philanthropy project will be led by the Monitor Institute, which has recently become part of the global strategy firm Deloitte Consulting LLP and is a sub-brand of Monitor Deloitte.

title: Nonprofit Clinic Project
description: The South African Institute for Advancement, also known as Inyathelo, was established in 2002 to promote the development of a strong and sustainable civil society sector in South Africa. It provides training, information, and networking opportunities to nonprofits and universities to advance democracy. The nonprofit clinic project provides one-on-one mentorship, training, and advice to nonprofits with a specific focus on organizational sustainability. Over the past two years, the grantee provided training that builds an organization’s ability to engage with its internal and external environment to attract resources, a concept termed advancement. Additionally, the grantee conducted one-on-one sessions with nonprofits seeking additional support and made materials available from its resource center. This grant will allow the grantee to continue supporting the growth of civil society organizations by providing technical support and advice to organizations in need of assistance, conducting training on advancement, and hosting workshops on topical issues affecting civil society organizations. It will also expand its clinic services at its new premises to provide support to more organizations.

title: Non-Profit Clinic Project
description: The South African Institute for Advancement, also known as Inyathelo, was established in 2002 to promote the development of a strong and sustainable civil society sector in South Africa. It provides training, resources, information, and networking opportunities to nonprofits to improve their capacity and sustainability. The Non-Profit Clinic provides one-on-one mentoring, training, and advice to nonprofits, with a specific focus on sustainability. Over the past two years, the grantee provided training that builds an organization’s ability to engage with its internal and external environment to attract resources. It also hosted leadership retreats and peer-to-peer learning workshops to improve the capacity of nonprofits and made resource materials available to supported organizations. This grant will continue to support the grantee to provide technical support and advice to organizations that require assistance, conduct training on advancement, and host workshops on topical issues affecting civil society organizations.

title: Nonprofit Clinic Project
description: The South African Institute for Advancement, also known as Inyathelo, works to build a vibrant democracy in South Africa by strengthening civil society organizations and higher education institutions and developing a strong philanthropic movement. It provides nonprofits with training, information, resources, and opportunities for learning. Over the past two years, the grantee has convened a group of local philanthropists on topics of common interest to develop the field of philanthropy, partnered with other Mott grantees to develop a code of governance for nonprofits, and provided practical guidance and tools to organizations on fundraising and other organization strengthening techniques. This grant will support the grantee to train nonprofits on sustainability and governance, provide tailored advisory services, and expand its resource center to make it more accessible to nonprofits.

title: Translating Climate Science for Actionable Solutions
geographic_focus: Ohio, Michigan, Wisconsin, Indiana, Pennsylvania, United States, New York, Minnesota, Illinois
description: Island Press, a leading publisher of environmental content in the United States, works to elevate the best ideas and information in the field to solve complex environmental problems. This grant provides partial support for a one-year project to disseminate the findings of the National Climate Assessment in the Great Lakes region, a federal report issued every four years on the impacts of climate change. Island Press will develop an easily accessible summary report for a nontechnical audience, which will be used as the basis for informational workshops in Michigan and national media outreach.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Citizens Campaign Fund for the Environment
description: The Great Lakes ecosystem supplies drinking water to millions of New York residents. The area’s lakes and rivers also support multibillion dollar industries and offer many recreational opportunities. Citizens Campaign Fund for the Environment is a New York-based environmental organization with a longtime commitment to the Great Lakes. With this general purpose grant, the grantee will advance its programs related to water resources, environmental education, energy education, environment and public health research, and endangered species and conservation. The grantee will pay particular attention to Great Lakes’ needs, in part, by helping update and implement New York’s Great Lakes Action Agenda, which is the state’s comprehensive plan to address Great Lakes issues. The grantee will also further develop its organizational capacity by updating management practices and communications systems.

title: Growing Michigan's Blue Economy
description: The Annis Water Resources Institute at Grand Valley State University is leading this research effort to understand and describe Michigan’s blue economy — how the state’s natural water assets and supporting water education, research, and technological innovation can be the basis for future economic growth. With this grant increase and associated grant period extension, the institute will distribute the results of the study in a Web-based, multimedia report that is more impactful and interactive than originally planned.

title: Growing Michigan's Blue Economy
description: Michigan, the Great Lakes State, has the opportunity to be a leader in the blue economy, which involves a range of economic development activities aimed at using a region’s freshwater resources to generate jobs and wealth. The Annis Water Resources Institute at Grand Valley State University, a leading water research institute, will lead an effort to document the current scope and future potential of blue economy activities in Michigan. The resulting report will be used to engage a range of stakeholders in discussions about the ways in which such economic development activities could be expanded and accelerated across the state.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen active civic participation in Bulgaria. The Citizen Participation Forum, an association of over 120 Bulgarian nonprofit organizations, will expand its membership and strengthen the capacity of its member organizations, create effective partnerships with other nongovernmental organization networks and public institutions, ensure participation of citizens and nonprofit organizations in decisionmaking processes on the local and national levels, and increase the knowledge and practice of effective participation among young people. The grantee has been working as an informal network since 2009 and was registered formally in October 2012. The grantee’s mission is to develop civil society in Bulgaria and strengthen citizen participation in public policymaking and decisionmaking. The grantee’s key past achievements include coordinating input from nongovernmental organizations into relevant policy and decisionmaking processes, introducing a citizen participation index, and increasing its organizational capacity. The grantee is based in Sofia, Bulgaria.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen active civic participation in Bulgaria. To this end, the Citizen Participation Forum, an association of over 130 Bulgarian nonprofit organizations, will expand its membership and strengthen the capacity of its member organizations; create effective partnerships with other nongovernmental organization networks and public institutions; and ensure participation of citizens and nonprofit organizations in decisionmaking processes on the local, national, and European Union levels. The grantee has been working as an informal network since 2009 and registered formally in October 2012. The grantee’s mission is to develop civil society in Bulgaria and strengthen citizen participation in public policymaking and decisionmaking. The grantee’s key past achievements include coordinating input from nongovernmental organizations into the development of a national strategy for civil society development and advocating for a proper implementation of the partnership principle during the development of the country’s operational agreement with the European Union for the period 2014-2020.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to develop community philanthropy and community foundations in Romania. To this end, the Romanian Federation of Community Foundations will strengthen its institutional capacity and develop high quality services for its members; support the development of new community foundations and expand its membership; create partnerships with relevant institutions in the civil society, public, and business sectors; increase the level of resources available for the development of the community foundation field; and increase the visibility of the Romanian community foundation movement on the national and international levels. During the previous grant period, the grantee increased its membership, strengthened its operational capacity, facilitated peer learning and sharing among its members, and revised and updated its standards of good practice for community foundations.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to develop community philanthropy and community foundations in Romania. The Romanian Federation of Community Foundations will strengthen its institutional capacity and develop high quality services for its members, support members’ efforts to build long-term assets for a sustainable future, support the development of new community foundations and expanding their membership, strengthen its participation in the international community philanthropy field, and increase the level of resources available for the development of the community foundation field. During the previous grant period, the grantee provided technical assistance and capacity building programs to the 12 member foundations, supported the development of four new community foundations, and raised over $100,000 for networkwide projects. The grantee is based in Cluj-Napoca, Romania.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to develop community philanthropy and community foundations in Romania. To this end, the Romanian Federation of Community Foundations will strengthen its institutional capacity and develop high quality services for its members; support the development of new community foundations and expand its membership; create partnerships with relevant institutions in the civil society, public, and business sectors; increase the level of resources available for the development of the community foundation field; and increase the visibility of the Romanian community foundation movement on the national and international levels. The federation was established in April 2012. All seven community foundations that currently exist in Romania are members of the federation. Since its establishment, the grantee has developed its long-term vision for the development of the community foundation field in Romania, created a branding and communications strategy, and developed principles of good practice for community foundations in Romania.

title: Bikes on the Bricks Event
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant supports activities for the Bikes on the Bricks event. Bikes on the Bricks is a popular motorcycle show and police skills competition that attracts tourists from across the Midwest. Downtown events help to increase foot traffic, boost sales at local businesses, provide family-friendly experiences, and elevate downtown Flint as a regional destination for arts, culture, and entertainment.

title: Bikes on the Bricks Marketing
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant supports marketing activities for the Bikes on the Bricks event. Bikes on the Bricks is a popular motorcycle event that attracts tourists from across the Midwest. Downtown events help to increase foot traffic, boost sales at local businesses, and elevate downtown Flint as a regional destination for arts, culture, and entertainment.

title: Regional Communication Centers
description: The project goal is to increase public knowledge of civic engagement practices in Russia. The Agency for Social Information has long gathered and distributed information about social and civic initiatives from across Russia. Recently it has identified and promoted the use of digital technologies in support of civic engagement. With Mott support, the grantee will join these two strands through the development of regional communication centers in five Russian regions. These centers will operate as hubs both for gathering information about the work of civic groups and for disseminating best practices related to use of information and communications technologies and multimedia resources in support of civic participation. Ultimately, these efforts will seek to reframe the narrative around the nonprofit sector to highlight its positive contributions to society. Founded in 1994, the Agency for Social Information is a Moscow-based, independent, information agency which draws on a network of 28 regional affiliates and provides informational support to the nonprofit sector in Russia.

title: Building Legal Capacity of the Non-Profit Sector in Russia
description: The program goal is to improve the legal literacy of Russian nongovernmental organizations. With this grant, Legal Team will administer a legal education and consultation service in 20 regions aimed at strengthening the capacity of Russian nongovernmental organizations to understand legal requirements, maintain proper documentation, and ensure regulatory compliance. It will also develop and disseminate a digest of frequently asked questions in order to provide easy access to information on common questions. This experience will allow the grantee to inform the Ministry of Justice of problematic issues in the application of regulations affecting the nonprofit sector. The Moscow-based Legal Team was established in 2012 with a focus on strengthening the legal capacity of the not-for-profit sector in Russia. It emerged from Lawyers for Civil Society, a Russian nonprofit established with support from the International Center for Not-for-Profit Law, and as such will draw on an existing regional network of lawyers specializing in noncommercial law.

title: Global Participation in the Community Foundations of Canada Conference
description: The program goal is to facilitate knowledge exchange and foster relationships between community philanthropy practitioners from around the world. Through travel support scholarships, this grant will provide the opportunity for 14 community philanthropy practitioners from Australia, Brazil, India, Ireland, Kenya, Latvia, Mexico, Pakistan, Romania, Russia, Scotland, Singapore, and South Africa to participate in the June 2013 Community Foundations of Canada biennial conference. Community Foundations of Canada is a national membership association of 184 community foundations. Its conference will bring together over 650 staff, board members, and volunteers from community foundations and other philanthropic organizations, mostly from Canada and the United States. Broader international participation will enrich the conference, and most of the scholarship recipients will have presentation roles in various sessions and events. Scholarship recipients will also participate in a consultation meeting to determine the goal, scope, format, timing, and other broad features of a future global symposium on community foundations.

title: Great Lakes Summit
grantee: Conference of Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Governors and Premiers
geographic_focus: New York, Illinois, Michigan, Ohio, Pennsylvania, United States, Minnesota, Wisconsin, Indiana
description: In April, Great Lakes governors and premiers will be meeting for a two-day summit in Chicago, entitled Accelerating Progress, which follows up on a three-day summit held in 2013, Strengthening Our Economy and Protecting Our Great Lakes. The Council of Great Lakes Governors, a nonprofit organization that coordinates regional initiatives, is organizing the event. With partial Mott support, the grantee will plan and host the 2014 summit.

title: Great Lakes Summit
grantee: Conference of Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Governors and Premiers
geographic_focus: Ohio, Minnesota, Michigan, Illinois, New York, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Indiana
description: The Council of Great Lakes Governors is a nonprofit organization that facilitates cooperation between the governors of eight Great Lakes states and the premiers of two Canadian provinces. With Mott support, the grantee organized last year’s summit entitled, Strengthening Our Economy and Protecting Our Great Lakes, which convened governors and premiers to discuss collaborative approaches to Great Lakes’ challenges, such as aquatic invasive species. With renewed Mott support, the grantee will reconvene Great Lakes’ leaders in Quebec City, Canada. The summit is entitled, Connecting Across Borders, and will focus on issues related to Great Lakes ecosystem health, transportation, and trade.

title: Great Lakes Summit
grantee: Conference of Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Governors and Premiers
geographic_focus: Wisconsin, Indiana, Pennsylvania, Illinois, United States, New York, Ohio, Michigan, Minnesota
description: Great Lakes governors and premiers will be meeting for a three-day summit, entitled Strengthening Our Economy and Protecting Our Great Lakes. The Council of Great Lakes Governors, a nonprofit organization that coordinates regional initiatives, is organizing the event. With partial Mott support, the grantee will plan and host the summit, as well as document its outcome.

title: Capacity Building
description: The United Way of Genesee County has undergone a significant positive transformation in the past two years, downsizing and streamlining operations and successfully meeting its annual campaign goals. This grant will enable the grantee to build upon these accomplishments and strengthen core operations by providing support for strategic planning and increasing staff capacity in the areas of community impact and investment.

title: Community Foundation Development
description: The program goal is to strengthen and grow community foundations in the Netherlands. Currently, there are four community foundations in the Netherlands, and they are located in Alkmaar, Amstelveen, Schiedam, and Texel. Stichting SBF has initiated three new pilot projects in Rotterdam, Eindhoven, and Maastricht. Responding to the growing interest in community foundations in the Netherlands, the grantee and its partners will provide technical assistance to new community foundations, bring existing community foundations together in a network, and raise awareness among government and society at large about the power and potential of community foundations. Established in The Hague in 2006, Stichting SBF promotes the social role and significance of philanthropy in the Netherlands.

title: Association of Community Advice Offices of South Africa (ACAOSA)
grantee: National Alliance for the Development of Community Advice Offices
description: The National Alliance for the Development of Community Advice Offices is committed to the development and long-term sustainability of community-based advice offices in South Africa. Initially a project of the Black Sash Trust, the grantee was established in 2005 by human rights organizations in response to the limited prospects for the long-term sustainability of community-based advice offices in South Africa. Since 2008, the grantee has been supporting the emergence of a representative voice for community-based advice offices by supporting provincial forums that represent their interests in the country’s nine provinces. Past support assisted with the establishment of the Association of Community-based Advice Offices of South Africa, whose aim is to bring together all community-based advice offices into one national association that will be the voice of this sector. This grant will enable the grantee to assist the association to register as an independent entity, develop its administrative capacity, and develop and manage program and operational plans.

title: Association of Community Advice Offices of South Africa (ACAOSA)
grantee: National Alliance for the Development of Community Advice Offices
description: The National Alliance for the Development of Community Advice Offices is committed to the development and long-term sustainability of community-based advice offices in South Africa. Since 2012, the grantee has been supporting the emergence of a representative voice for community-based advice offices by supporting provincial forums that represent their interests in the country’s nine provinces. Past support assisted with formalizing the forums through the establishment of the Association of Community Advice Offices of South Africa, whose aim is to bring together all community-based advice offices into one national association that will be the voice of this sector. This grant increase will enable the grantee to assist the association to register as an independent entity, develop its administrative capacity through recruiting staff, and develop and manage program and operational plans. The grantee will also host a conference to foster better understanding of the work of community-based advice offices. This grant increase has been made possible by a partnership with Atlantic Philanthropies in support of the community advice office sector.

title: Association of Community Advice Offices of South Africa (ACAOSA)
grantee: National Alliance for the Development of Community Advice Offices
description: The National Alliance for the Development of Community Advice Offices is committed to the development and long-term sustainability of community-based advice offices in South Africa. The grantee, initially a project of the Black Sash Trust, was established in 2005 by human rights organizations in response to the limited prospects for the long-term sustainability of community-based advice offices in South Africa. Past support assisted with the establishment of the Association of Community Advice Offices of South Africa. The association’s aim is to bring together all community-based advice offices into one national association to be the voice of the sector. This grant will enable the grantee to support the Association of Community Advice Offices of South Africa through management support and mentorship; guiding the board and strengthening governance; assisting with developing norms and standards policies for the community advice office sector; and providing training to community-based paralegals through the Dullah Omar School. This grant has been made possible by a partnership with The Atlantic Philanthropies in support of the community advice office sector.

title: Association of Community Advice Offices of South Africa (ACAOSA)
grantee: National Alliance for the Development of Community Advice Offices
description: The National Alliance for the Development of Community Advice Offices is committed to the development and long-term sustainability of community-based advice offices in South Africa. The alliance, initially a project of the Black Sash Trust, was established in 2005 by human rights organizations in response to the limited prospects for the long-term sustainability of community-based advice offices in South Africa. Since 2009, the grantee has been supporting the emergence of a representative voice for community-based advice offices by supporting provincial forums that represent their interests in the country’s nine provinces. The forums have led efforts to formulate guidelines for common service standards, minimum qualifications, and regulations within the community-based advice office sector. This grant will assist efforts to consolidate the work of the forums through the establishment of the Association of Community Advice Offices of South Africa, whose aim is to bring together all community-based advice offices into one national association that will be the voice of this sector.

title: Hunger Solution Center
description: This grant will support the Food Bank of Eastern Michigan’s capital campaign. The goal of the campaign is to raise $5.25 million to renovate a 62,000-square-foot warehouse facility known as the Hunger Solution Center. The grantee anticipates it will serve more clients each year from 2014 through 2021. The Hunger Solution Center will make it possible for the grantee to distribute more fresh and nutritional produce to its clients as well as provide additional warehouse space to improve the collection, processing, distribution, and repacking of emergency food products.

title: Enrique Diemecke 25th Anniversary CD
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: To celebrate the 25th anniversary of conductor Enrique Diemecke as Music Director of the Flint Symphony Orchestra, the Flint Institute of Music will release a CD of his work leading the Flint orchestra. The CD will feature music composed by Maestro Diemecke and performed by the Flint symphony between 1998 and 2011 and will highlight the quality of the Flint Symphony Orchestra under his leadership. A total of 5,000 CDs will be produced for sale, and the recordings will also be available for digital download.

title: Our State of Generosity
description: Our State of Generosity is a project aimed at capturing valuable learning about historical philanthropic leaders and their lessons in leadership in the state of Michigan over the past 40 years to be disseminated through a highly interactive online platform. Lessons will focus on the creation, cooperation, and efficiency of four philanthropy/nonprofit sector statewide infrastructure organizations — Council of Michigan Foundations, Michigan Nonprofit Association, Michigan Community Service Commission, and Grand Valley State University Dorothy A. Johnson Center for Philanthropy. Established in 1992, this center has focused on increasing the efficiency and effectiveness of the charitable sector by conducting research, teaching effective practices, and providing pathways to service. It is a unit of the College of Community and Public Service at Grand Valley State University, which was chartered by the Michigan legislature in 1960 in response to the need for a public, four-year college in Grand Rapids.

title: Executive Search
grantee: Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint
description: Serving more than 4,000 children annually, the Boys & Girls Club of Greater Flint serves as a critical provider of afterschool and summertime programming in several city neighborhoods. This grant will enable the grantee to identify and hire a new executive director and ensure a smooth transition of leadership as the club continues to implement its strategic plan and build its capacity to provide high quality services.

title: Institutional Capacity Building
description: The program goal is to increase constructive and active civic engagement in the development of human rights, tolerance and respect, and other democratic values and practices in Serbia and the region. To this end, the project supports the institutional and programmatic development of the Center for Cultural Decontamination, a long-standing, independent civic and cultural center in Belgrade, Serbia. The grantee is well-known for its promotion of democratic values through performances, exhibitions, concerts, public discussions, lecture series, and other informal educational activities. With Mott Foundation support in 2013-2015, the grantee improved its communication and dissemination capacities in order to increase accessibility of its programming and resources by a broader audience throughout Serbia; strengthened staff, management, and governance structures; and carried out an assessment and strategic planning exercise. During 2015-2017, the grantee will improve the quality and impact of its online presence; develop a long-term risk management and organizational development plan; and increase capacity for monitoring, evaluating, and documenting programmatic activities.

title: Institutional Capacity Building
description: The program goal is to increase constructive and active civic engagement in the development of human rights, tolerance and respect, and other democratic values and practices in Serbia and the region. The Center for Cultural Decontamination is a long-standing, independent civic and cultural center in Belgrade, Serbia, that promotes social inclusion through performances, exhibitions, concerts, public discussions, lecture series, and other informal educational activities. With Mott Foundation support, the grantee will strengthen its programmatic and organizational capacities to continue to play a critical role in Serbia’s democratization process over the coming years. Specific project activities will include improving communication and dissemination capacities in order to increase accessibility of its programming and resources by a broader audience throughout Serbia, strengthening management and governance structures, and carrying out an assessment and planning exercise. The grantee is based in Belgrade, Serbia.

title: Community-based Restorative Justice Mechanisms in Southeast Turkey
grantee: Diyarbakir Institute for Political and Social Research
description: The project goal is to increase the engagement of local communities in the peace process in southeastern Turkey. Established in early 2010 by a diverse group of experts and civil society leaders to provide field-based analysis and policy proposals on key issues, the Diyarbakir Institute for Political and Social Research is now well placed to play a critical role in the peace process. Through this project, the grantee will conduct in-depth, original research on community-based mechanisms that address issues of justice and reconciliation. To empower local communities to help shape the way these issues are addressed, the research will involve extensive consultations with a range of community leaders and stakeholders. Findings and analyses will be shared widely with local communities in the region, civil society organizations, government officials, and the public. There will be a published report in Turkish, Kurdish, and English and public presentations of the findings. The grantee is based in Diyarbakir, Turkey.

title: Cultural, Ecological, and Economic Rejuvenation of the Eastern Black Sea Region
grantee: Yayla (Gola) Culture, Arts, and Ecology Association
description: The project goal is to strengthen civic engagement and community development in the Eastern Black Sea region of Turkey. To this end, the activities within this phase of the project will focus on strengthening the organizational and programmatic capacity of the Yayla (Gola) Culture, Arts, and Ecology Association, a Turkish nonprofit association, to support civic leaders, young people, local community groups, and other stakeholders in this region. During 2014-2015, the grantee relocated its core staff and operations from Istanbul to the Eastern Black Sea region, networked with local civic leaders and nonprofits, and built its capacities for programming and management through site visits and technical assistance from other more experienced Turkish nonprofits. During the grant period, the grantee will build upon this past work and prepare for its longer-term engagement in the Eastern Black Sea region by deepening its connections with local communities and other stakeholders in the region; assessing the needs and priorities of local communities; designing and fundraising for projects and programs; and learning from other, prominent, Turkish nonprofits active in the field. Established in 2006, the grantee’s primary office is based in Arhavi, Turkey.

title: Cultural, Ecological, and Economic Rejuvenation of the Eastern Black Sea Region
grantee: Yayla (Gola) Culture, Arts, and Ecology Association
description: The project goal is to strengthen civic engagement and community development in the Eastern Black Sea region of Turkey. To this end, the project activities will focus on strengthening the organizational and programmatic capacity of the Yayla (Gola) Culture, Arts, and Ecology Association, a Turkish nonprofit association, to support civic leaders, young people, local community groups, and other stakeholders in this region. Since 2006, the grantee has organized an annual cultural and ecological festival in the region that highlights the region’s unique history, culture, and natural resources and brings national and international expertise and attention to both the region’s rich heritage and its challenges. The grantee also has organized workshops and educational opportunities to support sustainable, local community development in the region. During the grant period, the grantee will build upon this past work and prepare for its longer-term engagement in the region by relocating its main office and operations from Istanbul to the region and deepening its connections with local communities and other stakeholders. Established in 2006, the grantee is currently based in Istanbul, Turkey.

title: Local Documentation Centers in the Western Balkans
grantee: SENSE - Central European News Service Ltd.
description: The project goal is to increase civic engagement on issues of truth, justice, and reconciliation in the Western Balkans. To this end, SENSE – Central European News Service Ltd. will support the establishment of one local documentation center in Pristina, Kosovo, and two online, interactive documentation sites. The center and the online sites will provide access to information and testimony from the proceedings of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia in The Hague to a wide range of stakeholders. The grantee will draw from its archive of audiovisual material gathered from its regular monitoring of the tribunal’s proceedings since 1998, as well as its daily and weekly reports and analyses of the tribunal’s work. During 2014-2015, the grantee provided content and technical assistance on its presentation to the first local documentation center in the Balkans in the town of Srebrenica, Bosnia-Herzegovina, the scene of the massacre of nearly 8,000 Muslim men and boys in July 1995. The grantee also organized exhibitions of certain elements of the content of this center in Zagreb and Belgrade, and it launched the first online documentation site, which focused on the events surrounding the Croatian military offensive in August 1995. The grantee is registered in Zagreb, Croatia, and works mainly from its offices at the tribunal in The Hague.

title: Local Documentation Centers in the Western Balkans
grantee: SENSE - Central European News Service Ltd.
description: The project goal is to increase civic engagement on issues of truth, justice, and reconciliation in the Western Balkans. To this end, SENSE – Central European News Service Ltd. will establish up to five local documentation centers in Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia, and Kosovo. The sites being considered are Srebrenica, Vukovar, Pristina, Sarajevo, and Prijedor. These centers will provide access to information and testimony from the proceedings of the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia in The Hague to the people most affected by the conflicts. The grantee will draw from its archive of audio-visual material gathered from its regular monitoring of the tribunal’s proceedings since 1998 as well as its daily and weekly reports and analyses of the tribunal’s work. Each center will be equipped with state-of-the-art technology for accessing and searching relevant material and reports from the tribunal’s work. The grantee is registered in Zagreb, Croatia, and works mainly from its offices at the tribunal in The Hague.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Youth Initiative for Human Rights - Croatia
description: The program goal is to engage young people in decisionmaking processes to promote and strengthen the rule of law, accountability, and transitional justice in Croatia and the Western Balkan region. The Youth Initiative for Human Rights – Croatia focuses on building the capacity of young people to address these issues and on increasing dialogue among young people from all sides of the conflicts in the former Yugoslavia. During 2013-2015, the grantee organized training on transitional justice and civic engagement for young people from war-affected regions of Croatia, worked with young people and local communities to establish memorials, monitored and reported on progress to identify missing persons from the conflicts of the 1990s and prosecution of war crimes, organized educational activities, and developed regional exchanges and study visits for young people. During the grant period, the grantee will advocate for accountability and responsibility for war crimes and human rights abuses; foster a culture of truth-telling and acknowledgement; promote justice for victims; and encourage coexistence and respect for religious, ethnic, and other differences. The grantee will also strengthen its capacities by diversifying income sources through new partnerships and social entrepreneurship and continuing to develop regional programming with partner organizations in Serbia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and Kosovo. The grantee is based in Zagreb.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Youth Initiative for Human Rights - Croatia
description: The program goal is to engage young people in decisionmaking processes in order to promote and strengthen the rule of law, accountability, and transitional justice in Croatia and the Western Balkan region. Through a variety of activities, the Youth Initiative for Human Rights – Croatia will focus on building the capacity of young people to address these issues and increasing dialogue among young people from all sides of the conflicts in the former Yugoslavia. During the grant period, the grantee will advocate for accountability and responsibility for war crimes and human rights abuses, foster reconciliation through the development of a culture of truth-telling and acknowledgement, and strengthen leadership in these areas among young political leaders and students. The grantee will also strengthen its capacities by diversifying income sources through new partnerships and continuing to develop regional programming with partner organizations in Serbia, Bosnia-Herzegovina, and Kosovo. The grantee is based in Zagreb.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Youth Initiative for Human Rights - Croatia
description: The program goal is to engage young people in decision-making processes in order to promote and strengthen the rule of law, accountability, and transitional justice in Croatia and the Western Balkan region. Through a variety of activities, the Youth Initiative for Human Rights – Croatia will focus on building the capacity of young people to address these issues and on increasing dialogue among young people from all sides of the conflicts in the former Yugoslavia. Specifically, during the grant period the grantee will advocate for accountability and responsibility for war crimes and human rights abuses; foster a culture of truth-telling and acknowledgement; promote justice for victims; and encourage coexistence and respect for religious, ethnic, and other differences. The grantee will also strengthen its capacities by hiring a new executive director and increasing project management skills of other staff, diversifying income sources through new partnerships and social entrepreneurship, expanding programs to local communities, and developing regional programming. The grantee is based in Zagreb.

title: Monitoring BRICS Development in Brazil
description: In 2014 and 2015, Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa took steps to formalize the New Development Bank, a process that has been in formation for the past seven years. ActionAid Brasil, founded in 1999 and a member of the international ActionAid network, has been monitoring this new development finance institution and building capacity to engage and influence the Brazilian participation in this alliance. This grant renewal would support the grantee to consolidate and continue its work to achieve and strengthen social and environmental standards governing international financial flows, particularly from Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa. The grantee will also strengthen its network of nongovernmental organizations participating in related international dialogues.

title: Monitoring BRICS Development in Brazil
description: ActionAid Brasil is part of an international network that has been monitoring the development of the New Development Bank by BRICS countries—Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa—and analyzing the impacts of Chinese investment in the region. This grant renewal will enable the grantee to consolidate its national and international networks and monitor two BRICS summits.

title: Monitoring BRICS Development in Brazil
description: Over the past five years, Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa have been building a political alliance called BRICS, and in early 2013 announced the intention to create a BRICS development bank. In this project, ActionAid Brasil, a member of the international ActionAid network since 1999, will strengthen Brazilian civil society’s capacity to monitor and influence Brazilian government engagement in BRICS activities and related global governance forums. The project’s objectives are to strengthen the social and environmental standards governing international financial flows, particularly from BRICS, and help build a network of nongovernmental organizations participating in related international dialogue.

title: Summer Youth Expo
description: In Flint and Genesee County, there are many organizations offering free or low-cost summer programs, camps, educational and employment opportunities, feeding programs, and other services for children and young people. To help familiarize and encourage parents, particularly those families living in low-income neighborhoods, to take advantage of these activities, Priority Children is sponsoring a free Summer Youth Expo in May at the centrally located Riverfront Banquet Center. Between 35 to 50 local organizations will be on-site to meet with parents, address their concerns, and encourage them to take advantage of summer learning and recreational opportunities.

title: Increasing Literacy Levels for At-Risk Youth in College-Connected Programs
description: This grant will enable Mott Community College to continue an intensive and short-term, boot-camp-style program that raises students’ literacy and readiness levels to meet eligibility requirements for job training, high school diploma, GED, and/or postsecondary education programs. In the first year of this initiative, 252 low-skilled students enrolled in this remedial/refresher course with more than 165 increasing their skill levels by two grades. Recommended support will allow the grantee to further develop this course in an effort to boost and improve the academic habits and employability skills of low-skilled students.

title: Increasing Literacy Levels for At-Risk Youth in College-Connected Programs
description: This grant will enable Mott Community College to continue an intensive and short-term, boot-camp style program that raises students’ literacy and readiness levels to meet eligibility requirements for job training, high school diploma, GED, and/or postsecondary education programs. In the first year of this initiative, 252 low-skilled students enrolled in this remedial/refresher course with more than 165 increasing their skill levels by two grades. Support will allow Mott Community College to further develop this course in an effort to boost and improve the academic habits and employability of low-skilled students.

title: Increasing Literacy Levels for At-Risk Youth in College-Connected Programs
description: This grant will enable Mott Community College to continue Restart, an intensive short-term program designed to elevate students’ literacy and readiness levels. The goal is to reconnect participants to education on a path toward obtaining a high school diploma or GED, and pursuing higher education or employment opportunities. In addition to the learning component of the program, eligible students have the opportunity to apply for water distribution employment through Flint WaterWorks. Further, Restart staff will direct participants and their families impacted by water to information and service providers.

title: Increasing Literacy Levels for At-Risk Youth in College-Connected Programs
description: This grant will enable Mott Community College to pilot a remedial/refresher course entitled Literacy Initiative: Increasing Literacy Levels for At-Risk Youth in College-Connected Programs, which is designed to assist students in meeting the eligibility requirements for job training, high school diploma, GED, and/or postsecondary education programs. Through an intensive and short-term boot camp-style course, Mott Community College will increase students’ math, reading, computer, and communications skills up to program levels and workplace standards. Recommended support will enable Mott Community College to combine technology and instructional techniques designed to match the learning style and interests of the learners to engage students in intensive learning situations that will accelerate learning rates, boost basic skills, and improve academic habits and employability skills.

title: Financial and Program Planning Research Project
description: Genesee County Parks & Recreation Commission provides 11,000 acres of high quality recreation areas and year-round programming to area residents. Due to declining property values, the grantee is faced with a structural deficit that requires a sustainable solution. With Mott support, the grantee will research and identify a path to long-term financial stability. The project will include conducting surveys to better understand the public’s interests in the park system and updating the grantee’s Parks, Recreation, and Open Space Plan.

title: Building the Future of Philanthropy
description: This grant increase will support the Foundation Center’s six-year, $23.7-million capital campaign to position it as the leading research and data organization on global philanthropy. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) build a global data platform for philanthropy encompassing international data, standards and taxonomy, new forms of philanthropy, and knowledge products; 2) ensure that the grantee’s technology provides a strong foundation for its work via cutting edge applications and tools; and 3) empower donors with additional knowledge tools such as affinity group and regional association Web templates, advanced custom Web portals, and a new research portal. The investment plan also includes financing global philanthropy information centers, an internal venture fund, and physical space redesign. Established in 1956, the Foundation Center is dedicated to fostering public understanding of the foundation field by collecting, organizing, analyzing, and disseminating information on foundations, corporate giving, and related subjects.

title: Building the Future of Philanthropy
description: This grant increase will support the Foundation Center’s six-year, $23.7 million capital campaign to position it as the leading research and data organization on global philanthropy (FC2020 Investment Plan). Specifically, the grantee will: 1) build a global data platform for philanthropy encompassing international data, standards and taxonomy, new forms of philanthropy, and knowledge products; 2) ensure that the grantee’s technology provides a strong foundation for its work via cutting edge applications and tools; and 3) empower donors with additional knowledge tools such as affinity group and regional association Web templates, advanced custom Web portals, and a new research portal.
