title: Community Resource Centers in Ukraine
description: The program goal is to increase opportunities for participatory community development in Ukraine. To this end, the Kherson’s Regional Charity and Health Foundation will continue to support a network of community-based legal and information resource centers throughout Ukraine, enhancing their role as facilitators and incubators of active civic engagement. During the previous grant period, the grantee significantly improved an online portal to coordinate and integrate the activities of the legal information center network and expanded the network’s capacity to respond to urgent needs, including legal aid to internally displaced persons, as well as military personnel and their families. The grantee also produced a series of documentary films that appeared in human rights film festivals. Founded in 1989, Kherson’s Regional Charity and Health Foundation works to inspire citizens to take responsible action in order to promote the rule of law and democracy in Ukraine.

title: Community Resource Centers in Ukraine
description: The program goal is to support access to justice in small communities in Ukraine through strengthening of local justice institutions. The Charity and Health Foundation will work with community legal centers to help expand practice and understanding of new community-based sheriffs. The grantee and the networks will also research, monitor, and broadly publicize local experiences of how new models of community-based justice are improving lives of citizens. During 2015–2017, the grantee improved an online portal to coordinate and publicize the activities of the network of community legal centers and improved the network’s capacity to respond to present needs, including legal aid to internally displaced persons as well as military personnel and their families. In total, the centers served, directly and through online resources, over 60,000 Ukrainians seeking legal assistance. Based in Kherson, the Charity and Health Foundation works to inspire citizens to take responsible action in order to promote the rule of law and democracy in Ukraine.

title: Community Resource Centers in Ukraine
description: The program goal is to increase opportunities for participatory community development in Ukraine. To this end, the Kherson Regional Charity and Health Foundation will further develop community-based legal and information resource centers throughout Ukraine. Specifically, the grantee will expand the role of legal information centers from providers of legal and information support into facilitators and incubators of active civic engagement. The grantee will create a new online portal in order to support the activities of the legal information center network. Best practices and successes will systematically be collected and disseminated in order to assist centers to be not only responsive to specific requests for assistance but also proactive in helping foster community engagement. Finally, the grantee will produce a series of documentary films that tell the stories of rural residents who used the services of the legal information centers in pursuit of an important community interest. Founded in 1989, the grantee works to inspire citizens to take responsible action in order to promote the rule of law and democracy in Ukraine.

title: Return on Investment Roundtable
grantee: Council for Advancement of Adult Literacy
description: This grant will provide support to the Council for Advancement of Adult Literacy to study and analyze outcomes in adult literacy and workforce skills development. State-by-state surveys and a meeting with thought leaders in the field of adult literacy will form the basis for two reports that will highlight the effectiveness and return on investment of programs that address adult literacy and the skills necessary for successful participation in today’s workforce.

title: Back to the Bricks Policing and Public Safety
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide funds to support public safety enforcement and traffic patrolling at the Back to the Bricks festival in downtown Flint this August. Public safety policing is an essential component of success of the festival that brings thousands of exhibitors and festivalgoers to downtown Flint. The City of Flint is not able to provide the necessary additional police services free of charge due to a decline in municipal revenues.

title: Event Policing and Public Safety
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide funds to support public safety enforcement and traffic patrolling at festivals in downtown Flint. Public safety policing is an essential component of the festivals’ success which take place in the downtown Flint area and attract thousands of exhibitors and festivalgoers. The City of Flint is not in a financial position to provide the necessary additional police services due to a decline in municipal revenues.

title: Back to the Bricks Policing and Public Safety
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide funds to support public safety enforcement and traffic patrolling at the Back to the Bricks festival in downtown Flint this August. Public safety policing is an essential component of the success of the festival, which this year is anticipated to attract more than 500,000 exhibitors and festival goers. The City of Flint has traditionally absorbed the cost of police and traffic control services for the event, but is no longer able to provide these services free of charge due to a decline in municipal revenues.

title: College and Career Pathway Readiness: A District Audit for Sequencing Success
description: The grant provides support to the 114th Partnership to conduct an initial assessment as part of a strategic planning process for the Flint Community Schools. The assessment will provide information about the district, as well as recommendations on how to proceed with strategic planning. Comparative data from other districts will provide a framework for better understanding the outcomes that have been achieved for school districts engaged in a strategic planning process. With the assessment, recommendations, and comparative data, the Flint Community Schools can make informed decisions about implementing the strategic, structural, and cultural changes necessary to support college and career-ready goals for students.

title: Philanthropy House
description: Located in the heart of Brussels, Philanthropy House will increase the visibility, effectiveness, and potential impact of the foundation sector in Europe. Through conferences, debates, trainings, and exhibitions, it will welcome visitors to discover the important work of independent foundations in Europe. Philanthropy House was conceived and supported by six foundations located across Europe. Due to open its doors in November 2013, Philanthropy House will provide office space for leading European-level philanthropic infrastructure organizations, including the European Foundation Centre, the European Venture Philanthropy Association, and the Network of European Foundations. Funding from the Mott Foundation will support: 1) information, communications, and technology costs; and 2) the exhibition area and resource center on the ground floor of Philanthropy House. Established in 1989, the European Foundation Centre is an international association of foundations and corporate funders dedicated to strengthening European philanthropy.

title: Community Schools Technical Assistance
description: This grant provides support to the Children’s Aid Society for capacity building for the development and expansion of community schools in the city of Flint. The grantee’s National Center for Community Schools will work in partnership with the local community schools working group and newly-hired community schools staff in implementing nationally recognized best practices and developing a plan for expanding the scope and impact of community education being provided in the Flint Community School district.

title: Community Schools Technical Assistance
description: This grant provides support to the Children’s Aid Society for capacity building for the development and expansion of community schools across the state of Michigan and in the city of Flint. The grantee’s National Center for Community Schools will work in partnership with the Kent School Services Network on the statewide work to bring the leading national and local knowledge and best practices around community education to Michigan’s schools. Technical assistance will be provided to Flint Community Schools to develop a plan for expanding the scope of community education being provided in the district.

title: Superintendent Technical Assistance
description: This grant will provide support and technical assistance to the interim superintendent of Flint Community Schools. Flint Community Schools have undergone significant changes over the past decade, including declining enrollment and the need to close buildings and reduce staff. Ongoing decisions related to an operating deficit, a reduced school population, and an increased need to focus on math and technology require additional administrative support.

title: Superintendent Technical Assistance
description: This grant will provide support and technical assistance to the interim superintendent of the Flint Community Schools. The Flint Community Schools have undergone significant changes over the past decade, including declining enrollment and a growing deficit. Ongoing decisions related to student retention, implementation of a new educational plan, and improving financial and operating efficiencies require additional administrative support.

title: Superintendent Technical Assistance
description: This grant increase will provide support and technical assistance to the interim superintendent of the Flint Community Schools. The Flint Community Schools have undergone significant changes over the past decade, including declining enrollment and a growing deficit. Ongoing decisions related to student retention, implementation of a new educational plan, and improving financial and operating efficiencies require additional administrative support.

title: Superintendent Technical Assistance
description: This grant will provide support and technical assistance to the superintendent of the Flint Community Schools. The Flint Community Schools have been working on a districtwide turnaround effort with the aim of improving student academic outcomes and gaining financial stability. Ongoing decisions related to student retention, professional development, and improving financial and operating efficiencies require additional administrative support.

title: Superintendent Technical Assistance
description: This grant increase will provide technical assistance to the superintendent of the Flint Community Schools for the 2016-17 school year. Strategic initiatives that require additional support are being implemented to continue the district’s turnaround efforts, including building the capacity of staff, leadership, and the board, which has become even more important with the issues surrounding the city’s water system.

title: Superintendent Technical Assistance
description: This grant renewal will provide support for technical assistance to the superintendent of Flint Community Schools. The superintendent is implementing strategic initiatives as part of the ongoing district turnaround efforts that require additional support including central office leadership capacity building, grant writing, training and professional development, and architectural assistance.

title: Superintendent Technical Assistance
description: This grant will provide support and technical assistance to the interim superintendent of the Flint Community Schools. The grantee has undergone significant changes over the past decade, including dropping enrollment and the need to close buildings and reduce staff. Ongoing decisions related to an operating deficit, a reduced school population, and an increased need to focus on math and technology require additional administrative support.

title: STEM Support
description: This grant provides support to the Flint Community Schools for the Brownell Holmes STEM Academy to bolster teaching and learning within the developing STEM curriculum. Students will have the opportunity to participate in engaging and educational field trips; teachers will be provided with critical professional development in the STEM field; instructional materials in support of the STEM curriculum will be purchased; and two STEM technicians will be supported to aid in lesson preparation, classroom instruction, and professional development.

title: STEM Support
description: This grant provides support to the Flint Community Schools for the newly formed Brownell Holmes STEM (science, technology, engineering, and math) pod. A STEM facilitator will help develop and implement STEM curriculum, coordinate teacher and staff professional development, and work with community partners who can bring specialized STEM experiences to students. The STEM facilitator will also coordinate the purchase of supplies critical to a STEM curriculum, including tablet computers, science and engineering kits, and laboratory equipment, and will host engaging events for families and community partners to help create a sense of ownership of the STEM pod within the neighborhood.

title: Sarvis Center
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will allow the Flint Cultural Center Corporation to demolish the Sarvis Conference Center building on the cultural center campus. The grantee currently owns and maintains the 33-acre cultural center campus, manages the operations of The Whiting, Sloan Museum, and Longway Planetarium, and leases buildings to the Flint Institute of Arts and the Flint Institute of Music (including Bower Theater, home of the Flint Youth Theatre). The grantee will raze the building and prepare the land for future repurposing.

title: Sarvis Center
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will allow the Flint Cultural Center Corporation to purchase two properties on the cultural center campus. The grantee currently owns and maintains the 33-acre cultural center campus, manages the operations of The Whiting, Sloan Museum, and Longway Planetarium, and leases buildings to the Flint Institute of Arts and the Flint Institute of Music (including Bower Theater, home of the Flint Youth Theatre). The grantee will purchase the Sarvis Conference Center and Food Services building from the Flint Community Schools. Additional funds will allow the grantee to conduct an environmental assessment of the properties, evaluate potential reuse options for the buildings, and revise the Flint Cultural Center campus master plan to incorporate these properties.

title: Index of Philanthropic Freedom
description: The program goal is to measure philanthropic freedom in developed and emerging economies by examining the barriers and incentives for individuals, foundations, and corporations to donate money and time to civil society organizations. In June 2015, the Hudson Institute’s Center for Global Prosperity released the first-ever Index of Philanthropic Freedom which surveyed, ranked, and compared the ease of giving, both cross-border and domestic, in 64 countries around the world. During 2016-2017, the grantee will further popularize the index, conduct a survey methodology review, expand the number of countries to 75, and publish a new edition in 2017. The Hudson Institute is a policy research organization dedicated to innovative research and analysis that promotes global security, prosperity, and freedom. One of its policy centers, the Center for Global Prosperity, raises awareness about the role of the private sector, both for-profit and nonprofit, in the creation of economic growth and prosperity in any country.

title: Index of Philanthropic Freedom
description: The program goal is to foster the development of a conducive environment for philanthropy across countries by providing rigorous, comparative data and by raising awareness and understanding of philanthropy, especially in developing countries. In June 2015, the Hudson Institute’s Center for Global Prosperity released the first-ever “Index of Philanthropic Freedom” which surveyed, ranked, and compared the ease of giving, both cross border and domestic, in 64 countries around the world. Due to a change in Hudson Institute priorities, the index is transitioning to Indiana University’s Lilly Family School of Philanthropy. The school will enhance the research methodology, produce, and disseminate an updated 2017 “Index of Philanthropic Freedom”. It will also increase the number of countries surveyed to 75. The Lilly Family School of Philanthropy was founded in 2012. Its mission is to increase the understanding of philanthropy and improve its practice worldwide through critical inquiry, interdisciplinary research, teaching, training, and civic engagement.

title: Global Philanthropy Environment Index
description: The program goal is to foster the development of a conducive environment for philanthropy across countries by providing rigorous, comparative data and by raising awareness and understanding of philanthropy, especially in developing countries. In 2016, Indiana University’s Lilly Family School of Philanthropy took responsibility for publishing the Index of Philanthropic Freedom, which was first published by the Hudson Institute in 2015. Extensive research and analysis across 79 countries took place in 2016 and 2017, and the index will be published in April 2018. Following the publication, which will include 79 country reports, 11 regional reports, and one global report, the grantee will create related online and printed educational materials and organize a series of events in the United States and globally to share results and generate debate. The Lilly Family School of Philanthropy at Indiana University was founded in 2012. Its mission is to increase the understanding of philanthropy and improve its practice worldwide through critical inquiry, interdisciplinary research, teaching, training, and civic engagement.

title: Index of Philanthropic Freedom
description: The program goal is to measure philanthropic freedom in developed and emerging economies by examining the barriers and incentives for individuals, foundations, and corporations to donate money and time to civil society organizations. The Hudson Institute’s Center for Global Prosperity will create the first-ever Index of Philanthropic Freedom which will survey, rank, and compare the ease of giving, both cross-border and domestic, for an estimated 55 countries. Countries will be evaluated on: 1) the fairness and ease of nonprofit registration, operation, and dissolution; 2) tax incentives; and 3) ease of cross-border financial flows. The Hudson Institute is a policy research organization dedicated to innovative research and analysis that promotes global security, prosperity, and freedom. One of its policy centers, the Center for Global Prosperity, raises awareness about the central role of the private sector, both for-profit and nonprofit, in the creation of economic growth and prosperity in any country.

title: Seasonal Care Assistance
description: This grant will provide support to the Old Newsboys of Flint, Inc., an organization that has served thousands of low-income families in Genesee County with warm clothes, shoes, coats, hygiene products, and toys since 1924. The grantee meets the needs of children and families following disastrous emergencies, during the holiday season, and when school-aged children are in need of basic clothing items to attend and participate at school.

title: Seasonal Care Assistance
description: This grant will provide support to the Old Newsboys of Flint, Inc., an organization that since 1924 has served thousands of low-income families in Genesee County with warm clothes, shoes, coats, hygiene products, and toys. The grantee meets the needs of children and families following disastrous emergencies, during the holiday season, and when school-aged children are in need of basic clothing items to attend and participate at school.

title: Powerful Pathways: How High School Cultures Promote College and Career Awareness, Readiness, and Success
description: This grant will enable the American Institutes for Research to undertake an experimental study to determine the impact of school culture on promoting and influencing college and career awareness, readiness, and success for low-income students in Michigan. The grantee will identify a sample of eight academically successful Michigan high schools similar in size, academic performance, and socioeconomic status to compare and distinguish key differences in school culture as they relate to student success in school and after graduation. Recommended support will allow the grantee to test the efficacy of school culture in promoting life-long learning and apply findings from the study to improve the educational experiences of all high school students in Michigan.

title: School and Community Programming
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will allow the Flint Cultural Center Corporation, in partnership with other cultural center institutions, to provide educational programming to students attending Flint Community Schools and other at-risk students living in the community. Declining school budgets have forced area schools to reduce or eliminate arts and cultural programming from their curriculum, as well as restrict field trips to the Flint Cultural Center to take advantage of the high quality educational programs it offers. Due to Flint’s high poverty rate, many families cannot afford to take their children to the cultural center. The Flint Cultural Center educational outreach program will provide Flint students access to various educational programs and activities available from any Flint Cultural Center organization during the 2015-16 school year.

title: School and Community Programming
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will allow the Flint Cultural Center Corporation, in partnership with other cultural center institutions, to provide educational programming to students attending Flint Community Schools and other at-risk students living in the community. Due to the Flint water crisis, additional wraparound programs and educational opportunities are especially important to developing children. Declining school budgets have forced area schools to reduce or eliminate arts and cultural programming from their curriculum, as well as restrict field trips to the Flint Cultural Center to take advantage of the high quality educational programs it offers. Because of Flint’s high poverty rate, many families are not able to afford to take their children to the cultural center. The Flint Cultural Center’s Educational Outreach Program provides students access to various educational programs and activities available from any Flint Cultural Center organization during the 2016-17 school year.

title: School and Community Programming
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will allow the Flint Cultural Center Corporation, in partnership with other cultural center institutions, to provide educational programming to students attending Flint Community Schools and other at-risk students living in the community. In light of the Flint water crisis, it is more important than ever for Flint children to receive wraparound services and have exposure to different types of educational opportunities. The Flint Cultural Center Corporation educational outreach program will provide Flint students access to various programs and activities available from any Flint Cultural Center institution during the 2017-18 school year.

title: School and Community Programming
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will allow the Flint Cultural Center Corporation, in partnership with other cultural center institutions, to provide educational programming to students attending Flint Community Schools and other at-risk students living in the community. In light of the Flint water crisis, it is more important than ever for Flint children to receive wraparound services and have exposure to different types of educational opportunities. The Flint Cultural Center Corporation educational outreach program will provide Flint students with access to a variety of programs and activities available from any Flint Cultural Center institution during the school year.

title: School and Community Programming
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will allow the Flint Cultural Center Corporation, in partnership with other cultural center institutions, to provide educational programming to students attending Flint Community Schools and other at-risk students living in the community. The grantee’s educational outreach program will provide Flint students with access to a variety of programs and activities available from any Flint Cultural Center institution during the school year and summer months.

title: Flint Community Schools Programming
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will allow the Flint Cultural Center Corporation, in partnership with other cultural center institutions, to provide educational programming to students attending Flint Community Schools. Declining school budgets have forced Flint schools, like many districts, to reduce or eliminate arts and cultural programming from its curriculum, as well as restrict field trips to the Flint Cultural Center to take advantage of the high quality educational programs they offer. Due to Flint’s high poverty rate, many families are not able to afford to take their children to the cultural center. The Flint Cultural Center Educational Outreach Program will provide Flint students access to various educational programs and activities available from any Flint Cultural Center organization during the 2013-14 school year.

title: Alaska Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant to Alaska Children’s Trust will support the Alaska Statewide Afterschool Network to continue to build an afterschool and summer learning system that improves outcomes for children and youth through school-based or school-linked afterschool programs. Over the next three years, the network will support the development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) engage rural tribal organizations and their leadership across Alaska; 2) develop a plan to diversify funding to support the network; and 3) establish afterschool quality standards and youth worker core competencies for Alaska.

title: Alaska Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Alaska Children’s Trust, which coordinates the Alaska Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships, and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) create an Alaskan Afterschool Leadership Development Program to cultivate a diverse group of key champions; 2) develop a comprehensive plan to increase resources and quality for afterschool programs; 3) develop an afterschool program quality improvement system; and 4) support the development and distribution of the new afterschool program content in collaboration with the Foundation’s thematic partners.

title: Alaska Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Alaska Children’s Trust to coordinate a statewide afterschool network in Alaska. Over the next three years, the Alaska Statewide Afterschool Network will build a statewide coalition in support of afterschool programs, and coordinate a unified vision to inform policy and quality afterschool initiatives. During this grant, the network’s initiatives and priorities will include: 1) establishing the network as the convener for afterschool programming in the state of Alaska; 2) developing policies and securing resources to support school-based/school-linked afterschool programs; and 3) establishing standards to increase the number of high quality afterschool programs in Alaska.

title: Property Purchase
description: This grant provides support to Kettering University for the purchase of three properties along the University Avenue corridor. Purchasing these properties is believed to be an important step in securing strategic parcels along the corridor. The lots and structures will then be improved through collaboration with the University Avenue Corridor Coalition for suitable repurposing or returning the lots to green space.

title: Community Advice Offices and Farm/Forestry Committees Project
geographic_focus: Western Cape, Province of the, Eastern Cape, Province of
description: The Southern Cape Land Committee was established in 1987 and works with rural communities, farmworkers and farm dwellers, and small-scale farmers to create the conditions for agrarian reform. Past support assisted the grantee to educate people on farms about their rights and how to access them. Support was provided to eight rural community advice offices and 35 farmworker committees, representing the interests of over 2,200 farmworkers and farm dwellers. This grant will allow the grantee to support community advice offices and farm and forestry workers in rural parts of the Eastern and Western Cape provinces. The support will include assisting communities to organize themselves and understand their rights so that they can engage decisionmakers on accessing these rights, conducting research to better understand the living and working conditions of poor people on farms, and producing and disseminating information that enables people to access their rights.

title: Strengthening Access to Justice Through Community Advice Office Support Project
description: The Support Centre for Land Change (formerly known as the Southern Cape Land Committee) was established in 1987 and works with rural communities, farmworkers, farm dwellers, and small-scale farmers to create the conditions for reform. Support enabled the grantee to support community advice offices and farm and forestry workers in rural parts of the Eastern Cape and Western Cape provinces of South Africa. The support included assisting communities to organize themselves and understand their rights so they can engage decisionmakers on accessing these rights, conducting research to better understand the living and working conditions of poor people on farms, and producing and disseminating information that enables people to access their rights. This grant will enable the grantee to strengthen community advice offices so that they can better support farmworkers and poor people who live on farms.

title: Support to Advice Offices and Farm Communities
geographic_focus: Western Cape, Province of the, Eastern Cape, Province of
description: The Southern Cape Land Committee was established in 1987 and works with rural communities, farmworkers and dwellers, and small-scale farmers to create the conditions for agrarian reform. Over the next two years, the Support to Advice Offices and Farm Communities project will educate people on farms about their rights and how to access them. The grantee will work with 10 rural advice offices and 34 area farm committees, representing the interests of farmworkers and dwellers living on 298 farms in 11 local municipalities in the Eastern and Western Cape provinces of South Africa. The grantee will train farm committees and advice offices to address labor and tenure violations on farms and support advice offices to improve their fundraising and governance and administration systems.

title: Michigan Organizing Collaborative
description: The Harriet Tubman Center was established in 2008 to train community organizers with an emphasis on working in Michigan and the Midwest. The grantee also incubates new community organizing initiatives. This grant will provide partial support for a project to form a collaborative of community organizing groups in Michigan.

title: Increasing Food Distribution
description: This grant will provide funds to Carriage Town Ministries to purchase food in order to serve meals to the homeless and those in need of food assistance who come to the shelter. The grantee provides important safety-net services to individuals and families in the Flint area who are homeless or near-homeless, including food, safe and warm shelter, clothes, personal hygiene products, health services, and life skills courses.

title: Colorado Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Civic Canopy to coordinate the statewide afterschool network in Colorado. Over the next three years, the Colorado Statewide Afterschool Network will coordinate a statewide coalition in support of afterschool programs and build a unified vision to inform policy and increase quality afterschool initiatives. During this grant period, the network’s initiatives and priorities will include: 1) developing a network of statewide, regional, and local programs and partners to build public support around afterschool in Colorado; 2) supporting the development of policies that lead to long-term sustainable funding for afterschool; and 3) increasing the quality and success of afterschool programs by creating new professional development opportunities and resources.

title: Colorado Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Colorado Nonprofit Development Center which coordinates the Colorado Statewide Afterschool Network to continue development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) creating regional out-of-school time networks to enhance local partnerships; 2) developing a comprehensive plan to increase resources for out-of-school time programs and the network; and 3) fostering a system for training and technical assistance to ensure high quality, out-of-school time programming.

title: Colorado Statewide Afterschool Partnership
description: This grant to Civic Canopy will support partnership development among afterschool stakeholders in Colorado and enable the establishment of a cohesive statewide afterschool network. The grantee will bring together key decisionmakers and diverse afterschool programs and supporters around issues impacting afterschool and expanded learning programs. Through this Colorado Statewide Afterschool Partnership grant, activities will include holding a partner convening on afterschool and the development of a plan to expand afterschool opportunities at the state level.

title: Hawaii Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the University of Hawaii to coordinate a statewide afterschool network in Hawaii. Over the next three years, the Hawaii Statewide Afterschool Network will build a statewide coalition in support of afterschool programs and coordinate a unified vision to inform policy and increase quality afterschool initiatives. During this grant period, the network’s initiatives and priorities will include: 1) creating an alliance of statewide and local partners participating in the network; 2) developing standards for afterschool programs; and 3) supporting quality improvement measures to strengthen existing afterschool programs.

title: Hawaii Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the University of Hawaii which coordinates the Hawaii Statewide Afterschool Network to continue development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) hosting convenings and build partnerships with the outer islands, rural partners, and charter schools; 2) increasing dedicated afterschool resources through new partnerships with business and philanthropy; and 3) developing a self-assessment tool and resources to increase the number of programs implementing quality standards.

title: Hawaii Statewide Afterschool Partnership
description: Kaho’omiki will develop a coalition of organizations involved in afterschool and out-of-school expanded learning activities, as well as other community, business, and government organizations, to establish the first Hawaii Statewide Afterschool Network. The Hawaii partnership will focus on raising awareness of the importance of afterschool and summer learning opportunities to students’ academic and personal success. In addition to supporting the development of a statewide afterschool network, this Hawaii Statewide Afterschool Partnership grant will allow Hawaii to convene a statewide expanded learning summit.

title: Idaho Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Mountain States Group, Inc., to coordinate the statewide afterschool network in Idaho. Over the next three years, the Idaho Statewide Afterschool Network will build a statewide coalition in support of afterschool programs and coordinate a unified vision to inform policy and increase quality afterschool initiatives. During this grant period, the network’s initiatives and priorities will include: 1) expanding, informing, and engaging key stakeholders in the network; 2) designing and implementing targeted messaging to build awareness of afterschool and its impact on youth; and 3) assessing and mapping the afterschool programs throughout Idaho.

title: Idaho Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Jannus, Inc., which coordinates the Idaho Statewide Afterschool Network to continue development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) increasing communications activities to build public awareness about the importance of afterschool; 2) implementing new fundraising strategies to increase support for afterschool programs; and 3) creating and promoting a school-age quality track for afterschool providers.

title: Idaho Statewide Afterschool Partnership
description: The University of Idaho Foundation’s 4-H program and the Idaho State Department of Education’s 21st Century Community Learning Centers are coordinating efforts to establish an Idaho Statewide Afterschool Network. The Idaho partnership is focused on enhancing life skills and educational opportunities for children and youth, and will work to raise public awareness, provide leadership development and training, and develop standards that link school and community afterschool programs. Through the Idaho Statewide Afterschool Partnership grant the grantee will: 1) convene an Idaho Statewide Afterschool Network conference; and 2) work with a broad-based state alliance to define the vision and mission of a statewide afterschool network and expanded learning effort.

title: Montana Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Greater Gallatin United Way to coordinate the statewide afterschool network in Montana. Over the next three years, the Montana Statewide Afterschool Network will continue to build a statewide coalition in support of afterschool programs and coordinate a unified vision to inform policy and increase quality afterschool initiatives. During this grant period, the network’s initiatives and priorities will include: 1) assessing the need for high quality afterschool programs; 2) building relationships with current and potential afterschool supporters and stakeholders; and 3) increasing the resources available to support the network and afterschool programs.

title: Montana Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Rural Dynamics, Inc., which coordinates the Montana Statewide Afterschool Network to continue development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) increasing communications activities to build public awareness about the importance of afterschool; 2) increasing dedicated afterschool resources through new partnerships with businesses, philanthropy, schools, and communities; and 3) partnering with the Montana Office of Public Instruction to include afterschool courses in the online learning hub for educators.

title: Montana Statewide Afterschool Partnership
description: This grant to Greater Gallatin United Way will support the establishment of a Montana Statewide Afterschool Partnership to focus on increasing the availability of quality afterschool and expanded learning programs. The grantee will work to identify and convene a group of statewide partners to further develop the capacity of afterschool programs to meet the needs of Montana students. In addition to supporting the development of a statewide afterschool partnership, this grant will enable the grantee to inventory afterschool programs throughout Montana to determine their challenges, strengths, and how programs can better connect to their communities.

title: Tennessee Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the United Ways of Tennessee to coordinate a statewide afterschool network in Tennessee. Over the next three years, the Tennessee Statewide Afterschool Network will build a statewide coalition in support of afterschool programs and coordinate a unified vision to inform policy and increase quality afterschool initiatives. During this grant period, the network’s initiatives and priorities will include: 1) creating a sustainable structure of statewide, regional, and local partnerships for impacting policy, decisionmakers, and public will; 2) securing resources to sustain new and existing school-based and school-linked afterschool programming; and 3) implementing new quality initiatives for afterschool programs.

title: Tennessee Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the United Ways of Tennessee which coordinates the Tennessee Statewide Afterschool Network to continue development of policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The network’s specific initiatives will include: 1) developing an educational systems task force to make more intentional linkages to educational system partners and develop school-based and school-linked afterschool programming; 2) developing a comprehensive plan to increase resources for afterschool programs; and 3) updating Tennessee’s School Age Development Standards and creating a training module to ensure effective implementation.

title: Tennessee Statewide Afterschool Partnership
description: This grant will support the United Ways of Tennessee to establish a statewide partnership that will expand access and improve the quality of afterschool programs on behalf of children and youth. The Tennessee partnership will focus on the long-term goal of building public awareness and developing policy initiatives that will improve and sustain high quality afterschool programs. As part of this Tennessee Statewide Afterschool Partnership grant, the grantee’s activities will include creating an advisory group to support the partnership, and hosting a statewide partnership summit to develop a sustainability plan for the initiative and a future network.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Cities Initiative
geographic_focus: Ohio, Pennsylvania, Quebec, Illinois, Ontario, Michigan, New York, Minnesota, Wisconsin, Indiana
description: Cities play an important role in the management, protection, and restoration of their local water sources. Municipal leaders make daily decisions related to drinking water, wastewater, and waterfront development. The Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Cities Initiative brings a binational coalition of mayors together to support the protection and restoration of the Great Lakes. With prior Mott support, the grantee worked to halt the spread of invasive species, encouraged sustainable water management practices, and increased the organization’s membership base. With renewed Mott support, the grantee will also help reduce toxic algal blooms in the Great Lakes and take steps to strengthen its own organizational capacity.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Cities Initiative
description: The Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Cities Initiative brings a bi-national coalition of mayors together to support the protection and restoration of the Great Lakes. With prior Mott support, the grantee worked to halt the spread of invasive species, encourage sustainable water management practices, reduce toxic algal blooms, and increase the grantee’s membership base. This renewal grant will allow the grantee to continue and expand these efforts.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Cities Initiative
geographic_focus: Illinois, Ohio, Indiana, Ontario, New York, Michigan, Pennsylvania, Minnesota, Wisconsin, Quebec
description: The Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Cities Initiative was formed in 2003 and today is a coalition of over 100 U.S. and Canadian mayors and municipal officials dedicated to advancing the protection and restoration of the region and its water resources. The grantee helps its members integrate environmental, economic and social priorities to protect and advance a resource that supplies 20 percent of the world’s surface freshwater and provides drinking water and the basis for a thriving economy for 40 million people. With previous Foundation support, the grantee has helped animate the voices of mayors in regional decisions, contributing to important policies to form a foundation for protecting and advancing the interests of the lakes. Renewed funding will enable the grantee to continue to connect mayors across borders and boundaries, supply municipal leaders with trusted and reliable support on a range of water issues and provide a platform for mayors to express their views in state, provincial and federal decision making forums.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Cities Initiative
geographic_focus: Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, New York, Ontario, Illinois, Minnesota, Quebec, Ohio, Michigan, Indiana
description: Cities play an important role in the management, protection, and restoration of their local water sources. Municipal leaders make daily decisions related to drinking water, wastewater, and waterfront development. The Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Cities Initiative is a binational coalition of mayors that seeks to promote and advance the protection and restoration of the full Great Lakes Basin. With Mott support, the grantee will: 1) provide a voice for local governments on regional Great Lakes issues; 2) work to halt the spread of Asian carp; 3) encourage sustainable water management practices; 4) increase the grantee’s membership; and 5) invest in its own organizational development.

title: Digital Badges Initiative
description: This grant will enable the Mozilla Foundation to support the afterschool field in developing online badges, a symbol or indicator of an accomplishment, skill, competency, or interest, for youth in afterschool programs. Specifically, this grant will support the further development of: 1) the system supports, infrastructure, and policy initiatives needed for online badges and other competency-based learning approaches; and 2) the capacity of afterschool programs to offer badges and to support competency-based learning for youth. By incorporating new education technology opportunities, this project seeks to help youth more easily demonstrate the skills they acquire in afterschool and out-of-school time programs.

title: Digital Badges Initiative
description: This grant will enable the Mozilla Foundation to support the afterschool field in developing online badges, a symbol or indicator of an accomplishment, skill, competency, or interest, for youth in afterschool programs. Specifically, this grant will support the further development of: 1) the system supports and infrastructure needed for online badges; and 2) the capacity of afterschool programs to create and offer badges. Through incorporating new education technology opportunities, this project seeks to help youth more easily demonstrate the skills they acquire in afterschool and out-of-school time programs.

title: Fiscal Solvency and Service Effectiveness Project
description: This project continues Michigan State University’s examination of chronic fiscal stress in America’s older, industrial cities — this time focusing on the post-receivership restoration of local control and the best strategies for maintaining medium- and long-term fiscal solvency. The proposed research will assess the factors that determine the success or failure of states’ transition processes from local fiscal emergency to fiscal health and determine how different state policies shape local fiscal outcomes during and after receivership. The city of Flint will continue to play a prominent role in this project, both as a focus of the research and as a beneficiary of a six- to eight-month technical assistance effort intended to educate city administrators and city council about the research findings. The university will also publish two white papers and convene two meetings in order to disseminate the research findings with statewide and national audiences.

title: Fiscal Solvency and Service Effectiveness Project
description: This grant will enable Michigan State University to conduct a thorough examination of the range of policy solutions being employed to address the fiscal and economic problems facing many older industrial communities, including Flint, Michigan. To complete the proposed research project, the grantee will review and analyze the current causes of chronic fiscal stress; identify various policy options that have been proposed and/or enacted to address fiscal challenges in Flint and other communities; compare the relative effectiveness of various policy options; and produce a report and a series of outreach events to help shape debates and responses to fiscal and economic stress situations in Michigan and elsewhere.

title: Building a Case for Postsecondary Access and Success
description: With renewal grant support, the New America Foundation will assess the impacts and effectiveness of grantmaking activities under the access objective and provide learning support to the Foundation and its grantees in order to inform strategic refinements in the grantmaking activities and increase grantee effectiveness. Located in Washington, D.C., the New America Foundation is a public policy institute with the purpose of bringing new voices and ideas to the forefront of America’s public discourse by investing in outstanding individuals and ideas that transcend the conventional political spectrum. Its Education Policy Program uses original research and policy analysis to solve the nation’s critical education problems, serving as a trusted source of objective analysis and innovative ideas for policymakers, educators, and the public at large.

title: Building a Case for Postsecondary Access and Success
description: This grant will enable the New America Foundation’s Education Policy Program to produce a set of products to inform grantmaking activities proposed under the Success Beyond High School program area. The intended deliverables include a series of white papers, a chart book, and an evaluation plan. Collectively, these products will assist Mott in refining and evaluating the grantmaking strategies and communicating the strategies and their impacts on internal and external audiences. Located in Washington, D.C., the New America Foundation is a public policy institute that invests in new thinkers and new ideas to address the next generation of challenges facing the United States.

title: Service as a Strategy
description: Sagawa/Jospin, LLC, a firm led by two renowned experts in the civic engagement and community service fields, will convene a group of experts and practitioners to explore the potential that service and volunteerism might play in a strategy for the educational and economic advancement of young people living in low- to moderate-income communities. The project is intended to identify the areas of potential and points of leverage that might lead to wider utilization of service and volunteerism as a strategy for educational and economic advancement.

title: Early Education Curriculum and Education
description: This grant will provide support to HighScope Educational Research Foundation to conduct professional development for early childhood educators at multiple centers across the city of Flint. Professional development will include group training and individual coaching sessions. A city scan will also be performed, which will include the collection and analysis of data related to the availability of and need for high quality early education opportunities for children and families in the city of Flint.

title: Middle School Initiative
description: This grant will provide continued support to the After-School All-Stars program in Washington, D.C., including expanding its presence to additional sites over the next two years. The grantee’s mission is to provide comprehensive afterschool programs for at-risk middle school students to keep them safe and help them achieve in school and in life. As a result, the afterschool program will focus on a variety of areas such as tutoring, life skills, mentoring, and health and fitness. In addition, the Washington, D.C. chapter will serve as a pilot site for new and innovative national initiatives that will be disseminated to the afterschool education field.

title: Middle School Initiative
description: This grant will support the After-School All-Stars in implementing and developing an afterschool program at the Stuart-Hobson Middle School located in Washington, D.C. The mission of the After-School All-Stars is to provide comprehensive afterschool programs for at-risk middle school students to keep them safe and help them achieve in school and in life. As a result, the afterschool program will focus on a variety of areas such as tutoring, life skills, mentoring, and health and fitness. In addition, this program will serve as a pilot site for new and innovative national initiatives that will be disseminated to the afterschool education field.

title: Endowment for a Sustainable Future
description: The program goal is to strengthen the financial sustainability of a leading Romanian philanthropy support organization whose mission is to support the development of local communities by increasing the level and efficiency of private giving for public good. The Association for Community Relations will run an endowment building program to raise $750,000 and increase its total endowment to at least $1 million by 2019. Through this process, the grantee will strengthen its overall fundraising strategies and capacities and access new sources of funding. The grantee has a long-term commitment to strengthening its role as a support organization for philanthropy and community foundation development in both Romania and the Central and Eastern Europe and Russia region. Since its establishment in 2001, the grantee has been carrying out research on issues of philanthropy, building the capacity of nonprofit organizations to raise local human and financial resources, encouraging strategic corporate philanthropy, and developing and promoting innovative fundraising mechanisms.

title: Donors and Foundations Networks In Europe (DAFNE)
description: The project goal is to develop strategic philanthropy and strengthen philanthropic infrastructure in Europe. The Spanish Association of Foundations manage and develop the Donors and Foundations Networks In Europe (DAFNE), an informal network of 25 donor associations from 23 European countries, including eight countries in Central and Eastern Europe. The grantee, in cooperation with network members, will increase the level and quality of philanthropy in Europe, strengthen the representation of the philanthropic sector vis-à-vis the public and corporate sectors, increase the knowledge and appreciation of the contribution of philanthropy to social development, and strengthen the capacity and effectiveness of network members. The grantee’s specific achievements under this project include increasing the number of network members, strengthening the professional capacity of network members, and representing the network in European and international philanthropy fora and initiatives. The grantee is based in Madrid, Spain.

title: Donors and Foundations Networks In Europe (DAFNE)
geographic_focus: Russia, United Kingdom, Spain, Bulgaria, Norway, Netherlands, Ireland, Germany, Slovakia, Switzerland, Hungary, Romania, Italy, Finland, Belgium, France, Czech Republic, Ukraine, Austria
description: The project goal is to develop strategic philanthropy and strengthen philanthropic infrastructure in Europe. To this end, the Spanish Association of Foundations will manage and develop the Donors and Foundations Networks in Europe (DAFNE), an informal network of 24 donor associations from 20 European countries, including 7 countries in Central and Eastern Europe and Russia. More specifically, the grantee, in cooperation with network members, will increase the level and quality of philanthropy in Europe, strengthen the representation of the philanthropic sector vis-à-vis the public and corporate sectors, increase the knowledge and appreciation of the contribution of philanthropy to social development, and strengthen the capacity and effectiveness of network members. The grantee was established in January 2003 as a result of the merger of two national associations of foundations, and as of November 2013, it has 1,000 members. The grantee provides specialist information, training, and consultancy services to members and other interested stakeholders; carries out relevant research and advocacy projects; and represents the Spanish foundation sector on the national, European, and global levels.

title: Youth Substance Abuse Reduction Program
grantee: Institute for Behavior and Health, Inc.
description: This grant increase will provide funds to the Institute for Behavior and Health, Inc., to continue its work on the development of a model to deter substance abuse among youth. Central to the model is a focus on more intentional engagement of pediatric and adolescent physicians and parents as essential partners in identifying risk factors for youth substance abuse and identifying ways to curtail use.

title: Youth Substance Abuse Reduction Program
grantee: Institute for Behavior and Health, Inc.
description: This grant will provide funds to the Institute for Behavior and Health, Inc. to continue to advance the critical messaging aimed at curbing adolescent substance abuse. Central to this initiative will be physician education and working with lead organizations in the field to promote the acceptance and integration of consistent messaging that promotes a no-use policy of alcohol, tobacco, marijuana, or other drugs among youth.

title: Youth Substance Abuse Reduction Program
grantee: Institute for Behavior and Health, Inc.
description: This grant will provide funds to the Institute for Behavior and Health, Inc, to convene leaders in pediatrics, adolescent medicine, and national parent organizations to develop a strategy to help deter substance abuse among youth, with a particular focus on curbing marijuana use. The model will build on the importance of pediatric and adolescent physicians and parents as essential partners in identifying the risk factors for youth drug abuse and identifying ways to curtail use.

title: Strengthening Civic Participation in Ukrainian Cities
description: The program goal is to promote participatory approaches toward local urban development in Ukraine. The Centre for Society Research, also known as CEDOS, will focus on issues related to the definition, preservation, and use of public spaces and the role of local inhabitants in these processes. The grantee will work in four key areas: assessing and improving participatory local governance, strengthening connections among urban grassroots activists, fostering wider and deeper cooperation among different stakeholders, and developing online and offline information and training resources. In 2014–16, the grantee established an online course on urban civic engagement accessed by over 5,000 users. It created an open database and networking tool linking almost 1,000 urban grassroots initiatives from across Ukraine while producing weekly policy analyses of urban development issues. Registered in 2010, Centre for Society Research is a nongovernmental, nonpartisan organization located in Kyiv which seeks to promote democratic governance, civic participation, and knowledge-driven policymaking.

title: Strengthening Civic Participation in Ukrainian Cities
description: The program goal is to promote participatory and innovative approaches toward local urban development in Ukraine. The Centre for Society Research will focus on issues related to the definition, preservation, and use of public spaces and the role of local inhabitants in these processes. The grantee will work to address four key issues in this sphere — disempowered communities, corruption in urban development, the lack of coordinated efforts among urban campaigners, and the disconnect between grassroots civic activists and experts. The project will include analyses of critical urban issues, training and information support to active citizen groups, and the introduction of the practice of deliberative democracy in selected cases of urban planning and development. While primarily focused on Kyiv, the project will also take place in the cities of Lviv and Kharkiv. Registered in 2010, the Centre for Society Research is a nongovernmental, nonpartisan organization located in Kyiv which seeks to promote democratic governance, civic participation, and knowledge-driven policymaking.

title: General Purposes
description: The Social Justice Initiative was established in 2013 to contribute to building a South Africa characterized by peace, prosperity, and stability. Its vision is the creation and preservation of a just and fair society based on the democratic principles provided for in the country’s Constitution. The grantee seeks to address the financial crisis facing the social justice sector by increasing awareness of social justice causes among wealthy South Africans and encouraging them to fund programs that advance human rights and social justice. Past support assisted the grantee to establish mechanisms through which philanthropists can fund social justice causes, facilitate long-term relationships between philanthropists and the projects they support, and advocate for increased funding to the social justice sector. This grant will support the grantee to continue unlocking support from wealthy South Africans for social justice causes and matching funders with deserving causes.

title: General Purposes
description: The Social Justice Initiative was established in 2013 to contribute to building peace, prosperity, and stability in South Africa. Its vision is the creation and preservation of a just and fair society based on the democratic principles provided for in the country’s constitution. The grantee seeks to address the financial crisis facing the social justice sector. Over the next year, its main focus will be to increase awareness of social justice causes among wealthy South Africans and encourage them to fund programs that advance human rights and social justice. This grant will support the grantee to establish mechanisms through which philanthropists can fund social justice causes, facilitate long-term relationships between philanthropists and the projects they support, and advocate for increased funding to the social justice sector.

title: Flint Area Reinvestment Office
description: A project of the United Way of Genesee County, the Flint Area Reinvestment Office convenes community-, regional-, and state-based partners around grant opportunities and provides supportive services to enable partners to pursue grants and other resources more efficiently and effectively. This grant increase will enable the office to expand its efforts to coordinate and enhance Flint’s entrepreneurship services sector and position the sector to foster more entrepreneurship activity and attract additional resources.

title: Flint Area Reinvestment Office
description: This grant provides support to the Flint Area Reinvestment Office to carry out its mission to be a catalyst and facilitator for innovative community and economic development initiatives in the Flint region. A project of the United Way of Genesee County, the Flint Area Reinvestment Office convenes community-, regional-, and state-based partners around grant opportunities, and provides supportive services to enable partners to pursue grants more efficiently and effectively. Formerly a program of the Prima Civitas Foundation, the Flint Area Reinvestment Office was founded in 2009, and since that time has had direct involvement in securing more than $50 million in federal and state grants.

title: Flint Area Reinvestment Office
description: This grant provides support to the Flint Area Reinvestment Office to carry out its mission as a catalyst and facilitator for innovative community and economic development initiatives in the Flint region. A project of the United Way of Genesee County, the Flint Area Reinvestment Office convenes community-, regional-, and state-based partners around grant opportunities and provides supportive services to enable partners to pursue grants efficiently and effectively. Formerly a program of the Prima Civitas Foundation, the Flint Area Reinvestment Office was founded in 2009, and since that time, has had direct involvement in securing $52 million in federal and state grants. In 2014, the Flint Area Reinvestment Office broadened its activities to include developing and supporting entrepreneurship-related programming as a strategic focus.

title: Flint Area Reinvestment Office
description: This grant provides support to the Flint Area Reinvestment Office to carry out its mission as a catalyst and facilitator for innovative community and economic development initiatives in the Flint region.
