title: Flint Area Reinvestment Office
description: This grant provides support to the Flint Area Reinvestment Office to carry out its mission to bring federal and state funding and other resources into the Flint area. A project of the United Way of Genesee County, the Flint Area Reinvestment Office convenes community-, regional-, and state-based partners around grant opportunities, and provides supportive services to enable partners to pursue grants more efficiently and effectively. Formerly a program of the Prima Civitas Foundation, the Flint Area Reinvestment Office was founded in 2009, and since that time has had direct involvement in securing more than $47 million in federal and state grants for the Flint community.

title: Addressing Changes in International Development Finance
description: Eurodad is a network of 48 nongovernmental organizations from 19 European countries working on issues related to development finance, sustainable development, and poverty reduction. Over the grant period, the grantee will undertake a two-year research project analyzing the changes in development finance. This grant increase will also assist with the organization’s strategic planning process over the next year.

title: Addressing Changes in International Development Finance
description: Since 1990, Eurodad has led a network of European nongovernmental organizations working on issues related to development finance, sustainable development, and poverty reduction. The focus of the grantee is to strengthen civil society organization’s capacity, working to transform international development finance to be more transparent and sustainable. Over the past grant period, the grantee played an important convening and research role, helping nongovernmental organizations in Africa, Asia, Europe, and Latin America develop strong and successful policy advocacy related to international development finance. This project will continue to promote strong environmental and social standards for international development finance in order to ensure that sustainable development is the key outcome for these investments.

title: Addressing Changes in International Development Finance
description: Since 1990, Eurodad has led a network of nongovernmental organizations working on issues related to development finance, sustainable development, and poverty reduction. The grantee’s focus is to strengthen the capacity of civil society organizations in Europe and developing countries in order to transform international development finance, making it more transparent and sustainable. Over the past grant period, the grantee has played an important convening and research role, helping nongovernmental organizations in Africa, Asia, Europe, Latin America, and the Middle East develop strong and successful policy advocacy related to international development finance. This project will continue to promote strong environmental and social standards for international development finance to ensure that sustainable development is the key outcome for these investments.

title: Addressing Changes in International Development Finance
description: Eurodad is a network of 48 nongovernmental organizations from 19 European countries working on issues related to development finance, sustainable development, and poverty reduction. To better understand the challenges of the evolving development finance landscape, Eurodad, the European Network on Debt and Development, will undertake a two-year research project analyzing the changes in development finance. The project will work to build effective civil society coalitions on key development finance issues in order to inform and support advocacy; provide a comprehensive assessment of financing mechanisms used by development finance institutions and other international financial institutions; shape the development finance policy debate; and help set environmental and social standards that guide lending to developing countries.

title: Development Banks and Sustainable Development
description: In recent years, China has helped establish a new family of development finance institutions that rival the current multilateral development finance system. The impact made by the investments of these new institutions on ecosystems and community development has become a global issue. The Global Economic Governance Institute at Boston University has become a major source for research analyzing these impacts. Over the past grant period, this project produced a groundbreaking report on the environmental and social impacts of Chinese investment in Latin America, leading to important opportunities to engage with government officials, other development finance institutions, and major media outlets. For the next grant period, the institute will continue to help shape investments made by these development finance institutions with a focus on energy and infrastructure, as well as environmental and social safeguards.

title: China's Global Reach: The Social and Environmental Dimension
description: China has become one of the most important investment, finance, and trading partners for many developing countries. However, the impact of investments on ecosystems and community development in these countries has become a global issue. The Global Economic Governance Institute at Boston University has become a major source for research analyzing these impacts, particularly in South America. The institute will draw on its expertise to provide much needed research and help build the capacity of civil society and governments in South America and globally to address the impacts of Chinese investments. In addition, the institute will research China’s global investments in energy.

title: Pivoting a Shift in Overseas Lending of China's Policy Banks Towards a Greener and More Sustainable Path
description: China has emerged as an important new player in the world of development finance over the past decade. This increased overseas investment has had significant environmental, social, and market impacts. To address these impacts, it is crucial to develop not only sound environmental and social standards, but also initiatives that encourage investments to support sustainable and climate-friendly development. The Global Environmental Institute, a Chinese environmental nongovernmental organization, was established in 2004 to design and implement market-based models for solving environmental problems. It has years of experience working with Chinese development finance institutions in Southeast Asia and South Asia. This project will facilitate the improvement of environmental and social safeguards for China’s main development finance institutions and increase these institutions’ green investment portfolio through fostering small scale sustainable and climate-friendly projects in developing countries.

title: Supporting Southern Civil Society Engagement in Finance
grantee: Institute for Climate and Sustainable Cities
description: Financial institutions and large developing countries have taken up a new and expanding role in development finance, including responses to global threats such as climate change. Given these changes, it is vital for civil society organizations in developing countries to craft more effective strategies to engage in the international, national, and local discussions on how to finance the transition to a low-carbon economy. Through this project, the Institute for Climate and Sustainable Cities will address these capacity building needs, particularly in China and Southeast Asian countries. Over the last grant period, the grantee was successful in building a coalition of developing countries’ governments and nongovernmental organizations that raised the ambitions of climate mitigation, finance, and adaptation at the United Nations climate negotiations in Paris. Over the next grant period, work will focus on the Green Climate Fund as well as the new development finance institution investments on climate change, including those of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank.

title: Building an Asian Civil Society Community of Practice on Climate Finance
grantee: Institute for Climate and Sustainable Cities
description: Financial institutions and large developing countries have taken up new and expanding roles in development finance, including responses to global threats such as climate change. Given these changes, it is vital for civil society organizations in developing countries to craft more effective strategies to engage in the international, national, and local discussions on how to finance the transition to a low-carbon economy. Through this project, the Institute for Climate and Sustainable Cities will assist groups to develop such strategies and develop stronger collaborations, particularly in Southeast Asian countries. Over the last grant, the grantee was quite successful in building a coalition of nongovernmental organizations that monitored and strengthened standards of the Green Climate Fund; actively engaged Chinese development finance institutions related to energy infrastructure investments; and worked with Chinese organizations to engage their government representatives on climate finance. Over the next grant period, work will focus on the Green Climate Fund as well as Chinese development finance institution investments on energy and infrastructure.

title: Supporting Southern Civil Society Engagement in Finance
grantee: Institute for Climate and Sustainable Cities
description: The financial sector and large developing countries have taken up a new and expanding role in development finance, including responses to global threats such as climate change. Given these changes, it is vital for civil society organizations in developing countries to craft more effective strategies to engage in the international, national, and local discussions on how to finance the transition to a low-carbon economy. Through this project, the Institute for Climate and Sustainable Cities will address these capacity building needs, particularly in China and Southeast Asian countries. In addition, it will assist with the development of policy strategies to address environmental and social standards for climate and development finance going into Asia.

title: Energy and Infrastructure Development in the Amazon
description: This grant renewal will support the Instituto Centro de Vida, which is currently the secretariat of the Amazon Regional Network, to continue building capacity within its energy and infrastructure working group on the impacts of major development finance in the greater Amazon rainforest. In addition, the grantee will work with local communities in the Amazon’s Teles Pires and Tapajos watersheds to monitor and seek to mitigate impacts of a large hydroelectric complex planned in this, as yet, undeveloped region of the forest.

title: Energy and Infrastructure Development in the Amazon
description: The Instituto Centro de Vida is a Brazilian civil society organization that serves as the secretariat for the Brazilian Infrastructure Working Group and works with networks and impacted communities in Amazon river basins threatened by finance of large-scale hydroelectric development. This grant will enable the grantee to strengthen the new strategic plan of the Infrastructure Working Group. In addition, this project will support work with networks and local communities in the Amazon’s Teles Pires and Tapajos watersheds to monitor compliance with standards and seek to mitigate impacts of a large hydroelectric complex planned in the, as yet undeveloped, Tapajos River basin.

title: Energy and Infrastructure Development in the Amazon
description: The Instituto Centro de Vida is a Brazilian civil society organization that serves as the secretariat of the Brazilian Infrastructure Working Group and works with communities impacted by large hydroelectric development in Amazon rivers. Over the past project period, the grantee ran regular working group convenings, published a dossier on social and environmental impacts of the Teles Pires and Sao Manoel hydroelectric plants, and organized an important national conference on infrastructure development finance in the Amazon. Over this project period, the grantee will implement the working group’s action plan, conduct security trainings, and work with networks and local communities impacted by two large hydroelectric plants in the Amazon’s Teles Pires watershed and monitor developments of a proposed complex of hydroelectric plants on the Tapajos River.

title: Energy and Infrastructure Development in the Amazon
description: This grant to Instituto Centro de Vida will support the secretariat of the Amazon Regional Network to build understanding and capacity on the impacts of Brazilian Development Bank investments in energy and infrastructure in the Greater Amazon Rainforest, and particularly, to work with and support the network’s infrastructure working group. An additional component of the project will work with local communities in the Tapajos and Teles Pires watersheds of the Amazon Rainforest to monitor and seek to mitigate impacts of a large hydroelectric complex planned in this, as yet undeveloped, region of the forest.

title: BNDES and the Amazon
description: This project supports the specialized journalism agency Mongabay.org to increase the quality and quantity of journalistic coverage of Brazilian finance of energy development in the Amazon rainforest. This project will pay particular attention to exploring the impacts of Brazilian public finance of new large-scale hydroelectric projects in the Tapajos river basin, one of the last intact river systems in the Amazon rainforest. Mongabay.org is a specialist in science and environmental reporting about tropical forests, with partnerships for dissemination of material in English, Spanish, and Portuguese.

title: BNDES and the Amazon
description: Founded in 1992, Mongabay.org is a leading conservation news web service, specializing in science and environmental reporting about tropical forests, with partnerships for dissemination of material in English, Spanish, and Portuguese. This grant renewal will enable the grantee to continue its coverage of the environmental and social impacts of energy development and finance in the greater Amazon rainforest, and expand coverage beyond Brazil to include four other countries with borders in the Amazon: Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.

title: BNDES and the Amazon
description: This project supports the specialized journalism agency Mongabay.org to increase the quality and quantity of journalistic coverage of Brazilian finance of energy development in the Amazon rainforest. This project will pay particular attention to exploring the role that Brazil is playing in new hydroelectric power projects in the Tapajos watershed, one of the last intact river systems in the Brazilian Amazon. The grantee is a specialist in science and environmental reporting about tropical forests, with partnerships for dissemination of material in English, Spanish, and Portuguese.

title: Monitoring BNDES Sustainability
grantee: Instituto de Energia e Meio Ambiente
description: This project will support the Instituto de Energia e Meio Ambiente, a nonprofit Brazilian organization, to disseminate analyses of the environmental impacts of public investment in energy development in Brazil and South America. The technical outputs of the project will help strengthen civil society and public-sector expertise on environmental impacts and standards governing public finance of energy and infrastructure.

title: Monitoring BNDES Sustainability
grantee: Instituto de Energia e Meio Ambiente
description: The Instituto de Energia e Meio Ambiente is a nonprofit Brazilian think tank focused on research, analysis, and policy evaluation to contribute to socially and environmentally sustainable energy and transportation development and finance. Over the past project period, the grantee monitored thermoelectric development and finance, developed environmental standards, and organized the first international conference in Brazil on the importance of environmental standards for expansion of thermoelectric power plants. This project will support the grantee to research, develop, and propose landscape-level environmental and sectoral planning tools to guide and mitigate impacts of the planned expansion of fossil-fuel dependent power plants.

title: Monitoring BNDES Sustainability
grantee: Instituto de Energia e Meio Ambiente
description: This project will support the Instituto de Energia e Meio Ambiente, a nonprofit Brazilian organization, to develop a methodology and series of technical papers to analyze the sustainability of Brazilian Development Bank investment in energy development. The technical outputs of the project will help strengthen civil society expertise to improve social and environmental standards governing public finance of energy and infrastructure in Brazil and South America.

title: Midwest Energy News in Michigan
description: With many newspapers and other news outlets reducing their science and energy reporting, the public needs educational information on the changes taking place in the energy system. With prior Mott support, Fresh Energy, a Minnesota-based nonprofit and publisher of “Midwest Energy News”, expanded its journalistic coverage of renewable energy, energy efficiency, and clean transportation stories in Michigan. With continued support, “Midwest Energy News” will aim to generate a minimum of four pieces of original Michigan-focused reporting every month with the goal of making Michigan one of its top four states for readership.

title: Midwest Energy News in Michigan
description: With many newspapers and other news outlets reducing their science and energy reporting, the public needs educational information on the changes taking place in the energy system. With prior Mott support, Fresh Energy, a Minnesota-based nonprofit and publisher of “Midwest Energy News”, successfully expanded its journalistic coverage of renewable energy and energy efficiency stories in Michigan. With continued support, the grantee will generate a minimum of four pieces of original Michigan-focused reporting every month with the goal of maintaining Michigan’s ranking as one of its top four states for readership.

title: Midwest Energy News in Michigan
description: With many newspapers and other news outlets continuing to reduce their science and energy reporting, there is an ongoing need for providing the public with factual information on the changes taking place in the energy system. With prior Mott support, Fresh Energy, a Minnesota-based nonprofit and publisher of “Midwest Energy News”, continued to successfully expand its journalistic coverage of renewable energy and energy efficiency stories in Michigan. With continued support, the grantee will increase its production of Michigan-focused reporting to 60 pieces per year and maintain Michigan’s ranking as one of its top four states for readership.

title: Midwest Energy News in Michigan
description: With many newspapers and other news outlets reducing their science and energy reporting, the public needs and deserves educational information on the changes taking place in the energy system. This is particularly true in Michigan, where multiple clean energy policy ideas will be under discussion in 2014. Fresh Energy, a Minnesota-based nonprofit and publisher of “Midwest Energy News”, will expand its journalistic coverage of renewable energy, energy efficiency, and clean transportation stories in Michigan. With Mott support, “Midwest Energy News” will aim to generate a minimum of four pieces of original Michigan-focused reporting every month and make Michigan one of its top three states for readership.

title: Summer Youth Initiative Evaluation
description: This grant will provide support to the Corporation for a Skilled Workforce to conduct an evaluation of the Summer Youth Initiative. The initiative provides job training and employment opportunities to Flint area youth ages 14 to 18. The evaluation will be retrospective and include both impact evaluation and program evaluation, looking at qualitative and quantitative data for the past five years in order to gauge how participants have moved through the initiative and leveraged their participation to navigate transition points in their educational and career pathways. The project will also help define future research and assessment needs.

title: Barriers to Advanced Energy in Michigan
description: Manufacturing of advanced energy products, such as renewable energy and energy efficiency, already contributes more than $7 billion to Michigan’s economy, but the state could be doing much more in this economic sector. A number of market and policy barriers exist that are holding the sector back. The Institute for Energy Innovation, a Michigan-based nonprofit focused on promoting greater public understanding of advanced energy and its economic potential for Michigan, will research and publish a report on the barriers impeding the deployment of advanced energy technologies and business models in Michigan.

title: Capacity Building and Programmatic Support
description: This grant will support capacity building and sustainability activities during the executive transition currently under way at YouthBuild USA. The transition has created additional expenses to the organization, including executive coaching, enhanced travel, and staff professional development. Funding will help support these activities as well as special fundraising activities planned in conjunction with the retirement of YouthBuild’s founder. Headquartered in Boston, YouthBuild USA was founded in 1988 to unleash the intelligence and positive energy of low-income young people to rebuild their communities and their lives.

title: Capacity Building and Programmatic Support
description: This grant will enable YouthBuild USA to strengthen its overall management capacity and expand its programming domestically and internationally. In 2013, YouthBuild USA celebrated its 35th anniversary. Since its inception as a national nonprofit intermediary committed to connecting unemployed low-income 16- to 24-year-olds to education, work, and service opportunities, 120,000 young people in 273 communities have participated in YouthBuild and built more than 22,000 units of affordable housing in 46 states. Each year, more than 8,000 young people participate in local YouthBuild programs. Building off its thirty-plus years of success and service, the grantee will develop a growth plan over the next two years to guide its activities to increase the number of local programs and increase the number of young people served to 50,000 each year. Recommended support will enable YouthBuild USA to sustain and support senior leadership transition activities, enhance and support core international activities, support a training fellowship program for local program directors, and support national network and coalition activities focused on reconnecting youth.

title: Limpopo Legal Aid Cluster
description: The Humanist Institute for Cooperation with Developing Countries-South Africa (commonly referred to as HIVOS-South Africa) is part of the Dutch-based nongovernmental organization, HIVOS-Netherlands, which was established in the 1950s and works in many countries around the world to alleviate poverty and build stronger civil societies. The aim of the Limpopo Legal Aid Cluster program is to assist advice offices in the Limpopo province to deliver improved services to their beneficiaries. The program focuses on five advice offices that work with farm and migrant workers and other vulnerable groups. Over the next two years, the grantee will train the five advice offices on skills including fundraising, strategic planning, board development, and financial management. It will also assist the advice offices to conduct outreach programs on farms, network with each other, and build a body of knowledge on matters that affect farm and migrant workers. This grant has been made possible by a partnership with Atlantic Philanthropies in support of the community advice office sector.

title: Advice Office Support
grantee: Centre for Community Justice and Development
description: The Centre for Community Justice and Development was established in 2012 and works to further access to justice and to protect human rights through the law. It serves as an umbrella body to 15 advice offices in rural parts of the KwaZulu-Natal province of South Africa and provides them with financial and material resources. The advice offices provide legal advice and related services to poor people living in these areas. Past support enabled the center to: support the 15 advice offices to operate independently by registering as legal entities and thus enabling them to attract funding from local sources; train the 15 advice offices on fundraising, financial management, administration, planning, and reporting; and provide backup legal services to the advice offices and collate their cases through a central case management system. This grant will enable the grantee to continue with this work. This grant has been made possible by a partnership with Atlantic Philanthropies in support of the community advice office sector.

title: Advice Office Support
grantee: Centre for Community Justice and Development
description: The Centre for Community Justice and Development was established in 2012 and works to further access to justice and to protect human rights through the law. It serves as an umbrella body to 15 advice offices in rural parts of the KwaZulu-Natal province of South Africa and provides them with financial and material resources. The advice offices provide legal advice and related services to poor people living in these areas. Past support enabled the grantee to support the 15 advice offices through: training on topics including fundraising, financial management, administration, planning, and reporting; providing back-up legal services; and collating their cases through a central case management system. This grant will enable the grantee to continue training the advice offices toward greater independence and assist the advice offices to fundraise independently to secure their sustainability in the long term. This grant has been made possible by a partnership with Atlantic Philanthropies in support of the community advice office sector.

title: Advice Office Support
grantee: Centre for Community Justice and Development
description: The Centre for Community Justice and Development was established in 2012 and works to further access to justice and to protect human rights through the law. The grantee supports 15 advice offices in rural parts of the KwaZulu-Natal Province of South Africa and provides them with financial and material resources. Advice offices provide legal advice and related services to poor people living in these areas. Past support enabled the grantee to support the 15 advice offices through training on topics including fundraising, financial management, administration, planning, reporting, providing back-up legal services, and collating their cases through a central case management system. The grantee also assisted six of the advice offices to raise funds successfully. This grant will enable the grantee to continue to support the 15 advice offices toward greater independence and assist them to raise funds independently to secure their sustainability in the long term.

title: Advice Office Support
grantee: Centre for Community Justice and Development
description: The Centre for Community Justice and Development was established in 2012 and works to further access to justice and to protect human rights through the law. It supports advice offices that provide legal advice and related services to poor people living in rural areas of KwaZulu-Natal province of South Africa. Prior to its establishment in 2012, the grantee operated as a project of the University of KwaZulu-Natal. It served as an umbrella body to 15 advice offices and provided them with financial and material resources. The aim of this project is to train and support the 15 advice offices to operate independently. Over the next two years, the grantee will assist the advice offices to register as independent entities and train them on fundraising, financial management, administration, planning, and reporting. The goal is to enable the individual advice offices to attract funding from local sources. The grantee will also provide backup legal services to the advice offices and collate their cases through a central case management system. This grant has been made possible by a partnership with Atlantic Philanthropies in support of the community advice office sector.

title: Back-up Legal Services Program
grantee: Association of University Legal Aid Institutions Trust
geographic_focus: North-West, Province of, Western Cape, Province of the, Mpumalanga, Limpopo
description: The Association of University Legal Aid Institutions Trust was established to support and promote institutions that provide legal services to poor and marginalized communities in South Africa. It coordinates the work of Access to Justice Clusters, which are cooperative bodies of university-based law clinics, paralegal advice offices, justice centers, private practitioners, and legal, nonprofit organizations. The grantee provides support to community-based advice offices through the clusters to ensure that they effectively provide legal and related services to the country’s poor. This grant will support the grantee to provide backup legal services to community-based advice offices and poor people through the Access to Justice Clusters. The grantee will also provide financial support to a select number of advice offices to enable them to operate effectively. This grant has been made possible by a partnership with Atlantic Philanthropies in support of the community advice office sector.

title: Water Rate Study
description: This grant to the City of Flint will support a water and sewage rate study which includes a comprehensive review of water and sewer funds and budgets, water systems plans, wastewater plans, current usage data, and future planned growth analysis. A proposed framework for future rate decisions will also be included in the study.

title: Operating Support
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide operating support to the Flint Public Library. The grantee has been an institution in the Flint community since 1851. An average of 750 patrons visit the Flint Public Library each day utilizing services such as the Internet and computer training, research assistance, job searching, and resume creation. The grantee has a strong influence in the Flint community serving all citizens of varying ages, race, and income levels. With over 60 percent of cardholders being families, the grantee begins reaching out to citizens at a young age. There are many programs provided at no cost to the public and library cardholders accommodating patrons of all ages and points in life.

title: Operating Support
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide operating support to the Flint Public Library. The grantee has been an institution in the Flint community since 1851. An average of 981 patrons visit the library each day seeking assistance with services such as the Internet and computer training, research assistance, job searching, and resume creation. The grantee has a strong influence in the Flint community serving all citizens of varying ages, race, and income levels. With over 60 percent of cardholders being families, the grantee begins reaching out to citizens at a young age. There are many programs provided at no cost to the public and library cardholders accommodating patrons of all ages and points in life.

title: General Purposes
description: The project goal is to strengthen the field of philanthropy in the Western Balkans. The Catalyst Foundation will work regionally to promote the growth and improved transparency of the individual and corporate philanthropic culture in Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Kosovo, Macedonia, Montenegro, and Serbia. During 2016-2017, the grantee will: 1) expand and enhance the use of historic and current data on giving trends in the Western Balkans; 2) increase the quantity and quality of individual giving through crowdfunding and collective giving approaches, such as giving circles; 3) provide targeted services to corporate and private foundations to help improve philanthropic practices; and 4) strengthen the grantee’s organizational capacities. During 2014-2015, the grantee gathered and analyzed data on giving and published six reports annually on philanthropy at national levels in the Western Balkans, as well as annual regional, comparative reports. The grantee also strengthened individual involvement in and awareness of philanthropy in Serbia by organizing three giving circle events and publishing a practical guide to organizing giving circles for other nonprofits and community groups. The grantee made numerous presentations about its research and analyses and disseminated and published them via print media and social media. The Catalyst Foundation was registered in 2013 in Serbia and is based in Belgrade.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Serbia, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Albania, Croatia, Kosovo
description: The project goal is to strengthen the field of philanthropy in the Western Balkans. The Catalyst Foundation will work regionally to promote the growth and improved transparency of the individual and corporate philanthropic culture in Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Kosovo, Macedonia, Montenegro, and Serbia. During 2018–2019, the grantee will 1) gather and disseminate data on giving trends in the Western Balkans, 2) increase the quantity and quality of giving by developing and introducing tools and approaches for donors and nonprofits, and 3) strengthen philanthropy networks in the Western Balkans. During 2016–2017, the grantee gathered and analyzed data on giving and published annual reports on philanthropy at national levels in the Western Balkans. The grantee also launched an online database and new data management service for nonprofits in Serbia. The Catalyst Foundation was registered in 2013 in Serbia and is based in Belgrade.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, Croatia, Kosovo, Serbia, North Macedonia, Albania
description: The project goal is to strengthen the field of philanthropy in the Western Balkans. To this end, the Catalyst Foundation will work regionally to promote the growth and improved transparency of the individual and corporate philanthropic culture in Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Kosovo, Macedonia, Montenegro, and Serbia. During 2014-2015, the grantee will: 1) provide up-to-date and in-depth information, data, and analysis on philanthropy throughout the seven countries of the region; 2) promote the importance and impact of domestic donors and philanthropy to a broader audience; 3) strengthen individual involvement in and awareness of philanthropy; and 4) position itself as a stable and reliable knowledge partner to a broad range of philanthropy stakeholders throughout the region. The Catalyst Foundation was registered in 2013 in Serbia and is based in Belgrade.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to support greater and more effective civic engagement and participatory community development in eastern Serbia. To this end, the Zajecar Initiative will carry out a range of activities to encourage youth engagement and empowerment, stimulate community philanthropy, and promote accountable decisionmaking on the part of local government. Established in 2001 in Zajecar, Serbia, by a group of young people as a citizen-based watchdog organization, the Zajecar Initiative has grown into a leading civil society development organization in eastern Serbia. During 2014-2015, the grantee supported 23 youth-led projects that engaged more than 800 young people in their communities; operated a youth center that organized more than 250 workshops, cultural events, film screenings, and public discussions; built the capacity of the Step Forward Community Foundation in Zajecar; and launched two Internet platforms designed to give citizens access to information underlying government decisionmaking. During the next two years, the grantee will continue these core activities, with a particular focus on expanding its grantmaking activities, supporting the development of Zajecar’s community foundation, and encouraging community foundation development in the Balkan region.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to support greater and more effective civic engagement and participatory community development in eastern Serbia. To this end, the Zajecar Initiative will carry out a range of activities to encourage youth engagement, foster civic initiatives, and promote accountable decisionmaking on the part of local government. Established in 2001 by a group of young people as a citizen-based watchdog organization, the grantee has grown into a leading civil society development organization in eastern Serbia, where it is based. Its core activities include running a youth center; providing grants for local, community-based nonprofits and civic initiatives; promoting local giving and resource mobilization; and using communication and information technology to encourage accountability and transparency of local government decisionmaking. During the next two years, the grantee will continue these core activities, with a particular focus on expanding its grantmaking activities and supporting the development of a newly established community foundation in the city of Zajecar.

title: Leadership Across Boundaries Fund
description: This grant will assist the Institute for Educational Leadership with the implementation of their 50th anniversary celebration program. Since 1964, the grantee has worked to support education leaders in preparing children and youth for postsecondary education, careers, and citizenship. To commemorate the grantee’s half century of service and to showcase their commitment to partnerships and youth transitions, it will host a series of events throughout 2014, including: 1) an education policy seminar; 2) a 50th anniversary celebration; 3) a one-day symposium for education leaders; and 4) a series of multimedia products to highlight the anniversary.

title: General Purposes
description: The Young Women’s Christian Association is the oldest and largest multicultural women’s organization in the world and has served Flint and Genesee County communities for over 100 years with a mission of empowering women and eliminating racism. This grant will provide funding to the YWCA of Greater Flint enabling it to undergo a strategic planning process to help the organization align its mission and vision with its programming.

title: General Purposes
description: The Young Women’s Christian Association is the oldest and largest multicultural women’s organization in the world and has served Flint and Genesee County communities for over 100 years with a mission of empowering women and eliminating racism. This grant will provide funding to the YWCA of Greater Flint to support a number of important programs offered by the organization including Nina’s Place Transitional Living Center, Domestic Violence and Sexual Assault Services, and SafeHouse Emergency Shelter.

title: STEM Fellowship
description: This grant to the Pacific Science Center will support the Robert Noyce Fellowship in Informal STEM (science, technology, engineering, and math) Learning. The fellowship is a public-private partnership initiative geared toward advancing high quality informal science education, including in afterschool and expanded learning programs. This initiative will include: 1) strengthening collaboration between the Department of Education and other federal agencies in the area of informal STEM learning; 2) working to advance STEM learning in the 21st Century Community Learning Centers program; 3) building on the President’s Educate to Innovate campaign by building collaborations with the corporate, nonprofit, and philanthropic communities; and 4) working with leading researchers to identify priorities in informal STEM learning, including identifying new tools, strategies, and programs that improve STEM-learning opportunities.

title: STEM Fellowship
description: This grant to the Pacific Science Center will support the Robert Noyce Fellowship in Informal STEM (science, technology, engineering, and math) Learning. The fellowship is a public-private partnership initiative geared toward advancing high quality informal science education, including in afterschool and summer learning programs. This initiative will include: 1) strengthening collaboration between the U.S. Department of Education and other federal agencies in the area of informal STEM learning; 2) working to advance STEM learning in the 21st Century Community Learning Centers program; 3) building on the President’s Educate to Innovate campaign by building collaborations with the corporate, nonprofit, and philanthropic communities; and 4) working with leading researchers to identify priorities in informal STEM learning, including identifying new tools, strategies, and programs that improve STEM learning opportunities.

title: STEM Fellowship
description: This grant to the Pacific Science Center will support the Robert Noyce Fellowship in Informal STEM Learning. The fellowship is a public-private partnership initiative geared toward advancing high quality informal science education, including in afterschool and expanded learning programs. This initiative will include: 1) strengthening collaboration between the Department of Education and other federal agencies in the area of informal STEM learning; 2) working to advance STEM learning in the 21st Century Community Learning Centers program; 3) building on the President’s Educate to Innovate campaign by building collaborations with the corporate, nonprofit, and philanthropic communities; and 4) working with leading researchers to identify priorities in informal STEM learning, including identifying new tools, strategies, and programs that improve STEM learning opportunities.

title: Capitol Theatre Renovation
description: This grant will support renovations to the historic Capitol Theatre in downtown Flint and its reopening as a live entertainment venue. Built in 1928, the theater is an important underutilized asset in the downtown core area that, once restored, will complement and enhance other efforts to revitalize downtown Flint and reduce urban blight. Once fully operational, the theater has the capacity to attract between 60,000 and 80,000 visitors annually. The Flint Cultural Center Corporation, the supported organization of the Flint Cultural Center Foundation, will partner with the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation to redevelop and operate the theater.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to support the development of community foundations in Hungary. During the grant period, the Roots and Wings Foundation will establish six new community foundations; identify three additional Hungarian communities with potential to establish community foundations; strengthen the capacity of the initiative groups in these communities through training, consultancy, and international study visits; and increase the visibility of the Hungarian community foundation movement. The grantee will also create partnerships with nonprofit organizations and donors to secure the long-term future of its community foundation development program. In addition, the grantee will strengthen its own organizational capacity and financial sustainability. During the past grant period, the grantee identified and supported six initiative groups interested in establishing community foundations in their localities; strengthened the organizational capacity of the first community foundation in Hungary, the Ferencvaros Community Foundation in Budapest; and launched a national communication campaign to promote the achievements of the Hungarian nonprofit sector. The grantee is based in Budapest, Hungary.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to support the development of community foundations in Hungary. During the grant period, the Roots and Wings Foundation will promote the concept of community foundations; identify four Hungarian communities with potential to establish community foundations; and strengthen the capacity of the initiative groups in these communities through training, consultancy, and international study visits. Also, the grantee will create partnerships with nonprofit organizations and donors to secure the long-term future of its community foundation development program. In addition, the grantee will strengthen its own organizational capacity and financial sustainability. The grantee was established in May 2014 by a group of community development experts and practitioners interested in developing the community foundation field in Hungary. The grantee’s founders were instrumental in the establishment of the first community foundation in Hungary, the Ferencvaros Community Foundation in Budapest, in 2011. The grantee is committed to spreading the successful practices and lessons learned to other Hungarian communities and supporting their efforts to build community foundations.

title: Lessons of Protest Wave in Europe
description: The project goal is to better understand the causes and implications for civil society development of recent citizen protests, demonstrations, and discontent in Europe generally and, in particular, Central and Eastern Europe. To this end, the Bulgaria-based Centre for Liberal Strategies Foundation will study a wide range of approaches and practices to defining civic activism and measuring its impact and will propose a methodology for monitoring civic activism. In addition, the grantee will coordinate an international team of experienced researchers and practitioners from six countries — Bulgaria, Greece, Hungary, Russia, Spain, and Turkey — where the experiences of recent, strong protest movements provide valuable parallels and contrasts for the researchers. The grantee will host six roundtables in each of the participating countries, during which the key research questions will be debated. The discussions will be summarized in a final report, which will be widely publicized. Established in 1994, the grantee is an independent think tank whose mission is to carry out activities which promote public debate and exercise influence over decisionmaking processes. During the past grant period, the grantee developed and published research papers on the mass civic protests in Bulgaria, Russia, Spain, Turkey, and Ukraine and organized series of workshops and public events to discuss and publicize the research findings.

title: Lessons of Protest Wave in Europe
description: The project goal is to better understand the causes and implications for civil society development of recent citizen protests, demonstrations, and discontent in Europe generally and, in particular, Central and Eastern Europe. To this end, the Bulgaria-based Centre for Liberal Strategies Foundation will coordinate an international team of experienced researchers and practitioners, who will reflect on the wave of massive, peaceful citizen protests that engulfed Europe in 2010-2013 and will assess the long-term effects of these protests on societies and nonprofit sectors in Europe. The project will focus on four countries — Bulgaria, Russia, Spain, and Turkey — where the experiences of recent, strong protest movements provide valuable parallels and contrasts for the researchers. The grantee will host three workshops, during which the key research questions will be debated. The discussions will be summarized in a final report, which will be widely publicized. Established in 1994, the grantee is an independent think tank whose mission is to carry out activities which promote public debate and exercise influence over decisionmaking processes. It is an internationally recognized source of expertise concerning issues of transition in the Central and Eastern Europe and Russia region and contributes actively to the European debate on political, economic, social, and foreign policy issues.

title: East Matters
grantee: Stowarzyszenie im. Stanislawa Brzozowskiego - Krytyka Polityczna
description: The project goal is to strengthen discussion and interaction among civil society organizations and movements in Poland and other Eastern European countries. To this end, Stowarzyszenie im. Stanislawa Brzozowskiego – Krytyka Polityczna will organize seminars and short-term fellowships for civic leaders, journalists, and researchers from Central and Eastern Europe to enable them to analyze the changing political and social context. In addition, the grantee will work with partner organizations to develop and publish a series of sociopolitical debates and to organize international gatherings with the participation of civic activists from other European countries to discuss relevant East-West issues and joint action. The grantee was established in 2003 by a group of young political scientists and civic activists with the mission to combat economic, social, and cultural exclusion and increase civic participation in public life in Poland. During the past grant period, the grantee created a network of 200 activists, journalists, and academics working on strengthening civil society; organized study trips and internships in Poland for civic leaders from the region; and published a series of materials on democracy and civil society in the Polish, Russian, and Ukrainian languages.

title: East Matters
grantee: Stowarzyszenie im. Stanislawa Brzozowskiego - Krytyka Polityczna
description: The project goal is to strengthen discussion and interaction among civil society organizations and movements in Poland, Russia, and Ukraine, especially in view of the current deterioration of the relations between Russia and Ukraine and Russia and the West. To this end, Stowarzyszenie im. Stanislawa Brzozowskiego – Krytyka Polityczna will organize seminars and short-term fellowships for civic leaders, journalists, and researchers from Poland, Russia, and Ukraine to enable them to analyze the changing political and social contexts and develop new, more effective strategies for civic response. In addition, the grantee will work with partner organizations in Russia and Ukraine to develop and publish a series of sociopolitical debates. Finally, the grantee will organize an international gathering with the participation of civic activists from other European countries to discuss relevant East-West issues and joint action. The grantee was established in 2003 by a group of young political scientists and civic activists with the mission to combat economic, social, and cultural exclusion and increase civic participation in public life in Poland. In the past six years, the grantee has established good working relationships with colleagues in Russia and Ukraine and is expanding its international and regional work.

title: Global Community Philanthropy Summit
description: The program goal is to strengthen community foundations globally. This grant supports planning activities and implementation of a global summit on community philanthropy. Momentum for an event similar to a global symposium on community foundations, held in Berlin in 2004, has been building among leading global community philanthropy development organizations over the past several years. Such an event will raise the profile of community philanthropy, provide a platform for knowledge exchange, and energize the global community philanthropy field. Project activities will include establishing and conducting summit planning and coordination processes, program development, a communications strategy, funding and partnership development, and managing the event itself. The Global Fund for Community Foundations is a global, grassroots grantmaker seeking to promote community foundations and other local philanthropic institutions in the Global South and in the emerging economies of Central and Eastern Europe.

title: Global Community Philanthropy Summit
description: The program goal is to strengthen community foundations globally. This grant increase supports the preparation and execution of the Global Community Philanthropy Summit. The aim of the event is to raise the profile of community philanthropy, provide a platform for knowledge exchange, and energize the global community philanthropy field. The summit will take place on December 1-2, 2016, in Johannesburg, South Africa. Project activities include summit planning and coordination, program development, communications, funding and partnership development, advance research, and managing the event itself. This grant increase will provide additional support for research projects and bringing researchers to the summit. The Global Fund for Community Foundations is a global, grassroots grantmaker seeking to promote community foundations and other local philanthropic institutions in the Global South and in the emerging economies of Central and Eastern Europe.

title: Global Community Philanthropy Summit Planning
description: This grant supports a project to develop an action plan for a global summit on community philanthropy. Momentum for an event similar to a global symposium on community foundations, held in Berlin in 2004, has been building among leading global community philanthropy development organizations. Such an event will raise the profile, provide a platform for knowledge exchange, and energize the global community philanthropy field. Building upon meetings with important stakeholders and practitioners over the past three years, the Interaction Institute for Social Change will lead efforts to develop an initial draft plan for the summit, conduct a stakeholder analysis, convene a smaller design team and a broader planning team, and develop an action plan for the summit. The grantee provides network building, facilitation, leadership development, and consulting services to schools and school systems, domestic and international nonprofit organizations, coalitions, and foundations.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen civic participation and volunteerism in Bulgaria. To this end, the Time Heroes Foundation will increase the level of volunteering by promoting the concept of volunteerism in the mainstream and social media, increasing the visibility of volunteer contributions to social change, and increasing the capacity of nonprofits to work effectively with volunteers. In addition, the grantee will upgrade its current services and develop new services for skills-based volunteering. Also, the grantee will expand its program outreach and recruit volunteers from small and remote cities and marginalized groups. During the past two years, the grantee has established itself as the most popular service for volunteering in Bulgaria by supporting over 23,000 volunteers from 110 towns, establishing 16 young volunteer clubs in schools in 11 cities, and publishing a guidebook on good practice in volunteering. The grantee is based in Sofia, Bulgaria.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen civic participation and volunteerism in Bulgaria. To this end, the Time Heroes Foundation will expand the type and scope of services provided through its Internet-based platform to potential volunteers and volunteer-hosting organizations; expand its program outreach; recruit volunteers from small and remote cities and marginalized groups; strengthen its organizational capacity; and explore opportunities to start similar platforms in other Balkan countries. The grantee is a young and dynamic organization, founded in 2011 with the aim to build and develop a volunteering culture in Bulgaria, especially among young people and the professional class. To achieve this aim, the grantee has developed a very successful Internet-based platform that matches volunteers with charitable causes and projects that require volunteer input. The grantee has engaged over 7,000 volunteers supporting more than 400 charitable causes in 43 different cities and towns in Bulgaria.

title: National Service Programs on Federal Policy Convening
description: This grant will enable Voices for National Service, a program of City Year, Inc., to engage leaders in education, youth development, and national and community service fields to examine ways service can increase educational and employment opportunities for low- to moderate-income youth. Through its broad and diverse coalition, the grantee will bring together youth service and education stakeholders to highlight best practices, pinpoint barriers, and identify gaps in service opportunities. Their findings will become part of a national white paper highlighting the role national and community service is currently playing and the potential it has to support youth on their education-to-career journey.

title: Youth Serving Organizations on Service-Learning and K-12 Education Convening
location: St. Louis Park, MN, United States
description: The National Youth Leadership Council has been the premier leader in the education service-learning area for the past 30 years. It specializes in developing model programs, convening practitioners, conducting trainings for teachers and students, publishing research, and advancing service-learning education policies targeted at helping children grow and succeed as future leaders. The grantee is a leader in helping teachers understand and embrace service-learning as a magnifying teaching methodology that provides opportunities for all students to increase academic skills and knowledge while engaging in important activities that meet genuine community needs. This grant increase will provide the organization support to seek broader dissemination and deeper analysis for a prevalence study into service-learning practices.

title: Youth Serving Organizations on Service-Learning and K-12 Education Convening
location: St. Louis Park, MN, United States
description: The National Youth Leadership Council has been the premier leader in the education field, specifically the service-learning area, for the past 30 years. It specializes in developing model programs, convening practitioners, conducting trainings for teachers and students, publishing research, and advancing service-learning education policies targeted at helping children grow and succeed as future leaders. Today, the grantee is a leader in helping teachers and afterschool providers understand and embrace service-learning as a magnifying teaching methodology that provides opportunities for all students to increase academic skills and knowledge while engaging in important activities that meet genuine community needs. This grant will support efforts to: 1) elevate research, data, and stories that demonstrate service-learning as an effective strategy; and 2) publish articles on the findings and present the resources at national convenings.

title: Youth Serving Organizations on Service-Learning and K-12 Education Convening
location: St. Louis Park, MN, United States
description: The National Youth Leadership Council has been the premier leader in the education service-learning area, for the past 30 years. It specializes in developing model programs, convening practitioners, conducting trainings for teachers and students, publishing research, and advancing service-learning education policies targeted at helping children grow and succeed as future leaders. Today, the grantee is a leader in helping teachers understand and embrace service-learning as a magnifying teaching methodology that provides opportunities for all students to increase academic skills and knowledge while engaging in important activities that meet genuine community needs. This grant will support the grantee in its efforts to: 1) assess the current state of practice for service-learning within the United States; 2) document the exponential impact of service-learning as a promising practice for developing employment and 21st Century skills; and 3) develop a strategy to work with the statewide afterschool networks.

title: Strengthening TRANSEUROPA Network in CEE
description: The project goal is to strengthen grassroots civic participation in decisionmaking processes at the European level. To this end, European Alternatives Limited will expand its network of partner organizations in Central and Eastern Europe; strengthen the network’s organizational capacity; organize a series of joint events to promote citizen engagement and dialogue with European institutions; and provide input into the policy dialogue on the European Union level concerning issues of democratic governance, inclusive decisionmaking, transparent resource allocation, and operational effectiveness of European Union institutions. The grantee was established in 2007 with the mission to promote democracy, solidarity, and cross-border cultural exchange in Europe. During the past two years, the grantee enlarged its network with ten organizations and more than 200 individuals from Central and Eastern Europe, provided training and capacity building programs to more than 300 activists, and developed and disseminated a series of publications and training materials on key issues about democracy in contemporary Europe.

title: Strengthening TRANSEUROPA Network in CEE
description: The project goal is to strengthen grassroots civic participation in decisionmaking processes at the European level. To this end, European Alternatives Limited will expand its network of partner organizations in the Central and Eastern Europe and Russia region; strengthen the network’s organizational capacity; organize a series of joint events to promote citizen engagement and dialogue with European institutions; and provide input into the policy dialogue on the European Union level concerning issues of democratic governance, inclusive decisionmaking, transparent resource allocation, and the operational effectiveness of European Union institutions. The grantee was established in 2007 with the mission to promote democracy, solidarity, and cross-border cultural exchange in Europe. Since 2010, the grantee has been organizing the TRANSEUROPA Festival in several cities in Europe simultaneously, including cities in Bulgaria, Romania, and Serbia, allowing grassroots activists to participate in discussions on Pan-European issues.

title: European Community Foundation Initiative
description: The project goal is to develop the community foundation field and strengthen infrastructure for community foundations in Europe. In collaboration with national and European community philanthropy support organizations, Bundesverband Deutscher Stiftungen will manage and develop the European Community Foundation Initiative. Working with its partners, the grantee will strengthen the capacity of existing community foundations and their associations; promote the community foundation concept and facilitate the establishment of new community foundations; and strengthen the visibility and representation of community foundations vis-à-vis the public sector on the national and European levels. During the previous grant period, the grantee provided learning and exchange services to more than 250 community foundation practitioners from 19 European countries through study visits, bilateral exchanges, and thematic meetings. In addition, the grantee organized the first European conference of community foundations and published an overview of the field in Europe, as well as specific guides to the national community foundation movements in Germany, Italy, and the United Kingdom. The grantee is based in Berlin, Germany.

title: European Community Foundation Initiative
description: The project goal is to develop the community foundation field and strengthen infrastructure for community foundations in Europe. To this end, Bundesverband Deutscher Stiftungen, in partnership with the Center for Philanthropy in Slovakia and UK Community Foundations, and in coordination with the European Foundation Centre, will manage and develop the European Community Foundation Initiative. Working with its partners, the grantee will increase the level and quality of community philanthropy in Europe, strengthen the capacity of existing community foundations and their associations, promote the community foundation concept and facilitate the establishment of new community foundations, and strengthen the visibility and representation of community foundations vis-à-vis the public sector on the national and European levels. The grantee was established in 1948 with the mission to develop the foundation sector in Germany and strengthen civic engagement. The grantee is an umbrella organization of more than 20,000 foundations, and since 2004 has managed a national program for community foundation development, which has supported the establishment of over 300 community foundations to date. The grantee is based in Berlin, Germany.

title: General Purposes
description: The Casual Workers Advice Office was established in 2011 to give free legal advice to workers who have been dismissed or face other labor violations by their employers. Unfair dismissals constitute over 70 percent of its casework, followed by nonregistration of workers for unemployment insurance, wage-related problems, and underpayment of wages or nonpayment of overtime. Past support allowed the grantee to advise and support workers whose labor rights have been violated; conduct research into factors that inhibit women from asserting and defending their labor rights; and offer free advice on labor rights. The advice office also trains community-based advice offices on labor laws and supports them with difficult labor cases. This grant will assist the Casual Workers Advice Office to continue to offer advice and support to workers whose rights have been violated and to train and support community-based advice offices on various aspects of labor laws.

title: General Purposes
description: The Casual Workers Advice Office was established in 2011 to give free legal advice to workers who have been dismissed or face other labor violations by their employers. Unfair dismissals constitute over 70 percent of its casework, followed by nonregistration of workers for unemployment insurance, wage-related problems, and underpayment of wages or nonpayment of overtime. Past support allowed the grantee to advise and support workers whose labor rights have been violated, conduct research into factors that inhibit women from asserting and defending their labor rights, and offer free advice on labor rights. The advice office also trained community-based advice offices on labor laws and supported them with difficult labor cases. This grant increase will assist the Casual Workers Advice Office to produce educational materials to raise awareness about new labor rights, train workers on the new rights, and to provide legal assistance to workers who want to claim their rights.

title: General Purposes
description: The Casual Workers Advice Office was established in 2011 to give free legal advice to workers who have been dismissed or face other labor violations by their employers in South Africa. Unfair dismissals constitute the majority of its casework. Past support assisted the Casual Workers Advice Office to: advise and support workers whose labor rights were violated; launch awareness campaigns on new labor rights and assist workers to improve their working conditions; and assist workers to establish a workers forum to discuss common problems and explore possibilities for solidarity action. The grantee also trained community-based advice offices on labor laws and supported them with difficult labor cases. Ongoing support will allow the grantee to continue to offer advice and support to workers whose rights have been violated, train and support community-based advice offices on various aspects of labor laws, and raise awareness of labor rights among precarious workers and support them in accessing these rights.

title: General Purposes
description: The Casual Workers Advice Office was established in 2011 to give free legal advice to workers who have been dismissed or face other labor violations by their employers. The grantee trains paralegals from community-based advice offices on how to use the materials it has produced on worker rights and other labor matters and assists them when dealing with challenging labor cases. This grant will assist the Casual Workers Advice Office to advise and support workers whose labor rights have been violated, train advice offices on labor laws and support them with labor cases, conduct research around factors that inhibit women from asserting and defending their labor rights, and offer free advice on labor rights.

title: Supporting Youth Philanthropy in Communities
description: The purpose of the Supporting Youth Philanthropy in Communities project is to initiate a process whereby young people and community foundations and other community philanthropy organizations from around the world can be continuously learning from each other on how best to encourage and support youth philanthropy. This will involve creating an online discussion space, hosting an international gathering of youth community philanthropy leaders to explore existing initiatives and discuss possible new ideas and approaches in youth community philanthropy, and broadly disseminating the results through a publication. Of the 46 anticipated participants, 22 will be from outside North America. In addition to the publication, results will be presented at sessions at the fall Council on Foundations community foundation centennial and Council of Michigan Foundations conferences. The Council of Michigan Foundations is a membership association of more than 300 foundations and corporations making grants for charitable purposes.

title: Business Office Reconfiguration
description: This grant increase will provide support to the Flint Community Schools to aid in the reconfiguration of the district’s business office. In compliance with the district’s deficit elimination plan, it will restructure the business office and convert to an upgraded financial and human resources data management system — both initiatives aimed at bolstering the district’s operational effectiveness and implementing the controls required for long-term financial stability.

title: Business Office Reconfiguration
description: This grant will provide support to the Flint Community Schools to aid in the reconfiguration of the district’s business office. In compliance with the recently approved deficit elimination plan, the district will restructure the business office and convert to an upgraded financial and human resources data management system. Both initiatives are aimed at bolstering the district’s operational effectiveness and implementing the controls required for long-term financial stability and the improvement of education at the Flint Community Schools.

title: oDRussia
description: The program goal is to help foster independent and innovative analyses of current social and political trends in Eastern Europe. openDemocracy Limited is an online platform which publishes on a wide range of issues related to democratic processes, economic inequality, political accountability, and social development. Among its headline sections is oDRussia. This grant will help underpin oDRussia’s full evolution to a dual-language resource bringing a range of underrepresented voices to bear on journalism in this region. In 2014-2016, oDRussia experienced an average of almost 50,000 unique monthly views of materials, spiking to over 100,000 views in the wake of the crisis in Ukraine. It has increased its Russian language readership to almost a third of its overall audience, while maintaining its position as a provider of unique commentary for English language readers. Founded in 2001, openDemocracy Limited is an independent, public-interest, not-for-profit entity which publishes material under creative commons licensing on issues related to democratic practice, liberty, and human rights.

title: oDRussia
description: The program goal of openDemocracy Limited is to help foster independent critical analysis of current social and political trends in Russia and surrounding countries. The grantee’s online platform, openDemocracy.net, publishes on a wide range of issues related to democratic processes, economic inequality, political accountability, and social development. Among its headline sections is oDRussia, which focuses on events in and around Russia. This special opportunity grant will help support expansion of this unique resource, which draws on a range of both Russian and international commentators who analyze issues of everyday existence that reflect how Russians engage with society around them. While largely an English-language resource, oDRussia will seek to substantially increase its output of Russian-language material. It will also increase editorial partnerships to enhance coverage of a broader range of thematic issues. Founded in 2001, the grantee is an independent, public-interest, not-for-profit entity which publishes material under creative commons licensing on issues related to democratic practice, liberty, and human rights.

title: Flint Food Works Commercial Kitchen
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will support the continued development of the Flint Food Works Commercial Kitchen food business incubator at the Flint Farmers’ Market. The business incubator facility offers space, entrepreneurial programming, and technical assistance to small food enterprises and other culinary ventures that seek to create products for distribution. The project is managed by the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation’s supported organization, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, which works to improve the quality of life of Flint-area residents through the revitalization of downtown Flint and investments in infrastructures that provide people access to jobs, food, healthcare, and other essential services.

title: Flint Food Works Commercial Kitchen
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will support the continued development of the Flint Food Works Commercial Kitchen food business incubator located within the Flint Farmers’ Market. Flint Food Works has the capacity to incubate small food processors seeking to create nutritional products for distribution and prepared food for retail consumption. The kitchen offers a unique community benefit by providing nutritional education to residents on how to prepare healthy food that will mitigate the effects of lead. The project is managed by the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation’s supported organization, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation.

title: Flint Food Works Commercial Kitchen
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will support the continued development of the Flint Food Works Commercial Kitchen food business incubator located within the Flint Farmers’ Market. Flint Food Works has the capacity to incubate small food processors seeking to create nutritional products for distribution and prepared food for retail consumption. The kitchen offers a unique community benefit by providing nutritional education to residents on how to prepare healthy food that will mitigate the effects of lead. The project is managed by the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation’s supported organization, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation.

Flint Food Works has the capacity to incubate small food processors seeking to create nutritional products for distribution and prepared food for retail consumption. The kitchen offers a unique community benefit by providing nutritional education to residents on how to prepare healthy food that will mitigate the effects of lead. The project is managed by the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation’s supported organization, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation.

title: Flint Food Works Commercial Kitchen
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: The purpose of this grant is to support the development of a commercial kitchen food business incubator that will be located within the new Flint Farmers’ Market. The Flint Food Works Commercial Kitchen will have the capacity to incubate small food processors seeking to create value-added food products for wholesale distribution, as well as culinary ventures like catering and prepared food for retail consumption. The grant will also support first-year operating expenses associated with the transition of the market to its new downtown location. The project will be managed by the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation and its supported organization, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, which works to improve the quality of life of Flint-area residents through the revitalization of downtown Flint.

title: Center for Civil Society Innovation
description: The purpose of this initiative is to respond to the needs of nonprofits and other civic initiatives in Eurasia working to support democratic development in their countries. To this end, People in Need will establish and develop a new Center for Civil Society Innovation. The mission of the center will be to empower independent civil society representatives and organizations to address emerging challenges in their countries and communities. Through its efforts, the center will contribute to civil society in Eurasia becoming more self-reliant, resilient, and effective in increasing citizen participation in public processes and institutions. The center will work through a range of grantmaking and operational programming. During the first two years of the project, the grantee will oversee the registration of the new center; identify, hire, and build the capacity of core staff; establish and strengthen the center’s initial board; and assist with the development of the center’s medium- and long-term programmatic and operational strategies. The grantee will also carry out exploratory programming as the center is being established that will help to shape the center’s presence and create learning opportunities for ongoing program development. People in Need is based in Prague, Czech Republic.

title: Harold Alfond College Challenge Program Evaluation
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant will partially support the Harold Alfond College Challenge Program Evaluation. Created in 2008 as a pilot program in Portland, Maine, the Harold Alfond College Challenge automatically awards a $500 grant to every child born in Maine, as both an incentive to catalyze educational savings and to help more children develop college aspirations. Given its visibility and potential for replicability, evaluating its effects on children, families, and communities has implications not only for Maine, but for the nation as a whole. The anticipated findings could prove instrumental in advancing children’s savings account policies and practices.
