The Alfond Scholarship Foundation was created in 2008 to implement and manage the college challenge program.

title: Promoting a System of Early Financial Aid Accounts
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: With this grant, the Institute for Higher Education Policy will work to integrate savings strategies into national, state, and local initiatives designed to improve postsecondary education outcomes for low- and moderate-income students. Mott grant funds will enable the grantee to convene key stakeholders and identify strategies for better integrating children’s savings accounts into their access and success initiatives. The most promising integration strategies will be documented in a report and broadly disseminated for maximum visibility and impact. Based in Washington, D.C., the Institute for Higher Education Policy is a nonpartisan, nonprofit organization committed to promoting access to and success in higher education for all students.

title: Improving Postsecondary Outcomes in Michigan
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant will support the Michigan College Access Network’s efforts to increase college readiness, participation, and completion rates for Michigan residents, particularly among low-income, first-generation college students and students of color. Mott funding will support several specific projects including an annual conference, capacity building for afterschool professionals, and the grantee’s policy development efforts. Located in Lansing, the Michigan College Access Network is the leading organization working statewide to identify and implement policies and practices that decrease barriers and increase access to college.

title: Promoting Early Awareness and Commitment Financial Aid Strategies
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
geographic_focus: Indiana, Illinois, Nebraska, Ohio, North Dakota, Iowa, Minnesota, Missouri, Michigan, Wisconsin, Kansas, South Dakota
description: The National College Access Network is a Washington, D.C.-based nonprofit membership organization whose mission is to build, strengthen, and empower communities committed to college access and success so that all students, especially those from low-income, minority, and/or immigrant communities, can achieve college success. Given heightened attention on the issues of college completion and affordability, the grantee believes it is an opportune time to educate states and college completion stakeholders about ways to increase the effectiveness of financial aid policies as a tool to increase college enrollment and completion. With this grant, the grantee will work through its membership structure to encourage states — with a specific emphasis on Midwest states — to embed early awareness and commitment strategies within their existing need- and merit-based financial aid programs.

title: Teen Trendsetter Literacy Program
grantee: Barbara Bush Foundation for Family Literacy
description: This grant will support the Barbara Bush Foundation for Family Literacy to work in conjunction with the statewide afterschool networks to increase early literacy interventions through afterschool programs. This project will include: 1) working with the statewide afterschool networks to share promising practices and curricula among the afterschool field; 2) hosting a Barbara Bush Foundation roundtable for early literacy in afterschool; and 3) developing and disseminating information on successful elements of early literacy in afterschool, including on the Teen Trendsetters literacy mentorship program.

title: Afterschool and Service-Learning Initiative
location: St. Louis Park, MN, United States
description: This grant will support the National Youth Leadership Council in its efforts to integrate service-learning in afterschool programs as a strategy to increase students’ learning outcomes and civic participation in their schools and communities. The grantee will: 1) work with up to 15 statewide afterschool networks to integrate and support service learning in local afterschool programs; 2) develop a service-learning course for afterschool professionals; and 3) create a series of service-learning curriculum for afterschool programs.

title: Afterschool and Service-Learning Initiative
location: St. Louis Park, MN, United States
description: This grant will support the National Youth Leadership Council in its efforts to explore how afterschool and summer learning programs can integrate service learning as a strategy to increase learning outcomes for students. The grantee will: 1) work with up to five statewide afterschool networks to integrate and support service learning in local afterschool programs; 2) create a longer-term plan for how to infuse service-learning as a strategy for the statewide afterschool networks; and 3) work with the statewide afterschool networks and the National Summer Learning Association to develop resources and best practices for service learning and afterschool programs.

title: Increasing Science, Technology, Engineering and Math in Afterschool
description: This grant seeks to increase the availability of informal science education for students through afterschool and summer learning programs. Specifically, this grant will support the University of San Diego’s Center for Education Policy and Law to: 1) support the statewide afterschool networks in data collection and quality improvement efforts to increase the availability of STEM afterschool programs; 2) educate leaders at the local, state, and national levels on the importance of STEM afterschool programming; 3) disseminate a publication that highlights quality STEM programs, data, and outcomes; and 4) support technical assistance to the state networks in the area of STEM programming and evaluation.

title: Increasing Science, Technology, Engineering and Math in Afterschool
description: This grant seeks to increase the availability of informal science education for students through afterschool and summer learning programs. Specifically, this grant will support the STEM Next Opportunity Fund to: 1) support the statewide afterschool networks in data collection and quality improvement efforts to increase the availability of STEM afterschool programs; 2) educate leaders at the local, state, and national levels on the importance of STEM afterschool programming; 3) disseminate and promote the 11-state study and the STEM compendium; and 4) support technical assistance to the state networks in the area of STEM programming and evaluation.

title: Increasing Science, Technology, Engineering and Math in Afterschool
description: This grant seeks to increase the availability of informal science education for students through afterschool and summer learning programs. Specifically, this grant will support the STEM Next Opportunity Fund to: 1) support the statewide afterschool networks in data collection and quality improvement efforts toincrease the availability of STEM afterschool programs; 2) educate leaders at the local, state, and national levels on the importance of STEM afterschool programming; 3) support technical assistance to the state networks in the area of STEM programming and evaluation; 4) engage networks to scale impactful and exemplar STEM programming; and 5) develop STEM content and curriculum.

title: Increasing Science, Technology, Engineering and Math in Afterschool
description: This grant seeks to increase the availability of informal science education for students through afterschool and summer learning programs. Specifically, this grant will support the STEM Next Opportunity Fund to: 1) expand the statewide afterschool network STEM initiative to all 50 states; 2) support the statewide afterschool networks in data collection and quality improvement efforts to increase the availability of STEM afterschool programs; 3) educate leaders at the local, state, and national levels on the importance of STEM afterschool programming; 4) support technical assistance to the state networks in the area of STEM programming and evaluation; and 5) develop STEM content and curriculum.

title: Increasing Science, Technology, Engineering and Math in Afterschool
description: Through a joint partnership initiative with the Noyce Foundation, this grant to the University of San Diego seeks to increase the availability of informal science education for students across the country through afterschool and summer learning programs. Dr. Robert Noyce was the inventor of the integrated circuit and co-founder of Intel, and the family foundation that bears his name has provided significant leadership and funding nationwide to advance the area of science, technology, engineering, and math (STEM) education and science issues. Specifically, this grant will support the university’s Center for Education Policy and Law to: 1) support the statewide afterschool networks in data collection and quality improvement efforts to increase the availability of STEM afterschool programs; 2) hold a STEM afterschool summit focused on engaging policy and industry leaders at the state and national levels; 3) develop a publication that highlights quality STEM programs, data, and outcomes; and 4) support technical assistance to the state networks in the area of STEM programming and evaluation.

title: Principals as Leaders for High-Quality Afterschool and Summer Learning Opportunities
grantee: National Association of Elementary School Principals Foundation
description: This grant will support the National Association of Elementary School Principals Foundation to build the capacity of principals and afterschool leaders toward providing new enriching learning opportunities after school and over the summer months. The grantee will work to establish a national network of principals as leaders for high quality afterschool programs and support communities of practice. Specifically, this project will include: 1) conducting a needs assessment to identify strategies to increase quality and support for school-based and school-linked afterschool and summer learning programs; 2) developing best practices for how principals can utilize afterschool programs to support student academic and social development; 3) creating a national network of principals and states that can share exemplary afterschool practices; 4) working with states and districts to provide technical assistance to enhance afterschool programs; and 5) developing a special issue of “Principal” magazine focused on afterschool and summer learning opportunities.

title: Kindergarten to College Program
grantee: City and County of San Francisco
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: San Francisco’s Kindergarten to College Program is the first universal and automatic children’s college savings program in the country. Program administrators have set a goal of engaging 25 percent of all public school elementary students in active savings by 2018. To achieve this goal, the City and County of San Francisco will focus on expanded outreach strategies and family engagement activities. Support from the Foundation will enable the city to redesign program marketing materials and develop new dissemination strategies; make better use of social media and other technology-based communication tools; and design and implement strategies to increase the engagement of parents, teachers, and principals in the program. The San Francisco United School District is on the leading edge of the demographic trends taking hold in the United States—the majority of public school children come from minority families, including 38 percent Asian, 26 percent Hispanic/Latino, 13 percent white, and 8 percent African American. In addition, approximately 61 percent of students in the district are enrolled in the National School Lunch program.

title: Kindergarten to College Program
grantee: City and County of San Francisco
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: San Francisco’s Kindergarten to College Program is the first universal and automatic children’s college savings program in the country. Since the 2011 launch, the City Treasurer’s office has opened savings accounts for over 18,000 students in 74 elementary schools. Program administrators have set a goal of engaging 25 percent of all public school elementary students in active savings by 2017. To achieve this goal, the City and County of San Francisco will focus on expanded outreach strategies and family engagement activities. Support from the Foundation will enable the city to redesign program marketing materials and develop new dissemination strategies; make better use of social media and other technology-based communication tools; and design and implement strategies to increase the engagement of parents, teachers, and principals in the program. The San Francisco United School District is on the leading edge of the demographic trends taking hold in the United States — the majority of public school children come from minority families, including 38 percent Asian, 26 percent Hispanic/Latino, 13 percent white, and 8 percent African American. In addition, approximately 61 percent of students in the district are enrolled in the National School Lunch Program.

title: Role of Microenterprise and Sector Strategies in Connecting Young People to Prosperous Livelihoods
description: This grant will enable the Aspen Institute’s Economic Opportunities Program to explore how microenterprise and sectoral employment strategies can connect youth to productive employment pathways. The project builds on the Foundation’s grantmaking legacy in workforce development by pivoting these strategies toward a focus on youth. Located in Washington, D.C., the Aspen Institute works to develop practical leadership in today’s world. It accomplishes this mission through nonpartisan seminars and policy programs designed for leaders in business, government, the media, education, the arts, and the independent sector from democratic societies worldwide.

title: Role of Microenterprise and Sector Strategies in Connecting Young People to Prosperous Livelihoods
description: This grant will support the Aspen Institute’s efforts to prepare the next generation for the workforce by utilizing microenterprise and sector partnership strategies that can connect youth to productive employment pathways. The Role of Microenterprise and Sector Strategies in Connecting Young People to Prosperous Livelihoods project builds on the Foundation’s long time support for workforce development strategies for those facing multiple barriers to employment while pivoting these strategies toward youth.

title: Support the Growth and Development of National Service
description: This grant will enable Voices for National Service, a program of City Year, Inc., to better support the national service field, elevate the public discourse on national service, and share the unique value and impact of national service with key stakeholders and the public. This will be accomplished by supporting forthcoming research initiatives that will help make the case for expanding service opportunities across the country and continuing to elevate the public discourse on national service.

title: A Service Continuum Improving Career & Postsecondary Pathways
description: This grant will enable YouthBuild USA to engage low-income youth in meaningful service experiences that will support their education, college, and career success. The grantee will continue to connect low-income youth with national and service opportunities that strategically build their capacity and willingness to engage in college and career success.

title: A Service Continuum Improving Career & Postsecondary Pathways
description: This grant will help pilot and document YouthBuild USA’s A Service Continuum Improving Career & Postsecondary Pathways Program, which builds on the Foundation’s more than two decades of support for the grantee’s education, training, and workforce readiness strategies. The grantee will continue to connect youth with meaningful national and community service experiences that can lead to positive postsecondary education, career success, and community engagement outcomes.

title: Flint Community Schools Education Plan Support
description: This grant increase provides support to the NEA Foundation to aid the Flint Community Schools district in planning for the implementation of the district’s new educational plan as part of a comprehensive turnaround strategy. The NEA Foundation and district leadership will collaborate to align the education plan with other district planning tools, including school and district improvement plans, and identify ways to implement the plan with fidelity.

title: Flint Community Schools Education Plan Support
description: This grant provides support to the NEA Foundation to aid the Flint Community Schools district in analyzing the recently completed educational audit and developing a new educational plan as part of a comprehensive turnaround strategy. The NEA Foundation and district leadership will collaborate to lead a multistakeholder planning process that supports the creation of an innovative, integrated, and systemic education plan for Flint Community Schools.

title: Strategic Planning
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: Funding will support a team of consultants who specialize in urban public libraries to assist in the strategic planning of the Flint Public Library. Founded in 1851, the grantee is a historical institution in the city of Flint. The grantee plays a pivotal role in the community by filling technology gaps, assisting residents with job applications, teaching children how to read, and much more. With property taxes in Flint falling 69 percent in the past five years, the grantee has lost a large portion of public funding.

title: Multi Modal Development and Delivery
description: This grant will allow Smart Growth America to partner with Michigan state agencies on two related projects that promote more livable and environmentally sustainable communities. The grantee is a national organization dedicated to the broad adoption of compact development and multimodal transportation principles. The projects covered under this grant include: 1) assisting the Michigan Department of Transportation with implementation of Michigan’s so-called complete streets legislation, which is intended to make roads accessible to all users; and 2) partnering with the Michigan State Housing Development Authority on a series of studies that assess the potential for walkable urban development in the state’s metropolitan areas.

title: Developing Community Schools in Bulgaria
description: The project goal is to develop community schools in Bulgaria as a mechanism for creating effective partnerships between communities and schools. To this end, the National Network for Children will provide technical assistance and funding to the 13 existing community schools; introduce the community school concept to 20 new communities; document and publicize the project achievements; and create a broad support base for the community school concept among schools, community organizations, and educational authorities. In addition, the grantee will support learning and exchange between the Bulgarian community school movement and movements in other countries in the Central and Eastern Europe region. During the past grant period, the grantee created and trained a project team with support from the International Centre of Excellence for Community Schools (Mott grantee). The grantee also introduced the concept of community schools in 13 schools and supported these schools to run more than 20 trainings for teachers and parents in their communities and organize over 60 community initiatives with the participation of over 600 teachers, 800 parents, and 3,000 students.

title: Developing Community Schools in Bulgaria
description: The project goal is to introduce and develop the concept of community schools in Bulgaria as a tool for creating effective partnerships between communities and schools. To this end, the National Network for Children will create a project team of experienced community workers and educators from its member organizations. The grantee will cooperate with the International Centre of Excellence for Community Schools, a Mott grantee, to increase the team’s knowledge and understanding of the community school concept and practice around the Central and Eastern Europe and Russia region. In addition, the grantee will pilot the concept in 10 schools and strengthen the schools’ capacities to operate as community schools. Also, the network will document the experiences of the pilot phase. The grantee was established in 2003 with the mission to facilitate and strengthen the cooperation between nongovernmental organizations and all relevant stakeholders to ensure rights and welfare for children and families in Bulgaria. Currently, the grantee has 122 members working in different fields, including education, social welfare, and recreation.

title: Michigan Clean Energy Report
description: In order to develop and implement high impact actions to address clean energy issues, community organizations need accurate, current, and consistent information. Michigan Saves, dedicated to making energy improvements easy and affordable for citizens and businesses across the state, will research the current status of energy efficiency improvements and clean energy deployment in Michigan, with a focus on as many as eight mid-sized Michigan cities.

title: NGOsource
description: Launched in March 2013 as a project of TechSoup and the Council on Foundations, NGOsource is an online equivalency determination service for international grantmaking that offers a centralized repository of equivalency determinations for foreign organizations. NGOsource streamlines cross-border philanthropy to the benefit of grantmakers and the international grantees they serve. Since its launch, NGOsource has processed almost 1,500 equivalency determination requests from 136 grantmaker members for organizations in 103 foreign countries, facilitating approximately $150 million in international grants. During this grant period, NGOsource will continue evolving into a viable social enterprise, forecasting it will reach full sustainability by early 2018. Activities will include: 1) expanding outreach to increase grantmaker adoption rates; 2) increasing the number of equivalency determinations in the repository; and 3) refining tools and processes to streamline product offerings. Founded in 1987 as CompuMentor, TechSoup helps nonprofits globally to obtain and use technology to heighten their impact.

title: NGOsource
description: Launched in March 2013 as a project of TechSoup Global and the Council on Foundations, NGOsource is a membership service for United States grantmakers that streamlines and standardizes the equivalency determination process. The service aims to dramatically improve the efficiency of international grantmaking and to inspire a significant increase in cross-border philanthropy. Over 2015, NGOsource will improve the functionality of the service and raise funds needed to achieve financial sustainability through membership dues and fees. Mott funds will support collaborations with nonprofit information providers such as GuideStar and Foundation Center, application programming interface integration with commercial grants management systems, development of capability to work in several languages, cooperation with leading international grantmakers on strategies to seed the NGOsource repository with previously certified equivalency determinations, and expanded outreach to small- and medium-sized foundations. Founded in 1987 as CompuMentor, TechSoup Global helps nonprofits globally obtain and use technology to heighten their impact.

title: Ibero-American Network of Community Foundations
geographic_focus: Spain, Portugal, Central America, Mexico, South America
description: This grant provides support to Instituto Comunitario Grande Florianopolis to coordinate the activities of the Ibero-American Network of Community Foundations. Initiated in 2013, the network aims to strengthen community philanthropy organizations in Spain, Portugal, and Latin America. It currently has 32 members from Brazil, Mexico, Spain, Portugal, and Uruguay. Over the next two years, the network’s objectives are to: 1) structure governance and membership policies; 2) promote virtual and face-to-face exchange experiences; 3) improve communication among members and with other stakeholders; and 4) increase the participation of European members. Activities will include monthly virtual meetings; one in-person convening of country representatives in 2015; a full in-person member convening in 2016; peer exchanges for at least ten member practitioners, maintenance, and enhancement of a trilingual Web site with biweekly news; and the provision of promotional materials about the network and the social impact of its members. The network is managed by the Instituto Comunitário Grande Florianópolis, Brazil’s largest community foundation.

title: Office Relocation
description: This project grant will provide funding to support the relocation of the United Way of Genesee County offices from the First Merit Bank building to Plaza One on Court and Harrison Streets in Flint, Michigan. The new location will provide greater public access to the organization. The United Way of Genesee County supports a network of local nonprofit human service organizations and provides funding to nonprofits in the areas of education, health, income stability, and basic needs.

title: China-Latin America Sustainable Investments Initiative
description: This project supports development of legal expertise and training for organizations, communities, and Latin American countries receiving Chinese investment in energy and infrastructure. The project builds on experience with strengthening social and environmental standards in international financial institutions and deepening understanding and application of Chinese standards to its overseas investments. Titled the China-Latin America Sustainable Investments Initiative, this is a project of the Bank Information Center, a global nonprofit with deep experience working with international financial institutions.

title: China-Latin America Sustainable Investments Initiative
description: The China-Latin America Sustainable Investment Initiative, a project of the Bank Information Center, works with partners in South America to monitor Chinese investment and strengthen voluntary Chinese guidelines for social and environmental standards, using best international practice. Over the previous project period, the grantee worked with Chinese partners to research and publish its third legal manual on Chinese social and environmental guidelines and trained partners in Latin America in its use. This renewal grant will support the grantee to update the manual and work on specific Chinese investments in energy and infrastructure in Argentina, Brazil, Ecuador, and Peru.

title: China-Latin America Sustainable Investments Initiative
description: The China-Latin America Sustainable Investments Initiative at American University supports development of legal expertise and training for organizations, communities, and Latin American countries receiving Chinese investment in energy and infrastructure. The project builds on experience gained in strengthening social and environmental standards in international financial institutions and deepening understanding and application of Chinese standards to its overseas investments.

title: Outsourced CFO and Accounting Technical Assistance
description: This grant increase will provide continued support to the Flint Community Schools for temporary help in the business office, including chief financial officer and accounting positions. The district received approval of its state-mandated deficit elimination plan earlier this year, but careful monitoring and updating of the plan and the budget requires financial assistance from individuals with skill sets requisite for the complexities associated with a distressed district.

title: Outsourced CFO and Accounting Technical Assistance
description: This grant will provide support to the Flint Community Schools with interim help in the business office, including chief financial officer and accounting positions. The district is operating under a state-mandated deficit elimination plan that needs careful monitoring and updating, along with corresponding updates to the budget, which requires financial expertise from individuals with skillsets requisite for the complexities associated with a distressed district.

title: Outsourced CFO and Accounting Technical Assistance
description: This grant increase will provide support to the Flint Community Schools with interim help in the business office, including chief financial officer, accounting, and human resources assistance. The district is operating under a state-mandated deficit elimination plan that needs careful monitoring and updating, along with corresponding updates to the budget, which requires expertise from individuals with skill sets requisite for the complexities associated with a distressed district.

title: Outsourced CFO and Accounting Technical Assistance
description: This grant will provide support to the Flint Community Schools’ business office, including a chief financial officer and accounting assistance. The district is operating under a state-mandated deficit elimination plan that needs careful monitoring and updating, along with corresponding updates to the budget, which requires expertise from individuals with skill sets requisite for the complexities associated with a distressed district.

title: Outsourced CFO and Accounting Technical Assistance
description: This grant will provide support to the Flint Community Schools with interim help in the business office, including chief financial officer and accounting positions. The district received approval of its state-mandated deficit elimination plan earlier this year, but careful monitoring and updating of the plan and the budget for the upcoming year requires financial expertise from individuals with skillsets requisite for the complexities associated with a distressed district.

title: Sustainable Development Finance in South America
description: The Asociacion Ambiente y Sociedad is a Colombian nonprofit organization specialized in research, monitoring, and advocacy related to investment and development finance in Colombia and South America. Over the last grant period, the grantee monitored international investment in infrastructure in the region and engaged international and national financial institutions. This grant renewal will support the grantee’s efforts to analyze financial strategies and actors in regional integration; monitor national, regional, and international development finance institutions; and work with network partners to advocate for stronger transparency, accountability, and adherence to the highest standards.

title: Sustainable Development Finance in South America
description: The Asociacion Ambiente y Sociedad is a Colombian nonprofit organization specializing in research, monitoring, and advocacy related to investment and development finance in Colombia and South America. Over the last grant period, the grantee worked with regional coalitions to strengthen Chinese social and environmental commitments in its overseas investments. This grant renewal will support the grantee’s efforts to monitor Chinese investment, as well as implementation of the new social and environmental framework of the World Bank Group and engage in the process of updating the Inter-American Development Bank safeguards framework.

title: Sustainable Development Finance in South America
description: Development finance for integration of energy and infrastructure in South America is increasingly influenced by new actors, such as the Brazilian Development Bank and Chinese financiers, which have not adopted strong social and environmental safeguards, but instead rely on national standards. Meanwhile, the highest standards achieved at traditional international financial institutions are under review and may be eroded. This grant will support Asociacion Ambiente y Sociedad to analyze new financial strategies and actors in regional integration; monitor national, regional, and international development finance institutions; and work with network partners to advocate for stronger transparency and adherence to the highest standards.

title: Downtown Flint Summer Event Planning and Implementation
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to the city of Flint will support public safety and traffic engineering costs for downtown festivals and events. Event organizers and producers will work with the city to ensure that events have adequate public safety personnel as well as to clear traffic routes for events throughout the festival season.

title: Southeastern Water Supply Security and Sustainability
geographic_focus: Georgia, Tennessee, South Carolina, North Carolina, Alabama
description: With prior Mott support, River Network launched a project in the southeastern United States to deepen river and other freshwater groups’ understanding of water quantity issues: instream flow protections, interbasin transfer regulation, etc. As a result, there is increased understanding of how and why to protect and restore river flows in the Southeast. With additional Mott support, the grantee will build and facilitate a Southeast Flows Peer Learning Network that allows watershed and state-level river groups to learn from each other and other experts, leverage their skills and efforts, create new alliances, and spark innovative approaches to ongoing problems. Funds will also be used to support the grantee’s annual meeting in 2017, to be held in Michigan.

title: Southeastern Water Supply Security and Sustainability
geographic_focus: Georgia, Tennessee, South Carolina, North Carolina, Alabama
description: The southeastern United States, historically an area of relative water abundance, has experienced rapid expansion of water stress in the past several years. Fortunately, much can be done to redirect the water-use trajectory of the Southeast to move toward a water future that is secure and sustainable. River Network, a national leader in supporting river and watershed organizations, will help local watershed organizations in the Southeast become a stronger voice for sustainable water management. Project activities will include the development and dissemination of a basic information package on water supply issues and the provision of technical assistance to watershed groups.

title: Generation @ Junior Community Chest
description: The Lusa Community Chest is a community grantmaker established in 1990 to support community-based initiatives in the Free State province in South Africa. It makes small grants and trains community-based organizations in areas that help improve their performance. The Generation @ Junior Community Chest project promotes youth philanthropy by equipping young people in schools with skills and tools to respond to challenges they see in their communities. Young people learn to initiate and manage projects in order to improve the quality of life of those in need. Previous support enabled the grantee to introduce the project in more schools, support learners to identify the issues they want to address, and raise the funds they need to implement projects. This grant will support the grantee to continue to expand the program, document the experiences of learners that have participated in the program, and support the network of community chests of South Africa in rolling out the program.

title: Generation @ Junior Community Chest
description: The Lusa Community Chest is a community grantmaker established in 1990 to support community-based initiatives in the Free State province in South Africa. It makes small grants and trains community-based organizations in areas that help improve their work. The Generation @ Junior Community Chest project promotes youth philanthropy by equipping young people in schools with skills and tools that enable them to identify challenges in their communities and find solutions to those challenges. Young people learn to initiate and manage projects that improve the quality of life for people in their communities. Previous support enabled the grantee to encourage young people in schools to initiate projects that address a challenge in their community. Additionally, the groups organized an event to encourage communities to take ownership of their own development. This grant will support the grantee to continue to expand the program, document the experiences of learners that have participated in the program, and respond to the needs of young people that go through the program.

title: Generation @ Junior Community Chest
description: The Lusa Community Chest was founded in 1990 to support community-based initiatives in the Free State Province of South Africa. It makes small grants to community-based organizations and nonprofits working in poor communities. It also works with local businesses to design corporate social responsibility initiatives that are responsive to community needs and promotes the development of young people. The Generation @ Junior Community Chest project promotes youth philanthropy by encouraging young people in schools to be involved in improving the quality of life in their communities. Young people learn new skills that empower them to initiate projects that respond to the daily struggles of communities. This grant will support the grantee to introduce the Generation @ Junior Community Chest project in more schools and equip the youth with the necessary skills to initiate projects where they live. It will also provide support to existing Generation @ Junior Community Chest projects in schools, and introduce the project to the Community Chests of South Africa network — a network of six community chests working across the country.

title: Flint and Genesee Literacy Network Capacity Building
description: Mott Community College serves as the lead agency for the Flint and Genesee Literacy Network. The network is a coalition of community organizations, businesses, and governmental leaders working toward increasing literacy and basic skill levels in Genesee County. A recent planning process determined family literacy would serve as the priority area for the network over the next couple of years. With this grant, the grantee will engage the National Center for Families Learning to implement family literacy training, programming, and resources for network participants as well as the community at large.

title: Flint and Genesee Literacy Network Capacity Building
description: Mott Community College serves as the lead agency for the Flint and Genesee Literacy Network. The network is a coalition of community organizations, businesses, and governmental leaders working toward increasing literacy and basic skills levels in Genesee County. Family literacy is a priority area for the network. With this grant, the grantee will engage PolicyLink and Clear Impact to provide impact measurement and sustainability technical assistance.

title: Flint and Genesee Literacy Network Capacity Building
description: Mott Community College serves as the lead agency for the Flint and Genesee Literacy Network. The network is a coalition of community organizations, businesses, and governmental leaders working toward increasing literacy and basic skill levels in Genesee County. Family literacy was selected by the community as the priority area for the network over the next couple of years. The grantee will work with network partners to increase their capacity to deliver high quality family literacy programming.

title: Flint and Genesee Literacy Network Capacity Building
description: Mott Community College serves as the lead agency for the Flint and Genesee Literacy Network. The network is a coalition of community organizations, businesses, and governmental leaders working toward increasing literacy and basic skill levels in Genesee County. Family literacy was selected by the community as the priority area for the network over the next couple of years. The grantee will work with network partners to increase their capacity to deliver high-quality family literacy programming.

title: Flint and Genesee Literacy Network
description: Mott Community College serves as the lead agency for the Flint and Genesee Literacy Network. The network is a coalition of community organizations, businesses, and governmental leaders working toward increasing literacy and basic skill levels in Genesee County. The grantee will work with network partners to increase their capacity to deliver high-quality early education and family literacy programming with a particular focus on two-generation approaches.

title: Flint and Genesee Literacy and Basic Skills Network Capacity Building
description: For the past three years, Mott Community College has served as the lead agency for the Flint and Genesee Literacy and Basic Skills Network. The network is a coalition of community organizations, businesses, and governmental leaders working toward increasing basic skills and literacy levels in Genesee County. With this grant, the grantee will engage a team of specialized literacy consultants to lead a six-month planning process which will identify priority goals and objectives for the network.

title: Statewide Afterschool Network Support
description: This grant will allow BoardSource to support and strengthen the leadership capacity of the statewide afterschool networks. Specifically, this grant will support BoardSource to: 1) provide direct technical assistance in areas including building organizational capacity, board development and governance, fiscal management, and succession planning; 2) create and disseminate governance and nonprofit management tools for the statewide afterschool networks; and 3) enable each statewide afterschool network to become an organizational member of BoardSource.

title: Statewide Afterschool Network Support
description: This grant increase will allow BoardSource to continue its efforts in supporting and strengthening the leadership capacity of the statewide afterschool networks. Specifically, this project will support increased capacity in the areas of network sustainability and enhanced technical assistance for the statewide afterschool networks.

title: Statewide Afterschool Network Support
description: This grant will allow BoardSource to support and strengthen the leadership and capacity of the statewide afterschool networks. Specifically, this grant will support the grantee to: 1) provide direct technical assistance to meet the needs of the statewide afterschool networks; 2) provide sustainability training; and 3) enable statewide afterschool networks to become an organizational member of BoardSource.

title: Statewide Afterschool Network Support
description: This grant will allow BoardSource to support and strengthen the leadership capacity of the statewide afterschool networks. Specifically, this grant will support BoardSource to: 1) provide direct technical assistance in areas including building organizational capacity, board development and governance, fiscal management, and succession planning; 2) create and disseminate governance and nonprofit management tools for the statewide afterschool networks; and 3) afford each statewide afterschool network to become an organizational member of BoardSource.

title: Statewide Afterschool Networks Evaluation
description: This grant will support Public Profit in its efforts to develop and implement an assessment framework to further strengthen the national afterschool network. Specifically, Public Profit will work with the networks to: 1) document their work; 2) identify areas of strength and potential growth; 3) identify successful practices for established and emerging statewide afterschool networks to emulate; and 4) document and disseminate the work and impact of the overall national network.

title: Active Citizens - A Resource of Communities
description: The program goal is to promote the development of community-based philanthropy in support of local development in the Northwest district of Russia. In this project, the Arkhangelsk Centre of Social Technologies “Garant” will work closely with two initial pilot communities to help community leaders and officials identify and apply local resources to local community development challenges. Grantee staff will conduct regular training activities and consultations with community leaders. They will explore with local activists the possibility of establishing institutionalized forms of community philanthropy, drawing on the existing Northwest alliance of community foundations as a mentoring resource. A school for leaders will target promising community actors from at least 15 municipalities to help broaden the reach of the program’s activities. Since its inception in 1998, the Arkhangelsk Centre of Social Technologies “Garant” has worked on developing civil society infrastructure and community philanthropy across Northwest Russia and beyond.

title: Longway Planetarium Theater Renovation
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to the Flint Cultural Center Corporation will support a major upgrade to Longway Planetarium’s projection system. A state-of-the-art, full dome video projection system will be installed along with new seating and a new sound system. The new full dome video technology will enable Longway Planetarium to play an enhanced role in supporting science, technology, engineering, and math curriculum for both K-12 and higher education students. In addition to astronomy and star shows, full dome video allows for a much broader range of content to be projected, including science content such as biomedical, chemistry, earth science, engineering, and physics. This upgrade will expand the utilization of Longway Planetarium, create stronger partnerships with local schools and colleges, and better serve the residents of Flint and Genesee County.

title: DIA Settlement
description: Foundation for Detroit’s Future was created in 2014 and is a supporting organization to the Community Foundation for Southeast Michigan, a public charity dedicated to Detroit-area philanthropy. The grantee works to lessen the burdens of government, combat community deterioration and improve quality of life of the general public in and around the city of Detroit through, among other things, conducting activities and programs, and providing support and funding to governmental entities, charitable organizations and others. This grant will provide partial support to preserve and protect the city of Detroit’s art museum as an educational and cultural resource, foster and promote the economic revitalization and fiscal health of the city of Detroit, and enable the city to fulfill its municipal financial and civic obligations. Support for the Foundation for Detroit’s Future comes primarily through donor contributions.

title: Accountability in Practice: Lessons from the CAO
description: The Compliance, Advisor, Ombudsman office was established in 1999 as the independent accountability mechanism for the World Bank Group’s private-sector agencies. This office receives and responds to complaints from communities affected by projects funded or guaranteed by these World Bank Group agencies. Despite the importance of this office, relatively little outside analysis has been done regarding the implications of its activities and the lessons it provides for further accountability. Through this grant, the American University’s Washington College of Law will manage the preparation, editing, and distribution of a book, documenting the lessons learned from the Compliance, Advisor, Ombudsman’s first 15 years. In addition, the grantee will convene workshops to discuss the book’s findings and implications for other accountability mechanisms.

title: Shifting the Narrative: Addressing Africa's Energy Poverty Challenge
description: Nearly one in five people globally lack access to electricity, and this is a major development challenge facing the world’s poor, particularly in Africa. If the right policies, financing, and incentives are in place, micro-, small-, and medium-sized enterprises based in Africa could create energy solutions that will yield economic benefits for African communities while not exacerbating climate change impacts. Through this grant, Oxfam America has created a new analysis illustrating that addressing the energy challenges facing the poor in rural Africa will also provide the economic opportunities to address their poverty. The grantee will use this new analytical framework over the next grant period to influence U.S. investment in Africa’s energy sector to ensure that small-scale renewable energy is prioritized.

title: Shifting the Narrative: Addressing Africa's Energy Poverty Challenge
description: Nearly one in five people globally lack access to electricity, and this is a major development challenge facing the world’s poor, particularly in Africa. If the right policies, financing, and incentives are in place, African-led micro-, small-, and medium-sized enterprises could create energy solutions that will yield economic benefits for their communities while not exacerbating climate change impacts. Currently, nearly 80 percent of public financing is directed toward energy projects that do not meet the needs of the poor. With this renewal, Oxfam America will champion large-scale investment by the World Bank Group and African Development Bank for the deployment of clean energy technologies, distributed energy generation, and micro-grids that can help to lift communities out of poverty. To accomplish this goal, the grantee will undertake rigorous analyses of multilateral financial flows, inform ongoing policy debates, develop compelling messages that link energy access to sustainable development priorities, and engage with key international, national, and local civil society organizations.

title: Shifting the Narrative: Addressing Africa's Energy Poverty Challenge
description: Access to affordable energy continues to be a major development challenge facing the world’s poor, particularly in Africa. If the right policies, financing, and incentives are in place, African-led micro-, small-, and medium-sized enterprises could create energy solutions that will yield economic benefits for their communities while not exacerbating climate change impacts. With this renewal, Oxfam America will champion investment by the World Bank Group and African Development Bank for the deployment of clean energy technologies, distributed energy generation, and micro-grids that can help to lift communities out of poverty. To accomplish this goal, the grantee will undertake rigorous analyses of multilateral financial flows, inform ongoing policy debates, develop compelling messages that link energy access to sustainable development priorities, and engage with key international, national, and local civil society organizations.

title: Shifting the Narrative: Addressing Africa's Energy Poverty Challenge
description: Nearly one in five people globally lack access to electricity, and this is a major development challenge facing the world’s poor, particularly in Africa. Electricity is a key driver of business growth and economic development. If the right policies, financing, and incentives are in place, small and medium- sized enterprises based in Africa could create energy solutions that will yield economic benefits for African communities while not exacerbating climate change impacts. There is an opportunity to influence domestic investment in Africa’s energy sector to ensure that off-grid and mini-grid renewable electricity are prioritized in order to provide access to millions in poor rural communities. With this grant, Oxfam America will develop the research and communications strategy that helps to frame the debate on such energy access issues in Africa.

title: State of the Nonprofit Sector Annual Survey
description: The State of the Nonprofit Sector Annual Survey was initially created by the Nonprofit Finance Fund as a collective effort to understand the impact that the 2008 recession had on nonprofit organizations and their communities. At present, it is a key resource that is providing United States nonprofit sector stakeholders and the public with timely data on trends, challenges, opportunities, and actions in the whole nonprofit sector as well as in subsectors and geographic regions. This grant will support the exploration of opportunities to refine and improve the integrity of the processes and methodology applied in the survey and an analysis of the representativeness of the data collected. Founded in 1980, the Nonprofit Finance Fund is a leading community development financial institution that helps organizations connect money to mission effectively, and supports innovations such as growth capital campaigns, cross-sector economic recovery initiatives, and impact investing.

title: Community Education Initiative
description: This grant provides support to the Crim Fitness Foundation in its role as the lead agency for a reimagined community schools model for the Flint Community Schools. The second year of developing and implementing the community schools strategy will involve further building out the partners and programs at the Brownell Holmes STEM Academy pilot site and expanding to three new elementary schools: Eisenhower, Potter, and Durant-Tuuri-Mott.

title: Community Education Initiative
description: This grant provides support to the Crim Fitness Foundation in its role as the lead agency for a reimagined community schools model in Flint. The third year of developing and implementing the community schools strategy will involve adding new partners, expanding programs at all nine elementary schools, and beginning to initiate the strategy at the two high schools in the Flint Community Schools district. The community schools strategy will help make available the strong, research based educational and enrichment opportunities that are important interventions for individuals from birth to young adulthood who may have been exposed to lead, as those interventions may mitigate the long-term impacts of such exposure.

title: Community Education Initiative
description: This grant provides support to the Crim Fitness Foundation to continue to serve as the lead agency for the community schools model in Flint. The fourth year of implementing the community schools strategy will involve expanding the depth and impact of programs at all 11 Flint Community Schools district buildings. The community schools strategy will help make available the strong, research-based educational and enrichment opportunities that are important interventions for individuals from birth to young adulthood who may have been exposed to lead, as those interventions can help mitigate the long-term impacts of such exposure.

title: Community Schools Initiative
description: This grant provides support to the Crim Fitness Foundation in its role as the lead agency for a reimagined community school model for the Flint Community Schools. A community schools resource coordinator will be hired to develop and implement a 21st century, sustainable model of community schools at the Brownell/Holmes STEM Academy, which will serve as the pilot site. The resource coordinator will also conduct a needs assessment at other schools within the district with the aim of expanding the model across the district.

title: Educational Plan Implementation
description: This grant will support Flint Community Schools in implementing the newly developed educational plan. Operationalization of the educational plan will include aligning the educational plan, district improvement plan, and school improvement plans; providing professional development and technology to implement Teachscape, a model that focuses on teacher evaluations and feedback mechanisms; establishing a leadership academy to train current administrators and develop a pipeline of future leaders within the district; and following a professional learning communities model to promote a collaborative culture, teamwork, systematic interventions for students, and a results-oriented culture.

title: Art School Endowment
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to the Flint Institute of Arts will help build the Art School Endowment fund. The endowment provides general operating support for the art school, one of the largest museum art schools in the nation. The Art School has an annual enrollment of about 1,500 students and offers studio instruction in drawing, painting, photography, mixed media, printmaking, ceramics, glass mosaic, fiber, and metal sculpture, with scholarships available to those needing financial assistance. The school serves another 4,000 children and adults each year through summer camps for youth, free family activities, and a pre-college portfolio development program for high school students interested in pursuing a college education in the arts. The goal is to build the art school endowment to sustain its operations in perpetuity.

title: Financing Water Quality Improvements
description: EcoWorks is a nonprofit organization that seeks to advance the sustainable use of energy and natural resources in southeast Michigan through education, job training, consulting, and policy reform efforts. Through its experience working with Michigan communities and other partners, the grantee identified an opportunity to connect energy efficiency programs to water quality improvements. With Mott support, the grantee will develop a package of financing tools that will allow municipalities and businesses to pay for water quality improvements through savings gained from energy efficiency improvements to their water treatment equipment. These financing mechanisms will be tested in up to ten water or wastewater treatment facilities in southeast Michigan. The grantee will develop a report to share lessons learned, identify areas for improvement, and provide sample policies for developing similar tools in other Great Lakes states.

title: Great Lakes Showcase
geographic_focus: Indiana, Pennsylvania, Illinois, Minnesota, New York, Michigan, Ohio, Wisconsin
description: The Alliance for the Great Lakes, founded in 1970 as the Lake Michigan Federation, seeks to conserve and restore the Great Lakes freshwater ecosystem using policy, education, and local conservation efforts. The persistent, complex, ecological problems facing the Great Lakes require new approaches, which must be supported by a motivated and engaged citizenry. With Mott support, the grantee will assess the feasibility of a regional conference or other public platform for showcasing Great Lakes ideas and solutions in a way that increases public interest in these issues.

title: Building the Blue Economy
description: The Buffalo Niagara Riverkeeper is an environmental organization focused on protecting and restoring the Buffalo River and portions of Lake Erie and Lake Ontario. The organization developed an initiative to help Buffalo transform from a rust belt city into a vibrant community that capitalizes on local water resources to boost economic development while improving water quality in local waterways. With this Mott grant, the grantee will research and define measurable, achievable actions that promote the health and vitality of the Great Lakes while also advancing economic and social goals. A report will be developed to provide a framework and tool kit for advancing such strategies in Buffalo that can be applied to other communities in the Great Lakes region.

title: Improving Water Resources Management in the Great Lakes
geographic_focus: Wisconsin, Indiana, Illinois, Michigan, Pennsylvania, Minnesota, Ohio, New York
description: The University of Wisconsin-Madison’s Center on Wisconsin Strategy conducts research and helps implement solutions for improving environmental sustainability across all sectors. The center provides technical assistance, leads public outreach, and hosts policy learning networks for state and local government executives. With previous Mott support, the center investigated ways to help state transportation agencies and city managers work together to reduce polluted stormwater runoff. This grant renewal will allow the grantee to build on its stormwater efforts and help Great Lakes cities improve how they also integrate the management of wastewater and drinking water systems. The center will conduct research, coordinate with partners, and develop educational materials to help cities, utilities, and community groups protect freshwater resources while also ensuring safe and clean drinking water is delivered to homes and businesses.

title: Healthy Public Water Systems in the Great Lakes Basin - Mayor's Innovation Project
geographic_focus: Pennsylvania, Illinois, Indiana, Ohio, Minnesota, New York, Michigan, Wisconsin
description: The University of Wisconsin-Madison’s Center on Wisconsin Strategy conducts research and helps implement integrated solutions for improving environmental sustainability across all sectors. One of the center’s signature efforts is the Mayor’s Innovation Project, a national learning network for mayors and their senior staff focused on assembling best practices in a wide range of policy areas relevant to cities, including infrastructure and water. With prior Mott support, the project researched ways in which cities in the Great Lakes region can better integrate their water management services to create greater efficiency, cost savings, environmental and social benefits, and ultimately, improved water quality. The project also coordinated a network of nonprofits working in the Great Lakes region that have similar aims. With continued Mott support, the project will produce materials summarizing their findings and provide technical assistance to targeted Great Lakes cities, while also maintaining the network of partner organizations.

title: Improving Stormwater Management in the Great Lakes
geographic_focus: Michigan, Pennsylvania, Indiana, Illinois, Ohio, Minnesota, New York, Wisconsin
description: The University of Wisconsin-Madison’s Center on Wisconsin Strategy conducts research and helps implement integrated solutions for improving environmental sustainability across all sectors. The center provides technical assistance, conducts public outreach, and hosts policy learning networks for state and local government executives. With this grant, the center will research and pilot a program to help state transportation agencies and city managers coordinate stormwater management decisions to reduce costs and offer increased environmental and social benefits.

title: Community Foundations and Family Philanthropy
description: The goal of the Community Foundations and Family Philanthropy program is to enhance the effectiveness of families working with community foundations as their giving partners. With input from a community foundation advisory group, the National Center for Family Philanthropy will: 1) develop new programming and resources for families working with community foundations; 2) develop new programming and resources for community foundation staff and board members; 3) improve the center’s capacity, through technology and direct outreach, to engage giving families and staff at community foundations; and 4) build a network of subscribers to its online resources, FP Online, among the community foundation field. The National Center for Family Philanthropy, located in Washington, D.C., is the only national resource center that focuses solely on matters of importance to families engaged in philanthropy and their effective giving.

title: Leaders for Tomorrow
description: The project goal is to strengthen nonprofit leadership and increase the level of resources available to nonprofits in Central and Eastern Europe. To this end, the Slovak Fundraising Center will develop and deliver a yearlong leadership development program with a specific focus on local fundraising. During the grant period, the grantee will deliver three cycles of the program to at least 50 nonprofit leaders. In addition, the grantee will support the development of a network for regular exchange and collaboration among program alumni. Also, the grantee will fine-tune the business model of the program to ensure its long-term sustainability. During the past grant period, the grantee’s key project achievements included establishing a diverse and experienced international project team, developing a tailor-made leadership development program for civic leaders in Central and Eastern Europe, and training and mentoring successfully 50 project participants. The grantee is based in Trnava, Slovakia.

title: Leaders for Tomorrow
description: The project goal is to strengthen nonprofit leadership and increase the level of resources available to nonprofits in the Central and Eastern Europe and Russia region. To this end, the Slovak Fundraising Center will create a team of prominent trainers and resource people to design a yearlong leadership development program with a specific focus on local fundraising. During the grant period, the grantee will deliver three cycles of the program to at least 40 nonprofit leaders. In addition, the grantee will fine-tune the business model of the program to ensure its long-term sustainability. The Slovak Fundraising Center was established in 2009 with the mission to increase the effectiveness of local fundraising and strengthen professional capacities of fundraisers in Slovakia and internationally. The grantee provides information, training, and technical assistance to fundraisers in Slovakia and in the region. Also, together with its sister organization, the Czech Fundraising Center, the grantee is organizing an annual fundraising conference, which in 2014 attracted more than 140 participants from 11 countries in the region. The grantee is based in Trnava, Slovakia.

title: Delaware Statewide Afterschool Partnership
description: This grant to the University of Delaware will support partnership development among afterschool stakeholders in Delaware and will enable the establishment of a cohesive statewide afterschool network. The grantee will bring together a diverse group of key decisionmakers and supporters around issues impacting afterschool and summer learning programs. Specific project activities will include holding a partner convening on afterschool, organizing a steering committee, and developing a plan to increase quality afterschool opportunities in the state.

title: Delaware Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the United Way of Delaware to coordinate the Delaware Statewide Afterschool Network. Over the next three years, the network will build a statewide coalition in support of afterschool programs and coordinate a unified vision to inform policy and quality afterschool initiatives. The network’s initiatives and priorities will: 1) create a strategic communications plan to build awareness of afterschool programs; 2) develop a website with a multimodel clearinghouse of best practices, professional development, and resources for afterschool providers; and 3) revise the quality standards for afterschool programs in Delaware.

title: Delaware Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the United Way of Delaware, which coordinates the Delaware Statewide Afterschool Network to continue development of policy, partnerships, and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) build champions by hosting quarterly roundtable discussions; 2) develop and pilot a Youth Program Quality Assessment instrument tool and training;3) connect and integrate college and career ready models into afterschool and summer learning spaces for students; and 4) support the development and distribution of the new afterschool program content in collaboration with the Foundation’s thematic partners.

title: Delaware Statewide Afterschool Partnership
description: This grant to the University of Delaware will support partnership development among afterschool stakeholders in Delaware and enable the establishment of a cohesive statewide afterschool network. The grantee will bring together a diverse group of key decisionmakers and supporters around issues impacting afterschool and summer learning programs. Through this Delaware Statewide Afterschool Partnership grant, the grantee will hold a partner convening on afterschool and organize a steering committee to develop a plan to expand afterschool opportunities in the state.

title: Developing Community Schools in Romania
description: The project goal is to develop the community schools field in Romania as a tool for creating effective partnerships between communities and schools. To this end, the New Horizons Foundation will strengthen the capacity of the existing community schools, establish new community schools, increase its own capacity to support the community school field, and fundraise for the continuation and expansion of the project. During the last grant period, the grantee established 30 community schools and engaged over 20,000 students, teachers, and community members in various activities.

title: Developing Community Schools in Romania
description: The project goal is to introduce and develop the concept of community schools in Romania as a tool for creating effective partnerships between communities and schools. The New Horizons Foundation will create a project team of experienced community workers and educators, which will cooperate with the International Centre of Excellence for Community Schools to increase the team’s knowledge and understanding of the community school concept and practice around Central and Eastern Europe. In addition, the grantee will introduce the concept in 30 schools and strengthen the schools’ capacities to operate as community schools. The grantee will also document the experiences of the pilot phase and strategize for the expansion of the community school project in Romania in the future. The grantee was established in 1999 with the mission to promote and develop adventure education and service learning pedagogy for young people in Romania. Today, the grantee runs programs for young people in cooperation with teaching staff in more than 140 schools in 22 of the 41 counties in Romania.

title: Unlocking BNDES Operation Lifecycle
description: Founded in 2008, SITAWI Finance for Good is a Brazil-based nonprofit organization whose mission is to mobilize capital for positive environmental and social outcomes. For the past year, the grantee has been working in collaboration with Bank Information Center on assessing how financial institutions may upgrade their environmental and social safeguards, while coaching civil society organizations on how to better target their advocacy efforts. Under this grant, the grantee will support strategic investigation, analysis, and documentation about the Brazilian Development Bank’s evolving safeguards policies and instruments and explore how other infrastructure investors may enhance their own safeguards.

title: Unlocking BNDES Operation Lifecycle
description: Founded in 2008, SITAWI Finance for Good is a Brazil-based nonprofit organization whose mission is to mobilize research and capital for positive environmental and social outcomes. Over the past project period, the grantee analyzed the new social and environmental policy and restructuring of the Brazilian Development Bank. This project renewal will support a strategic investigation, analysis, and documentation of the Brazilian Development Bank’s policies and investments, as well as develop metrics to judge overall progress.

title: Unlocking BNDES Operation Lifecycle
description: This grant will support Sitawi Finance for Good to conduct research and documentation of the Brazilian Development Bank’s internal procedures of due diligence, structure, and decisionmaking processes. This research will be used to develop training for nongovernmental organizations to improve civil society’s effectiveness in working toward strengthening the bank’s governance and social and environmental safeguards policies.

title: Harrison Street Bike Lane
description: This grant to the City of Flint will support the transformation of Harrison Street in downtown Flint into a complete street that supports multiple modes of transportation. A new roadway design will reduce the number of lanes dedicated to vehicular traffic and create a two-way bicycle lane that is protected by pedestrian improvements, attractive landscape elements, and on-street parking. In addition to improving the function and aesthetics of the street and enhancing the vibrancy of the new Health and Wellness District, the design is intended to slow vehicular traffic and enhance pedestrian safety, especially in the high pedestrian traffic areas near the University of Michigan-Flint. The project will also help connect downtown Flint with existing and planned segments of Flint’s growing bicycle trail system.

title: Mainstreaming Green Credit Policy in Chinese Policy Banks
description: China has become a new leader in the world of international development finance to poor developing countries in Africa, other parts of Asia, and Latin America. To monitor and engage the Chinese government on its international development finance, it is important to develop the capacity of Chinese nongovernmental organizations to address these issues. The Chinese environmental organization, Green Watershed, is leading an effort to monitor new Chinese rules requiring environmental and social protections for its lending to developing countries — known as green credit policies. This grant will support the development and expansion of the grantee’s work on Chinese green credit policies and enhance its staff capacity to monitor this finance.

title: Exploring Best Practice Models and Pathways for International Clean Energy Finance
description: The Vasudha Foundation was established in 2014 to undertake research and advocacy related to international financial institution investments in the energy sector. It focuses on developing alternative models for renewable energy financing that can provide new pathways for international investments. Under this grant, it will continue to monitor the World Bank Group, the African Development Bank, and other international financial institutions’ lending for energy infrastructure to developing countries. In particular, the grantee will influence collaboration between Africa and India related to renewable energy investments and off-grid energy access solutions for Africa.

title: Exploring Best Practice Models and Pathways for International Clean Energy Finance
description: The Vasudha Foundation undertakes research and analysis that will be used to inform and shift international financial institution investments in the energy sector. The grantee focuses on developing alternative models for renewable energy financing that can provide new pathways for international investments. Under this grant, it will continue to monitor the African Development Bank and the World Bank Group’s financing for energy infrastructure to developing countries. In particular, the grantee will focus on building collaboration between African countries and India, related to renewable energy investments and off-grid energy access solutions for Africa.

title: Exploring Best Practice Models and Pathways for International Clean Energy Finance
description: Vasudha Foundation was established in 2014 to undertake research and advocacy related to international financial institution investments in the energy and energy infrastructure sectors. It focuses on developing alternative models for clean energy financing that can provide new pathways for international investments. Over the next two years, the grantee will monitor the World Bank Group and other international financial institutions’ lending for energy infrastructure to developing countries.

title: Exploring the Intersection of the Afterschool and Community Schools Movements
description: This grant will enable FowlerHoffman to conduct a scan of the current landscape of the community schools movement to determine potential intersections between afterschool programs and community schools.

title: General Purposes
description: The northwestern portion of Michigan’s Lower Peninsula is one of the fastest growing regions in the Midwest. In response to this swift growth, diverse stakeholders came together to launch the Grand Vision for the six-county region. The Michigan Land Use Institute, headquartered in Traverse City, is one of the organizations that spearheaded the community planning process from the beginning. The next three years are a vital time for the institute to help the region achieve the results imagined by the Grand Vision. This will include work to: promote local food buying programs; improve transit services and other transportation options; and expand the use of energy efficiency practices and renewable energy technologies. The grantee will also undertake measures to strengthen its own organizational capacity during the grant period.

title: E-DemLab
description: Established in 2007, the Podolian Agency for Regional Development works to ensure the successful and sustainable development of its home region through supporting an informed and engaged citizenry. The grantee will work with a range of information and communications technology specialists to enhance the capacity of civil society actors to improve governance in Ukraine. The program goal is to broaden access to and use of e-democracy tools in Ukraine. The grantee will stage a series of events aimed at overcoming the digital gap for vulnerable target audiences and engaging their capacities for e-democracy development. They will also create new products and applications to facilitate e-democracy practice while actively promoting internet safety and security as a critical feature underpinning online governance. In 2016–2017, the grantee developed a number of mobile applications used by citizens to improve government responsiveness in the city and region of Vinnytsia. It also organized coworking events in five other cities to expand this practice.

title: E-DemLab
description: The program goal is to broaden access to and use of e-democracy tools in Ukraine. The Podolian Agency for Regional Development will work with a range of information and communications technology specialists to enhance the capacity of civil society actors to improve governance in Ukraine. The grantee will stage a series of research and learning events to improve the understanding of challenges and opportunities for embedding e-governance and e-democracy practices. Informal conferences and other practical activities will focus on developing specific tools to facilitate more effective citizen self-organizations and engagement with their governments. An e-democracy portal will act as a repository of developed knowledge as well as a forum for consultation and support.
