Established in 2007, the Podolian Agency for Regional Development works to ensure the successful and sustainable development of its home region through supporting an informed and engaged citizenry.

title: Internally Displaced Persons and Communities: Building Tolerance Through Dialogue
description: The program goal is to support the development of strong and inclusive communities in Ukraine that are addressing the needs of internally displaced persons. The Ukrainian Women’s Fund will refine and expand, from four to six regions, a model for supporting and integrating internally displaced persons at the community level. Building on successful interventions to develop strong peer-to-peer linkages within communities, additional focus will be given to working more directly with local authorities in target locations. In 2015-2017, the grantee conducted training workshops for almost 1,000 participants in four pilot regions of Ukraine. It also supported 21 local initiatives aimed at facilitating community cohesion and encouraging active participation rather than dependence among displaced persons. Founded in 2000, the Ukrainian Women’s Fund helps women’s civic organizations play an active role in the processes of democratization of society and contribute to equality, justice, and respect for human rights.

title: Internally Displaced Persons and Communities: Building Tolerance Through Dialogue
description: The program goal is to support the development of strong and inclusive communities in Ukraine that are addressing the needs of internally displaced persons. The Ukrainian Women’s Fund will develop a model for supporting internally displaced persons at the community level in Ukraine based on a set of tools, procedures, trainings, and other activities. The grantee will test and refine this model based on work in four pilot regions in Ukraine and then disseminate it throughout the country. This project will strengthen the role of civil society not only in meeting urgent needs but in developing strategies for longer-term issues such as reconciliation and participation of internally displaced persons in community life. Founded in 2000, the Ukrainian Women’s Fund primarily helps women’s civic organizations to play an active role in the processes of democratization of society and to contribute to equality, justice, and respect for human rights.

title: Civic Engagement in Rural Communities
description: Established in 2017, Ecoaction is a successor organization to the National Ecological Centre of Ukraine. It is a nonprofit organization that encourages individuals to take common action to protect the environment with a particular focus on supporting rural communities. The program goal is to promote civic engagement in decision making in rural communities and throughout Ukraine. To this end, the grantee will provide training, technical assistance, and local campaign support to at least eight new communities in different regions of Ukraine whose environments are being jeopardized by industrial farming, gas drilling, and illegal waste dumping. The grantee will also conduct fact-finding missions, offer internships, and provide networking opportunities for local activists from different regions in up to another 12 communities. In 2015–2017, the organization from which Ecoaction emerged worked with civic groups in 15 communities to address local environmental issues. It also brought together over 200 community activists at a national campaigning workshop.

title: Civic Engagement in Rural Communities
description: The program goal is to promote civic engagement in decisionmaking in rural communities and small towns throughout Ukraine. To this end, the National Ecological Centre of Ukraine will provide training, technical assistance, and local campaign support to at least six communities in different regions of Ukraine whose environments are being negatively affected by industrial farming, gas drilling, mining, illegal waste dumping, or highway construction. The grantee will conduct fact-finding missions, offer internships, create an online local campaign manual, and provide networking opportunities for local activists from different regions in up to another 12 communities. Founded in 1991, the National Ecological Centre of Ukraine is a nonprofit organization that encourages individuals to take common action to protect the environment. The grantee’s members are scientists, journalists, artists, students, and others who strive to save nature by maintaining and creating new protected areas and to decrease human impact on the environment through policy change.

title: Strengthening Evidence, Engagement and Impact on Energy Poverty
description: Practical Action is an international nongovernmental organization that uses technology to address poverty in developing countries. To focus attention on the importance of addressing modern clean energy sources for poor people, Practical Action launched the “Poor People’s Energy Outlook” in 2010. This grant will support the publication over the next two years, continuing to provide the global environment and development community with data and information on small-scale, off-grid, renewable energy as a clear and viable approach to providing energy for poor rural communities. In addition, the grantee will develop comprehensive communication tools to ensure the publication will inform decisionmakers.

title: Sustainable Energy Access
description: According to the most recent data from the World Bank Group and the International Energy Agency, over 1 billion people in the world still do not have access to modern electricity. To address this challenge, the International Energy Agency has called for a global energy revolution, which will require a substantial shift of investment toward renewables and energy efficiency. Through this grant, Catholic Agency for Overseas Development will continue its research and refinement of a community-and practitioner-led energy development model to design distributed renewable energy systems for poor rural communities in Kenya and Indonesia.

title: Sustainable Energy Access
description: The global energy system is currently responsible for nearly 60 percent of global greenhouse gas emissions. This system does not meet the energy needs of over one billion people around the world — 95 percent of whom live in Sub-Saharan Africa and Asia. To address this challenge, the International Energy Agency has called for a global energy revolution, which will require a substantial shift of investment toward renewables and energy efficiency. Through this grant, the Catholic Agency for Overseas Development, working with other organizations, will test and refine a community- and practitioner-led energy development model to design distributed renewable energy systems for poor rural communities. They will also work to ensure that this energy development model’s lessons impact energy policymaking as well as bilateral, multilateral, and private sector investments.

title: Financing Clean Energy Access
grantee: International Institute for Environment and Development
description: Public and private investment in renewable energy generation capacity is increasing throughout Africa. In Tanzania, there is a broadly favorable policy environment with significant support from international donors. Due to this, financing of off-grid power through mini-grids that provide energy for small businesses or increased agricultural production has become an important new focus for funders. Under this grant, the International Institute for Environment and Development will provide case study-based research that will highlight the importance of financing for off-grid energy as well as the need for locally appropriate energy services designed around users’ needs and small business opportunities.

title: Financing Clean Energy Access
grantee: International Institute for Environment and Development
description: Globally, the centralized electricity grid model that is powered by fossil fuels is currently responsible for about 60 percent of global greenhouse gas emissions. In addition, this model does not deliver energy services for the poor in developing countries. The International Institute for Environment and Development is an international development and environment policy research organization, founded in 1971. It has collaborated with other nongovernmental organizations over the past eight years to develop an energy delivery model to provide small-scale, off-grid renewable energy in rural communities in Africa and Central America. Over this grant period, it will undertake activities to influence thinking, policy, and practice on small-scale, off-grid renewable energy; promote community-led approaches; build a base of evidence to support these approaches; and convene and influence global and national policymakers.

title: Promoting Energy Access for Africa
description: Over the past five years, the international community has begun to focus on addressing the lack of access to electricity for poor communities in much of the developing world. President Obama’s Power Africa initiative takes important steps to address this issue. Friends of the Earth will apply its expertise in working with domestic development and finance agencies to ensure that small-scale, off-grid renewable energy models are at the core of this international effort. It will undertake a plan of work that simultaneously combines research, advocacy, and capacity building to improve U.S. government policies, financing, and programs in order to advance renewable energy access in Africa.

title: Supporting China-Africa Energy Access Cooperation
description: Over the past decade, the steady growth of many economies in Africa, averaging five percent annually, has generated optimism for the continent. However, this growth has not been distributed throughout the populations. Though rich in both fossil-based and renewable energy resources, Sub-Saharan Africa has suffered from electricity power supply shortages and poor quality of services. The World Wildlife Fund will work with its offices in China and East Africa to shift Chinese financing of energy projects to address these energy access challenges in East Africa, particularly through small-scale renewable energy projects.

title: Building the Latin American Platform for Sustainable Energy and Equity
description: This grant will support a network of renewable energy practitioners in Latin America to share best practices and develop technical viability plans for small-scale renewable energy access in isolated communities in South America. Network members will also finalize and submit joint proposals for development finance investment in small-scale, renewable energy systems. Established in 2000, Renove is a network of Brazilian and South American renewable energy organizations.

title: Building the Latin American Platform for Sustainable Energy and Equity
description: This project will support a network of renewable energy practitioners in Latin America to share best practices. Network members will jointly develop proposals for development finance investment in small-scale, renewable energy systems for isolated communities in South America. The network is managed by the Brazilian organization Renove and has 27 members working in seven countries.

title: Sharing Indian Social Entrepreneurs' Lessons for African Off Grid Energy
description: Energy is widely acknowledged as a key tool to enhance economic growth and a country’s development. The predominant model of electricity generation and distribution is centralized, dependent on fossil fuels, and the largest contributor to climate change. For Africa, this model only provides 45 percent of the continent with electricity. In rural areas, less than 30 percent of the population have access to electricity. For rural Tanzania, the numbers are even more stark with less than 17 percent of the Tanzanian rural population having access to lighting or energy for livelihoods. Given their 20 years of experience in providing electricity in India, this grant will support the Solar Energy Light Company Foundation in coordinating a management approach to technical and entrepreneurial skill development, mentoring of innovators, and innovative financing models to develop social entrepreneurs in Tanzania.

title: Sharing Indian Social Entrepreneurs' Lessons for African Off Grid Energy
description: Energy is widely acknowledged as a key tool to enhance economic growth and a country’s development. The predominant model of generation and distribution is centralized, dependent on fossil fuels, and the largest contributor to climate change. In addition, this model has failed to provide 17 percent of the world’s population with access to lighting or energy for livelihoods. To address this challenge in India, the Solar Energy Light Company Foundation has been providing electricity for 20 years. Given their years of experience, this grant will support the grantee in providing technical assistance and capacity building for social entrepreneurs from other developing countries.

title: Light for a Better Life
grantee: IDEAAS-Instituto para o Desenvolvimento de Energias Alternativas e da Auto Sustentabilidade
description: IDEAAS-Instituto para o Desenvolvimento de Energias Alternativas e da Auto Sustentabilidade is a nonprofit Brazilian organization that develops renewable energy solutions for remote and rural communities. This project will support the grantee’s efforts to scale up programs to bring solar energy systems to remote Amazon forest communities. Two pilot programs have been established in the Tefe municipality in the Brazilian state of Amazonas. The grantee develops and implements small-scale solar electricity systems for individual and community needs and will develop a finance model to replicate successes.

title: Light for a Better Life
grantee: IDEAAS-Instituto para o Desenvolvimento de Energias Alternativas e da Auto Sustentabilidade
description: This project will support the Instituto para o Desenvolvimento de Energias Alternativas e da Auto Sustentabilidade to evaluate and scale up programs to bring solar energy systems to remote Amazon forest communities. Two pilot programs have been established in the Tefe municipality in the Brazilian state of Amazonas. The grantee develops and implements small-scale solar electricity systems for individual and community needs and will develop a finance model to replicate successes. The target populations for these systems are isolated communities in two federal environmental conservation areas along the Solimões River in the Brazilian Amazon.

title: Energy Distributed to Isolated Communities
description: This project supports advocacy and promotion by Instituto Socioambiental of three new, renewable energy access models in the Rio Negro, the middle lands of the Xingu River, and the Xingu Indigenous Park along the headwaters of the Xingu River. This grant increase will allow the grantee to produce and disseminate a documentary and short films demonstrating these renewable energy access models in the Brazilian Amazon.

title: Energy Distributed to Isolated Communities
description: This grant renewal will support efforts by Instituto Socioambiental to promote distributed renewable energy access solutions for isolated Amazon communities in Brazil and overcome barriers to the expansion of clean energy in isolated communities. Instituto Socioambiental is a large Brazilian nongovernmental organization that works on sustainable development and conservation of the Amazon rainforest.

title: Energy Distributed to Isolated Communities
description: This grant renewal will support efforts by Instituto Socioambiental to promote distributed renewable energy access solutions for isolated Amazon communities in Brazil and overcome barriers to the expansion of clean energy in isolated communities. Over the past project period, the grantee organized the first renewable energy access fair and policy symposium, bringing together communities from the greater Amazon rainforest, the private sector, and government. This renewal will support the grantee to work with energy regulators and develop monitoring and management systems of renewable energy models in isolated Amazon communities.

title: Energy Distributed to Isolated Communities
description: The Instituto Socioambiental works to implement sustainable and renewable energy for local communities in three of Brazil’s poorest and most isolated regions in the Amazon Rainforest. This project proposes to support efforts to implement a set of decentralized renewable energy solutions in these regions coupled with a structured dialogue with public policymakers to overcome regulatory and financial barriers to providing clean energy to isolated communities.

title: Solar Andes/Amazon Energy Access
description: Fundacion EcoAndina is an Argentinian organization that works with upper Andean communities to implement solar energy, energy efficiency, and water conservation solutions. This grant will support the grantee to promote, provide training, and monitor solar villages located in remote, rural communities in the upper Andean plateau region of Argentina and Bolivia. The high plateau region is home to hundreds of rural communities with no access to modern energy services because grid extension is cost prohibitive and access to bottled gas is intermittent at best. The Solar Villages program will promote replication of its integrated solar energy model in villages in the region.

title: Clean Energy Access in Andes/Amazon
grantee: Centro de Estudios y Promocion del Desarrollo
description: The Centro de Estudios y Promocion del Desarrollo is a 49-year-old Peruvian nongovernmental development institution that is working with poor rural communities to introduce innovative renewable energy solutions to improve the health, education, quality of life, and environment in five regions in Peru. The focus of this project is to support the grantee’s efforts to document the findings and lessons learned in the different renewable energy projects in order to develop a series of recommendations for replicating successful Peruvian renewable energy access models.

title: Assessing Feasibility of Integrated Watershed Commissions
description: The Robert B. Annis Water Resources Institute, part of Grand Valley State University, is located in Muskegon, Michigan. The institute seeks to integrate research, education, and outreach in support of enhancing and preserving freshwater resources. With Mott support, the institute will examine the feasibility of more effectively integrating water management decisionmaking in the state of Michigan. With the help of a multidisciplinary advisory group, the institute will develop a white paper that outlines opportunities for increasing the coordination of water management decisions across various municipal, county, and state jurisdictions in a way that also includes other freshwater stakeholders, including farmers, businesses, and environmental groups.

title: Protecting Water Quality From Hazardous Oil Spills
geographic_focus: Pennsylvania, Indiana, New York, Wisconsin, Ontario, Michigan, Minnesota, Ohio
description: In recent years, there have been significant increases in the transport of crude oil via pipeline, rail, and maritime vessels across the Great Lakes region. The Great Lakes Commission is an interstate agency tasked with helping its member states understand, and plan for, this type of new environmental risk to the region. With Mott support, the grantee will examine the freshwater risks of crude oil transport in the Great Lakes and begin to identify opportunities for addressing these challenges. The grantee’s research will be overseen by an advisory committee composed of representatives from government, tribes, industry, and environmental nonprofits.

title: Great Lakes Water Infrastructure Project
description: The Center for Neighborhood Technology is a nonprofit organization based in Chicago that designs and implements sustainable development strategies that help cities offer a high quality of life for residents. With prior Mott support, the grantee conducted a pilot program to help two Great Lakes communities adopt practices to address flooding and stormwater pollution, with special attention to protecting homes and businesses in vulnerable urban areas. With renewed support, the grantee will expand its programs to address broader water infrastructure challenges, such as providing safe and affordable drinking water to low-income families. The grantee will begin to develop replicable strategies that can bring multiple benefits to the Great Lakes region, such as protecting public health and reducing polluted stormwater runoff.

title: Great Lakes Water Infrastructure Project
geographic_focus: Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Ohio, Indiana, Michigan, New York, Illinois
description: The Center for Neighborhood Technology works with cities to provide research, tools, and solutions to advance sustainable and equitable communities. Based in Chicago, the organization has focused much of its work on water resource challenges in the Great Lakes region. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has provided workshops and technical assistance on water infrastructure challenges for Great Lakes cities, including Dearborn, Flint, and Gary. The Center has reached out nationally to share findings and seek additional solutions to advance policies and programs to enhance affordability and environmental sustainability. With additional support, the Center will convene and provide customized technical support for five Great Lakes cities and disseminate innovation strategy guides as resources for other Great Lakes cities.

title: RainReady Program
geographic_focus: New York, Pennsylvania, Ohio, Illinois, Minnesota, Indiana, Wisconsin, Michigan
description: Many Great Lakes’ cities have aging stormwater infrastructure which is unable to keep up with more frequent and intense rains. As a result, stormwater runoff washes toxic materials and sediments into local waterways and can also flood homes and businesses. The Center for Neighborhood Technology, a nonprofit organization based in Chicago, Illinois, designs and implements strategies that support livable and sustainable urban communities. With Mott support, the grantee will conduct a pilot program to help selected Great Lakes’ communities adopt practices to prevent and minimize flooding and water pollution. Based on the results, the grantee will refine and expand its RainReady program, develop a replicable model, and share information with other Great Lakes’ communities.

title: Sustainable Energy Use in Northern Michigan
description: The Groundwork Center for Resilient Communities (formerly the Michigan Land Use Institute), headquartered in Traverse City, is working to make northwest Michigan a model of ecological and economic sustainability, particularly with respect to energy use and generation. This renewal grant will allow the grantee to deepen and focus its efforts to expand solar deployment through residential and commercial installations, particularly via its new Groundwork Shines program, and encourage participation in energy efficiency programs in the Traverse City area. The grantee will also continue to share best practices and lessons learned through a variety of means including original journalism and networking activities.

title: Sustainable Energy Use in Northern Michigan
description: The Michigan Land Use Institute is working to make northwest Michigan a model of ecological and economic sustainability, particularly with respect to energy use and generation. With Mott support over the next two years, the grantee will focus its efforts to expand solar deployment and increase participation in energy efficiency programs in the Traverse City area. The grantee will also share best practices and lessons learned through a variety of means including original journalism and networking activities.

title: Michigan Green Communities Network
description: Local government officials and other local leaders across Michigan want to pursue clean energy initiatives for fiscal savings and other social and environmental benefits. They face a variety of challenges, however, in adopting such practices and policies, so there is a need for technical assistance, peer exchange, and implementation tools. Connecting local leaders and supporting their work through training, education, and communications is the focus of the Michigan Green Communities Network, a project of the Michigan Municipal League Foundation. This renewal grant will allow the network to continue to promote the adoption of clean energy and expand network member participation and geographic diversity. The grantee will raise the profile of the program through increased outreach and web-based tools to track community progress.

title: Michigan Green Communities Network
description: Local government officials and other local leaders across Michigan are implementing clean energy projects and programs that save money and offer social and environmental benefits. The Michigan Green Communities Network, a project of the Michigan Municipal League Foundation, seeks to connect such local leaders and support their work through training, education, and communications. With partial support from Mott, the network will continue to promote the adoption of clean energy and expand network member participation.

title: Clean Energy Solutions for Michigan Schools
description: Established in 1970, the Ecology Center works locally, statewide, and nationally on a range of issues including clean energy, toxic-free materials, and sustainable food systems. With prior Mott support, the grantee worked with K-12 schools across Michigan to reduce energy use and adopt renewable energy systems by building and expanding a network of schools and launching a pilot technical assistance program. With renewed support, the grantee will expand its technical assistance; increase outreach by distributing materials, sharing case studies, and engaging additional school stakeholders; and develop a strategy to evolve the program into a self-sustaining social enterprise.

title: Clean Energy Solutions for Michigan Schools
description: Established in 1970, the Ecology Center works locally, statewide and nationally on a range of issues including clean energy, toxic-free materials, and sustainable food systems. With this grant, the grantee will work with K-12 schools across Michigan to reduce energy use, adopt renewable energy systems, and integrate energy issues into related curriculum. The grantee will do so by strengthening and expanding an existing network of 67 schools, developing pilot projects in up to four schools, and exploring ways to advance the work into a self-sustaining, social enterprise.

title: Neighborhood Policing
description: This grant to the City of Flint will support public safety activities in local neighborhoods, as well as coordination between justice system departments. Flint continues to experience higher-than-average crime rates while contending with constrained financial resources for sworn officers in the Flint Police Department. Through this grant, a coordinator will support enhanced communication between trained public safety volunteers and police officers to bolster neighborhood safety strategies.

title: FABLAB for the Community
description: This grant will provide support to Mott Community College for the FABLAB for the Community, a workspace designed to support creativity and innovation, as well as provide access to sophisticated equipment at a reasonable cost to entrepreneurs and small business owners. Users are able to utilize the facility and transform their business ideas into marketable products. The goal of the project is to expand the capacity of the FABLAB to serve more residents and businesses in the Flint community and across the region.

title: FABLAB for the Community
description: This grant will provide support to Mott Community College for the FABLAB for the Community. The project is designed to provide entrepreneurs and small businesses access to sophisticated equipment at affordable rates. The lab is a space where users can transform a business idea into a marketable product and is a place for prototyping and small production runs. FABLAB for the Community plans to serve more residents and businesses in Flint and throughout the region during the grant period.

title: FABLAB for the Community
description: This grant will provide support to Mott Community College for the FABLAB for the Community, a workspace designed to support creativity and innovation, and provide access to sophisticated equipment at a reasonable cost to entrepreneurs and small business owners. Users are able to utilize the facility and transform their business ideas into marketable products. The goal of the project is to expand the capacity of the FABLAB for the Community to serve more residents and businesses in the Flint community and across the region.

title: Glenwood Cemetery Maintenance and Planning
description: The Board of Trustees of Glenwood Cemetery has entered into an agreement with the Historic Elmwood Foundation to restore and preserve Glenwood Cemetery as an active, historic cemetery serving the local community. This grant will support a master site plan and tree removal services for Glenwood Cemetery in Flint.

title: Glenwood Cemetery Maintenance and Planning
description: The Board of Trustees of Glenwood Cemetery has entered into an agreement with the Historic Elmwood Foundation to restore and preserve Glenwood Cemetery as an active, historic cemetery serving the local community. This grant increase will support continued grounds maintenance, debris removal, hydroseeding, and tree planting in accordance with the Arboretum Master Planting Plan.

title: Glenwood Cemetery
description: The Board of Trustees of Glenwood Cemetery has entered into an agreement with the Historic Elmwood Foundation to restore and preserve Glenwood Cemetery as an active, historic cemetery serving the local community. This grant will support a master site plan and tree removal services for Glenwood Cemetery in Flint.

title: John Mroz Executive Fund
description: The John Mroz Executive Fund was created to ensure that the EastWest Institute will be led by a highly qualified individual. Contributions to the fund will be used for recruiting, retaining, and supporting EastWest Institute’s new chief executive officer and president in the tradition of former President and Chief Executive Officer John Mroz. The EastWest Institute seeks to make the world a safer place by addressing the seemingly intractable problems that threaten regional and global stability. Founded in 1980, the EastWest Institute is an international, nonpartisan organization with offices in New York, Brussels, Moscow, and Washington.

title: Mississippi Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Operation Shoestring to coordinate a statewide afterschool network in Mississippi. Over the next three years, the Mississippi Statewide Afterschool Network will build a statewide network in support of afterschool programs and coordinate a unified vision to inform policy and quality afterschool initiatives. During this grant, the network’s initiatives will include: 1) identify and map the out-of-school time programs in Mississippi; 2) establish a representative and durable structure and governance for the network; and 3) develop quality standards to advance out-of-school time programs in Mississippi.

title: Mississippi Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Operation Shoestring, which coordinates the Mississippi Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships, and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) work with key state partners to develop a sustainability strategy for afterschool programs; 2) develop an afterschool Quality Rating Improvement System for the state; and 3) support the development and distribution of the new afterschool program content in collaboration with the Foundation’s thematic partners.

title: Mississippi Statewide Afterschool Partnership
grantee: United Way of the Capital Area
description: This grant will support partnership development among afterschool stakeholders in Mississippi and will enable the establishment of a cohesive statewide afterschool network. The United Way of the Capital Area will bring together a diverse group of key decisionmakers and supporters around issues impacting afterschool and summer learning programs. With this Mississippi Statewide Afterschool Partnership grant, the grantee will hold a partner convening on afterschool and organize a steering committee to develop a plan to expand afterschool opportunities in the state.

title: North Dakota Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the South East Education Cooperative to coordinate the North Dakota Statewide Afterschool Network. Over the next three years, the network will build a statewide coalition in support of afterschool programs and coordinate a unified vision to inform policy and quality afterschool initiatives. The network’s initiatives and priorities will: 1) develop and broaden partnerships to create a shared vision in support of youth; 2) establish a representative and durable structure of partnerships in support of the network; and 3) identify strategies to advance out-of-school time programs in North Dakota.

title: North Dakota Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the South East Education Cooperative, which coordinates the North Dakota Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships, and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) develop a State of Afterschool in North Dakota publication to educate people on afterschool and highlight the successes and gaps; 2) create new quality professional development opportunities to afterschool programs across the state; 3) develop a quality system for afterschool programs in North Dakota; and 4) support the development and distribution of the new afterschool program content in collaboration with the Foundation’s thematic partners.

title: North Dakota Statewide Afterschool Partnership
description: This grant will support partnership development among afterschool stakeholders in North Dakota and will enable the establishment of a cohesive statewide afterschool network. The South East Education Cooperative will bring together a diverse group of key decisionmakers and supporters around issues impacting afterschool and summer learning programs. With this North Dakota Statewide Afterschool Partnership grant, the grantee will hold a partner convening on afterschool and organize a leadership team to develop a plan to expand afterschool opportunities in the state.

title: Summit on Afterschool
description: The Schwarzenegger Institute, housed at the University of Southern California, will convene a Summit on Afterschool to raise awareness of the importance of afterschool programs. The summit will include leaders from the education, afterschool, government, business, and nonprofit sectors from states across the country.

title: Symposium on Afterschool
description: The Schwarzenegger Institute, housed at the University of Southern California, will convene a Symposium on Afterschool to raise awareness of the importance of afterschool programs. The symposium will include leaders from the education, afterschool, government, business, and nonprofit sectors from states across the country.

title: Afterschool and Community Schools Initiative
description: This project will support the Children’s Aid Society National Center for Community Schools to advance afterschool programs as part of a community school strategy. Specifically, this grant will support the center to: 1) develop resources and materials to help conceptualize and fortify the connections between afterschool and community schools; 2) support the center in providing technical assistance to grantees of the Full-Service Community School grant program, including the establishment of afterschool programs; and 3) provide support to the statewide afterschool networks on community schools.

title: Afterschool and Community Schools Initiative
description: This project will support the Children’s Aid Society National Center for Community Schools to advance afterschool programs as part of a community school strategy. Specifically, this grant will support the center to: 1) develop tools for community schools’ directors to provide better support and information on creating community schools, including how to establish quality afterschool programs; 2) develop and implement a Community School Directors Institute; 3) support the center in providing technical assistance to grantees of the Full-Service Community School grant program, including the establishment of afterschool programs; and 4) provide support to the statewide afterschool networks on community schools.

title: Afterschool Evaluation and Dissemination Project
description: This grant to Harvard University will support the afterschool field and its key stakeholders in developing a comprehensive plan to improve the accessibility of afterschool evaluation information, and to identify areas for further evaluation. This project will include: 1) developing a policy brief on existing afterschool evaluation and outcome data; 2) conducting key informant interviews to identify innovative evaluation practices; and 3) conducting an interactive process with afterschool and education leaders to develop recommendations for future afterschool evaluation and research projects.

title: Afterschool Data Project
description: This grant will support the Data Quality Campaign to work with statewide afterschool networks to help inform and include afterschool data as part of new state data education systems. Specifically, this grant will support the grantee in: 1) working with the statewide afterschool networks to identify afterschool program data to include in the state data systems; and 2) providing the afterschool field with a set of recommendations to improve afterschool participation in local, state, and federal education data systems.

title: Art School Endowment II
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to the Flint Institute of Arts will help build the endowment fund for its art school. This endowment will provide operating support for the art school, one of the largest museum art schools in the nation. The art school has an annual enrollment of about 1,500 students and offers studio instruction in drawing, painting, photography, mixed media, printmaking, ceramics, glass mosaic, fiber, and metal sculpture, with scholarships available to those needing financial assistance. The school serves another 4,000 children and adults each year through summer camps for youth, free family activities, and a pre-college portfolio development program for high school students interested in pursuing a college education in the arts.

title: Paul Torre Scholarship Fund
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will establish the Paul Torre Scholarship Fund endowment at the Flint Institute of Music. Paul Torre has been a part of the Flint Institute of Music for over three decades, serving as the president and chief executive officer for the past 20 years. In honor of a leader who has devoted his career to helping youth experience the performing arts and giving everyone the opportunity to participate, the Paul Torre Scholarship Fund will provide financial aid to allow students to take advantage of the vocal, instrumental, dance, and theater programs offered at the Flint School of Performing Arts and Flint Youth Theatre.

title: Atwood Stadium Improvements
description: The purpose of this grant is to provide support to Kettering University for renovations and improvements to Atwood Stadium. One of Kettering University’s objectives is to contribute to the economic revitalization of Flint, including the University Avenue corridor which connects the university to other key anchor institutions in the area and is home to Atwood Stadium. Installing updated field turf and improving the infrastructure of the stadium are intended to increase the level and diversity of stadium users, helping to bring additional activity, traffic, and revenue generation to the corridor.

title: Mt. Elliott Makerspace
description: This grant will support program and transition planning activities at the Mt. Elliott Makerspace. Located in the basement of the Church of the Messiah, the Mt. Elliott Makerspace is a neighborhood workshop where people of all ages create (make) and learn together. Its goal is to grow a network of visionary makers with the skills and determination to create happier and more meaningful lives. During the project’s open hours, residents of the Mt. Elliott community can engage in designed learning experiences as well as open explorations in a range of areas: transportation, electricity and energy, communications, wearables, design and fabrication, food and wellness, and music and arts. Through self-directed learning and exchanges across these disciplines, the Mt. Elliott Makerspace helps community members discover their passions, exercise their creativity, develop knowledge and hands-on skills, and build relationships with fellow community members. Church of the Messiah is located on Detroit’s lower east side and is part of the Episcopal Diocese of Michigan.

title: Documentary Film: The Good Ones
description: The Institute for Educational Leadership’s mission is to improve education and the lives of children and their families. The grantee brings together diverse constituencies and empowers leaders with knowledge and applicable ideas. The Good Ones is a 30-minute documentary that shares the stories of what works in education in South Africa, schools that shift the paradigm, and expectations of what happens in poor communities. Past support enabled the filming of The Good Ones, which consists of stories of three South African schools. Each of these schools has its own story, but all have the same goal — to use the power of education to change people’s lives. These schools are succeeding even though they work in harsh and hostile conditions in some of the poorest parts of South Africa. The Good Ones will explain why these schools are succeeding and will illuminate factors that make them effective. This grant increase will enable the completion of the film and will support outreach and distribution.

title: Documentary Film: The Good Ones
description: The Institute for Educational Leadership’s mission is to improve education and the lives of children and their families. The grantee brings together diverse constituencies and empowers leaders with knowledge and applicable ideas. “The Good Ones” is a 30-minute documentary that shares the stories of what works in education in South Africa — schools that shift the paradigm and expectations of what happens in poor communities. Over the next six months, “The Good Ones” will film the stories of three South African schools. Each of these schools has its own story, but all have the same goal — to use the power of education to change people’s lives. These schools are succeeding even though they work in harsh and hostile conditions in some of the poorest parts of South Africa. “The Good Ones” will explain why these schools are succeeding and will illuminate factors that make them effective.

title: Flint National Service Accelerator Initiative
description: This grant increase to the United Way of Genesee County will fund the Flint National Service Accelerator Initiative which began in 2011. Originally housed at the Boys and Girls Club of Greater Flint, the initiative has leveraged more than $3 million in local and federal dollars to increase the number of national service members providing direct service and capacity building personnel to Flint area organizations. The Flint National Service Accelerator Initiative assists area groups with application preparation for national service programs, program implementation and reporting, and professional development for members. This grant provides funds for a civic engagement manager to carry out this work. The increase will provide additional member support including training, unanticipated costs for Operation AmeriCorps, resources for new national service projects, and evaluation work.

title: Flint National Service Accelerator Initiative
description: This renewal to the United Way of Genesee County will support the Flint National Service Accelerator Initiative which began as a pilot project at the Boys & Girls Club of Greater Flint. The program is now embedded as part of the United Way continuum of volunteer and service opportunities. The initiative has leveraged more than $3 million in local, state, and federal resources to increase the number of national service members providing direct service and capacity building personnel to Flint area organizations. This grant provides funds for a civic engagement manager to implement the program which includes capacity building for local organizations seeking national service members, advising the Flint National Service Accelerator Fund housed at the Community Foundation of Greater Flint, and providing recruitment, training, and supervisory support to members and host sites.

title: Flint National Service Accelerator Initiative
description: This renewal grant to the United Way of Genesee County will support the Flint National Service Accelerator Initiative, which is part of a continuum of volunteer and service opportunities for the community. The initiative has leveraged over $4 million in local, state, and federal resources to increase the number of national service members providing direct service and capacity building personnel to Flint area organizations. This grant provides funds for a civic engagement manager to implement the program which includes capacity building for local organizations seeking national service members; advising the Flint National Service Accelerator Fund housed at the Community Foundation of Greater Flint; and providing recruitment, training, and support to members and host sites.

title: Flint National Service Accelerator Initiative
description: This renewal grant to the United Way of Genesee County will support the Flint National Service Accelerator Initiative, which is part of a continuum of volunteer and national service opportunities for the community. The initiative has leveraged over $4 million in local, state, and federal resources to increase the number of national service members providing direct service and capacity building personnel to Flint area organizations. This grant provides funds for a civic engagement manager to implement the program which includes capacity building for local organizations seeking national service members; advising the Flint National Service Accelerator Fund housed at the Community Foundation of Greater Flint; and providing recruitment, training, and support to members and host sites.

title: Flint National Service Accelerator Initiative
description: This renewal grant to the United Way of Genesee County will support the Flint National Service Accelerator Initiative, which is part of a continuum of volunteer and national service opportunities for the community. The initiative has leveraged over $4 million in local, state, and federal resources to increase the number of national service members providing direct service and capacity-building personnel to Flint area organizations. This grant provides funds for a civic engagement manager to implement the program which includes capacity building for local organizations seeking national service members; advising the Flint National Service Accelerator Fund housed at the Community Foundation of Greater Flint; and providing recruitment, training, and support to members and host sites.

title: Flint National Service Accelerator Initiative
description: This grant to the United Way of Genesee County will support the Flint National Service Accelerator Initiative which began in 2011. Originally housed at the Boys and Girls Club of Greater Flint, the initiative has leveraged more than $1.5 million in local and federal dollars to increase the number of national service members providing direct service and capacity building personnel to Flint area organizations. The initiative also assists area groups with application preparation for national service programs, program implementation and reporting, and professional development for members. Grant funds support a civic engagement manager to carry out this work.

title: Community Education Planning and Professional Development
description: The Foundation for Community Education is a national organization committed to the implementation of principles of the community education philosophy. The grantee will develop a program designed to expand the skills of professionals who are providing leadership in community education and community schools.

title: Hurley Children's Hospital Pediatric Center
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant increase to the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation will enable Hurley Children’s Hospital’s Pediatric Center to relocate to premises within the new Flint Farmers’ Market building in the downtown Flint Health and Wellness District. This move will allow the center to continue its mission of providing state-of-the-art medical services to low-income children. Greater proximity to downtown bus transit options will make critical medical services more accessible to Flint’s families and will facilitate the center’s partnership with Michigan State University’s College of Human Medicine’s pediatric residency program.

title: Hurley Children's Hospital Pediatric Center
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant to the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation will enable Hurley Children’s Hospital’s Pediatric Medical Center to relocate to the new Flint Farmers’ Market building in the downtown Flint Health and Wellness District. This move will allow the center to continue its mission of providing state-of-the-art medical services to low-income children. Greater proximity to downtown bus transit options will make critical medical services more accessible to Flint’s families, and will facilitate the center’s partnership with Michigan State University’s College of Human Medicine’s pediatric residency program.

title: Comprehensive Emergency Assistance Program
description: Shelter of Flint, Inc., provides services for approximately 1,300 homeless people per year. The vast majority of these clients are families who are economically challenged. The principal goal of the agency is to assist the homeless in achieving stability through a continuum of care model ranging from crisis prevention and counseling to elimination of the root causes of homelessness. This grant will help to support the grantee’s Comprehensive Emergency Assistance Program, which focuses on clients housed in the emergency shelter. Individuals and families will receive food and shelter assistance, as well as comprehensive case management services and the development of long-range plans toward permanent stability.

title: One Stop Housing Resource Center
description: Shelter of Flint, Inc., provides services for approximately 1,300 homeless individuals per year. The vast majority of these clients are families who are economically challenged. The principal goal of the agency is to assist the homeless in achieving stability through a continuum of care model ranging from crisis prevention and counseling to elimination of the root causes of homelessness. This grant will help support the grantee’s One Stop Housing Resource Center, which provides comprehensive housing placement services and basic needs referrals and services for people who are homeless.

title: Comprehensive Emergency Assistance Program
description: Shelter of Flint, Inc., provides services for approximately 1,300 homeless people per year. The vast majority of these clients are families who are economically challenged. The principal goal of the agency is to assist the homeless in achieving stability through a continuum of care model ranging from crisis prevention and counseling to elimination of the root causes of homelessness. This grant will help to support the grantee’s Comprehensive Emergency Assistance Program, which focuses on clients housed in the emergency shelter. Individuals and families will receive food and shelter assistance, as well as comprehensive case management services and the development of long-range plans toward permanent stability.

title: Joint Advocacy/Policy Institute
description: The Joint Advocacy/Policy Institute is a collaborative project of the Forum of Regional Associations of Grantmakers and the National Council of Nonprofits, two major United States networks of philanthropic and nonprofit associations. The project aims to enhance state-level collaboration between regional grantmaker associations and state nonprofit associations by creating mechanisms through which association leaders can interact more closely. This will be accomplished through two core strategies. The first strategy — raising awareness about the value of policy collaboration among the associations’ staff and board members — will involve a variety of joint activities over 2015 and part of 2016, including focused messaging about the importance and impact of policy work, conducting joint Webinars, producing case studies of existing collaborations, and seizing opportunities to work together when ad hoc policy threats arise. The second strategy involves planning and conducting a three-day Joint Advocacy/Policy Institute in the summer of 2016.

title: Great Lakes Program
grantee: Citizens Campaign Fund for the Environment
description: Founded in 1985, Citizens Campaign Fund for the Environment is a New York-based environmental nonprofit. The grantee has staff based in the City of Buffalo who focus on improving Great Lakes protection and restoration efforts. With prior Mott support, the grantee helped update New York’s Great Lakes Action Agenda (a state plan to address Great Lakes priorities); educated decisionmakers and the general public on Great Lakes issues; engaged in regional freshwater policy discussions; and expanded its outreach efforts. With this renewal, the grantee will continue this work and also help implement a water management plan for Lake Ontario and the St. Lawrence River; convene local and state stakeholders to improve municipal water infrastructure systems; and strengthen its organizational communications capacity.

title: Protecting Drinking Water and Restoring the Great Lakes
grantee: Citizens Campaign Fund for the Environment
description: Citizens Campaign Fund for the Environment is one of New York State’s most respected advocates for protection of citizens’ health and the environment. They are adept at effectively organizing and mobilizing coalitions of citizens and groups to educate decision-makers and the general public on Great Lakes issues. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee educated state leaders on the need for water infrastructure upgrades, and helped develop and implement a new plan to manage water levels on Lake Ontario. The grantee has led efforts to address emerging contaminants in water, including plastic pollution and pharmaceuticals. With this renewal grant, the grantee will reconvene a Drinking Water Coalition, continue to educate on the need for water infrastructure upgrades, and address emerging threats such as plastic and pharmaceutical pollution. The grantee will also use this support from the Foundation to expand its capacity to connect with and educate citizens and coalitions.

title: Great Lakes Program
grantee: Citizens Campaign Fund for the Environment
description: The Great Lakes ecosystem provides drinking water and recreational opportunities to millions of New York residents and supports multibillion dollar industries. Citizens Campaign Fund for the Environment is a New York-based, environmental organization with a longtime commitment to the Great Lakes. With Mott support, the grantee will help update New York’s Great Lakes Action Agenda (a state plan to address Great Lakes priorities); educate decisionmakers and the general public on Great Lakes issues; engage in regional freshwater policy discussions; and take steps to improve its communications capacity.

title: Re-AMP Local Solutions Working Group
description: The Minneapolis Foundation, one of the first community foundations, supports the Re-AMP Network as one of its operating partners. Re-AMP is comprised of nearly 170 organizations in eight states across the Upper Midwest with the mission to work collaboratively to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. The network’s Local Solutions Working Group provides leadership and guidance on how local government practices and other local action can effectively reduce greenhouse gas emissions. This grant will enable the working group to continue to support clean energy initiatives at the local level through networking activities, research, and information exchange.

title: Re-AMP Local Solutions Working Group
description: The Michigan Environmental Council, a statewide coalition of more than 70 organizations, will help staff and organize support for the Re-AMP Local Solutions Working Group program, a network of over 150 organizations addressing climate change and clean energy issues in the Midwest. The working group is focused on building momentum for climate action at the local and metro regional scale. Specific activities will include: 1) tapping knowledge within the network to add capacity and deepen expertise on local solutions; 2) exploring and enhancing alignment with external groups and networks that work on local solutions; and 3) convening working group members to facilitate learning and exchange. Mott funds will also be used to organize and support a set of meetings among foundation representatives broadly interested in climate and energy work in Michigan and the Midwest.

title: Great Lakes Water Efficiency Program
description: The Alliance for Water Efficiency, a nonprofit organization based in Chicago, promotes the efficient and sustainable use of water in North America. In particular, the grantee seeks to reduce the amount of water lost through municipal water supply systems. Reducing leaks can help maintain water levels for lakes, rivers, and aquifers while also lowering expenses for communities. With Mott support, the grantee will conduct two pilot projects with Great Lakes-based water utilities to show the practical application and benefits of using new software tools to: 1) assess water supply systems; and 2) develop strategies for reducing leaks. The grantee will also conduct workshops and meetings to educate water suppliers, decisionmakers, and other stakeholders about how best to apply these new tools to improve water efficiencies within municipal systems.

title: Harbor Maintenance and Upstream Sediment Reduction
description: Rivers, lakes, and wetlands are designed to incorporate a certain amount of soil, sand, and rock deposited by rainwater and snow melts. Reductions in the density of trees and plants that help keep soil in place have led to increased quantities of soil and sediments that run off into Great Lakes’ waterways. More frequent and intense storms also exacerbate soil erosion. With Mott support, the Delta Institute will research strategies for reducing sediment runoff into Michigan’s harbors and marinas. The grantee will examine how new funding approaches could reduce harbor maintenance costs, promote upstream conservation efforts, and employ urban best management practices. With offices in Chicago and Michigan, the grantee is a nonprofit organization with a mission to work with business, government, and communities in the Great Lakes’ region to develop market-driven solutions that build environmental resilience, economic vitality, and healthy communities.

title: Flint Farmers' Market Operating Support
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant increase provides additional general operating support for the Flint Farmers’ Market, a project of the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation and its support organization, the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, which have been leaders in the effort to revitalize downtown Flint. As a source of year-round access to fresh produce and as the on-premises host to the Hurley Pediatric Clinic, the market acts as a community hub in helping Flint residents combat the negative effects of lead exposure through healthy nutrition and general wellness promotion. In addition, the market maintains an active calendar of community events, makes community meeting space available to local groups, and supports local food entrepreneurs through a commercial kitchen co-working facility. The Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation receives and administers funds for charitable purposes and for the public welfare of Genesee County, Michigan, including support for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation.

title: Flint Farmers' Market Operating Support
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: The Flint Farmers’ Market is a key component of ongoing efforts to revitalize downtown Flint. Located in the Health and Wellness District, the market provides Flint residents with year-round access to fresh produce and locally grown foods. In addition, the market maintains an active calendar of community events, makes meeting space available to local groups, and supports food entrepreneurs through a commercial kitchen co-working space. In addition, market staff educates residents on the importance of healthy eating to mitigate the impact of lead. This grant will support operations of the facility as well as expanded programming. The Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation receives and administers funds for charitable purposes and for the public welfare of Genesee County, Michigan, including its supported organization, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, which operates the Flint Farmers’ Market.
