title: Flint Farmers' Market Operating Support
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: The Flint Farmers’ Market is a central component of ongoing efforts to revitalize downtown Flint. Newly relocated to the downtown Health and Wellness District, the market provides Flint residents with year-round access to fresh produce and locally produced foods. In addition, the market maintains an active calendar of community events, makes community meeting space available to local groups, and supports local food entrepreneurs through a commercial kitchen co-working facility. This grant will provide operating support for the facility as well as expanded programming. The Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation receives and administers funds for charitable purposes and for the public welfare of Genesee County, Michigan, including support for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, which operates the Flint Farmers’ Market.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purpose support to CFLeads, a national network of domestic community foundations committed to building stronger communities through community leadership. The grantee mainly serves community foundations through its educational offerings: Community Leadership Networks, Executive Leadership Institutes, CEO visits, and Issue Networks. In the last year alone, the grantee worked with 333 individuals from 208 community foundations. It also provides technical assistance, research, and resource materials on best practices and convenes a biennial forum. In 2017-2018, the grantee will continue its educational, technical assistance, research, and informational offerings, specifically supporting issue networks in the areas of family economic security, equity, and links with Latin American community foundations. Established in 1991 as the Coalition of Community Foundations for Youth, CFLeads changed its name and focused its work on community leadership in 2006. Established as a supporting organization of the Greater Kansas City Community Foundation, CFLeads will become an independent nonprofit organization in 2017.

title: Creative Industries Project
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will support research and development for the Michigan creative industries sector including arts and cultural nonprofit organizations. Creative Many Michigan (formerly ArtServe Michigan) will lead efforts to compile, review, and analyze statewide creative economy information and data. Additionally, a deeper analysis will be conducted in four key regions including Flint, Detroit, Ann Arbor, and Grand Rapids. This grant will fund data collection and engagement activities in Flint.

title: Financial Aid Policy Landscape Reports
geographic_focus: Minnesota, Illinois, Kansas, Michigan, Iowa, South Dakota, Missouri, Indiana, Wisconsin, North Dakota, Nebraska, Ohio
description: This grant will enable Engage Strategies to prepare comprehensive state reports that provide strategic information about the opportunities and challenges for promoting financial aid reforms in Midwest states. The reports will answer questions such as: How can financial aid reform strategies best be framed to garner support? Who are the most effective champions and spokespersons? and, most importantly, Would a Mott investment leverage change? These assessments will not only help the Foundation identify high impact efforts but also will help organizations active on these issues shape their public education and advocacy strategies and identify critical partners necessary to achieve results. Based in South Carolina, Engage Strategies is a for-profit consulting firm that provides strategic guidance and analysis services to foundations, businesses, and nonprofit organizations.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen the Ukrainian Philanthropists Forum’s capacity to develop a professional philanthropic sector in Ukraine. During 2015-2016, the grantee worked successfully in campaigning for the introduction of transparent and cost-effective giving via text message. It held over 30 capacity building events throughout the country, while also raising the profile of philanthropy through two international conferences and the increasingly popular National Ranking of Philanthropists. The grantee’s focus in 2017-2018 will be to provide professional support for volunteer initiatives, charitable organizations, and philanthropic institutions; advocate for a policy environment for philanthropic and volunteer activity that conforms to European standards; and increase its capacity to act as an informational and professional hub for mass media, volunteers, and charitable institutions on current trends of philanthropic sector development. Established in 2004, the Ukrainian Philanthropists Forum’s strategic priorities are to: 1) advocate for a favorable legal and fiscal framework for charitable activity; 2) increase public trust toward philanthropy in society; and 3) build the professional capacity of the philanthropic sector.

title: General Purposes
description: The Ukrainian Philanthropists Forum is an association of 27 local and international donors working in Ukraine. Since its establishment in 2004, the grantee has strengthened philanthropy by improving the level and effectiveness of philanthropic giving and by raising the profile and capacity of its members. Its overall strategic priorities are to: 1) advocate for a favorable legal and fiscal framework for charitable activity; 2) increase public trust toward philanthropy in society; and 3) build the professional capacity of the philanthropic sector. During 2015-2016, the grantee will provide professional support for volunteer initiatives, charitable organizations, and philanthropic institutions, many of which are newly emerged or in the process of reorienting their activities due to the current conflict in Ukraine; advocate for a policy environment for philanthropic and volunteer activity that conforms to European standards; and increase its capacity to act as an informational and professional hub for mass media, volunteers, and charitable institutions on current trends of philanthropic sector development. The grantee is based in Kyiv.

title: Property Acquisition (Walker School)
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Flint Cultural Center Corporation provides arts, culture, history, science, and educational programming through its member organizations Sloan Museum*Longway Planetarium and The Whiting. The grantee is also responsible for maintaining the 33-acre Flint Cultural Center campus. Approximately 175,000 students and adults will attend or participate in a variety of cultural, educational, and instructional programs and activities at these cultural center venues this year. This grant will allow the grantee to purchase the former Walker School building which borders on the cultural center campus.

title: Solarize Michigan
description: Despite being home to a robust solar supply chain, Michigan accounts for just two-tenths of one percent of national solar deployment. A number of communities across the country have initiated solarization programs to accelerate solar energy use by homeowners and small businesses through competitive contractor selection, community outreach, bulk purchasing, and similar measures. The Institute for Energy Innovation will initiate such a program in Michigan, beginning with at least three communities in the Great Lakes Bay Region of Michigan that includes Bay, Isabella, Midland, and Saginaw counties. In addition to a significant increase in residential solar deployment, the result will be a replicable model for use in other communities across Michigan.

title: Samuel Halperin Lecture and Public Service Award
description: The American Youth Policy Forum and the Institute for Educational Leadership will develop and host an annual event, featuring the Samuel Halperin Lecture and Public Service Award. The Samuel Halperin Lecture will include a lecture presented by a high level, nationally recognized speaker who has spent his or her career working in support of policies, practices, or research that improve outcomes for vulnerable, disconnected, or low-income youth and young adults. The Samuel Halperin Youth Public Service Award will recognize a young person who has made a commitment to public service or been engaged in public service activities.

title: Vital Voices 20 Initiative
description: This grant provides support to Vital Voices Global Partnership for the Vital Voices 20 Initiative. Over the past several decades, the grantee has worked with thousands of women leaders who are advancing economic, political, and social progress in their communities and beyond. Through the Vital Voices 20 initiative, the grantee will partner with a select group of the most engaged and visionary members of its network to develop tailored support to enable them to achieve their bold and innovative visions for changing their communities and countries.

title: Social Network Mapping Project
geographic_focus: Ontario, Ohio, Wisconsin, Indiana, Minnesota, New York, Illinois, Pennsylvania, Michigan
description: Limited resources, differing organizational priorities, and the sheer size of the Great Lakes Basin make it difficult for freshwater groups to get to know each other and collaborate. The Sustainability Network is a nonprofit organization based in Toronto, Ontario, that provides capacity building services to environmental organizations. With Mott support, the grantee will conduct a social network analysis based on a survey of approximately 200 Great Lakes organizations in the United States and Canada. The results will be shared with all Great Lakes groups to develop strategies to strengthen binational collaboration. The grantee will also use the results to provide targeted coaching, training, and networking opportunities to freshwater nonprofits in the Great Lakes region.

title: Chair in African Philanthropy
description: The Southern Africa Trust was established in 2005 to support lasting solutions to reduce poverty across the southern African region by generating knowledge and making grants to organizations that work on poverty-related issues. The Chair in African Philanthropy, a project of the Southern Africa Trust, was established to promote philanthropic knowledge and practice on the African continent. The chair promotes a narrative on African philanthropy that embraces traditional forms of giving. The Southern Africa Trust and the University of the Witwatersrand, the host of the chair, will be launching the chair at the Global Summit on Community Philanthropy taking place in Johannesburg, South Africa, December 1-2, 2016. This grant increase will help support the costs related to the launch.

title: Chair in African Philanthropy
description: The University of the Witwatersrand was established to provide high-quality, internationally competitive education, founded on high academic standards, cutting-edge research, public engagement, and productive partnerships with leading institutions throughout the world. The Chair in African Philanthropy (based at the business school) was established to generate knowledge on philanthropy in the continent from an African perspective. Past support enabled the university to set up the necessary structures and systems that will advance teaching and learning, promote dialogue that enriches practice, and produce new knowledge on African forms of giving. In addition, a visiting chair was appointed to oversee the establishment of the Chair on African Philanthropy. This grant will enable the Chair on African Philanthropy to deliver a teaching program on African philanthropy, produce research, host annual learning events for practitioners and academics from across the continent, and build partnerships and networks across the globe.

title: Chair in African Philanthropy
description: The Southern Africa Trust is a grantmaker that was established in 2005 to promote community involvement in policy dialogues. It makes grants to organizations that work to alleviate poverty through policy reform. The Chair in African Philanthropy, a project of the Southern Africa Trust, was set up to promote philanthropic knowledge and practice on the African continent. Through the Chair in African Philanthropy, the grantee aims to promote a narrative on African philanthropy that embraces traditional practices of giving. Efforts to document African practices of giving have so far been sporadic and disconnected. Where such knowledge is produced, it often does not form part of academic literature. The Chair in African Philanthropy at the University of the Witwatersrand will generate knowledge and allow for dialogue that enriches practice. This grant will enable the Chair in African Philanthropy to develop an academic and research framework and to set up governance and management structures.

title: Centre for Community Schools
description: The Nelson Mandela Metropolitan University was established in 2005 as a result of a merger between the Port Elizabeth Technikon and the University of Port Elizabeth (incorporating Vista University) in South Africa. The Centre for Community Schools is an entity of the university established to promote theoretical- and practice-based approaches to school improvement that are relevant and responsive to the contextual realities of schools. As part of its community outreach efforts, the center assisted in the establishment of a community of practice for a number of schools based in the Port Elizabeth area, called the Manyano Network of Community Schools. This grant will enable the Centre for Community Schools to support the Manyano Network of Community Schools and conduct research on how this model could be expanded to other parts of South Africa.

title: Reflection Group on Foreign Policies and International Order
description: The project goal is to increase awareness and understanding of how the foreign policies of Western powers, and the perception of these policies by others, are shaping international relations. To this end, the Centre for Liberal Strategies Foundation, a think tank based in Sofia, Bulgaria, will lead an in-depth and interactive examination and analysis of the West’s policies in various regions of the world, including Eastern Europe and Russia. During the grant period, the grantee will convene a high level reflection group of ten to twelve policymakers and policy analysts from within and outside the West to conduct study visits to five key countries — Russia, Turkey, Iran, India, and Greece. The group will prepare a series of ten analytical reports based on these five case studies. Public debates and closed-door meetings throughout Europe will be organized to discuss the issues. A final report will summarize key findings and policy recommendations.

title: Flint Community Data Platform
description: This project will support a community data platform designed and developed by the University of Michigan-Flint Outreach and Geography, Planning, and Environment departments’ staff and faculty. In the first full year of implementation, the grantee will work with local nonprofit partners, funders, schools, and government agencies to design and implement an online tool that aggregates and analyzes community-level data and provides free access to the public.

title: Flint Community Data Platform
description: This project supports a community data platform designed and developed by the University of Michigan-Flint’s Outreach and Geography, Planning, and Environment departments. In the first full year of implementation, the grantee will work with local nonprofit partners, funders, schools, and government agencies to design and implement an online tool that aggregates and analyzes community-level data and provides free access to the public.

title: Flint Community Data Platform
description: This project supports a community data platform designed, developed, and led by the University of Michigan-Flint’s Office of University Outreach in partnership with the Geographic Information Systems Center. With this renewal grant, the grantee will continue to work with local nonprofit partners, funders, schools, and government agencies to design and implement an online tool that aggregates and analyzes community-level data and provides free access to the public.

title: Flint Community Data Platform
description: This project supports a community data platform designed, developed, and led by the University of Michigan-Flint’s Office of University Outreach in partnership with the Geographic Information Systems Center. With this renewal grant, the grantee will continue to work with local nonprofit partners, funders, schools, and government agencies to design and implement an online tool that aggregates and analyzes community-level data and provides free access to the public.

title: Flint Community Data Platform
description: This project will support a community data platform designed and developed by the University of Michigan-Flint’s Outreach and Geographic Information Systems Center staff and faculty. In this pilot year, the grantee will work with local nonprofit partners, funders, schools, and the city of Flint to design and implement a prototype for the community. Data and related analyses will be publicly available.

title: On-Bill Financing Program
description: Michigan is still in the relatively early stages of the clean energy transition. Tools and technical assistance are needed to help early adopters navigate a range of financial and market barriers. With partial support from Mott, Michigan Saves will develop two such tools: an on-bill financing program for energy efficiency and renewable energy improvements, and an energy savings reporting system for nonprofits engaged in promoting the adoption of energy efficiency measures. Michigan Saves is a statewide organization that provides affordable financing options for homeowners, businesses, and local governments that want to adopt energy efficiency and renewable energy practices.

title: Geoffrey Canada Scholarship Fund
description: This grant will support the Geoffrey Canada Scholarship Fund. The Board of Trustees of the Harlem Children’s Zone launched a scholarship fund campaign to recognize the leadership and contributions of Geoffrey Canada, the longtime leader of the organization. The Geoffrey Canada Scholarship Fund will provide support to as many as 100 college students in the grantee’s 97-block area in central Harlem.

title: Dort Motor Company Building
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will enable the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, a supported organization of the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, to purchase and hold the historic Dort Motor Company Building until financing can be secured to redevelop the property into rental apartments. Located on Grand Traverse Street between W. Kearsley and Water Street, the building is in an emerging microdistrict at the edge of downtown. Further redevelopment of this area will help to tie downtown revitalization efforts to revitalization taking place in Flint’s Carriage Town neighborhood, and to efforts to transform the former Chevy-in-the-Hole brownfield site into a naturalized park and recreational amenity.

title: Building Sustainable Civil Society in the 21st Century
description: The project goal is to enhance the resilience and effectiveness of civil society around the world. During the project’s first phase, the Center for Strategic & International Studies built an international consortium of scholars and experts to conduct research and identify effective strategies for countering the closing space for civil society around the world. During the next phase, the consortium will identify and propose concrete remedies and innovative solutions to closing space through action-oriented research, a range of information products, and convenings. The consortium includes working groups on enhancing civil society sustainability, building local constituencies, strengthening global initiatives, and resolving the tension between security and civic space. Founded in 1962, the Center for Strategic & International Studies is one of the world’s preeminent international policy institutions focused on defense and security, regional stability, and transnational challenges ranging from energy and climate to global development and economic integration.

title: Building Sustainable Civil Society in the 21st Century
description: The project goal is to enhance the resilience and effectiveness of civil society around the world. The Center for Strategic & International Studies is building an international consortium of scholars and experts to conduct research and generate recommendations to address the issue of closing space for civil society. The consortium will examine the drivers of closing space and will identify remedies based on a combination of action-oriented research, a range of information products, and convenings. The consortium will include working groups devoted to issues such as the impact of foreign aid, increased connectivity of citizens in the digital age, levels of antiWestern sentiment, or the impact of post-9/11 security policies. Founded in 1962, the Center for Strategic & International Studies is one of the world’s preeminent international policy institutions focused on defense and security, regional stability, and transnational challenges ranging from energy and climate to global development and economic integration.

title: Student Retention and Recruitment
description: This grant will provide support to the Flint Community Schools to aid in the development and execution of a marketing campaign aimed at retaining and recruiting students to the district, which has become even more important with the issues surrounding the city’s water system. It is critical that the district bolster enrollment figures as it seeks to gain financial stability and improve student academic outcomes. The new districtwide educational plan, newly envisioned community schools model, and an expanded early childhood education program are among the important elements in re-attracting families to the district.

title: Student Retention and Recruitment
description: This grant will provide support to Flint Community Schools to aid in the development and execution of a marketing campaign aimed at retaining and recruiting students to the district, which has become even more important with the issues surrounding the city’s water system. It is critical that the district bolster enrollment figures as it seeks to gain financial stability and improve student academic outcomes. The new districtwide educational plan, newly envisioned community schools model, and an expanded early childhood education program are among the important elements in retaining and attracting families to the district.

title: Student Retention and Recruitment
description: This grant will provide support to the Flint Community Schools to aid in the development and execution of a marketing campaign aimed at retaining and recruiting students to the district. It is critical that the district bolster enrollment figures as it seeks to gain financial stability and improve student academic outcomes. The STEM-focused curriculum at the Brownell/Holmes STEM Academy, the new districtwide educational plan, and the newly envisioned community schools model are among the important elements in retaining and attracting families to the district.

title: Nonprofit Policy Forum
description: The program goal is to support scholarly research that provides the basis for constructive public policy development for philanthropy and the nonprofit sector. Launched in 2010 at Georgia State University, the “Nonprofit Policy Forum”, now a project of the Cleveland State University Foundation, is a professional journal that addresses public policy issues as they affect or are influenced by nonprofit organizations. Starting in 2016, the journal will be housed at the Center for Nonprofit Policy & Practice at Cleveland State University. The center serves the nonprofit sector through training and technical assistance to nonprofit organizations, scholarly and applied research, and education in the leadership and management of nonprofit organizations. Grant support will allow an increase of the annual number of issues from two to four, the provision of open access status, growth in readership and the flow of high quality manuscripts from scholars, and a transition to a broader base of continuous support, primarily from subscriptions and institutional sponsorships.

title: Spotlighting Tapajos Hydro Development
description: Uma Gota no Oceano (A Drop in the Ocean) is a Brazilian strategic communications agency that develops narratives, using strategic videos and information for print, broadcast, and social media. This project renewal will support the grantee to use strategic communications to raise public awareness about the impacts of large-scale hydroelectric development in the Amazon rainforest and alternative sustainable development options, particularly for the Tapajos River Basin.

title: Spotlighting Tapajos Hydro Development
description: Uma Gota no Oceano (A Drop in the Ocean) is a Brazilian strategic communications agency that develops narratives, using videos and information for print, broadcast, and social media. Over the past project period, the grantee grew its audience by 55 percent, developed media stories and videos and influenced major media networks to cover stories related to energy development finance and its impacts on sustainability and affected communities. The grantee will build upon its successful media strategies over the next project period to raise the public debate about key issues influencing sustainable energy development.

title: Spotlighting Tapajos Hydro Development
description: This project will support the Brazilian media group, Uma Gota no Oceano (A Drop in the Ocean), to develop print, broadcast, and social media material to raise awareness about the impacts of large-scale hydroelectric development in the Amazon rainforest. Specifically, the grantee will develop strategic communications campaigns to raise awareness among Brazilian middle and upper classes about hydroelectric projects proposed in the Tapajos River basin.

title: Atlantic Philanthropies Partnership Evaluation
description: Frayintermedia was founded by veteran journalist and media trainer Paula Fray to help train journalists and communicators across the African continent and has been providing training since 2005. The grantee has provided tailored training and mentorship support to many nonprofits on communication and facilitated a communications convening of Mott grantees in 2015. The grantee will conduct an evaluation of grants made through a partnership between the Mott Foundation and The Atlantic Philanthropies to support the community advice office sector in South Africa for the period 2013-2016. The evaluation will assess the impact of the grants on the overall work of the organizations that received support, the relevance of the supported programs relative to the needs of poor and marginalized communities, and whether the supported organizations achieved the anticipated outcomes. The grantee will engage all the organizations supported and will conduct desktop reviews, develop case studies, and produce a video as part of the evaluation. This grant has been made possible by a partnership with The Atlantic Philanthropies in support of the community advice office sector.

title: Operating System for Community Philanthropy
description: The project goal is to strengthen community philanthropy around the world by establishing links between the world’s premier global online giving platform and local philanthropic institutions in ways that will leverage and increase the efficiency of local giving. As part of its five-year, $17 million campaign to scale up its global crowdfunding platform to $100 million annually, GlobalGiving will develop an operating system for community philanthropy. During 2015-2019, the grantee will map the landscape of digital community philanthropy worldwide, launch locally customized and operated online giving platforms with community philanthropy organizations in up to three countries/regions, and create a community of practice to foster peer learning and ensure ongoing interoperability with the grantee’s online platform. With support from the Mott Foundation, GlobalGiving was founded in 2002 as a charity fundraising Website that gives social entrepreneurs and nonprofit organizations from anywhere in the world a chance to raise money to improve their communities.

title: Technology Promoting Citizen Participation in Ukraine
description: The program goal is to use new information technology to engage citizens in reform efforts in Ukraine. Following a needs assessment, the Sunlight Foundation will host the leaders of seven selected Ukrainian organizations in Washington, D.C., in September 2015. Over the course of a week, the grantee will work directly with the organizations’ leaders on specific challenges or projects they have identified regarding the use of technology to promote civic participation in Ukraine’s reform efforts. The Ukrainian leaders will also participate in the grantee’s annual two-day transparency camp. The grantee will provide follow-up technical assistance to help ensure that the Ukrainian leaders’ projects and ideas continue to flourish. Founded in 2006, the Washington D.C.-based Sunlight Foundation is a national, nonpartisan, nonprofit organization that uses the tools of civic technology, open data, policy analysis, and journalism to make government and politics more accountable and transparent to all.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to the Crim Fitness Foundation. Focusing on active living, physical fitness, nutrition, and mindfulness, the grantee offers year-round programming for children and adults throughout the greater Flint area. Nutrition and active living are recognized as important strategies to mitigate the impact of lead exposure, which is important for Flint residents and children as a result of the Flint water crisis. The grantee also serves as the lead agency for the community schools strategy, which provides access to a variety of wrap-around health and educational services for Flint Community Schools’ students and families. The Crim Festival of Races attracts more than 14,000 walkers and runners as well as tens of thousands of spectators each year.

Nutrition and active living are recognized as important strategies to mitigate the impact of lead exposure, which is essential for Flint residents and children as a result of the Flint water crisis. The grantee also serves as the lead agency for the community schools strategy, which provides access to a variety of wraparound health and educational services for Flint Community Schools’ students and families. The Crim Festival of Races attracts more than 12,000 walkers and runners as well as tens of thousands of spectators each year.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to the Crim Fitness Foundation. Focusing on active living, physical fitness, nutrition, and mindfulness, the grantee offers year-round programming for children and adults throughout the Greater Flint area. The Crim Festival of Races, which will celebrate its 40th anniversary in 2016, attracts more than 14,000 walkers and runners, as well as tens of thousands of spectators each year. It is one of the premier events in downtown Flint.

title: Genesee County Volunteer Engagement
description: This grant will enable the Volunteer Centers of Michigan, an affiliate of the Michigan Nonprofit Association, to work with the United Way of Genesee County to develop a new, dynamic, and sustainable volunteer center for Genesee County. The Volunteer Centers of Michigan will work with community stakeholders to redesign the local volunteer center to better align with Flint’s master plan, the five-year service plan, and Flint Community Schools, while supporting and meeting the needs of local nonprofit organizations and community members.

title: Cultural Center School Feasibility Study
description: This grant to the Flint Cultural Center Corporation will provide support for design and development activities to determine the feasibility of a school located on the Flint Cultural Center campus. The Cultural Center organizations currently provide a variety of cultural, educational and instructional programs and activities in the arts and sciences both on site and in area schools. There is interest in determining if a school located on the Cultural Center campus would provide additional avenues for providing high quality educational opportunities for residents in the region. High quality programming is crucial in Flint given its current water crisis because educational and enrichment opportunities are important interventions for individuals from birth to young adulthood to help mitigate the long-term impacts of exposure to lead.

title: Cultural Center School Feasibility Study
description: The purpose of this grant to the Flint Cultural Center Corporation is to continue planning the development of a STEAM-focused school on the cultural center campus. The cultural center organizations currently provide a variety of cultural, educational and instructional programs, including activities in the arts and sciences both on site and in area schools. A school located on the campus would be another avenue for providing high quality educational opportunities for residents in the region. These types of educational and enrichment opportunities are important interventions for individuals from birth to young adulthood to help mitigate the long-term impacts of exposure to lead.

title: Cultural Center School Feasibility Study
description: This grant will provide support for research and potential planning activities to determine the feasibility of a school located on the Flint Cultural Center campus. The Flint Cultural Center Corporation operates The Whiting, Sloan Museum, and Longway Planetarium. Approximately 193,000 students and adults annually attend or participate in a variety of cultural, educational, and instructional programs and activities at these cultural center organizations. In addition to offering national touring artists and live theater, the grantee also focuses on providing educational programming, both on-site and in area schools.

title: Governor's Service Awards Fund
description: This grant will enable the Capital Region Community Foundation to support the work of the Michigan Community Service Commission, the state’s lead agency on service and volunteerism, which seeks to engage all Michigan residents in addressing critical community challenges through national service and volunteerism. To support the continued growth and celebration of service and volunteerism within the state, the Michigan Community Service Commission hosts an annual Governor’s Service Awards event. This event provides a platform to shine a spotlight on volunteerism and its impact on the state and annually touches more than 2,000 individuals and organizations through its nomination process. The grantee administers the proceeds from the event to support service initiatives.

title: Dale Kildee, A Champion for Student Success
description: The Foundation for Mott Community College was created in 1986 to promote educational, literacy, cultural, and other activities through scholarships and a variety of activities benefiting Mott Community College and its students. This grant will provide support to the Foundation for Mott Community College in honor of Congressman Dale Kildee. Congressman Kildee has been a champion for at-risk, underserved populations and increased access to education. This grant will allow the grantee to provide assistance to students facing barriers to success.

title: Blight Remediation
description: This grant increase will provide support to Kettering University for the acquisition and demolition or remediation of blighted and abandoned properties along the University Avenue corridor. Purchasing these properties is believed to be an important step in securing strategic parcels along University Avenue and contributing to the revitalization of the corridor that connects several of the city’s key anchor institutions and assets.

title: Blight Remediation
description: This grant will provide support to Kettering University for the acquisition and demolition or remediation of blighted and abandoned properties along the University Avenue corridor. Purchasing these properties is believed to be an important step in securing strategic parcels along University Avenue and contributing to the revitalization of the corridor that connects several of the city’s key anchor institutions and assets.

title: Strengthening Great Lakes Leadership
geographic_focus: Ohio, Indiana, Illinois, Michigan, New York, Minnesota, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin
description: The mission of the Environmental Leadership Program is to support visionary, action-oriented, and diverse leadership for a just and sustainable future. Environmental leaders face complex challenges—ones that cannot be met by organizations or sectors in isolation. The grantee has trained over 1,200 rising environmental and social change leaders since 2000. With renewed support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee will recruit two annual groups of up to 20 emerging leaders working on conservation issues in the Great Lakes region in 2020 and 2021. These cohorts will attend three multi-day retreats, develop personal leadership plans, establish strong peer support networks, and enhance their knowledge and leadership skills.

title: Great Lakes Leadership Project
geographic_focus: Ohio, Wisconsin, Pennsylvania, Minnesota, Michigan, Indiana, New York, Illinois
description: Based in Maryland, the Environmental Leadership Program provides leadership training, coaching, and individualized support to environmental leaders across the United States. The grantee hosts leadership retreats for environmental leaders who represent a range of issue areas, seniority levels, geographic locations, and backgrounds. With Mott support, ten freshwater leaders from the Great Lakes region will participate in two retreats over a one-year period. Participants will improve their organizational management skills, build on existing personal strengths, and widen their professional networks.

title: Building a Platform for Youth Giving
description: The program goal is to support the involvement of youth in community philanthropy. To this end, the Foundation Center will build an online portal that will document, analyze, and promote effective youth grantmaking. The grantee will engage a committee of advisors to contribute to the portal’s navigational framework and knowledge management principles; develop a youth grantmaking map with filters and drill-down capabilities; and acquire and curate qualitative data, literature, and other new content about youth grantmaking. The portal will be launched in the spring of 2016 through a targeted e-mail and social media marketing campaign, presentations at conferences, and Webinars. After its launch, the grantee will conduct focused international outreach to expand the portal to youth grantmaking globally. Established in 1956, the Foundation Center is dedicated to fostering public understanding of the foundation field by collecting, organizing, analyzing, and disseminating information on foundations, corporate giving, and related subjects.

title: Enhancing Civic Engagement Through Active Citizenship Education
description: The program goal is to increase civic engagement in Ukraine by providing comprehensive educational programs for grassroots initiatives based on the principle of active citizen participation. Through its Institute for Leadership and Management, the Ukrainian Catholic University will refine courses and introduce methods and tools of participative decisionmaking, community mobilization, facilitation, and civic engagement into existing courses for its master’s in nonprofit management. It will also develop other certificate programs and trainings for nonprofit organization leaders while seeking to increase the pool of qualified trainers and strengthen the growing alumni network of the institute. In 2015-2017, the grantee held three extended Schools of Responsible Citizenship for 54 participants, supported 12 local projects involving over 2,000 participants from seven regions of Ukraine, and devised an online course in responsible citizenship intended to go live for the 2017-2018 academic year. Inaugurated in 2002, the Ukrainian Catholic University is a leading private educational institution in western Ukraine.

title: Enhancing Civic Engagement Through Active Citizenship Education
description: The program goal is to increase civic engagement in Ukraine by providing comprehensive educational programs for grassroots initiatives based on the principle of active citizen participation. The Ukrainian Catholic University, a leading private educational institution inaugurated in western Ukraine in 2002, will foster a new culture in Ukrainian society by involving community members into discussions of relevant issues, decisionmaking, and taking action. Drawing on the advice and guidance of experts in Poland, Austria, and the United States, the grantee’s Institute for Leadership and Management will develop new courses and introduce methods and tools of participative decisionmaking, community mobilization, facilitation, and civic engagement into existing courses for its Masters in Nonprofit Management and other certificate programs and trainings for nonprofit organization leaders. The grantee will also incorporate newly developed academic courses in active citizen participation into the curriculum of its undergraduate program of social pedagogy.

title: Building Broader Communities in the Americas
description: The project goal is to foster partnerships between community foundations in Latin America and the Caribbean and their counterparts in the United States and Canada, using interested stakeholders, such as immigrant groups, as channels of interconnectivity. Project activities will include: 1) exchanges of staff, boards, and donors of participating community foundations; 2) working group meetings and outreach to new stakeholders; 3) applied research, such as community-specific mapping exercises, mapping of corporate interests in the hemisphere and investigation of government programs that support diaspora/sending community partnerships; 4) tool development and sharing of best practices of supporting community philanthropy in a transnational context; and 5) a Leadership Fellows Program. The project will be managed by the Inter-American Foundation, an independent United States government agency created by Congress in 1969 to channel development assistance directly to the organized poor in Latin America and the Caribbean.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to safeguard the legal space for civil society and philanthropy globally. To this end, the International Center for Not-for-Profit Law will carry out a range of activities, including enhancing international norms and multilateral engagement to safeguard civic space, promoting appropriate country-level legislation, helping civil society organizations navigate laws once enacted, undertaking and disseminating research and analysis, and raising public awareness about the importance of civil society and cross-border philanthropy. The grantee is based in Washington, D.C.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to safeguard the legal space for civil society and philanthropy globally. The International Center for Not-for-Profit Law, based in Washington, D.C., will carry out a range of activities, including enhancing international norms and multilateral engagement to safeguard civic space, promoting appropriate country-level legislation, helping civil society organizations navigate laws once enacted, undertaking research and information sharing, and raising public awareness about the importance of civil society and cross-border philanthropy. To support its programmatic objectives, the grantee will also focus on developing the capacity of its in-country partners to address civic space challenges. The grantee will offer fellowship programs; organize professional development trainings at the country, regional, and global levels; and integrate civil society legal issues into university curricula to educate future lawyers, nonprofit leaders, and citizens on civil society issues.

title: General Purposes
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant provides general purpose support to Red Ink Flint. The grantee operates Flint Local 432, a performance venue located in downtown Flint for artistic programming and community convening. In 2016, 82 concerts were performed at the venue, including local musical talent as well as regional and national acts. Additionally, the grantee operates a makerspace program called Steamworks, which moved into space at Factory Two on Grand Traverse Street in 2017. Funds will support organizational, administrative, and programmatic costs for Red Ink Flint.

title: General Purposes
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant provides general purposes support to Red Ink Flint. The grantee operates Flint Local 432, a performance venue located in downtown Flint for artistic programming and community convening. In 2017, 67 concerts were performed at the venue, including local musical talent as well as regional and national acts. Additionally, the grantee operates the Factory Two makerspace, which opened on Grand Traverse Street in 2017. Funds will support organizational, administrative, and programmatic costs for Red Ink Flint.

title: General Purposes
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant provides general purpose support to Red Ink Flint. Red Ink Flint operates the Flint Local 432 performance venue located in downtown Flint for artistic programming and community convening. In 2014, 110 concerts were performed at the venue, including local musical talent as well as regional and national acts. Funds will support organizational, administrative, and programmatic costs.

title: Vaclav Havel Circle
description: This grant will provide funding for the Vaclav Havel Circle, a project of the Forum 2000 Foundation. The Vaclav Havel Circle is an initiative that aims to support the values of democracy and respect of human rights; assist in the development of civil society; and encourage religious, cultural, and ethnic tolerance.

title: Vaclav Havel Circle
description: The grant will provide funding for the Vaclav Havel Circle, a project of the Forum 2000 Foundation. The Vaclav Havel Circle is an initiative that aims to support the values of democracy and respect of human rights; assist in the development of civil society; and encourage religious, cultural, and ethnic tolerance.

title: Capacity Building for Community-Based Organizations
description: The Uthungulu Community Foundation was founded in 1999 to promote the development of communities in the Uthungulu district of KwaZulu-Natal in South Africa. It makes grants, provides training, and creates linkages between government, business, universities and civil society in the region. Past support has enabled the grantee to train young people in the district, make grants, and build the capacity of community-based organizations. This grant will enable the grantee to continue providing training to community-based organizations and unemployed young people in the Uthungulu district.

title: Capacity Building for Community-Based Organizations
description: The Uthungulu Community Foundation was founded in 1999 to promote the development of communities in the Uthungulu district of KwaZulu-Natal in South Africa. It makes grants, provides training, and creates linkages between government, business, universities, and civil society in the region. Past support from Mott has enabled the grantee to make grants to nonprofits and community-based organizations, provide training on topics related to building institutions, and promote the community foundation field in the country and the southern Africa region. This grant will enable the grantee to continue to implement programs that support the communities it serves, strengthen partnerships with local businesses and government, and provide training and advisory services to civil society organizations. The grantee will also continue to partner with government to provide support services to organizations working in the most marginalized communities in KwaZulu-Natal.

title: Downtown Property Acquisition of 126 West Kearsley
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will provide support to the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, a supported organization of the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, to acquire and hold the property located at 126 W. Kearsley Street in downtown Flint for future redevelopment in conjunction with adjacent properties. This property is located close to the Saginaw Street corridor and to public parking facilities and, once redeveloped, will further the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation’s charitable mission of improving and revitalizing downtown Flint.

title: Urban Scouting Program
grantee: Boy Scouts of America - Port Huron
description: This grant will provide support to the Urban Scouting Program operated by Boy Scouts of America, Water & Woods Field Service Council. The Urban Scouting Program provides Flint area youth with a scouting experience within the school setting during non-instructional hours. The program is designed to improve students’ school performance, personal behavior, communication skills, and access to scouting. Mott funds will help to support a portion of the salaries of a full-time and part-time staff member.

title: Building National Dialogues on Integrated Electricity Planning in East Africa
description: The World Resources Institute was founded in 1982 to provide information, ideas, and solutions to global environmental problems. The grantee’s mission is to move society to live in ways that protect the Earth’s environment for current and future generations. The grantee recently completed a study on mini-grids in Tanzania, which revealed that there remain critical gaps that are negatively impacting progress in providing energy access. This renewal grant will support efforts to address these gaps in order to accelerate access to distributed renewable energy in rural Tanzanian communities.

title: Building National Dialogues on Integrated Electricity Planning in East Africa
description: The World Resources Institute was founded in 1982 to provide information, ideas, and solutions for global environmental problems. With previous Mott support, the grantee recently completed market mapping tools for the Tanzanian off-grid energy sector, introducing critical information on energy demand and end users’ ability to pay into the energy planning process. This renewal grant will support efforts to refine the planning tool and make it available to key Tanzanian government agencies in order to ensure the effort’s sustainability. In addition, the grantee will work with local governments in key Tanzanian regions to facilitate their use of the tool in economic development projects. The grantee also will share this work and lessons learned with a broader group of African civil society organizations to improve their energy planning efforts.

title: Mini-grids for Energy Access in Sub-Saharan Africa: Lessons from Tanzania
description: In Africa, 315 million rural people are expected to gain access to electricity by 2040; of this, 140 million are projected to gain access through small-scale electrical grids. To achieve this goal, between 100,000 and 200,000 small-scale electrical grids will have to be developed. Several East African countries have had success in creating attractive policy environments, and projects are beginning to proliferate. However, little has been documented about how these small-scale electrical grids are operating in practice. The World Resources Institute, working with a Tanzanian research institution, will undertake research to document the accumulated knowledge, expertise, and community-level experience in deploying small-scale electrical grids in Tanzania. The research will form the basis of Webinar and training workshops to provide useful lessons for African countries, donors, and private-sector investors.

title: Enhancing Stakeholder Participation in the Development of Country Action Agendas in Africa
description: To transform the energy sector, it is necessary to account for diverse energy needs. Individuals, households, and communities require energy services in different forms in order to meet a variety of basic, livelihood, and societal needs. The challenge is to engage civil society, community, and business groups to ensure that their concerns are addressed so that actual transformation of the energy sector and increased energy access occurs. Through this project, World Wildlife Fund-US will work with World Wildlife Fund offices in key African countries. These groups will convene a series of workshops and consultations to assist in those African countries in the development of action agendas for transforming their energy sectors as well as ensuring energy access.

title: 2015 Energy Access Practitioner Network Investment and Finance Directory
description: The United Nations Foundation established the Energy Access Practitioner Network in 2011, which has become a global network of over 2,000 members. The network represents clean energy enterprises, nongovernmental organizations, governments, and academia operating in over 170 countries with the aim of catalyzing decentralized solutions for rural electrification in developing countries. A key constraint for these groups is access to financing to help build energy access enterprises. To address this constraint, the grantee will produce a second edition of its well-received publication, “Investing for Energy Access”, which will include a special section on the financing needs of mini-grids. This edition will also be enhanced with an online searchable database.

title: Sasaki Planning for the Health and Wellness District
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will allow the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, a supported organization of the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, to contract with Sasaki Associates, Inc., to complete a framework to guide future planning and investment in the Flint Health and Wellness District. The Uptown Reinvestment Corporation is a charitable organization that works to improve the quality of life of Flint area residents through revitalization of downtown Flint. The Health and Wellness District is a key component of downtown redevelopment that helps to provide Flint residents with access to jobs, healthcare, healthy food, and other essential services.

title: Technical Assistance for Improved Teaching and Learning
description: This grant allows Michigan State University to support Flint Community Schools with technical assistance aimed at improving teaching and learning across the district. The initiative will include four primary components: development of a student support system, strategic curriculum support and alignment, comprehensive organizational and operational alignment, and community schools support. The goal is to increase district capacity, improve school culture, increase operational efficiency, and improve student academic outcomes, which has become even more important with the issues surrounding the city’s water system.

title: Technical Assistance for Improved Teaching and Learning
description: This grant allows Michigan State University to support Flint Community Schools with technical assistance aimed at improving teaching and learning across the district. The initiative will include three primary components: effective teaching and learning strategies, student engagement through a rigorous curriculum, and leadership development. The goal of the work is to continue to increase district capacity, improve school culture, increase operational efficiency, and improve student academic outcomes.

title: Technical Assistance for Improved Teaching and Learning
description: This grant allows Michigan State University to support Flint Community Schools with technical assistance aimed at improved teaching and learning across the district. The initiative will include four primary components: development of a student support system, strategic curriculum support and alignment, comprehensive organizational and operational alignment, and community schools support. The goal will be to increase district capacity, improve school culture, increase operational efficiency, and improve student academic outcomes.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support the continued organizational and programmatic development of People in Need, one of the largest nonprofits in Central and Eastern Europe. Founded in 1992, the grantee provides relief and development assistance in response to natural disasters and violent conflict; promotes human rights, civic engagement, and civil society development; and supports social inclusion and integration for marginalized groups. In 2016, the grantee provided relief and development assistance in 24 countries through 227 projects, a 20 percent increase in volume from 2015 and a threefold increase since 2013. During the grant period, the grantee will expand its aid missions in Ukraine; respond to other humanitarian needs around the world; continue programming to reduce the social exclusion of children from marginalized groups in the Czech Republic; and provide technical assistance and support to civil society organizations and human rights defenders in countries under threat. People in Need is based in Prague, Czech Republic.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support the continued organizational and programmatic development of People in Need, one of the largest nonprofits in Central and Eastern Europe. Founded in 1992, the grantee provides relief and development assistance in response to natural disasters and violent conflict; promotes human rights, civic engagement, and civil society development; and supports social inclusion and integration for marginalized groups. Since its establishment, the grantee has worked in more than 50 countries. In 2014, the grantee delivered $35 million in aid to 21 countries, including $14.6 million in Syria, mostly in the form of food aid to more than 1.1 million people. During the grant period, the grantee will expand its aid missions in Syria and Ukraine, respond to other humanitarian needs around the world, continue programming to reduce the social exclusion of children from marginalized groups in the Czech Republic, increase programming to encourage civic engagement and leadership by young people in the Czech Republic, and provide technical assistance and support to civil society organizations and human rights defenders in countries under threat. People in Need is based in Prague, Czech Republic.

title: General Purposes
description: Michigan Energy Options has about 40 years of experience in the energy efficiency and renewable energy sector and is the only clean energy nonprofit in the state with offices in both the upper and lower peninsulas. Some promising models have been developed, and improved practices and technologies adopted, yet municipalities and related organizations continue to face many barriers in implementing clean energy solutions. This renewal grant will enable the grantee to deepen and expand the assistance it provides to communities in its service areas to overcome such barriers and continue to be uniquely positioned to address needs and opportunities that arise.

title: General Purposes
description: Michigan Energy Options has nearly 40 years of experience in the energy efficiency and renewable energy sector and is the only clean energy nonprofit in the state with offices in both the upper and lower peninsulas. Municipalities and related organizations, such as municipally owned utilities, want to deploy more clean energy technology quicker than they currently are but have been slow to move in this direction due to a number of barriers. With general purpose funding, the grantee will help local governments and other stakeholders address such barriers, primarily in mid-Michigan and the Upper Peninsula.

title: Advocacy Training
description: This grant will support the Alliance for Justice in providing customized advocacy trainings and resources for the statewide afterschool networks. The trainings and resources will provide an opportunity to build the capacity of the statewide afterschool networks to advance the afterschool field.

title: Advocacy Training
description: This grant will support the Alliance for Justice in providing a customized, in-person advocacy training for the statewide afterschool networks. The training will provide an opportunity to build the capacity of the statewide afterschool networks to enhance the afterschool field.

title: Assets Evaluation and Data Collection Project
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This renewal grant will continue support for data collection and evaluation activities under the Education program’s Advancing Innovations objective. During the grant period, Brandeis University’s Institute on Assets and Social Policy will collect, analyze, and interpret data from organizations working to advance children’s savings accounts. Initial project activities will focus on establishing a baseline for assessing progress. Thereafter, the grantee will assist the Foundation with assessing progress and impact on an annual basis. Since 2008, Brandeis University has been an evaluation, learning, and documentation partner to the Foundation on asset-building and savings strategies.

title: Assets Evaluation and Data Collection Project
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant will support data collection and evaluation activities for the Success Beyond High School program area. Brandeis University will help the Foundation track progress under the assets objective, which focuses on integrating children’s savings accounts into postsecondary access and success initiatives, particularly those that aim to improve outcomes for low- and moderate-income students. Initial project activities will focus on collecting field data to establish the evaluation baseline. Thereafter, the grantee will help the Foundation assess progress and impact by outcomes on an annual basis. Brandeis University’s Institute on Assets and Social Policy is dedicated to the social mobility of individuals and families — particularly, those traditionally left out of the economic mainstream — and to the expansion of the middle class. Since 2008, Brandeis University has been an evaluation, learning, and documentation partner to the Foundation on asset-building and savings strategies.

title: Promise Early Distribution Scholarship Program
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: The Wabash County Promise Initiative is a community-wide initiative designed to advance educational attainment and create a generation of educated, engaged, and economically self-sufficient young people. This grant will help the Community Foundation of Wabash County to continue support for the early distribution scholarship pilot. This component—targeting students in the 4th, 6th, and 8th grades—models the use of children’s savings accounts as a tool to incentivize and reward college preparation and planning, as well as the achievement of academic milestones shown to promote college-going identities, high school graduation and postsecondary success. The pilot also models how community foundations can support children’s savings account initiatives, and demonstrate a promising alternative to traditional scholarships.

title: Promise Early Distribution Scholarship Program
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: The Wabash County Promise Initiative is a community wide initiative designed to help students build college-going identities and save money for college. As a component of the broader Wabash County Promise Initiative, Community Foundation of Wabash County will use Mott support to pilot an early distribution scholarship program. This pilot program will target students in the 4th, 6th, and 8th grades, and model the use of children’s savings accounts as a tool to incentivize and reward college planning, college savings, and achievement of the academic milestones shown to foster a college-going identity and lead to high school graduation and postsecondary success. This pilot will model how community foundations can support children’s savings account initiatives and demonstrate a promising alternative to traditional scholarships, managed by community foundations or other organizations.

title: Whiting Design and Equipment Procurement
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Whiting Auditorium was built in 1967 and has a legacy of providing world-class live entertainment to over 67,000 patrons annually. This grant to the Flint Cultural Center Foundation will assist The Whiting with an analysis of design development work related to capital improvements throughout the facility that will address technical and theatrical equipment needs. In addition, it will provide for upgrades to the lighting and sound systems within public areas of the venue.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to increase the understanding of global policy trends and their potential impact on civil society. The Carnegie Endowment for International Peace is a unique global network of policy research centers in the United States, Russia, China, Europe, the Middle East, and soon South Asia. Its mission is to advance the cause of peace through analysis and development of fresh policy ideas and direct engagement and collaboration with decisionmakers in government, business, and civil society. Its policy research centers bring the benefit of multiple national viewpoints to bilateral, regional, and global issues. Established in 1910 in Washington, D.C., with a gift from Andrew Carnegie, the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace is a private, nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing cooperation between nations and promoting active international engagement by the United States.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to increase individual giving to local nonprofits and civic initiatives in Turkey. The Support Foundation for Civil Society, a Turkish foundation established in December 2014, will develop its organizational and programmatic capacities to facilitate systematic giving and mentoring to nonprofits by individuals and corporations in Turkey and internationally. In 2016–2017, the grantee awarded 27 grants totaling approximately $120,000. Grants supported small, issue-based, community-level nonprofits across Turkey that demonstrated innovative programming and a vision for further organizational development. The grantee is based in Istanbul, Turkey.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to increase individual giving to local nonprofits and civic initiatives in Turkey. Support Foundation for Civil Society, a newly established Turkish foundation, will develop its organizational and programmatic capacities to facilitate systematic giving and mentoring to nonprofits by individuals in Turkey. The grantee was established in December 2014 by a group of emerging philanthropists and civil society activists interested in pooling their own funds and expertise to support Turkish civil society development. During the grant period, the grantee will make grants to support small, issue-based, community-level nonprofits across Turkey that have innovative programming and a vision for further organizational development. The grants will be funded by annual contributions from individual and corporate donors, and the grantee will grow the number of donors over the next two years. Some of the donors and other experts from the private sector will act as mentors to grantees. The grantee is based in Istanbul, Turkey.

title: Energy Access for the Poor: Bringing a Development and Community Rights Perspective to Influence the Power Africa Debate
description: Over the past five years, a number of initiatives have been launched to bring affordable, reliable electricity to over 600 million people living in Sub-Saharan Africa who have no access to electricity, including the U.S. Power Africa initiative. Many of these programs have tended to promote top-down, large-scale projects, which predominately use fossil fuel or are large-scale renewable energy projects that provide limited benefit for poor communities. Small-scale, off-grid renewable energy is a new model that is successfully providing energy for poor rural communities in developing countries. To ensure expanded financial support for such off-grid renewable energy projects, the American Jewish World Service will develop a coalition of international development organizations working to build stronger commitments from United States government agencies working on the U.S. Power Africa initiative.

title: General Purposes
description: The Land Trust Alliance, a national organization representing land trusts, is nearing completion of its first major fundraising campaign, Together: A Campaign for the Land. The campaign will provide the grantee the capacity it needs to assist in the creation of the policies, institutions, and leaders necessary to ensure the long-term success of the land trust movement. This general purpose grant will help the grantee to finish the campaign successfully.

title: Strengthening New Development Bank Safeguards
grantee: Pontifical Catholic University Rio de Janeiro
description: The BRICS Policy Center is a think tank dedicated to studying the structural shift occurring in international development finance as Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa (BRICS countries) emerge as prominent global actors. Administered by the Pontifical Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro, the Center developed a research program over the past project period to deepen international expertise and dialogue on social and environmental safeguards for development finance. During the current grant period, the Center will continue to research and analyze the role of new development finance actors and institutions, such as China and the BRICS New Development Bank, and build a knowledge database to monitor and publicize Chinese investment in Latin America and the implementation of social and environmental standards.

title: Strengthening New Development Bank Safeguards
grantee: Pontifical Catholic University Rio de Janeiro
description: The BRICS Policy Center is a think tank dedicated to studying the structural shift occurring in international development finance as Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa emerge as prominent global actors. Administered by the Pontifical Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro, the BRICS Policy Center seeks to establish a research program to cultivate international expertise and dialogue on social and environmental safeguards for development finance, with emphasis on the role of new development finance institutions. Project activities will include publishing four regular newsletters and up to 40 policy briefs.

title: Technical Support to Maximize Renewable Energy Access Success
grantee: Instituto de Energia e Meio Ambiente
description: The Instituto de Energia e Meio Ambiente is a national Brazilian think tank with expertise in energy planning, electrical engineering, and environmental law and policy. Over the previous grant period, the grantee studied pilot renewable energy projects in isolated communities and analyzed the public policy and institutional and economic structures that support the diesel-based model of electrical supply in the Amazon. The grantee will build on this knowledge over the next grant period to monitor changes in diesel use and greenhouse gas emissions and propose public policy and institutional structures to support an expansion of renewable energy solutions for isolated Amazon communities.

title: Technical Support to Maximize Renewable Energy Access Success
grantee: Instituto de Energia e Meio Ambiente
description: The Instituto de Energia e Meio Ambiente is a national Brazilian think tank with expertise in energy planning, electrical engineering, and environmental law and policy. This grant will provide support to the grantee to study the social, cultural, financial, and regulatory barriers to expansion and replication of renewable energy access for isolated communities. Pilot renewable energy access projects will be studied to ensure they are replicable on a large scale and prepared to be embedded in public policy and investment in Brazil and the Amazon.

title: Solar Energy for Amazon River Dwellers
grantee: Centro de Estudos Avançados de Promoção Social e Ambiental
description: The Centro de Estudos Avançados de Promoção Social e Ambiental is a nonprofit organization in the Amazon founded in 1985 to promote sustainable community development and Amazon forest conservation by improving public policies and quality of life of children, youth, indigenous peoples, and minorities. Over the past project period, the grantee’s Health and Happiness Project installed solar electricity and pumping systems in four communities and one forest research center in the Tapajos-Arapiuns Extractive Reserve and held solar workforce and operations and management trainings for members of the reserve. Over the next project period, the organization will expand its installation of solar systems; test small-scale biogas production; participate in design and implementation of a national renewable energy trade fair; conduct training; and monitor and collect data to publish results of its systems operation and management for replication.

title: Solar Energy for Amazon River Dwellers
grantee: Centro de Estudos Avançados de Promoção Social e Ambiental
description: The Centro de Estudos Avançados de Promoção Social e Ambiental is a nonprofit founded in 1985 to promote sustainable community development and Amazon forest conservation by improving public policies and quality of life of children, youth, indigenous peoples, and minorities. The absence of sufficient energy access remains a significant barrier to community development and quality of life in low impact extractive reserves in the Amazon. The grantee’s Health and Happiness Project will work with forest communities in the Tapajos-Arapiuns Extractive Reserve to implement self-managed and sustainable rural solar power for both productive and social uses.

title: Renewable Energy for Extractive Reserves in the Amazon
description: This project will support the World Wildlife Fund and its partner, World Wildlife Fund Brazil, to continue working with forest-dwelling communities living in sustainable development reserves in the Amazon to design and implement a renewable energy, microgeneration development model. This experience and key government agency partnerships are being built to develop a national public policy for distributed renewable electrification of low-impact economic activities for traditional forest communities in the Brazilian Amazon. World Wildlife Fund Brazil has been working on environmental conservation and sustainable development in the region since 1971.

title: Renewable Energy for Extractive Reserves in the Amazon
description: This project will support the World Wildlife Fund, as it partners with World Wildlife Fund Brazil, to work with forest dwelling communities living in extractive and sustainable development reserves in the Amazon to design and implement a renewable energy, micro-generation development model. The goal of this model is to provide renewable sources of electricity for forest-dwelling communities and their sustainable, low-impact forest activities, such as harvesting and processing seeds and fruit. World Wildlife Fund Brazil has been working on environmental conservation and sustainable development in the region since 1971.

title: Distributed Solar Energy for the Xingu Indigenous Park
description: Instituto Socioambiental implements sustainable and renewable energy systems for local communities in Brazil’s poorest and most isolated regions in the Amazon rainforest. This project proposes to implement a mini-grid energy system including renewable solar energy in the Xingu Indigenous Park that will serve the population of 6,000 indigenous people from 16 different ethnic groups, living in 80 small communities. Upon its completion, the project will be a reference model for distributed renewable energy generation in isolated communities in the Amazon.

title: Blue Accounting
geographic_focus: Wisconsin, Ohio, Indiana, Minnesota, New York, Pennsylvania, Michigan, Illinois
description: Great Lakes leaders and decisionmakers across the region lack a basinwide view of the progress being made toward large-scale, overarching desired outcomes. Consequently, they also lack the information they need to prioritize efforts and investments. The Nature Conservancy, an international conservation group with a strong presence in the Great Lakes region, will work with a range of partners to build an information management platform to collect, maintain, and deliver progress metrics and related information to Great Lakes leaders.

title: Nelson Mandela Children's Hospital
description: The Nelson Mandela Children’s Hospital Trust was established in 2009 to initiate, promote, and support the provision of pediatric healthcare, training, and research through the establishment of the Nelson Mandela Children’s Hospital. The vision of the Nelson Mandela Children’s Hospital is to be a state-of-the-art specialist pediatric academic tertiary referral hospital providing child-centered, best quality medical services to the children of southern Africa, irrespective of their social and economic status. Mott has previously supported the hospital project through a grant to the Nelson Mandela Children’s Fund to undertake a feasibility study on the establishment of the hospital. This grant will contribute to the construction costs of the hospital, expected to start operating fully at the end of 2016.

title: Chronic Student Absenteeism Initiative
description: This grant will support the Advertising Council, Inc., to develop and implement a public awareness campaign as part of a new national initiative to reduce chronic student absenteeism. The project will include a national public service announcement campaign focused on: 1) increasing school attendance and retention; 2) developing a Website and toolkit for constituents; and 3) creating an integrated public relations and social media program.

title: General Purposes
