description: Established in 2001, the Center for Civic & Cultural Initiatives “Tamarisk” works to build the capacity of community activists and civil society organizations in Ukraine. Drawing on its long experience of working with community activists and civil society organizations in Ukraine, the grantee will pursue work in three key areas to help consolidate the civic energy that emerged with Ukraine’s Maidan Revolution. The program goal is to strengthen and expand community-based approaches to development and integration in Ukraine. Its strategic priorities over the coming period will be threefold: to build the capacity of community activists and civil society organizations, to improve mechanisms for engagement of civil society organizations with local authorities in the context of extensive local government reforms, and to further model comprehensive local development programs bringing together varied community stakeholders. In 2016-2018, the grantee held three “School of Positive Change” sessions for over 90 civil society organizations. The grantee also played an active role in organizing a civic coalition to inform and adopt the regional strategy for development of civil society in the Dnipropetrovsk region with a confirmed four-year budget allocation.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen and expand community-based approaches to development and integration in Ukraine. Drawing on its long experience of working with community activists and civil society organizations in Ukraine, the Center for Civic & Cultural Initiatives “Tamarisk” will pursue work in three key areas to help consolidate the civic energy that emerged with Ukraine’s Maidan revolution. First, it will continue to build capacity of community activists and civil society organizations through its annual School of Positive Change and associated training programs and networking events. Second, through its Dialogue program, it will work systematically to link community activists with formal civic leaders through an intensive program of discussions and activities to identify and resolve local issues. Third, the grantee will pilot a program of cross-sectoral engagement in community development and decisionmaking in three communities. Established in 2001, the Center for Civic & Cultural Initiatives “Tamarisk” works to build capacity of community activists and civil society organizations in Ukraine.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to provide comprehensive support to internally displaced persons and others affected by conflict in Ukraine. Through a network of online and offline legal advice centers, Goreniye will provide primary and secondary legal assistance to displaced victims of conflict in four regions (Dnipropetrovsk, Zaporizhiye, Kharkov, and Ukraine-controlled Donetsk) bordering on the conflict zone that has received the bulk of such migrants. The grantee will provide training services for local officials to improve service delivery and integration practices related to target groups. They will also work to build the self-organizing capacity of these target groups. From 2016–2018, the grantee provided primary and secondary legal assistance to over 30,000 Ukrainians affected by conflict. They trained 240 lawyers from within the state legal aid system on issues related to conflict victims and initiated training of paralegals from within the ranks of its clients. Based in Dnipro, Goreniye was founded in 2005 to provide wide-ranging assistance to disadvantaged and marginalized groups throughout Ukraine.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to provide comprehensive support to internally displaced persons and others affected by conflict in Ukraine. Through a network of legal advice centers, Goreniye will provide primary and secondary legal assistance to displaced victims of conflict in four regions (Dnipropetrovsk, Zaporizhiye, Kharkov, and Ukraine-controlled Donetsk) bordering on the conflict zone that has received the bulk of such migrants. The grantee will also develop a center for distance consultations, allowing clients to seek advice from access points throughout the regions; provide a range of services through educational workshops and training activities aimed at identifying opportunities for beneficial economic and social integration; and provide targeted legal and social support services for demobilized combatants who have returned in large numbers to their communities with little state provision of social or psychological support services. Based in Pavlohrad, Goreniye was founded in 2005 to provide wide-ranging assistance to disadvantaged and marginalized groups throughout Ukraine.

title: Strengthening the Role of Communities in Managing Local Development in Ukraine
grantee: Association of Small Towns of Ukraine
description: The program goal is to promote community participation in decision making related to decentralization reforms in Ukraine. The Association of Small Towns of Ukraine will create an online resource of best practices for community participation in the context of territorial reforms across Ukraine. It will also foster and coordinate a network of territories that have emerged through the decentralization process to develop and further share best practices; and implement a media and outreach campaign for the nearly 1,000 communities that are undertaking the reform process to promote democratic practices in community governance. In 2016–2018, the grantee worked in six pilot regions to assist in introducing and embedding best practices in community participation in local governance, resulting in 43 documented strategies for such engagement and five replicable road maps for institutionalizing democratic governance. Established in 2010 to serve and promote the interests of small municipalities across Ukraine, the Association of Small Towns of Ukraine works to improve local administration as well as engagement of community organizations in local governance.

title: Strengthening the Role of Communities in Managing Local Development in Ukraine
grantee: Association of Small Towns of Ukraine
description: The program goal is to promote community participation in decisionmaking related to decentralization reforms in Ukraine. These reforms will see increasing authority devolved to the municipal level. The Association of Small Towns of Ukraine will work with municipal authorities and community leaders in six selected pilot towns in three regions to address three critical areas of participatory municipal governance: transparent budget processes, monitoring the quality of public services, and economic development. The grantee will conduct a series of training activities in these areas and will also organize a study visit to Poland to learn from an analogous process of territorial administrative reform implemented there. Established in 2010 to serve and promote the interests of small municipalities across Ukraine, the grantee works to improve local administration, engagement of community organizations in local governance, and the promotion of the needs of small towns to higher levels of government.

title: EU-Russia Civil Society Forum
description: The program goal is to support dialogue between European Union-based and Russian civil society actors. The program will seek to foster a vibrant civil society and encourage solidarity in the face of growing moves to limit the space for independent action across the continent. The EU-Russia Civil Society Forum, currently a project hosted by the German-Russian Exchange, will work toward three objectives. First, through workshops and urgent actions, it will foster regular dialogue and support solidarity activities among its members on topics of common interest. Second, through research, policy analysis, public briefings, and targeted conferences, it will seek to raise awareness of civil society perspectives on current challenges facing the respective societies. Finally, the forum will strengthen its own institutional capacity with a view to registering as a separate legal entity. The German-Russian Exchange was registered in 1992 and is the leading nongovernmental organization in Germany working with civil society groups in Eastern Europe.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to increase effective citizen participation at local and national levels in Bosnia and Herzegovina. With Mott’s general purpose support, the Center for Civic Cooperation will build on its 20 years of experience to improve mechanisms for local level civic engagement in decisionmaking, increase awareness and protection of rights, build the capacity of local nonprofits, and strengthen its own organizational capacities. Established in 1996, the grantee has helped to rebuild communities in the aftermath of the war, assisted refugees and displaced people to return to their homes, provided educational and training programs to strengthen human rights and democratic practices in local communities, established an independent radio station covering southwest Bosnia, acted as a resource center for local nonprofits and citizen initiatives, and monitored and reported on the work of local government. The grantee is based in Livno, Bosnia and Herzegovina.

title: Community Acceptance of Wind
description: The University of Michigan’s Center for Local, State, and Urban Policy conducts, supports, and fosters applied academic research that informs local, state, and urban policy issues. This project will study existing wind farms in Michigan in order to identify local policies and practices that maximize community acceptance of wind development, as well as provide Michigan communities and individuals information on the potential pros and cons of developing wind energy in their community.

title: Service as a Strategy
description: This grant will enable the Points of Light Foundation to engage leaders in the education and national and community service fields to examine ways to scale service as a strategy in Flint and across the country. The grantee will: 1) develop shareable resources on national service; 2) coordinate a convening on citizen engagement; 3) prepare a report on citizen engagement; and 4) provide resources and technical assistance.

title: Connecting Freshwater Leaders Beyond the Great Lakes
grantee: The Board of Trustees of the University of Illinois
description: Chicago is the largest Great Lakes city on the U.S. side of the border and is home to many regional and national environmental organizations with programs focused on protecting and restoring the Great Lakes. These organizations have few connections with the low-income neighborhoods bordering certain lakefront and riverfront areas. The University of Illinois-Chicago’s Freshwater Lab recruits students from these communities and helps connect them to freshwater organizations based in the downtown area. With Mott support, the grantee will help its students build real-world skills related to freshwater policy, collaborate with community-based organizations to address Great Lakes challenges, and connect freshwater organizations with a new pipeline of talent. The grantee will also expand its successful educational model to at least three other higher education institutions across the region.

title: Healthy Great Lakes Program
description: The Canadian Environmental Law Association is a legal aid clinic that has worked for the past 50 years to protect human health and the environment by seeking justice for those harmed by pollution and by working to change policies. With previous support, the grantee launched the Healthy Great Lakes program to engage a broad network of individuals and organizations in shaping and making use of laws and policies that aim at the protection and restoration of the waters of the Great Lakes – St. Lawrence River Basin. The grantee has held online and in-person sessions to connect with a broad network of individuals and groups, organized and held two summits, planned projects and activities, and influenced government decisions to protect the Great Lakes. With renewed support, the grantee will refine the goals of the program to reflect their new strategic plan, lessons learned, and respond to changing policies stemming from the election of a new government in Ontario. The grantee will focus on safeguarding drinking water, preventing water pollution, wise management and use of water, integrated watershed management, and fish health. As a one-time addition to its work in the first year, the grantee will explore partnerships and cost-out an engagement organizing action plan and implementation strategy that targets young Canadians and encourages them to become more active in Great Lakes issues.

title: Great Lakes Program
description: Established in 1970, the Canadian Environmental Law Association is a nonprofit organization that provides legal assistance to individuals and communities and also conducts environmental policy research and analysis. With Mott’s support, the grantee will build its capacity to engage on Great Lakes freshwater policies. Over the next two years, the grantee will conduct policy analyses and engage in public processes to guide the Province of Ontario’s implementation of its freshwater programs. The grantee will also work closely with other nonprofits, government officials, First Nations representatives, businesses, agriculture representatives, and other Great Lakes stakeholders to increase public support for strong Great Lakes protections in Canada.

title: Water Project
description: The City of Flint, under emergency financial management, disconnected from the Detroit water system and began treating and utilizing water from the Flint River approximately 18 months ago as a short-term solution until the city could connect to the new Karegnondi Water Authority pipeline. Unfortunately, while utilizing Flint River water, high levels of lead have been identified in the water. Due to health concerns, it is necessary that the City of Flint switch back to Detroit water until the Karegnondi Water Authority pipeline is completed in mid-2016. Grant funds, along with funds from the City of Flint and the State of Michigan, will be used to pay the additional cost of purchasing Detroit water for the residents of Flint.

title: Every Hour Counts
description: This grant will support ExpandED Schools to develop a common measurement framework for afterschool programs to track children and youth across a range of youth outcomes, including academic, as well as social and emotional skills such as creative thinking, teamwork, self-regulation, and work ethic. The grantee will work with afterschool leaders and statewide afterschool networks to: 1) implement common youth outcome measures; 2) build capacity of participating cities and states to measure youth outcomes; and 3) inform policy and practice through national dissemination of lessons learned aimed at building understanding among leaders in the education, out-of-school time, and other relevant fields.

title: Mayors' Report Card on Education
description: This grant will support the development and release of the 2016 Mayors’ Report Card on Education to increase access to educational and afterschool opportunities for youth. This project will include: 1) the development of an online, interactive report on education information in 100 cities; and 2) the development of research-based practices such as college and workforce readiness to be shared across cities and states. The George W. Bush Institute at the George W. Bush Foundation will work with the statewide afterschool networks and local leaders to share information and best practices from the report.

title: 21st Century Community Learning Centers and Literary Skills
description: This grant will support the American Institutes for Research to partner with the Massachusetts Department of Elementary and Secondary Education, the Minnesota Department of Education, and the National Institute on Out-of-School Time at Wellesley College to complete a study that explores how high quality afterschool programs can promote literacy development for elementary school children. This study will also explore the role that social and emotional learning may play in supporting the development of literacy-related skills.

title: General Purposes
description: Flint Riverkeeper was founded in 2008 by a diverse group of Georgians with the mission of restoring and preserving the habitat, water quality, and flow of the Flint River for the benefit of current and future generations and dependent wildlife. With prior Mott support, the grantee has worked to promote policy reforms that improve the management of river flows in the Flint system; establish a comprehensive land conservation plan for the watershed as a means to restore flows; and build the local constituency necessary to make such progress. With renewed support, the grantee will undertake similar efforts to improve flow restoration while continuing to develop new relationships and build organizational capacity.

title: General Purposes
description: Flint Riverkeeper was founded in 2008 by a diverse group of Georgians with the mission of restoring and preserving the habitat, water quality, and flow of the Flint River for the benefit of current and future generations and dependent wildlife. Throughout the Flint River watershed, natural river flow patterns have been dramatically altered by a number of factors, including poorly planned land development, excessive withdrawals, and inefficient water use. Over the next two years, the grantee will promote policy reforms that improve the management of river flows in the Flint watershed; establish a comprehensive land conservation plan for the watershed as a means to restore flows; and build the local constituency necessary to make such progress.

title: Lower Flint River Project
description: The ecological health of Georgia’s Flint River, part of the larger Apalachicola-Chattahoochee- Flint River basin, is under stress due to a range of issues including chronic drought and poorly coordinated water use. The Nature Conservancy, a global conservation organization with a strong presence in Georgia, has been working in the lower segment of the Flint River to improve irrigation efficiency as a means to sustain the river’s natural flow. With this grant, the grantee will evaluate the impact of its work to date and identify new conservation strategies that may help further improve natural river flows.

title: New Approach to Water Management in Georgia
description: The Chattahoochee Riverkeeper, a longtime Mott grantee, will help lead an effort to develop a suite of solutions to the water supply challenges across the state of Georgia. The grantee will work with partner organizations in the Georgia Water Coalition to conduct various case studies on municipal, industrial, and agricultural water use, and build new relationships with agricultural and industrial stakeholders to develop a comprehensive set of water management policy recommendations. With Mott funds, the grantee will also help expand the core capacity of the coalition so that it can continue to conduct important network functions.

title: Community Energy Management in Southeast Michigan
description: Based in southeast Michigan, EcoWorks is working to drive down municipal utility costs and encourage communitywide energy initiatives. The technical expertise and services it provides to municipalities in the region is important given the ongoing lack of technical expertise, limited staff time, and fiscal constraints faced by many municipalities. With prior Mott support, the grantee and partner organizations expanded energy management services to approximately 30 mid-sized cities in southeast Michigan. With continued support, the grantee will build on the energy management planning progress that was achieved by the participating municipalities and focus on implementation of the clean energy projects identified.

title: Community Energy Management in Southeast Michigan
description: Many municipalities in Michigan lack the technical expertise or staff time to drive down their utility costs through conservation, let alone lead communitywide energy initiatives. As a result, important opportunities to deal with municipal budget shortfalls while simultaneously addressing climate change are lost. Based in southeast Michigan, EcoWorks offers a full package of energy management technical expertise to municipalities in the region. With this grant, the grantee and partner organizations will expand energy management services to approximately 30 midsized cities in southeast Michigan.

title: Advancing Climate Solutions in Traverse City
description: Traverse City has emerged as a clean energy leader across the state of Michigan with the adoption by its city commissioners in December 2016 of a target of 100 percent renewable electricity for municipal operations by 2020, carbon neutrality (i.e., a net zero carbon footprint) by midcentury, and the formation of a stakeholder advisory Green Team. Even with this forward-thinking approach, local governments in the Traverse City area lack the capacity to fully implement clean energy solutions and take advantage of available programs and benefits. Renewal support will allow SEEDS to build on its strong technical background and established convener role to provide energy management services to the city and county governments, including the municipally owned utility, toward reaching established targets and goals.

title: Advancing Climate Solutions in Traverse City
description: Like many municipalities in Michigan, local governments in the Traverse City area lack the capacity to fully implement clean energy solutions. Without the benefit of a dedicated energy manager, municipalities are often not in a position to take advantage of available programs and benefits that come from a strategic and consistent focus on energy efficiency practices and renewable technologies. With this grant, SEEDS, a local nonprofit, will utilize its strong technical background and established role as a convener to provide energy management services to the city and county governments, including the municipally owned utility.

title: Midwest Children's Savings Account Initiative
grantee: Heartland Alliance for Human Needs & Human Rights
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
geographic_focus: Illinois, Michigan, Indiana, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Ohio
description: This grant will enable Heartland Alliance for Human Needs & Human Rights to operate as a regional coordinator, supporting organizations working to advance state and local children’s savings account policies and initiatives across the Great Lakes states. Funding will support several activities, including facilitating research and strategic communications projects; creating peer learning and networking opportunities for advocates and policymakers interested in children’s savings accounts; organizing and educating policymakers and other children’s savings account stakeholders; and providing technical assistance to practitioners and program administrators designing and/or implementing children’s savings account initiatives. Headquartered in Chicago, Heartland Alliance for Human Needs & Human Rights is a comprehensive antipoverty organization that provides a comprehensive array of services in the areas of health, housing, and jobs, and leads state and national policy efforts which promote permanent solutions and lasting change for individuals and society.

title: Children's Savings Account Strategies for Community Foundations
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: The overall goal of this project is to encourage community foundations to promote and adopt programs and policies that help low-income families increase income and build assets. To this end, CFLeads will convene six to eight community foundation teams that will work together for two years to learn about and begin implementing specific family economic security strategies, including children’s savings accounts. Mott funding will support meetings and conferences, individual and group technical assistance, and dissemination of written deliverables. CFLeads is a national learning cooperative that advocates for and advances the practice of community leadership among community foundations.

title: Sustainable Energy for All
description: The United Nations Foundation was established in 1988 to support the goals and objectives of the United Nations. Sustainable Energy for All was set up as a United Nations initiative to promote and directly support new collaborations to address the challenges of expanding energy access, increasing energy efficiency, and growing renewable energy. Through this project, a coordinated global effort is being established to achieve the goal of universal energy access by mobilizing leaders and building effective coalitions and partnerships to fast track action and close financing gaps.

title: Sustainable Energy for All
description: The United Nations Foundation was established in 1988 in order to support the goals and objectives of the United Nations. Sustainable Energy for All was set up as a United Nations initiative to promote and directly support new collaborations to address the challenges of energy access, energy efficiency, and renewable energy. Through this project, a coordinated global effort will be established to achieve the goal of universal energy access by mobilizing leaders and building effective coalitions and partnerships to fast track action and efficiently close financing gaps.

title: Energy Change Lab Tanzania
description: Hivos is an international development organization, founded in 1968, that partners with civil society organizations in developing countries to seek new solutions to persistent global issues. With previous Mott support, the grantee has developed the Energy Change Lab Tanzania to support efforts that build future leaders and entrepreneurs to work in the Tanzanian off-grid energy sector. This grant increase, and associated grant period extension, will allow Hivos to assess the work of the Energy Change Lab over the past two years and determine the direction of its efforts to promote off-grid energy in rural Tanzania.

title: Energy Change Lab Tanzania
description: Hivos is an international development organization, founded in 1968, that partners with civil society organizations in developing countries in order to seek new solutions to persistent global issues. Under this grant, the grantee will develop the Energy Change Lab Tanzania in order to support efforts that build future leaders and entrepreneurs to work in the Tanzanian off-grid energy sector. This grant will focus on developing entrepreneurial capacity for off-grid renewable energy solutions in rural Tanzania and creating opportunities for livelihoods from the electricity provided.

title: Platform for Energy Access Knowledge
description: Katalytix provides technical communications services to support a clean energy future. The grantee has worked with public- and private-sector entities, as well as nongovernmental organizations, to develop media and public awareness campaigns. The grantee will lead this work creating the Platform for Energy Access Knowledge. Katalytix, doing business as Power for All, will work in tandem with the University of California Berkeley to develop research tools to help synthesize and cross-reference existing data on decentralized renewable energy policies and practices globally.

title: Towards Universal Energy Access
description: The United Nations Foundation was established in 1988 in order to support the goals and objectives of the United Nations. The grantee has been actively engaged in the efforts to provide electricity for poor rural communities in developing countries through the Energy Access Practitioner Network and the Mini-Grids Partnership. Through its efforts over the past two years, the grantee has helped to unify the distributed energy access sector; accelerate learning and development of the sector; and raise the profile of distributed energy on the global agenda. Over the next year, the grantee will continue to accelerate the deployment of clean energy mini-grids in developing countries, share knowledge among network members, and reassess their role in supporting the energy access sector.

title: Towards Universal Energy Access
description: The United Nations Foundation was established in 1988 in order to support the goals and objectives of the United Nations. The grantee has been actively engaged in the efforts to provide electricity for poor rural communities in developing countries through the establishment of the Energy Access Practitioner Network. Previous support funded a directory of investment and funding opportunities for companies involved in the Energy Access Practitioner Network. Over the next two years, the grantee will continue to accelerate the deployment of clean energy minigrids in developing countries, share knowledge among network members, and develop member-financing partnerships.

title: Development of Tanzanian Renewable Energy Micro-grids for Rural Communities
description: The Tanzanian Traditional Energy Development Organization is a nongovernmental organization working on sustainable energy development, based in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. For the past decade, it has been actively involved in implementing renewable energy and energy efficiency projects and programs in rural Tanzania. This project will contribute to the efforts to increase access to electricity from renewable energy mini-grids in rural Tanzania. The focus will be on raising awareness nationally and in selected districts in eastern Tanzania on the opportunities for mini-grid development and energy efficiency improvements.

title: Raising Michiganders' Standard of Living Project
description: This grant will provide two years of support for Michigan Future, Inc., and its Raising Michiganders’ Standard of Living project. The grantee’s overarching goal is to provide Michigan leaders with ideas on how to better position the state for success in an increasingly knowledge-driven economy. To develop and communicate this agenda, Michigan Future, Inc., will continue to build on its talent and educational framework as well as construct a detailed policy agenda. The grantee has assembled a team of experts to execute research and will create an advisory group of specialists and funders to provide guidance on policy development.

title: Innovation Conference for Community Foundations
description: The program goal is to help build the community leadership capacity of community foundations. Silicon Valley Community Foundation will host a first-ever Innovation Conference in October 2016. The aim of the conference is to provide a platform where community foundations can learn not only about how fast-paced technological change will affect the lives of their communities, but also how community foundations can position themselves to help maximize opportunities and minimize hardships that new technologies will bring. The grantee was created in 2006 as the result of a merger between the Peninsula Community Foundation and Community Foundation of Silicon Valley. It is currently the largest community foundation in the world, with over $6 billion in assets.

title: Metro Flint YouthBuild Program
description: This grant will provide gap funding for Metro Community Development’s Flint YouthBuild Program and promote economic and social recovery from the Flint water crisis by expanding educational, career, and life opportunities for Flint area youth. The program offers disadvantaged Genesee County residents, ages 18-24, education, job training, and employment services. In addition, Metro Flint YouthBuild provides young adults with academic support to obtain their GED and develops job readiness skills focused on the construction trades.

title: Framework for Aligning Teaching and Learning
description: This grant increase will provide support to the Flint Community Schools to implement a model of instruction to help refine and supplement teachers’ instructional skills to meet rigorous academic standards and develop principals’ skills to support teacher instruction, which has become even more important with the issues surrounding the city’s water system. The model focuses on essential classroom strategies for achieving rigor, standards-based planning, data reflection and action, collaboration, and creating optimal conditions for learning.

title: Framework for Aligning Teaching and Learning
description: This renewal grant will provide support to Flint Community Schools to continue the implementation of a model to help refine and supplement teacher instructional skills to meet rigorous academic standards and develop principals’ skills to support teachers in the classrooms. The model focuses on essential classroom strategies for achieving rigor, standards-based planning, data reflection and action, collaboration, and setting optimal conditions for learning.

title: Framework for Aligning Teaching and Learning
description: This grant will provide support to the Flint Community Schools to implement a model of instruction to help refine and supplement teacher instructional skills to meet rigorous academic standards and develop principals’ skills to support teacher instruction. The model focuses on essential classroom strategies for achieving rigor, standards-based planning, data reflection and action, collaboration, and setting optimal conditions for learning.

title: Georgia Sustainable Water Management Outreach Program
description: The Institute for Georgia Environmental Leadership is a network of diverse statewide leaders consistently collaborating to solve Georgia’s environmental challenges. A nonprofit organization, the grantee has developed a public policy education program related to water supply and conservation to address the existing conflicts over water sharing and management of water resources throughout the state of Georgia. This grant will enable the grantee to convene leaders and stakeholders from across the state to raise awareness of water supply issues and build support for resolving the water use conflicts in the state.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to build the capacity for effective community, national, and regional responses to the massive influx of refugees and migrants to the Western Balkans and Europe. To this end, Group 484 will cooperate with the Serbian government, international aid agencies, and other local nonprofits to provide humanitarian and other assistance to refugees transiting through Serbia; develop and implement local-level programming that empowers and engages young people in building an open and inclusive society; and engage with peer organizations at the national and European levels to promote better policies and practices related to refugees and migration. With 20 years experience in the field, the grantee is one of the leading nonprofits in the Western Balkans working on refugee and migration issues. During the grant period, the grantee will also focus on building its organizational capacities for research, advocacy, and outreach and strengthen its European-level partnerships and networking. Established in 1996, Group 484 is based in Belgrade.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to build the capacity for effective community, national, and regional responses to the massive influx of refugees and migrants to the Western Balkans and Europe. To this end, Group 484 will cooperate with the Serbian government, international aid agencies, and other local nonprofits to provide humanitarian and other assistance to refugees passing through Serbia; develop and implement local-level programming that empowers and engages young people in building an open and inclusive society; and engage with peer organizations at the national and European levels to promote better policies and practices related to refugees and migration. With 20 years’ experience in the field, the grantee is one of the leading nonprofits in the Western Balkans working on refugee and migration issues. During the grant period, the grantee will also focus on building its organizational capacities for research, advocacy, and outreach and strengthen its European-level partnerships and networking. The grantee was established in 1996 and is based in Belgrade.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to build the organizational and programmatic capacities of the Ana and Vlade Divac Foundation to address the economic and social development needs of poor and marginalized groups in Serbia, including refugees and migrants. During the next two years, the grantee will pursue a range of goals including leveraging financial support for large-scale humanitarian responses to the ongoing migration crisis in the Western Balkans; supporting the long-term economic empowerment of refugees and migrants, young people, and other marginalized groups in Serbia; increasing youth engagement in decisionmaking and community development; stimulating philanthropy in Serbia; and developing a strategy for building and managing its endowment. Prior support allowed the grantee to significantly increase its programmatic activities; expand its staff; and launch new youth programs, including the first local, youth-led grantmaking funds in Serbia. The grantee was established in 2007 and is based in Belgrade, Serbia.

title: Consultative Process for the National Endowment for Community Foundations in Romania
description: The project goal is to prepare the groundwork for the establishment of a national endowment fund for community foundations in Romania. The Romanian-American Foundation will increase the knowledge and understanding about the process of raising, managing, and using endowment funds among all interested stakeholders, including community foundations, support organizations, donors, and public institutions; strengthen the strategic communications and fundraising skills of community foundations and support organizations; support community foundations to carry out feasibility studies for their endowment building initiatives; and research the legal and fiscal conditions for the establishment of the national fund and create the necessary legal agreements and infrastructure for the fund. The grantee was established in 2009 with the mission to promote the development of a sustainable market economy and pluralistic democracy in Romania and has awarded more than 80 grants totaling over $12 million. The grantee is registered in the United States and operates out of its office in Bucharest, Romania.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen philanthropy and encourage civic participation in Kosovo by supporting the programmatic and organizational development of the Forum for Civic Initiatives, an indigenous grantmaking organization based in Pristina, Kosovo. During the next three years, the grantee will aim to distribute more than 160 grants totaling approximately $545,000 to community-based nonprofits in Kosovo. The grantee will also facilitate multisector community dialogue on key issues of sustainable development, provide networking and training opportunities to its grantees and other community-based nonprofits, and promote philanthropy at local and national levels. During the grant period, the grantee will pay particular attention to building its organizational capacities and sustainability through staff training, regional networking, long-term financial planning, and diversification of its funding base. The grantee is a member of the South-East-Europe Indigenous Grantmakers Network, which includes grantmakers in Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, and Montenegro.

title: Funders' Initiative for Civil Society
description: The program goal is to enable donors to provide system leadership and practical support for civil society actors addressing the global trend of closing space for civil society. The Funders’ Initiative for Civil Society, a project of Global Dialogue, provides stakeholders with research, information, and support to coordinate and align their grants and strategies. To date, the initiative has produced 12 publications, held sessions at 14 philanthropy sector events, organized a standalone conference for 70 funders, and has hosted webinars and produced research for groups of funders focused on various issues such as humanitarian action, digital rights, and transparency. In the coming year, the initiative will conduct a review involving research and consultation to assess how philanthropy can more effectively provide resources to civil society in the face of current and future threats. The initiative is a collaborative program managed by the grantee and directly involves a range of private funders—the Ariadne network, the International Human Rights Funders Group, and the European Foundation Centre. Founded in the United Kingdom in 2006, Global Dialogue implements programs supporting human rights, social change, and funder collaboration around the world.

title: Funders' Initiative for Civil Society
description: The program goal is to enable donors to provide system leadership and practical support for civil society actors addressing the global trend of closing space for civil society. Specifically, Global Dialogue, through its funder network called Ariadne, will coordinate the Funders’ Initiative for Civil Society in order to provide stakeholders with research, information, and support to coordinate and align their grants and strategies. The initiative will seek to become a point of contact between governments, regional and multilateral institutions, and philanthropic donors to advocate for civil society. Additionally, it will act as an urgent warning system for civil society organizations, human rights defenders, and funders facing growing threats to the space in which they operate. The initiative is a collaborative program managed by the grantee and directly involving a range of private funders, the Ariadne network, the International Human Rights Funders Group, and the European Foundation Centre. Founded in the United Kingdom in 2006, Global Dialogue implements programs supporting human rights and social change and funder collaboration around the world.

title: Introducing Venture Philanthropy in Central and Eastern Europe
description: The project goal is to promote and develop venture philanthropy and social entrepreneurship in Central and Eastern Europe. To this end, the European Venture Philanthropy Association will increase the knowledge and understanding of the various forms of venture philanthropy in the region; support the development of pilot venture philanthropy funds in Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Czech Republic, and Serbia; and explore opportunities to create venture philanthropy funds in cooperation with local philanthropists in other countries in the region. In addition, during the grant period, the grantee will seek additional funding for future expansion of the project. The grantee was established in 2004 and today has 214 members in 29 countries, which include social investors, private equity firms, foundations, consultancy companies, academic institutions, and financial institutions. The grantee is based in Brussels, Belgium.

title: Introducing Venture Philanthropy in Central and Eastern Europe
description: The project goal is to promote and develop venture philanthropy and social entrepreneurship in the Central and Eastern Europe region. To this end, the European Venture Philanthropy Association will increase the knowledge and understanding of the various forms of venture philanthropy in the region and explore opportunities to create venture philanthropy funds in cooperation with local philanthropists in the CEE region. In addition, during the grant period, the grantee will seek additional funding for future expansion of the project. The grantee was established in 2004 and today has 214 members in 29 countries, which include social investors, private equity firms, foundations, consultancy companies, academic institutions, and financial institutions. The grantee provides online and offline services to its members, including information, training, and networking opportunities. In addition, the grantee promotes good practice in venture philanthropy and engages policymakers in discussions on issues relevant to philanthropy and social impact investment. The grantee is based in Brussels, Belgium.

title: Real Estate Consulting
description: The purpose of this grant is to provide the YWCA of Greater Flint with consulting services that will assist it in relocation and renovation planning, environmental assessment, title work, legal fees, and other building holding costs. The grantee’s strategic plan, completed in 2015, identified the need to move to a smaller, more manageable space that will accommodate its programming more effectively and efficiently. The new, smaller facility will allow the grantee more flexibility for its core programming, including domestic violence and sexual assault services, and emergency shelter facilities.

title: Real Estate Consulting
description: The purpose of this grant is to provide the YWCA of Greater Flint with consulting services that will assist it in relocating. As the grantee continues to move through a strategic planning process, it has identified the need to move to a smaller, more manageable space that will accommodate its programming more efficiently and effectively. This grant will assist the grantee with managing its relocation, including identifying space needs and overseeing necessary renovations, as well as the disposition of its existing building.

title: School Success Mentor Program
description: This project will support Johns Hopkins University School of Education’s Everyone Graduates Center to launch and establish a data-driven, evidence-based mentoring program as part of a new national initiative to reduce chronic student absenteeism. This project will include: 1) launching the School Success Mentor Program in 30 communities across the nation; 2) developing a national infrastructure to provide leadership and technical assistance for the program; and 3) working to connect the School Success Mentor Program with existing afterschool initiatives.

title: Data Office
description: This grant will provide support to Flint Community Schools to hire personnel to staff a newly formed district data office, and will build the district’s capacity to provide the high quality educational programming and enrichment activities needed to bolster children against the negative effects of lead exposure. Establishing and staffing the data office will provide the district with the capability to support data-driven decisionmaking regarding student academics and district operations; help with the assessment and evaluation of programs and initiatives at the district; and maintain compliance with local, state, and federal grant requirements.

title: Life Sciences Market Needs Study
description: This grant will enable the Genesys Health Foundation to complete a market needs study to determine how a prospective life sciences business accelerator located in Genesee County can best meet demand for research and innovation in healthcare delivery. The grantee oversees charitable gifts and grants for Genesys Health System and Genesys Regional Medical Center in order to address community healthcare needs and improve access to healthcare services for those who are underserved. An accelerator would provide the basis for development of a regional life sciences industry cluster, which would create new jobs within Genesee County and help to diversify the area’s economy.

title: Flint Anchor Institutions Clean Energy Initiative
description: Founded in 2005, the Clean Energy Coalition is a nonprofit organization dedicated to promoting clean energy technologies as a way to create healthier, energy-independent communities. The grantee assists communities with developing energy efficiency, renewable energy, and clean vehicle projects. With Mott’s support, the grantee will convene anchor institutions, such as hospitals and higher education institutions in Flint, to explore ways to jointly pursue the adoption of clean energy technologies.

title: Energy Efficiency in Michigan
description: Elevate Energy is a nonprofit organization that designs and implements energy efficiency programs that lower costs, protect the environment, and ensure the benefits of energy efficiency reach those who need them most. With Mott’s support, the grantee will research two markets in Michigan that could benefit from more energy efficiency than they already do: low-income residential buildings and their residents, and nonprofit institutions.

title: Strengthening Dam Standards and Protecting Rivers
description: This project grant supports staff working on global and Andes-Amazon hydroelectric power development and finance and strengthens International Rivers’ work on international financial institutions, such as the World Bank Group, and national institutions, such as the Brazilian Development Bank. With this grant increase, International Rivers will partner with local community advocates to promote renewable energy alternatives to hydropower development.

title: Strengthening Dam Standards and Protecting Rivers
description: With offices in South America, Asia, Africa, and the United States, International Rivers is one of the most effective international, nongovernmental organizations working on river protection. By partnering with local communities in more than 40 countries, the grantee successfully promotes sustainable uses of freshwater systems around the world. Additionally, it plays a major role in international efforts to strengthen policies at public financial institutions. During the previous grant period, the grantee provided important information on the impacts of hydroelectric energy development during the World Bank safeguards review and during consideration of major large-scale hydroelectric development in the Greater Amazon Rainforest. This grant will support staff working on Andes-Amazon energy finance and development to strengthen social and environmental standards and promote sustainable solutions for river protection.

title: Strengthening Dam Standards and Protecting Rivers
description: With offices in South America, Asia, Africa, and the United States, International Rivers is one of the most effective international, nongovernmental organizations working on river protection. By partnering with local communities in more than 40 countries, the grantee is widely successful in promoting sustainable uses of fresh water around the world. Additionally, the grantee plays a major role in international efforts to reform the policies of public financial institutions. This project grant will support staff working on global and Andes-Amazon policy and ultimately will strengthen its work on international financial institutions, such as the World Bank Group, and national institutions, such as the Brazilian Development Bank.

title: Change the Course
description: The Bonneville Environmental Foundation, founded in 1998, is a nonprofit organization that works with the private sector to address environmental challenges. With Mott’s support, the grantee will expand its Change the Course program to the state of Georgia, which will engage the public and the business community in water scarcity issues. The grantee will also develop a book project that reinforces the Change the Course mission of expanding water education and awareness.

title: Flint Institute of Arts Glass Studio and Gallery
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant increase will provide additional support for the development and construction of a hot glass studio and gallery space located at the Flint Institute of Arts on the Flint cultural center campus. This new space will add 17,000 square feet to the Flint Institute of Arts’ building and will include stadium seating for 70-100 people. Annually, around 150,000 children and adults visit the galleries, participate in education programs, take art classes, or attend events held at the art institute. This glass studio and gallery will provide patrons a variety of new experiences and is unique in the community. The Flint Cultural Center Corporation, the supported organization of the Flint Cultural Center Foundation, owns and maintains the 33-acre cultural center campus.

title: Flint Institute of Arts Glass Studio and Gallery
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant increase will provide additional support for the development and construction of a hot glass studio and gallery space located at the Flint Institute of Arts on the Flint Cultural Center Campus. This new space will add 17,000 square feet and will include stadium seating for 70-100 people. Annually, around 150,000 children and adults visit the galleries, participate in education programs, take art classes, or attend events held at the art institute. This glass studio and gallery will provide patrons a variety of new experiences and is unique in the community. The Flint Cultural Center Corporation, the supported organization of the Flint Cultural Center Foundation, owns and maintains the 33-acre cultural center campus.

title: Flint Institute of Arts Glass Studio and Gallery
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: Founded in 1928 as an art school, the Flint Institute of Arts is currently located in the DeWaters Art Center building on the Flint Cultural Center campus. Improvements over the last decade, including the addition of new galleries, upgrades to the Art School kiln and studio space, expanded public areas, and ongoing enhancements to visitor amenities have allowed the art institute to continue to engage patrons and attract new audiences. Annually, around 150,000 children and adults visit the galleries, participate in education programs, take art classes, or attend events held at the art institute. The Flint Cultural Center Corporation, the supported organization of the Flint Cultural Center Foundation, owns and maintains the 33-acre cultural center campus. This grant will support the construction of a hot glass studio and gallery space to display glass and ceramic art work.

title: Design a Library for the Future
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide support to the Flint Public Library for consulting services to design and develop fundraising strategies for building renovations and upgrades. Modifications to the existing facility will enable the library to increase energy efficiency, enhance accessibility, and upgrade program space for 21st century needs and uses.

title: Feasibility Study for a Community Advice Office Centre of Excellence
grantee: National Alliance for the Development of Community Advice Offices
description: The National Alliance for the Development of Community Advice Offices is committed to the long-term sustainability of community advice offices as a way of ensuring access to justice within poor and marginalized communities in South Africa. Over the last ten years, the grantee has worked to institutionalize community advice offices as part of the wider justice network to ensure that poor people access their rights. This grant will assist with conducting a feasibility study for the establishment of an African Centre of Excellence for community advice offices that would focus on activities such as research and knowledge production and education and training, among others. The grantee will collaborate with civil society organizations in various parts of the African continent in conducting the feasibility study to ensure that the proposed center would meet their needs.

title: Connecting U.S. and Ibero-American Community Foundations with Puerto Rico
geographic_focus: Portugal, Brazil, United States, Mexico, Puerto Rico, Uruguay, Spain
description: The Puerto Rico Community Foundation will host a five-day event that will create and strengthen connections among community foundations from the United States, Puerto Rico, and Ibero-America. CFLeads board members from the United States will conduct a two-day site visit to get a firsthand understanding of the economic and fiscal crisis in Puerto Rico. On the third day, they will join their counterparts from the Ibero-American Network of Community Foundations to explore ways to create access and opportunities to quality education, health, economic development, arts, and other social resources. This will be followed by a joint meeting of the Ibero-American Community Foundation Network and members of the Puerto Rico Network of Foundations. The entire event will be part of the grantee’s 30th anniversary celebration. Founded in 1985, the mission of the Puerto Rico Community Foundation is to develop the potential of communities in Puerto Rico to achieve social and economic transformation.

title: Strengthening BNDES Accountability
description: Conectas is a Brazilian nongovernmental agency founded in 2001, working on strengthening social and environmental protections around development finance in Latin America, Asia, and Africa. Over the past project period, the grantee made important advances on transparency and dialogue with the Brazilian Development Bank and New Development Bank to advance environmental and social governance. Over the next project period, the grantee will build upon its work to strengthen governance standards and social and environmental policies of these development finance institutions to improve the sustainability of energy and infrastructure development in South America.

title: Strengthening BNDES Accountability
description: Conectas is a Brazilian nongovernmental agency founded in 2001, working on strengthening social and environmental protections in Latin America, Asia, and Africa. One important result of the grantee’s work has been the development of guidelines detailing rules and standards of transparency, accountability, and social-environmental impact assessment mechanisms of the Brazilian Development Bank. The grantee aims to enhance the governance standards and social and environmental policies of the Brazilian Development Bank, in order to guarantee that its energy and infrastructure investments are ecologically and socially sustainable.

title: Water Quality Transparency
description: This grant will allow the Community Foundation of Greater Flint to support Virginia Polytechnic Institute and Marc Edwards to act as advisors on the sampling of water, ongoing issues related to water quality, and water infrastructure upgrades. Mr. Edwards has 25 years of experience in water distribution system corrosion, leaks, lead and legionella, and his testing methodology helped to reveal the Flint water crisis. As a trusted expert in this field, he will participate in the federal, state and local disaster response.

title: 21st Century Community Learning Centers Institute
description: This grant to Foundations, Inc., will provide funding to support a large annual conference for afterschool educators and practitioners to build the capacity of afterschool programs and the afterschool field. The purpose of the conference is to provide afterschool educators, including the 21st Century Community Learning Centers administrators, with technical assistance and strategies to continue to enhance the quality of school-community afterschool programs. Session topics will include best practices, evaluation designs, data collection, and sustainability.

title: European Programme for Integration and Migration
description: The European Programme for Integration and Migration is a donor collaborative hosted by the Network of European Foundations for Innovative Cooperation. Established in 2005, this program strengthens the role played by civil society organizations in advocating for constructive approaches to migration in Europe. This is done through grantmaking, capacity development, and networking activities addressing a range of issues, including asylum seekers; undocumented migrants; and equality, integration, and social inclusion of vulnerable migrants. Between 2005 and 2015, this program has involved 20 European foundations in collaborative programming and grantmaking; leveraged funding from these foundations; awarded 55 grants to projects led by civil society organizations; and organized more than 20 pan-European exchange, training, and networking events involving grantees and funders. Based in Brussels, the Network of European Foundations for Innovative Cooperation strengthens cooperation among foundations in Europe.

title: Fundamentals of Civic Engagement
description: The program goal is to strengthen the capacity of young political, civic, and business leaders from Russia’s diverse regions and to link Russian participants with their peers from Europe. This grant will provide support to the School of Civic Education to conduct a series of six educational seminars focusing on understanding global issues and trends and how they relate to local issues and challenges. Two international conferences will be held in cooperation with the wider European network of similar schools to which the grantee belongs. All meetings will take place outside of Russia and will provide a critical opportunity to link participants with peers from around the world. Established in 2016, the School of Civic Education is based in the United Kingdom.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide funds to the Center for Michigan as it builds on its founding principles of public engagement, in-depth journalism, and public-driven policy work. The grantee has established itself as an independent and bipartisan source of information and education for the public on important policy issues, providing a link between citizens and the political system, engaging citizens in conversation, and ultimately having an impact on public policy.

title: Cummings School Renovations
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will provide support to the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation to renovate Cummings Elementary School as part of an effort to expand early childhood education programming within Flint. The school will open in fall 2016 through a partnership with Flint Community Schools, the University of Michigan-Flint, and the Genesee Intermediate School District, that will provide up to 220 children, ages birth to five years, with critical early childhood education opportunities. Expanding the number of high quality, early childhood education slots has become an urgent priority as a result of the Flint water crisis.

title: National Conference on Volunteering and Service
description: This grant will support the Points of Light Foundation’s National Conference on Volunteering and Service on June 27-29, 2016, in Detroit, Michigan. This conference provides a unique opportunity to send a contingent of national service members and supervisors from Flint to assist in building their knowledge and capacity.

title: Single Online Filing Portal
grantee: Multistate Registration and Filing Portal, Inc.
description: The goal of the project is to create an online portal that will allow nonprofit organizations to comply with all states’ registration filing requirements through a single online portal. The Multistate Registration and Filing Portal, Inc., is a nonprofit corporation created by state agencies in 2013 to develop and manage a single portal system of online registration for nonprofits. A single online portal will maximize efficiency, data transparency, and information sharing by enabling compliance with registration requirements for all states without duplication of data entry. Through public access, the portal will also allow for more timely, accurate, and complete data and research on the nonprofit sector. Over the next year, the portal will be developed and tested for 12 pilot states (including Michigan). Convenings with relevant stakeholders will be held to gather feedback and promote usage. The portal later will be expanded to include all 39 states that require registration.

title: Capacity Building
description: The purpose of this grant is to provide capacity building support to the Community Foundation of Greater Flint as it continues its work related to the Flint water crisis response. As emergency responders begin to exit the city of Flint, its residents will still have many long-term needs as the result of lead leaching into the water. The grantee will be working with a myriad of experts to ensure that they are creating and carrying out an effective strategy to meet as many long-term needs as possible through the water-related funds that have been established.

title: General Purposes
description: Founded in 1992, the Greater Flint Health Coalition works to achieve the collaborative and systemic changes needed to improve the health status of Genesee County residents and the quality and cost effectiveness of the local healthcare system. The grantee was established to be a neutral backbone and convening agency by healthcare, public health, businesses, and other community leaders. Additionally, the Greater Flint Health Coalition convenes 25 committees, task forces, and program teams. This grant will provide general purpose support for the grantee to increase its capacity to support the design, coordination, and delivery of health-related activities in response to the Flint water crisis.

title: General Purposes
description: Founded in 1992, the Greater Flint Health Coalition works to achieve the collaborative and systemic changes needed to improve the health status of Genesee County residents and the quality and cost effectiveness of the local healthcare system. The grantee was established to be a neutral backbone and convening agency by healthcare, public health, businesses, and other community leaders. Additionally, the Greater Flint Health Coalition convenes numerous committees, task forces, and program teams. This grant will provide general purposes support for the grantee to increase its capacity to support the design, coordination, and delivery of health-related activities in response to the Flint water crisis.

title: General Purposes
description: Founded in 1992, the Greater Flint Health Coalition works to achieve the collaborative and systemic changes needed to improve the health status of Genesee County residents and the quality and cost effectiveness of the local healthcare system. The grantee includes representatives from healthcare, education, business, and the nonprofit sector. This grant will provide general purpose support for the grantee to increase its capacity to support the design, coordination, and delivery of health-related activities in response to the Flint water crisis.

title: Community Foundation Leadership Metrics and Sustainable Development Goals
description: The Foundation Center will develop and disseminate community leadership metrics relevant to the work of U.S. community foundations and develop baseline information about the degree to which community foundations are incorporating the Sustainable Development Goals framework into their work. The work will be led by CFInsights—a service of the grantee, which collects and shares data and conducts analysis that helps community foundations improve their performance. Established in 1956, the Foundation Center is dedicated to fostering public understanding of the foundation field by collecting, organizing, analyzing, and disseminating information on foundations, corporate giving, and related subjects.

title: Community Foundations and Clean Energy in Michigan
description: The program goal is to strengthen the community leadership capacities of community foundations in Michigan that wish to support a transition to clean energy in their locales. While this grant supports an exploration and learning phase for a potential multiyear initiative, it will also provide a significant benefit to all community foundations with which it engages. The range of activities during this phase will: a) move the state’s community foundations towards deeper knowledge of and more action on transitioning their communities to clean energy; b) determine if there is solid interest from enough community foundations to merit launching a larger initiative in 2018; and c) identify potential candidates and engage them in the design of the multiyear initiative. The project will be led by the Council of Michigan Foundations, a statewide association of more than 330 grantmakers that provides its members with educational services, networking opportunities, and advocacy with policymakers.

title: Flint Future Action Coordination Team
description: The purpose of this grant is to fund a team of consultants who will support the Flint Future Action Coordination Team organized by Mayor Karen Weaver with the guidance of the Greater Flint Health Coalition. The Flint water crisis has had major public health, education, child and family services, and economic implications throughout the City of Flint. The Flint Future Action Coordination Team will convene the various working groups and stakeholders from the community in developing an organized, long-term response to the many issues created by lead-contaminated water. Consultants will help facilitate these meetings and coordinate activities to ensure collaboration among multiple municipal, state, federal, civic, neighborhood, nonprofit, academic, and private sector organizations working on issues related to the impact of the Flint water crisis.

title: Frozen Produce Program
description: This grant will provide funding for the Food Bank of Eastern Michigan to build a certified clean room at their Hunger Solution Center. The clean room will enable the grantee to receive and process millions of pounds of frozen vegetables on site for their Frozen Produce Program. The program will receive over one million pounds of donated produce that is high in calcium, vitamin C, and iron which are all recommended by the medical community to mitigate the effects of lead, especially in children.

title: Flint Child Health & Development Fund
description: This grant will support the Flint Child Health & Development Fund, which is designed to provide flexible resources to meet the needs of Flint children who have been exposed to lead in their water. The fund will complement state and federal funding to support children and their families with interventions that create a stronger likelihood of positive developmental outcomes, such as early childhood education, continuous access to a pediatric medical home, nutrition education and improved access to healthy food, access to infant and child behavioral health services, integrated social services, safe and healthy home environments, and assessments of interventions. The Foundation for Flint is a supporting organization of the Community Foundation of Greater Flint.

title: Flint BRAND Program
description: Genesee County Habitat for Humanity is an affiliate of Habitat for Humanity International, a nonprofit, ecumenical Christian housing ministry. In keeping with its mission of bringing people together to build homes, communities, and hope, Genesee County Habitat for Humanity works with neighborhood associations, block clubs, and other local grassroots groups on leadership development and other forms of capacity building. This grant will provide support for the Flint BRAND Program that builds the capacity of neighborhood groups to conceptualize, plan, and assist in implementing projects that have an immediate visible impact on their neighborhood’s environment, and help to improve Flint residents’ quality of life.

title: Flint BRAND Program
description: Genesee County Habitat for Humanity is an affiliate of Habitat for Humanity International, a nonprofit, ecumenical Christian housing ministry. In keeping with its mission of bringing people together to build homes, communities, and hope, Genesee County Habitat for Humanity works with neighborhood associations, block clubs, and other local grassroots groups on leadership development and other forms of capacity building. This grant will provide support for the Flint BRAND Program that builds the capacity of neighborhood groups to conceptualize, plan, and assist in implementing projects that have an immediate visible impact on their neighborhood’s environment, and help to improve Flint residents’ quality of life.

title: Neighborhood Impact Program
description: Genesee County Habitat for Humanity is an affiliate of Habitat for Humanity International, a nonprofit, ecumenical Christian housing ministry. In keeping with its mission of bringing people together to build homes, communities, and hope, Genesee County Habitat for Humanity works with neighborhood associations, block clubs, and other local grassroots groups on leadership development and other forms of capacity building. This grant will provide support to pilot a program that builds the capacity of neighborhood groups to conceptualize, plan, and assist in implementing projects that have an immediate, visible impact on the neighborhood environment, and help to improve Flint residents’ quality of life.

title: Giving Circles and Community Foundations
description: The project goal is to gain insight into how community foundations and other philanthropic intermediaries around the world relate to an increasingly popular form of community philanthropy—giving circles. Research will be conducted on the extent of giving circle activity worldwide, their scale and structure, and their interaction with community foundations and other host organizations. Factors that will be studied include models, structures, activities, composition, periods of existence, level of engagement, initiation processes, beneficiaries, host motivations, incentives, and receptivity. The study will map the global giving circle landscape, identifying challenges and opportunities that will help giving circles develop more productive relationships with community foundations and other philanthropic intermediaries. This will raise the potential to enhance philanthropy in communities. The project will be managed by the Johnson Center for Philanthropy, a unit of the College of Community and Public Service at Grand Valley State University in Grand Rapids, Michigan.

title: Giving Circles and Community Foundations
description: The project goal is to gain insight into how community foundations and other philanthropic intermediaries relate with an increasingly popular form of community philanthropy — giving circles. Research will be conducted on the extent of giving circle activity in the United States, the impact of giving circles on their members, and their impact on community foundations and other host organizations. Factors that will be studied include models, structures, activities, composition, length, level of engagement, initiation process, beneficiaries, and host motivations, incentives, and receptivity. The study will identify challenges and opportunities that could help community foundations, giving circles, and other philanthropic intermediaries to develop more productive relationships, thus raising the potential to increase philanthropy in communities, and make it more effective and responsive. The project will be managed by the Johnson Center for Philanthropy, a unit of the College of Community and Public Service at Grand Valley State University in Grand Rapids, Michigan.

title: Residential Service Line Technical Assistance
description: The grant will support the City of Flint’s efforts to develop a plan to replace all residential lead and galvanized service lines throughout the city. This grant will allow the city to hire a consultant to provide technical assistance, oversee operations of the FAST Start program, and advise Mayor Karen Weaver on all activities related to the water infrastructure in the city of Flint.

title: Mobile Mental Health Unit Project
description: This grant will provide support to Genesee Health System for a mobile mental health unit in Flint. The mobile unit staff will provide mental and behavioral health services, education on available resources, and referrals to other programs for adults and children impacted by the trauma and stress of the Flint water crisis. Funding will also support technical assistance from the Children’s Health Fund which has operated and deployed mobile mental health service units in other communities following a disaster. Services will be offered at a variety of locations throughout the community including events, neighborhood centers, schools, and other locations where residents gather.

title: Community Communications
description: This grant will provide funding for the United Way of Genesee County to lead a broad communications campaign in response to the Flint water crisis. The first phase of the communications efforts will focus on promoting a Web site and print publication for residents with regular updates about drinking water safety and information about available services and resources. The second phase of the communications campaign will focus on a social marketing approach to promote a healthy, positive future for Flint children and residents.

title: Strengthening GSEN in the CEE Region
description: The project goal is to increase the effectiveness and sustainability of grassroots, nonprofit initiatives in Central and Eastern Europe by encouraging social entrepreneurship approaches to social development. To this end, the Foundation for Social Entrepreneurs – UnLtd will expand the Global Social Entrepreneurship Network to several Central and Eastern European countries, including Hungary, Bulgaria, and Romania. To accomplish this, the grantee will: 1) establish partnerships with intermediary support organizations interested in advancing the concept and practice of social entrepreneurship; 2) strengthen their capacity to provide training, technical assistance, seed funding, and networking opportunities to social entrepreneurs in these countries; 3) connect partners to peers from around the world; and 4) and facilitate the exchange of experiences and ideas among them. The Foundation for Social Entrepreneurs – UnLtd is a U.K.-registered charity set up in 2002 with the mission to support social entrepreneurs at the early stage of their development and to enable them to thrive and grow through tailored packages of funds, practical support, and networking.

title: Flint River Restoration Project
description: This grant will provide project support to the Genesee County Parks & Recreation Commission for the Flint River Restoration Project. Funds will be used for professional design and engineering services, research and group facilitation consulting, and project management staff. The project is the result of a broad group of diverse partners coming together to create a vision for the Flint riverfront as a unique community asset that is accessible and safe for all residents to utilize, drive economic opportunities, and enhance local infrastructure by removing the Hamilton Dam.
