The project will support the overall economic development opportunities for Flint by creating greater connectivity from the University of Michigan-Flint to downtown and Kettering University, removing hazardous infrastructure, improving storm water and flood control systems, developing underutilized public property, and capping contamination at a former industrial site.

title: Upper Peninsula Energy Planning Project
description: Michigan’s Upper Peninsula currently faces unique and pressing challenges when it comes to reliable, affordable, and locally accessible energy. Residents are experiencing some of the highest electric rates in the nation. With this grant, the Superior Watershed Partnership will help lay the groundwork for a regional energy plan that will chart the transition to a new system that enables the region to manage its own energy future. The grantee will do so by assessing the region’s energy assets, costs, and demands, and by working with diverse stakeholders to build community-based support for a regional approach to energy planning.

title: Documentation, Verification and Dissemination of Gross Human Rights Violations in Turkey
grantee: Truth, Justice and Memory Studies Association
description: The project goal is to strengthen the role of civil society organizations in Turkey in promoting truth, justice, and accountability with respect to human rights violations in the country. The Truth, Justice and Memory Studies Association, a Turkish nonprofit organization, will systematically gather, analyze, and disseminate data on human rights violations in Turkey, particularly with respect to the long-standing Kurdish conflict in the southeast. Working with other nonprofits, the association will: 1) demonstrate the systematic and widespread character of human rights violations through research and analysis of documentation; 2) monitor and analyze the results of the prosecution of violations; and 3) raise awareness through reports, an online database and information platform, and an international workshop. The targeted research and analysis supported by this project will underpin the grantee’s broader and longer-term advocacy and educational activities. The grantee is based in Istanbul and was established in 2011.

title: Advancing the Next Generation of Civil Society Assistance
description: The Carnegie Endowment for International Peace will launch a two-year initiative to help funders, policymakers, and civic activists take the full measure of the changes buffeting civil society globally and advance efforts to rethink civil society assistance. Specific project activities will include: 1) establishing a civic activism scholars network; 2) convening six workshops and meetings; 3) publishing nine papers and reports; and 4) conducting ten interviews and consultations with assistance practitioners and policymakers. Through these activities, the grantee will generate knowledge, create linkages between the research and practice domains, and widely disseminate findings. Established in 1910 in Washington, D.C. with a gift from Andrew Carnegie, the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace is a private, nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing cooperation between nations and promoting active international engagement by the United States.

title: Productive Use of Energy Applications in Devergy Smart Solar Micro-Grids Pilot
description: Energy 4 Impact is a nonprofit organization, working with local businesses in Africa to extend access to energy in the region. Through this work, the grantee seeks to reduce poverty through accelerated access to modern energy products and services. This project will address the complexity of designing and implementing strategies for developing microenterprises that use energy produced by small solar energy microgrid companies operating in Tanzania.

title: Solar Energy for Chiribiquete Forest Dwellers
description: Amazon Conservation Team has been working with traditional communities in the Amazon rainforest to develop forest conservation and sustainable livelihoods. This project will bring renewable solar energy services to more than 50 communities in the Caquetá region of the Colombian Amazon, which lack access to modern energy services, and will develop sustainable community management systems for energy in these forest communities.

title: Building Capacity to Monitor Chinese Investment in Asia
description: Social and Environmental Entrepreneurs established the Inclusive Development International project in 2011. This project works to support and build the capacity of communities affected by international development finance investments that impact the ecosystems they live in as well as their livelihoods. With this grant, the project will support civil society organizations and networks to develop their capacity to influence Chinese development finance institutions in order to increase social and environmental accountability in their overseas investments.

title: An Equitable Water Future in the Great Lakes
description: The U.S. Water Alliance is a national nonprofit that brings together leaders representing utilities, business, government, and citizens’ groups to identify and advance broadly supported, practical, and achievable solutions to solve the country’s most pressing water management challenges. With Mott support, the grantee has brought together teams of local partners, anchored by a water utility, who are addressing water equity challenges in six cities nationwide. Three of these cities – Buffalo, Cleveland, and Milwaukee – are in the Great Lakes region. The grantee will take the lessons learned to date and begin the action and implementation phase of the project. Additionally, the grantee will extend the lessons it has learned in these six cities to address equity challenges in Detroit, Flint, and other Great Lakes cities.

title: An Equitable Water Future in the Great Lakes
description: The U.S. Water Alliance is a national nonprofit that brings together leaders representing business, government, and citizens’ groups to identify and advance broadly supported, practical, and achievable solutions to solve the country’s most pressing water management challenges. With Mott support, the grantee will conduct listening sessions in Great Lakes cities to inform the development of a national policy framework to advance integrated approaches to managing water resources. The grantee will also develop strategies to implement the national water agenda and disseminate information on the most effective practices, policies, and tools for cities across the nation, with a focus on the Great Lakes region.

title: Safe Drinking Water Policy Center
geographic_focus: Pennsylvania, Michigan, Indiana, New York, Illinois, Wisconsin, Ohio, Minnesota
description: The Northeast-Midwest Institute is a nonprofit organization dedicated to improving the economic and environmental health of the northeast and midwest regions of the United States. Headquartered in Washington, D.C., and with staff based in Michigan, the grantee provides data, research, and policy analysis to inform state and federal freshwater policy reforms and programs. This grant will support the development of a new research and policy program aimed at protecting the safety of drinking water. The grantee will also help Great Lakes citizens’ groups and municipalities assess the environmental and public health impacts of local water infrastructure decisions. In addition, the grantee will take steps to build its organizational capacity, with a focus on board development activities.

title: Afterschool Policy and System Building Initiative
description: This grant to the Massachusetts Afterschool Partnership will enable the Massachusetts Afterschool Partnership, to increase the availability of high quality afterschool and summer programs in Massachusetts. Through this grant, the network will work with partners to enhance coordination across education, child care, and workforce sectors in support of afterschool programs by: 1) developing a nonpartisan research paper on afterschool and summer learning programs in Massachusetts; 2) conducting a mapping project and return on investment analysis of existing afterschool program models; and 3) implementing a communications strategy to educate stakeholders, public groups, and families on the accessibility of afterschool and summer programs. The network will share lessons learned with other state networks to enhance coordination across sectors in support of afterschool programs.

title: Afterschool Policy and System Building Initiative
grantee: New York State Network for Youth Success, Inc.
description: This grant to AfterSchool Works! New York will enable the New York State Network for Youth Success, to increase the availability of high quality afterschool programs, summer learning, and community schools in New York. Through this grant, the network will focus on increasing public awareness of the importance of afterschool programs in New York by: 1) implementing a media campaign to raise awareness, highlight existing research, and engage new stakeholders; 2) holding annual summits to engage new partners across afterschool, summer, and community school constituencies; and 3) enhancing the existing statewide data system to improve access to consistent afterschool and summer program data. The network will share lessons learned with other state networks to increase the capacity of afterschool programs in other states to prepare youth for the workforce.

title: Afterschool Policy and System Building Initiative
description: This grant to Arkansas State University will enable the Arkansas Out of School Network to increase the availability of high quality afterschool and summer programs in Arkansas. Through this grant, the network will focus on building the capacity of afterschool programs to prepare youth for the workforce by: 1) connecting the workforce and education sectors; 2) developing new afterschool curricula on 21st century skills; and 3) supporting workforce, business, and industry leaders to create pathways for youth to develop workforce and 21st century skills over time and across settings. The network will share lessons learned with other state networks to increase the capacity of afterschool programs in other states to prepare youth for the workforce.

title: Afterschool Policy and System Building Initiative
description: This grant to the South Carolina Afterschool Alliance will enable the South Carolina Afterschool Alliance to increase access to high quality afterschool and summer programs in South Carolina. Through this grant, the network will focus on increasing access to quality programming for youth in rural areas of the state by: 1) serving as the information hub for education stakeholders to support improved afterschool opportunities in rural areas; 2) providing technical assistance, best practices, and research to school districts in support of high quality afterschool programing; and 3) designing and establishing a new quality improvement system in South Carolina. The network will provide valuable lessons to other state networks in supporting youth and rural communities through afterschool and summer learning programs.

title: Afterschool Policy and System Building Initiative
description: This grant to the Foundation for California Community Colleges will enable the California Afterschool Network to maintain and increase access to high quality afterschool and summer programs in California. Through this grant, the network will work with its partners to strengthen California’s existing system of afterschool and summer learning system by: 1) working to raise awareness of the importance of high quality afterschool and summer learning programs in California; 2) coordinating a state effort to address potential workforce shortages for afterschool programs; 3) leading field-based communications; and 4) developing a centralized database of afterschool programs. The network will share best practices with other state networks in strengthening an existing afterschool system to enhance quality and access for high-need students.

title: Afterschool Policy and System Building Initiative
description: This grant to the Minnesota Department of Education will enable Ignite Afterschool to increase access to high quality afterschool and summer programs in Minnesota. Through this grant, the network will focus on addressing the afterschool opportunity gap between low-income youth and their higher income peers in Minnesota by: 1) implementing a strategic communications effort that highlights research-based evidence on afterschool programs for policymakers, parents, and the public; 2) increasing youth and parent engagement in support of afterschool programs; and 3) deepening partnerships among key stakeholders to strengthen and expand the statewide network. This project will help inform the field nationally by providing tools that can be adapted for use in other states, including model approaches for addressing the opportunity gap, as well as partnership models that build capacity of statewide networks.

title: Afterschool Policy and System Building Initiative
description: This grant to United Ways of Texas will enable the Texas Partnership for Out of School Time to increase the availability of high quality afterschool and summer learning programs in Texas. Through this grant, the network will focus on raising awareness of the importance of afterschool programs with the education sector and business community by: 1) implementing a strategic communications plan highlighting effective afterschool programs in Texas; 2) connecting education, business, and workforce development sectors to increase workforce readiness among youth; and 3) developing a new public-private model in support of afterschool programming in the area of STEM. The network will share best practices with other state networks on connecting afterschool to state education and workforce initiatives.

title: Capacity Building
description: This grant will help to build the staff capacity of Communities First, Inc., a nonprofit housing developer and community development agency in Flint. The grantee’s mission is to promote and provide an improved quality of life for residents of distressed communities through economic development and affordable housing solutions. The current grant will partially fund positions related to project and fund development, strategic planning, and office management.

title: Capacity Building
description: This grant will help to build the staff capacity of Communities First, Inc., a nonprofit housing developer and community development agency in Flint. The grantee’s mission is to promote and provide an improved quality of life for residents of distressed communities through economic development and affordable housing solutions. The current grant will enable the grantee to partially fund positions related to project and fund development, strategic planning, and office management.

title: Civic Engagement Through Civic Theatre
description: The project goal is to strengthen civic engagement and democratic values in small towns in Bosnia and Herzegovina and Serbia through theater and related educational activities. The East West Centre Sarajevo, a Bosnian and Herzogovinian nonprofit, educational, and cultural organization, will produce and perform four original plays that address important social issues and create space for critical thinking and dialogue at the community level in Bosnia and Herzegovina and Serbia. Together, there will be 63 performances and 56 workshops for audience members, local artists, and actors. The performances will reach more than 22,000 people directly, with many more impacted and engaged through social media. The plays will address issues such as poverty, minority rights, inclusion, diversity, reconciliation, gender equality, and freedom of expression in ways that engage a wide and diverse local audience. The East West Centre Sarajevo was established in November 2005 and has produced many widely acclaimed theater pieces that have toured Bosnia and Herzegovina and internationally.

title: Climate Leadership Council
description: Founded in 1999, the New America Foundation is a nonprofit organization that nurtures new generations of public intellectuals to address major social, economic, and political challenges in ways that engage the public at large. With Mott support, the grantee will launch the Climate Leadership Council, a new international research and advocacy organization aimed at mobilizing global opinion leaders around the most effective, popular, and equitable climate change solutions. Activities will include recruiting founding members for the council, beginning operations in the United States and Europe, and preparing for a high-profile launch event in early 2017.

title: Jazz for Young People - Flint and National Afterschool Taskforce
description: Jazz at Lincoln Center is a not-for-profit arts organization dedicated to broadening and deepening participation in the jazz music genre. The grantee’s continuum of educational programs includes Jazz for Young People on Tour, which provides schools with expert jazz ensembles that offer professional development for teachers and interactive performances for students. As part of this project, the grantee will pilot the tour in Flint as a three-part concert series for Flint Community Schools’ students and their parents. This grant will also enable Jazz at Lincoln Center to convene a national taskforce of leaders from the afterschool and arts education fields, and develop a model for afterschool jazz arts education. The resulting model will be piloted and disseminated throughout the afterschool field and among school districts around the country.

title: Community Foundations and United Ways
description: The project goal is to strengthen the capacity of community foundations to positively engage with other forms of community philanthropy. The Charles Stewart Mott Foundation Chair on Community Foundations at the Indiana University’s Lilly Family School of Philanthropy, Dr. Laurie Paarlberg, will lead a preliminary study of the landscape of local community-based grantmaking, focusing on the characteristics and relationships between local United Ways and community foundations. This research will improve the understanding of the roles that both types of institutions play in local communities, potentially identifying effective practices for strengthening relationships between institutions and laying the groundwork for future research on community grantmaking. The Lilly Family School of Philanthropy at Indiana University was founded in 2012. Its mission is to increase the understanding of philanthropy and improve its practice worldwide through critical inquiry, interdisciplinary research, teaching, training, and civic engagement.

title: Capacity Building
description: Metro Community Development is a multiservice community development corporation dedicated to creating stable and vibrant neighborhoods and communities in Flint and Genesee County. The grantee serves as both an intermediary and a direct service provider for federal and state programs designed to assist low-income people with their housing and other financial needs. This grant will assist the grantee in strengthening the capacity of its asset-building and coalition-building activities, including its federal Community Development Financial Institution and Continuum of Care programs, which are integral to the economic and social recovery of Flint following the water crisis.

title: Capacity Building
description: Metro Community Development is a multiservice community development corporation dedicated to creating stable and vibrant neighborhoods in Flint and Genesee County. The grantee serves as both an intermediary and a direct service provider for federal and state programs designed to assist low-income people and help the community recover from the water crisis. Support will be used to strengthen the organization’s Asset Development, division which includes the federal Community Development Financial Institution Program. In addition, the grantee focuses on Community and Housing Development divisions.

title: Capacity Building
description: Metro Community Development is a multiservice community development corporation dedicated to creating stable and vibrant neighborhoods in Flint and Genesee County. The grantee serves as both an intermediary and a direct service provider for federal and state programs designed to assist low-income individuals and help the community recover from the water crisis. Support will be used to strengthen the grantee’s Asset Development Division, which includes the federal Community Development Financial Institution Program. In addition, the grantee focuses on Community and Housing Development divisions.

title: Capacity Building
description: Metro Community Development is a multi-service community development corporation dedicated to creating stable and vibrant neighborhoods and communities in Flint and Genesee County. The grantee serves as both an intermediary and a direct service provider for federal and state programs designed to assist low-income people with housing and capital access needs. This grant will assist Metro Community Development in strengthening the capacity of its asset-building and coalition-building activities, including its federal Community Development Financial Institution and Continuum of Care programs, which are integral to the economic and social recovery of Flint following the water crisis.

title: Factory Two Project
description: This grant will provide support to Red Ink Flint for the Factory Two Project. Factory Two is an affordable community makerspace where creative people gather to work on their product ideas and network with each other. Foundation support will help fund operations including staff for expanded hours, programming, and equipment purchases. Previous support was used to renovate the facility, equipment acquisition, and other startup costs. In addition to Factory Two, Red Ink Flint operates Flint Local 432, a performance venue located in downtown Flint that provides artistic programming and community convening in the city.

title: Factory Two Project
description: This grant provides project support to Red Ink Flint. The grantee will work with the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation to convert a former Dort Motor Car Company building into Factory Two, a community accessible makerspace where creative people will gather to work on their product ideas, learn, and network together. Funding will support build out of the facility, equipment purchases, and operations costs. Red Ink Flint also operates Flint Local 432, a performance venue located in downtown Flint that provides artistic programming and community convening in the city.

title: Help Centers
description: This grant will provide support for the Food Bank of Eastern Michigan to operate and provide food and nutrition assistance at two community Help Centers in Flint. The Help Centers will centralize a variety of water resources — such as bottled water, filters, and cartridges — and human services at two locations in Flint that are accessible to residents. The Help Centers will be operated by the Food Bank of Eastern Michigan in partnership with several organizations already assisting residents as a result of the Flint water crisis, including area churches, Genesee Health Systems, United Way of Genesee County, Michigan Works!, and the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services.

title: Drinking Water Infrastructure Program
description: The Bipartisan Policy Center is a nonprofit organization based in Washington, D.C., that crafts policy solutions that can be supported by both major political parties in the United States. This grant will provide partial support to bring together a bipartisan task force to foster a national dialogue about the importance of water infrastructure investments and the need to develop integrated solutions that include drinking water, wastewater, and stormwater. The grantee will work with Great Lakes leaders to ensure the region’s needs are taken into account in its national policy recommendations. The grantee will also disseminate briefing papers and develop media strategies to inform decisionmakers and build public support.

title: Right-Sizing Water Infrastructure
description: Older industrial cities in the Great Lakes region face water infrastructure investment and reinvestment needs that outweigh available resources. There is a need to right size such services — re-create them in order to match both the populations they serve and the available resources. The University of Michigan Water Center will convene academic and practitioner experts to address water infrastructure issues municipal leaders in the region are facing. Seminars, webinars, and a report will be among the results.

title: Urban Entrepreneurship Symposium
description: This grant will support the third annual Urban Entrepreneurship Symposium that will be held in Flint on October 19-21, 2016, and will focus on applying entrepreneurial innovations that can revitalize Flint and similar communities around the country. The event will feature a business case challenge, a community improvement pitch session, and networking reception, as well as workshops and keynote addresses from entrepreneurial leaders in Michigan and around the country. The Urban Entrepreneurship Initiative is a nonprofit organization whose mission is to facilitate the creation of innovative, sustainable business solutions to important urban problems. To accomplish its mission, the grantee provides educational opportunities, technical assistance, and networking experiences for aspiring and existing entrepreneurs.

title: Online Flint Publication
description: This grant will provide support to the Genesee Chamber Foundation to create an editorially independent online publication that covers the people and projects that are driving revitalization across the city of Flint. This work is especially important given the negative effects of the Flint water crisis on the city’s reputation and potential economic growth. Through weekly features and news stories produced by professional local writers, photographers, and videographers, the publication will aim to inform both local residents and audiences outside of the city about Flint’s revitalization, and attract resources from investors and decisionmakers that can contribute to Flint’s ongoing economic development and job growth. The grantee has selected Issue Media Group who will use a variety of methods to insure that content created for the publication is widely disseminated, including use of e-mail and social media channels, and through partnerships with other media organizations.

title: National Service and Volunteer Center Capacity Building
description: This grant to the United Way of Genesee County will provide additional capacity to support service throughout Genesee County. National service members and volunteers provide needed human resources to area nonprofits, government agencies, and schools. Volunteers help meet a variety of community needs such as blight elimination, neighborhood engagement, and tutoring and mentoring.

title: National Service and Volunteer Center Capacity Building
description: This grant to the United Way of Genesee County will provide the additional capacity to support the integration of the national service programs with the launch of the Volunteer Center. National service members and volunteers provide needed human resources to area nonprofits, government agencies, and schools. Additionally, members recruit and train local volunteers who help meet a variety of community needs such as blight elimination, neighborhood engagement, and tutoring and mentoring. This expanded area of work aligns with the grantee’s mission to give, advocate, and volunteer.

title: Service in Support of Afterschool
description: This grant will support the Service Year Exchange, Inc., to increase the number of service members supporting the statewide afterschool networks and the afterschool field. Specifically, the grantee will develop a set of tools and templates and provide training and technical assistance for the statewide afterschool networks and afterschool programs to assist in increasing the number of service members in the field.

title: Education Program Data Collection and Assessment
description: This project will support the development of an evaluation and data collection plan for the Foundation’s education program. Schaffer&Combs will work to develop a comprehensive evaluation framework and plan that both supports current program priorities and lays the groundwork for increased learning and more effective grantmaking and grantee performance in coming years. Established in 2008, Schaffer&Combs is an international management consulting firm based in San Francisco, with offices in Chicago and Durham.

title: ACT-SO Program
grantee: National Association for the Advancement of Colored People
description: The Afro-Academic, Cultural, Technological, and Scientific Olympics (ACT-SO) program is an academic mentoring, career exploration and enrichment program designed to recruit, stimulate, and encourage high academic and cultural achievement among African-American high school students. Mott support will enable the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People to implement various strategies and efforts aimed at expanding the ACT-SO program’s visibility, footprint, and impact as measured by increased participation by local chapters, increased student participation, and increased local and national partnerships that increase training and financial resources available to students. The National Association for the Advancement of Colored People is an African-American civil rights organization formed in 1909. Its mission is to ensure the political, educational, social, and economic equality of rights of all persons and to eliminate racial hatred and racial discrimination.

title: Flint National Service Accelerator Initiative Evaluation
description: This grant will support the United Way of Genesee County to engage a high quality evaluator to assess the impact of the Flint National Service Accelerator Initiative. Specifically, this grant will allow the evaluator to design and implement an evaluation that assesses the impacts of the Flint National Service Accelerator Initiative approach on the service members, the organizations that the members are placed with, and the greater community.

title: Center for Hope
grantee: Catholic Charities of Shiawassee and Genesee Counties
description: This grant will provide funding to Catholic Charities of Shiawassee and Genesee Counties to renovate the former St. Michael’s School Building. The organization is housed in this building and is part of the local safety net, providing a variety of critical social services to children, families, and individuals in Flint who are in crisis. The renovated space will enable Catholic Charities of Shiawassee and Genesee Counties to operate in a more efficient and sustainable manner.

title: Financial Recovery Technical Assistance
description: The purpose of this grant is to provide support to the City of Flint as it recovers from the water crisis. Additional staffing and consulting support will allow city leadership to function more effectively and efficiently as the recovery process is under way. As the Flint community faces unprecedented challenges, this grant will help to strengthen the economic development, grant writing, and community engagement capacity.

title: Wind Energy Stakeholder Committee
description: Established in 2001 as a project of the Midwest office of the Izaak Walton League of America, Wind on the Wires is a national conservation organization dedicated to advancing renewable energy in the Midwest. It became a stand-alone, nonprofit organization in 2011. With partial Mott support, the grantee will convene a 20-member committee that includes representation from state agencies, municipal associations, community leaders, local decisionmakers and administrators, and universities to identify best practices for developing utility-scale wind projects in local communities. The committee will develop model placement criteria for wind farms, work to reduce negative impacts to local communities, build relationships with municipal leaders, and evaluate how communities can benefit from wind power.

title: Culinary Arts Project
description: This grant will support renovations to the Woolworth Building in downtown Flint. The facility will reopen as a new and expanded culinary arts program for Mott Community College. Built in 1920, the structure is an important undeveloped asset that, once restored, will enhance other efforts to revitalize downtown and eliminate blight. Mott Community College’s primary goal is to increase enrollment in its culinary arts program and prepare students for successful careers and promising futures. A secondary goal is to contribute to efforts that foster a healthy community. The Uptown Reinvestment Corporation will serve as the developer and will own the building for seven to eight years before transferring ownership to Mott Community College.

title: Early Childhood Education Facility Construction
description: This grant will provide support to the Foundation for Flint for the construction of an early childhood education facility. The facility will be on the property behind Durant-Tuuri-Mott Elementary School. As part of an effort to expand early childhood education programming within Flint, the facility will open in fall 2017 and provide up to 220 children, ages birth to five years, with critical early childhood education opportunities. Expanding the number of high quality early childhood education slots has become an urgent priority as a result of the Flint water crisis. The Foundation for Flint is a supporting organization of the Community Foundation of Greater Flint established to serve the long-term health and development needs of Flint children and their families.

title: Flint Grocer Improvement Program
description: This grant to the Genesee Chamber Foundation will provide funds to establish the Flint Grocer Improvement Program. The focus of the program will be to address blight and the lack of access to healthy, affordable food to distressed and underprivileged residents of north Flint. The belief is that by making existing grocery stores more accessible, marketable, and overall inviting, local shoppers will be attracted to healthy food options that can aid in the reduction of long-term impacts of lead exposure. The Genesee Chamber Foundation will regrant funds to qualifying grocers to make the necessary enhancements and upgrades.

title: Sloan Museum Expansion/Renovation
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide funds to the Flint Cultural Center Corporation for the design phase of renovations to the Sloan Museum. The new design will include space for the Buick Gallery and increased public amenities such as a dining area and additional classroom space to accommodate school groups and others. Sloan Museum and Buick Gallery offer exhibits and educational experiences for youth and patrons to explore, discover, and appreciate science, technology, and history. A newly designed facility will enhance future program and exhibit opportunities in an effort to provide Flint and Genesee County residents with a world-class museum experience.

title: 100K IDEAS
description: This grant will support the Ferris Wheel Innovation Center located on the first floor of the repurposed Ferris building in downtown Flint. The grantee was established to help people in an economically disadvantaged community access supports that will help advance their business concepts. The goal is to foster education, encourage innovation and entrepreneurism, and promote economic stability in Flint. Local colleges and nonprofits will partner with the grantee to provide joint programming. Businesses located in the building will offer mentoring and counseling services. Additionally, college students will be hired to work with users and gain practical work experience that aligns with their future career goals.

title: Healthcare Startup Accelerator
description: This grant will help fund the launch of XLerateHealth, a healthcare business accelerator to be located in the Ferris Building in downtown Flint. The accelerator will serve as an entry point for entrepreneurs working to create healthcare-related enterprises. A high functioning accelerator will attract new businesses to the Flint area, spur economic growth, and create job opportunities for local residents. XLerateHealth will play a key role in the build-out of a regional health science entrepreneurial ecosystem in Flint and Genesee County.

title: Monitoring Hydropower Impacts in the Amazon
description: The Getulio Vargas Foundation is a Brazilian Think Tank and higher Education Institution dedicated to promoting Brazil’s economic and social development. Founded in 1944, the grantee has eight schools and more than 50 applied research centers. The grantee’s Center for Sustainability Studies, founded in 2003, helps companies and financiers understand, measure and assess risks and opportunities relating to environment, social responsibility, and corporate governance. This project will build upon the center’s methodology and monitoring of social and environmental impacts and compliance of the large-scale Belo Monte hydroelectric power project. Its results will help inform and mitigate impacts of planned hydroelectric investments in the greater Amazon.

title: General Purposes
description: Founded in 1991, the Association for Enterprise Opportunity is a national membership organization and trade association for microfinance and microenterprise development practitioners and organizations in the United States. This final year of general purpose support will enable the grantee to continue supporting the development of strong and effective microenterprise initiatives that assist underserved entrepreneurs in starting, stabilizing, and expanding businesses.

title: Coolidge Park Apartments
description: This grant to Communities First, Inc., will support redevelopment of the former Coolidge Elementary School in Flint into a mixed-use residential apartment complex that will consist of 54 new residential apartment units, including 42 affordable housing units. New commercial office and retail space will also be part of the development. The Coolidge Park Apartments project meets a significant need for new, high quality affordable housing options in Flint, and will help to stabilize the surrounding neighborhood.

title: Flint STEM Expansion and Recruitment
description: The purpose of this grant is to provide support to the University of Michigan-Flint for the expansion of STEM programs and facilities, and to implement a student success plan that will include strategies to enhance recruitment, retention, and graduation rates. These priorities will not only enhance the quality of education for students and expand the student base, they will also contribute to the economic and social renewal of Flint. The University of Michigan-Flint has been an anchor institution in the region for 60 years and has been committed to providing college students with high quality educational opportunities since its inception.

title: Flint SOUP Community Funded Micro-grant Program
description: This grant will support the Flint SOUP Community Funded Micro-grant Program. Funding will allow the program to expand its capacity to provide more opportunities for Flint residents to express their creative ideas, connect to the city’s broader entrepreneurial network, and offer technical assistance to innovators to help advance their concepts. Founded in 2012, Flint SOUP is a project of the United Way of Genesee County and has managed more than 30 business competitions where creators and entrepreneurs can obtain small amounts of financial support for their projects. While the program is designed to support business ideas, it simultaneously fosters community engagement and resident participation, which are needed after the water crisis.

title: Flint SOUP Community Funded Micro-grant Program
description: This grant will enable the Flint SOUP Community Funded Micro-grant Program to continue operations and provide more opportunities for Flint’s underserved residents to participate in entrepreneurship. Founded in 2012, Flint SOUP is a project of the United Way of Genesee County. The program has held more than 30 micro-grant competitions where creators and entrepreneurs can obtain small amounts of financial support and technical assistance to invest in their ideas. While the program is designed to support entrepreneurship, it simultaneously fosters community engagement and resident participation.

title: Flint SOUP Community Funded Micro-grant Program
description: This grant provides support for the Flint SOUP Community Funded Micro-grant Program. Funding will allow the program to expand its capacity to provide more opportunities for Flint residents to express their creative ideas, connect to the city’s broader entrepreneurial network, and offer technical assistance to innovators to help advance their concepts. Founded in 2012, Flint SOUP is a project of the United Way of Genesee County and has conducted more than 20 pitch competitions where creators and entrepreneurs can obtain small amounts of financial support for their projects. While the program is designed to support innovators, it simultaneously fosters community engagement through resident participation at pitch competitions.

title: Domestic Violence Services Reserve Fund
description: Each year, the YWCA of Greater Flint serves over 3,500 women and children who have been impacted by domestic violence and/or sexual assault. While federal and state grants cover the costs of these programs, the awards are structured as reimbursements, and there are significant delays in receiving payment. This grant will provide a reserve fund to be used each year by the YWCA of Greater Flint until government contracts can be fulfilled.

title: Early Childhood Capacity Building
description: This grant will provide funding to the Community Foundation of Greater Flint as it supports the expansion of early childhood education in Flint. Expanding access to high quality early childhood education has become an urgent priority as a result of the Flint water crisis. The grantee will hire an executive director to manage the early childhood education partnership including strategic planning, implementation, and oversight; governance; fiscal management and control; program operations and oversight; and external relations. The grant will provide support for the expenses related to hiring the executive director, staff costs, professional development, and office support.

title: Civic Park Construction Program
description: This grant will support the Urban Renaissance Center to develop its workforce development Civic Park Construction Program. The grantee is a faith-based nonprofit organization established by Joy Tabernacle Church with a mission to provide Flint’s young men with employment training, work experience, job security, and holistic wraparound services. The goal of the Civic Park Construction Program is to provide residents with the necessary skills and training to rehabilitate two structures in Civic Park and have them brought up to building code occupancy standards.

title: Senior Outreach Program
description: This grant will provide resources to the Valley Area Agency on Aging to host four large-scale community events for seniors in response to the Flint water crisis. The events will focus on disseminating water-related information, providing access to lead-mitigating foods, and addressing the transportation needs of Flint area seniors. Participating vendors will include area nonprofits working in these areas such as the Food Bank of Eastern Michigan, Genesee County Health Department, and Michigan State University.

title: Facility Upgrades
description: The purpose of this grant is to provide Whaley Children’s Center with essential facility upgrades that will directly affect the children who live there. Whaley Children’s Center is a residential treatment facility for children ages 5-17 who have lived in various foster homes and have experienced some sort of trauma. There are a variety of programs and strategies offered that allow staff to build a comprehensive treatment plan for each individual child based on their specific needs. This is the only facility of its kind in Genesee County, making it an invaluable asset to the community and the children who need it most.

title: Technology Upgrades
grantee: Family Service Agency of Mid Michigan
description: This grant will provide Family Service Agency of Mid Michigan with resources to upgrade its aging hardware and software systems. In order to better serve a growing aging population in Genesee County, the grantee needs to purchase and install new computers, backup and storage systems, and software for tracking client activities. The grantee serves low-income families and older adults in Genesee County.

title: Adult Career Pathway Program
description: This grant will support Mott Community College’s Adult Career Pathway Program, which will leverage many of the college’s existing educational and training programs to help connect unemployed adults, low-income workers, and youth to employment and a career pathway. The goal is to ensure that area residents can enter and advance into higher-wage occupations in high growth industries. Work experience and support services are integrated into the model and enable students and workers to combine school and work and advance along a career pathway over time. Providing residents with opportunities for job training and career advancement will help build Flint’s economic resilience to recover from the water crisis.

title: Employment Preparation Program
description: This grant will provide support to the St. Luke N.E.W. Life Center for the Employment Preparation program. Serving residents on the north side of Flint, the program works with individuals who are structurally unemployed and need a broad array of wraparound services to adequately prepare them to find and retain employment. The program will continue to expand its outreach to area employers for future job placements and establish an alumni network offering peer support to program participants and graduates. The grantee will also develop a more robust evaluation and tracking system to evaluate program successes and outcomes including graduate job retention. Providing residents with opportunities for job training and career advancement will help build Flint’s economic resilience to recover from the water crisis.

title: Berston Field House Capacity Building
description: This grant will assist the United Way of Genesee County and the Friends of Berston Field House in developing the staffing and organizational capacity to expand and improve the operation of Berston Field House. Friends of Berston Field House’s mission is to enhance the impact of Berston through quality education, athletics, the arts, and comprehensive social services. With this support, Friends of Berston Field House will hire a full-time executive assistant and fund developer, and complete a community assessment to identify services and activities they would like to see. This support will help manage the programming that takes place at Berston and expand fundraising efforts to ensure sustainability.

title: Older Industrial Cities Analysis
description: This grant will provide partial support to the Brookings Institution’s Metropolitan Policy Program to complete an in-depth analysis of the potential for inclusive economic growth in America’s older industrial cities. The Metropolitan Policy Program’s mission is to deliver research and solutions that help metropolitan leaders build an advanced economy that works for all. Intended as an expansion of the program’s influential 2007 study, the Older Industrial Cities Analysis and resulting report will establish a common narrative and set of policy recommendations to advance inclusive growth in post-industrial cities, while also providing individual cities with valuable analyses that can support their economic, workforce, and community development planning.

title: Access to Justice and the Judiciary
description: This grant will support the Democratic Governance and Rights Unit of the University of Cape Town to host a conference of access to justice players from at least nine African countries. The aim of the meeting is to increase awareness of the role of community-based paralegals in promoting access to justice and to explore ways of including them as recognized actors in the formal justice system. The meeting will be held in August 2017 in Kigali, Rwanda, and will include judges, officials from departments of justice, and nonprofit organizations that work within the access to justice area. The outcomes of the conference will feed into an envisaged African Centre of Excellence for Access to Justice, a project of the National Alliance for the Development of Community Advice Offices.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Independent Philanthropy Association of South Africa
description: The Independent Philanthropy Association of South Africa was established in 2015 as a voluntary association and network to represent and promote the common interests, concerns, and objectives of its members. Currently, the grantee has 26 members, including the Mott Foundation. The grantee’s secretariat is coordinated by GastrowBloch Philanthropy. Anticipated activities during this grant period will include hosting peer learning workshops, organizing an annual symposium focusing on philanthropic strategies in South Africa, maintaining its website to provide visitors with current and updated news and resources, and linking its members to regional African and global networks and resources on philanthropy development.

title: Long-term Sustainability of Community Foundations in Romania
description: The project goal is to support the long-term sustainability of Romanian community foundations. To this end, the Romanian Environmental Partnership Foundation will strengthen the fundraising capacities of Romanian community foundations, provide matching grants for institutional development and long-term reserve funds, and cooperate closely with other donors and support organizations to ensure timely and adequate support to community foundations. The grantee is one of the most effective grantmakers in Romania, and during the 18 years since its establishment, it has supported over 1,100 projects of more than 400 nonprofit organizations in the field of environment and community development. The grantee has been supporting the community foundation movement in Romania since 2009 by providing 23 grants totaling $575,000 to individual community foundations.

title: Addressing East Africa DRE Financing
description: Over one billion people around the world have no access to electricity, which has led to limited social and economic development. Mini-grid or other distributed renewable energy solutions can provide energy more quickly to poor rural areas through social enterprises and other private-sector opportunities. This is particularly true in Africa. However, a key barrier is financing for these small, African-led enterprises. This project will support SunFunder, a key financier of such small enterprises to continue and expand its lending to these enterprises and prove a business model for banks and other financial institutions.

title: African Development Bank Energy Financing
description: Christian Aid is a nonprofit organization with more than 70 years’ experience working to support communities and enable them to thrive. Based in the United Kingdom, Christian Aid works globally to eradicate the causes of poverty. Under this grant, they will support, build, and strengthen the capacity of the African Coalition for Sustainable Energy and Access network to work with multilateral development banks to shift investments away from fossil fuels and into renewable energy, while at the same time demanding from policymakers the delivery of renewable, sustainable, affordable, and reliable energy to the millions of Africans who are not connected to the grid.

title: National Report on Lead Exposure in Children
description: The recent public health crisis in Flint, Michigan, helped renew public support for addressing lead poisoning. The impacts of lead exposure are particularly harmful for children under the age of five, whose brains are still developing. By combining the best available science and input from impacted communities, this Pew Charitable Trusts report seeks to significantly: 1) reduce childrens’ contact with lead (via paint, water, soil, food, toys, etc.); and 2) improve the health of children who have already been exposed. Mott support will help the grantee incorporate input from Flint residents into its national research effort that includes analysis of scientific data, development of case studies, and listening sessions with focus groups. The final report will offer local, state, and national recommendations to address the impacts of lead in policies related to water infrastructure, housing, early childhood education, and health.

title: Strengthening Puerto Rico's Philanthropy Infrastructure
description: Established in 2009 by seven leading foundations, the Puerto Rico Foundations Network exists to enhance the ability of philanthropy and nonprofit organizations to improve the lives of vulnerable populations. A current high priority for the grantee is to strengthen Puerto Rico’s philanthropy infrastructure in order to respond to the crises facing the commonwealth—recovery from Hurricane Maria and huge fiscal debt. To advance this priority, the grantee will support collaborative efforts among foundations and community-based organizations, enhance the capacity of community-based organizations, advocate for policy alternatives to promote the resilience of organizations serving vulnerable groups, and engage more philanthropic actors in effective responses to Puerto Rico’s recovery.

title: Expanding Afterschool Opportunities Through National Service
description: This grant will support America’s Service Commissions to expand afterschool opportunities through national service. The grantee will map the current national service investment in afterschool, provide technical assistance and mini-grants to 13 state service commissions, and document promising practices for leveraging national service resources.

title: 21st Century Community Learning Centers Institute
description: This grant to Foundations, Inc., will provide funding to support an annual conference for afterschool educators and practitioners to build the capacity of afterschool programs and the afterschool field. The conference is one of the largest available for the administrators of the 21st Century Community Learning Centers and includes technical assistance and strategies to continue to enhance the quality of school-community afterschool programs. Session topics will include best practices in evaluation designs, data collection, college and career readiness, and sustainability.

title: Opportunity Youth Entrepreneurship Initiative
description: There are currently 5.5 million opportunity youth – defined as young people between the ages of 16 – 24 who are neither enrolled in school, nor participating in the labor market in the United States. In 2012, the Aspen Forum for Community Solutions launched the Opportunity Youth Incentive Fund, which is partnering with 23 communities around the country to design and implement collective impact and community collaboration strategies that build and deepen pathways that achieve better outcomes in education and employment for opportunity youth. Mott funding for the Opportunity Youth Entrepreneurship Initiative will enable Aspen Institute’s Forum for Community Solutions to pilot and infuse youth entrepreneurial education into the Opportunity Youth Incentive Fund network at scale. As part of this project, funding will enable the Flint, Michigan community to receive benefits associated with membership in the Opportunity Youth Incentive Fund national network.

title: Impact of Program and Practice Characteristics on Participant Outcomes
description: This grant will enable the University of California – Irvine to carry out further research to support afterschool programs. This project will allow the grantee to further build upon the Mott-funded Study of Promising After-School Programs and the Study of Early Child Care and Youth Development. Specifically, the grantee will follow up with the participants from the previous project to provide an unprecedented opportunity to identify potential long-term effects of organized afterschool activities on adult outcomes including educational attainment, earnings, occupation, family formation, physical and mental health, and civic engagement. In addition, this project will build upon previous work to complete a research synthesis of seminal studies on the positive impacts of afterschool programs on student outcomes.

title: Policy Conference 2017
description: The Detroit Regional Chamber Foundation is dedicated to creating a robust economy for businesses and individuals. This grant will support a session at the 2017 Mackinac Policy Conference focused on educating participants on why the state should analyze how the system of municipal finance impedes or accelerates a thriving community. The current municipal financing systems in Michigan do not provide sufficient revenue to adequately fund municipal services. The decline in revenue to cities over the past decade hinders the ability of cities to provide quality of living experiences that retain and attract businesses and residents. These dysfunctional systems most severely impact cities with a high population of low- and moderate-income residents.

title: Global Finance for Climate Sustainability
description: The Institute for Policy Studies works in collaboration with nongovernmental organizations, academics, and the financial sector to promote financing for sustainable energy and to address climate change. Over the grant period, the grantee has conducted policy research and civil society coordination on the early implementation of the Green Climate Fund. This grant increase will ensure continued involvement of the institute in building the capacity of developing country nongovernmental organizations as these organizations increasingly take the lead in engagement with and monitoring the activities of the Green Climate Fund.

title: Great Lakes Summit
grantee: Conference of Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Governors and Premiers
geographic_focus: Illinois, Michigan, Pennsylvania, New York, Indiana, Wisconsin, Ohio, Minnesota
description: The Conference of Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Governors and Premiers is a nonprofit organization that facilitates cooperation between the governors of eight Great Lakes states and the premiers of two Canadian provinces. With Mott support, the grantee organized a summit in 2015 entitled, “Connecting Across Borders,” which convened governors and premiers to discuss ways to expand their collaboration to address Great Lakes challenges, such as halting the spread of aquatic invasive species. With renewed Mott support, the grantee will reconvene Great Lakes leaders over three days in Detroit, Michigan, and Windsor, Ontario. The summit is entitled, “Creating the Future,” and will focus on Great Lakes ecosystem health and new resource management tools, such as the Blue Accounting online platform.

title: Building the Future of Philanthropy
description: This grant increase will support the Foundation Center’s six-year, $23.7 million investment capital campaign to position the it as the leading research and data organization on global philanthropy (referred to as its FC2020 Investment Plan). Specifically, the grantee will: 1) build a global data platform for philanthropy encompassing international data, standards and taxonomy, new forms of philanthropy, and knowledge products; 2) ensure that the grantee’s technology provides a strong foundation for its work via cutting edge applications and tools; and 3) empower donors with additional knowledge tools such as affinity group and regional association web templates, advanced custom web portals, and a new research portal. The investment plan also includes financing global philanthropy information centers, an internal venture fund, and physical space redesign. Established in 1956, the Foundation Center is dedicated to fostering public understanding of the foundation field by collecting, organizing, analyzing, and disseminating information on foundations, corporate giving, and related subjects.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Community Law and Rural Development Centre
description: The Community Law and Rural Development Centre supports a network of advice offices working in rural areas of the KwaZulu-Natal province in South Africa. The grantee provides training to advice offices which provide free essential legal services to poor communities on various topics. Past support enabled the grantee to train paralegals and management committees of advice offices while providing continuing legal education to advice offices in their network. This grant will enable the grantee to continue providing training to community advice offices in their network, finalize the accreditation of their training program, and build relationships with local business.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to facilitate the exchange of information and ideas among philanthropists, social investors, and others working for social change worldwide. To this end, the Alliance Publishing Trust carries out a range of publishing activities with regular products, including “Alliance”, a quarterly print magazine; “Alliance Extra”, an online newsletter for subscribers only; a “Latest from Alliance” blog, which offers daily opinions, news, and conference reports (quarterly); Alliance Breakfast Club meetings that bring together key sector personnel; and surveys and investigative commissions. Since 2012, the grantee has also organized the Olga Alexeeva Memorial Prize, an annual award to individuals demonstrating remarkable leadership in developing philanthropy in emerging market countries. Over the next two years, the grantee will continue to deliver the editorial package outlined above and add a podcast series, webinars, and a New Philanthropy Thinker column to its content offerings. It also plans to expand the scope of the Olga Alexeeva Memorial Prize. Alliance Publishing Trust is located in London.

title: General Purposes
description: The NGO Forum on ADB has advocated for sustainable development policies that are beneficial to local communities and the environment in the Asian region for two decades. It works to improve public participation, access to information, and good governance in the Asian Development Bank and the new Chinese development finance institutions. During the current grant period, the grantee is focusing its policy work on the review of the Asian Development Bank’s safeguard policy, as well as monitoring the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank’s project lending and discussions on their energy strategy and accountability mechanism. This grant increase will provide additional general purpose resources to ensure that this work will engage and be informed by a broad consultative process across Asia with the grantee’s 250 member organizations.

title: Increasing Food Distribution and Access
description: This grant will aid in the distribution of fresh and healthy food in Genesee County. The Food Bank of Eastern Michigan provides healthy, nutritious food to the most vulnerable community members through its partnerships with more than 200 agencies in the city of Flint. To meet this need, safe and reliable equipment is essential in the distribution of food. This grant will also provide funds for the benefit of St. Luke’s N.E.W. Life Center and the Flint Eastside Nazarene Compassionate Mission to procure highly nutritional food, personal care items, and program services like mobile pantry items.

title: New Approach to Water Management in Georgia
description: With this grant increase, the Chattahoochee Riverkeeper and its contractor partners will continue to build broad and diverse support for policies and practices that reduce water stress in over-allocated river systems in Georgia. Activities will include: improving regional water management plans, highlighting industrial practices that save water, building the capacity of individual groups working on these issues, and strengthening a network of such groups across the state.

title: Flint River Restoration Project
description: This grant will provide project support to the Genesee County Parks & Recreation Commission for the Flint River Restoration Project. Funds from this grant will be used for construction of the green cap on Phase III of Chevy Commons. The project is the result of a broad group of diverse partners coming together to create a vision for the Flint riverfront as a unique community asset that is accessible and safe for all residents to utilize, drive economic opportunities, and enhance local infrastructure by removing the Hamilton Dam. The project will support the overall economic development opportunities for Flint by creating greater connectivity from the University of Michigan-Flint to downtown and Kettering University, removing hazardous infrastructure, improving storm water and flood control systems, developing underutilized public property, and capping contamination at a former industrial site.

title: Lenore Croudy Family Life Center
description: This grant will provide support to Mott Community College to create the Lenore Croudy Family Life Center. Within this new space, the grantee will expand its early childhood education services, serving both more children and younger children; colocate its faculty offices and classrooms and observation space for students pursuing early childhood education degrees; and provide a resource center to help recruit, retain, and assist students with the completion of their college degrees.

title: International Program
description: Oil Change International has worked over the last decade to increase the transparency of international financial institution lending in the energy sector, ensuring that there is clearer data to inform policymakers in their discussions with these institutions as well as in international climate negotiations. Over the last grant period, the grantee has significantly expanded its tracking of public finance for fossil fuels, expanding the data to include all of the major multilateral development banks. This grant increase will allow the grantee to continue its research and media outreach work to shift multilateral and bilateral financing away from fossil fuel projects and toward support for renewable energy.

title: Faith in Finance Convening
description: With this grant, the Alliance of Religions and Conservation will convene global faith organizations to discuss their role in financing projects that lead to and support environmental sustainability. At a meeting in Zug, Switzerland, in October 2017, faith organizations will discuss how their investments might impact the field of environmental sustainability and will develop a set of guidelines to guide their practice.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide funds to the Center for Michigan to further expand its founding principles of public engagement, in-depth journalism, and public-driven policy work. The grantee has established itself as an independent and bipartisan source of information and education for the public on important policy issues, providing a link between citizens and the political system, engaging citizens in conversation, and ultimately having an impact on public policy.

title: Flint Anchor Institutions Clean Energy Initiative
description: Founded in 2005, the Clean Energy Coalition is a nonprofit organization dedicated to promoting clean energy technologies as a way to create healthier, energy-independent communities. The grantee assists communities with developing: 1) energy efficiency; 2) renewable energy; and 3) clean vehicle projects. This renewal grant will allow the grantee to work with anchor institutions in Flint to explore ways to jointly pursue the adoption of renewable energy and energy efficiency technologies.

title: BNDES and the Amazon
description: Founded in 1999, Mongabay.org is a top source of environmental news, analysis, information, and inspiration on the Internet. Over the past grant period, the grantee produced original stories on the impacts of large-scale hydroelectric development and finance in the Amazon, with a focus on the Tapajos River basin. Over the next grant period, the grantee will build on its body of reporting by covering finance and development of energy and infrastructure and its impacts on environmental sustainability in the greater Amazon.

title: Design a Library for the Future
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide technical assistance for the Flint Public Library’s building design project. Resources will support final architect schematic designs and a fully developed construction budget for library renovations. The library provides free, public programs and services for Flint area residents of all ages and learning levels.

title: Transcontinental Dialogue on Chinese Investment and Financing in the Global South
description: EarthRights International is a nongovernmental, nonprofit organization of environmental lawyers and advocates based in three countries — the United States, Peru, and Thailand. The grantee seeks to protect the environment and the communities where they work. The grantee will serve as the logistical coordinator to plan, organize, and host a conference for partners in Latin America and Asia to build networks and strategies around energy and infrastructure projects financed by Chinese institutions.

title: Strengthening New Development Bank Safeguards
grantee: Pontifical Catholic University Rio de Janeiro
description: The BRICS Policy Center is a think tank dedicated to studying the structural shift occurring in international development finance as Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa emerge as prominent global actors. Administered by the Pontifical Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro, the BRICS Policy Center has established a research program to cultivate international expertise and dialogue on social and environmental safeguards for development finance, with emphasis on the role of new development finance institutions. With this grant increase, the safeguards specialists team will grow to two experts.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purpose support to CFLeads, a national network of United States community foundations whose goal is to build stronger communities. The grantee accomplishes this by advancing effective practices, sharing knowledge, and galvanizing action on critical issues. The grantee serves community foundations through its peer learning products: Community Leadership Networks, Executive Leadership Institutes, and Issue Networks. It also provides technical assistance, research, and resource materials on best practices and convenes a biennial forum. In the last year alone, the grantee worked with 750 individuals from 370 community foundations. From 2019-2021, the grantee will continue its educational, technical assistance, research, and informational offerings, specifically supporting issue networks in the areas of children’s savings accounts, equity, and links with Latin American community foundations. Established in 1991 as the Coalition of Community Foundations for Youth under the Greater Kansas City Community Foundations, CFLeads became an independent nonprofit organization in 2017.

title: Expanding CSAs for Educational Success and Lifelong Asset Building
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant provides continuing support for Washington University’s research, communications, policy development, and technical assistance efforts aimed at advancing children’s savings account strategies at the state and national levels. In the short term, the grantee’s goal is to expand opportunities for all families to save for their children’s education, and in doing so, increase postsecondary education aspirations, access, and completion rates, particularly among low- to moderate-income students. Long term, the grantee views children’s savings accounts as the initial phase of a broader effort to embed inclusive and lifelong asset-building opportunities into the fabric of domestic social policy in ways that support educational, economic development, and financial security goals.

title: Advice Office Support Project
grantee: Association of University Legal Aid Institutions Trust
description: The Association of University Legal Aid Institutions Trust promotes access to justice for poor and marginalized communities through fostering partnerships between legal aid institutions attached to universities in South Africa and community-based advice offices. Past support has enabled the grantee to make small grants to advice offices, conduct workshops to inform people about their rights and how to access them, train and mentor paralegals working in community-based advice offices on various aspects of the law, governance, and office administration, provide backup legal services to paralegals in advice offices, and assist poor people with free legal advice and related services. This grant will continue to enable university law clinics to provide backup legal services to community-based advice offices and poor communities. It will also provide structured financial support to carefully selected advice offices in order to build capacity, provide the necessary infrastructure, and assist in developing a sustainable network of legal service provision.

title: Global Philanthropy Program
description: This grant supports the Council on Foundations’ Global Philanthropy Program, which is framed around four pillars of activity: 1) effective cross-border grantmaking, 2) policy and regulation of cross-border grantmaking, 3) global conversations and convening, and 4) developing global resources and thought leadership. Over the past 18 months, the grantee maintained a library of resources on international grantmaking on its website, worked with partners on the Financial Action Task Force’s recommendations affecting philanthropy, kept members aware of changing international regulations that impact cross-border philanthropic flows, held global conferences on a variety of topics including Sustainable Development Goals, hosted delegations of foreign philanthropic actors, and served on several global advisory boards. During the upcoming grant period, the grantee will continue to enhance and expand upon the four activity pillars. Founded in 1949, the Council on Foundations is a membership organization of private, community, and corporate foundations, primarily in the United States.

title: Municipal Finance System Reform
description: The Michigan Municipal League Foundation’s mission is to help create and maintain vibrant communities in Michigan by funding placemaking projects and educating community leaders and advocates. An important component of vibrant communities is an adequate government financing system that provides enough revenue for a city to provide governmental services. Unfortunately, Michigan does not have a funding system that meets this goal. When a city cannot sustain a reasonable level of services, the quality of life decreases dramatically for all of its citizens, resulting in increased blight, increased crime, and lower quality infrastructure. This grant will help support convenings of stakeholders to collaborate on developing a strategy to improve the municipal finance systems in the state of Michigan.

title: Buick City Pre-development Assessment
description: This grant to the Genesee Chamber Foundation will support a predevelopment assessment on a parcel of property at the Buick City brownfield site. The assessment will address an immediate demand for industrial square footage in the area and will provide key site information regarding redevelopment conditions. The project looks to build upon the previous work funded by the U.S. Economic Development Administration that conducted a feasibility study on the entire site.

title: Downtown Hotel Pre-design Study
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This project will allow for the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation to support the pre-development work for renovating the former Genesee County Savings Bank into a hotel for downtown Flint. This work includes an evaluation, analysis, design and engineering. This redevelopment effort aims to continue the resurgence of downtown and provide lodging for visitors to the city.

title: General Purposes
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant provides support to the Asset Funders Network for its core initiatives, including a focus on growing the number of funders and private investments in the Children’s Savings Account field. Started in 2005, as a project of Philanthropy New York, the grantee’s mission is to engage philanthropy to advance economic opportunity and prosperity for low- and moderate-income people. The grantee plays a critical role in sharing best practices with member grantmakers as it relates to research and innovations while helping them learn and connect with one another. Activities planned for 2019-2020 include a webinar series, in-person meetings, and material distribution related to the field-at-large, including policy reform and momentum building resources.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to build and strengthen an enabling environment for philanthropy. Worldwide Initiatives for Grantmaker Support is a global network linking 100 philanthropic associations and support organizations from 40 countries through international exchange, information services, networking, and peer-to-peer learning opportunities. Together these members serve and represent close to 100,000 philanthropic entities worldwide, including foundations, corporations, individual philanthropists, and community foundations. During 2017-2018, the grantee published research related to philanthropy and philanthropy infrastructure; disseminated information and analysis about the sector through social media, blogs, and an online newsletter; held capacity building workshops and online webinars; and organized its flagship global event, the WINGSForum, in Mexico City. In 2019-2020, the grantee will continue implementing a new, five-year strategy adopted in 2018, which is focused on three areas: making the case for philanthropy development, fostering an enabling environment for philanthropy, and strengthening the philanthropy support ecosystem where it is needed the most. Established in 2000 and incorporated in the United States in 2010, the grantee is based in Sao Paulo, Brazil.
