title: General Purposes
description: Established in 1990, the National Council of Nonprofits is the nation’s largest network of nonprofits, representing more than 25,000 organizations across the country. Its mission is to advance the vital role, capacity, and voice of charitable nonprofit organizations. The grantee works through its network of state associations to help nonprofits operate more effectively, engage in critical policy issues affecting the sector, and achieve greater impact in their communities. Over the past two years, the grantee advocated for tax and other policies favorable to the nonprofit sector, advanced solutions regarding the government-nonprofit contracting system, and strengthened its network. During this grant period, the grantee will continue to strengthen the capacity of nonprofits, give voice to nonprofits through public policy advocacy, and highlight the vital roles that charitable nonprofits play in benefiting local communities.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to Independent Sector, a leadership network for nonprofits, foundations, and corporations committed to advancing the common good. Founded in 1980, the grantee fulfills its mission by: 1) promoting policies that enable the nonprofit and philanthropic community to engage with public officials on a nonpartisan basis; 2) supporting the development and dissemination of strategies to strengthen volunteering, voting, giving, and other forms of citizen engagement; 3) convening opportunities for sector leaders to work together on key issues; 4) encouraging the sector to meet the highest standards of ethical practice and effectiveness; and 5) serving as the voice of the independent sector to the media, government, business, and international voluntary communities. Over the next two years, the grantee will help the sector make its voice heard among policy makers and serve as an advocate for, and disseminator of, innovative solutions to ongoing and emerging needs.

title: Campaign for Grade-Level Reading
description: This grant to the Tides Foundation will support the Campaign for Grade-Level Reading to: 1) expand and strengthen partnerships with the statewide afterschool networks; 2) develop targeted activities to deepen and broaden partnerships between statewide afterschool networks and state/local grade-level reading campaigns; and 3) support the Campaign for Grade-Level Reading’s core operations.

title: Afterschool Evaluation and Dissemination Project
description: This project will support the transition of the Harvard Family Research Project to Third Sector New England and to launch the Global Family Research Project. The Global Family Research Project will serve as a leading resource for afterschool and education practitioners and policymakers on research, innovation and best practices to support afterschool and summer learning opportunities around the globe. This project will support the afterschool field and its key stakeholders to improve the accessibility of afterschool evaluation information.

title: Membership and Administrative Support
description: This grant supports the membership and administrative costs of the Network of European Foundations for Innovative Cooperation, a nonprofit membership association based in Brussels. Its goal is to strengthen philanthropic cooperation among foundations, associations, and other nongovernmental organizations in Europe. In 2018, the grantee managed a portfolio of ten initiatives and external projects addressing key issues and geographies, including children and violence, integration and migration, dementia, the Balkans, and Tunisia. During 2019-20, the Brussels staff will manage projects and organize regular meetings of the board and the general assembly. The grantee currently has ten members and engages many other foundations, public donors, and other types of philanthropic organizations in its projects.

title: Building Capacity to Monitor Chinese Investment in Asia
description: The development finance landscape across Asia has changed rapidly over the past decade. Chinese investments in developing countries have increased exponentially and present a major shift in the source and structure of development finance. To address the environmental and social impacts of Chinese development finance, Inclusive Development International was established in 2012 to support and build the capacity of communities affected by these investments. The grantee has been key in raising awareness of the need to strengthen the environmental and social policies of Chinese development finance institutions, particularly the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank. Over the next grant period, the grantee will undertake work to strengthen civil society understanding of Chinese investments; convene diverse groups to develop strategies to address such financing; map Chinese finance and research on specific projects; and monitor implementation of Chinese development finance institutions’ environmental and social policies.

title: Schools of Choice Academic Impact Study
description: As of 2013, students in Genesee County are no longer expected to attend their home school district and have been able to choose the public school district of their choice when spots are available. Research is needed to better understand the impact of such choices on student achievement. Education Trust, Inc., will undertake both a literature review and secondary data analysis in order to better understand how student achievement is impacted by school choices.

title: General Purposes
grantee: CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation
description: Established in 1993, CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation is an international alliance of more than 4,700 members in 175 countries. Its mission is to strengthen civil society and citizen participation throughout the world, especially in areas where participatory democracy and citizens’ freedom of association are challenged. Recent accomplishments include the hosting of a World Assembly and International Civil Society Week in Fiji in 2017; the release of annual State of Civil Society reports; and maintaining the CIVICUS Monitor—a research tool to share reliable, timely data and analysis on civic space. This renewal will support CIVICUS’ implementation of its 2017-2022 strategic plan, which focuses on defending civic freedoms and democratic values; strengthening the power of people to organize, mobilize, and take action; and empowering a more accountable, effective, and innovative civil society. The grantee’s main office is in Johannesburg, South Africa.

title: Opportunity Youth Entrepreneurship Initiative
description: In 2013, the Aspen Forum for Community Solutions launched the Opportunity Youth Incentive Fund, which is partnering with 23 communities around the country to design and implement collective impact and community collaboration strategies that build and deepen pathways that achieve better outcomes in education and employment for opportunity youth. This grant will enable Aspen Institute’s Forum for Community Solutions to pilot and infuse youth entrepreneurial education into the Opportunity Youth Incentive Fund network at scale. As part of this project, funding will enable the Flint, Michigan community to receive benefits associated with membership in the Opportunity Youth Incentive Fund national network.

title: Residential Service Line Technical Assistance
description: This grant supports the City of Flint’s efforts to replace all residential lead and galvanized service lines throughout the city. This grant will allow the City to continue to retain a consultant to provide technical assistance, oversee operations of the fourth phase of the FAST Start program, and advise the mayor on all activities related to the water infrastructure in the city of Flint.

title: STEM Fellowship
description: This grant to the Pacific Science Center will support the Robert Noyce Fellowship in Informal STEM Learning. The fellowship is a public-private partnership initiative geared toward advancing high quality informal science education, including in afterschool and summer learning programs. This initiative will include: 1) strengthening collaboration between the U.S. Department of Education and other federal agencies in the area of informal STEM learning; 2) working to advance STEM learning in the 21st Century Community Learning Centers program; and 3) working with leading researchers to identify priorities in informal STEM learning, including identifying new tools, strategies, and programs that improve STEM learning opportunities.

title: Sustainable Energy Use in Northern Michigan
description: This grant increase will provide partial support to the Groundwork Center for Resilient Communities to host the inaugural Michigan Clean Energy Conference in 2017 in Traverse City. The event will focus on Michigan’s new clean energy economy and practical models to advance renewable energy and energy efficiency projects in communities across Michigan. The conference will be held in coordination with the Great Lakes Renewable Energy Association State Energy Fair in Traverse City and will involve many local and statewide partner groups.

title: New Approach to Water Management in Georgia
description: Chattahoochee Riverkeeper, a watershed protection group in Georgia, is leading an effort to develop a suite of solutions to water supply challenges faced across the state. This renewal grant will enable the grantee to continue these efforts to advance innovative solutions and meet shared water restoration, protection, and management goals. Funds will also be used to support the core capacity of the Georgia Water Coalition, of which the grantee is a founding member.

title: Lower Flint River Project
description: The ecological health of Georgia’s Flint River, part of the larger Apalachicola-Chattahoochee-Flint River Basin, is under stress due to a range of issues including chronic drought and poorly coordinated water use. With its strong presence in Georgia, The Nature Conservancy has been working in the lower segment of the Flint River to improve irrigation efficiency as a means to sustain the river’s natural flow. With Mott support, the grantee completed an assessment of the impact of its work to date and identified new potential conservation strategies. Renewed support will allow the grantee to build on its findings and develop new strategies to improve natural flows in the lower Flint River.

title: Health and Environmental Funders Network
description: This grant will support the Health and Environmental Funders Network, a project of Virginia Organizing, Inc., based in Charlottesville, Virginia. The network provides opportunities through meetings, webinars, and other means for grantmakers to gain a better understanding of the connections between environmental protection and public health, as well as to discuss grantmaking strategies and explore areas for collaboration. Over the next year, the network will expand its activities, connecting funders through issue-based workshops and its annual meeting that will be held in Detroit, Michigan.

title: Drinking Water Infrastructure Program
description: The Bipartisan Policy Center is a nonprofit organization based in Washington, D.C., that crafts policy solutions that can be supported by both major political parties in the United States. With prior Mott support, the grantee brought together a bipartisan task force to foster a national dialogue about the importance of water infrastructure investments and the need to develop integrated solutions that include drinking water, wastewater, and stormwater. This included working with Great Lakes leaders to ensure the region’s needs are taken into account. This grant renewal will allow the grantee to continue these efforts to inform decisionmakers and build public support on issues that are critical to water infrastructure, such as building regional solutions and addressing the affordability concerns of low- and moderate-income families.

title: Mobile Mental Health Unit Project
description: This grant will provide support to Genesee Health System for a mobile mental health unit in Flint. The mobile unit staff will provide mental and behavioral health services, education on available resources, and referrals to other programs for adults and children impacted by the trauma and stress of the Flint water crisis. Funding will also support technical assistance from the Children’s Health Fund which has operated and deployed mobile mental health service units in other communities following a disaster. Services will be offered at a variety of locations throughout the community including events, neighborhood centers, schools, and other locations where residents gather.

title: Strengthening Environmental-Social Framework in South America
geographic_focus: Peru, Colombia, Argentina, Brazil, South America
description: Created in 2008, the Latin American Network of Environmental Public Prosecutors is comprised of 300 public prosecutors from 19 Latin American countries. Public prosecutors in these countries build legal actions to strengthen compliance with environmental laws and engage in conflict resolution. International financial institutions have recently approved new social and environmental frameworks that seek to harmonize these standards with country-level environmental and social systems of law to mitigate impacts of large-scale energy and infrastructure development. However, standards in all of Latin America are generally weak, and understanding of international best practice is lacking. This grant to Uniselva Foundation will enable network public prosecutors in four Latin American countries to conduct a comparative legal analysis of international standards and country systems. They will conduct public workshops to deepen understanding of, and action to achieve, the highest environmental and social standards to mitigate environmental impacts of large infrastructure investment in Argentina, Brazil, Colombia, and Peru.

title: Multi-Agency Grants Initiative: Advice Office Regranting Project
description: Hlanganisa Institute of Development Southern Africa NPC, previously known as Hivos – South Africa, was established in 2006 to seek new and innovative solutions to persistent social challenges. The Multi-Agency Grants Initiative, managed by the grantee, is a collaborative venture between various funders in South Africa. Its purpose is to provide a responsive mechanism for making small grants to community-based organizations, including community advice offices. Past support to the grantee allowed them to disburse grants to 20 community advice offices, help unlock strategic partnerships for advice offices, promote women leadership in the governance structures of advice offices, and strengthen the institutional arrangements of these offices. Ongoing support will allow the grantee to continue to provide resources and capacity to community advice offices and to document the organizational capabilities of the staff at advice offices in the Free State province of South Africa.

title: Multi-Agency Grants Initiative: Advice Office Regranting Project
description: Hlanganisa Institute of Development Southern Africa NPC, previously known as Hivos — South Africa, was established in 2006 to seek new and innovative solutions to persistent social challenges. The Multi-Agency Grants Initiative managed by the grantee is a collaborative venture between various funders in South Africa. Its purpose is to provide a responsive mechanism for making small grants to community-based organizations, including community advice offices. Past support allowed the grantee to pilot a new model of support to advice offices in the Free State province, while continuing to build women leadership in the community advice office sector. Ongoing support will allow the grantee to continue in this direction with an additional activity to build and strengthen case management systems.

title: Metropolitan Policy Program
description: The Metropolitan Policy Program at Brookings Institution, an internationally known think tank, is well-positioned to assist in the development and deployment of strategy for the retooling of the American economy. With continuing support, the grantee will undertake a range of work to promote the economic competitiveness of metropolitan areas domestically and globally, including older industrial cities such as Flint. Activities will include original research, policy advocacy, analytical tool development, and network building.

title: Early Childhood Education Facility Construction
description: This grant increase will provide support to the Foundation for Flint for the construction of an early childhood education facility. The facility is on the property behind Durant-Tuuri-Mott Elementary School. As part of an effort to expand early childhood education programming within Flint, the facility will open in fall 2017 and provide up to 220 children, ages birth to five years, with critical early childhood education opportunities. Expanding the number of high quality, early childhood education slots has become an urgent priority as a result of the Flint water crisis. The Foundation for Flint is a supporting organization of the Community Foundation of Greater Flint established to serve the long-term health and development needs of Flint children and their families.

title: Capitol Theatre Re-Opening Community Engagement Project
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide support to the Flint Cultural Center Corporation for a series of community engagement and outreach activities for the first year of the Capitol Theatre’s reopening. Programming and events at the Capitol Theatre will provide entertainment through performances and films and serve as a gathering place for the community. Funding from this grant will support low-cost and free tickets; staffing for community performances; and receptions, tours and other events open to the public at the Capitol Theatre.

title: Community Education Initiative
description: This grant provides support to the Crim Fitness Foundation to continue to serve as the lead agency for the community education model in Flint. The fifth year of implementing the community education strategy will involve increasing the depth and impact of programs at all Flint Community Schools buildings and expanding to the International Academy of Flint charter school. The community education strategy will help provide the strong, research-based educational and enrichment opportunities that are important interventions for individuals from birth to young adulthood, especially for those who may have been exposed to lead.

title: Community Education Initiative
description: This grant provides support to the Crim Fitness Foundation to continue to serve as the lead agency for the community education model in Flint. The sixth year of implementing the community education strategy will involve increasing the depth and impact of programs at all Flint Community Schools buildings and the International Academy of Flint charter school, along with expansion to the Flint Cultural Center Academy. The community education strategy will help provide the strong, research-based educational and enrichment opportunities that are important interventions for individuals from birth to young adulthood, especially for those who may have been exposed to lead.

title: Community Education Initiative
description: This grant provides support to the Crim Fitness Foundation to continue to serve as the lead agency for the community education model in Flint. The seventh year of implementing the community education strategy will involve increasing the depth and impact of programs at all Flint Community Schools buildings, the International Academy of Flint charter school and the Flint Cultural Center Academy, as well as experimenting with an online version of the model.

title: 100K Ideas
description: This grant will support the Ferris Wheel Innovation Center located on the first floor of the Ferris building in downtown Flint. The grantee was established to help people in an economically disadvantaged community access supports that will help advance their business concepts. The goal is to foster education, encourage innovation and entrepreneurism, and promote economic stability in Flint. Local colleges and nonprofits will partner with the grantee to provide joint programming. Businesses located in the building will offer mentoring and counseling services. Additionally, college students will be hired to work with users and gain practical work experience that aligns with their future career goals.

title: 100K Ideas
description: This grant will support the Ferris Wheel Innovation Center located on the first floor of the Ferris Wheel building in downtown Flint. The grantee was established to help people in an economically disadvantaged community to access supports that will help advance their business concepts. The goal is to foster education, encourage innovation and entrepreneurism and promote economic stability in Flint. Local colleges and nonprofits will partner with the grantee to provide joint programming. Businesses located in the building will offer mentoring and counseling services. Additionally, college students will be hired to work with users and gain practical work experience that aligns with their future career goals.

title: Flint Children's Savings Account Feasibility Study
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: Commonwealth, a Boston-based nonprofit organization, has a proven track record researching and piloting innovative financial strategies. This grant will enable the organization to support and inform the planning and design of a children’s savings account initiative in Flint, Michigan. Activities planned during the grant period include focus groups with local stakeholders and families, as well as a feasibility study to identify financial technologies that can facilitate program participation and engagement.

title: General Purposes
description: Derecho Ambiente y Recursos Naturales is a Peruvian nongovernmental organization focused on sustainable development and conservation of the Amazon Basin. Over the last project period, the organization made significant contributions to reforming and implementing the environment and social standards that govern international and national financial institutions, including work with partners to mitigate the impacts of specific infrastructure and energy projects. This grant renewal provides general purpose support to the organization to implement its strategic plan 2018-2022 and to strengthen its work on energy development and access in the Peruvian Amazon state of Loreto.

title: Monitoring Infrastructure Investments in Argentina
location: Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires, Argentina
description: The Fundacion Ambiente y Recursos Naturales is an Argentinian nongovernmental organization that has worked for the past 31 years to promote sustainable development through policy, law, and civic engagement. Argentina, like its neighbors in South America, has developed investment agreements with Chinese and international financial institutions for large-scale energy and infrastructure development. Over the past project period, progress was made to influence sustainable energy investment and decrease social and environmental impacts of large-scale energy projects in Argentina. This project will support the grantee and two contracted partners, the Foundation for the Development of Sustainable Policies and Cauce, to monitor and provide information on the effective implementation of environmental sustainability, transparency, and public participation policies and regulations in energy projects supported by these public investment institutions.

title: Economic and Entrepreneurial Outreach
description: This grant will support the Economic Development Administration Center for Community and Economic Development at the University of Michigan-Flint. The center undertakes research that helps organizations identify economic development opportunities in a distressed region. In addition, support will allow the university to expand its entrepreneurial offerings to connect more Flint residents to entrepreneurial trainings and resources.

title: Flint Children's Savings Account Planning
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant to the Genesee Intermediate School District will provide funding to explore the feasibility of implementing Children’s Savings Accounts in Flint and Genesee County. During the next six months, the grantee will facilitate a learning and planning process, engaging key local stakeholders and visiting existing successful Children’s Savings Account programs in other communities. Through this process, the grantee will explore a series of program design questions, including technology platforms and leveraging opportunities. Final recommendations will be detailed in a discussion memo for the Foundation and planning stakeholders.

title: Blight Elimination and Neighborhood Stabilization
description: This grant will provide support to the Genesee County Land Bank Authority to demolish blighted and abandoned structures in neighborhoods located around Kettering University, Durant-Tuuri-Mott Elementary School, Chevy Commons, Mott Park, the Flint River, and Atwood Stadium. Demolishing these properties is an important step in stabilizing the neighborhood surrounding the EduCare early childhood education facility.

title: Marketplace Apartments
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will support a mixed-income housing development at the site of the former YWCA. The project will include 92 units of rental housing and ground-level retail. The Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation is the supporting organization of the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, which has identified quality and affordable housing as a core component to further revitalization in downtown Flint. Fifty-one percent of the units will be below market rate making rental affordable for working-class families.

title: Nonprofit Employment Data Project
description: The Nonprofit Employment Data Project is a collaboration between the Johns Hopkins University’s Center for Civil Society Studies and the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics that charts nonprofit employment, wages, and finances over time and in relation to other industries. At the beginning of 2017, the center launched a user-friendly, interactive database called Nonprofit Works, which provided nonprofit employment data from 1999 through 2012. During the previous grant period, the grantee has worked with the bureau to obtain the input of 2015 and 2016 data into Nonprofit Works. The grantee has extensively disseminated the results, most recently issuing “The 2019 Nonprofit Employment Report.” The grantee has also marketed the database, creating 261 user accounts and 23 paid memberships. Over the upcoming grant period, the grantee will add 2017 employment data released by the bureau and further enhance, update, and market the Nonprofit Works site. Johns Hopkins University is one of America’s premier research universities. The Center for Civil Society Studies seeks to improve the understanding and effective functioning of nonprofit, philanthropic, and civil society organizations.

title: Flint Children's Savings Account Planning
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant to the Community Foundation of Greater Flint will provide funding to support a six-month children’s savings account learning and planning process. The primary goal of this process will be to explore the feasibility of implementing children’s savings accounts in Flint and Genesee County. Final recommendations will be detailed in a discussion memo for the Foundation and stakeholders engaged in the planning process.

title: Michigan Communities for Financial Empowerment Network
grantee: Community Economic Development Association of Michigan
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: Through its Michigan Communities for Financial Empowerment program, the Community Economic Development Association of Michigan works to expand and strengthen financial security in communities across the state. Renewal support from the Mott Foundation will enable the grantee to expand the footprint of children’s savings accounts programs across the state. During the grant period, the grantee will raise awareness of children’s savings accounts, and support the planning and implementation of the strategy in at least three new sites. To accomplish these goals, the grantee will provide local communities with technical assistance and peer-learning opportunities, engage new stakeholders as champions for college savings strategies, and expand knowledge about the benefits of children’s savings accounts throughout Michigan. Based in Lansing, the Community Economic Development Association of Michigan is a nonprofit trade association serving community economic development professionals in Michigan.

title: Cities Building Bridges to Postsecondary Success
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This renewal grant will enable the National League of Cities Institute to help municipal leaders integrate children’s savings account strategies into their college readiness, access, and success initiatives. During the grant period, the grantee will continue to produce and disseminate informational materials, broker technical assistance, and provide peer learning opportunities for municipal leaders. The overall goal of this project is to establish a strong set of citywide examples that illustrate the promise of children’s savings accounts as an important component of comprehensive college and career readiness efforts. Established in 1958 and located in Washington, D.C., the grantee is a research, education, and training affiliate of the National League of Cities.

title: Asset Building Program
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: Renewal funding will support the New America Foundation’s continued efforts to promote children’s savings account programs and policies across states and municipalities. The specific activities proposed include: 1) working with state and local stakeholders to develop and promote children’s savings account policy ideas; 2) highlighting children’s savings account program design and implementation best practices; and 3) advancing policymakers’ understanding and leadership of children’s savings account strategies. The New America Foundation is a public policy institute whose purpose is to bring new voices and ideas to the forefront of America’s public discourse by investing in outstanding individuals and ideas that transcend the conventional political spectrum.

title: Teen Reviewers and Critics Program
description: This project will focus on supporting ArtsConnection’s afterschool program, known as the Teen Reviewers and Critics Program. This grant will document lessons learned and best practices for arts activities in afterschool programs that can be shared through the state afterschool networks.

title: General Purposes
description: The Climate Leadership Council is an international research and advocacy organization whose mission is to develop and promote a carbon dividends framework as a viable climate change policy solution. With Mott support, the grantee will pursue this aim by mobilizing opinion leaders, undertaking multidisciplinary policy research, educating policymakers, orchestrating public education campaigns, and developing strategic partnerships with business, research, and advocacy groups in the United States and internationally.

title: General Purposes
description: The Climate Leadership Council is an international research and advocacy organization whose mission is to develop and promote a carbon dividends framework as a viable climate change policy solution. During its first full year of operation, the grantee’s proposals received considerable attention from the media, policymakers, and the general public. With renewed support, the grantee will continue to pursue its aims by mobilizing opinion leaders, undertaking multidisciplinary policy research, educating policymakers, orchestrating public education campaigns, and developing strategic partnerships with business, research, and advocacy groups in the United States and internationally.

title: Determining the Economic Impact of Protecting and Restoring the Great Lakes
geographic_focus: Ohio, Wisconsin, Indiana, Minnesota, Illinois, Michigan, Pennsylvania, New York
description: The Great Lakes Initiative, a federally funded effort, has supported more than 3,000 ecosystem restoration projects in the Great Lakes Basin with $2.4 billion. The time has come to conduct an analysis of the economic benefits associated with the initiative, essentially calculating its return on investment. The Great Lakes Commission will arrange for such an analysis to be completed by a group of highly respected economists using robust economic modelling techniques. The grantee will broadly distribute the results of the analysis.

title: General Purposes
description: The Village Information Center was established in 1976 and has published hundreds of issues of the “East Village Magazine”. This monthly nonprofit publication provides Flint residents and nonprofit groups with news that affects the quality of life in neighborhoods. There is a companion website that offers the community access to news captured in the magazine, as well as new information that does not make the magazine’s publishing deadline. Between the printed magazine and the online portal, the grantee has a readership of approximately 15,000 people.

title: Whaley Historic House Restoration Project
description: The Whaley Historic House Museum, located at the entrance of the Flint Cultural Center, serves to preserve Flint’s rich cultural history and widespread accessibility to the arts and humanities through engagement with our community. In the fall of 2015, the structure suffered a devastating fire. This grant to Whaley Historical House Association, Inc., will help restore the museum building to its pre-fire condition and, where possible, historically accurate exterior and interior.

title: Sustaining the Great Lakes Project
geographic_focus: Minnesota, Illinois, Wisconsin, Indiana, Michigan, New York, Pennsylvania, Ohio
description: The Great Lakes provide habitat for fish and wildlife, serve as economic engines for various industries, and supply recreational opportunities and drinking water for more than 40 million people. The National Wildlife Federation, a national conservation group with a strong presence in the Great Lakes Basin, partners with regional and state-level organizations to protect and restore the Great Lakes ecosystem. The grantee led efforts to pass and implement the Great Lakes Compact, an interstate agreement that limits out-of-basin diversions and calls on all Great Lakes states to effectively manage their water resources. The grantee also plays an important role in improving Great Lakes water quality by addressing threats such as invasive species, toxic pollution, and harmful algal blooms. This renewal grant will allow the grantee to continue and deepen these efforts to protect and restore the Great Lakes, particularly through informing policy and monitoring implementation, providing scientific information and assistance, leading public education, and building a diverse base of collaborators.

title: African Development Bank Energy Financing
description: Christian Aid is a nonprofit organization with more than 70 years’ experience working to support communities and help them to thrive. Based in the United Kingdom, the grantee works globally to eradicate the causes of poverty. Under this grant, they will support and strengthen the capacity of the African Coalition for Sustainable Energy and Access network to address international financial institution lending in the energy sector. The focus will be on encouraging investments in distributed renewable energy, with an emphasis on developing livelihoods for rural Africans who are not connected to the electricity grid.

title: Flint School of Performing Arts Scholarships
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide funds for scholarships to the Flint School of Performing Arts at the Flint Institute of Music. Scholarship and tuition assistance funds provide resources so that all students can participate in the dance and music programs at the Flint Institute of Music. The grantee offers a wide variety of music, dance, and theater experiences through the Flint School of Performing Arts, Flint Youth Theatre, and the Flint Symphony Orchestra.

title: Endowment Fund
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide funds for the Flint Institute of Music Endowment Fund. The Endowment Fund provides unrestricted resources for the operations and programming of the Flint Institute of Music. The grantee offers a wide variety of music, dance, and theater experiences through the Flint School of Performing Arts, Flint Youth Theatre, and the Flint Symphony Orchestra.

title: Instructional Innovation Fund
description: This grant will provide funding for the Instructional Innovation Fund at Flint Community Schools. The fund is designed to provide teachers with opportunities and funding for innovative ideas and teaching practices. Projects could include ideas in technology, literature, math, reading, and science. All proposals will be judged by a team and will benefit both teachers and students within the district.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued general purpose support to the Philanthropy Roundtable, a national association of over 600 foundations, families, and individual philanthropists from across the United States. The grantee serves individual philanthropists and foundations that are refining their philanthropic strategies to maximize the impact of their resources, as well as emerging donors and entrepreneurs who are developing their philanthropic plans. It provides a variety of programs and services including a national conference, topical meetings, publication of Philanthropy magazine, thematic publications, and public policy work. Major issue-focused thematic areas include K-12 education, economic opportunity, veterans, character formation, civic education, and health. While the grantee is currently undergoing a strategic planning process, over 2019-2021 it anticipates continuing its educational and convening services and its vigorous support of public policy efforts to defend philanthropic freedom through its Alliance for Charitable Reform project.

title: Reading, Language Arts, and Social Studies Curriculum
description: This grant will enable Flint Community Schools to purchase new reading, language arts, and social studies curriculum across kindergarten through 12th grade. Much of the Flint Community Schools curriculum is outdated, putting teachers and students at a disadvantage in meeting desired proficiency levels. The district is working on a districtwide turnaround effort with the aim of improving academic outcomes so students graduate ready for college and career. Updated curriculum will help ensure teachers and students have access to current academic content and instructional materials to help meet that goal.

title: Mott Middle/Early College Replication
description: This grant will support Mott Community College to continue the research, outreach and replication of early/middle college high schools and programs in Michigan and nationally. As an early adopter of the early/middle college high school model, Mott Community College is entering its thirty-third year of offering a blended secondary and post-secondary school design for students that struggle in traditional high schools. The college responds to requests for establishing early/middle college schools and programs at high schools, community colleges, universities and career and technical education centers.

title: General Purposes
description: The Social Change Assistance Trust is a grantmaking organization established in 1984 that predominantly funds rural organizations in order to improve the quality of life in their communities. It supports programs that address human rights, gender equity, HIV/AIDS, and local economic development. Past support assisted the grantee to fund and support community advice offices in the Eastern Cape, Western Cape, Northern Cape, and Free State provinces. This grant increase will allow the grantee to collaborate with the Association of Community Advice Offices of South Africa to offer training to about 150 paralegals who work in community advice offices across South Africa.

title: Economic and Entrepreneurial Outreach
description: This grant will support the Economic Development Administration Center for Community and Economic Development at the University of Michigan-Flint. The center’s mission is to coordinate, inform, and contribute to economic development efforts that cultivate innovation and advance high-growth entrepreneurship in the seven-county, I-69 Thumb Region. Additionally, the center supports applied research projects and provides technical assistance to economic development organizations, private businesses, and nonprofits.

title: Economic and Entrepreneurial Outreach
description: This grant will support the Economic Development Administration Center for Community and Economic Development at the University of Michigan-Flint. The center’s mission is to coordinate, inform, and contribute to economic development efforts that cultivate innovation and advance high-growth entrepreneurship in the seven-county, I-69 Thumb Region. Additionally the center supports applied research projects and provides technical assistance to economic development organizations, private businesses, and nonprofits.

title: Love The Land, Pass It On Stewardship Endowment
description: The C. S. Mott Nature Preserve is one of the largest privately owned nature preserves in Michigan. The Grand Traverse Regional Land Conservancy, a widely-respected land trust based in Traverse City, protected the property in 2003 when it was under development threat. Mott’s permanently restricted gift to endow the long-term stewardship of the property will guarantee that the preserve will be forever managed in an effective and responsible fashion. The stewardship funds will help cover the cost of resource management, property management, trail maintenance, infrastructure maintenance, and capital infrastructure replacement.

title: Love the Land Campaign Universal Access Trails
description: Investing in important community conservation and access to nature projects represents the leading edge of the land trust movement. Universal access trails are particularly important for individuals, young and old, who face mobility challenges. With partial support from the Mott Foundation, the Grand Traverse Regional Land Conservancy will build universal access trails for two of its properties: the C. S. Mott Nature Preserve and Arcadia Marsh.

title: Teen C.E.O. Initiative
description: This renewal grant will provide support to Mott Community College for the Teen Creating Economic Opportunity Initiative. The project focuses on providing youth ages 14-18 with the entrepreneurial skills, abilities and mindset that will prepare them to succeed in the 21st century economy. Additionally, students will develop a higher education career pathway plan in the area of business that they have identified. The project will culminate with students showcasing their businesses to the public.

title: Engaging Youth in Service
description: This grant will support Youth Service America to engage up to 500,000 young people throughout the United States through 10,000 quality youth-led service projects. Youth Service America will focus efforts on bolstering youth engagement in Flint and Genesee County and across the United States by working with schools, afterschool programs, and nonprofit organizations.

title: GAPS: Transition Program
description: This grant will enable Mott Community College to continue and expand the GAPS: Transition Program. The program, which is a dropout intervention strategy developed by Mott Middle Early College High School staff, assists students in making the transition from middle school to the more rigorous middle/early college high school setting. During the grant period, the grantee will expand the GAPS: Transition Program to year-round and add high school to college services for students transitioning into higher education.

title: Double Up Food Bucks Project
description: This grant will provide additional support to the Fair Food Network’s Double Up Food Bucks Project in Flint. The project provides incentives for supplemental nutrition assistance program recipients to purchase fresh fruits and vegetables and dairy products at the Flint Farmers’ Market and grocery stores in Flint. Good nutrition, especially foods high in iron, calcium, and vitamin C, can help mitigate the impact of lead exposure to Flint children and adults.

title: Early Childhood Capacity Building
description: This grant increase will provide funding to the Community Foundation of Greater Flint as it supports the expansion of early childhood education in Flint. Expanding access to high quality, early childhood education has become an urgent priority as a result of the Flint water crisis. The grantee will employ an executive director to manage the Flint Early Childhood Collaborative, a project with the aim of increasing access to and the quality of early childhood education in Flint through strategic planning, research, advocacy, and participation in the Educare Learning Network.

title: General Purposes
description: The Village Information Center was established in 1976 and has published hundreds of issues of the “East Village Magazine.” The monthly nonprofit publication provides Flint residents and nonprofit groups with news that affects the quality of life in neighborhoods. A companion website offers access to news captured in the magazine, as well as new information that does not make the magazine’s publishing deadline. Between the printed magazine and the online portal, the grantee has a readership of approximately 15,000 people.

title: Early Childhood Capacity Building
description: This grant will provide funding to the Community Foundation of Greater Flint as it supports the expansion of early childhood education in Flint. Expanding access to high-quality early childhood education was always important for the city, but became even more important following the water crisis. The grantee employs an executive director to manage the Flint Early Childhood Collaborative, a project that aims to increase access to and the quality of early childhood education in Flint through strategic planning, research, advocacy, and participation in the Educare Learning Network.

title: Flint STRIVE Academy Youth Empowerment Program
description: This grant to Specialized Employment Services, Inc. will support the Flint STRIVE Academy Youth Empowerment Program for at-risk youth ages 14-18. The program provides young people with a summertime employment experience and follow-up support services during the school year. Through attitudinal training, skill enhancement, mentoring and tutoring, the goal is to encourage youth to complete high school and help with making informed career decisions. As part of their experience, students will participate in a service project distributing bottled water to Flint residents.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant increase provides general purpose support to Derecho Ambiente y Recursos Naturales, which works to monitor energy and infrastructure policies and projects and their impacts in Peru and the Peruvian Amazon. The grantee also provides legal and technical assistance to indigenous communities and nongovernmental organizations and networks to enable them to promote more environmentally and socially sustainable practices for energy development in Peru and across the Amazon River Basin.

title: Monitoring Infrastructure Investments in Argentina
location: Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires, Argentina
description: This grant increase will support Fundacion Ambiente y Recursos Naturales to monitor the effective implementation of environmental, transparency, and public participation policies impacting energy projects in Argentina supported by international financial institutions. Information will be disseminated to policymakers, media, and the public to shape sustainable energy policies and build organizational networks across South America. The grantee is a nongovernmental environmental organization based in Buenos Aires that has worked for the past 27 years to promote sustainable development through policy, law, and civic engagement.

title: Strengthening Evidence, Engagement and Impact on Energy Poverty
description: Over the next year, Practical Action will explore the expansion of its East Africa work promoting clean energy access to include Tanzania. It will identify existing actors in the sector, political and economic factors that influence the sector, and opportunities to strengthen the sector. The aim is to provide support to local stakeholders in Tanzania as well as understand how the Poor People’s Energy Outlook, one of the grantee’s primary contributions to the field, can be used to assist policy reform work in the country. The grantee expects its intervention in Tanzania will create an environment where entrepreneurs and the private sector can confidently make informed and sustainable investments in clean energy access. This grant increase will lead to recommendations and plans for potential activities that the grantee may undertake to add value to the ongoing efforts of others working on energy access in Tanzania.

title: Clean Energy Access in Andes/Amazon
grantee: Centro de Estudios y Promocion del Desarrollo
description: The Centro de Estudios y Promocion del Desarrollo is a 51-year-old Peruvian nongovernmental development institution that works with poor rural communities to introduce innovative renewable energy solutions to improve health, education, quality of life, and to protect the environment. The purpose of this project is to draw upon lessons learned from the previous project to promote and disseminate access and use of renewable energy to expand productive economic uses in remote rural communities in the Peruvian Andes.

title: General Purposes
description: The Village Information Center was established in 1976 and has published hundreds of issues of the East Village Magazine.The monthly nonprofit publication provides Flint residents and nonprofit groups with news that affects the quality of life in neighborhoods. A companion website offers access to news captured in the magazine, as well as new information that does not make the magazine’s publishing deadline. Between the printed magazine and the online portal, the grantee has a readership of approximately 15,000 people.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant increase will enable the Afterschool Alliance to provide additional support to the afterschool field, including the statewide afterschool networks, to respond to the challenging policy landscape and proposed cuts to afterschool programs. Specifically, this grant increase will: 1) support the implementation of a coordinated communications campaign to highlight the positive benefits of afterschool programs for students, families, and communities; and 2) provide additional capacity to the statewide networks to respond to the challenging policy environment.

title: Study on Afterschool Access and Participation
description: This grant will enable Marquette University to carry out further research on black families’ perception of and participation in afterschool programs by engaging 600 low-income and working-class parents in five cities: Baltimore, Cleveland, Dallas, Los Angeles, and St. Louis.

title: Collaboration for Healthy and Thriving Students
description: This grant to the Illinois State Board of Education will support a new state initiative, the Collaboration for Healthy and Thriving Students, to further advance afterschool and community school practices, services, and student outcomes. Pilot sites will implement coordinated educational services, including reading, math, science, and arts and music activities to create a model program that can be shared with statewide afterschool networks.

title: Community Advice Office Sustainability Project
grantee: National Alliance for the Development of Community Advice Offices
description: The National Alliance for the Development of Community Advice Offices was initiated in 2005 as an alliance of seven civil society organizations aimed at strengthening and sustaining the community advice office sector in South Africa. It is committed to the long-term development of community advice offices as a way of ensuring access to justice within poor communities. Community advice offices provide free, basic legal advice and other social services to poor people. Past support assisted the grantee to link advice offices with relevant training opportunities and to conduct research to help articulate the value of community advice offices. This grant increase will enable the grantee to improve its institutional capacity, and to provide direct support to community advice offices in the Eastern Cape, Gauteng, and Mpumalanga provinces.

title: General Purposes
description: The Casual Workers Advice Office was established in 2011 to give free legal advice to workers who have been dismissed or face other labor violations by their employers in South Africa. Past support assisted the Casual Workers Advice Office to 1) raise awareness of new labor rights among precarious workers and support them in accessing these rights; 2) support workers whose disputes have been referred to the Commission for Conciliation, Mediation and Arbitration and bargaining councils; 3) produce resources and general educational materials; and 4) hire additional staff and train existing staff. Ongoing support will allow the grantee to continue to offer advice and support to workers whose rights have been violated, undertake litigation by using its in-house counsel, and train and support community advice offices on various aspects of labor laws.

title: Florida Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Children’s Forum, which coordinates the Florida Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) building champions by hosting convenings throughout the state; 2) developing resources and hosting trainings on STEM, food security and third grade literacy for the afterschool field; 3) convening leaders to explore opportunities related to entrepreneurship and college and career readiness through afterschool programs; and 4) supporting the promotion and distribution of the Mizzen by Mott App.

title: Light for a Better Life
grantee: IDEAAS-Instituto para o Desenvolvimento de Energias Alternativas e da Auto Sustentabilidade
description: The Instituto para o Desenvolvimento de Energias Alternativas e da Auto Sustentabilidade is a Brazilian nonprofit organization that develops renewable energy solutions for remote and rural communities. Over the past project period, the organization made progress on a solar energy model providing kits to remote communities in the Brazilian Amazonian states of Para and Amazonas. Over this renewal period, the grantee will consolidate the business and finance model and monitor and evaluate the impact of the project since it began in 2015.

title: North Carolina Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: Public School Forum of North Carolina
description: This grant will support the Public School Forum of North Carolina, which coordinates the North Carolina Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) building champions by hosting regional convenings; 2) providing professional development opportunities to afterschool programs locally, regionally, statewide and virtually; 3) developing toolkits on professional development, implementation and evaluation for the afterschool field; and 4) supporting the promotion and distribution of the Mizzen by Mott App.

title: Monitoring Hydropower Impacts in the Amazon
description: The Getulio Vargas Foundation’s Center for Sustainability Studies is a higher education institution dedicated to promoting sustainable development in Brazil. Over the past grant period, the center worked with stakeholders and partners to develop a permanent institutional capacity to monitor the social and environmental impacts of the large-scale Belo Monte hydroelectric power project. Over the next project period, the Belo Monte monitoring activities will continue. Efforts will also be made to transfer the lessons learned to similar projects planned for the Tapajos River basin in order to improve the related social and environmental governance practices.

title: Maine Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the University of Southern Maine, which coordinates the Maine Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) strengthening statewide partnerships to support positive youth development and academic enrichment opportunities in afterschool and summer settings; 2) expanding network membership and developing afterschool champions to prioritize funding opportunities for high-quality programs; 3) providing leadership development to out-of-school time professionals through strategic partnerships; and 4) supporting the promotion and distribution of the Mizzen by Mott App.

title: TFN Global - Developing TFN in CEE/Russia
description: The program goal is to increase the level and impact of individual philanthropy in Central and Eastern Europe. To this end, Funding Network, a giving circle based in the U.K., will strengthen the capacity of its current partner organizations in the region and establish partnerships with new organizations interested in starting similar giving circles in their countries. More specifically, the grantee will provide information, technical assistance, and mentoring and facilitate international contacts and exchanges among its partners. The grantee will also publish and disseminate success stories and lessons learned from the development of these giving circles in Central and Eastern Europe. With this grant increase, the grantee will partner with another Mott grantee, the U.S.-based Johnson Center for Philanthropy, to assess the impact of its giving circle model in Central and Eastern Europe. Established in London in 2002 by a group of private philanthropists with the mission to increase the level, scope, and impact of charitable giving, the grantee now works in 15 countries around the world.

title: Rhode Island Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the United Way of Rhode Island which coordinates the Rhode Island Statewide Afterschool Network to continue development of policy, partnerships and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) partnering with the Rhode Island Community Foundation to support new state education agency afterschool initiatives; 2) developing and launching a quality afterschool STEM framework to improve quality; 3) providing professional development and training opportunities to afterschool programs; and 4) supporting the promotion and distribution of the Mizzen by Mott app.

title: Building Broader Communities in the Americas
description: The project goal is to foster partnerships between community foundations in Latin America and the Caribbean and their counterparts in the United States and Canada, using interested stakeholders, such as immigrant groups, as channels of interconnectivity. Project activities will include: 1) exchanges of staff, boards, and donors of participating community foundations; 2) working group meetings and outreach to new stakeholders; 3) applied research, such as community-specific mapping exercises, mapping of corporate interests in the hemisphere and investigation of government programs that support diaspora/sending community partnerships; 4) tool development and sharing of best practices of supporting community philanthropy in a transnational context; and 5) a Leadership Fellows Program. The project is managed by the Inter-American Foundation, an independent United States government agency created by Congress in 1969 to channel development assistance directly to the organized poor in Latin America and the Caribbean. A grant increase will allow for the engagement of a professional communications firm to establish clear messaging, develop information products, and develop a strategic communications plan for the initiative.

title: Confronting the Past in Serbia
description: The project goal is to deepen democratic values in Serbia and the Balkan region by strengthening the rule of law, respect for human rights, and civic participation. To this end, Women in Black will increase the active role of women in constructive efforts to deal with the legacies of the wars of the 1990s in the former Yugoslavia, bolster women’s participation in social and political decision making processes, and expand women’s impact on shaping post-conflict society and civil society in Serbia and the wider region. During the prior grant period, activities included organizing visits to memorials and commemorations of war crimes sites; organizing regular educational discussion groups; supporting new community-based women’s groups; using exhibitions, street theater, and public actions to raise awareness; launching a new regional initiative to provide women a platform for publicly stating facts about the crimes committed against them and their consequences; and providing training and support to women activists across Serbia. Based in Belgrade, Serbia, Women in Black was established in 1991 as a network of women activists who opposed the wars in the former Yugoslavia.

title: Community Development in Ukraine Through Community School Programs
description: The Ukrainian Step by Step Foundation will work with the Ukrainian Ministry of Education at the latter’s invitation to assist in advancing school reforms aimed in part at increasing community engagement with schools in Ukraine. Specifically, the grantee will work with the ministry to adapt the Community School Quality Assessment Standards as the basis for broader institutional audits of schools across the Ukrainian education system. The standards, developed by the grantee and international partners over many years and used in over 600 schools in Ukraine to date, rely on significant participation of all school stakeholders to assess school performance, classroom attainment, and community relevance. This grant increase will allow the grantee to adapt the standards, train school administrators and regional educational officials, and conduct pilot institutional audits in 12 schools prior to wider rollout of the scheme.

title: Grantmakers East Forum
description: This grant supports an affinity group of the European Foundation Centre to improve the effectiveness of grantmaking in Central and Eastern Europe and the former Soviet Union and to encourage new donor activity in the region. To this end, the grantee will organize the annual meeting of the group, called the Grantmakers East Forum, for interested grantmakers and donors working in this region. In 2018, the meeting will take place in Budapest, Hungary, and will focus on the theme of shrinking civic space. In 2016, the center organized the forum’s annual meeting in Hamburg, Germany, and in 2017, it took place in Vienna, Austria. These annual meetings provided opportunities for networking and information exchange, encouraged development of new philanthropic initiatives, and promoted good grantmaking practices. Based in Brussels, Belgium, the European Foundation Centre is an international association of foundations and corporate funders dedicated to strengthening European philanthropy.

title: Community Foundation Development Project
description: SGS Consulting provides consulting services to civil society organizations, multilateral agencies, and private foundations. Over the years, the grantee has provided technical assistance to organizations working in the philanthropy development and community advice office sectors in South Africa. Past support enabled the grantee to: 1) support organizations working in the two sectors to build knowledge of their respective fields; 2) increase the flow of resources; and 3) address capacity challenges within the sector. Additionally, the grantee provided technical support to network organizations in the respective sectors to strengthen the fields and increase learning. During this grant period, the grantee will build on the knowledge gained as a technical support facility to support the expansion and strengthening of community foundations in the southern Africa region. It will do this by identifying existing community foundation support organizations and supporting their efforts to grow the community foundation field.

title: Charity & Security Network
description: The Charity & Security Network helps nonprofit organizations promote and protect their ability to carry out programs that support peace and human rights, aid civilians in areas of disaster and armed conflict, and build democratic governance. The grantee does this by 1) convening stakeholders and sponsoring dialogue; 2) promoting legal frameworks based on protecting the positive contribution civil society makes to human security; and 3) coordinating advocacy to support national security rules that respect the work of legitimate civil society organizations. During the grant period, the grantee plans to focus on ensuring nonprofit organizations’ financial access to the international banking system, guarding against any new restrictions that may be placed on United States nonprofits, and assisting with the implementation of revised guidance to nonprofit organizations around the world by the Financial Action Task Force. The Charity & Security Network is a project of NEO Philanthropy, a funder intermediary launched in 1983 as Public Interest Projects.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Mexico, Texas, New Mexico, California, Arizona
description: The U.S.-Mexico Border Philanthropy Partnership is an independent, binational entity whose members include foundations, corporate giving programs, philanthropic individuals, academics, and nonprofit organizations. Its mission is to support a network of organizations that build prosperity through leadership, collaboration, and philanthropy in the U.S.-Mexico border region. Over the past eight years, the grantee has grown from 45 to over 300 members, provided capacity building technical assistance to members, facilitated connections between organizations from various sectors, and significantly raised awareness of cross-border issues. Goals for the next year include leading and advocating on transborder issues of interest to members, strengthening the philanthropic capacity of transborder communities, and strengthening the grantee’s own internal capacity and infrastructure.

title: Community Philanthropy Development in Brazil
grantee: Institute for the Development of Social Investment
description: The project goal is to promote community philanthropy in Brazil. The Institute for the Development of Social Investment will conduct research on organizations that have the potential to become community philanthropy organizations in the state of Sao Paolo, Brazil. Based on its investigations, the grantee will assess and select a set of ten organizations according to a development scale designed with input from national and international experts and convene a group of the five to eight most promising organizations for a three-session workshop. The workshop sessions will focus on understanding the community philanthropy organizations’ needs and collectively designing an ideal support platform for the development of community foundations in Brazil. Founded in 1999, the Institute for the Development of Social Investment is a philanthropy service organization that promotes private social investment and strategic philanthropy, primarily in Brazil but also throughout Latin America, and it is an affiliate of the Charities Aid Foundation Global Alliance.

title: Kansas Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: University of Kansas Center for Research, Inc.
description: This grant will support the University of Kansas Center for Research, Inc. which coordinates the Kansas Statewide Afterschool Network to continue development of policy, partnerships and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) developing a data collection strategy to showcase the impact, value and needs of afterschool programs; 2) providing technical assistance and training to afterschool professionals on the Kansas afterschool quality guidelines and tools; 3) implementing strategies to cultivate stronger school-based/school-linked programs; and 4) supporting the promotion and distribution of the Mizzen by Mott App.

title: Upper Peninsula Energy Planning Project
description: The Superior Watershed Partnership is a Marquette-based Great Lakes nonprofit which serves the communities and tribes in the 15-county region of the Michigan’s Upper Peninsula as a trusted regional leader on environmental matters. This role is important given the region’s pressing challenges regarding reliable and affordable electricity. The grantee is helping to lay the groundwork for a regional energy plan that will chart the transition to a new system that enables the region to manage its own energy future. Through additional research, technical analysis, and stakeholder outreach, this renewal grant will allow the grantee to complete the collaborative development of a regional energy framework that will serve as a guide for a comprehensive energy plan.

title: Hawaii Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the University of Hawaii which coordinates the Hawaii Statewide Afterschool Network to continue development of policy, partnerships and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) developing a comprehensive communications and outreach plan to build public awareness about the importance of afterschool; 2) surveying the afterschool field to gather information regarding staff capacity and professional development needs; 3) expanding training on trauma-informed care, social and emotional learning and academic supports; and 4) supporting the promotion and distribution of the Mizzen by Mott App.

title: Wisconsin Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: Marshfield Clinic Research Institute, a Division of Marshfield Clinic, Inc.
description: This grant will support the Marshfield Clinic, which coordinates the Wisconsin Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) building champions by hosting a community engagement process to expand afterschool programming in rural Wisconsin; 2) creating an online accessible data warehouse and dashboard for afterschool programs; 3) expanding training and resources on trauma-informed practice within the state and nationally; and 4) supporting the promotion and distribution of the Mizzen by Mott App.

title: Event Policing and Public Safety
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide funds to support public safety enforcement and traffic patrolling at festivals in downtown Flint. Public safety policing is an essential component of the success of the festivals that take place in the downtown Flint area and attract thousands of exhibitors and festival goers. The City of Flint is not in a financial position to provide the necessary additional police services due to a decline in municipal revenues.

title: Tennessee Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the United Ways of Tennessee, which coordinates the Tennessee Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) increasing communications activities to build public awareness about the importance of afterschool; 2) developing and launching quality assessment tools and implementation resources; 3) providing technical assistance and professional development opportunities to afterschool programs; and 4) supporting the promotion and distribution of the Mizzen by Mott App.

title: Missouri Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the University of Missouri – Columbia which coordinates the Missouri Statewide Afterschool Network to continue development of policy, partnerships and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) creating an afterschool youth ambassador program to educate key champions on the importance of afterschool; 2) developing an online training directory for afterschool professionals; 3) creating a statewide or regional approach to providing afterschool programs access to high tech STEM equipment, particularly for rural programs; and 4) supporting the promotion and distribution of the Mizzen by Mott App.

title: Great Lakes Water Infrastructure Project
description: The Center for Neighborhood Technology is a nonprofit organization based in Chicago that designs and implements sustainable development strategies that help cities offer a high quality of life for residents. This grant increase will support the work of a consultant to conduct an organizational assessment to analyze the structure and operations of the grantee to help maximize its performance and impact. While the organizational assessment is being conducted, the grantee will continue to expand its work to address water infrastructure challenges, such as providing safe and affordable drinking water to low-income families.

title: Northeast Minnesota Program
description: The Minnesota Environmental Partnership, an independent statewide network of more than 80 groups, has had a long-term commitment to Lake Superior through its Northeast Minnesota Program. With Mott support, the grantee has worked to reform freshwater quality and quantity policies, educate the public and decisionmakers, and build the capacity of grassroots groups. This grant increase will allow the partnership to further build its program staff capacity, as well as provide professional development services to membership organizations, and produce a report that assesses two state water infrastructure programs.

title: General Purposes
description: The Flint River and its tributaries are an important recreational resource for the region’s residents, while also providing important habitat for a variety of freshwater species and other wildlife. The Flint River Watershed Coalition works to protect the Flint River and its tributaries. With renewal support, the grantee will maintain all of its education and outreach efforts, as well as attend to its own organizational development needs. This will include efforts to enhance the urban sections of the river in Flint and support the work of chapters throughout the coalition.

title: Mayors Innovation Project
geographic_focus: Indiana, Ohio, Michigan, Wisconsin, New York, Pennsylvania, Illinois, Minnesota
description: The Mayors Innovation Project, an initiative of the University of Wisconsin, is a network of engaged municipalities and utility leaders with strong connections to national experts. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has provided technical support in Great Lakes cities on water and sustainability challenges and has built a body of expertise assisting cities in thinking holistically in an integrated fashion when facing water management challenges. Renewed support will enable the grantee to advance water affordability programs in Great Lakes cities, while learning from the best practices across the nation. Over the next two years, the grantee will conduct research, publish written findings, organize and host events, including one in Flint or southeast Michigan, and provide technical assistance directly to select cities on the critical question of how cities can provide clean, safe, and affordable water for their residents.

title: Drinking Water Infrastructure Program
description: The Bipartisan Policy Center has a solid reputation among Washington, D.C., thought leaders as a credible source of information, analyses, and policy recommendations. They have extended that reputation into the infrastructure space and are regularly sought out for expertise on water. Previous support from the Mott Foundation has enabled the grantee to elevate discussion about a federal role in water infrastructure upgrades and the critical issue of water affordability. While progress has been made, awareness and action to address these problems still fall short, even though nearly every city and town in America is affected. With this grant, the Bipartisan Policy Center will begin to catalog water affordability strategies nationwide and explore the potential of a federal affordability program based on an energy-sector model, the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Program. Such a model holds promise as a potential solution to assist residents of cities in the Great Lakes region.

title: Michigan Land and Water Policy Project
description: The Michigan United Conservation Clubs is the largest statewide conservation organization in the nation. Its membership includes conservationists, hunters, anglers, and trappers. With previous support, the grantee has played a key role in numerous policy discussions and decisions of importance to the Great Lakes, including funding for the Great Lakes Restoration Initiative and protecting the Great Lakes from the release of invasive species from ballast water. They undertook ambitious research to document the contribution of hunting and fishing to Michigan’s recreation economy, and they facilitated coalition efforts to reduce hydroelectric facilities’ impacts on downstream water. With renewed support, the grantee will continue monitoring hydroelectric operations; raise awareness and lead education efforts on Asian carp and other invasive species in coordination with other state organizations; create maps of water quality concerns in Michigan; and extend its work on the economic benefits of hunting, fishing, and trapping in Michigan.

title: Homeowner Occupied Repair Program
