description: This grant will provide support to Genesee County Habitat for Humanity to expand the work of its Homeowner Occupied Repair Program into the neighborhood surrounding the Educare Early Childhood Center currently under construction on the Durant-Tuuri-Mott campus. Residential improvements to homes will be targeted to the streets directly bordering the educational facility in an effort to fully meet the needs of the residential community. This work aligns with a core tenant of Genesee County Habitat for Humanity’s mission of bringing people together to build community.

title: Fund for Democracy and Solidarity in Europe
description: The program goal is to promote, protect, and reinvigorate the space for civic engagement in Europe. To this end, the Network of European Foundations for Innovative Cooperation will manage a grantmaking fund to: 1) support prodemocratic and proEuropean civil society organizations facing hostile environments; and 2) strengthen trust in democratic institutions in Europe. The Fund for Democracy and Solidarity in Europe will leverage knowledge and financial resources from at least ten foundations active in Europe to support innovative approaches responding to the closing space trend. The program will operate throughout the European Union and will focus on countries where the democratic system is under stress and where support for a liberal democratic system is being questioned.

title: Endowment Funds
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to the Community Foundation of Greater Flint will add to the endowment funds established for the benefit of the Flint Cultural Center Corporation, Flint Institute of Arts, and Flint Institute of Music. These endowments will provide needed operating support to these important community institutions. The grantee continues to serve a vital role in the charitable and nonprofit community in the Flint area by encouraging giving, as well as by providing grants and programs that improve the quality of life for all Genesee County residents and focus on the critical issues in the community. The Flint Cultural Center offers a variety of programs; live performances; hands-on learning experiences; music, dance, drama, and art instruction; and hosts community events for area residents of all ages and backgrounds.

title: Endowment Funds
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to the Flint Cultural Center Corporation will provide endowment funds to the organization including Sloan*Longway and The Whiting. Endowments provide needed operating support to ensure an array of exhibits, programming, and performances for area residents and visitors. The institutions on the Flint Cultural Center campus are essential to the quality of life of the region and provide educational opportunities for all ages.

title: Endowment Funds
description: This grant to the Community Foundation of Greater Flint will provide operating funds to the organization. The grantee provides grant support to local nonprofits, leadership on community problems, capacity for early education and food scarcity initiatives, and key support for water crisis recovery. Endowment support for operations will increase the grantee’s capacity to play an important role in the Flint community.

title: General Purposes
description: Many small, off-grid renewable energy companies have been launched over the past decade to address the energy access challenge in Sub-Saharan Africa. Most do not have access to financing that allows them to address needed innovations. To address these innovation challenges for the energy access sector, Stichting EnAccess was established. This general purpose funding will support its organizational development, as well as initial open source tools to accelerate energy access solutions that can drive sustainable, inclusive, and economically transformative development in off-grid communities throughout the world.

title: Greening Chinese Development Finance
description: China has become a major development financier over the past decade and has faced negative impacts related to some of its investments, which has led to some public opposition to further Chinese investments. Adding to these major investment flows, China launched the Belt and Road Initiative in 2013. It is an ambitious initiative to expand China’s global trade and foreign policy relations by bringing energy, transport, and communication infrastructure to link all of Asia to Europe, the Middle East, and Africa. Such an ambitious project is likely to have environmental and social impacts; thus the World Wildlife Fund in the U.S. and China have been working to engage with the Chinese development finance institutions and government to address these potential impacts. This grant will allow the grantee and World Wildlife Fund-China to develop a more collaborative strategy with other Chinese organizations to propose options for “greening the Belt and Road Initiative”. In addition, new communication mechanisms for monitoring and sharing information on investments for this initiative will be developed.

title: Sharing Indian Social Entrepreneurs' Lessons for African Off Grid Energy
description: Energy is widely acknowledged as a key tool to enhance economic growth and a country’s development. In Africa the predominant model of electricity generation and distribution is centralized, providing only 45 percent of the continent with electricity. In rural areas, less than 30 percent of the population has access to electricity from the centralized grids. For rural Tanzania, it is even more stark with less than 17 percent of the rural areas having access to energy. The Solar Energy Light Company Foundation, with 20 years of experience in off-grid energy access work in rural India, has supported key Tanzanian organizations to provide capacity building and business mentoring functions for young Tanzanian entrepreneurs. Over the next two years, the grantee will continue its ongoing work supporting the development of local energy entrepreneurs and increasing their capacities for energy access design, development, and deployment.

title: Building an Inclusive Financial Ecosystem for End Users and Enterprises
description: The Global Fund for Community Foundations is a global, grassroots grantmaker, established in 2009 to assist local philanthropy. It will work with the Tanzanian Association of Microfinance Institutions to provide training and capacity building for Tanzanian financial service providers to support micro-, small, and medium enterprises in the energy sector. Through this grant, capacity building programs will be established to help local-level finance service providers understand clean energy technologies as well as financing innovations for the renewable energy sector in Tanzania.

title: Solar Electrician and Entrepreneurship Training
description: The Salesian Missions have been providing education and technical training to poor children around the globe since 1947. The Salesians began its work to establish vocational training and youth empowerment centers across Tanzania in 1980. They are now interested in expanding their vocational training to address the energy access deficit in Tanzania. Tanzania’s national electric grid reaches very few people, with only seven percent of its rural populations having access to electricity. To reach the rural areas, it is crucial that there are adequate technical skills to help develop, sustain, and maintain off-grid solar electric assets deployed to these areas. Through this grant, the grantee and its Don Bosco training centers in Tanzania will expand their electrician training in two sites to include a three-year certificate program in solar electric training, to develop technicians, innovators, and entrepreneurs for the off-grid solar energy sector.

title: Matembwe-Ikondo Mini-Grid: Learning from the Past, Preparing for the Future
description: Providing sustainable energy for all is critical for 21st-century socio-economic development. A key challenge for rural delivery of electricity is the expense and lack of financing for households to connect to the service. These barriers to connection make it difficult for off-grid renewable energy providers to grow their businesses and reach profitability. CEFA International Cooperation launched its first rural electrification project in 1986 and it is still thriving with expanded generating capacity and new businesses established. With this grant, the grantee and other outside university researchers will address the key factors that have determined this project’s success and test interventions that can magnify those successes. The project will identify and make widely available a set of best practices and guidelines for the development and management of rural mini-grids to facilitate faster replication throughout Tanzania.

title: Vaclav Havel Circle
description: This renewal grant will provide funding for the Vaclav Havel Circle, a project of the Forum 2000 Foundation. The Vaclav Havel Circle is an initiative that aims to support the values of democracy and respect of human rights; assist in the development of civil society; and encourage religious, cultural, and ethnic tolerance.

title: Mexican Philanthropy House
grantee: Centro Mexicano para la Filantropia, A.C.
description: Founded in 1988 and currently with 1584 members nationwide, Centro Mexicano para la Filantropia, A.C. promotes and articulates the philanthropic and social responsible participation of Mexican citizens, organizations, and companies to achieve a more equitable and prosperous society. This grant will support the construction of a facility called The House of Philanthropy and Corporate Social Responsibility in Mexico City. The facility is being built on a plot of land owned by the grantee, which also will own the facility that includes two buildings separated by a common courtyard and a cafeteria. The aim is to provide an innovative, attractive meeting place to network, communicate, incubate, and grow philanthropy and civil society.

title: Development Banks and Sustainable Development
geographic_focus: South America, Southern Asia, Africa, Southeastern Asia, China
description: China has established a new family of development finance institutions that rival the current multilateral development finance system. The impact made by the investments of these new institutions on ecosystems and community development has become a global issue. The Global Development Policy Center at Boston University has become a major research center analyzing these impacts and providing useful data for relevant Chinese ministries. Through this grant, the center will continue its collaborative research and policy dialogue with governments, civil society, the private sector, and development finance institutions. In addition, this grant will assist key Chinese think tanks in undertaking additional research and developing best practices to assist in establishing policies for more sustainable Chinese development finance.

title: Shine: Investing in Energy Access for All
description: Energy access is a prerequisite for economic development and offers transformative opportunities for the world’s poor. The challenge is meeting the energy needs of those living without electricity in a way that does not increase greenhouse gas emissions, as well as financing this energy revolution. To address the financing needs, a coalition of faith and philanthropic leaders have developed the Shine campaign, based at the New Venture Fund, dedicated to ending energy poverty by 2030. This grant will support the development of an organizational infrastructure and integrated funding strategies to encourage philanthropic and faith community investments into small off-grid renewable energy companies in Africa and Asia. In addition, a new community of practice for foundations will be established to share successes, failures, and possible areas of collaboration for grantmaking in the energy access space.

title: Idaho Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Jannus, Inc. which coordinates the Idaho Statewide Afterschool Network to continue development of policy, partnerships and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) increasing communications activities to build public awareness aboutthe importance of afterschool; 2) providing professional development and training opportunities in alignment with the state afterschool quality standards; 3) creating resources to assist afterschool programs in addressing equity and inclusion to ensure all youth have access to STEM; and 4) supporting the promotion and distribution of the Mizzen by Mott App.

title: Flint River Restoration Project
description: This grant will provide project support to the Genesee County Parks & Recreation Commission for the Flint River Restoration Project. Funds from this grant will be used for project management, design and engineering costs, and technical assistance. The project is the result of a broad group of diverse partners coming together to create a vision for the Flint riverfront as a unique community asset that is accessible and safe for all residents to utilize, drive economic opportunities, and enhance local infrastructure by removing the Hamilton Dam. The project will support the overall economic development opportunities for Flint by creating greater connectivity between the University of Michigan-Flint, downtown, and Kettering University; removing hazardous infrastructure; improving storm water and flood control systems; developing underutilized public property; and capping contamination at a former industrial site.

title: South Carolina Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the South Carolina Afterschool Alliance, which coordinates the South Carolina Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) enhancing data collection to showcase the impact, value and needs of afterschool programs; 2) engaging youth to develop more and better summer and afterschool opportunities to address the learning and opportunity lost during COVID-19; 3) developing training on racial equity for afterschool professionals, school and community leaders and stakeholders; and 4) supporting the promotion and distribution of the Mizzen by Mott App.

title: Arkansas Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Arkansas State University which coordinates the Arkansas Statewide Afterschool Network to continue development of policy, partnerships and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) increasing the reach and scope of out-of-school time program system building efforts at a state and grassroots level; 2) supporting stakeholders to map resources and plan program expansion through allocating state revenue through existing funding streams; 3) developing and implementing quality building strategies to increase the effectiveness of out-of-school time programs; and 4) supporting the promotion and distribution of the Mizzen by Mott App.

title: Global Philanthropy Program
description: This grant supports the Council on Foundations’ Global Philanthropy Program, which is framed around three pillars of activity: 1) effective cross-border grantmaking; 2) policy and regulation of cross-border grantmaking; and 3) global conversations and convening. This grant increase will support the first-ever North American Community Foundations Summit in Mexico City in February 2018. The conference is being co-organized by the Council on Foundations, Comunalia (alliance of Mexican community foundations), and Community Foundations of Canada. Founded in 1949, the Council on Foundations is a membership organization of private, community, and corporate foundations, primarily in the United States.

title: General Purposes
description: The Council on Foundations is a national membership organization of more than 700 private foundations, community foundations, and corporate funders. Its mission is to provide the opportunity, leadership, and tools needed by philanthropic organizations to expand, enhance, and sustain their ability to advance the common good. Its near-term organizational goals are to: 1) position the council as a strategic leader that advances effective and dynamic philanthropy; 2) build and cultivate a collaborative and diverse philanthropic network; 3) continue to grow an effective and nimble organizational structure, grounded in sound financial systems and processes; and 4) foster a creative, collaborative, and entrepreneurial internal culture that encourages individual investment, which lends to the collective success of the grantee. This grant increase will provide partial support to the grantee to conduct a planning exercise to examine various scenarios that could threaten civil society in the United States as a result of the current political and policy environment, and to provide recommendations on how and when the grantee could or should respond to such scenarios on behalf of the philanthropic sector.

title: Oregon Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: Oregon Association for the Education of Young Children
description: This grant will support the Oregon Association for the Education of Young Children, which coordinates the Oregon Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) developing a comprehensive communications and outreach plan to build public awareness around the importance of afterschool and summer programs; 2) leveraging research findings into policy recommendations for supporting high-quality afterschool and summer programs; 3) expanding professional development offerings to engage more diverse populations within the afterschool community; and 4) supporting the promotion and distribution of the Mizzen by Mott App.

title: Illinois Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Metropolitan Family Services which coordinates the Illinois Statewide Afterschool Network to continue development of policy, partnerships and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) increasing communications activities to build public awareness about the importance of afterschool; 2) developing white papers and materials to educate the public on the value of afterschool and opportunity for growth; 3) creating best practices and resources to help afterschool providers implement and utilize quality standards; and 4) supporting the promotion and distribution of the Mizzen by Mott App.

title: Texas Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: Texas Partnership for Out of School Time
description: This grant will support the Texas Partnership for Out of School Time which coordinates the Texas Statewide Afterschool Network to continue development of policy, partnerships and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) establishing a corporate advisory council to help advise and leverage resources for the network; 2) conducting a mapping project of afterschool programs across the state; 3) cultivating and convening regional afterschool networks to share information and best practices for the field; and 4) supporting the promotion and distribution of the Mizzen by Mott App.

title: New Hampshire Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: Southeastern Regional Education Service Center, Inc.
description: This grant will support the Southeastern Regional Education Service Center, Inc., which coordinates the New Hampshire Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) creating an afterschool ambassador program to serve as champions in each county throughout the state; 2) providing professional development and coaching on quality standards to afterschool programs; 3) enhancing the statewide afterschool database of programs across the state; and 4) supporting the promotion and distribution of the Mizzen by Mott App.

title: General Purposes
description: The Foundation for Human Rights was established with support from the European Union to implement a human rights funding program in South Africa. It still receives the bulk of its funding from the European Union and is one of the most significant grantmakers in the country supporting the development and strengthening of a culture of human rights. Mott has supported the grantee to strengthen its internal capacity and has contributed to its research programs. This grant will provide general purpose support to the grantee to improve awareness of constitutional rights with an emphasis on socioeconomic rights and on vulnerable groups; enhance participatory democracy through public policy dialogues on constitutional rights; increase research on socioeconomic rights; and strengthen the capacity, engagement, and participation of civil society organizations in improving awareness of constitutional rights. The grantee will also make grants to community advice offices and design and implement programs that promote their sustainability.

title: General Purposes
description: The Social Justice Initiative was established in 2013 to contribute to building a South Africa characterized by peace, prosperity, and stability. Its vision is the creation and preservation of a just and fair society based on the democratic principles provided for in the country’s Constitution. The grantee seeks to address the financial crisis facing the social justice sector by increasing awareness of social justice causes among wealthy South Africans and encouraging them to fund programs that advance human rights and social justice. Past support assisted the grantee to unlock support from wealthy South Africans for social justice causes and matching funders with deserving causes. This grant will enable the grantee to assist social justice organizations in South Africa to find new sources of income to ensure their sustainability. It will continue to focus on wealthy individuals as a source of long-term funding.

title: Colorado Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Colorado Nonprofit Development Center, which coordinates the Colorado Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue the development of policy, partnerships and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) developing a data collection strategy to showcase the impact, value and needs of afterschool programs; 2) launching quality standards for afterschool programs; 3) creating a statewide professional development system; and 4) supporting the promotion and distribution of the Mizzen by Mott App.

title: Solar Energy for Chiribiquete Forest Dwellers
description: Amazon Conservation Team has been working with traditional communities in the Colombian Amazon rainforest to develop forest conservation and sustainable livelihoods, including renewable energy access. Over the past grant period, the grantee installed solar electrical energy kits for nearly 600 indigenous families living in isolated communities in the Caquetá region of the Colombian Amazon. Over the next grant period, the grantee will complete solar access for more than 50 communities and develop sustainable community management systems and advocacy for replication and universalization of solar access in the Colombian Amazon.

title: Capacity Building
description: Metro Community Development is a multiservice community development corporation dedicated to creating stable and vibrant neighborhoods in Flint and Genesee County. The grantee serves as both an intermediary and a direct service provider for federal and state programs designed to assist low-income residents. This grant will be used to strengthen the grantee’s Asset Development Division, which includes the federal Community Development Financial Institution program.

title: General Purposes
description: The Council of Michigan Foundations is a statewide association of over 300 grantmakers that provides its members with educational programs, technical assistance, networking opportunities, advocacy with policymakers and regulators, and collaborative work with leading national and regional philanthropic associations. Highlights from 2018 include 37 unique legislative visits, 90 learning programs, 276 policy-focused communications, 23 mentoring program graduates, and a 94 percent membership renewal rate. A listening tour by the newly appointed Chief Executive Officer yielded key themes for future work by the grantee: 1) advancing public policy; 2) cultivating the next generation of philanthropic leaders; 3) creating neutral space to have civic dialogue around hard conversations; and 4) supporting efforts that promote diversity, equity, and inclusion. These themes will complement the grantee’s existing priorities of expanding membership, offering a highly valued suite of services, continuing partnerships with peer infrastructure organizations, and advancing thought leadership to the field of philanthropy.

title: Memory Centre in the Constitution Hill Museum
description: The Constitution Hill Trust helps South Africans to respect their constitution, human rights, and democracy through their experience of the Constitution Hill precinct, which houses the Constitutional Court. Constitution Hill serves as a living memory of South Africa’s transition to democracy and a place where shared heritage and a common future are celebrated. It also runs programs that educate young South Africans about the constitution, its principles and workings, and the value and importance of democracy and human rights. This grant will assist the grantee to develop a museum of the Constitution. The museum will contain a dedicated memory centre and will be housed within a new visitor center.

title: Healthcare Startup Accelerator
description: This grant will support XLerateHealth, a healthcare business accelerator located in the Ferris Wheel Building in downtown Flint. The accelerator serves as an entry point for entrepreneurs working to create healthcare-related enterprises. A high functioning accelerator can attract new businesses to the Flint area, spur economic growth, and create job opportunities for local residents. XLerateHealth will play a key role in the build-out of a regional health science entrepreneurial ecosystem in Flint and Genesee County.

title: Double Up Food Bucks Project
description: This grant will provide additional support to the Fair Food Network’s Double Up Food Bucks Project in Flint. The project provides incentives for supplemental nutrition assistance program recipients to purchase fresh fruits and vegetables and dairy products at the Flint Farmers’ Market and grocery stores in Flint. Good nutrition, especially foods high in iron, calcium, and vitamin C, can help mitigate the impact of lead exposure to Flint children and adults.

title: Youth Entrepreneurship Landscape Scan
description: This grant will provide support to Formative Evaluation Research Associates, an independent nonprofit evaluation group based in Ann Arbor, Michigan, to conduct a K-12 Youth Entrepreneurship Landscape Scan in Flint and Genesee County. The goal of the study is to identify existing youth entrepreneurship-related programming available in the area and to highlight opportunities and gaps for funders and other stakeholders.

title: Teen CEO Initiative Expansion
description: This grant will provide additional support to Mott Community College for the Teen CEO Initiative Expansion. The goal is to expand the initiative from a summertime youth entrepreneurship experience for students ages 14-18 into a year-round afterschool program. The expanded 34-week afterschool program will assist young people in acquiring the skills needed to launch a business and/or prepare them for higher education and the workforce.

title: General Purposes
description: Established in 2005, the Ukrainian Philanthropists Forum is a professional association of charitable and philanthropic organizations. It currently has 41 members. The grantee’s mission is to foster a responsible, transparent, and accountable charitable community and to improve the effectiveness of Ukraine’s charitable sector. Key accomplishments over 2016-2018 include advocacy and support for the implementation of mobile giving, participation in the National Strategy for Civil Society Development in Ukraine, free online legal and fiscal consultations for charitable organizations, annual conferences, educational programs for foundations, and the development of a national charity rating system. The Ukrainian Philanthropists Forum strategic directions for 2018-2020 are: 1) development and implementation of standards for charitable organizations, 2) promotion of Ukraine’s charitable sector, and 3) reform of Ukraine’s social services sector.

title: Determining the Economic Impact of Protecting and Restoring the Great Lakes
geographic_focus: Indiana, Michigan, Ohio, Minnesota, Illinois, Wisconsin, New York, Pennsylvania
description: With this grant increase, the Great Lakes Commission will conduct a recruitment and hiring process to replace its executive director. The grantee is a key regional organization engaged in the protection and restoration of the Great Lakes ecosystem.

title: Strengthening Environmental-Social Framework in South America
description: Created in 2008, the Latin American Network of Environmental Public Prosecutors is comprised of 300 public prosecutors from 19 Latin American countries. Over the past project period, the Network organized six conferences in six countries in Latin America that focused on social and environmental protections for major infrastructure investments and precedent-setting legal cases in Latin America. This grant to Uniselva Foundation will enable the grantee to develop and publish educational materials, organize training events, and expand communications among prosecutors working in 19 countries in Latin America.

title: Tax Policy and Charities Project
description: The project goal is to improve the policy environment for the nonprofit sector and philanthropy in the United States. To this end, the Tax Policy and Charities project provides a rapid response to current debates over tax policy as it affects charities, upgrades continually a tax model that incorporates thousands of provisions in the tax code, and involves scholars and policy officials in both analysis and discussion of new tax proposals. Over the past two years, the project has produced and facilitated research and discussion on tax policy relating to charity. Future activities will include modeling tax and charity policy proposals, writing policy briefs and articles, providing congressional testimony, and producing other materials regarding major tax and charity issues. The project is implemented by the Urban-Brookings Tax Policy Center of the Urban Institute. The grantee is a national think tank that gathers data, conducts research, evaluates programs, offers technical assistance overseas, and educates Americans on social and economic issues to foster sound public policy and effective government.

title: Finding a Path Forward for Fiscally Sustainable Cities in Michigan
description: Research indicates that the municipal financial system in Michigan is not providing adequate revenue to Michigan cities that allows local government to provide services at an acceptable level. The purpose of this project is to develop a comprehensive, evidence-based framework for determining the local fiscal outcomes of state policy choices. Michigan State University will develop a web-based application allowing users to see customized data and analysis and a policy brief outlining how to use it to make relevant policy recommendations. They will also develop an academic article and participate in media engagements to communicate the research to stakeholders and the general public.

title: Rent and Utility Assistance Program
description: Since 1893, the Salvation Army of Genesee County has been working to alleviate hardships faced by Genesee County residents by providing assistance with basic needs such as rent and utility payments, emergency shelter, food, personal needs items, and transportation. This grant will help support the grantee with its financial assistance services administered through the Comprehensive Emergency Assistance Program to meet the growing needs of families in the community.

title: Property Acquisition and Demolition
description: This grant to Communities First, Inc., will support the removal of the structure at 1015 N. Saginaw Street that is blighted and a community nuisance. The building operates as a convenience store and is located directly across from Doyle-Ryder Elementary School. This acquisition and demolition will substantially contribute to the redevelopment of Flint into a healthy and vibrant community.

title: One Stop Housing Resource Center
description: Shelter of Flint, Inc., provides services for approximately 1,000 people each day. Most of these clients are families who are economically challenged. The principle goal of the agency is to assist the homeless in achieving stability through a continuum of care model ranging from crisis prevention and counseling to elimination of the root causes of homelessness. This grant will help support services for families through the grantee’s One Stop Housing Resource Center program. Individuals and families will receive food assistance as well as comprehensive case management services and the development of long-range plans toward permanent stability.

title: Service Education and Outreach Project
description: This grant will support Voices for National Service, a program of City Year, Inc., to undertake a communications initiative that will seek to enhance public awareness of the impact of national service programs across the country. This initiative will seek to provide the national service community with informational resources and tools to highlight national service, as well as leverage media and events to share the impact of national service with a broad audience.

title: Funders' Forum on Sustainable Cities
description: The Funders’ Forum on Sustainable Cities is an international, collaborative, foundation-led network committed to increasing philanthropy’s role and effectiveness in advancing sustainable and inclusive growth in cities, tackling urban poverty, promoting equitable development and opportunities, and strengthening local governance and citizen participation in local decisionmaking. Emerging from the Global Philanthropy Leadership Initiative, and with a secretariat in the European Foundation Centre, the forum will use this grant toward a range of activities in 2017. These will include speaker sessions and convenings examining opportunities for philanthropic engagement in urban agendas, avenues for cooperation between local authorities and philanthropic institutions in addressing urban sustainability challenges, and preparation for the World Urban Forum in early 2018 examining implementation of the New Urban Agenda emerging from the United Nations Habitat III Conference in 2016.

title: Michigan at a Crossroads Policy Guide
description: This grant will enable Michigan State University to produce a policy guidebook that will inform and shape public policy debates in 2019 and beyond. Using the best data and evidence available, the guidebook will frame the state’s most pressing policy challenges, identify potential policy solutions, and highlight the implications of different policy decisions. The guidebook will be published in hard copy, as well as electronically, and disseminated through social media channels and through a series of workshops across the state. In addition, the grantee will produce a series of mini-videos and brief transition memos summarizing each topic area.

title: Promoting Learning Opportunities and Supports for Youth
description: This grant will enable Editorial Projects in Education to increase media attention on the evolving policy landscape, as well as programmatic innovations and other developments in the afterschool field. During the grant period, the grantee will bring increased attention to afterschool issues (as well as other Education program priorities) through core reporting, outreach, and strategic communications activities. Editorial Projects in Education is the independent, nonprofit publisher of “Education Week” which, since 1981, has been considered the must read source of news and commentary on elementary and secondary education topics. Approximately 100,000 educators and policymakers read “Education Week” in print, and nearly 1.3 million users access edweek.org monthly.

title: New Economy Initiative for Southeast Michigan
description: The Community Foundation for Southeast Michigan launched the New Economy Initiative for Southeast Michigan to speed the transition of southeast Michigan to the new, knowledge-based economy. Since its inception in 2007, this philanthropic collaborative has provided grants and developed partnerships to support economic development infrastructure, innovative enterprises, and educational programs that prepare adults for the new economy. This grant renewal will provide continued support for the initiative’s second phase, which emphasizes creating new enterprises, attracting capital, and generating jobs through innovation and entrepreneurship.

title: Youth Entrepreneurship Curriculum for Afterschool Programs
description: VentureLab will provide training, technical assistance, and professional development materials that enable state afterschool networks to develop professional learning opportunities for local afterschool leaders. The goal of this effort is to increase the number of afterschool programs offering high quality entrepreneurship education programming and, ultimately, increase the number of youth who have opportunities to develop entrepreneurial skills and mindsets. VentureLab was founded in 2012 to empower the next generation of innovators and changemakers by teaching them to have the skillsets and mindsets associated with entrepreneurism. Through its educational and training activities, the grantee expands entrepreneurship learning opportunities for students across the K-12 continuum (especially girls) in the United States as well as internationally.

title: Gateway to Youth Entrepreneurship Program
description: The Network for Teaching Entrepreneurship’s current strategic plan calls for the grantee to reach at least 200,000 young people annually with its suite of entrepreneurship programs, which include online and in-person courses, BizCamps, and business plan competitions. Through this grant, the grantee will engage students in afterschool programs in its national business plan competition program. Since 1987, the grantee has created learning opportunities that activate the entrepreneurial mindset and develop start-up skills in young people, especially those living in low-income communities.

title: Advancing Relationship-Center Interventions
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant will advance evidence-based interventions and practices that expand the use of coaching/mentoring programs as a strategy to improve high school graduation as well as college and career readiness outcomes for young people. During the grant period, the National Mentoring Partnership will chart the landscape of existing programs, develop and promote a program framework that aligns with the Foundation’s interests and priorities, and promote the framework with practitioners, funders, and other relevant stakeholders. National Mentoring Partnership was founded in 1990 to build a national mentoring movement capable of scaling quality mentoring relationships for young people in America. Its stated mission is to close the mentoring gap by expanding the quality and quantity of mentoring relationships for young people.

title: Children's Savings Account Strategies for Community Foundations
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: The overall goal of this project is to encourage community foundations to promote and support children’s savings account programs. Renewal support will enable CFLeads to continue convening community foundation teams to learn about and begin supporting children’s savings account strategies. Grant funds will support meetings and conferences, individual and group technical assistance, and dissemination of written deliverables. CFLeads is a national learning cooperative that advocates for and advances the practice of community leadership among community foundations.

title: College Promise Campaign
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant will enable Civic Nation’s College Promise Campaign to expand the number and quality of children’s savings account strategies embedded in local and state college promise programs. To achieve this goal, Mott funding will support networking, stakeholder engagement, research, outreach, and strategic communications activities. Established in September 2015, the College Promise Campaign is a national initiative created to address the low numbers of low-income, first-generation, and underrepresented students attending and completing college due to financial barriers.

title: Linking Children's Savings Accounts to College Access and Success Strategies
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This renewal grant will enable the National College Access Network to promote children’s savings accounts among its members and within the college access and success community more generally. Specific activities include strategic communications, meetings and conferences, and educational outreach. These efforts will help attract more supporters and champions and ensure that children’s savings accounts are developed as part of a comprehensive college access and success strategy. Based in Washington, D.C., the National College Access Network’s mission is to build, strengthen, and empower communities committed to college access and success so that all students, especially those underrepresented in postsecondary education, can achieve their educational dreams.

title: Afterschool Policy and System Building Initiative
description: This grant to Voices for Georgia’s Children will enable the Georgia Statewide Afterschool Network to increase the quality and sustainability of afterschool programs across Georgia by strengthening the school-age policies and promoting participation in the state’s quality-rated, school-age program. This project will support the network to: 1) increase the number of programs with quality standards in Georgia; 2) work with partners to develop school-age policies and regulations; and 3) increase coordination of afterschool and child-care policies and programs. The grantee will share lessons learned with other state networks to enhance quality programs for disadvantaged students.

title: Supporting the National Network of Statewide Afterschool Networks
description: This grant increase will enable the Collaborative Communications Group to develop more opportunities for more youth in afterschool programs through supporting and implementing new partnerships with the statewide afterschool networks.

title: Afterschool Policy and System Building Initiative
description: This grant to the Alaska Children’s Trust will enable the Alaska Statewide Afterschool Network, to increase the availability of high quality afterschool programs and summer programs in Alaska. Through this grant, grantee will focus on supporting a policy initiative that will seek to increase access to afterschool programs. This grant will: 1) support the development and implementation of a statewide education campaign on the need for afterschool in Alaska; 2) provide technical assistance to partners on how to engage key stakeholders; and 3) build a network of afterschool champions in the state. The grantee will share lessons learned with other state networks in strengthening an existing afterschool system to enhance quality and access for disadvantaged students.

title: Afterschool Policy and System Building Initiative
grantee: Connecticut Network for Children and Youth, Inc.
description: This grant to the Connecticut After School Network will enable the Connecticut Statewide Afterschool Network to increase the availability of high quality afterschool programs and summer programs in Connecticut. Through this grant, the grantee will focus on improving the quality of afterschool programs, particularly in the area of social and emotional learning. This grant will: 1) improve program quality by building staff skills and knowledge of social and emotional learning, mental health, and parent engagement; 2) expand connections with parents; and 3) build a statewide cross-sector council around supporting students’ social and emotional learning and mental health. The grantee will share lessons learned with other state networks in strengthening an existing afterschool system to enhance quality for high need students.

title: Afterschool Policy and System Building Initiative
description: This grant to the Fund for Educational Excellence will enable the Maryland Statewide Afterschool Network to launch, support, and sustain an emerging statewide coalition in support of community schools. The grantee will serve as a vehicle to improve student outcomes through the addition of coordinated wraparound services, as well as provide a platform to significantly expand access to afterschool and summer learning opportunities. This grant will: 1) expand and convene a statewide community schools coalition; 2) develop materials and resources to support the education and outreach efforts of the coalition; 3) design and provide technical assistance and support for an evaluation and data collection framework for Maryland community schools; and 4) develop and implement new training and technical assistance opportunities specific to the Maryland community school field. The grantee will share lessons learned with other state networks on partnerships between afterschool and community schools.

title: Afterschool Policy and System Building Initiative
description: This grant to the Indiana Afterschool Network, Inc., will enable the Indiana Afterschool Network, to increase the availability of high quality, out-of-school time programs for children, youth, and families in Indiana’s most under-resourced communities. This grant will: 1) create a high level state partnership effort to increase afterschool and summer programs; 2) support the state Out-of-School Time Advisory Board to develop recommendations for improving quality afterschool programs in Indiana; and 3) increase the number of programs eligible for state credentials and additional resources. The grantee will share lessons learned with other state networks in strengthening an existing afterschool system to enhance quality for high need students.

title: Afterschool Policy and System Building Initiative
description: This grant to the Nebraska Children and Families Foundation will enable the Nebraska Statewide Afterschool Network to support underserved rural communities and develop partnerships that can support statewide policy change and program development. This grant will: 1) work with the Nebraska Department of Health and Human Services to reduce barriers for programs to meet school-based and child-care regulations; 2) develop, pilot, field-test, and scale up career exploration curriculum and activities for expanded learning programs; and 3) build local and state partnerships to ensure local relevance and sustainability. The grantee will share lessons learned with other state networks in strengthening an existing afterschool system to enhance quality for disadvantaged students.

title: Afterschool Policy and System Building Initiative
grantee: Marshfield Clinic Research Institute, a Division of Marshfield Clinic, Inc.
description: This grant to Marshfield Clinic, Inc., will enable the Wisconsin Statewide Afterschool Network to develop afterschool programming that better supports children who have experienced trauma. This grant will: 1) develop and provide training and technical assistance to support trauma-sensitive and responsive afterschool systems; 2) develop replicable services and guidance to afterschool programs in this area; and 3) support the development of policies focused on increasing trauma-sensitive afterschool programs. The grantee will share lessons learned with other state networks in addressing these challenges in support of children in afterschool programs.

title: Afterschool Policy and System Building Initiative
grantee: Oregon Association for the Education of Young Children
description: This grant to the Oregon Association for the Education of Young Children will enable the Oregon Statewide Afterschool Network to expand quality programs through a state effort known as TEAM Community: Total Engagement Across My Community. The goal of this project is to focus on the availability of high quality programs that provide meaningful family and community engagement and ensure equity and access to afterschool programs for all students in Oregon. This grant will: 1) conduct research and data collection on issues of equity; 2) expand the integration of service-learning; and 3) create a public awareness campaign around issues of equity and access. The grantee will share lessons learned with other state networks in strengthening an existing afterschool system to enhance quality and access for high need students.

title: School Success Mentor Program
description: This grant will support Johns Hopkins University School of Education’s Everyone Graduates Center to sustain a data-driven, evidence-based mentoring program as part of a national initiative to reduce chronic student absenteeism. This project will include: 1) sustaining the School Success Mentor Program in 30 communities across the nation; 2) enhancing the national infrastructure to provide leadership and technical assistance for the program; and 3) working to connect the School Success Mentor Program with existing afterschool initiatives.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to facilitate the exchange of information and ideas among philanthropists, social investors, and others working for social change worldwide. To this end, the Alliance Publishing Trust carries out a range of publishing activities with regular products, including Alliance, a quarterly print magazine; Alliance Extra, an online newsletter for subscribers only; a Latest from Alliance blog which offers daily opinions, news, and conference reports (quarterly); Alliance Breakfast Club meetings that bring together key sector personnel; and surveys and investigative commissions. In 2018, the grantee had over 24,000 readers of its various information products. During the upcoming grant period, in addition to the editorial work, the grantee will conduct webinars on its special features, Livestream breakfast club debates, and update its website to facilitate its new donation strategy. Established in 2006, Alliance Publishing Trust is located in London, England.

title: Capacity Building
description: The Hispanic Technology & Community Center of Greater Flint provides many programs and services to the greater Flint area. The grantee was established in 2001 in partnership with Mott Community College to provide educational, cultural, social, and technological opportunities for a better tomorrow. The grantee will utilize the grant to hire a coordinator to increase its capacity to serve Flint resident as a result of the water crisis.

title: Case Management System
description: With this grant, Flint Community Schools will purchase a software system to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of the community education strategy. The district will purchase a case management tool which will provide community school directors and school staff with the ability to track student academic and behavioral data along with an account of the community education programs and resources the student is receiving. With this information, community school directors and school staff can better align resources and supports with student needs.

title: Coordinated Enrollment Research
description: With this grant, the Community Foundation of Greater Flint will explore the feasibility of developing and implementing a coordinated enrollment system for early childhood education in Flint. With increased awareness and availability of early learning opportunities across the city, a coordinated enrollment system could improve the transparency, integrity, and access to the enrollment process.

title: Online Flint Publication
description: This grant will provide support to the Genesee Chamber Foundation to fund an editorially independent online publication that covers the people and projects that are driving revitalization across the city of Flint. This work is especially important given the negative effects of the Flint water crisis that are still lingering and damaging the city’s reputation and potential economic growth. Through weekly features and news stories produced by professional local writers, photographers, and videographers, the publication will inform both local residents and outside audiences about Flint’s revitalization, and attract resources from investors and decisionmakers that can contribute to Flint’s ongoing economic development and job growth. The grantee has selected Issue Media Group, who will use a variety of methods to ensure that content created for the publication is widely disseminated, including use of e-mail and social media channels, and through partnerships with other media organizations.

title: Capitol Theatre Equipment
description: This grant increase will support design and coordination work to outfit the historic Capitol Theatre with an augmented technical equipment package and additional modifications needed to maximize the theater experience for patrons and the community. The installation of a mechanical pit and lighting and sound enhancements will increase the efficiencies and flexibility of the theater’s performance spaces. Once fully operational, the theater has the capacity to attract between 60,000 and 80,000 visitors annually. The Flint Cultural Center Corporation, the supported organization of the Flint Cultural Center Foundation, will operate the theater.

title: Increasing Food Distribution
description: This grant will provide funds to Carriage Town Ministries to purchase food in order to serve meals to the homeless and those in need of food assistance who come to the shelter. The grantee provides important safety-net services to individuals and families in the Flint area who are homeless or near-homeless, including food, safe and warm shelter, clothes, personal hygiene products, health services, and life skills courses.

title: North End Soup Kitchen, Warming Center and Medical Transportation
grantee: Catholic Charities of Shiawassee and Genesee Counties
description: This grant will provide support to Catholic Charities of Shiawassee and Genesee Counties to operate intervention services for individuals and families in crisis. The North End Soup Kitchen and Center for Hope Warming Center will assist those with limited or no income by providing hot meals, personal needs items, and respite from cold weather during the harsh winter months. The St. Christopher Medical Transport Program will provide transportation for critically ill children and their families to medical appointments across the state.

title: Flint Diaper Bank
description: This grant will provide funds to the Food Bank of Eastern Michigan to support the Flint Diaper Bank program in providing diapers to low-income Genesee County residents. By utilizing the grantee’s sophisticated distribution system, the Flint Diaper Bank can ensure that diapers will reach the community’s most needy families and help relieve the stress of families and caretakers who often must choose between supplying diapers for their babies or purchasing other basic necessities.

title: Alabama Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase to Auburn University will support the Alabama Statewide Afterschool Network in hosting an institute focused on afterschool STEM for statewide afterschool networks and partners. The institute will provide participants an opportunity to share best practices and emerging models, while working with national experts at the forefront of afterschool and summer STEM programming.

title: Early Childhood Capacity Building
description: This grant will provide funding to the Community Foundation of Greater Flint as it supports the expansion of early childhood education in Flint. Expanding access to high quality early childhood education has become an urgent priority as a result of the Flint water crisis. The grantee will employ an executive director to manage the Flint Early Childhood Collaborative, a project with the aim of increasing access to and the quality of early childhood education in Flint through strategic planning, research, advocacy, and participation in the Educare Learning Network.

title: Parking Lot Improvements
description: With this grant, Flint Community Schools will resurface several of the district’s parking lots, prioritizing those that are in the greatest need of repair. As families and community members approach school buildings, the exterior physical appearance provides an important first impression about the district and the quality of services it will provide. Resurfaced parking lots will improve the safety of the school grounds and create a more welcoming environment for school staff, parents, and the community.

title: Change the Course
description: With this grant increase, the Bonneville Environmental Foundation will build on its efforts to expand its Change the Course program to the state of Georgia. Change the Course encourages individuals to take actions that conserve freshwater resources and enlists the private sector to support related ecosystem restoration projects.

title: Montana Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the School Services of Montana which coordinates the Montana Statewide Afterschool Network to continue development of policy, partnerships and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) engaging partners to embed STEM learning in the state’s workforce development initiatives; 2) developing and launching a school-age quality system that aligns with the quality standards for afterschool programs; 3) expanding professional development opportunities to afterschool programs locally, regionally and statewide; and 4) supporting the promotion and distribution of the Mizzen by Mott App.

title: Redevelopment of Downtown YMCA
description: This grant will support the YMCA of Greater Flint in conducting a feasibility analysis. The goal of this analysis is to determine the long-term future of its downtown facility. First built in 1961 at 411 E. Third Street, this building has served the primary recreational and programmatic functions for the YMCA for several decades, and now key information needs to be gathered to help shape the future of this site. Predevelopment work will include financial analysis, design aspects, environmental concerns, community engagement, and municipal approvals.

title: School Finance Research Project
description: In order for children to be prepared for and connected to opportunities in an ever-evolving economy, the public school funding system in Michigan must be reformed to provide funding which supports student achievement for all students in PreK-12. The School Finance Research Project, a project of the Oakland Schools Education Foundation, will determine the adequate amount of funding required to educate children in the PreK-12 system. The project will build on the results of the 2016 adequacy study by using multiple methodologies and addressing concentrations of high need students, geographically isolated districts, charter schools, preschools, special education, and career and technical education.

title: Collaborating to Protect and Restore the Great Lakes
geographic_focus: Illinois, New York, Pennsylvania, Ohio, Indiana, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Michigan
description: The National Wildlife Federation’s Great Lakes Regional Center combines policy, legal, communications, educational, and scientific expertise to educate decision makers, inform public policy, and conduct public outreach efforts. The grantee is a leading voice for the protection and restoration of the Great Lakes. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has led efforts to stop Asian carp from reaching the Great Lakes, advance regional strategies through the Great Lakes Water Resources Compact to prevent harmful diversions, stop pollution from phosphorus fertilizers and other chemicals, and inform federal policies to restore the Great Lakes. With renewed support, the Great Lakes office of the National Wildlife Federation will redouble its efforts around these themes.

title: Internally Displaced Persons and Communities: Building Tolerance Through Dialogue
description: The program goal is to support the development of strong and inclusive communities in Ukraine that are addressing the needs of internally displaced persons. The Ukrainian Women’s Fund will adapt its model for supporting and integrating internally displaced persons at the community level with a view to eliminating any stigma associated with internal displacement. Working in four regions, it will work with incipient community organizations aimed explicitly at integrating displaced persons with active local peers to achieve community change. In 2017-2019, the grantee conducted in-depth training and coaching sessions with community initiative groups in six target regions. This resulted in a wide range of community advocacy projects on issues such as environmental protection, administrative reform, support for the elderly, and access to social services. Founded in 2000, the Ukrainian Women’s Fund helps women’s civic organizations play an active role in the processes of democratization of society and contribute to equality, justice, and respect for human rights.

title: Michigan Land and Water Policy Project
description: Michigan United Conservation Clubs is Michigan’s oldest conservation organization. It is an umbrella group of hunting and fishing clubs, and recreational users of Michigan’s natural resources. With this increase, the grantee will make readily accessible and understandable the results of research they conducted to quantify the value of hunting and fishing to local economies.

title: Integrating Afterschool and School-Community Partnerships
description: This grant will support the American Youth Policy Forum to continue to support the development of high quality afterschool programs with a focus on college and career readiness. Recommended support will enable the grantee to: 1) conduct an environmental scan of afterschool programs with innovative and effective college and career readiness strategies; and 2) recommend strategies for increasing college and career readiness supports in afterschool programs.

title: Development Banks and Sustainable Development
description: In recent years, China has helped establish a new family of development finance institutions that rival the current multilateral development finance system. The impact made by the investments of these new institutions on ecosystems and community development has become a global issue. The Global Economic Governance Institute at Boston University has become a major source for research analyzing these impacts and providing useful data for relevant Chinese ministries. Through this grant increase, the institute will expand its work with key Chinese think tanks, facilitating additional research, and developing best practices to assist in developing policies for more sustainable Chinese development finance.

title: Lake Erie Protection and Restoration Project
description: The Ohio Environmental Council is a premier conservation advocacy organization in the state. With previous support, the grantee has focused attention on Lake Erie and its pollution problems and led efforts to improve Lake Erie communities by restoring coastal ecosystems. Recently, the grantee has turned more attention to drinking water, lead contamination, and affordability of clean, safe water supplies. With renewed support, the grantee will build on these efforts while forging a stronger relationship with the agricultural sector in Ohio to find common ground on Lake Erie’s pollution problems.

title: Healthy Flint Research Coordinating Center-Community Core
description: Flint Odyssey House, Inc., established the Healthy Flint Research Coordinating Center in 2016. This initiative was created to better advocate on behalf of community residents to help derive maximum health benefits from research conducted locally. The primary task of the Community Core is coordinating research conducted in Flint in order to minimize fragmented and duplicative efforts across local universities and hospitals, increase the community voice, and ensure ethical community involvement. The Flint Odyssey House is uniquely positioned to shepherd this work due to its existing connections and trust in the community.

title: Performance-Based Regulation Study
description: The Michigan Public Service Commission is developing a report on performance-based regulation, which differs from the traditional cost of service regulatory approach. Performance-based regulation can be used to advance a range of goals, including energy efficiency and renewable energy generation. The Regulatory Assistance Project will provide technical support to the commission as it develops the report. The Regulatory Assistance Project is a nonpartisan, nonprofit organization that helps energy and air quality regulators in the United States and abroad to navigate the complexities of power sector policy, regulation, and markets.

title: Hurricane Harvey and Other 2017 Natural Disasters Relief
description: With this grant, the Center for Disaster Philanthropy will build its capacity to provide natural disaster relief in the United States and abroad. In response to disasters in 2017, the grantee established several new funds and has been trusted with contributions from large and small donors to provide a coordinated and efficient response. Additional staff are required to handle the increased demands of responsibly providing support following these disasters.

title: Wildlife Trade Programme
description: The Alliance of Religions and Conservation will wind down its work related to biodiversity conservation. Key to this has been engaging the world’s faith leaders to promote the conservation of biodiversity, climate change resilience, and sustainable and spiritually principled living. These faith leaders are now prepared to sustain this work and will continue to raise awareness and create messaging and activities to help refute the practices of illegal killing, trade, and use of endangered wildlife in China, India, Indonesia, and Africa. During 2018, the grantee will offer final capacity building support to fully embed these programs within a variety of secular lead organizations.

title: Assets Evaluation and Data Collection Project
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This renewal grant will support the Institute on Assets and Social Policy at Brandeis University to continue to advance the children’s savings account field and measure success in the following areas: 1) strengthening program design and implementation; 2) promoting college savings account policies; and 3) connecting college savings accounts to local and statewide financial aid reform and college completion efforts. Brandeis University has partnered with the Foundation on asset-building and savings strategies since 2008.

title: Flint National Service Accelerator Fund
description: The Flint National Service Accelerator Fund helps Flint and Genesee County agencies leverage state and national service members through the Corporation for National and Community Service and its affiliates. Flint area service members support projects aligned with the City of Flint’s master plan and the Corporation for National and Community Service priorities including education, public safety, health, and the environment. Focus areas in Flint include community education, literacy, public safety, nutrition, and assisting Flint residents and nonprofits to recover from the Flint water crisis. Matching grants provide resources to local nonprofit agencies for the required member cost share, training, and travel reimbursement. The fund is held at the Community Foundation of Greater Flint and is administered in partnership with the United Way of Genesee County.

title: Flint National Service Accelerator Fund
description: The Flint National Service Accelerator Fund helps Flint and Genesee County agencies leverage state and national service members through the Corporation for National and Community Service and its affiliates. Flint area service members support projects aligned with the City of Flint’s master plan, emerging community needs, and the Corporation for National and Community Service priorities including education, economic opportunity, disaster services, environmental stewardship, healthy futures, and veterans and military families. Focus areas in Flint include community education, literacy, public safety, nutrition, and assisting Flint residents and nonprofits to recover and rise from the Flint water crisis. Matching grants provide resources to local nonprofit agencies for the required member cost share, training, and travel reimbursement. The fund is held at the Community Foundation of Greater Flint and is administered in close partnership with the United Way of Genesee County.

title: Policy Conference
description: The Detroit Regional Chamber Foundation is dedicated to creating a robust economy for businesses and individuals. This grant will support a session at the 2018 Mackinac Policy Conference focused on further educating participants on why the state should analyze how the system of municipal finance impedes or accelerates a thriving community. This session will build from the session sponsored in 2017.

title: Youth Entrepreneurship Curriculum for Afterschool Programs
description: VentureLab will provide training, technical assistance, and professional development materials that enable state afterschool networks to develop professional learning opportunities for local afterschool leaders. The goal of this effort is to increase the number of afterschool programs offering high quality entrepreneurship education programming and, ultimately, increase the number of youth who have opportunities to develop entrepreneurial skills and mindsets. The grantee was founded in 2012 to empower the next generation of innovators and changemakers by teaching them to have the skillsets and mindsets associated with entrepreneurism. Through its educational and training activities, VentureLab expands entrepreneurship learning opportunities for students across the K-12 continuum (especially girls) in the United States, as well as internationally.

title: Gateway to Youth Entrepreneurship Program
description: The Network for Teaching Entrepreneurship’s current strategic plan calls for the grantee to reach at least 200,000 young people annually with its suite of entrepreneurship programs, which includes online and in-person courses, BizCamps, and business plan competitions. Through this grant, the grantee will continue to develop new strategies to further expand its youth entrepreneurship programming especially for young people in low-income communities. Since 1987, the Network for Teaching Entrepreneurship has created learning opportunities that activate the entrepreneurial mindset and the essential skills young people need to compete in life.

title: Downtown Hotel Pre-design Study
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This project will allow the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation to support the pre-development work for renovating the former Genesee County Savings Bank building into a hotel in downtown Flint. This work includes an evaluation, analysis, design, and engineering. This redevelopment effort aims to continue the resurgence of downtown and provide lodging for visitors to the city.

title: Mexican Community Foundation Development
description: This grant will support the development of Mexican community foundations. The Inter-American Foundation manages a program that focuses on members of Comunalia, a network of Mexican community foundations. Over the next three years, the grantee will support the institutional strengthening of Comunalia and its members; manage a sub-grant challenge mechanism for community projects; and provide grants for applied research, donor engagement and education, and evaluation. This grant increase will support the creation of a Post-Earthquake Recovery Fund, which will leverage funds through a challenge mechanism from the United States, Canadian, and Mexican corporate and community foundations to support longer-term disaster recovery and prevention efforts in communities affected by recent earthquakes in Mexico. Funds will be channeled through Comunalia to the four community foundations in the affected areas, who will in turn also leverage local community support. The Inter-American Foundation is an independent United States government agency created by Congress in 1969 to channel development assistance directly to the poor in Latin America and the Caribbean.

title: Nonprofit Capacity Building
description: The purpose of this renewal grant is to support the Nonprofit Capacity Building project of the United Way of Genesee County, whose mission is to strengthen the nonprofit sector of Flint and Genesee County by providing organizations with nonprofit management information, professional development, capacity building, and technical assistance support. Since United Way began capacity building work in 2003, over 100 Genesee County agencies have received services that have allowed them to help more individuals in need, leverage new financial and human capital, and collaborate with cross-sector leaders to ensure alignment with community needs.

title: Nonprofit Capacity Building
description: The purpose of this renewal grant is to support the Nonprofit Capacity Building project of the United Way of Genesee County, whose mission is to strengthen the nonprofit sector of Flint and Genesee County by providing organizations with nonprofit management information, professional development, capacity building, and technical assistance support. Since the grantee began capacity-building work in 2003, over 100 Genesee County agencies have received services that have allowed them to help more individuals in need, leverage new financial and human capital, and collaborate with cross-sector leaders to ensure alignment with community needs.

title: Nonprofit Capacity Building
description: The purpose of this renewal grant is to support the Nonprofit Center of the United Way of Genesee County, which offers a broad range of services to support nonprofits through capacity building, volunteer management and national service resources. Since the grantee began capacity-building work in 2003, over 100 Genesee County agencies have received services that have allowed them to help more individuals in need, leverage new financial and human capital and collaborate with cross-sector leaders to ensure alignment with community needs.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purposes support to the United Way of Genesee County, a health and human services organization serving the residents of Genesee County through its four community impact focus areas of education, financial stability, health and basic needs. In addition to the core support areas, the grantee provides nonprofit sector capacity support through aligned fiduciary services and specific capacity building activities. The grantee was heavily involved in the response to the Flint Water Crisis, and since March 2020, has become a key organization in the community response to the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: School and Community Programming
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will allow the Flint Cultural Center Corporation, in partnership with other cultural center institutions, to provide educational programming to students attending Flint Community Schools and other at-risk students living in the community. The grantee’s in-person and virtual educational outreach programs will provide Flint students with access to a variety of programs and activities available from any Flint Cultural Center campus institution during the school year and summer months.

title: Early Childhood Capacity Building
description: This grant will provide funding to the Community Foundation of Greater Flint as it supports the expansion of early childhood education in Flint. Expanding access to high-quality early childhood education was always important for the city, but became even more important following the water crisis. The grantee employs an executive director to manage the Flint Early Childhood Collaborative, a project that aims to increase access to and the quality of early childhood education in Flint through strategic planning, research, advocacy, and participation in the Educare Learning Network.

title: Early Childhood Capacity Building
description: This grant will provide funding to the Community Foundation of Greater Flint to support the expansion of early childhood education in Flint. Expanding access to high-quality early childhood education was always important for the city, but became even more important following the water crisis. The grantee employs an executive director to manage the Flint Early Childhood Collaborative, a project that aims to increase access to and the quality of early childhood education in Flint through strategic planning, research, advocacy and participation in the Educare Learning Network.

title: Linking Children's Savings Accounts to College Access and Success Strategies
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This renewal grant will enable the National College Attainment Network to promote children’s savings accounts among its members and within the college access and success community more generally. Specific activities include strategic communications, meetings, conferences and educational outreach. These efforts will help grow demand for children’s savings account strategies as part of a comprehensive college access and success initiatives. Based in Washington, D.C., the grantee’s mission is to build, strengthen and empower communities committed to college access and success so that all students, especially those underrepresented in postsecondary education, can achieve their educational dreams.

title: Shine: Investing in Energy Access for All
