description: Nearly one billion people live without access to electricity. Rockefeller Philanthropy Advisors, through its Shine Campaign project, aims to address this global challenge by calling on leaders in the faith, philanthropic and nonprofit sectors to make principled investments in clean, affordable energy that put the most vulnerable communities first. In its first two years of operation, the Shine Campaign project has built an organizational backbone, raised awareness on the issue, and gained new financial commitments for clean energy access. With continued Mott support, the grantee will build on these successes through a range of research, networking and communications activities.

title: Operating Support
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Flint Cultural Center Corporation operates The Whiting, Sloan Museum and Longway Planetarium, and manages and maintains the 38-acre Flint Cultural Center campus which also includes Flint Cultural Center Academy, Flint Institute of Arts, Flint Institute of Music and Flint Public Library. In addition, the Capitol Theatre is operated by The Whiting. Students and adults participate in or attend a variety of cultural, educational and instructional programs and activities at these cultural center organizations. In addition to offering national touring artists and live theater, the grantee also focuses on providing educational programming both on site and in schools. This grant will provide operating support to the Flint Cultural Center Corporation for the benefit of its facilities, member organizations and programs.

title: Operating Support
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant increase will provide additional support to the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation and its supported organization, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation. Funding will allow the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation the flexibility to respond to new redevelopment opportunities in downtown Flint.

title: Operating Support
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Flint Institute of Arts, located on the Flint Cultural Center campus, features museum galleries, an art school and studio space and public areas that engage patrons and attract new audiences from across the region. Students and adults visit the galleries, participate in educational programs, take art classes or attend events held at the institute. The two newest galleries and the hot glass studio and foundry have increased regional interest in the Flint Institute of Arts as an arts destination, particularly for those interested in contemporary crafts and glassmaking. This grant will provide operating support to enable the grantee to present new exhibits that inspire and stimulate visitors, provide educational programming to area students, offer instruction in various art mediums to people of all ages and maintain its facilities.

title: Education and Economic Development Initiatives
description: This renewal grant provides partial support for the Genesee Area Focus Fund and its supported organization, the Flint & Genesee Chamber of Commerce, to deliver economic development and education and training services to the Flint area and build Flint’s economic resilience to recover from the Flint water crisis. The chamber increases business investment, job creation, and industry diversification through business retention, expansion, and attraction activities, as well as entrepreneurial support services. The chamber also enhances the region’s economic competitiveness and quality of life by providing workforce education and training programming across all age levels, and by engaging in special initiative projects with strategic partners.

title: YouthQuest After School Initiative
description: This renewal grant provides continued support to the Genesee Area Focus Fund for the YouthQuest After School Initiative. YouthQuest provides children and youth with opportunities to learn and grow through a safe, engaging and exciting afterschool learning experience surrounded by caring, responsible adults and sustained by involved and supportive community organizations.

title: Event Policing and Public Safety
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide funds to support public safety enforcement and traffic control activities at festivals in downtown Flint. Public safety is an essential component of the success of the festivals that take place in the downtown Flint area and attract thousands of exhibitors and festival goers. The City of Flint is not in a financial position to provide the necessary additional police services due to a decline in municipal revenues.

title: Event Policing and Public Safety
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide funds to support public safety enforcement and traffic control activities for festivals and events primarily in the downtown Flint area. Public safety is an essential component of the success of the festivals that take place in Flint and attract thousands of exhibitors and participants. The City of Flint is not in a financial position to provide the necessary additional police services due to a decline in municipal revenues.

title: Sloan Museum Renovation and Expansion Project
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to the Flint Cultural Center Foundation will provide funding for the design and renovation of the Sloan Museum facility. This grant will support design development activities, including construction costs, general contractor fees, and exhibit construction and installation costs. The new museum building will feature over 42,000 square feet of additional space and programming to benefit the region. The new design incorporates a variety of areas designed for young children and K-12 students by bringing a science center and history museum together under one roof. This new vision encourages discovery by embracing technology, incorporating advanced design thinking, and creating interactive history and science experiences.

title: News and Information Programs
description: This grant provides funding to National Public Radio in support of its news and information service. National Public Radio is recognized as one of the most trusted media brands in the country for its fair and fact-based coverage of national and international news. Each month, 99 million people are reached through radio, podcasts, websites, social media, and mobile apps with news and information to help create a more engaged public.

title: Flint River Restoration Project
description: This grant increase will provide project support to the Genesee County Parks & Recreation Commission for the Flint River Restoration Project. Funds from this grant will be used as a match for a Michigan Natural Resources Trust Fund grant, project management expenses, and in-stream restoration design and engineering costs. The project is the result of a broad group of diverse partners coming together to create a vision for the Flint riverfront as a unique community asset that is accessible and safe for all residents to utilize, drive economic opportunities, and enhance local infrastructure by removing the Hamilton Dam. The project will support the overall economic development opportunities for Flint by creating greater connectivity between the University of Michigan-Flint, downtown, and Kettering University; removing hazardous infrastructure; improving storm water and flood control systems; developing underutilized public property; and capping contamination at a former industrial site.

title: Financing Clean Energy Access
grantee: International Institute for Environment and Development
description: Modern energy helps make economic development possible as well as enhancing education, access to water, and gender equality. However, just having access to modern energy does not automatically result in development impacts. Due to this, financing of small businesses and increased agricultural production using off-grid power through mini-grids is an important new focus for funders. Over the last grant period, the International Institute for Environment and Development’s research has contributed to the expansion of new and enhanced financing mechanisms for local African companies and highlighted the importance of local level energy planning. Under this renewal grant, the grantee will fully develop a demonstration project that increases locally appropriate energy services designed around community needs.

title: Nevada Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the University of Nevada, Las Vegas, which coordinates the Nevada Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue development of policy, partnerships, and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) develop, pilot, and disseminate quality standards and resources; 2) partner with the Nevada Department of Education to implement an annual statewide afterschool conference; 3) develop a comprehensive communications and outreach plan about the importance of afterschool; and 4) support the development and distribution of the new afterschool program content in collaboration with the Foundation’s thematic partners.

title: Factory Two Project
description: This grant will provide support to Red Ink Flint to manage the Factory Two Project. In addition to the Factory Two Project, Red Ink Flint operates Flint Local 432, a performance venue located in downtown Flint. The Factory Two Project is an affordable community makerspace where creative people gather to work on their product ideas and network with each other. Foundation support will help fund operations including staff for expanded hours, programming, and equipment purchases. Factory Two will also help coordinate the first Flint Maker Festival in 2019.

title: Factory Two Project
description: This grant will provide support to Red Ink Flint to manage the Factory Two Project. In addition to the Factory Two Project, Red Ink Flint operates Flint Local 432, a performance venue located in downtown Flint. The Factory Two Project is an affordable community makerspace where creative people gather to work on product ideas and network with each other. Foundation funds will be used to support operations and programmatic activities.

title: Factory Two Project
description: This grant will provide support to Red Ink Flint to manage the Factory Two project. The Factory Two project is an affordable community makerspace located in downtown Flint where creative people gather to work on product ideas and network with each other. Foundation funds will be used to support operations and programmatic activities.

title: Africa Grantmakers' Affinity Group
description: The Africa Grantmakers’ Affinity Group, a project of the Tides Center, is a network of organizations and individuals funding development work in Africa. Since 2000, the grantee has worked to promote robust, effective, and responsive philanthropy to benefit African communities. Their goal is to build a network of informed funders who understand the current trends, can implement sound strategies, and identify key points of leverage. The grantee has led the establishment of the Africa Philanthropy Support Organizations initiative, a communications effort to connect funder networks based inside and outside of Africa. This grant increase will support the grantee’s efforts to bring together networks of funders inside and outside Africa by hosting events and producing communication material. In addition, this grant will support activities planned in the lead up to the 20th Anniversary of the Africa Grantmakers’ Affinity Group.

title: European Programme for Integration and Migration
description: The European Programme for Integration and Migration is a donor collaborative hosted by the Network of European Foundations for Innovative Cooperation. Established in 2005, this program strengthens the role played by civil society organizations in advocating for constructive approaches to migration in Europe. This is done through grantmaking; capacity development; and networking activities addressing a range of issues, including asylum seekers; undocumented migrants; and the equality, integration, and social inclusion of vulnerable migrants. Between 2005 and 2015, this program has involved 20 European foundations in collaborative programming and grantmaking; leveraged funding from these foundations; awarded 55 grants to projects led by civil society organizations; and organized more than 20 pan-European exchange, training, and networking events involving grantees and funders. This grant increase will support a new subfund aimed at building inclusive European societies. Based in Brussels, the Network of European Foundations for Innovative Cooperation strengthens cooperation among foundations in Europe.

title: European Programme for Integration and Migration
description: The European Programme for Integration and Migration is a donor collaborative hosted by the Network of European Foundations for Innovative Cooperation. Established in 2005, this program strengthens the role played by civil society organizations in advocating for constructive approaches to migration in Europe. This is done through grantmaking, capacity development, and networking activities addressing a range of issues, including asylum seekers; undocumented migrants; and equality, integration, and social inclusion of vulnerable migrants. Between 2005 and 2018, this program has involved 35 European foundations in collaborative programming and grantmaking; leveraged funding from these foundations; provided more than 16 million Euros to over 160 civil society organizations; and organized more than 50 pan-European exchange, training, and networking events involving grantees and funders. Based in Brussels, the Network of European Foundations for Innovative Cooperation strengthens cooperation among foundations in Europe.

title: Community Education Innovation Fund
description: This grant will provide funding in support of the Community Education Innovation Fund at the Crim Fitness Foundation. Designed to provide community school directors with opportunities and funding for innovative ideas and practices, the initiative is particularly aimed at fostering innovations around parent and community engagement. Garnering parental and community member involvement is essential in building a school district that can truly serve the needs of its students and a community that is strong and engaged.

title: Community Legal Centers in Ukraine
description: The program goal is to support access to justice in small communities in Ukraine through strengthening of local justice institutions. The Charity and Health Foundation will work with newly amalgamated communities to help expand practice and understanding of community-based sheriffs. The grantee will also research, monitor, and broadly publicize local experiences of how new models of community-based justice are improving lives of citizens and how they can positively inform wider law enforcement reforms. During 2017-2019, the grantee improved its online resources detailing the experience of community policing in rural areas based on the sheriff model. It produced six informational/instructional videos as well as a guide to best practices in community policing. This guide was subsequently adopted for official use in training future community police officers. Based in Kherson, the Charity and Health Foundation works to inspire citizens to take responsible action in order to promote the rule of law and democracy in Ukraine.

title: Community Legal Centers in Ukraine
description: The program goal is to support access to justice in small communities in Ukraine through strengthening of local justice institutions. The Charity and Health Foundation will work with newly amalgamated communities in territories of southeast Ukraine to help expand practice and understanding of community-based policing, with a particular focus on improving juvenile justice practices. The grantee will also research, monitor and broadly publicize local experiences of how new models of community-based justice are improving lives of citizens and how they can positively inform wider law enforcement reforms. During 2019-2021, the grantee produced over 300 online and offline publications detailing community justice practices and highlighting deficiencies in juvenile justice provisions in rural communities. The grantee also produced further material on community policing for inclusion in the curriculum of Ukraine’s leading institution for police training. Based in Kherson, the Charity and Health Foundation works to inspire citizens to take responsible action in order to promote the rule of law and democracy in Ukraine.

title: General Purposes
description: Many small, off-grid renewable energy companies have been launched over the past decade to address the energy access challenge in Sub-Saharan Africa. However, most do not have access to financing that allows them to develop needed innovations. To address these innovation challenges for the energy access sector, Stichting EnAccess was established. Over the past grant period, the grantee developed five projects that assisted local African energy access companies with upgrading their network and payments systems, providing customer survey capabilities, and in developing expanded mini-grid businesses. This general purpose funding will continue to support EnAccess’ organizational development, as well as expanding their open source tools to accelerate energy access solutions for off-grid communities in Africa.

title: General Purposes
description: The Social Justice Initiative was established in 2013 to create awareness of the importance of social justice causes in South Africa. It partners with philanthropists and civil society organizations to raise funds and support fair access to constitutional rights, better delivery of services, and a stronger democracy. Past support enabled the grantee to unlock over $5 million from wealthy South Africans to support 80 social justice organizations and causes. In addition, the Social Justice Initiative generated interest and support for social justice programs from the private sector. This grant will assist the grantee to continue unlocking funding for initiatives that pursue systemic change and promote access to justice, accountable governance, and human rights in South Africa.

title: News and Information Programs
description: This grant provides funding to National Public Radio in support of its news and information service. The grantee is recognized as one of the most trusted media brands in the country for its fair and fact-based coverage of national and international news. Each month over 105 million people are reached through radio, podcasts, websites, social media, and mobile apps with news and information to help create a more engaged public.

title: Community Education Innovation Fund
description: This grant will provide funding in support of the Community Education Innovation Fund at the Crim Fitness Foundation. Designed to provide community school directors with opportunities and funding for innovative ideas and practices, the initiative is particularly aimed at fostering innovations around parent and community engagement. Garnering parental and community member involvement is essential in building a school system that can truly serve the needs of its students and a community that is strong and engaged.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to the Council on Foundations, a national membership organization of more than 700 private foundations, community foundations, and corporate funders. The grantee’s mission is to provide the opportunity, leadership, and tools needed by philanthropic organizations to expand, enhance, and sustain their ability to advance the common good. Its near-term organizational goals are to: 1) position the council as a strategic leader that advances effective and dynamic philanthropy; 2) build and cultivate a collaborative and diverse philanthropic network; 3) continue to grow an effective and nimble organizational structure, grounded in sound financial systems and processes; and 4) foster a creative, collaborative, and entrepreneurial internal culture that encourages individual investment that lends to the collective success of the grantee. This grant increase will support additional expenses accrued by the council for its policy advocacy work, which has greatly intensified over the past six months.

title: General Purposes
description: The Council of Michigan Foundations is a statewide association of 300 grantmakers that provides its members with educational programs, technical assistance, networking opportunities, advocacy with policymakers and regulators, and collaborative work with leading national and regional philanthropic associations. This grant increase will support the grantee’s efforts to advocate for sound policies for the philanthropic sector through research, data, and policy analysis.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant increase supports the National Council of Nonprofits, the nation’s largest network of nonprofits, with more than 25,000 member organizations across the country. Its mission is to advance the vital role, capacity, and voice of charitable nonprofit organizations. The grantee works through its network of state associations to help nonprofits operate more effectively, engage in critical policy issues affecting the sector, and achieve greater impact in their communities. This increase will provide much-needed resources for the grantee’s policy advocacy work, as well as some administrative and communications costs associated with supporting it.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support the continued organizational and programmatic development of People in Need, one of the largest nonprofits in Central and Eastern Europe. Founded in 1992, the grantee provides relief and development assistance in response to natural disasters and violent conflict; promotes human rights, civic engagement, and civil society development; and supports social inclusion and integration for marginalized groups. In 2016, the grantee provided relief and development assistance in 24 countries through 227 projects, a 20 percent increase in volume from 2015, and a threefold increase since 2013. During the grant period, the grantee will expand its aid missions in Ukraine, respond to other humanitarian needs around the world, continue programming to reduce the social exclusion of children from marginalized groups in the Czech Republic, and provide technical assistance and support to civil society organizations and human rights defenders in countries under threat. People in Need is based in Prague, Czech Republic.

title: General Purposes
description: This renewal grant provides general purpose support to the Center for Community Progress to further its mission of combating negative effects associated with property vacancy and abandonment in post-industrial urban areas, with a special focus on assisting Flint neighborhoods develop strategies that promote inclusive growth and vitality. Headquartered in Flint, with an office in Washington, D.C., the grantee addresses these issues at federal, state, and local levels through a combination of technical assistance, policy reform, network building, knowledge sharing, communications programs, and leadership and education.

title: Employment Preparation Program
description: This grant will provide support to St. Luke N.E.W. Life Center for the Employment Preparation Program. Serving residents of north Flint, the program works with individuals who are structurally unemployed and need a broad array of wraparound services to adequately prepare them to find and retain employment. The program will continue to expand its outreach to employers for future job placements and establish an alumni network to offer support to participants and graduates. Additionally, the grantee will continue to develop a more robust evaluation and tracking system to measure programmatic outcomes. Providing residents with opportunities for job training and employment will help build Flint’s economic resilience to recover from the water crisis.

title: Fund for Democracy and Solidarity in Europe
description: The program goal is to promote, protect, and reinvigorate the space for civic engagement in Europe. To this end, the Network of European Foundations will manage a grantmaking fund to: 1) support civil society organizations working together to promote and protect the space for civic engagement, 2) improve the quality of public discourse in the digital age, and 3) strengthen independent, public interest journalism in Europe. The grantee will manage and grow a pooled fund, called Civitates, that makes grants and provides networking and technical assistance to nonprofits working on these issues across Europe. With funding from 16 foundations, in 2018-2019, Civitates awarded 38 grants totaling more than €2.6 million. The Network of European Foundations is based in Brussels, Belgium.

title: Technical Assistance for Improved Teaching and Learning
description: This grant allows Michigan State University to support Flint Community Schools with technical assistance aimed at increasing district capacity, improving school culture, increasing operational efficiency, and improving student academic outcomes. To achieve these goals, technical assistance will be focused on four primary components: districtwide systems, leadership development, classroom instruction, and climate and culture.

title: Technical Assistance for Improved Teaching and Learning
description: This grant increase will allow Michigan State University to continue to support Flint Community Schools with technical assistance aimed at increasing district capacity and operational efficiency and improving school culture and student academic outcomes. To achieve these goals, technical assistance will be focused on four primary components: districtwide systems, leadership development, classroom instruction, and climate and culture.

title: Capacity Building
description: This grant will help to build the staff capacity of Communities First, Inc., a nonprofit housing developer and community development agency in Flint. The grantee’s mission is to promote and provide an improved quality of life for residents of distressed communities through economic development and affordable housing solutions. The grant will partially fund positions related to project and fund development, strategic planning, and office management.

title: Capacity Building
description: This grant will help to build the staff capacity of Communities First, a nonprofit housing developer and community development agency in Flint. The grantee’s mission is to promote and provide an improved quality of life for residents of distressed communities through economic development and affordable housing solutions. The grant will partially fund positions related to project and fund development, strategic planning, and office management.

title: Flint BRAND Program
description: Genesee County Habitat for Humanity is an affiliate of Habitat for Humanity International, a nonprofit, ecumenical Christian housing ministry. Its mission is to bring people together to build homes, communities, and hope. The grantee works with neighborhood associations, block clubs, and other local grassroots groups on leadership development and other forms of capacity building. This grant will provide support for the Flint BRAND Program that builds the capacity of neighborhood groups to conceptualize, plan, and assist in implementing projects. These projects will have an immediate visible impact on neighborhood conditions and improve Flint residents’ quality of life.

title: Homeowner Occupied Repair Program
description: This grant will provide support to Genesee County Habitat for Humanity to expand the work of its Homeowner Occupied Repair Program into the neighborhood surrounding the Durant-Tuuri-Mott campus. Residential improvements to homes will be targeted to the streets directly bordering the educational facility in an effort to fully meet the needs of the residential community. Genesee County Habitat for Humanity will partner with local organizations to connect neighborhood residents and leverage additional resources for home repair. This work aligns with a core tenant of Genesee County Habitat for Humanity’s mission of bringing people together to build community.

title: Homeowner Occupied Repair Program
description: This grant will support Genesee County Habitat for Humanity to operate its Homeowner Occupied Repair Program in the neighborhood surrounding Durant-Tuuri-Mott campus. The grantee will partner with local organizations to connect residents to programs and leverage additional resources for home repair. This work aligns with a core tenant of Genesee County Habitat for Humanity’s mission of bringing people together to build community.

title: Blight Elimination and Neighborhood Stabilization
description: This grant will provide support to the Genesee County Land Bank Authority to engage in neighborhood revitalization activities around Kettering University, Durant-Tuuri-Mott Elementary School, Chevy Commons, Mott Park, Flint River, and Atwood Stadium. These activities will include demolishing blighted and abandoned structures, property cleanup, home improvement, paint, and minor repair. Demolishing properties is an important first step in stabilizing the neighborhood.

title: Capacity Building
description: The Hispanic Technology & Community Center of Greater Flint, known as the Latinx Technology & Community Center, provides many programs and services to enhance the dignity and quality of life for the Flint and Genesee County Latino community as well as those from other cultures. The grantee will utilize Mott Foundation funds to support an executive director position and building improvements to increase its capacity to serve Flint residents.

title: Flint-based Healthcare Startup Accelerator
description: This grant will provide support to XLerateHealth, a healthcare business accelerator located in the Ferris Wheel Building in downtown Flint. The accelerator serves as an entry point for entrepreneurs working to create healthcare-related enterprises. A high functioning accelerator can attract new businesses to the Flint area, spur economic growth and create job opportunities for local residents. XLerateHealth will play a key role in the build-out of a regional health science entrepreneurial ecosystem in Flint and Genesee County.

title: North End Soup Kitchen, Warming Center and Medical Transportation
grantee: Catholic Charities of Shiawassee and Genesee Counties
description: This grant will provide support to Catholic Charities of Shiawassee and Genesee Counties to operate intervention services for individuals and families in crisis. The North End Soup Kitchen and Center for Hope Warming Center will provide meals, personal need items, and a place to find warmth during the harsh winter months. The St. Christopher Medical Transportation Program will provide transportation for critically ill children and their families to medical appointments across the state.

title: Soup Kitchens, Warming Center and Medical Transportation
grantee: Catholic Charities of Shiawassee and Genesee Counties
description: This grant will provide support to Catholic Charities of Shiawassee and Genesee Counties to operate intervention services for individuals and families in crisis. There are three soup kitchens and the Center for Hope Warming Center that will provide meals, personal need items, and a place to find warmth during the harsh winter months. The St. Christopher Medical Transportation Program will also provide transportation for critically ill children and their families to medical appointments across the state.

title: Soup Kitchens, Warming Center and Medical Transportation
grantee: Catholic Charities of Shiawassee and Genesee Counties
description: This grant will provide support to Catholic Charities of Shiawassee and Genesee Counties to operate intervention services for individuals and families in crisis. There are three soup kitchens and the Center for Hope Warming Center that will provide meals, personal need items and a place to find warmth during the harsh winter months. The St. Christopher Medical Transportation Program will also provide transportation for critically ill children and their families to medical appointments across the state.

title: Flint Diaper Bank
description: This grant will provide funds to the Food Bank of Eastern Michigan to support the Flint Diaper Bank program in providing diapers to low-income Genesee County residents. By utilizing the grantee’s sophisticated distribution system, the Flint Diaper Bank can ensure that diapers will reach the community’s most needy families and help relieve the stress of families and caretakers who often must choose between supplying diapers for their babies or purchasing other basic necessities.

title: Flint Diaper Bank
description: This grant will provide funds to the Food Bank of Eastern Michigan to support the Flint Diaper Bank program in providing diapers to low-income Genesee County residents. By utilizing the grantee’s sophisticated distribution system, the Flint Diaper Bank can ensure that diapers will reach the community’s most vulnerable families and help relieve the stress from choosing between supplying diapers for their babies, or purchasing other basic necessities.

title: Flint Diaper Bank
description: This grant will provide funds to the Food Bank of Eastern Michigan to support the Flint Diaper Bank program in providing diapers to low-income Genesee County residents. By utilizing the grantee’s sophisticated distribution system, the Flint Diaper Bank can ensure that diapers will reach the community’s most vulnerable families and help relieve the stress from choosing between supplying diapers for their babies or purchasing other basic necessities.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will help support the New America Foundation in its efforts to realize its vision of a nation which supports: 1) thriving families, individuals, and communities with the time, stability, and opportunity to lead self-directed lives; 2) equitable, accessible, and high-quality education and training over a lifetime 3) universal access to digital technology and its benefits across all communities 4) a society that promotes economic opportunity for all; 5) equal representation in politics and participation in accountable governance; and 6) a secure, prosperous America that lives up to its values and commitments at home and abroad. This grant will allow the grantee to explore, working intensively in Flint, what role it could play working with a local government to improve its capacity.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint
description: This renewal grant provides general purpose support to the Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint. Focusing on education, creativity, physical activity and health, and family support services, the grantee offers year-round programming to young people between the ages of 7 and 17 in the Flint area. The grantee operates two sites, one located on the east side and the other on the south side of the city. Programs such as this have been particularly necessary in Flint during the water crisis given that educational and enrichment opportunities are important interventions to help mitigate the long-term impacts of exposure to lead.

title: Flint Community Schools Young Scientists
description: The Cranbrook Educational Community will continue to partner with Flint Community Schools to provide students with supplemental educational opportunities in STEM that correspond to grade-level content. Programming will include classroom outreach, intercession support and internship experiences for high school students.

title: Summer Youth Initiative and TeenQuest
description: This grant provides support to the Genesee Area Focus Fund to implement TeenQuest and the Summer Youth Initiative, which provide job training and employment opportunities for Genesee County teens in partnership with area employers. Teens participate in TeenQuest, a pre-employment training program, and are then eligible to apply for employment through the Summer Youth Initiative.

title: Genesee Early College
description: Genesee Early College is an innovative, educational program administered by the Genesee Intermediate School District in collaboration with the University of Michigan-Flint and six healthcare partners in the region. The focus of the project is to prepare high school students for academic and professional careers in health and sciences, technology, engineering and math fields. Students can earn up to 60 transferable college credits, as well as a high school diploma and scholarship money for higher education.

title: Flint Healthcare Employment Opportunities Program
description: This grant to the Greater Flint Health Coalition will support the Flint Healthcare Employment Opportunities Program. The goal of the program is to create sustainable employment opportunities and promote career advancement for area residents within the healthcare sector. Participants receive industry-focused life skills and career readiness training, occupational instruction, case management, and supportive services; as well as job development assistance. Preparing area residents for good-paying jobs in the medical field will help them, and the community, recover from the effects of the water crisis.

title: Flint STRIVE Replication Program
description: The Flint STRIVE Replication Program, a project of Specialized Employment Services, Inc., provides employment training, job placement, and support services for hard-to-serve Flint area residents. A replication of the East Harlem Employment Service’s workforce training program, Flint STRIVE prepares participants for the workforce through a 19-day, 130-hour intensive workshop that emphasizes the attitudinal prerequisites for successful employment. This grant will allow the grantee to train and place approximately 200 people into entry-level jobs, as the community continues to recover from the water crisis.

title: Tapology Youth Outreach
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide partial support for Tapology outreach programs which will take place online in 2020. Tap dance is an enduring American art form that increases physical activity and enhances cognitive development for participants. The grantee partners with local schools, community centers and the Flint Institute of Music to provide area youth with an introduction to tap dance and offers regular classes for all levels of ability. Each year the grantee’s outreach programming culminates into a four day festival that provides exposure for local students to the art and history of tap. This year the festival will be conducted completely online. Professional artists will continue to provide instruction for beginners, as well as more advanced workshops for experienced young dancers.

title: Music Around Town
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Music Around Town series, formerly known as Music in the Parks, is a broad community partnership led by the Flint Institute of Music. This program offers musical performances in public places around Flint. This year’s Music Around Town program will offer pop-up performances for essential workers and older adults in convalescent homes or facilities. Performances will follow all health guidelines for social distancing and masks.

title: Overture Program and Partnership with Flint Institute of Music
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This renewal grant will provide support to the Sphinx Organization to offer a continuum of music instruction to underserved students in Flint, Michigan. The Sphinx Overture program, which introduces students to classical music and violin, serves all Flint public elementary schools. In partnership with YouthQuest and the Crim Fitness Foundation, the program will provide students with free, afterschool group violin lessons. Music education supports cognitive stimulation and learning, and literacy skill development. Through a partnership with the Flint Institute of Music, students from the program will be eligible for more advanced violin lessons and classes at no cost. In addition, Sphinx Overture students and their families have access to a range of other cultural experiences and enrichment activities including artist-in-residence workshops and performances.

title: General Purposes
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant provides general purposes funding for the operations of the Greater Flint Arts Council, an independent agency which supports local artists and arts participants through several programs including public festivals and events. With a goal of being a catalyst for diverse artistic and cultural programs for the region, the grantee enriches the community with an array of cultural services, educational programs, publications, and events.

title: General Purposes
description: The Black Sash Trust was founded in 1955 by a group of women who were fighting for the recognition of human rights for all in South Africa. Its aim is to contribute to the creation of a society that has effective laws and comprehensive social protection for the most vulnerable. It conducts rights awareness programs for community-based organizations and poor and marginalized people. Past support assisted the grantee to successfully launch and execute initiatives based on systemic injustices faced by communities that need help from community advice offices. Initiatives included the extension of social security to children up to 18 years, equalizing the pensionable age for men and women to 60 years, and more recently, the Hands Off Our Grants initiative. Continued Mott support will assist the grantee in continuing its work with community advice offices on this initiative. The grantee will also co-create initiatives in collaboration with community advice offices on other systemic injustices faced by communities.

title: General Purposes
description: The project goal is to address systemic injustices facing poor and marginalized people in South Africa. To this end, the Black Sash Trust ensures that all people in South Africa have access to their socioeconomic rights, as enshrined in the South African Constitution. Past support allowed the grantee to work with a network of community advice offices to increase peoples’ access to social security and to address systemic injustices through various initiatives. This grant will assist the grantee to continue this work with the advice offices. The grantee will work towards ensuring that the right to social security and social assistance is protected, realized and advanced. The grantee was founded in 1955 by a group of women who were fighting for the recognition of human rights for all in South Africa. The Black Sash Trust’s aim is to contribute to the creation of a society that has effective laws and comprehensive social protection for the most vulnerable.

title: Flint Farmers' Market Operating Support
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will provide operational support for the Flint Farmers’ Market, a key institution in the ongoing efforts to revitalize downtown Flint. Located in the Health and Wellness District, the market provides Flint residents with year-round access to fresh produce and locally grown foods. The market maintains an active calendar of community events, provides attractive public meeting spaces and supports food entrepreneurs through a commercial kitchen co-working space. In addition, market staff educate residents on the importance of healthy eating to mitigate the impact of lead. The Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation receives and administers funds for charitable purposes and for the public welfare of Genesee County, and is the supporting organization of the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, which operates the Flint Farmers’ Market.

title: Downtown Security
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will support the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation’s efforts to promote safety and security in downtown Flint. The Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, a supported organization of the grantee, will contract with a security firm for guards to patrol the city’s downtown area.

title: Neighborhood and Community Planning
description: This grant supports the Genesee County Land Bank Authority’s planning and neighborhood revitalization activities. The grantee develops and operates a nationally renowned program to reclaim vacant and abandoned property and restore it to productive use. This function is overseen by a professional planning and development team that attracts resources, plans, coordinates and implements neighborhood interventions using a variety of tools and strategies. The Genesee County Land Bank Authority’s activities simultaneously enhance the quality of neighborhoods in Flint and promotes citizen stewardship by engaging neighborhood groups in planning the disposition and use of vacant structures, as well as maintaining vacant lots.

title: Flint and Genesee County Community Development Project
description: This renewal grant will provide the Flint office of the Local Initiatives Support Corporation with funding to transform distressed neighborhoods into livable communities. With a focus on creating sustainable communities, the grantee provides organizations with technical assistance as well as loans and grants for development projects that help move Flint forward after the water crisis.

title: General Purposes
description: The Village Information Center was established in 1976 and has published hundreds of issues of the East Village Magazine. The monthly nonprofit publication provides Flint residents and nonprofit groups with news that affects the quality of life in neighborhoods. A companion website offers access to news captured in the magazine, as well as new information that does not make the magazine’s publishing deadline. Between the printed magazine and the online portal, the grantee has a readership of approximately 15,000 people.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to the Crim Fitness Foundation. Focusing on active living, physical fitness, nutrition and mindfulness, the grantee offers year-round programming for children and adults throughout the greater Flint area. The grantee also serves as the lead agency for the Community Education Initiative, which provides access to a variety of wraparound health and educational services for many Flint students and their families. The Crim Festival of Races attracts more than 11,000 walkers and runners as well as tens of thousands of spectators each year.

title: Immigration Services
description: Established in 1988, the Arab American Heritage Council serves the needs of Arab Americans and other recent immigrants in the Genesee County area through programming such as immigration services and cultural events. During the grant period, the project will continue to help immigrants from all backgrounds navigate the American legal system and become acclimated to life in the United States by providing immigration forums and educational workshops, assisting with immigration casework, offering translation services and leading citizenship classes.

title: Flint and Genesee Literacy Network
description: Mott Community College serves as the lead agency for the Flint and Genesee Literacy Network. The network is a coalition of community organizations, businesses and governmental leaders working toward increasing literacy and basic skill levels in Genesee County. The grantee will work with network partners to increase their capacity to deliver high-quality early education and family literacy programming with a particular focus on two-generational approaches.

title: Flint BRAND Program
description: The purpose of the project is to implement transformative projects that leave sustainable, positive impact on their neighborhoods. The Genesee County Habitat for Humanity works with neighborhood associations, block clubs and other local grassroots groups on leadership development and other forms of capacity building. This grant will provide support for the Flint BRAND Program which builds the capacity of neighborhood groups to conceptualize, plan and assist in implementing projects. These projects will have an immediate visible impact on neighborhood conditions and improve Flint residents’ quality of life. Founded in 1990, Genesee County Habitat for Humanity is an affiliate of Habitat for Humanity International, a nonprofit, ecumenical Christian housing ministry. Its mission is to bring people together to build homes, communities and hope.

title: Operating Support
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will renew operating support for the ongoing redevelopment efforts of the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation and its supported organization, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, in downtown Flint. The Uptown Reinvestment Corporation and the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation have been leaders in efforts to revitalize Flint’s downtown district. The work has focused on redeveloping downtown properties for residential and commercial reuse, attracting new employers to downtown Flint and creating and enhancing community amenities for public use. This grant will be used by the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation to support staffing costs to facilitate the charitable purposes and functions of the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, as well as costs for office space rental, contracted services and technology.

title: Municipal Finance System Reform
description: The Michigan Municipal League Foundation’s mission is to help create and maintain vibrant communities in Michigan by funding placemaking projects and educating community leaders and advocates. An important component of vibrant communities is an adequate government financing system that provides enough revenue for a city to provide governmental services. Currently, Michigan does not have a funding system that meets this goal. When a city cannot sustain a reasonable level of services, the quality of life decreases dramatically for all of its citizens, resulting in increased blight, increased crime, and lower quality infrastructure. This grant will help support the development of an educational campaign to help residents and business leaders in Michigan understand how local governments are funded and ways to improve municipal finance systems.

title: Strengthening Access to Justice Through Community Advice Office Support Project
geographic_focus: Eastern Cape, Province of, Western Cape, Province of the
description: The Support Centre for Land Change (formerly known as the Southern Cape Land Committee) was established in 1987 and works with rural communities, farmworkers, farm dwellers, and small-scale farmers to create the conditions for reform. Previous support enabled the grantee to create a community of practice for community paralegals where peer experiential learning took place. This also helped community paralegals and advice offices to provide quality justice services, especially to farmworkers and farm dwellers. This grant will enable the grantee to improve and strengthen access to justice for marginalized communities, address systematic rights violations through joint advocacy efforts, and improve the efforts of community advice offices to become more financially sustainable.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Eastern Cape, Province of, Western Cape, Province of the
description: The project goal is to address systemic injustices faced by peri-urban and rural communities in South Africa. To this end, the Support Centre for Land Change will work with community advice offices to address systemic injustices faced by farmworker communities. Its goal is to ensure that people living in rural settlements and farms have increased access to and ownership of land, resources, and improved living and working conditions. The Support Centre for Land Change was established in 1987 to advance rural people’s human and constitutional rights within the land and agrarian context.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Northern Cape, Province of, Eastern Cape, Province of, Western Cape, Province of the, Free State
description: The Social Change Assistance Trust works to improve the quality of life in poor communities by supporting community-based organizations working in those communities. The grantee was established in 1984 to make grants, provide training, and facilitate sector-wide connections for organizations that promote access to justice, gender equality, youth empowerment, and food security. Past support enabled the grantee to make grants totaling $230,000 to community advice offices and other local development agencies. In addition to providing institutional strengthening support, the grantee provided training on gender-based violence. This grant will continue to support the Social Change Assistance Trust’s work with community advice offices in the Western Cape, Northern Cape, and Eastern Cape provinces by providing funding and capacity development training.

title: Clean Water Campaign
description: Environmental Advocates of New York has worked for more than 50 years to protect New York’s natural resources and the health of its residents from harmful pollution. Environmental Advocates of New York is one of the most respected conservation organizations in New York. Forty percent of New York state lies in the Lake Erie, Lake Ontario, or St. Lawrence River watershed. New York’s waters of the Great Lakes region suffer from many of the same problems faced in other parts of the region, including annual harmful algal outbreaks, billions of gallons of sewage overflows, and due to the legacy of an industrialized past, contamination from industrial chemicals. The Clean Water Campaign will focus on three priorities: 1) securing funds to repair crumbling water infrastructure across local communities; 2) securing funds to replace lead service lines that could expose people to unsafe levels of lead; and 3) identifying and preventing unregulated chemicals from contaminating water.

title: Downtown Land Use Plan
description: The Flint Downtown Development Authority is working to complete a comprehensive land use plan for downtown Flint that builds on the existing Imagine Flint Citywide Master Plan. This plan will serve as a guiding framework for future development within the area. Key components of the plan will include land use/real estate, placemaking, and traffic analysis.

title: Berston Field House Capacity Building
description: This grant will assist the United Way of Genesee County and the Friends of Berston Field House in developing the staffing and organizational capacity to expand and improve the operations of Berston Field House. Friends of Berston Field House’s mission is to enhance the impact of the field house through quality education, athletics, arts, and comprehensive social services. With this support, Friends of Berston Field House will hire essential staff for administration, fund development, and operations. This support will help manage the programming that takes place at Berston Field House and expand fundraising efforts to ensure sustainability.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will allow the Afterschool Alliance to continue its efforts to ensure that children and youth, particularly those in underserved communities, will have access to engaging afterschool opportunities that inspire learning and achievement in school and life. The grantee serves as a critical voice and organizer of the field, works with federal policymakers to advance opportunities for afterschool programs and ensures that the field’s lessons inform national education and youth policy initiatives. The grantee will continue to: 1) serve as an information source on afterschool programs; 2) be an effective voice in its efforts to expand quality afterschool programs; 3) increase access to research and data on the effectiveness of quality afterschool programs; and 4) continue the rollout of the “This Is Afterschool” campaign to highlight the positive impact of afterschool programs on children, families and communities. The grantee will also work with the 50 statewide afterschool networks to support state-level afterschool initiatives and serve as a member of the national Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative. In 2020, the Afterschool Alliance will assist in the rollout of the Mizzen by Mott App and the further development of the Foundation’s thematic partnerships.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to provide an enabling environment for nonprofits, philanthropy, and civic participation by promoting and protecting the freedoms of association, expression, and assembly. To this end, the International Center for Not-for-Profit Law will carry out a range of activities, including enhancing international norms and multilateral engagement to safeguard civic space, promoting appropriate country-level legislation, helping civil society organizations navigate laws once enacted, undertaking and disseminating research and analysis, and raising public awareness about the importance of civil society and cross-border philanthropy. The grantee is based in Washington, D.C.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to provide an enabling environment for nonprofits, philanthropy and civic participation by promoting and protecting the freedoms of association, expression and assembly. To this end, the International Center for Not-for-Profit Law will carry out a range of activities, including enhancing international norms and multilateral engagement to safeguard civic space, promoting appropriate country-level legislation, helping civil society organizations navigate laws once enacted, undertaking and disseminating research and analysis and raising public awareness about the importance of civil society and cross-border philanthropy. The grantee is based in Washington, D.C.

title: Articulating a Great Lakes Sustainability Strategy
geographic_focus: Indiana, Canada, Pennsylvania, Michigan, Ohio, Minnesota, Illinois, Wisconsin, New York
description: The Meridian Institute convenes groups to collaborate, develop strategies, and resolve conflicts for natural resource, environmental, and other challenges. This project seeks to promote the sustainable and responsible use of Great Lakes water resources by convening the industry to engage in the development and advancement of corporate standards and practices to protect and restore water resources in the region. Results will include a strategic framework and action agenda that helps advance company-specific initiatives.

title: General Purposes
description: This general purposes grant supports the Biodiversity Funders Group and its programs to foster collaboration and coordination among philanthropic foundations. Over the last grant period, the grantee grew its programs, adding the Chile Conservation Funders group. The grantee is a membership organization comprised of 72 funding institutions.

title: General Purposes
description: The Global Fund for Community Foundations is a grassroots grantmaker working to promote and support institutions of community philanthropy around the world. The grantee supports individual community foundations and other local grantmakers and their networks with a particular focus on the Global South and the emerging economies of Central and Eastern Europe. Through small grants, technical support, and networking, the fund helps these local institutions to strengthen and grow so that they can fulfill their potential as vehicles for local development. During this grant period, they will 1) support institutional capacity among community foundations and similar philanthropic organizations to build social capital and enhance local decision-making processes in communities; 2) promote collaboration and networks that advance the field of community foundations and other local philanthropic institutions to increase their effectiveness; and 3) influence and build the relationship between the community foundation field and policymakers, governments, and international development agencies.

title: Renewable Energy for Extractive Reserves in the Amazon
description: This project will support the World Wildlife Fund and its partner, World Wildlife Fund Brazil, to continue working on a national program for solar energy for forest-dwelling communities living in sustainable development reserves in the Amazon. Over the past grant period, the grantee built important partnerships with key government agencies and the private sector to advance national public policy for distributed renewable electrification for traditional forest communities in the Brazilian Amazon. Over the next grant period, the grantee and World Wildlife Fund Brazil will strengthen their networks, monitor and disseminate the findings from off-grid solar access models, and work at the local, national, and regional levels to promote policies for replication of renewable energy access for isolated forest peoples.

title: Regulation of Nonprofits and Philanthropy
description: The program goal is to support a healthy policy environment for the nonprofit and philanthropy sector. The Regulation of Nonprofits and Philanthropy project aims to document, enhance understanding, and promote dialogue related to the state and federal regulatory framework and its impact on charities, philanthropy, and the nonprofit sector. The project engages attorney generals and other state officials, federal regulators, academics, researchers, and nonprofit practitioners. In the past two years, the project has produced several research studies on state and federal charity regulation and enforcement. These studies have been presented at several relevant stakeholder gatherings and have spawned additional research and dialogue. Over the next two years, the project will produce research and analysis on state and federal regulatory issues affecting the charitable sector; present at a variety of academic and nonprofit forums and conferences; host a symposium; and disseminate research papers, briefs, and publications. The project is implemented by the Center on Nonprofits and Philanthropy at the Urban Institute—a think tank that builds knowledge about the nation’s social and fiscal challenges.

title: European Community Foundation Initiative
description: The project goal is to develop the community foundation field and strengthen infrastructure for community foundations in Europe. In collaboration with European community philanthropy support organizations, Bundesverband Deutscher Stiftungen will manage and develop the European Community Foundation Initiative. Working with its partners, the grantee will strengthen the capacity of existing community foundations and their associations, promote the community foundation concept and facilitate the establishment of new community foundations, promote the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals as a framework for community foundations and strengthen the visibility and representation of community foundations vis-à-vis the public sector on the national and European levels. During the previous grant period, the grantee provided learning and exchange services to more than 300 community foundation practitioners from 23 European countries through study visits, bilateral exchanges and thematic meetings. Also, the grantee pioneered a training program on the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals as a framework for planning and reporting the contribution of community foundations to the development of their communities. In addition, the grantee published guides to the national community foundation movements in Italy, Romania and Hungary. Bundesverband Deutscher Stiftungen is based in Berlin, Germany.

title: Charity & Security Network
description: The Charity & Security Network promotes and protects nonprofit organizations’ ability to serve communities, support peace and human rights, aid civilians in areas of disaster and armed conflict, and build democratic governance. The grantee does this by convening stakeholders and engaging in dialogue with policymakers, promoting legal frameworks that protect the positive contribution civil society makes to human security, and by coordinating advocacy to support national security policies that respect the work of legitimate civil society organizations. The grantee’s goals for the upcoming grant period include: providing capacity building; monitoring, reporting, and responding to government action to protect the sector from undue restrictions; countering lawfare attacks on nonprofits; and working to make national security standards compliant with humanitarian and human rights law. The Charity & Security Network is a project of NEO Philanthropy, a funder intermediary launched in 1983 as Public Interest Projects.

title: Flint Cultural Center Academy
description: The Flint Cultural Center Foundation will construct a new building to house the Flint Cultural Center Academy which is scheduled to open grades Kindergarten through 5th grade in the fall of 2019. When fully implemented (2022), the school will serve approximately 675 Kindergarten through 8th grade students from Flint and Genesee County. The vision of the Flint Cultural Center Academy is to demonstrate a unique application of education that challenges and surpasses the existing norms of student achievement and learning growth, while addressing the development of the whole child.

title: General Purposes
description: The Council of Michigan Foundations is a statewide association of 300 grantmakers that provides its members with educational programs, technical assistance, networking opportunities, advocacy with policymakers and regulators, and collaborative work with leading national and regional philanthropic associations. During 2017-2019, the grantee will pursue eight strategies: 1) engaging members where they want to be; 2) strategically recruiting new members; 3) connecting members to the assistance they need; 4) conducting active internal evaluation and assessment; 5) growing the sector’s collective voice in public policy; 6) expanding diversity, equity, and inclusion of the sector; 7) nurturing mission-aligned social enterprise opportunities; and 8) achieving organizational effectiveness. Additional funds are available for the general purposes of the organization, including data and policy analysis on the impact of the December 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act.

title: Flint Plays Project
description: This grant will provide support to the United Way of Genesee County to design and build six playgrounds throughout the city. Safe play is an important child development strategy linked to positive academic and behavioral outcomes for children. Neighbors and residents will be included in the design process and have an opportunity to volunteer on the day of construction.

title: Saginaw Bay Watershed Initiative Network
description: Founded in 1985, the Conservation Fund is a national organization that promotes conservation and sustainable economic development. The grantee’s Saginaw Bay Watershed Initiative Network seeks to advance economic, environmental and social sustainability in Michigan’s Saginaw Bay area. With partial support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has achieved the following during the last grant cycle: 1) regranted funds to partner organizations to improve water quality and freshwater habitat in the Saginaw Bay watershed; 2) developed a project focused on increasing the reach of the network to more diverse audiences and communities; 3) implemented recommendations from a Mott-supported report on septic system impacts on water quality in the basin; and 4) hosted a basin-wide conference, “State of the Bay,” in 2019. With this renewal, the grantee will continue to support the regranting program, focus on broadening the reach of the network to more diverse audiences, convene stakeholders in the Saginaw Bay watershed and build on previous successes with septic system education.

title: Great Lakes Business Network
description: The Groundwork Center for Resilient Communities serves communities in northwest Michigan to achieve a more sustainable and resilient future by supporting environmental protection; sustainable economic development; smart transportation; and healthy, local food initiatives. Their Great Lakes Business Network project was launched to elevate the voices of Michigan business leaders on key, Great Lakes issues. The project has proven successful, and with this grant, the grantee will develop a strategic plan to expand the membership of the Great Lakes Business Network and address an expanded range of issues. The grantee has focused initially around concerns about the oil pipeline crossing the Straits of Mackinac. The new plan will help identify and address additional issues.

title: Great Lakes Business Network
description: In January 2017, the Great Lakes Business Network was launched with 11 prominent business leaders. The network is a project of the Groundwork Center for Resilient Communities. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee completed a strategic planning process to explore prospects for expanding membership and issue focus. Renewed support will help the network expand its membership to include businesses in several states, and will address new issues including algae blooms in Lake Erie.

title: General Purposes
description: For 50 years, Clean Wisconsin has been Wisconsin’s leading voice for clean air and water. The grantee seeks to provide all residents with access to healthy air and clean drinking water; provide residents, businesses, and visitors an abundance of swimmable, fishable lakes, rivers, and streams; and promote an economy that is strong and powered by clean energy. With previous project support, the grantee has delivered public education campaigns to prevent harmful diversions of Great Lakes water, reduce pollution sources contaminating drinking water supplies, remove lead pipes, and advance clean water policies and funding. With this general purposes grant, Clean Wisconsin will pursue all of its objectives around climate change, clean energy, clean air and clean water. This will include efforts to: 1) strengthen clean water policies by educating the public, its members, the media and decision makers about programs to protect and restore the Great Lakes; 2) continue to grow its presence with tribes in northern Wisconsin and urban areas of southeast Wisconsin thus elevating voices in underserved areas; 3) develop leadership training for its staff and board; and 4) conduct research to build strong communications programs around Great Lakes issues.

title: General Purposes
description: The Minnesota Environmental Partnership is the largest and most active coalition of environmental and conservation groups in the state. Since 1998 the grantee has helped its member groups convene, communicate and collaborate to protect Minnesota’s bounty of water and land resources to ensure that all residents prosper from a sustainable future. Today, the need for a coalition that brings together conservationists with non-traditional partners to address issues cutting across cultural, social and economic barriers is more important than ever. With this grant, the grantee will help member groups advance environmental issues in the state, including efforts to strengthen and diversify state funding. The Minnesota Environmental Partnership will also expand its operations to protect the Great Lakes, and implement a new strategic plan that calls for forging stronger ties with indigenous groups, working with community groups seeking access to safe water and addressing other environmental justice issues.

title: General Purposes
description: The River Alliance of Wisconsin has empowered people to protect and restore water for 27 years. The grantee supports a network of local organizations and individuals who advocate to defend Wisconsin’s waters from pollution and overuse. Despite the grantee’s successes, Wisconsin faces many water challenges. More than half a million of the state’s residents cannot safely drink their water because of agricultural runoff, lead pipes and chemical pollution. Lakes and streams are shrinking because of over pumping and others are choked with algal blooms. With support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee will expand its organizational capacity to provide statewide leadership on water policy priorities, market-based water stewardship approaches, aquatic invasive species management, restoring free-flowing rivers and engagement with a diverse array of advocates. Central to the River Alliance of Wisconsin’s plans will be leading efforts to adopt and implement a statewide Wisconsin Water Agenda.

title: Healthy Great Lakes Program
description: The Canadian Environmental Law Association is a nationwide organization that provides legal aid, education, outreach and access to the decision making process for under-represented constituents in Ontario, Quebec and federally. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has provided trusted analysis and guidance for decision makers and the public on Great Lakes issues ranging from harmful contaminants in water, watershed planning and protection of drinking water. With renewed support, the grantee will expand its network of constituencies, emphasizing indigenous communities and others, connecting them with the establishment of sound public policies to protect and enhance the Great Lakes. The grantee will lead efforts promoting safe drinking water, free from lead and other toxic chemicals and maintaining strong local organizations to protect watersheds.

title: Great Lakes Leadership Summit
grantee: Conference of Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Governors and Premiers
geographic_focus: Minnesota, Illinois, Ohio, Pennsylvania, New York, Wisconsin, Michigan, Indiana
description: The Conference of Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Governors and Premiers is a nonprofit organization that facilitates cooperation between the governors of eight Great Lakes states and the premiers of two Canadian provinces. With prior Mott support, the grantee organized summits in 2013, 2014, 2015 and 2017, which convened governors and premiers to discuss ways to expand their collaboration to address Great Lakes challenges, such as halting the spread of aquatic invasive species. With renewed Mott support, the grantee will reconvene Great Lakes leaders over three days in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. The summit will focus on Great Lakes ecosystem health and sustainable economic development.

title: General Purposes
description: Founded in 1937, the Michigan United Conservation Clubs is the nation’s largest statewide coalition of conservation clubs. The grantee works to unite its 40,000 individual and 200 organizational members to conserve, protect and enhance Michigan’s natural resources and outdoor heritage. Since its founding, the grantee has provided a buffer in Michigan against political interference in fish and wildlife stewardship and habitat management, ensuring a science-driven approach to conservation issues. The COVID-19 pandemic has brought about an increase in the number of people hunting, fishing, camping and enjoying Michigan’s wealth of resources. With this grant, the grantee will help connect those people with conservation matters. The Michigan United Conservation Clubs will also work to ensure protection and restoration of Michigan’s Great Lakes, rivers and streams through advocacy, education, communications and stewardship.

title: Action for Clean Drinking Water
description: Midwest Environmental Advocates is the only nonprofit environmental law center in Wisconsin that provides legal and technical services directly to community members seeking to protect clean water. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has provided legal and technical support to citizens throughout Wisconsin’s Great Lakes basin on a range of issues including protecting surface and groundwater from pollution, preventing harmful diversions of Great Lakes water through implementing and defending the Great Lakes Compact, and strengthening its organizational capacity by adding staff, strengthening ties to Native American tribes, and diversifying its board of directors. With renewed support, the grantee will provide legal and technical resources to support community-based efforts to protect drinking water in rural and urban communities, work to recalibrate Wisconsin water quality standards to account for increased precipitation due to climate change, hold governments accountable for preventing harmful diversions of Great Lakes water and protecting drinking water, and engage in an organization-wide strategic planning effort.

title: General Purposes
description: The Minnesota Center for Environmental Advocacy has been a legal and scientific voice for Minnesota’s environment since 1974. The grantee’s team of lawyers and environmental scientists work on environmental issues across all branches of government. With this grant, the grantee seeks to defend existing programs, laws and regulations; improve water quality to ensure that Lake Superior and Minnesota waters are swimmable, drinkable and fishable; make Minnesota a leader in reducing climate change causing greenhouse gases; and forge alliances with underserved communities to combat toxic pollution. The grantee has added staff in Duluth who will work with an advisory team to protect Lake Superior. In the coming years, the grantee will work diligently to expand the constituencies they represent to advance equity and support underserved communities. The Minnesota Center for Environmental Advocacy will also work closely with Native American tribes to protect resources and defend tribal sovereignty.

title: Clean Water Act Implementation in the Great Lakes
geographic_focus: Minnesota, Wisconsin, Indiana, Michigan, Ohio, Illinois
description: The Great Lakes are one of our country’s greatest natural treasures, comprising about 20 percent of the earth’s fresh water supply and providing drinking water supplies for 42 million people. The federal Clean Water Act is one of the bedrock laws that protects this globally important resource, and the act allows citizens and citizen groups monitor and help implement its key provisions. The Environmental Law & Policy Center, a key regional environmental group based in Chicago, will monitor implementation of the act in six Great Lakes states.

title: Innovating Clean Water Financing and Community Engagement in the Great Lakes
geographic_focus: Michigan, Minnesota, Pennsylvania, Indiana, Wisconsin, Ohio, Illinois, New York
description: American Rivers is a national organization with a strong leadership footprint in the Great Lakes region.
