The grantee has actively engaged on water quality issues in the Great Lakes for many years, with an emphasis on diffusing sources of runoff and pollution. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has helped advance an integrated, holistic approach to water management that considers pollution from all sources and drinking water from source to tap. The grantee has supported community groups and partners and has produced a report on all eight Great Lakes state’s drinking water policies. With this renewal, American Rivers will continue to advance integrated water management with a special emphasis on green infrastructure solutions, ensuring that water services are equitable for disadvantaged communities, advancing innovative funding solutions and providing direct support for community groups.

title: Water Action Agenda
description: The Metropolitan Planning Council works with government, community, and business leaders to address planning and development challenges in the Chicagoland area. Communities around Chicago suffer from degrading water infrastructure, leaking pipes, and widely varying water rates. Lake Michigan is threatened by Asian Carp and other aquatic invasive species migrating up the Chicago River. The grantee will conduct water affordability research, provide training to local officials on water management best practices, and help lead the Chicago Area Waterways Advisory Council, a group striving to protect Lake Michigan from invasive species.

title: Water Action Agenda
description: The Metropolitan Planning Council is one of the Great Lakes region’s leading urban policy agencies. The grantee is based in Chicago and provides leadership on a range of issues at the local, state, and Great Lakes regional level. With previous support, the grantee has been developing and presenting its Drinking Water 1-2-3 Guide to local decision makers, has developed innovative water affordability assessment tools, and has been a leader in finding solutions to prevent Asian carp from migrating into Lake Michigan via the Chicago River. With renewed support, the grantee will: a) continue working to reduce lead in drinking water; b) release a water rate affordability study and promote on-the-ground implementation of best practices; c) roll out drinking water technical assistance training; d) research opportunities for appropriate water and effluent reuse; e) share lessons learned throughout the Great Lakes; and f) continue to drive forward initiatives to block Asian carp migration.

title: Great Lakes Water Infrastructure Project
geographic_focus: Pennsylvania, New York, Indiana, Ohio, Wisconsin, Illinois, Michigan, Minnesota
description: The Center for Neighborhood Technology works with cities to provide research, tools and solutions to advance sustainable and equitable communities. Based in Chicago, the grantee has focused much of its work on water resource challenges in the Great Lakes region. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has provided workshops and technical assistance on Great Lakes cities’ water infrastructure challenges, including in Flint and Chicago. The grantee has reached out nationally to share findings and seek additional solutions to advance policies and programs to enhance water affordability and environmental sustainability. With continued Mott support, the Center for Neighborhood Technology will design a program with community groups to provide technical assistance on sustainable water infrastructure for five Great Lakes cities and disseminate innovation strategy guides as resources for other Great Lakes cities.

title: Safe Drinking Water Policy Center
geographic_focus: Minnesota, Pennsylvania, New York, Indiana, Illinois, Wisconsin, Michigan, Ohio
description: The Northeast-Midwest Institute is a nonprofit organization dedicated to improving the economic and environmental health of the northeast and midwest regions of the United States. Headquartered in Washington, D.C., and with staff based in Michigan, the grantee provides data, research, and policy analysis to inform state and federal freshwater policy reforms and programs. This grant increase will support efforts to undertake research and policy work related to the grantee’s Safe Drinking Water Program.

title: An Equitable Water Future in the Great Lakes
description: The U.S. Water Alliance is a coalition of water utilities, consultants, environmental and community organizations that work together to advance a holistic approach to water management. With the Mott Foundation’s support, the grantee has become one of the leading organizations advancing water equity in the United States today. The term “water equity” refers to a condition in which all communities have access to safe and affordable water regardless of race or economic status, share in the benefits of water systems and are resilient in the face of climate change and other stressors. The Water Equity Task Force, the first ever cross-sector, multi-city endeavor to make water management equitable, demonstrates how water utilities and front-line community organizations can improve outcomes for low-income people and communities of color through collaboration. Renewed support from the Mott Foundation will enable the grantee to scale up its water equity leadership and support to 75 cities nationwide, including at least ten in the Great Lakes region. Mott Foundation support will enable the One Water Summit, the nation’s premier convening of water leaders, to be held in the Great Lakes region in 2022. The U.S. Water Alliance will also provide expertise and leadership to a national convening around water affordability at the Aspen Institute and to a team working in Michigan with utilities and non-government groups on water equity.

title: Mayors Innovation Project - Affordable Water
geographic_focus: Minnesota, Pennsylvania, New York, Ohio, Michigan, Wisconsin, Illinois, Indiana
description: The Mayors Innovation Project, centered at the University of Wisconsin, is a nationwide learning network of engaged mayors and city officials. The team convenes officials in high quality learning events to address contemporary topics including drinking water and infrastructure. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has provided technical support to Great Lakes cities on water, water affordability and sustainability challenges. Renewed support will enable the grantee to create a movement of cities that recognize that affordable water is critical, reasonable and achievable and to create a pathway to help them achieve that goal. The University of Wisconsin will convene water affordability academies and provide technical assistance through a peer-to-peer network.

title: Bretton Woods Project
description: ActionAid’s Bretton Woods Project has been a key actor on international financial institution reform issues since it was established in 1995. It works with nongovernmental organizations, researchers, and officials to scrutinize and reform policies and practices of international financial institutions, particularly the World Bank Group. Over the last grant period, the project helped to ensure that World Bank Group climate change commitments were kept as well as monitoring the COVID-19 response. With this grant, the Bretton Woods Project will continue its work to strengthen civil society engagement with the World Bank Group, ensure that key climate change commitments are kept and strengthened, ensure that a green transition is embedded into COVID-19 response and provide an information platform that supports policy reform efforts by civil society organizations in the United Kingdom and developing countries.

title: Development Banks and Sustainable Development
geographic_focus: Africa, China, World, Southern Asia, Southeastern Asia, South America
description: China’s development finance institutions have more assets than all others in the current multilateral development finance system, and they have harmed local communities and the environment in ways similar to other multilateral development banks in the past. The way the Chinese development finance institutions respond to the economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic could further impact local communities and the environment. Over the years, the Global Development Policy Center at Boston University has become a major research center analyzing these impacts and providing useful data for relevant Chinese ministries and other stakeholders. Through this grant, the grantee will continue its collaborative research and policy dialogue with governments, civil society, the private sector and development finance institutions. In addition, this grant will assist key Chinese think tanks in undertaking additional research and developing best practices to assist in establishing policies for more sustainable Chinese development finance.

title: Ensuring Development and Climate Finance Support Sustainable Development
description: The Center for International Environmental Law was founded in 1989 to strengthen international environmental law, policy, and management. This grant will support activities that promote and seek strong implementation of sound environmental and social policies and practices at the World Bank Group and other international financial institutions. Over the last grant period, the grantee’s expertise has led to strengthened implementation guidance for the new standards, and ensured that these standards reflect international best practice.

title: Addressing Changes in International Development Finance
description: Since 1990, Eurodad has led a network of nongovernmental organizations working on issues related to development finance, sustainable development and poverty reduction. The grantee works to strengthen the capacity of civil society organizations in Europe, Africa and Latin America to transform international development finance, making it more transparent and sustainable. Over the past grant period, the grantee has highlighted the fiscal, environmental and social risks of public-private partnerships and the need for comprehensive impact assessment as a feature of due diligence of such partnerships. This project will continue to promote strong environmental and social standards for international development finance to ensure that sustainable development is the key outcome for these investments.

title: Strengthening the ACCESS Coalition
description: To deliver on the United Nation Sustainable Development Goal on energy access, greater and better-targeted action is urgently needed to connect rural communities, especially in Africa. To address this challenge, it is critical that African civil society has the capacity to engage with national energy planning agencies to better inform investment decisions in the region, particularly via the African Development Bank and the World Bank Group. To encourage more African civil society engagement, the British development charity, Catholic Agency for Overseas Development, helped to establish the ACCESS coalition. Through this grant, the grantee will work to strengthen the ACCESS coalition and help to develop strategies to increase financing for off-grid renewable energy solutions in Africa.

title: General Purposes
description: The NGO Forum on the Asian Development Bank has been advocating for sustainable development policies that are beneficial to local communities and the environment in the Asian region for two decades. It works to improve public participation, access to information, and good governance at the Asian Development Bank and the new Chinese development finance institutions. Over the next two years, the grantee will continue to participate in the review of the Asian Development Bank’s environmental and social safeguard policies. The grantee also will monitor the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank’s project lending to better understand how well it complies with its stated policies. In addition, the grantee will expand its work to build the capacity of Asian civil society to engage more fully in national energy planning processes.

title: International Program
description: Oil Change International has worked for nearly two decades to increase the transparency of international financial institution lending in the energy sector, ensuring that there is better data to inform policymakers. The overarching goal of this project is to shift international development finance away from fossil fuels to clean energy and energy access for the poor in rural areas. Over the last grant period, the grantee’s work was pivotal in attaining commitments from key development finance institutions to move their financing away from fossil fuels. The grantee’s data collection and analysis has significantly expanded the capacity of civil society to track public finance for fossil fuels. With this renewal grant, Oil Change International will continue its work in support of renewable energy and energy access.

title: Mainstreaming Environmental Sustainability into a Changing Development Finance
description: Re:Common is an Italian organization formed in 2012 that grew out of a long-established, nongovernmental organization project addressing World Bank Group reform. The main goal of this project is to monitor the changes taking place in international development finance and ensure that this financing continues to support and promote sustainable development. This grant increase will support research and policy analysis as well as public awareness to address new development finance institutions that are promoting large-scale infrastructure and energy projects in developing countries.

title: Promoting Environmental and Social Standards in the Financial Sector
description: Urgewald is a German based organization that works to establish strong, binding environmental and social standards for international development finance institutions and to gain public support for responsible and accountable public international financial institutions. To achieve these goals, the grantee undertakes research, education and advocacy efforts with a global network of local communities, nongovernmental organizations and other partners. The grantee has played a key role in ensuring that the World Bank Group, Asian Development Bank and the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank’s environmental and social framework continue to maintain the highest standards for development finance lending. Over the next grant period, the grantee will monitor implementation and review of these banks’ environmental and social policies. In addition, Urgewald will work to ensure that their lending is aligned to agreed climate policies and supports of global goals on energy access.

title: Greening Chinese Development Finance
description: Over the past decade, China has provided sizable amounts of development finance. Many of these projects have caused negative impacts, which has led to public opposition in host countries to further Chinese investments. China’s focus on creating energy, transport, and communication infrastructure linkages from Asia to Europe, the Middle East, and Africa through its Belt and Road Initiative is ambitious and has the potential for either large-scale negative or positive environmental and social impacts. Over the last grant period, World Wildlife Fund in the U.S. and China have worked with civil society partners globally to develop a coordinated approach to encourage financing for a clean energy transition throughout developing Asia. Over the next two years, the grantee will focus on improving effectiveness of China’s risk management framework, increasing dialogue with Chinese development finance institutions, and strengthening the grantee’s capacity to work more collaboratively with other Chinese organizations.

title: Flint Cultural Center Academy Implementation
description: This grant to the Flint Cultural Center Corporation will support the implementation of the Flint Cultural Center Academy, a charter school operated in partnership with the campus institutions. The Flint Cultural Center Academy will offer a robust curriculum that leverages the educational and programmatic assets of the Flint Institute of Arts, Flint Institute of Music, Flint Public Library, Sloan*Longway, and The Whiting. During the first year of operation, the Flint Cultural Center Academy will serve 300 students in Kindergarten through fifth grade.

title: Solar Energy for Amazon River Dwellers
grantee: Centro de Estudos Avançados de Promoção Social e Ambiental
description: The Centro de Estudos Avançados de Promoção Social e Ambiental is a nonprofit organization in the Amazon founded in 1985 to promote sustainable community development and Amazon forest conservation by improving public policies and quality of life of children, youth, indigenous peoples and minorities. Over the previous grant period, the grantee’s Health and Happiness Project installed off-grid solar systems in five communities, organized technical trainings and contributed to a policy symposium and trade fair for renewable energy. Over this grant period, the project will work with isolated communities in the Brazilian Amazon region of the Tapajos River basin to design and implement sustainable community-managed renewable energy systems and monitor performance and organize trainings at its forest center. The grantee also will provide technical information to inform and expand a new public renewable electrification program.

title: Solar Electrician and Entrepreneurship Training
description: The Salesian Missions have been providing education and technical training to poor children around the globe since 1947. Vocational training centers across Tanzania began to be established in 1980. Over the past two years, the grantee has expanded their vocational training to address the need for technical expertise in solar energy and entrepreneurial skills for young Tanzanians. The solar electric training program has graduated over 300 marginalized young people in its first two years and has established two modern solar electric laboratories and training facilities in two rural regions of Tanzania. Through this renewal grant, the Salesian Missions and the Tanzanian Don Bosco vocational training centers will expand the solar electrician training program with extra efforts to recruit more young women into the program as well as enhance entrepreneurial training modules for the program.

title: Building an Inclusive Financial Ecosystem for End Users and Enterprises
description: The Global Fund for Community Foundations is a global, grassroots grantmaker, established in 2009 to assist local philanthropy. The grantee is working with the Tanzanian Association of Microfinance Institutions to provide training and capacity building for Tanzanian financial service providers to support micro, small and medium enterprises in the energy sector. With continued Mott support, capacity building programs will be maintained and expanded to help local-level finance service providers understand clean energy technologies as well as new approaches to financing the renewable energy sector in Tanzania.

title: SEforAll: Energizing Finance Initiative
description: Ensuring global access to sustainable energy for everyone will require a massive deployment of financial resources, but recent evidence shows that funding levels remain firmly below the required amounts. Catalyzing the finance needed begins with a clear, data-based understanding of the financial needs and gaps in funding. The Energizing Finance Initiative of Sustainable Energy for All, a project of the United Nations Foundation, provides such data in a series of annual and biennial reports and associated communications and outreach. The grantee, a non-profit partner of the United Nations, seeks to bring together the ideas, people and resources needed to drive global progress and tackle urgent problems.

title: Building National Dialogues on Integrated Electricity Planning in East Africa
description: The World Resources Institute was founded in 1982 to provide information, ideas and solutions for global environmental problems. With previous Mott support, the grantee has tailored its Energy Access Explorer tool for the unique needs of Tanzania. Using the tool and stakeholder engagement, the grantee has supported the development of integrated energy plans and strategies at both national and sub-national levels that define clear roles for grid and off-grid electrification. With this renewal grant, the World Resources Institute will continue to use its research and convening capabilities to facilitate dialogue between national agencies, local governments and private developers in implementing integrated electrification efforts in Tanzania. This grant renewal will also support expanded efforts in other African countries to help civil society organizations effectively engage in national-level integrated energy planning.

title: Supporting the Energy Access Ecosystem
description: Only 17 percent of Tanzania’s rural population has access to electricity. To reach these rural areas requires a basket of energy solutions from grid extension, rooftop solar home systems, mini-grids, and standalone systems. Off-grid clean energy models have gained traction across Africa as a strong alternative in areas where traditional grid extension will have difficulty reaching poor households. There is a cadre of entrepreneurs creating new business models that need to have adequate training and mentoring to ensure that these businesses can reach poor rural areas with lighting and livelihoods from clean energy. Through this grant, Fraxen Consulting will facilitate and coordinate the projects in Tanzania that are helping to build a stronger environment for such micro-, small, and medium enterprises to thrive.

title: Supporting the Energy Access Ecosystem
description: For Tanzania’s rural communities, low economic growth and inequality are ubiquitous. Their ability to access sustainable, clean energy can play a key role in addressing these challenges. To move forward, there is a need for renewable energy technical skills, entrepreneurial skills for small business development and capacity building to encourage local financial institutions to lend to the small businesses and their customers. This is the crux of a systematic approach to support local off-grid clean energy development and deployment. Fraxen Consulting has assisted in the development of these capacity building initiatives, particularly leading in the development of a new Tanzanian consortium to work on clean energy. Over the next two years, the grantee will continue to facilitate and build synergies for the projects in Tanzania.

title: Building Sustainable Local Energy Enterprises Serving the Poor
description: The Entrepreneurship Management and Development Foundation was established in 2010 to assist individuals and micro, small, and medium enterprises in Tanzania to develop stronger entrepreneurial skills. A particular focus is the development of off-grid renewable energy companies. Tanzania’s national electric grid reaches very few people, with only seven percent of its rural populations having access to electricity. To reach the rural areas, it is crucial that entrepreneurs are provided with adequate training and mentoring to develop these businesses. Through this grant, entrepreneurs will be trained in managing financial and operational concerns; balancing social and commercial goals; identifying products and solutions to meet the needs of poor clients; and developing viable supply and distribution networks to reach the most difficult areas.

title: Building Sustainable Local Energy Enterprises Serving the Poor
description: The Entrepreneurship Management and Development Foundation (IMED) is a nonprofit organization that seeks to help young entrepreneurs in Tanzania launch and grow successful enterprises. Tanzania’s national electric grid reaches very few people, with a very small percent of its rural populations having access to electricity. To reach the rural areas, it is crucial that entrepreneurs are provided with adequate training and mentoring to develop these businesses. With prior Mott support, the grantee developed a training program for the off-grid, clean energy sector. With renewed support, the grantee will refine and expand the program, supporting more clean energy entrepreneurs through a variety of services, including financing and other tools.

title: Impact of Partnerships and Trusts Supporting Civil Society in Eastern Europe
grantee: Research Foundation of the City University of New York
description: The project goal is to document and analyze the lessons learned from five donor partnerships that supported civil society development in Central and Eastern Europe during the past 20 years. Through field research and review of existing documentation, researchers will explore the setup, operation, and impact of five partnerships and trusts established over the last 25 years to support civil society development in Eastern Europe. The partnerships and trusts to be analyzed include 1) the foundations included in the Environmental Partnership Association, 2) the Baltic American Partnership Fund, 3) the Trust for Civil Society in Central and Eastern Europe, 4) the Balkan Trust for Democracy, and 5) the Black Sea Trust for Regional Cooperation. Results will be disseminated widely online and in publications, including Alliance magazine. The grantee will also share the report through its international fellows network. Founded in 1846, the City University of New York is among the nation’s leading urban public universities. The Research Foundation of the City University of New York was created to expedite and provide oversight of the management of funds obtained by faculty.

title: Mobilizing Social Assets for Productive Use of Renewable Energy in Rural Tanzania
description: Over the last decade of off-grid energy development in Africa, an important ingredient for the success of off-grid renewable energy has been elusive. Energy entrepreneurs have not been able to adequately assess the ability of off-grid, rural communities to receive, make good use of, and pay for new energy services. Better market and social assessment tools are needed to address this barrier. This project will support the University of Michigan, in partnership with the University of Dar es Salaam, to provide assessment tools for off-grid energy providers as they develop new energy systems. The Universities of Michigan and Dar es Salaam will work collaboratively with rural communities, local experts, and international partners to secure rural livelihoods through productive use of renewable energy.

title: Mobilizing Social Assets for Productive Use of Renewable Energy in Rural Tanzania
description: Over the last decade, an important ingredient for the success of off-grid renewable energy development in Africa has been elusive. Energy entrepreneurs have not been able to adequately assess the ability of off-grid, rural communities to receive, make good use of and pay for new energy services. Better market and social assessment tools are needed to address this barrier. Over the past grant period, University of Michigan researchers have helped prove that rural communities can successfully manage and benefit from well-planned off-grid energy projects. The grantee has worked with a local university to provide data on the capacity of last-mile rural communities to support off-grid energy services. The University of Michigan will work collaboratively with Saint John’s University, based in Dodoma, Tanzania, as well as other partners to catalyze off-grid energy projects that improve rural livelihoods through productive use of renewable energy.

title: Coolidge Park Apartments
description: This grant increase to Communities First, Inc., will support redevelopment of the former Coolidge Elementary School in Flint into a mixed-use residential apartment complex that will consist of 54 new residential apartment units, including 42 affordable housing units. New commercial office and retail space will also be part of the development. The Coolidge Park Apartments project meets a significant need for new, high-quality affordable housing options in Flint, and will help to stabilize the surrounding neighborhood.

title: Determining the Economic Impact of Protecting and Restoring the Great Lakes
geographic_focus: Pennsylvania, New York, Ohio, Minnesota, Wisconsin, Illinois, Michigan, Indiana
description: This grant increase to the Great Lakes Commission will expand on earlier efforts to estimate the economic impact of the federally funded Great Lakes Restoration Initiative. The grantee is a key regional organization engaged in the protection and restoration of the Great Lakes ecosystem.

title: Computer Science in Afterschool
grantee: New York City Foundation for Computer Science Education
description: This grant to the New York City Foundation for Computer Science Education will provide funding to support the Computer Science for All consortium’s annual meeting in Detroit, Michigan and to expand access to computer science in afterschool and summer learning programs.

title: Clean Energy Initiative
description: Michigan is in the midst of a major energy transition, which includes greater reliance on renewable energy sources, such as wind and solar, and reductions in energy demand through a variety of energy efficiency improvements. This “clean energy” transition presents opportunities and challenges that are felt acutely at the community level. Community foundations are well-positioned to help successfully address such challenges and opportunities. With this grant, the Community Foundation of Marquette County will create and distribute energy information materials, develop at least three demonstration sites that illustrate energy efficiency and renewable energy practices, and convene an energy awareness community event at the end of the project.

title: Clean Energy Initiative
description: Michigan is in the midst of a major energy transition, which includes greater reliance on renewable energy sources, such as wind and solar, and reductions in energy demand through a variety of energy efficiency improvements. This “clean energy” transition presents opportunities and challenges that are felt acutely at the community level. Community foundations are well-positioned to help successfully address such challenges and opportunities. With this grant, the Keweenaw Community Foundation, located in Michigan’s Upper Peninsula, will conduct a community-wide energy summit, promote energy efficiency among its nonprofit partners, and support the installation of a community solar installation.

title: Clean Energy Initiative
description: Michigan is in the midst of a major energy transition, which includes greater reliance on renewable energy sources, such as wind and solar, and reductions in energy demand through a variety of energy efficiency improvements. This “clean energy” transition presents opportunities and challenges that are felt acutely at the community level. Community foundations are well-positioned to help successfully address such challenges and opportunities. With this grant the Grand Traverse Regional Community Foundation, in collaboration with other community foundations and clean energy nonprofits in the region, will assist local governments’ efforts to establish and pursue ambitious clean energy goals.

title: Clean Energy Initiative
description: Michigan is in the midst of a major energy transition, which includes greater reliance on renewable energy sources, such as wind and solar, and reductions in energy demand through a variety of energy efficiency improvements. This “clean energy” transition presents opportunities and challenges that are felt acutely at the community level. Community foundations are well-positioned to help successfully address such challenges and opportunities. With this grant, the M&M Area Community Foundation, located in the border area of Michigan and Wisconsin, will work with up to 15 school districts to raise awareness and adoption of clean energy technologies.

title: Strengthening Dam Standards and Protecting Rivers
description: International Rivers is a U.S.-based, global organization working in more than 40 developing countries in Latin America, Asia, and Africa to promote sustainable use of freshwater river systems and minimize the social and environmental impacts of large-scale hydroelectric energy development. During the past grant period, the grantee monitored hydroelectric impacts in Brazil, Peru, and Colombia and contributed to strengthening Chinese commitments to the United Nations to improve its social and environmental performance. Over the next grant period, International Rivers will work with communities affected or potentially impacted by large-scale hydroelectric finance and development in the greater Amazon rainforest to ensure social and environmental safeguards are complied with and to enhance local understanding of energy planning, licensing, and construction of hydroelectric facilities in the region.

title: Growing Role of Brazil in Latin America
description: This grant supports the IPS-Inter Press Service in Montevideo, Uruguay to increase the quality and quantity of journalistic coverage of energy and infrastructure development and finance in Brazil and South America. Over the past grant period, the grantee mentored a network of 18 journalists and published 57 articles with photos and 10 videos on development in South America. Over this grant period, the network of journalists will be strengthened and coverage will focus on inspirational community development initiatives compared to large-scale, high-risk energy and infrastructure development. IPS-Inter Press Service is a global news agency operating in more than 100 countries and has been working in Latin America for more than 50 years with a network of journalists reporting from many countries in the region.

title: Downtown Hotel Pre-design Study
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant increase will allow the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation to support the pre-development work for renovating the former Genesee County Savings Bank building into a hotel in downtown Flint. This work includes an evaluation, analysis, design, and engineering. This redevelopment effort aims to continue the resurgence of downtown and provide lodging for visitors to the city.

title: Engaging Youth Through Service
description: This grant will support America’s Promise Alliance to engage young people throughout the United States in youth-led service projects. Specifically, the grantee will leverage the reach of their partners to mobilize up to 500,000 young people to pursue service in their communities.

title: General Purposes
description: The Flint River and its tributaries are an important recreational resource for the region’s residents, while also providing important habitat for a variety of freshwater species and other wildlife. The Flint River Watershed Coalition works to protect the Flint River and its tributaries. With this renewal grant, the grantee will maintain all of its education and outreach efforts, as well as attend to its own organizational development needs.

title: Perry Drug Store Building Renovation
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will provide funding to the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, a supported organization of the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation for the redevelopment of the former Perry Drug Store Building located at 600 S. Saginaw Street. The building will be converted into a small retail center for multiple tenants. The project furthers the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation’s charitable mission of improving and revitalizing downtown Flint.

title: 21st Century Community Learning Centers Institute
description: This grant to Foundations, Inc., will provide funding to support an annual conference for afterschool educators and practitioners to build the capacity of afterschool programs and the afterschool field. The conference is one of the largest available for the administrators of the 21st Century Community Learning Centers and includes technical assistance and strategies to continue to enhance the quality of school-community afterschool programs. Session topics will include best practices in evaluation designs, data collection, STEM, and community engagement.

title: Saginaw Bay Watershed Initiative Network
description: Founded in 1985, the Conservation Fund is a national organization that promotes conservation and sustainable economic development. The grantee’s Michigan office oversees the Saginaw Bay Watershed Initiative Network, which seeks to advance economic, environmental, and social sustainability in the Saginaw Bay area. With this increase, the grantee will broaden the scope of analyzing the problem of septic waste in the Saginaw Bay basin.

title: International Conference on Municipal Fiscal Health
description: The Lincoln Institute of Land Policy seeks to improve the quality of life through the effective use, taxation, and stewardship of land. This grant will support the International Conference on Municipal Fiscal Health. The conference will focus on key policy challenges and share sustainable solutions for cities.

title: Building Broader Communities in the Americas
description: The project goal is to foster partnerships between community foundations and other organizations in the U.S. and Canada. Project activities will include peer learning and convenings for community foundations and other organizations, presentations at conferences, regranting for community foundations to conduct mapping exercises, and a strategic plan. The project will be managed by CFLeads, an organization that helps community foundations build strong communities by advancing effective practices, sharing knowledge, and galvanizing action on critical issues. Established in 1991 as the Coalition of Community Foundations for Youth under the Greater Kansas City Community Foundation, CFLeads became an independent nonprofit organization in 2017.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to support and expand the field of community foundations in Mexico. Comunalia is an alliance of Mexican community foundations that focuses on local development and strategic social investment. Founded in 2011, it currently has 16 members and six associated groups. Over the next three years, Comunalia’s work will include: annual surveying of financial and operating characteristics and capacity building needs; webinars and workshops on issues of common interest; implementation assistance for programming related to disaster preparedness and community resilience, the Sustainable Development Goals, giving circles and youth philanthropy; technical assistance and training for legal and fiscal compliance, strengthening governance, fundraising, donor relations and other managerial challenges; networking and peer learning support; challenge grants to stimulate local and national giving; and support to newly emerging community foundations in Mexico.

title: International Fellows Program on Community Philanthropy
grantee: Research Foundation of the City University of New York
description: The Research Foundation of the City University of New York was created to expedite and provide oversight of the management of funds obtained by faculty. The International Fellows Program on Community Philanthropy is operated by the Center of Philanthropy and Civil Society within The Graduate Center of the grantee. Each year, the program offers emerging young leaders and seasoned community foundation practitioners from foreign countries opportunities to learn about community foundations through an intensive graduate program of research, seminars, conferences, and mentoring. Since its inception in 1989, 218 individuals from 66 countries have participated. The grantee’s program has sparked the creation of new philanthropic ventures and research resources in places as diverse as New Zealand, South Korea, Turkey, India, South Africa, and Uruguay. Founded in 1846, the grantee is among the nation’s leading urban public universities.

title: Advancing the Next Generation of Civil Society Assistance
description: The project goal is to help funders, policymakers, and civic activists take the full measure of the changes buffeting civil society globally and advance efforts to rethink civic engagement and civil society development assistance. The Carnegie Endowment for International Peace will include: 1) expanding a civic activism scholars network from ten to 12 scholars, 2) convening four workshops and international meetings, 3) publishing ten articles and two major reports, and 4) conducting interviews and consultations with at least ten assistance practitioners and policymakers. During 2016-2018, the grantee generated knowledge in the form of articles and reports and created linkages between the research, practice, and policy domains through workshops and briefings. Established in 1910 in Washington, D.C. with a gift from Andrew Carnegie, the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace is a private, nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing cooperation between nations and promoting active international engagement by the United States.

title: Youth Empowerment Partnership Programme
grantee: International Academy Berlin for Innovative Pedagogy, Psychology and Economy gGmbH
description: The project goal is to bring about sustainable change in local communities across Europe through innovative approaches to youth empowerment and community development. The International Academy Berlin for Innovative Pedagogy, Psychology and Economy gGmbH provides technical assistance, organizes networking opportunities, and coordinates joint initiatives for the Youth Empowerment Partnership Programme, a Europe-wide network of community-based youth projects. During 2017-2018, the grantee supported 20 local program sites and worked with 15 project partners across 17 European countries. The grantee provided direct technical assistance to local program sites in the network, trained young people and community stakeholders on a range of topics, and organized international networking opportunities for young people and practitioners. In 2018, more than 11,800 people were directly involved in community projects, including over 6,300 young people. The grantee and its partners secured significant European Commission funding for a range of projects. The grantee is based in Berlin, Germany.

title: South by Southwest Panel Sponsorship
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to Creative Many Michigan will support a panel session—Water Insights from the Great Lakes State—at the South by Southwest Conference in Austin, Texas. Panelists will highlight topics important not only to Michigan residents but issues that have national implications including water infrastructure and the fresh water quality of the Great Lakes. Panelists will also host a discussion session for a deeper dive into the topics and issues raised during the panel. The conference draws a broad audience of artists, creators, entrepreneurs and technology professionals working toward new solutions for challenges facing communities across the country.

title: Flint Cultural Center Academy
description: The Flint Cultural Center Foundation will construct a new building to house the Flint Cultural Center Academy. The Academy is scheduled to open in the fall of 2019 with grades Kindergarten through 5th. When fully implemented (2022), the school will serve approximately 650 Kindergarten through 8th grade students primarily from Flint and Genesee County. The vision of the Academy is to demonstrate a unique application of education that challenges and surpasses the existing norms of student achievement and learning growth, while addressing the development of the whole child.

title: Capitol Theatre Renovation
description: This grant increase will support renovations to the historic Capitol Theatre in downtown Flint and its reopening as a live entertainment venue. Built in 1928, the theater is an important undeveloped asset in the downtown core area that, once restored, will complement and enhance other efforts to revitalize downtown Flint and reduce urban blight. Once fully operational, the theater has the capacity to attract between 60,000 and 80,000 visitors annually. The Flint Cultural Center Corporation, the supported organization of the Flint Cultural Center Foundation, will partner with the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation to redevelop and operate the theater.

title: Advancing Entrepreneurship Education
description: This grant will support the Young Entrepreneur Institute at University School located in Hunting Valley, Ohio. Founded in 2005, the institute partners with organizations throughout Northeast Ohio to provide every young person with access to entrepreneurial education and experiences. One goal of this project is to increase opportunities for youth to understand and experience entrepreneurship by infusing entrepreneurship into the 50 state afterschool networks. The second goal is to increase engagement of regional ecosystems in youth entrepreneurship within under-served and under-resourced communities.

title: Global Philanthropy Forum
grantee: World Affairs Council of Northern California
description: Founded in 2001, the Global Philanthropy Forum is a project of the World Affairs Council of Northern California. The project aims to build, sustain, and continuously revitalize a learning community of private donors and social investors committed to international causes. Through conferences, tailored programs, and individual contacts, the project connects donors to one another and to foundation executives, policymakers, issue experts, leaders of civil society organizations, and social entrepreneurs. Over the past several years, the project has established partnerships and helped organize gatherings of philanthropists in Brazil and Africa. In 2020, the grantee will host an annual conference in Berkley, California. The project will continue to provide other learning and partnering opportunities, including its affiliate relationships with the Brazilian and African Philanthropy Forums. The World Affairs Council of Northern California is a nonprofit, nonpartisan educational organization devoted to engaging the public in a discussion of the transnational issues of tomorrow.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant increase will enable the Afterschool Alliance to provide additional support to the afterschool field, including the statewide afterschool networks, to respond to the challenging policy landscape and proposed cuts to afterschool programs. Specifically, this grant increase will: 1) support the implementation of a coordinated communications campaign to highlight the positive benefits of afterschool programs for students, families, and communities; and 2) provide additional capacity to the statewide networks to respond to the challenging policy environment.

title: Nonprofit Employment Data Project
description: The Nonprofit Employment Data Project is a collaboration between the Johns Hopkins University’s Center for Civil Society Studies and the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics that charts nonprofit employment, wages, and finances over time and in relation to other industries. Past results include the publication of a comprehensive national report based on nonprofit employment data over 1999-2009 and several state-level reports. In 2016 the grantee launched a user-friendly, interactive database called Nonprofit Works which provides nonprofit employment data through 2012. While an input of the 2015 data was anticipated and has already occurred, a grant increase and extension are needed to upload the 2016 data and utilize both years’ data in outreach, dissemination, and marketing efforts for Nonprofit Works—in the fall of 2018. Johns Hopkins University is one of America’s premier research universities. The Center for Civil Society Studies seeks to improve the understanding and effective functioning of not-for-profit, philanthropic, or civil society organizations.

title: Impacts and Alternatives to Current Investment and Development Patterns on Environmental and Sustainability Options in Latin America
grantee: Uruguayan Study Center of Appropriate Technologies
description: The Uruguayan Study Center of Appropriate Technologies is a nongovernmental academic organization that carries out research and promotes sustainable development models in South America. Over the past grant period, the grantee published widely in academic journals and mainstream media and held courses. Over the next grant period, the project will be completed and the grantee will finalize and publish its research on social and environmental impacts of energy and infrastructure investment in South America and environmentally sustainable alternatives.

title: Operating Support
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant increase will provide additional support to the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation and its supported organization, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation. Funding will allow the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation the flexibility to respond to new redevelopment opportunities in downtown Flint.

title: Strengthening New Development Bank Safeguards
grantee: Pontifical Catholic University Rio de Janeiro
description: The BRICS Policy Center, part of the Pontifical Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro, is a think tank dedicated to studying the transformation in international development finance and its influence on social and environmental standards for infrastructure development in South America and the Amazon. Over the past grant period, the grantee built an online “China Panel” to track investment in the region, developed and published research and analysis, and organized knowledge exchanges. The Pontifical Catholic University Rio de Janeiro will continue over the next grant period to deepen knowledge and data on key development finance transformations and the consequences for social and environmental governance.

title: Community Philanthropy Development in Brazil
grantee: Institute for the Development of Social Investment
description: The project goal is to promote community philanthropy in Brazil. Based on its prior research, the Institute for the Development of Social Investment will develop a strategic plan for the creation of community foundations in Brazil. The project will be broken down into four components. The first component is to meet with consultants that have experience in the community foundation field to enhance the grantee’s knowledge. The second is to meet with local philanthropic institutions to identify the challenges and opportunities of the community foundation model. The third is to engage investors and leverage local resources for community foundations. The fourth is to create a development plan for community foundations in Brazil. Founded in 1999, the Institute for the Development of Social Investment is a philanthropy service organization that promotes private social investment and strategic philanthropy, primarily in Brazil but also throughout Latin America, and it is an affiliate of the Charities Aid Foundation Global Alliance.

title: Community Philanthropy Development in Brazil
grantee: Institute for the Development of Social Investment
description: The project goal is to promote community philanthropy in Brazil. Over the past year, staff of the Institute for the Development of Social Investment developed a firm understanding of the community foundation concept, exposed more Brazilian philanthropists to the concept and developed a ten-year vision and a three-year operational plan to support the development of community foundations in Brazil. The grantee’s goals over the next two years are to: 1) help establish at least three new community foundations that are well-structured and operating in Brazil, as well as support at least five other groups in a structuring process; 2) create a fund with a matching strategy that will catalyze the engagement of local philanthropists; and 3) include community foundations in the Brazilian philanthropy ecosystem as a viable and impactful option for social investment. Founded in 1999, the Institute for the Development of Social Investment is a philanthropy service organization that promotes private social investment and strategic philanthropy, primarily in Brazil but also throughout Latin America, and is an affiliate of the Charities Aid Foundation Global Alliance.

title: Sustaining the Great Lakes Project
geographic_focus: Indiana, Minnesota, Michigan, Ohio, New York, Pennsylvania, Illinois, Wisconsin
description: The National Wildlife Federation, a national conservation group with a strong presence in the Great Lakes Basin, partners with regional and state-level organizations to protect and restore the Great Lakes from invasive species, toxic pollution, and harmful algal blooms. The grantee continues to deepen its efforts, particularly through informing policy and monitoring implementation, providing scientific information and assistance, leading public education, and building a diverse base of collaborators. This grant increase will allow the grantee to help identify information about the risks posed by and possible alternatives to Line 5, also known as the Mackinac Straits Oil Pipeline.

title: General Purposes
description: The Global Fund for Community Foundations was established to support and promote community philanthropy around the world. The grantee focuses on supporting the development of community foundations and other community philanthropy organizations as essential institutions in the broader civil society sector that advance the well-being of communities on the edges of society. It makes grants, provides technical support, and builds knowledge and evidence on the importance of people-centered and community-led development. Past support enabled the grantee to make grants to more than 52 organizations in 32 countries, support the development of these local institutions in emerging economies, and promote community philanthropy as an approach to development among funders and other development aid audiences. During this grant period, the grantee will promote networks and connections that advance the work of community foundations and other community philanthropy organizations and increase their effectiveness, strengthen relationships between the community foundation field and other parts of the development and philanthropic sectors, and support their capacity development to advance the field.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will renew general purpose support to Focus: HOPE, an anti-poverty and civil rights organization serving low-income residents of Detroit’s Oakman Boulevard neighborhood. Cofounded in 1968 by Father William Cunningham and Eleanor Josaitis, the grantee’s mission is to provide intelligent and practical solutions to overcome racism, poverty, and injustice. Mott funding will help support the grantee’s continued transition to a new business model as well as its core lines of work: early learning, youth development, workforce development, food justice, and community empowerment.

title: Cities Building Bridges to Postsecondary Success
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This renewal grant will enable the National League of Cities Institute to continue its efforts to increase the number of children’s savings account programs in the U.S. and to strengthen children’s savings account programs by creating stronger financial pathways to and through college. During this grant period, the grantee will continue to build and nurture the Southeast network to grow new children’s savings account initiatives in the region. Additionally, during this grant period, the grantee will amplify children’s savings accounts as part of the Foundation’s overall communications strategy, by working with national partners to support cities and regional consortiums to strengthen their existing programs. Established in 1958 and located in Washington, D.C., the National League of Cities Institute is a research, education, and training affiliate of the National League of Cities.

title: 21st Century Community Learning Centers Meeting
description: The grant will support the National AfterSchool Association annual convention on March 18-21, 2018. The purpose of this convention is to provide afterschool educators, including the 21st Century Community Learning Centers coordinators, with technical assistance and strategies to continue to enhance the quality of school-community afterschool programs.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purpose support to the Harlem Children’s Zone in its mission to end generational poverty in Central Harlem. With much acclaim, the grantee model reaches over 13,000 children, guiding them through academic excellence and successful transitions to college and future careers, ultimately making life beyond poverty attainable. Renewal support for the next two years will focus on deepening impact in areas that require intentional and concentrated assistance in alignment with the grantee’s strategic priorities, including: 1) an integrated college and career readiness approach for students served; 2) increased engagement with Harlem’s St. Nicholas community; 3) expanded wellness and mental health promotions for staff, students and families; and 4) succession planning to cultivate the next generation of Harlem Children’s Zone leaders.

title: Renewable Roraima: Studies for Isolated Community Electrification
description: The Instituto de Clima e Sociedade is a Brazilian philanthropic and regranting organization that promotes prosperity, justice, and low-carbon development in Brazil. Currently, the Brazilian Amazon state of Roraima is experiencing an energy crisis, with severe blackouts, and is almost entirely dependent on diesel fuel to meet the electrical needs of the state’s more than 500,000 people. The grantee will work with Brazilian partners and federal and state energy planners to develop a series of technical reports needed to develop a 100 percent renewable energy delivery model using solar, wind, and biomass for the Amazon state of Roraima.

title: Energy Distributed to Isolated Communities
description: Instituto Socioambiental supports efforts to promote distributed renewable energy access solutions for isolated Amazon communities in Brazil and to overcome barriers to the expansion of clean energy in isolated communities. This grant increase will promote the participation of indigenous peoples and local communities in the Brazilian Amazon state of Roraima in a series of convenings to build a state-wide renewable electricity plan, using solar photovoltaic, wind, and biomass in this remote region.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides renewal support to the Council on Foundations, a national membership organization founded in 1949 that currently represents over 750 private foundations, community foundations, and corporate funders. The council’s mission is to provide the opportunity, leadership, and tools needed by philanthropic organizations to expand, enhance, and sustain their ability to advance the common good. It does this by: 1) strengthening the existing bonds between funders who have a lot in common, while simultaneously building bridges between those whose differences provide fertile ground for learning and growth; 2) representing its diverse and varied membership to the public and to policymakers on Capitol Hill and in the Executive Branch; 3) listening to and having conversations with the philanthropic sector’s supporters and critics whose insights can help make us stronger; 4) offering trainings and professional development programs that build and cultivate an engaged network of philanthropic leaders; 5) helping grantmakers navigate the regulatory environment of giving in the United States and around the world; and 6) supporting an ecosystem where giving can thrive globally.

title: YouthBank Development in Turkey
geographic_focus: Turkey, Western Europe, Eastern Europe, Russia, World
description: The project goals are to encourage youth engagement in community development and stimulate local philanthropy in Turkey. The Community Volunteers Foundation supports the further development of YouthBank—a model for youth-led, community-based grantmaking—in Turkey. This grant increase will support the grantee to organize an international conference of YouthBank practitioners from Turkey, the Black Sea region, and Central/Eastern Europe. The conference will further enhance the skills and capacities of Turkish YouthBank practitioners by networking them with their peers in the wider region and building a support network that will last beyond the project period.

title: Advancing Entrepreneurship Education
description: This grant will support the Young Entrepreneur Institute at the University School located in Hunting Valley, Ohio. Founded in 2005, the institute partners with organizations throughout Northeast Ohio to provide every young person with access to entrepreneurial education and experiences. One goal of this project is to increase opportunities for youth to understand and experience entrepreneurship by infusing entrepreneurship into the Mott Foundation’s 50-state afterschool network. The second goal is to increase engagement of regional ecosystems in youth entrepreneurship within under-served and under-resourced communities.

title: General Purposes
description: The Eastern Cape NGO Coalition was established in 1995 to support the work of development organizations in the Eastern Cape province in South Africa. Its membership includes faith-based, community-based, and nonprofit organizations that work to build a vibrant civil society sector in the province. Past support enabled the grantee to bring together civil society organizations to discuss issues that impact their work, such as changes to legislation, poor service delivery to communities, and limited government funding for social services. The grantee also provided training to government officials and civil society practitioners on the asset-based community development approach and institutional strengthening modules. This grant will support the coalition to continue leading discussions and debates on issues that impact its members and the communities they serve. The grantee will also create spaces for dialogue between government, businesses, and civil society organizations to encourage partnerships.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide funds to the Center for Michigan to further expand its founding principles of public engagement, in-depth journalism, and public-driven policy work. The grantee has established itself as an independent and bipartisan source of information and education for the public on important policy issues, providing a link between citizens and the political system, engaging citizens in conversation, and ultimately having an impact on public policy.

title: Community Foundations and Clean Energy in Michigan
description: This grant increase will strengthen the community leadership capacities of community foundations in Michigan that wish to support a transition to clean energy in their locales. During 2017, the Council of Michigan Foundations, along with community leadership and clean energy experts, led a group of community foundations through a series of educational activities to help them understand and advance clean energy transition in their communities. Through that work, four community foundations submitted grant requests to the Mott Foundation. Over the next 20 months, the grantee will provide consulting support, technical assistance, and convening opportunities as the four community foundations implement their projects. They will also document and disseminate results of their work broadly to the community foundation field. The Council of Michigan Foundations is a statewide association of more than 330 grantmakers that provide its members with educational services, networking opportunities, and advocacy with policymakers.

title: Downtown Hotel
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: The Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation is seeking to renovate the former Genesee County Savings Bank building into a downtown Flint hotel. The full vision is a transformed city block that, in addition to the hotel, has a park space, restaurant, and banquet center. This project is essential for the continued resurgence of downtown Flint. Upon completion, the hotel will provide business and leisure travelers with an improved hospitality option.

title: Global Civil Society Information System
description: Over the past several years, the Center for Civil Society Studies at Johns Hopkins University has worked with the United Nations Statistics Division on revisions and expansions to the United Nations Handbook on Nonprofit Institutions in the System of National Accounts—its guidance to countries on gathering statistics about nonprofit institutions. The goal of this project is to enhance the quality, reliability, and accessibility of national-level data on nonprofit organizations and volunteering around the world. With the official release of the new handbook in May 2018, the grantee will undertake dissemination efforts to encourage implementation of the resulting broadened civil society sector statistical procedures into the statistical systems of countries around the world. This grant increase will also support the grantee’s staff working with Ukrainian civil society and government agency leaders to implement the handbook’s guidance in Ukraine.

title: Building Broader Communities in the Americas
description: The Inter-American Foundation, an independent United States government agency created by Congress in 1969 to channel development assistance directly to the organized poor in Latin America and the Caribbean. The project goal of Building Broader Communities in the Americas is to foster partnerships between community foundations in Latin America and the Caribbean and their counterparts in the United States and Canada, using interested stakeholders, such as immigrant groups, as channels of interconnectivity. This grant increase will provide resources for an additional community mapping exercise and a peer learning event on community mapping, a forum in the fall to discuss key topics and decide upon subsequent peer learning events, the selection of a topic for further research on transnationalism and community philanthropy, the formulation of a strengthened organizational structure for the Building Broader Communities in the Americas initiative, and the development of online and printed communications products.

title: Governor's Service Awards Fund
description: This grant will enable the Capital Region Community Foundation to support the work of the Michigan Community Service Commission, the state’s lead agency on service and volunteerism. Specifically, this grant will support the Michigan Community Service Commission to host the Governor’s Service Awards to assist in the continued growth and celebration of service and volunteerism in the state.

title: Engaging Youth in Service
description: This grant will support Youth Service America to engage young people throughout the United States in quality youth-led service projects. The grantee will focus efforts on bolstering youth engagement in Flint and Genesee County and across the United States by working with schools, afterschool programs, and nonprofit organizations.

title: Harold Alfond College Challenge Program Evaluation
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant will enable the Alfond Scholarship Foundation to continue with the second phase of the Harold Alfond College Challenge Program evaluation project. During the second phase of the project, the Alfond Foundation will use the research findings from the first phase to inform their program innovations and share findings with other children’s savings account programs and practitioners in efforts to build the field. Created in 2008 as a pilot program in Portland, Maine, the Alfond Scholarship automatically awards a $500 grant to every child born in Maine as an incentive to catalyze educational savings and to help more children aspire to attend college. With the replicability of the program and the extensive evaluation accomplished in the first phase of the program, the results have implications that will not only impact Maine, but children’s savings account programs across the country.

title: Kindergarten to College Program
grantee: City and County of San Francisco
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: San Francisco’s Kindergarten to College program is recognized as an exemplary model for children’s savings account programs in the country. Since its inception in 2011 as a two-year pilot program, Kindergarten to College has seen much success and today enters every kindergarten student in San Francisco public schools into an automatic savings account with a starting deposit of $50 and prospects of earning financial incentives. For the last two years, the project has made significant progress in strengthening policies and procedures, embedding itself within the larger spectrum of city services, improved its universalism approach and enhanced outreach, marketing, research, and strategic communications. With this grant, the City and County of San Francisco will continue strengthening its model with the following goals: 1) strengthen operations to manage greater scale complexity and innovation; 2) strengthen outreach to schools, communities, and families of students in elementary schools, while also extending reach to middle and high school students; and 3) continue to advance the cradle to career model to help provide opportunities for young people to achieve college or another post-secondary certificate on the pathway to adult success.

title: Children's Savings Accounts Awareness & Engagement Project
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant will enable Big Duck to support the Mott Foundation’s children’s savings accounts efforts. Specifically, the grantee will develop new messages and outreach materials designed to increase parent and student engagement in children’s savings accounts programs. The grantee will work with current Mott grantees, including the City and County of San Francisco and the Community Foundation of Wabash County, to develop and test outreach messages and materials. The final products will be shared with children’s savings accounts programs around the country. Since 1994, Big Duck has provided branding, campaign, and fundraising support for nonprofits and other organizations.

title: Genesee Youth Entrepreneurship Network
description: The Genesee Intermediate School District provides educational leadership that impacts instruction, learning, student achievement, productivity, and efficiency. The organization serves nearly 70,000 students and 8,500 educators across the county. This grant will provide the grantee with funding to launch the Genesee Youth Entrepreneurship Network pilot. The primary objectives are to expand the number of entrepreneurship programs for youth and increase the number of students who participate in entrepreneurship programs and experiences. The countywide project will help motivate all 21 high schools to engage students in grades 9 to 12 in entrepreneurship.

title: Recruiting and Retaining Diverse Educators
description: This grant will enable Education Trust, Inc. to research the potential of afterschool, summer bridge, and community school programs as a venue for recruiting, developing, and retaining diverse educators. During the grant period, the grantee will scan the field to identify relevant program models; document promising strategies and practices; disseminate learning and lessons to networks of youth educators; and develop resources to support schools, and communities who wish to adopt best practices or replicate relevant program models.

title: Ibero-American Network of Community Foundations
geographic_focus: Central America, Mexico, South America, Portugal, Spain
description: This grant provides support to Instituto Comunitario Grande Florianopolis to coordinate the activities of the Ibero-American Network of Community Foundations, an informal network initiated in 2013 with the aim to strengthen community philanthropy organizations in Spain, Portugal, and Latin America. Over the next two years, the network will strengthen the capacity of its members, expand its membership, promote the achievement of community foundations in the Ibero-American region, and strengthen its financial sustainability. The network is supported by the grantee, Brazil’s largest and most prominent foundation. During the past grant period, the grantee strengthened the governance structure of the network, increased the capacity of the network members by organizing over 25 webinars and online discussions, and published three reports on the social impact of its members.

title: Great Lakes Issues Media Coverage
description: Journalists and news organizations have a responsibility at every level to deliver consistent and well-informed coverage of environmental issues. The Society of Environmental Journalists helps reporters, editors, and producers deepen their knowledge and generate updated, forward-looking news reports on complex issues. With partial Mott support, the grantee will hold its 2018 annual conference in Flint, Michigan, hosted by the University of Michigan-Flint. The conference will offer more than three dozen sessions and nine full-day tours over five days, covering a range of issues including drinking water and freshwater conservation issues. The project will also include an intensive, three-day tour for a smaller group of journalists to Michigan’s Upper Peninsula.

title: General Purposes
description: The Africa Philanthropy Network is a continent-wide network of grantmaking and other philanthropic organizations working in Africa. The grantee was established in 2009 to promote learning and networking among philanthropy actors in the continent. Past support enabled the grantee to advance philanthropy in Africa by: 1) facilitating learning among its members through various platforms and events; 2) bringing the voice of African philanthropy to the broader philanthropy sector by connecting the network to the global philanthropy ecosystem; and 3) supporting efforts to build knowledge on philanthropy in Africa. This grant will enable the grantee to continue supporting the development of philanthropy in Africa by connecting organizations, hosting learning events for members, profiling philanthropy in Africa and generating knowledge on the sector. In addition, the Africa Philanthropy Network will strengthen its institutional capacity and increase its membership.

title: Program on Philanthropy and Social Innovation
description: The Aspen Institute’s Program on Philanthropy and Social Innovation seeks to inform and maximize the impact of philanthropists, social investors, and those they support so that each can contribute to the good society at home and abroad. The project’s primary activity is a yearly meeting of the Aspen Philanthropy Group—a group of foundation chief executives and selected strategic advisors. The project also organizes problem-solving working groups and roundtable discussions on critical topics to philanthropists and offers leadership development programming. Aspen Institute is a leading U.S. think tank, with an international network of partners that fosters values-based leadership and provides a neutral and balanced venue for discussing and acting on critical issues.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Albania, Croatia, Serbia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Kosovo, Montenegro
description: The project goal is to strengthen the field of philanthropy in the Western Balkans. The Catalyst Foundation works regionally to promote the growth and improved transparency of the individual and corporate philanthropic culture in Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Kosovo, Macedonia, Montenegro, and Serbia. During 2020–2021, the grantee will; 1) gather and disseminate data on giving trends in the Western Balkans, 2) increase the quantity and quality of giving by developing and introducing tools and approaches for donors and nonprofits, and 3) strengthen philanthropy networks in the Western Balkans. During 2018–2019, the grantee gathered and analyzed data on giving and published annual reports on philanthropy at national levels in the Western Balkans. In addition to print and online dissemination of its findings, the grantee made 67 public presentations about this data across the Western Balkans. The Catalyst Foundation was registered in 2013 in Serbia and is based in Belgrade.

title: Great Lakes Water Resources Project
geographic_focus: Indiana, Pennsylvania, Michigan, Illinois, Wisconsin, Ontario, New York, Minnesota, Ohio
description: The Great Lakes Environmental Law Center was established in 2008 as a not-for-profit environmental organization with a mission to protect the Great Lakes ecosystem. With prior Mott support, the grantee provided legal and policy support to assist with implementation of the Clean Water Act and the Safe Drinking Water Act at the state level; implementation of the Great Lakes-St. Lawrence River Basin Water Resources Compact; and protection of Great Lakes water quality through specific requests from partners. With renewed support, the grantee will continue supporting citizen groups to ensure safe and affordable drinking water, protect the Great Lakes from polluted stormwater, protect Lake Erie against harmful algal blooms, and protect streams and wetlands.

title: Integration Investments and Indigenous Peoples in South America
description: Founded in 1978, the Indian Law Resource Center is a nonprofit organization dedicated to protecting and promoting the rights of indigenous peoples in North, Central and South America. During the last grant period, the grantee began advancing a strengthened indigenous people safeguard policy at international financial institutions and building a dialogue between Amazon indigenous networks and public financial institutions. During the next grant period, the grantee will focus on strengthening the indigenous peoples’ safeguard at regional and national development banks in the Americas and providing legal analysis to help indigenous people in Roraima, Brazil, develop industrial wind power potential in their territory.

title: Fight Crime: Invest in Kids Report
description: This grant will support the Council for a Strong America to produce a comprehensive report on the positive impact that afterschool programs can have on reducing juvenile crime and keeping young people engaged in school and in their communities. Specifically, the grantee will: (1) compile data regarding juvenile crime from 3 p.m. to 6 p.m.; (2) produce the Fight Crime: Invest in Kids report; and (3) support the development of new afterschool champions.

title: General Purposes
