description: This grant provides general support to Candid, an organization that collects, analyzes and publishes information on philanthropic and nonprofit entities. The grantee currently houses databases with 29,000 research reports and data on 2.8 million nonprofits and 235,000 foundations. The grantee provides training to nonprofits and foundations while producing and disseminating its own research. Their strategic priorities are to: 1) connect nonprofits to the resources needed to thrive; 2) empower donors with knowledge tools to be more strategic; 3) build the global data platform for philanthropy; 4) communicate philanthropy’s contribution to making a better world; 5) encourage greater foundation transparency; and 6) ensure that technology provides a strong foundation for the center’s work. Candid was founded in 2019, when Foundation Center and GuideStar merged into one entity, consolidating much of the nonprofit and philanthropic sector’s data.

title: Michigan Lead and Copper Rule
description: The University of Michigan Water Center will provide education materials for municipal leaders, community groups and other engaged citizens, and technical assistance to the Michigan Department of Environmental Quality to support development and implementation of the revised Michigan Lead and Copper Rule. Prior Mott support was used to lead a team of collaborators and advisers to gain a better understanding of the major issues, barriers, and challenges facing long-term water infrastructure reinvestment in older industrial communities across Michigan. Governor Snyder’s Administration has proposed a new Lead and Copper Rule to replace the badly out-of-date federal rule, and this could impose costs and challenges for Michigan cities. This funding will enable experts from the University of Michigan, in collaboration with one of the nation’s foremost experts on lead in drinking water, to help municipalities and concerned citizens understand the new rule and formulate options to assist in its implementation. The team will also provide technical assistance to the Drinking Water Division of the Michigan Department of Environmental Quality to support implementation of the rule, once it is finalized.

title: Neighborhood Strategy Coordinator
description: This grant will support the Genesee County Land Bank Authority in coordinating a neighborhood enhancement strategy surrounding Durant-Tuuri-Mott Elementary School. These coordination efforts will include identifying the status of all neighborhood parcels, connecting with existing resources and partners, and identifying gaps or needs in the neighborhood. Close alignment with nonprofits, governmental agencies, institutions, neighborhood groups, foundations, and individuals is necessary to leverage revitalization resources and coordinate neighborhood improvement efforts.

title: Environmental Defenders Fund
description: The Environmental Defenders Fund operated by RSF Social Finance is a new program developed by funding institutions in 2017 to pool resources to support civil society and environmental and human rights advocates working at the community level. The goal is to implement a four-pronged strategy to protect, prevent, reveal, and redress increasing violence in the field. This grant would provide resources to enable the grantee to work with partners in South America, with a focus in Brazil.

title: Tools for Defending Environmental Defenders
geographic_focus: Peru, Ecuador, Colombia, South America, Bolivia
description: Founded in 1992, Land is Life is a nongovernmental organization that works with a trusted network of indigenous leaders, communities, and organizations to address threats to indigenous lands and forests and support solutions and opportunities for environmental protection and sustainable development while upholding indigenous peoples’ right to self-determination. This grant will support the grantee to work with its network of indigenous leaders in the Amazon to diagnose threats and develop tools to protect and prevent violence against environmental human rights defenders.

title: Detection and Protection for Environmental Defenders
description: The Franciscan Solidarity Service is a Catholic association in Brazil that promotes a vision of social action based on social, human, and environmental rights and Franciscan Christian principles, aimed at the construction of social and environmental justice. Over the proposed project period, the grantee’s professionals will work in the Brazilian Amazon to map threats to communities and environmental human rights defenders and promote strategies to improve safety and solidarity of communities and environmental human rights defenders.

title: School Finance Research Project
description: This grant will support a statewide comprehensive public education campaign about the need for school finance reform as recommended in the adequacy report completed by the Oakland Schools Education Foundation. The campaign will develop and implement strategies to better inform Michigan policymakers, parents, business, and community leaders of the differentiated needs of learners. It will work to help stakeholders recognize that failing to adequately meet the needs of different learners puts them at risk of permanent disadvantage compared to their more fortunate peers.

title: Flint Cultural Center Academy Implementation
description: This grant to the Flint Cultural Center Corporation will support the implementation of the Flint Cultural Center Academy, a charter school operated in partnership with the campus institutions. The Flint Cultural Center Academy will offer a robust curriculum that leverages the educational and programmatic assets of the Flint Institute of Arts, Flint Institute of Music, Flint Public Library, Sloan*Longway, and The Whiting. During the first year of operation the Flint Cultural Center Academy will serve students in kindergarten through fifth grade.

title: Great Lakes Water Resources Project
description: The Great Lakes Environmental Law Center is the only nonprofit environmental law organization headquartered in Michigan that provides support to community members facing challenges to provide clean, safe, affordable, and healthy water resources to people in Michigan. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has provided support to help citizens understand the strengths and weaknesses of legal approaches to address water challenges, and has then designed customized approaches to addressing those issues through litigation, policy change, or a combination of these and other tools. The grantee has helped groups address issues including drinking water quality and water affordability, as well as wetland, stream, and groundwater protection. With this grant renewal, the Great Lakes Environmental Law Center will continue its services to address these ongoing issues and will add the growing concern of contamination from PFAS chemicals to its work.

title: Global Philanthropy Environment Index
description: The program goal is to foster the development of a conducive environment for philanthropy across countries by providing rigorous, comparative data and by raising awareness and understanding of philanthropy, especially in developing countries. In 2016, Indiana University’s Lilly Family School of Philanthropy took responsibility for publishing the Index of Philanthropic Freedom, which was first published by the Hudson Institute in 2015. The most recent version of the index was published in April 2018. The grantee has since been promoting, presenting, and educating on the research. The grantee has also prepared for the next round of research to begin in 2020 with the intent to publish in 2021. Following the publication, the grantee will create online and printed educational materials and organize events in the United States and globally to share results and generate debate. The Lilly Family School of Philanthropy at Indiana University was founded in 2012. Its mission is to increase the understanding of philanthropy and improve its practice worldwide through critical inquiry, interdisciplinary research, teaching, training, and civic engagement.

title: Southeastern Water Supply Security and Sustainability
geographic_focus: Georgia, Alabama, Tennessee, South Carolina, North Carolina
description: With this grant increase, River Network will organize an informational session for the 2018 annual meeting of the Environmental Grantmakers Association to be held in Asheville, North Carolina. The session will focus on natural river flows and water supply issues in the southeastern U.S. and will include representatives from partner organizations in Georgia and Alabama.

title: Funders' Forum on Sustainable Cities
description: The Funders’ Forum on Sustainable Cities is an international, collaborative, foundation-led network committed to increasing philanthropy’s role and effectiveness in advancing sustainable and inclusive growth in cities, tackling urban poverty, promoting equitable development and opportunities, and strengthening local governance and citizen participation in local decision making. Emerging from the Global Philanthropy Leadership Initiative, and with a secretariat in the European Foundation Centre, the forum will use this grant toward a range of activities in 2018. These will include speaker sessions and convenings examining opportunities for philanthropic engagement in urban agendas and, specifically, avenues for cooperation between local authorities and philanthropic institutions in addressing urban sustainability challenges. Key events will include the World Urban Forum in Kuala Lumpur, the European Foundation Centre Annual General Assembly in Brussels, and the forum’s own annual conference to be held in Flint.

title: Michigan Nonprofits Count Campaign
description: The Michigan Nonprofit Association is a statewide membership association dedicated to serving the nonprofit sector through advocacy, capacity-building, technology services, civic engagement, and training. The Michigan Nonprofits Count Campaign is a program of the grantee, and the goal of the campaign is to mobilize, educate, and engage with communities about the 2020 Census to ensure everyone in Michigan is counted. Major activities will include forming a statewide Nonprofit Complete Count Committee, implementing a statewide communications strategy, developing tools and conducting trainings, collaborating with foundations, providing mini-grants to nonprofits, and coordinating with government,

title: Centre for Community Schools
description: The Nelson Mandela Metropolitan University was established in 2005 as a result of a merger between the Port Elizabeth Technikon and the University of Port Elizabeth in South Africa. The Centre for the Community Schools is an entity of the University that aims to promote, strengthen, and support the work of community schools in the Eastern Cape. To support the work of community schools in the province, the grantee assisted with the establishment of the Manyano Network of Community Schools—a community of practice made up of a number of schools based in communities across Port Elizabeth. This grant increase will enable the Centre for Community Schools to fully embed the community school concept in schools and support site coordinators as they complete their outreach work.

title: General Purposes
description: The goal of this project is to enhance the capacity and knowledge of philanthropic networks. In 2018-2019, the United Philanthropy Forum continued to expand its network, engaged on federal tax reform legislation and its impact on the charitable sector, strengthened partnerships and collaboration with other infrastructure organizations, advanced racial equity and inclusion within philanthropy, and improved its financial sustainability. In 2020-2021, the grantee will continue to lead a vibrant network; maximize the individual and collective capacity and impact of its members; provide learning, knowledge, and resources to its members; and strengthen its own capacity and sustainability. Formed in 1998 as the Forum of Regional Associations of Grantmakers, the United Philanthropy Forum is a national network of associations of grantmakers. Its current members are 80 philanthropy-serving organizations across the U.S. that represent more than 7,000 foundations and other philanthropic organizations.

title: Engaging Afterschool Programs in Geography, Exploration and Science
description: This project will support a three-year partnership between the National Geographic Society and the Mott Foundation focused on developing content and curriculum that will inspire and engage young people in afterschool programs to embrace geography, exploration, and science. The Mott Foundation 50-state network will be leveraged to fully implement this partnership through disseminating new curriculum and engaging afterschool educators. This grant will focus on development and implementation of the following: (1) afterschool educator curriculum assets; (2) educator training and certification; (3) educator community; and (4) robust and engaging student learning experiences. This project will also include evaluation and strategic communications components, as well as a digital dissemination strategy in coordination with the Mott Afterschool App that is currently under development. Along with Jazz at Lincoln Center, this project is part of an effort to add name brand, thematic partnerships to the afterschool grantmaking portfolio.

title: Innovations in International Philanthropy Symposium
description: Founded in 1915, The Boston Foundation is one of the nation’s oldest and largest community foundations. The inaugural “Innovations in International Philanthropy” symposium will be held in Boston in September 2018. The event will be co-hosted by The Philanthropic Initiative – a philanthropy advisory comprised of the grantee and New England International Donors – a community of more than 100 New England-based global philanthropists. The project goal is to support the sharing of knowledge and experience among international oriented philanthropists in New England. It will bring together an estimated 200 philanthropists, investors, funders, and companies to connect, inspire and learn from each other. At the symposium, a new publication, “Innovative Trends in International Philanthropy: A Call for Collaboration” will be released.

title: Impacts of Investments of the Brazilian National Development Bank on Regional Sustainability
description: The Instituto Socioambiental is a Brazilian nonprofit organization focused on integrated solutions to environmental and social challenges in the Amazon region. Over the previous grant period, the grantee worked with local partners to ensure compliance with social and environmental standards by the financiers and developers of the Belo Monte hydroelectric project on the Xingu River. Scientific monitoring by the grantee and local indigenous partners was officially accepted to guide the development of a water management system to mitigate impacts of the deviation of up to 80 percent of the Xingu River flows, and resettlement of forcibly evicted communities began. Over the next grant period, Instituto Socioambiental will consolidate its work monitoring and ensuring compliance with safeguards and leverage its achievements with project financiers, such as the Brazilian Development Bank and Inter-American Development Bank.

title: Strengthening the CEELI Institute’s Rule of Law Programming
description: The project goal is to strengthen the important role that the Central and Eastern European Law Initiative (CEELI) Institute plays in advancing the rule of law in Central and Eastern Europe and globally. To this end, the Friends of the CEELI Institute will support judges and lawyers through conferences, networking, and training opportunities. The CEELI Institute is an independent, Czech nonprofit, established in 2000. It is the permanent legacy of the Central and East European Law Initiative, a pro bono public service project started by the American Bar Association in 1990. A fully independent organization, the institute works in Central and Eastern Europe and globally to: 1) create independent, transparent, and effective judiciaries; 2) strengthen democratic institutions; 3) foster efforts to combat corruption; and 4) and promote human rights. The Friends of the CEELI Institute is a U.S. 501(c)(3) nonprofit based in Washington, D.C., with the mission of providing support and assistance to the CEELI Institute.

title: Great Lakes Program
description: River Alliance of Wisconsin is a statewide organization that works to improve the health of the Great Lakes Ecosystem. In the Great Lakes Program project, the grantee is working with state, local, and regional partners to advance water policy reform and support local groups working on freshwater projects. The purpose of the increase is to enable the group to conduct research and develop effective communications approaches to educate and mobilize citizens around invasive species issues.

title: General Purposes
description: Founded in 1970 as the Lake Michigan Federation, the Alliance for the Great Lakes seeks to conserve and restore the Great Lakes freshwater ecosystem through policy reform, public education, and local conservation projects. This grant increase is available for the general purpose of the organization, to include conducting polling in the Great Lakes states to evaluate public attitudes toward the Great Lakes, especially attitudes towards invasive species, and to create public education materials and work with partners to communicate information based on polling and research findings.

title: Engaging Afterschool Programs in Geography, Exploration and Science
description: This grant will support the National Geographic Society on their continuation of reaching the afterschool field through innovative and interactive field learning and online experiences for youth and afterschool educators. The grantee will focus on building capacity for long-term success to advance afterschool and summer learning in the afterschool field. The specific initiatives will include: 1) build leadership and capacity in the sciences by expanding professional development opportunities for afterschool educators; 2) increase access to enriching and unique high-quality learning experiences for youth in the afterschool setting; and 3) expand engagement and participation by creating a more robust marketing strategy through partnerships and network supports.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purpose support to the Environmental Grantmakers Association which offers venues for environmental grantmakers to share knowledge and foster debate on critical environmental issues. In particular, the grantee’s annual retreat is an important forum that allows grantmakers to network and discuss common goals.

title: Technical Support for Clean Energy in the Peruvian Amazon
description: Access to modern electricity services has not reached 40 percent of rural Peruvian people, many of whom live in the Peruvian Amazon. The Pontifical Catholic University of Peru’s Institute of Science of Nature, Territory, and Renewable Energies is an institute for research, academic training, and promotion of strategies for ecological, biodiversity, territorial conservation, and renewable energy expertise. Over the course of this project, the grantee will work with isolated communities in the Peruvian Amazon state of Loreto to diagnose energy needs; propose renewable energy solutions; and implement a pilot renewable energy project that can be replicated for isolated Amazon communities.

title: City Leaders Engaged in Afterschool Reform
description: This grant will support the National League of Cities Institute to engage city officials in developing high-quality afterschool and summer learning initiatives at the federal, state and local levels. Specifically, this project will: 1) support statewide afterschool networks in their efforts to engage municipal leaders; 2) expand the grantee’s communications initiatives to connect afterschool programs with the top priorities in cities; and 3) continue to raise awareness among municipal leaders in building high-quality afterschool and summer learning systems.

title: General Purposes
description: The Social Change Assistance Trust was established in 1984 to facilitate funding to rural community-based organizations that work to improve the quality of life in their communities. It makes grants to organizations that address inequality, human rights, social justice, local economic development, and HIV/AIDS. Past support enabled the grantee to provide funding and support to community advice offices based in the Northern Cape, Western Cape, Free State, and the Eastern Cape. This grant increase will assist the grantee to partner with the National Alliance for the Development of Community Advice Offices to offer training to over 125 paralegals working in community advice offices across South Africa.

title: Environmental Defenders Collaborative
description: The Environmental Defenders Collaborative, operated by the Global Greengrants Fund, is a program developed by funding institutions in 2017 to pool resources to support civil society and environmental and human rights advocates working at the community level. During the first grant period, an important convening of Supreme Court judges and civil society was founded on protecting environmental defenders in Brazil. This renewal will support the implementation of the four-pronged strategy to protect, prevent, reveal, and redress increasing violence in South America, with a focus in Brazil.

title: Environmental Defenders Collaborative
description: The Environmental Defenders Collaborative, operated by the Global Greengrants Fund, is a program developed by funding institutions in 2017 to pool resources to support civil society and environmental and human rights advocates working at the community level. With prior Mott support, the grantee leveraged Mott funding to increase by three-fold the small grants provided to protect and support environmental defenders in South America. With renewed support, the grantee will provide continued implementation of the strategy to protect defenders in South America, with a focus in Brazil.

title: Detection and Protection for Environmental Defenders
description: The Franciscan Solidarity Service is a Catholic association in Brazil that promotes a vision of social action based on social, human, and environmental rights and Franciscan Christian principles. Over the past grant period, the grantee researched and met with local Amazon communities and public agencies to study reported increases and causes of threats and violence against environmental and human rights defenders. The Franciscan Solidarity Service will, over the next grant period, develop security strategies and tools with selected Amazon communities impacted by large-scale development pressure in the forest.

title: Monitoring Infrastructure Investments in Argentina
location: Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires, Argentina
description: The Fundacion Ambiente y Recursos Naturales is an Argentina-based nongovernmental organization that has promoted sustainable finance and development through policy, law and civic engagement for 35 years. Over the previous grant period, the grantee monitored international, regional, and Chinese energy development finance and made important contributions to strengthening social and environmental guidelines for such finance overall and specifically in Chinese overseas investment. Over this grant period, the grantee and partners will continue to monitor energy development finance by international and national development finance institutions. The aim is to strengthen these institutions’ governance and transparency, and mitigate the social and environmental impacts of their investments.

title: Tools for Defending Environmental Defenders
geographic_focus: Bolivia, Peru, Ecuador, Colombia, South America
description: Founded in 1992, Land is Life is a nongovernmental organization working with a trusted network of indigenous leaders, communities, and organizations in the greater Amazon and globally. Over the last grant period, the organization developed a study with indigenous partners of the security threats to environmental defenders of indigenous lands and forests from large-scale development pressures. Over the next grant period, the grantee will implement a tool kit of security tools and strategies with three indigenous communities in the Amazon to protect and prevent violence against indigenous environmental defenders.

title: Early Warning System
geographic_focus: Argentina, Peru, Brazil, Ecuador, Bolivia, Colombia
description: This project will support the International Accountability Project to curate its Early Warning System web tool. The system data will be made available to civil society and local community partners to track energy and infrastructure project finance and trends in South America. The grantee is a nonprofit global organization working on community-centered development.

title: China-Latin America Sustainable Investments Initiative
description: The China-Latin America Sustainable Investment Initiative, a project of the Bank Information Center, works with partners in South America to monitor Chinese investment and strengthen voluntary Chinese guidelines for social and environmental standards, using best international practice. Over the previous grant period, the grantee updated its manual on social and environmental standards, trained Latin American agencies and nongovernmental organizations in its use and networked with Chinese partners. This renewal grant will support the grantee to continue monitoring and disseminating Chinese standards and finance of energy and infrastructure in Argentina, Brazil, Ecuador and Peru.

title: Unlocking BNDES Operation Lifecycle
description: Founded in 2008, SITAWI Finance for Good is a Brazil-based nonprofit organization whose mission is to mobilize research and capital for positive environmental and social outcomes.Over the past grant period, the grantee participated in consultations with the Brazilian Development Bank to improve transparency and monitor the implementation of the bank’s social and environmental management system. This grant renewal will support a strategic investigation, analysis and documentation of the Brazilian Development Bank’s policies and investments, as well as develop metrics to judge overall progress.

title: Strengthening BNDES Accountability
description: Conectas is a Brazilian nongovernmental agency, founded in 2001, working on strengthening social and environmental governance and accountability of development finance institutions. Over the past grant period, the grantee helped strengthen transparency and social environmental governance at the Brazilian Development Bank and New Development Bank, and monitored the implementation of the first New Development Bank financed energy project in Brazil. Over the next grant period, the grantee will evaluate the advances and setbacks civil society has made after seven years of focusing on social and environmental governance at major development finance institutions. Conectas will also strengthen its collaboration with impacted communities to improve their access to these institutions.

title: General Purposes
description: Derecho Ambiente y Recursos Naturales is a Peruvian nongovernmental organization focused on sustainable development and conservation of the Peruvian Amazon Basin. Over the last grant period, the grantee implemented its strategic plan and grew its core budget. The grantee also made significant contributions to reforming and implementing the environment and social framework at the World Bank Group and formed a network to engage in the Inter-American Development Bank social and environmental framework review. This grant renewal provides general purpose support to Derecho Ambiente y Recursos Naturales to implement the final two years of its current strategic plan, focusing on strengthening environmental governance and standards, sustainable development and Amazon forest conservation.

title: Monitoring BNDES Sustainability
grantee: Instituto de Energia e Meio Ambiente
description: The Instituto de Energia e Meio Ambiente is a nonprofit Brazilian think tank focused on research, analysis and policy evaluation to contribute to socially and environmentally sustainable energy and transportation development and finance. Over the previous grant period, the grantee monitored thermoelectric power development and finance, and its impacts on climate and freshwater resources. Over this grant period, the grantee will continue its research and data gathering, build a community of practice and engage the Brazilian Development Bank to strengthen social and environmental safeguards for financing planned natural gas-powered thermoelectric expansion.

title: Robert S. Collier Public Policy Endowment Fund
description: The Council of Michigan Foundations is creating the Robert S. Collier Public Policy Endowment Fund, honoring Rob Collier’s 23 years of service at the council, including 18 years as its President and CEO. The fund will be held in perpetuity with the distributions to be used for the express purpose of meeting the grantee’s annual government relations and public policy goals. The grantee is a statewide association of 300 grantmakers that provides its members with educational programs, technical assistance, networking opportunities, advocacy with policymakers and regulators, and collaborative work with leading national and regional philanthropic associations.

title: Adult Career Pathway Program
description: This grant will support Mott Community College’s Adult Career Pathway Program, which will leverage many of the college’s existing educational and training programs to help connect unemployed adults, low-income workers, and youth to employment and a career pathway. The goal is to ensure that area residents can enter and advance into higher-wage occupations in high-growth industries. Work experience and support services are integrated into the model and will enable participants to combine school and work and advance over time. Providing residents with job training and career advancement opportunities will help build Flint’s economic resilience to recover from the water crisis.

title: General Purposes
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant provides general purposes support for the Buckham Fine Arts Project, also known as Buckham Gallery. The grantee was incorporated in 1984 by a group of artists who saw the need for a contemporary gallery in downtown Flint. Over the past 30 years the grantee has held more than 300 exhibitions of visual art; poetry readings; performance art events; and dance, music, and film presentations. Buckham Gallery showcases local, regional, and international artists.

title: General Purposes
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant provides general purpose support for the Buckham Fine Arts Project, also known as Buckham Gallery. The grantee was incorporated in 1984 by a group of artists who saw the need for a contemporary gallery in downtown Flint. Over the past 30 years the grantee has held more than 300 exhibitions of visual art; poetry readings; performance art events; and dance, music, and film presentations. The grantee showcases local, regional, and international artists. Located in a new storefront space on the corner of South Saginaw and Second Streets, Buckham Gallery will offer a variety of Saturday programs throughout 2019.

title: Automation Risk in Flint
description: This grant will support New America in its mission of developing independent, non-partisan analysis and recommendations reflective of rigorous scholarship, and promoting those ideas through broad public discourse. Specifically it will fund development of localized data on automation risk of certain job categories in Flint, in order to empower and prepare local workforce planning efforts.

title: Blight Elimination and Neighborhood Stabilization
description: This grant will provide support to the Genesee County Land Bank Authority to engage in neighborhood revitalization activities around Kettering University, Durant-Tuuri-Mott Elementary School, Chevy Commons, Mott Park, Flint River, and Atwood Stadium. These activities will include demolishing blight elimination, property cleanup, paint, and home improvement. Demolishing properties is an important first step in stabilizing the neighborhood.

title: Launch Flint Pitch Competitions
description: This grant will support the Ferris Wheel Innovation Center to organize and implement business pitch competitions in Flint. The grantee was established to help entrepreneurs in an economically disadvantaged community gain access to supports that advance their ideas. Pitch competitions are a way to provide struggling entrepreneurs with the resources needed to move their business concepts forward. Competition winners will receive financial resources and all participants will receive mentoring from business professionals.

title: Renewable Roraima: Studies for Isolated Community Electrification
description: The Instituto de Clima e Sociedade is a Brazilian philanthropic organization that promotes prosperity, justice, and low-carbon development in Brazil. Over the past project period, the grantee worked with Brazilian partners and energy planners to develop a series of technical reports needed for a 100 percent renewable energy delivery model using solar, wind, and biomass for the Amazon state of Roraima. Over the next project period, the grantee will promote the plan and work with energy regulators to advance policy for indigenous-owned, large-scale wind power development and off-grid renewable energy for isolated communities.

title: Renewable Loreto
description: Derecho Ambiente y Recursos Naturales is a Peruvian nongovernmental organization with offices in Lima and Iquitos, the capital of the Peruvian Amazon Department of Loreto. Over the last two years, the grantee began work to bring renewable energy to isolated communities in the Amazon. With this grant, the grantee will expand the solar energy access work in the Peruvian Amazon. This project will provide dedicated support for expanding solar energy access to communities living in the buffer zones of Amazon protected areas in the Department of Loreto.

title: Infrastructure Improvements to Southwestern High School
description: This grant provides support to Flint Community Schools to make critical cosmetic and infrastructure improvements to Southwestern High School. The interior and exterior elements of the school building have fallen into a state of disrepair as the district has struggled with financial challenges for many years. The improvements will result in an environment that is safer and helps create a school climate that is more conducive to teaching and learning.

title: Clean Water Act Implementation in the Great Lakes Region
geographic_focus: Indiana, Illinois, Ohio, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Michigan
description: The Environmental Law & Policy Center is a leading public interest environmental legal advocacy organization. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has built a record from publicly available information that enforcement of the Clean Water Act—the bedrock law that protects Great Lakes water quality—has fallen markedly in the Midwest. With renewed support, the grantee will continue this research, publicly release the information and pursue strategies to hold the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency accountable. In addition, the grantee will monitor runoff from manure treatment facilities for large-scale farm animal operations in Ohio and Wisconsin and push for necessary pollution reduction measures.

title: Solar Electrician and Entrepreneurship Training
description: Since 1947, Salesian Missions has brought opportunity to millions of poor youth across 130 countries by providing thorough vocational education and technical training. This Salesian Missions network also includes the Don Bosco Vocational Training Centers, which have been providing technical training across Tanzania since 1980. Over the past four years, the Salesian Missions, together with the Don Bosco training centers in Tanzania, have provided 481 disadvantaged youth (23% women) with solar photovoltaic installation technical skills. Of these graduates,182 are now either self-employed or employed by solar companies in Tanzania. As part of this grant renewal, the Salesian Missions and the Don Bosco training centers in Tanzania will train an additional 129 underserved youth in solar photovoltaic installation while ensuring that 70% of those trained are either self-employed or employed by others in Tanzania’s solar sector. The organization will also actively promote the successful recruitment and retention of disadvantaged young women in the program.

title: Michigan Nonprofits Count Campaign
description: The Michigan Nonprofit Association is a statewide membership association dedicated to serving the nonprofit sector through advocacy, capacity building, technology services, civic engagement, and training. The grantee manages the Michigan Nonprofits Count Campaign, which is designed to mobilize, educate, and engage with communities in Michigan about the 2020 Census. The goals are to ensure that everyone in the state is counted. Major activities will include forming a statewide Nonprofit Complete Count Committee, implementing a statewide communications strategy, developing tools and conducting trainings, collaborating with foundations, providing mini-grants to nonprofits, and coordinating with government.

title: Michigan Nonprofits Count Campaign
description: The Michigan Nonprofit Association is a statewide membership association dedicated to serving the nonprofit sector through advocacy, capacity building, technology services, civic engagement and training. The grantee manages the Michigan Nonprofits Count Campaign in partnership with the Council of Michigan Foundations, a membership association of foundations in Michigan. The purpose of the Michigan Nonprofits Count Campaign is to mobilize and engage nonprofits across the state in support of a fair and accurate census count. In addition, the partnership is charged with building the capacity of nonprofits to address future concerns in communities and threats to citizen participation.

title: Help Centers
description: This grant will provide support for Genesee Health System to operate and provide a variety of resources at three community Help Centers in Flint. The Help Centers centralize food including lead-mitigating food and produce, bottled water (when available), filters, and cartridges. Health and human service providers are also available to assist residents on-site at all three locations. The Help Centers, which were previously managed by the Food Bank of Eastern Michigan, will be managed by the grantee, in partnership with several organizations already assisting residents as a result of the Flint water crisis, including area churches, United Way of Genesee County, and the Michigan Department of Health and Human Services. The Food Bank of Eastern Michigan will continue as a core partner for food and nutrition support.

title: Flint Filter Education and Testing Program
description: This grant will provide support to Freshwater Future to pilot a filtered water testing program and increase filter education in the community. The grantee will work with three key partners–Flint Development Center, Flint Neighborhoods United, and Genesee County Hispanic Latino Collaborative–to identify approximately 150 homes and community spaces for the pilot program. Additionally, all partners will work collectively to offer filter education to testing participants and the broader community.

title: Bachelor of Paralegal Studies and Community Based Paralegals
description: The project goal is to ensure that community-based paralegals have access to, and are included in, the Bachelor of Paralegal Studies at the Cape Peninsula University of Technology. To this end, the grantee will undertake research and explore ways to make the Bachelor of Paralegal Studies inclusive and accessible for community-based paralegals. During the first phase of this project, the grantee will conduct a comprehensive survey of community-based paralegals’ existing knowledge and draft a recognition of prior learning instrument. During the second phase of this project, the grantee will workshop the recognition of prior learning instrument with paralegals and provide recommendations on a teaching and learning methodology. The grantee is the first university in South Africa to launch an official Bachelor of Paralegal Studies degree program.

title: Nonprofit Tax Policy Research
description: The project goal is to inform policymakers and nonprofit practitioners of the impact of the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act on the nonprofit sector. Independent Sector will organize an expert convening, conduct research on unrelated business income tax, analyze the potential impact of different legislative proposals, and undertake market research on effective messaging. Throughout this process, the grantee will collaborate with other infrastructure groups and nonprofit coalitions to gather quantitative and qualitative data as it becomes available. In addition to sharing and curating the data they collect with others, the grantee will use its own platform to provide the public, policymakers, and the sector at large with relevant information to help inform ongoing advocacy. Founded in 1980, Independent Sector is a leadership network for nonprofits, foundations, and corporations committed to advancing the common good through research, advocacy, and resource development.

title: Employment Preparation Program
description: This grant will provide support to St. Luke N.E.W. Life Center for the Employment Preparation Program. Serving residents of north Flint, the program works with individuals who are structurally unemployed and need a broad array of wraparound services to adequately prepare them to find and retain employment. The program will continue to expand its outreach to employers for future job placements and establish an alumni network to offer support to participants and graduates. Additionally, the grantee will continue to develop a more robust evaluation and tracking system to measure programmatic outcomes. Providing residents with opportunities for job training and employment will help build Flint’s economic resilience to recover from the water crisis.

title: Transition Assistance Practice Group
description: The project goal is to improve the effectiveness of transition assistance to emerging democracies and postconflict societies, particularly with respect to the development of inclusive and dynamic civil society and civic space. To this end, the Institute for Integrated Transitions, an international nonprofit based in Barcelona, will put together a “transition assistance practice group” made up of experts and practitioners that have worked on political, social, and economic development in different contexts around the world. During the grant period, the practice group will work directly with groups of policymakers and civil society leaders that the grantee has convened through on-the-ground work in Colombia, Venezuela, the Gambia, and/or Zimbabwe. The practice group will support the country-based leadership groups with strategic guidance on matching available transition assistance with locally identified development priorities in their countries. Through direct involvement with the local expert group, the grantee and the practice group will make available know-how, key lessons, and innovative practices from other countries’ transitions, including South Africa and the countries of Central and Eastern Europe.

title: General Purposes
description: The Community Organisation Resource Centre was established in 2002 to support the development of the urban slums in South Africa. The grantee works with movements of people living in slums to enable homeless and landless communities to learn from one another and work together to engage government on the improvement of their living conditions. Past support enabled the grantee to work with community groups to collect data, build strong savings schemes and lead community-planning processes to leverage support and funding from local, provincial and national government. This grant will enable the grantee to continue supporting the Federation of the Urban Poor and the Informal Settlement Network, improve living conditions for the urban poor and connect them to movements of slum dwellers globally. The Community Organisation Resource Centre will continue to support learning exchanges and work with young people to bridge the inter-generational gap.

title: Flint Cultural Center Academy
description: The Flint Cultural Center Foundation will construct a new building to house the Flint Cultural Center Academy. The Academy is scheduled to open in the fall of 2019 with grades Kindergarten through 5th. When fully implemented (2022), the school will serve approximately 650 Kindergarten through 8th grade students primarily from Flint and Genesee County. The vision of the Academy is to demonstrate a unique application of education that challenges and surpasses the existing norms of student achievement and learning growth, while addressing the development of the whole child.

title: Education Trust-Midwest Michigan Policy Efforts
description: With this grant Education Trust will support its Midwest division to do the thoughtful and nonpartisan policy analysis for which it is known. Michigan leaders and a broad set of community stakeholders are grappling with the current condition of education in the state, and actively investigating the policy levers that can help make Michigan a top ten state for education in the nation. The grantee’s Midwest division will conduct research and analysis and participate in advocacy to help inform important policy conversations about education in the state of Michigan.

title: Access to Justice in Africa and the SDGs
description: The Socioeconomic Rights Project of the Dullah Omar Institute for Constitutional Law, Governance and Human Rights at the University of the Western Cape will organize participation of access to justice institutions in sub-Saharan Africa at the United Nations High-level Political Forum in July 2019. The forum meets every year during July to discuss the implementation of the Sustainable Development Goals. During 2019, the implementation of Goal 16 will be discussed at the forum. Goal 16 aims to promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide access to justice for all, and build effective, accountable, and inclusive institutions at all levels.

title: Multi-Agency Grants Initiative: Advice Office Regranting Project
description: Hlanganisa Institute of Development Southern Africa NPC, previously known as Hivos – South Africa, was established in 2006 to seek new and innovative solutions to persistent social challenges. The Multi-Agency Grants Initiative, managed by the grantee, is a collaborative venture between various funders in South Africa. Its purpose is to provide a responsive mechanism for making small grants to community-based organizations, including community advice offices. This grant increase will allow the grantee to provide additional support to community advice offices, promote gender and youth development in community advice offices, build team cohesion among paralegals in the Free State province, and contribute increased resources to evaluate the program.

title: Hawaii Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase will support the University of Hawaii, which coordinates the Hawaii Afterschool Alliance, to assist with travel to the statewide afterschool network meetings. The Hawaii Afterschool Alliance is a network of individuals and organizations that works to develop, support, and promote sustainable and quality summer learning and afterschool programs, resulting in enhanced emotional, physical, social, and academic outcomes for children and families in Hawaii.

title: Alaska Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase will support the Alaska Children’s Trust, which coordinates the Alaska Statewide Afterschool Network, to assist with travel to the statewide afterschool network meetings. The Alaska Statewide Afterschool Network is a network of individuals and organizations that works to support, strengthen, and advocate for quality programs for afterschool for children, youth, and families throughout Alaska.

title: Every Hour Counts
description: This grant will continue to support ExpandED Schools to develop a common measurement framework for afterschool programs to track children and youth across a range of youth outcomes, including academic, as well as social and emotional skills such as creative thinking, teamwork, self-regulation, and work ethic. The grantee will work with afterschool leaders and statewide afterschool networks to: 1) implement common youth outcome measures; 2) build capacity of participating cities and states to measure youth outcomes; 3) inform policy and practice through national dissemination of lessons learned to build understanding among leaders in the education, out-of-school time, and other relevant fields; and 4) assist in the development of student outcome measures related to the Foundation’s thematic partnerships and the Mott Afterschool App.

title: STEM Fellowship
description: This grant to the STEM Next Opportunity Fund will support the Robert Noyce-Ellen Lettvin Fellowship in Informal STEM Learning. The fellowship is a public-private partnership initiative geared toward advancing high-quality informal science education, including in afterschool and summer learning programs. This initiative will include: 1) strengthening collaboration between the U.S. Department of Education and other federal agencies in the area of informal STEM learning; 2) working to advance STEM learning in the 21st Century Community Learning Centers program; and 3) working with leading researchers to identify priorities in informal STEM learning, including identifying new tools, strategies, and programs that improve STEM learning opportunities.

title: Downtown Hotel
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: The Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation will renovate the former Genesee County Savings Bank building into a downtown Flint hotel. The full vision is a transformed city block that, in addition to the hotel, has a park space, restaurant, and banquet center. This project is essential for the continued resurgence of downtown Flint. Upon completion, the hotel will provide business and leisure travelers with an improved hospitality option.

title: Great Lakes Leadership Program
grantee: The Board of Trustees of the University of Illinois
description: The University of Illinois at Chicago’s Freshwater Lab is an initiative on the university campus that endeavors to train a new generation of Great Lakes water leaders; to conduct research on the Great Lakes basin; to communicate findings to the public; and to bring university students, researchers, elected officials, community leaders, and water professionals into productive dialogue. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the Lab has achieved these goals by hosting summits; developing a curriculum and a digital storytelling site called Freshwater Stories; hosting speakers and events; and coordinating courses on humanities and social science approaches to freshwater issues at the university and other Big Ten schools. To continue and extend work in proven areas of strength, the Lab now hopes to grow new leadership by developing an internship program for university students to work on Great Lakes issues, particularly in urban areas along the southern end of Lake Michigan. This planning grant will enable them to explore existing programs, gaps in what currently exists, and the specific needs that can be addressed by an urban university with one of the most diverse student bodies in North America.

title: Freshwater Lab Internship Program
grantee: The Board of Trustees of the University of Illinois
description: The University of Illinois at Chicago serves an urban population in the largest city of the Great Lakes region. The university’s Freshwater Lab works closely with agencies and community-based groups, including Mott Foundation grantees. With prior support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee designed a new internship program. The program will place students from the grantee’s diverse student population with Mott grantees, and other organizations primarily in the greater Chicago area. The internship program will span an academic semester and a summer session, thus giving students classroom training to build leadership and understanding of Great Lakes issues prior to practical training, and networking with professionals.

title: General Purposes
description: The Grand Traverse Regional Land Conservancy, founded in 1991, is a land trust serving a five-county region located in northwest lower Michigan. During the last grant period, the grantee made very significant progress on a multiyear capital campaign, securing funding commitments surpassing $80 million. The funds will be used to protect and maintain natural areas, scenic views and farmland in the service area. Renewed support will allow the grantee to successfully complete the fundraising campaign, even in the current uncertain economic times, and continue the full range of the organization’s work.

title: Informing State Legislatures: Statewide Afterschool Policy
description: This grant will continue to support the National Conference of State Legislatures in its work to educate state legislators about the positive impact of afterschool and to build state capacity to implement high-quality afterschool and summer learning opportunities. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) develop resources on the role afterschool and summer learning can play in state education, including to advance social and emotional learning; 2) engage legislators on the topic of afterschool and summer learning; 3) increase understanding of COVID-19 relief resources; and 4) continue to support the statewide afterschool networks as part of the Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative with an increased focus on effective data sharing practices.

title: General Purposes
description: The Foundation for Human Rights was established in 1996 with support from the European Union to implement a human rights funding program in South Africa. It receives the bulk of its funding from the European Union and is one of the most significant grantmakers in the country supporting the development and strengthening of a culture of human rights. Mott has supported the grantee to strengthen its internal capacity and has contributed to its research programs. This grant increase will provide general purpose support and enable the grantee to make grants to under-served community advice offices across the country.

title: Mapping the Policy Infrastructure of Digital Civil Society
description: The project goal is to investigate how digital public policy impacts civil society and how to strengthen and expand connections between civil society support organizations and digital policy experts. To this end, researchers at Stanford University, led by Dr. Lucy Bernholz, will conduct a series of interviews, review relevant literature and activities, convene interested parties, host a live virtual roundtable, and expand their nonresident fellowship program. The initial focus of this work is on the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and continental Europe. Dr. Bernholz and her team are based at the Digital Civil Society Lab at Stanford University’s Stanford Center on Philanthropy and Civil Society. The lab aims to understand how digital technology has transformed civil society and to shape these transformations to support a thriving and independent civil society in the digital age.

title: Promoting Community-Led Implementation of the Sustainable Development Goals
description: The project goal is to promote community-led implementation of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. To this end, the Brookings Institution will host a series of workshops, roundtable discussions, and public events. These activities will inform and evaluate how place-based leaders set and track goals; mobilize the investments and action to drive progress; and develop and disseminate relevant tools, policies, and networks to maximize impact. The grantee will engage cities, states, foundations, and other stakeholders that are championing the use of the Sustainable Development Goals and provide a neutral venue to coordinate, collaborate, and disseminate tools and findings.

title: STEM Fellowship
description: This grant to the STEM Next Opportunity Fund will support the Robert Noyce-Ellen Lettvin Fellowship in Informal STEM Learning. The fellowship is a public-private partnership initiative geared toward advancing high-quality informal science education, including in afterschool and summer learning programs. This initiative will include: 1) strengthening collaboration between the U.S. Department of Education and other federal agencies in the area of informal STEM learning; 2) working to advance STEM learning in the 21st Century Community Learning Centers program; and 3) working with leading researchers to identify priorities in informal STEM learning, including identifying new tools, strategies, and programs that improve STEM learning opportunities.

title: Engaging Youth Through Service
description: This grant will support America’s Promise Alliance to engage young people throughout the United States in youth-led service projects. Specifically, the grantee will leverage the reach of their partners to mobilize up to 20,000 young people to pursue service in their communities.

title: Oklahoma Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Oklahoma Public School Resource Center, which coordinates the Oklahoma Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue the development of policy, partnerships and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) developing a comprehensive communication and outreach plan; 2) conducting a survey of the afterschool field to determine professional development needs; 3) providing technical assistance to afterschool programs to improve quality; and 4) supporting the promotion and distribution of Mizzen by Mott.

title: Iowa Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Iowa Children’s Museum, which coordinates the Iowa Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue the development of policy, partnerships and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) leveraging partnerships to expand access to more equitable and high-quality afterschool and summer learning programs; 2) establishing afterschool and summer learning initiatives as a key strategy for addressing the lack of child care supports; 3) expanding quality improvement efforts statewide to enhance the access and status of afterschool and summer learning programs; and 4) supporting the promotion and distribution of Mizzen by Mott.

title: Massachusetts Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Massachusetts Afterschool Partnership, which coordinates the Massachusetts Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue the development of policy, partnerships and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) convening a summit to educate city and town leaders on the importance of afterschool; 2) engaging youth to develop more and better summer and afterschool opportunities to deal with the learning and opportunity lost during COVID-19; 3) developing a white paper on the contributions made by afterschool to sustain learning and recovery throughout the pandemic; and 4) supporting the promotion and distribution of Mizzen by Mott.

title: Utah Statewide Afterschool Network
location: Salt Lake City, UT, United States
description: This grant will support the Utah Afterschool Network which coordinates the Utah Statewide Afterschool Network to continue the development of policy, partnerships and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) strengthening the continuous improvement system to enhance afterschool educators performance to deliver high-quality enrichment and learning opportunities; 2) increasing awareness of afterschool and summer learning programs by leveraging state and local resources; 3) implementing a comprehensive communications strategy to create innovative partnerships to enhance and sustain collaboration among youth servicing organizations, education entities and state agencies; and 4) supporting the promotion and distribution of Mizzen by Mott.

title: Alabama Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the University of Alabama which coordinates the Alabama Statewide Afterschool Network to continue the development of policy, partnerships and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) developing a coalition of state and local partners to expand afterschool and summer learning; 2) creating regional hubs across the state to provide professional development and training; 3) developing a directory of afterschool programs in Alabama; and 4) supporting the promotion and distribution of Mizzen by Mott.

title: Ohio Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the PAST Foundation, which coordinates the Ohio Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue the development of policy, partnerships and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) building a diverse coalition of key champions and stakeholders to advocate for equitable opportunities for youth, families and communities; 2) partnering with state agencies to create a strategic plan to support youth through academic recovery and learning enrichment due to impacts of the pandemic; 3) establishing a statewide resource system for youth allies providing out-of-school time opportunities to enhance the quality of programs; and 4) supporting the promotion and distribution of Mizzen by Mott.

title: Southeast Michigan: Welcoming Community for Refugees and Migrants
description: The goal of this project is to develop a collective set of funding and programmatic strategies to support immigrant and refugee communities in southeast Michigan. For the first phase of the project, the Community Foundation for Southeast Michigan commissioned a landscape analysis of organizations, services, and funding for immigrants and refugees in the Oakland, Wayne, Macomb, Washtenaw, and Genesee counties. In the second phase, these results will be shared with a broad segment of southeast Michigan residents beyond only immigrant and refugee groups. Through a community engagement process, the project’s funders, implementers, and other interested stakeholders will learn community members’ reactions to the findings, which will feed into the development of a collaborative grantmaking strategy. Established in 1984, the Community Foundation for Southeast Michigan works to enhance the quality of life in southeast Michigan.

title: California Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Foundation for California Community Colleges, which coordinates the California Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue the development of policy, partnerships and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) strengthening key partnerships to expand the continuous quality improvement system of statewide supports to advance a field-informed strategy to increase access to high-quality enrichment and learning opportunities; 2) increasing cross-sector advocacy efforts to bring awareness of afterschool and summer learning programs positive influence on whole-child health and wellness supports; 3) implementing new strategies and models to support equity centered workforce pathways to advance the afterschool field; and 4) supporting the promotion and distribution of Mizzen by Mott.

title: West Virginia Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the West Virginia University Extension Service which coordinates the West Virginia Statewide Afterschool Network to continue the development of policy, partnerships and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) launching a statewide afterschool initiative to support young people impacted by the opioid crisis; 2) conducting a state mapping effort to identify gaps in services, effective practices for rural areas and areas for potential growth; 3) developing a toolkit for afterschool programs to support quality training for programs serving youth that have experienced trauma as a result of the substance misuse crisis; and 4) supporting the promotion and distribution of Mizzen by Mott.

title: Arizona Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Arizona Center for Afterschool Excellence, which coordinates the Arizona Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue the development of policy, partnerships and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) expanding continuous quality initiatives by strengthening existing partnerships and engaging new partners in the education and child care sector; 2) developing a collaborative network of key champions to advocate for sustainable funding and resources to increase access to high-quality afterschool programs and summer learning environments; 3) creating new professional development resources and training centered on equity and inclusion for the afterschool and education field to advance equitable opportunities for youth and families; and 4) supporting the promotion and distribution of Mizzen by Mott.

title: New York Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: New York State Network for Youth Success, Inc.
description: This grant will support the New York State Network for Youth Success, which coordinates the New York Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue the development of policy, partnerships and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) developing a statewide diversity, equity and inclusion initiative to increase the afterschool field’s capacity to serve historically marginalized youth; 2) supporting student learning recovery for all youth through expanded access to high-quality afterschool programs and community schools; 3) expand hybrid and virtual training credentials to increase equitable access to professional development for afterschool educators; and 4) supporting the promotion and distribution of Mizzen by Mott.

title: Washington Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support School’s Out Washington, which coordinates the Washington Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue the development of policy, partnerships and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) creating a sustainable structure for school-community partnerships through state, regional and local initiatives; 2) developing and expanding statewide strategies to secure resources to sustain new and existing school-linked afterschool programs; 3) providing a statewide professional development system to implement post-COVID-19 response supports for the afterschool and summer learning community; and 4) supporting the promotion and distribution of Mizzen by Mott.

title: Vermont Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Vermont Afterschool which coordinates the Vermont Statewide Afterschool Network to continue the development of policy, partnerships and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) developing a comprehensive statewide initiative to improve student health and learning outcomes through high-quality afterschool programs; 2) support the expansion of high-quality afterschool and summer learning programs to better meet the needs of young people and families in Vermont; 3) working with youth to establish a Vermont Youth Council; and 4) supporting the promotion and distribution of Mizzen by Mott.

title: Connecticut Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: Connecticut Network for Children and Youth, Inc.
description: This grant will support the Connecticut After School Network, which coordinates the Connecticut Statewide Afterschool Network, to continue the development of policy, partnerships and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) coordinating afterschool, child care and social-emotional learning programs in Connecticut to improve youth outcomes; 2) scaling exemplary program models that support student learning recovery and opportunity lost during COVID-19; 3) expanding the network’s diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives to increase equitable access for children youth and families; and 4) supporting the promotion and distribution of Mizzen by Mott.

title: Family Separation Crisis Fund
description: Founded in 1987, Hispanics in Philanthropy is a membership association for philanthropic institutions, corporations, organizations, and individuals. Its mission is to strengthen Latino equity, leadership, and voice to build a more equal and prosperous America and Latin America. The grantee is creating a special emergency fund in response to the crisis unfolding along the U.S.-Mexico border, where children in families seeking to immigrate to the United States, often asylum-seekers, are being separated from their parents. The fund aims to mobilize national support to provide a coordinated philanthropic response to this crisis. Emergency support will be provided to local and regional social service nonprofits, direct service organizations, and legal advocacy groups serving the border region on both sides.

title: TAP Network
description: The program goal is to support active and organized civil society participation in efforts to increase access to justice globally. The Transparency, Accountability, and Participation Network, a project of the Proteus Fund, will mobilize its membership of over 270 civil society organizations for coordinated action around implementation of Sustainable Development Goal 16, with its focus on peaceful, just, and inclusive societies. During the grant period, activities will include: 1) supporting members to work with and hold governments accountable to Goal 16; 2) promoting civil society engagement in formal mechanisms of implementation and review; and 3) and helping empower civil society through regional and national-level coordination and collaboration leading up to and including the “High-level Political Forums,” which are the formal mechanisms through which United Nations member states report on, review, and adjust commitments under the goals. Founded in 1994, the Proteus Fund convenes and facilitates donor collaboratives that strategically focus philanthropic resources toward the realization of a just, equitable, and democratic world.

title: Pathfinders for Peaceful, Just and Inclusive Societies: Civil Society Participation & Voice
description: The program goal is to ensure and increase active participation of civil society-based justice practitioners in research, advocacy, and implementation of access to justice goals under Sustainable Development Goal 16. The Pathfinders for Peaceful, Just and Inclusive Societies is a multi-stakeholder platform, convened by the governments of Brazil, Sierra Leone, and Switzerland and the New York University’s Center on International Cooperation. As part of advocacy efforts around United Nations High-level Political Forums to be held in 2019 and which will assess progress in achieving respectively Goal 16 and the broader Agenda 2030, the grantee will work to engage civil society organizations in contributing data and evidence on justice needs and grassroots responses to these needs globally. The grantee will also produce an analytical paper exploring the case for investing in civil society-based justice providers. Finally, they will ensure that civil society actors have platforms to participate prominently in regional and global meetings and events leading up to the High-level Political Forums.

title: Data Analysis for Advancing Access to Justice
description: The program goal is to produce new knowledge on legal needs globally. The World Justice Project will produce a follow-up to its Global Insights on Access to Justice report, broadening coverage to an additional 60 countries to better capture comparable data on legal needs and public access to justice. Working with a range of global partners, the grantee will also seek to develop a new assessment of the number of people with unmet justice needs (“the justice gap”) while also proposing an additional official indicator on access to justice within the context of Sustainable Development Goal 16. Additionally, through data collection and analysis, the grantee will work to support the business case for improved access to justice, underlining the benefits of timely investment in justice provision. Established initially as a project of the American Bar Association in 2006, the grantee was formally registered as an independent organization in 2009 working to advance the rule of law around the world.

title: Ludington State Park Land Acquisition
description: The state of Michigan’s Ludington State Park, located along the Lake Michigan shoreline between Muskegon and Manistee, is home to a wide range of natural communities and provides shelter for threatened and endangered species. The park’s natural beauty draws over 800,000 visitors annually, making it the region’s top tourist destination and a vital part of the local economy. Mott funds will be used to add additional acreage to the park, including pristine dune lands near the park’s primary entrance.

title: Clean Water For New York Campaign
description: Environmental Advocates of New York works to advance common-sense policies to make the state more ecologically sustainable and protect public health and the environment. With support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has built its organizational capacity to protect Great Lakes water resources. Activities have included mobilizing partners to understand the importance of investing in water infrastructure, leading a campaign to eliminate lead in drinking water, and working to raise awareness about chemicals in drinking water. With continued support, the grantee will highlight local success stories; generate media coverage; engage communities, local officials, and other stakeholders; and lead partner organizations in championing statewide policy change on clean water issues that benefits the Great Lakes.

title: General Purposes
description: UK Community Foundations is a membership organization of 46 community foundations across the United Kingdom. The grantee has supported the development and expansion of community foundations over the years by providing technical assistance, training, data collection, research, marketing, financial assistance and advocacy. Over the next three years, the grantee will continue to focus on supporting and promoting its members to act effectively as community leaders, conveners and funders. The grantee will also support its network to engage meaningfully with the Sustainable Development Goals. The UK Community Foundations network collectively gives grants totaling approximately £100 million annually to local groups throughout the United Kingdom.

title: Flint Filter Education and Testing Program
description: This grant will provide support to Freshwater Future to implement a permanent water testing laboratory at the Flint Development Center. The grantee will work with community partners including Flint Neighborhoods United, Genesee County Hispanic Latino Collaborative and others to identify Flint residents interested in having their water tested. Additionally, all partners will work collectively to offer filter education to testing participants and the broader community.

title: Metropolitan Policy Program
description: The Metropolitan Policy Program at Brookings Institution, an internationally known think-tank, works with local communities to assist in the development and strategy for retooling the American economy. With continuing support, the grantee will undertake a range of work to promote the economic competitiveness of metropolitan areas domestically and globally, including older industrial cities such as Flint. Activities will include original research, policy advocacy, analytical tool development, and network building.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purposes support to PEAK Grantmaking, Inc. for its efforts to assist a nationwide network of foundation grants managers. In this role, the grantee improves grantmaking by advancing the knowledge, skills, and abilities of grants managers and by leading grantmakers to adopt and incorporate effective practices that benefit the philanthropic community.

title: Supporting the Energy Access Ecosystem
description: Today six out of every ten Tanzanians lack access to clean energy services. An estimated $80 billion of energy investments will be required between 2019-40 to ensure universal access to modern energy services in the country. While the Government of Tanzania, the private sector and the development community have made significant investments to increase energy access, the International Energy Agency estimates that by 2030 some 44 million Tanzanians will still lack access to modern energy services. With Mott Foundation support over the past four years, Fraxen Consulting has been coordinating civil society efforts in Tanzania to demonstrate a model approach to accelerating access to modern energy services with distributed renewable energy solutions. With renewed support and drawing on lessons learned to date, the project will expand to include more stakeholders. Fraxen will strengthen its coordination and partnership-building function towards advancing solutions to energy poverty, particularly in off-grid communities of Tanzania.

title: Foundation Center and GuideStar Integration
description: This grant will support a merger between the Foundation Center and GuideStar, two of the philanthropic sector’s largest information platforms. Over time, both organizations have built a stable business model that provides data to millions while developing deep expertise and insight on the data. Jointly, these organizations have 16 million users, 4 billion pieces of data, 400 local partners, and 218 Internet platforms. A merger between them is a step toward centralizing data, resources, and knowledge, which will simplify information gathering and analysis for practitioners, foundations, donors, and other stakeholders.
