In addition to consolidating information resources, the combination of their networks will enable access for users to an expansive international array of partners and organizations. The Foundation Center and GuideStar are dedicated to fostering public understanding of the foundation field and nonprofit sector, respectively, by collecting, organizing, analyzing, and disseminating information on foundations, corporate giving, nonprofits, and related subjects.

title: Foundation Center and GuideStar Integration
description: The goal of this grant is to support the Foundation Center and GuideStar merger into the singular entity, Candid. Over time, both organizations have built a stable business model that provides data to millions while developing deep expertise and insight on the data. The grantee has made strides in centralizing its data and resources, as well as simplifying information gathering and analysis for practitioners, foundations, donors, and other stakeholders through its new website. This increase will enable the continued consolidation of the grantee’s business systems and databases, improvement of those systems, and integration of staff and organizational cultures. Candid is dedicated to fostering public understanding of the foundation field and nonprofit sectors by collecting, organizing, analyzing, and disseminating information on foundations, corporate giving, nonprofits, and related subjects.

title: Foundation Center and GuideStar Integration
description: This grant increase will continue to support for the integration between the Foundation Center and GuideStar, two of the philanthropic sector’s largest information platforms. Over time, both organizations have built a stable business model that provides data to millions while developing deep expertise and insight into the data. Jointly, these organizations have 16 million users, 4 billion pieces of data, 400 local partners, and 218 Internet platforms. During the previous grant period, Candid integrated its business and data systems, including the migration of 65 years worth of data, as well as its personnel. This increase will enable the grantee to continue integrating data systems and personnel. Candid is dedicated to fostering public understanding of the foundation field and nonprofit sector, respectively, by collecting, organizing, analyzing and disseminating information on foundations, corporate giving, nonprofits and related subjects.

title: General Purposes
description: The Casual Workers Advice Office was established in 2011 to give free legal advice to workers who have been dismissed or face other labor violations by their employers in South Africa. Past support assisted the grantee to successfully advocate for the inclusion of precarious workers as permanent employees with benefits; establish the Simunye Workers Forum, which meets every fortnight to discuss rights and responsibilities; and establish an in-house legal clinic staffed by an attorney to assist with rights violations. Ongoing support will allow the grantee to continue empowering precarious workers to exercise their rights and improve the quality of their lives, through organized meetings, research, education and legal assistance.

title: Neighborhood Arts and Cultural Events
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will support arts and culture projects through the Neighborhood Small Grants Program at the Community Foundation of Greater Flint. Neighborhood groups will implement resident-led efforts to create or enhance and expand existing artistic projects or events/performances. Funded projects will aim to stimulate civic engagement, improve neighborhood conditions, provide opportunities for self-expression, and/or enhance skills for residents to work together creatively.

title: National Service and Volunteer Center Capacity Building
description: This grant to the United Way of Genesee County will provide additional capacity to support service throughout Genesee County. National service members and volunteers provide critical resources to area nonprofits, government agencies, and schools to help meet a variety of community needs such as blight elimination, neighborhood engagement, and tutoring and mentoring.

title: Community Foundation Leadership Metrics and Sustainable Development Goals
description: The project goal is to help community foundations advance the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals at the local level. Over the past grant period, the grantee developed and tested community leadership metrics and established baseline information about the degree to which U.S. community foundations are incorporating the Sustainable Development Goals into their work. In the upcoming grant period, the grantee will institutionalize the annual collection of data on the work of community foundations related to the Sustainable Development Goals and community leadership. The grantee will also create and regularly convene a coordinating group of researchers working on this issue. The work is being led by CF Insights, a service of the grantee which collects and shares data and conducts analysis that helps community foundations improve their performance. Candid was established in 2019 as the result of a merger between Foundation Center, the leading source of information on U.S. philanthropy, and GuideStar, the leading source of information on U.S. nonprofit organizations.

title: Community Foundations and Sustainable Development Goals
description: The project goal is to help community foundations advance the Sustainable Development Goals at the local level. Over the past grant period, Candid regularly convened an SDG Working Group of researchers and philanthropy-serving organizations focused on promoting the adoption of the goals by community foundations within and outside the U.S. Over the next two years, the grantee will position CF Insights, a service of Candid which collects and shares data and conducts an analysis that helps community foundations, to improve their performance as a global hub for data collection and peer learning to promote further adoption of the goals. The grantee will expand the CF Insights data platform to include community foundations operating outside the U.S., host regular convenings of the SDG Working Group and develop an online peer learning resource platform. Candid was established in 2019 as the result of a merger between Foundation Center and GuideStar.

title: Global Philanthropy Program
description: This grant supports the Council on Foundations’ Global Philanthropy Program, which is framed around four pillars of activity: 1) strengthening cross-border grantmaking, 2) advocating for a global enabling environment, 3) facilitating global convenings and conversations, and 4) developing global resources and thought leadership. Over the past 18 months, the grantee expanded a library of resources on international grantmaking on its website, maintained close relationships with the U.S. Department of Treasury regarding international regulatory issues, hosted seven webinars for 490 registrants on global grantmaking topics, held 12 meetings of the Global Liaisons group of international institutions, promoted the use of Sustainable Development Goals by U.S. foundations, hosted delegations of foreign philanthropic actors, and served on several global advisory boards. During the upcoming grant period, the grantee will continue to enhance and expand upon the four activity pillars. Founded in 1949, the Council on Foundations is a membership organization of private, community, and corporate foundations, primarily in the U.S.

title: Global Philanthropy Program
description: This grant supports the Council on Foundations’ Global Philanthropy Program, which is framed around four pillars of activity: 1) strengthening cross-border grantmaking; 2) advocating for a global enabling environment; 3) facilitating global convenings and conversations; and 4) developing global resources and thought leadership. Activities over the past two years included publications and a blog series on responding globally to COVID-19, webinars on various global topics of interest to its members, convening funders around India’s new restrictions on foreign funding, disaster response pages regarding humanitarian crises in Haiti and Afghanistan, updating members on regulatory changes that affect giving to organizations in selected countries, and updates to Country Notes web pages for Mexico, Brazil, Canada, Australia, Czech Republic and Tanzania. During the upcoming grant period, the grantee will continue to enhance and expand upon the four activity pillars. Founded in 1949, the Council on Foundations is a membership organization of private, community and corporate foundations, primarily in the U.S.

title: Michigan Water Financing
description: The Nature Conservancy in Michigan is highly respected as a credible voice for solving complex problems by bridging environment, science, and economic priorities and building necessary partnerships – including with corporate leaders – to achieve policy reform. As the Great Lakes state and being surrounded by four of the five lakes, Michigan’s leadership in solving regional problems is of paramount importance. Like all states and provinces, Michigan faces a water infrastructure financing crisis that will eventually limit the state’s ability to grow and flourish in the decades to come. The Nature Conservancy, working in partnership with Michigan State University, will form an advisory committee and a team of fellows. These two groups will benefit from research from across the U.S. to identify the best methods for financing upgrades to water utilities and will formulate consensus recommendations on the best plan approach for Michigan.

title: Great Lakes Legislative Caucus Education
geographic_focus: New York, Minnesota, Michigan, Pennsylvania, Ohio, Wisconsin, Illinois, Ontario, Indiana
description: For over a decade, the Council of State Governments has brought together state and provincial policymakers from the Great Lakes region to learn about key issues affecting the lakes, exchange information and ideas, and build their capacity to be effective leaders and stewards of the lakes. The forum for this work is the Great Lakes-St. Lawrence Legislative Caucus, which includes over 200 members representing all eight Great Lakes states, and two Canadian provinces. The grantee will educate policymakers and convene them to share information and lessons from neighboring jurisdictions. New for the grantee is its Institute for Great Lakes-St. Lawrence Policy, an intensive learning program that takes policymakers on a “deep dive” into a single issue.

title: Community Foundation Development Project
description: The project goal is to support the development and expansion of community foundations in the southern Africa region. To this end, SGS Consulting plans to provide technical support and training to community foundation support organizations in specified countries, coordinate the establishment of a networking platform for support organizations in the region, provide structured support to community foundations in South Africa and document the experience of supporting the community foundation movement in the region to produce learning products. Past support enabled the grantee to conduct a landscape study to understand the community philanthropy field and the feasibility of growing the community foundation movement in the region. In addition, the grantee promoted the community foundation concept at significant events in the region, engaged with potential community foundation support organizations in five countries, built on previous work in South Africa to help establish community foundations and improved its knowledge of the community foundation field globally.

title: Great Lakes Program
description: Founded in 1980, Michigan Environmental Council is a statewide environmental nonprofit organization based in Lansing. With prior Mott support, the grantee helped implement the Great Lakes Compact, the Clean Water Act, and other freshwater policies that protect and restore the Great Lakes ecosystem. With this grant increase, Michigan Environmental Council will host a one-day workshop on Michigan Drinking Water Policy Priorities. This will help formulate new policies for responding to drinking water threats, including lead and emerging chemicals like PFAS. The grant increase will also support the continued work of a drinking water expert to improve standards for certifying lead-free drinking water plumbing materials and fixtures.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to provide comprehensive support to internally displaced persons and others affected by conflict in Ukraine. Through a network of online and offline legal advice centers, Gorenie will provide primary and secondary legal assistance to displaced victims of conflict in four regions (Dnipropetrovsk, Zaporizhiye, Kharkov and Ukraine-controlled Donetsk) bordering on the conflict zone that has received the bulk of such migrants. The grantee will provide training services for local officials to improve service delivery and integration practices related to target groups. The grantee will also work to build the self-organizing capacity of these target groups. From 2018-2020, the grantee provided primary and secondary legal assistance to over 50,000 Ukrainians directly impacted by conflict. Over 160,000 requests for legal and social benefit information were processed through Gorenie’s mobile legal assistance app. Based in Dnipro, Gorenie was founded in 2005 to provide wide-ranging assistance to disadvantaged and marginalized groups throughout Ukraine.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to provide comprehensive support to internally displaced persons and others affected by war in Ukraine. Through a network of online and offline legal advice centers, Gorenie will provide primary and secondary legal assistance to displaced victims of war in four regions (Dnipropetrovsk, Zaporizhiye, Kharkov and Ukraine-controlled Donetsk) bordering on the war zone that has received the bulk of such migrants. The grantee will provide training services for local officials to improve service delivery and integration practices related to target groups. The grantee will also work to build the self-organizing capacity of these target groups. From 2018-2020, the grantee provided primary and secondary legal assistance to over 50,000 Ukrainians directly impacted by war. Over 160,000 requests for legal and social benefit information were processed through Gorenie’s mobile legal assistance app. Based in Dnipro, Gorenie was founded in 2005 to provide wide-ranging assistance to disadvantaged and marginalized groups throughout Ukraine. This increase will allow Gorenie to update and improve legal and rights information for displaced persons, ensure security of staff, and open additional premises where people can find support and assistance under conditions of evacuation and martial law.

title: Centre on African Philanthropy and Social Investment
description: The University of the Witwatersrand was established to provide high-quality, internationally competitive education, founded on high academic standards, cutting-edge research, public engagement and productive partnerships with leading institutions throughout the world. The Centre on African Philanthropy and Social Investment, based at the business school, was established to bridge the gap in the study, research and practice of philanthropy in Africa. Past support has enabled the center to conduct research on several topics related to African philanthropy, develop curriculum for the academic programs and host events on topics relevant to philanthropy in Africa. This grant will support the center to deliver academic and certificate programs, conduct research and generate data on philanthropy in Africa, produce publications and build its capacity to deliver programs on a virtual platform.

title: Centre on African Philanthropy and Social Investment
description: The project goal is to promote philanthropy in Africa by generating new knowledge and building a cadre of experts, researchers and academics in African philanthropy, social investment and related disciplines. The Centre on African Philanthropy and Social Investment, a project of the University of the Witwatersrand, works to bridge the gap in the study, research and practice of philanthropy in Africa. To achieve this, the center has produced research on various forms of giving in Africa, delivered academic and certificate programs, hosted learning events and strengthened its capacity to deliver on the work. During this grant period, the center will; 1) deliver academic and certificate programs to build a cadre of experts in philanthropy; 2) produce academic research to build content for its programs and new information on philanthropy in the continent; 3) host learning events to share research and engage practitioners on various topics related to philanthropy; and 4) produce and disseminate publications on philanthropy in Africa.

title: Impact of National Service
description: This grant will support Voices for National Service, a program of City Year, Inc., to conduct and publish a cost-benefit analysis that will help demonstrate how national service programs lead to a significant return on investment for communities and the country at large. In addition, the analysis will help to raise awareness of the benefits of investing in national service.

title: Endowment Funds
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide endowment funds the Flint Institute of Arts. Endowments provide needed operating support to ensure that the organization can maintain quality visual arts opportunities and programs as well as related staff and operations. The grantee operates the second largest art museum in Michigan and the fifth largest art school in the country and also maintains a robust calendar of public programs for all ages.

title: Endowment Funds
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide endowment funds to the Flint Institute of Music. Endowments provide needed operating support to ensure that the organization can maintain quality music, performing arts, and theater programs as well as related staff and operations. The grantee serves youth and adults in the Flint area through the Flint Repertory Theatre, Flint Symphony Orchestra, and Flint School of Performing Arts.

title: Adult Career Pathway Program
description: This grant will support Mott Community College’s Adult Career Pathway Program. The program will leverage many of the college’s existing educational and training programs to help connect unemployed adults, low-income workers, and youth to employment and a career pathway. The goal is to ensure that area residents can enter and advance into higher-wage occupations in high-growth industries. Work experience and support services are integrated into the model and will enable participants to combine school and work, advancing over time. Providing residents with job training and career advancement opportunities will help build Flint’s economic resilience to recover from the water crisis.

title: Capacity Building
description: The Disability Network was founded in 1993 to provide services and supports to people with any type of disability in Flint and Genesee County. The organization connects people to services and programs that provide advocacy, technology, financial, educational, employment, accessibility, housing, healthcare, and basic living assistance. Funds raised from the Over the Edge rappelling event will help the Disability Network support new and existing programs and projects.

title: Rent and Utility Assistance Program
description: Since 1893, the Salvation Army of Genesee County has worked to alleviate hardships faced by Genesee County residents. This grant will support the Salvation Army’s financial assistance services administered through the Comprehensive Emergency Assistance Program. The goal is to help the Salvation Army better meet household demand for utility shutoffs and eviction, and foreclosure assistance.

title: Board Training and Coaching
description: This grant will provide support to Flint Community Schools to engage the Michigan Association of School Boards for assistance with board governance training and superintendent relations. As the district works within the Michigan Department of Education’s Partnership Agreement process, effective and efficient board governance and a strong relationship with the superintendent is more critical than ever.

title: Helping Young People to Employment Program
description: This grant will support the Helping Young People to Employment Program. The program is managed by Faith Foundation Resources, a nonprofit dedicated to working with low-income and at-risk people to help better their lives. The goal of the Helping Young People to Employment Program is to prepare youth aged 16-24 for work. Young people learn about the job training and career skills needed to become productive and responsible members of society. Courses focus on job readiness, learning the fundamentals of interpersonal skills, and financial literacy. After completion of an eight-week training program, youth are eligible to be placed into 20 to 30 hours of after school employment. Metro Community Development, a long-time Foundation grantee will serve as a fiduciary for Faith Foundation Resources.

title: Increasing Food Distribution
description: This grant will provide funds to Carriage Town Ministries to purchase food in order to serve meals to the homeless and those in need of food assistance who come to the shelter. The grantee provides important safety-net services to individuals and families in the Flint area who are homeless or near-homeless including food, safe and warm shelter, clothes, personal hygiene products, health services, and life skills courses.

title: Housing and Food Assistance
description: Shelter of Flint provides services for approximately 1,000 people each day. Most of these clients are families who are economically challenged. The principal goal of the agency is to assist the homeless in achieving stability through a continuum of care model ranging from crisis prevention and counseling to elimination of the root causes of homelessness. This grant will help support services for families through the grantee’s One Stop Housing Resource Center program and the Emergency Shelter program. Individuals and families will receive food assistance as well as comprehensive case management services and the development of long-range plans toward permanent stability.

title: Afterschool Policy and System Building Initiative
description: This grant to Explora will enable the New Mexico Statewide Afterschool Network to increase the quality of programs developed and implemented in underserved areas of New Mexico. This project will: 1) provide high-quality professional development opportunities for out-of-school time leaders in underserved communities; 2) improve access and quality of out-of-school time programs across New Mexico; and 3) increase the number of quality out-of-school time programs funded and sustained in areas not currently receiving funding. The grantee will share lessons learned with other state networks to enhance quality programs for underserved youth.

title: Afterschool Policy and System Building Initiative
description: This grant to Ignite Afterschool will enable the Minnesota Statewide Afterschool Network to continue the development of new policy initiatives and strategic partnerships to connect high-quality afterschool opportunities to workforce pathways for youth. This project will: 1) convene stakeholders and decision-makers to clarify barriers and solutions to youth employment pathways; 2) build consensus on policy recommendations for improving youth workforce pathways; and 3) promote and implement education and communication strategies to enhance the support of high-quality afterschool and youth employment programs. The grantee will share lessons learned with other state networks to enhance the policy and quality initiatives within their communities and states.

title: Afterschool Policy and System Building Initiative
grantee: New York State Network for Youth Success, Inc.
description: This grant will support the New York State Network for Youth Success, which coordinates the New York Statewide Afterschool Network to continue development of policy initiatives, strategic partnerships, and funding opportunities to benefit New York youth in high-quality afterschool programs. This project will: 1) increase the number of high-quality programs in New York; 2) develop new partnerships and support for addressing adverse childhood experiences in afterschool programs; and 3) increase the awareness, value, and impact of high-quality afterschool programs through a statewide afterschool marketing strategy. The grantee will share lessons learned with other state networks to enhance the advocacy initiatives within their communities and states.

title: Afterschool Policy and System Building Initiative
description: This grant to the University of Southern Maine will enable the Maine Statewide Afterschool Network to increase the availability of high-quality summer learning programs in Maine. This project will: 1) support the development and implementation of a statewide education campaign on the need for summer learning in Maine; 2) develop coalitions of key partners throughout the state; and 3) build a network of afterschool and summer learning champions in Maine. The grantee will share lessons learned with other state networks to increase access to summer learning programs.

title: Afterschool Policy and System Building Initiative
description: This grant to Vermont Afterschool will enable the Vermont Statewide Afterschool Network to launch, support, and implement the Change the Story: Youth in Afterschool project. This project will: 1) create a statewide afterschool youth council; 2) provide training and support to afterschool programs interested in elevating youth voice; and 3) develop and implement a statewide strategic communications campaign to support the need for afterschool and youth voice in Vermont. The grantee will share lessons learned with other state networks to enhance youth voice in afterschool programs.

title: Afterschool Policy and System Building Initiative
grantee: Public School Forum of North Carolina
description: This grant to the Public School Forum of North Carolina will enable the North Carolina Statewide Afterschool Network to continue the development of new policy initiatives and strategic partnerships to expand high-quality afterschool opportunities for youth in underserved rural communities. This project will: 1) increase the number of high-quality afterschool programs in rural communities; 2) provide professional development opportunities to rural partners to strengthen the quality of afterschool programs; and 3) implement a comprehensive policy initiative statewide to increase the awareness, value, and impact of high-quality afterschool programs. The grantee will share lessons learned with other state networks to enhance the policy and quality initiatives within their communities and states.

title: Afterschool Policy and System Building Initiative
description: This grant to United Ways of Tennessee will enable the Tennessee Statewide Afterschool Network to increase the capacity of afterschool programs to address the opioid crisis. This project will: 1) support the development and implementation of a statewide education and communications campaign on the value of afterschool; 2) provide professional development to support afterschool programs around prevention and intervention of opioid use; and 3) build a network of afterschool champions in the state. The grantee will share lessons learned with other state networks in addressing these challenges in support of children in afterschool programs.

title: Afterschool Youth Entrepreneurship Initiative
description: This grant to the Healthcare Collaborative of Greater Columbus will enable the Ohio Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to opportunities for high school youth to learn about and experience entrepreneurship in afterschool programs. This project will: 1) foster regional entrepreneurial ecosystems; 2) train afterschool professionals to deliver entrepreneurial curriculum to high school programs; and 3) develop local, regional, and statewide high school pitch competitions. The grantee will share lessons learned with other state networks to enhance youth entrepreneurial initiatives in afterschool programs.

title: Afterschool Youth Entrepreneurship Initiative
description: This grant to Central Susquehanna Intermediate Unit will enable the Pennsylvania Statewide Afterschool Network to establish Out-of-School Time Innovation Hubs throughout the state to provide greater access to entrepreneurial programs, STEM activities, and career-readiness models. This project will: 1) launch entrepreneurial and STEM programming and expand out-of-school time career pathway models; 2) design and implement professional development and trainings; and 3) reorganize and build the local and regional capacity of out-of-school time organizations. The grantee will share lessons learned with other state networks to enhance youth entrepreneurial initiatives in out-of-school time programs.

title: Afterschool Youth Entrepreneurship Initiative
description: This grant to the Wyoming Community Foundation will enable the Wyoming Statewide Afterschool Network to advance activities that will support the state’s efforts to successfully increase the skills and knowledge of the future workforce. This project will: 1) increase young people’s interest in new business development through entrepreneurship activities; 2) develop a curriculum and activity portal for afterschool programs; and 3) engage new business, industry, school districts, and higher education partners to support and develop joint initiatives focused on afterschool career readiness. The grantee will share lessons learned with other state networks to enhance youth entrepreneurial and workforce initiatives in afterschool programs.

title: Afterschool Youth Entrepreneurship Initiative
description: This grant to the Arizona Center for Afterschool Excellence will enable the Arizona Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to opportunities for high school youth to experience entrepreneurship in afterschool programs. This project will support the network to: 1) develop a summer entrepreneurship program for high school students; 2) enhance entrepreneurship curriculum to include soft skills and align with state quality standards; and 3) develop high school pitch competitions. The grantee will share lessons learned with other state networks to enhance youth entrepreneurship initiatives in afterschool programs.

title: Afterschool Youth Entrepreneurship Initiative
description: This grant to Nebraska Children and Families Foundation will enable the Nebraska Statewide Afterschool Network to increase the quality and sustainability of afterschool programs across Nebraska by expanding entrepreneurial opportunities for youth through regional and national partnerships in under-served rural afterschool communities. This project will: 1) increase the number of high-quality afterschool programs in rural communities; 2) design and develop entrepreneurial project-based programming for K-12 youth; and 3) expand strategic partnerships to support entrepreneurial initiatives. The grantee will share lessons learned with other state networks to enhance youth entrepreneurial initiatives in rural afterschool programs.

title: General Purposes
description: Founded in 1992, the Greater Flint Health Coalition works to achieve the collaborative and systemic changes needed to improve the health status of Genesee County residents and the quality and cost effectiveness of the local healthcare system. The grantee was established to be a neutral backbone and convening agency by healthcare, public health, businesses, and other community leaders. The Greater Flint Health Coalition convenes numerous committees, task forces, and program teams. This grant will provide general purposes support for the grantee to maintain its staffing levels to support the design, coordination, and delivery of health-related activities in response to the Flint water crisis.

title: General Purposes
description: Founded in 1992, the Greater Flint Health Coalition works to achieve the collaborative and systemic changes needed to improve the health status of Genesee County residents and the quality and cost effectiveness of the local healthcare system. The grantee was established to be a neutral backbone and convening agency for healthcare, public health, businesses and other community leaders. The Greater Flint Health Coalition convenes numerous committees, task forces and program teams. This grant will provide general purposes support for the grantee to maintain its organizational capacity and allow further progression of critical community initiatives to support the design, coordination and delivery of health-related activities in response to the Flint water crisis and pandemic.

title: Increasing Parental Engagement in Children's Savings Account Programs
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant will enable Ideas42 to support the Foundation’s efforts to provide more young people with children’s savings accounts. Specifically, Ideas42 will partner with San Francisco’s Kindergarten to College program to explore innovative ways to increase student and parental engagement in the program. Drawing insights from behavioral science, the grantee will recommend improvements to the initial “welcome kit” as well as outreach strategies along the broader set of program delivery channels and intervention points. The grantee’s staff will also suggest strategies to enhance the impacts of savings accounts on college-going aspirations and behavior. Ideas42 was founded out of research programs in psychology and economics at top academic institutions and uses behavioral science to help solve challenging social problems.

title: Fiscal Solvency and Service Effectiveness Project
description: This project continues support for Michigan State University’s efforts to document and promote solutions that help America’s older industrial cities address chronic fiscal stress. The City of Flint will remain a research focus, while new attention will be placed on Flint Community Schools–both as a focus on the research and as a beneficiary of technical assistance efforts intended to educate city and school leaders about potential solutions to the structural and managerial challenges confronting their institutions. The university will also publish two white papers and share relevant findings with statewide and national audiences.

title: Detroit Afterschool Initiative
description: The grant will provide support to the Community Education Commission for the implementation of the Get On And Learn Line program in the Northwest region of Detroit. The specific components for the grant will include: 1) providing a high-quality afterschool learning environment through innovative programs and partnerships; and 2) providing free reliable transportation for the participants in the region.

title: General Purposes
description: The European Foundation Centre is an independent membership association of foundations and corporate funders dedicated to promoting organized philanthropy in Europe and internationally. In 2019-2020, the grantee carried out a wide range of activities, including organizing an annual general assembly and conference in Paris in 2019 and a 30th anniversary event online in 2020. The grantee also organized learning and networking events for members and worked with the Donors and Foundations Networks in Europe to support an enabling environment for philanthropy in Europe. In 2021–2022, the grantee will focus on providing intellectual leadership on emerging policy agendas and societal trends that will impact institutional philanthropy, fostering connections within philanthropy and with external actors, providing a voice for European institutional philanthropy and developing a new membership strategy. Established in 1989 by seven of Europe’s leading foundations, the European Foundation Centre serves a core membership of over 190 members.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Independent Philanthropy Association of South Africa
description: The project goal is to support domestic philanthropy infrastructure in South Africa. To this end, the Independent Philanthropy Association of South Africa will undertake activities with the goal of advancing independent philanthropy. It will focus on four key areas, which are to: a) grow and transform philanthropy, b) be the voice of independent philanthropy, c) promote good practice in philanthropy, and d) support collaboration. The grantee was established in 2015 as a voluntary association and network to represent and promote the common interests, concerns, and objectives of its members.

title: Nonprofit Policy and Research Project
description: The project goal is to advance the nonprofit sector’s policy development and advocacy capacity. The Nonprofit Quarterly, whose mission is to promote active democracy and a thriving civil society, is one of the leading three publications serving the nonprofit sector in the United States. The Nonprofit Quarterly aims to build a practice to elucidate policy options and positions in a manner that addresses not only institutional perspectives, but those of the communities served by nonprofits and civil society more broadly. Specific activities include: 1)investigation of consequences of policy proposals affecting nonprofits and philanthropy; 2)organizing a policy committee dedicated to the best interests of civil society and communities; 3) commissioning research and white papers on priority policy positions; 4) dedicating senior editor time to vet and frame policy positions; 5) advancing ongoing dialogue on critical policy issues; and 6) developing new dissemination methods for this content. The Nonprofit Quarterly was launched as a national journal in late 1999 as a publication of Third Sector New England and in 2006 spun off into an independent publication.

title: Community Education First Tee
description: This grant will provide support to the Crim Fitness Foundation to partner with First Tee of Eastern Michigan to introduce the game of golf to students through community education. The opportunity will be available to students attending Flint Community Schools and the International Academy of Flint through the community schools program. Students will learn about the game of golf; not only how to play, but also the character development skills that are important to the game and translate to all aspects of life.

title: Middle School Curriculum and Teacher Training
description: With this grant, Flint Community Schools will implement a series of initiatives aimed at creating a middle school environment that garners students’ interest and is productive for effective teaching and learning. Specifically, the grantee will bolster middle school curriculum and provide teacher training to improve teaching and learning for students during these formative years. The new curriculum will offer more hands-on and project-based learning opportunities, and training will support teachers with the delivery techniques that foster this style of classroom engagement.

title: Integrating Advocacy: Building the Policy Capacity of Digital Civil Society
description: The project goal is to strengthen the capacity of nonprofits to recognize intersections with digital rights and policies and to engage in relevant digital rights policy advocacy. To this end, Stanford University’s Digital Civil Society Lab, led by Dr. Lucy Bernholz, will create 10 online learning modules specific to digital policy issues impacting civil society and actively support and coordinate the use of these materials. For each module, a variety of media will be created, including video explainers, scenario exercises, funder and nonprofit checklists, curated resource lists, and policy briefs. The lab will work with civil society networks and infrastructure organizations to disseminate and use the modules. The activities during this phase of the project will build on the findings and strategies described in the lab’s 2020 report entitled Integrating Advocacy. The lab aims to understand how digital technology has transformed civil society and to shape these transformations to support a thriving and independent civil society in the digital age.

title: Integrating Advocacy: Building the Policy Capacity of Digital Civil Society
geographic_focus: Europe, South America, World, United States, Africa, Central America
description: The project goal is to strengthen the capacity of nonprofits to recognize intersections with digital rights and policies and to engage in relevant digital rights policy advocacy. During the grant period, Stanford University’s Digital Civil Society Lab, led by Dr. Lucy Bernholz, will build on its robust assessment of the landscape and the resources it has created with the goal of connecting this work with nonprofits across the sector. To this end, the lab will work with its community of current and past fellows, which include 30 individuals across Europe, North America, Africa, Latin America and Australia and build relationships with other fellows programs. These fellows will be supported to disseminate and continue to build tools and resources for the sector. During the previous grant period, the grantee created six learning modules designed to help address digital issues that are core to the missions and activities of nonprofit organizations in the digital age. In creating and disseminating these tools, Stanford University’s Digital Civil Society Lab organized 14 learning events and workshops with more than 120 nonprofit representatives.

title: National Service and Volunteer Center Capacity Building
description: This grant to the United Way of Genesee County will provide additional capacity to support service throughout Genesee County. National service members and volunteers provide critical resources to area nonprofits, government agencies, and schools to help meet a variety of community needs such as blight elimination, neighborhood engagement, and tutoring and mentoring.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purposes support to PEAK Grantmaking, Inc. for its efforts to assist a nationwide networkof foundation grants managers. In this role, the grantee improves grantmaking by advancing the knowledge, skills, and abilities of grants managers and by leading grantmakers to adopt and incorporate effective practices that benefit the philanthropic community.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purposes support to PEAK Grantmaking for its efforts to assist a nationwide network of foundation grants managers. In this role, the grantee improves grantmaking by advancing the knowledge, skills and abilities of grants managers and by leading grantmakers to adopt and incorporate effective practices that benefit the philanthropic community.

title: Flint Cultural Center Academy
description: The Flint Cultural Center Foundation will construct a new building to house the Flint Cultural Center Academy. The Flint Cultural Center Academy is scheduled to open in the fall of 2019 with grades kindergarten through 5th. When fully implemented (2022), the school will serve approximately 650 kindergarten through 8th grade students primarily from Flint and Genesee County. The vision of the Flint Cultural Center Academy is to demonstrate a unique application of education that challenges and surpasses the existing norms of student achievement and learning growth, while addressing the development of the whole child.

title: TAP Network
description: The program goal is to support organized civil society participation to increase access to justice globally. The Transparency, Accountability, and Participation Network, a project of the Proteus Fund, will mobilize its membership of over 270 civil society organizations for coordinated action around implementation of Sustainable Development Goal 16, with its focus on peaceful, just, and inclusive societies. During the grant period, work will focus on 1) localization and capacity-building for network partners, 2) monitoring and accountability to assess Goal 16 progress, 3) global advocacy around Goal 16, and 4) reform of the Sustainable Development Goal review process. In 2018-2019, the grantee produced the Accountability Handbook, which underpinned 13 national workshops to improve reviews of Goal 16 progress. It hosted a series of side-events at the United Nations High-level Political Forum, which raised the profile of civil society actors, and orchestrated the civil society statement delivered at the official forum review. Founded in 1994, the Proteus Fund convenes and facilitates donor collaboratives that strategically focus philanthropic resources toward the realization of a just, equitable, and democratic world.

title: Data-Driven Progress for Access to Justice
description: The program goal is to produce new knowledge on legal needs globally. The World Justice Project will work to apply strategies that have increased the visibility, resources, and impact of other development areas to the field of justice. Its research and engagement agenda will use data and evidence as a means of diagnosing people’s most pressing justice needs, identifying the most successful programs that help people resolve their justice problems, mobilizing resources and political will to help people access justice, and designing justice reforms that measurably improve people’s lives. In 2018-2019, the grantee’s research on justice needs was central to establishing the case for “people-centered justice” as articulated by the Task Force on Justice and presented to the United Nations. The grantee also pushed successfully for a civil justice measure to assess progress in implementation of the United Nations target on access to justice. Established initially as a project of the American Bar Association in 2006, the World Justice Project was formally registered as an independent organization in 2009 working to advance the rule of law around the world.

title: Stronger Analysis for Progress on Access to Justice
description: The program goal is to produce new knowledge on legal needs globally. The World Justice Project will work to provide robust data and analysis of legal needs, the economic costs of access to justice and data collection and measurement in these areas. In addition, the grantee will develop a toolkit on civil justice indicators, to support wider efforts to measure access. The grantee will use the results of its research and analysis to advocate for more accessible, cost-effective and meaningful justice solutions, using events such as the World Justice Forum to showcase this work. In 2020-21, the grantee published “Global Insights on Access to Justice,” a comprehensive report on legal needs in 101 countries, providing comparable data to understand the magnitude and nuance of justice needs globally. Despite the pandemic, the grantee regularly convened partners to push forward on improving measurement of access to civil justice, following adoption of an official indicator for this under Sustainable Development Goal 16. Established initially as a project of the American Bar Association in 2006, the World Justice Project was formally registered as an independent organization in 2009, working to advance the rule of law around the world.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to increase access to justice in Ukraine through protection of fundamental rights and freedoms. Through its network of 29 member organizations, the Ukrainian Helsinki Human Rights Union will raise public awareness of the law and human rights through a range of monitoring, advocacy, and educational activities. It will provide legal information and services through its network of legal aid centers and will systematically examine opportunities for strengthening this network in the context of decentralization reforms. The grantee will conduct strategic litigation and advocacy on critical issues arising from cases brought to its attention. In 2017–2018, the grantee provided over 23,000 individual consultations through its legal aid centers. Additionally, it contributed to the development of a state policy on benefits in the wake of the conflict in the east of Ukraine. It successfully litigated a case at the European Court of Human Rights, which freed the possibility of agricultural land sales. Established in 2004, the Ukrainian Helsinki Human Rights Union works to promote practical observance of the range of international human rights instruments to which Ukraine is a party.

title: General Purposes
description: The Legal Aid Forum’s mission is to promote and support access to justice for all vulnerable groups of people in Rwanda. To this end, the grantee uses knowledge building, legal empowerment, human rights promotion, and institutional development as its core approaches. This grant will assist the grantee to strengthen its access to justice program through paralegal interventions, and reach more vulnerable people in all five provinces of Rwanda. The Legal Aid Forum was established in 2006 as a membership-based network of 38 national and international nongovernmental organizations, professional bodies, university legal aid clinics, and faith-based initiatives that support and/or provide legal aid services to people living in Rwanda.

title: General Purposes
description: The Paralegal Advisory Service Institute was established in 2007 to make justice accessible to all people in Malawi. By improving the efficiency and effectiveness of the justice system, the grantee aims to make the justice system responsive to the needs of all users, particularly the poor and vulnerable. They deploy trained paralegals to provide legal education, advice, and assistance in criminal justice processes. The grantee also promotes the work of the informal justice system by providing village mediation services as part of its civil justice approach. The grantee’s village mediation program complements both the formal and informal justice systems by resolving disputes at the early stages before they escalate. This grant will assist the Paralegal Advisory Service Institute to strengthen both its village mediation and criminal justice work, thereby increasing access to justice for poor and marginalized people in Malawi.

title: General Purposes
description: The project goal is to increase access to justice for poor and marginalized communities in Sierra Leone. To this end, Advocaid will work in several towns across Sierra Leone to ensure that women and girls receive free legal advice, fair legal representation, education on their rights, and social welfare support. Key interventions over the two year period will include providing legal services and education, social welfare services, and advocacy on access to justice for women. The grantee works with women and girls caught up in Sierra Leone’s often unjust legal system. It provides access to justice programs using paralegals and lawyers.

title: Strengthening the Legal Development Network's Member Organizations
description: The program goal is to increase community-based access to justice for the Ukrainian public. The Legal Development Network will work to strengthen and expand the current network of 25 community legal centers in Ukraine. Particular attention will be given to promoting the concept of community legal centers within the context of decentralization reforms, which involve the devolution of increased resources and authority for organizing public service to local administrations. The grantee will also update its online advisory resources, case management systems, and public information products to ensure more accurate information supporting both service delivery and advocacy strategies. Formally registered in 2015 and with its secretariat in Kyiv, the Legal Development Network has member organizations in 15 regions of Ukraine.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to cultivate a strong global movement for legal empowerment. Through the Global Legal Empowerment Network of over 1,500 organizations working in the field, Namati will develop and deliver a range of learning tools, peer exchanges, and knowledge resources. The grantee will advocate for greater investments in the field and will, where possible, channel funding and funders to critical geographic or thematic “anchor” partners within the network. The grantee will also undertake grassroots country-level programs in Kenya, Sierra Leone, Myanmar, India, Mozambique and, increasingly, within the United States focusing on specific issues such as land tenure, health rights, citizenship, and environmental justice. Finally, the grantee will develop and address a powerful learning agenda for the field. The grantee will seek to gather and disseminate critical evidence demonstrating how legal empowerment leads to substantive justice, thus addressing the challenge of Sustainable Development Goal 16, aimed at promoting peaceful, just, and inclusive societies. Established in 2011, Namati works to build a global movement of grassroots legal advocates who give people the power to understand, use, and shape the law.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Hague Institute for Innovation of Law
description: The program goal is to advance efforts to increase people-centered access to justice. With a mission to empower at least 150 million people who will be able to prevent or resolve their most pressing justice problems by 2030, The Hague Institute for Innovation of Law works to identify new ways of meeting people’s justice needs and transforming justice systems. The grantee will approach its work based on the core principle that effective interventions and programs require robust data on critical issues, including people’s justice needs, the impact of selected policies, the effect of innovative approaches to resolve issues, and the scalability of programs. With this grounding, The Hague Institute for Innovation of Law will undertake a series of justice needs and related research projects, foster and support justice innovations that broaden access, identify and collate effective access solutions, and undertake discrete systemic justice transformation efforts in targeted countries.

title: Flint Arts and Culture Capacity Building
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide funds to the Flint Cultural Center Corporation to hire technical assistance providers and consultants to maximize transparency and implementation of the new millage funding. Participating organizations will include Flint Cultural Center Corporation member organizations Sloan*Longway and The Whiting, Flint Institute of Arts, Flint Institute of Music, New McCree Theatre, Friends of Berston, and the Greater Flint Arts Council. The consultants will conduct an assessment of organizational needs and develop a subsequent plan for technical assistance and capacity building priorities for individual organizations and the collective group.

title: Mobilizing Social Assets for Productive Use of Renewable Energy in Rural Tanzania
description: There is an urgent need for data and research insights related to energy access solutions among off-grid last-mile communities in order to successfully achieve Sustainable Development Goal 7, universal access to modern energy services by 2030. The University of Michigan, a U.S.-based public research university, has collaborated over the past five years with St. John’s University of Tanzania to undertake longitudinal research aimed at improving strategies for the widespread use of solar energy services for better production among last-mile communities of rural Tanzania. Over the next two years, this project will enhance the sustainability and capacity of local partners to undertake long-term longitudinal monitoring of how village-based groups and institutions can advance the productive use of solar energy in rural Tanzania. The project also will build local capacity to accelerate data analysis and use of associated results to inform better decision-making among key stakeholders in Tanzania.

title: Curriculum, Technology, and Assessment Tools
description: With this grant, Flint Community Schools will provide students and teachers with a set of tools and resources to deliver instruction and assess academic progress. The grantee will purchase digital and paper curriculum and resources, provide student assessments, and service and update its technology platform for the use of digital curriculum across academic areas.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen the nonprofit sector in Michigan. To this end, the Michigan Nonprofit Association will continue its work in the areas of public policy, capacity building and civic engagement and education. During the previous grant period, the grantee carried out research and education initiatives on public policy issues; supported nonprofits in their efforts to become more diverse, equitable and inclusive; provided backend services such as information technology to nonprofits; and produced educational resources for the sector. During this grant period, the grantee will support civic engagement in communities; continue to carry out research and education initiatives on public policy issues; and provide leadership and support to nonprofits as they respond to current and emerging needs. Founded in 1992, the Michigan Nonprofit Association serves the nonprofit sector statewide by providing information and access to resources that can assist organizations in operating effectively, fulfilling their missions and efficiently meeting community needs.

title: General Purposes
description: This renewal grant will support the Michigan Nonprofit Association in its efforts to continue its work in the areas of civic and community engagement, public policy and nonprofit leadership. During the previous grant period, the grantee advocated on behalf of its members, completed the Nonprofit Leadership Census, started a Community Conversations series for BIPOC leaders and launched a redistricting project. During this grant period, the grantee will advocate on behalf of the nonprofit sector, engage with communities and develop sector leadership. Founded in 1992, the Michigan Nonprofit Association serves the nonprofit sector statewide by providing information and access to resources that can assist organizations in operating effectively, fulfilling their missions and efficiently meeting community needs.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support the Michigan Nonprofit Association in its efforts to continue its work in the areas of civic and community engagement, public policy and nonprofit leadership. During the previous grant period, the grantee advocated on behalf of its 650 members, awarded $35 million to nearly 2,000 nonprofits through the Michigan Nonprofit Relief Fund and promoted nonprofit trust in the We Are 501c3 initiative. During this grant period, the grantee will continue to advocate on behalf of the nonprofit sector, engage with communities and develop sector leadership. Founded in 1992, the Michigan Nonprofit Association serves the nonprofit sector statewide by providing information and access to resources that can assist organizations in operating effectively, fulfilling their missions and efficiently meeting community needs.

title: Nonprofit Policy and Research Project
description: The project goal is to advance the nonprofit sector’s policy development and advocacy capacity. The Nonprofit Quarterly, whose mission is to promote active democracy and a thriving civil society, is one of the leading publications serving the nonprofit sector in the United States. The grantee aims to build a practice of elucidating policy options and positions in a manner that addresses not only institutional perspectives but those of the communities served by nonprofits and civil society more broadly. Specific activities include: 1) investigating policy proposals affecting nonprofits and philanthropy; 2) producing traditional and new media products that inform the sector; and 3) developing and maintaining partnerships with philanthropic and nonprofit institutions and networks. The Nonprofit Quarterly was launched in late 1999 as a publication of Third Sector New England, and in 2006, it became an independent publication.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to increase the awareness, understanding, and engagement of the nonprofit and philanthropic sector with respect to digital policies and practices that impact the space for civic engagement. To this end, Access Now, a nonprofit registered in the United States and working globally, will empower and support nonprofits and other civil society actors through direct technical support, comprehensive policy engagement, advocacy, grassroots grantmaking, and convenings. Key outcomes and activities over the coming two years will include building and extending nonprofit coalitions and partnerships to address important digital policies and practices, such as internet shutdowns and disruptions; advocating for civil society-friendly frameworks to underpin the ongoing explosion of new technologies and innovation; and organizing RightsCon, the premier annual networking and learning event on digital policies, practices, and cutting-edge technological developments. Based in New York City, Access Now is a leading global resource and advocate for digital policies that impact individual users and civil society organizations.

title: Helping Young People to Employment Program
description: This grant will support the Helping Young People to Employment Program. The program is managed by Faith Foundation Resources, a nonprofit dedicated to working with low-income and at-risk individuals to help better their lives. The goal of the project is to prepare youth aged 16-24 for work. Young people learn about job training and career skills needed to become productive and responsible members of society. Courses focus on job readiness, learning the fundamentals of interpersonal skills, and financial literacy. After completion of an eight-week training program, youth are eligible to be placed into 20 to 30 hours of after school employment. Metro Community Development, a long-time Foundation grantee, will serve as a fiduciary for Faith Foundation Resources.

title: Advancing the Children's Savings Account Field
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant will continue support for Prosperity Now’s children’s saving account endeavors to expand the children’s savings account field through championing efforts to strengthen and sustain children’s savings account programs. In partnership with the Foundation, the grantee has contributed to significant growth in the field. As the world faces an economic crisis brought about by the COVID-19 pandemic along with the hits to state and local budgets, the children’s savings account field is also threatened. As children’s savings account programs must deal with the recent economic crises, Prosperity Now is preparing to aid the field in maintaining its progressive momentum post-pandemic.

title: Expanding CSAs for Educational Success and Lifelong Asset Building
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant provides continuing support for Washington University’s research, communications, policy development and technical assistance efforts aimed at advancing children’s savings account strategies at the state and national levels. In the short term, the grantee’s goal is to expand opportunities for all families to save for their children’s education, and in doing so, increase postsecondary education aspirations, access and completion rates, particularly among low-to moderate-income students. Long term, the grantee views children’s savings accounts as the initial phase of a broader effort to embed inclusive and lifelong asset-building opportunities into the fabric of domestic social policy in ways that support educational and financial security goals.

title: Flint Food Works Commercial Kitchen
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will support the continued development of the Flint Food Works commercial kitchen food business incubator located within the Flint Farmers’ Market. Flint Food Works has the capacity to incubate small food processors seeking to create nutritional products for distribution and prepared food for retail consumption. The grantee offers a unique community benefit by providing nutritional education to residents on how to prepare healthy food that will mitigate the effects of lead. The project is managed by the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation’s supported organization, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation.

title: General Purposes
description: The Council on Foundations is a national membership organization that currently represents 700 private foundations, community foundations, and corporate funders. Its mission is to provide the opportunity, leadership, and tools needed by philanthropic organizations to expand, enhance, and sustain their ability to advance the common good. The grantee’s top-level organizational goals are to amplify the work of philanthropy, advocate for philanthropy, and strengthen the philanthropic sector. Additional funding is needed for the grantee to balance its budget and to undergo a leadership transition in 2019. The grantee will also create a Dues Model Task force to re-examine all aspects of membership with an overarching near-term goal of increasing membership to 800 by January 1, 2020. In the longer term, the grantee will seek to grow its membership in order to enhance its legitimacy to represent the philanthropic sector in the United States and to ensure its financial sustainability.

title: Electricity Residential Ratepayer Policy Scan
description: The Utility Consumer Participation Board, a unit of state government, provides grants to qualified applicants that represent the interests of Michigan’s residential energy utility customers at proceedings before the Michigan Public Services Commission. With this grant, the Institute of Public Utilities at Michigan State University will undertake a research project that assesses the past impact of the board’s grantmaking, identifies current and emerging issues affecting residential ratepayers, and discusses future opportunities that would benefit residential ratepayers.

title: Pathfinders for Peaceful, Just and Inclusive Societies: Civil Society Participation & Voice
description: The program goal is to ensure accelerated implementation of access to justice goals under Sustainable Development Goal 16. The Pathfinders for Peaceful, Just and Inclusive Societies, a program of New York University, is a multi-stakeholder platform, convened by the governments of Brazil, Sierra Leone, Switzerland, and the New York University’s Center on International Cooperation. In 2018-19, through its Task Force on Justice, the grantee brought together government and civil society justice actors in a series of international convenings to advance a people-centered justice agenda. The grantee produced a series of background research reports outlining justice data collection strategies, pathways to justice reform, and cost for justice action. These culminated in the release of the Justice for All report in May 2019, which outlined strategies for addressing the “justice gap”—the five billion people worldwide without meaningful access to justice. In 2020-21, the grantee will build on this activity in three priority areas: working with national governments to accelerate implementation of Access to Justice strategies; engaging international and multi-lateral institutions and cross-sectoral partnerships to advance justice; and fostering an effective campaign for justice at international, national, and local levels.

title: Pathfinders for Peaceful, Just and Inclusive Societies: Civil Society Participation & Voice
description: The Pathfinders for Peaceful, Just and Inclusive Societies, a program of New York University, is a multi-stakeholder platform that seeks to promote solutions to overcome the lack of access to global justice. In 2020-21, the grantee produced a series of policy briefs on people-centered justice responses during the COVID-19 pandemic. They actively promoted people-centered justice through publication of a “Shared Strategy for Justice for All”, as well as through numerous convenings, including “the Global Week of Justice”. They also organized a first-of-its-kind national consultation on developing a people-centered justice reform strategy in Ukraine. In 2022-23, the grantee will continue their justice work in cooperation with the Justice Action Coalition, a multi-stakeholder coalition of countries and organizations championing equal access to justice for all. Their efforts will focus on three priority areas: 1) working with national governments to accelerate implementation of access to justice strategies in advance of the 2023 United Nations High-Level Political Forum; 2) engaging international and multi-lateral institutions and cross-sectoral partnerships to advance justice; and 3) fostering an effective initiative for justice at international, national and local levels.

title: Fiscal Solvency and Service Effectiveness Project
description: This grant continues support for Michigan State University’s efforts to document and promote solutions that help America’s older industrial cities address chronic fiscal stress. During the renewal grant period, the grantee will develop a range of potential scenarios for addressing structural deficits and assess the feasibility of each scenario with a particular focus on legal and political implications. The City of Flint and Flint Community Schools will remain a focus for the planned research activities, as well as a beneficiary of technical assistance efforts.

title: Western Balkans Community Foundations
geographic_focus: Serbia, North Macedonia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, Albania, Kosovo
description: The program goal is to expand and strengthen the community foundation field in the Western Balkans region. To this end, the Trag Foundation, a long-term Mott grantee based in Serbia, will work in Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Macedonia, Montenegro, and Serbia to increase the number of community foundations in the region. More specifically, the grantee will conduct feasibility studies in target countries, promote the concept and practice of community foundations, facilitate the establishment of new community foundations, and develop their capacities. In addition, the grantee will connect the new community foundations to existing networks and initiatives, including the European Community Foundation Initiative. Since its establishment in 1999, the grantee has provided over $13 million in grants to nonprofits in Serbia and the Western Balkans region and has established itself as a leading organization in the fields of philanthropy, civil society, and community development.

title: State Fiscal and Low-Income Initiatives Project
grantee: Center on Budget and Policy Priorities
description: This grant provides ongoing support to the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities for the State Fiscal and Low-Income Initiatives Project. Through this project, the grantee works to expand economic opportunity and fight poverty by ensuring that federal and state governments have adequate resources to meet basic needs and invest in good schools, childcare, quality health care and other priorities. To accomplish these goals, the grantee will: 1) monitor policy and budgetary changes to the social safety net; 2) prepare policy briefs and analyses of budget and fiscal policies; 3) facilitate networking and coordination at the state and local levels for low-income advocates; and 4) provide strategic and technical assistance to state and local policymakers, program administrators and nonprofit organizations working on policy and program issues affecting low-income families. Located in Washington, D.C., the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities is one of the premier policy research institutions in the United States.

title: Michigan Communities for Financial Empowerment Network
grantee: Community Economic Development Association of Michigan
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: The Community Economic Development Association of Michigan works to expand and strengthen financial security in communities across the state. During the grant period, the grantee will develop a children’s savings account policy framework, which will outline state-supported resources and infrastructure to promote the expansion of community-driven children’s savings account programs. The framework will draw upon lessons learned and promising practices in other states to help accelerate success. Based in Lansing, the Community Economic Development Association of Michigan is a nonprofit trade association serving community economic development professionals in Michigan.

title: Operating Support
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Flint Institute of Arts serves over 165,000 people through programs and visits each year. In 2018 the grantee added a contemporary craft wing and a hot glass studio and foundry, which includes a demonstration space for public viewing and state of the art equipment for glassmaking. This grant increase will ensure positive cash flow for operations until funding from the millage is received.

title: Metropolitan Policy Program
description: The Metropolitan Policy Program at Brookings Institution, an internationally known think tank, works with local communities to assist in the development and strategy for retooling the American economy. With continuing support, the grantee will undertake a range of work to promote the economic competitiveness of metropolitan areas domestically and globally, including older industrial cities such as Flint. Activities will include original research, policy advocacy, analytical tool development, and network building.

title: Genesee Youth Entrepreneurship Network
description: The Genesee Intermediate School District provides educational leadership that impacts instruction, learning, student achievement, productivity and efficiency. The organization serves nearly 70,000 students and 8,500 educators across the county. This grant will enable the grantee to continue the development and expansion of the Genesee Youth Entrepreneurship Network. The primary objectives are to expand the number of entrepreneurship programs for youth and increase the number of students who participate in entrepreneurship programs and experiences. The countywide project will help motivate all 21 high schools to engage students in grades 9 to 12 in entrepreneurship.

title: Neighborhood Arts and Cultural Events
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will support arts and culture projects through the Neighborhood Small Grants Program at the Community Foundation of Greater Flint. Neighborhood groups will implement resident-led efforts to create or enhance and expand existing artistic projects or events/performances. Funded projects will aim to stimulate civic engagement, improve neighborhood conditions, provide opportunities for self-expression, and/or enhance skills for residents to work together creatively.

title: Access to Justice Project
grantee: Catholic Commission for Justice and Peace of the Archdiocese of Lilongwe
description: The project goal is to increase and strengthen access to justice for people living in rural communities and under tribal authorities in Malawi. To this end, the Catholic Commission for Justice and Peace of the Archdiocese of Lilongwe will use a human rights and constitutional approach to expand its access to justice program to people living in rural communities in Malawi. Key interventions over the two-year period will include capacity building of village tribunals and community-based educators, awareness raising on gender-related legal instruments, enhancing coordination between formal and informal institutions, and engaging media. The grantee is one of the six commissions in the Archdiocese that aims to create a just and peaceful Malawian society. Although it is under the umbrella of the Archdiocese of Lilongwe, its mission goes beyond the institutional church boundaries and is nonpolitical and nonethnic.

title: Downtown Flint Property Acquisition and Stabilization
description: Communities First, Inc., seeks to acquire and manage the Flint Masonic Temple in order to preserve this historic community asset and spur economic activity in downtown Flint. With enhancements, the facility can offer community entertainment opportunities as well as support for small businesses.

title: Monitoring Environmental Impacts of Financial Flows for Infrastructure and Energy in South America
description: Ecoa-Ecology and Action is a science-driven nongovernmental organization working to strengthen social and environmental standards of public investment in energy and infrastructure in South America. Over the previous project period, the grantee worked on social and environmental safeguards review at the Inter-American Development Bank, monitored Chinese and Brazilian development finance and focused on social and environmental governance of emblematic energy and infrastructure, including the completion of the strategic environmental assessment of 144 hydroelectric projects in the Upper Paraguay basin. This grant renewal will continue work on monitoring investments in energy and infrastructure and emblematic projects, such as hydroelectric and hydroway expansion in the region.

title: South America Small Grants Program
description: The Socio-Environmental Fund CASA is a grantmaking and capacity-building organization focused on providing small grants to strengthen community, environmental and civil society organizations. Over the past grant period, the grantee made 37 small grants in 13 Brazilian states, with most going to the greater Amazon region. This grant will renew support for the South America Small Grants Program to support local communities and groups working on issues of energy infrastructure and sustainable finance in Brazil.

title: Building Community Foundations Capacity to Act on SDGs
description: The project goal is to increase the contribution of community foundations in Canada and globally to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. To this end, Community Foundations of Canada will create relevant learning content, build the capacity of Canadian community foundations to contribute to the United Nations goals, and share Canadian best practices globally.
