In addition, the grantee will leverage additional funds from public and private sources to increase the support available to community foundations for engaging with the United Nations goals. The grantee was established in 1992 as a network of 28 community foundations. Currently, the network includes 191 community foundations with $5.6 billion in combined assets. The grantee provides information, technical assistance, and networking opportunities to its members. Also, the grantee represents the Canadian community foundation field on the national and international levels and works across the civil society, business, and public sectors to boost efforts for building inclusive and sustainable communities.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides renewal support to the Council of Michigan Foundations as it continues to pivot to a new “Equity at the Center” strategic approach. During the previous grant period, the grantee hosted networking events, advocated on behalf of the sector, revamped its youth programs and hosted the Great Lakes Funder Collaborative. During this upcoming grant period, the grantee will continue to advocate on behalf of the sector, improve its member relations, continue to host the Great Lakes Funder Collaborative and develop its Leadership Fund. The Council of Michigan Foundations is a statewide association of over 300 grantmakers that provides its members with educational programs, technical assistance, networking opportunities, advocacy with policymakers and regulators and collaborative work with leading national and regional philanthropic associations.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purposes support to the Council of Michigan Foundations. During the previous grant period, the grantee hosted networking events, advocated on behalf of the sector, revamped its youth programs and hosted the Great Lakes Funder Collaborative. During this upcoming grant period, the grantee will continue to advocate on behalf of the sector, improve its member relations, continue to host the Great Lakes Funder Collaborative and develop responsive policy priorities. The Council of Michigan Foundations is a statewide association of nearly 300 grantmakers that provides its members with: 1) educational programs; 2) technical assistance; 3) networking opportunities; 4) advocacy with policymakers and regulators; and 5) collaborative work with leading national and regional philanthropic associations.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides renewal support to the Council on Foundations, a national philanthropic organization founded in 1949 that currently represents 796 members. The grantee’s mission is to foster an environment where philanthropy can thrive and cultivate a community of diverse and skilled philanthropic professionals and organizations who lead with integrity, serve as ethical stewards and advocate for progress. Notable activities during 2021 included: 1) hosting three large-scale convenings; 2) serving 47 mid-to-senior-level professionals through its Career Pathways leadership program; 3) adding ten new communities to its peer learning online platform, Philanthropy Exchange; and 4) continued advocacy for the sector by regularly communicating with congressional offices and federal agencies. In 2022, the grantee will focus on five key organizational goals: 1) embracing better ways of operating; 2) expanding philanthropy’s opportunities to thrive; 3) building common ground; 4) putting trust at the center of its work; and 5) developing a learning mindset.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to Independent Sector, a national membership organization that brings together a diverse community of changemakers at nonprofits, foundations and corporate giving programs working to strengthen civil society and ensure all people in the United States thrive. In the past year, the grantee has: 1) launched an important research compendium and benchmarking tool, The Health of the Nonprofit Sector; 2) co-created the National Infrastructure Investment Advocacy Group; and 3) engaged thousands of nonprofit and philanthropic leaders in its events. Over the next two years the grantee will focus on sector impact, community building and public policy to enhance health and equity in American civil society. Founded in 1980, Independent Sector currently has 495 organizational members and advances its mission by fostering a sense of belonging, catalyzing action and providing policy leadership across the full breadth of the charitable sector.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to Independent Sector, a national membership organization which brings together a diverse community of changemakers at nonprofits, foundations and corporate giving programs working to strengthen civil society and ensure all people in the United States thrive. In the past two years, the grantee has: 1) released its second annual “Health of the U.S. Nonprofit Sector” report; 2) engaged more than 3,000 people through Upswell Pop-Ups, Upswell Exchanges and the 2021 Upswell Summit; and 3) proposed and advocated for the “Seat at the Table” initiative. Over the next two years, the grantee will focus on sector health, community building and public policy. Founded in 1980, Independent Sector currently has 453 organizational members and advances its mission by fostering a sense of belonging, catalyzing action and providing policy leadership across the full breadth of the charitable sector.

title: General Purposes
description: Established in 1990, the National Council of Nonprofits is the nation’s largest network of nonprofits, representing more than 28,000 organizations across the country. The grantee’s mission is to advance the vital role, capacity and voice of charitable nonprofit organizations. The grantee works through its network of state associations and nonprofit partners to help nonprofits operate more effectively, engage in critical policy issues affecting the sector and achieve greater impact in their communities. During the past year, the grantee strengthened its network by providing knowledge support on operational matters that were especially needed during the pandemic. Over the next two years, the National Council of Nonprofits will: 1) carry out educational initiatives to promote a supportive policy environment for the work of charitable nonprofits; 2) expand its network and deepen the engagement of its members; and 3) provide trusted information to nonprofits, the media and the public.

title: General Purposes
description: Established in 1990, the National Council of Nonprofits is the nation’s largest network of nonprofits, representing more than 28,000 organizations across the country. The grantee’s mission is to advance the vital role, capacity and voice of charitable nonprofit organizations. The grantee works through its network of state associations and nonprofit partners to help nonprofits operate more effectively, engage in critical policy issues affecting the sector and achieve greater impact in their communities. During the previous grant period, the grantee championed, informed and connected the nonprofit sector. During the next grant period, the National Council of Nonprofits will focus on policy advocacy, member support, media outreach and narrative building.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will allow the Puerto Rico Funders Network to continue its mission to strengthen philanthropy and the nonprofit sector in Puerto Rico. A current high priority for the network is to improve and expand Puerto Rico’s philanthropy infrastructure as the commonwealth continues its recovery efforts following Hurricanes Irma and Maria. During this grant period, the grantee will continue to support collaborative efforts among foundations and community-based organizations, enhance the capacity of community-based organizations, advocate for policy alternatives to promote the resilience of organizations serving vulnerable groups, and engage more philanthropic actors in effective responses to Puerto Rico’s recovery. Established in 2009 by seven leading foundations, the grantee exists to enhance the ability of philanthropy and nonprofit organizations to improve the lives of vulnerable populations.

title: General Purposes
description: The project goal is to strengthen the philanthropic and nonprofit sector in Puerto Rico. To this end, Philanthropy Puerto Rico supports, educates and helps strengthen its members, grantees and the sector broadly. During the previous grant period, the grantee advocated on behalf of the nonprofit sector, convened and educated the sector and provided support to nonprofits. During this grant period, the grantee will expand its membership, inform and connect its network and support nonprofits through the Forward Fund. Established in 2009 by seven leading foundations, Philanthropy Puerto Rico exists to enhance the ability of philanthropy and nonprofit organizations to improve the lives of vulnerable populations.

title: General Purposes
description: Philanthropy Puerto Rico supports, educates and helps strengthen its members, grantees and the philanthropic and nonprofit sectors broadly. During the previous grant period, the grantee grew its membership, hosted convenings and learning events and hosted philanthropic initiatives. During this grant period, the grantee will focus on data generation and collection, philanthropy engagement in Puerto Rico and providing its members with support. Established in 2009 by seven leading foundations, Philanthropy Puerto Rico has grown to 19 members and exists to enhance the ability of philanthropy and nonprofit organizations to improve the lives of vulnerable populations.

title: General Purposes
description: Philanthropy Puerto Rico supports, educates and helps strengthen its members, grantees and the philanthropic and nonprofit sectors broadly. During the previous grant period, the grantee grew its membership, organized convenings and learning events and hosted philanthropic initiatives. During this grant period, the grantee will focus on data generation and collection, philanthropy engagement in Puerto Rico and providing its members with support. Established in 2009 by seven leading foundations, Philanthropy Puerto Rico has grown to 23 members and exists to enhance the ability of philanthropy and nonprofit organizations to improve the lives of vulnerable populations.

title: General Purposes
description: The project goal is to enhance the capacity and knowledge of philanthropic networks. In 2020-2021, the United Philanthropy Forum advocated on behalf of the nonprofit and philanthropic sector, partnered and collaborated with other infrastructure organizations in responding to COVID-19, worked to advance racial equity and assisted in developing the capacity of nonprofit organizations. In 2022-2023, the grantee will continue to lead a vibrant network; maximize the individual and collective capacity and impact of its members; and provide learning, knowledge and resources to its members. Formed in 1998 as the Forum of Regional Associations of Grantmakers, the United Philanthropy Forum is a national network of associations of grantmakers. Its current members are 89 philanthropy-serving organizations across the United States that represent more than 7,000 foundations and other philanthropic organizations.

title: General Purposes
grantee: CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation
description: Established in 1993, CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation, is a growing international alliance of more than 12,000 members in 175 countries. The grantee’s mission is to strengthen civil society and citizen participation throughout the world, especially in areas where participatory democracy and citizens’ freedom of association are challenged. Recent accomplishments include releasing annual State of Civil Society reports and maintaining the CIVICUS Monitor — a research tool to share reliable, timely data and analysis on civic space and publishing a special report entitled “Solidarity in the Time of COVID-19.” During the grant period, the grantee’s work will focus on defending civic freedoms and democratic values; strengthening the power of people to organize, mobilize and take action; and empowering a more accountable, effective and innovative civil society. The grantee’s main office is in Johannesburg, South Africa.

title: General Purposes
grantee: CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation
description: Established in 1993, CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation, is a growing international alliance of more than 15,000 members in 188 countries. The grantee’s mission is to strengthen civil society and citizen participation throughout the world, especially in areas where participatory democracy and citizens’ freedom of association are challenged. Recent accomplishments include releasing annual State of Civil Society reports and maintaining the CIVICUS Monitor — a research tool used for sharing reliable, timely data and analysis on civic space, connecting and supporting civil society actors through events and joint initiatives and developing a strategic plan for 2022-2027. During the grant period, the grantee’s work will focus on defending civic freedoms and democratic values; strengthening the power of people to organize, mobilize and take action; and empowering a more accountable, effective and innovative civil society. CIVICUS’ main office is in Johannesburg, South Africa.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will assist with building and strengthening an enabling environment for philanthropy in Europe. Philea is an independent membership association of foundations and philanthropic networks that provides intellectual leadership on emerging policy agendas and societal trends that impact institutional philanthropy while fostering connections within philanthropy by utilizing external actors through convenings and events. The grantee supports an enabling environment for philanthropy at the European level. Established in 1989 by seven of Europe’s leading foundations, the grantee was previously known as the European Foundation Centre. In 2022, the European Foundation Centre and the Donors and Foundations Networks of Europe combined to strenghhten the voice of the sector and became Philea. Philea serves a core membership of over 270 members and is based in Brussels.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will assist with building and strengthening an enabling environment for philanthropy in Europe. PHILEA is an independent membership association of foundations and philanthropic networks that provides intellectual leadership on emerging policy agendas and societal trends that impact institutional philanthropy while fostering connections within philanthropy by utilizing external actors through convenings and events. The grantee supports an enabling environment for philanthropy at the European level. Established in 1989 by seven of Europe’s leading foundations, the grantee was previously known as the European Foundation Centre. In 2022, the European Foundation Centre and the Donors and Foundations Networks of Europe combined to strengthen the voice of the sector and became PHILEA. PHILEA serves a core membership of over 320 members and is based in Brussels.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Independent Philanthropy Association of South Africa
description: The project goal is to support domestic philanthropy infrastructure in South Africa. To this end, the grantee will continue to grow its network of philanthropic members in South Africa, influence and learn from a wide network of relationships, advance knowledge and improve philanthropic practice, develop and execute a communications and marketing strategy, and implement a funding strategy in order to meet its goals. Past support helped the Independent Philanthropy Association of South Africa to increase its membership, organize journal club meetings in philanthropic practice, and host a number of in-person, hybrid and virtual convenings on various thematic issues for philanthropic interest. The grantee was established in 2015 as a voluntary association and network to represent and promote the common interests, concerns and objectives of its members.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Independent Philanthropy Association of South Africa
description: This grant provides general purposes funding to an organization that supports philanthropy infrastructure in South Africa. To this end, Independent Philanthropy Association of South Africa will: 1) continue to grow its network of philanthropic members in South Africa; 2) influence and learn from a wide network of relationships; 3) advance knowledge and improve philanthropic practice; 4) develop and execute a communications and marketing strategy; and 5) implement a funding strategy in order to meet its goals. Past support helped the grantee to increase its offering to philanthropic foundations, produce new knowledge on giving, increase its members and grow its institution. Established in 2015 as a voluntary association and network to represent and promote the common interests, concerns and objectives of its philanthropic members.

title: General Purposes
description: The African Philanthropy Forum was established in 2014 as an affiliate of the Global Philanthropy Forum. In 2017, the African Philanthropy Forum became an independent entity and continues to affiliate with the Global Philanthropy Forum. The goal of the grantee is to build a learning community of African philanthropists and social investors committed to inclusive and sustainable development throughout the continent. Through its annual conferences, the grantee has created platforms for current and emerging philanthropists to interact, learn, and share best practices to increase the impact of their work. Since its inception, the grantee has reached over 1400 philanthropists and social investors on the continent and has members in Cameroon, Egypt, Ethiopia, Ghana, Kenya, Morocco, Nigeria, Rwanda, South Africa, Tanzania, and Uganda. During this grant period, the grantee will: 1) create platforms that provide information on the state of philanthropy and social investment on the continent; 2) connect philanthropists and social investors to causes that address major challenges; and 3) expand the tools that members can access to enhance the effectiveness, efficiency, impact, and scale of their interventions.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to strengthen philanthropy by building a learning community of strategic African philanthropists and social investors committed to inclusive development in Africa. To this end, the African Philanthropy Forum will support efforts to respond to systemic issues on the continent, convene members to build a strong community of practice and provide practical tools to enhance their giving. In addition, the grantee will continue to grow its membership, produce and disseminate new knowledge on philanthropy in the continent and improve its member database. To date, the grantee has reached over 2,500 philanthropists and social investors from 14 countries across Africa. Past support enabled the African Philanthropy Forum to increase membership, build platforms that provide useful information to members, host conferences and other learning events, and conduct research that benefits the sector.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide renewal support to the African Philanthropy Forum whose goal is to strengthen philanthropy in Africa by building a community of strategic philanthropists and social investors committed to learning and advancing inclusive development. To achieve this goal, the grantee plans to: 1) support collaborative efforts that respond to systemic challenges in Africa; 2) promote strategic philanthropy as an approach to resource development in African countries; 3) convene members to build a strong community of practice; 4) provide practical tools to enhance members’ giving practices; and 5) generate knowledge that benefits the sector and its members. To date, the grantee has impacted the work of over 3,500 philanthropists and social investors across 14 countries in Africa. Past support has enabled the grantee to host in-person events in several countries, conduct research that benefits members and the sector, launch a platform that connects members to worthy causes in their countries and across Africa and partner with other like-minded organizations on areas of common interest to deepen philanthropy in Africa. The African Philanthropy Forum is based in Lagos, Nigeria.

title: General Purposes
description: The goal of the African Philanthropy Forum is to strengthen philanthropy in Africa by building a community of partners who, through their strategic giving, investments and influence, foster shared prosperity on the African continent. Past support has enabled the grantee to convene high-net-worth individuals, corporate funders and social investors to explore ways to respond effectively to regional issues. In addition, the grantee has expanded membership to the Middle East and North Africa region, contributed to thought leadership and research on philanthropy in Africa and partnered with other like-minded organizations to strengthen the philanthropy ecosystem in Africa. Over the next two years, the grantee will cultivate the next generation of African philanthropists, diaspora givers and corporate giving to increase the flow of resources and support to proximate organizations responding to immediate and long-term needs in communities. The grantee will leverage technology to unlock funding for nonprofits through an online platform that connects organizations to funders. The African Philanthropy Forum is based in Lagos, Nigeria.

title: General Purposes
description: The East Africa Philanthropy Network was established in 2003 to support the growth and development of philanthropy in East Africa. The grantee connects various philanthropic organizations in the region to build the philanthropy and civil society sectors. Significant achievements include establishing and supporting national forums in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda; hosting an annual regional conference that brings together business, government and civil society; and connecting the East Africa region to the global philanthropy ecosystem. In addition, the grantee has championed efforts to collect data that demonstrates the levels of giving in the region. This grant will enable the East Africa Philanthropy Network to deepen its work with national forums, produce knowledge to enhance the work of members and continue to connect the region to the global philanthropy sector.

title: General Purposes
description: The aim of the project is to promote the growth and development of philanthropy in East Africa by connecting various philanthropic organizations in the region. Established in 2003, the East Africa Philanthropy Network brings together foundations, trusts and other philanthropic organizations to strengthen their work and build a community of practice. Past support enabled the grantee to coordinate its members’ efforts in response to COVID-19, host learning workshops in response to the capacity building needs identified by members, and build a data portal to provide comprehensive data about the state of philanthropy in the region. This grant will enable the East Africa Philanthropy Network to support national forums, continue to generate data on the state of philanthropy in the region, and create platforms for networking and knowledge sharing for its members.

title: General Purposes
description: The goal of East Africa Philanthropy Network is to promote the growth and development of philanthropy in East Africa by connecting various philanthropic organizations in the region and promoting an enabling environment for philanthropy. Established in 2003, the organization brings together foundations, trusts and other philanthropic organizations to build a community of practice, promote learning, and deepen their work in the region. To achieve this, the grantee hosts learning events, produces research and supports regional forums. Previous support from the Mott Foundation enabled the grantee to convene members to discuss topical issues and champion causes that strengthened the sector. During this grant period, the East Africa Philanthropy Network will continue to: 1) generate knowledge and promote learning; 2) support the members’ collaboration efforts; 3) lead initiatives that protect and strengthen civic space in the region; and 4) build the secretariat’s capacity to respond effectively to the growing needs of its members.

title: General Purposes
description: The goal of East Africa Philanthropy Network is to support the growth of the philanthropy ecosystem in East Africa by connecting various philanthropic organizations in the region and promoting an enabling environment for philanthropy. Established in 2003 to bring together foundations, trusts and other philanthropic organizations to build communities of practice, advance learning and support the growth of professionalized philanthropy in the region. To achieve this, the grantee convenes members, produces research that expands knowledge in the sector and provides thought leadership on policies that enhance philanthropy. Previous support from the Mott Foundation enabled the grantee to continue to produce research, convene the sector and champion causes that advance philanthropy in the region. This grant will enable East Africa Philanthropy Network to: 1) conduct research on topics relevant to its members; 2) convene members to discuss sector-specific and field-wide topics; 3) lead initiatives that protect and strengthen civic space in the region; and 4) raise the profile of the sector in the region and globally.

title: Affinity Group of National Associations
grantee: CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation
description: The program goal is to strengthen the capacity of national and regional associations of civil society organizations globally. The Affinity Group of National Associations, a network which currently has 86 members from around the world, is managed by CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation. Over the past three years, the grantee has strengthened the coordination team for the affinity group, increased engagement of members, revised and reviewed membership criteria, built capacity among members to work with social movements and new forms of civic engagement, facilitated peer-to-peer learning among members on a range of issues and practice areas, and better aligned the affinity group’s work with the grantee’s initiatives. During the grant period, the grantee will increase members’ ability to amplify the voices of their constituencies and partners, strengthen the capacity of members to act as national and regional secretariats, and broaden collaboration and alliances across the membership around key civic space issues. CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation is an international alliance established in 1993 to strengthen citizen action and civil society worldwide.

title: Affinity Group of National Associations
grantee: CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation
description: The program goal is to strengthen the capacity of national and regional associations of civil society organizations globally. The Affinity Group of National Associations, a network that currently has 88 members from around the world, is managed by CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation. The affinity group is one of the most active networks within the grantee’s alliance. Over the past three years, the grantee has strengthened the affinity group members through training, regional meetings and networking opportunities. During the grant period, the grantee will build the expertise and voice of members as key actors for the expansion of civic space, create new partnerships and alliances among members on civic space issues, help members develop sustainability strategies and improve the affinity group’s governance and accountability. CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation is an international alliance established in 1993 to strengthen citizen action and civil society worldwide.

title: General Purposes
description: The Council of Michigan Foundations is a statewide association of 300 grantmakers that provides its members with educational programs, technical assistance, networking opportunities, advocacy with policymakers and regulators, and collaborative work with leading national and regional philanthropic associations. During 2017-2019, the grantee will pursue eight strategies: 1) engaging members where they want to be; 2) strategically recruiting new members; 3) connecting members to the assistance they need; 4) conducting active internal evaluation and assessment; 5) growing the sector’s collective voice in public policy; 6) expanding diversity, equity, and inclusion of the sector; 7) nurturing mission-aligned social enterprise opportunities; and 8) achieving organizational effectiveness. Additional funds are needed for the general purposes of the organization, including the education of decision-makers on the impact of the (December 2017) Tax Cuts and Jobs Act.

title: Energy Distributed to Isolated Communities
description: Instituto Socioambiental supports efforts to promote distributed renewable energy access solutions for isolated Amazon communities in Brazil and to overcome barriers to the expansion of clean energy in isolated communities. This grant increase will support the grantee to promote and host attendees at the Community Energy Fair in 2019, and build a budget and proposal for 100 percent solarization of the village of Tamandua in the Raposa Serra do Sul indigenous territory in the Brazilian Amazon state of Roraima.

title: Bachelor of Paralegal Studies and Community Based Paralegals
description: The Cape Peninsula University of Technology launched its bachelor’s degree in paralegal studies in 2017. This degree provides structured, accredited training to people who would like to become paralegals in South Africa. It is the only degree of its kind in South Africa. The project goal is to ensure that community-based paralegals can also benefit from this degree. Past support allowed the grantee to conduct a survey among community-based paralegals to scientifically gauge their formal and informal academic qualifications. The grantee assembled a task team to lead this survey, appointed a field survey company, completed a literature review, identified the target population, and drafted its findings in a report. Ongoing support will allow the grantee to use these findings to draft an appropriate “Recognition of Prior Learning” instrument, workshop it with community-based paralegals, identify the correct mode of delivery, and get further buy-in from community-based paralegals.

title: Membership and Administrative Support
description: This grant supports the membership and administrative costs of the Network of European Foundations, a nonprofit membership association based in Brussels. The grantee’s goal is to strengthen philanthropic cooperation among foundations, associations and other nongovernmental organizations in Europe. In 2020, the grantee managed a portfolio of eleven initiatives and external projects addressing key issues and geographies, including children and violence, integration and migration, dementia, artificial intelligence and the Balkans. During 2021-22, the Brussels-based staff will manage projects and organize regular meetings of the board and the general assembly. The Network of European Foundations currently has eleven members and engages many other foundations, public donors and other types of philanthropic organizations in its projects.

title: Membership and Administrative Support
description: This grant supports the membership and administrative costs of the Network of European Foundations, a nonprofit membership association based in Brussels. The grantee’s goal is to strengthen philanthropic cooperation among foundations, associations and other nongovernmental organizations in Europe. In 2022, the grantee managed a portfolio of nine collaborative projects addressing key issues and geographies, including gender equality, democracy, artificial intelligence, migration and the Balkans. During 2023-24, the Brussels-based staff will manage projects and organize regular meetings of the board and the general assembly. The Network of European Foundations currently has 12 members and engages many other foundations, public donors and other types of philanthropic organizations in its projects.

title: Membership and Administrative Support
description: This grant supports the membership and administrative costs of the Network of European Foundations, a nonprofit membership association based in Brussels. The grantee’s goal is to strengthen philanthropic cooperation among foundations, associations and other nongovernmental organizations in Europe. In 2024, the grantee managed a portfolio of eight collaborative projects unfolding under three main domains of action: democracy, social cohesion and international development. During 2025-27, the Network of European Foundations will continue to provide a space for funders’ learning and strategic collaboration by hosting projects and organizing partner events.

title: General Purposes
description: The goal of the project is to strengthen philanthropy in Africa by connecting the field and promoting learning. The Africa Philanthropy Network is a continent-wide network of grantmaking and other philanthropic organizations in Africa. It brings together foundations, intermediary grantmakers and practitioners from across Africa to learn, generate new knowledge and give voice to philanthropy. Previous support has enabled the grantee to support members to navigate the changes that were brought about by the pandemic, host learning events on a variety of topics relevant to members, produce knowledge that benefits the sector and connect the field in Africa to the global philanthropy field. In addition, the Africa Philanthropy Network has worked closely with other similar organizations to strengthen the ecosystem of philanthropy in Africa. During the next two years, the grantee will continue to strengthen networking and collaboration, connect Africa to the larger philanthropy ecosystem and contribute to the knowledge generated about philanthropy in Africa.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides funding to support the strengthening of philanthropy in Africa by connecting the field, promoting learning and enhancing the narrative of philanthropy in Africa. The Africa Philanthropy Network is a continent-wide network of grantmaking and other philanthropic organizations in Africa. The grantee brings together foundations, intermediary grantmakers and practitioners from across Africa to learn, generate new knowledge and give voice to philanthropy. During the previous grant period, the grantee produced new knowledge on philanthropy in Africa, promoted national and regional networking and hosted learning events. The grantee partnered with the Worldwide Initiative for Grantmaker Support to host the WINGS Forum in Africa. During the current grant period, Africa Philanthropy Network will build on its work to create connections across the philanthropy ecosystem in Africa, raise the profile of African philanthropy in global forums, produce knowledge on the culture of philanthropy in Africa and connect likeminded philanthropic organizations.

title: Philanthropy Infrastructure Development in Turkey
description: The project goal is to strengthen the culture of giving and the infrastructure for philanthropy in Turkey. To this end, the Third Sector Foundation of Turkey will provide training, technical assistance, networking opportunities, and knowledge resources to individuals, foundations, and corporations in Turkey who are interested in improving their philanthropic practices. The grantee will also build networks and foster collaboration across the sector. During 2017–2019, the grantee organized peer-learning and skill-building events for individuals and families, foundations, companies, and local civic initiatives to build the capacity for more strategic philanthropy; raised awareness of the importance of philanthropy and trends in strategic giving; and collected and published inspiring stories of individual philanthropy. Established in 1993, Third Sector Foundation of Turkey is a resource center for its more than 100 member associations and foundations as well as the sector in general.

title: Africa Grantmakers' Affinity Group
description: The project goal is to build a network of knowledgeable and engaged private funders who are interested in grantmaking practices that strengthen the impact of their funding. The Africa Grantmakers’ Affinity Group, a project of the Tides Center, convenes funders, curates information, and connects funders supporting work that benefits communities in Africa. Past support enabled the grantee to organize forums for members to reflect on the impact of COVID-19 on their grantmaking, discuss emerging issues affecting communities in Africa, and produce material on the history of the network. In 2022 and 2023, the grantee will continue to document its 20 year contribution to build a dynamic learning community, and define the role of the network in response to a changing philanthropy landscape.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to build and strengthen an enabling environment for philanthropy. Worldwide Initiatives for Grantmaker Support is a global network, linking more than 170 philanthropic associations and support organizations from around the world through international exchange, information services, networking and peer-to-peer learning opportunities. During 2019-2020, the grantee represented the sector and its members in various global and regional fora and networks; published research related to philanthropy and philanthropy infrastructure; disseminated information and analysis about the sector through social media, blogs, and an online newsletter; held capacity-building workshops and online webinars; and launched a series of online events as part of its flagship global event, the WINGSForum. In 2021-2022, the grantee will focus on making the case for philanthropy development, fostering an enabling environment for philanthropy and strengthening the philanthropy support ecosystem where it is needed the most. Established in 2000 and incorporated in the United States in 2010, the grantee is based in Sao Paulo, Brazil.

title: General Purposes
description: Worldwide Initiatives for Grantmaker Support is a global network, linking more than 195 philanthropic associations and support organizations from around the world through international exchange, information services, networking and peer-to-peer learning opportunities. During 2021-22, the grantee: 1) represented the sector and its members in various global and regional fora and networks; 2) published research related to philanthropy and philanthropy infrastructure; 3) disseminated information and analysis about the sector through social media, blogs and an online newsletter; 4) held capacity-building workshops and online webinars; and 5) launched a new strategy to strengthen the enabling environment for philanthropy. In 2023-24, the grantee will focus on building and strengthening an enabling environment for philanthropy by building members’ capacity for policy advocacy, increasing membership in the Global South and developing a new five-year strategic plan. Established in 2000, and incorporated in the United States in 2010, Worldwide Initiatives for Grantmaker Support is based in Sao Paulo, Brazil.

title: General Purposes
description: Worldwide Initiatives for Grantmaker Support is a global network, linking more than 230 philanthropic associations and support organizations from around the world through international exchange, information services, networking and peer-to-peer learning opportunities. During 2023-24, the grantee: 1) represented the sector and its members in various global and regional fora and networks; 2) published research related to philanthropy and philanthropy infrastructure; 3) disseminated information and analysis about the sector through social media, blogs and an online newsletter; 4) held capacity-building workshops and online webinars; and 5) launched a new strategy to strengthen the enabling environment for philanthropy. In 2025-26, the grantee will focus on building and strengthening an enabling environment for philanthropy by building members’ capacity for policy advocacy, increasing membership in the Global South. Established in 2000, and incorporated in the United States in 2010, Worldwide Initiatives for Grantmaker Support is based in Sao Paulo, Brazil.

title: General Purposes
description: Alliance Publishing Trust facilitates the exchange of information and ideas among philanthropists, social investors and others working for social change worldwide. To this end, the grantee carries out a range of publishing activities with regular products, including: 1) Alliance, a quarterly print magazine; 2) Alliance Extra, a weekly email service; 3) a Latest from Alliance blog which offers daily opinions, news and conference reports; and 4) Alliance events hosted around the special theme of each magazine issue and other selected themes. In 2021, the grantee had over 29,000 readers of its various information products. During this grant period, the grantee will publish Alliance Magazine quarterly in both print and digital formats, produce a range of content delivered digitally, organize regular in-person and online events and expand its coverage globally. Established in 2006, Alliance Publishing Trust is located in London, England.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Albania, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Kosovo, Serbia, Croatia
description: The Catalyst Foundation works regionally to promote the growth and improved transparency of the individual and corporate philanthropic culture in Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Croatia, Kosovo, Macedonia, Montenegro and Serbia. The project goal is to strengthen the field of philanthropy in the Western Balkans. During 2022–24, the grantee will: 1) gather and disseminate data on giving trendsin the Western Balkans; 2) develop and introduce services and products that increase nonprofit and philanthropy transparency and effectiveness; and 3) strengthen philanthropy networks in the Western Balkans and build its organizational capacities. During 2020-21, the grantee: 1) gathered and analyzed data on giving and published annual reports; 2) built digital tools for nonprofit management, data collection and crowdfunding; and 3) supported regional and national level donors’ fora. The Catalyst Foundation was registered in 2013 in Serbia and is based in Belgrade.

title: General Purposes
description: In early 2019, Foundation Center and GuideStar joined forces to become Candid. The new organization blends the leadership and staff of both organizations and maintains Foundation Center’s legal status and employer identification number. Foundation Center has been the largest source of information about philanthropy globally, and GuideStar has been the largest source of information on U.S. nonprofit organizations. General purposes support to Foundation Center has contributed to its strategic priorities, which are to: 1) connect nonprofits to the resources they need to thrive; 2) empower donors with knowledge tools to be more strategic; 3) build the global data platform for philanthropy; 4) communicate philanthropy’s contribution to making a better world; 5) encourage greater foundation transparency; and 6) ensure that technology provides a strong foundation for the grantee’s work. This grant increase will support the work of what has previously been GuideStar, which also had been receiving general purposes grant support from the Mott Foundation through 2018. That work involves collecting and maintaining data on millions of U.S. nonprofits and providing data services to thousands more, thus enhancing the sector’s transparency and allowing donors to make more informed giving decisions.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general support to Candid, an organization that collects, analyzes and publishes information on philanthropic and nonprofit entities. The grantee currently houses databases with 33,000 research reports and data on 1.8 million nonprofits and 242,000 foundations. The grantee provides training to nonprofits and foundations while producing and disseminating its own research. Candid’s strategic priorities are to: 1) connect nonprofits to the resources needed to thrive; 2) empower donors with knowledge tools to be more strategic; 3) build the global data platform for philanthropy; 4) communicate philanthropy’s contribution to making a better world; 5) encourage greater foundation transparency; and 6) ensure that technology provides a strong foundation for its work. Candid was founded in 2019, when Foundation Center and GuideStar merged into one entity, consolidating much of the nonprofit and philanthropic sector’s data.

title: Finance for Sustainable Development in South America
description: INESC is a nongovernmental organization established for the promotion and strengthening of representative and participative democracy in Brazil. Over the former grant period, the grantee made important contributions to sustainable energy and infrastructure finance in the Amazon and the transition from fossil fuels to a low carbon, renewable energy economy. Over this grant period, the grantee will focus on defending social and environmental standards for development in the Brazilian Amazon and promoting sustainable finance and international standards at national and international financial institutions.

title: International Society for Third-Sector Research
description: This grant provides continued support to the International Society for Third-Sector Research, a global membership association with over 1,000 members from more than 80 countries that encourages, supports, and provides academic legitimacy to the study of civil society. Founded in 1992 and based at Johns Hopkins University, the society’s major accomplishments include convening biennial international research conferences; publishing special reports, conference working papers, and a scholarly journal; and convening regional meetings of research networks on various continents. In mid-2018, the society became an independent nonprofit, which continues to be supported by Johns Hopkins University. This grant increase will provide partial resources needed to support a May 2019 seminar for PhD students from across Africa, with the Wits Business School’s Center for Philanthropy and Social Investment.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued support to the International Society for Third-Sector Research, a global membership association with over 900 members from more than 70 countries that encourages, supports, and provides academic legitimacy to the study of civil society. In 2020-2021, the grantee will improve its member’s experience; attract and retain scholars, researchers, and students from the Global South; and demonstrate the connection between research and policy impact. Founded in 1992 and originally based at Johns Hopkins University, the grantee’s major accomplishments include convening biennial international research conferences; publishing special reports, conference working papers, and a scholarly journal; and convening regional meetings of research networks on various continents. In mid-2018, the grantee became an independent nonprofit but continues to be supported by Johns Hopkins University.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued support to the International Society for Third-Sector Research, a global membership association with over 900 members from more than 70 countries that encourages, supports and provides academic legitimacy to the study of civil society. In 2022-2023, the grantee will: host its biannual conference in Montreal; improve its member’s experience; attract and retain scholars, researchers and students from the Global South; and host regional Ph.D. seminars. Founded in 1992 and originally based at Johns Hopkins University, the grantee’s major accomplishments include: convening biennial international research conferences; publishing special reports, conference working papers and a scholarly journal; and convening regional meetings of research networks on various continents. In mid-2018, the grantee became an independent nonprofit but continues to be supported by Johns Hopkins University.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Association for Research on Nonprofit Organizations & Voluntary Action
description: This grant provides renewal support to the Association for Research on Nonprofit Organizations & Voluntary Action, a leading U.S.-based national and international association that connects scholars, teachers, and practitioners interested in research on nonprofit organizations, voluntary action, philanthropy, and civil society. Founded in 1971, the grantee is a neutral, open forum that brings together both theoretical and applied interests, helps scholars gain insight into the daily concerns of nonprofits, and provides nonprofit professionals with connections to research they can use to improve their work. Principal activities include organizing an annual conference; publishing the leading scholarly journal in the field, the Nonprofit and Voluntary Sector Quarterly; providing tools and media that enable the grantee to support research, discussion and teaching; initiating and supporting the Association for Research on Civil Society in Africa; and organizing the annual Symposium on Public Policy and Nonprofits.

title: Chronicle of Philanthropy
description: The program goal is to support a robust information space for philanthropy and the nonprofit sector. The Chronicle of Philanthropy, the most prominent information source for the sector in the United States, is undergoing a process to revise its business model to enhance its financial sustainability. Acting as a fiscal sponsor, Philanthropy New York is overseeing a project that will include audience research followed by product evaluation, prototype development and testing, and product launch. Founded in 1988 and published by the Chronicle of Higher Education, the Chronicle of Philanthropy is an independent national media outlet covering all aspects of philanthropy and charitable organizations. Its website offers news updates, the complete contents of a printed monthly issue, and more than seven years of archived articles and data. Philanthropy New York was founded in 1979 in order to enhance the ability of philanthropic organizations and individual donors in the New York City region to serve the public good.

title: Global Civil Society Information System
description: Over the past several years, the Center for Civil Society Studies at Johns Hopkins University has worked with the United Nations Statistics Division on revisions and expansions to the United Nations Handbook on Nonprofit and Related Institutions and Volunteer Work in the System of National Accounts—its guidance to countries on gathering statistics about nonprofit institutions, volunteer work, and the social economy. The goal of this project is to enhance the quality, reliability, and accessibility of national-level data on nonprofit organizations and volunteering around the world. Since the official release of the new handbook in May 2018, the center has been undertaking education and dissemination efforts to encourage implementation of the resulting broadened civil society sector statistical procedures into the statistical systems of countries around the world. A grant increase and extension will allow the grantee to expand its work to promote and support the implementation of the new handbook.

title: Global Philanthropy Environment Index
description: The program goal is to foster the development of a conducive environment for philanthropy across countries by providing rigorous, comparative data and by raising awareness and understanding of philanthropy, especially in developing countries. The most recent version of the index was published in April 2018. The Lilly Family School of Philanthropy at Indiana University has since been promoting, presenting and educating on the research as well as working on the newest iteration of the report, set to be published in first quarter 2022. Following the publication, the grantee will create online and printed educational materials and organize events in the United States and globally to share results and generate debate. The Lilly Family School of Philanthropy at Indiana University was founded in 2012. Its mission is to increase the understanding of philanthropy and improve its practice worldwide through critical inquiry, interdisciplinary research, teaching, training and civic engagement.

title: Global Philanthropy Environment Index
description: The program goal is to foster the development of a conducive environment for philanthropy across countries by providing rigorous, comparative data and raising awareness and understanding of philanthropy, especially in developing countries. The Global Philanthropy Environment Index provides a framework for a comparative assessment of the philanthropic environment at the country level and allows for a global conversation on this important topic. Its findings help nonprofit leaders, scholars and policy makers to gain a thorough understanding of the evolving environment at the country, region and global levels, and to advocate for a more supportive environment for philanthropy worldwide. The Lilly Family School of Philanthropy at Indiana University was founded in 2012. Its mission is to increase the understanding of philanthropy and improve its practice worldwide through critical inquiry, interdisciplinary research, teaching, training and civic engagement.

title: General Purposes
description: Based in Washington, D.C., the International Center for Not-for-Profit Law’s goal is to provide an enabling environment for nonprofits, philanthropy and civic participation by promoting and protecting the freedoms of association, expression and assembly. To this end, the grantee will carry out a range of activities, including enhancing international norms and multilateral engagement to safeguard civic space, promoting appropriate country-level legislation, helping civil society organizations navigate laws once enacted, undertaking and disseminating research and analysis and raising public awareness about the importance of civil society and cross-border philanthropy.

title: Nonprofit Employment Data Project
description: The primary goal of the Nonprofit Employment Data Project is to develop and disseminate reports on U.S. nonprofit employment, wages and finances over time and in relation to other industries. During the previous grant period, the previous grantee, Johns Hopkins University, produced annual reports, developed an interactive data dashboard and produced monthly COVID-19 employment updates. The new grantee, George Mason University’s Nonprofit Center, will continue these project activities as well as incorporate additional data systems and explore the creation of a network of federal officials working on nonprofit data. The grantee was originally founded in 1949 as a branch of the University of Virginia, and it became an independent university in 1972. George Mason University is an innovative and inclusive academic institution committed to creating a more just, free and prosperous society.

title: Tax Policy and Charities Project
description: The project goal is to improve the policy environment for the nonprofit sector and philanthropy in the United States. To this end, the Tax Policy and Charities Project provides a rapid response to current debates over tax policy as it affects charities, continually upgrades a tax model that incorporates thousands of provisions in the tax code, provides analysis of current and longer-term tax issues and involves scholars and policy officials in a discussion of new tax proposals. Over the past two years, the project has produced and facilitated research and discussion on tax policy relating to charity. Future activities will include modeling tax and charity policy proposals, writing policy briefs and articles, providing congressional testimony and producing other materials regarding major tax and charity issues. The project is implemented by the Urban-Brookings Tax Policy Center of the Urban Institute. The grantee is a national think tank that gathers data, conducts research, evaluates programs, offers technical assistance overseas and educates Americans on social and economic issues to foster sound public policy and effective government.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to increase the awareness, understanding and engagement of the nonprofit and philanthropic sector with respect to digital policies and practices that impact the space for civic engagement. To this end, Access Now—a nonprofit registered in the United States and working globally—will empower and support nonprofits and other civil society actors through direct technical support, comprehensive policy engagement, advocacy, grassroots grantmaking and convenings. During 2019-2020, the grantee monitored and reported on the pandemic’s impact on digital rights and civil society, mobilized a network of more than 200 nonprofits globally to push against internet shutdowns, advocated to protect the .org domain, responded to more than 6,000 requests for digital security assistance via its dedicated helpline and published a major report on threats to freedom of assembly online. The grantee also organized its premier networking event, RightsCon, in Tunisia in 2019 and online in 2020. Based in New York City, Access Now is a leading global resource and advocate for digital policies that impact individual users and civil society organizations.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will assist Access Now in their efforts to increase the awareness, understanding and engagement of the nonprofit and philanthropic sector with respect to digital policies and practices that impact the space for civic engagement. To this end, during the grant period the grantee — a nonprofit registered in the United States and working globally — will empower and support nonprofits and other civil society actors through direct technical support, comprehensive policy engagement, advocacy, grassroots grantmaking and convenings. During 2021-22, the grantee: 1) monitored and reported on the pandemic’s impact on digital rights and civil society; 2) mobilized a network of more than 275 nonprofits globally to push against internet shutdowns; 3) responded to more than 2,500 requests annually for digital security assistance via its dedicated helpline; and 4) organized two editions of its premier networking event, RightsCon, online, attracting more than 9,000 participants in 2022. Based in New York City, Access Now is a leading global resource and advocate for digital policies that impact individual users and civil society organizations.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will assist Access Now in their efforts to increase the awareness, understanding and engagement of the nonprofit and philanthropic sector with respect to digital policies and practices that impact the space for civic engagement. To this end, during the grant period the grantee — a nonprofit registered in the United States and working globally — will empower and support nonprofits and other civil society actors through direct technical support, comprehensive policy engagement, advocacy, grassroots grantmaking and convenings. During 2023-24, the grantee: 1) monitored and reported on digital rights and civil society; 2) mobilized a network of more than 334 nonprofits globally to push against internet shutdowns; 3) responded to nearly 7,000 requests for digital security assistance via its dedicated helpline; and 4) organized its premier networking event, RightsCon, attracting more than 8,000 participants in 2023. Based in New York City, Access Now is a leading global resource and advocate for digital policies that impact individual users and civil society organizations.

title: Funders' Initiative for Civil Society
geographic_focus: Southern Asia, Western Europe, World, Eastern Africa
description: The program goal is to enable donors to provide leadership and practical support for civil society actors addressing the global trend of closing space for civil society. The Funders’ Initiative for Civil Society, a project of Global Dialogue, provides stakeholders with research, information and support to coordinate and align their grants and strategies. To date, the initiative produced 13 reports, held sessions at 14 philanthropy sector events, organized two conferences for funders, hosted webinars and produced research for groups of funders focused on various issues such as humanitarian action, digital rights and transparency. The initiative completed an extensive review of how philanthropy can more effectively provide resources to civil society in the face of current and future threats. During the grant period, the initiative will map specific strategies and implementation models for funders to address the key drivers of closing civic space. The initiative is a collaborative program managed by the grantee and directly involves a range of private funders. Founded in the United Kingdom in 2006, Global Dialogue implements programs supporting human rights, social change and funder collaboration around the world.

title: Funders' Initiative for Civil Society
geographic_focus: Western Europe, Southern Asia, World, Eastern Africa
description: The program goal is to enable donors to provide leadership and practical support for civil society actors addressing the global trend of closing space for civil society. The Funders’ Initiative for Civil Society, a project of Global Dialogue, provides stakeholders with research, information and support to coordinate and align their grants and strategies. During the previous grant period, the initiative mapped systemic drivers of closing civic space, supported funders in its efforts to counter the closing space and developed a framework on civic space and securitization. During this grant period, the initiative will focus on continuing to help funders respond to global repressive trends by focusing on narrative building and securitization. The initiative is a collaborative program managed by the grantee and directly involves a range of private funders. Founded in the United Kingdom in 2006, Global Dialogue implements programs supporting human rights, social change and funder collaboration around the world.

title: Funders' Initiative for Civil Society
geographic_focus: Western Europe, Southern Asia, World, Eastern Africa
description: The program goal is to enable donors to provide leadership and practical support for civil society actors addressing the global trend of closing space for civil society. The Funders’ Initiative for Civil Society, a project of Global Dialogue, provides stakeholders with research, information and support to coordinate and align their grants and strategies. During the previous grant period, the grantee started two large-scale initiatives, developed six additional donor coordination vehicles, published 10 new resources and organized 25 events. During this grant period, the grantee will focus on research and thought leadership, mobilizing its Civic Futures learning community and scaling its Narratives Network Initiative. The initiative is a collaborative program managed by the grantee and directly involves a range of private funders. Founded in the United Kingdom in 2006, Global Dialogue implements programs supporting human rights, social change and funder collaboration around the world.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support the continued organizational and programmatic development of People in Need, one of the largest nonprofits in Central and Eastern Europe. Founded in 1992, the grantee: provides relief and development assistance in response to natural disasters and violent conflict; promotes human rights, civic engagement and civil society development; and supports social inclusion and integration for marginalized groups. During the previous grant period, the grantee provided relief and development assistance in 23 countries, reaching more than 3.5 million people. During the grant period, the grantee will continue to respond to crises arising from war and conflict, natural disasters and the COVID-19 pandemic through its humanitarian relief programs and its support to civil society organizations working on education, human rights and social inclusion. People in Need is based in Prague, Czech Republic.

title: Integrating Advocacy: Building Policy Capacity
geographic_focus: Central America, North America, Africa, World, South America
description: The goal of this grant is to integrate advocacy and build policy capacity in civil society leaders across the world. During the grant period, the Stanford Center on Philanthropy and Civil Society will expand the study of the social and political impacts of technology and how they affect the health of society and democracy more broadly. To this end, the grantee will: 1) merge with the Cyber Policy Center and develop policy recommendations; 2) explore educational opportunities for students and professionals; and 3) assess its community outreach strategies. During the previous grant period, the grantee managed the Digital Civil Society Lab, supporting a network of practitioners who produced and disseminated usable knowledge on contemporary problems related to technology, political polarization and threats to democracy. Beyond the fellowships, the Lab disseminated its research and engaged with the sector through teaching and organizing globally accessible events.

title: Enabling Environment Program
geographic_focus: Western Africa, Mexico, Northern Africa, Eastern Africa, Southeastern Asia, Central America, World, Southern Asia
description: The project goal is to defend and promote civic space and foster a safe and enabling environment for civil society actors. To this end, the Fund for Global Human Rights, through its Enabling Environment Program, will support an array of strategies to broaden and protect civic space in specific contexts and in response to the needs of local nonprofits and activists. With global programming, the grantee is a public charity based in Washington, DC with an office in London.

title: Enabling Environment Program
geographic_focus: South America, World, Africa, Central America
description: The project goal is to defend and promote civic space and foster a safe and enabling environment for civil society actors. To this end, the Fund for Global Human Rights, through its Enabling Environment Program, will work at national, regional and global levels to counter the negative impacts on civic space from state and transnational counterterrorism, anti-money laundering and other security frameworks. The grantee will make grants and provide technical assistance to support networking, learning and collaboration on policy development and advocacy. With global programming, the grantee is a public charity based in Washington, D.C., with an office in London.

title: Enabling Environment Program
geographic_focus: South America, Africa, Asia, World, Central America
description: The project goal is to defend and promote civic space and foster a safe and enabling environment for civil society actors. To this end, the Fund for Global Human Rights — through its Enabling Environment Program — will provide grants and technical assistance to nonprofits at national, regional and global levels. This will ensure that civil society actors can thrive in the face of rising authoritarianism and the negative impacts on civic space from state and transnational counterterrorism, anti-money laundering and other security frameworks. During 2021-23, the grantee supported nonprofits in Kenya, Nigeria, the Philippines, Mexico, Guatemala and other countries through networking, research and advocacy grants. The grantee also worked closely with Funders Initiative for Civil Society to raise awareness of and strengthen funder collaboration around the threats to civic space. The Fund for Global Human Rights is a public charity based in Washington, D.C., with an office in London.

title: Scaling the Digital Activism Hub
description: The project goal is to build knowledge and capacity that will empower nonprofits to refine and communicate key messages and stories in an increasingly complex, cluttered, and hostile digital information landscape. To this end, Fundacja TechSoup, the European hub of TechSoup, will further develop and scale up its digital activism hub. The hub will be an online platform to equip nonprofits to develop content for social media and other online spaces, counter negative and false information, and communicate key messages effectively.

title: Learning Commons
description: With this grant, Kettering University will construct a new building on its campus. The Learning Commons will serve as the academic and social centerpiece of the university’s campus, providing a place that fosters collaborative learning and exploration. The building will be characterized by open areas for students to gather and work, technology to support student learning and engagement, space for cross-discipline collaboration, and physical and electronic library resources that can be accessed by Kettering University and other postsecondary students in Flint.

title: Education Trust-Midwest Michigan Policy Efforts
description: With this grant, the Education Trust will support its Midwest division to do the thoughtful and nonpartisan policy analysis for which it is known. Michigan leaders and a broad set of community stakeholders are grappling with the current condition of education in the state, and actively investigating the policy levers that can help make Michigan a top ten state in the nation. The grantee’s Midwest division will conduct research and analysis and participate in advocacy to help inform important policy conversations about education in the state of Michigan.

title: Education Trust-Midwest Michigan Policy Efforts
description: With this grant, the Education Trust will support its Midwest division to do the thoughtful and nonpartisan policy analysis for which it is known. Michigan leaders, and a broad set of community stakeholders are grappling with the current condition of education in the state and actively investigating the policy levers that can help make Michigan a top ten state in the nation. The grantee’s Midwest division will conduct research and analysis and participate in advocacy to help inform important policy conversations about education in the state of Michigan.

title: Glenwood Cemetery Maintenance
description: The Board of Trustees of Glenwood Cemetery has entered into an agreement with the Historic Elmwood Foundation to restore and preserve Glenwood Cemetery as an active, historic cemetery serving the local community. This grant will support the ongoing maintenance for Glenwood Cemetery in Flint.

title: Food Services Building Demolition
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide support to the Flint Cultural Center Corporation to demolish the Food Services building, which is located on the Flint Cultural Center campus near the Buick Gallery and The Whiting. Flint Community Schools is currently using the building for food preparation but will be relocating at the end of the current school year. When the building is no longer used for food preparation, demolition will be the best course of action to better address the evolving needs of the campus.

title: Advocacy Training
description: This grant will support the Alliance for Justice in providing customized advocacy trainings and resources for the statewide afterschool networks. The trainings and resources will provide an opportunity to build the capacity of the statewide afterschool networks to advance the afterschool field.

title: 21st Century Community Learning Centers Institute
description: This grant will support Foundations, Inc. to continue to provide comprehensive services and supports to enhance learning experiences and professional development opportunities to the afterschool field. The grantee will host an annual conference for 21st Century Community Learning Centers leaders and afterschool professionals working to improve the quality of afterschool programs. As one of the leading conferences for afterschool professionals, the conference provides best practices in program design, evaluation, community engagement, and program sustainability strategies.

title: Engaging Youth in Service
description: This grant will support Youth Service America to engage young people throughout the United States in quality youth-led service projects. The grantee will focus efforts to bolster youth engagement in Flint and Genesee County and across the United States by working with schools, afterschool programs, and nonprofit organizations.

title: Advancing the Next Generation of Civil Society Assistance
description: The project goal is to help funders, policymakers and civic activists take the full measure of the changes buffeting civil society globally and advance efforts to rethink civic engagement and civil society development assistance. To this end, the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace will expand a civic activism scholars network by adding experts on digital technology and rights; convene workshops and international meetings; publish reports and articles; and brief funders, practitioners and policymakers on key trends and dynamics. During 2019-2020, the grantee generated knowledge in the form of articles and reports and created linkages between the research, practice and policy domains through workshops and briefings. Established in 1910 in Washington, D.C. with a gift from Andrew Carnegie, the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace is a private, nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing cooperation between nations and promoting active international engagement by the United States.

title: Yo-Yo Ma Day of Action
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will support outreach and performance activities in Flint by renowned cellist Yo-Yo Ma. Through the University Musical Society in Ann Arbor, Mr. Ma is including Flint as part of his worldwide tour. He will partner with several Flint organizations for a day of artistic engagement that will include an informal performance or concert and a community conversation about the power of the arts.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Illinois, Wisconsin, Ohio, Michigan, Indiana, Minnesota, Pennsylvania, New York
description: The Northeast-Midwest Institute is a nonprofit organization dedicated to improving the economic and environmental health of the Northeast and Midwest regions of the United States. Headquartered in Washington, D.C., the grantee provides data, research and policy analysis to inform state and federal policy reforms and programs. This grant will support the organization’s general purposes including its significant initiatives on the Great Lakes, workforce development, safe drinking water and watershed conservation. The Northeast-Midwest Institute provides federal freshwater policy analysis to stakeholders in the Great Lakes and will be launching new initiatives on climate change impacts, public finance and affordable drinking water.

title: Supporting the National Network of Statewide Afterschool Networks
description: Collaborative Communications Group will continue to support and convene the afterschool ecosystem of grantees, including the 50 State Afterschool Network, the Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative and leading afterschool programs. For the Network, the grantee will coordinate all Network meetings including large Network conferences; manage webinars, the Network website and online community; provide professional development opportunities to the networks; help to coordinate technical assistance and assist in the ongoing rollout of the Mizzen by Mott app.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Indiana, Pennsylvania, Ohio, New York, Minnesota, Ontario, Michigan, Wisconsin, Illinois
description: Freshwater Future is a regional organization that is a catalyst for community action to strengthen policies and safeguard the waters of the Great Lakes region. Since its inception in 1996, with significant support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has provided over $4 million in grants and technical assistance to grassroots groups around the Great Lakes basin. With renewed support, the grantee will provide financial resources and capacity-building support for on-the-ground groups. The grantee will grow and support networks of organizations that are tackling Great Lakes issues. Freshwater Future will expand their capacity through enhanced fundraising.

title: General Purposes
description: Michigan Environmental Council is a coalition of nearly 70 environmental and faith-based organizations. Created 40 years ago, the grantee is committed to fighting threats against Michigan’s water, air and land with a particular focus on the Great Lakes; inland waters and drinking water concerns; sustainable agriculture; clean energy; and environmental health. With this grant, the grantee will focus on public engagement, education, relationship building, communications and operational activities to strengthen Michigan’s environmental protections and improve the Great Lakes. The Michigan Environmental Council will seek to expand Michigan’s environmental movement to include new leaders that reflect the state’s racial diversity and to overcome disinvestment in water infrastructure to ensure safe, affordable drinking water.

title: Disaster Preparation and Response
description: With this grant, the Center for Disaster Philanthropy will build its capacity to provide natural and man-made disaster relief in the United States and abroad. The grantee has been trusted with contributions from large and small donors to provide a coordinated and efficient response to disasters, and aims to help philanthropic partners develop the plans and strategies to be effective before, during, and after disasters.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Citizens Campaign Fund for the Environment
description: The New York based Citizens Campaign Fund for the Environment was founded in 1985 and is one of the largest, most respected grassroots environmental organizations in the state. The grantee has four offices in New York and leads public education initiatives to change behavior and protect the environment from water pollution including pharmaceuticals, plastics, pesticides and chemicals. The grantee’s work is especially important now, as it connects communities and neighborhoods with policy decisions at the state level.
