The financial fallout from the pandemic will impose tough decisions on New York State, and the grantee will help make the case that postponing protection of the environment will make problems worse and more costly. With this grant, the Citizens Campaign Fund for the Environment will lead a range of statewide education initiatives, including those that benefit and protect the Great Lakes and the people who depend on them.

title: General Purposes
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant provides general purpose support to Red Ink Flint. The grantee operates Flint Local 432, a performance venue located in downtown Flint for artistic programming and community convening. In 2018, 48 concerts were performed at the venue, including local musical talent as well as regional and national acts. Additionally, the grantee operates the Factory Two makerspace, which opened on Grand Traverse Street in 2017. Funds will support organizational, administrative, and programmatic costs for Red Ink Flint.

title: Technical Assistance for Improved Teaching and Learning
description: This grant allows Michigan State University to support Flint Community Schools with technical assistance aimed at increasing district capacity, improving school culture, increasing operational efficiency, and improving student academic outcomes. To achieve these goals, technical assistance will be focused on four primary components: districtwide systems, leadership development, classroom instruction, and climate and culture.

title: General Purposes
description: The Bank Information Center is a nongovernmental organization specialized in analyzing and strengthening social and environmental governance of development finance institutions. Over the last grant period, the grantee and its partners in developing countries made significant contributions to improving sustainable energy finance and safeguards at the Inter-American Development Bank and monitoring the implementation of the new Environmental Social Framework of the World Bank Group. Over the next grant period, the grantee will monitor new safeguards frameworks and work to ensure sustainable energy and infrastructure finance in the current and post COVID-19 contexts.

title: Capacity Building
description: Michigan Community Capital is a nonprofit community development corporation which is also designated as a Community Development Finance Institution and a Community Development Entity by the federal government. The grantee funds community development real estate projects across the state. This capacity building grant will help increase the number of communities it serves, specifically looking to address needs in postindustrial and smaller urban communities.

title: General Purposes
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant provides general purpose support to the Buckham Fine Arts Project, also known as Buckham Gallery. The grantee was incorporated in 1984 by a group of artists who saw the need for a contemporary gallery in downtown Flint. Over the past 30 plus years, the grantee has held more than 300 exhibitions of visual art; poetry readings; performance art events; and dance, music, and film presentations. The grantee showcases local, regional, and international artists. Located in a storefront space on the corner of South Saginaw and Second Streets, Buckham Gallery has expanded programming in the new space including a monthly Open Mic night, family art activities, and events for older adults.

title: Police Vehicle Technology
description: This grant will support the City of Flint to purchase and install technology equipment for Flint Police Department patrol vehicles. The equipment will streamline communications between the department and 911. Additionally, the added technology will increase information about the interaction between police officers and residents.

title: Neighborhood Arts and Cultural Events
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will support arts and cultural projects through the Neighborhood Small Grants Program at the Community Foundation of Greater Flint. Neighborhood groups will implement resident-led efforts to create or enhance and expand existing artistic projects or events/performances. Funded projects will aim to stimulate civic engagement, improve neighborhood conditions, provide opportunities for self-expression and/or enhance skills for residents to work together creatively. All projects and event implementers will follow COVID-19 public health guidelines.

title: Flint Fireworks
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to the Flint Downtown Development Authority will support a fireworks display for the 2021 Flint Juneteenth celebration. The grantee and several community partners, including the City of Flint, have organized a series of family friendly activities for a three-day Juneteenth celebration, including a parade from City Hall to Berston Field House. The events aim to bring the community together to commemorate the end of slavery.

title: Strengthening Land Trusts and Promoting Collaboration to Conserve Freshwater Systems in the Great Lakes Basin
geographic_focus: Michigan, Ohio, New York, Minnesota, Indiana, Wisconsin, Illinois, Pennsylvania
description: The Land Trust Alliance is a national organization that provides technical support, training and assistance to support land conservation, acquisition and protection. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee surveyed and assessed the capacity and willingness of land trusts to expand their effectiveness in improving water quality. The grantee provided training, mentoring and accreditation to advance land trusts excellence. With renewed support, the grantee will conduct one or more pilot projects with a land trust to advance measures to protect water quality and help land trusts navigate the COVID-19 pandemic by providing support to enhance organizational resilience, capacity and impact. Finally, the Land Trust Alliance will work with land trusts to engage a more diverse and inclusive constituency in land conservation.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support the Ferris Wheel Innovation Center located on the first floor of the Ferris Wheel building in downtown Flint. The grantee was established to help people in an economically disadvantaged community to access supports that will help advance their business concepts. The goal is to foster education, encourage innovation and entrepreneurism, and promote economic stability in Flint. Local colleges and nonprofits will partner with the grantee to provide joint programming. Businesses located in the building will offer mentoring and counseling services. Additionally, college students will be hired to work with users and gain practical work experience that aligns with their future career goals.

title: Migration and Forced Displacement Program
description: The project goal is to address the new and continued challenges facing immigrants throughout the Americas. The Hispanics in Philanthropy Migration and Forced Displacement Program accomplishes this through grantmaking, funder engagement, and communications efforts. Founded in 1981, the grantee is the leading philanthropic membership organization for grantmaking in Hispanic and Latino communities. Hispanics in Philanthropy works across the Americas to strengthen Latino leadership, equity, and voice by facilitating greater philanthropic investments in Latino communities.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to help address the long-standing and emerging issues facing immigrants in the Americas. Alianza Americas’ mission is to bring about a more inclusive, equitable, and sustainable way of life for under-served immigrant communities living in the United States and across Mexico and Central America. It accomplishes this through its action driven diplomacy, network advocacy, educational delegations and tours, a leadership institute, and mobile outreach supporting the caravans. Founded in 2004 by Mexican, Central American, and Caribbean immigrant leaders, the grantee is a network of over 50 members in 13 states, representing over 150,000 migrant families across the United States, with dozens of organizational partners in Mexico and Central America.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Centre for Community Justice and Development
description: The project goal is to increase access to justice for poor and marginalized people in South Africa. To this end, the Centre for Community Justice and Development will work with its network of 15 rural community advice offices in the KwaZulu-Natal province of South Africa. Key interventions include providing accredited training to community paralegals, advocacy on systemic rights violations in communities, financial and administrative support to advice offices, and applied research to inform the work of community paralegals. The grantee is a nonprofit organization that oversees the work of 15 community advice offices in the KwaZulu-Natal province of South Africa. It provides tailored support to advice offices to ensure that they provide a high quality service to poor and marginalized people in this province.

title: Access to Justice in Remote Areas of Sierra Leone
description: The project goal is to increase access to justice for poor and marginalized communities in Sierra Leone. To this end, the Legal Aid Board–Sierra Leone will provide access to justice services in five chiefdoms and five districts, across the four regions of the country. Key interventions over the two year period will include community legal education, training to paralegals and traditional leaders, community outreach, and the provision of mobile legal clinics. The Legal Aid Board–Sierra Leone is an independent government agency mandated by the Legal Aid Act to provide free justice services to people living in poverty in Sierra Leone.

title: Accredited Vocational Paralegal Training
description: The project goal is to increase the capacity of community paralegals in South Africa. To this end, the North-West University will implement vocational training programs for community paralegals. This training will be accessible for paralegals working in advice offices throughout all the provinces of South Africa. The grantee’s faculty of law has extensive experience in providing vocational training to community paralegals in South Africa. The North-West University was established in 2004 when the former University of the North West merged with the Potchefstroom University for Christian Higher Education.

title: Strengthening Community Paralegals in Ukraine
description: The Ukrainian Legal Aid Foundation has been an important actor in the growing ecosystem of accessible justice services in Ukraine. The need for community-based paralegals is significant given the variety of physical and financial barriers to accessing distant services. Drawing on growing experience in Ukraine and extensive experience of paralegal development abroad, the grantee will develop a specialized online training course for these community justice actors. The grantee will aim to train 300 paralegals over the initial grant period and introduce a protocol for regional supervision and mentoring of new paralegals to assist with particularly challenging issues and ensure that training standards are being met. The Ukrainian Legal Aid Foundation works to ensure access to justice in Ukraine through the support and provision of legal aid services and through the improving standards of justice provision.

title: Access to Justice in Africa and the SDGs
description: The Socioeconomic Rights Project of the Dullah Omar Institute for Constitutional Law, Governance and Human Rights at the University of the Western Cape will organize participation of access to justice institutions in sub-Saharan Africa at the United Nations High-level Political Forum in July 2019. The Forum meets every year during July to discuss the implementation of the Sustainable Development Goals. During 2019, the implementation of Goal 16 will be discussed at the Forum. Goal 16 aims to promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development; provide access to justice for all; and build effective, accountable, and inclusive institutions at all levels. This increase will allow the grantee to organize a side event at the High-level Political Forum in New York and to participate in various international preparatory meetings scheduled in the lead-up to the Forum.

title: Development Finance for Community Environment and Justice Defenders in Southern Africa
description: The project goal is to increase financing for community justice and environment defenders from mining companies and development financing institutions. To this end, the Southern Africa Resource Watch will research best practices by modeling this through meaningful community participation methods in Southern Africa. The grantee will also advocate for increased and sustainable financing for community justice and environment defenders that ensure independence. The Southern Africa Resource Watch is a regional nonprofit organization that promotes the transparent and accountable use of natural resources in Southern Africa.

title: African Centre of Excellence for Access to Justice Project
description: The project goal is to strengthen an African continental access to justice institution that will promote a learning and sharing agenda. To this end, the Paralegal Advisory Service Institute will coordinate the activities of the African Centre of Excellence for Access to Justice and serve as its secretariat. During this first year, the grantee will prioritize fundraising and increasing the membership base of the project. Grantee is one of the leading paralegal institutions in Africa and has a good reputation on the continent.

title: African Centre of Excellence for Access to Justice Project
description: The project goal is to strengthen the African Centre of Excellence for Access to Justice to promote a learning and sharing agenda. To this end, the Paralegal Advisory Service Institute will coordinate the activities of the African Centre of Excellence for Access to Justice and serve as its secretariat. The grantee will strengthen the capacity of the center; build its membership, communications and visibility; and enhance the provision of access to justice for poor and marginalized communities within the center’s member countries. The grantee is one of the leading community justice organizations in Africa.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will assist the Ukrainian Helsinki Human Rights Union in their efforts to increase access to justice in Ukraine through protection of fundamental rights and freedoms. Through its member organizations, which operate 19 public reception offices, the grantee will raise public awareness of the law and human rights through a range of monitoring, advocacy and educational activities. It will provide legal information and services through its network of reception offices and will systematically examine opportunities for strengthening this network in the context of decentralization reforms. The grantee will conduct strategic litigation and advocacy on critical issues arising from cases brought to its attention with a view to influencing systemic change in legal practice. In 2019–2020, the grantee provided nearly 20,000 individual consultations through its legal aid centers, despite the COVID-19 pandemic. It strengthened the operational efficiency of its reception centers, through important court victories, set important precedents for limiting pre-trial detention and treatment of suspects. Established in 2004, the Ukrainian Helsinki Human Rights Union works to promote practical observance of the range of international human rights instruments to which Ukraine is a party.

title: General Purposes
description: This renewal grant will provide support for the Flint Regional Science Fair, a volunteer-led organization that provides students in an eight-county area the opportunity to develop their scientific and engineering talents. The fair was founded in 1956 as part of the Foundation-funded community education program of Flint Community Schools and remains an important component of students’ scientific exploration today.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint
description: This renewal grant provides general purposes support to the Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint. Focusing on education, creativity, physical activity and health, and family support services, the grantee offers year-round programming to young people between the ages of 7 and 17 in the Flint area. The grantee operates two sites, one located on the east side and the other on the south side of the city. Programs such as this have been particularly necessary in Flint during the water crisis given that educational and enrichment opportunities are important interventions to help mitigate the long-term impacts of exposure to lead.

title: Community Education Initiative
description: This grant provides support to the Crim Fitness Foundation to continue to serve as the lead agency for the community education model in Flint. The community education strategy involves increasing the depth and impact of programs at all Flint Community Schools buildings, the International Academy of Flint charter school and the Flint Cultural Center Academy. The central elements of community education that made it so effective in responding to the water crisis — caring relationships, a holistic approach to student and family wellbeing and social emotional supports — remain critical as students begin to emerge from the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Technical Assistance for Improved Teaching and Learning
description: This grant allows Michigan State University to support Flint Community Schools with technical assistance aimed at increasing district capacity, improving school culture, increasing operational efficiency and improving student academic outcomes. To achieve these goals, technical assistance will be focused on four primary components: districtwide systems, leadership development, classroom instruction and climate and culture.

title: Technical Assistance for Improved Teaching and Learning
description: This renewal grant will allow Michigan State University to continue providing support to Flint Community Schools with technical assistance aimed at increasing district capacity, improving school culture, increasing operational efficiency and improving student academic outcomes. To achieve these goals, technical assistance will be focused on four primary components: support for engaging Flint Board of Education, superintendent and executive team support and coaching, principal support and coaching, and districtwide data and federal funding support.

title: Early Childhood Capacity Building
description: This grant will provide funding to the Community Foundation of Greater Flint to support the expansion of early childhood education in Flint. Expanding access to high-quality early childhood education has always been important for the city, but became even more important following the water crisis. The grantee employs an executive director to manage the Flint Early Childhood Collaborative, a project that aims to increase access to and the quality of early childhood education in Flint through strategic planning, research, advocacy and participation in the Educare Learning Network.

title: YouthQuest After School Initiative
description: This renewal grant provides continued support to the Genesee Area Focus Fund for the YouthQuest After School Initiative. YouthQuest provides children and youth with opportunities to learn and grow through a safe, engaging and exciting afterschool learning experience surrounded by caring, responsible adults and sustained by involved and supportive community organizations.

title: Community Education Innovation Fund
description: This grant will provide funding in support of the Community Education Innovation Fund at the Crim Fitness Foundation. The initiative is designed to provide community school directors with opportunities and funding for innovative ideas and practices. This year the focus will be on innovation in the remote learning environment as well as parent and community engagement.

title: Community Education Innovation Fund
description: This grant will provide funding in support of the Community Education Innovation Fund at the Crim Fitness Foundation. The initiative is designed to provide community school directors with opportunities and funding for innovative ideas and practices. This year, the focus will be on innovation around the four core goals of community education as students return to classrooms after spending considerable time learning remotely during COVID-19.

title: Summer Youth Initiative and TeenQuest
description: This grant provides support to the Genesee Area Focus Fund to implement TeenQuest and the Summer Youth Initiative, which provide job training and employment opportunities for Genesee County teens in partnership with area employers. Teens participate first in TeenQuest, a pre-employment training program, and are then eligible to apply for employment through the Summer Youth Initiative.

title: Genesee Early College
description: Genesee Early College is an innovative, educational program administered by the Genesee Intermediate School District in collaboration with the University of Michigan-Flint and healthcare partners in the region. The focus of the project is to prepare high school students for academic and professional careers in health and sciences, technology, engineering and math fields. Students can earn up to 60 transferable college credits, as well as a high school diploma and scholarship funds for higher education.

title: Flint Healthcare Employment Opportunities Program
description: This grant to Greater Flint Health Coalition will support the Flint Healthcare Employment Opportunities Program. The goal of the program is to create sustainable employment opportunities and promote career advancement for area residents within the healthcare sector. Participants receive industry-focused life skills and career readiness training, occupational instruction, case management and supportive services as well as job development assistance.

title: Advancing Illinois Leadership on Great Lakes Protection
description: Illinois Environmental Council Education Fund is a statewide umbrella organization that unites 60 local community and environmental groups throughout the state. Lake Michigan supplies nearly seven million residents with drinking water, and the state receives substantial economic benefit from the lake and suffers when it is not prioritized. Illinois faces threats to future supplies of safe drinking water, including threats from lead pipes and plumbing. The grantee will work with its member groups to: develop new leadership for Illinois on key Great Lakes agencies and institutions; work to protect Lake Michigan against an Asian carp invasion; encourage efficient water management practices and advance policies to require removal of lead service lines; and reduce plastic pollution in the Great Lakes.

title: Lake Michigan Water Program
description: The Illinois Environmental Council Education Fund is the state’s most vibrant coalition of environmental advocacy affiliate organizations. The grantee leads coalition building, education and outreach efforts in support of efforts to better protect Lake Michigan and resources within Illinois. With prior support from the Foundation, the grantee has elevated statewide awareness of the need to invest in upgrading Illinois’ aging water infrastructure, much of which in the Great Lakes basin is burdened with lead. The grantee has embarked on an initiative to reduce pollution from plastic waste which is of particular importance in the Great Lakes basin. With renewed support, the Illinois Environmental Council Education Fund will create conditions to support investment in Illinois’ crumbling water infrastructure, address plastic pollution and help forge a new state water plan, all while seeking to ensure that clean, safe and affordable drinking water is accessible across the state including population centers in the Great Lakes basin.

title: Employment Preparation Program
description: This grant will provide support to the St. Luke N.E.W. Life Center for the Employment Preparation Program. Serving residents of north Flint, the program works with individuals who are structurally unemployed and need a broad array of wraparound services to prepare them to find and retain employment. The program will continue to expand its outreach to employers for future job placements and will offer an alumni network to support participants and past graduates. Additionally, the grantee will use funding to begin making non-medical grade masks to help prevent the spread of the coronavirus.

title: Employment Preparation Program
description: This grant will provide support to the St. Luke N.E.W. Life Center for the Employment Preparation Program. Serving residents of north Flint, the program works with individuals who are structurally unemployed and need a broad array of wraparound services to prepare them to find and retain employment. The program will continue to expand its outreach to employers for future job placements and will offer an alumni network to support participants and past graduates.

title: Flint STRIVE Academy Youth Empowerment Program
description: This grant to Specialized Employment Services, Inc. will support the Flint STRIVE Academy Youth Empowerment Program for at-risk youth ages 14-18. The program provides young people with a summertime employment experience and follow-up support services during the school year. Through attitudinal training, skill enhancement, mentoring and tutoring, the goal is to encourage youth to complete high school and help with making informed career decisions.

title: Flint STRIVE Replication Program
description: The Flint STRIVE Replication Program, a project of Specialized Employment Services, Inc., provides employment training, job placement and support services for hard-to-serve Flint area residents. A replication of the East Harlem Employment Service’s workforce training program, Flint STRIVE prepares participants for the workforce through a 19-day, 130-hour intensive workshop that emphasizes the attitudinal prerequisites for successful employment.

title: Operating Support
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Flint Cultural Center Corporation manages and maintains the 38-acre Flint Cultural Center campus which includes Flint Cultural Center Academy, Flint Institute of Arts, Flint Institute of Music, Flint Public Library, Longway Planetarium, Sloan Museum and Whiting Auditorium. The campus contributes positively to the quality of life in Flint through educational and cultural enrichment opportunities and has a significant economic impact through earned revenue and employment. Students and adults of all ability levels participate in or attend a variety of cultural, educational and instructional programs and activities across the campus. This grant will provide operating support to the Flint Cultural Center Corporation for campus improvements, grounds and maintenance, marketing, and campus security.

title: Operating Support
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Flint Institute of Arts, located on the Flint Cultural Center campus, features museum galleries, an Art School and studio space, and public areas that engage visitors and attract new audiences from across the region. Students and adults visit the galleries, participate in educational programs, take art classes or attend events held at the institute. This grant will provide operating support to enable the grantee to present new exhibits that inspire and stimulate visitors, provide educational programming to area students, offer instruction in various art mediums to people of all ages and maintain its facilities.

title: School and Community Programming
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: Flint Cultural Center Corporation provides opportunities for city of Flint and Genesee County underserved youth and residents of all ages to participate in the face-to-face and/or virtual educational and community engagement activities provided by the following Flint Cultural Center campus institutions: Sloan Museum and Longway Planetarium, Flint Institute of Arts and Flint Institute of Music, including The Whiting and Capitol Theatre.

title: Music Around Town
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Music Around Town series, formerly known as Music in the Parks, is a broad community partnership led by the Flint Institute of Music. This program offers musical performances in public places around Flint and streamed through social media platforms. Additionally, this year’s Music Around Town series will offer pop-up performances honoring frontline workers. Performances will follow all health guidelines, with careful consideration for the health and safety of the audience and musicians.

title: Tapology Youth Outreach
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide partial support for Tapology outreach programs. Tap dance is an enduring American art form that increases physical activity and enhances cognitive development for participants. The grantee partners with local schools and community centers to provide area youth with an introduction to tap dance and offers regular classes for all levels of ability. Each year, the grantee’s outreach programming culminates into a four day festival that provides exposure for local students to the art and history of tap. Professional artists will continue to provide instruction for beginners, as well as more advanced workshops for experienced young dancers.

title: General Purposes
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant provides general purposes support to the Buckham Fine Arts Project, also known as Buckham Gallery. Over the past 30 plus years, the grantee has held more than 300 exhibitions of visual art; poetry readings; performance art events; and dance, music and film presentations. The grantee showcases local, regional and international artists. Located in a storefront space on the corner of South Saginaw and Second Streets, Buckham Gallery programming has included monthly open mic nights, family art activities and events for older adults.

title: Event Policing and Public Safety
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide funds to support public safety enforcement and traffic control activities for festivals and events primarily in the downtown Flint area. Public safety is an essential component of the success of the festivals that take place in Flint and attract thousands of exhibitors and participants. The City of Flint is not in a financial position to provide the necessary additional police services due to a decline in municipal revenues.

title: Economic and Entrepreneurial Outreach
description: This grant will support the Economic Development Administration Center for Community and Economic Development at the University of Michigan-Flint. The center’s mission is to coordinate, inform and contribute to economic development efforts that cultivate innovation and advance high-growth entrepreneurship in the seven-county, I-69 Thumb Region. Additionally, the center supports applied research projects and provides technical assistance to economic development organizations, private businesses and nonprofits.

title: Operating Support
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will renew operating support for the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation and redevelopment efforts through its supported organization, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation. The Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation and the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation have been leaders in efforts to revitalize Flint’s downtown district focusing on redeveloping properties for residential and commercial reuse, attracting new employers and creating and enhancing community amenities for public use. This grant will be used by the grantee to support staffing costs to facilitate the charitable purposes and functions of the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, as well as costs for office space rental, contracted services and technology.

title: General Purposes
description: This renewal grant provides general purposes funding to the Center for Community Progress. The organization supports work in Flint and nationally that addresses property vacancy and abandonment through a combination of technical assistance, policy reform, network building, knowledge sharing, communications programs and leadership and education. The grantee is headquartered in Flint and has an office in Washington, D.C.

title: Capacity Building
description: This grant will help to build the staff capacity of Communities First, Inc., a nonprofit housing developer and community development agency in Flint. The grantee’s mission is to promote and provide an improved quality of life for residents of distressed communities through economic development and affordable housing solutions. This grant will partially fund positions related to project and fund development, strategic planning and office management.

title: Capacity Building
description: This grant will help to build the staff capacity of Communities First, a nonprofit housing developer and community development agency in Flint. The grantee’s mission is to promote and provide an improved quality of life for residents of distressed communities through economic development and affordable housing solutions. This grant will partially fund positions related to project and fund development, strategic planning, office management and predevelopment expenses.

title: Homeowner Occupied Repair Program
description: This grant will support Genesee County Habitat for Humanity to operate its Homeowner Occupied Repair Program in the neighborhood surrounding Durant-Tuuri-Mott campus. The grantee will partner with local organizations to connect residents to programs and leverage additional resources for home repair. This work aligns with a core tenant of Genesee County Habitat for Humanity’s mission of bringing people together to build community.

title: Neighborhood Strategy Coordinator
description: This grant will support the Genesee County Land Bank Authority in coordinating a neighborhood enhancement strategy surrounding Durant-Tuuri-Mott Elementary School. These coordination efforts will include identifying the status of all neighborhood parcels, connecting with existing resources and partners and identifying gaps or needs in the neighborhood. Close alignment with nonprofits, governmental agencies, institutions, neighborhood groups, foundations and individuals is necessary to leverage revitalization resources and coordinate neighborhood improvement efforts.

title: Capacity Building
description: The Hispanic Technology & Community Center of Greater Flint, known as the Latinx Technology & Community Center, provides many programs and services to enhance the dignity and quality of life for the Flint and Genesee County Latino community as well as those from other cultures. The grantee will utilize Mott Foundation funds to support an executive director position to increase its capacity to serve Flint residents.

title: Flint-based Healthcare Startup Accelerator
description: This grant will provide support to XLerateHealth, a healthcare business accelerator located in the Ferris Wheel building in downtown Flint. The accelerator serves as an entry point for entrepreneurs working to create healthcare-related enterprises. A high-functioning accelerator can attract new businesses to the Flint area, spur economic growth and create job opportunities for local residents. XLerateHealth will play a key role in the build-out of a regional health science entrepreneurial ecosystem in Flint and Genesee County.

title: Flint Food Works Commercial Kitchen
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will support the Flint Food Works commercial kitchen located within the Flint Farmers’ Market. Flint Food Works has the capacity to incubate small food processors seeking to create nutritional products for distribution and prepared food for retail consumption. The program offers a unique community benefit by providing nutritional education to residents on how to prepare healthy food. Flint Food Works is managed by the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation’s supported organization, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation.

title: Flint Food Works Commercial Kitchen
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This renewal grant will provide continued support for the Flint Food Works commercial kitchen food business incubator located within the Flint Farmers’ Market. Flint Food Works has the capacity to incubate small food processors seeking to create nutritional products for distribution and prepared food for retail consumption. The program offers a unique community benefit by providing nutritional education to residents on how to prepare healthy food. Flint Food Works is managed by the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation’s supported organization, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation.

title: Flint SOUP Community Funded Micro-grant Program
description: This grant will enable the Flint SOUP Community Funded Micro-grant program to continue operations and provide more opportunities for Flint’s underserved residents to participate in entrepreneurship. Founded in 2012, Flint SOUP is a project of the United Way of Genesee County. The program hosts micro-grant competitions where creators and entrepreneurs can obtain small amounts of financial support and technical assistance to invest in their ideas. While the program is designed to support entrepreneurship, it simultaneously fosters community engagement and resident participation.

title: Flint SOUP Community Funded Micro-grant Program
description: This grant will enable the Flint SOUP Community Funded Micro-grant Program to continue operations and provide more opportunities for Flint’s underserved residents to participate in entrepreneurship. Founded in 2012, Flint SOUP is a project of the United Way of Genesee County. The program hosts micro-grant competitions where creators and entrepreneurs can obtain small amounts of financial support and technical assistance to support their ideas. While the program is designed to support entrepreneurship, it simultaneously fosters community engagement and resident participation.

title: Flint National Service Accelerator Fund
description: The Flint National Service Accelerator Fund helps Flint and Genesee County agencies leverage state and national service members through the Corporation for National and Community Service and its affiliates. Flint area service members support projects aligned with the City of Flint’s master plan, emerging community needs and the federal priorities. Focus areas in Flint include community education, public safety, nutrition and assisting Flint to recover and rise from the Flint water crisis and global pandemic. Matching grants from the fund provide resources to local nonprofit agencies for the required member cost share, training and travel reimbursement. The fund was previously held at the Community Foundation of Greater Flint but is now administered by the United Way of Genesee County, which also provides staffing for the Flint National Service Accelerator.

title: Flint National Service Accelerator Fund
description: The Flint National Service Accelerator Fund helps Flint and Genesee County agencies leverage state and national service members through the Corporation for National and Community Service and its affiliates. Flint area service members support projects aligned with the City of Flint’s master plan, emerging community needs, and state and federal priorities. Focus areas in Flint include community education, public safety, nutrition, and assisting Flint to recover and rise from the Flint water crisis and global pandemic. New program areas relating to climate change and social justice will provide additional areas of service in Flint. Matching grants from the fund provide resources to local nonprofit agencies for the required member cost share, training and travel reimbursement. The fund is administered by the United Way of Genesee County, which also provides staffing for the Flint National Service Accelerator.

title: Double Up Food Bucks Project
description: This grant will provide additional support to the Fair Food Network’s Double Up Food Bucks project in Flint. The project provides incentives for supplemental nutrition assistance program recipients to purchase fresh fruits and vegetables and dairy products at the Flint Farmers’ Market and grocery stores in Flint. Good nutrition, especially foods high in iron, calcium and vitamin C, can help mitigate the impact of lead exposure to Flint children and adults.

title: Double Up Food Bucks Project
description: This grant will provide support to the Fair Food Network’s Double Up Food Bucks project in Flint. The project provides incentives for supplemental nutrition assistance program recipients to purchase fresh fruits and vegetables and dairy products at the Flint Farmers’ Market and grocery stores in Flint. Good nutrition, especially foods high in iron, calcium and vitamin C, can help mitigate the impact of lead exposure to Flint children and adults. Started at five farmers markets, Double Up Food Bucks is now implemented at 234 sites in Michigan and is a national model for healthy food incentives across 29 states.

title: Flint National Service Accelerator Initiative
description: This renewal grant to the United Way of Genesee County will support the Flint National Service Accelerator Initiative, which is part of a continuum of community volunteer and national service opportunities. The initiative leverages local, state and federal resources to increase the number of national service members providing direct service and capacity-building personnel to Flint area organizations. This grant provides funds for a civic engagement manager to implement the program.

title: Neighborhood Arts and Cultural Events
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will support arts and culture projects through the Neighborhood Small Grants Program at the Community Foundation of Greater Flint. Neighborhood groups will implement resident-led efforts to create or enhance and expand existing artistic projects or events/performances. Funded projects will aim to stimulate civic engagement, improve neighborhood conditions, provide opportunities for self-expression and/or enhance skills for residents to work together creatively.

title: General Purposes
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant provides general purposes funding for the operations of the Greater Flint Arts Council, an independent organization which supports local artists and arts participants through several programs, including public festivals and events. With a goal of being a catalyst for diverse artistic and cultural programs for the region, the grantee enriches the community with an array of cultural services, educational programs, publications and events.

title: Parade of Festivals
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Greater Flint Arts Council continues to provide leadership for a coalition of stakeholders aimed at improving the image of the Flint area, including downtown, through increased participation in festivals and events especially during warm weather months. This funding supports a series of events and marketing activities designed to maximize the impact of established events and to cultivate newer and smaller events in downtown Flint and neighborhoods throughout the city.

title: Downtown Security
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This renewal grant will support the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation’s efforts to promote safety and security in downtown Flint. The grantee is dedicated to supporting revitalization projects that enhance quality of life and provide local and regional access to jobs, food, healthcare, and other essential services.The Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, a supported organization of the grantee, will contract with a security firm for guards to patrol the city’s downtown area.

title: Flint Farmers' Market Operating Support
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will provide operational support for the Flint Farmers’ Market, a key institution in the ongoing efforts to revitalize downtown Flint. Located in the Health and Wellness District, the market provides Flint residents with year-round access to fresh produce and locally grown foods. The market maintains an active calendar of community events, provides attractive public meeting spaces and supports food entrepreneurs through a commercial kitchen coworking space. The Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation is the supporting organization of the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, which operates the Flint Farmers’ Market.

title: Flint BRAND Program
description: The purpose of the project is to implement transformative projects that leave sustainable, positive impact on neighborhoods. The Genesee County Habitat for Humanity works with neighborhood associations, block clubs and other local grassroots groups on leadership development and other forms of capacity building. This grant will provide support for the Flint BRAND Program, which builds the capacity of neighborhood groups to conceptualize, plan and assist in implementing projects. These projects will have an immediate visible impact on neighborhood conditions and improve Flint residents’ quality of life. Founded in 1990, the grantee is an affiliate of Habitat for Humanity International, a nonprofit, ecumenical Christian housing ministry. Its mission is to bring people together to build homes, communities and hope.

title: Neighborhood and Community Planning
description: This grant supports the Genesee County Land Bank Authority’s planning and neighborhood revitalization activities. The grantee develops and operates a nationally renowned program to reclaim vacant and abandoned property and restore it to productive use. This function is overseen by a professional planning and development team that attracts resources and plans, coordinates and implements neighborhood interventions using a variety of tools and strategies. The grantees activities simultaneously enhance the quality of neighborhoods in Flint and promotes citizen stewardship by engaging neighborhood groups in planning the disposition and use of vacant structures, as well as maintaining vacant lots.

title: Flint and Genesee County Community Development Project
description: The Local Initiatives Support Corporation provides grants, loans and technical assistance to community development corporations. The grantee will focus on community development and technical assistance as part of its Opportunity in America’s Neighborhoods strategy. The grantee’s catalyzing opportunity strategy brings together a comprehensive set of tools to increase incomes, build equity and grow wealth.

title: Capacity Building
description: Metro Community Development is a multiservice community development corporation dedicated to creating stable and vibrant neighborhoods in Flint and Genesee County. The grantee serves as both an intermediary and a direct service provider for federal and state programs designed to assist low-income residents. This grant will be used to strengthen the grantee’s asset development division, which includes the federal Community Development Financial Institutions program.

title: General Purposes
description: The Village Information Center was established in 1976 and has published hundreds of issues of the East Village Magazine. This grant renewal will allow the grantee to cover more newsworthy stories to keep Flint residents informed about their community and life in neighborhoods. A companion website will offer access to news captured in the magazine, as well as new information that does not make the magazine’s publishing deadline.

title: Factory Two Project
description: This grant will provide support to Red Ink Flint to manage the Factory Two Project. In addition to Factory Two, the grantee operates Flint Local 432, a performance venue located in downtown Flint. Factory Two is an affordable community makerspace where creative people gather to work on product ideas and network with each other. As the Factory Two Project aims to rebuild its membership base following many challenges brought on by the pandemic, the grantee will use Mott Foundation funds to support operations and programmatic activities.

title: Soup Kitchens, Warming Center and Medical Transportation
grantee: Catholic Charities of Shiawassee and Genesee Counties
description: This grant will provide support to Catholic Charities of Shiawassee and Genesee Counties to operate intervention services for individuals and families in crisis. There are three soup kitchens and the Center for Hope Warming Center that will provide meals, personal need items and a place to find warmth during the harsh winter months. The St. Christopher Medical Transportation Program will also provide transportation for critically ill children and their families to medical appointments across the state.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to the Crim Fitness Foundation. Focusing on active living, physical fitness, nutrition and mindfulness, the grantee offers year-round programming for children and adults throughout the greater Flint area. The grantee also serves as the lead agency for the Community Education Initiative, which provides access to a variety of wraparound health and educational services for many Flint students and their families. The HAP Crim Festival of Races typically attracts more than 11,000 walkers and runners, as well as tens of thousands of spectators each year.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purposes support to the United Way of Genesee County, a health and human services organization serving the residents of Genesee County through its four community impact focus areas of education, financial stability, health and basic needs. In addition to the core support areas, the grantee provides nonprofit sector capacity support through aligned fiduciary services and specific capacity building activities. The grantee was heavily involved in the response to the Flint water crisis, and since March 2020, has become a key organization in the community response to the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Nonprofit Capacity Building
description: The purpose of this renewal grant is to support the Nonprofit Center of the United Way of Genesee County, which offers a broad range of services to support nonprofits through capacity building, volunteer management and national service resources. Since the grantee began capacity-building work in 2003, over 100 Genesee County agencies have received services that have allowed them to help more individuals in need, leverage new financial and human capital, and collaborate with cross-sector leaders to ensure alignment with community needs.

title: Immigration Services
description: Established in 1988, the Arab American Heritage Council serves the needs of Arab Americans and other recent immigrants in the Genesee County area through programming such as immigration services, civic engagement and cultural events. During the grant period, the grantee will continue to help immigrants from all backgrounds navigate the American legal system and become acclimated to life in the United States by providing immigration forums and educational workshops, assisting with immigration casework, offering translation services and leading citizenship classes.

title: Flint and Genesee Literacy Network
description: Mott Community College serves as the lead agency for the Flint and Genesee Literacy Network. The network is a coalition of community organizations, businesses and governmental leaders working toward increasing literacy and basic skill levels in Genesee County. The grantee will work with network partners to increase their capacity to deliver high-quality early education and family literacy programming with a particular focus on two-generational approaches.

title: Berston Field House Capacity Building
description: This grant will assist the United Way of Genesee County and the Friends of Berston Field House to sustain staff operations and increase organizational capacity. Friends of Berston Field House’s mission is to impact the community through education, athletics, arts, and comprehensive services. With this support, Friends of Berston Field House will be able to transition essential staff to full time.

title: European Programme for Integration and Migration
description: The European Programme for Integration and Migration is a donor collaborative hosted by the Network of European Foundations for Innovative Cooperation. Established in 2005, this program strengthens the role played by civil society organizations in advocating for constructive approaches to migration in Europe.This is done through grantmaking, capacity development and networking activities addressing a range of issues, including: asylum seekers; undocumented migrants; and equality, integration, and social inclusion of vulnerable migrants. Between 2005 and 2020, this program has: involved 36 European foundations in collaborative programming and grantmaking; leveraged funding from these foundations; provided more than 20 million Euros to over 300 civil society organizations; and organized more than 70 pan-European exchange, training and networking events involving over 3,500 participants. Based in Brussels, the Network of European Foundations for Innovative Cooperation strengthens cooperation among foundations in Europe.

title: Economic and Entrepreneurial Outreach
description: This grant increase will support the Economic Development Administration Center for Community and Economic Development at the University of Michigan-Flint. The grantee will host a series of round-tables that will build on the momentum gained through the 2018 Aspire to Transform Symposium held in partnership with The Brookings Institution. The goal is to leverage The Brookings Institution’s research to inspire dialogue and create solutions to economic and community development issues that are relevant to the Flint region.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will assist the Ukrainian Helsinki Human Rights Union in their efforts to increase access to justice in Ukraine through protection of fundamental rights and freedoms. Particular attention will be given to documenting and seeking redress from crimes arising from Russia’s illegal invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Through its member organizations, which operate 22 public reception offices, the grantee will connect civilian victims to relevant justice services, placing accountability and war-related monitoring and documentation at the heart of human rights work. It will educate a range of justice service providers in Ukraine about international humanitarian law and how to gather evidence and develop cases. It will additionally pursue war-related strategic litigation, both nationally and internationally. In 2021-22, the grantee provided nearly 20,000 individual consultations through its legal aid centers, despite the disruptions of the COVID-19 pandemic and a full-scale military invasion. Through its lengthy experience of bringing cases to the European Court of Human Rights, it has proven to be an important player in a Ukrainian government initiative to hold Russian forces accountable for destruction of property, with over 60,000 submissions received so far. Established in 2004, the Ukrainian Helsinki Human Rights Union works to promote practical observance of the range of international human rights instruments to which Ukraine is a party.

title: Youth Substance Abuse Reduction Program
grantee: Institute for Behavior and Health, Inc.
description: This grant will provide funds to the Institute for Behavior and Health, Inc. to continue to advance the critical messaging aimed at curbing adolescent substance abuse. Central to this initiative will be physician education and working with lead organizations in the field to promote the acceptance and integration of consistent messaging that promotes a no-use policy of alcohol, tobacco, marijuana, or other drugs among youth.

title: Youth Empowerment Partnership Programme
grantee: International Academy Berlin for Innovative Pedagogy, Psychology and Economy gGmbH
description: The project goal is to bring about sustainable change in local communities across Europe through innovative approaches to youth empowerment and community development. The International Academy Berlin for Innovative Pedagogy, Psychology and Economy gGmbH provides technical assistance, organizes networking opportunities and coordinates joint initiatives for the Youth Empowerment Partnership Programme, a Europe-wide network of community-based youth projects. During 2019-2020, the grantee supported 46 local program sites and project partners across 19 European countries. The grantee provided direct technical assistance to local program sites in the network, trained young people and community stakeholders on a range of topics and organized international networking opportunities for young people and practitioners. The International Academy of Berlin for Innovative Pedagogy, Psychology and Economy gGmbH, based in Berlin, Germany, and its partners secured significant European Commission funding for a range of projects.

title: Promoting Sustainability in Energy and Infrastructure Investments in Latin America
description: The Interamerican Association for Environmental Defense is a nonprofit environmental law and policy organization in Latin America and the United States. The grantee’s attorneys participate in regional and international processes to guide sustainable energy and infrastructure investments in Latin America. Over the previous grant period, the grantee worked on the revision of the Inter-American Development Bank Environmental and Social Framework, developed tools to protect environmental defenders and worked to improve best practices for environmental impact statements. Over the next grant period, the grantee will monitor the implementation of the new environmental social governance framework of the Inter-American Development Bank; coordinate and strengthen strategies to protect environmental defenders; and continue the analysis of international best practices for environmental impact review processes.

title: Youth Entrepreneurship Promotion
description: The Philanthropy Roundtable exists to help donors achieve their charitable goals and to protect their freedom to give as they choose. For more than 25 years, the grantee has supported philanthropists in their efforts to achieve results with their giving. This grant will support the work of the Economic Opportunity Program at the Philanthropy Roundtable. The goal of the project is to promote youth entrepreneurship among donors and build a network of funders to support the field.

title: Expanding Distributed Renewable Energy in the Amazon
description: The Brazilian Association of Distributed Generation is a trade group of more than 400 companies working in the renewable energy sector. This project would support the association to organize an Amazon forum for member companies and officials in Amazon municipalities. The project will promote policies and programs to expand access and supply chains for distributed solar energy in small Amazon cities and remote communities.

title: Renewable Energy for Extractive Reserves in the Amazon
description: This project supports the World Wildlife Fund and its partner, World Wildlife Fund Brazil, to work on establishing a public policy to support renewable energy access for forest-dwelling communities living in sustainable development reserves in the Amazon. The goal is to design and implement a renewable energy development model. This grant increase will enable the grantee to establish a network of organizations with similar goals. To support the network, the grantee will compile and publish the data and results of model renewable energy access projects in the Amazon.

title: Western Balkans Community Foundations
geographic_focus: Bosnia and Herzegovina, North Macedonia, Albania, Montenegro, Serbia, Kosovo
description: The project goal is to expand and strengthen the community foundation field in the Western Balkans region. To this end, the Trag Foundation will work to increase the number of community foundations in Serbia and facilitate learning and cooperation among community foundations in the region. More specifically, the grantee will promote the concept and practice of community foundations, facilitate the establishment of new community foundations and develop their capacities. In addition, the grantee will connect the new community foundations to existing networks and initiatives, including the European Community Foundation Initiative. During the past grant period, the Trag Foundation increased its capacity to support community foundation development, researched opportunities for community foundation development in six countries in the Western Balkans and supported the establishment of three new community foundations in Serbia.

title: General Purposes
description: The Flint River and its tributaries are an important recreational resource for the region’s residents while also providing important habitat for a variety of freshwater species and other wildlife. The Flint River Watershed Coalition works to protect the Flint River and its tributaries. With this renewal grant, the grantee will maintain all of its education and outreach efforts and attend to its own organizational development needs.

title: Community Advice Office Support Project
description: The project goal is to increase access to justice for poor and marginalized communities in South Africa. To this end, ProBono.Org will work closely with community advice offices in the Gauteng province of South Africa. Key interventions include back-up legal services, capacity-building, and financial support to community advice offices. The grantee is a non-partisan civil society organization that subscribes to the values of transformative constitutionalism, the rule of law, and social justice. Its primary focus is to harness the skills and expertise of legal practitioners to deliver pro bono civil legal assistance to organizations working for social justice and to expand access to justice for low-income, vulnerable, and marginalized communities.

title: Healthy Flint Research Coordinating Center-Community Core
description: Flint Odyssey House established the Community Core of the Healthy Flint Research Coordinating Center in 2016. This initiative was created to better advocate on behalf of community residents to help derive maximum health benefits from research conducted locally. The primary task of the Community Core is to coordinate research conducted in Flint to prevent fragmented and duplicated work across local universities and hospitals, increase the community voice, and ensure ethical community involvement. The Flint Odyssey House is uniquely positioned to shepherd this work due to its existing connections and trust in the community.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to cultivate a strong global movement for legal empowerment. Namati will work to strengthen the Global Legal Empowerment Network, which brings together over 2,300 organizations. The grantee will build capacity of additional regional anchor organizations to take on greater responsibility for convening, learning and advocacy. The grantee will continue country-level programs in Kenya, Sierra Leone, Myanmar, India, Mozambique and within the United States, focusing on specific issues such as land tenure, health rights, citizenship and environmental justice. Additionally, the grantee will gather and distribute compelling evidence of the efficacy of legal empowerment approaches in addressing people’s justice needs. In 2019-20, the grantee successfully challenged an exclusionary law in Kenya that would have left five million Kenyans without legal protection. The grantee helped inform important protections for land tenure in Sierra Leone and Myanmar. In the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic, the grantee launched a dedicated fund to channel support to legal empowerment groups addressing health, social and economic consequences in their communities. Established in 2011, Namati works to build a global movement of grassroots legal advocates who give people the power to understand, use and shape the law.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will assist Namati in their efforts to cultivate a strong global movement for legal empowerment. The grantee will work to strengthen the Global Legal Empowerment Network which now brings together over 3,000 organizations. The grantee will further build the capacity of regional anchor organizations to move greater responsibility for convening, learning and advocacy from its U.S. headquarters. The grantee will also continue country-level programs in Kenya, Sierra Leone, Myanmar, India, Mozambique and within the U.S., focusing on specific issues such as land tenure, health rights, citizenship and environmental justice. Additionally, through an extensive program of research and analysis, the grantee will gather and distribute compelling evidence of the efficacy of legal empowerment approaches in addressing people’s justice needs. In 2021-22, communities supported by the grantee in Kenya successfully petitioned for easing of that country’s identification procedures. In Sierra Leone, new laws protecting land rights were adopted following years of local legal struggles to secure these rights. The grantee also helped establish the Mid-Atlantic Environmental and Economic Justice Coalition of 30 organizations in U.S. Mid-Atlantic states. Established in 2011, Namati works to build a global movement of grassroots legal advocates who give people the power to understand, use and shape the law.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will assist Namati in their efforts to cultivate a strong global movement for legal empowerment. The grantee will work to strengthen the renamed Grassroots Justice Network which now brings together representatives from over 4,100 organizations. The grantee will aim to establish the Grassroots Justice Academy as the leading learning vehicle for legal empowerment. The grantee will also continue country-level programs in specific countries tentatively identified as Kenya, Sierra Leone, Myanmar, India, Mozambique and within the U.S. Particular attention will be given to issues of land, the environment and climate justice. In 2023-24, the grantee and its community paralegal partners directly helped over 360,000 people benefit from legal practices and protections. Outcomes included: 1) improved procedures for securing identification documents in Kenya; 2) transparent environmental health information for property buyers in Maryland; and 3) strengthened health privacy protections in Mozambique. Established in 2011, Namati works to build a global movement of grassroots legal advocates who give people the power to understand, use and shape the law.

title: Afterschool College and Career Readiness Initiative
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant to the Nebraska Children and Families Foundation will enable the Nebraska Statewide Afterschool Network to develop a college and career readiness system for afterschool programs in Nebraska. This project will support the network to: 1) build a network of partners in the state focused on college and career readiness; 2) convene partners, stakeholders, and students to design, pilot, and scale college and career readiness programming; and 3) incorporate children’s savings accounts and financial literacy training into the programming. The grantee will share lessons learned with other state networks to enhance college and career readiness initiatives in afterschool programs.

title: Afterschool College and Career Readiness Initiative
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant to the Fund for Educational Excellence will enable the Maryland Statewide Afterschool Network to develop a middle and high school college and career readiness framework, toolkit, and training for afterschool, summer, and mentoring programs. This project will support the network to: 1) create a college and career framework, curriculum, and toolkit; 2) develop multi-level training and professional development to disseminate resources; and 3) facilitate a college and career professional learning community for afterschool, summer, and mentoring professionals. The grantee will share lessons learned with other state networks to enhance college and career readiness initiatives in afterschool programs.

title: Afterschool College and Career Readiness Initiative
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant to the Indiana Afterschool Network, Inc. will enable the Indiana Statewide Afterschool Network to strengthen the role of afterschool programs by increasing engagement and exposure to college and career readiness for K-12 children, youth, and families. This project will support the network to: 1) expand and develop new partnerships to align statewide college and career exploration and affordability initiatives; 2) develop resources to increase student and family exposure and engagement in college and career readiness; and 3) provide resources and professional development for afterschool professionals on college and career readiness. The grantee will share lessons learned with other state networks to enhance college and career readiness initiatives in afterschool programs.

title: Afterschool College and Career Readiness Initiative
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant to the University of Missouri-Columbia will enable the Missouri Statewide Afterschool Network to increase the number of middle and high school 21st Century Community Learning Centers programs offering quality college and career readiness programming to low-income youth. This project will support the network to: 1) identify local and state initiatives, organizations and other entities that support college and career readiness; 2) increase the resources, supports, and professional development available to afterschool professionals; and 3) assist key partner organizations to expand their projects to include afterschool as a strategy for college and career readiness. The grantee will share lessons learned with other state networks to enhance college and career readiness initiatives in afterschool programs.

title: Jazz at Lincoln Center Content Development
description: This grant will support Foundations, Inc. to: 1) co-develop new innovative program curricula and resources with Jazz at Lincoln Center for the Mott afterschool App to increase the quality and sustainability of afterschool programs; and 2) provide comprehensive services and supports to enhance learning experiences and professional development opportunities to the afterschool field.

title: VISTA Project
description: This grant will support the Afterschool Alliance to partner with AmeriCorps VISTA to: 1) enhance the capacity of statewide afterschool networks; 2) increase utilization of the afterschool meals program; 3) support STEM learning opportunities within the afterschool field; 4) increase access to high-quality education, enrichment, and mentoring opportunities for young people of color; and 5) support the statewide afterschool networks to provide trauma-informed training and resources for afterschool program staff.

title: Advocacy Training
description: This grant will support the Alliance for Justice in providing customized advocacy trainings and resources for the statewide afterschool networks and afterschool grantees. The trainings and resources will build the capacity of the Advancing Afterschool grantees to educate policymakers and increase access to quality afterschool programs for young people.

title: Education Policy Institute
description: This grant will provide funds for Furman University to operate the White-Riley-Peterson Policy Institute, which brings together a diverse group of 15 emerging leaders from the afterschool and education fields to serve as fellows. Over the course of a year, fellows will work with policy experts, complete an intensive policy curriculum and participate in national networking opportunities. The fellowship will enable participants to positively contribute to the development of policies and practices that support afterschool and summer learning opportunities for children across the country.

title: General Purposes
description: Established in 1990, the National Council of Nonprofits is the nation’s largest network of nonprofits, representing more than 25,000 organizations across the country. Its mission is to advance the vital role, capacity, and voice of charitable nonprofit organizations. The grantee works through its network of state associations to help nonprofits operate more effectively, engage in critical policy issues affecting the sector, and achieve greater impact in their communities. The grantee is best known for its robust public policy advocacy, including defending the Johnson Amendment, ensuring a fair 2020 census count, removing new taxes on nonprofits, and expanding the charitable giving deduction. The grantee requests a grant increase so that it can undertake a process to ensure its long-term sustainability.

title: Midwest Children's Savings Account Initiative
grantee: Heartland Alliance for Human Needs & Human Rights
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
geographic_focus: Minnesota, Ohio, Wisconsin, Illinois, Indiana, Michigan
description: This grant will enable Heartland Alliance for Human Needs & Human Rights to organize the Midwest Children’s Savings Account Consortium. The overall goal of the project is to encourage and support the development of new and existing children’s savings account initiatives. During the next two years, the grantee will promote savings account initiatives and organize networking opportunities for interested stakeholders. Located in Chicago, Illinois, the grantee is a comprehensive anti-poverty organization.

title: Children's Savings Accounts Strategies for Community Foundations
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: The overall goal of this project is to form a strategy to gain momentum in connecting community foundations and children’s savings accounts programs. The work of CFLeads encourages community foundations to promote and adopt programs and policies that help low-income families increase income and build assets. In recent years, the grantee has built a history of supporting the development of children’s savings accounts within a small cohort of community foundations. However, the grantee hopes to access the larger field of community foundations to explore interest and knowledge in children’s savings accounts programs. To further uncover interest in children’s savings accounts, CFLeads will survey its constituents to understand the larger field of community foundations’ level of interest, as well as discover the types of learning opportunities that will work best for them.

title: General Purposes
description: The Climate Leadership Council is an international research and advocacy organization whose mission is to develop and promote a carbon dividends framework as a viable climate change policy solution. The council’s proposals have received considerable attention from the media, policymakers, and the general public. With renewed support, the grantee will continue to pursue its aims by expanding its stakeholder network, undertaking multidisciplinary policy research, educating policymakers, and orchestrating public education campaigns.

title: General Purposes
description: The Climate Leadership Council is an international research and advocacy organization whose mission is to develop and promote a carbon dividends framework as a viable climate change policy solution. The grantee’s proposals have received considerable attention from the media, policymakers, and the general public. With renewed support, the grantee will continue to pursue its aims by expanding its stakeholder network, undertaking multidisciplinary policy research, educating policymakers, and orchestrating public education campaigns.

title: General Purposes
description: The Climate Leadership Council is a research and advocacy organization whose mission is to develop and promote a carbon dividends framework as a viable climate change policy solution. The grantee aims to influence the international climate policy debates, but is currently focused primarily on the United States. The grantee’s proposals have received considerable attention from the media, policymakers and the general public. With renewed support, the Climate Leadership Council will continue to pursue its aims by expanding its stakeholder network, undertaking multidisciplinary policy research, educating policymakers and orchestrating public education initiatives.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to encourage the development of philanthropy and civic engagement in Turkey. The Support Foundation for Civil Society, a Turkish foundation established in December 2014, will develop its organizational and programmatic capacities to facilitate systematic giving and mentoring to nonprofits by individuals and corporations in Turkey and internationally. In 2016-2018, the grantee awarded 59 grants totaling approximately $275,000 with funds raised from more than 390 individual and institutional donors. Grants supported small, issue-based, community-level nonprofits across Turkey that demonstrated innovative programming and a vision for further organizational development. The grantee is based in Istanbul, Turkey.

title: East Africa Philanthropy Infrastructure Assessment
description: The project goal is to generate knowledge about the state of giving in East Africa through research. Charities Aid Foundation will conduct a study in Kenya, Uganda, and Tanzania with the aim of understanding the culture of giving and philanthropy and the state of civil society in the region. In addition, the study will focus on understanding the policies and mechanisms that enable giving and the institutions that exist in identified countries to support and promote philanthropy. Findings will be shared widely and serve as a resource to developing policy messages at country and regional levels.
