Charities Aid Foundation has over 90 years of experience working to stimulate philanthropy and social investment through research and by advocating for a favorable policy environment for giving. Based in the United Kingdom, it has a global alliance of locally registered organizations in the United States, South Africa, Australia, India, Bulgaria, Brazil, Canada, and Russia. Through its global alliance network, the grantee has been able to produce research on giving from different parts of the world.

title: Impact of Partnerships and Trusts Supporting Civil Society in Eastern Europe
grantee: Research Foundation of the City University of New York
description: The project goal is to document and analyze the lessons learned from five donor partnerships that supported civil society development in Central and Eastern Europe during the past 20 years. Through field research and review of existing documentation, researchers will explore the setup, operation, and impact of the five donor partnerships and trusts established over the last 25 years to support civil society development in Eastern Europe. This grant increase to the Research Foundation of the City University of New York will support additional field work and a broader dissemination strategy.

title: Mobile Mental Health Unit Project
description: This grant will provide support to Genesee Health System for a mental health mobile clinic in Flint. The mobile clinic staff will provide mental and behavioral health services, education on available resources, and referrals to other programs for adults and children impacted by the trauma and stress of the Flint water crisis. Services will be offered at a variety of locations throughout the community including events, neighborhood centers, schools, and other locations where residents gather.

title: Community Philanthropy Development in Brazil
grantee: Institute for the Development of Social Investment
description: The project goal is to promote community philanthropy in Brazil. Over the past two years, the Institute for the Development of Social Investment has: 1) supported Brazil’s three existing community foundations; 2) created a toolkit for community foundations; 3) helped establish two new community foundations; 4) supported initiative groups in another seven locations; and 5) raised funds from Brazilian sources to support community foundations. Over the next two years, the grantee plans to: 1) support the establishment of at least six new community foundations; 2) foster a favorable enabling environment for community foundations; 3) expand the knowledge and engagement of civil society with community foundations; and 4) increase the number of national and local supporters of community foundations. Founded in 1999, the Institute for the Development of Social Investment is a philanthropy service organization that promotes private social investment and strategic philanthropy, primarily in Brazil, but also throughout Latin America, and is an affiliate of the Charities Aid Foundation Global Alliance.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to support the field of community foundations in Mexico. Founded in 2011, Comunalia is an alliance of 17 Mexican community foundations focused on local development and strategic social investment. Over the past three years, the grantee conducted a broad range of work to expand and strengthen Mexico’s community foundation field, including helping members adopt Vital Signs and Sustainable Development Goals, developing online knowledge resources and channeling financial resources to community foundations. In addition, the grantee and its members have generously hosted community foundation stakeholders from other Latin American countries. Over the next three years, Comunalia will pursue the following objectives: 1) strengthen Mexican community foundations’ institutional capacities; 2) increase its own resources and foster new income streams for its members; 3) promote the creation of new Mexican community foundations; 4) raise the profile of community foundations in Mexico; and 5) strengthen itself internally to increase its reach and impact.

title: Small Grants and Capacity Building Program
description: The project goal is to expand and strengthen the community foundation field in southern Africa. To achieve this, the Southern Africa Trust will promote the community foundation concept by supporting established and emerging community foundations and other similar philanthropic organizations. In addition, the grantee will develop the capacities of new community foundations, provide small grants to emerging community foundations and initiatives, and create platforms for networking that advance the field of community foundations in the region. Since its establishment in 2005, the Southern Africa Trust has provided over $16 million in grants to civil society organizations, making it one of the leading indigenous grantmaking organizations in the region. In the past, the grantee supported community philanthropy initiatives in South Africa through Mott support. It will build on this experience to support community foundation development in the region.

title: Community Foundation Development in Kenya
description: The goal of this project is to support the development of community foundations in Kenya. To achieve this goal, the Kenya Community Development Foundation will increase awareness and understanding of the community foundation concept in Kenya, build the capacity of existing community foundation initiatives to support their evolution into community foundations, facilitate knowledge exchange in the field, and support community foundations to build long-term sustainability strategies. In addition, the grantee will build support for community foundations at the national level by identifying key collaborators and develop a long-term strategy for community foundation development in Kenya. The grantee is a grantmaking organization established in 1997 to support poor and marginalized communities to improve their quality of life and take charge of development activities in their communities. Over the years, the Kenya Community Development Foundation has built strong partnerships with government and businesses to support community-led development in communities that are on the margins of society.

title: Community Foundation Development in Ghana
description: The purpose of the project is to develop community foundations in Ghana. To achieve this goal, the Pure Trust Social Investors Foundation will increase awareness and interest in the community foundation concept in communities across Ghana and expand knowledge and understanding of the concept among key stakeholders and potential partners. In addition, the grantee will pilot fundraising events to assess interest in communities, adapt the concept to the Ghanaian context, and develop a long-term strategy for community foundation development in Ghana. The grantee was established in 2014 to create social and economic solutions that are inclusive of the poorest in communities across Ghana. The Pure Trust Social Investors Foundation has extensive experience in working with communities to build structures that contribute to their upliftment.

title: Community Foundation Development in Kenya
description: The project goal is to support the development of community foundations in Kenya. Over the last two years, the Kenya Community Development Foundation has worked with existing initiative groups to adopt the community foundation model. This included bolstering their leadership and governance structures, strengthening their ability to raise local funding and building connections between the groups. In addition, the grantee improved its understanding of the community foundation concept and documented case studies from the field. During this grant period, the grantee will expand its work to other communities that have the potential to establish community foundations, deepen their support to existing groups and document their experiences as a community foundation support organization. Additionally, the grantee will connect community foundations that emerge from this project and continue to raise support from other sectors for the community foundation field in Kenya. Based in Nairobi, the Kenya Community Development Foundation was established in 1997 to promote community-driven approaches to development in Kenya.

title: Community Foundation Development in Kenya
description: The project goal is to support the development of community foundations in Kenya. Over the last two years, the Kenya Community Development Foundation has worked with initiative groups in 11 of Kenya’s 47 counties to support their growth. This included supporting their community engagement efforts, strengthening their leadership and governance structures, building their capacity to raise funding from local sources and connecting the initiative groups to share experiences. In addition, the groups improved their visibility through developing websites and other online platforms with the support of the Kenya Community Development Foundation. During this grant period, the grantee will focus on building the initiative groups’ grantmaking capabilities, deepening their support to existing groups, extending support to several other groups interested in becoming community foundations and participating in regional and global events focused on building community foundations. Additionally, the grantee will provide tailored support to the initiative groups to build their community leadership role. Based in Nairobi, the Kenya Community Development Foundation was established in 1997 to promote community-driven approaches to development in Kenya.

title: Small Grants and Capacity Building Program
description: The project goal is to expand and strengthen the community foundation field in southern Africa. Over the last two years, the Southern Africa Trust has worked with community foundations in South Africa and Zimbabwe to respond to the effects of COVID-19 on communities. Support included making small grants, strengthening their capacity to raise funds from local sources and highlighting the work of community foundations in national newspapers to raise their profile and build their credibility. Over the next two years, the grantee will expand its small grants program to provide seed grants to nascent community foundations in additional countries. Additionally, the grantee will create platforms to profile the community foundations that are coming into existence and connect them to similar organizations in the region. Since its establishment in 2005, the grantee has provided funding to organizations working to reduce poverty and inequality in the region. In recent years, the Southern Africa Trust has promoted community philanthropy to uplift poor and marginalized communities.

title: Community Foundation Development in Ghana
description: The goal of the project is to develop community foundations in Ghana. Over the past year, the Pure Trust Social Investors Foundation introduced the concept of community foundations to 20 communities in 10 regions across the country. The grantee produced learning materials, supported 10 initiative groups, and launched one community foundation. Over the next three years, the grantee will provide support and tools to the initiative groups, create a learning community and platforms, continue to popularize the community foundation concept and pilot local resource mobilization activities. Based in Tamale, in the northern region, the Pure Trust Social Investors Foundation was established in 2014 to create social and economic solutions that are inclusive of the poorest communities across Ghana.

title: Community Foundation Development in Ghana
description: The project goal is to support the development of community foundations in Ghana. The PureTrust Foundation LBG introduced the community foundation concept to 75 communities across Ghana since the start of the project in 2020. To date, there are 21 registered community foundations supported through the project. During the previous grant period, the grantee introduced the community foundations to the concept of endowments, connected them to global learning platforms and convened the foundations to encourage learning. Over the next grant period, the grantee will continue to: 1) strengthen existing community foundations by building their capacity to raise resources and other forms of support from their communities; 2) deepen support for endowment building and grantmaking; and 3) support networking efforts. Based in Tamale, in the northern region, the PureTrust Foundation LBG was established in 2014 to create social and economic solutions that are inclusive to the poorest communities across Ghana.

title: European Community Foundation Initiative
description: The project goal is to develop the community foundation field and strengthen infrastructure for community foundations in Europe. In collaboration with European community philanthropy support organizations, Bundesverband Deutscher Stiftungen will continue to manage and develop the European Community Foundation Initiative. Working with its partners, the grantee will strengthen the capacity of existing community foundations and their associations, promote the community foundation concept, facilitate the establishment of new community foundations, advance the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals as a framework for community foundations and strengthen the visibility and representation of community foundations vis-à-vis the public sector on the national and European levels. During the previous grant period, the grantee organized a wide range of peer learning activities for more than 250 community foundation practitioners from 21 European countries through study visits, bilateral exchanges and thematic meetings. Also, the grantee implemented a training program on the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals and published a biannual review of the community foundation field in Europe. Bundesverband Deutscher Stiftungen is based in Berlin, Germany.

title: European Community Foundation Initiative
description: The project goal is to develop the community foundation field and strengthen infrastructure for community foundations in Europe. In collaboration with European community philanthropy support organizations, Bundesverband Deutscher Stiftungen will continue to manage and develop the European Community Foundation Initiative. Working with its partners, the grantee will: 1) strengthen the capacity of existing community foundations and their associations; 2) promote the community foundation concept; 3) facilitate the establishment of new community foundations; 4) advance the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals as a framework for community foundations; and 5) strengthen the visibility and representation of community foundations vis-à-vis the public sector on the national and European levels. During the previous grant period, the grantee organized a wide range of peer learning activities for more than 240 community foundation practitioners, including study visits, bilateral exchanges and thematic meetings. Also, the grantee implemented a training program on the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals and maintained an up-to-date online directory of community foundations in Europe. Bundesverband Deutscher Stiftungen is based in Berlin, Germany.

title: Building Broader Communities in the Americas
geographic_focus: South America, Central America, Caribbean, North America
description: The Building Broader Communities in the Americas initiative, managed by CFLeads and implemented in partnership with the Inter-American Foundation, aims to build stronger, more resilient communities throughout the Americas by enhancing the effectiveness of community foundations’ responsiveness to them. Achievements in 2019-2020 include two in-person convenings, a web page, the issuance of a request for proposals for post-mapping transnational community projects, a strategic plan refresh and the hiring of a project director. Over the next three years, the initiative will continue to pursue its four desired outcomes: 1) building understanding of transnational communities in the hemisphere, 2) strengthening relationships among community foundations and transnational stakeholders to solve common problems, 3) increasing knowledge about community foundation practices that can support transnational communities, and 4) encouraging more effective giving in Latin America and the Caribbean. Established in 1991 as the Coalition of Community Foundations for Youth, CFLeads is a U.S.-based national network of community foundations committed to community leadership.

title: Connecting Communities in the Americas
geographic_focus: Central America, South America, Caribbean, North America
description: The Connecting Communities in the Americas, managed by CFLeads, is an initiative that has the mission of inspiring and strengthening community foundations and partners for local impact as they address issues that transcend borders. Since 2016, over 200 organizations have participated in Connecting Communities in the Americas, including 150 community foundations from 13 countries in North, Central and South America. Over the past three years, its activities have included monthly virtual peer resource-sharing events, annual convenings, publications and grants for mapping, action and learning exchange grants. Over 2024 and 2025, the initiative will support community foundations with new mapping, action and learning exchange grants, continue peer learning activities, create and disseminate learning products, conduct a symposium in Brazil in 2024 and convene a gathering in North America in 2025. CFLeads is a U.S.-based national network of community foundations committed to community leadership.

title: Connecting Communities in the Americas
geographic_focus: Central America, South America, North America, Caribbean
description: Under the fiscal sponsorship of the International Community Foundation, Connecting Communities in the Americas is an initiative that brings together community foundations, philanthropy serving organizations and other partners across the Americas committed to strengthening local impact through shared learning and collaboration. Since 2016, the initiative has engaged over 600 participants and more than 260 organizations across 13 countries. Over the past three years, activities have included monthly virtual peer resource-sharing events, annual convenings, publications and grants for mapping, pilot projects and learning exchanges. Over the next three years, this initiative will support: 1) network coordination; 2) community research projects; 3) learning exchange subgrants; 4) travel stipends; 5) publication of a multilingual learning document; 6) monthly virtual peer resource sharing sessions; and 7) activity interpretation services. Founded in 1990, the International Community Foundation is located in National City, California, and focuses on strengthening humanity through community, primarily by connecting donors and stakeholders in the United States with nonprofits in Latin America.

title: International Fellows Program on Community Philanthropy
grantee: Research Foundation of the City University of New York
description: The Research Foundation of the City University of New York was created to expedite and provide oversight of the management of funds obtained by faculty of the City University of New York. The International Fellows Program on Community Philanthropy is operated by the Center on Philanthropy and Civil Society within the Graduate Center of the City University of New York. Each year, the program offers emerging young leaders and seasoned community foundation practitioners from foreign countries opportunities to learn about community foundations through an intensive graduate program of research, seminars, conferences, and mentoring. Since its inception in 1989, 208 individuals from 63 countries have participated in the program. The grantee’s program has sparked the creation of new philanthropic ventures and research resources in places as diverse as Australia, Colombia, India, Mongolia, Nepal, South Korea, and Ukraine. This grant increase will enable the grantee to carry out research and evaluation reflecting on the 30 years of achievement of the International Fellows Program and strategizing for its future.

title: East Africa Community Foundation Initiative
description: The project goal is to foster learning, networking and joint action amongst community foundations and community foundation support organizations in East Africa. To achieve this, the East Africa Philanthropy Network will create a platform that brings together the community foundation field in the region and creates connections that advance their work. In addition, the grantee will profile the community foundation field by documenting and disseminating information on its existence, work and impact in communities across the region. Established in 2003, the East Africa Philanthropy Network brings together foundations, trusts and other philanthropic organizations to build a learning community and strengthen the philanthropy field and practice in the region. With members in Kenya, Tanzania, Rwanda and Uganda, the grantee creates learning opportunities for members and produces knowledge that benefits the philanthropy sector in the region and profiles its work in the wider philanthropy field.

title: East Africa Community Foundation Initiative
description: The project goal is to foster learning, networking and joint action amongst community foundations and community foundation support organizations in East Africa. To achieve this, the East Africa Philanthropy Network will provide a space for community foundations and community philanthropy organizations to connect, share experiences and participate in wider philanthropy conversations. In addition, the grantee will profile the work of community foundations through case studies, and case stories that support cross-border learning. Established in 2003, the East Africa Philanthropy Network brings together foundations, trusts and other philanthropic organizations to build a learning community and strengthen the philanthropy field and practice in the region. With members in Kenya, Tanzania, Rwanda and Uganda, the grantee creates learning opportunities for members, produces knowledge that benefits the philanthropy sector in the region and profiles its work in the wider philanthropy field.

title: East Africa Community Foundation Initiative
description: The project goal is to foster learning, networking and joint action among community foundations and community foundation support organizations in East Africa. To achieve this, the East Africa Philanthropy Network will support learning circles, exchanges and convenings for community foundations in East Africa. In addition, the grantee will conduct research on community foundation practices and publish quarterly updates to promote the community foundation concept in the region. Established in 2003, the grantee brings together foundations, trusts and other philanthropic organizations to build a learning community and strengthen the philanthropy field and practice in the region. With members in Kenya, Tanzania, Rwanda and Uganda, the East Africa Philanthropy Network creates learning opportunities for members, produces knowledge that benefits the philanthropy sector in the region and profiles its work in the wider philanthropy field.

title: Building Community Foundations Capacity to Act on SDGs
description: The project goal is to increase the contribution of community foundations in Canada and globally to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. Over the past several years, Community Foundations of Canada has created relevant learning content, built the capacity of Canadian community foundations to contribute to the goals, and shared Canadian best practices on advancing the goals globally. To date, the grantee has trained more than 130 community foundations on programming and impact measurement and delivered more than 100 learning products related to the Sustainable Development Goals. Community Foundations of Canada was established in 1992 as a network of 28 community foundations. Currently, the network includes 191 community foundations with close to $6 billion in combined assets. The grantee provides information, technical assistance and networking opportunities to its members. Community Foundations of Canada also represents Canadian community foundations on the national and international levels and works across the civil society, business, and public sectors to boost efforts for building inclusive and sustainable communities.

title: SDG Program in Africa
description: The project goal is to support community foundations in Africa to understand and apply the sustainable development goals to their work. To achieve this, SGS Consulting will produce user-friendly material to clarify the goals, train community foundations on how to use the goals in their daily work and produce case studies to demonstrate how they are contributing to achieving the goals. In addition, the grantee will support an informal network of community foundations from different countries to exchange experiences. The grantee will also support community foundations to connect to the sustainable development goal platforms in their countries. To build on the work of supporting the development of community foundations in specific countries in southern Africa, the grantee will implement the project in South Africa, Tanzania, Zambia and Zimbabwe. In addition to supporting the development of community foundations in South Africa, SGS Consulting provides technical assistance to community foundation support organizations in the region to enhance their ability to expand the field in their countries.

title: SDG Program in Africa
description: The goal of this project is to support community foundations in Africa to understand and apply the sustainable development goals framework in their daily work. Previous Mott Foundation support has enabled SGS Consulting to work with several community foundations, and their support organizations, in the region to produce case studies that illustrate how community foundations are contributing to achieving global goals. To build on this work, the grantee will conduct research on the experience of community foundations in applying a sustainable development goal framework to their work. In addition, the grantee will: 1) support the community foundations to monitor their performance against the indicators; 2) support connections and conversations on the goals in the region; and 3) develop a series of publications to put a spotlight on how community foundations are responding to the sustainable development goals. The focus of the project will continue to be in southern Africa, with a specific focus on South Africa, Zambia, Zimbabwe and Tanzania.

title: Increasing the Contribution of European Community Foundations to the SDGs
description: The project goal is to increase the engagement and contribution of European community foundations to the U.N. Sustainable Development Goals. To this end, the Fagaras Research Institute will: 1) raise the awareness of European community foundations about the different ways in which they can engage with the SDGs; 2) strengthen the capacity of European community foundations to use the SDGs framework; 3) increase the connectedness of the community foundation field to national, European and global civil society efforts to impact the SDGs agenda; and 4) increase the awareness of public institutions about the community foundation field’s contribution to the SDGs. Since its establishment in 2017, the grantee has developed a global network of over 60 researchers, practitioners and students from 15 countries. During the past two years, the grantee has been working on engaging community foundations in Romania with the SDGs. The Fagaras Research Institute is based in the city of Fagaras, Romania.

title: Increasing the Contribution of European Community Foundations to the SDGs
description: The project goal is to increase the engagement and contribution of European community foundations to the U.N. Sustainable Development Goals. To this end, the Fagaras Research Institute will: 1) improve and expand data collection and analysis on community foundations and the SDGs; 2) strengthen the capacity of European community foundations to use the SDG framework; 3) strengthen the interaction between community foundations and policymakers involved in the SDG process; and 4) strengthen the engagement of community foundations with local communities on SDG-related issues. During the past grant period, the grantee established working relationships with over 400 community foundations and support organizations working on the SDGs, published a baseline report on the engagement of European community foundations with the SDGs and developed and disseminated widely 20 learning products on the SDGs. The Fagaras Research Institute is based in the city of Fagaras, Romania.

title: Increasing the Contribution of European Community Foundations to the SDGs
description: The project goal is to increase the engagement and contribution of European community foundations to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). To this end, the Fagaras Research Institute will: 1) improve and consolidate data collection and analysis on community foundations and the SDGs; 2) build the capacity of European community foundations to use the SDG framework; 3) deepen the interaction between community foundations and policymakers involved in the SDG process; and 4) strengthen the engagement of community foundations with local communities on SDG-related issues. During the past grant period, the grantee worked with over 400 community foundations and support organizations working on the SDGs, published a report on the engagement of European community foundations with the SDGs and developed and disseminated widely 10 learning products on the SDGs. The Fagaras Research Institute is based in the city of Fagaras, Romania.

title: Recruiting and Retaining Diverse Educators
description: This renewal grant will support The Education Trust’s continuing work to diversify the educator workforce by promoting strategies that build pipelines for afterschool and out-of-school staff of color to become teachers. Goals planned for the renewal grant period include: 1) educating federal and state policymakers about viable strategies, and 2) conducting additional research to inform the field’s understanding of the best ways to recruit, prepare and support more diverse educators. Based in Washington, D.C., the grantee is a research and advocacy organization working to close opportunity gaps and raise achievement for students of color and students from low-income families.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will renew general purpose support to Focus: HOPE, an anti-poverty and civil rights organization serving low-income residents of Detroit’s Oakman Boulevard neighborhood. Cofounded in 1968 by Father William Cunningham and Eleanor Josaitis, the grantee’s mission is to provide intelligent and practical solutions to overcome racism, poverty and injustice. Mott funding will help support the grantee’s continued transition to a new business model as well as its core lines of work: early learning, youth development, workforce development, food justice and community empowerment.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to help address the long-standing and emerging issues facing immigrants in the Americas. Alianza Americas’ mission is to bring about a more inclusive, equitable and sustainable way of life for under-served immigrant communities living in the United States and across Mexico and Central America. During the previous grant period, this was accomplished through delegations and learning tours, partnerships across borders, building the capacity of migrant leaders and by strengthening the grantee’s communication capacity to spotlight the social inequalities immigrant communities are facing. During this grant period, the grantee will strengthen transnational networks, advocate on behalf of migrants, strengthen United States’ policy coalitions and uplift the voices of migrants. Founded in 2004 by Mexican, Central American, and Caribbean immigrant leaders, Alianza Americas is a network of over 50 members in 13 states, representing over 150,000 migrant families across the United States, with dozens of organizational partners in Mexico and Central America.

title: Strengthening Great Lakes Leadership
geographic_focus: Indiana, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Ohio, Illinois, Michigan
description: The mission of the Environmental Leadership Program is to support visionary, action-oriented and diverse leadership for a just and sustainable future. Over the years, the grantee has developed a very robust curriculum delivered in retreat settings to build the capacity of more than 1,300 emerging and mid-career environmental professionals. With prior Mott support, the grantee provided its core programming in a regional format to leaders in the Great Lakes, though the organization did move to a virtual format over the last two years due to the pandemic. With renewed support, the grantee will deliver its fellowship program to as many as 20 Great Lakes leaders each year, including five people of color, using a hybrid program delivery model.

title: General Purposes
description: The Groundwork Center for Resilient Communities has been promoting community resilience models from northwest lower Michigan since 1995. The grantee focuses on community-based policy leadership through supporting a clean environment, strong economy and sustainability. The grantee does this by researching and developing local successes and sharing lessons learned with broad appeal to regional audiences. The grantee prioritizes food and farming, clean energy, water policy and transportation. With this grant, Groundwork Center for Resilient Communities will pursue all of its priorities, including the expansion of the Great Lakes Business Network.

title: Clean and Affordable Drinking Water: Growing Advocacy and Organizational Capacity in the Great Lakes
geographic_focus: Pennsylvania, Illinois, Wisconsin, New York, Minnesota, Ohio, Indiana, Michigan
description: River Network is a national organization that provides training to advance organizational effectiveness, and sharpen skills and capacity to address issues like access to clean, safe and affordable drinking water. With prior Mott support, the grantee expanded its technical assistance around drinking water issues and organized partner groups to respond to programmatic challenges and opportunities presented by the COVID-19 pandemic. Renewed support will enable the grantee to assist new organizations as they confront affordability and aging infrastructure challenges. The grantee will also provide training to build the capacity of Great Lakes groups around drinking water issues, addressing equity issues, provide consulting, training and mentoring around organizational effectiveness and support robust participation at River Rally, a leading national conference.

title: Freshwater Lab Internship Program
grantee: The Board of Trustees of the University of Illinois
description: The Freshwater Lab at the University of Illinois at Chicago develops cohorts of Great Lakes leaders through an internship program for university students from diverse backgrounds. The interns are placed in organizations focused on freshwater conservation, including Mott grantees, public agencies and community-based groups primarily in the greater Chicago area. The internship program spans an academic semester and a summer session, giving students classroom training to build leadership and understanding of Great Lakes issues as well as gain practical training and networking with local professionals. With continued support, the grantee will expand the number of students participating in the program and provide mentoring to alumni of the program.

title: General Purposes
description: For over 35 years, Environmental Defence Canada has been active on environmental issues at the provincial and national levels through engagement with stakeholders, organizations and the general public. The organization works to safeguard Canada’s freshwater resources, decrease Canadians’ exposure to toxic chemicals, end plastic pollution, tackle climate change and build a clean economy. To help address these issues, Environmental Defence Canada will engage and educate stakeholders and participate in opportunities to help ensure restoration of the Great Lakes, build the capacity of environmental organizations in Canada and raise awareness of public health issues in Ontario.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Heart of the Lakes Center for Land Conservation Policy
description: Heart of the Lakes Center for Land Conservation Policy is Michigan’s only institution whose mission is to serve and support land conservancies in the Great Lakes state. With prior Mott support, the grantee helped its members protect a total of 672,967 acres of forests, coastlines and farmlands, while supporting and strengthening members and helping them raise the visibility of land trusts and their importance to Michigan’s conservation heritage. The grantee was instrumental in forming a multi-partner initiative to tell the story of protecting public lands and their value to the state. With renewed support, the grantee will continue and expand efforts to support and serve land trusts and will launch a new project to explore opportunities for conservation and redevelopment of urban lands.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Cities Initiative
geographic_focus: Wisconsin, Pennsylvania, Illinois, New York, Minnesota, Quebec, Michigan, Indiana, Ontario, Ohio
description: Founded in 2003, the Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Cities Initiative is a coalition of over 100 U.S. and Canadian mayors and municipal officials dedicated to advancing the protection and restoration of the region and its water resources. The grantee helps its members integrate environmental, economic and social priorities into solutions that protect the Great Lakes — a resource that holds 20% of the world’s surface freshwater, provides drinking water for 40 million people and is the basis for the regional economy. With previous Mott Foundation support, the grantee has helped contribute to the development of measures that protect and advance the interests of the Great Lakes. Renewed funding will enable the grantee to continue to connect mayors across boundaries, supply municipal leaders with trusted and reliable information on a range of water issues and provide a platform for mayors to express their views in decision-making forums.

title: Technical Assistance to Boost Great Lakes Communication
geographic_focus: Illinois, Michigan, Indiana, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Ontario, New York, Ohio
description: Since its inception in 1996, with significant support from the Mott Foundation, Freshwater Future has provided over $4 million through 1,200 grants for capacity building and technical support to groups working to protect and restore the waters of the region. With this project, the grantee will provide education, technical support, training, and tools to Mott grantees to more effectively utilize communications to advance organizational objectives. The grantee will regularly reach out to other Mott grantees to anticipate communications needs and help them plan and execute communications tactics and activities. Freshwater Future will expand its capacity by gaining communications expertise through this project and from the skills of a consulting team.

title: Health and Environmental Funders Network
description: This grant will provide support to Virginia Organizing for its Health and Environmental Funders Network. The network seeks to mobilize philanthropy around solutions for environmental health and justice. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the network has helped address environmental challenges and expand understanding of the public health stake in a clean, healthy environment. Continued support will enable the network to mobilize resources on critical environmental health and justice issues, including a new emphasis on lead exposure.

title: Growing a National Drinking Water Movement
description: The Water Foundation, a California-based organization that addresses pressing water protection and restoration problems, is expanding its focus outside of California and beginning to address drinking water. Millions of people in the United States live in places where safe and affordable water is not available. Outdated and crumbling infrastructure exacerbate these challenges, and climate change further threatens drinking water supplies with harsher droughts, more violent flooding, and warmer temperatures. While foundations have responded in cases like the Flint water crisis, much more needs to be done. To address these challenges, the grantee will begin planning for a national convening of funders, grantees, and partners. In preparation for the national convening, the grantee will host or partner on four regional round tables on drinking water throughout the country over the coming year.

title: Growing a National Drinking Water Movement
description: Based in California, the Water Foundation has a national network of partners that advances lasting solutions to secure safe water for people, restore and sustain freshwater ecosystems and build climate resilience. Methods used include direct grantmaking, field building and campaign strategy development. During the previous grant period, the grantee hosted four drinking water roundtables throughout the country including one for the Great Lakes region. These conversations brought together 25-30 key water leaders in each case to build partnerships and define priority drinking water issues, strategies and solutions. During the next grant period, the grantee will grow a network of drinking water citizen leaders that have emerged in the wake of the COVID-19 pandemic and support them through message testing and polling, create a resource bank of tools and templates accessible to local leaders across the country, coordinate with and provide support to local leaders in at least three locations (including one in the Great Lakes region) and amplify and spread success stories.

title: Change the Course Great Lakes
description: The Bonneville Environmental Foundation’s Change the Course program is a unique initiative that has been piloted in the Colorado River basin and Georgia. The grantee will bring the program to the Great Lakes region, starting in Michigan. Change the Course partners with corporations to raise funds for projects, designed with local nongovernmental organizations, to address high-priority water protection needs. The program has identified more than 20 prospective corporate partners, and initiated a first project to address drinking water safety in Flint.

title: Great Lakes Islands Alliance
description: There are nearly 30 year-round island communities in the Great Lakes. Though independent by choice, they are facing economic, social, and ecological challenges that require a greater degree of collaboration and cooperation. Northland College in Wisconsin has provided administrative support for the formation of the Great Lakes Islands Alliance. The project is a voluntary network connecting individual island leaders and developing tools to aid collaboration. With support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee will lead a team of collaborators to establish the Great Lakes Islands Alliance as a legal entity, an influential voice for policies to protect the interests of Great Lakes islands, and a support network for year-round island communities.

title: Great Lakes Leadership Summit
grantee: Conference of Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Governors and Premiers
geographic_focus: Michigan, Wisconsin, Pennsylvania, Indiana, Illinois, Minnesota, New York, Ohio
description: The Conference of Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Governors and Premiers is an organization of critical importance for this region and is based in Chicago. The grantee coordinates collaborative activities among the chief executives of the ten states and provinces to advance resource protection and sustainable economic development. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has hosted the premier high-level summit of its kind every two years. With renewed support, the grantee will host another summit in 2021, either in Cleveland or virtually. These summits often lead to coordinated policy and project activities. One such activity that has emerged is an impact investment program that leverages private capital for stewardship objectives. This grant will also support further development of that innovative initiative and its potential application to invasive species control.

title: Great Lakes Leadership Council
geographic_focus: Michigan, Minnesota, Other, Ohio, Illinois, Indiana, Wisconsin
description: For over a decade, the Council of State Governments has brought together state and provincial policymakers from the Great Lakes region to learn about key issues affecting the lakes, exchange information and ideas and build their capacity to be effective leaders and stewards of the lakes. With prior Mott support, the grantee educated policymakers and convened them to share information and lessons from neighboring jurisdictions, and launched the Patricia Birkholz Institute for Great Lakes-St. Lawrence Policy, an intensive learning program that took policymakers on a “deep dive” into the nutrient pollution issue. With renewed support, the Council of State Governments will maintain all of the activities of the project, including a new Birkholz Institute program on climate resilience.

title: General Purposes
description: Environmental Advocates of New York was founded 50 years ago and has been on the front lines leading major environmental victories in New York. The grantee’s vision is: a future where clean water, air and a stable climate are recognized as fundamental human rights; people and their communities, particularly those that are disadvantaged, are thriving; and New York ecosystems are intact and healthy. During this grant period, the grantee will embrace a comprehensive approach to protecting water from source to tap, while building a statewide initiative that integrates frontline communities with local officials, labor and other groups. A key priority for the grantee will focus on fighting climate change, transitioning away from fossil fuels and ensuring justice for those most vulnerable to climate change impacts.

title: Clean Water Act Implementation in the Great Lakes Region
geographic_focus: Ohio, Illinois, Minnesota, Michigan, Indiana, Wisconsin
description: The Environmental Law and Policy Center is a leading public interest environmental law organization based in Chicago with offices throughout the Great Lakes region. With prior Mott support, the grantee cataloged and reported on Clean Water Act permit violations and enforcement in the Great Lakes region. The grantee also monitored polluted runoff from large-scale farm animal operations in the western Lake Erie basin. With renewed support, the Environmental Law & Policy Center will expand its work on nutrient pollution to Wisconsin and engage at the federal level to build support for Great Lakes protection and restoration.

title: Tribal Science, Training and Communications Project
grantee: Great Lakes Indian Fish and Wildlife Commission
description: The Great Lakes Indian Fish and Wildlife Commission works with tribal governments in Michigan, Wisconsin and Minnesota to protect tribal interests in the ecology of ceded territories in the northern portions of those states. With previous grant support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee identified and implemented steps to participate effectively in permitting and environmental reviews. With continued support, the grantee will increase baseline water monitoring, map vital wetland habitats in areas of interest to the tribes where land use changes are proposed, help implement aspects of the federal Clean Water Act and introduce students to natural resource management and tribal self-governance careers.

title: Lake Superior Water Resources Project
description: The Minnesota Center for Environmental Advocacy has been a leading legal and scientific voice for Minnesota’s environment since 1974. With previous Mott support, the grantee has advocated for the protection of Minnesota wetlands; worked to restore Lake Superior watersheds; sought to protect Lake Superior from invasive species; worked to improve access and affordability to clean, safe water in Minnesota; and sought to protect the Lake Superior watershed from threats from mining activities. With this increase, the grantee will expand its investment in the organization’s leadership by hiring a consultant to assist with organizational development, strategic planning, and formation of a Scientific Advisory board.

title: Sustaining the Great Lakes Project
geographic_focus: Ohio, New York, Michigan, Minnesota, Illinois, Wisconsin, Pennsylvania, Indiana
description: The National Wildlife Federation, a national conservation group with a strong presence in the Great Lakes Basin, partners with regional and state-level organizations to protect and restore the Great Lakes from invasive species, toxic pollution, and harmful algal blooms. The grantee continues to deepen its efforts, particularly through informing policy and monitoring implementation, providing scientific information and assistance, leading public education, and building a diverse base of collaborators. This grant increase will allow the grantee to support the Healing Our Waters-Great Lakes Restoration Conference, water affordability outreach, and also to engage businesses in efforts to stop Asian carp from entering the Great Lakes.

title: PFAS Action Network
description: The Ecology Center is a Michigan-based organization with extensive experience and a national reputation of excellence for addressing toxic chemical science, health impacts and solutions to contamination problems. The grantee will lead efforts to unite groups in Michigan and eventually throughout the Great Lakes seeking to address the contaminants per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), often referred to as “forever” chemicals because their strong chemical bonds don’t break down in nature. PFAS chemicals are used in a wide range of consumer products despite a body of science indicating that they are linked to numerous serious health effects in humans. Nearly two million Michigan residents have PFAS-contaminated drinking water. The Ecology Center will bring together groups to form the PFAS Action Network, which will share best practices, communications resources, research and organizing strength.

title: Our Water, Our Future
description: PennFuture is a premier voice for resource conservation and environmental protection in Pennsylvania. With partial Mott support, the organization plans to open an office in Erie, the fourth largest city in Pennsylvania located on the state’s 63-mile Lake Erie shoreline. Staff working out of the grantee’s new office in Erie will: organize and equip residents, community groups, academics, and others with a greater understanding of water protection tools available to them; develop a Common Agenda for Clean Water that sets forth short- and long-term solutions to water protection and restoration in the watershed; and deploy legal and regulatory expertise to protect water quality in the Lake Erie basin.

title: General Purposes
description: Founded in 1998, PennFuture is a statewide environmental advocacy organization working for clean air, clean water and a healthy climate. The grantee’s signature strategies (legal, policy, communication and outreach) were devised to counter the pressing environmental threats in the state. The grantee has opened a new office in Erie, Pennsylvania to set forth Great Lakes protection and restoration solutions. Additionally, the grantee focuses on civic engagement in communities of color, greenhouse gas reduction and public health. Over the next two years, PennFuture will address priority environmental policy issues and grow its capacity to meet emerging threats, and expand its reach to engage underrepresented individuals and communities throughout Pennsylvania.

title: Michigan Water Financing
description: The Nature Conservancy in Michigan is highly respected as a credible voice for solving complex problems by bridging environment, science and economic priorities; and building necessary partnerships with Michigan policy leaders to achieve policy reform. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee engaged a diverse group of stakeholders in a series of workshops to develop a suite of recommendations to address the challenge of financing Michigan water utilities in the 21st century. This process underscored that the problems faced by water systems are inseparable from larger issues of equity for low-income communities and communities of color that have faced decades of systematic discrimination. With renewed support, the Nature Conservancy will work with partners to forge a research and communications strategy to identify financial structures to address these challenges and the dialogue to build support to make it successful in Michigan.

title: Michigan Water Resources Protection and Financing
description: The Nature Conservancy in Michigan is highly respected among government leaders, public agencies and nonprofit partners. The grantee’s mission to conserve the lands and waters on which all life depends is at the heart of their interest in ensuring that clean water meets the needs of both people and nature. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee engaged a diverse group of stakeholders in a series of workshops that emphasized that water quality and water affordability is important for all Michiganders, and that a new path must be charted to ensure that water utilities can meet their true costs without burdening those who already struggle to pay water bills. The grantee has been researching policy options, engaging key stakeholders and advancing policy recommendations. With renewed support, the Nature Conservancy will advance policy solutions that increase funding for water infrastructure and utilities, ensures equitable assistance flows to lower-income households, improves management of rural septic systems and updates tools to better manage water withdrawals.

title: Protecting Great Lakes Water Resources
description: Michigan Trout Unlimited has played a preeminent and highly respected role as the conservation voice for cold-water fishery protection, and effective water resource management for several decades. Large-quantity water withdrawals in the Great Lakes states have expanded over the last decade, and threaten the state’s waters and the resources that depend on them. Additionally, the potential of Asian carp establishment in the Great Lakes poses the most severe and clear threat to the system today. Michigan Trout Unlimited will use this grant to properly educate their members in the Great Lakes region, along with partner group members, about these problems and equip them to be effective citizen advocates.

title: African Development Bank Energy Financing
description: Christian Aid is a nonprofit organization with more than 70 years of experience working to support communities and help them to thrive. Based in the United Kingdom, the grantee works globally to eradicate the causes of poverty. Under this grant, the grantee will support and strengthen the capacity of the African Coalition for Sustainable Energy and Access Network. The grant will include an evaluation of the network and identification of ways to strengthen African civil society engagement in promoting distributed renewable energy for rural African communities.

title: Advancing and Protecting Sustainability Standards in Development Finance
description: Against the backdrop of threats and challenges posed by the global COVID-19 pandemic, Friends of the Earth will build on its longstanding successful efforts to reform critical international finance institutions, particularly in the energy, extractive and natural resources sectors. With renewed support, the grantee primarily seeks to expand its new Banks and Biodiversity initiative, which encourages Chinese and other trend-setting banks to adopt “No Go” (off-limits) policies for financing in or near vulnerable geographic areas. A second workstream will target development finance institutions to boost support for improved renewable energy access and climate-related policies. Both workstreams will entail a blend of advocacy, research and deepened engagement at the institutional and project levels.

title: Building Capacity to Monitor Chinese Investment in Asia
description: Asia’s development finance landscape has changed rapidly over the past decade. Chinese investments in developing countries have increased exponentially and present a major shift in the source and structure of development finance. To address the environmental and social impacts of Chinese development finance, Inclusive Development International was established in 2012 to support and build the capacity of communities affected by these investments. The grantee has been key in raising awareness of the need to strengthen the environmental and social policies of China-influenced development finance institutions, particularly the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank. Over the next grant period, the grantee will undertake work to inform civil society about key developments in Chinese development finance overseas, research and disseminate actionable data on Chinese investment chains and influence the trajectory of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank’s internal standards and practices.

title: General Purposes
description: The NGO Forum on the Asian Development Banks has been advocating for sustainable development policies that are beneficial to local communities and the environment in the Asian region for two decades. It works to improve public participation, access to information and good governance at the Asian Development Bank and new Chinese development finance institutions. Over the past grant period, the grantee has seen increased renewable energy investments and reduced fossil fuel project funding. Over the next two years, the grantee will lead the civil society process for the review of the Asian Development Bank and Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank’s environmental and social safeguard policies. The grantee also will monitor the project lending for both institutions to ensure that post-COVID-19 financing will comply with these policies. In addition, work on national energy planning processes will be expanded to better assist communities with their local energy access needs.

title: Accelerating Pro-Poor Clean Energy Solutions
description: Access to affordable energy continues to be a major development challenge facing the world’s poor. With past Mott Foundation support, Oxfam America, an international development organization, has engaged with international financial institutions to advance clean energy solutions around the world, particularly in Africa. With this grant renewal, the grantee aims to expand its clean energy efforts to East Asia and other geographies that are facing similar threats of poor environmental, social and governance practices within the energy sector. Through a range of advocacy activities, Oxfam America’s efforts will primarily center around influencing donor institutions and national governments to shift their finance flows and energy interventions towards pro-poor clean energy access.

title: Exploring Best Practice Models and Pathways for International Clean Energy Finance
description: Vasudha Foundation USA undertakes research and analysis that is used to inform and shift international financial institution investments in the energy sector. Building on previous support, the grantee will continue to monitor the African Development Bank and the World Bank Group’s financing for energy infrastructure to developing countries. Given the economic shocks of the COVID-19 pandemic, the grantee will focus on the need for energy access solutions that address both livelihoods and community resilience, especially in terms of building South-South energy collaborations between African countries and India.

title: Greening Chinese Development Finance
description: Over the past decade, China has provided sizable amounts of development finance. Many of these projects have caused negative impacts, which has led to public opposition in host countries to further Chinese investments. China’s focus on creating energy, transport and communication infrastructure linkages from Asia to Europe, the Middle East and Africa through its Belt and Road Initiative is ambitious and has the potential for either large-scale negative or positive environmental and social impacts. With this grant increase, the World Wildlife Fund will work with non-governmental organization partners to encourage other investors to hold the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank and the Asian Development Bank accountable to strong Environmental, Social and Governance policies. Facilitating this information sharing will enhance the two banks’ capacity to promote risk management in overseas energy finance contributing to the shift away from coal to clean energy.

title: Expanding Distributed Renewable Energy in the Amazon
description: The Brazilian Association of Distributed Generation is a trade group of more than 400 companies working in the renewable energy sector. Over the course of the project thus far, the grantee promoted the benefits of clean energy access and helped build supply chains for distributed solar energy in small Amazon cities and remote communities. The first Amazon Forum on Renewable Energy was organized for member companies and Amazon officials. The second Forum, as well as a Solar Training Road and Boat Show, will be organized during this grant period to build on lessons learned and meet community demand.

title: Off Grid Innovations for Livelihoods
description: The international nongovernmental organization, EnAccess, established in 2017, has developed a methodology for identifying and sharing lessons learned by new and existing energy access entrepreneurs through an open-source online tool. Through this project, the grantee will expand its work, collecting data and disseminating lessons from a broader range of micro-, small-, and medium enterprises in order to address the challenge of financing off-grid livelihood projects. It will document the lessons learned from such projects and share them with a broader community of energy access companies as well as foundations and donors. EnAccess will undertake this work through contracting with small local companies that have experience in delivering livelihoods-based energy access projects but do not have access to financing to expand their businesses in this segment of the clean energy sector.

title: Energy Distributed to Isolated Communities
description: The Instituto Socioambiental is a Brazilian social-environmental nongovernmental organization with decades of expertise working with Indigenous communities in the Amazon. Over the past project period, the grantee worked with energy distributors and renewable energy networks to strengthen a new Brazilian federal program, More Light for the Amazon, and expanded its off-grid renewable demonstration projects in the Brazilian Amazon. This grant renewal will support the grantee to continue its work with energy regulators and renewable energy networks and consolidate its monitoring and management systems of renewable energy models in isolated Amazon communities.

title: Shine: Investing in Energy Access for All
description: Nearly 800 million people live without access to electricity. Rockefeller Philanthropy Advisors, through its Shine Campaign project, aims to address this global challenge by calling on leaders in the faith, philanthropic and nonprofit sectors to make principled investments in clean, affordable energy that put the most vulnerable communities first. Over the last two years, the Shine Campaign project has successfully worked to unlock finance for energy access and build a community of practice among donors and practitioners in the field. With continued Mott support, the grantee will deepen and expand its work, including the launch of investment and regranting facilities that deliver financial resources to community-led clean energy enterprises in remote communities of Africa and Asia.

title: Sharing Indian Social Entrepreneurs' Lessons for African Off Grid Energy
description: Expanding energy access is a key to unlocking increased economic growth in developing countries such as Tanzania, particularly in rural areas. The Solar Energy Light Company Foundation, with over 10 years of experience in off-grid energy access work in rural India, has supported key Tanzanian organizations to provide capacity building and business mentoring functions for Tanzanian clean energy entrepreneurs. Over the next two years, the grantee will continue supporting its partners in Tanzania while also developing complementary programs to scale up clean energy access initiatives in the country and share lessons learned in Tanzania with clean energy access practitioners globally.

title: Engaging Youth in Service
description: This grant will support Youth Service America to engage young people throughout the United States in quality youth-led service projects. The grantee will focus efforts to bolster youth engagement in Flint and Genesee County and across the United States by working with schools, nonprofit organizations, and afterschool programs.

title: Solar Village: Vila Limeira
description: World Wildlife Fund and it’s partner World Wildlife Fund Brazil work in the Brazilian Amazon to achieve a national off-grid solar energy program for isolated communities living in extractive reserve conservation units. This project will support the grantee to train technicians, build, and monitor the success of one of the first 100 percent solar villages in the Amazon rainforest.

title: Solar Village: Tamandua
description: The Instituto Socioambiental’s Energy and Community program promotes off-grid renewable energy for remote indigenous communities in the Brazilian Amazon. This project will support the organization to train technicians, build, and monitor the success of one of the first 100 percent solar villages in the Brazilian Amazon state of Roraima.

title: General Purposes
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: Started in 2005 as a project of Philanthropy New York, Asset Funders Network is a national membership organization for grantmakers working to build economic opportunity and prosperity for low- and moderate-income people. To accomplish its mission, the grantee works with its members to develop shared expertise, align and coordinate grantmaking strategies and provide leadership on priority issues. During the renewal grant period, the grantee will continue organizing educational and networking activities, connecting grantmakers to experts and other technical assistance providers and promoting funder collaborations that increase the level and effectiveness of philanthropic support for asset-building issues. Mott funding will also support an enhanced focus on growing funder engagement and support for children’s savings account programming.

title: General Purposes
description: This renewal grant will provide general support to the Harlem Children’s Zone, whose mission is to end intergenerational poverty in Central Harlem and become the model for how other long-distressed communities nationwide and around the world can do the same. The grantee identified two overarching goals for the renewal grant period: 1) continue providing high-impact, wraparound supports to young people living in Central Harlem; and 2) capitalize on its success to achieve sustainability. Created in 2000, the Harlem Children’s Zone annually provides education, health and employment services to over 20,000 children and families living in a 97-block area in Central Harlem.

title: Sustainable Finance Center
description: The World Resources Institute is a global environmental think tank that works with governments, the private sector, and civil society to identify solutions to urgent environmental challenges. The support of the Foundation has enabled the grantee to continue its work to help shift global financial flows toward more climate compatible and sustainable development that responds to the needs of the poor. The overarching goal of this project is to improve the social and environmental performance of public international financial institutions. This renewal grant will focus on deploying empirical research and open-source, digital analytical tools to help facilitate the greening of the China-led Belt and Road Initiative, as well as help ensure that the multilateral development banks meet international climate goals.

title: Dullah Omar School for Paralegalism
description: The Social Change Assistance Trust is a grantmaking organization established in 1984 to promote human rights and social justice by making grants to community-based organizations. It supports programs that promote access to justice, gender equality, youth development, and local economic development. Past support enabled the grantee to fund community advice offices in the Eastern, Western, and Northern Cape provinces; train and mentor paralegals and management committees in community advice offices; explore the establishment of a youth fund; and strengthen community-driven philanthropy by encouraging local fundraising. This grant will support the Social Change Assistance Trust to implement the Dullah Omar School for paralegalism to provide training to paralegals from across the country.

title: South American Regional Fund
geographic_focus: South America, Chile, Bolivia, Colombia, Ecuador, Argentina
description: The Fondo de Mujeres del Sur is a grantmaking and capacity building organization focused on providing small grants to strengthen community, environmental, and civil society organizations. This grant will enable the grantee to implement the South America Regional Fund to support local communities and groups working on issues of energy infrastructure and sustainable finance in South America.

title: Promoting Community-Led Implementation of the Sustainable Development Goals
description: The project goal is to promote a community-led implementation of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. To this end, the Brookings Institution will host a series of workshops, roundtable discussions, and public events. These activities will inform and evaluate how place-based leaders set and track goals; mobilize the investments and action to drive progress; and develop and disseminate relevant tools, policies, and networks to maximize impact. The grantee will engage cities, states, foundations, and other stakeholders that are championing the use of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals and provide a neutral venue to coordinate, collaborate, and disseminate tools and findings. This grant increase will help the grantee to add community foundation focused research questions, outreach, and analysis to the overall project products.

title: Afterschool Education and Outreach Project
description: This grant will provide support to Collaborative Communications Group to continue to sustain the statewide afterschool networks and the afterschool field through education and outreach in policy development, communications and research. To advance afterschool programs, this project will build bridges between local, state and federal governments and the afterschool field, and will assist the networks as they navigate changes underway with federal education policy and state and federal budget challenges.

title: Property Acquisition and Neighborhood Stabilization
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: The Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation will acquire blighted property within targeted neighborhood commercial corridors. This work will support reinvestment in city neighborhoods and key civic institutions. Once acquired, these properties will be remediated to improve surrounding conditions and combat community deterioration.

title: General Purposes
description: The Paralegal Advisory Service Institute was established in 2007 to make justice accessible to all people in Malawi. It deploys trained paralegals to provide legal education, advice and assistance in criminal and civil justice processes. Past support assisted the grantee to scale its work on both criminal and civil justice services. The grantee was also instrumental in providing justice services safely during the COVID-19 pandemic. Ongoing support will assist the Paralegal Advisory Service Institute to continue to ensure that due process rights are respected and upheld and that well-functioning and sustainable criminal and civil justice services are implemented in urban and rural areas of Malawi.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support increased access to justice for poor and marginalized people in Malawi. The Paralegal Advisory Service Institute will do this by providing timely, effective and inclusive justice services. To this extent, the grantee will use its network of paralegals and community village mediators to provide justice services throughout the northern regions of Malawi. Past support allowed the grantee to scale its work on both criminal and civil justice services, especially as Malawi is recovering from the consequences of managing COVID-19. The Paralegal Advisory Service Institute was established in 2007 to make justice accessible to all people in Malawi and deploys trained paralegals to provide legal education, advice and assistance in criminal and civil justice processes.

title: Learning Commons
description: With this grant increase, Kettering University will construct a new building on its campus. The Learning Commons will serve as the academic and social centerpiece of the university’s campus, providing a place that fosters collaborative learning and exploration. The building will be characterized by open areas for students to gather and work, technology to support student learning and engagement, space for cross-discipline collaboration and physical and electronic library resources that can be accessed by Kettering University and other postsecondary students and community members in Flint.

title: Summer Youth Initiative and TeenQuest
description: This grant provides support to the Genesee Area Focus Fund to implement TeenQuest and the Summer Youth Initiative, which provide job training and employment opportunities for Genesee County teens in partnership with area employers. Teens participate first in TeenQuest, a preemployment training program, and are then eligible to apply for employment through the Summer Youth Initiative.

title: Summer Youth Initiative and TeenQuest
description: This grant provides support to the Genesee Area Focus Fund to implement TeenQuest and the Summer Youth Initiative, which provide job training and employment opportunities for Genesee County teens in partnership with area employers. Teens participate first in TeenQuest — a preemployment training program — and are then eligible to apply for employment through the Summer Youth Initiative.

title: Tools for Defending Environmental Defenders
description: Founded in 1992, Land is Life is a nongovernmental organization working with a trusted network of indigenous leaders, communities and organizations in the greater Amazon and globally. Over the past grant period, the grantee began implementing a methodology with Indigenous communities in the Ecuadoran and Colombian Amazon to develop consultation protocols to address development pressure and security threats to environmental defenders of indigenous lands and forests. Over the next grant period, the grantee will consolidate the development of the protocols, strengthen territorial monitoring and work toward state and court recognition of the tool to protect and prevent violence against indigenous environmental defenders.

title: Nevada Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase will help support the After-School All-Stars to support the Nevada Statewide Afterschool Network, focused on developing policy, partnerships, and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. The grant will support: 1) developing partners among afterschool stakeholders in Nevada; 2) establishing a cohesive statewide afterschool network; and 3) creating a steering committee for the network.

title: 21st Century Community Learning Centers and Literary Skills
description: This grant increase will enable the American Institutes for Research to continue partnering with the Massachusetts Department of Elementary and Secondary Education, the Minnesota Department of Education, and the National Institute on Out-of-School Time at Wellesley College to collect additional data and analyze the impact high-quality afterschool programs can have on the development of literacy skills for elementary school-aged children and the role that social and emotional learning may play in supporting the development of literacy-related skills.

title: Upper Midwest CSA Consortium
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant will enable the Indiana Youth Institute to help lead the Upper Midwest Children’s Savings Account Consortium. The grantee’s leadership will support programs and organizations working to advance state and local children’s saving account initiatives across the Great Lakes region and stoke demand for children’s savings account programs in the Midwest region, creating an environment where new programs can develop. Additionally, the grantee will provide technical assistance to existing programs to ensure high quality and growth. The Indiana Youth Institute, which is headquartered in Indianapolis, promotes the healthy development of Indiana children and youth through its service of people, institutions and communities in Indiana.

title: Migration and Forced Displacement Program
description: The project goal is to address the new and continued challenges facing immigrants throughout the Americas. The Hispanics in Philanthropy Migration and Forced Displacement Program accomplishes this through grantmaking, rapid COVID-19 response, funder engagement, capacity building and communications efforts. During the previous grant period, the grantee provided over $2 million in grants to nonprofits across the Americas, strengthened nonprofits and responded swiftly to COVID-19. During this grant period, the grantee will continue these activities and respond to the emerging needs of the Hispanic and Latinx community. Founded in 1981, Hispanics in Philanthropy is the leading philanthropic membership organization for grantmaking in Hispanic and Latino communities.
