The grantee works across the Americas to strengthen Latino leadership, equity and voice by facilitating greater philanthropic investments in Latino communities.

title: Community Advice Office Support Project
description: The project goal is to increase access to justice for poor and marginalized communities in South Africa. To this end, ProBono.Org will work closely with community advice offices in the Gauteng province of South Africa. Past support assisted the grantee to consolidate its work with community advice offices in the Gauteng province. With a narrowed focus, the grantee increased the quality of support it provided to advice offices. With this grant, ProBono.Org intends to continue its support to community advice offices and increase its reach in the Gauteng province. Key interventions include back-up legal services, capacity-building, and financial support to community advice offices. The grantee is a nonpartisan civil society organization that subscribes to the values of transformative constitutionalism, the rule of law, and social justice. Its primary focus is to harness the skills and expertise of legal practitioners to deliver pro bono civil legal assistance to organizations working for social justice and to expand access to justice for low-income, vulnerable, and marginalized communities.

title: Community Advice Office Support Project
description: The goal of the Community Advice Office Support Project is to increase access to justice for poor and marginalized communities in the Gauteng province of South Africa. To this end, ProBono.Org will work with a network of seven community advice offices to provide free justice services in poor and marginalized communities. The grantee will also use its network of attorneys to help facilitate their mandatory pro bono hours towards back-up legal support. Working in partnership with attorneys, the grantee will provide legal training sessions on various topics to community paralegals. The grantee is a nonpartisan civil society organization that subscribes to the values of transformative constitutionalism, the rule of law and social justice. ProBono.Org’s primary focus is to harness the skills and expertise of legal practitioners to deliver pro bono civil legal assistance to organizations working for social justice and to expand access to justice for low-income, vulnerable and marginalized communities.

title: Afterschool and Service-Learning Initiative
location: St. Louis Park, MN, United States
description: This grant will support the National Youth Leadership Council to integrate service-learning into afterschool programs to increase student engagement in their schools and communities. The grantee will: 1) work with up to 16 statewide afterschool networks to integrate service-learning into local afterschool programs; 2) develop service-learning curriculum for afterschool programs that can be part of the Mott Afterschool App; and 3) create and support a learning community to share information and best practices on service-learning in afterschool programs.

title: Library Renovations and Upgrades
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide support to the Flint Public Library to renovate the existing building located on the Flint Cultural Center campus. The 60-year-old facility will undergo renovations to update aging systems, modernize the facility with state-of-the-art technology, and create flexible and vibrant meeting and learning spaces. This grant also provides support for a move to a temporary location while renovations take place. The newly renovated building will continue to be a community hub for residents and a place for literacy and learning for people of all ages.

title: Research Project: Creating an Enabling Environment for Community Paralegals in Africa
description: The project goal is to generate knowledge and evidence on the impact of community paralegals in addressing injustices in Africa. To this end, the University of the Western Cape will work with the African Centre of Excellence for Access to Justice in its first phase of research to document the environment in which community paralegals operate. The two organizations will conduct research in selected African countries where community paralegals operate, but little documentary evidence exists about the environment in which they operate. These countries are Ghana, Mozambique, Nigeria, Tanzania, Uganda, and Zambia. The Dullah Omar Institute for Constitutional Law, Governance and Human Rights at the University of the Western Cape has extensive experience in conducting legal and social research and executing informed advocacy on justice services.

title: Economic Analysis of Lead Service Line Replacement
description: The Pediatric Public Health Initiative at Michigan State University will complete an economic analysis of the costs and benefits of lead service line replacement in Michigan. Concerns about the costs to municipalities of compliance with Michigan’s recent lead and copper rule have been raised. The research team will also create and distribute a public-facing report for an academic journal article. This grant will enable municipalities, stakeholders, and concerned citizens better understand the benefits of the new rule.

title: Early Warning System
geographic_focus: Brazil, Peru, Ecuador, Colombia, Bolivia, Argentina
description: This project will support the International Accountability Project, a nongovernmental organization focused on reforming development finance, to curate its Early Warning System web tool and develop its network of administrators. Over the past grant period, the grantee increased the number of financial institutions and development projects monitored, built a regional network of partners to use the Early Warning System and monitored trends in social and environmental governance and transparency of development finance. Over the next grant period, the grantee will curate the Early Warning System, support partners and networks in its use and engage development finance institutions to improve and promote more sustainable energy and infrastructure finance and development.

title: Early Warning System
geographic_focus: Brazil, Peru, Colombia, Bolivia, Argentina, Ecuador
description: This project will support the International Accountability Project, a nongovernmental organization focused on reforming development finance, to curate its Early Warning System web tool and develop the tool’s network of administrators. The Early Warning System organizes, summarizes and standardizes policy and project loans from international development finance institutions. Over the past grant period, the grantee broadened and deepened its work in South America, achieved greater transparency for financing projects and welcomed three new organizations in South America to co-lead the Early Warning System. Over the next grant period, the grantee will curate and use the Early Warning System, support partners and networks, and identify trends in energy development finance to ensure more sustainable energy and infrastructure finance and development.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Illinois, Indiana, Ohio, Ontario, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Michigan, New York, Pennsylvania
description: Freshwater Future serves a vital role as an intermediary between large organizations and smaller, grassroots groups. The grantee catalyzes action to strengthen policies to safeguard the Great Lakes by providing a small grants program, consulting services, and capacity building support. With prior support, the grantee has provided support to over 2,000 community groups, addressing local challenges and elevating voices to effect change on the state, provincial, or federal policy levels. This grant increase is available for the general purpose of the organization including securing services for facilitation of a multi-stakeholder meeting on drinking water affordability issues.

title: Access to Justice Programme
description: The Elders, a grouping of prominent global leaders, will promote equal access to justice for all. They will undertake global advocacy efforts to frame a narrative around people-centered justice that seeks to address people’s critical justice needs. They will also encourage commitments of additional financial resources to these efforts while also identifying and resolving obstacles to substantive changes in improving justice provision. In addition, the grantee will work to highlight efforts to eliminate gender-based violence as part of the broader quest for justice. This work will focus principally on affecting global policy dialogues on justice in the context of the Sustainable Development Goals, although the grantee will also work to support justice reforms in specific countries, principally in Africa. Initiated by Nelson Mandela, The Elders brings together prominent and experienced political, cultural, and social leaders to work towards solutions of pressing global problems.

title: Supporting the National Network of Statewide Afterschool Networks
description: Collaborative Communications Group will continue to support, convene and enhance the afterschool ecosystem of grantees, including the 50 State Afterschool Network, the Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative and leading afterschool programs. For the 50 State Network, the grantee will coordinate all Network meetings including large national afterschool and education conferences; manage webinars, the Network website and online community; provide professional development opportunities for the 50 State Network; collaborate with Mizzen by Mott to increase quality programs; and implement convenings as needed to advance partnerships in the afterschool and education sectors.

title: General Purposes
description: The Legal Aid Forum was established in 2009 with a mission to provide and promote equitable access to justice for indigent and vulnerable persons in Rwanda. Past support allowed the grantee to increase its reach in providing justice services, undertake legal education and awareness, build the capacity of community paralegals and publish research on access to justice and legal empowerment. In addition to providing justice services, continued support to the Legal Aid Forum will allow it to standardize the curriculum of paralegals, conduct paralegal trainings and coordinate the work paralegals in Rwanda.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support increased access to justice for poor and marginalized people in Rwanda. To this end, the Legal Aid Forum will continue implementing its justice services through paralegals, lawyers and its network of legal services members. The grantee will conduct trainings for paralegals, hold legal aid clinics and strengthen its technology to provide justice services. Past support has helped the grantee to reach 2,551,809 beneficiaries through legal representation in and out of court, legal education of communities and training of paralegals. The Legal Aid Forum was established in 2009 with a mission to provide and promote equitable access to justice for indigent and vulnerable persons in Rwanda.

title: Solar Energy for Amazon River Dwellers
grantee: Centro de Estudos Avançados de Promoção Social e Ambiental
description: The Centro de Estudos Avançados de Promoção Social e Ambiental is a nonprofit organization in the Amazon founded in 1985 to promote sustainable community development and Amazon forest conservation by improving public policies and quality of life of children, youth, indigenous peoples, and minorities. Over the project period, the grantee is expanding its installation of solar systems, testing small-scale biogas production, participating in design and implementation of a national renewable energy trade fair, conducting training, and monitoring and collecting data to publish results of its systems operation and management for replication. With this increase, the organization will supply four villages with solar water pumping systems.

title: General Purposes
description: This general purposes grant will help to establish a new Tanzanian-led non-governmental organization, the E-LICO Foundation. The E-LICO Foundation brings together the experience and expertise of Tanzanian energy access professionals, who want to improve rural livelihoods by the use of solar powered agricultural equipment. This grant will assist in the establishment of its organizational system and infrastructure as well as expand the network of stakeholders and partnerships. In addition, the grantee’s staff will work with local farmers and their communities to develop and implement pilot solar drip irrigation projects in key regions of Tanzania.

title: Building National Dialogues on Integrated Electricity Planning in East Africa
description: Since 1982, the World Resources Institute has been providing information, ideas and solutions to solve some of the world’s most intricate environmental challenges. Over the past grant period, the grantee has enhanced the quality of data and strengthened the capacity of various stakeholders using the Energy Access Explorer — an open-access online geospatial assessment tool — to support energy access planning and programs. The tool is used in five African countries and India. During the next grant period, the grantee will strengthen the functionality of the Energy Access Explorer by incorporating new datasets and expanding its application for the productive use of renewable energy services. The World Resources Institute will also strengthen the technical capacity and knowledge sharing among key users of the Energy Access Explorer tool across several countries.

title: Bretton Woods Project
description: ActionAid’s Bretton Woods Project has been a key actor on international financial institution reform issues since it was established in 1995. Over the last grant period, the project helped to lock in World Bank Group commitments to climate change and a green energy transition. The project also monitored the impacts of the COVID-19 recovery response, focusing on transparency and accountability for investments in energy and infrastructure. With this grant, the Bretton Woods Project will continue its work to strengthen civil society engagement with the World Bank Group, ensure the bank’s new climate change commitments are implemented and use its publications to provide a voice for civil society analysis and recommendations in the United Kingdom and developing countries.

title: Development Banks and Sustainable Development
geographic_focus: Southeastern Asia, Africa, South America, China, Southern Asia, World
description: China’s development finance institutions have more assets than all other actors in the multilateral finance system. Those institutions invest in energy and infrastructure projects around the world, often resulting in environmental damage and harm to local communities, as well as contributing to climate change. The Global Development Policy Center at Boston University has become a major research center analyzing the impacts of Chinese development finance and providing open-access data to researchers and policymakers in China and in countries that receive Chinese finance. With this grant, the grantee will continue its collaborative research and policy dialogues with governments, civil society, the private sector and development finance institutions. In addition, this grant will also support a China Global Fellows program, aimed at building a new generation of scholar-researchers on these issues.

title: African Development Bank Energy Financing
description: Over the past 70 years Christian Aid has been supporting efforts to advance sustainable development, eradicate poverty, support civil society and provide disaster relief in the developing world. During the last grant period, the grantee strengthened the capacity of more than 50 civil society organizations and coalitions in Africa to monitor and inform investment policies of the Africa Development Bank and other multilateral finance institutions. These efforts were aimed toward shifting investments away from fossil-fuel development to increased investments in decentralized renewable energy solutions, which help solve global climate change. During the next grant period, Christian Aid will consolidate and expand on these efforts by increasing its civil society partnerships to enable broader regional and national level civil society organization engagement on these issues.

title: Addressing Changes in International Development Finance
description: Since 1990, Eurodad has led a network of nongovernmental organizations working on issues related to development finance, sustainable development and poverty reduction. The grantee works to strengthen the capacity of civil society organizations in Europe, Africa and Latin America to transform international development finance, making it more transparent and sustainable. Over the past grant period, the grantee has deepened its engagement with partners to focus on the environmental and social risks and opportunities for improving development finance as it responds to the COVID-19 pandemic. This grant will allow the organization to consolidate its work on promoting strong environmental and social standards for international development finance and to reflect on and share lessons learned.

title: Promoting Environmental and Social Standards in the Financial Sector
description: Urgewald is a German based organization that works to establish strong, binding environmental and social standards for international development finance institutions and to gain public support for responsible and accountable development financial institutions. To achieve these goals, the grantee undertakes research, education and advocacy efforts with a global network of local communities, nongovernmental organizations and other partners. Over the next grant period, the grantee will monitor implementation and review of the World Bank Group’s, Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank’s and Asian Development Bank’s environmental and social policies, as well as trigger an international public debate through publications and media discourse about development finance institutions’ resettlement policies for human populations.

title: Technical Assistance to Boost Great Lakes Communication
geographic_focus: Pennsylvania, Michigan, Minnesota, Wisconsin, Ohio, New York, Indiana, Illinois
description: Since its inception in 1996, with significant support from the Mott Foundation, Freshwater Future has provided over $4 million through 1,200 grants for capacity building and technical support to groups working to protect and restore the waters of the region. During the previous grant period, the grantee has made an average of over $22,000 in technical services available to partner organizations to support and enhance their communications capacity. The grantee has also made available training videos on a variety of topics that support the community of freshwater organizations in the Great Lakes region. During the next grant period, Freshwater Future will expand the pool of organizations receiving direct technical support and continue to provide training and tools to other organizations to more effectively utilize communications to advance organizational objectives.

title: Great Lakes Program
description: River Alliance of Wisconsin is a statewide organization that works to improve the health of the Great Lakes Ecosystem. In its Great Lakes Program project, the grantee is working with state, local, and regional partners to advance water policy reform and support local groups working on freshwater projects. The purpose of the increase is to enable the group to conduct research and develop effective communications approaches to educate citizens around a Wisconsin water agenda.

title: Great Lakes Ecosystem Project
description: The Ohio Environmental Council is a statewide environmental organization that leads efforts to protect and restore Lake Erie and its tributaries. The grantee provides scientific, legal, and policy analyses and technical assistance to citizens, nonprofits, and decision makers. With prior Mott support, the grantee has helped implement the Great Lakes Compact, prevent invasive species, and protect drinking water through integrated water management. With this increase, the grantee will commission a report on Ohio’s water infrastructure investments and water affordability at the community and individual level.

title: PFAS Action Network
description: The Ecology Center is a Michigan-based organization with extensive experience and a national reputation of excellence for addressing toxic chemical science, health impacts and solutions to contamination problems. With prior Mott support, the grantee led the formation of the PFAS Action Network, a coalition of community-based organizations, state and national groups working together to support each other and coordinate efforts to protect communities from the class of toxic chemicals known as PFAS. Working together in the first year, the groups established an operating structure, formed a steering committee, hired staff, launched the network and identified policy priorities. With renewed support, the Ecology Center will assist and coordinate community member groups, convene meetings, develop communications materials and provide contract support to network members and partners.

title: Philanthropy Panel Study
description: This grant provides support for the Philanthropy Panel Study, an ongoing research study managed by the Indiana University’s Lilly Family School of Philanthropy that collects detailed data on the giving and volunteering habits of several thousand American households over time and over generations. It is conducted in conjunction with the University of Michigan Institute for Social Research’s Panel Study of Income Dynamics, which has surveyed families since 1968 and to which a philanthropy component was added in 2001. The dataset produced by the study is the best, most accurate resource for measuring giving and volunteering in the U.S. and is used extensively by researchers. The Lilly Family School of Philanthropy at Indiana University was founded in 2012. The grantee is dedicated to improving philanthropy by training and empowering students and practitioners to be innovators and leaders who create positive and lasting change in the world.

title: Afterschool and Service-Learning Initiative
location: St. Louis Park, MN, United States
description: This grant will support the National Youth Leadership Council to integrate service-learning into afterschool programs to increase student engagement in their schools and communities. The grantee will: 1) work with four statewide afterschool networks to deepen and expand service-learning into local afterschool programs; 2) develop resources for afterschool programs that can be placed on Mizzen by Mott; 3) support a learning community to share information and best practices on service-learning in afterschool programs; and 4) create profiles on the various methods of integration of service-learning within the statewide afterschool networks and afterschool programs.

title: Assets Evaluation and Data Collection Project
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: Brandeis University’s Institute for Economic and Racial Equity is a research institute that promotes programs and policies that expand economic opportunity and equity for individuals and families, particularly households of color. Renewal funding will enable the Institute to continue advancing the children’s savings account movement by helping stakeholders utilize and leverage data to accelerate best practices, promote coordination and collaboration and inform policy. Key activities planned for the renewal grant period include collecting and sharing data on key field metrics, coordinating the grantee learning community and preparing a summative analysis of field progress. The Mott Foundation has supported Brandeis University on asset-building and savings strategies since 2008.

title: General Purposes
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant provides general purpose support to Red Ink Flint. The grantee operates Flint Local 432, a performance venue located in downtown Flint for artistic programming and community convening. In 2019, 52 concerts were performed at the venue, including local musical talent as well as regional and national acts. Additionally, the grantee operates the Factory Two makerspace, which opened on Grand Traverse Street in 2017. Funds will support organizational, administrative and programmatic costs for Red Ink Flint.

title: Launch Flint Pitch Competitions
description: This grant will support the Ferris Wheel Innovation Center to organize and implement business pitch competitions in Flint. The grantee was established to help entrepreneurs in an economically disadvantaged community gain access to supports that advance their business or product ideas. Pitch competitions are a way to provide struggling entrepreneurs with the resources needed to move their concepts forward. Competition winners will receive financial resources and all participants will receive mentoring from business professionals.

title: Upper Midwest CSA Consortium
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant will enable the Indiana Youth Institute to help lead the Upper Midwest Children’s Savings Account Consortium. The grantee’s leadership will support programs and organizations working to advance state and local children’s saving account initiatives across the Great Lakes region and stoke demand for children’s savings account programs in the Midwest region, creating an environment where new programs can develop. Additionally, the grantee will provide technical assistance to existing programs to ensure high quality and growth. Over the course of two years, the grantee, along with the Heartland Alliance, aims to continue advancing high-quality children’s savings accounts in the region, while laying the groundwork for the planning and funding needed to advance children’s savings accounts in the region in the longer-term. The Indiana Youth Institute, which is headquartered in Indianapolis, promotes the healthy development of Indiana children and youth through its service of people, institutions and communities in Indiana.

title: Midwest Children's Savings Account Initiative
grantee: Heartland Alliance for Human Needs & Human Rights
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
geographic_focus: Nebraska, Minnesota, Wisconsin, Iowa, Ohio, Michigan, Illinois, Indiana
description: This grant will enable Heartland Alliance for Human Needs & Human Rights to organize the Midwest Children’s Savings Account Consortium. For over four years, the grantee has cultivated and led the Midwest Children’s Savings Account Consortium, providing support for an active group of stakeholders in the Midwest region working to advance children’s savings account programs and policies. This has catalyzed the launch of new children’s savings account programs, supported the expansion of existing programs and created an environment ripe for the growth of children’s savings accounts in the region. When this children’s savings account project began in January 2017, 24 children’s savings account programs were covering 21 counties in the region. By the end of 2020, the number of children’s savings account programs in the region more than doubled, with 55 children’s savings account programs covering 53 counties. Over the course of two years, Heartland Alliance, along with the Indiana Youth Institute, aims to continue advancing high-quality children’s savings accounts in the region, while laying the groundwork for the planning and funding needed to advance children’s savings accounts in the region in the longer term.

title: Sustainable Development Finance in South America
description: The Asociación Ambiente y Sociedad is a Colombian nonprofit organization specializing in research, monitoring and advocacy related to investment and development finance in Colombia and South America. Over the last grant period, the grantee worked with regional coalitions to strengthen public consultation in the development of the Inter-American Development Bank Group’s Environmental Social Policy Framework and Chinese social and environmental commitments in its overseas investments. This grant renewal will support the grantee’s ongoing efforts to monitor Chinese investment, as well as the implementation of new social and environmental frameworks at international financial institutions.

title: Path Forward for Michigan's Cities
description: The Lincoln Institute of Land Policy works with partners to develop and advance effective approaches to solve critical economic, social, and environmental challenges. It will address the municipal financial distress of Michigan cities by building cross-sectoral coalitions to advance solutions to the issue.

title: Travel and Learning Fund
description: The project goal is to advance the Civil Society program’s objectives and outcomes by supporting exchange, networking, and interaction among key nonprofits, practitioners, and experts, including Mott grantees, working in the program’s thematic areas of interest. To this end, the Institute of International Education will establish a travel and learning fund to support individuals working on civic space, community philanthropy, access to justice, or other areas of interest to the Civil Society program. During the grant period, approximately 30 people will receive financial support in order to: participate in study visits and exchanges; attend conferences and events; or conduct field studies and research that results in a report or publication that benefits the field. Based in New York, the Institute of International Education manages similar funds for foundations around the world.

title: Sloan Museum Renovation and Expansion Project
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant increase to the Flint Cultural Center Foundation will provide additional funding for the design and renovation of the Sloan Museum facility, which will now be called the Sloan Museum of Discovery. The funds will support design development activities, including construction costs, general contractor fees, and exhibit construction and installation costs. The new museum building will feature over 42,000 square feet of additional space and programming to benefit the region. The new design incorporates a variety of areas designed for young children and K-12 students by bringing a science center and history museum together under one roof. This new vision encourages discovery by embracing technology, incorporating advanced design thinking, and creating interactive history and science experiences.

title: Sloan Museum Renovation and Expansion Project
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant increase to the Flint Cultural Center Foundation will provide additional funding for the design and renovation of the Sloan Museum, which will now be called the Sloan Museum of Discovery. The funds will support design development activities including construction costs, general contractor fees, and exhibit construction and installation costs. The new museum building will feature over 42,000 square feet of additional space and programming to benefit the region. The new design incorporates a variety of areas for young children and K-12 students by bringing a science center and history museum together under one roof. This new vision encourages discovery by embracing technology, incorporating advanced design thinking, and creating interactive history and science experiences.

title: Library Renovations and Upgrades
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide support to the Flint Public Library to renovate the existing building located on the Flint Cultural Center campus. The 60-year-old facility will undergo renovations to update aging systems, modernize the facility with state-of-the-art technology, and create flexible and vibrant meeting and learning spaces. This grant also provides support for a move to a temporary location while renovations take place. The newly renovated building will continue to be a community hub for residents and a place for literacy and learning for people of all ages.

title: Metropolitan Policy Program
description: The Metropolitan Policy Program at Brookings Institution, an internationally known think tank, works with local communities to assist in the development and strategy for retooling the American economy. With renewal support, the grantee will undertake a range of work to promote the economic competitiveness of metropolitan areas domestically and globally, including older industrial cities such as Flint. Activities will include original research, policy advocacy, analytical tool development and network building.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support New America in its mission of developing independent, nonpartisan analysis and recommendations reflective of rigorous scholarship, and promoting those ideas through broad public discourse. Some Flint-specific work may focus on assisting populations of color to have more opportunities in the current economy.

title: Blight Elimination and Neighborhood Stabilization
description: This grant will provide support to the Genesee County Land Bank Authority to engage in neighborhood revitalization activities around Kettering University, Durant-Tuuri-Mott Elementary School, Chevy Commons, Mott Park, the Flint River, and Atwood Stadium. These activities will include property demolition, blight elimination, property cleanup, painting, and home improvement. Demolishing properties is an important step in stabilizing the neighborhood.

title: General Purposes
description: Founded in 2006, AdvocAid is a human rights organization that provides holistic justice services to women and girls in Sierra Leone using a legal empowerment approach. Past support has allowed the grantee to provide legal services to 159 women per month, in eight towns across Sierra Leone. The grantee also represented 159 women in court and conducted 42 legal education sessions for poor and marginalized people. This grant will allow AdvocAid to continue its justice services with women under its new 2021-2025 strategy, which prioritizes access to justice.

title: General Purposes
description: Founded in 2006, AdvocAid is a human rights organization that provides holistic justice services to women and girls in Sierra Leone using a legal empowerment approach. Past support has allowed the grantee to provide justice services to over 2,000 women and girls in Sierra Leone. The grantee has also launched a scholarship program to encourage more women to become lawyers in Sierra Leone. This grant will allow AdvocAid to continue its justice services to poor and marginalized women and girls in Sierra Leone under its 2021-25 strategy which prioritizes access to justice.

title: Carriage Town/Durant-Tuuri-Mott Neighborhood Revitalization
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: The Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation will redevelop three to four residential housing units in the Carriage Town Historic District, all of which are owned by the Genesee County Land Bank Authority. The homes will be sold as owner-occupied units in the neighborhood. In addition, the grantee will demolish the liquor store located at 847 Stevenson Street that is currently vacant and blighted and within close proximity to the Educare facility and Durant-Tuuri-Mott Elementary School.

title: Dullah Omar School for Paralegalism
description: The project provides training for community-based paralegals in South Africa. The Dullah Omar School for Paralegalism, a project of the Social Change Assistance Trust, was launched in 2015 by a group of organizations working with community-based paralegals to provide coordinated training targeted at young paralegals to build their skills. Over the years, the school has provided accredited and nonaccredited training to community-based paralegals working in community advice offices across the country. The school has also exposed paralegals to important issues affecting the sector and created opportunities for paralegals to network and learn from one another. The grantee is a grantmaking organization that was established in 1984 to promote human rights and social justice by making grants to community-based organizations and supports programs that promote access to justice, gender equality, youth development, and local economic development. This grant will enable the Social Change Assistance Trust to implement the Dullah Omar School for Paralegalism to provide training for paralegals across the country in order to build the next generation of community-based paralegals.

title: Dullah Omar School for Paralegalism
description: The Dullah Omar School for Paralegalism — a project of the Social Change Assistance Trust — was established in 2015 by a group of organizations working with community-based paralegals to provide coordinated training for young paralegals. The school provides accredited and non-accredited training to paralegals working in marginalized communities in South Africa. In the past, the school provided training to over 150 paralegals and exposed them to the current issues affecting the sector and access to justice more broadly. The school also provided opportunities for paralegals to connect and share experiences. The grantee is a grantmaking organization that promotes human rights and social justice by making grants to community advice offices and other local development agencies. The grantee supports groups that promote access to justice, gender equity, local economic development and human rights. During the current grant period, Social Change Assistance Trust will continue to implement the project by bringing together over 80 community-based paralegals to develop their skills, access theoretical and ideological education and increase their management capacity to lead the advice offices in their communities effectively.

title: Strengthening Dam Standards and Protecting Rivers
description: With offices in South America, Asia, Africa, and the United States, International Rivers is one of the most effective international, nongovernmental organizations working on river protection. By partnering with local communities in more than 40 countries, the grantee successfully promotes sustainable uses of freshwater systems around the world. Additionally, it plays a major role in international efforts to strengthen policies at public financial institutions. This grant increase will support International Rivers’ search to replace its executive director as well as costs to retain a firm to conduct a board evaluation.

title: Philanthropy Panel Study
description: Managed by the Indiana University’s Lilly Family School of Philanthropy, the Philanthropy Panel Study collects detailed data on the giving and volunteering habits of several thousand American households over time and over generations. The study is conducted in conjunction with the University of Michigan Institute for Social Research’s Panel Study of Income Dynamics, which has surveyed families since 1968 and to which a philanthropy component was added in 2001. The dataset produced by the study is a comprehensive and accurate resource for measuring giving and volunteering in the U.S. and is used extensively by philanthropy and social sector researchers. Founded in 2012, the Lilly Family School of Philanthropy at Indiana University is dedicated to improving philanthropy by training and empowering students and practitioners to be innovators and leaders who create positive and lasting change in the world.

title: Solar Village: Vila Limeira
description: World Wildlife Fund and it’s partner World Wildlife Fund Brazil work in the Brazilian Amazon to achieve a national off-grid solar energy program for isolated communities living in extractive reserve conservation units. This increase will continue support to the grantee for training technicians, building, and monitoring the success of one of the first 100 percent solar villages in the Amazon rainforest.

title: Solar Energy for Chiribiquete Forest Dwellers
description: Amazon Conservation Team has been working with traditional communities in the Colombian Amazon rainforest to develop forest conservation and sustainable livelihoods, including renewable energy access. Over the past grant period, the organization’s solar energy access initiative expanded to benefit 5,500 people in nearly 1,200 indigenous families and made progress toward universalizing renewable energy access. Over the next grant period, the grantee will expand solar access for the health and development of a sustainable value chain and work on policy for replication of solar energy access in the Colombian Amazon.

title: Advancing Solutions to Water Affordability
geographic_focus: Indiana, Wisconsin, Ohio, Minnesota, Illinois, Pennsylvania, New York, Michigan
description: There is growing concern in the Great Lakes region and across the nation about the rising cost of water, the need to invest $1 trillion in upgrades in water infrastructure nationally over the next 25 years, and the burden this will place on low income households. Elevate Energy has worked from its base in Chicago to address affordability issues in the energy sector. With this grant, the grantee will bring together community groups and water professionals from across the Great Lakes region to share research, lessons learned, and advance solutions to issues of water affordability, work one-on-one with a water utility to pilot specific solutions, and explore the feasibility of establishing a region-wide water affordability technical assistance program for Great Lakes utilities.

title: 21st Century Community Learning Centers Summer Institute
description: This grant will provide funding to support a convening of the 21st Century Community Learning Centers, held in partnership with Synergy Enterprises, Inc., and the U.S. Department of Education. The 21st Century Community Learning Centers initiative supports nearly 2 million children and youth in over 11,000 school-community afterschool programs across the country. The purpose of the annual summer institute is to provide afterschool administrators and staff with technical assistance and strategies to continue to enhance the quality of school-community afterschool programs.

title: Solar Village: Tamandua
description: The Instituto Socioambiental’s Energy and Community program promotes off-grid renewable energy for remote indigenous communities in the Brazilian Amazon. This grant increase will continue to support the grantee to train technicians, build, and monitor the success of one of the first 100 percent solar villages, located in the Brazilian Amazon state of Roraima.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Centre for Community Justice and Development
description: The project goal is to increase access to justice for poor and marginalized people in South Africa. To this end, the Centre for Community Justice and Development will work with its network of community advice offices in the KwaZulu-Natal province of South Africa to provide justice services. Past support helped the grantee increase the number of advice offices with which it works. It also adjusted its work to be responsive to the COVID-19 pandemic by providing both humanitarian and justice relief to poor and marginalized people affected by the lockdown in South Africa. Continued support will allow the grantee to recruit and train community paralegals, assist advice offices with fundraising and financial reporting, conduct research, and help communities recover from the destruction caused by the lockdown due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Monitoring Hydropower Impacts in the Amazon
description: The Getulio Vargas Foundation’s Center for Sustainability Studies is a higher education institution dedicated to promoting sustainable development in Brazil. Over the past grant period, the center worked with civil society organizations and universities in the Amazon to develop the Independent Territorial Monitoring Network with 28 members and published a book on monitoring the social and environmental impacts of large-scale energy and infrastructure investment in the Amazon. Monitoring activities that began around the large-scale Belo Monte hydroelectric power project informed the transfer of lessons learned to similar projects planned for the Tapajos River. Over the next project period, the grantee will consolidate the network and connect it to actors from financial institutions to strengthen and expand the network’s influence on investment in the Amazon.

title: Identifying Water Infrastructure Funding Options
description: Michigan faces a water infrastructure funding gap of approximately $800 million per year, covering wastewater, drinking water, and stormwater. Closing this funding gap is imperative if Michigan is to meet its responsibility to citizens and the environment. The Michigan Environmental Council will lead a collaborative project with partners to research and analyze various funding solutions to address Michigan’s pressing water needs.

title: 21st Century Community Learning Centers Summer Institute
description: This grant will provide funding to support a convening of the 21st Century Community Learning Centers held in partnership with Synergy Enterprises, Inc. and the U.S. Department of Education. The 21st Century Community Learning Centers initiative supports nearly 2 million children and youth in over 11,000 school-community afterschool programs across the country. The purpose of the annual summer Institute is to provide afterschool administrators and staff with technical assistance and strategies to continue to enhance the quality of school-community afterschool programs.

title: Solar Electrician and Entrepreneurship Training
description: The Salesian Missions have been providing education and technical training to poor children around the globe since 1947. The grantee began its work to establish vocational training and youth empowerment centers across Tanzania in 1980. They have now expanded their vocational training to address the energy access deficit in Tanzania. To reach the rural areas, it is crucial that there are adequate technical skills to help develop, sustain, and maintain off-grid solar electric assets deployed to these areas. With this increase, additional funding will provide students with field visits to mini-grid sites, internships with energy access providers, and entrepreneurship training. Additional project management staff will be hired to expand the impact of the Solar Technician Training Program.

title: Sustainable Energy for All
description: The United Nations Foundation was established in 1988 to support the goals and objectives of the United Nations. Sustainable Energy for All was set up as a United Nations initiative to promote and directly support new collaborations to address the challenges of expanding energy access, increasing energy efficiency, and growing renewable energy. Through this project, a coordinated global effort is being established to achieve the goal of universal energy access by mobilizing leaders and building effective coalitions and partnerships to fast track action and close financing gaps. This grant increase will support the expansion of the grantee’s efforts to address energy access, particularly through support and development of mini-grids.

title: Aviation Academy
description: The Genesee Intermediate School District is a regional service agency that provides leadership to improve education and enhance lifelong learning for youth and adults. As part of its work, the grantee administers Genesee Career Institute, a state-of-the-art career and technical education center that prepares high school students for immediate entry into the workforce after graduation. This grant will help support the development of a new aviation academy at Genesee Career Institute. The academy will prepare students for careers in the aviation industry.

title: Engaging Afterschool Programs in Geography, Exploration and Science
description: This grant increase will enable the National Geographic Society to continue developing the content supports for the Mott Afterschool App and the afterschool field. In addition, the increase and extension request will allow additional time for the grantee and Mott Foundation to work towards alignment in approaches for the Intellectual Property legal language pertaining to content development for the Mott Afterschool App and additional items related to data collection.

title: Renewable Roraima: Studies for Isolated Community Electrification
description: The Instituto Clima e Sociedade is a Brazilian philanthropic organization that promotes prosperity, justice and low-carbon development in Brazil. Over the past project period, the grantee worked with Brazilian partners to build the Roraima renewable energy forum, which successfully expanded renewable energy access in the Amazonian state. This grant renewal will support the development and testing of business models for expanding renewable energy access in the Brazilian Amazon.

title: Billy Durant Society and Entrepreneurial Support
description: The Genesee Chamber Foundation is a supporting organization of the Flint & Genesee Chamber of Commerce and is organized to receive and administer funds for educational and charitable purposes, and the public welfare of Genesee County. This grant will support the launch of the Billy Durant Society, a small diverse group of community stakeholders (universities, schools, government, entrepreneurs, and businesses) that will convene regularly to develop ideas and solutions for moving economic development forward in Flint and Genesee County. In 2019, Billy Durant Society members will travel to a city with a robust economic development system and participate in site visits and discussions on entrepreneurship and small business development. In 2020, national representatives will come to Flint to educate Billy Durant Society members about economic development and sustainable strategies that can help lead to prosperity in Flint.

title: Nebraska Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Nebraska Children and Families Foundation to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will: 1) implement innovations that take advantage of one-time pandemic funding and contribute to the development of a more sustainable afterschool sector in Nebraska; 2) continue developing a network of state and local partnerships that lead to a more supportive policy environment that allows more communities to launch and sustain high-quality expanded learning opportunity programs; 3) grow a diverse and sustainable funding base that supports efforts to enhance Nebraska’s expanded learning opportunities sector as programs expand across the state; 4) cultivate a robust set of local and statewide partnerships that allow the Nebraska state afterschool network and its community partners to support more high-quality expanded learning opportunity programming; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen by Mott.

title: Education Program Data Collection and Assessment
description: This project will continue to support the development of an evaluation and data collection plan for the Foundation’s education program, with a particular focus on the Advancing Afterschool area. Schaffer&Combs will further develop an evaluation framework and assessment of the 50-state afterschool network that both supports current Education Program priorities, and lays the groundwork for increased learning and more effective grantmaking and grantee performance in the coming years. Established in 2008, Schaffer&Combs is an international management consulting firm based in San Francisco, with offices in Chicago and Durham.

title: Advancing Solutions to Water Affordability
geographic_focus: New York, Michigan, Illinois, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Minnesota, Indiana, Wisconsin
description: Elevate Energy is a nonprofit organization based in Chicago that designs and implements water and energy programs to ensure access to clean and affordable water, heat and power. With prior Mott support, the grantee convened community groups and water professionals from across the Great Lakes to share research, lessons learned and advance solutions for water affordability. They developed a water utility pilot program and explored the feasibility of establishing a region-wide technical assistance program for utilities. With renewed support, the grantee will research mounting levels of water bill debt in the Great Lakes region, learn about and communicate the lived experience of having water bills that aren’t affordable and provide education and training to utilities and advocates on water affordability challenges and solutions.

title: STEM Fellowship
description: This grant to the STEM Next Opportunity Fund will support the Robert Noyce-Ellen Lettvin Fellowship in Informal STEM Learning. The fellowship is a public-private partnership initiative geared toward advancing high-quality informal science education, including in afterschool and summer learning programs. This initiative will include: 1) strengthening collaboration between the U.S. Department of Education and other federal agencies in the area of informal STEM learning; 2) working to advance STEM learning in the 21st Century Community Learning Centers program; and 3) working with leading researchers to identify priorities in informal STEM learning, including identifying new tools, strategies and programs that improve STEM learning opportunities.

title: General Purposes
description: The Alliance for the Great Lakes is a leading organization working to solve some of the Great Lakes’ biggest challenges. Founded in Chicago more than 50 years ago, the grantee has 22 staff members across the region and in Washington, D.C. With grant support from the Mott Foundation and others, they have made notable progress protecting the lakes from non-native carp and other invaders coming from ships and have helped communities with local water challenges including service shutoffs, fouled drinking water and hot spots of toxic sediments. With this grant, the grantee will execute a new strategic plan that firmly embeds justice, equity, diversity and inclusion into all aspects of their operation. The Alliance for the Great Lakes will undertake advocacy and education efforts to create and strengthen policies that provide safe, clean and accessible water for the more than 40-million residents of the Great Lakes region and ensure that the Great Lakes are protected for today and tomorrow.

title: Protecting Water Resources in the Great Lakes State
description: Michigan Trout Unlimited is a premier group protecting cold water and healthy aquatic habitat in the Great Lakes State. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has helped secure Michigan and neighboring states’ support for preventing invasive carp and other species from damaging Great Lakes water resources and has been the leader of efforts to review and reform state programs to manage water use and withdrawals. Today, these threats continue and the failure of dams near Midland in 2020 underscore the need for better approaches to dam management and removal. With renewed grant support, the grantee will lead efforts to review and refresh water withdrawal processes and programs, help stave off invasive species and seek to restore Michigan rivers by removing dams.

title: Ariadne Network Membership
description: This grant supports the membership and administrative costs of Ariadne, a network of funders who work together to promote and protect civil society and human rights in Europe. Ariadne is a project of Global Dialogue, a nonprofit organization registered in the United Kingdom and based in London. The network has 155 members from 22 European countries. Key activities of the project include an annual conference focused on a range of issues important to members, an annual skill-building workshop, a series of roundtables focused on policy and contextual updates and trends, and periodic workshops and webinars on selected issues. With an active online portal, the project facilitates ongoing exchange among members on rapidly changing issues, including the closing space for civil society. Through its networking activities during the next two years, the project will focus on encouraging and assisting funders to think critically about and play a positive role in addressing the most pressing issues in Europe, including the rise of far-right populism, xenophobia, and the closing space for civil society.

title: National Service and Volunteer Center Capacity Building
description: This grant to the United Way of Genesee County will provide additional capacity to support service throughout Genesee County. National service members and volunteers provide critical resources to area nonprofits, government agencies and schools to help meet a variety of community needs such as blight elimination, neighborhood engagement and tutoring and mentoring.

title: Facility Improvements
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will support technology infrastructure upgrades and facility improvements for MacArthur Recital Hall and the Flint Repertory Theatre at the Flint Institute of Music. The grantee is home to the Flint Symphony Orchestra, Flint Repertory Theatre, and the Flint School of Performing Arts. Audiences and participants had more than 270,000 encounters with the Flint Institute of Music programs and performances in 2018.

title: Synergy: Unlocking Potential in the European Philanthropy Support Ecosystem
grantee: Donors and Foundations Networks in Europe
description: The project goal is to enhance the professionalism and effectiveness of European foundations and their national-level support organizations. To this end, the Donors and Foundations Networks in Europe, a network of 30 donor associations from 28 European countries, will strengthen the capacity of the network to share learning and jointly develop the skills and knowledge necessary to support and grow philanthropy in Europe. Through an annual conference, smaller periodic workshops and meetings, and peer-to-peer exchanges, staff from foundations and national associations will have the opportunity to learn from their colleagues in the sector as well as from other stakeholders and experts. The Donors and Foundations Networks in Europe was established as an informal network in 2009 and operated as a project of the Spanish Association of Foundations. In 2018, the grantee registered as an independent Belgian not-for-profit association based in Brussels.

title: Afterschool Youth Entrepreneurship Initiative
description: This grant to the Massachusetts Afterschool Partnership will enable the Massachusetts Statewide Afterschool Network to build new ecosystems and partnerships to advance high-quality entrepreneurship opportunities in afterschool and summer learning programs. This grant will support the network to: 1) develop entrepreneurship training and curriculum to engage older youth in afterschool settings; 2) grow and promote an ecosystem for public schools to include entrepreneurship in afterschool settings; and 3) engage new and existing partners throughout the state. The grantee will share lessons learned with other state networks to enhance youth entrepreneurship initiatives in afterschool programs.

title: Afterschool Youth Entrepreneurship Initiative
location: Salt Lake City, UT, United States
description: This grant to the Utah Afterschool Network will enable the Utah Statewide Afterschool Network to create an afterschool and summer youth entrepreneurship initiative aimed at impacting high school students. This grant will support the network to: 1) provide mini-grants to afterschool and summer learning programs to increase entrepreneurial opportunities; 2) facilitate an entrepreneurial leadership academy for both in school and out of school leaders; and 3) educate key stakeholders on the importance of afterschool and entrepreneurship. The grantee will share lessons learned with other state networks to enhance youth entrepreneurship initiatives in afterschool programs.

title: Afterschool Youth Entrepreneurship Initiative
description: This grant to the South Carolina Afterschool Alliance will enable the South Carolina Statewide Afterschool Network to incorporate entrepreneurship into the South Carolina College and Career Digital Badges initiative to further expand learning opportunities for high school students. This grant will support the network to: 1) develop entrepreneurship curriculum and lesson plans; 2) host a youth summit on entrepreneurship; and 3) provide research and data on the benefits of afterschool and youth entrepreneurship. The grantee will share lessons learned with other state networks to enhance youth entrepreneurship initiatives in afterschool programs.

title: Afterschool Youth Entrepreneurship Initiative
description: This grant to the University of Missouri – Columbia will enable the Missouri Statewide Afterschool Network to develop a program that prepares afterschool students for local, regional and state entrepreneur opportunities. This grant will support the network to: 1) engage students in afterschool and summer learning programs in a youth entrepreneurship pathway; 2) provide training on youth entrepreneurship for the afterschool field; and 3) develop communications resources on the role of afterschool and youth entrepreneurship. The grantee will share lessons learned with other state networks to enhance youth entrepreneurship initiatives in afterschool programs.

title: Afterschool Youth Entrepreneurship Initiative
description: This grant to the New Jersey School-Age Care Coalition will enable the New Jersey Statewide Afterschool Network to develop an entrepreneurship professional learning institute that provides high-quality training and implementation of an entrepreneurship program for youth at the secondary level. This grant will support the network to: 1) provide training on youth entrepreneurship for the afterschool field; 2) establish a youth entrepreneurship learning community; and 3) develop a communications plan to raise awareness of afterschool and youth entrepreneurship. The grantee will share lessons learned with other state networks to enhance youth entrepreneurship initiatives in afterschool programs.

title: Work-Readiness Program
description: Founded in 1976 Peckham, Inc. is a nonprofit community rehabilitation organization that provides job training and competitive employment opportunities for people with disabilities. The grantee operates 30 rehabilitation and human services programs in Michigan and has satellite manufacturing locations in Arizona and Kentucky. In 2019, the grantee expanded operations to the Flint area and anticipates providing up to 200 apparel manufacturing job opportunities over the next 24 months. Funding will help Peckham, Inc. develop a customized training curriculum for new employees, hire a job trainer and two job coaches, and provide temporary assistance to help people overcome barriers to work.

title: Afterschool Youth Entrepreneurship Initiative
description: This grant to the University of Hawaii will enable the Hawaii Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to opportunities for high school youth to learn about and experience entrepreneurship in afterschool programs. This grant will support the grantee to: 1) create a summer entrepreneurship program for high school students; 2) design training that aligns with Native Hawaiian values for afterschool providers; and 3) educate key stakeholders on the importance of afterschool and entrepreneurship. The grantee will share lessons learned with other state networks to enhance youth entrepreneurship initiatives in afterschool programs.

title: Community Foundation Development Fund
grantee: Academy for the Development of Philanthropy in Poland
description: The program goal is to strengthen the capacity of community foundations in Europe to contribute to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. To this end, the Academy for the Development of Philanthropy in Poland will provide tailor-made grantmaking and technical assistance programs to community foundations in Europe to stimulate innovation in identifying and implementing local responses to global challenges. The grantee will develop a series of learning materials to support community foundations in their work on the global goals. In addition, the grantee will support European community foundations’ responses to the refugee crisis resulting from the Russian invasion of Ukraine. During the past grant period, the grantee provided 17 grants totaling more than $330,000 to community foundations in 12 countries to support their engagement with the global goals as well as 15 grants totaling over $280,000 to community foundations in eight countries supporting Ukrainian refugees. The grantee also published a series of learning materials and organized learning events to increase the capacity of European community foundations to contribute to the global goals. The Academy for the Development of Philanthropy in Poland is based in Warsaw, Poland.

title: Mississippi Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Operation Shoestring which coordinates the Mississippi Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will: 1) spearhead the development of an exemplary model of afterschool programs in Jackson, Mississippi; 2) enhance youth outcomes by integrating afterschool data from programs and schools; 3) work with key state partners to design and implement education recovery funding to help Mississippi youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen by Mott.

title: South Dakota Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support EmBe which coordinates the South Dakota Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will: 1) develop and implement an out-of-school time leadership institute for educators; 2) establish a youth voice council; 3) work with policymakers to design and implement education recovery funding to help South Dakota youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen by Mott.

title: Indiana Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Indiana Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will: 1) build up equitable access to statewide afterschool programming through an awareness initiative and deepened relationships with state agencies; 2) enhance data collection and analysis to support afterschool champions and promotion of youth service providers; 3) work with policymakers to design and implement education recovery funding to help Indiana youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen by Mott.

title: Maryland Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Fund for Educational Excellence, Inc. which coordinates the Maryland Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will: 1) create sustainable afterschool programs as part of Maryland’s community school initiative and education recovery plan; 2) enhance youth outcomes by integrating afterschool data from programs and schools; 3) work with policymakers to design and implement education recovery funding to help Maryland youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen by Mott.

title: Wyoming Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Wyoming Community Foundation to continue development of policy, partnerships and funding to benefit youth in afterschool programs. In addition to Wyoming’s state innovation project described below, this grant also provides support to further policies, improve quality practices and develop strategies to reach more students and families. Specific initiatives will: 1) support the development of school-age health and safety rules; 2) provide professional development and leadership around the development of healing centered engagement and trauma informed strategies; 3) work with policymakers to design and implement education recovery funding to help Wyoming youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen by Mott.

title: Service Education and Outreach Project
description: This grant will support Voices for National Service, a program of City Year, Inc., to continue a communications initiative that will seek to enhance public awareness of the impact of national service programs across the country. Specifically, this initiative will: 1) develop resources highlighting the impact of national service; and 2) leverage media and events to share the impact of national service with a broad audience.

title: Minnesota Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Ignite Afterschool which coordinates the Minnesota Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will: 1) launch streamlined accreditation processes for school-age care programs and establish uniform quality standards in youth programming across Minnesota; 2) implement uniform quality professional development linked to statewide standards which will be updated annually with provider feedback and improved data collection; 3) work with policymakers to design and implement education recovery funding to help Minnesota youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen by Mott.

title: New Mexico Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Center of Southwest Culture which coordinates the New Mexico Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will: 1) create a sustainable structure of statewide, regional and local partnerships to support the development and growth of statewide policies to secure resources needed to sustain new and existing school-based or school-linked out-of-school time programs; 2) support continuous quality improvement through statewide professional development, training, information dissemination and events; 3) work with policymakers to design and implement education recovery funding to help New Mexico youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen by Mott.

title: Alaska Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Alaska Children’s Trust which coordinates the Alaska Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will: 1) create a staffing ecosystem in Alaska that fosters growth of the afterschool field and supports high-quality program delivery to youth; 2) improve statewide program quality and delivery through adoption of standardized best practices for providers and the network; 3) work with policymakers to design and implement education recovery funding to help Alaska youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen by Mott.

title: New Jersey Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the New Jersey School-Age Care Coalition which coordinates the New Jersey Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will: 1) embed a focus on equity into afterschool systems in New Jersey; 2) establish a statewide Youth Advisory Committee to help develop future afterschool programs; 3) work with policymakers to design and implement education recovery funding to help New Jersey youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen by Mott.

title: Research Project: Creating an Enabling Environment for Community Paralegals in Africa
description: The project goal is to generate knowledge and evidence on the impact of community paralegals in addressing injustices in Africa. To this end, the University of the Western Cape has collaborated with the African Centre of Excellence on Access to Justice by providing research support to document the work of community paralegals. Continued support will allow the grantee to increase its reach on the work of community paralegals in three Francophone African countries. The grantee will also collaborate to build an informative online platform to document community paralegal infrastructure in Africa.

title: Education and Economic Development Initiatives
description: This renewal grant provides partial support for the Genesee Area Focus Fund and its supported organization, the Flint & Genesee Chamber of Commerce, to deliver economic development and education and training services to the Flint area and build Flint’s economic resilience to recover from the Flint water crisis and COVID-19 pandemic. The Chamber increases business investment, job creation and industry diversification through business retention, expansion and attraction activities, as well as entrepreneurial support services. The Chamber also enhances the region’s economic competitiveness and quality of life by providing workforce education and training programming across all age levels, and by engaging in special initiative projects with strategic partners.

title: Advancing Entrepreneurship Education
description: This grant increase will provide additional funds to the Young Entrepreneur Institute at University School located in Huntington Valley, Ohio. Dollars will be used to support programming and travel costs for the 11 Statewide Afterschool Networks that received Opportunity Grants to work on youth entrepreneurship. In addition, increased funding will support additional capacity for Young Entrepreneur Institute to continue serving the needs of the network.

title: European Community Foundation Initiative
description: The project goal is to develop the community foundation field and strengthen infrastructure for community foundations in Europe. In collaboration with European community philanthropy support organizations, Bundesverband Deutscher Stiftungen will manage the European Community Foundation Initiative. Working with its partners, the grantee will strengthen the capacity of existing community foundations and their associations, promote the community foundation concept and facilitate the establishment of new community foundations, and strengthen the visibility and representation of community foundations vis-à-vis the public sector on the national and European levels. This grant increase will enable the grantee to strengthen its work on engaging foundations in addressing the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals on the local level. To this end, the grantee will increase the understanding of the global goals and their relevance to the work of European community foundations and strengthen the skills of community foundations to utilize the global goals’ framework in their programming.

title: Developing Community Foundations in Colombia
description: The project goal is to develop community foundations in Colombia. To this end, Evaluar Consultores S.A.S will increase the knowledge and understanding of key stakeholders about community foundations and their practice in different regions in the world, generate interest in the community foundation concept in Colombia, pilot local resource mobilization events, and develop a long-term strategy for community foundation development in Colombia. The grantee will carry out these activities in an inclusive, participatory manner and build collaborative relationships with key stakeholders for the development of a community foundation movement in Colombia. The grantee is a small, private company providing consultancy services to companies, public institutions, nonprofit organizations, and international development agencies in Colombia, since its establishment in the 1980’s. Over the years, the grantee has gained deep knowledge and understanding of the context in Colombia from the grassroots in nearly every geographic region up to the national level. The grantee provides technical assistance, networking opportunities, facilitation, mentoring, and training to its clients throughout Colombia and the region. Since the beginning of 2019, and with Mott support through a Foundation Administered Project, the grantee has been working on promoting the concept and practice of community foundations in Colombia.

title: Developing Community Foundations in Peru
description: The project goal is to develop community foundations in Peru. To this end, Mosaico Laboratorio Creativo will increase the knowledge and understanding of key stakeholders about community foundations and their practice in different regions of the world, adapt the concept of community foundations to the Peruvian context, and develop a long-term strategy for community foundation development in Peru. The grantee was established in 2017 by a group of young professionals with the mission to strengthen initiatives and organizations working in the social, educational, cultural, and artistic fields and motivate citizens to work collaboratively in favor of those most in need. The grantee advances its mission by creating spaces and experiences that increase trust and foster solidarity among people and institutions. The grantee’s key services include workshops and retreats for young civic leaders and social entrepreneurs to discover and develop authentic purpose in life and work; consultancy and mentoring for projects and initiatives in the private, public, and nonprofit sectors to maximize their scale, sustainability, and impact; and facilitation of networks, platforms, and ecosystems to strengthen creativity and innovation in communities and the society in Peru. Mosaico Laboratorio Creativo is based in Lima, Peru.

title: Virginia Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support James Madison University which coordinates the Virginia Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people.
