Specific initiatives will: 1) establish regional networks in eight communities across the state to promote comprehensive afterschool and summer learning programs; 2) enhance youth outcomes by integrating afterschool data from programs and schools; 3) work with policymakers to design and implement education recovery funding to help Virginia youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen by Mott.

title: Kentucky Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Save the Children Federation which coordinates the Kentucky Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will: 1) cultivate a network of afterschool ambassadors serving as experts and champions on the value of afterschool in communities across Kentucky; 2) further establish the network as a hub of training and resources for providers and programs to implement high quality, responsive programming; 3) work with policymakers to design and implement education recovery funding to help Kentucky youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen by Mott.

title: Louisiana Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Louisiana Tech University to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will: 1) expand statewide policy and diversify funding for afterschool programs through increased outreach and advocacy efforts as well as the collection and distribution of data, research and resources; 2) strengthen coordinated afterschool efforts by cultivating new and existing partnerships and increase statewide stakeholder awareness and engagement; 3) build a continuous quality improvement system with tools, resources, and support to strengthen quality programs, improve staff competencies and create positive youth outcomes; 4) build a STEM ecosystem with tools, resources and supports that strengthen STEM out-of-school time programs and create positive youth outcomes, especially for girls and youth of color; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen by Mott.

title: North Dakota Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the South East Education Cooperative which coordinates the North Dakota Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will: 1) support the development and growth of policies that will secure the resources needed to sustain new and existing out-of-school time programs; 2) use momentum from the Network’s Quality Workgroup to continue making positive strides in advancing quality of school-age afterschool and summer learning programs across the state; 3) work with policymakers to design and implement education recovery funding to help North Dakota youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen by Mott.

title: Delaware Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the United Way of Delaware which coordinates the Delaware Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will: 1) support youth in eight communities by launching a comprehensive afterschool quality initiative; 2) enhance youth outcomes by integrating afterschool data from programs and schools; 3) work with policymakers to design and implement education recovery funding to help Delaware youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen by Mott.

title: Afterschool Support
location: Port St. Lucie, FL, United States
description: The Women of Zion Outreach Ministry provides an afterschool program for children in its community. The program offers children a safe place to be after school where they are surrounded by caring adults who help with homework, teach computer skills, provide mentoring and character development lessons, and offer a variety of enrichment activities.

title: Pennsylvania Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Central Susquehanna Intermediate Unit which coordinates the Pennsylvania Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will: 1) join more than 20 other states in establishing a dedicated and reliable funding stream for out-of-school time programs; 2) share resources and best practices on how program developers and providers can develop and sustain strong partnerships with community-based organizations, businesses and school districts; 3) work with policymakers to design and implement education recovery funding to help Pennsylvania youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen by Mott.

title: Georgia Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Voices for Georgia’s Children which coordinates the Georgia Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives include efforts to: 1) increase the utilization of youth development quality standards; 2) connect afterschool and summer learning to other education and youth development issues, such as children’s behavioral health programming; 3) incorporate afterschool and summer learning policy priorities at the federal, state and local levels; 4) educate and engage communities, business leaders and other stakeholders around the importance of afterschool and summer programming for young people; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen by Mott.

title: Access to Justice in Remote Areas of Sierra Leone
description: The Legal Aid Board–Sierra Leone was established in 2015 by the country’s Legal Aid Act. The main purpose of the board is to provide justice services to poor and marginalized people in Sierra Leone, who otherwise cannot afford legal services. Past support allowed the grantee to extend its justice services to two districts in Sierra Leone’s most rural regions, which are generally hard to reach. The grantee also participated in drafting Sierra Leone’s Voluntary National Review on the implementation of the Sustainable Development Goals. This grant will allow the Legal Aid Board–Sierra Leone to continue its rural justice services and ensure justice for those who need it most in Sierra Leone.

title: Access to Justice in Remote Areas of Sierra Leone
description: The project goal is to increase access to justice for poor and marginalized people in Sierra Leone. To this end, the Legal Aid Board of Sierra Leone — established in 2015, by the country’s Legal Aid Act — will continue to provide justice services to people in remote rural locations that are hard to reach. The grantee will also continue with its outreach and training activities, including its support to community advice bureaus. Past support has helped the grantee to increase its footprint from 16 to 23 regional offices and reach 370,340 people with community outreach and legal services. The main purpose of the Legal Aid Board of Sierra Leone is to provide justice services to poor and marginalized people in Sierra Leone, who otherwise cannot afford legal services.

title: General Purposes
description: The Ohio Environmental Council is a comprehensive, effective and respected environmental advocate for a healthier, more sustainable Ohio. With a Mott Foundation general purposes grant, the grantee will address four priority issues with related program teams — energy, water, land and democracy — to fulfill their overarching mission of a clean, beautiful Ohio where diverse people, innovation and natural treasures thrive. With previous support from Mott, the grantee has focused on the work of its water team, tackling invasive species, toxic algae and chemical contaminants that threaten Ohio’s waterways and drinking water with a commitment to justice, equity, diversity and inclusion. This water policy work will also continue under this new general support grant.

title: Mobile Mental Health Unit Project
description: This grant will provide support to Genesee Health System for a mental health mobile clinic in Flint. The mobile clinic staff will provide mental and behavioral health services, education on available resources and referrals to other programs for adults and children impacted by the trauma and stress of the Flint water crisis and the pandemic. Services will be offered virtually and at a variety of locations throughout the community including events, neighborhood centers, schools and other locations where residents gather.

title: Riverfront Event Center Improvements
description: The University of Michigan-Flint is an anchor institution in downtown Flint. In that role, it provides both educational and economic benefit to the broader community. The Riverfront Residence Hall and Event Center is the only conference space in the city of Flint large enough to host regional and national conferences and seminars, but the movable wall that allows that space to be reconfigured for various events is inoperable. Grant support will replace the wall and allow the grantee to fully realize the educational and economic benefits of the conference center facility.

title: African Centre of Excellence for Access to Justice Project
description: The project goal is to strengthen the African Centre of Excellence for Access to Justice to promote a learning and sharing agenda. To this end, the Paralegal Advisory Service Institute will continue to host and coordinate the activities of the African Centre of Excellence for Access to Justice. Past support has allowed the grantee to increase the center’s membership to 14 members in 13 African countries, strengthen partnerships with global institutions, collaborate with others to publish research findings on community paralegal infrastructure, co-organize convenings to discuss research findings and attend sessions of the African Commission on Human and Peoples Rights. The grantee will continue to implement initiatives to ensure the recognition and financing of community paralegals in Africa and strengthen its resources, offerings and other benefits to its members across the continent. The Paralegal Advisory Service Institute is one of the leading community justice organizations in Africa.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Catholic Commission for Justice and Peace of the Archdiocese of Lilongwe
description: The Catholic Commission for Justice and Peace of the Archdiocese of Lilongwe was founded in 1992 with the primary objective of consolidating democratic and human rights gains. The grantee has since become a key stakeholder in ensuring that Malawians enjoy their rights and access justice. Past project support allowed the grantee to scale its access to justice work, through providing justice services to vulnerable groups in the Nkhotakota region of Malawi. This grant will assist the grantee to provide civil justice services and conduct oversight over the judicial system in Malawi to ensure that it is just and fair.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Catholic Commission for Justice and Peace of the Archdiocese of Lilongwe
description: This grant will support increased access to justice for poor and marginalized people in Malawi. To this end, the Catholic Commission for Justice and Peace of the Archdiocese of Lilongwe will continue to implement primary and informal justice work in the central region of Malawi. The grantee’s activities will include providing justice services through its network of community paralegals, training of paralegals, documenting the work of community paralegals, networking and learning from Malawian and other African organizations doing similar work. Past support has allowed the grantee to train 384 paralegals in 17 districts in Malawi. Community paralegals mediated over 400 cases and made referrals to various other organizations. Founded in 1992, the Catholic Commission for Justice and Peace of the Archdiocese of Lilongwe is a well-established and credible organization working towards peace and justice in Malawi.

title: Free City Mural Festival
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will support the Free City Mural Festival to install 15 murals in south Flint including along the South Saginaw corridor. The Flint Public Art Project is working with residents, the Southside Business Association, and the City of Flint to identify suitable locations for the works of art and has attracted local, national, and international artists to produce the murals. A community festival to celebrate this project will take place along South Saginaw Street in mid-October.

title: Music Education Program
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will support the construction and equipment for a music studio at Sylvester Broome Empowerment Village. The community center located on the north side of Flint serves approximately 300 young people through a variety of academic, athletic and arts programs every day. The music studio will offer classes and other opportunities primarily to young people ages 13-18, but will also be a resource to others in the community.

title: Health and Environmental Funders Network
description: This grant supports Virginia Organizing for its project, the Health and Environmental Funders Network. The Health and Environmental Funders Network is a group of funders and donors whose mission is mobilizing philanthropy around environmental health and justice solutions. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the Network has helped address environmental challenges and expanded its understanding of the connections between public health and a clean, healthy environment. Continued support will enable the Network to mobilize resources on critical environmental health and justice issues, including a new emphasis on lead exposure and emerging water contaminants.

title: Energy and Infrastructure Development in the Amazon
description: The Instituto Centro de Vida is a Brazilian civil society organization that serves as the secretariat of the Brazilian Infrastructure Working Group and works with communities impacted by large hydroelectric development in Amazon rivers. Over the project period, the grantee has organized webinars and regular Infrastructure Working Group convenings and monitored the social and environmental impacts of the Teles Pires and Sao Manoel hydroelectric plants. This grant increase will support the grantee to consolidate the infrastructure working group and prepare the second conference on infrastructure finance in the Brazilian Amazon.

title: Housing and Food Assistance
description: Shelter of Flint provides services for approximately 1,000 people each day. Most of these clients are families who are economically challenged. The principal goal of the grantee is to assist the homeless in achieving stability through a continuum of care model ranging from crisis prevention and counseling to elimination of the root causes of homelessness. This grant will help support services for families through the grantee’s One Stop Housing Resource Center program and the Emergency Shelter program. Individuals and families will receive food assistance as well as comprehensive case management services and the development of long-range plans toward permanent stability.

title: Rent and Utility Assistance Program
description: Since 1893, the Salvation Army of Genesee County has worked to alleviate hardships faced by Genesee County residents. This grant will support the grantee’s financial assistance services administered through the Comprehensive Emergency Assistance program. The goal is to help the Salvation Army better meet household demand for utility shutoffs, eviction, and foreclosure assistance.

title: Facility Upgrades
description: The purpose of this grant is to provide Whaley Children’s Center with essential facility upgrades that will directly affect the children who live there. The grantee is a residential treatment facility for children ages 5-17 who have lived in various foster homes and have experienced some sort of trauma. There are a variety of programs and strategies offered that allow staff to build a comprehensive treatment plan for each individual child based on their specific needs. This is the only facility of its kind in Genesee County, making it an invaluable asset to the community and the children who need it most.

title: Increasing Food Distribution and Access
description: This grant will aid in the distribution of fresh and healthy food in Genesee County. The Food Bank of Eastern Michigan provides healthy, nutritious food to the most vulnerable community members through its partnerships with more than 200 agencies in the city of Flint. To meet this need, safe and reliable equipment is essential in the distribution of food. This grant will also supply nine Flint agencies with coolers and freezers to increase its capacity to store and distribute more fresh and frozen produce.

title: General Purposes
description: Founded in 1997, the National Center for Family Philanthropy is the only national nonprofit dedicated exclusively to families who give and those who work with them. The center provides resources, expertise, and support to families in order to transform their values into effective giving that makes a lasting impact on the communities they serve. The grantee’s five-year goal is to provide resources, expertise, and direct support and guidance to more than 5,000 families engaged in philanthropy and indirect support to an additional 10,000 families. A grant increase will help support the transition of the grantee’s founding president to the role of senior fellow where she will oversee a fellowship program and focus on research, writing, and developing intellectual property for the center.

title: Education Scenario Analysis
description: With this grant, the Education Trust will conduct a series of conversations with leaders in the education field who can help inform the thinking about how to assist struggling and distressed school districts. These experts will explore the critical issues of school choice, school funding, and educator talent, all of which have direct and important implications for school districts and student outcomes.

title: Unified Enrollment System
description: With this grant, the Community Foundation of Greater Flint will lead the implementation of a unified enrollment system to better serve families and early childhood education providers in Flint. The project will increase the efficiency and transparency of early learning opportunities across the city.

title: Early Childhood Education Research
description: With this grant, the Community Foundation of Greater Flint will support a multiyear evaluation of early childhood education efforts in Flint. The evaluation will first focus on the impact of high-quality practices at the Educare Flint and Cummings Great Expectations centers and then measure the impact that high-quality hubs can have on the early childhood education ecosystem across the city.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will allow Philanthropy Puerto Rico to continue its mission to strengthen philanthropy and the nonprofit sector in Puerto Rico. A current high priority for the grantee is to improve and expand Puerto Rico’s philanthropy infrastructure as the commonwealth continues its recovery efforts following Hurricanes Irma and Maria. During this grant period, the grantee will continue to support collaborative efforts among foundations and community-based organizations, enhance the capacity of community-based organizations, advocate for policy alternatives to promote the resilience of organizations serving vulnerable groups, and engage more philanthropic actors in effective responses to Puerto Rico’s recovery. Through this increase, the grantee will strengthen their advocacy work, create a foundation database, and have new issue-based gatherings. Established in 2009 by seven leading foundations, the grantee exists to enhance the ability of philanthropy and nonprofit organizations to improve the lives of vulnerable populations.

title: Community Water Lab
description: This grant will support the operations of the Community Water Lab at the Flint Development Center. The grantee, Evergreen Community Development Initiative, operates the Flint Development Center which is located in a former Flint Community School elementary building. The Community Water Lab will be equipped with state-of-the-art technology. Scientists and staff of the lab will work with residents to collect water samples, test for multiple contaminants, provide results and work with households to address any identified issues.

title: Entrepreneurship Network
description: This grant will support the launch of the Entrepreneurship Network at Mott Community College. The goal is to support students interested in entrepreneurship through a coordinated network of supports, resources, knowledge, and technology. The Entrepreneurship Network will help expand programming and assist the grantee in creating an environment that encourages students to further develop their innovative ideas. Supporting entrepreneurship is a way to bring economic opportunity and prosperity to Flint.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Hague Institute for Innovation of Law
description: The program goal is to advance efforts to increase people-centered access to justice. The Hague Institute for Innovation of Law will work through three main avenues to identify new ways of addressing people’s justice needs. Through justice needs surveys and other research, the grantee will: 1) produce informative and actionable data; 2) support ongoing justice innovations to support scalable models of service delivery on justice issues; and 3) support transformative efforts of various jurisdictions to help recast justice system processes and procedures. In 2019-20 the grantee completed three extensive justice needs surveys in Morocco, Mali and Fiji. In addition, the grantee supported nearly 50 justice entrepreneurs in the development of accessible and affordable justice innovations and produced a benchmark report identifying the cost-effectiveness of people-centered justice reforms. Established in 2005, the Hague Institute for Innovation of Law seeks to find innovative solutions to justice problems around the world.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Hague Institute for Innovation of Law
description: The Hague Institute for Innovation of Law will work through five core competencies to advance people-centered justice. This includes gathering robust data, applying evidence-based practice, scaling effective community justice services, creating enabling environments to engage broad constituencies in justice practices, and strengthening learning across networks of people-centered justice practitioners and policymakers. The grantee will do so initially in selected countries including Ethiopia, the Netherlands, Niger, Tunisia and Uganda, with an intention to add Kenya and Ukraine in the future. In 2021-22, the grantee completed four extensive justice needs surveys in Burkina Faso, Niger, Uganda and the United States. Despite the challenges of the COVID-19 pandemic, the grantee also assisted 16 justice innovators to make significant progress in scaling their innovative services and practices. Established in 2005, the Hague Institute for Innovation of Law seeks to find innovative solutions to justice problems around the world.

title: TAP Network
description: The program goal is to support organized civil society participation to increase access to justice globally. The Transparency, Accountability, and Participation Network, a project of the Proteus Fund, will mobilize its membership of over 270 civil society organizations for coordinated action around implementation of Sustainable Development Goal 16, with its focus on peaceful, just and inclusive societies. During the grant period, work will focus on: 1) strengthening civil society influence in accountability processes; 2) building civil society capacity to evaluate Goal 16 implementation; and 3) improving data collection and monitoring of national government commitments to Goal 16. In 2020-21, the grantee produced a series of critical resources for civil society actors working to support Goal 16. These equipped network members to better track mechanisms and measures in place which underpin Goal 16 implementation. The grantee also hosted a series of events linked to United Nations review meetings, bringing civil society perspectives to these discussions. Founded in 1994, the Proteus Fund convenes and facilitates donor collaboratives that strategically focus philanthropic resources toward the realization of a just, equitable and democratic world.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support the After-School All-Stars to continue to drive quality afterschool programming across the country. The mission of the grantee is to provide comprehensive afterschool programs that keep children safe and help them succeed in school and life. This grant will help the After-School All-Stars to support its chapters in ensuring high-quality programming, expanding program reach, improving staff retention, increasing sustainability, and educating key champions.

title: Nevada Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support University of Nevada, Las Vegas which coordinates the Nevada Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will: 1) strengthen the networks’ outreach through the development of an ambassador program with an emphasis on youth voice; 2) increase program quality across the state through the creation of an online hub for program self-assessment, professional development tools and communication strategies; 3) work with policymakers to design and implement education recovery funding to help Nevada youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen by Mott.

title: Michigan Works! Network Scan
description: This grant will support a research study of the Michigan Works! network to learn about its programming and best practices. Public Policy Associates, Inc., a national public policy research, development, and evaluation firm headquartered in Lansing, Michigan will conduct the external analysis. A final report will provide leaders in Michigan with the insights needed to identify opportunities to support and enhance Michigan Works! programs that seek to address the middle-skill jobs gap and the needs of hard-to-serve people searching for employment.

title: Michigan Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Michigan Association of United Ways which coordinates the Michigan Statewide Afterschool Network to continue the development of policy, partnerships and resources to benefit youth in afterschool programs. Specific initiatives will include: 1) increasing the reach and scope of Out-of-School Time program system-building efforts at a state and grassroots level; 2) expanding professional development and data-driven practices to promote a culture of continuous improvement to support a skilled Out-of-Time workforce; 3) building strategic partnerships with stakeholders to map resources and plan program expansion through new and existing funding streams; and 4) supporting the promotion and distribution of the Mizzen by Mott App.

title: Michigan Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Michigan Association of United Ways which coordinates the Michigan Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will: 1) develop a youth engagement and empowerment initiative that centers youth in the values and practices of afterschool across the state; 2) continue building data collection and evaluation practices to increase quality afterschool programs; 3) identify opportunities to remove barriers for afterschool and unify providers in strategic communications; 4) work with policymakers to design and implement education recovery funding to help Michigan youth recover and thrive; 5) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 6) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen by Mott.

title: Creating Access to Justice Fund
description: Peregrine Environmental Consultants, a public interest consultancy, was established to address environmental and social standards of the international development finance institutions, particularly the World Bank Group. The World Bank Group continues to finance projects that either do not provide the promised benefits to local communities or results in disproportionate harm to local communities—thus failing in the bank’s fundamental development mission. This project will establish a multi-stakeholder process to catalyze the creation of Access to Justice and Remedy fund(s) that would assist project-affected communities in their efforts to engage with, and address the impacts of, World Bank Group projects.

title: Global Investigative Journalism Conference Fellowship Program
description: This grant will cover the costs of a one-year fellowship for a Brazilian journalist with the Global Investigative Journalism Network, including attendance at the Global Investigative Journalism conference in 2019. The grantee was founded in 2003 and serves as an international hub for journalists, with 182 member organizations in 78 countries, and daily news feeds in eight languages.

title: Maintenance of City Parks
description: This grant will provide funding for the City of Flint to contract with Genesee County Parks for the maintenance of six parks around the city and ten park properties along the Flint River. City parks provide recreational green space for residents and are utilized for a variety of activities. This grant will ensure current maintenance levels in these parks continue.

title: Security System Upgrades
description: This grant will support internal and external security system upgrades at the Sylvester Broome Empowerment Village community center. The grantee has a growing number of offerings for young people and families including several programs in the visual and performing arts. The community center serves approximately 300 school-aged children each day many of whom live in the surrounding neighborhoods on the north side of Flint.

title: Building Renovations
description: This grant will provide funding to the Greater Flint Health Coalition for the redevelopment of the 120 West First Street building, located in downtown Flint. The renovated facility will serve as a central location for the grantee’s staff and programs that support the health and well-being of residents in Flint and Genesee County.

title: Advocacy Center Expansion
description: Voices for Children Advocacy Center is an accredited advocacy agency whose programs include forensic interviews, multidisciplinary team and case reviews, on-site medical exams, referrals to mental health evaluation, the Court Appointed Special Advocates program, and prevention services. This grant will support the expansion of their program and administrative offices which will allow them more room to serve more children.

title: General Purposes
description: The Casual Workers Advice Office was established in 2011 to give free legal advice to workers who have been dismissed, or face other labor violations by their employers in South Africa. Past and existing support assisted the Casual Workers Advice Office to: 1) raise awareness of new labor rights among precarious workers and support them in accessing these rights; 2) support workers whose disputes have been referred to the Commission for Conciliation, Mediation, and Arbitration and other bargaining councils; 3) produce resources and general educational materials; and 4) hire additional staff and train existing staff. This increase will assist the grantee to restore its offices, after it was looted and burned by xenophobic violence happening in Johannesburg.

title: Sports Equipment Infusion
description: With this grant, the Crim Fitness Foundation will purchase and maintain sports and recreation equipment for use at the thirteen community education sites and at four community centers. The equipment will help increase access to and participation in physical fitness and recreational activities for children and adults across Flint.

title: Downtown Placemaking
description: This grant will help the Downtown Development Authority establish a placemaking project focused on programming public spaces. The grantee will hire a full-time director for the project and leverage additional resources to coordinate events for the community.

title: VISTA Project
description: This grant will support the Afterschool Alliance to partner with AmeriCorps VISTA to: 1) enhance the capacity of statewide afterschool networks; 2) increase utilization of the afterschool meals programs; 3) support STEM Learning opportunities within the afterschool field; 4) increase access to high-quality education, enrichment and mentoring opportunities for young people of color; and 5) support the statewide afterschool networks to provide child trauma-informed training and resources for afterschool program staff.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued support to Grantmakers for Education, a leading national association that works to advance the field of education philanthropy. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) sustain and improve overall programming and communications activities that help education grantmakers succeed in their work; and 2) provide staffing support and coordination to the Out-of-School Time impact group to increase access to high-quality out-of-school time experiences for young people.

title: Entrepreneurship Network
description: This grant will support the Entrepreneurship Network at Mott Community College. The goal is to support students interested in entrepreneurship through a coordinated network of support, resources, knowledge and technology. The network will help expand programming and assist the grantee in creating an environment that encourages students to further develop their innovative ideas. Supporting entrepreneurship is a way to bring economic opportunity and prosperity to Flint.

title: Strengthening the Legal Development Network's Member Organizations
description: The program goal is to increase community-based access to justice for the Ukrainian public. The Legal Development Network will work to strengthen and expand the current network of 30 community legal centers in Ukraine. Continuing attention will be given to equipping centers with skills and capacity to work with local authorities in providing access to justice. The grantee will also seek to integrate the network into international partnerships to further build capabilities of members. In 2019-2021, the grantee conducted 11 legal needs surveys in different regions of Ukraine, resulting in six access to justice programs in participating communities. Despite the COVID-19 pandemic, network members nearly doubled the number of clients served in 2020, compared to the previous year. Working with Ukrainian and international partners, the grantee also initiated widespread discussion on “people-centered justice” and how this can be achieved in Ukraine. Formally registered in 2015 and with its secretariat in Kyiv, the Legal Development Network has member organizations in 15 regions of Ukraine.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides funding to an organization whose goal is to increase community-based access to justice for the Ukrainian public. The Legal Development Network, a network of 22 organizations operating 30 community legal centers in Ukraine (as well as three outside of Ukraine since Russia’s illegal invasion) will work to strengthen the resilience and responsiveness of its members. Through mentoring of local partners, repeated engagements with local administrations, and building capacity of member organizations, the grantee will work to ensure high quality legal assistance for those in need despite the numerous challenges such assistance faces. In 2022-23, the grantee more than doubled the number of people to whom it offered legal assistance, despite — or because of — the invasion of Ukraine. Over 200,0000 people were supported with legal assistance and information at home, and a new service for supporting Ukrainians abroad was established, serving a similar number. Formally registered in 2015 and with its secretariat in Kyiv, the Legal Development Network has member organizations in 15 regions of Ukraine.

title: Michigan News and Information Programs
description: This grant provides funding to the University of Michigan – Ann Arbor’s Michigan Radio in support of its news and information service. Michigan Radio is a trusted media brand in the state, known for its fair and fact-based coverage of state, national, and international news. Michigan Radio reaches its audience with radio content, podcasts, websites, social media, and mobile apps, providing news and information to help create a more engaged public.

title: Launch Michigan
description: Launch Michigan, a project of the Council of Michigan Foundations, aims to seed critical policy and practice change that will accelerate improvement in the quality of education for Michigan students. The project is a collaborative effort driven by a steering committee consisting of representatives from the public, private, and philanthropic sectors. The effort is undertaken in the belief that improving the K-12 education system in Michigan is fundamental to the long-term prosperity of our state and is vital to every student and family in our community.

title: Helping Young People to Employment Program
description: This grant will support the Helping Young People to Employment Program. The program is managed by Faith Foundation Resources, a nonprofit dedicated to working with low-income and at-risk individuals to help better their lives. The goal of the project is to prepare young people ages 16-24 for work. Participants learn about job training and the skills needed to become productive and responsible members of society. Courses focus on job readiness, learning the fundamentals of interpersonal skills and financial literacy. After completion of an eight-week training program, participants are eligible to be placed into 20 to 30 hours of part-time employment. Metro Community Development, a long-time Foundation grantee, will serve as a fiduciary for Faith Foundation Resources.

title: Helping Young People to Employment Program
description: This grant will support the Helping Young People to Employment Program. The program is managed by Faith Foundation Resources, a nonprofit dedicated to working with low-income and at-risk individuals to help better their lives. The goal of the project is to prepare young people ages 16 to 24 for work. Participants learn about job training and the skills needed to become productive and responsible members of society. Courses focus on job readiness, learning the fundamentals of interpersonal skills and financial literacy. After completion of an eight-week training program, participants are eligible to be placed into 20 to 30 hours of part-time employment.

title: Berston Field House Capacity Building
description: This grant increase will assist the United Way of Genesee County and the Friends of Berston Field House to enhance security and improve on site access to healthy and nutritious foods. Friends of Berston Field House’s mission is to impact the community through education, athletics, arts, and comprehensive services.

title: Mexican Community Foundation Development
description: This grant will support the development of Mexican community foundations. The Inter-American Foundation manages a program that focuses on members of Comunalia, a network of Mexican community foundations. Over the next three years, the grantee will support the institutional strengthening of Comunalia and its members; manage a sub-grant challenge mechanism for community projects; and provide grants for applied research, donor engagement and education, and evaluation. This grant increase will support technical assistance and training for grassroots development and community philanthropy as well as a new challenge grant fund. The Inter-American Foundation is an independent United States government agency created by congress in 1969 to channel development assistance directly to the poor in Latin America and the Caribbean.

title: Building Broader Communities in the Americas
description: The project goal is to foster partnerships between community foundations and other organizations in North, Central, and South America. Project activities will include peer learning and convenings for community foundations and other organizations, presentations at conferences, regranting for community foundations to conduct mapping exercises, and a strategic planning process. The project will be managed by CFLeads, an organization that helps community foundations build strong communities by advancing effective practices, sharing knowledge, and galvanizing action on critical issues. The purpose of this increase is to enhance the grantee’s capacity to work on the Building Broader Communities in the Americas initiative through support for a project director, a strategic plan, and travel funds. Established in 1991 as the Coalition of Community Foundations for Youth under the Greater Kansas City Community Foundation, CFLeads became an independent nonprofit organization in 2017.

title: Community Foundation Development in Austria
description: The project goal is to develop community foundations in Austria. To this end, the Austrian National Foundations Association (Verband für gemeinnütziges Stiften) will launch a ten-year program to foster a strong and vibrant community foundation movement in Austria. Through this program, the grantee will develop 50 community foundations spread throughout all federal provinces and capable of effectively addressing multiple local challenges, including income inequality, migration and climate change. During the first two years, the grantee will focus on building the capacity of the project team, publicizing the community foundation concept and supporting the most promising local initiatives to develop community foundations. The Austrian National Foundations Association was established in 2014 with the mission to strengthen the charitable foundation sector in Austria and today it has over 100 members. The grantee’s past achievements include strengthening the capacity of its members and developing policy proposals for improving the legal and fiscal environment for philanthropy in Austria.

title: Community Foundation Development in Spain
description: The project goal is to develop community foundations in Spain. To this end, the Spanish Association of Foundations will launch a ten-year program to foster a strong and vibrant community foundation movement in Spain. Through this program, the grantee will develop at least 40 new community foundations, covering 50 percent of Spain’s territory; create a national network of Spanish community foundations; ensure that the community foundations adhere to internally developed quality standards; and encourage the Spanish community foundations to play a leadership role in addressing the Sustainable Development Goals on the local level. Additionally, the grantee will connect the Spanish community foundation movement internationally. During the first two years, the focus will be on building the capacity of the project team, publicizing the community foundation concept, and supporting the most promising local initiatives to develop community foundations.

title: Raising Awareness and Educating U.S. Community Foundations on the SDGs
description: The program goal is to encourage community foundations to advance the Sustainable Development Goals at the local level. To this end, the Kansas Association of Community Foundations will prominently include content on the Sustainable Development Goals and their adoption by community foundations at its annual national Growing Community Foundations Conference. This grant will support a panel of experts and community foundation practitioners at the conference’s opening plenary as well as another breakout session. The grantee will also add a module on the goals used by community foundations to their CFExpressTraining online resource. Founded in 2005, the Kansas Association of Community Foundations strengthens and promotes community philanthropy in Kansas, educates its members and others on effective philanthropic operations and fosters collaboration and the exchange of information regarding philanthropic programs and issues.

title: Youth Entrepreneurship Curriculum for Afterschool Programs
description: VentureLab will continue to provide capacity building and support for the Mott-funded 50 State Networks’ youth entrepreneurship work, as well as content on Mizzen by Mott. Since 2017, the grantee has provided training, technical assistance and professional development resources to the state afterschool networks, enabling the networks to increase the number of afterschool programs offering high-quality entrepreneurship education programming and has increased the number of youth who have opportunities to develop entrepreneurial skills and mindsets. Additionally, VentureLab will continue to develop and implement evaluation and data collection tools that measure and report the impact of entrepreneurial education on educators and students.

title: Cities Building Bridges to Postsecondary Success
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This renewal grant will enable the National League of Cities Institute to continue its efforts to increase the overall number and quality of children’s savings account programs in the United States by helping city leaders connect them to existing city and state initiatives that create stronger financial pathways to and through college and support families’ economic security. During this grant period, the grantee will continue to build and nurture efforts to grow new children’s savings account initiatives in the southeast region. Additionally, during this grant period, the grantee will amplify children’s savings accounts as part of the Mott Foundation’s overall communications strategy, by working with national partners to support cities and regional consortiums to strengthen their existing programs. Established in 1958 and located in Washington, D.C., the National League of Cities Institute is a research, education and training affiliate of the National League of Cities.

title: William S. White Fund for Innovation in Community Philanthropy
description: This grant supports the establishment of the William S. White Fund for Innovation in Community Philanthropy at the Council of Michigan Foundations. The permanently endowed fund will support an array of programs and initiatives, including possible fellowships, internships, research, pilot projects, study visits, consulting, awards, and other activities that will advance the knowledge and practice of community philanthropy. The fund will honor the legacy of William S. White, as a founder of the Council of Michigan Foundations and as a strong supporter of community foundations and community philanthropy. The grantee is a statewide association of over 300 grantmakers that provides its members with educational programs, technical assistance, networking opportunities, advocacy with policymakers and regulators, and collaboration with leading national and regional philanthropic associations.

title: Ariadne Network Membership
description: This grant supports the membership and administrative costs of Ariadne, a network of funders who work together to promote and protect civil society and human rights in Europe. Ariadne is a project of Global Dialogue, a nonprofit organization registered in the United Kingdom and based in London. The network has 139 member institutions in 21 countries. Key activities include the development of a working group on racial equity, support to Candid in the development of a GrantCraft Guide on climate justice, support to members to understand the impact of digital technology on civil society and continuing to co-convene a working group on women’s rights. Established in early 2009, Ariadne is a network of private funders who work together to strengthen philanthropy, help funders act strategically and encourage new donors to enter the field with maximum impact.

title: Ariadne Network Membership
description: This grant supports the membership and administrative costs of Ariadne, a network of funders who work together to promote and protect civil society and human rights in Europe. Ariadne is a project of Global Dialogue, a nonprofit organization registered in the United Kingdom and based in London. The network has 148 member institutions in 20 countries. Key activities included organizing more than 20 events online and offline, publishing a range of resources for funders, launching a mentoring program and convening members for the annual Grant Skills Week. Established in early 2009, Ariadne is a network of private funders who work together to strengthen philanthropy, help funders act strategically and encourage new donors to enter the field with maximum impact.

title: International Fellows Program on Community Philanthropy
grantee: Research Foundation of the City University of New York
description: The Research Foundation of the City University of New York provides oversight of the management of funds obtained by faculty. The Centre on Philanthropy and Civil Society manages the International Fellows Program on Community Philanthropy within the grantee’s Graduate Center. The program provides an opportunity for practitioners from around the world to learn about community foundations and the community philanthropy field. Emerging leaders and senior fellows participate in an intensive program of research, seminars and mentoring. Recently, the program hosted affinity groups led by the program’s alumni on specific topics that are identified by the fellows. Thus far, 236 individuals from 70 countries have benefited from the program. The program has contributed to the creation of organizations and other philanthropy-related ventures in countries such as Egypt, Nepal, Singapore, Italy, Russia and Indonesia.

title: International Fellows Program on Community Philanthropy
grantee: Research Foundation of the City University of New York
description: The Research Foundation of the City University of New York provides oversight of the management of funds obtained by faculty. The Center on Philanthropy and Civil Society manages the International Fellows Program on Community Philanthropy within the grantee’s Graduate Center. The program provides an opportunity for practitioners from around the world to learn about community foundations and the community philanthropy field. Emerging leaders and senior fellows participate in an intensive program of research, seminars and mentoring. Recently, the program hosted affinity groups led by the program’s alumni on specific topics that are identified by the fellows. Between the program’s inception in 1989 through 2023, 257 individuals from 74 countries will have benefited from the program. The program has contributed to the creation of various philanthropy-related ventures in countries such as Egypt, Nepal, Singapore, Italy, South Africa, Poland and India.

title: International Fellows Program on Community Philanthropy
grantee: Research Foundation of the City University of New York
description: The Research Foundation of the City University of New York provides oversight of the management of funds obtained by faculty. The Center on Philanthropy and Civil Society manages the International Fellows Program on Community Philanthropy within the university’s graduate center. The program provides an opportunity for practitioners from around the world to learn about community foundations through an intensive program of research, seminars and mentoring. Between the program’s inception, in 1989, through 2025, 273 individuals from 75 countries will have benefited and the program has contributed to the creation of various philanthropy-related ventures in countries such as Brazil, Nepal, Ukraine, Turkey, Zimbabwe, Indonesia and Ghana. Over the next two years, the Research Foundation of the City University of New York will test the feasibility of working with philanthropic research centers in Africa and Latin America to cohost and run these programs with the aim of ultimately transitioning such programming to institutions in the Global South.

title: Broadening Cross-Cultural Participation and Diversity in Great Lakes Advocacy
description: With partial support from the Mott Foundation this project features an environmental fellows program that places graduate students in environmental organizations and foundations across the United States. The program fills a vital need to build a pipeline of future leaders from previously under-represented racial, ethnic and social classes. Historically, research shows that people of color are not well represented in environmental organizations, including those in the Great Lakes region. With renewed support to the project, now housed at Yale University, three such fellows will be placed in Great Lakes organizations each year out of a nation-wide class of 30 fellows. All of the fellows will be supported with training and mentoring. In addition to the fellowship program itself, the project includes a national convening for the fellows and a robust national research agenda.

title: Bachelor of Paralegal Studies and Community Based Paralegals
description: The project goal is to increase the knowledge and capacity of community paralegals in South Africa. To this end, the Cape Peninsula University of Technology will continue to offer its bachelor’s degree in paralegal studies to selected community paralegals. Past support allowed the grantee to undertake a national study on the existing qualifications of community paralegals with a view to recognize the qualifications. The grantee also undertook preparations to ensure that community paralegals would successfully complete this degree. These included developing a mixed model of learning pedagogy, developing materials and facilitating staff workshops to help understand the nature and circumstances of community paralegals. Ongoing support will assist community paralegals from across South Africa to access the blended model of learning to obtain this qualification. The Cape Peninsula University of Technology is the largest technical university in the Western Cape Province of South Africa.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Kituo Cha Sheria Legal Advice Centre
description: The project goal is to increase access to justice for poor and marginalized people in Kenya. To this end, Kituo Cha Sheria Legal Advice Centre will undertake activities to address the structural barriers in accessing the formal and informal justice systems. The grantee will work with indigent communities, civil society organizations, paralegals, and marginalized populations to increase access to justice for all people in Kenya. The grantee is a nongovernmental organization, established in 1973 to empower poor and marginalized communities to gain access to justice. Kituo Cha Sheria Legal Advice Centre is the oldest organization to provide legal aid and empowerment programs in Kenya.

title: General Purposes
description: The project goal is to increase access to justice for poor and marginalized people in Kenya. To this end, the Legal Resources Foundation Trust will provide access to justice, using a legal empowerment approach in selected locations in Kenya. Working in partnership with community justice institutions and the Kenyan Paralegal Support Network, the grantee will provide justice services to address day-to-day problems and systemic injustices faced by poor and marginalized communities. The Legal Resources Foundation Trust is an independent human rights organization that promotes access to justice through human rights education, research and advocacy initiatives.

title: Promotion of Paralegalism
grantee: International Commission of Jurists - Kenya Section
description: The project goal is to increase access to justice for poor and marginalized communities in Kenya. To this end, the International Commission of Jurists–Kenya Section will provide justice services through a network of paralegals to poor and marginalized people in Kenya. The grantee will also assess the structural barriers in accessing justice in Kenya and propose recommendations on how to overcome these barriers. The grantee is an autonomous national nonprofit institution established in 1959. The International Commission of Jurists – Kenya Section’s vision is that Kenya has a just, free and equitable society and its mission is to protect human rights and promote the rule of law, justice and democracy in Kenya and across Africa.

title: Strengthen Community Justice in Rural Malawi
grantee: Centre for Human Rights Education Advice and Assistance
description: The project goal is to increase access to justice for poor and marginalized people in Malawi. To this end, the Centre for Human Rights Education Advice and Assistance will provide community justice services in Chikwawa and Mwanza districts of Malawi. The grantee will empower the users of both formal and informal systems to know and claim their rights and demand accountability from the justice system. It will also bridge the gap between the formal and informal justice systems. The grantee is an independent nonprofit trust that provides justice services and strategic litigation and undertakes advocacy in helping Malawians access justice.

title: Developing Community Foundations in Colombia
description: Since 2019 Evaluar Consultores has laid the groundwork for a long-term program to support community foundation development in Colombia. Activities under the previous grant period include conducting a landscape assessment, testing the concept with various stakeholders, participating in learning events with experienced community foundation development practitioners from other countries, developing a guidebook for legal and tax considerations, setting up a library of Spanish-language materials on community philanthropy and preparing a report on challenges and opportunities. Over 2021-2022, the grantee will elaborate and implement a five-year strategic plan to promote community foundation development in Colombia. Planned activities will include propagating the concept, providing training and technical assistance, supporting ten initiative groups, facilitating the creation of at least two community foundations and establishing a community foundation support organization as a nonprofit entity. Founded in 1986, Evaluar Consultores is a small, private company providing consultancy services to businesses, public institutions, nonprofit organizations and international development agencies in Colombia.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support community foundation development in Colombia. Established in 2022, TerritoriA is an independent nonprofit founded specifically to continue the community foundation development work. The grantee’s planned activities over the next two years include; 1) further propagating the concept; 2) generating knowledge about community philanthropy; 3) providing training and technical assistance; 4) supporting at least 10 new initiative groups; 5) facilitating the creation of at least three new community foundations; and 6) developing and implementing a sustainability strategy. With Mott Foundation support, the grantee will continue to support the community foundation concept in Columbia. Previous support from the Mott Foundation to the organization Evaluar Consultores has expanded the community foundation concept with various Colombian stakeholders throughout the region.

title: Developing Community Foundations in Peru
description: The project goal is to develop community foundations in Peru. Over the past year, Mosaico Laboratorio Creativo researched the potential for community foundation development in Peru and introduced the concept to 141 social sector practitioners and philanthropic leaders. The grantee published two online learning materials, engaged seven initiative groups, piloted a local resource mobilization event and articulated a three-year strategy for developing community foundations in Peru. Over the next two years, the grantee will continue to popularize the community foundation concept, design and administer a community foundation start-up program for up to twelve initiative groups and support the creation of three registered community foundations with technical assistance and matching grants. Based in Lima, Peru, Mosaico Laboratorio Creativo was established in 2017 by a group of young professionals with the mission to strengthen initiatives and organizations working in the social, educational, cultural and artistic fields to motivate citizens to work collaboratively in favor of those most in need.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support community foundation development in Colombia. Established in 2022, TerritoriA is an independent nonprofit founded specifically to foster the development of community foundations and community philanthropy. Results over the past two years include establishing four new Colombian community foundations, forming five initiative groups to create new community foundations, creating ten knowledge products and raising and managing additional funds to support community foundations in Colombia. Over 2025-2026, TerritoriA’s work will be directed toward achieving the following outcomes: 1) at least five new community foundations in Colombia; 2) another five initiative groups in the process of formation as community foundations; 3) ten multi-sector alliances to promote community philanthropy in Colombia; 4) a national mapping of at least 400 community philanthropy actors; 5) participation in at least ten local, national and international civil society learning spaces; and 6) enhancing the sustainability of Colombian community foundations as well as TerritoriA itself.

title: Developing Community Foundations in Peru
description: The project goal is to develop community foundations in Peru. Over the past three years, Mosaico Laboratorio Creativo introduced the community foundation concept to 600 social sector practitioners, developed relationships with 17 potential funding allies and worked with initiative groups in seven communities. The grantee also published the guide “Community Foundation Movement in Peru.” Over the next two years, the grantee will expand and consolidate the movement of community foundations in Peru, anticipating the formalization of at least four additional community foundations. The grantee’s activities will include research, communication resources, educational publications, study visits, training, technical assistance, matching grants and networking events. Established in 2017, Mosaico Laboratorio Creativo was created to strengthen initiatives and organizations working in the social, educational, cultural and artistic fields to motivate citizens in Peru to work collaboratively in favor of those most in need.

title: Developing Community Foundations in Peru
description: The project goal is to develop community foundations in Peru. Over the past two years, Mosaico Laboratorio Creativo’s Comuna Nación program: 1) introduced the community foundation concept to 754 public, private and civic leaders; 2) helped three community foundations get legally constituted; and 3) supported initiative groups in eight more communities, five of which are in the process of becoming community foundations. Over the next two years, the grantee will expand and consolidate the movement of community foundations in Peru, anticipating the formalization of at least seven more community foundations and the identification of at least three additional initiative groups. The grantee also will develop standards and minimum requirements for Peruvian community foundations and strengthen the capacity and sustainability of Comuna Nación. Established in 2017, Mosaico Laboratorio Creativo was created to strengthen initiatives and organizations working in the social, educational, cultural and artistic fields to motivate citizens in Peru to work collaboratively in favor of those most in need.

title: News and Information Programs
description: This grant provides funding to National Public Radio in support of its news and information service. The grantee is recognized as one of the most trusted media brands in the country for its fair and fact-based coverage of national and international news. Each month, over 105 million people are reached through radio, podcasts, websites, social media and mobile apps with news and information to help create a more engaged public.

title: Maintenance of City Parks
description: This grant will provide funding for the City of Flint to contract with Genesee County Parks for the maintenance of six parks around the city and ten park properties along the Flint River. City parks provide recreational green space for residents and are utilized for a variety of activities. This grant will ensure current maintenance levels in these parks continue.

title: Maintenance of City Parks
description: This grant will provide support to the City of Flint to continue the maintenance of parks and properties along the Flint River comprising 532 acres. City parks provide recreational green space for residents and are utilized for a variety of activities. Parks have been especially important during the pandemic as residents sought places to gather outdoors with social distancing options available. This grant will ensure that city parks are once again maintained to a level that gives Flint residents the opportunity to enjoy these community assets in a variety of ways throughout the year.

title: Flint River Restoration Project
description: This grant increase will provide project support to the Genesee County Parks & Recreation Commission for the Flint River Restoration Project. Funds from this grant will be used as a match for a Michigan Natural Resources Trust Fund grant, closing costs, and professional services. The project is the result of a broad group of diverse partners coming together to create a vision for the Flint riverfront as a unique community asset that is accessible and safe for all residents to utilize, drives economic opportunities, and enhances local infrastructure by removing the Hamilton Dam. This project supports the overall economic development opportunities for Flint by creating greater connectivity between the University of Michigan-Flint, downtown, and Kettering University; removing hazardous infrastructure; improving storm water and flood control systems; developing underutilized public property; and capping contamination at a former industrial site.

title: Michigan News and Information Programs
description: This grant provides funding to the University of Michigan’s Michigan Radio in support of its news and information service. Located in Ann Arbor, Michigan Radio is a trusted media brand in the state, known for its fair and fact-based coverage of state, national and international news. Michigan Radio reaches its audience with radio content, podcasts, websites, social media and mobile apps, providing news and information to help create a more engaged public.

title: Flint Farmers' Market Capital Improvements
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: The Flint Farmers’ Market is a key component of ongoing efforts to revitalize downtown Flint. Located in the Health and Wellness District, the market provides Flint residents with year-round access to fresh produce and locally grown foods. The market maintains an active calendar of community events, provides meeting space to local groups, and supports food entrepreneurs through a commercial kitchen co-working space. In addition, market staff educates residents on the importance of healthy eating to mitigate the impact of lead. This grant will support capital improvement projects at the facility. The Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation receives and administers funds for charitable purposes and for the public welfare of Genesee County and is the supporting organization of the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, which operates the Flint Farmers’ Market.

title: Community Water Lab
description: This grant will support the operations of the community water lab at the Flint Development Center. The grantee, Evergreen Community Development Initiative, operates the Flint Development Center which is located in a former Flint Community School elementary building. The community water lab will be equipped with state-of-the-art technology to test water for multiple contaminants. Scientists and staff of the lab, including youth, will work with residents to collect water samples, test for multiple contaminants, provide results and work with households to address any identified issues.

title: Increasing Science, Technology, Engineering and Math in Afterschool
description: This grant seeks to continue to increase the availability of informal science education for students through afterschool and summer learning programs. Specifically, this grant will support the STEM Next Opportunity Fund to: 1) expand the statewide afterschool network STEM initiative to all 50 states, including through the Million Girls Moonshot initiative; 2) support the statewide afterschool networks in data collection and quality improvement efforts to increase the availability of STEM afterschool programs; 3) educate leaders at the local, state and national levels on the importance of STEM afterschool programming; 4) support technical assistance to the state networks in the area of STEM programming and evaluation; and 5) partner with the Mizzen by Mott app to increase STEM content and distribution to the afterschool field.

title: Increasing Science, Technology, Engineering and Math in Afterschool
description: This grant seeks to increase the availability of informal science education for students through afterschool and summer learning programs. Specifically, this grant will support STEM Next Opportunity Fund to: 1) expand the statewide afterschool network STEM initiative to all 50 states, including through the Million Girls Moonshot initiative; 2) support the statewide afterschool networks in data collection and quality improvement efforts to increase the availability of STEM afterschool programs; 3) educate leaders at the local, state, and national levels on the importance of STEM afterschool programming; 4) support technical assistance to the state networks in the area of STEM programming and evaluation; and 5) partner with Mizzen by Mott to increase STEM content and distribution of Mizzen to the afterschool field.

title: Great Lakes Washington Program
geographic_focus: Minnesota, Pennsylvania, New York, Ohio, Illinois, Michigan, Indiana, Wisconsin
description: The Northeast-Midwest Institute is a nonpartisan, Washington, D.C.-based nonprofit organization dedicated to promoting economic and environmental vitality for the Northeastern and Midwestern regions of the United States. With prior support from Mott, the grantee provided opportunities for federal decisionmakers, regional stakeholders, and other interested parties to jointly identify and promote regional Great Lakes priorities related to water quality, water conservation, habitat protection and restoration, and invasive species. With this grant increase, the grantee will support an opportunity for education on Asian carp that addresses preventing the introduction of silver and bighead carp into the Great Lakes.

title: General Purposes
description: The Metropolitan Planning Council is one of the Great Lakes region’s leading urban policy groups, focusing most of its work in the Chicago metropolitan region. Chicago, like many cities in the Great Lakes region, faces a series of environmental and public health challenges, such as flooding and access to clean drinking water, which are exacerbated by climate change and other trends. With prior project support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee undertook several Great Lakes regional planning activities, including the control of invasive species and drinking water affordability issues. With general purposes support, the grantee will conduct research, educate stakeholders, provide technical assistance, facilitate coalition meetings and host convenings on a range of issues, including stormwater management, infrastructure investment and environmental justice.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides renewal support to the Council on Foundations — a national philanthropic organization founded in 1949 that currently represents 846 members. The grantee’s mission is to foster an environment where philanthropy can thrive and cultivate a community of diverse and skilled philanthropic professionals and organizations who lead with integrity, serve as ethical stewards and advocate for progress. During the previous grant period, the grantee: 1) produced new knowledge products; 2) hosted peer learning communities; 3) created a Public Policy Action Network; and 4) continued advocacy for the sector. During this upcoming grant period, the Council on Foundations will focus on four key organizational goals by embracing better ways of operating, expanding philanthropy’s opportunities to thrive, building common ground and fostering a culture of trust and belonging.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides renewal support to the Council on Foundations — a national philanthropic organization founded in 1949 that currently represents over 900 members. The grantee’s mission is to foster an environment where philanthropy can thrive and cultivate a community of diverse and skilled philanthropic professionals and organizations who lead with integrity, serve as ethical stewards and advocate for progress. During the previous grant period, the grantee: 1) produced new knowledge products; 2) hosted peer learning communities; 3) created a focus on trust in institutions; and 4) continued its advocacy for the sector. During this upcoming grant period, the Council on Foundations will focus on four key organizational goals by embracing better ways of operating, expanding philanthropy’s opportunities to thrive, building common ground and fostering a culture of trust and belonging.

title: Social Sector Infrastructure Mapping and Assessment
description: The program goal is to map and assess the organizational infrastructure for the nonprofit and philanthropic sector in the U.S. The New Venture Fund will act as a fiscal sponsor to pool funds provided by at least five U.S. infrastructure funders and commission research to develop a shared social sector typology and map. This, in turn, will be used to: 1) assess the value of the current social sector infrastructure and how it may need to evolve in light of external trends; 2) identify areas where strategic funding can help position the infrastructure to address future challenges; and 3) encourage additional investments aimed at strengthening the capacity of infrastructure organizations currently and in the future. Established in 2006, the New Venture Fund provides a platform to support innovative and effective public interest projects.

title: Generosity Commission
description: The program goal is to support research, widespread public education and public policy recommendations that will promote giving, volunteering, and civic engagement in America. The Giving USA Foundation is establishing the Generosity Commission, a nonpartisan group that will bring together a breadth of stakeholders, voices, and expertise to explore profound questions about the future of giving, volunteering, and other forms of civic engagement in America. The commission’s goals are to: 1) end the 15-year decline in household giving by adding 20 million Americans who give; 2) reverse a 10-year low in volunteerism; 3) unlock Millennial and Generation Z potential for giving and volunteering; 4) renew all forms of generosity as American priorities; and 5) reinforce the vital role of the nonprofit sector in the United States. Established in 1985 as the charitable arm of the Giving Institute, a trade association of fundraising consultants, the Giving USA Foundation publishes data and trends about charitable giving.

title: Generosity Commission
description: The program goal is to support research and public education to promote giving, volunteering and civic engagement in America. The Giving USA Foundation has established the Generosity Commission, a nonpartisan group that will bring together a breadth of stakeholders, voices and expertise to explore profound questions about the future of giving, volunteering and other forms of civic engagement in America. Over the past year, a working group has recruited high-profile members for the commission, funded research on giving and volunteering trends and raised over half of the $3 million total budget for the entire project. In the coming year, project activities will include additional research, a public launch of the commission, a survey and national conversation and the broad dissemination of public recommendations to increase generosity in America. Established in 1985 as the charitable arm of the Giving Institute, a trade association of fundraising consultants, the Giving USA Foundation publishes data and trends about charitable giving.

title: General Purposes
description: How sub-Saharan African countries like Tanzania meet the energy needs of their young, fast-growing and rapidly urbanizing population will significantly determine outcomes on solving global climate change. E-LICO Foundation is a Tanzanian nonprofit that works with rural communities to co-design and implement off-grid renewable energy initiatives which create jobs, while reducing greenhouse gas emissions that cause climate change. Over the past two years, the grantee has established an organizational framework that has piloted several innovative solutions for accelerated access to off-grid renewable energy services for productive use which lower carbon emissions that cause climate change, while improving community livelihoods in the rural Tanzanian regions of Dodoma and Iringa. Within the next two years, E-LICO will replicate and scale up the most impactful and proven off-grid renewable energy solutions, while also strengthening its organizational capacity, partnerships, and outreach.
