This is expected to establish a model for rural off-grid renewable energy access, which can be expanded nationally and internationally.

title: Legal Empowerment Basket Fund for Land and Environmental Justice
description: The project goal is to leverage financing for community justice and environment defenders in mining affected communities. To this end, Namati will design a legal empowerment basket fund for land and environmental justice. During this phase of the project, the grantee and other stakeholders will undertake an intensive design process that draws on research, grassroots case experiences, and stakeholder consultations to develop an effective institutional design and operating procedure. This will include a feasibility assessment and identification of partners. Established in 2011, Namati works to build a global movement of grassroots legal advocates who give people the power to understand, use, and shape the law.

title: General Purposes
description: The European Foundation Centre is an independent membership association of foundations and corporate funders dedicated to promoting organized philanthropy in Europe and internationally. The grantee does this in part by establishing and operating thematic groups focused on specific issues. This grant increase will support the work of one of these groups, the Funders’ Forum on Sustainable Cities, through meetings, publications and related activities to increase efforts to promote sustainable and inclusive growth in cities.

title: Leadership and Community Conversations
description: This grant will support an ongoing set of convenings, meetings, and community conversations about important topics of leadership, inclusion and equity, and youth development. Under the leadership of the Community Foundation of Greater Flint, key leaders will be engaged to present to and network with youth and young professionals. The goal of this initiative is to instill a sense of hope and support the aspirations of young people to fulfill their potential.

title: Great Lakes Water Resources Project
geographic_focus: Ohio, Indiana, Illinois, Michigan, Wisconsin, Pennsylvania, New York, Minnesota
description: The Great Lakes Environmental Law Center is a nonprofit environmental law organization headquartered in Michigan that provides support to community members facing challenges in securing clean and affordable drinking water and healthy natural water resources. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has helped Michigan residents navigate legal approaches to address water challenges and identified solutions for various water issues. The grantee has assisted groups working on water quality, drinking water affordability and the protection of lakes, wetlands and streams. With this renewed support, the Great Lakes Environmental Law Center will continue its services to address ongoing water issues, such as contamination from toxic and persistent chemicals and water diversions from the Great Lakes basin.

title: General Purposes
description: For 50 years, Clean Wisconsin has been Wisconsin’s leading voice for clean air and water. The grantee seeks to provide: 1) all residents with access to healthy air and clean drinking water; 2) provide residents, businesses and visitors an abundance of swimmable, fishable lakes, rivers and streams; and 3) promote an economy that is strong and powered by clean energy. With previous grant support, the grantee has delivered public education initiatives to prevent harmful diversions of Great Lakes water, reduce pollution sources contaminating drinking water supplies, remove lead pipes and advance clean water policies and funding. With this general purposes grant, Clean Wisconsin will pursue all of its objectives around climate change, clean energy, clean air and clean water. This will include efforts to: 1) strengthen clean water policies by educating the public, its members, the media and decision makers about programs to protect and restore the Great Lakes; 2) continue to grow its presence with tribes in northern Wisconsin and urban areas of southeast Wisconsin thus elevating voices in underserved areas; 3) develop leadership training for its staff and board; and 4) conduct research to build strong communications programs around Great Lakes issues.

title: Action for Clean Drinking Water
description: Midwest Environmental Advocates is the only nonprofit environmental law center in Wisconsin that directly provides legal and technical services to community members seeking to protect clean water. With previous Mott Foundation support, the grantee has provided legal and technical support to residents of Wisconsin on a range of issues, including addressing groundwater pollution and preventing harmful diversions of Great Lakes waters. During the same period, the grantee also strengthened its own capacity and strengthened ties to Native American tribes. With renewed support, the grantee will help communities address the most pressing threats to safe water in Wisconsin, especially nutrient pollution of surface and ground water, lead in drinking water and the regulation of PFAS (per- and polyflouroalkyl substances) — a ubiquitous class of toxic chemicals found in the environment.

title: Collaborating to Protect and Restore the Great Lakes
geographic_focus: Indiana, Michigan, Ohio, Illinois, Wisconsin, New York, Pennsylvania, Minnesota
description: The National Wildlife Federation’s Great Lakes Regional Center, based in Michigan and serving the states and provinces of the region, is a leader in engaging partners to work toward protection and restoration of the Great Lakes. The grantee leverages policy, legal, communications, education and scientific expertise to support sound policies and leads several coalitions representing conservation, business, tribal and urban constituencies. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has led a coalition in support of the Great Lakes Restoration Initiative, a federal program that cleans up and restores the lakes. The grantee has also advanced efforts to thwart non-native carp and other invasive species, has engaged community groups to ensure that drinking water is affordable and protected from dangerous chemicals and has sought to protect the lakes from an aging pipeline carrying petroleum under the lakes. With renewed support, the National Wildlife Federation will lead coalitions that seek to prevent invasive species from spreading, prevent pollution from nutrients and dangerous chemicals, ensure affordable drinking water, protect the lakes from resource extraction and restore habitat and water quality that has been damaged in the past.

title: Saginaw Bay Watershed Initiative Network
description: Founded in 1985, the Conservation Fund is a national organization that promotes conservation and sustainable economic development. The grantee’s Saginaw Bay Watershed Initiative Network seeks to advance economic, environmental and social sustainability in Michigan’s Saginaw Bay area. With partial support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has achieved the following during the last grant cycle: 1) regranted funds to partner organizations to improve water quality and freshwater habitat in the Saginaw Bay watershed; 2) developed a project focused on increasing the reach of the network to more diverse audiences and communities; and 3) implemented recommendations from a Mott Foundation supported report on septic system impacts on water quality in the basin. With this renewal, the Conservation Fund will continue to support the regranting program, focus on broadening the network’s reach to more diverse audiences, build on previous successes with septic system education and resume its State of the Bay conference which had been put on hold due to the pandemic.

title: Growing a National Drinking Water Movement
description: The Water Foundation, a grantmaker supporting water policy reform nationwide, seeks to build long-term solutions that increase access to clean and affordable drinking water. With prior support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has accomplished this by strengthening connections between community-based groups, traditional environmental organizations and decision-makers nationwide. With continued support, the grantee will support such organizations in the Great Lakes region to track and influence federal and state-level infrastructure spending and connect Great Lakes groups and leaders to similar initiatives at the national level.

title: General Purposes
description: Minnesota Environmental Partnership is the largest and most active coalition of environmental and conservation groups in the state. Since 1998 the grantee has provided assistance for its members to convene, communicate and collaborate to protect the state’s natural resources and environmental health for its residents. With support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee is promoting protections for land and water, especially in the Lake Superior region, through an equity lens. The grantee is also a leader in the state-level coalition to address climate change. Renewed general purposes support will help advance all of Minnesota Environmental Partnership’s goals, including the effort to integrate environmental justice into its work on water quality, climate change and Great Lakes restoration.

title: General Purposes
description: Founded in 1998, PennFuture is a statewide environmental organization working for clean air, clean water and a healthy climate. The grantee specializes in legal, policy, communication and outreach strategies to respond to the pressing environmental threats in the state. Additionally, the grantee focuses on civic engagement in small- to mid-sized communities across the state. Over the next two years, PennFuture will address priority environmental policy issues and grow its capacity to meet emerging threats and expand its reach to engage underrepresented communities throughout Pennsylvania.

title: General Purposes
description: River Alliance of Wisconsin supports a strong network of local organizations around the state that address threats to Wisconsin’s waters. The grantee established the Wisconsin Water Agenda, a plan to manage water as it exists in nature. Environmental challenges from water pollution and overconsumption, impaired rivers and streams, emerging contaminants and mining, aquatic invasive species, as well as climate change impacts, drive the Wisconsin Water Agenda. With renewed funding, the grantee will expand and move the plan forward toward sustainable water management, build the capacity of local watershed groups and deepen relationships with diverse conservation partners to encourage meaningful action towards change in the Great Lakes region and beyond.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Ohio, Michigan, Ontario, New York, Illinois, Wisconsin, Pennsylvania, Minnesota, Indiana
description: Freshwater Future is one of the only binational environmental nonprofit organizations in the Great Lakes region. The grantee provides grants, capacity building, technical expertise and training to support local groups and leaders working to protect waters in their communities. Since its inception in 1996, with significant support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has provided over $5 million in grants and technical assistance to grassroots groups around the region. Recently, the grantee has focused more of its efforts and resources to provide support to community-based groups in urban areas to ensure safe drinking water. With renewed support, the grantee will provide financial support and technical assistance to support local groups and networks collaborating on Great Lakes policy issues. Freshwater Future will continue to grow their organizational capacity through expanded fundraising.

title: General Purposes
description: The Grand Traverse Regional Land Conservancy, founded in 1991, is a land trust serving a five-county region located in northwest lower Michigan. During the last grant period, the grantee made very significant progress on a multiyear capital campaign, securing funding commitments surpassing $90 million. The funds will be used to protect and maintain natural areas, scenic views and farmland in the service area. Renewed support will allow the Grand Traverse Regional Land Conservancy to successfully transition out of the fundraising campaign and continue the full range of the organization’s work.

title: Healthy Great Lakes Program
description: The Canadian Environmental Law Association is a nationwide organization that provides legal aid, education, outreach and access to the federal decision-making process for residents of Ontario and Quebec. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has provided trusted analysis and guidance for decision-makers and the public on Great Lakes issues, including water contaminants, watershed planning and drinking water protection. With renewed support, the grantee will expand its network, deepen connections with indigenous communities and educate on sound water policies in the Great Lakes. The Canadian Environmental Law Association will lead efforts to promote safe drinking water, expedite the lead line removal process and cultivate strong local organizations to protect watersheds.

title: Innovating Clean Water Financing and Community Engagement in the Great Lakes
description: American Rivers is a national organization whose mission is to protect wild rivers, restore damaged rivers and conserve clean water for people and nature, and has long prioritized the importance of the rivers of the Great Lakes region. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has been actively working on water quality issues with an emphasis on green infrastructure especially in disadvantaged communities. The grantee has been able to establish an effective network of local water leaders and increase the capacity of local governments in the Great Lakes’ basin to utilize green infrastructure funding. With renewed support, American Rivers will build on their previous work in the region to engage on the equitable distribution of historic levels of federal infrastructure funds in Great Lakes states that result in clean water for people and the region’s waterways.

title: Great Lakes Water Infrastructure Project
description: Based in Chicago, the Center for Neighborhood Technology provides research, tools and solutions to cities to help create sustainable and equitable communities. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has provided workshops and technical assistance on water infrastructure challenges faced by Great Lakes cities, including Flint and Chicago. The grantee has created water infrastructure toolkits and interactive mapping to assist communities with need assessments and water infrastructure solutions. With continued support, the grantee will design new programs with and for community groups to engage in sustainable water infrastructure decision-making. The Center for Neighborhood Technology will also expand a model approach it previously developed with Mott Foundation support to new communities to identify lead service lines needing replacement.

title: Lake Michigan Water Program
description: The Illinois Environmental Council Education Fund is an established environmental organization with over 100 affiliates. The grantee leads coalition building, education and outreach efforts protecting Lake Michigan and water resources within Illinois. With prior support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has elevated statewide awareness of the dangers of lead pipes and the need to expedite lead service line replacement. The grantee also launched an initiative to reduce pollution from plastic waste in the Great Lakes basin. With renewed support, the Illinois Environmental Council Education Fund will create conditions to support investment in Illinois’ crumbling water infrastructure, address emerging contaminants in water and help forge a new state water plan, all while seeking to ensure that clean, safe and affordable drinking water is accessible across the state with a focus on urban centers in the Great Lakes basin.

title: General Purposes
description: Founded in 1937, Michigan United Conservation Clubs is the nation’s largest statewide coalition of conservation clubs. The grantee works with its 40,000 individuals and 200 organizational members to conserve, protect and enhance Michigan’s natural resources and outdoor heritage through advocacy, education, communications and stewardship. With prior Mott Foundation support, the grantee has promoted a science-driven approach to conservation issues in Michigan. With continued support, the grantee will work with member organizations and other stakeholders to address threats to freshwater biodiversity and other conservation challenges, build its own organizational capacity and develop new partnerships with diverse communities.

title: General Purposes
description: The Minnesota Center for Environmental Advocacy has been a legal and scientific voice for Minnesota’s environment since 1974. The grantee’s team of in-house lawyers and scientists work to address environmental issues across all branches of government. With prior Mott Foundation support, the grantee has been able to defend existing environmental laws and regulations, improve water quality in Lake Superior and across the state, advance climate change solutions, strengthen long-standing partnerships with Native American tribes in the region and increase capacity in Duluth to partner and engage more fully with community-based organizations. Renewed support will help advance progress toward protecting Minnesota’s environment with a focus on natural resource protection, water quality and environmental justice.

title: An Equitable Water Future in the Great Lakes
description: The U.S. Water Alliance is a coalition of water utilities, consultants, environmental groups and community organizations that work together to advance a holistic approach to water management. The grantee is one of the leading organizations advancing the goal of water equity in which all communities have access to safe and affordable water regardless of race or economic status, share in the benefits of water systems and are resilient in the face of climate change and other stressors. With prior Mott Foundation support, the grantee launched the Water Equity Network which now numbers 28 member cities, including several in the Great Lakes region. With continued support, the grantee will grow and deepen the impact of the network with the aim of reaching 75 cities by 2025. The grantee will also work with network members in the Great Lakes and nationally to demonstrate how to use available federal infrastructure dollars to achieve more equitable water management outcomes. Funding will also support the U.S. Water Alliance’s signature annual event, the One Water Summit, to be held in the Great Lakes region in 2022.

title: Technical Assistance to Boost Great Lakes Communication
description: Since its inception in 1996, with significant support from the Mott Foundation, Freshwater Future has provided over $4.7 million through 1,260 grants for capacity building and technical support to groups working to protect and restore the waters of the region. With prior Mott support, the grantee worked with a communications consulting firm and together they provided technical support to organizations active in the Great Lakes basin to strengthen their communications capacity. With renewed support, the grantee will continue the arrangement with the consulting firm, expand the pool of organizations receiving direct technical support and continue to provide training and tools to other organizations to more effectively utilize communications to advance organizational objectives.

title: Charity & Security Network
description: The Charity & Security Network promotes and protects nonprofit organizations’ ability to serve communities, support peace and human rights, aid civilians in areas of disaster and armed conflict and build democratic governance. During the previous grant period, the grantee convened stakeholders, engaged in dialogue with policymakers, promoted legal frameworks that protect the positive contribution civil society makes to human security and provided legal and policy analysis on relevant issues to nonprofits, policymakers and other stakeholders. The grantee’s goals for the upcoming grant period include: analyzing and raising awareness about the criminalization of genuine nonprofit humanitarian and peacebuilding efforts; assessing and addressing the negative consequences of sanctions policy and law; improving access for nonprofits and philanthropic organizations; and countering lawfare attacks on nonprofits. The Charity & Security Network is a project of NEO Philanthropy, a funder intermediary launched in 1983 as a Public Interest Project.

title: 21st Century Community Learning Centers Institute
description: This grant to Foundations, Inc., will provide funding to support an annual conference for afterschool educators and practitioners to build the capacity of afterschool programs and the afterschool field. The conference is one of the largest available for the administrators of the 21st Century Community Learning Centers and includes technical assistance and strategies to continue to enhance the quality of school-community afterschool programs. As one of the leading conferences for afterschool professionals, the conference provides best practices in program design, evaluation, community engagement, and program sustainability.

title: General Purposes
description: The Biodiversity Funders Group is a professional association of environmental, conservation and climate and energy grantmakers founded in 1987. Today, the grantee comprises approximately 70 member institutions, predominantly private foundations. More than 200 other grantmaking institutions benefit from its activities as program partners. The grantee reaches nearly 1,000 philanthropical staff and trustees, mostly in the United States and also in Canada, England, Switzerland and other countries, and promotes peer funder learning and collaboration.

title: Engaging Older Youth in Service
description: This grant will support America’s Service Commissions to expand youth service opportunities throughout the United States. Specifically, this grant will support the grantee to: 1) map the current national investments in youth service; 2) provide technical assistance and minigrants to 10 state service commissions; and 3) document promising practices for expanding youth service programming.

title: 21st Century Community Learning Centers Meeting
description: Due to the coronavirus pandemic, this grant supported the virtual National AfterSchool Association convention. In addition, grant funding will support utilizing the grantee’s various communications outlets to promote the Mizzen by Mott App throughout the course of the year to their members and convention attendees.

title: Expanding National Service and Replication of the Flint National Service Accelerator Initiative
description: This grant will allow Service Year Alliance to support communities in their efforts to build and strengthen national service. Specifically, this grant will support the grantee in: 1) coordinating a convening; 2) providing technical assistance; and 3) developing resources to strengthen the service field.

title: Georgia Manor
description: Communities First’s mission is to build healthy, vibrant communities through economic development, affordable housing, and innovative programming. This grant will help further their mission by supporting the redevelopment of the Georgia Manor apartment complex located in Flint’s historic Carriage Town neighborhood.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Free State, Northern Cape, Province of, Western Cape, Province of the, Eastern Cape, Province of
description: The Social Change Assistance Trust works to improve the quality of life in poor communities by supporting community-based organizations that promote access to justice, gender equity, youth empowerment and food security. To achieve this, the grantee makes grants, provides training and connects organizations working in the Eastern Cape, Western Cape and Northern Cape provinces. Activities under the previous grant included making grants of over $500,000 to 30 community advice offices and local development agencies in the three provinces, enabling the organizations to respond to immediate needs in the wake of COVID-19. Building on previous work, the grantee provided training to women on gender-based violence, increased the number of organizations receiving support and funding and produced four publications that profile the work of the grantees and partners. During this grant period, the Social Change Assistance Trust will continue to support community advice offices in improving the lives of poor communities through its programs.

title: Regulation of Nonprofits and Philanthropy
description: The program goal is to support a healthy policy environment for the nonprofit and philanthropy sector. The Regulation of Nonprofits and Philanthropy project aims to document, enhance understanding and promote dialogue related to the state and federal regulatory framework and its impact on charities, philanthropy and the nonprofit sector. The project engages attorney generals and other state officials, federal regulators, academics, researchers and nonprofit practitioners. In the past two years, the project has produced several research studies on state and federal charity regulation and enforcement. These studies have been presented at several relevant stakeholder gatherings and have spawned additional research and dialogue. Over the next two years, the project will: 1) produce research and analysis on state and federal regulatory issues affecting the charitable sector; 2) present at a variety of academic and nonprofit forums and conferences; 3) host a symposium; and 4) disseminate research papers, briefs and publications. The project is implemented by the Center on Nonprofits and Philanthropy at the Urban Institute — a think tank that builds knowledge about the nation’s social and fiscal challenges.

title: Afterschool College and Career Readiness Initiative
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant to the Arkansas State University System Foundation will enable the Arkansas Statewide Afterschool Network to increase the availability and expansion of financial education and college affordability planning by enhancing quality afterschool and summer learning opportunities for underserved youth. This project will support the network to: 1) create a scalable model to mitigate barriers associated with college affordability planning; 2) increase the number of college savings accounts and participation in college affordability programs; and 3) build support and awareness among new and key stakeholders to address the critical gap of youth and families engaged in financial literacy and college affordability planning. The grantee will share promising practices and resources with the 50 state networks and the Mizzen by Mott App to enhance college and career readiness initiatives in afterschool programs nationally.

title: Afterschool College and Career Readiness Initiative
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant to the Central Susquehanna Intermediate Unit will enable the Pennsylvania Statewide Afterschool Network to increase the availability and expansion of financial education and college affordability planning by enhancing quality afterschool and summer learning opportunities for underserved youth. This project will support the network to 1) administer a financial literacy and college affordability assessment and needs survey with the afterschool field; 2) develop and promote financial literacy tutorials and resources for afterschool staff and students; and 3) pilot an afterschool financial literacy model with the afterschool community. Central Susquehanna Intermediate Unit will share promising practices and resources with the 50 state networks and the Mizzen by Mott App to enhance college and career readiness initiatives in afterschool programs nationally.

title: Afterschool College and Career Readiness Initiative
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant to Vermont Afterschool will enable the Vermont Statewide Afterschool Network to increase the availability and expansion of financial education and college affordability planning by enhancing quality afterschool and summer learning opportunities for underserved youth. This project will support the network to 1) expand access to financial literacy programs at the elementary and middle school levels; 2) build financial literacy into Vermont Afterschool’s high school initiatives; and 3) develop a statewide communications plan to build awareness about the importance of afterschool. Vermont Afterschool will share promising practices and resources with the 50 state networks and the Mizzen by Mott App to enhance college and career readiness initiatives in afterschool programs nationally.

title: Afterschool College and Career Readiness Initiative
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant to the Wyoming Community Foundation will enable the Wyoming Statewide Afterschool Network to increase the availability and expansion of financial education and college affordability planning by enhancing quality afterschool and summer learning opportunities for underserved youth. This project will support the network to 1) develop a mentorship model and program for youth to navigate barriers associated with college affordability; 2) increase the number of youth and families participating in financial wellness and college planning initiatives; and 3) build awareness and alignment among new and key stakeholders to address the gap of supports for youth and families engaged in financial literacy and college affordability planning. The Wyoming Community Foundation will share promising practices and resources with the 50 state networks and the Mizzen by Mott App to enhance college and career readiness initiatives in afterschool programs nationally.

title: Technical Support to Maximize Renewable Energy Access Success
grantee: Instituto de Energia e Meio Ambiente
description: The Instituto de Energia e Meio Ambiente is a Brazilian think tank with expertise in energy planning, electrical engineering and environmental law and policy. Over the previous grant period, the grantee contributed technical data and analysis that contributed to the creation of a new federal program to expand renewable energy access in the Amazon. During the next grant period, the grantee will work with electrical distributers and energy agencies to ensure new solar programs include energy for productive economic activity, as well as technical proposals for scaling up sustainable solar supply chains and decommissioning solar equipment once it is no longer in use.

title: Advancing Renewable Energy Access in the Amazon
description: The Brazilian Institute for Consumer Defense is a large nongovernmental organization focused on ensuring all Brazilian citizens have access to essential goods and services and to social development, sustainable consumption and a healthy planet. Over the grant period, specialists in environment, energy and communications will work toward expanding public policy and finance for clean energy access for all Brazilians, including isolated communities in the Amazon.

title: Growing Role of Brazil in Latin America
description: This grant supports the IPS-Inter Press Service in Montevideo, Uruguay, to increase the quality and quantity of journalistic coverage of energy and infrastructure development and finance in Brazil and South America. Over the past grant period, the organization’s coverage was picked up by more than 200 news outlets and a workshop on biogas development attracted participation from 12 journalists from across the region. The current project will continue to examine energy finance and development in South America through stories, photos, videos and a book. IPS-Inter Press Service is a global news agency operating in more than 100 countries and has been working in Latin America for more than 50 years with a network of journalists reporting from most countries in the region.

title: Forecasting Amazon Fires
description: The Woods Hole Research Center is a premier scientific organization working globally to solve climate change, and in Brazil to protect the Amazon rainforest. This grant will support the creation of forecast maps of forest degradation and fire potential for wide dissemination in Brazil to combat illegal fires and forest destruction.

title: Centre on African Philanthropy and Social Investment - Community Philanthropy Literature
geographic_focus: Eastern Africa, Southern Africa, Western Africa
description: The University of the Witwatersrand was established to provide high-quality, internationally competitive education, founded on high academic standards, cutting-edge research, public engagement and productive partnerships with leading institutions throughout the world. The Centre on African Philanthropy and Social Investment, based at the University’s business school, was established to bridge the gap in the study, research and practice of philanthropy and social investment in Africa. Since its establishment in 2018, the center has developed academic programs on philanthropy and social investment in Africa, conducted research on various topics in different countries across the continent and facilitated discussions about the role of philanthropy in the continent. This grant will enable the center to produce new literature about community philanthropy and community philanthropy organizations in Malawi, Mali, Mozambique, Rwanda and Sierra Leone.

title: Adopting the SDGs as a Frame for Organizational Strategy
geographic_focus: Collier, Charlotte, Lee, Hendry, Glades, United States
description: The program goal is to encourage community foundations to advance the Sustainable Development Goals at the local level. To this end, the Southwest Florida Community Foundation will conduct a two-year research and development project to integrate the Sustainable Development Goals as the guiding framework for its work. Activities will include: 1) hiring a full-time animator and data analyst to coordinate with staff and others to articulate, organize, and utilize the goals as the primary design and assessment framework for the organization; 2) acquiring a high-end data analytics tool; 3) issuing reports regarding using the Sustainable Development Goals framework for its local grantmaking; 4) analyzing donor-advised and field-of-interest funds and aligning them to the goals; 5) initiating discussions with donors to demonstrate how the grantee can tie its local and national giving to a global framework; and 6) issuing a report for the field on the experience of deploying the goals as a framework for traditional community foundation functions.

title: Community Foundations, Economic Mobility and the Sustainable Development Goals
description: CFLeads is launching the Economic Mobility Action Network, a peer network of initially six community foundation teams from around the country that will design and implement an economic mobility agenda in their communities over the next two years. The grantee will enlist an expert from the Brookings Institution and other community foundation peers to introduce the Sustainable Development Goals to this network. It will then test the possibilities for the participating community foundations to integrate the goals as a guiding framework for their economic mobility work. Expertise and peer learning will primarily be delivered through two meetings in 2020 as well as consulting and technical assistance. Established in 1991 as the Coalition of Community Foundations for Youth, CFLeads became an independent nonprofit organization in 2017. Its mission is to help community foundations build strong communities by advancing effective practices, sharing knowledge, and galvanizing action on the critical issues of our time.

title: Thrive Central Florida
geographic_focus: Polk, Seminole, Osceola, Sumter, Orange, Marion, Lake, Brevard, Volusia
description: The program goal is to encourage community foundations to advance the Sustainable Development Goals at the local level. To this end, the Central Florida Foundation will advance the Thrive Central Florida initiative—an integrated approach to utilizing the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals and the Social Determinants of Health to create a more cohesive way to solve complex social issues in Central Florida. Founded in 1994, the grantee is a public grantmaking foundation that connects philanthropy and strategy to address community issues, manages and invests charitable gifts, offers donors personalized service and expert grantmaking advice and connects donors with charitable organizations that meet their philanthropic goals.

title: Developing Community Foundations in Chile
description: The Community of Solidary Organizations is a network of 240 nongovernmental organizations with a mission to build a community of strengthened and connected organizations that can influence the development of a just and sustainable society in Chile. A group of Chilean stakeholders, led by a current Mott grantee charged with raising awareness about the community foundation concept in Chile, has collectively determined that the Community of Solidary Organizations is best equipped to lead a full-fledged program to develop community foundations in their country. Accordingly, over a six-month period, the grantee will create a development plan for such a program. Activities will include: 1) establishing the program’s advisory council, priorities and performance indicators; 2) developing a narrative to best articulate the community foundation concept; 3) discovering territories where there is an interest in establishing community foundations; 4) developing a training plan for local leaders; and 4) creating a three-year program deployment plan.

title: Strengthen Community Justice in Rural Malawi
grantee: Centre for Human Rights Education Advice and Assistance
description: The goal of the Strengthen Community Justice in Rural Malawi project is to increase access to justice for poor and marginalized people in Malawi. To this end, the Centre for Human Rights Education Advice and Assistance will provide access to justice services in the Chikwawa, Chiradzulo, Dedza, Mwanza and Nsanje districts in the southern regions of Malawi. The grantee proposes to use a legal empowerment approach in addressing injustices, while navigating both the formal and informal justice systems. The grantee is an independent nonprofit trust that provides justice services, does strategic litigation and undertakes advocacy in helping Malawians access justice.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Centre for Human Rights Education Advice and Assistance
description: The project goal is to increase access to justice for poor and marginalized people in Malawi. To this end, the Centre for Human Rights Education Advice and Assistance will provide free justice services to people who cannot afford them in Malawi. The grantee will also use the lessons learned from their work to address systemic injustices faced by Malawians and elevate their stories to policymakers and audiences that matter. Established in 2000, the Centre for Human Rights Education Advice and Assistance works to uphold human rights, and the rule of law and provide access to justice to marginalized people in Malawi.

title: Opening Justice
description: The project goal is to develop and expand justice commitments of governments participating in the Open Government Partnership. To this end, the grantee will assist its members in developing and adhering to commitments on justice within their national action plans for open government. To support this effort, the grantee’s secretariat will pursue three areas of work with members. Through co-creation, the grantee will work with national governments and their civil society partners to identify and include innovative approaches to addressing access to justice needs within national policy frameworks. Through commitments, the grantee will share examples of effective justice plans and policies for those intending to take on new commitments. Through coalitions, the secretariat will organize an exchange on emerging practices in order to inspire uptake of justice reform more broadly among members. The Open Government Partnership currently brings together 78 national governments, along with local government and civil society partners, to promote transparency, accountability, and more responsive governance.

title: Legal Empowerment Learning Agenda
description: The Bernstein Institute for Human Rights at the New York University School of Law seeks to advance legal empowerment research and learning through the Legal Empowerment Lab and Shared Learning Agenda research and collaboration activities. The grantee will train academics and grassroots practitioners jointly in participatory research methods to inform richer analyses of legal empowerment outcomes. A series of learning resources will be produced and specific research projects will be undertaken, all of which will actively feature practitioners and their beneficiary partners. Together, these activities are intended to ensure that the legal empowerment field is itself learning directly from those impacted by injustice.

title: Equipment Upgrades
grantee: Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint
description: This grant will support the installation of a new heating and cooling system at the Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint’s Averill Avenue facility. Every day, the grantee serves approximately 125 young people at the facility during the school year and 176 during the summer months. Ongoing heating and cooling issues have impacted services in the winter when the building gets too cold and in the summer when the building is too hot. This upgrade will ensure that the facility can remain open regardless of the temperature outside.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides funding to an organization focused on enhancing the capacity and knowledge of philanthropic networks. In 2022-23, the United Philanthropy Forum advocated on behalf of the nonprofit and philanthropic sector and also partnered and collaborated with other infrastructure organizations through four key pillar areas: 1) racial equity, diversity and inclusion; 2) public policy; 3) philanthropic practice; and 4) knowledge management. In 2024-25, the grantee will continue to lead a vibrant network; maximize the individual and collective capacity and impact of its members; and provide learning, knowledge and resources to its members. Formed in 1998, as the Forum of Regional Associations of Grantmakers, the United Philanthropy Forum is a member of the national network of associations of grantmakers. Its current members are nearly 100 regional and national philanthropy-serving organizations across the United States that represent more than 7,000 foundations and other philanthropic organizations.

title: General Purposes
description: Alliance Publishing Trust facilitates the exchange of information and ideas among philanthropists, social investors and others working for social change worldwide. To this end, the grantee carries out a range of publishing activities with regular products, including: 1) Alliance, a quarterly print magazine; 2) weekly newsletters, including one dedicated to climate philanthropy and social investment; 3) latest news and columns dedicated to sector trends and daily developments in the philanthropic world; and 4) Alliance events hosted around the special theme of each magazine issue and other selected themes. In 2024, the grantee reached its highest ever readership and delivered growing earned revenue in key income lines. The grantee had over 38,000 readers of its various information products. During this grant period, the grantee intends to publish Alliance Magazine quarterly in both print and digital formats, produce a range of content delivered digitally, expand its coverage globally and organize regular in-person and online events including the first summit for the world’s philanthropy media.

title: Advancing the Next Generation of Civil Society Assistance
description: The project goal is to help funders, policymakers and civic activists understand and respond to the diverse forces shaping civic space and civic activism. To this end, the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace will expand membership in its two key networks, the civic research network and the digital democracy network; convene workshops and international meetings; publish reports and articles; and brief funders, practitioners and policymakers on key trends and dynamics. During 2020-2023, the grantee generated knowledge in the form of articles and reports and created linkages between the research, practice and policy domains through online and in-person workshops and briefings. Established in 1910 in Washington, D.C. with a gift from Andrew Carnegie, the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace is a private, nonprofit organization dedicated to advancing cooperation between nations and promoting active international engagement by the United States.

title: Fund for Democracy and Solidarity in Europe
description: The program goal is to promote, protect and reinvigorate the space for civic engagement in Europe. To this end, the Network of European Foundations will manage a grantmaking fund, called Civitates, to: 1) support civil society organizations working together to protect the space for civic engagement; 2) improve the quality of public discourse in the digital age; and 3) strengthen independent, public interest journalism in Europe. The grantee will manage and grow the fund and make grants and provide networking and technical assistance to nonprofits working on these issues across Europe. During 2020-2021, the grantee awarded more than €3.4 million in grants through Civitates and increased the number of foundations participating in the fund from 16 to 23. The Network of European Foundations is based in Brussels, Belgium.

title: Civitates: the Fund for Democracy and Solidarity in Europe
description: The program goal is to promote, protect and reinvigorate the space for civic engagement in Europe. To this end, the Network of European Foundations will manage Civitates, a grantmaking fund to: 1) improve the space for independent civil society organizations and media to operate and promote constructive civic engagement; 2) foster a healthy online and offline environment for public debate and discourse; and 3) catalyze effective public and private funding for democracy and civic space in Europe. The grantee will manage and grow the fund, make grants and provide networking and technical assistance to nonprofits working on these issues across Europe. Since its establishment in 2018, through Civitates, the grantee has awarded approximately €10 million in grants to 50 organizations in 18 European countries. Civitates is supported by 18 private foundations. The Network of European Foundations is based in Brussels, Belgium.

title: Scaling the Digital Activism Hub
geographic_focus: Western Africa, Eastern Europe, Central America, South America
description: The project goal is to build knowledge and capacity that will empower nonprofits and other civil society actors to use digital technology and communications strategies effectively to advance their missions. To this end, Fundacja TechSoup, the European hub of TechSoup, will further develop and scale up its online digital activism platform, called Hive Mind, and deepen its work to support digital activism in West Africa, Latin America, and Central and Eastern Europe. During the previous grant period, the grantee built Hive Mind, an online global resource to help civil society actors to develop content for social media and other online spaces, counter negative and false information and communicate key messages effectively. The platform has 4,100 registered users who can access content in nine languages. Fundacja TechSoup also established partnerships with leading nonprofits in West Africa and Latin America in order to better serve civil society in these regions.

title: Shaping Civic Space in the Digital Age
grantee: European Center for Not-for-Profit Law Stichting
description: The project goal is to promote, protect and enhance civic space in the digital age. To this end, the European Center for Not-for-Profit Law Stichting, a nonprofit registered in the Netherlands, will: 1) research opportunities and challenges facing civic space and inform the field; 2) strengthen cross-sectoral alliances and coalitions to work on key issues; and 3) contribute to global and regional discussions and guiding documents. Through research, analysis, technical assistance, networking and engagement with key stakeholders, the grantee will build the capacity of civil society and safeguard civic space online. The grantee is based in The Hague.

title: Shaping Civic Space in the Digital Age
grantee: European Center for Not-for-Profit Law Stichting
description: The project goal is to promote, protect and enhance civic space in the digital age. To this end, through research, analysis, technical assistance, networking and engagement with key stakeholders the European Center for Not-for-Profit Law Stichting, a nonprofit registered in the Netherlands, will build the capacity of civil society and safeguard civic space online. During the previous grant period, the grantee organized six workshops with over 70 nonprofit representatives, activists and experts, including Roma activists, representatives from the European disability network, youth organizations and human rights watchdog groups. The grantee also launched an online learning center with resources on key digital rights issues impacting civic space, built the capacity of national level groups in six countries and engaged with United Nations agencies setting civic space norms and standards. The European Center for Not-for-Profit Law Stichting is based in The Hague.

title: General Purposes
grantee: European Center for Not-for-Profit Law Stichting
description: The European Center for Not-for-Profit Law Stichting, is a nonprofit registered in the Netherlands working to build the capacity of civil society and safeguard civic space. The grantee aspires to protect and promote the rights to freedom of association, assembly and expression in the digital age through research, analysis, technical assistance, networking and engagement with key stakeholders. During the previous grant period, the grantee provided expertise on artificial intelligence regulation to the United Nations Human Rights Committee, the White House and to a group of 149 global investors. European Center for Not-for-Profit Law Stichting also created an Expert Hub of over 100 experts from 50 countries who provided peer-mentoring and training to reverse anti-money laundering and counterterrorism financing restrictions impacting civil society organizations.

title: Renewable Energy for Extractive Reserves in the Amazon
description: This project will support the World Wildlife Fund and its partner, World Wildlife Fund Brazil, to continue working on a national program for solar energy for forest-dwelling communities living in sustainable development reserves in the Amazon. Over the prior grant period, the grantee contributed to the installation of 31 solar systems in three Amazonian extractive reserves and actively raised the visibility of pilot project results, broadening the discussion of solar energy among the public and private sectors. During this grant period, the grantee will continue to monitor outcomes of community managed solar energy pilots, promote solar photovoltaic value chains in Amazon municipalities and coordinate a network of nongovernmental organizations working on renewable electrification in the Brazilian Amazon.

title: Financial Recovery Technical Assistance
description: The purpose of this grant increase is to provide additional support to the City of Flint as it continues to recover from the water crisis. Experienced staff and consulting support will allow city leadership to function more effectively and efficiently as the recovery process continues.

title: YouthQuest Evaluation
description: Michigan State University will conduct an evaluation of YouthQuest, a research-based afterschool program offered to students at Flint Community Schools and the International Academy of Flint. High-quality afterschool programs can have a positive impact on students’ academic outcomes, behavior and measures of well-being. This evaluation will assist the YouthQuest team with program monitoring toward continuous improvement.

title: Technical Assistance
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Whiting Auditorium and recently renovated Capitol Theatre are currently programs of the Flint Cultural Center Corporation. The Flint Cultural Center Corporation and the Flint Institute of Music have signed a Memorandum of Understanding that establishes terms and conditions under which the grantee will manage and operate the Whiting Auditorium and the Capitol Theatre for a seven-month period while the possibility of a permanent consolidation is explored. This grant will provide consulting help and technical assistance for the due diligence period of exploration.

title: Technical Assistance
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Whiting Auditorium and recently renovated Capitol Theatre are currently programs of the Flint Cultural Center Corporation. The grantee and the Flint Institute of Music have signed a Memorandum of Understanding that establishes terms and conditions under which the Flint Institute of Music will manage and operate the Whiting Auditorium and the Capitol Theatre for a seven-month period while the possibility of a permanent consolidation is explored. This grant will provide consulting help and technical assistance for the due diligence period of exploration as well as for strategic planning for the Flint Cultural Center Corporation moving forward.

title: What's Up Downtown Capacity Building
description: This grant will help the Greater Flint Arts Council fund What’s Up Downtown, a placemaking project focused on programming public spaces. The grantee will utilize the funds to support a full-time director for the project and leverage additional resources to coordinate events for the community.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to help address the long-standing and emerging issues facing immigrants in the Americas. Alianza Americas’ mission is to bring about a more inclusive, equitable, and sustainable way of life for under-served immigrant communities living in the United States, Mexico, and Central America. The grantee accomplishes this through its action-driven diplomacy, network advocacy, educational delegations and tours, a leadership institute, and mobile outreach supporting the caravans. The purpose of this increase is to enable the grantee to provide support to Kino Glaz, an organization in El Salvador that provides innovative afterschool programs in high-risk urban communities. Founded in 2004 by Mexican, Central American, and Caribbean immigrant leaders, Alianza Americas is a network of over 50 members in 13 states, representing over 150,000 migrant families across the United States, with dozens of organizational partners in Mexico and Central America.

title: Choice Neighborhood Blight Elimination
description: This grant will support the City of Flint Choice Neighborhood Initiative by funding the Genesee County Land Bank Authority to demolish blighted properties in the broader Choice Neighborhood Initiative area to support reinvestment, strengthen neighborhoods, and improve public safety.

title: Building Sustainable Local Energy Enterprises Serving the Poor
description: The Entrepreneurship Management and Development Foundation was established in 2010 to assist individuals and micro, small and medium enterprises in Tanzania to develop stronger entrepreneurial skills. A particular focus is the development of off-grid renewable energy companies. To reach rural communities that have no access to electricity, it is crucial that entrepreneurs are provided with adequate training and mentoring to develop these businesses. With this grant increase, the grantee will add a special module focused on technical skills related to renewable energy, increase broader awareness of opportunities in off-grid renewable energy and build capacity for community trainers to provide ongoing coaching and guidance.

title: General Purposes
description: The Bank Information Center is a nongovernmental organization specialized in analyzing and strengthening social and environmental governance of international financial institutions, primarily the World Bank Group. Over the last grant period, the grantee and its partners in developing countries worked on finalizing the new Environmental Social Framework of the World Bank Group. This increase will be available for the organization’s general purposes, which includes helping Bank Information Center’s partners participate in consultations organized by the Inter-American Development Bank.

title: 21st Century Community Learning Centers Institute
description: This grant will provide support to Foundations, Inc. to continue to provide comprehensive services and supports to enhance learning experiences and professional development opportunities to 21st Century Community Learning Center’s leaders and the afterschool field. The comprehensive services and supports will focus on showcasing Mizzen by Mott resources throughout the year with targeted marketing strategies through virtual events. These events include mainstage presentations, interactive workshop experiences, content partner showcases and social media events. These learning experiences for afterschool educators will expand their strategies and skillsets to enhance the quality of school-community afterschool programs.

title: 21st Century Community Learning Centers Institute
description: This grant will support Foundations, Inc. to offer comprehensive services and supports to enhance high quality learning experiences and professional development opportunities to 21st Century Community Learning Center’s leaders and the afterschool field. These events include: 1) expert panel discussions; 2) interactive workshop experiences; 3) content partner showcases; 4) virtual learning supports;and 5) social media events. The learning experiences for afterschool and summer learning educators will expand their strategies and skill sets to enhance the quality of school and community-based out of school-time programs.

title: 21st Century Community Learning Centers Institute
description: This grant will support Foundations, Inc. to offer comprehensive services and supports to enhance high-quality learning experiences and professional development opportunities to 21st Century Community Learning Centers’ leaders and the afterschool field. These events include: 1) expert panel discussions; 2) interactive workshop experiences; 3) content partner showcases; 4) virtual learning supports; and 5) social media events. The learning experiences for afterschool and summer learning educators will expand their strategies and skill sets to enhance the quality of school and community-based out-of-school time programs.

title: Impact of Program and Practice Characteristics on Participant Outcomes
description: This grant will enable the University of California, Irvine to carry out further research to support afterschool programs. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) complete the analysis of a longitudinal study which addresses the impact on youth who participate in afterschool programs up through age 26; and 2) conduct a comprehensive meta-analysis of afterschool programs, including 21st Century Community Learning Centers programs.

title: Fiscal Solvency and Service Effectiveness Project
description: This renewal grant provides support for Michigan State University’s efforts to document and promote solutions that help America’s older industrial cities address chronic fiscal stress and advance overall fiscal health. During the grant period, the grantee will develop a range of potential scenarios for addressing structural deficits and assess the feasibility of each scenario with a particular focus on legal and political implications. The City of Flint will remain a priority for continuing research activities.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides renewal support to the Council on Foundations, a national philanthropic organization founded in 1949 that currently represents 760 members. The grantee’s mission is to foster an environment where philanthropy can thrive and cultivate a community of diverse and skilled philanthropic professionals and organizations who lead with integrity, serve as ethical stewards and advocate for progress. Despite being virtual for most of 2020 due to the pandemic, the grantee continued to provide a wide variety of programmatic offerings, including regularly produced newsletters for specific constituencies, eight sector publications, regular communications with congressional offices and federal agencies, 66 virtual events for more than 6,000 participants, the Career Pathways leadership development program and approximately 2,000 responses to requests for information on legal matters. In 2021, the grantee will embark on the implementation of a new three-year strategic plan that will help philanthropic institutions and leaders improve, provide engagement opportunities for members and position the Council on Foundations as the primary organization representing the interests of philanthropy.

title: Great Lakes Now
geographic_focus: Ohio, New York, Minnesota, Wisconsin, Ontario, Pennsylvania, Michigan, Indiana, Illinois
description: Great Lakes Now is an initiative of Detroit Public Television that provides communities and residents with accessible, important news and information related to the health of the lakes, including water quality. The 40 million residents of the Great Lakes watershed are blessed with an abundance of fresh water and share an affinity for the lakes, but many are unaware of how the lakes are changing, nor of the impacts of their actions and choices on the health of the lakes. With a potential reach of 20 million viewers and a diverse and deeply invested audience, Great Lakes Now has the unique potential to raise awareness of water issues and inspire residents to value and protect this vital natural resource. With support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee will devote increased reporting capacity to cover more drinking water content. Detroit Public Television will also provide support to a partner station and will host a convening of Great Lakes journalists.

title: Great Lakes Now
description: Great Lakes Now is an initiative of Detroit Public Television that provides communities and residents with accessible, important news and information related to the health of the lakes, including water quality. Even as the Great Lakes provide astounding benefit to the region’s 40-million residents and the regional economy, many communities continue to grapple with the effects of aging infrastructure and pollution threatening the availability of safe and affordable drinking water. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, Great Lakes Now has grown dramatically and is now available in 20 markets through 31 stations. Previous support has also led to the creation of the Great Lakes News Collaborative with three other media outlets. With renewed support, the station will continue to grow its coverage of Great Lakes and drinking water issues and expects to collaborate with partners to produce and publish at least 250 articles this year.

title: Bridge Magazine Michigan Environment Watch
description: The mission of Bridge Magazine, a project of the Center for Michigan, is to inform Michigan residents through fact-based, nonprofit, nonpartisan journalism that identifies and reports on critical issues important to civic life. Michigan and the Great Lakes Basin are ground zero for some of the most pressing environmental issues of our time. As Michigan’s traditional newspapers decline, their ability to cover Great Lakes issues is also diminished. Meanwhile, Bridge Magazine and its Michigan Environment Watch segment are growing rapidly. This grant will increase awareness and understanding of the policies and practices that threaten the Great Lakes and the state’s drinking water supply through more in-depth journalism and collaboration with other partner organizations.

title: Bridge Michigan: Michigan Environment Watch
description: The mission of Bridge Michigan, a project of the Center for Michigan, is to inform Michigan residents through fact-based, nonprofit, nonpartisan journalism that identifies and reports on critical issues important to civic life. Michigan and the Great Lakes basin are ground zero for some of the most pressing environmental issues of our time. While Michigan’s traditional newspapers have declined, Bridge Michigan and its environment watch segment are growing rapidly. With previous support, the grantee was instrumental in working with three other news organizations in launching the successful Great Lakes News Collaborative. This grant will support Bridge Michigan as a key member of the collaborative and increase awareness and understanding of the Great Lakes and drinking water issues through more in-depth journalism.

title: Michigan Radio - The Environment Report
description: Michigan Radio at the University of Michigan is the most listened to public radio station in Michigan. The station’s Environment Report is hosted by one of its veteran and most respected reporters. In an era of cutbacks and closures among journalism establishments and growing public concern about cutbacks in enforcement of bedrock environmental protection laws, Michigan Radio fills an important need. With support from the Mott Foundation, Michigan Radio will boost its coverage of Great Lakes and drinking water issues, collaborate and share content with other grantees, and boost distribution through digital and social media platforms.

title: Michigan Radio - The Environment Report
description: Michigan Radio, the state’s premier public radio station, broadcasts over four stations in the Great Lakes State. The station’s Environment Report is an ongoing news segment that explores the relationship between the natural work and everyday lives of Michiganders. With prior Mott support, Michigan Radio expanded news coverage of Great Lakes and drinking water issues and became a leading member of the Great Lakes News Collaborative. With renewed support, the Environment Report will produce more original content on these topics for broadcast and digital media platforms. The University of Michigan will continue its active engagement with the Great Lakes News Collaborative, sharing content and coordinating story production.

title: Uniting Great Lakes Science, Data and Journalism
description: Circle of Blue is an online news publication covering water issues across the globe. The need for this grant is grounded in the challenge of raising awareness to effect changes in policy and action to better protect the Great Lakes and those who depend on them. With this grant, the grantee will integrate storytelling with science and data to better inform the region’s environmental policy and civic action. The project merges compelling journalism with historical and real-time data to engage and inform citizens, media and policymakers as they encounter new threats to Great Lakes water quality and equitable access to safe water for all.

title: Uniting Great Lakes Science, Data and Journalism
description: Circle of Blue is an online magazine covering water issues across the globe. A staff of award-winning and veteran reporters cover drinking water, Great Lakes and a range of other water issues and events. With prior Mott support, the grantee has been a founding member of the Great Lakes News Collaborative, a unique union of journalistic talent from four of the Great Lakes region’s most trusted content providers. The grantee helped raise awareness of household water debt and insecurity and the impacts of climate change on immigration within the region, among other stories. With renewed support, the grantee will continue to support and lead the collaborative and guide its team to uncover underreported and vital stories about the Great Lakes and drinking water.

title: Increasing Food Distribution
description: This grant will provide funds to Carriage Town Ministries to purchase food in order to serve meals to the homeless and those in need of food assistance who come to the shelter. The grantee provides important safety net services to individuals and families in the Flint area who are homeless or near homeless including food, safe and warm shelter, clothes, personal hygiene products, health services, employment training, and life skills courses.

title: Engaging Youth in Service
description: This grant will support Youth Service America to engage young people throughout the United States in quality youth-led service projects. The grantee will focus efforts to bolster youth engagement in Flint and Genesee County and across the United States by working with schools, nonprofit organizations and afterschool programs.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Kituo Cha Sheria Legal Advice Centre
description: The project goal is to increase access to justice for poor and marginalized people in Kenya. To this end, Kituo Cha Sheria Legal Advice Centre will work with a network of community paralegals to provide access to justice services, undertake strategic litigation, research relevant areas of justice provision and legal empowerment, monitor the implementation of alternative justice systems, and participate in regional and continental efforts to promote access to justice. Past grant support helped the grantee to ensure that Kenya includes two access to justice goals within its Open Government Partnership Action Plan, participate in activities of the African Centre of Excellence for Access to Justice, and provide justice services to poor and marginalized people in Kenya through the COVID-19 pandemic. With 48 years of experience, it provides justice services and addresses systemic injustices in Kenya, East Africa and Africa as a whole and is Kenya and East Africa’s oldest justice and legal empowerment organization.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Kituo Cha Sheria Legal Advice Centre
description: The organization’s goal is to increase access to justice for poor and marginalized people in Kenya. To this end, the Kituo Cha Sheria Legal Advice Centre will work with a network of community paralegals to provide access to justice services, undertake strategic litigation, research relevant areas of justice provisions and legal empowerment, monitor the implementation of alternative justice systems, and participate in regional and continental efforts to promote access to justice. Past support allowed the grantee to provide justice services to approximately 8,000 people and reach 1.5 million people in awareness-raising activities. The grantee worked with 400 community paralegals across 27 community justice centers. The Kituo Cha Sheria Legal Advice Centre is the oldest organization of its kind, having celebrated its 50th year of existence in 2023.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support the Citizens Research Council of Michigan, whose mission is to secure good government for the citizens of Michigan. Good government is a government that is representative of, and responsible and accountable to, the public; effective in carrying out its responsibilities and providing services; and efficient in the use of its resources.

title: 21st Century Community Learning Centers Summer Institute
description: This grant will provide funding to support a convening of the 21st Century Community Learning Centers held by Synergy Enterprises, Inc. in partnership with the U.S. Department of Education. The 21st Century Community Learning Centers Summer Initiative supports nearly 1.7 million children and youth in over 11,000 school-community afterschool programs across the country. The purpose of the annual Summer Institute is to provide afterschool administrators and staff with technical assistance and strategies to continue to enhance the quality of school-community afterschool programs.

title: Increasing CSA Engagement and Equity Through Behavioral Design
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant will enable Ideas42 to continue its support of the Foundation’s efforts to provide more young people with children’s savings accounts. For two years, the grantee and San Francisco’s Kindergarten to College program have worked together to understand barriers that families face in saving for college and design pilot solutions that leverage behavioral science to address these barriers. Continuing its partnership with Kindergarten to College, the grantee will support the program in refining high-level outreach designs for targeted populations, implementing them, and testing whether the designs have the desired effect with targeted populations. Through the recommended phases of this grant, Ideas42 will propose concrete strategies for use with underrepresented families to children’s savings accounts programs nationally.

title: Capacity Building
description: Michigan Community Capital is a nonprofit community development corporation which is also designated as a Community Development Finance Institution and a Community Development Entity by the federal government. The grantee funds community development real estate projects across the state. This capacity building grant will help increase the number of communities it serves, specifically looking to address needs in postindustrial and smaller urban communities like Flint.

title: Youth Recreation Landscape Scan and Playground Assessment
description: This grant will support Formative Evaluation Research Associates to conduct a youth recreation landscape scan and complete a playground assessment for Flint. There are two goals for the project: 1) assess existing youth recreation programming and provide recommendations for improvement; and 2) identify the resources needed to build, maintain, and replace playgrounds and play structures in Flint over the next 20 years.

title: Afterschool Education and Outreach Project
description: This grant will provide support to Collaborative Communications Group to continue to build the capacity of the 50 State Afterschool Network and the afterschool field in the areas of policy analysis, communications and research. To advance afterschool programs, this project will build bridges between local, state and federal governments and the afterschool field, and will assist the networks as they navigate new federal, state and local education policies impacting afterschool programs.

title: Capacity Building
description: This grant will support capacity building at the Genesee Intermediate School District. Funding will allow the grantee to recruit more students from lower income districts in career and technical education programs offered at the Genesee Career Institute. The Genesee Intermediate School District oversees the institute, which provides instruction and experiential learning in career areas that help prepare high school students for immediate entry into the workforce upon graduation or for moving into post-secondary education.

title: Equipment for Genesee Career Institute
description: Genesee Intermediate School District provides educational leadership and state-of-the-art learning opportunities for students and adults in Genesee County. In addition, the grantee’s focus on early childhood education, specialized schools and robust professional development programming enables them to offer educational programs and services that reach beyond the classroom to benefit the broader community. This grant will allow the grantee to purchase two pieces of equipment for students enrolled in the Health Sciences and Construction Trades programs at Genesee Career Institute. The equipment will fill the gap between classroom and hands-on skill development to enhance the curricula and promote learning.

title: Zillion Solutions Program Expansion
description: This grant will support expansion of the Zillion Solutions program at University of Michigan-Flint. Launched in 2017, Zillion Solutions is an annual pitch competition designed to get more students interested in entrepreneurship and innovation. The program is designed to generate participation across all academic units on campus including dual-enrolled high school students. The goal of program expansion is to help build a culture of entrepreneurship and innovation throughout the university.

title: Statewide Afterschool Network Support
description: This grant will allow the National Summer Learning Association to support the development, growth and sustainability of the statewide afterschool networks. Specifically, this grant will support the National Summer Learning Association to: 1) provide technical assistance to meet the needs of the statewide afterschool networks, particularly in light of COVID-19; and 2) provide sustainability training through an experiential learning series.

title: Financing Afterschool Program Models
description: This grant will support Augenblick, Palaich and Associates, Inc. to increase the afterschool field’s capacity and knowledge of school financing systems and the costs of afterschool program models. Specifically, this grant will support the grantee to: 1) develop a series of briefs on the impact of COVID-19 on school financing systems and school funding formulas; 2) provide technical assistance to statewide afterschool networks and other education grantees on school financing systems; 3) conduct a cost analysis and study of high-quality afterschool program models; and 4) develop a cost estimation workbook to estimate resources needed to implement high-quality afterschool programs.

title: Mizzen by Mott Content Development
description: This grant will provide support to Jazz at Lincoln Center to complete the development of content for Module 2 of the afterschool jazz curricula focused on jazz appreciation and youth development practices as a thematic partner with the Mizzen by Mott App. The completion of Module 2 will include Sets 1 and 2 with multiple interactive lessons as well as all audio and video components for Module 2. This grant will also support the marketing of the grantee’s jazz curricula to the afterschool field through a multimedia campaign in partnership with Foundations, Inc. to support the multiple rolling launches of the Mizzen by Mott App. The innovative content and partnership will support high-quality learning experiences for youth in afterschool programs.

title: 21st Century Community Learning Centers and Integrated Service Delivery Systems
