description: This grant will enable American Institutes for Research to continue their analysis of 21st Century Community Learning Centers and the impacts high-quality afterschool programs and summer learning initiatives have through the implementation of integrated service delivery systems to support positive youth, family and community development.

title: BOOST Conference
description: This grant will provide support for the Foundation for California Community Colleges’ Best-Out-of-School-Time annual conference scheduled for October 26-29, 2020. The Mizzen by Mott App will be showcased at the convening and throughout the year using targeted marketing strategies through virtual and live events. These events include a keynote presentation, interactive workshop experiences (virtual and live), marketing showcases and special events. These learning experiences for afterschool educators will expand their strategies and skill sets to enhance the quality of school-community afterschool programs.

title: National Service and Volunteer Center Capacity Building
description: This grant to the United Way of Genesee County will provide additional capacity to support service throughout Genesee County. National service members and volunteers provide critical resources to area nonprofits, government agencies and schools to help meet a variety of community needs such as blight elimination, neighborhood engagement, tutoring and mentoring.

title: Gateway to Youth Entrepreneurship Program
description: Since 1987, the Network for Teaching Entrepreneurship has held to the belief that entrepreneurship education has the power to open doors for youth in under-resourced communities. During this grant period, the grantee will continue to develop new strategies to further expand its youth entrepreneurship programming especially for young people in low-income communities through its BizCamps, which are designed to inspire students to pursue their future careers, including small business startups. Network for Teaching Entrepreneurship will also continue to provide technical assistance to the 50 State Afterschool Network infrastructure, as well as engage with Mizzen by Mott.

title: General Purposes
description: The Council of Michigan Foundations is a statewide association of over 300 grantmakers that provides its members with educational programs, technical assistance, networking opportunities, advocacy with policymakers and regulators, and collaborative work with leading national and regional philanthropic associations. Key themes for the grantee’s current work are: 1) advancing public policy; 2) cultivating the next generation of philanthropic leaders; 3) creating neutral space to have civic dialogue around hard conversations; and 4) supporting efforts that promote diversity, equity, and inclusion. A grant increase will enable the grantee to shift its business model to focus more on supporting and strengthening its core services. It will also allow the Council of Michigan Foundations to undertake a three-year “transformation plan,” which will substantively realign its strategies, program priorities, and resources for a stronger and more sustainable organization.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will allow the Afterschool Alliance to continue its efforts to ensure that young people and families—particularly those in underserved populations—will have access to engaging afterschool and summer learning and enrichment opportunities that inspire achievement in school and life. The grantee is playing a pivotal role in responding to challenges posed by the COVID-19 pandemic, serves as a critical voice and organizer of the field, works with federal policymakers to advance opportunities for afterschool and summer learning programs and ensures that the field’s lessons inform national education and youth policy initiatives. The grantee will continue to: 1) lead the field in meeting the needs of young people during the pandemic; 2) serve as an information source on afterschool programs and resource for policymakers, programs and educators; 3) be an effective voice in its efforts to expand quality afterschool programs and innovative models; and 4) increase access to research and data on the effectiveness of quality afterschool programs. The Afterschool Alliance will also work with the 50 statewide afterschool networks to support state-level afterschool initiatives and support the further development and implementation of the Mizzen by Mott App.

title: Greater Flint Urgent Relief Fund for Pandemic Response
description: The breadth and depth of the impact the coronavirus will have on the well-being of Flint and Genesee County is still evolving. Challenges will include the health and well-being of individuals, the capacity of nonprofits that support them, and the overall economic impact to the community. The Greater Flint Urgent Relief Fund for Pandemic Response, a project of the Community Foundation of Greater Flint, is designed to quickly coordinate and deploy resources to nonprofit organizations in the Greater Flint area that are working with communities disproportionately affected by the coronavirus outbreak.

title: European AI Fund: Capacity Building with European Civil Society
description: The project goal is to build a strong, informed and united civil society that can take part in policy debates on artificial intelligence and related digital technologies. Through this engagement, civil society actors will aim to enhance the benefits and minimize the risks of the digital transformation of society. To this end, civil society and digital rights funders will create a pooled fund within the Network of European Foundations. The fund will support the core capacity of digital rights nonprofits, outreach to key issue-specific nonprofits and their networks and specific collaboration and networking opportunities across the sector. During the grant period, the fund aims to make grants totaling more than $5.8 million. The Network of European Foundations is based in Brussels, Belgium.

title: Technical Assistance
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Whiting Auditorium and recently renovated Capitol Theatre are currently programs of the Flint Cultural Center Corporation. The Flint Cultural Center Corporation and the Flint Institute of Music have signed a Memorandum of Understanding that establishes terms and conditions under which the grantee will manage and operate the Whiting Auditorium and the Capitol Theatre while the possibility of a permanent consolidation is explored. This grant increase will provide continued consulting help and technical assistance for the due diligence period of exploration.

title: Technical Assistance
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Whiting and recently renovated Capitol Theatre are currently programs of the Flint Cultural Center Corporation. The Flint Cultural Center Corporation and the Flint Institute of Music have signed a Memorandum of Understanding that establishes terms and conditions under which the grantee will manage and operate the Whiting and the Capitol Theatre while the possibility of a permanent consolidation is explored. This grant increase will provide continued consulting help and technical assistance to complete the due diligence process and legal agreements.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to provide information and legal support to immigrants as they migrate into the United States. To this end, the Asylum Seeker Advocacy Project hosts online communities that provide real-time information and support as well as legal emergency rooms that allow asylum seekers to access legal aid without physically being with a lawyer. Additionally, the grantee advocates and litigates for a more equitable and just immigration system. Founded in 2015 as an all-volunteer effort, the grantee joined the Urban Justice Center in 2016 as a fiscally-sponsored project. In July 2019, the Asylum Seeker Advocacy Project became an independent 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: United States, Canada, Central America, Mexico
description: The program goal is to provide legal support to immigrants as they migrate from their home countries into the United States. To this end, Justice in Motion matches immigrants with experts in their network of lawyers and nonprofits that can provide legal support; trains lawyers on representing immigrants; advocates on behalf of immigrants in the United States, Mexico and Central America; and runs initiatives on longstanding and emerging issues facing immigrants. The grantee was founded in 2005 and was originally called Global Workers Justice Alliance, focusing on providing legal assistance and expertise to migrant workers. In 2016, the grantee changed its name to Justice in Motion and expanded its mission to include humanitarian immigration and civil rights work.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to provide information and legal support to immigrants as they migrate to the United States. To this end, American Gateways educates immigrants and the public on their legal rights, provides individualized technical assistance on cases and directly represents individuals in the immigration court system. Additionally, the grantee has been quick to respond to the needs of individuals in detention centers during the COVID-19 pandemic, providing virtual assistance. Founded in 1987, American Gateways provides quality, affordable and trustworthy legal services to the immigrant community in Texas.

title: School Transportation Study
description: The School Finance Research Collaborative was created to determine the true cost to educate a child from K-12. This grant will support the development of a white paper exploring school transportation methods utilized across the country.

title: Raising Michiganders' Standards of Living
description: Michigan Future, Inc. is a non-partisan, nonprofit organization whose mission is to be a source of new ideas on how Michigan can succeed as a world-class community in a knowledge-driven economy. This grant will support the grantee in their endeavor to raise the standard of living for all Michigan residents.

title: Strengthening New Development Bank Safeguards
grantee: Pontifical Catholic University Rio de Janeiro
description: The BRICS Policy Center is a project of the Pontifical Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro dedicated to studying the transformation in international development finance and its influence on social and environmental standards for energy development in South America and the Amazon. Over the past grant period, the think tank expanded its online databases that track Chinese investment in the region, researched the weakening of environmental governance in South America and organized knowledge exchanges. The Pontifical Catholic University Rio de Janeiro will continue over the next grant period to deepen monitoring and analysis of key financial institutions in the transition to a low-carbon energy future and the consequences for social and environmental governance.

title: Emergency Pandemic Food Distribution
description: The breadth and depth of the impact the coronavirus will have on the well-being of Flint and Genesee County is still evolving, but one of the most crucial needs is for the community’s most vulnerable residents to have adequate food during the peak of the outbreak. Through this grant, the Food Bank of Eastern Michigan will purchase food that will be delivered to porches or picked up at drive-through locations throughout Flint and Genesee County in order to meet that need.

title: Opening Justice
description: The project goal is to develop and expand justice commitments of governments participating in the Open Government Partnership. To this end, the grantee will assist its members in developing and adhering to commitments on justice within their national action plans for open government. To support this effort, the grantee will work with national governments and their civil society partners to identify innovative approaches to embed access to justice needs within governing practices. Further, the grantee will work with local partners to help build institutional support for justice. Finally, the secretariat will continue efforts to sustain a global “Coalition on Justice” to provide coordinated advocacy to advance access to justice. In 2020-21, the grantee produced a series of policy papers outlining strategies for adopting justice commitments. Member state commitments to open justice saw the highest impact on effective governance among all issues addressed through the partnership. The Open Government Partnership currently brings together 78 national governments, along with local government and civil society partners, to promote transparency, accountability and more responsive governance.

title: Opening Justice
description: The project goal is to develop and expand justice commitments of governments participating in the Open Government Partnership. This grantee currently brings together 78 national governments — along with local government and civil society partners — to promote transparency, accountability and more responsive governance. The grantee will work toward three key goals in 2024-25. The grantee will work to see that members are taking meaningful steps to build fair, accessible and accountable justice systems that resolve people’s problems effectively. The grantee will support member efforts to work with partners at the national, local and international levels to help mobilize expertise and political buy-in to support people-centered justice reforms. Additionally, the grantee will work to see that members are advancing concrete reforms to make justice systems that are open to public scrutiny, user-centered and that harness technology for innovation in this respect. In 2022-23, the partnership saw the number of justice commitments grow to 316 across more than 150 national open government action plans, making justice the leading subject area of open government commitments.

title: Data-Driven Progress for Access to Justice
description: The program goal is to produce new knowledge on legal needs globally. The World Justice Project will work along four key activity areas — data, research, policy and engagement — to strengthen the evidence base for people-centered approaches to justice reform. This will include carrying out legal needs surveys in over 25 countries, identification of proper sources and data-collection methods related to measurement of progress in addressing civil justice needs, creation of a policy tool identifying key obstacles to be overcome in implementing people-centered justice programs, and public engagement to promote wider support for people-centered justice reforms. In 2022-2023, the grantee produced a range of research and analysis, notably key reports to the United Nations High-level Political Forum assessing the current state of evidence underpinning justice reforms, and in particular, analysis around the viability of data sources to be used in measuring civil justice outcomes under Sustainable Development Goal 16. Established initially as a project of the American Bar Association in 2006, the World Justice Project was formally registered as an independent organization in 2009 working to advance the rule of law around the world.

title: Supporting Statewide Afterschool Networks
description: This grant will continue support for FowlerHoffman to provide comprehensive technical assistance to the statewide afterschool networks. Over the next two years, the grantee will focus on: 1) advising and supporting the 50 statewide afterschool networks to increase network sustainability and effectiveness, particularly in light of COVID-19; 2) assisting in the implementation of the assessment protocol for the statewide afterschool networks; and 3) supporting the implementation of the thematic partnerships and the Mizzen by Mott App. In addition, FowlerHoffman will continue to identify current opportunities for the statewide afterschool networks and make recommendations for how to advance afterschool programs and the networks for the future.

title: Capacity Building
description: Michigan Community Capital is a nonprofit community development corporation which is also designated as a Community Development Finance Institution and a Community Development Entity by the federal government. The grantee funds community development real estate projects across the state. This capacity building grant will help increase the number of communities it serves, specifically looking to address needs in post industrial and smaller urban communities like Flint.

title: Advancing Solutions to Water Affordability
description: There is growing concern in the Great Lakes region and across the nation about the rising cost of drinking water, the need to invest $1 trillion in upgrades in water infrastructure nationally over the next 25 years, and the burden this will place on low-income households. Elevate Energy has worked from its base in Chicago to address affordability issues in the energy and water sectors. With this increase, the grantee will assist the City of Flint in developing solutions for water affordability.

title: Neighborhood Murals
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide funds for the Flint Public Art Project to design and create murals in Flint neighborhoods. The murals provide a way to engage the community of Flint, beautify neighborhoods and support economic development. The grantee, which typically draws on local, national and international artists to paint murals, will feature the works of local and national talent over the next year in the wake of the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Home Ownership Improvement Loan/Grant Pool
description: Genesee County Habitat for Humanity constructs new and rehabilitates existing housing throughout Genesee County to provide low-to-moderate income individuals and families with affordable housing options. The grantee will provide home improvement loans and grants for city of Flint residents that own their homes.

title: Flint-area Nonprofit Organizational Assessment
description: This grant to the Nonprofit Network will support an organizational assessment of Metro Community Development, a longtime Foundation grantee. The goal of the assessment is to collect data that can help Metro Community Development evaluate whether or not the organization is making progress towards advancing its mission and achieving its goals. Additionally, once the assessment process is complete, Nonprofit Network will provide technical assistance, coaching and other strategic support to Metro Community Development.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide funds to Crossover Downtown Outreach Ministries to meet the food, clothing and personal care needs of families and individuals in Flint and the surrounding area. The ministry provided services to over 16,000 individuals in 2019 and has continued to adapt services in response to COVID-19. This general purposes grant will ensure that the services are available to those who need them as the grantee faces decreases in revenue and increases in expenses related to the pandemic.

title: Flint Diaper Bank
description: This grant will provide funds to the Food Bank of Eastern Michigan to support the Flint Diaper Bank program in providing diapers to low-income Genesee County residents. By utilizing the grantee’s sophisticated distribution system, the Flint Diaper Bank can ensure that diapers will reach the community’s most vulnerable families and help relieve the stress from choosing between supplying diapers for their babies or purchasing other basic necessities.

title: HVAC System Upgrades
description: This grant will support the purchase and installation of a new HVAC system for the Shelter of Flint. As the largest shelter in the county, the grantee serves some of the most vulnerable residents in the community. The current HVAC system is in need of significant repairs and is inefficient for the current size and usage within the building. Approximately 530 unduplicated individuals including many children spend 15,000 nights at the shelter each year.

title: Tutoring and Interpreter Services
description: The Latinx Technology & Community Center provides many programs and services to enhance the dignity and quality of life for the Flint and Genesee County Latino community as well as those from other cultures. The grantee will utilize Mott Foundation funds to support expanded tutoring and translation/interpreting services.

title: Accessible Baseball Field in Mundy Township
description: This grant will support the construction of the first accessible baseball field in Genesee County through a partnership between the Miracle League of Greater Flint and Mundy Township. The field, part of the Mundy Miracle Commons park in Mundy Township, also inspired the township to incorporate principles of increased accessibility throughout the park, including paths that accommodate motorized devices and a playground that will utilize universal design guidelines. This is the only such park in the region and partnerships with organizations such as the Genesee Intermediate School District, The Disability Network, Crim Fitness Foundation and Mass Transportation Authority will help ensure residents throughout the region can access this important recreational area.

title: Sk810 Skate Park Design and Implementation
description: This grant will support design and implementation of a poured-in-place concrete public skateboard park in Flint. Led by a group of local volunteers, the skatepark will offer a safe place for Flint residents to recreate. The skatepark will be constructed at the Swartz Creek Golf Course which currently houses a temporary skatepark and is located near several area schools. Once completed, the park will be the only established skatepark in Flint.

title: Adult Career Pathway Program
description: This grant will support Mott Community College’s Adult Career Pathway Program. The program will leverage many of the college’s existing educational and training programs to help connect unemployed adults, low-income workers and youth to employment and a career pathway. The goal is to ensure that area residents can enter and advance into higher-wage occupations in high-growth industries. Work experience and support services are integrated into the model and will enable participants to combine school and work, and advance in their careers over time.

title: Berston Field House Capacity Building
description: This grant will assist the United Way of Genesee County and the Friends of Berston Field House to sustain staff operations and increase organizational capacity in the areas of technology and fund development. Friends of Berston Field House’s mission is to impact the community through education, athletics, arts and comprehensive social services.

title: Downtown Blight Removal
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: The Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation is a supporting organization to the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation and a public charity that works to improve the quality of life of Flint residents. The grantee’s downtown revitalization efforts and investment in infrastructure provides people access to jobs, food, healthcare and other essential services. This grant will support the demolition of blighted structures and improved safety for downtown residents and college students living in the area.

title: Activist Education for Paralegals
description: The project goal is to increase the activism capacity of community paralegals to be able to advocate for systemic solutions to systemic injustices. To this end, the Tshisimani Centre for Activist Education will design and test a tailored training curriculum geared towards increasing activists’ capacity and building solidarity across nonprofits working in the justice sphere in South Africa. The grantee was established in 2015 with the mandate to assist activists in building their own capacities, using creative means to elevate injustices and seeking solutions to addressing them.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support the Center for Michigan in pursuing its mission of making Michigan a better place by encouraging greater understanding and involvement in policy issues among the state’s citizens and making sure their voices are regularly heard.

title: Medical Professional Housing during Pandemic
description: With the spread of coronavirus, Genesee County health workers are working unprecedented hours to address the needs of those in our community who have been infected during this pandemic. University of Michigan-Flint will provide doctors and nurses working at Genesee County hospitals a welcoming, safe, and convenient place to rest from their duties. The grantee will also provide an alternative for professionals who are concerned with possibly exposing family members to the virus.

title: Flint Restaurant Consortium for Healthcare Workers
description: The Freedom Center is located in Genesee County with many outreach programs that assist communities internationally. The grantee will be working to help purchase and deliver meals to local Flint area hospital workers during the coronavirus pandemic. The meals will be purchased from Flint restaurants.

title: Tools for Defending Environmental Defenders
geographic_focus: Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, Bolivia, South America
description: Founded in 1992, Land is Life is a nongovernmental organization working with a trusted network of indigenous leaders, communities and organizations in the greater Amazon and globally. With Foundation support, the grantee helps indigenous partners address the security threats to environmental defenders of indigenous lands and forests. This grant increase will allow Land Is Life to dedicate additional resources to activating and supporting their strong relationships with indigenous leaders and communities to prepare for and mitigate the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Flint Restaurant Consortium for Healthcare Workers
description: The Freedom Center is located in Genesee County with many outreach programs that assist communities internationally. The grantee will be working to help purchase and deliver meals to local Flint area hospital workers during the coronavirus pandemic. The meals will be purchased from Flint restaurants.

title: Legal Empowerment Basket Fund for Land and Environmental Justice
description: The project goal is to leverage financing for community justice and environment defenders in mining affected communities. Past support has helped Namati to undertake a feasibility study for an independent financing structure, supported by both private sector investors and development finance institutions. In addition, the grantee engaged more than 60 private sector stakeholders on the findings of the feasibility structure. The grantee also convened a working group of more than 20 civil society stakeholders in Africa, Asia and Latin America to identify key principles and recommendations for the design of an independent fund. Additional funding will help the grantee to support the establishment of a basket fund for community support during investment. The grantee will work with key stakeholders to design a financing mechanism that can cover the range of support communities need throughout the investment life cycle in affected communities. Established in 2011, Namati works to build a global movement of grassroots legal advocates who give people the power to understand, use and shape the law.

title: Legal Empowerment Basket Fund for Land and Environmental Justice
description: The project goal is to leverage financing for community justice and environment defenders in areas where their land is considered for largescale commercial purposes. Past Mott Foundation support has helped Namati to undertake research on the viability of a private fund to support community land and environmental justice. The grantee also engaged private investors on this, while building support for frontline justice actors to engage in various forums related to private financing. The grantee also created multiple opportunities to bring frontline justice actors together with industry leaders to develop principles for just carbon projects with credits. This grant will assist the grantee in strengthening its support network to call for private financing of frontline justice actors while creating new pathways for financing using carbon credits as an entry point. The grantee will continue to work with other organizations in holding the World Bank and its subsidiaries accountable for not investing in companies and projects that cause harm. Established in 2011, Namati works to build a global movement of grassroots legal advocates who give people the power to understand, use and shape the law.

title: Double Up Food Bucks Application Development
description: The Double Up Food Bucks program, which is operated by the Fair Food Network, has been critical to increasing access to healthy foods for families in Flint since 2011. Double Up Food Bucks allows families receiving supplemental nutrition assistance program benefits to double their available dollars for fruits and vegetables. The model has adapted over time depending on the current environment in Flint. During the Flint water crisis, the program expanded to reach more families with lead-mitigating foods and now the grantee is increasing program innovation due to the COVID-19 pandemic. This grant will support the development of an electronic application for enrollment in Double Up Food Bucks, thereby eliminating the need for an in-person appointment to enroll.

title: Technical Assistance
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Whiting Auditorium and recently renovated Capitol Theatre are currently programs of the Flint Cultural Center Corporation. Initially, the grantee and the Flint Institute of Music signed a Memorandum of Understanding that established terms and conditions under which the Flint Institute of Music managed and operated the Whiting Auditorium and the Capitol Theatre for a seven-month period, during which time the two organizations explored a permanent consolidation. This grant increase will provide support for consultants and technical assistance providers to help the grantee complete a full transition of operations from the Flint Cultural Center Corporation to the Flint Institute of Music, and for the grantee to complete and implement a new strategic plan.

title: General Purposes
description: Established in 1990, the National Council of Nonprofits is the nation’s largest network of nonprofits, representing more than 25,000 organizations across the country. The grantee’s mission is to advance the vital role, capacity and voice of charitable nonprofit organizations. The grantee works through its network of 44 state associations to help nonprofits operate more effectively, engage in critical policy issues affecting the sector and achieve greater impact in their communities. The grantee’s special focus is small and mid-sized groups that depend on it for free access to the timely information, policy analysis and applied advocacy they need to deliver their missions. The grantee has been at the forefront of public policy advocacy for the nonprofit sector, most recently leading the effort to include nonprofits in provisions of the Coronavirus Aid, Relief and Economic Securities Act. This grant increase will enable the National Council of Nonprofits to continue to lead on policy work by expanding its legal and communications capacity.

title: General Purposes
description: The project goal is to support landless and homeless communities to improve their living conditions. The Community Organisation Resource Centre achieves this goal by: 1) creating platforms for learning, connections and solidarity among and for homeless and landless communities; 2) supporting communities to collect data and profile their settlements to engage effectively with local government structures on improvements to the settlements; and 3) working with movements of slum dwellers to engage local, regional and national government. The grantee will work with the Federation of the Urban Poor and the Informal Settlement Network to engage effectively with government on the improvement of slums and broader service delivery, grow its savings programs to use as leverage for additional funding, and collect data to demonstrate the need to improve living conditions in slums. In addition, the Community Organisation Resource Centre will continue to connect the two movements to the international community of slum dwellers and support learning exchanges.

title: General Purposes
description: Established in 1990, the National Council of Nonprofits is the nation’s largest network of nonprofits, representing more than 32,000 organizations across the United States. The grantee’s mission is to advance the vital role, capacity and voice of charitable nonprofit organizations. The grantee works through its network of state associations and nonprofit partners to help nonprofits operate more effectively, engage in critical policy issues affecting the sector and achieve greater impact in their communities. During the previous grant period, the grantee championed, informed and connected the nonprofit sector. During the next grant period, the National Council of Nonprofits will focus on launching equity-centered programs, safeguarding nonprofit nonpartisanship and strengthening the member network.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to Independent Sector, a national membership organization which brings together a diverse community of changemakers at nonprofits, foundations and corporate giving programs working to strengthen civil society and ensure all people in the United States thrive. In the past two years, the grantee has: 1) released its second annual “Health of the U.S. Nonprofit Sector” report; 2) engaged over 1,000 sector leaders at the 2023 Upswell Summit; and 3) proposed and advocated for the Seat at the Table initiative. Over the next two years, the grantee will focus on nonprofit workforce and sector health, community building and public policy. Founded in 1980, Independent Sector currently has 453 organizational members and advances its mission by fostering a sense of belonging, catalyzing action and providing policy leadership across the full breadth of the charitable sector.

title: General Purposes
description: The Social Justice Initiative was established in 2013 to create awareness of the importance of social justice causes in South Africa. The grantee partners with philanthropists and civil society organizations to raise funds and support fair access to constitutional rights, better delivery of services and a stronger democracy. Past support enabled the grantee to unlock over $5 million from wealthy South Africans to support 80 social justice organizations and causes. In addition, the grantee generated interest and support for social justice programs from the private sector. This grant increase will enable the Social Justice Initiative to make grants to organizations dealing with social justice issues resulting from COVID-19 responses in South Africa.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Free State, Eastern Cape, Province of, Northern Cape, Province of, Western Cape, Province of the
description: The Social Change Assistance Trust works to improve the quality of life in poor communities by supporting community-based organizations working in those communities. The grantee was established in 1984 to make grants, provide training and facilitate sector-wide connections for organizations that promote access to justice, gender equality, youth empowerment and food security. Past support enabled the grantee to make grants totaling $230,000 to community advice offices and other local development agencies. In addition to providing institutional-strengthening support, the grantee provided training on gender-based violence. This grant increase will enable the Social Change Assistance Trust to provide additional funding to community advice offices and other local development agencies that are on the frontlines of providing an immediate response to the COVID-19 pandemic in rural communities.

title: General Purposes
description: The Black Sash Trust was founded in 1955 by a group of women who were fighting for the recognition of human rights for all in South Africa. The grantee’s aim is to contribute to the creation of a society that has effective laws and comprehensive social protection for the most vulnerable. Past and existing support assisted the grantee to successfully launch and execute initiatives based on systemic injustices faced by communities that needed help from community advice offices. Initiatives included the extension of social security to children up to 18 years, equalizing the pensionable age for men and women to 60 years, and more recently, the Hands Off Our Grants initiative. This grant increase will assist the Black Sash Trust to provide additional monitoring and support to document rights violations and successes in the execution of a COVID-19 relief grant by the South African Government.

title: Lead-free and Affordable Water in Michigan
description: The Water Center at the University of Michigan is a multi-disciplinary group of experts on Great Lakes and Michigan water issues. The team supporting the Water Center on this project includes Michigan State University’s Extension Service and an expert in lead contaminated public water systems. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the Water Center worked with the State of Michigan to develop a series of science-based fact sheets aimed at water suppliers and their customers, regarding the state’s new lead and copper rule that was approved in late 2018. The Water Center also evaluated the challenges that Michigan cities were facing on the need to maintain and improve infrastructure that supplies and treats water while facing a shrinking population and shrinking revenues. With renewed support, the Water Center will assist with outreach on lead safety materials developed previously and will work with utilities and other stakeholders to develop a deeper understanding of the breadth of the water affordability challenge facing Michigan cities. The results will lead Michigan utilities closer to solutions for delivering safe and affordable water in a financially sustainable manner.

title: Developing Community Foundations in Chile
description: The program goal is to support the emergence of community foundations in Chile. To this end, in 2021 the Community of Solidarity Organizations took on the role of a community foundation support organization. During the past nine months, the grantee: 1) learned from other regional and global support organizations; 2) met local leaders in various communities around the country; 3) worked with a communications firm to develop a Chilean narrative for community foundations; 4) hired staff to run a long-term program; and 5) developed a plan of action for the next several years. Over the next two years, the grantee will train, pilot and support various territorial initiative groups, leading to the establishment of at least three community foundations in Chile. Founded in 2008, the Community of Solidarity Organizations is a network of 240 nongovernmental organizations with a mission to build a community of strengthened and connected organizations that can influence the development of a just and sustainable society in Chile.

title: Developing Community Foundations in Chile
description: The project goal is to support the development of community foundations in Chile. Since late 2021, the Community of Solidarity Organizations has defined and promoted the concept of community foundations with Chilean philanthropy, civil society, academia, government and media. It has trained a team to execute a community foundation development program. After prospecting many possible locations, initiative groups were formed in three territories. The grantee will continue to stimulate the emergence of community foundations in Chile and strengthen those that come into being through technical assistance, seed and challenge grants, networking and learning resources. The grantee anticipates the formation of at least five community foundations in Chile over the next two years. Founded in 2008, the Community of Solidarity Organizations is a network of 260 nongovernmental organizations that support collaborative action to build a just, equitable and sustainable society in Chile.

title: Community Foundation Development in Austria
description: The project goal is to develop community foundations in Austria. To this end, Austrian National Foundations Association — Verband für gemeinnütziges Stiften — will: 1) increase the capacity of the project team to support community foundation development in Austria; 2) develop and publish community foundation-related learning resources; 3) support the establishment of at least four community foundations; and 4) identify new communities interested in establishing community foundations. The grantee will also raise additional resources for the project from local and national sources in Austria. During the past grant period, the Austrian National Foundations Association promoted the community foundation concept on the national and local levels, introduced 33 communities throughout Austria to the program, created a series of learning materials and provided capacity building to eight initiative groups interested in creating community foundations.

title: Remote Learning Technology during Pandemic
description: This grant will provide Flint Community Schools with funds to secure the technology required to efficiently and safely deliver educational content to its students in a remote learning environment. As a result of the coronavirus pandemic, schools have been closed, and it is uncertain when they might reopen. In the meantime, it is essential that students continue to have educational opportunities and social-emotional supports at home.

title: Community Philanthropy Development in Brazil
grantee: Institute for the Development of Social Investment
description: The project goal is to promote community philanthropy in Brazil. Since 2018, the Institute for the Development of Social Investment has worked to raise awareness and build knowledge about community foundations in Brazil. The grantee recruited and trained 10 initiative groups that registered new community foundations, supported three existing community foundations, and helped the formation of another five new initiative groups. The grantee also disseminated knowledge about community foundations and provided them with national exposure. Over the next two years, the grantee will continue to strengthen, promote and support the development of community foundations in Brazil through: 1) consultancy and mentoring; 2) networking opportunities; 3) study trips; 4) curated online information resources; 5) national exposure; and 6) matching grant funds. Founded in 1999, the Institute for the Development of Social Investment is a philanthropy service organization that inspires, supports and promotes strategic philanthropy and its impact, primarily in Brazil, but also throughout Latin America.

title: Community Foundation Development in Spain
description: The project goal is to develop community foundations in Spain. To this end, in 2020, the Spanish Association of Foundations launched a 10-year program to foster a strong and vibrant community foundation movement in Spain. Through this program, the grantee will: 1) develop at least 40 new community foundations, covering 50% of Spain’s territory; 2) create a national network of Spanish community foundations; 3) ensure that the community foundations adhere to internally developed quality standards; and 4) encourage the Spanish community foundations to play a leadership role in addressing the Sustainable Development Goals on the local level. During the next two years, the grantee will focus on promoting the concept of community foundations, developing new community foundations and strengthening their capacities and facilitating networking among community foundations on the national and international levels. During the past grant period, the Spanish Association of Foundations increased the capacity of the project team, publicized the community foundation concept, supported the most promising local initiatives to develop community foundations and facilitated the establishment of two new community foundations.

title: Community Foundation Development in Spain
description: The project goal is to develop community foundations in Spain. To this end, in 2020, the Spanish Association of Foundations launched a 10-year program to foster a strong and vibrant community foundation movement in Spain. Through this program, the grantee will work to: 1) develop at least 40 new community foundations, covering 50% of Spain’s territory; 2) create a national network of Spanish community foundations; 3) ensure that the community foundations adhere to internally developed quality standards; and 4) encourage the Spanish community foundations to play a leadership role in addressing the Sustainable Development Goals on the local level. During the past grant period, the grantee publicized the community foundation concept, supported local initiatives to develop community foundations and facilitated the establishment of two new community foundations, bringing the number of community foundations in Spain to nine. During the next two years, the Spanish Association of Foundations will focus on promoting the concept of community foundations, developing and strengthening new community foundations and facilitating networking among community foundations on the national and international levels.

title: Community Foundation Development in Zambia
description: The project goal is to develop community foundations in Zambia. To achieve this goal, the Zambia Governance Foundation will increase awareness of the community foundation concept in communities across Zambia and expand knowledge and understanding of the concept among key stakeholders and potential partners. In addition, the grantee will pilot fundraising initiatives to assess interest in communities and adapt the concept to the Zambian context. The grantee will develop a long-term strategy for developing community foundations and identify sources of income for the field in Zambia. The Zambia Governance Foundation was established in 2009 to strengthen the role of civil society in the national development process through grants, capacity development and information sharing. Over the years, the grantee has worked with communities to support their efforts to improve their quality of life.

title: Community Foundation Development in Zambia
description: The project goal is to develop community foundations in Zambia. To achieve this goal, the Zambia Governance Foundation will increase awareness of the community foundation concept in communities across Zambia. The grantee will also expand knowledge and understanding of the concept among key stakeholders and potential partners. Over the past two years the grantee has worked with communities to map their assets and identify opportunities to raise funds. In addition, the grantee has produced materials that are needed to support initiative groups to build the capacities they need to become community foundations. This grant will enable the Zambia Governance Foundation to deepen support to initiative groups in the communities identified, bolster local leadership on the community foundation concept and build support for community foundations nationally.

title: Community Foundation Development in Zambia
description: The project goal is to develop community foundations in Zambia. To achieve this goal, the Zambia Governance Foundation will deepen support to community foundation initiative groups and established community foundations in the country. This support will include creating stronger links between community foundations, potential partners and key stakeholders. Over the past two years, the grantee has supported the initiative groups to build community buy-in and ownership. In addition, the grantee has refined their community foundation development processes. This grant will enable the Zambia Governance Foundation to support community foundations to access external support and investors, build their capacity for financial assets, map community natural resources and build local leadership for community foundation work.

title: General Purposes
description: UK Community Foundations is a membership organization of 47 community foundations across the United Kingdom. The grantee has supported the development and expansion of community foundations over the years by providing technical assistance, training, data collection, research, marketing, financial assistance and advocacy. Over the next two years, the grantee will continue to focus on supporting and promoting its members to act effectively as community leaders, conveners and funders. The grantee will also support its network to engage meaningfully with the Sustainable Development Goals. The UK Community Foundations network has collectively granted more than £1 billion to local groups throughout the United Kingdom.

title: General Purposes
description: UK Community Foundations is a membership organization of 47 community foundations across the United Kingdom. The grantee has supported the development and expansion of community foundations over the years by providing technical assistance, training, data collection, research, marketing, financial assistance and advocacy. Over the next two years, the grantee will continue to focus on supporting and promoting its members to act effectively as community leaders, conveners and funders. The value of the community foundations’ collective endowment has grown from £815 million as of 2023 to £856 million in 2025.

title: General Purposes
description: The Derecho Ambiente y Recursos Naturales is a Peruvian nongovernmental organization focused on sustainable development and conservation of the Peruvian Amazon basin. Over the last grant period, the grantee implemented its strategic plan, made significant contributions to strengthening environmental and social policy at the Inter-American Development Bank and helped promote adherence to the Escazu Agreement, which will protect environmental defenders in Latin America. This grant renewal provides general purposes support to Derecho Ambiente y Recursos Naturales to develop and implement a new strategic plan beginning in 2023 and to build on the institutional gains achieved over the past five years.

title: Monitoring Infrastructure Investments in Argentina
location: Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires, Argentina
description: The Fundacion Ambiente y Recursos Naturales is an Argentina-based nongovernmental organization that has promoted sustainable finance and development through policy, law and civic engagement for 35 years. Over the previous grant period, the grantee made progress monitoring Chinese development finance compliance with safeguards and the World Bank’s financing of fossil fuel development in Argentina. Important contributions were made to strengthening environmental social governance of international and Chinese development finance. During this grant period, Fundacion Ambiente y Recursos Naturales will work with its partners to monitor and analyze the factors and financial actors shaping energy development and project selection in Argentina.

title: General Purposes
description: The project goal is to increase access to justice for poor and marginalized people in Kenya. To this end, the Legal Resources Foundation Trust will continue its work with the vision of building a just and equitable society in Kenya. Past support assisted the grantee in providing justice services, launching a justice radio station, and building a paralegal movement in Kenya. The Legal Resources Foundation Trust is a longstanding nonprofit organization in Kenya that addresses systemic and individual injustices on a daily basis.

title: General Purposes
description: The project goal is to increase access to justice for poor and marginalized people in Kenya. To this end, the Legal Resources Foundation Trust will continue in its efforts to contribute to a justice sector that is just, inclusive and responsive and protects, respects and fulfills the fundamental rights and freedoms of people in Kenya. It will continue to serve on the coordinating council of the Paralegal Society of Kenya and use various platforms to advocate for people-centered justice. Past support has allowed the grantee to provide justice services to approximately 28,000 people. It also provided training to over 400 community paralegals, while running an online radio station called Haki.fm. The Legal Resources Foundation Trust is a longstanding nonprofit organization in Kenya that addresses systemic and individual injustices on a daily basis.

title: STEM Fellowship
description: This grant increase to the STEM Next Opportunity Fund will support a second fellowship at the U.S. Department of Education, entitled the Afterschool and Summer Learning Fellowship. This fellowship is a public-private partnership initiative geared toward advancing high-quality afterschool and summer learning programs and will build upon the first fellowship established through this project, the Robert Noyce-Ellen Lettvin Fellowship in Informal Learning. This initiative will: 1) strengthen collaboration between the U.S. Department of Education and other federal agencies in the area of afterschool and summer learning; 2) work to advance evidence-based afterschool and summer learning programs, including the 21st Century Community Learning Centers program and initiatives established through the American Rescue Plan; and 3) work with leading researchers to identify priorities in afterschool programs, including identifying new tools, strategies and technical assistance that improve expanded learning opportunities.

title: STEM Institute
description: This grant to the STEM Next Opportunity Fund will support an institute focused for the Million Girls Moonshot key stakeholders, including the afterschool network STEM teams and funding, implementation and coalition partners. The institute will provide participants an opportunity to share best practices and emerging models, while working with national experts at the forefront of afterschool and summer STEM programming.

title: Matembwe-Ikondo Mini-Grid: Learning from the Past, Preparing for the Future
description: Providing sustainable energy for all is critical for 21st century socio-economic development. A key challenge for rural delivery of electricity is the expense and lack of financing for households to connect to the service. These barriers to connection make it difficult for off-grid renewable energy providers to grow their businesses and reach profitability. CEFA International Cooperation launched its first rural electrification project in 1986. The project is still thriving with expanded generating capacity and new businesses established because it is now a community-owned asset with the communities being served involved in its decisionmaking. With this grant increase, the grantee will work to further strengthen off-grid energy enterprises in the agriculture and public service sectors. The grantee will also use the additional funds to document and share the project’s successes in order to advance general understanding of off-grid energy’s benefits.

title: Shifting the Narrative: Addressing Africa's Energy Poverty Challenge
description: Access to affordable energy continues to be a major development challenge facing the world’s poor, particularly in Africa. If the right policies, financing, and incentives are in place, African-led micro-, small-, and medium-sized enterprises could create energy solutions that will yield economic benefits for their communities while not exacerbating climate change impacts. In respone, Oxfam America seeks to influence development finance institutions’ energy investments through integrated energy planning at the national level. With this grant increase, the grantee will deepen its work on such energy planning processes by promoting collaboration among clean energy advocates in developing countries.

title: Teen Reviewers and Critics Program
description: This grant will allow ArtsConnection to scale up and further expand and disseminate their arts afterschool programs through the statewide afterschool networks. Specifically, this grant will provide support for the grantee to: 1) create digital professional development modules for afterschool educators that include arts program content; and 2) develop an online youth alumni network to provide online mentorship opportunities for youth in the teen programs and to inform digital ArtsConnection programming nationally.

title: Detection and Protection for Environmental Defenders
description: Franciscan Solidarity Service is a Catholic association in Brazil that began working in 2018 on strategies to protect environmental social defenders living and working in the Brazilian rainforest. Over the past grant period, the grantee participated in the Life by a Thread campaign in three Brazilian Amazon regions under strong threat from deforestation and large-scale energy and infrastructure development. Franciscan Solidarity Service will — over the next grant period — make progress on developing community-based security protocols and expand the capacity of traditional and Indigenous community funds to ensure resources for protection programs.

title: BNDES and the Amazon
description: Founded in 1999, Mongabay.org is a nonprofit conservation and environmental news platform of original reporting in English, Indonesian, Spanish and Brazilian Portuguese. The grantee produces coverage of energy development and finance and its impacts on environmental and social sustainability in the greater Amazon. The COVID-19 pandemic has increased demand for high-quality journalism. This increase will support Mongabay.org staff to continue reporting on critical Amazon issues and respond to the increased communication demands resulting from the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: South America Small Grants Program
description: The Socio-Environmental Fund CASA is a grantmaking and capacity-building organization focused on providing small grants to strengthen local community, environmental and civil society organizations in Brazil. Strategic grassroots organizations and leaders are supported to work on sustainable energy development and finance. This grant increase will assist the grantee’s small grants program to provide emergency funds to manage issues related to the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: South American Regional Fund
geographic_focus: South America, Argentina, Ecuador, Colombia, Bolivia, Chile
description: Fondo de Mujeres del Sur is a grantmaking and capacity-building organization focused on providing small grants to strengthen community, environmental and civil society organizations. The grantee helps manage the South American Regional Fund to support local organizations and impacted communities working on issues of energy infrastructure and sustainable finance in South America. This grant increase will assist the grantee’s small grants program to provide emergency funds to manage issues related to the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Renewable Loreto
description: The Derecho Ambiente y Recursos Naturales is a Peruvian nongovernmental organization with offices in Lima and Iquitos, the capital of the Peruvian Amazon Department of Loreto. Over the last two years, the grantee brought off-grid solar energy and training to six communities in the Peruvian Amazon, strengthening forest protection, community resilience and economic activities. With this renewal grant, the grantee will expand the solar energy access, training and sustainability models to promote scaling up and replication of the model in Peru.

title: African American Small Business Restart Support
description: The Genesee Chamber Foundation is a supporting organization of the Flint & Genesee Chamber of Commerce. The grantee is organized to receive and administer funds for educational, scientific and charitable purposes, and for the public welfare of Genesee County. This grant will help support African American-owned businesses to reopen safely after the COVID-19 pandemic and contribute to the economic recovery of a low-income community.

title: Integration Investments and Indigenous Peoples in South America
description: For more than 40 years, the Indian Law Resource Center has been an important voice for indigenous peoples in the Americas and a source of legal expertise to improve policies, practices and accountability at national and international development finance institutions. Over the prior grant period, the grantee successfully advanced social and environmental safeguard review and implementation by the World Bank and Inter-American Development Bank. Major achievements include convincing the banks to apply whichever legal and policy standards — domestic or international — provide the best protections to indigenous peoples and the environment. Over the next grant period, the Indian Law Resource Center will build evidence to improve scrutiny and accountability of the banks, strengthen capacities to ensure full and proper implementation of environmental and social policy standards and harmonize new bank standards to best international practices.

title: Strategic Planning to Reopen K-12 Schools
description: This grant will provide support to the Council of Michigan Foundations to contract with an organization that will assist Michigan leaders with the development of a strategic plan to operationalize the reopening of Michigan’s K-12 schools in the continued midst of the COVID-19 pandemic. Reopening schools in a safe, equitable and efficient fashion will require a thoughtful plan as the virus remains a threat.

title: Emergency Operating Funds
description: The purpose of the Flint Downtown Development Authority is to correct and prevent deterioration in the downtown district, encourage historical preservation, create and implement development plans in the district, promote economic growth and redevelopment of the district and encourage the expansion of commercial enterprises in the downtown district. This grant will help support the grantee during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to help address the long-standing and emerging issues facing immigrants in the Americas. Alianza Americas’ mission is to bring about a more inclusive, equitable and sustainable way of life for under-served immigrant communities living in the United States, Mexico and Central America. The grantee accomplishes this through its action-driven diplomacy, network advocacy, educational delegations and tours, a leadership institute and mobile outreach supporting the caravans. The purpose of this increase is to enable the grantee to provide financial and technical support to Otros Dreamers en Accion (Other Dreamers in Action) in the publication, marketing and distribution of an e-book version of Maggie Loredo’s book, “Los Otros Dreamers.” Founded in 2004 by Mexican, Central American and Caribbean immigrant leaders, Alianza Americas is a network of over 50 members in 13 states, representing over 150,000 migrant families across the United States, with dozens of organizational partners in Mexico and Central America.

title: Advancing Entrepreneurship Education
description: This grant will support the Young Entrepreneur Institute at the University School located in Hunting Valley, Ohio. Founded in 2005, the institute partners with organizations throughout northeast Ohio to provide every young person with access to entrepreneurial education and experiences. The goals of this project are to increase the opportunities for young people to understand and experience entrepreneurship by infusing entrepreneurship into the 50 State Afterschool Network infrastructure and to increase engagement of regional ecosystems in youth entrepreneurship within under-served and under-resourced communities.

title: Paycheck Protection Program Technical Assistance
description: The Opportunity Resource Fund is a nonprofit community development financial institution certified by the United States Department of Treasury. As a community development financial institution, the grantee borrows money at reduced rates and re-lends dollars for small business loans, affordable housing and development of real estate and community facilities. This grant will allow the grantee to help small businesses and nonprofits in Flint and Genesee County secure Paycheck Protection Program loans authorized through the Coronavirus Aid, Relief, and Economic Security Act. Access to federal loans is important for economic recovery as businesses and workers try to overcome the affects of the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Youth Programming and Educator Training
description: This grant will support Youth Entrepreneurs, Inc. which is located in Wichita, Kansas. Founded in 1991, the grantee provides educators with entrepreneurship training, curriculum resources and support to provide entrepreneurship education and experiences for low-income youth. One goal of this project is to increase opportunities for young people to understand and experience entrepreneurship through the 50-state afterschool network. The second goal is to spread entrepreneurship programming into states and cities identified by Youth Entrepreneurs. The third goal is to provide professional development and training opportunities for out-of-school time instructors.

title: Statewide Afterschool Network Support
description: This grant will allow the National Summer Learning Association to support the development and sustainability of the statewide afterschool networks. Specifically, this grant will support the National Summer Learning Association to: 1) provide technical assistance to the 50 State Afterschool Network, particularly in response to the learning recovery needs of youth; 2) share best practices on afterschool funding models; and 3) significantly expand access to afterschool programs through American Rescue Plan funding and beyond.

title: YouthBuild USA Headquarters Relocation
description: This grant will support a continuing leadership transition and organizational transformation effort by helping YouthBuild USA move its headquarters from Somerville, Massachusetts, to the Roxbury neighborhood of Boston. The grantee believes the move will lead to several positive outcomes, including increased ability to attract and retain talent, opportunities for greater collaboration with mission-related organizations and deeper staff connections to a large population of program participants. The grantee was established in 1990 in East Harlem, New York, to provide education, counseling and job training opportunities to unemployed, disconnected youth. Today, YouthBuild USA has expanded to more than 250 sites in 48 states, plus more than 20 countries internationally.

title: Expanding Entrepreneurial Education
description: This grant will provide support to Lemonade Day to expand its programming to reach more youth with its entrepreneurial and whole child social-emotional approach. Specifically, this grant will support the grantee’s reach and impact by: 1) increasing access and opportunity for underserved youth to benefit from a curriculum highlighting business and life skills; 2) offering opportunities for the community to engage in youth entrepreneurship through mentoring, communications and business collaborations; and 3) engaging with the 50-state afterschool network in states outside of the grantee’s network. Lemonade Day will also contribute content to the Mizzen by Mott App.

title: Spotlighting Tapajos Hydro Development
description: Uma Gota no Oceano (A Drop in the Ocean) is a Brazilian strategic communications agency that develops narratives, using videos and information for print, broadcast and social media. The grantee develops media stories and videos and influences major media networks to cover stories related to energy development finance and its impacts on sustainability and affected communities. The grantee continues to build upon its successful media strategies to raise the public debate about key issues influencing sustainable energy development. The arrival of the coronavirus pandemic imposed a more difficult and challenging reality, which required additional staff to focus on this issue to ensure information reaches indigenous communities as well as for the voice of traditional peoples to reach the professional press. This grant increase will help support such coronavirus strategic communications work.

title: Sustainable Energy Finance and Development
description: The Juruena River is one of two important tributaries that flows into the vast Tapajos River in the Brazilian Amazon. It is home to numerous indigenous peoples and important biodiversity and freshwater resources. Operação Amazonia Nativa (Operation Native Amazon) has worked in the region for more than 50 years. This grant will support the grantee to map the actors promoting hydroelectric finance and development and monitor environmental and social impacts to strengthen safeguards for project finance.

title: International Program
description: Oil Change International has worked for nearly two decades to increase the transparency of international financial institution lending in the energy sector, ensuring that there is better data to inform policymakers. Over the prior grant period, the grantee’s work was pivotal in securing commitments from several development banks to align with international commitments on climate change and end public finance for fossil fuels by the end of 2022. The grantee’s data collection and analysis has significantly expanded the capacity of civil society to track implementation of this commitment and other public finance for fossil fuels. With this renewal grant, Oil Change International will continue its work in support of renewable energy and energy access.

title: Identifying Water Infrastructure Funding Options
description: Michigan faces a water infrastructure funding gap of approximately $800 million per year, covering wastewater, drinking water and stormwater. Closing this funding gap is imperative if Michigan is to meet its responsibility to citizens and the environment. The Michigan Environmental Council leads a collaborative project “Water for All Michigan” to research and analyze various funding solutions to address Michigan’s pressing water needs. The COVID-19 pandemic, its economic fallout and the federal, state and local government responses to the pandemic have made water infrastructure, water security and water equity issues more dynamic; and the potential solutions equally so. This grant increase will allow the grantee to incorporate this evolving landscape of challenges and opportunities into the overall project.

title: General Purposes
description: The Environmental Grantmakers Association receives general purposes support to implement its mission to promote just, effective philanthropy supporting harmonious relationships between people and the planet. Over the past grant period, the grantee completed and approved a new strategic framework, held a strategic planning process, and held two successful virtual retreats and other peer funder support activities. The Environmental Grantmakers Association will implement its new strategy framework and continue to provide important forums for grantmakers to network and discuss common goals.

title: Midland Flood Response Fund
description: The goal of this project is to support Midland in its efforts to recover from the collapse of two dams which resulted in significant flooding. To this end, the Midland Flood Response Fund at the United Way of Midland County was created to support the recovery efforts. The grantee was founded in 1920 and uses a collaborative and data-driven approach to positively impact the community.

title: Exploring Best Practice Models and Pathways for International Clean Energy Finance
description: The Vasudha Foundation undertakes research and analysis that will be used to inform and shift international financial institution investments in the energy sector. The grantee focuses on developing alternative models for renewable energy financing that can provide new pathways for international investments. With this grant increase, the grantee will continue to monitor the African Development Bank and the World Bank Group’s financing for energy infrastructure to developing countries. In particular, the grantee will focus on building collaboration between African countries and India, related to renewable energy investments and off-grid energy access solutions for Africa. The Vasudha Foundation will also collect data on such energy investments and delve deeper into some of the issues that will arise from the data collected.

title: Technical Assistance for Improved Teaching and Learning
description: This grant allows Michigan State University to support Flint Community Schools with technical assistance aimed at increasing district capacity, improving school culture, increasing operational efficiency and improving student academic outcomes. To achieve these goals, technical assistance will be focused on four primary components: districtwide systems, leadership development, classroom instruction and climate and culture. With this grant increase, the grantee will provide additional technical assistance around planning for the 2020-21 school year.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support the Center for Michigan in pursuing its mission of making Michigan a better place by encouraging greater understanding and involvement in policy issues among the state’s citizens and making sure their voices are regularly heard.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support the Center for Michigan in pursuing its mission of making Michigan a better place by encouraging greater understanding and involvement in policy issues among the state’s citizens and making sure their voices are regularly heard.

title: Accredited Vocational Paralegal Training
description: The project goal is to increase the capacity of community paralegals in South Africa. To this end, the North-West University will implement vocational training for community paralegals. This training will be accessible for paralegals working in advice offices throughout South Africa. Past support helped the grantee to launch this program and offer this training to 86 community paralegals across all provinces in South Africa. The training assisted paralegals to apply the law to their work and provided them with a certificate after an official assessment was done. The North-West University was established in 2004 when the former University of the North-West merged with the Potchefstroom University for Christian Education.

title: Accredited Vocational Paralegal Training
description: The project goal is to increase the capacity of community paralegals in South Africa. To this end, the North-West University will implement vocational training for community paralegals. This training will be accessible for paralegals working in advice offices throughout South Africa. Past support helped the grantee to deliver its six university-accredited modules to 483 community paralegals in South Africa. The training assisted paralegals in applying the law to their work and provided them with a certificate following an official assessment. North-West University was established in 2004 when the former University of the North-West merged with the Potchefstroom University for Christian Education.

title: Promotion of Paralegalism
grantee: International Commission of Jurists - Kenya Section
description: The project goal is to increase access to justice to poor and marginalized communities in Kenya. The International Commission of Jurists – Kenya Section does this by supporting its network of six community justice institutions, staffed by community paralegals. Prior support from the Mott Foundation helped the grantee: 1) strengthen its support to these networks; 2) increase the representation of community paralegals at important national taskforces and meetings on access to justice; and 3) register the former Paralegal Support Network of Kenya as an independent entity now called the Paralegal Society of Kenya. This grant will allow the grantee to continue supporting its network of community justice institutions, build capacity of paralegals on Kenya’s Alternative Justice System Policy and continue to tell the stories of community paralegals. The International Commission of Jurists – Kenya Section was established in 1959 and has a membership of more than 500 members of the Kenyan Bar and Bench.

title: Promotion of Paralegalism
grantee: International Commission of Jurists - Kenya Section
description: The project goal is to increase access to justice for poor and marginalized communities in Kenya. The International Commission of Jurists – Kenya Section does this by supporting its network of six community justice institutions, staffed by community paralegals. Prior support helped the grantee: 1) strengthen its support to these networks; 2) increase the representation of community paralegals at important national task forces and meetings on access to justice; and 3) serve as president of the Paralegal Society of Kenya. This grant will allow the grantee to continue supporting its network of community justice institutions, build capacity of paralegals on Kenya’s Alternative Justice System Policy and continue to tell the stories of community paralegals. The International Commission of Jurists – Kenya Section was established in 1959 and has a membership of more than 500 Kenyan jurists.

title: Supporting Statewide Afterschool Networks
description: This grant will support FowlerHoffman to continue providing comprehensive technical assistance to the statewide afterschool networks. Over the next grant period, the grantee will focus on: 1) advising and supporting the 50 statewide afterschool networks to increase network sustainability and effectiveness, particularly in light of COVID-19; 2) assisting in the implementation of the assessment protocol for the statewide afterschool networks; and 3) supporting the implementation of the thematic partnerships and the Mizzen by Mott App. In addition, FowlerHoffman will continue to identify current opportunities for the statewide afterschool networks and make recommendations for how to advance afterschool programs and the networks for the future.

title: COVID-19 Masks
description: The purpose of this project is to provide the Food Bank of Eastern Michigan with one million masks for redistribution to prevent the spread of COVID-19. The grantee will use its warehousing and distribution system to provide masks to organizations in Flint and Genesee County, including nonprofits, Flint City Hall and schools.
