Established in 1981, the Food Bank of Eastern Michigan solicits, stores and distributes food, either directly or through a network of more than 400 partner agencies in 22 counties.

title: COVID-19 Masks
description: The purpose of this grant increase is to provide the Food Bank of Eastern Michigan with one million masks for redistribution to prevent the spread of COVID-19. The grantee will use its warehousing and distribution system to provide masks to organizations in Flint and Genesee County, including nonprofits, Flint City Hall and schools. This increase is in addition to the one million masks that were previously provided and distributed to Flint and Genesee County organizations.

title: College Promise Campaign
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant will enable the College Promise Campaign at the Rockefeller Philanthropy Advisors to continue embedding children’s savings accounts into traditional college promise programs. Since 2017, the Mott Foundation has provided support to the campaign for its work to develop a College Promise-Children’s Savings Account integration network. In efforts to expand this network, the campaign is entering phase two of this work that will expand the network to more communities and improve the quality of integrated programming. Continued support will build on the activities initiated during the first phase of the College Promise-Children’s Savings Account project, which included networking, stakeholder engagement, outreach and strategic communications activities.

title: Building Support for Summer Learning
description: This grant will support the National Summer Learning Association in its efforts to increase access to high-quality summer learning programs across the country. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) support the statewide afterschool networks in developing summer learning opportunities for children and youth; 2) raise public awareness about the importance of summer learning; 3) support the ongoing rollout and promotion of the Mizzen by Mott app; and 4) educate and inform the field on best practices for summer learning.

title: Helping People Complete Higher Education
description: The goal of this project is to reengage former University of Michigan-Flint students who did not complete their education to return and finish their degree. The grantee will accomplish this by incentivizing students to return to school with nine free credits. In addition, the grantee will provide a personalized needs assessment, work plan and other supports throughout the returning student’s education. If successful, the University of Michigan-Flint will expand the project to be more inclusive, with the long-term goal of establishing a new college within the university for non-completers nationwide.

title: Teen C.E.O. Initiative
description: This renewal grant will provide support to Mott Community College for the Teen Creating Economic Opportunity Initiative. The goal of the project is to provide disadvantaged youth with a summertime opportunity to build their entrepreneurial business skills, explore higher education and investigate career pathways.

title: PBS Newshour Student Reporting Labs
description: This grant will provide support to the Washington Educational Telecommunications Association’s PBS NewsHour Student Reporting Labs to adapt journalism content focused on youth development practices and workforce skills as a premier partner with the Mizzen by Mott App. The curriculum will provide afterschool educators with easy to execute activities while developing youth voice and career exploration opportunities for youth. This grant will also support the engagement and marketing of the grantee’s Student Reporting Labs curricula to the afterschool field through a multimedia campaign to support the multiple rolling launches of the Mizzen by Mott App. This innovative content and partnership will support high-quality learning experiences for youth in afterschool environments and provide opportunities for youth to explore new career pathways.

title: Seeding the Community Foundation Movement in Chile
description: The project goal is to lay the groundwork for a community foundation movement in Chile. The Center for Philanthropy and Social Investment at the Adolfo Ibanez University will facilitate a three-phase learning journey with a group of stakeholders (foundations, social organizations, companies and community leaders) from Chile’s community philanthropy ecosystem. The aim is for the participants to fully understand the value of community foundations, identify the role different stakeholders can have in their development, establish a roadmap to promote community foundations and disseminate learnings from the process and the roadmap among a wider audience. Founded in 2015, the Center for Philanthropy and Social Investment is the first academic institution in Chile that promotes the culture and practice of strategic giving in Chile. The Center is part of the School of Government at the Adolfo Ibanez University, Chile’s leading private, non-profit university that was legally incorporated in 1988 with a mission to provide an education based on personal responsibility and freedom.

title: Community Foundations and United Ways
description: The project goal is to strengthen the capacity of community foundations to positively engage with other forms of community philanthropy. The Charles Stewart Mott Foundation Chair on Community Foundations at Indiana University’s Lilly Family School of Philanthropy, Dr. Laurie Paarlberg, is leading a study of the landscape of local community-based grantmaking, focusing on the characteristics and relationships between local United Ways and community foundations. This research will improve the understanding of the roles that both types of institutions play in local communities, identifying effective practices for strengthening relationships between institutions and laying the groundwork for future research on community grantmaking. A grant increase will allow for the study to be extended to include the examination of factors associated with the development of COVID-19 funds that are jointly supported by local United Ways and community foundations.

title: General Purposes
grantee: CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation
description: Established in 1993, CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation is an international alliance of more than 4,700 members in 175 countries. The grantee’s mission is to strengthen civil society and citizen participation throughout the world, especially in areas where participatory democracy and citizens’ freedom of association are challenged. Recent accomplishments include the hosting of a World Assembly and International Civil Society Week in Fiji in 2017, the release of annual State of Civil Society reports and maintaining the CIVICUS Monitor—a research tool to share reliable, timely data and analysis on civic space. This grant increase will support the grantee’s response to the COVID-19 pandemic by expanding its Solidarity Fund—a funding mechanism to support members with urgent programmatic and organizational costs. CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation’s main office is in Johannesburg, South Africa.

title: Capacity Building
description: This grant will support capacity building at the Genesee Intermediate School District. Funding will allow the grantee to recruit more students from lower income districts in career and technical education programs offered at the Genesee Career Institute. The grantee oversees the institute, which provides instruction and experiential learning in career areas that help prepare high school students for immediate entry into the workforce upon graduation or for moving into post-secondary education.

title: Infrastructure Improvements to Southwestern High School
description: With this grant, Flint Community Schools made infrastructure improvements to Southwestern High School including repainting hallways, repairing and replacing floor and ceiling tiles and repairing restroom facilities. This grant increase will allow the grantee to repair the parking lot at Potter Elementary School.

title: Legal Empowerment Learning Agenda
description: The Bernstein Institute for Human Rights at the New York University School of Law seeks to advance legal empowerment research both through the Legal Empowerment Lab and through collaborative research activities contained in a field-wide Shared Learning Agenda. The grantee will continue to support academics and grassroots practitioners jointly in participatory research methods in order to inform richer analyses of legal empowerment outcomes. A series of learning resources will be produced and specific research projects will be undertaken, all of which will actively feature practitioners and their beneficiary partners, including participants of the jailhouse lawyer initiative. Despite restrictions imposed by the COVID-19 pandemic, the grantee was able to hold 15 Learning Lab sessions, bringing together 28 participants from 15 countries. They also produced a series of handbooks on participatory research and legal empowerment practice. Additionally, the New York University’s Bernstein Institute for Human Rights virtually accompanied a range of practitioners in order to help better understand broader policy implications of their grassroots work.

title: Legal Empowerment Learning Agenda
description: The Bernstein Institute for Human Rights at the New York University School of Law seeks to advance legal empowerment research both through the Legal Empowerment Lab and through collaborative research activities contained in a field-wide Shared Learning Agenda. The grantee will continue to support academics and grassroots practitioners jointly in participatory research methods in order to inform richer analyses of legal empowerment outcomes. A series of learning resources will be produced and specific research projects will be undertaken, all of which will actively feature practitioners and their beneficiary partners, including participants of the Jailhouse Lawyer Initiative. In 2022-2024, 18 participants from 11 countries participated in intensive learning workshops and regular co-learning sessions with peers, generating new evidence around the effectiveness of legal empowerment strategies in combating injustices in widely disparate contexts.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Healthy Flint Research Coordinating Center, Inc.
description: This grant will support the Healthy Flint Research Coordinating Center, which was formed in 2016 and was created to better maximize health benefits from research conducted locally. With this grant, the grantee will help to further develop its programs, which coordinate research and prevent fragmented and duplicated work across universities and hospitals. An additional goal is to increase resident input and ensure ethical community involvement throughout the research process.

title: Program on Philanthropy and Social Innovation
description: The goal of this grant is to support, inform and maximize the impact of philanthropists, social investors and those they support through the Aspen Institute’s Program on Philanthropy and Social Innovation. The project’s primary activity is a yearly meeting of the Aspen Philanthropy Group—a group of foundation chief executives and selected strategic advisors. The project also organizes problem-solving working groups and roundtable discussions on critical topics to philanthropists, offers leadership development programming and partners with organizations to showcase leaders, programs and trends in philanthropy. Established in 1949, Aspen Institute is a leading U.S. think tank with an international network of partners that fosters values-based leadership and provides a neutral and balanced venue for discussing and acting on critical issues.

title: Advancing Renewable Energy Access in the Amazon
description: The Brazilian Institute for Consumer Defense is a large nongovernmental organization focused on ensuring all Brazilian citizens have access to essential goods and services and to social development, sustainable consumption and a healthy planet. Over the previous grant period, the grantee published five technical reports and held convenings with electricity distributors to strengthen the More Light for the Amazon federal program to bring renewable energy access to isolated communities in Brazil. Over the next project period, the grantee will launch a listening project to work with local Amazon communities to improve renewable energy access and examine energy subsidies that support dependence on diesel fuel in the forest.

title: Flint Cultural Center Academy Operating Support
description: This grant will provide funds to the Flint Cultural Center Foundation to assist the Flint Cultural Center Academy with operating support in 2020. The school’s budget is particularly challenged as a result of the financial implications from the COVID-19 pandemic. This support will help the school live up to its mission of serving students with high-quality educational opportunities including daily visits to the Flint Cultural Center institutions.

title: European AI Fund: Capacity Building with European Civil Society
description: The project goal is to empower a diverse and resilient ecosystem of civil society organizations that have the capacity and the resources to take part in policy debates on artificial intelligence and related digital technologies. Through this engagement, civil society actors will aim to enhance the benefits and minimize the risks of the digital transformation of society. To this end, a pooled fund within the Network of European Foundations will engage private funders and provide more than $4 million in grant support to digital rights and issue-specific nonprofits. During the previous grant period, 13 foundations contributed to the fund, which in turn supported 24 organizations with approximately $2.4 million in grants. The Network of European Foundations is based in Brussels, Belgium.

title: 50th Anniversary Capital Campaign
description: The goal of this project is to support the Association of Black Foundation Executives’ 50th anniversary campaign for which it seeks to raise $25 million over the next five years. Through this campaign, the grantee will raise funds to organize collective investments in Black communities, expand its philanthropic advising services, diversify its membership and improve its own internal capacity. Founded in 1971, the Association of Black Foundation Executives is a national membership organization of predominantly Black trustees and staff of private, community and corporate foundations.

title: Foundation Review Issue on Community Leadership and SDGs at Community Foundations
description: The program goal is to encourage community foundations to advance the Sustainable Development Goals at the local level. To this end, the Dorothy A. Johnson Center for Philanthropy at Grand Valley State University will publish a themed issue of its quarterly journal, “The Foundation Review”, which will focus on how community foundations and other place-based funders are using the United Nation’s Sustainable Development Goals as a part of their community leadership, grantmaking and evaluation work. The publication will be provided to print as well as online subscribers, with open access. Along with publishing the issue, the grantee will conduct a set of dissemination, training and agenda-setting conversations. Established in 1992, the Dorothy A. Johnson Center for Philanthropy is an academic center within the College of Community and Public Service at Grand Valley State University. “The Foundation Review” is the first peer-reviewed journal of philanthropy, written by and for foundation staff and boards and those who work with them.

title: General Purposes
grantee: World Affairs Council of Northern California
description: The goal of this project is to support the World Affairs Council of Northern California in its work to increase global connectivity and awareness. The grantee’s programmatic activities include the Global Philanthropy Forum and the Global Policy Forum, providing financial support and education to young people on global issues and hosting a radio show and podcast. The World Affairs Council of Northern California is a nonprofit, nonpartisan educational organization devoted to engaging the public in a discussion of the transnational issues of tomorrow.

title: Unlocking BNDES Operation Lifecycle
description: SITAWI Finance for Good is a Brazilian nonprofit organization founded in 2008 to mobilize research and capital for positive environmental and social outcomes. Over the past grant period, the grantee: 1) tracked fossil fuel and renewable energy investment by the Brazilian Development Bank; 2) began an analysis of social and environmental impacts and finance of oil and gas extraction in the Amazon; and 3) worked to strengthen safeguards at the bank. Over the next grant period, Sitawi Finance for Good will continue its bank monitoring activities, work toward incorporating new climate safeguards at the financial institution and publish its comprehensive report on the finance and impacts of Amazon oil and gas exploitation.

title: Identifying Promising Practices
description: This grant will continue to support the American Institutes for Research to increase evidence-based quality afterschool programs for young people. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) develop tools and resources to assist afterschool educators in cultivating “whole child learning” that addresses the social, emotional, and academic needs of young people; 2) support the afterschool field in developing new learning models as schools reopen, including blended and distance learning approaches; 3) provide ongoing technical assistance and up-to-date resources to the afterschool field; and 4) continue to work with the Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative to advance high-quality afterschool and summer learning programs, including addressing issues of racial equity in education.

title: Launch Flint Pitch Competitions
description: This grant will support the Ferris Wheel Innovation Center to organize and implement business pitch competitions in Flint. The grantee was established to help entrepreneurs in an economically disadvantaged community gain access to supports that advance their business or product ideas. Pitch competitions are a way to provide struggling entrepreneurs with the resources needed to move their concepts forward. Competition winners will receive financial resources, and all participants will receive mentoring from business professionals.

title: GAPS: Transition Program
description: This grant will enable Mott Community College to continue and expand the GAPS: Transition Program. The program, which is a dropout intervention strategy developed by Mott Middle/Early College High School staff, assists students in making the transition from middle school to the more rigorous middle/early college high school setting and then from high school into higher education. The program includes both summer and school year support for students as well as workshops for parents.

title: China-Latin America Sustainable Investments Initiative
description: The China-Latin America Sustainable Investment Initiative, a project of the Bank Information Center, works with partners in South America to monitor Chinese investment and strengthen voluntary Chinese guidelines for social and environmental standards, using best international practices. Over the previous grant period, the grantee published the first Spanish-language report on the China Development Bank and worked with nongovernmental organizations worldwide to urge China to adopt mandatory social and environmental standards for overseas investments, particularly in energy finance. This renewal grant will support the grantee to update its manual on Chinese social and environmental guidelines and support Latin American partners engaging on the impacts of Chinese development finance in the region.

title: Philanthropic Initiative for Racial Equity
description: The program goal is to increase the amount and effectiveness of resources aimed at combating institutional and structural racism in communities. The Philanthropic Initiative for Racial Equity will accomplish this by consulting with grantmakers on the application of a racial justice lens in their grantmaking; improving racial justice data defining, analysis and reporting; training organizations and identifying mechanisms for accountability, quality control and coordination on racial justice; educating foundation and philanthropy-serving organization trustees on racial justice; and partnering with organizations supporting increased global racial justice grantmaking. Founded in 2002 and hosted by the Tides Center, the Philanthropic Initiative for Racial Equity project is dedicated to combating racism through capacity building, education and the convening of grantmakers and grantseekers.

title: Expanding Entrepreneurial Education
description: Since 2006, Lemonade Day has aimed to prepare youth for life through critical teachings that bridge the gap from home to school and career. Working in over 90 cities in the last 15 years, the grantee has immersed 1.5 million kids into its entrepreneurial and experiential learning journey, earning over $352.5 million in sales, generating $270 million in profit and $142 million in donations. With renewed funding support, the grantee will continue to expand its programming to reach more youth with its entrepreneurial and whole child social-emotional approach. Specifically, this grant will support the grantee’s reach and impact by: 1) increasing access and opportunity for underserved youth to benefit from a curriculum highlighting business and life skills; 2) offering opportunities for the community to engage in youth entrepreneurship through mentoring, communications and business collaborations; and 3) engaging with the 50 State Afterschool Network in states outside of the grantee’s network. Lemonade Day will also contribute content to the Mizzen by Mott App.

title: Youth Programming and Educator Training
description: This grant will support Youth Entrepreneurs, Inc. d/b/a Empowered, which is located in Wichita, Kansas. Founded in 1991, the grantee provides educators with entrepreneurship training, curriculum resources and support to provide entrepreneurship education and experiences for low-income youth. Goals for this project include: 1) increasing opportunities for young people to understand and experience entrepreneurship through the provision of technical assistance and partnership with the 50 State Afterschool Network; 2) spreading entrepreneurial mindset programming into states and cities identified by Empowered; and 3) providing professional development and training opportunities for educators promoting entrepreneurship.

title: Entrepreneurial Ecosystem Engagement
description: This grant will support SIPI to implement Phase II of coordinating and aligning Flint’s nascent entrepreneurial ecosystem. The goals of Phase II are to: 1) create a shared vision for the ecosystem; 2) develop a strategy for effective coordination; 3) convene regular meetings with entrepreneurial service providers; 4) collaborate and host networking and meet-up events for local entrepreneurs; and 5) develop tools to enhance coordination and communication among entrepreneurial service providers, as well as current and prospective entrepreneurs.

title: Centering Equity at the Community Foundation of Greater Flint
description: The goal of this project is to build the internal and external capacity to work on racial equity at the Community Foundation of Greater Flint. The grantee has been building its capacity to work on these issues over several years, but the COVID-19 pandemic forced it to juggle multiple urgent priorities. The grantee plans to continue to address COVID-related issues, but will now prioritize racial equity through the appointment of a dedicated staff person to work on racial equity, further incorporating equity into its business model, implementing equity initiatives in the community and increasing local nonprofits’ understanding of structural racism.

title: Greater Flint Urgent Relief Fund for Pandemic Response
description: The breadth and depth of the impact COVID-19 will have on the well-being of Flint and Genesee County is still evolving. Challenges will include the health and well-being of individuals, the capacity of nonprofits that support them and the overall economic impact to the community. The Greater Flint Urgent Relief Fund for Pandemic Response, a project of the Community Foundation of Greater Flint, is designed to quickly coordinate and deploy resources to nonprofit organizations in the Greater Flint area that are working with communities disproportionately affected by the COVID-19 outbreak. This grant increase will provide additional support to the fund as COVID-19 remains a challenge.

title: General Purposes
description: The Food Bank of Eastern Michigan typically distributes approximately 30 million pounds of food annually throughout its 22 county service area. The grantee is also currently helping the community by distributing two million disposable masks in response to COVID-19. General purposes funding will assist with the overall operations of the Food Bank of Eastern Michigan during this period of increased demand for the kinds of services and supports the grantee lends to the community.

title: Advancing the Children's Savings Account Field
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: For over 40 years, Prosperity Now has focused on ensuring prosperity for all, as a leading intermediary on national research, practice and policy dedicated to financial stability and wealth. With continued Mott Foundation support since 1983, the grantee’s endeavors have significantly built the children’s savings account field. With renewed support, the grantee will continue to expand the children’s savings account field through championing efforts that strengthen and sustain children’s savings account programs. Prosperity Now is prepared to aid the field in maintaining its progressive momentum to support efforts that ensure that every child in America has a children’s savings account by 2025 through its technical assistance, research, networking and stakeholder engagement efforts at the national, state and local levels.

title: Identifying Promising Practices
description: This grant will continue to support American Institutes for Research to increase evidence-based quality afterschool programs for young people. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) identify current state and local systems supporting afterschool program quality; 2) provide ongoing technical assistance and up-to-date resources to the 50 State Afterschool Network and the afterschool field; 3) continue to work with the Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative to advance high-quality afterschool and summer learning programs, including addressing issues of racial equity in education; and 4) work with the Foundation to support future planning efforts to benefit the afterschool sector and the young people it serves.

title: PBS Newshour Student Reporting Labs
description: This grant will continue to provide support to the Washington Educational Telecommunications Association’s PBS NewsHour Student Reporting Labs to adapt journalism content focused on youth development practices and workforce skills as a premier partner with the Mizzen by Mott App. Specifically, this project will support: 1) adapting PBS journalism content to be hosted on Mizzen; 2) direct engagement with educators to supplement SRL curricula, including virtual office hours for Mizzen users and participation in afterschool conferences; and 3) providing marketing and promotional support of the grantee’s SRL curricula to the afterschool field through a multimedia campaign. This innovative content and partnership will support high-quality learning experiences for youth in afterschool environments and provide opportunities for youth to explore new career pathways.

title: General Purposes
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant provides general purposes support to Red Ink Flint. The grantee operates Flint Local 432, a performance venue located in downtown Flint for artistic programming and community convening. In 2020, 33 events took place, including local musical talent as well as regional and national acts, most of which were live streamed. Additionally, the grantee operates the Factory Two makerspace, which produced over 12,000 pieces of personal protective equipment for local organizations including hospitals and health care facilities. Funds will support organizational, administrative and programmatic costs for Red Ink Flint.

title: Anti-Dumping Initiative
description: With this grant, the City of Flint will implement an anti-dumping initiative aimed at restoring, protecting and preserving the city’s neighborhoods. Working alongside Flint residents and other invested community partners, the grantee will take a proactive stance against neighborhood blight, particularly the practice of dumping, and help restore pride in the community.

title: Blight Elimination and Neighborhood Stabilization
description: This grant will provide support to the Genesee County Land Bank Authority to engage in neighborhood revitalization activities around Kettering University, Durant-Tuuri-Mott Elementary school, Chevy Commons, Mott Park, the Flint River and Atwood Stadium. These activities will include property demolition, blight elimination, property cleanup, painting and home improvements. Demolishing properties is an important step in stabilizing the neighborhood.

title: Raising Awareness and Educating U.S. Community Foundations on the SDGs
description: The program goal is to encourage community foundations to advance the Sustainable Development Goals at the local level. To this end last year, the Kansas Association of Community Foundations prominently included content on the goals and their adoption by community foundations at its annual national Growing Community Foundations Conference. The grantee also added a module on the goals to its CFExpressTraining online resource. Over the next 16 months, the grantee will create a learning collaborative of five rural community foundations from Kansas that will work together to apply the goals in their communities. Progress and results will be shared at annual Growing Community Foundations conferences over the next three years. Founded in 2005, the Kansas Association of Community Foundations strengthens and promotes community philanthropy in Kansas, educates its members and others on effective philanthropic operations and fosters collaboration and the exchange of information regarding philanthropic programs and issues.

title: Economic Analysis of Lead Service Line Replacement
description: The Pediatric Public Health Initiative at Michigan State University will complete an economic analysis of the costs and benefits of lead service line replacement in Michigan. Concerns about the costs to municipalities of compliance with Michigan’s recent lead and copper rule have been raised. Over the past year, the new regulations and policy initiatives in Michigan and in other communities have resulted in groundbreaking new data quantifying lead in drinking water. Due to the new data being available, the grantee will use this grant increase to take advantage of the opportunity to evaluate and disseminate this new information for publication and manuscripts in peer-reviewed journals.

title: Mott Youth Entrepreneurship Fellows Program
description: The Hopewell Fund specializes in helping donors, social entrepreneurs and changemakers launch new, innovative social change projects. The grantee provides fiscal sponsorship and project incubation services that enable donors to execute their visions. Hopewell Fund will serve as the fiscal sponsor for the NextGen Chamber of Commerce on the Mott Youth Entrepreneurship Fellows Program. The fellows program is designed to ignite and grow the culture of youth entrepreneurship in Genesee County. In addition, the work will include policy roundtables that will bring together business, thought leaders and policymakers to explore policy barriers for youth entrepreneurs at the local, state and federal levels.

title: Oregon Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: Oregon Association for the Education of Young Children
description: This grant will support the Oregon Association for the Education of Young Children, which coordinates the Oregon State Afterschool Network, to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) build a stronger professional development infrastructure, with a focus on streamlined and accessible training; 2) deepen relationships with local education districts to expand access to responsive afterschool programming across Oregon; 3) work with education stakeholders and policymakers to design and implement education recovery funding to help Oregon youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen resources.

title: Mobile Student and Family Resource Center
description: The Genesee Intermediate School District will repurpose a school bus into a mobile resource and learning center to reach students and families in community locations. This will provide an expanded outreach opportunity to help education staff and families connect in a remote fashion particularly when school buildings are closed due to the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Maine Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the University of Southern Maine which coordinates the Maine Afterschool Network to expand access to high quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) increase the number of afterschool programs available for youth by seeking to expand community schools and establish a new Center for Community Schools in Maine; 2) enhance youth outcomes by launching a new statewide training program that addresses youth mental health needs in afterschool and summer learning programs; 3) work with education stakeholders and policymakers to design and implement education recovery funding to help Maine youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen resources.

title: Downtown Security
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant increase will provide additional support to the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation and its supported organization, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation. Funding will allow the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation to pay for around-the-clock security personnel to support safety and security efforts in downtown Flint. Additional security is needed to protect residents, infrastructure and consumer confidence in the city’s central business district.

title: Colorado Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Colorado Nonprofit Development Center which coordinates the Colorado State Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) increase the number of afterschool programs available for young people through increasing recruitment and retention of workers in afterschool programs; 2) enhance youth outcomes by providing statewide training on Colorado’s afterschool quality standards; 3) work with education stakeholders and policymakers to design and implement education recovery funding to help Colorado youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen resources.

title: Community Foundations Addressing Racial Equity
description: The Association of Black Foundation Executives will assist community foundations across the country to advance racial equity. The grantee will provide a series of learning opportunities and focused racial equity training for up to 40 community foundation staff and board members, equipping them with the shared knowledge, skills and tools needed to better understand the foundations of race, racism and racial equity. The grantee will develop templates for the creation of community “fact sheets” to organize data on racial inequities and potential solutions to address them and provide a summary report to share observations with participating community foundation leaders. In addition, the grantee will collect data from community foundations on the presence of Black donor-advised funds. Founded in 1971, the Association of Black Foundation Executives is a national membership organization of predominantly Black trustees and staff of private, community and corporate foundations.

title: Florida Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Florida Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) increase the number of afterschool programs available for young people through increasing recruitment and retention of afterschool program staff, including a new Out-of-School Time Fellowship Program; 2) enhance youth outcomes by developing and providing training programs on quality standards for summer learning programs; 3) work with education stakeholders and policymakers to design and implement education recovery funding to help Florida youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen resources.

title: New Hampshire Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: Southeastern Regional Education Service Center, Inc.
description: This grant will support the Southeastern Regional Education Service Center, Inc. which coordinates the New Hampshire Afterschool Network to expand access to high quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) increase the number of afterschool programs available for young people through advancing professional development and career advancement opportunities for afterschool program staff; 2) enhance youth outcomes by launching a career connected learning project to increase career development supports for young people; 3) work with education stakeholders and policymakers to design and implement education recovery funding to help New Hampshire youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen resources.

title: Development Finance for Community Environment and Justice Defenders in Southern Africa
description: The project goal is to increase financing for community justice and environment defenders from mining companies and development financing institutions in Southern Africa. To this end, the Southern Africa Resource Watch will workshop its toolkit developed for governments, corporations, development finance institutions, civil society and communities in applying the best financing principles for environment and justice defenders in Southern Africa. The grantee will also continue to engage the African Development Bank and the International Council of Mining and Metals on financing and grievance mechanisms for injustices and rights violations. Past support helped the grantee to research mining companies’ financing practices in the Democratic Republic of Congo, Mozambique, South Africa, Zambia and Zimbabwe. Based on this research, the grantee developed a toolkit to assist in the better application of financing practices. The Southern Africa Resource Watch is a regional nonprofit organization that promotes the transparent and accountable use of natural resources in Southern Africa.

title: Development Finance for Community Environment and Justice Defenders in Southern Africa
description: The project goal is to increase financing for community justice and environment defenders from mining companies and development finance institutions in Southern Africa. To this end, the Southern Africa Resource Watch will pilot the implementation of its toolkit on community-grievance redress mechanisms in selected communities in South Africa, Zimbabwe, Zambia and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The toolkit allows communities to negotiate financing for their institutions and embeds the principle of free, prior and informed consent. The grantee also plans to use community foundations as an entry point in piloting the implementation of the toolkit. Past support allowed the grantee to research mining companies’ financing practices in the Democratic Republic of Congo, Mozambique, South Africa, Zambia and Zimbabwe. Based on this research, the grantee developed a toolkit to assist in applying better financing practices. The grantee also raised awareness about the toolkit. The Southern Africa Resource Watch is a regional nonprofit organization that promotes the transparent and accountable use of natural resources in Southern Africa.

title: Tennessee Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the United Ways of Tennessee which coordinates the Tennessee State Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) increase the presence of youth voice in afterschool programs across the state through a youth advisory council and programming that empowers youth as change agents; 2) expand partnerships in rural communities, the business community and across state agencies to increase access and quality of afterschool programming across Tennessee; 3) work with education stakeholders and policymakers to design and implement education recovery funding to help Tennessee youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen resources.

title: North Carolina Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: Public School Forum of North Carolina
description: This grant will support the Public School Forum of North Carolina which coordinates the North Carolina State Afterschool Network to expand access to high quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) develop regional networks within North Carolina to support staff professional development, build partnerships and better respond to the needs of local youth; 2) leverage local and statewide partnerships to advance afterschool program quality standards across North Carolina; 3) work with education stakeholders and policymakers to design and implement education recovery funding to help North Carolina youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen resources.

title: South Carolina Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the South Carolina Afterschool Alliance, which coordinates the South Carolina State Afterschool Network to expand access to high quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) develop partnerships to address youth mental health challenges through training for afterschool professionals and creating mental health career pathways for youth; 2) build sustained support for mental health services for youth and families by aligning state and local resources and educating the public through strategic communications; 3) work with education stakeholders and policymakers to design and implement education recovery funding to help South Carolina youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen resources.

title: Impacts of Investments of the Brazilian National Development Bank on Regional Sustainability
description: The Instituto Socioambiental is a Brazilian nonprofit organization focused on integrated solutions to environmental and social challenges in the Amazon region. Over the previous grant period, the grantee worked with local partners and Indigenous people to develop an important alliance to monitor the impacts of large-scale development and ensure compliance with social and environmental standards by the financiers operating or proposing high-risk projects along with the Xingu River basin. Over the next grant period, the Institute will monitor cumulative social and environmental impacts, provide technical support to local communities and develop communications strategies to protect the basin.

title: State Priorities Project
description: The State Priorities Project is a national network of over 40 state organizations that leverage state budget and fiscal analysis in order to advance poverty alleviation policies and programs. This recommendation partially supports the Alaska Children’s Trust’s efforts to formally join the national network and establish a project in Alaska. Specifically, Mott Foundation funding will enable the grantee to: 1) build a coalition of partners to create and guide the new project; 2) educate nonprofit leaders and other stakeholders about the importance of participation in Alaska’s budget and tax policy debates; and 3) strengthen the grantee’s organizational outreach and communications capacity. Based in Anchorage, Alaska Children’s Trust is a nonprofit organization that works statewide to prevent child abuse and neglect.

title: Wisconsin Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: Marshfield Clinic Research Institute, a Division of Marshfield Clinic, Inc.
description: This grant will support the Marshfield Clinic, which coordinates the Wisconsin State Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) augment professional development practices to address youth mental health challenges through training for afterschool professionals; 2) undergo a rebranding initiative to expand the network’s reach to youth-serving programs, educate the public on the role of afterschool and build new partnerships; 3) work with education stakeholders and policymakers to design and implement education recovery funding to help Wisconsin youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen resources.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to provide an enabling environment for nonprofits, philanthropy and civic participation by promoting and protecting the freedoms of association, expression and assembly. To this end, this grant increase will allow the International Center for Not-for-Profit Law to scale up its work on protecting peaceful assembly in the United States. The grantee is based in Washington, D.C.

title: Missouri Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the University of Missouri, Columbia, which coordinates the Missouri Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) increase the number of afterschool programs available for young people by providing comprehensive professional development and workforce supports for the afterschool field in Missouri; 2) enhance youth outcomes by leading a bi-state initiative to build additional afterschool opportunities in the Greater Kansas City metro area; 3) work with education stakeholders and policymakers to design and implement education recovery funding to help Missouri youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen resources.

title: Supporting College and Career Readiness in Afterschool
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant will provide support to the Michigan College Access Network to administer technical assistance coaching and professional development to state afterschool networks implementing college and career readiness initiatives for afterschool programs. This grant will build the capacity of network leads and staff to create new strategies, partnerships and high-quality learning experiences to assist youth and families with navigating post-secondary barriers. The high-quality learning opportunities created will better prepare youth and families for a successful college experience through financial education, college affordability planning and college and career exploration.

title: College of Innovation and Technology
description: This grant will provide funding to the University of Michigan–Flint for the development and implementation of the College of Innovation and Technology. This new college will address the growing demands of industry and the expressed interest of students. It will be the second of its kind in Michigan and will fill a critical gap among higher education options for the engineering and technology field, combining the best characteristics of a liberal arts degree with those of a technical degree.

title: Children's Facility: Expanding Health and Wellness in Flint
description: Genesee Health System will provide support for the construction of a new purpose-built facility to house its children’s mental health and integrated medical care program areas in one building. Families will be able to access a variety of services in one place, including comprehensive neurological evaluations, case management and community programs that are vital to children and families in the Flint region. These services are crucial to addressing the mental and behavioral health challenges of children in the community, particularly following the Flint Water Crisis and the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Afterschool & Summer Recovery and Opportunity Fund
description: This grant will support the Grantmakers for Education to administer a pooled fund supporting the afterschool field in the wake of COVID-19. The fund, entitled the “Afterschool & Summer Recovery and Opportunity Fund” will support the afterschool and out-of-school time sector by: 1) stabilizing afterschool intermediary organizations; 2) assisting the field and programs to develop robust remote learning approaches; 3) development of reopening and recovery strategies; and 4) coordinating participating funders to leverage impact and opportunities on behalf of children, youth and families during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Remote Learning Technology Support
description: This grant increase will provide Flint Community Schools with funds to secure the technology required to efficiently and safely deliver educational content to its students in a remote learning environment. As a result of the COVID-19 pandemic, schools have been closed and it is uncertain when they might reopen. In the meantime, it is essential that students continue to have educational opportunities and social-emotional supports at home.

title: Texas Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: Texas Partnership for Out of School Time
description: This grant will support the Texas Partnership for Out of School Time which coordinates the Texas Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) work with Network partners to advance a comprehensive system of afterschool and summer learning programs in Texas; 2) develop a statewide evaluation and continuous improvement system to support quality afterschool and summer learning programs; 3) work with education stakeholders and policymakers to design and implement education recovery funding to help Texas youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen resources.

title: Idaho Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Jannus, Inc. which coordinates the Idaho State Afterschool Network to expand access to high quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) empower youth to inform resource and program development to address youth mental health challenges in Idaho; 2) enhance youth outcomes by expanding access to Idaho’s afterschool quality standards and professional development resources; 3) work with education stakeholders and policymakers to design and implement education recovery funding to help Idaho youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen resources.

title: General Purposes
description: The European Foundation Centre is an independent membership association of foundations and corporate funders dedicated to promoting organized philanthropy in Europe and internationally. The grantee provides intellectual leadership on emerging policy agendas and societal trends that will impact institutional philanthropy, fosters connections within philanthropy and with external actors and provides a voice for European institutional philanthropy. This grant increase will support efforts to increase and facilitate closer collaboration with other European philanthropy infrastructure organizations that advance similar goals and engage in related activities.

title: Education and Economic Development Initiatives
description: This renewal grant provides partial support for the Genesee Area Focus Fund and its supported organization, the Flint & Genesee Group, to deliver economic development and education and training services to the Flint area and build Flint’s economic resilience to recover from the Flint water crisis and COVID-19 pandemic. The Group increases business investment, job creation and industry diversification through business retention, expansion and attraction activities, as well as entrepreneurial support services. The Group also enhances the region’s economic competitiveness and quality of life by providing workforce education and training programming across all age levels, and by engaging in special initiative projects with strategic partners.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will allow the Afterschool Alliance to continue its efforts to ensure that young people and families — particularly those in underserved populations — will have access to engaging afterschool and summer learning and enrichment opportunities that inspire achievement in school and life. The grantee is playing a pivotal role in supporting youth during the COVID-19 pandemic, serves as a national leader for the afterschool field, works with federal policymakers to advance opportunities for afterschool and summer learning programs and ensures that the field’s lessons inform national, state and local education and youth policy initiatives. The grantee will continue to: 1) lead the field in meeting the needs of young people during the pandemic; 2) serve as an information source on afterschool programs and resource for policymakers, programs and educators; 3) be an effective voice in its efforts to expand quality afterschool programs and innovative models; and 4) increase access to research and data on the effectiveness of quality afterschool programs. The Afterschool Alliance will also work with the 50 State Afterschool Network to support afterschool expansion through the American Rescue Plan and other state and local afterschool initiatives.

title: Neighborhood Development Capacity
description: The Local Initiatives Support Corporation’s mission is to forge resilient and inclusive communities of opportunity across America – great places to live, work, visit, do business and raise families. This grant will support the creation of a construction apprenticeship program as well as create a redevelopment strategy for vacant property.

title: Afterschool Youth Entrepreneurship Initiative
description: This grant to Children’s Forum will enable the Florida Statewide Afterschool Network to: 1) expand opportunities for young people to learn about and experience entrepreneurship in existing afterschool, STEM and summer learning programs; 2) connect with local, regional and state entrepreneurship organizations to help integrate entrepreneurship into afterschool and summer learning programs; and 3) partner with organizations such as chambers of commerce, businesses, career technical education and higher education to expand successful entrepreneurship models in communities of high need.

title: Afterschool Youth Entrepreneurship Initiative
description: This grant to Louisiana Tech University will enable the Louisiana Statewide Afterschool Network to: 1) expand opportunities for young people to learn about and experience entrepreneurship in existing afterschool, STEM and summer learning programs; 2) connect with local, regional and state entrepreneurship organizations to help integrate entrepreneurship into afterschool and summer learning programs; and 3) partner with organizations such as chambers of commerce, businesses, career technical education and higher education to expand successful entrepreneurship models in communities of high need.

title: Afterschool Youth Entrepreneurship Initiative
grantee: Texas Partnership for Out of School Time
description: This grant to the Texas Partnership For Out of School Time will enable the Texas Statewide Afterschool Network to: 1) expand opportunities for young people to learn about and experience entrepreneurship in existing afterschool, STEM and summer learning programs; 2) connect with local, regional and state entrepreneurship organizations to help integrate entrepreneurship into afterschool and summer learning programs; and 3) partner with organizations such as chambers of commerce, businesses, career technical education and higher education to expand successful entrepreneurship models in communities of high need.

title: Afterschool Youth Entrepreneurship Initiative
description: This grant to the Nebraska Children and Families Foundation will enable the Nebraska Statewide Afterschool Network to increase the quality and sustainability of afterschool programs across the state. This grant will support the network to: 1) continue to expand opportunities for youth to learn about and experience entrepreneurship in afterschool and summer learning programs; 2) strengthen entrepreneurial ecosystems; and 3) connect and align ecosystem partners to expand learning opportunities and create pathways to entrepreneurship.

title: Afterschool Youth Entrepreneurship Initiative
description: This grant to the Healthcare Collaborative of Greater Columbus will enable the Ohio Statewide Afterschool Network to increase the quality and sustainability of afterschool programs across the state. This grant will support the network to: 1) continue to expand opportunities for youth to learn about and experience entrepreneurship in afterschool and summer learning programs; 2) strengthen entrepreneurial ecosystems; and 3) connect and align ecosystem partners to expand learning opportunities and create pathways to entrepreneurship.

title: Afterschool Youth Entrepreneurship Initiative
description: This grant to the Central Susquehanna Intermediate Unit will enable the Pennsylvania Statewide Afterschool Network to increase the quality and sustainability of afterschool programs across the state. This grant will support the network to: 1) continue to expand opportunities for youth to learn about and experience entrepreneurship in afterschool and summer learning programs; 2) strengthen entrepreneurial ecosystems; and 3) connect and align ecosystem partners to expand learning opportunities and create pathways to entrepreneurship.

title: Afterschool Youth Entrepreneurship Initiative
description: This grant to the Wyoming Community Foundation will enable the Wyoming Statewide Afterschool Network to increase the quality and sustainability of afterschool programs across the state. This grant will support the network to: 1) continue to expand opportunities for youth to learn about and experience entrepreneurship in afterschool and summer learning programs; 2) strengthen entrepreneurial ecosystems; and 3) connect and align ecosystem partners to expand learning opportunities and create pathways to entrepreneurship.

title: Illinois Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Metropolitan Family Services which coordinates the Illinois State Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) increase the number of afterschool programs available for young people through increasing recruitment and retention of workers in afterschool programs; 2) enhance youth outcomes through emphasis on equity in professional development and program accessibility and design; 3) work with education stakeholders and policymakers to design and implement education recovery funding to help Illinois youth recover and thrive; 4) Work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen resources.

title: Hawaii Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the University of Hawaii which coordinates the Hawaii State Afterschool Network to expand access to high quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) increase the number of afterschool programs available for young people through increasing recruitment and retention of workers in afterschool programs; 2) enhance youth outcomes by providing statewide training on Hawaii’s afterschool quality standards; 3) work with education stakeholders and policymakers to design and implement education recovery funding to help Hawaii youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen resources.

title: Servall Building Redevelopment
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will provide funding to the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, a supporting organization of the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, for the redevelopment of the former 1st Source Servall Appliance Parts building located at 630 W. Kearsley Street. The building and adjacent properties will be redeveloped into the new headquarters for the nonprofit Flint River Watershed Coalition and its Kayak Flint rental program. The project furthers the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation’s charitable mission of improving and revitalizing downtown to address the blight and economic stagnancy that has plagued Flint in recent decades.

title: Genesee County Youth Career Academy
description: Founded in 1976, Peckham, Inc., is a nonprofit community rehabilitation organization that provides job training and competitive employment opportunities for people with disabilities. The grantee operates 30 rehabilitation and human services programs in Michigan and has satellite manufacturing locations in Arizona and Kentucky. In 2019 the grantee expanded its apparel manufacturing operations to the Flint area. This grant will provide support for the Genesee County Youth Career Academy to help reduce recidivism, improve social functioning and increase job skills training for at-risk, court-involved youth.

title: Grassroots Legal Empowerment Fund
description: The Fund for Global Human Rights will establish and operate a 10-year, $100 million Legal Empowerment Fund to support grassroots legal actors focused on ensuring access to justice for marginalized and vulnerable communities around the world. The grantee will seek to draw support from a variety of public and private donors and use these resources to provide long-term organizational support for the field. Specifically, the project will support groups to invoke the law, regulations and policies to access justice; organize and take collective action to reform the legal framework to provide better protections for communities; and generate and share learning both on best practices in the application of legal empowerment strategies as well as on adaptation and developing new approaches. The grantee will also attract more funding and influence funding practices to prioritize long-term flexible support to grassroots groups. Established in 2002, the Fund for Global Human Rights is a public foundation that works to advance human rights globally by providing frontline activists, organizations and movements around the world with funding, technical assistance and opportunities for national and transnational organizing. Additional information about the Legal Empowerment Fund can be found at http://www.legalempowermentfund.org.

title: Arkansas Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Arkansas State University System Foundation which coordinates the Arkansas Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) increase the number of afterschool programs available for young people through implementing statewide professional development programs, including a new leadership institute for afterschool providers; 2) enhance youth outcomes by establishing an Arkansas Youth Voice and Opportunity Corp to involve youth in the development of future afterschool programs; 3) work with education stakeholders and policymakers to design and implement education recovery funding to help Arkansas youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen resources.

title: Montana Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the School Services of Montana which coordinates the Montana Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) expand the number of afterschool programs available for young people in Montana by supporting a state policy and practice agenda with Network partners; 2) develop a coordinated state model among the juvenile justice and afterschool sectors to better support at-risk youth; 3) work with education stakeholders and policymakers to design and implement education recovery funding to help Montana youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen resources.

title: Coalition for Human Rights in Development Community Resource Exchange
description: The Coalition for Human Rights in Development is a global network of nongovernmental organizations, housed at Social and Environmental Entrepreneurs; working to mitigate the social and environmental impacts of large-scale infrastructure and energy finance. This grant will support the coalition to build and implement a pilot Community Resource Exchange to develop and connect talented professionals and organizations to share skills, tools and resources with and among communities seeking to defend their rights in the context of development investments. Over time, the collective capacity and evidence base developed by the exchange will help to transform development finance and the international investments system to be more responsive to community needs and environmental sustainability.

title: Ensuring Development and Climate Finance Support Sustainable Development
description: The COVID-19 pandemic has impacted the way development finance institutions engage with affected communities and civil society organizations. It has also surpassed expectations in its severity and impact globally and presents challenges to development and climate finance to build back better. This grant increase will support the Center of International Environmental Law to work with the multilateral development banks to define the best standards for participation, expose and confront efforts to exploit the pandemic to avoid public scrutiny for controversial projects and lay the foundation for long-term transformation around development finance decision-making.

title: COVID-19 Justice Rescue Fund
grantee: Hague Institute for Innovation of Law
description: Through its Justice Accelerator, the Hague Institute for Innovation of Law has supported a portfolio of 110 justice startups since 2011 of which 75 are successfully operational in 2020. These startups provide critical services needed in the current and post COVID-19 era: help with domestic violence, access to welfare schemes, legal services for small and medium-sized enterprises, crime prevention and much more. The grantee will operate a one-million Euro, time-limited, COVID-19 Justice Rescue Fund, a program open to all its 75 Accelerator alumni, consisting of grants to support short-term expenses for operational continuity as well as training to ‘pivot’ these startups to improve their product/service, team, revenue and impact for the (post) COVID-19 era. A rigorous selection process will determine which alumni meet the criteria and get to participate. Established in 2006, the Hague Institute for Innovation of Law works to find innovative solutions to justice problems around the world.

title: COVID-19 Grassroots Justice Fund
description: The COVID-19 Grassroots Justice Fund is intended as a short-term response to help fill the immediate financing gaps faced by grassroots justice defenders as they seek to meet the growing consequences of inequality and injustice spurred by the pandemic. The project aims to help these frontline workers save lives and address the escalating, intertwined health, economic and justice crises confronting communities around the world. This grant will help shore up grassroots justice organizations and innovative grassroots approaches that are vital in addressing the immediate justice challenges of vulnerable communities and the financial challenges hitting empowerment groups. The grantee, working in partnership with Namati and other justice actors, will administer and distribute responsive grants to address immediate needs. Based in Washington D.C., the Fund for Global Human Rights has distributed over $100 million to community-based rights organizations around the world.

title: Michigan Justice Fund
description: This grant will support the Community Foundation of Greater Flint and its partnership with the Michigan Justice Fund, a collaboration of Michigan philanthropic organizations. The project seeks to increase equitable justice across the state through data analysis, coalition building, policy research and is currently focused on reducing inequalities impacting individuals reentering society after incarceration. This grant will be used to fund groups and organizations in the Flint area that are working with returning citizens through the Community Foundation of Greater Flint.

title: Nonprofit Census and Mapping Initiative
description: The goal of this project is to map Michigan nonprofits led by Black, Indigenous or people of color and evaluate their needs. To this end, the Michigan Nonprofit Association will partner with data gathering organizations, including the Johnson Center at Grand Valley State University and Data Driven Detroit, to locate the appropriate nonprofits, which will then be verified through 990 filings, grantee membership data, Fluxx database systems, desk research and surveys. The grantee will also conduct a needs assessment of organizations surveyed to better serve their specific needs. The grantee will focus on areas with high densities of nonprofits. Founded in 1992, the Michigan Nonprofit Association serves the nonprofit sector statewide by providing information and access to resources that can assist organizations in operating effectively, fulfilling their missions and efficiently meeting community needs.

title: Media Literacy and Journalism Content for Afterschool Programs
description: This grant will enable the Pulitzer Center to develop and promote diversity, equity and inclusion; media literacy; and journalism content for afterschool programs. The final content, which will be distributed on the Mizzen by Mott app, will include lesson plans and activities designed to engage young people on global issues that foster curiosity and critical thinking. To help ensure quality delivery of the content, the grantee will create professional development resources for afterschool educators, including workshops, webinars and teaching tips. Based in Washington, DC, the Pulitzer Center works to raise awareness of underreported global issues through direct support for quality journalism across all media platforms and to provide a unique program of education and public outreach.

title: Community Resource Hub for Safety and Accountability
description: The New Venture Fund is the fiscal sponsor for the Community Resource Hub for Safety and Accountability project. The project’s long-term goal is for all people to have access to resources and tools to advocate for systems change and accountability in law enforcement, and ultimately, to create a better, more fair and effective system of law enforcement. During 2021, the grantee will support groups working to advance safety and law enforcement accountability in their communities by: 1) providing a clearinghouse of research and best practices; 2) providing technical assistance to groups active on police accountability issues; and 3) convening organizations for shared learning. Based in Washington, D.C., the New Venture Fund incubates and hosts projects and also provides tools and other supports that accelerate the impact of hosted projects.

title: Racial Equity Roundtable
description: The goal of this grant is to support the Community Foundation of Greater Flint in its leadership of and work within the Greater Flint Coronavirus Taskforce on Racial Inequities. Led by the grantee, the taskforce is a partnership of nonprofits, health experts, government and businesses who came together to address the health and economic racial inequities that are apparent in the wake of COVID-19. The taskforce will support equitable public policy, health and economic initiatives and community-focused diversity, equity and inclusion training.

title: Youth Mentorship Community of Practice
description: This grant will support Mott Community College to pilot the Youth Mentorship Community of Practice project. The two-year pilot is designed to provide leadership and financial support to five Black-led mentorship groups that serve youth in the Flint-area. In addition to leadership capacity-building, the project will promote higher education and workforce opportunities for youth participating in each of the five mentoring programs.

title: Human Relations Commission
description: The City of Flint will utilize this grant to reestablish the Human Relations Commission to help reduce discrimination and increase mutual understanding among Flint residents.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: New York, Ontario, Michigan, Illinois, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Minnesota, Indiana, Ohio
description: Freshwater Future is a regional organization that is a catalyst for community action to strengthen policies and safeguard the waters of the Great Lakes region. Since its inception in 1996, with significant support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has provided over $4 million in grants and technical assistance to grassroots groups around the Great Lakes basin. This grantee fills a critical niche in the Great Lakes community as an organization solely dedicated to supporting individuals and communities working to protect land and water resources. This grant increase will be available for the organization’s general purposes, including an initiative to secure equipment for a community lab in Flint, Michigan to test for PFAS, a chemical contaminant found in water.

title: Michigan Statewide Broadband Planning
grantee: Michigan Association of Intermediate School Administrators
description: The Michigan Association of Intermediate School Administrators will lead an initiative aimed at achieving digital inclusion and equity for residents across Michigan. Phase one of this work includes an assessment of the current status of internet connectivity and the development of a comprehensive plan to leverage public and private partnerships to connect all Michigan residents to broadband service. While this has long been an important issue, it is particularly relevant as Michigan’s children shifted to a remote learning environment as a result of COVID-19, laying bare the stark inequities in sufficient internet access.

title: FEMA Map Update
description: The City of Flint will develop a Federal Emergency Management Agency Letter of Map Revision request to support the Flint Riverfront Restoration Project. This project focuses on the main channel of the Flint River, between the Grand Traverse Street Bridge and the upstream limits of the City of Flint at Carpenter Road, including portions of the tributaries.

title: Beirut Humanitarian Aid Response
description: American Near East Refuge Aid is facilitating and supplying critical shipments of medical equipment as well as capacity building support to the hospitals and health centers in Beirut, Lebanon following a devastating explosion in a warehouse at the city’s port. This grant will provide funds as part of the humanitarian aid response to the people impacted by this disaster.

title: Telemedicine and Remote Services for the Uninsured
description: This grant to the Genesee County Free Medical Clinic will provide equipment such as laptops and software to deliver telemedicine services to its uninsured clients. All Genesee County residents are encouraged to conduct non-emergent appointments via telehealth during the COVID-19 pandemic. Grant funds will also support staffing for services to clients during the pandemic such as alternative food distribution and pharmacy services.

title: General Purposes
description: Afterschool Alliance works to advance opportunities for afterschool and summer learning programs and ensures that the field’s lessons meet national, state and local education and youth policies. The grantee will continue to: 1) lead the field in meeting the needs of young people in the wake of the pandemic; 2) serve as an information source on afterschool programs and resource for policymakers, programs and educators; 3) be an effective voice in its efforts to expand quality afterschool programs and innovative models; and 4) increase access to research and data on the effectiveness of quality afterschool programs while playing a pivotal role in supporting youth to recover from the COVID-19 pandemic. This grant will allow the Afterschool Alliance to continue its efforts to ensure that young people and families — particularly those in underserved populations — have access to engaging afterschool and summer learning opportunities.
