The Afterschool Alliance will also work with the 50 State Afterschool Network to support afterschool expansion through the American Rescue Plan and other federal, state and local afterschool initiatives.

title: Facility Upgrades
description: The purpose of this grant increase is to provide Whaley Children’s Center with essential facility upgrades that will directly affect the children who live there. The grantee is a residential treatment facility for children ages 5-17 who have lived in various foster homes and have experienced some sort of trauma. There are a variety of programs and strategies offered that allow staff to build a comprehensive treatment plan for each individual child based on their specific needs. This is the only facility of its kind in Genesee County, making it an invaluable asset to the community and the children who need it most.

title: General Purposes
description: The Global Fund for Community Foundations was established to support and promote community philanthropy around the world. The grantee focuses on supporting the development of community foundations and other community philanthropy organizations as essential institutions in the broader civil society sector that advance the well-being of communities on the edges of society. It makes grants, provides technical support and builds knowledge and evidence on the importance of people-centered and community-led development. Past support enabled the grantee to make grants to more than 52 organizations in 32 countries, support the development of these local institutions in emerging economies and promote community philanthropy as an approach to development among funders and other development aid audiences. This grant increase will contribute towards a fund that supports community foundations and other community philanthropy organizations to work in their communities on the immediate and longer-term response to COVID-19.

title: Youth Ambassadors Program
description: This grant to WOW Outreach will support the Youth Ambassadors program. The goal is to provide opportunities for Flint’s most challenged young people to establish hope and belief in their ability to succeed and live a happy, prosperous life. Established in 2007, the grantee’s mission is to generate conversation that ignites action and collaboration among youth, families and the community to give hope to those living in historically disinvested communities.

title: Mizzen Innovation Project
description: This grant will allow After-School All-Stars to help support and inform the expansion of the Mizzen by Mott App. Specifically, this grant will provide support for the grantee to: 1) test and support the ongoing development of the app; 2) create content; and 3) assist with professional development resources.

title: Expanded Learning for K-12 Students
grantee: Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint
description: The Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint will expand their programming for students from the Flint area by providing a safe, welcoming and nurturing environment as they attend school remotely in response to COVID-19. The grantee will provide academic, enrichment, recreation and social-emotional supports to students during the school day and afterschool hours. This will be a tremendous benefit to students and their families as they continue to adapt to the changing landscape brought about by the pandemic.

title: Expanded Learning for K-12 Students
description: The Sylvester Broome Empowerment Village will expand their programming for Flint area students by providing a safe, welcoming and nurturing environment as they attend school remotely in response to the COVID-19 pandemic. The grantee will provide academic, enrichment, recreation and social-emotional supports to students during the school day and afterschool hours. This will be a tremendous benefit to students and their families as they continue to adapt to the changing landscape brought about by the pandemic.

title: Support for Special Projects
description: The goal of this grant is to support the Community Foundation of Greater Flint in building its capacity for special community projects in the Flint community. To accomplish this goal, the grantee will be hiring a dedicated staff person who will work closely with the Chief Executive Officer to provide him with both operational and administrative support.

title: Expanded Learning for K-12 Students
description: The Evergreen Community Development Initiative will expand their programming for Flint students by providing a safe, welcoming and nurturing environment as they attend school remotely at the Flint Development Center in response to COVID-19. The community center will provide academic, enrichment, recreation and social-emotional supports to students during the school day and the afterschool hours. These services will be a tremendous benefit to students and their families as they continue to adapt to the changing landscape brought about by the pandemic.

title: Berston Field House Expanded Learning for K-12 Students
description: This grant to the United Way of Genesee County will expand programming for Flint area students at Berston Field House by providing a safe, welcoming and nurturing environment as they attend school remotely in response to COVID-19. The community center will provide academic, enrichment, recreation and social-emotional supports to students during the school day and afterschool hours. This will be a tremendous benefit to students and their families as they continue to adapt to the changing landscape brought about by the pandemic.

title: Zillion Solutions Program Expansion
description: This grant will support expansion of the Zillion Solutions program at University of Michigan-Flint. Launched in 2017, Zillion Solutions is an annual pitch competition designed to get more students interested in entrepreneurship and innovation. The program is designed to generate participation across all academic units on campus including dual-enrolled high school students. The goal of program expansion is to help build a culture of entrepreneurship and innovation throughout the university.

title: Zillion Solutions Program Expansion
description: This grant renewal will support the continuation and refinement of the Zillion Solutions program at University of Michigan-Flint. Launched in 2017, Zillion Solutions is an annual idea competition created to increase student interest in entrepreneurship, innovation and/or problem solving. The program is designed to generate participation across all academic units on campus, including dual-enrolled high school students. The goal of the program is to help build a culture of entrepreneurship and innovation throughout the university.

title: Advancing the Sustainable Development Goals in Puerto Rico
description: The program goal is to support community foundation efforts to play a leadership role in helping their communities to address the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. The Puerto Rico Community Foundation will integrate its Community Capitals programmatic framework with the Sustainable Development Goals and align a diverse set of key institutional stakeholders in Puerto Rico around these goals. This will advance social justice and equity and build community wealth. The grantee will develop a set of indicators, gather relevant data and present the findings in a public dashboard and a local version of a Vital Signs report. The grantee will then organize roundtables aimed at developing strategic collaboration to address the goals and promote strategies that could lead to a Voluntary Local Review by Puerto Rico’s government. Founded in 1985, the Puerto Rico Community Foundation promotes and strengthens social justice and equitable access to community resources on the island of Puerto Rico.

title: Flint Dangerous Tree Removal
description: The Genesee Conservation District partners with the City of Flint to maintain over 26,000 street trees. This grant will support the removal of dangerous trees throughout Flint. All of the street trees in the city have been assessed and those that pose a safety risk have been identified for removal. The grantee will work closely with neighborhood organizations and residents to provide information about this initiative and to educate residents about the many benefits of a healthy urban canopy.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Indiana, Ohio, New York, Minnesota, Wisconsin, Pennsylvania, Michigan, Illinois
description: Founded in 1970, as the Lake Michigan Federation, the Alliance for the Great Lakes seeks to conserve and restore the Great Lakes freshwater ecosystem through policy reform, public education and local conservation projects. With Mott support, the grantee has engaged in policy discussions around aquatic invasive species and the Great Lakes Restoration Initiative, delivered public education and outreach programs and implemented organizational development strategies. This grant increase will be available for the organization’s general purposes, including efforts to adjust to the challenges posed by COVID-19.

title: Take Action Campaign
description: The Groundwork Center for Resilient Communities, based in Traverse City, promotes sustainable systems in food, energy and transportation with a focus on the northwestern section of Michigan’s lower peninsula. The grantee has launched a fundraising campaign to increase its impact in the medium-term and stabilize the financial foundation of the organization in the long-term. This Mott grant is an early contribution to the campaign.

title: Construction - College of Innovation and Technology
description: This grant will provide $2.2 million to the University of Michigan-Flint to support construction costs for the new College of Innovation and Technology facility. The College of Innovation and Technology is currently housed in the newly renovated Murchie Science Building. Once completed, the new facility will house state-of-the-art laboratories and serve Flint and the region as a hi-tech center for training in advanced manufacturing and cyber-related programs. The university is making significant new investments in student success initiatives and is committed to grow enrollment to over 10,000 students.

title: Mott Middle/Early College Replication
description: This grant will support Mott Community College to continue the research, outreach and replication of early/middle college high schools and programs in Michigan and nationally. As an early adopter of the early/middle college high school model, Mott Community College is entering its thirty-sixth year of offering a blended secondary and post-secondary school design for students that struggle in traditional high schools. The college responds to requests for establishing early/middle college schools and programs at high schools, community colleges, universities and career and technical education centers.

title: Focus on Flint - Residential Demolition
description: Genesee County Land Bank Authority’s mission is to restore value to the community by acquiring, developing and selling vacant and abandoned properties in cooperation with stakeholders who value responsible land ownership. The grantee will utilize this grant to demolish deteriorated vacant residential structures in Flint neighborhoods. Specifically, this project will: 1) demolish vacant houses that are beyond repair; 2) demolish properties that have been burned; and 3) demolish homes listed on the City’s Property Portal that are designated as needing demolition but currently no funds are available.

title: Solar Energy for Amazon River Dwellers
grantee: Centro de Estudos Avançados de Promoção Social e Ambiental
description: The Centro de Estudos Avançados de Promoção Social e Ambiental is a nonprofit organization in the Amazon founded in 1985 to promote sustainable community development and Amazon forest conservation by improving public policies and quality of life of children, youth, indigenous peoples and minority populations. Over the previous grant period, the grantee focused on strengthening off-grid clean energy for health and vaccine preservation, solar-powered access to potable water and power for productive uses such as refrigeration of fruit pulp. The grantee also trained solar technicians at its Active Forest Center in the Tapajos River region of the Brazilian Amazon. Over the next grant period, Centro de Estudos Avançados de Promoção Social e Ambiental will work with isolated Indigenous communities in the Tapajos to implement sustainable community-managed renewable energy, continue its training programs and help organize a policy symposium and trade fair on renewable electrification for isolated communities.

title: Downtown Hotel
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant increase will support construction costs needed to finalize the rehabilitation and renovation work for a boutique hotel in downtown Flint. The Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, a supporting organization of the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation and a public charity, works to improve the quality of life of Flint area residents through the revitalization of downtown. This project is essential for the continued resurgence of downtown Flint. Upon completion the hotel will provide businesses and leisure travelers with an improved hospitality option.

title: Focus on Flint - Senior Home Repairs
description: Genesee County Habitat for Humanity constructs new and rehabilitates existing housing throughout Genesee County to provide low-to-moderate income individuals and families with affordable housing options. This grant will be utilized to make repairs to city of Flint seniors’ homes that are in need of minor repairs.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Healthy Flint Research Coordinating Center, Inc.
description: This grant will support the Healthy Flint Research Coordinating Center, which was formed in 2016, to better maximize health benefits from research conducted locally. With this grant, the grantee will further develop its programs, which coordinate research and prevent fragmented and duplicated work across universities and hospitals. In addition, the organization will increase resident input and ensure ethical community involvement throughout the research process.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Healthy Flint Research Coordinating Center, Inc.
description: This grant will support the Healthy Flint Research Coordinating Center, which was formed in 2016, to better maximize health benefits from research conducted locally. With this grant, the grantee will further develop its programs, that coordinate research and prevent fragmented and duplicated work across universities and hospitals. In addition, the Healthy Flint Research Coordinating Center will increase resident input and ensure ethical community involvement throughout the research process.

title: Focus on Flint - Home Ownership Improvement Loan/Grant Pool
description: Genesee County Habitat for Humanity constructs new and rehabilitates existing housing throughout Genesee County to provide low-to-moderate income individuals and families with affordable housing options. This grant increase will provide additional support for the grantee to provide home improvement loans and grants for city of Flint residents that own their homes.

title: Capacity Building
description: The Hispanic Technology & Community Center of Greater Flint, known as the Latinx Technology & Community Center, provides many programs and services to enhance the dignity and quality of life for the Flint and Genesee County Latino community as well as those from other cultures. The grantee will utilize this grant to support an executive director position to increase its capacity to serve Flint residents.

title: Capacity Building
description: The Latinx Technology & Community Center provides many programs and services to enhance the dignity and quality of life for the Flint and Genesee County Latinx community as well as those from other cultures. The grantee will utilize Mott Foundation funds to support organizational and staff capacity building aimed at diversifying revenue through translation and interpretation services.

title: Truth, Racial Healing and Transformation Endowment
description: The goal of this project is to support the Community Foundation of Greater Flint in its efforts to create an endowment fund for racial equity. The grantee received a $300,000 challenge grant from the W.K. Kellogg Foundation in 2017 for which it needs to raise an additional $300,000 for a final endowment of $600,000. The endowment fund originates from the Truth, Racial Health and Transformation framework, which the grantee has been using to develop racial equity programming but will have the flexibility to support any project focusing on racial equity.

title: Focus on Flint - Blight Elimination Task Force
description: Genesee County Lank Bank Authority’s mission is to restore value to the community by acquiring, developing and selling vacant and abandoned properties in cooperation with stakeholders who value responsible land ownership. The grantee will utilize this grant to advance the work of the Blight Elimination Task Force.

title: Launch Michigan
description: Launch Michigan, a project of the Council of Michigan Foundations, has been working since 2018 as an advocate for critical policy and practice change that will accelerate improvement in the quality of education for Michigan students. The project is a collaborative effort driven by a steering committee consisting of representatives from the public, private and philanthropic sectors. The effort is undertaken in the belief that improving the K-12 education system in Michigan is fundamental to the long-term prosperity of our state and is vital to every student and family in our community.

title: Adult Career Pathway Program
description: This grant will support Mott Community College’s Adult Career Pathway program. The program will leverage many of the college’s existing educational and training programs to help connect unemployed adults, low-income workers and youth to employment and a career pathway. The goal is to ensure that area residents can enter and advance into higher-wage occupations in high-growth industries. Work experience and support services are integrated into the model and will enable participants to combine school and work, and advance in their careers over time.

title: Work-Readiness Program
description: Founded in 1976, Peckham, Inc., is a nonprofit community rehabilitation organization that provides job training and competitive employment opportunities for people with disabilities. The grantee operates 30 rehabilitation and human services programs in Michigan. In 2019, the grantee expanded operations to the Flint area and has hired 66 individuals of the 200 anticipated. Funding in 2020-21 allowed Peckham, Inc. to develop a customized training curriculum for new employees in Flint utilizing the iStrive program, which is based on cognitive behavioral intervention to reduce barriers for long-term employment. In 2021-22, the grantee will engage with Michigan State University in a comprehensive evaluation of the iStrive program.

title: Overture Program and Partnership with Flint Institute of Music
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This renewal grant will provide support to the Sphinx Organization to offer a continuum of music instruction and cultural experiences to underserved students in Flint. The Sphinx Overture program, which introduces students to classical music and violin, serves all Flint public elementary schools. In partnership with YouthQuest and Crim Fitness Foundation, the program will provide students with free, afterschool group violin lessons. Through a partnership with the Flint Institute of Music, students from the program will be eligible for more advanced violin lessons and classes at no cost.

title: Neighborhood Murals
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide funds for the Flint Public Art Project to design and create murals in Flint neighborhoods. The murals provide a way to engage the community of Flint, beautify neighborhoods and support economic development. The grantee will continue to feature the works of local and national talent over the next year and offer programming that engages neighborhoods while following all public health guidelines.

title: Metropolitan Policy Program
description: The Metropolitan Policy Program at Brookings Institution, an internationally known think tank, works with local communities to assist in the development and strategy for retooling the American economy. With renewal support, the grantee will undertake a range of work to promote the economic competitiveness of metropolitan areas domestically and globally, including older industrial cities such as Flint. Activities will include original research, policy advocacy, analytical tool development and network building. In addition, some work directly with the Flint organizations will be funded through this grant.

title: Economic and Entrepreneurial Outreach
description: This grant will support the Economic Development Administration University Center for Community & Economic Development at the University of Michigan-Flint. The center’s mission is to coordinate, inform and contribute to economic development efforts that cultivate innovation and advance high-growth entrepreneurship in the seven-county, I-69 Thumb Region. Additionally, the center supports applied research projects and provides technical assistance to economic development organizations, private businesses and nonprofits.

title: What's Up Downtown Capacity Building
description: This renewal grant will provide support for the Greater Flint Arts Council to fund What’s Up Downtown, a placemaking project focused on programming public spaces. The grantee will utilize the funds to support a full-time director for the project and leverage additional resources to coordinate events for the community.

title: Home Ownership Improvement Loan/Grant Pool
description: Genesee County Habitat for Humanity constructs new and rehabilitates existing housing throughout Genesee County to provide low- to moderate-income individuals and families with affordable housing options. This renewal grant will provide additional support for the grantee to provide home improvement grants for low-income residents that own homes in the city of Flint.

title: Entrepreneurship Network
description: This grant will support the Entrepreneurship Network at Mott Community College. The goal is to support students interested in entrepreneurship through a coordinated network of support, resources, knowledge and technology. The network will help expand programming and assist the grantee in creating an environment that encourages students to further develop their innovative ideas. Supporting entrepreneurship is a way to bring economic opportunity and prosperity to Flint.

title: Berston Field House Capacity Building
description: This grant will assist the United Way of Genesee County and the Friends of Berston Field House with organizational capacity building in the area of fund development. Friends of Berston Field House’s mission is to impact the community through education, athletics, arts and social services. The Berston Field House hosts a variety of events that bring residents together to celebrate with one another and to connect with programs and resources throughout the community.

title: Community Water Lab
description: This grant will support the operations of The McKenzie Patrice Croon Flint Community Lab at the Flint Development Center. The grantee, Evergreen Community Development Initiative, operates the Flint Development Center, which is located in a former Flint Community School elementary building. The McKenzie Patrice Croon Flint Community Lab will be equipped with state-of-the-art technology to test water for multiple contaminants. Scientists and staff of the lab, including youth, will work with residents to collect water samples, test for multiple contaminants, provide results and work with households to address any identified issues.

title: Mobile Mental Health and Outreach Project
description: This grant will provide support to Genesee Health System for mental health services and community outreach in Flint including staff for a mobile mental health clinic that travels throughout the community. The grantee will provide mental and behavioral health services, education on available resources and referrals to other programs for adults and children impacted by the trauma and stress of the Flint water crisis and the pandemic. Services will be offered virtually and in-person at a variety of locations throughout the community including events, neighborhood centers, schools and other locations where residents gather.

title: Tutoring and Interpreter Services
description: The Latinx Technology & Community Center provides many programs and services to enhance the dignity and quality of life for the Flint and Genesee County Latino community as well as those from other cultures. The grantee will utilize Mott Foundation funds to support expanded tutoring and translation/interpreting services.

title: Informing State Legislatures: Statewide Afterschool Policy
description: This grant will support the National Conference of State Legislatures in its work to educate state legislators about the benefits of quality afterschool programs and to build capacity to implement comprehensive afterschool and summer learning opportunities. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) convene an afterschool boot camp for legislators focused on education and supports for young people, particularly as they recover from the pandemic; 2) conduct ongoing activities to educate legislators on the role of afterschool and summer learning programs in future education systems; and 3) work with the Mott Foundation to support future planning efforts to benefit the afterschool sector and the young people it serves.

title: Sloan Museum Dialogue to Action in Flint
description: This grant to the Flint Cultural Center Corporation will advance the Sloan Museum’s efforts to engage with the Flint community and develop a museum that is more diverse, equitable, accessible and inclusive. These efforts are aligned with the vision and mission of the new Sloan Museum facility, which aims to better reflect the community in which it resides and more fully collaborate with all residents.

title: Supporting College and Career Readiness in Afterschool
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant will provide support to Michigan College Access Network to administer technical assistance, coaching and professional development to state afterschool networks implementing college and career readiness initiatives for afterschool programs. This grant will build the capacity of the networks and college and career readiness partners to create new strategies, partnerships and program models to assist youth and families with navigating barriers to post-secondary opportunities. The high-quality learning experiences and resources developed and implemented will better prepare youth and families for a successful college experience by engaging with financial education, college affordability planning and college and career exploration.

title: State Fiscal and Low-Income Initiatives Project
grantee: Center on Budget and Policy Priorities
description: This grant provides ongoing support to the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities for the State Fiscal and Low-Income Initiatives Project. Through this project, the grantee works to expand economic opportunity and fight poverty by ensuring that federal and state governments have adequate resources to meet basic needs and invest in good schools, childcare, quality health care and other priorities. To accomplish these goals, the grantee will: 1) monitor policy and budgetary changes to the social safety net; 2) prepare policy briefs and analyses of budget and fiscal policies; 3) facilitate networking and coordination at the state and local levels for low-income advocates; and 4) provide strategic and technical assistance to state and local policymakers, program administrators and nonprofit organizations working on policy and program issues affecting low-income families. Located in Washington, D.C., the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities is one of the premier policy research institutions in the United States.

title: Focus on Flint - Dumpsters for Community Cleanup Project
description: Neighborhood Engagement Hub supports grassroots organizations, block clubs and groups that desire to create change in their community through hard work. The grantee offers training programs and basic consultation services to help organizations move their ideas from concepts to action. Foundation funding will allow the grantee to manage citywide cleanup projects in 2021. Residents identified neighborhood cleanups as a priority through the Focus on Flint initiative.

title: Building Support for Summer Learning
description: This grant will support the National Summer Learning Association in its efforts to increase access to high-quality summer learning programs across the country. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) support implementation of high-quality summer learning opportunities; 2) expand resources for parents through its discoversummer.inplay.org website; 3) expand a Summer Learning Innovation Fellowship to support emerging education leaders of color; and 4) increase youth voice in summer programming.

title: Great Lakes Islands Alliance
description: The Great Lakes Islands Alliance is a project of the Stewardship Network, a national organization based in the Great Lakes region with strengths in strategic planning, fiduciary management and organizational development. The project is a fledgling network of leaders from 15 Great Lakes islands with year-round populations. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the project established clarity on policy and communications; recommendations for governance and stability; and goals and action plans for the coming years. With renewed support to the Stewardship Network, the project will execute plans to advance stewardship of island natural resources, help enhance the stability of island communities and pursue plans to formalize governance procedures and financial planning.

title: Entrepreneurial Ecosystem Engagement
description: This grant will support SIPI to lead the coordination and alignment of Flint’s entrepreneurial ecosystem. The goals of this grant renewal are to: 1) drive collaboration and leverage the strength of the Flint entrepreneurial ecosystem through the development of strategic plans that drive entrepreneurship across the city; 2) create programs to support a stronger mentorship pool and networks for Flint entrepreneurs; 3) convene regular meetings with entrepreneurial service providers; 4) collaborate and host networking and meet-up events for local entrepreneurs; and 5) develop programs to enhance coordination and communication among entrepreneurial service providers, business peer groups and prospective entrepreneurs.

title: Racial Equity Building Institute for the Americas
geographic_focus: Central America, North America, Caribbean, South America
description: The Puerto Rico Community Foundation plans to establish a permanent institution, the Racial Equity Building Institute for the Americas, which will create synergy between local, regional and national movements in North, Central and South America and the Caribbean. The grantee will also strengthen relationships among local leaders, funders, nonprofits, universities and corporations who are leading research and action around racial equity and justice. This grant will support the following outcomes: 1) mapping the landscape of Afro-descendant communities and anti-Black racism organizations, eventually plotting their corresponding communities in the United States; 2) identifying and building an initial leadership network, comprised of prominent funders, researchers and community leaders; and 3) building a strong infrastructure for the institute, ensuring that it is set up for success and impact over the next five to ten years. Founded in 1985, the Puerto Rico Community Foundation promotes and strengthens social justice and equitable access to community resources on the island of Puerto Rico.

title: Technical Support to Maximize Renewable Energy Access Success
grantee: Instituto de Energia e Meio Ambiente
description: The Instituto de Energia e Meio Ambiente is a Brazilian think tank with expertise in energy planning, electrical engineering and environmental law and policy. Over the previous grant period, the grantee contributed technical data and analysis to the implementation of the More Light for the Amazon federal program to expand renewable energy access in the Amazon and developed a robust method for estimating the number of people without access to reliable electricity in the Amazon. During the next grant period, the grantee will build geo-referenced tools to identify and expand renewable energy access for productive economic activity and for decommissioning solar equipment at the end of its lifecycle in the Amazon.

title: Genesee County Youth Career Academy
description: Founded in 1976, Peckham, Inc., is a nonprofit community rehabilitation organization that provides job training and competitive employment opportunities for people with disabilities. The grantee operates 30 rehabilitation and human services programs in Michigan. In 2019, the grantee expanded operations to the Flint area and has hired 66 individuals of the 200 anticipated. This grant will provide continued support for the Genesee County Youth Career Academy to help reduce recidivism, improve social functioning and increase job skills training for at-risk, court-involved youth ages 15-18, as well as expanding to serve middle school students ages 10-14 as part of the Junior Youth Academy.

title: Genesee County Youth Career Academy
description: This grant will provide continued support to Peckham, Inc. for its Genesee County Youth Career Academy. The grantee’s programs help to reduce recidivism, improve social functioning, increase job skills training and provide mentoring for at-risk, court-involved youth ages 15-18. The grant will also support the grantee in expanding to serve middle school students ages 10-14 as part of Peckham’s Junior Youth Academy in partnership with the Genesee County 7th Judicial Circuit Court and Mt. Morris Consolidated Schools.

title: Written Insights: Addressing Educational Inequities Through Community Schools
description: The Netter Center for Community Partnerships at the University of Pennsylvania will oversee the writing of a book that will chronicle the experiences and lessons of the modern-day community schools movement. The book will cover cross-cutting themes including partnerships, equity, shared leadership, results, policy, research and documentation, communication, capacity building, financing, infrastructure and flexibility. The authors will make the case that the community schools strategy is essential in all public schools as the nation grapples with COVID-19 and systemic racial issues.

title: Community Foundations Addressing Racial Equity
description: The project goal is to help community foundations advance racial equity using the framework of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. During the previous grant period, the Association of Black Foundation Executives conducted racial equity training workshops for 53 staff and board members from 20 community foundations, organized in two cohorts. Participants were exposed to a structural frame of reference, a shared language for talking about issues of race and a sense of what an intentional approach requires to be most effective. In addition, the grantee identified 20 community foundations that launched or expanded funds to support Black communities. In the upcoming grant period, the grantee will continue its training activities and plans to organize four cohorts for a total of approximately 100 participants from an estimated 35 community foundations. Founded in 1971, the Association of Black Foundation Executives is a national membership organization of predominantly Black trustees and staff of private, community and corporate foundations.

title: Bachelor of Paralegal Studies and Community-Based Paralegals
description: The project goal is to strengthen the capacity of community paralegals in South Africa through accredited university offerings. To this end, the Cape Peninsula University of Technology will continue to offer its bachelor’s degree in paralegal studies to community paralegals across South Africa. Past support helped the grantee to organize the first and second intake of community paralegals into the course and provide them with the support needed to succeed. It did this successfully and plans to build on this momentum with its third and fourth intakes. Ongoing support will assist community paralegals from across South Africa to access the blended model of learning to obtain this qualification. The grantee also plans on undertaking research on topics related to community paralegals. The Cape Peninsula University of Technology is the largest technical university in the Western Cape Province of South Africa.

title: African Centre of Excellence for Access to Justice Project
description: The project goal is to support learning and networking of community justice organizations in Africa. To this end, the Paralegal Advisory Service Institute will continue to host and coordinate the activities of the African Centre of Excellence for Access to Justice with this goal in mind. Past Mott Foundation support has allowed the grantee to: 1) increase its membership; 2) elevate its profile by participating in key regional and international forums on access to justice and sustainable development; 3) collaborate with the African Peer Review Mechanism and Open Government Partnership on people-centered justice in Africa; and 4) strengthen its coordination and management. The project will unlock peer learning, amplify local voices, reinforce African community justice institutions, research people-centered justice in Africa and unlock resources for sustainable financing. The Paralegal Advisory Service Institute is one of the leading community justice organizations in Africa.

title: General Purposes
description: The Casual Workers Advice Office was established in 2011 to give free legal advice to workers who have been dismissed or face other labor violations by their employers in South Africa. Past Mott Foundation support has helped the grantee to continue organizing precarious workers to address systemic injustices that they may face. It has won permanent employment for 15,000 workers through their justice services. During South Africa’s hard COVID-19 lockdown, it secured various victories to ensure that the largest public employment insurance pay benefits to people who might lose income because of the difficult economic situation. Continued support will assist the Casual Workers Advice Office to provide justice services to precarious workers, organize workers to address the systemic injustices that they face and strengthen its organization to support workers and its mandate.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will assist the Ukrainian Helsinki Human Rights Union in their efforts to increase access to justice in Ukraine through protection of fundamental rights and freedoms. Particular attention will be given to the growing range of rights and justice issues arising from Russia’s illegal invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. The grantee will connect civilian victims to relevant justice services, placing accountability and war-related monitoring and documentation at the heart of human rights work. The grantee will also pursue war-related strategic litigation, both nationally and internationally. Additionally, the grantee will increase focus on emerging transitional justice issues of re-integration and social-psychological consequences of war. In 2023 alone, the grantee, through its 21 public reception offices, provided almost 20,000 individual consultations through its legal aid centers, responding to justice needs ranging from displacement to war crimes. Through its lengthy experience of bringing cases to the European Court of Human Rights, the grantee has proven to be an important player in a Ukrainian government initiative to hold Russian forces accountable for violations of international humanitarian law with over 77,000 submissions received so far. Established in 2004, the Ukrainian Helsinki Human Rights Union works to promote practical observance of the range of international human rights instruments to which Ukraine is a party.

title: Bachelor of Paralegal Studies and Community-Based Paralegals
description: The project goal is to strengthen the capacity of community paralegals in South Africa through accredited university offerings. To this end, the Cape Peninsula University of Technology will continue to offer its bachelor’s degree in paralegal studies to community paralegals across South Africa. Past Mott Foundation support helped the grantee to organize the first, second, third and fourth intake of community paralegals into the course and provide them with the support needed. The grantee did this successfully and plans to build on this momentum with its new intakes. Ongoing support will assist community paralegals from across South Africa to access the blended model of learning to obtain this qualification. The Cape Peninsula University of Technology is the largest technical university in the Western Cape Province of South Africa.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will collectively address the systemic injustices that precarious workers face. To this end, the Casual Workers Advice Office will continue to work with other advice offices and organizations to meet the justice needs of precarious workers. The grantee will also continue to train community paralegals on contemporary labor-related laws. Past Mott Foundation support has helped the grantee to continue organizing precarious workers to address systemic injustices. The grantee also assisted precarious workers to organize themselves into institutions that serve their needs. In this regard, it won a Labor Court victory upholding all workers’ constitutional rights to form organizations free of prior state approval. These injustices often take up a large portion of advice office caseloads. Established in 2011, Casual Workers Advise Office gives free legal advice to workers who have been dismissed or face other labor violations by their employers in South Africa.

title: General Purposes
description: The NGO Forum on ADB has been advocating for sustainable development policies that are beneficial to local communities and the environment in the Asian region for two decades. Over the past grant period, the grantee has seen significant new commitments from both the Asian Development Bank and Chinese financial institutions to align their portfolios with climate commitments. Over the next two years, the grantee will continue to lead the civil society process for the review of the Asian Development Bank and Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank’s environmental and social safeguard policies, while simultaneously reviewing the implementation of those policies. The NGO Forum on ADB will also monitor the project lending for both institutions to ensure the broad commitments to climate alignment are reflected in project finance.

title: Factory Two Project
description: This grant will provide support to Red Ink Flint to manage Factory Two. In addition to Factory Two, the grantee operates Flint Local 432, a performance venue located in downtown Flint. Factory Two is an affordable community makerspace where creative people gather to work on product ideas and network with each other. After two years of significant disruption due to the pandemic, Factory Two programming has largely returned to normal in 2022. With funding from the Mott Foundation, the grantee will continue to support operations and programmatic activities that increase membership, classes and available opportunities for youth.

title: General Purposes
description: The Bank Information Center is a nongovernmental organization that specializes in analyzing and strengthening social and environmental governance of international financial institutions, primarily the World Bank Group. Over the last grant period, the grantee and its partners in developing countries monitored development bank climate finance, commitments to exclude fossil fuel finance and development and implementation of Amazon funds by the Inter-American Development Bank. Over the next grant period, the Bank Information Center will work to strengthen social and environmental safeguards across development finance institutions and develop a framework for ensuring communities impacted by development finance are compensated.

title: Focus on Flint - Hiring Young People for Neighborhood Cleanup and Beautification
description: Neighborhood Engagement Hub supports grassroots organizations, block clubs and groups that desire to create change in their community through hard work. The grantee offers training programs and basic consultation services to help organizations move their ideas from concepts to action. Foundation funding will support the hiring of young people to perform neighborhood cleanup and beautification work. Residents identified youth employment as a priority through the Focus on Flint initiative.

title: Michigan News and Information Programs
description: This grant provides funding to the University of Michigan’s Michigan Radio in support of its news and information service. Located in Ann Arbor, Michigan Radio is a trusted media brand in the state, known for its fair and fact-based coverage of state, national and international news. Michigan Radio reaches its audience with radio content, podcasts, websites, social media and mobile apps, providing news and information to help create a more engaged public.

title: Operating Support
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will renew operating support for the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation and redevelopment efforts through its supported organization, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation. Both organizations have been leaders in efforts to revitalize Flint’s downtown district and will continue their focus on redeveloping properties for residential and commercial reuse, attracting new employers and creating and enhancing community amenities for public use.

title: The Education Trust-Midwest Michigan Policy Efforts
description: The Education Trust will support its Midwest division to continue advancing meaningful educational equity and excellence efforts at the state and local levels to address the concerns of challenged districts, such as Flint Community Schools. The grantee’s Midwest division remains well-positioned to inform Michigan’s education policy landscape through equity-focused research and data; whether in regards to long-standing issues, such as early literacy and school funding or the new challenges brought about by the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: General Purposes
description: The Village Information Center was established in 1976 and has published hundreds of issues of the East Village Magazine. This grant increase will allow the grantee to cover more newsworthy stories to keep Flint residents informed about their community and life in neighborhoods. A companion website will offer access to news captured in the magazine, as well as new information that does not make the magazine’s publishing deadline.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will renew general-purpose support to Focus: HOPE, an anti-poverty and civil rights organization that serves residents of Detroit’s Oakman Boulevard neighborhood. Cofounded in 1968 by Father William Cunningham and Eleanor Josaitis, the grantee’s mission is to “provide intelligent and practical solutions to overcome racism, poverty and injustice.” Mott funding will help support the grantee’s core lines of work: workforce development and education; early learning and youth development; and food justice.

title: North Flint Food Market
description: North Flint Reinvestment Corporation is a nonprofit community development corporation focused on battling economic and environmental injustices. Established in 2011 by the Foss Avenue Baptist Church’s leadership, the grantee takes a place-based, holistic approach to revitalizing the severely distressed neighborhood in which it is located. This grant will support the development of the North Flint Food Market to be located on the north side of Flint near the intersection of Pierson and Clio Roads. Food scarcity is a long-standing and well-documented concern for those living in this part of town and many residents have limited transportation options for shopping elsewhere.

title: Strengthening Community Paralegals in Ukraine
description: The program goal is to strengthen the practice of community paralegals in Ukraine. Such community-based paralegals have become increasingly important in providing legal, health, humanitarian and related information and services in the wake of Russia’s illegal invasion of Ukraine. Drawing on its growing pre-war experience in Ukraine and on extensive experience of paralegal development abroad, the Ukrainian Legal Aid Foundation will develop a series of specialized online training courses for these community justice actors. The grantee will also work to develop mutually supportive networks of paralegals, community health care workers, civic advisors and others working to provide information and legal support to Ukrainians in order to supplement resources available from the state. In 2020-22, the grantee developed a comprehensive online training course for community paralegals with over 200 participants completing the course and a further 200 beginning the process. Over this time, paralegals dealt with over 10,000 enquiries on a range of legal issues affecting Ukrainians. The Ukrainian Legal Aid Foundation works to ensure access to justice in Ukraine through the support and provision of legal aid services and through improving the standards of justice provision.

title: World Resources Institute Sustainable Finance Center
description: The World Resources Institute is a global environmental think tank that works with governments, the private sector and civil society to identify solutions to urgent environmental challenges. The support of the Mott Foundation has enabled the grantee to sustain a decade-long effort to help shift global financial flows toward sustainable development that is more climate compatible and responds to the needs of the poor. This grant will focus on consolidating previous policy gains into concrete improvements in investment decisions and support a 10-year retrospective on changes and opportunities for multilateral and Chinese public finance in reaching international climate goals.

title: Capital Improvements
description: Genesee County Habitat for Humanity is an affiliate of Habitat for Humanity International, a nonprofit, ecumenical Christian housing ministry. The grantee’s mission is to bring people together to build homes, communities and hope. The grantee works with neighborhood associations, block clubs and other local grassroots groups on leadership development and other forms of capacity building. Genesee County Habitat for Humanity will use funds to replace the roof and repair other structural damage at its headquarters.

title: HBCU Executive Leadership Institute
description: In 2019, Clark Atlanta University developed a plan for the Executive Leadership Institute program. The program’s overall goal is to prepare and support future presidents of the nation’s historically black colleges and universities. With Mott Foundation funding, the grantee will begin implementing the program by recruiting program fellows, developing credentialed training courses and organizing networking events. Based in Atlanta, Georgia, Clark Atlanta University was established in 1988 through the consolidation of Atlanta University and Clark College—two of the nation’s oldest Historically Black Colleges and Universities.

title: Kansas Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: University of Kansas Center for Research, Inc.
description: This grant will support the Center for Positive Youth Development at the University of Kansas which coordinates the Kansas Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) increase the number of afterschool programs available for young people through implementing a strategic communications campaign to advance afterschool and summer learning opportunities; 2) enhance youth outcomes by leading a bi-state initiative to build additional afterschool opportunities in the Greater Kansas City metro area; 3) work with education stakeholders and policymakers to design and implement education recovery funding to help Kansas youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen resources.

title: Increasing the Impact of Land Conservation on Great Lakes Water Quality
geographic_focus: Minnesota, New York, Ohio, Wisconsin, Michigan, Pennsylvania, Illinois, Indiana
description: The Land Trust Alliance is a national organization of local land trusts that provides technical support, training and assistance to support land conservation, acquisition and protection. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee provided such services to land trusts in the Great Lakes region working at the intersection of land and water conservation. The grantee also assessed Great Lakes land trusts’ current water protection efforts and identified strategies to increase their impact. Two successful pilot projects were also completed in the region. With renewed support, the Land Trust Alliance will be able to effectively use the assessment results to refine its programming and inform its work going forward to increase land trusts’ capacity to protect freshwater resources.

title: City Leaders Engaged in Afterschool Reform
description: This grant will support the National League of Cities Institute to engage city officials in developing high-quality afterschool and summer learning initiatives at the federal, state and local levels. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) expand access to afterschool programs as part of the United States Department of Education’s Engage Every Student Initiative; 2) strengthen the capacity of city leaders to partner with school superintendents and community-based organizations to support programs funded through the American Rescue Plan Act; 3) continue to raise awareness among municipal leaders in building high-quality afterschool and summer learning systems; and 4) work with the Mott Foundation to support future planning efforts to benefit the afterschool sector and the young people it serves.

title: Housing Construction in Carriage Town Neighborhood
description: Michigan Community Capital is a nonprofit community development corporation which is also designated as a Community Development Finance Institution and a Community Development Entity by the federal government. The grantee funds community development real estate projects across the state. This grant will provide match funding for a housing construction and redevelopment project in the Carriage Town neighborhood. Michigan Community Capital will partner with the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, a supported organization of the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation on the development.

title: Strengthening Community Paralegals in Ukraine
description: The project goal is to strengthen the practice of community paralegals in Ukraine. Building on its initial efforts to develop a flexible and responsive system for managing legal assistance requests, the Ukrainian Legal Aid Foundation will give special attention to refining digital processes for linking paralegal assistance with the formal state-supported legal aid system. This will allow for better coordinated and more responsive assistance. Additionally, the grantee will work to strengthen mutually supportive networks of paralegals, community health care workers and related professionals in order to provide psycho-social support to paralegals working on traumatic issues. In 2022-2024, over 200 paralegals received training through the grantee’s online course. Over 11,000 consultations were provided to clients, with the bulk of these receiving further support from the state legal aid system. The grantee organized over 100 meetings to bring paralegals together with social service agencies, civil society partners and psychological support services aimed at strengthening service provision. The Ukrainian Legal Aid Foundation works to ensure access to justice in Ukraine through the support and provision of legal aid services and through improving the responsiveness of the justice system.

title: New Tree Planting
description: The Genesee Conservation District works closely with the City of Flint to maintain the city’s tree canopy. The organization has focused primarily on the removal of dead and dangerous street trees over the last several years. This grant will provide funding to plant approximately 250 new street trees in all nine wards throughout Flint over the next two years. Trees are essential for the survival of both wildlife and people and serve as an invaluable community resource.

title: Rhode Island Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Rhode Island Foundation which coordinates the Rhode Island Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) increase the number of afterschool programs available for young people through coordinating state and local policies to advance afterschool and summer learning opportunities; 2) enhance youth outcomes by leading a workforce development initiative to support the afterschool workforce in Rhode Island; 3) work with education stakeholders and policymakers to design and implement education recovery funding to help Rhode Island youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen resources.

title: Youth Skilled Trades and Pre-apprentice Program
description: With this grant, Active Boys in Christ will to provide a free summer program that teaches youth hands-on basic plumbing, electrical, carpentry and cooking skills. The Active Boys in Christ organization has licensed plumbers, electricians, carpenters and an executive chef that volunteers to work with the youth. During the program character lessons on honesty, forgiveness, respect and integrity are taught.

title: Reconnecting Fathers with Families and Work
description: With this grant, InvolvedDad will strengthen families through parental engagement. The grantee will empower men to be engaged fathers by providing training, coaching and peer support in a safe environment. The program utilizes a combination of research-based techniques and approaches informed by mentors that have struggled with the crisis of fatherlessness firsthand. The mentors encourage men to face the issues and wounds that prevent them from being fathers, address those issues head on and then empower the men with tools and techniques to manage fatherhood.

title: Grassroots Legal Empowerment Fund
description: The Fund for Global Human Rights will establish and operate a 10-year, $100 million Legal Empowerment Fund to support grassroots legal actors focused on ensuring access to justice for marginalized and vulnerable communities around the world. The grantee will seek to draw support from a variety of public and private donors and use these resources to provide long-term organizational support for the field. Specifically, the project will support groups to invoke the law, regulations and policies to access justice; organize and take collective action to reform the legal framework to provide better protections for communities; and generate and share learning both on best practices in the application of legal empowerment strategies as well as on adaptation and developing new approaches. The grantee will also attract more funding and influence funding practices to prioritize long-term flexible support to grassroots groups. Established in 2002, the Fund for Global Human Rights is a public foundation that works to advance human rights globally by providing frontline activists, organizations and movements around the world with funding, technical assistance and opportunities for national and transnational organizing. Additional information about the Legal Empowerment Fund can be found at http://www.legalempowermentfund.org.

title: General Purposes
description: The Association of Charitable Foundations is the membership body for U.K. foundations and grant-making charities. Driven by a belief that foundations are a vital source for social good, the grantee’s mission is to support foundations to be ambitious and use their resources effectively. To this end, the grantee engages in policy development, provides research and information and organizes a wide-ranging program of events and learning. The Association of Charitable Foundations’ 400 members collectively hold assets of around £50 billion and give over £2.5 billion annually.

title: Travel and Learning Fund
description: This grant will advance the Civil Society program’s objectives and outcomes by supporting exchange, networking and interaction among key nonprofits, practitioners and experts, including Mott grantees, working in the program’s thematic areas of interest. To this end, the Institute of International Education will operate a travel and learning fund to support individuals and organizations working on civic space, community philanthropy, access to justice or other areas of interest to the Civil Society program. During the grant period, the grantee will support: participation in study visits and exchanges; engagement in virtual and in-person conferences and other events; and field studies and research projects that result in a report or publication that benefits the field. Based in New York, the Institute of International Education manages similar funds for foundations around the world.

title: INSPIRE - Initiative for Strategic Philanthropy and Intelligent Resources
grantee: Association for the Practice of Transformation
description: The program goal is to strengthen community philanthropy in Europe and globally. To this end, the Association for the Practice of Transformation will continue to develop and manage INSPIRE — Initiative for Strategic Philanthropy and Intelligent Resources as an informal network of community foundation practitioners and experts. More specifically, the grantee will strengthen and expand the network, produce and share knowledge about community foundations in various contexts and promote good practice for community foundations and their support organizations. In the past three years, the grantee trained 83 community philanthropy practitioners from 10 countries, strengthened and enlarged the INSPIRE — Initiative for Strategic Philanthropy and Intelligent Resources network and supported exchange and learning among network members. The grantee is based in Brasov, Romania.

title: INSPIRE - Initiative for Strategic Philanthropy and Intelligent Resources
grantee: Association for the Practice of Transformation
description: The project goal is to strengthen community philanthropy globally. To this end, the Association for the Practice of Transformation will continue to develop and manage INSPIRE — Initiative for Strategic Philanthropy and Intelligent Resources as an informal network of community foundation practitioners and experts. In the past three years, the grantee has engaged 220 community foundation and philanthropic support organization practitioners from 82 organizations through codesigning, facilitating and providing knowledge in over 60 learning events. The grantee has also: 1) led in-person study visits; 2) held annual “Thinkfrastructure” virtual conferences; 3) facilitated online workshops and practitioner circles; and 4) created a host of knowledge resources on its website. Over the next three years, the grantee will continue convening practitioners, producing knowledge resources and supporting experimentation and innovation in the community foundation field. This will include a global gathering for community foundation support organizations in 2025. Established in 2018, the Association for the Practice of Transformation is located in Brasov, Romania.

title: General Purposes
description: The Global Fund for Community Foundations supports the growth and development of community foundations and other community philanthropy organizations around the world. It provides funding, promotes learning and connection across the field and generates knowledge about community philanthropy. Past grant support enabled the grantee to create awareness on the value and contribution of community philanthropy organizations to the broader development agenda. In addition to making grants and providing technical support to its partners, the grantee provided platforms for community foundations to engage with international development agencies and civil society organizations to contribute to the development agenda. In 2022 and 2023, the Global Fund for Community Foundations will continue to make grants, provide technical support and profile community philanthropy through research and convenings.

title: General Purposes
description: The Global Fund for Community Foundations provides funding, promotes learning, builds a global network of community foundations, and generates knowledge about community philanthropy. Additionally, the grantee advances conversations that promote a community-led approach to development. Activities under the previous grant included strengthening and deepening the evidence base for community philanthropy through research and publications produced by members of the network. In addition to making grants, the grantee has led conversations and a movement that is focused on shifting power from international aid to communities to localizing the development agenda. In 2024 and 2025, the Global Fund for Community Foundations will continue to make grants, conduct research that shapes conversations on community philanthropy, convene the sector on topical issues, and support learning.

title: Sustainable Communities: Addressing SDGs on a Local Level in Latin America
geographic_focus: Central America, Mexico, Caribbean, South America
description: The Center for Philanthropy and Social Investment at the Adolfo Ibanez University will promote the development of sustainable communities throughout Latin America, based on an agenda that includes the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. The center will highlight the role of community foundations as valuable contributors to the development of sustainable communities. The center will also produce a guide, seven case studies and two online courses on sustainable communities, the Sustainable Development Goals and community foundations. These will be shared through webinars, seminars, podcasts, videos and other events. Founded in 2015, the Center for Philanthropy and Social Investment promotes the culture and practice of strategic giving in Chile and is part of the School of Government at the Adolfo Ibanez University, Chile’s leading private, non-profit university. Legally incorporated in 1988, the grantee’s mission is to provide an education based on personal responsibility and freedom.

title: Sustainable Communities: Addressing SDGs on a Local Level in Latin America
geographic_focus: Central America, Mexico, Caribbean, South America
description: The project goal is to promote the advancement of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals by community foundations in Latin America. To this end, the Center for Philanthropy and Social Investment at Adolfo Ibanez University (known by its Spanish-language acronym as UAI) launched the program “Sustainable Communities: A Path for Activating the SDGs at a Local Level” in 2021. To date, the grantee has convened an advisory committee, developed a program framework, delivered a webinar, produced seven podcasts, written seven case studies and established an online knowledge center. Over the next year, the grantee will produce a report on the contribution of philanthropic entities to the Sustainable Development Goals in Latin America, develop a toolkit, conduct a training program for philanthropic associations, maintain an “SDGs and Sustainable Communities” website and broadly disseminate all produced knowledge resources. Founded in 2015, the Center for Philanthropy and Social Investment promotes the culture and practice of strategic giving in Chile and is part of the School of Government at UAI, Chile’s leading private, non-profit university that was legally incorporated in 1988.

title: Community Foundations, SDGs and Racial Equity
description: The program goal is to help community foundations use the framework of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals to advance racial equity in their communities. To this end, the Charles Stewart Mott Foundation Chair on Community Foundations at Indiana University’s Lilly Family School of Philanthropy, Dr. Laurie Paarlberg, will lead a cross-national research team to design and pilot a study that will describe shifts in diversity, equity and inclusion in community foundations in the United States, Canada and Australia. The study will identify early adopters of justice philanthropy, describe the process to move toward it and explore how the SDGs and other global frameworks advance racial justice work. The Lilly Family School of Philanthropy at Indiana University was founded in 2012. Its mission is to increase the understanding of philanthropy and improve its practice worldwide through critical inquiry, interdisciplinary research, teaching, training and civic engagement.

title: Community Foundations, SDGs and Racial Equity
geographic_focus: United Kingdom, Canada, Australia and New Zealand, United States
description: The program goal is to help community foundations use the framework of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals to advance justice and racial equity. To this end, the Charles Stewart Mott Foundation Chair on Community Foundations at Indiana University’s Lilly Family School of Philanthropy, Dr. Laurie Paarlberg, is leading a cross-national research team on a four-year project that will describe shifts in diversity, equity and inclusion in community foundations in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom and Australia. In the first year, a literature review was conducted, a pilot quantitative analysis was conducted, sites were selected for case studies, a global research team was assembled and additional funding was solicited. Over the next three years, data will be collected and analyzed, case studies written, a cross-national study completed and results broadly disseminated. The Lilly Family School of Philanthropy at Indiana University was founded in 2012 and its mission is to increase the understanding of philanthropy and improve its practice worldwide through critical inquiry, interdisciplinary research, teaching, training and civic engagement.

title: SDG Adoption by Mexican Community Foundations
description: The program goal is to advance the adoption of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals by community foundations in Mexico. To this end, Comunalia will partner with Pacto Global in Mexico to provide technical support, workshops, communication strategies, reference materials, digital tools and funding opportunities to Mexican community foundations. The project will include monthly two-hour workshops, grants to five community foundations, technical assistance in developing partnerships and alliances with local and national entities and help in raising visibility around the Sustainable Development Goals. Launched in 2009, and constituted as a nonprofit legal entity in 2011, Comunalia is an alliance of community foundations in Mexico that focuses on local development and strategic social investment and currently has 16 members.

title: SDG Adoption by Mexican Community Foundations
description: The program goal is to advance the adoption of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals by community foundations in Mexico. To this end, over the past two years Comunalia deepened the knowledge and integration of the goals at nine community foundations through training, mentoring and financial support. During the upcoming grant period, the grantee will map existing initiatives related to the goals and define priority issues and common indicators for all of its current 17 members. It will create a data dashboard with local disaggregated data and common indicators and develop a communications strategy and resources for use by the entire alliance, as well as by individual community foundations. Launched in 2009 and constituted as a nonprofit legal entity in 2011, Comunalia is an alliance of community foundations in Mexico that focuses on local development and strategic social investment.

title: Advice Office Support Project
grantee: Association of University Legal Aid Institutions Trust
description: The project goal is to increase access to justice for poor and marginalized people in South Africa. To this end, the Association of University Legal Aid Institutions Trust will strengthen its existing programs to support selected community advice offices and university legal aid clinics to provide justice services. Past support helped the grantee increase the number of advice offices and law clinics with which it works. These clinics were situated in the Eastern Cape and Free State provinces. The grantee also responded to the COVID-19 pandemic by increasing grants to advice offices and providing responsive accompaniment services virtually. The Association of University Legal Aid Institutions Trust was established in 1998 and plays an important role in providing resources and back-up legal services to advice offices in South Africa.

title: Community Justice in Africa Features
description: The project goal is to elevate the work of African community justice institutions in the media. To this end, the Adamela Trust will use its The Continent newspaper to publish news reporting and features on community justice work in Africa. It will publish work outside of capital cities, where injustices are rife and often invisible. The grantee proposes to do this by appointing a communities editor, who will work closely with journalists in various African countries to produce the articles. The Adamela Trust is charitable trust, based in South Africa. It is the publisher of The Continent and the Mail and Guardian newspapers.

title: Community Foundation Development Fund
grantee: Academy for the Development of Philanthropy in Poland
description: The program goal is to strengthen the capacity of community foundations in Europe to contribute to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. To this end, the Academy for the Development of Philanthropy in Poland will provide tailor-made grantmaking and technical assistance programs to European community foundations to help them consolidate their work on the global goals. The grantee will develop a series of learning materials to increase the knowledge and expertise about the global goals available to the community foundation field. In addition, the grantee will document and publicize the contribution of European community foundations to the global goals. During the past grant period, the grantee provided 22 grants totaling more than $297,000 to community foundations in 11 countries to support their engagement with the global goals as well as 19 grants totaling over $260,000 to community foundations supporting Ukrainian refugees. The Academy for the Development of Philanthropy in Poland also published a series of learning materials and organized learning events to increase the capacity of European community foundations to contribute to the global goals.

title: Community Foundations Addressing Racial Equity
description: The project goal is to help community foundations advance racial equity using the framework of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. During the previous grant period, the Association of Black Foundation Executives conducted racial equity training workshops for 53 staff and board members from 20 community foundations, organized in two cohorts. Participants were exposed to a structural frame of reference, a shared language for discussing issues of race and a sense of what an intentional approach requires to be most effective. In addition, the grantee identified 20 community foundations that launched or expanded funds to support black communities. In the upcoming grant period, the grantee will continue its training activities and plans to organize four cohorts totaling approximately 100 participants from an estimated 35 community foundations. Founded in 1971, the Association of Black Foundation Executives is a national membership organization of predominantly black trustees and staff of private, community and corporate foundations.

title: Global Philanthropy Forum
grantee: World Affairs Council of Northern California
description: Founded in 2001, the Global Philanthropy Forum is a project of the World Affairs Council of Northern California. The project goal is to build, sustain and continuously revitalize a learning community of private donors and social investors committed to international causes. The grantee accomplishes this through conferences, tailored programs and connecting donors to policymakers, issue experts, leaders of civil society organizations and social entrepreneurs. Over the past several years, the grantee has established partnerships and helped organize gatherings all over the world with a growing interest in participation from individuals outside of the United States. In 2020, due to COVID-19, the grantee pivoted from hosting the conference in Berkeley, California to hosting the conference virtually. In 2021, the grantee plans to organize the conference virtually, host an educational web series and continue to connect philanthropists and social investors. The World Affairs Council of Northern California is a nonprofit, nonpartisan educational organization devoted to engaging the public in a discussion of the transnational issues of tomorrow.

title: Early Childhood Implementation
description: This grant will provide funding to the Community Foundation of Greater Flint to support the expansion of early childhood education in Flint. Expanding access to high-quality early childhood education has always been important for the city, and became even more important following the water crisis.
