As fiscal sponsor for the Flint Center for Educational Excellence, the grantee ensures operations of the Flint Early Childhood Collaborative, a project that aims to increase access to and the quality of early childhood education in Flint through strategic planning, research, advocacy and participation in the Educare Learning Network.

title: Technical Assistance for Improved Teaching and Learning
description: This renewal grant will allow Michigan State University to continue providing support to Flint Community Schools with technical assistance aimed at increasing district capacity, improving school culture, increasing operational efficiency and improving student academic outcomes. To achieve these goals, technical assistance will be focused on implementation of the FCS Strategic Plan 2022-27. The grantee will support the district’s implementation of four primary components: 1) scholar focus; 2) teaching and instruction; 3) climate and culture; and 4) data knowledge and application.

title: Technical Assistance for Improved Teaching and Learning
description: This renewal grant will allow Michigan State University to continue providing support to Flint Community Schools with technical assistance aimed at increasing district capacity, improving school culture, increasing operational efficiency and improving student academic outcomes. To achieve these goals, technical assistance will be focused on supporting district leaders in the development and implementation of a multi-phase plan for restructuring the learning environments for Flint Community School scholars. The grantee will support the district’s implementation of four primary components of its strategic plan: 1) scholar focus; 2) teaching and instruction; 3) climate and culture; and 4) data knowledge and application while building capacity of leaders to implement the district’s planned reduction in school facilities.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint
description: This renewal grant provides general purposes support to the Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint. Focusing on education, creativity, physical activity and health, and family support services, the grantee offersyear-round programming to young people between the ages of 7 and 17 in the Flint area. The grantee operates two sites, one located on the east side and the other on the south side of the city. Programs such as this have been instrumental in mitigating the negative effects of both the water crisis as well as the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic in the city of Flint. By providing students with highly engaging educational and enrichment opportunities in a safe and supportive environment, the Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint continues to stay true to its mission to enable young people in the Flint area to reach their full potential.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint
description: This renewal grant provides general purposes support to the Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint. The grantee focuses on education, creativity, physical activity and health and family support services while offering year-round programming to young people between the ages of 7 and 17 in the Flint area. The grantee operates two sites, one located on the east side and the other on the south side of the city. Programs such as this have been instrumental in mitigating the negative effects of both the water crisis, as well as the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic. By providing students with highly engaging educational and enrichment opportunities in a safe and supportive environment, the Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint continues to stay true to its mission to enable young people in the Flint area to reach their full potential.

title: Community Education Innovation Fund
description: This grant will provide funding for the Community Education Innovation Fund at the Crim Fitness Foundation. The initiative is designed to provide community school directors with opportunities and funding for innovative ideas and practices. The focus during the current grant period will be on reconnection efforts as students are expected to return to classrooms full time after spending parts of the past several school years with remote and hybrid education during COVID-19.

title: Community Education Initiative
description: This grant provides support to the Crim Fitness Foundation to continue to serve as the lead agency for the community education model in Flint. The community education strategy involves increasing the depth and impact of programs at all Flint Community Schools buildings, the International Academy of Flint and the Flint Cultural Center Academy. The central elements of community education that made it so effective in responding to the water crisis — caring relationships, a holistic approach to student and family well-being and social emotional supports — remain critical as students emerge from the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: YouthQuest Afterschool Program
description: This renewal grant provides continued support to the Genesee Area Focus Fund for the YouthQuest Afterschool Initiative. YouthQuest provides children and youth with opportunities to learn and grow through a safe, engaging and exciting afterschool learning experience surrounded by caring, responsible adults and sustained by involved and supportive community organizations.

title: Youth Skilled Trades and Pre-apprentice Program
description: With this grant, Active Boys in Christ will provide a free summer program that teaches youth hands-on basic plumbing, electrical, carpentry and cooking skills. The grantee has licensed plumbers, electricians, carpenters and an executive chef that volunteer to work with the youth. During the program, character lessons on honesty, forgiveness, respect and integrity are also taught.

title: Reconnecting Fathers with Families and Work
description: With this grant, InvolvedDad will strengthen families through parental engagement. The grantee will empower men to be engaged fathers by providing training, coaching and peer support in a safe environment. The program utilizes a combination of research-based techniques and approaches informed by mentors who have struggled with the crisis of fatherlessness firsthand. The mentors encourage men to face the issues and wounds that prevent them from being fathers, address those issues head on and then empower the men with tools and techniques to manage fatherhood.

title: Helping Young People to Employment Program
description: Operated by Faith Foundation Resources, the Helping Young People to Employment Program prepares young people for the workforce by developing essential soft skills that employers seek. The program encourages participants ages 16-24 to graduate from high school and pursue higher education opportunities and activities that support obtaining gainful employment. Approximately 50 youth from Flint will participate in the workforce development portion of the Helping Young People to Employment Program. Those youth will also receive additional wraparound services, training to graduate from high school and support to ensure that they will be employed within six months of program completion.

title: Helping Young People to Employment Program

The program encourages participants ages 16-24 to graduate from high school and pursue higher education opportunities and activities that support obtaining gainful employment. Approximately 50 youth from Flint will participate in the workforce development portion of the Helping Young People to Employment Program. Those youth will also receive additional wraparound services, training to graduate from high school and support to ensure they will be employed within six months of program completion.

title: Adult Career Pathway Program
description: This grant will support the Adult Career Pathway program at Mott Community College. The program will leverage many of the college’s existing educational and training programs to help connect unemployed adults, low-income workers and youth to employment and a career pathway. The goal is to ensure that area residents can enter and advance into higher-wage occupations in high-growth industries. Work experience and support services are integrated into the model and will enable participants to combine school and work and advance in their careers over time.

title: Adult Career Pathway Program
description: This grant will support the Adult Career Pathway program at Mott Community College. The program will leverage many of the college’s existing educational and training programs to help connect unemployed adults, low-income workers and youth to employment and a career pathway. The goal is to ensure that area residents can enter and advance into higher-wage occupations in high-growth industries. Work experience and support services are integrated into the model and will enable participants to combine school and work and advance in their careers over time.

title: Flint STRIVE Replication Program
description: The Flint STRIVE Replication Program, a project of Specialized Employment Services, Inc., provides employment training, job placement and support services for hard-to-serve Flint area residents. A replication of the East Harlem Employment Service’s workforce training program, Flint STRIVE prepares participants for the workforce through a 15-day, intensive workshop that emphasizes the attitudinal prerequisites for successful employment.

title: Flint STRIVE Replication Program
description: The Flint STRIVE replication program, a project of Specialized Employment Services, Inc., provides employment training, job placement and support services for hard-to-serve Flint area residents. A replication of the East Harlem Employment Service’s workforce training program (STRIVE New York), Flint STRIVE prepares participants for the workforce through a 15-day, intensive workshop that emphasizes the attitudinal prerequisites for successful employment.

title: Flint STRIVE Academy Youth Empowerment Program
description: This grant to Specialized Employment Services, Inc. will support the Flint STRIVE Academy Youth Empowerment Program for at-risk youth ages 14 to 18. The program provides young people with a summertime employment experience and follow-up support services during the school year. Through attitudinal training, skill enhancement, mentoring and tutoring, the goal is to encourage youth to complete high school and help with making informed career decisions.

title: Flint STRIVE Academy Youth Empowerment Program
description: This grant to Specialized Employment Services, Inc. will support the Flint STRIVE Academy Youth Empowerment Program for at-risk youth ages 14 to 18. The program provides young people with a summertime employment experience, and follow-up support services during the school year. Through attitudinal training, skill enhancement, mentoring and tutoring, the goal is to encourage youth to complete high school and to help with making informed career decisions.

title: Employment Preparation Program
description: This grant will provide support to the St. Luke N.E.W. Life Center for their Employment Preparation Program. Serving the residents of North Flint, the program works with individuals who are structurally unemployed and are in need of a broad array of wraparound services to prepare them for obtaining and retaining employment. The program will continue to expand its outreach to employers for future job placements and will offer an alumni network to support participants and past graduates.

title: Employment Preparation Program
description: This grant will provide support to the St. Luke N.E.W. Life Center for its Employment Preparation Program. Serving the residents of North Flint, the program works with individuals who are structurally unemployed and are in need of a broad array of wraparound services to prepare them for obtaining and retaining employment. The program will continue to expand its outreach to employers for future job placements and will offer an alumni network to support participants and past graduates.

title: School and Community Programming
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: Flint Cultural Center Corporation provides opportunities for city of Flint and Genesee County underserved youth and residents of all ages to participate in the face-to-face and/or virtual educational and community engagement activities provided by the Flint Cultural Center campus institutions. The Flint Cultural Center Corporation includes Sloan Museum and Longway Planetarium, Flint Institute of Arts and Flint Institute of Music, and The Whiting and Capitol Theatre.

title: School and Community Programming
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: Flint Cultural Center Corporation provides opportunities for city of Flint and Genesee County underserved youth and residents of all ages to participate in the face-to-face and/or virtual educational and community engagement activities provided by the Flint Cultural Center campus institutions. The Flint Cultural Center Corporation includes Sloan Museum of Discovery and Longway Planetarium, Flint Institute of Arts and Flint Institute of Music, including The Whiting and Capitol Theatre.

title: Operating Support
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Flint Institute of Arts, located on the Flint Cultural Center campus, features museum galleries, a media arts space, an art school, studio space and public areas that engage visitors and attract new audiences from across the region. Students and adults visit the galleries, participate in educational programs, take art classes or attend events held at the institute. This grant will provide operating support to enable the grantee to present new exhibits that inspire and stimulate visitors, provide educational programming to area students, offer instruction in various art mediums to people of all ages, provide community events and programming and maintain its facilities.

title: General Purposes
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Flint Institute of Arts — located on the Flint Cultural Center campus — features museum galleries, a media arts space, an art school, studio space and public areas that engage visitors and attract new audiences from across the region. Students and adults visit the galleries, participate in educational programs, take art classes or attend events held at the institute. This grant will provide general purposes support to enable the grantee to present new exhibits that inspire and stimulate visitors, provide educational programming to area students, offer instruction in various art mediums to people of all ages, provide community events and programming and maintain its facilities.

title: Music Around Town
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Music Around Town series, formerly known as Music in the Parks, is a broad community partnership led by the Flint Institute of Music. This program offers musical performances in public places around Flint which are streamed through social media platforms. Additionally, this year’s Music Around Town series will continue to offer pop-up performances honoring frontline workers. The public locations offer residents access to multiple free performances of the musicians from the Flint Symphony Orchestra.

title: Music Around Town
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Music Around Town series, formerly known as Music in the Parks, is a broad community partnership led by the Flint Institute of Music. This program offers musical performances in public places around Flint and Genesee County which are also streamed through social media platforms. The public locations offer residents access to multiple free performances of the musicians from the Flint Symphony Orchestra, Flint School of Performing Arts, Flint Repertory Theatre and other local talent.

title: Overture Program and Partnership with Flint Institute of Music
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This renewal grant will provide support to the Sphinx Organization to offer a continuum of music instruction and cultural experiences to underserved students in Flint. The Sphinx Overture program, which introduces students to classical music and violin, serves all Flint public elementary schools. In partnership with YouthQuest and Crim Fitness Foundation, the program will provide students with free afterschool group violin lessons. Through a partnership with the Flint Institute of Music, students from the program will be eligible for more advanced violin lessons and classes at no cost.

title: Overture Program and Partnership with Flint Institute of Music
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This renewal grant will provide support to the Sphinx Organization to offer a continuum of music instruction and cultural experiences to underserved students in Flint. The Sphinx Overture program, which introduces students to classical music and violin, serves all Flint public elementary schools as well as community organizations such as Boys and Girls Clubs of Greater Flint. The program will provide students with free afterschool group violin lessons. Through a partnership with the Flint Institute of Music, students from the program will be eligible for more advanced violin lessons and classes at no cost.

title: Tapology Youth Outreach
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide partial support for Tapology outreach programs. Tap dance is an enduring American art form that increases physical activity and enhances cognitive development for participants. The grantee partners with local schools and community centers to provide area youth with an introduction to tap dance and offers regular classes for all levels of ability. Each year, the grantee’s outreach programming culminates into a four-day festival that provides exposure for local students to the art and history of tap. Professional artists will continue to provide instruction for beginners, as well as more advanced workshops for experienced young dancers.

title: Tapology Youth Outreach
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide partial support for Tapology Outreach programs. Tap dance is an enduring American art form that increases physical activity and enhances cognitive development for participants. The grantee partners with local schools and community centers to provide area youth with an introduction to tap dance and offers regular classes for all levels of ability. Each year, the grantee’s outreach programming culminates into a four-day festival that provides exposure for local students to the art and history of tap. Professional artists will continue to provide instruction for beginners, as well as more advanced workshops for experienced young dancers.

title: General Purposes
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant provides general purposes support to the Buckham Fine Arts Project, also known as Buckham Gallery. Over the past 30 plus years, the grantee has held more than 300 exhibitions of: 1) visual art; 2) poetry readings; 3) performance art events; and 4) dance, music and film presentations. The grantee showcases local, regional and international artists. Located in a storefront space on the corner of South Saginaw and Second Streets, Buckham Gallery programming has included monthly open mic nights, family art activities and residency programs.

title: General Purposes
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant provides funding to the Buckham Fine Arts Project, also known as Buckham Gallery. For more than 30 years, the grantee has held over 300 exhibitions including: 1) visual art; 2) poetry readings; 3) performance art events; and 4) dance, music and film presentations. The grantee showcases local, regional and international artists. Located in a storefront space on the corner of South Saginaw and Second streets, Buckham Gallery programming has included monthly open mic nights, family art activities and residency programs.

title: Event Policing and Public Safety
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide funds to support public safety enforcement and traffic control activities for festivals and events primarily in the downtown Flint area. Free and low-cost events are very important to the vitality of the city and the people who live here. Public safety is an essential component of the success of the festivals that take place in Flint and attract thousands of exhibitors and participants. The city of Flint is not in a financial position to provide the necessary additional police services due to a decline in municipal revenues.

title: Neighborhood Arts and Cultural Events
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will support arts and culture projects through the Neighborhood Small Grants Program at the Community Foundation of Greater Flint. Neighborhood groups will implement resident-led efforts to create or enhance and expand existing artistic projects, events and performances. Funded projects will aim to stimulate civic engagement, improve neighborhood conditions, provide opportunities for self-expression and enhance skills for residents to work together creatively.

title: Neighborhood Arts and Cultural Events
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will support arts and culture projects through the Neighborhood Small Grants Program at the Community Foundation of Greater Flint. Neighborhood groups will implement resident-led efforts to create or enhance and expand existing artistic projects, events and performances. Funded projects will aim to stimulate civic engagement, improve neighborhood conditions, provide opportunities for self expression and enhance skills for residents to work together creatively.

title: Flint Fireworks
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to the Flint Downtown Development Authority will support a fireworks display for the 2022 Flint Juneteenth celebration. The grantee and several community partners, including the city of Flint, have organized a series of family friendly activities for a three-day Juneteenth celebration, including a parade from City Hall to Berston Field House. The events aim to bring the community together to commemorate the end of slavery.

title: Neighborhood Murals
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide funds for the Flint Public Art Project to design and create murals in Flint neighborhoods. The murals engage the Flint community, attract visitors, beautify neighborhoods and support economic development. The grantee will continue to feature the works of local and national talent over the next year and offer programming that engages neighborhoods in the design and implementation process through workshops, festivals and other programming with the artists.

title: Neighborhood Murals
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide funds for the Flint Public Art Project to design and create murals in Flint neighborhoods. The murals provide a way to engage the community of Flint, beautify neighborhoods and support economic development. The grantee will continue to feature the works of local and national talent over the next year and offer programming that engages neighborhoods while following all public health guidelines.

title: Parade of Festivals
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Greater Flint Arts Council continues to provide leadership for a coalition of stakeholders aimed at improving the image of the Flint area, including downtown, through increased participation in festivals and events especially during warm weather months. This funding supports a series of events and marketing activities designed to maximize the impact of established events and to cultivate newer and smaller events in downtown Flint and neighborhoods throughout the city.

title: Parade of Festivals
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Greater Flint Arts Council continues to provide leadership for a coalition of stakeholders aimed at improving the image of the Flint area, including downtown, through increased participation in festivals and events, especially during warm weather months. This funding supports a series of events and marketing activities designed to maximize the impact of established events and to cultivate newer and smaller events in downtown Flint and neighborhoods throughout the city.

title: General Purposes
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant provides general purposes funding for the operations of the Greater Flint Arts Council, an independent organization which supports local artists and arts participants through several programs, including public festivals and events. With a goal of being a catalyst for diverse artistic and cultural programs for the region, the grantee enriches the community with an array of cultural services, programs and events. The grantee also administers two regranting programs that support regional artists and arts organizations.

title: General Purposes
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant provides general purposes funding for the operations of the Greater Flint Arts Council, an independent organization which supports local artists and arts participants through several programs, including public festivals and events. With a goal of being a catalyst for diverse artistic and cultural programs for the region, the grantee enriches the community with an array of cultural services, programs and events. The Greater Flint Arts Council also administers two regranting programs that support regional artists and arts organizations.

title: General Purposes
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant provides general purposes support to Red Ink Flint. The grantee operates Flint Local 432, a performance venue located in downtown Flint for artistic programming and community convening. In 2021, 114 events took place, including live and online music performances by local artists, as well as theater productions and other arts activities. Additionally, the grantee operates the Factory Two makerspace, which resumed limited operations in 2021 for youth and adult makers. Funds will support organizational, administrative and programmatic costs for Red Ink Flint.

title: General Purposes
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant provides general purposes support to Factory Two. The grantee operates Flint Local 432, a performance venue located in downtown Flint for artistic programming and community convening. In 2022, 156 events took place, including live and online music performances by local artists, as well as theater productions and other arts activities. Additionally, the grantee operates the Factory Two makerspace. Funds will support organizational, administrative and programmatic costs for Factory Two.

title: Arts Programming at Genesee Valley Regional Center
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide support for arts-based workshops to young people living at the Genesee Valley Regional Center, a youth detention facility in Genesee County. The Youth Arts Unlocked program has offered workshops at the center since 2011. The program uses a research-based, trauma-informed curriculum to deliver visual arts, dance, poetry, yoga and theater to boys and girls living at the facility.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support the Citizens Research Council of Michigan with its mission of securing good government for the citizens of Michigan. Good government is a government that is representative of, and responsible and accountable to, the public; effective in carrying out its responsibilities and providing services; and efficient in the use of its resources.

title: Education and Economic Development Initiatives
description: This renewal grant provides partial support for the Genesee Area Focus Fund and its supported organization, the Flint & Genesee Group, to deliver economic development and education and training services to the Flint area and build Flint’s economic resilience to recover from the Flint water crisis and COVID-19 pandemic. The Flint & Genesee Group increases business investment, job creation and industry diversification through business retention, expansion and attraction activities, as well as entrepreneurial support services. The organization also enhances the region’s economic competitiveness and quality of life by providing workforce education and training programming across all age levels, and by engaging in special initiative projects with strategic partners.

title: Economic and Entrepreneurial Outreach
description: This grant will support the Economic Development Administration University Center for Community & Economic Development at the University of Michigan-Flint. The center’s mission is to coordinate, inform and contribute to economic development efforts that cultivate innovation and advance high-growth entrepreneurship in the seven-county, I-69 Thumb Region. Additionally, the center supports applied research projects and provides technical assistance to economic development organizations, private businesses and nonprofits.

title: Economic and Entrepreneurial Outreach
description: This grant will support the Economic Development Administration University Center for Community & Economic Development at the University of Michigan-Flint. The center’s mission is to coordinate, inform and contribute to economic development efforts that cultivate innovation and advance high-growth entrepreneurship in the seven-county, I-69 Thumb Region. Additionally, the center supports applied research projects and provides technical assistance to economic development organizations, private businesses and nonprofits.

title: University Avenue and Downtown Blight Removal
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: The Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation is a supporting organization to the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation and a public charity that works to improve the quality of life of Flint residents. The grantee’s downtown revitalization efforts and investment in infrastructure provides people access to jobs, food, healthcare and other essential services. This grant will support the demolition of blighted structures and improved safety for University Avenue and downtown residents and college students living in the area.

title: Downtown Security
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This renewal grant will support the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation’s efforts to promote safety and security in downtown Flint. The grantee is dedicated to supporting revitalization projects that enhance quality of life and provide local and regional access to jobs, food, healthcare, and other essential services. The Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, a supported organization of the grantee, will contract with a security firm for guards to patrol the city’s downtown area.

title: Downtown Security
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This renewal grant will support the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation’s efforts to promote safety and security in downtown Flint. The grantee is dedicated to supporting revitalization projects that enhance quality of life and provide local and regional access to jobs, food, health care and other essential services. The Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, a supported organization of the grantee, will contract with a security firm for guards to patrol the city’s downtown area.

title: Operating Support
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will renew operating support for the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation and redevelopment work of its supported organization, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation. Both organizations have been leaders in efforts to revitalize Flint’s downtown district and will continue their focus on redeveloping properties for residential and commercial reuse, attracting new employers, and creating and enhancing community amenities for public use.

title: Flint Farmers' Market Operating Support
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will provide operational support for the Flint Farmers’ Market, a key institution in the ongoing efforts to revitalize downtown Flint and ensure residents have access to fresh produce and healthy meal options. Located in the Health and Wellness District, the market provides Flint residents with year-round access to fresh produce and locally grown foods. The market maintains an active calendar of community events, provides attractive public meeting spaces and supports food entrepreneurs through a commercial kitchen coworking space. The Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation is the supporting organization of the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, which operates the Flint Farmers’ Market.

title: What's Up Downtown Capacity Building
description: This renewal grant will provide support for the Greater Flint Arts Council to fund What’s Up Downtown, a placemaking project focused on programming in public spaces. The grantee will utilize the funds to support a full-time director for the project and leverage additional resources to coordinate opportunities for residents and visitors to enjoy and participate in family friendly activities in downtown Flint.

title: Capacity Building
description: This grant will help to build the staff capacity of Communities First, a nonprofit housing developer and community development agency in Flint. The grantee’s mission is to promote and provide an improved quality of life for residents of distressed communities through economic development and affordable housing solutions. This grant will partially fund staff positions related to real estate development projects, finance and fund development, marketing and family and community engagement programs, along with office technology upgrades and predevelopment expenses..

title: Home Ownership Improvement Loan/Grant Pool
description: This renewal grant will provide funds that will enable Genesee County Habitat for Humanity to continue its Home Ownership Improvement Loan/Grant program. This multifaceted program enables city of Flint residents who either cannot afford or do not qualify for other home improvement lending programs to address vital home repair needs. Needs addressed by the program include façade improvements, structural repairs, abatement services, accessibility modifications and any other health, safety or code related issues. Programs like the Flint Home Ownership Improvement Loan/Grant program help to strengthen neighborhoods and improve the quality of life for Flint families.

title: Flint BRAND Program
description: The purpose of the grant is to implement transformative projects that leave sustainable and positive impact on neighborhoods. Genesee County Habitat for Humanity works with neighborhood associations, block clubs and other local grassroots groups on leadership development and other forms of capacity building. This grant will provide support for the Flint BRAND Program, which builds the capacity of neighborhood groups to conceptualize, plan and assist in implementing projects. These projects will have an immediate visible impact on neighborhood conditions and improve Flint residents’ quality of life. Founded in 1990, Genesee Habitat for Humanity is an affiliate of Habitat for Humanity International, a nonprofit, ecumenical Christian housing ministry. Its mission is to bring people together to build homes, communities and hope.

title: Neighborhood and Community Planning
description: This grant supports the Genesee County Land Bank Authority’s planning and neighborhood revitalization activities. The grantee develops and operates a nationally renowned program to reclaim vacant and abandoned property and restore it to productive use. This function is overseen by a professional planning and development team that attracts resources and plans, coordinates and implements neighborhood interventions using a variety of tools and strategies. The grantee’s activities simultaneously enhance the quality of neighborhoods in Flint and promote citizen stewardship by engaging neighborhood groups in planning the disposition and use of vacant structures, as well as maintaining vacant lots.

title: Flint and Genesee County Community Development Project
description: The Local Initiatives Support Corporation provides grants, loans and technical assistance to community development corporations. The grantee will focus on community development and technical assistance as part of its Opportunity in America’s Neighborhoods strategy. The grantee’s catalyzing opportunity strategy brings together a comprehensive set of tools to increase incomes, build equity and grow wealth.

title: Capacity Building
description: Metro Community Development is a multiservice community development corporation dedicated to creating stable and vibrant neighborhoods in Flint and Genesee County. The grantee serves as both an intermediary and a direct service provider for federal and state programs designed to assist low-income residents. This grant will be used to strengthen the grantee’s asset development division, which includes the federal Community Development Financial Institutions program.

title: General Purposes
description: The Village Information Center was established in 1976 and has published hundreds of issues of the East Village Magazine. This grant renewal will allow the grantee to cover more newsworthy stories to keep Flint residents informed about their community and life in the neighborhoods. A companion website offers access to news captured in the magazine, as well as new information that does not make the magazine’s publishing deadline.

title: General Purposes
description: The Village Information Center was established in 1976 and has published hundreds of issues of East Village Magazine. This grant renewal will allow the grantee to cover more newsworthy stories to keep Flint residents informed about the public sector, community and life in the neighborhoods. A companion website offers access to news captured in the magazine, as well as timely information for residents and other readers.

title: Entrepreneurial Ecosystem Engagement
description: This grant will support SIPI to lead the coordination and alignment of Flint’s entrepreneurial ecosystem. The goals of this grant renewal are to: 1) increase awareness of resources available to local entrepreneurs; 2) support economic diversification by building on assets that provide entrepreneurs in Flint with a competitive advantage, such as healthcare and social enterprises; 3) convene regular meetings with entrepreneurial service providers; 4) collaborate and host networking and meet-up events for local entrepreneurs; and 5) develop programs to enhance coordination and communication among entrepreneurial service providers, business peer groups and prospective entrepreneurs.

title: Entrepreneurial Ecosystem Engagement
description: This grant will support SIPI in leading the coordination and alignment of Flint’s entrepreneurial ecosystem. The goals of this grant renewal are to: 1) increase the awareness of resources available to local entrepreneurs; 2) support the growth of mentorship in the Flint entrepreneurial community; 3) reduce barriers that limit access to financing and other resources for entrepreneurs from marginalized communities; 4) utilize data tracking to measure impact of the ecosystem; and 5) increasing the impact of the ecosystem through convening subcommittees focused on specific areas of the work.

title: Launch Flint Pitch Competitions
description: This grant will support the Ferris Wheel Innovation Center to organize and implement business pitch competitions in Flint. The grantee was established to help entrepreneurs in an economically disadvantaged community gain access to support that advances their business or product ideas. Pitch competitions are a way to provide struggling entrepreneurs with the resources needed to move their concepts forward. Competition winners will receive financial resources and all participants will receive mentoring from business professionals.

title: Launch Flint Pitch Competitions
description: This grant will support the Ferris Wheel Innovation Center to organize and implement business pitch competitions in Flint. The grantee was established to help entrepreneurs in an economically disadvantaged community gain access to support that advances their business or product ideas. Pitch competitions are a way to provide struggling entrepreneurs with the resources needed to move their concepts forward. Competition winners will receive financial resources and all participants will receive mentoring from business professionals.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support the Ferris Wheel Innovation Center located on the first floor of the Ferris Wheel building in downtown Flint. The grantee was established to help people in an economically disadvantaged community gain access to support that advances their business concepts. The goal is to foster education, encourage innovation and entrepreneurism and promote economic stability in Flint. Local colleges and nonprofits will partner with the grantee to provide joint programming. Businesses located in the building will offer mentoring and counseling services. Additionally, college students will be hired to work with users and gain practical work experience that aligns with their future career goals.

title: Flint Food Works Commercial Kitchen
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This renewal grant to the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation will provide continued support for the Flint Food Works commercial kitchen food business incubator located within the Flint Farmers’ Market. Flint Food Works has the capacity to incubate small food processors seeking to create products for distribution and prepared food for retail consumption. The program offers a unique approach to economic development by providing support to newly forming food entrepreneurs who often struggle to become viable businesses.

title: Entrepreneurship Network
description: The Mott Community College Entrepreneurial Network program is designed to develop student’s skills and knowledge to start their own business, work in a family business, expand a current business or seek employment in a small business. The program includes a solid base of business, analytical, personal and problem-solving skills, along with providing students with basic accounting, law, marketing and management knowledge. This grant will support the Entrepreneurship Network at Mott Community College to encourage students interested in entrepreneurship through a coordinated network of support, resources, knowledge and technology. The network will help expand programming and assist the grantee in creating an environment that encourages students to further develop their innovative ideas. Supporting entrepreneurship is a way to bring economic opportunity and prosperity to Flint.

title: Entrepreneurship Network
description: The Mott Community College Entrepreneurial Network program is designed to give students the skills and knowledge needed to develop their own business, work in a family business, expand a current business or seek employment in a small business. The network provides students with a basic business foundation through programming that includes personal finance, basic accounting, law, marketing and management. This grant will support the Entrepreneurial Network at Mott Community College to work with students interested in entrepreneurship through a coordinated network of support, resources, knowledge and technology. As a complement to Mott Community College’s Entrepreneurship & Small Business Management degree program, the network will help to give students a pathway to future economic success.

title: Teen C.E.O. Initiative
description: This renewal grant will provide support to Mott Community College for the Teen Creating Economic Opportunity Initiative. The goal of the project is to provide disadvantaged youth with a summertime opportunity to build their entrepreneurial business skills, explore higher education and investigate career pathways.

title: Teen C.E.O. Initiative
description: This renewal grant will provide support to Mott Community College for the Teens Creating Economic Opportunity Initiative. The goal of the project is to provide underrepresented and disadvantaged youth with an opportunity to build their entrepreneurial business skills, explore higher education and investigate career pathways during the summer.

title: Factory Two Project
description: This grant will provide support to Factory Two, Inc., to manage the Factory Two Project. Factory Two is an affordable community makerspace where creative people gather to work on product ideas and network with each other. In addition to Factory Two, the grantee operates Flint Local 432, a performance venue located in downtown Flint. With funding from the Mott Foundation, the grantee will continue to support operations and programmatic activities that increase membership, classes and available opportunities for local residents.

title: Flint SOUP Community Funded Micro-grant Program
description: This grant will enable the Flint SOUP Community Funded Micro-grant Program to continue operations and provide more opportunities for Flint’s underserved residents to participate in entrepreneurship. Founded in 2012, Flint SOUP is a project of the United Way of Genesee County. The program hosts micro-grant competitions where creators and entrepreneurs can obtain small amounts of financial support and technical assistance to invest in their ideas. While the program is designed to support entrepreneurship, it simultaneously fosters community engagement and resident participation.

title: Flint SOUP Community Funded Micro-grant Program
description: This grant will enable the Flint SOUP Community Funded Micro-Grant program to continue operations and provide more opportunities for Flint’s underserved residents to participate in entrepreneurship. Founded in 2012, Flint SOUP is a project of the United Way of Genesee County. The program hosts micro-grant competitions where creators and entrepreneurs can obtain financial support and technical assistance to invest in their ideas. While the program is designed to support entrepreneurship, it simultaneously fosters community engagement and resident participation in an economically disadvantaged community.

title: Flint-based Healthcare Startup Accelerator
description: For over 10 years, XLerateHealth has aimed to cultivate and grow impactful health care innovation throughout the country, particularly in regions where health care is underfunded and innovation is often unrecognized. While there are over 100 health care accelerators in the United States currently, the grantee was one of the first half dozen in the United States and the first health care accelerator in the Midwest/Southeastern United States. With renewed funding support, the grantee will continue to serve as an entry point for entrepreneurs working to create health care-related enterprises in Genesee County. Located in the Ferris Wheel building in downtown Flint, the accelerator aims to attract new businesses in the Flint area to spur economic growth and create job opportunities for local residents. As the regional health, science and entrepreneurial ecosystem continues to expand, XLerateHealth will play a key role in its build-out.

title: Soup Kitchens, Warming Center and Medical Transportation
grantee: Catholic Charities of Shiawassee and Genesee Counties
description: This grant will provide funds to Catholic Charities of Shiawassee and Genesee Counties that will enable the grantee to provide essential services to individuals and families in crisis. Supported services include the Center for Hope warming center and three soup kitchens, which provide warm spaces, personal need items and meals to vulnerable residents during the harsh winter months, and the St. Christopher Medical Transportation Program, which provides rides for chronically ill children and their caregivers to out-of-county medical appointments.

title: Soup Kitchens, Warming Center and Medical Transportation
grantee: Catholic Charities of Shiawassee and Genesee Counties
description: This grant will provide funds to Catholic Charities of Shiawassee and Genesee Counties that will enable the grantee to provide essential services to individuals and families in crisis. Supportive services include the Center for Hope’s warming center which provides a warm space for the unhoused for the months of December through March, meals for vulnerable residents via three soup kitchens, and the St. Christopher Medical Transport program, which provides rides for chronically ill children and their caregivers to out-of-county medical appointments.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to the Crim Fitness Foundation. Focusing on active living, physical fitness, nutrition and mindfulness, the grantee offers year-round programming for children and adults in the greater Flint area. The grantee also serves as the lead agency for the Flint Community Education Initiative, which provides access to a variety of wraparound health and educational services for many Flint students and their families. The Crim Fitness Foundation organizes and manages the HAP Crim Festival of Races which typically attracts more than 11,000 walkers and runners, as well as tens of thousands of spectators each year.

title: Double Up Food Bucks Project
description: This grant will provide support to the Fair Food Network’s Double Up Food Bucks project in Flint. The grantee provides incentives for supplemental nutrition assistance program recipients to purchase fresh fruits, vegetables and dairy products at the Flint Farmers’ Market and grocery stores in Flint. Good nutrition, especially foods high in iron, calcium and vitamin C, can help mitigate the impact of lead exposure to Flint children and adults. Started at five farmers markets, Double Up Food Bucks is now implemented at 234 sites in Michigan and is a national model for healthy food incentives across 29 states.

title: Flint Diaper Bank
description: This grant will provide funds to the Food Bank of Eastern Michigan to support the Flint Diaper Bank in providing diapers to low-income Genesee County residents. By utilizing the grantee’s integrated distribution system, the Flint Diaper Bank can ensure that diapers will reach the community’s most vulnerable families.

title: Nonprofit Capacity Building
description: The purpose of this renewal grant is to support the Nonprofit Center of the United Way of Genesee County, which offers a broad range of services to support nonprofits through capacity building, volunteer management and national service resources. Since the grantee began capacity building work in 2003, over 100 Genesee County agencies have received services that allowed them to help more individuals in need, leverage new financial and human capital and collaborate with cross-sector leaders to ensure alignment with community needs.

title: Nonprofit Capacity Building
description: The purpose of this renewal grant is to support the Nonprofit Center of the United Way of Genesee County, which offers a broad range of services to support nonprofits through capacity building, volunteer management and national service resources. Since the grantee began capacity building work in 2003, over 100 Genesee County agencies have received services that allowed them to help more individuals in need, leverage new financial and human capital and collaborate with cross-sector leaders to ensure alignment with community needs.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purposes support to the United Way of Genesee County, a health and human services organization serving the residents of Genesee County, through its community impact focus areas of education and basic needs. In addition to the core areas, the grantee provides nonprofit sector capacity programming through aligned fiduciary services, specific capacity-building activities, volunteering and national service support. The United Way of Genesee County was heavily involved in the response to the Flint water crisis and the community response to the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purposes support to the United Way of Genesee County, a health and human services organization serving the residents of Genesee County, through its community impact focus areas of education and basic needs. In addition to the core areas, the grantee provides nonprofit sector capacity programming through aligned fiscal sponsor services, specific capacity-building activities, volunteering and national service support. The United Way of Genesee County is a leader in responding to emerging community needs, including the response to the Flint water crisis and the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Flint National Service Accelerator Fund
description: The Flint National Service Accelerator Fund at the United Way of Genesee County helps Flint and Genesee County agencies leverage state and national service members through AmeriCorps and its affiliates. Flint area service members support projects aligned with the city of Flint’s master plan, emerging community needs and state and federal priorities. Focus areas in Flint include community education, public safety, nutrition and assisting Flint to recover and rise from the Flint water crisis and pandemic. Matching grants from the fund provide resources to local nonprofit agencies for the required member cost share, training and travel reimbursement. The fund is administered by the United Way of Genesee County, which also provides staffing for the Flint National Service Accelerator Initiative.

title: Berston Field House Capacity Building
description: This grant to the Friends of Berston will build organizational capacity in the areas of marketing and organizational sustainability. Friends of Berston’s mission is to impact the community through education, athletics, arts and community services. The nearly 100-year-old Berston Field House facility hosts a variety of events that bring residents together to celebrate with one another and to connect with programs and resources throughout the community.

title: Capital Campaign
description: This grant will contribute to the $2.5 million capital campaign for a new building for Crossover Downtown Outreach Ministries. The organization has operated in the downtown area for three decades, providing clothing and other items for families and individuals in need. The new, larger facility will increase its ability to serve the growing demand for services, including services that assist clients with addressing the root causes of poverty.

title: Immigration Services
description: Established in 1988, the Arab American Heritage Council serves the needs of Arab Americans and other recent immigrants in the Genesee County area through programming such as immigration services, civic engagement and cultural events. During the grant period, the grantee will continue to help immigrants from all backgrounds navigate the American legal system and become acclimated to life in the United States by providing immigration forums and educational workshops, assisting with immigration casework, offering translation services and leading citizenship classes.

title: Immigration Services
description: Established in 1988, the Arab American Heritage Council serves the needs of Arab Americans and other recent immigrants in the Genesee County area through programming such as immigration services, civic engagement and cultural events. During the grant period, the grantee will continue to help immigrants from all backgrounds navigate the American legal system and become acclimated to life in the United States by providing immigration forums and educational workshops, assisting with immigration casework, offering translation services and leading citizenship classes.

title: Maintenance of City Parks
description: This grant will provide support to the city of Flint to continue the maintenance of parks and properties along the Flint River comprising 532 acres. City of Flint parks provide recreational green space for residents and are utilized for a variety of activities. The importance of parks has been reaffirmed during the pandemic and as interest in outdoor activities continues to grow. This grant will ensure the city of Flint parks continue to be maintained to a level that gives Flint residents the opportunity to enjoy these community assets in a variety of ways throughout the year.

title: Maintenance of City Parks
description: This grant will provide support to the city of Flint to continue the maintenance of parks and properties along the Flint River comprising 532 acres. City of Flint parks provide recreational green space for residents and are utilized for a variety of activities. The importance of parks has been reaffirmed during the pandemic and as interest in outdoor activities continues to grow. This grant will ensure the city of Flint parks continue to be maintained to a level that gives Flint residents the opportunity to enjoy these community assets in a variety of ways throughout the year.

title: Community Water Lab
description: This grant to the United Way of Genesee County will support the operations of The McKenzie Patrice-Croom Flint Community Lab at the Flint Development Center. The McKenzie Patrice-Croom Flint Community Lab is equipped with state-of-the-art technology to test water for multiple contaminants. Scientists and staff of the lab, including youth, will work with residents to collect water samples, test for multiple contaminants, provide results and work with households to address any identified issues.

title: Mobile Mental Health and Outreach Project
description: This grant will provide support to Genesee Health System’s mental health and outreach program in Flint. The mobile clinic staff will provide mental and behavioral health services, education on other resources available to clients and referrals to other programs. This program serves adults and children impacted by the compounded trauma and stress due to the Flint water crisis and the COVID-19 pandemic. The grantee offers services both virtually and in person at locations throughout the community and residents can easily access much needed mental health support and other resources.

title: Soup Kitchens, Warming Center and Medical Transportation
grantee: Catholic Charities of Shiawassee and Genesee Counties
description: This grant increase will enable Catholic Charities of Shiawassee and Genesee Counties to keep its warming center open during the daytime hours, providing a safe and warm place for individuals and families to escape the cold. This expanded capability is especially important as the community responds to COVID-19.

title: Science Panel for the Amazon: Key Dialogues on Sustainable Development and Forest Conservation
description: Almost 17 percent of the greater Amazon and 20 percent of the Brazilian Amazon have already been deforested and the aquatic system disturbed. Scientists warn that this globally important tropical rainforest may never recover if the current development model driving deforestation and extraction of commodities continues. To reverse the trend, the Sustainable Development Solutions Network has coordinated a prestigious science panel for the Amazon to work with the international community, including international financial institutions, to propose a science-driven conservation and sustainable development model for the rainforest. This proposed project would support the grantee to conduct a series of dialogues with financial institutions and mainstream media to promote the science panel’s recommendations for forest protection and low impact economic development.

title: General Purposes
description: The Association of Charitable Foundations is the membership body for United Kingdom foundations and grantmaking charities. Driven by a belief that foundations are a vital source for social good, the grantee’s mission is to strengthen trusts and foundations to rise to the challenges of our time. These challenges include the cost of living crisis, rising inequalities, climate change and ensuring the sector is diverse, equitable and inclusive. To this end, the grantee engages in policy development, provides research and information and organizes a wide-ranging program of events and learning. The Association of Charitable Foundations has over 450 members.

title: Program Integration and Enhancement
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will support technical assistance to fully integrate the programs, staff and systems of The Whiting and The Capitol Theatre into the Flint Institute of Music operations. The grantee will work with a team of consultants to develop and implement a branding and marketing campaign, finalize job descriptions and recruitment plans for new positions and design and deliver staff and board training and professional development for the new organizational structure.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Wisconsin, Indiana, Pennsylvania, Michigan, Ohio, New York, Minnesota, Illinois
description: The Northeast-Midwest Institute is a nonprofit organization dedicated to improving the economic and environmental health of the Northeast and Midwest regions of the United States. Headquartered in Washington, D.C., the grantee provides data, research and policy analysis to inform state and federal policy reforms and programs. The grantee delivers federal freshwater policy education to stakeholders in the Great Lakes and will launch a new communications initiative and scale up its manufacturing policy initiative. This grant will support the Northeast-Midwest Institute’s general purposes, including its significant initiatives on the Great Lakes, workforce development, safe drinking water and watershed conservation.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Citizens Campaign Fund for the Environment
description: Founded in 1985, the New York-based Citizens Campaign Fund for the Environment is one of the largest and well respected grassroots environmental organizations in the state. The grantee leads public education initiatives to raise awareness and promotes efforts to protect the environment from ongoing threats to clean water, clean air and healthy communities. These initiatives connect those communities with policy decisions at the state level through coalitions and consensus building. With this grant, the Citizens Campaign Fund for the Environment will lead a range of statewide education initiatives including those that protect and benefit the Great Lakes and the people who reside in the region.

title: Great Lakes Collaboration in New York State
description: The Buffalo Niagara Waterkeeper is one of the largest and most successful conservation organizations in the Great Lakes region and is a powerful voice in western New York. The state borders two of the lower Great Lakes — Erie and Ontario — and the St. Lawrence River. Nearly 45 percent of the state’s land area is in the Great Lakes Basin, with over 400 miles of Great Lakes shoreline. Despite the enormous economic and ecological importance of this resource, officials too often cede priority to downstate New York. In addition, many communities along this freshwater coast are becoming more vulnerable to an unpredictable and changing climate. With support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee will elevate the spotlight of the state on its Great Lakes assets and challenges and will assist in raising awareness to a changing climate and steps needed to enhance resiliency and adaptation.

title: Strategic Planning and a Water Camp
description: We the People of Detroit is an important environmental justice group working on water policy issues in Michigan and nationally. Founded by five women leaders, the grantee has responded to water shutoffs, high residential water rates and pollution crises in their hometown and beyond. Support from Mott will help the grantee manage its rapid growth through strategic and succession planning. One of the grantee’s aims is to encourage youth to become more involved in their communities and take a more active interest in how they interact with water resources today and can impact water policy in the future. We the People of Detroit, therefore, will also use Mott funds to help launch a camp for urban youth in Idlewild, Michigan that will encourage careers in water science and stewardship.

title: Youth Empowerment Partnership Programme
grantee: International Academy Berlin for Innovative Pedagogy, Psychology and Economy gGmbH
description: The project goal is to bring about sustainable change in local communities across Europe through innovative approaches to youth empowerment and community development. The International Academy Berlin for Innovative Pedagogy, Psychology and Economy gGmbH provides technical assistance, organizes networking opportunities and coordinates joint initiatives for the Youth Empowerment Partnership Programme, a Europe-wide network of community-based youth projects. During 2021-22, the grantee supported 42 local program sites and project partners across 20 European countries. The grantee provided direct technical assistance to local program sites in the network, trained young people and community stakeholders on a range of topics and organized international networking opportunities for young people and practitioners. The International Academy Berlin for Innovative Pedagogy, Psychology and Economy gGmbH, based in Berlin, Germany, and its partners secured significant European Commission funding for a range of projects.

title: Capital Improvements: Boiler Upgrades
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will support critical capital upgrades for Flint Institute of Music facilities, including the Flint School of Performing Arts. The installation of new boilers, related electrical controls and ventilation and air filtration systems will increase air quality and energy efficiency for the facilities. During a typical year, over 100,000 people use Flint Institute of Music facilities for a variety of educational and performing arts programs.

title: Strategic Planning to Reopen K-12 Schools
description: This grant will provide support to the Council of Michigan Foundations to contract with an organization that will assist Michigan leaders with the second phase of a strategic plan for reopening of Michigan’s K-12 schools with a lens toward addressing the health issues that were exacerbated by COVID-19. The long-term success of students will be contingent on thoughtful and effective strategies that address the physical and mental health challenges they have experienced as a result of the coronavirus pandemic.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Hague Institute for Innovation of Law
description: The Hague Institute for Innovation of Law will work through four core competencies to advance people-centered justice. This includes accurately diagnosing justice needs in key countries, designing people-centered solutions, delivering scalable justice reforms and strengthening learning across networks of people-centered justice practitioners and policymakers. From 2023-24, the grantee completed extensive justice needs surveys in Tunisia, Uganda, Iraq and Colombia. Its people-centered guidelines on solving land and family disputes were put into practice in Nigeria. Similar guidelines for employment disputes were introduced in Tunisia. It supported 17 new justice startups to help bring innovative approaches to solving community justice problems to wider audiences. The grantee continued to play a central role in fostering international justice partnerships, including through its role in developing a justice financing framework aimed at supporting efforts to increase financial support to people-centered justice reforms globally. Established in 2005, the Hague Institute for Innovation of Law seeks to find innovative solutions to justice problems around the world.

title: Capacity Building
description: This grant will help to build the staff capacity of Communities First, a nonprofit housing developer and community development agency in Flint. The grantee’s mission is to promote and provide an improved quality of life for residents of distressed communities through economic development and affordable housing solutions. This grant will partially fund staff positions related to real estate development projects, finance and fund development, marketing, and family and community engagement programs, along with office technology upgrades and predevelopment expenses.

title: General Purposes
description: EnAccess, a Netherlands-based nonprofit organization, is committed to accelerating the development of economically transformative clean energy access solutions. With prior Mott support, the grantee has provided thought leadership to the energy access field, developed high-risk concepts that sparked innovation in the sector and strengthened its own organizational systems. With renewed support, the grantee will work to increase awareness around open source solutions for energy access by supporting the community of innovators, increasing the ease of adoption of new open source innovations and bringing experts together to build industry-wide standards to accelerate progress toward universal energy access.

title: Harold Alfond College Challenge Program Evaluation
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant will enable the Alfond Scholarship Foundation to continue implementing the Harold Alfond College Challenge Program Evaluation, the nation’s first statewide children’s savings account program. Anticipated priorities and activities during the renewal grant period include family outreach, stakeholder engagement, policy development and evaluation. The grantee will also advance field-building by utilizing and disseminating research findings from the first two grant periods to inform new program design innovations in Maine and nationally. Created in 2008 as a pilot program in Portland, Maine, the college challenge program automatically awards a $500 grant to every child born in the state as an incentive to catalyze educational savings and to help more children aspire to attend college.

title: Kindergarten to College Program
grantee: City and County of San Francisco
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: The City and County of San Francisco’s Kindergarten to College program was the first universal and automatic municipal children’s college savings program in the country. Since its inception in 2011, the program opened savings accounts for more than 40,000 students, the majority of whom are children of color, and has encouraged families, half of whom are low- and moderate-income, to save more than $5 million and earn millions more in program incentives. The Kindergarten to College program has also inspired replications in cities around the country. Renewal funding will support planning, evaluation and outreach efforts that help the grantee prepare for the next phase of program operations, which will include the launch of California’s statewide children’s savings account initiative and the first group of program graduates.

title: Promise Early Distribution Scholarship Program
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: The Wabash County Promise Initiative is a community-wide initiative designed to advance educational attainment and create a generation of educated, engaged and economically self-sufficient young people. This grant will enable the Community Foundation of Wabash County to further the design and implementation of the early distribution scholarship component, which models the use of children’s savings accounts as a tool to promote college-going identities, high school graduation and postsecondary success. The component also models how community foundations can support children’s savings account initiatives and demonstrate a promising complement to traditional scholarships.

title: Michigan Communities for Financial Empowerment Network
grantee: Community Economic Development Association of Michigan
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: The Community Economic Development Association of Michigan works to expand and strengthen financial security in communities across the state. During the grant period, the grantee will coordinate statewide engagement and education activities that increase awareness and support for Children’s Savings Accounts. Based in Lansing, the grantee is a nonprofit trade association serving community economic development professionals in Michigan.

title: Monitoring Environmental Impacts of Financial Flows for Infrastructure and Energy in South America
description: Ecoa – Ecology and Action is a science-driven nongovernmental organization working to strengthen social and environmental standards of public investment in energy and infrastructure in South America. Over the previous project period, the grantee worked with a coalition of organizations focused on environmental social governance at the Inter-American Development Bank, monitored Chinese and Brazilian development finance and focused on social and environmental impacts of hydroelectric projects proposed in the Pantanal, the world’s largest wetlands. During this grant period, Ecoa will continue work on monitoring investments in energy and infrastructure development in the region and reflect on accomplishments over this 22-year project.

title: South America Small Grants Program
description: The Socio-Environmental Fund CASA is a grantmaking and capacity-building organization focused on providing small grants to strengthen community, environmental and civil society organizations. Over the past grant period, the grantee went from making an average of 92 small grants a year to 400 a year, many addressing energy development impacts in the greater Amazon region of Brazil. This grant will renew support for the South America Small Grants Program to support local communities and groups working on issues of energy infrastructure and sustainable finance in Brazil.

title: Supporting the Energy Access Ecosystem
description: For Tanzania’s rural communities, low economic growth and inequality are ubiquitous. Their ability to access sustainable, clean energy can play a key role in addressing these challenges. To move forward, there is a need for renewable energy technical skills, entrepreneurial skills for small business development and capacity building to encourage local financial institutions to lend to the small businesses and their customers. This is the crux of an “ecosystem approach” to support local off-grid clean energy development and deployment. Fraxen Consulting has assisted in developing these capacity-building initiatives, particularly leading in the development of a new Tanzanian consortium to work on clean energy. With this increase, the grantee will enhance the coordination work among the ecosystem partners.

title: Great Lakes Islands Alliance
description: The Great Lakes Islands Alliance — a project of the Stewardship Network — is a bi-national, voluntary collaborative network consisting of nearly 200 island leaders from 20 islands in the Great Lakes region. With previous Mott Foundation support, the grantee was able to hire a project manager, expand its membership and increase its impact in these off-shore communities to protect and conserve natural environments on islands. With renewed support, the grantee will be able to strengthen the connections and communications among and between islands and islanders. Members will continue to seek and implement island-appropriate solutions to an array of environmental challenges, from rising lake levels to climate resiliency to water pollution, while advancing stewardship of island natural resources.

title: Flint Division of Public Health Expansion Endowment
description: Michigan State University has served the people of the state of Michigan since 1855 through its unique role as a Land Grant Institution. Its College of Human Medicine, founded in 1964, was the nation’s first community-based medical school. Building upon an active presence in Flint since the mid-1960’s, the College of Human Medicine launched Michigan State University’s College of Human Medicine’s Flint campus in 2011. With this grant, the grantee will increase the impact of its Flint Division of Public Health program by elevating it to a university department and hiring additional faculty, staff and endowed professors of public health. The program has a successful track record of engaging with Flint residents to improve health, contributing to the local economy and educating a new generation of health professionals.

title: General Purposes
description: The Michigan Environmental Council is a coalition of over 80 environmental and faith-based organizations. Since 1980, the grantee has been committed to: 1) addressing environmental threats to Michigan’s water, air and land; 2) inland waters and drinking water concerns; 3) sustainable agriculture; 4) clean energy; 5) environmental health; and 6) protecting the Great Lakes. With this grant, the grantee will focus on engaging members, community leaders and residents as effective local advocates for shared goals, and helping steer powerful, diverse collaborations and fortifying drinking water protections. The Michigan Environmental Council will seek to expand Michigan’s environmental movement, improve operational activities, strengthen Michigan’s environmental protections, ensure access to affordable drinking water and improve the ecological condition of the Great Lakes.

title: General Purposes
description: AdvocAid’s goal is to provide justice services, using a legal empowerment approach, to women and girls in Sierra Leone. To this end, the grantee will continue to provide justice services to women in selected cities in Sierra Leone, using a network of paralegals and social workers. The grantee will also represent women and girls in court, where the reasons for their injustices are systemic in nature. The grantee plans to continue monitoring police stations and correctional centers where women are held. Past support has allowed the grantee to deepen its justice services and address the lack of legal representation for women in Sierra Leone, while addressing the socioeconomic reasons women find themselves in the justice system. Established in 2006, AdvocAid is a human rights organization that provides holistic justice services to women and girls in Sierra Leone using a legal empowerment approach.

title: Strengthening Fundacion Emerger Colombia
