description: Asociacion Ambiente y Sociedad is a Colombian nongovernmental organization engaged in strengthening transparency and social environmental governance of development finance. This project will assist the grantee with incubating the Emerger Fund in Colombia to make small grants to local organizations working on energy and infrastructure finance and sustainable development.

title: General Purposes
location: Santa Cruz de la Sierra, Bolivia
description: The Fundación Socioambiental Semilla is a Bolivian nongovernmental organization founded in 2018 that provides small grants to local organizations and leaders to strengthen social-environmental governance of development project finance that impacts their communities. This grant will support the institutional development and consolidation of the grantee to implement a small-grantmaking strategy in five South American countries.

title: Strengthening and Consolidating the Socio-Environmental Fund Peru
description: Derecho Ambiente y Recursos Naturales is a Peruvian nongovernmental organization engaged in strengthening transparency and social environmental governance of development finance. This grant will enable the organization to incubate a Socio-Environmental Fund of Peru to make small grants to local organizations impacted by energy and infrastructure development.

title: Finance for Sustainable Development in South America
description: The Institute for Socioeconomic Studies is a nongovernmental organization established for the promotion and strengthening of representative and participatory democracy in Brazil. Over the past grant period, the organization established itself as a national and international technical reference in monitoring and reporting on fossil fuel subsidies in Brazil, led a coalition of organizations working to curtail the use of natural gas for electricity generation and made progress on strengthening safeguards and responsible exit from harmful projects at the International Finance Corporation — a member of the World Bank Group. A focus on promoting a clean and just energy transition, coalition building and strengthening safeguards will be priority themes for INESC over the next grant period.

title: Afterschool College and Career Readiness Initiative
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant to Nebraska Children and Families Foundation will enable the Nebraska Statewide Afterschool Network to increase the availability and expansion of college and career exploration, financial literacy or college affordability planning by enhancing quality afterschool and summer learning opportunities for underserved youth. This project will support the grantee to: 1) increase the number of college savings accounts and participation in financial literacy initiatives among youth and families; 2) create a scalable model to mitigate barriers associated with college affordability planning; and 3) expand the work with new and existing stakeholders to address the critical gap of youth and families engaged in financial literacy and career exploration. The grantee will share promising practices and resources with the Mott-funded 50 State Networks and Mizzen by Mott to enhance college and career readiness initiatives in afterschool programs nationally. The grantee is also a recipient of funding from the Advancing Afterschool portfolio as a statewide afterschool network. This grant will support the Nebraska Children and Families Foundation to build upon a specific opportunity within their state to leverage additional resources and partnerships for afterschool and summer learning programs.

title: Afterschool College and Career Readiness Initiative
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant to the Fund for Educational Excellence will enable the Maryland Out-of-School Time Network to increase the availability and expansion of college and career exploration, financial literacy or college affordability planning by enhancing quality afterschool and summer learning opportunities for underserved youth. This project will support the grantee to: 1) increase the awareness and participation in financial literacy and college preparedness initiatives among youth and families; 2) expand and implement professional development opportunities for afterschool professionals around college and career readiness strategies to support the afterschool community; and 3) engage new and existing stakeholders as thought partners to address the lack of supports for youth and families to engage in college and career readiness exploration. The grantee will share promising practices and resources with the Mott-funded 50 State Networks and Mizzen by Mott to enhance college and career readiness initiatives in afterschool programs nationally. The grantee is also a recipient of funding from the Advancing Afterschool portfolio as a statewide afterschool network. This grant will support the Fund for Educational Excellence to build upon a specific opportunity within their state to leverage additional resources and partnerships for afterschool and summer learning programs.

title: Afterschool College and Career Readiness Initiative
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant to Indiana Afterschool Network, Inc., will enable the grantee to increase the availability and expansion of college and career exploration, financial literacy or college affordability planning by enhancing quality afterschool and summer learning opportunities for underserved youth. This project will support the grantee to: 1) design and implement an innovative program model focused on college and career exploration and employability skills to be utilized in out-of-school time settings; 2) implement professional development strategies and resources for afterschool professionals to support youth engagement in college and career readiness initiatives; and 3) leverage relationships with key stakeholders to engage new partners in workforce development strategies across the state. The grantee will share promising practices and resources with the Mott-funded 50 State Networks and Mizzen by Mott to enhance college and career readiness initiatives in afterschool programs nationally. The grantee is also a recipient of funding from the Advancing Afterschool portfolio as a statewide afterschool network. This grant will support the Indiana Afterschool Network, Inc., to build upon a specific opportunity within their state to leverage additional resources and partnerships for afterschool and summer learning programs.

title: Afterschool College and Career Readiness Initiative
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant to the University of Missouri – Columbia will enable the Missouri Afterschool Network to increase the availability and expansion of college and career exploration, financial literacy or college affordability planning by enhancing quality afterschool and summer learning opportunities for underserved youth. This project will support the grantee to: 1) increase access to college and career exploration program models for youth and families through afterschool partners; 2) implement professional development strategies for afterschool professionals to offer post-secondary exploration learning experiences; and 3) engage new and existing stakeholders to expand partnerships in college affordability planning and workforce development initiatives. The grantee will share promising practices and resources with the Mott-funded 50 State Networks and Mizzen by Mott to enhance college and career readiness initiatives in afterschool programs nationally. The grantee is also a recipient of funding from the Advancing Afterschool portfolio as a statewide afterschool network. This grant will support the University of Missouri – Columbia to build upon a specific opportunity within their state to leverage additional resources and partnerships for afterschool and summer learning programs.

title: General Purposes
description: The YMCA of Greater Flint has long been an important part of the Flint community. The grantee operates three sites: a downtown Flint facility, a Pierson Road facility and Camp Copneconic. Since 1961, the headquarters building in downtown Flint has provided essential services for physical and mental health wellness, as well as serving as an important gathering place for the community. In recent years, the downtown location has been particularly important to low-income individuals, the elderly and communities of color who have limited access to wellness opportunities. Camp Copneconic also continues to be an essential service for youth across Genesee County. Although the grantee has still been providing essential services to the community throughout the pandemic, its revenue and fund raising have been significantly impacted by the pandemic. This grant provides two years of general purposes support to allow the YMCA of Greater Flint to maintain its services, including keeping the downtown location open.

title: General Purposes
description: Traditional and Indigenous forest dwellers in the Amazon rely mainly on canoes and boats to travel in the rainforest. Additionally, forest clearing for roads and other linear infrastructure brings deforestation and degradation in its wake. The Kara Solar Foundation and its partners in the Achuar territory of Ecuador have developed the first solar-powered boats and linked them to efforts to solarize their villages. This project will provide general-purpose support to replicate the solar transport and electrification model in other Amazon Indigenous territories in Ecuador, Brazil, Suriname/French Guiana and also in the Solomon Islands.

title: Renewable Loreto
description: Derecho Ambiente y Recursos Naturales is a Peruvian nongovernmental organization with offices in Lima and Iquitos, the capital of the Peruvian Amazon Department of Loreto. Over the last two years, the grantee began work to bring renewable energy to isolated communities in the Amazon. With this increase, the grantee will add additional photovoltaic systems to improve refrigeration and commercialization of fish resources, solar radios to improve access to education and reduce water contamination by single-use batteries.

title: Renewable Energy Access for Sustainable Livelihoods and Conservation in the Amazon
description: Access to modern, clean energy is a major challenge in the greater Amazon rainforest. This grant supports the World Wildlife Fund to expand and replicate renewable energy access in the Amazon countries of Bolivia, Colombia and Suriname. The grantee will work both regionally and nationally to overcome financial and regulatory barriers to renewable energy expansion and provide technical support for demonstration projects in the three countries.

title: Meals for COVID-19 Vaccination Workers
description: The demand for Genesee County COVID-19 vaccinations is very high, and volunteers are crucial to this effort. This grant will support the Genesee Chamber Foundation with providing meals to volunteers and health professionals working to distribute vaccinations in Flint and Genesee County through the health department. Additionally, meals purchased under this initiative will be procured from local restaurants in Flint, a high poverty and economically distressed community, to bring in revenue to an industry negatively impacted by the pandemic and executive orders to close.

title: Access to Justice in Remote Areas of Sierra Leone
description: The project goal is to increase access to justice for poor and marginalized people in Sierra Leone. To this end, the Legal Aid Board — Sierra Leone will continue to provide justice services to people in remote rural locations that are hard to reach. The grantee will also continue its outreach and training activities, including support for community advice bureaus. Past support has helped the grantee reach 175,776 people through a network of 13 community paralegals in hard-to-reach areas of the country. The paralegals also monitored local court proceedings and other justice institutions to ensure that due process and human rights were followed in their work. The Legal Aid Board was established in 2015 by the country’s Legal Aid Act, with the main purpose of providing free justice services to people in Sierra Leone.

title: Flint Healthcare Employment Opportunities Program
description: This grant to Greater Flint Health Coalition will support the Flint Healthcare Employment Opportunities Program. The goal of the program is to create sustainable employment opportunities and promote career advancement for area residents within the healthcare sector. Participants receive industry-focused life skills and career readiness training, occupational instruction, case management and supportive services, as well as job development assistance.

title: Flint Healthcare Employment Opportunities Program
description: This grant to Greater Flint Health Coalition will support the Flint Healthcare Employment Opportunities Program. The goal of the program is to create sustainable employment opportunities and promote career advancement for area residents within the healthcare sector. Participants receive industry-focused life skills and career readiness training, occupational instruction, case management and supportive services, as well as job development assistance.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purpose support to the Hlanganisa Institute of Development Southern Africa NPC as it continues its efforts to increase access to justice for poor and marginalized people in South Africa. During this grant period, the grantee will support a network of community advice offices with financial and training resources to provide justice services. Past support has helped the grantee to provide resources to community advice offices in the Free State province of South Africa. The grantee is a leading grantmaker for community organizations in South Africa and has extensive reach in rural areas, where in many instances, advice offices are the only institutions providing free justice services.

title: General Purposes
description: Hlanganisa Community Fund NPC’s goal is to increase access to justice for poor and marginalized people in South Africa. To this extent, the grantee plans to continue supporting a network of community advice offices with resources to provide quality justice services. The grantee also plans to address systemic gender and youth marginalization by empowering women and youth in advice offices with leadership capabilities, while building these offices to be secure and sustainable. The grantee will pilot a roving paralegal clinic in areas where there are no advice offices. Past support has helped the grantee to increase the number of advice offices it supports while deepening its accompaniment to these offices. It also successfully raised funds from other sources to support its work with community organizations. Hlanganisa Community Fund NPC is a leading grantmaker for community organizations in South Africa and has extensive reach in rural areas, where in many instances, advice offices are the only institutions providing free justice services.

title: Capacity Building
description: This grant increase will help to build the staff capacity of Communities First, a nonprofit housing developer and community development agency in Flint. The grantee’s mission is to promote and provide an improved quality of life for residents of distressed communities through economic development and affordable housing solutions. This increase will partially fund positions related to project and fund development, strategic planning and office management and predevelopment expenses.

title: Flint Institute of Science and History Museum Technical Assistance and Planning
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide funds for the Flint Cultural Center Corporation to complete a due diligence and strategic planning process for the Sloan Museum to become an independent nonprofit organization called the Flint Institute of Science and History. The newly renovated museum will serve Flint area children and families, beginning in early childhood, and offer expanded STEAM programming and activities.

title: VISTA Project
description: This grant will allow the Afterschool Alliance to continue deploying AmeriCorps VISTA members as a critical asset to the growth and sustainability of statewide afterschool networks. Dedicated to the efforts of improving the afterschool networks and programs who serve underserved communities and families, Alliance VISTAs have been instrumental in maintaining and expanding the necessary facets of quality programming for young people. This grant will support 25 VISTAs in networks to address the following: combating childhood hunger and nutrition through adoption of meals programs; introduce and expand quality STEM learning; increasing access to high quality educational programming for young people of color; and support afterschool programs and staff in response to the substance misuse crisis.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant increase will enable the Afterschool Alliance to provide additional support to afterschool programs and state afterschool networks serving young people during the pandemic. Specifically, this increase will support: increased technical assistance to afterschool programs and schools regarding learning recovery strategies and resources, expanded outreach and communications tools about federal and state education policies and plans, and additional technical assistance for statewide afterschool networks regarding the American Rescue Plan.

title: Equity and Leadership Development
grantee: New York State Network for Youth Success, Inc.
description: This grant will support the New York State Network for Success — Network for Youth Success — to collaborate with the Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative and the 50 State Afterschool Network to support the statewide afterschool networks with advancing equity centered initiatives through their policies, practices and programs.

title: Afterschool Education and Outreach Project
description: This grant will provide support to Collaborative Communications Group to continue to build the capacity of the 50 State Afterschool Network ecosystem and the afterschool field in the areas of policy analysis, communications and research. To advance afterschool programs, this project will build bridges between local, state and federal governments and the afterschool field and will assist the networks as they navigate new federal, state and local education policies impacting afterschool programs.

title: General Purposes
description: The E-LICO Foundation, a development nonprofit in Tanzania focused on sustainable energy solutions, is developing successful model projects demonstrating how distributed renewable energy, particularly solar, can be used to support productive economic uses that build local economies and reduce environmental impact. Additional general support will enable the grantee to expand this work, including in the Dodoma region of Tanzania.

title: Mizzen by Mott Content Development
description: This grant will support Jazz at Lincoln Center and their afterschool partners to implement engagement and marketing strategies to expand user engagement and Mizzen by Mott brand awareness among the out-of-school time community. The grantee will partner with Mizzen to bring high-quality content and resources to afterschool and summer learning professionals to engage youth through a one-of-a-kind interactive jazz curriculum that supports youth voice, academic enrichment, STEM and arts-based learning experiences. The multi-media marketing approach will be implemented through a series of events and professional development opportunities throughout the year with national and regional afterschool partners.

title: Coalition for Community Schools
description: This grant will provide support to the Coalition for Community Schools, a project of the Institute for Educational Leadership, to strengthen the integration of community schools and afterschool to reach more children, youth, and families. Specifically, this grant will support the coalition to: 1) build strong connections and partnerships between community schools and the statewide afterschool networks; 2) align and build capacity to increase and sustain afterschool through community schools; and 3) identify and create synergies between community schools and afterschool standards, professional development and training.

title: STEM Fellowship
description: This grant to the STEM Next Opportunity Fund will support the Afterschool and Summer Learning Fellowship and the Robert Noyce-Ellen Lettvin Fellowship in informal STEM learning. The fellowships are a public-private partnership initiative geared toward advancing high-quality afterschool, summer learning and informal STEM learning. This initiative will: 1) strengthen collaboration between the U.S. Department of Education and other federal agencies in the areas of afterschool and informal STEM learning; 2) work to advance afterschool and STEM learning in the 21st Century Community Learning Centers program; and 3) work with leading researchers to identify priorities, new tools, strategies and programs that improve afterschool and STEM learning opportunities.

title: Governor's Service Awards Fund
description: This grant will enable the Michigan Nonprofit Association to support the work of the Michigan Community Service Commission, the state’s lead agency on service and volunteerism. Specifically, this grant will support the Michigan Community Service Commission to host the Governor’s Service Awards to assist in the continued growth and celebration of service and volunteerism in the state.

title: Engaging Youth in Service
description: Engaging young people in quality service and service-learning opportunities is a proven method to build 21st century skills. This grant will provide continued and increased support to Youth Service America as they continue to push their National Days of Service program to reach more young people — focusing on youth of color and underserved youth — with the opportunity to serve their community. Through the program, Youth Service America funds, trains, and provides additional capacity building for K-12 schools, afterschool programs, nonprofits and community organizations as they support young people in designing and leading service projects. In addition to supporting Youth Service America’s National Days of Service campaign, this grant will continue to support bringing service to the afterschool networks through regranting and network capacity building. The afterschool work is due in part to a multi-organization partnership between Youth Service America, the Afterschool Alliance and the National Youth Leadership Council.

title: Expanding National Service and Replication of the Flint National Service Accelerator Initiative
description: Service Year Alliance, based in Washington, DC, works to make a year of paid, full-time service an opportunity for all young Americans by expanding partnerships and awareness, shared recruitment efforts and lifting up the impacts of service. During the previous grant period, Service Year Alliance advanced place-based national service initiatives by convening more than 35 communities to highlight and learn from the Flint National Service Accelerator model and executed a challenge grant opportunity for four communities to expand their models and create funder partnerships. This grant will provide for individual and group collaboration support for place-based national service initiatives from around the country—including the Flint National Service Accelerator—to identify barriers to service, build stronger community relationships and disseminate lessons for the improvement of the national service field. Lessons learned from these pioneering place-based national service initiatives will empower communities to adopt initiatives of their own to generate a culture of service, address community-defined needs, grow local talent and develop cross-sector partners in the case making for greater investment in national service opportunities.

title: National Service and Volunteer Center Capacity Building
description: This grant to the United Way of Genesee County will provide capacity to support national service and volunteerism throughout Genesee County. National service members and volunteers provide critical resources to area nonprofits, government agencies and schools to help meet a variety of community needs such as blight elimination, neighborhood engagement, tutoring and mentoring.

title: Great Lakes Collaboration in New York State
description: Buffalo Niagara Waterkeeper — based in western New York on the shores of Lakes Erie and Ontario — is one of the largest and most respected conservation organizations in the state. The grantee has a strong presence in the region and uses its voice to bring attention to water quality and climate issues impacting New York and the Great Lakes. The grantee raises public awareness of these issues which has helped advance policies and increase environmental protections of and investments in the Great Lakes. With support from the Mott Foundation, Buffalo Niagara Waterkeeper will continue to: 1) elevate the profile of western New York in the state; 2) support critical water quality protection efforts; 3) enhance climate resilience, especially in vulnerable coastal communities; and 4) address ongoing threats to the Great Lakes which challenge the region.

title: Science Panel for the Amazon: Key Dialogues on Sustainable Development and Forest Conservation
description: More than 240 scientists and researchers came together in 2020 to form the world’s first high-level science initiative dedicated to the survival of the Amazon basin. Convened under the auspices of the Sustainable Development Solutions Network, this Science Panel for the Amazon launched its first Amazon Assessment Report as well as three policy briefs over the previous project period, all of which garnered good media attention. A presentation of the Panel’s findings and recommendations were also held with key development banks and leaders at the international Climate Conference in 2022. During this grant period, the grantee will continue analysis and dialogues with financial institutions, including mapping the key finance institutions operating in the Amazon, particularly for energy and infrastructure. Policy briefs and dialogues with development finance institutions will promote the Panel’s recommendations and new ways of mobilizing finance for conserving and restoring nature, as well as for sustainable low-forest-impact development.

title: General Purposes
description: The Flint River and its tributaries are an important recreational resource for the region’s residents while also providing important habitat for a variety of freshwater species and other wildlife. The Flint River Watershed Coalition works to protect the Flint River and its tributaries. With this renewal grant, the grantee will maintain all of its educational, programmatic and outreach efforts, and attend to its organizational development needs.

title: Promoting Sustainability in Energy and Infrastructure Investments in Latin America
description: The Interamerican Association for Environmental Defense is a nonprofit environmental law and policy organization in Latin America and the United States. Over the previous grant period, the grantee monitored implementation and compliance with new safeguards policies and the exclusion of fossil fuel finance at the Inter-American Development Bank and worked to strengthen measures to improve protections for environmental defenders. Organization attorneys also worked on cases at the accountability mechanism of the Inter-American Development Bank related to large hydroelectric dams in Colombia, Chile and Guatemala. Over the next grant period, the Interamerican Association for Environmental Defense will continue to monitor the implementation of the new environmental social governance framework of the Inter-American Development Bank, strengthen strategies to protect environmental defenders and prepare a report on lessons learned over the course of this project.

title: Youth Entrepreneurship Curriculum for Afterschool Programs
description: This grant to VentureLab will continue to support spreading and promoting youth entrepreneurship opportunities for young people and to reflect the growth of entrepreneurship in the afterschool field. Since 2017, the grantee has provided training, technical assistance and professional development resources to the state afterschool networks, enabling the networks to increase the number of afterschool programs offering high-quality entrepreneurship education programming and has increased the number of youth who have opportunities to develop entrepreneurial skills and mindsets. During this grant period, VentureLab will continue its youth entrepreneurship capacity and ecosystem building for the afterschool field, including the 50 State Afterschool Networks.

title: Open Internet for Democracy Initiative
grantee: National Democratic Institute for International Affairs
description: The project goal is to build a network of champions to guide the development of an open and democratic internet and digital sphere. To this end, the National Democratic Institute for International Affairs, in partnership with the Center for International Private Enterprise and the Center for International Media Assistance, implements the Open Internet for Democracy Initiative. The Initiative involves each partner carrying out a range of aligned activities, including community building, networking and capacity development for digital rights activists, leaders and organizations. As part of this initiative, during the grant period, the grantee will develop resource materials, design and conduct workshops for digital rights activists and strengthen leadership within the field. Founded in 1983, the National Democratic Institute for International Affairs is a nonprofit organization working to strengthen and expand democracy worldwide.

title: Empowering Midwestern Environmental Justice Organizations Addressing Water Equity
geographic_focus: Minnesota, Ohio, Indiana, Illinois, Wisconsin, Michigan
description: There are many water equity and ecological challenges that are disproportionately impacting communities of color in the Midwest, such as access to clean and affordable drinking water. The Midwest Environmental Justice Network, a project of the Minneapolis Foundation, focuses on building disadvantaged groups’ capacity in the Great Lakes to address water equity issues and other related environmental justice concerns. With partial Mott support over the next two years, the network will provide large and small grants as well as technical assistance to frontline groups to strengthen their internal operations and more effectively engage on a range of water policy issues.

title: Genesee Early College
description: Genesee Early College is an innovative, educational program administered by the Genesee Intermediate School District in collaboration with the University of Michigan-Flint. The focus of the initiative is to prepare high school students for academic and professional careers in any interest area but with a particular focus on health and STEM fields. Students can earn up to 60 transferable college credits, as well as a high school diploma and scholarship funds for higher education.

title: Genesee Early College
description: Genesee Early College is an innovative, educational program administered by the Genesee Intermediate School District in collaboration with the University of Michigan-Flint. The focus of the initiative is to prepare high school students for academic and professional careers in any interest area but with a particular focus on health and STEM fields. Students can earn up to 60 transferable college credits, as well as a high school diploma and scholarship funds for higher education.

title: Education Policy Institute
description: This grant will continue to provide funds for Furman University to operate the White-Riley-Peterson Policy Institute, which brings together a diverse group of 35 emerging leaders from the afterschool and education fields to serve as fellows. Over the course of a year, fellows will work with policy experts, complete an intensive policy curriculum and participate in national networking opportunities. The fellowship will enable participants to positively contribute to the development of policies and practices that support afterschool and summer learning opportunities for children across the country.

title: Operating Support
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Flint Cultural Center Corporation manages and maintains the 38-acre Flint Cultural Center campus which encompasses the Flint Cultural Center Academy; Flint Institute of Arts; and Flint Institute of Music, including The Whiting, Flint Public Library and Flint Institute of Science and History (Sloan Museum and Longway Planetarium). The campus contributes positively to the quality of life in Flint through educational and cultural enrichment opportunities and has a significant economic impact through earned revenue and employment. Students and adults of all ability levels participate in or attend a variety of cultural, educational and instructional programs and activities across the campus. This grant will provide operating support to the Flint Cultural Center Corporation for campus improvements, grounds and maintenance, marketing and campus security.

title: General Purposes
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Flint Cultural Center Corporation manages and maintains the 38-acre Flint Cultural Center campus which encompasses the Flint Cultural Center Academy; Flint Institute of Arts; and Flint Institute of Music, including the Whiting Auditorium; Flint Public Library and Flint Institute of Science and History (Sloan Museum of Discovery and Longway Planetarium). The campus contributes positively to the quality of life in Flint through educational and cultural enrichment opportunities and has a significant economic impact through earned revenue and employment. Students and adults of all ability levels participate in or attend a variety of cultural, educational and instructional programs and activities across the campus. This grant will provide general purposes support to the Flint Cultural Center Corporation for campus improvements, grounds and maintenance, marketing and campus security.

title: Flint-based Healthcare Startup Accelerator
description: For over 10 years, XLerateHealth has aimed to cultivate and grow impactful health care innovation throughout the country, particularly in regions where health care is underfunded and innovation is often unrecognized. While there are over 100 health care accelerators in the United States currently, the grantee was one of the first half dozen in the United States and the first health care accelerator in the Midwest/Southeastern United States. With renewed funding support, the grantee will continue to serve as an entry point for entrepreneurs working to create health care-related enterprises in Genesee County. Located in the Ferris Wheel building in downtown Flint, the accelerator aims to attract new businesses in the Flint area to spur economic growth and create job opportunities for local residents. As the regional health, science and entrepreneurial ecosystem continues to expand, XLerateHealth will play a key role in its build-out.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support the Ferris Wheel Innovation Center, an organization established to help people in an economically disadvantaged community gain access to support that assists in advancing their business concepts. The goal is to foster education, encourage innovation and entrepreneurism and promote economic stability in Flint. Local colleges and nonprofits will partner with the grantee to provide joint programming. Businesses located in the building will offer mentoring and counseling services. Additionally, college students will be hired to work with users and gain practical work experience that aligns with their future career goals.

title: Emergency Operating Funds
description: The purpose of the Flint Downtown Development Authority is to correct and prevent deterioration, encourage historical preservation, create and implement development plans, promote economic growth and redevelopment, and encourage the expansion of commercial enterprises, all within the downtown district boundaries. This grant will provide the grantee with emergency operating funds during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Mariachi Music & Folklorico Dance Instruction
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to El Ballet Folklorico Estudiantil will support mariachi music and folklorico dance cultural education and instruction in Flint. The majority of participants are Hispanic, however, the program is open to all interested young people. Program participants showcase their talent and newly acquired skills at in-person community events and virtual concerts. The program fee is extremely low and does not cover the full cost of staffing. This grant will help ensure continued high quality instruction and access for any child who wishes to participate, regardless of ability to pay.

title: Industrial Heartland Case Study
description: The Center for Automotive Research is a nonprofit research organization of professionals with knowledge of the transportation industry, high-level policy analysis and strategic planning skills. The global transition to a low-carbon future poses a set of opportunities and threats to the Midwestern automotive industry’s competitive advantage, as several forces align to bring about a vehicle electrification revolution. The Industrial Heartland Case Study project aims to better understand past automotive industry dislocations; the state of automotive, mobility transformations and workforce transition issues; and serves as a resource for stakeholders in Michigan and surrounding states.

title: Advocacy Training
description: This grant will support the Alliance for Justice in providing customized advocacy trainings and resources for the 50 State Network and afterschool grantees. The trainings and resources will build the capacity of the Advancing Afterschool grantees to educate policymakers and increase access to quality afterschool programs for young people.

title: General Purposes
description: The Detroit Regional Partnership Foundation aims to support the Southeast Michigan region with business attraction and economic development initiatives. The grantee brings a particular focus on job creation for the under- and unemployed as well as diversity, equity and inclusion so individuals and the community prosper.

title: General Purposes
description: The Detroit Regional Partnership Foundation aims to support the Southeast Michigan region with business attraction and economic development initiatives. The grantee brings a particular focus on job creation for the under- and unemployed as well as diversity, equity and inclusion so individuals and the community prosper.

title: General Purposes
description: The Detroit Regional Partnership Foundation aims to support the Southeast Michigan region with business attraction and economic development initiatives. The grantee brings a particular focus on job creation for the under- and unemployed as well as diversity, equity and inclusion so individuals and the community prosper.

title: Industrial Heartland Case Study on Environmental Justice
description: Massachusetts Institute of Technology’s Industrial Heartland Case Study on Environmental Justice project, part of the second phase of the Roosevelt Project, explores the challenges facing the United States economy as it moves through the global transition to a low-carbon future, including the challenges and opportunities around justice and economic equity in the Upper Midwest. With Mott Foundation support, the grantee will focus an equity lens on how the transition to electric vehicles will affect communities in Michigan and neighboring states, influence environmental policy and impact workforce issues.

title: Community Foundation Development in Uganda
description: The project goal is to develop community foundations in Uganda. To achieve this goal, CivSource Africa will increase awareness of, and interest in, the community foundation concept, produce tools to support the development of community foundations, generate a community of supporters for the concept and create a long-term strategy for the growth and development of community foundations. Established in 2017, the grantee promotes philanthropy and giving in Uganda. The grantee provides advice, technical support and grantmaking services to individual philanthropists and other philanthropic organizations in the country. In addition, the grantee strengthens the capacity of nonprofits, conducts due diligence and connects the two sides to build a stronger civil society sector in the country. As one of a few organizations in the country working to promote local philanthropy, CivSource Africa has produced learning products that promote local philanthropy and giving, participated in regional learning events on community philanthropy and supported local groups to raise resources and support from communities.

title: Community Foundation Development in Uganda
description: The project goal is to develop community foundations in Uganda. Over the past year, CivSource Africa conducted research in two districts to explore the development of community foundations. The grantee identified five initiative groups, produced learning materials and provided capacity development support to the groups. Over the next two years, the grantee will identify initiative groups in additional districts, provide support and tools to the groups, create a learning community and platforms, continue to popularize the community foundation concept and pilot local resource mobilization activities. Based in Kampala, CivSource Africa was established in 2017 to refine the practice and footprint of philanthropy in Uganda and the rest of Africa.

title: Community Foundation Development in Uganda
description: The goal of the project is to support the development of community foundations in Uganda. Previous support enabled CivSource Africa to support a cohort of 18 community foundation initiatives by providing customized training on leadership, resource mobilization and grantmaking. In addition, the grantee exposed the initiative groups to other programs and groups to strengthen their institutional capacity. Over the next two years, the grantee will introduce a group of leaders and community groups to the community foundation concept, build on the support provided to existing groups and support the emergence of a community of practice. Based in Kampala, CivSource Africa was established in 2017 to refine the practice and footprint of philanthropy in Uganda and the rest of Africa.

title: Community Foundation Development Project
description: The goal of the project is to strengthen and expand the community foundation field in southern Africa. To achieve this goal, SGS Consulting will continue to provide support to existing community foundation support organizations in select countries in the region while identifying opportunities to support the growth of community foundations in South Africa. Additionally, the grantee will support the growth of a community foundation network in the region, create spaces for mutual learning and provide custom-made technical assistance to community foundation support organizations. Past support enabled the grantee to identify initiative groups and work with them to become community foundations. SGS Consulting has also supported community foundation support organizations in five countries in the region.

title: TFN Global Service for Community Foundations
description: The project goal is to strengthen newly established and emerging community foundations in select countries and regions. To this end, The Funding Network, a giving circle based in the United Kingdom, will adapt and deliver a set of its global services to address the needs of emerging and newly established community foundations and community foundation support organizations in Africa, Europe and Latin America. The grantee will facilitate regional and international exchanges and will provide information, technical assistance and mentoring to its international partners. Established in London in 2002 by a group of private philanthropists with the mission to increase the level, scope and impact of charitable giving, the grantee now works in 25 countries around the world. With previous grant funds, the Funding Network supported partner organizations in 21 countries to organize 80 events and raise over $2 million for 234 social change projects with support from more than 5,000 donors.

title: Vital Signs - SDGs Community Engagement Platform
description: The program goal is to advance the adoption of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals by supporting a community foundation in Brazil, which can serve as a model to other community foundations in Latin America. Founded in 2005, the Instituto Comunitario Grande Florianopolis is Brazil’s first community foundation, serving the state of Santa Catarina. Several years ago, the grantee began to use the the Vital Signs community data mapping and reporting methodology first pioneered by community foundations in Canada. The grantee will build an interactive community engagement platform that will link the grantee with the SDGs, in order to better address complex issues in Santa Catarina. The grantee will then implement a communications campaign to raise awareness and engage people around the region’s main issues, aligning them and their efforts with the SDGs.

title: SDGs and Social Impact Investing for Community Foundations
description: The program goal is to encourage community foundations to advance the Sustainable Development Goals at the local level. To this end, Chicago Community Trust will develop a toolkit for community foundations, fund managers and donors to integrate the goals into their social impact reporting. The grantee will also explore the feasibility of applying the goals to document the holistic impact of community foundations and to communicate that impact to key stakeholders. The grantee will also assess opportunities to incorporate the goals into the way social impact investing is conducted, such as supporting fund managers of color and ensuring transparency with reporting. The Chicago Community Trust is one of the nation’s largest and oldest community foundations. Founded in 1915, its mission is to improve the lives of the people living in metropolitan Chicago, with a long-term organizational priority on closing the racial and ethnic wealth gap.

title: Promoting Learning Opportunities and Supports for Youth
description: This grant will provide support to Education Week, an Editorial Projects in Education initiative, to expand media attention and coverage around the evolving policy landscape and the intersection of the afterschool field within the education ecosystem. The data-driven initiative will bring increased awareness to out-of-school time issues as well as the impacts of afterschool and summer learning by highlighting program innovations, creative school and community-based partnerships and key supports needed to help young people thrive socially and emotionally in academic settings to recover from the impacts of the pandemic. Editorial content will be shared through a multimedia strategy including print, web, social, live forums and other platforms.

title: Afterschool and Service-Learning Initiative
location: St. Louis Park, MN, United States
description: This grant will support the National Youth Leadership Council to integrate service-learning into afterschool programs to increase student engagement in their schools and communities. The grantee will: 1) work with three statewide afterschool networks to deepen and expand service-learning into local afterschool programs; 2) create profiles on successful and sustainable integration of service-learning within the statewide afterschool networks and afterschool programs; 3) support a learning community to share information and best practices on service-learning in afterschool programs; and 4) research and create a multi-state analysis of policies impacting service-learning implementation.

title: Exploring Best Practice Models and Pathways for International Clean Energy Finance
description: Vasudha Foundation USA undertakes research, analysis and knowledge-transfers between countries in the Global South to improve access to renewable energy and increase international financial institution investment in clean energy. With prior Mott Foundation support, the grantee compiled and analyzed critical data on growing energy access in African countries as well as mapped out key projects and sources of finance. The information is used to underpin African civil society’s engagement with national governments as well as the African Development Bank and the World Bank. This grant will conclude this work by creating a repository of data recording progress on energy access and related investment from 2015 to date. Vasudha Foundation USA will also produce two public-facing reports documenting lessons learned, making recommendations for further engagement and identifying areas for future work.

title: Accelerating Pro-Poor Clean Energy Solutions
description: Access to affordable energy continues to be a major development challenge facing the world’s poor. With past Mott Foundation support, Oxfam America, an international development organization, has engaged with international financial institutions to advance clean energy solutions around the world, particularly in Africa. Over this grant period, the grantee will continue to provide research and technical support to partners in the Global South with the aim of increasing accountability for climate finance and accelerating the pace of a just and sustainable energy transition. Additionally, the grantee will document lessons learned over the past eleven years of the project.

title: Advancing and Protecting Sustainability Standards in Development Finance
description: Friends of the Earth — part of the largest network of affiliated environmental advocacy organizations in the world — will build on its longstanding successful efforts to reform critical international financial institutions, particularly in the energy, extractive and natural resources sectors. With renewed support, the grantee seeks to expand its work on encouraging Chinese financial institutions to implement environmental and social standards and take concrete steps to limit or reduce environmental harm in development finance. The grantee’s Banks and Biodiversity initiative encourages Chinese and other trend-setting banks to adopt “No Go” (off-limits) policies for financing in or near vulnerable geographic areas. Friends of the Earth blends advocacy, research and deepened engagement at the institutional and project levels.

title: Great Lakes Leadership Summit
grantee: Conference of Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Governors and Premiers
geographic_focus: Indiana, Pennsylvania, Ohio, Minnesota, Illinois, Michigan, New York, Wisconsin
description: The Conference of Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Governors and Premiers is an important organization in the region, providing a platform for the chief executives of the eight Great Lakes states and two Canadian provinces to convene and help advance protection and encourage sustainable development of this finite resource. With support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee will host a leadership summit in Cleveland, Ohio which serves as a launching pad for critical projects that benefit the environment and citizens in the region. Held every two years, the summit brings together hundreds of leaders to focus on the most important issues facing the Great Lakes and sets an agenda for policy moving forward.

title: Helping Cities Finance Water Improvements
description: The Michigan Municipal League Foundation is dedicated to making Michigan’s communities better by innovating programs, connecting ideas and people, serving members with resources and services and inspiring positive change for Michigan communities. Michigan has an estimated $800 million annual gap in needed investments in drinking water and wastewater infrastructure. While funding to help meet part of this gap is increasing from federal COVID-19 relief programs and state coffers, many municipalities, such as Flint, need assistance in accessing these funds due to a variety of factors, especially lack of staff capacity. This project will enable the grantee to hire and embed two employees at the Michigan Department of Environment, Great Lakes and Energy who will target and provide direct assistance to these municipalities.

title: Partnership for Disaster Recovery and Resilience
description: The goal of this project is to promote the recovery and resilience of nonprofits and communities impacted by hurricanes Eta and Iota and prepare them to respond more effectively to future disasters. To this end, the Inter-American Foundation will provide grant support, through the Partnership for Disaster Recovery and Resilience, to civil society organizations that build community resilience; mitigate the impacts of extreme weather; and strengthen the economic, civic and social ties among community members. The grantee, an independent United States government agency, was created by Congress in 1969 to channel development assistance directly to the organized poor in Latin America and the Caribbean.

title: Afterschool Youth Entrepreneurship Initiative
description: This grant to the University of Hawaii will enable the Hawaii Statewide Afterschool Network to increase the quality and sustainability of afterschool programs across the state. This grant will support the network to: 1) continue to expand opportunities for youth to learn about and experience entrepreneurship in afterschool and summer learning programs; 2) strengthen entrepreneurial ecosystems; and 3) connect and align ecosystem partners to expand learning opportunities and create pathways to entrepreneurship.

title: Afterschool Youth Entrepreneurship Initiative
location: Salt Lake City, UT, United States
description: This grant to the Utah Afterschool Network will enable the Utah Statewide Afterschool Network to increase the quality and sustainability of afterschool programs across the state. This grant will support the network to: 1) continue to expand opportunities for youth to learn about and experience entrepreneurship in afterschool and summer learning programs; 2) strengthen entrepreneurial ecosystems; and 3) connect and align ecosystem partners to expand learning opportunities and create pathways to entrepreneurship.

title: Afterschool Youth Entrepreneurship Initiative
description: This grant to the South Carolina Afterschool Alliance will enable the South Carolina Statewide Afterschool Network to increase the quality and sustainability of afterschool programs across the state. This grant will support the network to: 1) continue to expand opportunities for youth to learn about and experience entrepreneurship in afterschool and summer learning programs; 2) strengthen entrepreneurial ecosystems; and 3) connect and align ecosystem partners to expand learning opportunities and create pathways to entrepreneurship.

description: This grant to the University of Missouri – Columbia will enable the Missouri Statewide Afterschool Network to increase the quality and sustainability of afterschool programs across the state. This grant will support the network to: 1) continue to expand opportunities for youth to learn about and experience entrepreneurship in afterschool and summer learning programs; 2) strengthen entrepreneurial ecosystems; and 3) connect and align ecosystem partners to expand learning opportunities and create pathways to entrepreneurship.

title: Afterschool Youth Entrepreneurship Initiative
description: This grant to the Massachusetts Afterschool Partnership will enable the Massachusetts Statewide Afterschool Network to increase the quality and sustainability of afterschool programs across the state. This grant will support the network to: 1) continue to expand opportunities for youth to learn about and experience entrepreneurship in afterschool and summer learning programs; 2) strengthen entrepreneurial ecosystems; and 3) connect and align ecosystem partners to expand learning opportunities and create pathways to entrepreneurship.

title: Afterschool Youth Entrepreneurship Initiative
grantee: Oregon Association for the Education of Young Children
description: This grant to Oregon Association for the Education of Young Children will enable the Oregon Statewide Afterschool Network to: 1) expand opportunities for young people to learn about and experience entrepreneurship in existing afterschool, STEM and summer learning programs; 2) connect with local, regional and state entrepreneurship organizations to help integrate entrepreneurship into afterschool and summer learning programs; and 3) partner with organizations such as chambers of commerce, businesses, career technical education and higher education to expand successful entrepreneurship models in communities of high need.

title: Afterschool Youth Entrepreneurship Initiative
description: This grant to Voices for Georgia’s Children will enable the Georgia Statewide Afterschool Network to: 1) expand opportunities for young people to learn about and experience entrepreneurship in existing afterschool, STEM and summer learning programs; 2) connect with local, regional and state entrepreneurship organizations to help integrate entrepreneurship into afterschool and summer learning programs; and 3) partner with organizations such as chambers of commerce, businesses, career technical education and higher education to expand successful entrepreneurship models in communities of high need.

title: Afterschool Youth Entrepreneurship Initiative
description: This grant to James Madison University will enable the Virginia Statewide Afterschool Network to: 1) expand opportunities for young people to learn about and experience entrepreneurship in existing afterschool, STEM and summer learning programs; 2) connect with local, regional and state entrepreneurship organizations to help integrate entrepreneurship into afterschool and summer learning programs; and 3) partner with organizations such as chambers of commerce, businesses, career technical education and higher education to expand successful entrepreneurship models in communities of high need.

title: Operating Support
grantee: Flint Institute of Science and History
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to the Flint Institute of Science and History will support the operations of the Sloan Museum of Discovery and Longway Planetarium. A new museum will include over 98,000 square feet of exhibits as well as educational and community programming. The new facility is slated to open in late spring 2022. The state-of-the-art Longway Planetarium offers multiple shows for all ages and programming both onsite and through virtual classroom support. Summer camps, workshops and a monthly trivia night are among other regular programs offered through the museum and planetarium. The temporary space at Courtland Center will remain open until September 2021 and has been well received by the public both before and during the pandemic. The space attracted new audiences and allowed longtime supporters and visitors to stay connected with Sloan during renovations.

title: Whiting Capital Improvements
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide the Flint Cultural Center Foundation funds for capital improvements to The Whiting, which were identified through a detailed facility assessment. Though the facility is generally in good condition, the upgrades and maintenance work will improve the overall operations of the facility and address a number of aging systems. These facility needs are typical of a venue that welcomes large groups of visitors over time. The Whiting is home to the Flint Symphony Orchestra and offers a broad range of public performances and activities including Broadway plays, comedy shows, high school graduations and holiday programs. More than 70,000 people attend events at The Whiting each year.

title: Audit Support
description: The City of Flint aims to be transparent and accountable to the public with its financial status. This grant will support the grantee’s comprehensive annual financial report which will be made public upon completion.

title: General Purposes
description: This renewal grant will provide general purposes support to American Gateways as they work to supply information and legal support to immigrants during relocation to the United States. During the previous grant period, the grantee conducted community outreach, provided legal assistance, hosted legal clinics and provided direct legal representation. During the upcoming grant period, the grantee will conduct community outreach and education on immigrants’ rights, provide individualized technical assistance on cases and directly represent individuals in the immigration court system. Founded in 1987, American Gateways provides quality, affordable and trustworthy legal services to the immigrant community in Texas.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Mexico, United States, Canada, Central America
description: Justice in Motion provides legal support to immigrants as they migrate from their home countries into the United States. During the previous grant period, the grantee facilitated cross-border collaborations, provided legal services to immigrants, hosted virtual trainings on migration issues and immigration law and reunified families. During this grant period, the grantee will work on asylum access and protection, labor migration under temporary foreign worker visas and reunifying families. The grantee was founded in 2005 and was originally called Global Workers Justice Alliance, focusing on providing legal assistance and expertise to migrant workers. In 2016, the grantee changed its name to Justice in Motion and expanded its mission to include humanitarian immigration and civil rights work.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purposes support to the Asylum Seeker Advocacy Project as they continue to supply legal resources and information to immigrants, as well as improve the systems that serve immigrants. During the previous grant period, the grantee conducted impact litigation that resulted in exponential growth, helped over 150,000 members receive work permits and supported more than 400 families in receiving justice. During this upcoming grant period, the grantee will respond to the ongoing needs of its members, expand its legal support systems and work towards system change through impact litigation. Founded in 2015 as an all-volunteer effort, the grantee joined the Urban Justice Center in 2016 as a fiscally sponsored project. In July 2019, the Asylum Seeker Advocacy Project became an independent 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization.

title: Migration and Forced Displacement Program
description: The project goal is to address the new and continued challenges facing immigrants throughout the Americas. The Hispanics in Philanthropy Migration and Forced Displacement Program accomplishes this through grantmaking, funder engagement, capacity building and communications efforts. During the previous grant period, the grantee served migrants through regranting to migrant-serving organizations, narrative change around migration, funder education activities and capacity and network-building support services. During this grant period, the grantee will regrant, increase donor awareness on migration issues, provide learning opportunities and continue to build a positive narrative around migrants. Founded in 1981, Hispanics in Philanthropy is the leading philanthropic membership organization for grantmaking in Hispanic and Latino communities. Hispanics in Philanthropy works across the Americas to strengthen Latino leadership, equity and voice by facilitating greater philanthropic investments in Latino communities.

title: General Purposes
description: The purpose of this grant is to help address the long-standing and emerging issues facing immigrants in the Americas. Alianza Americas’ mission is to bring about a more inclusive, equitable and sustainable way of life for under-served immigrant communities living in the United States and across Mexico and Central America. During the previous grant period, the grantee led delegations to Mexico and Central America, supported transnational coalitions and provided learning opportunities for multiple audiences. During this grant period, the grantee will: 1) strengthen transnational networks; 2) educate policymakers; 3) host delegations; 4) advocate on behalf of migrants; and 5) support its membership. Founded in 2004 by Mexican, Central American and Caribbean immigrant leaders, Alianza Americas is a network of over 50 members in 13 states, representing over 150,000 migrant families across the United States, with dozens of organizational partners in Mexico and Central America.

title: Expanding Distributed Renewable Energy in the Amazon
description: The Brazilian Association of Distributed Generation is a trade group of more than 400 companies working in the renewable energy sector. With prior Mott Foundation support, the grantee organized a second Amazon Forum and conducted a successful solar roadshow that visited 72 Brazilian cities and trained more than 2,000 people in solar energy use. With an aim to build supply chains and markets for solar energy in remote Amazon regions over the next grant period, the Brazilian Association of Distributed Generation will promote private-sector engagement and knowledge exchange as well as public training and adoption of solar through the continued roadshow and model projects.

title: General Purposes
description: Conservation and good natural resource management are essential for poverty alleviation, sustainable economic development, food and freshwater security, conflict avoidance and human health. To effectively address this set of interconnected issues, policymakers need high-quality information from trusted sources on a range of topics. Since its founding in 2010, the ICCF Group has served this educational role in the U.S. and internationally, currently supporting conservation caucuses in seventeen countries. With general purposes support, the grantee will continue to deliver a successful series of briefings, roundtables and workshops on a range of issues, including on forests and energy for federal policymakers in the U.S.

title: Meals for COVID-19 Vaccination and Hospital Workers
description: This grant increase will support the Genesee Chamber Foundation with providing meals to volunteers and health professionals at vaccination sites, as well as health care workers at hospitals in Flint and Genesee County as they continue to respond to the COVID-19 pandemic. Additionally, meals purchased under this initiative will be procured from local restaurants in Flint, a high poverty and economically distressed community, to bring in revenue to an industry negatively impacted by the pandemic with restricted capacity orders.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support the Center for Michigan in pursuing its mission of making Michigan a better place by encouraging greater understanding and involvement in policy issues among the state’s citizens and making sure their voices are regularly heard.

title: South Saginaw Street Corridor Property Acquisitions
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: The Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation will fund and direct the acquisition of vacant and blighted properties along the South Saginaw Corridor through its supported organization, Uptown Reinvestment Corporation. Uptown Reinvestment Corporation will perform due diligence and coordinate the purchase and maintenance of several residential, commercial and greenspace properties with the goal of preparing the corridor for potential redevelopment uses such as office spaces, residential housing and light industrial. This work will help facilitate business growth and support reinvestment in city neighborhoods.

title: Operating Support
grantee: Flint Institute of Science and History
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to the Flint Institute of Science and History will support the operations of the Sloan Museum of Discovery and Longway Planetarium. The new museum is around 107,000 square feet with permanent and rotating exhibits as well as educational and community programming. The new facility opened in July 2022 with a series of community tours and events. The state-of-the-art Longway Planetarium offers multiple shows and programming for all ages both onsite and virtually. Summer camps, workshops and monthly trivia nights are among other regular programs offered through the museum and planetarium.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Flint Institute of Science and History
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to the Flint Institute of Science and History will support the general purposes of the Sloan Museum of Discovery and Longway Planetarium. The new museum facility is around 107,000 square feet with permanent and rotating exhibits as well as educational and community programming. The Sloan Museum of Discovery opened in July 2022 and has seen record level attendance since that time. The state-of-the-art Longway Planetarium offers multiple shows and programming for all ages, both onsite and virtually. Summer camps, workshops and monthly evening events such as trivia nights are among programs offered through the museum and planetarium.

title: Understanding the Impact of Chinese Investment and Engagement in Latin America
description: The Chinese government is currently the largest lender and a major investor and trading partner for a number of resource- and biodiversity-rich nations in Latin America. Given the pressing need to accurately report on the environmental, social and governance dimensions of Chinese infrastructure and energy projects in this region of concern, China Dialogue was founded in 2008 by former BBC journalists to inform readers and push the boundaries of discussion on controversial topics. This grant will enable China Dialogue to consolidate and build on its recent growth in readership and reach, and to continue with its core mission of reporting on the China-Latin America relationship and its sustainable development challenges.

title: Land Water and Climate Justice Efforts in the Global South
description: Today, there is increasing global recognition that economic growth and prosperity in South and Southeast Asian developing countries, often driven by development finance institutions’ investments in infrastructure and energy, which requires rural community action to mitigate attendant social and environmental risks. Established in 1992 and inspired by the Jewish commitment to justice and “Tikkun Olam” (“heal the world”) ethos, American Jewish World Service has worked to build a more just, equitable and sustainable world through community-driven change, supporting 519 grantees partners in 18 countries. Grant support to the grantee’s Land, Water and Climate Justice program efforts in the Global South will help its team better provide financial and capacity-building support to its considerable networks of rural community partner organizations who lead such efforts in South and Southeast Asia, as well as to connect these networks to other Mott grantees active in these two regions.

title: General Purposes
description: With offices in South America, Asia, Africa and the United States, International Rivers is one of the most effective international, nongovernmental organizations working on river protection. By partnering with local communities in more than 40 countries, the grantee successfully promotes sustainable uses of freshwater systems worldwide. Additionally, the grantee plays a major role in international efforts to strengthen policies at public financial institutions. This grant will be available for the general purposes of International Rivers, including a review and revision of its strategic plan to achieve long-term sustainability.

title: Unlocking BNDES Operation Lifecycle
description: Founded in 2008, SITAWI Finance for Good is a Brazil-based nonprofit organization whose mission is to mobilize research and capital for positive environmental and social outcomes. This grant increase will support SITAWI to conduct research and prepare studies on the finance and social and environmental governance of oil and gas exploration in the Brazilian Amazon.

title: Capacity Support for Water Safety
grantee: Michigan League of Conservation Voters Education Fund
description: Michigan League of Conservation Voters Education Fund is a leader of efforts to secure funding and sound policies to protect, restore and enhance Michigan water resources. Through a recently formed water table, the grantee has been working with a coalition of state groups and frontline, community-based organizations to forge a collective plan for sharing information and resources, while coordinating strategies. Working together, the groups now focus to move from planning to implementing initiatives around water issues facing the state and its residents, including access to clean, safe and affordable drinking water, cleaning up and preventing pollution from the class of pernicious chemicals known as PFAS and funding to fix failing water infrastructure. The grantee will advance its goals through support to the members of the water table with regrant dollars, communications materials and support, lessons from successful initiatives in other states and coordination and capacity support to advance collective initiatives.

title: Regional Cooperation on Aquatic Invasive Carp
description: This project will support engagement by the eight Great Lakes states and two provinces in the improvement and protection of the Great Lakes ecosystem. The improvements will help prevent invasive Silver, Black and Bighead Carp from entering the Great Lakes. The Great Lakes Commission — a regional organization formed by the eight states and chartered by Congress — will lead the effort with the aid of a skilled facilitation firm. Invasive carp have migrated up the Mississippi and Illinois Rivers and threaten to breach an electric fence that is keeping them at bay. Scientists predict an invasion would harm rivers and lakes throughout the region. The effort is expected to lead to a long-term forum by which the states and provinces will work in cooperation with the United States Army Corps of Engineers on final design, construction and cost-share requirements for the project.

title: Technical Assistance for Improved Teaching and Learning
description: This grant increase allows Michigan State University to support Flint Community Schools with technical assistance aimed at increasing district capacity, improving school culture, increasing operational efficiency and improving student academic outcomes. To achieve these goals, technical assistance will be focused on four primary components: districtwide systems, leadership development, classroom instruction and climate and culture.

title: Tools for Defending Environmental Defenders
description: Founded in 1992, Land is Life is a nongovernmental organization working with a trusted network of indigenous leaders, communities and organizations in the greater Amazon and globally. Over the past grant period, the grantee finalized a consultative process with indigenous communities in the Ecuadoran Amazon leading to the development of a Free Prior Informed Consent protocol that addresses development pressure and security threats to environmental defenders of indigenous lands and forests. Over the next grant period, the grantee will replicate the methodology to develop a new protocol in a different setting, consolidate recognition of the protocols and create a regional network to protect and prevent violence against indigenous environmental defenders.

title: Summer Community Development Internships
description: The goal of this project is to develop and enhance community assets through meaningful internships. The Flint Community Initiative, a project of Michigan State University, accomplishes this through an internship program that is focused on community development in Flint. The internships are 10 weeks long and end with a project showcase. Projects planned in 2021 are focused on neighborhoods and education and have been adapted to be virtual, with flexibility available for in-person work upon the lifting of all COVID-19 safety restrictions. The program was founded after community conversations in 2019 indicated a desire for continued community and capacity building work after the water crisis.

title: Whiting/Capitol Operating Support
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Flint Institute of Music, located on the Flint Cultural Center campus, reaches more than 300,000 people through lessons, classes, outreach programs, performances and concerts during a typical year. This grant will provide operating support for The Whiting and Capitol Theatre for staffing and initiatives that increase accessibility to diverse populations. The Flint Institute of Music began operating The Whiting and Capitol Theatre in 2021.

title: General Purposes
description: The Western Reserve Land Conservancy is Ohio’s largest land conservancy and one of the largest in the nation. The grantee is centered in the Cleveland area and serves a 21-county region with a vision to provide thriving, prosperous communities nourished by vibrant natural lands, working farms and healthy cities. Achieving this vision requires reversing trends that have seen urban communities deal with redlining, predatory lending, poverty and declining property values; and farmers struggle to reverse pressures that have led to a loss of 700,000 acres since 1950. With this grant from the Mott Foundation, the grantee will undertake a wide range of work, including efforts to connect people to nature in greener cities, parks, trails, greenways and rural lands and endow a fund to steward preserved land in perpetuity through its Conserve, Connect and Sustain Campaign.

title: Shine: Investing in Energy Access for All
description: GreenFaith — through its Shine project — seeks to catalyze collaborations that unlock resources to integrate decentralized energy solutions into efforts towards improved livelihoods, human rights and climate change solutions in the Global South.
