Over the past grant period, the grantee mapped more than 100 community-led energy access enterprises, created the Shine Women’s Council and launched the Shine Covid Response Fund. During the next grant period, GreenFaith will continue to educate and activate a network of energy access funders and other stakeholders as well as determine the best institutional structure for its long-term sustainability.

title: Afterschool Education and Outreach Project
description: This grant will provide support to Collaborative Communications Group to continue to build the capacity of the 50 State Afterschool Network ecosystem and the afterschool field in the areas of policy analysis, communications and research. To advance afterschool programs, this project will build bridges between local, state and federal governments and the afterschool field and will assist the networks as they navigate new federal, state and local education policies impacting afterschool programs.

title: Accelerating Energy Transition in the Amazon
description: The Regulatory Assistance Project is an independent, nonpartisan, nongovernmental organization dedicated to accelerating the transition to a clean, reliable and efficient energy future. This project will support the grantee to build on its experience with off-grid renewable energy access in the United States to assess and develop a roadmap for accelerating decarbonization and access to renewable energy in the Brazilian Amazon.

title: General Purposes
description: Independent Sector is a national membership organization that brings together a diverse community of changemakers at nonprofits, foundations and corporate giving programs working to strengthen civil society. In the past year, the grantee has launched a research compendium and benchmarking tool, co-created the National Infrastructure Investment Advocacy Group and engaged thousands of nonprofit and philanthropic leaders in its events. Over the next two years, the grantee will focus on sector impact, community building and public policy to enhance health and equity in American civil society. A grant increase will help Independent Sector to advance the nonprofit sector’s priorities.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to provide information and legal support to immigrants as they migrate into the United States. To this end, the Asylum Seeker Advocacy Project hosts online communities that provide real-time information and support as well as legal emergency rooms that allow asylum seekers to access legal aid without physically being with a lawyer. Additionally, the grantee advocates and litigates for a more equitable and just immigration system. After an unusual court case ruling in 2020, in order to have access to work permits after 185 days as opposed to 365 days, asylum seekers must be members of either CASA or the Asylum Seeker Advocacy Project, significantly increasing the grantees’ membership and stretching its capacity. This increase will allow the grantee to hire new staff, increase fundraising capacity and improve its technological infrastructure. Founded in 2015 as an all-volunteer effort, the grantee joined the Urban Justice Center in 2016 as a fiscally-sponsored project. In July 2019, the Asylum Seeker Advocacy Project became an independent 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization.

title: Campus Site Work Improvements
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to the Flint Cultural Center Corporation will provide funds for the installation of the sculpture along the roundabout on the Flint Cultural Center Campus. Funding will support the engineering, construction and materials for installation of the 70 foot sculpture, which will be centrally located on the campus. The large scale work will be visible from Robert T. Longway Blvd. and serve as a visual point of arrival for the campus. The Flint Institute of Arts purchased the sculpture in 2021 for its permanent collection. The grantee has partnered with the art museum, as well as organizations across the Flint Cultural Center Campus to develop and complete this process.

title: New Sculpture
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will support the purchase of a large sculpture that will be installed on the Flint Cultural Center campus as part of the northern entrance. The size of the sculpture will also help increase the visibility of the campus from Robert T. Longway Boulevard. The campus serves as a destination to over 600,000 visitors during a typical program year. The artwork will be part of the permanent collection at Flint Institute of Arts.

title: Lead-free and Affordable Water in Michigan
description: The Water Center at the University of Michigan is a multi-disciplinary group of experts on Great Lakes and Michigan water issues. The team supporting the Water Center on this project includes Michigan State University’s Extension Service and an expert in lead-contaminated public water systems. The Water Center worked with the State of Michigan to develop a series of science-based fact sheets aimed at water suppliers and their customers, regarding the state’s new lead and copper rule that was approved in late 2018. The Water Center also evaluated the challenges that Michigan cities were facing on the need to maintain and improve infrastructure that supplies and treats water while facing a shrinking population and shrinking revenues. With this grant increase, the Water Center will support the communication plan and rollout strategy for the Michigan statewide affordability study and will ensure that a key member of the team is able to fully participate in the effort.

title: General Purposes
description: This increase provides general support to Candid, an organization that collects, analyzes and publishes information on philanthropic and nonprofit entities. The grantee currently houses databases with 29,000 research reports and data on 2.8 million nonprofits and 235,000 foundations. The grantee provides training to nonprofits and foundations while producing and disseminating its own research. With this increase, the grantee will work with nonprofits to upload their data profiles, including demographic information, and engage with academia to increase research on nonprofits. Candid was founded in 2019, when Foundation Center and GuideStar merged into one entity, consolidating much of the nonprofit and philanthropic sector’s data.

title: Raising Michiganders' Standards of Living
description: Michigan Future, Inc. is a non-partisan, nonprofit organization whose mission is to be a source of new ideas on how Michigan can succeed as a world-class community in a knowledge-driven economy. This grant will support the grantee in their endeavor to raise the standard of living for all Michigan residents.

title: African Centre of Excellence for Access to Justice Project
description: The project goal is to strengthen the African Centre of Excellence for Access to Justice Project to promote a learning and sharing agenda. To this end, the Paralegal Advisory Service Institute will manage and coordinate the activities of the project. The grantee will strengthen the capacity of the center; build its membership, communications and visibility; and enhance the provision of access to justice for poor and marginalized communities within the center’s member countries. The grantee is one of the leading community justice organizations in Africa.

title: Accelerating the Scaling Up of Finance for People-Centered Justice in Lower Income Countries
geographic_focus: Eastern Africa, Southeastern Asia, Asia, Middle Africa
description: The Overseas Development Institute will conduct research into people-centered justice reforms in lower-income countries in order to identify learning and scaling opportunities. Detailed case studies will be done in five countries including Bangladesh, Kenya, Malawi, Sierra Leone and Uganda. These will examine how reforms were adopted, total costs and related financing and what lessons may be adopted for other contexts. Particular attention will be given to cost effectiveness and financing needs for adaptation and scaling of successful reforms. Findings will be shared with governments, development agencies, and other funding and justice partners. Established in 1960, and based in the United Kingdom, the Overseas Development Institute works to inspire people to act on injustice and inequality through research, convening and advocacy.

title: Go Blue Guarantee Pilot Program for the University of Michigan - Flint
description: The goal of this project is to offer high-achieving, low-income students financial support in their studies at the University of Michigan-Flint. To this end, the grantee will launch the Go Blue Guarantee for current and incoming students. The Go Blue Guarantee provides full tuition to all students who meet the income threshold and academic criteria. This is anticipated to both attract more students and help with student retention for those who may have financial hardship. Additional funding from both the Flint and Ann Arbor campuses will combine with this grant to ensure that the approximately 20% of the UM-F’s student body who meet the economic and academic criteria will receive full tuition support.

title: General Purposes
description: Indigenous peoples in the Amazon rely mainly on canoes and boats to travel in the rainforest and they generally lack access to clean electricity. Clearing forest for roads and other linear infrastructure brings deforestation and degradation in its wake. The Kara Solar Foundation and a growing group of partners have developed some of the first solar transport and electrification models built with and for Indigenous communities. Over the past grant period, the organization expanded its model from one Achuar community in Ecuador to Amazon Indigenous communities in Brazil, Peru and Suriname. This renewal will support Kara Solar to continue to replicate its model by developing the solar transport and electrification models, expanding training, innovating supply chains and fostering enterprises.

title: Sustainable Energy Finance and Development
description: Operation Native Amazon is a Brazilian nongovernmental organization specializing in protecting the Amazon Forest, rivers, and the Indigenous peoples who call the forest home. Over the last project period, the organization mapped and monitored an increase in hydroelectric finance and development in the Juruena River basin. This project renewal will support the organization to work with partner organizations to mitigate the environmental and social impacts of hydroelectric development and oil and gas exploration slated for the Middle Jurua River basin in the Amazon forest.

title: Research Project: Creating an Enabling Environment for Community Paralegals in Africa
description: The project goal is to generate knowledge and evidence on the impact of community paralegals in addressing injustices in Africa. To this end, the University of the Western Cape has collaborated with the African Centre of Excellence on Access to Justice by providing research support to document the work of community paralegals. Continued support will allow the grantee to increase its reach on the work of community paralegals in three North African countries. The research continues to build an informed map of community paralegal activities and people-centered justice across Africa.

title: Research Project: Creating an Enabling Environment for Community Paralegals in Africa
description: The project goal is to generate knowledge and evidence on the impact of community paralegals in addressing injustices in Africa. To this end, the University of the Western Cape has collaborated with the African Centre of Excellence on Access to Justice by providing research support to document the work of community paralegals in 18 African countries. Continued support will allow the grantee to increase its reach on the work of community paralegals in four additional African countries. The research continues to build an informed map of community paralegal activities and people-centered justice across Africa. The University of the Western Cape also plans to publish a book to spotlight the work of community justice workers in Africa.

title: Sustainable Development Finance in South America
description: The Asociación Ambiente y Sociedad is a Colombian nonprofit organization specializing in research, monitoring and advocacy related to investment and development finance in Colombia and South America. Over the last project period, the organization strengthened its regional networking to monitor international and China-led development finance institutions. Special focus was given to COVID-19 loans, energy and climate finance and the Amazon Initiative — an Inter-American Development Bank effort coordinating different streams of financial and technical assistance for the Amazon region. A database of 223 projects was built and shared with the public. Ambiente y Sociedad will continue to monitor energy and infrastructure finance, and curate its website and project database. The organization also will continue to focus advocacy on climate finance and the Amazon Initiative.

title: Youth Recreation Landscape Scan and Playground Assessment
description: This grant increase will support Formative Evaluation Research Associates to complete a youth recreation landscape scan and complete a playground assessment for Flint. There are two goals for the project: 1) assess existing youth recreation programming and provide recommendations for improvement; and 2) identify the resources needed to build, maintain and replace playgrounds and play structures in Flint over the next 20 years.

title: Investing in Community Foundations
description: Community foundations have been at the core of the Council on Foundations, a national philanthropic organization that currently represents 760 members, since its founding in 1949. The grantee’s mission is to foster an environment where philanthropy can thrive and cultivate a community of diverse and skilled philanthropic professionals. At present, roughly 40% of U.S. community foundations are members of the grantee and roughly two-thirds are accredited by the Community Foundation National Standards Board, a supporting organization of the Council on Foundations. In order to advance a healthy policy environment for philanthropy and to advance local-level engagement with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, over the next three years the grantee will strengthen its work and support of community foundations through four areas of specialized engagement: leading on public policy, enhancing National Standards, expanding its community foundation reach and building community through the Sustainable Development Goals.

title: American Leadership on the SDGs
description: The project goal is to promote a community-led implementation of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. To this end, the United Nations Foundation has launched the American Leadership on the SDGs project. The grantee will build a coalition of local multistakeholder networks, serve as a knowledge hub for U.S. efforts, elevate location innovation and action through coordinated communication and a storytelling effort, and coordinate and support new commitments and policy efforts leading to greater action on the Sustainable Development Goals from the local to the federal level. Outputs will include community-level convenings, an annual event on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly, an online resources hub, storytelling, social media initiatives, research products, policy briefs and a regular newsletter. Founded in 1998, the United Nations Foundation acts as a strategic partner to help the United Nations mobilize the ideas, people and resources it needs to deliver on its mission.

title: Strengthening and Consolidating the Socio-Environmental Fund Peru
description: Derecho Ambiente y Recursos Naturales is a Peruvian nongovernmental organization engaged in strengthening transparency and social environmental governance of development finance. With prior support, the grantee incubated the Socio-Environmental Fund of Peru, a small grants fund for local organizations impacted by energy and infrastructure development. With renewed support, small grants will continue to be made for this purpose while the grantee also strengthens the capacity of the Fund to become in the future an independent small grantmaking organization.

title: Renewable Roraima: Studies for Isolated Community Electrification
description: The Instituto Clima e Sociedade is a Brazilian philanthropic organization that promotes prosperity, justice and low-carbon development in Brazil. Over the past grant period, the grantee worked with Brazilian partners to build the Roraima renewable energy forum, which successfully expanded renewable energy access in the Amazonian state. The organization also supported the planning and implementation of a second Energy and Community Conference, which brought together more than 300 community leaders, energy policy experts, private sector representatives and policy makers to raise awareness and proposal for clean energy access. Over the next year, the organization will develop participatory recommendations for expanding clean energy access and consolidate its lessons learned over the course of this project.

title: Connecting Communities in the Americas
geographic_focus: North America, South America, Central America, Caribbean
description: The Connecting Communities in the Americas (formerly known as Building Broader Communities in the Americas) initiative, managed by CFLeads and implemented in partnership with the Inter-American Foundation, aims to build stronger, more resilient communities throughout the Americas by enhancing the effectiveness of community foundations’ responsiveness to them. The initiative helps to increase understanding of transnational communities in the hemisphere, strengthen relationships among community foundations and transnational stakeholders to solve common problems, advance knowledge about community foundation practices that can support transnational communities and encourage more effective giving in Latin America and the Caribbean. A grant increase will support an additional transnational community mapping project, travel stipends for U.S. and Canadian community foundation representatives to participate in an event in Gaudalajara, Mexico and short-term consultant fees for the initiative. CFLeads is a U.S.-based national network of community foundations committed to community leadership.

title: Social Sector Infrastructure Mapping and Assessment
description: The program goal is to map and assess the organizational infrastructure for the nonprofit and philanthropic sector in the U.S. The New Venture Fund will commission research to develop a shared social sector typology and map. This, in turn, will be used to: 1) assess the value of the current social sector infrastructure and how it may need to evolve in light of external trends; 2) identify areas where strategic funding can help position the infrastructure to address future challenges; and 3) encourage additional investments aimed at strengthening the capacity of infrastructure organizations currently and in the future. This grant increase will be used to support additional research needed to complete the project. Established in 2006, the New Venture Fund provides a platform to support innovative and effective public interest projects.

title: General Purposes
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: Started in 2005 as a project of Philanthropy New York, Asset Funders Network is a national membership organization for grantmakers working to build economic opportunity and prosperity for low- and moderate-income people. To accomplish its mission, the grantee works with its members to develop shared expertise, align and coordinate grantmaking strategies and provide leadership on priority issues. During the renewal grant period, the grantee will continue organizing educational and networking activities, connecting grantmakers to experts and other technical assistance providers and promoting funder collaborations that increase the level and effectiveness of philanthropic support for asset-building issues, including children’s savings accounts.

title: Community Foundations Advancing Welcoming and Sustainable Development Goals
description: The program goal is to encourage community foundations to advance the Sustainable Development Goals at the local level. To this end, Welcoming America will map how community foundations are engaging with immigrant integration work, crosslink its newly-updated Welcoming Standards to the Sustainable Development Goals, bring together community foundation and welcoming leaders through a virtual convening, develop a white paper and other resources to help community foundations initiate work on welcoming and the goals, identify and support a cohort of up to 15 community foundations to learn together through in-person and virtual convenings, provide one-on-one coaching to this cohort and design a second phase of the initiative for subsequent cohorts. Information about the project and its results will be disseminated at the grantee’s nationwide convenings during this time period. Founded in 2009 as a nonprofit, non-partisan organization, Welcoming America works to create inclusive communities where immigrants and all residents can thrive.

title: Community Foundations Advancing Welcoming Standards and Sustainable Development Goals
description: The program goal is to encourage community foundations to advance the Sustainable Development Goals at the local level. To this end, over the past two years, Welcoming America has conducted interviews with 17 community foundations on how they engage in welcoming work, mapped its Welcoming Standard to the Sustainable Development Goals, convened a cohort of community foundation leaders at its 2022 conference, facilitated webinars and office hours and analyzed and consolidated learnings in a white paper. Over the next two years, the grantee will host four training workshops, convene at least 15 community foundations and three strategic partners at its 2024 conference, capture up to four case studies, publish two blog pieces and include at least 15 new community foundations into its Welcoming Network by the end of 2024. Founded in 2009 as a nonprofit, non-partisan organization, Welcoming America works to create inclusive communities where immigrants and all residents can thrive.

title: American Leadership on the SDG's
description: The project goal is to promote community-led implementation of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals in the United States. During the past four years, the United Nations Foundation has led the American Leadership on the Sustainable Development Goals program. This initiative has fostered collective action in new communities across the country by convening stakeholders, compiling and sharing best practices, producing research and amplifying local stories. Over the next two years, the program will continue to amplify what works, share useful resources and provide evidence and dialogue in support of domestic activities on the Sustainable Development Goals. Outputs will include targeted roundtables and convenings, an annual event on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly, a communications toolkit and resources, research products, policy briefs and a regular newsletter. Founded in 1998, the United Nations Foundation acts as a strategic partner to help the United Nations mobilize the ideas, people and resources it needs to deliver on its mission.

title: Promoting Community-Led Implementation of the Sustainable Development Goals
description: The project goal is to promote the community-led implementation of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. To this end in 2018, the Center for Sustainable Development at the Brookings Institution established the Local Leadership on the Sustainable Development Goals initiative. This effort entailed supporting community foundations, businesses, universities and other local institutions in adapting and advancing the goals locally; hosting private roundtables and public events to showcase innovations; and building a set of resources and tools to support current and future implementation of the goals on a local level. Over the next two years, the Brookings Institution’s Center for Sustainable Development plans to raise awareness of the Sustainable Development Goals for community foundations in various philanthropic media and event spaces, strengthen the emerging ecosystem of community foundation leadership on the goals and help adapt a 17 Rooms-X process model of engaging on the goals for use by community foundations.

title: Adopting the SDG Framework
description: The program goal is to encourage community foundations to advance the Sustainable Development Goals at the local level. To this end, the Community Foundation for Greater Flint will build its capacity to adopt the goals as a framework to holistically evaluate its work and to communicate impact to its donors, peers and community. The grantee will conduct an internal analysis of the intersectionality between its work and the goals, collect baseline data in Genesee County and assess the community’s capacity to organize and improve performance on the goals. The grantee will then develop a plan to adopt the goals as a framework for evaluating and communicating its impact, especially around racial equity, and as a comprehensive business model and practice. Founded in 1988, the Community Foundation for Greater Flint is a major local philanthropic entity that strives to accelerate equitable and sustainable improvements in the quality of life for all Genesee County residents.

title: Energy Distributed to Isolated Communities
description: The Instituto Socioambiental is a forerunner in providing development solutions to protect the Amazon rainforest and the Indigenous people who call it home. This project supports the ongoing efforts of the organization to implement and develop management models for off-grid solar renewable energy projects in isolated Xingu River basin and Indigenous communities in the Raposa Serra do Sol Indigenous Territory in the state of Roraima. Over the next grant period, the project coordinators will hold meetings to monitor federal renewable energy universalization programs, share lessons learned and promote the social and environmental benefits of off-grid renewable energy. They will provide technical trainings and assistance to ensure successful replication, implementation and management of off-grid solar energy systems in the indigenous territories in the Xingu River basin and Amazon state of Roraima.

title: Advancing the SDGs
description: The program goal is to encourage community foundations to advance the Sustainable Development Goals at the local level. To this end, starting in October 2021, the Community Foundation for Greater Flint has developed a framework for mapping grantee outcomes and donor-advised funds in the areas of education and equity; completed a comprehensive analysis of recent funds distributed and their alignment with the goals; assessed existing data measures utilized by the foundation, its partners and grantees; and aligned its community engagement work on racial equity with the goals. In the coming grant period, the grantee will expand its Sustainable Development Goal alignment efforts to its finance, operations and community leadership areas; develop a community dashboard; raise awareness about the goals with grantees and key partners; and further integrate and operationalize the goals in its work. Founded in 1988, the Community Foundation for Greater Flint is a major local philanthropic entity that strives to accelerate equitable and sustainable improvements in the quality of life for all Genesee County residents.

title: General Purposes
description: For nearly 40 years, Environmental Defence Canada has been active on environmental issues at the provincial and national levels through engagement with stakeholders, organizations and the general public. The organization works to safeguard Canada’s freshwater resources, decrease Canadians’ exposure to toxic chemicals, end plastic pollution and build a clean economy. To help address these issues, Environmental Defence Canada will engage and educate stakeholders and participate in opportunities to help ensure the restoration of the Great Lakes, strengthen the organization’s capacity and raise awareness of public health issues in Ontario.

title: General Purposes
description: This renewal grant will provide general purposes support to the Harlem Children’s Zone, whose mission is to end intergenerational poverty in Central Harlem and become the model for how other long-distressed communities nationwide and around the world can do the same. Created in 2000, the Harlem Children’s Zone annually provides education, health and employment services to over 20,000 children and families living in a 97-block area in Central Harlem.

title: General Purposes
description: The Groundwork Center for Resilient Communities has promoted sustainable community practices in Michigan since 1995. With partial support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has provided policy leadership in its home region of northwest lower Michigan in support of a clean environment, a strong economy and resilient communities. The grantee pursues its agenda in the priority areas of food and farming, clean energy, water policy and transportation. With renewed support, Groundwork Center for Resilient Communities will continue work in all of its priority program areas, which will include expanding and strengthening the Great Lakes Business Network.

title: Amplifying Community Voices to Defend their Human Rights and Environment
description: Infrastructure and energy projects constructed by development finance institutions like the World Bank and Asian Development Bank often come with environmental, social or governance risks. To address these risks, Accountability Counsel deploys lawyers to engage with these development finance institutions’ accountability offices in order to advocate for people harmed by these institutions’ projects in infrastructure and energy. Over the grant period, the grantee will amplify the voices of communities to assist people to effectively use development finance institutions’ accountability offices to defend their rights and remedy harm caused by internationally financed projects and access justice.

title: Mariam C. Noland Public Spaces Fund
description: The project goal is to support the construction, maintenance and programming of public spaces in southeast Michigan. To this end, the Community Foundation for Southeast Michigan will create a fund to celebrate Mariam Noland’s retirement — known as the Mariam C. Noland Public Spaces Fund. This fund will provide support for public spaces including parks, trails, nature preserves or civic commons. The grantee was established in 1984 for the betterment of the residents of Wayne, Oakland, Macomb, Monroe, Washtenaw, St. Clair and Livingston counties and enhances the quality of life in southeast Michigan by making strategic investments in programs and organizations that benefit the region.

title: General Purposes
description: The Grand Traverse Regional Land Conservancy, founded in 1991, is a land trust serving a five-county region located in northwest lower Michigan. In total, the conservancy has protected over 46,000 acres of land and 153 miles of shoreline along the region’s rivers, lakes and streams. During the last grant period alone, the conservancy protected 830 acres of land and two and a half miles of shoreline, built over four miles of new trail, began a multi-year pollinator habitat restoration project and opened two new public nature preserves. The organization also completed construction on its new offices and education center, which serves as a regional hub of conservation activity for a range of partner organizations. With renewal support, the conservancy will pursue a range of land and water quality protection projects, continue to leverage the use of its new headquarters to promote collaborative conservation projects and build organizational strength and staff capacity.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will renew general purposes support to Focus: HOPE, an anti-poverty and civil rights organization that serves residents of Detroit’s Oakman Boulevard neighborhood. Cofounded in 1968 by Father William Cunningham and Eleanor Josaitis, the grantee’s mission is to provide intelligent and practical solutions to overcome racism, poverty and injustice. Mott Foundation funding will help support the grantee’s core lines of work: 1) workforce development and education; 2) early learning and youth development; and 3) food justice.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will renew general purposes support to Focus: HOPE, an anti-poverty and civil rights organization that serves residents of Detroit’s Oakman Boulevard neighborhood. Cofounded in 1968 by Father William Cunningham and Eleanor Josaitis, the grantee’s mission is to provide intelligent and practical solutions to overcome racism, poverty and injustice. Mott Foundation funding will help support the grantee’s core lines of work: 1) workforce development and education; 2) early learning and youth development; and 3) food justice.

title: General Purposes
grantee: CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation
description: Founded in 1993, CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation is a dynamic global network of over 15,000 members across 188 countries. The organization is dedicated to strengthening civil society and promoting citizen engagement, particularly in contexts where democratic participation and freedom of association are under threat. Among its recent achievements are the publication of its annual State of Civil Society reports and the ongoing development of the CIVICUS Monitor — a vital resource offering real-time data and analysis on civic space worldwide. The grantee also connects and equips civil society actors through convenings, collaborative initiatives and the implementation of its 2022–27 strategic plan. During the grant period, the organization and its strategic partners will develop a system to detect early signs of civic space restrictions by building on the CIVICUS Monitor methodology and designing tools to support timely responses. The grantee is also preparing to host the first International Civil Society Week since the COVID-19 pandemic and will launch a new community cohort of civil society innovators, drawn from two decades of Nelson Mandela–Graça Machel Innovation Awards winners. CIVICUS: World Alliance for Citizen Participation is headquartered in Johannesburg, South Africa.

title: Hunters and Anglers for Climate Solutions
description: A comprehensive approach to addressing climate change should include solutions that harness the power of natural systems. Such nature-based climate solutions include forestry and agricultural practices that sequester carbon and land protection strategies that help communities adapt to the extreme weather events associated with climate change. The Theodore Roosevelt Conservation Partnership, a national organization representing hunter and angler groups from across the country, is leading an effort to support nature-based climate solutions at the federal level. With Mott support, the grantee will conduct opinion research, develop an interactive map highlighting successful projects and undertake additional activities to educate decision makers, hunters, anglers and other stakeholders about nature-based climate solutions.

title: Building Capacity to Monitor Chinese Investment in Asia
description: Chinese investments in developing countries have increased exponentially over the past two decades, presenting a major shift in the source and structure of development finance. Since 2012 when it was founded, Inclusive Development International has been vital in raising awareness of the need to strengthen the environmental and social policies of China-influenced development finance institutions, particularly the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank. Over the next grant period, the grantee will continue its efforts to deter harmful energy and infrastructure projects, and promote shifts in Chinese overseas investment toward projects that protect the environment, respect the rights of local communities and support a just energy transition.

title: Renewable Energy Access for Sustainable Livelihoods and Conservation in the Amazon
description: Access to modern, clean energy is a major challenge in the greater Amazon rainforest. This grant supports the World Wildlife Fund to expand and replicate renewable energy access in the Amazon countries of Bolivia, Colombia and Suriname. With prior Mott support, the project focused on assessing opportunities for renewable energy expansion, gathering lessons learned from existing pilot projects and implementing renewable energy systems pilot projects to support sustainable livelihoods and conservation in specific territories. Over the next grant period, the grantee will build upon progress and lessons learned and develop strategies to overcome barriers and create conditions to enable renewable energy expansion in diverse forest contexts. Efforts to include women and enhance collaboration, planning and decision-making will be undertaken to support renewable energy expansion and exchange lessons learned among Colombian and Bolivian actors.

title: Clean and Affordable Drinking Water: Growing Advocacy and Organizational Capacity in the Great Lakes
geographic_focus: New York, Wisconsin, Indiana, Illinois, Minnesota, Pennsylvania, Michigan, Ohio
description: River Network is a national organization that provides training to advance organizational effectiveness and sharpen advocates’ skills and capacity to address a range of issues including access to clean, safe and affordable drinking water. With prior Mott support, the grantee provided such capacity building support to groups and individuals in the Great Lakes region. River Network also convened key individuals and organizations to build regional collaboration on drinking water issues. Renewed support will enable the grantee to continue to focus on water affordability, community resiliency and equitable water infrastructure investment. The grantee will also build the capacity of Great Lakes groups around drinking water issues by providing consulting and mentoring. Grant funds will also be used to help Great Lakes stakeholders attend River Rally, a leading national conference.

title: General Purposes
location: Santa Cruz de la Sierra, Bolivia
description: The Fundación Socioambiental Semilla is a Bolivian nongovernmental organization founded in 2018. It provides small grants to local organizations and leaders to strengthen the social and environmental standards governing the flow of development finance to projects impacting their communities. This grant renewal will continue to support the institutional development of Fundación Socioambiental Semilla to implement its small grantmaking strategy in Bolivia.

title: Land Water and Climate Justice Efforts in the Global South
description: In Southeast Asia, large-scale investments in energy and infrastructure projects have driven rapid economic growth. Still, that growth comes at the expense of the environment and of communities that suffer the impacts of resource extraction, pollution, illegal takings of land and displacement. Established in 1992, American Jewish World Service has worked to build a more just, equitable and sustainable world through community-driven change, currently supporting 541 grantee partners in 17 countries. Support to the grantee’s Land, Water and Climate Justice program efforts in the Global South will help the organization provide financial and capacity-building support to its considerable networks of rural community partner organizations who lead such efforts in South and Southeast Asia. The project team also will connect these networks to other Mott grantees active in the two regions.

title: Statewide Equity Fund
description: The project goal is to support a Michigan funder collaborative that will ensure federal resources are allocated in an equitable way. To this end, the Council of Michigan Foundations will pilot a Statewide Equity Fund so Michigan philanthropy can strategically guide and leverage funding from the CARES Act, the American Rescue Plan and other recently allocated public resources toward equity-centered approaches. The Statewide Equity Fund will provide regional collaboratives and philanthropic institutions with information regarding federal funding policy, technical support, tools and expertise, and seed funding for innovative approaches. The Council of Michigan Foundations is a membership organization of over 300 philanthropic stakeholders. Its mission is to enhance, improve and increase philanthropy.

title: Statewide Afterschool Network Support
description: This grant increase will allow the National Summer Learning Association to support the development, growth and sustainability of the Statewide Afterschool Network. Specifically, this increase will support the grantee to provide additional technical assistance to the Statewide Afterschool Network to address the range of needs of young people and families in light of the pandemic and support the afterschool field as it expands programs through federal and state recovery initiatives, including the American Rescue Plan.

title: Grantmakers for Thriving Youth
description: This grant will support the National Public Education Support Fund to support Grantmakers for Thriving Youth to facilitate and convene funders in education, child and youth development and other allied fields.

title: Leveraging National Service in Support of Afterschool
description: This grant will support America’s Service Commissions to expand afterschool opportunities by leveraging national service to provide additional capacity. Specifically, this grant will support America’s Service Commissions to provide resources to expand or launch new national service programs for the afterschool field.

title: Afterschool Resources and Trainings
description: This grant will support Foundations, Inc. to curate content and resources for afterschool and summer learning programs and summer camps to keep kids and staff safe as the field continues to navigate COVID-19.

title: Afterschool Capacity Building
description: This grant will support the Michigan Association of United Ways, which coordinates the Michigan Afterschool Partnership, to continue the development of policy, partnerships and resources to increase equitable opportunities for children, youth and families in Michigan. Specific initiatives will include: 1) increasing the reach and scope of out-of-school time program system-building efforts at a state and grassroots level; 2) building strategic partnerships with stakeholders to map resources and plan program expansion through new and existing funding streams; 3) expanding professional development and data-driven practices to promote a culture of continuous improvement to support a skilled out-of-school time workforce; and 4) enhance organizational capacity to cultivate new strategies and polices to expand high-quality out-of-school environments.

title: Superintendents as Leaders for High-Quality Afterschool and Summer Learning Opportunities
description: This grant will support the American Association of School Administrators to work with school leaders as they implement afterschool programs focused on learning recovery for young people and to advance racial equity for young people of color. This project will focus on: working with the 50 State Afterschool Network to develop a series of tools and models of practice that support school district and community partnerships, developing a multimedia strategic communications initiative to inform superintendents and local districts and coordinating a professional learning community of at least eight school districts to support new afterschool programs.

title: Supporting Quality Afterschool Programs
description: This grant will support the American Camp Association to provide quality initiatives in afterschool and summer programs. Specifically, this grant will: 1) support the grantee to provide resources to the 50 State Afterschool Network to expand quality initiatives for the afterschool and summer learning field; and 2) foster connections between the 50 State Afterschool Network and summer camps.

title: Afterschool Capacity Support
description: This grant to STEM Next Opportunity Fund will provide additional resources for the 50 State Afterschool Network to coordinate the nationwide expansion of afterschool programs and learning recovery supports for young people. The project focuses on expanding the capacity of the 50 State Afterschool Network to address learning loss among young people resulting from the pandemic and to significantly increase equitable and sustainable education opportunities for young people, families and communities.

title: Lake Erie Protection and Restoration Project
description: The Ohio Environmental Council is a major conservation advocacy organization in the state. With prior Mott support, the grantee focused attention on Lake Erie and its pollution problems and led efforts to improve Lake Erie communities by restoring coastal ecosystems. Recently, the grantee has turned more attention to drinking water, lead contamination, and affordability of clean, safe water supplies. An estimated 13 million people get drinking water from Lake Erie, a water source at risk due to massive toxic algae blooms that are especially prevalent in the Western Lake Erie basin. With this grant increase, the Ohio Environmental Council will develop, with partners, a report addressing phosphorus reductions and the financial costs of such reduction in the basin.

title: Strategic Planning and a Water Camp
description: We The People of Detroit is an important environmental justice group working on water policy issues in Michigan and nationally. Previous support from the Mott Foundation has helped the grantee manage its rapid growth, undertake long-term planning and launch its youth water camp in Idlewild, Michigan, that encourages careers in water science and stewardship. With continued support, We The People of Detroit will strengthen its organizational capacity, continue a citizen science project on community-level water issues and grow its youth water camp.

title: Monitoring BNDES Sustainability
grantee: Instituto de Energia e Meio Ambiente
description: The Instituto de Energia e Meio Ambiente is a nonprofit Brazilian think tank focused on research, analysis and policy evaluation to contribute to socially and environmentally sustainable energy and transportation development and finance. Over the previous grant period, the grantee monitored the social and environmental impacts of thermoelectric power development and plans by development finance institutions to expand natural gas-fired thermoelectric generation into the electrical mix. Over the next grant period, the Instituto de Energia e Meio Ambiente will consolidate a community of practice to address the impacts of gas-fired thermoelectric expansion and develop more robust social and environmental safeguards for its finance.

title: Monitoring BNDES Sustainability
grantee: Instituto de Energia e Meio Ambiente
description: The Instituto de Energia e Meio Ambiente is a nonprofit Brazilian think tank focused on research, analysis and policy evaluation to contribute to socially and environmentally sustainable energy and transportation development and finance. This grant increase will support the cost of professional facilitation and a web organizing tool to coordinate a community of nongovernmental organizations working on development finance of natural gas-powered thermoelectric expansion in Brazil.

title: Harnessing Technology to Reduce Fires in the Amazon
description: Woodwell Climate Research Center is a premier scientific organization working globally to solve climate change, and in Brazil to protect the Amazon rainforest. This grant will support the grantee to work alongside its Brazilian counterpart, Amazon Environmental Research Institute, to further analyze and strengthen technology and partnerships in the Amazon to reduce forest destruction in this globally important eco-region.

title: Harnessing Technology to Reduce Fires in the Amazon
description: The Amazon Environmental Research Institute is a Brazil-based nonprofit scientific organization working on the sustainable development and conservation of the Brazilian rainforest. This project will support the grantee to collaborate with Woodwell Climate Research Center to develop technology and implement strategies to reduce deforestation and fires and increase protection and conservation of this importanteco-region and its traditional peoples.

title: Advancing Solutions to Water Affordability
geographic_focus: Ohio, Michigan, Pennsylvania, Minnesota, Illinois, Indiana, Wisconsin, New York
description: Elevate Energy is a nonprofit organization based in Chicago that designs and implements programs to ensure access to clean and affordable water, heat and power. With prior Mott Foundation support, the grantee enacted a broad spectrum of drinking water affordability initiatives, including research on water rates, community-based programs to fix water shutoffs and technical assistance provided to water utilities. With renewed support, the grantee will continue similar work, including researching water debt challenges faced by low-income families and providing education and training on water affordability solutions to water utilities and other partner groups.

title: Bridge Michigan Environment Watch
description: Bridge Michigan, a project of the Center for Michigan, is a leading statewide, nonprofit public service news and information platform in Michigan. Its Environment Watch report provides in-depth reporting on Great Lakes and drinking water issues. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, coverage of these issues has gained audience support and growth, increased readership and subscribers, as well as garnered several awards. With renewed support, Bridge Michigan will continue to produce in-depth, collaborative, public-service Environment Watch journalism as a contributing partner in the Great Lakes News Collaborative.

title: Uniting Great Lakes Science, Data and Journalism
description: Circle of Blue is a member of the Great Lakes News Collaborative, a partnership among four news outlets covering water issues in the Great Lakes. This grant increase will allow the grantee to serve the collaborative as a resource for its reporters and newsrooms, as well as continue to create and provide original content and share stories with and among partners.

title: Great Lakes Now
description: Detroit Public Television’s Great Lakes Now initiative provides robust reporting, a monthly television program and community engagement events to broad audiences centered around freshwater issues throughout the Great Lakes region. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, Great Lakes Now has won numerous awards and grown its broadcast reach in 20 markets across 31 stations reaching over 4.5 million viewers. As a partner in the Great Lakes News Collaborative, Great Lakes Now has contributed video content which compliments print and radio reporting. With renewed support, Great Lakes Now will continue to produce monthly broadcast episodes with supplemental digital content, including daily articles on greatlakesnow.org, as well as educational resources to raise awareness and build understanding of Great Lakes issues.

title: Michigan Radio - The Environment Report
description: Michigan Radio is an award-winning, public radio station housed at the University of Michigan. With Mott Foundation’s support over the last two years and despite COVID-19 demands for media attention, Michigan Radio’s Environment Report was able to devote increased coverage to Great Lakes and drinking water issues and broaden their audience reach. The station also solidified its relationship as a partner in the Great Lakes News Collaborative. With renewed support, the station will produce more in-depth stories across more platforms and develop community engagement journalism to address issues of diversity, while continuing to share and co-create content for and with the Great Lakes News Collaborative partners.

title: People-Centered Oversight
description: The Levin Center, at Wayne State University Law School, was established to strengthen the integrity, transparency and accountability of public and private institutions by: promoting and supporting bipartisan, fact-based oversight; advancing good governance, particularly with respect to the legislative process; and promoting civil discourse on current issues of public policy. This grant will support the pilot of the People-Center Oversight project in Flint to create a scalable model for building public engagement with the government that will help to address the epidemic of hopelessness, resignation and misinformation that impede reform and pose a threat to our democracy.

title: Alabama Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Voices for Alabama’s Children which coordinates the Alabama Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) create a framework to expand school-age child care and educate stakeholders on the importance of state funding policies and program quality investments; 2) inform statewide policies that allocate the necessary funding and resources to sustain both new and existing school-based and school-linked afterschool programs; 3) work with education stakeholders to design and implement education recovery funding to help Alabama youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen Education, Inc. resources.

title: Education Program Data Collection and Assessment
description: This project will continue to support the development of an evaluation and data collection plan for the Foundation’s Education Program, with a particular focus on the Advancing Afterschool, Youth Engagement and College and Career Readiness areas. Schaffer&Combs will build upon the evaluation framework and assessment for the Advancing Afterschool area to support additional Education Program areas. This project will continue to support current Education program priorities and lay the groundwork for increased learning and more effective grantmaking and grantee performance in the coming years.

title: Improving Early Childhood Care and Education Quality
description: Child Care Network works to promote the success of children, families and the community through quality child care education, advocacy and family support. With this grant, the grantee will bolster its efforts around supporting the family, friend and neighbor child care program and the early childhood talent pipeline program. These two programs help ensure that regardless of the option a family chooses for child care, the child will receive high quality care.

title: Operating Support
grantee: Flint Institute of Science and History
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Sloan Museum has operated a temporary space at Courtland Center since they closed the museum for renovations in 2018. This grant will provide funds for exhibits and other expenses while Sloan at Courtland Center remains open until the new facility, including exhibits, is completed. Over 125,000 individuals have visited Sloan at Courtland Center since its opening including traveling exhibits such as Tropical Rainforest Adventure and Dinosaurs Unearthed.

title: Film Appreciation Academy for Youth
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide funds to iMichigan Productions for a film appreciation program for youth in Flint. Working with partners such as Berston Field House and the Flint Public Library, the iMichigan team will develop and implement a curriculum that explores the filmmaking genre. Filmmaking is a complex process and offers a variety of career pathways for those who are interested in the art form or the more technical aspects of the industry, such as sound engineering and editing. This program will explore all facets of filmmaking.

title: Flint Community Journalism Support
description: Through this grant, the Community Foundation of Greater Flint will support the capacity building and writing needs of local community publications including The Flint Courier News, Flintside, Flint Beat, East Village Magazine and Our Community, Our Voice. These locally led news organizations provide trusted information and stories for local residents, and have been especially important as the community recovers from the water crisis and navigates the pandemic.

title: Capital Improvements
description: The Latinx Technology & Community Center is a community service and educational agency with the dedicated purpose to enhance the dignity and quality of life for the Flint and Genesee County Latinx community and other cultures. This grant will support the renovations of the second floor of the grantee’s building, which will allow for additional programming at the center.

title: Increasing Food Distribution
description: This grant will provide funds to Carriage Town Ministries to purchase food in order to serve meals to the homeless and those in need of food assistance who come to the shelter. The grantee provides important safety net services to individuals and families in the Flint area who are homeless or near homeless including food, safe and warm shelter, clothes, personal hygiene products, health services, employment training and life skills courses.

title: Basic Needs Support
description: With this grant, St. Luke N.E.W. Life Center will provide basic needs support to participants in its existing programs and residents who live in their neighborhood. Following the Flint water crisis and the COVID-19 pandemic, the grantee has seen increased demand for emergency housing, food assistance and transportation needs. The center will partner with other area agencies to leverage basic needs funds and help meet the needs of Flint families.

title: Meeting College Students' Basic Needs
description: Mott Community College, through its Lenore Crowdy Family Life Center, helps address the basic needs of its students with a food pantry, clothing closet and broad array of social service providers. Many of the college’s students are low income, sometimes just above the threshold for which they would qualify for state benefits. These extra supports help students stay in school and complete their studies, preparing them for successful futures.

title: Travel and Learning Fund
description: The project goal is to support exchange, networking and interaction among key nonprofits, practitioners and experts, including Mott Foundation grantees. To this end, the Institute of International Education, Inc. will operate a travel and learning fund to support individuals and organizations working on civic space, community philanthropy, access to justice or other areas of interest. In the period 2021-2024, the grantee supported almost 60 individuals to participate in learning events across a range of issue areas, including community philanthropy, digital human rights and indigenous access to civil justice. Based in New York, the Institute of International Education manages similar funds for foundations around the world.

title: The Education Trust-Midwest Michigan Policy Efforts
description: The Education Trust will support its Midwest division to continue advancing meaningful educational equity and excellence efforts at the state and local levels to address the concerns of challenged districts, such as Flint Community Schools. The grantee’s Midwest division remains well-positioned to inform Michigan’s education policy landscape through equity-focused research and data; whether in regards to long-standing issues such as early literacy and school funding or the new challenges brought about by the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Georgia Manor
description: Communities First’s mission is to build healthy, vibrant communities through economic development, affordable housing, and innovative programming. This grant increase will help further the grantee’s mission by supporting the increased cost of the redevelopment of the Georgia Manor apartment complex located in Flint’s historic Carriage Town neighborhood.

title: Youth Skilled Trade and Pre-apprenticeship Program
description: With this grant, Active Boys in Christ will provide a free summer program that teaches youth hands-on basic plumbing, electrical, carpentry and cooking skills. The grantee has licensed plumbers, electricians, carpenters and an executive chef that volunteers to work with the youth. During the program character lessons on honesty, forgiveness, respect and integrity are taught.

title: Vermont Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Vermont Afterschool which coordinates the Vermont Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) advance values-centered practices to expand partnerships, improve professional development and program quality and enhance data collection efforts; 2) elevate youth voice to inform policy considerations, organizational leadership and community engagement in support of afterschool; 3) work with education stakeholders to design and implement education recovery funding to help Vermont youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen Education, Inc. resources.

title: General Purposes
description: The Neighborhood Engagement Hub hired its first executive director in 2017 and has continued to grow and develop since that time. The grantee leads the planning and implementation of the Neighbors Changing Flint Workshop series, acts as a fiscal sponsor for several grants and sponsorships for different neighborhood organizations and supports residents in project planning and implementation. Additionally, the Community Tool Shed that is operated by the grantee is an invaluable resource for residents and neighborhood groups to maintain the exterior of homes and parks throughout the city. This general purposes grant provides support to the grantee as it navigates its first leadership transition.

title: Weave: The Social Fabric Project
description: Weave: The Social Fabric Project was established in 2018 to highlight the problem of America’s social fragmentation and its solution. Through this project, the Aspen Institute will connect and inspire new generations and lift up the work of “weavers” — people who know their neighborhood well and are motivated by a deep calling to reach out to those who are marginalized. Project activities include establishing a Weave Advisory Board, connecting and supporting weavers by offering local chapters, establishing a weaver speakers bureau, identifying and inspiring new weavers, introducing and integrating weavers into the networks and systems of community change, and effectively communicating the impact of weaving on the social crises of our nation. Established in 1949, Aspen Institute is a leading U.S. think tank with an international network of partners that fosters values-based leadership and provides a neutral and balanced venue for discussing and acting on critical issues.

title: General Purposes
description: The North Flint Reinvestment Corporation is a community and economic development corporation organized to implement a holistic approach to community revitalization in north Flint. The corporation is comprised of a grassroots network of public and private sector partners committed to rebuilding and revitalizing economically distressed neighborhoods in north Flint. This grant will help the grantee to have the resources necessary to operate at a higher level.

title: Accelerating Innovations in Access to Justice through Research
description: The project goal is to research and document best practices on innovations in access to justice in communities at the grassroots of Africa. In this regard, Barefoot Law will commence this research in Malawi, Kenya and Uganda, where the justice gap remains wide. Key activities will include: desktop and field research, learning webinars, research publications and an international conference on legal aid innovations. Barefoot Law is a Ugandan nonprofit organization founded in 2013, with the mission to get the law to protect vulnerable people across Africa. It empowers people to develop legal solutions for their justice needs through innovative use of digital technologies.

title: West Virginia Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the West Virginia University Research Corporation which coordinates the West Virginia Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) explore partnerships with workforce and economic stakeholders to develop programming for youth professional skills, career exploration, and grow visibility of afterschool as an economic driver; 2) increase program quality by continuing to drive the improvement of statewide quality systems and develop new, aligned professional development resources; 3) work with education stakeholders to design and implement education recovery funding to help West Virginia youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen Education, Inc. resources.

title: Oklahoma Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Oklahoma Public School Resource Center which coordinates the Oklahoma Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) develop a strong strategic funding approach, align goals and resources, and establish active standing committees to secure long-term sustainability and engagement; 2) build relationships with key stakeholders and increase career exploration, mentorship and internship programming for youth with a focus on STEM; 3) work with education stakeholders to design and implement education recovery funding to help Oklahoma youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen Education, Inc. resources.

title: Modernizing Michigan Local Government Fiscal Transparency
description: The University of Michigan’s Center for Local, State and Urban Policy works to foster effective communication between academic researchers, stakeholders and the policymakers dealing with today’s state, local and urban policy problems. The Center for Local, State and Urban Policy will work to modernize and digitize Michigan local government financial reporting, with the city of Flint as the first pilot site.

title: Technical Assistance
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: In 2021 the Flint Cultural Center Corporation transferred operations of the Whiting Auditorium and the Capitol Theatre to the Flint Institute of Music. Initially, the grantee and the Flint Institute of Music signed a Memorandum of Understanding that established terms and conditions under which the Flint Institute of Music managed and operated the Whiting Auditorium and the Capitol Theatre until the permanent consolidation was complete. This grant increase will provide support for legal and accounting service providers to help the grantee complete a full transition of operations from the Flint Cultural Center Corporation to the Flint Institute of Music.

title: Massachusetts Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Massachusetts Afterschool Partnership which coordinates the Massachusetts Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) partner with local education agencies to expand community schools models by embedding afterschool programs in districts; 2) educate state leaders to highlight the impact of afterschool to demonstrate the need for state-level funding and collaboration; 3) work with education stakeholders to design and implement education recovery funding to help Massachusetts youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen Education, Inc. resources.

title: National Service and Volunteer Center Capacity Building
description: This grant to the United Way of Genesee County will provide capacity to support national service and volunteerism throughout Genesee County. National service members and volunteers provide critical resources to area nonprofits, government agencies and schools to help meet a variety of community needs such as blight elimination, neighborhood engagement, tutoring and mentoring.

title: New York Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: New York State Network for Youth Success, Inc.
description: This grant will support the New York State Network for Youth Success, Inc. which coordinates the New York Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) continue to work with state education and policy leaders to inform a New York universal afterschool initiative; 2) grow work with STEM ecosystems to create more accessible STEM focused programming geared towards workforce development; 3) work with education stakeholders to design and implement education recovery funding to help New York youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen Education, Inc. resources.

title: General Purposes
description: EnAccess — a Netherlands-based nonprofit organization — is developing a global network of innovators who openly share their knowledge and technologies to accelerate the adoption and use of modern energy access solutions in developing countries. Previous support to EnAccess has enabled the organization to develop several integrated components to such an ecosystem. These components include identifying gaps in the energy access sector and supporting the creation and adoption of the required technologies and tools to address such gaps. This work has also included the curation of an open repository of high-quality, proven energy access technologies and software, as well as the promotion of their widespread use across the energy access community. During this grant period, the grantee will support open-access innovations to support the use of off-grid solar solutions in agricultural value chains. EnAccess will also strengthen its aid to local innovators and associated innovation ecosystems to support the widespread adoption and use of existing open innovations.

title: Utah Statewide Afterschool Network
location: Salt Lake City, UT, United States
description: This grant will support Utah Afterschool Network which coordinates the Utah Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) leverage partnerships to develop and launch a data collection system to align metrics, streamline program reporting and inform effective advocacy for afterschool; 2) assess and improve tools, trainings and additional resources to create more effective programming and professional development opportunities; 3) work with education stakeholders to design and implement education recovery funding to help Utah youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen Education, Inc. resources.

title: California Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Foundation for California Community Colleges which coordinates the California Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) educate stakeholders across the education, health and human service sectors on the importance of afterschool as an opportunity to continuously support student mental health; 2) create systemic workforce solutions through pathways into, within and through afterschool; 3) work with education stakeholders to design and implement education recovery funding to help California youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen Education, Inc. resources.

title: Iowa Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Iowa Children’s Museum which coordinates the Iowa Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) enhance professional development opportunities for afterschool providers through new partnerships statewide, with a focus on staff and youth wellbeing; 2) utilize family engagement strategies to improve youth outcomes, share resources and generate new partnerships with key afterschool stakeholders; 3) work with education stakeholders to design and implement education recovery funding to help Iowa youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen Education, Inc. resources.

title: Washington Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support School’s Out Washington which coordinates the Washington Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) strengthen the statewide coalition of youth development and childcare providers to bolster advocacy and program quality throughout the afterschool continuum; 2) scale responsive professional development and program quality resources to providers across the state, with a focus on more robust local and regional efforts; 3) work with education stakeholders to design and implement education recovery funding to help Washington youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen Education, Inc. resources.

title: Arizona Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Arizona Center for Afterschool Excellence which coordinates the Arizona Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) continue to engage with state agencies to support efforts such as a new child care development fund plan and development of school-aged program guidelines; 2) expand professional development offerings for providers in Arizona, including the development of a credentialing initiative; 3) work with education stakeholders to design and implement education recovery funding to help Arizona youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen Education, Inc. resources.

title: Connecticut Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: Connecticut Network for Children and Youth, Inc.
description: This grant will support the Connecticut Network for Children and Youth, Inc. which coordinates the Connecticut Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) actively lead state-level initiatives including supporting statewide child care and social-emotional learning coalition efforts; 2) support local afterschool collaborative hubs to raise program quality, build local champions and pilot new afterschool outreach and engagement models; 3) work with education stakeholders to design and implement education recovery funding to help Connecticut youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen Education, Inc. resources.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Western Cape, Province of the, Eastern Cape, Province of, Northern Cape, Province of, Free State
description: The organization’s goal is to improve the quality of life in poor communities in South Africa by supporting community-based organizations that promote access to justice, gender equity, human rights, youth empowerment and food security. To this end, the Social Change Assistance Trust makes grants to community advice offices and local development agencies working in the Eastern Cape, Limpopo, Free State, Western Cape and Northern Cape provinces. In addition, the grantee provides training and connects organizations working in these areas. Activities under the previous grant included making grants of over $1,200,000 to 57 community advice offices, local development agencies, and other support organizations across five provinces. The grantee has built partnerships across multiple sectors and issues to unlock funding that reaches communities, including on topics such as climate change and gender based violence. During this grant period, the Social Change Assistance Trust will continue to support community advice offices and local development agencies to improve the quality of life for communities on the margins.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Western Cape, Province of the, Northern Cape, Province of, Eastern Cape, Province of, Free State
description: The organization’s goal is to improve the quality of life in poor communities in South Africa by supporting community-based organizations that promote access to justice, equity, human rights, youth empowerment and food security. To this end, the Social Change Assistance Trust makes grants to community advice offices and local development agencies working in the Eastern Cape, Limpopo, Free State, Western Cape and Northern Cape provinces. In addition, the grantee provides training and connects organizations working in these areas. Activities under the previous grant included making grants of over $1,200,000 to 59 community advice offices, local development agencies and other support organizations across five provinces. The grantee has built partnerships with foundations, multilateral organizations and businesses to unlock funding that reaches communities in response to various issues impacting communities, including climate resilience, gender justice and youth empowerment.
