During this grant period, the Social Change Assistance Trust will continue to support community advice offices and local development agencies to improve the quality of life for communities on the margins.

title: Standing Up the New Chronicle of Philanthropy
description: The program goal is to improve the information space for philanthropic and nonprofit organizations which will, in turn, support better policymaking and practice within the sector. Established in 1988, the Chronicle of Philanthropy is the nonprofit and philanthropic sector’s most prominent information source. In order to expand its reach and better serve the sector, the grantee is spinning off to become an independent nonprofit organization. Over the next two years, the grantee will employ contractors necessary to fully launch the new organization including consultants in organizational development, communications, governance and executive search and professional services such as legal, accounting and human resources. In addition, over the next two years, the grantee will add 13 new staff members to develop the Chronicle of Philanthropy’s independent business capability, digital capacity, explanatory journalism and an expanded opinion section.

title: Ohio Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the PAST Foundation which coordinates the Ohio Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) develop a strong strategic funding approach, align goals and resources, and establish active standing committees to secure long-term sustainability and engagement; 2) build relationships with key stakeholders and increase career exploration, mentorship and internship programming for youth with a focus on STEM; 3) work with education stakeholders to design and implement education recovery funding to help Ohio youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen Education, Inc. resources.

title: Service Education and Outreach Project
description: This grant will support Voices for National Service, a program of City Year, Inc., to continue a communications initiative that will seek to enhance public awareness of the impact of national service programs across the country. Specifically, this initiative will: develop resources highlighting the impact of national service; and leverage media and events to share the impact of national service with a broad audience.

title: Great Lakes Leadership Council
geographic_focus: North America, Indiana, Illinois, Michigan, Ohio, Wisconsin, Minnesota
description: Over the last two decades, the Council of State Governments has brought together state and provincial policymakers from the binational Great Lakes region to learn about key issues affecting the lakes in both the United States and Canada, offering ways to collaborate and build their capacity to be effective leaders and stewards of this freshwater resource. With prior Mott Foundation support, the grantee educated and convened policymakers through forums and institutes to exchange information and share ideas and pursue opportunities collectively. Renewed support will enable the Council of State Governments to continue its programs and activities, creating a space for members to discuss and advance cooperative solutions to the problems impacting the Great Lakes with a strong regional voice.

title: General Purposes
description: Infrastructure and energy projects constructed by development finance institutions like the World Bank and Asian Development Bank often come with environmental, social or governance risks. To address these risks, Accountability Counsel lawyers engage with development finance institutions’ accountability offices to advocate for people harmed by these institutions’ projects in infrastructure and energy. This grant will provide general purposes support to strengthen the grantee’s capacity to influence development finance institutions’ accountability offices to defend the rights of affected communities and remedy harm caused by internationally financed projects. Such support will also provide the Accountability Counsel stability and flexibility to respond to important unanticipated opportunities that may arise.

title: Capacity Support for Water Safety
grantee: Michigan League of Conservation Voters Education Fund
description: Michigan League of Conservation Voters Education Fund is a leader in efforts to secure funding and sound policies to protect, restore and enhance Michigan water resources. The grantee has been working with a coalition of state groups and frontline, community-based organizations — the water table — to forge a collective plan for sharing information and resources while coordinating strategies. With continued Mott Foundation support, the grantee will assist members of the water table with regrant dollars, communications materials and coordination to advance collective initiatives on water contamination, infrastructure and affordability issues.

title: Kindergarten to College Program
grantee: City and County of San Francisco
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: The City and County of San Francisco’s Kindergarten to College program was the first universal and automatic municipal children’s college savings program in the country. Since its inception in 2011, the program opened savings accounts for more than 52,000 students, the majority of whom are children of color, and has encouraged families, half of whom are low- and moderate-income, to save more than $15 million and earn millions more in program incentives. Its first cohort of participants graduated high school in 2023. Kindergarten to College has also inspired replications in cities around the country. Renewal funding will support planning, evaluation and outreach efforts that help the grantee prepare for the next phase of program operations, which will include distributions for high school graduates and integration with CalKIDS, the statewide college savings account initiative.

title: Tax Policy and Charities Project
description: The Tax Policy and Charities Project goal is to improve the policy environment for the nonprofit sector and philanthropy in the United States. The project provides a rapid response to current debates over tax policy as it affects charities, continually upgrades a tax model that incorporates thousands of provisions in the tax code, provides analysis of tax issues and involves scholars and policy officials in a discussion of new tax proposals. Over the past two years, the project has fostered and facilitated research and discussion on tax policy relating to charity. Future activities will include modeling tax and charity policy proposals, writing policy briefs and articles, providing congressional testimony and producing other materials regarding major tax and charity issues. The project is implemented by the Urban-Brookings Tax Policy Center of the Urban Institute. The grantee is a national think tank that gathers data, conducts research, evaluates programs, offers technical assistance overseas and educates Americans on social and economic issues to foster sound public policy and effective government.

title: Statewide Children's Savings Account Outreach Initiative
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: The state of California has led the Children’s Savings Account movement for over a decade, beginning with San Francisco’s Kindergarten-to-College initiative, which was the first municipal CSAs program in the country and has inspired dozens of replications across the state and nationally. Last summer, the state announced a universal statewide expansion of the California Kids Investment and Development Savings Program, funded with $2 billion of American Rescue Plan funds and expected to serve nearly four million participants. Foundation funding will help support outreach and education efforts that raise awareness of, and participation in, the expanded program and ensure the aspirational and educational benefits of CSAs reach the state’s most underserved communities. Coordinating and complimenting regional CSAs activity already underway in the state will be a key priority during the grant period. This project will be led by the ScholarShare Investment Board — the state agency charged with overseeing the state’s 529 college savings program and designing and implementing the CalKIDS effort.

title: Fiscal Solvency and Service Effectiveness Project
description: This renewal grant provides support for Michigan State University’s efforts to document and promote solutions that help America’s older industrial cities address chronic fiscal stress and advance overall fiscal health. During the grant period, the grantee will develop a range of potential scenarios for addressing structural deficits and assess the feasibility of each scenario with a particular focus on legal and political implications. Special focus will be given to how states and municipalities deploy American Rescue Plan and other federal funds allocated during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: PFAS Action Network
description: The Ecology Center is a national leader in addressing toxic chemicals in the environment, such as pre-and polyfluoroalkyl substances, known as PFAS, and is the co-founder and coordinator of the Great Lakes PFAS Action Network, a coalition of PFAS-impacted communities and environmental organizations founded in 2021. With partial support from the Mott Foundation, the network has grown its membership and public visibility, becoming a trusted source on PFAS issues for citizens, the media and policymakers. With renewed support, the network will continue to provide resources and support to citizen leaders from impacted communities so they can collectively aim to stop further PFAS contamination, clean up contaminated sites and support the immediate needs of communities harmed by PFAS.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Heart of the Lakes Center for Land Conservation Policy
description: Heart of the Lakes Center for Land Conservation Policy is Michigan’s only organization whose mission is to serve and support land conservancies in the Great Lakes state. With prior Mott Foundation funding, the grantee continued to advance the work of its members, increased engagement with partners and communities, initiated a capacity-building program for urban conservation, and facilitated coalitions to promote the outdoors. With renewed funding, Heart of the Lakes Center for Land Conservation Policy will focus on investing in public lands, ensuring equitable access to the outdoors, promoting nature-based climate solutions, leveraging strategic partnerships and supporting conservation organizations around the state.

title: 10 Cents a Meal in Flint and Genesee County
description: 10 Cents a Meal in Flint and Genesee County for Michigan’s Kids & Farms is a state-funded program providing schools and early childhood education centers with match incentive grant funding up to 10 cents per meal to purchase and serve Michigan-grown fruits, vegetables and legumes. The program is also a statewide food systems-change initiative that empowers schools and early childhood education centers to purchase healthy, locally grown produce, improve nutritional options for children and build local economies. This grant will support Groundwork Center for Resilient Communities to provide technical assistance, education, networking and awareness of the program’s benefits to the Flint community and its supporting organizations.

title: General Purposes
description: For over 50 years, Environmental Advocates of New York has been at the forefront of and has made critical progress toward protecting, enforcing and strengthening the policies that impact the health of New York’s water, climate and communities. The grantee connects policy to people across the state and in the Great Lakes region, prioritizing the needs of communities disproportionately impacted by environmental harms. With renewed funding from the Mott Foundation, the grantee will continue to advocate for innovative strategies and dedicated funding to advance their key priorities of clean water, climate resilience and healthy communities in New York state.

title: Broadening Participation in Great Lakes Advocacy
description: This Yale University project features an environmental fellows program that places graduate students in environmental organizations and foundations across the United States. The program fills a vital need to build a pipeline of future leaders from previously under-represented racial, ethnic, socioeconomic and other groups to help sustain an environmental workforce in the Great Lakes region and nationally. Research shows that people of color have historically not been well represented in environmental organizations and philanthropic giving. With renewed Mott Foundation support, three Yale environmental fellows will be placed in Great Lakes organizations each year out of a nationwide class of 35 graduate fellows. Fellows will receive training and professional development. In addition to the fellowship program, the project includes a national convening for the fellows and a robust national research agenda.

title: Empowering Midwestern Environmental Justice Organizations Addressing Water Equity
geographic_focus: Indiana, Minnesota, Wisconsin, Ohio, Michigan, Illinois
description: The Midwest Environmental Justice Network — a project of the Minneapolis Foundation — is led by and for community-based organizations in a twelve-state area working to connect and support grassroots groups and diverse leadership to address environmental issues impacting their communities at the local level. With previous Mott Foundation support, the network has been able to increase its communications and outreach and grow its partner engagement on environmental policies and programs. With renewed support, the network will continue to provide financial resources, peer learning, training and capacity building for groups working specifically on water conservation and drinking water access and affordability in the eight-state Great Lakes region.

title: Environmental Defenders Collaborative
description: Founded in 1993, the Global Greengrants Fund is a global organization supporting grassroots-led efforts to protect the planet and the rights of people through a participatory grantmaking model. The Environmental Defenders Collaborative, operated by the grantee and funded by a number of institutions, supports civil society and environmental and human rights advocates working at the community level. With prior Mott support, the collaborative leveraged Mott funding to increase by threefold the small grants provided to protect and support environmental defenders in South America. With renewed support, the Global Greengrants Fund will continue implementation of its strategy to protect defenders in South America, with a focus on Brazil.

title: Technical Assistance to Boost Great Lakes Communication
geographic_focus: New York, Indiana, Minnesota, Ohio, Michigan, Wisconsin, Midwest, Illinois
description: Since 1996, Freshwater Future has provided over $5 million in almost 1,300 grants for capacity building and technical assistance to groups working to protect and restore water in the Great Lakes region. With prior Mott Foundation support, the grantee worked with a communications consulting firm to provide technical support to organizations active in the Great Lakes basin to strengthen their communications capacity. With renewed support, Freshwater Future will continue working with a consulting firm, expand the pool of organizations receiving direct technical support and provide training and tools to other organizations to utilize communications to advance their organizational priorities more effectively.

title: Developing Community Foundations in Hungary
description: The project goal is to support the development of community foundations in Hungary. During the grant period, the Roots and Wings Foundation will expand and strengthen the Hungarian community foundation movement by increasing the effectiveness of existing community foundations, supporting the development of at least eight new community foundations and facilitating networking and sharing among community foundations. In addition, the grantee will increase its capacity to serve as a community foundation support organization in Hungary and Europe. The grantee was established in 2014 by a group of community development experts and practitioners interested in developing the community foundation field in Hungary. The grantee’s founders were instrumental in the establishment of the first community foundation in Hungary, the Ferencvaros Community Foundation in Budapest, in 2011. The Roots and Wings Foundation is committed to spreading the successful practices and lessons learned to other Hungarian communities and supporting their efforts to build community foundations.

title: General Purposes
description: The project goal is to raise awareness about social justice causes in South Africa. The Social Justice Initiative was established to mobilize resources from local philanthropists in support of social justice causes that promote fair access to constitutional rights, better delivery of services and a stronger democracy. Previous support from the Mott Foundation has enabled the grantee to provide thought leadership on social justice issues in the country, build solid relationships with philanthropists supporting social justice causes, and raise funds in support of organizations leading social justice work. During this grant period, the grantee will continue to champion social justice causes among wealthy South Africans to grow their support base, lead discussions on social justice issues and channel resources and funds to causes that pursue systemic change and promote access to justice, accountable governance and human rights in South Africa.

title: Flint and Genesee Literacy Network
description: Mott Community College serves as the lead agency for the Flint and Genesee Literacy Network. The network is a coalition of community organizations, businesses and governmental leaders working toward increasing literacy and basic skill levels in Genesee County. The grantee will work with network partners to increase their capacity to deliver high-quality early education and family literacy programming with a particular focus on two-generation approaches.

title: Scaling the Digital Activism Hub
description: The project goal is to build knowledge, communities of practice and capacity to support civil society actors at a time of unprecedented pressure and threats worldwide. To this end, Fundacja TechSoup developed the Digital Activism Program in response to persistent and emerging challenges and trends in the rapidly changing digital space. This relates to increasing awareness of the dangers of technology, including Artificial Intelligence, and the potential to leverage its power for good through collaboration and spreading positive and factual narratives in an increasingly hybrid world. During the previous grant period, the grantee expanded Hive Mind — an online global resource to help civil society actors to pool resources, share expertise and coordinate actions — leading to a more powerful and collective force for positive change. The grantee also organized global gatherings and expanded its global network of partners to better serve civil society in Africa and Latin America. Moving forward and adapting to the rapidly changing environment, Fundacja Techsoup will strengthen its global network, reassess its community of practice model, and redesign key functions to enhance collaboration, contribution and learning within the community.

title: Philanthropy Panel Study
description: Managed by Indiana University’s Lilly Family School of Philanthropy, the Philanthropy Panel Study collects detailed data on the giving and volunteering habits of several thousand American households over time and over generations. The dataset produced by the study is a comprehensive and accurate resource for measuring giving and volunteering in the U.S. and is used extensively by philanthropy and social sector researchers. During the previous grant period, the grantee collected, analyzed and disseminated the Philanthropy Panel Study data and findings. During the upcoming grant period, the grantee will continue this work and develop a new fact sheet to complement the data. Founded in 2012, the Lilly Family School of Philanthropy at Indiana University is dedicated to improving philanthropy by training and empowering students and practitioners to be innovators and leaders who create positive and lasting change in the world.

title: Philanthropy Panel Study
description: Managed by Indiana University’s Lilly Family School of Philanthropy, the Philanthropy Panel Study collects detailed data on the giving and volunteering habits of several thousand American households over time and over generations. The dataset produced by the study is a comprehensive and accurate resource for measuring giving and volunteering in the U.S. and is used extensively by philanthropy and social sector researchers. During the previous grant period, the grantee collected, analyzed and disseminated the Philanthropy Panel Study data and findings. During the upcoming grant period, the grantee will continue this work and develop new fact sheets to complement the data. Founded in 2012, the Lilly Family School of Philanthropy at Indiana University is dedicated to improving philanthropy by training and empowering students and practitioners to be innovators and leaders who create positive and lasting change in the world.

title: Ariadne Network Membership
description: This grant supports Ariadne’s core operations, including membership services and administrative costs. Ariadne is a European network of funders committed to promoting and protecting civil society and human rights. The network operates as a project of Global Dialogue, a United Kingdom registered nonprofit based in London, and currently connects more than 600 funders and philanthropists. Key achievements during the previous grant period included: 1) hosting over 20 online and in-person events; 2) publishing resources tailored to funders’ needs; 3) launching a mentoring program; and 4) convening members for the annual Grant Skills Week. During this grant period, Ariadne will undertake a strategic review process and deliver another set of events tailored to funders needs amidst growing restrictions and fewer resources. Established in 2009, Ariadne strengthens philanthropy by helping funders act strategically, collaborate effectively and welcome new donors into the field with greater impact.

title: European AI Fund: Capacity Building with European Civil Society
description: The project goal is to empower a diverse and resilient ecosystem of civil society organizations that have the capacity and the resources to take part in policy debates on artificial intelligence and related digital technologies. This will allow civil society actors to seek accountability for harms caused by artificial intelligence and advance work supportive of a public interest vision for artificial intelligence that serves people and society. To this end, a pooled fund within the Network of European Foundations will engage private funders and provide more than $7 million in grant support to digital rights and issue-specific nonprofits. The pooled fund will also hold space for learning and networking opportunities among funders and civil society actors. Since the launch of the fund in 2020, 17 foundations have contributed to the fund, which in turn supported 47 organizations with approximately $8.6 million in grants. The Network of European Foundations is based in Brussels, Belgium.

title: Charity & Security Network
description: The Charity & Security Network promotes and protects nonprofit organizations’ ability to serve communities, support peace and human rights, aid civilians in areas of disaster and armed conflict and build democratic governance. During the previous grant period, the grantee convened stakeholders, engaged in dialogue with policymakers, promoted legal frameworks that protect civil society’s positive contribution to human security, and provided legal and policy analysis on relevant issues to nonprofits, policymakers and other stakeholders. The grantee’s goals for the upcoming grant period include sharing information and analysis and convening key stakeholders on issues related to access to resources and financial services, sanctions, counterterrorism laws that criminalize civil society activities and using legal proceedings to decrease public participation. The Charity & Security Network is a project of NEO Philanthropy, a funder intermediary launched in 1983 as a Public Interest Project.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support the continued organizational and programmatic development of People in Need, one of the largest nonprofits in Central and Eastern Europe. The grantee: 1) provides relief and development assistance in response to natural disasters and violent conflict; 2) promotes human rights, civic engagement and civil society development; and 3) supports social inclusion and integration for marginalized groups. During the previous grant period, the grantee provided relief and development assistance in 27 countries, reaching more than 4.3 million people, including 890,000 people in Ukraine and neighboring countries following Russia’s full scale invasion. During the current grant period, the grantee will continue to respond to crises arising from war, conflict and natural disasters through its humanitarian relief programs and its support to civil society organizations working on education, human rights and social inclusion. Founded in 1992, People in Need is based in Prague, Czech Republic.

title: Service Education and Outreach Project
description: This grant will support Voices for National Service, a program of City Year, Inc., to continue a communications initiative that will seek to enhance public awareness of the impact of national service programs across the country. Specifically, this initiative will develop resources highlighting the impact of national service; provide strategic communications training to national service champions; and leverage media and events to share the impact of national service with a broad audience.

title: Freshwater Lab Internship Program
grantee: The Board of Trustees of the University of Illinois
description: The Freshwater Lab at the University of Illinois at Chicago develops cohorts of Great Lakes leaders through an internship program for university students from diverse backgrounds. The interns are placed in organizations focused on freshwater conservation, including nonprofit organizations, public agencies and community-based groups primarily in the greater Chicago area. The internship program and coursework span an academic semester and a summer session, giving students classroom training to build leadership and understanding of Great Lakes issues and gain practical training and networking with local professionals. With continued support, the grantee will expand the number of students participating in the program and create a strong network of alumni mentors.

title: National Service Fellowship
description: This grant to the STEM Next Opportunity Fund will help support a fellow at AmeriCorps. This fellowship is a public-private partnership initiative geared towards leveraging AmeriCorps to advance high-quality afterschool and summer learning programs. This initiative will: 1) strengthen collaboration between AmeriCorps and the United States Department of Education and other federal agencies in the area of afterschool and summer learning; 2) work collaboratively with afterschool and summer learning programs and AmeriCorps to lift up best practices and models for collaboration; and 3) support the development of new AmeriCorps programs focused on afterschool and summer learning.

title: Improving Early Childhood Care and Education Quality
description: Child Care Network works to promote the success of children, families and the community through quality child care education, advocacy and family support. With this grant, the grantee will bolster its efforts around supporting the family, friend and neighbor child care program and the early childhood talent pipeline program. These two programs help ensure that regardless of the option a family chooses for child care, the child will receive high-quality care.

title: Activist Education for Paralegals
description: The project goal is to increase the activism capacity of community paralegals to be able to advocate for systemic solutions to systemic injustices. To this end, Tshisimani Centre for Activist Education will continue providing education opportunities for community paralegals through its various offerings. Particular attention will be given to developing community paralegals’ understanding of the systemic nature of injustices and inequalities and how to tackle these challenges. Past support allowed the grantee to undertake foundation courses with selected community paralegals in South Africa; develop materials that can be shared and used more widely for community organizations and their staff; and participate in seminars related to community justice. The Tshisimani Centre for Activist Education was established in 2015 with the mandate to assist activists in building their own capacities, using creative means to elevate injustices and seeking solutions to addressing them.

title: The Praxis Program – A Foundation Course for Emerging Leaders
description: The project goal is to increase the capacity of community paralegals to be able to advocate for systemic solutions to systemic injustices. To this end, Tshisimani Centre for Activist Education will redefine its offerings to dig deeper into how it could reach sustained impact of its work. It plans to research and develop a new curriculum, test said curriculum and introduce a two-year education offering for community paralegals that is geared towards learning from different sectors and building solidarity. Past support has helped the grantee to implement its education offerings to both community paralegals and grassroots nonprofit stakeholders across South Africa. The Tshisimani Centre for Activist Education was established in 2015 with the mandate to assist community members in building their own capacities, using creative means to elevate injustices and seeking solutions to addressing them.

title: European Programme for Integration and Migration
description: The European Programme for Integration and Migration is a donor collaborative hosted by the Network of European Foundations. Established in 2005, this program strengthens the role played by civil society organizations in advocating for constructive approaches to migration in Europe. This is done through grantmaking, capacity development and networking activities addressing a range of issues, including exploring alternatives to detention, protecting migrant rights at borders, fostering inclusion, supporting children and youth on the move, protecting freedom of movement and developing strategic messaging on migration. Between 2005 and 2022, 23 foundations have joined this program, pooling approximately 29 million Euros to support almost 400 civil society organizations in 38 countries. Based in Brussels, the Network of European Foundations strengthens cooperation among foundations in Europe.

title: Servall Building Redevelopment
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant increase will provide additional funding to the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, a supporting organization of the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, for completing the redevelopment of the former 1st Source Servall Appliance Parts building located at 630 W. Kearsley Street. The building and adjacent properties will be redeveloped into the new headquarters for the nonprofit Flint River Watershed Coalition and its Kayak Flint rental program. The project furthers the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation’s charitable mission of improving and revitalizing downtown to address the blight and economic stagnancy that has plagued Flint in recent decades.

title: Help Center Capital Improvements
description: This grant to Bethel United Methodist Church will provide funds for facility repairs. The repairs are needed due to the high volume of Help Center Capital Improvements’ activities at the site since 2016. The Help Centers started as a response to the water crisis and have continued to provide needed resources during the pandemic. Each week, heavy semitrucks deliver food, water and other resources to the Help Center sites which have had a significant impact on the parking lots and warehouses. The Help Centers work with many other organizations across the city, including the Food Bank of Eastern Michigan, Genesee Health System, Hamilton Healthcare Network and Genesee County Health Department.

title: Help Center Capital Improvements
description: This grant to Asbury Community Development Corporation will provide funds for facility repairs at the Help Center Capital Improvements site located at Asbury United Methodist Church in Flint. The Help Centers started as a response to the water crisis and have continued to provide needed resources during the pandemic. Each week, heavy semitrucks deliver food, water and other resources to the sites, which have had a significant impact on the parking lots and warehouses. The Help Centers work with many other organizations across the city, including the Food Bank of Eastern Michigan, Genesee Health System, Hamilton Healthcare Network and Genesee County Health Department.

title: Help Center Capital Improvements
description: This grant to United Way of Genesee County will provide funds for facility repairs at R.L. Jones Community Outreach Center located at Greater Holy Temple Church of God in Christ in Flint. The repairs are needed due to the high volume of Help Center activities at the site since 2016. The Help Centers started as a response to the water crisis and have continued to provide needed resources during the pandemic. Each week, heavy semitrucks deliver food, water and other resources to the Help Center sites which have had a significant impact on the parking lots and warehouses. The Help Centers work with many other organizations across the city, including the Food Bank of Eastern Michigan, Genesee Health System, Hamilton Healthcare Network and Genesee County Health Department.

title: Consolidation Plan - Building Purchase and Renovation
description: This grant will provide funding to Genesee County to purchase the University Tower building in downtown Flint and consolidate many of its services into the new location. The County will realize economic and operational efficiencies from this move as it closes several oversized and outdated buildings across the county. Downtown businesses will benefit from additional foot traffic and most importantly, Flint and Genesee County residents will benefit from a single point of access for most governmental services in a location that is centrally located.

title: Conservation of the Slate River Forest
description: The Nature Conservancy, a global conservation organization, has identified over 100,000 acres in Michigan’s Upper Peninsula especially worthy of permanent protection and sustainable management. These places would connect wildlife corridors and fill in key areas of protection while also offering opportunities to forge public-private partnerships that balance conservation with compatible economic development. Across all these opportunities, the Slate River property is the most urgent and rare. With this partial funding from the Mott Foundation, The Nature Conservancy will acquire the property, develop a stewardship plan and engage with a range of stakeholders to manage the property in a way that emphasizes conservation outcomes, while also supporting the local economy and recreational activities.

title: Community-Centered Forest Protection in the Keweenaw Peninsula
description: The Nature Conservancy, a leading global conservation organization, has identified an opportunity to protect over 35,000 acres at the tip of the Keweenaw Peninsula in Michigan, while also pioneering new approaches to conservation. The project has the potential to tap unconventional sources of revenue, allow the local community to exert control over the use of its natural resources and support a sustainable economic future for the region. Foundation funds would be used during the early stages of the project to acquire a purchase option, develop a community-centered protection plan in consultation with local leaders and document the lessons learned from the project.

title: Creating Opportunities and Building Capacity for Urban Conservation in Michigan
description: Nationally, parks serving primarily non-white and low-income neighborhoods are smaller in size and four to five times more crowded than parks serving white and high-income households. This uneven distribution of high-quality urban open space and parks is evident throughout the Great Lakes, including older industrial cities in Michigan. To address these deficiencies, The Conservation Fund — a leading national conservation organization — will undertake a project with three goals: increase coordination among different urban conservation stakeholders, increase the capacity of such local stakeholders to successfully execute urban land conservation projects and provide loans and grants that can be used for property acquisition and to strategically unlock other funding. The Conservation Fund will pursue these goals through a combination of technical assistance, regrants and revolving loan funds.

title: Powered by Youth Voice: Future Directions for Afterschool
description: This grant to ExpandED Schools will advance new directions for the afterschool field by empowering young people as designers of future afterschool programs. Building upon the Ralph C. Wilson, Jr. Foundation’s Generator Z initiative, this project will leverage the creativity, passion and knowledge of young people to design new afterschool programs. Specifically, this grant will include support to survey over 1,000 youth across all 50 states, convene teams of young people to develop their ideas and host a challenge event for participating youth. Through directly engaging young people, this project will result in youth-driven ideas that will guide a new generation of afterschool programs, practice and policy.

title: Youth Substance Abuse Reduction Program
grantee: Institute for Behavior and Health, Inc.
description: This grant will provide funds to the Institute for Behavior and Health, Inc. to continue to advance the critical messaging aimed at curbing adolescent substance abuse. Central to this initiative will be physician education and working with lead organizations in the field to promote the acceptance and integration of consistent messaging that promotes a no-use policy of alcohol, tobacco, marijuana or other drugs among youth.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Association for Research on Nonprofit Organizations & Voluntary Action
description: This grant provides support to the Association for Research on Nonprofit Organizations & Voluntary Action, a leading U.S.-based national and international association that connects scholars, teachers and practitioners interested in research on nonprofit organizations, voluntary action, philanthropy and civil society. Principal activities include: 1) organizing an annual conference; 2) publishing the leading scholarly journal in the field, the Nonprofit and Voluntary Sector Quarterly; 3) providing tools and media that enable the grantee to support research, discussion and teaching; 4) initiating and supporting the Association for Research on Civil Society in Africa; and 5) organizing the annual Symposium on Public Policy and Nonprofits. With this increase, the grantee will enhance membership recruitment efforts, build and sustain partnerships with academic and nonprofit institutions and become a more diverse, equitable and inclusive organization. Founded in 1971, the grantee is a neutral, open forum that brings together both theoretical and applied interests, helps scholars gain insight into the daily concerns of nonprofits, and provides nonprofit professionals with connections to research they can use to improve their work.

title: Strengthening New Development Bank Safeguards
grantee: Pontifical Catholic University Rio de Janeiro
description: The BRICS Policy Center — an initiative of the Pontifical Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro — focuses on analyzing the evolving landscape of international development finance and its impact on social and environmental standards in South America. Over the past grant period, the Center enhanced its online databases to monitor Chinese investments in the region, established a tracking system for the clean energy transition and contributed to workshops and other knowledge-sharing initiatives. Over the next grant period, the Center aims to intensify its scrutiny and analysis of pivotal financial institutions involved in the shift towards cleaner energy. Additionally, Pontifical Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro will collaborate with key stakeholders to promote the adoption of socially and environmentally responsible loan criteria within international financial institutions.

title: General Purposes
description: The Alliance for the Great Lakes is a leading organization working to address and solve some of the biggest environmental challenges facing the region. For over 50 years, the Alliance has been focused on improving water quality and water infrastructure, reducing agricultural pollution, stopping invasive species and restoring the Great Lakes through local partnerships, volunteerism and coalition building. With renewed support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee will continue its advocacy and education efforts to create and strengthen policies that provide safe, clean and accessible water for the more than 40 million residents of the Great Lakes region and ensure the Great Lakes are protected and healthy for future generations.

title: Harold Alfond College Challenge Program Evaluation
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant will enable the Alfond Scholarship Foundation to continue the Harold Alfond College Challenge Program, recognized as the nation’s first statewide children’s savings account program. During the renewal grant period, the anticipated priorities and activities include program implementation and evaluation. In addition, the grantee will support broader field-building by sharing research findings from the first two grant periods to inform program design innovations both in Maine and nationally. Established in 2008 as a pilot program in Portland, Maine, the college challenge program automatically awards a $500 grant to every child born in the state to encourage educational savings and to foster aspirations for higher education.

title: News and Information Programs
description: This grant provides funding to National Public Radio in support of its news and information service. The grantee is recognized as one of the most trusted media brands in the country for its fair and fact-based coverage of national and international news. Each month, over 105 million people are reached through radio, podcasts, websites, social media and mobile apps with news and information to help create a more engaged public.

title: Community Justice in Africa Features
description: The project goal is to elevate the work of African community justice institutions in the media. To this end, All Protocol Observed NPC will use its newspaper, The Continent, to publish news reporting and features on community justice work in Africa. It will publish work outside capital cities, where injustices are often rife and often invisible. Past support has allowed the grantee to publish over 20 articles on people-centered justice in Africa. All Protocol Observed NPC used a unique model of recruiting journalists in specific countries to write their own stories. One of its community justice articles was also nominated for a One World Media prize.

title: Community Justice in Africa Features
description: The project goal is to elevate the work of African community justice institutions in the media. To this end, All Protocol Observed NPC will use its newspaper, The Continent, to publish news reporting and features on community justice work in Africa. It will publish work outside capital cities, where injustices are often rife and often invisible. Past support has allowed the grantee to publish over 40 articles on people-centered justice in Africa. All Protocol Observed NPC used a unique model of recruiting journalists in specific countries to write their own stories.

title: General Purposes
description: For over 50 years, Clean Wisconsin has worked to protect and preserve Wisconsin’s clean water, clean air and natural heritage. With an active membership and advocacy base of more than 20,000, their staff of experts conducts sound science, engages in public policy, takes legal action and fosters strong partnerships with allies and stakeholders to help ensure a safe, healthy environment for all. The grantee’s work has led to policy advances such as protections against PFAS contamination, reductions in agricultural runoff and cleanup of urban stormwater while growing partnerships and coalitions to address these issues. With renewed support, Clean Wisconsin will continue to advance its mission through policy advocacy, scientific research, regional collaboration and education, and community engagement to help ensure a more resilient and environmentally just future for the state, including communities in the Great Lakes region.

title: Michigan State University Flint Campus Expansion
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will provide funding to the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, a supporting organization of the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, for the construction of new office and meeting space for Michigan State University’s College of Human Medicine’s Flint campus adjacent to its existing space in the former Flint Journal Building. The additional space will both accommodate the expansion of public health expertise and resources in Flint and contribute to the vibrancy of the Health and Wellness District in downtown Flint.

title: Michigan News and Information Programs
description: This grant provides funding to the University of Michigan’s Michigan Radio in support of its news and information service. Located in Ann Arbor, Michigan Radio is a trusted media brand in the state known for its fair and fact-based coverage of state, national and international news. Michigan Radio reaches its audience with radio content, podcasts, websites, social media and mobile apps, providing news and information to help create a more engaged public.

title: Tribal Science, Training and Communications Project
grantee: Great Lakes Indian Fish and Wildlife Commission
description: The Great Lakes Indian Fish and Wildlife Commission works with tribal governments in Michigan, Wisconsin and Minnesota to protect tribal interests in the ecology of ceded territories in the northern portions of those states. With previous Mott support, the Commission identified the tools and information needed to be effective participants in mine permitting and environmental review processes, including baseline data collection and improved wetland mapping. With renewed support, the Commission will continue to participate fully on water quality issues and ecosystem protection, while also cultivating the next generation of leaders through an internship program to expose students to careers in natural resource management and tribal culture.

title: Pathfinders for Peaceful, Just and Inclusive Societies: Civil Society Participation & Voice
description: The Pathfinders for Peaceful, Just and Inclusive Societies, a program of New York University, is a multi-stakeholder platform that seeks to promote solutions to overcome the lack of access to global justice. In 2022-23, efforts by the Pathfinders and its partners to promote people-centered justice as an organizing principle in offering justice services, saw 60 countries endorse these principles. Twenty-one of these countries joined in the Justice Action Coalition, along with civil society and other partners, to further advocate for people-centered policy change. This growing campaign for people-centered justice contributed to key international actors including United States Agency for International Development and the United Nations Development Program, to explicitly adopt people-centered principles in their programming. In 2024-25, the grantee will continue their justice work in cooperation with the Justice Action Coalition, a multi-stakeholder coalition of countries and organizations championing equal access to justice for all. Their efforts will focus on three priority areas: 1) working with national governments to accelerate implementation of access to justice strategies; 2) engaging international and multi-lateral institutions and cross-sectoral partnerships to advance justice; and 3) fostering an effective initiative for justice at international, national and local levels.

title: Flint Home Explosion Fund
description: This grant will provide support to the Flint residents impacted by the November 22, 2021 Flint Home Explosion Fund. The United Way of Genesee County established the fund, at the request of the City of Flint, to help aid Flint residents who were directly impacted by the home explosion that occurred in the 3900 block of Hogarth Avenue on Flint’s west side. The grantee will work with the City of Flint to address residents’ needs.

title: Improving Equity and Accountability for Native American Communities with Community Foundations
description: The program goal is to investigate how United States community foundations can more effectively engage with Native communities to advance equity. Native Americans in Philanthropy will lead a series of convenings and conduct other data-gathering efforts through its networks of Native stakeholders, focused on the role of community foundations in relation to Native communities. Afterward, the grantee will produce a report that will share findings and recommendations for long-term, sustainable accountability and meaningful partnerships between Native communities and community foundations. While community foundations and their donors will be the ultimate audience for the work, this project will center the voice of Indigenous community leaders and provide them a platform for candid and honest guidance to community foundation leaders and their donors. Founded in 1990, Native Americans in Philanthropy promotes equitable and effective philanthropy in Native communities.

title: Protecting Water Resources in the Great Lakes State
description: Michigan Trout Unlimited is among the state’s leading organizations working to protect and conserve cold water streams and healthy aquatic habitats in Michigan. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has made progress on water management and large-quantity water withdrawal programs, dam management and dam removal and member engagement on Great Lakes environmental health issues. With renewed support, Michigan Trout Unlimited will continue to help improve the state’s water use and withdrawal program, advise landowners on dam removals and educate the public about threats to the Great Lakes, including invasive species and climate change impacts on watersheds.

title: Promoting Bioeconomy Financing for the Amazon
grantee: Nonprofit Enterprise and Self-Sustainability Team, Inc.
description: The Nonprofit Enterprise and Self-Sustainability Team, Inc., is a nonproft organization focused on building sustainable small businesses, associations and cooperatives. The grantee’s new initiative in the Amazon is now supporting establishment of forest conservation enterprises. This grant will support the grantee to conduct research and document lessons learned from conservation enterprises engaged in the Amazon into policy recommendations for development finance institutions.

title: Christopher Stallworth Fund
description: The grant will provide funds to the Community Foundation of Greater Flint for the Christopher Stallworth Fund. The funds will provide support to the Flint community for activities that celebrate Chris’ life and acknowledge the things that he held dear. Examples of projects that could be supported include community gathering and engagement activities, mentoring of young people, entrepreneurship activities and grassroots workforce activities.

title: Equitable School Funding: Empowering Michigan Stakeholders with Nonpartisan Data and Expertise
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: Education Trust is a research and advocacy organization working to close opportunity gaps and raise achievement for students of color and students from low-income families. The Midwest division engages Michigan based organizations and leaders to advocate for equitable funding and opportunity for Michigan children. The Education Trust-Midwest will provide nonpartisan data and best practice expertise to better inform citizens, leaders and major educational stakeholders, including leading journalists, corporate and civil rights leaders and policymakers about equitable funding.

title: Hasselbring Senior Center Improvements
description: With this grant, the City of Flint will make interior and exterior improvements to the Hasselbring Senior Center. The center is highly valued as a place for Flint’s seniors and other community members to gather for activities, recreation, meals and socialization. However, the center operates on a modest budget and funds typically aren’t available for maintenance, repairs or updates beyond those that are most critical. The updates at Hasselbring will make the space safer, more inviting and engaging for those who spend time at the center and will position the center for greater sustainability as a community asset into the future.

title: Brennan Senior Center Improvements
description: With this grant, the City of Flint will make interior and exterior improvements to the Brennan Senior Center. The center is highly valued as a place for Flint’s seniors and other community members to gather for activities, recreation, meals and socialization. However, the center operates on a modest budget and funds typically are not available for maintenance, repairs or updates beyond those that are most critical. The updates at Brennan will make the space safer, more inviting and engaging for those who spend time at the center and will position the center for greater sustainability as a community asset into the future.

title: Jurists Promoting Access to Justice and Defending the Rule of Law in Africa
description: The project goal is to build better relationships between community paralegals and the formal legal fraternity in Africa. To this end, the International Commission of Jurists will undertake various activities to create space for meaningful conversations between the judiciary, lawyers and community paralegals. This grant will support these engagements in southern Africa, with a goal to replicate the project at scale. The grantee was established in 1952 with the purpose of promoting justice and human rights within the formal legal sector. With headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland, this grant will be executed by the International Commission of Jurists’ Africa Program based in Johannesburg, South Africa.

title: Building Renovation
description: Legal Services of Eastern Michigan offers free civil legal assistance to low-income people across a 14-county service region in mid-east Michigan. The grantee’s mission is to use legal skills to address the causes and effects of poverty with special emphasis on the issues affecting the survival needs of low-income people. This grant will support the stabilization of the organization’s building which will allow the grantee to continue to provide services to the community that they serve.

title: Community Foundation Development in Ghana
description: The goal of the project is to develop community foundations in Ghana. Over the past year, the PureTrust Foundation LBG introduced the concept of community foundations to 20 communities in 10 regions across the country. The grantee produced learning materials, supported 10 initiative groups and launched one community foundation. Over the next three years, the grantee will provide support and tools to the initiative groups, create a learning community and platforms, continue to popularize the community foundation concept and pilot local resource mobilization activities. Additionally, this grant increase will enable the PureTrust Foundation LBG to provide challenge grants to new community foundations to help build their fundraising capability and funding base.

title: Forming and Strengthening a Network of Community Foundations in Costa Rica
description: The project goal is to support the formation and strengthening of community foundations in Costa Rica. To this end, the Forever Costa Rica Association will strengthen the existing network of seven Costa Rican community foundations by developing a financial sustainability strategy and providing capacity-building workshops. The grantee will also organize and conduct domestic and international learning exchanges and award matching grant funds to network members aimed at stimulating local giving. The grantee will develop a communications strategy for the network and raise awareness about community foundations throughout the country with the anticipation of identifying at least two new prospects to join the network by the end of the two-year grant period. The Forever Costa Rica Association was created in 2010 to enhance partnerships and mobilize resources for biodiversity conservation and human well-being in Costa Rica.

title: Community Foundation Development in Costa Rica
description: The project goal is to support the formation and strengthening of community foundations in Costa Rica. Over the past two years, the Forever Costa Rica Association provided technical assistance, seed capital, financial sustainability planning and experience exchange opportunities for Costa Rica’s seven community foundations. The association also supported the process of the creation of Costa Rica’s first community foundation network, COMUNIFF. During the next two years, the Association aims to consolidate a strong, well-governed and financially sustainable community philanthropy movement in Costa Rica. This will include: 1) implementing financial sustainability plans; 2) building robust governance systems; 3) enhancing operational capacity; 4) supporting networked collaboration; and 5) enabling effective local fundraising and partnerships. The Association also envisions that two new organizations will join COMUNIFF in the near future. The Forever Costa Rica Association was created in 2010 to enhance partnerships and mobilize resources for biodiversity conservation and human well-being in Costa Rica.

title: Community Foundation Development in Malawi
description: The purpose of the project is to develop community foundations in Malawi. To achieve this goal, World Connect Malawi will increase awareness and interest of the community foundation concept, expand knowledge and understanding among partners and identify initiatives that have the potential to become community foundations. Additionally, the grantee will test resource and asset development initiatives, adapt the concept to the Malawian context and develop a long-term plan for expanding the community foundation concept in the country. The grantee was established in 2021 as an independent grantmaking entity and supports communities to lead their own development by identifying challenges in their communities and using their time, treasure and talents to resolve these challenges. Since 2018, World Connect Malawi supported over 121 communities across the country to unlock over $1 million towards activities prioritized and led by the communities themselves.

title: Community Foundation Development in Malawi
description: The purpose of the project is to develop community foundations in Malawi. Over the past year, World Connect Malawi introduced the community foundation concept to 10 groups that expressed an interest in becoming community foundations. Support to the groups included capacity-building training, governance restructuring and registration with the Malawian government. The grantee partnered with local media groups to create awareness of the community foundation concept nationally. Over the next two years, the grantee will increase the number of groups that are exposed to the community foundation model, provide ongoing support and training to existing groups, produce learning materials, build a community of supporters and continue to raise awareness about community foundations in the country. Additionally, the grantee will support the emergence of a network of community foundations to enable learning. Based in Lilongwe, the grantee was established in 2021 as an independent grantmaking entity to support community-led development. Since 2018, World Connect Malawi supported over 121 communities across the country to unlock over $1 million towards activities prioritized and led by the communities themselves.

title: Organizational Assessment and Planning
description: The purpose of the Flint Downtown Development Authority is to: 1) remedy and prevent deterioration; 2) encourage historical preservation; 3) create and implement development plans; 4) promote economic growth and redevelopment; and 5) encourage the expansion of commercial enterprises within the downtown district boundaries. This grant will be utilized to complete an organizational assessment and a strategic plan to guide the growth and development of the organization, which will allow the grantee to continue to serve the downtown community in a low-income urban area. The plan will include input from residents and a broad range of stakeholders in order to further develop a downtown that is comprised of diverse community enterprises and accessible to everyone.

title: General Purposes
description: The Climate Leadership Council is a research and advocacy organization whose mission is to develop and promote a carbon dividends framework as a viable climate change policy solution, primarily in the United States. With past support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has had considerable success influencing the discussion about climate change solutions in the media, among policymakers and with the general public. Renewed support will allow the grantee to pursue its aims by utilizing its stakeholder network, undertaking multidisciplinary policy research, educating policymakers and informing the public. This will include the launch of a new research center focused on climate and trade policy and the continuation of a public seminar series named in memory of the grantee’s founder.

title: General Purposes
description: Conservation and good natural resource management are essential for poverty alleviation, sustainable economic development, food and freshwater security, conflict avoidance and human health. To effectively address this set of interconnected issues, policymakers need high-quality information from trusted sources on a range of topics. Since its founding in 2010, the ICCF Group has served this educational role in the U.S. and internationally, currently supporting conservation caucuses in seventeen countries. With general purposes support, the grantee will continue to deliver a successful series of briefings, roundtables and workshops on a range of issues, including forests and energy for federal policymakers in the U.S.

title: Hunters and Anglers for Climate Solutions
description: A comprehensive approach to addressing climate change should include solutions that harness the power of natural systems, such as forestry and agricultural practices that sequester carbon. The Theodore Roosevelt Conservation Partnership, a national organization representing hunter and angler groups from across the country, is leading an effort to support nature-based climate solutions at the federal level. With prior Mott Foundation support, the partnership conducted research, launched an interactive map highlighting successful climate solution projects and undertook additional activities to educate decision-makers, hunters, anglers and other stakeholders about nature-based climate solutions. With this renewal grant, the grantee will add new content to their online interactive map, develop complimentary digital video content, work with corporate leaders to promote nature-based climate solutions and continue to educate a range of stakeholders, including decision-makers, hunters and anglers from diverse communities.

title: Emergency Operating Funds
description: The purpose of the Flint Downtown Development Authority is to correct and prevent deterioration, encourage historical preservation, create and implement development plans, promote economic growth and redevelopment, and encourage the expansion of commercial enterprises, all within the downtown district boundaries. This grant will provide the grantee with emergency operating funds during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Education and Economic Development Initiatives
description: This renewal grant provides partial support for the Genesee Area Focus Fund and its supported organization, the Flint & Genesee Group, to deliver economic development and education and training services to the Flint area and build Flint’s economic resilience. The Flint & Genesee Group increases business investment, job creation and industry diversification through business retention, expansion and attraction activities, as well as entrepreneurial support services. The organization also enhances the region’s economic competitiveness and quality of life by providing workforce education and training programming across all age levels, and by engaging in special initiative projects with strategic partners.

title: Innovative Financing for Local Agrisolar Entrepreneurs - Uganda
description: The Innovation Village Hub, a Ugandan nonprofit organization, was founded in 2017 to address the challenge of youth unemployment in Uganda. Over the years, the grantee has established a nationwide youth entrepreneurship ecosystem that combines affordable co-working spaces with entrepreneurship training, technical support and financing services. With this grant, The Innovation Village Hub will provide targeted start-up incubation and acceleration services aimed at increasing the share of financial flows going to local entrepreneurs who are providing solar energy services across key agricultural value chains in Uganda.

title: Better Financing for Local Solar Energy Entrepreneurs in East Africa
description: Access to affordable and equitable financing is the biggest barrier to achieving Sustainable Development Goal 7 — universal access to modern energy services by 2030. For the seventh consecutive year, the world has failed to invest the required financing towards the goal. The Kenya Climate Innovation Center has been working since 2012 to provide business development advisory services and financing to local entrepreneurs creating climate and clean energy solutions in Kenya. With this grant, the grantee will expand its provision of business development advisory and financing support services to support local entrepreneurs working to enable accelerated access to solar energy services for productive use within rural off-grid communities of Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania.

title: Community Advice Office Support Project
description: The goal of the Community Advice Office Support Project is to increase access to justice for communities in the Gauteng province of South Africa. To this end, ProBono.Org will continue to work with community advice offices in Gauteng to provide justice services to poor and marginalized people. It will also continue to use its network of legal practitioners to provide backup legal support to community paralegals while organizing and conducting training on various aspects of the law. Past support has allowed the grantee to support advice offices in Gauteng with justice services while undertaking training and community outreach activities on various aspects of the law. ProBono.Org’s primary focus is to harness the skills and expertise of legal practitioners to deliver pro bono civil legal assistance to organizations working for social justice and to expand access to justice for low-income, vulnerable and marginalized communities.

title: Strengthening the ACCESS Coalition
description: Energy development finance investments by the African Development Bank and the World Bank Group in Africa can be better transformed towards more distributed renewable energy services to increase the likelihood of meeting sustainable development goals on the continent. To address this challenge, this grant to Loughborough University will support the ACCESS Coalition to continue engaging African civil society towards influencing national and regional development finance institution investments away from fossil fuels to distributed renewable energy solutions. The grantee will support the ACCESS Coalition to strengthen its governance and support its member organizations towards more effective engagement of the African Development Bank and the World Bank Group distributed renewal energy investments. This work continues the Mott Foundation’s earlier three years of support to the ACCESS Coalition, which has increased civil society participation and engagement with the African Development Bank and the World Bank Group towards improved quantity and quality of investments for distributed renewable energy in Africa.

title: Prahl Center Renovations
description: This grant will provide funding to Mott Community College for significant renovations to its Marie Prahl College Center. The current building, built in 1971, is outdated and inefficient both in terms of its physical design and its ability to provide programming and services to students. As Mott Community College nears its 100th year anniversary in 2023, renovating the center that serves as the heart of the campus is a symbolic renewal but, more importantly, a very tangible renewal in meeting the needs of students today and into the future.

title: Baker College Site Redevelopment Plan
description: This grant will provide funding to Communities First, Inc. to purchase the now-shuttered Baker College Flint campus and transform it into a mixed-use property that will provide space for social service organizations, businesses, vocational and technical skills training, and apartments for individuals and families.

title: General Purposes
description: Founded in 1934, the Metropolitan Planning Council has been committed for many years to addressing critical environmental issues faced by Chicago, Illinois and the Great Lakes region, including the sustainable management of the region’s water resources. During the previous grant period, the grantee: 1) conducted research; 2) led collaborative policy development processes; and 3) helped implement policies and practices on a range of issues such as transit, housing and water resources. With renewed Mott Foundation support, the Metropolitan Planning Council will continue its full range of programming including efforts to promote green stormwater infrastructure and accelerate lead service line replacement.

title: Action for Clean Drinking Water
description: Midwest Environmental Advocates is the only Wisconsin-based nonprofit environmental law center that directly represents and assists local communities to address threats to safe, clean and abundant water in the state. With previous Mott Foundation support, the grantee has provided legal and technical support to Wisconsin communities on issues ranging from groundwater pollution to lead poisoning to the regulation of toxic chemicals like PFAS found in the environment. With renewed support, the grantee will help residents — including Tribal and rural communities — address the continued threats to safe water, especially nutrient pollution and lead in drinking water and advance the protection of wetlands.

title: Accountability Research Center
description: The Accountability Research Center at American University aims to improve the social and environmental outcomes of development finance institutions by holding those institutions accountable to their own commitments for engaging affected communities. With Mott Foundation support, the grantee will collaborate with organizations in developing countries to monitor projects and assess whether and how the World Bank and, more recently, the Inter-American Development Bank, deliver in practice on commitments to transparency, participation, sustainability and accountability. Through its leadership of the Citizen Engagement Working Group, a dialogue space between World Bank officials and civil society organizations, the Accountability Research Center at American University will leverage its research by reporting back to policymakers within the banks, and by sharing information and coordinating with civil society partners working toward the same goal.

title: Ensuring Development and Climate Finance Support Sustainable Development
description: The Center for International Environmental Law was founded in 1989 to strengthen international environmental law, policy and management and ensure that environmental protection and community decisionmaking drive investment decisions at international financial institutions. Over the prior grant period, research and recommendations from the grantee have been incorporated into social and environmental policies at the International Finance Corporation and the Inter-American Development Bank. This renewal grant builds on two decades of efforts to promote strong implementation of environmental and social policies and practices at the World Bank Group, by ensuring that the accountability process results in meaningful, effective remedy for communities that have suffered harm.

title: Energy Convergence for Off-Grid Amazonian Communities Program
description: Michigan State University has been awarded a five-year grant from the National Science Foundation Convergence Program to support an interdisciplinary team of engineers, hydrologists, climatologists and social scientists to develop innovative energy solutions for isolated communities impacted by large-scale hydroelectric development in the Amazon. This project will complement that award by supporting the team to work with a federal Brazilian university and two local communities in the Tapajos River basin to assist in design and implementation of innovative sustainable energy systems, provide training for local technicians and document and disseminate media products on the benefits and results of the program for replication.

title: General Purposes
description: The International Energy Initiative Brasil is an independent, nongovernmental organization founded by sustainable energy development experts in 1991. The grantee’s mission is to promote — initiate, strengthen and advance — the efficient production and use of energy for sustainable development. This general purposes support will enable the grantee to implement its strategic plan focusing on solutions for energy poverty, renewable energy and energy efficiency in Brazil, and specifically the Brazilian Amazon.

title: Facility Planning and Pre-development
description: With this grant, the YMCA of Greater Flint will conduct facility planning and pre-development work as it explores the construction of a new building in downtown Flint. Architectural and environmental studies will help the grantee’s leadership develop plans for a sustainable and enhanced downtown facility that would serve Flint and Genesee County residents with increased opportunities for health and wellness as well as safe and affordable housing options.

title: Grand Canyon National Park's Indigenous Affairs Program
description: The Grand Canyon Conservancy, in collaboration with the Inter-tribal Working Group made up of representation from each of the 11 tribes associated with the Grand Canyon, will advance the work of the Indigenous Affairs program, providing factual, authentic and culturally appropriate information about the tribes to the 6 million annual visitors to the Grand Canyon.

title: Capacity Strengthening on Digital Security in West Africa
description: The project goal is to increase the awareness, understanding and engagement of civil society organizations in West Africa to the digital security risks that impact their work and the communities they serve. To achieve this, the West Africa Civil Society Institute will identify and raise awareness about the digital security risks, generate new knowledge on the issues and strengthen the capacity of civil society organizations and actors. Through this project, the grantee will: 1) map the digital security risks for nonprofits in the region; 2) produce material that will create awareness around these risks; 3) provide training to organizations on ways to mitigate the risks; 4) document the stories of change; 5) support a community of practice; and 6) apply the knowledge generated to support policy reform efforts for the sector. The West Africa Civil Society Institute works to strengthen the institutional and operational capacities of civil society organizations in the region.

title: Capacity Strengthening on Digital Security in West Africa
description: The project goal is to increase awareness and understanding of digital security risks to civil society organizations in West Africa. To achieve this, the West Africa Civil Society Institute produces knowledge, provides training and exposes nonprofits to policies that affect them. During the previous period, the grantee provided training on digital security to civil society organizations in Senegal, Cote d’Ivoire, Nigeria and Ghana. The grantee also launched a report that mapped the landscape in West Africa on digital security. To build on this work, the grantee plans to: 1) extend the training to other countries in the region; 2) build a cadre of trainers; 3) document knowledge and evidence on digital rights advocacy across the region; and 4) improve partnerships between policymakers and civil society through dialogue. Based in Ghana, the West Africa Civil Society Institute works to strengthen the institutional and operational capacities of civil society organizations in the region.

title: General Purposes
description: PHILEA, also known as the European Foundation Centre, is an independent membership association of foundations and corporate funders dedicated to promoting organized philanthropy in Europe and internationally.
