The grantee focuses on providing intellectual leadership on emerging policy agendas and societal trends that will impact institutional philanthropy, fostering connections within philanthropy and with external actors, providing a voice for European institutional philanthropy and developing a new membership strategy. In 2022, the European Foundation Centre and the Donors and Foundations Networks of Europe will combine their operations and programming, with the Donors and Foundations Networks of Europe being merged into the grantee. Additional grant funds will support this process and the increased operational and programmatic costs. Established in 1989 by seven of Europe’s leading foundations, the European Foundation Centre serves a core membership of over 190 members.

title: General Purposes
description: The Biodiversity Funders Group is a professional association of environmental, conservation and climate, and energy grantmakers. Approximately 70 member institutions — predominantly private foundations — support the organization. More than 200 other grantmaking institutions benefit from the grantee’s activities. Every year, the grantee provides timely information and opportunities for networking and collaboration for participating funders. This includes multiple webinars every month, an electronic newsletter and yearly gatherings convened by individual programs and working groups, including the Funders of the Amazon Basin.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Pennsylvania, Ontario, Ohio, New York, Michigan, Wisconsin, Indiana, Illinois, Minnesota
description: Freshwater Future, a Great Lakes regional organization founded more than 20 years ago, helps communities address pressing water issues by providing grants, capacity building and technical expertise to local groups and leaders. Over the past two years with partial Mott Foundation support, the grantee has undertaken a range of activities including making more than 80 small grants to community-based organizations, providing organizational capacity-building assistance to 30 groups and helping over 300 community groups engage in a range of policy issues including Great Lakes restoration and access to safe and affordable drinking water. With renewed support from the Mott Foundation, Freshwater Future will continue to assist community-based organizations with small grants and technical assistance while also building its organizational strength by expanding and diversifying its revenue sources.

title: Collaborating to Protect and Restore the Great Lakes
geographic_focus: Pennsylvania, Ohio, New York, Wisconsin, Indiana, Illinois, Minnesota, Michigan
description: The National Wildlife Federation’s Great Lakes Regional Center is a leader in engaging partners to work toward the protection and restoration of the Great Lakes. The grantee leverages policy, legal, communications, education and scientific expertise to support sound policies and leads several coalitions representing conservation, business, tribal and urban constituencies. With previous Mott Foundation support, the grantee has advanced protection and restoration of the Great Lakes on issues ranging from invasive species to emerging contaminants to water affordability. With renewed support, the National Wildlife Federation, through continued coalition building, will deepen its work to protect people and wildlife from threats to the Great Lakes posed by climate change, water pollution, invasive species, dangerous chemicals and resource extraction.

title: Entrepreneurship Community of Practice
description: Community Initiatives is a dedicated fiscal sponsor whose sole purpose is to provide best-in-class infrastructure for nonprofit leaders. For 25 years, the grantee has supported nonprofits in their efforts to achieve results with their endeavors. This grant will allow Community Initiatives to support the Entrepreneurship Funders Network in their effort to promote youth entrepreneurship among donors and build a network of funders to support the field.

title: Afterschool Youth Entrepreneurship Initiative
description: This grant to EmBe will enable the South Dakota Afterschool Network to: 1) equip out-of-school time providers with entrepreneurship training curricula and tools; 2) partner with key stakeholders to host a statewide youth entrepreneurship pitch event; 3) engage Native Youth and Communities with entrepreneurship initiatives; 4) collect and share data with out-of-school time field and entrepreneurship network partners; and 5) promote awareness and support for youth entrepreneurship in out-of-school time.

title: Afterschool Youth Entrepreneurship Initiative
description: This grant to Center of Southwest Culture will enable the New Mexico Out-of-School Time Networkto: 1) expand opportunities for young people to learn about and experience entrepreneurship in existing afterschool, STEM and summer learning programs; 2) connect with local, regional and state entrepreneurship organizations to help integrate entrepreneurship into afterschool and summer learning programs; and 3) partner with organizations such as chambers of commerce, businesses, career technical education and higher education to expand successful entrepreneurship models in communities of high need.

title: Afterschool Youth Entrepreneurship Initiative
description: This grant will allow the Children’s Forum to assist the Florida Afterschool Network in their effort to increase the quality and sustainability of afterschool programs across the state. The grantee will work to: 1) continue to expand opportunities for youth to learn about and experience entrepreneurship in afterschool and summer learning programs; 2) strengthen entrepreneurial ecosystems; and 3) connect and align ecosystem partners to expand learning opportunities and create pathways to entrepreneurship.

title: Accelerating Energy Transition in the Amazon
description: The Regulatory Assistance Project is an independent, nonpartisan and nongovernmental organization dedicated to accelerating the transition to a clean, reliable and efficient energy future. With previous Mott Foundation support, the grantee assessed and developed strategies for accelerating energy decarbonization, self-reliance and resilience in Brazil’s remote and isolated Amazon communities, resulting in a “roadmap” for a fast and affordable transition to clean energy. With renewed Mott Foundation support, the Regulatory Assistance Project will seek to implement the roadmap with analysis and recommendations to reform relevant programs and regulations.

title: Afterschool College and Career Readiness Initiative
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant to Vermont Afterschool will enable the grantee to increase the availability and expansion of college and career exploration, financial literacy or college affordability planning by enhancing quality afterschool and summer learning opportunities for underserved youth. This project will support the network to: 1) expand partnerships to increase integration of college and career readiness and financial wellness supports into Vermont’s universal afterschool and summer learning initiatives; 2) create workforce development pathways for older youth in afterschool and summer learning programs; and 3) develop resources and professional development for afterschool educators around college and career readiness and financial wellness to support youth. The grantee will share promising practices and resources with the 50 State Afterschool Network and Mizzen by Mott to enhance college and career readiness initiatives in afterschool programs nationally. This grant also will support Vermont Afterschool’s efforts to build upon opportunities that emerge within their state to leverage additional college and career readiness resources and partnerships for afterschool and summer learning programs.

title: Afterschool College and Career Readiness Initiative
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant to Wyoming Community Foundation will enable the Wyoming Statewide Afterschool Network to increase the availability and expansion of college and career exploration, financial literacy or college affordability planning by enhancing quality afterschool and summer learning opportunities for underserved youth. This project will support the network to: 1) create workforce development and career pathways for older youth through afterschool and summer learning programs; 2) develop tools and resources for afterschool educators around college and career readiness and financial literacy to support youth; and 3) expand partnerships to increase integration of college and career readiness and financial wellness supports in rural and underserved communities. The grantee will share promising practices and resources with the 50 State Afterschool Network and Mizzen by Mott to enhance college and career readiness initiatives in afterschool programs nationally.

title: Afterschool College and Career Readiness Initiative
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant to the Arkansas State University System Foundation will enable the Arkansas Statewide Afterschool Network to increase the availability and expansion of college and career exploration, financial literacy or college affordability planning by enhancing quality afterschool and summer learning opportunities for underserved youth. This project will support the network to: 1) increase implementation of high quality college and career readiness program strategies in afterschool and summer learning settings; 2) expand accessibility of financial literacy tools and resources for afterschool educators around college and career readiness to support youth and families; and 3) deepen key partnerships to increase integration and funding to support college and career readiness initiatives for afterschool and summer learning programs. The grantee will share promising practices and resources with the 50 State Afterschool Network and Mizzen by Mott to enhance college and career readiness initiatives in afterschool programs nationally.

title: Afterschool College and Career Readiness Initiative
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant to Central Susquehanna Intermediate Unit will enable the Pennsylvania Statewide Afterschool Network to increase the availability and expansion of college and career exploration, financial literacy or college affordability planning by enhancing quality afterschool and summer learning opportunities for underserved youth. This project will support the state network to: 1) create workforce development and career pathways for youth through STEM career exploration; 2) develop financial literacy tools and resources for afterschool educators around college and career readiness to support youth; and 3) expand partnerships to increase integration of college and career readiness and STEM career exploration through afterschool programs. The grantee will share promising practices and resources with the 50 State Afterschool Network and Mizzen by Mott to enhance college and career readiness initiatives in afterschool programs nationally.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Western Cape, Province of the, Eastern Cape, Province of
description: The project goal is to address systemic injustices faced by peri-urban and rural communities in South Africa. To this end, the Support Centre for Land Change will continue to implement activities within its three areas of focus. These areas are the Extended Farm Worker Program, the Land Access and Land Use Program and the Environmental Justice Program. Working with advice offices, these programs seek to address systemic injustices faced by poor and marginalized people in peri-urban and rural communities. The grantee was established in 1987 to fight against forced removals in South Africa. The Support Centre for Land Change has since evolved as one of the leading organizations in the Western and Eastern Cape provinces of South Africa.

title: Increasing the Impact of Land Conservation on Great Lakes Water Quality
geographic_focus: Wisconsin, Ohio, Minnesota, Illinois, Indiana, New York, Pennsylvania, Michigan
description: The Land Trust Alliance is a national organization that provides technical support, training, capacity building and other assistance to support land conservation across the country. Seventy-five of their member land trusts work in the Great Lakes Basin, protecting land and water quality in the region. With previous Mott Foundation support, the grantee provided services that strengthened land and water conservation, helped build effective networks of land trust practitioners and increased support of local projects. With renewed support, the Land Trust Alliance will be able to continue to address the needs of land trusts, in the face of climate change, to advance conservation goals and better protect and safeguard water quality in the Great Lakes region.

title: VISTA Project
description: This grant will allow the Afterschool Alliance to continue deploying AmeriCorps Volunteers in Service to America members as a critical asset to the growth and sustainability of statewide afterschool networks and their partners. Dedicated to the efforts of improving the afterschool networks and programs for underserved communities and families, Alliance VISTAs have been instrumental in expanding quality programming for young people. This grant will support up to 25 VISTAs in networks to address: 1) combating childhood hunger and nutrition through adoption of meals programs; 2) introducing and expanding quality STEM learning; 3) increasing access to high quality educational programming for young people of color; 4) supporting afterschool programs and staff in response to the substance misuse crisis; and 5) strengthening academic supports for student recovery.

title: Accelerating Innovations in Access to Justice through Research
description: The project goal is to research and document best practices on access to justice innovations in communities at the grassroots of Africa. To this end, Barefoot Law will continue using its participatory research methodology to document justice innovations that work for poor and marginalized communities across Africa. The focus of this grant will be to deepen its work in Kenya and Malawi, while undertaking baseline research in Zambia. Past support has allowed the grantee to undertake baseline research in Kenya, Uganda and Malawi. The findings of this research were published in a report and discussed at various forums, including the annual Legal Aid Innovations Conference organized by the grantee. Barefoot Law was founded in 2013 in Uganda, with the purpose of empowering people to develop legal solutions for their justice needs.

title: Strengthening BNDES Accountability
description: Conectas is a Brazilian nongovernmental agency, founded in 2001, working on strengthening social and environmental governance and accountability of development finance institutions. During the previous grant period, the grantee helped strengthen transparency and social environmental governance at the Brazilian Development Bank and New Development Bank, and monitored the implementation of the first New Development Bank financed energy project in Brazil. With this grant increase, The grantee will develop activities related to the Inter-American Development Bank and the implementation of the Leticia Pact and also will deepen knowledge of Chinese investments in the region.

title: Advice Office Support Project
grantee: Association of University Legal Aid Institutions Trust
description: The project goal is to increase access to justice for poor and marginalized people in South Africa. To this end, the Association of University Legal Aid Institutions Trust will continue to implement its cluster model program to provide financial, accompaniment and backup legal support to community advice offices in selected provinces in South Africa. It will also continue to build capacity of community paralegals and assist them with outreach activities. Past support has allowed the grantee to use its network to provide frontline justice services to more than 78,000 people. The Association of University Legal Aid Institutions Trust was established in 1998 and plays an important role in providing resources and backup legal services to advice offices in South Africa.

title: Mobile Student and Family Resource Center
description: The Genesee Intermediate School District Mobile Student and Family Resource Center, which includes the Mobile Education Lab, is a resource and learning center utilized by Genesee County school districts to reach students and families in community locations. This outreach opportunity is a mobile, flexible multi-use venue that increases access for Genesee County families to important educational and community supports, services and resources.

title: General Purposes
description: The Environmental Grantmakers Association receives general purposes support to implement its mission to promote just philanthropy, supporting people and the planet. During the previous grant period, the grantee undertook a range of activities including: 1) convening annual fall retreats for its more than 200 member organizations; 2) co-sponsoring dozens of educational webinars; and 3) releasing its first report on racial equity in environmental philanthropy. With continued support from the Mott Foundation and its other members, the Environmental Grantmakers Association will continue to provide important forums for grantmakers to network and discuss common goals with an overarching commitment to racial equity as a driver of its work.

title: Books Before Boxing Afterschool Program
description: Books Before Boxing — an out-of-school time program operated by Downtown Boxing Gym near downtown Detroit — provides college and career counseling, one-on-one academic support and mentoring, health and wellness education and a diverse range of enrichment activities to students ages 8 to 18. Mott Foundation funding will enable the grantee to expand programming to more students by increasing academic staff and operational inputs including food, transportation services and supplies. Downtown Boxing Gym was created in 2007 to prepare students for success in both postsecondary education and the workforce.

title: Linking Children's Savings Accounts to College Access and Success Strategies
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This renewal grant will enable the National College Attainment Network to promote children’s savings accounts among its members and within the college attainment community more generally. Specific activities include strategic communications, meetings, conferences and educational outreach. These efforts will help build the case and grow demand for children’s savings account strategies as part of comprehensive college access and success initiatives. Based in Washington, D.C., the grantee’s mission is to build, strengthen and empower communities committed to college access and success so that all students — especially those underrepresented in postsecondary education — can achieve their educational dreams.

title: Expanding CSAs for Educational Success and Lifelong Asset Building
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant provides continuing support for Washington University’s research, communications, policy development and technical assistance efforts aimed at advancing children’s savings account strategies at the state and national levels. In the short term, the grantee’s goal is to expand opportunities for all families to save for their children’s education, and in doing so, increase postsecondary education aspirations, access and completion rates, particularly among low-to moderate-income students. Long term, Washington University views children’s savings accounts as the initial phase of a broader effort to embed inclusive and lifelong asset-building opportunities into the fabric of domestic social policy in ways that support educational and financial security goals.

title: College Promise Campaign
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant will enable the College Promise Campaign at the Rockefeller Philanthropy Advisors to continue embedding children’s savings accounts into traditional College Promise programs to further expand their impact by incorporating children’s savings accounts into their designs to help students earn their certificates and degrees. In this third phase of work, the grantee will continue to: 1) strengthen the College Promise-Children’s Savings Account Partnership Network to maximize reach and impact; 2) increase the number and quality of children’s savings accounts embedded in local and state College Promise programs; and 3) expand awareness about the holistic impact of children’s savings accounts in the College Promise movement.

title: Re-Envisioning the CSA Field: From Small-Dollar to Large-Dollar CSAs
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: Although many children and families still lack savings accounts, the field’s recent growth has created a platform for advancing the next generation of children’s savings account policy innovations. While research evidence also shows that low- and moderate-income families successfully save in children’s savings accounts, field leaders are exploring innovative strategies for increasing seed deposits and growing overall account balances, especially among low- and moderate-income families. With Mott Foundation support, the University of Michigan will begin building the research and policy case for a shift from small- to large-dollar children’s savings accounts. To accomplish this goal, the grantee will publish research and policy briefs summarizing research findings and laying out policy arguments, prepare op-eds and blogs to help highlight ideas and create a network of stakeholders to help disseminate and promote new ideas.

title: Genesee Youth Entrepreneurship Network
description: The Genesee Intermediate School District provides educational leadership that impacts instruction, learning, student achievement, productivity and efficiency. The organization serves nearly 70,000 students and 8,500 educators across the county. This grant will enable the grantee to continue the development and expansion of the Genesee Youth Entrepreneurship Network. The primary objectives are to expand the number of entrepreneurship programs for youth and increase the number of students who participate in entrepreneurship programs and experiences. The countywide project will help motivate all 21 high schools to engage students in grades 9 to 12 in entrepreneurship.

title: General Purposes
description: This renewal grant will continue general purposes support to the Harlem Children’s Zone, whose mission is to end intergenerational poverty in Central Harlem and become a model for other communities engaged in similar efforts. Created in 2000, the Harlem Children’s Zone annually provides education, health and employment services to over 20,000 children and families living in a 97-block area in Central Harlem. Based on its successes, Harlem Children’s Zone has been the model for three federal initiatives and has leveraged $500 million in federal funding for over 60 communities around the country.

title: Fiscal Solvency and Service Effectiveness Project
description: This renewal grant provides support for Michigan State University’s efforts to document and promote solutions that help America’s older industrial cities address chronic fiscal stress and advance overall fiscal health. During the grant period, the grantee will develop a range of potential scenarios for addressing structural deficits and assess the feasibility of each scenario with a particular focus on legal and political implications. Special focus will be given to how states and municipalities deploy American Rescue Plan and other federal funds allocated during the COVID-19 pandemic. Finally, Mott Foundation funds will also support direct technical assistance to the City of Flint on a limited basis.

title: North Flint Food Market
description: North Flint Reinvestment Corporation is a nonprofit community development corporation focused on battling economic and environmental injustices. Established in 2011 by the Foss Avenue Baptist Church’s leadership, the grantee takes a place-based, holistic approach to revitalizing the severely distressed neighborhood in which it is located. This grant will support the development of the North Flint Food Market to be located on the north side of Flint near the intersection of Pierson and Clio Roads. Food scarcity is a long-standing and well-documented concern for those living in this part of town and many residents have limited transportation options for shopping elsewhere.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purposes support to The Funders Network, formed in 1999, formerly known as the Funders’ Network for Smart Growth and Livable Communities. The grantee is a resource and focal point for foundations, nonprofit organizations and other philanthropic partners who are working to create equitable, just and environmentally conscious communities. The grantee’s mission is to strengthen and expand funding and philanthropic leadership that yield environmentally sustainable, socially equitable and economically prosperous regions and communities. The mission of The Funders Network includes increasing the representation of people of color in philanthropic leadership positions.

title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to support the organizational and programmatic development of People in Need, one of the largest nonprofits in Central and Eastern Europe. Founded in 1992, the grantee: 1) provides relief and development assistance in response to natural disasters and violent conflict; 2) promotes human rights, civic engagement and civil society development; and 3) supports social inclusion and integration for marginalized groups. During the grant period, the grantee will continue to respond to crises arising from war and conflict, natural disasters and the COVID-19 pandemic through its humanitarian relief programs and its support to civil society organizations working on education, human rights and social inclusion. Based in Prague, Czech Republic, this grant increase will enable People in Need to respond to the humanitarian needs arising from the war in Ukraine and support the work of Ukrainian civil society organizations during the crisis.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purposes support to the American Immigration Council as they work to assist immigrants and improve the overall immigration system. The grantee: 1) manages a network of nearly 14,000 lawyers and law students, interpreters and social workers that provide support for immigrants; 2) conducts impact litigation and advocacy; 3) researches and analyzes immigration policy; and 4) collaborates with civic and business leaders to develop plans that improve the social and economic wellbeing of immigrants. Founded in 1987, the American Immigration Council focuses on working toward a more fair and just immigration system that opens its doors to those in need of protection and harnesses the skills that immigrants bring.

title: Strengthening the Ukrainian Community Foundation Field
description: The project goal is to support Ukrainian community foundations as they respond to critical humanitarian needs that have arisen as a result of Russia’s war on Ukraine. Established in 1999, Ednannia is a recognized indigenous grantmaker, well regarded for its rigorous, transparent, responsive and effective processes to support community-level, grassroots organizations throughout Ukraine. The grantee has supported community foundation development in Ukraine since 2009 through technical assistance, information, education and regranting. The grantee will provide grants to up to 18 Ukrainian community foundations in order to ensure that they can effectively respond to the needs of their communities, internally displaced persons, donors and volunteers. They will also support local authorities in establishing shelters for the displaced, coordinate logistics of humanitarian support deliveries and collect funds for their communities. In addition to managing the regranting process, Ednannia will continue to provide informational and organizational development support to the community foundations.

title: Community Foundation Development Fund
grantee: Academy for the Development of Philanthropy in Poland
description: The program goal is to strengthen the capacity of community foundations in Europe to contribute to the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. To this end, the Academy for the Development of Philanthropy in Poland will provide tailor-made grantmaking and technical assistance programs to community foundations in Europe to stimulate innovation in identifying and implementing local responses to global challenges. The grantee will develop a series of learning materials to support community foundations in their work on the global goals. Additionally, this grant increase will allow the grantee to help European community foundations address the current pressing challenges related to Ukrainian refugees in Europe following Russia’s war on Ukraine. To this end, the grantee will provide small grants to community foundations in European host countries for a wide range of refugee-related activities, including purchase and distribution of humanitarian aid, volunteer recruitment and training, and integration and adaptation services for people arriving from Ukraine.

title: European Programme for Integration and Migration
description: The European Programme for Integration and Migration is a donor collaborative hosted by the Network of European Foundations for Innovative Cooperation. Established in 2005, this program strengthens the role played by civil society organizations in advocating for constructive approaches to migration in Europe.This is done through grantmaking, capacity development and networking activities addressing a range of issues, including: 1) asylum seekers; 2) undocumented migrants; and 3) equality, integration, and social inclusion of vulnerable migrants. Between 2005 and 2020, this program has: 1) involved 36 European foundations in collaborative programming and grantmaking; 2) leveraged funding from these foundations; 3) provided more than 20 million Euros to over 300 civil society organizations; and 4) organized more than 70 pan-European exchange, training and networking events involving over 3,500 participants. Based in Brussels, the Network of European Foundations for Innovative Cooperation strengthens cooperation among foundations in Europe. This grant increase will contribute to a special fund assisting refugees in Europe following Russia’s war on Ukraine.

title: TAP Network
description: The program goal is to support organized civil society participation to increase access to justice globally. The Transparency, Accountability and Participation Network, a project of the Proteus Fund, will mobilize its membership of over 270 civil society organizations for coordinated action around implementation of Sustainable Development Goal 16, with its focus on peaceful, just and inclusive societies. During the grant period, work will focus on: 1) strengthening civil society influence in accountability processes; 2) building civil society capacity to evaluate Goal 16 implementation; and 3) improving data collection and monitoring of national government commitments to Goal 16. In 2020-21, the grantee produced a series of critical resources for civil society actors working to support Goal 16. These resources equipped network members to better track mechanisms and measures in place which underpin Goal 16 implementation. The grantee also hosted a series of events linked to United Nations review meetings, bringing civil society perspectives to these discussions. This increase will support increased engagement and participation of African civil society actors in United Nations monitoring and accountability processes and related events. Founded in 1994, the Proteus Fund convenes and facilitates donor collaboratives that strategically focus philanthropic resources toward the realization of a just, equitable and democratic world.

title: Monitoring Infrastructure Investments in Argentina
location: Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires, Argentina
description: The Fundacion Ambiente y Recursos Naturales is an Argentina-based nongovernmental organization that has promoted sustainable finance and development through policy, law and civic engagement for almost 40 years. Over the previous grant period, the grantee made progress in monitoring and analyzing the factors and financial actors shaping energy development and project selection in Argentina. In the current grant, the grantee and partners will continue monitoring development projects in the country funded by international financial institutions, focusing on infrastructure and energy projects. The goal is to strengthen the socio-environmental standards governing such projects.

title: Genesee County Youth Career Academy
description: This grant will provide continued support to Peckham, Inc. for its Youth Career Academy-Genesee and Mentor.Flint programs. The grantee’s programs help to reduce recidivism, improve social functioning and job skills training, and provide mentoring for at-risk, court-involved youth ages 15-18. The grant will also support the grantee in serving middle school students ages 10-14 in partnership with the Genesee County 7th Judicial Circuit Court and Mt. Morris Consolidated Schools.

title: General Purposes
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Flint Institute of Music, located on the Flint Cultural Center campus, was established in 1917. Today it reaches more than 250,000 people during a typical year through lessons, classes, outreach programs, performances and concerts. Flint Institute of Music is home to the Flint School of Performing Arts, Flint Symphony Orchestra and Flint Repertory Theatre and in 2021 began operating the Whiting Auditorium and Capitol Theatre. Collectively, the venues offer a variety of performing arts shows and events, including concerts and community programs. This grant will provide general purposes support for the Flint Institute of Music.

title: What's Up Downtown Capacity Building
description: This renewal grant will provide support for the Greater Flint Arts Council to fund What’s Up Downtown, a placemaking project focused on programming in public spaces. The grantee will utilize the funds to support a full-time director for the project, and leverage additional resources to coordinate opportunities for residents and visitors to enjoy and participate in family-friendly activities in downtown Flint.

title: Home Ownership Improvement Loan/Grant Pool
description: This renewal grant will provide funds that will enable Genesee County Habitat for Humanity to continue its Home Ownership Improvement Loan/Grant program, known now as the Critical Home Repair Program. This multifaceted program enables city of Flint residents who either cannot afford or do not qualify for other home improvement lending programs to address vital home repair needs. Needs addressed by the program include façade improvements, structural repairs, abatement services, accessibility modifications and any other health, safety or code related issues. Programs like the Home Repair Program help to strengthen neighborhoods and improve the quality of life for Flint families.

title: Neighborhood and Community Planning
description: This grant supports the Genesee County Land Bank Authority’s planning and neighborhood revitalization activities. The grantee develops and operates a nationally renowned program to reclaim vacant and abandoned property and restore it to productive use. This function is overseen by a professional planning and development team that attracts resources and plans, coordinates and implements neighborhood interventions using a variety of tools and strategies. The grantee’s activities simultaneously enhance the quality of neighborhoods in Flint and promotes citizen stewardship by engaging neighborhood groups in planning the disposition and use of vacant structures, as well as maintaining vacant lots.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support the programming and administrative needs of the Latinx Technology and Community Center. The community center provides a variety of cultural and education programs for youth and adults including English as a Second Language and Spanish as a Second Language classes, tutoring and youth programs. The physical presence of the Latinx Technology and Community Center on Flint’s eastside has established the community center as a trusted resource for members of the Latinx community who have educational or resource needs. The Latinx Technology and Community Center works with individuals and families to meet their needs internally or through a strong referral network of organizations including health and human service agencies.

title: Flint and Genesee County Community Development Project
description: Local Initiatives Support Corporation provides grants, loans and technical assistance to community development organizations. As a part of its catalyzing opportunity strategy, the grantee will utilize a comprehensive set of tools to support increasing incomes, building equity and growing wealth in the local community.

title: Zillion Solutions Program Expansion
description: This grant renewal will support the continuation and refinement of the Zillion Solutions program at University of Michigan-Flint. Launched in 2017, Zillion Solutions is an annual idea competition created to increase student interest in entrepreneurship, innovation and/or problem solving. The program is designed to generate participation across all academic units on campus, including dual-enrolled high school students. The goal of the program is to help build a culture of entrepreneurship and innovation throughout the university.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Healthy Flint Research Coordinating Center, Inc.
description: This grant will support the Healthy Flint Research Coordinating Center, which was formed in 2016, to better maximize health benefits from research conducted locally. With this grant, the grantee will further develop programs to coordinate research and prevent fragmented and duplicated work across universities and hospitals. In addition, the Healthy Flint Research Coordinating Center will increase resident input and ensure ethical community involvement throughout the research process.

title: Flint Cultural Center Academy High School
description: With this grant, the Flint Cultural Center Corporation will begin the design and planning phase for a Flint Cultural Center Academy high school. The new school will provide ongoing educational opportunities for the students who attend the Flint Cultural Center Academy K-8 school.

title: Blueline Donuts Build Out
description: This grant to Carriage Town Ministries will allow the grantee to purchase the interior furnishings and equipment needed to open Blueline Donuts, a low-barrier transitional employment program with real customers, real world expectations of its employees and real opportunities to transform lives.

title: Mayors Innovation Project - Affordable Water and Infrastructure Technical Assistance
geographic_focus: Wisconsin, Pennsylvania, Minnesota, Illinois, New York, Michigan, Ohio, Indiana
description: The Mayors Innovation Project, centered at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, is a nationwide learning network of engaged mayors and city officials. The team convenes officials in high-quality learning events to address contemporary topics, including drinking water and infrastructure. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has provided technical support to Great Lakes cities on water infrastructure, water affordability and sustainability challenges. Renewed support will enable the University of Wisconsin-Madison to support a network of Great Lakes cities that are prioritizing water affordability and create pathways to help them achieve water infrastructure upgrades.

title: Connecting Community and Family Philanthropy in Latin America
description: The program goal is to support the emergence and strengthening of community foundations in Latin America. Grand Valley State University’s Dorothy A. Johnson Center for Philanthropy proposes to conduct research aimed at trying to understand and explain the engagement of Latin American families in place-based philanthropy and especially in community foundations. The research methodology will consist of a literature review and a field scan, an estimated 40 in-depth qualitative interviews and the development of mini-case studies. Other deliverables will include a primary report, a recommendation and best practices summary and dissemination events and dialogues. This project will focus on Mexico, as it is seen as the first phase of a broader, multiyear research effort to cover several countries in Latin America. Established in 1992, the Dorothy A. Johnson Center for Philanthropy is an academic center within the College of Community and Public Service at Grand Valley State University.

title: Connecting Community and Family Philanthropy in Latin America
description: The project goal is to support the emergence and strengthening of community foundations in Latin America. During the first phase of this research project, Grand Valley State University’s Dorothy A. Johnson Center for Philanthropy developed and applied a rigorous methodology for exploring the relationship between family philanthropists and community foundations in Mexico. The resulting conclusions and recommendations will be shared with relevant stakeholders in the fall of 2024. The goal of the project’s second phase is to develop a methodology that will be widely applicable across national contexts in Latin America. Deliverables will include self-assessment methods, virtual and in-person dissemination events and support for implementation locally. Established in 1992, the Dorothy A. Johnson Center for Philanthropy is an academic center within the College of Community and Public Service at Grand Valley State University.

title: Care of Civic Space
grantee: Centro Mexicano para la Filantropia, A.C.
description: The program goal is to promote a more favorable enabling environment for Mexican civil society. In 2021, a group of 20 organizations and networks formed Care of Civic Space, a coalition that aims to safeguard and promote the right of citizens to participate through organized civil society on matters of public interest. Centro Mexicano para la Filantropia, A.C. will serve as a platform to support and expand this coalition. Activities will include mapping of existing efforts to support civil society, regular national and regional convenings, the creation of 10 regional “promoter nuclei,” public awareness-raising of the role and value of civil society in Mexico and promotion of the right of civil society to participate in public interest matters. Founded in 1988, Centro Mexicano para la Filantropia, A.C. promotes the philanthropic and social responsible participation of Mexican citizens, organizations and companies to achieve a more equitable and prosperous society.

title: Manifest Your Citizenship
grantee: Centro Mexicano para la Filantropia, A.C.
description: The program goal is to promote a more favorable enabling environment for Mexican civil society. Started in 2021, a coalition of Mexican organizations and networks was created to safeguard and promote the right of citizens to participate through organized civil society on matters of public interest. In the pervious grant period, the program solidified its structure and programs, updated its name and grew to 30 organizations, reaching approximately 2,500 civil society organizations across Mexico. Centro Mexicano para la Filantropia, A.C. will continue to serve as a platform to support and expand this coalition. In the next grant period, activities will include: 1) mapping of existing efforts to support civil society; 2) regular national and regional convenings; 3) public awareness-raising of the role and value of civil society in Mexico; 4) and promotion of civil society’s right to participate in public interest matters. Founded in 1988, Centro Mexicano para la Filantropia, A.C. promotes the philanthropic and socially responsible participation of Mexican citizens, organizations and companies to achieve a more equitable and prosperous society.

title: Early Childhood Capacity Building
description: This grant will provide funding to the Community Foundation of Greater Flint to support the expansion of early childhood education in Flint. Expanding access to high-quality early childhood education has always been important for the city, but became even more important following the water crisis. The grantee employs an executive director to manage the Flint Early Childhood Collaborative, a project that aims to increase access to, and improve the quality of, early childhood education in Flint through strategic planning, research, advocacy and participation in the Educare Learning Network.

title: Strengthening the Legal Development Network's Member Organizations
description: The program goal is to increase community-based access to justice for the Ukrainian public. The Legal Development Network will work to strengthen and expand the current network of 30 community legal centers in Ukraine. Continuing attention will be given to equipping centers with skills and capacity to work with local authorities in providing access to justice. The grantee will also seek to integrate the network into international partnerships to further build capabilities of members. In 2019-2021, the grantee conducted 11 legal needs surveys in different regions of Ukraine, resulting in six access to justice programs in participating communities. Despite the COVID-19 pandemic, network members nearly doubled the number of clients served in 2020, compared to the previous year. Working with Ukrainian and international partners, the grantee also initiated widespread discussion on “people-centered justice” and how this can be achieved in Ukraine. This increase will allow the grantee to increase provision of legal services and help coordinate other assistance for people displaced following Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. Formally registered in 2015 and with its secretariat in Kyiv, the Legal Development Network has member organizations in 15 regions of Ukraine.

title: Strengthening Community Paralegals in Ukraine
description: The Ukrainian Legal Aid Foundation will work closely with the coordinating center for Legal Aid of the Ministry of Justice to enhance skills and training of paralegals to increase assistance to Ukrainians experiencing consequences of Russia’s invasion of their country. Paralegals will help coordinate humanitarian and legal assistance in conjunction with relevant government agencies and other civil society partners.

title: General Purposes
description: In the face of the ongoing war in Ukraine, the Ukrainian Helsinki Human Rights Union will use additional funds for several purposes. These include: securing a level of protection to its employees, including life-saving relocation needs; expanding its network of public reception offices network to additional regions of Ukraine in order to increase citizens’ access to legal assistance; monitoring and documenting brutal human rights abuses and war crimes committed by Russia’s occupation forces in order to hold criminals accountable domestically and internationally; strengthening capacity of legal practitioners on documentation; and knowledge of international humanitarian law and applicable human rights law.

title: Summer Community Development Internships
description: This grant provides support to Michigan State University for the Summer Community Development Internships program, which seeks to develop and enhance community assets through meaningful internship experiences. This is accomplished through an immersive 10-week summer internship program open to both Michigan State University undergraduate and graduate students. This summer’s program centers around five projects chosen from 10 project proposals submitted by local community organizations. The focus areas include equitable grantmaking, environmental justice and other community engagement projects.

title: Double Up Food Bucks Project
description: This grant will provide support to the Fair Food Network’s Double Up Food Bucks project in Flint. The project provides incentives for supplemental nutrition assistance program recipients to purchase fresh fruits and vegetables and dairy products at the Flint Farmers’ Market and grocery stores in Flint. Good nutrition, especially foods high in iron, calcium and vitamin C, can help mitigate the impact of lead exposure to Flint children and adults. Started at five farmers markets, Double Up Food Bucks is now implemented at 234 sites in Michigan and is a national model for healthy food incentives across 29 states.

title: Genesee Early College
description: Genesee Early College is an innovative educational program administered by the Genesee Intermediate School District in collaboration with the University of Michigan-Flint. The focus of the initiative is to prepare high school students for academic and professional careers, while offering a unique learning experience that is fully integrated on the campus of a four-year university. Students can earn up to 60 transferable college credits, as well as a high school diploma and scholarship funds for higher education.

title: Technical Assistance for Improved Teaching and Learning
description: This renewal grant will allow Michigan State University to continue providing support to Flint Community Schools with technical assistance aimed at increasing district capacity, improving school culture, increasing operational efficiency and improving student academic outcomes. To achieve these goals, technical assistance will be focused on supporting district leaders in developing and implementing a multi-phase plan for restructuring the learning environments for Flint Community School scholars. The grantee will support the district’s implementation of four primary components of its strategic plan: 1) scholar focus; 2) teaching and instruction; 3) climate and culture; and 4) data knowledge and application while building the capacity of leaders to implement the district’s planned reduction in school facilities.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint
description: This renewal grant provides general purposes support to the Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint. The grantee focuses on education, creativity, physical activity, health and family support services while offering year-round programming to young people between the ages of 7 and 17 in the Flint area. The grantee operates two sites, one located on the east side and the other on the south side of the city. Programs such as this have been instrumental in mitigating the negative effects of challenges such as the water crisis, learning loss resulting from the COVID-19 pandemic and the impact of poverty. By providing students with highly engaging educational and enrichment opportunities in a safe and supportive environment, the Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint continues to stay true to its mission to enable young people in the Flint area to reach their full potential.

title: School and Community Programming
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Flint Cultural Center Corporation provides opportunities for underserved youth and residents of all ages in the city of Flint and Genesee County to participate in educational and community engagement activities provided by the Flint Cultural Center campus institutions. The Flint Cultural Center Corporation includes Sloan Museum of Discovery, Longway Planetarium, Flint Institute of Arts and Flint Institute of Music (which includes The Whiting and Capitol Theatre).

title: General Purposes
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Flint Cultural Center Corporation manages and maintains the 38-acre Flint Cultural Center campus — which encompasses: 1) the Flint Cultural Center Academy; 2) Flint Institute of Arts; 3) Flint Institute of Music; 4) the Whiting; 5) Capitol Theatre; 6) Flint Public Library; and 7) Flint Institute of Science and History (Sloan Museum of Discovery and Longway Planetarium). The campus contributes positively to the quality of life in Flint through educational and cultural enrichment opportunities and has a significant economic impact through earned revenue and employment. Students and adults of all ability levels participate in or attend a variety of cultural, educational and instructional programs and activities across the campus. This grant will provide general purposes support to the Flint Cultural Center Corporation for campus improvements, grounds and maintenance, marketing and campus security.

title: General Purposes

description: The Flint Cultural Center Corporation manages and maintains the 38-acre Flint Cultural Center campus which encompasses the: 1) Flint Cultural Center Academy; 2) Flint Institute of Arts; 3) Flint Institute of Music; 4) Whiting; 5) Capitol Theatre; 6) Gloria Coles Flint Public Library; and 7) Flint Institute of Science and History (Sloan Museum of Discovery and Longway Planetarium). The campus contributes positively to the quality of life in Flint through educational and cultural enrichment opportunities and has a significant economic impact through earned revenue and employment. Students and adults of all ability levels participate in or attend a variety of cultural, educational, and instructional programs and activities across the campus. This grant will provide general purposes support to the Flint Cultural Center Corporation for campus improvements, grounds and maintenance, marketing and campus security.

title: General Purposes
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Flint Institute of Arts — located on the Flint Cultural Center campus — features museum galleries, a media arts space, an art school, studio space and public areas that engage visitors and attract new audiences from across the region. Students and adults visit the galleries, participate in educational programs, take art classes or attend events held at the institute. This grant will provide general purposes support to enable the grantee to present new exhibits that: 1) inspire and stimulate visitors; 2) provide educational programming to area students; 3) offer instruction in various art mediums to people of all ages; 4) provide community events and programming; and 5) maintain its facilities.

title: Music Around Town
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Music Around Town series, formerly known as Music in the Parks, is a broad community partnership led by the Flint Institute of Music. This program offers musical performances in public places around Flint and Genesee County, which are also streamed through social media platforms. The public locations offer residents access to multiple free performances by the musicians from the Flint Symphony Orchestra, Flint School of Performing Arts, Flint Repertory Theatre and other local talent.

initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Music Around Town series, formerly known as Music in the Parks, is a broad community partnership led by the Flint Institute of Music. This program offers musical performances in public places around Flint and Genesee County. The public locations offer residents access to multiple free performances by the musicians from the Flint Symphony Orchestra, Flint School of Performing Arts, Flint Repertory Theatre and other local talent. The series also includes performances at events such as the Flint City Bucks soccer games and Flint Firebirds hockey games.

title: Summer Youth Initiative and TeenQuest
description: This grant provides funding to support the Genesee Area Focus Fund to implement TeenQuest and the Summer Youth Initiative, which provide job training and employment opportunities for Genesee County teens in partnership with area employers. Teens participate first in TeenQuest — a preemployment training program — and are then eligible to apply for employment through the Summer Youth Initiative.

title: Flint Healthcare Employment Opportunities Program
description: This grant to the Greater Flint Health Coalition will support the Flint Healthcare Employment Opportunities program. The goal of the program is to create sustainable employment opportunities and promote career advancement for area residents within the health care sector. Participants receive industry-focused life skills and career readiness training, occupational instruction, case management and supportive services, as well as job development assistance.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Flint Institute of Science and History
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to the Flint Institute of Science and History will support the general purposes of the Sloan Museum of Discovery and Longway Planetarium. The museum facility is around 107,000 square feet with permanent and rotating exhibits as well as educational and community programming. The Sloan Museum of Discovery opened in July 2022 and has seen record-level attendance since that time. The state-of-the-art Longway Planetarium offers multiple shows and programming for all ages, both onsite and virtually. Summer camps, workshops and monthly evening events such as trivia nights are among programs offered through the museum and planetarium.

title: Adult Career Pathway Program
description: This grant will support the Adult Career Pathways program at Mott Community College. The program will leverage many of the college’s existing educational and training programs to help connect unemployed adults, low-income workers, and youth to employment and a career pathway. The goal is to ensure that area residents can enter and advance into higher-wage occupations in high-growth industries. Work experience and support services are integrated into the model, enabling participants to combine school and work and advance in their careers over time.

title: Overture Program and Partnership with Flint Institute of Music
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This renewal grant will provide support to the Sphinx Organization to offer a continuum of music instruction and cultural experiences to underserved students in Flint. The Sphinx Overture program, which introduces students to classical music and violin, serves all Flint public elementary schools as well as community organizations such as the Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint. The program will provide students with free afterschool group violin lessons. Through a partnership with the Flint Institute of Music, students from the program will be eligible for more advanced violin lessons and classes at no cost.

title: Tapology Youth Outreach
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide partial support for Tapology, Inc.’s Youth Outreach programs. Tap dance is an enduring American art form that increases physical activity and enhances cognitive development for participants. The grantee partners with local schools and community centers to introduce area youth to tap dance and offer regular classes for all ability levels. Each year, the grantee’s outreach programming culminates into a 4-day festival that exposes local students to tap dancing’s art and history. Professional artists will continue providing instruction for beginners, as well as more advanced workshops for experienced young dancers.

title: Flint STRIVE Academy Youth Empowerment Program
description: This grant to Specialized Employment Services, Inc. will support the Flint STRIVE Academy Youth Empowerment Program for at-risk youth ages 14 to 18. The grantee provides young people with a summertime employment experience and follow-up support services during the school year. Through attitudinal training, skill enhancement, mentoring and tutoring, the goal of this project is to encourage youth to complete high school and to help with making informed career decisions.

title: Event Policing and Public Safety
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide funds to support public safety enforcement and traffic control activities for festivals and events primarily in the downtown Flint area. Free and low-cost events are very important to the vitality of the city and the people who live here. Public safety is an essential component of the success of the festivals that take place in Flint and attract thousands of exhibitors and participants. The city of Flint is not in a financial position to provide the necessary additional police services due to a decline in municipal revenues.

title: Flint STRIVE Replication Program
description: The Flint STRIVE Replication Program, a project of Specialized Employment Services, Inc., provides employment training, job placement and support services for hard-to-serve Flint area residents. A replication of the East Harlem Employment Service’s workforce training program — STRIVE New York —, Flint STRIVE prepares participants for the workforce through a three-week, intensive workshop emphasizing the attitudinal prerequisites for successful employment.

title: Trauma Informed Campus Design
description: This grant to Whaley Children’s Center will provide funds to renovate and furnish facilities on its campus. The grantee is a residential facility that serves children from age five to 17 who have been abused and/or neglected. The trauma that these children experience impacts both short- and long-term development and behaviors. Recent developments in the field of trauma-informed care suggest that the physical environment has a significant impact on children who have experienced trauma. Whaley Children’s Center is undergoing a broad effort to implement trauma-informed design practices across its campus. This project will help to transform the grantee’s family game room into a space that is welcoming, demonstrates a safe environment and provides some degree of privacy for family visits.

title: Engaging Youth in Service
description: This grant will provide continued support to Youth Service America as it drives its National Days of Service program to reach more young people — focusing on youth of color and underserved youth — with the opportunity to serve their community. Through the program, Youth Service America funds, trains and provides additional capacity building for K-12 schools, afterschool programs, nonprofits and community organizations as it guides young people in designing and leading service projects. In addition to the National Days of Service campaign, this grant supports bringing service to afterschool programs through regranting and network capacity building.

title: Tackling Finance of Gas Expansion in South America
description: Development banks, including the Brazilian Development Bank, are promoting increased use of oil and gas and the expansion of gas into the electrical sector. Given the role fossil fuels play in accelerating climate change, these development strategies are problematic. 350.org is a global environmental organization based in the United States and has developed a strong team in South America since it was founded in 2008. This project grant will support the grantee to engage its grassroots network to address the social and environmental impacts of fossil fuel finance and expansion in South America.

title: Great Lakes Water Resources Project
geographic_focus: Illinois, Wisconsin, Minnesota, New York, Michigan, Pennsylvania, Ohio, Indiana
description: The Great Lakes Environmental Law Center is a nonprofit environmental law organization headquartered in Michigan. The grantee supports local community members on water resource management issues. Previous Mott Foundation support has enabled the grantee to advance legal protections and public engagement related to drinking water quality, affordability and water resources protection in lakes, wetlands and streams. With renewed Mott Foundation support, the Great Lakes Environmental Law Center will continue collaborating with various stakeholders to advance legal protections and policy solutions to key water management issues, including water quality, affordability and the sustainable protection of Michigan’s water resources.

title: Youth Programming and Educator Training
description: This grant will support Youth Entrepreneurs, Inc. d/b/a Empowered. Founded in 1991, the grantee provides educators with entrepreneurship training, curriculum resources and support to provide entrepreneurship education and experiences for low-income youth. Goals for this project include: 1) increasing opportunities for young people to understand and experience entrepreneurship through the provision of technical assistance and partnership to the afterschool field; 2) spreading entrepreneurial mindset programming into states and cities identified by Empowered; and 3) providing professional development and training opportunities for educators promoting entrepreneurship.

title: Innovating Clean Water Financing and Community Engagement in the Great Lakes
description: American Rivers is a national organization whose mission is to protect wild rivers, restore damaged rivers and improve water quality for people and nature, and has long prioritized the importance of the rivers of the Great Lakes region. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, American Rivers has advanced green infrastructure solutions to stormwater pollution through innovative and equitable funding strategies. The grantee has an effective network of local water leaders engaged with local governments in the Great Lakes basin to capitalize on federal infrastructure funding, especially for vulnerable communities. With renewed support, American Rivers will build on their previous work in the region to help ensure the equitable distribution of federal infrastructure funds in Great Lakes states that result in clean water for people and the region’s waterways.

title: Countywide Blight Elimination Project: Leveraging American Rescue Plan Act Funds
description: This grant combined with other funding sources will improve neighborhoods in the city of Flint and Genesee County through the demolition of approximately 2,415 structures and the maintenance of the properties afterward. Flint residents have identified blight elimination and specifically demolition of blighted properties as a citywide priority. The Genesee County Land Bank has a significant track record in demolition, having demolished more than 8,450 blighted structures since 2004 in Flint and Genesee County.

title: Next Generation Industry and Job Creation
description: With this grant, the Flint & Genesee Chamber Foundation and its supported organization, the Flint and Genesee Group, will begin site planning and preparations for locating future industry in the county. The region is a prime location for the manufacturers and jobs of tomorrow because of its location near transportation assets and suppliers, access to freeways and a robust talent pool. The project will lead to economic development strategies and job opportunities in an economically disadvantaged post-industrial community.

title: Enterprising Ventures of Color
description: This grant will provide funding to the Community Foundation of Greater Flint, convener of the Greater Flint Coronavirus Taskforce on Racial Inequities, to support capacity building work for eight Flint-based nonprofit organizations led by people of color. The philanthropic subcommittee of the taskforce recognized the need for a new approach to building capacity among Black-led and Black-serving organizations in the community. The subcommittee identified Enterprising Ventures of Color as a strong provider with experience in increasing capacity and developing resources for organizations. The Community Foundation of Greater Flint will work with Enterprising Ventures of Color to facilitate the final year.

title: Assets Evaluation and Data Collection Project
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: Brandeis University’s Institute for Economic and Racial Equity is a research institute that promotes programs and policies that expand economic opportunity and equity for individuals and families, particularly households of color. Renewed Mott Foundation funding will enable the Institute to support the growth and development of the Children’s Savings Account (CSA) field by coordinating CSA stakeholders, informing policy and applying and leveraging data to accelerate best practices. Significant activities planned for this grant period include: 1) data collection and evaluation; 2) supporting a learning network of grantees; 3) thought leadership; and 4) a summative report of the field’s last decade. The Mott Foundation has supported Brandeis University on asset-building and savings strategies since 2008.

title: Regulation of Nonprofits and Philanthropy
description: The project goal is to support a healthy policy environment for the nonprofit and philanthropy sector. The Regulation of Nonprofits and Philanthropy project at the Urban Institute is a vehicle to develop, promote and disseminate research on the federal-state regulatory framework and its impact on nonprofits. The project also serves as a platform for ongoing dialogue about ways to improve the regulatory framework. The project engages: 1) attorney generals and other state officials; 2) federal regulators; 3) academics; 4) researchers; and 5) nonprofit practitioners. In the past two years, the grantee produced research and analysis on state and federal regulatory issues affecting the charitable sector, hosted a symposium and publicized research papers and briefs. Over the next two years, the grantee will continue to conduct research and distribute the results through publications and presentations, as well as update and expand the Legal Compendium — a unique tool for nonprofit regulatory analysis. The project is implemented by the Center on Nonprofits and Philanthropy at the Urban Institute — a think tank that builds knowledge about the nation’s social and fiscal challenges.

title: Northeast Ohio SDG Learning Cohort
description: The program goal is to encourage community foundations to advance Sustainable Development Goals at the local level. To this end, the Cleveland Foundation will create a learning exchange cohort with other community foundations and local stakeholders in Northeast Ohio on aligning their giving areas with the goals. The grantee will convene stakeholders over 15 months for learning and alignment sessions, publish a teaching case study and/or report around goal alignment efforts, identify common benchmarks and shared measurements to further a regional vision, conduct a 17 Rooms-X exercise and develop a dashboard to capture the Northeast Ohio learning cohort’s Sustainable Development Goals alignment efforts. Founded in 1914, the Cleveland Foundation is the nation’s first community foundation.

title: Community Center Capital Improvements
description: This grant will provide support to the Evergreen Community Development Initiative for renovations and updates to the Flint Development Center, a community center located on the north side of Flint. The community center opened in 2017 having raised $500,000 for the initial renovations to the former Bunche Elementary School building. The current grant will enable the grantee to complete all the remaining interior renovations and upgrade the playgrounds and basketball courts outside.

title: Water Equity in Milwaukee's Diverse Communities
description: Milwaukee Water Commons is a grassroots organization focused on community engagement and organizing around water and climate resilience in the Great Lakes region, with an emphasis on environmental justice. Much of the decision-making and resulting policies around water and climate have not included the communities most impacted. The grantee’s programs and projects are intended to address this need by strengthening community and water leadership, advancing Milwaukee as a water city centered around equity and justice and informing policy through initiatives to build water, climate and racial equity in Milwaukee and the Great Lakes region. This grant will support programs and projects that address water issues in Milwaukee, Wisconsin and the Great Lakes, such as: 1) holding public events to increase awareness of water issues; 2) creating a drinking water initiative and water equity task force; and 3) serving on advisory committees for local, state and national organizations on water.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support the organizational and programmatic development of People in Need, one of the largest nonprofits in Central and Eastern Europe. Founded in 1992, the grantee provides relief and development assistance in response to natural disasters and violent conflict, promotes human rights, civic engagement and civil society development and supports social inclusion and integration for marginalized groups. During the grant period, the grantee will continue to respond to crises arising from war and conflict, natural disasters and the COVID-19 pandemic through its humanitarian relief programs and its support to civil society organizations working on education, human rights and social inclusion. This grant increase will enable the grantee to respond to the humanitarian needs arising from the war in Ukraine and support the work of Ukrainian civil society organizations during the crisis. People in Need is based in Prague, Czech Republic.

title: Harnessing Technology to Reduce Fires in the Amazon
description: The Woodwell Climate Research Center is a premier scientific organization working globally to solve climate change and in Brazil to protect the Amazon rainforest. Partnering with Brazilian research institutions, the grantee is investigating how fire, exacerbated by human activities and a changing climate, is the greatest threat to the stability of ecosystems and social structure in the Amazon. Over the last grant period, the grantee investigated climate-fire dynamics and collected data on smoke exposure in Amazonian communities. With renewed support, the Woodwell Climate Research Center will increase understanding of the links between fire, climate and deforestation and the implications for human health and societal changes. The overall goal is to increase the resilience of forests and communities in the face of growing fire risks.

title: Tribal Science, Training and Communications Project
grantee: Great Lakes Indian Fish and Wildlife Commission
description: The Great Lakes Indian Fish and Wildlife Commission works with tribal governments in Michigan, Wisconsin and Minnesota to protect tribal interests and natural resources of ceded territories in the northern portions of those states. With support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has identified and implemented steps to participate effectively in permitting and environmental reviews, conducted baseline water monitoring, mapped vital wetland habitats and helped implement aspects of the federal Clean Water Act. With this increase, the grantee will expand its monitoring protocol to collect data on water levels and chemistry in the Sand River of the Lake Superior Basin.

title: General Purposes
description: The Ohio Environmental Council is a statewide organization dedicated to making a positive impact on Ohio’s natural resources, its people and its economy. The grantee is going through a leadership transition and has launched a national search for a new executive director. This grant increase will help the Ohio Environmental Council hire a consultant to manage the search process.

title: Development Banks and Sustainable Development
geographic_focus: China, World, South America, Southern Asia, Africa
description: The Global Development Policy Center at Boston University — a prestigious institution of higher learning — has evolved into a major center of policy-oriented research for financial stability, human well-being and environmental sustainability. Its largest component, the Global China Initiative, was established with Mott Foundation support and has become a valuable and trusted source of open-source data on Chinese overseas investment and analysis on its impact. With this grant, Boston University’s Global Development Center will: 1) continue to track China’s overseas aid and investment; 2) shift the composition of such finance towards environmentally sustainable and socially inclusive projects; and 3) help build a new generation of scholars and researchers on these issues.

title: Engaging Youth in Service
description: This grant will provide support to Youth Service America as it drives its National Days of Service program to reach more young people — focusing on youth of color and underserved youth — with the opportunity to serve their community. Through the program, the grantee funds, trains and provides additional capacity building for K-12 schools, afterschool programs, nonprofits and community organizations as it guides young people in designing and leading service projects. In addition to the National Days of Service campaign, this grant will build service-learning expertise in afterschool programs through professional development and youth-led project support.

title: Documenting War Crimes in Ukraine
description: The program goal is to improve reporting on, and documenting of, potential war crimes arising in Ukraine following Russia’s invasion in February 2022. To this end, the Global Investigative Journalism Network will update and expand its toolkit of issue and practice guides, tip sheets and trainings that assist journalists and correspondents to understand both the news value and the forensic needs of documenting evidence of a war crime. The toolkit will be translated into Ukrainian and Russian initially and will be distributed throughout the grantee’s network. This effort will be boosted by engagement of a Ukrainian-speaking editor able to respond quickly to requests from Ukrainian journalists for resources to document potential crimes. Founded in 2003, the Global Investigative Journalism Network has grown to include 227 member groups in 82 countries and works to link together the world’s most enterprising journalists, giving them the tools, technology and training to uncover abuses of power and lack of accountability.

title: Centre on African Philanthropy and Social Investment
description: The goal of the project is to promote philanthropy in Africa by generating new knowledge and building a cadre of experts, researchers and academics focused on African philanthropy, social investment and related disciplines.
