The Centre on African Philanthropy and Social Investment, a program of the University of the Witwatersrand, works to produce research on philanthropy, train a cadre of philanthropy professionals, and connect academic research and knowledge to the practice. Past support has enabled the Centre to: 1) host convenings; 2) produce research on philanthropy and social investment in Africa; 3) train and graduate doctoral students; and 4) provide short training programs. In addition, the Centre has also launched a podcast series to document experiences in philanthropy and social investment. During this grant period, the grantee will continue to train academics in philanthropy, host public lecturers and other learning events, produce research and publications to expand knowledge on philanthropy in the continent as well as introduce new training programs in response to the changing landscape. In addition, the Centre on African Philanthropy and Social Investment will continue to host podcasts to document the experiences of professionals in philanthropy and social investment and discuss research outcomes to make them more accessible.

title: Uniting Great Lakes Science, Data and Journalism
description: Circle of Blue is an online magazine highlighting water issues around the world. The grantee’s staff includes experienced and award-winning reporters who cover drinking water, climate impacts and other critical issues threatening the Great Lakes. As a member of the Great Lakes News Collaborative — a partnership across newsrooms and media outlets — the grantee has brought its expertise and content to a variety of stories from water access and insecurity to harmful algal blooms in Lake Erie. With renewed support, the grantee will continue to support and lead the collaborative with in-depth reporting and photojournalism, cultivate the next generation of reporters through internships and heighten public awareness concerning Great Lakes water issues.

title: Helping Cities Finance Water Improvements
description: The Michigan Municipal League Foundation is dedicated to making Michigan’s communities better by innovating programs, connecting ideas and people, serving members with resources and services and inspiring positive change for Michigan communities. With prior Mott Foundation support, the grantee was able to develop MI Water Navigator, a tool to provide resources and technical assistance for cities to access funds for drinking water projects. This tool is now being replicated as a model community-driven technical assistance program in other states and nationally. This grant will enable the Michigan Municipal League Foundation to continue its services to help cities submit final proposals for drinking water and to gain financial resources to implement projects in their communities.

title: STEM Fellowship
description: This grant to the STEM Next Opportunity Fund will support the Afterschool and Summer Learning Fellowship, the Robert Noyce-Ellen Lettvin Fellowship in informal STEM learning and the School Aged and Early Care Fellowship. The fellowships are a public-private partnership initiative geared toward advancing high-quality afterschool, summer learning and informal STEM learning and cross-agency partnerships to support afterschool and summer learning. This initiative will: 1) strengthen collaboration between the U.S. Department of Education and other federal agencies in the areas of afterschool and informal STEM learning; 2) work to advance afterschool and STEM learning in the 21st Century Community Learning Centers program; and 3) work with leading researchers to identify priorities, new tools, strategies and programs that improve afterschool and STEM learning opportunities.

title: Enterprising Ventures of Color
description: This grant will provide funding to the Community Foundation of Greater Flint, convener of the Greater Flint Coronavirus Taskforce on Racial Inequities, to support capacity-building work for eight Flint-based nonprofit organizations led by people of color. The philanthropic subcommittee of the Taskforce recognized the need for a new approach to building capacity among Black-led and Black-serving organizations in the community. The subcommittee identified Enterprising Ventures of Color as a strong provider with experience in increasing capacity and developing resources for organizations. Community Foundation of Greater Flint will work with Enterprising Ventures of Color to facilitate a two-year program that will provide resources to enhance operations at the eight Flint-based nonprofit organizations selected, while simultaneously building individual and organizational capacity within these organizations. The program also will offer activities and roundtable sessions for other nonprofit leaders and funders that aim to increase trust-based philanthropy.

title: Understanding the Impact of Chinese Investment and Engagement in Latin America
description: The Chinese government is currently the largest lender and a major investor and trading partner for many nations in Latin America, providing significant finance for energy and infrastructure projects. China Dialogue reports on the environmental, social and governance dimensions of Chinese investments, pursuing its mission of increasing transparency on the China-Latin America relationship and the associated climate and sustainable development challenges. The grantee’s team of former BBC journalists inform readers globally and regionally, with reporting in English, Spanish and Portuguese. This renewal grant will enable China Dialogue to consolidate and expand its reach and readership as it merges its news outlets into a global platform, Dialogue Earth.

title: Promoting Environmental and Social Standards in the Financial Sector
description: Urgewald is a German-based organization that works to establish strong, binding environmental and social standards for international development finance institutions and build public support for responsible and accountable development finance institutions. To achieve these goals, the grantee undertakes research, education and advocacy efforts with a global network of local communities, nongovernmental organizations and other partners. Over the next grant period, the grantee will monitor the implementation and review of the environmental and social policies of the World Bank Group, Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank and Asian Development Bank. Urgewald will also provide research and coordination support to key civil society networks in Europe and Asia working toward these same goals.

title: Advancing Renewable Energy Access in the Amazon
description: The Brazilian Institute for Consumer Defense is a prominent nongovernmental organization dedicated to: 1) ensuring citizens proper access to essential goods and services; 2) promoting social development; 3) sustainable consumption; and 4) environmental health. Over the previous grant period, the grantee published recommendations to enhance the Light for All federal program, which aims to provide universal access to electricity in remote parts of the country. Over the next grant period, the grantee will focus on facilitating public hearings to advocate for service improvements and regulatory adjustments to address the specific needs of consumers in Amazon regions. Additionally, the Brazilian Institute for Consumer Defense will launch campaigns and raise awareness about the social and economic impacts of renewable energy access for isolated communities in the Brazilian Amazon.

title: Harnessing Technology to Reduce Fires in the Amazon
description: The Amazon Environmental Research Institute, a nonprofit research organization based in Brazil, collaborates with partners to better understand fire dynamics in the Amazon. The grantee is increasing the understanding of the complex interplay between: 1) fire; 2) climate factors such as drought and temperature extremes; 3) deforestation; and 4) human well-being. Over the last grant period, the grantee delivered rapid and reliable knowledge to support fire control initiatives through research and extensive outreach efforts. In this renewal, the Amazon Environmental Research Institute will further unravel how fire regimes catalyze forest ecological and social changes in the Brazilian Amazon. The aim is to facilitate adaptation strategies and enhance the resilience of forests and communities in the rapidly changing landscape.

title: Renewable Loreto
description: The Derecho Ambiente y Recursos Naturales is a Peruvian nongovernmental organization with offices in Lima and Iquitos, the capital of the Peruvian Amazon Department of Loreto. Over the last grant period, the organization has successfully brought off-grid solar energy systems to communities in the Peruvian Amazon, bolstering community resilience and actively contributing to solutions for climate change. With the renewal of this grant, the grantee aims to further its impact by gathering valuable insights, developing detailed recommendations for reform and disseminating them to enhance access to renewable energy by communities throughout the Peruvian Amazon. Additionally, Derecho Ambiente y Recursos Naturales will continue to develop off-grid solar energy systems, focusing on promoting sustainable production practices at the community level.

title: General Purposes
description: The Derecho Ambiente y Recursos Naturales is a Peruvian nongovernmental organization focused on sustainable development and conservation of the Peruvian Amazon basin. During the previous grant period, the grantee: 1) initiated the implementation of a new strategic plan; 2) made significant contributions to strengthening environmental and social policy at the Inter-American Development Bank; 3) monitored projects by other development finance institutions; and 4) helped promote adherence to the Escazu Agreement, which will protect environmental defenders in South America. This renewal grant supports continued implementation of the grantee’s strategic plan, including efforts to strengthen social and environmental safeguards at international finance institutions. Derecho Ambiente y Recursos Naturales will also monitor the expenditure of funds addressing climate change to ensure the rights of Indigenous peoples are protected and Amazonian forests are conserved.

title: Diversity in Journalism
description: Michigan State University’s Knight Center for Environmental Journalism and its affiliated Great Lakes Echo news service teaches and graduates students to be professional environmental reporters. Recognizing the need to diversify the student body and newsrooms focused on Great Lakes reporting, the Center will develop a diversity in journalism program. This grant will support student scholarships for coursework, conferences and internships to provide professional experiences beyond the classroom, also contributing to the scope of stories by students with diverse perspectives.

title: Bridge Michigan Environment Watch
description: Bridge Michigan’s Environment Watch is a digital newspaper published by the Center for Michigan, a nonprofit organization that seeks to make Michigan better through high-quality, nonpartisan journalism and audience engagement. Since its launch in 2011, the online publication has grown dramatically and earned a reputation as one of Michigan’s most trusted news outlets. Bridge Michigan is also one of five nonprofit news outlets that participate in the Great Lakes News Collaborative, a Mott-funded initiative that seeks to improve news coverage of water issues in the region. Bridge Michigan is one of the pillars of the Collaborative. With renewed support, the Center for Michigan will continue to produce in-depth, high-quality, public-service journalism for its Environment Watch publication and the Great Lakes News Collaborative.

title: Michigan Radio - The Environment Report
description: Michigan Public (formerly known as Michigan Radio) is a public radio station whose license is held by the University of Michigan. It is the most-listened-to public radio station in Michigan, with an audience of more than 1.5 million listeners. Over the past four years, with support from the Mott Foundation, the station has enhanced its coverage of water issues in the Great Lakes basin with stories that are broadcast and appear on the station’s website. Michigan Public is also a pillar of the Great Lakes News Collaborative, a Mott-funded initiative to enhance news coverage of the Great Lakes and water issues. Renewed support will enable the University of Michigan to continue this work through Michigan Public while reaching out to younger listeners with new types of social media content about the Great Lakes and water issues.

title: Public Safety Support
description: This grant will provide funds to Genesee County in support of the Office of Genesee County Sheriff to increase patrols and responses to crime occurring in the greater downtown Flint area. The Office of Genesee County Sheriff cooperates with law enforcement across the community to proactively prevent crime and to respond when crime occurs. This grant will support additional sergeants and deputies assigned to the area who respond to 911 calls and provide a presence at special events and other large gatherings.

title: Connect Humanity: Expansion to Latin America
description: The goal of this grant is to enhance civic space by bridging the digital divide and increasing digital equity. The newly established fund for digital equity, Connect Humanity will support communities in Latin America to build the internet infrastructure and skills they need to participate fully in a digital society. During the grant period, the grantee will map and analyze needs and opportunities, disburse up to nine planning grants and make at least two initial investments. As part of its capacity development, the grantee will hire two staff members from the region, build partnerships with local nonprofits and other stakeholders and collaborate with private and public funders to leverage investments. Established in 2021, Connect Humanity is a 501(c)(3) organization registered in the state of California.

title: Strengthening the ACCESS Coalition
description: Loughborough University — a recognized institution of higher learning in the United Kingdom — supports the Alliance of Civil Society Organizations for Clean Energy Access, which aims to coordinate action by civil society organizations working to deliver universal energy access. With prior Mott Foundation funding, the coalition successfully increased civil society participation and collaboration with the African Development Bank and the World Bank Group. This grant will allow the grantee to support the coalition as it strengthens its ability to convene and lead African civil society efforts to guide national and regional development finance institutions away from fossil fuels and towards distributed renewable energy solutions. Loughborough University will support the coalition to complete its transition to an independent, international organization based in Kenya, strengthen its operational effectiveness and build its capacity to offer technical support to its members. Critically, the coalition will support regional evidence-based advocacy aimed at increasing investment for energy access and ensuring community participation in energy project planning and implementation.

title: Michigan Communities for Financial Empowerment Network
grantee: Community Economic Development Association of Michigan
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: The Community Economic Development Association of Michigan works to expand and strengthen financial security in communities across the state. Since 2011, the Mott Foundation has supported the grantee’s efforts coordinating statewide engagement and education activities that increase awareness and support for children’s savings accounts. With this grant, the grantee will lay the groundwork for statewide expansion of children’s savings account programs by developing infrastructure, promoting the field, engaging new funders and providing technical assistance to programs serving children and families. Based in Lansing, the Community Economic Development Association of Michigan is a nonprofit trade association serving community economic development professionals in Michigan.

title: Flint Police Department Public Safety Support
description: This grant to the city of Flint will provide funding for a combination of efforts to increase public safety and reduce crime in the city. Public safety is a top priority for residents, and multiple law enforcement units are working together to address crime in the city. This grant includes funds for staffing and technology, which will add capacity to the Flint Police Department to receive and respond to real-time data about crime occurring in the city. Funds for solving previous crimes are also supported by this grant.

title: General Purposes
description: Minnesota Environmental Partnership is a broad coalition of environmental and conservation groups from across the state. The grantee has provided leadership and opportunities for its members to convene, communicate and collaborate to protect the state’s natural resources and environmental health. With prior support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has advanced equity and protections for land and water, with a focus on Lake Superior. The grantee is enabling and leading the coalition to address climate change impacts, especially in vulnerable communities. Renewed support will advance progress toward integrating environmental justice into their overall goals of clean water, climate resilience and Great Lakes policy work in the state.

title: International Program
description: Oil Change International documents international public finance support for fossil fuel-based energy production and advocates for a shift in support towards renewable energy. Its Public Finance for Energy Database has tracked public investment in the energy sector over the past 20 years providing high-quality data to international policymakers and civil society. With Mott Foundation support, the grantee has been a significant force in persuading development banks to commit to ending funding for fossil fuels and adopt new lending policies. This renewal grant will enable Oil Change International to continue its work to increase and improve public finance for renewable energy.

title: Endowment for Operations and Maintenance of a State Park in Downtown Flint
description: This grant to the Community Foundation of Greater Flint will establish a permanent operations and maintenance endowment for the new state park in Flint. The park — comprised of approximately 230 acres — will be anchored at Chevy Commons in the heart of the city and include Riverbank Park, Happy Hollow Nature Preserve and Mott Park Recreation Area. A number of public, private and philanthropic partners have worked together to establish the first state park in Genesee County, previously the only county in Michigan without one. The park will be accessible to residents and visitors as a safe and welcoming place to recreate for enjoyment and overall health and well-being.

title: Expanding Civic Space in East and Southern Africa
geographic_focus: Mozambique, Zimbabwe, Botswana, Kenya, Zambia, Uganda, Tanzania
description: The goal of the project is to increase awareness, understanding and engagement of nonprofits with regards to the laws and policies related to anti-money laundering and counterterrorism. To this end, the Defenders Protection Initiative, a nonprofit registered in Uganda, will strengthen the capacity of nonprofits in East and Southern Africa to engage effectively with these policies and understand their impact on civic space. Planned activities over the next two years will include: 1) producing accessible information on relevant policies; 2) building the capacity of regional networks and coalitions to engage effectively on previously-established regulations; and 3) promoting cooperation between nonprofit actors and other stakeholders at a national and regional level. In addition, the grantee will create opportunities for the regional networks to engage in global discussions on specific topics related to anti-money laundering and counterterrorism. Established in 2013, the Defenders Protection Initiative promotes a safe and secure working environment for human rights defenders and nonprofits by strengthening their capacity on safety and security management.

title: Expanding Civic Space in East and Southern Africa
geographic_focus: Zambia, Kenya, Botswana, Uganda, Tanzania, Mozambique, Zimbabwe
description: The project goal is to increase awareness, knowledge and engagement of nonprofits with policies and laws related to counterterrorism and money laundering. To achieve this, the Defenders Protection Initiative builds and strengthens the capacity of civil society organizations to push back on the policies using credible information. During the previous period, the grantee hosted information workshops in five countries in East and Southern Africa, produced learning material on anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism policies and hosted a regional convening. This grant will enable the grantee to support a platform for regional engagement with relevant bodies, provide tools to strengthen civil society and conduct studies on the effects of the Financial Action Task Force’s greylisting on civil society organizations. The Defenders Protection Initiative is a national nonprofit registered in Uganda to protect human rights defenders.

title: Civic Compass
location: Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires, Argentina
geographic_focus: Mexico, Caribbean, Central America, South America
description: The project goal is to increase the awareness, understanding and engagement of the nonprofit and philanthropic sector with respect to digital policies and practices that impact the space for civic engagement. To this end, Civic Compass, a thought leadership division within Civic House, will conduct research and policy development on the challenges posed by big tech platforms, digital media and government regulation over the citizen sector. The project will include providing training and strategic advice on citizen mobilization and creative advocacy in order to enhance the capacity of civil society organizations working to reduce the effects of a shrinking civic space. The grantee strives to build knowledge about issues affecting the relationship between technology, the internet and representative democracy in Latin America. Based in Argentina with offices in Brazil, Colombia and Mexico, Civic House has over ten years of experience working with a new generation of citizen-based initiatives that use technology to drive social change.

title: Civic Compass
location: Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires, Argentina
geographic_focus: Caribbean, Central America, Mexico, South America
description: The project goal is to increase the awareness, understanding and engagement of the nonprofit and philanthropic sector with respect to digital policies and practices that impact the space for civic engagement. To this end, Civic Compass, a thought leadership division within Civic House, will expand research into artificial intelligence and internet regulation’s impact on civil society and further investigate technology’s effect on shrinking civic space in Latin America. At a time of increasing challenges to fund nonprofit organizations in the region, the grantee will also explore an alternative model for its sustainability via a combination of fee-for-service and grants. Based in Argentina with offices in Brazil, Colombia and Mexico, Civic House will capitalize on newly built regional and global partnerships as well as over 20 years of experience working with a new generation of citizen-based initiatives that use technology to drive social change.

title: Energy Convergence for Off-Grid Amazonian Communities Program
description: This project supports Michigan State University, in partnership with a federal Brazilian university, to develop and implement a community engagement model for delivering renewable energy systems in the Tapajos-Arapiuns basin of the Brazilian Amazon. Over the previous grant period, researchers worked closely with communities to understand their needs and co-design energy systems. The grantee provided training for local technicians and installed energy systems in several communities. The grant renewal will support implementing renewable energy systems in additional communities, train technicians and disseminate information through media products. Michigan State University and its partners will also engage with leaders in the energy sector to promote participatory community engagement as a scalable solution for electrifying isolated communities in the Amazon and combat climate change.

title: Ensuring Development and Climate Finance Support Sustainable Development
description: The Center for International Environmental Law works to advance the right to information, public participation and access to justice on environmental matters as well as ensure that investment decisions align with the development objectives of local communities. With Mott Foundation support, the grantee has assisted communities in Chile, Colombia and Panama to use non-judicial accountability mechanisms to change the way energy and infrastructure projects are implemented and secure changes in the policies of development finance institutions. The grant builds on long-standing efforts to improve the policies and practices of the World Bank Group by ensuring that accountability processes result in effective remedies for affected communities.

title: Gus Macker Tournament
description: This grant to the Sylvester Broome Empowerment Village will support the 2022 Gus Macker Tournament. In 2021, the once dormant three-on-three basketball tournament returned to Flint. In its first year, it attracted over 6,000 visitors and 549 participants. The purpose is to raise funds for the grantee’s sports programs, increase tourism and positively impact the economy in the Genesee County area. Attendance and participation in 2022 is expected to increase due to people gathering again more frequently and the additional marketing activity for the event. Both adults and youth participate in the tournament.

title: Health Disparity Project
grantee: American Red Cross — East Central Bay-Michigan Chapter
description: This grant to the American National Red Cross East Bay Chapter in Flint will support the organization’s efforts to address health disparities in Flint and Genesee County. Black residents are disproportionally impacted by sickle cell disease that often requires frequent blood transfusions to alleviate pain and other symptoms. Sickle cell patients have a better response to treatment when blood is donated by someone of the same race or ethnicity. This program aims to triple the number of Black donors by 2025 to better serve patients with sickle cell disease.

title: Arts Programming at Genesee Valley Regional Center
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide support for arts-based workshops to young people living at the Genesee Valley Regional Center, a youth detention facility in Genesee County. The Youth Arts Unlocked program has offered workshops at the center since 2011. The program uses a research-based, trauma-informed curriculum to deliver visual arts, dance, poetry, yoga and theater to boys and girls living at the facility.

title: Film Appreciation Academy for Youth
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant increase will provide additional funding to iMichigan Productions, Inc. for a film appreciation program for youth in Flint. Working with local organizations such as Berston Field House and the Flint Public Library, the iMichigan team will develop and implement a curriculum that explores the filmmaking genre. Filmmaking is a complex process and offers a variety of career pathways for those who are interested in the art form or the more technical aspects of the industry, such as sound engineering and editing. This program will explore all facets of filmmaking.

title: Help Center Capital Improvements
description: This grant increase to United Way of Genesee County will provide additional funds for facility repairs at R.L. Jones Community Outreach Center located at Greater Holy Temple Church of God in Christ in Flint. The repairs are needed due to the high volume of Help Center activities at the site since 2016. The Help Centers started as a response to the water crisis and have continued to provide needed resources during the pandemic. Each week, heavy semitrucks deliver food, water and other resources to the Help Center sites which have had a significant impact on the parking lots and warehouses. The Help Centers work with many other organizations across the city, including the Food Bank of Eastern Michigan, Genesee Health System, Hamilton Healthcare Network and Genesee County Health Department.

title: University of Michigan-Flint Department of Public Safety Support
description: This grant will provide funds to the University of Michigan-Flint Department of Public Safety to increase patrols and responses to crime occurring on campus and in the greater downtown Flint area. Department of Public Safety officers cooperate with law enforcement across the community to proactively prevent crime and to respond when crime occurs. This grant will support four additional full-time officers and one sergeant to the department. The Department of Public Safety will work in partnership with the Office of Genesee County Sheriff and the Flint Police Department to reduce crime and increase public safety in the greater downtown area.

title: Renewable Energy for Extractive Reserves in the Amazon
description: This project supports the World Wildlife Fund and its partner, World Wildlife Fund Brazil, in enhancing solar energy access for forest communities in sustainable development reserves in the Amazon. Over the last grant period, the grantee has coordinated a network of civil society organizations working on renewable electrification, produced informative radio programs, and facilitated cooperation between the Brazilian government, the Brazilian Development Bank, energy forums and local communities. With the renewal of this grant, World Wildlife Fund will continue to: 1) engage with key stakeholders to accelerate a renewable energy expansion in the Amazon; 2) create renewable energy access guidelines for extractive reserves; and 3) consolidate lessons learned from the coordination of a network of civil society groups.

title: Integration Investments and Indigenous Peoples in South America
description: The Indian Law Resource Center has been a crucial advocate for Indigenous peoples in the Americas for over 40 years, providing legal expertise to enhance policies, practices and accountability at national and international development finance institutions. During the previous grant period, the grantee gathered evidence to improve the accountability of development banks, strengthened capacities for implementing environmental and social policy standards and evaluated the safeguard policies of South American countries against those of multilateral development banks. In the upcoming grant period, the Indian Law Resource Center will continue to: 1) enhance Indigenous peoples’ capacities in selected South American countries to hold financial institutions accountable; and 2) push international and national development finance institutions to adopt safeguards that benefit Indigenous peoples.

title: Accountability Research Center
description: The Accountability Research Center at American University — a major university based in Washington, D.C. — works to improve the social and environmental outcomes of development finance institutions, strengthen accountability and enhance affected community participation in decision and policy making. With prior Mott Foundation support, the grantee led a series of dialogues between World Bank officials and civil society organizations. It also worked with organizations in developing countries to monitor the implementation of World Bank-financed projects and assess their compliance with social and environmental safeguards. This renewal grant will enable the Accountability Research Center at American University to continue advocating for stronger civic engagement at the World Bank due to shifting priorities in response to the challenge of climate change.

title: Powered by Youth Voice: Future Directions for Afterschool
description: This grant increase will provide additional funds to ExpandED Schools for the Powered by Youth Voice: Future Directions for Afterschool project. Additional funding will allow the grantee to support meeting costs for travel, lodging and coordination of the youth-led Capstone Challenge event in Fall 2022.

title: Blight Demolition
description: This grant to the Friends of Berston will support the purchase of blighted property adjacent to the historic Berston Field House. The grant also provides funds for abatement and demolition of the structure located on the property and the removal of an underground tank. The project will eliminate blight and increase opportunities for future productive use of the property, which could include green space or an outdoor recreation area operated by Berston Field House.

title: Great Lakes Now
description: Great Lakes Now is an award-winning monthly television program and multimedia news website managed by Detroit PBS. The television show and daily digital content are shared with public television stations in the eight Great Lakes states and two Canadian provinces that border the lakes. Great Lakes Now is also a member of the Great Lakes News Collaborative, a Mott-funded effort to bolster news coverage of Great Lakes and water issues, and is the only television station participating in the Collaborative. Great Lakes Now’s website has the most comprehensive catalog of articles produced by the five nonprofit media outlets in the Collaborative, which greatly increases the reach and readership of those stories across the Great Lakes basin. With renewed support, Great Lakes Now will increase its production of original, in-depth content and make it possible for the other four media partners in the Collaborative to share that content on their respective websites.

title: Help Center Capital Improvements
description: This grant increase to Asbury Community Development Corporation will provide additional funds for facility repairs at the Help Center site located at Asbury United Methodist Church in Flint. The Help Centers started as a response to the water crisis and have continued to provide needed resources during the pandemic. Each week, heavy semitrucks deliver food, water and other resources to the sites, which have had a significant impact on the parking lots and warehouses. The Help Centers work with many other organizations across the city, including the Food Bank of Eastern Michigan, Genesee Health System, Hamilton Healthcare Network and Genesee County Health Department.

title: Help Center Capital Improvements
description: This grant increase to Bethel United Methodist Church will provide additional funds for facility repairs. The repairs are needed due to the high volume of Help Center activities at the site since 2016. The Help Centers started as a response to the water crisis and have continued to provide needed resources during the pandemic. Each week, heavy semitrucks deliver food, water and other resources to the Help Center sites which have had a significant impact on the parking lots and warehouses. The Help Centers work with many other organizations across the city, including the Food Bank of Eastern Michigan, Genesee Health System, Hamilton Healthcare Network and Genesee County Health Department.

title: Unlocking BNDES Operation Lifecycle
description: SITAWI Finance for Good is a Brazilian nonprofit organization established in 2008 to mobilize research and capital for positive environmental and social outcomes. During the previous grant period, the grantee continued monitoring banking activities while advancing awareness of social and environmental impacts and safeguards related to oil and gas exploitation in the Brazilian Amazon. With this grant, SITAWI Finance for Good will strengthen community capacities to monitor and discuss social and environmental safeguards for oil and gas activities in the Medio Juruá River basin in the Brazilian Amazon.

title: Regulation of Nonprofits and Philanthropy
description: The program goal is to support a healthy policy environment for the nonprofit and philanthropic sectors. The Regulation of Nonprofits and Philanthropy project aims to document, enhance understanding and promote dialogue related to the state and federal regulatory framework and its impact on charities, philanthropy and the nonprofit sector. This grant increase will enable the grantee to merge two large legal data sets, the Urban Institute’s own Legal Compendium and Dr. Teresa Harrison’s Legal Text Data. The grantee will also integrate the merged data into the National Center for Charitable Statistics Open Data Platform and the new Nonprofit Organization Research Panel Platform. The project is implemented by the Center on Nonprofits and Philanthropy at the Urban Institute — a think tank that builds knowledge about the nation’s social and fiscal challenges.

title: Berston Field House Capital Improvements
description: This grant will support the renovation and construction of new facilities for the community center housed at Berston Field House. Located in an economically challenged part of the city, Berston has served Flint residents in a variety of ways for nearly 100 years. The new amenities at Berston will enable the organization to increase its educational, recreational and enrichment programming for residents. The updated athletic facilities will provide access to participants of all ages and ability levels, thereby encouraging health and wellness. Enhanced gathering spaces and new classrooms will bring the community together to celebrate, learn and share ideas and opportunities with one another.

title: Healthy Great Lakes Program
description: The Canadian Environmental Law Association provides legal aid, education and access to decision-making process in the Province of Ontario. With previous Mott Foundation support, the grantee has provided analysis and guidance for decision-makers and the public on Great Lakes issues, including water contaminants, watershed planning and drinking water protection. With renewed support, Canadian Environmental Law Association will: 1) expand its network; 2) deepen connections with indigenous communities; and 3) continue to advocate for sound water policies in the Great Lakes basin.

title: INSPIRE - Initiative for Strategic Philanthropy and Intelligent Resources
grantee: Association for the Practice of Transformation
description: The program goal is to strengthen community philanthropy globally. To this end, the Association for the Practice of Transformation has launched INSPIRE — Initiative for Strategic Philanthropy and Intelligent Resource — as an informal network of community foundation practitioners and experts. More specifically, the grantee strengthens and expands the network, produces and shares knowledge about community foundations in various contexts and promotes good practice for community foundations and their support organizations. This grant increase will provide resources needed to better engage community foundations and community foundation support organizations beyond Europe, such as from Latin America, Africa, North America and the United Kingdom.

title: Justice 2023 - Seizing the Opportunity of the Sustainable Development Goal Summit
description: The project goal is to elevate the voices of African civil society organizations at the 2023 United Nations High-level Political Forum and the Sustainable Development Goal Summit. Particular attention will be given to African nonprofits working in the area of access to justice and addressing Sustainable Development Goal 16. To this extent, the United Nations Foundation will: 1) provide strategic advice, insights and technical assistance; 2) broker partnerships with other actors working in this area especially around the UNmute civil society campaign; and 3) promote links with its work on young leaders, activists and thinkers, including its support for the Unlock the Future Coalition. The United Nations Foundation is a strategic partner to help the United Nations mobilize the ideas, people and resources it needs to deliver a diverse and durable constituency for collective action.

title: Advancing Entrepreneurship Education
description: This grant will support the Young Entrepreneur Institute at the University School located in Hunting Valley, Ohio. Founded in 2005, the grantee partners with organizations throughout northeast Ohio to provide every young person with access to entrepreneurial education and experiences. The goals of this project are to: 1) increase the opportunities for young people to understand and experience entrepreneurship by infusing entrepreneurship into afterschool and out-of-school time programs; and 2) increase engagement of regional ecosystems in youth entrepreneurship within under-served and under-resourced communities.

title: Clean and Affordable Drinking Water: Growing Advocacy and Organizational Capacity in the Great Lakes
geographic_focus: Pennsylvania, Illinois, Minnesota, Wisconsin, Ohio, Michigan, New York, Indiana
description: River Network is a national organization that provides training to advance organizational effectiveness and sharpen skills and capacity to address issues like access to clean, safe and affordable drinking water. For over 20 years, River Network has trained community organizations and leaders to protect their local waterbodies with its widely admired Clean Water Act Owner’s Manual. With this grant increase, River Network will update and reissue the manual and provide new related training programs.

title: Monitoring BNDES Sustainability
grantee: Instituto de Energia e Meio Ambiente
description: The Instituto de Energia e Meio Ambiente is a nonprofit Brazilian think tank dedicated to research, analysis and policy evaluation to promote socially and environmentally sustainable energy and transportation development. Over the last grant period, the grantee monitored electric power plants’ social and environmental impacts and scrutinized plans by development finance institutions to expand natural gas-fired generation. With the renewal of this grant, the grantee will continue monitoring the expansion of natural gas in the country and will extend its focus to include isolated systems in the Brazilian Amazon. Additionally, Instituto de Energia e Meio Ambiente will develop a web-based platform to assist financial institutions in the Brazilian energy sector to incorporate social and environmental risks and impacts in their decision-making.

title: Assessing Opportunities to Support Great Lakes Community Based Organizations
description: In order to successfully build a more just and sustainable environmental movement in the Great Lakes region, more must be done to cultivate the strength and leadership of communities of color. Justice Outside, a national organization with roots in the outdoor education field, specializes in leadership development and capacity building as a means to build equity in outdoor access and other environmental programs. With this planning grant, Justice Outside will explore opportunities to expand its programming in the Great Lakes region.

title: Technical Support to Maximize Renewable Energy Access Success
grantee: Instituto de Energia e Meio Ambiente
description: The Instituto de Energia e Meio Ambiente is a Brazilian think tank specializing in energy planning, electrical engineering and environmental law and policy. During the previous grant period, the grantee advanced renewable energy access in the Amazon by demonstrating the viability of solar-battery systems, mapping community energy needs and forging technical cooperation agreements with the government. The grantee also identified regulatory, financial and data gaps that still limit universal access to electricity, especially for productive uses. The grantee also developed a web platform with lessons from pilot projects and provided policy analysis. Over the next grant period, Instituto de Energia e Meio Ambiente will further expand renewable energy access in the Amazon by helping to strengthen regulations, coordinate energy and sustainable community forest production policies, close data gaps, and develop environmentally responsible models for off-grid solar systems. These efforts aim to ensure both household and productive energy needs are met while supporting government accountability and long-term system sustainability.

title: Lake Michigan Water Program
description: The Illinois Environmental Council Education Fund was established in 1975 and has over 100 affiliates working to protect water resources in the state, including the Lake Michigan basin. As part of its Clean Water Program, the grantee builds coalitions and educates the public and decision-makers about water issues. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has raised awareness and made progress on several issues facing the state and region, including lead service line replacement, toxic chemical pollution reduction and invasive species control. With renewed support, the Illinois Environmental Council Education Fund will further the goals of its Clean Water Program with a focus on safe and affordable drinking water.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purposes support to the Asylum Seeker Advocacy Project as it continues to supply legal resources and information to immigrants, improve the systems that serve immigrants and build a virtual community of asylum seekers in the United States. During the previous grant period, the grantee conducted impact litigation that resulted in long-lasting changes to work permit regulations and grew its network by over 300,000 additional asylum seekers. During this upcoming grant period, the grantee will respond to the ongoing needs of its members and expand its legal support systems and digital offerings. Asylum Seeker Advocacy Project members live in every U.S. state and territory and come from over 175 countries. Considering members’ asylum-seeking children, the organization now serves 950,000 asylum seekers — or 1 in 360 individuals living in the United States.

title: Western Balkans Community Foundations
geographic_focus: Albania, Serbia, North Macedonia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, Kosovo
description: The project goal is to expand and strengthen the community foundation field in the Western Balkans region. To this end, the Trag Foundation will work to increase the number of community foundations in Serbia and facilitate learning and cooperation among community foundations in the region. More specifically, the grantee will promote the concept and practice of community foundations, facilitate the establishment of new community foundations and develop the capacity of community foundations in the region. In addition, the grantee will connect the new community foundations to existing networks and initiatives, including the European Community Foundation Initiative. During the past grant period, the Trag Foundation: 1) increased its capacity to support community foundation development; 2) facilitated the establishment of three new community foundations in Serbia; 3) strengthened the capacity of the existing community foundations; and 4) supported the establishment of their national network.

title: Sustainable Development Goals Aotearoa New Zealand
description: The project goal is to advance the adoption of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals by community foundations in New Zealand. To this end, Community Foundations of New Zealand will orient its member community foundations to the goals by: 1) conducting a webinar series; 2) publishing a blog series; 3) developing a template presentation; 4) creating an information segment on its website and in its newsletters; 5) holding dedicated sessions at its next three annual conferences; and 6) creating example policies and templates relating to grantmaking and reporting that is informed by the Sustainable Development Goals. Established in 2014, Community Foundations of New Zealand is a national membership body that supports the growing network of currently 17 local community foundations across New Zealand.

title: SDG Adoption by Mexican Community Foundations
description: The program goal is to advance the adoption of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals by community foundations in Mexico. To this end, Comunalia is providing technical support, workshops, communication strategies, reference materials, digital tools and funding opportunities to Mexican community foundations. An ongoing series of webinars that are open to all Mexican community foundations also provides links to outside organizations working to advance the goals. The project includes small subgrants to community foundations in order to implement their work to adopt the goals on a local level. More Mexican community foundations are participating in this implementation than originally anticipated — hence, a grant increase is needed to augment the subgranting fund pool.

title: Buick City Redevelopment
description: This grant will provide funding to the city of Flint to prepare the remaining portions of the Buick City site for redevelopment. Buick City is one of Flint’s oldest industrial areas and at its peak, the 352-acre site had more than 27,000 workers. Buick City was transferred to the RACER Trust in 2011 following General Motors 2009 bankruptcy filing. Outside of one development on 60-acres of the cleanest portion of the 412-acre site, the remaining portions have been fenced off. These fenced off portions have large concrete foundation slabs, abandoned utilities and contamination. Without the ability to address these legacy costs to make the site more competitive with greenfield locations, the site would likely languish undeveloped. When combined with American Rescue Plan Act funds, this grant provides an opportunity to support the city of Flint’s efforts to bring in an experienced real estate development company to address these legacy costs. Once fully redeveloped, the site has the ability to provide over 3.5 million square feet of light industrial and warehouse facilities resulting in approximately 3,500 new jobs.

title: Community Foundation Development in Latin America
geographic_focus: Peru, Chile, Costa Rica, Mexico, Argentina, Brazil, Colombia
description: The program goal is to support the emergence and strengthening of community foundations in Latin America. To this end, Landa Zambrano Asociados S.C. will provide technical assistance and capacity building to community foundation support organizations, their partners and stakeholders primarily in Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Mexico and Peru. This will be accomplished through virtual coaching sessions, webinars, site visits, workshops, presentations and meetings with potential investors and other stakeholders. The grantee will also: 1) support cross-learning among the various stakeholders; 2) provide learning connections with other relevant global actors; and 3) develop an evaluation framework for community foundation support organizations and help them develop a common communications strategy, platform and projects. Founded in 2020 and located in Monterrey, Mexico, Landa Zambrano Asociados S.C. is a private consulting firm that supports entrepreneurs, leaders and organizations to launch their social initiatives.

title: Travel and Learning Fund
description: The project goal is to advance the Civil Society program’s objectives and outcomes by supporting exchange, networking and interaction among key nonprofits, practitioners and experts, including Mott Foundation grantees, working in the program’s thematic areas of interest. To this end, the Institute of International Education, Inc. will operate a travel and learning fund to support individuals and organizations working on civic space, community philanthropy, access to justice or other areas of interest to the Civil Society program. This increase will accommodate increased demand from the field as the pandemic eases and travel resumes. During the grant period, the grantee will support: 1) participation in study visits and exchanges; 2) engagement in virtual and in-person conferences and other events; and 3) field studies and research projects that result in a report or publication that benefits the field. Based in New York, the Institute of International Education, Inc. manages similar funds for foundations around the world.

title: General Purposes
description: The Alliance for the Great Lakes is a well-established regional organization working to protect and restore the Great Lakes ecosystem and thus improve the lives of people throughout the basin. For the last several years, the grantee has been working with another organization, the Southeast Environmental Task Force, to strengthen the Calumet Connect Partnership, a coalition of community-based groups pursuing clean water and climate resilience on the Southeast side of Chicago. This grant increase is for the general purposes of the Alliance for the Great Lakes, including its interest in building the organizational capacity of the task force so that Calumet Connect becomes a fully community-led partnership addressing the needs of the corridor for both people and wildlife.

title: General Purposes
description: Michigan Future, Inc. is a non-partisan, nonprofit organization whose mission is to be a source of new ideas on how Michigan can succeed as a world-class community in a knowledge-driven economy. This grant will support the organization’s efforts to inform the development and advancement of strategies that strengthen the state economy and increase prosperity for all Michigan households, especially asset-limited, income-constrained employees. Activities planned for the two-year grant period include: 1) policy research; 2) policy development; 3) networking and convening; and 4) advocacy.

title: China-Latin America Sustainable Investments Initiative
description: The China-Latin America Sustainable Investments Initiative, a project of the Bank Information Center, partners with organizations in South America to monitor Chinese investments and enhance social and environmental standards governing Chinese-financed projects in the region. During the previous grant period, the grantee updated its manual on Chinese social and environmental guidelines and expanded its support for Latin American partners addressing the impacts of Chinese development finance in the region. The renewal grant will enable the grantee to advance its efforts by: 1) producing in-depth reports on Chinese-funded projects; 2) building and strengthening relationships with Chinese stakeholders; and 3) expanding its network of civil society organizations in Latin America and globally. Bank Information Center will also provide updates on Chinese investments, prepare policy briefs, create informative content on Chinese guidelines and policies and host capacity-building events for partner groups in the region.

title: General Purposes
description: The Bank Information Center partners with civil society organizations in developing countries to ensure that the operations and policies of the World Bank Group and other international financial institutions support local communities and mitigate any project impacts. With prior Mott Foundation funding, the grantee helped strengthen social and environmental governance at the World Bank Group, the InterAmerican Development Bank and the African Development Bank and built the capacity of local organizations to scrutinize project implementation. With renewed general purpose support, the Bank Information Center will seek to strengthen the social and environmental safeguards of the private lending arms of multilateral development banks, ensure projects on the ground are implemented as designed and advocate for incorporating nature-based solutions in climate change projects.

title: Facility Improvements
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide funds to increase accessibility and capacity of the New McCree Theatre facility. In March 2020, the organization purchased the former Charity United Methodist Church on Clio Road as a permanent home. The 23,000 square-foot facility is two stories with a balcony area for seating and equipment. This grant will fund the installation of glass railings in the balcony in order to offer seating for shows in this area of the theater. Funds will also be used to install a chairlift between the main floor and the lower level increasing accessibility for programming and community events.

title: Engage Every Student Initiative
description: This grant will support the American Association of School Administrators to establish a national technical assistance consortium for local school districts seeking to increase afterschool and summer learning programs. This consortium will align with the new Engage Every Student Initiative that seeks to establish an afterschool program spot for every youth who needs one through use of education recovery resources, including American Rescue Plan funding. Specifically, this grant will support the American Association of School Administrators to: 1) establish a national technical assistance consortium supporting school districts, community-based providers and municipal partners; 2) establish a call center to provide timely support to local school and community-based staff; 3) coordinate a Superintendent Speakers Bureau; and 4) coordinate a multimedia communications campaign to promote Engage Every Student Initiative and its goals and the technical assistance consortium.

title: 21st Century Community Learning Centers Summer Institute
description: This grant will provide funding to support the annual convening of the 21st Century Community Learning Centers held by Synergy Enterprises, Inc. in partnership with the U.S. Department of Education. The 21st Century Community Learning Centers initiative supports nearly 1.7 million children and youth in over 11,000 school-community afterschool programs across the country. The purpose of the annual summer symposium is to provide 21st CCLC administrators and staff with technical assistance and strategies to continue to build high-quality 21st CCLC afterschool and summer learning programs.

title: General Purposes
description: The International Energy Initiative Brasil is an independent, nongovernmental organization founded by sustainable energy development experts to promote energy efficiency and renewable energy production. During the previous grant period, the grantee began implementing its new strategic plan, growing the professional team and promoting renewable energy through a range of activities. With this renewal, the International Energy Initiative Brasil will build financial and institutional strength and advance renewable energy solutions in the Brazilian Amazon by producing reports and engaging partner networks.

title: Global Philanthropy Program
description: This grant supports the Council on Foundations’ Global Philanthropy Program which is framed around four pillars of activity: 1) strengthening cross-border grantmaking; 2) advocating for a global enabling environment; 3) facilitating global convenings and conversations; and 4) developing global resources and thought leadership. With previous Mott Foundation support, the grantee has produced publications on responding globally to COVID-19, conducted webinars on various global topics of interest to its members, convened funders around India’s restrictions on foreign funding and updated members on regulatory changes that affect giving to organizations in selected countries. With this grant increase, the council will be able to host a peer learning circle for its members and other foundations in North America to support philanthropy’s response to the crisis in Ukraine. This will be done in partnership with the German Marshall Fund, Community Foundations of Canada and Philanthropic Foundations of Canada.

title: Jurists Promoting Access to Justice and Defending the Rule of Law in Africa
description: The goal of this project is to build better relationships between community paralegals and the formal legal fraternity in Africa. To this end, the International Commission of Jurists will continue to undertake various activities to create space for meaningful conversations between the judiciary, lawyers and community justice workers. This grant will support these engagements in southern and east Africa, with a goal to replicate the project at scale. Previous Mott Foundation support has helped the grantee to find different means of engagement between the judiciary and community justice workers. It assisted the United Nations Special Rapporteur on the Independence of Judges and Lawyers in launching her first report on the prospects of legal empowerment. The International Commission of Jurists was established in 1952 with the purpose of promoting justice and human rights within the formal legal sector. Its headquarters is situated in Geneva, Switzerland.

title: Re-Envisioning the CSA Field: From Small-Dollar to Large-Dollar CSAs
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: Although many children and families still lack savings accounts, the field’s recent growth has created a platform for advancing the next generation of children’s savings account policy innovations. While research evidence also shows that low- and moderate-income families successfully save in children’s savings accounts, field leaders are exploring innovative strategies for increasing seed deposits and growing overall account balances, especially among low- and moderate-income families. With Mott Foundation support, the University of Michigan will begin building the research and policy case for a shift from small- to large-dollar children’s savings accounts. To accomplish this goal, the grantee will publish research and policy briefs summarizing research findings and laying out policy arguments, prepare op-eds and blogs to help highlight ideas and create a network of stakeholders to help disseminate and promote new ideas.

title: Community Legal Centers in Ukraine
description: The program goal is to support access to justice in small communities in Ukraine by strengthening local justice institutions. The Charity and Health Foundation will work with newly amalgamated communities in territories of southeast Ukraine to help expand practice and understanding of community-based policing, with a particular focus on improving juvenile justice practices. The grantee will also research, monitor and broadly publicize local experiences of how new models of community-based justice are improving lives of citizens and how they can positively inform wider law enforcement reforms. During 2019-21, the grantee produced over 300 online and offline publications detailing community justice practices and highlighting deficiencies in juvenile justice provisions in rural communities. The grantee also produced further material on community policing for inclusion in the curriculum of Ukraine’s leading institution for police training. In the wake of Russia’s illegal invasion of Ukraine, the Charity and Health Foundation will gather and distribute information about successful community organizing aimed at providing community safety and accessible social and legal assistance.

title: Statewide Afterschool Network Support
description: This grant will allow the National Summer Learning Association to support the development and sustainability of the statewide afterschool networks. Specifically, this grant will support the National Summer Learning Association to: 1) provide technical assistance to the 50 State Afterschool Network; 2) share best practices on afterschool funding models; and 3) address the potential fiscal cliff and the impact on programs when American Rescue Plan funding expires.

title: Solar Energy for Amazon River Dwellers
grantee: Centro de Estudos Avançados de Promoção Social e Ambiental
description: The Centro de Estudos Avançados de Promoção Social e Ambiental, a nonprofit organization founded in 1985, is dedicated to promoting sustainable community development and conserving the Amazon rainforest by enhancing public policies and improving the quality of life for children, youth, Indigenous peoples and traditional communities. In the previous grant period, the grantee collaborated with isolated Indigenous communities in the Tapajós River basin to: 1) implement sustainable, community-managed renewable energy solutions; 2) continue its training programs; and 3) organize a policy symposium and trade fair focused on renewable electrification for remote communities in the Amazon. In the upcoming grant period, the grantee will prioritize strengthening off-grid clean energy solutions for Indigenous health units in the Tapajós River region of the Brazilian Amazon. Centro de Estudos Avançados de Promoção Social e Ambiental will also focus on training solar technicians in local communities, emphasizing the inclusion of women and Indigenous leaders.

title: General Purposes
description: Afterschool Alliance seeks to ensure that all children, youth and families have access to afterschool and summer learning programs. To meet this goal, the grantee will continue to: 1) lead the field in meeting the needs of young people post-pandemic and beyond; 2) serve as an information source on afterschool programs and resource for policymakers, programs and educators; 3) be an effective voice in its efforts to expand quality afterschool programs and innovative models; and 4) increase access to research and data on the effectiveness of quality afterschool programs. This grant will allow the grantee to continue its efforts to ensure that young people and families — particularly those in underserved populations — have access to engaging afterschool and summer learning opportunities. The Afterschool Alliance will also work with the 50 State Afterschool Network to support afterschool expansion through the American Rescue Plan and other federal, state and local afterschool initiatives.

title: Harrison Street Mixed-Use Facility
description: With this grant, the YMCA of Greater Flint will partner with the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation to construct a new multi-use facility in downtown Flint designed to co-locate affordable housing, a community wellness center and youth education and family programming. The building will include 55,000 square feet for a new YMCA facility and 50 affordable and market-rate apartments. Together, the new facility will increase the vitality and vibrancy of downtown Flint while addressing the housing and wellness needs of Flint and Genesee County residents of all ages.

title: McFarlan Home Capital Improvements
description: This grant will provide funding to McFarlan Charitable Corporation for the renovation of Court Street Village, an affordable senior housing complex. Court Street Village includes two separate buildings, both of which will undergo a full renovation. The renovation includes all new plumbing, heating ventilation and cooling, painting, cabinetry, flooring, appliances and exterior finishes. Upon completion, the two buildings will include 268 units of senior housing in Flint, which includes 39 assisted living and memory support units not previously available at the location. Of the 268 units, 256 will be affordable housing units, including 37 of the 39 assisted living units. Flint has over 13,000 seniors living within the city with average household incomes significantly below the state average. The renovation will provide much needed quality housing to serve these residents.

title: Feasibility Study and Fundraising Plan and Implementation
description: This grant will provide funding for a feasibility study and implementation plan as the Flint Children’s Museum seeks to relocate. The current site of the Flint Children’s Museum on University Avenue has been a good location for the organization; however, the building contains environmental hazards and is only 11,000 square feet, which limits exhibits and programming. The museum offers low-cost, educational programming and hands-on learning for young children from birth to eight years old. The feasibility study will assess the current fund development capacity of the museum and develop a fundraising plan for its $20.25 million relocation and renovation project.

title: South Saginaw Street Property Acquisition
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant increase will provide additional resources for the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation to fund and direct the acquisition of two additional vacant properties along the South Saginaw Corridor through its supported organization, Uptown Reinvestment Corporation. Uptown Reinvestment Corporation will perform due diligence and coordinate the purchase and maintenance of several properties with the goal of preparing the corridor for potential redevelopment uses such as office spaces, residential housing and light industrial. This work will help facilitate business growth and support reinvestment in city neighborhoods.

title: General Purposes
description: The Flint River and its tributaries are an important recreational resource for the region’s residents, as well as an important habitat for a variety of freshwater species and other wildlife. The Flint River Watershed Coalition works to protect the Flint River and its tributaries through a variety of education and community engagement activities. With this grant increase, the grantee will maintain all of its programs during a period of leadership transition and financial challenge with the goal of building a stronger and more sustainable organization.

title: Early Childhood Education Research
description: With this grant increase, the Community Foundation of Greater Flint will continue supporting a multiyear evaluation of early childhood education efforts in Flint. The evaluation will first focus on the impact of high-quality practices at Educare Flint and Cummings Great Expectations centers, and then measure the impact that high-quality hubs can have on the early childhood education ecosystem across the city.

title: An Equitable Water Future in the Great Lakes
description: The U.S. Water Alliance is a national coalition of water utilities, consultants, environmental groups and community organizations that work together to advance a holistic and equitable approach to water management. With prior Mott Foundation support, the grantee launched the Water Equity Network, which has grown to 45 member cities, including several in the Great Lakes region. With continued support, the U.S. Water Alliance will expand the Network and form new Water Equity Action Taskforces to advance progress on water management and provide opportunities to learn and leverage resources through city to city and community partnerships.

title: Network for Schools Excellence Support
description: The goal of this grant is to support the Community Foundation of Greater Flint in its efforts to improve educational opportunities and outcomes for children in Flint. The grantee will develop a framework and lead a coordinated effort to impact a network of K-12 schools serving Flint children. The grantee will engage and align parent and community interests in the development of this community of practice.

title: Mariachi Music & Folklorico Dance Instruction
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to El Ballet Folklorico Estudiantil will support mariachi music and folklorico dance cultural education and instruction in Flint. The majority of participants are Hispanic; however, the program is open to all interested young people. Program participants showcase their talent and newly acquired skills at in-person community events and virtual concerts. The program fee is extremely low and does not cover the full cost of staffing. This grant will help ensure continued high-quality instruction and access for any child who wishes to participate, regardless of ability to pay.

title: Infrastructure Improvements
description: This grant to the Genesee County Free Medical Clinic will provide funds for outdoor infrastructure improvements including installation of a digital sign and repairs to the clinic’s parking lot that is currently in poor condition. The clinic provides uninsured county residents with access to vital medical and mental health services that might otherwise be unavailable to them.

title: Steam Engine 464 Assessment
description: The Genesee County Parks & Recreation Commission is dedicated to providing all residents of Genesee County with high-quality recreational and educational facilities and programs. Genesee County parks are widely utilized as accessible and affordable opportunities for local residents to experience recreation and nature. Attendance at most facilities has increased over the past several years, including during the pandemic when outdoor recreation areas were heavily used by friends and families to gather safely. This grant will enable the grantee to perform a critical maintenance assessment of Engine 464 of the Huckleberry Railroad at Crossroads Village.

title: Capacity Building
description: This grant will provide funding to support the fundraising and leadership development capacity of the Shelter of Flint. The Shelter of Flint is an essential human service organization serving individuals and families in need of a safe place to stay. The grantee receives a high percentage of its funding from the government which is often reimbursement-based and allows limited, if any, funds for overhead or indirect costs. Through increased fundraising and leadership capacity, the Shelter of Flint aims to increase its unrestricted dollars from individuals and organizations in order to remain nimble and address the needs of its clients and facilities in a timely manner.

title: Christopher Stallworth Fund
description: The grant will provide funds to the Community Foundation of Greater Flint for the Christopher Stallworth Fund. The funds will provide support to the Flint community for activities that celebrate Chris’s life and acknowledge the things that he held dear. Examples of projects that could be supported include community gathering and engagement activities, mentoring of young people, entrepreneurship activities and grassroots workforce activities.

title: Support for Special Projects
description: The goal of this grant is to support the Community Foundation of Greater Flint in building its capacity for special projects in the Flint community. To accomplish this goal, the grantee hired a dedicated staff person in 2021 with a history of working collaboratively in Flint. The director of special projects and initiatives works closely with the chief executive officer to provide them with both operational and administrative support.

title: Targeted Neighborhood Façade Improvement
description: This grant will support Genesee County Habitat for Humanity in operating its Targeted Neighborhood Façade Improvement Program in the neighborhood surrounding the Durant-Tuuri-Mott campus. In addition to repairing exteriors to homes in the area, the grantee will partner with local organizations to connect residents to additional programs and resources to help with critical home repairs not covered by the Targeted Neighborhood Façade Improvement Program. This work aligns with a core tenet of Genesee County Habitat for Humanity’s mission of bringing people together to build community.

title: Flint Community Journalism Support
description: Through this grant, the Community Foundation of Greater Flint will support the capacity building and writing needs of local community publications including The Flint Courier News, Flintside, Flint Beat, East Village Magazine and Our Community, Our Voice. These locally led news organizations provide trusted information and stories for local residents, and have been especially important as the community recovers from the water crisis and navigates the pandemic.

title: Advancing the Children's Savings Account Field
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: For over 40 years, Prosperity Now has focused on ensuring prosperity for all as a leading intermediary on national research, practice and policy dedicated to financial stability and wealth. With continued Mott Foundation support since 1983, the grantee’s endeavors have significantly built the children’s savings account field. With renewed support, the grantee is committed to strengthening existing Children’s Savings Account programs, fostering innovation in the field and centering racial equity in the Children’s Savings Account program design and operations. Additionally, Prosperity Now is prepared to aid the field in maintaining its progressive momentum to support efforts that ensure that every child in America has a children’s savings account by 2025 by ensuring new programs have the support and tools they need to be effective and sustainable and to support the development of the field as a whole.

title: Saginaw Bay Watershed Initiative Network
description: The Conservation Fund is a national organization that promotes conservation and sustainable economic development. The grantee’s Saginaw Bay Watershed Initiative Network seeks to advance economic, environmental and social sustainability in Michigan’s Saginaw Bay area. With previous Mott Foundation support, the grantee regranted funds to support projects that improve water quality and freshwater habitat in the watershed and hosted its State of the Bay conference with record attendance. With this renewal, the Conservation Fund will continue to: 1) support the regranting program; 2) broaden the network; and 3) develop projects that increase public awareness about the issues in the region that impact land, water and community.

title: Equitable School Funding: Empowering Michigan Stakeholders with Nonpartisan Data and Expertise
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: The Education Trust is a research and advocacy organization working to close opportunity gaps and raise achievement for students of color and from low-income families. The Education Trust-Midwest engages Michigan-based organizations and leaders to advocate for equitable funding and opportunities for Michigan children. The Midwest division will provide nonpartisan data and best practice expertise to better inform citizens, leaders and major educational stakeholders, including leading journalists, corporate and civil rights leaders, and policymakers about equitable funding.

title: General Purposes
description: The Minnesota Center for Environmental Advocacy has been a legal and scientific voice for Minnesota’s environment for 50 years.
