The grantee’s team of in-house lawyers and scientists works to address environmental issues across all branches of government. With prior Mott support, the grantee achieved several legal victories that protect people in the Lake Superior watershed and across the state from pollution, toxic chemicals and unsafe drinking water. Renewed support will help advance progress toward protecting Minnesota’s environment with a focus on: 1) natural resource protection; 2) water quality; 3) climate change solutions; and 4) environmental justice.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Cities Initiative
geographic_focus: Ontario, Pennsylvania, Minnesota, Wisconsin, Illinois, Indiana, Quebec, Michigan, New York, Ohio
description: The Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Cities Initiative is a coalition of over 260 U.S. and Canadian mayors and municipal officials dedicated to advancing the protection and restoration of the region and its water resources. The grantee provides services to its members to integrate environmental, economic and social priorities into solutions that protect the Great Lakes. With previous Mott Foundation support, the grantee convened, collaborated and advanced policies for the benefit of coastal cities within a regional water equity framework. With renewed support, the Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Cities Initiative will continue to advance and expand policies and member priorities across communities.

title: Flint's Got Talent Youth Showcase
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will support WOW Outreach in its efforts to implement the first Flint’s Got Talent Holiday Showcase. The talent showcase idea was generated from the organization’s Youth Ambassador program participants. Youth Ambassadors are young people from the Flint area that are between the ages of 14 and 19 years old and have a reputation for developing quality programs for teens by teens. The showcase will feature 10 area teens and offer live audience voting to select the top act. WOW Outreach will provide assistance to the 10 showcase participants, including performance coaching and referrals to existing programs to further hone their skills and talent.

title: Film Appreciation Academy for Youth
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide funds to iMichigan Productions, Inc. for a film appreciation program for youth in Flint. Working with partners such as Berston Field House and the Flint Public Library, the iMichigan Productions team will develop and implement a curriculum that explores the filmmaking genre. Filmmaking is a complex process and offers a variety of career pathways for those who are interested in the art form or the more technical aspects of the industry, such as sound engineering and editing. This program will explore all facets of filmmaking.

title: National Partnership for Student Success
description: This grant will support the Everyone Graduates Center at Johns Hopkins University to establish a network hub, the National Partnership for Student Success, to provide technical assistance connecting local education agencies with service providers in five, evidence-based service areas for student recovery: 1) academic tutoring; 2) mentoring; 3) post-secondary transition; 4) student success coaching; and 5) wraparound student supports. Launched in July 2022, the National Partnership for Student Success is a cross-agency partnership between the Department of Education and AmeriCorps and aims to recruit 250,000 volunteers over the next three years. The goals of this initiative include increasing the number of school districts implementing these strategies and the number of adult volunteers serving to improve student outcomes.

title: 100th Anniversary Community Celebration
description: This grant provides project support to the United Way of Genesee County, a health and human services organization serving the residents of Genesee County through its community impact areas of education and basic needs. Since 1922, the grantee has provided invaluable assistance and support to the community and has continued to evolve with local needs. The United Way of Genesee County has a number of local activities planned to celebrate its 100th anniversary with the community and this grant will support those activities.

title: Defining Big Trends that Impact the Future of Education
description: The education field has been changed significantly by recent trends, including the COVID-19 pandemic, a national reckoning on race and a once-in-a-generation influx of federal education funding. Understanding how these and other trends may impact instruction and learning is critical to any efforts to transform education systems. This grant will enable Nelson Mullins Riley & Scarborough LLP to identify and frame major trends that could greatly impact education — and efforts to improve educational outcomes — over the next 10-15 years. Planned activities include a literature review, historical reflection, data analyses, as well as interviews and focus groups with thought leaders from different roles and perspectives across the education ecosystem and beyond. Nelson Mullins is a U.S. law firm that has significant consulting experience in policy, strategy, law and advocacy to drive improvements in the U.S. education system.

title: The Water Table
description: The next few years of policy actions, agreements and infrastructure investments in the water sector will profoundly affect the quality of life in the United States for years to come. Philanthropy can — and must — play a more pivotal role in addressing these challenges. The Water Table, a collaborative funder effort housed at the Water Foundation, aims to identify and activate promising water solutions through strategic philanthropic investments in the United States. With support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee will continue to advance strategic water solutions, align and grow water philanthropy and facilitate and expand a learning community of water funders.

title: State Fiscal and Low-Income Initiatives Project
grantee: Center on Budget and Policy Priorities
description: This grant continues support for the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities to expand economic opportunity and eliminate poverty. The grantee is known for its efforts to ensure federal and state governments have adequate resources and prioritize investments in basic needs, education, childcare and healthcare. To accomplish these goals, the grantee will continue: 1) monitoring policy and budget changes to the social safety net; 2) preparing policy briefs and analyses of budget and fiscal policy; 3) supporting and coordinating low-income advocates working at the state and local levels; and 4) providing strategic and technical assistance to state and local policymakers and program administrators overseeing policy and programs affecting low-income families. Located in Washington, D.C., the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities is one of the premier policy research and development institutions in the United States.

title: Expanding CSAs for Educational Success and Lifelong Asset Building
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant provides continuing support for Washington University’s research, communications, policy analysis and technical assistance efforts aimed at advancing children’s savings account strategies at the state and national levels. In the short term, the grantee’s goal is to expand opportunities for all families to save for their children’s education, and in doing so, increase postsecondary education aspirations, access and completion rates, particularly among low-to moderate-income students. Long term, Washington University views children’s savings accounts as a key pillar in a comprehensive effort to embed inclusive and lifelong asset-building opportunities into the fabric of domestic social policy in ways that support educational and financial security goals.

title: General Purposes
description: River Alliance of Wisconsin supports a strong network of local organizations around the state that address threats to Wisconsin’s waters, such as invasive species, pollution and climate change. With previous Mott Foundation support, the grantee helped: 1) build the capacity of local groups to protect water; 2) deliver programs to achieve clean water outcomes; and 3) engage communities to take action for clean water. With renewed funding, River Alliance of Wisconsin will continue to support local watershed groups and create new programs and sustainable water management plans to address urgent water issues in the state and Great Lakes region.

title: New Jersey Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the New Jersey School-Age Child Care Coalition, which coordinates the New Jersey State Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) build a more sustainable and diverse afterschool workforce by providing resources for equitable recruitment, hiring and partnering with state agencies for robust career pathways development; 2) establish a youth advisory board to create engaging opportunities for young people to use their voice, contribute to program design and lead change in afterschool; 3) work with education stakeholders and policymakers to design and implement education recovery funding to help New Jersey youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen resources.

title: General Purposes
description: This renewal grant will provide general purposes support to American Gateways as they work to provide vital immigration legal services to the most vulnerable immigrants in Central Texas and the United States at large. During the previous grant period, the grantee conducted community outreach, provided legal assistance, hosted legal clinics and provided direct legal representation. During the upcoming grant period, the grantee will conduct community outreach and education on immigrants’ rights, provide individualized technical assistance on cases and directly represent individuals in the immigration court system. Founded in 1987, American Gateways provides quality, affordable and trustworthy legal services to the immigrant community in Texas.

title: Building Support for Summer Learning
description: This grant will support the National Summer Learning Association in its efforts to increase access to high-quality summer learning programs across the country. The grantee engages a broad range of 25,000+ leaders of school districts, youth serving government agencies, non-profit and corporate partners from across the country focused on improving the lives of youth. This project will support the grantee to continue to: 1) bring together a network of leaders and organizations promoting and offering summer learning opportunities to youth; 2) build multi-sector partnerships to expand summer learning opportunities for youth; and 3) create special events and high-profile opportunities to raise awareness of the importance of summer learning opportunities for youth.

title: Mizzen Content and Partnership Development
description: This grant will support Learn Fresh to increase access to world-class digital learning curricula through the Mizzen online platform. Specifically, this grant will enable Learn Fresh to: 1) adapt innovative curricula for the out-of-school time field and Mizzen, including NBA Math Hoops; 2) provide professional development opportunities for afterschool educators; and 3) develop and implement a marketing campaign to engage afterschool educators in Mizzen and Learn Fresh curricula.

title: Bretton Woods Project
description: The Bretton Woods Project, an initiative of the preeminent development organization ActionAid, has been a key actor on international financial institution reform issues since it was established in 1995. Over the last two years, with Mott Foundation support, the grantee advocated for better alignment of the World Bank’s climate and energy work with the Paris Agreement as well as greater transparency and accountability on the World Bank’s climate commitments. With this grant, ActionAid will continue to: 1) ensure that the World Bank’s climate commitments are implemented; 2) strengthen civil society engagement with the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund; and 3) remain a highly respected repository of information, analysis and recommendations on World Bank policy and operations.

title: Michigan Radio Transmitter Replacement Project
description: This grant provides funding to the University of Michigan’s Michigan Radio to support replacement and installation of the outdated transmitter that is currently being used for WFUM-FM broadcasts. Michigan Radio’s WFUM-FM is the only public radio station available to Flint area residents and is responsible for providing the community with fair and fact-based news coverage, weather alerts and emergency broadcast notifications. A new transmitter would ensure that Flint area residents have continued free access to a trusted media source for years to come.

title: Program Integration and Enhancement
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant increase will provide additional funds needed to complete the full integration of the programs, staff and systems of The Whiting and the Capitol Theatre into Flint Institute of Music operations. The grantee will work with a team of consultants to develop and implement a branding and marketing campaign, finalize job descriptions and recruitment plans for new positions and design and deliver staff and board training and professional development for the new organizational structure.

title: Diversity in Journalism
description: The Knight Center for Environmental Journalism at Michigan State University (MSU) teaches students to be professional environmental journalists through coursework, conferences and internships at media outlets. With previous Mott Foundation support, the Knight Center developed a project to increase diversity among its environmental journalism students. In the first two years of this project, nine students received scholarships for coursework at MSU, eight received scholarships to attend a professional development conference, and eight students received internships at the U.S.-based media outlets in the Mott-funded Great Lakes News Collaborative. With renewed support, more students from diverse backgrounds will be trained as environmental journalists.

title: General Purposes
description: The purpose of this increase is to support the philanthropic and nonprofit sector’s response to Hurricane Fiona. To this end, Philanthropy Puerto Rico supports, educates and helps strengthen its members, grantees and the sector broadly. During the previous grant period, the grantee advocated on behalf of the nonprofit sector, convened and educated the sector and provided support to nonprofits. During this grant period, the grantee will expand its membership, inform and connect its network and support nonprofits through the Forward Fund. The grantee will accomplish this by organizing third sector disaster recovery and resiliency efforts, catalyzing additional funds for recovery and compiling available resources for individuals and nonprofits. Established in 2009 by seven leading foundations, Philanthropy Puerto Rico exists to enhance the ability of philanthropy and nonprofit organizations to improve the lives of vulnerable populations.

title: Democracy Initiative
description: The program goal is to promote a better understanding of democracy and the importance of civic engagement in the United States. The Associated Press — through the Democracy Initiative — plans to advance election integrity and trust in the system, work with local media to build common ground in their communities and address mis- and disinformation. As a factual, independent and nonpartisan organization with credibility across many constituencies, the grantee will improve civic literacy through deepening its explanatory journalism and assisting smaller newsrooms across the U.S. Founded in 1864, the Associated Press is an independent global news organization dedicated to factual reporting.

title: New Tree Planting
description: The Genesee Conservation District works closely with the city of Flint to maintain the city’s tree canopy. The vitality of a healthy tree canopy requires both the removal of dead and dangerous trees, as well as the planting of new trees. This grant increase will provide funding to increase the planting of new street trees from 250 to 315. The tree planting will take place in all nine wards throughout Flint over the two-year grant period. Trees are essential for the survival of both wildlife and people, and serve as an invaluable community resource.

title: Promise Scholars
description: With this grant, the University of Michigan-Flint will support junior- and senior-level students through the Promise Scholars program. Designed to support students who came to the university after experiencing academic disadvantages in high school, the Promise Scholars program provides stipends, workshops and coaching designed to help students persist and graduate from the university with a four-year degree.

title: Michigan State University Flint Campus Expansion
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant increase will provide additional funding to the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, a supporting organization of the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, for the completion of the construction of a new office and meeting space for Michigan State University’s College of Human Medicine’s Flint campus adjacent to its existing space in the former Flint Journal Building. The additional space will both accommodate the expansion of public health expertise and resources in Flint and contribute to the vibrancy of the Health and Wellness District in downtown Flint.

title: Water Solutions Fund
description: The 2021 bipartisan Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act offers a critical opportunity to address the nation’s backlog of water infrastructure needs while also rethinking how we manage our water resources and systems to advance environmental, health and justice goals. To take advantage of this opportunity, the Water Foundation has launched the Water Solutions Fund, a national pooled fund designed to ensure that implementation of the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act realizes its full promise by focusing on three areas: reforming policy, developing model projects and building nonprofit capacity at the local, state and national levels to effectively influence water infrastructure decision-making. This one-time grant will help capitalize the pooled fund and support its annual operations.

title: African Development Bank Energy Financing
description: Christian Aid, a relief and development agency based in the United Kingdom, has projects across the globe, including in Africa. Over the past eight years of Mott Foundation support, Christian Aid has established and supported a network of more than 50 local civil society partners that continue to influence the policies of the African Development Bank and other multilateral development banks toward better environmental, social and economic safeguard practices and community outcomes. Over the next two years, the grantee will strengthen civil society engagement with the African Development Bank and other multilateral development banks toward a more just approach to financing locally led decentralized sustainable renewable energy solutions in Africa. The grantee will work to reduce investments in fossil fuels while at the same time working to increase investments in renewable energy by the African Development Bank and other multilateral development banks.

title: General Purposes
description: The NGO Forum on ADB works to make the policies and operations of the Asia Development Bank and the Asia Infrastructure and Investment Bank more sustainable, accountable and aligned with the development priorities of local communities in Asia and the Pacific. With Mott Foundation support, the grantee secured significant commitments from both institutions that bring them closer to alignment with the Paris Agreement. Over the next two years, NGO Forum on ADB will: 1) continue its advocacy for complete decarbonization of the two banks’ investment portfolio; 2) lead civil society participation in discussions on the clean energy transition; and 3) build the capacity of its members to constructively engage with Chinese financial institutions.

title: General Purposes
description: For the past 25 years, PennFuture has been a leading statewide organization in Pennsylvania, pushing for environmental progress through legal advocacy, policy engagement and citizen involvement in decision-making. With partial Mott Foundation support over the last two years, much of this work has focused on the goals of clean water, clean air and clean energy. With this grant, PennFuture will pursue similar goals embedded in its new five-year strategic plan, including a strong commitment to work in the Lake Erie watershed out of its office in Erie.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will renew general purposes support to Focus: HOPE, an anti-poverty and civil rights organization that serves residents of Detroit’s Oakman Boulevard neighborhood. Mott Foundation funding will help support the grantee’s core lines of work: 1) workforce development and education; 2) early learning and youth development; and 3) food justice. Cofounded in 1968 by Father William Cunningham and Eleanor Josaitis, Focus: HOPE’s mission is to provide intelligent and practical solutions to overcome racism, poverty and injustice.

title: Community Foundation Development Project
description: The project goal is to strengthen and expand the community foundation field in southern Africa, with a particular focus on South Africa. To achieve this goal, SGS Consulting will consolidate support to community foundation support organizations in select countries in the region. This shift will enable the grantee to expand and deepen its community foundation development efforts in South Africa, building on progress made in the last two years. Additionally, the grantee will engage a diverse group of funding institutions to expose them to the opportunities community foundations provide to achieve community development goals and unlock funding. Past support enabled SGS Consulting to identify initiative groups in three provinces in South Africa, work with them to become community foundations and support regional work in five countries.

title: Travel and Learning Fund
description: The project goal is to advance the Civil Society program’s objectives and outcomes by supporting exchange, networking and interaction among key nonprofits, practitioners and experts, including Mott Foundation grantees, working in the program’s thematic areas of interest. To this end, the Institute of International Education, Inc. will operate a travel and learning fund to support individuals and organizations working on civic space, community philanthropy, access to justice or other areas of interest to the Civil Society program. This increase will accommodate increased demand from the field as the pandemic eases and travel resumes. During the grant period, the grantee will support: 1) participation in study visits and exchanges; 2) engagement in virtual and in-person conferences and other events; and 3) field studies and research projects that result in a report or publication that benefits the field. Based in New York, the Institute of International Education, Inc. manages similar funds for foundations around the world.

title: Cities Building Bridges to Postsecondary Success
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This renewal grant will enable the National League of Cities Institute to continue expanding the overall number and quality of children’s savings account programs in the United States by helping city leaders connect them to existing city and state initiatives that create stronger financial pathways to and through college and support families’ economic security. During this grant period, the grantee will: 1) continue to provide educational, technical assistance and networking opportunities for municipal leaders interested in exploring and/or pursuing savings account initiatives; and 2) continue to assist municipalities across the country. Although the overall scope of this project is nationwide, the grantee will primarily center activities in the southern United States where fewer children’s savings account programs exist. Established in 1958 and located in Washington, D.C., the National League of Cities Institute is a research, education and training affiliate of the National League of Cities.

title: Expanding Entrepreneurial Education
description: Since 2006, Lemonade Day has aimed to prepare youth for life through critical teachings that bridge the gap from home to school and career. Working in over 90 cities in the last 15 years, the grantee has immersed 1.5 million kids into its entrepreneurial and experiential learning journey, earning over $352.5 million in sales, generating $270 million in profit and $142 million in donations. With renewed support, the grantee will continue to expand its programming to reach more youth with its entrepreneurial and whole child social-emotional approach. Specifically, this grant will support the grantee’s reach and impact by: 1) increasing access and opportunity for underserved youth to benefit from a curriculum highlighting business and life skills; 2) offering opportunities for the community to engage in youth entrepreneurship through mentoring, communications and business collaborations; and 3) engaging with the 50 State Afterschool Network in states outside of the grantee’s network. Lemonade Day will also contribute content to Mizzen Education, Inc.

title: General Purposes
description: Founded in 1937, the Michigan United Conservation Clubs engages its grassroots members to conserve, protect and enhance Michigan’s natural resources. With previous Mott Foundation support, the grantee has pursued its mission through four key pillars of activity: advocacy; education; communications; and land stewardship. With renewed support, the Michigan United Conservation Clubs will continue its major programs, including a focus on protecting and restoring the Great Lakes while also building its own organizational strength.

title: Informing State Legislatures: Statewide Afterschool Policy
description: This grant will support the National Conference of State Legislatures in its work to educate state legislators about the benefits of quality afterschool programs and to build capacity to implement comprehensive afterschool and summer learning opportunities. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) conduct ongoing activities to educate legislators on the role of afterschool and summer learning programs in future education systems; 2) serve on a national advisory for the 50 State Network; and 3) work with the Mott Foundation to support future planning efforts to benefit the afterschool sector and the young people it serves.

title: General Purposes
description: Michigan Future, Inc. is a non-partisan, nonprofit organization whose mission is to be a source of new ideas on how Michigan can succeed as a world-class community in a knowledge-driven economy. This grant will support the organization’s efforts to inform the development and advancement of solutions that strengthen the state economy and increase prosperity for all Michigan households, especially asset-limited, income-constrained workers. Activities planned for the two-year grant period include: 1) policy research; 2) policy development; 3) networking and convening; and 4) outreach and advocacy.

title: The Water Table
description: Federal and state governments in the United States are making historic investments in water infrastructure. At the same time, water systems across the country are heavily impacted by climate change. The Water Table funder collaborative, a project of the Water Foundation, addresses these opportunities and challenges by facilitating learning, coordination, and action among funders and partner organizations across the country. With support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee will continue to advance strategic water solutions, align and grow water philanthropy and facilitate and expand a learning community of water funders.

title: Tackling Finance of Gas Expansion in South America
description: 350.org is a global environmental organization founded in the United States in 2008 with a strong presence in South America and a focus on amplifying Indigenous and local voices. During the previous grant period, the grantee mobilized its grassroots network to address the social and environmental impacts of the finance and development of fossil fuel resources in the region. During this grant period, the grantee aims to reduce fossil fuel investments in environmentally sensitive areas of Colombia, Argentina and the Brazilian Amazon by building a strong climate movement across South America. 350.org will support civil society networks and equip frontline communities and climate leaders with the skills to engage with fossil fuel financiers, advocate for clean energy solutions and actively participate in energy transition discussions.

title: Case Management Upgrade and Toll Free Service Expansion Project
description: This project will support the Legal Aid Bureau – Malawi to upgrade its case management system and expand its toll-free helpline. The grantee is the official independent government institution with a mandate of increasing access to justice in Malawi, as found in the Legal Aid Bureau Act 28 of 2010. Established in 2016, the Legal Aid Bureau works in four regional offices and 14 districts in Malawi.

title: Books Before Boxing Afterschool Program
description: This grant will continue to support Driven by Growth, formally named Books Before Boxing — an out-of-school time program operated by Downtown Boxing Gym near downtown Detroit — to provide college and career counseling, one-on-one academic support and mentoring, health and wellness education and a diverse range of enrichment activities to students ages 8 to 18. This project support will enable the grantee to continue to: 1) deliver high-quality out-of-school time programming; 2) expand services that respond to the emergent needs of students; 3) support comprehensive evaluation efforts to understand program outcomes for students; and 4) increase awareness of high-quality program models in Michigan.

title: Flint Center for Educational Excellence Support
description: This grant to Community Foundation of Greater Flint will enable the Flint Center for Educational Excellence to continue to lead a coordinated effort to improve educational opportunities and outcomes for children in Flint. The work of the Flint Center for Educational Excellence reflects the Charles Stewart Mott Foundation’s grantmaking focus on supporting educational opportunities for Flint kids and seamlessly weaves together six initiatives: 1) community education; 2) afterschool programming; 3) the Flint Early Childhood Collaborative; 4) a parent collaborative; 5) a Community Council on Education; and 6) the Network on School Excellence. The Flint Center for Educational Excellence’s catalytic impact on the Flint education ecosystem will enhance how schools and other organizations support Flint kids and families.

title: Berston Field House Capacity Building
description: This grant to the Friends of Berston will build organizational capacity in the areas of fund development, marketing and organizational sustainability. The grantee’s mission is to impact the community through education, athletics, arts and community services. The more than 100-year-old Berston Field House facility hosts a variety of events that bring residents together to celebrate with one another and to connect with programs and resources throughout the community.

title: Berston Field House Capacity Building
description: This grant to the Friends of Berston will build organizational capacity in the areas of fund development, marketing and organizational sustainability. The grantee’s mission is to impact the community through education, athletics, arts and community services. The more than 100-year-old Berston Field House facility hosts a variety of events that bring residents together to celebrate with one another and to connect with programs and resources throughout the community.

title: Great Lakes Water Infrastructure Project
description: Based in Chicago, the Center for Neighborhood Technology collaborates with over 40 community-based organizations committed to serving low-income and communities of color to address water quality, pollution and other environmental issues. With previous Mott Foundation support, the grantee provided technical assistance to cities with water infrastructure challenges to help create sustainable and resilient communities. With renewed support, the Center for Neighborhood Technology will help identify the priorities and build the capacity of its partners by providing resources to advance equitable and sustainable water infrastructure solutions.

title: Ecoright Landscape Mapping
description: Climate change has become a politically polarizing issue in the United States. Fortunately, this is beginning to shift. A small, but growing, network of nonprofit organizations and leaders is working to equip stakeholders with information and ideas to help build durable, bipartisan solutions to climate change. With this grant, DEPLOY/US, a key organization focused on building the ecosystem of nonprofits and leaders working right of center on climate change as a crucial foundation for bipartisan action, will map the landscape and identify pathways to scale the capacity and impact of this field.

title: Food and Agricultural Climate Alliance
description: Scientists estimate that approximately one-third of the greenhouse gas emissions reductions needed by 2030 must come from absorbing climate pollution in forests, wetlands, grasslands and on agricultural land. In 2020, the Environmental Defense Fund — a major national environmental organization — helped convene and launch the Food and Agriculture Climate Alliance, a group of more than 60 agricultural and environmental leaders that promote shared climate policy priorities. With partial support from the Mott Foundation, the Environmental Defense Fund will help build the capacity of the alliance at the state and regional levels.

title: Center for Climate and Trade
description: This grant provides support to the Climate Leadership Council which recently launched the Center for Climate and Trade. This Center is a think-tank to help provide policymakers the intellectual framework, policy analysis and fundamental methodologies to implement effective climate and trade policies. With nearly 25% of all global greenhouse gas emissions embodied in goods traded internationally, the United States is in a position to use climate and trade policy to establish market incentives for exporters to the United States to lower the carbon intensity of their operations. This grant provides support to the Center’s activities, including research and publication, stakeholder convenings and public communications.

title: General Purposes
description: Reducing the risks of climate change is vital to the United State’s long-term economic and national security interests. The Conservative Coalition for Climate Solutions is a relatively new organization and is well-positioned to provide conservative thought leadership in this critical and complex policy arena. Broadly speaking, C3 Solutions promotes a set of policy ideas meant to increase and diversify U.S. energy supplies, accelerate energy innovation, build a resilient and reliable infrastructure and steward healthy environments while expanding economic freedom. The grantee will work to advance these ideas by educating conservative policymakers and other stakeholders, strengthening coalitions of conservative organizations involved in climate and energy conversations and growing C3 Solution’s online news magazine and other public communications, among other activities.

title: Natural Climate Solutions Scoping Project
description: Climate change has become a polarizing issue in the United States. The Niskanen Center, a well-respected centrist think tank based in Washington, D.C., proposes to identify areas of potential bipartisan agreement around natural climate solutions and a broad category of land use practices — including agricultural and forestry — that are beneficial for the climate. The grantee will produce one or more papers describing its findings, including at least one paper for philanthropic leaders identifying high-leverage opportunities to fill funding gaps.

title: General Purposes
description: Two-thirds of all Americans believe we are not doing enough to address climate change, yet there is a lack of bipartisan climate action in the United States. To help address this issue, the American Conservation Coalition was founded in 2017 to be a unifying voice for grassroots conservatives, particularly younger people, who want their leaders to address the climate crisis. General purposes support from the Mott Foundation will help the grantee undertake work in three major areas: 1) growing grassroots support; 2) influencing the media landscape; and 3) educating grasstops stakeholders.

title: Christopher Stallworth Fund
description: The grant will provide funds to the Community Foundation of Greater Flint to transition the Christopher Stallworth Fund from a non-endowed donor-advised fund to an endowed donor-advised fund. The endowment fund will provide support to the Flint community for activities that celebrate Chris’ life and acknowledge the things that he held dear. Examples of projects that could be supported include community gathering and engagement activities, mentoring of young people, entrepreneurship activities and grassroots workforce activities.

title: Documenting Ukraine
description: The Vienna-based Institute for Human Sciences launched the Documenting Ukraine project in March 2022. By the end of February 2023, the grantee had supported more than 200 projects by Ukrainian scholars, creative professionals, journalists, public intellectuals, civil society leaders and archivists. These projects establish a factual record or bring meaning to events related to Russia’s war on Ukraine through artistic interpretation and intellectual reflection. In the next phase of the project, the grantee will provide: 1) an additional 200 grants; 2) oral history and archive development fellowships; 3) non-residential fellowships at the Center for Urban History in Lviv; 4) workshops to focus on the development and maintenance of an archive; and 5) an oral testimony project. Founded in 1982 — as a place for dissenting thinkers of Eastern Europe and prominent scholars from the West to meet in neutral Austria — the Institute for Human Sciences is an institute of advanced studies in the humanities and social sciences.

title: Community Water Lab
description: This grant to the United Way of Genesee County will support the operations of the McKenzie Patrice Croom Flint Community Lab at the Flint Development Center. The lab will be equipped with state-of-the-art technology to test water for multiple contaminants. Scientists and staff of the lab, including youth, will work with residents to collect water samples, test for multiple contaminants, provide results and work with households to address any identified issues.

title: Campus Site Work Improvements
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant increase to the Flint Cultural Center Corporation will provide funds for the lighting and final installation costs of the sculpture along the roundabout on the Flint Cultural Center campus. The previous grant supported the engineering, construction and materials for installation of the 70-foot sculpture, which will be centrally located on the campus. The large-scale work will be visible from Robert T. Longway Blvd. and serve as a visual point of arrival for the campus. The Flint Institute of Arts purchased the sculpture in 2021 for its permanent collection. The grantee has partnered with the Flint Institute of Arts, as well as organizations across the Flint Cultural Center campus, to develop and complete this process.

title: Sandra N. Smithey Fellowship Fund at the Accountability Research Center
description: This grant will enable American University — a major university based in Washington, D.C. — to launch the Sandra N. Smithey Fellowship Fund for Equity and Accountability in International Development. As a former program officer at the Mott Foundation, Sandra Smithey brought a unique combination of rigor and passion for responsive, sustainable and pro-poor development that delivers real benefits to communities, including access to renewable energy and human-centered infrastructure. The Fellowship is designed to reflect these qualities by providing opportunities for advocates from around the world to share their experiences and lessons learned with the development community.

title: Multi-Agency Grants Initiative: Advice Office Regranting Project
description: The project goal is to support community advice offices in South Africa. To this end, the Hlanganisa Institute of Development Southern Africa NPC will support a number of community advice offices in the Free State and KwaZulu-Natal provinces of South Africa. Previous support has allowed the grantee to support this work in the Free State province. The increase will allow it to support advice offices in the KwaZulu-Natal province. Hlanganisa Institute for Development in Southern Africa is a well established nonprofit with a footprint in all provinces of South Africa that supports community organizations.

title: Expanding Educational Opportunities in Michigan
description: Michigan Association of United Ways seeks to establish a public-private partnership initiative to advance afterschool programming for Michigan’s youth and families. The overall goal of this initiative is to ensure that all Michigan youth have access to quality afterschool and summer learning opportunities. Specifically, this initiative will strive to: 1) build needed capacity at the state level in Michigan; 2) implement quality standards and training; 3) develop communications initiatives; and 4) conduct program evaluation to ensure that young people have access to the afterschool programs they need moving forward.

title: Harrison Street Mixed-Use Facility
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: With this grant, the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation will partner with the YMCA of Greater Flint to construct a new mixed-use facility in downtown Flint designed to co-locate affordable housing, a community wellness center and youth education and family programming. The building will include approximately 55,000 square feet for a new YMCA facility and 50 affordable and market-rate apartments. Together, the new facility will increase the vitality and vibrancy of downtown Flint while addressing the housing and wellness needs of Flint and Genesee County residents of all ages.

title: Engaging Older Youth in Service
description: This grant will support America’s Service Commissions to expand youth-service opportunities throughout the U.S. The grantee will provide eight subgrants to state service commissions to develop model youth-service programs, facilitate a learning cohort of state service commission and in- and out-of-school time staff in service learning as a strategy for youth engagement; and support the identification of sustainable funding opportunities for youth programming. Since 2017, America’s Service Commissions has been working with state service commissions and other national partners, including state afterschool networks, to prioritize the development of opportunities to engage youth in service.

title: National Service Fellowship
description: This grant to the STEM Next Opportunity Fund will help support a fellow at AmeriCorps. This fellowship is a public-private partnership initiative geared towards leveraging AmeriCorps to advance high-quality afterschool and summer learning programs. This initiative will: 1) strengthen collaboration between AmeriCorps and the United States Department of Education and other federal agencies to leverage afterschool and summer learning for student recovery; 2) work collaboratively with afterschool and summer learning programs and AmeriCorps to lift up best practices and models for collaboration; and 3) support the development of AmeriCorps programs focused on afterschool and summer learning.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support increased access to justice for poor and marginalized people in Malawi. The Paralegal Advisory Service Institute will do this by providing timely, effective and inclusive justice services. To this end, the grantee will use its network of paralegals and community village mediators to provide justice services in Malawi. Past support allowed the grantee to provide justice services to thousands of people in 29 districts of Malawi. It trained networks of community justice workers to undertake this work, while participating in policy discussions to increase access to justice for everyone in Malawi. The Paralegal Advisory Service Institute was established in 2007 to make justice accessible to all people in Malawi and deploys trained paralegals to provide legal education, advice, and assistance in criminal and civil justice processes.

title: Nonprofit Employment Data Project
description: The project goal is to develop and disseminate reports on U.S. nonprofit employment, wages and finances over time and in relation to other industries. During the previous grant period, George Mason University launched the project, produced annual reports, developed an interactive data dashboard and supported efforts to accelerate the release of data by the U.S. government. During the next two years, the grantee will continue these project activities as well as incorporate additional data systems and explore the creation of a network of federal officials working on nonprofit data. Established in Virginia as an independent university in 1972, George Mason University is an innovative and inclusive academic institution committed to creating a more just, free and prosperous society.

title: General Purposes
description: The purpose of this grant is to help address the long-standing and emerging issues facing migrants in the Americas. Alianza Americas’ mission is to bring about a more inclusive, equitable and sustainable way of life for under-served migrant communities in the United States and across Mexico and Central America. During the previous grant period, the grantee led delegations to international forums, supported transnational coalitions and uplifted the voices of migrants through various media and capacity-building initiatives. During this grant period, the grantee will: 1) strengthen transnational networks; 2) educate policymakers; 3) host delegations; 4) advocate on behalf of migrants; and 5) support its membership. Founded in 2004 by Mexican, Central American and Caribbean migrant leaders, Alianza Americas is a network of over 55 members in 18 states, representing over 150,000 migrant families across the United States, with dozens of organizational partners in Mexico and Central America.

title: Migration and Forced Displacement Program
description: The project goal is to address the new and continued challenges facing migrants throughout the Americas. The Hispanics in Philanthropy Migration and Forced Displacement Program supports frontline organizations, migrant leaders, and a broad ecosystem of funders, nonprofits and civil society organizations that address issues migrant communities face as they settle into new environments. During the previous grant period, the grantee served migrants through regranting to grassroots migrant-serving organizations, narrative change around migration, funder education activities, and capacity and network-building support services. During this grant period, the grantee will expand donor awareness on migration issues while building stronger networks that facilitate collaboration and a positive narrative around migrants through an intersectional lens. Founded in 1981, the grantee is the leading philanthropic membership organization for grantmaking in Hispanic and Latino communities. Hispanics in Philanthropy works across the Americas to strengthen Latino leadership, equity and voice by facilitating greater philanthropic investments in Latino communities.

title: Mott Youth Entrepreneurship Fellows Program
description: The Hopewell Fund specializes in helping donors, social entrepreneurs and changemakers launch new, innovative social change projects. The grantee provides fiscal sponsorship and project incubation services that enable donors to execute their visions. During this grant period, the Hopewell Fund will serve as the fiscal sponsor for the NextGen Chamber of Commerce in an effort to encourage and empower the entrepreneurially eager youth population in Genesee County. The Next Gen Youth Entrepreneurship Initiative and Entrepreneurship Forum will occur over two years, to continue the work of ongoing partnerships and implement new program features, including a statewide youth entrepreneurship study, a scholarship for youth entrepreneurs and an entrepreneurship forum hosted in Genesee County for 2023 and 2024.

title: Entrepreneurship Community of Practice
description: Community Initiatives is a dedicated fiscal sponsor whose sole purpose is to provide best-in-class infrastructure for nonprofit leaders. For 25 years, the grantee has supported nonprofits in their efforts to achieve results with their endeavors. Community Initiatives will serve as the fiscal sponsor for the Entrepreneurship Funders Network. This grant will allow the Entrepreneurship Funders Network to: 1) convene philanthropic funders to examine the field of youth entrepreneurship; 2) seek, share and build knowledge about how best to impact the field; and 3) explore the possibility and potential of collaborative action.

title: Michigan Communities for Financial Empowerment Network
grantee: Community Economic Development Association of Michigan
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: The Community Economic Development Association of Michigan works to expand and strengthen financial security in communities across the state. Since 2011, the Mott Foundation has supported the grantee’s efforts coordinating statewide engagement and education activities that increase awareness and support for Children’s Savings Accounts. With this grant, the Community Economic Development Association of Michigan will continue to support the development of existing and emerging programs by deploying statewide data and account management infrastructure, communicating field impact, activating champions and providing technical assistance. This proposed project scope will: 1) remove barriers from communities hoping to start their own programs; 2) encourage statewide investment into the field; and 3) help local programs meet their community’s needs more efficiently and equitably — making postsecondary education and career training more accessible and believable for all students.

title: General Purposes
description: The project goal is to increase access to justice services in Rwanda. To this end, the Legal Aid Forum will continue implementing its justice services through paralegals, lawyers and its network of legal service providers. The grantee will conduct training for paralegals, hold legal aid clinics, prioritize the implementation of Rwanda’s Alternative Dispute Resolution Policy, and strengthen its technology to provide justice services. Past support has helped the grantee to provide justice services to over 12,000 people, while training over 1,000 community paralegals. The Legal Aid Forum also undertook research on the Rwandan government’s implementation of the United Nations Universal Periodic Review recommendations. Additionally, the grantee was instrumental in launching Rwanda’s first Alternative Dispute Resolution Center. The Legal Aid Forum was established in 2006 with a mission to provide and promote equitable access to justice for indigent and vulnerable persons in Rwanda.

title: South America Small Grants Program
description: The Socio-Environmental Fund CASA provides small grants and capacity-building support to strengthen community organizations facing threats posed by development projects supported by international financial institutions. Over the past grant period, CASA supported twenty grassroots organizations with subgrants and other measures while also contributing to the growth of the Southern Funds Alliance, a regional network of small grant funds. The renewal will allow CASA to continue to provide support to up to 20 local community organizations in Brazil focused on energy infrastructure and sustainable finance. CASA will also document and broadly share lessons learned from its decades of work.

title: Uniting Great Lakes Science, Data and Journalism
description: Circle of Blue is an online magazine that covers water issues around the world and in the Great Lakes basin, as a partner in the Great Lakes News Collaborative (GLNC). The grantee’s staff includes experienced and award-winning journalists who produce original, in-depth investigative reporting and multimedia news stories on drinking water, climate impacts and other critical issues threatening the Great Lakes. Circle of Blue’s expertise on water policy enhances the GLNC’s capacity to explore and explain complex water issues that intersect climate, agriculture, health, energy and politics. The grantee also provides water expertise, leadership and project management services that strengthen the GLNC. With renewed support, Circle of Blue will continue to support the collaborative with in-depth reporting and photojournalism, project management services, cultivation of the next generation of reporters through internships, and heightened public awareness concerning Great Lakes water issues.

title: Afterschool Education and Outreach Project
description: This grant will enable Collaborative Communications Group to continue to support the 50 State Afterschool Network and the afterschool field in the areas of policy analysis, communications and research. To advance afterschool programs, this project will: 1) build bridges between local, state and federal governments and the afterschool field; and 2) assist the networks as they navigate the American Rescue Plan funding and the potential fiscal cliff, and state and local education policies impacting afterschool programs.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Wisconsin, Pennsylvania, Ohio, New York, Indiana, Minnesota, Illinois, Michigan
description: For more than 45 years, the Northeast-Midwest Institute has provided research, data, policy analysis and education to inform state and federal policy reforms and programs, with an emphasis on the Great Lakes. With previous Mott Foundation support, the grantee made progress on several initiatives related to issues such as harmful algal blooms and invasive species, helping to improve the economic and environmental conditions in the region. With renewed support, the Northeast-Midwest Institute will continue to engage in policy education and coalition building to deliver on its initiatives and programs for the benefit of the region.

title: Afterschool Youth Entrepreneurship Initiative
description: This grant increase will provide additional funds to the University of Hawaii for the Hawaii Statewide Afterschool Network to enable the network to expand access for youth to learn about and experience entrepreneurship in afterschool and summer programs.

title: General Purposes
description: The Michigan Environmental Council is a coalition of 100 leading environmental and conservation organizations in Michigan. Since the 1980s, the grantee has positioned itself as a champion for securing lasting protections for Michigan’s air, water, land and natural resources, as well as the human livelihoods that depend on them. This grant will enable the grantee to advance water protections and climate change solutions in Michigan and the broader Great Lakes region and strengthen the Michigan Environmental Council’s internal capacity to effectively serve its growing membership and the environmental conservation movement in Michigan.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Citizens Campaign Fund for the Environment
description: With over 120,000 members, the New York-based Citizens Campaign Fund for the Environment, is one of the largest grassroots environmental organizations in the state. Founded in 1985, the grantee conducts research, educates the public and supports policies that protect the environment from ongoing threats to clean water, clean air and healthy communities. With previous Mott Foundation support, the grantee connected community priorities to environmental policy decisions at the state level through coalitions and consensus building. With renewed funding, the Citizens Campaign Fund for the Environment will lead a range of statewide education initiatives, including those that protect and benefit the Great Lakes and the people who reside in the region.

title: Coalition for Human Rights in Development Community Resource Exchange
description: The Coalition for Human Rights in Development is a global network of nongovernmental organizations — housed at Social and Environmental Entrepreneurs — working to mitigate the social and environmental impacts of large-scale infrastructure and energy finance. This grant will support the second phase development of the Community Resource Exchange to build the capacity of and connect talented professionals and organizations to share skills, tools and resources with and among communities seeking to defend their rights in the context of development investments. Over time, the collective capacity and evidence base developed by the exchange will help to transform development finance and the international investments system to be more responsive to community needs and environmental sustainability.

title: Monitoring Hydropower Impacts in the Amazon
description: The Getulio Vargas Foundation’s Center for Sustainability Studies is a higher education institution dedicated to promoting sustainable development in Brazil. Over the past grant period, the grantee worked with civil society organizations and universities in the Amazon to develop the Independent Territorial Monitoring Network and almost doubled the membership to 50 organizations. Over the next project period, the grantee will continue to strengthen the network and its efforts to monitor pubic investment by the Brazilian Development Bank to decarbonize and accelerate growth in the Amazon.

title: Strengthening BNDES Accountability
description: Conectas is a Brazilian nongovernmental agency, founded in 2001, working on strengthening social and environmental governance and accountability of development finance institutions. Over the past grant period, the grantee worked to ensure the Brazilian Development Bank, the New Development Bank and the Inter-American Development Bank strengthen and comply with social and environmental safeguards and climate commitments. The grantee’s attorneys also worked with communities impacted by large-scale energy finance and development. Over the next project period, Conectas will continue its focus on national and international financial institutions and will deepen its analysis and communication of the impacts of Chinese development finance in the region.

title: Growing Role of Brazil in Latin America
description: This project, operated by IPS-Inter Press Service aims to increase the quality and quantity of journalistic coverage of energy and infrastructure development and finance in Brazil and South America. Since this project began in 2010, the grantee has mentored a network of 14 journalists and published a total of 488 articles and 50 videos covering the impacts of large-scale development and finance on communities and the environment. The reporting has tracked the gradual transition over time to more environmentally and socially sustainable development in light of climate change and its impacts. With renewed support, the grantee will continue to examine energy finance and development in South America through articles and videos. IPS-Inter Press Service is a global news agency operating in more than 100 countries and working in Latin America for more than 50 years with a network of journalists reporting from many countries in the region.

title: Public Safety Support
description: This grant will provide funds to Genesee County in support of the Office of Genesee County Sheriff to increase patrols and responses to crime occurring in the greater downtown Flint area. The Office of Genesee County Sheriff cooperates with law enforcement across the community to proactively prevent crime and to respond when crime occurs. This grant will support additional sergeants and deputies assigned to the area who respond to 911 calls and provide a presence at special events and other large gatherings.

title: National Urban League & Afterschool Initiative
description: This grant will support the National Urban League to work in partnership with the afterschool field to increase access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people, particularly youth from marginalized communities. Specifically, this project will support the National Urban League and Afterschool Initiative which seeks to: 1) increase recruitment and retention of afterschool educators through expanded professional development supports; 2) work with the 50 State Network to increase training for afterschool educators in the areas of cultural competence, equity and youth voice; and 3) develop recommendations for increasing equitable education opportunities in the afterschool sector. The National Urban League’s Equity and Education Project will work closely with the 50 State Network and other afterschool leaders to share new trainings, exemplary models and best practices across the country.

title: Daybreak Fund
description: The Windward Fund serves as a host organization for initiatives that address environmental issues through innovative solutions. The Daybreak Fund — a project of the Windward Fund — is designed to promote nature-based climate solutions in the Lake Michigan region. Daybreak Fund provides grants to community-based organizations for sustainable on-the-ground approaches to improve environmental conditions in their communities. These grants support innovative projects and partnerships that address climate change, water quality and social equity. The Mott Foundation is contributing to the larger fund along with other donors from around the basin.

title: Property Acquisition and Renovation - 701 MLK
description: Communities First Inc. will purchase the property at 701 Martin Luther King Avenue and renovate it for future retail use. The property is currently abandoned and in danger of becoming blighted. This purchase and renovation will lead to neighborhood redevelopment and restabilization.

title: Property Acquisition and Demolition - 517/523 MLK
description: Communities First Inc. will purchase the properties at 517 and 523 Martin Luther King Avenue and hold them for future development opportunities. One of the properties is abandoned and in danger of becoming blighted and the other is expected to become vacant in the near future. This purchase will lead to neighborhood redevelopment and restabilization.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant increase will support and expand the field of community foundations in Mexico. Comunalia is an alliance of Mexican community foundations that focuses on local development and strategic social investment. Founded in 2011, the grantee currently has 17 members and six associated groups. The grantee’s activities include: 1) annual surveying of financial and operating characteristics and capacity-building needs; 2) webinars and workshops on issues of common interest; 3) implementation assistance for programming related to community resilience, the Sustainable Development Goals, giving circles and youth philanthropy; 4) technical assistance and training for legal and fiscal compliance, strengthening governance, fundraising, donor relations and other managerial challenges; 5) networking and peer learning support; 6) challenge grants to stimulate local and national giving; and 7) support to newly emerging community foundations in Mexico. This grant increase will provide support for a visit of civic and community leaders from Argentina that will share findings and reflect on key learnings of Comunalia’s experiences in community philanthropy. The Argentinian group will visit four Mexican community foundations and participate in a gathering of community foundations from South and North America in Guadalajara.

title: Connect Humanity: Expansion to Latin America
description: The project goal is to enhance civic space by bridging the digital divide and increasing digital equity in Latin America. Connect Humanity is a nonprofit impact fund established in 2021 and registered in the state of California as a 501(c)(3) organization. After successful research into Brazil’s internet infrastructure and training of small internet service providers, the grantee seeks to further its programming in the country toward international expansion. During the grant period, the grantee will grow existing initiatives by training representatives of community-focused internet service providers on investment readiness. As part of its capacity development, the grantee will hire an investment manager to deliver a landscape analysis and case study report on successful development finance investment mechanisms and models from other sectors, including climate finance. To maximize its impact, Connect Humanity will strengthen relationships with the private sector and governmental agencies and advocate for an enabling regulatory environment conducive to the needs of small internet service providers and the communities they serve.

title: Budgeting and Accelerating People Centered Justice
geographic_focus: Southeastern Asia, Asia, Middle Africa, Eastern Africa
description: ODI will consolidate research into people-centered justice reforms in lower-income countries in order to identify learning, scaling and financing opportunities. Drawing on extensive research carried out to this point, the grantee will work to systematize available information for funders and policy makers to support clearer understanding of justice funding choices. Particular attention will be given to cost effectiveness and financing needs for adaptation and scaling of successful reforms. From 2021-23, the grantee carried out detailed investigations of justice delivery in over a dozen countries in Africa and Asia. The grantee produced three substantial research reports on its findings and held numerous roundtable discussions with donors and policy makers on its findings. Its work helped to clarify understanding of broad range of justice funding mechanisms and opportunities that are in current operation. Established in 1960 and based in the United Kingdom, ODI works to inspire people to act on injustice and inequality through research, convening and advocacy.

title: Advancing Decriminalization of Poverty and Status
description: The International Legal Foundation will work together with diverse stakeholders to introduce common standards in the administration of justice aimed at decriminalizing poverty and status. Together with United Nations member states, civil society justice actors, academics and others, the grantee will help convene, coordinate and communicate about an expert group tasked with developing justice policy reform standards that aim to reduce or eliminate discriminatory practices in the enforcement of the law. These standards will be introduced for review and adoption by relevant United Nations bodies, including the U.N. Human Rights Council and the Commission on Crime Prevention and Criminal Justice. Founded in 2001, the International Legal Foundation works to address the global crisis in access to justice through improvements to legal aid provision and related policies. The grantee works both in specific countries in Africa and Asia, while also advocating for policy change globally.

title: Support for U.N. Special Rapporteur on the Independence of Judges and Lawyers
description: This grant will support the work of the U.N. Special Rapporteur on the independence of judges and lawyers. The Rapporteur is an independent human rights expert appointed by the U.N. Human Rights Council with a broad global mandate focused on human rights issues relating to judicial systems and the legal profession. Over the course of their three-year term, the Rapporteur will focus on highlighting legal empowerment as an important strategy for buttressing the independence of judges and lawyers, and for improving access to justice more widely for marginalized and vulnerable groups.

title: Developing an Achievable Strategic Vision for Access to Justice in South Africa Research Project
description: The project goal is to inform a strategic vision on realizing the right to access justice for people in South Africa. To this end, the Foundation for Human Rights will undertake research on how people access justice in South Africa. Additionally, the foundation will host consultative meetings to inform, disseminate and enact the research findings. These activities will involve key stakeholders, including community advice offices, local development agencies, university legal aid clinics, nonprofit organizations, Legal Aid South Africa and South Africa’s Department of Justice and Constitutional Development. The Foundation for Human Rights was established in 1996 by the European Union and the Government of South Africa to address the historical legacy of apartheid and to promote and advance human rights based on South Africa’s Constitution.

title: General Purposes
description: The National Center for Family Philanthropy provides resources, expertise and support to families in order to transform their values into effective giving that makes a lasting impact on the communities they serve. During the previous grant period, the grantee hosted the National Forum on Family Philanthropy, produced knowledge resources and increased its staff capacity. During this grant period, the grantee will provide educational opportunities, host networking events and create and update resources in its Knowledge Center. Founded in 1997, the National Center for Family Philanthropy is the only national nonprofit dedicated exclusively to families who give and those who work with them.

title: JUST Ukraine: Empowering Communities for Access to Justice
description: Right to Protection will provide a range of legal support and services to internally displaced persons and other persons affected by conflict as a result of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. Working across 22 regions of the country, the grantee will undertake continuous research into legal and related needs of displaced populations. It will provide responsive legal information, assistance, and where appropriate, litigation to ensure justice needs are met. Additionally, it will work to address systemic legal issues that may act as barriers to conflict affected groups securing their rights.

title: Building an Inclusive Financial Ecosystem for End Users and Enterprises
description: The Global Fund for Community Foundations is a grantmaking organization that supports grassroot organizations. In partnership with the Tanzania Association of Microfinance Institutions, the grantee has over the last four years engaged 40 micro-finance institutions to develop and expand financial products for distributed renewable energy solutions in Tanzania. In the next year, the Global Fund for Community Foundations will further strengthen the capacity of micro-finance institutions to provide better financial services for the productive use of solar energy services in rural Tanzania.

title: Sustainable Energy for All
description: The COVID-19 pandemic has significantly slowed progress toward achieving universal access to sustainable energy services by 2030 — Sustainable Development Goal 7. Efforts need to be redoubled based on comprehensive and reliable information. This project is led by the United Nations Foundation and supports the United Nations Sustainable Energy for All initiative to collect and synthesize key sustainable energy finance trends to inform decision making. Over the last two years, the grantee has completed several analytical studies and knowledge briefs to track trends in financial flows in support of sustainable energy access. Over the next year, the United Nations Foundation will build upon this work and extend its outreach efforts to enable better decision-making to increase the availability of sustainable energy choices.

title: DREEM Hub Tanzania
description: The World Wildlife Fund has supported environmental conservation work in Tanzania for the past 60 years, including initiatives that advance access to productive use of renewable energy services. This project supports the World Wildlife Fund to accelerate access to the productive use of solar energy services across two agricultural value chains. The organization will achieve this goal by establishing a centralized coordinating hub to support access to distributed renewable energy services for productive use at its Tanzania office. The hub will support a strong network of partner organizations, which will, in turn, facilitate better access to solar technical skills, local solar enterprise development and financial services. The lessons learned from this model will help influence the sustainable energy access field and inform related public policy with the aim of reducing greenhouse gas emissions, improving climate adaptation strategies, creating jobs and incomes as well as enabling more climate resilient livelihoods among participating local communities in Tanzania.

title: Improving Strategic Communications and Public Engagement on Off-Grid Renewable Energy Solutions in East Africa
description: The lack of strong strategic communications, media and public engagement on distributed renewable energy services is one of the major barriers to the achievement of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 7 on universal access to modern energy services by 2030. The African Centre for Media Excellence has been working to address this challenge. Established and led by local media practitioners nearly 15 years ago, the grantee is a nonprofit media support organization that has contributed significantly towards a more vibrant, free and skilled media fraternity so that the media can more effectively inform local African communities to engage their leaders on sustainable development matters in several East African countries. With this grant, the grantee will improve public awareness and engagement on the adoption and use of distributed renewable energy solutions in the agricultural sector across Tanzania, Kenya and Uganda. In addition, the African Centre for Media Excellence will monitor key trends and provide recommendations to media practitioners on improving the public narrative and perception of distributed renewable energy solutions and work to enhance the capacity of the media fraternity in the region to report on distributed renewable energy and agricultural development issues.

title: Scaling Africa's Distributed Renewable Energy Ecosystem Model through Social Entrepreneurship
description: A resilient, active and well-networked community of local social entrepreneurs is needed to facilitate accelerated access to distributed renewable energy services to achieve the United Nations Sustainable Development Goal 7 on universal access to modern energy services by 2030. Since 1981, Ashoka has pioneered a systematic process of building such a network. With this grant, the grantee will comprehensively map and support 12-15 high-potential social entrepreneurs to deploy distributed renewable energy solutions in specific agricultural value chains. Ashoka will also award fellowships to support the long-term engagement of two exceptional African social entrepreneurs working on various aspects of distributed renewable energy services within East Africa.

title: Connecting the Afterschool and Teacher Pipeline(s) in Michigan
grantee: Berrien County Regional Educational Service Agency
description: The purpose of this project is to develop and pilot a high-quality, streamlined and cost-effective teacher certification pathway for afterschool professionals. Mott Foundation funds will support program design and implementation activities as well as research, including interviews with potential providers and participants. This project will be implemented in collaboration with the Michigan Educator Workforce Initiative, a statewide effort to strengthen and grow Michigan’s educator talent pipeline. The Berrien Regional Education Service Agency is Michigan Educator Workforce Initiative’s fiscal sponsor.

title: Neighborhood Public Safety Projects
description: This grant will support public safety projects through the Neighborhood Small Grants Program at the Community Foundation of Greater Flint. Neighborhood groups will implement resident-led efforts to create or enhance and expand existing public safety projects or events. Funded projects will aim to stimulate civic engagement, improve neighborhood conditions and provide opportunities for residents to address crime prevention and reduction strategies.

title: Emergency Operating Funds
description: The purpose of the Flint Downtown Development Authority is to address and prevent deterioration, encourage historical preservation, create and implement development plans, promote economic growth and redevelopment and encourage the expansion of commercial enterprises, all within the downtown district boundaries. This grant will provide operating funds to the Flint Downtown Development Authority and is needed as a result of a decrease in parking revenue, which is a significant source of funding for the organization.

title: Sloan Exhibits Project
grantee: Flint Institute of Science and History
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant for the Sloan Museum of Discovery will provide funds for exhibit enhancements, including augmented reality features and additional exhibits in the newly renovated museum. The museum opened to the public in July 2022 despite the challenges of COVID-19 and increasing supply and labor costs. This grant will support new features throughout the exhibit galleries, incorporate additional immersive experiences and complete important educational materials that accompany the exhibits.

title: Early Childhood Implementation
