description: This grant will provide funding to the Flint Center for Educational Excellence to lead the expansion of early childhood education in Flint. This effort will be supported through the Flint Early Childhood Collaborative, which aims to increase access to and the quality of early childhood education in Flint through strategic planning, research, advocacy and participation in the Educare Learning Network.

title: Flint Center for Educational Excellence Technical Assistance
description: The Flint Center for Educational Excellence — an affiliated entity of the Community Foundation of Greater Flint — will lead and coordinate six cooperative efforts. Three current initiatives, Flint Early Childhood Collaborative, the community education initiative and afterschool programming will be strategically aligned with three new initiatives, a parent collaborative, the Community Council on Education and the Network for School Excellence. The Community Foundation of Greater Flint will contract with national technical assistance providers to guide implementation of each initiative. Best and promising practices will be shared in the community to leverage innovation with the goal of helping Flint kids thrive.

title: Flint Center for Educational Excellence Technical Assistance
description: The Flint Center for Educational Excellence, an affiliated entity of the Community Foundation of Greater Flint, will lead and coordinate six cooperative efforts. Three current initiatives — the Flint Early Childhood Collaborative, community education initiative and afterschool programming — will be strategically aligned with three new initiatives — a parent collaborative, the Community Council on Education and the Network for School Excellence. The Community Foundation of Greater Flint will contract with national technical assistance providers to guide the implementation of each initiative. Best and promising practices will be shared in the community to leverage innovation with the goal of helping Flint kids thrive.

title: Operating Support
description: With this grant, the Flint Center for Educational Excellence will continue its efforts to improve educational opportunities and outcomes for Flint kids. The organization pursues this goal through the operation of six initiatives: community education, afterschool programming, the Flint Early Childhood Collaborative, the Network for School Excellence, the Flint Parent Collaborative and the Community Council on Education. In addition to these core initiatives, focus areas during its first year as an independent organization will include strategic leadership in local and state conversations about education, operational and financial oversight, board relations, and community stakeholder relations.

title: Community Education and Afterschool
description: The Flint Center for Educational Excellence — an affiliated entity of the Community Foundation of Greater Flint — will deliver a full-service community education strategy in 14 Flint area schools. The focus for the newly established Flint Center for Educational Excellence in its first year is to integrate community education and afterschool initiatives, which previously were provided by two separate organizations, into a seamless model. The new model will include afterschool programming, adult education, health services, early childhood education connections and parent and community engagement. Best and promising practices from demonstration sites will be shared with other schools in the community to leverage innovation with the goal of helping Flint kids thrive.

title: Community Education and Afterschool
description: The Community Foundation of Greater Flint — through the Flint Center for Educational Excellence — will deliver a full-service community education strategy in 14 Flint area schools. The model will include: 1) afterschool programming; 2) adult education; 3) early childhood education connections; and 4) parent and community engagement. Best and promising practices from demonstration sites will be shared with other schools in the community to leverage innovation with the goal of helping Flint kids thrive.

title: Community Education and Afterschool
description: With this grant, the Flint Center for Educational Excellence will lead community education in 17 Flint area schools. As part of a comprehensive community education model, afterschool programming will be offered in all schools except for the two early childhood education centers. This year will bring a focus on providing high-quality programming in all sites, expanding into early childhood education, improving enrollment systems, and developing and scaling innovation through diverse funding streams.

title: General Purposes
description: This renewal grant will provide support for the Flint Regional Science & Engineering Fair, a volunteer-led organization that provides students in an eight-county area the opportunity to develop their scientific and engineering talents. The fair was founded in 1956 as part of the Mott Foundation-funded community education program of Flint Community Schools and remains an important component of students’ scientific exploration today.

title: Mariachi Music & Folklorico Dance Instruction
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to El Ballet Folklorico Estudiantil will support mariachi music and folklorico dance cultural education and instruction in Flint. The majority of participants are Hispanic; however, the program is open to all interested young people. Program participants showcase their talent and newly acquired skills at community events and concerts. Classes take place at the Latinx Technology and Community Center. The program fee is extremely low and does not cover the full cost of staffing. This grant will help ensure continued high-quality instruction and access for any child who wishes to participate, regardless of ability to pay.

title: Mariachi Music & Folklorico Dance Instruction
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to El Ballet Folklórico Estudiantil will support mariachi music and folkloric dance education and instruction in Flint. The majority of participants are Hispanic; however, the program is open to all interested young people. Program participants showcase their talent and newly acquired skills at community events and concerts. Classes take place at the Latinx Technology and Community Center. The program fee is extremely low and does not cover the full cost of staffing. This grant will help ensure continued high-quality instruction and access for any child who wishes to participate, regardless of ability to pay.

title: Arts Programming at Genesee Valley Regional Center
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide support for arts-based workshops to young people living at the Genesee Valley Regional Center, a youth detention facility in Genesee County. The Youth Arts Unlocked program has offered workshops at the center since 2011. The program uses a research-based, trauma-informed curriculum to deliver visual arts, dance, poetry, yoga and theater to boys and girls living at the facility.

title: Arts Programming at Genesee County Juvenile Justice Center
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide support for arts-based workshops to young people living at the Genesee County Juvenile Justice Center, a youth detention facility in Genesee County. The Youth Arts: Unlocked program has offered workshops at the center since 2011. The program uses a research-based, trauma-informed curriculum to deliver visual arts, dance, poetry, yoga and theater to boys and girls living at the facility.

title: Michigan Spark Grant Partnership
description: The Council of Michigan Foundations leads, strengthens and supports Michigan’s philanthropy community, grounded in a shared commitment to center equity in grantmaking. This grant from the Mott Foundation will support a new partnership between the Department of Natural Resources and Michigan philanthropy to equitably distribute Michigan Spark grants. The Spark grant program was launched to increase the quantity and improve the quality of outdoor spaces in communities where they are lacking. The Council of Michigan Foundations, on behalf of its members, will administer up to $27.5 million and additional private sector support to create or restore public outdoor recreation facilities, increase access to greenspace and develop programming for historically under-funded, low-capacity communities that have limited resources.

title: Local Journalism Support
description: This grant to the United Way of Genesee County will provide operating support for Flintside and Flint Beat, two community-based journalism outlets. Flintside and Flint Beat cover news across the city. Both outlets offer an online publication that focuses on information and stories that highlight important community issues that impact Flint residents. While the editorial teams continue to operate independently, the two media outlets have come together to consolidate back-office operations to create more administrative efficiencies and opportunities for staff recruitment and fundraising.

title: Mott Youth Entrepreneurship Fellows Program
description: The Hopewell Fund and its partner organizations seek to encourage and empower the Genesee County youth population by continuing youth entrepreneurship programs. These programs include the Next Gen Youth Entrepreneurship Summit and the formalized expansion of a year-long Youth Entrepreneurship Fellowship. During this grant period, the grantee will serve as the fiscal sponsor for the NextGen Chamber of Commerce to offer youth and community members ongoing access to a unique, hands-on avenue for entrepreneurial education, skill development and opportunities with lasting benefits for years to come.

title: Entrepreneurship Community of Practice
description: Community Initiatives is a dedicated fiscal sponsor providing best in class infrastructure for nonprofit leaders. For nearly 30 years, the grantee has supported nonprofits in their efforts to achieve results. Community Initiatives will serve as the fiscal sponsor for the Entrepreneurship Funders Network. This grant will allow the grantee to: 1) convene philanthropic funders to examine the field of youth entrepreneurship; 2) seek, share and build knowledge about how best to impact the field; and 3) explore the potential of collaborative action.

title: Youth Entrepreneurship Curriculum for Afterschool Programs
description: This grant to VentureLab will continue to support the expansion and promotion of entrepreneurship education opportunities for youth. This project aims to reflect the growth of entrepreneurship education in the afterschool field. Since 2017, the grantee has provided training to educators and youth, technical assistance and professional development resources to educational communities, specifically afterschool programs. With its engagement, the grantee works with its partners to increase the number of afterschool programs offering high-quality entrepreneurship education programming, further increasing the number of youths who have opportunities to develop entrepreneurial skills and mindsets. During this grant period, VentureLab will continue its youth entrepreneurship capacity and ecosystem building for the afterschool field, including meeting and growing the demand for youth entrepreneurship programing.

title: Genesee Youth Entrepreneurship Network
description: The Genesee Intermediate School District provides educational leadership that impacts instruction, learning, student achievement, productivity and efficiency. The grantee serves nearly 70,000 students and 8,500 educators across the county. This grant will enable the grantee to continue to cultivate an innovative mindset and instill a lasting appreciation for the importance of entrepreneurship among Genesee County teens in grades 9-12. The main goal of this youth entrepreneurship program offers support to high school faculty advisors, who give youth the chance to explore their entrepreneurial ideas, enhance key skills, and gain hands-on experience in creating and presenting business plans, pitches and prototypes.

title: Detection and Protection for Environmental Defenders
description: The Franciscan Solidarity Service is a Catholic association based in Brazil that began working in 2018 on strategies to protect environmental defenders in the Brazilian Amazon. During the past grant period, the grantee helped create a network of community-led territorial funds in the Amazon and contributed to developing a national environmental defenders program. In the next grant period, the organization will monitor the implementation of the national program and will continue to strengthen the capacity of its network to support Indigenous and traditional community funds.

title: Program on Philanthropy and Social Innovation
description: The goal of the grant is to support, inform and maximize the impact of philanthropists, social investors and those they support through the Aspen Institute’s Program on Philanthropy and Social Innovation. During the previous grant period, the grantee: 1) hosted the Aspen Philanthropy Group — a group of foundation chief executives and select strategic advisors; 2) convened the Seminar for Mid-America Foundation CEOs; 3) developed philanthropic leaders; and 4) convened and supported the Nonprofit Data Working Group. During the upcoming grant period, the grantee will focus on advancing philanthropy by hosting summits, advancing nonprofit data and developing philanthropic and nonprofit leaders. Established in 1949, Aspen Institute is a leading U.S. think tank with an international network of partners that fosters values-based leadership and provides a neutral and balanced venue for discussing and acting on critical issues.

title: General Purposes
description: The International Energy Initiative Brasil is an independent, nongovernmental organization founded by sustainable energy development experts in 1991. The grantee’s mission is to promote, initiate, strengthen and advance the efficient production and use of energy for sustainable development. This grant increase is available for the general purposes of the organization, including work to develop an event in the Amazon on clean, renewable energy access for remote communities and to strengthen the organization to become a leader in promoting a just and equitable energy transition.

title: Tribal Nations Conservation Pledge and Funding Collaborative
geographic_focus: Illinois, Minnesota, Michigan, Indiana, Ohio, Wisconsin
description: Founded in 1990, Native Americans in Philanthropy promotes effective and equitable philanthropy in Native communities and is dedicated to connecting philanthropy, federal agencies and Tribal Nations to distribute funding and resources directly to Tribal Nations. A newly created Tribal Nations Conservation Pledge and Funding Collaborative seeks to address the negative impacts of climate change and other threats to the nation’s lands and waterways that disproportionately affect Indigenous peoples. The Pledge and Fund help Tribes gain critical resources to overcome barriers and implement projects using their traditional ecological knowledge to protect and conserve natural resources. This grant from the Mott Foundation will support an assessment and planning in the Great Lakes region to build capacity, provide technical assistance and align funding opportunities for Great Lakes Tribes. Funds regranted to Great Lakes Tribes will leverage resources for projects to protect freshwater ecosystems in the basin on Tribal lands or ceded territories while also protecting the vulnerable people who live there.

title: Great Lakes Leadership Summit
grantee: Conference of Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Governors and Premiers
geographic_focus: New York, Illinois, Indiana, Ohio, Minnesota, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Michigan
description: The Conference of Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Governors and Premiers provides a platform for the chief executives of the eight Great Lakes states and two Canadian provinces to convene and help advance protection and encourage sustainable development of the region. With support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee will host a leadership summit in Quebec City, Canada, which will serve as a launching pad for critical projects that benefit the environment and citizens in the region. Held every two years, the summit brings together hundreds of leaders to focus on the most important issues facing the Great Lakes and sets an agenda for moving forward. The most recent summit, held in Cleveland and also supported by the Mott Foundation, yielded many beneficial initiatives including a regional forestation program.

title: Financial Recovery Technical Assistance
description: The purpose of this grant is to support the city of Flint with capacity building as it continues recovery from the water crisis and moves into addressing subsequent post-water crisis challenges. The city of Flint faces unprecedented challenges as it recovers from the water crisis and the COVID-19 pandemic. Additional staffing and consulting expertise will position city leadership to function more effectively and efficiently in meeting the needs of Flint residents.

title: 21st Century Community Learning Centers Institute
description: This grant will support Foundations, Inc. to offer comprehensive services and supports to enhance high-quality learning experiences and professional development opportunities to 21st Century Community Learning Centers’ leaders and the afterschool field. These events include: 1) expert panel discussions; 2) interactive workshop experiences; 3) content partner showcases; 4) virtual learning supports; and 5) social media events. The learning experiences for afterschool and summer learning educators will expand their strategies and skill sets to enhance the quality of school and community-based out-of-school time programs.

title: Upper Midwest CSA Consortium
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: The Midwest Children’s Savings Account Consortium was created in 2017 to expand children’s savings account policies and initiatives across the Great Lakes Region. Renewal funding will enable the City of St. Paul’s Office of Financial Empowerment to organize the Consortium, support organizations working to advance state and local children’s savings account policies and initiatives and further the overall CSA movement in the region and nationally. Planned activities include stakeholder outreach and education, technical assistance, networking and peer learning and policy development efforts. St. Paul’s Office of Financial Empowerment was established in 2019 to advance economic democracy that promotes prosperity for all St. Paul residents.

title: Sustainable Energy Finance and Development
description: Operation Native Amazon is a Brazilian organization dedicated to protecting the Amazon rainforest, its rivers and the Indigenous peoples who rely on them. Over the last grant period, the organization collaborated with local partners to address the environmental and social impacts of hydropower and oil and gas exploration in the Middle Jurua and Juruena river basins. With renewed support, Operation Native Amazon will continue supporting traditional communities and Indigenous peoples in Amazonas and Mato Grosso.

title: Great Lakes Collaboration in New York State
description: Buffalo Niagara Waterkeeper, based in western New York on the shores of Lakes Erie and Ontario, is one of the largest watershed organizations in the state. The grantee has a strong presence in the region and uses its voice to bring attention to water quality and climate issues impacting New York and the Great Lakes. With previous Mott Foundation support, the grantee raised public awareness of these issues, which has helped advance policies and increase environmental protections and investments in the Great Lakes. With renewed support from the Foundation, Buffalo Niagara Waterkeeper will continue to: 1) elevate the profile of western New York in the state; 2) support critical water quality protection efforts; 3) enhance climate resilience, especially in vulnerable coastal communities; and 4) address ongoing threats to the Great Lakes which challenge the region.

title: Science Panel for the Amazon: Key Dialogues on Sustainable Development and Forest Conservation
description: Convened under the Sustainable Development Solutions Network, the Science Panel for the Amazon brings together over 300 scientists to provide evidence-based guidance for protecting the Amazon basin. Over the last grant period, the Panel developed analysis and policy briefs on forest protection and the role of financial institutions as well as engaged with over 40 financial institutions. In the next grant period, the Panel will: 1) compile science-based policy guidance on tropical forests, sustainable cities and restoration efforts; and 2) expand dialogues with financial institutions across Amazonian countries.

title: Digital Protection Program
description: The project goal is to strengthen the digital protection of civil society actors, organizations, collectives and groups that promote and defend human and digital rights in Central America and Mexico. To this end, Fundacion Acceso will research and monitor the state of digital protection of the above groups and individuals; provide technical assistance and training; promote the development of innovative practices; and support networking in local, regional, national and global digital rights spaces. Fundacion Acceso was created in 1992 with the aim of building the capacity of Central American civil society organizations, with a specific focus on using modern communications technology. Its current mission is to contribute to mitigating the violation of rights related to the physical, technological and psychosocial security of populations in situations of vulnerability and/or risk in Central America and Mexico.

title: Al Sur Coalition
description: The project goal is to enhance the capacity of a coalition of Latin American organizations to advocate for human rights in digital environments in Latin America. The Al Sur Coalition is composed of 11 leading Latin American organizations that coordinate responses to threats and advocate at national, regional and global forums for the promotion of human rights, in particular freedom of expression and privacy, in their relation to digital environments. Project activities will include documentation of threats and abuses, joint reports to authorities, capacity enhancement and sustained advocacy in relevant forums. Founded in 2005 in Chile, Derechos Digitales is an independent, nonprofit organization that works throughout Latin America. Its main objective is developing, defending and promoting human rights in the digital sphere. Derechos Digitales is both a core participant and the fiscal sponsor for the Al Sur Coalition.

title: New Office Space Build Out
description: With this grant, the Crim Fitness Foundation will build out and outfit office and meeting space within the new Harrison Street mixed-use facility. The grantee will co-locate with the YMCA of Greater Flint and be situated alongside 50 apartment units in the newly constructed facility. The new office space will provide opportunities for collaboration with the YMCA and the continued provision of health and wellness initiatives for residents in the Flint and Genesee County community.

title: Operating Support
description: This grant provides operating support to the Crim Fitness Foundation, a Flint-based organization that focuses on active living, physical fitness, nutrition and mindfulness through year-round programming for children, young people and adults in the greater Flint area. The Crim Fitness Foundation has led the Community Education Initiative in Flint area schools since 2014. However, the initiative will shift to a new organization in 2023, and this grant will help support a smooth transition.

title: Strategic Planning and a Water Camp
description: We The People of Detroit is a community-based grassroots nonprofit organization that works on water policy issues in Michigan and nationally. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee: 1) strengthened its organization leadership and operational processes; 2) hosted the annual Great Lakes Youth Water Policy Camp in Idlewild, Michigan; and 3) secured other technical and funding partnerships. With continued support, We The People of Detroit will strengthen its institutional capacity and host Community Research Collective retreats as well as the Great Lakes Youth Water Policy Camp to advance community and youth engagement on water issues.

title: Promoting Digital Inclusion and Rights in Africa
geographic_focus: Western Africa, Eastern Africa, Southern Africa
description: The project goal is to raise awareness about digital rights and the digital civic space in Africa in order to build a rights-respecting, inclusive and innovation-friendly digital policy environment in Africa. To this end, Paradigm Initiative plans to produce and publish in-depth research that informs discussions and policies; and convene internet freedom activists and other stakeholders to share experiences, learn and collaborate on areas of common interest. The grantee was established in 2008 to connect underserved African youth to digital opportunities while ensuring their rights are protected. In addition, the grantee produces research that informs advocacy efforts focused on the development of public policies for internet freedom in Africa. Headquartered in Nigeria, Paradigm Initiative has offices in Cameroon, Kenya, Senegal, Zambia and Zimbabwe.

title: West Africa Security Project
description: The project goal is to strengthen the capacities, readiness and participation opportunities for national and regional civil society organizations to tackle the security-related drivers of a shrinking civic space in West Africa. To achieve this, Spaces for Change, a nonprofit registered in Nigeria, will train nonprofits in West Africa to engage effectively with these policies and understand their impact on civic space. Planned activities over the next two years will include strengthening the capacity and agency of national and regional movements and coalitions; ensuring civil society organizations adhere to the security laws; building the capacity of civil society organizations to engage effectively on previously-established regulations; and producing and disseminating new evidence and homegrown knowledge to equip organizations with information on how to pushback on problematic security norms that restrict civic space. Spaces for Change was established to uphold and protect human rights in all aspects of life by increasing the participation of communities in the development of social and economic policy.

title: Promoting Digital Inclusion and Rights in Africa
geographic_focus: Western Africa, Southern Africa, Eastern Africa
description: The project goal is to promote digital rights and inclusion in Africa by raising awareness of the threats to digital security and advancing an inclusive, innovation-friendly and rights-respecting digital policy environment. Over the past two years, Paradigm Initiative: 1) produced in-depth research on the state of digital rights and inclusion in Africa; 2) convened internet freedom activists and other stakeholders; 3) supported efforts to advance digital rights in specific countries across Africa; and 4) represented the region in international digital rights platforms. This grant will support the grantee to continue producing research that highlights cross-cutting issues that affect digital rights and internet freedom in Africa. In addition, the grantee will host its annual convening of digital rights activists to forge relationships and shape digital rights policy on the continent. The grantee was established in 2008 to connect underserved African youth to digital opportunities while ensuring their rights are protected. Headquartered in Nigeria, Paradigm Initiative has offices in Cameroon, Kenya, Senegal, Zambia and Zimbabwe.

title: West Africa Security Project
description: The project goal is to strengthen the capacities, readiness and participation opportunities for national and regional civil society organizations to tackle the security-related drivers of a shrinking civic space in West Africa. To achieve this, Spaces for Change advocated for the correct implementation of global anti-money laundering standards, as well as countering the financing of terrorism standards by states, businesses, security agencies, regulators, legislatures and financial institutions. This included conducting research, providing training, convening various actors and providing technical support to governments. This grant will support the grantee to extend its support to countries within the region that lack the technical capacity to undertake terrorism financing risk assessments of the nonprofit sector. Spaces for Change was established to uphold and protect human rights in all aspects of life by increasing community participation in the development of social and economic policy.

title: Protecting and Promoting Civic Space in Kenya
description: The project goal is to defend and promote civic space and foster a safe and enabling environment for civil society actors. To achieve this, the Defenders Coalition will safeguard the work of civil society organizations and human rights defenders working in the frontlines of the rule of law, transparency and corruption by building their capacity and producing research regarding civic space in Kenya. This work will enable these actors to respond to and mitigate any safety and security risks they face. The grantee will convene activists to build solidarity and encourage collective action, conduct strategic capacity strengthening in response to emerging challenges for human rights defenders in the country, and build evidence on the extent and types of human rights violations and their impact on civic space. Defenders Coalition is a nonprofit organization based in Nairobi, Kenya. It strengthens the capacity of civil society actors and human rights defenders to work effectively and reduce their vulnerability to the risk of persecution.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Collaboration on International ICT Policy for East and Southern Africa
description: This grant provides funding to an organization whose goals include advancing digital freedoms, supporting progressive digital policies and building community activists’ capacity and digital resilience. To achieve this, the Collaboration on International ICT Policy for East and Southern Africa plans to provide thought leadership, information and connections to create an enabling environment for civil society organizations in the digital space. Planned activities include conducting research that informs practice, building a digital rights community of practice, working with other organizations to build the capacity of digital rights institutions to engage effectively with existing policies and providing small grants to new and fledgling digital rights groups. The grantee was established in 2004 to respond to the lack of timely and accessible information on technology-related issues. While the organization’s focus was originally on East and Southern Africa, programming has expanded across the continent in recognition of the existing gaps, and has staff based in Uganda, Kenya and Cameroon.

title: Advancing and Protecting Sustainability Standards in Development Finance
description: Friends of the Earth US promotes a healthier and more just world. The grantee is part of a federation of 73 organizations that campaign internationally, nationally and locally to protect the environment and people’s rights. With prior Mott Foundation funding, the grantee improved the implementation of climate, social and environmental protections at Chinese development finance institutions and strengthened the capacity of affected communities to oppose projects that would harm the climate, biodiversity or community wellbeing. With renewed support, Friends of the Earth will seek to ensure that Chinese and international financial institutions support an energy transition that does not harm biodiversity and advances sustainable development objectives.

title: After-School All-Stars Endowment
description: This grant to the After-School All-Stars will support the grantee’s new Growth & Impact Endowment Fund. The purpose of the Endowment Fund is to ensure that the All-Stars — one of the leading afterschool providers in the nation — can expand access to more youth and sustain high-quality programs in the coming years. Through the Endowment Fund, the grantee will assist in meeting increased demand for afterschool programs, particularly as youth recover learning loss resulting from the pandemic. The Endowment Fund will support expanded afterschool and summer enrichment programs at existing program sites, and support the expansion of After-School All-Star programs into new communities.

title: Rx Kids Cash Allowance Pilot
description: Michigan State University will partner with University of Michigan and Give Directly to implement and research the impact of an innovative prenatal and infant cash allowance initiative that seeks to advance health equity by proactively addressing maternal and infant economic instability. Rx Kids leans on the science of early childhood and the life-long consequences of exposure to early adversity. The pilot program aims to fill a scientific gap in health disparities research with a community-level disruption of poverty before and during early childhood, when it is most prevalent and most toxic. Through Rx Kids, expectant mothers in Flint will receive a one-time prenatal cash transfer of $1,500, and all infants will receive monthly allowances of $500 per month in their first year of life. The initiative will impact approximately 1,200 Flint mothers and their newborns per year.

title: Technical Assistance to Boost Great Lakes Communication
grantee: Petoskey - Harbor Springs Area Community Foundation
geographic_focus: Midwest, Michigan, Minnesota, Wisconsin, Ohio, Indiana, New York, Illinois
description: This grant to the Petoskey-Harbor Springs Area Community Foundation will support the communications capacity building and technical assistance work of Freshwater Future. Since 1996, Freshwater Future has provided over $5.8 million through over 1,400 grants for capacity building and technical assistance to groups working to protect and restore water in the Great Lakes region. With prior Mott Foundation support, Freshwater Future worked with a communications consulting firm to provide technical support to organizations active in the Great Lakes basin to strengthen their communications capacity. Through this grant, the Petoskey-Harbor Springs Area Community Foundation will assist Freshwater Future as they continue working with a consulting firm, expand the pool of organizations receiving direct technical support, and provide training and tools to program participants and other organizations on effective communications strategies.

title: Digital Protection Program
description: The project goal is to promote digital security and comprehensive protection for organizations and individuals working to defend civic space and human rights in Central America and Mexico. To this end, Fundacion Acceso will: 1) adopt a holistic protection approach to support civil society actors through its Digital Protection School; 2) provide technical assistance and training; 3) develop innovative learning and communities of practices; and 4) support networks and collaborative knowledge exchange at the local and regional levels. In addition, the grantee will review its organizational risk analysis and strengthen its technological infrastructure and systems. These efforts build on the achievements from the previous grant period, which included providing digital protection support to more than 40 civil society organizations in the region. Fundacion Acceso was founded in 1992 to build the capacity of civil society organizations in Central America and Mexico. Over the years, its work has taken on different priorities based on the needs of organizations in the region.

title: Strengthening the Ukrainian Community Foundation Field
description: The project goal is to strengthen the Ukrainian community foundation field to support local civil society’s response to the ongoing conflict and involvement in Ukraine’s recovery and reconstruction. Since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, Ednannia mobilized a total of $877,000 in support of Ukrainian community foundations’ efforts to help their communities respond to emergency needs. In the program’s first year, the grantee awarded 45 grants to 15 community foundations totaling $520,000, which was matched by another $298,000 from local donors. Over the next two years, the grantee will provide core support to existing Ukrainian community foundations, seed grants to new community foundation initiatives and matching grant funds to support local civic groups involved in recovery and reconstruction. The grantee will also provide support to the network of Ukrainian community foundations. Established in 1999, Ednannia is an indigenous grantmaker which is well regarded for its rigorous, transparent, responsive and effective processes to support community-level, grassroots organizations throughout Ukraine.

title: General Purposes
description: Traditional and Indigenous forest dwellers in the Amazon rely mainly on canoes and boats to travel in the rainforest. Additionally, forest clearing for roads and other linear infrastructure brings deforestation and degradation in its wake. The Kara Solar Foundation and its partners in the Achuar territory of Ecuador have developed the first solar-powered boats and linked them to efforts to solarize their villages. This increase will be available for the general purposes of the grantee including participation in a high-profile clean energy conference in Brazil where Kara Solar Foundation can strengthen its profile and attract new supporters.

title: Renewable Energy for Extractive Reserves in the Amazon
description: This project will support the World Wildlife Fund and its partner — World Wildlife Fund Brazil — to continue working on a national program for solar energy for forest-dwelling communities living in sustainable development reserves in the Amazon. As part of this project, the grantee monitors outcomes of managed solar energy pilots, promotes solar photovoltaic value chains in Amazon municipalities and coordinates a network of nongovernmental organizations working on renewable electrification in the Brazilian Amazon. With this grant increase, the World Wildlife Fund will conduct an energy needs audit in selected extractive and sustainable development reserves to help accelerate the universalization of energy access in remote communities of the Brazilian Amazon.

title: Network for Schools Excellence Support
description: The goal of this grant is to support the Community Foundation of Greater Flint in its efforts to improve educational opportunities and outcomes for children in Flint. The grantee will develop a framework and lead a coordinated effort to impact a network of K-12 schools serving Flint kids. The grantee will engage and align parent and community interests in the development of this community of practice.

title: Coalition for Human Rights in Development Community Resource Exchange
description: The Coalition for Human Rights in Development is a global network of nongovernmental organizations — housed at Social and Environmental Entrepreneurs — working to mitigate the social and environmental impacts of large-scale infrastructure and energy finance. With prior Mott Foundation funding, the grantee established and developed the Community Resource Exchange, which shares skills, tools and resources to build the capacity of grassroots organizations and communities seeking to: 1) defend their rights; 2) promote environmental sustainability; and 3) make energy and infrastructure investments more responsive to their needs. With renewed support, the Community Resource Exchange will continue to facilitate peer learning and capacity building as well as strengthening collective campaigns on shared challenges.

title: General Purposes
description: Accountability Counsel supports communities around the world to protect their environment and human rights. Infrastructure and energy projects funded by development finance institutions often come with substantial social and environmental risks. The grantee engages with these institutions’ accountability mechanisms to advocate for communities, secure remedies and ensure that lending policies do not cause harm. With prior Mott Foundation funding, the grantee strengthened its organizational and programmatic capacity to respond to community requests, develop strategies and engage with decision-makers. With renewed general purposes support, Accountability Counsel will continue to work alongside communities to halt or delay harmful investments, conduct data analysis to illuminate systemic barriers and use lessons learned to advocate for investments that are responsive to community needs.

title: Northwoods, Freshwater and Natural Climate Solutions in Michigan
description: A comprehensive response to climate change will require a range of actions, including carbon sequestration in healthy forests. The Great Lakes Northwoods, which span across northern Michigan and neighboring states, contain some of the most resilient and connected forests in the central United States. The Nature Conservancy, a global conservation organization with a robust presence in Michigan, is working to protect the state’s Northwoods and the climate, freshwater, economic and biodiversity benefits the forest provides. With partial support from the Mott Foundation over the next two years, the grantee will undertake a range of activities in the Northwoods, including demonstrating sustainable forestry practices, promoting the use of verifiable and market-leading carbon credit markets, encouraging public agencies to improve policies, programs and practices for better climate outcomes and creating science-based management tools to improve collaboration and the efficient use of available resources.

title: Michigan Communities for Financial Empowerment Network
grantee: Community Economic Development Association of Michigan
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: The Community Economic Development Association of Michigan works to expand and strengthen financial security in communities across the state. Since 2011, the Mott Foundation has supported the grantee’s efforts coordinating statewide engagement and education activities that increase awareness and support for children’s savings accounts. With this grant, the grantee will focus on expanding access to children’s savings accounts across Michigan. This proposed project scope will work to: 1) build a data-driven infrastructure; 2) empower local communication; 3) champion the cause of children’s savings accounts by actively engaging with philanthropic and corporate stakeholders to generate additional funding; and 4) enhance the capacity of local programs. This project promises significant long-term benefits for Michigan’s students and the state’s overall economic well-being.

title: Advancing the Children's Savings Account Field
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: For over 40 years, Prosperity Now has focused on ensuring prosperity for all as a leading intermediary on national research, practice and policy dedicated to financial stability and wealth. With continued Mott Foundation support since 1983, the grantee’s endeavors have significantly built the children’s savings account field. With renewed support, the grantee is committed to: 1) strengthening existing Children’s Savings Account programs; 2) fostering innovation in the field; and 3) centering racial equity in the Children’s Savings Account program design and operations in initiatives across the country. Prosperity Now continues to ensure that new programs have the support and tools they need to be effective, sustainable and enriching to the entire field.

title: Global Philanthropy Program
description: This grant supports the Council on Foundations’ Global Philanthropy Program which is framed around four pillars of activity: 1) strengthening cross-border grantmaking; 2) advocating for a global enabling environment; 3) facilitating global convenings and conversations; and 4) developing global resources and thought leadership. In October 2022, the council launched a monthly Philanthropy for Ukraine briefing series for U.S. and Canadian foundations, in partnership with the German Marshall Fund, Community Foundations of Canada and Philanthropic Foundations of Canada. A total of 176 persons from over 100 organizations registered for the five webinars between October 2022 and February 2023. This grant increase will permit the grantee to continue the series as a set of six peer learning circle meetings, with webinars occurring every other month and the issuance of six monthly Ukraine digests over the next year. The Council on Foundations will also continue to update its online Ukraine resource hub.

title: Africa Giving Platform
description: The project goal is to strengthen community philanthropy by developing an online giving platform that is accessible, low cost and benefits civil society organizations in Africa. The platform will profile organizations that do not have access to global giving facilities or the internet and will enable individuals to give to organizations of their choice. To ensure that organizations on the platform are credible, Sivio Institute will vet the organizations and provide them with the necessary support to be compliant with the vetting process. In addition, the grantee will profile newly established community foundations to unlock funding from communities in the diaspora. The grantee was established in 2018 to contribute to Africa’s inclusive socioeconomic transformation by promoting pro-poor policy development processes, advancing community-led development and nurturing citizen agency. The Sivio Institute is registered in the United States, but is based in Zimbabwe and is expanding its operations to South Africa.

title: Finance for Sustainable Development in South America
description: INESC is a nongovernmental organization committed to strengthening civil society in Brazil. During the previous grant period, the grantee advanced its energy agenda by: 1) publishing reports on fossil fuel subsidies; 2) expanding its monitoring of the energy sector to include subsidies for renewable sources; 3) enhancing its strategic communication; and 4) engaging with financial institutions on social and environmental safeguards. In the next grant period, the grantee will continue work in Brazil to tackle inefficient fossil fuel subsidies to strengthen the country’s global climate leadership. INESC will also work to ensure that investments in the energy transition adhere to robust social and environmental safeguards.

title: Community Water Lab
description: This grant will support the operations of The McKenzie Patrice Croom Flint Community Lab at the Flint Development Center. The McKenzie Patrice Croom Flint Community Lab will be equipped with state-of-the-art technology to test water for multiple contaminants. Scientists and staff of the lab, including youth, will work with residents to collect water samples, test for multiple contaminants, provide results and work with households to address any identified issues.

title: General Purposes
description: The National Center for Family Philanthropy provides resources, expertise and support to families to transform their values into effective giving that makes a lasting impact on the communities they serve. During the previous grant period, the grantee: 1) increased its number of members; 2) grew its brand awareness and partnerships with other organizations across the sector; 3) hosted the National Forum on Family Philanthropy; and 4) produced knowledge resources. During this grant period, the grantee will provide educational opportunities, host networking events and produce the third edition of its Trends in Family Philanthropy research report. Founded in 1997, the National Center for Family Philanthropy is the only national nonprofit dedicated exclusively to families who give and those who work with them.

title: Mizzen Education, Inc. Operation and Growth Support
location: Marina del Rey, CA, United States
description: This grant will continue to support Mizzen Education, Inc. in its efforts to increase access to world-class digital learning curricula through the Mizzen Education, Inc. online platform. Specifically, this grant will enable the grantee to: 1) increase access to Mizzen Education, Inc.’s online curricula and resources for afterschool educators; 2) provide professional development opportunities for afterschool educators; and 3) support the development of Mizzen Education Inc. as a 501(c)(3) organization to well-position the grantee for future growth.

title: Mizzen Education, Inc. Operation and Growth Support
location: Marina del Rey, CA, United States
description: This grant will continue to support Mizzen Education, Inc. in its efforts to increase access to world-class digital learning curricula through the Mizzen Education, Inc. online platform. Specifically, this grant will enable the grantee to: 1) increase access to Mizzen Education, Inc.’s online curricula and resources for afterschool educators; 2) provide professional development opportunities for afterschool educators; 3) continue to partner with the 50 State Afterschool Network and other afterschool organizations to increase access to quality programs; and 4) support the further development of Mizzen Education, Inc. as a stand alone nonprofit organization.

title: Supporting the National Network of Statewide Afterschool Networks
description: Collaborative Communications Group will continue to support, convene and enhance the education and afterschool ecosystem of grantees, including the 50 State Afterschool Network, the Afterschool Technical Assistance Collaborative and education stakeholders. For the 50 State Afterschool Network, the grantee will: 1) coordinate all Network meetings including large national afterschool and education conferences; 2) manage webinars, the Network website and online community; 3) provide professional development opportunities for the 50 State Afterschool Network; 4) collaborate with Mizzen Education, Inc. to increase quality programs; and 5) implement convenings as needed to advance partnerships in the afterschool and education sectors. The overall outcome of this project is to improve quality afterschool programs by coordinating the afterschool field at the national and state levels.

title: VISTA Project
description: This grant will support the Afterschool Alliance to continue deploying AmeriCorps Volunteers in Service to America (VISTA) members for the growth and sustainability of statewide afterschool networks and their partners. Dedicated to the efforts of improving the afterschool networks and programs for underserved communities and families, the grantee’s VISTA project has been instrumental in expanding quality programming for young people. This grant will: 1) support the VISTA project in afterschool networks to address childhood hunger and nutrition; 2) introduce and expand quality STEM learning; 3) mitigate impacts of substance misuse; 4) strengthen academic supports for student recovery; and 5) produce an impact and evaluation report on the VISTA program.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will continue to support the After-School All-Stars to continue to lead quality afterschool programming across the country. The mission of the grantee is to provide comprehensive afterschool programs that keep children safe and help them succeed in school and life. Specifically, this grant will enable the grantee to provide additional programming to young people in the following areas: 1) academic support and credit recovery to support educational advancement; 2) social emotional learning and mental health supports; and 3) mentorship with caring adults. This grant will support the After-School All-Stars to provide high-quality programming, improve staff retention and educate key champions with a focus on helping youth recover from the pandemic.

title: Wabash County Promise Endowment Fund
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: With support from the Mott Foundation, the Community Foundation of Wabash County designed and piloted an innovative scholarship program that harnesses the power of children’s savings accounts to positively influence student identity, school engagement and academic outcomes. Evaluation of the Early Award Scholarship program identified positive impacts on savings, college planning and student academic performance. This grant would enable the grantee to establish an endowment fund, creating a permanent stream of funds to support the program’s initial seed deposits and ongoing incentive awards. Based in Wabash, Indiana, the grantee had more than $78 million in assets as of December 2021, including 350 permanently endowed funds.

title: Improving Equity and Accountability for Native American Communities with Community Foundations
description: The goal of this project is to support the advancement of racial equity for Native communities by U.S. community foundations, applying the framework of the Sustainable Development Goals. In 2022, Native Americans in Philanthropy conducted a study of community foundations and received input from Native leaders. This resulted in a report that provided an assessment of the current state of community foundation interaction with Native communities and offered recommendations for how to improve relationships between them. These findings gave the basis for a further proposed six-year educational, relationship-building and resource-leveraging project. During the current grant period, the grantee will: 1) convene relevant stakeholders to share and discuss the report; 2) conduct a research study that will explore the link between the Sustainable Development Goals and community foundation data-gathering processes; 3) design a workshop curriculum; 4) develop a strategic communications plan; 5) hire a regional coordinator for the first of four regions; and 6) establish the first of four communities of practice, each of which will include up to 20 community foundations. Founded in 1990, Native Americans in Philanthropy promotes equitable and effective philanthropy in Native communities.

title: Tapology Youth Outreach
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide partial support for Tapology outreach programs. Tap dance is an enduring American art form that increases physical activity and enhances cognitive development for participants. The grantee partners with local schools and community centers to provide area youth with an introduction to tap dance and offers regular classes for all levels of ability. Each year, the grantee’s outreach programming culminates into a four-day festival that provides exposure for local students to the art and history of tap. Professional artists will continue to provide instruction for beginners, as well as more advanced workshops for experienced young dancers.

title: STEM Fellowship
description: This grant to the STEM Next Opportunity Fund will support the out-of-school time and STEM fellowship network. The fellowships are a public-private partnership initiative geared toward advancing cross-agency partnerships to expand access to high-quality afterschool, summer learning and informal STEM learning for youth and families. This initiative will work to: 1) strengthen collaboration between the U.S. Department of Education and other federal agencies in the areas of afterschool and informal STEM learning; 2) advance afterschool and STEM learning in the 21st Century Community Learning Centers program; and 3) collaborate with leading researchers to identify priorities, new tools, strategies and programs that improve afterschool and STEM learning opportunities.

title: Fiscal Solvency and Service Effectiveness Project
description: This grant provides support for Michigan State University’s overall efforts to document and promote solutions that help America’s older industrial cities address chronic fiscal stress and advance overall fiscal health. In 2023-2024 the grantee began collecting fiscal data on water infrastructure for about 350 Michigan municipalities in order to assess the condition and sustainability of these systems. During the current grant period, the grantee will complete analysis and recommend strategies that help municipalities develop asset management plans that identify long-term system needs — including operating and maintenance strategies — and ensure safe and reliable water service. As with previous grant periods, Michigan State University will provide direct technical assistance to the City of Flint on a limited basis as mutually agreed upon.

title: Public Awareness Campaign
description: With this grant, Kettering University will develop and implement a comprehensive marketing and communications initiative aimed at reaching local, national and international audiences. The initiative will center on four strategies: brand development and positioning; reputation; enrollment; and web and digital presence. Collectively, the initiative will raise awareness about the university, reinforce the value of the institution to a broad audience and invest in targeted marketing. As a result, the university will attract more students interested in high-demand STEM field careers and provide them with the strong educational experiences that are available on Kettering University’s campus.

title: Reinvestment Office of Greater Flint
description: This grant to the Greater Flint Health Coalition supports establishing an office within the organization that focuses on the coordination of advocacy and funding efforts geared towards improving the quality of life for Genesee County residents. The goal of of Greater Flint Health Coalition’s Reinvestment Office is to serve as a neutral convener that will work with community partners in the public and private sectors to identify funding opportunities and areas of investment needed to move the needle in a positive direction on Genesee County health rankings.

title: Great Lakes Journalism in Canada
description: The Narwhal is a nonprofit online news magazine that publishes in-depth and investigative journalism about the natural world in Canada. They are widely recognized as one of the best environmental publications in Canada and one that strives to include First Nation/Indigenous voices in every article they publish. With Mott Foundation funding, the grantee will be able to join the Great Lakes News Collaborative, a partnership across newsrooms and media outlets. They will deepen their reporting in the Great Lakes with existing partners in the Collaborative, expanding the geography and diversity of coverage and media capacity in the region. They will be able to participate in, contribute to and share content of the Collaborative to further raise awareness of the issues and threats to the Great Lakes.

title: Resource Recovery and PFAS in Chicago Convening and Collaboration
description: Current Innovation NFP is a nonprofit water innovation organization headquartered in Chicago, Illinois. Founded in 2016, the grantee’s mission is to provide the space to convene diverse partners on water issues, accelerate policy innovation and solve pressing water challenges such as toxics and contamination in the Great Lakes and beyond. With Mott Foundation funding, the grantee will organize events to educate and engage water professionals and advocates, build partnerships and networks at the local, state and regional levels and provide technical assistance for water projects that advance environmental and economic equity.

title: Great Lakes Islands Alliance
description: The Great Lakes Islands Alliance — a project of the Stewardship Network — is a bi-national, voluntary collaborative network consisting of over 250 island leaders from 20 islands in the Great Lakes region. With previous Mott Foundation support, the grantee was able to expand its membership and implement island-appropriate solutions to an array of environmental challenges, from rising lake levels to climate resiliency to water pollution. With renewed support, the Stewardship Network will be able to strengthen the connections and communications among and between islands and islanders while advancing stewardship of island natural resources.

title: Solar Energy for Amazon River Dwellers
grantee: Centro de Estudos Avançados de Promoção Social e Ambiental
description: This grant increase will cover costs of travel and participant travel, logistical support and communications and materials by Centro de Estudos Avancados de Promocao Social e Ambiental to support the Energy and Communities event in the Brazilian Amazon. This event brings together nongovernmental and community leaders from Indigenous, Quilombolo and river-dwelling forest peoples, government agencies and private sector renewable energy companies to advance renewable energy access for isolated communities in the greater Amazon rainforest.

title: General Purposes
description: Inclusive Development International supports communities around the world in determining their own development paths and protecting their rights and resources from harmful projects. The grantee provides strategic advice, training and support to communities impacted by projects financed by multilateral development banks and other development institutions to access accountability mechanisms. With this general purposes grant, the grantee will work with communities to advance strategies that ensure investments in energy and infrastructure protect the environment and respect human rights.

title: Expanding Distributed Renewable Energy in the Amazon
description: The Brazilian Association of Distributed Generation is an organization that represents over 400 companies in the renewable energy sector. With prior support from the Mott Foundation, the organization successfully hosted an Amazon Forum and conducted a solar roadshow, visiting 109 cities across Brazil and training over 2,000 individuals in solar energy use. In the upcoming grant period, the organization will continue its roadshows and outreach efforts to promote solar energy supply chains and markets in remote Amazon regions. The Brazilian Association of Distributed Generation will also foster knowledge exchange, deliver public training and provide technical support to identify and implement the most suitable renewable energy systems for isolated Amazonian communities.

title: Summer Community Development Internships
description: This grant provides support to Michigan State University for the Summer Community Development Internship program open to both Michigan State University undergraduate and graduate students. This internship program, which seeks to develop and enhance community assets through meaningful internship experiences, is accomplished through an immersive 10-week summer internship program centered around five projects that were chosen from nine project proposals submitted by local community organizations. This summer’s focus areas include equitable grantmaking, youth civic engagement, urban planning and other community engagement projects.

title: Development Finance Accountability Mechanisms
description: This two-year project will engage leaders in the development finance field in a collective initiative to evaluate and re-imagine accountability mechanisms at international development finance institutions, including the World Bank and International Finance Corporation. Working in collaboration with current and former accountability analysts and civil society advocates, Peregrine Environmental Consulting, a public interest consulting firm, will gather historical data, produce two books and a series of opinion pieces, and carry out a detailed set of oral histories. The information will be shared, discussed, and refined in public lectures and conferences, as well as a podcast. Teaching materials will be developed for university use and the entire project will be documented in a publicly available research archive.

title: Solar Electrician and Entrepreneurship Training
description: The Salesian Missions of Don Bosco is an international nonprofit that has been providing education and technical training to poor children and youth around the globe since 1947. The grantee’s local chapter in Tanzania has been operating vocational training centers since 1980. Over the past four years of Mott Foundation support, the grantee trained over 1,000 vulnerable youth as qualified solar technicians, and over 30% have either been formally employed in the solar sector or have established solar enterprises. Over the next two years, the grantee will strengthen its organizational capacity, strengthen partnerships with other organizations as well as build stronger networks between its alumni and existing students through mentorship and career support.

title: Sharing Indian Social Entrepreneurs' Lessons for African Off Grid Energy
description: SELCO Foundation is a pioneering nonprofit organization focused on delivering sustainable energy services to the poor in India in a manner that creates assets and results in long-term poverty alleviation. Over the past eight years with Mott support, the grantee has provided technical support services aimed at transferring its successful experiences in India to sustainable energy access initiatives in Tanzania. With additional support, SELCO Foundation will synthesize and share lessons learned to date and facilitate cross-learning opportunities among energy access stakeholders in Africa and India.

title: Land Water and Climate Justice Efforts in the Global South
description: Founded in 1985, American Jewish World Service aims to build a more just, equitable and sustainable world by financing community-driven advocacy and acting as a connector and strategic advisor to its grantee partners. It invests approximately $30 million a year and supports more than 500 groups and networks in 14 countries. Prior Mott Foundation funding supported the Land, Water and Climate Justice program’s work with partners in Southeast Asia monitoring the impact of large-scale investments on communities and the environment. With renewed support, American Jewish World Service will continue its long-term support for organizations and networks supporting affected communities.

title: Operating Support
description: This grant provides operating support to the Crim Fitness Foundation, a Flint-based organization that focuses on active living, physical fitness, nutrition and mindfulness through year-round programming for children, young people and adults in the greater Flint area. The grantee led the Community Education Initiative in Flint area schools from 2014 to 2023. However, the initiative shifted to a new organization and this grant will further support a smooth transition.

title: Education Policy Institute
description: This grant will continue to provide funds for Furman University to operate the White-Riley-Peterson Policy Institute, which brings together a diverse group of 17 emerging leaders from the afterschool and education fields to serve as fellows. Over the course of a year, fellows will work with experts, complete an intensive policy curriculum and participate in national networking opportunities. The fellowship will enable participants to positively contribute to the development of practices that support afterschool and summer learning opportunities for children across the country.

title: Northwoods, Freshwater and Natural Climate Solutions in Michigan
description: The Great Lakes Northwoods, which span across northern Michigan and neighboring states, contain some of the most resilient and connected forests in the central United States. The Nature Conservancy, a global conservation organization with a robust presence in Michigan, is working to protect the state’s Northwoods and the climate, freshwater, economic and biodiversity benefits the forest provides. With partial support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee will continue to undertake a range of activities to benefit the Northwoods, including: 1) modeling sustainable forestry practices; 2) demonstrating the use of carbon credit markets; 3) encouraging public agencies to improve policies, programs and practices for better climate outcomes; and 4) creating science-based management tools to improve collaboration and the efficient use of available resources.

title: General Purposes
description: Kara Solar Foundation is advancing a proven model of solar river transport that strengthens Indigenous cultures, protects rainforest ecosystems and builds technical and economic strength in remote Amazonian territories. Over the last grant period, the grantee maintained a fleet of solar-powered boats in Achuar territory in Ecuador, providing fuel-free trips that supported education, health access and cultural activities. The grantee also expanded its reach to Peru, Brazil and Suriname; deepened local technical capacity through multilingual training materials and workshops; and launched new technologies to build a resilient, community-led clean energy value chain. Over the next grant period, Kara Solar will scale its impact through: 1) expanding solar rivers networks; 2) developing productive solar technologies that support Indigenous livelihoods; and 3) establishing itself as a regional knowledge hub to spread solar mobility and energy sovereignty across the Amazon River basin.

title: Flint Fireworks
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to the Flint Downtown Development Authority will support a fireworks display for both the 2023 Flint Juneteenth celebration and Independence Day festivities in July. The grantee and several community partners, including the city of Flint, have organized a series of family friendly activities for a multiday Juneteenth celebration, including a parade from Max Brandon Park to Riverbank Park in downtown Flint. Independence Day will also include a combination of performances, activities and fireworks. The events aim to bring the community together to commemorate important historical events in this country.

title: Solar Energy for Chiribiquete Forest Dwellers
description: Amazon Conservation Team has been working with traditional communities in the Colombian and Peruvian Amazon to improve the quality of life for communities, promote the protection of isolated Indigenous peoples and implement solar energy solutions. Past grant efforts made progress toward expanding renewable energy access to isolated communities, strengthening local governance and management capacity, providing opportunities for social development and contributing to the livelihoods of vulnerable communities. Over the next grant period, the grantee will continue to establish sustainable local renewable energy systems in remote areas, focusing on Colombia’s middle and lower Caquetá and Putumayo Rivers and in Peru’s Pupuña and Atacuari Indigenous reserves, providing them with solar-powered lighting and cell phone charging solutions. Additionally, the project aims to protect isolated Indigenous peoples by installing solar energy systems in prioritized surveillance posts.

title: General Purposes
description: E-LICO Foundation is a local Tanzanian nonprofit that co-designs and implements innovative model projects supporting the productive use of solar energy services in rural communities. Over the past four years, the grantee has benefited over 18,000 people through its community-focused projects, demonstrating several alternative productive uses of solar energy solutions. These model projects have created jobs and improved thousands of rural livelihoods in Tanzania’s Dodoma and Iringa regions. In the next two years, the grantee will scale proven models for advancing the productive use of solar energy by engaging suitable partners. It will also facilitate public engagement through suitable communications and knowledge management products. In addition, E-LICO will lay the foundation for the long-term sustainability of its interventions in the productive use of the solar energy services sector of Tanzania by strengthening its organizational capacity.

title: DREEM Hub Kenya - Solarizing Key Agricultural Value Chains
description: One in five Kenyans are estimated to lack access to electricity and instead rely on costly and polluting fossil fuels that exacerbate global climate change. This limited access to electricity services is particularly severe in Kenya’s rural areas, where 70% of the population depends on agriculture. The Kenya Climate Innovation Center is a Kenyan nonprofit organization that provides technical, operational and financial support services to empower farmers and entrepreneurs to respectively adopt and deliver innovative climate change solutions in East Africa. Through this project, the grantee plans to support 1,000 underserved entrepreneurs with business and technical support services to help increase access to productive use of solar energy services within the dairy and horticulture value chains. Additionally, the grantee will establish a revolving solar energy loan fund to improve access to affordable financing in the sector. The Kenya Climate Innovation Center will also create an independent distributed renewable energy ecosystem hub organization in Kenya for long-term organizational sustainability.

title: DREEM Hub Kenya - Solarizing Key Agricultural Value Chains
description: The Kenya Climate Innovation Center is a nonprofit organization that has been supporting innovative climate solutions in East Africa since 2012. Over the past grant period, the grantee has completed the research and design phase of a program for advancing the productive use of solar energy services in different rural off-grid regions of Kenya. The grantee has also secured several strategic partnerships to this end. This renewal grant will enable the grantee to implement several initiatives to accelerate access to the productive use of solar energy services in Kenya. Kenya Climate Innovation Center will also establish an independent and self-sustaining hub organization to sustain these efforts in Kenya.

title: DREEM Hub Uganda – Solarizing Key Agricultural Value Chains
description: Heifer Project International is an international development nonprofit organization that has been operating in Uganda since 1982. During this time, the grantee has enabled nearly 1 million farmer households across Uganda to increase their incomes, realize decent livelihoods and bolster their resilience to shocks, including those caused by global climate change. Both agriculture and energy sectors account for nearly 70% of annual carbon emissions in Uganda and provide excellent opportunities for addressing climate change. The project will advance access to solar skills, jobs and entrepreneurship development opportunities for underserved entrepreneurs across Uganda’s dairy sector value chains. The project will also expand access to affordable financial services for the productive use of solar energy solutions among disadvantaged farmers, dairy cooperatives and other value-chain participants. In addition, the project will strengthen the capacity and coordination among key agricultural and solar energy stakeholders by establishing a well-governed and self-sustaining hub organization in Uganda.

title: DREEM Hub Uganda – Solarizing Key Agricultural Value Chains
description: Since 1982, Heifer Project International, a global development nonprofit organization, has operated in Uganda, improving incomes, livelihoods and climate resilience for nearly 1 million farmer households. Over the past grant period, the grantee trained over 600 women and youth, evaluated the feasibility of solar energy services at four dairy cooperatives, and secured six strategic partnerships to advance the productive use of solar energy services in Uganda. This renewal will enable the grantee to support an additional 400 underserved youth and women entrepreneurs with solar skills, jobs and entrepreneurship opportunities in Uganda’s dairy sector. The grantee will also enhance access to financial and business development services for off-grid solar energy users and continue strengthening collaboration among key stakeholders through a self-sustaining Distributed Renewable Energy Ecosystem Model Hub initiative in Uganda.

title: General Purposes
description: The organization’s goal is to increase access to justice for poor and marginalized people in Rwanda. To this end, Haguruka will provide comprehensive justice services to people in Rwanda. It plans to strengthen the capacity of its staff, while using a network of approximately 400 paralegals to provide justice services, targeting women and children as beneficiaries. Haguruka was established in 1991 with a mission to promote and defend the rights of women and children.

title: Supporting the Energy Access Ecosystem
description: Fraxen Consulting is coordinating civil society efforts in Tanzania to demonstrate a model approach to accelerating access to modern energy services with distributed renewable energy solutions. With Mott’s support over the past six years, the grantee has facilitated several coordination meetings amongst key partners on access to distributed renewable energy services, proactively identified and recruited new partners as well as enabled partner capacity building through local and international exchange learning visits. During the next grant period, Fraxen Consulting will continue to strengthen its organizational capacity as well as improve women and youth engagement on the productive use of solar energy services.

title: Great Lakes Leadership Council
geographic_focus: Michigan, Illinois, Wisconsin, Indiana, Ohio, Minnesota, North America
description: The Council of State Governments has brought together state and provincial policymakers from the binational Great Lakes region to learn about key issues affecting the lakes in the United States and Canada for over two decades. The Midwest office supports a caucus of policymakers to collaborate and build capacity to be effective leaders and stewards of this freshwater resource. With prior Mott Foundation support, the grantee educated and convened policymakers through forums and institutes to exchange information, share ideas and pursue opportunities collectively. Renewed support will enable the Council of State Governments to continue its Midwest programs and activities, creating a space for members to discuss and advance cooperative solutions to the problems impacting the Great Lakes with a strong regional voice.

title: Strengthening BNDES Accountability
