description: Conectas is a Brazilian nongovernmental organization working to strengthen the social and environmental standards practiced by development finance institutions. Over the past grant period, the organization worked to promote stronger compliance with such safeguards across key financial institutions, including the Brazilian Development Bank, the New Development Bank and the Inter-American Development Bank. The organization also supported communities affected by large-scale energy and infrastructure projects. Over the next grant period, the organization will continue to advance civil society engagement and elevate the voices of impacted communities in the development and implementation of financial institutions’ policies and safeguards. Conectas will prioritize strengthening the social and environmental policies and climate commitments of targeted development banks.

title: Developing Community Foundations in Argentina
description: The project goal is to support the formation and strengthening of community foundations in Argentina. To this end, the Inter-American Foundation will provide support to three initiative groups that have a strong interest in establishing, or transitioning into becoming, community foundations. These groups are located in Moreno (near Buenos Aires), Mendoza and Neuquen. Grants of $25,000-$28,000 will be awarded to each group for planning and diagnostic activities, stakeholder dialogues, administrative and legal expenses, subgrant funds and other expenses relevant to the establishment of community foundations. The grantee will match Mott support with another $50,000 of its own funds as well as provide ongoing support through exchanges, technical assistance and project implementation management and oversight. The Inter-American Foundation is an independent United States government agency created by Congress in 1969 to channel development assistance directly to the poor in Latin America and the Caribbean.

title: Gus Macker Tournament
description: This grant to the Sylvester Broome Empowerment Village will support the 2023 Gus Macker Tournament. In 2022, the event attracted over 7,000 spectators and nearly 550 participants. The purpose is to raise funds for the grantee’s sports programs, increase tourism and positively impact the economy in the Genesee County area. Both adults and youth participate in the tournament.

title: Renovation Project
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to the Greater Flint Arts Council will provide funds for renovations to its headquarters located on Saginaw Street in downtown Flint. The building improvements will create more space on the second and third floor of the building for the community, artists, and arts and culture groups to convene and showcase their work. The renovations will also increase accessibility and improve safety in the building. This project is supported by multiple funders who value the work that the council does on behalf of the arts community.

title: Flint Fireworks
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to the Flint Downtown Development Authority will support a fireworks display for both the 2024 Flint Juneteenth celebration and Independence Day festivities in July. The grantee will work with several community partners, including the city of Flint, Flint Institute of Music and Juneteenth organizers to offer a series of family-friendly activities for a multiday Juneteenth celebration, including a parade from Max Brandon Park to Riverbank Park in downtown Flint. Independence Day will also include a combination of performances, activities and fireworks. The events aim to bring the community together to commemorate important historical events in this country.

title: Flint Fireworks
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to the Flint Downtown Development Authority will support a fireworks display for both the Flint Juneteenth celebration and Independence Day festivities in July. The grantee will work with several community partners, including the city of Flint, Flint Institute of Music and Juneteenth organizers to offer a series of family-friendly activities for a multiday Juneteenth celebration, including a parade from Max Brandon Park to Riverbank Park in downtown Flint. Independence Day will also include a combination of performances, activities and fireworks. The events aim to bring the community together to commemorate important historical events in this country.

title: Michigan Water Resources Protection and Financing
description: The Nature Conservancy, a global conservation organization with deep roots in Michigan, has been researching policy options, engaging key stakeholders and advancing policy recommendations that address a range of water policy issues. With this grant increase, the conservancy will provide technical assistance to a working group tasked with devising a policy solution that makes drinking water safe and affordable for all residents of the State.

title: Michigan Powerplants to Parklands
description: Older coal-fired powerplants are being retired across the country, including in Michigan. The Environmental Law and Policy Center, a regional environmental group based in Chicago, sees an opportunity to transform these Michigan sites by reusing some of the land for parks and recreation and some of the land and existing infrastructure for new renewable energy generation. With support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee and partner groups will engage community leaders and other stakeholders to assess the viability of and support for the project.

title: Economic Mobility Initiative
description: This grant provides support to the Harlem Children’s Zone’s Economic Mobility Initiative, a seven year, $300 million, 11-site pilot program designed to enhance the organization’s successful cradle-to-career model by ensuring young people have the capital — financial as well as human and social — needed at critical stages to overcome poverty and launch successful lives. The initiative’s strategies — which include children’s savings accounts, youth opportunity funds and family allowances–have the potential to inform future directions for economic mobility and children’s policies in the United States. Launched in 2000, the Harlem Children’s Zone initiative works in a 97-block area of Central Harlem to break cycles of intergenerational poverty through research-driven, community-tested strategies.

title: General Purposes
description: Environmental Defence Canada is active on environmental issues at the provincial and national levels through engagement with stakeholders, organizations and the general public. The organization works to: 1) safeguard Canada’s freshwater resources; 2) decrease Canadians’ exposure to toxic chemicals; 3) end plastic pollution; and 4) build a clean economy. To help address these issues, Environmental Defence Canada will engage and educate stakeholders and participate in opportunities to help ensure the restoration of the Great Lakes, strengthen the organization’s capacity and raise awareness of public health issues in Ontario.

title: Advancing and Protecting Sustainability Standards in Development Finance
description: Friends of the Earth, part of the largest network of affiliated environmental advocacy organizations in the world, continues to build on its longstanding successful efforts to reform critical international financial institutions, particularly in the energy, extractive and natural resources sectors. With this increase, the grantee seeks to support its biennial general meeting and pre-conference, the first such in-person conference since 2018. It will bring together Friends of the Earth groups from all over the world for planning and direction of the Friends of the Earth International Federation. The result will be stronger coordination and cooperation across the network, which will help advance the goals of Mott-supported projects.

title: Durant Plaza Planning
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide funds for a landscape architect to develop a feasibility study and scope of work for improvements to Durant Plaza, which is located between the Sloan Museum of Discovery and the Whiting on the Flint Cultural Center campus. This space is frequently used by campus institutions and partners for a wide variety of community and family activities such as the Crim Kids Classic and Holiday Walk. The architect will provide recommendations for improvements that will increase safety, accessibility and functionality of the space.

title: Partnership for Disaster Recovery and Resilience
description: The program goal is to promote the recovery and resilience of Central American communities impacted by Hurricanes Eta and Iota and prepare them to respond more effectively to future disasters. To this end, the Inter-American Foundation is providing grant support, through the Partnership for Disaster Recovery and Resilience, to civil society organizations that build community resilience; mitigate the impacts of extreme weather; and strengthen the economic, civic and social ties among community members. A grant increase will allow for current and possible additional subgrantees in Central America to learn more about effective community philanthropy practices, in particular through dialogues and exchanges with community foundations in Costa Rica and Mexico. The Inter-American Foundation is an independent United States government agency created by Congress in 1969. It invests in community-led development across Latin America and the Caribbean, directly engaging local leaders, innovators and entrepreneurs in underserved areas to create more prosperous, peaceful and democratic communities.

title: Downtown Flint Crosswalk Assists
description: This grant will allow for the purchase and installation of six crosswalk assists to be placed at key intersections along Saginaw Street in downtown Flint. The crosswalk assists will allow individuals with disabilities to move more freely, connect to opportunities for civic participation and access their communities as their neighbors and peers do.

title: Powered by Youth Voice: Future Directions for Afterschool
description: This grant increase will provide additional funds to ExpandED Schools for the Powered by Youth Voice: Future Directions for Afterschool project. Additional funding and grant extension will allow fiscally sponsored Every Hour Counts to continue supporting the six communities identified in the original grant project, convene a summer virtual meeting with the youth, disseminate the final research report, present on the initiative at the Engage Every Student event in July 2023 and distill lessons learned for the project’s final report.

title: Sustainable Development Finance in South America
description: Asociación Ambiente y Sociedad is a Colombian nonprofit organization dedicated to research, monitoring and advocacy on investment and development finance in Colombia and across South America. During the last grant period, the organization focused on monitoring energy and infrastructure finance while maintaining a publicly accessible website and project database. In the upcoming grant period, the organization will concentrate on continuing its advocacy on climate finance in the Colombian Amazon and strengthening networks of civil society organizations to enhance monitoring of development finance in the region.

title: Upper Midwest CSA Consortium
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: The Upper Midwest Children’s Savings Account Consortium was created in 2017 to expand children’s savings account policies and initiatives across the Great Lakes Region. Renewal funding will enable the City of St. Paul’s Office of Financial Empowerment to: 1) organize the Consortium; 2) support organizations working to advance state and local children’s savings account policies and initiatives; and 3) further the overall children’s savings account movement in the region and nationally. Planned activities include stakeholder outreach and education, technical assistance, networking and peer learning and policy development efforts. The city of St. Paul’s Office of Financial Empowerment was established in 2019 to advance economic democracy that promotes prosperity for all St. Paul residents.

title: Mott Middle/Early College Replication
description: This grant will support Mott Community College as it transitions its role in the research, outreach and replication of early/middle college high schools and programs in Michigan and nationally. The grantee was an early adopter of the early/middle college high school model, offering a blended secondary and post-secondary school design for students that struggle in traditional high schools. The college responds to requests for establishing early/middle college schools and programs at: 1) high schools; 2) community colleges; 3) universities; and 4) career and technical education centers.

title: Promise Early Distribution Scholarship Program
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: Since 2016, the Mott Foundation has supported the Wabash County Promise Initiative — a community-wide initiative designed to advance educational attainment and create a generation of educated, engaged and economically self-sufficient young people. Using research on what shapes college aspirations in children, the Community Foundation of Wabash County and its partners — local nonprofits, three public school districts, two private schools, local businesses and city and county government — harness the power of children’s savings accounts to help students build college-going identities and influence their college aspirations. Interim findings from the evaluation of the Early Award Scholarship pilot identified positive impacts on college savings, college planning and student academic performance. Based on these successes, this grant increase provides tie-off support to continue program operations for two additional years and enable the Community Foundation of Wabash County to ensure program operations continue after the Foundation funding ends.

title: Growing Michigan Together Population Council
description: The Michigan Municipal League Foundation supports innovative work through partnerships, grants and programming that creatively and intentionally bring people together and build equitable community wealth in the state of Michigan. This grant will support the Michigan Municipal League Foundation’s work with the Growing Michigan Together Council to advise the Governor on strategies that will mitigate the state of Michigan’s population decline.

title: Budgeting and Accelerating People Centered Justice
description: ODI-Global will consolidate research into people-centered justice reforms in lower-income countries in order to identify learning, scaling and financing opportunities. Drawing on extensive research carried out to this point, the grantee will work to systematize available information for funders and policy makers to support clearer understanding of justice funding choices. Particular attention will be given to developing and disseminating a policy framework for financing frontline justice services. In 2024-25 and following previous detailed investigations of justice delivery in over a dozen countries in Africa and Asia, the grantee focused attention on the development of a draft financing framework for frontline justice services. The framework and supporting background materials, developed by the grantee and partner organizations within the Justice Action Coalition, represent the most comprehensive case for funding people-centered justice. Established in 1960 and based in the United Kingdom, ODI-Global works to inspire people to act on injustice and inequality through research, convening and advocacy.

title: Advancing Solutions to Water Affordability
description: Elevate Energy, based in Chicago, works nationally to implement programs to ensure access to clean energy and safe and affordable water for all. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee’s water program advanced water affordability and lead service line replacement in partnership with Chicago-area municipalities and community partners. With renewed support, Elevate Energy will continue to build on the success of its water programs to provide solutions to water challenges faced by residents in Chicago and the state of Illinois.

title: Operating Support
location: Marina del Rey, CA, United States
description: This grant will support Mizzen Education, Inc. to increase access to world-class digital learning curricula through the Mizzen by Mott online platform. Specifically, this grant will enable Mizzen Education, Inc. to: 1) increase access to Mizzen’s online curricula and resources for afterschool educators; 2) provide professional development opportunities for afterschool educators; and 3) support the transition of Mizzen from the Mott Foundation to Mizzen Education, Inc., a 501(c)(3) organization, to well-position Mizzen for future growth.

title: Frontline Justice Project
description: The project goal is to build a strong body of evidence to expand justice services in the United States. To this end, Rockefeller Philanthropy Advisors’ Frontline Justice Project will support a nascent, but growing movement of justice workers, a new category of legal helpers specifically trained to support people in resolving their legal challenges. It will do this by executing rigorous research and building a body of evidence on what works in expanding the scope of justice service providers. Frontline Justice is a new project sponsored by Rockefeller Philanthropy Advisors with the aim of giving real meaning to “equal justice under law” as enshrined in the founding documents of the United States.

title: Partnership for Ukraine
description: This grant will provide support for the Czech Environmental Partnership Foundation’s Partnership for Ukraine program. Over the course of this grant period, Ukrainian local leaders from various sectors will undertake seven study visits, in groups of 10-15 persons, to Central European communities. The visits will focus on the topics of climate change adaptation, renewable energy sources, energy efficiency, sustainable reconstruction of buildings and infrastructure, drinking water, wastewater treatment and waste management. Participants will also learn about and experience the processes of local consultation with residents. The grantee will subsequently provide project consulting, connections with Central European experts and networking opportunities among program participants and other Ukrainian local leaders. The Czech Environmental Partnership Foundation is a member of the Environmental Partnership Association, together with its sister foundations from Bulgaria, Hungary, Poland, Romania and Slovakia. These organizations have operated as an informal network to protect the environment and support local communities since the 1990s and they were legally constituted as an association in 2004.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides support to Open Briefing whose goal is to maintain an open civic space for civil society to operate without reprisals and indiscriminate attacks. The grantee plans to address this work at two levels. Firstly, it aims to provide holistic safety and security support to human rights defenders. This support includes physical, cyber and psychological offerings. Secondly, it will use the lessons it learns in providing individual human rights defenders support to be part of global conversations on the importance of maintaining an open civic space. Open Briefing is an organization that builds resilience and resistance among the people and communities that challenge power. Established in 2011, the grantee has thus far answered 347 calls for assistance to human rights defenders in 68 countries.

title: Better Financing for Local Solar Energy Entrepreneurs in East Africa
description: Since 2012, the Kenya Climate Innovation Center has been working to provide business development advisory services and financing to local entrepreneurs creating climate and clean energy solutions in East Africa. With Mott Foundation support, the grantee is providing business development advisory and financing services to local entrepreneurs working to accelerate access to solar energy services for productive use within rural off-grid communities of Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania. With this grant increase, the grantee will organize a regional meeting to facilitate better knowledge sharing, networking and coordination amongst the Mott-supported renewable energy access partners in East Africa.

title: Swahili Coast Community Foundation Development
description: The project goal is to support the development of community foundations in the Swahili coastal region of Kenya. To achieve this goal, the Aga Khan Foundation will increase awareness and interest in the community foundation concept, expand knowledge and understanding among partners and identify initiatives that have the potential to become community foundations. Additionally, the grantee will test resource and asset development initiatives, adapt the concept to the Swahili coast context and develop a long-term plan for expanding the community foundation concept in the region. The Aga Khan Foundation has worked to improve the lives of millions of people globally since 1974 by working with communities to build self-reliance. Additionally, the grantee has been active with communities on the Swahili coast of Kenya for several decades, fostering and building strong relationships with civil society, local government and private businesses. The grantee plans to build on the longstanding history, expertise and relationships to explore the potential for nurturing local community foundations on the Swahili coast.

title: National Partnership for Student Success
description: This grant will support the Everyone Graduates Center at Johns Hopkins University to establish a network hub, the National Partnership for Student Success, to provide technical assistance connecting local education agencies with service providers in five, evidence-based service areas for student recovery: academic tutoring, mentoring, post-secondary transition and student success coaching, and wraparound student supports. Launched by the White House creating a cross-agency partnership between the Department of Education and AmeriCorps, the initiative aims to recruit 250,000 volunteers in these roles over the next three years. The goals of this initiative include increasing the number of school districts implementing these strategies and the number of adult volunteers serving in these roles to improve student outcomes.

title: Monitoring Hydropower Impacts in the Amazon
description: The Getulio Vargas Foundation’s Center for Sustainability Studies is a higher education institution dedicated to promoting sustainable development in Brazil. With previous Mott Foundation support, the grantee worked with civil society organizations and academic institutions in the Amazon to establish the Independent Territorial Monitoring Network and has grown its reach and membership to 70 organizations. With renewed support, the Getulio Vargas Foundation will continue to strengthen the network and its ability to monitor investments by public and private financial institutions as well as facilitate Indigenous peoples’ participation into policy development.

title: Flint's Got Talent Youth Showcase
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will support iMichigan Productions to implement the second Flint’s Got Talent Showcase in partnership with WOW Outreach. The event will take place at the Capitol Theatre in downtown Flint. The talent showcase idea was originally generated by WOW Outreach’s Youth Ambassador program participants. The showcase will feature performances from area teens and young adults and offer live audience voting to select the top act. In 2022, iMichigan Productions worked closely with WOW Outreach to implement the showcase managing all aspects of the event production.

title: Youth Mentorship Community of Practice
description: This grant will support the Mott Community College Youth Mentorship Community of Practice project. The two-year project is designed to provide leadership and financial support to five Black-led mentorship groups that serve youth in the Flint area. In addition to leadership capacity building, the project will promote higher education and workforce opportunities for youth participating in each of the five mentoring programs.

title: Targeted Neighborhood Façade Improvement
description: This grant will support Genesee County Habitat for Humanity in operating its Targeted Neighborhood Façade Improvement Program in the neighborhood surrounding the Durant-Tuuri-Mott campus. In addition to repairing exteriors to homes in the area, the grantee will partner with local organizations to connect residents to additional programs and resources to help with critical home repairs not covered by the Targeted Neighborhood Façade Improvement Program. This work aligns with a core tenet of Genesee County Habitat for Humanity’s mission of bringing people together to build community.

title: Entrepreneur Mentor Pilot
description: This grant to the Ferris Wheel Innovation Center will support the continued growth of Flint’s entrepreneurial ecosystem through development of a mentorship program facilitated by SIPI. By leveraging the insights and knowledge of experienced entrepreneurs and business owners, entrepreneurs will gain the guidance needed to navigate the challenges often faced when starting a new venture. The project includes development of a training program that will ensure continuity in facilitation, development of a pool of mentors and mentor stipends.

title: Health Disparity Project
grantee: American Red Cross — East Central Bay-Michigan Chapter
description: This grant to the American Red Cross of East Central Bay-Michigan in Flint will support the organization’s efforts to address health disparities in Flint and Genesee County. Black residents are disproportionally impacted by sickle cell disease that often requires frequent blood transfusions to alleviate pain and other symptoms. Sickle cell patients have a better response to treatment when blood is donated by someone of the same race or ethnicity. This program aims to triple the number of Black donors by 2025 to better serve patients with sickle cell disease.

title: General Purposes
description: The organization’s goal is to increase access to justice for poor and marginalized people in Rwanda. To this end, Haguruka will provide comprehensive justice services to people in rural communities of Rwanda. Past support has allowed the grantee to assist over 2,000 people with justice services, build the capacity of over 4,000 justice workers, and continue to address systemic injustices facing women and children. Continued support will allow Haguruka to continue providing quality justice services to poor and marginalized rural communities in Rwanda while implementing organizational strengthening initiatives.

title: Capitol Theatre Program Reserve
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide the Flint Institute of Music with funds to attract and market more high-profile and niche genre shows at the Capitol Theatre in downtown Flint. Shows at the theatre provide entertainment, spur economic development and improve quality of life for the Flint area. This grant will enable the Flint Institute of Music to further activate the Capitol Theatre venue and diversify both the types of performances and audiences.

title: Amplifying Youth Voice in Afterschool
description: This grant to Youthprise seeks to empower young people to design afterschool programs of the future. Youthprise will work with the 50 State Network and afterschool leaders to engage young people in policy, practice and quality initiatives that benefit afterschool programs and the youth they serve. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) provide technical assistance to the 50 State Network on youth leadership, voice and choice; 2) support four states to further embed youth voice initiatives in state afterschool initiatives and infrastructure; and 3) explore youth-led grantmaking efforts throughout the project.

title: Early Warning System
geographic_focus: Ecuador, Peru, Brazil, Argentina, Colombia, Bolivia
description: International Accountability Project advocates for development practices that prioritize human rights, environmental protection and community-led development. With Mott Foundation support, the grantee set up and continues to develop the Early Warning System, an online tool supported by a staff team, that organizes information on investments by international financial institutions. Over the past grant period, the grantee continued to develop the Early Warning System and build the capacity of communities to use the information and engage development finance institutions. With renewed support, the International Accountability Project will: 1) curate and use the Early Warning System; 2) support communities and partners; 3) analyze trends; 4) and advocate for sustainable energy and infrastructure finance.

title: Community Education and Afterschool
description: The Flint Center for Educational Excellence — an affiliated entity of the Community Foundation of Greater Flint — will deliver a full-service community education strategy in 15 Flint area schools. The focus for the newly established Flint Center for Educational Excellence in its first year is to integrate community education and afterschool initiatives, which previously were provided by two separate organizations, into a seamless model. The new model will include afterschool programming, adult education, health services, early childhood education connections and parent and community engagement. Best and promising practices from demonstration sites will be shared with other schools in the community to leverage innovation with the goal of helping Flint kids thrive.

title: Network for School Excellence
description: The goal of this grant is to support schools participating in the Network for School Excellence. International Academy of Flint will participate in the Network for School Excellence as it leads a coordinated effort to impact a strategically identified group of K-12 schools serving Flint kids. International Academy of Flint will analyze school-based data and align funding with initiatives designed to improve educational opportunities and outcomes for students.

title: Network for School Excellence
description: The goal of this grant is to support schools participating in the Network for School Excellence. Flint Cultural Center Academy will participate in the Network for School Excellence as it leads a coordinated effort to impact a strategically identified group of K-12 schools serving Flint kids. Flint Cultural Center Academy will analyze school-based data and align funding with initiatives designed to improve educational opportunities and outcomes for students.

title: Network for School Excellence — Durant-Tuuri-Mott
description: The goal of this grant is to support schools participating in the Network for School Excellence. Flint Community Schools will participate in the Network for School Excellence as it leads a coordinated effort to impact a strategically identified group of K-12 schools serving Flint kids. Durant-Tuuri-Mott Elementary will analyze school-based data and align funding with initiatives designed to improve educational opportunities and outcomes for students.

title: Network for School Excellence — Doyle-Ryder
description: The goal of this grant is to support schools participating in the Network for School Excellence. Flint Community Schools will participate in the Network for School Excellence as it leads a coordinated effort to impact a strategically identified group of K-12 schools serving Flint kids. Doyle-Ryder Elementary will analyze school-based data and align funding with initiatives designed to improve educational opportunities and outcomes for students.

title: Network for School Excellence
description: The goal of this grant is to support schools participating in the Network for School Excellence. Carman-Ainsworth Community Schools will participate in the Network for School Excellence as it leads a coordinated effort to impact a strategically identified group of K-12 schools serving Flint kids. Dye Elementary will analyze school-based data and align funding with initiatives designed to improve educational opportunities and outcomes for students.

title: Network for School Excellence
description: The goal of this grant is to support schools participating in the Network for School Excellence. Westwood Heights School District will participate in the Network for School Excellence as it leads a coordinated effort to impact a strategically identified group of K-12 schools serving Flint kids. Hamady Elementary School and McMonagle Elementary School will analyze school-based data and align funding with initiatives designed to improve educational opportunities and outcomes for students.

title: Network for School Excellence
description: The goal of this grant is to support schools participating in the Network for School Excellence. Beecher Community School District will participate in the Network for School Excellence as it leads a coordinated effort to impact a strategically identified group of K-12 schools serving Flint kids. Dailey Elementary School will analyze school-based data and align funding with initiatives designed to improve educational opportunities and outcomes for students.

title: Investing in Community Foundations
description: The program goal is to strengthen the U.S. community foundation field by enhancing community foundations’ leadership in achieving local impact. Since mid-2021, the Council on Foundations has been working to improve its support of community foundations through four areas of specialized engagement: leading on public policy, enhancing Community Foundation National Standards, expanding its community foundation reach and building community through the Sustainable Development Goals. One indicator of its progress thus far is that community foundations membership in the council has increased from 315 in mid-2021 to 383 at present. A grant increase will allow the council to improve and streamline its peer benchmarking data capacity for community and other foundations, develop a new centralized hub for information on Sustainable Development Goal adoption by community foundations and enhance how the council leverages data internally to inform its work. Founded in 1949, the Council on Foundations is a membership organization of private, community and corporate foundations, primarily in the U.S.

title: Understanding the Impact of Chinese Investment and Engagement in Latin America
description: China is home to the largest development finance institutions in the world and has invested over $500 billion in developing countries to support energy, infrastructure and logistics projects. Dialogue Earth (formerly China Dialogue) works with a network of specialist editors based in Latin America, Africa and Asia to provide accurate and sober reporting on China’s development and climate impacts. With prior Mott Foundation support, the grantee consolidated all its reporting within a single multilingual platform and developed a dedicated portal focusing on Latin America. With renewed support, Dialogue Earth continues to report on the impacts of Chinese development finance in Latin America.

title: Partnership for Ukraine
description: This grant will provide support for the Czech Environmental Partnership Foundation’s Partnership for Ukraine program. Over the course of this grant period, Ukrainian local leaders from various sectors will undertake seven study visits, in groups of 10-15 persons, to Central European communities. The visits will focus on the topics of: 1) climate change adaptation; 2) renewable energy sources; 3) energy efficiency; 4) sustainable reconstruction of buildings and infrastructure; 5) drinking water; 6) wastewater treatment; and 7) waste management. Participants will also learn about and experience the processes of local consultation with residents. The grantee will subsequently provide project consulting, connections with Central European experts, and networking opportunities among program participants and other Ukrainian local leaders. The grantee is a member of the Environmental Partnership Association, together with its sister foundations from Bulgaria, Hungary, Poland, Romania and Slovakia. These organizations have operated as an informal network to protect the environment and support local communities since the 1990s. They were legally constituted as an association in 2004.

title: Promotion of Community Foundations in Argentina
location: Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires, Argentina
description: The program goal is to establish a solid base for a community foundation movement in Argentina. To achieve this, over the next 18 months, the Public-Private Lab, a fiscal sponsee of the Group of Foundations and Companies, will focus on: 1) strengthening its capacities as a community foundation support organization; 2) adapting the community foundation model to the Argentine national context; and 3) identifying communities with the potential for its development. The grantee will also conduct strategic communications to promote the model and build leadership and community management capacities through training, mentorship and technical assistance to local leaders. The Public-Private Lab was established in Argentina in 2022 as an initiative to foster multisectoral partnerships that contribute to sustainable and comprehensive development. Established in 2001, the Group of Foundations and Companies is an Argentine civil association composed of foundations and companies committed to sustainable development. Its mission is to promote and mobilize resources strategically for the public good.

title: Michigan Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Michigan Association of United Ways which coordinates the Michigan Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) increase the number of afterschool programs available for young people through supporting the new state afterschool program in Michigan; 2) enhance youth outcomes by supporting youth voice in the design of future afterschool programs and incorporating diversity, equity and inclusion standards; 3) work with education stakeholders and policymakers to design and implement education recovery funding to help Michigan youth recover and thrive; 4) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems; and 5) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen resources.

title: General Purposes
description: Environmental Advocates of New York has been at the forefront of and has made critical progress toward protecting, enforcing and strengthening the policies that impact the health of New York’s water, climate and communities. The grantee works across the state and in the Great Lakes region, prioritizing the needs of communities disproportionately impacted by environmental harm. With renewed funding from the Mott Foundation, Environmental Advocates of New York will continue to advocate for innovative strategies and dedicated funding to advance the priorities of clean water, climate resilience, healthy communities and sustainability in New York state.

title: Great Lakes Leadership Summit
grantee: Conference of Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Governors and Premiers
geographic_focus: Illinois, Minnesota, Ohio, Michigan, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Indiana, New York
description: The Conference of Great Lakes Governors and Premiers signed into law the Great Lakes Compact in 2008. The Compact provides a comprehensive management framework for achieving sustainable water use and resource protection for the Great Lakes. With this grant increase, the grantee will plan and host a gala and symposium to celebrate the 15th anniversary of the Compact in partnership with the University of Michigan in Ann Arbor.

title: General Purposes
description: Formed in 1999, the Funders’ Network is a philanthropy-serving organization that provides support to foundations, nonprofit organizations and other partners working to create equitable, just and environmentally sustainable communities. This renewal grant will provide general purposes support to the Funders Network for all of its programs, including the PLACES Fellowship, a leadership development program, and its Urban Water Funders Group, a working group of funders aligned around issues such as access to safe and affordable drinking water.

title: Energy Distributed to Isolated Communities
description: The Instituto Socioambiental is a pioneer in developing strategies to protect the Amazon rainforest and Indigenous Amazonian communities. This project creates and implements management models for off-grid solar renewable energy systems in remote Indigenous communities, particularly in the Xingu River basin and the Raposa Serra do Sol Indigenous Territory in Roraima. Previous work successfully installed off-grid renewable energy systems and provided training to community members. Over the next grant period, the grantee will continue offering technical training and support to ensure the successful replication, implementation and management of off-grid solar energy solutions in these territories. Additionally, it will monitor federal renewable energy universalization programs while engaging with civil society and regulators to enhance the effectiveness of these programs’ implementation.

title: Comprehensive Evaluation
description: The Community Foundation of Greater Flint, through the Flint Center for Educational Excellence, will contract for research and evaluation services of its educational initiatives. The goal is to evaluate overall impact of both the Flint Center for Educational Excellence and the initiatives it operates to move the needle on academic outcomes and measures of well-being for Flint kids.

title: Good Laundry
description: This grant to the United Way of Genesee County will support the physical build-out of Good Laundry, a project on the north side of Flint that combats hygiene poverty by giving low-income residents access to laundry facilities. Studies show that one in five students go to school in the U.S. wearing dirty clothes. By providing families with access to laundry facilities, a chronic barrier to student success can be eliminated and chronic absenteeism could potentially be reduced.

title: Capacity Building
description: This grant will provide funding to support the fundraising and leadership development capacity of the Shelter of Flint. The grantee is an essential human service organization serving individuals and families in need of a safe place to stay. The grantee receives a high percentage of its funding from the government which is often reimbursement-based and allows limited, if any, funds for overhead or indirect costs. Through increased fundraising and leadership capacity, the Shelter of Flint aims to raise unrestricted dollars from individuals and organizations in order to remain nimble, and address the needs of its clients and facilities in a timely manner.

title: Neighborhood Violence Prevention
description: This grant will support the work of the Community Foundation of Greater Flint and its partners to engage in violence prevention strategies. This will include trainings for community organizations and residents in areas such as conflict resolution, communication, mediation and mentoring. As part of this grant, community conversations will engage residents in high risk areas of Flint to develop long-term, trusted relationships that can help to prevent violence. Funds will also support community-based grief support.

title: Planning
description: This grant to the Neighborhood Engagement Hub will support a planning phase for neighborhood community development work. The organization will engage residents and other key stakeholders to design a neighborhood planning process that focuses on safety, stabilization, blight elimination and long-term economic development. Once the plan is developed, the Neighborhood Engagement Hub will work with neighborhoods throughout the city to create a customized community development plan for each area, including implementation plans that leverage existing resources and new opportunities.

title: Downtown Flint Arches
description: This grant to the United Way of Genesee County will provide funds for the Genesee County Historical Society to make improvements to the nine arches located along Saginaw Street in downtown Flint. The work will include structural and stabilization repairs, painting and the installation of LED lights. In 1899, the Saginaw Street arches were among the first of its kind to bring electrical lighting to a community main street in the United States. They have since become a source of community pride, celebrating Flint’s proud carriage industry heritage that put Flint on the global map.

title: Flint River Testing and Monitoring
description: This grant to the University of Michigan-Flint will support ongoing monitoring and testing of the Flint River. The testing will be conducted in partnership with the Flint River Watershed Coalition and analyzed by qualified laboratories. Testing will monitor the levels of a variety of chemicals in the river and will expand the number of sites that have historically been tested. The Flint River is currently used for a variety of activities such as fishing, kayaking and tubing. Contact with the river is expected to increase substantially once the in-river construction of the Flint River Restoration Project is complete.

title: Berston Field House Capacity Building
description: This grant to the Friends of Berston will build organizational capacity in the areas of fund development, marketing and organizational sustainability. The grantee’s mission is to impact the community through education, athletics, arts and community services. The nearly 100-year-old Berston Field House facility hosts a variety of events that bring residents together to celebrate with one another and to connect with programs and resources throughout the community.

title: Centennial Celebration
description: Mott Community College is celebrating its 100th anniversary in September 2023. Over the past 100 years, the college has served Flint area students with educational opportunities leading to degrees, certificates and credentials in a broad array of careers. The college will host a community celebration to recognize its history and raise awareness about the ongoing opportunities available to Flint area students of all ages.

title: Student Analytic and Advocate Support Systems
description: With this grant, Mott Community College will pilot a system designed to increase degree and certificate completion for its students. The first aspect of this strategy is aimed at adult learners and will include using attendance and academic data to serve as an early alert for students who may need extra support. This support will be coordinated through two advocates. The second aspect is to conduct a nationwide scan of early alert systems to determine which might be implemented at the college to support all students.

title: Reconnecting Fathers with Families and Work
description: With this grant, InvolvedDad will strengthen families through parental engagement. The grantee will empower men to be engaged fathers by providing training, coaching and peer support in a safe environment. The program utilizes a combination of research-based techniques and approaches informed by mentors that have struggled with the crisis of fatherlessness firsthand. The mentors encourage men to face the issues and wounds that prevent them from being fathers, address those issues head-on and then empower the men with tools and techniques to manage fatherhood.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint
description: This grant increase provides general purposes support to the Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint. This increase will allow the grantee to provide needed additional compensation for critical staff. The grantee focuses on education, creativity, physical activity, and health and family support services while offering year-round programming to young people between the ages of 7 and 17 in the Flint area. The grantee operates two sites, one located on the east side and the other on the south side of the city. Programs such as this have been instrumental in mitigating the negative effects of both the water crisis, as well as the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic. By providing students with highly engaging educational and enrichment opportunities in a safe and supportive environment, the Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint continues to stay true to its mission of enabling young people in the Flint area to reach their full potential.

title: Educator Pipeline and Retention, Planning
description: The Education Trust will support its Midwest division to develop an analysis of the educator workforce landscape for schools that serve Flint kids. Specifically, this grant will support: 1) a landscape analysis of educator workforce initiatives in Michigan; 2) an analysis of the workforce challenges for local schools and afterschool providers; and 3) a comprehensive set of recommendations to address workforce challenges.

title: Expanding Education Opportunities Through Children's Savings Accounts
grantee: National Association of State Treasurers Foundation, Inc.
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: In 2022, 16 states were implementing statewide children’s savings account initiatives. The Mott Foundation’s support will enable the National Association of State Treasurers Foundation to create a forum where its members can learn about savings strategies, network with peers around the country and share best practices and innovations. Activities planned during the two-year grant period include virtual and in-person meetings and collection and analysis of data relevant to the administration and oversight of children’s savings account programs. The National Association of State Treasurers Foundation was created in 2000 to promote and improve the educational initiatives of the state treasurers association and its members.

title: Community Schools Film Project
description: The grant will support Stone Lantern Films to advance a documentary film project on the nationwide movement for community schools. Specifically, this grant will support: 1) the development phase of a new community schools’ documentary; and 2) a comprehensive plan to produce the full-length film.

title: Written Insights: Addressing Educational Inequities Through Community Schools
description: The Netter Center for Community Partnerships at the University of Pennsylvania will continue to document and disseminate a book that chronicles the experiences and lessons of the modern-day community schools movement. The book covers cross-cutting themes including partnerships, equity, shared leadership, results, policy, research and documentation, communication, capacity building, financing, infrastructure and flexibility. Now that the book is completed, this grant will provide additional support to further disseminate and promote the project to a broad range of stakeholders across the country.

title: Flint Diaper Bank
description: This grant will provide funds to the Food Bank of Eastern Michigan to support the Flint Diaper Bank in providing diapers to low-income Genesee County residents. By utilizing the grantee’s integrated distribution system, the Flint Diaper Bank can ensure that diapers will reach the community’s most vulnerable families.

title: Basic Needs Support
description: With this grant, St. Luke N.E.W. Life Center will provide basic needs support to participants in its existing programs and residents who live in the surrounding neighborhood. Following the Flint water crisis and the COVID-19 pandemic, the grantee has seen increased demand for emergency housing, food assistance and transportation needs. The center will partner with other area agencies to leverage basic needs funds and help meet the needs of Flint families.

title: Trauma Informed Campus Design
description: This grant to Whaley Children’s Center will provide funds to upgrade facilities on its campus. The grantee is a residential facility that serves children from age five to 17 who have been abused and/or neglected. The trauma that these children experience impacts both short- and long-term development and behaviors. Recent developments in the field of trauma-informed care suggest that the physical environment has a significant impact on children who have experienced trauma. Whaley Children’s Center is undergoing a broad effort to implement trauma-informed design practices across its campus. This project will install acoustic treatments, which help eliminate extraneous noise, in the family game room and other recently renovated spaces.

title: Technology and Information Systems Capacity Building
description: This grant to Factory Two, Inc. will support a pilot program focused on technology capacity building for Flint area nonprofits. Led by a program manager and an advisory group of local technology providers, the program will offer technology assessments, mini-grants and access to free and low-cost technology resources. Most nonprofits do not have information technology staff onsite and rely on external expertise for recommendations, implementation and ongoing support. This program will offer these services through a trusted, local nonprofit organization.

title: Technical Advisory Support to Local DREEM Partners in Kenya and Uganda
description: EED Advisory Limited is a multidisciplinary Pan-African consulting firm providing technical, analytical and advisory services in the cross-cutting sectors of energy, water and climate change. With this grant, EED Advisory Limited will provide strategic technical guidance and support services to local nonprofits in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda that seek to secure better funding opportunities in order to advance the productive use of solar energy services in key agricultural value chains in the two countries.

title: General Purposes
description: The Groundwork Center for Resilient Communities has promoted sustainable community practices in Michigan since 1995. With partial support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has provided policy leadership in its home region of northwest lower Michigan in support of a clean environment, a strong economy and resilient communities. The grantee pursues its agenda in the priority areas of food and farming, clean energy, Great Lakes protection and transportation. With renewed support, Groundwork Center for Resilient Communities will continue working in all of its priority program areas, including expanding and strengthening the Great Lakes Business Network.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Heart of the Lakes Center for Land Conservation Policy
description: Heart of the Lakes Center for Land Conservation Policy is Michigan’s only organization whose mission is to serve and support land conservancies in the Great Lakes state. With prior Mott Foundation funding, the grantee: 1) continued to advance the work of its members and partners to protect and invest in land and water; 2) initiated urban conservation services; and 3) facilitated coalitions to promote the outdoors. With renewed funding, Heart of the Lakes Center for Land Conservation Policy will focus on investing in public lands, ensuring equitable access to the outdoors and supporting conservation organizations in communities all around the state.

title: Advancing Decriminalization of Poverty and Status
description: The International Legal Foundation will work together with diverse stakeholders within United Nations structures to consolidate principles and guidelines on the elimination of discrimination in law enforcement and criminal justice systems. Together with United Nations member states, civil society justice actors, academics and others, the grantee will help complete research and drafting of these standards. These standards will be introduced for review and adoption by relevant United Nations bodies, including the United Nations Human Rights Council and the Commission on Crime Prevention and Criminal Justice. In the period 2023-25, an expert meeting convened by the grantee published an initial report on combatting discrimination in criminal justice systems. This was followed by development of 22 draft principles on ways to eliminate discrimination in justice systems for discussion and review by relevant United Nations bodies. Founded in 2001, the grantee works to address the global crisis in access to justice through improvements to legal aid provision and related policies. International Legal Foundation works both in specific countries in Africa and Asia, while also advocating for policy change globally.

title: JUST Ukraine: Empowering Communities for Access to Justice
description: Right to Protection will provide a range of legal support and services to internally displaced as well as persons affected as a result of Russia’s invasion of Ukraine. Working across 22 regions of the country, the grantee will provide responsive legal information, assistance, and where appropriate, litigation to ensure justice needs are met. The grantee will train judges and their assistants, while also providing wider legal education services to the public. Additionally, the grantee will address systemic legal issues that may act as barriers to conflict-affected groups securing their rights. During 2023 through 2025, the grantee provided over 150,000 legal consultations through its multiple online and offline channels. The grantee prepared a comprehensive study assessing impacts on victims of the war, their compensation needs and access to legal remedies. Formally established in 2013, Right to Protection is dedicated to protecting the rights of asylum seekers, refugees, stateless and undocumented persons as well as internally displaced and conflict affected persons.

title: General Purposes
description: The Grand Traverse Regional Land Conservancy, founded in 1991, is a land trust serving a five-county region located in northwest lower Michigan. In total, the conservancy has protected over 48,000 acres of land and 157 miles of shoreline along the region’s rivers, lakes and streams. During the last grant period alone, the conservancy: 1) protected 1,300 acres of land and over three miles of shoreline; 2) opened one new public nature preserve; and 3) enrolled two of its existing preserves in the nationwide Old Growth Forest Network. With renewal support, the Grand Traverse Regional Land Conservancy will pursue a range of land and water quality protection projects, continue to promote collaborative conservation projects with partners and build organizational strength and staff capacity.

title: Data-Driven Progress for Access to Justice
description: The program goal is to produce new knowledge on legal needs globally. The World Justice Project will work along three key activity areas — data collection and analysis, policy advocacy and technical assistance — to strengthen the evidence base for people-centered justice reform. This will include: 1) developing justice policy measurement frameworks; 2) identification of key tools and technologies to adapt and adopt justice innovations efficiently; and 3) capacity-building for justice sector actors in diverse country contexts. In 2024-25, the grantee generated a wide variety of research findings and analytical reports, including detailed assessments of the rule of law, democracy and justice across 110 subnational regions in the 27 European Union member states as well as other countries as diverse as Colombia, Malawi, the Dominican Republic and Uzbekistan. The grantee also launched the Warsaw Principles for the Rule of Law at the World Justice Forum. Established initially as a project of the American Bar Association in 2006, the World Justice Project was formally registered as an independent organization in 2009 working to advance the rule of law around the world.

title: Kindergarten to College Program
grantee: City and County of San Francisco
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: The City and County of San Francisco’s Kindergarten to College program was the first municipal children’s savings account program in the country. Since its inception in 2011, the program has opened savings accounts for more than 56,000 students, motivated thousands of low- and moderate-income families to save millions of dollars, and inspired replications in cities and states around the country. Last fall, researchers found that the program significantly boosted students’ on-time high school graduation and postsecondary enrollment, establishing a critical proof point for the children’s savings account movement. Renewal funding will support continued implementation and help the City and County of San Francisco prepare for the next phase of program operations, which will emphasize family outreach and engagement strategies as well as integration with California’s statewide college savings account initiative.

title: Michigan State University Flint Campus Expansion
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant increase will provide additional funding to the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation — a supporting organization of the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation — for the completion of the construction of a new office and meeting space for Michigan State University’s College of Human Medicine’s Flint campus adjacent to its existing space in the former Flint Journal Building. The additional space will both accommodate the expansion of public health expertise and resources in Flint and contribute to the vibrancy of the Health and Wellness District in downtown Flint.

title: Paterson Building Renovation
description: Communities First will purchase and renovate the Paterson Building, a historic building located on Saginaw Street in downtown Flint. The building is currently blighted and has been condemned. The renovations will help reactivate the Paterson Building, contributing to the vibrancy of downtown Flint. The renovated space will include office and commercial usage. Communities First will relocate its offices into the downtown space.

title: Michigan News and Information Programs
description: This grant provides funding to the University of Michigan’s Michigan Radio in support of its news and information service. Located in Ann Arbor, Michigan Radio is a trusted media brand in the state known for its fair and fact-based coverage of state, national and international news. Michigan Radio reaches its audience with radio content, podcasts, websites, social media and mobile apps, providing news and information to help create a more engaged public.

title: PFAS Action Network
description: Since 1970, the Ecology Center has operated as a national nonprofit focused on issues related to toxic chemicals, including per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), in the environment. With prior Mott Foundation support, the grantee and its partners within the Great Lakes PFAS Action Network organized the National PFAS Conference. The grantee provided information on the impact and management strategies of PFAS to Michigan policymakers and other stakeholders. With continued Mott Foundation support, the grantee will support impacted communities to improve their communications and engagement with public officials and businesses on PFAS-related concerns. Additionally, the Ecology Center will broaden the direct engagement of the Great Lakes PFAS Action Network in more states across the Great Lakes region.

title: Operating Support
location: Marina del Rey, CA, United States
description: This grant will continue to support Mizzen Education, Inc. in its efforts to increase access to world-class digital learning curricula through the Mizzen Education, Inc. online platform. Specifically, this grant will enable the grantee to: 1) increase access to Mizzen’s online curricula and resources for afterschool educators; 2) provide professional development opportunities for afterschool educators; and 3) support the transition of Mizzen from the Mott Foundation to Mizzen Education, Inc., a 501(c)(3) organization to well-position Mizzen for future growth.

title: Pathfinders for Peaceful, Just and Inclusive Societies: Civil Society Participation & Voice
description: The Pathfinders for Peaceful, Just and Inclusive Societies program of New York University is a multi-stakeholder platform that seeks to promote solutions to overcome the global lack of access to justice. In 2024-25, the University, through its Pathfinders program, cemented its position as a co-secretariat of the Justice Action Coalition, a partnership of over 20 member states and civil society partners that promote people-centered justice. In this role, the grantee helped advocate for new models of financing justice and communicating about the need for justice in society. The University also helped launch the African Alliance for People-Centered Justice, while continuing to support of its Ibero-American counterpart. In 2026-27, the grantee will continue its core activities in support of people-centered justice. These activities will include: 1) enhancing its role within the Justice Action Coalition, 2) strengthening regional alliances for justice, 3) piloting the Justice Financing Framework with select countries; and 4) producing new analytical research and policy briefs. Additionally, the University will pilot new activities including the fostering of an Asia-Pacific Alliance for People-Centered Justice identifying new strategies for bridging the justice gap and developing new justice partnerships at sub-national levels.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant supports Open Briefing to maintain open civic spaces and human rights that allow community-driven solutions to flourish. The grantee provides holistic security support to grassroots individuals and organizations to strengthen their physical security, digital resilience and collective wellbeing. During the previous grant period, the grantee: 1) received 1,127 calls for assistance from civil society organizations, community groups and social movements at risk; 2) performed 10,705 hours of mentoring and accompaniment; and 3) trained more than 2,039 at-risk people in 226 holistic security workshops around the world. During 2025 to 2028, the grantee will disrupt attacks and reprisals against those at the frontline by providing holistic security mentoring and accompaniment in high-risk cases and emergency contexts, notably via its rapid response mechanism. Open Briefing will also produce resources and guides in multiple languages and build collective capacity through addressing gaps in community-based support around the world.

title: Renewable Energy Access for Sustainable Livelihoods and Conservation in the Amazon
description: This project supports the World Wildlife Fund, a global conservation organization with a robust presence in the Amazon region, to expand and replicate renewable energy access projects in the Amazon. With previous Mott Foundation support, the grantee helped communities in Bolivia and Colombia install solar systems that lowered costs and emissions, improved livelihoods and promoted women’s participation. With renewed support, the grantee will build on these pilots, expand awareness and strengthen advocacy to speed adoption of renewable systems. The World Wildlife Fund will also share data and lessons learned with authorities and local governments to encourage renewable energy access and inform territorial development planning.

title: Network for School Excellence
description: The goal of this grant is to support schools participating in the Network for School Excellence. Carman-Ainsworth Community Schools will participate in the Network for School Excellence, leading a coordinated effort to impact a strategically identified group of K-12 schools serving Flint kids. Dye Elementary will analyze school-based data and align funding with initiatives designed to improve educational opportunities and outcomes for students.

title: Network for School Excellence (DTM)
description: The goal of this grant is to support schools participating in the Network for School Excellence. Flint Community Schools will participate in the Network for School Excellence as it leads a coordinated effort to impact a strategically identified group of K-12 schools serving Flint kids. Durant-Tuuri-Mott Elementary will analyze school-based data and align funding with initiatives designed to improve educational opportunities and outcomes for students.

title: Network for School Excellence (DR)
description: The goal of this grant is to support schools participating in the Network for School Excellence. Flint Community Schools will participate in the Network for School Excellence as it leads a coordinated effort to impact a strategically identified group of K-12 schools serving Flint kids. Doyle-Ryder Elementary will analyze school-based data and align funding with initiatives designed to improve educational opportunities and outcomes for students.

title: Frontline Justice Project
description: The project goal is to expand justice services in the United States. To this end, Rockefeller Philanthropy Advisors will support a nascent, but growing movement of justice workers, a new category of legal helpers specifically trained to support people in resolving their legal challenges. The grantee will do this by executing rigorous research and building a body of evidence on what works in expanding the scope of justice service providers. In its first year, this initiative brought together over 150 justice actors for the first time to exchange experience on effective community justice work. The grantee also worked with 14 state level Access to Justice Commissions to identify opportunities for engaging more widely with community justice work. Frontline Justice is a new project sponsored by Rockefeller Philanthropy Advisors with the aim of giving real meaning to “equal justice under law” as enshrined in the founding documents of the United States.

title: General Purposes
description: The project goal is to address systemic injustices facing poor and marginalized people in South Africa. To this end, the Black Sash Trust ensures that all people in South Africa have access to their socioeconomic rights, as enshrined in the South African Constitution. Past support allowed the grantee to continue working with advice offices in monitoring the implementation of social grants in South Africa, convene a civil society working group on basic income support, uncover corruption in South Africa’s social grants system, and litigate to ensure the government delivers on its constitutional rights relating to social security. This grant will assist the grantee to continue this work with the advice offices. The grantee will work towards ensuring that the right to social security and social assistance is protected, realized and advanced. The grantee was founded in 1955 by a group of women who were fighting for the recognition of human rights for all in South Africa. The Black Sash Trust’s aim is to contribute to the creation of a society that has effective laws and comprehensive social protection for the most vulnerable.

title: Mariachi Music & Folklorico Dance Instruction
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to El Ballet Folklórico Estudiantil will support mariachi music and folkloric dance education and instruction in Flint. The majority of participants are Hispanic; however, the program is open to all interested young people. Program participants showcase their talent and newly acquired skills at community events and concerts. Classes take place at the Latinx Technology and Community Center. The program fee is extremely low and does not cover the full cost of staffing. This grant will help ensure continued high-quality instruction and access for any child who wishes to participate, regardless of ability to pay.

title: Network for School Excellence
description: The goal of this grant is to support schools participating in the Network for School Excellence. International Academy of Flint will participate in the Network for School Excellence, leading a coordinated effort to impact a strategically identified group of K-12 schools serving Flint kids. International Academy of Flint will analyze school-based data and align funding with initiatives designed to improve educational opportunities and outcomes for students.

title: Network for School Excellence
description: The goal of this grant is to support schools participating in the Network for School Excellence. Beecher Community School District will participate in the Network for School Excellence, leading a coordinated effort to impact a strategically identified group of K-12 schools serving Flint kids. Dailey Elementary School will analyze school-based data and align funding with initiatives designed to improve educational opportunities and outcomes for students.

title: 21st Century Community Learning Centers Institute
description: This grant will support Foundations, Inc. to offer comprehensive services and supports to enhance high-quality learning experiences and professional development opportunities to 21st Century Community Learning Centers’ leaders and the afterschool field. These events include: 1) expert panel discussions; 2) interactive workshop experiences; 3) content partner showcases; 4) virtual learning supports; and 5) social media events. The learning experiences for afterschool and summer learning educators will expand their strategies and skill sets to enhance the quality of school and community-based out-of-school time programs.

title: Network for School Excellence
description: The goal of this grant is to support schools participating in the Network for School Excellence. Westwood Heights School District will participate in the Network for School Excellence as it leads a coordinated effort to impact a strategically identified group of K-12 schools serving Flint kids. Hamady Elementary School and McMonagle Elementary School will analyze school-based data and align funding with initiatives designed to improve educational opportunities and outcomes for students.

title: Network for School Excellence
description: The goal of this grant is to support schools participating in the Network for School Excellence. Flint Cultural Center Academy will participate in the Network for School Excellence as it leads a coordinated effort to impact a strategically identified group of K-12 schools serving Flint kids. Flint Cultural Center Academy will analyze school-based data and align funding with initiatives designed to improve educational opportunities and outcomes for students.

title: Comprehensive Evaluation
description: The Community Foundation of Greater Flint – through the Flint Center for Educational Excellence – will contract for research and evaluation services of its educational initiatives. The goal is to evaluate the overall impact of both the Flint Center for Educational Excellence and the initiatives it operates to move the needle on academic outcomes and measures of well-being for Flint kids.

title: Comprehensive Evaluation
description: The Flint Center for Educational Excellence will contract for research and evaluation services of its educational initiatives. The goal is to evaluate the overall impact of the initiatives as a whole as well as the individual initiatives it operates to move the needle on academic outcomes and measures of well-being for Flint kids.

title: General Purposes
description: The YMCA of Greater Flint has long been an important part of the Flint community. The grantee operates three sites: a downtown Flint facility, a Pierson Road facility and Camp Copneconic. Since 1961, the headquarters building in downtown Flint has provided essential services for physical and mental wellness, as well as serving as an important gathering place for the community. However, the building is dated, inefficient and costly to operate. This grant provides general purposes support to allow the YMCA of Greater Flint to maintain its services, including keeping the downtown location open.

title: Capacity Building
description: This grant will support the Genesee Area Focus Fund to increase the staff capacity at its supported organization, the Flint & Genesee Group. Mott Foundation support will allow the Group to meet the current and future needs of large-scale developers and next generation employers of Genesee County. This grant will provide funding for two positions that will focus on the future of industry and workforce development in order to increase positive economic development outcomes.

title: Freshwater Lab Internship Program
grantee: The Board of Trustees of the University of Illinois
description: Since 2016, the Freshwater Lab at the University of Illinois Chicago has: 1) trained emerging water sector leaders with different backgrounds through individualized student internships; 2) supported 16 student internships at 16 different organizations within the Greater Chicago area; 3) completed research on industrial water reuse; 4) exposed students to the latest innovations in Great Lakes policy and governance; 5) strengthened networks among host organizations; and 6) directly supported over 60 students in water management projects, such as beach clean ups, guest lectures, research and public outreach. Continued Mott support will allow the Lab to fund 15 additional student internships, continue its research on industrial water reuse, expand the network of host organizations and improve its fundraising in order to support the long-term sustainability of the Freshwater Internship program.

title: Recruiting and Retaining Diverse Educators
description: This renewal grant will support Education Trust’s continuing work to increase the diversity of the educator workforce by educating stakeholders about effective solutions to improve the recruitment and retention of teachers of color. Objectives planned for the renewal grant period include: 1) continuing to increase awareness of viable and sustainable strategies to increase the diversity of the educator workforce, including building the afterschool staff-to-teacher pipeline; 2) informing federal and state policies to increase the diversity of the educator workforce, including by increasing investments in teacher residency models that provide opportunities for afterschool staff of color to become teachers; and 3) conducting additional research to inform the field’s understanding of the best ways to recruit, prepare and support more diverse educators. Based in Washington, D.C., Education Trust is a research and advocacy organization working to close opportunity gaps and raise achievement for students of color and students from low-income families.
