title: Defining Big Trends that Impact the Future of Education
description: Recent trends, such as the COVID-19 pandemic, national discussions on race and potential changes in the federal role in education, have significantly affected the education field. Understanding how these and other trends may impact instruction and learning is important for efforts to transform education systems and improve outcomes for young people. This grant will support Nelson Mullins Riley & Scarborough LLP in continuing their work with Education program grantees to: 1) identify key drivers of change over the next decade; 2) assess their implications for education and youth development; and 3) develop strategic responses. Planned activities include developing resource materials, in-person and virtual presentations and a recorded webinar series. Nelson Mullins is a U.S. law firm with extensive consulting experience in policy, strategy, corporate law and advocacy aimed at improving the U.S. education system.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Central America, Canada, United States, Mexico
description: Justice in Motion provides legal support to immigrants as they migrate from their home countries into the United States. During the previous grant period, the grantee facilitated cross-border immigration protection and legal services through its Defender Network, hosted virtual trainings on migration issues and immigration law and reunified families. During this grant period, the grantee will work on: 1) immigration protection for asylum seekers; 2) reunifying families; 3) migrant labor rights; and 4) expansion of the Defender Network. Founded in 2005, the grantee was originally called Global Workers Justice Alliance and focused on providing legal assistance and expertise to migrant workers. In 2016, the grantee changed its name to Justice in Motion and expanded its mission to include humanitarian immigration and civil rights work.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purposes support to the American Immigration Council as it works to assist immigrants and improve the overall immigration system. The grantee: 1) manages a network of nearly 16,000 lawyers and law students, interpreters and social workers that provide support for immigrants; 2) conducts impact litigation and advocacy; 3) researches and analyzes immigration policy; and 4) collaborates with civic and business leaders to develop plans that improve the social and economic well-being of immigrants. Founded in 1987, the American Immigration Council focuses on working toward a more fair and just immigration system that opens its doors to those in need of protection and harnesses the skills that immigrants bring.

title: Great Lakes Journalism in Canada
description: The Narwhal is a nonprofit, online news magazine that publishes in-depth and investigative journalism about the natural world in Canada while striving to include First Nation/Indigenous voices in every article. In 2023, The grantee joined the Great Lakes News Collaborative, a Mott-funded partnership among several newsrooms. The grantee has been a valuable contributor to the Great Lakes News Collaborative, producing and sharing articles that increased its collective audience and raised public awareness of important issues that affect ecosystems and communities across the Great Lakes basin. With renewed support, The Narwhal will continue to produce outstanding coverage of Great Lakes issues for its readers and the other media outlets in the Great Lakes News Collaborative.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support the Center for Michigan in pursuing its mission of making Michigan a better place by encouraging greater understanding and involvement in policy issues among the state’s citizens and making sure their voices are regularly heard.

title: Brownell Holmes Renovation
description: This grant will support the Flint Community Schools to develop and renovate Brownell STEM Academy and Holmes STEM Middle School Academy, creating a K-8 education campus in Flint. Specifically, this grant will support: 1) renovations for Brownell STEM Academy and Holmes STEM Middle School Academy; 2) construction of a Cube, innovative community facility; 3) campus improvements to athletic fields and student play structures; and 4) development of an early childhood wing in Brownell.

title: Downtown Flint Arches
description: This grant to the United Way of Genesee County will provide funds for the Genesee County Historical Society to improve the nine arches along Saginaw Street in downtown Flint. The work will include structural and stabilization repairs, painting, and the installation of LED lights. In 1899, the Saginaw Street arches were among the first of its kind to bring electrical lighting to a community main street in the United States. They have since become a source of community pride, celebrating Flint’s proud carriage industry heritage that put Flint on the global map.

title: Galvanizing Sustainable Development Goals Engagement Among Community Foundations
description: The goal of the project is to advance the adoption of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals by community foundations in the U.S. as a means to enhance their community leadership role. CFLeads will begin the project by developing a case statement for U.S. community foundation engagement with the Sustainable Development Goals. It will then establish a community of practice of 10 community foundations with varied experience in applying the goals to their work. Over the course of two years, through a guided peer learning process, these community foundations will help the grantee develop a tool for aligning a community foundation’s work with the goals and executing an implementation plan. The grantee will also create a strategy and program for engaging community foundations in learning opportunities around the goals as well as a document that demonstrates the relevance and importance of tying the work to activate the goals to community leadership practices. CFLeads is a U.S.-based national network of community foundations committed to community leadership.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides funding to an organization focused on the advancement of community foundations in Australia. To this end, Community Foundations Australia will foster the establishment of new community foundations in underserved regions, strengthen the organizational capacity of existing community foundations, and align the activities of community foundations with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, emphasizing local priorities and needs to maximize relevance and impact. Activities will include: 1) developing an Australian community foundation “SDG Playbook”; 2) conducting workshops and training sessions for staff, board members and volunteers of Australian community foundations; 3) conducting community needs assessments that are aligned with the goals; and 4) developing partnerships with other relevant stakeholders in order to implement the goals on the local level.

title: Community Foundation Climate Collaborative
description: The goal of this project is to build the awareness and capacity of community foundations to use the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals as a tool for aligning and informing their work around climate change and climate justice. To this end, the Community Foundation Climate Collaborative will build awareness of the goals among its members and incorporate the goals’ framework into its learning sessions and in-person convenings. The collaborative will build the capacity of its members to identify meaningful targets and indicators for their environmental and climate-related priorities and develop cases of those that illustrate the practices and benefits of incorporating the goals into their climate change and climate justice grantmaking. The Community Foundation Climate Collaborative currently has 46 members in the United States. It is part of a larger network, the Community Foundation Opportunity Network, whose fiscal sponsor is the New Hampshire Charitable Foundation.

title: Building a Movement to Ensure Water is Affordable Nationwide
description: Nearly one in three Americans struggle to pay their water bills on time. A robust federal water affordability program would help address this problem. The Water Foundation, a grantmaking organization supporting innovative water policy initiatives nationwide, will lead a multi-stakeholder scoping process to assess the feasibility of establishing such a program.

title: Michigan News and Information Programs
description: This grant provides funding to the University of Michigan’s Michigan Public in support of its news and information service. Located in Ann Arbor, Michigan Public is a trusted media brand in the state known for its fair and fact-based coverage of state, national and international news. Michigan Public reaches its audience through radio content, podcasts, websites, social media and mobile apps, providing news and information to help create a more engaged public.

title: Swahili Coast Community Foundation Development
description: The project goal is to support the development of community foundations in the Swahili coastal region of Kenya. In 2024, the Aga Khan Foundation piloted the community foundation model in Mombasa, Kilifi, Kwale and Lamu. A total of 16 initiative groups were established after several consultation meetings, training on the community foundation concept and a learning visit to South Africa. Since the start of the pilot, the initiative groups have engaged with authorities on their intention to establish community foundations, consulted with communities on the main issues affecting their development, tested fundraising activities and raised in-kind support. Additionally, the initiative groups collectively raised over $13,000 in cash and in-kind contributions within the first six months of the project. During this grant period, the grantee will support the initiative groups to become community foundations by assisting with their legal formation, establishing a governance structure, building capacity for resource mobilization and engaging communities effectively. The Aga Khan Foundation has worked to improve the lives of millions of people globally since 1974 by working with communities to build self-reliance. In Kenya, the Aga Khan Foundation has offices in Nairobi and Mombasa.

title: Sacred Heart Tiny Home Village
grantee: Catholic Charities of Shiawassee and Genesee Counties
description: This grant will provide support to Catholic Charities of Shiawassee and Genesee Counties to build a community of tiny homes that will house men and women who have served in the military regardless of discharge status. Included in the plans for the village are 26 units of 280-400 square-foot tiny homes, eight of which will be Americans with Disabilities Act compliant, and a community resource center. This first of its kind project will provide not only transitional housing to homeless veterans, it will also provide wraparound services and a supportive community of neighbors with a similar life experience.

title: Property Acquisition and Renovation - 641 S. Saginaw
description: Communities First will purchase and redevelop the building at 641 S. Saginaw St., a historic building located in downtown Flint. The building is currently condemned, partially collapsed and in need of stabilization. The redevelopment of the building will make it available for future commercial usage, contributing to the vibrancy of downtown Flint.

title: University Avenue and Downtown Blight Removal
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: The Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation is a supporting organization to the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation and a public charity that works to improve the quality of life of Flint residents. The grantee’s downtown revitalization efforts and investment in infrastructure provide people with access to jobs, food, health care and other essential services. This grant will support the demolition of blighted structures and improved safety for University Avenue and downtown residents and college students living in the area.

title: Project Brainy: Building Resiliency and Addressing Learning Loss
description: This grant will support McLean Hospital’s Institute for the Study of Resilience in Youth in implementing a new afterschool curricula focused on supporting youth mental health, wellness and accelerated learning. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) work with the 50 State Network and Mizzen Education, Inc. to implement the “Project Brainy” curricula nationally; 2) develop trainings for afterschool educators to implement the program; 3) work with Mizzen Education, Inc. to develop content for its platform; and 4) conduct an evaluation of the program’s impact on youth.

title: News and Information Programs
description: This grant provides funding to National Public Radio in support of its news and information service. The grantee is recognized as one of the nation’s leading providers of non-commercial news, information and cultural programming, and it is dedicated to offering objective, trusted information about the events shaping the world. Each week, over 43 million people are reached through radio, podcasts, websites, social media and mobile apps with news and information to help create a more engaged public.

title: Rx Kids Cash Allowance Pilot
description: Michigan State University will partner with University of Michigan and GiveDirectly to implement and research the impact of an innovative prenatal and infant cash allowance initiative that seeks to advance health equity by proactively addressing maternal and infant economic instability. Rx Kids leans on the science of early childhood and the lifelong consequences of exposure to early adversity. The pilot program aims to fill a scientific gap in health disparities research with a community-level disruption of poverty before and during early childhood, when it is most prevalent and most toxic. Through Rx Kids, expectant mothers in Flint will receive a one-time prenatal cash transfer of $1,500, and all infants will receive monthly allowances of $500 per month in their first year of life. The initiative will impact approximately 1,200 Flint mothers and their newborns per year.

title: Gateway to Youth Entrepreneurship Program
description: Since 1987, the Network for Teaching Entrepreneurship has held to the belief that entrepreneurship education has the power to open doors for youth in under-resourced communities. During this grant period, the grantee will implement strategies to further expand its youth entrepreneurship programming, especially for young people in low-income communities, through its BizCamps, which are designed to inspire students to pursue their future careers, including small business startups. Funding will also support the Entrepreneurial Spirit Awards, highlighting youth entrepreneurship programming to nationwide stakeholders.

title: City Leaders Engaged in Afterschool Reform
description: This grant will support the National League of Cities Institute to engage city officials in developing high-quality afterschool and summer learning initiatives at the federal, state and local levels. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) strengthen the capacity of city leaders to partner with school superintendents and community-based organizations to support programs funded through the American Rescue Plan Act; 2) continue to raise awareness among municipal leaders in building high-quality afterschool and summer learning systems; 3) expand access to afterschool programs as part of the United States Department of Education’s Engage Every Student Initiative; and 4) work with the Mott Foundation to support future planning efforts to benefit the afterschool sector and the young people it serves.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides continued support to Grantmakers for Education, a leading national association that works to advance the field of education philanthropy. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) sustain and improve overall programming and communication activities that help education grantmakers succeed in their work; and 2) provide staffing support and coordination to the Out-of-School Time impact group to increase access to high-quality out-of-school time experiences for young people.

title: Grantmakers for Thriving Youth
description: This grant supports Grantmakers for Thriving Youth, a project of the National Public Education Support Fund, facilitating and convening a group of funders in education, child and youth development and other allied fields. The project is a funder’s forum that promotes equitable systems, structures and opportunities for a comprehensive approach to learning and development so all young people can build and strengthen skills and capacities they need to thrive in learning, work, citizenship and life. Over the course of the project the grantee will: 1) convene a funders group to create grantmaking strategies to support conditions for youth thriving in education; 2) deepen funder understanding of strategies to advance equity and youth voice in the grantmaking sphere; and 3) create space for learning and collaboration to support a healthy education workforce.

title: Identifying Promising Practices
description: This grant will continue to support American Institutes for Research to increase evidence-based quality afterschool programs for young people. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) identify current state and local systems supporting afterschool program quality; 2) provide ongoing technical assistance and up-to-date resources to the 50 State Afterschool Network and the afterschool field; 3) serve on the national advisory for the 50 State Afterschool Network; and 4) work with the Mott Foundation to support future planning efforts to benefit the afterschool sector and the young people it serves.

title: Sylvester Broome Empowerment Village Facility Assessment
description: This grant will provide funds for Sylvester Broome Empowerment Village to engage an architectural and engineering firm to conduct a comprehensive facility assessment. The building — a former Flint elementary school — was constructed in 1921. Presently, the facility is used for a variety of afterschool and summer programs for young people. The assessment will provide recommendations for maintenance needs and immediate short- and long-term repairs.

title: Building Policy Capacity for Lean Funders
description: The project goal is to deepen and expand the work of Exponent Philanthropy to support and encourage lean funders across the country to engage in and fund civic engagement and policy advocacy. The grantee will enhance the advocacy-related elements of its most popular tools, resources and programming to provide its network with accessible and innovative approaches to locally-led advocacy at the city, state and federal level. With nearly 1,600 members, Exponent Philanthropy is the largest philanthropic network in the country and the only membership association that specifically focuses on families, companies and individuals who practice philanthropy with few to no staff — called “lean philanthropy.”

title: MSU Dairy Store Feasibility Study
description: This grant will provide funds for Michigan State University to undertake a feasibility analysis of locating a Michigan State University Dairy Store outlet and retail space in downtown Flint. Downtown Flint has many existing retail, restaurant and bar businesses, but fewer with family offerings. The Michigan State University Dairy Store would diversify the existing mixture of food offerings by adding ice cream and contribute to the economic success of downtown Flint by attracting new visitors. The scope of study will assess the economic, market, technical, financial and management feasibility of locating a store in downtown Flint.

title: Michigan Powerplants to Parklands
description: Older coal-fired powerplants are being retired across the country, including in Michigan. The Environmental Law and Policy Center — a regional environmental group based in Chicago — sees an opportunity to transform these Michigan sites by reusing some of the land for parks and recreation, and some of the land and existing infrastructure for new renewable energy generation. With prior support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee worked with a private utility, community groups and other stakeholders to assess the viability of this approach at a retired coal plant site near Bay City, Michigan. An additional one year of support will allow the Environmental Law & Policy Center and its partners to complete the assessment.

title: General Purposes
description: The American Conservation Coalition was founded in 2017 to be a unifying voice for grassroots conservatives, particularly younger people, who want their leaders to address the climate crisis. The grantee undertakes work in three major areas: 1) growing grassroots support; 2) influencing the media landscape; and 3) educating grasstop stakeholders. Over the last year, the grantee enjoyed considerable success, highlighted by over 600 media hits with a 200% membership growth and 20 million social media impressions. With partial support from the Mott Foundation, the American Conservation Coalition will continue the full range of its activities, including growing its membership and expanding its media presence.

title: General Purposes
description: Reducing the risks of climate change is vital to the United States’ long-term economic and national security interests. The Conservative Coalition for Climate Solutions provides conservative thought leadership in this critical and complex policy arena. Broadly speaking, the grantee promotes a set of policy ideas meant to: 1) increase and diversify U.S. energy supplies; 2) accelerate energy innovation; 3) build a resilient and reliable infrastructure; and 4) steward healthy environments while expanding economic freedom. With prior Mott Foundation support, the grantee advanced these ideas by: 1) educating conservative policymakers and other stakeholders; 2) strengthening coalitions of conservative organizations involved in climate and energy conversations; and 3) growing the organization’s online news magazine and other public communications. With renewed support, the Conservative Coalition for Climate Solutions will continue this full range of activities including the publication of signature documents, such as “Free Economies are Clean Economies,” and high-level participation at major events such as the United Nations conference on climate change in Azerbaijan.

title: Food and Agricultural Climate Alliance
description: Scientists estimate that approximately one-third of the greenhouse gas emissions reductions needed by 2030 must come from absorbing climate pollution in forests, wetlands, grasslands and agricultural land. In 2020, the Environmental Defense Fund — a major national environmental organization — helped convene and launch the Food and Agriculture Climate Alliance, a group of more than 80 agricultural and environmental leaders that promote shared climate policy priorities. Over the last year, the grantee has helped build support for climate-smart agricultural practices by: 1) networking with state and regional producer groups; 2) engaging in strategic communications; 3) educating policymakers about the advantages of climate-smart agricultural practices; and 4) producing reports on the benefits of such practices. With renewed support from the Mott Foundation, the Environmental Defense Fund will continue a similar range of activities over the next year, including efforts to demonstrate the benefits of climate-smart agricultural programs recently created at the federal level.

title: Ecoright Landscape Mapping
description: Climate change has become a politically polarizing issue in the United States. Fortunately, there are signs that this may be beginning to shift. A small, but growing, network of nonprofit organizations and leaders is working to equip stakeholders with information and ideas to help build durable bipartisan solutions to climate change. With this grant, DEPLOY/US — a key organization focused on building the ecosystem of nonprofits and leaders working right of center on climate change as a crucial foundation for bipartisan action — will identify pathways to scale the capacity and impact of this field.

title: General Purposes
description: As the world’s largest economy and second-largest source of greenhouse gas emissions, the United States must play a leadership role in addressing the climate crisis. Citizens Climate Education, a national group, works to build a diverse and well-informed citizenry to actively engage in civic processes that enable climate policy advances, regardless of the political party in power. With general purposes support from the Mott Foundation, Citizens Climate Education will expand the number and diversity of its grassroots volunteer members and help them through education and training to make climate solutions a top-tier issue across the country.

title: Promoting Bioeconomy Financing for the Amazon
grantee: Nonprofit Enterprise and Self-Sustainability Team, Inc.
description: The Nonprofit Enterprise and Self-Sustainability Team, Inc. promotes the growth of resilient small businesses, associations and cooperatives. Since 2020, the grantee has been supporting community-led sustainable economic ventures in the Amazon. During the previous grant period, the grantee conducted in-depth research and formulated insights from existing forest enterprises. Using these findings, they developed policy recommendations specifically tailored for development finance institutions to secure their support for low-impact, forest-based economic activities led by local Amazon communities. With renewed support, the grantee will expand the reach of the recommendations to a wider audience within the development finance sector and foster meaningful dialogue and partnership between local communities and development finance stakeholders. The project aims to establish the bioeconomy as a significant investment sector and to ensure that investments are available in a way that effectively supports community-driven forest economies while contributing to forest conservation.

title: Sustainable Energy Finance and Development
description: Operation Native Amazon is a Brazilian nongovernmental organization that protects the Amazon rainforest, rivers and Indigenous communities. The project supports the grantee’s collaboration with local partners to address the environmental and social repercussions of hydroelectric and oil and gas ventures in the Middle Jurua and Juruena River basins. With this increase, Operation Native Amazon will amplify community advocacy and mobilization efforts, facilitate public dialogues and foster knowledge and strategy exchange between communities across both territories.

title: Impacts of Investments of the Brazilian National Development Bank on Regional Sustainability
description: The Instituto Socioambiental is a Brazilian nonprofit dedicated to addressing environmental and social challenges in the Amazon. Over the previous grant period, the grantee collaborated with local partners and Indigenous communities to monitor the social and environmental impacts of large-scale infrastructure and energy projects in the Xingu River basin, offering technical and strategic communications support. In the upcoming grant period, the grantee will enhance community-led monitoring initiatives and provide technical assistance for specific projects, recommending safeguards for investors. Instituto Socioambiental will also produce and disseminate knowledge on large-scale infrastructure projects’ cumulative impacts on Indigenous peoples.

title: Capacity Building
description: This grant will support the Genesee Area Focus Fund to increase the staff capacity at its supported organization, the Flint & Genesee Group. Mott Foundation support will allow the the Flint & Genesee Group to meet the current and future needs of large-scale developers and next generation employers of Genesee County. This grant will provide funding for two positions that will focus on the future of industry and workforce development in order to increase positive economic development outcomes.

title: College Promise Campaign
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant will enable the College Promise Campaign at Rockefeller Philanthropy Advisors to continue embedding children’s savings accounts into traditional College Promise programs to further expand their impact and help students earn their certificates and degrees. In its fourth phase, the grantee aims to: 1) expand the College Promise – Children’s Savings Account Peer Learning Network from 66 to 80-plus communities; 2) increase the number and quality of children’s savings accounts embedded in local and state College Promise programs; 3) expand awareness about the impact of children’s savings accounts in the College Promise movement; and 4) work with children’s savings account researchers and thought leaders to incorporate detailed integrated children’s savings account program information into the Expanding the College Promise database and MyPromise, making it publicly available to students, families, programs and practitioners.

title: Dunamis Ukraine: Powering Civil Society and Local Communities
description: The goal of this project is to support civil society resilience in Ukraine. Dunamis Ukraine is an initiative aimed at empowering Ukrainian civil society with essential skills and knowledge for recovery and reconstruction, elevating citizen voices at the local level, and nurturing the next generation of leaders for Ukrainian civil society. The initiative will comprise a blend of in-person and remote learning, reaching approximately 100 participants via: 1) a core course; 2) mentoring; 3) research; 4) capstone projects; 5) professional development; and 6) career support. The initiative is integrated within the Invisible University for Ukraine, a hybrid certificate program of the Central European University that has reached over 600 graduate and undergraduate students from more than 70 Ukrainian universities since spring 2022. Founded in 1991, the Central European University is an undergraduate and graduate-level “crossroads” university where faculty and students from more than 100 countries come to engage in interdisciplinary education, pursue advanced scholarships and address some of society’s most vexing problems.

title: Technical Advisory Support to Local DREEM Partners in Kenya and Uganda
description: EED Advisory Limited is a Pan-African consulting firm that has provided technical, analytical and advisory services to advance solutions in energy, water and climate change since 2013. This grant increase and associated grant period extension will allow the grantee to implement its Distributed Renewable Ecosystem Model Fellowship program for two additional years. To ensure continuity of the program, EED Advisory Limited will also evaluate and implement strategies to secure sustainable and long-term funding from diverse sources.

title: General Purposes
grantee: National Network of Local Philanthropy Development in Ukraine
description: This grant will help to support the development of community foundations in Ukraine. Initially established in 2014, the National Network of Local Philanthropy Development in Ukraine became active in 2019 as a full-fledged community foundation support organization. Its purpose is to develop social capital and philanthropic culture for the sustainable development of communities in Ukraine. Currently, the grantee supports its 15 community foundation members through: 1) capacity building; 2) communication; 3) advocacy; 4) regranting funds; and 5) building an enabling environment for philanthropy. The grantee also supports YouthBank Initiatives. The grantee intends to apply general purposes funding to improve its organizational capacity through additional skills training for the staff. National Network of Local Philanthropy Development in Ukraine will also upgrade its website, conduct a study on philanthropy in Ukraine, publish a magazine about philanthropy, and create and publish a course on philanthropy.

title: Property Demolition
description: This grant will provide Kettering University with support to demolish the property it owns at 1222 Glenwood Ave. The Glenwood Avenue property borders the new state park that sits in the heart of Flint. This project will encourage the revitalization of the neighborhood that homes the state park. It will create a space where locals, as well as tourists, can convene for an array of activities. This is a critical step in the ability to create a safe, sustainable green space that will promote a healthy community and enhance the beautification of the state park.

title: Summerfield Early Childhood Education Center Improvements
description: With this grant, the Genesee Intermediate School District will manage facility improvements to the former Summerfield Community School, which is currently being used as an early childhood education center owned by Flint Community Schools and operated by the intermediate school district. Repairs and upgrades will include a new roof, boiler system and windows; a replaced parking lot; and a reconfigured main entrance. Together, the updates will lead to increased energy efficiency, improved building access and aesthetics, and an enhanced learning environment for the young children and their families at the center.

title: General Purposes
description: The purpose of this grant is to provide comprehensive support to internally displaced persons and others affected by the conflict in Ukraine. Through a network of online and offline legal advice centers, Gorenie will provide legal, social and psycho-social assistance to displaced victims of conflict in four regions — Dnipropetrovsk, Zaporizhia, Kharkiv and Ukraine-controlled Donetsk — bordering on the conflict zone that have continued to be home to large populations of displaced persons. The grantee will provide training services for local officials to improve service delivery and integration practices related to target groups. The grantee will also work to build the self-organizing capacity of these target groups. In 2020-2023, during the period of the pandemic and subsequent full-scale invasion of Ukraine, the grantee provided legal, social and humanitarian assistance to over 300,000 people affected by conflict. Based in Dnipro, Gorenie was founded in 2005 to provide wide-ranging assistance to disadvantaged and marginalized groups throughout Ukraine.

title: TAP Network
description: The goal of this project is to support organized civil society participation to increase peace, inclusion, and access to justice globally. The Transparency, Accountability, and Participation Network — a project of the Proteus Fund — will mobilize its membership of over 270 civil society organizations for coordinated action around implementation of Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 16, with its focus on peaceful, just and inclusive societies. During this grant period, work will focus on: 1) mobilizing, engaging and building capacity of civil society partners to foster a global network focused on advancing SDG 16; 2) building civil society capacity to evaluate SDG 16 implementation; and 3) sharing and learning to develop knowledge, practice and public understanding around efforts to promote peaceful, just and inclusive societies. In 2022-23, the grantee produced a series of practical resources for civil society actors working to promote participation and accountability in addressing SDG 16. It further sought to strengthen regional network members and worked to ensure that under-represented voices were heard at United Nations and related events. Founded in 1994, the Proteus Fund convenes and facilitates donor collaboratives that strategically focus philanthropic resources toward the realization of a just, equitable and democratic world.

title: Health and Equity Impacts of the Flint State Park
description: This grant will support a research study to evaluate the health and equity impacts of Flint’s new state park. Researchers at Michigan State University will leverage data from the Flint Registry, a database created to assess health outcomes of residents impacted by the water crisis, to recruit residents to participate in the three-year study. The team will use cutting edge data collection methods to assess the psychological, biological, health, environmental and behavioral outcomes of residents who have improved access to parks. Results will be shared with residents, community partners and the environmental field.

title: STEM Fellowship
description: This grant to the STEM Next Opportunity Fund will support the out-of-school time and STEM fellowship network. The fellowships are a public-private partnership initiative geared toward advancing cross-agency partnerships to expand access to high-quality afterschool, summer learning and informal STEM learning for youth and families. This initiative will work to: 1) strengthen collaboration across several federal agencies in the areas of afterschool and informal STEM learning; 2) advance afterschool and STEM learning in the 21st Century Community Learning Centers program; and 3) collaborate with leading researchers to identify priorities, new tools, strategies and programs that improve afterschool and STEM learning opportunities.

title: Film Appreciation Academy for Youth
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide funding to iMichigan Productions, Inc. for a film appreciation program for youth in Flint. Working with partners across the community, including nonprofits and school districts, the grantee will offer courses and events that explore filmmaking, including potential careers in the industry. Filmmaking is a complex process and offers a variety of career pathways for those who are interested in the art form or the more technical aspects of the industry, such as sound engineering and editing. This program will explore all facets of filmmaking.

title: Protecting Water Quality and Ecosystems in Indiana's Lake Michigan Watershed
description: The Conservation Law Center is a statewide organization working to conserve lands and improve water quality through Clean Water Indiana, its statewide water policy program to address multiple problems impacting water resources in the state and region. As a pro bono legal and technical assistance provider, the grantee has a proven track record of success in improving the quality and accelerating the pace of environmental progress in Indiana and across the Great Lakes basin. This grant from the Mott Foundation will help advance the goals of Clean Water Indiana, including support of a legal aid program to assist communities in the Lake Michigan watershed disproportionately impacted by environmental harm.

title: Empowering Midwestern Environmental Justice Organizations Addressing Water Equity
geographic_focus: Minnesota, Wisconsin, Ohio, Indiana, Illinois, Michigan
description: The Midwest Environmental Justice Network — a project of the Minneapolis Foundation — is led by and for community-based organizations in a twelve-state area. The Network connects and supports grassroots groups and diverse leadership to address environmental issues impacting their communities at the local level. The Network has grown partner engagement on environmental policies and programs in Great Lakes states. With this grant increase, the grantee will take advantage of a new opportunity to advance the goals of the Network.

title: Early Wealth Building Initiative
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: Leaders across the political spectrum have shown increased interest in establishing saving and investment accounts at birth. Through its Early Wealth Building Initiative, the Aspen Institute’s Financial Security Program aims to leverage this interest to expand these accounts nationally. Over the next five years, the initiative will prioritize two main objectives: 1) developing and diversifying a bipartisan and cross-sector group of leaders and stakeholders who support early wealth accounts; and 2) inform policy discussions with evidence-based, high-quality program design and implementation principles. Planned activities during the initial grant period include policy research and analysis, convening and coalition-building, and policymaker and public education. Founded in 1949, the Aspen Institute is a global, nonprofit organization dedicated to fostering a free, just and equitable society.

title: Michigan Communities for Financial Empowerment Network
grantee: Community Economic Development Association of Michigan
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: The Community Economic Development Association of Michigan works to expand and strengthen financial security in communities across the state. Since 2011, the Mott Foundation has supported the grantee’s efforts coordinating statewide engagement and education activities that increase awareness and support for children’s savings accounts. With this grant, the grantee will focus on expanding access to children’s savings accounts across Michigan. This proposed project scope will work to: 1) improve Children’s Savings Account Network engagement; 2) increase access to resources and provide responsive technical assistance to children’s savings account programs; and 3) strengthen the overall impact and sustainability of children’s savings account efforts in Michigan. This project promises significant long-term benefits for Michigan’s students and the state’s overall economic well-being.

title: Expanding Education Opportunities Through Children's Savings Accounts
grantee: National Association of State Treasurers Foundation, Inc.
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: Renewed support from the Mott Foundation will enable the National Association of State Treasurers Foundation, Inc. to: 1) build on the success of the recently formed children’s saving account forum; 2) continue connecting state children’s savings account program administrators and its other members to learn about savings strategies; 3) provide networking opportunities for program administrators; and 4) share best practices and innovations. Activities planned during the two-year grant period include virtual and in-person meetings and collection and analysis of data relevant to the administration and oversight of children’s savings account programs. The National Association of State Treasurers Foundation was created in 2000 to promote and improve the educational initiatives of the state treasurers’ association and its members.

title: Children's Savings Account 10-Year Progress Assessment
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: The current Education program plan concludes in December 2024. OE Consulting will work with Foundation staff and grantees to assess the collective progress made from 2015 through 2024 toward the approved outcomes for the children’s savings account grantmaking strategies. The study will include interviews with current and former grantees, staff and other relevant field stakeholders. Findings will be shared with Foundation staff, management and grantees to help inform future strategic directions in the children’s savings account field.

title: Mission of Mercy Free Dental Clinic
description: This grant to the Michigan Dental Association Foundation will support the organization’s efforts to host a two-day dental clinic in Flint that will address the most pressing dental care needs of as many as 2,000 local residents. The two-day event, Mission of Mercy Free Dental Clinic, will enable residents — regardless of their income or insurance status — to receive no-cost dental treatment and dental education.

title: Flint River Watershed Coalition Leadership Transition
description: This grant to the Genesee County Parks and Recreation Commission will support the Flint River Watershed Coalition as it navigates a leadership transition. Since 2021, the coalition has experienced significant turnover in the executive director role. Beginning in October 2023, the grantee has loaned a staff person with significant nonprofit leadership and grants management experience to serve as acting director at the coalition. In partnership with the Genesee County Parks & Recreation Commission, the coalition board has agreed to retain the acting director until May 2025, at which time a permanent leader will be named.

title: General Purposes
description: This renewal grant will allow the Afterschool Alliance to continue its efforts to ensure that young people and families — particularly those in underserved communities — will have access to high-quality afterschool and summer learning and enrichment opportunities that inspire achievement in school and life. The grantee has long served as the national leader for the afterschool field, works with federal policymakers to advance opportunities for afterschool and summer learning programs and ensures that exemplary program models inform national, state and local education and youth policy initiatives. The grantee seeks to continue to: 1) lead the field in meeting the needs of young people in afterschool programs; 2) serve as an information source on afterschool programs and resource for policymakers, programs and educators; 3) be an effective voice in its efforts to expand quality afterschool programs and innovative models; and 4) increase access to research and data on the effectiveness of quality afterschool programs. The Afterschool Alliance seeks to work with the 50 State Afterschool Network to support afterschool expansion through federal, state and local afterschool initiatives.

title: General Purposes
description: This renewal grant will allow the Afterschool Alliance to continue its efforts to ensure that young people and families — particularly those in underserved communities — will have access to high-quality afterschool and summer learning, and enrichment opportunities that inspire achievement in school and life. The grantee has long served as the national leader for the afterschool field, works with stakeholders to advance opportunities for afterschool and summer learning programs, and ensures that exemplary program models inform national, state, and local education and youth policy initiatives. In 2026, the grantee seeks to implement the Accelerator for Afterschool Investment, which will coordinate and support efforts to increase access to high-quality afterschool programs funded at the state level. Through the Accelerator for Afterschool Investment, Afterschool Alliance intends to: 1) provide technical assistance to the 50 State Network to advance state afterschool programs; 2) track and report on progress to expand access to afterschool networks in states; and 3) develop and share best practices and other resources to sustain and expand access to afterschool networks for children, youth and families.

title: Atwood Stadium Planning
description: With this grant, Kettering University will conduct a thorough general conditions assessment of Atwood Stadium in partnership with LaBella Associates. The resulting report will provide recommendations for renovations and upgrades. Updates may include: 1) code upgrades; 2) expanded concourses; 3) improved food and beverage stations; 4) the modernization of bowl seating; 5) additional restroom facilities; and 6) enhancements to ensure compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act.

title: General Purposes
description: The Clooney Foundation for Justice works to support those suffering from mass and systemic injustices, because of who they are, what they do, or where they might find themselves. All over the world, journalists and human rights defenders are detained, prosecuted and jailed. Women, girls and minorities are subject to unfair laws and targeted for abuse. Ukrainians are at the forefront of Russia’s aggression, with potential war crimes and crimes against humanity being committed against them. The grantee seeks to address this by: 1) gathering evidence of mass human rights abuses; 2) providing free legal support to victims; and 3) working to ensure that perpetrators are held to account. Established in 2016, the Clooney Foundation for Justice works in more than 40 countries and actively investigates war crimes in Ukraine, monitors sham trials targeting women and journalists, and fights against a global trend of authoritarianism that seeks to punish those who speak truth to power.

title: Lake Erie Protection and Restoration Program
description: The Ohio Environmental Council is a multi-issue, effective and respected statewide environmental organization promoting a healthier and more sustainable Ohio. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee made significant progress in the state and Great Lakes region working on: 1) climate; 2) energy; 3) public engagement; 4) water issues, including toxic chemicals and harmful algal blooms in Lake Erie; 5) water affordability; and 6) infrastructure investments such as lead service line replacement. With this grant, the Ohio Environmental Council will continue to advance the work of its water program and team to address threats to Ohio’s waters and Lake Erie.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purposes support for the Michigan CDFI Coalition to ensure that low- and moderate-income individuals, businesses and communities gain access to the banking system. To meet the goal of increasing access to the banking system, the grantee will: 1) create and provide direct technical training opportunities to low- and moderate-income borrowers; 2) undertake best practice research, sharing and implementation amongst members; 3) ensure no wrong door to enter the banking system, including designing a referral system for borrowers; 4) produce and share reports on banking needs in low- and moderate-income communities based on extensive data collection; and 5) through ongoing education to policymakers, highlight the need for more resources being deployed directly to Michigan community development financial institutions.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purposes support for the Michigan CDFI Coalition to ensure that low- and moderate-income individuals, businesses and communities gain access to the banking system. To meet the goal of increasing access to the banking system, the grantee will: 1) create and provide direct technical training opportunities to low- and moderate-income borrowers and organizations that support those borrowers; 2) undertake best practice research, sharing and implementation amongst members; 3) ensure no wrong door to enter the banking system, including designing a referral system for borrowers; 4) produce and share reports on banking needs in low- and moderate-income communities based on extensive data collection; and 5) through ongoing education to policymakers, highlight the need for more resources being deployed directly to Michigan community development financial institutions.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purposes funding to Michigan Community Capital to ensure that projects benefiting low- and moderate-income individuals in Flint, specifically, and Michigan, more broadly, are supported. Throughout Michigan, communities like Flint are unable to attract significant capital to complete development projects that would benefit low- and moderate-income individuals. In addition to building new housing, the grantee serves as a Community Development Financial Institution and a certified Community Development Entity. In this capacity, Michigan Community Capital provides three resources to assist communities with development projects: 1) New Market Tax Credit allocations; 2) loans, including construction and permanent financing; and 3) technical assistance services.

title: Operating Support
description: This grant will provide operating support funding to Michigan Community Capital to ensure that projects benefiting low- and moderate-income individuals in Flint, specifically, and Michigan, more broadly, are supported. title: Network for School Excellence
description: The goal of this grant is to support schools participating in the Network for School Excellence. Beecher Community School District will participate in the Network for School Excellence, leading a coordinated effort to impact a strategically identified group of K-12 schools serving Flint kids. Dailey Elementary School will analyze school-based data and align funding with initiatives designed to improve educational opportunities and outcomes for students.

title: Technical Assistance and Capacity Building
description: The Flint Center for Educational Excellence will continue to lead and coordinate six cooperative efforts: 1) the Flint Early Childhood Collaborative; 2) community education; 3) afterschool; 4) the Flint Parent Collaborative; 5) the Community Council on Education; and 6) the Network for School Excellence. The grantee will contract with technical assistance providers to guide the implementation of each initiative. Best and promising practices will be shared in the community to leverage innovation with the goal of helping Flint kids thrive.

title: 601 to 605 N. Saginaw Street Property Acquisition
description: With this grant, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation will purchase and secure the properties which span from 601 to 605 North Saginaw Street just north of the Flint River. The acquisition will prevent the building on the site from becoming blighted and will position the parcels for future development, contributing to economic development and community revitalization.

title: 601 to 605 N. Saginaw Street Holding Costs
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: With this grant, the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, with its supported organization the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, will maintain and secure the properties that span from 601 to 605 North Saginaw Street just north of the Flint River. Proper maintenance of the property is important to guard against blight and ensure the property is ready for future development, leading to economic development and community revitalization.

title: 1203 Beach Street Acquisition
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: With this grant, the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation will purchase and maintain the property located at 1203 Beach Street, just north of the I-69 highway. The acquisition will prevent the building on the site from becoming blighted and will position the parcels for future development, contributing to economic development and community revitalization.

title: Flint River Watershed Coalition Operations
description: The Flint River and its tributaries are a critical recreational resource for the region’s residents while also providing a vital habitat for a variety of freshwater species and wildlife. The Flint River Watershed Coalition works to protect the Flint River and its tributaries. In 2024, the Coalition became a program of the Genesee County Parks and Recreation Commission. With this grant for operations, the Flint River Watershed Coalition will maintain all of its educational, programmatic and outreach efforts and attend to its organizational development needs.

title: Local Journalism Support
description: This grant to the United Way of Genesee County will provide operating support for Flintside and Flint Beat, two community-based journalism outlets. Flintside and Flint Beat cover news across the city. Both outlets offer an online publication that focuses on information and stories that highlight important community issues that impact Flint residents. While the editorial teams continue to operate independently, the two media outlets have come together to consolidate back-office operations to create more administrative efficiencies and opportunities for staff recruitment and fundraising.

title: Health and Equity Impacts of the Flint State Park
description: This grant will support a research study to evaluate the health and equity impacts of Flint’s new state park. Researchers at Michigan State University will leverage data from the Flint Registry, a database created to assess health outcomes of residents impacted by the water crisis, to recruit residents to participate in the three-year study. The grantee will use cutting-edge data collection methods to assess the psychological, biological, health, environmental and behavioral outcomes of residents who have improved access to parks. Results will be shared with residents, community partners and the environmental field.

title: Technical Support to Maximize Renewable Energy Access Success
grantee: Instituto de Energia e Meio Ambiente
description: The Instituto de Energia e Meio Ambiente is a Brazilian think tank specializing in energy planning and environmental law and policy. This grant supports the development of tools to expand renewable energy access for sustainable livelihoods in the Amazon. With this grant increase, the grantee will assess lessons learned from a decade of experiences by civil society and offer recommendations with pilot renewable energy projects in Brazil. The findings will inform the implementation of Brazil’s federal Light for All program and offer valuable insights on the challenges of universalizing renewable energy in isolated Amazonian communities. Many will benefit from the results, including decision-makers in Brazil and other South American countries, nonprofit partners and the philanthropic community.

title: Energy Distributed to Isolated Communities
description: The Instituto Socioambiental, a nongovernmental organization dedicated to protecting the Amazon rainforest and its Indigenous peoples, is developing model off-grid solar renewable energy systems in the Brazilian Amazon. This grant increase will support a convening in the Xingu River basin territory, one of the first Indigenous areas to receive renewable energy systems under the federal Light for All program. At the four-day networking meeting, community leaders, civil society organizations, energy companies, regulators and other stakeholders will share information, coordinate activities and build stronger partnerships. The goal of this project is to ensure the successful implementation and management of off-grid solar energy systems in the Xingu and apply the lessons learned to broader communities throughout the Amazon region.

title: Institutional Development
description: The Association for Communities Participatory Development is a nonprofit alliance of local councils and territorial communities established in 2020 to develop democratic, open and inclusive local governance by promoting participatory practices and underscoring the significance of resident involvement in local development. Currently, the grantee includes more than 40 local government and civil society representatives, representing 24 territorial communities from seven Ukrainian regions. With an institutional development support grant, the grantee will: 1) establish and formalize a network of past and current project participants; 2) create a platform for knowledge exchange through a robust website; 3) undergo comprehensive strategic planning; 4) support the professional development of staff; 5) upgrade its office equipment and supplies; 6) increase its visibility and influence through better outreach; and 7) establish a monitoring, evaluation and learning framework.

title: CSO Coalition on Human Rights and Counter-Terrorism
description: The project goal is to ensure the protection of civic space and human rights in United Nations counter-terrorism responses. To this end, Saferworld USA, a nonprofit working on preventing violent conflict and addressing the drivers of insecurity, will strengthen the Civil Society Coalition on Human Rights and Counter-Terrorism. Activities will include advocacy, dedicated support for coalition partners and building the capacity of the coalition. This project responds to the growing transnational counter-terrorism architecture and its harmful implications for human rights and civic and humanitarian space. Saferworld USA will build on its efforts in the last four years to improve the discourse on counter-terrorism’s impact on civic space.

title: TAP Network
description: The goal of this project is to support organized civil society participation to increase peace, inclusion and access to justice globally. The Transparency, Accountability and Participation Network, a project of the Accountability Lab, Inc., will mobilize its membership of 250 civil society organizations for coordinated action around the implementation of Sustainable Development Goal 16, with its focus on peaceful, just and inclusive societies. During this grant period, work will focus on: 1) mobilizing and engaging civil society partners to foster a global advocacy network focused on advancing Sustainable Development Goal 16; 2) sharing and learning to develop knowledge, practice and public understanding around efforts to promote peaceful, just and inclusive societies; and 3) collecting and developing compelling stories of civil society promoting peaceful, just and inclusive societies in support of a positive narrative. In 2024-2025, the grantee produced a series of practical resources for civil society actors working to promote participation and accountability in addressing Sustainable Development Goal 16, particularly around key United Nations policy convenings. The grantee further sought to strengthen regional network members and worked to ensure that underrepresented voices were heard at the United Nations and related events. Founded in 2012, the grantee finds new ways to shift societal norms, solve intractable challenges and build “unlikely networks” for change.

title: Downtown Hotel Financial Stabilization Support
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: With this grant, the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation will continue its efforts of downtown revitalization by supporting the future sustainability of the Hilton Garden Inn hotel. The hotel opened in the midst of the COVID-19 pandemic, reducing the number of overnight guests and visitors to the restaurants. The downtown hotel is an important community asset and contributes to downtown Flint revitalization efforts and community vitality. It is an amenity for existing arts and cultural institutions, hospitals, the city’s colleges and universities, as well as a place for guests of Flint and Genesee County residents.

title: Michigan Justice Fund
description: This grant will support the Community Foundation of Greater Flint and its partnership with the Michigan Justice Fund — a collaboration of Michigan philanthropic organizations. The grantee seeks to increase equitable justice across the state through data analysis, coalition building and policy research. It is currently focused on reducing inequalities impacting individuals reentering society after incarceration. This grant will provide greater Flint with representation on the Michigan Justice Fund Advisory Committee and fund groups and organizations in the Flint area that are working with returning citizens through the Community Foundation of Greater Flint.

title: Technical Advisory Support to Local DREEM Partners in Kenya and Uganda
description: Local nonprofits in East Africa receive less than 15% of the total annual grant funding available for climate solutions on the continent. EED Advisory Limited, a local multidisciplinary and Pan-African consulting firm, works to solve this challenge by providing technical, analytical and advisory services to improve the competitiveness of local nonprofits for the available funding. With prior support, the grantee analyzed common requirements of climate funders and assessed the capacity needs of local nonprofits. The grantee also delivered three in-country training workshops to improve the capacity of local nonprofit fundraising for projects on the productive use of solar energy in Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania. With renewed support, the grantee will deepen its capacity-strengthening efforts for local nonprofits on climate fundraising. To this end, EED Advisory Limited will: 1) operate a dedicated technical assistance facility on climate fundraising; 2) run a climate finance fellowship program; and 3) strengthen local nonprofit collaboration opportunities through networking events.

title: Amplifying Youth Voice in Afterschool
description: This grant increase will provide additional funds to Youthprise for the Amplifying Youth Voice in Afterschool project. The grantee seeks to empower young people to design afterschool programs of the future, with additional funding expanding this work. The overarching goal of the project is to embed youth voice and youth leaders as a core part of the 50 State Network infrastructure. With this increase, the grantee will expand its current efforts to embed youth voice initiatives in state afterschool initiatives and infrastructure as well as explore youth-led grantmaking efforts throughout the project. Specifically, additional support will enable Youthprise to support an additional state in creating a youth voice strategic plan within its state afterschool initiative and infrastructure.

title: Engage Every Student Initiative
description: This grant increase will enable the American Association of School Administrators to expand support for the Engage Every Student Initiative, which seeks to establish an afterschool program spot for every youth who needs one through use of education recovery resources, including American Rescue Plan funding. Seizing the opportunity to amplify a new programmatic area and looking forward to a changing funding landscape, the grantee will use this grant increase to: 1) support the July 2024 Engage Every Student Summit, including ensuring Engage Every Student National Recognition Program awardees can attend and share their work; 2) leverage partnerships to create resources for the development of post-American Rescue Plan funding strategies; 3) identify 10 states to deepen technical assistance efforts; and 4) partner with the National Summer Learning Association to elevate best practices for summer learning among local districts.

title: Expanding Educational Opportunities in Michigan
description: With Mott Foundation and partner funder support, the Michigan Association of United Ways is working to establish a public-private partnership initiative to advance afterschool programming for Michigan’s youth and families. The overall goal of this initiative is to ensure that all Michigan youth have access to quality afterschool and summer-learning opportunities. With this increase, the grantee will expand its current efforts to: 1) conduct a robust evaluation of statewide afterschool programs; 2) further develop communications initiatives; and 3) continue to support afterschool expertise and capacity at the state level.

title: General Purposes
description: Established in 1990, the National Council of Nonprofits is the nation’s largest network of nonprofits, representing more than 28,000 organizations across the country. The grantee works through its network of state associations and nonprofit partners to help nonprofits: 1) operate more effectively; 2) engage in critical policy issues affecting the sector; and 3) achieve greater impact in their communities. A grant increase is recommend to support the search and hire of the next President and CEO.

title: General Purposes
description: Alianza Americas’ mission is to bring about a more inclusive, equitable and sustainable way of life for under-served immigrant communities living in the United States and across Mexico and Central America by helping to address the long-standing and emerging issues facing these communities. As the grantee undergoes an executive leadership transition, a grant increase will support a search committee and hiring firm to identify the next executive director.

title: Advancing Afterschool 10-Year Progress Assessment
description: This grant proposes to support the 10-year progress assessment of the Mott Foundation’s Advancing Afterschool portfolio. Specifically, this grant will support: 1) development of a strategic assessment of the 50 State Afterschool Network and major afterschool objective areas; 2) conduct an updated survey of the 50 State Afterschool Network; and 3) conduct an in-depth study of six state networks to inform the Mott Foundation’s future afterschool grantmaking.

title: Michigan Central Station Children's Endowment Initiative
description: This grant to The Children’s Foundation will support the Michigan Central Station Children’s Endowment Initiative. The purpose of the initiative is to help secure the future of 10 Detroit area youth-serving organizations within 15 miles of the Michigan Central Station. The grantee will provide $500,000 to 10 youth-serving organizations to start or grow an endowment. Each organization receiving support will also receive resources to help secure additional matching funds within two years, resulting in the establishment of a $1.5 million endowment. The initiative will lead to ensuring that some of the Detroit area’s youth-serving organizations have an opportunity for financial security, and empowerment to provide environments that lead to brighter futures for youth. Additionally, this grant will provide support to leverage the knowledge, vision and passion of youth to participate in the ideation and development behind the initiative. Young people will also contribute to the assessment process of the selected youth-serving organizations.

title: 21st Century Community Learning Centers Institute
description: This grant will support the expansion of quality afterschool programs through a new initiative entitled “Expanding Out-of-School Time: from Reach to Impact”. Specifically, this grant will support and leverage the annual Beyond School Hours conference and a series of virtual convenings to: 1) increase alignment and coordination of state and federally funded afterschool programs; 2) host a special convening of state and national afterschool leaders to identify opportunities for expansion; 3) provide a series of virtual convenings focused on increasing participation in quality afterschool programs; and 4) support the distribution of Mizzen Education, Inc. curricula to programs.

title: Northwoods, Freshwater and Natural Climate Solutions in Michigan
description: The Nature Conservancy, a global conservation organization with a robust presence in Michigan, is working to protect the state’s natural areas and the climate, freshwater, economic and biodiversity benefits these lands and waters provide. With this grant increase, the grantee will research the feasibility of a new natural resource management public funding mechanism in the state.

title: Alaska Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase will support the Alaska Children’s Trust which coordinates the Alaska Statewide Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase, the grantee will continue to: 1) increase the number of afterschool programs available for young people through state afterschool policy and quality initiatives; 2) work with education stakeholders, program providers and policymakers to reduce disruptions for youth and families as American Rescue Plan funding ends; and 3) work with the Mott Foundation to design future afterschool programs and ecosystems.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Centre for Human Rights Education Advice and Assistance
description: The Centre for Human Rights Education Advice and Assistance will provide free justice services to people who cannot afford them in Malawi, in an effort to increase access to justice for those who are poor and marginalized. The grantee will also use the lessons learned from their work to address systemic injustices faced by Malawians and elevate their stories to policymakers and audiences that matter. Established in 2000, the Centre for Human Rights Education Advice and Assistance works to uphold human rights and the rule of law and provide access to justice to marginalized people in Malawi.

title: Public Safety Support
description: This grant will provide funds to Genesee County in support of the Office of Genesee County Sheriff to increase patrols and responses to crime occurring in the greater downtown Flint area, covering approximately 30% of the city. The Office of Genesee County Sheriff cooperates with law enforcement across the community to proactively prevent crime and to respond when crime occurs. This grant will support additional sergeants and deputies assigned to the area who respond to 911 calls and provide a presence at special events and other large gatherings.

title: Reinvestment Office of Greater Flint
description: This grant to the Greater Flint Health Coalition supports an office within the organization that focuses on the coordination of advocacy and funding efforts geared toward improving the quality of life for Genesee County residents. The goal of the project is to serve as a neutral convener that will work with community partners in the public and private sectors to identify funding opportunities and areas of investment needed to move the needle in a positive direction on Genesee County health rankings.

title: Reinvestment Office of Greater Flint
description: This grant to the Greater Flint Health Coalition supports an office within the organization that focuses on coordinating advocacy and funding efforts geared toward improving the quality of life for Genesee County residents. title: General Purposes
description: UK Community Foundations is a membership organization of 47 community foundations across the United Kingdom. The grantee has supported the development and expansion of community foundations over the years by providing technical assistance, training, data collection, research, marketing, financial assistance and advocacy. Over the next two years, the grantee will continue to focus on supporting and promoting its members to act effectively as community leaders, conveners and funders. The grantee will also support its network to engage meaningfully with the Sustainable Development Goals. This grant increase will support community foundation practitioners from Latin America, Africa and Europe to participate in the UK Community Foundations conference in October 2024.

title: General Purposes
description: Infrastructure and energy projects constructed by development finance institutions like the World Bank and Asian Development Bank often come with environmental, social or governance risks. To address these risks, Accountability Counsel lawyers engage with development finance institutions’ accountability offices to advocate for people harmed by these institutions’ projects in infrastructure and energy. This grant increase is for general purposes, including plans to organize a convening of peer organizations working on the accountability of international financial institutions with the objective of developing an agenda for accountability advocacy over the next five years.

title: Bretton Woods Project
description: ActionAid’s Bretton Woods Project has been a key actor on international financial institution reform issues since it was established in 1995. With previous Mott Foundation support, the grantee helped to lock in World Bank Group commitments to climate change and a green energy transition. The grantee also monitored the impacts of the COVID-19 recovery response, focusing on transparency and accountability for investments in energy and infrastructure. With this increase, ActionAid will help ensure civil society participation in ongoing G20 discussions on the future size, shape and scope of operations of international financial institutions.

title: Operating Support
description: With this grant, Kettering University will provide higher education opportunities for students seeking a hands-on learning environment, a co-op work experience and degrees within in-demand fields. Focus areas include: 1) a highly qualified teaching and administrative staff; 2) engaging and hands-on curriculum and laboratory spaces; 3) marketing and communications designed to attract students who would enjoy and be successful at the university; 4) scholarships to lessen the financial burden of students; and 5) other core initiatives of the school.

title: Expanded Critical Care Programs at C.S. Mott Children's Hospital
description: With this grant, the University of Michigan C.S. Mott Children’s Hospital will reconfigure and optimize the space it has within its current physical footprint to keep up with patient demand for the medical care it is uniquely positioned to provide. Known for its innovation in medical advancements and exceptional patient care, C.S. Mott Children’s Hospital has experienced a consistent increase in demand since its inception.

title: Clean and Affordable Drinking Water: Growing Advocacy and Organizational Capacity in the Great Lakes
geographic_focus: Wisconsin, New York, Michigan, Indiana, Minnesota, Ohio, Pennsylvania, Illinois
description: River Network is a national organization whose mission is to grow and strengthen the nationwide network of water, justice and river advocates. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee provided training, workshops, toolkits and other resources for member groups to advance clean water protections in the Great Lakes region. With renewed support, River Network will continue to build the capacity of and collaboration among various partners to address water challenges facing the region and convene advocates at River Rally, the organization’s national conference.

title: General Purposes
description: Formed in 1999, the Funders’ Network is a philanthropy-serving organization that provides support to foundations, nonprofit organizations and other partners working to create equitable, just and environmentally sustainable communities. This renewal grant will provide general purposes support to The Funders Network for all its programs — including its Urban Water Funders Group — a working group of funders aligned around issues such as access to safe and affordable drinking water.

title: The Water Table
description: Federal and state governments in the United States are making historic investments in water infrastructure. At the same time, water systems across the country are heavily impacted by climate change, while recent court decisions make it more difficult for federal agencies to effectively manage the nation’s water resources. The Water Table funder collaborative, a project of the Water Foundation, addresses such opportunities and challenges by facilitating learning, coordination, and action among funders and partner organizations across the country. With partial support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee will continue to advance strategic water solutions, align and grow water philanthropy, and facilitate and expand a learning community of water funders.
