title: Strengthening and Consolidating the Socio-Environmental Fund Peru
description: Derecho Ambiente y Recursos Naturales is a Peruvian nongovernmental organization that supports Indigenous and grassroots groups in defending their environmental and community rights against the impacts of harmful infrastructure, extractive and energy projects. With prior support, the grantee incubated the Socio-Environmental Fund of Peru, which has since provided small grants and technical assistance to more than 40 local organizations affected by energy and infrastructure development. With renewed support, the Fund will continue channeling small grants for this purpose while also strengthening its institutional capacity to evolve into an independent organization.

title: General Purposes
description: Clean Wisconsin has worked to protect and preserve Wisconsin’s clean water, clean air and natural heritage for over 50 years. An active membership and advocacy base of more than 20,000, along with a staff of experts, helps ensure a safe, healthy environment for all. The grantee, with partners and in coalitions, has advanced policies that protect the Great Lakes, including those that address PFAS contamination, agricultural runoff and urban stormwater issues. With renewed support, Clean Wisconsin will continue to advance its mission through policy advocacy, scientific research, regional collaboration and education, and community engagement to help ensure a more resilient and environmentally just future for the state and the Great Lakes region.

title: General Purposes
description: The Alliance for the Great Lakes is a leading organization working to address and solve some of the biggest environmental challenges facing the region. For over 50 years, the Alliance has been focused on protecting and restoring the Great Lakes, safeguarding clean water and strengthening community resilience. The Alliance for the Great Lakes will continue its efforts to support policies that provide safe, clean and accessible water for residents of the Great Lakes region and ensure the Great Lakes are protected and healthy for future generations.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Michigan League of Conservation Voters Education Fund
description: The most pressing environmental challenges facing Michiganders include: 1) access to safe and affordable drinking water; 2) the impacts of climate change; and 3) the health effects of air pollution. The ability of citizens to effectively participate in the decisions that impact public and environmental health is also a concern. The Michigan League of Conservation Voters Education Fund works to educate policymakers, other stakeholders and the general public about ways to effectively address such challenges. With general purpose support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee will work on a range of water and climate issues while also building its own organizational strength.

title: General Purposes
description: The purpose of this grant is to provide comprehensive support to internally displaced persons and others affected by the conflict in Ukraine. Through a network of online and offline legal advice facilities, Gorenie will provide free primary legal assistance to displaced victims of conflict in regions bordering on the conflict zone. Additionally, the grantee will conduct monitoring and reporting on the conditions facing displaced persons to help inform international assistance efforts, while also implementing legal awareness and economic development training for these communities. In 2024-25, the grantee provided legal, social and humanitarian assistance to approximately 100,000 people affected by conflict. Based in Dnipro, Gorenie was founded in 2005 to provide wide-ranging assistance to disadvantaged and marginalized groups throughout Ukraine.

title: Metropolis Building Facade Improvements
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: With this grant, the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, through its supported organization the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, will make façade improvements to the former Metropolis building in downtown Flint. Repairs to the building’s exterior will improve the aesthetics, contribute to the enjoyment of residents and visitors, help attract new businesses to downtown Flint and ultimately boost the local economy.

title: Great Lakes Water Resources Project
geographic_focus: New York, Indiana, Michigan, Ohio, Minnesota, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Illinois
description: The Great Lakes Environmental Law Center is a nonprofit environmental law organization headquartered in Michigan that provides legal and other technical support on water resource management issues to citizen leaders and local community organizations. With this grant increase, the grantee will also provide financial assistance to its local partners so they can more effectively participate in the public proceedings and processes impacting environmental and public health issues in their communities.

title: Servall Building Repairs
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: With this grant, the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, through its supported organization the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, will make necessary repairs to the former 1st Source Servall Appliance Parts building on Kearsley Street in downtown Flint. The space is now used by two nonprofit organizations — the Flint River Watershed Coalition and Keep Genesee County Beautiful. A properly functioning building is necessary for the two organizations as they lead recreational and educational activities and initiatives that directly and positively impact Flint and Genesee County residents.

title: Orchard Manor and Orchard Grove Construction
description: With this grant, Communities First will construct two new apartment buildings near the intersection of Ballenger Highway and Flushing Road at the border of the city of Flint and Flint Township. Together, the new construction will provide 74 mixed-income housing units located near a commercial corridor and a residential neighborhood. Of the 74 total units, 32 will be permanent supportive housing units. In addition to apartment homes, the buildings will feature space for: 1) community gathering; 2) supportive services; 3) a gym and wellness activities; 4) a children’s play area; and 5) tenant storage. The apartment buildings will help address the need for new and diverse housing options for Flint residents.

title: Foundations for Ukraine
description: The program goal is to foster more effective and increased philanthropic investment into Ukraine’s civil society. To this end, the International Alumni Center in Berlin, Germany will establish a platform for philanthropic actors called Foundations for Ukraine. The platform will: 1) improve coordination and availability of information among funders on the needs in Ukraine, thematic focus areas, approaches and partners; 2) support learning processes that help to make philanthropic activity in Ukraine better informed, more efficient and more effective; and 3) increase philanthropic funding that goes into Ukraine, mainly through increasing the number of funding organizations consistently investing in Ukraine’s resilience, recovery and renewal. Founded in 2017 by the Robert Bosch Stiftung, the International Alumni Center serves as a center of expertise for impact networks in philanthropy and related fields.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Independent Philanthropy Association of South Africa
description: This grant provides general purposes funding to an organization that supports philanthropy infrastructure in South Africa. To this end, the Independent Philanthropy Association of South Africa will: 1) continue to grow its network of philanthropic members in South Africa; 2) influence and learn from a wide network of relationships; 3) advance knowledge and improve philanthropic practice; 4) develop and execute a communications and marketing strategy; and 5) implement a funding strategy in order to meet its goals. Past Mott Foundation support helped the grantee to increase its offering to philanthropic foundations, produce new knowledge on giving, increase its members and grow its institution. The Independent Philanthropy Association of South Africa was established in 2015 as a voluntary association and network to represent and promote its philanthropic members’ common interests, concerns and objectives.

title: Community Water Lab
description: This grant increase to the United Way of Genesee County will support the operations of the McKenzie Patrice Croom Flint Community Lab located at the Flint Development Center on the north side of the city. The lab is equipped with state-of-the-art technology to test water for multiple contaminants. Scientists and staff of the lab, including youth, will work with residents to collect water samples, test for multiple contaminants, provide results and work with households to address any identified issues.

title: Mott Middle College Instructional Delivery Model Analysis
description: With this grant, the Genesee Intermediate School District will examine the instructional model being provided at Mott Middle College, a high school that serves Flint and Genesee County students with nontraditional pathways to college and careers. Engaging subject area experts and community stakeholders, district leadership will identify opportunities to evolve the model to ensure students are prepared for college and career upon completion of the novel high school program.

title: Media Outreach Materials
description: The United Way of Genesee County will serve as the fiscal sponsor for this project, supporting the Flint City Bucks and Flint Style Soccer with the development of a media outreach package to help tell the story about the two soccer programs. Content will be shared through social media, radio, print, television and blogs. The intent is to raise awareness about the programs and the opportunities they bring to Flint, including youth recreation, entertainment for residents and visitors, community vitality and economic development.

title: Strengthening Culinary Programs
description: With this grant, Mott Community College will initiate two strands of work aimed at strengthening its culinary arts program. First, a building manager will be hired to oversee the day-to-day operations, lead an accreditation process, expand open hours and coordinate community events. Second, the culinary facility will offer a series of celebrity chef and community engagement activities. The efforts will collectively reintroduce the Culinary Arts Institute to prospective students and the community.

title: General Purposes
description: The Alliance for the Great Lakes is a leading organization working to address and solve some of the biggest environmental challenges facing the region. For over 50 years, the grantee has focused on: 1) improving water quality and infrastructure; 2) reducing agricultural pollution; 3) stopping invasive species; and 4) restoring the Great Lakes through local partnerships, volunteerism and coalition building. This grant increase is available for the general purposes of the organization, including a new program funded in large part by the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency to advance environmental justice goals in the Lake Michigan basin.

title: Zillion Solutions Program Expansion
description: This grant will support the continuation and refinement of the Zillion Solutions program at the University of Michigan-Flint. Launched in 2017, Zillion Solutions is an annual idea competition created to increase student interest in entrepreneurship, innovation and/or problem-solving. The program is designed to generate participation across all academic units on campus, including dual-enrolled high school students and high school students involved in entrepreneurship programs in Genesee County schools. The program aims to help build a culture of entrepreneurship and innovation throughout the university and beyond. The one-time grant increase will be utilized to create an online Canvas course that will increase student access to the program and address some staffing capacity issues resulting from the program’s growing popularity.

title: Protecting and Promoting Civic Space in Kenya
description: The project goal is to defend and promote civic space and foster a safe and enabling environment for civil society actors. To achieve this, the Defenders Coalition safeguards the work of civil society organizations and human rights defenders working at the frontlines of the rule of law, transparency and corruption. The grantee provides training that builds the capacity of human rights defenders and civil society organizations to respond to imminent attacks resulting from their work. In addition, the grantee convenes activists to build solidarity and encourages collective action. This work enables actors to respond to and mitigate any safety and security risks they face. Recent protests and subsequent violence and intimidation of activists in Kenya have increased the demand for the grantee’s work. This grant increase will support the grantee to expand the scope and reach of its services in support of human rights defenders involved in protests. This will include providing legal, medical and other forms of support. Defenders Coalition is a nonprofit organization based in Nairobi, Kenya. It strengthens the capacity of civil society actors and human rights defenders to work effectively and reduce their vulnerability to the risk of persecution.

title: Flint Health Services Scan
description: With this grant, the University of Michigan will conduct a study to explore opportunities for greater involvement in the Flint area. The study will examine how the C.S. Mott Children’s Hospital could partner with Flint health entities to reduce health disparities and gaps in care for Flint and Genesee County children.

title: Flint Community Lab Operating Plan
description: This grant to the United Way of Genesee County will assist with the creation of a business and operational plan for the McKenzie Patrice Croom Flint Community Lab, as well as staff training and professional development to implement the plan. Opened in 2020, the lab is a unique operation where a community-based water testing site is operated by and for Flint residents. The lab works with area youth, high school and college-aged students to collect water samples from residents to test for toxic substances such as lead and copper and to share information about test results and community resources. The lab is also staffed by a director who oversees operations and a chief chemist who implements the testing protocols and procedures while providing training for interns. The lab was certified by the state of Michigan in 2024.

title: Community Advocacy and Violence Interruption Project
description: This grant to the Hurley Foundation will allow Hurley Medical Center’s sole patient outreach advocate to continue supporting the well-being of Flint residents through health education, reducing barriers to care, and assisting residents and families affected by gun violence while grantee staff continue to work toward securing additional funding for the program. Hurley Medical Center’s ability to employ a culturally competent patient advocate helps create an environment where residents feel their concerns are heard and addressed in a way that aligns with their cultural background. Ultimately this can lead to better health outcomes for residents and a more inclusive health care environment.

title: Flint Steel Drums Program
grantee: Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint
description: This grant will support the continuation of the Steel Drums Program at the Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint. The program has been part of the activities offered by the grantee for over ten years. Due to a leadership transition, this grant will provide one-time funding to train and coach new instructors and continue the program without disruption as new funding sources are pursued for future years. Up to 12 young people will participate and perform at events and festivals throughout the community.

title: Teen Grantmaking Initiative Flint Pilot Program
grantee: Arab Community Center for Economic and Social Services (ACCESS)
description: This grant to the Arab Community Center for Economic and Social Services will support a program called the Teen Grantmaking Initiative. In partnership with the Arab American Heritage Council, a Flint-based organization, the enrichment program will offer an opportunity for diverse teens, including Arab American young people, to increase their civic engagement, leadership skills and knowledge of philanthropy. Participants will learn about and experience assessing community needs, fundraising and grantmaking through this initiative.

title: Better Financing for Local Solar Energy Entrepreneurs in East Africa
description: Since 2012, the Kenya Climate Innovation Center has been supporting local climate entrepreneurs with business development advisory services and affordable financing to advance climate and clean energy services in Kenya. Previous support enabled the grantee to expand its clean energy entrepreneur support services in Kenya and within two additional countries in the region, Uganda and Tanzania. The Center supported 30 entrepreneurs working on the productive use of solar energy services. These solar entrepreneurs, in turn, created 500 jobs and benefited more than 20,000 farmers with various clean energy services. The Center also convened two regional stakeholder meetings that brought together more than 90 different sector stakeholders from the three countries to share lessons and best practices on the productive use of solar energy services in East Africa. With this grant, the Center will consolidate these achievements by establishing a knowledge management platform that documents lessons learned to improve overall performance in the sector. The Kenya Climate Innovation Center also will continue to facilitate regional and in-country collaboration and coordination among various stakeholders.

title: Budgeting and Accelerating People Centered Justice
description: ODI-Global will consolidate research into people-centered justice reforms in lower-income countries in order to identify learning, scaling and financing opportunities. Drawing on extensive research carried out to this point, the grantee will work to systematize available information for funders and policymakers to support clearer understanding of justice funding choices. Particular attention will be given to cost effectiveness and financing needs for adaptation and scaling of successful reforms. From 2021-23, the grantee carried out detailed investigations of justice delivery in over a dozen countries in Africa and Asia. The grantee produced three substantial research reports on its findings and held numerous roundtable discussions with donors and policymakers on its findings. This work helped to clarify understanding of the broad range of justice funding mechanisms and opportunities that are in current operation. Established in 1960 and based in the United Kingdom, ODI-Global works to inspire people to act on injustice and inequality through research, convening and advocacy.

title: Statewide Children's Savings Account Outreach Initiative
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: The state of California has led the Children’s Savings Account movement for over a decade — beginning with San Francisco’s Kindergarten-to-College initiative — which was the first municipal Children’s Savings Account program in the country and has inspired dozens of replications across the state and nationally. In 2021, the grantee announced a universal statewide expansion of the California Kids Investment and Development Savings Program, expected to serve nearly four million participants. Mott Foundation funding will help support outreach and education efforts that raise awareness of, and participation in the expanded program and ensure the aspirational and educational benefits of Children’s Savings Account Outreach Initiative reach the state’s most underserved communities. This project will be led by the ScholarShare Investment Board — the state agency charged with overseeing the state’s 529 college savings program, and designing and implementing the CalKIDS effort.

title: Mizzen Education, Inc. Operation and Growth Support
location: Marina del Rey, CA, United States
description: This grant will continue to support Mizzen Education, Inc. in its efforts to increase access to world-class digital learning curricula through the Mizzen Education, Inc. online platform. Specifically, this grant will enable the grantee to: 1) increase access to Mizzen Education, Inc.’s online curricula and resources for afterschool educators; 2) provide professional development opportunities for afterschool educators; and 3) support the development of Mizzen Education, Inc. as a 501(c)(3) organization to well-position the grantee for future growth.

title: Afterschool and Service-Learning Initiative
location: St. Louis Park, MN, United States
description: This grant will support the National Youth Leadership Council to integrate service-learning into afterschool programs, increasing student engagement in their schools and communities. The grant increase will: 1) engage one additional statewide afterschool network to deepen and expand service-learning into local afterschool programs; 2) create additional resources for successful and sustainable integration of service-learning; 3) support a learning community to share information and best practices on service-learning in afterschool programs; and 4) augment the research and development of a multi-state analysis of policies impacting service-learning implementation.

title: Engaging Older Youth in Service
description: This grant increase will support America’s Service Commissions to expand youth-service opportunities throughout the U.S. The grantee will: 1) provide eight subgrants to state service commissions to develop model youth-service programs; 2) facilitate a learning cohort of youth development staff in service learning best practices; and 3) support the identification of sustainable funding opportunities for youth programming. Since 2017, America’s Service Commissions has been working with state service commissions and other national partners, including statewide afterschool networks, to prioritize the development of opportunities to engage youth in service.

title: Youth Engagement 10-Year Progress Assessment
description: The current Education program plan concludes in December 2024. Red Lantern Consulting, LLC will work with Mott Foundation staff and grantees to assess the collective progress made from 2015 through 2024 toward the approved outcomes for the Youth Engagement program area grantmaking strategies. The assessment will include interviews with current and former grantees, staff and other relevant field stakeholders. Findings will be shared with Foundation staff, management and grantees to help inform future strategic directions and interest for relevant youth engagement grantmaking.

title: Partnership for Ukraine
description: This grant will support the Czech Environmental Partnership Foundation’s Partnership for Ukraine program. Since the program’s launch in 2023, the grantee has provided 170 fellowships (week-long study tours to Central Europe in groups of 10-15 participants) for Ukrainian government, business, media and civil society leaders from localities throughout Ukraine, focusing on energy and environment-related issues. Along with other activities, the grantee has also supported 10 pilot projects in local Ukrainian communities. Over the next three years, the grantee plans to continue providing fellowships, consolidate a network of 250 program alumni, support local pilot projects and establish an independent Ukrainian Environmental Partnership Foundation. Established in 1994, the Czech Environmental Partnership Foundation is a member of the Environmental Partnership Association for Central Europe. The Czech Environmental Partnership Foundation’s mission is to improve the state of the environment, promote sustainable development, and strengthen civil society in Czechia by providing financial and technical support to nongovernmental organizations.

title: Family Informed Year-Round Support
description: The Family Informed Year-Round Support program, a key initiative of the Flint Freedom Schools Collaborative, is dedicated to creating a safe and supportive space for families. The primary focus is supporting parents, caregivers and community members in addressing barriers that impact success for kids and families. This grant will assist Flint parents and caregivers by creating a series of parent engagement sessions personalized to their needs as communicated in the grantee’s summer program survey. The program will connect parents to the Flint Parent Collaborative and other city resources that help kids and parents thrive. Further, the grant will assist parents and caregivers in Flint to connect with other cities that are building strong parent engagement networks.

title: Enterprising Ventures of Color Evaluation
description: This grant to the Community Foundation of Greater Flint will provide funding for a consultant to conduct an external evaluation of the Enterprising Ventures of Color capacity building cohort. The cohort included eight nonprofit organizations led by people of color. The 18-month program was designed by a national organization and included peer networking, executive coaching, technical assistance and consultations. The evaluation will include interviews, focus groups and will document outcomes along with lessons learned from the program to inform the community and philanthropic organizations about future capacity-building opportunities for Flint.

title: Investigating Artificial Intelligence in Education
description: This grant will support a comprehensive research study of artificial intelligence technologies, specifically generative artificial intelligence, within the K-12 and afterschool fields. Opportunity Labs — a consultant with experience in education practice and research from the local to national level — will conduct research and analysis of the current and potential impacts of artificial intelligence in education, providing valuable insights and frameworks for informed and impactful philanthropic engagement. Additionally, the grantee will facilitate a roundtable discussion on artificial intelligence with leaders from the afterschool field.

title: Beecher High School
description: This grant will support the Beecher Community School District in renovating Beecher High School, reopening the traditional high school with a focus on expanding career pathways for Beecher students. Specifically, this grant will support: 1) renovating Beecher High School; 2) redesigning the high school to incorporate a career academy focus; and 3) expanding the student learning spaces.

title: Strengthening Culinary Programs
description: With this grant, Mott Community College will continue strengthening its culinary arts program. With a new building manager in place to oversee the day-to-day operations, the second year of this initiative will focus on: 1) advancing into a two-year accreditation process; 2) increasing community involvement; and 3) expanding culinary services in banquet and catering operations, public cooking classes and signature culinary events. The efforts will continue reintroducing the Culinary Arts Institute to prospective students and the community.

title: Brownell Holmes Renovation
description: This grant will support the Flint Community Schools in developing and renovating Brownell STEM Academy and Holmes STEM Middle School Academy, creating a K-8 education campus in Flint. Specifically, this grant will support: 1) renovations for Brownell STEM Academy and Holmes STEM Middle School Academy; 2) construction of a Cube, innovative community facility; 3) campus improvements to athletic fields and student play structures; and 4) development of an early childhood wing in Brownell STEM Academy.

title: General Purposes
description: Since 1995, the Groundwork Center for Resilient Communities has been dedicated to promoting sustainable practices across Michigan. With partial support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee has taken a leadership role in northwest lower Michigan, advocating for a clean environment, a robust economy and resilient communities. Their focus areas include: 1) food and farming; 2) clean energy; 3) water policy; and 4) transportation. This general purposes funding increase will enable the Groundwork Center for Resilient Communities to continue its work across all priority areas including support for its Strong Future Fund, which aims to ensure organizational stability and continuity during a period of leadership transition.

title: Governor's Service Awards Fund
description: This grant will enable the Michigan Nonprofit Association to support the work of the Michigan Community Service Commission, the state’s lead agency on service and volunteerism. Specifically, this grant will support the Michigan Community Service Commission in hosting the Governor’s Service Awards to assist in the continued growth and celebration of service and volunteerism in the state.

title: General Purposes
grantee: National Network of Local Philanthropy Development in Ukraine
description: This grant will help to support the development of community foundations in Ukraine. Initially established in 2014, the National Network of Local Philanthropy Development in Ukraine became active in 2019 as a full-fledged community foundation support organization. The network’s mission is to advance the culture of philanthropy through community foundations as local leaders of sustainable development in Ukraine. Over the past 18 months, the Network grew its membership from 15 to 22 community foundations, and also added four more Youth Bank Initiatives, bringing the total to 28. Key objectives for the next two years are to: 1) develop and implement a certification system for community foundations; 2) design and implement a financial sustainability model for both community foundations and the network; and 3) advocate for local philanthropy by strengthening the community foundation brand and helping to develop a more favorable policy environment. The National Network of Local Philanthropy Development in Ukraine anticipates adding 10 new community foundations and 10 new Youth Bank Initiatives by the end of 2027.

title: Superior Storytellers
description: With this grant, Michigan Technological University will lead the Superior Storytellers project, an initiative aimed at engaging youth in placed-based learning experiences on Lake Superior. The summer program will provide young people the opportunity to work along other stakeholders in the Keweenaw Peninsula to explore and develop interconnected geological and human stories that serve as the foundation for the area’s past, present and future.

title: General Purposes
description: The Keweenaw Community Foundation has been serving the Keweenaw and Houghton County communities of Michigan’s Upper Peninsula since 1994. In addition to its traditional grantmaking activities, the grantee has, in recent years, expanded its role by helping to convene and facilitate multi-stakeholder discussions to address complex community issues. This includes leadership on the Keweenaw Heartlands project, which aims to sustainably manage thousands of acres of forested land at the tip of the Keweenaw Peninsula for community benefit. With general purposes support, the Keweenaw Community Foundation will build its organizational capacity to continue to lead the Keweenaw Heartlands project and other initiatives that meet the needs of the communities it serves.

title: Tribal Climate Resiliency Project
description: The Keweenaw Bay Indian Community of the Lake Superior Band of Chippewa Indians’ homeland is located along the shores of Lake Superior in the Upper Peninsula of Michigan. The Community has long been devoted to the protection and stewardship of Lake Superior and the Great Lakes region, including the water, wetlands and forests within it. With funding from the Mott Foundation, the grantee will be able to address climate change impacts that are threatening the Tribe’s way of life and implement climate resiliency plans developed by the Natural Resources Department of the Keweenaw Bay Indian Community.

title: Girl Scouts Programming in Genesee County
description: With this grant, the Girl Scouts of Southeastern Michigan will provide scouting opportunities to girls in Flint and Genesee County. Activities are provided in leadership, STEAM education, outdoor experiences, financial literacy and life skills training through a supportive and engaging environment. With rising membership and associated costs, it has become more challenging for girls to participate, and this grant will help make programming more accessible.

title: General Purposes
description: TechSoup, based in San Francisco, will partner with tech companies to offer access to technology and services tailored to the needs of nonprofits, helping them enhance their operations, expand their reach and increase their impact. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) develop its global network to provide education, access to discounted or donated software and hardware and community support that nonprofits need to unlock their potential; 2) offer educational programs, webinars and consultancy to build digital skills and foster collaboration among nonprofits; and 3) open its infrastructure and amend its operating model so that organizations can share their insights, driven by their local experience and data. This will allow the grantee to respond to still-present demands of the global pandemic and a civil society ecosystem that is at risk of falling behind the curve and being less capable of meeting society’s pressing needs. The grantee has been a trusted civil society actor since 1987 and successfully adapted through technology changes with recent curation of artificial intelligence tools for nonprofits. TechSoup has provided access to software for 1.4 million organizations worldwide and distributed products and grants valued at $21 billion.

title: State Children's Savings Account Assessment
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant will enable Engage Strategies to prepare landscape assessment reports that provide strategic information about the opportunities and challenges for promoting children’s savings accounts across states and nationally. The reports will answer questions such as: how can this strategy best be framed to garner support; who are the most effective spokespersons; and, most importantly, where could Foundation support continue to leverage change? These assessments will not only inform potential future grantmaking but will also help grantees shape their advocacy strategies and identify critical partners necessary to achieve results. Based in South Carolina, Engage Strategies is a for-profit consulting firm that provides strategic guidance and analysis services to foundations, businesses and nonprofit organizations.

title: Endowment Funds
description: This grant to the University of Michigan will provide operating funds through an endowment to support the C.S. Mott Children’s Hospital. The grantee operates the hospital to serve children in the region and beyond and is seen as the go-to care provider for children with the most complex and challenging conditions. Endowment support for operations will increase the C.S. Mott Children’s Hospital’s capacity to play an important role in children’s health care services.

title: Berston Field House Capital Improvements
description: This grant will support the renovation and construction of new facilities for the community center housed at Berston Field House. Berston Field House has served Flint residents in a variety of ways for over 100 years. The new amenities at the field house will enable the organization to increase its educational, recreational and enrichment programming for residents. The updated athletic facilities will provide access to participants of all ages and ability levels, thereby encouraging health and wellness. Enhanced gathering spaces and new classrooms will bring the community together to celebrate, learn and share ideas and opportunities with one another.

title: General Purposes
description: The Detroit Regional Partnership Foundation aims to support the Southeast Michigan region with business attraction and economic development initiatives. The grantee brings a particular focus on job creation for the under- and unemployed as well as diversity, equity and inclusion so individuals and the community prosper.

title: Communications for Social Good
description: With this grant, the Communications Network will serve as the fiscal sponsor for a project that will be developed by Hattaway Communications. The project will create practical, adaptable resources for foundations and nonprofits to: 1) use artificial intelligence productively and ethically to enhance the impact of social good communications; and 2) communicate with their audiences in ways that build trust and encourage productive engagement in civic space.

title: Community Foundation Development in Spain
description: The project goal is to develop community foundations in Spain. To this end, in 2020, the Spanish Association of Foundations launched a 10-year program to foster a strong and vibrant community foundation movement in Spain. Through this program, the grantee will work to: 1) develop at least 40 new community foundations, covering 50% of Spain’s territory; 2) create a national network of Spanish community foundations; 3) ensure that the community foundations adhere to internally developed quality standards; and 4) encourage the Spanish community foundations to play a leadership role in addressing the Sustainable Development Goals on the local level. During the next five years, the grantee will focus on promoting the concept of community foundations, developing and strengthening new community foundations and facilitating networking among community foundations on the national and international levels. During the past grant period, the Spanish Association of Foundations publicized the community foundation concept, supported local initiatives to develop community foundations and facilitated the establishment of two new community foundations, bringing the number of community foundations in Spain to nine.

title: Regulation of Nonprofits and Philanthropy
description: The project goal is to support a healthy policy environment for the nonprofit and philanthropy sector. The Regulation of Nonprofits and Philanthropy project at the Urban Institute is a vehicle to develop, promote and disseminate research on the federal-state regulatory framework and its impact on nonprofits. The project also serves as a platform for ongoing dialogue about ways to improve the regulatory framework. The project is implemented by the Center on Nonprofits and Philanthropy at the Urban Institute — a think tank that builds knowledge about the nation’s social and fiscal challenges.

title: Frontline Justice Project
description: The project goal is to expand justice services in the United States. To this end, Rockefeller Philanthropy Advisors will support a nascent, but growing, movement of legal helpers specifically trained to support people in resolving their legal challenges. The grantee will do this by executing rigorous research and building a body of evidence on what works in expanding the scope of justice service providers. This additional funding will allow the grantee to finalize its training curriculum for community justice workers and to launch a networking and mentoring platform for justice workers. Additionally, it will support expansion and consolidation of the National Leadership Council and Justice Worker Task Force. In its first year, this initiative brought together over 150 justice actors for the first time to exchange experience on effective community justice work. The grantee also worked with 15 state-level Access to Justice commissions to identify opportunities for engaging more widely with community justice work. Frontline Justice is a project sponsored by Rockefeller Philanthropy Advisors with the aim of giving real meaning to “equal justice under law” as enshrined in the founding documents of the United States.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides funding to an organization whose goal is to increase community-based access to justice for the Ukrainian public. The Legal Development Network, a network of 22 organizations operating 30 community legal centers in Ukraine (as well as three outside of Ukraine since Russia’s illegal invasion) will work to strengthen the resilience and responsiveness of its members. Through mentoring of local partners, repeated engagements with local administrations and building capacity of member organizations, the grantee will work to ensure high quality legal assistance for those in need despite the numerous challenges such assistance faces. In 2022-23, the grantee more than doubled the number of people to whom it offered legal assistance, despite, or because of, the invasion of Ukraine. Over 200,000 people were supported with legal assistance and information at home and a new service for supporting Ukrainians abroad was established, serving a similar number. With growing turmoil in the funding environment for civil society organizations and increasing uncertainty over the direction and consequences of the war, the grantee will work to strengthen its resiliency in order to better serve its constituency. Formally registered in 2015 and with its secretariat in Kyiv, the Legal Development Network has member organizations in 15 regions of Ukraine.

title: Charles Stewart Mott Foundation Fund for Flint Non-Endowed Donor-Advised Fund
description: This grant to the Community Foundation of Greater Flint will support a non-endowed donor-advised fund. Over time, the fund will provide grant dollars to one or more organizations that provide services and programming to Flint area residents.

title: European Programme for Integration and Migration
description: The European Programme for Integration and Migration is a donor collaborative hosted by the Network of European Foundations. Established in 2005, this program strengthens the role played by civil society organizations in advocating for constructive approaches to migration in Europe. This is done through grantmaking, capacity development and networking activities addressing a range of issues, including: 1) exploring alternatives to detention; 2) protecting migrant rights at borders; 3) fostering inclusion; 4) supporting children and youth on the move; 5) protecting freedom of movement; and 6) developing strategic messaging on migration. Between 2005 and 2024, 23 foundations have joined this program, pooling approximately 29 million Euros to support almost 400 civil society organizations in 38 countries. Based in Brussels, the Network of European Foundations strengthens cooperation among foundations in Europe.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purposes support to American Gateways as they work to provide vital immigration legal services to the most vulnerable immigrants in Central Texas and the United States at large. The grantee will conduct community outreach and education on immigrants’ rights, provide individualized technical assistance on cases and directly represent individuals in the immigration court system. Founded in 1987, American Gateways provides quality, affordable and trustworthy legal services to the immigrant community in Texas.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purposes support to the Asylum Seeker Advocacy Project as it continues to supply legal resources and information to immigrants, improve the systems that serve immigrants and build a virtual community of asylum seekers in the United States. These grant funds will enable the grantee to respond to the ongoing needs of its members and expand its legal support systems and digital offerings. Asylum Seeker Advocacy Project’s over 700,000 members live in every U.S. state and territory and come from over 175 countries. Considering members’ asylum-seeking children, the organization now serves more than 1 million asylum seekers.

title: TFN Global Service for Community Foundations
description: The project goal is to strengthen newly established and emerging community foundations in select countries and regions. To this end, The Funding Network, a giving circle based in the United Kingdom, will strengthen its network of community foundations and community foundation support organizations in over 30 countries in Africa, Europe and Latin America. The grantee will facilitate regional and international exchanges and will provide information, technical assistance and mentoring to its international partners. Established in London in 2002 by a group of private philanthropists with the mission to increase the level, scope and impact of charitable giving, the grantee now works in 30 countries around the world. With previous grant funds, The Funding Network supported partner organizations in 16 countries to organize 50 events and raise over $770,000 for 156 social change projects with support from more than 3,500 donors.

title: Flint Community Schools High School Design
description: The Flint Community Schools provide K-12 public education to children living in the city of Flint. The grantee’s school buildings are aging and outdated. With this grant, the Flint Community Schools will begin the design and planning phase for a new high school. Specifically, this grant will support completing phase one of a high school design process and developing schematic design documents.

title: Genesee County Trail Analysis
description: With this grant, Genesee County will revisit the trails plan that was developed in its master plan. Genesee County currently has over 95 miles of nonmotorized trails which residents enjoy for cycling, walking and running. Trails create a sense of place, build community, encourage recreation and physical fitness, and contribute to economic development and quality of life. However, the Genesee County trail segments are generally not connected and/or lack signage that would allow users to more easily make connections. Genesee County will explore options for creating a connected trails system.

title: Renewable Energy for Extractive Reserves in the Amazon
description: This project supports the World Wildlife Fund in expanding solar energy access for communities in the Amazon rainforest. Activities focus on coordinating civil society organizations in the Energy and Communities Network and collaborating with Brazilian government entities on off-grid solar projects as part of the Amazon Region Protected Areas Communities initiative. With this grant increase and associated grant period extension, the organization will consolidate important gains in both aspects of the project and position the work for continued success in the long term.

title: Downtown Hotel Financial Stabilization Support
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: With this grant increase, the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation will continue its efforts of downtown revitalization by supporting the future sustainability of the Hilton Garden Inn Flint Downtown hotel. The hotel opened in the midst of the COVID-19 pandemic, reducing the number of overnight guests and visitors to the restaurants. The hotel is an important community asset and contributes to downtown Flint revitalization efforts and community vitality. It is an amenity for the area’s existing arts and cultural institutions, hospitals, and colleges and universities, as well as a place for guests of Flint and Genesee County residents.

title: Broadening Participation in Great Lakes Advocacy
description: Founded in 1701, Yale University is one of the oldest universities in the United States. During the previous grant period, the grantee placed seven graduate environmental fellows across seven Great Lakes organizations. In addition, the grantee has completed several associated research studies, hosted the annual New Horizons in Conservation conferences and established a publicly accessible online directory of U.S. environmental professionals. With additional support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee will: 1) continue to place three environmental fellows annually in Great Lakes organizations; 2) further develop the online directory of environmental professions; 3) host the annual New Horizons in Conservation conference; and 4) continue the ongoing research on improving participation within the U.S. environmental nonprofit sector.

title: Advancing Renewable Energy Access in the Amazon
description: The Brazilian Institute for Consumer Defense is a nongovernmental organization focused on: 1) ensuring citizens’ access to essential goods and services; 2) promoting social development; 3) sustainable consumption; and 4) environmental health. The grantee raises awareness about the social and economic impacts of renewable energy access for isolated communities in the Brazilian Amazon. This grant increase and associated grant period extension will support the grantee’s continued efforts to improve the implementation of the federal electrification program. The additional funding will enhance program implementation oversight, foster community engagement and help ensure that solar energy systems reach those who need them most.

title: Downtown Hotel Financial Stabilization Support
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: With this grant increase, the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation will continue its downtown revitalization efforts by supporting the future sustainability of the Hilton Garden Inn Flint Downtown hotel. The hotel opened in the midst of the COVID-19 pandemic, reducing the number of overnight guests and visitors to the restaurants. The downtown hotel is an important community asset contributing to downtown Flint’s revitalization efforts and community vitality. It is an amenity for the city’s existing arts and cultural institutions, hospitals, and colleges and universities, as well as a place for guests of Flint and Genesee County residents.

title: Renewable Loreto
description: This project supports Derecho Ambiente y Recursos Naturales in expanding renewable energy access in the Amazonian region of Loreto, Peru, by developing off-grid solar energy systems at the community level to improve health, education and sustainable production. It also seeks regulatory reforms to enhance renewable energy access across the Peruvian Amazon. With this grant increase and associated grant period extension, the organization will further demonstrate the benefits of off-grid systems, build regional alliances and promote knowledge exchange with partners from Brazil, Colombia, Chile and Ecuador to advance Indigenous leadership in renewable energy systems. These activities will ensure that the organization consolidates substantial gains from the project and positions the work for continued success in the long term.

title: General Purposes
description: The International Energy Initiative Brasil is an independent, nongovernmental organization founded by sustainable energy development experts to promote energy efficiency and renewable energy production. The organization works to build financial and institutional strength and advance renewable energy solutions in the Brazilian Amazon by producing reports and engaging partner networks. This grant increase is available for the organization’s general purposes, including conducting studies on gender and energy access, participating in related nonprofit networks and positioning International Energy Initiative Brasil for continued success.

title: Integration Investments and Indigenous Peoples in South America
description: For over 40 years, the Indian Law Resource Center has been an important voice for Indigenous peoples in the Americas and a source of legal expertise to improve policies, practices and accountability at national and international development finance institutions. Over the prior grant period, the grantee successfully advanced social and environmental safeguard review and implementation by the World Bank and Inter-American Development Bank. In the current grant period, the Indian Law Resource Center continues to hold financial institutions accountable and push international and national development finance institutions to adopt safeguards that benefit Indigenous peoples. This grant increase will enhance policy advocacy and capacity-building activities by supporting a convening of Indigenous leaders and community members in Jujuy, Argentina, in 2025. This gathering will be a critical platform for exchanging knowledge, experiences and strategies to further protect Indigenous rights and environments.

title: Unlocking BNDES Operation Lifecycle
description: SITAWI Finance for Good is a Brazilian nonprofit organization established in 2008 to mobilize research and capital for positive environmental and social outcomes. During the previous grant period, the grantee strengthened community capacities to monitor and discuss social and environmental safeguards for oil and gas activities in the Medio Juruá River basin in the Brazilian Amazon. With this grant renewal, SITAWI Finance for Good will continue to support communities by building their capacity to respond to oil and gas exploration proposals and other threats such as climate change.

title: Improving Strategic Communications and Public Engagement on Off-Grid Renewable Energy Solutions in East Africa
description: The African Centre for Media Excellence is a nonprofit organization providing media support services in Africa. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the organization has directly benefited over 400 journalists and media practitioners with various media support services including the production of articles, podcasts, social media and other related products and offerings. The organization also undertook journalist training, media monitoring and research on the productive use of solar energy services in East Africa. Furthermore, the organization designed and completed a social and behavior change pilot program on the productive use of solar energy services in the Dodoma region of Tanzania. With additional support, the organization will continue its media support by enhancing the strategic communication capabilities of journalists, media outlets, nonprofits and other key partners on the productive use of solar energy services. African Centre for Media Excellence will also publish its own articles to facilitate more public engagement and awareness on the productive use of solar energy services in East Africa.

title: Scaling Africa's Distributed Renewable Energy Ecosystem Model through Social Entrepreneurship
description: Ashoka is an international nonprofit organization that fosters a global ecosystem of social entrepreneurs focused on innovative solutions to address a range of development challenges, including global climate change. With previous support, the grantee mapped and identified over 140 social innovators advancing renewable energy services in East Africa’s agricultural sector. The grantee provided targeted technical assistance to a select group of 12 leading innovators, one of whom was chosen to join the global Ashoka Fellowship Network. With renewed support, Ashoka will continue to strengthen the ecosystem of partners and social entrepreneurs, as well as provide expanded technical assistance services to select social entrepreneurs working to advance the productive use of solar energy services in key agricultural sectors of East Africa.

title: Innovative Financing for Local Agrisolar Entrepreneurs - Uganda
description: Since 2017, The Innovation Village Hub, a local nonprofit in Uganda, has been supporting youth entrepreneurship development in Uganda to benefit local communities and the environment. With previous support, the grantee has strengthened the capacity of 80 solar entrepreneurs through the provision of business advisory financial and technical assistance services. With this grant, the Innovation Village Hub will: 1) consolidate these achievements by supporting agrisolar entrepreneurs to scale up their operations in more rural off-grid communities; 2) establish three agrisolar hubs to serve as a one-stop-shop solution for rural farmer training and technical support; and 3) work with local financial institutions to expand financial services for agrisolar entrepreneurs and farmers.

title: Accountability Research Center
description: The Accountability Research Center at American University, a major university based in Washington D.C., works to improve the social and environmental outcomes of development finance institutions, strengthen accountability and enhance affected community participation in decision and policymaking. This grant increase will extend, for an additional year, the work to ensure that the World Bank delivers on its commitments to civic engagement and deliver promised project benefits to marginalized communities.

title: Strengthening the ACCESS Coalition
description: Loughborough University, a recognized institution of higher learning in the United Kingdom, supports the ACCESS Coalition, which aims to coordinate action by civil society organizations working to deliver universal energy access. With this increase, the grantee will extend its support for the ACCESS coalition for one additional year and further strengthen its ability to convene and lead African civil society efforts to guide national and regional development finance institutions away from fossil fuels and towards distributed renewable energy solutions. In addition, Loughborough University will support the ACCESS Coalition in recruiting a new advocacy and research officer to support data-based campaigns on increasing investment for energy access in Africa, targeting the World Bank and the African Development Bank.

title: Empowering Midwestern Environmental Justice Organizations Addressing Water Equity
geographic_focus: Indiana, Ohio, Wisconsin, Michigan, Minnesota, Illinois
description: The Midwest Environmental Justice Network — a project of the Minneapolis Foundation — is led by and for community-based organizations in a 12-state area working to connect and support grassroots groups and diverse leadership to address environmental issues impacting their communities. With previous Mott Foundation support, the network has been able to increase its communications and outreach and grow its partner engagement on environmental policies and programs. With this grant increase, the network will continue to provide financial resources, peer learning, training and capacity building for groups working specifically on water conservation and drinking water access and affordability in the eight-state Great Lakes region.

title: Tribal Nations Conservation Pledge and Funding Collaborative
geographic_focus: Indiana, Ohio, Michigan, Minnesota, Wisconsin, Illinois
description: Founded in 1990, Native Americans in Philanthropy promotes effective and equitable philanthropy in Native communities and distributes funding and resources directly to Tribal Nations. The Tribal Nations Conservation Pledge and Funding Collaborative, a pooled fund to which Mott contributes, builds capacity and provides technical assistance and financial resources for Tribal Nations to overcome barriers and implement projects that protect and conserve natural resources on Indigenous land. This grant increase will support the continued advancement of the pledge and collaborative for Tribes in the Great Lakes region.

title: General Purposes
description: Formed in 1999, The Funders Network is a philanthropy-serving organization that provides support to foundations, nonprofit organizations and other partners working to create equitable, just and environmentally sustainable communities. Over the last year, the organization pursued its mission through a range of activities, including: 1) its annual conference and other convenings; 2) working groups on cross-cutting issues; 3) pooled grantmaking initiatives; and 4) leadership development programs. This renewal grant will provide general purposes support to The Funders Network for all its programs, including the Urban Water Funders Group.

title: Healthy Great Lakes Program
description: The Canadian Environmental Law Association has a long history of advancing water policy improvements across Ontario. Leveraging deep expertise and collaborative relationships, the grantee works to ensure equitable access to safe drinking water, provide legal advocacy, and empower communities through education and engagement. With this grant increase and associated grant period extension, the Canadian Environmental Law Association will increase its capacity to sustain and expand research, community relationship building and effective public education efforts.

title: Protecting Water Quality and Ecosystems in Indiana's Lake Michigan Watershed
description: The Conservation Law Center is a statewide organization working to conserve lands and improve water quality through Clean Water Indiana, its statewide water policy program to address multiple problems impacting water resources in the state and region. As a pro bono legal and technical assistance provider, the grantee has a proven track record of success in improving the quality and accelerating the pace of environmental progress in Indiana and across the Great Lakes basin. This grant increase and associated grant extension from the Mott Foundation will help advance the goals of the Conservation Law Center, including in communities in the Lake Michigan watershed disproportionately impacted by environmental harm.

title: Lake Michigan Water Program
description: The Illinois Environmental Council Education Fund has over 100 affiliates working to protect water resources in the state, including the Lake Michigan basin. As part of its Clean Water Program, the grantee builds coalitions and educates the public and decision-makers about water issues. With Mott Foundation support, the grantee has raised awareness and made progress on lead service line replacement, toxic chemical pollution reduction and invasive species control. With this grant increase and associated grant extension, the Illinois Environmental Council Education Fund will further the goals of its Clean Water Program with a focus on safe and affordable drinking water.

title: General Purposes
description: For the past 25 years, PennFuture has been a leading statewide organization in Pennsylvania, pushing for environmental progress through legal advocacy, policy engagement and citizen involvement in decision-making. This work has focused on the goals of clean water, clean air and clean energy. This grant increase will be available for the organization’s general purposes, including work related to Lake Erie and Erie County.

title: General Purposes
description: River Alliance of Wisconsin supports a strong network of local organizations around the state that address threats to Wisconsin’s waters, such as invasive species, pollution and climate change. With Mott Foundation support, the grantee helps build the capacity of local groups to protect water, deliver programs to achieve clean water outcomes and engage communities to take action for clean water. This grant increase will be available for the organization’s general purposes.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Ontario, Ohio, New York, Pennsylvania, Indiana, Michigan, Minnesota, Wisconsin, Illinois
description: Freshwater Future, a Great Lakes regional organization founded more than 20 years ago, helps communities address pressing water issues by providing grants, capacity building and technical expertise to local groups and leaders. Over the past two years, with partial Mott Foundation support, the grantee has undertaken a range of activities, including: 1) making more than 80 small grants to community-based organizations; 2) providing organizational capacity-building assistance to over 30 groups; and 3) helping dozens of community groups engage in a range of policy issues, including Great Lakes restoration and access to safe and affordable drinking water. With renewed support from the Mott Foundation, Freshwater Future will continue to assist community-based organizations with small grants and technical assistance while also building its organizational strength by expanding and diversifying its revenue sources.

title: Capacity Support for Water Safety
grantee: Michigan League of Conservation Voters Education Fund
description: Michigan League of Conservation Voters Education Fund is a leader in efforts to secure funding and sound policies to protect, restore and enhance Michigan water resources. The grantee has been working with a coalition of state groups and frontline, community-based organizations, the Michigan Water Table, to share information and resources while coordinating strategies. With continued Mott Foundation support, the grantee will assist members of the Michigan Water Table to advance collective initiatives on water infrastructure and contamination issues.

title: Protecting Water Resources in the Great Lakes State
description: Michigan Trout Unlimited is a statewide coalition of 7,000 individuals and 19 local chapters working to conserve Michigan’s cold-water fish and their watersheds. This grant increase and associated grant period extension will support the grantee to: 1) continue direct engagement and public education of its membership on watershed conservation issues; 2) complete an inventory and assessment of Marquette and Au Sable watersheds; and 3) support the organization’s efforts on dam removal.

title: General Purposes
description: Founded in 1937, Michigan United Conservation Clubs is one of the largest statewide coalitions of conservation clubs representing the interests of hunters and anglers. The grantees membership includes 40,000 individuals and 200 organizational members. This grant increase, and associated grant period extension, is available for the organization’s general purposes. These activities will include: 1) strengthening its governance systems; 2) engagement of its members on key ongoing Great Lakes freshwater issues; 3) undertaking technical reviews of freshwater management issues; and 4) expanding its youth engagement activities on freshwater and environmental conservation issues in Michigan.

title: Action for Clean Drinking Water
description: Midwest Environmental Advocates is a Wisconsin-based nonprofit environmental law center that directly represents and assists local communities in addressing threats to safe, clean and abundant water in the state. With Mott Foundation support, the grantee has provided legal and technical assistance to Wisconsin communities on issues ranging from groundwater pollution to lead poisoning to the regulation of toxic chemicals. With this grant increase, Midwest Environmental Advocates will help residents, including tribal and rural communities, address the continued threats to safe drinking water.

title: General Purposes
description: Founded 50 years ago, the Minnesota Center for Environmental Advocacy is a legal and scientific voice for Minnesota’s environment. With prior Mott support, the grantee achieved several legal victories that protect people in the Lake Superior watershed and across the state from pollution, toxic chemicals and unsafe drinking water. This grant increase will be available for the organization’s general purposes including a new CEO search and transition.

title: Collaborating to Protect and Restore the Great Lakes
geographic_focus: Pennsylvania, Ohio, New York, Indiana, Michigan, Minnesota, Wisconsin, Illinois
description: The National Wildlife Federation’s Great Lakes Regional Center is a leader in engaging partners to work toward the protection and restoration of the Great Lakes. The grantee leverages policy, legal, communications, education and scientific expertise to support sound policies and leads several coalitions representing conservation, business, Tribal and urban constituencies. With previous Mott Foundation support, the grantee has advanced protection and restoration of the Great Lakes on issues ranging from invasive species to emerging contaminants to water affordability. With renewed support, the National Wildlife Federation will deepen its work to protect people and wildlife from continued threats to the Great Lakes.

title: General Purposes
description: Founded in 1934, the Metropolitan Planning Council is committed to addressing critical environmental issues faced by Chicago, Illinois and the Great Lakes region, including the sustainable management of the region’s water resources. With prior Mott Foundation support, the grantee helped to implement policies and practices on a range of issues such as transit, housing, and water resources, including efforts to promote green stormwater infrastructure and accelerate lead service line replacement. This grant increase will be available for the organization’s general purposes including its water resource protection programs.

title: Capacity Building
description: This increase will support the Genesee Area Focus Fund to increase the staff capacity at its supported organization, the Flint & Genesee Group. Mott Foundation support will allow the grantee to meet the current and future needs of large-scale developers and next generation employers of Genesee County. This grant will provide funding for additional positions and marketing that will increase positive economic development outcomes.

title: Artist in Residency Programming
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant to the Flint Institute of Arts provides funds for an artist in residency program. In 2025, two glass artists will come to Flint for a residency in the Hot Shop. The artists will also provide programming for Flint-area youth and produce new artwork to add to the museum’s permanent collection.

title: Commission on the American Workforce
description: In January 2025, the Bipartisan Policy Center launched the Commission on the American Workforce, a 15-month initiative to inform pending reauthorization of several federal childcare, education and workforce development programs. Comprised of scholars, business leaders, government officials, and policy experts, the commission is charged with developing a national bipartisan strategy and recommendations for building a workforce for the future, nurturing the talent necessary to remain a global leader, and ensuring access to economic opportunity for every American. Located in Washington, D.C., the Bipartisan Policy Center is a think tank that promotes bipartisan solutions to challenges facing the United States.

title: Michigan Powerplants to Parklands
description: Older coal-fired power plants are being retired across the country, including in Michigan. The Environmental Law and Policy Center sees an opportunity to transform many of these sites for parks, recreation and renewable energy generation. With this grant increase, the Center and its partners will make substantial progress in reimagining and redeveloping the Dan E. Karn coal plant site located in Bay County, Michigan. The project aims to establish grid-connected, large-scale solar energy generation, which will produce clean power, create jobs and generate property tax revenues. Additionally, it will create new parklands, conservation areas and outdoor recreation spaces while ensuring the protection of safe, clean and healthy water resources.

title: General Purposes
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Flint Cultural Center Corporation manages and maintains the 38-acre Flint Cultural Center campus which encompasses: 1) the Flint Cultural Center Academy; 2) Flint Institute of Arts; 3) Flint Institute of Music; 4) the Whiting; 5) Capitol Theatre; 6) Flint Public Library; and 7) Flint Institute of Science and History (Sloan Museum of Discovery and Longway Planetarium). The campus contributes positively to the quality of life in Flint through educational and cultural enrichment opportunities and has a significant economic impact through earned revenue and employment. Students and adults of all ability levels participate in or attend a variety of cultural, educational and instructional programs and activities across the campus. This grant will provide general purposes support to the Flint Cultural Center Corporation for campus improvements, grounds and maintenance, marketing and campus security.

title: Future Proofing the Compact
grantee: Conference of Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Governors and Premiers
geographic_focus: Minnesota, Michigan, Illinois, Ohio, Wisconsin, Indiana
description: Representing and uniting eight Great Lakes states and two provinces, the Great Lakes St. Lawrence Governors and Premiers is instrumental in protecting the region’s water resources. For instance, the grantee is deeply involved in implementing the Great Lakes Compact, a regional water management agreement designed to control diversions outside the basin and effectively steward water resources within the basin. Partial funding from the Mott Foundation will support a planning and research project to ensure there is consistency in decision-making when it comes to the long-term implementation of the Great Lakes Compact.

title: Film Appreciation Academy for Youth
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide funding to iMichigan Productions, Inc. for a film appreciation program for youth in Flint. Working with partners across the community, including nonprofits and school districts, the grantee will offer courses and events that explore filmmaking and potential careers in the industry. Filmmaking is a complex process and offers a variety of career pathways for those who are interested in the art form or the more technical aspects of the industry, such as sound engineering and editing. This program will explore all facets of filmmaking.

title: Coalition for Human Rights in Development Community Resource Exchange
description: The Coalition for Human Rights in Development is a global network of nongovernmental organizations — housed at Social and Environmental Entrepreneurs — working to mitigate the social and environmental impacts of large-scale infrastructure and energy finance. With this increase, the grantee will support the participation of its members from several African countries to engage with the upcoming G20 meeting in South Africa.

title: Civil Society Participation at G20
description: The Institute of Economic Justice is a South African think tank working to advance economic policy that supports human rights, communities and environmental wellbeing. The Group of 20 is a key pillar of global policymaking. Yet, there is insufficient civil society participation and oversight and no mechanism to transmit experiences and lessons learned by civil society from one country hosting the Group’s presidency to another. This grant will support the Institute as it works with the South African presidency of the Group of 20 to advance policies for a just energy transition and climate finance that does not fund harmful infrastructure.

title: Advancing a People's G20: Strengthening Participation and Putting Inequality on the Agenda Beyond G20
description: The project goal is to create an environment that will enable civil society to participate meaningfully in South Africa’s presidency of the Group of 20 nations. To this extent, Oxfam South Africa will strengthen grassroots initiatives, to ensure that economic justice and climate action remain at the forefront of global debates. Working with its network of local, national and regional partners it will support communities with the knowledge and tools to engage in economic and climate governance processes. Oxfam South Africa is part of the International Oxfam Confederation, which views itself as a global movement of people.

title: Strengthening Civil Society Engagement at the G20 in 2025 and Beyond
description: The project goal is to strengthen the voice of civil society organizations in the deliberations of the Group of 20 Nations meetings in South Africa. To this extent, the African Climate Foundation will work with a network of organizations to implement both an insider and outsider approach to raise the ambition and accountability of the Group of 20 Nations in international financial architecture reform toward climate action and development. Working with other stakeholders, the grantee also plans to participate in a People’s Summit, where approximately 20 organizations will join efforts to investigate appropriate and sustainable financing for ambitious climate actions. Established in 2020, the grantee is the first strategic intermediary grantmaker in Africa working at the nexus of climate change and development. The African Climate Foundation’s mission is to support interventions that deliver long-term socioeconomic transformation and inclusive development in Africa.

title: North Flint Food Market Opening
description: The North Flint Reinvestment Corporation — a 501(c)(3) community development corporation — has taken a place-based, holistic approach to revitalizing the severely distressed neighborhood surrounding the North Flint Food Market site on Pierson Road near Clio Road and North Saginaw Street. This geography is identified in the city of Flint’s Imagine Flint Master Plan as one of the most underserved areas of Flint. Food scarcity is a long-standing and well-documented concern for those living in this part of town and many residents have limited transportation options for shopping elsewhere. Based on community feedback, in 2016, the North Flint Reinvestment Corporation began efforts to open a grocery store in this high-need area in a way that would support community ownership, buy-in and stewardship. This grant provides support for the pre-opening and opening expenses of the store.

title: Youth Entrepreneurship Curriculum for Afterschool Programs
description: This grant increase will support VentureLab to continue its youth entrepreneurship capacity and ecosystem building for the afterschool field, including meeting and growing the demand for youth entrepreneurship programing. Specifically, this increase will expand their regranting program initiated in 2024, providing subgrants to a new cohort of four additional state afterschool networks. Through this work, participating states will grow their youth entrepreneurship initiatives, receive additional technical assistance and resources from VentureLab and spark increasing demand and awareness of youth entrepreneurship programming.

title: MiLEAP Early Childhood Fellow
description: With this grant, the University of Michigan will create a new fellowship position to help strengthen access, affordability and quality within Michigan’s early childhood education system.
