The fellowship will support the state of Michigan’s efforts to expand pre-K for all children by: 1) conducting a landscape analysis to inform the development of a comprehensive early childhood data collection system; 2) building evidence-based recommendations for the state to move towards a coordinated early childhood enrollment system; and 3) researching preschool and kindergarten curriculum and best practices to identify policy and/or administrative changes that will improve the transition between pre-K and kindergarten.

title: Downtown Flint Sign Upgrades
description: This grant to the Flint Downtown Development Authority will provide funds for a new sign in downtown Flint. The current digital sign was installed in 2008 and is in need of a physical and technological update. The new sign will also be used to promote events and programs in Flint, share information about small businesses and alert residents in the event of an emergency.

title: Philanthropic Tax Policy Analysis
description: The project goal is to support philanthropic actors with timely and reliable data to understand the breadth and impact of the sector on communities and the economy nationwide, and to understand how proposed changes in the regulation and taxation of the sector may impact those same communities. Grand Valley State University’s Dorothy A. Johnson Center for Philanthropy will conduct research related to private foundations and tax policy and philanthropy’s contribution to the tax system. The research conclusions will be delivered in a brief report that can be shared with and utilized by foundations as support material for continued tax-exemption status. Established in 1992, the Dorothy A. Johnson Center for Philanthropy is an academic center within the College of Community and Public Service at Grand Valley State University.

title: Youth Mentorship Community of Practice
description: This grant will support the Mott Community College Youth Mentorship Community of Practice project. The two-year project is designed to provide leadership and financial support to five mentorship groups that serve youth in the Flint area. In addition to leadership capacity building, the project will promote higher education and workforce opportunities for youth participating in each of the five mentoring programs.

title: Financial Recovery Technical Assistance
description: The purpose of this grant is to support the city of Flint in lessening operational challenges. The city of Flint faces unprecedented challenges as it recovers from the water crisis, the COVID-19 pandemic and the uncertainty of federal funding. Additional staffing and consulting expertise positions city leadership to function more effectively and efficiently in meeting the needs of Flint residents.

title: General Purposes
description: Founded in 2000, and incorporated in the United States in 2010, Worldwide Initiatives for Grantmaker Support is based in Sao Paulo, Brazil. The grantee has established a global network, linking more than 230 philanthropic associations and support organizations from around the world through international exchange, information services, networking and peer-to-peer learning opportunities. During 2023-24, the grantee: 1) represented the sector and its members in various global and regional fora and networks; 2) published research related to philanthropy and philanthropy infrastructure; 3) disseminated information and analysis about the sector through social media, blogs and an online newsletter; 4) held capacity-building workshops and online webinars; and 5) launched a new strategy to strengthen the enabling environment for philanthropy. During the current grant period, the grantee will focus on strengthening an enabling environment for philanthropy by building members’ capacity for policy advocacy as well as increasing membership in the Global South. This grant increase will strengthen the organization and its sector-supporting programs as operations pivot due to a changing funding environment.

title: Advancing the Children's Savings Account Field
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: For over 40 years, Prosperity Now has focused on ensuring prosperity for all as a leading intermediary on national research, practice and policy dedicated to financial stability and wealth. With continued Mott Foundation support since 1983, the grantee’s endeavors have significantly built the children’s savings account field. With renewed support, the grantee is committed to: 1) strengthening innovation in the children’s savings account field; 2) conducting the annual survey, monitoring growth in the field, and using data to build sustainable programs; and 3) strengthening capacities to design, deliver and sustain children’s savings account programs. Prosperity Now continues to ensure that new programs have the support and tools they need to be effective, sustainable and enriching to the entire field.

title: Data-Driven Progress for Access to Justice
description: The program goal is to produce new knowledge on legal needs globally. The World Justice Project will work along four key activity areas: 1) data; 2) research; 3) policy; and 4) engagement to strengthen the evidence base for people-centered approaches to justice reform. As part of its public engagement to promote wider support for people-centered justice reforms, the grantee will stage the World Justice Forum in Warsaw in June 2025. This will provide an opportunity to position legal empowerment practice as a critical component in strengthening the rule of law and accountable democracy. In 2022-23, the grantee produced a range of research and analysis, notably key reports to the United Nations High-level Political Forum assessing the current state of evidence underpinning justice reforms. In particular, analysis around the viability of data sources to be used in measuring civil justice outcomes under Sustainable Development Goal 16. Established initially as a project of the American Bar Association in 2006, the World Justice Project was formally registered as an independent organization in 2009 working to advance the rule of law around the world.

title: Atherton East Demolition
description: The dilapidated Atherton East buildings will be abated and demolished to increase neighborhood safety and beautification in a high-need area. The apartments, which were illegally built on a flood plain, had perpetual infrastructure issues for the residents and families living there. The now abandoned building attracts crime, illegal dumping and continues to erode as a blighted property. The abatement and demolition of the property will support the community revitalization of Flint.

title: Spread the Warmth
description: This initial grant will provide suport to the Empowerment Plan to manufacture and distribute 500 coats to unhoused individuals in Flint. In 2024, nearly 4,000 individuals experienced homelessness on a single night in Flint and Genesee County. Hypothermia is a leading cause of preventable injury and death among unhoused individuals. Coats are vital in reducing these risks and connecting this population to a potential workforce opportunity in the development of the physical coat making.

title: Arts Programming at Genesee Valley Regional Center
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will provide support for arts-based workshops to young people living at the Genesee County Juvenile Justice Center, a youth detention facility in Genesee County. The Youth Arts: Unlocked program has offered workshops at the center since 2011. The program uses a research-based, trauma-informed curriculum to deliver visual arts, dance, poetry, yoga and theater to boys and girls living at the facility.

title: Superintendents as Leaders for High-Quality Afterschool and Summer Learning Opportunities
description: This grant will enable the American Association of School Administrators to support state and local education leaders in implementing high-quality afterschool and summer learning programs. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) provide technical assistance to state superintendents and district leaders on exemplary afterschool program models; 2) develop and implement a communications initiative to share best practices among education stakeholders; 3) convene state education leaders and state networks to expand afterschool program access; and 4) work deeply in up to 12 states to develop exemplary program models and practices that can be shared across all 50 states.

title: Impact of Program and Practice Characteristics on Participant Outcomes
description: This grant will support continued research into the impact of high-quality afterschool programs on positive youth development. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) conduct a meta-analysis on the impact of afterschool participation on youth social and behavioral outcomes; 2) conduct a longitudinal analysis focused on the impact of afterschool participation on success in the workforce; and 3) develop several summary papers on the effects of afterschool participation based on existing research.

title: Children's Savings Account 10-Year Progress Assessment
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: As part of the Foundation’s strategic planning process, grants were approved to support 10-year assessments of Education program grantmaking activities. OE Consulting received grants to examine afterschool and children’s savings account grantmaking; Red Lantern Consulting is evaluating the youth entrepreneurship and service objectives. This grant extension, along with the corresponding grant increase, will allow the grantee to collect additional information and summarize findings across the four reports and prepare a consolidated assessment report, executive summary and graphic presentations for Foundation staff. These materials will provide a historical record of grantmaking activities and guide future grantmaking efforts under the new program plan. Findings will also be shared with grantees and other field leaders as appropriate.

title: Expanding Educational Opportunities in Michigan
description: The Michigan Afterschool Partnership will seek to continue a public-private partnership initiative to advance afterschool programming for Michigan’s youth and families. The overall goal of this initiative is to ensure that all Michigan youth have access to quality afterschool and summer learning opportunities. Specifically, this initiative will continue to seek to: 1) build needed capacity at the state level in Michigan; 2) implement quality standards and training; 3) develop a communications initiative; 4) coordinate a new statewide afterschool committee of key stakeholders; and 5) conduct program evaluation to ensure that young people have access to the afterschool programs they need moving forward.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant increase will provide tie-off support to Focus: HOPE, an anti-poverty and civil rights organization that serves residents of Detroit’s Oakman Boulevard neighborhood. Mott Foundation funding will help support the grantee’s core lines of work: 1) workforce development and education; 2) early learning and youth development; and 3) food justice. Cofounded in 1968 by Father William Cunningham and Eleanor Josaitis, Focus: HOPE’s mission is to provide intelligent and practical solutions to overcome racism, poverty and injustice.

title: State Fiscal and Low-Income Initiatives Project
grantee: Center on Budget and Policy Priorities
description: This grant continues support for the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities to expand economic opportunity and eliminate poverty. The grantee is known for its efforts to ensure federal and state governments have adequate resources and prioritize investments in basic needs, education, childcare and healthcare. To accomplish these goals, the grantee will continue: 1) monitoring policy and budget changes to the social safety net; 2) preparing policy briefs and analyses of budget and fiscal policy; 3) supporting and coordinating low-income advocates working at the state and local levels; and 4) providing strategic and technical assistance to state and local policymakers and program administrators overseeing policy and programs affecting low-income families. Located in Washington, D.C., the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities is one of the premier policy research and development institutions in the United States.

title: Fiscal Solvency and Service Effectiveness Project
description: This grant increase and corresponding grant period extension will enable Michigan State University to continue documenting and promoting solutions that help America’s older industrial cities address chronic fiscal stress and advance overall fiscal health. In 2023-24, the grantee began collecting fiscal data on water infrastructure for about 350 Michigan municipalities in order to assess the condition and sustainability of these systems. During the extended grant period, the grantee will: 1) complete the analysis; 2) recommend strategies; and 3) provide technical assistance to help municipalities develop asset management plans that identify long-term system needs — including operating and maintenance strategies — and ensure safe and reliable water service.

title: General Purposes
description: This increase will enable the Harlem Children’s Zone to provide needed services to participating youth as well as to continue to strengthen its comprehensive education model of programming. Specifically, this increase and extension will enable the grantee: 1) additional time to address potential shifts in education funding that could impact programming; and 2) to ensure that youth attending Harlem Children’s Zone programs receive necessary support to recover from learning loss.

title: Educare and Cummings Operating Support
description: With this grant, the Genesee Intermediate School District will continue to provide high-quality early childhood care and education at Cummings Great Expectations and Educare Flint. Both centers offer expanded hours, additional staff and family resources designed to help Flint kids be ready for kindergarten and beyond. To date, these extra costs have been covered by state funds in response to the Flint water crisis, but those funds are now transitioning away, and new funding streams will need to be identified.

title: Building and Strengthening Civic Infrastructure
description: The program goal is to build and strengthen civic infrastructure in the U.S. To this end, the University of Virginia’s Karsh Institute of Democracy will equip leaders and citizens with the skills, knowledge and relationships needed to rebuild the civic fabric in their local communities. During the grant period, the institute will organize two national convenings of civic leaders. These gatherings will provide a platform for a diverse group of civic leaders, practitioners and community foundations from across the country to come together to share learning and joint action.

title: Travel and Learning Fund
description: The project goal is to support exchange, networking and interaction among key nonprofits, practitioners and experts, including Mott Foundation grantees. To this end, the Institute of International Education, Inc. will operate a travel and learning fund to support individuals and organizations working on civic space, community philanthropy, access to justice or other areas of interest. In the period 2021-24, the grantee supported almost 60 individuals to participate in learning events across a range of issue areas including community philanthropy, digital human rights and indigenous access to civil justice. Based in New York, the Institute of International Education, Inc. manages similar funds for foundations around the world.

title: General Purposes
description: This program goal is to address the long-standing and emerging issues facing migrants in the Americas. Alianza Americas’ mission is to bring about a more inclusive, equitable and sustainable way of life for underserved migrant communities in the United States and across Mexico and Central America. This grant supports Alianza Americas to: 1) strengthen transnational networks; 2) educate policymakers; 3) host delegations; and 4) support its membership. Founded in 2004 by Mexican, Central American and Caribbean migrant leaders, Alianza Americas is a network of over 55 members in 18 states, representing over 150,000 migrant families across the United States, with dozens of organizational partners in Mexico and Central America.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support the continued organizational and programmatic development of People in Need, one of the largest nonprofits in Central and Eastern Europe operating globally. The grantee: 1) provides relief and development assistance in response to natural disasters and violent conflict; 2) promotes human rights, civic engagement and civil society development; and 3) supports social inclusion and integration for marginalized groups. During the previous grant period, the grantee provided relief and development assistance in 26 countries, reaching more than 3.5 million people. The grantee has helped more than 3 million people in Ukraine since Russia’s invasion. During the current grant period, the grantee will continue to respond to crises arising from war, conflict and natural disasters through its humanitarian relief programs and its support to civil society organizations working on education, human rights and social inclusion. Founded in 1992, People in Need is based in Prague, Czech Republic.

title: Institutional Development
description: The Association for Communities Participatory Development is a nonprofit alliance of local councils and territorial communities established in 2020 to develop democratic, open and inclusive local governance by promoting participatory practices and underscoring the significance of resident involvement in local development. Currently, the association includes more than 40 local government and civil society representatives, representing 24 territorial communities from seven Ukrainian regions. An institutional development support grant is helping the grantee: 1) formalize a network of past and current project participants to undergo strategic planning; 2) support the professional development of staff; 3) upgrade its office equipment; 4) improve its communications capacity; and 5) establish a monitoring, evaluation and learning framework. A grant increase will allow the association to conduct a Civic Participation Forum in November 2025 through a strategic partnership with the Association of Ukrainian Civic Initiatives. A successful forum will enhance the visibility and influence of the Association for Communities Participatory Development, contributing to its future sustainability.

title: General Purposes
description: PHILEA is an independent membership association of foundations and philanthropic networks that provides intellectual leadership on emerging policy agendas and societal trends that impact institutional philanthropy while fostering connections within philanthropy by utilizing external actors through convenings and events. The grantee supports an enabling environment for philanthropy at the European level with core programs, such as The Funders Forum on Transitioning Cities. This grant increase will assist with building and strengthening an enabling environment for philanthropy in Europe.

title: Youth Engagement 10-Year Progress Assessment
description: Through this grant increase, Red Lantern Consulting, LLC will work with Mott Foundation staff and grantees to deepen assessment and evaluation of the collective progress made from 2015 through 2024 toward the approved outcomes for the Youth Engagement program area grantmaking strategies. This work will: 1) support the further analysis and dissemination of the evaluation and assessment findings; 2) convene grantees for peer learning and collaboration; and 3) expand field research to nurture successful transitions for the Foundation, grantees and the field.

title: Genesee County Trails: Silver Lake, Embury-Cook, Perry and Iron Belle
description: With this grant, Genesee County will complete four non-motorized trail segments across the county. Each of the trail segments are listed as tier one priorities in the Genesee County Regional Non-Motorized Plan and are identified locally as the top multimodal priorities with strong public support. The trails will promote healthier life styles, strengthen community connections and spur new economic development opportunities.

title: Flint City Bucks and AFC Soccer Clubs
description: With this grant, the United Way of Genesee County will serve as the fiscal sponsor for a project grant to support the Flint City Bucks and Flint City Association Football Club soccer programs. The two teams are popular soccer clubs in Flint. Funds will support the women’s league, hosting the Mexican national soccer team and activities that make the games fun for families.

title: General Purposes
description: The Chill Foundation provides young people with opportunities to develop skills and experiences related to boardsports and outdoor activities, focusing on those who might not otherwise have access. The grantee’s programs integrate experiential learning with mentoring and coaching, along with a values-based curriculum. Funding from the Mott Foundation will support the ongoing operation of the organization’s core programs, catering to the needs of youth and youth-serving agencies. Headquartered in Burlington, Vermont, the Chill Foundation reaches over 3,000 young individuals annually across more than 22 cities and 9 countries worldwide.

title: Capital Improvements
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: This grant will support capital improvements to the lower level of the Floyd McCree Theatre building. The renovations will increase safety, functionality and aesthetics in the community and programming spaces. The theatre provides summer and afterschool programming that services children from ages 5-17. The Floyd McCree Theatre also provides a mainstage series of full-length, community theater productions each year.

title: Future Flint Homes Project
description: The Genesee County Land Bank Authority seeks to renovate homes to create more affordable housing opportunities in the city of Flint. Fully funded, the project seeks to create 16 renovated properties for Flint residents and families. Through the Future Flint Homes project, the Land Bank will engage local and minority-owned subcontractors in key trades, providing economic opportunities to those in the community who can benefit most. The project also intends to create jobs by employing and training additional staff in home renovation.

title: Center for Climate and Trade
description: This grant provides support to the Center for Climate and Trade, a project of the Climate Leadership Council. The Center is a think-tank that aims to provide policymakers the intellectual framework, analysis and fundamental methodologies to implement effective climate and trade policies. Over the past two years, the Center has produced dozens of reports on a range of subjects, focusing much of its work on the carbon border adjustment policy idea. With additional funding from the Mott Foundation, the organization will pursue several related activities, including stakeholder convenings, research and publication, and technical education for decision makers and other interested parties.

title: Food and Agricultural Climate Alliance
description: The Environmental Defense Fund, a national environmental organization, works on a range of environmental issues, including climate-smart agriculture. Such efforts include: 1) promoting the use of federal funds for conservation and climate action; 2) elevating farmer voices; and 3) improving agricultural practices to achieve lasting environmental and economic benefits. With this grant increase, the Environmental Defense Fund will continue a similar range of activities and solidify gains for long-term success.

title: General Purposes
description: As one of the world’s largest economies and a major greenhouse gas emitter, the United States has a unique opportunity to lead in addressing climate change. Citizens’ Climate Education aspires to foster an informed and diverse citizenry that is actively engaged in climate policy. The grant increase will support the organization’s general purposes, including strengthening and strategically involving its grassroots coalition and enhancing the quality and accessibility of its training programs. This targeted support will enable Citizens’ Climate Education to adapt to the fluid political landscape while continuing to create meaningful opportunities for climate action.

title: Special Exhibit
initiative: Enriching Lives Through Arts and Culture
description: The Flint Institute of Arts will showcase the work of M.C. Escher during a special exhibition in 2026 for area residents and visitors to experience. The mathematically and geometrically oriented work offers significant educational opportunities and potential partnerships with math and science teaching institutions in Flint and the broader region. The exhibit also pays homage to Flint’s history as a place of innovation, including design and engineering successes.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purposes support to the Council on Foundations — a national philanthropic organization founded in 1949 that currently represents over 900 members. The grantee’s mission is to foster an environment where philanthropy can thrive and cultivate a community of diverse and skilled philanthropic professionals and organizations who lead with integrity, serve as ethical stewards and advocate for progress.

title: Improving Equity and Accountability for Native American Communities with Community Foundations
description: The goal of this project is to support the advancement of racial equity for Native communities by U.S. community foundations, applying the framework of the Sustainable Development Goals. In 2023, Native Americans in Philanthropy issued a report that provided an assessment of the current state of community foundation interaction with Native communities. Based on these findings, the grantee developed a 6-year educational, relationship-building and resource-leveraging project. In year one, the grantee: 1) established relationships with regional community foundations; 2) created a model for future outreach in other regions; 3) hired staff and developed an internal work plan; 4) held an initial place-based workshop; and 5) implemented a pilot challenge grant program. A grant increase will enable the following activities in year two: conducting three regional workshops, establishing connections with the grantee’s Tribal Philanthropy Coalition and issuing community foundation match challenge grants to Tribal Communities. Founded in 1990, Native Americans in Philanthropy promotes equitable and effective philanthropy in Native communities.

title: General Purposes
description: The goal of this grant is to increase access to justice for poor and marginalized people in Kenya. To this end, the Legal Resources Foundation Trust will continue in its efforts to contribute to a justice sector that is just, inclusive, responsive and protects as well as respects and fulfills the fundamental rights and freedoms of people in Kenya. The grantee will continue to serve on the coordinating council of the Paralegal Society of Kenya and use various platforms to advocate for people-centered justice. Past support has allowed the grantee to provide justice services to approximately 28,000 people. The grantee also provided training to over 400 community paralegals while running an online radio station called Haki.fm. The Legal Resources Foundation Trust is a longstanding nonprofit organization in Kenya that addresses systemic and individual injustices on a daily basis.

title: General Purposes
description: Established in 1990, the National Council of Nonprofits is the nation’s largest network of nonprofits, representing more than 32,000 organizations across the United States. The grantee works through its network of state associations and nonprofit partners to help nonprofits operate more effectively, engage in critical policy issues affecting the sector and achieve greater impact in their communities.

title: General Purposes
description: Based in Washington, D.C., the International Center for Not-for-Profit Law will carry out a range of activities, including: 1) enhancing international norms and multilateral engagement to safeguard civic space; 2) helping civil society organizations navigate laws once enacted; 3) undertaking and disseminating research and analysis; and 4) raising public awareness about the importance of civil society and cross-border philanthropy.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to Independent Sector, a national membership organization which brings together a diverse community of changemakers at nonprofits, foundations and corporate giving programs working to strengthen civil society.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purposes support to the American Immigration Council as it works to improve the immigration system overall. The grantee: 1) manages a network of nearly 16,000 lawyers and law students, interpreters and social workers that provide support for immigrants; 2) conducts impact litigation and advocacy; 3) researches and analyzes immigration policy; and 4) collaborates with civic and business leaders to develop plans that improve the social and economic well-being of immigrants. Founded in 1987, the American Immigration Council focuses on working toward a fairer and just immigration system that opens its doors to those in need of protection and harnesses the skills that immigrants bring.

title: Civitates: the Fund for Democracy and Solidarity in Europe
description: The program goal is to promote, protect and reinvigorate the space for civic engagement in Europe. To this end, the Network of European Foundations will manage Civitates, a grantmaking fund to: 1) improve the space for independent civil society organizations and media to operate and promote constructive civic engagement; 2) foster a healthy online and offline environment for public debate and discourse; and 3) catalyze effective public and private funding for democracy and civic space in Europe. The grantee will manage and grow the fund, make grants and provide networking and technical assistance to nonprofits working on these issues across Europe. Since its establishment in 2018, through Civitates, the grantee has awarded approximately €10 million in grants to 50 organizations in 18 European countries. Civitates is supported by 18 private foundations. The Network of European Foundations is based in Brussels, Belgium.

title: The Ally Challenge Family Fun Night
description: This grant to the Tournaments for Charity will assist the organization in hosting the Family Fun Night at the annual Ally Challenge presented by McLaren. The PGA Tour Champions event will provide Flint and Genesee County families, many of whom live in economically disadvantaged communities, with access to highly engaging activities that promote physical activity, good sportsmanship and teamwork.

title: Summerfield Early Childhood Education Center Improvements
description: With this grant, the Genesee Intermediate School District will manage facility improvements to the former Summerfield Community School, which is currently being used as an early childhood education center owned by Flint Community Schools and operated by the intermediate school district. Additional repairs and upgrades will include: 1) updating student restrooms; 2) replacing doors and flooring; 3) upgrading classroom cabinets, countertops, sinks and faucets; 4) replacing soffits, lighting and mansard roof panels; and 5) expanding the playground and fencing. Together, the updates will lead to improved building and yard aesthetics and an enhanced learning environment for the young children and their families at the center.

title: Senior & Enrichment Center
description: With this grant, the Charter Township of Mundy will complete construction of its new and permanent location for the Senior & Enrichment Center. The new center will be located at the Mundy Miracle Commons, adding to the current amenities and offering Genesee County residents a variety of activities and resources aimed at fostering a healthier and more connected community.

title: Operating Support
description: With this grant, Kettering University will provide higher education opportunities for students seeking a hands-on learning environment, a co-op work experience and degrees within in-demand fields. Focus areas include: 1) a highly qualified teaching and administrative staff; 2) engaging and hands-on curriculum and laboratory spaces; 3) marketing and communications designed to attract students who would enjoy and be successful at the university; 4) scholarships to lessen the financial burden of students; and 5) other core initiatives of the school.

title: Promoting Environmental and Social Standards in the Financial Sector
description: Urgewald is a German-based organization that works to establish strong, binding environmental and social standards for international development finance institutions and builds public support for responsible and accountable development finance institutions. To achieve these goals, the grantee undertakes research, education and advocacy efforts with a global network of local communities, nongovernmental organizations and other partners. With this increase, Urgewald will organize a strategy retreat to develop plans for long-term engagement with multilateral development banks on accountability, advocacy and system-level influence.

title: Evaluation and Learning Partner for the With Youth, For Youth Initiative
description: This grant will support Public Profit to conduct an evaluation of the afterschool With Youth, For Youth initiative led by Youthprise. The purpose of the evaluation is to document the successes and lessons learned in order to develop a blueprint-style guide for other organizations to use to infuse youth voice and leadership into afterschool systems. The findings will be used for a final report, a playbook-style blueprint to support other expanded learning intermediaries in infusing youth voice and leadership into afterschool systems and a one-pager for afterschool champions.

title: Expanding Entrepreneurial Education
description: Since 2006, Lemonade Day has aimed to prepare youth for life through critical teachings that bridge the gap from home to school and career. Working in over 90 cities in the last 15 years, the grantee has immersed 1.5 million kids into its entrepreneurial and experiential learning journey, earning over $352.5 million in sales, generating $270 million in profit and $142 million in donations. With renewed and increased support, the grantee will continue to expand its programming to reach more youth with its entrepreneurial and whole child social-emotional approach. Specifically, this grant will support the grantee’s reach and impact by: 1) increasing access and opportunity for underserved youth to benefit from a curriculum highlighting business and life skills; 2) offering opportunities for the community to engage in youth entrepreneurship through mentoring, communications and business collaborations; and 3) engaging with the 50 State Afterschool Network in states outside of the grantee’s network. Lemonade Day will also contribute content to Mizzen Education, Inc.

title: Strategic Public Financing for Afterschool and Summer Learning
description: This grant will enable the Children’s Funding Project to conduct strategic fiscal analysis of existing state and federal resources supporting youth in afterschool programs and identify potential resources that could help expand access. Specifically, the grantee seeks to work with the 50 State Afterschool Network to: 1) identify a baseline of the range of funding supporting children and youth in afterschool programs; 2) provide technical assistance to the 50 State Afterschool Network and partners on state finance policy and budgets; and 3) map potential new funding sources to support afterschool and summer learning programs.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose support to Philanthropy Roundtable, a growing network of several hundred business leaders, philanthropists and foundations committed to advancing shared values of liberty, opportunity and personal responsibility through effective charitable giving. The grantee serves individual philanthropists and foundations that are refining their philanthropic strategies to maximize the impact of their resources, as well as emerging donors and entrepreneurs who are developing their philanthropic plans. The grantee provides a variety of programs and services including: 1) a national conference; 2) topical meetings; 3) publication of Philanthropy magazine; 4) thematic publications; and 5) public policy work.

title: Program on Philanthropy and Social Innovation
description: The goal of this grant increase is to enhance the support and maximize the impact of philanthropists, social investors and those they support through the Aspen Institute’s Program on Philanthropy and Social Innovation. This grant supports the grantee to advance philanthropy by hosting summits that focus on nonprofit data and develop philanthropic and nonprofit leaders. Established in 1949, Aspen Institute is a leading U.S. think tank with an international network of partners that fosters values-based leadership and provides a neutral and balanced venue for discussing and acting on critical issues.

title: Delaware Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase will support the United Way of Delaware which coordinates the Delaware Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase and extension, the grantee will continue to: 1) support efforts for increased funding for afterschool and summer programs; 2) strengthen and coordinate a unified voice to educate state leaders; and 3) leverage afterschool to advance statewide educational initiatives such as STEM learning and college and career readiness.

title: Florida Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase will support the Children’s Forum which coordinates the Florida Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase and extension, the grantee will continue to: 1) educate key stakeholders on the importance of increased access to engaged learning and quality afterschool programming; 2) develop career pathways and technical assistance resources to advance professional development opportunities for afterschool providers; and 3) expand quality initiatives and increase access to communities that may have limited resources.

title: Georgia Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase will support Voices for Georgia’s Children which coordinates the Georgia Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase and extension, the grantee will continue to: 1) enhance and expand statewide education and outreach efforts in collaboration with youth development partners; 2) strengthen and cultivate strategic partnerships with state leaders to sustain and grow champions for afterschool programs; and 3) leverage statewide data on the afterschool workforce to develop professional development strategies.

title: Indiana Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase will support the Indiana Afterschool Network, Inc. which coordinates the Indiana Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase and extension, the grantee will continue to: 1) create community conversations that are centered around the benefits of afterschool and feature afterschool programs; 2) support the development and growth of statewide initiatives to sustain new and existing out-of-school-time programs; and 3) develop local and regional afterschool leaders through specialized professional development opportunities.

title: Kansas Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: University of Kansas Center for Research, Inc.
description: This grant increase will support the University of Kansas Center for Research, Inc. which coordinates the Kansas Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase and extension, the grantee will continue to: 1) strengthen statewide infrastructure including leadership development, cross-sector collaboration, and professional development for providers; 2) inform strategies that prioritize sustainable funding in afterschool across Kansas; and 3) build statewide communications efforts and partnerships with regional and local organizations to advance afterschool as a benefit for communities.

title: Maine Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase will support the University of Southern Maine which coordinates the Maine Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase and extension, the grantee will continue to: 1) develop outreach strategies to amplify youth and community voice that center around the benefits of afterschool and feature afterschool programs; 2) convene youth, families, service providers, policymakers, and community leaders to elevate the importance and need of afterschool; and 3) update its database of youth-serving organizations to enhance collaboration and resource sharing.

title: Mississippi Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase will support the Community Foundation for Mississippi which coordinates the Mississippi Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase and extension, the grantee will continue to: 1) build partnerships with statewide organizations and initiatives to elevate afterschool-aligned solutions for student outcomes and community health; 2) raise public awareness and engagement with afterschool programs through strategic outreach efforts; and 3) enhance its communications capacity and digital infrastructure to share impact data across Mississippi.

title: North Dakota Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase will support the South East Education Cooperative which coordinates the North Dakota Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase and extension, the grantee will continue to: 1) increase the number of afterschool programs available for young people through supporting state afterschool policy and quality initiatives; 2) strengthen the partnership between child and family serving systems to support the afterschool field in the state; and 3) increase the number of afterschool programs in the state meeting quality standards for out-of-school time.

title: Oklahoma Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase will support the Oklahoma Public School Resource Center which coordinates the Oklahoma Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. title: Oregon Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: Oregon Association for the Education of Young Children
description: This grant increase will support the Oregon Association for the Education of Young Children which coordinates the Oregon Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase and extension, the grantee will continue to: 1) improve program quality by increasing access to high-quality professional development opportunities; 2) encourage collaboration within the afterschool field and across other sectors; and 3) inform the development of sustainable initiatives to grow new and existing afterschool programs.

title: Rhode Island Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase will support the Rhode Island Foundation which coordinates the Rhode Island Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. title: South Dakota Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase will support the Black Hills Special Services Cooperative which coordinates the South Dakota Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase and extension, the grantee will continue to: 1) support the development and growth of statewide initiatives to sustain new and existing out-of-school-time programs; 2) strengthen statewide partnerships to ensure consistent afterschool messaging and program quality innovations; and 3) update statewide data collection and mapping efforts to demonstrate the status and need for afterschool programs.

title: Virginia Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase will support James Madison University which coordinates the Virginia Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase and extension, the grantee will continue to: 1) promote continuous quality improvement through staff professional development; 2) establish a base of sustainable funding for afterschool programs; and 3) identify and educate state leaders on the importance of increased access to engaged learning and quality afterschool programming.

title: Washington Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase will support School’s Out Washington, which coordinates the Washington Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase and extension, the grantee will continue to: 1) strengthen the statewide coalition of youth development and childcare providers to bolster program quality throughout the afterschool continuum; 2) increase visibility of the afterschool and summer learning sector; and 3) support youth and community-based champions of the youth development field.

title: West Virginia Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase will support the West Virginia University Research Corporation which coordinates the West Virginia Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase and extension, the grantee will continue to: 1) elevate the impact of afterschool in the education and youth serving fields to expand access to afterschool programs; 2) increase program quality by continuing to drive the improvement of statewide quality systems and develop new, aligned professional development resources; and 3) amplify the role of afterschool programs in preparing youth for future careers.

title: Wisconsin Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: Marshfield Clinic Research Institute, a Division of Marshfield Clinic, Inc.
description: This grant increase will support the Marshfield Clinic Research Institute which coordinates the Wisconsin Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase and extension, the grantee will continue to: 1) strengthen and develop new statewide partnerships to support youth; 2) increase public support for afterschool programs; and 3) increase access to high-quality afterschool programs.

title: Alaska Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase will support the Alaska Children’s Trust which coordinates the Alaska Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase and extension, the grantee will continue to: 1) maintain and develop systems to increase access to high-quality afterschool programs in Alaska; 2) develop new partnerships to expand curricula and project-based learning; and 3) develop Alaska’s afterschool workforce through the development of career pathway programs.

title: Colorado Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase will support the Colorado Nonprofit Development Center which coordinates the Colorado Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. title: Connecticut Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: Connecticut Network for Children and Youth, Inc.
description: This grant increase will support the Connecticut Network for Children and Youth, Inc. which coordinates the Connecticut Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase and extension, the grantee will continue to: 1) increase the sustainability of high-quality afterschool programs in Connecticut; 2) expand partnerships to serve youth with the highest needs in the state; and 3) support initiatives that raise awareness of the importance of afterschool in Connecticut.

title: Hawaii Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase will support the University of Hawaii which coordinates the Hawaii Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase and extension, the grantee will continue to: 1) support the alignment of afterschool with broader education strategies in the state; 2) increase quality of afterschool programs across the state; and 3) increase the number of afterschool programs available for young people through increasing recruitment and retention of workers in afterschool programs.

title: Idaho Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase will support Jannus, Inc. which coordinates the Idaho Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase and extension, the grantee will continue to: 1) Develop a statewide message framework on the importance and impact of out-of-school programming; 2) support a statewide Youth Advisory Committee to strengthen the out-of-school-time field’s responsiveness to young people’s needs; and 3) strengthen the out-of-school-time field’s ability to meet the mental health needs of youth in Idaho.

title: Illinois Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase will support Metropolitan Family Services which coordinates the Illinois Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase and extension, the grantee will continue to: 1) increase public awareness of the impact of afterschool on youth in Illinois; 2) coordinate broad coalitions of youth development professionals to improve afterschool quality and access in the state; and 3) increase the number of afterschool champions in the state.

title: Iowa Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase will support the Iowa Children’s Museum which coordinates the Iowa Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase and extension, the grantee will continue to: 1) enhance professional development opportunities for afterschool providers through new partnerships statewide, with a focus on staff and youth wellbeing; 2) utilize family engagement strategies to improve youth outcomes, share resources and generate new partnerships with key afterschool stakeholders; and 3) increase the sustainability of high-quality afterschool programs.

title: Maryland Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase will support the Fund for Educational Excellence which coordinates the Maryland Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase and extension, the grantee will continue to: 1) increase the sustainability of high-quality afterschool programs for youth in Maryland; 2) increase public and private support of afterschool programs aligned with the expansion of community schools; and 3) support quality improvement of afterschool programs in the state.

title: Minnesota Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase will support Ignite Afterschool which coordinates the Minnesota Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase and extension, the grantee will continue to: 1) develop a broad coalition of afterschool supporters within Minnesota; 2) expand the Network’s capacity to implement new programs and initiatives to support youth; and 3) expand access to high-quality afterschool programs in the state.

title: Montana Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase will support School Services of Montana which coordinates the Montana Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase and extension, the grantee will continue to: 1) expand the number of afterschool programs available for young people in Montana by advancing public awareness with Network partners; 2) provide training, technical assistance and continuous improvement tools to support high-quality afterschool programs in the state; and 3) increase access to afterschool for at-risk and hard-to-reach youth through cross-sector partnerships and collaborations.

title: Nebraska Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase will support the Nebraska Children and Families Foundation which coordinates the Nebraska Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase and extension, the grantee will continue to: 1) develop future-ready career pathway programs focused on engineering, teaching, conservation and STEM; 2) elevate youth voice to inform afterschool programs and policy; 3) launch a public outreach campaign building upon the upcoming America After 3PM study; and 4) expand support for underserved community through new public and private partnerships.

title: New Jersey Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase will support the New Jersey School-Age Child Care Coalition which coordinates the New Jersey Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase and extension, the grantee will continue to: 1) deepen its partnerships to increase sustainability of afterschool programs for youth in New Jersey; 2) expand support for afterschool educators to help address statewide staffing shortages; 3) work with partners to conduct a new study on the cost of afterschool and school-age programs; and 4) support the development of a quality rating scale for school-age programs.

title: New Mexico Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase will support the New Mexico Foundation which coordinates the New Mexico Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase and extension, the grantee will continue to: 1) increase the sustainability of afterschool programs for youth in New Mexico; 2) provide technical assistance and professional development services to school districts, charter school and community-based organizations implementing afterschool programs; 3) support the development of curricula in STEM, youth entrepreneurship and service learning; and 4) identify and address high-need areas through updated data mapping of existing afterschool programs.

title: New York Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: New York State Network for Youth Success, Inc.
description: This grant increase will support the New York State Network for Youth Success, Inc. which coordinates the New York Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase and extension, the grantee will continue to: 1) increase the sustainability of afterschool programs for youth in New York through creating new partnerships and engaging new champions; 2) implement site leader institutes to increase professional development for afterschool educators; 3) provide statewide technical assistance to existing programs on quality tools and standards, including those funded through 21st Century Community Learning Centers, and 4) increase STEM opportunities for youth in afterschool programs.

title: Pennsylvania Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase will support the Central Susquehanna Intermediate Unit which coordinates the Pennsylvania Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase and extension, the grantee will continue to: 1) implement a comprehensive plan to establish workforce development pathways for middle school and high-school age youth in afterschool programs; 2) expand access to afterschool programs through creating new partnerships with business and the government sector; and 3) develop career exploration toolkits aligned with high-demand industries such as healthcare, STEM, skilled trades, education and media/arts.

title: Texas Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: Texas Partnership for Out of School Time
description: This grant increase will support the Texas Partnership for Out-of-School Time which coordinates the Texas Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase and extension, the grantee will continue to: 1) increase sustainability of high-quality out-of-school time programs for youth in Texas; 2) build a statewide quality framework and tools to enhance quality programs; 3) increase professional development services with a focus on mental health and well-being supports for youth; and 4) map existing programs to build a database of afterschool opportunities.

title: Utah Statewide Afterschool Network
location: Salt Lake City, UT, United States
description: This grant increase will support the Utah Afterschool Network which coordinates the Utah Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase and extension, the grantee will continue to: 1) increase the sustainability of high-quality afterschool programs with a focus on STEM, entrepreneurship and career development; 2) build a sustainable, statewide data collection system for afterschool programs; and 3) expand professional development services for afterschool educators, particularly on youth well-being and mental health supports.

title: Wyoming Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase will support the Wyoming Community Foundation which coordinates the Wyoming Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase and extension, the grantee will continue to: 1) advance credit for learning models in afterschool programs; 2) implement a public awareness campaign in support of expanding access to afterschool opportunities; 3) increase professional development services for the afterschool workforce; and 4) lead a coordinated effort to expand afterschool programs that focus on workforce development.

title: Alabama Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase will support the VOICES for Alabama’s Children which coordinates the Alabama Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase and extension, the grantee will continue to: 1) increase sustainability for high-quality afterschool programs, including through increased STEM partnerships; 2) expand tailored training for afterschool providers on state quality standards and best practices, particularly in STEM learning; 3) enhance data collection to capture the impact on and outcomes for youth in afterschool programs; and 4) increase statewide communications efforts with a focus on parent voice.

title: Arizona Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase will support the Arizona Center for Afterschool Excellence which coordinates the Arizona Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase and extension, the grantee will continue to: 1) increase the sustainability for high-quality afterschool programs for youth in Arizona; 2) implement the new credentials to increase professional development support for the afterschool workforce; 3) develop and launch quality standards for STEM learning in afterschool programs; and 4) coordinate partners from across state agencies to align resources for youth in afterschool programs.

title: Massachusetts Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase will support the Massachusetts Afterschool Partnership which coordinates the Massachusetts Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase and extension, the grantee will continue to: 1) increase the sustainability of high-quality afterschool programs; 2) conduct research on state educational funding to support new afterschool opportunities; 3) launch an afterschool task force to better align state programs and resources; and 4) implement a leadership development series for afterschool educators.

title: South Carolina Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase will support the South Carolina Afterschool Alliance which coordinates the South Carolina Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase and extension, the grantee will continue to: 1) increase the sustainability of high-quality afterschool programs for youth in South Carolina; 2) enhance quality programs through updating quality assessment tools and increased training for afterschool educators; 3) increase college and career exploration and coaching for youth through afterschool and summer learning programs; and 4) increase public awareness of afterschool programs strategic communications and elevating youth voice.

title: Vermont Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant increase will support Vermont Afterschool which coordinates the Vermont Statewide Afterschool Network to leverage opportunities to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. With this increase and extension, the grantee will continue to: 1) support efforts to establish universal access to afterschool programs in the state; 2) deepen the alignment across existing programs and funding serving youth in afterschool; 3) increase coaching and technical assistance for afterschool educators, including on how to support mental health needs among youth; and 4) increase youth voice and leadership in afterschool programs.

title: Youth Programming and Educator Training
description: This grant increase will support Youth Entrepreneurs, Inc. d/b/a Empowered. Founded in 1991, the grantee provides educators with entrepreneurship training, curriculum resources and support to provide entrepreneurship education and experiences for low-income youth. Goals for this project increase include: 1) increasing opportunities for young people to understand and experience entrepreneurship through the provision of technical assistance and partnership to the afterschool field; 2) spreading entrepreneurial mindset programming into states and cities identified by Empowered; and 3) providing professional development and training opportunities for educators promoting entrepreneurship.

title: University of Michigan-Flint Department of Public Safety Support
description: This grant will provide funds to the University of Michigan-Flint Department of Public Safety to increase patrols and responses to crime occurring on campus and in the greater downtown Flint area. Department of Public Safety officers cooperate with law enforcement across the community to proactively prevent crime and to respond when crime occurs. This grant will support four additional full-time officers and one sergeant for the department. The Department of Public Safety will work in partnership with the Office of Genesee County Sheriff and the Flint Police Department to reduce crime and increase public safety in the greater downtown area.

title: Public Safety Support
description: This grant will provide funds to Genesee County in support of the Office of Genesee County Sheriff to increase patrols and responses to crime occurring in the greater downtown Flint area, covering approximately 30% of the city. The Office of Genesee County Sheriff cooperates with law enforcement across the community to proactively prevent crime and to respond when crime occurs. This grant will support additional sergeants and deputies assigned to the area who respond to 911 calls and provide a presence at special events and other large gatherings.

title: General Purposes
description: Black Sash Trust’s goal is to address the systemic injustices faced by poor and marginalized people in South Africa. To this end, the grantee aims to ensure that all people in South Africa have access to their socioeconomic rights, as enshrined in the Constitution of South Africa. Past support allowed the grantee to: 1) continue working with advice offices in monitoring the implementation of social grants in South Africa; 2) convene a civil society working group on basic income support; 3) uncover corruption in South Africa’s social grants system; and 4) litigate to ensure the government delivers on its constitutional rights relating to social security. This grant will assist the grantee to continue this work with the advice offices. The grantee will work toward ensuring that the right to social security and social assistance is protected, realized and advanced. The grantee was founded in 1955 by a group of women who were fighting for the recognition of human rights for all in South Africa. The Black Sash Trust aims to contribute to the creation of a society that has effective laws and comprehensive social protection for the most vulnerable.

title: TAP Network
description: The goal of this project is to support organized civil society participation to increase peace, inclusion and access to justice globally. The Transparency, Accountability, and Participation Network (TAP) — a project of Accountability Lab, Inc. — will mobilize its membership of over 270 civil society organizations for coordinated action around implementation of Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 16, with its focus on peaceful, just and inclusive societies. During this grant period, work will focus on: 1) mobilizing, engaging and building capacity of civil society partners to foster a global network focused on advancing SDG 16; 2) building civil society capacity to evaluate SDG 16 implementation; and 3) sharing and learning to develop knowledge, practice and public understanding around efforts to promote peaceful, just and inclusive societies. This increase will support costs of a special side event on financing for justice to be held during the Fourth International Conference on Financing for Development in Sevilla, Spain as well as participation of TAP regional partners in activities around the UN General Assembly and World Social Forum.

title: Operating Support
description: This grant to the Saint Mark Community Outreach Center will support the restoration of staffing and essential services for an under-resourced community. These services include programs to fight food insecurity, after-school activities and mental health support. According to 2023 Census data, Flint has a median household income of $36,194, which is one of the lowest in the state. Many of the north Flint residents who rely on the critical services provided by the Saint Mark Community Outreach Center have incomes that fall below this median level.

title: Haskell Football Field
description: This grant will support the Flint Police Foundation to install a multipurpose sports field adjacent to the Haskell Community Center. The field will be available to area youth and groups who want to use the field for football, soccer and lacrosse. The Haskell Community Center is part of the historic Civic Park neighborhood, and this new field will increase access to physical and recreational activities for youth in the area.

title: General Purposes
description: There is a need in the U.S. for public education about the benefits of clean energy tax credits and similar policy provisions that address the causes of climate change. Clean Future Forum, a national nonprofit organization focused on the goal of reducing greenhouse gas emissions, will work with partner groups at the local level in selected states to educate leaders about the positive impacts of clean energy and climate investments.

title: General Purposes
description: Clean Future Forum is a national nonprofit organization focused on the goal of reducing greenhouse gas emissions. With prior Mott Foundation support, the grantee worked with partner groups at the local level in selected states to educate leaders about the positive impacts of clean energy investments. With renewed support from the Mott Foundation, Clean Future Forum will continue similar efforts in 2026.

title: General Purposes
description: The United States, as the second-largest emitter of greenhouse gases, is a major contributor to the global climate crisis. At the same time, American clean energy innovation can also be a big part of the solution. Recognizing this opportunity, the mission of ClearPath — a conservative-leaning clean energy advocacy organization — is to accelerate American innovation to reduce global energy emissions. With partial Mott Foundation support, ClearPath will undertake a range of activities aimed at educating policymakers about the benefits of clean energy innovation and deployment.

title: General Purposes
description: ClearPath, a conservative-leaning clean energy advocacy organization, seeks to accelerate American innovation to reduce global energy emissions. With previous Mott Foundation support, the grantee undertook a range of activities aimed at educating policymakers about the benefits of clean energy innovation and deployment. With additional support, ClearPath will continue to pursue its policy research and educational activities.

title: General Purposes
description: While bipartisan support is essential for durable climate action in the U.S., the network of conservative climate actors remains underfunded, under-coordinated and insufficiently powerful to deliver the durable bipartisan coalitions required for long-term success. The mission of DEPLOY/US, a national intermediary organization, is to strengthen the ecosystem of conservative organizations working to achieve fair and durable climate policies. With partial support from the Mott Foundation, DEPLOY/US will continue to support the field through regranting, coalition coordination, strategic communications and learning and evaluation.

title: General Purposes
description: The mission of DEPLOY/US — a national intermediary organization — is to strengthen the ecosystem of conservative organizations working to achieve durable climate policies that reduce carbon emissions and strengthen U.S. competitiveness. With prior support from the Mott Foundation, the organization expanded its impact through more than 30 regranting partnerships and a comprehensive media and capacity-building strategy. With additional Mott Foundation support, DEPLOY/US will continue to support the field through regranting, coalition coordination, strategic communications and learning and evaluation.

title: General Purposes
description: The American Conservation Coalition was founded in 2017 to build the conservative environmental movement, particularly among young Americans. The grantee undertakes work in three major areas: 1) growing grassroots support; 2) educating key decision-makers and stakeholders; and 3) influencing the media landscape. Over the last year, the grantee enjoyed considerable success, highlighted by over 1,400 media hits and over 700 million social media impressions. The grantee’s membership now tops 85,000 young conservatives across the country. With partial support from the Mott Foundation, the American Conservation Coalition will continue the full range of its activities.

title: General Purposes
description: The Conservative Coalition for Climate Solutions provides thought leadership on clean energy and climate change policy issues. With prior Mott Foundation support, the grantee undertook a range of related activities: 1) educating conservative policymakers and other stakeholders; 2) strengthening coalitions of conservative organizations involved in climate and energy conversations; and 3) growing the organization’s online news magazine and other public communications. With renewed support, the Conservative Coalition for Climate Solutions will continue this work while also building its organizational capacity for heightened impact.

title: General Purposes
description: Nature is Nonpartisan, a national organization launched in 2024, aims to unite Americans around their shared love of nature. With partial Mott Foundation support over the next two years, the organization will communicate with the general public, grow national and local networks of advocates, and work closely with federal partners to ensure environmental progress is sustainable.

title: Connecting Communities in the Americas
geographic_focus: North America, South America, Caribbean, Central America
description: The Connecting Communities in the Americas, managed by CFLeads, is an initiative that has the mission of inspiring and strengthening community foundations and partners for local impact as they address issues that transcend borders. Since 2016, over 200 organizations have participated in Connecting Communities in the Americas, including 150 community foundations from 13 countries in North, Central and South America. Over 2024 and 2025, the initiative supported community foundations with: 1) new mapping; 2) action and learning exchange grants; 3) virtual peer learning activities; 4) the creation and dissemination of learning products; and 5) conducting in-person convenings in Brazil and the United States. A grant increase will allow for the continuation of the initiative in light of a reduction in funding from the Inter-American Foundation and the transition of the initiative to a new organizational host in 2026. CFLeads is a U.S.-based national network of community foundations committed to community leadership.

title: Strengthening the Ukrainian Community Foundation Field
description: The project goal is to strengthen the Ukrainian community foundation field. Since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, Ednannia has mobilized over $2.1 million to help Ukrainian community foundations respond to emergency needs, maintain their institutional viability and address local challenges. Thus far, the grantee has awarded grants to Ukraine’s 15 community foundations, as well as their network, totaling $1.8 million and anticipates awarding another $100,000 before the end of the year. A grant increase will allow the grantee to support an additional seven community foundations that were established in mid-2025. Over 2026-2027, the grantee will provide core support and local funding challenge grants to all 22 Ukrainian community foundations as well as seed grants to any new community foundation initiatives that may emerge. Established in 1999, Ednannia is an indigenous grantmaker well-regarded for its rigorous, transparent, responsive and effective processes to support community-level, grassroots organizations throughout Ukraine.

title: Operating Support
description: With this grant, the Flint Center for Educational Excellence will continue its efforts to improve educational opportunities and outcomes for Flint kids. The organization pursues this goal through the operation of six initiatives: 1) community education; 2) afterschool programming; 3) the Flint Early Childhood Collaborative; 4) the Network for School Excellence; 5) the Flint Parent Collaborative; and 6) the Community Council on Education. In addition to these core initiatives, other focus areas will include strategic leadership in local and state conversations about education, operational and financial oversight, board relations and community stakeholder relations.

title: High School Operations
description: With this grant, the Flint Cultural Center Academy will offer high school course work for students who have completed its elementary and middle school programs. Operating out of University of Michigan – Flint’s Northbank Center, the aim is to provide the enriching educational opportunities that students have experienced in the school’s K-8 program. This grant will assist with the purchase of curriculum, school facility rental fees, recreation center rental fees, security services, elective classes and athletic uniforms and equipment.

title: General Purposes
description: The Michigan Environmental Council is a statewide nonprofit that has been working since the 1980s to promote the sustainable management of air, water and land resources in Michigan through a network of more than 100 member organizations. This grant increase will support the Council’s general purposes, including efforts to expand its partnerships for improved water quality and affordability outcomes in Michigan.

title: African Development Bank Energy Financing
description: Christian Aid, a relief and development agency based in the United Kingdom, has projects across the globe, including in Africa. Over the past ten years of Mott Foundation support, the grantee has established and supported a network of more than 50 local civil society partners that continue to influence the policies of the African Development Bank toward better environmental, social and economic safeguard practices and community outcomes. In the past two years, the grantee has strengthened civil society engagement with the African Development Bank on renewable energy financing.
