With this increase and associated grant period extension, Christian Aid will consolidate civil society coordination, deepen technical capacity and drive sustainable action to increase the African Development Bank’s financing for decentralized renewable energy systems.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Michigan League of Conservation Voters Education Fund
description: Among the most urgent environmental issues confronting Michiganders are: 1) ensuring access to safe and affordable drinking water; 2) addressing the far-reaching effects of climate change; and 3) managing the health risks posed by air pollution. There is also an ongoing need to empower citizens to participate meaningfully in decisions that affect public and environmental well-being. The Michigan League of Conservation Voters Education Fund is committed to educating policymakers, stakeholders and the broader community about effective strategies for tackling these challenges. With this increase in general purpose support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee will continue its core work protecting Michigan’s air, land and water while focusing on water affordability.

title: Daybreak Fund
description: The Windward Fund serves as a host organization for initiatives that address environmental issues through innovative solutions. The Daybreak Fund — a project of the Windward Fund — is designed to promote nature-based climate solutions in the Lake Michigan region. Daybreak Fund provides grants to community-based organizations for sustainable on-the-ground approaches that address climate change, water quality and social equity. This grant increase from the Mott Foundation is contributing to a larger fund to support additional projects in the current grant cycle.

title: Early Educator Wage Sustainability Pilot
description: With this grant, the Child Care Network, as head of the Region 6 Early Childhood Regional Childcare Coalition, will lead the Advancing Wage Sustainability for Early Educators pilot project. The pilot project is offered through the Michigan Department of Lifelong Education, Advancement and Potential. Local funds are matched 2:1 by the state in an effort to understand whether monthly stipends offered to child care workers help to improve retention and attraction to the field.

title: Social Enterprise Hub Building Renovations
description: The Social Enterprise Hub project will renovate a building in Genesee County to expand the physical space and program services of St. Luke N.E.W. Life Center. The Social Enterprise Hub will serve Flint and Genesee County residents who are structurally unemployed with workforce development training, job opportunities and job placement support.

title: INSPIRE — Initiative for Strategic Philanthropy and Intelligent Resources
grantee: Association for the Practice of Transformation
description: The project goal is to strengthen community philanthropy globally. To this end, the Association for the Practice of Transformation will continue to develop and manage INSPIRE — Initiative for Strategic Philanthropy and Intelligent Resources as an informal network of community foundation practitioners and experts. The grantee engages community foundation and philanthropic support organization practitioners through knowledge production, resource sharing and learning events. The most significant of the latter was a global gathering of community foundation support organizations held in Bucharest in April 2025. A grant increase will allow the grantee to build on this momentum and strengthen the global community foundation support ecosystem through additional regional gatherings. Established in 2018, the Association for the Practice of Transformation is located in Brasov, Romania.

title: Capacity Building Planning
description: Under the fiscal sponsorship of the Flint Freedom Schools Collaborative, the Power Initiative will convene nonprofit stakeholders to identify resources, gaps and shared opportunities to build stronger Flint organizations that are more responsive to the needs of Flint residents.

title: The Sectoral Employment Impact Study
description: Launched in 2004, the Sectoral Employment Impact Study produced some of the most significant evidence in the workforce development field and changed national narratives about job training and poverty alleviation. This grant will enable the Economic Mobility Corporation to extend the study and examine impacts 15 to 17 years after the original participants were enrolled in the program. Planned activities during the three-year grant period include: 1) data collection and analysis; 2) publishing reports; and 3) dissemination of findings to practitioners, policymakers, funders, researchers and other workforce development stakeholders. The Economic Mobility Corporation identifies, develops and evaluates programs and policies that enable disadvantaged individuals to acquire the education, skills and networks needed to succeed in the labor market so that they can support themselves and their families.

title: A History of United States Community Foundations
description: The project goal is to complete the manuscript of “A History of United States Community Foundations: The First 100 Years,” originally initiated by Eleanor Sacks. Dr. Laurie Paarlberg, Charles Stewart Mott Foundation Chair of Community Foundations at Indiana University’s Lilly Family School of Philanthropy, will complete the book. A contract with the publishing firm Springer is in place, which includes Dr. Paarlberg’s contributions. Grounded in extensive archival research, the book examines the intellectual, philanthropic, social and economic contexts that have shaped the evolution of community foundations over the past century. Such a book, which will be both scholarly and accessible to practitioners, will be an important contribution to the field’s advancement. This grant will support professional editing services, travel to the Rockefeller Archives Center for completion of research and the costs of a research assistant to complete the compilation of a bibliography.

title: Local Journalism Support
description: This grant to the United Way of Genesee County will provide operating support for Flintside, a community-based online publication. Flintside focuses on positive stories and important community issues that impact Flint residents. Created, in part, for Flint residents to tell their own stories rather than outside publications telling the story of Flint and those who live here, Flintside is part of a large local journalism ecosystem in Flint. Flintside also provides training and support to neighborhood-based journalists who focus on local stories and solutions.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support the Center for Michigan in pursuing its mission of making Michigan a better place by encouraging greater understanding and involvement in policy issues among Michigan’s citizens and making sure their voices are regularly heard.

title: General Purposes
description: The Detroit Regional Partnership Foundation aims to support the Southeast Michigan region with business attraction and economic development initiatives. The grantee brings a particular focus on job creation for the under- and unemployed, as well as expanded opportunities for individuals and the community to prosper.

title: General Purposes
description: Derecho Ambiente y Recursos Naturales works to strengthen monitoring and governance of development finance in the Amazon Basin. This grant increase will be available for the general purposes of the organization, including a regional dialogue process on development finance and the energy transition in South America. There is a need to convene key civil society actors, indigenous organizations and think tanks to assess challenges, strengthen participation in multilateral development bank decision-making and produce a collectively developed work plan to guide civil society engagement in the region.

title: Building A Future-Ready Technology Infrastructure
grantee: City and County of San Francisco
initiative: Graduating High School College & Career Ready
description: This grant will enable the City and County of San Francisco to modernize the Kindergarten-to-College program’s technology infrastructure. Mott Foundation funds will support the development of a mobile-friendly, scalable platform that enables integration with other savings programs, tracks multi-source deposits and manages creative incentives among other features. These upgrades, along with new partnerships, aim to increase participation and maximize the program’s impact on students’ long-term college savings and aspirations. San Francisco’s Kindergarten-to-College program was the first universal children’s savings account initiative in the U.S. Since its launch in 2011, the program has: 1) opened savings accounts for over 56,000 students; 2) helped families save $18.5 million for postsecondary expenses; and 3) increased college enrollment by 12 percentage points among historically underrepresented students.

title: Flint Beat Journalism and Community Engagement
description: This grant to the United Way of Genesee County will provide operating support and community engagement funds to Flint Beat. Flint Beat, an independent news organization founded in 2017, covers news across the city. The publication focuses on information and stories that highlight important community issues, such as education, that impact Flint residents. The team at Flint Beat includes editorial staff, reporters and administrative support. This grant will support general operations and expand coverage of issues and information that impact the education ecosystem in Flint.

title: General Purposes
description: The Global Fund for Community Foundations provides funding, promotes learning, builds a global network of community foundations, and generates knowledge about community philanthropy. Additionally, the grantee advances conversations that promote a community-led approach to development. Activities under the previous grant included strengthening and deepening the evidence base for community philanthropy through research and publications produced by members of the network. In addition to making grants, the Global Fund for Community Foundations has led conversations and a movement that is focused on shifting power from international aid to communities in an effort to localize development.

title: Flint Community Emergency Preparedness and Fire Safety Program
grantee: American Red Cross — East Central Bay-Michigan Chapter
description: This grant to the American Red Cross — East Central Bay-Michigan Chapter in Flint will help reduce fire risk and casualties by funding smoke alarm installation and fire safety education. These programs teach residents, especially youth, to identify fire hazards and develop safety plans. Alongside providing free smoke alarm installation, American Red Cross volunteers visit homes to spot fire risks and offer tailored advice on designing fire safety and evacuation plans. The program also includes educational workshops for youth, distributes multilingual materials and works with local emergency services to improve fire response in Flint’s high-risk neighborhoods.

title: Marian Hall Apartments
description: With this grant, Communities First will renovate the Marian Hall building, located on the northern edge of downtown Flint, and demolish several adjacent buildings. The project will result in new, quality, mixed-income rental unit options for people seeking housing in downtown Flint, remove blight and help to stabilize the neighborhood in which the building sits.

title: Masonic Temple Renovations
description: With this grant, Communities First will renovate the historic Masonic Temple building, which is located on South Saginaw Street in downtown Flint. The renovations will enable the building to be used once again for an array of public events. The grantee will host many of its events in the space and hire staff to promote and schedule events for community participation. The venue will also be available for rent for private events. A tenant will be sought to operate the newly renovated kitchen and restaurant on the building’s lower level, to once again serve Flint area residents and visitors. The mid-sized venue offered by the Masonic Temple is currently missing in Flint and will contribute to an improved quality of life and vibrancy of downtown Flint.

title: General Purposes
description: Philanthropy Puerto Rico supports, educates and helps strengthen its members, grantees and the philanthropic and nonprofit sectors broadly. The grantee will focus on data generation and collection, philanthropy engagement in Puerto Rico and providing its members with support. Established in 2009 by seven leading foundations, Philanthropy Puerto Rico has grown to 23 members and exists to enhance the ability of philanthropy and nonprofit organizations to improve the lives of vulnerable populations.

title: Michigan Natural Resources Trust Fund Anniversary and Education
description: The Michigan Natural Resources Trust Fund, established in 1976, provides a permanent funding source for public acquisition of conservation land and public outdoor recreation. In 2026, on the Michigan Natural Resources Trust Fund’s 50th anniversary, the Michigan Department of Natural Resources (DNR) proposes to raise public awareness of the Trust’s positive impact around the state. With partial support from the Mott Foundation, the DNR will develop and distribute public education materials and host public events that highlight how the Trust’s investments have benefited conservation projects and communities throughout Michigan.

title: Economic Impact of Protecting and Restoring the Great Lakes
geographic_focus: New York, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, Indiana, Michigan, Minnesota, Illinois, Ohio
description: Since 1955, the Great Lakes Commission has worked to protect the Great Lakes and their related economies and ecosystems. The Commission undertook a 2017 economic impact study, which showed that each dollar invested in the Great Lakes Restoration Initiative from 2010 to 2016 could generate over three dollars in additional economic activity by 2036. Different Great Lakes stakeholders widely used the study to support decision-making, and federal funding to the Great Lakes has since increased from approximately $2 billion to nearly $5 billion. With partial support from the Mott Foundation, the Commission and its partners will undertake an analytical study to update and determine the current economic impact of investments made with Great Lakes Restoration Initiative dollars. The study results will be widely shared with different stakeholders.

title: Helping Young People to Employment Program
description: Operated by Faith Foundation Resources, the Helping Young People to Employment Program prepares young people for the workforce by developing essential soft skills that employers seek. The Program encourages participants ages 16-24 to graduate from high school and pursue higher education opportunities and activities that support obtaining gainful employment. Approximately 50 youth from Flint will participate in the workforce development portion of the Helping Young People to Employment Program. Those youth will also receive additional wraparound services, training to graduate from high school and support to ensure they will be employed within six months of program completion.

title: Global Philanthropy Environment Index
description: The Global Philanthropy Environment Index — at Indiana University’s Lilly Family School of Philanthropy — provides a framework for a comparative assessment of the philanthropic environment at the country level and allows for a global conversation on this important topic. The goal of the program is to foster the development of a conducive environment for philanthropy across countries by providing rigorous, comparative data, to raise awareness and understanding of philanthropy, especially in developing countries. The Index’s findings help nonprofit leaders, scholars and policymakers gain a thorough understanding of the evolving environment at the country, regional and global levels, and advocate for a more supportive environment for philanthropy worldwide. The Lilly Family School of Philanthropy at Indiana University was founded in 2012. Its mission is to increase the understanding of philanthropy and improve its practice worldwide through critical inquiry, interdisciplinary research, teaching, training and civic engagement.

title: Centennial Youth Innovation Challenge
description: This grant will support the Mott Centennial Youth Innovation Challenge that aims to engage 10,000 youth in entrepreneurship. Led by the Network for Teaching Entrepreneurship, this project will leverage other youth entrepreneurship partners and the afterschool field to bring an exciting entrepreneurship pitch competition to youth and in-and out-of-school programming across the U.S. Awards totaling $1,000,000 will be distributed to participating youth, as well as resources and technical assistance to grow their entrepreneurial skills. A robust media campaign will be developed for this project to celebrate participating youth, high-quality educational programming and the Foundation’s 100-year legacy of supporting youth achievement.

title: Community Safety Prevention and Intervention Programs
description: This grant to the Community Foundation of Greater Flint will support programming for the Community Safety Collaborative and participating partners. Through these funds, residents will receive conflict mediation training. Programming will also include support for a youth diversion program, public awareness about community violence and additional youth outreach programming.

title: Technical Assistance for Teaching, Learning and Fiscal Stability
description: This grant to Flint Community Schools will support the initial phase of a comprehensive academic transformation initiative aimed at improving student achievement and aligning instruction across all grade levels. The initiative will focus on curriculum redesign, data-informed decision-making and strengthening the K–12 educational pipeline. As part of this work, the grantee will: 1) redesign the curriculum at the high school and Brownell-Holmes STEM Campus; 2) develop a real-time data system to track student performance; and 3) build teacher and leadership capacity through professional development and coaching. Strategic partnerships with local universities and STEM organizations will support curriculum development and career pathway opportunities. These efforts will help lay the foundation for a more coherent and effective instructional system that prepares all students for post-secondary success.

title: Stabilizing Enrollment
description: This grant to Flint Community Schools will support the development of a comprehensive plan to strengthen student retention and engagement by improving transitions from elementary to middle school and expanding middle school athletics programming. The initiative will explore a transition to a PreK–8 model in select schools and create new athletic and extracurricular opportunities to support student development and school connection. These efforts are designed to reduce attrition, improve academic continuity and build stronger pathways from kindergarten through high school graduation.

title: Demolition Assessment
description: This grant to Genesee County will provide funds to hire a consultant to provide a detailed cost estimate for the demolition of the former Genesee County Administration Building and adjoining facilities. The information will assist with future planning for the building and/or site. In August 2025, the Genesee County administrative offices relocated to 900 S. Saginaw in downtown Flint.

title: Charles Stewart Mott Foundation Fund for the Keweenaw
description: This grant to the Keweenaw Community Foundation will support a non-endowed donor-advised fund. Over time, the fund will provide grant dollars to one or more organizations that have the responsibility to sustainably manage approximately 22,500 acres in Michigan’s Keweenaw Peninsula, commonly known as the Keweenaw Heartlands.

title: Transitional Employment and Mentoring Program
description: This grant to Carriage Town Ministries will allow them to facilitate a collaborative, low-barrier workforce development program, which provides unsheltered individuals living in the local parks the opportunity to receive training, case management and emergency shelter while earning competitive wages during the summer season.

title: Engine 464 Restoration
description: This grant to the Genesee County Parks & Recreation Commission will allow critical maintenance on Huckleberry Railroad’s Engine 464 at Crossroads Village. The Genesee County Parks & Recreation Commission is dedicated to providing all residents of Genesee County with high-quality recreational and educational facilities and programs. Genesee County parks are widely utilized as accessible and affordable opportunities for local residents to experience recreation and nature. Attendance at most facilities has increased over the past several years, including during the pandemic when outdoor recreation areas were even more heavily used by friends and families to gather safely.

title: Grand Blanc Relief Fund
description: This grant to the Community Foundation of Greater Flint will support a field of interest fund for the victims of the senseless violence at the Church of Latter-day Saints on September 28, 2025. Funds will be used to support a variety of immediate and longer-term needs of those who have been directly impacted by this tragic event.

title: Genesee County Trails: Fenton Road Phase One
description: With this grant, Genesee County will complete a nonmotorized trail segment in Fenton Township. The trail will be near population sites with homes, businesses, schools, parks and other community amenities. This will promote healthier lifestyles, strengthen community connections and spur new economic development opportunities.

title: Afterschool Education and Outreach Project
description: This grant will enable the Bipartisan Policy Center to support the 50 Statewide Afterschool Network and the afterschool field in the areas of policy analysis, communications and research. To advance afterschool programs, this project will: 1) build bridges between the afterschool field and local, state and federal government initiatives; and 2) assist the networks as they navigate federal programmatic changes in the education and afterschool field.

title: Trails Staff Support, Website Design and Marketing
description: With this grant, Genesee County will add capacity to manage a large trails and sidewalks expansion project across the Flint and Genesee County area. The grantee will also seek contracted services support to develop a website to make trails information readily accessible and available to residents and visitors, and develop marketing and branding for the trails systems.

title: Flint BRAND Program
description: The purpose of the grant is to implement transformative projects that leave a sustainable and positive impact on Flint neighborhoods. Genesee County Habitat for Humanity works with neighborhood associations, block clubs and other local grassroots groups on leadership development and other forms of capacity building. This grant will provide support for the Flint BRAND project, which builds the capacity of neighborhood groups to conceptualize, plan and implement projects. These projects will immediately impact neighborhood conditions and improve Flint residents’ quality of life. Founded in 1990, Genesee County Habitat for Humanity is an affiliate of Habitat for Humanity International, a nonprofit, ecumenical Christian housing ministry whose mission is to bring people together to build homes, communities and hope.

title: Warming Center Case Management
description: This grant to the United Way of Genesee County will support case management services at the 2025-26 Warming Center sites. The funds will be used to work with unhoused individuals and gain a better understanding of episodic and chronic challenges that have contributed to their lack of a long-term housing solution. Flint has experienced an increase in homelessness in the last year, and both providers and partners seek to better understand the contributing factors and design solutions that will result in fewer chronically unhoused individuals.

title: Increasing Food Distribution
description: This grant will provide grant dollars to the Food Bank of Eastern Michigan to purchase protein-rich foods, which will supplement the produce and shelf-stable foods it supplies to local feeding programs and food pantries. This one-time emergency grant addresses the rising demand for programs that combat food insecurity, supporting low-income residents of Flint and Genesee County as they face higher food prices, changes in federal funding priorities and ongoing economic uncertainty.

title: Flint Farmers’ Market Enhancements
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: With this grant, the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation — through its supported organization the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation — will lead two enhancement projects at the Flint Farmers’ Market. The first project is to enclose a portion of the Market’s underutilized outdoor pavilion, which will expand the functionality of the space for vendors and visitors and bolster downtown’s placemaking and economic vitality. The new multifunction space will feature designated areas for food trucks, a new centralized bar and exterior amenities including a music stage, recreational games, community tables and a fire pit. The second project is to improve the loading dock and storage area, which will lead to greater efficiency for Market vendors, including food entrepreneurs based out of the Market’s commercial kitchen. These projects will support efforts to draw visitors to the Market, improve the attractiveness and vibrancy of downtown, and support small business development in Flint.

title: Philanthropic Survey for U.S. Territories
geographic_focus: Virgin Islands of the United States, United States, Puerto Rico, American Samoa, Guam, Northern Mariana Islands
description: The project goal is to strengthen civic spaces throughout the U.S. To this end, Right to Democracy will explore and develop strategies to better engage U.S.-based partners to support civil society and philanthropic infrastructure for communities in U.S. territories. The grantee will conduct a comprehensive assessment of national philanthropy and civil society in U.S. territories to provide funders with actionable insights to: 1) expand the total amount of philanthropic investments in U.S. territories; 2) shift towards greater place-based and trust-based philanthropic practices; and 3) identify areas where the knowledge and experience of people in U.S. territories has the greatest potential to be transformative in achieving the goals of philanthropy. The grantee works with partners across all five U.S. territories and their 6 million+ diaspora to build a movement for advancing democracy, equity and self-determination by supporting and strengthening civil society in each territory. To achieve this, Right to Democracy focuses on engaging with local and national partners to build and expand the philanthropic infrastructure of the territories.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides funding to an organization focused on enhancing the capacity and knowledge of philanthropic networks. In 2026-27, the United Philanthropy Forum will advocate on behalf of the nonprofit and philanthropic sector in partnership with other infrastructure organizations through five key pillar areas: 1) advocacy and public policy; 2) philanthropic practice; 3) knowledge management; 4) member services; and 5) philanthropic infrastructure sustainability. The grantee will lead a vibrant network; maximize the individual and collective capacity and impact of its members; and provide learning, knowledge and resources to its members. Formed in 1998, as the Forum of Regional Associations of Grantmakers, the United Philanthropy Forum is the only professional network that connects regional and national philanthropy-infrastructure organizations to share their vast knowledge and expertise, develop their professional skills and advance their individual and collective work. Its current members are nearly 100 regional and national philanthropy-infrastructure organizations across the United States that represent more than 7,000 foundations and other philanthropic organizations.

title: General Purposes
grantee: European Center for Not-for-Profit Law Stichting
geographic_focus: North America, South America, Europe, World, Africa
description: The European Center for Not-for-Profit Law Stichting is a nonprofit registered in the Netherlands that works to protect and expand civic space globally. The grantee will build on its achievements by providing legal and policy expertise, strengthening civil society organizations and coalitions, developing practical tools, and engaging national and multilateral institutions. During this grant period, the grantee will focus on: 1) emerging threats to civic space related to artificial intelligence; 2) security and financial regulations; 3) restrictions on protest and civil disobedience; and 4) declining resources for civil society. The European Center for Not-for-Profit Law Stichting will also strengthen its use of foresight to help partners anticipate and respond to emerging restrictions.

title: Funders' Initiative for Civil Society
description: Global Dialogue — based in London, United Kingdom — promotes human rights and social change by supporting collaboration among funders and grantmakers worldwide. Through the Funders’ Initiative for Civil Society, the grantee provides research, strategic analysis and convening opportunities that help philanthropy respond to the global trend of shrinking civic space. During the previous grant period, the Funders’ Initiative for Civil Society expanded its influence through research, donor education and strategic grantmaking, while successfully launching the independent Global Narrative Hive and strengthening its Civic Futures initiative. During this grant period, the grantee will update its flagship Rethinking Civic Space analysis, deepen its Civic Futures work on national security and civic space, and expand engagement with climate philanthropy to strengthen donor understanding of the enabling conditions necessary for civil society to thrive.

title: General Purposes
description: Based in Washington, D.C., the International Center for Not-for-Profit Law safeguards the legal, financial and operating environment for civil society organizations and philanthropic actors worldwide. During this grant period, the grantee will launch a new strategic plan and carry out a range of activities including: 1) engaging with multilateral and regional bodies to strengthen norms related to freedoms of association, assembly and expression; 2) providing comparative legal analysis, technical assistance and strategic advice to civil society and government actors; 3) arranging training and legal consultations; 4) producing country‑based and thematic research on laws affecting civil society and philanthropy; and 5) hosting briefings, convenings and communications efforts to counter stigmatization on the role of civil society organizations.

title: Charity and Security Network
description: The Charity and Security Network — a project of NEO Philanthropy — is a resource and advocacy center that works at the intersection of nonprofit rights and national security laws and policies to protect the operating environment for civil society. During the grant period, the grantee will: 1) facilitate and coordinate shared learning and resources among its members; 2) convene stakeholders; 3) engage in dialogue with policymakers; and 4) coordinate advocacy in support of policies that protect and enable the work of legitimate civil society organizations consistent with human rights and humanitarian law. These efforts are a continuation of the grantee’s previous achievements in building resources around persistence, risk mitigation and resiliency for organizations. The Charity and Security Network is a funder intermediary launched in 1983 as a Public Interest Project.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support PHILEA in strengthening the philanthropy ecosystem in Europe and its connections globally. The grantee is an independent membership association of foundations and philanthropy infrastructure organizations that: 1) connects the sector; 2) generates practical knowledge; 3) facilitates peer learning and international exchange; and 4) strengthens the conditions in which philanthropy operates. PHILEA’s membership includes organizations in more than 30 countries and, through national infrastructure members, connects nearly 9,000 public-benefit foundations.

title: General Purposes
description: Worldwide Initiatives for Grantmaker Support (WINGS) is a global network of more than 260 philanthropy support organizations and grantmaker associations working to strengthen philanthropy worldwide through peer learning, research, convening and policy engagement. Based in São Paulo, Brazil, WINGS connects philanthropic infrastructure organizations across 60 countries to strengthen giving ecosystems and promote an enabling environment for philanthropy. During the previous grant period, WINGS: 1) expanded its global network; 2) strengthened regional philanthropy ecosystems; 3) increased philanthropy’s engagement in international policy processes; and 4) launched new initiatives supporting philanthropy transformation. This grant will enable Worldwide Initiatives for Grantmaker Support to strengthen philanthropy support ecosystems in the Global South, expand its work to improve the policy environment for philanthropy, advance more equitable philanthropic practices and develop its next organizational strategy.

title: Advancing the Next Generation of Civil Society Assistance
description: Carnegie Endowment for International Peace has long standing work producing research and actionable ideas to promote international cooperation and advance knowledge surrounding some of the world’s most challenging problems. While this grant represents a continuation in substance of previously supported activities, it introduces a new project phase and title — Civic Action: Finding Opportunities Under Pressure — that reflects an expanded analytical agenda responding to intensifying geopolitical, technological and financial pressures on civil society defenders worldwide. Through its Democracy, Conflict and Governance Program, the grantee will convene two key global networks — the Civic Research Network and the Digital Democracy Network — that bring together scholars, civil society defenders and technologists to analyze emerging civic trends and inform policymaking. Under the new project phase, the grantee will examine how civil society defenders are adapting to escalating repression, changing donor landscapes and new forms of youth driven mobilization while also exploring the implications of technology, AI and geopolitical competition for civic participation. The Carnegie Endowment for International Peace is an independent research institution based in Washington D.C. with global centers and 170 experts throughout the world.

title: Manifest Your Citizenship
grantee: Centro Mexicano para la Filantropia, A.C.
description: The project goal is to promote a more favorable enabling environment for Mexican civil society. Started in 2021, a coalition of Mexican organizations and networks was created to safeguard and promote the right of citizens to participate through organized civil society on matters of public interest. During the previous grant period, the program solidified its structure and programs, updated its name and grew to 38 organizations, reaching approximately 2,500 civil society organizations across Mexico. Centro Mexicano para la Filantropia, A.C. will continue to serve as a platform to support and expand this coalition. In the next grant period, activities will include: 1) mapping of existing efforts to support civil society; 2) regular national and regional convenings; 3) public awareness-raising of the role and value of civil society in Mexico; and 4) promotion of civil society’s right to participate in public interest matters. Founded in 1988, Centro Mexicano para la Filantropia, A.C. promotes the philanthropic and socially responsible participation of Mexican citizens, organizations and companies to achieve a more equitable and prosperous society.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Collaboration on International ICT Policy for East and Southern Africa
description: This grant advances the goal of strengthening and expanding the digital civic space that enables the protection and promotion of human rights while fostering innovation and sustainable development. To achieve this, the Collaboration on International ICT Policy for East and Southern Africa plans to provide thought leadership, information and connections to create an enabling environment for civil society organizations in the digital space. Planned activities for 2026-27 include: 1) responding to and documenting developments related to the digital civic space; 2) providing technical support for critical human rights actors, deepening movements and partnerships; and 3) advancing public interest litigation. The grantee was established in 2004 to respond to the lack of timely and accessible information on technology-related issues. While the Collaboration on International ICT Policy for East and Southern Africa’s focus was originally on East and Southern Africa, programming has expanded across the continent in recognition of the existing gaps with staff based in Uganda, Kenya and Cameroon.

title: Civic Compass
location: Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires, Argentina
geographic_focus: World, South America, Central America, Caribbean
description: The project goal is to strengthen the capacity of civil society organizations in Latin America to engage in digital policy and regulatory processes that affect civic space, democracy and economic and social rights. Civic House will: 1) expand its advocacy capacity-building programs; 2) strengthen research and monitoring of civic space; and 3) convene civil society, government, academia and private-sector actors around digital governance. The project will build on the grantee’s regional experience and partnerships while deepening support for organizations navigating an increasingly restrictive civic environment.

title: Protecting and Promoting Civic Space in Kenya
description: The project goal is to defend and promote civic space and foster a safe and enabling environment for civil society actors and frontline human rights defenders. To achieve this, the Defenders Coalition will champion the safety, security and well-being of human rights defenders, particularly marginalized and discriminated groups in Kenya by equipping them with knowledge. The grantee will provide physical protection for frontline defenders, support efforts for an enabling environment for civic space at the county and national levels, and build a strong institution to support these efforts. This work will enable human rights defenders and other civil society actors to respond to and mitigate any safety and security risks they face. The grantee is a nonprofit organization based in Nairobi, Kenya. In addition, Defenders Coalition strengthens the capacity of civil society actors and human rights defenders to work effectively and reduce their vulnerability to the risk of persecution.

title: Expanding Civic Space in East and Southern Africa
geographic_focus: Botswana, Mozambique, Zimbabwe, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia, Kenya
description: The project goal is to increase awareness, knowledge and engagement of nonprofits with policies and laws related to counterterrorism and anti-money laundering. To achieve this, the Civic Advisory Hub builds and strengthens the capacity of nonprofits to push back using credible information. With support from the Defenders Protection Initiative, the grantee has facilitated high-level engagements on anti-money laundering and counterterrorism funding through: 1) an annual conference; 2) dialogue platforms; and 3) research. Additionally, the grantee has provided capacity strengthening and technical support to groups working at the forefront of counterterrorism finance. The grantee was established as a separate arm of the Defenders Protection Initiative to lead work on anti-money laundering and counterterrorism finance in the region. The Civic Advisory Hub was formally registered as an organization in 2022 to support civil society organizations across the continent.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: World, Central America, South America, Mexico
description: The program goal is to strengthen the capacity of civil society actors to prevent and respond to digital rights violations in Latin America. Derechos Digitales addresses the growing misuse of surveillance technologies against journalists, human rights defenders and marginalized communities. As states across the region expand the use of spyware, facial recognition and social media monitoring without adequate legal safeguards, the grantee responds by generating authoritative evidence, advancing rights-based policy standards and training civil society defenders. Building on its leadership within the Al Sur Coalition and prior results in regional coordination, research and international advocacy, the grantee will: 1) monitor and document surveillance practices; 2) engage policymakers and global governance forums; and 3) provide training and technical support to those most at risk. Founded in 2005 in Chile, the grantee is an independent, nonprofit organization that works throughout the region. Derechos Digitales’s main objective is developing, defending and promoting human rights in the digital sphere.

title: Enabling Environment Program
geographic_focus: World, Central America, Asia, South America, Africa
description: The Fund for Global Human Rights is a public charity based in Washington, D.C., with an office in London that supports grassroots human rights organizations and movements around the world. Through its Enabling Environment for Human Rights Defenders Program, the grantee provides grants, technical assistance and strategic accompaniment to strengthen civil society organizations working in restrictive operating environments. During the previous grant period, the program supported more than 25 initiatives across Africa, Asia and Latin America, strengthened collaboration with the Funders Initiative for Civil Society, and expanded learning on strategies to address the misuse of security frameworks to restrict civic space. During this grant period, the grantee will: 1) deepen support for grassroots networks and movements; 2) expand work with youth and justice movements; 3) strengthen cross-regional learning and collaboration; and 4) continue engaging philanthropy on effective responses to shrinking civic space.

title: Scaling the Digital Activism Hub
description: The project goal is to strengthen civil society’s digital readiness by building the knowledge, relationships and practical capacities organizations need to navigate an increasingly complex digital environment. Building on seven years of implementation across Europe, Africa, Central Asia and Latin America, Fundacja TechSoup’s program combines research, peer learning, capacity building, and locally led initiatives to help civil society organizations use digital technologies safely, ethically and effectively. Fundacja TechSoup is a Warsaw-based nonprofit that supports civil society organizations worldwide through technology, capacity building and cross-sector partnerships.

title: General Purposes
geographic_focus: Central America, Mexico, United States, Latin America
description: The program goal is to increase direct support to local-level human rights and justice workers that tackle some of the most pressing challenges in Latin America. Justice in Motion provides legal support and information to immigrant communities and their families across the United States, Mexico and Central American borders. This is achieved through building the Defender Network, a regional coalition of legal rights experts that navigate local systems to make long lasting change. During the previous grant period, the grantee facilitated cross-border protection and legal services that reached thousands of migrants, expanded the reach and services of the Defender Network and worked to ensure that federal funding was allocated to reunifying families. With renewed support, the grantee will strengthen the Defender Network by: 1) providing transnational support for legal action; 2) building a movement of lawyers in the United States, Mexico and Central America who can work across borders to ensure portable justice; and 3) leveraging the multinational perspective and experience of staff and the Defender Network to inform policies that protect migrant communities and civil society at large. Founded in 2005, the grantee was originally called Global Workers Justice Alliance and focused on providing legal assistance to migrant workers. In 2016, the grantee changed its name to Justice in Motion and expanded its mission to include humanitarian immigration and civil rights work.

title: Advice Office Support Project
grantee: Association of University Legal Aid Institutions Trust
description: The project goal is to increase access to justice for poor and marginalized people in South Africa. To this end, the Association of University Legal Aid Institutions Trust will continue to implement its cluster model program to provide financial, accompaniment and backup legal support to community advice offices in selected provinces in South Africa. The grantee will also continue to strengthen the capacity of community paralegals and assist them with outreach activities. Past support has allowed the grantee to use its network to provide frontline justice services to more than 76,000 people. The Association of University Legal Aid Institutions Trust was established in 1998 and plays an important role in providing resources and backup legal services to advice offices in South Africa.

title: General Purposes
description: The goal of this grant is to address systemic injustices faced by poor and marginalized people in South Africa. To this end, the Black Sash Trust will implement various activities aimed at addressing the structural drivers of poverty, unemployment and inequality. It plans to achieve this by championing comprehensive social protection and, in collaboration with community advice offices, expanding access to justice for millions of South Africans living in poverty. Founded in 1955, the grantee was established to protest the cruelty of apartheid laws. For 70 years, the grantee has worked to advance human rights and democracy in South Africa. The Black Sash Trust’s aim is to contribute to the creation of a society that has effective laws and comprehensive social protection for the most vulnerable.

title: Accredited Vocational Paralegal Training Project
description: The project goal is to increase the capacity of community paralegals in South Africa. To this end, the North-West University will continue implementing its vocational training for community paralegals. This training will be accessible for paralegals working in advice offices throughout South Africa. Past support helped the grantee deliver six training modules to community paralegals across South Africa. The training helped community paralegals to apply legal theory to their practical daily work and was delivered both in person and online. North-West University was established in 2004 when the former University of the North-West merged with the Potchefstroom University for Christian Education.

title: Community Advice Office Support Project
description: The project goal is to increase access to justice for poor and marginalized people in South Africa. To this end, ProBono.Org will support a network of community advice offices to provide justice services to low-income and marginalized individuals who predominantly reside in informal settlements in the Gauteng province of South Africa. The grantee will equip these advice offices with the necessary tools and learning opportunities to provide justice services. With its network of pro bono attorneys, the grantee will offer backup legal support to the advice offices. ProBono.Org was established in 2006 with the purpose of increasing access to justice by serving as a clearinghouse that facilitates the provision of pro bono legal services to vulnerable and impoverished individuals.

title: Dullah Omar School for Paralegalism Project
description: The Dullah Omar School for Paralegalism — a project of the Social Change Assistance Trust — was established in 2015 by a group of organizations working with community-based paralegals to provide coordinated training for young paralegals. The school provides accredited and non-accredited training to paralegals working in marginalized communities in South Africa. In the past, the school provided training to over 150 paralegals and exposed them to the current issues affecting the sector and access to justice more broadly. The school also provided opportunities for paralegals to connect and share experiences. The grantee promotes human rights and social justice by making grants to community advice offices and other local development agencies. The grantee supports groups that promote access to justice, gender equity, local economic development and human rights. During the current grant period, the Social Change Assistance Trust will continue to implement the project by bringing together over 80 community-based paralegals to develop their skills, access theoretical and ideological education and increase their management capacity to lead the advice offices in their communities effectively.

title: General Purposes
description: The goal of this grant is to address systemic injustices faced by peri-urban and rural communities in South Africa. To this end, the Support Centre for Land Change will work with community advice offices to address systemic injustices related to rural land and resource access as well as climate resilience and land-use. People living and working in rural South Africa face daily and systemic injustices as it relates to the use of land. The grantee, working with community advice offices, seeks to improve the quality of life of people in rural areas. The Support Centre for Land Change was established in 1987 to help people living in rural parts of South Africa to access justice.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Centre for Human Rights Education Advice and Assistance
description: The goal of this grant is to increase access to justice for poor and marginalized people in Malawi. To this end, the Centre for Human Rights Education Advice and Assistance will implement a comprehensive set of interventions that reinforce access to justice, dignity and protection of vulnerable populations. The grantee will strengthen community legal awareness through targeted civic education and outreach activities, ensuring that individuals understand their rights and available avenues for redress. Established in 2000, the grantee envisions a Malawian society that upholds human rights, justice and the rule of law. Its mission is to promote and protect human rights by supporting vulnerable and marginalized people to access justice.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Kituo Cha Sheria Legal Advice Centre
description: The goal of this grant is to increase access to justice for poor and marginalized people in Kenya. To this end, Kituo Cha Sheria Legal Advice Centre will implement a series of activities to decrease the justice gap in Kenya. Activities are organized under the following five thematic program areas: 1) legal aid and empowerment; 2) land, climate and environmental justice; 3) governance, human rights and rule of law; 4) forced migration and refugee protection; and 5) socioeconomic justice. Kituo Cha Sheria Legal Advice Centre was established in 1973, making it Kenya’s oldest access to justice nonprofit organization.

title: Promotion of Paralegalism Project
grantee: International Commission of Jurists - Kenya Section
description: The project goal is to promote and scale access to justice for poor and vulnerable people in Kenya. The International Commission of Jurists – Kenya Section plans to do this by leveraging, optimizing and driving the implementation of existing laws and policies on people-centered justice. Prior support has allowed the grantee to undertake and publish research on justice financing and implementation. The grantee also supported and sustained an active network of over 400 community paralegals in six counties of Kenya. The International Commission of Jurists-Kenya Section was established in 1959 and has a membership of more than 500 Kenyan jurists.

title: General Purposes
description: The Legal Resources Foundation Trust’s goal is to increase access to justice for poor and marginalized people in Kenya, while also implementing activities related to sustainable public financing for people-centered justice. To this end, the grantee will provide justice services through its network of community paralegals to people in 15 counties in Kenya. In addition, the grantee will undertake research and other activities in collaboration with the government and other stakeholders to ensure that Kenya has a sustainable, people-centered justice system. The Legal Resources Foundation Trust is one of the leading justice organizations in Kenya, and has over 30 years of experience in promoting justice, equity and human rights.

title: Accelerating Innovations in Access to Justice through Research Project
description: The project goal is to research and pilot best practices for access to justice innovations at the grassroots level in selected African communities. To this end, BarefootLaw will build on previous research to deepen its innovation learnings in Kenya, Zambia and Malawi. The grantee plans to do this by: 1) mapping community justice stakeholders; 2) engaging communities; and 3) training community justice actors on innovative justice approaches. The grantee will also document best practices and learnings in popular and academic publications. BarefootLaw was established in 2013 to leverage digital technologies to create new ways for people to overcome barriers to accessing legal information and justice.

title: Jurists Promoting Access to Justice and Defending the Rule of Law in Africa Project
description: The project goal is to build better relationships between community paralegals and the formal legal fraternity in Africa. To this end, the International Commission of Jurists will continue to bridge the gap between the formal legal sector and those in the informal sector. The grantee plans to engage the justice sector, including the training of judges and lawyers, support strategic litigation where necessary, and use media and communication tools to promote a greater understanding of primary justice. Past support has helped the grantee to: 1) organize convenings; 2) engage African and global human rights stakeholders; 3) support litigation; 4) publish research; and 5) train judges and lawyers. The grantee was established in 1952 with the purpose of promoting justice and human rights within the formal legal sector. International Commission of Jurists headquarters are situated in Geneva, Switzerland.

title: Legal Empowerment Basket Fund for Land and Environmental Justice Project
description: The project goal is to leverage financing for community justice and environmental defenders in areas where their land is considered for large-scale commercial purposes. Past Mott Foundation support has helped Namati publish various toolkits on how carbon projects can benefit communities and their institutions, serving as innovative financing for their work. The grantee also convened 120 justice defenders from around the world to develop collective recommendations to the world’s largest carbon standard, called Verra. Verra has a substantial influence on actors in the carbon credit ecosystem as it provides the best standards for carbon projects. Continued support will assist the grantee to build the capacity for frontline organizations to engage carbon markets, support member-led initiatives for national carbon policies and lead on collective initiatives at a global level to shape standards. Established in 2011, Namati works to build a global movement of grassroots legal advocates who give people the power to understand, use and shape the law.

title: African Centre of Excellence for Access to Justice Project
description: The project goal is to support learning and networking of community justice organizations in Africa. To this end, the Legal Aid Forum will host and coordinate the activities of the African Centre of Excellence for Access to Justice. Activities will include: 1) capacity building for network members; 2) documenting effective delivery models in access to justice; 3) improving the governance structure of the African Centre of Excellence for Access to Justice; and 4) participating in key Sustainable Development Goal 16 fora. The Legal Aid Forum was a founding member of the African Centre of Excellence for Access to Justice and currently serves as the host of the Centre.

title: Development Finance for Community Environment and Justice Defenders in Southern Africa Project
description: The project goal is to increase financing for community justice and environmental defenders from mining companies and development finance institutions in Southern Africa. To this end, the Southern Africa Resource Watch will continue its efforts to encourage mining companies to support community justice and environmental defenders, while strengthening grievance mechanisms to hold companies accountable. Past support has enabled the grantee to develop and pilot toolkits that help communities negotiate social financing that contributes to development outcomes. The grantee also helped build trust between mining affected communities, justice actors, mining companies and government in areas where this has been possible. The Southern Africa Resource Watch is a regional nonprofit organization that promotes the transparent and accountable use of natural resources in Southern Africa.

title: Legal Empowerment Learning Agenda Project
description: The Bernstein Institute for Human Rights, a center at New York University School of Law, seeks to advance legal empowerment research both through the Legal Empowerment Lab and through collaborative research activities contained in a field-wide Shared Learning Agenda. The grantee will continue to support academics and grassroots practitioners jointly in participatory research methods in order to inform richer analyses of legal empowerment outcomes. A series of learning resources will be produced and specific research projects will be undertaken — all of which will actively feature practitioners and their beneficiary partners — including participants of the Jailhouse Lawyer Initiative. In 2024-26, 19 participants from 15 countries participated in intensive learning workshops and regular co-learning sessions with peers, generating new evidence around the utility and cost effectiveness of legal empowerment strategies in combating injustices in widely disparate contexts including supporting street vendors in Brazil and Zimbabwe, and local participatory budgeting in South Africa.

title: Opening Justice Project
description: The Open Government Partnership will work to help member countries build fairer, more accessible, transparent and people-centered justice systems. Work will focus on advancing reforms through peer learning, coalition-building and targeted country support. Activities include: 1) facilitating cross-country exchanges; 2) strengthening global and regional justice coalitions; 3) supporting ambitious justice commitments through the Open Gov Challenge; 4) engaging judicial actors more deeply in open government processes; and 5) amplifying evidence and storytelling on what works in justice reform. In 2024-25, Open Government Partnership convened 10 peer-learning events, provided targeted support to 19 member countries and saw the total number of open justice commitments among members rise to 352.

title: Justice Data Observatory
description: The Justice Data Observatory — a global initiative of the American Bar Foundation — is focused on building evidence to promote people-centered access to justice globally. During the grant period 2026-28, the Observatory will seek to grow its existing work and mandate through convening groups of researchers, policymakers and practitioners across low, middle and high-income countries, with a particular focus on deepening Global South participation. The Observatory will also: 1) develop innovative and policy-relevant approaches to shared research questions on people-centered access to justice; 2) support the production and dissemination of original research findings and evidence through online and offline publications, research papers and policy briefs; and 3) advocate for evidence-based approaches to people-centered justice policy and practice, including through global outreach and partnerships with core partners such as the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development and the World Bank.

title: Community Foundations for Civic Health: Building Common Ground
description: The Community Foundations for Civic Health: Building Common Ground project is designed to increase the number of community foundations confidently strengthening civic health and building common ground in the U.S. The five-year goal is to engage 250 community foundations by providing knowledge resources, peer learning opportunities, technical assistance, matching grants, measurement and evaluation tools, and storytelling and amplification. Anticipated outcomes during the first year include: 1) scoping the civic health and common ground building capacities of U.S. community foundations; 2) engaging at least 50 community foundations through a virtual learning series and a “deep-dive” peer learning cohort; 3) awarding matching grants; 4) issuing an initial measurement report; and 5) hosting an annual Civic Health Summit. CFLeads is a U.S.-based national network of community foundations committed to community leadership.

title: Community Foundations Building Common Ground
description: This grant provides support to the Council on Foundations — a national philanthropic organization founded in 1949 that currently represents over 900 members — and its efforts to reach more community foundations with its Building Common Ground programming. The grantee’s mission is to foster an environment where philanthropy can thrive and cultivate a community of diverse and skilled philanthropic professionals and organizations who lead with integrity, serve as ethical stewards and advocate for progress. During this upcoming grant period, the grantee will: 1) reduce the barrier to entry for community foundations to engage in the Building Common Ground work; 2) create space specifically for community foundations to learn from each other; 3) launch a grant program with wraparound capacity building for community foundations; and 4) amplify stories of community foundations’ impact on bridging differences. The Council on Foundations will leverage its extensive community foundation network, core strategic focus on building common ground and strong partnerships with subject matter experts to further build the capacity of community foundations across the United States.

title: Civic Listening with Community Foundations
description: The American Conversations Project is a coordinated national effort to bring together civic organizations, local partners and national media to support an estimated 10,000 conversations across the country and synthesize what Americans are saying as the country commemorates its 250th anniversary. A significant part of the project will be the Civic Listening with Community Foundations initiative, through which up to 100 community foundations will host an estimated 2,500 conversations. These conversations will be analyzed and synthesized into local insights that will form the basis for community foundations to launch building common ground efforts. The project and associated initiative will be implemented by the National Conference on Citizenship, which was founded in 1946 and chartered by Congress in 1953 to support American democracy and the ideals of citizenship.

title: Trust for Civic Life: Community Foundations Building Common Ground
description: The project goal is to surface, support and spread community foundations’ efforts that allow communities to increase civic participation, build common ground and provide a roadmap for their peers to replicate effective models. The project will be implemented by the Trust for Civic Life, a cross-ideological coalition of national philanthropic and private sector members that was established in 2023. It is a sponsored project of Rockefeller Philanthropy Advisors, a global philanthropic service organization founded in 2002 that has thus far facilitated over $4 billion in grantmaking to more than 70 countries. The Trust conducts annual grantmaking, research and learning in partnership with local civic organizations, of which to date almost a third have been community foundations. Over the coming year, the Trust for Civic Life will support building common ground efforts with at least five community foundations, with a focus on rural regions including urban centers and small towns.

title: Advancing Common Ground Through Community Philanthropy
description: The program goal is to engage with community foundations across the United States in launching or deepening efforts to build welcoming communities and strengthen common ground. Welcoming America will provide the framework, tools and partnership to community foundations that are both already involved in the organization’s network or are ready to introduce their programming to local communities. Over the next two years, the grantee will reach 150 community foundations by: 1) advancing sustainable welcoming plans, policies and programs that foster connection; 2) equipping community foundations with practical tools to lead narrative efforts that emphasize shared values and belonging; and 3) activating a broader set of community foundation leaders to invest in welcoming as a strategy for strengthening civic cohesion. The grantee is a national nonprofit that helps communities become more inclusive and welcoming to newcomers and long-term residents alike. Founded in 2009, Welcoming America works with local governments, nonprofits and community organizations to create environments where everyone can belong and thrive.

title: Swahili Coast Community Foundation Development
description: The project aims to support the development and long-term sustainability of community foundations in Kenya’s Swahili coastal region. Over the past three years, the Aga Khan Foundation U.S.A. has supported the establishment of 16 community foundation initiative groups across Mombasa, Kwale, Kilifi and Lamu counties. Each group has established representative governance structures. Collectively, the groups mobilized more than $36,000 in cash and in-kind contributions, demonstrating growing local ownership and commitment. Building on this progress, the grantee will provide targeted support over the next two years to strengthen the institutional capacity of the community foundations through: 1) tailored organizational capacity strengthening; 2) governance and policy development training; 3) coaching and mentorship; and 4) resource mobilization and sustainable financing capacity development. These interventions will strengthen governance, enhance organizational effectiveness, and position the community foundations as sustainable, locally led institutions capable of mobilizing resources and responding to community priorities. Since 1974, the grantee has partnered with communities to improve quality of life by strengthening local institutions and promoting long-term self-reliance. In Kenya, the Aga Khan Foundation U.S.A. has offices in Nairobi and Mombasa.

title: Community Foundation Development in Kenya
description: The project aims to strengthen the development of community foundations across Kenya. Over the past two years, the Kenya Community Development Foundation has worked with initiative groups in 11 of Kenya’s 47 counties to support their growth. This has included: 1) strengthening community engagement; 2) enhancing leadership and governance structures; 3) building capacity to mobilize funding from local sources; and 4) facilitating peer learning by connecting initiative groups to share experiences. During this period, the grantee also participated in national, regional and international forums to share its experience as a community foundation and its approach to supporting the growth of community foundations across the country. Over the next two years, the grantee will support the establishment of two urban-based community foundations, drawing on its experience as an urban community foundation. The grantee will also provide tailored support to the existing initiative groups, document their experiences and lessons learned, and strengthen their efforts to build financial reserves. Established in 1997 and based in Nairobi, the Kenya Community Development Foundation promotes community-driven approaches to development across Kenya.

title: Community Foundation Development in Malawi
description: The goal of this project is to strengthen and expand community foundations in Malawi. Since the project’s inception, Mudzi Connect (formerly World Connect Malawi) has introduced the concept of community foundations to 16 groups. This initiative has resulted in the establishment of 10 active community foundations. To further raise awareness of this concept, the grantee has partnered with local media outlets to conduct regular interviews. Over the next two years, the grantee aims to support an additional six initiative groups and strengthen the existing 10 community foundations. This support will include efforts to build income-generating facilities and establish endowment funds, ensuring the long-term sustainability of these community foundations. Additionally, the grantee will facilitate the development of a network of community foundations to foster collaboration and mutual learning. Since its inception in 2018, the grantee has supported over 121 communities across the country, unlocking more than $1 million for activities that are community-led and community-prioritized. In 2021, Mudzi Connect became an independent grantmaking entity to further support community-driven development.

title: African Community Foundation Support Network
description: This project will strengthen connections, promote knowledge generation and enhance the credibility of community foundations across Africa through a continent-wide network. The network will facilitate collaboration, peer learning and the exchange of experience, while generating research, case studies and practical tools that strengthen the movement’s visibility, identity and standards of practice. The Initiative for Community Advancement, a South African community foundation established in 2018, has demonstrated the transformative role that community foundations can play in advancing locally led development through sustained commitment and community-driven action. Over the past year, the initiative has helped build an emerging network of community foundations in Southern Africa. Building on this work, the project will expand the network to include community foundations across the continent, fostering shared learning, collective action and stronger locally rooted philanthropic institutions that support sustainable community development.

title: Community Foundation Development in Zambia
description: The project goal is to develop community foundations in Zambia. The Zambia Governance Foundation will build on previous work to support the establishment of community foundations in the provinces of Zambia. This will include introducing the community foundation concept to key stakeholders in the three provinces. Over the past two years, the grantee supported the establishment of 11 community foundations that are at different stages of growth. This grant will enable the Zambia Governance Foundation to support the development of community foundations in the main metropolitan cities in Zambia by: 1) building resources and capacity for growth; 2) creating spaces for learning; and 3) documenting the lessons. In addition, the grantee will continue to support the group of community foundations that have been supported over the previous grants. The Zambia Governance Foundation was established in 2009 and strengthens the institutional capacity and autonomy of civil society organizations.

title: Developing Community Foundations in Chile
description: The project goal is to support the development of community foundations in Chile. Since late 2021, the Community of Solidarity Organizations has defined and promoted the concept of community foundations with Chilean philanthropy, civil society, academia, government and media. It has trained a team to execute a community foundation development program. After prospecting many possible locations, initiative groups were formed in three territories. The grantee will continue to stimulate the emergence of community foundations in Chile and strengthen those that come into being through technical assistance, seed and challenge grants, networking and learning resources. The grantee anticipates the formation of at least eight community foundations in Chile over the next two years. Founded in 2008, the Community of Solidarity Organizations is a network of 281 nongovernmental organizations that support collaborative action to build a just, equitable and sustainable society in Chile.

title: Brazilian Community Foundation Development
grantee: Institute for the Development of Social Investment
description: Since 2018, the Institute for the Development of Social Investment has worked to raise awareness and build knowledge about community foundations in Brazil. During the past two years, the grantee supported 14 community foundations and mobilized $1.2 million in donations to the program as well as in contributions to its matching grants to the community foundations. Over the next two years, the grantee will pursue the following pillars of action: 1) fostering the creation of new community foundations and bolstering the institutional capacity of existing ones; 2) strengthening the ecosystem and collective action of community foundations; 3) raising the visibility of the community foundation model; and 4) mobilizing supporters and resources for the community foundation ecosystem. Founded in 1999, the Institute for the Development of Social Investment is a philanthropy service organization that inspires, supports and promotes strategic philanthropy and its impact, primarily in Brazil, but also throughout Latin America.

title: Latin American Community Foundation Development
geographic_focus: Peru, Chile, Mexico, Argentina, Colombia, Costa Rica, Brazil
description: The program goal is to support the emergence and strengthening of community foundations in Latin America. To this end, Landa Zambrano Asociados S.C. will provide technical assistance and capacity building to community foundation support organizations, their partners and stakeholders primarily in Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Mexico and Peru. During the previous grant period, the grantee supported the establishment of a Latin American community foundation support organization network that today connects 56 community and territorial foundations across Latin America and more than 10 community foundations in the Iberian Peninsula. With this grant, the grantee will: 1) support cross-learning among the various stakeholders; 2) develop a collection of case studies highlighting the range of community foundations models in Latin America; and 3) design an evaluation framework for community foundation support organizations and help them develop a common communications strategy, platform and projects. Founded in 2020 and located in Monterrey, Mexico, Landa Zambrano Asociados S.C. is a private consulting firm that supports entrepreneurs, leaders and organizations to launch their social initiatives.

title: Developing Community Foundations in Peru
description: The project goal is to develop community foundations in Peru. Over the past two years, Mosaico Laboratorio Creativo’s Comuna Nación program: 1) introduced the community foundation concept to 789 public, private and civic leaders; 2) supported seven legally constituted community foundations; and 3) pursued three new regions as potential sites for new community foundations. Over the next two years, the grantee will: 1) expand the community foundation movement in Peru in four new territories; 2) strengthen the institutional and fundraising capacity of existing community foundations; and 3) diversify Comuna Nación’s sustainability strategy and bolster its role as Peru’s community foundation support organization. Established in 2017, Mosaico Laboratorio Creativo was created to develop initiatives and organizations working in the social, educational, cultural and artistic fields to motivate citizens in Peru to work collaboratively in favor of those most in need.

title: CSO Coalition on Human Rights and Counter-Terrorism
description: The project goal is to transform the multilateral counterterrorism architecture so that it better promotes and protects civic space, human rights and fundamental freedoms. To this end, Saferworld USA, a nonprofit that works to prevent violent conflict and address the drivers of insecurity, will continue to host and strengthen the Civil Society Coalition on Human Rights and Counter-Terrorism. Activities will include United Nations advocacy, dedicated support for regional and national coalition partners, and continued efforts to build the coalition’s governance and membership. This request supports the coalition’s work following the 2026 United Nations Global Counter-Terrorism Strategy Review and as the coalition undertakes a strategy review to shape a new five-year plan.

title: Leadership Coaching
description: The project goal is to provide coaching and leadership support to leaders of civil society organizations, equipping them to navigate complex and rapidly changing environments while strengthening their impact. As civic space continues to shrink, funding becomes increasingly uncertain, technology evolves rapidly and climate-related disruptions intensify. Civil society leaders face mounting pressure to: 1) anticipate emerging challenges; 2) adapt to shifting conditions; and 3) respond effectively. Navigating this complexity has become one of the most significant challenges facing civil society leadership today.
