The project aims to equip these leaders with the tools, skills and support they need to lead with confidence, resilience, and adaptability in an increasingly uncertain world. To achieve this goal, Spring will: 1) provide customized virtual leadership coaching; 2) deliver targeted training at relevant convenings; and 3) offer training to small cohorts of leaders on financial resilience and other priority areas. Established in Canada in 2022, Spring works to strengthen the capacity of social and climate justice leaders around the world through leadership coaching and training programs.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides funding to the Buckham Fine Arts Project, also known as Buckham Gallery. For more than 30 years, the grantee has held over 300 exhibitions and showcases, including visual art, literary readings, performances and other arts presentations. The grantee showcases local, regional and international artists. Located in a storefront space on the corner of South Saginaw and Second streets, Buckham Gallery focuses on contemporary art programming and exhibitions.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant to El Ballet Folklórico Estudiantil will support mariachi music and folkloric dance education and instruction in Flint. The majority of participants are Hispanic, however, the program is open to all interested young people. Program participants showcase their talent and newly acquired skills at community events and concerts. Classes take place at the former Walter E. Scott Elementary School in Flint. The program fee is extremely low and does not cover the full cost of staffing. This grant will help ensure continued high-quality instruction and access for any child who wishes to participate, regardless of ability to pay.

title: General Purposes
description: The Flint Cultural Center Corporation manages and maintains the 38-acre Flint Cultural Center campus which encompasses the: 1) Flint Cultural Center Academy; 2) Flint Institute of Arts; 3) Flint Institute of Music; 4) Whiting Auditorium; 5) Capitol Theatre; 6) Gloria Coles Flint Public Library; and 7) Flint Institute of Science and History (Sloan Museum of Discovery and Longway Planetarium). The campus contributes positively to the quality of life in Flint through educational and cultural enrichment opportunities and has a significant economic impact through earned revenue and employment. Students and adults of all ability levels participate in or attend a variety of cultural, educational, and instructional programs and activities across the campus. This grant will provide general purposes support to the Flint Cultural Center Corporation for campus improvements, grounds and maintenance, marketing and campus security.

title: Community Celebration Fireworks
description: This grant to the Flint Downtown Development Authority will support a fireworks display for both the Flint Juneteenth celebration and Independence Day festivities in July. The grantee will work with several community partners, including the city of Flint, the Flint Institute of Music and Juneteenth organizers, to offer a series of family-friendly activities for the annual Juneteenth celebration, including a celebration at Max Brandon Park and a parade. Independence Day will also include a combination of performances, activities and fireworks. The events aim to bring the community together to commemorate important historical events in this country.

title: General Purposes
description: The Flint Institute of Arts — located on the Flint Cultural Center campus — features museum galleries, a media arts space, an art school, studio space and public areas that engage visitors and attract new audiences from across the region. Students and adults visit the galleries, participate in educational programs, take art classes or attend events held at the institute. This grant will provide general purposes support to enable the grantee to present new exhibits that: 1) inspire and stimulate visitors; 2) provide educational programming to area students; 3) offer instruction in various art mediums to people of all ages; 4) provide community events and programming; and 5) maintain its facilities.

title: General Purposes
description: Located on the Flint Cultural Center campus, the Flint Institute of Music was established in 1917. Today, it reaches over 200,000 people during a typical year through lessons, classes, outreach programs, performances and concerts. The grantee is home to the Flint School of Performing Arts, Flint Symphony Orchestra and Flint Repertory Theatre and, in 2021, began operating the Whiting Auditorium and Capitol Theatre. Collectively, the venues offer a variety of performing arts shows and events, including concerts and community programs. This grant will provide general purposes support for the Flint Institute of Music.

title: Music Around Town
description: The Music Around Town series, formerly known as Music in the Parks, is a broad community partnership led by the Flint Institute of Music. This program offers musical performances in public places around Flint and Genesee County. The public locations offer residents access to multiple free performances by the musicians from the Flint Symphony Orchestra, Flint School of Performing Arts, Flint Repertory Theatre and other local talent. The series also includes performances at events such as the Flint City Bucks soccer games and Flint Firebirds hockey games.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Flint Institute of Science and History
description: This grant to the Flint Institute of Science and History will support the general purposes of the Sloan Museum of Discovery and Longway Planetarium. The museum facility is around 107,000 square feet with permanent and rotating exhibits as well as educational and community programming. The Sloan Museum of Discovery opened in July 2022 and has seen record-level attendance since that time. The state-of-the-art Longway Planetarium offers multiple shows and programming for all ages, both onsite and virtually. Summer camps, workshops and monthly evening events such as trivia nights are among the programs offered through the museum and planetarium.

title: Parade of Festivals
description: The Greater Flint Arts Council continues to provide leadership for a coalition of stakeholders aimed at bringing the community together and improving the image of the Flint area through increased participation in festivals and events throughout the year. This grant supports a series of events and marketing activities designed to maximize the impact of established events and cultivate newer, smaller events in downtown Flint and neighborhoods across the city.

title: Overture Program
description: This grant will provide support to the Sphinx Organization to offer a continuum of music instruction and cultural experiences to underserved students in Flint. The Sphinx Overture program, which introduces students to classical music and violin, serves Flint public elementary schools as well as community organizations. The program will provide students with free afterschool group violin lessons. Through a partnership with the Flint Institute of Music, students from the program will be eligible for more advanced violin lessons and classes at no cost.

title: Youth Outreach
description: This grant will provide support for Tapology, Inc.’s Youth Outreach programs. Tap dance is an enduring American art form that increases physical activity and enhances cognitive development for participants. The grantee partners with local schools and community centers to introduce area youth to tap dance and offer regular classes for all ability levels. Each year, the grantee’s outreach programming culminates in a four-day festival that exposes local students to the art and history of tap dancing. Professional artists will continue providing instruction for beginners, as well as more advanced workshops for experienced young dancers.

title: Parks Maintenance
description: This grant will provide support to the city of Flint to continue the maintenance of parks and properties along the Flint River, comprising 532 acres. City of Flint parks provide recreational green space for residents and are utilized for a variety of activities. The importance of parks was reaffirmed during the pandemic as interest in outdoor activities grew. This grant will ensure the city of Flint parks continue to be maintained to a level that gives Flint residents the opportunity to enjoy these community assets in a variety of ways throughout the year.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purposes support to the Friends of Berston, which operates the Berston Field House facility and programming. The field house is over 100 years old and serves Flint residents through educational, enrichment and recreational programs. As a community hub, residents use the facility for a variety of community building and gathering activities, such as resource fairs, Thanksgiving giveaways and celebrations. The capital project that is currently underway will significantly expand programming and other opportunities for the organization.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will support the general purpose needs of the Latinx Technology & Community Center. The grantee provides a variety of cultural and educational programs for youth and adults, including English as a Second Language and Spanish as a Second Language classes, tutoring and youth programs. The physical presence of the grantee on Flint’s east side has established the community center as a trusted resource for members of the Latinx community who have educational or resource needs. The Latinx Technology & Community Center works with individuals and families to meet their needs internally or through a strong referral network of organizations, including health and human service agencies.

title: Violence Interruption and Community Advocacy
description: This grant to the Hurley Foundation will allow Hurley Medical Center’s patient outreach advocate to provide community advocacy and violence-prevention support for Flint residents. As the region’s only level 1 trauma center, Hurley Medical Center serves families in crisis and uses the Patient Resource and Community Advocate program to connect victims of violence, their families, and other vulnerable residents to resources, crisis support and safety education. The program also strengthens violence interruption efforts through partnerships with community-based organizations and local law enforcement, gunlock safety education, emergency response training and outreach programs that promote safer decision-making among youth, adults and seniors. Hurley Medical Center’s ability to employ a culturally competent patient advocate helps build trust with residents, reduce barriers to support and serve as a bridge among medical care, public safety partners and the Flint community.

title: Network for School Excellence
description: The goal of this grant is to support schools participating in the Network for School Excellence. Beecher Community School District will participate in the Network for School Excellence as it leads a coordinated effort to impact a strategically identified group of K-12 schools serving Flint kids. Dailey Elementary School will analyze school-based data and align funding with initiatives designed to improve educational opportunities and outcomes for students.

title: Network for School Excellence
description: The goal of this grant is to support schools participating in the Network for School Excellence. Carman-Ainsworth Community Schools will participate in the Network for School Excellence as it leads a coordinated effort to impact a strategically identified group of K-12 schools serving Flint kids. Dye Elementary will analyze school-based data and align funding with initiatives designed to improve educational opportunities and outcomes for students.

title: Community Education and Afterschool
description: With this grant, the Flint Center for Educational Excellence will lead community education in 14 Flint area schools. As part of a comprehensive community education model, afterschool programming will be offered in all schools except early learning centers. This year will bring a focus on: 1) improving the quality and reach of the Thrive afterschool program; 2) empowering youth, parents and community stakeholders in the initiative; and 3) piloting and scaling promising practices through the Network for School Excellence.

title: Comprehensive Evaluation
description: The Flint Center for Educational Excellence will contract for research and evaluation services of its educational initiatives. The goal is to evaluate the overall impact of the initiatives as a whole, as well as the individual initiatives it operates to move the needle on academic outcomes and measures of well-being for Flint kids.

title: Operating Support
description: With this grant, the Flint Center for Educational Excellence will continue its efforts to improve educational opportunities and outcomes for Flint kids. The organization pursues this goal through the operation of six initiatives: 1) community education; 2) afterschool programming; 3) the Flint Early Childhood Collaborative; 4) the Network for School Excellence; 5) the Flint Parent Collaborative; and 6) the Community Council on Education. In addition to these core initiatives, focus areas during this year will be enhancing organizational stability and maximizing program impact, strengthening pathways that support academic growth and achievement for Flint kids, and advancing community-led cradle-to-career transformation efforts.

title: Network for School Excellence
description: The goal of this grant is to support schools participating in the Network for School Excellence. Flint Cultural Center Academy will participate in the Network for School Excellence as it leads a coordinated effort to impact a strategically identified group of K-12 schools serving Flint kids. Flint Cultural Center Academy will analyze school-based data and align funding with initiatives designed to improve educational opportunities and outcomes for students.

title: Network for School Excellence
description: The goal of this grant is to support schools participating in the Network for School Excellence. International Academy of Flint will participate in the Network for School Excellence as it leads a coordinated effort to impact a strategically identified group of K-12 schools serving Flint kids. International Academy of Flint will analyze school-based data and align funding with initiatives designed to improve educational opportunities and outcomes for students.

title: Network for School Excellence
description: The goal of this grant is to support schools participating in the Network for School Excellence. Westwood Heights School District will participate in the Network for School Excellence as it leads a coordinated effort to impact a strategically identified group of K-12 schools serving Flint kids. Hamady Elementary School and McMonagle Elementary School will analyze school-based data and align funding with initiatives designed to improve educational opportunities and outcomes for students.

title: GAPS: Transition Program
description: This grant will enable Mott Community College to continue and expand the GAPS: Transition Program. The Program — a dropout intervention strategy developed by Mott Middle/Early College High School staff — assists students in transitioning from middle school to the more rigorous middle/early college high school setting and then from high school to higher education. The Program includes both summer and school-year support for students as well as workshops for parents.

title: Student Analytic and Advocate Support Systems
description: With this grant, Mott Community College will enter the second year of its pilot program designed to increase degree and certificate completion for its students. The strategy is aimed at adult learners and will include using attendance and academic data to serve as an early alert for students who may need extra support. This support will be coordinated through four advocates who will build relationships with students and help ensure barriers are removed for student success. In this second year of the pilot, all adult freshman students will have an adult advocate assigned, compared to the smaller initial cohort of the first year.

title: Strengthening Culinary Programs
description: With this grant, Mott Community College will continue strengthening its culinary arts program. With a building manager in place to oversee the day-to-day operations, the third year of this initiative will focus on: 1) completing the accreditation process; 2) increasing community involvement; and 3) expanding culinary services in banquet and catering operations, public cooking classes and signature culinary events. The efforts will continue to reintroduce the Culinary Arts Institute to prospective students and the community.

title: Operating Support
description: This grant supports the Genesee County Land Bank Authority’s planning and neighborhood revitalization activities. The grantee develops and operates a nationally renowned program to reclaim vacant and abandoned property and restore it to productive use. This function is overseen by a professional planning and development team that attracts resources and plans, coordinates and implements neighborhood interventions using a variety of tools and strategies. The Genesee County Land Bank Authority’s activities simultaneously enhance the quality of neighborhoods in Flint and promote citizen stewardship by engaging neighborhood groups in planning the disposition and use of vacant structures, as well as maintaining vacant lots.

title: Demolition of Public Blight for Neighborhood Stabilization
description: With this grant, the Genesee County Land Bank Authority will demolish publicly owned blighted properties along and adjacent to Saginaw Street from the Flint River in downtown Flint to just north of Berston Field House. The demolition work will lead to improved neighborhood stabilization, safety, and quality of life for residents and visitors who traverse the central corridor in Flint.

title: Flint Farmers' Market Operating Support
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: This grant will provide operating support for the Flint Farmers’ Market, a key institution in the ongoing efforts to revitalize downtown Flint, by ensuring access to healthy meal options. Located in the Health and Wellness District, the market provides Flint residents with year-round access to fresh produce and locally grown foods. The market maintains an active calendar of community events, offers attractive public meeting spaces and supports food entrepreneurs through a commercial kitchen coworking space. The Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation is the supporting organization of the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, which operates the Flint Farmers’ Market.

title: Operating Support
description: This grant will provide operating support funding to Michigan Community Capital to ensure that projects benefiting low- and moderate-income individuals in Flint, specifically, and Michigan, more broadly, are supported. Throughout Michigan, communities like Flint are unable to attract significant capital to complete development projects that would benefit low- and moderate-income individuals. The grantee serves as a Community Development Financial Institution and a certified Community Development Entity. In this capacity, Michigan Community Capital provides three resources to assist communities with development projects: 1) New Market Tax Credit allocations; 2) loans, including construction and permanent financing; and 3) technical assistance services.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general purposes support for the Michigan CDFI Coalition to ensure that low- and moderate-income individuals, businesses and communities gain access to the banking system. To meet the goal of increasing access to the banking system, the grantee will: 1) create and provide direct technical training opportunities to borrowers and organizations that support those borrowers; 2) undertake best practice research, sharing and implementation amongst members with a renewed focus on community development financial institutions that have not participated in past activities; 3) ensure no wrong door to enter the banking system, including designing a referral system for borrowers; 4) produce and share reports on banking needs in low- and moderate-income communities based on data collection; and 5) highlight the need for more resources being deployed directly to Michigan community development financial institutions through ongoing education to policymakers.

title: Flint Neighborhood Corridor Strategy
description: This grant to Local Initiatives Support Corporation Flint will support the development of a corridor and neighborhood strategy focused on two Flint districts: the University Avenue Corridor/Grand Traverse District and the Latinx Technology & Community Center. The grantee will: 1) conduct a landscape analysis and conditions assessment for each corridor; 2) engage residents, business owners, and community stakeholders through site visits and interviews; and 3) develop an action plan for each corridor identifying near-, medium- and longer-term priorities as well as implementation partners. Early implementation activities, such as placemaking, storefront activation or small-business support, will be identified during the grant period.

title: Local Child Poverty Solutions Coalition
description: The United Way of Genesee County, in partnership with the Greater Flint Health Coalition and Community Foundation of Greater Flint, will establish and convene the Child Poverty Elimination Coalition as the community’s coordinating body for Flint’s child poverty strategy. The Coalition will bring together local organizations, advocates and executive leaders to establish a common understanding of child poverty in Flint, align efforts around the conditions that contribute to poverty, and advance policy and systems changes that improve economic mobility for Flint children and families. A central focus will be establishing and tracking baseline data to understand the conditions facing Flint families and measure progress over time. Building on the research and dashboard developed by University of Michigan Poverty Solutions, the Coalition will maintain the dashboard, monitor key indicators and use the data to help partners identify priorities and measure the impact of local strategies. The Coalition will also engage local, state and national advocates working on direct cash, tax credits and other economic supports, and help connect additional direct cash pilots in Flint to shared outcomes and evaluation. This supports the Flint Area program’s Child Poverty and Policy Solutions strategy by creating a sustained community structure that connects data, local implementation, and advocacy while aligning local, state and national resources around a common goal of reducing child poverty.

title: Double Up Food Bucks
description: This grant will provide support to the Fair Food Network’s Double Up Food Bucks project in Flint. The grantee provides incentives for Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program recipients to purchase fresh fruits, vegetables and dairy products at the Flint Farmers’ Market and grocery stores in Flint. Good nutrition, especially foods high in iron, calcium and vitamin C, can help mitigate the impact of lead exposure on Flint children and adults. Started at five farmers markets, Double Up Food Bucks is now implemented at 234 sites in Michigan and is a national model for healthy food incentives across 29 states.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant provides general purpose funding to the United Way of Genesee County, a health and human services organization serving the residents of Genesee County through its impact focus areas: Set to Learn (supported learning and youth success) and Basic Needs (emergency support services, access to health, economic mobility and safety). In addition to the core focus areas, the grantee provides nonprofit sector capacity support through aligned fiduciary services and specific capacity-building activities. United Way of Genesee County also responds to unforeseen emergencies in the community with financial and human resources.

title: Housing Predevelopment Design and Feasibility
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: The Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation — through its supported organization, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation — will lead a predevelopment design and feasibility analysis across four strategic housing and mixed-use sites in and near downtown Flint. The four sites represent potential high-impact opportunities for increasing Flint’s housing supply, strengthening neighborhoods and catalyzing development near and along the Flint River and University Avenue corridor.

title: Bretton Woods Project
description: The Bretton Woods Project, an initiative of the development organization ActionAid, has been a key actor on international financial institution reform issues since it was established in 1995. With Mott Foundation support, the grantee successfully ensured that the World Bank’s lending aligned with the Paris Agreement, strengthened transparency in climate financing and coordinated civil society engagement with the World Bank. With this grant, ActionAid will seek to ensure that the policies promoted by the World Bank and the International Monetary Fund facilitate an energy transition that protects the environment, upholds the rights of communities and contributes to positive development impacts.

title: Commercial Banks and Climate
description: BankTrack is one of the world’s leading civil society organizations focused on commercial banks. Since its inception in 2003, the grantee has worked to transform private sector commercial bank lending so that it better serves people, protects ecosystems and upholds human rights. The grantee’s strategies combine research, policy engagement, coalition coordination and community-led advocacy. With Mott Foundation support, BankTrack will seek to reduce commercial bank financing for coal, oil and gas expansion.

title: Global Public Finance Program
description: Oil Change International works to create the conditions necessary for a just and equitable fossil-fuel-free world. The grantee employs research, data transparency, and advocacy to accelerate the shift of public finance away from fossil fuels and toward renewable energy and facilitate a just energy transition. The grantee’s Public Finance for Energy Database has tracked public investment in the energy sector over the past 20 years, providing high-quality data to international policymakers and civil society. With prior Mott Foundation support, the grantee successfully called for a significant reduction in multilateral bank investment in fossil fuels. This grant will support Oil Change International in defending recent gains toward ending fossil fuel finance, preventing backsliding and strengthening energy transition finance policies within national development banks.

title: Climate Aligned Development Financing Models
description: Recourse is an international civil society organization that works to ensure development finance supports a just and equitable energy transition. The grantee combines research, coalition-building and advocacy to inform the policies and practices of multilateral financial institutions, particularly multilateral development banks and the International Monetary Fund. With this grant, Recourse will seek to ensure that two critical policy reviews at the International Finance Corporation and the International Monetary Fund strengthen environmental and social safeguards and align macroeconomic policy frameworks with climate goals.

title: TAI Collaborative
description: The Trust, Accountability and Inclusion Collaborative is a global funder network advancing participatory governance across democracy, fiscal justice and climate finance. Hosted by Capital for Good, the Collaborative functions as connective infrastructure, convening philanthropic actors, generating shared analysis and facilitating coordination in a fragmented and rapidly evolving field. With Mott Foundation support, the Collaborative will implement its 2025-29 strategic framework, with an emphasis on strengthening funder practices, integrating accountability into climate and fiscal agendas, and resourcing civil society under conditions of shrinking civic space. The grant will also support the Collaborative to commission a series of learning products on emerging climate financing tools.

title: MDBs Align Fully with the Paris Agreement
description: The Bank Information Center partners with civil society organizations in developing countries to ensure that the operations and policies of the World Bank Group and other international financial institutions support local communities and mitigate any project impacts. With prior Mott Foundation funding, the grantee: 1) helped strengthen social and environmental safeguards of the private lending arms of multilateral development banks; 2) improved project monitoring; and 3) advocated for the incorporation of nature-based solutions in climate change projects. With renewed support, the grantee will combine field-based project monitoring, policy advocacy and civil society convening to address the persistent gap between climate commitments and outcomes experienced by communities impacted by energy transition infrastructure projects. In addition, the Bank Information Center will seek to advance climate-aligned energy and financing policies in borrowing countries.

title: Latinoamérica Sustentable
description: Latinoamérica Sustentable — a project of the Bank Information Center — works to strengthen the accountability of international financial institutions and partners with organizations in South America to monitor Chinese investments in sectors critical to the energy transition. With prior Mott Foundation support, the grantee strengthened its ability to monitor and document adverse project impacts and developed strong relationships with key institutions such as the Asia Infrastructure Investment Bank and the Chinese Chamber of Commerce for Metals, Minerals and Chemicals Importers and Exporters. With renewed support, Latinoamérica Sustentable will continue its monitoring, advocacy, partner coordination, and capacity building focused on improving environmental and social governance standards for Chinese overseas investments linked to critical minerals and the global energy transition.

title: Development Finance for Just Transitions in the Global South
geographic_focus: Southern Africa, China, Asia, South America
description: Countries across the Global South face an urgent need to mobilize large-scale, affordable climate finance without exacerbating debt distress or fiscal instability. The Global Development Policy Center at Boston University — a prestigious institution of higher learning — seeks to advance financial stability, human wellbeing and environmental sustainability. With prior Mott Foundation funding, the grantee strengthened the transparency of Chinese development finance institutions, shifted Chinese development finance towards investment in cleaner energy and trained a new generation of scholar-advocates. With this grant, the Global Development Policy Center will work to enable an increase in energy transition financing through work on three interrelated areas: 1) debt sustainability; 2) country platforms; and 3) China’s role in development finance institutions.

title: Just and Equitable Energy Transition in Argentina
location: Ciudad Autónoma de Buenos Aires, Argentina
description: Fundación Ambiente y Recursos Naturales is an Argentinian civil society organization advancing sustainable development through policy, legal advocacy and civic engagement. With prior Mott support, the grantee supported communities affected by fossil fuel and other energy projects and engaged financial actors on associated risks. With this grant, the grantee, together with its partners Fundación CAUCE and Fundeps, will continue to monitor energy projects and strengthen the governance of energy finance in Argentina. Activities include: 1) monitoring energy and infrastructure projects; 2) engaging in safeguards and policy processes; 3) supporting affected communities; and 4) analyzing how conditions imposed by the International Monetary Fund constrict fiscal space and influence energy investment decisions.

title: Reforming Finance to Advance an Equitable Energy Transition
description: International public and private finance for the energy transition increasingly lacks transparency and accountability, enabling the continued fossil fuel expansion. Urgewald is a German organization that conducts research, public education and advocacy on the environmental and human rights risks of energy and infrastructure projects by engaging commercial banks, private investors and multilateral development banks to shift capital away from fossil fuels towards sustainable alternatives. With prior Mott Foundation support, the grantee monitored implementation of the environmental and social policies at key multilateral development banks and supported civil society networks in Europe and Asia. With this grant, Urgewald will strengthen the integrity of energy transition finance by addressing multilateral development banks’ indirect support for fossil fuel expansion, reinforcing accountability frameworks for blended development finance and aligning commercial banking practices with climate goals.

title: Developing Tools for the Energy Transition in Brazil
grantee: Instituto de Energia e Meio Ambiente
description: The Instituto de Energia e Meio Ambiente is a Brazilian think tank dedicated to research, analysis, and policy evaluation to promote an energy transition that aligns with economic and social development objectives. With this grant, the grantee will strengthen transparency in energy planning and finance, improve the use of socio-environmental criteria by public and financial institutions and increase civil society’s capacity to influence renewable energy investment decisions.

title: Ensuring a Sustainable Energy Transition in Brazil and South America
grantee: Pontifical Catholic University Rio de Janeiro
description: Brazil’s fast-moving energy transition is creating urgent needs for greater transparency, accountability and protection of communities as large-scale renewable infrastructure and mineral projects expand without adequate oversight. The BRICS Policy Center, a leading research institute at the Pontifical Catholic University of Rio de Janeiro, has deep expertise in development finance, national investment platforms and the geopolitical drivers of the transition. With prior Mott Foundation funding, the grantee documented Chinese investments in clean energy transition and their impacts on vulnerable communities in the Pan-Amazon region (Brazil, Colombia, Peru, Ecuador and Bolivia) while promoting the adoption of socially and environmentally responsible loan criteria within international financial institutions. With this grant, the BRICS Policy Center will: 1) strengthen public scrutiny of Brazil’s climate finance architecture; 2) improve oversight of the Brazil Climate Investment Platform; 3) expand analysis of China’s role in transition finance; and 4) build civil society capacity to ensure the energy transition upholds community rights and protects the environment.

title: Lessons Learned: Removal of Indigenous Lands' Intruders
initiative: Land, Water and People of the Amazon Basin
description: Indigenous lands and other protected areas in Brazil face mounting threats from illegal invasions, land grabbing and environmental degradation. The Center for Sustainability Studies of the Getulio Vargas Foundation is a higher education institution dedicated to promoting sustainable development in Brazil. With funding from the Mott Foundation on a previous project, the grantee created and now coordinates the Independent Territorial Monitoring Network. This network brings together civil society, Indigenous and traditional communities, and research institutions, working closely with government agencies and partners to advance community-led monitoring and territorial protection. With this grant, lessons learned from recent removal operations will be documented, institutional frameworks strengthened, and coordination among government agencies, Indigenous organizations and civil society improved to enhance the effectiveness of territorial protection in the Amazon.

title: Capacity-Building on Land Rights in Brazil and Peru
initiative: Land, Water and People of the Amazon Basin
description: The Indian Law Resource Center has been a key advocate for Indigenous peoples in the Americas for over 40 years, providing legal expertise to strengthen territorial rights, accountability and Indigenous participation in decision-making. In the previous grant period, the grantee trained more than 60 Indigenous leaders from Brazil and Peru on multilateral development banks and how to engage in their policies and project cycles. Over the next grant period, the Indian Law Resource Center will strengthen Indigenous participation in decision-making processes in the Amazon, with the goal of improving environmental and social safeguards tied to large-scale development programs and investments.

title: Advancing Land Rights and Integrity in the Amazon
grantee: Instituto Internacional de Educação do Brasil
initiative: Land, Water and People of the Amazon Basin
description: The Instituto Internacional de Educação do Brasil is a Brazilian civil society organization with more than 25 years of experience supporting Indigenous peoples and traditional communities in the Amazon regarding land rights, territorial governance and forest management. With this grant, the grantee will work with four representative community associations in the Juruá and Madeira river basins. These associations are composed of and led by community members and serve as the governance organizations of their collective territories. The project will advance the legal recognition of about 880,800 hectares of collectively used forest lands, improve coordination with public agencies and strengthen local leadership to support long-term forest protection and sustainable livelihoods.

title: Amazonian Peoples’ Climate Resilience
initiative: Land, Water and People of the Amazon Basin
description: The Amazon Environmental Research Institute, a nonprofit research organization based in Brazil, works to advance understanding of fire and other climate dynamics in the Amazon. In the previous grant period, the organization analyzed and disseminated evidence on how fire regimes drive ecological and social changes in the Brazilian Amazon. In this renewal, the grantee will deepen research on climate-induced changes in the forest, support climate adaptation strategies and expand knowledge dissemination, with the goal of strengthening the resilience of forests and communities.

title: Investment Threats in the Amazon: IDB Policies and Programs
initiative: Land, Water and People of the Amazon Basin
description: The Bank Information Center is a civil society organization with extensive experience monitoring development finance institutions and helping them improve their transparency, accountability and safeguard policies. Building on this track record, the project aims to strengthen accountability and improve social and environmental outcomes across the Inter-American Development Bank’s investments in the Amazon. Over the grant period, the grantee will support civil society oversight and engagement of Indigenous peoples and traditional communities around the grantee’s Amazon Forever and Conexión Sur programs, which finance sustainable forest production and large-scale infrastructure across the region. The grant will also support efforts to document lessons learned, strengthen the grantee’s Amazon Advisory Panel and build local capacity to engage meaningfully in Bank Information Center-led processes.

title: Strengthening Indigenous Territories to Address Environmental Threats and Illicit Pressures
grantee: Center for Climate Crime Analysis Brazil
initiative: Land, Water and People of the Amazon Basin
description: The Center for Climate Crime Analysis Brazil is an organization connected to the Center for Climate Crime Analysis Netherlands, with a multidisciplinary team in Brazil that uses legal and geospatial analysis to detect and prevent illicit activities that drive deforestation in the Amazon. This grant will support the development and initial implementation of an environmental management plan for the Maró Indigenous Territory in Pará. In the region, illegal logging, land grabbing and expanding extractive activities are intensifying pressure on Indigenous lands. The project aims to use the planning process as a tool to strengthen Indigenous capacity to anticipate, manage and respond to emerging risks.

title: General Purposes
initiative: Land, Water and People of the Amazon Basin
description: Derecho Ambiente y Recursos Naturales is a Peruvian nongovernmental organization focused on sustainable development and conservation in the Amazon basin. In the previous grant period, the organization continued to implement its strategic plan, including efforts to strengthen social and environmental safeguards governing the flow of international investment to the region. In the next grant period, the organization will continue implementing its strategic priorities, including strengthening oversight of infrastructure investments in the Peruvian Amazon and protecting against further deforestation by expanding community-based monitoring and other territorial protection practices. Derecho Ambiente y Recursos Naturales will also advance community-centered renewable energy solutions that support forest conservation, climate resilience and the rights of Indigenous peoples and traditional communities.

title: Improving Environmental and Infrastructure Policies in Xingu
initiative: Land, Water and People of the Amazon Basin
description: Instituto Socioambiental is a Brazilian nonprofit dedicated to advancing sustainable development in the Amazon and the rights of these communities to self-determination. During the previous grant period, the grantee strengthened community-led monitoring and produced critical knowledge on the cumulative impacts of large-scale hydropower and mining investments in the Xingu basin. Over the next grant period, Instituto Socioambiental will strengthen communities’ participation in decision-making processes amid growing pressures from infrastructure investment and mining activities. The project will also expand access to renewable energy solutions to strengthen sustainable livelihoods.

title: Community-Driven Amazon Resilience Strategy
initiative: Land, Water and People of the Amazon Basin
description: The Woodwell Climate Research Center is a leading scientific organization working globally to address climate change and, in Brazil, protect the Amazon Rainforest. Building on its expertise in fire science, climate risk analysis and geospatial tools, the grantee partners with Brazilian research institutions to address mounting pressures from climate change and human activities, including fire, drought, smoke, mining and deforestation. Over the last grant period, the grantee examined the links between climate-induced risks and their implications for human health. With this renewal, the grantee will provide capacity-building for Indigenous leaders to monitor their territories on climate-induced threats. Woodwell Climate Research Center will also develop a pilot community-driven monitoring system that integrates Indigenous knowledge with satellite data to strengthen community resilience to fire and other climate-related risks.

title: Integrated Community-Led Infrastructure in the Tapajos Basin
grantee: Centro de Estudos Avançados de Promoção Social e Ambiental
initiative: Land, Water and People of the Amazon Basin
description: The Centro de Estudos Avançados de Promoção Social e Ambiental, a nonprofit organization founded in 1985, promotes sustainable development and the conservation of the Amazon by strengthening public policies and improving livelihoods for Indigenous and traditional communities. During the previous grant period, the grantee expanded off-grid renewable energy access for primary health care facilities and trained local solar technicians in the Tapajós River basin. During the next grant period, Centro de Estudos Avançados de Promoção Social e Ambiental will implement renewable energy technologies in the Tapajós-Arapiuns Extractive Reserve while strengthening community governance to manage the systems.

title: General Purposes
initiative: Land, Water and People of the Amazon Basin
description: Fondo Emerger is a Colombia-based small-grant fund, established in 2018, that supports grassroots organizations, Indigenous peoples, and local communities working to protect ecosystems and livelihoods. In the Colombian Amazon, communities face accelerating deforestation driven by illegal mining and infrastructure expansion, placing increasing pressure on forests and livelihoods. This general purposes grant will strengthen Fondo Emerger’s institutional capacity to ensure transparent and efficient grantmaking that responds to these escalating threats and supports community-led conservation in the Colombian Amazon.

title: General Purposes
initiative: Land, Water and People of the Amazon Basin
description: Fundación Ñeque provides small grants and technical assistance to Indigenous peoples and traditional communities across Ecuador. These groups work to protect forests and enhance climate resilience. This general purposes grant will support both the organization’s institutional capacity and its grantmaking program, ensuring transparent and effective grant administration while expanding financial and technical support to community-led conservation initiatives in the Ecuadorian Amazon.

title: Small Grant Funds for Community Resilience in Bolivia
initiative: Land, Water and People of the Amazon Basin
location: Santa Cruz de la Sierra, Bolivia
description: Fundación Socioambiental Semilla is a Bolivian organization that offers small grants and technical assistance to Indigenous and traditional groups and communities. These groups work to protect forests and enhance climate resilience in the Amazon. This grant will support the grantee’s small-grants program in the Bolivian Amazon, helping communities address deforestation, extractive pressures and climate effects. This project also aims to boost sustainable livelihoods and territorial governance. Additionally, this grant will enhance Fundación Socioambiental Semilla’s institutional capacity, ensuring transparent and effective grantmaking that promotes community-led conservation and climate-resilient development.

title: Renewable Community-Led Infrastructure in the Tapajós Basin
initiative: Land, Water and People of the Amazon Basin
description: This project supports Michigan State University in implementing a community-engaged model for renewable energy systems in the Tapajós-Arapiuns basin of the Brazilian Amazon. Over the previous grant period, the grantee installed renewable energy systems, trained local technicians, and shared lessons through media and academic publications. Over the next grant period, the grantee will expand solar infrastructure in selected communities. The grantee will also strengthen the Federal University of Western Pará, increasing its capacity to train students and communities in solar technology and system maintenance. Michigan State University will share lessons for expanding community-centered renewable energy across the Amazon.

title: Territorial Rights and Mining Expansion in the Amazon Basin
initiative: Land, Water and People of the Amazon Basin
description: Amazon Watch is an environmental and human rights organization that partners with Indigenous peoples to protect the Amazon rainforest and defend territorial rights. This grant will support Indigenous-led efforts to address the potential social and environmental impacts of mining projects in the Amazon through technical assistance, strategic communications and engagement with key actors. The grantee will strengthen coordination among Indigenous organizations and civil society groups, and facilitate exchanges with other communities affected by mining. The project aims to reinforce territorial protection while generating lessons and forging partnerships that can inform broader efforts to address mining expansion in Indigenous territories across the Amazon basin.

title: Making One Water Policy Progress
geographic_focus: Wisconsin, North America, Midwest, United States, Michigan, Illinois, Ohio, Indiana
description: The Alliance for the Great Lakes is a leading regional organization focused on protecting and restoring the Great Lakes, safeguarding clean water and strengthening community resilience. With support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee will advance policies that provide safe, clean and accessible water for residents of the Great Lakes region and help ensure the Great Lakes are protected and healthy for future generations.

title: Bridge Michigan Environment Watch
description: Bridge Michigan’s Environment Watch is a digital newspaper published by the Center for Michigan, a nonprofit organization that seeks to make Michigan better through high-quality, nonpartisan journalism. Bridge Michigan is also a contributing partner in the Great Lakes News Collaborative, a Mott-funded initiative that seeks to improve news coverage of water issues in the region. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, coverage of these issues has gained audience support and growth, increased readership and subscribers, as well as garnered several awards. With renewed support, the Center for Michigan will continue to produce in-depth, high-quality, public-service journalism for its Environment Watch publication and the Great Lakes News Collaborative.

title: Saginaw Bay Watershed Initiative Network (WIN)
description: The Conservation Fund is a national nonprofit organization that has advanced sustainable development through innovative land conservation programs since 1985. The Saginaw Bay Watershed Initiative Network is a multistakeholder effort in Michigan led by the grantee over the past 20 years. The initiative works with local communities in the watershed to identify priority projects that protect water and other environmental resources while supporting economic and social sustainability. The Conservation Fund, through this project, will support a watershed regranting program, strengthen public engagement on key watershed issues and pilot a funding mechanism to advance nature-based water solutions through place-based initiatives.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Cities Initiative
description: The Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Cities Initiative is a coalition of over 400 U.S. and Canadian mayors and municipal officials dedicated to advancing the protection and restoration of the region and its water resources. The grantee provides services to its members to integrate environmental, economic and social priorities into solutions that protect the Great Lakes. With previous Mott Foundation support, the grantee convened, collaborated and advanced policies for the benefit of coastal cities within the region. With renewed support, the Great Lakes and St. Lawrence Cities Initiative will continue to advance and expand policies and priorities across member communities.

title: Protecting Treaty Resources through Water Protection
grantee: Great Lakes Indian Fish and Wildlife Commission
description: The Great Lakes Indian Fish and Wildlife Commission works with tribal governments in Michigan, Wisconsin and Minnesota to protect tribal interests in and the ecology of ceded territories in the northern portions of those states. A Commission priority is for tribes to be effective participants in permitting and environmental review processes, using science to inform decision-makers about potential impacts on tribal resources. With prior support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee expanded its water monitoring, data collection and wetland mapping. With renewed support, research will inform and enhance members’ ability to participate fully on water quality issues and ecosystem protection, while building capacity through a natural resource management internship program.

title: Increasing the Impact of Land Conservation on Great Lakes Water Quality
geographic_focus: Michigan, Minnesota, New York, Ohio, Wisconsin, Illinois, Indiana, Pennsylvania
description: The Land Trust Alliance is a national nonprofit that coordinates technical and capacity-building support for its nationwide network of land trust members. Over the past two decades of Mott Foundation support, the Alliance has: 1) established a Midwest Great Lakes program; 2) convened practitioners; 3) hosted the first Land Trust Land & Water Summit; and 4) piloted demonstration projects to improve water quality. With this grant, the Alliance will support its members in expanding nature-based water and land conservation solutions. The Alliance will enhance the capacity of its member land trusts to implement water and land conservation solutions in the Great Lakes region. The Land Trust Alliance will also facilitate the exchange of best practices on water and land conservation among its land trust members in the Great Lakes region.

title: Michigan Clean Water Project
grantee: Michigan League of Conservation Voters Education Fund
description: Michigan faces many water resource challenges, including inadequate infrastructure funding, toxic contamination and uneven access to safe and affordable drinking water. These challenges are deeply interconnected and without coordinated, forward-looking policy leadership, they will continue to compound. Over the next two years, with partial Mott Foundation funding, the Michigan League of Conservation Voters Education Fund will lead a nonpartisan education program aimed at ensuring that infrastructure, toxic contamination, affordability and natural resource protection are treated as a unified “source to tap” challenge requiring integrated solutions. The grantee, a well-established statewide group, has years of experience informing Michigan citizens and policymakers about water issues and other environmental challenges.

title: Michigan Clean Water Corps
description: Founded in 1855, Michigan State University is a leading research institution with more than 50,000 students and recognized expertise in water science, community engagement and extension. The Michigan Clean Water Corps project aims to leverage 51 years of statewide water quality data collected through their volunteer-driven initiative, which involves over 5,000 participants. Through this project, the grantee will: 1) conduct comprehensive statewide analyses of water data to pinpoint priority water quality threats; 2) identify emerging trends; and 3) propose actionable solutions across Michigan’s diverse watersheds. Additionally, the grantee will deploy practical tools and foster strategic partnerships in six key watersheds to empower communities to make informed decisions regarding water resource management. Ultimately, the project seeks to create a scalable model that transforms citizen science efforts into lasting improvements in community water governance and management.

title: General Purposes
description: Milwaukee Water Commons is a grassroots organization focused on community engagement and organizing around water and environmental justice in the Great Lakes region. The grantee helps strengthen community and water leadership and inform policy through initiatives to build water, climate, and racial equity in Milwaukee and Wisconsin. The grantee addresses the need to include community input, especially for those who have historically been excluded from the process, on topics such as lead service line replacement and contaminants in drinking water. A new grant from the Mott Foundation will support the Milwaukee Water Commons’ water programs, partnerships and policy work in the city, state and region.

title: Midwest Environmental Justice Network
geographic_focus: Indiana, Minnesota, Michigan, Ohio, Wisconsin, Illinois
description: The Minneapolis Foundation, a Minnesota-based community foundation, supports the Midwest Environmental Justice Network, a project led by and for community-based organizations across a 12-state region. The Network connects and supports leaders of grassroots groups to address environmental justice and water equity impacting their communities at the local level. With prior Mott Foundation funding, the grantee increased its membership, financial resources and regranting to build capacity and collective strength. With renewed support, Minneapolis Foundation will provide peer learning, training, capacity building and grants for groups working on water issues in the Great Lakes region. The Network will also increase its outreach and communications to share strategies and stories of its members to grow the network.

title: General Purposes
description: Minnesota Environmental Partnership is a broad coalition of environmental and conservation groups from across the state. The grantee provides leadership on water policy as well as opportunities for its members to convene, communicate and collaborate to protect the state’s natural resources and environmental health. With prior support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee advanced equity for underserved communities and protections for land and water, with a focus on Lake Superior. Renewed support will advance progress toward their overall goals of clean water, climate resilience and Great Lakes policy work in the state and region.

title: Freshwater and Forests in Michigan
description: Michigan’s northern forests and the associated freshwater resources face a series of interrelated threats rooted in decades of forest management that have eroded the forest’s ecological diversity. The Nature Conservancy, a global conservation organization, works to protect and restore Michigan’s Northwoods and waters through a variety of means. Over the next two years with partial Mott support, the grantee will build a replicable, science-based model that links forest health directly to freshwater quality. Specific activities will include managing more forested land with water-focused practices, developing new markets for tree species that have outsized positive impacts on water quality and sharing lessons learned with key partners and other stakeholders.

title: Ohio Clean Water Project
description: The Ohio Environmental Council is a multi-issue, statewide environmental organization. With prior support, the grantee has helped Ohio make progress on a number of water issues including: 1) lead service line replacement; 2) funding for water quality improvements; and 3) voluntary best management practices that reduce agricultural runoff. With this grant, the Ohio Environmental Council will continue its work to protect Ohio’s waterways, including Lake Erie, and share lessons learned with stakeholders in other states and nationally.

title: Water Quality Demonstration Project
description: The Savanna Institute is a nonprofit organization dedicated to supporting small- to medium-scale farmers in the Great Lakes in adopting agroforestry models that restore soil health, improve farm viability and deliver measurable water-quality benefits. The grantee’s proposed project aims to deliver three outcomes. First, the organization will scale agroforestry as a nature-based solution to improve water quality in the Great Lakes region through a network of model agroforestry farms. Secondly, the grantee will further develop a framework that links measurable water-quality improvements from agroforestry to financial incentives for farmers. Lastly, the Savanna Institute will engage various stakeholders through strategic communications on the potential role of agroforestry as a tool for nature-based water-quality improvement and rural economic transformation in the Great Lakes region.

title: Michigan Radio - The Environment Report
description: Michigan Public is an award-winning public radio station housed at the University of Michigan and is the largest public radio station in the state. With prior support from the Mott Foundation, the station has enhanced its coverage of water issues in the Great Lakes basin with stories that are broadcast and appear on the station’s website. Michigan Public is also a contributing member to the Great Lakes News Collaborative, a Mott-funded initiative to enhance news coverage of the Great Lakes and water issues. Renewed support will enable the University of Michigan to continue this work through Michigan Public, broadening its audience reach and content related to the Great Lakes and water issues.

title: General Purposes
description: Since 2008, We The People of Detroit, a community-based nonprofit organization, has been working to advance water resource protection and conservation in Detroit, across Michigan and nationally. With this grant, the grantee will strengthen its organizational and operational capacity. The grantee will also deliver results across its three core program areas: 1) the Water Policy Education and Engagement Program; 2) We the Youth of Detroit; and 3) the Community Research Collective.

title: Daybreak Fund
description: The Daybreak Fund is a project of the Windward Fund, which hosts and fiscally sponsors various innovative environmental initiatives. The Daybreak Fund is a donor collaborative that pools financial and technical support from multiple funders to accelerate nature-based, community-centered water and climate solutions across the Lake Michigan basin. The Daybreak Fund supports projects that restore wetlands and forests, expand regenerative agriculture and green stormwater infrastructure. The Daybreak Fund also strengthens Indigenous leadership in water stewardship. With partial funding from the Mott Foundation, the Daybreak Fund will continue to support several model water resource conservation projects annually. The model projects will deliver multiple benefits, including improved drinking water quality, protection of surface and groundwater and enhanced community well-being in the Great Lakes region.

title: Clean Water Initiative
description: American Rivers is a national organization whose mission is to protect wild rivers, restore damaged rivers and improve water quality for people and nature. The organization’s Clean Water Program addresses the challenges of polluted waterways, aging water infrastructure and water management at the local, state and national levels. With partial support from the Mott Foundation, American Rivers will implement the Clean Water Program, which will include working on urban rivers, developing a national stormwater policy and building broad-based public support for clean water and stormwater solutions.

title: General Purposes
description: The Biodiversity Funders Group is a philanthropic network of environmental, conservation, climate and energy funders, founded in 1987, that serves as a learning, coordination and collaboration hub across the biodiversity field. With approximately 80 member institutions and activities benefiting more than 200 grantmakers, the grantee provides regular webinars, newsletters and annual convenings through its programs and working groups, including the Funders of the Amazon Basin group. Building on growing membership and shared goals, Biodiversity Funders Group will continue to: 1) advance cross-funder collaboration; 2) convene leaders from climate, conservation and Tribal communities; and 3) promote more impactful biodiversity philanthropy in the U.S. and around the world including the Amazon.

title: Building Collective Power for Clean Water through Indigenous Leadership
description: Native Americans in Philanthropy is the only national, Native-led organization dedicated to strengthening relationships among tribal nations, tribal-led organizations and funders. The organization builds capacity, provides technical assistance, and funds land and water projects in Indigenous territories to help address persistent barriers, including access to clean water. With funding from the Mott Foundation, Native Americans in Philanthropy will support, engage with, and advance tribal-led efforts and policies to safeguard water resources nationally.

title: General Purposes
description: Water utilities and other water management organizations across the U.S. are facing a range of interrelated challenges. These include disparities in access to safe and affordable drinking water, wavering federal support for water infrastructure spending and climate change. New ways of managing the nation’s water resources are needed. The U.S. Water Alliance — a highly regarded national nonprofit — is well-positioned to help fashion such new approaches. Over the next two years, with general purposes support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee will: 1) support leaders in the field; 2) drive local action; 3) advocate for water funding and related policy reforms; and 4) use strategic communications to build public understanding and support.

title: General Purposes
description: Clean, reliable freshwater is essential for communities and ecosystems to thrive, yet our nation’s waters are facing grave threats, including pollution, overuse and ineffective management practices. In response, the Water Foundation is working across philanthropy, government and the nonprofit field to build durable One Water solutions that deliver clean, affordable water from source to tap. With partial funding from the Mott Foundation, the grantee will advance this vision by supporting state-level efforts that pioneer and demonstrate sustainable water management approaches, sharing these success stories nationally through strategic communications and convening partners to coordinate activities.

title: Data Collection and Evaluation-Annual Field Survey
description: This grant will enable the University of Michigan to develop a national survey and research database of children’s savings account programs. More than a simple inventory, the project will identify existing programs, classify them using a clear definition, assess their alignment with key design principles and create a standardized resource for research, philanthropy and policy development. The database will serve the broad field, including researchers, policymakers, practitioners and funders. The grantee’s Center for Assets, Education and Inclusion is a leading research center in the Child Development Account field, having conducted many of the studies that have shaped practice and informed policy development, including evaluations of San Francisco’s Kindergarten to College program, Maine’s Harold Alfond College Challenge and Promise Indiana in Wabash County.

title: Linking the College Attainment and Early Accounts Fields
description: This renewal grant will enable the National College Attainment Network to promote children’s savings accounts among its members and within the college attainment community more generally. Specific activities include strategic communications, meetings, conferences and educational outreach. These efforts will help build the case and grow demand for children’s savings account strategies as part of comprehensive college access and success initiatives. Based in Washington, D.C., National College Attainment Network’s mission is to build, strengthen and empower communities committed to college access and success so that all students — especially those underrepresented in postsecondary education — can achieve their educational dreams.

title: Advancing Early Wealth Accounts Policy and Practice
description: In July 2025, Trump Accounts were signed into law, facilitating a national expansion of early savings accounts. Through its Early Wealth Building Initiative, the Aspen Institute’s Financial Security Program aims to ensure the new program and similar savings initiatives are well designed and benefit all children, especially those living in underserved communities. During the renewal grant period, the grantee will prioritize two main objectives: 1) develop and diversify a bipartisan and cross-sector group of leaders and stakeholders who support early wealth accounts; and 2) inform policy discussions with evidence-based, high-quality program design and implementation principles. Planned activities during the initial grant period include policy research and analysis, convening and coalition-building, and policymaker and public education. Founded in 1949, the Aspen Institute is a global, nonprofit organization dedicated to fostering a free, just and equitable society.

title: Building Bridges to Postsecondary Education
description: This grant to the National League of Cities Institute will expand educational savings efforts and strengthen municipal approaches that activate savers’ educational aspirations. During the grant period, the grantee will elevate awareness of: 1) Children’s Savings Accounts; 2) 529 accounts; and 3) emerging 530A accounts, including available seed funding. The grantee will work with cities and partners to identify program elements that sustain family engagement and advance postsecondary outcomes. The National League of Cities Institute will also continue supporting municipalities seeking to launch or strengthen Children’s Savings Accounts programs through guidance and local leadership development.

title: Advancing Early Accounts Policy and Practice
description: The Urban Institute is a nonprofit research organization and think tank based in Washington, D.C., established in 1968 to enhance lives and strengthen communities through research, data analysis and policy recommendations. For more than a decade, the Institute has shown leadership in early wealth-building strategies, including children’s savings accounts. With support from the Mott Foundation, the Institute will serve as a national intermediary in the early wealth field, linking policy, practice and research to maximize the long-term effectiveness of savings strategies for children. Planned activities during the grant period include: 1) convening a national learning community; 2) conducting research; and 3) publishing practical guidance to ensure insights from the learning community benefit the broader sector.

title: Arkansas Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support Arkansas State University, which coordinates the Arkansas Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) increase the number of afterschool programs available for young people in Arkansas; 2) increase the quality of afterschool programs through equipping afterschool and community leaders with the tools needed to design and implement high-quality programs; 3) expand parent and youth coalition building in the state to educate local and state leaders on the importance of afterschool access; and 4) increase access to quality afterschool programs through Mizzen Education, Inc.

title: California Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Foundation for California Community Colleges, which coordinates the California Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) leverage California’s large afterschool system to increase whole-child supports in the state; 2) establish the Network as a state and regional intermediary of child, family and workforce initiatives; 3) create systemic workforce solutions through pathways into, within and through afterschool; and 4) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen Education, Inc. resources.

title: Louisiana Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Children’s Coalition for Northeast Louisiana, which coordinates the Louisiana Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) deepen strategic partnership with partners to support the 21st Century Community Learning Centers program’s outreach, guidance and implementation support; 2) increase engagement with state and local policymakers to elevate childcare and afterschool as workforce infrastructure; 3) expand access to childcare and out-of-school time programs in parishes implementing four-day school weeks; and 4) improve program quality and sustainability by supporting and strengthening the out-of-school time workforce.

title: North Carolina Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: Public School Forum of North Carolina
description: This grant will support the Public School Forum of North Carolina, which coordinates the North Carolina Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) support regional collaboratives focused on expanding access to afterschool programs in the state; 2) build data collection and dissemination systems to communicate the unmet demand for and impacts of afterschool programming in the state; 3) strengthen the afterschool workforce through regional professional development networks; and 4) increase access to quality afterschool programs through Mizzen Education, Inc.

title: New Hampshire Statewide Afterschool Network
grantee: Southeastern Regional Education Service Center, Inc.
description: This grant will support the Southeastern Regional Education Service Center, Inc., which coordinates the New Hampshire Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) position afterschool as a critical support within the cradle to career continuum of care for New Hampshire’s children and youth; 2) establish statewide and regional professional development offerings for afterschool workers; 3) develop tools to inform programs and policymakers of the afterschool landscape in the state; and 4) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen Education, Inc. resources.

title: Ohio Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the Ohio Children’s Alliance, which coordinates the Ohio Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. This grant provides support to improve quality practices, and develop strategies to reach more students and families in alignment with the long-term vision for the state. This grant will include the accomplishment of the following outcomes and activities: 1) work with partners and allies to establish a dedicated funding stream in Ohio to support out-of-school time programs; 2) build and leverage strategic partnerships to advance high-quality out-of-school time programming statewide; and 3) increase afterschool programs that assist youth in workforce preparation, including STEM, entrepreneurship education, critical workplace soft skills, and partnerships with employers that support career exploration and pathways.

title: Tennessee Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the United Ways of Tennessee, which coordinates the Tennessee Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) design and work with partners to implement a statewide policy roadmap to increase access to afterschool programs for youth in Tennessee; 2) educate policymakers through hosting events and releasing coordinated communication materials demonstrating the positive impact of afterschool programs; 3) identify youth and family program needs and afterschool program deserts through implementing regional community surveys; hosting webinars and convening programs; and 4) strengthen the network through further diversifying its membership and partnerships.

title: Missouri Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the University of Missouri, Columbia, which coordinates the Missouri Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) work with education stakeholders to increase access to afterschool through state initiatives; 2) lead statewide coordination of professional development and education pathways for afterschool staff; 3) develop resources for local programs to communicate the impact of afterschool within their communities; and 4) support the promotion and distribution of Mizzen Education, Inc. resources.

title: Nevada Statewide Afterschool Network
description: This grant will support the University of Nevada, Las Vegas, which coordinates the Nevada Statewide Afterschool Network to expand access to high-quality afterschool programs for young people. Specific initiatives will include: 1) increasing access to high-quality afterschool programs through state afterschool policy and quality initiatives; 2) providing professional development and technical support to program leaders and staff; 3) collaborating with cross-sector partners to align field priorities to support positive outcomes for youth; and 4) supporting the promotion and distribution of Mizzen Education, Inc. resources.

title: Afterschool Education and Outreach Project
description: This grant will enable the Bipartisan Policy Center to support the 50 Statewide Afterschool Network and the afterschool field in the areas of policy analysis, communications and research. To advance afterschool programs, this project will: 1) build bridges between the afterschool field and local, state and federal government initiatives; and 2) assist the networks as they navigate programmatic changes in the education and afterschool field.

title: Afterschool Leadership & Development Collaborative
description: Foundations, Inc., will lead the Accelerator for Afterschool Investment — an initiative of the 50 State Afterschool Network — to increase access to high-quality afterschool programs through state-level funding. The grantee has supported the development of educators for the past 30 years by meeting the unique needs of educators and education entities through support services, professional development and educational resources. Specific outcomes of the initiative include: 1) increasing afterschool network leadership’s policymaking acumen; 2) strengthening systems of support for afterschool network leaders; and 3) deepening engagement of afterschool program staff within high-priority states.

title: Institute for the Study of Development and Resilience in Youth
description: This grant proposes to support a new youth engagement research and practice initiative focused on positive adolescent youth development in afterschool programs.
