Specifically, this project will assist in establishing the Institute for the Study of Development and Resilience in Youth to: 1) analyze national research on adolescent learning and development; 2) work with the afterschool ecosystem to translate research into practice to inform policy development and youth engagement; and 3) convene experts and stakeholders to summarize research findings regarding adolescent youth and afterschool participation.

title: Philanthropy and Social Innovation Project
description: With this grant, the Aspen Institute will lead its Program on Philanthropy and Social Innovation. The program goal is to support, inform and maximize the impact of philanthropists, social investors and those they support. Established in 1949, the Aspen Institute is a leading U.S. think tank with an international network of partners that fosters values-based leadership and provides a neutral and balanced venue for discussing and acting on critical issues.

title: Acquisition of the Weinstein Building
grantee: Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation
description: With this grant, the Foundation for the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, through its supported organization, the Uptown Reinvestment Corporation, will acquire the former Weinstein Electric building at 213 West First Avenue in Flint. Purchasing and maintaining the building will prevent blight, contribute to neighborhood stabilization and position the property for potential future use opportunities.

title: Summer Youth Initiative and TeenQuest
description: This grant provides funding to support the Genesee Area Focus Fund to implement TeenQuest and the Summer Youth Initiative, which provide job training and employment opportunities for Genesee County teens in partnership with area employers. Teens participate first in TeenQuest — a preemployment training program — and are then eligible to apply for employment through the Summer Youth Initiative.

title: Mott Foundation Youth Choice Awards
description: This grant will provide funding for Flint area youth-driven projects aimed at creating positive change through community service. In honor of the Mott Foundation’s centennial anniversary, this grant will give kindergarten through 12th-grade students who attend schools within the city limits of Flint, schools included in the Flint Center for Educational Excellence Network, and nonprofits located in Flint the opportunity to elevate their voices through service projects and by selecting additional Centennial Youth Choice Award winners.

title: Affordable Housing Project Support
description: This grant will enable United Way of Genesee County to take advantage of a $10 million state allocation aimed at expanding affordable housing options in Flint for underserved residents. The funding will be used to engage a specialized consultant who will guide the housing project from the pre-development phase through to completion. Additionally, this grant will support cash flow needs and cover loan interest expenses while United Way of Genesee County awaits reimbursement from the approved state funds.

title: FCS Playground Renovations
description: This grant enables Flint Community Schools to modernize five elementary playgrounds, using the Brownell STEM Academy Model as a blueprint. The project ensures all elementary students have safe, inclusive, and developmentally appropriate spaces that foster physical activity and social-emotional growth. In partnership with the Flint Center for Educational Excellence, the district will use a community co-design process — engaging staff, families and neighborhood leaders — to create playgrounds that serve students and the broader community alike. This parks and playgrounds initiative is part of a Mott Foundation centennial strategy to celebrate and elevate the bright spots that make Flint a great place to live, work and play.

title: Climate Finance for Sustainability in South Africa
description: The Institute for Economic Justice is a South African think tank working to advance economic policy that upholds human rights, community participation and environmental sustainability. With Mott Foundation support, the grantee successfully served as an Official Resource Partner to South Africa’s government during the country’s presidency of the G20. Under this new project, the Institute for Economic Justice will combine rigorous policy research with coalition building and strategic advocacy to help ensure both adequate levels of energy transition financing in South Africa as well as an investment plan that is aligned with the country’s development objectives while centering human rights, environmental protection and community priorities.

title: Lake Michigan Water Program
description: The Illinois Environmental Council Education Fund has over 150 affiliate members working to protect water resources in the state, including the Lake Michigan basin. As part of its Clean Water Program, the grantee builds coalitions and educates the public and decision-makers about pressing water issues. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee raised awareness and made progress on several issues facing the state and region, including lead service line replacement, plastic pollution and invasive species. With renewed support, the Illinois Environmental Council Education Fund will further the goals of its Clean Water Program with a focus on safe and affordable drinking water.

title: Wisconsin Water Agenda
description: River Alliance of Wisconsin supports a strong network of local organizations around the state that address threats to Wisconsin’s waters, such as mining, water pollution and water overuse. The grantee builds the capacity of local groups to protect water and engages communities to take action for clean water. With support from the Mott Foundation, River Alliance of Wisconsin will continue to support local watershed groups to address urgent water issues in the state and the Great Lakes region.

title: Great Lakes Islands Alliance
description: The Great Lakes Islands Alliance (the Alliance) — a project of the Stewardship Network — is a binational, voluntary collaborative network comprising over 300 island leaders from 20 islands in the Great Lakes region. The Alliance implements island-appropriate solutions to an array of environmental challenges, from rising lake levels to invasive species to water pollution. With previous support from the Mott Foundation, the grantee expanded its membership and communications and hosted an Island Summit. With renewed support, the Stewardship Network will be able to strengthen the connections and communications between islands and islanders while advancing stewardship of island natural resources.

title: General Purposes
description: The Environmental Grantmakers Association is a leading membership association for environmental philanthropy, uniting and coordinating efforts for more than 200 foundations and giving programs across North America and beyond. With previous support, the grantee has completed signature convenings, peer learning and field-wide research for its members. The grantee has also helped its members sharpen their grantmaking strategies, stay current on emerging environmental threats and opportunities, and coordinate action across the philanthropic sector. With continued support, the grantee will sustain its core member coordination and programming support services. The Environmental Grantmakers Association will also continue to convene its annual fall retreats, undertake research on public policy and environmental philanthropic giving trends, and catalyze philanthropic leadership development through a dedicated fellowship program.

title: Support for U.N. Special Rapporteur on the Independence of Judges and Lawyers
description: This grant will support the work of the United Nations (U.N.) Special Rapporteur on the Independence of Judges and Lawyers. As an independent U.N. expert, the Rapporteur, based at the Bernstein Institute for Human Rights at New York University, connects civil society, justice users and political actors to address justice issues. The four main focus areas continue to be: 1) reimagining access to justice through legal empowerment and support for community justice workers; 2) protecting legal actors under threat; 3) strengthening judicial independence to combat corruption; and 4) defending democracy. In 2023-26, the Rapporteur produced six official reports for the U.N. General Assembly and the Human Rights Council. The Rapporteur visited six countries for formal justice assessments and made over 400 submissions to national governments addressing a wide range of challenges to the rule of law. These included over 100 rapid-response letters and appeals addressing threats to justice actors.

title: Endowment
description: As the Crim Fitness Foundation approaches its 50th anniversary in 2027, it is building an endowment to improve operational efficiency and strengthen long-term financial sustainability. The organization plays an important role in the greater Flint area and beyond with its signature Crim Festival of Races events, as well as other programs that promote physical, mental and social well-being.

title: Mott Foundation Youth Choice Awards
description: This grant will provide funding for Flint area youth-driven projects aimed at creating positive change through community service. In honor of the Mott Foundation’s centennial anniversary, this grant will give kindergarten through 12th-grade students who attend schools within the city limits of Flint, schools included in the Flint Center for Educational Excellence Network, and nonprofits located in Flint the opportunity to elevate their voices through service projects and by selecting additional Centennial Youth Choice Award winners.

title: Mott Foundation Youth Choice Awards
description: This grant will provide funding for Flint area youth-driven projects aimed at creating positive change through community service. In honor of the Mott Foundation’s centennial anniversary, this grant will give kindergarten through 12th-grade students who attend schools within the city limits of Flint, schools included in the Flint Center for Educational Excellence Network, and nonprofits located in Flint the opportunity to elevate their voices through service projects and by selecting additional Centennial Youth Choice Award winners.

title: Mott Foundation Youth Choice Awards
description: This grant will provide funding for Flint area youth-driven projects aimed at creating positive change through community service. In honor of the Mott Foundation’s centennial anniversary, this grant will give kindergarten through 12th-grade students who attend schools within the city limits of Flint, schools included in the Flint Center for Educational Excellence Network, and nonprofits located in Flint the opportunity to elevate their voices through service projects and by selecting additional Centennial Youth Choice Award winners.

title: Mott Foundation Youth Choice Awards
description: This grant will provide funding for Flint area youth-driven projects aimed at creating positive change through community service. In honor of the Mott Foundation’s centennial anniversary, this grant will give kindergarten through 12th-grade students who attend schools within the city limits of Flint, schools included in the Flint Center for Educational Excellence Network, and nonprofits located in Flint the opportunity to elevate their voices through service projects and by selecting additional Centennial Youth Choice Award winners.

title: South Africa Justice Donors Project
description: The project goal is to increase funding for justice projects in South Africa. To this end, the Social Justice Initiative will coordinate and organize interested philanthropic and development funders in South Africa. Key activities include convening funders, engaging donors, undertaking research and sharing information. The Social Justice Initiative is a South African philanthropic intermediary organization that mobilizes and deploys resources to strengthen civil society organizations working to address injustice and inequality.

title: Clean Water Group
description: Communities, farms and ecosystems across the United States face increasing water-related threats stemming from pollution, extreme weather, unsustainable development, increased demand, aging infrastructure and resource mismanagement. A coordinated effort is needed to reverse these trends and ensure that all Americans benefit from clean, safe, affordable and reliable water that supports healthy rivers, habitats, productive lands and resilient communities. To build the necessary level of collaboration and cooperation, American Rivers, a major environmental organization, is working with a group of clean water leaders to develop a comprehensive blueprint aimed at catalyzing a national water movement.

title: Flint Youth Entrepreneurship Summit & Fellows Program
description: Since 2021, the Hopewell Fund and its partner organizations, the Next Gen Chamber of Commerce and Next Gen HQ, have worked to encourage and empower Genesee County youth with its youth entrepreneurship programs. The programs feature a youth entrepreneurship summit and a fellowship program. During this grant period, the grantee will serve as the fiscal sponsor for the Next Gen Chamber of Commerce to focus on deepening Flint’s role as an exemplary youth entrepreneurship ecosystem by expanding access, participation and outcomes within a single community. The Hopewell Fund will deliver the annual summit and year-long fellowship program in Genesee County, engaging 200 students at the summit, activating 150 mentors, judges, advisors and partners, and supporting a 15-student fellowship cohort through sustained, accelerator-style programming.

title: Genesee Youth Entrepreneurship Network
description: The Genesee Intermediate School District provides educational leadership that impacts instruction, learning, student achievement, productivity and efficiency across the county. This grant will enable the grantee to continue cultivating an innovative mindset and instill a lasting appreciation of entrepreneurship among Genesee County teens in grades 9-12. During this grant period, the grantee will focus on: 1) reaching more underrepresented youth through targeted program expansion and in-school learning opportunities; and 2) strengthening strategic community partnerships that deepen mentoring, career exposure and long-term ecosystem sustainability. These efforts will ensure that youth entrepreneurship in Genesee County continues to grow equitably, inclusively, and in alignment with workforce and economic development goals.

title: Zillion Solutions Program Expansion
description: This grant will support the continuation and expansion of the Zillion Solutions program at the University of Michigan-Flint. Launched in 2017 by the Hagerman Center for Entrepreneurship and Innovation, Zillion Solutions is an annual competition created to increase student interest in entrepreneurship, innovation and/or problem solving. The program is designed to generate participation across all academic units on campus, as well as dual-enrolled and Genesee County high school students. The goal of the program is to help build a culture of entrepreneurship and innovation throughout the university and beyond.

title: Teen C.E.O. Initiative
description: This renewal grant will provide support to Mott Community College for the Teens Creating Economic Opportunity, or “Teen C.E.O.” initiative. The goal of the project is to provide underrepresented youth with an opportunity to build entrepreneurial business skills, explore higher education and investigate career pathways through a summer learning experience. The program will engage youth through: 1) technical training and skill building with digital and fabrication technologies; 2) connecting youth with local leaders and mentors; and 3) facilitating live business pitch competitions and community showcases to celebrate youth accomplishments.

title: Flint Entrepreneurial Ecosystem Youth Mentorship Program
description: This grant will support SIPI, Inc. to lead in the coordination and alignment of Flint’s entrepreneurial ecosystem. With seven years of leadership in the Flint entrepreneurial network, the grantee is a trusted partner locally. Now supported through the Youth Engagement program area, the grantee will prioritize youth entrepreneurship strategies as key components of the project. Goals of this grant project include: 1) integrate youth engagement within the broader network; 2) elevate mentorship as a shared infrastructure opportunity; 3) strengthen partner coordination and engagement, with a focus on youth serving organizations; 4) improve communications and shared learning opportunities across the community; and 5) reduce barriers for early-stage and under-resourced entrepreneurs to more easily navigate business development pathways.

title: Entrepreneurship Network
description: This grant will support Mott Community College’s Entrepreneurship Network in creating a coordinated support and referral system that helps students pursue entrepreneurial ambitions by leveraging partnerships with organizations such as Factory Two, 100K Ideas, the FABLAB, VetBiz and Kettering University’s Small Business Center. Through workshops, networking events, mentorship and coaching, the project will: 1) connect students to entrepreneurial resources and ecosystem partners; 2) provide skill-building and networking opportunities that foster entrepreneurial development; and 3) offer individualized guidance from business mentors and community leaders to help students refine and advance their business ideas.

title: Youth Entrepreneurship Ecosystem Capacity Project
description: This grant will support the Ferris Wheel Innovation Center, known as 100K Ideas, to strengthen entrepreneurial thinking among youth as emerging professionals through hands-on programs and ecosystem collaboration. The grantee, established in 2017, aims to help entrepreneurs grow in under-resourced communities. During this grant period, the goals are to: 1) engage youth in entrepreneurial skill building; 2) prepare youth as emerging professionals for the workforce; 3) strengthen the local entrepreneurial ecosystem; and 4) expand entrepreneurial education across Flint and Genesee County. Together, these efforts will prepare the next generation to succeed in a world where innovation and an entrepreneurial mindset are essential.

title: East Africa Community Foundation Initiative
description: The project goal is to foster learning, networking and joint action among community foundations and community foundation support organizations in East Africa. To achieve this, the East Africa Philanthropy Network will support learning circles, exchanges and convenings for community foundations in East Africa. In addition, the grantee will conduct research on community foundation practices and publish quarterly updates to promote the community foundation concept in the region. This grant increase will enable the grantee to support the first ever convening of community foundations in Africa. Established in 2003, the East Africa Philanthropy Network brings together foundations, trusts and other philanthropic organizations to build a learning community and strengthen the philanthropy field and practice in the region.

title: Mott Foundation Centennial Community Video Project
description: This grant to the Flint Institute of Music will support the performance and video production of the positive social, economic and cultural aspects of the Flint community. title: General Purposes
description: The program goal is to support the field of community foundations in Mexico. Founded in 2011, Comunalia is an alliance of 17 Mexican community foundations focused on local development and strategic social investment. Beginning in 2025 and continuing through 2027, the grantee is pursuing the following objectives: 1) strengthening Mexican community foundations’ institutional capacities; 2) increasing its own resources and fostering new income streams for its members; 3) promoting the creation of new Mexican community foundations; 4) raising the profile of community foundations in Mexico; and 5) strengthening itself internally to increase its reach and impact. A challenge grant increase will provide an incentive for Comunalia to match funds from national Mexican resources, thereby reducing its dependence on international donors.

title: SCALE Project
description: The purpose of this grant is to expand a new fellowship program for supporting afterschool program leaders and staff. Specifically, this grant will build upon the Supporting Communities of Afterschool Leaders Empowered program to design a local-level model for cities and communities to deliver intensive training, individualized coaching, and applied learning to support continued sustainability and quality of afterschool programs for young people.

title: Sierra Leone Justice Needs and Satisfaction Survey Project
grantee: Hague Institute for Innovation of Law
description: The Hague Institute for Innovation of Law will conduct a nationally representative Justice Needs and Satisfaction Survey in Sierra Leone. The survey will seek to measure the prevalence and impact of civil, administrative and criminal justice problems, the formal and customary pathways people use, the costs and barriers they experience, and the outcomes they achieve. The institute will work with the Ministry of Justice, national partners and a stakeholder reference group to adapt the questionnaire to Sierra Leone’s legal and cultural context. Results of the survey will be analyzed alongside the existing Justice Financing Framework to identify service gaps, expenditure priorities, cost-effectiveness opportunities and a baseline for future reform. Established in 2005, the Hague Institute for Innovation of Law seeks to find innovative solutions to justice problems around the world.

title: Flint Healthcare Employment Opportunities Program
description: This grant to the Greater Flint Health Coalition will support the Flint Healthcare Employment Opportunities program. The goal of this program is to create sustainable employment opportunities and promote career advancement for area residents within the healthcare sector. Participants receive industry-focused life skills and career readiness training, occupational instruction, case management and supportive services, as well as job development assistance.

title: Support for Differently Abled Adult Workers
description: Peckham, Inc., a nonprofit rehabilitation organization, facilitates Manufacturing EDGE, a community-based career exploration and readiness initiative designed to connect Flint area adults with disabilities ages 18 and older to opportunities in advanced manufacturing. The program will help residents who may be interested in manufacturing careers, but are unsure how to enter the industry, build foundational knowledge, workplace readiness skills and connections to local employers. Grant funding will directly support accessible workshops, digital learning resources, employer engagement activities and supportive services that reduce barriers to participation.

title: Employment Preparation Program
description: This grant will provide support to the St. Luke N.E.W. Life Center for its Employment Preparation Program. Serving the residents of north Flint, the Program works with individuals who are structurally unemployed and are in need of a broad array of wraparound services to prepare them for obtaining and retaining employment. The grantee will continue to expand its outreach to employers for future job placements and will offer an alumni network to support participants and past graduates.

title: General Purposes
description: The Chill Foundation expands access to boardsports and outdoor experiences for young people who might not otherwise have these opportunities. The grantee’s programs combine experiential learning with mentoring, coaching and a values-based curriculum. During this grant period, funding would support the continuation of Chill’s core programs for youth ages 11–19 and the expansion of Chill Evolution to serve alumni ages 18–26. Continued support would enable Chill to sustain high-quality core programming nationwide while advancing priority strategic goals, including alumni engagement through Chill Evolution. Programming will focus on mentorship, job-readiness support, and ongoing connection to boardsports and the outdoor industry.

title: Adult Career Pathway Program
description: This grant will support the Adult Career Pathways program at Mott Community College. The program will leverage many of the college’s existing educational and training programs to help connect unemployed adults, low-income workers, and youth to employment and a career pathway. The goal is to ensure that area residents can enter and advance into higher-wage occupations in high-growth industries. Work experience and support services are integrated into the model, enabling participants to combine school and work and advance in their careers over time.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant increase supports the transition of the Nonprofit Employment Data Project — housed at George Mason University — as it becomes affiliated with Independent Sector. This new partnership comes at a critical time, as the sector continues to make progress in gaining better and more regular access to nonprofit employment data from the federal government. The Nonprofit Works tool, developed by the Nonprofit Employment Data Project team, provides ready access to hard data on the economic impact of the nonprofit sector, giving users the ability to determine: 1) how many people work for nonprofits in each state, city and county; 2) how average wages for nonprofits compare to those in other sectors; and 3) key trends in nonprofit employment or wages over time. Founded in 1980, Independent Sector currently has 453 organizational members and advances its mission by fostering a sense of belonging, catalyzing action and providing policy leadership across the full breadth of the charitable sector.

title: Higher Education Awareness Campaign
description: With this grant, Diploma Equity Project will provide leadership for the Level Up Michigan initiative, launching a statewide campaign aimed at boosting awareness about the no-cost opportunities that are available for Michigan residents seeking post-secondary degrees and certificates. Ultimately, the initiative aims to “take cost off the table” when individuals consider post-secondary options and thereby increase the number of individuals who participate in higher education. This is important for both Michigan’s residents and for the future prosperity of the state.

title: Davin Pierson Torre Seeing Stars Legacy Fund
description: The Flint Institute of Music, located on the Flint Cultural Center campus, was established in 1917. Today, the grantee reaches more than 250,000 people each year through lessons, classes, outreach programs, performances and concerts. The grantee is home to the Flint School of Performing Arts, Michigan’s largest community arts school and the 8th-largest in the U.S. The grantee offers comprehensive music, dance and theater instruction to over 3,500 students of all ages and skill levels. This grant will provide seed funding for the Davin Pierson Torre Legacy Fund, which will finance the Flint School of Performing Arts’ Seeing Stars Fund, a tuition assistance program that supports economically challenged students in engaging in high-quality arts instruction.

title: Harold Alfond College Challenge Program Evaluation
description: Mott Foundation support will enable the Alfond Scholarship Foundation to continue the Harold Alfond College Challenge Program, the nation’s first statewide children’s savings account program. In addition to implementation, evaluation is a primary focus for the renewal grant period. To advance broader field-building goals, the grantee will continue to share best practices, lessons and ongoing evaluation findings. Established in 2008 as a pilot in Portland, Maine, the program automatically awards a $500 grant to every child born in the state to encourage additional education savings and foster higher education aspirations.

title: Athletics Expansion
description: University of Michigan-Flint is an important anchor institution for downtown Flint and the city more broadly. The university is committed to ensuring that it is an attractive choice for students seeking higher education across the region, while also being a strong contributor to the local community. As its next stage of growth, the university will develop and launch an intercollegiate athletics program on its campus. This will be achieved through renovating its current athletics facility; investing in equipment, technology, marketing and other startup costs; and hiring an athletic director and other staff. An intercollegiate athletics program is expected to be attractive to current and prospective students, lead to a more vibrant campus experience, and foster greater community engagement and affinity with the university.

title: Operating Support

title: MSU Flint Dairy Store
description: With this grant, Michigan State University will bring its Dairy Store to Flint. This will provide opportunities for access to fresh foods, job training and entrepreneurship assistance, as well as community building for residents and visitors in Flint and beyond.

title: Artist in Residency Programming

description: With this grant, the Flint Cultural Center Academy will offer upper school coursework for students who have completed its elementary and middle school programs. Operating out of the University of Michigan-Flint’s Northbank Center, the aim is to provide the enriching educational opportunities that students have experienced in the school’s K-8 program. This grant will assist with the purchase of curriculum, school facility rental fees, security services, elective classes, athletic staff and equipment, and a school bus.

title: Genesee County Trails: Grand Traverse Greenway Trail
description: With this grant, the Genesee County Parks & Recreation Commission will lead the construction of the north phase of the Grand Traverse Greenway Trail. The trail segment will begin at Kearsley Street in Flint’s state park and extend south to I-69. This is an important connector, beginning to directly link people to the state park via nonmotorized trails. This project supports public access to outdoor recreation, promoting health, connectivity, and environmental stewardship for residents of Flint and the surrounding community.

title: DDA Trees
description: The purpose of this grant is to fund the replacement of trees in downtown Flint, primarily along Saginaw Street. The trees will add to the beautification of downtown infrastructure by providing a natural landscape while also contributing to improved environmental quality and community health. Vibrant downtowns require continuous enhancements, such as trees, to be inviting to residents and visitors.

title: Seeds of Connection
description: The project goal is to improve equity, accountability and inclusion for Native American communities with community foundations, thus helping community foundations build common ground between Native and non-Native communities. Through its Seeds of Connection initiative launched in early 2025, Native Americans in Philanthropy: 1) conducted four gatherings in the Southwest and Western regions of the United States involving a total of 65 participants; 2) established a Community of Practice; and 3) awarded $300,000 in challenge grants to four community foundations with matching requirements to provide funding to Native communities. Over the next two years the grantee will take the Seeds of Connection initiative to other regions, such as the Northwest and Midwest, continue providing challenge grants to community foundations to drive more funding to Native communities and expand its Community of Practice. Founded in 1990, Native Americans in Philanthropy promotes equitable and effective philanthropy in Native communities.

title: Great Lakes Water Resources Project
geographic_focus: Illinois, Minnesota, Ohio, Michigan, Pennsylvania, Wisconsin, New York, Indiana
description: The Great Lakes Environmental Law Center, a Michigan-based nonprofit environmental law organization, provides legal and technical support to citizen leaders and community organizations working on water resource management issues. This grant increase will enable the organization to continue offering financial assistance to local partners in their ongoing pursuit of legal protections to conserve and safeguard water resources from pollution.

title: Community Safety Prevention and Intervention Programs
description: This grant to the Community Foundation of Greater Flint will support programming for the Community Safety Collaborative and participating partners. Through these funds, residents will receive conflict mediation training. Programming will also include support for a youth diversion program, public awareness about community violence and additional youth outreach programming.

title: Flint State Park
description: With this grant, the Genesee County Parks & Recreation Commission will expand the scope of completed construction at the new state park. Funding will ensure the completion of the park’s full trail network and support construction of the Chevy Commons Play Garden. This project will enhance public access to outdoor recreation opportunities while promoting improved health and wellness outcomes for Flint residents and the surrounding community.

title: Strengthening Territorial Governance in the Brazilian Amazon
initiative: Land, Water and People of the Amazon Basin
description: Repórter Brasil is a Brazilian nonprofit that uses investigative journalism and data analysis to help ensure that environmental laws and land rights are upheld. Weak land governance in the Amazon, including illegal land claims and overlapping land records, threatens forests and the rights of Indigenous peoples and Traditional Communities. Over the grant period, the grantee will enhance its database of rural property registrations to track land tenure and compliance with environmental protection rules. Repórter Brasil and partner groups will use the data to make the case for improved land governance and territorial protection.

title: Spread the Warmth
description: This grant will provide support to the Empowerment Plan to manufacture and distribute 500 coats to unhoused individuals in Flint. In 2024, nearly 4,000 individuals experienced homelessness on a single night in Flint and Genesee County. Hypothermia is a leading cause of preventable injury and death among unhoused individuals. Coats are vital in reducing these risks and connecting this population to a potential workforce opportunity in the development of the physical coat-making.

title: STEM Next Opportunity Fellowship
description: This grant will support STEM Next Opportunity Fund’s fellowship program, a public-private partnership initiative expanding access to high-quality afterschool, summer and informal STEM learning for youth. For more than a decade, the STEM Next Opportunity Fellows have been key champions of expanded learning opportunities at the federal and state levels. With a new focus on increasing state-level decision-making and resources, this project will: 1) strengthen state strategies to grow afterschool and informal STEM learning; 2) support allocations of state resources from the 21st Century Community Learning Centers program; and 3) collaborate with leading researchers to identify priorities, strategies and programs that improve afterschool.

title: U.S. Nature Initiative Water Pillar
description: Americans consistently and overwhelmingly support the goal of clean and abundant water for people and nature. Over the past decade, however, federal water protections have been weakened through a combination of congressional action, administrative rollbacks and court decisions. One response is to create new approaches to managing water resources at the state level. The U.S. Nature Initiative — a fiscally sponsored project of the California-based Resources Legacy Fund — provides the technical assistance and resources needed to achieve long-lasting conservation outcomes in the states. With partial support from the Mott Foundation, the initiative will work to secure public support for innovative water management practices addressing water quality, water supply, climate resilience and water infrastructure.

title: General Purposes
initiative: Land, Water and People of the Amazon Basin
description: Kara Solar Foundation is advancing a proven model of solar-powered river transportation that strengthens Indigenous communities, protects ecosystems and builds capacity in remote Amazonian territories. This increase will be available for the general purpose of the grantee, including expanding the staff team, improving the solar boat technology and providing community training programs in Ecuador. It will also enable Kara Solar Foundation to convene a regional learning exchange and provide training to partner organizations in Brazil and Peru.

title: Renewable Energy for Extractive Reserves in the Amazon
initiative: Land, Water and People of the Amazon Basin
description: This project supports the World Wildlife Fund in expanding clean energy access for communities in the Brazilian Amazon through coordinating civil society organizations and working with government agencies on off-grid solar energy. With this grant increase, the grantee will promote the use of electric-powered boats using solar energy. This will support sustainable livelihoods and reduce dependence on fossil fuels. Activities include: 1) mapping existing initiatives; 2) assessing financing opportunities; and 3) bringing together government, technical, private-sector and civil society partners to identify priorities and coordinate action. The project will also develop practical recommendations for communities to adopt electric mobility.

title: Centennial Family Fun Days
description: Since its founding, the Flint community has been at the heart of the Foundation’s grantmaking. In 2026, the Mott Foundation is choosing to commemorate its centennial anniversary in a variety of ways, including a Family Fund Day celebration. The event consisted of free, family-friendly activities on June 5-7, 2026, across the Flint Cultural Center campus. Exhibits and activities at institutions, such as the Sloan Museum of Discovery and Flint Institute of Arts, were open and free to anyone who attended the event. Additionally, an outdoor stage featured local performances, the Gloria Coles Flint Public Library offered free books as part of the Summer Reading Challenge Kickoff and the Flint Cultural Center Academy hosted a free, 3-on-3 basketball tournament.

title: General Purposes
description: Since 1980, the Michigan Environmental Council, a statewide nonprofit, has been promoting the sustainable management of air, water and land resources in Michigan. This work is largely accomplished through its network of more than 100 member organizations. This grant increase will support the Council’s general purposes, including recognizing and honoring environmental leaders in the state, updating the organization’s strategic plan and continuing efforts to protect and restore water resources across Michigan.

title: Flint Home Improvement Fund
description: This grant will provide funds enabling Genesee County Habitat for Humanity to continue its vital Flint Home Improvement Fund program. This multifaceted program enables residents of the city of Flint who either cannot afford or do not qualify for other home improvement lending programs to address critical home repair needs. Needs addressed by the program include: 1) façade improvements; 2) structural repairs; 3) abatement services; 4) accessibility modifications; and 5) any other health, safety or code-related issues. Programs like the Flint Home Improvement Fund help to strengthen neighborhoods and improve the quality of life for Flint families.

title: Reforming Finance to Advance an Equitable Energy Transition
description: Urgewald is a German organization that conducts research, public education and advocacy on the environmental and human rights risks of energy and infrastructure projects, by engaging commercial banks, private investors and multilateral development banks to shift capital away from fossil fuels towards sustainable alternatives. With this grant increase, Urgewald will organize a series of meetings to accelerate civil society efforts to respond to recent challenges to multilateral development banks’ accountability systems and develop longer-term strategies.

title: Finance for Community-Owned Power Generation
description: Community-owned clean energy assets could generate sustainable income by selling surplus electricity to the grid, but securing development finance for this kind of infrastructure remains extremely difficult. Founded in 1982 and now operating in more than a dozen focus countries, the World Resources Institute is an international organization that works to improve people’s lives, protect nature and stabilize the climate by using research to catalyze change. With this grant, the grantee will identify practical pathways to unlock development finance for community-owned clean energy in South America with particular attention to whether communities can generate revenue by selling surplus electricity into the grid.

title: Neighborhood Murals
description: This grant will provide funds for the Flint Public Art Project to design and create murals in Flint neighborhoods. The murals provide a way to engage the Flint community in art, beautify neighborhoods and support economic development. The grantee will continue to feature the works of local and national talent over the next year and offer programming that engages neighborhoods and youth in the mural creation process.

title: Rx Kids Cash Allowance Pilot
description: Michigan State University will partner with University of Michigan and GiveDirectly to implement and research the impact of an innovative prenatal and infant cash allowance initiative that seeks to advance health equity by proactively addressing maternal and infant economic instability. Rx Kids leans on the science of early childhood and the lifelong consequences of exposure to early adversity. The pilot program aims to fill a scientific gap in health disparities research with a community-level disruption of poverty before and during early childhood, when it is most prevalent and most toxic. Through Rx Kids, expectant mothers in Flint will receive a one-time prenatal cash transfer of $1,500, and all infants will receive monthly allowances of $500 per month in their first year of life. The initiative will impact approximately 1,200 Flint mothers and their newborns per year.

title: General Purposes
grantee: Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint
description: This grant provides general purpose support to the Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint. The grantee focuses on education, creativity, physical activity, health and family support services, while offering year-round programming for young people ages seven to 17 in the Flint area. With two locations in total, the grantee serves both the east and south side of the city. Programs such as this have been instrumental in mitigating the negative effects of challenges such as the water crisis, learning loss resulting from the COVID-19 pandemic and the impact of poverty. By providing students with highly engaging educational and enrichment opportunities in a safe and supportive environment, the Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint continues to stay true to its mission to enable young people in the Flint area to reach their full potential.

title: Youth Entrepreneurship Model Program Pilot
grantee: Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint
description: This grant will support the Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint in expanding youth entrepreneurship and leadership opportunities for young people ages seven–17 through a comprehensive developmental pathway that introduces entrepreneurial thinking early and builds increasingly advanced, hands-on experiences over time. The initiative will: 1) provide entrepreneurship education and financial literacy programming that equips youth with foundational business and money management skills; 2) expose participants to career exploration, mentorship, and connections with local entrepreneurs to broaden awareness of entrepreneurial and career pathways; 3) create real-world entrepreneurial experiences through a Youth Entrepreneurship & Career Fair, BGC Marketplace and Youth Business Concept Competition where youth can develop, market and pitch their ideas; 4) establish a youth-led media and podcast program that strengthens communication, storytelling and leadership skills while amplifying youth voice; and 5) foster confidence, agency and leadership by helping young people see themselves as future business owners, innovators and community leaders. Through these interconnected experiences, Boys & Girls Clubs of Greater Flint will create meaningful opportunities for youth to develop entrepreneurial mindsets, workplace-ready skills and leadership capabilities while strengthening Flint’s broader youth entrepreneurship ecosystem.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general operating support to NFTE to expand access to high-quality entrepreneurship education while strengthening the infrastructure needed to grow and sustain the youth entrepreneurship field. The grant will support NFTE’s efforts to: (1) expand the reach and impact of its Aspiring Entrepreneurs Program, providing more middle and high school students with entrepreneurship education and career-connected learning opportunities; (2) successfully integrate NFTE and BUILD, creating a family-of-brands model that preserves the unique strengths of each organization while leveraging shared infrastructure, technology, partnerships, and organizational capabilities; and (3) strengthen field-building efforts through investments in research, cross-sector collaboration, and AI-enabled curriculum and tools that prepare young people to thrive in an increasingly AI-driven economy. Through this work, NFTE will enhance program quality, expand pathways for young people, and help build a more connected and sustainable youth entrepreneurship ecosystem.

title: Youth Entrepreneurship Regional Pitch Competition Scaling
description: This grant will support the Young Entrepreneur Institute (YEI) at the University School in advancing the Mott Foundation’s Youth Leadership Initiative by expanding access to high-quality entrepreneurship education, leadership development and educator capacity-building in Flint and other target communities. Drawing on its 20-year track record of supporting K-12 educators and young people, YEI will: (1) provide educator training and professional development to strengthen the ability of teachers and youth-serving professionals to deliver effective entrepreneurship education; (2) build local and regional capacity to support sustainable youth entrepreneurship ecosystems, particularly in Flint and other priority communities; (3) leverage its experience cultivating entrepreneurship ecosystems in Northeast Ohio and Northwest Arkansas to inform community-based strategies and partnerships; (4) expand youth engagement and leadership opportunities through entrepreneurship learning experiences, pitch challenges and innovation-focused activities; and (5) contribute to national field-building efforts by applying its expertise in K-12 entrepreneurship competitions and youth entrepreneurship programming. Through these efforts, YEI will help create stronger pathways for young people to develop entrepreneurial mindsets, leadership skills and real-world experiences while equipping educators and communities with the tools needed to sustain and scale youth entrepreneurship opportunities.

title: Youth Entrepreneurship Ecosystem Funders Initiative
description: This grant to Community Initiatives will help support the Entrepreneurship Funders Network (EFN) in strengthening the youth entrepreneurship field through funder collaboration, ecosystem learning and shared storytelling that advance the Mott Foundation’s Youth Leadership strategy. Specifically, EFN will: 1) convene and facilitate the Youth Entrepreneurship Community of Practice, bringing together funding partners to build shared knowledge, aligned strategies and coordinated investments in youth entrepreneurship; 2) lead an Ecosystem-to-Impact Learning Initiative to better understand how investments in youth entrepreneurship pathways connect to and are influenced by broader entrepreneurial ecosystems; and 3) develop and test a Collective Narrative Campaign that elevates shared messages, lessons and stories across the field to increase visibility, understanding and support for youth entrepreneurship. Through these efforts, EFN will help strengthen field coordination, expand learning among funders and practitioners, identify effective ecosystem-building approaches, and position Flint as both a contributor to and beneficiary of national youth entrepreneurship and leadership field-building efforts.

title: General Purposes
description: This grant will provide general operating support to Lemonade Day to strengthen the organizational capacity needed to expand equitable access to youth entrepreneurship opportunities nationwide while deepening its engagement in Flint and Genesee County. The grant will support the grantee’s efforts to: 1) strengthen program quality and adult capacity through investments in organizational infrastructure and community partnerships; 2) expand access and opportunity pathways by reaching approximately 75,000 young people, including growing participation and strengthening the youth entrepreneurship ecosystem in Flint and Genesee County; and 3) strengthen policy and field infrastructure by building the local and national networks that sustain high-quality entrepreneurship experiences for youth. Through this work, Lemonade Day will continue providing hands-on entrepreneurial experiences that help young people develop financial literacy, leadership and business skills while strengthening community engagement and opportunity pathways.

title: Youth Leadership Grantee Learning Coordinator
description: This grant will support Red Lantern Consulting, LLC in serving as a strategic learning and field-building partner for the Foundation’s Youth Leadership initiative. Building on the grantee’s successful 2025 evaluation of the Youth Engagement portfolio, the organization will help the Foundation strengthen its efforts to position Flint as a model community while advancing youth entrepreneurship and leadership opportunities nationally. Specifically, the grantee will: 1) provide field-building strategy and advisory support to help identify emerging opportunities, challenges and trends in the youth entrepreneurship and leadership fields; 2) convene and facilitate Brain Trust meetings that bring together practitioners, experts and partners to inform strategy, strengthen relationships and surface promising practices; and 3) support ongoing learning, sense-making and decision-making by synthesizing insights from the field and helping staff translate knowledge into strategic action. Through these activities, Red Lantern Consulting, LLC will help the Foundation build the knowledge, partnerships and systems necessary to inform grantmaking, strengthen ecosystem development and advance long-term youth leadership and entrepreneurship outcomes.

title: Youth Entrepreneurship Model Building and Innovation
description: This grant will support Project Invent’s national youth entrepreneurship model, which uses a train-the-trainer approach to equip educators with the tools, curriculum, coaching, and support needed to engage young people in solving real-world community challenges through invention and entrepreneurship. Through this grant, the grantee will: 1) provide hands-on invention and entrepreneurship experiences that help students identify problems, design solutions, build prototypes and pitch their ideas; 2) train and support educators and facilitators to deliver high-quality, student-centered innovation learning experiences; 3) connect youth with community partners and industry mentors to ensure inventions address authentic needs and expose students to entrepreneurial and STEM career pathways; 4) strengthen students’ entrepreneurial mindsets, creativity, problem-solving and confidence through real-world application; and 5) deepen evidence of effective youth entrepreneurship practices and expand pathways for youth to advance their inventions and entrepreneurial potential, particularly for students with limited access to such opportunities.

title: Youth Entrepreneurship Policy Study and Report
description: This grant will support the Center for an Urban Future in researching, producing and disseminating a comprehensive policy report on youth entrepreneurship in New York City as a response to declining entry-level employment opportunities for young people. Through quantitative analysis, stakeholder interviews, focus groups and a review of promising programs nationwide, the grantee will: 1) document the need for greater investment in youth entrepreneurship and entrepreneurship education; 2) assess the current landscape of resources, supports and service gaps for young entrepreneurs in New York City; 3) identify and elevate effective youth entrepreneurship models that could be replicated and scaled; 4) develop policy research to expand entrepreneurship pathways and supports for young people; and 5) drive awareness of those research findings through report dissemination, stakeholder engagement, media outreach, advocacy efforts, and a public policy forum involving policymakers, practitioners, funders, educators, and youth entrepreneurs.

title: Water Infrastructure Needs Assessment for Michigan
description: The University of Michigan’s Water Center — part of the Graham Sustainability Institute — will develop a comprehensive water infrastructure needs assessment for Michigan. The Water Center addresses critical and emerging water resource challenges by fostering collaborative, user-driven research that informs policy and management decisions.

title: General Purposes
description: Philanthropy for Active Civic Engagement is a national network of 90 funders in the United States that aims to equip and mobilize the philanthropic community to strengthen American democracy by fostering vibrant civic participation. This grant will enable Philanthropy for Active Civic Engagement to: 1) increase member engagement; 2) build coalitions for actions; 3) strengthen the civic field; and 4) shape a unifying civic narrative. For more than 20 years, Philanthropy for Active Civic Engagement has created learning spaces, relationships and opportunities for collaboration among funders working to bolster democracy and civic life. Philanthropy for Active Civic Engagement brings this expertise to a moment when the challenges facing American civic culture are more urgent and interconnected than ever.

title: TAP Network
description: The goal of this project is to support organized civil society participation to increase peace, inclusion and access to justice globally. The Transparency, Accountability and Participation Network, a project of the Accountability Lab, Inc., will mobilize its membership of 250 civil society organizations for coordinated action around the implementation of Sustainable Development Goal 16, with its focus on peaceful, just and inclusive societies. In order to strengthen its future practice in this area, the grantee will use this increase to commission an independent evaluation of its success in achieving its goals both substantively and organizationally.

title: Thrive Youth Sports Program
description: This grant will fund the Flint Center for Educational Excellence to implement Thrive Sports, a coordinated youth sports and youth-development pilot strategy embedded within Thrive Afterschool and Community Education programming. Funds will help build the staffing, coaching, transportation, event logistics and operational infrastructure needed to launch the model across eight Flint sites, expanding universal access to structured sports and physical activity for youth ages 5-12.

title: Resource Navigation
description: This grant to the Gloria Coles Flint Public Library will support the pilot of a resource navigation program. The Flint Digital Futures Initiative is a community-based model that connects Flint residents with individualized support, technology education, workforce pathways, and coordinated referrals to address barriers to employment and long-term stability. Building on the library’s trusted role as a hub for lifelong learning, digital access and community connection, the project will serve approximately 35–40 participants through personalized resource navigation plans and follow-up support. Resource navigation includes workforce development, credentialing, financial wellness, health care, housing, food security and other essential services. By embedding resource navigation at the Gloria Coles Flint Public Library, the project will help residents access pathways to stabilizing supports while strengthening the library’s role as a Flint community anchor.

title: Flint Community Needs Assessment
description: The city of Flint’s newly established Division of Health Strategies and Advancement is the city’s first executive-level department dedicated to public health. As one of its first initiatives, the division seeks to conduct Flint’s first comprehensive, resident-centered Community Health Needs Assessment across all six zip codes. The project will address gaps in local health data through a representative resident survey and community listening sessions that capture lived experiences, priorities and recommendations. Findings will identify health disparities, barriers to care and key social determinants of health, while creating a data-driven tool to guide future public health strategies, resource allocation, partnerships, and funding opportunities that improve the health and well-being of Flint residents.

title: Health and Equity Impacts of the Flint State Park
description: This grant will support researchers at Michigan State University in completing baseline biomarker data collection, and developing a publicly accessible Flint Parks and Greenspace Dashboard to evaluate and improve equitable access to these spaces in Flint. Building on two years of research, the project will integrate survey data, park audits, greenspace analyses, and health data into a community-facing resource that helps residents identify park amenities and opportunities for recreation.

title: Healthy Behavior Support for Teens
description: This grant will enable HealthCorps to support youth wellness through its near-peer model in school and afterschool settings. Specifically, the grantee proposes to: 1) provide new youth wellness resources for afterschool programs focused on serving adolescents; 2) work with the 50 State Afterschool Network to identify areas of high need and expand the grantee’s program model; and 3) develop and implement a new technology platform to expand HealthCorps’ reach.

title: Re-Envisioning the CSA Field: From Small-Dollar to Large-Dollar CSAs
description: As children in established children’s savings account programs reach college age, new research offers an opportunity to better understand how these accounts support postsecondary enrollment and how program design can improve outcomes for children from low- and moderate-income families. With renewed Mott Foundation support, the Center for Assets, Education and Inclusion at the University of Michigan will extend research on targeted scholarship programs and Maine’s statewide account program, examine differences in wealth accumulation across households, and translate findings into practical guidance for policymakers and program leaders. The project will connect lessons from existing programs to the federal Trump Accounts framework, with particular attention to how state and community investments can supplement federal deposits. Research reports, policy briefs, public data tools and direct briefings will help inform the next generation of children’s savings account policies. The Center for Assets, Education and Inclusion at the University of Michigan is a leading research center in the asset-building field.

title: Nonprofit Capacity Building
description: The purpose of this grant is to support the United Way of Genesee County, which offers a broad range of services to support nonprofits through capacity building, volunteer management and national service resources. Since the grantee began capacity building work in 2003, over 100 Genesee County agencies have received services that allowed them to: 1) help more individuals in need; 2) leverage new financial and human capital; and 3) collaborate with cross-sector leaders to ensure alignment with community needs.

title: Governor's Service Awards Fund
description: This grant to Michigan Nonprofit Association will support the 2026 Governor’s Service Awards, an annual statewide event recognizing individuals, businesses, and nonprofit organizations whose volunteerism, service and philanthropy have strengthened communities across Michigan. Held in Flint on November 19, 2026, the event celebrates civic leadership while generating support for volunteer and community service initiatives administered by the Michigan Community Service Commission.

title: Mott Foundation Youth Choice Awards
grantee: Trading Hammers for Hammers Foundat Ion
description: This grant will provide funding for Flint area youth-driven projects aimed at creating positive change through community service. In honor of the Mott Foundation’s centennial anniversary, this grant will give kindergarten through 12th-grade students who attend schools within the city limits of Flint, schools included in the Flint Center for Educational Excellence Network, and nonprofits located in Flint the opportunity to elevate their voices through service projects and by selecting additional Centennial Youth Choice Award winners.

title: Mott Foundation Youth Choice Awards
description: This grant will provide funding for Flint area youth-driven projects aimed at creating positive change through community service. In honor of the Mott Foundation’s centennial anniversary, this grant will give kindergarten through 12th-grade students who attend schools within the city limits of Flint, schools included in the Flint Center for Educational Excellence Network, and nonprofits located in Flint the opportunity to elevate their voices through service projects and by selecting additional Centennial Youth Choice Award winners.

title: Helen Taylor Freshwater Fund
description: In honor of retiring State Director Helen Taylor’s 30-year career, the Nature Conservancy has established a fund in her name to protect Michigan’s freshwater resources. This grant will add to this fund, which will support freshwater land protection, innovative research and partnerships that keep Michigan’s waters healthy for generations.
